If front desk staff (or even parking staff in the UNATTENDED booth in the garage) took the time to make guests aware of parking issues, I would have planned accordingly. The only option was to use the convention center garage across the street, which does allow anyone to walk in off the street. Hotel did remove all parking fees from my bill and cover the $-.-- fee in the other garage. The front desk said they have enough parking for - car per room, clearly the hotel has no clue as to what goes on in its garage.
Too much noise from the rooms, had to call security twice during the night. Again, this is a college town and most likely many people find their way to the rooms of hotel guests. However, the hotel had no security or check points to stop non-guests from taking elevators up to guest rooms. Management did make adjustments on my bill to compensate for their short comings. However, the sense of out of control guests and no oversight of their parking confirms I will not stay at this location again. I should have figured something out when all other downtown hotels were booked for this weekend, except for the Hilton.

We arrived at this hotel late at night and decided not to stay. It was a strange environment. I could see through the windows that there were fans in the rooms, which I took as a bad sign, ie that the a-c might not be working. The building looked very old and run down. There were a couple of shady drunk people wandering around (it was a weekend nite). And I noticed people kept looking out their windows for some reason. The area itself wasn't that great. There were a number of places that advertised the same or cheaper prices. 
I had originally made a reservation online. Fortunately they were kind enough to cancel (I had to call three different numbers and got lucky). I guess that was the only good point.

We stayed in this hotel for - night in August ----. For anyone who wants to experience downtown Memphis, the location of this hotel is perfect. There is a trolley stop right outside the back door and you are only a few blocks from Beale St. It was very relaxing to open our curtains and watch the trolleys and horse drawn carriages go by. The staff at the hotel was very friendly and helpful. Breakfast included plenty of hot and cold items, including sausage and eggs. The pool area was nice and included a hot tub. There was also free wifi throughout the hotel. When in Memphis I will definitely stay here again.

We stayed in the New Yorker for one night on a business trip...and I probably wouldn't want to stay any longer. The rooms are small, probably big enough for just --- people who aren't looking for an oasis but a place to sleep after touring NYC. The bed was very comfortable but I thought it was strange that the blanket they gave us was so thing, so as a result we had to blast the heat on all night. Wasn't very impressed with the bathrooms. They definitely need updating and it gives the feel that no matter how many times you clean it, it still feels kinda dirty. It's definitely very different from any Sheraton, Holiday Inn, Marriott or Radisson I've ever been in. 
That being said, the location was unbeatable. It was a quick -- minute walk to Times Square, Macys and endless shopping is right at your fingertips. The subway is also just right outside the hotel making it super convenient.

If you've ever been on the Tower of Terror at Disneyland this is exactly what it looked like. Probably because the hotel is so old, but I definitely would be afraid of staying here by myself overnight.

I've stayed at this hotel in the past mostly due to the location and proximity to where I'm doing business. However there are a few things to note. The front desk staff while they are friendly and accomodating do a quick --- if a phone call comes in and then you're second in line, wihch is annoying. The rooms are OK, but can use some renovating. My room had some cosmetic issues, like broken tiles in the bath and kitchen. the One bedroom suite has the queen bed crammed into a very small space. In addition I had one of the interior rooms. While it is quiet, you get absolutely no sun or sky view at all. What you do get is an alley view and another room directly across from your window. Not much to write home about. The couch has had better days; the cushions were shot. The person or persons who designed this building with the rooms situated as mine is obviously didn't care about what guests would want or desire. 
In addition note that valet parking is all this place has and at $---night its kind of a ripoff. But there really is no other choice unless you want to try street parking and risk getting towed.
As said earlier the rooms could use a renovation. In addition the A-C is very loud as is the refridgerator. Both seem to be on constantly. Not very environmentally friendly. 
The hotel maids are anything but quiet during the day. One afternoon I was working in the room and all I could hear was one mail screaming something in Spanish to another. What about the people who are sleeping during the day? I bet those maids wouldn't appreciate someone yelling outside their door while they are sleeping or working, no?
One more complaint and then I'll stop. The hot and cold water do not mix well when taking a shower. Its either scalding hot or cold, no inbetween. I'm not sure what thats all about, but at $----night it would be nice to get something inbetween, no?
Thats all. I'll end with this is probably the last time I'll stay here. Its time to find a hotel in Beverly Hills that actally lives up to the Beverly Hills name!

Christmas Road Trip Adventure!!
We were traveling back from Austin, TX to Orange County, CA, and told by family and friends NOT to stop in El Paso, that there wasn't any place safe or nice to spend the night, etc, etc.
Well stubborn us, we needed to find some place nice that had internet in the room for my wife to get some work done during the road trip and, and after some googling, we decided on the Doubletree Hotel El Paso Downtown-City Center, and boy were we glad we did.
Starting with a phone call to check availability and a quick transfer to their reservations line, I got a little frustrated with the agent before getting disconnected. We just decided to show up and book the room since it was a Monday night and they appeared to have plenty of rooms.
The hotel was easily accessible off the I---. Upon arrival and a quick trip to the lobby restrooms, our check-in at the front desk was very efficient, especially with the clerk finding my Hilton Honors account to help expedite the process. The warm cookies are always a nice touch.
Our room was clean and comfortable. View of the hillside star and a downtown X-Mas lights display was a plus. My wife connected to the internet no problemo and got what she needed to get done done while the kidlets unwound from the first leg of our return drive.
Room service for dinner was quick, with just one very minor error on our kid's order which we didn't bug about. Just make sure to double-check under each plate cover.
Time to crash and room temperature was very comfortable. Very restful sleep.
Checkout was easy, no errors on our bill. Starbucks in the lobby was a god-send for hitting the road and finishing last leg.
THANK YOU DOUBLETREE FOR OUR DESERT OASIS FIND!!!

I have stayed here a couple of times before with my wife. This time I was with a friend. We had - economy rooms. These were small,but very clean and comfortable. Apart from the bed which I found super comfortable, I notice that the TVs have been updated & there are now more channels available. This was appreciated when we got in early one evening.
This is an ideal place for those people who will not have a car. The Old Town Transit Station is less than - minutes walk away. From there you can get the trolleys and buses. They're fast, convenient and good value.
I love that this place, which has always been great, doesn't rest on it's laurels. They constantly make improvements, which although small, really make a difference.
All this and their really genuinely helpful and friendly staff, are what makes me come back everytime I'm in San Diego. 
I wouldn't hesitate to recommend the Old Town Inn.

We stayed here one night when attending an event in the Marriott next door. Check in was smooth. However, the rooms are very worn and the carpets in the hallway were dirty. The hot water in the shower was not that hot. The bathroom sink was clogged and when I called for someone to address it, noone ever showed up. We had to leave to our evening event so I never called again. Lastly, the room was not equipped with the sheets-blanket for the sofa bed. I had to call for that also. All in all, this hotel is not up to the usual Residence Inn standards. There are better options in the city at this price point.

We arrived at Hotel Valencia around -pm on a Saturday night with no reservation. The front desk staff was extremely friendly, and we got a king room for $--- (we did talk them down about $-- from their original offer). The room was wonderful!! It had a modern asian flair. All of the surfaces were high quality and clean with a large flat screen TV. There was a hopping scene in the bar off the courtyard until --pm. Our room overlooked the courtyard which was crowded with people. We were just starting to wonder what time it closed when it promptly quieted and the courtyard was suddenly vacant. The noise from the bar scene was gentle, not very loud and not at all annoying. However, if you did want to go to sleep early it might bother you a little. We didn't mind it at all. We didn't hear any other sounds from other rooms. We were on the top floor with views of the beautiful pool and courtyard. We don't get out much and were amazed at the number of people walking around Santana Row during the evening. There are several restaurants and bars. It was fun to be reminded of how lots of people spend Saturday night out!
The next morning there was a very nice buffet breakfast next to the courtyard that was included with the room. Hot eggs, bacon, cereal, toast, coffee, etc. It was wonderful to sit in the sun in the courtyard to sip coffee and plan our day. 
The bed was extremely comfortable, well appointed and very clean. I love the down comforter with a sheet-duvet so there is no yucky bedspread. We were delighted to discover this wonderful hotel and plan to stay here again. Santana Row is a great shopping location and there are a number of restaurants to choose from. Even my husband had fun and he is definitely NOT a big shopper! We had dinner at Left Bank which was great (order the french fries for an appetizer!)
I would definitely recommend this as a weekend getaway. There is shopping during the day at Santana Row and across the street at Vanity Fair Mall, great restaurants and a fun night scene.

Me and - of my girls stayed at the hotel's Quad buckbed room this weekend and we loved it! The hotel was clean, very close to Time Square and the subway. Room was bigger than I expected for the area, not saying it was huge, but definately bigger than others I've stayed in in that area.
Would make - suggestions tho... add a towel hook right outside the shower so its easier to access your towel after showering. And add an extra curtain (like the one for the closet) in front of the shower-toilet area so theres a dry space to get dressed after showering too.
But regardless... we loved it! It was just overall awesome!!! The staff was super friendly and helpful at all hours of the day-night... we really couldn't have asked for a better stay. Definately will recommend it and will definately be back!

Very Unfriendly, they overcharged me and did not even answer my complaint mail no answer at all.
Very unfriendly people working at hotel, very noisy not easy to sleep.
they forget to put towels in my room and I had to go to reception to have some towels, very bad experience I will not go that hotel anymore.

I have stayed at other Drury Inns and enjoyed them, which is why I booked a room at this property for a recent three night stay. This hotel was not nearly as nice as the other Drury Inns I stayed at. Even the location was a lot less desirable, very busy street in an industrial-commercial area. The closest thing I saw to aesthetics was the same pile of fast food litter which sat in the parking lot for my entire stay would shift periodically with the wind. I would not stay here expecting the Drury Inn experience you get in Amarillo or other places.

I have just returned from a stay at the Downtown Marriott (-nd--th Oct). I was travelling with - friends & we stayed in a - double bedded room. I was a little worried about - of us in one room; the amount of space, one badroom, getting ready etc. However our room was great, it was clean, had everything we needed and enough space & storage for us all. Admittedly we were not in it very much as there is so much to do in New York, but as a base and for the price it was excellent. Do not go if you are after luxury and personality. The only thing I could fault is the fact that one of the elevators was not working (you had to wait a good few minutes for one to arrive) and the staff on the reception desk were not very friendly. I'd reccomend it to anyone going to New York who wants somewhere that is clean & good value as a base.

Walls are thin and you really hear every noise. The NBA all star weekend was occurring why we were there and it was so loud we complained after hours of trying to fall asleep. The heater ran all night and would blow cold air out periodically. It was loud and rattling. The bathroom had broken tiles, holes in the wall, cigarette burns on the sink and paint rubbing away on the towel holder. The room overall looked like there had been fights in there with dents in the metal door. The paint job was sloppy and looked like there was no attention to detail. There was something crusty on the desk that hadn't been wiped down. It was a miserable hotel in a terrible location and I would not recommend anyone stay there. We locked valuables in our car when we were gone because we didn't feel safe. Please look for another hotel. Not this one!!!!

Upon checking in, the room had an odor. I found a spider on the wall in one of the bedrooms, scotch tape stuck to one wall, crumbs on the kitchen floor (underneath overhang of cabinets), top of refrigerator dusty and cobweb dangling from kitchen cabinet, outlets and light switches were dirty also. I told my husband that I wanted to go elsewhere, but he talked me out of it. The next day I left a $-.-- tip for housekeeper with a note that asked for detailed cleaning. There was no detailed cleaning done, in fact on her way out of our room she dropped two dirty hand towels on the floor (doesn't a person, especially a housekeeper turn around to give a final glance to her cleaned room). On consecutive housekeeping, crumbs were still not swept up. Also, the fireplace timer didn't work, you have to get down on the floor and remove the front plate and manually flip the switch to either on or off (by the way it looks like they have never vacuumed under there, there are papers, dust bunnies, etc). One final note, it was windy while we were here and the one bedroom window doesn't sit flush and you could here the windy blowing sounding like a train all night long. Never complained to mgmt about housekeeping (afraid she may clean the toilets with my toothbrush, just made a mental note not to stay here again.

We -my son and me - had a nice stay in S. F. The Carlton is located really centrally - and even at night we didn't feel uncomfortable in that area.
Especially the staff was very, very friendly and helpful.
The room was clean and cosy, nice view from our room, nice lobby.
(We had our breakfast only in near restaurants, at night the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Fly"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (just beneath the Carlton) can be recommended.)

We enjoyed the really nice elevators (worldmaps and nice pictures !).
We hope that we will have the opportunity to come and stay here again ...

We were greeted very nicely upon our arrival by the doorman and immediately we were helped with our - heavy suitcases. The female front desk agents were helpful and formal but I noticed that they never smiled at all. That seemed strange to me because the men were very attentive whenever we entered or left the hotel and they would smile. I guess it's just a Washington female thing. Anyways, the room was very nice and there were plenty of towels and hot water even during the winter. The beds were great but our room did tend to get cold even with the heating system on. We had two windows that would get veeery cold especially at night. Not even the heavy curtains would hold back the cold. The bathroom ran the same fate. The cold from that window would make you shake just by stepping out of a hot shower. The hotel has a great location (close to a metro station)which we used from the airport and back. You can't beat a $-.-- fare and just be one block from your hotel. There were - elevators that were very efficient in moving the guests around the building and everything was in optimal condition. My only complaint would be the lack of a light in the closet area upon entering the room. It was dark and we had a hard time locating our things in this area. Our room was a corner room #---. In spite of this issue, I would come back to this hotel if I once again find a good rate as I did on this trip.

Stayed at Warwick for a couple of days for a conference in Midtown. Location is excellent, walking distance to Time Square, Rockefeller Center, ..etc.
Hotel staff were friendly and services were generally good, though I was out of the hotel most of the time. 
Hotel has the antique look and is very elegantly decorated. Room is quiet and comfortable, above average for this price range.
Technology wise this hotel is terrible. There was a MP--connectible alarm clock so that is nice. LCD TV but only analog channels which defeats the purpose of having HDTV. There is only two free electrical plugs which is not enough for me to charge my cell phone and other devices. They are also very hard to reach, unlike many hotel that has electrical outlets on the table lamp.
Wifi is not free and there are two tiers of Wifi you can pay - $-- per day for slow and $-- for fast. I paid for the $-- which is bearable for basic web surfing and emails but not fast enough for even low resolution videos from Youtube. Come one Warwick, surely if a $-- a night model can include free Wifi you guys can do it too. Stop being so greedy !
Overall, this is a good hotel if you do not have high tech needs.

This hotel is rather lovely, brand new. I am not quite certain if my room had been slept in truly, because it had a new smelling aroma, like when you move into a new home. Very refreshing, located directly on the Riverwalk, couldn't have enjoyed my stay more. My room was very big, and I loved how I had a refridgerator so that I could keep my beverages cold. I would very much so suggest this hotel, it was great. The staff was so helpful, housekeeping was polite and made every effort to say hi.

Right on river. Walk out the back door and you are on the riverwalk. Cross over on the walking bridge and hop a boat for a historic tour of the river area. Takes about -- minutes and costs $-.--. You also get a chance to scope out the riverside restaurants and pick one to come back to later. The hotel iteself is part of the tour due to its unique construction. Currently undergoing renovations which will be completed in January of ----, the hotel is fully operational. Beautiful room with king bed overlooking the river. Will be returning here in the future.

I have stayed at the Marquis on several occasions. It is pricy, but you get what you pay for. It is very lovely, especially when decorated for the holidays. The rooms are large for NYC standards, very clean, and most have great views. Our view was of the Hudson River this time around, and it was very pretty. What should have been a $-- ride according to the concierge turned into a $-- trip (I tracked him on Google and he took the super LONG way). The Park Hyatt does have a car however it was only offered to us one time, after I complained about cab drivers ripping us off. We are not high maintenance or demanding so we walked a lot. Call it exercise. The M is a good alternative though the closest station is a good walk as well.
Without kids none of the items above would have been an issue and we certainly hold none of them against the Park Hyatt.The only real complaint we had that the Park Hyatt could address was the size of the TV's. In the end, I would definitely consider staying at Luxe City Center next time I am in the area. The stay was great. If with family or wanting a pool, I might consider elsewhere that actually has a pool though.

If you can't afford La Jolla or Coronado, go for a reputable name motel in Del Mar, Solana Beach, Cardiff, Encinitas, Leucadia, La Costa, or Carlsbad. We arrived as a school party. The foyer looks impessive and vast, but the reception is always a waiting process, no matter what hour of the day and night. The standard of helpfulness of the staff varies from pleasant and effective to impolite bordering on hostile. There are apparently three standards of room, with the web site only showing the top two, corporate and ----. If you end up with a standard room, beware! Out of - rooms allocated to our group, three had to be changed. One had a cockroach running about, mine had a brown oozing damp patch that smelled horrible, a third was a double bedded room when we asked for and were told it was a twin bedded room. Even getting a simple plug ( a stopper they call it in the US) proved beyond them. After the third time of asking, a maintenance man arrived and put the stopper on the key entry slot. To my dismay it was a bath stopper and didn't fit the sink. 
Internet access is not free, and varies from - dollars for -- minutes to -- dollars for the day. Given that all of the public buildings we visited AND Times Square have free open wifi access, I find this a bit quaint.
The damp foul smelling patch I discovered by mistake and to my horror when trying to open the window and stood in the patch. Upon putting a hotel towel on the patch it immediately stained brown. Upon taking this down to reception and waiting the obligatory -- minute minimum, I was treated discourteously for daring to have put their towel containing their filth on their counter,. The manager was consulted and to be fair to him, he was actually courteous and professional. My room was changed to a ---- - even here the main room light didn't work. I would say this is the minimum standard one would expect of even the most modest hotel in the UK. The standard rooms come with cracked and falling off plaster and scuff marks along the wall, old, tired decor as standard. To finish off our stay, I went to sign out and place our luggage in the secure area we had been promised when we arrived. We were told that sometimes these are allocated, sometimes they are not, and in our case it was not. I expressed my dissatisfaction about this and was then given a key to a room for the party to use as a luggage store. I was advised that this was a room that wasn't normally occupied, so my expectations were already low. However, when I opened the door the room contained twin beds, one of which looked like it had just been vacated by its occupant, the bathroom had a towel on the floor and a hole in the ceiling. In the corridor, plaster had been botch repaired and not painted afterwards. I havre photographic evidence of all of the above. In conclusion, if you are looking for a place to stay in New York, I would advise to avoid the Penn like the plague or you just might catch it!

Just got done with a convention at the hotel in July '--. The short take is that this is a HUGE hotel and is only really geared for conventions. I would never recommend to stay here for pleasure. 
The good: It's beautiful, enormous, nice meeting rooms, good food in the conference areas. It's pretty close to downtown-old town with tons of restaurants, but it's a cab ride away. The workout facilities are the best I have ever seen in a hotel-resort, though they cost extra. The workout is like a fully equiped LA Fitness! Staff was pretty nice too.
The bad: There's really only - restaurants in the place plus take out place that is only open certain hours. This place is ENORMOUS yet there are only - sit down restaurants?! I ate in both of them and they were overpriced and not very good. In fact, they pretty much sucked. There are no restaurants in walking distance either. The pool was a major letdown and was about as nice as something you'd find at a YMCA but with a pool bar in it. Very disappointing for afternoons when you're trying to catch a little relaxation between meetings. There are beautiful, park like grounds around this hotel and they couldn't do a better pool? Weird. No free internet, the rooms were so small you had to go outside of them to change your mind, and the atrium in the atrium wing was seriously about -- degrees. The room was cold, but you'd be sweating by the time you get to the elevator if you have a suit on.
Bottom line. This place is only geared toward conventions. They don't care about individual traveler experience and it shows in the amenities. For such a beautiful property, it was a strange contradiction and I would not recommend staying here if you had a choice as there are so many other options in a city the size of Dallas.

I can't believe Crowne Plaza would possibly keep its name attached to this place. I've stayed in CP hotels before and have found them perfectly serviceable business-style hotels. This was completely awful. 
It was unbelievably dirty everywhere - hall carpets didn't look like they'd been cleaned in months, everything else was equally filthy (eg dirt in every drawer). 
The only benefit of this place is the location (which for us worked due to airport proximity but had nothing else to recommend it) but I would not stay there again, no matter how cheap.

Booked this hotel because the reviews online aren't too bad and it was amongst the cheaper -+ stars ones in manhattan, although it was the most expensive hotel in our US trip. 
There's a F line subway exit on the right of the hotel, M-- bus is nearby too and it can take you to several sights. WHOLE FOOD MARKET is about - minutes away towards the left. Tenement museum and SOHO are both walkable. 
The receptionists are quite friendly and professional, the delivered our luggage to our room before we got back to the hotel. We didn't even get to pay tips to whoever that helped send the luggage up. But it was a nice feeling that they weren't doing it just for the tips.
The room, is very small, which was expected from NYC. however furnitures had obvious signs of wear and tear, which makes the room look old rather than 'modern'. The wardrobe was thin and tiny, there's hangers inside but you really can't hang anything in there. There's no safe in the room. But one pair of slippers are provided. There's no snack bar in room but a bottle o FIJI water. 
The bath tub wasn't very clean and it hasn't been clean een till the day we left. Toiletry products had not been replaced-refilled at all during our stay. They use BULGARI products which seemed too luxurious for a room like this where they provide disposable foam cups in bathroom. 
We had a room in the back so it wasn't facing the main street but we could still hear abit of noise coming from the pubs.
The breakfast is complimentary. Very simple but not the worst we've seen. They serve ILLY coffee. 
During our stay one day we went back to our room to find out the rubbish bin was on the desk! Bottle water has not been replaced and there was dirt in toilet that had not been flushed away after cleaning. It was so gross we almost went to complain because this is not what we gave tips for! 
Anyway it you are looking for location and value, when you can find a good price online this might not be a bad choice, but the room was a let down for the price we pay.

This hotel is a great option for a family. We ended up with just two of us rolling around the spacious - bedroom suite, but the rate was fair. Don't look for luxury appointments - it's more like suburban tract house, but clean and comfortable. On-site parking (free, maybe because I'm a Marriott Rewards member) and a complete, fresh breakfast at no charge make for convenience and savings. And with Dupont Circle just two blocks away, there's plenty of variety in food nearby. This is a good location to get around from, either by car or Metro, too.

Our room was perfect, and all the staff was very friendly and very helpful....Georgia Rios is a very sweet lady and you could not ask for betty service ........Made our trip very enjoyable, thank you to all..........Will definately stay her again.
Cindy and Bill Drake

We were here for - nights. Very knowledgeable and friendly staff. Great at giving advice on how to get around, restaurants and other things we needed. Rooms had fridge, microwave and tv. Free parking and only half a block to the bus and - blocks to the cable car! We would definitely stay here again.

The staff is super friendly helpfull, the rooms are great nice design and clean. you can walk from the airport to the hotel and they also hav an excellent shutlle service.
Also the brakfast is great 
absolutely great place to relax after a long flight

We upgraded to the Jr. Suite as we were travelling with our - yr. old great-niece & -- yr. old great-nephew. It worked out really well having the additional room & the sleeper sofa. The room was comfortable, quiet and relaxing. The check-in service was prompt & courteous. We went to Sea World & this hotel was conveniently located. There were several restauraunts, a grocery store & a Target close by, which made it easy to pick up food & extras. We enjoyed our stay and would stay at the Wyndham Garden SD again. Thanks for the hospitality.

On our recent cross country trip we arrived in Denver looking for a room at -am. The area was well lit and had a nice skyline view and convienient to I---. The front desk agent Anton was very welcoming and friendly. This location has an included hot breakfast in the morning with made to order omlets. Our room was very clean,large,had a mini fridge the beds were soft and comfortable. the only thing missing was a microwave but there is one in the lobby for guest use. We didnt utilize the pool or fitness room that was available. There is also a computer and printer for guest use free of charge.For the rate and location i would stay here again.

Three friends stayed for a concert at the Chicago Theatre, just a block and a half away. We had plenty of room in a freshly carpeted room with two queen beds. Front desk service was lively and helpful as was the doorman throughout the the afternoon and evening. We ate dinner at the adjacent restaraunt, and again service was really good as was the food. 
Everything was better than expected.

My company put me up here when my truck broke down, they were very quick to send the shuttle van to the shop to pick me up! $--.--
Comfy bed, carpet could use a shampoo, but was vacuumed. Wall paper in bathroom should be replaced instead of patched.
I stayed on the back side in room #--- which was fairly quiet, except for when the neighbors closed the door.

My thanks to the staff of the Hampton Inn - Denver International Airport for making my stay comfortable and successful. I am a business traveler stuck in Denver with minimum luggage due to blizzard conditions in the East. The staff at the Hampton Inn were proactive in anticipating and meeting every need for making my stay comfortable and enabling me to be productive.

This hotel is at a great location, the rooms are amazing and I love the purple color. The price is great as well. Such a different type of hotel that makes you feel like you're in the future. I also loved the rooftop. Everything is so efficient at Yotel. Probably the best hotel in NYC if you don't mind the small rooms.

The room was luxurious all around. The valet, although pricey, is understandable given the location. The complimentary iced coffee (morning) and wine-sangria-tea-lemonade (afternoon) were all nice perks. When I entered the outdoor pool area on the fourth floor, I thought I had walked onto the set of a beer commercial: a bar and pool filled with half-naked men and women enjoying their stay. That said, it was a nice place to relax and spend an afternoon. 
My only complaint would be the noise: dogs barking in the wee hours of the night; then a pot-smoking, hip-hop-blasting jerk nextdoor. It took an hour of calling the front desk before this guy finally settled down around -:--am. Meanwhile, our room (with a shared suite door) reeked of marijuana smoke. A bit of bad luck, I suppose. Had anyone asked how our stay was, I would have been happy to mention this.

When I usually book a hotel, I do one of those online bids and keep my fingers crossed that the hotel given is halfway decent. I didn't bid this time, instead selecting the Holiday Inn Express Fisherman'sWharf and I am glad I did. Even though the place was packed, our room was very quiet and our bed very comfortable. The breakfast was great and the free internet was a plus. We were so close to everything yet far enough to avoid hearing all the outdoor noises. The staff at the front desk and phone staff were very respectful. My advice to prospective tourists and on line bidders is to refrain from the bargain bidding web sites and choose this hotel outright. The comfortable setting, free breakfast, internet and fine staff makes the Holiday Inn Express Fisherman's Wharf a wise and cost efficient selection.

My wife and I came to Seattle for the Celtic Woman concert at the Paramount Theater. We were surprised to see just how close it was to our event, and to so many incredible dining choices located within walking distance. The staff was attentive, very knowledgable about the locations of everything we asked about. I feel the pricing ws very good, and deserving of our business the next time we visit the theater.

The lobby is impressive but the room we stayed in was dreadful. Old, dark, weirdly decorated... not what youd expect from a Hilton. The location is convenient, but there are far better hotels nearby for this price.

My stay at this Country Inn and Suites here was excellent. Great nights sleep in a comfortable bed and a very clean room. I've stayed at number of Country Inn's and Suites around the nation when travelling and this one ranks the highest. Their attention to detail is what sets this one apart. The entire hotel, including the grounds outside are immaculately clean. It's located in a nice business park. There's a nice fitness center in the hotel, but jogging-walking outside is also great in this area. Lots of nearby restaurants too. The management and the staff here is top notch and very professional as well as friendly. They should train other hotels how to treat their guests.

My husband booked this hotel at the last minute because it had a pool and complimentary breakfast. We orginally were booked at the Hyatt Regancy.
The worst thing about this hotel is that is it -- floors up and to get from the parking gargage (down a long hallway) to the elevator and then to another elevator to get to your rooms takes about -- minutes.
The rooms were okay. Nothing great about them. The room was clean. The shower water pressure was awesome! The beds were hard. They do have a pillow menu where you can pick the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""type"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of pillow you would like. We had a nice view of the city. 
We walked everywhere. It was a long walk w- - children and a stroller but we all survived. We walked to Michigan Ave, Navy Pier and Millenium Park. I think next time we will pick a hotel a little more centrally located. 
We had free breakfast because it was included in military discount. It was okay. Never would I have paid $-- a person for it!!!! Our bill before the coupons taken off was $--.-- for - adults and - children. Basic foods: eggs, hashbrowns, bacon, sausage, fruit and bagels.

Just returned from a - night stay at The Mandarin Oriental Boston and it was exceptional!
Upon arrival we were greeted by a helpful bell boy who took our luggage and lead us to reception. Check in was efficient and friendly. We were allocated our rooms, numbers --- and ---; both of the Back Bay category. 
The rooms were beautifully appointed with a view to the front of the hotel. Every conceivable convenience and comfort had been thought of. The rooms were large with walk in wardrobe, seating area, writing desk, large tv and mini bar. 
Bathrooms were wow! Walk in shower, bath and separate toilet. Toiletries were luxurious. Fluffy towels and robes provided.
The bed was very comfortable with Frette bed linen, pure luxury!
Maid service was discreet and efficient.
Whilst there my partner and I used the gym and again it was without fault.. Each station having towels and water. Headphones (disposable) were supplied for tv-radio and fruit and cold towels for post workout.
Breakfast in the Asana restaurant was excellent. The menu was varied and the portions more than enough to start the day. Beverages were also replenished as required. Staff great.
I must pay special thanks to the staff at the Mandarin Oriental, especially Kelly the concierge and Tim the bell boy. Nothing was too much trouble. 
Another nice touch of this hotel is the direct undercover access to the Prudential shopping Plaza.
The lobby area provided a welcome rendezvous for afternoon tea-drinks.
Superb location for sightseeing, shopping and restaurants. 
A truly fabulous luxury hotel with a relaxed and friendly atmosphere. Wonderful experience from start to finish.
Bravo Mandarin Oriental Boston!

I am Best Western Elite member and have stayed at many of their properties but this property was a shocker. 
As reported by another reviewer, the breakfast is horrendous; the free internet is so slow. And this is just the good part.
The front desk has only - person ever manning it and at peak times the lines get so long. While the staff are trying to be polite you get the sense that they have heard about all the complaints and there is nothing to be done. The room we were given (while spacious) had a terrible bed. On the first night there was so much noise from the streets. Later I found out that there was roof top party on the car park beside the hotel !!! Now if there was air con in the room I could have closed the window - that was yet another unpleasant surprise.
I did ask to change the room but they just pointed me to other rooms that were much worse. As I said the staff know all the problems and have answers for all of them.
And to round it off, the safe in the room does not work. We used the safes in the reception area which turned out to be a good idea. On one of the trips to the reception desk, I came across this couple who were complaining that their passports had been taken from the safe. I was surprised since I was told by the reception that the safes don't work at all. I am not sure what happened to that couple but we made sure we did not leave our valuables in the hotel.
While the location is ok, I would not recommend this hotel to anyone. I most certainly will not be going back.

Absolutely loved staying at Hollywood Inn Express South Hotel. The hotel is -.- miles from Hwy --- and - miles from Hollywood and - miles from downtown, so it was easy to move around easily. The hotel rooms were nice and clean with free car parking. 
The swimming pool is too small but we never cared for it. There is a wireless internet available with good speed in rooms. The hotel provide coffee, doughnuts and juice in the morning breakfast which was good. Overall, my experience staying here was really good and I recommend this hotel to everyone.

I have stayed at the Boston Copley twice in the last year. Each time the room was clean and nice, but this is a huge impersonal convention type hotel, not the kind of place I usually like and really it's a little unlovable. But the Westin Copley has a couple of things going for it. First, if you pay a little extra you get a mesmerizing view of the Charles river and city, really wonderful. Second, the location is just fantastic. It's a short walk from the train station and has a Starbucks right downstairs. But even more importantly, you can walk to the Boston public library, the Charles river walking trails, the shops and restaurants of Newbury Street, the Boston Common and other key sights. I prefer real street life, but the hotel is also attached to a huge mall with a lot of nice shops and restaurants. So the key to staying here is to make the most of the location and not expect much in the way of atmosphere from the hotel.

I would highly recommend this hotel for your visit to San Diego! It is in a great location (literally ----- minutes away from everything) and the staff, especially Brian, is extremely helpful and they follow up on requests as well as housekeeping. In fact, when we checked in, Travelocity had booked us the wrong type of room so Brian upgraded us to a more than comparable room without hesitation. It was spacious and very clean. Beds were comfortable and doors were quiet....did not hear any slamming in the mornings. Complimentary breakfast, beer & wine, and some nights even free dinner...wow! In today's economy, this really helped out my family of four to have an awesome stay and vacation there! Will be talking about this place to friends and family.

We travelled to Boston a couple of weekends ago to watch a college game, as well as to play tourists. After skimming thru some briefs hotel reviews, the choice came down to between The Langham & Hotel Commonwealth. (Note: We chose Hotel Commonwealth because The Langham was undergoing some lobby renovation). Having hailed from Asia where hotel hospitality, amenity and sevice are second to none, we were very pleased with our weeeknd stay at the Hotel Commonwealth in Boston. It is truly a Class Act in every aspect. From the moment we checked in, Ester at Front Desk was such a star in making us feel welcome right away. We ere given a much appreciated room upgrade, and when we were desperate for a dinner reservation on a Saturday night at the very last minute, Brandon (Front Desk-Concierge) shone like a knight in shinning armor to come to our rescue and found us a place we had some of the best lobsters-seafood in town. The location of Hotel Commonwealth was prime, and convenient, as everything was within walking distance. The decor and interior were immaculately upkept, and primed in great taste. The turndown service was going beyond the mile, the staffs (from valets to housekeeping) extended such warmth and service, and the experience was special, and definitely worth more than what we paid in tariffs two-folds. So, if you get a chance to experience the Hotel Commonwealth during a stay in Boston, do it, and you ought to ahve a brilliant time like we did!!!

I stayed at a London Suite:
Highlights:

-Automated curtains… awesome
-Consistently clean

Cons:

Stayed here for - nights for a work trip, and enjoyed my King Study...good size room, bigger than a typical hotel room, which gives you some space between your bed and the door, making it a little quieter in bed. Front desk staff extremely helpful and nice. Breakfast was ok, better than some Hampton Inn's, but not as good as others. Beds comfortable of course. Only problem with location is that it can be a pain to get some places due to SW Loop --- being a one-way, but just use side streets...tons of restaurants and a mall around, so it's a nice area. Will stay here again!

I stayed at the Mandarin in early July after a major renovation. The guest rooms that occupy -----th floors of the third tallest building of SF are so well appointed. I was in a bridge to bridge room that literally had the sweeping view of the golden gate bridge to the other bridge that goes to Oakland and being on the --th floor, I felt like I was literally floating in the sky.
The service is superb from the moment you step out of the car til the moment heading out to the airport. They are adding a brand new spa and a fitness center (due to open at the end of Sept) and the new lobby feels very modern and open. I can't wait to return!!!!

I had read several reviews that were quite scary..but decided to follow through anyway..The pickup at the airport was very prompt, in fact the hotel shuttle was excellent..they provided free transport to downtown and back..the location to Graceland can't be beat...and no charge to park..the staff was very nice and helpful...the breakfast was OK....We did have some comments on the not so good...we found a dirty men's athletic sock in nightstand as well as some cookies...a drawer in the sitting room has - of the knobs missing..no big deal but also couldn't be too big a deal to rectify...I happened to notice another room a few doors down also was missing a knob on the same dresser....must be a hot item..
Overall, the hotel experience was at best very average but In all honesty some of the postives did balance things somewhat...it definitely is not a luxury resort...I do think they could use some refurbishing and some attention to small details...there was no water available in the coin machine that had - designated water positions.
On checking out I met - ladies who had just arrived from the UK the evening before and this was their first trip to America and they mentioned that they were booked into the hotel for TEN days...that in my opinion would be closer to a sentence than a vacation by choice...after the Graceland experience there is very little else in the area and Memphis for that matter...I think --- days gives you an opportunity to see the highlights quite comfortably. Hopefully this helps someone plan their Elvis vacation. I do suggest to incorporate Nashville if at all possible.
Ron B.

I know there are grande dames in Boston hotel circles. . but for comfort, location, staffing, and facilities, the Hotel Commonwealth cannot be beat.
I stay at the property each year during a baseball trip. . . and Fenway Park is just around the corner. . but even if you weren't doing baseball, this hotel has the best of all possible worlds in a great location.
If I have one complaint and it is minor. .. food service is not particularly to my tastes. . why not just good food but efforts are made to modernize and make it trendy, which seems to distract what otherwise would be a great dining experience. 
All hotel groupies should try this place!!!!

I honestly don't understand all the rave reviews on here for this hotel. It's a decent place but not really anything special. The free drinks and snacks are a nice touch for a hotel in this price range, but many others offer this as well. They really need to update the decor and furnishings of this hotel, very --s looking. Most of their competition have done so already, including most Hamptons and LaQuintas. The wifi is spotty at best.
The staff also could be described as adequate, nothing better or worse. You will get mostly blank stares or shrugs from them when asked a question. 
The area is horrendous as far as traffic and congestion are concerned. It's a good thing there are several restaurants within walking distance, because it's a real hassle to take your car out in this neighborhood. However the restaurants are just your average, national chain places, so if you want a decent meal you will have to get in your car.
Lastly, I don't see why everyone is so impressed with the security gate. Yes, you need a room key card to get through the gate, but so what? If someone wants to make mischief, he can just park in the Friday's lot right next door and walk over, as they are connected! Besides the gate is problematic, as I usually had to swipe my card several (more than five) times before it would work.
All in all, not a horrible place, but certainly there are better options nearby at a similar price.

Great hotel, friendly and effiecient staff, Magnolia club excellent for breakfast and evening wind down, rooms clean and comfortable
Only problem that I had was accessing the internet; Hotel staff were unable to help with this. Some of my colleagues had the same problem.

My partner and I returned to Denver for a two week stay. Having greatly enjoyed the massages on one other occasion two years ago at the Brown Palace, we had planned on visiting the Brown while we were in town. That first time we had stayed the weekend at the Brown in addition to the massages. This time like last time, we did the couples package for massages. The service was great - from taking the reservations, the masseuses' services, and the brief visit later by the receptionist who was at the desk when we arrived. That receptionist had not been at the desk when we were finished. But from wherever she was coming from within the hotel heading toward the spa, she diverted and came to our table. We were sitting at one of the tables that was in front of the spa, having high tea (as our way to end the pleasant afternoon at the Brown). We were not facing the spa. So it was quite a nice touch and surprise that she came up to us and spoke with us briefly to include inquiring about the service. We had not expected that. That was nice. The attendants (Ida and Corey) providing the massages were most professional, friendly, answering a variety of questions, checking just enough during the massage to not take away from the experience. I had the deep tissue massage - you would want to pay attention and hope that the massage is done right. I'd say it was. My partner and I had been to other spas since our first spa visit at the Brown and that first spa treatment was the standard we used when we compared it to others. This second time around was just as good as the first. We plan on visiting the Brown Palace each time we return to Colorado (I hope every year).

All the reviews are right. This is a great facility, rooms great, big gym with modern equipment, staff great, shuttle service great. What we didn't know was that our lodge also had a big entrance room equipped with baskets and refrigerators full of yoghurt, icecream, fruit and little snacks - all free. We loved it.
The shuttle makes half hourly trips to the airport and train station.. To get from the airport you walk over the bridge into the carparking area and locate the hotel shuttle service areas (I think we had to go down one level) and give the hotel a call from the free telephone (there's a list with a different number for each hotel). Great service.
We left our cruise documents behind in the room and the staff were able to locate them and fax our boarding passes to us. Thank you so much to the staff involved, especially the cleaning staff who handed them in.

The Pan Pacific Seattle is quite a beautiful hotel and the level of service was first-rate. The views from the wall of windows were outstanding, and the bathroom is one of the best: the tub is very deep and there is a separate shower room. 
The location is OK - Whole Foods and Starbucks couldn't be more convenient, but it was maybe a -- minute walk to the main shopping and -- minutes to Pike Place. Neighborhood felt safe. Hotel parking is expensive, but that is the case anywhere in Seattle. And their friendly valet service includes in-and-out privileges, which is nice. 
The main disappointment for us was the condition of the room. While generally clean and stylish, it didn't quite live up to the standard of the rest of the hotel. There were some small stains in the carpet here and there, black smudges on the cabinets, and the loveseat was the most uncomfortable piece of furniture I've encountered in a hotel! The cushion squishes down, leaving your legs hanging over the hard frame in the front. Another disappointment was the minibar policy - even in the Executive Suite there is only an area for about - pop cans left for personal use. The rest is electronically monitored, so that if you move one of their bottles, you pay! A note said they will remove all the drinks on request - for a fee of $--! Ridiculous. And finally, the fitness center is located in a separate building across a small courtyard. It's not far at all, but it would be a lot more convenient right inside the hotel.
Bottom line: we had a good stay, but there are other hotels in Seattle in the same price range that are better.

Nice, clean, extremely friendly staff, but could do with a renovation. 
In terms of location, a bit far from the centre, but direct train to the tourist areas, bus to Haight-Asbury and not far to Alamo Sq (Painted Ladies). Great if you don't want to be in the crazy centre.
Breakfast not very varied, not much fruit.

My experience with the Westin St. Francis hotel was miserable. I had a ring missing from my hotel room. Their first re-action was that this never happens at their hotel. Then they kept asking me if I checked my room thoroughly. I explained that I checked so thoroughly, I found black panties that were not mine and condoms that were not mine. Even after telling them this, they kept asking if I checked the room. This was very annoying. The safe did not work and this became an issue with their insurance. They told thier insurance the safe did work but neglected to say that it only worked after they fixed it after my ring was missing. They treated me with no respect. To me, service is what a hotel is about, and the service was horrible. Who cares what the rooms are like if you are treated like dirt.

We booked in for - Nights.... got out after -..... the ONLY place in my -.- weeks in the USA where i didnt feel safe. Felt safer on the new york subway....
Staff where unpleasent and looked like they didnt want to be there...
We where meant to get a complimentary breakfast...BUT no sign of it.
Rooms where OK... BUT things where broken.. clock radio didnt work...television brooke after first day...and they eventually replace it.... Mold on shower curtain.

Our experience with this property was just fine. The - of us are - feet and over so it was nice to have - separate beds (- beds and a pull out). Myself and my girlfriend stayed for five days, a --th Birthday present for her! My husband and I had an amazing stay. The location is great, the staff is very friendly and the hotel itself is gorgeous. Our room was large and wonderfully appointed. We would definitely stay here again!
Wonderfully responsive and supber attention to making my stay a stellar experience!!!!

Great place to stay. Room amenities made my stay very comfortable and enjoyable. The free access to a computer and internet was very appreciated as well as having access to the internet via Wi-Fi. The night club lounge was pleasant for an evening cocktail. Having breakfast on site was helpful. Location was just right for my business transit.

The location of this Hilton is convenient, close to the - train. We were very disappointed upon arrival when our reserved top floor double room was reduced to the -th floor. The price was comparable at $---, but $--- with taxes (beware for all NY hotels, taxes are high).
The Rooms: Clean and compact with comfy bedding. Bathrooms are clean and although small, not uncomfortable, the BIG problem was it smelled of MOLD and we even saw some in the shower.

This is a solid choice for a NYC hotel, but I expected a bit more from a Hilton to be honest.

Stayed at the Essex House between -- Nov - - Dec. This was a special treat for my boyfriends --th. 
After a very swift and easy transit by cab from JFK we were checked straight in and told we had been upgraded from a Queen to a King room on the -th floor. Great location and very handy for -th Avenue, Times Square and Broadway etc and I would stay there again for sure.

We just stayed at the Fitzpatrick and our entire experience at this hotel was excellent from making our reservation to the time we checked out. The friendly Customer Service is the
best of the best of all the many hotels we have stayed in.
The location is great. A relatively quiet street, close to Grand Central Station. It is an easy walk to Times Square, St Patricks and Roc Center. 
They serve a fantastic Irish breakfast and many other fine foods. The bar tenders are very friendly and are a wealth of information.
Confortable rooms with nice size bath.
This is a great price for value hotel-shop for specials!

Stayed here for five days for a conference. Beautiful location, albeit it's a bit out of the way. Fabulous pool in the bigger building. I stayed in their smaller (and newly acquired) building and was glad -- the other building was nicer, but it was a lot larger and a LOT louder.

I stayed in room ---. THe lock on the door worked about --% of the time. The staff were helpful in getting this resolved, but I had to go back down to the lobby each time to get a newly charged card. The kitchen area was very nice, aluminum fridge, nice countertops, but the furniture in the sitting area was beat up. Also for the most part the room was clean, but the bathroom needed some deep cleaning. They had a great shuttle service with dropoffs for shopping and for all the local hospitals. If I were a patient or a patient's family, I would find it to be a good value and very friendly to thier needs.

I stayed in this boutique-y hotel for the Greenbuild conference week of November --. Very friendly, and I appreciated the daily happy hour at - p.m. You can sit in the chairs by the fire and watch the (rather sketchy) world go by outside the large windows. The Grand Cafe prices were out of my league, although I sprang for some wonderful French onion soup there. Choice of free papers in the morning. The rooms and beds were comfy, and the service was very attentive. Walk to Chinatown, Market Street, cable cars, and Moscone Center.

A couple nights ago me and my girlfriend stayed in this hotel. From the outside the area was a litle shady but not bad. It sarts when we got inside the room. The first thng that i noticed was that there was some sort of drink that had obviously been thrown at the door and not cleaned, after looking closer at the door I realize thatthe door must have been beat in at some point because the door frame appeared to be glued and puttied back in and the bar lock had been replaced, because the old holes were stil there.  The next morning after opening up all the windows at day time, it comes to our attention that there are dried blood splatters all over the room, even the ceiling, as if someone had been shot there because there was also a large portion of the rug had been replaced. The site was absolutely repulsive. Do not stay there. no matter how cheap they are.

My boyfriend and I stayed here on the --rd December and from --th until -th December. The hotel is basic, but clean and staff were friendly. James on the front desk was always happy to chat and recommend different restaurants and places to go in the area. The hotel is a short walk from Union Square and Greenwich Village and close to -th so it is easy to walk up to the Empire State Building and Times Square. There was a Walgreens, Subway and Starbucks very close by and a diner just across the street. Although the hotel did not have en suites, the bathrooms were very clean and neither of us had to wait to use one at any time. The bedrooms were small, but about average by New York standards and also very clean - a door hanger could be left outside your room in the morning if you required a maid. 
The price per night was very reasonable - a lot cheaper than hotels around the Times Square-particularly touristy area. I would definitely recommend staying here, as all the sites of the city are easily accessible and the area is much more relaxed than further uptown.

The room was nice and adequate and they did check us in before we were scheduled to be checked in...however, we did not receive the 'vouchers' necessary for the free accompanying Irish breakfast and did not know at all that we needed vouchers--and this was after calling down to the front desk to ask how it all worked the night before and then asking the waiter in the restaurant in the morning, who told us we could order absolutely anything. Management tried to charge the entire family's breakfast to us and then amended to wanting to charge us for our child's morning meal because it did not have the word 'Irish' in front of it. We were told the waiters are officially not hotel employees and therefore were not able to knowledgeably inform us of the voucher--but this doesn't explain why we didn't receive the vouchers upon check in or why no one said anything when we phoned downstairs to ask the night before. There needs to be better communication & acceptance of responsibility for miscommunication instead of making us feel like we had to argue on principal. Unfortunately, this somewhat soured the visit, esp. for a couple who first became engaged at a guest house beside Phoenix Park in Dublin.

We popped into NYC for one night to see a show. We wanted to be in the Times Square-Theater District. This hotel was a great bargain for the price and centrally located to the other things we wanted to do. We would definitely stay there again.

hotel looked fine in the foyer till you paid for a room. went to check the pool out no water in and absolutely filthy, at night there were all sorts of people on car park fixing bikes and revving car engines didn't feel safe to leave hotel after dark especially being senior citizens. hotel in a run down area of memphis would not recommend it at all. pay that extra ten dollars it will be worth it and find somewhere else

My daughter and i visited this hotel in December ---- over the christmas period.
