We only stayed overnight, but found the hotel to be above average in every way. The room was clean and well-appointed, though the bathroom
is small. There were two up-to-date computers in the lobby for Internet email checking. The staff was pleasant and helpful. The location - near the Speedway Racetrack- was perfect for our family. I
definitely recommend this hotel as a fine place to stay and a good value.

My wife and I stayed at the Hilton Austin in Austin, Texas this week. We were here for a conference. The hotel is very clean and new. Nicely decorated. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The food was delicious. The fitness center and spa were also quite nice for a business hotel. The location is in the heart of downtown Austin and is close to everything.

We booked the hotel through Priceline ($--- per night) and were a little worried after reading the reviews. We checked in early, hoping to request a good room. When we got there the place was pitch black (I'm not kidding). Employees were walking around with lanterns. A utility crew had cut through a power line and the whole block was dark. Knowing that the --th floor (the tower floor) was supposed to house luxury rooms, and since the elevators were out, we volunteered to take a room up there. A manager said no problem. Before we could get to the stairs, the lights came back on. Our room was enormous, with a desk, computer hookups, a big TV, bathrobes, and even an exercise bicycle. On top of that, there is a small cafe on the tower floor- continental breakfast and delicious pre-dinner snacks were included. The staff was friendly and efficient. Everything was clean. The location is tremendous--walked to everything. I guess we got lucky!

A very nice surprise to find a clean, affordable and simple hotel..that has the kindest employees in downtown Phoenix......close to university, museums, etc. 
Found this place online, and stayed over a week at this location in Phoenix,and frankly the hotel was well maintained, and clearly in transition from old mode..to plans of new.....rennovations. The staff....Walt and Joe were helpful daily, well informed and knowledgeable of local restaurants, bus service, and great out of the way places to eat...Authentic, and straight forward staff.....Location was excellent to rail, bus, restaurants, theatre, and museums without the go home broke price tag.
Breakfast was limited, basic..so hopefully this will change. However, I recommend the place, and certainly will return.......

This is is a trendy, and cheap during the off season hotel at a great location in Chicago. It isn't as nice as Palomar LA-Westwood, which is one of my favorites in the LA area, however the rooms were big and comfortable, as were the beds. They have a nice deck area upstairs and an indoor pool as well.

I have stayed at the Renaissance three times now, each trip during the Presidents week holiday. While it is the off-season, the city and particularly the Inner Harbor still retains all of its charm. I discovered the Renaissance by a freind's request when I first went down a few years ago for a quick escape from New York. Since then, I have decided to do that same february --day getaway twice and the Renaissance never fails to impress. 
First and foremost, it's location is undoubtedly unbeatable. There are numerous hotels along the Inner Harbor, however, this one is most ideally situted right at the harbor's northwestern apex. It features a skybridge direcly into the Harborplace - hence the name - which is a great collection of local and brand name stores, exquisite restaurants and remarkable views as well as two private entrances into the adjacent Gallery Mall. Wheather you are a shopper or not, if ever it rains or snows, or there is any reason at all to stay in, both the Gallery and the Harborplace offer a myriad of restaurants, shops, fountains, etc. The hotel is equadistant to the Aquarium, Maryland Science Center, Camden Yards, Federal Hill and beyond. 
Equally impressive - as always - are the rooms-service. I happened to get the same room i had two years ago, just one floor higher, ----- as opposed to -----. Despite a lofty $--- a night in the off season, the views, especially from such high floors, are incredible. With the naked eye you can see traffic on I -- in the distance, the Francis Key Bridge, Federal Hill, the Habrorplace, the Power Plant (see below), and Camden Yards. As for service, the staff is very reputable and accomodating. I found upon entering my room on Sunday that there was no alarm clock, or any clock at all in the room. Nor were there any binoculars next to the little sign stating that the room featured binoculars. I went to the front desk and recieved binoculars, and the clock came up within -- minutes. I do believe that the most accomodating, friendliest, simply most hospitable staff member i have EVER encountered in my travels is Margaret. Though I am not quite sure what her position is, should you chose to dine in the Fells Point room on the -th floor, she will be the older woman with a slight southern accent seating you. She also seems to be the manager because while not escorting patrons to their seats she is negotiating with waiters, calling the kitchen to request another dish, etc. If there is anything you find out of order or a dish in the buffet that you want or that there is no more of, she will personally call not only the kitchen, but the lobby lounge and any other location in the hotel where food inventory might be found and make sure it is delivered to the table. 
Renovation: In order to keep a trully pleasant atmosphere during the summer season - when this hotel gets booked solid and my $--- room starts at $--- - renovations are done during the off season. I, fortunately, was staying on a sunday (no construction work), then Presidents Day (holiday) and so only on my check-out day, Tuesday, did I hear noise. Yes, there was quite alot of noise around the pool-courtyard area but it comes with the territory of staying at such a high-demand property in the middle of winter.
Reccomendations: 
Power Plant - The Power Plant --- years ago was a real, working power plant on the Inner Harbor. -- years ago it was a crude and delapitating sight, or so I hear. In ---- it was revamped and while maintaining all orignal detail, it now houses an ESPN Zone, Hard Rock Cafe and in my opinion, the coolest Barnes and Noble Bookstore on Earth. Walk into that B&N and there before you are the original smokestacks rising - floors above you! Bookshelves wrap around these massive pillars and you can even walk under them and look up through them! Truely fascinating
Little Italy - My first time here, just walk across the canal bridges near the Power Plant-Aquarium and you're there. I ate at Delesio's, a little Itialian trattoria just - blocks from the Inner Harbor and a -- minute walk from the hotel. Amazing Gnocci!
All in all, while Baltimore does not strike the average vacationer as a great getaway, with the help of the Renaissance it truely is. For me it is a comfort destination, an always-there possibility. I didnt feel like really planning anything this week, and I woke up not even sure if I was going to go anywhere. I made up my mind, got on a late afternoon amtrak and was in the pool by -:-- that night. Before de-boarding I knew exactly where I would stay, eat and sightsee. The Renaissance always helps to complete my sort-of annual (about every --- years)Baltimore escape.

Nearly brand new hotel. Clean, modern decor. Nice pool. Only had breakfast there, which was ok, nothing spectacular, but prices were reasonable. There is a Jimmy Johns-pizza place-McDonalds in walking distance. I forgot my iHome in the room, and the staff were extremely helpful and gracious in packing it up and sending it to me thru UPS. Only thing I didn't like was the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""door"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to the bathroom. It resembles a barn door that slides, and unfortunately it slid open..while I was using the bathroom! Strange decor choice..

I flew into Indianapolis one day early and needed a place to stay. A friend recommended this hotel. I had never stayed at a La Quinta before but decided since the price was so reasonable it was worth a try.
I found the room to be comfortable and clean and the staff very friendly. The hotel is right by the highway so I could hear the traffic but, again, for the price I paid I'm not complaining.
The fridge and microwave were a definite plus.
The breakfast was simple and did the trick and the free wi-fi was very much appreciated.
In fact when I got to my other hotel, I kept commenting on how I was paying three times as much for my room but still had to pay for breakfast and wi-fi.
Would recommend this hotel chain to anyone looking for a no-frills, good value hotel.

I was booking my hotel a little late, a week before my Event. The Host Hotel was 'The Sheraton'(Big Box Hotel Chain). As a result, I wasn’t getting a good price on the room, and I decided to shop. I usually skeptical of lower priced hotels that are not “Name Brand”, but I decided to try Hotel Indigo. I actually was able to book my whole trip including air-hotel for less than it would have cost to stay at the host hotel.
I must say I am delighted I was willing to try something new. The hotel has a stylish boutique design and feel, and the room was very cozy.
Not to mention that the feel was different than any other hotel stay that I have ever had because of the Night Manager –Trina- that checked me, and did whatever she could to make my stay the best. Now you may just think she was doing her job, but I felt as a hotel guest that she went the extra mile, and even made me feel like I was a local business that really appreciated my business. As a result she remembered my name, and kindly would inquire how my meetings for day were going, and if there was anything she could help me with. I know people say we are in a recession, but I believe we are in a period of weeding out, and survival of the fittest in our economy- It are businesses like the Hotel Indigo, that will build a reputation for being the best small and service oriented hotels, that will be in business and going strong for years to come as a result of taking care of their customers.
Side Note- as I left the conference on Sunday, I couldn’t help but notice the long lines of people that stood impatiently waiting to check-out and check-in at the host hotel – The Sheraton, and all I could do was laugh since I not only stayed at a better hotel- but It was by far best VALUE. 
If I ever have a conference again or know of someone coming to Dallas for business, and they want the best service, and best value to choose Hotel Indigo- and support the businesses that spur this economy!
If you decide to stay there as a result of this review...Be sure to tell 
Trina, the Night Manager---That Mr. Lee reommended you stay there!

We visited The US Grant for a few days in august during a business trip. While the overall hotel is up to - star standards; (turn down service, room amenites, decor,) The poorly lit and narrow hallways made the hotel feel as if it was still the turn of century at the time it was built. Even during the daytime the atmosphere seemed subdued. No loud noise to complain of and the room service and hotel cleanliness was impeccable. However I disregarded earlier posts regarding the surrounding area, while very accessible to the gaslamp district, the amount of homeless people around the hotel was staggering. There needs to be a medical clinic and shelter in the area in order to accommodate the homeless needs in that area.

this was the worst hotel I've ever stayed at, the televisions don't work, I called three times and eventually had to go to the front desk where I still WAS NOT HELPED. Besides the location there is nothing good about this place, the elevators are VERY slow there apparently are no stairs, and the rooms don't have anything useful in them. My boyfriend spent alot of money for our stay and we could not enjoy ourselves because of how horrible the hotel was. I'm shocked people actually stay here.

Night Hotel is in a great location half a block away from Times Square - yet it is relatively peaceful. The interior design is good - dark and brooding, with a fabulous lobby and a black-white color scheme running throughout the property. Staff were friendly, helpful and accommodating - offering advice and tips on what to see in NYC and when. My room - a King room - was small (to be expected in NYC) but well maintained - but overall it was pretty good value for the location. The only drawbacks are: the entire hotel is very dark (as the name would suggest) - which is fabulous from a design point of view but not so good from a more practical perspective. Also, the hotel bar does not open on Sundays - probably pretty normal from a local's perspective, but irritating for a tourist. The alternative is a charmless Irish bar over the road... Having said that, when it is open, the food is tasty and the service good.

Stayed at this Hotel in May. Have been to NY a few times now and have done the obvious Tourist sites, so decided to stay in Tribeca-Soho area of Manhattan and was not disappointed. The hotel was great for our long weekend break and well placed for all the sites-shops and restaurants in the area. -mins walk took us to Broadway(downtown) where the shopping is flabby. Restaurants were great from great diners for breakfast to Nobu for some fantastic sushi. Hotel had a great little restaurant great for breakfast and a little pantry where there were a few vending machines to buy some snacks, toiletries etc that you might want. Edwin the concierge was brilliant, so helpful and always smiling - great asset to the hotel. Next time I am in NY I will certainly be staying at this hotel. Last point, Subway right outside hotel taking you all over Manhattan, so you can see all the Tourist Sites if you've not been to NY before

We came to Philly to visit family who live nearby and found the hotel to be the perfect location for us. There was very easy access for pick up and drop off after all our activities. The views were amazing and we enjoyed watching both the river and the city skyline from our corner room. BTW we think the Philly skyline is one of the prettiest anywhere. The bed was comfy with plenty of soft pillows just like i love. The room decor is very nice and relaxing and we enjoyed the turn down service as well. However, why is there no fan in the bathroom? We saw many many places with no bathroom fan. Talk about steamy! Although we would have enjoyed the fitness room and pool, we simply had no time. It was great to have a mini-fridge and a safe in the room, but of course that is expected anymore. We were only able to take in the free breakfast one of the mornings, but it was very very good. Service at the hotel and at the restaurant were excellent.

While I was surprised to see how small - double beds look in a room (been a while since I haven't been able to get my room of choice with a King), but there was plenty of space, all I needed for business travel. Service was good throughout the hotel.

Ok so let's be clear, staying in New York is never going to be the cheapest thing you ever do, but when you stay in a hotel that's so impressive you forget how expensive it was, you're onto a very good thing. In this case, that impressive hotel is most definitely the Trump Soho.
Situated on the edge of Soho, New York's coolest place, filled with everything from designer stores to neighbourhood pizza parlours (Ben's Pizza on the corner of Spring and Thompson is thoroughly recommended - just don't think you can share a --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" pizza between two, because it really can't be done!!) , Trump Soho is in a great location.
The whole place is so beautifully and tastefully decorated that if I was rich enough, I'd like someone to do my house up just like it - bronze metallic leather wingback chairs and huge sculptural chandeliers in the lobby, leather walls and block wood panelling in the corridors and lifts, super comfy armchairs, gorgeous bathroom tiling and oversized button-down headboard in the guest suites. Our room also featured what looked like a --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" TV, with an all-in-one remote that controlled the electric curtains (oh yes!), the room temperature and lighting - genius. The bathroom, which had a separate bath alongside the super duper shower, also gave us two sinks - vanity units, which when you have two girls sharing, makes all the difference! 
There were lots of nice little touches in the room, including a very handy little kitchenette type area (with a fridge, microwave and sink), a wardrobe which lit up when you opened the door, a total of three phones (one next to the bed, one on the TV - desk unit, and one in the bathroom), plenty of notepaper and pens, a bench - ottoman at the end of the bed, and lots of useful guest information, such as the pillow menu on offer, which naturally we took full advantage of! One of the most impressive extras were the bathrobes on offer, which were just fabulous!! I often find that towels and robes in American hotels really aren't big enough for anyone over a size -- to use comfortably, but the Trump Soho totally confounded my previous experiences, as the robe and bath towels were all plenty big enough, and I just regret that I didn't purchase a robe to take home with me - maybe next time.
The reception, concierge, bellboy and housekeeping staff were all really helpful, friendly and professional - particular thanks must go to Roger, our check-in receptionist, who very kindly managed to wangle us a corner room, and Mike, our favourite bellboy - and our one negative experience with service (a rather embarrassing and uncomfortable incident at the pool area and bar) was very quickly rectified at main reception when checking out. 
No doubt about it, Mr Trump knows what he's doing when it comes to creating a hotel experience to remember in New York, I was massively impressed by the Trump Soho, and wouldn't hesitate in recommending it.

While we are not too impressed with our first visit to Texas, the hotel certainly offset the negative of the heat and bad drivers. The location is set back a little, which was very nice. It was not too busy and so close to the highway and --- turn around. The hotel is very welcoming. There is plenty of free parking and we noticed a rope-type of barricaded basketball area with special flooring on the side of the building where the indoor pool is. The lobby was very nice. The staff greets you immediately with a very pleasant tone. Everything is clean so far! Slightly different and unique decor than other hotels where they have high stools at a counter for people to watch the large screen tv, eat, talk, etc., in addition to the regular chairs, tables, couch, etc. We were unexpectedly very early, but hoped we could check in early if our room was ready. Thankfully, it was ready! All along the way up to and including our room was clean. I found the bed to be a little odd. I can't explain it, but the mattress was......different. The pillows were great! Still slept well. The only negative in our room and in the lobby were some furniture that needed to be reupholstered, because the furniture is clean and in perfectly working condition. Normal wear and tear just needs to be replaced. We went to do some shopping for our kitchenette and when we returned we discovered how good the mid week social hour is. Free beverages including wine and beer along with food. The staff is incredibly accommodating. We were going to be in our room quite a bit during the days so we did not have maid service on any of the days, but I did see them frequently as I replenished my room with supplies, gave them trash, etc. They were very nice and accommodating, as well. Katherine and Robert M at the front desk were incredibly nice and went above and beyond expectations. The FREE breakfast offered a large variety of items from eating very healthy to not so healthy. Completely your choice!! Waffles, eggs, fruit, bacon or sausage (depends on the day), biscuits and gravy, juices, salsa, sour cream, cereal, etc. All together, it was an extremely great stay and would definitely go back. I would have rated this hotel a - if it wasn't for some of the furniture that needs attention. I would have rated it - --- if I was allowed to!!

I loved my stay!!! We have just returned from our - night stay in the Comfort Inn-I was apprenhensive about our choice of hotel after reading the reviews-yet we all look for different things! I chose it for location, the relaxed style and the breakfast. We had a very comfy room, clean linen, towels replaced daily and plenty of them. Plenty of hot water for bath and shower. Tea and coffee facilities in the lobby- Breakfast was fine-I didn't want to be looking for somewhere to eat first thing in the morning-donuts, waffles cereals,toast, muffins plenty to set you on your way. Brendans is excellent for a meal -quite a transformation from the breakfast area in the morning. No trouble with noise(I had packed ear plugs just incase!!!) Take on board the age of the building and the fact you are there mainly to sleep! Computer in the lobby-very handy The Grays hop on hop off bus is a 'yes' Fabulous views from the Rockefleller Centre.

Served up right. Pleasant staff, great transportation availability, clean comfortable rooms.
Stayed at club level which provide nice views, snacks etc. 
Enjoyed our stay and would stay there again. Couldn't ask for more.

My family & I spent - nights at this hotel. The location is great & the staff very helpful, but this is a very old hotel that's been refurbished very poorly & it shows if you know where to look (lots of mildew in the sink, around the tub, etc.)
My wife and daugher shared one of the - double beds in our room and by the middle of the second day, we noticed that their arms and legs were covered in bedbug bites. I tore the bed apart & found several bedbugs between the mattress and boxspring.

Had to spend - nights in Jacksonville for business. I like Omni's very much. I did have a few small gripes which may seem petty, but not to me.

The real issue I had was with the shower. The water was warm, but I couldn't get it hot. Who doesn't want a hot shower? And more importantly, the shower liner was really mildewy and smelled terrible. Not quite the optimal shower experience.
On the positive side, front desk people were incredibly helpful and friendly, the rooms were clean and spacious, and the internet free if you are an Omni member.
Not bad, but not great.
Dirty sheets and bathroom. If you are going to have white furnishings, dust once in a while. Dark halls and the renovations are not complete. Understaffed.

The first thing I would say about this hotel is that the lobby and the look of it is beautiful ad feel of Southern charm and elegant beauty. When the lobby is not crowded and full of people waiting for the ducks to make an appearance, it is elegant. The service from and at the bar was excellent. I loved the spa and my daughter and I used the gym daily and had a great massage and treatment at the spa and loved it. The gym is adequate for some cardio and a few weights, but nothing spectacular.
The rooms were nicely decorated and the beds were comfortable.
this being said, I have to say that I will never go back: The bathrooms are unacceptable. When we asked for a small table, they said they couldn't find one and that only the rooms in the concierge level had larger bathrooms. I felt like I was camping!
Unless the rooms have been renovated since my visit last year, I would highly recommend another hotel with better bathroom facilities and just go to the Peabody for the duck walk and an drink.

Great hotel, cute spacious rooms, la'occitane soaps. Loved it. And i'm probably the most spoiled woman in the world.

The staff is very friendly (the desk attendant gave treats to our dog) and helpful. The morning breakfast (rolls-bagels-fruit-hardboiled eggs) is palatable and filling. There are nice touches like afternoon cookies and round the clock coffee. 
In summary, one could pay double or triple the amount to stay in a hotel with superfine linens, marble baths, etc and then get hit with parking-gym extras, but this hotel is very reasonable. The location and the staff makes this hotel one of those special finds. I didnt even want to write this review because I didnt want the hotel to get more crowded, but my wife forced me too....

I stayed at the Jacksonville Hyatt for one night for business, and it was just what you'd expect from an older, large Hyatt Regency property. Everything was perfectly adequate, but nothing was stellar. My favorite things about the hotel were the bed, which was quite comfortable, and the staff, who were all extremely friendly and helpful.

Tough to walk from here anywhere but is a short car ride to lots of places. Two young guys came in at - a.m. and created lots of noise for an hour but the street noise wasn't bad once we were inside. Bed was comfortable and the refrigerator worked fine. Nothing fancy but a good price.

The only downside we can think of is that the bathroom was a bit on the small side ..... but it was more than adequate..

Loved It! The room had lots of space and the beds and pillows were fantastic. I only wish they had extra pillows or more than - pillows on a queen size bed. The shower was large and the bathroom is divided so more than one person can be getting ready at a time. The staff was always friendly and helpful. It was a great experience and I can't imagine staying anywhere else in the Phoenix area!!

I can't say enough about this place to explain the level of hospiltality and quality of what they offer. This was our second visit to the hotel. The staff for the most part were all very efficient and friendly. The restaurant both inside and out was pleasant with an excellent breakfast buffet. The bar needs more space to accommodate busy times and is not user friendly.
There are NO seating areas in the lobby. The rooms are becoming shabby, ours was an upgraded one and not up to Fairmont standards The location is fairly close to the shops of Georgetown

This is a great place to stay away from the hussle of Midtown and Times Square.
Rooms are clean, large by NY standards and very comfortable.
We only had a drink in the bar once, but we were greeted by a rather sarcasitc waiter and for that reason decided not to bother again. 
The larder in the lobby was excellent for picking up a snack late at night.
Ideal for the subway to other parts of NY and great shopping a -----min walk.

What a great location. Just north of Tribeca and at the start of SoHo, this new hotel is exactly where my wife and I wanted to spend our couples get away in NYC. We had a good size room that was very clean and faced north looking right at the empire state building. We couldn’t have asked for a pretty view at night with the lights of NYC twinkling. The bed was so comfortable my wife wanted to buy one to bring home. Thank goodness we took the train down. We splurged a bit and got a club level room. This was definitely worth it, not only because of the freebies they hand out but because the club lounge has the best view in the whole hotel up on the --st floor with a huge patio with a --- degree view of new york. 
Everyone on the staff was friendly and helpful. The bell man even suggested a great breakfast place called Bubbies a few blocks away. The hotel is right around the corner from a bunch of great restaurants in Greenwich Village and SoHo. The place we ate at on Friday night was perhaps one of the best we have ever been to anywhere. The place was called David Burkes Kitchen. I knew the name from Top Chef but was still impressed by what was served. I will definitely return to the Sheraton Tribeca hotel and am already planning my next trip.

We got this at a AAA rate of $--.-- ($--.-- with tax). It's a ways from downtown, and not by any good dinner restaurants (have to drive a couple exits up I---). The room itself was good size, and so was the bathroom. The bathroom had good counter space and a nice shower, but some of the towels were a bit tattered. We found it to be nice and quiet. 
The breakfast was good. Although we didn't eat the waffles, eggs, ham and hashbrowns, it was nice that they offered hot items. We really liked the whole grain bagels and yogurt. 
I'd give this hotel a solid B if you're looking for just a place to rest your head, or don't mind driving to get places. We had driven all day to get there, so we just didn't like getting back in the car to get to dinner.

This inn offers guests a fabulous location, near shops, restaurants, and the subway, and yet it is also tucked into a residential area far enough so that there is more quiet and a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""local"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" feel to be had. For the relatively hefty price tag of this room each night, the substantial size of the room, with its kitchenette and separate sitting area, and the attractiveness of the main amenities seem to be at the expected, higher-end of the spectrum, but there were some exceptions, which I'll note below:
- Desk in the sitting area has hard plastic chairs accompanying it --- think stiff plastic lawn chairs and you will be thinking of more comfortable seating than these chairs. If you intend to do significant amounts of work during your stay, perhaps the inn's office will loan you one of its padded chairs instead. I did like the way that I could use their printer for free as I was doing my work, though. That part was a nice touch for the working guest. 
- The linens are said to be high-thread-count and luxurious, but they did not feel this way to me and my partner. They felt rough and scratchy, unlike better-quality bedding I have experienced at other hotels in the same price point and even less. As other guests have noted, the beds seem to be far more firm and uncomfortable than I have gotten used to at other hotels. 
- The bathroom is not very comfortable. Some other reviewers a few years ago wrote about the lack of counter space and shelf space, and a manager replied that this issue was going to be fixed. In the room I occupied, there were small shelves added to the walls, but these were not really helping out with the problematic lack of counter space. In fact, the small metal shelf in the shower was tilted downward on the wall to the extent that not much could even sit on it without the contents of the shelf (i.e., soap, shampoo, etc.) sliding off onto the floor time and again. 
- Strange that there was a lack of well located electrical outlets in the room. One would think a modern inn would try to meet the power needs of their guests. There were many outlets available, but they were just not by the chairs and desk where you would expect them. 
- The carpet could have been cleaned and-or replaced in the room I occupied. Ugly traffic-related stains were apparent throughout the sitting room. 
Some guests have commented negatively on the continental breakfast and coffee at this inn, but I think this part was just fine. One doesn't expect much else in this type of inn, and what they did offer in regard to the coffee-espresso machine was satisfactory --- for me at least. 
So, with all this said, would I stay here again? I think my partner's comment says it all: """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I don't know if I would choose it first if I needed a place to stay in Boston again, but it wasn't bad. It wasn't unpleasant."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" If you want a good, solid room with attractive furniture (except for the desk chairs), no insect issues, decent but could-be-improved amenities, and you can pay a higher price for accommodations to be in a fabulous location, then you'll like this Inn as a second or third choice, if not your first.

My Fiancee and I stayed here for - nights while visiting San Francisco and I am so glad we did. It was a typical W Hotel, swanky but clean with a fun atmosphere. The location was great, walking distance from pretty much everything! I would recommend to anyone staying in the area.

This is a fantastic hotel. It's small and welcoming and the staff is outstanding. The location couldn't be better -- you are right next to Times Square but on --rd Street so you don't have the noise. It's exciting for everyone, yet not overwhelming for older adults (we traveled with our parents and our teenagers). The -nd floor dining-relaxing area is excellent. There is breakfast in the morning, wine & cheese in the evening, and drinks and snacks all day. We loved that we could let our teenagers sleep late while we got up early and had breakfast. It was also nice for our older relatives to take a break & read the paper or watch TV without having to go back to their room. The rooms are typical New York City sized (not large) but clean and comfortable. The staff is attentive and knowledgable. The Casablanca has a great relaxing vibe . . . until you take a few steps outside the door and find yourself in the most exciting area of New York City. Fun, fun, fun!!!

We booked a room at the Blackstone to go to Printer's Row. It was a perfect location- we could walk there. It was the nicest hotel we have ever stayed at in Chicago. The lobby was beautifully decorated! They had a deli-restaurant on the first floor with very good food for reasonable prices.
The room was newly renovated in a contemporary theme with a grand flair.
We've stayed in a lot of places in the Chicago area and this is one of the top - in our opinion.
Check it out if you need to be in the South Loop area. You won't be disappointed!

For the price and location, this is an outstanding value. The staff was extremely helpful, friendly and professional. I will most definitely be using this facility again on my next trip to San Francisco.

Good mid-town location and spacious rooms make this place good value by Manhattan standards. Only con was the noise coming up from --th street below our apartment in the small hours - if you want quiet at night, ask for rooms away from the street.

The hotel is well located and comfortable, but thestandard rooms are on the small side.
However, I amended my booking to arrive earlier than planned, sent - emails well prior to the cancellation period stipulated to confirm that my original booking had been cancelled, phoned to confirm same, and yet then they charged me a no show fee !!!
Now they are refusing to refund the no show fee, saying they have no record of a cancellation despite my providing evidence of a reply from them to one of my emails requesting confirmation of the cancellation !!!
Dealing with Park South over this matter is akin to dealing with a bureaucracy in ----'s Soviet Russia, they either do not reply tp phone calls-emails or give the most inane reasons for their actions. My experience with entities that are reluctant to refund legitimate monies claimed is that they are probably about to go broke.

I stayed in May. I was in town for a job interview. the price was excellent for value, received and the location, next to Japantown, was convenient. The hotel was a bit 'echo-y' in the halls, and the rooms often had doors between them, but I had no trouble sleeping. And , again, for the price it was great.

I have stayed at the Kabubi Hotel (Used to be called Miyako) many times. I can not rate it anything but a great place to stay and relax. The service is great and every one is extremely friendly and competent. The rates are reasonable and the rooms extremely clean and quiet. I always try and plan my trips far enough in advance so I am able to stay there. I can not recommend it enough.
Frank Butterfield

In a nutshell I tried to get a - star hotel from Priceline.com but ended up with this place. Paid $--- per night. Unsure I went to the web site and it appeared very nice and thought we got a great deal...until we got there. When we finally found it I thought it would be ok. There were lots of bungalows in groups and they appeared to be nice. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lobby"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was a separate building and it was clean and beautiful. Staff manning the desk was nice but seemed to talk down to you like it was an honor for you to be in the same room as them. $-- parking fee way too much. When we got to our bungalow we went inside and noticed the floors were not clean. Floor was made of a some kind of wood-tile and needed a was badly. There was a rug runner in the center of the room and it was dirty. There were spider webs occupied with their residents. Cob webs in the corners. Knobs missing from the AC unit. There was algae growing in the ring at the base of the sink. The two queen beds were newer and were comfortable to sleep in...Thank Goodness. There was a small refrigerator in a cabinet that had a door that was barely holding on to its hinge. The bathroom door was a sliding door that came out of the wall and was old and the paint was all scratched. When you turned on the light switch to the bathroom the sound was so loud and hummed like an Apache helicopter..no joke. The dust in the fan was disgusting and was very thick. We had dinner at the restaurant. Food was average at best and prices were through the roof. The pool was warm and the hot tub was warmer. We didn't go in either one because they needed to be cleaned and by -pm there still were not clean. I cannot recommend this place to anyone. Quite a shame really because the potential was there. The grounds are taken care of but not the sleeping quarters. One good thing...you are just over a small bridge from Sea World. Overall, it was a glorified campground and even though we paid half price we felt ripped off and priceline lost a customer.

I've stayed here three times over the last five months and after the last stay, I'm not sure I'd return. There is no doubt Hotel Valencia is at a perfect location with great shopping and food. The rooms are big and nice. Everything is clean and orderly although the armchair in the room shows some age. There are some nice features in the room such as the cool radio. The bed is really comfortable. You can park your car in a nearby garage for free. 
As a business traveler, however, there are a few things sorely missing. First, the internet is outrageously slow. There is no safe to put away any valuables and I always end up lugging everything around. There are very few electrical outlets, definitely not close to the desk if you want to or need to work. One time I checked in late at night and the TV didn't work. To their credit, they moved me into a giant suite. 
Customer service could also be improved. For my last stay, through no fault of the hotel, my corporate travel agent split my stay into two consecutive reservations. At check-in, they told me there was no way they could link my two reservations so i only have to check out once at the end of my stay. At any other hotel, they would have been able to link my two reservations. In addition, no one told me that the parking garage implemented new rules and that we were not supposed to park on the main floor. Every morning during my last stay, I found my car """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""locked"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" behind chains. Since the whole floor was behind chains, I thought it was some special arrangement the garage had for the morning, only to find out on Day - that the hotel was supposed to have told us not to park overnight on the main level.
I think it'd be a really fun place to stay for pleasure but it's not exactly ideal for a business stay.

For our second stay in San Francisco, we chose this hotel based on its location. It's a perfect base for exploring this wonderful city. Excellent transport links close by with Chinatown and The Embarcadero within easy walking distance. 
We were given an interior room in the historic building which turned out to be a blessing as you could barely hear the noise outside. 
The room itself was on the small side but we only needed somewhere to crash after a busy day sightseeing. There were a couple of issues with the aircon not working and a blocked toilet but these were fixed as soon as they were reported. The TV's reception was a bit dodgy on some channels but we didn't report this so I don't know if this was a general problem or not. The room was kept very clean and I didn't notice any dirt whatsoever. 
A very nice touch was the complimentary snack bag given to us shortly after checking in.
Definitely make use of The Daily Grill at least once for breakfast, especially if you're given the free vouchers.
Overall, a great stay and I'd stay there again if I return to SF.

The hotel was well kept, decorated in a much earlier style (definitely has an old fashion feel) with the large chandeliers and heavy use of wall papers. Beautiful place. I ate breakfast in the restaurant twice, food was good, kind of standard fare for a hotel breakfast, nothing to brag about. Service was good. I found the hotel staff to be friendly. Overall good experience, I think I might choose a slightly smaller hotel next time. I spent two nights here and then three nights at the Topaz hotel and while the Topaz wasn't as fancy I preferred staying there. 
I found the pillows to be uncomfortable but I'm sure if I really cared enough I could have asked for a different set of pillows. Overall, nice hotel, excellent staff.

Plus points: Checkin was quick and friendly. Hot towel at the checkin counter a nice touch. Room is a nice size, all amenities very good. Bathroom is nice - I actually like the 'wet' area for the bath + shower. Toiletries etc. are own brand but seem pretty good. The hotel is also in a good location suitable for business or pleasure - near the loop and Michigan avenue. Having the kitchenette in the room is good too (but read the negative) - housekeeping washed up the cup-saucer-bowl-measuring-cup I left out. They also supply an electric kettle as well as the nespresso machine.
Negative points: housekeeping is a bit random, on the one evening I was in the room they came round to do the turndown service at about -pm. It would be better if they could ask for a preferred time and schedule to those times.
Also I bought some milk+cereal to have a simple breakfast in the room. Housekeeping disposed of the milk on my second to last night. Maybe I left it out, but it would have been nice to have a note at the very least about why they removed it. The fridge is also full of the usual overpriced minibar junk. I'd recommend making a specific point of confirming with housekeeping they aren't going to throw anything away. Also a point for our UK visitors - no teapot or coffee jug, but you can use the measuring cup.
Compared with the Peninsula and the - Seasons it's close but not quite as good.
-- Harry

We stayed for a weekend here after getting a great deal on Hotwire. Best thing about this hotel is the location! The room was clean, Durty Nelly's Pub downstairs, right outside awesome restaurants and shopping. The room positves: clean, mini fridge, Peter Thomas Roth toiletries, balcony, elevator system is neat, ice on every floor, room service until - am, pay per view movies and HBO. Didn't like no vent in bathroom, shower took long to drain, pillows were bleh, noice due to construction on upper floor, and you can hear peopl in hallway....like the drunk girl at - am yelling wooo-hooo. We layed out at the pool one day and while it was small they did have a set up where you could order beer, margaritas, and snacks while laying out. Got crowded but we were happy we had chairs and is summer after all. Overall, this place is decent and fine for a weekend getaway! We traveled as a couple with no kids so this suited us. We were there for fun not a luxurious spa hotel.

The hotel looks cool from the outside as well as the mod-looking lobby and restrooms (although I feel bad for anyone who is intoxicated that tries to use the lobby bathroom as it is incredibly dark). As soon s you check in, the hotel goes WAY down hill, starting with their customer service.
Prior to the stay, the person who booked the rooms for us received cancellation emails, even though we had not canceled. We were strictly told to arrive at -pm to check-in; we arrived at -:--pm and waited more than an hour for our rooms to be ready - and each time we checked the status of our room we received dirty looks from the receptionist. They did not offer us a drink, or anything to compensate for our long wait. Once we finally got to our rooms I was not impressed. The beds are literally inches off the floor, I found a dirty tissues on the floor, the walls were cracked and chunks were taken out, the shower had tiles that were cracked and dirty shower curtains. On the last day we all received random wake-up calls early in the morning for no reason as we hadn't asked for one.
In addition, the valet driver broke my colleague's car door and he was given the run around in regards to when the valet company's manager would be in - needless to same he filed a claim and is trying to resolve it.
Hotels and restaurants are all about customer service, this place clearly did not have that, and it was also a dump to stay in. I think I will stay at the Holiday Inn next time.

We stayed in this hotel for four nights and it offered everything we needed. To be honest, there is so much to do and see in NYC that all we did in our room was sleep and shower. Room was small but it was very clean and comfortable. Had a shower with a small bath tub that you could fill up and sit in which worked perfectly well if a little unusual. We were on the ground floor close to reception and the bar but room was very quiet. Free wifi was a bonus. 
Hotel is right next to the --- subway stop on the - line which is really convenient and there's a -- hour supermarket a couple of doors away and loads of nice cafes for breakfast. Short stroll to Central Park. 
From everyone we've spoken to we can't imagine getting a better deal in New York. We would definitely go back and highly recommend.

I have just returned from The Wellington Hotel and what can i saw.... The perfect location. Although i have to say the rooms are not the best, they were clean and served a purpose. We stayed from Saturday --nd October for - nights, we were on --th floor with our room overlooking Central Park. We didn't have air conditioning which was fine for when we were there as the weather was nice but not too hot, we just opened the window, air con would have been required if it was any hotter. The room itself did need some maintenance such as plug sockets was coming away from the wall and the light in the bathroom was a little too close to the shower for my liking but in the grand scheme of things, does that really matter?
We had breakfast included which was good. There was enough choice and most of the staff were very friendly. There was occasionally a queue for breakfast depending what time you get there but it didn't take long to get seated. 
The reception staff were friendly.... and the men at the doors were helpful.
The location.... Was in the best place it could have been, could of streets from -th Ave, as you come out of the main door at the hotel Time Square is just down the street and in clear view with Central Park only a couple of blocks the other way.
All in all i would reccommend this hotel, providing you are not very fussy.

I stayed at this hotel on a business trip twice in one week. After a long flight from Toronto it was nice to be quickly checked in by friendly staff. From the outside the hotel looks a bit drab. The lobby was ordinary with seating for those waiting for the shuttle to the airport. The hallways looked worn as did the rooms in a way. It seems they are gradually upgrading but it does require a facelift. 
The room with king size bed seemed narrow but was fine. There was a fridge (microwave would have been nice) but no LCD TV (yet). The room and bathroom were clean and everything including WiFi was functional. Although in both rooms I was in the water temperature fluctuated by quite a bit while showering… at - am anyway. When I advised the front desk I was told that no one has complained since they upgraded their hot water system. On the subject of shower there is a dispenser for shampoo, conditioner and liquid soap instead of small bottles.
Although I was concerned about outside noise, I did find the room quiet (top floor). The heating unit was not noisy at all in the first room but in the second one I had to adjust the cover to stop the rattling. The bed and pillows were comfortable and I had a great sleep.
Breakfast was the usual items which was fine. I appreciated that it opened at -am to cater to those who have early flights. There is a restaurant onsite but I did not try the food there as there are several restaurants around that the shuttle drivers (who are great as mentioned) are happy to drive you to. The Emerald Thai was quite good.
There is a small business centre with pc’s and a printer; handy for printing out boarding passes.
Overall I thought the hotel offers good value for the price and I would return. Hopefully they’ll have flat screen TV’s and the water temperature control resolved.

I loved the location. This hotel is located in the perfect place. It is one block from the mall and close to countless places to eat, party, and shop. It is located one block from the trolley service and directly on the bus line. This hotel is the perfect location for someone that has never been to San Diego...everything is right at your fingertips. The hotel is now owned by Wydham and available for timeshare parcipants. The staff was helpul and friendly. The only down side is that they want to sell you more ownership during your visit. Just say """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" if you are not interested. Do not fall for the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""free gift"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" bribes if you are not interested.

its true the reviews i read about this hotel on trip advisor but i thought id give it the benefit of the doubt because the hotel we really wanted to stay in was booked for our time in new york......anyway back to this hotel we needed - rooms we had - people in our family so when we checked in they gave us - rooms on separate floors,when we asked to have rooms next to one another the best they could do was on the same floor but still separated so we took that offer up as it was --pm and we just spent -- hours on a plane and was exhausted.

DONT BOTHER!!!!!!!! GO SOMEWHERE ELSE!!!

The hotel is in a fabulous location - a very short walk to Union Square and right on the tram line to go to fishermans wharf. Chinatown, little Italy all only a short walk away. We didn't have any expectations so were quite impressed actually. There is a convenience shop across the road and a full mini bar and fridge and a coffee machine in every room. The rooms are a little quirky (odd!) but very comfortable and clean. The staff are very helpful. I would definitely recommend this hotel. It is great value for money.

My partner and I stayed here in Feb for four nights and thee hotel surpassed all our expectations. The hotel is immaculate, clean, luxurious and very welcoming.
The staff at the hotel are very professional, yet extremely friendly and we often struck up a bit of conversation with the door men and they were all very funny and friendly.
The location is perfect for being a tourist and Times Sq is just two blocks away which has a great atmosphere at night.
Our room was massive and spacious and we had a view of Hudson River which was great. The bathrooms are modern, clean and the shower was huge with a waterfall shower head - bliss!
If you're visiting the Big Apple, this is definitely the hotel to pick!!!!!

We booked this hotel because we were traveling on a budget. We actually booked the room for $--- a night. We were really nervous when we were pulling up, the area seemed a little shady. However, to our surprise we were staying in the most beautiful hotel. Everything on the interior has been remodeled. Its a very very modern hotel. We had flat screen tvs and the most comfortable bed. we had a delicious breakfast on the roof in the morning. We were about a mile from all the major shops and then we took the bus to fisherman's wharf. I think it was like $- bucks round trip and it took about -- minutes. We walked at night time from the mall and it was a okay but if I did not have my husband I would have felt unsafe. But you cannot beat this hotel. Its spectacular. I was shocked. We only booked one night because we were unsure and we ended up staying g - nights. It was well worth it. I would recommend this for hotel for anyone. Its clean, beautiful and the staff was outstanding. They helped us to get reservations and gave us directions anywhere we needed to go.

perfect location in downtown seattle walking dostance to dining , shopping , pretty much any thing in DT .
 Rooms are very dated , reletively small bathrooms and paper thin walls. could hear when the room next door using their bathroom !
 free Coffe in the lobby early in the morning ( - to - ) was a nice touch.
 If you become a kimpton memebr (its free ) you can use wifi for free . 
for the price paid , I've stayed in better hotels in Seattle . 
 a printed list in the washroon tells you what items you can get for free in the hotel ,that lst include shower cap , toothbrush,.... you'll find a toothbrush in your room too , but if you use it you must pay for it , the list in the washroom refers to the toothbrush you should have asked for from the house keeping not the one already put in your room ! that one you should pay for !

This was the first time that my family and I went to NY. We opted for this hotel mainly because it had free parking (within the hotel). This having been said, we were pleasantly greeted by the parking attendant. The only perk was to leave our keys with the attendant due to possible moving of our car within the indoor parking lot. We didn't really feel comfortable with this, but he reassured us that he would find a spot where he would not have to move our car for the duration of our stay. SInce we were not going to use our car in NY, we retrieved our keys and all was good.
We had a room with - beds (for our kids and for us). The room were very nice rooms, very clean and well decorated. The bathroom was a complet bathroom with tub and it was furnished with complimentary soaps and many clean towels. The bathroom was just as clean and the rest of the room. No complaints there ! 
Our room was located across from the pool. The pool closed at - pm as to not bother any guests. What is wonderful, I thought, about the pool it that it has a roof covering half the pool which my kids loved because they could still go swimming under the covering protection when it rained. There was also a lifeguard present. 
Next to our room, was a mini fitness center and an ice machine. The television was functional and it offered an array channels. The location of the hotel couldn't be better. Across the street it a police station and it is about - minutes from Times Square. We even took advantage of the free security box at the front desk to put our passports and other valuables.
The room service maid was cordial (I believe her name was Isabella or Elizabetha)....she was so respectful and polite, as was the front desk staff. One front desk clerk (I don't remember her name) advised us on places to eat (which btw was great) and places to visit. She helped tremendously !
Ok....ok, so now that I have related all the good stuff......Allow me to share with you my petpeeves.......
I have no idea why the beds sheets are all top sheets. Why they don't have fitted mattress sheets is beyond me. (Mind you, we went to NJ after NY and that hotel had no fitted sheets on the mattresses either !! Go figure!!)
The bed was clean (NO BED BUGS !!) but when you wake up in the morning, the sheets are all over the place and the thought of sleeping on the actual mattress is not very appealing...at least not to me.
The AC worked well, but a bit on the noisy side. When we were there, it rained and the humidity was high. It would have been great to have the option of putting on some heat. After calling the front desk, he advised us that there is no heater, but offered to bring up more blankets and covers. I don't know why this hotel has no heater. Does it not get cold in NY? Maybe this is common in NY hotels.....I don't know, but I didn't like it.
Overall, I would definately go back to the Travel Inn and I recommend it....bring a sweater!!!

Very nice friendly clean hotel with a nice clean room IN A GREAT LOCATION AT A GREAT PRICE. We were so glad we picked this place, and spent the money we saved indulging in great meals, especially at Jaleo and Zatinya. Morning baked goods from Le pain quotidienne around the corner.

There can only be two reasons for anyone to stay at the Midtown Hotel in Boston. One if you are affiliated with the Christian Science Church, it's directly across the street. The other reason is if you are unable to get any other hotel reservation in Boston.
The hotel was charging the same as other major hotels during a meeting in Boston; it wasn't worth half of the rate they charged, and even at that anything other than basic services simply are not available.
Give this place a pass.

Excellent location, my husband is a wheelchair user. Having informed and booked the hotel on the basis it was suitable we were disappointed that there is no access from street for wheelchair user, we had to use a side workers entrance! Restaurant is not accessible as down steps so we were unable to use! We moved rooms three times as first two rooms were not accessible and only had a bath, no roll in shower!.

If you want to touch of European flavor and flair, stay here! My wife and I have traveled in Europe for more than -- years from the Arctic Circle, to Spain, to Greece and points in between staying in hostels, hotels, dumps, and dives, and luxurious too. San Francisco --- September ---- (Holiday Inn Fisherman’s Wharf)
Travelers: Couple (age -- & --) from central coast California
Hotel: Holiday Inn Fisherman’s Wharf
We got a room through Priceline at the Holiday Inn Express in the Beach Building (across the street from the main building and lobby). It was a typical Holiday Inn with dated furnishings, but clean, comfortable FULL size beds (not queens) and a clean bathroom with hot showers ($----night on Priceline for a three star). Street noise was loud at times, with trash and recycling trucks heard at early hours in the streets, as well as normal traffic. A room key was required to access the elevator and a night guard manned a concierge desk after hours, so there was added security. 
Location: Great location to access all of the tourist activities. Super close to the Wharf and an easy walk to North Beach Washington Park and Chinatown. Also, you have quick access to both Powell Cable Car lines ($-pp one way). We used the F line ($-pp with free transfers within -- minutes) for cheaper trips to the Ferry Building and Union Square on Market St. Parking was $-- a night at the Holiday Inn!!! There is unlimited in and out, but be prepared to pay that $---night. Our building had a Denny’s that was open -- hours, but with all of the Wharf and North Beach right there, find something unique and authentic. 
Activities-Itinerary:
Friday: We drove up on Friday morning from Santa Barbara County on the ---. It took roughly four hours to get to the city and another hour to get through the traffic to the Wharf. We were able to check in when we arrived at -:--pm. From there we walked up Columbus Ave to Rogue Ales Public house for some beer tasting and lunch. The Kobe tacos were simple, but good and the French Dip was good as well (we were there for the beer – try some of the brewer’s tea and chamomile beers). From there we walked up to Coit Tower for some views. It was $- to go up in the tower, so we passed. The marine layer (fog) was in, but you could still see a good bit, however some of the views down were blocked by trees and shrubbery. From Coit Tower we walked down the stairs of Telegraph Hill towards the Embarcadero. The little stair walkways pass through beautiful houses with unique gardens and paths (look for wild parrots in the trees). Our legs were still feeling good so we continued our walk onward to Market St and down -nd to --st Amendment for more beer tasting (the walk was relatively flat and easy). We opted for some outdoor seating in their beer garden to try a few of their unique cans (get the Hell or High Watermelon Wheat). After resting our feet and having a few cold ones, we headed to AT&T Park for the Giants-D-Backs game. While the air temperature was probably low --’s, it was freezing! Bring jackets, long pants, socks, and maybe a warm hat and gloves (lesson learned). The Giants won and there was a great playoff type energy in the stadium! We had some Boudin chowder in bread bowls ($-.--ea) and some Peet’s coffee during the game (not your typical ballpark food, but it was cold). Post game we took the N Line to the F Line back to the Wharf. From there we hit up Buena Vista Café for some Irish coffee and then called it a night.
Saturday: This was a jam-packed day with lots of walking. We started by taking the F Line to the Ferry Building to browse the Farmer’s Market. Tons of gourmet food (Cowgirl cheese, deli meats, oysters, fish, etc.), drinks and produce to choose from. Very busy at --:--am though. After some coffee and some lox and cream cheese on sour dough we walked to Chinatown. Getting off the main drag (Grant), we checked out the Fortune Cookie Factory (very small and up an alley way) to get some fresh cookies ($-.-- for a huge bag) and Ten Ren Tea Co (on Grant) for some tea sampling. We then hit up Gold Mountain for some Dim Sum. This place was jammed pack with what appeared to be locals (we were the only tourist it seemed). We were sat at a large long table with other older Chinese couples, but it was in a prime position to get fresh Dim Sum right out of the kitchen. At $- a piece (--- dumplings) we were able to try quite a bit (the red bean dumplings were my favorite – so sweet). It was a great experience! From Chinatown we walked to Union Square (quite hilly, so be prepared). Once in Union Square we took the F line to The Castro and proceeded to walk down to the Haight. There were tons of great shops, vintage, hippie stuff, etc. We took pictures at the Haight-Ashbury intersection and then walked towards Golden Gate Park. Hit Amoeba music store for some vinyl and a huge selection of new and used music. We stopped off at Cha Cha Cha for some sangria (pitcher for $--) and tapas (plantains were delicious) before heading into GGP to visit the Japanese Tea Garden ($-pp). The tea garden was small, but beautiful. We did not opt for tea, but they had a nice open air café where tea was served in small pots and we saw some people eating simple sushi. There is also a nice little gift shop. From the garden we walked north through the park to catch the MUNI - back to Union Square. In Union Square we did some shopping and dined at Burger Bar (great milkshakes and good burgers). After a long day, we took the F line back to the Wharf.
Sunday: We walked around the wharf and got a light lunch at Cioppino’s (caprese salad, cup of chowder, and crab and shrimp cocktail were all good). It was easy to get a table at --:--am. From there we took the Blue and Gold ferry from pier -- to Sausalito ($--pp round trip). This gave some great views of the bay, Alcatraz, the GG bridge and Sausalito. Got some ice cream, did some wine tasting, shopped at some galleries (bought local artist jewelry) and had some wine and sushi at Sushi Ran (huge Saki selection and a pretty decent wine selection- they know there stuff, sushi was pretty good as well. Get off the main drag, there are some decent restaurant options). It was a nice relaxing day. Hopped back on the ferry (Note: there are two lines, one for bikes and one for pedestrians. Also, there are two ferries, one to pier -- and one to the Ferry Building). We went to the Ferry Building because that boat came first. From there we walked back up Telegraph Hill past Coit Tower to North Beach. By -pm it was very busy with tourists on Columbus Ave. After checking out various Italian eateries, we decided on Michelangelo’s Café. The lobster ravioli in vodka tomato sauce, eggplant parmesan, bread, bottle of house chianti and chocolate bobb were all delicious. They also served a simple bruschette, and topped off the meal with little Italian cookies and gummy bears. The whole meal was about $-- and the service was excellent. Very friendly! After another long day, we walked back to the Holiday Inn to call it a night.
Monday: Breakfast at the Buena Vista Café. They had classic bacon and eggs, potatoes, toast, but also some unique eggs Benedict dishes that seemed popular (crab, tomato). I think their strong suit is still the Irish coffee. Seating is first come, first serve, just hop onto a table or at the counter or join another party (note the bar counter to the left only serves drinks, no food). The café is at a scenic little corner with the Powell-Hyde Cable Car turnaround, Alcatraz in the distance, a view of the Golden Gate Bridge and it is also very close to Ghirardelli’s. After a nice breakfast we headed south on the PCH for a scenic drive back to the central coast. Took a quick stop in Monterey for some crab sandwiches at Liberty Fish Co on the wharf and then continued down highway -. We stopped at several vista points for views and encountered a little traffic at some one-way-controlled traffic areas due to construction, so it took over seven hours to get back. Make sure you stop at the elephant seal rookery in San Simeon (and Hearst Castle if you have time).
Overall it was a great trip! Next time we will finally do Alcatraz, get a closer view of the Golden Gate Bridge, spend more time shopping in the Haight, and hopefully make it up to Healdsburg for some zinfandel tasting in the Dry Creek Valley and some Pinot in the Russian River Valley. I hope this review was helpful!

I was here for - nights. There was only one time I can remember hearing my neighbor, and that was very faint and didn't last long. i saw a lot of other reviewers complaining about noise so it may be dependent on the location of your room and the types of neighbors you have. I really had no complaints about noise. A coworker on a different floor did complain about the light rail making noise pretty late and pretty early. I was on the --th floor and faced Curtis St and never heard it.
My only complaint was the air conditioner. It was extremely noisy. Regardless of the fan settings, it was so loud I was unable to hear the tv. It became a huge pain because I'd be watching a show on tv, the ac would kick on and I'd miss all the dialog until it turned off. The Closed Captioning feature on the tv wasn't working either.
Otherwise, I really enjoyed my stay. My room was big enough and very clean. I could walk very easily to the convention center, shopping areas, and restaurants.

I spent one night at the Embassy Suites LAX North with my family prior to an early flight home. Nobody slept as we had tremendous noise issues from two sources: (-) externally from flights taking off all night -- unlike many airport hotels at which we have happily stayed -- the windows here did not appear to be insulated for sound and the noise from departing jets was terrible; (-) internally from a family in the suite next door - i travel frequently on business and have never heard noise transmission like this. When the person in the neighborhing suite shut down their cellphone, my wife thought I had shut mine down instead. We could hear conversations from next door perfectly clearly.

Reasoably well located being close to the Subway at --th Street on Line - - c.--- yards walking distance. Downside is that rooms are very small with small double beds and the fact there are just two lifts to service c-- floors means you can spend a fair time waiting for a lift. At busy times you may find there is no space if you are joiningg to go downstairs from a lower floor. Breakfasts were good with a reasonable choice of food. A plus is the room cleanliness and general helpfulness and friendliness of the staff. Bar prices not cheap - a bottled beer worked out at $-- including tip.

This was my -rd stay at Park Central. I stay here because I loooove the location. Close to Times Square and everything ELSE to be honest. Fabulous lobby; very modern. Easy check-in. Friendly Valet, always (it'll cost you $-- bux-night ya'll to keep your car there.) We've stayed in the new part twice before. No problems. The problem is this...the OLD PART. Keep stuff up to date...at LEAST make sure you have working elevators that broke down all Saturday during the day and Sunday during the day...the sweet front desk folks let us use the service elevator. How horrible is it that guests have to struggle to get up to their room after a long day? And worse is that the poor people at the front desk have to deal with pretty angry patrons. So Park Central, Slap some paint on it. Do some Checks on your equipment. Respect your property...it's like they gave up on the other half. Sad. On a positive note, I love the people who work there and the location, but this is the first time I actually thought of paying a few extra bucks for a better spot that elevators are in working order.

This hotel is fantastic !!!! beautiful, great service, ,good location,walking distance to shop and restaurant. Housekeeping excellent and the staff in the front desk are very nice especially Jesus with the helpful tips...

Andaz has quickly become my staple NYC hotel. The location couldn't be better (right across the NY Library.) The staff's young and hip, but extremely attentive. The complimentary wine in the evenings is just the icing on the cake. I love the mini-bar with non-alcoholic beverages included and snacks. The gym downstairs is huge for Manhattan standards. The bar in the basement is phenomenal.

I am from Australia and stayed for - nights. From the minute we arrived we were met by the amazingly friendly and helpful valet. The lovely girl on reception referred to us by name everytime she saw us. Amazing location right across the road from the baseball stadium!! 
Overall amazing experience with super helpful staff! Thank you.

We stayed downtown for a night get-away and to go out to dinner. The hotel is very easy to get to and the valet parking made the stay extra easy. We stayed in a suite that was modern and very well appointed. Absolutely everthing we needed was available. They transported us to our restaurant and back. And then to top it off, they had a big, hot breakfast in the morning. The perfect place run perfectly!!

We stayed at the Carlton Hotel from -- November for - nights and to be honest I tried to change our booking following reading the negative reviews on tripadvisor. I couldn't get the booking changed so held my breath and hoped for the best. How glad I am that we had to go to the Carlton. The hotel is situated on Sutter Street which is about a -- minute walk from Union Square, I know everyone keeps going on about the front desk staff but they have to be seen to be believed they are so helpful and friendly, really genuine and really do go the extra mile to make sure you have a great stay. Our room was based at the back of the hotel and had a massive bed, the room and bathroom were both tastefully decorated. 
The hotel is near the Tenderloin area which is not the best area in the city, but the staff do warn you on checkin not to go near it, we unfortunately wondered into it and did feel very threatened and vulnerable, although no one approached or even spoke to us, but we had been warned and should have paid more attention to where we were going.
Other reviews have also stated that the walls are paper thin in the hotel, I can categorically state that I am a light sleeper and I did not hear a single sound from the other rooms during our entire stay. I certainly could hear traffic and fire sirens but hey what do you expect if you are staying in the middle of a major city.
I really don't know what the negative reviewers are talking about, I am so glad I took a chance and stayed at this wonderful hotel.

Location is fantastic just minutes away from all attractions. Quiet, clean and well run. The front desk staff could not be better. All were very helpful in giving us directions and offering suggestions. Hampton Inns are the best -- and this one is great. So close to the airport -- I will be back again and again.

We were happy enough with our stay here. The room was small with - people and lots of luggage. The breakfast was good and filled us up for the day. The main problem is that without a car this hotel is a little out of the way. We had to rely on the bus. The staff wrere very helpful and always polite and could not do enough for us. If I was to return to San Iego I might stay somewhere In the city next time if I did not have a car.

Excellent breakfast. Nice clean spacious rooms. Layout is cool to be able to look out the balcony and see the atrium. And to be able to have breakfast or just have a get together in the atrium. Loved it there. Would definitely go back and well worth the $$

On a more positive note the room was basic, clean and had a great view but needed a bit of TLC. Most staff in the hotel were friendly but the staff behind the reception were unfriendly and were not interested in helping you.
