This hotel ruined our holiday to New York and the whole experience of new year, the hotel is very overpriced and over rated. I will be telling friends and family who visit New York not to stay here. 
I WOULD NEVER STAY AT THIS HOTEL EVER AGAIN THERE IS FAR BETTER AND CHEAPER IN TIMES SQUARE THE HOTEL HAS LEFT ME FEELING CHEATED OUT OF MY HARD EARNED CASH.

Hotel is situated right on union square and has a cable car stop right outside but the trolley is nearly always full by the time it reaches this stop ( trolley driver told me it is called fantasy island as you don't stand too much chance of boarding there). Unlike other reviews both the wife and i found the beds very uncomfortable and didn't sleep very well in them. Room was in the new section and even though we were quite high up the street noise was quite loud though this could be that i live in the country and not used to city noises.

stylish small boutique hotel. Good rooms and bathrooms. bar and small pool on roof with superb views. Fast and friendly staff, as you expect but easy going in an la way. Walking distance to lacma and a few restaurants. Good kocation for rest of city.

Old Town Inn is very nice, small hotel. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The pool is great. The location of the hotel is also nice. (near Old Town). Only the breakfast was not my favourite, but ok.
I would recommend this hotel to everyone. It´s really nice!

My wife and I traveled to Chicago with friends for a long weekend. Had a great room in the West tower overlooking the river. The service of the staff and the amenities were great. Try the BIG bar or the Irish Pub. Both great places for a drink. Hotel was located in a convenient location so we could walk Michigan ave. or take a short cab ride to other areas. A very enjoyable weekend.

We wanted to stay in a hotel that had some character this hotel oozes glamour and is very elegant. We were not disappointed with our choice. We did book a supieror room and on checking in found the reception and bell staff very friendly and helpful. We were upgraded to a poolside cabana room and we accepted even though we were fully aware of the reviews mentioning the noise problem from Tropicana Bar. We found the music was louder during the day then late at night, however we were at the Tropicana bar until --.--am anyway. I have read alot of the comments that the hotel is dark this is true however I found it to be in keeping with the hotels atmosphere and creates the elegant ambience expecially in the main lobby and bar areas. We had pre dinner drinks in Teddys-Library bar great atmosphere and dined in Dakota for dinner the service and food was great. The hotel is very central to everything in Hollywood and there was even a movie premier across the road. You will also find that most of the tour groups leave from the Kodak Theatre across the road. The only down side was that the concierge didn't book our airport shuttle after she said she would and we were lucky enough to get one at the last minute (- hour before we had be picked up).

Very nice hotel, all the staff were very friendly towards us.
We had a studio room and were expecting something that you could just walk around the bed, but our room was huge for manhattan rooms and the price.
Maureen on the concierge desk was especially helpful on several occasions for booking tickets and general advice. She knows her stuff!
Very well placed hotel in terms of transport links.
We had e-mailed in advance to ask for a room on a high floor and are needs were catered to.
Would recommend going to Ginger House for some food if you like chinese food, its across the street and down one block i think. Very good food.
would easily go back to this hotel again!

My kids loved this place! It was hard to get them to behave like they weren't at home, because they just felt like they were. Everyone was so friendly and accomodating, even the guests on the elevator.

A very nice hotel made better by staff people such as HENRY ROBINSON who was friendly and helpful and went out of his way to make our stay enjoyable.
As for the restaurant, the chefs apparently have a very different concept of what """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""well done"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" means, but if you like your burgers with a pulse, go for it. The waitress (Michelle) commiserated with us and comped me with a free dessert (which was excellent).

One of the most impressive features of this hotel is the views. Even the bathroom has floor to ceiling windows- except for the areas that should be private.
The hotel room was large, clean and modern .
Located in the heart of Philly, everything was in walking distance.
I'm not sure about the rest of their service, but check-in was a breeze.

We stayed at the solita and thought it was a fantastic little hotel in SOHO. The rooms are small but hey its New York City. The furnishings were modern and the staff was absolutely fantastic. The girl at the front desk gave us great advice on local places to eat. I will definately plan on staying there again.

What a wonderful place in a wonderful part of the city. My business partners and I had previously stayed at the OMNI and the Hyatt Hotels. We heard about thus place from - of the companies we were visiting in the area. We were treated like people, not numbers and the staff coulldn't be more gracios and helpful. Our trip was a great success and we had a great time. We'll never go back to the big guys! We were appreciated and were treated as such. This hotel is in the middle of the most historic mile in America. It was convenient to get everywhere. There must be -- restaurants with every cuisine imaginable and all within walking distance. We enjoyed every one we went to.

Great location!! Good value for money in Manhattan. Hotel was within walking distance to Empire State Building, Macys, -th Avenue and Time Square. Metro is just a few metres away from the hotel entrance. Hotel staff were very friendly and helpful, especially Matthew and Gulbiye. They even offered to send a fridge and microwave up to my room.
Located one block off Michigan Ave. and by many great restaurants. Free WiFi, large room with contemporary decor, microwave-mini-fridge and friendly staff. Will stay here again.

I picked the Oxford because it was the most affordable place in the lower downtown area. I wasn't expecting much, but ended up being very pleased.
It's in a great location within walking distance to a number of nice restaurants, a couple of blocks from --th street and right next to Union Station. 
The hotel was great. Staff was very friendly and professional. I normally am turned off by pushy service staff and having to tip multiple people just to get to my room, but the staff at the Oxford was very polite and asked to provide service. The front desk manager was very professional while still being fast and polite.
The rooms are good size for a historic hotel and have modern conveniences. Expect a creaky wood floor, but all the modern conveniences. I liked that the rooms had some character instead of the typical cookie cutter hotel chains. Views aren't great mostly because of the location so I wouldn't pay more for a room with a view. 
We also ordered room service after a couple too many beers at the football game and it was very good. I'll definatly stay here again.

Great smaller hotel, very big rooms very well equipped, within walking distance to all must see nyc spots!! We had a great time despite the service. 
However, every thing i requested from front desk was met with a NO!! Forget using the 'customize your stay' option on-line because it wont be in your room. ONE bellman only is in charge of locking- securing your luggage so plan to wait!! Of course, frontdesk will tell you they cant help ( dont bother asking)! Pushed my checkin to -:--(front desk said nothing they could do, sorry charlie)! No bottled water on site so ' you can go to corner store to guy some' again, thanks front desk. 
I travel extensively and can honestly say ive never felt like an interruption to front desk like this. I paid rack rate --- per night versus using hotwire: guess that made my lack of service even worse. 
By the way, major issues with heating in our room! During three day stay, two visits from maint man. Front room way hot at -- degrees and bedroom couldnt heat up past --!! Bring sweaters and flip flops.

I had read the negative reviews and was concerned about room quality & cleanliness. Our room was very good - clean & in good repair. The grounds are absolutely beautiful - several pools, waterfalls, beach access. It felt like Hawaii. The Barefoot Grill Restaurant (on the property) served a wonderful breakfast with a view of the bay.
We had a few minor requests for extra towels and to have the outside light turned on that were dealt with promptly. The staff was friendly and very accommodating.
We would definitely look forward to staying there again.

We arrived from the UK rather tired from a late flight to find that our allocated room was not what we were expecting. We informed the management and, even though the hotel was full, they promised they would do their best to get us the accomodation we had expected. Next day our room was changed effortlessly and we got precisely what we were hoping for! We had an excellent stay at the Barclay, getting superb service from the concierge and front office management at all times. We lunched in the restaurant and were delighted with the scallops and tarte tatin! The calvados bar is something else, i tried a ---- vintage calvados that was the most exquisite version of that wonderful digestif i have ever tasted! We already loved New York, the Barclay enhanced our perception of the Big Apple even further. We were sad to leave and will be very happy to come back.

We travelled from CA as a family (wife and three daughters ages -, - and -). We stayed Sunday through Wednesday then moved on to drive through Sedona then a day visit in the Grand Canyon. I booked over -- days in advance directly on their website and was able to take advantage of a great advanced booking discount for a Deluxe Suite. A few days before our trip I read more reviews on tripadvisor and have to say I became very nervous about all the bad reviews I was seeing. So nervous that my wife and I considered canceling last minute. We went though with the visit and I must say we were very happy with our decision. The suite was very spacious and was located right next to the entrance of the Oasis making it very convenient for us all. It was clean, had a decent view (-th floor room) - we were even guided into our room my a staff member..which was a nice personal touch. Before taking our luggage up to the room I asked to see the room since we were so nervous about it might look. Yes, the TVs were fairly old---but none of us minded at all (which is surprising considering I am a technology geek). The room was great so we moved in. My only criticism would be the quality of the mattresses - our King bed was very comfortable, however, it dipped in in the middle and was pretty noticeable. My - year old spent most her time with mom and dad in the lazy river and wave pool while the - and - year old hopped around between the water slide and lazy river. It was not very crowded (I believe Arizona schools started the Monday we were there which could have been a factor) and the staff was helpful. There were lifeguards everywhere which was comforting. 
The had a nice location - the Arizona Mills Mall was just down the street and Target was a quick -- minutes away. This provided good, lower priced, food alternatives and a place to grab necessities like bottlled water, etc. The kids begged to stay longer but we had to move on to our next destination. 
Overall - great experience and would recommend to any family looking for a few days of fun in the sun.
Lots to do and can walk to many things - shopping, good restaurants all within striking distance. Great rooms

Our family of - stayed here, The rooms were clean, neat, well stocked with towels etc. The rooms are not huge, but everything is like that in New York, space is at a premium, for what we paid i can't complain. The location of this hotel is wonderful, it has an exit from Penn station metres from the entrance.
The Hotel has an old style charm, very New York, The staff were helpful, we had a great time.
Empire State building is a -----min walk away. We walked to Central Park, Broadway & basically all over the place, we did & recommend the open top bus tours (Grayline) as this gives you great bearings as to where everything is & how far away things are too. 
Happily recommend this hotel.

Our friends selected this hotel, and we were trying to adhere to a $---- per night budget in San Francisco. These rooms fell well within that range, and when we arrived, we were upgraded to larger """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""suites"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Very Victorian furnishings and spacious public rooms. Modern granite baths.

So I called the front desk and the operator told me that the front desk does not take calls this late at night. Excuse me I said, we just left the desk minutes ago and explained my problem. Once in the sleeping part of the room you have but - lamps again with -- watt bulbs that by far could only illuminate the nearest - feet surrounding the bulb itself. An old velvet sofa chair for my son and one bed for my husband and I. Two pillows, one sheet, one blanket is all you have. No microwave for leftovers that may have been needed for reheating and no room in a small fridge for - cans of soda. I'm thankful my son likes his soda warm. 
Sorry St Giles you failed my expectations miserably. Being from Chicago I expected more from a presumed - star hotel and believe me when the description talks about classic style and original looks the hotel has--one should run as fast as they can as this is code for """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""our stuff is old and original."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Nothing new, nothing nice, nothing updated.

Never again will we stay at this HoJo, and it is unfortunate because the hotel is indeed very convient to Downtown (was a few minute trip), the hotel was clean and the staff is very friendly. However the owner is aweful and made what could have been a great travel experience one in which I find myself writing this review. Normally, when there is an issue, it is the owner who makes everything right. Oddly, the owner had made an error in assigning our room in the hotel, and it was the staff who had to tactfully calm her (the owner) down, after she tried to blame us for her error. Unfortunate indeed, as she has wonderful staff and actually a very nice hotel, but this was un-called for in our opinion, and unacceptable for future stays in the Jacksonville area, of which we travel to quite frequently.

The room was clean, quiet, comfortable, and attractive. The desk folk were impressively helpful and gracious--I was allowed to check in early due to the availability of my room. Also, I paid a very reasonable amount for the room because of specials that were available. Further, I liked the location: close to AMNH, Central Park, and subway lines.

I traveled to El Paso for business, I have an extended stay. This hotel has met all of my expectations, Check-in was superb, there were nine in our party and front desk personnel treated us with great respect. The rooms are outstanding, very well maintained by a highly exceptional House Keeping Staff. Not only could I fall asleep on the comfortable couch, but the bed just calls me in, with so many soft pillows you can’t help but to lie down and enjoy. This hotel is located in excellent location just off I--. Easy access to the airport, with a shuttle service that will go out their way to assist you. The hotel has the most outstanding front desk staff that I have ever encountered in the many hotels that I have stayed in. I could mention them all but one in particular, a confident and competent UTEP student who greets me at the door with a smile and always made me feel at home. I will always remember my stay here thanks to her.

Arrived in the evening, but had no worry of losing room as this dump was literally empty. Right near the bridge that goes over to Arkansas. Since we arrived late we assumed we'd be stuck in a room facing the screeching non-stop traffic. Fortunately we were placed in the back of the motel. This alone did not help our experience. First impression of this dank and dark room was the overwhelming toxic smell of bleach. Although this would give the impression of cleanliness, too much of such smell is also nauseating. Bathroom ceiling was so low I thought I'd have to amputate my legs in order to stand in the shower and I'm not that tall. The clorox stench gave no comfort as the pulling back of the comforter proved to be very UN-CLEAN. Stains, bloody galore or whatever it was. Carpets seemed gritty. Just afraid for all personal hygiene. Even though we had driven all day we wanted to get out for any reason not to stay in the room. Went to downtown Beale St, nice area. Passed Sun Studio and Graceland but came back reluctantly as fatigue wore us down. At least we'd get some rest. WRONG! In the middle of the night, the power to the hotel seemed to have been turned off and our heater as well. Woke up in shivers! Woke up early, checked out and discovered we were charged slightly higher rate than from internet. Felt it wasn't worth complaining about even though it was sub-standard comfort. Drive away from this place FAST!!

The staff at Kimpton was very accomodating and attentive to my every need. I had actually reserved a room at the Westin on Michigan Avenue, and given flight delays was checking in to the Westin around midnight. The front desk representative did not excuse herself when she was helping me to aid another customer, and actually checked me into a dirty room. There were used towels and leftover food everywhere. When I called the front desk, she did not appear to be very apologetic, and did not offer me any real compensation in terms of a room upgrade, etc. After going to my second room, I noticed that the air was incredibly smoky and I had requested a smoke free room. Devastated and overly annoyed, I checked out and went to the Allegro. The front desk representative not only gave me my company rate despite the untimeliness of my checkin, but apologized for the lack of a king room. The space at the Kimpton is not as vast as the Westin, but the decor and the ambience is very chic. The fitness room esp. is very nice and clean.

The location of this hotel just off Times Square cannot be rivalled. As would be expected from an old building the bedrooms are of modest size and do not feature a bath. Rooms are well maintained and the monochrome decor is well presented throughout.
Breakfast buffet is served in the bar each morning which is far too dark for this time of the day and there is no staff in sight to offer any assistance. In fact I would say that my biggest gripe with this hotel is the lack of good North American service that features in so many other NY hotels as standard. Staff here appeared a bit too 'cool for school' and not particularly interested in their guests other than to try and drag them into the empty bar in the evenings.
Room service was alright - standard food which was well presented but not mind-blowing.
Overall - stars - - for location but pretty much everything else - stars.

I booked the Hotel Del Sol over the Internet, so I had no idea what to expect. I have been burned in the past by bogus descriptions of hotels. Not this one. The Hotel Del Sol is the best bargain in San Francisco. I got a room for $-- a night, which includes parking (a BIG DEAL in S.F.). The staff was incredibly friendly and helpful, rooms extremely clean (with Avedia products) and it was in a super neighborhood w-i walking distance to the Marina Green and Chestnut Street shops. I would recommend this place to anyone. It was fantastic.

We actually stayed in Jan ---- but could not chose that date. Robert the manager was very helpful and answered all my emails promptly before we arrived. We had a one bedroom apt on the top floor and the view and balcony were amazing. Also had a full kitchen which was great as we were staying for a week. We were starving so he called the italian restaurant next door and asked them to stay open for us - great meal too! Free breakfasts were a great treat too - as was the free internet and local calls. we were recommended by a friend to stay at the Rex and it really lived up to the recommendation!. The room was just great and the staff were so helpful, nothing was too much trouble and they certainly knew their city. It's a great location and agreat hotel with a special ambience. When we go back to SanFranciscso we will certainly stay at the Rex

We stayed at the Hotel Contessa the first weekend in December. It is ideally located at a quieter section of the riverwalk right next door to the Westin. This beautifully designed hotel has a wonderful patio area along side the river. We enjoyed cocktails after dinner and listened to the Spanish influenced guitarist performing in the Cork lounge. My only word of caution: If you like to turn in before --:--pm make sure you tell the desk that you don't want a room facing the atrium-bar area. The music travels and it could be quite loud in your room.If they want to be a - star hotel, they need to offer guests airport transportation. 
 Overall, I would say this is probably the best hotel on the riverwalk.

Nice looking building from the outside with a good location at --th Street West and -th Avenue - close to Times Square, Central Park and a number of subway lines. The lobby is quite attractive with a fish aquarium from floor to ceiling, statues with a sitting area and a small stylish check-in desk - staff were friendly and efficient. There are a number of elevators - all on the small side but typical for older NYC buildings.
I had booked a larger room - appx --- square feet - the standard rooms are --- sqaure feet and come with a smaller bed. There was decent closet space and a sizeable bathroom that was well designed with many mirrors, bathtub-shower combination with good water pressure and temperature, great lighting and good storage space.
The room was clean and had a neat blue neon type underlighting that gave the room a nice ambient feeling and had great lighting with lamps over the bed, halogens with dimmer in the ceiling and accent lights.
For improvements and to rank higher in my opinion, the rooms need some upgrade treatments:
* The chairs in the room were not comfortable to sit in and read - a nice reading chair would be good for a room in a hotel of this calibre
* The bed was a mattress sitting on a wood frame - it was reasonably comfortable but would have been better with a boxspring-foundation underneath
* The windows could use more upgraded sound proofing - I have stayed in NYC before so I do have an idea of amount of noise to expect, however I was on a bit of a loud street and close to it (was on -nd floor facing onto --th) and believe that the windows would benefit from more soundproofing
* The clothes dresser was or functioned as if it was a cheaper design - the drawers stuck and the piece screamed lower quality (again for a hotel this calibre, I expected better)
All in all the stay was decent and it is a good hotel - if the above areas were improved, my rating would be above average.

We just returned from a one night stay at The Hyatt Hill Country

Everything from the grounds,to the rooms , to the lobby seemed to

Stayed at the Airport Inn ----- ot -----. Best location. Shuttle to and from airport and Graceland. The friendliest and most helpful people. They go out of there way to make you feel right at home. Thank you to all for making our stay very pleasureable.

I stayed here recently for a week long conference and found the hotel and its staff to be very helpful overall. The rooms are large and the bathroom was quite clean. I found the check in and out process to be quite easy. Even though the restaurants are a little pricey and can be slow when busy I still enjoyed the food and the experience.
Nice motel, clean rooms, great location to explore some parts of the city by foot, only a bit noisy.

LOCATION, LOCATION , LOCATION, this is the best feature of this hotel, you’re within a block of Boylston street and - blocks from Newburry street which both have lovely shops and many options for eating, if you walk them in direction to Fenway Ball Park you’ll see many restaurant options. Do not stay here; it is not worth the savings. Terrible hotel, terrible service. We encountered an issue and tried to get it resolved with the onsite staff; however, they all from security to the front desk clerk proved to be useless. I stayed at the st.regis hotel for - nights in february. The Hotel itself is very nice, the lobby is beautiful and the rooms look nice altough a bit too simple considering the fact that they underwent a restoration - year ago.
The service is what drags the hotel down in my rankings. Altough the service standards in US can´t be compared to europe, middle east or Asia, you expect at least basic standard procedures.
When I arrvied there was one door man ( who was acting very strange, almost too childish) and and a bellman talking to each other almost forgeting they were at work. The the butler came, which i dont understand the purpose of. Feels like St.regis promote the butler service for its name, but they are definetly no real butlers. My overall impression is that they have a very beautiful Hotel, but the service is way too low for it being worthy of a St. Regis. If you want to stay at a S,t Regis please stay at Rome or London. The location is great, but i rather stay in a hotel a bit further away from the attractions if it provides betetr service, because in the end, that is what distinguishes hotels from each other.
PS. It must have been the worst fitness center i have seen in a - star hotel, Smaller than my bedroom in my house.

I stayed at this hotel for one night. The room was very clean and the bed very comfortable. Location is excellent, right off Michigan Ave, and Lake Shore Dr. is close. Staff was very courteous. This hotel, compared to others I have stayed at in the area for the same price ranks much higher in comparison. I will stay here again as well as recommend The Knickerbocker.

Stayed at The Drake for a week long business trip. What an inredible property. The room (Executive King Lakeview Suite) was beautiful, the staff were attentive and professional. All in all, a first class experience.

Obviously suffering from cutbacks the Fairmont Dallas was a huge disappointment. Having been attracted to the Knickerbocker by a -- hour sale, and never having visited Chicago, we were guarded in our expectations. This hotel is in a great location, has friendly, helpful staff (especially the Concierge desk) , and has done a great job renovating the guest rooms. We booked a junior suite which gave us a bit more room and an extra flat-screen T.V. The window overlooked the back of another building across a courtyard, but I was so happy to have a window that opened to allow in fresh air that it really didn't matter. I have environmental allergies that are often set-off in hotels, but I had absolutely no issues here. Our room felt and looked clean and fresh. We came in by train and cabbed it everywhere (highly recommended for first-timers to Chicago), so I can't comment on parking. The only part of the hotel that still looked a bit shabby were the elevators - which unfortunately contributes to a first impression; however, this was soon forgotten because of the rest of our experience. If you want to pay higher prices for grander accommodations go ahead - but we more than satisfied with our stay at the Knickerbocker...and I am generally pretty picky about where I stay.

Sometimes luck of the draw is luck; picked this hotel out from hotels.com on the train into Seattle. It was great! The rooms are very comfortable -- leopard print terrycloth robes are funky! Was in town for a conference located just down the street from the Congress Plaza. As other reviewers have noted, it's quite old. But you won't get a better deal for your money in downtown Chicago. As long as you don't mind the worn furnishings and decay of bygone extravagance, it's a steal.

Well priced, convenient location, friendly and capable staff at reception, breakfast very basic (plastic cups, plastic cutlery, etc) but sufficient.
Rooms clean but small, beds comfortable, quality amenities provided in bathroom

Besides being a super value for the $ (no joke! best bang for your buck!)...the is something unique going on at this place. I spend so much time away from home but this place is the next best thing. 
I am not sure why but when you are there, your stress level goes down and you feel a sense of...family? I am NOT the kind of guy who will hang out in the lobby. I go to my room and thats that. This hotel is highly rated but be forewarned, from the hotel's own website: """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The Hotel Rex elevator will be undergoing an upgrade and will be unavailable for use February -th through March --st. Thank you for your cooperation.""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""

Just returned from another excellent stay at the Lenox. I've had the pleasure of staying here several times over the last year while I'm in in Boston on business. I travel frequently for work, and always look forward to my nights at the Lenox. I've enjoyed it so much that I've returned with my family during Red Sox weekends. The property is right in the heart of the Back Bay, providing easy access to all the neighborhood amenities. It underwent a renovation recently and the common areas and rooms were beautifully updated. The attentive staff is, hands down, some of the best in the business--particularly for an independent hotel. An absolute must try!

This hotel was great- within walking distance to most seattle sites and had GREAT service. The front desk staff was friendly, and very helpful. Extra props to Michael B, one of the men at the front desk. He went out of his way to help us with whatever we needed. I would come back to this hotel in a heartbeat. Recommended for anyone who is taking a trip up there. 
We had taken the train and was within easy walking distance of the hotel. Also about a - minute walk to the bus tunnels. A little hard to find the hotel, but overall worth it.

In general, an excellent stay and an excellent hotel. Staff were without exception helpful, polite and friendly (almost falling over themselves to apologise when I had problems with the AC), the room was pretty large and quite well furnished, there was plenty of parking, maid service was thorough, it was close to lots of malls etc. (including a Whole Foods), and the kitchen was reasonably well equipped.
The only real downsides were that the kitchen didn't have an oven (although this is fairly typical of such suite hotels), and that the breakfast was a bit poor - although the selection was reasonable, the items were a bit cheap (even by American breakfast standards) and often there wasn't even real crockery. On the other hand, it is free. There were also some evening drink and snack nights, which were also free.
All in all, I would recommend this as somewhere to stay - but it might be worth finding somewhere else to eat breakfast unless you're on a tight budget.

This is a typical Fairfield Inn but the staff are exceptionally friendly and go out of their way to make you feel right at home. South of the city center but central to most locations. Pool and spa are relaxing after a rough day... been here before but my first review of the place. A definite place to go back to when needed...

If you stay here, be sure to ask for a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""larger"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room with no adjoining doors to the room next door.

This hotel was awesome. Valet was quick, what a beautiful hotel. Check in and check out were so quick. Elevators were fast.

I'm sorry the last reviewer had a horrible time, but my experience was the complete opposite.

I would highly recommend this extremely family friendly resort to just about everyone. However, if you choose this hotel, ask for either the Camelback or Sedona buildings because the Mountainview building isn't going to start being renovated until August.

Because of the difficulties with our registration, we were upgraded to a superior room, with a view of the surrounding buildings. The room was fine, clean, and well kept, but our soaps were left untouched for at least one day. Generally a forgettable stay.

Room service from the DB restaurent is efficient and excellent.
The breakfast, its brioche and the whole menu is to die for.
Nicely located on --th street, but prefere the Sofitel next door, better value, better rooms, better atmosphere you can go to DB for breakfast next door.

Overall, the hotel is nice. Has others have noted, the RenCen is huge and confusing. (Although, over the years, they have improved signage and it is easier to find one's way around than in the past.)

Not quite rude, but verging up on it. As an example, the first day I returned to my room at -:-- p.m. and the room had not yet been made up. This review may sound a bit picky--overall, it is a good place to stay in Detroit. However, for a high end hotel, I expect a bit more :)

Fantastic Hotel! Amazing Staff! The entire staff was extremely Friendly, welcoming, and helpful. The rooms were extremely spacious and clean. My girlfriend and I attending the The Roof party for New Year's Eve. Lloyd did an amazing job with the event! Kevin and Matt were top-notch bar tenders...service was first-class. Thanks for such a wonderful experience. I would highly recommend this hotel!
Jeff F.

Fantastic Hotel. Superbly furnished rooms.
Bar area far too small. They might as well not bother with it.

Good breakfast range but not much fresh fruit, some days only apples. Wish they would put tea bags in the rooms but you can get them from the breakfast area.

This hotel is beautiful. It even smells fabulous. But, I am not at all impressed by the services I received. I was here on business with a convention. Everyone “passes the buck” and seems to have no clue about anything. I asked the valet a simple hotel question and they sent me to the Bellman. The location of RH is perfect, one block away from Grand Central Station and metro ( - lines). Times Square is only - block away (---- min) and - min from Central Park. Great view of NY skyscrapers. For breakfast we found a nice bakery a couple of blocks away, Specialties, for a cheap meal.
I did notice that they charge for local calls, internet service, & parking. But we didn't use any of these (took the train to Seattle) so didn't have any of these extra fees. I recommend the Crowne Plaza especiallly if you can get this good rate!

I found the Hampton at the last minute when other plans fell through and I was very pleased with it. It is has recently been redecorated and refurbished. The rooms are immaculate, modern, attractive and comfortable. The bathroom is above average with stone tiling, a beautiful tub-shower with good water pressure. The hotel soaps were not great, but other than that they give you a beauty kit, a shoe cloth, mouthwash, shampoo, conditioner and lotion. There is a hair dryer and coffee maker.
They also provide you with an ironing board and an iron.
The service was excellent. If I ever needed anything it was taken care of very quickly and in an extremely friendly manner. The people who work there seem to genuinely care about the guests and doing their job well.
There is no restaurant in the hotel, but there is room service and a free breakfast in the morning in the lobby on the -th floor.
There is also a nice fitness room and when I arrived they were in the process of installing a computer center. They also provide a laundry service.
I loved how convenient it was to the museum, millenium park, theater, the train, shops, the post office - everything really.
Although I saw a lot of business travelers, there were a wide variety of people staying at the Hampton.

Stayed here for - nights at the end of our West Coast road trip. Hotel is well located, if you have a car, for Hollywood, Disney, etc, and better than paying top $ elsewhere. The staff ,especially the concierge, were spot on and eager to help.
Rooms were fine, with great beds. Ate in the bar area, which was priced OK, and met our needs at the end of a long day touring around. Ate out a couple of nights, which is where the car comes in, as you need to travel ---- miles. Pool was clean and well kept, with a good fitness centre-health club. 
Happy to recommend.

We had a great stay at this hotel. The location was perfect! A short walk to the Venice Beach boardwalk and plenty of restaurants, bars etc. Considering where it was it was very quiet too. We had a rental car and parking was provided for just $- per day. The room was a good size and very clean and tidy, we had a small balcony. The breakfast was good for a free breakfast. I can highly recommend the Baja Cantina next door for a great Mexican meal and margaritas! Overall a great little hotel.

I had the pleasure of staying at the Casablanca Hotel from -- September - - October ----. I would like to say from the moment I was greeted by the friendly staff at reception to each and every time I entered or left the premises that all staff encountered would go out of their way to acknowledge me.
This is a wonderful place to stay, the room was a perfect size for a solo traveller. The bed was perfect, just what a tired body needed after walking all day. The linen was lovely and changed daily. I even had a visit from the housekeeping supervisor to check how happy I was with the housekeeping, needless to say all was of a high standard.
The room whilst not having a view was quiet and no street noise intruded during the night. Although, the sounds of the sirens do tend to create their own lullaby after a time.
Ricks Cafe is a lovely spot to sit and unwind. The staff overseeing breakfast were very kind and nothing was ever a problem for them. 
The design of the hotel is soothing and comfortable.
If I had to say that a negative existed during my stay it would only be that the Casablanca appears to be a place for the mature traveller (--ys +). Whilst all guests I encountered were friendly a younger demographic (-----'s) would have been welcomed for company as I was travelling solo.
Overall I could not fault one aspect of my stay and would definately stay again in the future.

I've stayed at hundreds of different hotels over the years and not one single time have I ever been randomly charged for something a few days after I had left.  Well needless to say I wouldn't stay at this dump ever again. I can't believe after all those hotels I've stayed at I've never ever been charged a penny more than I should have, as it should be. Well, my trip started with a bus ride from the airport to the hotel that was scary at best. Riding a Humvee through Fallujah is safer than being out in that neighborhood. 
Anyhow, we checked in, only to find out our room wasn't ready because there was a SWAT team with rifles and shotguns raiding the hotel's third floor looking for someone and they wouldn't let us upstairs. Overall, this hotel was a bad dream. Im glad I can laugh about it now, but wish I stayed elsewhere. Do yourself a favor and stay somewhere else.

Ideal Location for business or pleasure. Beautifully appointed rooms and ameniites 
( FRESH!) Staff were all very friendly and accommodating from the doorman and front desk staff to the room service and housekeeping team. On business so could not enjoy all that the Hotel had to offer......maybe next time

Stayed at the Crowne Plaza after reading reviews on this site. Perfect location, Personel at hotel were more than accomodating. We stayed in the executive King room with a very large bathroom and a very comfortable bed on --th floor. We enjoyed the view facing west and saw some great sunsets after a cocktail in the lounge across the hall. We will stay here again. Thanks to the concierge for some great recomendations for dinner and thanks to the staff for the complimentary desert sent to our room on my wifes birthday

There's a rather odd flair to the wall colourings and paintings in vast lobby and hallways of the Maxwell Hotel. Once in your room though, classiness takes the forefront. The rooms are large and tastefully decorated. You get a big-screen TV, Keurig coffee maker, and the bathroom countertop is made of granite ... or maybe marble. Add to that its great downtown location and you've got a winnner.

I had stayed here when it was a Park Hyatt and it still is a great place to stay in SFO. We had a studio suite with a separate living room separated by an awkwardly placed tv credenza. Clean, sophisticated, and a good deal as well. Will return on the next trip to San Francisco.

I'm not a city girl so staying at the Bay Club was just perfect for us. Great views and staff. Loved the breakfast buffet to start our day.Rexlxing in the hot tub was wonderful. Check out the concerts at Humphrey's right next door. We saw Tony Bennett from the pool. Not very far from anything but you do need a car.

I recently planned a stay for - days in June for my parents --th anniversary. They made planning it from Illinois very easy. My parents received excellent service, it's all they talked about. The location of the hotel was perfect, my parents had dinner reservations at a restaurant that was just a short walk from the hotel and they were only a short walk from the White House. My parents were surprised with champagne and chocolate covered strawberries, which was a very nice touch!! I thank The Madison Hotel for making my parents anniversary very memorable!!!
nice staff and everything you could need right there, but the rooms need to be updated for the price.

Nice small hotel in a convenient neighborhood, close to Pike Place Market and downtown. Comfortable rooms are generous although lighting could be improved. Staff is helpful and friendly. In Touch members (Kimpton) get free internet and perks. Parking fee is excessive.

I stayed at the Grant in ---- and was fairly impressed enough to come back again in ----. The rooms near the street were refurbished a couple of years ago, so I requested a room there. It's not as noisy as I thought. The room is pretty clean, especially the bathroom. It's a great no-frills place to stay that is central to many of the sights in S.F. Don't expect luxury here, but it's a great bargain nonetheless.

I recently booked a weekend away at the Westin Copley Plaza in Boston to relax and go shopping with my spouse. We received a very good online rate through the Westin website for a King sized bed in a standard room. 
Our room was one of the newly renovated rooms and it was very clean, very large, and extremely quiet. We heard no noise from the hallway or other floors during our stay. 
I had ordered champagne and chocolate covered strawberries to be available on arrival and they were. The strawberries tasted like they were just picked fresh.
I had also called the concierge desk the day before to book dinner reservations. The woman at the desk was able to secure the reservations, at Sorellina for us, which came highly recommended. All I can say is that it was the best meal out I've had in years.
Every single staff member was courteous, and the hotel was amazing. Definitely an A+ experience.

This Hilton Garden Inn is very well located in downtown Chicago. I was withing walking distance or a short cab ride to wherever I wanted to go. The building is slightly dated, but well kept. The pool and exercise room are located on the --th floor and very nice. The exercise room was very spacious compared to some other properties in which I have stayed. The staff was very professional and helpful. Quick with a smile and snappy service. Yes. I used the word """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""snappy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".
I would definitely stay here again. Love downtown Chicago.

Not the best location but who cares, a taxi or - blocks to subway and you can be anywhere you want. the hotel is so great almost didn't want to go out. The room was fantastic, Travelling with daughters so had two queen beds, which were the most comfortable of all our trip. After a month of travel from West to East and back again, feel qualified to make that comment. Spotlessly clean, large room, with a study. Bathroom well equipped even with a tv in the mirror.
The pool area on --th floor was inviting and a great place to relax.
The room service breakfast was delicious.
Service was second to none, the hotels attention to detail made our stay the best in the whole of USA. Highly recommend this hotel.

LOCATION:
The hotel is located near I-- and is close to Greektown.
The hotel itself is relatively convenient. There are two El-train stations close to the hotel, the Clinton-Green-Pink line and the UIC-Halsted Blue line (both approximately - blocks away). You can commute from O'Hare and-or Midway airports from the hotel. There are also bus stations across the street that will take you to the Loop. Union Station is also close to the hotel, I believe it is about --- stops (- blocks) from the hotel. Cabs-taxis are also plentiful. 
NOTE: parking is expensive in downtown Chicago so factor the cost of parking in the equation when deciding to drive a car. ALSO, there is a parking charge for the hotel. Call or check on line (I am unsure of the parking fee because we used public transportation and did not drive).
There are a number of stores close to the hotel itself. There is a Walgreens behind the hotel, there is also a Dominic's Supermarket across the street that has a Starbucks. There is also a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""regular"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Starbucks and a number of restaurants if you go South on Halstead. 
HOTEL:
The hotel is not that special outside. The lobby was clean and there was a lounge area. There is a restaurant attached and a bar. I cannot comment on the bar or restaurant since we did not eat or hang out at the hotel bar. There is a business center where you can print your boarding pass or access the web. There is also wifi, but the signal in our room was a little weak. The staff is helpful and polite. Being from Los Angeles, the Midwest charm is not lost on me.
ROOM:
We booked a suite on the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no-kids floor"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of the hotel. The hotel offers travelers a few floors that offer late housekeeping (after -- am I believe) and does not allow kid-guests on those floors. This is perfect for those who sleep light or would like to sleep-in. Courtesy is also expected from the guests if you are staying in these """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no-kids"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" floor, meaning no loud music, no banging of doors, and no parties. 
The suite that we got had a living room, a desk, and a bedroom. The bedroom, bathroom and living room were all separated by doors and the room looks like a one bedroom apartment. You have a couch and a flat panel TV in the living room. The living room can be dark and gloomy during the day because the bedroom is the only room that has a natural source of light. Our room did not come with a fridge.
The bedroom was ample sized and had a flat panel TV as well. The king-size bed was comfortable and the sheets were nice. I was very comfortable in the bed and was able to sleep well at night. I noticed that some reviews complain about street noise. Closing the window-door to the balcony in the bedroom eliminates the street noise. I may not be as noise sensitive as the other reviewers, but at -- floors up I could not hear any noise once I closed the sliding door. 
The bathroom was ample sized and clean. My only complaint was the weird shower head. I would suggest to the management to install full sized showerheads. 
OVERALL: I would stay at the Crowne Plaza again. The hotel location on the East side of I-- may be a little far from Michigan Ave or Millennium Park, forcing you to take a bus, hire a taxi or walk -- or more minutes to Millennium Park (one reviewer claimed that it was a -- minute walk, it is more than - mile to Millennium Park which would take -- minutes or more if walking leisurely).
If another hotel had the same quality and price and located in the loop or close to the Magnificent Mile, just on convenience I would book that other hotel.

I stayed at this hotel for three nights to attend a nearby business convention. The room was so nice, very clean and had everything I needed. Ellen at the front desk went out of her way to assist me in making some of my travel arrangements. I really enjoyed the hotel and wish I could have taken advantage of the pool and the breakfast.
The Sofia my favorite Boutique Hotel in San Diego and always my first choice for a place to stay. Rooms are well appointed and service is wonderful.

We stayed at the Easton Residence Inn the night before I had eye surgery in Columbus. Having stayed there before, we knew it was a wonderful hotel in a wonderful part of town. It definately lived up to our expectations. Needing to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""rest"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" my eyes for - hours after surgery, we asked and received a late check out. Breakfast was great as usual. Our bed was very comfortable. Shower was handicapped accessible, though we didn't need it, and would have preferrred a tub. Front desk and breakfast staff were kind and accommodating. I felt good enough after resting my eyes to shop at Easton for - hours :)

Location: - blocks from Moscone Convention Center, few blocks from museums, Embarcadero, Union Square, major shopping and restaurants.
Lobby: nice and efficient, concierge is very helpful and mostly knowledgeable about the city, front desk is friendly and accommodating. Cons - no help at curbside with luggage.
Restaurant: breakfast is buffet style only - quite inconvenient, Starbucks in the lobby has very limited selection comparing to standard Starbucks around the country.
Room: very clean, good AC system, quiet (double-windows), good selection of pillows (ask for feather if prefer), large bathroom. Cons - hairdryer with very short cord (I was laughing when someone said it in the review but it is true).
Business: wi-fi reception throughout the hotel, business center is two PCs in the lobby and one printer, due to convention in town - line to use the printer was quite long.
Overall: good quality hotel in the center of beautiful city.

My room, bed, and bathroom was dirty and not clean. The sheets had blood stains, cigarette burns, and hair...after taking a shower I reached for a towel that had someones hair all in the towels with stains all over the towels...the towels looked dirty and not clean...this was my worst experience staying at a hotel...I will never stay at a motel - again...

This graceful historic property is not for everyone. Like an old tapestry it is fraying in places and may seem dated and worn. Nonetheless, we enjoyed our stay. The rooms in the original building are large by San Francisco standards, and the lobby is quite ornate. Other public areas in the hotel aren't quite as nice. The location is hard to beat. It's a good place if you're in town to tour.

the room was clean, the hotel is in the famous Lombard street. It is about -- minutes walking from the wharf. the neightborhood is safe and pretty quite at night. There is a refrigerator, a coffee maker and a microwave in the room. They offer very good donuts for breakfast. Free parking!

This hotel was booked for me and - co-workers for a conference in town. Used to staying at """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""standard"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" --star hotels for business travel, like Hyatt, Marriott, etc. I have to say that this hotel was unacceptable for me.
 The hotel had a stale, musty odor that was covered up with too much fragrance. The room was clean enough, but the dated furniture, ratty carpet and damp smell made me reconsider. After one of what was supposed to be five nights, I checked out. What's worse, I found a room at the Hard Rock hotel (five stars, amazing) that was only $-- more a night...definitely worth the change.
All of the women in my group checked out and switched hotels, while the men were able to tough it out. Apparently the rooms in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""new"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" part of the building sounded a bit better than mine, which faced the courtyard.

Stayed for - nights. Room as expected from photos on website, but bathroom smaller than it looks in the pictures. Comfortable bed with plenty of pointless cushions on top (but no more than a lot of other hotels - don't really understand the point of it, but then I'm not an interior designer) Only one bathrobe in room but another sent up when requested (actually another - sent up?!) , our NYC hotel only had one robe as well, another thing I don't understand when the room is for two guests. 
Room well equipped with everything you require, fridge with minibar (extortionate as usual) that we emptied and filled with our own stuff, luckily not one of those that charges you as soon as you remove something.
Rooftop pool OK - quite small.
Location OK - T station right at front door and right across from Prudential centre if shopping is your thing.
Decent value for Boston for price we paid.

The Drake was everything we expected it to be! Our room was lovely, roomy and verycomfortable--bathrobes, minibar, bottledwater, evening turndown service, pleasanthousekeeping staff. Afternoon Tea was adelightful experience--delicious food,attentive waitstaff, cosy setting, wonderfulambience--highly recommend the experience.We explored the hotel from top to bottom--sawall the beautiful ballrooms and meeting rooms,and appreciated The Drake's place in history.
Great staff from the Shuttle Drivers to the Front Desk and a Bar Tender who knows the Calffornia Wines

The service definitely met and exceeded expectations from the front desk staff, concierge, to the bellman and doormen. Everyone we interacted with was very attentive to detail, gave excellent recommendations for shopping and dining experiences, and demonstrated professionalism consistently.
The rooms were cozy with incredible floor to ceiling glass windows which provided a panoramic views of the city. The shower and bathtub was a treat however the closet area was a bit dated with the hanger support starting to come out of the wall. The bed was definitely great to sleep on with a large flatscreen to watch your favorite networks on. 
The location was incredible right in the heart of the Meat Packing District where shopping, dinning, people watching, and nightlife are at it's best.
-- hour room service saved our lives as we arrived the first night around -am from a long flight from the west coast. Thank you for having this! The fitness center has incredible --- view of the city. The equipment is average with minimal weight resistance machines for different parts of the body so don't expect too much here. There is enough in the fitness center to get a decent workout however. 
Getting access to the bar at the top of the hotel was difficult due to private functions and cryptic communication of how to access the club and bar after -:--pm. It seemed as though the hotel employees had no idea how to access the club specifically. This was frustrating especially since this was a big part of the appeal of the hotel for evening entertainment. 
Overall our experience was wonderful and we would absolutely visit again.

I Really liked this hotel. Good prices. It is very nicely situated in the center city. Chestnut street is lively and full of nice shops. Just head one block south to walnut street for high end upmarket shopping. the Shopes at the liberty place is just in front of the hotel. City hall is like a - minutes walk. I also walked to the historic old city (-- minutes walk). The gay area is also close by (aeound --th and --th streets) and lots of nice bars and nice restaurants. Now back to the hotel, the reception is on the first floor (a bit weird), friendly people there, quick checking in, the room is nice, modern, large , with everything an average traveller might need and a very comfy bed with nice linen. a bit noisy in the morning if you're overlooking --th street (i wanted to kill that guy screaming at -am !). I had food delivered to my room, but you have to wait for the delivery guy in the lobby cause they can't use the elevator without the hotel card. Voila. I recommend this hotel!

We enjoy the location, being away from the hustle and bustle of downtown (if you want Union Square this is too far but we love it) Fantastic staff , beautiful accommodations. You pay a high price for this luxury but will not be disappointed. We have stayed --+ times and love the FHP. PS: only wish they had a bigger fitness facility or spa, but guests have access to a Club nearby.

This is a wonderful Embassy Suites which is clean and very close to the freeway. We especially enjoyed the made to order breakfast and eating it outside surrounded by beautiful flowers. More information on this hotel available at prasadandassociates.com. The sofabed in such hotels are not always of the best quality but at this hotel the sofabed was wonderful and offered a good night's sleep. Would definately stay at this hotel again!

The rooms are nothing special here (sort of Marriott anywhere decor), but the grounds are spectacular with strolling peacocks and a lushly landscaped courtyard pool that captures that romantic San Antonio atmosphere. Have a mango margarita delivered to you while lolling in the whirlpool, or laze on a porch swing on one of the historic buildings located on the property. The location is excellent, within a few blocks of the Riverwalk, yet you are far enough away to avoid the noise and bustle when you wish. Despite the peacocks, your pet is welcome here, too.

We stayed at the Iroquois for three nights in November.
The night we arrived there was no doorman-bellman ton duty to help with luggage so we dragged our heavy cases from the car, up the steps and into hotel. The check in staff were polite but unfriendly. 
I had booked a superior room and requested one with natural daylight and a view if possible. The room we were given was a rude shock!
It was tiny by any standards - absolutely not suitable for two people. We could not stand in the room together along with our luggage. As we had flown for twenty four hours from Australia we had planned to order room service for dinner. Our plans had to change - there was Nowhere to eat in the room.
A very small desk on one side of the bed doubled up as nightstand but no nightstand on the other side, I made do with the window sil to balance a glass of water on.
The Frette robes were yellowed all over and really threadbare in places, the door handle came off the bathroom door, so we had to leave that open to avoid being locked in.
There was no natural light At All in the room - the window faced a brick wall, so that, coupled with the Tiny size of the room made for a very claustraphobic experience so bad we moved room next day and paid the extra for a slightly larger room.
So disappointed with the Iroquois - we won't be staying again.

We stayed at tower -- for the first part of our honeymoon. It was amazing!! The sunset deck is so relaxing, and the service from all the staff from the restaurant, deck, and hotel was excellent. Can't wait to go back!

Actually, the Hotel Circle South strip isn't too bad. Most of the hotels are set back far enough from the freeway that it isn't even noticed. Although, on the north side, I did notice one of the hotels next to the freeway. We stayed five nights and got the one bedroom king with a sofa sleeper in the living area for - adults and - little ones. I requested a room on the top floor and got it, although it turned out that we were across from the elevator. The good thing is the - kids didn't even notice any noise traffic as they were knock out tired! We slept on the sofa one night and noticed noise traffic only once. We had also put a little barricade of sandals, towels, whatever at the bottom of the entrance door to keep the noise at a minimum.
The room was clean and the maid service was excellent. The king mattress was a little stiff than we were use too, but after the first night we were ok. Thin walls?? We didn't even notice our neighbors until our last night when the kid was yelling at his dad for one short moment. Unless, we were lucky and had no neighbors...All I can say for thin walls is that most hotel walls are not sound proof and you're going to hear some noise. I actually started worrying (a little :) before we arrived about the thins walls from all of the previous reviews, but was pleasantly surprised that we did not experience it. As long as we are respectful and try not to make to much noise and keep the kids from jumping on the floor too much..
Directions to all of the nearby parks and places were on the back of the card that held our room keys which was very convenient. The swimming pool was a little cold, but the kids didn't seem to mind. The breakfast was ok with plenty to eat, just gotta find that table to sit at....
Oh, be sure you don't park near the garbage bins, we got trapped by the garbage truck one morning waiting for the man to unload - bins of garbage. Unless, you leave latter in the morning...sorry can't remember what time it was...
I hope you enjoy your stay as we did.

Hotel is ok and fair value. Close to Fisherman's Wharf, full of tourists. Very, very full, to the extent that you can't move.
Top tip - you may wish to skip breakfast and pay elsewhere. The queue is very long and when you get to the front ... well ... the egg must be made from recycled tyres. It can't be egg. And by the time you've found a table anything that was warm will be cold. It just doesn't work.
That said, the rest of the hotel is fine. Odd thing in our room was the coffee maker in the bathroom - ugh.
DO - go to Alcatraz (just brilliant, made by the audio tour; book ahead); buy a transit ticket ($-- for - days' use of buses, cable cars, metro, street cars); go up Coit tower for great views; take some warm clothes (pretty chilly in the fog, even in August)
DON'T - eat at Fisherman's Wharf (in our experience it's poor value for money - walk a few blocks to get much better food for less - try cafe Maria which is great); spend much time in Fisherman's Wharf (unless you just love full-on tourism); bother with a car - use public transport (see above) - good vfm from buses etc (and the hills are SO scary to drive); expect to see Monk (invisible in our stay)

After reading many negative comments about this hotel, I was nervous about going. I just want to say, my experience here was wonderful! The hotel is in a great location, wonderful staff, great complementary breakfast and internet & we never had to wait more than - minutes for an elevator. The room I booked was the Terrace Studio and it was very small because it was the last one available, but we were offered a bigger room, but declined because we wanted the balcony-terrace. They have the best tasting water in the lobby with grapefruit and lime!
I would definitely go back!

Was the worst hotel I have ever stayed at. The people in the room next to us were having a party until -am. Security didnt do anything except continue to warn them. So we got no sleep that evening. Also the pullout couch was so uncomfortable. It was flat and you could feel all the springs digging in your back. I would never stay here again.

A really excellent hotel; every single member of staff was friendly and helpful. The room was good and very quiet; very comfortable bed, a good bathroom with an excellent shower. We all rated the hotel very highly indeed andf would recommend it without hesitation.

This Hotel has nothing memorable. We went to this hotel for Los Angeles Half marathon, and chose it because it was conventiently located near a metro station for transportation from the finish line and it was near some Hollywood attractions... the room was not clean, the smell was awful and the hotel seems a little bit unkempt... the only thing good about it is that the room was big.. that's it.

We have stayed here three times now, once with our children and twice by ourselves. The room is really nice the bedding is terrific. The hospitality and service are wonderful. What we love the most is the location and the two outstanding restaurants downstairs, Eastern Standard and Island Creek Oyster Bar. The food and service is amazing and the design and decor is truly inspiring. We highly recommend a trip to the Commonwealth!

The hotel was very nice and clean. The staff was very polite and answered any questions we had. I thought the location was ideal because it's only two blocks from Seattle Center and that's where we were doing most of our activities. It's also not that far of a walk down to the piers, it took us only about -- minutes. The neighborhood didn't seem sketchy or bad and the hotel had cameras and you had to use your room key to get in the front door after a certain time. The view from the rooftop deck is quite nice if you manage to go up on a nice day. I think that the only complaint that I have is that all the pillows that they have there are too soft and some kind of down or synthetic down.

Great place to stay. Only bad points for me was the patchy service.
In the very quiet restaurant service seemed to vary from from perfunctory to surly. One of the receptionists was a bit tired and grumpy, whilst another was chirpy and lovely. Concierge was really good at chatting-up the female guests, whilst leaving guys with bags to leave like me waiting. 
Location is awesome & I had a fabulous room that had everything you could want. It was clean and very comfortable. Refreshing iced lemon water at reception was a good idea and a welcome touch.
Ground floor lobby area had a bit of a weird and confusing lay out. Large bar and restaurant and function rooms with a tiny reception counter. The lift and coridoors leading to the bedrooms seemed a bit tired or maybe have just had a hard life.
Despite the almost Jeckyl and Hyde service, I would definately go back.

I stayed at the Waldorf=Astoria for one night on business. I was really looking forward to my stay, and have to say I was a bit disappointed. The hotel itself is full of history, icons and the lobby and public spaces are beautiful. 
The room was disappointing. It was average in size for NYC, but the finishes were old and worn down. The tub had a slow drain and there was obvious damage on the bottom of the tub. Paint on the ceiling of the bathroom was flaking and outlets and switches were old and ragged. The room was very clean, just in need of a face lift. 
Beds were comfortable. Room service was great. Staff was friendly.
Would I stay there again? Probably not. For the high price tag, you can find more modern hotels with better accommodations.

Stayed at the St. Regis for a few days while spending a long weekend in DC. With the bed taking up the majority of the room and all the furniture up against the walls there wasn't enough room in some places for two people to squeeze by each other. The room did have a large bathroom, with marble countertops and twin vanities, and a very large mirror. One of the most useful items I found in the room was the full length mirror in the walkway, so you can do one last check before you head out the door. I wish more hotels incorporated this into their rooms.

The staff was very friendly and accommodating. One evening they saw me taking pictures of the area and provided recommendations of nearby sites with lighting to assist with my photographs. They always had someone at the door of the lobby to greet you with a smile.
I enjoyed my stay at the St. Regis and would come back again, but overall I don't think I got the value for my money. There are other better hotels that charge the same price, just a block away.
