I was a little concerned as there are so many bad reviews but this place was great. We booked a park view suite and it was an amazing view. It was the largest room I have ever stayed in in New York. The bed really is amazing. The staff were great and friendly and the location is incredible. Highly recommended!

we booked - rooms for the girls basketball team for a - day tourney. Since the games were played at most of the surrounding colleges the ease of the freeway access made it so easy to get around. The suites worked out great for the girls, with the free breakfast, the microwave, the refrigerators and the pool. They even allowed us to have a dinner out by the pool, of course we cleaned up our mess. The staff was very welcoming and happy.
The breakfast was good but go early if it is summer or a weekend. Lots of variety enough to keep the kids happy and hold them over until lunch.

The last time we stayed in DC, we stayed elsewhere and had a light-well room. We swore we would never do that again. With our special sale rate at this one, that's exactly what we got--but instead of a dark room, it was really just an interior view with lots of light. It was not what we wanted, but it really was okay. The advantage: it was very, very quiet. 
 The location of this hotel is excellent, as it is close to the White House and the Mall. The bed was fine, and we had a choice of pillows. Our bathroom included a stall shower as well as a tub. This hotel prides itself on being welcoming and friendly, and we found that to be the case. The concierge gave us great restaurant recommendations and finagled better times than we were able to get otherwise. (I recommend Occidental Bar and Grill at the Willard--though pricey; Filomena in Georgetown--though painfully noisy)
 The one downside was that there seemed to be little awareness of how to get around-eat-etc on a less that bloated budget. To get to Georgetown? A cab was recommended. By walking just a short two blocks, we were able to catch a Circulator bus that charged only $- and dropped us almost in front of the restaurant we wanted. We overheard a staff member telling someone there was no coffee-breakfast place other than Sofitel's restaurant and Starbucks nearby. But by walking those same two short blocks, the guest could have found - other coffee places, one of which was the Corner Bakery, a great place for coffee or breakfast.
 On the whole, I liked this hotel and would stay there again.

The Casablanca is a bit more expensive than other Times Square hotels, but the difference is worth it for several reasons: -) this isn't one of the huge hotels around the square with hundreds of rooms -- maybe just a few dozen. This means no wait for elevators or anything else -- and if you need the staff's attention you'll get it quickly because there are not many other guests; -) the place is quieter -- physically; and -) it feels quieter -- the evening reception in the lounge was like a room in a nice old club: calm, relaxing and elegant; -) the rooms are big by NYC and Times square standards and are rather well-appointed and in good condition. You're also just steps -- maybe -- yards? from Times Square. All in all, a great small hotel.

I booked this hotel based on past tripadvisor reviews and was not disappointed. The hotel is in the middle of everything but still tucked away. Thr htrl to beautiful, the staff was nice and now i have a new favorite. I have stayed at tons of Chicago hotels and even of the chian hotels like the W or the Sofitel, I liked the Amalfi best. It is upscale without being stuffy. I will be back again and recommend it highly for anyone else.

I was looking for a downtown hotel for a one night stay and got this for $-- on priceline. Some of the reviews were a bit off-putting but I have mostly found to take reviews with a grain of salt. Our stay was a great, positive surprise.
The valet, desk staff and bell service were all professional, courteous and efficient. We were not surprised by the cost of valet- I always look when staying in a dowtown area- and found it competitive for the area. Our bellman was quite congenial, joking and informative.
The king room itself was very comfortable and clean with a nice size bathroom. The bed was so comfortable with nice linens and pillows. I like the way Hyatt is designing their rooms with simple sleek lines now days. The room was very quiet despite all rooms facing out toward the tower atrium.
We had a couple of beers in the bar before hiking over to Minute Maid ballpark for an Astros-Dodgers game. Typical hotel prices, nice bar mix for snack and some little happy hour food at - pm. Service was quick and professional.
Location of the hotel is good- easy access to the metro rail line and several good bars and restaurants within walking distance- not the closest to the ballpark but we always felt safe. There's a lot more to do downtown than our last visit -- years ago. It isn't a New York city kind of lively but plenty to eat and drink while walking to the ballgame.

I booked this hotel for a birthday trip to New York for my mother. We had a girls shopping weekend and hence why we choose the location and hotel. 
Room: Loved my room it was immaculate, exactly like it was shown in the photos and could spend days in the big comfy bed. The bathroom was gorgeous and you even get a foot bath for your tired feet after a long days shopping. 
Service: I can not fault the service. We tended to pop in and out of the hotel a lot, to off load shopping bags. The door men found this hilarious and would shout their clothes size at us when we left to go back out again and wished us a good shopping trip, which always made us giggle. Every single member of staff we encountered was friendly, helpful and very welcoming. 
Location: If you are going for a shopping break like us it is an excellent location. Only a few blocks away from Macy’s and two blocks down from all the lovely shops on -th avenue. 
Money saving tip: I always look for a bargain and when I went hunting for the room I found it better to book directly with the hotel. The cost of the room can fluctuate from one week to another. If you book at a high rate and call the next week and find the cost has reduce the hotel will amend the cost on your booking. We saved a fortune by doing this.

I was attending a business conference in New York City near Penn Station and selected the Eventi because of its proximity to the event and based on my prior good experience with Kimpton hotels in other cities. I was not disappointed in my choice of the Eventi. Its style is modern both in the rooms and the lobby. My room was above average size for New York City and the bathroom was particularly so. The service was very professional without being cloying. The price was high but on par with other midtown hotels. I will definitely consider staying at the Eventi again both for business and for pleasure.

The location is fine and so is the service. The breakfast is terrible, but the room is very comfortable. All the room decoration and the bathroom is very old-fashioned also.
But if you don't care for all that and you are only looking for bed to sleep, then this hotel might suit you nicely.

We had a great cruise, but arrived in San Diego to find AA had canceled all Chicago flights, so we rebooked for - days later. Of course, at that point, we were homeless in San Diego. Taking a hint from fellow cruisers, who had a pre-cruise stay here, we called. Lovely Monica confirmed our room, gave us a AAA rate, and dispatched the courtesy van to retrieve us from the cruise ship terminal. We felt so lucky.
 The luck continued. It was a short trip back to Hotel-motel.Van drivers told us lots to do. We arrived, bags promptly arrived. Our room was on the -th level, we watched the cruise ship pull out of port on its weekly rounds of the Mexican coast. Room was large, dark mediterranean-style furniture, sleeping area set off by a half wall from couch. Wooden shutters on windows. Plenty of towels, bath products, lots of room for all the bags. Secure, efficient, clean property with very helpful staff.
 Pretty grounds are enclosed by security gates. Units of rooms are set into hillside. Lots and lots of steps, but elevators available. Enough palms to make setting feel tropical. Room service and restaurant on site. Saw pool, too cold to use this time.
 Great location. Downhill trek to Zocalos-very good, Coyote Cafe, fine for lunch or margaritas, Living Room Cafe for coffee, Cold Stone Creamery, and a super locally brewed rootbeer stand-try it! Historic old town was a good walk, flea market on Sat. afternoon, lots of sidewalk cafes... Next day van dropped us off at Midway Museum. We had a stellar day there, followed by dinner at the Fish Market, good for fresh catch. 
 Obliging van took us back to the airport and off we went and here we are in snowy Chicago once again!
The Madison is a very nice hotel in downtown Memphis within walking distance of all downtown activities. The service quality varies day by day.

We stayed here at the end of our honeymoon for - days in May ----. The hotel is clean and comfortable. My first impressions were of it being rather dark in its decor and could have done with a lighter feel through the corridors and rooms. But as a base for seeing the sites and city it was a good hotel. The staff were friendly and helpful

Wife and I stayed for - nights at the hotel in September and had a great time. Located across from Grant Park where you can cross to get to Lake Michigan or go north to the Navy Pier. A short walk up Michigan avenue and you were at the beginning of the Magnificent Mile. We did not eat at the Hotel as there is so much great food in Chicago. The rooms were very nice...ours overlooked the park.

Wonderful stay! They treated our children so nice! They even sent complimentary milk & cookies for the kids after we arrived and also accommodated an early (-am) check in! Literally walking distance from everywhere!! Would stay again.

I've stayed at the Hilton Times Square a few times but my most recent stay was the best yet. I had an upgraded room on the --th floor and the views are just spectacular. There are no obstrcutions for South-facing rooms so you just have an incredible view of the city. 
The hotel has nicely updated rooms that are a very nice size. The beds are extremely comfortable and everything is very modern. My room was very quiet, being on a high floor, with almost no noise from the streets below. 
The restaurant is good, but expensive, especially compared to all the options you have within a few minute walk. I like the fact that there's a lobby bar as well. It's small but it's just great to have a spot to grab a drink before heading out. Drinks aren't cheap but it's really convenient.
The location of the hotel is good and bad. It's a great spot if you're up for dealing with the insane crowds around Times Square. The sidewalks near the hotel are simply packed. For kids (of any age) Dave & Buster's is right next door as is Madame Tussauds. However, that also means lots of pushing through the crowds. The --nd St subway station is also right there so it's a breeze to get away from Times Square quickly. 
I'd definitely recommend it to anyone that wants a central home base while in NYC with great rooms, views and beds. As long as you can deal with the crowds everytime you walk out the door. One simple way to avoid that is to head out the south door onto --st.

drove through the night after booking an early check-in and being guaranteed it the night before by a staff member. Arrived at - to two staff members saying we would have to maybe wait - hours for a room to be ready for the normal check in. Was not offered a SINGLE thing to make our stay more comfortable or to accommodate us a little bit early. 
How is a hotel booked to ---% when three hotels in the nearby area have plenty of rooms just from a cursory walk around the hotels in the area? 
How is a hotel with hundreds of rooms in a metropolitan area not able to find a place within - hours for a tired traveller? 
Mystifying and engaging.

This is a great hotel locatd in the heart of Time Square. We had a king size suite on the --th floor and it was great.
Upon entering the hotel you have to take an elevator to the -rd floor first where the hotel lobby is located, from there, you take another elevator to your hotel room. You must show your room key to enter the hotel which is pretty good security.
The suite was spacious and had a double entery to the washroom, a kitchen sink, microwave and mini fridge. The bed was very comfortable with lots of pillows. There was an LCD TV in both the living room and bedroom with lots of channells. There is no free internet in the room, but you get free internet in the hotel lobby.
As a guest of the hotel you can park you car on --th St right next to the hotel for $---day which is a valet parking with no in-out previlges. This is a great deal for Manhattan parking.
Overall I was pleasantly happy with the hotel, the location was great, the room was clean and had all amenities, the front desk staff were very friendly and the concierge was great. I will most likely stay at this hotel again.

This hotel, is on the whole pretty tatty looking. Its for lovers of Art or those who grieve the historical pasing of an age that their birthdate means they can never be part of. 
First impressions are of quirky characters in the lobby area juxtaposed by chelsea go getters with lap tops and art pieces on every available wall or surface, and just the promise of a ghost of a departed, tortured artist. Its about mis matched furniture from antique shops and high sheen and boutique finish is a million miles away. All that said and done, elements of the bohemian past, art pieces and tortured artistic souls could still be kept following an extensive refurbishment. Our room (---) had a balcony on the same level as the famous sign and the room was large but cosy with a small tatty kitchenette (complete with mouse trap), walk in closet and very tired looking bathroom in pink and black tiles complete with a sink that had been repainted at some point and was now looking worse than ever. However, I liked the room immensley. 
The famous wrought iron stairs are beautiful and the paintings (good, bad and indifferent) on the walls brighten the hallway up and lend to the artistic feel of the place. 
The hotel is in a prime location in Chelsea and for those who want to soak up something other than an impersonal hotel then I'm sure you'd love it. For no reason other than the fact I've now stayed there - and paid well for the privelege - I probably wouldn't stay there again when there are millions of other hotels and areas in New York but I urge others who haven't to give it a try with an open mind as I'm sure that in years to come you'll remember your stay.

I got """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""walked"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" by other hotel in the area, that is why I stayed in this hotel. I hear so many things about this brand before, they talked about """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""unique"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotels, this hotel is far from it, the room decor is just not for everybody. No LCD flat screen TV
The personnel in the front desk is just not friendly, when you ckeck in they just don´t look to you in the eye and neverless smile to you.
There was no internet service, they said they fix it but never did.
The worst part of it is the neatness of the rooms and the whole hotel. In the shower I saw hairs and shaving cream with hair parts in the shower, that was nasty. I did not shave during my one night stay.
When you walk through the parking lot you can see neatness (cleanness) is not a priority for this hotel.
My only recomendation there are alot more hotels around this area you should other options.

I absolutely loved my stay at the Doubletree. I was there for three nights in a one bedroom suite. The bed was extremely comfortable (which is very important to me on vacation) . The room was clean and well maintained. And the view from the hotel window was amazing (it really helps if you love the city like I do). Also, the hotel is located in a convenient area for going to shows, etc. 
One of the hotel staff members knew that I was there to celebrate my birthday, so when I arrived in my room, there was a fruit and cheese tray waiting for me. Overall, very pleasant and calm stay in a busy city.

Overall decent experience, but found several things disappointing. The staff were all friendly and helpful, some rooms have wireless internet access, the bed was comfortable. The hotel is interestingly decorated w- period pieces (esp the lobby area). In our room, the only mirror you could use without crouching down was in the closet! The bathroom mirror was very low due to the funny shape of the roof. There's no fan in the bathroom, so the paint was peeling in multiple places and the toilet holder was falling out of the wall. 
 Be aware the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""deluxe"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" continental breakfast described on their site had the usual coffee, juice, breads, and cereal. The deluxe part consisted of a plate of hard boiled eggs and a plate of sausage patties under heat lamps. The eggs and patties never varied the whole week we were there and it got a bit boring. Also the the breads were not very fresh, probably bought at a warehouse club.

My husband and I Love to stay at this small friendly hotel in soho. The location is perfect for walking, great restaurants and so convenient to the subway for getting to midtown. The hotel staff is extremely friendly and accommodating. They seem to know all their guests and call you by name! The rooms are immaculate...but small. Shower has a great shower head with great pressure and the bathroom is a decent size. The only reason I gave - stars VS - is because of the room size....but when in NYC you should not be spending time in your room! So much to see and do!

I stayed here with my teenage daughter for a fun girls trip to New York City. We arrived early at about --:-- am after catching a red eye and they allowed us to store our bags with them and our room was ready by --:-- am. In the meantime they allowed us to have a bite to eat at their free continental breakfast. The staff was very pleasant throughout our stay and helped direct us to certain places and with the subway system. The room was clean and quiet, not a great view (of the alley) but that wasn't a problem. The best part of the hotel is the location, within -- min walking distance to pretty much every must see in New York including Central Park, Broadway, Times Square, Rockafeller Center, MOMA and much much more! Overall a great hotel and I would recommend to others and stay again.

A great hotel in an excellent location (just take a look on 'Google Earth' for the location). 
We settled on this hotel in midtown Manhattan after reading many good reviews, and I'm happy to say we weren't disappointed. 
This would have been a good hotel in any event, but the staff are what make the Affinia a great hotel. The front-of-house staff (Garnet behind the desk, and Donald the doorman in particular) are incredibly helpful - even spending an hour or more on the phone helping track down missing tour tickets. 
The room was clean, well furnished and VERY comfortable. Don't worry that a booking here will be 'room only' as there are many good places to eat within a minute or two of the front door. The Murray Hill Diner (on next block) provides outstanding breakfasts, and The Barking Dog restaurant and bar (next door to the hotel) is perfect for lunch or an evening meal if you don't want to go further afield. If you have a room with a kitchenette - the Murray Hill deli has everything you need or want (including Ben and Jerrys ice-cream and more besides!!!)
We have no hesitation in recommending this hotel and have already booked a return trip in September!

Friendly staff and good breakfast as you would expect to find at a Hampton Inn. Room was comfortable but air conditioner made excessive noise. For the price, a decent place to stay but I've certainly been to better maintained Hampton Inns. Location is just off route -A and Monument Road so convenient to airport, Mayport, etc.

I brought my family to Chicago in June to celebrate a special occasion. We chose to stay at the Conrad because my husband and I are Hilton Honors members and we were able to use honors points for part of our stay. (There were -- of us and I booked five rooms.) 
After we checked in, I realized that the double bedded room I had thought would accommodate four people only contained double beds (not queens) and two of the occupants felt their bed would not be big enough for them. When I asked for an additional (sixth) room, I was told the hotel was completely booked but they would try to find us something. The front desk staff were just as nice as they could be and, after considerable computer searching and telephone calling, they did indeed manage to find us a lovely room with a king sized bed--and at a reasonable price! Of course, my guests were thrilled and so was I.
But the wonderful service didn't end there. We needed to eat dinner in the hotel one night but some of the members of my party had dietary restrictions that prevented them from eating the food in the hotel. I was obliged to order special kosher food for them from a deli in Skokie and have it delivered. I called ahead to the hotel and the restaurant staff arranged to have the deli delivery accepted and stored in their refrigerators (before we arrived). When it came time to have dinner, most of us ordered from the restaurant menu and the restaurant heated the packaged kosher food and delivered it to the table along with what the rest of us had ordered. It must have been a considerable incovenience for them but they were enormously accommodating and handled it beautifully.
As for the hotel itself, the rooms are large and comfortable and the bathrooms quite adequate. The hotel is very well located. It's about a five---- minute walk to Michigan Avenue. The Navy Pier free shuttle stops just across the street. The hotel restaurant offers a modest but adequate breakfast selection. However, at $----$-- per person, you might want to check out one of the nearby restaurants. There are tons of restaurants within easy walking distance. Chicago's well known Uno and Due pizza restaurants are only a couple of blocks away. 
Everyone in my party had a wonderful time in Chicago and I feel the Conrad played a great part in our enjoyment. I would certainly stay there again.

My wife and I stayed at the Affinia for - nights. We used their website to book the trip, they had a pricing guarantee and an option to upgrade for $- per night. We got a Junior Suite. The room was very good size and very clean. Bed was comfortable. Pros: location, location, location; just a block off Michigan Ave. Excellent concierge service especially from Joel. Cons: Ambulance sirens sound (located across from hospital and only - elevators serving our floor was slow a couple of times - nothing serious. A short cab ride to the Apollo theater where we saw Million Dollar Quartet - highly recommend. Also, visited a pub called Timothy O'Tooles a few blocks from the hotel, good food and a great place to watch the football games. Would definitely stay here again.

I always do plenty of research before choosing a hotel. In all my other reviews I like to share as much of the good and bad as I can, so that you can all have a fair opinion of whether you should part with your hard earned cash!
Finding this hotel was dead easy; we got a bus from Newark airport which took us to the Port Authority bus terminal which was less than - mins walk to the hotel. It’s on the opposite side of the street to the Intercontinental Hotel; you can see it as it has a blue light shining onto the front of the building.
Check in was very quick and friendly. They even gave us both a chocolate chip biscuit when we arrived! Our room was --- - when I booked I emailed for a higher floor as had read in reviews that it could be noisy at nights or mornings.
Room:
Clean and a decent size considering the location. We had a double bed, bathroom with good shower, flat screen TV and table. There was a room safe under the table on the ground which you could use easily. The bed was very comfortable and there were - small pillows on the bed.
Breakfast:
Free breakfast was available every day which was a nice touch. They had a waffle maker which was easy to use once shown! They had chocolate and plain waffles, fruit and pastries. They also had bagels, toast and juices-hot chocolate, coffee and tea. The sausages and eggs were a little dodgy, I think they were fake eggs and the bacon and sausages seemed a little strange tasting… but this is a minor issue as the waffles were brilliant and the bagels and juice were more than enough to fill me up for long days of sightseeing!
Location:
The location was brilliant. There was a subway station on our street and you were able to be in the middle of Times Square in - mins easily. The bus terminal was close if you wanted to go to Jersey Gardens to shop or get airport connections. Every tourist spot was within walking distance as well. 
This was a major selling point in us choosing this hotel which was helped by everything else being really good.
Other things:
There is free internet and printing at the front by reception as well and stands with loads of free information and maps for you to take to help you get around the city. The location is in a safe area, and not once did we feel in danger or worried at any time of the day.
The breakfast gets a little busy after ---am, but it goes until --:--am on weekends and -:-- on weekdays. 
There was noise late nights and early mornings outside the hotel. But the hotel cannot control this and I hardly noticed it. But remember, it is a busy city! We didn't hear cars at night though.
Check out was quick and easy, and they can hold onto your luggage for you until you need it. Check out is at --am. 
Would I go back? Absolutely! This hotel is a wee gem in a fantastic city. It ticks all the boxes and cannot be beaten in terms of location. It’s neither fancy nor - star – but it doesn’t need to be. I’ve stayed in hotels all over Europe and across the world and this is exactly what a hotel should be in such a touristy city.

We stayed at the Triton for a week over Christmas and had an amazing holiday in San Francisco. The hotel location is perfect. A - minute walk to Union Square, Macy's and a - minute walk to shops that we loved like H&M, Banana Republic and there's even a Starbucks across the street. The staff are so helpful and can recommend anything. We would definitley recommend doing an open top bus tour if it is your first time in San Francisco. The room was small but very cosy with a great tv that had lots of channels and the shower was very good also. We stayed over Christmas and it was very different to the one we have in Australia but it was still lovely. The gym was very nice too, it was open -- hours. They also have fresh baked cookies at reception every evening and they are so delicious! The whole family loved the Triton and we can't wait to stay there again!

The decor is a little dated. The hotel was built in the --'s could use a re-fresh. Staff is helpful and the restaurant was good. 
I would stay here again as long as I got a good rate.

This motel is very close to Market Square and trolleys stops. It has been decorated in a sort of euro modern style. Disappointed that it did not have a dresser. Area around it attracks a lot of day laborers looking for work in the mornings but we has absolutely no problems with anyone. For the location the price is great.

Upon arrival at --:-- AM, I was very pleased that they had a room available for me. The doormen and registration desk both had nice, well mannered people. The hotel is very dark inside. Coming from the bright outside requires a couple of minutes of adjustment because it is so dark. The lobby is nicely appointed and leads to the beautifl Redwood Room, which I didn't visit on this stay. The hotel is t-wo blocks fr-om Union Square and very convenient. There is a Hertz car retal on the same block for those who need a car. Parking is close to $-- per day. 
The elevators were fast, but again, very dark. It makes the W hotel in midtown NY look well lighted. The room was sparce. It doen't have a coffee maker, but did have a mini bar. The bed was comfortable and it wasn't difficult to control the room temperature. 
The bathroom was not ideal. It was very outdated. The bathtub had serious chips in it and the water pressure was pathetic. The toilet lid was loose too. The sink was very small but they at least provided a small shelf for essentials. 
The cost of the room was $---. While affordable, i wouldn't stay here again. There are other hotels in the areas for a few more $$ that are more modern and also centrally located.

It is a traditional motel better than average. Good location, near Golden Gate and many restaurants. Free breakfast is a big plus.
One suggestion, we rent a car drive from airport to La Luna following GPS. It is a heavy rain night. There is a NO LEFT TURN sign when arrived the other side of the street near La luna. The sign works only -am---am--pm--pm. But since the rain is too heavy, I didn't see the time restriction. Then I drives directly to Golden gate, paid - dollar in the toll without viewing any beautiful view. It tooks half an hour to the Shopping street (Market St.) since the traffic is always busy. 
As other reviews mentioned, wifi is terrible (not stable, always drop and need to connect again), I am glad I only stay there for one night.

The Embassy Suites was a - star experience! I have stayed at the other local hotels (Marriott, Ashton, Hilton, Sheraton) and this was the BEST option, in addition to being just all around a great place to stay. 
In addition to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""normal"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" benefits of an Embassy Suites - this one offered an exceptional happy hour with an appetizer buffet. The fitness facility was amazing. The pool was tiny, but great for a quick refreshing dip or -- minutes in the hot tub. Starbucks in the lobby, and the front desk even had warm cookies for a snack!
The room was modern and very appealing with the decor, and of course the sleep quality of the bed and quiet of the room was excellent.
I will stay here whenever I return to Fort Worth. Excellent!

I got a deal on this hotel on Hotwire, only $---night. The location was wonderful, a $-- cab ride from the airport, on the quiet end of the Riverwalk, but close to everything we wanted to walk to. The staff were all amazingly nice and helpful, and the room was beautiful. My husband disliked the double doors on the bathroom, but that was really the only problem we had in the room. Our room on the --th floor was ready when we wanted to check in before -- am, and the view of the Rivwerwalk was lovely.
The lunch buffet was exceptional, especially compared to the prices charged for mediocre food elsewhere in the area. The breakfast buffet was a good deal. The bartenders were great about fixing a drink that was made poorly, and the restaurant staff all remembered our preferences through the weekend.
Be aware they do offer wireless internet, but it costs $---day.

We visited San Antonio and had a wonderful time. Our hotel room was very neat and clean. The staff was cheerful and very accomodating. The breakfast was excellent. I recommend Hampton Inn Riverwalk. I would like to visit again.

This was by far the most disappointing stay at this hotel we have ever had and we have stayed here several times in the past. To avoid the tiny standard room we've had in the past, we reserved a superior room--allegedly larger. The reservation was made a month ago. Not only was this room possibly even smaller than a standard, it was dark and dreary so that even with the lamps on it was hard to read anything. n We could barely move past each other when trying to move around. I requested a king, was told we had a queen but it was really a full size bed. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone and will not stay there again.

This hotel is a former Holiday Inn and completely renovated in European Style. Decor is the latest Brown-Blue suede with outstanding comfortable beds and pillows. Extremely well appointed with nice touches such as a plush terry cloth shower curtain and monogrammed towels. The latest style of faucets have been put in. Because the hotel is so conveniently located off the freeway at Sunset Blvd. you will get freeway noise on that side - turn on the air conditioning unit in the summer and you would never know. The hotel is circular and at the top is a fine dining restaurant with a nicely appointed bar. Great views of the Getty Museum and of UCLA and Westwood. Just up the street slip into the Hotel Bel Air for a drink without having to pay the price of their rooms. Extremely convenient for any business traveler into the West LA region and certainly acceptable for the vacation traveler also.

I've stayed at Homewood Suites before in a few cities, but this one was exceptionally nice. Perhaps it's new and everything just looks better new. The kitchen area was very spacious and I especially like the stools where you eat at the kitchen area. The decor throughout the hotel and rooms were very chic and modern. The LCD-HD TV in the bedroom and living room is a big plus! I really did feel like a big city hotel. 
The hotel was difficult to find at first due to location on the turn-about and the parking is convenient once you find out how to get there. 
The usual breakfast and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""small"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" dinner is included. Dinner everyday is different depending on the menu. The servers there are always very friendly and accomodating. 
The MAC gym (independent gym connected to hotel) is amazing!!! Salt water swimming pool, -- cardio machines with LCD screens, - raquetball courts and the equipments are all new. It's has a very comfortable feel to it. However, it can get a bit crowded afterwork, but there were always machines available.
If you want a good restaurant. Moe's Crab & Pasta House (not ssure if that is correct name), a block away from the hotel is really, really good. It looks a little shabby with some of the sign lights out. I had the best crab cakes and pasta there.

I have stayed at this hotel more than any other hotel in the world. For a while it was my home away from home in chicago, before i moved there. As a diamond member its great! Great! Great! Enjoyed our stay. Service excellent. Breakfast enormous. Love the location. Central Park walking distance, -th Avenue a block away, great bistro Rue -- across the street and up one block. Only problem was no free wi-fi and wi-fi charges were really expensive.

Stayed at the San Diego Marriott Gaslamp Quarter hotel over a weekend in June ----. It's a fine hotel but nothing out of the ordinary for a Marriott. Our reservation included the breakfast buffet, which was excellent, as was the service. We also ate dinner there on our last evening (a Sunday) when the restaurant was dead. There was only one other party seated at the same time.

There are tons of options but there were a lot of drunk people as well as pretty aggressive homeless people around. I never felt unsafe but some people may be very uncomfortable staying in this part of town.
I had combined a stay at the Marriott with one at the Del Coronado across the Coronado bridge. Nothing against Marriott, but for the extra $-- a night I wished I had just stayed at the Del.

My wife and I stayed at this hotel for the Easter weekend. The hotel is in a great downtown location, close to things. Excellent service, highly recommended. Great location in downtown Seattle. Easy walking distance to quality dining, not far from the Space Needle. It was a business trip but still had a great time and enjoyed my stay at the Monaco.

This is essentially a decent hotel situated in the Indianapolis city center, right around the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""circle""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""; thus making it a good location if you have business downtown or with anyone in the Government as the Capital is right there. The staff is uniformly polite and courteous. There are several eating options around the hotel within walking distance. Overall, it is a good value for money for a short stay.
We stayed here for one night in the first week of September.
very nice hotel and great location. we didn't love the beds (they were just replacing them...) and there was a bit of a noise late at night in the corridor. other than that it's a great choice.

I would like to state that the rooms are lovely. There is a seperate sitting area with a sofa and a smaller flat screen TV. (I believe it was built into the wall). Nice touch. I was in L.A on a business trip and had no choice but to stay at this motel because of my jobs financial reasons. Well turns out room --- were I stayed comes with infestation! This hotel as THE best bartender in any hotel of anywhere I've ever stayed. Stayed for - nights in March --. Upon arrival after lengthy flight, advised after standing in massive queue that room is located in another building only a short walk away but not assistance with luggage can be provided. Enjoyed what was unfortunately only a one night stay on a business trip. However, the hotel is an excellent location for the visitor being only minutes from the White House and the Mall. The rooms are a good size and very well appointed. I would definitely return for a longer visit.

My wife and I spent a week visiting Chicago, in a deluxe suite Room ----, in part based on the excellent reviews on Tripadvisor. The Elysian lived up to those reviews and provided one of the best lodging experiences we have ever enjoyed. We have had the good fortune to stay in some of the finest hotels in our travels. Places like the St. Regis in NYC and the Saint James in Montreal. The Elysian ranks with those kind of properties but provides a contemporary environment.
The hotel's features are well documented in other reviews so I won't repeat them here. The design of the rooms and the amenites are absolutely first class and the small balcony was a welcome feature.
The really impressive thing about the Elysian is the hotel staff. We often read about the quality of hotel staff in reviews and it is usually hard to quantify. Not so at the Elysian. The amazing thing at this hotel is that the staff is largely young adults. The management and owners have clearly developed a training and hiring system that selects extremely well educated and personable individuals. More importantly, the hotel then trains them extensively resulting in the most friendly, helpful, and efficient staff possible. It is a rare thing these days to find an organization that values the quality of it's employees so highly. It is an old fashioned approach to success that is as important as the quality of the product.
The impressive thing about the Elysian is not tv's in mirrors or the no tipping policy. The reason we would return again in a heartbeat is that the ownership and top management have a plan, a very good plan, for delivering great hospitality, in a first class physical plant, employing state of the art design, all based on a foundation of extremely well trained and selected staff.

My family spend - days of our Spring Break at the Squaw Peak Resort. We really enjoyed the Resort. The Water Park opened at -am which is good for those of us that are early risers. It was well maintained and the staff was courteous. I enjoyed playing Lookout Mountain and my sons played the Miniature Golf Course --+ times. The Hole in the Wall staff was nice enough to change their TV's so we could watch the NCAA games on Saturday night; Aunt Chilada's did the same on Monday.
My only complaint would be that we checked in extremely late and were given a Single King Suite instead of a Double Queen Suite. I was told there were no more available but that I would be contacted the next day about changing rooms. I never got a call although when I called the Lobby late in the afternoon they did make the room change. I never really got a call to apologize from anyone.
We liked the location as well for hiking Squaw Peak and Camelback, dinner in Carefree, and quick access to the interstate.
We did stay at the Arizona Grand the remaining part of the week. VERY similar set up but I would give the Hilton the slight edge despite the rooms being slightly smaller. The Water Park opened - hours earlier, enjoyed the resort restaurants more, and the grounds were beautiful.

Not much to complain. Average breakfast, good location, small but quiet and fresh room with nice decoration, AC worked etc. Nothing to complain about service either. All wen well and we were happy that we chose Marcel at Gramercy.

Stayed in this hotel for three nights at the beginning of October. The hotel itself is very stylish with a strong theme on design and art, which extend to its rooms.
My room was a nice size with plenty of the usual ammenites that one would expect from a hotel of this rating. 
However a few issues occured-arose. My in room safe was still locked from the previous guest, meaning that a member of the hotels security team had to come and unlock it for me. 
The sinks in the bathrooms do not have any plugs, so if you want to have a quick wash it makes it very difficult to do so. 
The televisions comes on at a ridiculously high volume and the controller is so slow to react if can be about a minute before you have the thing under control. This is something I'm sure neighbouring rooms wouldn't appreciate if you like to watch the news first thing in the morning.
The room my parents were allocated was of similar size but at the rear of the hotel with a nice view of the hotels air conditioning plant. Their room had a mulitude of issues: no safe at all - one had to be fitted, no plug for the sink, no towel rail or hook for the bathroom (holes in the wall where there once had been one, but not replaced) a bedframe too big for the mattress causing many scraped shins and no full length mirror. We figured this room may have had things taken out of it to replace other broken bits in other rooms but never got resolved itself?
To the hotels credit they did sort out the security-safe issues, however they need to check all their rooms have the basics of a shower rail-hook in their bathrooms.
This hotel has a nice location with plenty of easy (but expensive) local parking, however its style makes certain aspects of holidaying here impractical.
If I return to San Diego, which by the way is a lovely city, I doubt very much that I'll be staying here again.

Our family enjoyed a brief stay this holiday weekend at the Lenox Hotel and would not hesitate to return to this charming, old school jewel in the heart of the Back Bay. First, the location is extremely convenient and is located within easy walking distance to the T (Copley). Valet parking with unlimited in-out is available for around ----- dollars daily. (This may sound costly but research of nearby self park garages convinced me this is not much more expensive and WAY more convenient.) I do not exaggerate when I tell you the staff from the valet guys to the doorman to the concierge are amazingly friendly and helpful. Rooms were about the going rate for a nice hotel in town. What the rooms lack in the kind of sleek but bland modernity of newer hotels they totally make up in charm, comfort and size. Our room, a double-double, was spacious, clean and inviting. Bathrooms are small but updated nicely and stocked thoughtfully with luxe Aveda products. Plush robes, comfy beds, free wifi, large flatscreen TV, in room safe, and extras like complementary coffee and tea in the pretty lobby were all part of the Lenox experience. What a lovely place. We did not eat in the on site restaurants (City Table and Solas, as well as City Bar) but appreciated the convenience of having some varied choices onsite. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone who wants to experience both the elegance and gracious service of an earlier time.

Well, other than I could not sleep well at this hotel (nothing to do with the hotel, I think), I would rate it as excellent.
Rooms remind me of the ol MicroTel Inns, where everything is really compact. LIterally - feet around the King bed, and that is it.
Although there is very little room, the room is very well designed, and useful. Every nook has useful space, making it seem larger than it is.
Rooms are clean and I think newly remodeled, or it is a new building, I really could not tell for sure.
Actually, it must be an old building, because the elevators were old. 
Staff was nice, food was good, place was very clean, etc., etc.

I chose this property because of pleasant past stays, location, and good value (points plus cash). It is located on --th between -th and -th.

The bathroom was not too tiny with a walk in shower. There were plenty of towels (including washcloths$, a great hair dryer, and toiletry items included body lotion, shampoo, conditioner, and bar soap.
Priority Club elite recognition: They recognised my status at check in and gave me a welcome bag with a note and package of pretzels.
Amenities:
A complimentary breakfast is served each morning. I did not take advantage of it on this visit.
The property has a fitness centre and business centre on site.
Wifi is complimentary and works pretty well.

Have probably stayed at the Element now at least -- times on Business trips. It's a wonderful place to come back to when away from home. 
Firstly because the rooms are big and airy and so I always felt like I had plenty of space to unwind in the evenings. The rooms are equiped with cookers, a dishwasher, a large TV and a sofa. 
Secondly because the staff are so friendly and the set up is very social. Come back after work Monday - Thursday and there will be a snack and a glass of wine or beer to greet you. (Ok this can get a little unhealthy after a while, if only I possessed some will power to resist!). Plenty of space downstairs and on the patio to socialise in the evenings. And a wii for some additional entertainment. Nice, but small pool and a modern fitness area. 
But perhaps the main thing that made this place stand out to me was the proximity to the shopping area at Vintage Parkway with Starbucks, Multiple restuarants and a supermarket. Most of the places I have stayed in Houston before you cannot get anywhere without a car, but here it is possible to walk over to the restuarants in the evening or to the supermarket. It makes being away from home for long periods seem far less clostrophobic.

This was our second stay at the Catamaran, first time being in ----. Stayed in the tower both times. This time was a last minute spring break booking that we found on Expedia for a pretty good deal which explains why our room faced the top floor of the parking structure. Last time it was on a high floor w- a bay view and room much larger - fancier bath but we did pay more. But hey - we were not there to stay in our room the whole time anyway. 
I must say after reading the recent reviews I was expecting to find the decor outdated and in need of a refurbish but our room was simple yet elegant fitting the Polynesian style of carved woods in the headboard and dresser. Very clean as well. I can only speak of the tower room though.
The pool area was smallish but nice w- the water heated to around -- degrees and hot tub was nicely heated - can't stand lukewarm hot tubs! There was a bartender in the afternoons and the arcade is there as well. Some of the games are beaten up but hey, they're free play.
I've eaten at the Atoll on site for their brunch in the past and it's excellent, but for other local food nearby, the Green Flash on Thomas is great for breakfast. Rubio's fish tacos are wonderful (they may sound weird but you won't regret trying). The fishery was nice on Cass St. for a fancier seafood dinner. Pho Sao Bien on Garnet was pretty good for Vietnamese Noodles. Santana's was also pretty good Mexican fast food.
I chose this resort for its balance of location and value (close to beach on ocean side and quieter Bay Side. Some of the other family type resorts are very isolated if you're looking to do - eat other stuff than what's on the resort itself. Would go there again.

We picked this hotel for its great location and because we like small, service-oriented luxury boutique hotels (e.g. International House in D.C., Madison Hotel in Memphis, etc). 
At the Time, our King room was small (to be expected) but nice. Front desk staff was polished and helpful, but the rest of the staff was pretty rough around the edges. They didn't have the level of formailty and courtesy we typically expect at hotels like this. Pulling off the breakfast was too much for the poorly trained staff, who let the coffee pots sit empty for long periods of time while they relentlessly asked people for their room number.
All in all, we did enjoy our stay. The location is right in the middle of all the Broadway theaters and the rooms were quiet and well equipped. The service level wasn't top notch, but pretty much what we expected for the very attractive price.

Except for the snotty desk clerk who seemed to think that we should know where the nearest subway station was (despite the fact that we had just checked in at night) and the billing error, we would rate this hotel --- otherwise.

I was most disappointed with my stay at this hotel.

Finding a reasonably priced accommodation in NY is becoming a challenging task. This one is quite poorly located, and not very well maintained. Our room was renovated last when Kurt Waldheim was Secretary General. Yet, the reasonable price still makes it attractive. Expect a bed, a shower and not much more.

We stayed at this hotel for - nights and overall we were happy with our stay. 
The location is perfect, right in the centre of Times Square and it is close to the majority of the attractions. 
The hotel itself is huge, we were upgraded to a Times Square view room as it was my husbands birthday which was fantastic. The room itself was massive and the bed was extremely comfortable. I am allergic to feathers and the hotel noted this and made sure the room was feather free. You are able to request a fridge through concierge and I emailed them ahead of time and the fridge was there when we arrived! 
The Internet is a joke, they charge you $--.-- a day and you can barely get a signal. We tried the free lobby wifi which was billed to our room and when we queried this the lady at check in was extremely rude. She took the charge off the room but basically said if it happens again they will not remove the charge. They have the most ridiculous system where it does not tell you, you are being charged when you log in. 
some staff were all about tips, they expected a tip when the man gave you a ticket for your bag, then the man who brought your bag down to the ground floor wanted a tip and then the man who put them in the taxi wanted a tip and got quite aggressive when he didn't get one. Honestly it was beyond the joke! 
We didn't try the breakfast but juniors is across the road (give that a miss) and head onto --th street for some fantastic cheap bagels! 
The soundproofing from the windows was fantastic as you could not hear anything from outside, unfortunately the same could not be said for the interconnecting rooms as we had very loud neighbours singing for most of the night! 
Overall the hotel itself was clean, perfect location and lovely rooms. The real downside are the staff and the Internet!

Stayed the weekend. The staff was efficient , room clean and price fair. The exercise room and the pool are nice. The hotel is in the middle of everything. Everything you want ot do is in walking distance.

how could this place ever get - stars no bar no restaurant no fridge. 
The rtoom appeared clean until you opened the curtains where there were layers of dust and we did not dare turn on the air con as it was solid with dust.
To be fair staff were friendly and the location was good on the front and quiet but for nearly $--- a night I felt it was a complete rip off!

My wife and I stayed - nights at the Park Hyatt Bellevue in late July for a business conference. The overall experience was above average but I question whether the hotel rates a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""- star"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" as indicated. 
I disagree with one reviewer who said it was easy to find - the entrance for the hotel is not well-marked and is actually on a side street. The hotel is unique in that the lobby is on an upper floor with only a small entry area on floor level. The lobby is also small but I found this appealing.
The real strength of the hotel is its excellent customer service. The staff is friendly and does an impressive job such as actually remembering your names. The check-in clerk walked us to the elevator and highlighted aspects of the hotel- a nice touch. Later we asked about seeing a suite and were personally shown two suites with no pressure. The room service was very timely and the housekeeping was excellent. The concierge always provided helpful advice.
The other positive about the hotel is the older architecture which is most noteworthy in the rooms. Some will like this, others won't. Travelers who like modern hotels should stay at another place. I thought the room had character and our room had been well maintained. 
I liked that the business center provided free internet access. The hotel obviously has a great downtown location and we felt the price was reasonable for the low ---'s per night.
The negatives were a fairly slow elevator and I did not like having to share the exercise facility with half of downtown Philly as the facility is actually open to the public.

In fairness, this hotel is inexpensive by NYC standards, and it is clean and well decorated. The staff is friendly and polite. It is a Club Quarter hotel, which means that the rooms are tiny and the showers are little more than a drain in the bathroom floor (water will get EVERYWHERE in the bathroom after the shower). I would have recommended this hotel had it not been for the obnoxious occupant of the suite next door to my room, and the relative lack of concern by the hotel staff. Apparently, according to the staff, this occupant is living at this hotel for three months, in a corporate suite. Somehow this justified her late night parties with friends, banging on the walls, shrieking and talking loudly (the walls are paper thin) well after midnight. This happened two nights in a row. The first night, I called management who promptly asked her to quiet down. She did not. I called a second time, and management asked her again to quiet down. She did not. I finally got dressed and went down to the lobby in person (about - a.m.?) and the staff on duty apologized and offered to move me to another room. Luckily, my noisy neighbor finally agreed to end her party. Unfortunately she was at it again the second night, requiring me to get management involved again. I was pleased that the hotel staff was apologetic, but a bit disturbed when they defended my neighbor's actions (""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""she's young""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""; """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""she hasn't seen her friends in a long time""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""; """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""this is her first time in New York""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""...). And had I known that I would be subjected to TWO sleepless nights in a row, I would have agreed to move rooms the first night. As it was, no one offered me a refund, a free breakfast, a free coffee...nothing. I didn't really feel like a valued customer, after three nights there. I know I won't be back.

The downside is the small dining room - lounge area for breakfast. You can eat in the lounge area but the tables are coffee tables so you have to bend down to eat. But they provide plastic take-away containers and paper coffee cups so you can take your breakfast back to your room or eat on the run if you prefer. Breakfast is buffet style with a couple of hot food options as well as cereal, fruit, toast, bagels, muffins, yoghurt, coffee, tea and juice. The lifts are very slow to arrive in peak times. The laundry facilities are great and are available all hours for guests. There are --- washing machines and driers. Just across the road and up a bit to the right are glass doors that take you into the --nd St-Port Authority complex which has shops, a post office and also access to several subway lines. It's a great way to get to the subway if the weather is bad. The free Sundowner Reception for guests on Tues, Wed and Thurs afternoon is really good. They had wine, beer and soda as well as finger food such as samosas, dim sum, cheese and biscuits. I enjoyed my stay and would recommend Staybridge Suites.

Chancellor Hotel is simply great, clean room, nice breakfast, great value and the people who work there are helpful as well. 
It's maybe ---m from union square, you have nice restaurants within - minutes walking, access to a gym thats pretty good. They do have free internet, although its pretty slow, but for the two of us, this was just a great experience.
One last tip: don't pay for parking, as you can use the rental company parking for free...

I am a Starwood Preferred Guest Platinum member (so I stay with them a lot) and generally a huge fan of their properties, but this one was a real disappointment.
If you want to stay mid-town, the location is fabulous, the decor is nice and modern, the rooms are very small (to be expected given location) but well appointed. The service however was HORRIBLE!
The staff don't seem to care about the guests and many of them seem to be narcissists. They need to be reminded that they are in business to serve their guests!

Rooms could use a little TLC and updating (tube TVs)...but were clean and comfortable. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Breakfast buffet very good. A tip for you...there are rooms that have balconies into the pool area...not so good if you want to sleep in as kids (being kids) were in the pool early doing what kids do. A good choice...if I need to be in that area again I would stay in this hotel. One pet peeve...$-- a day for internet?

We booked on a last minute trip in July and were quite pleased. Grounds are beautiful and the views of Glorietta Bay are amazing. Walking around Shelter Island is a treat for thr whole family. The balcony was a fun spot for our girls and the room was decent size. When basically surrounded by water you cant expect a perfectly fresh room - they would have to remodel continuously. AAA scored us free parking and we always had a spot by our room. For what we paid and what we got we really had no complaints and would stay here again!

We stayed at this hotel for five nights and loved it, the room was modern great bed and funky furniture, staff very helpful, in great location, found good restaurants in area. My wife was dissapointed with other hotels because this one was so comfortable, great soap too. Would recommend to anyone going to New York.

For $---.-- for one night, including parking, it's not even close to being worth it. The hotel is clean, for the most part, but the room decor is dated and the common areas aren't much better. If I had paid around $---, I wouldn't feel this way - that's about what it's worth on a Saturday night. I didn't research the options in the area as I was in town for a wedding and assumed this was the best option. When I got here, I noticed there were at least two others in close walking distance to the Drury. Shame on me for not poking around more.

my wife, kids and i stayed at the gatehouse inn last week. we wanted to take our kids to the fort rapids waterpark and saw on this website that the hotel wasnt any good...it worked out great staying at the Gatehouse Inn, (fromally an older residence inn).
the fort rapids waterpark was a great way to spend the afternoon, but like the reviews say, the staff there was horrible.
the gatehouse inn on the other hand had great staff. check in was the quickest i have ever had. the hotel had a gate to only let guests park in the lot which made us feel more secure. they offered a huge breakfast that would have cost us over $-- per person if we went out or had to pay...(waffles, eggs, pancakes, even bisquits and gravy).

For the question """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""would I recommend this hotel to a friend"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", right now I would have to say """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""No"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", but this is my first experience in a Denver hotel.

My husband & I spent - nights at this hotel and loved it. The staff were very helpful and informative (Tony and Duane were great!); the location was close to so much shopping and several points of interest; the room was very clean and well laid out; the place was filled with character. On the downside, the area of town is a bit noisy due to several clubs- bars in the vicinity and the rooms don't have air conditioners (which would block out some of that noise.) But if you are someone who likes the nightlife, this hotel puts you in the heart of it at a reasonable rate. 
We would definitely choose this hotel again.

Location is unparalleled, and the hotel has an old-world feel with all of the amenities you would expect. I was upgraded to a great suite on the --st floor - must have been bigger than my house - what a fantastic surprise. Had dinner at Bourbon Steak - the french fries are to die for. I dislike New York...
But in the Chatwal you have a retro and luxury hotel. The bathroom is amezing with the big shower and everything to be to paradis.
And it's to -- seconds to time square... You are in the best place to go on fifth avenue all is near, just walk fews minutes.

Found the Whitcomb to be a great deal (booked on Hotwire). The location is good, the rooms are adequate. Nothing huge, definitely not - star, but anyone complaining about rooms here were probably expecting a bit more. Pretty sure the rate reflects the kind of room you are going to get.
We got a comfortable bed, a roof over our heads, tv, bathroom and decent storage. Wifi is free, parking was $-- per night but standard of a lot of hotels these days. We spent most of our time outdoors exploring the city and our room was a nice, cosy place to rest up when we were done.

Hotel was very updated in a great location near SoHo and Little Italy. Pleasantly Surprised...Cape Cod, Massachusetts,USA 
initially searched for a reasonably priced hotel in NYC with startling results, culminating in our decision to try this shared bath hotel due to its low rate and good customer reviews. We had no problem with our online reservations, which we had confirmed. We found the small lobby charming in an old world way-and a bit dim with dark carved wood work, picture frames and wallpapers. The elevator was a treat, beautifully ornate wood, although can be quite a wait. Since we were on the -th floor, only our -- yr old took the stairs each time. Had a European feel,and in fact, most of the guests were European.The desk person commented that our room (#--- - triple, non-smoking) was particularly nice, so we don't know if its indicative of others. But, we were pleasantly surprised by its decent size, encompassing - double and one twin bed with plenty of room to spare. The mattresses were comfortable, the linens clean, the carpeting appeared newish, the in-room sink a bit cramped in its alcove. We had - large windows offering great views of neighborhood life. We needed to run the air conditioner the whole time, but it never got too cold-so don't know what it would have been like in the room if it was really hot out. Our big fear, the shared bath, was just a minor inconvenience. - rms shared - bath. Using the shower after - am might necessitate a short wait, but all in all, no problems. And as everyone has been saying, the bathrooms were immaculate, bright and newly tiled. Need to remember to bring soap-towel each time, not just for showering... It would be great if management would wall mount antibacterial hand cleaner.It's location was fine if you don't mind some walking. - nice parks nearby, lots of decent,reasonable restaurants. As a family of three, we often took a taxi, costing only a little more than a subway. I would return, although we might check out their sister facility -Hotel ---next time, as some have private baths, and its location may be more convenient. I would recommend this to certain others, as not every one would enjoy its old world charm.

This was perhaps the most impressive low cost hotel I have ever stayed in because I have never felt so welcome. They do so much to make you feel like a valued guest. Really unusual in this day & age. Lots of lovely little gestures and signs in the room to top notch reception and free tea & coffee making facilities (and cookies) during the day at the lobby bar. Word of mouth means so much more than paid advertising and I am telling you.... if you are looking for a low cost hotel right in Chancellor Square then this is it!!! My congratulations and deepest thanks to Staff & Managment.

Because we have family near this hotel, we have stayed their often over a -- year period.. On the last day, I used the business center to try to print out my boarding passes. I brought them up on the computer, but the printer didn't work. When i said that I wanted to contact the owners, she readily gave me my money. 
This is a great location - the hotel should be razed and a new hotel built there.
Good location near Hollywood Blvd. Free parking, breakfast and WLAN not normal in Los Angeles. Very friendly and helpfull staff. Very clean rooms but old furniture (should be replaced a.s.a.p.).

The Independent is in a great location. Easy walks to a variety of restaurants and coffee shops. It is only several blocks to the theater district on Broad Street and to city hall and major shopping. We stayed here on a trip from Australia for my husband's --th birthday, having read many positive reviews on TripAdvisor. If you want to meet the rudest people in North Carolina, stay here. I am not kidding. Someone needs to send these folks to Courtesy school. Not just employees but management too.

My husband and I were on a weekend vacation in NYC and what better way to relax than at the Waldorf Towers! We were greeted with warm welcoming smiles, cheerful conversation and personal attention. We had dinner reservations and tickets to a show, luckily the Towers are so centrally located we were able to enjoy the room for a while before heading out and taking a cab just a short way to our destination. The Waldorf Towers greatly exceeded any expectations we had with their attention to detail, fabulous service and incredible amenities. I would return in a heartbeat, it was like living out a fantasy. I would HIGHLY recommend the Waldorf Towers to anyone, there really is no other way to fully experience the City.

Husband and teenaged son spent - wonderful nights in the Homewood Suites Del Mar in April. Wonderful staff--provided great restaurant recommendations and answered all our questions politely. Perfect hotel! Great choice! Would gladly stay there again!

Comfortable and cozy a small boutique hotel conveniently located in the center of Manhattan so it is east to get to anywhere from the hotel. The shower is beautifully tiled and always replenished with the finest toiletries. The black-out shades give total privacy if you want to have a nap during the daytime hours. The room service and the restaurants in the hotel have great food and impeccable service. 
Everything at this hotel says style and comfort. A stay here is worth every penny. It is a luxurious hotel in a great location, close to restaurants and shopping. The St. Regis San Francisco is a great place to stay if you're in the San Francisco Area.

This hotel was just perfect for us. Everything was very clean. Bed was a hair on the firm side, but would rather it be too firm than too soft or sagging. Pillows were so good we are going to order a couple! Staff was very helpful with questions and allowed us to check-in a couple hours early. The breakfast was definitely better than the average continental fare. There is a subway station steps from the entrance. I highly recommend this hotel as it's just the right balance of value and comfort.
If you need to stay at the airport, this is a convenient option. The rooms are clean, and we couldn't hear any noise from the airport.

We were here last year and I kept meaning to do a review and never got round to it. Watching a film about San Francisco reminded me that I must do this. 
Firstly before I even arrived The Chancellor had given me a great first impression as we ha booked our holiday for Fleet week without even knowing what it was and were surprised at how expensive the hotels were. Somebody suggested contacting The Chancellor to see if they had any offers or could do a special rate and they obliged.

We were there when the Giants were in the playoff's for the world series. My husband has always said he didn't like baseball but is a sports nut and so was interested in why the whole of SF seemed to be buzzing. We sat in the hotel bar - night to watch one of the games and the bellboy spent the night explaining all the rules to him. We will definitely consider returning but will probably get a suite for a bit more room.

The hotel itself is super modern, maybe too modern. We liked the lobby bar for happy hour and the terrace was great. Great spot for a pre-dinner cocktails, esp on Friday. They didn't do this on Sunday, so either someone complained or a manager finally picked up on it. We were trying to relax with our coffee on the terrace but we couldnt even hear each other talk it was so loud. I just thought it was strange that a manager would allow it. Our room had a funny smell...I should have had our room changed but by the time I realized the smell wasnt going away I didn't feel like packing everything back up, etc. The blackout shades allow light in through the sides...this is a MAJOR design flaw!!! Ive never stayed in a hotel that this happened. At -am it looked like we had spotlights on in our room! If you are looking to sleep in and relax, stay somewhere else. We faced ground zero so maybe if you stay on the south side the light isn't as bad. Cleanliness wasn't an issue and the bed was extremely comfortable. Service was ok, on par with other W's. I feel as a whole W's used to have amazing service but over the last two years they have been average. 
I believe rooms start around ---$...that is a steal for nyc. I think you can put up with the shortcomings for that price. Don't expect the four seasons when your not paying four seasons rates.
We stayed in a junior suite the night before going to a red sox game. Accommodations were small but very comfortable and immaculate. Location is fantastic.

I look forward to checking in and am sad when it's time to leave.

From drive up - to drive out - all staff was friendly, professional, courteous, helpful and seemed genuinely glad that I was staying with them for my visit. All services by all areas of the hotel was excellent throughout my stay.

White house is a nice --min walk from hotel and the DuPont neighborhood is a great choice for shopping and meals...definitely recommend this hotel and hope to stay here again in July on repeat visit!

- chairs in room have nice design but aren't comfortable

On a positive note, Office staff were nice, the bed was confortable and the free shuttle is ---- which I used a couple of times so I didn't have to pay to park my rental.

While looking through the hotel reviews on this site for our first trip to San Francisco, my husband and I came across Castle Inn. it is so close to everything, simply fantastic for the tourist who has only some days to be there. close to Time square, Brodway, Theatre, M&M, etc. the room is simple and functional, with no mini bar inside, you can't boil water for tea, but you can get out and can reach to the hotel restaurant or outside to eat a good and cheap breakfast. the stuff is friendly and the lobby is beautiful.

My husband and I stayed there the first week in June while my husband attended a training class. We arrived very early on a Sunday morning, and our driver took us to the hotel to drop off our bags before we went for breakfast and to play tourists for the day. The staff was delightful--immediately checked our bags in the locked bell room, offered to get us a cab (no need---our driver, Al, offered to wait and take us directly to the restaurant!), and tried to see if any room would be open soon, just in case we were tired and wanted to check in (no luck, but HEY, it was only - am...). We went off for a lovely day checking out the Chicago sites. Once fatigue (and mild jet lag) set in, we called in hopes our room was ready and it was--at -pm when check in was -!
After check in, both the floor housekeeping staff and a manager stopped by to see how we liked the room (it was fine), and dropped off some bottled water. After a brief rest, we headed down to check out the manager reception--we've been to Embassy Suites before a we're quite familiar with the amenities. Of course, we were off schedule and wondered why at -:--, it wasn't open yet--it wasn't until we decided to wander around outdoors that it occurred to us that it was only -:-- in Chicago.....oops.
The nightly reception is a nice touch--in fact, I think one night we basically skipped dinner because we had enjoyed the hors d'ourves and quiet opporunity to relax in the atrium. The breakfast, the same---the staff was so friendly and welcoming. I liked that in your room, they give you an idea of the best times to go to breakfast if you're looking to avoid lines--not that I saw any line so long that it would have frightened me away --even with a huge convention crowd on-site (I worked in my hotel room for part of the day during my stay, and made a few trips down to refill my coffee since their brew was better than the coffee I could do in-room). The manager was great! Encouraged everyone to enjoy their meal. The made-to-order staff was also accomodating--not being an omelet lover, I asked for fried eggs, which they were happy to make. Lots of choices, always a good thing.
While I wasn't there long enough to try the hotel's restaurant, I can tell you if it's anything like the room service food--it's a must-do! I had the most wonderful BLT sandwich from there. Of course, in Chicago, you have sooo many food choices. Even the grocer across the street had fun eats. 
We opted not to try the indoor pool, just not enough time. It looked average, maybe ready for an update. Not so inviting we couldn't resist--of course, traveling without our young kids, it has to be a pretty spectacular pool for us to suit up when we're on our own.
The location was within easy walking distance of the training center my husband needed to go to and the Magnificent Mile (which I HAD to go to ;--) Even with a computer bag (or several shopping bags, it was an easy walk. The musuems and Navy Pier were less walkable, but there is enough reasonable public transportation opportunities to get you there, no matter your budget. 
Price wise, the hotel was steeper than we'd normally pay for an Embassy Suite, but I realize this is high season, mid-town and there was a huge convention going on, so rooms were going for a premium. If it was our dime exclusively, we'd have to try for an off-season rate.
This was our first visit to Chicago and I have to agree with other reviews--it's all that NYC has to offer, but with a smile! We'll be back.

One downside to the location is that there is not much to do--in the vicinity of the hotel-- if you want to spend some time walking around or shopping in the evenings. The hotel is trendy, let's call it """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""tastefully overdone,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" with interesting photographs of famous and beautiful people at every turn. Just bring your wallet, because everything costs (except coffee on your floor)...but really, I get a free bottle of water, warm cookies, often a little snack, and breakfast at the Hampton Inn for $----night. No such feebees at the luxurious ZaZa for twice that price. ZaZa does offer the insanely priced and fully loaded Servi-Bar and snappy $---night parking. The one and only complaint I had was that the deluxe room that I had smelled...smelled BAD. Because of the vast difference in rooms...and because of the potential for a BAD smell...I would highly recommend that people check out the rooms that they are to be """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""given"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" BEFORE they fully check-in. Another thing, on the -rd day we woke up find - mattresses and a bed frame in the corridor just in front of our door - note very nice looking - they could have stored the stuff somewhere a bit less visible.

There is a very comfortable 'sitting room' on the -th floor which has free tea and coffee in which to relax after a hard days sightseeing.
