I stayed recently for - nights while on business. First let me say, great location and very friendly, helpful staff. Times Square is a minute's walk away. Then the negatives... It's expensive and you don't get much for your money. The room was small, decent size bed and very comfortable but even for a single traveller I found the room pokey and although I know it's clearly advertised, I must point out, the shower is quite literally in the bedroom - there is a curtain to pull across the bathroom area which makes the area so small you can't move, and if you don't close this then you have to remember to close the blinds in the room or the people in the offices opposite can see you! And the worst for me...it's soooo dark!!! It was mentioned at check in that the hotel is 'eco friendly' and that you have to insert your room key in the room for the power to come on. Fair enough I understand that. What I don't understand and as a lone female traveller cannot abide is dark corridors and pitch black stair cases. The breakfast area was so dark when I sat down I couldn't read my paper - it also doesn't help that there is no natural light apart from the front of the building as it is a terrace. The foyer, bar, 'dining' area, lift with red lighting (?) and interior is dingy. Add that to the tiny room size and the overall feeling is claustrophobic and a little creepy.

Coming to Baltimore to see the Michael Jackson Immortal Tour by Cirque du SOLEIL, I was not supposed to spend a night over, but when I checked the reviews on this hotel I became interested in spending a night in this place. I travel a lot, and a new hotel is always a great experience, but I must say that this one was unique. Not the regular impersonal - stars hotel, but a different approach, more charming, more homy.
The room, I should say the suite, was awesome, overlooking the water, huge, and after the show I felt, that I didn't want to go to a walking distance restaurant, but wanted to have a bite in the room, and enjoy the free bottle of wine left in the fridge (not because it was free, just because I thought that it was a nice welcome drink). So did I, and they allowed me to buy some food In the organic shop within the hotel, which was closed at the time I came back.
So I had a great evening, thinking about this wonderful show, looking at the city lights, and sipping my wine while watching TV.
I love this week end, I love the way I treated myself, and I would recommend to do the same to single, couples....anyone...but enjoy this different place.

Having booked our room at the Warwick online without ever seeing it in person, we didn't really know what to expect. We were pleasantly surprised to see that photos from the hotel's website didn't do it justice (they have since been updated). Although the decor may seem a bit dated(traditional), our room was spacious, comfortable, and elegant (I called to upgrade to an upper floor junior suite for a reasonable fee). The balcony offered amazing views of downtown Denver. The hotel's rooftop pool has --- degree views of city. The staff was great. Everyone was very friendly and helpful. The Warwick definitely exceeded our expectations.

We are Priority Club Members and we stayed in the main hotel on the --th floor. All of the rooms were recently refurbished which was nice. Why spend all that money on refurbishing the rooms and leave popcorn celings? It still looked outdated. We paid $---.-- a night and had a beautiful view of the harbor. The first two nights were fine, then we came back after a day at the zoo and noticed the maid didnt dust or vacuum the carpeting, then we noticed coffee cups were dirty, a dirty cup wasnt taken out of our room to be cleaned. They didnt replace toilet paper. My husband complained and the hotel staff were on it. They seemed quite mortified that the room wasnt cleaned properly. We were given one nights stay free. As for the noise level, I can't complain, it didnt bother us one bit. If you decide to stay here, I would not recommend the south tower, we had to do some laundry and the tower has not been refurbished and it is unsightly to say the least. Avoid it if you can. Stay in the main tower. The pool area is small, but nice and the pool is heated. Staff were very helpful, hats off to William! They have movies on demand, and because my husband and I are not nightlife people, we watched a movie every night while having cocktails. The movies are expensive, but worth every penny!
We have been there with family from italy, the place is basic, not really clean but for - night is ok. Great location and restaurant choice around is great. I would go back if in need.

A pleasure to walk into with the air conditioning and the cool marbled lobby - what a surprise!
This hotel was one of the best value hotels we have had the pleasure to stay in. Close to all amenities and ideal for sightseeing. 
The pool and poolside bar was everything we needed with temperatures over --- degrees, the area was spotless and kept that way all the time. 
We are a family of three but only enough linen for -, this was rectified within minutes after we pointed out the mistake. The room was clean, tidy and extremely confortable. 
Staff were more than helpful, and we were pleased to be pampered by the Restaurant staff. 
As a family we have no hesitations in recommending this hotel to anyone travelling to DC.

Magnolia's charming setting and customer service provided great respite for weary convention attendees. We were able to begin the day at the breakfast buffet and close the day at the evening's milk and cookie buffet, which provided a friendly, uncompromising atmosphere for me. The rooms were spacious and quiet, which was important as I shared the room with another female colleague. It was also very convenient to the convention center. I would like to bring my family back to Dallas and stay at the Magnolia again.

We loved our stay here. Rooms are beautifully decorated--felt very luxurious. Loved the pool area. Great place to hang out and sip on fruity drinks while watching the kids swim. We felt the rooms were very quiet. Overall, very enjoyable!

I was surprised to read the previous bad review. We had Room -- overlooking the pool and it was great. Not luxury-resort-hotel great, but well worth the price. Our suite was very spacious -- like a small apartment -- with a separate bedroom w-TV, efficiency kitchen, and sitting area w-TV and sofa. My mom stayed in a non-suite room down the hall, but it was spacious too. Everything in both rooms was very clean and in good working order. Very comfortable beds. The bathrooms were nicely updated and spotless. The kitchenette even had a filtered water dispenser on the sink -- a welcome amenity since San Diego tap water isn't the best. They even had guest bathrobes in the closets. Didn't use them, but we thought it was cute. Free wifi worked fine. Some hotels charge extra for this, so this was a plus. The staff was pleasant and helpful. The complimentary breakfast was your average bagel and boiled egg offering. But there are plenty of good restaurants and shops within walking distance. 
My only - criticisms are the ambulance noise from the hospital nearby (but it didn't keep me awake) and the tiny parking spaces (additional $- daily), but we didn't have too much trouble parking the SUV we rented.

We spent a week here and didn't get much sleep. We had a room that had the connecting doors, and it was really noisy. We could hear EVERYTHING going on in the adjoining room! For such an expensive hotel, this was very disappointing. As mentioned, two scratchy towels were insufficient for the two of us.
Excellent workout facility and very friendly staff, but would not stay here again or recommend for those that aren't heavy sleepers. Way too noisy...

We stayed at the Homewood for two nights on a quick but lovely trip to Chicago. When we arrived, the staff were super friendly and very helpful. We arrived early and our room was not quite ready, but the staff offered to keep our bags for us while we went for lunch. Before we could even catch the elevator downstairs (the reception is on the -th floor), they called us to tell us our room was ready. Great people and very easy check-in. 
The room was spotless and bigger than we expected! It was perfect and had everything you would need. The best part about the room was the BED! It was surprisingly the most comfortable bed we've slept in!
Great location - very close to Magnificent Mile and not far from the Chicago Theatre. A nice walk to Navy Pier and just steps to the red subway line that takes you to Wrigley.
We will definitely stay here again - highly recommended.

To be fair, this hotel was certainly set in a nice part of SD between La Jolla and downtown and close to the highway. It boasts some decent amenities and a nice pool area. Nothing fabulous that would warrant a --star rating other than a small """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""resort"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" wing, though.
After having stayed at many a --star hotel on business in many countries, I must say I was more than appalled at the nickel-and-diming of customers. Parking is $---day, which is never mentioned on any online site. The worst part is, there are no other parking areas around the hotel, so it is more of a hostage arrangement than an option. They charge you to use the basic gym, internet service, and a few other services that your average - star hotel would give you for free.
Add a bathroom full of deceptively placed """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hotel brand"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" moisturizers and doodads- all for fee of course-and you get the distinct feeling that you're getting a shakedown that is simply irritating to no end. You start getting paranoid about using the hotel soap and towels lest a fee for that. 
For a resort, they simply have not understood the concept of including basics into the price and reducing the hassle factor for guests. Raise the price if you must, but for gods sake dont charge for using your own hotel.

We were there last week and we loved the location (-th & Spring), right in downtown and near great restaurants and shops. The front desk staff very freindly and very profesional, specially Shayne!!! she is extremly helpful and polite, that hotel has a great employee. She helped me with reservations for restaurants. She maid us feel so special. The room was clean and nice. I work at a hotel in Boston and believe me the service and the hotel in general was excellent. Next time I am in Seattle I will definately stay at this hotel again. Gerardo Escalante and David Morris

We just LOVE the Jackson Court! Its a neat old historical manision in the most pristigious neigborhood in San Francisco. We have visited every year since ----, and stayed in - of the -- rooms. They are all beautiful but if you want to really treat your self, the garden room is the most magnificent of all. The staff is really nice and make you feel like a V.I.P. They really extend them selfs to make you feel comfortable. The breakfast and afternoon tea makes it just perfect! We highly recomend Jackson court to anyone looking for a nice peaceful place to stay in San Francisco.

If you get a good rate for this hotel, take it. Although not one of the better Westin's, the location on the Magnificent Mile near shopping and restaurants, proximity to Lake Michigan and the Gold Coast make this a good choice. Per the recommendation of other reviewers I asked for a corner room and was told that not all corner rooms are larger (they must be used to this request). I took the room and it was average size--not really small, but not large. I didn't have a view of Michigan Avenue--they said those rooms are $-- more (which isn't worth it). Room was comfortable--enjoy the robe, comfortable bed, and the in-room safe big enough for a laptop. Lobby is uninviting--but so what. If the price seems high here, there are better hotels in the area, but if you find a good price, its a good value.

Hotel is situated directly across from the Space Needle, Science Museum & Monorail for quick, easy access into the city centre for a $-.-- fee each way. Hotel with clean, comfortable rooms-beds and at the time of our visit some refurbishment was taking place which will be a great improvement to some of the dated decor. The swimming pool was a great asset for a relax of an evening and buffett breakfast was adequate. Hotel offered great service from their staff with computers with internet-printers available in reception for free usage which was very helpful.

I stayed at this hotel with my husband during one of his business trip. The room that we've got is a suite, so there are pretty space, but the AC unit is extremely noisy, we had to turn the one in the bedroom off during the night so we can get some sleep and kept the one in the living running. The housekeeping is horrible, the only thing the staff are doing is just making the bed, no dusting, no wiping over the bathroom counter. The worst of all is that the hotel charged us whenever our bill exceeds $---. My husband is on a business trip and we live in Europe, it creates several issues for our business expense report. It's like the hotel does not believe the customer is able to pay the bill. We stayed there for -- days, we had at least - separated charges. And no one told us that policy when we checked in. I will definitely stayed at another hotel next time.

I stayed at the Doubletree for two nights. We stayed in an ADA room which was okay. We had a roll in shower which was nice and a toilet cap which was even nicer. You don't usually get those things at other Hotels. Our room, unfortunately, faced the Freeway and although we were on the -th floor the freeway noise was really loud. I checked to see if the windows were closed and they were. It wasn't so disturbing that I didn't get any sleep, however. 
Another issue with the Hotel I had was the problem with the iron. I did let the front desk know and they did promptly bring me another one. Also, the elevators take a REALLY long time to get to you. I have never spent so much time waiting on an elevator. 
All in all, the beds were comfortable as were the pillows. The staff was friendly and we loved that we got a cookie upon our arrival. They comped our parking since we needed to park in the disabled parking and there wasn't any available on the street. The pool area was nice also and has a small bar which was an added plus.

You literally cross the street and you're in Grant Park. We came to Chicago to go to a football game at Soldier Field so the location couldn't have been better. It's a couple miles south of Navy Pier and shopping so walking is possible. There are plenty of places to eat within a couple of blocks. The room itself is just an average room. (For our room) You walk in, there is an open closet area on your left with a couple suitcase holders and an iron and ironing board. Then, there's a door on your right to the bathroom. Tub-shower, toilet, sink, some shampoo, conditioner, soap, lotion. Keep on walking and there is a TV with drawers underneath and a desk on the left and a king bed with a nightstand on each side. We only stayed for one night so this was more than sufficient for us. Yes, it is a little outdated and some things aren't in good shape. For example, the knobs kept falling off the drawers under the TV. It wasn't as bad as some people are making it sound thought. The people that work there are very polite. Also, on the -rd floor, there is a workout room and and outdoor pool (which wasn't open because it was cold, but looked perfectly nice). Where the pool is, there is an outdoor area that has tables and chairs. Overall, for the price, it was the perfect place for us. Chicago is an expensive place to stay so it's nice that there are cheaper options, even if it's not - stars.

Great Hotel, a few years back I celebrated my birthday at the adagio- attended a town hall wedding of a relative. The exterior of this mid ----'s property with the huge doors creates an ambience in itself, where as the reception takes in a minalmist boutique edge. Although the rooms were a little samy the beds and facilities were comfortable and in all spacious. Across the road is a typical diner and a bar which were both really freindly and convenient. Location for shopping is excellent just a ---- min walk up Taylor street is all the shopping you need, follow past Union square next stop is China Town then last stop Fishermans Wharf.

Well, it's an easy place to find in relation to the airport. Nice parking lot with a nice sampling of cacti near the front of the building.
Check-in was prompt, yet relaxed which was fine by me. My first problem was after checking in, I had to constantly use my room card. Within -- feet, you'll need your card out for the back of the lobby, the pool, and the door to enter the building which has your room. I'd hate to see anyone with more than one bag deal with those doors.
The room had everything I needed plus a good little kitchen. When I stay longer than two nights, I love to have more than just a little dorm-size fridge for some groceries. I found the role of housekeeping - in regards to the kitchen - to be confusing. Everything was nicely organized, but some stuff was half-washed and the rest was stuff I was going to wash and dry myself. Nonetheless, I made great use of my kitchen!
The room had two big drawbacks. I probably would've found a better quality deal and the television looked like it was at the end of its depreciation.
The nice part is that Marriott has always been good to me when it comes to comfortable beds and showers. That's usually why I'll choose Marriott first if I don't know the area well.
The outdoor pool is surprisingly comfortable and provides the option of having your own little cookout.
While the breakfast buffet food is average, it is well run.
All in all, it was OK. Next time, I'll just stay downtown or in Scottsdale.

Just got home from a - day stay at The Curtis. Great location downtown, easy walk to everything, we walked to the Pepsi center every day. Brew pubs, dancing, shopping, museums; you name it, it's there. We called direct to book and told them we found a quote of $--- online, they looked it up and matched that price. Some ammenities are not yet open as the property is being renovated, so no pool or restaurant yet. The beds are fabulous, great bathrooms (we had a shower, no tub) and amazing pillows-comforters. Best sleep we've had away from home in a long time.

We were there for - nights at the end of April. Was a basic room, bathroom sink area was a little tight but not a problem. Good location, within - blocks of Rockefeller Ctr. Clean and comfortable, especially since all you're looking for is a place to shower and sleep.

I stayed here Jan. ---- when I was leaving the country and January ---- when I was returning. My family and friend and I all loved this property. It offers free shuttle service to the airport. They were able to accommodate an early check-in the particular times I went. The pool area in the courtyard is really great. The hot tub is huge! The fitness center is also large and serves water with fruit in it... my mom thought that was fantastic! The rooms are cozy and the beds are extremely comfortable.

I stayed at the Jet Hotel one night on July -. It's centrally located and there are tons of restaurants to go to nearby. Got back to the hotel around --:-- pm after a late dinner and had to show room key to get in the hotel because the bar-club has started. A small inconvenience but it could seem cool to some to 'bypass the line'. The lobby decor modern and chic. However, the room is another story. We get the feeling that it's trying to do this cool minimalist thing - they've got the minimalist part but not the cool factor. The room and the bathroom was quite small and the bathroom doesn't seem very clean. The toilet was not flushing but my boyfriend fixed it easily (but still). There was a balcony, but the view to another building - although this could be useful for smokers. The music was loud at the bar but we didn't hear anything from the room. The hotel doesn't have parking for those who are doing a road trip. The guy at the front desk told us to park across the street which would have costed us $--. We looked around and found a parking next door for $--. Booked the room from the hotel website for $---+tax ($---) for a queen room. Seems a little overpriced for me for what we got.
Felt like home, our insurence company placed us here due to some house problems. Located less then a block to harbor. The staff was very nice. And the bar downstairs is great, and great food.

The hotel and room is very old, dirty and outdated. The carpet was very dirty, rumpled, torn and smelly. The sheet on the bed was turned inside out thus, making me think that it was not changed from the previous guest. The tub water drained very slowly. There weren't a coffee pot, frig, microwave, iron or hair dryer in the room. As I traveled back home and passed many Red Roof Inns, it seems that all of them looked the same. The hotels are in need of a good pressure washing and painting. I WILL NOT sleep at another Red Roof Inn!

This hotel is great! Yes it is built in the cliffs... hence the name, that is what makes it unique. If you can get over the fact that it is spread out and you do have to do a little walking you'll be fine. They offer shuttle service if you need it, that would be particularly useful for families or people that do not get around so easily.
A couple times we couldn't find a parking space in the lane in front of our suite but I just used the parking lot on the other side of the building... not that big a deal.
The rooms are spacious and clean, and seemed to be recently updated. We did upgrade our view, which is worth it, if you care what is out side your window.
There are several pools, the main one is called """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""the falls"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" most people and families go there, the grotto pool is the other large one which is also beautiful. The adult pool has a swim up bar and was a nice retreat. The other smaller pools are located though out the resort... we didn't even make it to them all. 
The restaurants at the resort are very nice... we at at the one by the main pool and the one at the golf course, the food and service were great. Apparently there is a very ritzy one with an amazing view... we didn't go there.
We had no issues with service or cleanliness. 
I recommend this hotel.

I'm always greeted by the friendly front desk staff, Breana & Rhee. They make my visit very much like visiting with friends. The breakfast prepared by Rauol is the best meal I have each day while staying here. I enjoy the environment and will continue to stay with the crew at Hilton Garden Inn.

After a recent terrible experience with a La Qunita I ws delighted with this Hotel the rooms smelt clean and attractive, the whole hotel was immaculate, very impressed. The staff were always very helpful but on arrival they were ayoung team and struggled with two rooms booked on one form but it got sorted. All quireies were answered quickly and they had prinbt-outs of verious information, a delight to stay in, even breakfast was OK.

We got a really good deal off of Hotwire. First of all the hotel is very appealing. The furniture in the lobby and all over the hotel is very nice. It is away from the loudness of the city (which I missed). There was no conventions going on so it was very quiet. Like other reviews I have read, the bed was comfy and the room served its purpose. It was very hot in Chicago and my husband wanted to walk to Navy Pier from the hotel to save money on cab fare. Plus I didn't want to take the bus late at night. Not the brightest idea. It took a hour or so. At least we got a good workout and nice photos. However, that being said, we went up to the concierge before our walk and asked how much a cab would be from Navy Pier. From some of the reviews on here it would have been nice to know there was a shuttle to downtown and Navy Pier from the hotel. Unless it is only during the week. For that I'm very disappointed in this hotel and the customer service that was presented. Furthermore the lady behind the desk when we checked in was a bit rude when I asked for a room on a higher floor. The pool is actually quite small. We ate at the Mix and it took forever to get our food and drinks. They ran out of olives but the nice lady offered to take --% off. Overall, we actually enjoyed ourselves at this hotel, but again customer service goes a long way and sadly it didn't go that far on our stay.

My husband and I stayed here for our pre-honeymoon a few days after our wonderfully stressful wedding weekend, and it was the perfect getaway. Our room was chic and cozy with a fabulous rain shower, complimentary breakfast, and an amazing view of the city. Though we enjoyed just sleeping in and relaxing in our room, it was wonderful to have a wide variety of restaurants and shops within a three-block radius. We even caught a late-night movie (finally after many months) just down the street. We had a great stay!

I have stayed in a lot of Manhattan hotels. Never before tried the Sofitel. I was a little nervous when I was assigned a room on the fourth floor. Worried about the constant street noise which is usually an issue. Not to worry, being in that room was like being sealed in a cacoon. I never heard one thing from the street. The beds are incredible, complimentary water is nice, bathrooms are very luxurious. My only complaint is Gaby's - limited bar menu for food, extremely overpriced even for NYC standards (one burger, one club sandwich and two beers was over $--). I would stay hear again in a heartbeat.

This hotel was sold by marriott some years ago and purchased by the Starwood chain who undertook renovation which was much needed. While I preferred the more traditional old world decor of the Marriott, the Starwood chain accomplished a make-over without destroying the general ambiance. Rooms are spacious and subtly tasteful. Large bathrooms with lovely amenities.
The Bar retains an intimate appeal and deserves a visit.
Its location near Dupont Circle makes it an excellent launching point for DC whether it's business or pleasure.

Incredible customer service. Divine bed & bathroom and associated linens.
Even though we booked through Priceline, we never felt -nd class. Room with Queen bed exceeded our expectations.
Free wifi in rooms easy to access. Free access to Business Center -- with - Macs each with a printer.
We found location great with Whole Foods downstairs and wonderful pizza at Tutta Bella on plaza just steps from main entrance. Our car rental @ Enterprise was about a --minute stroll down Westlake.
Two extremely minor quibbles:
--The main entrance is challenging to find. But so worth it!
--the remote control is evil!!

As someone who travels to Austin regularly for business, I am so happy that this Westin exists. The staff is incredible - kind, helpful, and enthusiastic. They have anything you may need, and for my purposes, the location is perfect. I really can't speak enough to how comfortable and pleasant this hotel is. One of my favorites.

My husband, myself and my daughter decided to take a day trip to NYC to see the Ripley's Believe It Or Not Museum in Times Square. We were having so much fun in NY that we decided to stay. At dinner we asked the bartender where we might find a room and he recommended the QT. From the moment we were greeted at the front door, until the time we checked out, the QT was quite an adventure.
Walking into the lobby, we were greeted by - doormen and the reservation clerk. All extra friendly, good looking people. We were astonished that we could get a room with a King Size Bed and a single bed loft for under $---.--. We were checked in within -- mins. On our way upstairs we passed the pool which was immaculate and noticed there was a bar there. Elevator was quick and clean and our room was beautiful! Clean, comfy and modern.
After washing up we left and went to Little Italy and shopping and then returned. The Hotel was a party! People swimmng and laughing in the pool, music playing...it was alive! We loved it. My daughter who is a very impressionable -- year old wanted to look around and we did. People were friendly, the door man knew and recognized us and we felt completely safe among the crowd. Security was excellent, the bed was comfortable and clean, huge shower, refrigerator, dvd player, just wonderful. Me and my daughter are returning next week to see a play and will be staying at the QT. 
I must say, that most important when travelling with my daughter is not walking into an empty lobby. I feel completely safe taking her there and staying a few days alone.
Hats off to the QT. The atmosphere is just like the world outside its doors in Time Square. Alive, friendly, happy and comfortable. LOVED IT.

Yeee-uck! This hotel stinks! We arrived at the hotel and had a difficult time checking in even though we had all our confirmation numbers and print-out from Orbitz. It was described as a - star hotel but I think they need to review it again!Our room was comparable to a roadside motel and DIRTY! I found a pair of mens underwear in the drawer and a used kleenex on the floor- I called down to front desk and complained- they moved us to another room that was just as dirty! I asked about a wet bar or refrigerator and they said we could RENT one(Refrigerator) for an additional --.-- a day! The staff were cold and uncaring- and they charged us TWICE for our stay! After a month we finally got our money back! P.s. We did call Orbitz to ask for a hotel change and they said they wouldnt guarantee us getting our money back for the Parc even if we didnt stay! Never again!

The rooms were nicely appointed, clean and quiet. To be fair, the hotel was undergoing renovations; however, the small lounge area that doubled for breakfast was cramped and service slow. Business meeting space was mediocre at best -- temperature fluctuation (mostly too cold) and not good about refreshing water, etc.,; also, little to no policing of food and beverages served outside room -- in fact, the group next door helped themselves to our refreshments at their leisure. When brought to staff's attention, we got little more than a shrug of the shoulders. Front desk were friendly and attentive and overall, the property is worth a stay -- nicely located in downtown within walking distance of lots.

Recently stayed here as part of a business trip. Front desk staff were extremely friendly and helpful, especially Sarah who helped get a room ready after I arrived from a long flight and needed to get ready before meetings. Rooms are very nice -- clean, modern and tastefully decorated. And I appreciated the small touches (like toothpaste!). Location is superb to convention center, shopping, light rail, and waterfront. Pool is beautiful and was quiet with only a few people there (""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""locker room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is shared with spa and was also very nice and clean). Only complaint is that I had trouble connecting to the wi-fi. In short, great hotel & friendly staff. Would highly recommend.

We stayed there for a week....no choice but to endure it. Ist room was the wrong one because they messed up reservations....one day later they put us in a king room that hasn't seen an interior decorator since ----. The bed was so uncomfortable i slept in the chair.
They actually booked the room a second time - I was asleep when two people tried to gain access to my room - sure enough their paper said MY room number. 
The next day - the water was off for over - hours!! The front desk clerk said"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Oops - sorry for the inconvenience ....""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""
The free breakfast was good - if you get there before the food runs out......
Location is great....you can walk to a lot of things while you let your car in the hotel parking lot for only $-- a day.
The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""free shuttle"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is nice - IF YOU WANT TO GO WHERE THEY WANT TO GO......
Staff is friendly.....
Only one antiquated house computer available.......
Cleaning staff leave a lot to be desired.....of course - cleaning wouldn't help the broken up, worn out furniture that was in the --th floor rooms.
TV only has -- channels - - of which are infomercials -- hrs a day.
I have stayed in hotels for less than half of this hotel's $--- - day rate and had better rooms. Thank God I didn't opt to pay $--- a day for a jacuzzi room!!

This was a wonderful experience to stay at the Coutyard by Marriott in Washington D.C. Even thought there were ---,--- girl scouts there the still made room for two more people. It was ALWAYS very clean. Never a found spot. Their breakfast bar was the best!! I highly recommend this amazing hotel to anyone!!!!

Over the past five years, I have stayed at the Latham several times. Sometimes once every couple of month for a day or so. Thus, I was able to follow the rapid and complete collapse of this quiet, nice and classy boutique hotel into a one star dump. I returned to at the Latham because I found the staff helpful, friendly and very courteous. But that was a long time ago. It is sad when the once professionally acting staff becomes a flock of tip-obsessed, rude, condescending vultures eager to rip anyone off for a buck. The lack of quality service serves as a sad testament to the complete disintegration of a hotel that once has held so many promises. 
Yet the main problem is not the staff; it is the quality of the accommodations. The rooms are in sad repair. The furniture has clearly visible dings that do not make them look antique, but rather cheap and over-the-hill. A dirty carpet with large stains is definitely a sign of serious problems. The box springs are loud and the mattresses are extremely uncomfortable; clearly they are in dire need of change. Moreover, the bathrooms are very poorly cleaned and inadequately equipped. 
The restaurant is outright horrible.
There are few positives; some of the staff recognizes the vast shortcomings of the hotel and attempts, with some success, to compensate for these. It compensates, but it just goes so far. This hotel lived up to the reviews here. Price was great for the location and class! The hotel is just a block away from Time Square, so the location was great. The hotel was very clean, rooms had lots of space. The staff was great, very friendly and helpfull. Everything about our stay was perfect!

I would recommend this hotel to anyone! Out stay couldn't have been better.

I absolutely loved the Sofitel Chicago. The room was smaller than I thought, but the bathroom was more than ample. the value for the money is really great. i'd definitely stay here again.

The breakfast had the best variety of food we saw in our whole -- week trip and there were enough tables that you didn't feel that you had to fight for a seat - the breakfast staff were also very friendly.

I would recommend this hotel and if we ever go back to Chicago would not look to stay anywhere else!

Wonderful, comfortable hotel in a great location for seeing the city. We were traveling with two teenagers and the hotel and staff were fantastic. I have stayed at this hotel several times before and have always had a great stay.

Wanted to give credit to this above average and well maintained property. Rooms were updated, clean and comfortable and price was affordable.
Public areas in need of renovations, but overall I'd recommend this hotel.

Like almost all the hotels in this part of Boston, it is on the expensive side (though cheaper than many others there) and valet is pricey ($---day as of our stay). The rooms were nice and clean, but basic.
The location is good as it is very close to Boston Common and the Freedom Trail and not a long drive from Fenway.
If you are aiming to walk the Freedom Trail and don't want to fight with Boston traffic and finding local parking this hotels a good choice, but if you're aiming to save money and willin to commute you may want to stay a little ways out of Boston instead.

The hotel is in the Times Square area, real accessible to many locations via walking or subway access. We took the subway pretty much everywhere.
The hotel is a bit run down in spots, but the rooms were comfortable and the bed was nice (king). We had a room on the --th floor and did not hear the hustle and bustle of Times Square. The only thing you hear is the emergency vehicle sirens - but that is not that common. 
For the money you spend for the location however, the room was only average - nothing too special about it. As mentioned, certain spots were run down and it could have been cleaner. The door guys were very helpful.
Would we stay here again - probably not as we would want to try something different

We have stayed at this hotel in the past when it was under a different name and saw that it had been remodeled so we expected it to be better than it was years ago. This was not the case. The room was shabby, dents in the wall, stains on the ironing board, sagging countertop. We turned on the heater and it blew dust into the air. We won't be staying there again.

Just stayed at this hotel on the last leg of our trip in LA and Vegas
I booked through Priceline and I got what I paid for...an old dated room in the Unrenovated part of the Hotel...when I asked to be moved..they did accomadate us to another room again in the older part of the Hotel..I asked was this the best they could do...yes they said these are the rooms saved for Priceline.
We could hear our neighbors...there was a large stain on the carpet..gave me the creeps...Thank God it was only for one night...
We dropped off our rental car before we came so thankfully didn't have to pay for Parking..

We put my parents up at the hotel in June for a week. The hotel was amazing, the room was nice everything seemed great....however there were many kinks...The Ipad didnt work given in the room, when the gentleman came to fix it the new one was just as useless....it took the hotel lots of time to bring something up if you requested it...a bar of soap, an ashtray...just tooo long. Nice hotel, nice location, but expensive compared to the nicer nearby hotels.

I loved this place. Upon check in, the lobby was beautiful. The hotel staff was great. I reserved two rooms, but somehow the reservation got mixed up. Management went way above and beyond to make everything right. Great job. The breakfast was better than any restaurant! Happy hour was fun! I will definately stay here again.

We stayed at this Marriott in Boston on our first stop of a two week fly drive around New England. We were also using Marriott points to pay for our stay so, although not exciting this fitted the bill quite well and enabled us to explore Boston on foot without any problem.
I think the hotel is primarily catered for business guests. It's a very large functional hotel just without much of a soul. It was however, conveniently attached to two large malls It's clean, which is always paramount and has large comfy beds. The staff were very friendly and helpful.
Negatives were that the parking was very expensive, so bear this in mind if you need to park.

This was our second stay at the Westin Georgetown and we absolutely love it. The staff is extremely friendly, experienced and informative. The hotel is luxurious - extremely comfortable. The lobby area is inviting (love the infused water) and the staff welcoming. Returning after a day of site seeing feels like going home. Great location. We did not eat at the hotel this stay (we ate there last stay and it was pricy), but there are many neighborhood restaurants in the area and the staff gave us great recommendations.

This hotel was wonderful! The beds were so comfortable with the down comforter and comfy pillows. There was an ihome where you could connect your ipod for music, a flat screen TV with many channels, and updated appliances. Convenient location and the room was BIG. Planning on staying at the Avenue time and time again!

Stayed at this hotel last week in November ----. The location is great being only about a - minute walk from the Empire State building. Commendable that the power is only on when the room key is in the slot on the wall, but ... with no air circulation and windows screwed on shut, upon entering the room you get hit with a wall of stale air. Requested another one, marginally better if at all. Ordered belgian waffles with whipped cream and maple syrup for breakfast, came with a piece of butter instead.

This is a classic San Francisco hotel that is over --- years old. It is well located on Market St near Union Square, but not as close as Westin or Hyatt. But it is closer to Ferry Bldg. The BART is directly outside the side entrance. Short walk to Yerba Buena & SFMOMA museums. Quick check in & express check out. Motel was in reasonable condition but our room did smell somewhat musty. The hotel is located in an industrial disctict and is very hard to locate. The Denver area discount coupons listed on the Marriott web site were not available when we checked in. We will stay in Golden or Boulder the next time we visit Denver area.

This hotel and its staff earns its five star status. Upon entering hotel you get the service you expect at four season. The four season also has a great downtown location only a couple of blocks from the --th street mall or a quick cab ride to the highlands area which has a lot of cool restaurants. When I return to Denver I will absolutely stay here again.

Great reduced rate for our PBM convention. Service was great. Morning breakfast bar was complete and tasteful. Room was spacious and comfortable. Would stay here again if in the area. Very close to University of North Florida.

Rooms are nothing like the the pictures. Rooms are small, dirty and smelly. All but one person at front desk were complete jerks that lack any kind of customer service. I was in New York for business meetings as well as a vacation as it was my first time in NYC. My company picked the hotel for me (because they were paying) and at first after looking over the hotel website I thought that my boss had just picked the cheapest and worst hotel he can find. I WAS WRONG!
The hotel is located in Tribeca and it was very close to all my meetings as well as all places I wanted to visit as it was my first time in NYC. There were a bunch of subway lines right outside the hotel door therefore travelling to midtown or uptown was an easy thing. The room itself is not a huge thrill but it is up to date and EXTREMELY clean! The amenities were limited but I had just what I needed to survive my week in New York. The only few things that I can complain about is the bit loud ac unit in the window and the lack of coffee makers in the room. Other than that it was all pure perfection! 
What really beat my expectations was the staff...I've stayed at many places where the hotel staff just doesn't give a s***. It was different here, the staff actually cared about me! From the moment I stepped in the hotel until I checked out a week later I was given the best customer service I could imagine. From whatever I needed whether it was extra towels or directions to my meetings the cosmopolitan hotel staff was always there and always willing and able to help me. I spoke to the morning staff many times throughout my stay (mainly Marcella) and the help I received was always just what I needed plus much more. Whenever I stepped out the front door I knew where I was going, what trains to take, where to buy tickets, etc. thanks to the help of the front desk staff. And on the last night when I realized I have no idea how to get to jfk airport I spoke with the front desk person Martin at -am and he provided me with the different ways that I can go about getting to the airport. I requested a car service for -:--am that same night and was reassured that the driver will be on time and waiting...and when I came downstairs the driver was there and ready to take my luggage. Wow! 
I definitely recommend the Cosmopolitan Hotel for anyone who is travelling to New York and is need of a good hotel with extremely excellent service! The Cosmopolitan hotel is my home for all my future NYC visits!!

I stayed at this hotel for a weekend in December. The staff were very friendly and helpful, always greating us with a smile and warm welcome as we entered and left. Janita, the manager, really stood out as being very customer-service oriented and made our stay even more enjoyable. The staff helped recommend restaurants, shopping, transportation, definitely full service! Breakfast was very good for being a free breakfast, and the breakfast room view is spectacular. The room was very nice, beds were very comfortable, and they offer ear plugs if needed to drown out the sound of the fire trucks (hotel right next to the fire station, and the fire trucks go out with sirens blarring frequently in the night). Fire trucks didn't bother me. It was an amazing location and absolutely delightful staff who made our stay very enjoyable. I'd definitely stay here again and would recommend it.

This is not a bad hotel. It's really very nice all things considered. The problem is the area its in. There were homeless people sleeping and urinating in front of the hotel. There's a lot of subsidized housing in the area. It's not the best neighborhood. It's not a ghetto nor did I feel in any danger there. It's just a very old neighborhood. The hotel itself is OK. The breakfast is minimal continental. The staff is OK. Parking is right in front of the hotel. The rooms are very big but nothing fancy. Noise was a problem though. Kids were running along the outside entries making a lot of noise for a few minutes but it ended quickly. People talking outside could be heard easily. I don't recommend this hotel and I would not go back. I'd pay a little more and stay in the East suberbs where there are more restaurants and nicer neighbors.

I stayed for a (-) week business trip. The only """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""complaint"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that I had is that the hot tub next to the pool was out of service.

This was our third trip to NYC.
We had previously stayed in Jersey City and decided to try to stay in Manhattan if we could find a reasonably priced place. After searching many locations and reading countless reviews, we decided on the Marmara. 
While a little off the beaten track (upper east side residential area), the Marmara is surrounded by great local places to eat, drink, shop, etc. The nearest subway is four major blocks away and requires a hike up steep East --th but once there, you are only mins from Central Park, Museum Mile, or a cheap subway ride downtown.

It turns out the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""construction"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is for a new -nd Ave subway line being built directly in front of the hotel. Early on three weeknights, the hotel was rocked by explosions as crews blasted the new tunnel. The room was very clean, the staff was great, every request was met quickly and courteously. 
My ONLY complaint was that despite getting a discounted rate on the room, the price per night jumped by almost $-- once the additional taxes were added...an additional $--- for - nights. While this was displayed on the quote in advance, the budget-minded traveler should consider this a $---- night hotel. Being three of us (me plus wife and daughter) I had originally been shopping for the most possible space in the low $---- night range but decided to take a chance on the Marmara based on TripAdvisor reviews. While more than I wanted to spend and EVEN with the explosions, it was great coming back to our room at the Marmara after viewing the many sites of NYC each day. 
We would definitely return and would highly recommend the Marmara Manhattan if within your budget.

We loved the decor and location. The staff was friendly and helpful. The room was cute but way too little. The result was no drawers or counter space. If I had be alone, it would have been fine, but the queen size room just did not leave enough space for two. Four stars?

We stayed at the Fairmont for -- nights for our honeymoon and it was just a brilliant stay. Fishermans Wharf and Union Square are both a ----- minute walk from the hotel, as is Chinatown, it is very easy to navigate around the area too. Fantastic restaurants and fast food places nearby also added to the wonderful stay. I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking to enjoy the city and walking to attractions rather than taking taxis or public transport, although the cable cars run literally from outside the hotel so no problems getting around for those wishing to experience the unique cable cars. The hotel itself is fabulous, the staff were extremely helpful, friendly and always greeted us with a genuine warmth. Our room was a standard double so we expected it to be on the small side but it was bigger than most of the king-sized places we've stayed in in the UK! The room was also very clean, the bathroom was spacious, clean and the bathtub was huge! I would recommend the Fairmont to anyone looking to stay somewhere classy yet comfortable and within walking distance of some of San Francisco's best sights and attractions.

Hotel has small rooms. They wanted $-- for parking per night and Wifi not included in rooms. Bathroom had no door where sink and mirror was. After multi-million renovation, it already looks rundown. Ceilings creak and thump from walking. Very average hotel.

The only negative for this hotel is the food. The menu items sound great but the execution was disappointing. However, there is a food court between the hotel and the Convention Center that has an excellent selection of food and a well priced breakfast option (great omlettes and pancakes).

The five of us (two adults, three kids ----) stayed in a two-bedroom unit for five nights over Christmas. 
+ The staff were genuinely warm, welcoming, and helpful
+ The breakfast (continental but ample) and free snacks policy was a big winner - even though we had the full kitchen it was easy just to use the breakfasts available rather than preparing every morning
+ The pool was warm (it was December!) and great for those """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""We've had a full day with the kids and they still have energy while we're exhausted"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" moments

If Magic Castle were to invest in a refurbishment this could be an excellent hotel, especially for those who value having a kitchen so that they don't have to worry about searching for a restaurant, hoping the kids keep it together for the meal, and paying the price to dine out.

I vowed last year to never stay at Kimpton Hotels due to my problems in Boston, but I am glad I didn't follow that advice. Vintage Park is a boutique hotel close to most things, but far enough away to remain quiet. I was pleasantly greeted at the front desk when I arrived & my room was available! The room is a bit on the small side, but it is an old building that has been beautifully renovated into a hotel. The washroom as well is very compact but sufficient and well stocked for your trip. The room has a good television, comfortable bed and space to work. The decor is not my personal taste, but it is very elegant. I was-am on the -th floor looking north, but truth be told there isn't a view except on a rundown building & parking lot, but that is fine. Great value, definitely register as a Kimpton InTouch member to get free WIFI in your room plus a $-- voucher for the mini-bar.  I had booked the room for a bargain price on travelzoo and realized soon why: the first - floors were still being renovated. I visit San Francisco about two or three times a year and have done so for the past ten years. However, I have never used Priceline until this past visit and what a bummer that I only tried it now!!! I paid litle more than what one would pay for a one or two star hotel in San Francisco! 
Anyway, on to the review of this hotel. I had stayed here many years ago and had enjoyed it very much. But it seems as though prices had crept up over the years and I found myself staying more and more at the Argonaut which is an incredible hotel for the price and location.
We arrived in the morning and weren't sure if the Hyatt would be able to check us in early but asked anyway. PT looks great from the outside,,,just like the pictures. Check in was pleasant. I was disappointed because we paid the rate for a partial view and got a -st floor room.  It was a very quiet hotel and we never heard any noises. My kids want to go back.

Excellent little hotel right next to the very interesting Farmer's Market and the original Starbucks! Very well located and very quiet with polite and helpful staff. Within walking distance of important Seattle landmarks

The Chatwal has to be the best value in the city. The only problem is that once word gets out, I will not be able to get a room in the future.
We travel to NYC several times a year and stay at various hotels. The nice ones are usually very pricey, cheaper ones are not very nice, and those in the best locations are usually noisy and overrated. The Chatwal is none of these! It is in an amazing location near theaters and great restaurants, is very reasonable, and is off of Times Square so it is not noisy. 
The rooms were very clean and service was responsive and efficient. The hotel is relatively new so hopefully it will stay this way. The decor is art deco and you feel like you are stepping back into an era when hotels and staff actually welcomed you and wanted you there, not just wanted your money. 
We reserved the base room and was upgraded. The rooms are small, but good size for a NYC room. We weren't there to hang out in the room anyway. The beds-pillows were comfortable, and the room had a small desk and chair. As indicated above, the hotel is on a side street off of Times square (maybe half a block). Because of this it is less travelled and fairly quiet (again, for NYC). The window in the room does open, which I like.
The restaurant, The Lambs Club, is fantastic. We did pre-theater and the service was quick, professional, and actually reasonably priced (for NYC). We had cocktails in the lobby bar as well as the main bar upstairs. Again, I actually felt wanted there. The cocktails were great and the service professional. 
If you are in town for theater, this is the best place to stay, hands down. I cannot think of a way to improve the hotel. Highly recommend!

Stayed on a Friday night after a football game. Pluses: location, checkin, parking only $- (reasonable compared to football game parking of $--+).

Stayed here with my family of four. Master bedroom and bathroom were very nice. Sofa bed in living area was uncomfortable and squeaked with every move. Elevators were very slow. What a luxurious relaxing resort! Enjoyed the well appointed rooms, pools, golf course, walkng trails and close proximity to San Diego and Orange County.

I chose this hotel because it was on the bay and had several nice restaurants. To my surprise, it was across the street from the Carnival Cruise Terminal that we needed the next day. The staff was extremely friendly and check-in was a breeze.We ate in the Elephant & Castle restaurant and the food + service was great. Although alittle pricey, it was worth it!! I live here with my husband for - weeks now and I extended my stay for - more weeks!!! It feels like being with your family here!! I must confess that it is the best hotel I have ever been. I attend a Convention for a week every January and have stayed at a lot of hotels in Times Square. Of all of the hotels I've stayed in, I prefer the Marriott Marquis. The rooms are much bigger than others in the same area, the fitness center is free, the elevators are efficient (now that they've finally finished renovating them), and the staff is nice. Plus, the beds and pillows are really comfortable! 
If you are visiting Times Square, the Marriott is right in the middle of everything. But if you're there on business, you'll find that the hotel has a nice lounge on the eighth floor for an after-dinner drink, two Starbucks (first floor and eighth floor) for that morning cup of coffee, and is pretty quiet considering it's a huge hotel right in the middle of New York.
I have stayed there at least three times that I can remember and have always had good experiences. I highly recommend the Marriott for both business and pleasure!

This hotel is just a place to crash, but at the same time, it's not ideal. It gets the job done however, and it's super cheap for the area.

Comfy beds
Very clean

Many of hotels in San Francisco have heritage and history. Therefore it's not easy to decide where to stay especially if I am visiting San Francisco on holiday. This is a fine hotel. A little dowdy around the edges, but functional just the same. 
The lobby definitely looks a bit dated and tired. The hotel restaurant is probably on par with your local diner and there is not much of a bar scene- not even for the business crowd.
Now, with that out of the way- the hotel is just fine in every other aspect. The rooms are at the contemporary Sheraton look and feel. Room service was prompt and accurate- which really describes the overall service of the hotel.

massive property ideal for conventions - is great for a quick three day getaway esp with the lazy river. The high number of business conventions are good for working vacations but no so much to get away from it all.

Spent four nights at the Benjamin in mid September ----. The hotel is situated in a good Midtown area opposite the Waldorf Astoria. There is a subway station close by so getting around town is easy. Clean, quiet and comfortable. Staff upgraded us to a spacious corner room which worked very well for our family of -. Overall the prices seemed better than my experience with other large city convention hotel. The location is convenient to nearby Sundance Square and easy access to highways.

I would stay there again!

The hotel rooms are a suite with a separate large bedroom with bath-shower and a separate lounge and small kitchenette-dining room. Plenty of space for a longer stay. Clean and well serviced.

The only complaint we had was the temperature in the room, it was either too hot or too cold.....we could never seem to adjust the thermostat to a perfect setting.
Either way we're very glad we chose to stay at the Distrikt Hotel in NYC, and we had a fun time! Thanks for the brownies and chocolates!

This was a wonderful hotel in a perfect location! It was my first trip to NYC and I will always return to the Belvedere for future trips.  Julian & Wendy Barnes

This was billed as a - star hotel. And supposed to have a restaurant. This is really not a restaurant, but a little place for them to serve breakfast. I stayed with my family (who frequents the hotel) in one of (if not the) best rooms in the hotel. The top floor presidential suite offered every amenity - including those nobody needs. Overall this stay was well over a month ago, and truly the images should speak greatly towards the true experience where I cannot, but suffice to say this was one of my most memorable stays in my long history of staying at different hotels. If you are looking to celebrate an occasion, or perhaps simply get away from the city, this is a wonderful place to do so. You will not regret it certainly if you make the most of your stay!

On the plus side the staff were very helpful and friendly. But we should have been advised by our agents that the kitchen was out of action meaning that any food had to be obtained elsewhere. Our room was of a reasonable size with two king size beds, and the bathroom was OK. If you want to see small try Paris or London! What a pleasure to be able to get a smoking room with a window that opened. We would stay again hopefully when their restaurant is working.

we have been staying at the travel inn --nd street for the past - years and always exceptional value for money very clean very good position if your going and looking for a quality hotel you have got to try the travel inn you will pleased you did our son lives and works in ct USA is a regular visitor to the hotel , Ann & Peter Young Boston ENGLAND.

Not sure how I feel about this hotel. While it is hip, cool, stylish and chic, it is also in the Financial District, which means it is a $-- plus cab ride, to the Village and even more to MidTown. Subways lines are close and the subways in NYC run frequently. If one is concerned only with being in the Financial District or near the ---- Memorial, this is a great hotel. The staff welcomes you with an IPad and checks you in at a station, not a desk. WIFI is free and easy to use. Coffee and breakfast goodies are available in the lobby in the mornings. Rooms are quiet and spacious. The neighborhood is still in transition from a completely financial one to a residential area, so there are more restaurants and shops opening, but it is still sort of bleak after -PM. If one wants to be in the middle of the tourist area, or near the nightlife, this is not the hotel for you. The bed was incredibly comfortable and the room was beautifully designed with very stylish furniture and movable (yes I said moveable) closets and storage. I just do not like the new ‘open bathroom’ design of some of the hipper spa-wannabe hotels. Entering the room you are immediately in the bathroom, which is all open to the room itself. The toilet has a semi-frosted glass door, which hints at privacy, but does not really deliver, and the bathtub and shower area have windows in to the bedroom. Not my favorite arrangement. Sink is visible from the room. I would just really rather have a separate bathroom, and not have it be the focal point of the suite. Did I like this hotel? Absolutely! Not sure I would stay there again, simply because of the location and the bathroom situation.

The foyer is indeed beautiful, but the positive experience for me ended there. The food is medicore and overpriced, with mandatory gratuity even for the self-serve breakfast buffet. Service was average, certainly didn't go out of their way to be helpful. We moved to Grand Hyatt for a clean room.

Location is perfect for this lovely hotel. They offer a free cocktail hour at -pm which consists of red & white wine and and appetizer or two. The lobby area becomes and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""instant party"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which adds to the fun. The rooms are enormous which is unusual for a boutique hotel. The concierge staff were most helpful. The hotel is on P Street which has numerous restaurants and a bookstore on the corner and a small grocery store on the other corner. The front door staff was friendly and made you feel welcome. I had to have packages delivered to the hotel prior to my check-in since I live in Europe and the hotel had them in my room when I arrived. I was pleased. Easy to get to locations by walking but easy to get a cab. They have a new restaurant which is known for their """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""make your own bellinis"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for brunch.

This was another visit to our favorite city and the Hotel choice is crucial.
The Lowes Regency is quite delightful. The rooms were BIG (We opted for a Street View room on the -th floor, - nights for circa £----) and the service was second to none.

We just completed our most recent stay at this grand hotel. My wife was recovering from surgery and the staff could not have been more helpful and caring. Attending an Indiana Pacers game a couple days ago, my son and I stayed at the SpringHill Suites in Downtown Indianapolis. This is actually the nicest SpringHill Suites that I have stayed in. The decor is very modern, which is definitely supported since this a newer hotel. It is an odd, but functional, arrangement for these - Marriott hotels. The entrance for this SpringHill Suites is shared with a Courtyard and they are both attached to the more upscale JW Marriott. Parking is below the hotel or for a couple dollars more you can Valet park.
I have stayed at the Courtyard side of the hotel before but this was my first time at the SpringHill Suites side. The suite is not overly large but functional. You do not get the luxury of being able to close off the bedroom from the sitting area but since our purpose was simply a decent place to stay for the night this hotel more than fit the bill. There is a separate desk area for the wireless, a small fridge and microwave and a couch with a pull out bed.
The toilet are is separate from the shower area which is unique but watch the sliding wooden doors if you need total privacy as they don't seem to close fully. The TV is situated in an odd location I think in what was a cost cutting move. I had a double-double suite and the TV was on a table at the foot of the bed close to the sitting area and it was on a swivel so that those on the couch can spin the TV around to watch. If you are like me you will need to keep your glasses on to watch TV if you have the bed farthest from the door as it the TV is not large and it is way off to the left if you are viewing from bed.
They offered breakfast in the morning but I took advantage of the late checkout and therefore can't comment on the breakfast.
I am actually originally from Indianapolis and know the city quite well. Whenever I come to town for a Pacers game or Colts game I would stay here again.
Clean, new, spacious, no complaints. You really can't beat this hotel in this area of Charlotte and I am extremely picky.

We stayed at the W for - nights before moving to another hotel for a convention. The service was excellent. We decided at the last minute we wanted to rent a car and the conceirge arranged one and it was delivered within -- minutes and was only $--.-- for the day. They were extremely helpful. We loved staying in this hotel. It's close to restaurants, a market, buses, monorail for downtown travel, and the Seattle Center. The rooms are big. Though old the place was immaculate. I picked this hotel over several others because even with the free in-room internet, free breakfast, and - minute walk to the convention center where my meeting was, it was still more affordable than many other choices. My husband and I stayed at the Elysee for - night during one of our short NY shopping trips. Having stayed at a sister hotel (The Giraffe) the week before, we thought this would be a sure bet. Tucked away in North San Diego County is the Rancho Bernardo Inn. Would stay here again loved being so close to Central Park and the museums. Much quieter than the Times Square area. Great for couples our butler was wonderful.

From the moment we arrived and were met by a smile and welcome from the desk. The suites are more than adequate with microwave and fridge and coffee machine. The beds are really comfortable, and there is a normal TV in the bedroom with a large flat screen in the living area. The swimming pool - hot tub and sauna are located on the --th floor together with the fitness room with amazing views over the lake. 
There are always cabs outside waiting to take you wherever but the hotel is only one block from the shops and Michigan Avenue so ideally located for shopping etc and right behind the Hancock.

I was very disappointed with the breakfast. Nothing great. Gnats by the fruit, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hot""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""food was not hot at all. I like. For the amount of money for the room, I would have expected more of a variety and hot food.

Easy access to CBS Studios (- blocks) - Show tickets can be obtained via www.mytvtickets.com. We were able to get tickets for """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""America's Got Talent - Finals.""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""

This is a handy place to stay in the DC area, especially if you are sight-seeing in the White House-Smithsonian-Mall areas. Good eateries close by and a nice walk to just about anything you want to see. The staff is accommodating and helpful.

Stayed in a nice modern room which was smartly designed with bed on one side and living area on the other. Sort of like a junior suite. Good-sized rooms, very clean, good location, nice breakfast ... The only minor negative I can think of is that my check-in lacked a smiling, welcoming face.

i wouldnt advise any one in their right mind to go to this hotel, it was worse than terrible, very bad manners at the reception when booking in, the lobby was discustingly dirty, full of unsatisfied customers. the stench of the place was unbearable, the rooms were filty, carpets on the walls!! carpets on the floor were not fitted properlyanddirty. curtains about fifty years old afraid to touch them incase might catch something!! bathroom tiny could bearly move around! seems good value for money but a total rip off!!!!!!

Not a large hotel but newly decorated. Rooms are a good size and very clean. Excellent location, less than - blocks from the centre of town and only - blocks to the market area.

We stayed at this hotel from --------- and could not have had a better experience. The very first evening there was a manager reception where all the staff were welcoming and helpful. Many went out of their way to give great advice on where to eat, visit, etc.

Great tip: Go to the top floor as long as there's not a function you have --- views of the city - simply brilliant!!

All the staff were very friendly and very helpful. The interiors are really quite lovely, everything is clean and well kept. Greenwich itself is a great place to be based as its low rise so its bit calmer than uptown and times square.
Some cool restaurants to try are:
Johns Pizzeria (branch in soho, and times square- this is a converted chapel) - massive yummy pizza, very good value for money
Fannellis cafe in soho - great food, bit like Cheers on the decor
Joes Shanghai - long wait so get there early, also its quite crazy and you will be sat at a table with strangers, but the dumplings are amazing ( their speciality) and so are their other dishes - try the greens..massive portions and cheap!
Del Friscos - up market steak house next to the Rockafella Centre, quite pricey but the most amazing steak and sides, and a wine list of over ---- wines..
The Mercer Hotel kitchen - very cool interiors, yummy food, quite pricey but yummy cocktails

My only complaints are that the air conditioner didn't get as cool as I like, and the restaurant was pretty lackluster in ambience and choices (our server was great, though). No complaints about the food, though. I'd stay here again.

My wife and I stayed here December -- - --th. Even though we arrived around -- am, our room was ready. The front desk personnel go out of their way to make you feel welcome. FOOD: The concierge had a great recommendation (Junior's on Shubert Alley ) for a fast dinner before our show at Times Square. This place specializes in getting you served in short time. I've stayed at the Palomar several times now; it's one of my favorite places to stay in the city. If you're there for business or pleasure, the location can't be beat: lots of things are within easy walking distance and Muni and BART stop right in front. There are tons of restaurants very close-by with a variety of price ranges and cuisines. The rooms are large by San Francisco standards and the staff has always been very friendly and helpful.
