Because the hotel is right on Market Street, some of the rooms can have a fair amount of street noise. Also, the lobby is pretty small. There's no coffee maker in the room, but there's water in the lobby and free wine at -pm, as well as coffee outside the restaurant in the morning.
Overall, I highly recommend it.

This hotel is within a business park so the location is out of the way. Not much around in terms of resturants & shops. The hotel does provide frequent shuttle service. The rooms were a true suite set up ( I think this use to be an Embassy Suites). Large bathrooms. Comfortable bed. Nice flat screen TV. Everything was super clean. All hotel employees were very nice & helpful. I had an early morning flight into Charlotte. Arrived to the hotel by -am and they graciously let me check right in - not even a raised eyebrow. I was extremly pleased with my experience - thank you Renaissance Charlotte Suites!
We stayed here over a weekend. The staff was very helpful and gave us tips and directions to the state fair. Good food in the hotel restaurant and very clean rooms and lobby.

I was a little skeptical when I opened the door and was greeted by a funky smell. Then I looked around the room and was disappointed at how tiny it was. 
As the evening set in, all of a sudden it was like the room was transformed. The lighting was perfect, the size didn't seem to matter as much, the funky smell was replaced with my perfume and lotion and the bed that looked lacking of linens was extremely cozy. 
I enjoyed the claw footed bath tub - that was a nice touch. Despite being about - blocks from Union Centre it was quiet. The floors were creaky but that's expected with an older building. 
The breakfast could use some work. Why go half way - it's a very French place - breakfast is served in the Jeanne D'arc restaurant - complete with statues and what looks like instruments of torture - serve a French breakfast. I would gladly pay an extra $-- for that.
The staff was extremely friendly and helpful and was a welcomed addition to the overall experience.
I would say it's my favourite place that I stayed at (out of - places) during my week long trip to California.
Very nice large room, the quality is as I would expect a good - star hotel to be. Our room was very large and comfortable. We paid about $---, so work on rates as $--- is too much.

I stayed here for business, but wouldn't be my first choice. The hotel rooms need to be updated, and with so many other hotel chains in the area offering free breakfast, I think Red Lion should do the same. On the plus side - Instead of waiting for a shuttle, you can just walk to this hotel from the airport. About a ---- minute walk, directly across the street. For an overnight stay, it's okay.

Cow Hollow Motor Inn is a JEWEL in San Francisco! Affordable, clean and a great location. We have walked to the marina area, Palace of Fine Arts, etc...The location is excellent for those wishing to use bus transportation. We have stayed there four times and have a fifth time coming up in May! Cannot wait.

Stayed here last week and found the location to be very convenient to Fisherman's Wharf, North Beach and Chinatown. The walls were very thin and it was noisy at night. The wireless connection was super bad so I would not select this hotel again when in town for business. The bar opens at -:--pm, we couldn't get a glass of wine before dinner!!!! Breakfast was included with the room and that was the best part of the stay.

Firstly I challenge anyone to find a hotel in downtown Chicago that can compare with Four Points for value for money, location, freindliness of staff and quality of accomodation.
We stayed at the Four Points at the begining of April ----, afetr a relatively short drive (go airport express, good value), from O Hare we arrived at the hotel and were greeted by smiling freindly staff who made checking in quick and easy and even supplied a map of the area, you need to use your room key to operate the elevator which is a great security measure.
We were on the seventh floor, there's a fitness room and pool (with a spa) on the fifth, which were both spotlessly clean. We were extremely pleased with our room, again spotless and big! you get much more room for your money as opposed to say New York.
With this being our first visit to Chicago we were keen to visit the sights, and thankfully due to the superb location of the hotel this made it so much easier, we were able to walk nearly everywhere except the United Center (to see the hawks) and Lincoln Park where we visited the zoo which we couldn't believe was free!! a super day out for the family, only being one street away from The Magnificent Mile meant that taking a leisurely stroll you were in the centre of downtown before you knew it. The cabs were cheap and drivers friendly and courteous. 
The hotel staff were more than happy to arrange cabs and even sorted out our transfer back to O Hare.
I cannot reccommend this place highly enough it was fantastic, and worthy of all the positive reviews posted on this site.

On a combined business-family getaway, we spent one night here, and would return. It is much prettier and more relaxing than a person from the Northeast would expect a major airport hotel to be. There was a neighborhood with a lot of restaurants and a nice Vons supermarket, just a very short drive away. Front desk staff was very helpful with directions. Walking along the bay, sitting on the balcony, and the small pool were all pleasant. It is not a vacation resort; it's a business-oriented airport hotel, but very nicely done.

Pros - Very close to airport, very quiet rooms (you cant hear the airplanes taking off even though it is right across from the airport), friendly staff, VERY comfortable beds with lots of pillows, large rooms, ice and vending machines close to all rooms, nicely appointed bathrooms, free shuttle (runs every -- min, no reservation needed), convenience store on site, ATM, warm cookies on check in.
Cons - Hotel is spread out so pay attention to how to get to your room as you may get lost,
Feather pillows (synthetic available on request), Pay parking ($-- self-day $-- valet-day),
warm cookies on check in.
We have stayed at this hotel several times, and others in the area. It may cost a little more to stay here, but we feel it is worth it for the quiet rooms and the very comfortable beds.

This place is incredible. The views from the rooftop are spectacular and the service was A+. The drink menu has some seriously delicious and refreshing cocktails, and our server was sweet as pie, always fast despite being at full capacity, and very friendly. We had a group of -- friends enjoy the sunset and our drinks on a clear Friday night. We were of course in cute dresses, but once the sun went down and it was chilly the hostess brought us blankets! So no need to worry about ruining your outfit with a lame coat, you'll be warm and toasty while you enjoy the night air and the cool views of Venice and beyond. A MUST when visiting LA, especially if you're looking for a young cool scene.

This is a small motel not a hotel in a fairly grotty part of LA. The rooms are basic but very clean and frankly has everything you need and free parking was a big plus. The staff were very pleasant and helpful and we received a welcome pack when we arrived which was a nice touch. The best thing about this place is the price, for what we got it was very good value. The location is the worst part. We prefer to stay somewhere where we can walk to a couple of nice restaurants. There was nothing around other than a couple of very grotty convenience stores. It would have been a great place for just one night but we were there for - so disappointed. Realistically, we wouldn't stay here again.

The hotel is about a - min walk from Fenway Park. There are a ton of great restaurants around the hotel. The front desk staff was great and vary professional. I only had two problems with my stay here. The parking is in a building next to the hotel and is not run by the hotel; it is run by a company called LAZ. We were not told about this at the time of booking. When we showed up to park the LAZ guys asked us for our keys to park our car for us because its a red sox game day and we cant self park here and that they had to do it. Kind of threw us off a bit, we didn’t really trust giving some strange guy our car keys. All went well with them though they are vary professional and kind. The hotel is located in a vary busy part of town. Get there early if there is a sox game or else you will be circling around the hotel waiting for the game crowd to leave. The room we stayed in is great if your looking for just a bed to sleep in. It was nothing special. The rate was a little high for what we got but id pay it again just for its location to Fenway.
Great downtown Seattle hotel, we stayed on the --th floor during -th of July weekend. We slept very well. It's about - blocks from the fish market.

This is our second stay at the Elysee and it didnt dissapoint. We had requested a room with a balcony as we had on our last stay but unfortunately we couldnt get one still the room we had, --- was fine with a huge and very comfortable bed( have to admit I did check the matress and all was clear) and two large windows.The room is at the front of the hotel though very little noise. As is usual the staff were fantastic,very pleasant and helpful at reception confirming reservations and providing directions and the staff in the club room always cheerful and charming.The wine and cheese evenings are a definite plus as sometimes we were too tired to eat out and found this just enough before an early night.We had planned to have drink in the Monkey Bar but it was closed for the weekend.There is much reference made to the single elevator however this was not a problem for us and we never had to wait for long.We very much enjoyed our stay at the Elysee and will be back again.

Although I originally intended to stay at the Double Tree Inn during my visit to Detroit for the Winter Blast Festival, due to an error by my friend, we ended up staying at the Westin. Personally, I feel that the Double Tree Inn is a far superior alternative for the price. The rooms are larger and the level of service at least meets or exceeds that of the Westin. However, there was little reason for complaint until this morning. After I had taken all of my things down to my car I realized that I'd left my cell phone in the room on the bed. I was absolutely certain of this as I'd read the morning news and checked the weather as I do EVERY day before getting started. 
To my surprise, upon returning to my room, the sheets had already been removed from the bed and were thrown into the corner of the room. Also, my phone was nowhere to be found. I attempted to have my friend call the phone and found that it had been turned off. I immediately sought out the housekeeping staff on the floor and when I found the housekeeper I asked if she'd cleaned room ----. She stated that she had not, but that she'd taken the sheets off the bed. I told her that I was certain I'd left my phone in the room on the bed, but she said that she had not seen it, but that she would go with me to the room to see if perhaps either of us had missed it. After we both thoroughly searched the room, I asked the housekeeper if I could attempt to call my phone from the room to see if it might ring. She said that she did not know the number to dial out from a hotel room phone so she could not assist me. I found it very unusual that a hotel employee would not be able to provide this information. Upon contacting guest services I was given the number to dial out and my phone again went straight to voicemail. When I stated that I knew someone had to have my phone because I knew the battery had a full charge (after charging all night) and that I never turn my phone off due to the nature of my job, she became visibly irritated and nervous. At this point I was fairly certain she had taken my phone. The housekeeper then took down my friend's phone number and stated that she would check with other housekeepers to see if anyone else had found the phone, again I found this unusual because it seemed that she was the only one working the floor and only the sheets had been taken off the bed (this did not seem like a job for more than one housekeeper). 
I then informed the housekeeper that I would notify someone at the front desk that my phone had been stolen from my hotel room. Again, the housekeeper appeared nervous and assured my friend and me that she would promptly notify us if any of the other housekeeping staff had seen the phone. When I informed the front desk of the apparent theft of my phone, security was notified and after about twenty minutes my phone """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""miraculously"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" showed up in the hands of the hotel staff. They informed me that the phone had been found turned off and under some towels on the floor of the bathroom. I knew that this was ludicrous as I had never taken my phone into the bathroom, I had last used it in the bedroom, and I would NEVER have turned my phone off. I knew at once that the housekeeper had stolen my phone and returned it when it was clear that I knew she had taken it and that I was going to take the issue up with security. However, the security staff was rude, dismissive, and made it clear that they did not intend to pursue the matter any further. I'm sure that they could have at least made the effort to see if the housekeeper had again entered the room instead of dismissing my complaint as some kind of weird conspiracy theory. For me, the ending of this trip really marred my perception of the professionalism and trustworthiness of the staff of the Westin Book Cadillac. Not only is there a good chance that your valuables will be subject to theft, but there is also a good chance that you will be treated rudely by a tactless security staff with poor customer service skills. I can think of no reason to stay at this hotel again, especially considering the myriad of other hotels in the downtown Detroit area with a comparable or superior standard of comfort and an exceedingly higher level of customer service.

The hotel staffw ere lovely and welcoming.
However, the hotel itself was not very clean, very run down in general, and in need of refurbishment.
BUT great great location! To be reommneded for budget travellers, if you're not too fussy! the price was great too.

I've stayed at the Indigo Chelsea @--x in the past year for business and my review reflects appreciation for their consistency in service as much as it does the specific features mentioned. I am a professional, self-employed female, married w-adult children, residing in Suffolk County,Long Island and working in Manhattan. Since I often work late and miss the last train of the day, I routinely stay overnight, at hotels in the Midtown or Chelsea area. Combined with occasional stays with husband for dinner-theater, I stayed at Manhattan hotels -- nights in ----. Most of my stays are at hotels in the Hilton family due to the array of choices in proximity to my office and the generous perks for diamond members. 
 While the Indigo is a longer walk from my office than several other good hotels-- I continue to return, consider my stays there a treat, and have never been disappointed. 
The lobby has an artsy, youthful look yet a warm, appealing feel. Both the staff and fellow patrons are friendlier and more helpful than one might expect in New York City. The murals on the corridors of each floor are lovely and invigorating. While the rooms are average in size (for Manhattan), the decor, such as mirrors framed like the sun and natural wood floors, seems to enlarge the footage.

The Aveda toiletries add a nice touch as do the cotton robes (always fresh) and the slippers wrapped in plastic. Televisions are high quality, large and offer an array of free channels, most in HD --there's no need to spend $----- for in-room movies you never wished to see in the first place. The hotel offers - HBO channels with different movies-serials-specials on each round-the-clock, including one in Spanish and one that's family-oriented. Each room also has a modern (Keurig-type) coffee-maker with a generous supply free of charge.
My final comment is most relevant to patrons who check in late pm or early am hours, and on nights I work very late -- it factors significantly in choosing the Indigo over other hotels. 
Checking into NYC hotels at -- pm or later can be very trying on busy nights when decent hotels are full, even if your reservation is guaranteed and-or pre-paid. After a handful of weird experiences in recent years, I've learned to confine myself to hotels in the Hilton, Priority Club, and Affinia chains (all reliable) on late work nights. On one occasion, for example, I was told my ($---) room was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""being prepared"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" at --:-- pm and -- mins. later, checked into a room with fresh clouds of cigarette smoke, a residual odor of pot smoke (despite it being a M****** w- a non-smoking policy) and a half-eaten Whopper in the garbage. Another time, at a - star hotel, I was told to wait -- mins. before getting a long-winded apology from the manager. Apparently my (prepaid) room was given away despite the clerk logging my - pm call that I'd arrive at -- pm. I was offered a free upgrade to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""deluxe"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" at an affiliated hotel --- in another borough! Rather than navigating the NYC subway system at midnight or spending $-- on a taxi, I said no thanks and dozed in Penn Station for an hour as the next train home was -:-- am.
At the Indigo Chelsea, whether or not I call in advance to alert the desk of my late arrival --- the evening manager, Diane, (if she's not a manager, she ought be) is exceptional, with her welcoming attitude and professional demeanor. The Indigo Chelsea is a gem in many regards, and I strongly recommend it for both business and recreational stays. It's an excellent choice for anyone arriving at or departing from Penn Station -- hardly a - minute walk -- and easily accessible to midtown, both east and west.

I stayed in this hotel the weekend before Christmas last December for - nights. I picked it based on reviews and was not disappointed. The location was great, just - blocks from the Empire state building a - blocks the other direction from Macys. (Macys had --Hr opening that weekend)!. Also the train station is only - blocks away. The hotel, though small and narrow was very clean and new looking. The room though small (as is standard) had everything I needed and was very clean and nice. I was on something like the --th floor and had a view of the top of the Empire building out my window.

Breakfast as a buffet and was included in the rate. The breakfast room is a bit small and has no windows- both mornings I had trouble getting a seat and a few people ended up eating standing up. I gues it was rush hour for breakfast!. The food selection was average - cerals, doughnuts, bagels etc. However it was enough to get me started for the day.
Overall I was very happy with the hotel selection and would stay there again. Christmas is also a great time to visit New York! There was a great buzz about the place.

Writing this review while sitting in the lounge of the Casablanca, sadly about to leave for the airport. The location is ideal, just around the corner from Times Square. The staff could not be more polite, helpful and friendly. The relaxed atmosphere of Ricks Cafe is ideal for the plentiful continental style breakfast including fresh fruit salad, pastries, breads, cereals, bagels, teas and coffee, as well as for the wine and cheese reception with nibbles, which allows guests to gather before their evening activities. Would highly recommend the New York Pass, which offers great value to a large number of attractions - and the Casablanca is a great central starting point for many of them. Our room was clean, comfortable and quiet. I cannot speak too higjhly of this hotel - -----.

And I also commend the hotel's restaurant, which produced surprisingly good food. My personal lunch favorite: the grilled cheese sandwich and tomato soup, which, although not haute cuisine, might have been the best that I've ever had. I really enjoy this hotel. It is huge (over -,--- rooms) and somewhat chaotic when you enter but a really fun place. Great bars right in the hotel! I have stayed here two times and I really enjoyed both trips. The location really could not get any better. The room was modern and comfortable. I would definitely recommend this hotel to friends.

We just got back from - nights at Humphreys and we LOVED it. Our room was on the first floor facing the gardens and it was beautiful! The pool was very nice with a great bar. 
The concerts did not bother us (but we were located on the opposite end of the hotel), when we closed the patio door we couldn't hear it at all.
Our - and - year olds loved it and we will definitely stay here again. I highly recommend it to families with children.
The staff was great and the location was perfect for day trips around San Diego.

Stayed one night between Xmas and New Year's. Got a great price for a lovely hotel just - blocks off Michigan Ave. using a AAA discount. Hotel decor is contemporary and clean. Very appealing. Friendly front desk staff. Walkable to many Chicago attractions. We got by without a car by taking the Metra train and walking from the station - about a -- --- min walk.

I was here on business, so unfortunately I did not get to experience some of the extra activities the hotel offers. First off, I would like to say that the staff was very friendly and helpful. I had a small repair that needed to be done to my room, which was done expeditiously. I think this place is good for business travelers who need to start the morning with a good meal and wind down after work. The breakfast was hearty, and the social hour was adequate. I was expecting more; however, I realize that was my own expectation based on experiences with other hotels--the Brookshire stayed true to the meaning of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""social hour."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Also, you definitely can't beat the location. It's within walking distance from the Harbor, which was great.
I only have - complaints: Although there is an individual control for the A-C, there seems to be an overriding master control. It was pretty warm in the room in the mornings and at night. Regardless of how low I turned the thermostat, it remained almost -- degrees. It seemed like the cool air was reserved for the afternoons, because when I would return from work in the early evening, it was nice and cool. By the time I would return from dinner, it was warm again. I didn't bother to complain, because it was obvious that the hotel wanted it that way. Secondly, there were no towel racks in the bathroom. I don't think I have ever been in a hotel bathroom that didn't have this. The bathrooms are very small, but I think the hotel should be able to fit at least - rack in there somewhere.

The sign out front says """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""A Unique Bed and Breakfast"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", but for those familiar with B&Bs you should know that this is more like a hotel or inn, in that you don't get acquainted with the host or sit down to a great breakfast with the other guests. Continental breakfast (store bought pastries and cold cereal) is served with plastic spoons and Styrofoam bowls, brought to your room by the staff. The bath towels were very small. There was a plunger beside the toilet which we had to use several times in our --night stay in the Southwestern themed room. The location is fantastic for walking or cycling to Balboa Park. The price is reasonable for the area. Good housekeeping.

Unfortunately the Radisson Lexington is a lovely old building in desperate need of a refit and refresh. The lifts are fast but tired looking as are all the carpets and walkways.
It is good (relatively) value but you could probably do better and will no doubt wish you'd stayed at the nearby W hotel or the Hilton. 
We breakfasted downstairs once, it was ok, a rushed NYC experience so fun from that regard but the food was pretty poor and my fiance did get sick later in the day so not really very good.
Across the road the Hilton's breakfast - brunch area is excellent so try there instead.
The staff were helpful although I somehow joined club carlsson which I didn't really want to do. Weird.

I would hate to start off negative but the girl who checked me in had a crappy attitude. I wish I could remember her name, I know it begins with a D. She even rolled her eyes at me at one point! The other staff was absolutely amazing, definitely made up for miss grump. Tammy went out if her way to help me on several occasions. Because of her I will come back, as well as Brandy who was a sweetheart. the rooms were beautiful and clean. All in all it was a wonderful stay.

Nice hotel in a great location. Loved the room's large and well-appointed bathroom. Great respite from the lively and crowded Union Square area. Weak points - the mediocre and over-priced breakfast and staff who appeared to be scripted and lacking in genuine warmth.

The hotel is very old and dirty. Staffs are very unfriendly. Room is small and extremely dirty. 
bed quality sucks! its like a JELLO .When we walked in our room we noticed that bedsheets are dirty and stinking. So we asked for new bedsheets but the new ones weren't clean either. you could see dirty spots on them... So we went and bought our own bedsheets from the closest store... after all this hassle at the last night of our stay we saw a COCKROACH is walking on our bed. We left the room to report it to the manager , but the manager wasn't on site and we didn't get any apology from the staff... So, we left the hotel and we got a room in different hotel for a high price due to last minute booking.... 
We finally got our money back from pickwick but it ruined our trip
IT WAS REALLY A BAD EXPERIENCE... Please BEWARE...

I stayed at the Hilton for one night with my mother who was visiting the area. Great location to walk around the Gas Lamp district and tons of shops-restaurants. The hotel is directly on the water so there is a bit of a breeze but great views of Mission Bay. Plenty of options in the hotel for food, drinks, coffee (Starbucks) and gym. 
I would definitely stay there again!

I chose to stay at this relatively new Hampton Inn again after a successful stay in March. This is a lovely property, very near Chinatown. I have stayed in two rooms - one a spacious king executive room with a sofa and one an average king. Both were quiet and well appointed. Bathtubs are small and shallow, but since most of us shower these days, it's not a big issue. Free high speed internet is great - but it is only wireless in the lobby. Tip - if your traveling cord is short, ask to borrow one from the front desk - they have very long connection cords for the room that will enable you to work from somewhere other than the desk. On both visits, this was a very popular hotel with tourist families. Breakfast is noisy and despite the staff's best efforts, they can't keep up with kids' spills. On my second trip, the ac wasn't working in the first room I tried. They responded quickly, moved me within -- minutes and were very, very nice. It is easy to catch a cab on the busy corner nearby.

Can find no fault with this hotel for the price paid. Location is excellent (just across the street from the famous Brown Palace) and one block from the --th Street Mall. Room was clean and comfortable, no problems at all. Full buffet breakfast included in the price was a plus. Would definitely recommend this hotel.

Great location in the historic district. We were able to walk everywhere very easily. Food in the Italian restaurant was the best ever. A little pricey but great...especially the wine selection. The tour of wines were so much fun. They were brought on a sort of wine glass tree with a few ounces of each wine selection and they were really fine wines. The ladies at the front desk were very helpful with our plans. A bowl of apples are always available at the front desk to grab on your way out for a snack during your travels. There is a starbucks just around the corner and a GREAT little bakery with the best cookies-cupcakes. Can't think of the name but in a tiny pink building. We got a cookie every day when we walked back to our room. Our room was very large. Nice, comfy king bed and very clean. Our only disappointment was that the view room was overlooking a large freeway until you look out onto the river. The freeway noise was pretty loud during the day but I didn't seem to notice it at night. We stayed on the third floor which was the highest floor. Our room did not get cleaned until very late on one day. We came back to our room at about - and it was still unmade. When we asked them to clean it they did so promptly. Otherwise it was a good stay and good location. I would stay here again.

My husband planned a surprise weekend getaway for us in Denver. We are from Wichita, Ks and were extremely disappointed. He upgraded us to a King Executive Suite and it was horrible. He signed up for a King and we got two queens. When we called down to let them know fo their mistake they accused us fo not reserving the right room, even thought we had a printed reservation confirmation for a King. They didn't comp us a night or even try to make things right. Our AC unit sounded like a frieght train running through the room. Very ran down. We stayed on the --th floor of the tower so maybe the other side is better? Also had a -- min wait in line to check in. The valet parking was wonderful and the breakfast buffet was good too. We were told by the local to stay in the Westin or the Hyatt. We will not return to the Sheridan in DT Dever. The location was good, but there are other hotels in the area that are better. We were sadly disappointed by this hotel.

We booked a room with a queen size bed and got a mini suite instead. 
The room was clean. The bathroom was clean. The furniture is old and rotting. The bed was clean but not that comfortable. The door to our patio would not lock. The lighting was not great. The neighborhood is not good. We could hear the ambulances passing by all night. Our room had central air but did not work. At one point my husband checked to see the temperature of our room and it was -- degrees!!! We didn't have breakfast and were quick to leave the next morning. Would never stay again.
I highly recommend this hotel. It is beautiful. The rooms are large and the service was -st rate. We also enjoyed the pool and health club on the --th floor of the hotel.

This is a high quality Georgetown hotel. The staff is polite and friendly. The concierge is very accommodating but made a few mistakes. I guess when you present yourself as unimpeachable you must then deliver sans error. The room was large and nice, but the temperature control did not work. The bathroom lacks a lock on the toilet door and the tub would not drain. But, the bathroom was well appointed. A comfortable recliner or comfortable chair and ottoman would have been nice. The flat panel TV was adequate but had an international program that was confusing. Pay per view movies were either hard to find or absent. Basically, I would certainly stay again, but as a Four Seasons Hotel, it could use some tweaking. The front door staff was great.

The travelocity site erroneously lists this hotel as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""opening July ----"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which is incorrect... we stayed in April ---- and the hotel staff indicated that it has been open since February.

Although its situated just around the corner from a main road and across the street from a strip mall, it's frontside faces small forrest of pine trees that wrap about --- of the way around the hotel. After check-in on a late thursday afternoon, we meandered into a lovely """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lounge"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" area where a manager's special offered a really impressive make-your-own-taco bar, with gobs of fresh chips and salsa, soft drinks, a wide selection of Wolfgang Puck coffees (always available), all for free. A real treat was the pool and spa which thankfully was heated just right to offset the unseasonably cool weather we had. We spent most of the afternoon in the pool surrounded by the local """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""forrest"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which gave made it a very peaceful serene environment. Because the hotel was not particular busy the two nights we were there, we had the pool to ourselves. 
Finally, the location is minutes from wide variety of nice restaurants... we ate a the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Seven Bridges"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" down the road about a quarter mile. And it only took us about -- min to get downtown to the and to the Zoo. 
All in all, the hotel was a really nice surprise and a provided a surprisingly relaxing getaway in the big city. Highly recommended.

We've been to this resort many times and each time has been very enjoyable. We've stayed bayside and in the garden villas and always have had great rooms. The rooms are clean. The staff we have encountered have always been friendly. Dive-in movies at the main pool are fun for the kids. The resort is beautiful and well maintained.

We did lots of research and when our first and second choice hotels weren't available we decided to go for this one which had some reasonable reviews. We were really impressed with the hotel nothing fancy but the staff were all really friendly and helpful. We had a slight flood in the bathroom (our fault) and maintenance were quick and sorted the problem out with no fuss. The bathroom was a bit small but the room was fine with two double beds we were on --th floor overlooking --th Street. We didn't find the room to be noisy in fact one of the advantages of this hotel is it is just away from the noise main routes through NY but convenient enough for all the attactions. Didn't use the hotel restaurants as there were a couple of diners just along the street which were great value. We would definately consider this hotel next time we come to NYC.

We stayed here one week for our first time visit to NY. The location was perfect for shopping, eating and sightseeing. Close to the subway, broadway, time square, fith avenue, central park etc.
The room was big, clean and quiet. The free internet service was great and made our stay i NY easier.
Next time in NY we probably chose a hotel in the meat packing district but for a first time visitor the hotel is great.

The room was a fantastic deal for $-- per night. The room was clean and nicely appointed with a large, flat screen tv, microwave, and large mini fridge with a separate freezer compartment.
I found it comparable to a Holiday Inn Express or a Hampton, with the exception of the lower quality bedding and towels. I stayed - nights, and the housekeeping during the stay wasn't very professional. The bed was sloppily made and a piece of paper was left on the floor.
 The free breakfast offered a plethora of white carbs to choose from.
One turn off was the congregation of smokers out front when I arrived. Despite the fact that it is a non-smoking hotel, the hallways still smell like old musty cigarette smoke.
I am not sure I would have been as satisfied had I paid the full room rate.

Have stayed at this hotel several times in the past and I think the rooms are excellent value - large, clean and well set out with sinks and televisions and towels. The location is great with subway stops nearby and cafes in the neighbourhood. However I had read about problems with noisy air conditioners in previous Tripadvisor reviews and I have to say, everyone is right. Hotel --, you really need to sort this issue out because those airconditioners are horrible! I think it is the units above dripping all over the ones below, the noise is phenomenal and on a rainy AND hot night it can be impossible to ignore. Plus we had issues with our light bulbs which meant they kept flickering even after they were switched off - we asked for this to be fixed several times but it never was. Otherwise a great value stay with very clean rooms and bathrooms - just be wary of these issues!

Excellent hotel, great room (free upgrade, with fizz & chocs for our anniversary). Very clean, tidy and welcoming. Good free breakfast, free coffee-tea all day, beautiful roof top terrace with bar overlooking Empire State.
All staff very pleasant and so helpful. Good food in the Metro Grill, we would come back every night for a cocktail before bed! Everyone works so hard to make your stay as comfortable as possible.
Highly recommended for position, subway at end of street, Maceys on the corner, Empire State one block. Try Brendan's Bar & Grill opposite too for good food and drinks.
Thank you Hotel Metro for a wonderful week !!

What a lovely find! We checked in on a Thursday evening and were invited to a warm wine reception (with good wine and a friendly sommalier) and the concierge helped us make reservations at a four star restaurant. The staff was unpretentious and courteous. Unfortunately, our babysitter called to let us know that our son had a fever of ---. We immediately had to check out but the manager said, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Don't worry about the charge."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" We never got to stay the night but so appreciated his generosity! We will definitely reschedule!

This hotel is great value for money. The location is excellent with Central Park and Times Square only a few blocks away. The rooms are spacious and clean but a bit dated. The hotel could do with a renovation. Don't let this put you off though. I have stayed here twice now and would definitely stay again. It is listed as a --- star hotel so it isn't pretending to be something it isn't. :)
after reading reviews was not sure about staying here. after spending - day at the milford it was great would surely stay there again

Sweet receptionist. Nice concierge, not very knowledgeable of the area. Nice breakfast - $-- for two omlettes and two juices. Dirty bathroom. Dust and pubic hair in several different spots around the bathroom and the bathtub. Lukewarm water in shower. Called reception, they promised to send someone to fix the shower and clean the rooms. On the afternoon on the next day water was hot, but bathroom still dirty with pubic hair remaining in several different spots. Nice pool with very attentive lifeguard. Chambermaids noisily kept slamming doors all morning making it hard to sleep.

Did the Clipper combination from Victoria. Very impressed with how clean & friendly the staff were. The free shuttles were handy & very convenient to use. Free breakfast was ok but no meat. Didn't do dinner but had appies & drinks.. Don't try the sliders. Really to far to walk anywhere so thats why the free shuttle I guess. Pool & hot tub looked good but no change room!. To many kids so didn't use. Very well run outfit. Get the higher floors . The roar on the second floor was a little noisy.

We stayed at this Embassy Suites on the first and last nights of a touring trip around Colorado. Classic Embassy Suites, superb happy hour and breakfast, fine workout facility, immaculate room, and conveniently close to both the airport and downtown.

Absolutely wonderful! The rooms are great and well appointed; not much closet space though. Room service was fablous (although be careful the service staff waits for a tip but there's a --% tip and service fee already calculated in the bill and when confronted he told me that it was a slow night and --% wasn't enough). The valet guys were wonderful, patient and understanding. The coffee shop was having some staffing issues but when staffed was a great place for coffee and conversation. Edgar is the friendliest and most accomodating staff member!

The Marriott Downtown is ideally located in downtown Philadelphia, which itself differtiates positively frm many other US downtown location. WElcome at the reception desk is friendly, check-in was fast. The room is spacious, but I had not the impression that it had been renovated lately. Housekeeping reluctant. No noise isolating windows, so you experience what's going on on the street quite well. Overall the price-value is poor.
WLAN still costly.

Stayed here December - January for - nights. After arriving a day late due to airline delays and after commuincating this with a female manager regarding my delay, we arrived to what can only be described as a fantastic customer service experience. The said female manager had upgraded our Hilton net direct booking for a King room, to an amazing executice king on the top floor with a private balcony. The room was huge, comfortable and a killer view of the bay. The balcony was fantastic. The bed was extremely comfortable and the room itself was in immaculate condition. Maid service was also excellent. Executive room facilities were also great. The only things I was a bit disppointed with were, the buffet breakfast we had our first morning in the restaurant, way over priced for what you get, also the cocktail bar, there was a waitress who thought her job was not to serve the customers, but to stand and joke with friends and the bar tender for most of the time we spent there. Having said that these points were minor compared to the experience we had with the lady manager and the room we were given.
Also the location is fantastic, you have North Beach (great italian), Chinatown and downtown right on your door step, fishermans wharf and Union Square all so close to walk to.
I cannot say enough about how good this hotel was.

I was extremely impressed with the Seaport Hotel and would highly recommend it to anyone looking to stay in the seaport region of Boston. There is nothing negative I can say about our stay. We were in town for a conference at the BCEC and our group consisted of - adults and - teens. All staff members went out of their way to help us and absolutely no one made us feel like second class citizens because our group was not comprised of business travelers. I was especially impressed with the concierge and the Front Desk members for their exemplary """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""above and beyond"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" attitude and service.

If you want to see DC, this is a great location from which to start and end your day. While in appearance to be in a business district, the walk to the Capitol is five minutes, Union Station is at most a ten minute walk (A Metro station is also at Union Station). Other reveiws I had read prior to booking complained about no place in area to eat other than hotel restaurant. I did not even require the hotel restuaruant. Nearby Union Station had and incredible eatery selection, from fast food to fine dining. Chinatown is also a ten minute walk from the hotel. Cabs were always available in front of hotel. Hotel lobby undergoing massive renovation during my stay; the check in staff told us they would provide a room where we would not be bothered by the noise, which was absolutely true.
I arrived in DC by train and departed out of Reagan National Airport. As stated earlier, the train station is a stone's throw from the hotel, and the cab ride to the airport was fifteen minutes and a $-- fare. Rooms are a bit above average; I loved the four pillows on each bed!

Stayed a week in October. Excellent location if you want to stay in this part of town. The pluses are that """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Seinfeld"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" neighborhood feel and the fact that you are away from the chaos of midtown. The minuses are mostly mediocre restaurants (although plenty of them), and very little nightlife. The hotel was comfortable and modern, and the staff friendly. The staff was, however, extremely young and it seemed as if they were students trying to make extra money rather than folks seriously looking to get ahead in the hotel industry. The two (not a day over --) doormen spent most of their time trying to pick up the even younger looking girls at the front desk. I thought this comical, but if you are looking for a polished staff, be prepared to be disappointed. I should also note that there was no bar in the lobby, so it was not the type of place that would lend itself to meeting other travelers.
I have stayed at both the Lucerne and the Excelsior in the past. On The Ave. is just as comfortable as those two, but lacks their charm. The Excelsior has the best rooms overall, but some disagreeable staff people. The Lucerne has a great staff and lots of charm (and one of the few good restaurants in the area), but a number of rooms with odd configurations, i.e. the door to your suite might open into the bedroom). Like the restaurants and other hotels in the area, On The Avenue is good...but not great.

Everything about this place is perfect...everything. The service, the beds, the rooms, Keurig coffee makers. The pool area is a wonderful place to spend the day. Extremely romantic, and food is incredible. Try the poutine! It's a great location, but we really didn't want to leave the property. Will be back!

I recently stayed on property because it was close to AT&T park for the Giants game I attended. The hotel had a very modern design and feel to it in the lounging areas and room design itself. The check in was easy and we went right to our room. Very large room with wonderful city-scapes and beautiful night time lights. In addition, we had a treadmill in our room?!?!?! Not sure if that was standard, but it was an interesting addition. The only peaceful area of that floor was the bathroom in the shower with the water running. Other than that, there were many city sounds and people sounds to keep any light sleeper awake. Since our stay was just one night, it was not horrific, but I'm not sure I would stay there again. The price of convenience should not be the sacrifice of a good night's sleep.

While not worthy of the -.- stars given it by hotwire (-.- to - are more like it), there's nothing really wrong with this financial district hotel, if you can get it at a reasonable rate. Rooms are smallish, but adequate for a business stay, or a weekend, tho romantic, it ain't! The main problem is that it just isn't close to anything. Tadich Grill is the only """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""name"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" restaurant nearby, altho the hotel's own restaurant isn't bad, if you like beer and pub food. Skip the expensive breakfast there and go to McDonald's a couple of blocks away. Hotel is close enough to Muni and Bart so it's easy to get anywhere. A couple of desk clerks didn't speak English very well, and-or were very busy, so it was easier to go across the street to the Meriden and ask the concierge there for assistance.
I'd stay here again for the $-- Hotwire rate, but I wouldn't be excited about it.

Spent - nights here couldn't fault it. Thought it was one of the best places I've stayed. In saying that, I never used the pool or the dinning area, just stayed in it.
Was there for -st wedding anniversary.
Good to get to JFK site and being a Dallas (TV show) fan it was handy to jump the train to Southfork.
Would go again.

The hotel room provided a spacious, modern room to sleep in while visiting New York. Friendly staff. Limited services, but what they offered was good. Especially liked having free internet and workout room. If I had to be picky and find faults .... no ipod docking station and some noise from the elevators. 
It's not the kind of hotel you lounge around and think, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""What a great hotel."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" The whole point is to provide a nice base for visitting New York. And for that, it was prefect. Wonderful location that was near the tourist areas, but not in a tourist area. Away from the hoards (well, it's still in Manhattan, so there are lots of people... just not hoards of tourists.) It's on the border of a business zone and a neighborhood filled with shops and restaurants for residents, not tourists. But if you want the tourist stuff, it's easy to get to. Much is walkable. And if you want to take the subway, you've got access to several lines from a station on the block.

Have just returned from a - day stay. Fantastic hotel, the concierge Tanya went out of her way to ensure we got the best from our stay, so much so that in - days we did the helicopter tour, went up the Empire State, did the horse and carriage through Central Park, visited Grand Central Station, Tiffany's Macy's Bloomindales, all the shops on -th Avenue, - restaurants and had a limo ride as well! - of us stayed in a - bed suite, which was clean, spacious and had great views. There was complimentary cheese and wine, coffee and tea and Tanya even sent wine to our room one evening while we were getting ready to go out. The location is central for all the main attractions. We chose to travel by taxi as opposed to using the bus or underground, the most we paid was $-- to get to the ferry for the Statue of Liberty.
Would definitely return to this hotel.

his is a hotel I would thoroughly suggest you use if you would like to be only a - minute walk from The Walk of Fame on Hollywoo-d Blvd ( you can view the Hollywood sign from there).
This is a clean and fairly modern hotel in a courtyard shape with a swimming poll and lounging area utilizing the courtyard. The staff are very helpful and polite and happy to point out places of interest and book tours of the rich and famous. Breakfast is included and each room has WiFi and a fridge (nice to store any wine or beer you may wish to purchase from the store just across the street). Loads of nice restaurants in walking distance including a Hawaiian BBQ and Russian restaurant on the same street as the hotel.
For a real treat try Musso and Franks just down from the Grauman Chinese Theater. Been there since ---- and has entertained almost every star in the last --- years (Chaplain had his own table there) Big Prime Rib was $--.-- but it was worth it just for the experience and sitting there you would swear it was the ----'s. On the other side of the street is The Pig and Whistle where I had the best Chicken Piccata I have every had. One last point. Over the road from the hotel is a little club called The Woods. After you have park the car (free under ground parking) it would be well worth a visit for a nightcap before you turn in. There is not enough good things I can say about this hotel which I would have loved to have spent another weeks stay in.
Good deal @$---.-- per night.

I stayed at the SLS only one night travelling to LA for business. Really cool and beautiful hotel with a good location near shopping and restaurants and service minded staff. Though I do think the lighting is too dark for a business traveller with work to do, as previous reviewers have mentioned. The pool on the roof is also very nice.
There is nothing wrong with the hotel, it is really beautiful and rooms are lovely with comfortable beds and amazing bathrooms. TV is an enormous flat screen and everything is just top class.
My only negative comments are the overly expensive extras, that should not be extras in a hotel of this standard. Internet costs -- dollars per DAY, which is just crazy these days, especially when they make a big deal about lending you a lap top... For the loan of an adapter I was charged -- (refundable, of course) and breakfast is a massive -- for the tasty but somewhat small buffet. This to me seems strange when rooms are quite pricy and clientel posh - do I really need to first reserve --- dollars on my credit card for minibar and then -- for an adapter? And to me --- dollars for an overnight stay is way too much money. 
I also think it's strange not to give any extras at a hotel of this standard. Internet costs as does everything in the room, and I mean e-v-e-r-y-t-h-i-n-g. From the small piece of chocolate to the designer dice to the minibar snacks to the schampoo bottles - everything has a price tag. And you do not get anything when you check in, not even a mint on the pillow. When you pay for this standard a complementary fruit basket would be a nice touch. Instead you have a -- dollar price tag on the bottle of water that looked like a welcoming gift. Unclassy.
I stayed in a room with an extra door, I guess it can be opened to make the next door room to a family room. This caused me problems. My neighbour decided to take someone """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""home"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for the night and woke me up at -:--. I thought I had Mary J Blige in my room but soon noticed it was his stereo blasting away. I called about this twice and the second time he kind of got the message. I was able to fall asleep but I do wish they had been more firm. I told them I had been travelling for almost -- hours and had meetings in the morning but they where unable to just tell my neighbour that music is not ok AT ALL at - in the morning... At - I was woken up by some lovely moaning that really did not leave anything to the imagination. This is just silly for a hotel that wants to be sleek and cool. They should invest in some soundproofed doors. I hate to think what small kids would have been asking mommy would they have stayed in my room. Of course my neighbours lack of brains is not the hotels fault but I just wish they would have offered me to change rooms or told my neighbour to just turn off the music completely.

This was my first holiday i took without my parents and as expected was quite nervous to be alone in NYC with just one of my friends, but the staff were amazing and extremely helpful! they gave us advice on which subway trains to catch to go places to where was good to eat! only problem we had was that we booked a room with - double beds and we arrived to find one double, but they switched us the next day when a room was available (although we were out at the time they switched us and couldnt understand why our entry cards wouldnt work in our old room's door!!) they even moved all our stuff and put it in exactly the same place were it was in the other room, even down to where are toiletries were placed in the bathroom!! i strongly recommend this place!!

Although the hotel is located away from all the action, it’s only a short (--min) bus ride to Santa Monica. So if you are keen to go to the beach or to down-town Santa Monica, but don't want to spend too much $$$, then this is a great hotel.
The room I had was very spacious, wonderful decor (as shown on their website), very comfortable bed and everything was in great order. Although I thought the internal courtyard would be noisy, it certainly wasn’t.
The staff were very friendly and happy to help out. It is however a shame that most of the windows face the courtyard and first-floor walkways and don’t have sheer curtains to allow the guests to open the drapes without being seen by passersby.
I would certainly stay here again.

We had two small children and had enough room for all of us. The bathrooms are large with a tub and separate shower. The concierge service was very good. They seemed very knowledgeable about the areas restaurants. The only two complaints we had was the restaurant at the hotel, Pesca, had bad service on two different occasions. On two different occasions we waited an extremely long time to get service at the restaurant. Once for a to-go order and another to get a glass of wine at the bar. The other complaint is the valet is a little expensive ($---day) and they take ----- minutes to get your car. Call down to the valet before going down to the lobby. It will save you some time. The hotel is located in a very busy part of the Riverwalk with many restaurants within walking distance. The Alamo is also within a ten minute walk. Overall, we will stay at this hotel again.

Got a great pre-paid internet rate and really enjoyed the suite! Found the service at the front desk, in the bar and breakfast area just OK. The location worked really well for us the location we were visiting in the area. Good mall and area stores, good selection of restaurants in the area.

Once again, we stayed at the Hotel Edison for our Memorial Day visit to New York. As always, we love this hotel. While the rooms are not fancy, the location is fantastic and the rate is outstanding, very reasonable by New York standards. While some of these reviews talked about rude staff, we have always found them helpful, and we stay here two to three times a year.
And while people talk about rooms, seriously, if you're in New York, how much time are you going to spend in our hotel room? Between theater, restaurants, walking the city and the park, and visiting with friends, we see it to sleep. Give me a clean room in a good location, and I'm happy.
Only complaint, which others have noted, is the lack of electric outlets. It's an old building.
Still our New York choice!

After a disastrous experience at the Essex House, I moved over to the Warwick. What a difference! Instead of being rude and condescending like they were at Essex House, the staff went out of their way to be friendly and accommodating. The room was bigger than at the Essex House and less expensive. All in all, a very pleasant experience. Highly recommended

Spent a week at this hotel with my wife for our --th wedding anniversary.
Good location, near Grand Central Station. We stayed on the top floor in a suite with dining-living area, kitchenette and large, spacious bedroom. Very quiet, with height above ground and glazing keeping out all the street noise and effective A-C maening the rooms were a comfortable temperature amid the heatwave outside.
Bed very comfy, bathroom with rain shower pretty good, though shower power on the low side and had an annoying habit of turning the water flow into the bathtub mid shower. TV reception was a bit poor on some of the channels.
Kitchen facility was useful for simple-ready meals, and although there were pots & utensils there was no kettle, toaster etc. Big fridge was great for ice making however and the Amish market further down E--th street was useful for supplies.
We didn't use the restaurant, and enjoyed our own breakfasts in the room, usually dining out in the evening. Staff were friendly & helpful. Business centre was often full - free computer use but only - terminals...
Views over the East River and Chrysler building were fab.

Stayed here for my girlfriend's birthday over a weekend in June. While the rooms were on the smallish side, they were nicely decorated and the bed was extremely comfortable. I had called prior to our trip to have the concierge make dinner reservations for us. I had casually mentioned to him that we were making the trip to celebrate her birthday and upon arrival in our room we found a compimentary birthday cake and bottle of champage. During our stay, the staff was extremely friendly, polite, and helpful. We found the concierge staff to be especially helpful. We are looking forward to another trip to Seattle and stay at the Monaco!

We stayed at this hotel on October -st, ----. What a gorgeous place to stay. I had requested a room facing the canal, which even though it was raining was a great view. Katie on the front desk when we checked in was super, super kind & helpful. The hotel was in a quiet area of downtown, and I'd dare say a safe area as we walked, (our own choosing), to a restaurant down by the Capitol building. It was a very clean hotel and the bed was quite comfortable as well. Now that we know this hotel is here, we'll take the extra time to get off the interstate and go downtown for sure.

I was lucky enough to be invited to a very nice business conference in Boston, held at the Fairmont Copley Plaza. The Grand Dame has had a very impressive makeover. Lots of Glitter, and not short of Glam. I felt a little out of place, being the basic country bumpkin. However, they were very, very gracious, the food was outstanding, and the service was unsurpassed. I enjoyed getting insights of their make over and items in progress from Ralph, a very attentive attendant at all of our meals. He was just an example of lots of eager help from the front door to the maid service. We stayed at the Ritz at Central park last year and these people could give them a very good run for the money.

We stayed at the IC Times Square for one weekend night in mid-November ---- with a family of -. As a former Manhattanite, I have a to agree that this hotel is a welcome addition to what was a gritty neighborhood, but like most of the periphery of Midtown, is now enjoying a broad based renewal. 
Our stay was very enjoyable, and we found the property stylish and comfortable. We stayed on the --rd floor in a very quiet room with two beds. If you stay in this class of hotel either domestically in the USA or internationally, you'll find the IC TS to be very much in line with your expectations: nice view, nice bath, great towels, and quality amenities. 
We arrived on the early side (- a.m.), dropped bags & valeted the car, and checked in. The front desk staff was as courteous as you would expect at an IC, and as a room was not immediately available, they took our cell number and called at --:-- a.m. when a room was free. From a personal perspective, I thought this was a nice touch. We had not intended on taking a room that early anyway as we had other plans.
In regards to the neighborhood, you can read reviews below to get a flavor of it. Five years ago my wife and I went to a diner around the corner from the current location and commented to each other that we were in the 'middle of nowhere', even though we lived less than -- blocks away. Now, with Shake Shack, the Times Square pedestrian changes, European style cafes, and of course the IC, the eastern edges of Hells Kitchen are a nearly different place. There are a couple of topless adult joints around the corner that remind you that you are in a neighborhood that is in a state of flux, and I doubt they'll still be there in - years if not sooner. The edginess of the neighborhood adds to an authentic New York experience. And in case you're wondering, we never felt unsafe or unwelcome. New York City is embracing these changes rather well.
My only hesitation with our stay came with a couple of confused calls to the front desk where a call back was promised but never received over a late check out time. In the end a staffer gave us the late check out (-:-- p.m.) but when we got back to our room at -:--, our card keys did not work. I left the family in the hallway and went to the front desk to get the situation sorted out, which was done in a courteous manner. Obviously the staff is still coming up to speed a bit, and perhaps the newer folks are learning the ropes on the weekends. Given the overall good experience, I'll give them a mulligan on this.
I'll give a plug to the bell staff who were prompt, courteous, and pleasant. Between the bags and the car, we interacted with them a bit and they exceeded my expectations.
I can easily recommend this hotel for both personal and business stays. We've stayed at ICs across the globe (join the loyalty club if you haven't already), and this property is very much in line with our other experiences; quality room, courteous staff, well located, but at a price.
If you're like us, we tend to put quality of experience before cost savings, and on this score, the IC TS fit the bill.

This was my -th time to stay at The Westin Riverwalk in San Antonio! It is a beautiful hotel, the rooms are clean and the beds are so comfortable!! Ideally located right on the Riverwalk and close to all the fun that there is to do in San Antonio! You can walk to the shops, Alamo, Hemisphere, and some excellent restaurants. This property also has a very nice pool. The staff was so helpful...it was a great weekend get-away!

Was not impressed with my stay at Baymont considering the cost. It did have a nice indoor pool and spa though. Staff was not all that friendly or helpful. Breakfest was good, but their sitting area was too small and not enough places to sit. Also I felt rushed when I got ready to leave.

We stayed here for - nights on a recent visit to San Diego. The location was wonderful for our trips to the zoo, seaworld and the wild animal park. Overall, an excellent location and a good value.

we used this hotel as a base for exploring San Antonio and were very happy with it. We were on the -th floor in a newly remodeled suite. similar to room described in the previous review.

The service was OK, but nothing exceptional. The lobby was cold and drafty. Would stay elsewhere next time.

We have stayed at the Doubletree - times for Hockey Tournaments, and we are treated like family by the staff. They are incredibly accomodating and helpful. The rooms are comfortable and clean. We always have an amazing stay at the DoubleTree, and I refuse to stay anywhere else in the Detroit area.

Great location, - minutes walk to most midtown attractions, hotel lobby superb, staff were friendly and helpful. Room was nice with the exception of the bathroom which was in need of refurb - decorating, but nothing you could not live with. Temperature control in the room was 'fun', either blast furnace hot or north pole cold. That said I would stay here again.

The Sir Francis Drake may be old, but if you get a good price it is just fine. It's located a block off of Union Square with a trolley stop right out front. I am Platinum Elite with Marriott and much to my surprise and disappointment upon checking in this past Friday for a - night weekend stay was closure of the Club Lounge for the weekend.... actually EVERY weekend. This was our second stay at travelodge. This second time, we had a much nicer room with a city view. This hotel is for the budget minded because the carpeting is old and the furniture is dated, but the bathrooms are updated and well lit. I never felt the hotel was dirty, just worn. The small room was adequate for our overnight stay. It's within walking distance from BART and had a nice free French toast breakfast. The hotel had an artsy feel to it with prints and original artwork everywhere.

Have stayed at a number of Garden Inns and I would rate this one as one of the poorer, if not the poorest.

-- min away from the loop, walking. Carpet in the room wasn't as clean as it could have been. Definitely not a destination for a romantic getaway. Otherwise it was alright to spend two nights in.

Location is ideal. - minute walk to gaslamp district and easy access to Hwy-. Back door is right by sea port village. Lobby area and bar are impressive. Room was average with comfortable bed. LOBBY:
Upon my weekday - p.m. arrival, I was surprised the foyer was so dark and nightclub-like. The lobby was always bustling! It is small, so don't expect to find a seat in the morning if you are waiting for someone.
ROOM:

The room itself was quiet. I didn't hear hallway noise or neighbors bustling. But, there was considerable street noise around the clock, but that is to be expected while staying in the city. I felt very safe as a ---something woman travelling alone.

AMMENITIES

STAFF:

The help was VERY kind at the front desk, in the hallways and at the door. Kudos to them for being nice people willing to help out!
LOCATION:

I would NOT recommend this hotel to others as it just wasn't a 'comfortable' stay. The in-room experience was not up to snuff! Next year when I visit for work I will stay elsewhere.

I have stayed here many times and it has been fine, but this stay is slightly more revealing. The place seems to be more worn out, grimy in spots, noisy and not as good in many respects. Per a random dude's advice on the street, my wife and I found ourselves on the --th or --th floor having drinks. It turned into a - hr late night party that we'll never remember!

I can see how a picky person could rip this place apart. I was skeptical about staying here. Small hotel just west of SoHo, but was extremely pleasantly surprised at how perfect it was - especially for the money. My only complaint (given the low price of the hotel) is that the ice machine in the hallway sounds like a plan landing. Extremely loud all night long.

Lovely trip with my daughter. We celebrated her --th birthday with a bit of shopping. Hotel location was centralized and we felt very safe. Nice quarters and staff. The rooms were nice, room service was perfect and the location very convenient for downtown and the convention center. I stayed at the Novotel for two nights [out of a seven night stay in New York] in September ----. The remaining nights were spent at the W Hotel New York on Lexington Avenue and the Empire Hotel. I’ve completed separate reviews of each hotel, my favorite hands down being the Empire Hotel. 
First impression: After three-nights in a suite at the W Hotel, I loathed the idea of downgrading to this hotel. Even though it cost me nothing to say here since it was billed at the expense of my companion’s employer, I almost wanted to pay to stay somewhere else.

Check-in was efficient; although I was dubious the hotel only had two rooms for our offering. We had booked a king superior room, but were offered a noisy king by the elevator with a terrible view, or double beds on a higher floor with a great view of Time Square. We opted for the later. 
If views and proximity to Time Square are important, I can understand why one would stay here because the hotel clearly delivered on its promise of sweeping views of Time Square. Adjacent to the lobby is a wonderful outdoor wrap around terrace. I would imagine it would be a prime location to observe the legendary Macy’s Thanksgiving and Christmas Day parade and the New Year’s Eve festivities. On the other hand, if views are not your chief concern, I don’t see why on earth anyone would pay over $--- for a two nights stay (especially given that September is probably considered a shoulder travel season and there are a plethora of more upscale accommodations offering more bang for your buck) . 
Usually the Trip Advisor ratings are right on, but I’m baffled that somehow the Novotel manages to rate significantly higher than, say, the W Hotel, where I had a far better experience during three additional nights in September.

It was also a good location for restaurants and walking to the sites of Boston. The bed was super comfy too. My wife and I spent a week's vacation at The French Quarters in June this year , and would highly recommend this little hotel. Great hotel , memorable experience.

I ate breakfast in the restaurant at street level and it was very good.
The hotel is beginning to show the needs for some updating in the rooms and the public areas.

I would consider staying here again based on the staff and location.

Situated in the heart of fashionable Back Bay, Copley Square Hotel is surrounded by retail enticements from every angle. Street shopping is abundant on Newbury and Boylston, while those preferring indoor one-stop options could head to Prudential Centre or Copley Place Mall. If you like to explore on foot, the hotel is reasonable walking distance to many downtown attractions, including Fenway Park, but access to the T, Boston’s subway system, is practically around the corner. The standard room accented with gaudy decor is quite tight and lacks a mini bar despite the oversized furniture. To make up for that, the hotel offers complementary refreshment service three times a day. As for the bathroom, good quality toiletries were provided but the leaky shower was an annoyance. Although Boston is a wired city, free wi-fi at the hotel is an added bonus and the daily guest memos are a thoughtful touch, providing useful info on weather and recommended activities.

We booked this hotel on Priceline-$--, great rate. The hotel was VERY nice, very clean, very upscale accomodations. But we did appreciate how clean and nice the room and hotel were. We probably wouldn't stay there again with our small children but we DEFINITELY would if it were just my husband and I there for the weekend.

otherwise the hotel is weel situated and the staff is really excellent and helpful

The pictures on the internet and what the hotel actually looks like are very different. I am sure the hotel was very nice a number of years ago, but now it is way past due for a remodel. I've stayed at this property numerous times over the last few years, but my recent trip in the last few days will be my last.
I'm not sure if it is the harsh economic times in the US or just the hotel is being a victim of its own success and the owners are being greedy.
Check in was warm and welcoming. But there was a sting in the tail. I was told that the internet, which in the past had been complimentary was now chargeable. I don't seem to recall seeing that in the booking parts on the website. And being in the highest tier of the loyalty program and having booked an Executive Room didn't make any difference.
I was also told that the Executive lounge was open, which it hadn't been on my previous visits and I had been given vouchers for drinks and breakfast. So you can imagine my surprise to find that the lounge wasn't in fact serving breakfast or drinks. Very disappointing - what is the point in booking an Executive Room if you don't get the perks? I eventually was given some breakfast vouchers but no apology for not being given them in the first place.
Speaking of perks, again being an elite member of Priority Club program, didn't result in a room upgrade. It was a nice enough room on the top floor overlooking the park (maybe that counts as an upgrade being on the top floor?) If you like sunny rooms then high up on this side will give you plenty of that. I know that room upgrades are subject to availability, but Hilton does a much better job in telling you if you have been upgraded and if you haven't offering you something in return, But more of that later.
The hotel restaurant and staff, were, however, excellent. The Chef, George Lopez, came out and talked with my guests and explained the food which was a real nice touch. They also had a great deal on with a free (excellent) bottle of house wine with two main courses. Can't rate all of that highly enough. The rest of the staff around the hotel were very friendly too.
One thing that will impact you if you staff here, and rather confirms my view of margin maximisation on the management's behalf, are the lifts-elevators. Expect to wait an eternity for them even when the place isn't busy (it was my perception that it wasn't busy during my stay.) And expect to be packed in when it is busy.
There were only two working out of four and this was similar to my last visit in September. Can't see why it would take so long to fix them - granted an old building but refurbished a few years ago.
I've brought considerable business to this hotel over the last couple of years. Not just my own stays but numerous other colleagues who have stayed there and eaten in the restaurant and spent money in the bar. The staff there are all excellent. However, there are better value hotels in DC, where you'll get complimentary internet and faster lifts-elevators.
I know I'll be voting with my feet and my wallet. It isn't that I can't afford the internet cost but I feel I was mislead on so many fronts and that the hotel failed to deliver its side of the deal. Hilton here I come.......

My husband and I stayed at the W Chicago City Center on a recent """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""fun"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" trip to Chicago. This is a great property. One of the best hotels in Chicago, if not the U.S. Very few hotels make everything work and when they do it is typically an expensive experience. The Radisson Blu Aqua is able to provide an amazing experience at an outstanding value. 
The hotel is in a great location, within walking distance (or short cab ride) to many attractions. The hotel is absolutely stunning both inside and out. We spent Christmas and New Year in San Francisco and chose the Omni for our place to stay. From the moment we arrived (before we got out of the taxi) we were made incredibly welcome by Daryl the doorman. Our experience at check in was really personal and we were given our Select Guest beverage vouchers for our morning drink. My daughter was really pleased to see a Birthday cake in our room when we opened the door. This was arranged by the hotel and no charge made. The room was very clean an plenty of room for the three of us. The room service was always on time, and one time when it wasn't we were given some muffins as an apology! The maid service could not have been better either.
The bar was cosy and friendly and like the restaurant a little pricy but quality food and drink.
There is not one thing I can genuinely say I could remotely think about in a negative way. All the staff were a pleasure to speak to, the service was always excellent and the decor of the hotel was very seasonal. The Christmas tree and decorations and Christmas music in the lobby were welcoming and cosy. Frequent warm apple cider, apples and ginger cookies were a welcome treat each evening.
We were made welcome and felt part of the family during our stay away from home over Christmas.
I stay in many hotels in the UK as part of my work and I can honestly say that the Omni has been the most pleasurable hotel stay I have ever experienced. This may sound over the top but it's true. I would certainly use this hotel again if in San Francisco.

The hotel was really nice and the staff was extremely friendly and helpful. We were able to stay on a discounted rated so it was wonderful. I am not sure if I would pay the full price to stay there. We had a corner room which was really neat with the huge glass windows to look at the city. Watch out for the $-- valet fee that is extra and the only parking available.

Our heater worked on-off. It's not a very large hotel and I would say I wasn't a fan of the surrounding areas. The valet was extremely friendly and ended up knowing our names by the end of our stay. The front desk was extremely helpful in assisting us with maps, directions and eateries. Overall, I was satisfied with this three-star hotel

My husband and I stayed at the Chancellor hotel about a week ago. San Francisco was the last leg of our road trip and we wanted to stay somewhere comfortable with a good location. Actually the whole room looks a little --'s...the carpet was a zebra pattern (maybe supposed to be waves?) of teal and a darker blue, the furniture was a worn oak color and the curtains a pinkish mauve.
