There was a couch in the room, a microwave and a small fridge...all great additions to the large room. But I once I took a step out on the balcony, any issues with the room decor went right out the door! You are looking right down on the always entertaining Pacific boardwalk and are literally steps from the ocean. Not even a road between you and the water, just the boardwalk then sand! There is a lifeguard station right there, and the beach was pristine! It was spectacular! We parked the car in the underground secure parking ($-- a day, and worth it!) and never got back in. There are tons of restaurants, bars, stores and shops within walking distance and we had a blast! The customer service was first rate, the free breakfast with make your own waffles was lovely and we will be coming back to this hotel in February for a whale watching trip, I do not think I will stay anywhere else in San Diego! If fancy is your main criteria, you can look elsewhere, but for a family friendly hotel with excellent customer service, large clean rooms and the most wonderful location in San Diego...This is where you need to stay!

The most important item in any hotel stay is the quality of the bed. I was very pleased with the bed quality and I found it to be very clean and completely comfortable. As is often the case in Texas, the air conditioning is necessary at night so one almost has to keep the room cold and cuddle up under mounds of bedding - this was no exception. When I read some of the other reviews about the hotel location, that sent my mind racing and I wondered what I was in for. Let me say that the hotel isn't any harder to get to than any other in Texas just because they lay out the roads the way they do. Texas is very frustrating for drivers from other states because they have frontage roads everywhere and the whole state is oriented to car travel. Therefore, I will say that the hotel was not that hard to find and it was in an acceptable location. I would not have been concerned about having to go to the car at night.
The staff was some of the friendliest I have ever seen. Sharp, helpful and very astute. The service here is excellent.
The room itself was nicely laid out and I have to give this hotel credit - they have HD TV's and they actually have HD service on the channels. Not all hotels do that and it drives me nuts. Whenever I can find a hotel that offers flawless television and everything works electronically, that impresses me.
The one thing that I will mention which may be a concern to some folks is the loud noise when the toilet is flushed. My toilet ran a bit and I had to become """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""the plumber"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to reach inside the tank and adjust the little seal on the bottom of the tank. Easy enough, but I was not impressed with the cheap quality of the device and I could easily see where someone could have this problem happen to them. Mine was not serious and I did not report it to management - yet. However, a slight adjustment will probably fix it if anyone else has the problem. Or just call management. I hate to call them out if it is something I would do at home myself anyway.
So the bottom line is that if you are going to be in Austin on business and are considering the Hyatt Place North Central, rest assured it is ready for business and is well kept and excellent for business travel. I would certainly consider staying here again.

We are looooong time Marriott timeshare owners now re-evaluating Marriott properties within the Marriott system, and this is the third such property evaluated since June ----. Please see my other reviews; one was good and one dismal.

... Would I stay there again? not very likely. But then again """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""it's a hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" nothing else.

This hotel is a very nice place to spend the night. The staff is courteous and knowledgeable. Although one is in an enormous city, there are many entertaining things to do in the area. Taxis are readily available.

Stayed at Sheraton BH as part of business in the area. Although there's not much to do within walking distance (however I do recommend the Mexican restaurant for takeout -- Juanita's), the hotel itelf is terrific. After hurricane damage in ----, it appears they completely renovated the hotel. 
Lobby is very nice with a new business center - internet cafe; in-house gift shop for any last-minute items-snacks; restaurant with a solid breakfast buffet (including custom-made omelettes); and room with nice large flatscreen and comfortable beds.
If you're renting a car, I would highly recommend this hotel as you can easily jump on the --- and head to the Galleria for shopping or downtown (you must brave Houston traffic volumes though!). It's basically halfway between the airport and downtown. 
Staff are friendly and helpful, the rooms well appointed and the rate was very reasonable! I will always stay here whenever I'm in the area.

Wanted to choose Dolyce mansion, but decided to choose this instead for an exceptional offer on expedia.
Anyway, we werent disappointed. The place is great after the refurbishment... The bed is soft and great. The room is spacious and my wife was excited over the Loccitane products...
Parking is not free, but we have no problems with that.
If I need to attend a convention in San Jose, Sainte Claire it will be...

Took a friend here for her --th birthday, I've stayed a few times before on business with the firm picking up the tab and always happy. This time stayed - nights at my expense and very well worth it, from the speedy, friendly check in, one of the concierges took us and out bags to the room and gave us lots of info.
The room was on the top floor, great views, spotlessly clean, fabulously comfortable beds, huge flat screen tv, good bathroom with a floor to ceiling mirrored wall, good powerful shower and a proper hairdryer.
Cannot fault the staff here, from reception, Bell hops, Conceirge, bar staff to the Housekeeping staff, unfailingly polite and helpful.
On my friends birthday, we returned to out room in the afternoon to find a bottle of Champagne on ice, with - flutes and a lovely letter from the hotel manager, a super touch.
The location is ideal, right across the street from The Prudential Mall, connected by a walkway to the Copley Place Mall, and it's also a shortcut to the shops, bars and restaurants of Boylston St...very useful to get there under cover when the temperature is --C!
The Old Town Trolley Tour picks up from the hotel door and runs every ----- mins all day, a multi day ticket was about $-- and good for - consecutive days.
I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this great, individual hotel ( on prev visits in summer I've enjoyed the rooftop pool and bar as well).
Thanks to all the staff.

I know my last review of this hotel just a few months ago raved about the place and I must admit I still love this hotel compared to some of the other places iv stayed but to be balanced I must admit this most recent stay was less then ideal!
Upon arrival into a very congested lobby and waiting some time to be served I found myself without a room for a further -- minutes as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""housekeeping have yet to service your room""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""! I arrived around - pm so this seemed unusual. No apology given.
When I finally got to my room which was perfectly clean, comfortable and acceptable I discovered that the air conditioning in the room was totally ineffective at cooling the room. Also whenever water was running be it the sink, shower or toilet it sounded like someone was banging away with a jack hammer behind the bathroom wall!
On the second day of my visit despite being out of the room without the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""do not disturb"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sign on the door my room was never serviced! I had to ring down for fresh towels in the end.
On check out I waited TWENTY MINUTES before I was seen to despite there only being one couple ahead of me in the line. - staff at the desk and plenty more passing through chatting to one another. I began to get very frustrated. I then had an issue with my bill where a charge of over $-- was placed for drinks and a meal I never had at one of the bars. The receptionist insisted in making me check receipts! Turned out it was from the previous guest in my room but in total took almost -- minutes from leaving my room to actually getting out of the hotel!
But there are positives! The location....WOW! The beds...AMAZING and most of the staff I dealt with where lovely! The fitness club and spa area are also top notch!
On this occasion I'll put this one down to a bad experience but I shall be back I'm sure!!!!!
Great Hotel, Great Service, Beautiful rooms with Terrace views of river

Ancient motel with many coats of paint and some interesting decor. Cold, quiet AC, plenty of hot water w-adjustable shower head. Carpet was a little worn, bed was better than expected, but scratchy sheets and comforter made it less than desirable. Lots of dings and the outer doors facing the parking lot showed signs of nights that didn't go well for previous guests. But, it was quiet the night of our stay and we encountered friendly enough folks moving about. Good waffles, pleasant staff. I might stay here again, but I guess I have become a bit of a hotel snob, preferring the security of the modern hotel and the comfort that new amenities bring. But, in a pinch, this'll do. For the price, you get an okay room. They try to dress this old girl up to look appealing, but it just can't hide the fact that it'll take more than paint to compete with newer budget hotels. Nice try.

Stayed here the week of thanksgiving. I loved this place! The decor is really fun and a change from all the chain hotels. We paid for an upgrade room, which i believe was well worth the money. Also, make sure you are signed up for their loyalty program, so you get the free wifi and some other amenities. Our room was very clean and very spacious! Again, i loved the decor and furnishings. I'm sure this will not be the case for everyone, but if you like a unique experience, the Allegro will fit the bill. They go above and beyond in the service dept, our jacuzzi tub didn't work and they were there within -- min to fix it. The front desk staff was so welcoming!
The fitness center was really nice. Not sure if the hotel was not really full...but we always seemed to be the only people there. We did not have any noise issues, but we also had a corner room. 
The price seems inline for other similar hotels with similar amenities. I felt we got way more for our money than we would have at another hotel.
Highly recommend this hotel to others! Make sure to ask for anything special that you need, they will do their best to accomodate and make your stay special.

The staff at this hotel are some of the best I have ever encountered. They were all friendly, helpful, and professional. The shuttle driver was just great. The room was very clean and the microwave and refrig were a welcomed plus. I would highly recommend this hotel and I will definitely stay there again. Thank you!!!!

We stayed one night at the hotel in mid October. We were upgraded to a - story villa. Very nice accomodation- bedroom upstairs with - queen beds,a bathroom, and large outdoor deck. Downstairs a living room with a sofabed, kitchen and bathroom. The villa was very clean and everything in working order. The property is large - we were very close to the waterpark, but also had a private pool for the villas. The waterark was entertaining for the kids- -- and --. They enjoyed the slide, lazy river and sports pool- none were crowded. We played a round of mini golf which was fun- nothing spectacular though. We ate at the restaurant at the waterpark- service was fine and the food good. The hotel is not located near many reataurants or stores so a car is helpful. We are HiltonHonors members so were given breakfast vouchers which can be used at a sit down restaurant or the Starbucks in the hotel lobby. We used them at Starbuck which worked out great. Overall the property is beautiful with great pools and outdoor areas.

We cannot fault the XV, the room was exceptional both in decor and cleanliness, the bed one of the most comfortable ever tried in a hotel. The service within the hotel and Moo Restaurant-Bar faultless The food delicious both in the restaurant as well as room service. If there were two minor criticisms these would be no bath tub in the bathroom and the reception lobby area is very small and does not lend itself to being utilised as an area to read-relax for more than just two or three people. Would definately recommend for leisure or business in Boston.

Our stay at the hotel was fine. The room was clean and we used it for only sleeping. We didnt spend much time in there. The only complaints would be the old, slow, elevators, and the shower has no water pressure. There was not a continental breakfast. The location worked out good for us as we have a student residing across the street at the University Center.

Just come back from - nights at this hotel and was very very disappointed. The bar on the --th floor is now closed!!!, the menu in the restaruant is poor, and the very expensive New York steak on the menu was full of fat. We tried room service for a burger and chips and a bottle of wine... not good and cost £--- + !!! if this had been a - star and we had of paid £-- - £--- a night I would have said it was ok, but its a % star and cost £--- for - nigts !!!
Battery Park area is very nice and clean, views from rooms ( we were on -th floor ) were very nice, and the air con was great.

I have recently returned from a stay at the Westin Times Square as part of our honeymoon. The whole experience was a delight from the moment we checked in. The girl at the desk knew it was our honeymoon and was very pleasant wishing us all the best etc. We requested that we have a room that was high up in the hotel and had a good view. As it was our honeymoon, the girl gave us a room that was two upgrades above what we paid for. She was fantastic to us. The room was huge by NY standards and had great views of the city. Very comfortable bed and even had a view of the Empire State Building. We also spent a very pleasant evening in the hotel bar, the bar staff were very pleasant and we really enjoyed 'chilling out' with a few cocktails in the westin's bar.
Location is also fantastic for this hotel, right on Times Square. New York never fails to impress and the westin added to the whole experience, I would definitely recommend this hotel.
If i am being slightly critical...it is in my nature!.......the room needed some slight attention in terms of appearance, but that is me being critical...the whole hotel was a fantastic experience.

I was travelling for business and stayed at the Dupont Circle Hotel in DC for two nights in October. First I was given a room at the -th floor, king bed and supposedly nonsmoking. The room, however, smelled terrible, besides being very small and with no view whatsoever. I checked my colleague’s room (at the same floor) and it had the same smell, although with larger size and a view. I complained at the front desk because my reservation was clear about a nonsmoking room. They informed the hotel was fully booked for the night and there was nothing they could do. 
Next morning I complained again and then was transferred to a hotel on the third floor, much larger and with no smell whatsoever (same rates though). 
Besides that, the hotel has a nice bar and is kind of trendy. Location is great. But one has to be lucky when given the room. I guess the first room I stayed compared to the second one and to my colleague’s room should be considered different categories.

This hotel is a pretty good hotel at about -- minutes from the downtown of Seattle. The hotel is clean, comfortable for it's category, with large rooms and good services. WiFi is free and working well. The breakfast, unlike other hotels of the same category, is good and abundant with many choices. The location is also good because is in front at a big commercial center with many shops and restaurants where eat. The peoples at the front desk are always kind and also available to solve every problem. Parking free. Suggested to everyone like to stay in Seattle without spend a lot of money and above all with own car.

Brought my wife down for appointments at Mayo Clinic. Hotel offers Mayo Clinic discount and is a smooth -- minute drive away down Butler Blvd. Staff is friendly and accomodating. Rooms are quiet and clean. Room a little larger than most in this price range. Free breakfast was very good as free breakfasts go. Bed clean and comfortable. Grounds are well landscaped and clean. The only thing that bothered me slightly was the air conditioning system. It has a large unit under the window and cuts on and off frequently instead of constantly blowing. Bathroom is clean and roomy with a nice shower. Would stay here on return visit.

We stopped in the Argonaut for two nights on the way from Sydney to London. We had a bad first leg of the flight but the stay at the Argo refreshed us all and we enjoyed the hotel no end. 
Lets get this out the way early, the hotel is gorgeous! I'd best liken it to a Disney Delux hotel. Disney would certainly be proud of it. You can see the pictures of the lobby and the rooms on this site and in person the quality of the fittings are first class.
I knew we'd love the look and feel of the hotel when I booked it but what I didn't realise was how good the staff were. They seem to have recruited the friendliest and most helpful people they could in all of the roles within the hotel. From the front door to the housekeeping they are fantastic. 
Internet was free and quick. Lots of room freebies. Quiet rooms which surprised me after reading comments on here. Our room was a good size too.
We loved everything about the hotel and can't wait for a chance to go back!

The location is great, just off Time Square. The bed is very comfortable. Good value for money - free local call, free breakfast. Except my wireless connection doesnt work in my room, a hassle to keep going down to the bar area to get online...the shower water pressure could be more powerful. On the whole, I love this hotel and will certainly come back again.

This hotel is definitely overpriced for what you get. The room we were in was very musty and it appeared that the odor was coming from the air conditioner. We ended up leaving the window open most of the time to air the room out. The pool facilities were definitely in need of repair. The jacuzzi was semi-functional as many of the jets were broken. The breakfast in the morning paled in comparison to the usual Marriott fare. Coffee was horrible and the selection could hardly be called continental. More like continental light. Definitely gonna take a pass on this one next time we are in Indianapolis.

My Wife and I stayed in this hotel on a vacation we took to Chicago. We both loved this hotel in everyway possible. The rooms were absolutely spoteless everytime you walked into them, beds were comfortable, and room service was outstanding as well. We ate at all of the restaurants that were in the hotel during our stay, and did not have a bad meal in any of them. What I like most about this hotel was something that maybe some people might not care about, but I did. All of the staff was down to earth, and very friendly. I don't mean friendly like it's their job to be friendly, I mean that they really made you feel like they really wanted to help you to enjoy your stay in their hotel as well as you visit to Chicago. I am from a very small town in the midwest, and when we stayed here it was the very first time I had ever been to a city the size of Chicago. The town I am from has a population of --- people. The lobby of this hotel will hold more people than that. So needless to say it was a bit of culture shock to be in a city that large, and trying to find our way around was a little bit nerve racking. I also grew up in the country, and when I walked into the lobby of this hotel I actually thought that surely they would kick my hillbilly, blue jean & boot wearing rearend out, but everyone was extremely nice. The concierge helped us everytime that we had any questions about where we should eat, what we should go do, or the easiest way to get from point A to point B and back. The bellhops were hillarious, and would joke around with us everytime that we saw them. I didn't quite understand that you were supposed to tip the guy who blows his whistle to get you a cab (again I grew up in a town that has never even seen a cab) so at the end of the trip I gave the guy $-- dollars to make up for everytime that I hadn't tipped him throughout the week. Anyway, I could keep going on about this hotel, and how much I loved it, but I think you get the point. If you are looking for an extremely nice hotel, with friendly staff who do an excellent job, and who will help make your trip the best it can be then you can't go wrong staying at the Palmer House Hilton!

The hotel is new but the rooms are way small. I mean, way small. There's a tiny close built into the wall and I had to turn sideways as I passed the window heat-AC unit when walking from my bedside to the bathroom. The small TV matches the small room. The staff is pleasant and the location is solid being close to downtown and connected to TGI Fridays. Breakfast choices are OK with Jimmy Dean sandwiches available to microwave. The Internet was free and there's a nice business center in the lobby with a printer available.

I can honestly say we didn't have any problems. Our shower and tub area was clean. (either it was fairly new or the housekeeper in that area does a good job keeping it clean.) Our room looked like it was recently painted, the floors were clean and I didn't see no critters (cockroaches)
The A-C worked great! It was very hot and humid outside so this was a big plus. 
The staff was really nice and polite and helped us out getting information that we requested.
Breakfast was good, they have like - or - waffle-makers so you don't have to wait. 
They also have - pools so if there is too many people in one you can go to the other.
They only bad thing was we didn't have a micro-fridge in the room, but we had a coffee maker, blow-dryer, and iron and ironing board.
When we go back to Texas we will more then likely stay here again.

My wife and I stayed here for - nights in early November on our recent extended trip to the U.S. 
This hotel was fantastic, commencing with a very warm greeting followed by convenience in location. Close to Boston Gardens, Train Station, Convenience shops, Dunkin Donuts , great Pubs and Restaurants. All of these are within walking distance.
The room itself, whilst not large was very modern, the bed is extremely comfortable, well maintained and the bathroom fairly spacious.
The only Con to our experience at this hotel was the elevator being offline for - nights. There is only one elevator, we where on the -th floor so we had to walk up and down, however this did not bother us with the exception of check out in getting our bags down the stairs.
It certainly was challenging for the staff to manage this, however the hotel staff maintained excellent service and where kind enough to componsate our bill, which was much appreciated.
There is no going past this hotel and would recommend it to any traveller. I certainly upon return to Boston would stay here again.
I travel frequently for business, usually at least one week in every month. From check in to check out the entire staff was very welcoming, helpful, and informative.

A friend and I traveled to Hollywood and stayed in this hotel. It was a quaint, comfortable shady getaway in the midst of a city. We enjoyed the fireplace and lifesize ottomans while! lounging in the pool area. Most of all the customer service was excellent. The people in the front desk area and housekeepers went out of their way to make it a great stay.
Thank you

We( - women in their --'s) stayed - days at this hotel last year when it was the Rhiga Royal. This was our first trip to Manhattan. The entire stay was excellent. The fascilities are top notch, large suites for Manhattan, excellent helpful, courteous staff. They were more than helpful. Since a major renovation and now part of the Luxury Group, I'm sure it is more fantastic. The location is excellent. Carnegie Deli is close by, excellent coffee shop on the corner, near Central Park, subway stop, blocks from Times square......close to everything. I would stay there again, however it is pricey. Upon checking out, I felt I was making a down payment on a house and don't drink the bottled water in the room. They charge $-.-- per bottle.

the best thing is the hotel is its location. The hotel is old, the staff is horrible they are rude, regular, with all the passengers share this view. They never responded to anything. There are many choices to go.

This is a new hotel and it's fantastic. The layout of the rooms is different than older Embassy suites. The door from the hall opens to a kitchen area and living room area. The bedroom and bathroom are to the side of the living room area. And with the bathroom against the wall to the hall, the bedroom is wonderfully quiet. The hotel is not just new, but also spotless. The staff was exceptional in their service. It's close to the Columbus airport and the shuttle service was very responsive. I couldn't say one negative thing about this hotel or its staff.

My husband & I stayed here with our - year old after a day trip to the SD Zoo. This was located in the Hotel Circle area, which is conveniently located to the freeway & airport, but I would not stay in this area next time. The area was a bit rundown and you have to pay a parking fee of $-.---day. This hotel was newly renovated and the rooms were nice and clean, but the pool area faced the parking lot--not very nice. If you mind the buzz of the freeway, make sure you request a room that doesn't overlook it (ours did). Also, if you plan on ordering pizza from one of the menus that the room offers, stay away from Verona's Pizza. The food was not good at all (we took a bite and couldn't eat the rest, we are not that picky). When I called them back to let them know we were not satisfied, the so called mgr told me they don't give cash back and that I could call the owner the next day and hung up on me. The next morning we went to the breakfast area to enjoy the complimentary breakfast. This was a chaotic mess. We got there around -ish and it was very crowded. There was cereal, little pastries-muffins, boiled eggs, bagels-toast, coffee-juices, some fruit and the dreadful do-it-yourself waffle station. There was a long line, and the waffle station was a bit dirty from all of the spilled batter. I think it would be better if they had an employee in charge of the waffle making. At least have someone to oversee all of these hungry guests trying to make their own waffles. Also, the tables were not cleared or cleaned. I saw - ladies refill the cereal machine, but no one cleaning up after the guests. Finally. there were non-quests enjoyonh the free breakfast as well--we overheard a group saying they live nearby and were coming back the next day to take advantage of the free food. Again, there wasn't an employee maintaing the breakfast area. The crowd and the uncleanliness ruined the whole breakfast experience. (We usually enjoy the same type of breakfast at the Holiday Inn Express in Cardiff) So we decided to skip the pool and check out early. I would not stay here again.

I travel quite a bit, and typically stay at four- or five-stars. I would definitely rate this as one of the nicest places I've stayed at anywhere! Excellent service and free internet make this a bargain. The hotel is an independent, and I decided to stay here after spending a few days at the Manhattan Sofitel next door, because Expedia had a great air-room deal, and the Iroquois looked cozier. Couldn't be happier I did! Great location, rooms are small, but that's midtown. Wonderful location for theatres and Central Park, and manageable on foot in nice weather if you want to stroll to the Museums on the Upper East Side or down to Greenwich Village. Close to all subway lines if you're not up for that. I would stay here again & again & again, look no further for your perfect Manhattan home-away-from home!

Service was great. Staff was helpful in every way. Hotel was clean. Close to a lot of great places. Got a corner room and the only pitfall was it was on the street with the sign flopping in the breeze which made a noise, but, I got use to it. Room was plenty big. Bathroom was small and dated. Price that I got was expensive for the type of hotel and room, but it was in a great area. I really enjoyed staying there and would again if I could afford it.

I don't want to waste energy thinking about this place any longer, but did want to warn future guests.
The rooms were stale smelling and the AC did not work. Rust-mold in the bathroom.
If you pay more than $----night your are being robbed. Unfortunately, I paid way more than that, so live and learn.

I stay at the Adolphus when travelling on business several times a year. The rooms are elegant and well appointed. The staff is always friendly and attentive. Room service is always delivered when promised and the food is good. The French Room is a wonderful experience. The room is beautiful; the food was fantastic and the waiter, Carlos was wonderful. This is by far my favorite hotel.

I'm accustomed to big city parking rates, but I was floored to learn upon check-in that the overnight rate at the St. Francis was FIFTY dollars PLUS tax, for a total of FIFTY-SEVEN dollars. Yikes!! That seems like robbery to me. Even the desk staff seemed horrified by it, quietly hinting that cheaper parking was available nearby if you were up for the inconvenience. Notwithstanding overnight parking rates, the location seemed great during the day. However, when the sun went down and the street performers came out, things didn't seem so ideal. One individual had an entire drumset set up on the corner across the street from the hotel. While in the room, it sounded like he was in there with us. For us, these two items are enough to send us elsewhere on our next trip to the city which is unfortunate as the hotel otherwise has a lot to offer.

I have stayed at the Hotel Icon in Houston many times. The changes I have noticed since it became a Marriott property are few; It still remains my favorite place in Downtown Houston. Overnight valet parking is steep, but I have found it that way at almost all downtown hotels.
The interior design and furnishings in the lounge and lobby are beautiful. The guest rooms and bathrooms are very well appointed - they make you feel as if you've stepped back in time! 
All employees are very professional and helpful.
I would highly recommend the Hotel Icon for anyone looking for a spectacular get-away!
Very close to several downtown attractions.

I am normally a diehard Marriott guy but stayed in this hotel for business reasons and was pleasantly surprised. Hyatt calls this a luxury hotel and I agree. The hotel has a huge beautiful lobby that sets the tone of the place. I paid a little extra for a view room and Grand Club Lounge access and boy was it worth it. My room was very nice with a beautiful view of downtown, Pine Street and the water. I loved watching the ferries come and go. The Grand Club Lounge is easily one of the best I have ever seen. Very high end spread in the morning and evening with coffee, sodas and water all day long. The Hotel is right next to the convention center and short walking distance to tons of shopping, restaurants and the Pike Place Market. Everything in downtown is close and easy to get to. If you are going to stay in downtown don’t bother to rent a car. Just get a taxi to and from the airport and save the hassle and cost of parking. Restaurant service is from the attached Ruth Chris. Good food but not cheap. There are tons of restaurants in every price range close by and all over downtown if you don’t want to eat there. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Room was modern and immaculate with a huge bathroom. My only small gripe is the single power outlet at the desk. In order to plug my laptop and phone charger in I had to unplug the desk lamp. You pay a little more for this place but I feel you get what you paid for. I will definitely come back to this hotel.
Tips:
Ask for a high floor with a view. The Roosevelt hotel is right next to the Hyatt and could block a water view if you are on a lower floor. Make sure you are above it.
The Grand Club Lounge is well worth the extra money. Terrific high end spread in the morning and evening with very reasonably priced wine & liquor during happy hour. It has great views and is a very comfortable place to hang out. I have seen many lounges and this was easily one of the best.
Bring a power strip if you plan to work at the desk. My room only had one outlet available at the desk.

Would recommend against staying here unless you want a room to crash after partying or in which to change from daytime pool party (think Vegas meets MTV the Hills) to nighttime clubbing. The only common or outdoor space that exists is the roof-top pool deck, which is physically beautiful, but squatted in by a permanent drunken circus of preening -- year olds and a rope line at the elevator bay vigorously discourages hotel guests from even going up. And is outwardly hostile to paying guests. What's left? A patio abutting Hollywood blvd (loud thoroughfare) perched atop escalators into the subway -- and the ice in my drink served there stank like day-old fish.
This is not a hotel focused on guests - its a giant nightclub. If that's what you want, the W is doing a good job which accounts for the positive reviews. If you are also looking for a place to stay that offers more than a room and rude bouncers at every turn, I'd look elsewhere -- many nicer and less-expensive options. Sad disappointment for the W chain.

I've stayed at this hotel before for the annual Hustle Up the Hancock, so I had to look back to see if I posted a previous review. I had not. And, I think that I know why: the rooms do nothing for me, but the staff makes a good impression. I don't want to ding the hotel because I like the staff, but then I never look forward to staying there either.
Pros: Really personable staff. I only stay there for the event, so perhaps they put their best foot forward at that time. When staff members are able to deal with families carrying multiple bags, stuffed animals, and a talkative kid, I give them kudos for the extra effort.
Also, the rooms were clean....
Cons: Room decor. The rooms didn't have a personality. They were too functional (barren), even for a mid-range hotel. There were also lots of bare walls. They need to have a good interior designer come in to make some quick fixes.
Finally, I think that I really wanted to be at the Westin next door, although from being in its lobby it doesn't seem as kid friendly as the Hilton!

If you book your hotel through hotwire, priceline etc. and get a discount, get ready to be treated as if you're staying for free!
My husband and I booked this hotel two weeks in advance through hotwire. When we checked in, we requested a room with a king bed and were told that they didn't have any available. We checked in at - pm and there weren't many people around in this -- story hotel. This was later verified by another staff who also said that they should have many rooms with a king bed at the time we checked in!. We were told that we can only get a room with two queen beds. The staff's attitude was totally annoying, but there was nothing else to do since we had already paid for two nights. The beds were not queen as they claimed but they were double instead! My husband and I ended up sleeping in different beds, which were really old and not comfortable at all. It goes without saying that we didn't have a harbor view from our room, probably also because we booked it through hotwire! Even though, there were not many people staying in the hotel, almost every room in our hallway was occupied and it was very very noisy! We had hardtime falling asleep and when we did, we woke up in the middle of the night with horrible noises coming from the next room through the thin walls.
In short, our stay was a complete torture! My husband and I stayed in many hotels all across the country and never experienced something like that in a so-called """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""--star hotel""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""! Nice view and closeness to the airport are the only pros we could see. This hotel doesn't deserve its - stars!! Don't waste your money! You can do much better than Hyatt Harborside!

OMG, what a rip. STAY AWAY!!!!!!!!!!
The renovations on the surface look very nice but it seems they did not extend to the staff. 
The bellperson is also the shuttle driver so if they are out running people around town there is no assistance with your luggage and the luggage racks are so scarce that they are virtually impossible to find. Thankfully the valet helped me schlep my bags up to my room, he got a great tip.
The hotel was at ---% occupancy and the staff was not equiped to handle that type of volume. There were not enough towels for many rooms, houskeeping did not throw out food for days. There were moldy blueberries on the breakfast buffet at the make your own waffle station, and the Chef trained at CIA, he says.

My husband and I drive out from CT for a wedding in Chicago at the end of June - early July, ----. What a TREAT this place was after such a LONG drive! There are so many wonderful things to say about The Talbott. Where to start?

Overall our stay was fantastic! Everyone got to know us personally, BY NAME. When we go back to Chicago at some point, there is no doubt that we wll stay at the Talbott. The staff was wonderful, they had great information, and were very helpful in helping us book many tourist attractions, including the wine tours. We also received many tips on places to eat, shop and drink. (Ask for Kevin who gave us most of our information!). This was great cause nether of us had been to the area before. The location seemed to be in the center of everything we wanted to do, so we walked just about everywhere we wanted to go. I would recommend this hotel to anyone visiting San Fran, and when we travel out there again, it is where we are staying.

Stayed at Loews Denver Hotel on a Sunday night in December for one night when we were in town to see Portland Trailblazers game versus Denver. Upon arrival we were greeted promptly by hotel staff and got our room. We went up to our room and had been given wrong room. Called from the room and the front desk sent someone up with new room key down the hall. Went to that room and it was fine. I did notice the paint was chipped and peeling back from the wall in the shower area. That is always a downer as you feel like you are staying in a place that needs a face lift.
On Monday morning we woke up to construction noise-banging either in the room next to us or above us. This was at ---- hrs in the morning and that was kind of disappointing. At least they could of told us to warn us.
Did order room service for icecream and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hot"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" cookies according to the menu. Icecream was good, cookies were cold. 
Used the shuttle service to go to game and it was great! Staff was very friendly.
The biggest disappointment was probably the location of the hotel. I did not like the location. Not much around and some shady areas across the street on two sides of the hotel. My better half made the reservation and she said the website said Cherry Creek area. You are not within walking distance to Cherry Creek at this place. You could take shuttle, but don't stay here thinking you are staying in Cherry Creek area.
All in all it was an OK stay. I would not return here and probably would give a very neutral review to friends. Bottom line, I think you can do better than this hotel if wanting to stay in downtown Denver or Cherry Creek area.

Our family stayed here on our way to the Grand Canyon and then again on our way back home from the Grand Canyon. The hotel is located in a very convenient location right off the I--. It's a Hilton so what can I say except that...On both of our overnight stays hotel staff were very friendly and the rooms were quite and clean. I would enjoy another stay here again for business or pleasure.

Our room at The Quincy was furnished nicely and had a pleasant, contemporary feel to it. The accommodation was spacious and well-kept and the service at the hotel was friendly and attentive. The bathroom was a little outdated but clean.
The location of The Quincy was perfect for first-time visitors to DC. It is within easy walking distance to the White House, Dupont Circle, the Potomac River and the Capitol (if you're feeling energetic).

Came for a conference and loved it, the facilities were outstanding and everything was a short walk from my room which, by the way, was very spacious and came complete with a huge comfortable bed. The room service was a godsend after a full day of seminar although the Barefoot Bar provided relaxed dining with super friendly staff. The pool area looked great from the observation tower although I didn't get time to enjoy it and the coffee bar at reception made delicious coffee to enjoy next to the fireplace. All in all, a great experience.
A perfect place to stay in downtown Philadelphia! I hope to stay here again!

Pros: Right by the financial centre, noon checkout, decent size rooms, retro charm, nice looking lobby
Cons: Less close to the touristy piers (but not that far), a million light switches (main switches not bright enough), poor view outside, loud air conditioning unit
There's nothing wrong with the Omni hotel, it's quite serviceable. But it's a lot like plenty of other hotels in San Francisco, so it would seem. As someone from the often dull United Kingdom, I'm baffled why SF hotels seem to opt for dim rooms. There were two (rather cool-looking, retro) light switches but they barely illuminated the room - that took the other four lamps. Too many switches, too much faff. 
The view outside was also poor. I was looking out over other office buildings, so unless the curtains were closed there was limited privacy. These other office units had air conditioning units that made noise, as did the one in the hotel room.
On the up side there's everything here you could need for business: a desk, Wi-Fi, ethernet (no cable though), a good shower, reasonable bed, noon checkout and walkable from the financial centres. 
The attached Bob's restaurant is also meant to be decent, as are the giant to-order breakfasts. 
The retro charm of the detail and grand lobby also carries plenty of appeal. I'd happily stay again, but it's just a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""normal"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel well located for business, not an must-go-to social hub.

My daughters and I stayed at the James for a Spring Break trip to Chicago and I recently came back for a work trip. I have to say that I'm a forever fan and wholeheartedly recommend to anyone looking for a respite in Chicago.
The staff is the friendliest and most service oriented I've ever encountered. They're very attentive and not only take care of any needs or questions I pose, they foresee anything I need and take care of without me even knowing it was a need.
When traveling with my young daughters, everyone was incredibly sweet to them, making them feel even more special than they felt by staying at such a cool place. We all felt incredibly welcome.
One of my biggest pet peeves of business travel is paying for wireless access. Not at the James, wireless is free.
The rooms are simple yet posh. The beds are very comfortable and the rooms are quiet. The bath products are Kiehl's (a major selling point for me) and the little extras in the room made me feel like I wasn't just making another business trip in some generic hotel.
All of this at an incredible value. It really isn't too good to be true.
Thank you for making both of my trips so memorable and comfortable. I will never book another hotel in Chicago!

Situated close to restaurants, the Dupont Circle Metro station and the zoo, we were very pleased with the standard of accommodation offered at this lovely hotel. Staff were welcoming and helpful. Complementary wine is served each evening alongside nibbles, and coffee is available in the lobby until -am. I stayed at this hotel after their renovation. Everything was amazing, specially the service and the quality of the rooms. Room service is very prompt. The staff is amazing; i felt as if i was staying at a - star hotel. The manager is very friendly and is always available.

We (my college-age daughter and I) arrived at the Allegro on ------ and were warmly welcomed. We were able to have an early check-in which was very much appreciated. The room was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cute"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (ok, small), but was completely perfect. Everything was clean and well appointed. We stayed for - nights at this hotel--staff very polite and helpful! Concierge very helpful in arranging side trips and restaurant recommendations. We loved the hotel and our room that was immaculate and extremely comfortable. Best Location close to a lot of great restaurants and easy to get around town.. Overall, we would like to come back to this Hotel

All of the hotel staffs including the reservation manager are not willing to listen to their customers complaint about their hotel including the way they do business with their own vendors. Stay out of this hotel. You will be regretted!!!!

Can't say enough about the location - literally -- minutes from the airport (non-rush hour), maybe - minutes to Sea World and the beaches. The decor was modern, silver and black. The second-floor lounge offers free coffee and hot chocolate during the day and is a relaxing place to read. There was also continental breakfast and happy hour snacks, but the staff couldn't keep up with demand from a sold-out hotel. That didn't matter. The Fairfield was convenient and clean, and the front desk representatives were pleasant and helpful. The room was fine and seemed clean. It isn't my favorite place I have stayed in NYC but I would stay there again if I needed a reasonably priced room. I did find the neighborhood seemed a big sketchy but that might just be me. There are menus if you wish to get food in your room but the food is from local restaurants, not from the hotel. 
Breakfast is included; it was decent, nothing special. It was a buffet, nothing cooked to order, but with enough variety to satisfy most guests. 
Supposedly there is a nice rooftop bar, I think it's touted as the highest rooftop bar in Manhattan or something like that, but we never went up there.

My wife and I and two other couples just spent a wonderful weekend in New York at the Intercontinental the Barclay. It was not our first time there and once again the hotel did not disappoint us. There are many reasons why we continue to return to the Barclay. We love its location, we love the design of the hotel, we love the rooms, but most of all and what really keeps us coming back is the service. Everybody we dealt with treated us like we were the most important guests at the hotel. Whenever we called to request ice, more towels, glasses, etc,, they arrived in minutes with a friendly smile. The Concierge service is excellent. The Concierge is always available to recommend shops and restaurants and provide you with whatever New York information you need. What impressed me the most however, is the courteous and helpful service we received from Guest Relations and especially AnnMara Gayle. Well Done Intercontinental -You did it again.

A small hotel with everything! Really well placed for sight seeing on foot but quiet enough to g.et a good night sleep after sightseeing all day.Friendly staff very clean and excellent if on a budget.Would stay there again!
Had a great stay. Next to airport and got a great deal on priceline. Clean and comfy.

This hotel has been a favourite each year when we make our mammoth flight from Sydney to Charlotte to visit my husbands family.
Rooms are comfortable and clean. Beds are really comfortable and the staff really obliging.

I have NO hesitation recommending this hotel to anyone. Very very pleased with everything that it provides.

We had a fabulous sleep every night. The little touches such as the coffee machine in the room, dressing gown, weather forecast cards, newspapers daily and little chocolates made a big difference. I became addicted to the free fruit iced teas you could fill up on in the reception, and you could have coffees to take away with you in the morning. 
There was a keypad safe in the room, along with an iron and ironing board. There was a powerful hair dryer and a good range of shampoo, shower gels and moisturisers...topped up as required. 
The location was perfect for us...as it is on w--th st...only - streets away from Times Sq. It was on a quiet st...but we felt very safe walking about.

There is a -- pm check out time on the hotel. After we checked out the hotel held our bags for us for a few hours until we were ready to leave for the airport. They arranged a taxi for us...which was only a few dollars more expensive than the yellow taxis. 
Overall we had an amazing stay at the Disrtikt. We would certainly recommend this hotel to anyone wishing to visit New York. Very clean, very comfy and friendly helpful staff. Everything you would look for in a hotel and more!
Beautiful rooms, excellent service and unbeatable food at Mooo! the restaurant affiliated to the hotel. It's absolutely perfectly positioned too, just shy of the common. A great hotel.

We had originally booked - night through the conference and when we attempted to add - more nights - and receive the conference rate - we were given the runaround by - reservations people who couldn't confirm the original reservation but yet assured us the new rooms would be connected to the original room and rate. The location of the hotel was excellent and walking to many of the cities historic landmarks was easy. Many good restatraunts and clubs very close to the hotel. The folks at the front desk were extremely helpful. One person (Jim) in particular stood out and provided us with great information that helped us make the trip more enjoyable. The rooms were very large and the ipod docking stations in the rooms were a nice touch. The kitchen included a fairly large refrigerator with ice maker, four burner stove, micro-wave, & dishwasher. The maids in the hotel washed our dishes and kept the rooms extremely clean. Will definetly come back for a Rockies baseball game and stay at this hotel (stadium was about a -- minute walk away from Coors Field).

Over the last decade of traveling for business I've stayed at about -- different Hyatts across the country, so I'm kind of comparing this one to the others. Great restaurant on top of the hotel that gives a --- degree view of the city AND has great food! If I wasn't so loyal to Hyatt, I'd probably pick another hotel downtown because of the room.

I didn't realize the hotel only opened beginning of the month, amazing!!
My wife and I went to New York to celebrate our --th Wedding Anniversary, having been there on our honeymoon.
We arrived in NY very early, the day after a big snowstorm...we were not looking forward to hanging around in the cold for a half a day for check-in (would we be surprised!)...when I ordered the shuttle to the hotel, of course being new, it was unknown...had a bit if a 'Abbott-Costello' conversation with the shuttle dispatcher: """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""name of hotel?"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", me: """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""--- -th Ave"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" dispatcher: """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no the name, not the address"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", me: """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""that is the name and it is also the address""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""...

We arrived at -.-- am and optimistically asked for an early check-in. The staff were very friendly, and perhaps sympathetic due to the weather, and what can I say, within an hour we had a room. We were very grateful since it was so cold outside
The room is small, but did not feel claustrophobic at all, the decor simple yet very nice, the bed was very comfortable, the bathroom was of a good size with a great shower. Best of all, the price...esp. since we stayed for - nights! I did thorough research before booking and let me say that for price and location, there simply is no better value. If I ever get to NY again, I know exactly where I will be staying.

The room had a king size bed, a desk and one secretary's chair on casters. The room had no other seating and was approximately --- square feet, maybe less. I felt like I was in a cruise ship cabin. As a Marriott Silver Elite level guest, I expected better and felt let down.

My husband and I stayed for the long weekend after Thanksgiving. This was our first stay at the Iroquois Hotel. We loved it! The staff was friendly and the room was as described. It was one of the cleanest rooms we have ever stayed at. The bathroom was updated and wonderful. We received a free breakfast with our reservation. It was GREAT! We would surely stay here again.

I found no flaws with the room or hallways, and the staff was very knowledgeable and helpful. I will stay here again when I return.
This property was very clean and convienent for sight-seeing in Philly, and the city tours pick you up from the lobby at -- AM, which is great for families and business travelers alike. The hotel valet parking may seem expensive, however when compared to the other hotels in this city, you will find it to be reasonable. Unlike some other reviews I had read about their parking, it is actually charged to your room as it should be, you do not have to pay cash. 
The breakfast is average continental fare with powdered eggs, try the diner across the street for something better to start your day, or walk three blocks to the Terminal Market. And try the City Tavern for an unique """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""living history"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" experience for lunch or dinner, the tour trolleys can take you nearby from the hotel for lunch.

Area doesn't seem safe, room was dirty, holes in walls, door to room didn't close securely, cobwebs in corners, baseboard heaters falling off walls. We arrived on Sunday July -, the start of a - day heatwave that the news kept saying was the worst temperatures for the last -- years. We stayed for - days--nights the entirely length of the heatwave...lucky us. 
The hotel is located Midtown-East side with it being in a bit of a business district. The hotel is not overly hard to find but since it is on busy -rd Ave and right near a corner...but be prepared when you arrive or leave to have a hasty loading time..no messing around when unloading-loading...since traffic is right upon you if leaving at a busy time of day since it is near a corner.
The hotel lobby is clean, simply appointed, satisfactory and while not much room to sit if waiting for someone, it also is the place where occurred the only true complaint with our stay. 
My -- year old son was entering through the front doors of the hotel with myself following directly behind him. As we entered my son opened the right side door and started to negotiate around the door and walk-in when the doorman tried to grab the door from my son who was nearly past the door. At that moment the doorman also while grabbing the door from my son also triggered with his other hand a button that automatically and unexpectedly opened both doors. It happened so quick and my son was so close to the other door which had been closed that when the door popped unexpectedly open it hit my son square in his head, especially along the top part of his nose, right along the bridge of his glasses. It bent the bridge of the glasses. since I was right behind him I saw my son going ...oww loudly ..and also grabbing the top bridge of his nose and the glasses. The doorman looked at us surprised....gave my son and myself the rudest look..like we were at fault...(as if someone purposely walks into a door). I spoke out loudly so that the doorman could hear me...and said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sorry""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""...and then motioned for him to come in to the lobby and see how we were doing, be courteous and apologize. the doorman looked at me turned around outside and walked away up the street a little staying outside....certainly I could have went back out and got him but didn't want to appear hostile...which somehow in the goofy world I would have been accused of. Additionally my son was just sitting there holding his nose, obviously not liking the pain. Anyway, my son just wanted to go the room so we went up to our room....but the doorman never came back later and apologized..my wife and myself both went back down and talked to the head doorman, an assistant manager on duty, a loss prevention officer who came up to our room and even an representative from Marriott who called to see how we were doing and offering compensation to replace his glasses or pay for a visit to the doctor since my son got quite a bruise from the mishap. While all said they were sorry, there is something to be said about people owning up to just being human. The doorman may have hurt my son by accident but he should be man enough to give apology. 
While it did bend the bridge of his glasses my son chose to just live with it and move one and when we got back home Costco was able to send them of to reposition them at no charge. We eventually got the doorman's name which was Ramon from the conversation we had with the loss prevention officer right after the event occurred. 
I am not bitter toward Marriott...everyone else did their job correctly and most importantly courteously. I am sure a number of you on here would be wanting blood from Marriott for the mishap..but things sometimes just happen...but I am still a perturbed that Ramon would not take the time to simply say sorry. I think it was quite out of place for a Marriott employee to not call, come up to our room or talk to us any of the times we saw him later in the lobby...with one time him purposedly avoiding us when I finally caught his eyesight one time...I motioned for him to come over nicely and he gave me a scowl and walked back outside. I am sorry for naming him by name.but I do still think he owes us a simple apology.,,he seems bitter for his job...what a shame. 
The moral of this stories...slight complaint...please watch yourself walking in the door and be nice to the doorman....he probably has had a rough life and afraid of losing his job or something. Sad that people..especially often hard New Yorkers...can't take a reality check in their life and learn to say I am sorry and a few other words of kind endearance to prove they are wonderful people which I am know them to be. 
Otherwise..please stay here...the rooms are above averaged in size...especially by New York standards..Marriott level service was definitely there.. we never lacked for anything, towels, sheets. The room we stayed in had - queens and a sofa bed which was good for us since we had ourselves and a -- year teenager and a -- year old teenage girl. This made it so both teenagers had a bed and since the room was a above averaged sized we could lay all the bags out and not trip over any of them.....great especially if you for those folks on your trip who may have all of those clothes, makeup and such. 
We paid --- a night plus tax which was pretty reasonable for as many people we had compared to other hotels where we would have got quite a bit less, smaller room and no where near as central. Also free Wi-Fi which worked good the whole stay. 
The other slight complaint is that the hotel regulates the room temperature..it will not go below -- degrees..so if you are one of those types who get a hotel room and put the a-c to deep freeze..this place is not for you. My boyfriend and I loved this hotel! Immediately upon arrival, we were greeted promptly by a friendly, smiling front desk attendant. Great location, felt safe walking in the area at night after going out evenings. Near shopping, restaurants, art galleries, China Town, public transportation. The room was very clean. Good accommodations. NIce staff. A little noisy in the morning on our side of the building due to ally with trash pick up for hotel and restaurant below our window which we preferred to keep open. It is the second time we choose the Sohotel hotel for our holidays in New York and we are always very happy! First about the staff! All of them are very welcoming and helpful. Junior was very nice, he was always available to give us adices about our visits or very helpful when we needed something. Then, the rooms are very clean ans spacious. The price is not too bad when you know the price of a room in any hotel in New york! Great hotel in the middle of meatpacking. Loved the location and the food. Can really recomend the breakfast.

The Rouge was an accjdent choice when its sister hotel, George, which we picked originally was full. Not having been to Washington DC before, there was no real preference for where to stay; somewhere described on internet postings as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""near the White House, Memorials and Museums"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""with friendly staff"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" seemed reasonable. By signing up with the Kimpton Hotel loyalty programme, guests have an option of US$-.-- breakfasts or cocktails, as well as a US$-- voucher to raid the mini bar. There is free internet in the common area as well as continental breakfast each morning. The breakfast has tea, coffee, hot chocolate, fruit, muffins, bagels, juice. The lower level (basement) has a microwave and ice machine. During the day, the bar isn't open and it becomes a place to sit and read the paper or watch TV. The large common area also has comfortable seating and at night this area doubles as a club. It is up a few stairs and one night there was a private party up there. The steps made it easy for the management to close it off for the private event. Each room has toiletries, iron-ironing board, hair dryer, CD-

With plenty of great restaurants and bars within walking distance, we felt right at home in the neighborhood. The interior patio was a great place to relax with a beer or a glass of wine; the local DJ added to the experience on Wednesday night. Rooms are very spare, and the lighting provided for reading in bed is awful, but the amenities (shampoo, lotion, etc.) were elegant. Don't go for luxury, but do go for location; ask for a room away from the street and the patio.

I did get to the hotel late the first night and was so tired that I ate dinner down in the restaurant, which I normally do not do. The chef came out and discussed the menu with me and with his recommendation, I ordered the grilled filet of salmon in lemon butter with sauteed spinach and REAL mashed potatoes. A glass of Chardonnay complimented the meal and I can tell you that the meal was really, really delicious. The hotel was clean and the front desk persons that helped me, always looked straight at me while we were talking, and all had smiles on their faces, which means a lot when you are dealing with the public. Subway access was just a couple of blocks on either side. Taxis were fairly easy to hail also. A Duane Reed was within walking distance.
