Anyway, since I mentioned this to the hotel, they wrote to me and said all I need to do is request this upon check-in and all will be sorted.
Concierge; Godsend. Staff at the concierge desk knew everything you didn't know, booked trips for you, made reservations, etc etc, then printed off the details for you in case you forgot. Brilliant!
Food: I didn't eat or drink at the hotel as I was out all the time!
Lobby: Beautiful, The public areas of the hotel were spotless and stunning.
Staff: Perfect. The door staff were brilliant. Very humourous, and even sorted out a stupid taxi driver that couldn't understand a word I was saying! Use the hotel limo if you get the chance; the drivers are first rate.
I would stay here every trip to New York if it weren't for the price. You do get what you pay for and this place is worth every single penny!!
The view is excellent, the room clean, but the service left much to be desired. We had items amenities everyday and had to call to ensure our receipt of basic items. I thought this was the Hilton..

It is a standard $--,-- from the PHL airport. Once you enter you are treated like royalty, such friendly staff. The lobby is small and intimate. The rooms are amazing- huge, beautifully furnished with a desk, free internet, huge TV, big sofa in a room that must be ---x the size of a normal hotel room. The bathroom was a piece of work with a TV and separate bath and shower. My wife had to take as many of the shampoo's and body wash (there is one for the am and one for the pm!) and they were packaged in large tubes.
The Bar does a great happy hour- it is fancy but the drinks are fabulous and $- (cocktail) and $- for beer-wine. The hor d'oeuvres were magnificent. We then ate in the restaurant- had a fixed price - course meal for $--- well worth it.
The pool and exercise room was large and the pool was warm. The staff was amazing (have I mentioned that?). You have to ask for a coffee machine (you get one of those fancy Keurig ones!) but well worth it at no extra cost.

We had a great stay at the Chancellor Hotel - I only wish we could have stayed longer! 
The only downsides - some of which are mentioned by other guests - cannot be helped due to the location of the hotel. Self parking is offsite at a lot around the corner, views are not great for each room and the rooms themselves are on the small side (though decorated wonderfully!) Keep in mind that the hotel is situated right next to Union Square and thus does not have much room. 
But because of the location, it's a half a block walk to the giant Macy's and shopping centers in Union Square (we could see the big Xmas tree from our room) and just a few blocks from the cable car turnaround and Chinatown. There's also a cable car stop directly outside the hotel.
The have a cozy lobby bar, free cookies on arrival, candy jars and rubber duckies in the room and a pillow menu. All the staff we encountered were friendly and professional.
The windows opened and we spent part of the evening enjoying a breeze while listening to a gentleman in the Square playing Xmas jazz music!
The Chancellor was a charming hotel in a fantastic location for a very, very reasonable price. If we stay in the Union Square area in the future, the Chancellor will be where we stay!

We stayed at the Algonquin whilst I was visiting to run the marathon. We arrived last Thursday (-st Nov --) and left on Monday -th Nov. A few days before we travelled we saw some negative comments from guests and it caused us some concern.
We needn't have worried. The only bad thing about this hotel was that during our stay there was some construction happening on some nearby land which was noisy but they did not work at the weekend. However the staff advised us as soon as we arrived and promised that if we found the noise too much that they would be happy to move us as soon as a room became availble. We were fine with it. I have read negative feedback about the dark foyet etc and wonder whether the people who booked actually looked at the pictures of the hotel first as it is obviously not a bright modern hotel!!!
Great hotel, great staff (didn't like one girl on the reception who was miserable and unhelpful) the rest were great. Kevin, Sean and a lovely English chap (can't remember his name) were all really helpful on the door and for helping with luggage etc.
Matilda the cat was super, I left - cats at home who I missed so having her around was comforting. I would definitely return to this hotel.
This hotel is very central with great access to Times Square and -th avenue and I couldn't fault it. It's also worth mentioning that they have a good gym too which is pretty much open all the time.

The view from our Balcony of the Bay was amazing! The beds were comfortable and the staff friendly.
(Though i did request to change rooms as the original one had an obstructed bay view, and i had paid for a Bay view. They did change us so for this I'm happy. Also we left the room at --am and came back at -pm and the room had not been attended too)

This hotel used to be okay years ago, but on my last stay I crossed it off my list. Bedspread was stained and seemed dirty. Pillows STANK, and that's one of my hotel pet peeves is old, stinky pillows. The rest of the room was okay, but I need restful sleep when I'm traveling on business...and sleeping in a dirty stinky bed doesn't do it.

My husband and I stayed at The Chancellor for a few nights last Feb and we don't have a bad word to say about it. The location's great, staff were helpful, there's complimentary tea, coffee and home-made cookies in the lobby any time of day or night, and the rooms have this 'old world' charm that you'll never find at a chain hotel.
A massive heart-felt thanks to the gentleman on night shift when we checked-in who organised a bottle of sparkling wine and a card wishing us a happy marriage when I mentioned that we'd just been married in Vegas, when he asked where we'd come from. We didn't get so much as a congratulations at The Venetian in Vegas so I was very surprised when this nice bottle of wine and a card turns up in our room!
We'll be back at The Chancellor in ---- - I wouldn't stay anywhere else in San Fran.

My husband and I couldn't be more thrilled with our stay at Hotel Teatro to celebrate our -st Anniversary. We indulged and stayed in the suite (room ---) and loved it! The Hotel offers a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Romance Package"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that was divine. Rose petals lead us from the door into the bedroom, a rose petal heart on our bed, etc. Ask about their available packages.
The attention to detail is superb. The manager on duty left a hand signed anniversary card, etc. You get what you pay for. The prices aren't cheap but for a special occasion, both hotel and staff don't disappoint.

My wife and I stayed here for a week in late May, ---- while we were between homes. (We live in Cambridge.) We stayed in a Commonwealth Room, and it was a flat-out fabulous room. The room is very large, w-a large separate sitting area separated from the sleeping area by a heavy curtain, and a luxurious (large, again) bathroom with a separate w-c (a very nice touch). In addition to the size and the standard luxurious amenities, e.g., excellent toiletries, - large TVs, direct-dial phones in each room, the room had nice details such as small lights positioned in the archway-like structure that separates the sleeping and sitting areas and another small light focused on a decorate vase in the entryway.
All of the hotel staff -- front desk, turndown service, doormen, bellmen -- were extremely courteous and professional. We didn't use the exercise room but I got a look at it and it was small but well-equipped for its size. The food at Great Bay (the adjoining restaurant) was quite good, though the service was spotty.
For the price we paid (we booked thru the hotel), I can't imagine a better value in Boston. Irrespective of price, this was one of the best hotel stays I've had anywhere. Not the absolute best but certainly among the best.
We'll hopefully be here again soon, for a getaway-without-kids-and-dog weekend.

After a two week trip round the west coast where we had stayed in motels costing a quarter of the price of the Crowne Plaza but had received excellent customer service, I was expecting the same kind of thing when my husband and I stayed at the CP in BH for three days...how wrong can you be?
We checked in okay...the receptionist was very helpful and outr first night passed without any bother. The next night we asked the concierge about how to get around in LA and did she have a map, as when we were in San Fran, the hotel there had given us a map of ALL the streets in San Fran, had advised us on best places to eat, where to get buses, trams and cable cars from and where to avoid. All the concierge at CP did was chuck a map of the Star Lines sight seeing bus,which was a very basic map that did NOT have all the street names on it. When we said that no, we didnt want a taxi and that we wanted to walk to places, she laughed in our faces. Not a good sign. We then asked her about places to eat and she just pointed in the direction of the Bistro that is attached to the hotel! So we asked again, and she shrugged and said that because she didnt really eat out, she couldnt recommend anywhere! We were suprised by this lack of local knowledge as we had had such good service in San Fran. After spending the day in Hollywood,we went back to the hotel to ask about tickets to Universal Studios. There was now a guy in the concierge seat who, I think, had obviously watched too man mafia films...he sat back in his chair, looking down on us stupid english tourists and even tutted when my husband asked why taxis that the hotel booked were so expensive? Once again, we asked for a more detailed map of the area, only for the guy to get very rude and give us yet another bus tour map. When I pointed out that we had already got that map and was there any other he could give us he said no and that couldnt we work the map out? So annoyed! The next day after going to Universal (our taxi driver was great!) there was yet another person on the desk. He was very polit and helpful but even he could not give us a map of the area. He did manage to give us a map of restuarants near where we were so that helped a little bit....but what really upset me was the fact that on the day we were leaving the same concierge we had seen on the first day was getting a map printed off by the reception staff to give to a guest!! All the other staff were very helpful anf friendly....I just think that the concierge staff need to be more knowledgable about the area surrounding the hotel, listen more to guests feedback as they could let the concierge know about good places to eat, what to do, what to avoid etc...and have more customer care training...or take a lesson from some of the other staff there!

This hotel was great for the price. The only fault I found in it was the street nose (honking horns) which I realize is hard to avoid in NYC. I would recommend a room on a higher floor. I was on the second floor. 
The room was on the smaller side but was average size by NYC standards. I was expecting the room to be much smaller. My dad and I had more than enough room. 
The staff was extremely friendlly and accomodating. We arrived at --am. Check in is at -pm. They held our bags in the office for us. Not sure if it was locked up but we didn't have any valuables so we weren't too worried.
It's a really great location. One block from the subway. We were able to walk to many of the places we were visiting. It's about a ten minute walk to Lombardi's Pizza in Little Italy (don't miss it!). It's about two blocks away from Katz's Deli (overpriced). 
It's a great hotel expecially considering you mostlly sleep and shower in a hotel when you're in NYC.

Me and my boyfriend stayed here for the night and The Lafayette hotel is a great hotel for someone on a budget. they just finished renovating their rooms and a lot of the hotel and they look pretty good. There is nothing better than a place with a history and some personality and this place has a lot of it. ever room has a name of a celebrity from the past. ex, our room was Gary Cooper.
The room was big enough and very clean. Had no oder, the bed was HUGE and comfortable. new carpet, flat screen tv that works very well. New light fixtures, movement sensor lights in the room and bathroom. and has a very good air conditioner. The ONLY issue we had was the air conditioner started to leak really bad but that was just our room.
The bathroom was nice. it has a working and clean toilet. has a nice shower thats big enough and a free standing old style sink. 
The service was very good, everyone was more than nice to us. we called for towels and they were very nice, when we had the leak, we called and they sent someone up right away, offered us to switch rooms and everything. They also helped us with finding interesting places to go around the city. 
Location: The location in the city is great because you are really close to absolutely anywhere you wanna be in san deigo. (we recommend old town, its great) its -miles from old town, - from gaslamp, its really convenient. The surrounding of the hotel is not bad really. its actually got some cute little places. and its not scary or loud or anything like that. 
The breakfast is not bad. they had coffee, hot tea, cold water, and orange juice. they had bagels with cream cheese, butter, jelly. They also had some cereal and milk. and also waffles which were very good. best part were the waffles. 
We didnt use the pool or the gym but both looked really nice. The FREE PARKING is actually great. its underground parking with key entry. so very safe and close by. and of course free. 
If youre expecting luxury, this is probably not your hotel but if youre just looking for a few good night stays, this is the place. we will come back if we come back to san deigo.

Phenomenal staff -- so accommodating and friendly! Entire hotel was well appointed and very clean. Huge breakfast (including hot items) which was unexpected but very much appreciated. (I stayed in the Hampton Inn Times Square North a couple years ago, and the free breakfast was very basic.)

Good location but the rooms were soo small there was hardley room to move around. We were really disappointed at the small rooms we were triping over our luggage. The location was great empire state building right around the corner. We did not have breakfast here as it was a bit pricey and we chose to go to the many little delicatesens close by where we met some great travelers like us. The staff was helpful and pleasant especially the doormen nice helpful fellas. We probabley would not stay here again.

My stay did not start off well as my cab driver hit construction at the end of the block and told me I'd need to walk the last block and a half to the hotel, but once I arrived, it was a good experience.
Room size varies - mine was smallish, while a colleague was pleased with the size of his room. Ask for a larger room. 
The vibe is very boutiquey and I'd say a bit on the masculine side. My room had a huge, brown leather upholstered headboard and a plaid throw blanket. I can't be sure, but the sheets may well have been Frette, they were very high quality, as were the Kiehl's toiletries in generous sample sizes.
There is a nice bar in the Lobby with a library vibe, which markes for a good after work stop.

My wife and I just stayed at the W for four nights last weekend and it was amazing. The hotel took care of our every need. The lounge, room, bar etc was first rate. I was especially impressed with Eddie and Nelson were extremely helpful and they made the trip extra special for us!
PS. The bed was one of the most comfortable I have ever slept in.

The Seattle Pan Pacific Hotel is a great all around place to stay. After a hard day of sight seeing it is nice to be able to come back to polite doormen, an elegant lobby and quick elevators that risk you to your room. My corner room had a fantastic view of the Spaceneedle and was very comfortable. The room was kept clean and tidy by the staff and had all the amenities one would expect. The price was quite high with add ins but in the end it was worth it. Do yourself a favor and stay here.

Stayed again at the Westin over the Canadian Thanksgiving (Columbus Day) weekend. 
It is a nice enough hotel - close to the airport, with decent shared shuttle service with the Holiday Inn down the road. 
Check in was quick and efficient - even tho my room was from Priceline, the front desk pro actively found my Starwood account number and added it for my incidentals.
The room itself was fine, huge desk area, comfortable bed, nice bathroom.
The hotel itself is in a bit of a need of a reno, everything is fine, but just feels a bit late ----s.
All in all, there is very little I remember about this hotel, and it is - days later. Not a bad thing, really.

Stayed here a year ago and the hotel was much better. The hotel restaurant and wine bar was a nice touch to this hotel since there are no amenities. Upon arriving this time (January ----) I noticed that the restaurant and wine bar where closed. Oh well, now on to the rooms.
I was upgraded to a larger room but it was still very small compared to the other hotels in the area. The furniture looked like it was as old as the hotel. I think ben Franklin carved his initials in the desk in the corner of the room. The -- inch TV barely worked and had no features other than basic cable. 
The toilets only would flush when you held the knob down and thanks to gravity it would flush.
I would say for the price it wasn't horrible (I only paid $--.-- per night). Overall, I'd say if you are looking for a no frills hotels that might be haunted and if they re-open the restaurant and bar I would stay here again for the price.

As a single woman traveller, I must admit the hotel takes great care of its guest... From the friendly reception to the excellent concierge.. they were very patient despite my numerous demands!!! I had such a wonderful time in Boston, thanks to Nine Zero.. Absolutely wonderful! A special thanks to Kelly for all her help.. :)

This hotel was very clean and modern and at just - blocks from the White House, a perfect location for sightseeing. The lobby is very small with only a couple of chairs and the front desk but there is a fairly spacious club room with comfortable seating, a tv, two computers with internet (and complimentary tea and coffee Mon-Fri) on the -nd floor. There is also complimentary cold bottled spring water throughout the hotel which was brilliant. 
My room was very small (even though mine seemed to be a room for disabled access which is usually bigger) and I get the impression this is the same everywhere in the building but it was clean, comfortable and well maintained. There was a linen cupboard on each floor for you to help yourself to any extra things you needed. If you're looking just for a place to sleep it's fine but I wouldn't recommend it if you plan on spending a lot of time in the room as you might start to feel claustrophic - especially if like me you have an internal facing room. Also the walls were very thin and the room doors noisy when they close. The wireless internet in my room never worked for me and I heard many people at the desk with the same problem. However I just used the club room pc's instead without any issues. 
The area the hotel is in is definitely a business district and mostly closes down at weekends but it seemed very safe (lot's of other tourist around) and there was construction to the side and across the street from the hotel. I was never bothered too much with noise as I was on the opposite side and in an internal facing room. There were a few places in walking distance to eat (I can recommend Famous Luigi's if you like pizza or Italian) and you can order room service from the hotel itself or from a few local restaurants. The hotel restaurant is small and quite expensive and the menu quite limited but the food is nice. I felt breakfast especially was expensive at $-- for a full buffet but the tip was included in this. I ended up eating out most of the time anyway. There isn't really a place to sit in the bar except for the -- or so stools, I didn't feel encouraged to spend any time there. 
The desk staff were helpful and friendly with checking in and out and whenever I asked for directions or recommendations. Overall I was very happy with my stay and would stay there again.
If you're sightseing definitely buy a two day tour to see as much as possible. I got mine from Tourmobile which includes Arlington Cemetary. Wear comfortable shoes!

This hotel is a gem in the center of Georgetown. It is an excellent value. Our room was spacious and well-appointed. The entire staff was genuinely friendly, not the fake, forced politeness you get at other hotels. All sweet people, helpful and cheerful. The restaurant has fresh, real food. Good from breakfast through lunch, to a nightcap at the end of the day. It felt like home.

This hotel is a terrific bargain on the Miracle Mile. It's very clean, spacious, and located right across from several major stores and attractions. It has a fantastic little martini bar downstairs and is within a short walk to the Chop House. I will stay in this hotel every time I visit Chicago.

Stayed at this hotel for the first time. The location is ideal. The hotel is across the street from the Metreon, and Union Square is a quick - minute walk. The hotel has a corporate feel to it. The front desk person was somewhat surley, but he did grant our request for a room with - double beds on an upper floor. The bar on the --th floor has incredible views, and allows children which was a plus for us. The room was a nice size, and the bathroom was wonderful. We did not hear any noise outside our hotel room at all. The parking is outrageously priced as reported by others, but because of the convenient location, we did not have to take taxis, even for an evening performance at the Curran theatre. Two beefs, no honor bar, and no coffee-maker in the room.

Motel is now America's Best Value Inn. I was hunting for it in the list and couldn't find it. I had to match the address and matched the pictures. Not much has been improved here from the previous company. We had to split rooms to get two double beds in each room. We were told the rooms were not available together due to maintainance issues. The one room had a king bed and the other had two double beds. We needed them on the first floor because of problems with stairs. The king room, my room was not ready either. When my friend turned on the water faucet fell off. She was able to get it on but could not get it to work. I was going to call the office and found the phone was not hooked up. Searching for a phone jack I came across the plate for a phone jack but no phone jack. It may have been behind the headboard but I couldn't get to it. The office couldn't put us in another room. The clerk sent a handy man to fix it. He couldn't find the part and stuck a piece of meta, sort of like what you would put in a baked potato .With so many rooms down for maintainence he couldn't get a faucet off one of them? We could move itt up and back gently. The rug was dirty and there were two big dirt spots or burns? There was grafatti on the bathroom door. The toilet was also brokern and rocked. There wasn't a breakfast. Onlyt coffee was available. I would have liked to have left but the other people in our party were in for the night. The pool is closed for the season. Don't stay here.

Solid comfort suites, the AC in our room on the first floor was cold enough to allow you to hang meat in the room. Bed was comfortable, foldout bed was in great shape, but had to stand the coffee table up to make room. Bathroom is very small, but the sink is on the outside. Had a new refrigerator and microwave. 
Very close to a couple of convenience stores and - minutes from malls and several other stores.
Nicest thing for my son was the -- hour pool and hot tub, even after a long day out, he could still come back and swim. 
Good internet access and had a Texas-shaped-waffle maker for breakfast.

Visited Houston on a - day business trip. This was my first stay at a Courtyard I usually stay at the regular Marriotts propertys.
The Hotel is convinently located in Houston downtown near several entertaining sites (baseball and basket ball) amoung others.
Room was good, nice big bed a sofa and a working table with internet. Hotel charges $-- for valet parking, there are several parking options aroud the building you might want to consider them before paying the hotel.
The only thing that i did not like was the staff, i found them to be a little stiff and botherd when i needed there services. I think they had few people working during those days, that might off streesd out the staff.
Hotel has a nice pool and a jacuzzi.

Last minute stay in NYC and booked through discount travel site. Had no idea what to expect and was pleasantly surprised! Room very clean, not extremely spacious but understandable in city. Very convenient location, great staff interactions and concierege was very helpful providing info for attractions including step by step to and from directions. By far, best of the experience is the view. NYC skyline can't be beat... would recommend!

Friendly staff, nice reception, on the river but about -- minute walk from the main part of the River Walk. Compared to other hotels on the trip this one was quite expensive, but compared to other hotels on the river walk it provided good value. Breakfast buffet is OK for $-- each, always available with the refills.

This was our first time at a Howard Johnson and the hotel was attractively done, the price was very nice and the breakfast being included was just amazing. We stayed - nights and each morning was eggs, sausage, biscuits, gravy, donuts, muffins, cereal, waffles, bagels ect. We ate in our jammies and got around nice and slow, no rush.
Bigger than all of this, we came to San Antonio to visit a brother, and the second day of our stay I got a call from home in Missouri that our dad died. I was not near a fax of my own or anything I needed for such an event. BUT, the general manager of the hotel, Labib is his name, faxed funeral stuff out for me, received faxes for me, and was all around a fine and compassionate new friend. Sarah at the front desk, also helped us plan our day trips with her great suggestions. Go and enjoy!!

Stayed here for a few nights for DU graduation. Perfect location, just a few minutes on the highway from DU. Even though it is next to the highway, you don't hear it too much, you will still hear some traffic though.
Beds were decent, bathroom was decent, nothing outstanding but worth the price paid. Loved having a kitchen to make snacks, etc. Pool was clean and a good temperature. 
Don't expect too much from the Complimentary Breakfast... Coffee was full of grounds, muffins are bland, but they do offer name-brand yogurt, cereal, juice, etc. 
I'd stay here again if needed though I'd go to King Soopers around the corner and get my own breakfast foods.

We also had a reservation through expedia at the Vagabond (with a confirmation #) and arrived Friday Sept. -nd to find a lobby full of angry people who also had reservations and had been told there were no rooms available. The manager was rude to everyone. After contacting expedia we were all transferred to another hotel. The other hotel was nicer but charged $-- US a night for parking. The whole thing took hours and we missed half a day of the music festival we had come to see.

We had a very pleasant stay in mid-May. Our room was a suite with a marina view and it was apparently one that has had a recent renovation. The bathroom and kitchen cabinets were new. We had very little contact with staff but when we did they were friendly. A great area for walking around this small island. Also very close to downtown and Point Loma. Yes, the place has been there for a while but this is a positive for the mature flora on the grounds.
Love the hotel and the friendliness of the staff... So very helpful and pleasant...

I booked the pod hotel on the advice of a friend, having decided to come to New York for - nights on very short notice.
The hotel was significantly cheaper than any other options that I had found.
My single room was small, but spotless, with everything that I needed (including free wireless). The shared bathroom was just next door, and was pristine. The piped quiet relaxing music was a nice touch!
I lost my door key, and the front desk replaced it (a swipe card) with no fuss whatsoever. The staff were friendly and helpful.
I didn't stay for breakfast - walked round the corner to Tal's bagels instead (definitely worth the ---- minute walk!)
A great place to stay, and a real bargain in New York

I stayed at the ATT center over the past weekend for an event hosted by UT Austin. The hotel was nicely appointed, as expected. 
*Good
- Staff was helpful and attentive
- Bed was comfortable
* Average
- The entrance isn't well marked or obvious at first pass
- The bedside alarm wasn't reset, so I was woken up at - am by a shrieking alarm clock that I didn't set
- On a somewhat related note, the alarm clock is bright blue and adds a lot of brightness to the room at night
Overall, a good place to stay, especially if you need to be close to the University.

We stayed at the Michelangelo Hotel -------- - ------- and loved every minute of our stay. The location was the best in Manhattan - close to theater, shopping & many tourist sights, but off -th Ave so the rooms are quiet. We were on the -rd floor & seldom heard any traffic noise.
The room was well-sized and comfortable while the hotel lobby & lounge were beautiful and luxurious.
For the most part during our stay, the weather was warmer than we expected and we appreciated having full control of the air conditioner in the room. It was automatic, similar to central air conditioning units in our home in Texas, so it cycled on and off to maintain the desired temperature.
And the tub! I'm normally a shower person, but couldn't resist taking some long soaks in the HUGE tub. What a way to relax from a long day of sightseeing!
I loved this hotel & will stay here again when I next visit NYC.

Booked for $-- on Priceline. Room was King Bed.
Lobby was busy, but there was a convention staying at the hotel. Staff was nice and courteous. The bathroom from other units was audible, and the hallway wall seemed thin, but it never woke me up.
We weren't in the room much, but the location was great if you are in town for a sightseeing weekend like we were. Few blocks from the State-Lake L stop that put you on a few different lines.
While the room was a bit small, it was very comfortable and the hotel is very close to Union Station and the metro, as well as the Capitol. The staff were very nice and helpful.

I usually do not step out of my safe zone when traveling. Let me explain, there are chains of hotels that give you a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""safe"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" feeling in strange place. So I actually cancelled my safe hotel for the Shoreham. I was not disappointed. Very convenient to shopping, museums, food and the subway. 
The Shoreham is an interesting place. Something very different in mostly good ways. Great staff in the lobby. I passed on the complimentary drink at checkin. Elevators are small but the rooms are above average for NYC. Not bad. I have seen smaller. Massage chair was great. Shower temp and pressure were oh so nice. Bed was comfortable.
The strange. Sink and toilet are so close together you have to reach under the sink to flush. One of those we installed it and did not think moments. I have been in hotels where the shower nozzle meets your belly button. So this was more of a wtf than a major issue. 
The convenient. Grocery store right around the corner to avoid mini bar surprises at checkout. Subway on a few blocks away. 
Beware. My hotel bill had someones food and drink from the bar on my first night. The front promptly took it off. Mistakes happen. 
I would definitely stay here again. I just wish they were part of a loyalty program.

This hotel was very clean. I am a very picky person and I could not find one thing wrong with this place. The room was gorgeous and had an awesome view of Phoenix. I felt like a VIP. The staff at the fron desk was very nice and they took care of my bags for me while I went to a meeting (after I had checked out). Great place. I will be staying there again next time I go to Phoenix for business.

Very nice place to spend - or - nights. Everyone is very friendly and helpfull.
Nice breakfast, good connections.
Parking costs --$-night and it's an hidden cost.
If your neighbour is not quite, you may hear some noise. Room Are not perfectly isolated.
Anyway I will suggest it for a short period

We were in Houston for an event and choose the Sheraton North because it is so close to the airport and they have a free -- hour shuttle (every -- minutes). Upon arrival, we called the hotel from the airport and were told the shuttle would be there within -- minutes. We had to call the hotel twice before the shuttle finally showed up -- minutes later. Our room was clean, but the worn-torn carpet gave it a tired feeling. I think they must put a governor on the air conditioning because it would not go below --*. The room never felt cool and the humidity (especially after morning showers added to it) in the room was horrible. $-- for wifi. Starbuck in room coffee was a plus. I would recommend this hotel for a night before heading out on an early morning flight just because they offer the free shuttle. It is not a destination hotel. 
 We were in Houston for an event downtown. We asked the valet to call a taxi for us before going downstairs (they told us it would be about -- minutes). The valet had to call several taxi companies and finally got one to come. By then, we were running a little late and didn't clarify with the driver before getting in and leaving the hotel. The continental breakfast is fine and what is standard for this type of hotel.
I would use the hotel again without hesitation.

We stayed here with our family for a family vacation. I made reservations through American Express Travel Agency so we could use our points. Even with that, the hotel is expensive. We got two rooms, one for parents and the other for our daughter and her fiance. Our room, a double was spacious and with a good view of --nd street. We started our USA tour staying at this hotel and it was great.

The restaurant inside was a little pricey but offered very high quality food.

I've stayed in a lot of hotels in New York and as a mid range traveller i'm mostly interested in location. The location one block from the N-R line and -- minute walk from other major subway stations was ideal.
The hotel is clean and while the rooms are fairly basic they are more than adequate. This is the first time i've been prompted to write a review on this website and i'm doing so to commend the great staff at the hotel.

I stayed overnight at the Fairmount for a business meeting and wished I could have moved in! The hotel is beautifully furnished, elegant without being fussy, and well equipped for both business and pleasure visits. Besides the luxe touches that have become almost standard, like comfy beds and robes and abundant desk outlets, the Fairmount includes details that other hotels would do well to add, such as snake-neck reading lamps attached to the bed that cast a cool spotlight right on your page; in-room Keurig coffee makers; and window panels that actually open for some fresh air. Even the coffee service at our meeting included classy touches like flavored syrups, and there were gigantic hot soft pretzels and mustard instead of the usual gluey cookies. One thing I can't comment on is price, because my room was prepaid, but I'll definitely check this place out on my next tourist trip to DC.

Had an early meeting in SD , stayed at the Hyatt. Room was great. Front desk staff very helpful. Breakfast buffet, so-so, great gym, and convenient location off the freeway. If you need a business style hotel, north off downtown SD, I would look no further than the Hyatt.

Just returned from a - night visit at the Drury Inn & Suites on the Riverwalk. Nice and clean hotel. I am a very fussy traveler who reads all the reviews and wanted to write a review for once! I'm not one to overpay for a hotel room. I like to get a good deal and stay somewhere nice, but I don't like paying alot. The prices of the hotels on the Riverwalk are very high. This was the best hotel for the money that I could find after hours of shopping. My husband and I were very happy with my choice. They have a great breakfast, happy hour with - free drinks each night and soda and popcorn each afternoon included in your rate. They also have a pool and hottub for relaxing. I was most impressed with the cleaniness of the city after visiting many ciites. The hotel has lots of security. For me, a bit much. I do like to feel safe, but this was a very nice area. 
The location was so convenient on the Riverwalk for walking and going to eat. We didn't get a car and walked everywhere. The Riverwalk is very close even if you're not a walker. We walked up on the streets to the Marketsquare ( -- mn walk), Tower of the Americas- -- mn; The Alamo, and the Rivertown Mall. Unless you need to leave the city or have a longer visit, you do not need a car. The cab seemed overpriced; -- min ride for $--. The staff at the hotel are great!! Very friendly and helpful.
We had a King room facing the River. Very nice and comfortable. The bathroom area is a bit crowded, but no biggy. Nice separate sink area.

The hotel is very nicely located. It's a very short walk from the Gallery-Chinatown subway stop. We took a subway from the airport to here, and walked to the hotel from the subway. Not my favorite thing to do at -- PM with luggage, but it felt reasonably safe. We encountered one domestic dispute between a couple happening in the subway station that made us uncomfortable that evening, but nothing else the whole trip that made us ill at ease in the neighborhood. It feels very safe to walk between the subway and the hotel in the daytime. No problems at all, plenty of others doing the same thing. We took the subway every day to go see the sights. Probably about a mile's walk from the capitol. 
The hotel is very nice. Rooms were extremely clean, as was the whole hotel. Room was in very good repair. Beds are super comfortable, lots of pillows on each bed. Climate control worked perfectly. Staff were very pleasant and helpful. There's a business center where you can print for free, handy when checking in for a flight. Unlike many hotels in DC, wireless internet is free. There's a little shop with snacks, which was handy late at night. It rained throughout our stay, so in a couple cases we took cars instead of the subway. There's a staff person in the front lobby dedicated to helping with transportation issues. One car we preordered from them arrived -- minutes late. Plenty of taxis drive by in the morning if you need one last minute. They recommended a reservation on Sunday morning because so many folks were leaving at the same time. There's a small but very nice pool, hot tub, and exercise room (Well equipped with cardio, weights, stability balls). Didn't use it, but there are laundry facilities on site. In contrast to other reviews, we had NO issues with any street noise. We found the hotel to be very quiet.
Breakfast is one of the best I've found included at any hotel. Many types of rolls, muffins, doughnuts, bagels, breads, juices, milk, coffee, cereal, - types of eggs, sausage or ham, biscuits, gravy, yogurt, bananas, apples, oranges, and cut fruit.
Very, very nice hotel. Would stay here again in a heartbeat. For the price, and with this location, it really can't be beat.

Stayed here for a few nights while introducing out-of-town guests to Hollywood and Los Angeles. This was not a good deal for the price (we paid extra to have a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""suite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which is not a suite at all but a regular hotel room plus a small sofa bed).

When I inquired at the front desk, I was told the wireless service was only available in the tiny lobby next to the front desk. This hotel is in a good area if you want to walk to the sights on Hollywood Boulevard (it's about a half mile walk). But the sidewalks are not well-maintained, so be careful. There is a mini-market and Starbucks one building over from the hotel that is convenient.
During most of the day and evening, it is near impossible to make a left-hand turn out of the parking lot, so plan accordingly.

The Whole Foods store across the street was amazing - Old Chicago restaurant next door was good for a quick dinner.

The room was surprsingly small with a very small bathroom. Disappointing,

We highly recommend the scallops and the clam chowder (when in Rome). My husband called ahead to have a flower arraignment set up for me in our room, and both the flowers and the arraignment were classic and beautiful. We look forward to our next visit at the Mandarin Oriental.

The seating area for the breakfast was comfortable and spacious. The hotel room was cozy; the beds were comfortable. The rooms were nothing fancy, but they were very clean and comfortable.

Not going to happen with glass shower doors! They did have another mirror and small table right outside of the bathroom that we were able to use. Even though it was a negative, we loved that everything was so new and clean that we were happy to work around that. 
The breakfast and evening reception were great. Lots of beverages and food choices. The two dining rooms were really lovely! 
The staff was EXTREMELY helpful and went out of their way to accomodate us. We were traveling with - people, and on the day we were checking out, we wanted to check out a few more sites before heading home. They graciously agreed to store our bags (and A LOT of them with all - of us).

This would be a great hotel for families or a couple looking for a nice get-away. Can't say enough great things about this hotel.

We stayed on the Riverwalk side, and really appreciated the location being a little bit away from the hustle and bustle (and noise) of the main Riverwalk. We skipped the Hotel's restaurant (on the riverwalk level) until the last night, and man were we sorry we had waited until the last night. It was one of the best meals we have ever had! My husband got the filet mignon, and he STILL raves about that steak. He said it is worth the cost of the trip back just for the filet from the Drury's restaurant! The section of chinatown that this hotel is in remains quiet, but is within walking distance to great shops, subway and restaurants in both Chinatown and Little Italy. Frankly the sound seems to reverberate in the corridors and there is quite a bit of noise both from within the hotel and from the neighborhood in general. Beside the bedroom & bathroom being elegantly spacious, rooms were clean, reception staff services were excellent. I've stayed at the cute farmers Daughter hotel previously and the Park Plaza Lodge is definitely on my list to stay.

To be honest, the last hotel we chose in NYC was off of Times Square and we were SO disappointed. Unbelievable small, dirty, old...yuck. For the last couple of years, I have stayed here on several occasions with the most recent the Roger Waters (Pink Floyd) concert. I will definitely return to this hotel for future San Diego business trips!

A selection of newspapers in the lobby included the Chicago Tribune, the Wall Street Journal and the Financial Times. USA Today was at your door in the morning. The location of the Monaco is a plus, It's one block off Michigan and a short walk across the river to the Magnificent Mile. We will look for a Klimpton property on future trips and the Monaco when we make it back to Chicago

There are a number of restaurants that are fairly close, and a couple that you can walk to. The hotel offers a shuttle bus that will take you places too. This is located in a business park and not much else around.

Very comfortable beds, huge clean rooms, big tv. Shuttle service was awesome. Dropped us in heart of city right up till ten thirty. And picked us up til that time also

the grounds are beautiful and the room was ok. All of the dining facilities were average with the best food at Trellis's. 
My biggest frustration was losing my bill (in order to get reimbursed by my company). This older motel had a firm bed, plenty of hot water and (much to our surprise) an additional sleep sofa as well as a microwave and refridgerator in a non-kitchen unit. I rarely write reviews but was so pleased with this hotel that I feel compelled to. I picked this hotel based on a few factors: (-) reviews on Tripadvisor; (-) location; (-) pool; and (-) I found a rate on the hotel's website that included parking (normally $-- a night so this was a big bonus). I could not have been more pleased with this choice! Location was perfect: a block from Reading Terminal (indoor food market w- gourmet selections, great place to grab a bite to eat, where everyone can get what they want and you don't have to spend a fortune, try a cheese & choc chip cannoli from Termini Brothers Bakery -- yum!), across the street from City Hall and walking distance to Independence Park to the east and the science museums to the west. Pool was small (as we expected based on the reviews) but was clean and perfect for our - kids to have an afternoon swim. When booking, try to find the Philly Overnight package (- night min.) that includes parking. That was an even better deal than we thought as it included in and out privileges which many valet rates don't. Also, the day we checked out they told us we didn't have to get our car out until -pm! Since they'll hold your bags for you, you can really make use of your last day in Philadelphia. A couple of tips for families: drive to the zoo (we loved the zoo but regretted our public transportation adventure) and try Marathon Grill, a Philadelphia chain with a location - blocks from the hotel - trendy decor but suitable for kids with an upscale diner-like menu. Note that they are putting in a Starbucks and a new restaurant in the hotel which should be great additions once they open.

Close to airport, great shopping, and excellent restaurants.

Stayed recently at the Fairmont. The location is great with - cable stops right outside. The hotel has an old world charm. Maybe getting slightly old, and will need refurbishment soon. Would stay again because of the location.

Twelve Ursuline Academy Classmates got together to have lunch and celebrate the birthday of five ladies. The hotel staff was most attentive, greeted us at the table while having lunch and later found us a place to sit in the already well attended lobby. It was a day and night to remember. Will visit again on Thursdays to enjoy the lively ambiance of this hotel.

Location ideal for the convention centre just across the road. Nice fresh omlettes for breakfast and helpful staff. There's a decent sized pool and gym along with a computer room that's handy. The hotel is a bit oddly laid out with the reception accesible by lift but the rooms are a really good size.

I was not real impressed with the hotel, despite its pretty good reviews. I arrived to find that while the common areas were well appointed, my room was worn and small. The heater-ac was very loud, a large gap under the door, where the light shown through all night, and an extremely small bathroom with dirty grout, a couple pubic hairs or two, and cheap, crooked towel bars that looked like they had been knocked off the walls several times, probably considering the very limited space. I didn't feel the price and size of the room was a good value, considering how many choices there are in the Magnificent Mile area. The Horton Grand Hotel is certainly a unique hotel with its historic architecture and atypical interior design and appointments in the public areas. In addition, its location is by all means excellent given its proximity to the Gaslamp Quarter and access to public transit for excursions outside the immediate area. That said, there are plenty of hotels in the area that have equally desirable locations and the Horton really isn't the type of hotel that one might enjoy if there's an expectation of comforts such as room service, fitness center, business services, and a large room w- accommodating furniture where one might wish to lounge and work. Quite frankly, because there were no lounge chairs in the room it became quite tiresome sitting on the bed as a comfortable alternative to the straight back wooden chairs that were in the room. While the bed was comfortable it certainly didn’t rival the more luxurious bedding and “sleep systems” that are offered by many fine hotels. 
Upon entering the room where I stayed an old and musty smell was present and the smell persisted throughout my stay. However, I suspect that is to be expected from an old property and perhaps it even adds to the historic character of the hotel. The Horton advertises rooms appointed with antiques. However, I actually found the furniture in my room to be more reminiscent of some of the older hotels where I've stayed along Route --. In other words, less “antique” and more """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""outdated."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" 
 I found the front desk staff to be helpful when I inquired about basic information regarding transportation, restaurant recommendations, and entertainment venues. However, the staff didn't appear to have the type of knowledge or expertise to offer access to reservations-tickets that one usually finds available from a quality concierge. 
While I am certainly pleased to have experienced a stay at the historic Horton Grand Hotel, I wouldn't stay at this property again or recommend it to other travelers who are looking for more comfortable accommodations with amenities that make a long business trip bearable.

General Manager
Palmer House Hotel
Delivered via email (commentsph@hilton.com)
October --, ----
Dear Sir or Madam:
I stayed in room XXX at the hotel recently, and I was very disappointed with aspects of the room and of the service. As a Hilton customer for many years, and a former Diamond HHonors member, I’ve had the opportunity to stay in many Hilton properties. The problems I noted make me wonder if you ever visit or use the average rooms in your hotel (you should, if you don’t). I also wonder why these things are not reported to maintenance by the housekeeping staff. Is there no QA or QC function that randomly tests all aspects of a room (there should be, if there’s not)?
Closet
The closet door will not stay open, so while I was standing in the closet working with my clothes, it kept hitting me in my back.
The string on the closet light is way too long and right in your face and shoulders when trying to get your clothes. A hotel of this type should have a wall switch, at least, or more appropriately a switch built into the jamb so that the light comes on when the door is opened. At the very least, the light string should not be placed so as to hit people in the face when they try to use the closet.
Bathroom
Again, the door won’t stay in the closed position without being latched. The room is so small that the door can’t be left in the fully open position when showering. So, you have no choice but to latch it, which causes an excessive amount of moisture in the room, due to no active ventilation, as evidenced by peeling paint on the ceiling.
Due, I suppose to the passive vent being in the shower, the curtain wants to suck in to the shower, giving a person no room to shower. To avoid that, one must rest it on the tub lip, and then the floor floods.
The placement of the soap holders on the side wall of the shower is in the almost exact position someone has to stand in to use the shower, which makes the shower extremely narrow in that critical spot. The lack of thought that goes into things like this never ceases to amaze me. Put those things on the front or back wall (or just nearer the front or back of the sidewall), and the problem is solved. Given the curtain sucking in and the soap holder placement, it’s a very narrow shower, indeed!
The lighting globes were installed crookedly, and the GFI outlet was amazingly crooked. Don’t you or your staff have any pride in how your rooms look?
Service
The TV listing in your Guest Directory is inaccurate – the channels do not match up with the TV. Do you know how frustrating it is to try and watch TV after a long day of travel and work, and you have no idea what channel is what. It’s very frustrating to try to find the channels and to remember where they are. I pointed the problem out to the front desk clerk (Vera, I think, on -----), and she seemed surprised. It would not be a surprise if there was a QA function. Who is charged with keeping that book up to date? What else was wrong it in (e.g., safety information)? I asked the front desk for an updated listing that morning before I left for work, and I didn’t get it – nor did I get an explanation of why I didn’t get it – very sorry service. I assume my book was not the only one outdated, so all of your customers are suffering.
When I attempted to use the Zip-Out checkout on the phone, I only heard a few clicks and then another dial tone. There was nothing in the instructions on the phone or on the receipt to indicate that’s the way it worked. As it seemed to be malfunctioning, I waited in a long line at the front desk to checkout - again, a very frustrating encounter that could have been easily avoided by disclosing simple information.
Someone (everyone?) at the hotel needs to approach the hotel through the customer’s eyes. I don’t want to be frustrated while in my hotel. If I stay at the Palmer House again, how will you ensure these things don’t recur?
The receipt says to send feedback to commentsph@hilton.com, but if that is supposed to be a web link, it doesn’t work. I hope it works as an email address.
Sincerely,

This hotel is ok. The rooms are average and a little outdated looking. The bathrooms are tiny. The parking garage is kind of a pain. But on the plus side, the customer service is excellent and you can walk to the Gaslamp district in about -----min.
The deal breaker for me was the wifi. The hotel only has - floors...how could I only have - bar on wifi, which would constantly cut in and out? Unacceptable at a hotel positioned at business travelers. Time to invest in a -nd router.

I booked this hotel for one night and then read the reviews. So I was prepared for the worst. The worst didn't happen. But what I saw was a hotel with an ownership problem. Either the owners do not have the cash to update the hotel properly or they have resigned themselves to watching the property decline. And the guests are the ones who pay for this decision. I have to conclude that the employees pay for this situation as well.
Check-in was seamless. The person who checked me in was very nice and efficient. The other clerk was on the phone handling a dispute over a charge for a reservation that apparently had a date mix-up. There seemed to be an impass in that discussion, and I didn't hear any kind of resolution approaching. The parking lot was never close to full, so it didn't seem like the hotel would have lost any revenue had a guest not showed up. (I realize this is a common revenue protection scheme, though if the person is calling to get it resolved, I wonder why a hotel that doesn't actually lose revenue --- by denying another person a booking --- doesn't just give in and offer some concession like a free room night in exchange, hoping that the person comes for a later stay.)
I was told about the $-.-- amenities fee and was told what the amenities were. There is a corner in the lobby set aside as the business center, which I would have used to print some documents except it was always busy. I heard one person complain that the speed was very slow. Wireless in the room was not blazing, but was better than I expected and there's no obnoxious sign-in procedure like the HIltons and some other brands use.
There is also a hold on your credit card for potential damages. I have no idea how they handle this, but I'm watching my accounts closely. They must get a rough crowd, though I didn't see anything unseemly.
There was apparently only one luggage cart, and it wasn't up front. The desk clerk paged someone to bring it up front, but I didn't see it quickly (or ever, really) and decided to move my bags myself in two trips.
The guest rooom doors were secure and controlled by card. The room was clean and had no visible damage to the furnishings. I think I was in a renovated room. But read on.
The front desk helped me get on the wireless, which was easy.
The front desk called about a half hour after I arrived to make sure the room was okay. I hadn't really examined everything.
The TV remote had lots its battery cover, and the batteries would stay in. Some tape had been applied, but it was more of a hindrance than a help. Just replace it, why don'tcha? A sign of no budget.
Beds were adequate as were linens and towels. However, the pillows were very cheap and way, way overused --- completely broken into lumps of foam --- you know the feeling. A sign of no budget.
The bathroom was clean except the tub fixture was exposed to the pipe and was on crooked. It wouldn't divert the flow completely to the shower. No budget to replace it.
Soaps were those tiny soaps you can buy for - cents. No budget.
The pool looked large and inviting, and people were using it.
The air conditioner was missing its diverter vent (No budget), and so to have air conditioning, I had to put up with a cold breeze coming directly across the bed. I eventually turned it off and decided to put up with a warmer room.
Besides the A-C problem, I slept fairly well given the sorry pillows.
In the morning, the nice operator called a taxi immediately with zero hesitation.
So, in my experience, the hotel has an adequate, and sometimes excellent, staff. But they are working with no money. This pervades their policies and how they care for their rooms. I feel sorry for the staff having to put up with this lack of investment. But if the owners have no money, I understand that, too.
Just know going in that you are not staying at a national chain with amenities and normal upkeep, and you will be happy. It seems perfect for college students and others that want budget travel and can put up with some inconveniences and lack of repair.

I've seen people complain on here because of the price - you're smack in the center of a fairly large city - what do you expect?
Room was a standard Queen and had an amazing view - something different were - huge windows in the bathroom. At night it was even cooler. You're right next to city hall so you can walk everywhere and there's a dunkin doughnuts and starbucks across the street. 
The place is art deco (I guess) but we enjoyed it, the bed is at an angle within the room which was different. Kurig's instead of coffee pots so the coffee in the room was good. Lemonade and coffee and treats for dogs (it's pet friendly) in the lobby at most times too. There were ten weddings going on while we were there so there are a TON of people - but again - center of a city. Place seems to have a pretty hip bar downstairs too - it was always packed. REALLY good concierge also w- great walking maps. 
My big advice is don't park here - --bucks a day! If you turn right onto --th (heading away from City Hall) you'll see a huge green PARK sign on your right - -----hrs. Completely worth it to roll my bad across the street.

The people at the desk were very nice, helpful, and professional, but the room had a noisy AC, sheets looked like they hadn't been washed from last guest, but fortunately we only had to stay there ond night. Thanks heavens no bedbugs!

The Brookshire was one of those rare gems you find when you least expect it. We had a wonderful time with our - year old son. Our room was clean, bright and offered an incredible view of the inner harbor. The breakfast each morning delicious and well prepared. The evening hors d' oeuvres were exceptional and a great way to start the evening (the homemade Old Bay potato chips were incredible). We had a wonderful time at the Crabby Hour at the Pier - hotel. That was another incredible thing about the hotel; all of the things that you could do at the sister hotels. We have never had such an experience. The staff was excellent with our son and a delight to be with. I wish that we could remember names, but my sone expecially liked the young woman working the front desk on the day we arrived (I believe that her name was Marisol??) and the gentleman who drove the shuttle between the hotels (again, we can't remember his name but we think it was George). Everyone was professional and made us feel more than welcome. We would highly recommend this hotel to anyone travelling to Baltimore; expecially those with a family who do not want to bother with having to drive around town and find parking all the time. An excellent stay.

I have only one horrible memory of our stay here, an employee by the name of Nabila. She apparently claims to be a manager but works in the flower shop in the lobby. Our soccer team was at the hotel for a prestigious tournament and had over -- rooms in the hotel for our group. Another mom and I were in the lobby waiting for our team to return from a game and we had two coolers with us to pass out Gatorade and water to our team. Nabila saw us there and told us we can't stand in the lobby as there were two weddings coming. I explained what we were doing and she said we cannot be there, we had to move. I again explained that we were paying guests at the hotel and had every right to stand in the lobby waiting for our team and she then proceeded to accuse us of selling our water and Gatorade. At this point we moved closer to the elevator and a father went to speak to the front desk manager. Nabila followed him there and tried to argue with this dad and even tried to call security. The front desk manager even told her to be quiet so he could address our concerns. Not once did she apologize for her rude behavior and accusations. This type of service is unacceptable at a hotel of this price and supposed four-star rating.

We booked this hotel via an auction site and while it was represented as a -.- star (out of possible - stars for Seattle), I feel that is being overly generous. While the place is very clean and the front desk staff are lovely and helpful, it really is geared to the very budget-concious traveller and I would barely give it - stars. 
The location is the most remote of all downtown hotels on the city map (it's on the other side of the highway where most other hotels are situated between I-- and the waterfront) and there was really nothing of interest to us in the vicinity of the hotel since we don't hang out at hospitals. This really brings down the value of the hotel, to my mind.
The included breakfast was headache-inducing as there are not nearly enough staff to service the area. We, and many other people, ended up spending the majority of our time in the restaurant standing around waiting for things like cutlery, coffee, etc.
The rooms are clean and our room was relatively quiet and the huge flatscreen tvs are great. We also appreciated the shuttle service to the actual downtown area. 
We would not stay here again (or ever use an auction site to book a room again to avoid this situation) but I would definitely recommend this to budget concious travellers.

We were looking specifically for a place near Times Square so we could just walk anywhwere we wanted to. Well, this place is certainly that! Great rooms, very clean and a wonderful staff.
We had an eight floor room, so we did get a little more noise than what rooms ten or higher may experience. We were also on the Port Authority side. But even then...considering you're right in the heart of Manhattan Island, two blocks off Times Square, we didn't have many noise issues to deal with at all. This hotel is a great starting off point for pretty much anything with the subway being nearby.
The staff is very helpful, but I would say don't bother leaving a message for the concierge. I did twice prior to our arrival (email and phone) and never heard back. But with how busy they are...I can see why! The lobby is a bit small so it can get crowded, but they're very efficient with moving people through check in.
Also...the most common complaint was the elevators and the wait for them. I do architecture for a living and can tell you they likely couldn't have done anything better with them. They have a very large amount of people in a very small footprint. Three elevators is likely all they could do. Just be patient and allow and extra five minutes.

My husband and I stayed at the Phoenix Park Hotel for - nights over the ---- Thanksgiving holiday. We got a TERRIFIC rate on our room, which we booked directly with the hotel using their reservation system.
At check in, we were offered a Queen bed room with a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""good view,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" or a King bed room, apparently without much, or any, view. We decided on the Queen room and were told that if we weren't satified with it, that we could switch. All of the staff we had contact with were pleasant and accomodating.
Our room, #---, was a bit on the small size, but certainly adequate for two people. The room was nicely furnished in semi-antique, period style pieces in keeping with the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Irish"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" theme of the hotel. There was a small desk with a straight-back upholstered chair, and an additional work space in front of a rather large vanity-chest of drawers combo. The bed was unbelievably comfortable! We LOVED the fact that we could partially open the two windows in the room for cool, fresh air while we were sleeping.
The bathroom, while small, was adequate. It had a tub-shower combination with a curved rod for ease of showering without the curtain getting in the way. The towels were luxurious and made especially for the hotel as their logo and name were woven in. The bathroom even had a scale. Two very nice robes were provided for our use. 
The room had a fairly roomy closet with a safe. Other features of the room included a ironing board, a flat screen cable TV, a mini-fridge, and coffee-tea making accessories.
Our room faced east with a view of Union Station, which is located only a block away. Union Station offers all sorts of dining possibilities at fairly reasonable prices, as well as various shops and access to the Washington DC Metro system, as well as Amtrak, and local train lines. You can also board several of the hop-on, hop off bus-trolley tours in front of Union Station.
The Phoenix Park Hotel has a on-site Irish pub and restaurant, The Dubliner, which serves a large variety of tasty meals, including breakfast, at fairly reasonable prices. We ate there and also enjoyed drinks as well on several occasions. The Dubliner advertises that they have live music - nights a week, but we weren't in the establishment when the entertainment was going on.
In addition to the eateries in Union Station and The Dubliner, there are a number of other places to dine within a couple of blocks of the hotel, including yet another Irish pub, which is located right next to The Dubliner. There is a fairly large liquor store two blocks away. The Capitol is only about a ----- block walk.
We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Phoenix Park Hotel, and will certainly stay here again when we visit Washington DC!

This is a place with original bath's, taps, tiles, plate glass mirrors that show thier age, chest of draws with marble tops that matches the bedside tables, years of paint work on the door frames, odd shaped rooms . I feel privileged to stay in what should be considered to be a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""must see"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on any tour of New York. I love it and will be back.
I have stayed with Doubletree, Detroit-Dearborn several times for meeings, and would recommend it to anyone.

I've looked at other reviews of this hotel and agree that it is getting tired - but I had a perfectly adequate stay.
I booked an Executive Room, and the room I was given didn't match up to an Executive at UK Holiday Inns - it was simply a massive room. With a small bathroom. The plus:

To improve:

This hotel was in a terrific location. The staff was pleasant and the rooms were nicely appointed. The elevator system was a bit slow the entire time we were there, but it was absolutely horrendous on the weekends. We were stuck on the --th floor on Saturday evening for -- minutes before we could get an elevator. After reading the reviews that stretch back for a few years, I somehow doubt that was the truth. What is the point of staying in a great location when you can't get off your floor. Also, there were no soda machines on the guest floors, which meant that you had to make a potential hour long round trip just to get to the -th floor to get a soda. The hotel should either bite the bullet and book fewer rooms or fix the elevator system. It's greedy to take in the profits from unsuspecting travellers when they know that the system cannot possible support the number of gueasts staying in the hotel.

Overall, a very pleasant weekend stay.
Room: Very clean & well maintained, comfortable beds, excellent linens, felt spacious. Sound insulation was great- didn't hear a peep from people above or below us, or in the hallways.
Lobby & common areas: Well kept and attractive. Lobby wi-fi was free, but it was tricky finding a spot with a good signal. 
Service: Doormen were always friendly and polite. Front desk service was mixed- the gentleman who checked us in (Jay) was incredibly friendly and helpful, chatting and joking with us, giving a good overview of the hotel, and recommending places to eat at the late hour we checked in. Later in the stay we found that our room phone wouldn't make outgoing calls (even after dialing - as instructed, there was no dial tone, just a busy signal)- when I called down to get this fixed, first I was accused of not leaving a credit card# for incidentals (which I had), then was told I wasn't dialing - (which I was). I had to call down - times before he finally reset the system and it worked. Not a huge deal, but the man I was dealing with was condescending and rude. It was totally unnecessary.
Location: Very close (-- min walk) to the Capitol building and east side of the Mall. Because we were only there for - days and only seeing places on the Mall, the location was good. We walked one day and took the Metro from Union Station the next. Union Station was - blocks away, and a great place to get inexpensive meals. There were very few other amenities (restaurants, groceries, drugstores, etc) in the area, though, especially on the weekend (there were a few cafes-delis that were weekday only).
I got an great price for this weekend stay and thought it was excellent value. If I was staying for longer than a few days, though, I would probably pay the extra money for a Dupont Circle or Georgetown location. Once our day at the Mall was done, there was little reason to stroll around the hotel's neighbourhood.

I have stayed at the Triton at least - or - times and I am never disappointed. The staff provides wonderful service and the coffee is ready early. Great location for shopping and restaurants within a quick walk. The rooms are not huge, but clean and comfortable.

this hotel was magnificent, right from the beginning the valet taking our car was wonderful, pointed us in the right direction to our dinner reservations later that evening as well as how to walk to the Art Institute. check in was smooth, room was available for early check in at --am with no problem. Location cannot be beat, only a mile to museums, restuarants and night life all around, only a $- cab ride to theaters (who can walk in heels?), staff very helpful. I recently stayed here for a business trip and was completely impressed. Recently renovated, clean, very friendly and helpful staff. Looking forward to my stay in July.

Just back from first trip to DC. Stayed at the Carlyle Suites Hotel. Great choice. The staff was extremely friendly, helpful and very professional. The rooms were beautiful, spacious, comfortable and immaculate. Charming restaurants in the hotel where we had several meals that were all excellant.
