Our room, and every public room, is full of history and its artifacts. The sitting areas, with - fireplaces, are furnished with authentic love seats, chairs, and tables. The lamps, although electric, look like they could have been made in the early ----s. The staff was gracious and concerned about the quality of our stay. The free breakfast was tasty and generous and the coffee that is available -- hours is among the best I've ever tasted. Every day at - pm, free sherry and cookies are served. The best thing about our stay is the overall look and feel of a luxurious bygone era. The worst thing was a less than luxurious bed, but given that, it was still very comfortable.

we were there for - days on vacation and had a great time.the property is fairly close to all the attractions but when we chose to take public transportation we had plenty of choice nearby.I would recommend it for somebody that doesn't want to spend --- -night for a hotel room where they will not spend a lot of time.it is clean, modern and the staff very helpful.we asked for more towels and got them right away.we would definitely stay there again.

great service it just that i came back from a party at -:--am and there wasnt no water at my room so i couldnt take a shower then the next day i wanted to use the pool and they told there were going to call me so that i could use it and that for me is really dumb it supposed to be public open who knows!! so i couldnt use it

This property is your cookie cutter springhill suites. Feels like it was recently renovated, all the usual amenities are present - the lobby has a nice little bar and seating area (first time I'd seen a bar that was staffed with bartender at a springhill suites). 
Note if you drive: google maps takes you some weird backwards way down an alley to find the entrance. Ask to hotel for better directions. 
 Valet and self parking have exact same price, by the way. Only one valet so you may have to wait awhile to find him. 
Our room was in the connected historical building which made it a little inconvenient to walk to-from the front entrance (up an elevator, down a hall to a hidden elevator, up again and down more halls to my room). Given that our building was --- years old I was hoping for some charm but you really just get basic normal modern insides, except for some squeaky hallway floors. Room itself was fine - typical. Not much to complain about except the sink area for getting ready (two people can't fit at same time) and the complete lack of a full length mirror. 
Also our room was right outside the housekeeping closet and you could easily hear their hallway conversations. further, the doors slam pretty loudly so get a room away from the stairs, which lots of people took to avoid the slow elevators - resulting in lots of slamming doors from the stairwell. 
One warning: we had gone to breakfast and returned to our room, forgetting to latch the door from the inside. Sure enough, in walks a housekeeper without so much as a knock, even though the do not disturb sign was on the door. She was all the way through the living room before she realized we were inside, or even looked for that matter, which implied (to me anyway) that this is a regular habit. 
Front desk staff were friendly but busy many times - had to wait to speak to them every time we needed anything (they were always on the phone or dealing with another guest in front of us). 
Overall decent value - I may go back, due to convenient location on Main St. Trolley line and walking distance to Beale St. but there are about - other similar quality properties right next door that may be less likely to invade your room.

We too stayed at the hotel for Easter of ----. The rate was reasonable through Expedia. However, don't expect too much luxury. Everything is cut back to the bare minimum. Can't complain but don't go in with hopes of accommodations other than the bare necessities. Note: Gregory was very hospitable and a real asset to the team!

I have read many reviews about this hotel. Many bad ones and I for one would have to say that for it being N.Y.C. I thought the hotel was great. Its in the heart of the theatre district. Across the street from *CHICAGO* and - block from all of times square. Its basically on broadway. We walked all of times square and thru alot of great resturants and stores. Its also - block away from a subway station that gets the - train for you guys who want to go down to the financial district or to catch the south ferry its very convinient. The rockerfeller center and radio city music hall are down the street if you like to walk. Central park is up a few blocks but besides that i dont know what else to say. The staff were super polite and helped us even getting a car(lincon towncar) to the airport for cheeper than what a cab drover quoted us. Rooms were fairly small but all we did was go there to sleep and shower so unless you are planning to stay in your room for long periods of time i would give it an a+++.
Beautiful hotel, rooms were nice bed was comfortable, close to everything we needed.

I stayed at the MotorCity for a family reunion dinner and program. Pluses include : the location (close to downtown) the free Valet , the well appointed and large rooms, comfortable beds, Celebrity watching (Tiger players , etc ) and some of the staff. Negatives include : the location (run down neighbor ) , refrigerators that ONLY accomodate overpriced hotel liquour and snacks that you get CHARGED for if you disturb the sensors beneath the bottles (seriously there is not enough spare room in the fridge for a bottled water!), inconsistent room and bell person assistance. and maid service that doesnt prepare rooms till -p or later for check in.

Our stay was excellent! Ramon the reservations manager was incredibly helpful and knowledgeable! He made Mary Kay Director's experience one to remember! We will be back in ---- and are looking forward to another great stay!

staff excellent and very helpful, notably front desk Tennille, concierge David and manager Frances. Gracious and interested in our having the best experience, even at the busiest times. If possible, we always stay at Affinias on our frequent trips to NYC. location good for the city. Room was spacious for NYC and kitchenette and refrigerator were handy.

I stayed at the Carlyle for a few days after I had surgery at one of NYC's top hospitals. The hotel staff could not have been nicer and more accommodating of my needs for a soft diet and refrigerator in the room to house my jello supply. The restful and no-stress atmosphere contributed greatly to the beginning of my recovery. While I enjoy staying at the Carlyle when I am able to take advantage of all of the amenities of the hotel and the neighborhood, I am particularly grateful that the hotel goes out of its way to help out-of-town patients take advantage of the world class medical care available in New York.

So I spent the last few days traveling and sleeping on my friend's air mattress. It was horrible and my back was sore and I decided that today my boyfriend and I should splurge and get a really nice room. The Arizona Biltmore looks really nice in the pictures on their website, but it was about the worst disaster I've ever had in any hotel.

so my verdict on the whole hotel: the grounds are very beautiful. 
everything else is lame. stay somewhere else.

I stayed here for three nights in April ----. Booked a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""king suite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which was supposed to have two rooms plus bath. Instead, had one room that was approximately - feet wider and - feet longer than a king-sized bed. The dresser drawers could not be opened fully as they hit the bed. Very noisy, facing Geary Street. No a-c. When we checked in, hotel said the room I had requested (been promised??) was already in use. Nice bathroom with jacuzzi tub, though very noisy fan made it unpleasant. No closet, just a place to hang clothes. Not perfectly clean but not terrible. We visited friends who were staying at the Adagio which was much nicer. There are a couple of other hotels along Geary that also looked worth checking out. Try the Savoy, it looked fun. The fish murals are pretty funky. The location of this hotel was great, the little cafe off the lobby was nice, the staff was pleasant though unwilling to move me. Reminded me a bit of European hostels.

Hotel Kabuki is a wonderful hotel in the heart of Japantown San Francisco. The ambiance is mixture of feudal Japan and modern day Kyoto. The rooms were immaculate and the view breath taking. The housekeeper and overall staff extremely approachable. The restaurant has a nice atmosphere and the food will make a glutton out of any anorexic. The bartender seem like he came right out cheers. I will always go back to hotel Kabuki whenever staying San Francisco.

From the time we rolled in on Wednesday afternoon until the time we left on Sunday morning the stay was awsome. The room was spendid, quiet, roomy and the bed was very comfortable. Good coffee in the room and great room service the one time we had it. The entire staff went out of their way, in our opinion, to provide anything we needed (directions, recommendations, etc.). This is the best kind of place for a SF getaway weekend. Be nice and leave a gratuity for the cleaning staff...they earn it every day.

Wife and I took our daughter and two of her friends to NYC for daughter's --th birthday on March ----- . As we only live --- miles or so from NYC I decided to drive into the city as I was able to get on somewhat cheap parking. Previously we haven't taken Beiber Bus to City or drive to Seacacus Junction station and take the short train ride to Penn Station. We left early Saturday morning and ended up going thru Holland Tunnel instead of LIncoln Tunnel. However, the easy drive up Eight Ave where the girls a chance to see the City.
 As we go to NYC twice a year or so, we are familiar with hotels. This time with - people and wife insistent that we all stay in the same room (not adjoining rooms) limited our choices. We ended up at Doubletree Times Square where we stayed before. The two full bed separate suite as just what we needed. They hadn't had rooms available for the two months leading up to the trip, but rooms opened the week before the trip. It wasn't cheap, but it was a - person room in Times Square. I like this hotel because the subway is literally next door.
After selfparking car at garage suggested by hotel we dropped bags at hotel and checked-in. As it was still before noon, room was ready, but they took cell number and stayed they would call when room was ready. When to Rock Center, NBC store (girls bored there), St. Pat's and shopping on Fifth Avenue which was the girls' objective. However, instead of going to the unique stores they wanted to go to the same stores we have at malls at home. I stood outside and people watched while they shopped. Ended up at FAO Schwarz and took subway back to Times Square. We had lunch at John's Pizza on --th St which was good as usual. Our room was ready and we walked back to hotel. I napped while women shopped in Times Square area. 
We just grabbed a snack from a food cart and went to see Spiderman. Show was good. Music wasn't memorable, but the special flying effects were unlike anything else I've ever seen. Our seats in the fifth row of the balcony weren't the best as we couldn't see some the flying action and it was difficult to see when the action was at the front of the stage. 
After the show I wanted to go to the Shake Shack at --th and -th, but the line was half a block long. We ended up at the Brooklyn Diner. We had burgers, chicken and waffles, and mac and cheese which was all fine and typically overprice.
I had an uncomfortable night on the sleeper sofa from a combination of the ever present bar made the bed less than ideal and the girls were talking well into the night. Next morning we took subway to Chinatown and enjoyed dim sum at Oriental Gardens. Food was very good, some on carts, and some you had to order and I never figured out which. After Chinatown shopping and walking up Broadway into the Village and shopping there, we took subway to Union Square. On a recommendation we went to Max Brenner for dessert. She didn't have reservations, but the took cell number and called us when our table was ready. This allowed girls to go shoe shopping and I went to The Strand bookstore which is an outstanding store. The girls liked their smores with the little fire pot at table and their chocolate fondue and waffles. Wife's dark hot chocolate was great and my chocolate hazelnut granita-milkshake was good, but small. Restaurant was very loud, hot and the menu was confusing and was not overall impressed.
Took subway back to Hotel and got bags and walked half block to garage to get car. Didn't get parking ticket stamped at hotel which was difference between $-- and $-- so wife went back and got ticket stamped. On the way home we stopped at Carlos Bakery in Hoboken as daughter is a big fan of CakeBoss. We hadn't told her and she was surprised. 
All in all it was a good trip as the girls enjoyed themselves and daughter had a birthday to remember.

We spent three nights at this hotel in September --. We felt that this hotel was value for money. It was well located to most of the main tourist attractions, and I would recommend walking around San Francisco as much as possible as opposed to taking buses, you get a great feel for the place. We walked down Columbus Street, with great Italian restaurants, to Union Square and back most days and it was great exercise!
The rooms were spacious, although beds a little smaller than I have had in other hotels. The bathroom was averaged sized and well equipped. There was an ice machine on each floor, and speedy lifts. Our view was mainly of buildings, but we had not paid for a bay view so we didn't mind.
Only real gripe was that a couple of the assistants on the front desk were not friendly, and one was extremely patronising, which I did not appreciate. However, we didn't let this spoil our stay in San Francisco. We definitely want to return, you could spend three weeks in this place. My favourite place on the west coast hands down. I would reccomend this place due to comfort, location and value for money.

The location is easy to get to and within walking distance of many restaurants as well as a grocery store. Clean rooms with nice balcony views as well as good lounging areas- pool.
Tula's restaurant is affordable and has some of the best, freshest food I've eaten at a hotel while traveling. Most items $-- or less on dinner menu!
They also have a pretty nice fitness center.

The hotel is new and the rooms are really large. Some reviewers had suggested that the rooms are small, and this is really off the mark. 
Furthermore, white furniture and walls give the sense of even more space. The bathrooms are really wonderful - excellent water pressure, incredibly nice sink and plenty of towels, as well as plush robes. 
Hotel has a complimentary gym, which is not large, but includes around - cardio machines (- ellipticals, treadmills, bikes), a range of freewieghts and matts. Also, has an adjoining pool. The restaurant Rice is excellent. It is not overpriced, especially in comparison to the downtown's other venues. The service strives to provide one with a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""W experience"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", although might still benefit from some polishing. On offer there is also a CD and DVD library. No complimentary web access however. You will be asked to pay extra should you wish to check your email on a computer located in a lounge. By and large, a really nice hotel.

We stayed here for our honeymoon and I asked for reservations for --------------- as part of the Memphis Music Experience package;I was told we did not have to be out of our hotel room until --:--am -------...WRONG! With - kids in tow, we stayed for our FIRST visit to DC. I was a little concerned about some of the reviews i had read, but this was the PERFECT PROPERTY for our trip...close to a metro, great breakfast, good size room, evening reception...what more could you want!
I would definitely recommend for families!!

We bought the Groupon for the Clarendon and just got back from a trip to AZ. This hotel just had a weird vibe to it. I'm really not sure what they're trying to do (maybe they're not sure either), but it seems like they don't have a direction. 
Some good things... the pool area is fantastic, the front desk staff is very helpful, the hotel offers free snacks at night (candy bars, chips, granola bars, whatever you want), and the rooms are very spacious. 
Some bad things... the location isn't the greatest. Definitely not downtown Phoenix. The hotel is a -- minute walk plus -- minute light rail ride to the downtown area. Also, the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""fitness center"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is a complete joke. The treadmill literally stopped working while my girlfriend was running on it. They have some dumbbells but no bench or anything to sit on. Also, the insulation is very poor. And the artwork on the hallway walls is all about murders and killings... very, very strange.

I recently stayed in the Manhattan Club with my family, which included my - year old, over Thanksgiving for the Macy's Parade. Every aspect of our reservation and stay was incredibly easy. The Manhattan Club staff was so helpful when we booked our room last spring, we knew we needed to book early because of the parade, and they even gave us a room overlooking the parade route - so we didn't even have to leave our room to watch the parade! Our room was huge (a one bedroom suite with - bathrooms and a living room!), and completely affordable. The entire suite was very clean and the bathrooms were spotless. The beds were comfortable and all the linens were top-notch. My family and I cannot wait to return to New York City again and stay in this fabulous hotel...especially since we were able to walk everywhere!
Foreign desk clerk acted indifferent. The place smelled. Broken windows. Seedy part of town.

My husband and I stayed at this hotel for - days (weekend getaway). Staff was great. Location of the hotel is good. The rooms don’t look like “Marriott” rooms. I feel like I shouldn’t have paid Marriott price for this hotel. This hotel doesn’t deserve Marriott’s name on it. No microwaves or refrigerator in the rooms; let me add that the entire hotel doesn’t have microwaves for the guests even in the lobby. Beds are comfortable. The AC makes a loud noise when it’s turned on and running. Also, for the price I paid, I should have got at least a flat-screen TV, but I got an ancient small box TV. Another thing is that you have to pay for wi-fi when many surrounding hotels have it for free. Please look around the area before booking this hotel; there are many hotels for similar price with better quality. DO NOT be fooled by Marriott's name!!!

I stayed at the westin riverwalk a month ago and thought the overall service was great I would especially like to commend the vallet service. Someone was always there to get the door give me directions and put bags in my car when need be. bryant and rene were very helpful in making sure all my needs were taken care of. also carlos helped me have my car brought to me without having to wait. also beau and jose and the other doormen were very friendly and made sure I was taken care of

My family and I recently took a trip to San Antonio. As a platinum elite member, I have stayed at many Marriott's throughout California and Texas. I can't say that I've ever been more impressed with the level of service that I received from this hotel staff. From the reservationist to the morning greetings from the hotel General Manager (Ron Schoonover), assistant General Manager (Dedrick Perkins) and the Director of Sales (Joe Gamez). There aren't many places in which employees at this level are available to the direct customer. I felt very good when approached by ALL staff and continously asked if my stay was ok and if there was anything they could do to make it more enjoyable. If there was an issue, it was quickly resolved and followed up on by the hotel staff. It was very clear to me and my family we had chosen the right hotel as it felt we were with family that cared. These employees clearly love their job and know how to do it well. I would like to thank Joe, Dedrick, J.R., Ron and his entire staff for making this one of the best trips we've had in quite some time. It's not only the great amenities and great property that make a stay enjoyable; in my opinion, it's about the WORLD CLASS SERVICE from the staff that makes a difference. THANK YOU!!!

Location was perfect, close to pike market and other shopping. Parking was -- a day with in out privileges and was very handy. Our - yr old was playing on the floor in our room and picked up what turned out to be a piece of dry dog poop. This was absolutely disgusting and management didn't really seem to care and only offered to have someone come up and clean it up. We will not be returning to this hotel.

Well first off didnt get the Crylser Building view requested at time of booking, not a problem, limited rooms have it.
Room we did get was very spacious and clean. Bathroom was a bit small relative to the size of the room but was adequate and clean without being amazing. We didnt use the kitchen as there is so many places to eat in NYC.
Hotel is in great location, - min walk to subway and -- min walk to Macys and on to the other shops!
This was my -nd time in NYC and will be definitely returing to Dumont as it was a great hotel. Our first trip we stayed at the Sofitel which is a more impressive hotel lobby wise etc but there wasnt a major difference when it came to the rooms and you do pay alot more for the Sofitel!
Would recommend.

Nice hotel within walking distance of the National Mall, Capitol and other attractions. Food was great, room was nice (although would have preferred a better view) and staff were helpful and friendly. Didn't use pool area, but it looked clean and lively. Rate was quite expensive, althoug we did book late and parking was very expensive.
last night in Colorado, booked on marriott website. Excellent suite, great location and on site secure parking. Very helpful staff and brilliant free breakfast. Only needs a pool to be perfect...

I stayed at OnTheAve for a week just now, and before this time, for two weeks in '-- and two weeks in '--. I stayed again this time as the location and value for money are perfect. I had a bad start this time though.
The second floor stunk of smoke like a cheap freeway motel. The room didnt smell, but the common areas stunk and I wasnt going to stay there. I changed to another room, but on the second night had to move again as the room wasnt as of the higher standard type I paid for. The next room had a TV that wasnt working. To their credit, they had arranged to replace it as soon as I moved into the room, but they didnt have the equipment to mount it on the wall, so it was to be on the desk. I needed to use the desk. My fourth room was a major upgrade to say sorry, with a box of truffles, and an apologetic message (and it seems free internet for half the nights). The room was LOVELY. The service was great. I have stayed at quite a few Hampton Inns before, and this hotel was no different in terms of the comfort that I have come to expect from the chain.
One of my concerns was that the hotel was located across the road from a fire station; however, this turned out to be no problem at all.
The location was great, and considering that the hotel was just a couple of blocks from the river, the price was competitive too.
The wireless Internet connection was surprisingly fast.

This is the second time we stayed at this property, the second time was not as good as the first, of course the location did not change, and that is what makes this hotel , you can walk the waterfront, grab a ferry, and take the elevator to the market and downtown. The hotel itself was very busy the weekend we stayed there, so I can excuse some of the problems, I was very disappointed with the first room they tried to give us, it faced a wall. The second room was much nicer, and had a water view and a great view of Mount Ranier. I was also surprised that the front desk staff gave us no information about the club level,if I did not ask we would probably not remembered that they had one.

This hotel is a wonderful gem. I really don't want to write a good review as I want to keep this place to myself. The rooms are a wonderful size, the bathroom is great and the bed absolutely perfect. This was the best nights sleep that my partner and I have had in years. We really did not want to check out. The location to Pike place market is ideal, literally step out of your hotel and there it is.

My boyfriend and I recently stayed for - nights here. While we had read the many reviews from TripAdvisor that admonished the hotel for its lacking service we entered our stay with an open mind. Sadly, the reviews we had read beforehand proved to be correct.
The hotel is in a wonderful location: two blocks from the White House. The lobby is attractive and the hotel's bar and restaurant more modern but equally appealing (we did not dine at the restaurant). Nightly at -pm there is a Champagne Saber ceremony which is neat to watch and guests get a free glass of champagne. 
We stayed in a metropolitan suite which was beautiful. Our bathroom had a large shower, two separate sinks, and nice amenities. Our room was very large, had a very comfortable bed, large flat-screen tv with DVD player, and lounge area. The one drawback was the view which was of a very poorly maintained alley.
The service: Check-in was a nightmare. The front desk woman was incredibly rude and offered no sympathy for the room not being ready at -pm. While waiting until -pm in the lobby, I witnessed a dozen or so other people also experiencing frustration for having to wait. A simple smile, apology and offer of complimentary beverage could have gone a long way. 
The terrible service did not end there. There is no accessible ice machine so requesting a bowl of ice from the staff is cumbersome. The service does not smile, as if your request had somehow put them out of their way. I will just note that all of our experiences with the hotel staff were less than courteous. However, one event was remarkably surprisingly. Before retiring for the evening, my boyfriend called the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""butler service"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for a bucket of ice. Twenty minutes later, a staff woman came to the room saying that she had just been to our room and had given us a bucket of ice. My boyfriend, still at the door, replied that she must be mistaken and that we would still like a bucket of ice (which she did not have). The woman charged into the room and turned to me (I was in a robe on the bed) and said, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I just gave you a bucket of ice"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I told her she was mistaken and my boyfriend eventually got her to retrieve a bucket of ice but I thought it astonishing that a staff member at a St. Regis hotel would take it upon herself to enter a room, uninvited, to reproach a hotel guest. Amazing...
Other than our encounters with the hotel staff, our stay was pleasant. I would only recommend this hotel to people who desire optimal location, great amenities, but expect to deal little with the hotel staff.

Stayed for a recent convention and was a bit let down. First and foremost, what you pay for in this place is location, location, location. You are within walking distance of just about everything one would want to do in Chicago. 
But....the Hyatt food was lousy and overpriced in both food locations I used. Construction was intrusive, and the carpet in my hallway was threadbare at best. The in room coffee is simply something one spits out of their mouth upon first taste and everything about the hotel itself just seems a bit worn out. The bed was comfortable, but very near being not so. The fact that a place this expensive is without a pool or spa is laughable.
You can do better for this type of money in Chicago, but you may have to take a cab or two due to location challenges.

This hotel is a hidden gem near Byrant Park. I've stayed in various hotels in NYC including some high end boutiques- you just can't beat this one for the value and service. I booked this hotel completely relying on other reviews on trip advisor. It seemed that for the low NYC price it would not be so nice. It met all my expectations. Large rooms, breakfast included, bar, helpful staff and perfect location close to everything-uptown and downtown. I highly reccommend this property.

The W hotel was great. Laurelin provided - star service booking us dinner reservations, club reservations and also getting us Cub tickets. She made our trip to Chicago seemless and lots of fun. I will absolutely be back!

Definitely NOT your usual downtown hotel, the Curtis has a very cool retro vibe. All service was EXCELLENT during my recent stay. Each floor has a pop culture theme--I stayed on the Sci Fi Floor which had some Sci Fi items (e.g., Mulder's """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I want to believe"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" poster from The X-Files) in the common area; the rooms are not """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""themed."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" My room was nice (comfortable mattress, comforter with duvet, MANY pillows) and bathroom (roomy shower stall only) very nice. The restaurant and cocktail lounge-sidewalk bar were also great. And Starbucks is right around the corner. Very convenient to theatre district, shopping, and business headquarters. I'd go back in a heartbeat!

Very clean, they even clean the duvet covers, which is important to me. The room was fairly spacious for a NYC room. Great breakfast in the morning of anything you could possibly want. Coffee and tea all day long. In a fantastic location to shop, see sights and eat yummy foods.

They charged --- euros Night for a room without a WINDOW. and with a huge noise of the AC !!
They changed me the room to another one and the sound of the AC of the building next to it was impossible to sleep.
There was very POOR of light in the room.
The man in the afternoon in the reception was always smiling but when you asked something he said I will bring it to your room and the plug never came.
If they charged me --euros would be acceptable, otherwise NOT.
A hotel NOT TO GO BACK EVER AGAIN !!

Because my husband has Gold Passport, we often use Hyatt, and the one in Embarcadero just because it's next to the Ferry Building, but if you must choose Hyatt, the other Hyatt in downtown SF is far superior in every way. Hyatt at Embarcadero is NOT for you, if you value any kind of service. 
My husband usually books our room on Hyatt.com. When he arrives at the check in counter, he hates to be served by Chinese staff, because my husband is of Chinese heritage and his general experience at this Hyatt is that he is treated poorly by fellow Chinese -- like in HK. 
For this weekend trip, because my husband has been very busy, I booked our trip. I purchased flight and hotel together through AA. However, had I purchased them separately, the cost was merely few dollars more at the Hyatt AAA member price. When we checked in, the Asian female staff said that this stay does not count because it was discounted and not through Hyatt.com. WHY ARE THE CUSTOMERS NEVER INFORMED ABOUT THEIR OPTIONS BEFORE WE PURCHASE? I would have had to inconvenience my husband during his busy schedule, but he would have booked through Hyatt.com. Or, in the future, I shall choose to try another non-Hyatt hotel if I can get a competitive vacation package. We have absolutely no reason to stay at Hyatt if there is no Gold Passport advantage; in fact, we have not received any offer for a while that would encourage us to keep patronizing Hyatt! 
And the check in staff always try to charge us extra for any water view. This time, she said that for $-- extra (by the way, the price is different every time, and she did not inform us about the tax and assessment that are charged on top of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""upgrade""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""), she can put us in a room with great bay view in a much higher floor. During our last visit, my husband got into a big argument match about this """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""upgrade,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and we were too exhausted to bother this time, so we agreed to the upgrade. 
When we entered room ----, the water was only visible behind the Ferry Building if I stood by the left end of the window and looked out at an angle. The overall view from the room were high rises. We opened the window to look out at the water for which we paid extra, but because of the nasty smell of cigarettes from adjacent rooms, we had to close the window. 
The concierge service is absolutely disappointing, and really night and day from the other Hyatt in downtown SF. The most upsetting part of the interaction is that they do not value the guests' time. They really take their time to figure out for themselves what guests are inquiring. 
The rooms and amenities are pretty standard. This time, the room ran out of toilet paper, and when my husband called for a roll, no one ever came; I got up, changed, went out, and looked for someone with a cleaning cart in the hallway, but I could not find one, so I called this time and offered to go pick one up if no one is available. The woman did not know that no one had yet delivered that toilet paper and insisted that she'll send someone to deliver the toilet paper; a guy finally came with a toilet paper and a box of tissues, which we did not need.

Been to a number of Four Seasons properties and found this among the best. The decor in the rooms and bathroom plumbing suits my taste perfectly: very contemporary, clean lines, Asian in overall style but also very comfortable. I had a corner room with wonderful views, a huge walk-in shower that had both rain and hand-held heads and a standalone bathtub. Service was top-notch throughout the hotel. The spa is beautiful with a huge men's area (assume women's is same) including large jacuzzi and steam room. Outdoor pool, small but useful gym. After many mediocre massages in world famous spas, was quite happy to get a really good, deep tissue massage here (the masseur was James). Only ate breakfast here, but he food was excellent. I had their Carnitas Huevos Rancheros one day (try it!) and Eggs Benedict another. Location is super - right across the street from the Performing Arts complex, easy walk to terrific dining and also quite close to the Cherry Creek running-biking trail. It may have been more expensive than some other hotels in downtown Denver, but I felt I got good value. Highly recommended!

Claimed that this is a newer remodeled hotel however our room and every other room had insulation coming off the doors or missing. This missing insulation caused light to come through when we were trying to sleep and you could hear details from every conversation of people walking by. The air conditioner looked like it had not been cleaned for months and when we turned it on dust filled the room. When we called the front desk to address the above issues, the female front desk attendant was rude and commented that the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""maintenance worker gets off at -- and probably will not have time to fix the problems."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" We insisted that the problems be fixed and she reluctantly sent the maintenance worker to our room. Why do paying customers have to insist on basic customer service? In general, a very noisy hotel with very thin walls. We definitely will not stay at this hotel in the future as first impressions are lasting impressions. Why does the General Manager continue to apologize as this is little consolation for the inconvenience and unpleasant stays after-the-fact.

This is a fairly standard and consistent Embassy Suites hotel. Rooms are nice, common areas are clean and breakfast and manager's reception is what you would expect. For a rate of just over $---, this is a great pick if you're needing to stay in this area.

There is a parking garage next to the office. But never safe! They just sleep like us during the night. My car's front window was broken the next morning right after check-in. My GPS and camera that were kept in the box under the dash board and thus not seen from outside were stolen. I felt terrible all the way staying in SF. Anyway don't rest assured after parking your car. Their garage is open to anybody like other streets of SF. 
Without this, my family and I would have more fun....

Every Hotel-Motel should put the most into the mattress quality. That's the #- thing I check for each time I stay somewhere. In our - queen, one was newer and too firm, and the other was worn out and sagging. When I find a place with great beds, I never go anywhere else in that town. We will try somewhere else next time, but the deal was great at $---night for - nights. It's cheaper, because its - miles north up the --- from Hotel Circle. The staff was perfect. They resopnded to our every need. They offered to change our rooms to the newer ones, but we were settled in already. We asked for a microwave and got it (no chg). The grounds are very well kept (in a mom & pop sort-of-way). The older rooms (Building A, B, C, or D) are huge, and we chose them over the newer, smaller rooms in Building E with newer mattresses (only because we were already unpacked). Look out for this: A, B, C, D have only a -x- shower; while E has shower-bathtubs (same price). The walls in --- were thin enough that my wife and I were given an awakening performance by our next door neighbors. We didn't use the pool, but it was heated and looked great.
The summary: If your San Diego budget is below $----night, this is a great pick. You need a car if you stay here, which is okay, it is still only - extra minutes to Sea World, Zoo, beaches, harbor, etc.
This is a great ** (- star), but a stretch at *** (- star).

We only stayed here one night, but we found the room to be clean and comfortable. 
The staff was excellent beginning to end.
Not much to say other than this Four Points did exactly what we were looking for.

We debated where to stay in Denver and are so glad we picked the Magnolia. The location was perfect for exploring downtown on foot and we were able to walk to a concert at the Fillmore. The hotel is clean, friendly and unpretentious. We didn't take advantage of some of the extras (cocktail hour, gym, lounge, etc.) but there was lots of activity and a good vibe. The rooms are nothing fancy but adequte, clean and comfortable.

We stayed here for - nights on our way to San Francisco, really pleased with our choice of hotel. Rooms were large, bathrooms large with fantastic walk-in showers, plenty of towels, shampoo etc.
Beds were the most comfortable I have slept in when travelling, we all slept so well which is a huge bonus when you are rushing around and suffering jet lag!
We ate in The Rock every night, not very adventurous but it meant the kids could go up to the room to sleep while we finished off some drinks-dessert. Food was good, pizza-pasta-burgers etc, fast, friendly service.
We had bagels-coffee-juice etc from the little cafe takeaway which was good quality and tasty although quite slow service at times.
We used the fitness room and pool, small but functional, nice to have there if you want to use it.
Hotel is a little out of the way, but close to the Space Needle where you can catch the monorail for a couple of dollars to downtown Pike Place etc.

Great location, one block from Beale Street. Across the street from the Peabody. The Hampton was very clean, and staff helpful. The Hampton breakfast was the normal free breakfast. 
The only negatives were the price of the parking $-- per night, and overall price. That being said, I would still stay there again.

I stayed here for business because another hotel was already full. I liked it when we arrived and the staff at the front desk was very helpful. When I got to my room I realized it was like a W Hotel but just a little less nice. No big deal. I was still happy with everything. Then came the evening. I accidentally took the wrong elevator from my floor which ended up on the roof. There was some 'classic LA lounge' on the roof. I asked the 'bouncer' that was far less than friendly how I get to the lobby and he was a total a-hole. Then I met with co-workers and went to go to my room two different times in the evening and was harassed by the staff in the lobby near the elevators. I guess that rooftop d-bag lounge is a big thing so you will be harassed every time you go to the elevator if you have a wristband. What the...? I just want to go to my room...stop asking me about wristbands! I will not stay at this place again. If their d-bag lounge is that important than I can stay at many other places in downtown LA. And so can all of my co-workers that I told about this one night stay...

What a memorable stay at this luxurious hotel that presents as grand the first sight of it. We stayed on the --th floor of the tower, overlooking the city that stretched forever with city lights. The room we had was quite large and had all of the amenities we needed. The food was wonderful, though the cost of cocktails in teh lounge was a bit surprising to say the least. 
With the hotel perched upon the hill, we took a venture down to Union Square, just a few blocks down very steep hills. Although we chose to walk back up to the hotel, the streetcar was available to bring you back directly to the hotel.
Overall a very pleasurable experience!

My wife and I stopped here from -- Dec to --th Dec ----, prior to getting on the Queen Mary for a cruise.
It was all as expected, warm, clean, very friendly staff. We had two queen beds in a large room with a view of the bridge.
The rate included a continental breakfast which was well supplied and set us up for the morning.
It is in a good location to walk to a lot of sights and there are subways near by.
There were other Brit families staying at the time - who were happy with what was on offer. The free internet was a bonus. The mananger was helpfull and answered my emails quickly

Complimentary shuttle from and to the airport. Bountiful and decent priced breakfast buffet. Beautiful hotel. The suite we had was enormous; bedroom, living room with kitchenette and bathroom. The pool looked nice, but we didn't have time to try it out. Very comfortable beds-bedding.

This hotel is in a great location within walking distance to many good restaurants, bars and local attractions. The hotel staff are friendly and accommodating. Very nice pool and pool bar-restaurant. The rooms are spacious with upgraded amenities, clean and have comfy beds. With all that being said, it is really the view from the balcony overlooking the marina that sets this hotel apart from others I have stayed in. Be sure to get a room on an upper floor with an outside balcony facing the marina, it is just beautiful!

Just got back from Chicago had to go there for a medical appt for my daughter. The staff at this hotel were so helpful. Even printed out directions for getting around town. Very comfy rooms, suprisingly very quiet also. The hotel was almost like an oasis from the hustle and bustle of the city. The tree lined street the hotel is located on was lovely! Very conveniently located. If I ever return to Chicago no matter what my budget is for the trip this hotel will have my business. They were great. Coffee and tea vailable ---- in the lobby. And the coffee was great. Cant say enough how much we enjoyed our stay here. Would recommend to anyone.

Unfortunately, when you're at the nexus of downtown you're kind of between buildings with no view. Our room overlooked an odd cement courtyard. Other than that, though, the Red Lion exceeded my expectations on all levels. 
The service is exemplary and the staff really went the extra mile to make sure our stay was worry free. They let us check in an entire cart of luggage for what ended up being - days after we checked out and were extremely gracious in all interactions. Check in couldn't have been simpler. 
The restaurant stops serving food rather early, I want to say midnight. The ceilings in the guest rooms are unusually high which makes the hotel feel very spacious and classy. The beds are dreamily comfortable, although the walls are not entirely sound proof and we were woken by the room at the head of our bed several times. 
They offer an excellent breakfast buffet (hot food, coffee, etc.) for $- per person, which is a killer deal. Another cool thing about the Red Lion is that it is immediately next to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""diamond building"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", the center of the Seattle jewelry industry.

The hotel is a few blocks west of Union Square on Post Street. Post is much safer and quieter than Geary St. where I stayed last time. There aren't as many pan handlers. Market St. is also just a few blocks away. There are many ethnic restaurants a block down the street on Jones and on Post. A drugstore is a block or so away on Geary and Taylor. There are numerious neighborhood groceries within a block as well.
The hotel is packed because the rates are very reasonable for a well-located hotel.
I was in a ground floor renovated room. The hotel has the potential for grace and comfort. Sadly, the owner did not not invest adequately in its renovation. The windows are thin, letting in drafts and street noise. There are no window screens and flies visit, looking for supper. The construction of the shower stall did not allow for proper closing of the door. However, unlike many newer hotels, the furnture, though shabby, offers plenty of drawer space. The ceilings on my floor were relatively high. The rooms could have been comfortable and lovely, if only the owner had invested in adequate quality renovation and spent just a bit more for furniture and room fans.
The staff was friendly and attentive. Breakfast is sweet rolls and coffee with some fruit. There is a Happy Hour with snack mix, Ritz crackers and sliced supermarket cheese. Free wine is provided but I don't drink so I can't report on that. 
There are also computers for guest use in the lobby and in the first floor hallway. Wifi is available in rooms. I could not get cell phone reception in my room but I really didn't mind.
San Francisco is so expensive that for the $---.-- per night that I paid, I am not sure that I could get anything better. I also don't spend that much time in my room so the accommodations met my needs. 
I think I would have paid a bit more to see this lovely old building get the treatment it deserves. The ghosts of those who frequented these rooms when the hotel was grand must be sighing in despair. If they appear this Halloween, perhaps they can ask the owner to properly restore their former haunt.

We chose this hotel partially based on reviews from this web site. It did not disappoint. We were pleased to find the staff friendly and helpful, without the snobbishness that comes with some of these higher priced hotels. We were delighted to receive the bottle of champagne the staff sent up for our anniversary. The Sofitel is a nice sized hotel, but not overly huge. The lobby is comfortable and inviting. Our rooms were a good size and fairly quiet, given the location. Very comfortable bed as well. We had good breakfasts at the diner down the street, and other meals while we were out. On our last night there, we were exhausted from all the walking and wanted to eat someplace good and nearby. The concierge recommended Osteria al Doge down the street, and we enjoyed an excellent meal in a relaxed setting to celebrate our --th anniversary. Sofitel would be my first choice in hotels the next time we travel to NYC.

Great Find! I was traveling on business in the area and found this place through tripadvisor site. I much prefer the boutique hotels over the big chains, and hotels like the Moorpark are the reason why. The lobby appears to be more like a home than a hotel. The staff are so friendly and helpful, and the rooms are perfect. Great size, nice-clean furniture, and a wonderfully comfortable bed. I typically prefer to stay in the downtown areas to walk to everything, but this was worth the - mile drive to downtown San Jose.

We have stayed at Pier - twice now when i have appointments at Johns Hopkins ( they have an arrangement with Pier - , even a shuttle to the hospital) anyway, the staff here is customer service oriented ... they are always ready to take care of you and help you with any questions about the area or their hotel ( and they act like it's THEIR and hotel and you are the most important guest in the Inner Harbor ! They take an ownership about the way they want to see that your stay is a wonderful one.

A beautiful and clean hotel that my fiancee and her children were excited to be at! They were very happy with all the amenities,and we would gladly stay there again when we visit the family there! Highly recommended!

No free breakfast as stated online.
No hot water when I wanted to take a shower, morning or evening. I complained about this each morning (- days). There was hot water at - one evening, but that wasn't when I wanted to shower.
The rooms are nicely appointed and the beds are comfortable.

Our one night stay was wonderful. The hotel is beautiful, convient to multiple restaurants and shopping, and the staff is very accommodating. We went to the spa where the staff and facilities were outstanding. The indoor pool and hot tub area was very relaxing and has a beautiful view of the golf course. Overall, it was a wonderful stay!

The hotel is situated directly on the Magnificent Mile and yards away from the river, just walk out straight into the centre of Chicago. I managed to get a good rate through Hotwire, but the IC still honored my Ambassador status and upgraded me to a larger corner room in the Historic Tower with all other benefits. I was pleased with the large room and the two-way view to Downtown and Lake Michigan. Historic decor in this part of the hotel: I liked it but perhaps not to everyone's taste. Very comfortable bed, great power shower but a rather shallow bathtub and only average quality toiletries. The towels were not especially thick. Staff were very helpful, especially when my keycard stopped working -- minutes before a late -pm check-out: an immediate offer was made to extend the check-out to -pm.
The swimming pool is a must for its historic associations, but note that it is set up for lane swimming and may not be a suitable diversion for families with young children.
The wireless internet is charged extra and was not particularly quick. I chose the $-- --week option but was pleasantly surprised that the charge was automatically reduced to about $-- at the end of my --day stay.
The Starbucks in the lobby offers a cheaper option for breakfast coffee and a bun.
If you can get a good rate at this porperty, go for it.

I stayed at the Radisson on Fisherman's Wharf from -----th Feb, ----. When I checked in the front desk staff member was extremely nice and friendly and very helpful, giving me a map and pointing out and circling things I should do and see. I paid for a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""run of house"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room so was given whatever room they felt like giving me. Turned out to be a nice big double room on the -th floor. Shame about the renovations though, I had to cart all my bags out of the main building where you check in and haul them over to a -nd entrance and up to the -th floor. Luckily enough I met some fellow Aussie's in the lift who helped carry my bags to my room! The room itself was great, very big with a nice bathroom and flat screen tv. The sleep number beds were pretty crummy though - one of the beds didn't work so I tried the other one and it is so hit and miss with trying to set it and when you roll over at night time it sometimes made a clunking noise. EEK! Renovations were going on literally right outside my door and on the exterior of my room's wall in the hallway. It started at about -am and lasted til about - or -pm some nights. I had to walk past - stands in the middle of the hallway telling me that the section that my room was in is closed for renovations! My door handle was covered in dust everyday when I got home! I asked to be moved on my -rd day there but the only room available absolutely reeked of cigarette smoke! I'd rather stay in a noisy room than a stinky room like that! So went back to my old room and just put up with the noise. Also, my room was overlooking the carpark and had some rowdy people walking through there sometimes screaming! (the hotel had - university sports teams staying at the time too so sometimes it sounded as if there was a herd of elephants running up and down the hall!)
So the only good things about this hotel are the staff and the location. 
I really wouldn't stay here again if I could help it!

The service and friendliness of the employees here really stands out. The rooms are really big and the location can't be beat. The only thing this hotel needs is a makeover. The decor is a bit dated, but other than that we really enjoyed our stay. The happy hour at the hotel bar is awesome, and so are the bartenders!

My daughter and I stayed at the Cornell Hotel de France for - nights in August this year. It was just wonderful. 
The room was very clean and decorated very quaint & lovely. The bathroom had an old-fashioned tub with a surrounding shower curtain. Breakfast in the morning was a lovely added bonus - beautiful room on the lower floor that felt like being in a castle.
The management was very helpful and friendly. The location was great - just steps from Union Square & Chinatown.

Great stay, clean rooms and friendly staff. Norma's for breakfast is a MUST! Check in was a little slow due to a computer issue but Alex at the front desk was wonderful. Location was perfect- close to Central Park, Nobu -- where we had dinner and shopping. Did not get a chance to use the Spa on this trip but will definitely return to check it out.

Just got back from San Diego and stayed - nights at this hotel. Booked it through AAA so got a decent rate for the proximity to the ocean. It's hardly --- short block and there's the ocean - you can hear it from outside. It's a few blocks away from the main drag going through Pacific Beach (Garnet) which I was happy about. We had a queen bed which was quite spacious and had a microwave, large dorm-sized (not the rectangular boxes) fridge, utensils, plates, cooktop.
Downside: internet is not free, breakfast is a joke - donut-like stuff and coffee, decaf, OJ - absolutely nothing else, night staff (we came in really late) was a bit odd and insisted on trying to make the printer work for me to check-in - after -- minutes I really stressed to him that I didn't want to wait any more, there's no restaurant
Upside: heated pool is nice and clean, they have a shower area to clean your feet after walking the beach, proximity to the beach was a real treat, they have a laundry
Neutral: parking could be a problem - not sure if they have enough spaces for all of the rooms, bed was rock hard - we were fine with it, but others may not like that, also, the room was a bit dark

We booked two rooms at this hotel a week before arriving. The second room was for my friend; we were disappointed that they did not put the two rooms together, but rather on two different floors. Our room was a quiet, corner room and was spacious, clean, and well-appointed. Beds were comfortable and the bathroom was clean. We used the work-out center in the mornings. Parking is beneath the hotel at $---day with in-and-out privileges. The hotel provides a free shuttle service which makes various stops around tourist sites almost hourly. The walk downhill to Pikes Place is about -- minutes. Breakfast is included in the price at the adjoining restaurant---it had a nice selection of fruits, cereals, juices, eggs, waffles, yogurt, etc. The restaurant itself was chic.

Based on Tripadvisor reviews I decided not to stay here, but I did attend a conference which was held here. I didn't see the rooms first-hand but heard a few stories that confirmed my decision to not stay here. To be fair many of the travellers I heard from at the conference said the rooms were fine, but again I won't relay those stories since I don't have first hand experience. What I can tell you about are the public areas and conference facilities.
Service: I found the staff to be very friendly and helpful at all times and I would like to give them the highest marks for that. I spoke to front desk agents twice, as well as had some interaction with the housekeeping staff and restaurant staff.
The hotel overall's appearance is old and tired like a real budget property. It is not near anything so you need a car if you want to get away for a while. The public areas appeared clean, just not very modern. The restrooms were clean with one that stayed out of service during our visit. The meeting room was comfortable. I ate at the buffet twice, once for a breakfast and one for a lunch. Both were delicious. Breakfast was $-.--. The lunch was included in my conference price so I don't know what it was, but one night for dinner they had chicken and tilapia for $--.--, but on another night it was about $-- (which I didn't eat) and that seemed a bit high.
I stayed near Easton Town Center, about - miles away, and was not disappointed. Great variety in things to do and restaurants close by. They also have a free shuttle that will take you around in the local area.

I'm a senior female. The staff was great from the time I got out of the car to the time I left. They handled my baggage and referenced me by name each time I approached the front desk. I will definitely stay here again.

Do not be fooled by their fancy website and quite friendly """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""prior-to-your-arrival"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" service. They promise that ALL guest rooms are """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cozy and comfortable"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and (according to Boston guides) re-furbished. Perhaps some of the rooms have indeed been renovated, but I stayed in one of the Economy Twins and it was a mistake. Dump, smelly, with dirty carpet, greasy stains on the walls and towels worse than the cloths used to wipe dogs feet after a walk on a rainy day. I must admit that the staff is very friendly and helpful, but that's all as regards recommendation for this hotel. And the room price included an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""energy surcharge"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", which reminded me of hotels in Eastern Europe in ----s...

Our family stayed in the hotel for one night! It was clean and the staff was pleasant and helpful! Check in and out was easy! The night club was not an issue since we stayed on the opposite side of the hotel. The beds are a bit hard but my husband was finally happy. 
Pool was small but the kids had a great time! The soa did not work which we were really looking forward to after a long day of touring DC. The gym was clean and equipped enough to get in a decent workout. 
Super close to the metro which is super easy to use;)
There is also a super market and a few restaurants right near the hotel.

The location is great. That is the only good feature here. We thought that this would be a modern boutique hotel. Older building that has been redone on the quick and cheap. Nothing particularly nice about this hotel. The pictures make it seem more modern than it actually is. Mattress was terrible. Woke every morning with pain. Will not stay here again.

Helpful staff went out of their way to find us a room even after on-line booking site failed to save our reservation. Harborside accomodated us for our entire stay at a very fair rate. Room was spacious, clean and comfortable. Computers in lobby, staff is knowledgeable about local eateries, activities and nightlife. Oh yes and did I mention location! We were steps away frmo the Subway, and never had too wait long for a cab on the rainy days (Boston weather), oh yes and parking is just - blocks away (not bad for such a cramped city). Historic sites literally accross the street, aquarium, downtown, shopping. This is a great example of what a small city hotel should be, fair price and just the right amount of accomodations for a savvy traveler such as myself ;)

This hotel is situated right next to Ground Zero. The view was really impressive. The hotel is clean and staff was great in the bar, concierge, front desk areas. The only thing that was not great was the restaurant, the service was slow and food overpriced for what you got! If they fix the restaurant situation I would have probably given them a -!

For Boston`s oldest hotel, this is a classy old lady and within walking distance to all the downtown tourist attractions...just outside the door follow the bricks in the sidewalk of the Freedom Trail. The room was tight but with all the major and new amenities, like flat screen tv and free Internet with two beverages served each morning to your room if you sign-up for the free Omni Club membership. There is also an excellent health room with great exercise equipment, free headphones for tv`s on aerobic machines and a loaded fruit basket! Very nice rooms, it looks like it has been upgraded...not like the old DoubleTree's. Not a lot around, but close to the airport

I would definately stay there again. It was close to the subway & close to my shuttle bus which was near the Waldorf Astoria. Excellent place to stay. I didn't know what to expect, especially since this trip was not planned, but I was pleasantly surprised with guest service. My family and I will stay here again. Thanks.

It was altogether a great experience staying at The Chelsea Pines. It was a very personal service with real care in helping us with ideas of where to go and what to do. It was our --th wedding anniversary and a lovely bunch of white roses was delivered to our room from the owners. If we return to New York we have no doubt we would stay there again.

Stayed at Hilton weekend of August ---th. Great location in proximity to Comerica Field, Ford Field and Greektown. Front desk staff very polite and helpful and decent buffet breakfast for $--.--. Would definately recommend this location.

I travel to Jacksonville frequently on business and often stay at the Jacksonville Marriott. It is located on the southside, about - miles south of downtown. I truly enjoyed my - night stay at the Residence Inn. I had an issue the first time that I attempted to say at the hotel. Thank you staff and Amelia.

Enjoyed our stay at Coventry Inn in San Francisco. Free Parking, large clean room, reasonable prices. Walking distance to eating establishments. It is noisy on the Lombard Street side due to Traffic, but did not interupt our sleep and I would stay here again!

Have stayed here many times for work over the last - months. LOVE the Hotel & Staff!! They always make you feel welcome and go out of the way to meet your needs.

Headed to Charlotte for a long weekend with my family. Searched numerous hotels and found rooms at this Holiday Inn. I was hesitant due to the fact that some reviews were less-than-positive. However, we were surprised to find that the hotel has been renovated and updated and is nicely done. The rooms were clean and comfortable but both had a musty, humid smell to them. We ran the air conditioners for the entire stay and that helped significantly. We ordered room service our first evening and dinner was good with plentiful portions. We ate at Cafe Siena in the hotel for breakfasts. The first day (Sunday) breakfast was quite good with a buffet and omelets to order. The next day, we arrived at the same time but the buffet was depleted and not being refilled very quickly. They were out of several buffet items and I asked if they would be refilled and was told they would. However, after -- minutes of waiting, my sons decided to eat cereal and grits and not wait on the eggs, bacon and biscuits. That was a bit of a disappointment since the previous day's buffet was much better. The location of this property is great...near restaurants, Epicenter,Time Warner Arena and about a -- minute walk to the Panthers stadium. The Uptown area is quite safe and well-lit so we walked both to and from the game (which ended at -pm). The staff was extremely pleasant and friendly and helpful. Housekeeping was prompt and attentive and, again, very friendly. The rooftop pool-hot tub looked small but would still be welcome on hot days. The rooms have granite countertops, flat screen tv's and newly finished tile floors and newer bedding. Overall, this is a nicely-located hotel and not your average Holiday Inn with valet parking, room service and upgraded amenities. This is a great place to stay if you want central-location and proximity to restaurant and shopping.

We stayed for a night, and were pleasantly surprised by convenient shuttle service to metro and to airport. Breakfast was plentiful, but the breakfast room got crowded and stayed crowded through the morning, making it very difficult to get desired food. The shuttle drivers can use some customer service training. One of them was very rude to an Asian couple who did not speak very good English. The on-site bowling alley and restaurants were convenient, although there were quite a few police officers patrolling through the bowling alley.

I stayed at this hotel for three nights in January for a conference. The hotel is situated within walking distance to Times Square, but is not on the Square. My floor had six rooms on it and I was about --- of the way up the building. I did have a couple of longer waits for the elevator but not really bothersome.
The lobby is fairly small and the staff helped me with my check-in without incident. The Candlewood has a pantry that operates on the honor system. They carry soft drinks and snacks and such. I tended to walk around the corner to a small convenience store and pick up items at a lower price.
The room is small (see my photos) yet clean and filled with amenities such as microwave, hotplate, dishwasher and refrigerator. My fridge was not turned on when I entered the room, and I noticed it the following morning when I went for my now tepid soda (breakfast of champions, right?). The room was icy upon entry as the heat-A-C unit was turned off. It warmed quickly but I was a bit put off by this reception. The hotel provides an information sheet that claims a DVD player is in the room but mine was absent (not that I brought any DVDs with me anyway).
The bathroom has a commode, sink and tub with shower. No super-duper showerhead in the Candlewood; you should stay at the HI Express or Hampton next door if you want an upgrade on the showerhead. There was nowhere to hang a wet towel except over the shower curtain rod. The towels were good and I had enough for my entire stay.
Candlewood Suites do not provide housekeeping service except once a week. During my entire stay they did not enter my room to empty the trash, make my bed, or provide new towels. The information sheet tells guests that the housekeeping service is done once a week and to contact the front desk if you require any service before then. I did not know this extended to trash service so I find this unusual. I didn't see any roaches and I didn't suffer from any bedbugs. So I guess they respected my privacy!
The exercise room in the basement has a TV, elliptical, two treadmills and two stationary bikes along with a nautilus in a cramped room. The equipment all appeared to be in good working condition during my stay.
The wifi worked fine for my needs. The hotel has no business center so you have to go next door to print your airline boarding passes or have the front desk staff do it for you.
I walked to the Javits Convention Center, -th Avenue, Times Square, Hell's Kitchen all without feeling threatened although NYC in January has a curious gift of the wind blowing in your face no matter what direction you walk. There are several good restaurants around the area, as well as pubs. Depending upon your tastes, you can find virtually any kind of food. John's Pizza was good, Stitch was comfortable, Houndstooth is similar to Stitch, and dive bars like Rudy's and Smiths by Birdland are fun.
Other than the housekeeping aspect I found this hotel to meet my expectations and needs based on price and location. If you have more than two people I would seek other accommodations, or if you prefer more service or a more central location expect to spend more. I will recommend this hotel with these caveats.

I loved this hotel. The lobby is really cool and the rooms are wonderful. The mattress is super comfortable. The decor in the rooms is modern, hip and very neat. We were only here for one night and I would absolutely have loved to have stayed longer. Check in was smoothe and easy. The staff was helpful, quick and very nice. My room was on the --rd floor and the view was fabulous. This hotel is the whole package. Very cool!

Fabulous location. Short walk to Petco, the Convention Center, and all that the Gaslamp district has to offer. The gym is tiny (- ellipticals, - treadmills) and so is the pool, but the rooms are comfy and have a full kitchen. Included breakfast is quite good, though if you want bacon or sausage you need to ask for that.

The Bull and Bear Restaurant has undergone a nice renovation, and the Waldorf's overall atmosphere of classic and restrained elegance was once again on display, We look forward to staying at there again soon.

Yes I know it an airport hotel. But it is a Marriott. Should be a Motel -.

I stayed at this hotel a few times prior to the updates, and last week stayed at this hotel after the room renovations--what a huge improvement! The Milford is in THE PERFECT location in Midtown Manhattan and it's so nice to see that they have made those rooms new again. Don't be fooled when you get off the elevator by the very dark hallways...the rooms are wonderful. They did a good job at making it updated, yet keeping it affordable to average folks. The entire staff was amazing and went out of their way to be helpful and friendly. We interacted with the front desk a few times, housekeeping twice, two managers, the doorman, etc. and everyone made us feel welcome. I would highly recommend this to someone looking for a clean hotel room, in a great location at an affordable price.

Sorry for this late review , but better late than never :-) We are a couple from Denmark who stayed at this lovely hotel in january ----. From the moment we stepped into the hotel we felt very welcome - the manager Greg is very nice, helpful and friendly, although he didn´t dare to go in the sea swimming with us :-) The hotel is right on the beach and has a nice roof top that ovelooks the beach. The rooms was small but nice (we had seaview) , but the bed could be bigger or maybe a room with twin beds. 
It is in the quiet end of venice beach and you can walk to the lively part of venice beach in -- minutes and around the corner - minutes away there are some good restaurants :-)
We would like to return another time :-)

Under renovation, I was able to get a $-- rate. Rooms nice, but need the renovation, breakfast buffet quite good. Quiet, pool alittle bit out of the way but nice. Right across from Terminal one. A great stay.

We are a party of five (hubby, kids aged -- - --,me) who just finished staying at the Mayflower Renaissance Marriott hotel for $--- night from Nov -- - --th during Thanksgiving week visiting our UCLA daughter who is completing an internship there. The hotel is very historical and in a great location, about - blocks to Dupont Circle, .- mile to the White House, and -.-- miles or so away from the Smithsonian museums. We pretty much walked everywhere except when we went to Mt Vernon.
