Our stay at the Denver Ritz Carlton was very pleasant. It was apparent when we arrived that we were going to be lavished with exceptional service from the entire staff of the Ritz. The high light of the experience with the hotel staff was meeting Chris of the Engineering department. An articulate nice professional well groomed man who demonstrated great pride in the Ritz Carlton Denver. 
The Health Club was a first class operation with a wonderful layout and modern equipment. 
I am not a fan of hotel restaurants, but Elway’s at the Denver Ritz is special.

i love to travel in the united states, and always stay at la quinta inns because they are affordable and very accommodating.
this la quinta was also very nicely accommodated, with a very large swimming pool which i loved, and also a delicious breakfast.
i think the best feature of my stay here at the hotel is the peaceful and quiet environment. the outdoor courtyard was really nice for reading with the benches.
if i am in phoenix next time, this is where i will stay.

I booked this hotel on line and the photos that were shown were not of this hotel. This hotel had the entry doors on the outside. The room was dirty and the furniture very old. We checked in and as soon as we saw the room turned around and checked out.

I've stayed here before, and whilst I'm still a Gold Elite I thought I'd stay here again, as the status means I'd probably get upgraded, and also lounge access - handy for the free internet as I don't like paying for net access if I can avoid it. It does form part of my decision of where to stay nowadays, and it's time some of the large chains realised that fleecing their customers is not right, though I can understand why they do it as the business travellers expense it so they can charge the high rates.
Got a room on the concierge floor (--th), and no complaints with the room. You know what you're getting with a Marriott, they tend to feel the same wherever you are. Very comfortable bed as always, and blackout curtains so you can sleep at any time of the day or night - handy for those bright Times Square lights! No noise issues from the street either.
Had a few issues with the lift this time, which has never happened before. They do tend to get very crowded at peak times (E.g. -.--pm when people head for the theatres) so leave a bit earlier, and you'll be fine.
I'll be staying here again if I get a good rate. If you want to be in the middle of the action, nearby the theatres and don't mind a large impersonal hotel then this is the place to be.

I thought this was an excellent business hotel. I had a quiet room and thanks to TA, had a room facing west on a high floor. The staff was excellent and attentive. My room was clean and spacious. Did I say quiet? Well, it was. The lounge on the highest floor was fun but the wait staff seemed overworked and we had to wait for our drinks. My only complaint is the fault of mother nature- the hills! Walk over one block and much easier to navigate. Walking down is no problem but cut over and the walk back up is much more doable.

the vallet refused to park my car without a huge tip because it was cold .when i told mgmt. they said they would fix it buy refunding one night instead they deducted money from my account.and said they have no record of telling me that.

From meeting Angel on the door as we arrived it was fantastic, Dominic, all the bar staff and restaurant staff were real good company. Superb service from each and everyone of you and cant wait to get back, top quality people across the hotel, if you are the manager then please take note of these comments, Regards to you all, a great experience.
Regards
Les Jones & Kathryn Hibbert

Hotel itself was ok, owned by Ramada group. The staff sucked, the lady at the front desk was kind of rude and did not even smile. I was put at a quiet corner room, which was ok until I found out they were renovating the stairs and painting. The maintenance guy had a key card and before knocking he just barged in to my room. Thankfully I was just unpacking that time. After that had happened I tried to call down to front desk which had a busy tone for -- mins. Finally I had to go out so I went downstairs to talk to front desk. This is when I found out why there was busy tones. The people there were chatting and when the phone had rang, they just press the busy button. I've asked to switch rooms but they said they had a full house. I've also asked for nobody to do room service, but they ended up coming anyways. Nobody seems to listen.
Now for the brighter side of things. It's only a block away from Metro train and some great rapid lines to West hollywood area. The red line is great, it intersects with lots most of the lines. --- block away you will find great take out, Mexican take out, Chinese was good ( I'm Chinese). Subway if you want something familiar. Being from Vancouver, our taste buds are very picky because Vancouver is food Heaven.. (this is take out we are comparing)
The breakfast Buffet has good sausages and eggs. Also has cereal, bagels, toast and fruit. They have a waffle iron, but nobody to make them. 
So it was a great location, ok place, bad service. Would've been better if I got a smile, and no guy barging in my room (he probably wanted to use the bathroom)

We stayed here for a family trip and wanted somewhere central, roomy and clean. We were on the --th floor - North Tower. Check in was quick and easy with friendly staff. The room was a little tired, but on the positive side roomy and light. It really came in to its own on the -th of July when we had front row seats for the Macy's fireworks.
The AC was working, although not very cold. The pool, however was cool and very welcome given the weather. It's a shame that it closes at -pm as evening swimming would be great! 
The lobby staff were very helpful in looking after our luggage until we were ready to leave. They also booked us a hotel car to JFK and quoted $-- including tip. The driver was obviously taken aback at not being offered an additional tip on arrival.

$---.-- per night. Great location (- block from beach). Great service. Pets allowed. Heated pool and lobby bar. Nice clean rooms with new LCD tv's. No noise in hallway. This is now our favorite hotel in SF. The location is awesome! Parking was $--.-- per night. Just drive - blocks up Mason and overnight parking is --- that. Cab or walk back to hotel. Cable car stop is - blocks. The Raddison across street is same price but not as nice. You will like this hotel for the price.

My husband and I, we have stayed here about -years ago and were kind of frightend by the size of the room. This time we returned here with our daughter due to a business trip and the room size and certain services frightened us again. 
The doormen weren't efficient and welcoming, nor were the taxis waiting in front of the hotel. The reception was however very nice. Our room was small and as we travelled from Asia, we had more than - pieces of luggages. We could only have one opened, the rest we needed to have them open and stored under the bed. 
The ventilation in the bathroom was constantly on and so lound that we couldn't bare the door of the bathroom opened. The heater seemed not to work properly. 
The first impression of the lobby might be trendy, and indeed the room itself, however not the bathroom at all, was also in a trendy setting, however it is definitely not a family friendly hotel and absolutely not the room rate worth.
The only positive point was that we were STARWOOD Gold level members, so we could stay in our room until -pm, as our plan took off at --pm.

I spent three nights (--- - ---) at this hotel while in San Francisco for a conference. The hotel is very attractive, with clean rooms and beds to die for. I mean, this must be what laying on a cloud feels like. However, despite the wonderful bed, I was unable to sleep the first night because I had a room on the sixth floor overlooking the alley and the dumpsters that I became very well aquainted with. I was compensated by the hotel for this lack of sleep resulting from the dumster noise in the form of a new room on the thirteenth floor and a comped room (first night).
I thought this was very stand-up and customer-oriented by the hotel - hence my high rating. I felt that I was treated very well and always with the utmost courtesy.
The one final point is that the housekeeping staff need to ensure that the creamer in the little coffee packets are not stale. I had this experience but they quickly brought fresh replacements.

Very close to downtown,our stay was very pleasurable...right from check-in everything was clockwork in this hotel.
Rooms are very comfortable with great views of the bay,with higher floorshaving better view.
Modern amenities ...very modern bathrooms.
 Very good restaurant...with great breakfast.Very helpful staff doing their best for you.

I stayed at the Monaco for - nights on business. It's a really warm, atmospheric place with loads of character - I loved the decor, the fact that dogs are allowed to stay, the sitting room with huge fireplace and wine reception every evening, the food in the Grand Cafe, the in-room yoga kit and on-demand yoga channels... the list goes on.
The hotel is on the edge of the Tenderloin (it's to the southwest of the hotel) which is not the most desirable part of SF, and it's a few blocks from Union Square, but San Fran is easily navigable on foot (or bus or cable car) so it was no problem for me.

I stayed there one night on a business trip. Good location in downtown, service was superb all the way from check-in to check-out the next day. As SPG Gold member, got upgraded to the suite, that was large and comfortable. Access to Club level was also a nice touch. Room furnishings and design were not the greatest, in my opinion, but everything was clean and functional. No complaints about sleep quality and bed either. The only little caveat: Internet wasn't free, and this is a serious shortcoming in my book. For SPF Preferred guests it is free sometimes, but it wasn't a case. It is not about money as is, this is more of the basic rights for traveller nowadays: free wi-fi, large hotel chains in US are falling behind with this amenity, not sure why?!

I recently had an extended stay at the Residence Inn. As I was in the limbo of temporary housing while trying to find a home for my family in Denver, the Residence Inn did an outstanding job of meeting my needs. The fantastic central location was clean and the staff was so friendly. They fed me in the morning and evenings on most nights. The ladies who prepared the breakfasts made me feel like family. I was having trouble sleeping and they so graciously gave me a new mattress while I was on a business trip. It did the trick! They reserve my room each time I checked out and back in which gave me a sense of comfort and familiarity. They outfitted the room with everything I needed and were always giving me tips about the city and things to see and do. I use their shuttle service many times to take me around. They made it really easy stay there - and it was for almost - months. Thanks again to Sherry and the team making me feel at home (away from home).

The Serrano was a gem of a hotel. The rooms were adorable and immaculately clean, the beds were incredibly comfortable and the sheets and pillows were delightful to sleep in. I was with my family and they were very helpful with tourist ideas and the kind of restaurant we were looking for, sending us to places that weren't too touristy and part of the locals, which is what we wanted and asked for. 
We had - little ones with us and the staff was warm and welcoming to all of us. It's an older hotel and eclectic in style, but that's part of its charm. They offer complimentary coffee and tea in the morning and nice cool lemon water in the afternoon. 
The shower water pressure was awesome in all of our rooms - the one thing we all raved about! And the Aveda products were a nice amenity. Minimal noise from being in Union Square area. A few blocks away is a little dicey of a neighborhood, but it's safe and secure around the hotel and there'd be no reason to venture that way anyway. It's really close to all of the Union Square activity.
I'd definitely stay here again. No complaints.

From the minute we were met at the door to departure, the staff went out of their way to make us feel welcome. My daughter just loved interacting with the staff. The rooms were immaculate, the service was impeccable and the location was perfect,. The restaurant Urbana on site is not to be missed. We will be returning very soon.

I live in the Boston area and stayed at the Westin for a quick last-minute getaway. We paid $--- for a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Riverview Deluxe"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room and I'm so sorry we did. The room was incredibly ordinary. Although the view across rooftops to the Charles was nice, it wasn't worth the money.
The shower was good, but the tub didn't drain. The climate control didn't work properly (we were hot) and the bathroom was small -- needing renovation and new grout. The beds were very comfy. The location is excellent -- attached to the shopping centers. The oddly-shaped and dark lobby was always crowded with convention-goers and business people. Overall, this is a business hotel and wildly overpriced. 
You'd do much better across the street at the Copley Plaza, where for a little less money you get much more style and grandeur. Or, for the same price, choose the Ritz Carlton or Four Seasons, a few blocks away, but much nicer and on the park.
My favorite hotel rooms in Boston are the harbor view rooms at the Boston Harbor Hotel (at Rowes Wharf). Those rooms are plush, gorgeous, updated and have amazing views. The hotel is much friendlier and service-oriented. It's just a short walk from there to Quincy Market, Copley or downtown.
I would not stay at the Westin again.

We recently stayed here on our west coast road trip. What a great hotel! And the rate is very good! There are so many things we loved about the hotel....the great vibe, the great look of the rooms, clean, great coffee-espresso machine in the room, big flat tv, microwave popcorn!, quiet, friendly and helpful staff, big lobby which is great for lounging, a couple blocks from City Center, complimentary bicycle to use, etc.
I think it was our favorite hotel on our trip and we stayed at the - Seasons in San Francisco and the Fairmont in Santa Monica. Everything is true about the great reviews it's been getting.
I think the only negative I can think of is that it doesn't have a free breakfast. However they have an espresso bar right beside the lobby desk that sells breakfast items, and from what I can remember it was inexpensive and good. As well, the room did not have a tub. For us that's no big deal, but for someone who needs it, it would be for them.
We definitely enjoyed our stay and wish we had more than - night.

We stayed at this hotel during the first weekend in December. The location couldnt be more perfect, Broadway, Times Square, -th Avenue, Rockefeller Centre and all the other places you want to visit are right at your doorstep. And the best thing is that its at a bargain price. Other hotels in the area I am sure would be much more.
The room was smaller than a normal hotel room but not too small. The amenities were great, a really clean bathroom with a really hot shower and a heater that was truly great especially as it was freezing outside. The bed was so comfortable, after a long day walking the NYC streets we slept like babies.
We didnt eat at the restaurant however it was always full every night. There is free coffee --hours a day in a lounge behind the lobby where you can relax if you want to not stay in your room to plan your adventures. There is also a --hours convenience store on the corner right near the hotel for those nightime snacks too.
The checkin staff were friendly and it was no problem for them to do our internet checkin for our flight home, a wonderful help. Everything went really smoothly during our stay.
We will be definately recommending this hotel to all our friends, you cant beat it for price and location! 
A little gem in the heart of one of the worlds most fascinating cities.

My daughter and my mom decided to surprise my step dad for a last minute Valentine weekend getaway. I was told about this hotel and booked - rooms. One for my daughter and myself (- queen beds), and one for my parents (King). 
Stepping into the lobby was as if in a time warp-in a good way. Everything was accessible from the computers to the breakfast area.
After we found our rooms, my daughter found the joy in jumping from one bed to the other. (she can't do this at home). Everything in the room met my needs especially how clean the room was. This hotel had some of the softest beds I've slept in for a hotel. I was pleased.
The next day, we experienced the breakfast. This was Sunday and on this day, they serve bisquits and gravy. There was also a choice of - cold cereals, yogurt, assortment of bagels and bread, fruits, juice, coffee, milk, and of course the famous belgian waffles. This was the best breakfast I've ever seen in a hotel for not being a restaurant.
Before leaving our room for the day, the maid came by. I asked her not to worry bout the beds but we needed cups and the garbage taken out. She didn't quite understand what I was saying, a little English-Spanish barrier, but she was incredibly nice.
Sunday night, my daughter (my valentine) went to the restaurant in the parking lot. Saffron Grill. The food was amazing and we didn't have to walk-drive anywhere. After going to bed, I did have a neighbor above me that would fall down every - or so steps with a loud """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""thud"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". This happened most of the night but I reminded myself we were in a hotel. 
Check out was a breeze on Monday... we left very happy.
This hotel was close to EVERYTHING. Just a few minutes from Woodland Park Zoo, the Northgate Mall, and downtown Seattle. I loved it.
Thank you and we can't wait to come back.

The Hyatt is a nice hotel located within walking distance of HP Arena. We stayed there to attend a concert. We were pleased there were many restaurants within a - minute walk. The hotel was clean, safe with a nice free breakfast. The only thing lacking, which is minor, they didn’t have a hotel store and no stores nearby like Wal-Green, ---- nearby. Overall, a good experience. I would stay there again without hesistation.

I stayed at the Gansevoort for four nights in June ---- on a business trip. It was one of the worst hotel stays I've ever experienced.
The front desk agents didn't wear nametags - very indicative of the Gansevoort's attitude towards customer service: anonymous, impersonal, and apathetic. Nobody is accountable for anything.
The TV wasn't working when we got in the room, so the bellhop promised he would send somebody to fix it. Nobody came. A couple of hours later, we had to call the operator to ask them to send somebody.
Later on that afternoon, we decided to go up to the roof to check out the view from the much-hyped rooftop pool. As we exited the elevator, a couple of security bouncers stopped us and told us we were not allowed to go into what looked like a lounge area because it was reserved for a private party. We asked if we could go into the pool area and a woman -- not the security people who just talked to us -- interjected and told us the pool is only for hotel guests. I could not believe the impudence of this woman assuming we weren't hotel guests! (By the way, the Gansevoort rented out this lounge area every night of our four-night stay so don't expect to be able to hang out there.)
The rooftop parties were pretty loud. The hotel has -- floors, and despite being six stories down on the -th floor, I could hear the music anyway. Very annoying at midnight when you're trying to get some sleep.
The hotel is also not environmentally friendly (they changed the sheets after the first day). I had to write a note daily to the housekeeper asking them not to change the sheets. On two of the days, I was there when Housekeeping came in, and even with the note I had written, both days the housekeeper started removing the sheets from the bed and I had to stop her, saying it wasn't necessary. While most hotels provide cards in-room asking you to place the card on your bed as a sign to let Housekeeping know not to change your sheets, it's disappointing and irresponsible that the Gansevoort provides no such water- and energy-saving option to its guests.
Because there is a nightclub at the hotel, there is a velvet rope at the hotel's front door in the evenings. After a long day, I found it annoying and inconvenient getting stopped at the door and having to produce my room key before being allowed entrance.
On the second day of my stay, I called my company's travel department and complained about the terrible service. They spoke with someone in Sales (first name Kristen - can't remember the last name) and Kristen assured our travel department that she would contact me to find out what they can do to alleviate the problems I had been having. On the third day of my stay, I called my company's travel department again to let them know Kristen never contacted me and they left a message for her, but I never heard from Kristen (or anyone from Sales). I thought it was dishonest and in bad form to promise to do something and then not do it.
DO NOT TO STAY AT THIS HOTEL. It's not worth your money and the staff won't care about you. There are plenty of other places to stay at in New York (check the reviews of the top-rated hotels here on Tripadvisor.com -- you'll see the PR-sales managers replying to bad reviews asking past guests to contact them about the problems they had. That's what I call good service and you're much better off giving them your business.

Great location for a motel. The staff worked hard and all seemed very friendly. We found the motel very clean and the shower had a powerful water stream. The motel even located a vase for us to use one evening!

First sight of the interior is quite spectacular - the waterfall flowing into the courtyard, with the rooms onto balconies all round the outside. It was so restful.
The rooms (we had a suite) were spacious, comfy and clean. 
I had a lovely complimentary pina colada in the evening, and the breakfast was lovely- eaten in the courtyard - with masses of choice. Shame we only had one night there, our last in America after travelling for - weeks - it was probably the nicest hotel of all those we stayed at.

This is simply a great hotel in a great location. The staff was excellent, knowledgeable about the neighborhood and helpful. The night staff was particularly curteous and professional. This will become my go-to hotel for all my Chicago travel.

There was a stain on the carpet, an upholstery button was broken on one chair, three lights didn't work, the shower floor was old -- but the worst was the giant air shaft that it appears the majority of the rooms have as a view. Very depressing. I was glad I was there for only two nights. The staff are efficient, the food is ordinary, the location ideal. But the room I was in needed serious renovation.
The iPod dock was the nicest touch. I was able to charge my iPhone AND play music.
Would never recommend this hotel simply on the giant air shaft issue.

I travel to NYC for business once a month, so I'm always on the lookout for good deals on clean, comfortable,and convenient hotels that aren't swamped with tourists. Hotel Metro definitely fit the bill. The location can't be beat - blocks from Penn Station and steps to the subway. The rooms are as small as you'd expect from a boutique hotel in Manhattan, but very clean and comfortable. The staff were courteous and helpful; they struggled with my reservation but were willing to help. Free WiFi and continental breakfast are much-appreciated amenities for a business traveler, and the Gilchrist and Soames shampoo etc. were a nice bonus. This isn't a hotel with a lot of character, but it's a perfect place for a few nights in the city for those of us who have to get work done.

Stayed two nights. Good location, generally friendly staff. I payed $--- per night. According to these posts people are paying --% less. What I payed was too much. There was one wash cloth the first day and the next the maid left none. The room was on the small side- no window view- reasonably quiet.There was a defective short bureau door which did not close properly and I kept hitting my leg on it. Also difficult to get ice . Had to call twice. They only bring you a little bit. Also you have to que up and take a special elevator to the roof. I didn't bother - no access through the hotel elevators

I recently spent - nights here -my first at an Embassy Suites. The staff was terrific. Every single employee I encountered was friendly and helpful. The rooms were very clean and comfortable. It was great having the extra room to spread out and relax, especially for a longer stay. I liked the atrium and the fish ponds. The waterfall could get a little loud, but didn't bother my sleep.
The morning breakfast was very plentiful and varied. It was kept well stocked with fresh fruit, yogurt, coffee, and breads - plus the cooked to order omelets and sides of potatoes and breakfast meats. A great way to start the day. 
The manager's reception was a nice surprise - complementary cocktails and trays of fresh veggies, hummus and the best pita chips I have had. 
I only got to use the pool once, but it is bigger then the photos and the landscaping is pleasant. There is also a good Jacuzzi.
As others have noted, the plumbing is a little weird – my shower ran hot then cold. The toilet would randomly start running – usually in the middle of the night. I did call and someone came up to work on it right away, and it got better, but was not completely resolved.
I would certainly stay here again!

I originally stayed at the Dana in Nov. ---- on business. I stayed in the bay side - Queen room which was clean but overpriced for the time of year. I again booked a - queen room for - days in late June ---- and this time got stuck in a - queen room overlooking the marina and boy was that a complete dump. The room smelled of old musty shoes, absolutley no room to put your luggage, and the advertised """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Queen"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" beds, are simply full size. The only thing in that room that was queen was the headboard. The bed was about - inches narrower than the headboard. In addition, bring your own pillows because they are simply old stuffed rags in a pillow case. I went to the front desk to complain about it and the blond genius looked at me as if I was speaking a foreign language and simply said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""All our beds are queen size"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".
 How can you argue with logic like that? Simply put. The Dana needs major renevation. The photos on their website are completely deceptive. This place is an overpriced dump on the water. I do not recommend this hotel to anybody and I would not recommend staying there.
Great staff, location and room. Very clean. The staff made sure we had a room with a great view

Losing light, power, telephone, then water during Hurricane Sandy meant this hotel's limited attractions faded fast. Its advantage is its location but with the elevators down other than the service elevator at the back of the hotel, it was no place to stay during the storm. So I left early but that didn't stop the hotel claiming for it all on my credit card. Not your fault there was a storm, St. Giles, but I think not nice to charge when nothing was operational.

Our stay was okay ,,, The Room was smaller then previous hotel and as we had arranged a rollaway for our son we had to cancel it as there was no way it would fit without us having no spare room .... Our Son and daughter then slept in the Queen Bed and it wasn't too bad !!!! The view from room was nothing to look at , as was a dried up hill... The noise from above when trying to sleep was abit annoying to start with as sounded like a wee heard of elephants but we cranked up the air condition to cover it ... The Air conditioner wasn't working properly to start with but the front desk quickly had that sorted for us ... The hotel is old BUT like any hotel I like to stay in as long as it is clean I am happy with this .. Pool area was ok but lost the sun early because of high trees surrounding this.. When I get off the giant, sensory overload exhibit floor that is Comic-Con, I want peace & quiet and no random loud parties popping up in the next room. Third, the building: I love being in an historic space and wandering around early morning or late at night looking at all the details. The restoration job on the place is excellent, and the displays all throughout the place are wonderful.
Fourth, the location: For me, it's a perfect location. Step out the door and to my left is Cafe ---, my fave breakfast spot. To my right is a bank with two working ATMs and rarely any line, a critical need for the convention. I'm steps away from Sushi Nippon, The Field and The Cheese Shop (which also delivers to the Horton Grand if you're too lazy to walk -.- blocks). There is also an independent mini-grocery half a block away for when you discover you forgot to pack your toothpaste or lost another lighter. And of course it's within easy striking distance of the convention center, especially if you cut through the parking lot on Second Ave.
Simply put, the Horton Grand Hotel has absolutely everything I need in a hotel for Comic-Con.
Because I haven't quite kicked the habit yet, I do wish there was an ashtray somewhere out front. The Horton Grand, like most hotels these days, is a non-smoking facility.
The closet space is period-correct, so bring your own hangars if you have too many outfits!

I have raved about this hotel in the past and then fell out big time with the new owners a year or so back. After several bottles of corporate Chardonay they persuaded me to stay again and write an updated review. Here it is.....
So far the refurbishment is limited to the ground floor open areas and the -th floor suites. What was a cosy warm (but arguably dull and damp) environment has been replaced by an open area where there is no privacy and no demarkartion between what is bar (adults) and not bar (infants). Every single person I met (and I truly mean everyone) expressed emotions ranging from concern (polite) to fear about sitting at the bar - and this was not helped by a TV in a mirror that agian serves no purpose. It probably looked great on some graphic designers lap top in New York but in the real World it sucks. 
The refurbished suites are not much better. Granted the old Yellow decor (which had over time acheived an organic tinge of yellow that the original makers could never forsee) has been replaced by a 'trendy' shade of grey - but that's it. A few extra twiddly things in the bathroom but nothing new (I was not upgraded so I did not get to try out the bed). But for most folks this makes no odds because the rest of the hotel is just the same as it always was and further refurbishment wont take place until the fall.
On the pluss side (and it is a genuine plus) the door locks-keys have been replaced on all floors so the electronic keys now work more than once.
Nania...... you enter into a modern looking, but disfunctional ground floor (with no butler or automatic front door) pass through reception and press the call button for the lift. When the lift arives you walk through the back of the wardrobe into another world, much older, much darker and very yellow and it reminds you of ....?
This is work in progress, although thankfully whilst I was there there was no work (or progress) being made, and I honestly believe that the new management has good intentions but I dont know what they are trying to do with the joint. If you want a boutique hotel, this is not it. If you want a -* hotel, this is not it. If you want a family hotel, this is not it. If you want a hotel that caters for business people, this is not it. This hotel has lost its soul.
Let's hope the WIP helps find it a new soul.
I will return and keep you updated.

Where do I begin.....
 My teenage son and I decided to take a last-minute excursion from Columbus, OH to Chicago in early August ----. Our plan was to see the Planetarium, Sears Tower, Chinatown, the Navy Pier,take an evening boat ride on Lake Michigan, then head back home. Two days were plenty for all this. 
 I looked online at Hotels.com. I had never used their site before--and honestly never will again. Thank goodness for TripAdvisor!
 Online, the hotel didn't look fancy, but it did look clean and it was inexpensive by Chicago standards, BUT.....
 When we got to the hotel, I should have turned back. First of all, the photos from the site must've been taken in the ----s when the Skylark was last painted. When I walked in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lobby"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", I was greeted with a thick, bullet-proof glass covered in stickers, flyers and warnings--the most note-worthy being the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""CHICAGO POLICE WARNING: NO PROSTITUTION! Area Under Surveilance."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Yikes! 
 The guy at the check-in was rude and without looking up, put his index finger in the air to say, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Wait a minute."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" He had trouble finding my reservation and tried to get me to pay him again (I had paid online and had my receipt with me). He finally found the reservation.
 When we got to the room, the doorknob was broken, but the lock at least worked. The first thing we noticed was the cable line stapled to the wall around most of the room, until it reached the TV. My son (age --) turned on the TV while I checked out the rest of our little slice of heaven and after a few minutes, asked me if I'd rather watch a Chinese language channel or PORN!! Ummm... I chose Chinese. We don't speak Chinese, but I figured it was more appropriate family fair than a violent porno! There were only two channels.
 I then noticed the hundreds of moth holes in the ratty curtains. The sun shone through them like hundreds of little stars (We tried to make the best of this, can you tell?) 
 Our NON-SMOKING room had an ashtray and a partially used matchbook with """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Hampton Inn"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" stamped on it. The phone had a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Days Inn"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sticker on the front. Somebody went to a hotel auction.
 When my son sat on his bed (there were two double beds), the headboard fell off the nails that propped it against the wall! We couldn't stop laughing!
 I checked the sheets and pillows for stains and fluids, but the sheets were actually clean and the beds were surprisingly comfortable.
 When I went in the bathroom and closed the door, I had a huge shock--there were what appeared to be two bullet holes in the wall and old red splatters from what I imagine was blood (or perhaps burritos as another Skylarker noted below). There was also a huge dent in the wall about - --- feet up and another smaller dent in the wooden door at the same height. My son stared at that for awhile and figured out that it may have resulted from someone's head accidentally being lodged against the wall and giving that Skylarker an inexpensive rhinoplasty. Nice! Also, grafitti on the back of the door gave us something interesting to read.
 What else....the inside of the toilet was clean, but I made the mistake of closing the lid--oooh! Behind the seat, well, use your imagination! The shower was clean and there was plenty of hot water. The towels were stained and painfully scratchy.
 In the separate vanity area, I was sickened. I had sat my toothbrush on the countertop before brushing my teeth. AFTERward, I noticed a few short, curly, thick black hairs on the countertop. Again, let your imagination run free! I pitched my toothbrush. 
 On the globe-style light fixtures over the vanity, there was THICK dust from the ages and more """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""splatters"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". WHAT HAD HAPPENED IN THIS ROOM?
 My son and I popped over to Burger King, came back to the room, watched a little Chinese TV, and drifted off to sleep. I left the TV on all night to drown out the shouting and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""other"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" noises coming from our energetic neighbors.
 In the morning, we took photos, thinking nobody would ever believe us! As we were leaving, we noticed a gentleman getting out of an older model Cadillac with a young lady wearing a tube top and tiny shorts. She stumbled to their room in her ultra-high stilletto heels and they disappeared inside to perhaps discuss world events.
 When I went back to the front desk to turn in my key, I tried to tell the young girl behind the bullet-proof glass about everything. She just stared at me.  Would I recommend this place? You know, I just might! I think if you have a very, very good sense of humor, are up-to-date with your vaccines, and have recently paid your life insurance premium--you're good to go. If not, sleeping in the car might be a better option.
 Ahhh, family vacation memories. We'll never forget our little adventure at the lovely Skylark Motel! Thanks for reading.

What a nice surprise was our six night stay at this property! Top notch customer service. Well maintained facility with everything, from pool to exercise room to laundry, in working order. Clean (and recently updated we think) studio suites with comfortable beds and good bathroom layouts.

We imagine that’s because management is paying attention and fostering that culture. So good for them all around!
Springhill Suites as brand still won’t be our first choice for amenity level, but we feel we got more than we paid for at this property, all things considered. A very good value and we're pleased to recommend it.
Summary above, details follow.
TOP NOTCH SERVICE: Our good service experience started at check in. We had requested an upper floor (this is a four floor hotel) with a pond outlook based on other traveler recommendations. And when we arrived, we found that very kind of room had been assigned. Well done.
However, when we got to the room we realized the southern exposure of the front of the building that overlooked the pond was going to provide more heat in the room than we prefer. We also found the room was substantially smaller than we’d be comfortable in for an extended stay. So we asked for a room on the back of the hotel, noisier but cooler, and asked if there was anything larger too.
While we normally avoid rooms next to elevators or ice machines, on this property those rooms are bigger than some of the others, and with the help of the delightful young woman at the desk on our arrival (Fay) we ended up with a room next to an ice machine that was just right for size, location and quiet, even as she had to make a personal visit to a couple of rooms to narrow down the one that would work best for us.
That kind of service focus continued with the “how are you…how was your day…how can I help you..” greetings at the desk from all extended throughout the visit. Up to the day we left when the staff on duty thanked us, sincerely it seemed, for choosing their Springhill Suites and saying they hoped we’d come back. Good training and performance both. 
EXERCISE ROOM and POOL: Both adequate in size and well maintained.
LAUNDRY: Well maintained, a couple of washers and dryers in good working order.
FREE BREAKFAST: We’re happy with fresh fruit and yogurt and those were provided here, but also unexpected other healthy options, like raw walnuts and peanut butter. There was the standard plethora of proceessed American breakfast food, but we noted miso soup and steamed rice as daily breakfast offerings along with kimchee noodles.
BATHROOMS: Well laid out for size given the low end nature of Springhill Suites, with extra towels provided. Grab bar in the shower gets a big “woohoo” from us as safety feature.
ROOM: Beds were comfy, suite furniture laid out for easy convenience, fridge and kitchenette sink came in handy.
WIFI: Free and worked well.
PARKING: Ample free parking in lot.
LOCATION: Minutes to downtown Austin and convenient freeway access to travel to points west that we wanted to visit as well.
ACCESSIBILITY: Although we did not look at the accessible rooms on prem, we noted there did seem to be some assigned even on upper floors. (There’s a “woohoo” for you when it is so often the case that these rooms get assigned to the worst spots on the first floor.) In addition, all public areas of the hotel seemed nicely accessible as we looked about.

Before we went to dinner we checked out the wine bar in the lobby, Eno. It was great. We ordered wine and cheese flights. They matched the cheese to the various wines we ordered and it was truly outstanding. Would definitely recommend the hotel and location.

We stayed at the hotel in late November. We were very pleased with how clean the rooms were. The staff went our of their way to help. The location was great. In short walking distance to attractions, transportation and food. Thanks for a very pleasent stay while in Hollywood.

I stayed in this hotel with my mother in Dec. ----. We booked quite early and got very good rates for the location. Regarding the location it is smack in the middle of everything. Close to walk to all attractions in and around Fisherman's wharf. A min walk from trolly F which takes you to the rest of the interesting places SF has to offer. A good location to go for a hike from asa well.
The rooms are comfy and ready for a good night sleep. Clean and accomodating. The room has a safe which was also convenient. 
The hotel provided a light breakfast which was just what we needed. It was simple and identical to those of many other Holiday Inn hotels.
If you wish to visit these areas of SF I would warmly suggest this area. If you wish to see the more lively, night life rich places check out accomodation closer to market street and the BART hub.

We attended a conference at the JW, and it is fine for the business traveler. If you are looking for a personal luxury experience this is not the hotel for you. The normal amenities were lacking in the rooms i.e. shower caps, mini bar, turn down service. The meeting rooms are huge which makes it hard to hear, while the standard rooms were small. The pool and spa are spectacular, but if the weather is bad, as it was for several days of the stay, the pool is of no use. The spa and golf courses are the best features of the property. The very best of our stay was the outstanding staff. Management should be commended for the staff training. Maybe it is just San Antonio,Texas, but everyone was as friendly as could be.

I really enjoyed staying at this hotel. When my daughter and I checked in we were given an upgrade. The room was very spacious and the view of the Space Needle was nice. We took advantage of the complimentary shuttle service. The only negative thing was the noise of the trains if you are in a room on the city side. Otherwise it was a wonderful place to stay.

My husband and I travel frequently, and always stay in first-class hotels. The Boston Harbor stands above all the rest, in quiet elegance, customer service, ambience, you name it! 
We had a beautiful suite that afforded us great views of the harbor, dotted with sailboats and yachts. The room had floor to ceiling drapes, a well stocked mini bar, large screen television in the living room, beautiful bathroom, large, very comfortable bed. We enjoyed good service in the casual restaurant, and wonderful cocktails in the bar. 
If you have budget constraints, save until you have enough to enjoy a night at this hotel. You will never forget it! On our next visit to Boston, this is where we will stay.

The website for this hotel looked so cool and sexy. I was really looking forward to my stay. But I was underwhelmed by my experience here. The best thing this hotel has going for it is its location adjacent to Bryant Park and the library. The park was cool and lovely and we got to enjoy coffee out there every day of our stay.
But once you get inside the hotel, what a let down. The guys at the front desk didn't have our reservation on file when we checked in, even though we called and spoke to someone the night before to confirm. After keeping us waiting, they finally gave us a room. And the sparseness in the decor made me feel like I was in a hospital room. The hallways in our floor were all white. No artwork. Our room was a white box with furniture for tiny people. No artwork. No color. No character. It was depressing to be in the room. I expected a really fun NY experience and I got blandola.
To be fair, they did do some things right. Our bathroom was very large by NY standards. We had a separate shower with good water pressure and a really nice bath tub. The bar in the basement was a happening scene if you're into that type of thing. And our rooms were clean and quiet. Despite loud slamming doors in the morning, no other noise disturbed our sleep.
Overall, not impressed. We are in search of a new NY hotel.

Location:
Just off Chinatown, with close access to the - and N-R subways (Canal St station). There is a Burger King and McDonalds nearby on Canal St, and a Duane Reade pharmacy on nearby Broadway. The area is a bit gritty, not a problem during the day when it is busy, but maybe an issue late at night.
Lobby: The main revolving door was out of service, so everyone had to use a single side-door off the main street. Concierge is on the ground floor, but you have to take the escalator up one floor to reach the main lobby-check-in. They served iced tea in the lobby for free, which was nice during summer.
Check-in: No problems. Fast and no mistakes.
Room: Small. There is almost no gap to pass between the tv-counter in the front of the room and the bed, which also makes the room look cramped due to poor placement of in-room furniture. Bed is big and comfortable, AC was working fine. TV was a flat-screen, plenty of channels to watch. Nothing remarkable about the decor. Bathroom is a bit dated. Room can be noisy; you can hear traffic and general noise from outside, and you can hear (and feel) when the subway passes underneath the hotel. The room was clean. Housekeeping was reliable everyday.
Check-out: Fast and problem free, but the staff didn't seem very friendly or at all interested if we needed transport. 
Overall: This is an average-quality hotel. You get what you pay for. If you just need a clean room in a decent location at a decent price, then this is your place. Otherwise look elsewhere if you want a nice hotel experience.

My husband and I stayed at this hotel over labor day weekend. Room was very small and compact but the location of the hotel is excellent. Not sure I would stay at this particular hotel again though as the room was small for the two of us. We did not have room to even walk beside each other and always felt we were in each other's way. One person had to sit on the bed if the other was doing something else. The a-c was also loud and clicked on every few minutes. Woke my husband up many times during the night. The location of the hotel is great though. It is in the middle of everything!

The area is great and the rooms are fine, but it seemed like every day I was here they opened the pool to the general public and had a party. It meant I couldn't really enjoy it as a paying hotel guest because of the crowds (I wasn't looking for a continuous nightclub atmosphere); and I couldn't really enjoy the room, either, because of the volume-bass level of the music played. 
I don't know if it's just the time I happened to be here- I would recommend calling ahead for their schedule- or whether it's a regular thing, but had I known it was going to be MTV Spring Break ---- before I booked, I'd have stayed elsewhere.

Almost exactly - years ago I stayed at the Serrano Hotel and at that time I found it to be an excellent hotel which is why I chose to return on my recent visit to San Francisco. It is also a part of the Kimpton brand which is a hotel chain I respect. However I found my recent visit somewhat disappointing.
Firstly we booked into the queen room, which I mistakenly thought was the same type of room we had stayed in last time. This was not the case as the room was tiny with barely enough room to walk round the bed (and clearly nowhere to put our two cases). While disappointed by this (and I feel the room was too small to be offered by a prestigious hotel) this would have been far less of a problem if the room was well designed and maintained. The tiny room had large pieces of furniture in it making it even smaller, the large drawer unit containing the mini bar and that the TV stood on was so large that the wardrobe door did not open fully. The door to the room opened straight at the head of the bed (meaning it was noisy and light from under the door was visible when you were in bed) and did not open fully because it hit the night stand. 
Even more annoying was the hotels use of 'nighlight' style light switches in the bedroom. There were two of these located in the main part of the room at mid level directly visible when lying in bed. After trying to sleep with these surprisingly bright lights in my eyes for half a night I got up and used whatever I could (towels and toilet paper) to block the light as best as I could and then I could finally get some rest. It was also extremely frustrating in a world of powered gadgets that there was not a single power socket available in the bedroom (they were all occupied and behind furniture) so my husband and I had to resort to leaving our phones and other electronic equipment to charge in the tiny bathroom, being very careful not to get them wet.
The bathroom was small but again could have been fine if well designed but this was not the case. In particular the toilet was next to the door and but the Toilet paper holder had been placed on the wall on the other side of the room. Whilst the room was small this was just beyond the reach of someone with normal arm length without getting up from the toilet.
I find the decor of the Kimpton hotels general pleasing and cute in a slightly traditional kind of way. However our room had been very badly 'touched up' (I avoid saying renovated). For instance the wood trim was obviously tired and in need of a repaint, instead of sanding back old paint, filling dents and carefully repainting it was clear paint had just been slapped on resulting in paint all over the edge of the wallpaper.
I also felt that the cleanliness of the room was not up to the standard we expected. I found items generally dusty, particularly in the bathroom and dirty wine glasses taken from the wine tasting in the lobby were not cleared from our room.
The lobby of the hotel is however lovely and the check in staff very efficient but I found the wines offered at the wine tasting generally of a poor quality. 
In the morning they offer complimentary tea and coffee but when we were there the only tea on offer was earl grey. When I asked a member of staff if they had green tea he was very helpful and went to check but only came back with English breakfast. I decided to have the English breakfast tea (I needed the caffine after not sleeping) but then there was only half and half or soy milk to put in it. I asked again but was sent to the restaurant next door to ask them for some normal milk. The staff were again very helpful but it made the whole process of making a cup of tea very frustrating and time consuming.
$-- valet parking only. With tips it costs you $-- to park and use your car a couple of times. Room air conditioner was terrible. Room and bathroom were tiny. Staff unfriendly. Do not stay here.

I had a fantastic experience at the Andaz Wall Street. As a Diamond, I have high expectations of Hyatt properties, and my experience has exceeded my expectations across visits. 
From the friendly greeting in the lobby from the staff member who remembered me, to a special upgrade in recognition of my birthday, to friendly and attentive staff at the Wall & Water restaurant (who also remembered me), I have had an excellent experience.
The rooms themselves are big and modern (I had an incredible suite on the most recent stay, but have also had very nice """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""standard"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" rooms), and the location is good downtown. The concept is also great (e.g., free minibar) -- and they had a helpful running map for my --mile run along the East River.
One nit: the complementary Diamond breakfast ($-- credit) needs to be taken in the restaurant, and cannot be applied to room service (unlike the Andaz -th Avenue, for example). 
I am very much looking forward to my next stay.

Normally stay at full-service hotels. Had tix for a show and found a good price on the hilton.com site, we're HH members and the reviews of others on this site gave us encouragement to try their Hamption Inn hotel for a change.
It was clean, well taken care of, friendly staff and had a better then expected breakfast buffet.
Location was perfect - we felt safe walking in the area of the hotel.
Can't beat it for the price.
Will be back.

I stayed recently for a business trip and was seriously impressed. Little touches like a personal note propped up beside the complimentary trio of deserts and bottled water to welcome you when you arrive, and a note under the door to remind guests that the clocks were going back really made the experience of staying there a delight for me. The staff were uniformly professional, helpful, and courteous - I was particularly impressed that they all made an effort to remember my name from the reception staff to the bar and doormen. A brief hold up when I arrived saw me settled in the hotel bar, complimentary drink in hand, while it was dealt with. Quite honestly it ranks as one of the nicest places I've stayed in terms of how fantastic the quality of service was.
My room was small but perfectly proportioned. Bedding was of very good quality, the bathroom was fabulous and I was very pleased to see a Bose sound system in the room. Complimentary bottled water is offered by a knock on the door in the evening and the food that arrived when I ordered room service was very, very good. It is pricey, but absolutely worth it.
I wouldn't hesitate to go back and shall look forward to doing so next time I'm there!

There were several problems with this motel. let me first tell you about the pluses: it was very conveniently located. It is inexpensive for the location.
Now the minuses: poor upkeep, everything looked used, dented, broken, smudged, or dirty. The room was very small, so small that one of ran into the table every time he got up in the night. And worst of all, the carpeting was sticky. When I was getting ready to leave I looked at the soles of my feet, they were black! Unless you have nowhere else to stay, spend the extra ----- dollars and stay in a better place!

I was doubtful when my traveling companion suggested this hotel in times square, but I had an absolutely fantastic time here last week. The hotel is so convenient, with a garage if you need to park, plus all the amenities of a really legit midrange hotel: minibar, huge room and closet, ice machine, bathtub, etc. All if these things are big luxuries in nyc. The hotel's location is bustling with tourists, which isn't everyone's idea of a good time, but that means you can get whatever you need (such as lipstick from sephora or a diet coke from McDonald's) in five minutes in the middle of the night. I loved staying on the --th floor: the view was gorgeous and it was so wonderfully quiet. I did eat in the lounge and the food was good, straightforward but satisfying. I never thought it would be my style to stay in times square but this Hilton has totally changed my mind.

I stayed in this hotel for -.- days with my dog. On the second day after I had been walking him around already for a day half they asked me to leave cuz of my dog!!! Just like the other OMNI's I've stayed at - NY and LA - the Omni Chicago is top notch! The staff was wonderful, and the room was awesome. Very spacious, clean, and comfortable. Plus, I can't say enough about the OMNI pref guest program. Even the restaurant wasn't bad. Plus, the location can't be beat. It's within walking distance of everything!

I booked a trip to New York to celebrate my Wife's birthday. I chose the Edison based on reviews on Expedia. We were delighted with the location of the hotel as it is right on Times square. The Hotel itself has an old world charm not unlike British station hotels such as the Adelphi in Liverpool. I found the staff polite and generally helpful. I contacted guest services prior to arrival to arrange for a bottle of wine in the room. They also left my wife a birthday card and chocolates. I was delighted when they called our room just after we checked in to check that everything was satisfactory which I thought was a nice touch.
We would certainly stay here again.

I could live at this hotel, except for the daily valet fee - if you bring a car. The location is great, you can hop on the light rail only a block away, don't bring your car it is pricey to valet. You can walk to great restaurants, coffee, massage and shopping. The decor is fresh, bright, modern and spotless. A great little free happy hour and the breakfast each morning has something for every taste. Our room was huge, very comfortable for our - night stay. I loved that there was a recycle bin in the room.

Nice environment, great location, had a nice time at the Redwoodroom on Saturday for drinks....velvet room opened up for a Live Concert.....great location....close to shopping big names....close to cablecar,restaurants....rooms are very modern and complete...stayed on the --th floor studio....I highly recommend it.

Beautiful room, view, great staff. Had dinner Friday evening in the restaraunt which was fantastic, and then there was live music which was tasteful and helped make our evening even better. Check out is at noon, not --am like many other places which is nice. Had lunch also when we checked out which was very good too. Will stay here again as soon as we get the chance. Great place for a romantic getaway.

We had the getaway package for - nights. The view of the lake and the bats were great. 
We feel the rooms are way overpriced. The prices are what you might expect in a top-notch convention hotel in Texas.The hotel is within walking distance of fine restaurants. However, you cannot expect complimentary coffee in the lobby. And The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""free"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" breakfast coupons cover only $--. for two persons. The sleep number bed is not a comfortable as you would expect. All in all it is overpriced for an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""old"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel.

You can't really go wrong with the Coventry Motor Inn. Clean spacious rooms, kind staff, great location for Lombard, Chestnut and Union st. It feels more like a hotel than like a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""motor inn"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The one point deducted above is because I was given an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""inner room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", window overlooking a white brick wall for all - nights of my stay! Lucky I was at the top floor so I got just a little daylight. Unsure about lower floors. This is rather depressing to wake up in the morning and all you can see through the window is that wall, a few feet from your window. The hotel management should be aware of that and try to move their guests to other rooms as soon as those become available.
The other rooms I heard people complain about are the rooms closest to the elevator. The doors are not noise proof and there's an ice machine next to the elevator...
Another thing: the rooms don't have a mini fridge, I only discovered when we left I could actually rent one for additional payment.

I did a lot of research before my trip and was a little put off by some of the reviews. Speaking with some locals I decided I'd check it out. How often do you get to stay at the Waldorf Astoria!
I had an amazing time. I opted for the $-- check-in upgrade that was sent to me via e-mail on my online booking and ended up getting a fantastic upgrade to a room with two bathrooms and a sitting room. It made the whole stay that much more comfortable and for only $-- a night!
The restaurants and conference areas were fantastic as well and service staff was friendly and helpful. The rooms and common areas were clean and comfortable. We even took advantage of the Sunday Buffet!
All in all a good trip and I’d stay again.

My husband and I stayed here for our Anniversary trip from April -- - --, ----. It was a wonderful experience beginning to end! This was our -th visit to the Distrikt Hotel, New York City, New York.

Upon checking in at -:-- p.m., Will, at the front desk was so helpful and professional making sure our room was ready for us. With keys, a complimentary continental breakfast coupon and a $-- coupon for food at the Collage Bistro in hand, we took the elevator to the --th floor to Room ----. It was a beautiful King room with a city and river view. Very quiet, super clean! We booked a stay at the Embassy Suites Airport for the BCS National Championship game in January ----. As soon as we turned off the interstate, we knew we had made a mistake. The hotel is in a very run-down area and isn't close to anything that looks even remotely nice.
We did check in and walk up to see the room. Considering the age of the hotel, the room was pretty good. Clean, well-maintained and comfortable. Unfortunately, we couldn't get past the location and opted to check out. The staff was very nice and allowed us to pay the cancellation fee instead of the entire one night's lodging. 
Be sure to do your homework and investigate the location to see if it's something that works for you. If it does, then you will find this hotel to be a clean, reasonable choice.

The Willows hotel is my favorite place to stay when visiting Chicago. It is located in a great neighborhood near the lakefront with a huge selection of Restaurants and shops in walking distance. The hotel is quiet and the rooms are very clean. I find the staff to always be exceptionally kind and helpful which really makes this hotel feel like a home away from home.

A few things have been said in previous reviews about some unfortunate circumstances and I must say that I had experienced some of them during my first stay at the W Dallas. But the place was so suited to my taste that I decided to give them another try and it was well worth the second trip. 
 As an SPG Platinum member, I was placed both times in a “marvelous suite” and this room has got to be among the best of all the W's I've stayed at (and I've stayed at practically every one in the US). In contrast to the stark and cramped early incarnations of W rooms, this suite was extraordinarily spacious, bright, and airy. The gargantuan two-rooms were furnished with ultra comfy velvety sectionals, funky office chairs, and the usual inviting W signature bed. The living room was so huge that it housed a dining room table large enough to accommodate a wedding banquet. Floor to ceiling windows with sweeping city views and streaming sunshine added to the “WoW” factor. Gadgets are the usual for a swanky ultramodern room including extra large plasma TVs and space-age phones. I found the glass-abundant bath room motif chic and stylish but would have to agree with previous reviewers that the layout leaves little privacy for the occupant and even less to the imagination of roommates and service staff. Best extra-room amenity is the very well kept fitness center with, unlike most hotel gyms, actually enough room, weights, and cardio equipment to support a real exercise routine.
 A noticeable improvement the second go-around was the service. Door staff were in abundance but minus the attitude and more forth coming with service. Front desk check-in and out was considerably warmer and more efficient. A couple of minor glitches (phone not working, bottle opener missing) were expeditiously addressed and all the while, a Whatever-Whenever agent kept track of the fixes until issues were resolved. Room service was particularly pleasant and the meal scrumptious.
 All in all a fabulous stay at the W-Dallas that I hope I can experience again in the near future.

My mom and I stayed for - nights in late July. Our room was very clean, the staff friendly, all spoke great English! Overall, we would definitely stay again and recommend this hotel to our friends and family!

This place was awesome!

I think this will be one of my new go to hotels in the DC area! Location is awesome, right across the street from the metro and pretty central to any sightseeing you want to do if that's your thing.

I've read some of the poor reviews and I can't agree. Then again, I stayed in a Jr. Suite...so I'm not sure how much difference there is from the standard room. Having lived here all of my life, I'm glad I got to see the city from this room on the --th floor.

Tree at front desk was up on her customer service and made stay a pleasure. I ask for unusual information and she called me within - minutes with answer

This was the second time that we have stayed at the Warwick in Seattle and both times it has been exceptional. The people are the best and the hotel is one of the cleanest we have ever stayed in

Boutique, cosy. Actually tired and small. Staff were great but gave us poor advice about where to eat. Don't eat locally - go right out of the door and second right down Stockton where there are loads of quality places to eat. 
Location of Boheme is great. We walked to Union Square through China town and it's an easy walk to Peir -- too. Just don't go left and left again unless you want a smutty style experience.

I spent one night here for a business trip. I arrived late and was excited at check in to find out that I had been upgraded to a parlor suite. Front desk staff friendly. Lobby pretty but room was horrible. Carpet dingy and stained. Couch in the room was an old plaid pattern and was very worn. Lighting was not good. Carpet so dingy I did not want to walk barefoot. The hotel was right by Penn Station and Madison Square Gardens. It was about -- blocks from Times Square (easy walking). The hotel is old and our room was very small. New beds, central ac-heat, and flat screen tv. The tub and tile in the bathoom was old and simply painted over. If you don't mind a smaller room I would recommend.

My husband and I stayed at the Holiday Inn for - nights while attending a conference in Seattle. For $-- more we decided to book a suite with a separate bedroom which was great. I had to get up early for the conference and could do so and get ready in the morning without waking him up. The bedroom had a King bed and its own TV, also nice in the evening when we each wanted to watch something different.
The main room had a sofa, large TV, computer desk, and small kitchen area with sink, fridge, and microwave so very handy if you wanted to bring snacks or juice-food into your room, great for a quck bite. There was also a working coffee maker, iron, and blow dryer which are big necessities for me and must haves when i travel for business. Internet was included in the price of the room which enabled me to keep in touch with my office.
We were on the top floor (-th) and was really quiet ~ I only heard other people coming and going a few times so would have to say i had a really good sleep both nights. The bed was comfortable and the bathroom spotless. 
My conference was at the Bell Harbour Convention centre so within a few mintues drive with parking at the Art Institute across the street. I paid way more for parking at the AI while at the convention center, so really apppreciated the cheap rate at the Holiday Inn for $-- per night. One day i took a cab to the convention centre, cost $-.-- so not an astronomical amount or distance. 
We were given a $-- voucher for breakfast at the Emerald Grill restaurant next door, my husband actually used it without problem and had a good breakfast.We also ate dinner there and appreciated that we could basically take a few steps for a meal that was very good without having to really go anywhere. There is a workout room at the hotel which I did not use, but my husband did. He found the faciliites very basic and room a little small, but it is adequate for a quick workout. 
The hotel itself is a short drive to Pike place and other sites in Seatlle. we did not have much time to do site seeing but did take a drive through the downtown area. I would be happy to stay here again and would recommend it. Its not fancy but very clean and comfortable and a decent price. Staff were great and check-in and out which really contributes to a good stay.

Stayed here for three nights this week for business. The hotel is very nice, very clean, and in a good location. It is on the Riverwalk and close to many good restaurants. It is also a short walk from the Rivercenter Mall and the Convention Center. The hotel was packed as there were several conferences in town as well as the height of tourist season and Dallas Cowboys Training Camp. Despite the crowds and at times hurried guests, every employee that I interacted with was friendly, helpful, and professional. The valets were as busy as I've ever seen and being well over --- degrees they had to be terribly hot but they were smiling and very polite. The only drawbacks were that I could hear the people in the room next door talking and laughing and I could hear guests in the hallways returning to their rooms late at night. I also wish they had free internet access in the guest rooms. The only breakfast served is in the restaurant - we chose to head to Sip Cafe a few blocks down for a quick and tasty breakfast.

We booked this as it had good reviews, well they were right!
We were a little hesitant as there was some possible noise from the Hospital nearby and to be honest we thought the price was very cheap.
BUT WOW. It was fantastic value, the night we got there the kids jumped straight in the pool and there was complimentary beer, wine, nachos and snacks! 
In the morning there was complimentary breakfast, now we have stayed at some hotels in the past which offered this and didnt have high expectations, however, another WOW, there was fresh fruit, juices, bagels, waffles and more! Fantastic.
Outside there was BBQs by the pool. So in the evening we had a couple of complimentary beers, nachos and popcorn while we cooked our BBQ and the kids swam in the pool!
Excellent base to travel from, easy access to Balboa Park and San Diego Zoo. We spent - nights here and could have stayed longer. The border shopping centres were only --mins away.

I have stayed in many hotels in San Diego over the years and the Homewood Suites San Diego-Del Mar was the best hotel I've ever stayed in! My spouse and I stayed overnight in the One-Bedroom King Suite and it was not only spacious, but also extremely quiet. The breakfast in the morning was delicious. Just stayed at Jurys for Boston marathon last weekend. Perfect hotel to stay if your running. Staff was very helpful and location was just what I was looking for. We at downstairs for lunch twice and I was very pleased with the food. We've stayed at the Ritz Carlton and Four Seasons in the past. I will be staying at Jury's from now on. Bed was extreamly comfortable, flat screen tv, huge glassed in shower, towel heater, and great service. Room wasn't huge but it was comfortable. They actually impressed me!

The one bedroom suite was perfect for our family with - teens. The bathroom was huge, the decor made the place feel like we were staying in someones guest room in a home, which was a good thing. The bed was very comfortable. It was a short walk downhill to get to Union Square and the hotel is located on a somewhat more residental street although still just around the corner from shopping, Chinatown and many choices of restaurants nearby.
The lobby is small, breakfast in the restaurant was good, all in all a good experience.
Thanks to the Opal my husband and I have now brought bed bugs into our house. It has been a very stressful and costly lesson to us. Please be aware of the risks of bed bugs when staying at the Opal.

I stayed at pod -- for - nights in late September in the twin room. Very clean hotel and room was well laid out. Grand Central Station is just two streets away, which was very convenient. Coffee and tea in the lobby was a nice touch for a budget hotel. Will definitely return!

We were pleasantly surprised by the quality of the rooms but beyond that we were assisted by Todd, at the front desk with a wireless problem. He spent a lot of time fixing the problem and went way above what we expected.....nice job Todd!!!!!

We stayed for - nights and really thought that this should be rated as a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""-"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" star not a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""-"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" star. In the middle of downtown. Convinient to many restaurants as well as the convention center. Easy to walk to many different places.

The hotel itself was very nice. The room was fine althou a bit small but 
hey its new york . I booked a studio through a Travelzoo for $-- a night and half off parking during your stay. Upon arrival, I was pleasantly surprised to find out that the hotel was in the middle of Georgetown, only a few steps from all the dining and shopping, and the waterfront! The front desk was extremely helpful, upgrading me to a one bedroom upon learning it was my first visit to GS. They also gave me several excellent restaurant suggestions (Sea Catch!). Although the elevators are a little slow, the room more than made up for it! The one bedroom has a full kitchen, HUGE walk-in closet in the entryway ( seriously could be another bedroom!), a spacious living and dining area with two couches, dining room table and flat screen TV. This came in handy when I wanted to sleep but my other half wanted to watch sports! There is a good sizes double vanity bathroom with above average shampoo, soap, etc. The bedroom is separate with plenty of space for storage and a delightfully comfortable bed and another flat screen. There are plenty of windows to allow natural light in to make it feel more comfortable. In the morning, we were able to take advantage of the free breakfast before heading to the game, which is more than your typical cereal and Danishes. We ate a hearty egg and bacon biscuit, but they had a good selection (even at ten o'clock!). Although the metro is a good walk, it's not unbearable. The room service was prompt and detailed. The only negative that I can mention is that there was construction going on outside our window, so we were woken up by beeping trucks fairly early during the week, but really, you will get that type of noise in any hotel located on the main drag.
Overall, will definitely consider staying here again when visiting DC!

Rising well above the Indy skyline sits a glass beauty, modern, impressive and inviting. The rooms itself are nice, modern and many have fantastic views. They feature modern amenities and style that you typically don't see in Marriott properties. Feels a bit downscale for such a nice place, but everything else is solid. The beds are firm, typical of Marriott. I am not a fan but I know some like a super firm bed so it works for them. 
Service is good, for a Marriott. It could be better, again not as good as less expensive Westin properties I have stayed in, but good for Marriott (which is typically poor, rude and unaccommodating in my experience).
If you are in town for business (or pleasure) I would say this is hands down the best option in town.

We had a great time here. On first arriving our room was not ready so we were upgraded into a larger room. The staff were fantastic and always so friendly and helpful. The apartments were great although the kitchen could be better stocked with utensils etc. This hotel is in a great location within walking distance to many popular tourist attractions. We would definitely return.

Why stay at this Hilton? Convenience pretty much, if you need to be downtown. The rooms are clean, decent size, but nothing fancy. Furniture is pretty much Ikea-like. There is a gym with basic equipment, and an indoor pool.

In town for a mega-convention (---- nurses!) at the Convention Center which was just across the street from the Hyatt. Got cheated out of a proper holiday this year so spent for three nights at the Hudson what we'd normally spend on a week. Great weekend but the Hudson was AWFUL -- the biggest disappointment in a very rich travel life. For almost $--- per night, we got a tiny room with no bathtub and a dark non-view of the courtyard. 
A former New Yorker had recommended the Hudson based on the chic lobby and bar, which is all you should bother seeing. For all the vaunted design touches, they all-too-often fail in the function department. 
The funky lamps in our room were too dim to illuminate a space only four feet wider than the bed. In the equally dim elevators, the floor numbers are brass on brass and people had to get down and squint to see which button to push. Our room had no dresser -- just an inconveniently high cubby hole from which you had to pull down all the items to find the one you wanted. 
Also, the air in our room was painfully dry -- like being on an airplane -- so much so that my upper lip swelled up!
My sister spent similar cash at the Tribeca Grand this fall and her experience was much, much better. Go to the Hudson to look around the eye-catching lobby, buy an over-priced cocktail in the bar so you can scan for stars, then go somewhere with value for money to rest your head for the night.
Only the location was good.
p.s. Not to cast aspersions, but I find the raves about this hotel highly suspect, unless the posters are rich and can afford a bigger room.
