My room was situated at the front of the building on the --th floor. I was greeted kindly by the reception and with nice (not artificial) smiles for the rest of my stay. They really are very professional and friendly in this hotel. It feels more like a boutique hotel than a chain. And as for the location - to say it is fantastically situated would be an understatement! The subway is next to the hotel - literally. The drugstore next door - Duane Reade is cheap, big and open -- hours. And if you don't find what you want there (which would surprise me), there is a -- hour CVS drugstore one block down on Lexington avenue. There are numerous -- hour eateries in the area (we're talking one or two blocks away from the hotel). Shopping-wise (my main hobby), you have lexington avenue just behind the hotel, then (in order) Park Avenue, then Madison Avneue, then Fifth avenue - the latter is a five minute walk tops (and believe me, when you're laden with shopping bags like I was - you don't underestimate distance)! It is a five minute walk down Lexington avenue to Grand Central Station. And if you don't like walking (which I don't), the subway takes you directly to Times Square (five minutes), --th street and Penn Station (-- minutes), and the centre of Soho (-- minutes) - and a whole host of other places, and that's just line 'E'!!! You are close enough to the action to be able to pop back to the hotel for a break and a coffee during shopping or sightseeing trips, but not so close that you can't escape the crowds. I was seriously impressed with this hotel. For what it lacks in fantasy, it makes up for in service, comfort, amenities, location, price... and everything else! Thankyou to the entire staff for a wonderful stay. You make this hotel what it is.

Stayed at the Sofitel for my wedding night and I must say the room we had was wonderful. We had a Jr. Suite which was not much more than the regular room. Everything about the room was great. The only complaint I would have is that the shower pressure was very weak. But I'm glad I chose this hotel for my wedding night. If you're looking for a first class hotel in a great section of the city, I would say give the Sofitel a shot.

The hotel is perfectly placed in the middle of Manhattan. A good place if you have business in the area, and close to the subway if you want to get fast around. It is clearly a business hotel. Nothing fancy or romantic. It is fuctional, has spacious rooms (should be at this price!), is quiet, clean and everything works. There is free internet with enough bandwith. The breakfast buffet is absolutely boring and tasteless. The free coffee and tea bar is a great thing when you get home at night. The staff is wilingly doing their job - but at no time enthusiastic or smiling. So nothing really wrong - but then again nothing really exiting. I will use it again if I have meetings close by. - the only thing that really was somewhat stupid is the rule that the HHonors point do not apply when you have booked through an agent.

There was a man directly above us hitting his child and she was screaming her head off. We could everything clear as a bell through the vents. I called down to the front desk - times and still nothing (even thought she kept promising security was on their way up). Finally I went down with my phone in my hand and threatened to call the police if security did not go up-the security guard knew nothing about it.
There is internet-but only in non-smoking rooms. Hotel stunk. Like chlorine and garbage, In the room, hallways and lobby. Neighborhood is awful and you have to drive to the beach. Workers were just shy of rude-not helpful or friendly at all, and they moved incredibly slooooow. Plus its pretty shabby looking. Just not worth it at all.

Average all of the reviews, and you have things about right. My bet is that some rooms are really good...others not so. We just returned from a weekend in Chicago to see the sights. Bought the Go Chicago card, and used the Grey Line hop on - hop off to get around. We had a standard king room in the south tower on the --th floor, and observations are as follows:

The 'Could be better""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""

Would I recommend it? If you are on a budget, only need a place to sleep, and plan to be outside most of the time...then yeah.

Good hotel, out of the harbour front area, but in -- min wals to Pike Market and shops and monorail only ---- mins. Take the short walking tour if possible it shows you the centre and gives you a good taste of Seattle's sights.

Stayed for my birthday with my husband and friends. Our welcome on arrival was warm and our rooms were as expected. The bed was one of the most comfortable I have ever stayed in. The brekfasts were very good and the on tap coffee, soft drinks and cakes was excellent, as was the wine and cheese each evening. All the staff go out of their way to be helpful and make you feel special.
 Make sure you get a new york pass, not a new york city pass to get you into sights free and to fasttrack you through. The hop on and hop off buses are great but bear in mind each circular route takes about --- hours, with the downtown route being the most useful. If you get a chance to see a show, Sister Act is fantastic!
 Would definitely return to the Casablanca if we visit New York again.

Had a few nights here as part of a family birthday-anniversary trip(including LA and Hawaii).Hotel staff are really helpfull and friendly and the small things such as 'on tap' tea & coffee at reception and umberellas(it rained very hard a couple of nights) do really make a difference - the rooms are fine , very comfy and as the hotel is not massive (but is tall) you dont wait hours for the lift and the views (high up) are fantastic.
Short walk to Times Sq and easy to get everywhere(they also sent me a birthday cake :) )

Simply my favorite hotel in the area. Next door’s Hilton Garden Inn, which offers a decent dinner and it is just across the Homewood Suites parking lot (they share). The breakfast at Homewood is substantial, the coffee decent and the rooms are spotless.

Within minutes of major San Diego attractions and San Diego State University, but not “too close” if that makes sense. So free parking, not overloaded with people. My preference, may not be yours.
Nice hotel close to the river walk. We would stay again.

We decided to take a last-minute trip for Thanksgiving, and wanted to be comfortable for our family of - without spending too much. With the suites, free breakfast, and manager's reception (free drinks!) nightly this place covered it all.

I could move to my choice of properties in the Chicago area but choose to stay where I am at the Residence Inn. I use them this trip and any future trips to Chicago I know where I will be staying!

When I was there, there seemed to be some plumbing issues. There were some clear bang sounds coming from the tubes around - am on the first night, then a hot water problem on the next morning, and then a night with much less noise and better water heat.

Toilet rocked, water to toilet ran almost non stop; bathroom door didn't shut -out of alignment by over - inch, once you managed to get it shut it woke everyone up trying to get out; tub very slow to drain - well over ankle deep by end of fast shower. I’ll never stay here again and will book any other company but Hampton from now on.

We stayed here for three nights. The room was spacious and very comfortable. Staff was very helpful in trying to help us locate a nearby church.

Excellent in every way, staff, location, cleanliness, room size, comfortable bed & bathroom. We had - women in one rm w-- dbl beds, more than enough room for us to move around & ALL of our stuff. When I arrived at the Peninsula after the usual traffic filled ride from O'Hare, I was completedly frazzled and must have shown it. This hotel is in a great location very close to many historical sites, including the White House. We usually walked from our hotel to many of the sites and felt very safe. The lobby and lounge are beautiful. Our favorite aspect of this hotel was its lovely French food. Breakfast was a sheer pleasure. The guestrooms are spacious and the housekeeping staff very professional and pleasant. I read this hotel's great reviews on TripAdvisor and was equally pleased with our stay.

All in all great stay.

Place was under renovation and had this really beat and worn down feel to it. Renovation areas werent covered, floors were uneven, stained carpets, and the rooms werent very clean either. Very old, tired look. On the plus side check in - out services were speedy and we got free wifi.

The Marriott staff was awesome and did everything they could to accommodate me. They had the fastest room service I've ever seen and the food was delicious. Aside from the check-in staff, the employees were top notch all the way.
The beds were very comfortable and the room furnishings were up-to-date and clean. Internet worked flawlessly and was quite fast.
The valet was terrible and didn't even leave his little podium to greet me or the gentlemen that pulled up behind me. After a while we both got out, unloaded our own luggage and traipsed over to the valet. He might have wanted us to park our own cars? The parking fee (self-park or valet) at this property is totally unjustified, they have more than enough land and its not as though its any where near downtown or the ocean. Another sad Marriott add-on just like charging for their internet service daily.
Check-in was unreasonably slow considering there were - staff members and only - other people checking in. The first set of keys that I got didn't work and after lugging --- lbs of luggage back down to get a set that did work, no one even offered to assist me going back up.

Rooms clean and tidy..good location..value for money. I was greeted by very helpful young Indian boy..he couldn't have been more helpful and happy to have you stay...however the next morning in reception I encountered a young Indian girl that was rude and sarcastic! ,

Even though I have stayed there before and am a platinum elite status I was barely greeted, and acknowledged, on arrival: “no upgrade, lucky we have room for you -- minutes before checking time of -pm on a Saturday night in August.” 
 So my cubicle next to the elevators and storage room with one jail like window was sleep able but barely breathable and certainly not enjoyable. Think college dorm size-rate. And I do visit NYC often, btw so I know NYC rooms. I did call mgr. to ask for a re-do, but he essentially said we are busy, go away. So I did. I had my son arrive the next day, and my son checked in under my name next day and they charged me $-- more than the room rate I was registered for, so when I came home I had to fix all that.

Worst hotel experience I have ever had. Filthy carpet, furniture and bathroom. Every corner of this room was covered in stains of Lord only knows what. typical marriot, clean tidy, good staff and expensive to eat and drink.

pool was a nice surprise lovely and warm although we did not see the pool boy so had to go in to order drinks
pity marriot charge for internet access, all the budget hotels give it free now, i ended up in starbucks to update our blogg

The purpose of this trip was to visit Loyola which was less than -- miles away. Having stayed at the Inner Harbor area in the past we felt more at ease staying there than in an area of Baltimore that may not be as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""good"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Rates for hotels in the area run high so I went on Priceline and secured this hotel at a very attractive $--.-- per night. Checking in was a breeze. They honored my requested for double beds and allowed - in the room, no problem. 
Parking is $--.-- per DAY. Once the ticket has been validated by the front desk you are able to take the car in and out of the garage all day with no additional charge. 
The room was not the biggest Marriott hotel room I have been in, however we had - queen size beds, a desk with free wireless high speed internet, coffee service, flat screen tv etc. The beds were extremely comfortable, and not a bed bug in sight. (of course I checked, I'm from NY)
Once we were settled in, we had no problem finding a cab to the Inner Harbor which is -- blocks away. It was late afternoon, I have MS, and different legs at different times of day, lol, so we chose a cab. It was $-.-- with tip. Once there we were able to walk around the Harbor, and hopped another cab to Fells Point which took less than -- minutes and $-.-- from the Inner Harbor. 
Fells Point was great. A bag piper was playing on the steps of town square to serenade people on and off the water taxis from the Inner Harbor. An Orioles double header had been in full swing, cheers and jeers bursting out of the bars as we walked by. Fells Point is a young, urban area, with a decidedly historic feel. Great little shops, restaurants, and bars galore. 
We hailed another cab back (legs) to the hotel to pick up my daughter who had been sleeping soundly behind our double locked doors AND the key card enabled locked glass doors that block entrance to the hotel rooms unless you have a key to that hallway! Nice touch Marriott! That cab ride was approx $--.-- for the longer ride to Camden Yards. Still reasonable! (My husband says he should have taken out the car...of course, Dear) 
Finally, we went back to the Inner Harbor for dinner at Phillips Restaurant for Crab Cakes etc. They were good. The service was great. My daughter was developing a sinus infection. Our server went out into the food court and BOUGHT her Tylenol with her own money. That was above and beyond and very much appreciated. 
Once we checked out this morning, enjoyed breakfast at the hotel restaurant. Actually, I did not want their breakfast buffet, but from the moment we walked in - people asked or suggested that we would be having the buffet. By the time the waitress came over to pour the coffee and hand us the menus, she said, """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" we have the breakfast buffet""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""....and I said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""which I guess everyone wants us to choose vs ordering from the menu?"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and she explained that you can't possibly get this much food for $--.-- anywhere, and it's so good. Guess what we ordered???? 
And you know what? I ordered - eggs over easy. And they were the best eggs I have had out ever. They had biscuts in a beef gravy...I can't begin to describe how delicious that was. My husband had french toast that I could smell as I walked up to the table. He ate every last bite. This was the kind of buffet you hope for but NEVER find. Well, now you know, it's at the Marriott Camden Yards!!!! Shhhh don't tell anyone... 
One last note, some other reviewers knocked the service at this hotel. That was not our experience at all. And let me tell you, I ask for directions everywhere, for everything. And I forget alot of things. Well, you get the picture. I come in contact with a lot of people. They were always very courteous, helpful, wrote directions for us more than once, printed tickets, arranged for wake up calls, and really extended themselves on every level. 
Bravo Camden Marriott! You clearly value your patrons and we value you! 
The bathroom was spotless.

I would have given this hotel a - out of - but the pool situation made me so angry that I must drop it to a -. 
If you are coming here and thinking of going swimming on the week-end think twice about going there. This hotel either rents out its space or they don't actually have a swimming pool. We originally booked a room with two beds for a girls weekend at $----night. Seven days before we were scheduled to arrive, our trip plans had to change. As a result, we cancelled that reservation. It appears to me that the renovations have been done on the less expensive side and that they're reusing as much of the existing materials as possible. While I appreciate the attempt at this, much of the wood work wasn't stripped or sanded prior to painting and any wood work that was rotting or water damaged previously was simply painted and reused. If I were the management of Milford Plaza I would be upset with the work of the shotty contractors - paint dripped on the new carpet, globs of paint dripping down the walls that was never cleaned up, holes for the shower weren't aligned with the faucet, door knobs poorly reinstalled - just a few examples of what we saw in our room. Whether it was previous water damage or nicotine from a previously smoking room - when the ceiling and wood trim was covered in steam (from the shower) - yellow beads of water would trip from the white and gray paint. Had we paid the original price - I would have been extremely dissatisfied with my overall experience and the hotel.

We recently stayed at this hotel for just one night after arriving into Phoenix on a late flight from the east coast. The hotel isn’t too far from the airport, but it is probably three miles or so from it. Airport hotels in Phoenix aren’t clustered right around the airport like they are in some other cities, so be aware of this. We had printed directions ahead of time, but especially at night, coming from the rental car center, we wouldn’t have known where to go otherwise. 
The hotel is generally pretty nice. We’ve stayed at better and worse Marriotts in the past. The hotel is perched right at the intersection of a couple highways, so I’d recommend requesting a room away from the highway if you’re worried about noise. We were given a room on the side away from the highway and had a nice view facing Scottsdale and Camelback Mountain. 
The hotel itself is nice enough. The lobby is nice, and the grounds are well manicured with free parking. The rooms are a decent size, and ours was clean. The room décor is a little outdated, a sort of southwestern motif. There have been updates made to the rooms, such as the new Marriott bedding. It was the light fixtures, furniture, etc. that looked outdated. A full renovation of our room had not been completed, and the same goes for the hallways. 
Otherwise, we didn’t really see anything remarkable about this hotel. It served perfectly well for a quick night by the airport before moving on to the Grand Canyon. I wouldn’t stay here for a vacation. 
In terms of things in the area around the hotel, I don’t think there was much within walking distance. A couple minutes drive up the road will get you to some grocery stores, Target, and chain restaurants. The area generally looked safe, but not fancy. I think it’s a perfectly acceptable place to stay for a night near PHX.

This was a quirky place that we ended up staying last minute due to our flight home being cancelled. We were intrigued by the charming historical value of the place. The place really is fascinating as a gallery of antiques and curiosities, however we arrived on a Saturday night, only to be told (apologetically) that the elevator was out of service and we would be staying on the -th floor. I was - months (visibly) pregnant and we were surprised that there was no offer to help carry our bags up to the room. When we got there, the bed only had two flat pillows and the mattress was quite firm. We called down to the desk to ask for more pillows and were told (apologetically) that there was only one person working in the hotel (?!) and that was the person we were speaking to at the front desk, so if we wanted pillows we would have to walk back downstairs (- flights) in order to pick them up ourselves. Totally understandable that they couldn't leave the front desk unattended, not understandable that there was no other staff to take care of this. As you might imagine from the fact that there are - floors, this is not a small B&B but a full scale hotel.
The whole place kind of gave me the creeps, I didn't sleep well, worried that while neat in the daylight, is kind of akin to something out of a horror movie at night. The room linens were shabby and thin. The towels seemed more like dish cloth material than towel material. Not sure what was going on with this place overall. 
Breakfast was mediocre, basic chain hotel type spread. Wifi did not work on the -th floor...Lobby is a nice place to sit, but not practical overall. Parking was inexpensive and near by.
front desk was helpful. Good location.

Years ago, The Colonnade was a great hotel. When a conference I was attending included it among its listings, I did not hesitate to book a room here. Just before the trip, I checked TripAdvisor reviews and was alarmed to see a rash of negative reports, mainly citing ongoing construction. I sent an e-mail to the hotel and received reassurance from the director of rooms that I would be assigned a room well-away from the construction zone. Well, I was, but that was all you could say about the room. In contrast to previous stays, it was small, dark and very worn out. The sheets were thin, showing through to a double-sized mattress pad turned sideways on a king-size bed and the thin blanket was totally pilled with its satin lining in shreds. Curtain liners were unraveling.. You get the picture, not anywhere near a --star hotel. Guestroom WiFi is contracted out to Guestlinx and is quite expensive - $--.-- for --days. It worked the first night, then the entire system went down; I spent a long time dealing with the outsourced automated system before getting to a human being in India or somewhere on a connection so bad he could not hear me and hung up. I had to start over. again, not --star service. The shower head was cheesy and water pressure was uneven. Noise from the hallway (near the elevator) came right into the room, worst of all was the last morning at - AM I was subjected to loud yelling and swearing in the hall. Although the staff was very nice and breakfast at Brasserie Jo quite nice, I would not consider returning to The Colonnade. There are too many other better options in Boston. Even though I e-mailed the director of rooms my displeasure during my stay, I heard back nothing, and no compensation was offered me when upon checkout I replied in the negative to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""was everything OK?"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I am sorry to add a negative review, as this was an old sentimental favorite, but there were just too many things wrong to retain my former loyalty. Look elsewhere.

We just spent - nights at the Washington Court Hotel, our second time back to D.C. We wanted a place with a great location near our planned attractions (official buildings, the Mall, and museums) and also close to the Metro. This location satisfies both of those quite well. Walking distance to Senate office buildings-Capitol-Supreme Court, where we had plans while we were there; Mall is close by too. And taxis are abundant, and the rates are very reasonable. We wound up using the Metro only once, via Union Station, a short walk away. Very accessible location for getting around by foot. The Capitol area nearby is gorgeous, with parks, flowers, shade trees and benches - very welcoming. 
I also really wanted a view, and we got it. We booked through Destination DC and got an Executive King for about $----night, plus tax and fees and all that. I called the hotel directly after I made my reservation, and made my view request clear, and we got a room with a great view of the Capitol building. Although there are three other hotels in very close proximity to this one, The Washington Court is the only one high enough (-- stories) to afford you that view. You will need a room high enough to get it, so ask away AND don't expect the cheapest rooms to get you a view (they will be on the lower floors). I paid a little extra and got what was important to me. Also in D.C., room rates go down as you approach the weekend, so plan your dates accordingly and the rates will even out to a decent rate. 
The room: Nice, roomy, basic enough, a little """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""moderne"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in styling for my tastes but comfortable in every way. King bed, down comforter. There were a few shabby spots -- like the door to the room looks like it has water damage (water?) and the closet rods are beat up. I don't ever expect to see anything looking beat up in a good hotel, so this was a detraction and distraction from any otherwise very good room. SUPER quiet. We rested very well here from our long walks around town!
The bathroom, however, was d-e-l-u-x-e. They spent all the extra money in there! It's B-I-G and the shower is even bigger!! Two shower heads, roomy enough for - people (I don't suggest that, just giving an idea of size). Nice lighting, plenty of mirrors and shelf space. Really a very special bathroom. Extra points for this.
Two closets - again, extra points, even with those beat-up closet rods. Plenty of room for all our stuff.
Wound up ordering room service every day, whether for lunch, dinner or breakfast (love that order card that you leave on the door by midnight for service the next morning). Delivery timing was good, but - out of - breakfasts were missing something that we ordered. Sometimes got a newspaper, sometimes did not. So room service gets an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""uneven"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" mark from me. Food quality was very good throughout our stay, however. Breakfast was always good. For lunch-dinner, we sampled delish soup, best buffalo chicken wings we've had in a long time, and the hotel makes excellent burgers.
Ate downstairs in the very attractive atrium restaurant once, for lunch. Nouvelle American cuisine, very good food and looked great on the plate. Lots of effort there.
Doormen were terrific - we thoroughly enjoyed Sam, who feeds the sparrows by hand, and Tyrone, who loves his cats. Also think I met Justin (on a Wednesday afternoon) who was very helpful and I'm sorry to be unsure of his name. These gents were wonderful; kind and helpful to all, gracious, and they make a great first impression.
We were disappointed by neighborhood restaurants. Hyatt for dinner one night - extremely salty food and very expensive, and everything is a la carte. Tried to go to the Dubliner around the corner, but after -- minutes, no one had come to our table (and they seated us practically on top of other people, on both sides; very uncomfortable) so we got up and left. Went next door to Kelly's Irish Times -- eesh, don't bother. Not for food; it's a bar that also happens to serve food that's not very good. And it was dirty. Ick. You can also head up to Union Station for food, but the atmosphere of a busy train station with the smell of exhaust and a noisy P.A. system shouting all the time just doesn't lend itself to fine dining. Took a cab to Old Ebbitt Grill and had a splendid meal at a reasonable price, so get out of the neighborhood to eat if you don't eat in the hotel itself. This was the only real drawback to the location of this hotel. 
Sorry to go on and on, but I rely extensively on Tripadvisor reviews when I travel, and feel I owe it to others to give as much detail as possible. We would definitely return to this hotel due to its prime location, the splendid view, comfort of the hotel amenities, and good room service food.

I live in NYC. I chose this hotel for the convenience & the cost. My daughter is in elementary school & I took her for a night in """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The City"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". It was all good. here's the details... 
Small hotel, tiny room, cool NYC vibe & great location. The only drawback is that this hotel is dimly lit on purpose. Dark hallways, elevator, etc... 
Keep in mind that this is a good review! When being a tourist in Manhattan nothing is affordable, easy to do or obvious. Therefore I chose a simple route. 
Most of us stay in a big city to SEE the big city. Across the street is Central Park, Time Warner's trendy shopping center, & the Upper West Side is right there! 
If you come to Manhattan looking for something """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Wow & Fabulous"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", go to the generic Times Square hotels w- a view of the large neon signs & tons of people for lots of money.
This lovely little hotel is for those of us looking for a comfortable & simple vacation. Sleep well & off you go to explore!

The pricing was excellent. However, the cleanliness was below standard. The mirrors were smudged, we could see finger prints and smudges everywhere we went. The sheets were were not fitted properly on the beds and when we weak up in the mornings the sheets would be half way on the beds. The rooms had a foul odor. Breakfast was good. The hotel staff was very helpful and professional.

This hotel is - minutes from LAX but very quiet. Beds are comfortable and room is clean. Hallways could use a little updating but the lobby was very nice. There is an internet cafe with complimentary computers, internet and Wi-Fi in the lobby. But you have to pay for in room Wi-Fi. The shuttle is fast and so was check-in. All in all good airport hotel.

The Colonnade Hotel is beautiful, in a great location, and has a fabulous restaurant. The rooms are luxuriously appointed, immaculate & very comfortable. The staff is very committed to the comfort of their guests, and are all very friendly & accommodating. I will definitely stay at this hotel again!

Country inn & Suites in Denver was my temp home for a couple of weeks for business. It was a very pleasant stay with no problems. Rooms were spacious and clean, bed was very comfortable. Front desk agents very friendly and warm, especially Troi! I appreciated the compliementary hot breakfast and they offered free snacks and beverages at all times. Shuttle service was to-from airport was effiecent and drivers were friendly, especially Rob!

Went with my wife to see Jame Taylor and Carol King at Wachovia Center. Stayed here to ramp it up a notch. The rate with a $!)) meal credit made it a steal>
service tatrted with an e mail from the concierge> he was helpful in arranging transportation and dineing reservations prior to check in>

stayed here for four nights in an historic room with my wife and twenty year old daughter.while the staff were nice and hotel facilities were also nice we just could not get passed the fact that the rooms were too small, and the bathroom far too small and not practical at all. we also could here all the street nosie and were unable to get any quality sleep,suggest they sound proof these rooms better..On a good note the hotel is in a good position to resturants and shops.

The location itself was great, the rooms were spacious but i must admit they smelled a little like mildew, not sure if that was just our room tho, so i will only minus one star for that, other than that the staff was super friendly and the location was great

I was initially worried because some of the negative reviews. We stayed here for two nights on a recent getaway to NYC and couldn't have been happier.
-. Atmosphere - this hotel is beautiful. From the carved wood in the elevators to the marble fireplace in my room (which I thought about trying to sneak out in my suitcase) to the mosaics in the lobby entryway, I loved it. To those who say it is """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""dated,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I say go stay at a cookie cutter hotel that looks the same wherever you go!

-. Room Service - pricey, but hey this is NYC.

-. WiFi - we need to stay in touch with our jobs. I wish that the wi-wfi (in a hotel of that caliber) was free. As I was buying bottles of champagne at $--- a pop, one would think that internet access would be provided!

I had read some of the previous reviews and was not sure what to expect. Flatotel exceeded any expectations!! Clean, Warm, Comfortable, with friendly helpful and VERY courteous Staff. Just a couple of downsides - on arrival we had to wait for one of our rooms (we had booked - in total) - but it was worth it to get an upgrade!! once we got in to our rooms we needed an extra bedsheet and extra duvet - lets face it, this is a HUGE hotel - these were brought up within minutes - excellent service. When we were leaving, we were able to leave our luggage safely in a secure room so we could enjoy our last morning in New York. Overall I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone - we certainly will be back!!!

I had a wonderful time while in Denver staying at the Quality Inn. It is not in the center of the downtown area, nor is it out near the airport. However, they make up for this with their shuttle service, which will take you to a lot of different destinations within about a - mile radius. This included the --th St Mall, the Colorado Convention Center, stadiums, etc. They leave on the hour, and you just have to call and they will pick you up on the next run. Staff is super friendly, including the shuttle drivers, and a few that I remember fro the front desk are Patricia, Yvonne, Teresa, and a couple others that I did not get their name. Great breakfast and Betty visits your table to see if everything is OK. I would stay here again with no hesitation. Their prices are great!!

The beds were incredible. I actually purchased the pillows from the Marriott site after this visit. The bar was great and the ambiance was very nice. The only thing weird about the stay was the voice for the elevator. It sounded like the person was from long island which made me laugh every time I was on it. The staff was very nice and seemed to know their frequent guests which I find very informative. I travel for business frequently and I appreciate it when the staff goes out of their way for you. This hotel is newer and has balconies so make sure you get a room with one.

I do agree that the decorations are a bit bla. However, the location and cleanliness of the hotel more than make up for what it is lacking in interior design. The bed is also extremely comfortable and the L'Occitane amenities are a magnificent touch. I have been known as a very picky traveler and I would recommend the Commonwealth to anyone. This hotel is spotless!!

Just returned from celebrating an anniversary in town...just wanted to get away for the night so hopped on the subway to go to this hotel. I'd been here for parties before for parties but never stayed the night. 
Upon arrival, were told by the employee at the front desk that the room we reserved would not be available (a gansevoort suite on the smoking floor), even though I had called the day before to ensure the room would be available, and was assured it was. It's a great view, just unfortunate about the other patrons yelling and trashing the pool. I hadn't seen that many trucker hats in NYC in years. 
We had room service twice. Breakfast and the fruit platter (with white and red wine gelatin cubes, yum!) were really good. The dinner entrees were adequate. They serve La Colombe coffee,
 my favorite. 
Saturday evening they brought us a split of prosecco and some chocolates for our anniversay which was very nice. 
All the staff with the exception of the individual at the front desk were really great, they all had a big smile and were willing to help. 
The hotel is not for everyone - it's young, has a party atmosphere especially on weekends, and some of the other clientele dont really care if they're ruining it for everyone else. It's unfortunate. Next time I think we'll try the Standard.

Typical Hampton Inn & Suites, felt like it was in need of a bit of updating like the furniture and pillows but great location, comfortable and more than suitable. What sets it apart is the staff, all so helpful and nice. I really enjoyed the young gal who checked me in and recommended places to eat and visit. It was rainy and cold and she made m feel warm and welcomed! Kudos and I hope to see you again......
Gym was perfect for a quick workout, pool was delightful and hot tub hit the spot, breakfast was nice, good selection of food and the location is perfect!

As everyone else says on here...

The electronic safe would not work correctly and a call down to reception brought security who had it rectified in less than - minutes. We always felt safe wherever we went and whatever time of day, nothing like the tv! Eating out was not a problem as their are so many places to eat around once you have your bearings though a good street map is advised to achieve this. I would recommend a stay at this hotel to anyone, it's not cheap but you do get what you pay for at the end of the day. All in all we thoroughly enjoyed our stay in the big apple at the Intercontinental Barclay.

I had to attend a charity dinner function and decided to stay in San Francisco for the weekend. A quick phone call to the hotel and I was accomodated and the employees are so helpful. The room is so clean and well thought off for the convenience of the guest. Very relaxing atmosphere and felt so safe.

We were planning a trip to - cities in the states, and since we are students, we were looking for the cheapest and best-value accommodations (that wasn't a hostel). Certainly not a - star or - star but what a find. The location was so close to the subway to Times Square and the other attractions in NYC that this was great. My family and I stayed here for two nights and we loved the hotel. The room decor was contempory, staff were very friendly and welcoming. We ate breakfast and dinner here and the food was excellent. It was a bit noisy on Saturday night and I can't comment on the parking but I would definately recommend and atay here again.

Would have given them a - star rating but for the Chicago fire department. Not sure if any part of the hotel can escape the early morning sirens. My husband Stuart and I had the pleasure of spending two nights at the Chelsea Pines Inn during a recent brief trip to New York City. We needed a comfortable but affordable hotel in the Chelsea neighborhood, and we were attracted to the favorable reviews for Chelsea Pines Inn. I have to admit we were a little skeptical of any establishment with such overwhelmingly positive reviews, but I'm here to tell you: it's all TRUE!
First and foremost, the LOCATION is excellent, within convenient walking distance to the High Line, Chelsea Market, and many attractive bars and restaurants. We spent our entire time exploring the immediate neighborhood on foot, but there's a subway stop right at the corner if you're planning to venture further afield.
Next on the list are COMFORT and CLEANLINESS. The towels and bed linens were of very good quality, and the entire hotel was spotlessly clean -- breakfast area, lobby, etc.
Now, let's hear it for PROFESSIONAL, ATTENTIVE STAFFING. The front desk staff folks (led by the indomitable Jay Lesiger) were a joy to deal with -- knowledgeable, welcoming, helpful -- and all members of the support staff were personable and industrious. Clearly, everyone who works here ENJOYS working here, and that's not so common these days.
Now for the EXTRA SPECIAL FEATURES. We were traveling light (no laptop), so we LOVED the business center on the second floor, where we were able to have free access to the Internet and our email accounts - no hassles or hidden charges. Without a doubt, though, the BEST """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""amenity"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" at Chelsea Pines Inn is the resident cat, Charlie, who visited us in our room each night and greeted us in the breakfast area each morning. We miss our four cats dearly when we travel, so having a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""loaner"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" available when we're away from home is a real bonus!
Note that if you're accustomed to staying in corporate hotels or franchise establishments, you might find the rooms and bathrooms at CPI to be a bit small, but hey, this is New York City -- you'd pay dearly for those larger spaces. What impressed us was that, although the room and bathroom were small, everything you might need was right there: a sturdy wooden dresser, ample closet space (with good quality hangers), a nicely-designed walk-in shower, adequate surfaces for toiletries and accessories, a tiny fridge (just right for beer and wine), a well-designed bathroom area, and a large flat-screen TV. I might suggest the addition of a towel rod outside the bathroom, to encourage guests to air-dry their towels for re-use the next morning. Also, a row of wall hooks would be useful in winter, as a place to hang scarves and coats (not that we had this problem in July!).
Another expected pleasure is the landscaped garden area behind the inn -- quite a luxury to see at this price point, and a great place to sit enjoying coffee and breakfast in the morning. Our room (on the back of the inn, overlooking the garden) was very quiet, and we appreciated the always-secure access from the street into the front foyer.
All in all, we had a great experience staying at CPI, and we've already recommended it to several friends who are considering trips to NYC. We'll definitely stay there on our next trip to NYC - and the next one, and the next one!

It is located right next to a Target and tons of othe shopping and places to eat. And there is a Main Event right there too, we mwt up with some friends and went bowling, played pool and had a few drinks, which was fun.
The only complaints we had were very very minor. There was a guy talking on his cell phone at night right outside our room. We asked him to quiet down and he apologized and went to the lobby. No big deal, it happens. The bathroom light was a little dim when taking a shower, but so what?
I don't know who can honestly expect a decent room for under $--- anywhere, in response to the complaints about the price. 
I have paid alot more for nasty places and would definately return to this chain!

My Husband and I stayed at The Mosser for - nights on the first leg of our tour of the PCH. I chose the hotel based mainly on the location and pric we were able to secure. I ignored some of the reviews left by others on this site and just hoped that the better reviews were correct and I do have to say that we weren't disappointed! The location was excellent, just a short walk to Union Sq, Bart Station and cable car turnaround, small and basic rooms (well you are on the city centre!) but very clean and lots of nice toiletries left for you to sample, comfortable beds and nice coffee and muffins in the lobby every morning, this obviously is not meant as a breakfast as there is no proper seating, more of a cool complimentary morning snack which is very nice considering most city centre hotels don't offer anything in the way of free food! The hotel's website pictures the rooms etc as they are so there are no nasty surprises. We stayed in a room with a private bathroom so cannot comment on the shared facilites but can imagine they would be very clean going by the standard of our room.
All in all I would definitely recommend this hotel if you are travelling on a budget and just want a base to rest your head at the end of a hectic sightseeing day however couples on Honeymoon etc wanting a bit of luxury in the city will obviously not get that here, but as I said you can see this perfectly from the website before you decide and book anyway

I stayed here for a night after a long and delayed bus ride from Vancouver and it was just what I was hoping for. Warm and inviting room, nice decor, very clean bathroom and bed was luscious with choice of pillows. The room was a good size and had everything you could need. TV with cable, wifi, coffee-tea etc. Toiletries were quite good too.
There was a little room with computers and printers downstairs which came in handy with bookings etc although, there were only - computers and - working printer so at times there was a bit of a wait.
Complimentary breakfast was great!! Everything that you could expect and more, bacon, eggs, pastries, bagel, toast, fruit, muffins, cereal, coffee-tea, juice, yoghurt! Breakfast room was nice and spacious too, didn't have to wait for a table at all.
Location was good for us as it was only a couple of blocks to the Greyhound station and a few blocks in the opposite direction to the space needle and seattle center. There was a good pizza place about - min walk away, however, other than that not a lot happening in the area. Streets were very quiet.
Staff were fine but not necessarily friendly, seemed to rush you through as quickly as possible and didn't really want to help out with transport to the airport other than booking a town car. We ended up getting the greylines airport shuttle from Warwick Hotel down the road and saved about $-- doing it.
Overall, a great place for --- night stay but if you want to see all that seattle has to offer, not just the space needle - consider staying a little further downtown.

We stayed at the Elan for our honeymoon trip to the US. We loved it.
- Close to markets, shops, Sunset strip, restaurants
- Friendly, polite, knowledgable staff
- Value for money
- Rooms fantastic, good space, immaculate condition
- Try the Brazilian restaurant up the road (-- mins walk) as recommended by the Reception staff, expensive, but worth it!.

Came here for the weekend for my friend's bday. We stayed here once before. Very nice hotel and clean. Only problem we had is that we could basically hear our neighbors conversation. Also the dog show was that weekend, and there were dogs barking all night, pain in the butt when you're trying to sleep.. Seemed like they were all on our floor. We would come here again, just not on dog show weekend.

The lobby way is fab and the decor beautiful.
Rooms are small and basic but its Manhattan and they were very clean.
Staff friendly and great.
THE BEST PART.......roof top bar and club, by far one of the best parts of our trip!
The club really comes alive at night and you can spend hours sitting in the sunshine watching the world go by from up there.
We were lucky enough to catch a concert wth Jay Z and Eminem being filmed on the roof top opposite while we were there sipping champagne..... GOOD TIMES!
Would stay again.

This was our second visit to the Roosevelt Hotel. Upon checking into the hotel, we were upgraded to a deluxe room. Pleasant surprise! 
The room had a nice view of the Mann's Chinese theatre and all the action down below. Room service was prompt and very good. We didn't hear any strange noises this time, but we did capture some interesting orbs on camera. The Tropicana bar by the pool is a must, good people watching spot. Would definitely stay at this hotel again.

I took my husband to the Novotel for his --th Birthday! We spent - nights here and it was his -st trip to NYC! (We both travel quite a bit and my husband travels internationally for work)
We were very pleased at check-in with the hotel and the staff.
They acknowledged his b-day by giving us a complimentary drink ticket for the hotel bar which was really nice.
We had a clean, spacious room with a pretty good view of Times Square. The room-bathroom were both clean and comfortable. The location of this hotel was amazing for walking to most major tourist attractions as well as easy access to the subway.
I will recommend this hotel to all of my friends based on the cleanliness, location and price.

I've stayed at this and many other Seattle hotels over the years, and Inn at the Market always comes through. The location is wonderful, rooms clean and comfortable. If you want to be downtown, Inn at the Market is a great place. Rooms in Seattle are getting pricey, and Inn at the Market is still a pretty good value.

I stayed a weekend at this hotel. I thought it was going to be wonderful and a place I'd go back to. But on Sunday morning I noticed red welts on my body which kept developing over the next ten days. They were itchy & uncomfortable for two weeks. My doctor confirmed that they appeared to be bed bug bites. When I called the hotel (Tuesday) to alert them to the bugs in room ---, they gave me the run around. I left a phone message and an email. I called again the next day and was treated rudely by a manager. Several hours after this call, a lawyer telephoned me and never really addressed my concerns re: what if I brought them into my home.

I can only guess that the other reviewers stayed in some other version of this property than i stayed in, as the loud party next door only ceased to be a distraction when i was moved at - AM. Also, the renovations that were to have been completed, and feel free to confirm this, but they were definitely still painting. Kind of sad because the location, the exterior, the setting, everything the others said is true, it's just the staff, ask them for anything, toothpaste, shaving cream, no help, but directions and they draw a map of the state of California. Could use quality control but mostly, they could use selectivity when it comes to parties. I'm not sure there is anything special about the property but i can see where others could think so, as it could be so much better.

The --- Hotel offers a great prive-value place to stay near Times Square in New York City. It is a small hotel (-- rooms) so make your reservations early for prime travel dates-like Christmas time in NYC .
Location, location, location! Next to Restaurant Row, a few blocks from Times Square and Radio City Music Hall to name a few nearby places to visit. 
The rooms are a nice size and clean. It may not be the Ritz but for the price it can not be beat! The staff is great-they go out tof their way to make your stay with them memorable. 
For NYC-this is a don't miss..............................

We stayed at the Galleria Park hotel during the San Francisco portion of our honeymoon, and really enjoyed it. First, the location is absolutely perfect. From the hotel, Union Square is a short walk away, the Chinatown gate is within a block or two, and all of the MUNI lines are available at Market street a block or two in the other direction. It made an excellent base of operations for our many trips exploring the city.
The room itself was a bit on the small side, but more than sufficient for the two of us. The decor and ambiance throughout were modern and classy. One slight downside is that our room was on the inside, so the window looked out to an open area with hotel on all four sides. I'd call it a courtyard, but it wasn't pretty, and I think it just held things like air conditioners and the like.
On the other hand, if you do want to get outside without going far, the hotel has a nifty rooftop park with plants and a walking-running track. That was pretty nice to get some fresh air. There's also a complimentary wine hour, which we attended once, and didn't return since the wine was so awful. I can't really complain about free wine, but I certainly wouldn't plan my schedule around it.
Overall, the Galleria Park was a very nice hotel and we had a pleasant stay there. It was pretty expensive, but that may just be SF in general, rather than this hotel specifically. Also, there's a pretty hefty charge for the valet parking, but the valets were very friendly and helpful. Besides that, no complaints, and it really is in the perfect location.
Both my room and the room my friends got were awesome. Clean, spacious well appointed. GREAT LOCATION! I would recommend this hotel to anyone!

Stayed at this hotel on March ----- with a group of --. We arrived near -:--am and although none of our rooms were ready, they did check us in to one room so we could store ALL of our luggage, eat their wonderful breakfast and then be off to St. Patrick's Day parade. After touring most of the day, we returned and our rooms were ready and check-in was so easy. We did have a few minor issues in a couple of rooms, but the front desk clerks and housekeeping corrected them within -- minutes. 
As for the rest of the stay, the rooms were cleaned thoroughly, breakfast was always plentiful (great waffles) and clean. ALL of the front desk personnel (except for one) was very personable, gave great recommendations for restaurants, sites, subways, etc. On our last day, as our flight was not until -pm, they let us keep one room to store all of our luggage again AND they called and arranged for transportation to LaGaurdia. All in all, a great trip and I would recommend for anyone traveling alone or in a group. FELT SAFE

The room was clean and comfortable. David at the front desk was knowledgeable and personable. Efficient housekeeping-breakfast staff. The Van driver Dillan helped enhance our visit with great information and points of interest in San Diego. Kudos to the owner and Management for taking pride in your hotel!

I had an advance reservation for two rooms for my family to stay over one night. Their check in is at -:--pm and I arrived at -:--pm. The desk told me rooms weren't ready and would be ready in -- mins which I thought was reasonable since I was there a bit early. Waited until -:--pm yet my rooms weren't ready. I approached a staff at the desk and asked how much longer I had to wait since I have kids but he couldn't give me an answer and just disappeared. At -:-- I asked for a manager on duty and spoke to him but no help there either. Only answer I got was that they had a major check out in the morning and they did not know when they would have my rooms ready. Was told if I would like to cancel the reservation that is the only thing they can do but couldnt even tell me if they can refund my money. Called the main corporate, yet no help there either. Now I'm writing this at Sleep Inn that's not too far away in frustration to warn fellow tripadvisor users. Be aware.

This is really not my type of hotel - huge, boring, impersonal, blunt, business-like - but there are a lot of good things to say. The gym is great, which is really important! And there are several great yogastudios nearby, which is even better. The location is perfect and there is a large grocery store across the street, which means you can buy your own breakfast, etc. All in all, for being a type of a hotel I don't really like, it is absolutely perfect! And Boston is of course a wonderful city!

The location of this hotel was perfect. It was walking distance to the Magnificent Mile (Coach and Ann Taylor on same block). The rooms were sufficient. Nothing to 'wow' over but clean and sufficient. Front desk was very helpful.

I looked on line for a hotel in Denver! I actually wanted one with a nice big bathtub. The Magnolia Hotel came up. I read many reviews and wasn't so sure after I read them. Said the hotel was noisy and staff not very helpful. Rooms not cleaned, and beds not so good and other things. I actually called the Hotel directly and told them what I had read and actually got a better deal then I would have if I would have gotten it threw a cheap hotel sight! The rooms were very nice and we had no problems. The Bed was very comfortable. The room was like an apartment. Very nice! Perfect for walking down to the --th street mall. We did not park our car with them but drove around to find a cheaper place across the street to park. Totally recommend that to everyone! 
Only bad was that I forgot my phone charger and I had only gotten to the car and turned around to go back in and they had already gone threw my room. hmm Why so fast I am not sure. My phone charger was gone but I did end up getting it back. They had to search for it. So be sure and double check your room before you leave!

After a frustrating month, a bad break-up & surgery, I decided to take a week's vacation to Chicago. Being short on funds for an entire week's stay, I decided to go through Priceline. Luckily, my bid was accepted by the Hyatt Regency Chicago.
As a Priceline customer, I expected a basic room without a view. But I was still excited because the location was wonderful, so I posted on the Hyatt Regency Chicago's FB page letting them know that I was coming for my birthday. To my surprise, when I checked in, I given a gorgeous room with a view, my Hyatt Gold Passport number was written down for me (since I always forget it) and I was offered late checkout. Yes, I know that late checkout is pretty standard for Gold Passport members, but I didn't expect it since I reserved through Priceline. After getting settled in my room, I went out for dinner, and came back to a birthday card and some yummy treats for my birthday! I have NEVER had a hotel even acknowledge my birthday before, let alone leave a surprise for me.
Throughout my entire week stay, I was treated wonderfully. Housekeeping was excellent, and I got fresh towels every day even when they were hung up. I never had to worry about my safety, and I love the security of needing a room key to use the elevator after --:--pm. The room was quiet, the bed was extremely comfortable, the bathroom was clean, and hotel staff was always polite and cheerful.
The hotel is located in a great place as well. Just south of the Chicago River and east of Michigan Ave, you can walk to just about everywhere... and if you can't, there are multiple CTA stops within walking distance (for all CTA lines!) and the buses are easy to catch. The Theater District is just southwest of the hotel, the Magnificent Mile starts west and heads north, and just about any type of restaurant you would ever want is right there. Navy Pier is also within walking distance or you can take a short bus ride.
I adored this hotel and will stay here in the future! It was a wonderful week... and to cap it off and make it perfect, my best friend & I started became a couple during out vacation together. This was literally the best vacation I have ever had, and the Hyatt was a big part of why it was special.

I never sleep well in hotels - I slept like a baby at the Magnolia! The extra blanket was so nice bc I always get cold and the bed and pillows were so soft. Our floor was nice and quiet even though I know the entire hotel was booked. The staff was so friendly and helpful and we just loved it. The evening reception and cookie were a sweet memorable touch and we were within walking distance of everything making this the perfect hotel.

EXcellent value for money and experienced good customer service on arrival. Airport shuttle went to plan and driver was really friendly. If you want value for money and a one-night stay airport side I would recommend this hotel. Breakfast included was also good for the money paid.

I don't think you could get a better hotel in New York for the money. It's an old building, the rooms and bathrooms aren't big, and the plumbing is VERY noisy. But the location is great (easy to get to and from JFK via Penn Station over the road), you can walk to all the Midtown tourism sites, and a cab from the Times Square area is only about $- when you want to get back quickly at night. Very safe, comfortable and clean, staff were all helpful, courteous and efficient (I rang down one night when some kids were making a lot of noise, security were on it within minutes). Both the Tick Tock diner and hotel bar are great for food and drinks and just downstairs - though you're not short of places to eat round here. After checking out on the last day you can store your bags for just $- each. There's an amazing cinema round the corner if you want to go out but your feet have given up on you. Not the Plaza, but amazing value for money. I'd happily stay there again.

The location is absolutely great but everything else is not worthy what you pay for. The staff was nice but the room was very small and extremely noisy because of a huge A-C unit. The bathroom was old and one day they forgot to clean the room. There is no bar in the hotel, no coffee pot or refrigerator in the room. Overall I would not recommend this place.

Stayed here with a friend for - night after coming to Philly for a concert. The location of this hotel is great if you're doing anything downtown. Our room was very clean and large. The bathroom was one of the biggest i've seen in a hotel room. The beds were amazing, they were so comfortable. The hotel is huge with a great athletic room. The pool is small, but there was no one else in it so it worked out fabulously. Also, there's a great view of downtown from the pool. Without a doubt, if i ever end up in Philly again I will be staying here.

First time back to Philadephia in -- years for my Husband's --th Reunion from Jefferson. Wanted our - night stay to be somewhere luxurious and in the middle of everything. The Sofitel Philadelphia fit the bill perfectly! Upon arrival we were greeted by doormen who took our bags and lead us directly to check-in. Escorted to our beautiful One bedroom King Suite. Room was very nice with granite clad bathroom, fab toiletries, beautiful fluffy towels, thick robes, huge dressing room, sitting area with couch, chair, desk and tv....and of course the king size bedroom with the most amazing Frette linens, down feather bed, pillows and comforter. 
Headed down to the lobby bar for martini's (GREAT!) and then out for some strolling through Center City-Rittenhouse Square. Great shops and restaurants are steps away. Had dinner at Alma de Cuba and can not say enough about its great food and vibe. 
This hotel was a true value (booked online with Soffitel site and got the Sofitel Getaway special...King suite and full breakfast for - for $--- a night!) Friends of our stayed at Lowe's by Reading Market for more than that for a regular room. The hotel restaurant had a great breakfast menu. Try the scrambled egss on puff pastry with asparagus. 
This hotel exceeded our expectations. When traveling to Philadelphia, we will definately stay here again.

Best location for a New York hotel ever! Grand Central Station round the corner for the subway to Greenwich Village and Soho shops - museums and Rockefeller just up -th Avenue, crazy pubs and action at Times Square and a relaxing Bryant Park for people watching after you are shopped out. The staff at the Library Hotel were so welcoming and helpful - top tips on bars and shops to visit, a friendly smile and welcome as we came and went. The complimentary cheese and wine reception on floor - each night was the best way to meet our friends and discuss our days activities before heading out for food and drinks.
We will be back with bells on! Ronnie and Jennie, Washington, UK

What a great hotel - very boutique friendly feel to it. The rooftop bar is fabulous on a warm evening. Didnt get time to use the gym but it did look great with lots of free weights and machines, aerobics etc.. The location is very good with all the attractions on your door step. You must visit the bar attached to the hotel as the staff are wonderfull and the food is superb. Overall much better than much more expensive hotels I have stayed in in New York

I am giving this hotel a poor rating for just a couple reasons. A group I was with met up in San Antonio this past week. We were told that we had to stay on the Riverwalk. That is why we chose to stay at The Westin Riverwalk. First of all parking is a nightmare unless you want to pay the $-- valet charge every time. We had to walk several blocks to find open parking one night. They have quite the monopoly there. The staff was great! Everyone we talked to was helpful and polite. The real issue was with our room. We were asked if we wanted a a minibar key, but when we got to our room there wasn't a minibar or refrigerator. Maintenance brought us a refrigerator (I guess they are first come first serve...weird), but wasn't sure what happened to our minibar. Also, our shower had to be unclogged to even use and the bathroom was very dirty with mold on the tile. filth and hair in the shower, and hair all in the hair dryer drawer. Also, the amenity channel advertised a shuttle service that doesn't exist. The topper was the noise. On Saturday night there was music and a DJ that could be heard well enough to identity the song in our room until almost midnight. The next morning there was what I can only guess to be drilling and hammering that started before -am on our floor. No free meals either. I always look forward to a breakfast as a nice hotel. The rooms were nothing to get excited about and our window view wasn't nice. It was a beautiful building, a great location, and an outstanding staff. With the room issues and noise I feel that we would have been better off staying at the nice looking Holiday Inn up the street and save some money to apply towards a dog kennel and parking. It wasn't the most expensive accommodations but all rooms should be clean, stocked, and quiet.

I just returned from my fave city and stayed at the Holiday Inn Select. This is the first time I've stayed there and had reservations as I'd read reviews on this hotel before I went. It's in a good location, pretty much close to everything. The deal I got was great and the room was very spacious and comfortable. I'd read that there was alot of noise, and whilst you are close to MGH and a fire station, and yes, you can hear sirens, I didn't find it particularly noisy. The staff were pleasant enough and whilst I didn't think the restaurant offered a very good range of meals, consequently I didn't eat there, but there are a ton of places close by. I'd definitely stay there again.

First of all.. WOW! I just had to get that out of the way. I was so impressed by this hotel that I just have to write about it. I stayed at Santuary for -- days, the end of September through the beginning of October. I come a lot every Fall-Winter and visit family and friends, usually staying for a weekend. This time since I was staying longer I chose to book a hotel instead of staying with friends. I've stayed at various hotels in the city over the years and they are just that... Hotels. And with Sanctuary, it was all in the name. Every member of staff, no matter the shift change, made me feel like I was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""HOME"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". From the moment I arrived to the final goodbyes. Everyone greets you with a smile, is beyond accomodating to your every request, and is very personable. When my sister came over to my room to babysit my son while I ran errands, the concierge and even door men all asked about him whenever he wasn't with me. The whole place is so cozy feeling. Not to mention the beds. Those are some remarkable beds. My girlfriend came in town and stayed with me the last - days of my trip. I can't say that at ANY hotel I've ever stayed at that there has been a day I have not left my room. Now that's saying a lot since we were literally right next door to TIMES SQUARE. We were in such a great location. So close to everything, literally steps, but completely unaffected by any noise or crowds. Now, I can go on and on about Sanctuary but I'll make it short and sweet. My favorites: The amazing, personable staff, the modern yet welcoming design, the array of choices for snacks and drinks in the mini bar, the bed that feels like a cloud in heaven, the location in which you are close to EVERYTHING, the delicious breakfast bar, the fact that you'll never have to hail your own cab, the list goes for miles. I highly recommend you experience the Sanctuary Hotel for yourself. You will be delightfully pleased. I am, without a doubt, enjoying many more stays there!

I stayed at this hotel for - nights recently with my sister and our friend, and we were very pleasantly surprised. We were aiming to do New York on a budget, and found this hotel reasonably priced, in a good location,so decided to give it a go. On arrival, staff were very friendly and check-in was quick. We were pleased with our room on the -th floor which we were sharing- it was very spacious, with a kitchenette facility. Throughout our stay the room was kept very clean. We found the the staff to be very friendly and keen to help (much more so than a lot of hotels we have visited in the U.K for a similar price!), although if being picky,on our last day (Sunday), there were some different members of staff on who didn't seem quite so helpful as we had been used to the rest of the week. The location was excellent for our sightseeing and exploring. As we were out and about most of the time, we didn't get much time in the club room until our last day (unfortunately, as it's very nicely designed and is the ideal place to chill out). The hotel runs cheese and wine evenings here throughout the week, so would've been nice to have gone to that. All in all, we were very pleased with all that this hotel had to offer and had no complaints whatsoever. I would definitely recommend, and would stay here again if returning to N.Y.

Most Best Westerns at least include breakfast in the room rate, even their less-expensive properties. This one is among the more expensive BWs, and it does not. The place is well located in Hollywood, the room was clean, and there was free parking available, but the TV remote barely worked and was frustratingly difficult to get to do what I wanted. It still surprised me a lot to find that even the usual basic breakfast of toast, muffins and cereal wasn't provided here.

Our room --- had numerous problems. There were - large cracks in the granite around the sink. The top of the toilet had a large crack . The refrigerator was frosted over,and leaked water - it was very old. We saw - roaches the first morning, and two the second. The staff tried their best- they were friendly and helpful, but there just isn't enough of them. Our room didn't get cleaned until - pm the second day, because there was too much work, and not enough people. The breakfast line for fresh cooked was at least -- people long on a Saturday morning. This was aggravated by the fact that they did not put the bacon out with the precooked eggs. You had to stand in line, and ask the cook if you wanted bacon. There wasn't any sausage or perhaps that was behind the counter too. I love Embassy Suites! I love the two rooms, the frig and microwave, the coffeemaker (the one in our room leaked, and the coffee was terrible). I love the manager's reception, and the lovely big breakfasts. And I am willing to pay more for all these amenities - but don' t stay at this one. I know they are suppose to be renovated in January, but they never should have let this hotel get in this condition. I did complain the second afternoon, and they offered to move us. But for one more night it wasn't worth the hassle. I was concerned when i read some of the recent reviews right before our trip. I wish I had acted on them.

I took my husband to THE DREAM for his --th birthday WE LOVED IT! The aquatic decor and ice blue lighting gives good karma as soon as you walk in. 
The rooftop bar was excellent great views, and the rooms were super comfy. We will go back to the Dream New Yor!

The rooms were average-sized, even the executive floors. The breakfast was really scrumptious and even our picky eater of a daughter loved the different offers every morning (eggs, pancakes, waffles, salmon, various beverages, fruit, etc). Although we didn't have a view of the water from our bedroom, we got a great view of it every morning at breakfast. The hotel doesn't have a pool but a fitness center. We just went over to the hotel where our relatives were (Westin) to swim in the pool.

When I first arrived at the Intercontinental Barclay, I was so absolutely charmed by the beautiful room that I took a picture of it. Then, the nightmares started. During my first night, I requested a wake-up call. The next morning, I decided to sleep in and when my wake-up call occurred, I simply slept through it. The phone kept ringing. And ringing. And ringing. (In every other hotel I've stayed at, the wake-up call stops after a certain number of rings.) I finally picked up the phone and hung it up. The next thing I know, the doorbell rang very loudly (each room has a doorbell). It was the security guard (!), who came by to make sure I woke up. Sleepy and confused, I thanked him and went back to sleep. I've never stayed at a hotel where they send a security guard to hunt you down and make sure you wake up. The next day, there was a water spill in the bathroom. I called the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Care Line"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (I think that's the name of it) and requested some towels. I was in my room, toweling off from the shower, when the doorbell rang. The person who rang the doorbell didn't wait for me to open the door -- he simply walked in on me, NAKED! Even though there was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""do not disturb"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sign on the door, he ignored it and walked in. I screamed and slammed the door shut. After I got a towel to cover myself, I opened the door slightly and asked what he wanted. He said he was told there was a leak in the bathroom, and what did I want him to do about it? I told him that I just needed towels. He refused to get me any towels and insisted on coming into the room to see the water in the bathroom. Remember, I was still just in a towel! He fought with me when I kept telling him that all I needed was extra towels to mop up the mess. I finally refused to let him in and bolted the door in frustration. I used a blanket and bedcover to soak up the water, and complained, very loudly, to the manager. I asked the manager why his staff simply ignores """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""do not disturb"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" signs and walk in on guests? He had no answer. The last nightmare occurred during my last morning. Once again, I requested a wake-up call, for - a.m. Since I was already up when the call occurred, I simply ignored it. Once again, the phone kept ringing and ringing and ringing. I picked up the phone and hung it up. I did this about a half dozen times -- the phone wouldn't stop ringing! When I finally took the receiver off the line, the ringing started on the second line. This kept going on for half an hour! I finally picked up the phone and talked to the person on the other end (the hotel operator) and asked why she kept bothering me. She told me it was HOTEL POLICY to make sure the guests actually wake up. Hmmmm. I'm a grown-up, and don't need a mother at the Intercontinental Barclay to force me to wake up. This was a horrible, annoying intrusion. When I complained to the manager, asking him why the operator couldn't figure out that I was already up, since I kept picking up the phone and hanging it up, he just referred to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hotel policy."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I've NEVER stayed at a hotel where they try to force you out of bed!!!! When I was checking out, at -:-- a.m., I once again spoke to a manager and voiced my dissatisfaction with having hotel employees walk in on me, naked, when there was a do not disturb sign on the door. On our last night we were slightly disturbed by noise in the rooms around us, but it was not too bad and I can't blame the hotel for the behaviour of other guests.
I don't want to sound too negative, because other than these issues - there was nothing wrong with the hotel. The breakfast was slightly better than average for this type of hotel and to have parking in the middle of San Francisco (it was a - mile walk to Fisherman's walk which took about -- minutes to walk at a decent pace, an hour if you ambled) The rooms were clean, TV were old CRTs which seems to be standard for this type of hotel in the US.
Small breakfast area. Very difficult to get in and out of the one-way parking structure. Suggest staying at one of the nearby hotels like Hyatt, Hilton, etc.....

We stayed here for a week and spent - nights in a queen sized room, and then upgraded to a junior suite for the last -, as we got married so though we would splash out!

The rooms were lovely - we were in the Music room first and then the Love room (both our first choices). Both were much more spacious than I expected, very clean, and with lovely comfortable beds. What made this hotel really stand out for me were how valued they made us feel as guests. I have only - minor gripes - firstly the housekeeping were a little bit too vigorous, and managed to throw away a bag of mine containing a couple of my things. Also, the laundry costs were too high in my opinion. However, these were minor and didn't hamper my enjoyment of our stay.

The front desk people & outdoor greeters were awesome. The room looked out onto a brick wall which was only about - feet away. It was a shock at first but we got used to it. We got a rate of $-- on Priceline. They put us in a hospitality suite with two roll-aways! On the other hand, the cots were comfortable and the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", strange as it looked, was bigger than a regular room. In ---- the Embassy Suites Market Center was my favorite hotel in Dallas. Last year everything from the check in, the room, happy hour and the breakfast was excellent.

We were originally booked at the New York Palace but a couple of weeks prior to our trip, we found a great deal for the Millennium Bway on Travelzoo. We will definitely return to the Millennium Broadway on our next visit to NYC because it was such a positive experience. Our room was clean and spacious, the hotel staff were friendly and helpful, the location was ideal, and the price was a bargain by NYC standards.

Having stayed here on business at least - weeks per year between ---- and ---- when it was known as the Georgetown Dutch Inn and, because the hotel location is in a prime area for dining and shopping, we decided to try it again on a vacation. Very very nice hotel. Comfortable beds, very clean....but kind of a rip-off when you're trying to save $$. We got this room through Priceline at a great rate. My husband and I booked the Monaco at Hotwire, and the hotel was a nice surprise.
We booked a queen room, but asked if they could fetch us a king room.
Once we arrived, we were told Bria at front desk that the upgrade wouldn't be possible, once the hotel was packed.
So, she gave us a complimentary breakfast for one day instead, in a way to compensate things.
