I promised I would thank Bria and Rachel, and so I did! They are very kind (all people at front desk are very polite, always smiling!), they made our stay and our wedding anniversary very special.
The hotel is super, well situated, in the heart of the action, the rooms are nice, clean and quiet.
We highly recommend.

This hotel proved to be an excellent choice from the very first moment I stepped in. I travelled with a group of people and not all of them spoke English. Despite that, check in was smooth and fast. Rooms are up to Kimpton’s standards. Comfortable beds, high quality toiletries, nice mini bar selection and complimentary fast internet connection. The happy hour did the trick as all of us enjoyed the wine. I totally loved the architecture (the hotel’s coral colored walls) as well as the room design that definitely show attention to the last detail. The idea of having George (the golden fish) welcoming every guest proved to be brilliant. Instantly put a smile on our faces.
Room was very nice,service was good, just blocks from the Space Needle. Was very quiet,we were worried because of construction going on nearby.

Spent - days - nights at the Galleria Park Hotel while attending a family wedding in San Francisco. The Galleria is very conveniently located close to shopping, sites and restaurants. 
The hotel offers a wine tasting which we enjoyed.
The room was clean and the bed were very comfortable however I found the room small and tight to walk around furniture. My cousin and I shared the room and for two women it lacked enough mirrors, electrical outlets and the lighting was poor. With a bit of updating it would be a fabulous hotel, right now it is a good hotel.
The people at the front desk were very pleasant and helpful. I would stay here again.

I stayed here for three nights during a conference that was also held at the hotel. I was a bit put off by the two separate check-in desks, one marked """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Elite Guests"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and the other for the common people. A front desk clerk at the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""elite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" desk quickly reacted to a line forming at the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""common folk"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" desk and began to check in """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""commoners"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" so check-in was rather smooth.

The bathroom had not been cleaned very thoroughly. A price sticker was stuck to the floor, hair was on the toiletries tray and in the bathtub, and at least one of the toiletry bottles had been opened and used. Clearly the housekeeping staff needs additional training and closer supervision.
The in-room directory of services and hotel signage listed two restaurants that had been closed permanently. When I asked the concierge for a dinner recommendation, she recommended the one remaining hotel restaurant and offered a discount coupon. The food was very good and the service attentive -- which I particularly appreciated as I was dining alone.
After a restful sleep in a very comfortable bed -- with the air conditioner cooling the room -- on my first night in the hotel, I suffered through a sleepless night on my second night, thanks to a very warm and very stuffy room and what I feared was a defective air conditioner. I called the front desk in the morning and was told by an unsympathetic clerk, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I wish you'd called earlier -- I would have told you to open the window."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" The clerk went on to explain that the hotel had turned off the air conditioning and turned on the heat. (The outside temperatures were in the high --s at night and the --s during the day.)

The meeting rooms were quite comfortable -- one was even a little chilly -- so I was hopeful that the problem had been resolved. Unfortunately, when I returned to my room to change for dinner, I found that my room was even warmer and even more stuffy. All in all, great stay for a fair price.

Excellent service, clean, comfortable and quiet rooms, incredible breakfast and reception included in the cost of your hotel room. Very impressed, highly recommend this newer botique hotel, will stay here again!

We stayed at the White Swann for - nights around the first of February and loved it. We just had our spring conference here today. The service was awesome!!!! Chris, Dave, Wanda, Liz, and Clement took excellent care of us. Thank you for making our conference a success. IF you are interested in SERVICE and NOT glitz...this is the hotel for you. I spent four nights at the Marqueen Hotel in Seattle, and found it very delightful. For the price, the room was very spacious and felt a bit more like a well-decorated studio apartment than a stuffy hotel room. The kitchen was a lovely bonus (Seattle cuisine is so good! It wasn't a big deal, they offered to put us in another room but the water soon stopped dripping. Not a big deal. Overall, very delightful stay at the Marqueen. I will never stay anywhere else when I'm in Seattle.

Was there the second time. A really nice hotel with decent and quiet rooms. The central location directly near the Union square and also to the BART and the cable cars made it the perfect place for discovering the town and the bay area. Also the staff is very nice and really tries to help e.g. if you are looking for a shuttle transfer to the airport.

This hotel was booked only for an overnight stay, as we were flying out early AM, and all other airport hotels were either booked or the shuttles were not running at -AM. Probably the worst hotel I have stayed in Houston area. Old AC units sitting on corridor for days not being cleaned up. Tiny lobby area with free breakfast, so all hotel guest can share the sole table with - seats. The lobby area stinks.

We held our family reunion in Dallas and stayed at the Sheraton Hotel. The staff was professional but very warm and friendly at the same time. Anything we needed the people were more then willing to help us. I loved the decor and the layout of the building and would gladly stay there again.

Best thing about the hotel is its location. You're a -- second walk from Michigan Avenue.

The Chicago L station is less than a ten minute walk.
Our room was small, but nicely appointed. Free wireless access was appreciated. Bed was average and bathroom was clean. Room was pretty dark when the curtains were closed.
Staff was friendly. They brought up a luggage cart when we left and delivered toothbrushes when we realized we forgot to pack them.
Some things to keep in mind that some may see as negatives, but didn't really bother me because we were there just to sleep.
This isn't a full-service hotel.
* there's not a convenient circular drive to drive up your car where a bellmen will greet you and take your bags
* there is no conceriege service
* the lobby is miniscule so checked bags are not readily available (given space constraints)
There are only four elevators for this --+ floor hotel. One was not working the morning we left, so there was a very, very long wait.
Signs were present noting their environmental concerns. We hanged the towels as directed, but they were still swapped out, rather than allowing us to reuse them. I hate that.
All in all, if you're looking for a moderately priced hotel in downtown Chicago that is close to Michigan Avenue with relatively easy access to parking and the L, this is the place for you.
If you're looking for a snazzy business or conference hotel, this will likely disappoint you.

The Oxford is a beautiful and lovingly maintained historic property. The location can't be beat for any business downtown. It is within easy walking distance of shopping and excellent restaurants (the best was right across the street). A complimenary town car will take you anywhere within a --mile radius. I appreciated getting the tip from other TripAdvisor reviewers about the fee for parking. We did the math and realized that it was cheaper for us to take the airport shuttle and not use a car downtown, even if we had to take a cab once or twice. And it worked out great.
However, what makes the Oxford outstanding is the unparalleled service. Every single staff member we met seemed happy to serve us. There is good service and then there is cheerful good service - and we got cheerful excellent service. As just one example, the minibar from our room happened to be out for repair, and the staff promptly delivered a refrigerator to our room, since I had medication that needed to be kept cold.
I would highly recommend this property.

SLS has a great staff, everyone new my name and was always very interested. The team of employees were very aware, kind and sensitive. The SLS is very fortunate to have such a industrious and thoughtful staff...kudos to Rachael and Avery who made my stay extremely enjoyable...mydaughter is well !!!

Stayed for - nights on a get away weekend. Very please with location, accommodations and the great fron desk staff. Room was nice. Stayed here in April and this visit prior to an early am flight. Didn't have any breakfast this trip due to the early flight. It is a great hotel if you want to use Universal Studios with a regular shuttle service to the park up till -pm..perhaps that could do with running a little later.
Would stay here again without any hesitation.

Took my --yr-old granddaughter for a - day adventure in Chicago. Chose primarily due to price-proximity to tourist attractions. Location is superb. Decent places within two block radius to grab bites to eat on the cheap. """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Classier"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" restaurants nearby and within a quick -- minute cab.

Was nicer than I expected. Had third floor room not facing traffic, so no noise problem. I have stayed here several times when I have a very early flight to catch out of Midway. Hotel is convenient and has free parking. For the price, the hotel is adequate. It could use some updating but the staff is accomodating, price is right and it is quiet and convenient. It is now a Clarion property. Perhaps they will upgrade it.

I understand that not all experiences will be the same; however, for my wife and I this has been one of the greatest we have had - and we have had many. The Royal Palms will not be just another check on the list of resorts and get-a-ways we have had, instead it will become a fairly frequent """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Good ol' Reliable"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to which we return again and again when in need of exquisite scenic beauty and the utmost in relaxation. This is a modest hotel with a very outdated and off-putting lobby. The parking is extremely cramped and difficult to negotiate on the side and front of the hotel. If you park in the front in the double spaces, you need to leave your keys. The parking spaces on the side are challenging, even for a small car (maybe the Smart car is an exception, but we did not see one.) The room on the third floor in the back was fine, quiet, included a microwave and small fridge, and safe as well as Internet access (Ask for the Internet access UN-PW when you check in.) It would appear that some rooms in the front are larger and have balconies. However, balconies facing the street would seem to have little value to us. 
Breakfast is some coffee, roll or bagel or English Muffin, banana, and some cereals. The breakfast room is too small. Take the tray from the coffee machine in the room and use it to bring your breakfast back to your room. There is a Denny's right next door if you prefer a better breakfast. There are many restaurants in the area.
The hotel is within easy walking distance to UCLA campus, the Hammer Museum, Westwood shops and restaurants, Trader Joes, Ralphs, etc. It is also within -- minutes (non rush hour) to the Getty Museum and, in the other direction, to the LACMA. 
Really, the small lobby, breakfast room, and tiny parking spots are the worst parts of this hotel. Otherwise, the location and overall rooms are fine.

We stayed in a queen size bedroom at Hotel Havana for four days and appreciated its funky old world charm. It was an intimate boutique hotel with the feel of a grand inn. I highly recommend for couples and adults who like something a little off the beaten path. 
LOCATION: Hotel is on the river and less than a -- minute stroll to the main section of River Walk. It's situated in a fairly quiet part of downtown that is still convenient to all the sites. We were able to walk to the Alamo and La Villita quite easily.
SERVICE: Staff was extremely friendly, attentive and courteous. We were first assigned a street level room and they were very accommodating when I asked if we could switch to one on a higher level. We were always greeted when entering the hotel and the staff even escorted us to our cars with umbrellas to protect our luggage from the rain as we walked out.
ROOMS: Our room was moderately sized, clean, comfortable. It was decorated with dark, antique furniture styled with a modern take and lined with beautifully shuttered windows that provided lots of natural light. Because the building is old, you will hear some creaks and occasional muffled noise when people walk nearby or shut the door. I didn't find it to be a major problem. Bed was very comfortable and there were nice touches with the --s style fridge, art deco radio and robes. One point was taken off becaused I did wish there was a bit more sturdier drawer storage for clothing as there are no closets, our nightstand was a little chipped and our toilet seat was a loose (which was promptly fixed). It's a great boutique hotel and great value, but not quite the level of luxury.
DECOR: The decor had a lot of charm that brought out the character of the old building. It was filled with dark wood floors, poster art and unique antique furniture that varies slightly from room to room. The lobby area has velvet covered chaises and chairs and there was even an old-style red striped study equipped with a long table and lights for for reading. The second floor had community access to a beautiful balcony with a cozy seating area to enjoy coffee, lounge or read. Lots of of other neat little details and nooks to discover!
This is more of a hotel for adults as it is a low-key atmosphere not right on RiverWalk and doesn't have amenities like pools and rec rooms for children.

We like Kimpton Hotels and this one was perfect. Location is fun and convenient to activites and public transportation -- we use buses and subways in NYC. Lovely rooms, polite staff, comfortable lobby.

I stayed - nights at the Serrano while attending a conference at the Hilton. Service was great- very warm and genuine. I took full advantage of both the free offerings -morning coffee and evening wine. Both were good quality & sure can't beat the price! Also used the fitness room several times. Good quality machines, everything worked. I had a few special requests during my stay & they were very gracious. Highly recommend this hotel if you need to be in this area. It does border the Tenderloin & so there are quite a few street people wandering the area. Also probably not the best place for kids (no pool, rooms on the small side, etc.)

We came down to look at real estate for the weekend and booked the hotel for the location. Close to the airport and highway made it an easy and convenient for travel. The room was clean and comfortable with a microwave and small fridg. We paid $-- a night and I booked it on LaQuinta.com. Breakfast in the morning & fresh homemade cookies in the lobby at night were an added bonus. Can't beat the friendly and helpfull staff. What a great deal!

Very handy for Central Park but initial impressions were that the hotel is grubby and very tired, e.g. one of our plug sockets was hanging off the wall.
Some of the staff seemed unhelpful and disinterested - unless trying to persuade us to book a stretch limo for any given journey!

We stayed at Hotel Diva for four nights as part of our honeymoon in April ----. Check-in was quick and simple and we loved the Jelly Belly jelly beans at the check-in counter downstairs.
Upon entering the room, we found it to be quite small, particularly the bathroom, and the window had no view to speak of. However, the bed was the most comfy bed we experienced throughout our whole trip and was instantly sleep inducing. There was also welcome free wi-fi.
The hotel concierge was extremely helpful in offering advice, as well as arranging tours and taxis for us. 
The hotel is perfectly located in the centre of San Francisco, close to shops, restaurants, bars and transport. The tours we did offered pick-up direct from the hotel.
While breakfast is not included in the price, there are plenty of local eating options, including cheap diners and a delicious creperie.
While the hotel had some odd features (blue lights in the lift, condoms in the rooms and a vague 'sexy' theme), I would recommend it to other travellers, particularly for the comfortable beds, good value and convenient location. I would say its main let down is the small bathrooms.

I Spent A Night At Yotel On ------ With My Boyfriend And We Were Extreemly Satisfied! The Guy Who Helped Me Check In To My Room Was Super Nice & Knowledgable About The Hotel. The Fourth Floor Is Very Nice! The Room Was Pretty Tiny But TIDY! Everything You Might Possibly Need Is In The Room And It Is Well Organized. I Love The Fact That The Bed Moves Because I Get Better Sleep With Elevation As Oppose To Laying Flat (Don't Ask Why, I Just Do). The Bed Was Super Comfortable! I Found NO And I Mean NO Stains On My Sheets Or Towels So Major Plus To The Room Attendant For Their Attention To Detail. The Hotel, has a back to the --ish kind of feel, with updated amenities. Loved the room decor, from the paint on the walls, to the artistic lamps and furniture. We really enjoyed the romantic feel of the entire space from the lobby, and bar, to the restaurant """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Cafe Andree' """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". My girlfriend and I had a very enjoyable stay, and look forward to returning soon.

My wife and I stayed here ------- for - nights. The location is perfect, across the street from airport, but on Harbor Island. It is a beautiful location and great walking along the bay path in front of the hotel. The hotel has a free shuttle to the airport.
This is a - star very upscale resort on the bay. The lobby is very nice and great for people watching. We are Starwood Gold members and there is a separate check in for SPG members. There are - pools, boat rentals out front, ping pong tables, a spa, modern gym, and a cool area called Microsoft link in the lobby. The rooms are very nice. I love when they answer the phone from the room...hello Mr....
Downsides are parking price (save money on this...hint...check out SAN airport parking off site rates). Internet is NOT wireless in rooms. 
If you are flexible on your dates, they have great rates many times. Check on Sheraton web site or Kayak. Enjoy your stay. We are returning next month!

Great location and cool idea with pool yet service was not good. Bar closed early and steam-sauna off early despite -- hour claim. No one ever greeted us as we entered hotel. Pool is open to the public for a fee so don't expect an intimate experience. Rooms are small and dimly lit. Breakfast was okay yet very small room so seating is limited. Fitness center includes - exercise bikes and a small group of weights. Would recommend for location only. Geared toward European tourist who value price over service and ammenities. Would HIGHLY recommend The Perfect Pint Pub next store over the hotel pool bar.

We were looking for an affordable place to stay in Boston and we got an amazing deal at the Best Western through a Travel Agency. For ---$-night, free parking and breakfast included, this --star hotel was more than what we expected.
Check-in was very easy. Reception staff was very helpful. Manager was friendly. Breakfast was acceptable. Room was clean and of decent size. Bathroom was very clean.
No complaints until the last morning when, right before checkout, we realized that we had shared the room with a mouse or some other rodent!!! A chocolate bar had small bite marks all over it as if some animal had tried to eat it through the wrapper!! 
As we were leaving anyway, we did not make a big fuss out of it. The employee at the reception made a note of it, and told us that they have had a rodent problem in the past!! 
It might just be bad luck. We might even go back to this hotel as the location and price are unbeatable. But we will definitely never leave any food or candies in our room again!

The W Downtown is a perfect location for anything in the FiDi. Right across the Freedom Tower and close enough to Battery Park if you're planning on checking out the Statue of Liberty-Ellis Island. Standard rooms are small (it is NYC after all) but well appointed, bright and modern. I of course love the Bliss amenities! The desk staff were welcoming and friendly. I would love to visit again in warmer weather as it looks like the lobby bar opens up to a terrace. Would be great on a beautiful summer night! For breakfast in the morning, we went right around the corner to George's Diner rather than eating at the hotel and were not disappointed. Overall a great stay and would definitely return.

An Art Deco style hotel that offers excellant value for money. Maid service and clean linen everyday, including weekends. Contintental breakfast offers everything you could wish for in this title. Fresh fruit salads fresh fruit bagels toast cheese croisants muffins cereals. It is centrally located and a must for anyone wishing to explore New York without having an hours journey before getting any where. We visited with our late teens sons, and none of us had a bad word to say about it.

We always like to stay at Embassy Suites and this hotel didn't disappoint. Very nice, modern building. Great downtown location and the typical breakfast - drinks perks at Embassy Suites. Rooms were great - comfortable and clean.
Would definitely stay here again.

My stay at Andaz San Diego was one of the best experiences ive had with any hotel. As a diamond member they really went above and beyond to accomodate and make my stay memorable. This is a very nice hotel, located in the entertainment district of San Diego. My room was very clean with attentive housekeeping staff, the food was excellent, and the staff was most helpful. Because of the location, there was some street noise, which was substantial on St. Patrick's Day. The noise presented no problem for me. I would definitely recommend this hotel to others visiting the San Diego area.

My family stayed at the Paradise Point on October -th, -th and checked out on the -th. (Family of - Dad, Mom, Kids --, -- and -) Upon arriving the grounds look great - you feel like you are arriving at a resort in Hawaii. The Lobby is very attractive. We had booked a Lanai Garden Room, but upon arrival my husband decided to upgrade to a bayside suite. The checkin attendant was quick and friendly. The kids slept out in the living room on the pull out couch. We had a king size bed in a separate bedroom. A single bathroom is shared by all. The toiled is in with the shower so one person at a time had the whole bathroom. The room definitely showed it's age. The Bay outside was ok, but there were signs about the water not being safe after a rain (runoff). We did not feel that the bay water was swimmable and was cold. The room had a kitchenette, but no utensils, etc... That night we were cold (being from Phoenix) and turned on the heater. Our room filled with smoke and the fire alarm went off. No one called or noticed from the front desk. We fanned the room out till the alarm stopped. It was late and we did not want to change rooms so we went to bed with the smell of smoke in the room. The next morning we called the front desk. They did not seem to care about it - said they would send a repairman while we were at Seaworld. No apology, etc... We decided to see how the repair went. Seaworld was great. Our daughter got splashed by Shamu so when we got back to the room she layed her wet sweatshirt out on our deck chair. The sweatshirt was from Paris and had sentimental value for her. Well in the morning it was gone. She was crying and called the front desk to see if anyone had turned it in. They did not seem interested - did not act like they cared - and did not have it. I know it should not have been left outside, but they could have been like - oh no! We will definitelykeep our eyes open and watch for it (ie at least feign fake concern). The heater did work the second night so we did not pursue that issue. The last morning we called to see if we could get a late check out (a Weds in the middle of October) and they said no. There hotel book says to ask about late check out, but I guess they were busy?! We did check out then go to the pool for awhile. The pool is very nice. In summary the good points are the beautiful grounds, great pool - nice and heated, the barefoot cafe - where the staff was actually very nice! The bad points are substandard accomodations for the price, mostly uncaring staff. I would only stay here at a discounted rate - definitely not for full price!

Extremely noisy and unpleasant. Trains run so close that the whole building trembles. Motel - TVs. No working internet unless you pay extra --$. One of the worst hotels in Columbus. Don't waste your money there. Certainly nothing to do with what you would expect from the Marriott brand.

Currently staying in a - x double bed room here which is way too small for - people & very poor value at $--- per night. Stayed in bigger, nicer, cheaper rooms in NYC. This is a good, well situated conference hotel. I stress these factors because a) if you are not part of a conference you may want to avoid the hustle and bustle, and b) the facilities for those with a Gold or Diamond card is well below par. There is something called `the Diamond Lounge' which allows access also to Gold Card members. However, the room is rather small, looks and feels like a small conference room and is light on food. I stayed at a Hampton Inn just before reaching Boston and the breakfast fodder was much better. The Boston Hilton had scrambled eggs and porridge as the hot food selections. The lounge is closed in the evening and there is no alcohol of any kind on offer. There is a very small bar in the hotel lobby but it didn't seem to attract too many people. Our hotel was one of several involved in the same conference and if I was going to drink and entertain in the evening I would pick any one of the other hotels. One small compensation is that there is a pool. Talking about small, our upgraded room was on the large size but other reviews suggest that people who were not upgraded got smallish rooms. 
The location to the largely indoor mall shopping areas was very good and you are only -.- small blocks from the `T' (Prudential) on the Green Line. 
Too get a good view you need to be on a floor above the --th. We were on the --th floor and the view was good. However, our view was of the lessor two views. We were in a low numbered room (---) but the better views were opposite in the higher numbered rooms.

We stayed here June --th-July -rd. We had a room facing away from the Freeway and the noise was not to bad. You could faintly hear it, but it did not bother my husband who is very picky about road noise. We did suggest a quiet room at check in. 
Our room was not ready when we arrived at -pm, so they gave us a parking pass and pool key. We just hung by the pool and had lunch. They had a family burger meal (- burgers, fries, cookies, and drinks) for $-- that was great. The burgers were huge and very tasty. 
Our room was ready about -:--, so we checked in and had hot showers before heading out for dinner. We took the free shuttle to Universal Walk and ate at a hotdog place and went for a movie at the theaters. The shuttle was great and a real quick - min ride. They drop you right at the entrance to Universal Studios. The bus does fill up quick in the evening, so make sure you are there ----- min early or you will have to wait for the next bus if it is full (they do not allow standing on the bus). One time this happened to a couple of ladies and the bus driver said he would return for them right away and not make them wait for the next bus in an hour. 
We did eat at Tulla's on the property and the food was OK. The burgers we had on the first day came from here and they were wonderful, but the breatfast buffett was just OK. I actually liked it better when I ordered off the regular menue. We did not eat here for dinner.
The beds in the room were the best we had all vacation and they had different pillows to choose from. Overall we had a great stay and would not hessitate to stay here again if we are in the area.

My teenagers and I love Embassy Suites and this one on the Bay in San Diego was wonderful. Super clean room, nice, friendly staff and excellent free breakfast made our stay even better. We were on the --th floor and had windows that actually opened. They had had complimentary earplugs that came in handy to block out the streets sounds. 
The concierge was very helpful and gave us lots of advice on things to do (even some free things) in the city. San Diego is awesome and we will definitely come back to the Embassy Suites!

Whilst I wouldn't rave on about this hotel as much as the other posters I would say that this is a nice hotel and a good pick to stay in downtown Memphis.
As regards parking - you are advised to call the hotel for directions to the closest parking lot, but, for some reason, the lady who answered when I called seemed reluctant (or maybe just unable) to give me any directions! Self-parking is actually just round the corner from the hotel, but the parking lot is quite unpleasant and a little scary with broken glass scattered about. 
Once in the hotel there were a lot of positives - we had a nice high floor room, with a view of the river, the kitchenette was very handy indeed and there was free internet connection. 
There is also a great roof terrace with hot tub, which I think is probably the best feature of the hotel as there are good views across the river and the rest of the city and also of the Peabody roof terrace!
Hot breakfast is also included in the price, plus a weekday 'Social Hour', which included hot food and wine and beer, which is obviously a very nice bonus.

My husband and I loved this hotel. The staff were very friendly and eager to help. Cookies and fruit were supplied daily in the lobby. We were on the --th flour up above any possible traffic noise. With our window open every night we were serenaded with a saxaphone which only added to the atmosphere. The room was big enough for two with a fridge and a great walk-in closet. The Chancellor even has a pillow menu, which I was happy to try out. We would highly recomend this hotel for anyone to stay in San Francisco.

Every time I stay at this hotel the customer service gets better and better. Thanks to Ryan Shafi my trip away from my family seems easier to handle. His customer service and excellent attitude made my stay enjoyable.

We checked in at - pm and left our bags returning shortly after - pm. Finally they secured a room. We were reserved for a King Superior and asked if there were any Hilton Honors upgrades. We received the standard lines from Fevan, such has """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""it will be a lovely room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I'm sorry we're FULLY committed"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Porters to reception to security to cleaners were absolutely brilliant (even when faced with obnoxious and arrogant guests). 
Room was adequate and clean and serviced meticulously well. Beds and linen were perfect and the turnover service includes a weather forecast to help you plan the following day.
Bad points
Fitness Centre - those two words have no business being next to each other in the hotel literature. It is laughable and consists of a treadmill, two bikes and a basic Multi-gym BUT you are given free passes to the brilliant Equinox gym which is - mins away. Also, with Central Park being on the doorstep, there are other options. 
Roof top lounge - if private party, guests are not (always) allowed to enter.
Lifts - not able to service the traffic at peak times. (waited approximately -- mins on one occassion to get to my room)
WILL go again

We had a great time at this hotel. You have to have their breakfast buffet, it's wonderful. This is a charming boutique hotel; it's small and easy to navigate. The rooms are not very large, but you're hardly in the room in NYC! Close to the theater district and a short walk to Times Square. There are several nice restaurants close by as well. The hotel is clean and reasonably priced, considering it's location. If you're looking for a good deal in an expensive city, this is one of them.

This was our first trip to San Francisco after spending a few days in Vegas.The hotel is over --- years old but has had renovations.Decent size rooms with free WiFi.The staff was very helpful with any questions that we had.The hotel is a stones throw from China Town and just around the corner from Union Square.The Hop on Hop off bus stops across the streeet from the hotel.The walk to the piers is about -- to -- minutes up and down hills.If I returned to San Fran I would definately stay in this hotel and I would also recomend it to friends.

I attended a wedding this weekend and had business in DC today. My family joined me for the wedding and decided to see the sites in DC while I attended my meeting. My in-laws have raved about the Embassy Suites at Georgetown for some time, so we decided to try it. It's well worth it. We had a suite, so that everyone slept comfortably. My small children woke up early so we were able to close the door to allow my wife to sleep in some - a truly appreciated, rare treat! I took my three kids down to breakfast and their morning fish feeding. It was a little crazy with lots of people enjoying the free (and fabulous breakfast), which resulted in my daughter getting temporarily separated from me. She started to cry, but Daphne was right there beside her to comfort her until I returned. It wasn't more than -- seconds, which could have been a lifetime for my daughter had Daphne not been there. Daphne was a great example of the great service we received. Everyone from my family highly recommends this place. We certainly will be back.

This by far was the worst hotel I have ever stayed in. There were dead cockroaches left in hallways over night. My associate had dried feces in his room on the actual toilet seat when he first got into his room. All the carpet in hallways are ripped with duct tape, and did I mention that they charged me $---.-- a night. It was so pathetic I wouldn't pay $--.-- for this hotel. One of the few hotels that I have given - stars. Stayed for - nights and really enjoyed the experience.
The hotel has recently been renovated and it really shows. the rooms are excellent in every way. All mod cons, comfort, nice views. The bathroom was small but very modern and functional.
A crib was provded for my baby and I have to say it was better than any crib other hotels have provided.
The hotel has a restaurant and we were offered --% off our -st visit there. 
The location is good and is in close proximkity to the Prudential and Copley shopping centres. Theres some great restaurants nearby too. Bear in mind that the hotel is a half hour walk from the main boston downtown area and the location is more suited to shopping.

Above average FOR THE PRICE in such a safe, CENTRAL location. We booked - units for family members coming from across the US, Australia, Europe and the Middle East. At the time of booking (directly with The Copley House), we requested emailed photos of the rooms reserved for us, as a record. 
The BEST part of our stay was having so many family members in close accommodation for such a happy occasion as a wedding, being able to meet all together in one room for a drink, or to share a meal. Looking back, this meant far more than the standard of the accommodation - a waste to spend more for fancy rooms when our holiday was about visiting with family members separated by long distances (and airfares), and seeing Boston.
Downside and Upside points listed below.
Downside: 
-. The rooms we were assigned on arrival did not always correspond with the photo shown, as had been agreed on booking.
-. The carpets were in need of a good clean and did not get vacuumed at all that we noticed.
-. Not a full complement of cutlery in some kitchens, nor was it very clean. Housekeeping needs to learn to wash dishes hygienically.
-. Rooms were overheated and temperature not adjustable, so we had to have the windows open.
-. Shower stall drained very slowly only in at least - studio. 
-. Pull out bed mattresses uncomfortable in some studios.
-. We were told there was a 'short' flight of stairs down to the room reserved for a -- yo - in fact, - very steep flights. Would not meet requisite standards for people with disabilities or the very elderly in my country.
Upside:
-. Excellent location.
-. The staff was EXTREMELY helpful and friendly.
-. Complaints were dealt with promptly such as: room change to one similar to photo; lumpy springless mattress thrown out and replaced with a new one...
-. Bathrooms were cleaned daily, fresh towels daily.
-. We had free parking for - weeks.
-. We kept our rooms at a much reduced rate when we were away for a night.
-. Studio was bright, well appointed with furniture, beds comfortable, linen clean.
-. Laundromat across the street, supermarket nearby.

St Regis Hotel Detroit is a classic older building that has been restored and is in very good condition. The staff was friendly. Room was reasonably clean and not overly worn. Our room on the -th floor was very quiet. As others have said the heater will drive you out. It was below freezing outside and we had to have the window open all night to cool the room down to a bearable temperature, even though the thermostat was turned all the way down. Valet parking is $-- a night and you will want to use it. Forget the breakfast in the morning. Although the coffee was decent the food was just old frozen bagels granola bars and packaged cakes. For the price compared to other Detroit hotels it was a good value. With a little work it could be even better. Be aware that this hotel is in the New Center area, not right downtown. The Fisher Theater is very close and the old GM building is right across the street. Many of the building are connected with Skywalks.

My wonderful husband took me their for our --th Wedding Anniversary (as a surprise). Upon our arrival, there was a gift waiting for us at the front desk from the hotel manager. It was a beautiful picture frame. As we were checking in they upgraded our room. Later that evening we had reservations at the steakhouse on the property (forgive me but I can't remember the name). You must eat there...it is to die for!!! The Chef has you try """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""special"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" food and after dinner he will send out a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""special"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" drink for your table. The next day, later in the afternoon, the hotel manager had chocolate covered strawberries and a bottle of champange sent to our room. WOW! 
We stayed a total of - nights and wished we could have stayed longer. This is our favorite hotel to stay in all of Arizona. 
The Resort has several resturants to choose from...any are sure to please ones appetite. 
Last but certainly not least, the employees...all are extremely courteous! Keep up the wonderful work! That's what keeps us coming back...NOT the free stuff...to me and my husband it's """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""ALL"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" about the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""CUSTOMER SERVICE""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""!!
Thanks for the beautiful memories... :)

Room smelled musty. There were several homeless guys out front of hotel and sketchy looking folks hanging around the adjacent neighborhood. The room needs updating (chipped paint, closet won't shut, carpets look old, faded and dirty). High Speed wireless internet is a joke; it hardly stays connected long enought to check email.
Spend another $- and go to a Hampton inn or Holiday Inn. 
I come to Austin often on businees and thought I should save some company $ by staying here. That was a mistake. 
THIS IS A DUMP!

We have been lodging at the Marriott Marquis from January --th to January --th. I have been to that hotel a few times in the past and always loved that experience. 
Now they have changed and for the elevators you have those new key card pads. I can imagine that it may be really disturbing for some poeple, but ones you realize how it works it is great. You only have to push the number of the floor you want to go and to wait for the assigned elevator. I read all those reviews and was afraid we had to wait, but we had not to wait.
But, ....
The problem at the Marriott Marquis is their concierge service, in the past I always had good experiences with them but this time they were really unfriendly. We wanted to book a limo for a trip through New York, the lady that served me was not really friendly and they offer only one company and really not at the best price. Then we tried using their concierge service a second time the next day (with an other concierge) for a restaurant reservation and this time he was even nastier then the first one.
But still we really enjoyed our stay.

Very surprised to read other reviews listed here. Travel to NY very frequently and was very disappointed in this Hotel. Yeah, it's on the Park but most rooms don't face it and those that do face the Park are closet size. Actually changed rooms - times (which I never do). Hotel is far too expensive not to have a decent room. Front desk clerk was downright rude and nasty. Hotel lobby is busier than Grand Central Station. Many New Yorkers use lobby to cross from --th to --th Street.. Creates chaotic, unwelcoming atmosphere. Hotel also nickels and dimes you for everything. $-- pp to use fitness center, $-- to have wine glasses brought to room, huge phone and internet fee, etc.
Only highlight was restaurant and lounge atmosphere. That's it.

To be honest, the smell of public areas is terrible, but once in your room, it is a clean small room, really what you pay for (cheap), and an incredible location.
We saw other comments abut homelss people and the night club next to the hotel. The truth is only car noises were anoying. You see homeless peolple all over the area, even outside the big hotels, and the night club is nothing to worry about.
Again, get some Glade from home and the hotel is great if you want to save some bucks.

Stayed here with the family for - nights at the end of August. Great place to stay in Boston if you're a tourist, can't beat the location - right across the street from Quincy Market. Staff are very friendly and helpful. We stayed in a suite - huge, modern and plush. The only downside is the noise - our room was on the second floor above the hotel's bar - quite noisy at night. Otherwise, nice place, will stay here again and would recommend it to anyone touring Boston.
Close to all main atractions; friendly staff. Room was very comfortable, metro and bus stops very close.

This ---- hotel has been beautifully renovated by Wyndham. As our room wasn't ready for early checkout we were upgraded to a double king with antique beds and very comfy bedding. The hotel is only a couple of blocks from the Riverwalk and has an elegance many of the newer hotels right on the river lack.

There are things that you could pick on about this hotel. The location, while right across the street from the Galleria, is not particularly scenic, surrounded by large vacant lots and surface parking. And the service was a little rough around the edges at times, although very friendly.
The size and decor of the rooms more than make up for these minor shortcomings however, especially for the price. The rooms are huge, and ours (on one of the upper SPG floors) had one of the highest ceilings I have ever seen in a hotel room. The interior design is clean and modern, without being minimal or cold. The iPod dock and auxiliary inputs for the TV were a nice touch, and the bar-height table and stools would be a perfect place to get some work done.
Great value overall, and highly recommended.

The hotel was clean bed was very comfortable The staff god not have been more helpful.the only thing lacking was draw space for clothes and the room could have been a little bigger but over all very nice would stay again

Stayed here a few nights on business. It's a bit dated but clean. 
Pros:
- Comfortable beds, pillow, sheets
- Courteous staff
- Complementary hot breakfast - eggs, bacon (one day, sausage the other two), waffles plus assorted pastries. Not gourmet by any means but decent.
- Wifi worked well for me
- Value for the money
- Pretty quiet - not a lot of road or airport noise
- Location- took me about ----- mins to get to-from lower Uptown
Cons:
- AC in the room a bit noisy
- Old, small tv (not flat panel)
- Sandpaper towels

Booked through Priceline. Got - rooms for $--- a night. Check-in staff were very nice. They put us on the concierge floor so we could have adjoining rooms. The kids stayed in one while my wife and I stayed in the other. Nice! All the hotel staff were great the whole time. The beds are top notch. We slept great. Had a minor problem with the air conditioning, but it was fixed soon enough. Because it is tucked in right next to - freeways, GPS won't get you in and out. Use an old fashioned map and you'll be fine. The kids didn't like the pool. They said the bottom was slimy.

Things definitely didn't get off on the right foot when I got there and found out that my reservation had been cancelled. It was probably partially my own fault, since I had inquired the day before about cancellation policies because a friend was waffling about going with me, but they were able to put me in a single room (---) that served its purpose.
As many have said, it does have an institutional feel. It almost felt like a college dorm. The room was very basic but surprisingly big for a single, with a twin bed, dresser (both on the worn side)and a decent-sized closet. Aside from some stray hairs (not mine) on the floor and a three-day old NY Times under the bed, it was very clean, as was the bathroom. I was also surprised how quiet it was...you'd hear the occasional door slam or people walking around, but nothing major at all.
I do have to compliment the staff, who were very accomodating and friendly, especially during check-in.
I wish we had the ability to do half-star ratings on here, since it's actually closer to three-and-a-half level...nothing remarkable but well-maintained and especially well-staffed.

This was our first visit to NYC and we were torn between this and the Library hotel. The Sofitel won due to price and in the end i am glad we picked this one. The hotel has an air of sophistication about it the minute you walk into the lobby. Lots of fresh flowers and scented candles litter the entrance along with big comfy leather sofas. Our room was on the --th floor and we had a great view of the Chrysler building. The reception staff upgraded our room on arrival and we had a beautiful room with plenty of space, a nice --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" tv, lots of hanging space and a bathroom with separate shower.
I would certainly recommend this hotel to anyone wanting a nice, clean hotel off a main street and within striking distance of Times Square and -th Avenue

Stayed at this hotel on our way to Cleveland passing through Indy.
The room was clean. Bed was comfy. Quiet hotel.
I didn't necessarily notice the security issues that another review noted, but I can see that happening. It's honestly not the best part of Indy, but not the worst. The area is definitely so-so. 
Someone did scrape the bumper of my car in the parking lot. Could have been the guy wandering the lot with a broom but not sweeping trash. But that's my only downfall of the place. Which is honestly just the downfall of people not being able to drive.

I stayed at the intercontinental SFO on a business trip in January- hotel is conveniently located downtown within reasonable walking distance to the waterfront, Chinatown, and just a block from the Moscone West convention center. I had a room on the --th floor with a FANTASTIC view of the city. Rooms are clean and nicely appointed- bed was very comfortable. Staff was very friendly and allowed me to check in early. There is a gym on the -th floor that is open --h which is very convenient, and provides water and fruit as well. The lobby bar is a nice meeting spot (try the Italian mojito) but if you really want to be blown away, head to the View bar on the --th floor of the Marriott (a couple blocks away)!

The Affinia Dumont exceeded all our expectations. The rooms were immaculate with ample closet space, basic Kitchens and safes. The staff were the best I have encountered anywhere. They were knowledgable about any and everything. and willing to spend time answering questions. We asked for a room with a view and we were given one on the --th floor with a breathtaking view of the East River. The hotel is in a great, safe area, much more upmarket than the popular Times Square area and within easy walking distance of most of the famous stores. We used the subway almost every day and it was safe, simple and inexpensive. There are several local deli's and a Starbucks on the corner.

After reading review after review of hotels in NYC, I chose the Warwick. We couldn't have been more pleased with our stay at the Warwick. We were greeted very warmly when we checked in...our room was FANTASTIC on the --th floor overlooking -th Avenue...very roomy with a very comfortable bed and a nice size bathroom and VERY CLEAN and quiet. We called for a coffee pot for the room and it was there within minutes. The location of the hotel is great...within walking distance to Central Park and Times Square. The subway is not far away and the front desk is so helpful in giving directions. We had buffet breakfast in the hotel restaurant every morning and it was very good and a very nice buffet. A great way to start the morning. Actually, I can't say anything bad about this hotel. I would HIGHLY RECOMMEND the Warwick to anyone staying in New York City.

My husband and I stayed at the Warwick this weekend for his birthday and our anniversary, we had a great time! I had booked a suite and when we arrived we were told that we'd been upgraded to the Presidential Suite (Thank You!!). The staff was very nice. The valet service was included in our package, we also used the car service which was so convenient! Our suite was spacious and clean. The bed was comfortable, the HVAC worked well. The shower had great water pressure. Good location. We'll go back.

Location and hotel were excellent for NYC standards. Very pricey and small room but very clean and comfy beds and we had a view of the Empire State Building! Near red line stop on subway, convenient for travel in city! Comfortable stay.

I had stayed at the W several years ago on several business trips and never liked it. While I expected the rooms to be small, the staff really made you feel that they were doing you the favor in allowing you to stay in the hotel. NOT THIS TIME! Customer service was certainly high on their list. I was delighted to find that I could request a coffee maker. They brought it up with many coffee & tea K-cups. I then got a call to make sure I had gotten the unit. I had but explained that I could not figure out how to use it. No problem - they came back and showed me what I doing wrong! My daughter and I had a drink in the bar and she wanted a hot toddy. The bartender found out how to make it and brought it over, checking with us to make sure it was ok. All in all, a totally different experience.

Stayed here for my first few nights in Chicago on recommendation from a friend. I was disappointed when I pulled up late at night because I couldn't find where to park, thought that there was nothing around the hotel (middle of nowhere, etc.), but my opinion completely changed. First, there was hot coffee and a selection of teas available late at night (cookies too, but I didn't try any of them so I can't report). I went in (twice) to the extremely friendly and helpful night manager who explained (twice, and patiently - I was tired...) where to park my car. I went out for a walk and found that the hotel is --- a block to the beautiful lake, less than - blocks to restaurants and bars in a lively area, and - block from a really great gym (free for hotel guests). That the hotel was on a quiet, residential street was actually a nice bonus because it provided a quiet reprieve during an otherwise very hectic week!
It is a small, boutique hotel (very Euro-style with strange narrow hallways to rooms, etc., but that really just adds to the character) with an equally teeny elevator that I could barely fit my suitcase in (which may be more of a reflection of my own packing than on the hotel). The rooms are also small, as several other commentators noted here, but that's not really an issue when everything is nicely appointed and otherwise comfortable (it's a hotel - I'm not buying it for storage space!). I stayed in a king sized bedroom, but I heard that the suites are quiet large, featuring a little kitchenette and separate living room area. My bed was so comfortable and soft with down pillows and the plushest blanket I have ever encountered in a hotel on top of the bedspread (available for $-- in the lobby downstairs). The basket of goodies and wine selection was a nice added touch and pretty reasonable ($- for a little packet of cookies- sweets and $-- for a nice bottle of wine - I had a bottle of the Sterling Merlot, and the wine glasses and cork screw were convenient too...I've been in several hotels where there's wine in the mini bar and no wine glass, so I figured someone else may appreciate this note).
The bathroom was very quaint in a shabby chic kind of wine. I thought it was quiet pretty anyway, and I really appreciated the higher end quality of soaps and bath products with their own little dispensers for shampoo, conditioner and shower gel in the shower itself (no little minis to take home!). 
What I didn't like: the ceiling wall seemed very thin, and I could always hear the person upstairs walking around, coming in, going out, etc. It was much louder than anything I've heard in any other hotel. The breakfast featured a good selection of yogurts and a couple of cereal boxes, but there weren't any healthy bread options (just white bread, white bagels, sweet muffins, etc.), and I would have appreciated some kind of whole grain or wheat option. The internet was pay per day (I think $--), and parking was $-- per day and not particularly convenient. It is valet only and you really need to allot ----- minutes to wait for your car each time. 
Overall, if I were to stay near Wrigley Field or if I wanted to stay near a more diverse, quaint part of Chicago than the city, I would consider the Majestic first. It's convenient to downtown if you have a car (just straight onto lakeshore and you're there in ---- minutes) and pretty convenient to any train station. The hotels downtown are much more expensive, though there is a phenomenal selection of very upscale hotels (The W, The Drake, Trump, The Wit, Palmer House, etc.).
If you are coming to this part of town though, I will do a plug for the place I did a short-term contract on: www.wrigleyview.com. It's walking distance (less than - mile) from the Majestic, and a relaxing, comfortable way to enjoy a Cubs game and the Wrigley Field experience without being down in the stadium itself.

They tried to get us to pay (for a planned - night stay) before we even saw the room (we didn't). They asked everyone in our party for identification, also before seeing the room. Very odd. Something strange was definitely going on. When we went to see the room, everything was dingy, and dark. There was only one overhead light which was very dim. No lamps or other lighting. In the darkness the room appeared dirty, and the carpet was definitely stained. We got out of there as quickly as possible, and ended up staying in - other hotels for our four nights. I can't imagine anyone thinking this place was OK to stay.

We searched high and low for a hotel for our first family vacation in - years. Let me tell you, the hotel webstie does not do justice to this great hotel. The rooms (- BR suite) were large and comfortable, the kitchen was small but very usable (saved a ton on breakfasts), the master bedroom had a king size bed with what felt just like our tempur-pedic mattress, and the kids said that the pull out queen bed was comfy. The neighborhood was awesome and safe (with a great market just around the corner and a great place to eat called Nicks that delivers), the hotel staff was super friendly and helpful. When we go back next year, there is not another place that we will even consider. Subway - blks away, central park - blocks away. STAY HERE, YOU WON'T REGRET IT!!!!

My husband and I have stayed at other Springhill Suites and were quite satisfied with our stay.
The hotel is dated, which is not a problem, as long as the customer service aspect is maintained.
My husband lost a pair of sunglasses, he called the front desk to report the loss. He was told that all lost items were locked up and only housekeeping could access the room. He was pomised a call back which did not happen. He had to call twice AND go back to the hotel for resolution. The walls were very thin. We could hear the people in the next room having a normal conversation. My husband asked to be moved, which he was, to another room. The toilet would not flush. We had to move again. The hotel needs a renovation at most. I normally rate my experiences with the Marriott chain on a high scale, however, this property did not meet my expectations.

Great location! Near cable car, Union Square, in the heart of China town, right next door to north beach, easy hike to Coit Tower. Rooms are spacious, clean, wifi is easy to hook up too. Fantastic views of the city and ocean. Quiet location compared to Union Square. Overall a great value. Park car at starts garage on California and Kearney a way better price...

Just spent a night there. Decent room, but not overwhelming. Biggest issue was rudness of the desk staff-low end service from them -- they appeared to be overwhelmed--especially if asked a question..if you need anything the door people are great. 
Had a --- day meeting and those facilities were very good. I rated service average as the people involved in the meeting were very good, the desk people were low end so the service averages out to average---make sense--hope so

We stayed here on our annual family trip with the proverbial group from - to --. We appreciated being right on the Riverwalk. The hotel is beautiful, converted from an old municipal building with very high ceilings everywhere and beautiful decor.

I am writing this review while at the hotel. The walls in this hotel are very thin. People are simply talking in the next room and you can hear everything! At -:--am we had to call the front desk about the room next door. They were laughing and talking, not being rowdy, we felt bad, but the walls here are too thin. If you do stay, get a room not facing the highway, again, very noisy. And I sleep with earplugs!
If you are wanting to enjoy Easton Town Center, the walk in the winter is too far (we have stayed at Easton Center, much more convienent when you have shopping bags - goodies get heavy) and the shuttle here is scheduled, will not just run you over and drop you off.
Breakfast bar is your standard breakfast bar that most hotels offer.
This hotel gets a poor rating due to the noise issues.

I booked this hotel -- days before my arrival date and After I arrived at this hotel, the man sitting on the desk just gave me a nice smile and said """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I dont have any available rooms for today """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" what the hell!! after that he just sat clicking on his computer until he offered me one night at the Ritz Carlton ( this hotel costs more than ---$ a night ! wow .. I went there and slept for one night and came back to complete my stay in New York at the Marriott .. I loved this Marriott location ! you will never find a better location .. The rooms are ok, not bad .. I booked a room with a view of the Times Sq. but It wasn't as I expected. Poor view. This hotel is always crowded, if you do not like crowded places DO NOT book this hotel .. I would recommend this hotel just for its location. I think you may find cheaper hotels with better rooms, but not a better location!

My Fiancé and I stayed here for a week while on holiday fom the U.K, fantastic location very central to all SF attractions, we couldn't of choose better after hours of reading up on hundreds of different hotels in several locations! Everything was within walking distance, the BART, muni and cable car are right outside the door! My gripe was that we had booked a cheap deal through a separate website and when we arrived we were given a twin room to our huge disappointment ( especially as i planned to ask her to marry me while in SF so i wanted it to be special) I asked reception if they had any double rooms and was told no but could upgrade to a new sea view room which had a double bed for $-- extra a night, we accepted, but I wasn't to pleased as the hotel seemed less than half full, later on we asked a different reception clerk ( one who didn't recognise us ) if there was any standard doubles available for our stay length and was surprised to be told yes, abit sneaky of us I know but we were pretty sure they were pulling a fast one. This was a very bad stunt for a Hyatt to pull and it ended up costing us a big chunk of our spending money just to sleep in the same bed. My Fiancé didn't want me to kick up a fuss about it at the time as she just wanted to enjoy the holiday, but hey that's what Tripadvisor is for! we have always stayed with Hyatt on our travels and on buisness at home and never encountered this!

The pool is well maintined, better to use it during the day, if with the family, as the bar on the -th floor is a hot spot in el paso. The maid service was exceptional and the rate for military family members was impressive. Keep your key cards on you at all time, as the elevators work on a security based key card program, making it impossible to get up past the -nd floor without a key card.
When using the garage..make sure to have the staff explain how to get from the lobby via the elevator system..dont guess..it is an odd set up and if your in a hurry can make one late, waiting on an elevator for the garage.
Eat else where the food is ok, but well overpriced. Walk to the visitors cente and ask how to walk to either the garden restuarant or Tablas, which is right around the block, and in a safe area.

The hotel is very nice; rooms were okay and we had an upper floor corner room; but the carpet was old and looked dirty. This is a --star hotel at best and not a -+star. The lobby is misleading for what you pay. The restaurant on-site is excellent and i would recommend the mac & cheese appetizer.

This was a nice, clean hotel in the middle of Downtown Chicago. The room was a bit small, but clean, quiet and comfortable. It's an older hotel, so the hallways are snaky and it doesn't look flashy, but it is within walking distance of Michigan Avenue and many restaurants. Parking is free. I'd stay again.

I checked into the Diva on my own for five nights in early July. I'd been to Vegas the preceding week and fancied a chance to recharge my batteries in SF.
I checked in quickly and was given a smoking room as requested. The room was exceptionally clean, modern and comfortable. Groovy metal installations on the walls and modern light fittings looked great. At the rear of the hotel you don't expect a view, so that was no problem. The bathroom was compact but had plenty of towels and was clean. One small issue with the shower curtain not keeping everything in the tub, but generally fine. When the shower head did come off it was fixed relatively quickly.
The TV worked and the range of channels was cool. The internet facilities on my floor worked and the connections were quick. The staff on the front desk were friendly and helpful. For location, Diva is spot on, just a block from Union Square and two up from Market Street. Great place to stay - nice, clean rooms with nice added touch - CD Player, bathrobes, bathtub and shower stall. Staff at hotel provides great service, alway accomdating to guest needs. Very convenient to shopping and tourist spots - near Michigan Ave and Lake Michigan.

(The wedding was not at the hotel).

A pure European taste reminding us good old days.

From the perspective of someone that used to live in NY, the location is fabulous. The staff were exceptionally friendly and helpful. The room was lovely. The bed was super comfortable. Was passing through town on a long road trip to visit family with friends and stopped at this hotel for a room .. EXCELLENT staff and very clean hotel with quite, comfortable rooms. Will stop at this hotel again when I'm in the area

This is our third visit to -S Seattle. We're spoiled, and you will probably see me replicating this review for any -S property.

We made the trip to New York last weekend to see a few days of tennis at the US Open in Queens. The Andaz on -th was a perfect location for us. Easy access to pretty much every Manhattan subway line, and a --line station right in Bryant Park across the street to get out to Flushing Meadows for tennis each day. We ate breakfast at the restaurant two mornings, and while expensive, it was very tasty. The best part of all, though was the service. If they had not given me the Doubletree Chocolate Chip cookie upon check-in I might have forgotten it was part of the chain. The rooms were nicely upgraded from a standard DTree. This hotel has no connection with any European hotels of similar name. We were there for five nights on holiday. 
Our room, which overlooked the swimming pool, had a somewhat tired appearance. There was white debris on the carpet when we arrived which was only removed on the third day after we had rearranged furniture so that it could not be overlooked. We asked for a fridge and a large noisy one with a very bright light on the front was provided. There was no microwave available. There were no extra pillows, which for someone with arthritis was unhelpful and unusual. 
As the location is only three blocks from Times Square the position of the hotel is very convenient. It is also good for exploring Hell's Kitchen and Restaurant Row. There is a nearby subway station. If you like walking you can get quite easily around a lot of Manhattan on foot from the hotel. 
There was a very helpful girl in the gift shop who went to a lot of trouble in helping us to book our shuttle to Newark on our last day. She deserved praise and got it from us.

After extensive research, my partner and I booked into the Inn New York City for a - day trip in Sep ----. If you have already spent many hours looking for somewhere good to stay then stop looking - you need to stay here.
We arrived early (flying in from UK) c -pm, so dropped our luggage and went for lunch while they finished the room. (Check-in is stated as -pm so this was fine). We got back at -pm, and all our luggage was already in the room, a complimentary bottle of fine, fresh cakes-pies, etc.

The kitchenette works well, and complimentary items and continental breakfast was a nice touch. You could easily buy food locally, prepare and eat-in every night if you wanted.
The hotel is a short walk from the ---Broadway Subway which takes you anywhere you need to go. There is a fine deli-pharmacy nearby. We walked to the Lincoln Center and Central Park in a few minutes.

The Chandler is in an excellent Manhattan location.

My room was fairly small but this is not unusual in Manhattan and iIt had everything you could wish - and more besides. The bathroom was quite big, clean and had good toiletries. Everything was clean and well looked after, bed linen was excellent quality.
My only slight complaint is that they only offer a full breakfast menu. If, like me, you just want coffee, fruit juice and a pastry, you have to go outside - or pay the full price. Overall I would recommend this without hesitation and would love to stay again.

Again, the rooms look brand new, were perfectly clean, the bed was comfortable (typical Hilton) and all the amenties you would need. Plenty of good restaurants in the area. We ate at Mike Ditka's restaurant (and he actually came in and ate a few tables from us) and the food & atmosphere was great. We had drinks on the --th floor of the John Hancock building - which on a clear night is spectacular. 
Overall, this is an excellent choice for the Magnificient Mile area of Chicago.

One less fortunate aspect was that it's not easy to come by a taxi out front and the staff just watched me walking aimlessly around with my luggage rather than offering to hail one for me. Alas, the noise was a deal breaker. Although I love the neighborhood, I won't be back to the Nolitan!

The valet parking is expensive (as might be expected from the center of a densely popiulated city) but worked as advertised and was not unduly slow for a property that does not have a parking lot or garage on the premises.

Oh, the shower! It spits. The location might be enough to sway me to stay here again, but it would have to be a good rate. I gotta have a good or even decent shower, folks...

For the price, there are plenty of other really nice hotels in the same area. I would not stay here again unless they did some serious renovation.

I traveled to San Diego with my boyfriend in November ----. He was working in San Diego for the week and his company put him up in the Marriott Residence Inn. I came along to spend time with him and to see San Diego.
We had a rental car, which was necessary since this hotel's location is not central at all. It is about -- minutes from downtown San Diego. But driving around San Diego provided that you need a car regardless, and we found cheap-free-plentiful parking everywhere so this was never a problem. In fact, having a hotel further away forced us to explore more which was appreciated.
The hotel room was spacious and clean, with a comfortable bed. A full kitchen with necessary supplies, flat screen tvs and standard bathroom complete the setup. I found the desk to be perfect for doing work during the day, with an upgraded office chair. 
There is a small gym with good equipment, a nice pool and a hot tub. There is also a barbeque that you can use and a working fire pit which the staff set up every night. This was a very cozy touch.
I was particularly impressed with the lobby layout and breakfast bar. The choices for breakfast were plentiful, healthy, hearty and tasty. Both American and European tastes were well represented with hard boiled eggs, fresh eggs, hash browns, breakfast meats, yogurts, granola, muffins, oatmeals, fresh fruit, cereal, make your own waffles etc. I think that this is one of the best breakfasts I have ever enjoyed! And a nice touch for travelers staying longer is that every day they varied one or two of the items to keep the selection interesting.
It was never too crowded and all the items were really fresh. The coffee was good and they kept it fresh and hot (and available!) all day. 
The lobby-breakfast area had comfortable varied furniture, including plugs for working (and free wifi), a fireplace and a nice flatscreen tv. It was very cozy and in the evening they had free dinners and drinks for guests to relax with.
Most importantly, I found the staff at this hotel to be extremely courteous and friendly. Requests were handled promptly and the hotel had thought of many small details to increase the comfort of their guests. I am very satisfied with my stay.

The morning complimentary breakfast was very nice with a very large selection. The rooms were clean inside. The only downside was the pile of trash bags (literally as tall as myself) on the corner of -th and the trash in and around a nearby nightclub... for that matter I notice the entire city of New York was having trouble with a lot of trash on the street. This is probably something that the Hampton has no control over as the area directly in front of the Hampton was very nicely decorated and clean.

We had a wonderful getaway weekend atop Nob Hill ... at an amazing price of only $--- per night, booked just a few days before our trip. Now, taxes and parking ($--) are the usual San Fran awful ... and food and bev at the hotel are pricey. However, if you just use it for lodging and rest, you cant beat the Stanford Court.

We would stay there again.

 The shuttles ran all the time, and they even had one with a wheelchair lift, so we didn't have to walk on the skybridge to the terminal. I plan to stay here next time.

Just reinforcing the views from previous reviews.
If you have a car, stay here or the Columbus. Both the locations are great, very clean and comfortable. This hotel is going through an upgrade, so the well worn carpets will be history. You can walk to Union Street as well as Chestnut St. where restaurants and shops are aplenty. For the jogger- runner, the Presidio and Crissy Field are great routes . How wonderful to have the Golden Gate Bridge constantly in your sight.
Try for a room on the side or back.
Enjoy SF.
Really enjoyed my stay here. Great hotel with super restaurants. Excellent for UT and not far too downtown Austin

Our room had two massive double beds, HDTV, free wi-fi and a free to use safe. The air conditioning in the room made our stay very comfortable as we visited when it was extremely hot. The staff at the hotel were very helpful and friendly allowing us a late check out and organising transport back to Newark airport. 
While the price was not the cheapest in the world, i think it was very good value for money for a hotel in Midtown. I would definately stay in this hotel if i visit New York again.

Hampton inn times square south was great value for money. The staff were helpful and friendly and the rooms were always spotless. The free breakfast, whilst quite simple, was convenient. I would stay there again.

We stayed three nights in Radisson Blu Aqua. Our room had a very modern, stylish features combined with eclectic design and attention to detail. A room minibar was available to us as well. As a green tea lover I appreciated the possibility to have organic Rishi tea in room. The room was very spacious with bay windows and a balcony. Bathroom was equipped with rain shower and a tub. Beds are very comfortable. Even though our room was facing east we had a very good view of Millenium Park. The hotel has very helpful staff. The Filini restaurant has attentive servers and serves all kinds of breakfasts which are reasonably priced. The hotel swimming pool has only two lanes but the indoor gym is big, clean and is equipped as a regular gym with free weights, cardio and machines (not a hotel one) with sauna and steam. Conveniently located from public transportation. All downtown attractions can be reached by foot in very short time.

Room = Problems. The room was good size with the normal living and bedroom area. Needs some updating (carpet and living room furnuiture come to mind first). Gym - Functionally decent.

Overall the hotel needs some work, especially on the bug business. I realize it's a city hotel and that bugs are existent, but they need to get that under control STAT! Business center was good, appreciated the internet connection in the lobby area. Staff was pleasant and tried their best to accomodate, but it is what it is....family flop hotel in need of some updating and a good exterminator.

The hotel was lovely. The room was attractive, comfortable and clean. Wish there was an indoor pool. While the pool is heated, it is in a windy area and the day I went to the pool was pretty chilly. The restaurant was comfortable, which, as a solo traveler, I greatly appreciated. The service and food were great. 
The only negative I experienced was that I was a little miffed that connecting to the internet cost $--.-- a day. This price wasn't worth it during a family visit. Had to play catch up after the trip.

I have spent the last - weeks at the Hotel Indigo in Dallas. I love this hotel. The staff and management are great. They always make you feel welcomed and at home. The rooms are comfortable and give you the feeling of being in a cottage. everything about this hotel is great. I travel to Dallas a lot and will always stay there.

My benchmark is the cleanliness of the liquid waffle machine ( a gooey concoction found these days in most complimentary breakfast offerings) - normally a mess at most hotels. The hotel is close to the Metro Mall and it offers a wide variety of places to eat in the evening. I had no issues at all with noise despite the proximity to Interstate --.
A well managed property where people genuinely care - a hotel I would stay at again and recommend.

The good: The Roaring Fork restaurant had amazing steaks and salads. No kidding. Might be the best NY strip I've had in ages. I'd almost be tempted stay at this fairly dumpy place just for the food. Great location, though, and very nice staff. In fact the staff should be commended for soldiering on at such a past-its prime property.
I think this is what happens when a hotel gets greedy and decides to see how long they can wait before they have to do a remodel. Well, they waited too long on this one and have subsequently damaged their reputation.

Excellent location accross the street from Copley metro station. Nice continental breakfast included, free internet service for guests. Enjoyed the clean modern art decor rooms. Good value for money as Boston hotels are expensive.
nicely decorated hotel. Room service is slow. There's a big supermarket nextby and there were trucks loading at night time. A bit noisy.

On Union Square, amazing location, good service, great room, wonderful view from the restaurant. I don't have anything else to say but RECOMMENDED! Much better than Westin St Francis. ;)

Overall, it is a very nice hotel with upscale service. Highly recommended.

The Michelango was beautiful and the staff top-notch. I intend to stay there next time I'm in NYC. We were upgraded to a junior suite for $-- more and it was a lovely room. Great decor and nice touches.
