This is the second time I've stayed at this hotel (amazing price from Hotwire both times), and I can't tell you how pleased I am. Not only does it have everything you'd expect from a nice hotel (modern and attractive decor, comfortable bed, fabulous pillows), but the thing that really makes me love it is all the little extras. They really go out of their way to make everything as comfortable as possible. Like the quality Neutragena products in the bathroom-- including a face wash and facial moisturizer (with SPF!) that I would actually use on my face; a real rarity from a hotel. Or the nice Wolfgang Puck coffee maker that lets you make one or two (very good) cups at a time. Little things like that. Also, the staff goes out of their way to make sure you're happy. On my most recent visit, for example, they happily exchanged a six-pack of Sam Adams that had been in our car for a six-pack of ice-cold Sam Adams from the bar. 
In addition to the great comfort, they also had really good security, which I appreciated. (Even though the name of the hotel is Dearborn, it's actually in Detroit, but just barely so you shouldn't let that put you off.) A keycard is required in the elevator to access the upper floors, and when someone calls for your room number they're required to supply your name as well in order to be connected.
Overall, a great place to stay; I can't wait to go back.

Great location...nice accomodations...good service...but there were enough small annoyances that added up to spoil the overall experience for me. Here's the good and the bad.
Good: 
-. You really can't beat the location...you're close to Grand Central Station, Time Square, the UN. Walking distance to everything. Great shopping, theater, restaurants.
-. The rooms are very nicely appointed and decent size for NYC. I had a Junior Suite on the --th floor. Furnishings are nice. Bed-mattress are good. Bathrooms are a very good size. Wasn't expecting a bidet (but maybe that should be expected in a international destination like NYC?). 
-. And the employees were solid...but that takes us to the bad. Because I depended on the Hilton people to give me their very best because I had a couple issues as you'll see.
BAD:
-. You need to do some research and look into parking options before you arrive. Parking is over $-- a night with no in-out priviledges. Find a parking lot before you come. The bellman was very nice and I appreciated him making sure that I had all the facts on cost before leaving my car with him at the curb. I get the impression that overnight parking in the neighborhood lots was probably about $--.
-. When I checked in, the front desk clerk verbally confirmed that I was there for two nights. But when I came back to the room after breakfast the next day, my room key wouldn't work. I supposed it was just demagnetized but was surprised when hotel security met me at the front desk and informed me that no -- he had locked me out of my room because he didn't show a second night's reservation. I showed them both my email confirmation from Hilton and my company travel agency showing two nights and relayed my previous conversation with the front desk clerk and they corrected it -- BUT why did it take four Hilton employees, and -- minutes and why was the only explanation I received that there was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""glitch"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in the system.
-. I'm here on business. My time is precious to me. As a Diamond member, you're given a breakfast coupon. It's your typical Hilton buffet breakfast which is fine, but I was in a bit of a hurry. No time for a true sit down breakfast. I wanted to just grab a couple things and a cup of coffee and head back to my room to finish getting ready but was told that if I wanted to do that, I needed to call room service?? Are you kidding? You won't let me take my danish, my fruit and a cup of coffee and be on my way? That was ridiculous. 
-. Room wasn't cleaned until close to -pm but perhaps that was due to the reservation snafu. It was eventually cleaned and cleaned well. 
-. Business Center -- Huh? -- cents a minute to use the PC to check into my flight? Printing out a boarding pass costs what per page? (I haven't seen something like that in years. Good hotels recognize budgeting the expense of operating a business center as a cost of courting business travelers. The Hilton Manhattan East should eliminate this kind of nickle and diming. I certainly don't see it at their other properties so it surprised me. 
-. Older hotel -- okay so the elevator never lines up exactly with the floor you land on and you have a tiny speed bump to manuever over coming in and out of the elevator. No biggee. 
-. Old pipes -- okay, so I have to hold the handle down on the toilet and it doesn't so much flush with a whoosh! but rather it drains (to be clear and fair -- it works, just not as well and as fast as one would hope)
So those negative things are all small but combine them all over one stay and it results in me writing a very rare semi-negative review for Hilton. I love the Hilton family. I'll certainly give the Hilton Manhattan East another chance. The things they did well are truly the important things. Maybe it was a fluke. I'd be happy to provide an update after my next stay.

I really want to give the hotel a great review. I tend to search out boutique hotels wherever I go. Funky can be very nice. There is a lot to like about the the place. The decor was whimsical and fun. The bed was comfortable with plush bedding and clean crisp sheets. The bathroom was very cute with a true art deco throwback theme. The staff were super helpful and polite. The view was superb. The location awesome.
But there was a gaping fault: cutting corners in maintenance that gave the place a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cheapness factor."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Under the exterior window in my room was significant water damage. I don't know if the window had been left open during a previous rainstorm (or a few storms) because the wall underneath it was disintegrating. The drywall was crumbling and I could see deep into the wall. It really looked bad. I could say it started to spoil the stunning view out the window. It wasn't a small spot that could be overlooked. The damage covered several feet, the whole wall sagged and there was damage to the window sill as well. I can't imagine this had just happened (it wasn't wet) or that the management didn't know about it. This sort of dilapidation is something you find in a roach motel not a -.- star $--- dollar room. 
The thing that was most incongruous was the fact other parts of the room were very nice and well maintained. Why the blinders to this gaping fault? Was it cheapness?
Some other things that might drive customers away. The upholstered furniture in the common areas of the lobby should be shampooed more often because there were darkish dirt spots on the top of chairs where people's hands often touched (you know... those pink squarish chairs in the lobby photos). Again... gives an impression of cheapness and isn't that tough to make right! Exterior paint on older wood-framed windows of basement bar was rotten and looked bad... Repeat... cheapness factor. (To give the hotel credit on this one... they mentioned on the website that there is a future - million dollar exterior renovation scheduled!)
Having said all this, I would like to emphasize that with a little attention to detail this hotel was just inches from being an EXCELLENT experience. If they didn't cut corners in certain detail areas I would say it was worth every penny and definitely could measure up to its -.- star rating. 
Here is to hoping!

My husband and I stayed here from March -- to --. We have no complaints about the hotel. We used the kiosks near the front desk to check ourselves in, and the phone in our room to check ourselves out. We had a queen room on the --th floor near the elevator and although we could hear the elevators going up and down, it was not loud enough to keep us up at night. We couldn’t hear any street noise.

Bring comfy shoes and a spring jacket; the weather was gorgeous.

We had stayed at the Drake a year before so were excited to see how the two hotels compared (the Drake is right across the street). The staff were extremely friendly. The room was pretty small, but more updated than the Drake's guestrooms. The bed was very comfortable and so nice to plop down on after a night of walking the Mag Mile! The hotel's location is perfect. All in all, you can't go wrong with the Millennium Knickerbocker.

We stayed at the Affinia Dumont on a recent trip - day to New York. We chose the hotel based on Trip Advisor reviews and were not disappointed. The staff were extremely welcoming and helpful, we had little cause to make any requests, but when we did they were dealt with promptly. We had a suite, which was spacious and certainly more than adequate for the three of us, (two adults and our - year old son). Our son was extremely impressed by the option of having a sound pillow!! The rooms were clean and well serviced. 
We had breakfast at the 'Barking Dog' which has an extensive menu and again excellent and efficient service. we also ate a couple of times at the 'Cinema Cafe' (couple of minutes walk away), which we would also recommend for food and service
We found the location of the Affinia Dumont perfect for our requirements. We could walk to nearby attractions, (Empire State building, Times Square, Maceys ...). And chose to take a taxi when we went further afield, (hailed by the doorman). The subway is also accessible.
Overall we had a fantastic trip and would definitely both recommend the Affinia Dumont and choose to stay there should we return to New York.

If you have a reason to stay on the East Side (Third Avenue in the vicinity of --nd Street), this could be the hotel for you. Rooms are a tad small, but the bed is mega-comfortable. The neighborhood has plenty of bars and restaurants within walking distance. The conceirge was extra-helpful with requests for information about the neighborhood.
Paid a bit under $--- for the room, which is not high by New York standards. Still, I've stayed in almost as good for a lot less. If you can get a deal on a room here, it's worth it.

We stayed at the Hotel Mela at the end of May for four nights. Our room wasnt ready on arrival but the check In process was pretty efficient and staff were ok too.
The problem with this hotel is the size. We were given a room which was absolutely tiny...and i mean tiny. We have stayed in rooms described as small before but this was as joke. We barely had room for the suitcases on the floor it was more like a cell!
After a call down to the front desk I was informed that we would have to pay for an upgrade. I was pretty annoyed with the hotel by this point but then miraculously they managed find a bigger room in the same category...so no extra charge. This new room was much much better. Far more room, looking out onto the street and enough room to sort outselves out in.
So thats the bad bit. The good points:
Great location - less that - minutes walk to Times Square. Very central, walking distance to many sites like Rockerfeller, Grand Central Station, Macy's etc...
Rooms are generally very clean, modern with nice bathrooms. The LCD TV is also a nice touch. We didnt try any of the food as Times Square is right outside.
Overall its a good choice provided you get a nice room. If I had to stay there again I would have to be guaranteed a decent size room before I booked.

My -- year old daughter and I stayed here for a week. As other reviews state, the surroundings are not the best, but we the rest of the plus points made up for it. With regards to getting around, we found the hotel well situated as the subway at the end of the street took us wherever we wanted to go. The room was absolutely perfect for us, and the kitchenette was particularly useful as we didn't want to eat out every day. Breakfast was great and we didn't find the crowds a problem. We did have some very noisy neighbours, but only for a couple of nights. All of the staff were exceptionally helpful and pleasant. Due to some fairly poor weather, we extended our stay at a very reasonable price. I would highly recommend this hotel.

Stayed at this hotel weekend of May ----- to attend Rockies games. The location is not ideal for doing things downtown, and it's a little difficult to find given all the one-way streets. Overall, this hotel is OK if you don't mind being out of the way from where most things are downtown. But, the beds are so very uncomfortable, I will never stay there again.
On the plus side - the staff were very nice.

We booked this hotel for New Years Eve stay with friends as we had to be """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""close"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to Union Square and preferred to be away from TS madness. I would definitely stay again without hesitation the location for Soho-West Village shopping and restaurants ad yes even Union Square - can't be beat.

Only real negative would be the small size of the room. Other suggestion: better bathroom amenities; better soundproofing (heard people in other rooms and the hall, waking us up at night). Probably smaller than average room for the price in NYC. But otherwise a wonderful hotel. Comfortable mattress. Great desk chair (Humanscale). Clean and bright room. Bathroom amenities were just average, nothing special. Nice buffet breakfast in the restaurant on the top floor. Water Dispenser in the hall was a good touch. Extremely friendly staff.

We had a flight into LA that arrived about -am. Then we left early the next day around --am. We spent the night here, and it was just perfect for what it was- a convenient airport hotel. It was clean, comfortable and easy to use. The breakfast that is included was just fine and exactly as one would expect. I would recommend this hotel very much if you need to overnight at LAX.

We were invited to a wedding at the New York palace and made it our homebase for our first trip to New York. The location is perfect, right in the middle of everything. A very busy two days but we always had a great comfy place to come back to. The trees, lights, flowers and staff made our experience very memorable. We look forward to visiting the city again.

Average overall but was fine for our needs. Thought we would be in a Japanese hotel but really just a refurbished hotel from the --'s with japanese decor. Still, staff all very pleasant. You really can't beat the location of this hotel, right on State Street in the loop! We had a wonderful stay over the weekend. Our room was very nice, with the decor being modern. The Tremont was clean and comfortable. The beds are new and fabulous. I felt completely safe in this hotel, everyone on staff was polite and friendly. I easily walked the six blocks to the Inner harbor, and a little further to Fells Point and Little Italy. Being on the --th floor offered a great view.

The Orchard was perfect for us. A relaxed and quiet atmosphere. The room was spacious and very clean with a good sized bath, and, everything worked including the free wi-fi. Staff were all very friendly and helpful including good suggestions re places to eat. The location couldn't have been better - two blocks to Union Square and two more to Market Street, and right on the Powell Street cable car line, yet still relatively quiet. The only thing we felt that could use improvement were the nature and quality of the offerings in the restaurant. If we return to San Francisco, we'll stay at the Orchard.

We stayed here twice, at the beginning and end of our trip. Clean location and reasonably quiet.. Literally within a ---minute walk of the El Paso Airport terminal building. The halls are a little run-down (wallpaper peeling off the walls) but the rooms are clean and the beds are comfortable. The first room they put us in had faulty air conditioning but I reported it to the front desk and they switched us to another room right away. Standard free breakfast with frozen waffles, cereal, etc. Lots of restaurants and other services within a --minute drive away.

Stayed at this hotel in April ----. Got a nice room which was clean and comfortable. They serve excellent hot breakfast which is worth a lot. Check in took very long, because the hotel didn't have enough people at the front desk. I pity the lady who did what a few people should have done together.

We stayed at the Hilton in Austin during a two week tour of Texas. We went all over the state from Austin all the way out to Big Bend and back through Dallas. We stayed at several hotels this being the best. The hotel is nice and clean. The location is nice in that you are not right on -th St but only a short walk over. The staff was friendly and willing to accomodate to your needs. There are plenty of hotels to chose from in Austin but I think the Hilton or Driskill would probably be your best choice. They are a little more expensive than some but the old saying, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""you get what you pay for"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" stands out.

Was an older building but super nice staff and great location right off Union Square Park…. Lots to do and great places to eat right outside the door. Will go back when I'm in New York. Great delis !!!!

absolute worst hotel i have ever stayed in! I wouldnt stay here again even if you payed me to. The staff was extremely rude and the shower walls had mold on them. too much noise throughout the hotel! The manager jason was rude and acted like he could care less about less complaints. I guess its just shocking for a manager to be ok with noise in the hallways and mold on the shower walls.
If you want one place to rest & relax with family, this is it!

I've stayed in inexpensive motels and hotels plenty my entire life. They're not impressive but sometimes you just need a place to stay that has a clean bed and bathroom. I was shocked at how disgusting this place was. We booked our trip through Expedia for $---night for a conference we were attending in San Jose.

But the rooms were disgustingly gross and dirty. The bed sheets were clean, but that was about it. (I even saw the cleaning lady put sheets in the on-site washer). The bathroom, carpets, walls, everything else had not been cleaned. 
You get out of the shower and your wet feet created dirty footprints on the white bathroom tiled floor. Just to be clear, my feet had been in socks and shoes all day...they weren't creating the dirt, the floor was already dirty. 
After the shower footprint incident, I wore socks or shoes the entire time I was in the room to create a barrier between my feet and the floor and worst carpet I've ever seen in my life. There were clear water stains all of the carpet and they were dark and very dirty looking. 
The walls in the room and bathroom had dirty marks and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""stuff"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on them. The ironing board cover was stained and I had to put a towel down on top of it so I could iron my shirt. You get the picture.

Located close to town. The approach is bit disorienting as you pass by a abandoned building. The Hotel looks pretty much used but our queen bed room was fine and clean.
Our room was on the -th floor the shared balcony that run all around the building offers a nice view at the Mississippi river. Service is really minimal. But you get what you pay for.

I am a very loyal SPG consumer, so when I recently needed to travel to San Fran for personal reasons, I decided to cash in some points for some free nights. I stayed at the Palace, and although the location is good, the lobby is beautiful, and the value is okay (that should have been my tip off for the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""luxury collection""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""), I would have preferred to stay somewhere else. I lifted it at some point and saw that they had put boards under the mattress to make it firmer. I was disgusted that a hotel that was in the luxury collection could have fallen to such a level. Stay at either the Westin St. Francis or the Westin on Market -- you will have a much better stay. Avoid this hotel.

Then, it's quite love-less for a W, both service-and design wise, not very spectacular from the outside, not particularly special in the rooms.
Our room was a fairly large and expensive one but it let us down on several levels that we wouldn't expect from a W, mouldy corners in the bathroom and toilet, left-over painter's tape on the shower head and a broken door in the wardrobe not allowing the thing to ever close properly. Yea- if it was so easy! First no one picked up. Then we were promised to get one and waited for -- minutes. Called again, another wait. Oh- one really good thing: The restaurant downstairs was absolutely lovely, great food and totally unexpected in this city. Super-pricey though, just be warned.
Very pleasant stay, right in the centre of things. Be artful on bus tours-they're a rip off as city is so small-do the freedom trail-you see it all anyway

I stayed at this hotel with my wife, our son and her parents. The convenience of the kitchen facilities were perfect as we were travelling with a - month old. 
The first thing we noticed was the wonderful service from the desk staff, very friendly and helpful. When we got to our room on the --rd floor we were all impressed by the size and facilities available, it really was a home from home all topped of with a view of the Empire State Building (which unfortunately I don't get in my home!).
We have to say that there was no issues with cleanliness as our room was immaculate with the bed linen and towels changed regularly. 
The location was good, although it will be fantastic when the new subway line is finished as it will be - blocks from a new station. And although there is construction noise it didn't affect us with the doors and windows shut, and with air con we didn't need them open anyway. But it is only a short walk to the subway, and Central Park is only a few blocks away. Even midtown is walkable and you go past some nice shops and restaurants. 
Everything you need is close by, plenty of little supermarkets to get food and drink. Restaurants closeby are good value and good food.
I cannot recommend this hotel enough, it was everything we needed and hoped for and from our point of view there were no downsides to it.

My family and I stayed at Homewood Suites overnight this past weekend; the location seemed a little weird at first when we drove in (sort of smushed into the back of a strip mall), but in fact we had a very nice stay, and I would highly recommend it. Nice room, clean, comfy bed, good night's sleep. Kids enjoyed the pool, the free breakfast was great. Free wireless, no problems in that department. Not all hotels in the area are as nice-- we discovered this the hard way: after checking out of the Homewood Suites, we drove to the airport... got on the plane.... waited for - hours on the tarmac.... then had to deplane (mechanical problem). Hotel restaurants - Starbucks (long lines) and Urban Tavern (good service and food). 
Overall - good hotel, convenient for a conference but if on vacation, pay the extra money to stay closer to the Fishermans Wharf area where everything is happening.

We had read other travellers reviews and were quite worried about staying here. However i was plesantly surprised with this hotel. The room we had had the most fantstic view of the city. The beds were really comfortable, the room was clean, bathroom cleaned daily. The staff were very friendly, any problems we had were dealt with immediately. Lifts worked well. Hotel organised cabs for return flight, standard fee $-- to Newark.. Lovely area, away from the hustle and bustle but so easy to get into the city, minutes walk to the subway. We used ---rd. Felt very safe at all times of the day. Saved a great deal staying here. Fantastic if all you want is a clean comfortable bed to sleep in, most of your other time should be spent out exploring the city there is just so much to see and do. We will definately be returning.

Didn't like the Oxford.

No real issues other than I want something more modern when paying top $

My wife and I spent a long weekdend in Boston. June --th- July -nd. I did not want to pay center city prices. Since we are avid users of the T, we wanted to be close to a T stop. The made to order included breakfast and the nightly manager's reception was a definite plus. We are Hilton honors members and usuallly gravitate to Embassy Suites. As pointed out by other reviewers there are some differences at this Embassy Suites. You do not have the large atrium with all of the rooms coming off of it. Your room opens onto a hall instead. This eliminates one of my pet peeves found in most Embassy Suites. That is the - AM door slam which tends to reverberate throughout the cavernous atrium. If you are sleeping on the pullout, this is something you can't miss. The rooms are a little smaller, but not to the extent that it causes a problem. They have at least - shuttle busses. (I counted) They are very close to the airport. Our view overlooked the Dollar rent a car lot with the airport in the backround. If you have kids who love planes, you can look out the windows and watch the planes take off. You also overlook the new astroturffed ball fields. Bring your soccer ball and enjoy. The new T station is a very short walk from the hotel. You simply come out the main entrance, cross the street, walk around the fields to the left, and run right into the T station. If you are in Boston for a few days and plan to use the T for your travels, get the - day link pass for only -- dollars. The T is an experience in itself. Lots of people watching and always a station convenient to your destination. Boston is a walking city, and the T helps you to do that. The hotel has a business center with computers for your use. There is a small gym with a couple of treadmills and a few other machines. The pool was mainly frequented by children nonstop. There was supposed to be adult supervision, but I rarely saw any. So if you are an adult looking for a little relaxation in the hot tub, this is not the place for it. I don't fault the hotel for this situation though. Just a product of the me generation. To sum it up, I would use this hotel again in a heartbeat when visiting Boston. P.S. There is a kiosk located by the front desk for you to print out your boarding passes. (very convenient indeed)

the location is the best, room are clean and nice, didn't be upgraded by s.p.g. may be because I took the room with points. I think service could be better. Just love to go out and have dinner in Wisconsin St, great area for shopping and restaurants.

This was a great hotel with friendly, accommodating staff. We stayed for three nights over the Thanksgiving holiday. It was wonderful. The gym and pool are probably the nicest I have seen in a hotel. The location was great. You have skywalks to the Prudential shopping center and the hotel is attached to fine boutique shops. Two tube stations are close to the hotel. Food was very good at the hotel restaurant and reasonably priced. Room service was quick and the attendant was very helpful. Yes valet parking is expensive, but that is the norm for city parking everywhere in the world. The staff was extremely friendly, talkative and helpful. We went away for Thanksgiving break and some rest and relaxation. We were not disappointed. I would go back in a heartbeat.

I have stayed at the Blakely twice now, both times in one bedroom suites. Each time there were three people staying in the rooms. The space was well done and the beds comfortable with a Daybed in the living room. This hotel is well located and has a continental breakfast included.It is not a large hotel and the staff is very helpful. A good restaurant is located on the premises and those staying at the hotel get a discount.

This is an amazing hotel. Architecturally alone it is worth a visit, but the grounds, service, and amenities are top notch as well. Dining was good but not great, but that was the only thing that wasn't exceptional.

We are planning a trip to San Francisco March ---- and I have started looking into different hotels just to try something different but after reading other reviews The Campton Place seems to have most of the others beat. Perhaps the fact that I stayed at the Renoir because it was a sponsor of the nearby Folsom Street Fair shows that I'm not afraid of seeing strange sights on the street. Actually that might sum it up -- if you'd be afraid to go to Folsom, the Renoir or any hotel in SOMA isn't for you. If you enjoy diversity and appreciate businesses that support diversity, consider the Renoir.
However, consider the Renoir for what it is. Compared to other hotels in more touristy areas, it's got cheap rates. For those rates, you get a clean room in a hotel with the style and ambience of an older European hotel (not of an American chain of motels). The area is a bit noisy at times, but the earplugs that were supplied solved that issue. There was no air conditioning (as there is not in most non-chain European hotels), but San Francisco nights are cool, and during the day you should be out and about exploring the city.
The Renoir is very conveniently located in terms of public transit. You can take BART from the airport to the Civic Center station directly across -th St from the hotel. That station also has Muni subway lines. The F line streetcars stop directly across from the hotel on Market Street, and there are lots of Muni buses nearby that go to all parts of the city. If you're a gay tourist, the Castro is only minutes away!
The one complaint I do have about the Renoir is its lack of hot water. The faucets are mis-labeled -- as the friendly maintenance supervisor explained to me, if you turn the shower faucet all the way to the left as it is marked, you'll get nothing but cold water; instead you have to turn it just a fraction and let it run, but unfortunately I never got more than lukewarm water. That, for me, is almost a deal breaker. It was okay for this trip since I was already there, and I got decent rates for Folsom, but I'm not sure that I'll return to the Renoir.

My only quibble was that the standard Queen room was very small and overpriced given how cramped it was. I would recommend getting a larger room when staying at the Brown Palace if you can afford it. We stayed at Hotel Majestic in December ----, the location was great, the antique furniture fabulous , the restaurant and bar at the Hotel are perfect! Our bedroom was very spacious with a nice bathroom. One small complaint...the decor (curtains and carpets etc) was 'dated' and old..they need to be replaced. All in all a good experience and reasonable rate too.

Love it. -- min or less to walk to everything, times square, fao schwarz, empire state building, ect. Very friendly staff. Very clean rooms and bedding. Great breakfast bar with real food not just cereal. Can't wait to stay again.

We stayed overnight the week after Christmas and wish we could have stayed longer. All of the public rooms were beautifully decorated with furnishings appropriate for a home built in the colonial era, and the gas fireplaces made them welcoming and cozy. We were happy to find tea was being served as we arrived and enjoyed unwinding after our trip before one of the fires. We had a delicious and unusual dinner at M Restaurant, which is across the courtyard. The hotel is a couple of blocks to Walnut Street Theatre and a couple more blocks to Independence Hall. Many of the diners at M Restaurant seemed to be planning to go to the theater, because the restaurant was filled early and emptied out before - PM. We had a comfortable, quiet suite that looked out on the courtyard. The staff was very helpful and pleasant.

Not worth the money; over priced, poor quality and service; cheap décor, inexperience wait staff and no hospitality. Skip the Bar Rojo…drinks in plastic cups (and they’re not red solo cups either); the Achiote Restaurant was fair, but I would visit a nearby eatery instead. Don't bother with the internet access - a $ -.-- charge to be dropped every -- minutes was just frustrating. The New Year’s Eve package is not all it promotes itself to be. No one could confirm our dinner reservation, we had to physically go downstairs to the restaurant to do it ourselves. There was NO effort in making the evening special. The only nice thing about this visit was Ramon, Joyce and Julio from the restaurant; JD the bell hop; and Timmy for the pads. Very disappointing…

Needs to get coffee machines in the rooms. New carpet would be nice. Great staff. Awesome views and location is fantastic. Great hotel for pets. Dog park close by. However, the homeless and drug peddlers on the boadwalk takes away from this hotel.

Wife's sister recommended this place as close to her apartment. The place had been remodeled but was still dumpy. No amenities ... had to use a coffee machine near the pool and of course no continental breakfast.
The bed was bad and I was glad to leave after two nites stay. No restaurants within walking distance and scary place at nite there. Glad they had good, secure parking with plently of spaces as hardly anyone was staying there.

I booked a mother-daughter weekend for one night here this past month. I got lost trying to find the inn, called them to let them know we were coming and asked for directions from a fairly uninterested front desk. 
Upon arrival, we found that there was a wedding taking place and a sign on the second floor asking guests to take the emergency exit back staircase and avoid the lobby due to a private event as they use the lobby as part of the events scheduled there. Well, the emergency exit door was locked at the bottom (wouldn't that be dangerous in a fire??) so we had to trek back up the steep stairs and use the lobby stairs - irrespective of any party. (There was no one around when we exited.)
 Impressive in their attention to detail in the guestrooms. However, it is NOISY. You hear everything including the guest in the room next door using the toilet. The baseboards & and room corners were black with accumulated dirt. They just need to be ripped out and redone - or at least repainted.
The morning we were checking out, we asked for directions at the front desk and suggestions on shopping places. But the person at the front desk said they had no idea as they were from out of town!! They couldn't find a city map and ended up giving us the wrong one with no guidance whatsoever. I wouldn't expect that of a small, inn. I probably wouldn't stay here again which is a shame because the innkeepers seemed concerned about details - just not all the correct ones.

We stayed here on a PriceLine bid and for what we paid, felt the hotel was very fine. I would have been disappointed had we paid full price. In our case, the staff was extremely pleasant and helpful. Very friendly reception, many pleasantries and helpful information. Went to lobby later for a wireless kit and they just handed me one. Also was advised where to park my oversized vehicle at no charge. The room was very nicely done, beds were fantastic and work area spacious, well lighted and easy access to plugs and connections. Now, the bathroom really needed some work for sure. The fixtures were pretty creaky, there was a weird drain hole in the ceiling of the shower, the curtain was flimsy and too short for the tub. Having said that, the shower was a wonderful experience (probably thanks to the dated fixtures) with loads of hot and powerful water. We would stay here again in a minute for the right price. Contrary to other posts (perhaps Hilton reads these), we found the staff to be outstanding.

The room was spectacular. The shower a dream. Great breakfast. Nice people. Would definitely recommend highly. I think we got it through Expedia the same day we traveled, so we got a pretty good deal on a huge cool room. Decided to stay another night and had to downgrade to a smaller, regular room, but it was still great.

I Stayed at this hotel for a conference. If my work didn't foot the bill, I would never stay here, because it is way too expensive. However, the service is FIVE star!!!....and you pay for it (from hailing a cab for me, my dealings with front desk, to having room service actually offer to pour my first cup of coffee! And no, I did not accept the offer.....however, maybe I should have enjoyed the service, since my bagel and coffee cost me $--.--!!
 After a -- hour trip from the east coast to the west coast, I developed a cold. I called front desk to see if there was a gift shop on site where I could purchase cold meds. The employee said that there wasn't a gift shop on site, but they would be more than happy to deliver meds to my room. She even told me to feel better. I was so happily surprised that someone actually told me to feel better, I was grinning ear to ear.....(now this is before my bagel-coffee sticker shock)....The doorbell rang to my room within minutes, and a very smiley guy gave me alka seltzer. I was so impressed, that I gave him a $- tip. Then a few minutes later, a follow up call came to the room and again, a friendly voice told me to feel better. WOW, i thought....this is SERVICE. The friendly voice then told me that a $--. charge will be added to my room for the - alka seltzer tablets. A very expensive remedy, but it was worth it, because it worked!! 
The room was beautiful....they had the automatic darkening curtains, which I didn't discover until my -rd night....bathrobes, ironing boards.....and a great little fridge stocked with $- beers and $- M+Ms. I was really, really impressed.....the only tiny thing that freaked me out was the hair on the sheets......so I just moved to the other bed and didn't say a word about it. I can't wait to re-visit Seattle and I would definitely recommend this hotel to others!

Stayed this past Saturday night, thanks to an amazing deal on priceline! The rooms are small, but so nice. Great decor, color scheme, bed, linens, lighting. Wonderful bathroom, really nice. The service was wonderful checking in and out, all around wonderful service. Went to the Padres game Sunday, and they held our bags. Free street parking after -:-- pm on Saturday and all day Sunday, so you can't beat a Saturday stay over. Would definitely stay again and recommend to others.

In the heart of timesquare, best location. In the city that never sleep, you would never notice the time in this area. I am out shopping until -AM and so much happenning round the clock. The hotel is very secure, the staff are friendly. We booked a suite and the room is big, clean and comfortable. So many restaurant, shops and theatre that'll keep you occupied. Best place to stay in Manhattan.

As the final part of our journey down Route -- we decided to return to San Diego again having stayed here (in another hotel) - years ago, plus we do not like Santa Monica (we stayed -- minutes to take photos at the end of the Mother Road).
We stayed here for - nights on the basis of the location and comments. I was slightly concerned about some of the review comments about the trains and trams - my concerns were well founded.
We had two rooms, one facing the back and the train lines and the other on the side facing down town. I heard the first trains and tried to move rooms but no others were available that night. My Wife usually sleeps through most noise but this room was the exception. Neither of us slept all night - what a racket these trains make - hooting and tooting all night long - and during the day. Our Daughters stayed in the other room and were also wakened but not as much. We moved next day into a side facing room which was a bit quieter but we still never got a full sleep.
It's a real shame because in every other way this hotel is great. It has an integral car park, a swimming pool facing the sea - naval base, fantastic complimentary breakfast and is within walking distance of down town. You can take the trams but at $- a ride why bother - the exercise does you good.
Perhaps double glazing is needed to cut out the noise or the toiletries should include earplugs but that would be unsafe - you might not hear the fire alarm.
So if you are a trainspotter this hotel will do you fine, if you are a light sleeper (like me) then perhaps the Holiday Inn just over a bit from this hotel and further away from the trains is the better choice - it's where we will go next time. It's a real shame that the hotel was built so close to the rails - see my photos.

After reading the reviews on tripadvisor I was a bit weary of this hotel but as we had booked online our room was non refundable. Upon arriving I was pleasantly surprised! The atrium is now decorated tastefully and the front desk staff were wonderful. We were in town for a convention and the location made it very easy to catch the tram to the convention center. The bartenders and room service were wonderful and prompt. The room we had was river front and a suite definately worth the money! I have stayed at many Wyndhams and while this was not the best (it is still under construction for rennovation) it is certainly not as bad as i had feared. 
I would definately recommend this hotel to anyone in the area, and also to dine next door at the Chart House the food was incredible!!!!

The property is nice and seems new - large, clean rooms with no smell of mildew that is so typical these days of an older or poorly maintained property. Front desk friendliness was a mixed bag - I know I should remember the names of the friendlier staff, but for some reason I only remember the one who refused to make eye contact (Yvonne, I think her name was).
Housekeeping could use some improvement. Despite my request for extra soap, shampoo and conditioner, there was none provided for the second day. Coffee-condiments were not refilled either. Food that was accidentally spilled the previous night was not vacuumed. 
Breakfast was average at best: eggs seemed a bit raw with chunks of over-cooked pieces, muffins seemed a little dated and fruit was limited to unripe bananas and apples.
Location next to the airport comes with its negatives, but with Houston's no-zoning philosophy, you can't find the perfect location anyway.

Hotel room is very roomy but the upkeep is lacking. Rooms airconditioning was not sufficient to cool the room in summer and there was no hair dryer in the room ( a feature that I expect in any american hotel).
The roof top bar is nice, and worth a visit.

Had a two night stay at the hotel. It was just after the renovations and was lovely. The bathroom was a little small, but the room was fine for two people. There was a great pool and spa and a nice little cafe-restaurant. The hotel is a little out of the city which meant the cab rides were a little more than you would like. Staff were very friendly

beautiful, modern, european looking hotel. The suites are large enough for a family, seperate bedroom and living room, large TV in each room. Each room has privacy. Location is close to O'Hare airport and shuttles run every -- minutes. I got the room on priceline for half of what it was listed on the website. Highly recommend this hotel.

Love the location - just off Times Square and theatre district - but if you book here - ask to be located in the Annex - it is the newer part of the hotel. The main part of the hotel is hit and miss with rooms - some of them are in serious need of renovation.

Booked this place due to its location and proximity to the event I was attending and for the great price. The location is very good, right on the Mall. The lobby was obviously just redone, and looks very nice. It included several computers and a place to hook up your laptop since FREE WIRELESS IS ONLY AVAILABLE IN THE LOBBY! How can a major hotel undergo such an extensive renovation and not even have internet in the rooms?!! Oh wait, the front desk said there is internet in the rooms and for a fee in the form of WEB TV. Ridiculous, because when I have to work on the road, I like to do it in the comfort of my own room. The rooms look nice, and actually the beds are very comfortable, but maybe due to the remodel, many things were still not functioning right. There was no standard book providing us with basic hotel info, such as check-out, amenities, etc. The TV was difficult to work. The bathroom door did not lock, the fan did not work, and the drains were VERY slow. How can this be when everything was just redone?! Anyhow, I only stayed for one night. It was cheap and in a great location, but considering the recent remodel, I expected a better stay with things that were functioning correctly.

Ok 
 Bellperson ignored me and when I asked where is the front desk, he pointed with his finger and didn't even helped me with my luggage. The front desk wasn't helpful either. He didn't even show me my room and where to go. I went to a wrong way and he shouts my name and point with his hand where the elevator is. When I went back to the room, the room view was a construction site with a lot noise. I booked an executive room and I've never been treated like this. So I turned back and went to another - star hotel. What a bad service and an insult.

We stayed for - nights in a connectIng two bedroom suite on the fourth floor overlooking Central Park with our two kids, ages - and --. 
The rooms were very large and although a higher room would have afforded a more expansive view of the park, our kids loved watching the horse carriages, vendors, and tourists walking in and around the park. 
Pros:
Phenomenal service, especially when dealing with the multiple problems with our tvs.
Great location by Central Park, the Zoo, and a very cool water play structure inside the Park.
Beds are beyond comfortable!
Concierge floor lounge serves delicious light breakfast, light dinner, snacks and drinks. 
Cons:
Not overtly kid-friendly. 
Tiny lobby restaurant.
No pool. 
All in all, definitely a touch notch hotel in a very convenient location, but don't go expecting special family amenities.

I live in New York city and wanted to find a nice place to get away in the city for my birthday, so I took a chance and booked a room on priceline, requesting the highest star rating available for the price--I entered, $---. I ended up with a room at the Hilton New York. I figured, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""eh, It's a pretty decent hotel, but nothing spectacular"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I checked in and decided to see if I could charm my way into a bigger room. (I was booked in a pretty small-queen bed room) I told them it was my birthday and that I wanted something more luxurious than my own home and guess what?- they offered me a suite for only $--- extra. AND not just any suite, a ---- sqft PENTHOUSE on the executive floor with a wet bar, A whole wall of amazing bay window views of central park, - bathrooms, a huge bed room, a kitchen. WHAAA???? It was of course worth xtra $---. I truly felt like a rockstar. Hilton's ok in my book. Moral of the story: Ask and you shall receive.

The Beresford Arms Hotel is located in a building on the National Register of Historic Places. This should be your first clue that it is very old. But, while old, it is well taken care of. Our room, one of the Junior Jacuzzi Suites, was VERY clean. 
My first impression when I walked into the room was disappointment. I had expected something a little different based on the description of the aforementioned “Junior Jacuzzi Suite”. I had assumed the beds were in a separate room and that there was a sitting room, but I checked the website again and it said “sitting area”, not sitting room. Of course, we didn’t have a sitting “area” either, but that wasn’t really necessary. The furniture is dated, but as I said the room is quite clean, looked freshly painted and the bathroom was sparkling white. I was pleased that there was very good lighting in our room.
There is no air conditioning in the room. We had three windows that we kept open, but they don’t have screens and on the last morning, all of a sudden, flies started coming in. It was entertaining trying to chase them out! The hotel does provide fans, though, and we had two that we kept running most of the time when we were in the room. There is also a heater if you happen to be there when it’s cold.
The bathroom had new flooring, double sinks and included a bidet next to the toilet! I never did try that out. There is a Jacuzzi tub in the room, which I used several times, but it is a single person tub, so don’t expect to lounge around with your other half if you are there with a significant other. I was there with my mom so this was not an issue. 
There was free wireless Internet access in the room, but it was VERY slow. I had brought my laptop, but I rarely used it because it was just too brutal to do so. They do have two computers in the lobby, though, for guest use and while I didn’t check for sure, I believe it is complimentary. The room has a television with a VCR built in. Apparently they have movies you can rent for $-. If you want to watch a movie, you may want to bring one with you. The TV has few channels, but you have all of the usual local channels and a few national ones like TNT available.
It’s my understanding that the facilities vary room to room as far as kitchenette-wet bar-etc. Our room had a wet bar with a refrigerator, microwave and coffee maker. Interestingly enough, while there were tea bags, and sugar, etc, there was no coffee. It would have been nice if they provided coffee to go with the coffee maker because for only four days, we weren’t going to go hunt down a store with coffee. But, you do have dishes, glasses, mugs, and silverware, so you can easily make things and eat in your room. It would have been nice to have a table to eat at, though, and I think that was part of what I assumed would be in the “sitting area” that was mentioned in the description of the room. 
Each morning they provide coffee and tea downstairs in the lobby, as well as some fruit and pastries. I recommend grabbing the cutting board from your wet bar to take down and use as a tray if you’re bringing things up to your room. It’s a good way to at least have snack before heading out for the day. They also have a wine, tea, and cheese reception each afternoon, but we were so busy that we never even got a glimpse of it so I cannot comment.
The location is great. It is - blocks from Union Square, one block from Geary on the corner of Post & Jones. It’s a gentle incline as you walk from Union Square to get there, but quite a hill if you are walking from Geary. You can be in Union Square in - minutes and to the Powell Street BART station in ----- minutes. I'm not sure if they had parking or not, though, because we did not have a vehicle so I didn't ask. There is no fitness center or pool, but you can get a workout walking up the hills in the area!
There are tons of restaurants around. We really enjoyed Honey Honey, a restaurant one block from the hotel on Post Street that served breakfast lunch and dinner. We only tried the Crepes, but they were delicious and the atmosphere was very nice. We had planned to try Dottie’s True Blue Café, on Jones, around the corner from the hotel, but there was always a line and it was way too silly to wait an hour to be seated for breakfast. Instead, we found the Olympic Café right around the corner on Geary that had fantastic omelets and no line! You won’t be hurting for restaurants in this area. Also, right across Jones is a little market that sells beer, wine, water, sodas, snacks, etc. I was very happy with the location of the Beresford Arms and it was close to bus stops, which was our preferred transportation while in San Francisco.
After four days, my impression of the Beresford Arms Hotel changed. I am very happy we stayed there. Our room was kept spic and span (we did leave a tip each morning on our pillow, which might have helped) the beds & pillows while not quite Marriott or Hilton standard, were very comfortable, and overall, it was a good stay. I would like to have screens on the windows, definitely faster Internet, and maybe some movie channels on the television; I recommend you bring VHS movies with you, microwave popcorn, and a package of coffee if you are a coffee drinker, but the Beresford Arms is a comfortable hotel and we recommend it. We purchased our room as a package deal with airfare through Expedia. The room portion was about $--- for - nights in the Jacuzzi suite with - queen beds. You can get the room cheaper than that, but it depends on the time of year and when you book.

We booked our six nights through Hotels. The check-in was quick and easy. The room was very small and hot when we first arrived. Luckily, there are (noisy) air-conditioners installed in every room, so the temperature was quickly fixed. The rooms are very clean and very tiny. Bed was very comfortable. Our biggest complaint comes from a incident that happened on the third day at - AM. We were still asleep when we woke up in the sound of water splashing on our bathroom floor. I found out the water was coming from upstairs through the ceiling. The water stank bad and sure enough I called the reception right away. They promised to fix the problem ASAP and they surely fixed the leakage quickly, but nobody ever came to clean up the mess in our bathroom (even though they said the problem was fixed). So, a big negative remark for the service in this situation. Also, we never saw any of the receptionists smiling during our stay, so it was not the most pleasant customer service experience altogether. The rooms are clean (unless you count the bad smelling water pouring from upstairs) and the location is great, less than -- meters from a metro stop and --- meters from Empire State building. There is a low-cost internet connection in the lobby. The rooms have fridges which is nice. Our room was quiet which meant it had a lousy view. I would'n go there a second time because of lack of smiles and poor reaction to the aforementioned problem situation. If you have the money, go to a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""real"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel.

We spent the ---- Labor Day weekend at this hotel. It was VERY conveniently located, in an area of town we had not explored previously. Plus they were running a special!
The lobby was lovely. The furnishings in the room were pretty average, as were the bathrooms. Bathroom amenities were excellent. Initial first impression was good.
However, when I turned down the bed, I was surprised to find that the fitted sheet was inside out. Getting up close and personal while I fixed that problem, I noted that there was dust in more than half the corners of the headboard, which was divided into small squares, -- in all, ten were dusty. There was also some kind of (feather, dust, or maybe a piece from a dirty feather duster?) prominent on the middle of the duvet. Closer inspection of the bathroom turned up badly shined polished brass fixtures and mold in two corners of the tub enclosure. The glass doors were spotless, as was the mirror. 
I documented all this and took a copy downstairs to the night manager. He assured me that it would be taken care of on Saturday, and that he would let me know the resolution. Had my doubts, but thanked him and retired.
Guess what! It wasn't taken care of. Not really a surprise, given the fact that it was a holiday weekend. Still a disappointment. 
That said, all the good things at the beginning of the review still hold, and none of the problems were dangerous or life threatening. Unless you have a mold allergy.
And the best part of the trip...Saturday we were truly tired after walking all day and exploring, so we cancelled our reservation at a place our daughter had recommended, and ate at Bistro --- and had a wonderful meal. 
All in all, a bit disappointed, but overall OK

This is definitley not a resort, and isn't near anything, so if you stay here make sure you have a car.
We checked in late and left early, and this hotel met our needs nicely. It's reasonably priced, and the room was large and clean.
The pool and fitness room were adequate. I would stay here again.

I stayed at this hotel in Jan of ---- for - nights. We stayed on the -rd floor. The rooms were nice and clean. No elevators. Rooms decorated in art deco style. Decent sized room for NYC. Hotel located in a residential-resteraunt area. LOTS of great little resteraunts and bars in the area...lots of night life with nice friendly people, no obnoxious dance clubs. You must have your room key to get in the front door and there was always a friendly attendant at the front desk, which made us feel safe. Located within walking distance to times square and close to the theatre district, but I'd rather be a little closer to a subway station, but if it's nice weather then you don't mind walking a bit to save a few hundred bucks.
Breakfast is included in your stay (rare for NYC) and they had a large assortment of fresh pastries, bagles, coffe, tea, juice and muffins.
There were only - things we found to be negative about this hotel:
Our room faced the street, which is VERY noisey -- hrs a day and the walls are pretty thin too! we could hear the people in the next room talking! and people getting back to their room at -am were always noisey in the halls. The second thing was the heat...no thermostat in your room, so you can't control your temp...our room was SO hot the first night...then we learned to leave the window open during the day and it was fine for the last - nights.
All in all if you visting NYC to see the sites this is a great place for you to stay and save some cash! I would recommend.
A nice overall stay. Only one night, so perhaps not long enough to really get a good idea of the hotels amenities. I would stay here again when in NYC

I have stayed at other Residence Inn's, and this one was by far the worst from a room quality persective mainly. Have they renovated yet? Even if so, Residence Inn sells it's product based on how much room you have to spread out, and this was a closet. Rooms in NYC are bigger. Unneeded furniture could have been removed to help this issue. Decor was rather dated, location is ok for -th Street fun, not great. Have stayed at the InterContinental downtown before and that location was great, still teensy rooms though, but that is a historic property so I can accept that. I wouldn't bother with this hotel again. - stars encompasses quite a bit for me - an AVERAGE stay. They were not 'poor' as I didn't get cooties or encounter anything really bad, but if i could -.- would be more like it here. I have stayed at MUCH nicer Fairfield Inn's.

Stayed here recently for - nights and found the hotel really nice. Located conviently for most things in Chicago right on the riverfront. Hotel itself looked fairly modern and staff were really friendly and helpful (we had an error with the phones which we didn't know, and were charged $-- but the staff wiped the bill for us, which was a nice touch). Would definately stay here again!

The hotel is clean enough but the rooms are absolutely tiny. You can barely move in it. The TV is fixed onto the bed and as such I kept kicking it at night. Too expensive for what it's worth. Location is not that bad but there are loads of bums going around. No AC, just a noisy fan. The offer of a bag with a condom and sex lube was a bit awkward.

This is my -nd night of a --night stay for business. The office I'm working in is a --minute walk, so that's wonderful. The breakfast buffet is quite expensive, $--.-- for food that was simply mediocre. Dinner, on the other hand, wasn't overpriced. I had seafood linguini for $--. The only thing is, it wasn't fantastic by any stretch. One thing I'm very impressed with is the service and the attitude of the staff: absolutely wonderful! Right now it's -:-- p.m. on a Wednesday night and in my -nd floor room I have been hearing the sounds of a jazz band playing downstairs for the past couple of hours. I can even feel the bass through the floor. I'm hoping it ends soon. Definitely ask for a higher floor. The rooms are just OK. Fine, but nothing exciting. One cool thing is that there's a mini fridge in each room. Another great thing is there's free Internet in every room. The rooms definitely have a ----s feel to them. No flat panel TVs, peeling wallpaper, an alarm clock that's completely uncomprehensible. One more thing: You can hear doors slamming at night. My recommendation is putting a bathroom towel under the door (there's a large gap).

As a Priority Member I am generally always satified by the hotel experience marketed by the Crowne Plaza and IHG. In this case my pick-up at the airport was timely, but my check-in was great. Gary and Tim provided the welcome smiles and chatting needed after a long day of work and travel. The bonus discount dinner coupon on top of the free coctail coupon was the icing on he cake.
We spent a recent Saturday night and enjoyed it tremendously. Hotel is in a great location and the staff is top notch. Rooms are very nice and have a great view of the city. Will definitely be back!

The Grand Hyatt has a gorgeous lobby, and the rooms and service were very good and the location was great. The only reason I decided to write a review was because I thought people should know what the pool situation is. The pool is not very large and if you're there like we were during cherry blossom time, it will be packed in the evenings. We never went because there was a line of parents with kids waiting for someone to leave so they could get in. I can't imagine it was a great place to be either if it was that crowded. If a pool is important to you or you are picking this place because it has one, be sure you aren't here at a busy time.

The Westin is located just a couple of minutes walk from central Times Square and within a ---- minute walk of Hells Kitchen which has a brilliant selection of restaurants and is a bit less touristy than the Times Square restaurants. Also very close to the Port Authority bus station which is useful if you're planning on any outings! 
We stayed on the --th Floor and had a beautiful view over the Hudson river, on a clear day we could see for miles! 
The rooms are a little tired but are a good size and were clean, we had - double beds (they aren't as big as normal Amercian doubles) and enough space for - girls & all our clothes-shoes! There wasn't a mirror above the dressing table (obviously a room designed by a man!!) so doing make up etc was a bit tough in the bathroom- as the last review said the lighting isn't great but we made do. No trouble with noise or anything, all we could hear were police-ambulance sirens which I guess is to be expected in a busy city! 
Overall I would return and would recommend for a reasonably priced hotel in a great spot.

I stayed here for a leisure weekend to see a concert at the nearby TD Northbank stadium. It you are in town for an event at the stadium, this hotel is very convenient as it is within walking distance. However, if you rented a car, the parking price here is expensive: $---day. Besides that, they tell you to call -- minutes in advance to have your car brought around, but at least once, it took longer than that because the valet had brought the wrong car. Also, at one point, the valet gave me the keys for another car. The room itself is a bit on the small side, but the décor and layout of the room is quite lovely. One thing I would say is that there are too many pillows for such a small room. The leopard print bathrobes are a nice touch. There are also socks you can buy hung up in the closet. The drinks in the minibar were not cold (I think the fridge may have been broken). The personnel are friendly, and always ask if there is anything they can do for you. Someone will email you shortly before your stay to stock your room with your favorite beverage and newspaper-magazine which is a nice touch. The bath products are Aveda and very nice. I needed to print-sign documents, their business center printer was out of ink and they made everything happen for me. The breakfast buffet, bar, front desk and maid staff was very friendly. The room was nicely and recently renovated, although they need more outlets for the number of electronics people have these days. Nice location with views of the harbor and bay. Love the balcony. I would recommend this to anyone going to the San Diego area.

Tony's work booked the hotel. The bed was wonderful! I heard the train during the day, but slept well at night. Did hear some partying on one night. The maid was wonderfully sweet. I loved the breakfast bar. Priced for the area. Next time, I would rent a car and see more of the sites! We saw a lot, but could have done more. Oh, the waiters & waitresses at their restaraunt were wonderful as is the Itallian restaurant next door.

The recommendations from travellers on Trip Advisor were accurate. We arrived at this hotel and were not suprised by what greeted us. Totally recommend for travellers on a budget who are only after a room to stay the night.
Pros: Large, spacious room (walk-in robe)

This is a decent boutique hotel, no more and no less. The boutique feel isn't really carried through all aspects.
The area is a bit rough. I live in a large city so it's not like I am just not used to urban areas. 
You definitely would not want to explore the area at night. We sure didn't. During the day, the surrounding area is pretty deserted and there really isn't anything to see. There are about - or - revitalized blocks near the hotel on Main street that are in sharp contrast to the rest of the area.

One positive about the hotel is that the restaurant on the ground floor is really good for dinner. Far better than I expected.
The hotel does not however have a good number of public spaces to spend time in. It's basically the lobby or your room. If there was anywhere to explore in the area around the hotel this would be less of a problem.
Service was good for the most part and the staff seemed attentive and pretty eager to please, however there was a strange noise coming through air vents in my room that I reported but no one ever came to check out and try to fix. 
The rooms are small, but clean and pretty well kept. 
Overall it was an ok choice for business, but I wouldn't stay here again if it was for vacation

Stayed there for a wedding with my girlfriend over the weekend. Construction noise every day including Saturday and Sunday. Water was shut off from -- AM to - PM on Monday! Is this a - star hotel or class B real estate in NYC? Rooms were also dirty and staff was by far sub par. Overall, skip and go with many other great hotels the city has to offer. Stayed here for three nights, and was *very* impressed. I will certainly stay here again on future trips to New York.
Location is superb, being just half a block away from Times Square, while being down one of the quieter cross-streets, so you're certainly not getting Times Square levels of noise.
Reception area was modern, bright, gleamingly clean, and manned by friendly and professional staff. Just off the reception was a small fitness room with some gym equipment, and a business centre with two internet computers and a printer, all of which you could use for free. Complimentary continental breakfast was also included, and there was also a drinks vending machine and a flight check-in kiosk for printing boarding passes for airlines based on the USA. There's an elevator to all floors.
The room was compact, but it certainly didn't feel cramped and I felt quite at home there. The bed was *very* comfortable; the TV looked brand new and had a wide range of cable channels; a writing desk, chair, coffee maker and air-con - heater were provided; and the bathroom was small but functional and clean with a very good shower.
And, to top it all off, the price was excellent for central Manhattan.
I would recommend this hotel to anyone, particularly tourists looking for an affordable, central base for exploring NYC. It may not be the fanciest luxury hotel in Manhattan, but for the price it's unbeatable.
I just want to mention what an outstanding Manager you have in Aurelia Gaskin. She was very friendly and helpful to myself and co-workers.

For our purposes, this hotel was ideally located...about -- minutes from a wedding off of Capital of Tx Hwy and -- minutes from downtown Austin. This is an older Hampton Inn, but there is plenty of parking and lots of trees to shade the lot and the western side of the building. There is a nice outdoor pool but no hot tub. The lobby and breakfast area seemed to be the newest part of the facility....it looks closer to what newer Hamptons look like across the country. The breakfast was just about the best one I have had at a Hampton lately. The biscuits were hot and fresh and their gravy to top them with was also fresh and hot. They also had fruit, cereals, donuts, bagels, bread for toasting, english muffins, yogurt, and waffle batter to make your own waffles with. The front desk staff was very friendly during check-in-out. The hotel and its guests were quiet and so was the location. There is a low-lying office building right nextdoor on one side and a Shell station and a Burger King on the other side. The only down side was that there was not a lot you could walk to from there, i.e. shopping and restaurants. Overall, I thought this was a great property for the rate we paid (about $-- a night with AAA).

My husband and I stayed here after special event at the Four Seasons. The location was very convient, very close to the L and right off the Mag. Mile. We had reserved our room thought the Knickerbocker website and got an excellent deal that was made even better when we were upgraded to a suite upon arrival. The room was very omfortable and had a very nice shower and bath. The staff was very courteous and they kept our luggage for us while we were shopping after we had checked out. The two problems we encountered were that the in-room Internet cost an additional $-- a day which seemed a bit ridiculous for such an expensive hotel already, and the hallways were pretty loud due to very thin entry doors. Overall, we had an excellent stay and would definitely consider going back.

Just stayed three nights at this fine, beautifully appointed hotel. Small suite on the --th floor, wonderful furnishings, nicely served continental breakfast just down the hall. It is a small and perfectly situated hotel in the Loop area, walking distance to the Art Instititute, the new Millennium Park, and much more. It was a safe and busy neighborhood even until midnight, shopping, decent restaurants and theaters nearby. 
 A lovely lobby and small but excellent fitness center just off the lobby (clean and comfortable, windows out on to the street, treadmills, elliptical trainer and universal wieght machine and more.)
 Super friendly staff, too. I have stayed in a lot of hotels in Chicago, and this is definitely one of my favorites, for families or business, whatever.

Don't judge the hotel by the outside. We drove up to find the valet just sitting out on the road and basically told us we can park our own car. Based on the outside and the valet, we weren't expecting much. We were pleasantly surprised when we walked in and found that the hotel is pretty nice inside and our room was very spacious. There is a lot of road construction around the area when I stayed early part of may ----..The hotel sits in a peaceful location..The breakfast is good..All service is good..The hotel seems a slight bit older although I have not verified the age..The price for the area unless you can find a special in my belief is a little high..I would stay again, but allow more time for high traffic in the area, and construction if still present..The business center is a little bit small compared to what I am used to..

We stayed here for a week in April and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The hotel staff were very helpful and polite. We didn't eat in their resturant, but could have confidently. We wanted to see as much of NYC as possible.
The rooms were spacious and clean. 
It was near to Times Square, but not too near to be noisy.

We stayed at this Drury Inn while traveling with a HS Baseball team over spring break. This is a nice hotel with great perks such as the breakfast and kickback. I truly believe young families were able to feed the kiddos off the kickback! I was impressed with the spread. The rooms are larger than average and the bathroom counter space was nice for two women sharing a room! 
The hotel was completely booked being spring break which tested our patience at times. However, the staff did their best to keep the team together and meet the needs of the --+ entourage of parents traveling with the group. The hotel sits above the parking garage so the elevators are very busy. The pool was nice but very busy with small kids while we were there. 
All in all, this is a very nice hotel. Hard to get to the first time but once you figure out the clover leaf under the highway, you can get around fairly easily. This was my first Drury Inn experience and I will be staying there in the future!

We arrived at the hotel in the middle of the night. We were greeted in a friendly and helpful manner. The area was a little doubtful, but the hotel felt safe, welcoming and, to our delight, was extremely clean! I had been worried that such an inexpensive hotel would be rather run down and shabby. I need not have worried. This hotels speciality must be cleanliness, with service a close second. Amenities were basic (a coffee pot would have been nice), and the bathroom was miniscule. However, I wanted a room to sleep in and get my bearings in Jacksonville. This hotel was great for that. I would stay here again, the price and convenience were great, but the cleanliness was amazing! Highly recommended! I noticed that pets are welcome, so next time I will bring my dog too.

We checked into Stay having been stranded by a pesky volcano and following -- nights of -*+ accomodation across the USA and - night at an airport hotel in Queens... I'd selected it based on price (£--- for four nights), reviews and location after a very frantic evening surfing the internet looking for somewhere affordable and well located for cheap-free entertainment... and I was not dissapointed.

Hotel is TOTALLY smoke free and you are asked to sign a waiver when you check in, which states that if you do smoke in your room you are liable to a $--- charge (I think)... so if you can't do without a smoking room, this is not the hotel for you.
Also asked to sign a waiver at check in that states that if you use the minibar to chill you own drinks you are also liable for a charge, which seems a little excessive - would've been nice to have a nice cold bottle of water in the room, but hey ho!!!!!!!!
Location is fabulous. From the entrance of the hotel you can see the red steps of Times Square. Literally a minutes' walk away. Close to Rockerfeller, Empire States, Broadway and the subway... so really can't complain in terms of location.
Rooms are 'compact and bijous' but do have all the necessary elements to keep you happy... decent bed, great TV, safe, radio alarm... No coffee-tea making facilities though. Makes an ideal - night NYC crash-pad, but would not recommend if you are intending to spend lots of time in your room as cabin-fever would set in quickly!! Small bathroom with shower but very clean and very nice complimentary toiletries.
Agree with other comments that the lifts are incredibly slow... we were on the ninth floor and it took ages... 
Free wifi access in the lobby made keeping in touch with home fairly easy.
Drinks etc. expensive in the hotel bar - but there are that many alternatives close by (highly recommend the Pig n Whistle next door which has great service and lovely tapas) that this shouldn't be a reason not to stay here.
Bearing in mind our 'unique' circumstances, the reception staff could not have been more helpful - holding a room for us while we returned to JFK to check out the situation and cancelling it without penalty when we found out we were going home!!!
All in all, would highly recommend this hotels for young(ish!) couples needing a good base in NYC for a few days sightseeing.

We stayed for four nights over Christmas. There were some really great things about the hotel - staff seemed very jolly, the free """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""mini bar""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""; basically you can select soft drinks, chips, candies from a huge selection - for free, -- hours a day. On the downside our room was barely big enough for cat swinging and the recent renovations themselves look like they need some renovating. 
Our main complaint was that our room was really noisy. The walls are paper thin and, apparently unlike the other guests, we are in the minority as we like to sleep until -.--am or so when we are on vacation. Sadly we were woken daily at -am by stomping up and down stairs outside, doors slamming and whoever happened to be in the room next door - thanks to an adjoining door they literally sounded as though they were in the same room as us. Also slightly off-putting - the ashtray for our floor was right outside our window and by our air conditioning unit so a few times we had the A-C on only to find moments later our room smelling of smoke. Also pretty annoying was the lack of regulation of hot water in the shower - every day there was leaping in and out of the stream of water from either being scalded or frozen. 
It's a sad indictment of LA hotels that this is ranked the best hotel - it is not the worst I have ever stayed in, but it's no star. All in all the location is pretty good, and rates reasonable, if you are a smoker that doesn't need much sleep-privacy and is OK with an invigorating game of hot-cold in the shower every morning this is the perfect place for you!

My husband and I stayed at this hotel while doing some sight-seeing around the area. We usually stay at the Hilton chain and did not feel that this hotel was up to par with other Embassy Suites hotels. The rooms were tired and worn, less atmosphere than you come to expect from Embassy. Rooms were clean and the staff was very friendly. 
However, I would still recommend this hotel based on location. It is a half mile walk to the National Mall and even closer to the Ford's Theatre and several good restaurants. Of course remember that the National Mall is -.- miles long so be prepared to walk once you get there. 
We found this location to be very safe. We went walking at -:-- at night to go see the monuments and didn't get back to the hotel until --:--. We never did feel unsafe throughout our entire walk.
