We had a corner city view studio. Really loved having the kitchenette that had a full size fridge. We were able to bring our leftovers from dinner back to the room and heat them up for a late night snack. The free breakfast was good, just what you need to start the day of right. The hubby loved the waffles, I was a fan of the yogurt with granola and fresh cut pineapple. We used the gym once it had all the machines you would need. The pool was perfect for a quick dip to cool off after a day of walking around, the whirlpool was nice too. The hotel also stored our luggage prior to our leaving which was very helpful. Overall we really enjoyed our stay and hope to be back soon.

This place has improved a lot. I did get one of the - room suites w- a fridge. There is a bit of runway noise but the location is right at the airport--just use earplugs and you'll sleep. I think this is a great place if you need to be at the airport because all you have to do is cross a parking lot and you are there. Free wifi in the room and - computers in the lobby that you can use. I was on the -th floor and there was a table w- hot coffee, cups, cream etc. set up right next to the elevator--I thought that was really nice!!
This is a residential building. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hotel rooms"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" are ILLEGAL. I felt like a squatter. No services. Just awful.

The front desk staff was friendly enough, and the continental breakfast had a pretty good lineup. The bed was a decent size too. As for the room, they seem pretty stingy with the towels, the gym machines are definitely some of the first to have ever been invented (and something was floating in the gallon of water inside the gym...), and the building has a strange mix of an old carpet and cigarette odor. I sprayed Lysol everywhere and still couldn't get rid of the smell. The bathroom is extremely small but usable for one night. I'm glad I spent one night here because if it was more than that I would have just lost my money and gone back to my powerless apartment. The walls must be extremely thin. I could hear my neighbors clearly and whenever their doors closed I felt the vibration through my bed's headboard.

I guess it depends on which staff person you speak with, because when I called and asked I was told that they cost $---night. For those who really don't feel like dealing with the dogs in the elevator, good luck, because this hotel welcomes them.

Just a Couple small problems. Bartender called at --:-- pm (with the kids in bed) to inform me that he had to close out my tab, only problem is that we had not visited the bar. Regardless, the charge did not show up on my bill the next morning. Also failed to bring a crib sheet for the little one. Small issues but otherwise great hotel, almost,perfect!

Stayed - nights on the --th floor in a corner room (----). View was incredible, out one window, we could see the SoL and out the other, the Brooklyn Bridge. CHELSEA INN ROCKS!!!

My family of four, including two teenage boys stayed at the Boston Park Plaza for - nights and really enjoyed our stay. We received very good service and would definitely stay there again if we return to Boston. Everyone, including the desk clerk, concierge, door man, and housekeeping staff were friendly as well as helpful. I have no complaints and would highly recommend the Boston Park Plaza.

Traveling with a small (even a well behaved dog) makes finding a place to stay for one or two nights very challenging when you are on the road. What a surprise at LaQuinta Inn Indianapolis East. When we asked to see the room first (due to a poor experience at another hotel earlier in our travels), the gal Vida at the desk was extremely accommodating. The room was charming, the bedding attractive, and since we asked for a suite, we had the small refrigerator we needed as well as a microwave. The room was spotless, the bedding wonderful, and towels as white as snow. The breakfast in the morning was basic but well set up and once again everything was clean and orderly. Thank you La Quinta Inn Indianpolis East for doing it well and making travels with """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Harley"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" enjoyable for us.

Very nice hotel with an awesome location. Not sure why they call this a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""resort"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" since there are no hotel ammenities. You can't beat the location; right on the Riverwalk just above Landry's Seafood with other popular restaurants like Joe's Crab Shack, the County Line, and Hard Rock Cafe a stone's throw away. It is less than a - minute walk to the Alamo and all of the tourist attractions in the area. The Buckhorn Saloon-Museum-Restaurant is just on the corner with the Children's Museum around the corner. Walgreen's is conveniently located for some light grocery shopping perfect for easy breakfast essentials. Even though it's on the Riverwalk, the noise wasn't loud enough to interfere with you sleep even with the nightclub next door. My only concern would be for handicapped travelers since the hallways are pretty tight as well as the rooms which are chocked full of furniture. There is also only one elevator which gets busy during peak times. If you're a handicapped traveler, you should inquire about the handicapped accessibility of a room. I was also surprised that housekeeping didn't come daily to make up the room or the beds - oh well, not a huge deal and being located this close to everything sure makes it worth it! Highly recommended!

We recently stayed here for an extended weekend over Veteran's day. Rooms were great, down to the little details like the Biscoff cookies instead of a traditional pillow mint. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Bobby at the front desk made us feel right at home. Justin gave us GREAT recommendations for restaurants, in areas close to the hotel and also in other neighborhoods. We were not disappointed at any meal. Overall, great experience at Palomar!

We stayed at the Hotel -- NYC for - nights during June ---- and had a great time!
The location is fantastic- you're virtually opposite Times Sq and very close to the theatre district (Rent is playing right next door).
We were upgraded to a superior room- and the room was great-a decent size (for NYC!) and very clean and well maintained.
As part of our package, we also had breakfast included- a great way to start the day and we had a choice of bagels and various pastries.
The staff are also very friendly and helpful and made us feel very welcome.
I would definately stay here again when I next visit NYC!

I stayed at Hotel Nikko during a business conference. Solid - star hotel with good services and services. Rooms are clean and adequately spacious, good bathroom amenaties and great location in the center of town. Too bad that newspapers are not delivered to the room but if you go downstairs early you have your pick of Journal, US Today or New York Times. One word of caution. The upcharge on services is terrible like most hotels. I shipped two small packages using the business center and they charged me $---!!!! Food service if you have a meeting there is expensive as is internet access ($-.-- per hour). Service and personnel were good.

We stayed in this hotel for -- days during a Sweet Adeline convention just last week. The hotel facilities were very clean and new, with amazingly comfortable beds and pillows. I highly recommend this hotel and look forward to returning. It is also in a great location close to the --th street mall and convention centre.

I stayed here for one night on my way through New York to LA. I needed to be up early on the Sunday morning. What a mistake to stay here. Even though I asked for a quiet room I was given one only a few floors above the main atrium which pumped music out way too loud. I could hear every word of every song. This hotel thinks it's a nightclub and should advertise as such. Don't stay here if you actually need a hotel room to sleep in.

I stayed at the Embassy Suites Houston Downtown as part of a large conference in October ----, and thoroughly enjoyed both the hotel and the great service.
It's very new, and you can tell. The facilities are modern and clean, with funky decorating the rooms. Comfy beds, separate bedroom, nice little bathroom; a small self catering area with minifridge and microwave means that you can look after yourself if you don't want to go out to eat.
Breakfast is included and is absolutely fabulous! Cereal, porrige, bacon, eggs, sausages, pancakes, toast, bagels, yoghurt, juice and made to order omelettes. A lovely, large breakfast room that is kept spotlessly clean, even with the high volume of guests; the hotel was completely full but I didn't have to wait for seating.
Had a swim in the pool, which was very nice and stocked up with guest towels. There's also a coin operated laundry which was a blessing for me as I was travelling for two weeks.
The hotel is well situated if you are attending an event at the Toyota Center or Convention Center, and is only a few short blocks to the business district. If you're new to Houston, be aware that Houston's nearby CBD has absolutely no night life at all - it's purely a business area and everything shuts down at night, even the McDonalds closes! There's very little shopping in this area either. It's really set up for conferences and events.
This year my convention is in Denver, and based on this experience I'll be staying at the Embassy Suites there too.

We stayed at the Hampton for - nights during our sons graduation from MCRD. It is way overpriced, we payed $---.-- per night and the room was very average, small, one queen bed a desk and a chair, I expected more. When we checked in the clerk couldnt find our reservations, she set us up in a room that was already occupied so when we went in there was another family already there, how embarrasing.There were no towels at the pool but the pool was very nice, clean well kept. Continental breakfast was also good but all tables were sticky. For a hotel that assures ---% satisfaction gauranteed, it wasnt all that satisfing.

Once again we stayed at the Beverly Garland for our trip to LA to see Billy Elliott. The hotel is so conveniently located and we love the service and the friendly staff. Our room was spacious and clean and we enjoyed eating lunch poolside with friends. I also love that they have a gym, a laundry facility and a movie theatre! It is the best hotel for the money anywhere in LA! I forgot to mention the pillows. We had - pillows clearly marked as Hard and Soft. How great!

I chose to stay here for my first trip to Boston. I needed to check in a day early and stay a day later than planned. The staff was very friendly and helpful. They made great recommendations for food and sight seeing. There is lots to do within walking distance of this hotel. This is a historic building in the theater district of Boston so the rooms are pretty small. But it had everything I needed- bed, desk, flatscreen, bathroom. Overall I think the price was pretty decent for downtown in a big city. I would definitely stay here again.

I've got the top tier status with Marriott and Westin. Having recently stayed at the Westin at LAX I thought I'd give the Marriott a try. While I was underwhelmed with rooms at both properties I was struck by a few things at the Marriott that give it an edge over the Westin:

-Westin lounge was tired and lame - Marriott had a nice spread of food and beverage options.

Just back from a - day stay at the O'Brien Historic Hotel, and it definitely met and mostly exceeded my expectations. Loved it, and will stay again!
The pros: perfect location - block from the riverwalk and walking distance to absolutely everything downtown; safe area to walk; cheap parking; friendly staff; great balcony; comfortable beds; best price of any comparable property near the riverwalk.
 The cons: very small bathroom (-nd and -rd floor--not sure about whirlpool rooms on -st--corner rooms appeared slightly larger) with no vent fan; early morning light on east side (back of hotel), small parking lot.
Room Tips: (in case you read no further!)--Rooms on the backside of the hotel -nd and -rd floors face east and have a single door leading out to a balcony. Problem is, they still let in a great deal of morning light, and have no curtain on them. One of the beds is just a few feet from this door, so If you are light sensitive, get a room on the front side of the hotel. Other reviews mention road noise from the front, though in our room, the fan-A-C blocked most ambient noise without being too annoying. Also, rooms in the mid-section of the hotel on the second floor (----- and ------ maybe? not sure) open into the hotel's breakfast eating area. Noise could be a problem. The balcony is covered on the -nd floor, but not the -rd, fyi.
Have to say, this place is absolutely perfect if location is paramount, especially if you are a single or couple. The bathroom was as small as it could be and still be functional, but had nice amenities like a makeup mirror, plenty of light and nice size tub-shower with good water pressure and adjustable spray head. One glaring omission in this city of high heat and humidity is a bathroom vent fan. Completely ridiculous, given the climate!! There is definitely a musty smell in the room due to high humidity if you turn off the A-C. Common in many SA hotels, in my experience, so can't fault them too much. The remedy for this is opening the door onto the balcony, if you are in a balcony room. Not sure what you would do in summertime....so I'm not sure I would stay here in the heat of summer. A-C did a good job (nice to be able to set it yourself), but hard to say if it would keep up in summer. Humidity could be an issue.
Yes, the parking is limited, but I counted approximately-- spaces, maybe more, for a hotel with --+ rooms, and there is a parking lot across the street and a parking garage one block up. Some of the hotel's parking is in the rear, some across the street. You can't beat the price of $--.--!! All rooms appeared full at the time we were here (holiday weekend) and we got the last space at midnight on a Friday night, and later had no problem finding a spot when we moved the car. Cleanliness was good, but the hotel opened in ---- and little things show its age, such as small areas of torn wallpaper, bathroom doors which need to be repainted, old toilet seats etc. According to one staff member, they are getting ready to install new carpeting, and they just put in new doors from the balcony rooms to the balcony, so it appears they are addressing routine maintenance issues related to aging.

If you are going to NYC to sightsee, this hotel maybe ok. If you are going to do any type of business, or if you need to connect to your home office via the internet, stay somewhere else.

Extremely swanky place. Excellent service from the bell boys to the maids. Yummy drinks and appetizers. It was hard not to notice the slightly racy art work hanging on the walls. Cover your eyes if you're offended by suggestive photos of men in speedos and women looking like they're a little too cold, if you know what I mean. The bedding was VERY comfortable with tons of pillows. Great location within easy walking distance to lots of fantastic and trendy restaurants and bars. This place drips with a modern feel...This ain't your momma's hotel...

Okay, this hotel has dropped BIG time. I went - years ago for a birthday weekend and was blowed away by the beautiful ceiling and shopping area available in the hotel. Sure, the view from the rooms remind you of Shawshank Redemption but the hotel was still great. 
Fast Forward to Valentines Weekend ----, I couldnt wait to get back especially with the renovations being touted on the hotel website. We stayed in the Executive Level ( Save your money) . New bedding in the room that was the extent of the renovation. I questioned the concierge why the in room hotel information book listed things we didnt have and was informed that """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""yes, the books were inaccurate, and they heard that alot"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" ???? There is no coffee pot in the rooms. None of the rooms have coffee pots. The bathrooms are Very small if you leave the door open you will have even less room so close the door you get about - more inches. The pool is worse than a City pool that has been deserted. It looks like someone just cut a small hole in the floor and filled it with water. We stayed here for - nights in October and wish we could have stayed here for another few. Lovely pool-jacuzzi overlooking the ocean on Pacific Beach. The rooms were nice and big with a very nice en-suite. Front desk staff and cleaning staff couldn't have been friendlier and we will stay here from now on when visiting San Diego.

The service that we receive at this Hampton Inn is top of the line! From the front desk to the bellmen, to the cleaning staff, you just can't get any better. Everyone goes out of their way to accommodate you and make you feel at home. The rooms are very comfortable, especially the beds! Since we travel on business, it's a nice, relaxing atmosphere. The breakfast buffet is really good, there's something for everybody. The work out room isn't extensive, but really not a deal breaker. As far as location, you're right smack in the middle of midtown--right next to most of the theaters and a block from Broadway-Times Square, very handy for shopping and eating!

I don't expect as much with hotels in Manhattan as the rooms are naturally going to be smaller and older than most places. The Michelangelo was very nice for New York. It's location between Time's Square and Central Park was AMAZING for my visit. We were just there for the weekend, saw a show on Broadway and walked back to the Stage Deli, then the hotel was right there! I love running the Central Park, so it was perfectly located just - short blocks south of the Park. We didn't have a view, but you can walk right outside and see Times Square and walk right up to the park and have amazing views in all directions. 
In the room, our bed was comfy and the A-C worked well. The water pressure was crazy high and hard to control, but this is probably pretty common in NYC. There was a nice vanity outside of the bathroom that allowed my wife to get ready while I showered without being in the way. You really can't beat the location!

Stayed here with my girlfriend in October during hurricane Sandy. Even with the city in chaos the staff of the Belvedere were impeccable and they needed to be with some particularly tricky customers knocking around. The hotel is very nice and we really enjoyed our stayed here. The rooms were probably the nicest of the - hotels we stayed in while in New York. The doorman Luis stood out in particular of all of the staff! Thoroughly recommended the Belvedere!

First of all there is no microwaves in the rooms to warm up food so you have to buy THEIR food which is VERY expensive. The sheets and covers are old. The room is very small. There is hardly any parking and it cost $--.-- a day to park. The t.v. only has like - channels. The food- beverage credit sucks because everything is more than $-.--!!! The customer service is poor the front desk- concierge. I would not recommend this hotel! Don't stay here!!!

Stayed at this Hotel and found the best staff anywhere, especially William! The WiFi was not working really well on the --th floor so we spent quite a bit of time in the foyer doing our surfing. I witnessed a couple customers explaining some problems and one lady was quite upset. William spoke to her at length, showed compassion and empathy with her problems and sorted everything out for her. This guy should be paid more!!! Back to the hotel... the room we stayed in (----) was tiny, but we had expected that, it's New York. The room was clean and the housekeeping was excellent. A good breakfast is provided each morning too.

Located within a few miles of Sea-Tac this is a very large hotel with a Starbucks, gift shop, meeting rooms, breakfast room, bar and dining room. The food was a little expensive-$-- for a burger and $-- for an omelette alone. However it was good enough.
I had a spacious and clean suite with fridge, microwave, nice sized table and a comfortable bed. I loved that the heating system was quiet. I had plently of outlets, but my suite on the --th floor had recently been remodeled. The walk out balcony was a nice surprise.
It has a main tower, which is the best place to stay as you are close to everything, as well as several wings. From the wings it was a bit of a hike to the restaurants and front desk.
Nice pool and fitness areas. 
Parking is expensive at $-- for valet and $--.-- for self-park per night. Free shuttle to and from airport helps. Verify internet price-not free.
Good jumping off spot for wherever you want to go.

I had lived in midtown in Memphis for - years but hit town when my friends were gone so had to stay in a hotel. I was very familliar with midtown and could practically see my old house from the hotel room. You have got to see the lobby to believe it. Madonna Inn, anyone? They have done it up in neo-Italianate fakery - it is a riot. Give your eyes time to adjust to the low, mood lighting. Ornately framed prints of famous works of art hanging all over the place on the dark, wood panelling and red velour wallpaper and on the CEILING! Blasting some thud thud dance music too. This is all beside the point but if I still lived in Memphis I would send visitors here just to see the lobby. Nice desk service, fresh apples, slightly scary elevator and a rather average room. Too bad the rooms aren't decorated too. Clean enough and no odor. Great shower, onery tv remote. -th floor so a nice view of midtown. Had my own car and knew my way around so it was fine for me and CHEAP!

Wow, what an experience to stay at The Drake, modern comfort with so much history. Executive King Room is large and well appointed with a huge comfortable bed & pillows. Executive lounge access comes with the room and is just fabulous. It has a good selection continental breakfast including cut fruit, hard boiled eggs, cheeses, breads, smoked salmon and Lavazza espresso machine. The view from the lounge is truly magnificent on a sunny day, like an idyllic paradise. 
Staff in the exec lounge, front desk and housekeeping were friendly, sensitive and obliging. It's the little things they've done which made us feel really welcome, like offering to print our Citypass tickets and car reservation at the Front Desk free of charge, breaking a $-- on several occasions, or the waiter leaving a busy breakfast service to find us more club soda when the breakfast bar had run out, or, when we returned to the room one day and found the Housekeeper half-way through servicing the room, she immediately offered to leave and come back later so we could change and leave for the day without delay.
The location of the hotel is ideal for tourists right near John Hancock tower. It's easy to get to the tourist bureau where tour buses go from, or catch a bus from Michigan Ave to most popular tourist locations. Paid ~$----night including taxes which was cheap for a deluxe room in this class of hotel through Agoda, by far the best value in the central city. The only caution I'd give is to watch the room service or in house restaurant rates as they're very pricey.
We've had a great stay and would highly recommend the place. Will return if we visit Chicago again.

Affinia -- is a cute, small, friendly """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""boutique"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel. The room was quite spacious by New York standards,with a desk area, cupboards, armchair and a FABULOUS kingsize bed with a wonderful mattress and an amazing choice of pillows. The bathroom was large and had a bath as well as a shower. There is a bit of traffic noise, distant sirens etc, but I think this is pretty much a backdrop to New York and it didn't prevent us sleeping. The location is not particularly interesting, as it is situated mid-town, there are some bars and restaurants around but not all that exciting. Grand Central station and the subway is about a ----- minute walk away, plus there are lots of cabs if you do want to go further afield. It feels like a very safe area and the staff were friendly and helpful.

Just left the hotel and have nothing but the best to say about this hotel. I know now why it gets such high marks. We were lucky to get this hotel thru a Priceline bid. When we arrived at the hotel we were treated with five star service. We are in touch members and it did not matter that we had Pricelined our hotel. Web were given $-- mini bar credit and free wine tasting. Would recommend anytime when in Seattle. Excellent in every way. Will choose when traveling back to Seattle for future visits.

First of all, the price you pay usually has a lot to do with setting expectations. My booking was relatively last minute which meant i paid over $--- for one night in what seemed to be a busy week in New York (although the room was booked by my assistant). The main reason for booking it was the location in midtown close to a conference I was attending.
When I checked in, I pointed out that I had paid quite a lot for the room as the receptionist said most people pay about $--- per night. I was hoping this might get me a better room but I was wrong. 
Despite paying a high price they literally put me in the smallest room on the floor (I could see that from the emergency exit map). The room was tiny with you falling on the bed the minute you enter the room. The bathroom had a sliding door as there was not enough room for a swinging door.
The bathroom was very outdated and dirty. THe air con was in the window and was way to loud to leave on while sleeping. Overall this is a run down budget hotel with a bunch of completely different sized rooms so you essentially are signing up for a lottery in terms of whether you get an ok sized room or a closet like i got. 
It is also worth saying that the elevators are also ridiculously slow. The rooms look like they begin on the --th or --th floor but the waiting time to go up or down was seriously long. 
The only redeeming factor for this hotel is the location. Otherwise there are much better hotels in New York if you are paying $---. This is definitely a $--- a night hotel.

We stayed at this hotel because it has only been open less than a year and we've already stayed at the Marriott and the Renaissance downtown. I like this location best since it's closest to both the museums, parks and marina. Word of caution, the walls are thin and you can hear everything being said or done in the rooms next to you and even in the hallway. The gym is top of the line and there is a spa although I didn't partake in any of the amenities. We didn't eat in the hotel except for on the concierge level for breakfast which was nicer than most. The JW is located - blocks from the Art Institute and close enough to walk to the Macy's on State street. You can take the redline to get to the Water Tower. The bathroom layout was spacious enough for two people with a deep soak tub but no jets. The staff is very nice and courteous but the lobby bar is too bright to be considered intimate. For that reason, we chose to go to the W across the street for cocktails. I recommend renting bikes at Millenium Park and riding along Lake Shore Drive or taking a sight seeing cruise on Lake Michigan.

I had checked this website before booking this hotel so I thought everything would be ok. I thought wrong. The hotel staff was rude and not helpful. The room smelled bad and we kept running out of toilet paper and it would take forever to get some sent up to the room. I will never stay here again!

This one is a winner - great, new decor, spacious rooms (although I had reserved a Jr suite and none were available on first floor), lovely breakfast area, really helpful front desk staff, pretty pool area with tables & umbrellas, plenty of parking. Bed was comfy, pillows were plentiful. Really enjoyed this LaQuinta!!
You can't beat this LaQuinta for the money - it's not a luxury property, of course, but very, very nice!! I'll go back for sure.

Hi there stayed here for - nights for a conference in Chicago in January ----, the hotel is in a good location however it is very old and tired. The bathrooms are old and not the best and I would not recommend for that special get away or holiday.
It was ok for the room price on a business trip and everything else was booked out from the conference and Motor show that was on the following week.
Would I stay there again not really unless it was a business trip type of scenario.
The staff were great and the bell man was helpful this sort of made up for the other items

I stayed here for - nights. Every member of the staff I interacted with was friendly and really wanted to help. The room was clean and conmfortable and the right size. I am not sure why some of you reviewers complain about room size:. Does everything have to be supersized in the U.S.? They should see the size of hotel rooms in Europe. This hotel is a great value. Free wifi was fast and relaible. My room had a view of the river through a small window. Yes, a larger window with more light coming in would be nicer, but how much time during daylight hours does anyone spend in the hotel? Filtered bottled water on each floor and the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""guest closet"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" stocked with extra room supplies is a plus. The closet also has iron-board for guest use. About - blocks from the blue line station: -- min ride to O'Hare.
A couple of suggestions to the hotel management:
-. The restaurant should invest in regular unflavored black tea: it was annoying that they had none during breakfast
-. Don't tell me that the only way to get to McCormick place is by taxi. Let your front desk person know that Bus #- goes door to door from the hotel (Michigan Ave) to McCormick Place, for $-.--.

My wife and I stayed one night at this hotel after attending my nearby company Christmas party. Since we didn't feel like dropping over $--- for a night at the hotel of the party, I booked a night at the Bradford for a mere $--. The hotel staff was very friendly and accomodating. Facilities were in great condition. The free attached parking garage was a plus since it was raining the night we checked in. Nice free continental breakfast buffet in the lobby the next morning.
Our room had all the amenities you would need if you are a business traveler or someone in need of a cheap stay such as we were. Kitchenette, huge refrigerator, high speed internet, --- TV channels, etc. Room was very clean. My only complaint that keeps me from giving it a - is that the bed was not that comfortable and the sheets felt like they were disposable and made of paper.
We love staying downtown and this hotel is in the heart of it.Staff is very helpful and nice,

Booked two rooms when staying in San Francisco for a friend's birthday treat. I travel a lot on business - this hotel exceeded my expectations. It was one of the best decisions of the trip. I split the holiday between two hotels in the city and really regretted leaving the Crowne Plaza.
(-) Location
An easy walk from the Powell Street BART station (I took the BART from the airport). Great for shopping, being two blocks from Union Square. Great for all the city-centre attractions. The cable-car stops outside reception! Takes you down to Powell - Market Street, or down to Fishermans Wharf.
(-) Rooms
We had a standard room. Quality and cleanliness very high. Most rooms seem to have a large bay window. My room was at the back of the hotel and I could see the bay and quite a lot of the city, including Coit Tower and the Transamerica Pyramid. The bay window is great. The room is bigger as a result and you get a much wider view from your hotel. The beds are very comfortable. Every room has a CD player and they even provide a relaxing """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sleep-advantage"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" CD.
(-) Food - Facilities
Didn't try the restaurant - so many choices in San Fran!!
The breakfast was great (Crowne Plaza's usual standard). There is also a coffee-shop - Deli in the hotel that does fantastic egg & bacon breakfast muffins - dangerous!! Lot's of coffee choices, bagels, muffins, cereals etc - I recommend it for a faster getaway in the morning. There is a friendly bar. We were also given vouchers on arrival that gave you a free drink in the bar and concessions at the restaurant etc.

This property is far from new. It has a familiar design that I have visited in other cities, but never one in such a worn and tired state. 
The positives include location - it is situated very close to the Convention Center, the Water Garden and the Omni, which is where my conference was being held. The Molly Trolly will take you around the immediate area, where you will have a wealth of shopping and eating opportunities. 
Another positive is clean quite rooms and comfortable beds.
Now, the peculiar and not-so-good...where to start, and how to be reasonable? Let's see, dinner leftovers...where is the refrigerator? What? No fridges or microwaves in the rooms? Hmmm...the front desk says they no longer have them.
Okay, warm water from the faucet, better get some ice. What? No ice machine? Hmmm...the front desk says even numbered floors, but not floor -. Guess what? Floor - has a broken ice machine, so off to floor - where some ice was finally procured.
Broken door handle in bathroom, toilet paper holder damaged, scuffs and scratches abound, stains all over carpet, stains in upholstery of chair, small bathroom with stained sinktop, apparently from harsh abrasive cleaner. These are indicators of a well worn property. The room was clean, even though it was well worn with scuffs, scrapes and stains.
As mentioned above, the room was quite, with the exception of the toilet, which was not only unbelievably loud when flushed, but it endlessly flushed itself. When other rooms flushed, the water was drawn through the trap and was very noisy, then belched water back that sometimes splashed out of the bowl, and during the brief time the trap was drawn dry it released a nasty whiff of odor into the room.
So, in my opinion and experience, this property is not up to Radison standards, or at least not my expectations of the Radison brand. It was very expensive for the condition, but it is downtown, so prices will run higher. However, i would expect to find a nicer motel nearby for the cost of this one. 
On a side note, this reservation was made for me rather than by me. I informed the front desk at check-in that I was a Starwood member, but much to my disappointment it fell upon deaf ears. Perhaps members who receive acknowledgement get nicer rooms. Meanwhile, the entire Starwood group took a hit for this; I will probably book at a non Starwood property in whatever city I visit next.
This hotel is clean, nice, staff is very nice and easy location to get to. My room has everything I needed. Great place to stay!

I was genuinely excited about this hotel. The pictures looked great and the amenities seemed worthwhile, but it was a splurge. The best parts were, as we hoped, the pool, bed (amazing!), toiletries, and restaurant. 
The bill, however, was nearly $-- more per night than we were quoted. This came from the standard -% tax, a daily $-- surcharge (but you can make international calls and get candy at the front desk!), and a whopping --% transient lodging tax. --%? Why is this tax being pushed onto tourists?
Neat experience, but way too expensive for our taste. If we ever visit Phoenix again with its ridiculous tourist tax, I think we'll pass on this place.

The hotel is conveniently located in the center. The rooms are big emogh and conveninetly equipped. I stayed in a high floor rrom. Breakfast is a bit expensive but rich. The spa is well equiped and clean.
Oveall it is a very good choice for business and pleasure

The JW Marriott at Desert Ridge is a great hotel with great amenities: - Golf courses, several excellent restaurants; Meritage Steakhouse and Roy's both with great food, ambiance and a excellent wine list. The grounds are beautiful, a long lazy river and excellent swimming pools.

I have known this hotel under various names over the years. Thankfully, it is back to its former glory. Perfect but unobtrusive service, spacious room, very nice public areas. Parking and WiFi are too expensive. Especially the WiFi, that is now taken for granted like hot water or television.

My husband and I stayed at the Boston Park Plaza during a recent """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""extra long"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Labour Day Weekend. Here's my overall take on the place:
*The location is excellent - it's in close walking distance to the subway, Boston Common, Newbury Street...we were very happy with this aspect of the hotel
*The price - the Park Plaza certainly wasn't cheap, but it was the most reasonable of the centrally located hotels that I looked at (I also managed to get a --% discount by booking it online on a day that they were having a special, so that helped, and for some reason I got a voucher for a complimentary upgrade).
*The room itself - is only OK. The furnishings are a bit tired looking, and the size of the room is fairly small. Thank goodness we got an upgrade from the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Plaza Petite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""'Queen room""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""...the Queen room was pretty small, so I can't imagine how squished the Petite room would have been! 
*The service - prior to our trip, the service I received from anyone I spoke with was pretty lousy. Prior to booking, I called because the hotel website was down (it gave me a continuous error message when I went to book). The woman I spoke to said that yes, she knew it was down, but she couldn't give me the same price as the website, and she would have someone call me the next day to assist me. When no one called that next day, I called the day after, and got a very snotty, unhelpful attitude from the representative I spoke with (ie....the hotel staff is very busy which is why they didn't call me back, it's not their fault the website was down, and there was no supervisor I could speak with to help me further... etc etc). Being frustrated with trying to get help from anyone over the phone, I went back to the website - thankfully it was working and my request went through (discount and all). That said, I was a bit apprehensive about the service we might get once we arrived given they were so unhelpful prior to our arrival, however I found that all staff we encountered during our visit were friendly, prompt and helpful...a pleasant surprise.

We stayed here for - nights on route to LA and had a near perfect stay. Very comfortable rooms, with all the extras you´d expect. Excellent reception staff very willing to help and lovely breakfasts with fast and efficient service. Recommended!
One note: The valeting does not apply to motorbikes, and as we were on a hired Harley we had to find our own parking.
Amazing rooms. Great location. A bit pricey but worth it in my opinion. Definitely staying here again

I stayed at the L.A. Sky boutique hotel February -- and --th of ----. It is located among strip malls on a busy street. The building is basically an old cheap motel remodeled and decorated to appear like a chic boutique hotel but they missed a few elements. The parking lot looks sketchy. You can hear EVERY noise from your neighbors' rooms, as well as every step and conversation in the courtyard (your room door is directly in the courtyard). I arrived Sunday night for a job interview Monday morning, and was awakened in the middle of the night by a loud group of party goers. In the early morning I could hear my neighbor snoring, then using the bathroom, blowing his nose etc. etc. The room was nicely decorated and of good size with a comfortable bed. The bathroom nice and good size also. I would recommend looking at other hotels in the area that did not cost too much more.

Recently stayed in a corner suite on floor --. Bed linens and towels were of high quality and bed was comfortable. The tv was some sort of flat tube with a shaky cable connection that we had to keep moving around to get any picture at all and there were few plugs to plug in anything like a computer or phone charger. An extension cord ran under the bed to plug in the bedside light. Most of the room was clean; except for mold on the bottom of the shower door and a lot of dust behind the curtains when we closed and opened them.
At check-in, we weren't told about complimentary coffee in the mornings (happened upon it on our final day there) or any other amenities that the hotel may have offerred. There are no ice machine so expect to tip whenever you need fresh ice. The sink near the bar and frig in the room drained so slowly that we couldn't empty much into it without it overflowing. 
The concierge didn't seem to enjoy his job and he was a little patronizing when explaining that one train station was only --- block closer than the other. Parking valets and bell men were awesome, though, so they made up for him.
We may stay again if the price is right because of the close proximity to restaurants, outdoor dining, the train, and shopping. We would never, however, pay full price for a room in this hotel.

I admit that I panicked when I saw the lobby. It definitely needs massive re-modeling of all public areas and some new outfits for the staff wouldn’t hurt (one of them had a torn jacket). 
But – the room was great – lots of space and very comfortable (just the bath was way too simple – if the shower head was new and could have some options for massage it would have been great). We got a newspaper to our room and the location is awesome – the Airporter stops right there and it’s within a walking distance from everything. The staff was supper nice especially the concierges (Joe and Isaiah, if I got the names right) who had good recommendations.

I used to live at this hotel when it was called Pickwick Arms. Pickwick Arms was a low budget run down hotel, but with charm. The Pod is a designer hotel targeting young budget travelers. I accept the small space for that price. But I don't accept the rude attitude to the lady we met at the front desk. We had booked two rooms. The Double Double Pod and the Townhouse. She said, as if I was to blame, that the townhouse was closed so they had books four rooms for us instead. I said: """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Fine, as long as we pay the same."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" She was also mumbling to her colleague about us, making the atmosphere really tense, we were standing right there, we could hear her! It ended up with us in two Double Double Pods for the same price, but I'll never set my foot in that place ever again.

The TA reviews were accurate on this one. Our stay was a week Tues thru Sun. We arrived early, however was offered to hold our luggage till we could check in. The room was updated and very clean, however small. This is standard for NYC. The breakfast was good, did not expereience the LARGE crowds previously mentioned. There were times where it was full but everyone moved through and the outside patio was very ice. The front desk personnel were great expecially Lydia. Two young women walking through the area late at night was a little nerving but we had no problems. I have no complaints.

Nighttime manger just shrugged his shoulders. They really don't care and i suspect that is why the rooms Are dirty and the bathrooms smell. Lots of other choices in this city that I would recommend you consider first. I checked in and promptly checked this one off my list forever.

Ok if you do not plan to do anything in your room but sleep. No breakfast or coffee before ----, bad coffee, skimpy breakfast-not worth it. No free internet, no free phone, they don't call cab for you, no safe for money-valuables, no central place to sit, some desk clerks were apathetic or rude, others were excellent. Only the suites (they have only -) have coffee makers or refrigerators. I asked for a coffee maker (I like Starbuck's)-'can't give you because of policy'. Alarm clock is at desk table screwed to outlet-not at bedside. Called for wake up call-they called -- minutes late. They shake head yes to everything-don't assume that they underdstand.

I went to the Keating in early August. First impression, was WOW what a cool hotel. Gadgets galore very swanky! The room smelt musty as the shower was open concept. (it was right in front of the bed). A great place for voyeurs but not two buddys traveling together. The hotel is in a great location right in the heart of the GASLAMP distrcict. The breakfast was awful! Stale muffins, outdated yogurt and ripened bananas. My biggest quam was the singled paneled windows. I stayed at the hotel for - nights and had - TERRIBLE sleeps. You are right beside a bar and the music is blarring. You can hear everything. They gave earplugs with the room --- now I see why. With this hotel you sacrifice a good night's sleep with swanky rooms and locaton.
Staff was great and friendly.
Overall, a negative experience.

Five stars for sure! Clean and perfect for family trip! - minute walk to the shipyard where you can hop on a ferry for $- and be dropped off to walk around the city all day. The pool and workout room were spectacular and the rooms were perfect with the beautiful scenary out the windows! We will be back!

I got a great deal on this hotel when I did this year's Nike Womens Marathon. It was only a block and a half from the starting line, on the trolley line and near everything in Union Square. We had a Starbucks on site. They also have a very good restaurant-bar at the hotel. All kinds of restaurants and shopping are right in the area. The rooms are very nice, service was very good. I would definitely stay here again.

People are courteous but had a problem with credit billing. They credited it twice to my credit card and then another to another card. I hope they get improved on this major aspect of handling their transactions.

Two friends and I were travelling from Seattle WA and Portland OR on a driving trip. We had experienced several O.K. to very bad motels and decided to stay in the Marriott on recommendation of another friend's father. Thanks, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Dad"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" as the room was comfortable, as were the beds. Heavenly rest for our weary bodies on the final leg of our three week journey. The Marriott was conveniently located so we could enjoy Fisherman's Wharf and an easy taxi ride from other sights. One bad part of the sightseeing was our Greyhound bus tour of the city.
Traffic was horrible. Our - hour tour ended up being - --- hours and because of fog we could not see some of the sights. Totally boring afternoon! Would not recommend this tour.

Directly on Times Square, front door adjoins the front door to Legally Blonde. Right in the middle of the action, but crowds and pace on the sidewalks may be a bit intense for some, and particularly for anybody with a stroller or walking aid.
Definitely worth upgrading to a package that includes the complimentary breakfast buffet. The buffet included fresh fruit, hot oatmeal, hot breakfast meats, omelettes and eggs made to order, pancakes and waffles to order, cold meat and cheese selection, smoked salmon, juices, breakfast pastries. Something for everyone, and open until --:-- each morning. 
Our suite had two double beds plus living room and pull out couch. Decor very pleasant, kitchenette was helpful. Extra sink and large mirror in kitchenette area doubled as an extra vanity. Three women and all their stuff fit nicely, not crowded, very comfortable.
The fitness center is under construction, temporary quarters are crowded but servicable. The business center had three computers and servicable printer, all worked well and was convenient.
No complaints, great stay, will return if travelling with family. For a romantic holiday, go several blocks away from Times Square for a more calm and relaxing experience.

Spent - nights with - other people (which included the weekend). Price was great! Location is northwest SA and surrounded by businesses and their parking lots (which felt very safe and was actually quiet). Manager was neither friendly nor rude...just there. Office closed at -pm and opened back up in the morning for breakfast (which was bare minimum: waffles you make, glazed doughnuts, juice, coffee, dry cereal, oatmeal packets). Pool and hottub looked small but clean. Housekeeping came every day. Room was clean enough with sofabed, - double beds, kitchenette with - microwaves (- didn't work), small fridge, - burner stove, sink and dining table with - chairs. Area recommendations
Only an hour from Fredericksburg, -- min from downtown, a few min from I--- and not far at all from restaurants, shopping, etc...

I stayed here one night last week for business. Check in was seamless, though it was --:-- PM. I got to the room easily enough, the outdoor elevator was pretty cool. I was on the --th floor, again, great. It ended there. The room stunk - I'll assume it was LA smog. The TV was cheap and took me a while to get it turned on - I know how to use a TV. I went to set the alarm clock - sorry, doesn't work. Didn't even display the time. Though they apparently work in other rooms because my neighbor's went off at - AM and never stopped. It was incredible noisy for being so far removed from street level, and that's not including my other neighbor who was, for some reason, up and making tons of noise at -AM. Get this - two of the four receptacles I tried, didn't work. The toilet sit didn't go up all the way - it hit the counter-top and rested on my back while using the toilet. Overall, I love Starwood hotels and wish I had just tried the Sheraton down the street. Maybe next time. And PS, you can see in other people's rooms pretty clearly.

The staff at this hotel is fantastic. Everyone goes out of their way to make your stay here the best. The rooms are large, with a microwave and a large refrigerator. I was here for a convention and their meeting rooms are great and they exceeded all our needs. What ever we needed the staff provided. Everyone went way beyond our expectations. I stayed - nights and could not ask for a better room. Our group is already thinking of returning next year because our experience this year was so positive.

Here for a much deserved girls weekend with my daughter. I was working with a tight budget and had my doubts when booking, but the price could not be beat. I was rewarded with a wonderful stay and can not think of a single complaint during our four day stay. All of the staff were extra friendly, but have to really compliment the shuttle drivers for prompt, courteous service and recommendations of things to do in the area. The resturant was great and the servers went out of their way to make sure we had a great breakfast each morning. Price was right and the portions are extra large so could be shared. Our room was in the back of the property and we were never bothered by noise. We enjoyed the pool and hot tub. Overall a really great stay and we have booked two rooms in April for Spring Break. We cannot wait to come back to San Diego.

Reserved a Labor Day Weekend special birthday celebration through whatahotel.com (second trip through that site this year). Rate and extras were superior and I checked on that right up until a couple of days before we left. Received a room upgrade as to view on arrival. The room was spacious. The bed was very comfortable. After an excursion we returned to find a birthday cake in our room. At an afternoon tea, the piano player played """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Happy Birthday"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for my wife and complementary chocolate covered strawberries with lighted candle were brought to our table.
Other than the tea, we only at breakfast at the hotel, but the meals were excellent. During our trip, we sampled egg dishes, pancakes, french toast and sides. All delicious. Service was attentive in all respects.. Complementary driver for trips within a limited distance made some travel convenient and more stylish and comfortable.
My wife had a smile on her face the entire stay.

The hotel itself was fine. Our room was nice enough. No complaints about the location, the room, etc. We have stayed at other hotels near the airport and found them really sketchy, but this one seemed to be in decent area. We stayed here one night due to an early flight the following morning. The front desk staff were very pushy about the airport shuttle and the breakfast. They asked us several times as to whether or not we were going to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""take advantage"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of their airport shuttle. We nicely told them repeatedly that we had already decided to use either the hourly parking or curbside valet offered by the Charlotte airport, but they continued to ask and try to pursude us to use their shuttle. It was just a little too much, too pushy. No means no. I understand if they would have just informed us of their services, but they just kept on and on. It was quite uncomfortable. Then, the next morning when we tried to check-out, they were pushy again with their breakfast. We informed them that we would just pick up something at the airport, but they were over the top about trying to convince us to eat at their hotel. Please people, take it down a notch! If you plan to stay here, just be prepared to be assertive and stand your ground.

Apparently there was a race on in Indy so lodging was a bit scarce. It was essentially our only choice in our price range. Now, we wish we'd have gone ahead and paid a little more. 
 The front desk staff were a bit slow but friendly. The first room we were assigned had smeared pizza on the carpet and when we alerted the staff they more than happy to assign us a new room. The hotel is sporting a banner that announces that they have all new rooms which isn't all together true. It appears some of the decor and bedding are fairly new, but the airconditioner wasn't and the bathroom tub wasn't either. The bathroom, overall, was not satisfactory. The sink faucet hadn't been properly installed and leaked water everytime you turned it on. The bathroom itself was tiny and we bumped our elbos and shoulders several times. The fixture that had been placed over the tub was cheap with the paint-surface peeling off in huge sheets. The beds were fairly comfortable, but one of the bed skirts was dirty and I couldn't help but be bothered by the stain everytime I looked at it. Housekeeping comes around quite early which is frustrating if you are looking to sleep in past -:--. Doesn't matter whether you place the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Do not Disturb"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sign on the door or not because the door and walls are so thin, when they knock on your neighbors door it's like they knocking on yours. 
 The hotel offers breakfast but this info was nowhere when I booked on line and no one bothered to mention it when we checked in so we ate elsewhere.
 Overall, if you can find somewhere else to say, I'd advise you to do so. The location is convenient but aside from that, the place is lacking.

We stayed at the Chancellor Hotel for - nights in late November and our stay was great. We arrived around --PM on our first night and check-in was very smooth. Our room was on the top floor, very clean, and decorated very tastefully. The bathroom was small, but more than adequate, and the complimentary bath products were very nice. The hotel was in a beautiful historic building with a lot of character. We were in San Francisco to celebrate my birthday and hotel had a complimentary bottle of wine waiting for us in our room. It was such a nice treat!
The -- hour coffee and tea, cookies, and apples were a very nice touch. The pillow menu was also amazing--it was fun trying out different types of pillows. 
We did eat breakfast at the hotel one day and it was our favorite breakfast in San Francisco (even better than Sears Fine Food in our opinion). Service was great. 
The location made it very easy to walk or take the Cable Cars around the city, and the hotel is only a few blocks from the BART station. 
We will definitely stay at the Chancellor again.

Nice hotel, but a bit of a walk in the heat from -th Street and other attractions. Rooms are small, and there don't seem to be any options for bigger rooms. Good gym and pool.
Lounge is nice but small, with fridge full of cold drinks available all the time. Breakfast was decent, but only - hot item per day.
Parking is a complete ripoff at $-- per night - many lots around hotel offer cheaper parking.

I travel to San Francisco frequently for work, and always stay at the Hotel Carlton. It's a great, small, out-of-the-way, affordable hotel with friendly staff. I joined the Joy of Life club (the Carlton's loyalty program) and they gave me a free bottle of wine!

I got this hotel thru priceline as a one night stay before our cruise. We arrived at -:--pm Thursday March -- and Veni H. was the one that checked us in. We were allowed to get to our room at that time, which was nice since we just drove from Orange County Airport after flying in from Portland and being up since -am. I put down a $--- cash deposit which was returned the next morning, minus the $-- parking fee, so you do not need a credit card like a previous poster said. The room we were assigned was number ---, on the -th floor overlooking the pool. The room had two beds and was nicely furnished. Everything, including the bathroom was very clean and working properly. The kids and I swam in the heated pool and really enjoyed the warm San Diego sun. The lobby was very nice and offered three computers with free internet and big screen televisions. The hotel was close to the Mission Valley Mall where we had lunch and close to the freeway for easy access. The only improvements I would suggest are that the faucet in the bathroom needs to be longer to make washing the hands easier and there needs to be four bath towels and not just three. It makes no sense to have a room for four with only three bath towels. Veni H. checked us out on Friday and she did a very good job and was very friendly and even knew my name. Overall, this was a great way to start our cruise vacation and I look forward to stay at this hotel again. Please feel free to see the pictures I took of our hotel stay and the video I will post on youtube. 
Robert Ghitea

I'll agree with most of the posts on this hotel. The location is great. If you're up to walking, you can pretty much walk anywhere from this hotel. If you don't feel like walking, but feel like checking out the sites the Philly Phlash stops right outside the hotels front door. We used this service one day to we planned visiting the museum, Eastern State Penitentiary, then going back to the historical areas. For a family of - it was $-- for all day off-on services. 
The room was great. It was a little worn and some of the furniture had cracks, but that didn't effect our stay one bit. After a week in other hotels w- all of us staying together in one room, it was nice having our own seperate room and having the kids on the sleeper sofa (kitchen always a plus too). The sleeper sofa was supposed to be queen sized, but it was probably a bit smaller. The kids definately didn't have as much room in this as they did a normal queen at other hotels. 
Someone complained about the elevators and internet service. Elevators seemed very quick to us. We stayed on the --th (actually --th) floor and with the expection of one time, the elevators were very prompt which actually surprised me. The internet service was wireless and it wasn't as quick as home, but it was still good. I've been in hotels where the wireless was just a waste of my time to even try and log in and use my laptop. I had no problem here, very responsive. 
Staff (including the valets) were very helpful and friendly. The Reading Terminal was very close (but closes early - or -pm) and had a great selections for food. There are numerous other selections nearby too. You definately won't starve...and if you have a sweet tooth for Dunkin' Donuts, there is one on the first floor on the corner. 
Our three night stay was very pleasant. I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again if I ever came back to Philly. Oh yeah, we also did go to a Phillies game...didn't bother with the subway (the wife was a bit nervous about trying out the Philly subway because of all the homeless in the area and especially with the possibility of traveling late night after the game), we drove down Broad St and it was fairly quick. Just down the road, but many stop lights.

It took me - months to write this review. I stayed at this crappy hotel in January, ---- because I was taking classes at Hopkins. The lobby belies what the guest rooms truly are. I thought I was at Motel - when I first walked into the first room I was assigned to. It was dark, grungy, and the bathroom had a shower stall that needed MAJOR repair and updating. I asked for a change of room because the curtains had a stench of old tobacco smoke, even though it was a non-smoking room. My next room was a tad better, brighter and cleaner, although I had to put up with a toilet with a leaky flush, peeling wallpaper, and dangerous half-hanging electrical wall sockets. I didn't change to another room because I was afraid what I might be assigned to next. I swear, it was like playing russian roulette! The front dest staff could sometime be friendly and helpful, but only if there was a manager in the vacinity. It is shameful that this property is part of the Hilton family. I had submitted a complaint to the Hilton Corporation in ----. It is now ---- and I am still waiting for a response.

This was a good place to stay that is nicer then a backpackers but doesn't have the extras that you would normally expect in a hotel. It was clean with a nice bed and to chill out it would be good. We ordered some take away and wanted to leave the rest in the fridge (which is in a common area) but that didn't work. This would be a good place to stay if you are into sci-fi as well because there are many little nifty things that they have put in the rooms. The check in is similar to checking into the airport and they seem to have used this as the main theme of the hotel. Ok for an inbetween place if you are sightseeing and want just a nice bed for the evening. Wouldn't be ok if you wanted to spend a bit of time in the room or hotel.

We've been to San Fran a bunch of times and have stayed around Union Sq and North Beach... So this time I looked for a great hotel away from the fray to make other parts of the great city a priority, and it was very easy to find Hotel Drisco because it's at the top of the tripadvisor popularity. We had a nicely sized King-room on the -nd floor with a view looking south-east. 
Location: Near the top of P.Heights, so everything is down... to the north, down a few VERY steep blocks then flattening to Marina-Cow Hollow...to the south, down medium steep blocks to Fillmore. We walked to to Alamo Sq (painted ladies), which was -.- miles and was pretty easy straight along Divisadero. We also took a bus to Haight...only a couple blocks away to get the bus and about -- minutes. Also took a $--(w-tip) cab ride to Mission.
Service: Very good. Helpful, friendly, professional. What you'd expect from a solid --star boutique hotel. 
Room: Comfy bed - slept well, good shower and plenty of room for my wife and I to move around. 
Breakfast: Fairly full continental lay-out. Nice pastries, cereals... My only complaint about the whole experience was that the cream for coffee wasn't fresh on - straight mornings. 
We had a great - day long weekend spending time in GG Park, Presidio, Haight, Mission, Marina and the Driso was the perfect hotel for that itinerary.

Stayed in a junior suite for three nights in late November. The hotel was in a central location and things were ‘OK’ I suppose, but I travel regularly for business and pleasure and maybe it’s just me, but I remember a time when the Hyatt did more than just be ‘OK’. Examples included:
- Flying in from the UK, we were visiting New York for the first time to celebrate a ‘milestone’ (i.e. ends with a ‘-’) birthday for my wife. I mentioned this to the hotel in advance, and again when we checked-in and it was never even acknowledged. I’m not expecting champagne in the room (although I've had this from the Hilton in the past), but a smile and a ‘congratulations’ would have been nice
- Whilst we didn't get a “happy birthday” from the reception staff, we did get told our room wasn't ready (at three in the afternoon) and when we came back yet again at -pm the member of staff just said “wait a moment” and walked away to obviously try and fit us in somewhere...-- minutes later I was still standing there until another member of staff asked if I was OK and went to find out what had happened
- To be fair, the room was a good size and with a nice view over Grand Central station. But no bathrobes, no tea and coffee making facilities, tiny bathroom and no HDTV. For a US Hyatt hotel, the absence of bathrobes and a kettle was surprising, but watching TV programmes that looked like they were received via a metal coat-hanger on stuck on the roof was really shocking.
- No free wifi, not even in public areas! I know it’s great fun for a hotel that has a large proportion of business travellers to charge for internet, but it’s nearly ---- now and free wifi should be standard, not an added bonus
- When I inquired about going into the Regency (executive) lounge, I was told that I would not be allowed access because I was ‘only’ a Platinum member. So despite staying in a suite and having the misfortune to drop to the second-highest tier after being a Diamond Hyatt member for the past three years I was not allowed into the promised land of free canapés and soft drinks
That’s not to say it’s not a nice hotel, and it is in a central location. But when my baby is screaming at -am and there isn’t a kettle to boil some water for his formula, my proximity to Spiderman the Musical didn't really seem like such an important factor.
So maybe it isn’t the hotel at all, maybe it’s me and I just ask too much, but I’ve shown considerable loyalty to this brand over the years and when it came to the crunch they didn’t deliver. I’m sure they will promise to do better next time, but I don’t plan to fly ---- miles to celebrate another birthday any time soon.
There was a time when Hyatt was considered miles above the Hilton, but from now on I’ll be switching to the Hilton, and I’ll be telling my friends and colleagues to do the same.

I booked this place for its location more than anything else, just off the mile and a short walk to the pier. The room was small but had everything we wantedand it was clean. The desk staff were really great and gave us some fantastic tips for places to eat. Our claim to fame was that we sat next to Gloria Estefan in a pizza place just around the corner. There is a starbucks and a supermarket on the same block. we went to the pool ( which was freezing) for a quick dip and thats is looking a bit tatty. There are more fancy hotels but you will pay a premium unless you can get them cheap. Despite being in the centre of Chicago we had a room on the inside of the hotel so it was very quiet. Overall i was quite happy with the stay but the hotel is a bit non descript and forgettable.

Nice to find a clean, cost effective lodging option in the Westwood neighborhood. Rooms were nicer than the lobby and exterior would suggest. Rooms were clean and comfortable. Parking is available. As other reviewers have noted, spaces are very narrow and smaller vehicles are recommended. Did not participate in the breakfast offerings; coffee, tea, toast, cereal and fruit were available. Location is excellent for shops, restaurants, museums, and UCLA.

I expected the Watertown Hotel to be a nice place – and it was – but the thing that separated it from the pack of hotels I've stayed at lately is the attitude of the employees. Whatever you asked, it seemed, the answer was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Yes."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Can I get a computer in my room? Sure. Can I use your office computer to print out -- sheets of data? No problem. Call me a car that can take me to the airport for a more-than-reasonable price? Right away. There was never any of that infuriating, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Sorry, I'll have to ask the manager,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" or, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Corporate says we're not allowed to do that."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I asked, and they said yes – even when I took more than one chocolate chip cookie.
A few more nice things about Watertown: The rooms are well laid out, with the bathroom and dressing area tucked away in a private nook behind the TV stand-wardrobe; the University District restaurants, coffee houses, and shops are a five-minute walk away – closer than it looks on a map – and downtown Seattle is a ---minute drive; the free breakfast (eggs, bacon, fruit, bagels, toast, spreads, juices, cereals) is generous, and the restaurant area and outside tables are great spots to relax with a cup of coffee all through the day; the parking is free! 
Fourteen members of my family stayed at Watertown and its sister property the University Inn, which is a block down the street. The Watertown is definitely an adult hotel. The University Inn is better for children, with more of a family vibe and a nice little pool. I'd stay at either one again.

With so many hotels to choose from in San Francisco, I was hoping I had selected one that I could call Excellent and Hotel --- fit the bill! The hotel and room exceeded my expectation and the location is perfect! Following check-in by a very helpful staff, we walked across the street from the hotel and hopped on a cable car - even my -- year-old daughter thought that was pretty cool! Our room was large and very comfortable for the three of us (- adults, - teenager). And after my husband dragged us around the city until --:--pm we were happy that there was a Starbucks on an opposite corner! 
Would definitely recommed this hotel and it will be my first choice when we visit San Francisco again!

Booked a suite for a bachelor party. Staff were great at check in, room was exceptional, and the hotel facilities are excellent. Partied at the rooftop bar (closes at -.--?) and ate in the restaurants, everything was great. It is a pricey hotel but if you want a good place to have fun this is it.

My boyfriend and I stayed at the Benjamin ----- Jan ---- and had a great time. The furniture is classy, the marble bathrooms elegant and the Aveda shower products divine. The sheets are so comfortable and the down comforter was the best. The walk in closet gave us lots of room even if the room itself wasn't the biggest. We each had our own bathrobes. The view was just of the building across the street, but looking down from the --th floor onto busy Lexington Ave. was fun. The concierge-couldn't have been nicer or more accommodating-and we never felt looked-down upon even though we're a young couple. They answered every question we had with kindness and authority. The location is great, just a few blocks from Grand Central and Times Square. If you are coming from JFK, I suggest taking the AirTrain ($-)to the E subway ($-) and getting off at Lexington and --rd instead of paying $--+ for a taxi, unless it's really late at night. I took the subway (as a girl alone at -.-- am) from the hotel to JFK and it worked out fine, I didn't ever feel unsafe or get lost. The public transportation in this city is awesome! The Fin Bar in the hotel is nothing special, but it's a nice place to relax and have a cold beer, with excellent service and nice decor. I'd definitely go there again!

Unbeatable wharf location. Close to all shops-dining. Expensive parking. Rooms and bathroom a bit small but clean and comfortable. Nice balcony with two chairs-table view of bay and city. Front desk staff was very fast and pleasant. Very cozy outdoor fire pit area that was perfect to sit by with a drink and relax after seeing all the sights.

Hotel included in Titan travel tour. Bedrooms small, bathroom tiny. Price of food and room service very good. Maid service pathetic, stayed - nights room cleaned twice. Complained at reception before going out in evening but room still not cleaned.
Ran out of toilet paper had to beg of other guest. Tried to change travellers cheques but both times reception said they had no money.

After reading a few of the negative reviews of this hotel, I must admit I was a little skeptical. However, my stay at the Hilton Times Square March ----- was nothing short of fantastic! We arrived an hour or two before check-in time, and they put us in a room right away, on the --nd floor. While our window did not overlook Times Square, it had a sweeping view of the Hudson River on the right, and a gorgeous view of the Empire State Building at night. We could even see the Statue of Liberty straight ahead! The room was immaculate and had so much room, even more room than some of the hotels in the South! The bed was comfortable and the bathroom towels were big and soft. The hotel staff downstairs in the bottom floor were always nice no matter what time we got in at night. Even the bartenders at the bar in the lobby were very friendly. I've been to New York three times in the past three years and this was the best stay I've had. I'll definitely be staying there when I return!

The Steinhart Hotel is one of four in the Personality Hotels chain. We picked it mainly because it offers apartments, our preferred option when traveling these days especially with our two teenagers in tow for space and independence. 
We found Sutter St to be an eclectic neighbourhood populated by all cultures. The Academy of Art University has a residence nearby so there are quite a few students and artistic oriented types mulling around. The Lower Nob Hill address is really an in-between kind of street some walking blocks from Nob Hill, a wealthy district and Union Square, the shopping mecca. 
The surrounding area has no real attraction but is littered with """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""mom and pop"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" type restaurants, small businesses and several hotels. People are friendly and you get the sense of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""living amongst the locals"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". There is a drop off laundry, Sutter Cleaners across the road providing good efficient service and a wonderful Gelato shop five doors down. Food is defiantly not a problem with a huge range of restaurants and eateries, grocery shops and a deli around the hotel vicinity. The neighbourhood is quiet at night.
The hotel itself is housed in a historical building, the residence of Mr Steinhart who donated the Steinhart Museum to the city of San Francisco. The architecture is wonderful and it transports you back to the early ----s. Our apartment was on the third floor overlooking the back courtyard. It was huge with separate bedroom, adequate functioning kitchen, dining and living areas as well as lots of closet space. The kids slept on rollaways in the living room which closes off for privacy. The only unfortunate thing was that the rooms did not receive a lot of natural lighting and were dark, so lights had to be on all the time. The neighbours are really close so blinds need to be down for privacy but it looked like all the apartments shared a similar fate. The lighting inside was adequate but brighter bulbs would have been appreciated. It became home in San Francisco very quickly for us. 
The Hotel front desk is manned from - am to - pm by a resident manager. He was welcoming and helpful but sometimes hard to find, probably due to being the only person responsible for the hotel. The is no concierge as well. Apartments are cleaned once a week, and the is a laundry downstairs (make sure you have coins and laundry powder). Don't forget the door pass codes especially after hours or you might be waiting a long time for someone to come by to let you in. There are no business facilities but there is free wifi in the rooms. Just beware that the fax machine does not work and there is no access to printers when the hotel manager is not around.
Would we return? Depends on what we need. Yes for longer stays and no for shorter visits or on business. The Steinhart is not at the centre of action but it has charm.

I came here after a bad experience across the street at the Sheraton. I walked in got a room that I wanted right away after being on a red eye flight. They honored my corporate rate and were very professional. The laday at reception Delores was so nice and kind she called house keeping and had a room ready in no time.
Sometimes people working at hotels forget that they are in a service industry . They did not at the Hilton, I would stay here again and recomend it to anyone.

Hotel is extremely clean. Fantastic location. We were lucky because our room was not ready so we were upgraded to a waterfront room free of charge w-no contest by Edgewater's insistence.
Shuttle is very flexible and convenient (though not terribly handicap accessible).
Highly recommended though pricey.

This hotel seems to get mixed reviews. It may not be the best Ritz Carlton but it is certainly a very nice hotel. When we checked in it was a little busy, but the hotel staff handled the situation very well and efficiently. Our room was good sized and comfortable. It may not have had a major wow factor, but it was in very good shape and had a large window that overlooked the skyline even though the hotel is on the lower floors of a tall building. The bathroom was standard Ritz, with lots of marble, separate tub, shower, and water closet. 
The rest of the hotel is very attractive with nice earth tones used and contemporary artwork placed throughout the hotel. The overall feeling created is of a small boutique hotel with modern touches. Some however may find the atmosphere in the hotel restaurant Jer-Ne a little too club like for a Ritz Carlton. We had breakfast here each day. The food was okay, the service very good.
A highlight of this hotel is the access to a sports club for a fee of fifteen dollars. Our package included admission. We feel strongly that spas and gyms should always be included in the price of the room, but this is one time when we would not have complained about the charge. This is one amazing gym. Very large and upscale, it is a place that could keep you busy for some time with lots of different activities.
The staff at the hotel was very friendly and helpful, even by Ritz Carlton standards. The immediate area around is nothing to write home about. But the location is central and Boston is a compact city making walking easy to most locations. Overall, this is a very nice hotel with great service that lives up to Ritz standards.
