 Overall, we had a good stay. We spend a lot of time on the city exploring and the hotel was just used to rest, shower and sleep. We think it was good, for the rate we paid, $-- a night. Not bad for San Francisco. With the money we saved, we did a lot of other things and we ate very well. 
 I almost forgot, the hotel personnel was very nice and helpful, specially Elli at the front desk. She gave us a lot of options for restaurants in the area. We most likely will go back to this hotel.

A week later I'm looking at my credit card activity online, and sure enough, the hotel already billed me the cost of my stay. I called the hotel, politely asking whether they had possibly made a mistake and billed me in advance. The gentleman on the other line raised his voice at me, saying they never charge people in advance, it's the travel website's fault, I need to contact them. I replied that my credit card activity clearly stated that the charge came from the Seattle Pacific Hotel, that there was no way the hotel website could bill me in the hotel's name, and whether he could please check on this. He responded even more rudely that he already told me they never bill anyone before check-in, he would charge my credit card when I arrived regardless, and that he couldn't help me. Not knowing what else to do, and not wanting to pay twice, I contacted the helpdesk of the travel website to clear it up. A week later, finally, the money has been credited back to my account, and I've booked a room somewhere else. If you're like me and think bad things tend to happen to other peple rather than yourself, think again before you book a room at this hotel -- or they might just scam you out of your money. I can't believe people like this stay in business!

I booked for a night over Labor day weekend. They had a Staycation package with a hotel credit. We planned to use the pool and room service and it all worked out as planned. Even without stepping foot in the Casino, we had a good time. I had heard that the Burgers in the restaurant were good, so we ordered. Yum - carmelized onions, etc... yes it was more expensive than a Big Mac, but its a rare treat. We were on the Concierge floor so even better. We could avoid using the mini bar and just grab a few sodas, coffee, etc.. I don't drink, so the light stuff is fine for me.
The room, very nice. Comfy bed, robe, etc... Since the hotel is newly built, it has all the amenities and then some including a Bose sound system and TV in the bathroom, dual head shower, etc... My only slight surprise is there was not a tub in my room. Not sure if you have to ask for one, but the shower was very nice. Everyone in my family went in and stayed for a long time. 
The pool was a good size. A little shallow, a little cold at first, but no one was there, so we had it to ourselves. Nice cabanas to sit out. The hot tub was in the shower area. Again, nice showers, steam room. I didn't have time for the spa, but maybe on another trip.
If you're close by and need a night off, I'd recommend it. Only down side is its not really downtown, so you can't walk to anything, nor is it River Front, but the valet will arrange for your car to come around and valet parking is included in the price (unlike many hotels in Chicago, etc...) All you have to do is tip.

I don't know what all the complaining is about. The Monarch is an affordable hotel in downtown San Fran. It doesn't have all the bells and whistles, but the sheets are clean, the water in the shower is hot and the hotel is clean. Sure, there are homeless people around, but that is what a city is all about. When people go on vacation, no one goes out to see the suburbs...the city is where the diversity and real life is. 
It is a few blocks away from Union Square, near Van Ness which takes you to all the major highways and there are amenities everywhere. 
Sure, there is an adult video store across the street but it is on a main road and near everything. Stop being so judgemental and cranky. If you don't like the grit, stay in the burbs.

Was here for a convention and got a room upgrade to the Wardman Tower. Aside from a SUBSTANTIAL walk from the Lobby, the room was spacious and had an older charm. The general appearance suggests that a renovation is needed to make the room warmer and more enticing. 
The food at the hotel is adequate. Go elsewhere.
The help ranges from fabulous management types to really inefficient union workers. 
Marriott needs to do some work in this regard.

Very nice rooms and staff, expect a good solid Hilton service in a modern tower, however the construction in ground zero can still be bothersome. You will experience great views on the higher floors of Manhattan and Brooklyn as well as the new freedom towers. Would recommend staying there only when they have specials or bidding through Priceline as regular night price is the outrageous $---+

We spent five nights at this hotel and were very satisfied with the location, the rooms and the staff. Although one of the elevators was waiting for a repair part, we were able to get to our room on the --th floor with little difficulty. The rooms aren't large, but they are reasonable for the location. It was spotlessly clean, the breakfast was more than sufficient, and the front desk staff were outstanding and helpful. It was about a eight block walk to Time's Square, it is in the fashion district and there are restaurants, shopping and of course Broadway shows close by.

We stayed here for - days last month attending a bridge tourneyment.
My wife played in the tourneyment. The staff and food service were just outstanding.
We also stay at Mariott's when ever we can because of the way management takes of their guests.

We stayed at the Chancellor for - nights whilst sightseeing in San Francisco. The hotel is in an excellent location, just off Union Square. 
One of the terminus points for the Powell-Hyde cable car line was only about - minutes walk from the hotel. Riding this cable car is an easy and fun way to get to the Fishermans Wharf and Pier -- areas. If shopping is your thing, there are many, many shops and department stores within a few blocks of the hotel. 
Our room was well-presented, clean and of a decent size. The only real problem was the lack of air conditioning in the room; this was no surprise as the hotel's website makes clear that A-C is not available. It was very hot during some of our stay in San Francisco and the room's ceiling fan wasn't really up to keeping the room cool.
Tea, coffee and cookies are available free-of-charge in the hotel lobby. Breakfast was not included in the price of our room. There is a restaurant within the hotel. We ate breakfast there one morning, which was ok but a little expensive.

We stayed at the Belvedere July -----, ----. Having had some negative experiences in the past at Manhattan hotels, we were very pleasantly surprised by the quality of the Belvedere for the price ($--- a night, which to me is high, but not by NYC standards). All the staff members we encountered were friendly and efficient. Our room was spacious and looked recently renovated - very clean and pleasantly decorated. The bathroom fixtures also appeared to be new and well cared for. Housekeeping was great. The lobby and elevators were lovely old art deco. The view from our room (--th floor) was breathtaking. The - elevators are very small; this never caused us any problem until the day we checked out. Lots of others were checking out also and the volume did cause a wait of -- minutes for the elevator. We didn't eat at the restaurants - had breakfast around the corner at the Olympic, which served good, hearty food for a reasonable price. The location of this hotel can't be beat for access to the theatre district, the great Hell's Kitchen restaurants and all other midtown attractions. I highly recommend!

It was a men's trip. Me, Son, Grandson. This place offered a roll-a-way bed for free! All the places on the Wharf are just a few blocks away. Beware $-- a night to park a car? What's with that!!! The room was clean, lobby was nice, coffee in the morning, not bad. Room price went up $-- a night when tax was added??? San Francisco...It almost seems they will pad the bill in every possible instance. Hint: Stay away from the Imperial Palace restaurant in Chinatown, the one off Grant and Washington. Bad food and the worst-rude service I have ever encountered. The Stinging Rose on Columbus is great, prices are a little high, but worth it.
We did the Hop on Hop off, two day ride ($--). That's a great way to see the town and cross the golden gate in an open top red bus. 
The walk across the Golden Gate was very hazardous with all the high speed bicyclists jetting through as though they were the privileged one percent. (Coming so close to families pushing strollers with babies-this is a terrible accident just waiting to happen.)
Until next time America...

It's a typical modern business centric hotel. No better and no worse than any other large chain. I've stayed twice with my family and was upgraded on one occasion. To be honest the upgraded room was slightly bigger with a better view but no major difference apart from that. It really is at the top of one of the hills and therefore the climb up can be pretty steep. It's next to a couple of tram lines so you can mitigate that easily enough.
Had a few drinks at the bar at the top of the hotel and the views of SF were fantastic, worth a trip even if you are not staying there.
Fairly expensive though, I'd look for somewhere cheaper in the future. 
BTW - As usual in these types of big hotel internet connectivity was extra which I find absurd as most small hotels give it away free.

My wife and I went to New York for a week for our Anniversary. I looked at several hotel reviews and websites and Sofitel's reviews, website and location stood out. Two blocks from time square, - block from bryant park, - blocks from Central Station and right in between - and -th ave. 
We booked a luxury room with the Haute Cuisine package which includes a daily breakfast and one dinner. The Gaby restaurant was amazing, the food was great both breakfast and dinner, and the staff was just beyond great, very attentive. One night after walking all day, we arrived at the hotel and my wife wanted some coffe, so we down to the Gaby restaurant and asked for a cup of coffee to go. I was expecting to pay for it but the amazing staff brought - to go cups a full pot of coffee and a hor dourves tray and told us it was on the house. 
On our first night after checking in we went for a small walk to bryant park and came back to our room and found an amazing chocolate dessert that said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Happy Anniversary"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and on the - night, we had just walked in the room when a nice staff member brought us a bottle of champagne in an ice bucket and two glasses. Let me just say that I never asked for it and was never charged for it, they only knew it was our anniversary because the reception staff asked me if we were there for business or leisure and I responded that we were their for our anniversary.
My wife and I had great time in New York and Sofitel made it even more special.

I stayed - nights for a conference. I got a PURE allergy-free room and it was renovated, beautiful and very clean. It still had that new carpet smell. The beds were very comfortable. The room had an air filtering machine that could be loud if its turned up high, so I switched it to low to quieten it. The air conditioning is powerful and cold but very noisy. However I got used to the a-c noise after the -nd night.
There is truck traffic noise outside which woke me in the pre-dawn hours. And there's an ice machine outside my door which woke me at -am when another guest got ice, - nights in a row! The sound of tumbling ice cubes was very loud. He must be sick or injured to be getting ice like that!
Maid service was great, bathroom cleaned well and toilet paper stocked up. The front desk was polite. Even though my room wasn't ready when I checked-in in the morning, they called me on my cell when it was ready and I could check-in.
I did not try the hotel bars and restaurants so I can't judge those.
Valet parking was inefficient. They didn't link my ticket to my room so the parking attendant had to ask me when I checked-in and what room I was in when I went to retrieve my car to leave the hotel. I didn't have to pay it though because the conference paid.
Overall I might recommend this place, despite the noise. Just ask for a room away from the ice machine and on a quiet side (if there is one).

Am disappointed reading these bad reviews. I stayed at this hotel for - nights in March and it was excellent. We were booked in immediately upon arrival and given free upgrades to superior rooms. My room was spacious, clean and airy with a HUGE queen-size bed - possibly the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in. I had an awesome view of the Empire State Building from my room. All staff I came across were friendly and helpful, especially Mihaela, the owner of the Dresden Gift Shop in the lobby - so lovely and welcoming!
This hotel is ideally located - right across the street from Penn Station and Madison Square Garden and about -- mins walk from Times Square.
I'll definitely be staying in this hotel when I return to New York!

This hotel is right next to the World Trade Center site so traffic and noise is a problem outside - but inside, we were overlooking the construction and heard nothing. The hotel is remarkably convenient, even if you have to get to mid-town, the subways are very close. The hotel itself is very modern and comfortable, the bathrooms are huge by NY standards, but we found the staff to range from super-helpful to completely clueless. It was kind of funny to see such a difference in one hotel.

We decided to stay at this hotel after finding a deal on their weekend impulses on their website. It was only $-- per night. We were very satisfied with our entire stay. The room was nice with two double beds. It was me, my husband, and our two kids (ages - and -). The beds were big enough for us but might be too small for four adults or people who need more room. The continental breakfast was good. They had strawberries and whipped cream to put on top of the waffles after you make them. They had four waffle makers on two of the mornings and three on one morning. When there were four waffle makers, there was no line to make waffles. We did have to wait about five minutes on day with only three. There were plenty of tables to sit at in their dining area so we didn't have to wait for a table. The kids went swimming the first day. There were not very many people at the pool and it was nice and quiet. They have umbrellas on the tables to block the sun which was great because it was very sunny while we were at the pool. We went to the river walk on the first night there and I think it was about a -- minute drive. We went to Sea World the next three days and it took about -- minutes to get there. We were very happy with the location of the hotel and the price. We will definately stay here again soon for our next trip to Sea World.

Typical corporate hotel experience: bland, clean rooms and professional service. Hotel security was also reasonably prompt in breaking up a group of drunken revelers noisily celebrating in the hallways at four am. If your room is high enough (and faces the right direction), the views of the city are great. 
But what sets the hotel apart is its location, which has both pluses and minuses. In nice weather being on the river--and close to riverside attractions--could be very pleasant. However, it only adds to the chill factor in the winter. The hotel is also relatively close to the old part of the city and the historical sites, although it is cut off from them by the chasm of the highway. It is not especially convenient to center city or the museums, so consider carefully why you're coming to Philly.

We stayed here for - nights in September ----. The room we stayed in was very small, no room for a wardrobe just a small cupboard. The staff where very good and the room was fairly clean, location is excellent. Because of the excellent location it can be a bit noisy at night, but at the end of the day you're in New York there arent many quiet areas it really is a -- hour city.

I stay in August ---- and the hotel was fairly new. The Omni is attached to the Dallas Convention Center which makes it a perfect location if you are attending a conference. You can walk directly to the conference center on the second floor so that we didn't need to go outside in the --- degree heat. The rooms are modern although the air conditioning in my first room did not work properly. The staff was exteremely accomodating and moved all my unpacked stuff to a nicer room. I widh there was a real desk to work at instead of a counter by the TV. Definitely not enough outlets in the room. The doormen were fantastic and remembered me during my entire stay. There is a small lounge in the lobby where you can have a drink. We told the bartender Nick what ingredients we liked and he whipped up some fantastic cocktails. I ate at the sports restaurant twice and Texas Spice twice. Both were okay. Not great, not bad. All in all, this was a great hotel for my - day stay.

First off, I should state that my Friday night stay was gratis. Yes. """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Free"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I decided to cash in my Starwood free weekend night reward at the best that Starwood had to offer in LA, and live it up. Of course, nothing really comes free in LA, which is to be expected. Parking (valet only) is $--.---night ($-- + $-.-- tax). And eating, drinking, and tipping for all the excellent service offered at the hotel will rack up a pretty hefty balance by the end of any stay.
The front desk was as efficient as possible at prime time (-pm) on a Friday afternoon...though perhaps a little too efficient. Made my way to my room (---), which turned out to be an accessible room. I really wished that the front desk person had notified me about this or asked if this was okay with me, because it was not. I'm not a fan of open or only curtained-off showers that get the whole bathroom floor wet, or wardrobes where the rod is situated so low that the bottom of my hanging dresses are crumpled on the closet floor. Though, these things are clearly important for someone wheelchair-bound. And for an accessible room it was really nice, otherwise.
Called down to the front desk from the room and asked for a room change. There wasn't another one available 'til ---pm though, so they promised to call and let me know when it was ready, via my cell. So, my friend and I got changed and went up to relax at the pool on the -th floor. 
Pool area is more """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""seen and be seen"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""group tanning salon"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" than """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""let's get your swim on"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". It gets crowded on the weekend, and it's a little confusing at first trying to find an empty chaise or daybed. There seems to only be one guy who's in charge of handing out towels at the entrance, as well as taking the old ones away from the chaises when ppl leave. Often, people are deterred from claiming a vacated chair because the used towels and leftover food-drink trays are left there for so long. I think this could be addressed if the servers who are walking the pool perimeter better communicate with the towel guy or participate in bussing after the departing guests themselves.
But once you have a spot, it's a nice place to relax on a hot day, with some cool drinks and lunch-snack. It is a small space though, and no offense to people who have families, but the peace is kind of disrupted when people bring their gaggle of young children up to the pool. The atmosphere at this hotel is pretty adult-oriented and it surprises me that people would want to bring their kids here. I can imagine what kids might do to the abundant reflective surfaces in the rooms, and I shudder for the housekeeping staff.
After a few hours, returned to room ---; still no word from front desk, so called down again, and this time they sent up a bellman to help move us. Bobby the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Luggage Ambassador"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" showed up and he was great. Moved us to a second floor terrace room (sliding glass door leads to a furnished patio area).
Superior rooms are about --- sq. ft, of swanky modern style. Lots of tinted reflective surfaces, square edges, leather, glass, low lighting, --- thread count sheets, and tongue in cheek decorative touches. Large shower-only in bathroom, no tub. The mini-bar is not so mini. It's pretty awesome actually. Full-sized bottles of several premium liquors (including Patron), lots of snack variety, mini fridge with all the rest of the usual suspects. And the best part - NO BIBLE! Yes, Finally! The only things I'd change in the room is to -: make the safe easier to access for someone shorter than -'-"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (at -'-"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I could reach in, it was just difficult to see if I'd gotten everything out...maybe add a curved mirror to the inside roof of the safe?), and -: it would be nice if the room had a folding luggage rack.
The hotel is gorgeous and fun and the hotel staff are attentive service-providers. Big, fancy gym and business center are open ----. Restaurants are impressive-looking spaces. The Bazaar is amazing and YUMMY, and attracts a huge following, esp on weekend nights. Hotel guests have priority for reservations at The Bazaar and other SBE-managed hot spots (Katsuya, Area, Hyde, The Abbey, XIV, etc.). The concierge staff (Alex and Freddo) were knowledgeable and helpful, and Neil the doorman-Valet director extraordinaire was really on the ball. And I'd like to thank Dan, one of our house car drivers who literally stopped traffic to help us get to our destination across the street.
Overall, this hotel feels like a hip - star Vegas boutique hotel; I've stayed at the Encore, Wynn, TheHotel, Caesar's, and Venetian, and other than the lack of a bathtub, and all of those other things that make Vegas mega-resorts feel bloated, the SLS has """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""it"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" - the glamor, luxury, indulgent atmosphere, and the beautiful people. Come here to indulge and have a good time, but like Vegas, leave the kids and penny-pinching at home.
This is the hippest Starwood property I've stayed at (I'm a fan of Westins & Le Meridiens), and I'd come back again.

I was nervous before arriving at the hotel to see our rooms after reading about the bad reviews posted here. I didn't really bother with checking the reviews before i booked it. I just assumed that because it is part of Wyndham it should be nice and the hotel looked great on the pictures. When we got there, they had the rooms all ready and waiting for us an hour before check in time, they also made sure that the two Jr. suites I booked were next to each other as I have requested. The lady from the front desk offered extra blankets and towels right away as soon as she noticed that we have extra guests staying on the pull out. The rooms did not disappoint, it was exactly as expected and more,two flat screen tv's was an awesome. I don't know why they were getting a lot of bad rap about the service, but the maids who cleaned our room were great, there were no bed bugs ( first thing we did was check!) and the room was newly remodeled and clean. Sure the tv had only -- channels but who wants to watch tv on their vacation all day anyway? The heated pool was also an added plus. Some issues, parking was difficult to find at night time and if other guests weren't talking outside our room in the hallway at -am in the morning ( but that wasn't the hotel's fault, just some inconsiderate people who taught it was their business to be loud and obnoxious). We will definitely be booking from this hotel every time we are in San Diego. It is so close to Sea World!

Travelled from Ireland to stay in this hotel very near to the White House it is also beside metro stations very easy to visit all the monuments - museums in the city . Room was spacious a nice surprise in a city centre hotel, bed was very comfortable, large tv. The room-bathroom were keep spotless by the cleaning staff. Staff at all times were very friendly and helpful. Hotel had nice bar area to have a drink or meal in the evening but many nice restaurants within walking distance of the hotel . I would definely stay at the Capital Hilton again

This is a Super- motel..except it may offend Super -. So the first night, my bathroom light is out. I tell them, the next day it is fixed.The next night the heat is out. The third night my laundry does not show up.... and the staff all along is treating you like a problem child. The location of this hotel is one of the best you can get. But thats it!! EVERYTHING else is going to suck. Guarenteed.... and I hav stayed at the Copthorne in Singapore (from the same chain) and the Church Street Millineum, both of which are absolutely fine; of course Copthorne being miles ahead as the staff actually aims to please. 
This place - Best avoided.

This Hampton Inn is fine. My husband and I stayed here for two nights while at Mayo Clinic. The king rooms only have showers with not bathtub and the Internet is a bit slow at times but the staff more than makes up for any deficits! Their prompt attention to guest needs is outstanding! Upon checking in and finding that our room had no bathtub I called to see if we could change rooms. Within - minutes someone came to our room to bring us the key to another room and help us move our luggage! At another time I had a slight problem with the AC not cooling and the maintenance person was there within - minutes of my call. A member of the housekeeping staff immediately went downstairs to get more decaf coffee packets when I asked her if more were available - even when I suggested she could bring them up later in the day or I could pick them up myself at the desk. 
We would certainly stay here again!

I'd stay here again, but would request a room much higher up. I think all the rooms down one hallway are right over the Elephant-Castle restaurant next door, which is open until midnight daily. It was bad. The staff was very helpful and the room plenty large enough for my husband and me. The bathroom was tiny but we were just there a weekend so it was not a big deal. I liked the do-it-yourself water bottles - nice that you don't have to pay. We were short on time so ate breakfast at the Elephant Castle - VERY slow and indifferent service and the food was just edible.

We stayed here for our first trip to NYC. It was in a fairly decent location (near theatres) and right around the corner from Times Square. It was a little noisy with the traffic outside, but its NYC! Restaurants were close and there were subway stations not far so getting around was easy. There was a continental breakfast, but I would skip it. There are plenty of street vendors in the area you can stop by on your way out.

I had a conference here in March ----. I stayed two nights at the Hyatt via priceline to save money and then transferred to this hotel on the last night. The Hyatt (which is within walking distance, across a couple of parking lots) is a FAR nicer place. Great service, great rooms. This Marriott is just average. The rooms are not huge, the bathrooms could use remodeling, and the atmosphere is pretty blah. The Denver tech center area is pretty much a ghost town on the weekends. There are a few restaurants in large plazas surrounded by office parks; you need to go downtown (short drive, or via light rail) for any kind of nightlife.

I stayed with my parents at the Muse Hotel in NYC from Dec. ---Jan. -rd. We arrived around --:-- A.M. and the room was not ready. They tried to give us a room at that time but didn't have anything available, so we left our luggage and left to the Metropolitan Museum. We got back around -:-- P.M. and the room was ready (check in is at -:-- P.M.). The Closing of the streets was affecting the access to the hotel after -:-- P.M. on Dec. --st but it was very well organized by the hotel. We had no problem moving through Times Square with the room key and a letter from the hotel. We stayed in a remodeled room with - beds (they are full size) and the room was fairly ample. Flat screen tv, mini bar, daily newspaper, robes, cordless phone, i-pod port...everything we needed for a great stay in the city. Check in was smooth and the hotel people were very friendly at all times. As other reviews mentioned, there's a wine reception in the afternoon at the hotel lobby, which was very nice. Didn't get to eat at The District restaurant so cannot comment on it. We were charged for some items from the mini bar that we did not consume but I addressed the situation to the front desk and they didn't ask any questions and removed the charges. The location is one of the best things about The Muse! It is closed to everything but on a street that is not noisy at all. Also, you get the personalized attention from a boutique hotel that is not found on a bigger chain hotel. I will definitely stay at The Muse again and again!!

We stayed at the hotel at the end of May ----. We had a good, clean room just opposite the Safeco Field. We could even see some of the players from our room during one match. The hotel's location is great for sports event at the Safeco Field or the Qwest Field. The staff was friendly and the pool seemed fine. Please be aware of the noise and ask for a quite room. We woke up several times during the night due to some loud train siren which did not really help us with our jet leg.

Hotel is extremely nice, very convient to most stuff but parking is like $-- a day. Yikes. I think some other folks mentioned the lofty parking prices but they are probably the highest I'd seen in the city. I was there for - days and left the car parked the entire time and just decided to walk everywhere. Everything was reasonably close. The longest walk was the Prime Rib restaraunt which it was late so I took a cab back. My office was about -- blocks and the warf probably another - blocks or so. The room was a good size, the bed was comfortable, clean and very hip. The restaraunt was reasonably priced for a swanky hotel. The bus boy kept reminding us when the they closed. Guess he didn't want us holding him up... Our waiter was great and the food was pretty good. 
I'd definately stay again but I would just take a cab from the airport and walk everywhere or take a cab. Less hassle and cheaper in the long run.

Stayed here for - nights in October ---- with my father and son. The room was ready for us just after lunch, which was especially nice seeing as we had just flown in from Sydney.
The room was clean and reasonably well appointed. The plasma screen TV was appreciated. We had no noise from the hallways or the street outside.
The hotel is a - min walk to Fisherman's Wharf, which is pretty much the tourist centre of San Francisco. The hire car offices are around the corner which is also convenient.
We did not eat at the note, preferring to find our own meals at the many and varied restaurants in the area.
Will I stay here again? Yep, not a problem.

We went with our family and friends and it was perfect. The location was probebly the best part. The beds were really comfertable, the service was great, and it was a beautiful hotal! If you want a nice treat they have very good sorbet! They have a very nice pool and spa as well! It is close to some of bostons great attractions! On every floor they have great little canies to help you start your day! One thing that was really cool was, riding on a peddy cab looking at the beautiful arch! Everybody we saw was nice to the kids! They even gave the kids a little story coloring book! The second we called for the pull out coach to be made, they were in our room making it! Another thing that was great was the housekeeping, they were in and out of our room very fast! Everything about this hotal was great! I recommend this hotal to anyone!

A very disappointing hotel. The rooms are plain and unimaginitive and are totally blocked from natural light by the highest building in Boston which is positioned next to it. The age of the hotel is noticable. Acomplete lack of public rooms. Only one bar which is dark and miserable, nowhere else at all for guests to relax. Noise from weddings on the - nights we were there was unbelievable. A companion found a FLEA in her bed. Staff smiled politely but were toally ineffectual. They just didn't want to know, were smug, huffy, snappy and useless in dealing with the public, from the bellman to the manager. Take my advise and avoid this place like the plague. I don't give bad reviews, read my others, but don't stay here.

It was my boyfriend and I first trip to NYC. Knowing that the hotels were expensive and there are alot of bad places in NY, I decided to do some research. Based on my research, I found Herald Square to be the best deal and reviews. In addition to the great reviews, the other hotel guest left some great tips in which we used during our stay. (i.e. where to eat-Speedys, and hotel only takes money for the lockers and for the super shuttle. There is also a real good restaurant northeast of Speedys. I forget the name of the restaurant, but we went there for drinks one night and had breakfast there the next morning.) So, if you have time to read through all of the reviews, do so, to get more tips. It was VERY helpful. 
Although the hotel received good reviews, I was still a little hesistant. But I was VERY HAPPPY with our stay at Herald Square. It was safe, clean and the staff was very friendly. I would stay here again. 
Room: we received an upgrade to our room. It was expecting something small, but it was nice to have something just a bit bigger.

I am so glad I booked here. Unfortunately Hurricane Sandy arrived on the second day of my trip. I knew it was coming and flew in anyway as my appointments were quite urgent. While most of my appointments were cancelled since the storm surge was worse than even the weather forecasters expected - knocking out power in lower Manhattan - the DoubleTree Suites has a backup generator (I checked) and given their location, they didn't need it. They never lost regular power (thank goodness!). Yet with the mass transit knocked out they were operating on a very thin staff. They housed some of their staff at the hotel. And they were mobbed with people from lower Manhattan trying to find housing. So while they were at max occupancy and minimal staff they did an outstanding job. What more do you need to know about a hotel's quality of staff? Under tremendous stress they were gracious and effective. Housekeeping and room service - restaurant services were curtailed for two days. Yet they called my room to see what I needed. They brought me the few supplies I needed replenished and took out my garbage. Housekeeping and full services were restored amazingly quickly given the devastation of the storm and the tremendous difficulty for the staff to find a way back into work. You can read other reviews about how great the location is (it is) and how great the suites are (they are), but what really showed their quality was how they handled the storm. I loved the suite. Comfy - and the fridge and microwave came in quite handy. I bought supplies from a couple of delicatesans nearby that never closed. I ate in my room several times to take stress off the hotel. They have won a very loyal customer out of me! Way to go, DoubleTree Suites, Times Square! Thanks for your care and your competence. You were OUTSTANDING.

I tried to order room-service breakfast one morning, but gave up after (twice) letting the phone ring for ----- rings and receiving no reply. The concierge desk wasn't helpful or knowledgeable about restaurants or bus routes.
These things didn't add up to an awful or disastrous stay, just an unsatisfactory one. If this had been a budget hotel, some of the shortcomings would be more acceptable. When I'm next in Seattle on business, I'll definitely stay elsewhere.

The price was steep, I'll give it that, but not nearly as steep as the competition, and for the market, it was actually quite a bargain.

On a positive note, several of the staff members were very friendly and professional. And the location is excellent. 
Overall, I strongly recommend that you avoid this hotel.

We had closed down the wedding reception and had gathered in a few groups, in rooms and by the pool, as we had done on the two previous evenings without issue. Obviously a new night security guard was in place this evening and recognizing the possibility of a noisy gathering he took interest. I fully understand his job and the responsibilities he has to the facility and its guests, however he needs training in the art of tact and diplomacy. Fortunately a compromise was reached; we were given an area to continue our conversations and celebrations and even assisted with some of the amenities, the evening continued without incident.

First thing to mention is that I did not pick this hotel directly, but rather got it through priceline, so our rate was very good. The Hotel is so conveniently located within Grand Central Terminal that if you arrive by train, you never have to even step one foot outside before reaching your hotel room. You can also get to almost anywhere else in the city from there. We took the train from Stamford (just -- minutes to Grand Central) and within - minutes of arriving at Grand Central Terminal we were checking into our hotel. The line wasn't too long, about a - minute wait. There are many electronic check in kiosks, but we opted to check in directly since we prefer a more personable check in, and to make sure that we are happy with the room they selected. The front desk was very pleasant and found us a very nice room on a high floor with a King bed. Views in this hotel are very limited since tall buildings surround it on all sides, but we were able to get a decent view of the Met LIfe Building. As some other reviewers mentioned, you can hear some hallway noises, conversations, and televisions from the neighboring rooms from time to time. It was not unbearable, but perhaps it is worse when the hotel is at full occupancy. Hard to know. Some better soundproofing would be nice, but this is fairly common in large hotels.
One noticeable plus was the over sized walk in closet. Not sure if this is standard or if we just lucked out, but we had a walk in closet that was almost twice the size of the bathroom. They had an ironing board in there, which is also a huge plus. You need to pull it out to iron, since there are no outlets in the closet, but it wasn't an issue. 
The bathroom is a bit on the small side, but perfectly fine. It was very clean with marble and granite and very nice Portico bath products and a hairdryer. The shower pressure was decent, with a large Speakman shower head. The towels were a bit rough, likely from countless washes, but fine. Some reviewers mentioned that there was no toothpaste offered, but from my experience at many hotels, toothpaste is almost never offered unless requested. I'm sure if we needed it they would send some up, or you could easily go down to the hundreds of shops in Grand Central Terminal and pick up any supplies you need. 
There is a convenient ice machine and vending machine on the floor just down the hall from the elevators. There is no mini-bar in the room, but this ended up saving us a lot of money in the end. There are plenty of delis and stores all around the area, so you can get outside food and drinks easily. We did not order room service or eat in any of the hotel restaurants.
The fitness center is better than most NYC hotels, with plenty of Life Fitness brand machines and towels, water, and full cable television programming on the ellipticals, treadmills, etc. At first I was sorry I didn't bring my own headphones, but soon I realized that they supply you with free headphones near the towels. The only downside was on our second day when there was some error with the red emergency phones within the Gym. The Police came back a couple times during my workout, creating a distraction and speaking in a very loud and accusatory tone warning us all not to touch the red phones or they would shut down the fitness center. It was very uncomfortable. I was close to finishing my workout so I decided to cut it short. I have no idea how it ended. Either way, I felt the Hotel security could have handled this situation much better by putting a security guard there after the first incident or having better surveillance cameras. I'm sure there was a technical problem with the phones, which should have been their first consideration before assuming it was a prank or somehow intentional. On the bright side, if there ever is an emergency there, at least you can be assured that the authorities will arrive within seconds.
The cleaning staff was very efficient and left our room spotless every day.
We had a small problem with our in-room security safe. The safe was already closed and locked beforehand, so we could not use it. We called the front desk and they sent a security agent over (within minutes) but they could not fix it since they needed special equipment to drill it open. They apologized for the inconvenience. It was fine, since the Hotel is very secure anyway.
Overall, it is a very nice hotel and we slept very comforatably each night, which is the most important aspect of any hotel. The beds were very stylish and comfortable. The rooms were spacious for NYC standards.
Because it is such a large hotel, I realize it is often hard to get personable service, yet we had many positive experiences with the tour desk, cleaning staff, and other hotel representatives. It did take a bit long to get the front desk to answer the phone, but it varied depending on the time of day and how busy they were at the time. At one point we were on hold for over - minutes and I just gave up but on another day they answered it right away.
The most important thing to remember is that if you smile and are pleasant and nice to people, they will usually smile and be nice back. You can help make your own experience better by having a positive attitude. If you are uptight and demanding to anyone then you are unlikely to be treated well and will be unhappy with service anywhere. Contrary to several reviews on this site, no one within the hotel staff was ever rude to us during our stay. Everyone was very pleasant.
If you can book this hotel at a discounted rate, it is an excellent choice. On the other hand, if you have money to burn and want complete pampering and perfect service, then I would suggest a higher end hotel.

We stayed at the Park Plaza for a week due to my husband attending a convention. My DD (-) and I played tourist for the week and found the location of the hotel to be perfect for what we wanted to see. There is a T station half a block away and for a $-- --day ticket the two of us travelled everywhere. Note under --s are free on the T! The room was adequate for us. Two comfy double beds and two bathrooms made it simple. The bathrooms are small and the showers even smaller, but we managed. We had two minor issues while we were there and both were attended to incredibly promptly by housekeeping-maintenance. I highly recommend the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""City Pass"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to save you money getting into some major attractions. It also allowed us to skip the line for tickets. Boston is a great place to visit with so much to see and do. I highly recommend the Park Plaza as a place to stay. Parking isn't cheap though, valet parking was $-- per night! I thought that a bit outrageous just to park my car and not move it for a week.

We stayed at this hotel last weekend while visiting PB and the area. The location is ideal as we were steps from the boardwalk and ocean. There is also an amazing restaurant located in front of the hotel. The room we stayed in was comfortable and although there was not any air conditioning, the room was a perfect temperature when the balcony door was open. The bathroom was on the smaller side. We did not find the area to be loud when sleeping. The only noises we heard was the ocean, and on occasion, the elevator. One issue was with parking. We were able to secure a spot, however, it was difficult to park in the evening as the spots are very tight, but we were able to manage.

Stayed here and was in a beautiful suite as shown in the pictures....although it is a great hotel though I don't think the location is the best if you want to explore New York, it might have amazing views over Central Park but I feel you are in the tourist section nearer times square, and when I stayed mid-town I felt this was much better for walking around NY and exploring.....
very clean and great hotel....however did spot a cockroach in the reception one day!!!
good food though, delicious breakfast....think as there is such a range of hotels in NY I probably wouldn't stay again unless it was at a great value as the suite was very spacious which is rare in New York.

Checking in reminded us of being in as busy airport. So back down and changed rooms which was achived very quickly biut now no upgrade but still got a good view and now a quiet location.
Breakfast was outstanding even by Hilton standards and very friendly and efficient staff.

Car parking very expensive so we ended our rental early and walked and took taxis and saved a bundle Would we go back?-yes for the breakfast -probably the best hotel breakfast we ever had-yes for location but probably a NO for the sheer size and feeling of impersonal servcice that comes with being so big

When visiting Universal Studios this is the right place to stay. The hotel is the usual good Hilton standard (the seafood buffet in the restaurant is five star with crab legs, oysters, sushi, sashimi, lobster, carvery and crepe stations etc.). It is clean, modern and a bit boring to look at but the location is a blast. Our room was on a low floor (actually under lobby level) and handicap friendly. we had the view of the hotel's outdoor pool but the high rooms have probably got more interesting views. Parking was not too expensive for Los Angeles and the staff was helpful. Tickets to the Universal Studios are sold at the hotel and from there it is a five minute walk to get to the park. I do not like when wifi is not included (you don't pay extra for aircondition or tap water, do you?) but it was at least not too expensive.

We stayed here for a week as a family of - and we really like the location.
Must say this time there was a different guy on reception (haven't seen him on past visits) when we checked in who was ok but I didn't really warm to him - but the valet guy was fabulous and totally made up for the check in.
Being just a couple of blocks from Westfield Mall is a huge plus - so many places to eat, and a Ralph's right across the street is a bonus too.
Valet parking does add up after a week but that's LA for you - just the way it goes - all the guys are great so you don't feel like you're getting ripped off or anything.
The rooms are clean and neat - it's nothing fancy, but its decent - having a microwave and fridge when you're travelling as a family is always appreciated, as is the included breakfast.
The young lady on reception when we checked out was friendly and efficient - and we will be back!

Fitness center machines not working and water dispenser had no water all weekend. Asked for crib and no one ever called us back. Asked for advice on things to do and told to google it. My boyfriend and I stayed in the Chancellor Hotel from -st - -th September inclusive. The hotel is in a fantastic location and has a fantastic service! All the staff were very friendly and helpful. Everything about this hotel was excellent. I would gladly recommend this hotel to any customer, whether young or old!!! The hotel was very nice, we had a room on floor six which had a mini kitchenette - we found this handy for keeping drinks cold. The bathroom was clean and again absolutely no complaints there. Try and do your homework where parking is concerned as it can be very expensive.
We were in walking distance to all main areas in San Fran and would recommend this hotel.

The location was perfect for us. Close enough to the main section of the Riverwalk but just far enough away to escape and have some peace and quiet time. Beautiful historic building. We enjoyed both pools, loved all of the views! The room was very nice and clean, super comfy bed. Valet was excellent.

I have to say, up front, that I am picky. It amazes me that hotels that claim to cater to business travelers regularly manage to botch the basics, thought they are often quick to remedy problems. The Omni Fort Worth was a refreshing change of pace, in that absolutely everything worked as advertised. I used online checkin and let the hotel know that I'd be there at -- am. I knew I was ridiculously early, and was prepared to check my bags on arrival and to go away for a few hours. My room was ready when I got there at --:-- am; I had only to stop at the rack by the front desk and pick up my key. I was even more surprised that my room preferences - high floor, away from the elevator, were all met. My corner room was spacious and well laid-out - more square than rectangular, with plenty of room to move around, and with large, floor to ceiling windows. The interior design was very tasteful, but with a distinctively Western tone. Every morning, a tray with a small pot of coffee, a glass of fresh-squeezed orange juice, and several newspapers was delivered to my room (complimentary for Omni Select Guest members). Even though the hotel appeared to be full, my room was always made up before - pm each day. I never cared much for turn-down service, but it was sooo nice to return to my room each evening after dinner to find my bed turned down, the room softly lit, and soothing music playing. Every staff person I encountered was genuinely friendly, competent, and knowledgeable. The public spaces were were comfortable places to wait, and it was possible to carry on a conversation in a normal tone of voice even though it was quite busy most of the time. I was there on business, so the hotel was perfect for that, but otherwise it was kind of disconnected from everything except the Convention Center (just across the street) and Sundance Square. Except for a balky ironing board, my stay was perfect. i was there for four days, and was sorry to have to leave- it was just so comfortable and easy to be there.

I have been travelling on business for more than ten years and this has been one of the most memorable experiences I have had. The staff really know how to make you feel like you are a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""guest"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in their hotel. In particular, Boris and Rita are the consummate professionals. Their people skills and customer service skills exceeded my expectations. I also loved the amenities in the room. No cheapie toiletries here.
What would have made my stay even more amazing would be to have a magnifying makeup mirror in the bathroom, disposable cups and glasses (feels more sanitary) and bottled water in the room.
However no gadget or gizmo can replace service excellence and I certainly experienced service excellence at this hotel.

Since UT System is a client I visit the medical district often and I really like the location and layout of the rooms. Big suites and the ones that have been refurbished are even better. It's like a home away from home. While I never need the --- bath at the entryway it's nice to have if there are meetings in the living room.
I've only eaten once for breakfast in the hotel and it wasn't good at all so I've avoided it for all future trips. I'm not sure it's fair to judge a restaurant on one experience but I've stayed away since then.
I typically will walk to Main Street or Fannin and grab dinner or coffee. 
I (and co-workers) continue to visit and plan to as long as rooms are available.

My wife and I stayed at the Tapatio Cliffs Hilton the last week of August, and had a really great experience. We arrived on a Thursday night, and were immediately impressed with how friendly everyone was. We checked in quickly (HHonors), and were driven up the hill to our room. When the sun came up the next day, we realized we had been driven about --- yards, so it's definitely walkable without luggage. We had a very nice two room suite next to the presidential pool; clean and well cared for
This hotel has a lot of choices for entertainment with - pools, and we spent a lot of our time at the pool all by ourselves. It was really, really relaxing. The fitness center is nice and does have a fairly decent selection of free weights. We hiked every morning from the hotel and there are a couple of different trails to choose from, although they're not extremely isolated (you're in metro Phoenix, so we expected as much). Going left under the highway led to better trails. 
We only ate dinner at the hotel one night; at the Casades (since it's casual). They have Mexican food. It was ok, but we had a great Tex Mex meal - minutes away Sierra Bonita restaurant. The bellman recommended it, and it was a really good choice.

If you're in San Antonio to party, this is probably a great, chic hotel. If I was there staying out until -am every night, the noise really wouldn't have been an issue.
However, I was there on a business trip and needed to get some sleep so I could be functioning at -am. This LOOKS like a business hotel, but it is not. If you stay at a Westin or a W, you'll hear nothing from outside or inside the hotel. 
At the Valencia you can hear ALL the street noise, clubs, street sweepers, whatever.
You also get treated to all the conversations, bathroom noise, and whatever else the folks in the room next to you are doing.
The staff is great, the decor is chic, but for business (or if you just value your sleep) avoid this hotel. Which is a shame, because it's a nice hotel. If they just put some attention into sound proofing it'd be world class.
If a hip hotel can be sound proofed in New York, it can be done in San Antonio. I can't recommend a hotel that isn't willing to all the necessary steps to ensure guest comfort.

The rooms were beautiful and inviting. The pyramid restaraunt service was superb. Yet, the restaurant services were extremely slow in the bar area. When my party received our food, it wasn't hot. I also received food that was over cooked from room service. 
However, Mr. Tony Bennett treated my team members and I with a consistent warm greetings and always extended a helping hand with travel services or luggage.
I especilay loved that Fairmont Dalltheory provided room keys with the company's name that I am affiliated with on them. Furthermore, pink lemonade and cookies awaited our arrival each time my co workers and I entered the hotel. With that said I would definitely stay at the Fairmont again.

My wife and I stayed two nights at this nicely decorated and conviently located hotel in October of this year. While eating the tastey breakfast provided each AM in the lavishly furnished and decorated dining hall, the owner of the hotel stopped and talked with us. She asked how we liked the hotel and if we had any concerns. We were completely pleased with the hotel and told her such. She proceeded to tell us about all the exciting activities offered in San Antonio. She is a real ambassador for the city. She also said that she personally had done the decortating of the hotel. she has done a terrific job.The hotel is only three or four blocks from the Alamo and Riverwalk. We walked to both and had a great time. Thanks Sherry for the boat tickets. We really enjoyed the ride. Hope to go back for the Thanksgiving dinner.
The Bells

We stayed here whilst it was beeing refurbished so were a bit apprehensive. We needn't have been. We entered the reception area and were surprised to find rennovations were almost complete, and was now looking extremely
grand and luxurious. The clerk was most helpful giving us all our special requests and upgraded us free to a suite. The lifts were plentiful and quick.
Our room was extremely clean, the linen white and expensive, and the en-suite
was new and obviously recently remodeled. The only down side was no view but being in New York for the first time didn't matter as we were out all the time. This hotel is also directly opposite penn st station so no need for a taxi, just walk across the road. We have told all our friends not to stay anywhere else and cant wait to return.

We picked this Hotel because the had an indoor pool (pool open ----pm) and pets are allowed ($---.-- refundabl deposit). This hotel was not to far from Time Square, and Radio City. No Cooffee pot or alrm clock in the room, if you didnt have a watch you would be in a jam. Nintendo listed as a accommodation but there was a $-.-- charge for one game (per --min) did think that was fair. Also no Continental Breakfast - but there was a Restaurant in the Hotel. Great for familys, not to pricy for having a pool in a hotel in the CITY. Would stay there again.

I just came back from a weekend stay with my husband. Yes, the hotel is not the Four Seasons. But you are not paying Four Seasons prices. The location is priceless, and if you book through their website, you can get their wonderful breakfast buffet included ($-- value for - people-just book their luxury escape rate), and a chance to ask in writing the type of room you want. Join their Gold Ambassador's club and you will receive even more perks (Free upgrade, Free night stay coupon, snacks in your room, etc.) We did that while we stayed at the Intercontinental Cozumel and got upgraded to a beach front suite! 
Chicago is a great city, and the view from our --st floor room in the historic tower was amazing. Ask for that room when booking, and you won't be disappointed.

I will keep this review short and sweet. My husband and I stayed at The Inn at the Market - night before we were getting on a cruise to Alaska. Like other reviews have stated, from the moment you pull up to the valet there is someone there to assist, greet, and make you feel 'that special something' that only a certain level of customer service can provide. ALL of the staff went above and beyond for us. It happened to be my birthday and we were upgraded to the - story condo.....and there was cupcakes waiting for us...incredible!! The roof-top deck is SO beautiful!! I highly recommend you bring a nice glass of wine, and that special someone up there with you to see the sunset.....again incredible. The beds were great, the view amazing and the overall feel of the Inn is very special. Thank you to everyone at The Inn at the Market for making our stay so wonderful.
Autumn and Lenny

We stayed in a luxury king, purchased through Jetsetter for a long weekend to celebrate my husbands birthday. We had plans to shop and eat, as we visit New York about twice a year. In that area, I have stayed at The Millenium, Intercontinental, Premier, Westin. I rate this hotel higher. My feeling is that guest services are in the details. Free coffee and tea in the mornings, an excellent gym (for a hotel in the city), immaculate rooms and water at turndown. The service was attentive by New York standard, but really friendly by any standards. It was a nice change to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""fend for yourself"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" attitude. To me, although it isn't the best location as midtown can be a real circus, there is no better place to set as home bas to explore. We go all over, from the Village to Harlem, and the subway lines are all easily accessible from the Sofitel.
Eric checked us in, and after confirming a special surprise I wanted to be delivered for my husband, the hotel sent him something sweet too, which was lovely. Eric remembered our newspaper preferences, and after watching me rummage through the stack, arranged to have the ny Times delivered to our room. We had excellent martinis with a friend at the Gaby bar, and had room service once after feeling peckish after a show. Food was hot, came quickly and correctly. You do need to ask for a sheet if you get warm at night. The linens are fine but they have a covered duvet, not a separate sheet. The bathroom and room itself was pretty big for New York, and the bathroom had good lighting for sprucing up. 
All in all, a hit for us. I have an annual conference in NYC, and think I may blow the conference hotel and stay here!

This is a beautiful, well-kept historic hotel, that will please just about anyone, but those desiring ultra-modern decor and design. We were upgraded (for a $--.per night rate) to a huge corner suite with two over-sized twin beds, overlooking the lake (a huge lake view!). The room was really tastefully decorated and it looked as though it had been renovated recently. The high tea in the Palm Court was excellent, as was the breakfast room service. It is a pleasure to just walk around the hotel, as all the common areas are gorgeous. Service is excellent--concierges especially helpful. Celebs and royalty have stayed here and I have to say that we felt almost famous. Michigan Avenue location is great--walking distance to the city's main attractions. Only negative was that the maids used a strong chemical product of some sort which bothered us one night, and so we had to request no more sprays.

We have stayed at the Coast Gateway Seattle well over - dozen times since ---- and have yet to be disappointed.
We have found the staff to be friendly, accommodating and most helpful with special requests. With - children we must book - rooms to accommodate all the bodies and often stay on both ends of our flights (or Mariner games) just to get in a few extra moments of pampering. We cannot say enough about the kindness shown the children and ourselves. The desk staff are quick at check-in-out and room service from the Sharps Roaster Ale House next door is always prompt.
The beds are comfortable and the airport """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""noise"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is practically non-existent. While the bathrooms themselves are on the small side, it functions for the intended purpose. The rooms are spacious, and when staying on the airport side the upper floors offer terrific views of the airport and hours of viewing pleasure if you like to people watch. The bathroom amenities are generous and the bath linens are satisfactory.
The morning complimentary breakfast offers fresh made waffles w- your choice of toppings, yogurt, various breads & bagels, hard-boiled eggs, oatmeal, coffee, tea, a variety of juice options, milk, hot chocolate, apple cider and three choices of cereal. We always walk away more than satisfied and the children look forward to breakfast before flying out.
The business center is well supplied and complimentary. Access is controlled by the front desk so there are no children in the way when you need to print tickets or check email. Computers are up to date.
Although a pool- spa would be a nice addition, they offer a small fitness room that has limited equipment that is adequate to get a decent workout.
The property offers airport shuttle service and while we have never waited more than -- minutes to get the shuttle, we have begun to walk to and from the airport just to stretch our legs a little more. The airport doors are only a - minute walk away so the location is excellent for a little pre-flight fresh air.
The Park and Fly lot is located at Masterpark Lot C, about -mile north from the property. While it is a little bit of a hassle, the security and service of Masterpark is excellent and well worth the extra time and energy.
We will continue to use the Coast Gateway as our primary Seattle area hotel. While we have on occasion stayed at other properties in Seattle, The Coast Gateway is the our preferred option and we have recommended this property to dozens of our family and friends and no one has been disappointed with many returning anytime they travel.

Ok location (if you have a car) Not that much within walking distance around the hotel. Rooms were nice with a good bed, but without any of the things you would normally expect to find in a regular hotel room. No fridge (or icebucket), no hairdryer etc. I would not recommend it for couples on vacation, but for short business trips.

I spent one night in August at the Oxford Hotel in downtown Denver, CO and I wished I'd had several more there. The place is beautifully historic but the rooms are beautifully updated so there is none of the mustiness you might expect in an old hotel. The bathrooms especially were nice. The hotel also had a nice attached restaurant and is in a lovely part of Denver, just a block from my favorite destination, The Tattered Cover bookshop.

Pros - good price, clean room, comfortable bed, friendly staff 
Cons- smells like a casino hotel, needs more towels, lobby and hallways can be updated, food for dinner was mediocre
(I'm probably being over critical )

We just returned from a - night stay at the Tuscan Inn. Upon arrival we were greeted immediately and got checked in within - minutes.
I'm not sure why so many people say the rooms are small here, but our standard king size bed room was huge in my opinion. We were at the end of a hall with a small courtyard view. 
This room was a nite respite from all the noise of the city and a a great quiet getaway at night.
We were extremely pleased with the cleanliness of the room. It doesn't get cleaner.
The bed was extremely comfortable and the amenities were excellent. They provide you with great aveda products in the bathroom. Free Wifi in your room, and the free wine reception in the evenings was great.
All the staff was friendly, though I found the maintanence and housekeeping staff to be the warmest in the building.
I did not take advantage of the concierge service, but I saw many people were receiving great service from them.
We would defenitely stay here again.
Great value and service for the price!

I stayed at the Allerton during the Taste of Chicago for the -th of July weekend ----.
We must have gotten the smallest single ever made. As soon as we stepped into out hotel room, we were in the bathroom. I had seen my friend's single and it was decent. I booked the room on the hotel's website for about $--- a night and I was not satisfied.
I did not try the hotel's restaurant or bar. There is no pool. The good thing about the hotel was that it was located in the middle of the magnificent mile.
The next time I visit Chicago, I will not be at the Allerton.

My friend and I stayed at this location on Monday night, May -, ----. As we were leaving to check-out we received a phone call from the room phone from the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""manager"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" frantically informing us to stay inside of our room and that there was a man outside claiming we stole his wallet. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""manager"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" proceeded to throughly frighten my friend and myself by telling us that if we didn't either return the wallet or knock on the door and tell this """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""man"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that we didn't have it, the man would come into our room, rape and kill us. Needless to say, we were panicked and scared for our lives. We hadn't spoken to anyone that night, let alone take anyone's wallet. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""manager"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was yelling that the man would kill us, repeatedly and asked if we could defend ourselves, the whole - yards. I wish I was merely making this up, as it was unbelievably traumatic. He informed that he had already called the cops, but my roommate decided to call herself, as the man on the line, though he had the same accent as the man I had spoke to at the front desk the night prior, I was unsure if it was him at all. He kept asking for us to beat on the door and ask the man to leave, but I refused as he'd just informed that the man had a gun. Why would I go to door? He then proceeded to tell that if we wouldn't comply he would give the man the key to our room so he could rape and kill us. I was beyond frightened, but a part of me was confounded as I didn't hear any commotion outside, yet I wanted to be safe rather than sorry and my friend and I hid in the bathroom speaking to the --- operator. The police arrived evacuated us to the front, yet to our surprise no one else was under the same distress. A team of officers checked the motel, but nothing or no one was found. And oddly the cops never officially took down our story, but merely offered that the hotel was known for a lot of prostitution and drug trafficking, and that perhaps the hotel was attempting to run a scam, but there wasn't more to be investigated. And strange enough, a manager wasn't offered to speak to us, or anything of the like. My friend and I were thoroughly afraid. And I felt little was done to alleviate the distress we went through. I'm assuming they didn't understand the severity of the call we received, but I would have hoped more could have done. Don't stay at this hotel. Really enjoyed our latest stay at the Grand Hyatt in Washington DC over Spring Break. The hotel is very nice, clean, service was also very welcoming. I loved the location the most. We did not eat in the hotel so can't offer any information as to the Cafe. We did however use the Starbucks in the hotel for coffee and the deli for breakfast once. I'd rate the La Quinta Denver Airport location at average to above average. We tried to book hotel rooms for overnight stays on the way to and from Mexico. Unfortunately, on the way to Mexico, our travel date was also the weekend of a major sporting event in Denver, so rooms were in short supply. La Quinta had availabilty and the rates were reasonable (booked on Expedia with AAA discount.) I booked based on the quality I've seen at our local La Quinta, and was not disappointed in the hotel in Denver.
The hotel room itself was very roomy, with a comfortable couch, coffee table, desk and chairs. The bed was also comfortable. The bathroom was very large, bright and clean. The room included a small refrigerator and microwave, plus coffee maker.
Service from reception staff the first night was strange. Arriving around -pm, we hoped to find a restaurant nearby that was open. The staff seemed irritated that we asked for recommendations on where to go. The hotel itself is located near a Bennigan's and Village Inn, as well as several other hotels. The hotel next door had a restaurant -- which was empty and closed by -pm. The pancake house was also empty. Bennigan's was doing good business, and the food was fine. There is a new Ruby Tuesdays restaurant being built behind the La Quinta, and the area is obviously still developing. Not much to do once you are in the hotel at night.
On check in the first night we asked about the free airport shuttle. They advised we did not need to sign up for a ride, however I'd strongly advise getting your name on the list. There were problems on the trip to the airport, with a lot of competition between air flight crews and people trying to get to the airport. The crew members felt they should have priority on spots on the bus. Everybody got there, but it was a cozy ride...
La Quinta offers a decent free breakfast bar with cereal, baked goods, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""made to order"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" omelets, juice, coffee, etc. They also put out cookies in the evening. 
We'd stay here again. It's not the tops, but a very good deal for the price.

I too had some trepedations after some of the reviews here, so we were very pleasantly surprised and relieved to have a different experience than some have had, so much so, not only do we recommend this hotel, but we would book to stay there again. I would like to let you know why.....
We arrived earlier than anticipated and bell hops were outside ready to help with luggage, but without any small bills to tip, we declined, no probs, we were not hassled. The entrance foyer and lounge was spotless and smelled so good! - over the weeks holiday we realised they must have had some kind of aroma pumped through the air con. The air con worked fine. Yes the staff were a bit frosty, but this isn't Disneyland, its a busy hotel, they were polite and professional, just didn't have wall to wall grins, but thats ok. 
The downside was the - pm check in, but we knew that in advance, and they have a secure area for luggage so fine, we went out! We booked two rooms with twin doubles for our family, we have two -- year old boys, and the rooms were spotlessly clean, fresh towels, modern, full air con and a safe. No probs. Beds made, bathrooms cleaned every day. The rooms were a good size and great TV channels too. The bathrooms were also a good size and stock contantly stocked up daily. 
Yes, the - lifts only have two working in each bank of -, and the strange thing is that the apology sign is screwed to the wall...a bit permanent we thought, but don't let this spoil your holiday. We took the stairs down and the lifts up, just you wait a bit longer sometimes. Not as long as the hour..oh yes...an hour, just to go down in the lift from the top of the Empire State! so the hotel we got used to, far less a wait I can tell you. 
We asked for a fan for our boys room and within -- minutes we had it. The drinks machine took my money and no coke, within -- minutes a drink was delivered to me to replace it. 
The hotel is in a brilliant spot, near to subway, cabs, central park, etc., but thank the lord a walking distance away from the noisy and smelly Times Square. 
Stay here and don't let slow lifts ruin your holiday. We had a fantastic time and would definately book this hotel again, it was good value for money. You want - star? book it and pay the price. Any problem we had or query was quickly answered and found the staff helpful. 
The security staff there are fantastic, all the staff very smart and professional. If you don't like your room, tell them and they will do everything to move you if they can, we know, we saw it happen. This is a good hotel. Their website does not do them justice, search the net and find other photos and reviews, its a big hotel, with a nice modern interior. Many we passed in NY made us glad we had booked at this hotel.
Enjoy, go bite the apple.

Stayed here over the Thanksgiving holiday. Rooms were very neat. Bathrooms were a little tight. But over all a good bang for the buck. Breakfast was the basic Continental breakfast but no complimentary dinner like in the Long Island Residence Inn. A little light on the staff throughout the facility and the basic pool and lounge area in the back. Again, a good bang for the buck!

We stayed here for a conference--the hotel was completely booked up and they seemed to be overwhelmed, even though you would expect they are used to this, as they are attached to the convention center. The room was fine, but a bit small, and could use some """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""freshening up"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (black marks on the shower curtain, bathroom ceiling starting to peel, room overly warm at night even with the thermostat turned down). They still don't have wireless Internet service at this hotel and you have to pay $-.-- per day for wired broadband (which was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""down"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for - of the - days we were here.) The room comes with a very short ethernet cable, so that you have to sit at the desk to use it. A note says that -- foot cables are available but when I called the front desk to request one, they were all out. The service at this hotel is not very gracious. When I finally called back after the time had elapsed, they sounded annoyed rather than apologetic and just said they couldn't help me because the hotel was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sold out"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and they were out of what I required. The pillow situation was really exasperating. The bed truly was very comfortable, but the pillows were awful. There were two sizes--huge square pillows and little tiny rectangle pillows--and all were very high and firm. Great for watching TV, but for me, impossible for sleeping. I need something flatter and squishier for sleeping. These felt like giant marshmellows that didn't """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""give"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" at all, and I slept horribly. When I called the next morning to request a standard sized, normal, flatter pillow, it was a huge hassle. First they said they didn't have any other pillows, then they admitted they were just out of them, then they said they would call me back in -- minutes and didn't do so. I had to have a long discussion with someone who told me that no one had ever complained about these pillows before, etc., etc., before finally two regular pillows were found and sent up. Why does everything have to be such a hassle? I am not a princess--even at cheap motels I have always been satisfied with the pillows, in the past. Another minor complaint--on our last day the housekeeper forgot to leave any bath towels at all (just hand towels), which we didn't discover until one of us emerged soaking wet from the shower and had to use a hand towel to dry off. I could go on with other minor complaints, but the only other thing I will say is that the pool is TINY, so if you expect to swim laps, don't bother trying.
