We stayed at the Hotel Kabuki last week- Its location is close to a lot of great restaurants in Japan town as well as the nearby Fillmore District. As another reviewer mentioned, We found the Hotel staff to be very helpfull, but the hotel itself to be a bit on the average side. The lobby and attached bar-restaurant are very nice (a great happy hour in the bar!), but we found the room and hallways to be tired. In the room for example, the rice paper privacy screens were falling apart in places, and the beds were not on the new side. While waiting for the elevators, we couldn't help but notice that the hallways and curtains were a bit on the dingy side.
San Francisco was very busy during our stay (US Open in town, lots of College graduations happening etc.) so the Hotel's rates were naturally higher then normal which didn't help things- We expected a lot more from the Hotel considering the price we paid....

W Chicago is a trendy, upscale refurb of a formerly discount-type hotel on Chicago's lakefront. 
Our stay was a big disappointment. Our non-smoking room was seriously smokey. The space was tiny. The room was noisy. We could even hear guests next door talking at normal conversational levels, as well as the elevators going up and down all night! The lighting and atmosphere in the hotel is creepy--even sort of tawdry. Of greatest concern was that everything just seemed dirty, worn and unkept. Parking is an outrageous $-- per night. This is a hotel trying so hard to be hip that it's forgotten the basics.
On the positive side, the staff was accomodating. The bed was nice, and the LCD TV was great. Room service food was quite good.
You can do much, much better at other downtown hotels, especially at these prices. We cannot recommend the W.

My husband and I styed at the Hilton Garden Inn downtown Washington DC for - nights, --th sept - -th Oct this year.. It is in a great location well within walking distance of a huge variety of attractions. The hotel was very well presented, clean and gave the impression of being a more expensive hotel than it actually is. The staff were all friendly, helpful and professional. Food was second to none, and a very reasonable price. Accommodation was lovely, clean and modern and a quiet air conditioning system!. The little touches such as the shampoo, conditioner, soaps were lovely, with the towels appearing to be of a higher quality than other hotels, very soft and fluffy. Nothing was too much trouble for the staff, who were extremely polite and helpful. A little gem in the centre of downtown, which competes extremely well with the bigger more expensive hotels in the area. We would highly recommend a stay here, we enjoyed it so much we are going back.

We stayed at the Hotel Metro for - nights in May ----.
When we arrived our room was not quite ready so they stored our luggage and advised us that tea and coffee was free ---- and to help ourselves. Always a bonus after a long day site seeing.
Once our room was ready we went to unpack and as it was my husbands birthday there was a welcome note, some chocolates and bottled water for him - a nice touch. The room was a good size and the bed was comfy.
We were on the --th floor at the front of the hotel and the road noise was quite load but apart from this no complaints.

I would definately recommend this hotel - Enjoy your stay!

Three of us (my husband, myself and our daughter) stayed at this hotel for - nights while at a dance competition at the Pike Performing Arts Center. The hotel rooms were spacious & included a kitchenette (full fridge, microwave, stove, counter area for eating). The beds were comfortable (although the queen-size is not a standard queen), heating-AC worked well. Bathroom was clean. Note they do not clean rooms daily unless you specifically ask for it. (That was fine for us since we weren't in the room one full day!) Staff will provide you w-extra towels upon request. (We requested extras w-o any issue at all.) The pool area was also clean & staff replaced towels often. The location was easy to get to-from the Pike Center. Parking & internet were complimentary. Staff were friendly & helpful. My husband inadvertently left a fairly expensive pair of headphones behind in our room & the staff called us at home the same day we left to report it & mailed them back to us immediately. (Thank you!). The ONLY thing that bothered me a little was that even though we were on a non-smoking floor the hallways had a smokey odor. The room thankfully did not. I would definitely stay again if in the area.

I conducted an extensive search to find the best hotel that would offer a government-military rate for a conference we were attending in the Baltimore area. This hotel was very convenient to Inner Harbor shops and night life, provided suites with kitchen type facilities and I found that they don't put their gov-mil discount customers in less desirable rooms. A government employee or military member could wind up with any suite in the place for the current government rate (it's better to call ahead and request the type suite-view you prefer). Another person in our party had already booked a -- person group into a Hilton Garden Inn but we decided to give the Tremont Plaza a try instead. I was in suite ---- located on the northeast corner of the --th floor and I must say that the view was fantastic, especially out my bedroom window and the suite was HUGE! After our stay everyone who stayed there OVERWHELMINGLY APPROVED and would go back to stay there again in a heartbeat! One thing I read about the hotel that wasn't true: Two different reports that --th and above floors are """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""concierge"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" floors and include complimentary breakfast and cocktails turned out to be false, I asked about that and no one knew what I was talking about. All of the staff we spoke with was very knowledgeable concerning restaurants, night life and other things to do in Baltimore. Myself and one other person in the conference arrived too early on a Sunday to check in but Donna at the front desk had us fill out the paperwork so that when we came back from lunch we could just get our key from the desk. She even arranged to keep our bags and have the valet park the car so we could go get a bite and catch some football. The biggest disappointment was the hotel's restaurant. The food was reasonably good although it was fairly expensive and the breakfast menu was somewhat limited. Whenever I was there or observed it from the bar area they seemed under staffed. This wasn't such a big deal during our Dinner because there wasn't very many folks there that night. During breakfast there was only one sever for the entire restaurant (guessing about -- tables) and the hostess had to jump in and help out (everyone at our table tipped her rather than the server for her help) because our server just couldn't get to us. I also noticed that neither of the servers (dinner or breakfast) seemed to speak english very well. These shortcomings however were easily overcome by the myriad of restaurants within walking distance to the hotel. We also found out that no restaurant in Baltimore seems to be willing to separate the check. The hotel restaurant only requests that you let them know before you order if you would like separate checks. Overall a large group of veteran travelers were EXTREMELY pleased with our experience at the Tremont Plaza and we are all eagerly looking forward to our next trip to Baltimore so we can stay there again. A very special thanks to Gretchen (sales manager) for all her help getting us set up, did I mention that the staff there was fantastic?!?!?!?!.

We have often stayed at the Burnsley All Suite Hotel. Each time we stay, we comment that this is our favorite hotel in Denver, and why would we stay any place else. The views from the upper floors (especially those facing North) are amazing and we spend a great deal of time looking out the windows or on the patio trying to identify places that we normally experience at street level. Happy Hour in the lounge is great fun and the live music is superb (we favor the jazz). Dinner and brunch are real treats. In fact, there is so much to do at the Burnsley, we seldom leave the building until it is time to depart the city. If we DO go out, it is just a short hop to all the activities of the urban area. You can even get a ride to-from the hotel if you don't feel like driving yourself (think struggling with the traffic & parking at Coors Field or Sports Authority Field at Mile High). We love you, Burnsley, and we can't wait to come back """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""home.""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""

This is a great hotel for a business stay. Quick check in, ample and well-lit parking, nicely laid-out room with an empty fridge (Target is just across the way.) Bar with small takeout selection, including fruit, and lots of seating areas. -- hour fitness. Two TV's, sparkling bath, good lighting, nice teas and coffee -- in short, everthing one needs for a comfortable stay.

I experienced great service from the workers. The rooms were extremely clean and comfortable. I chose to get a room with the bathrooms outside of the room; I was a little weary about this, but the bathrooms were very clean and was actually a fun experience. It is a central location, in the center of all the shopping. Overall was a great experience, would definitely stay here again!

I would have to give a top rating to service in this hotel. Except for the gal that checked us in on our first night who said they had upgraded us and it was a smoking room. Are you kidding me??!!! Since when is it an upgrade from a requested non-smoking room to a smoking room?? They told us there were no non-smoking larger rooms available that night. We were then finally changed back to our original room, a deluxe queen non-smoking. Deluxe?? I would have hated to see the classic queen room. I had read the reviews on here before we left for our vacation and decided that after seeing the manager apologize so many times for the quality of the rooms that they must have paid better attention to them and corrected the problems. Wrong! Our first room was so musty it made you wheeze, and I don't have allergies. The furniture was bad- from the very badly stained fabric chair at the desk to the scratches and dents on all of the wood furniture. As in another review the little tray with the snacks and water you could purchase was very dusty, as were it's contents. We were on the -th floor towards back and the noise from street was barely heard. The second night I asked for another room, hopefully larger, as the deluxe room was very small. We did get another room, #---, a Regis Deluxe room, which was bigger and it had a sitting area with fireplace. I did have to pay an additional fee per night though. It was a lot cleaner. Like I said before the service here is outstanding! Too bad the rooms don't measure up to the service.
A lovely full service hotel with a cozy inn feeling. The rooms were nice sized and the service was excellent.

If you can't stay at the Ritz or Four Seasons, this is the next best thing. This hotel is new and the rooms are very nicely decorated. The bathrooms have separate showers and tubs. Everything is marble and you get nice french toiletries -Rogers & Gallet. It is close to Rittenhouse Square - nice restaurants and shopping.

We were able to get this hotel through hotwire for a good rate. I would never stay here at the standard booking price but that is just me. The location is great for the Children's Museam and Aquarium and someday if it ever reopens, the Boston Tea Party. Positives:

Negatives:

The primary reason for a hotel is sleep but the pillows are the type that once you put your head on them they go as flat as the sheets. Some love soft pillows. Its a negative for me.

I stay at airport hotels often. I live near LAX so the airport hotels near LAX are the ones I stay at frequently..
 The rooms here are your standard airport fare. 
I asked for drinking glasses - hours ago ( the room didnt have any ), well none yet. I guess ill just brush my teeth and rinse under the spigat.
The internet is weak and lame, even though I signed into the most expensive option. 
When I check in, I asked for a room on the Century Blvd side. There is a dog kennal in the back, as well as an airport runway. I was told by the front desk person the following :"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" you booked thru a third party, ( priceline, expedia, travelocity etc ). You get the whats left rooms, ie the dogs and planes. 
I never experienced this at the other LAX hotels. 
Daily Grill is good.....

From start to finish we had a great stay at this hotel! Even before we arrived, having emailed the hotel directly with questions - the staff responded straight away & were very helpful. 
Arriving from Australia & being too early to check in (but we could have if the room hadn't have had someone else staying in it the previous night), the staff were happy to hold our suitcases in a secure room while we went out & started exploring the Walk of Fame. 
The location is FANTASTIC - perfect for weary travellers who have spent their days out & about. So close to the subway (jump on it & travel - mins to Universal Studios), or straight through the mall across the road & you're at the historic & very fabulous El Capitan theatre. Ask at reception about their discounted tickets for Universal Studios - they saved us $-- per entry. 
While the suite is a little old - it was clean & very large & it's nice to have room to spread out. Having the free internet access was also a bonus. 
I WOULD HIGHLY RECOMMEND this hotel - it's great value for money & you'll love the location. Thanks again to the fabulous staff for being so helpful & friendly during our stay!!

We visited New York for a week in March and could not recommend this hotel highly enough. The room was spacious and very clean. It provided a comfortable place to relax after a long day walking around the city. 
The staff in the Morgan were extremely helpful. The concierge provided us with great advice on a number of occassions which was greatly appreciated. As well as this the doorman was always very polite and friendly to chat to. 
The complimentary breakfast was lovely, there is a great selection of cereals, fruit and pastries. Another nice touch is the 'living room' where we waited after checking out of our room. 
The location of the Morgan is perfect for sightseeing and shopping in NY. It is within walking distance of Bryant Park as well as the Empire State Building, Madison Square Garden and broadway. It was also very convenient as there are subway stations located nearby which we used several times to go downtown. 
Overall, the hotel met our needs perfectly and we will certainly return. I would wholeheartedly recommend the Morgan as it is great value for money.
Very quiet and clean - much nicer than other nearby hotels for the same or less money. No great views but otherwise no complaints. Free internet in lobby on wi-fi so bring a laptop!

We had a great stay the The Westin Copley Place. We were traveling with our - sons visiting colleges and loved the location of the Hotel. The staff was very friendly and accommodating. The rooms were very clean and nicely decorated. I usually hate hotel beds but this one, I wanted to stay in for awhile. Our rooms were upgraded without asking when we arrived and we had a gorgeous view of the River looking into Cambridge. I hesitated to give a rating of Excellent only b-c the lobby furniture while lovely looking needs to be refurbished. It is showing some age and high usage but is far from horrible.

Fab little hotel only -- min walk from union square! We had one of the renovated rooms as shown on their website, which was quirky but fab! It has the original hitchcock staircase still in use, and constantly plays the film Vertigo in the lobby haha! The staff were really friendly, and our experience couldnt be faulted, but on exploring the hotel further it was very obvious which floors had been renovated and which hadnt, and obviously cant comment on those rooms, but the floors did look a little shabby! 
If i ever return to san francisco i would definately stay here! If your ever at a loose end in the evening try the ghost walk from the queen ann hotel further up sutter st, it was a really enjoyable night even for us the most sceptical of people!

We checked in early Friday morning to a most accommodating front desk person. We were shown our room which was basically what we expected for the price. All seemed well until the second night when the toilet began to overflow. My boyfriend went down to the front desk to make them aware of the situation, but the front desk did not seem to care. He asked for another room and was told there was none available. He then asked for a plunger and was told """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I'm sorry, I can't leave the front desk to find you one."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" He didn't know what to do; how do you stay in a place with no washroom facilities and the night clerk was of absolutely no help and of really bad attitude. My boyfriend then went to another hotel down the street to ask if they had a plunger, but no they could not provide him with one. He asked if they knew where he could get one, they told him at the Duane Reade drug store in Times Square. So at -:-- a.m., because of the refusal on the part of the hotel staff to do anything, he walked over to Duane Reade to buy a plunger. We asked for a discount on the room but they only agreed to reimburse the $-.-- he had paid for the plunger, saying we had made the reservation through Hotel Conexions and that we would have to take it up with them.

Spent three nights on a girls' road trip. Wow. I am very very picky and this wonderful place certainly lives up to its reputation. The service was impeccable; best I have ever seen. The staff are great and go out of their way to make sure you feel like royalty. The location cannot be beat. We had a suite which is more like an apartment with a full kitchen. This is a keeper. Would absolutely stay here again. Room was spotless; furniture looked new. Really worth the money and I frequently don't say that.

It has been a poor decision when I chose to book this hotel for - nights’ stay during our vacation to Houston, TX. After checking in at the hotel we were provided keys of a room where we found tons of garbage, lots of empty liquor bottles on the table and floor, and foul smell. When we reported this at the reception, they provided us another room which was equally unimpressive. Then we were moved to another room (stating that this is the last room they have, all others are occupied) where we found very dirty and stain-marked carpet, beds with uncomfortable mattress, small kitchen with stove top, mini fridge and small microwave (and not full kitchen as Extended Stay Americas website suggested). There is a portable TV in the room and the wireless internet was horribly slow. The bed sheet and towels provided were totally worn out due to excessive use or poor laundry. The bath room had a shower; however, poor drainage and low elevation of the shower ensured that water would flow out and drain the entire area including the kitchen area located outside just the bathroom (sic!!). There is no housekeeping that we found during our entire stay. I would definitely not return or recommend this hotel to anyone!

I booked this hotel on a website in which I would not find out the name until after the purchase and was a bit horrified with the reviews when going in. I found my experience was slightly better than reported in some of the bad reviews. 
The location is nice if you are looking to stay in the main part of the city. There is a lot of access to shops and restaurants, all of the main tourist attractions, and a short ride to both the Wrigleyville and Wicker Park neighborhoods where all of the best nightlife is (but where few hotels are available). 
However, I am happy that I was out doing other things, and not spending time in the hotel, which was dirty and outdated. When we arrived, our room wasn't ready so we had to sit in the lobby. The chairs and rug were filthy, and many of the seats on the chairs were worn down and uncomfortable. 
When we arrived in our room, it was better than expected. No sign of bed bugs, and it was dirty from use over time, but no overt signs of previous inhabitants were seen. It was a bit small and there was little space to walk or get ready but given that it is an historic hotel in downtown Chicago this is something that could be overlooked. It would have been nice to have a floorlength mirror in the bedroom area (or any mirror at all), but again not a big deal, just something to know. The room was not unbearably hot and we did not need to use the a-c. The traffic noise below was also not an issue, especially given the proximity to Michigan Avenue.
A couple of big problems- one was that the toilet kept running, and on a few occasions we had to take the top off to make sure it was actually filling up. Second, the shower pressure was really really low to the point where it was difficult to rinse the shampoo out of our hair. 
We did not have a lot of interaction with the front desk staff, other than when we checked in. However, they did not seem overly friendly. There were two slow elevators for the entire building, but we did not have to wait a long time.

I selected this motel near Hollywood for several reasons: affordability, location, and the TA reviews.
Travelodge is a budget hotel chain that offers the basic necessities at a reasonable rate. With that in mind, realize that your expectations needed to be lowered. Yes, it would've been nice if the walls and windows had some sound proofing, my neighbors didn't snore, and the floors didn't creak. On my first of six nights, I awoke to a bunch of guys talking loudly in the parking lot at about - am. A call to the front desk did fix the problem.

Now on to the good. There's free wifi. The TV has many cable channels including all HBO channels. There's a pool that's clean. Free parking. A safe in the room. And a big plus for me was the LA Metro subway is only a block away. If walk past the Metro station (Vermont-Sunset) there's a very nice section of shops and restaurants. If your'e walking toward Wendy's you're going the wrong way. I felt pretty safe on the streets. Of course you'll find homeless people and other sorts wandering around, but it's a major city -- get used to it.
Bottom Line. In my travels around LA I've seen many hotels like this. Some better, and some much worse. I'd recommend this place for a short stay with the expectation that this won't be a night at the Hilton.
Good environment and service in genberal but very poor policy on communications. Internet charges applied besides the high rate and the most horrific telephone charges ($--.--minute for US calls!!).
Very nice full service hotel at a great location. Right next to the Powell street BART stop. The view was fantastic.

At check out I asked the lady at the information desk if she would book us a taxi to the airport. She did this and took a $-- deposit. We really liked New York and just wished that the hotels were cheaper. Certainly the most expensive city to stay in that I have visited.
This hotel is awesome. We enjoyed everything about it. Very comfortable accommodations. Very clean. Gotta love the bathroom TV. Nice touch. A+++++

A friend and I found this hotel through Trip Advisor and was was a great deal in comparison to other hotels in the area. We had a redeye flight and ended up checking in at about - in the morning. Great place for family's. Very clean and comfortable beds. Fully equipped kitchen with separate dining area, nice living room with a sofa and a chair. Breakfast was okey with healthy and not very healthy choices .

Very pleased with this hotel from the moment I arrived and they let me check in early (-- a.m.) to the day I departed. Three friends and I stayed at the Omni on August --, ---- when we flew to Chicago to go the Oprah Winfrey Show. Everyone wanted to stay in this hotel because Oprah's guests stay there. The beds are comfortable, and there is an iron and ironing board in the closet. You DO have to take two elevators, but that really isn't such a big deal. You have to enter the suite through a short hallway that seems to be wasted space, but there was virtually no noise ever in our suite. We did not try the restaurant or room service so can't vouch for the food. There are TONS of fabulous places to eat in Chicago (including a Starbucks right around the corner for breakfast), so I wouldn't have wanted to eat at the hotel anyway. We had a AAA rate of about $--- per night which I thought was a very good value for the large suite. I DEFINITELY would stay there again. We have been in Chicago many times before, and there just isn't a better location than the Omni!

Not only is the building and location superb but the people working in this hotel make it what it is, a great place to stay and visit WASHINGTON

A solid hotel with a good bar serving the best cappuccino I've had in ages. Friendly welcome. The room was clean, the bathroom spacious. The beds were comfortable - we both slept well. Stayed here - or more times. Always consistent W quality in rooms, staff, etc. Walk to everything in Boston. High energy as expected from W, but no complaints.

Staff are superficially friendly and when something goes wrong they are either unable to help of can't be bothered. After talking to some of the reception staff they are all training or at collage learning to play hotels.

The hotel is aiming at different client, the loud weekend crew people drunk shouting in the corridors late at night, I even heard a fight one night. And the business men-women that need something completely different. It cannot do both
The walls are very thin and you can hear what your neighbours are up to including flushing the loo
The good points are it's very very clean, the rooms are a descent size and it's in a good location. It could do a lot better. And to end on a positive note the guys that run the courtesy car and the cleaning staff are fantastic, shame the glamorous staff are as good.
would I stay there again not on business but if I had a new girlfriend and wanted to take her somewhere nice for a night. But for a long stint again no-way

My one year old daughter kept picking things up from the carpet that were from previous guests - like hair pins that I don't use and that would be easily picked up by a vacuum cleaner. The hotel is in need of major refurbishment (torn couches etc), the bed was extremely soft, and like I said, we found stuff on the floor from previous guests - though people without small children may not notice.

It's located very conveniently for all the major west side subway stops, a quick walk across the park to the east side or across the road from the bus to the east side. If it was clean, I would stay here again even with the rude staff.

The --year old spent one full-day and one half-day at the Nickelodeon Camp at the JW Marriott property and enjoyed his time there. My mother and I also enjoyed our mani-pedicure at the Spa salon.

I have travelled across the country twice with my yellow lab dog. A majority of the places have been chain hotels or motels but some have been mom and pop places as well. I have even had situations where I have checked into a hotel, told them I have a pet, and they SHRUG like it is no big deal (no waivers to sign, no charges, no specific rooms). I have never had an issue until this instance. 
So I checked the policy online (hotels and their website) on this place and there were no restrictions but just that they charge a reasonable rate for pets. He continued to mutter under his breath that we should have called ahead and that we should always call ahead. But his tone of voice was very rude and I didn’t appreciate him scolding me that every time I stay in a hotel, I should call ahead. Cool, well bring me to tears over this because I am tired, just drove - hours, and like the parents of Jesus you told me that there is no room at the inn. Umm, refund my money and let me get the heck out of here then because this was obviously an honest mistake and I was sick of saying “I’m sorry” to this guy. I had to call hotels.com, get my money refunded, have them call the owner to verify the fact that I was not allowed to check in and able to get a full refund. Then he did start saying to the man on the phone for hotels.com “make sure you book her a room somewhere else, I don’t want her to leave unless she has a room somewhere else or I will try and get her something here”. I appreciated that but it was a little too late. So then I called up La Quinta because I know they don’t care if you have pets (and don’t even charge you) and booked a room last minute. I would prefer to give my money to a mom and pop place but if I am going to be treated like that, then I will give my money to a corporate place. When I was leaving, the owner came out to my car and told me to leave him a good review. And then he complained about the reviews that people leave that are negative. Well, I am sorry but I wasn’t about to give you a positive review because of how you initially treated me and I didn’t even get to see the rooms. 
If you want people to call ahead for one of your limited numbers of pet friendly rooms, then say so on your website! Specify this on all of the websites that you use for booking like hotels, expedia, etc. That ONE line of information could have saved me a huge headache.

I am a native New Yorker who has only recently started re-visiting the city after having lived elsewhere for more than -- years. I've stayed at the Hanbee several times over the last year or so, as well as at least one other hotel in Manhattan.

Rooms at the Hanbee are well decorated, scrupulously maintained and seem larger than they are. The bathrooms are modern and large. Overall, the rooms are comfortable and more than just a place to catch a few hours of sleep and I rate their value as excellent.
 The Hanbee is, however, on the corner of two very busy streets in an area that's very busy as well, so it is not quiet. In fact, this is the only thing about the hotel on which I can't give it an excellent rating, and it's nothing that the hotel or its staff can do anything about. As other reviewers have pointed out, the higher floors are quieter (the highest I've been on is the fifth floor) and I would recommend a room on the street side (either Bowery or Grand) rather than the back of the hotel. Street noise doesn't ever bother me, and as I've only had street side rooms in the past, noise hasn't been an issue. But whatever was going in the back last time I stayed - in a room at the back of the hotel - was very sleep disruptive and impossible to either close out or drown out. As I said, though, this isn't the hotel's fault, so should be taken as a recommendation regarding room choice requests rather than as a criticism.
The Hanbee is extremely good value for the money, especially in the off season, and I highly recommend it to anyone staying in the city.

Stayed here with my parents on Fathers Day weekend. It's a lovely little hotel and got a ton for a great price. We had the Corporate Suite on the top floor, we had a big living room, fold out couch, dining room, kitchen, huge balcony, small bathroom, large walk in closet and a comfy king sized bed! It is extremely noisy at night. The hotel is smack in the middle of a police station and a hospital. So....loud sirens ALL night long. If you are a light sleeper, DO NOT stay here.
The service was o.k. There usually wasn't anyone ever at the front desk, so no use in asking directions or suggestions. Check in and Check out was a breeze, but if you have an issue or some problem that is when it gets tricky.

Great convenient and peaceful location for this hotel - right on the edge of Broadway, with everything just a short walk away - including a great family-run pizzeria-bar a couple of doors away, and a well-stocked deli on the corner. Anyone looking to stay somewhere in Pacific Beach, This is the hotel you want!

 Since we arrived just after lunch, our room was not quite ready. One of the managers walked us into the bar and offered us complimentary drinks while we waited.  Of all of the hotels we've stayed at in the United States and Europe, this ranks among the best.

Above average rooms with great views. Bathrooms need work but if you are going away on businsess this is my favorite hotel in the city so far. Everything you need is right around the corner and service is great.

This is a beautiful hotel, in a convenient location for conventions, with an easy walk to piers for touring after business is done. The staff was the friendliest I have encountered in a year. This is a pricey hotel, but it is San Francisco after all.

The room faced the park and lake, so it was nice to wake up to a view each morning. I did not eat at any of the hotel restaurants but did have room service. Service was prompt but what gets to me is the automatic --% service charge. I realise it's a standard at all the Marriott's I have stayed in but I don't have to like it.
The room was a good size but some things left me puzzled. I assumed it was a room kitted out for people with a disability-mobility issues (given the size of the bathroom and low hanging hooks and rails) but some things (like having a bathtub) did not make sense. 
I did not like the low hanging rail in my room as I could not hang anything long up. I also thought the light switches were a pain. The only thing not acceptable was the cleanliness of the towels. Everyday I was given new towels and without fail, there was always at least one in the pile that was stained. 
The hotel is within walking distance from a number of attractions and transport options. In honesty, I would probable stay at a more centrally located hotel on a future visit.

The personnel had multi identities. The waiter at dinner time was also a bell boy or a doorman during day time. The same as the manager or whatever he was. Actually it's what - Ben Franklins did for me through priceline.com. Stayed - nights here this past weekend. OK, so there were three good things and three bad things, and while I think the good wins out, let me cover the bad ones first. First, these rooms haven't been updated since the Reagan Administration. Second, the beds really do need to be replaced. Third, no wireless Internet in the rooms (this is an airport hotel supposed to be catering to *business* people?). Despite these shortcomings, overall I thought this was a GREAT place to stay. First, I always find the convenience of walking down a hall from the airport terminal and into the hotel lobby a plus, but the hotel is also right across the street from several car rental places (including mine, AVIS), making it very easy for me to get to my car the next morning. Second, I noticed upon walking in that the hotel restaurant was *jammed* and people seemed to be happy and enjoying their food. This made me feel a little more confident in calling for room service. The food was surprisingly good. Most hotels like this one tend to specialize in wildly overpriced and frankly underwhelming food ... this hotel broke both molds in that the food was less overpriced and the quality significantly exceeded my expectations. Third, the hotel swimming pool (and I've noticed this about airport hotels being better at this, the Hilton at O'Hare is another good example) is clearly not the standard, useless -- footer (fine for family play time but nothing else) but a nearly standard length lap pool, allowing business travelers who happen to be serious lap swimmers (that would be me) a VERY welcome break from the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""--+ laps to a mile"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" pools we so often get stuck with. I would REALLY appreciate their adding wireless Internet and replacing the mattresses, but I would definitely stay here again.

I am overall satisfied with this hotel, but for the price i expected a little bit more. would stay here again, but not for a stay-at-the-hotel vacation

PC's location is terrific, not just for Lincoln Center, Columbus Circle, and all the conveniences nearby like Barnes & Noble, the gym, Balducci's, etc. Also it's a block away from the - and - train and several Broadway bus lines, so you can get around town easily and inexpensively. What I liked the best about this place was the staff. The doormen, desk people, housekeeping and maintenance people, they all give top-notch service. They were unfailingly friendly and helpful. I felt very well taken care of at PC and I recommend it highly. My only caveat is that it's expensive. But you get what you pay for here.

Worst hotel experience ever . Filthy dirty hotel !!!! Loud noises all night. Would not even recommend to an enemy.

The room is lovely, very nicely decorated and the staff was friendly and helpful. My husband and I enjoyed the evening """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Happy Hour"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in the downstairs bar. We stayed at the Orlando late August ---- and were just delighted by the service, I have to say we travelled from LA by car to Vancouver and our last hotel on the way home was this wonderful spot and it was in our top - hotels of a very long trip. We stayed here from -rd---th November whilst visiting San Francisco for a holiday and were not disappointed. We booked late- the night before so got a great deal. We arrived with not having had the best start to the holiday as my partner had lost his wallet on the plane, and the staff could not have been more helpful. They were so friendly and polite, and our room was upgraded to a king room with a view straightaway. The room itself wasn't huge, but plenty big enough- with an unbelievably comfy king-size bed. The view was just amazing- from the --th floor we could see Union Square, the TransAmerica Pyramid, etc. The bathroom was very spacious, and the shower pressure was amazing- nearly knocked me off my feet! The only thing slightly disappointing was that internet access was charged for additionally- but that's a small point. We also had a large flatscreen TV, excellent climate control, and tea-coffee maker.
Went to the hotel bar once, and the waiter was extremely friendly, and drinks were not expensive. However, DON'T eat in the hotel. The food was VERY poor quality for what you paid. I ordered the sea bass and I could swear I was given cod instead - didn't look at all like sea bass and my partner's pizza seemed to have been microwaved and he could not finish it. The restaurant itself is a tiny room at the back of the hotel- much like a disused conference room, and freezing cold. I recommend skipping this and going to one of the nearby restaurants- there are hundreds to choose from all at the same or better prices!
The location of the hotel was excellent- literally seconds from the Muni Bart station, the cable car stop, the streetcar stop, and bus stops. Several resturants across the street from the hotel all reasonably priced and good food, or go to Union Sq - blocks away (--mins walk) for plenty more restaurants to choose from. Italian on the corner of Ellis St is very nice. You cannot go wrong with this location!
Transfer from the airport on BART is $-.-- one way, and takes around --minutes. Very convenient given the proximity of the hotel to the station, and much cheaper than a taxi. The streetcar stops less than a block away from the hotel, and goes all the way down to Fisherman's Wharf, Pier -- and the Ferry Building etc. Shopping nearby is excellent- less than a block away from Bloomingdales at the San Francisco shopping centre, and - blocks away from Union Sq with Macy's, Tiffanys etc...

Great location like all the other reviewers say. Surprisingly good service -- not always a given in NYC regardless of the price. The rooms are small and dated, but perfectly fine for business travelers, and you're unlikely to spend much time in them anyway.

One week stay in a studio which was plenty of room. Full kitchen provided opportunity to avoid eating out every meal. Bathroom was small but at least the sink area was separate making it much better. Comfortable bed and furniture. Nice pool area and lobby area. Breakfast varied from day to day but Texas shaped waffles always can be made. Did not enjoy the hot items on two of seven days but enough other items to make do. The most impressive thing was the responsiveness of the front desk when we checked in. We arrived early before check-in time and a room was available. However, it was in building -- which was quite a walk and my wife could not physically make the walk. We called the front desk and within ten minutes we had a new room assignment in building eleven almost next to the pool and lobby. Went to Kemah one night and it was a short drive. Passed the space center on the way. Mall, restaurants all nearby. McDonald's, Starbuck's and Perry's Steakhouse all walkable from the hotel.

The most amazing aspect of the JW Marriott is definitely the staff. They are so helpful and nice and seem to really care about you. I really can't stress that enough.
The lobby is very modern and is not even a year old. Free internet access is available in the lobby of the hotel but not in the rooms or the executive lounge. The elevators are *extremely* (no sarcasm here!) fast. This definitely helps with the crowding and people flow of the hotel.
The corridors of the hotel are nice. Now the rooms. The rooms were very inviting and extremely clean. The view from my room was absolutely breathtaking even on the river-park side. The bathrooms are great and stocked with plenty of towels. The anti-slam toilet seats and drawers are a nice touch. Safes are available in the room without a fee. The beds were great. The executive lounge is a great thing to invest in. It comes with breakfast, snacks around lunch, hors d'ouvres, and the best part, desserts. Coffee, milk, activia, sparkling water, regular water, and Pepsi products are available all day. (Not -- hours but most of the day.) Oh, and complimentary printing and internet usage are available. 
There is also a Starbucks in the hotel, along with Osteria Pronto and High Velocity. Also the hotel is connected to Circle Center Mall via SkyWalk and the Convention Center.
Yes, no negatives about this hotel. It was absoluutely great. I strongly reccommend staying here and investing in the executive lounge. You don't have to have a room with executive lounge access, you can simply buy a pass to the lounge for $---night-room.

The staff was courteous and helpful staff, and there were a number of extra touches to add to the stay. The contemporary styling provides a nice aesthetic. I stayed at the Hilton LAX with my wife and son for a few days before flying to Hawaii and again after returning before our flight back to the UK.
We had a rental car and used the valet service which we found to be efficient, our bags were unloaded and taken to our room by friendly staff. 
The lobby was very busy as you would expect of a airport hotel, but we got checked in quickly thanks to a dedicated HH desk. The checkin desk staff were fantastic and made us feel very welcome.
We had a top floor room which was a good size and very clean, although the decor is a bit dated. The beds are of the usual Hilton standard, very comfortable.
We used the executive level lounge for breakfast which was good and plentiful. It does get busy and can be difficult to find a seat. There is a good view of the airport from here also. 
There are some nice restaurants in the lobby and a nice bar area too which we took advantage of after tiring days touring the sights.
We had used room service late one evening and it arrived within the estimated time. Very nice and refreshing too.
There aren't any room safes but there is a secure area by the check in desk with saftey deposit boxes which are free to use.
Overall we had two pleasant stays at the Hilton LAX and would certainly stay here again.

During a recent stay, I spilled something on a shirt I needed that night. I asked for some detergent to get it out. I was so impressed, and I will continue to stay there whenever I am in Austin.

Hotel is due for refurbishment and the hotel management do apolgise for this in advance. however full price is charged nonetheless. ideally placed for exploring New York. minutes away from Central Park and Times Square. hotel was in good shape the beds were really soft and i had a good night sleep the breakfast was very good the staff was very good.....the bad was the tv sets flat screen lg picture quality was poor and had to turn up the volume to -- just to hear it. and the the bathroom was rather warm. with no air flow .ugly was the housekeeping staff. just a bad attitude.

I can't think of a better place to stay given the amenities and the price for a boutique hotel.

Dirty and dated. Noisy rooms.

I'm giving a review of - because the people are so nice, and the room was a good size, other than that.....

I made the mistake of asking the concierge a very routine question, but it just highlighted her lack of knowledge of anything outside her immediate realm of comfort and her reality. Our attempt to have breakfast one morning was met by FINALLY being acknowledged and being led to a long table for about -. There was just - of us. I gave the James an average, when it seemed so poor, on the merit of their location, the fact that I loved Chicago and that, with a sweep of a magic wand, if most of the present staff would just disappear and be replaced by competent professionals, this place has great potential.

I stayed at this Holiday Inn earlier this month for over a week and it was the worst experience. This hotel is horribly located, next to a blighted building in a dingy area very out of the way. I liked that the shared bathroom- shared toilet- bedroom all had nice bright lighting. 
The downside to the room is that there isn't any real place to hang your towels (but they are changed everyday) - this could be easily remedied by placing a couple of hooks on the room wall. The location to Union Square is excellent. There is a BART station nearby, making it easily accessible from the SFO airport. It is also about a --minute walk to the North Beach eateries - and the downhill is on the way back:) 
I would stay here again and save my money for shopping.

Stayed here for one night ( less than - hours) due to Delta cancel flight. 
The room is clean and spacious. The walkway can be confusing and abit dark but if stay just for a transit then no problem. 
Free shuttle every -- minute to LAX with a stop at Westin. Helpful staffs

otherwise I would have been extremely disappointed. Yes I used SPG points to stay, otherwise it would have been ---$ to stay at this overpriced hotel. The rooms are no better then the aloft that I had just stayed at in Ashburn, VA. Forget about parking anywhere near this hotel, and the valet is --$ and they make sure you are out by noon. The staff was exactly what is expected at a high price hotel. they bend over backwards for you and expect a tip!

This hotel provides great service and amenities! They took care of us from restaurant reservations to storing our luggage while we went sightseeing.
Highly recommended hotel!

A nice Hilton in the Chelsea-Fashion District. Cant really complain here...nice service, nice restaurant and rooftop bar...great location..rooms are decent-small, but that is nyc!! dont expect views..only buildings around this area.

I love to stay at the Budget Lodge Downtown Phoenix when I go to Chase Field to watch the Diamondbacks and when I go to spring training games. The hotel is clean, I mean clean, and the rooms always smell fresh. The location is ideal and the owners are so pleasant and accomodating. I can't imagine staying anywhere else.

Staybridge Suites in Dallas-Addison is a fabulous, friendly and family-oriented place which has a special place in my heart. I will stay no place else in the area as I have been spoiled by the comfort, friendliness and home-like feel of the Staybridge Suites in Dallas-Addison. The staff and managment are wonderful, sweet people who care about each and every guest. I have witnessed these interactions during my eight or nine visits to this hotel. It's a home away from home. I can't wait to see my new family again at this hotel when I return in a few weeks. Warmly, Dale Liuzza from New Orleans.

Once again we had a fabulous experience at a Sofitel hotel. We have stayed with them in Rio, Montreal, Amsterdam and now New York City. They are each unique but with understated elegance, charm and amazing service. The lobby is very European boutique. Quiet, understated and lovely. The room was very nice (small but that's NYC) with a lovely marble bath. We had a delicious breakfast in their French restaurant """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The Gaby"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Food and service were great. If we visit a city that has a Sofitel Hotel that's where we will stay, because they never disappoint a guest.

I chose Milner because after reading other reviews I thought it offered a good price-quality ratio and it fit perfectly my expectations.
The hotel is very well located, a couple minutes walk from Boston Commons and easy to reach many sites - places on foot. Boston is a great city for walking and I enjoyed starting my day with a strall around, from Milner hotel. Othewise subway is again a couple of blocks away, which is very convenient. 
It is a charming old building with pleasant atmosphere. Everything worked well - shower, internet; the room was clean and ok in size. The staff was friendly and helpful.
Breakfast was rather basic but again relatively nice: fruit salad, bagels with cream cheese, some donuts, cereal, coffee... you would not stay hungry. The breakfast room felt quite crowded in the mornings and once I could not find a table but the stuff was very accomodating and helped to sit in the next room.
The only strange thing which I did not like at all was that my room seemed to have a small angle tilt or maybe it was just the bed, so when sleeping I was sliding slowly to one side of the bed... had to sleep in diagonal to keep my balance :). It was one of the single rooms on the third floor. Funny, I've never encountered such problem anywhere else.
Overall, I was very satisfied with location, quality and price and would gladly stay again.

I came here with my friends and we had a great time here! The restaurant-bar had great food at a decent price! Beds were so comfortable! Staff and management were wonderful! I throughly enjoyed my stay at the hotel. Throughout my stay, the staff was very helpful, friendly and courteous! When I checked in, Ronnie at the front desk was extremely polite and friendly. She gave me a corner room, and that was a real bonus. The view was great, and I enjoyed the privacy of being way at the end of the hallway. I also appreciated that there was a microwave and a refrigerator in the room. My only minor complaint was that I could hear some noise from the room next door coming through the vent in the bathroom.
The hotel is in a great location. There is a Red Line 'L' stop right outside, and there are lots of stores and restaurants within walking distance. There is a grocery store across the street that's convenient if you want to save money by buying food instead of eating all of your meals at restaurants.

If I could stay anywhere in Boston, it would be at Jury's. Our first experience staying there was about - --- years ago, for just one night. Ever since then, whenever we have an occassion to stay in downtown Boston, we stay at Jury's. Immaculately clean, spacious marble bathrooms, and excellent location. Just across the street from Grill -- if you are looking for a good meal too!

Well, I'm back again and this place just keeps getting better each time.
The lobby has been refurbished since I was here last . A new look but the same wonderful service from everyone I encountered.
We requested the same room as our last visit and that was arranged and also requested a fridge in the room and that was waiting for us as well along with a nice welcome gift.
Took advantage of the pillow menu and the bed was just right.
Spent one day walking absolutely everywhere and a soak in the very deep bath tub was just what I needed.
Once again we ate breakfast in the restaurant each day and loved it.
This place is perfectly located and is really good value.
Looking forward to our next stay.
I stayed at this hotel for a conference at the end of May. It is in a great location but the day after my stay, the hotel was closed for renovations to be opened as a different hotel chain.

We stayed at the Hotel Solamar while attending a wedding in San Diego. All of the employees went out of their way to be friendly and accomodating. The management of this hotel really cares about creating a very welcoming atmosphere. Our room on the ninth floor was quiet, clean, and comfortable, and we had a view of the Petco baseball park. The location of the hotel is excellent. The gaslamp district is within a short walk, and features many excellent restaurants and bars. Valet parking is expensive, but the attendants did a great job parking and retrieving our car. We would definitely stay at this hotel on future visits to San Diego.

Good location but not cheap. Pet hate of charging an extra -- dollars for wifi a day is rather ridiculous after forking out -k over three days. Can't say I'd recommend as there are far nicer places around with character and better service.
very nice professional staff. The location was perfect for sightseeing in Phila.

We will definitely stay again.

Beautiful hotel, excellent staff and prime location - what more could you want in Chicago? I travelled with my three kids, ages -, - and -. Concierge got us set up at Shedd Aquarium, and we had Cubs tickets, with Wrigley Field a -- minute cab ride away. We will definitely return!!

We enjoyed a stay with our best friends on his birthday. The sunset was so beautiful. The wave gently wash up below the rooms and make a lovely sound for sleeping. Each cottage is decorated beautifully and is very comfortable. The patio out your backdoor is private with a gate that opens onto the pier, also private just for you and the other hotel guests. This is truly an amazing place to stay.

I was expecting the hotel to be just okay. I was surprised to find the hotel to be clean, great location, the most comfortable beds, great breakfast (although pricey), and the service to be exceptional.

I did mention my concerns at checkout and was given the name and phone number of the GM. I have placed two calls and left messages without response. It is now clearly apparent why the property is declining in the manner it is, the management just doesn't care. We love the location and just wanted to give honest constructive feedback to help improve things. My suggestion to anyone looking to book a hotel in NYC is to look elsewhere.

WOW!! I stayed at the Miyako in LA..had a conference to go to recently. I booked my hotel-flight and had read some reviews here. At first, I was just slightly leary...but decided to give it a go. The hotel and the rooms are always clean and customer service is the best.

If you want to pay extra to say in a suite, fine - go for it. We didn't need air conditioning in November and found the overhead ceiling fan and open windows more than adequate. And our room (---) was incredibly quiet. NO street noise other than the occasional cable car. 
I can't say enough good things about this hotel and I will definitely recommend it to all of my friends - and should I ever return to San Francisco, this is the only place I'll consider staying. The Chancellor made my trip to San Francisco absolutely wonderful. Thank you!

I booked this hotel despite reading all of the reviews on here for - reasons -) the price (£--- for - nights) and -) the location (literally - minute walk from Times Square).

As for the room, it did not look at all like the photos on the hotel's website. The carpet was quite dirty, particularly in the corners. There was an ample sized wardrobe, a dressing table, an old tv and nothing else. The bedding was clean, as was the bathroom.
A maid came in on one of our days and just straightened up the sheets on the bed, and replaced the dirty towels. 
Both me and my friend got bitten during the holiday, but we couldn't tell if this had happened in the hotel or outside. 
On the last day I looked under the bed to check I hadn't left anything and saw two rat traps under there, I was thankful at that point that I was going home!
At the end of the day I would recommend this hotel because if you're going to New York for a tourist holiday you're rarely in the room. I didn't expect high standards for the price I paid, and I was pleasantly surprised because it wasn't half as bad as many of these reviews had made out. If you're going to stay here I'd recommend taking your own towels and not walking barefoot on the carpet!

Though less expensive, you get what you pay for. Good: location, water pressure, breakfast. Bad: check in, sleep quality, uncontrollable air conditioning, terrible pillows. Overall not a good experience and I wont’ be back.
We got a good rate and got two rooms. We arrived before check-in time (so that’s my fault, I knew it was a chance we were taking) and the front desk asked me if I would like rooms next to each other. I said it didn’t matter but I would prefer it if it wouldn’t delay our rooms being ready. Well, at regular check in time two hours later that somehow turned our rooms not being ready into “the computer has you locked into two rooms next to each other, so we’ll need to wait for them to become available”. Any excuse that starts with “the computer” should be removed from service vocabulary. Someone (maybe on my unclear direction) made that our computerized preference, so unmake it if we want to get rooms instead of waiting! Painful. The people were nice about it at the front desk and the valet handled our bags fine, but we did end up waiting around for -- mins or so. Not awesome.
Worst sleep ever. The bed has one of those softness controls – we couldn’t find the stupid thing but that didn’t matter, the bed wasn’t the problem. The A-C and pillows were the problems. The A-C didn’t do whatever we told it to do. It turned on and off and blew directly on us, which I don’t mind, but then alternating our being cold and hot (the comforter would work in the Antarctic) was uncomfortable. As soon as we’d fall asleep the air would turn and we’d be uncomfortable again. The pillows are hollow. They are like two bed sheets filled with air. Touch them and they deflate into useless, flat, uncomfortable nothings. I don’t even understand how this works or why anyone would want it.
Water pressure was awesomely strong and had an adjustable shower head, which I needed to stay awake after the bad night’s sleep. Breakfast was a positive surprise. The chefs and servers were very conversant, pleasant and fun. It seems the people are not the problem at the Hilton. Shame we won’t be back.

We stayed here at the end of May for a week and absolutely loved it. The hotel is quite small, and had scaffolding up during our stay so it didn't look that nice from the outside, but once we were inside it looks really nice. The lobby is small but has got a nice water feature, and some comfy sofas. But what makes this hotel is the amazing staff and their level of service.
The staff here are awesome, especially Irene on reception. They couldn't do enough to help us whether it was recommending restuarants, sights to see and things to do. All members of staff that helped us were lovely, and went out of their way to do whatever they could. They gave us a free upgrade when we checked in to a city view room on the --th floor. They also booked us a car back to the airport on our last day which was $-- including tolls, tax and tip. 
The room was quite big for NYC standards, and had a wardrobe, drawers, a microwave and a fridge. The bed was the comfiest thing ever and we had such good sleep every night. The bathroom was also quite big, with towels replaced every day and Neutrogena products. The shower was great - good pressure and was always hot. There is a HD tv in the room with about --- channels to watch on cable. The air conditioning was good, although a little noisy so I probably wouldn't leave it on all night! There was also a sun block blind and a black out blind which kept the room a bit cooler. There is also a tea and coffee maker in the room. 
There is internet access downstairs in the lobby, and you have to use your key card to get in. There are only two computers, so we weren't able to get online a couple of times as it was too busy. There is also a printer, photocopier and shredder for guests to use. I didn't use the gym so I can't comment on that, and we didn't eat in the hotel, but the bar-restuarant area looked really nice. 
The lifts weren't really a problem when we were there. There are only -, so I would imagine there is probably quite a long wait during busy times of day, but we were always up early and back late, so never really waited for longer than about - minutes. The only problem we found with the lifts was that they are really noisy overnight. You can hear the doors opening and closing and the lift pinging from inside your room. Plus the walls of the rooms are a little thin so we could sometimes hear other guests chatting and watching tv. This wasn't really a massive problem though!
The hotel is about - blocks from Macys, just around the corner from Penn station and MSG. It took us about -- minutes to walk up to Times Square. There is a subway stop on each end of the street anyway so its really easy to get around. We walked up to Central Park one day too which took about -- minutes. There are loads of places to eat around the hotel. Try the Bread Factory just past MSG for bagels, or Fresh and Co (opposite MSG) for freshly made salads, pasta and sandwiches. We ate in Mustang Sallys one night which is just around the corner (they also provide the hotels room service) which is a kind of sports bar, and the food was really nice and not too expensive. 
I would recommend this hotel really highly to anyone. The street it is on doesn't look the nicest, but we always felt safe, and the flowers outside in the mornings make it look loads better! Plus it is a lot quiter as you are away from all the noise of Times Square. The staff are amazing and I will definitely stay here again when I come back to NYC.

We enjoyed staying at the Conrad and the room was lovely. I did find the lobby to be much more simple than I expected. It bordered on austere and had no warmth to it. But the staff and location made it a good stay.

I lived in this building (one of the small rooms) right before it was converted into the Hudson and they did a great job with it. I went back and stayed there for a long weekend to see what it was like. It is true that the rooms are small, but they are clean. The hotel tries to be trendy but that is what New York is about. If you are looking for fun, this is a good place (and location) to be. You can walk to so many places from here. I wouldn't suggest this place for families or people who want to relax.

Wife and I stayed there before-after a cruise. Before the cruise we were toward the back and the big trains like Amtrak do come in loud and clear especially when they blow the whistle whilst crossing streets. On Sunday night after cruise we were in the front on the street and the noise was barely noticeable.
The value and location of the hotel far outweigh the noise factor - unless you are in the very back right next to the train tracks. Plus you are right at the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""trolley"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (actually light rail) stop and about - blocks from the cruise ship terminals, Midway museum, etc.

Great food, good beer, an excellent view of downtown SD, and nice price. Outdoor seating is available.

The Chestnut Hill Hotel has undergone renovation that places it in a solid category. The rooms are reminiscent of an old fashioned hotel, but upgraded with free wireless, flat screen TVs, and nice modern bathrooms. They are still putting the finishing touches on the structure. More than the building, I will remember the high quality of service from the staff - recognizing guest after guest and referring to them by name, making any accommodation quickly and generously. Also, located on Germantown Ave puts it among hundreds of small, locally-owned shops. Great place.

loved this place,first time we stayed here was a month after ---- and it has got a well worn feel but it was always very metallic and shabby by design, it was ahead of its time!
The front desk staff were very friendly and the(included in the rate) breakfast was perfect.Yes the paintwork could do with an update but overall i would recommend this hotel as a good base for a short break in New york !

Otherwise, the subway awaits to whisk you anywhere you like and is a short walk. No idea about parking, but you'd have to be barking mad to drive in NYC anyway.
The room was smallish, but that was fully expected in such a good NYC location. It was very clean, modern and comfortable, no complaints at all in the two week stay. Considering my only other hotel options remotely in the pricerange I paid were shared bathrooms or way out of the way, this was tremendous value, and if I could get the room for the same price again, I'd stay here in a flash.

We chose this hotel based on it's location directly across the street from the Times Union Theater. We didn't eat in the restuarant but the bar is very nice and the service was excellent. Despite the issues we had during our stay, the staff was so friendly and accomodating that we won't hesitate to stay here again on our next visit to Jacksonville!

Was in Jacksonville for - nights for a conference of ---+ people. The hotel never felt crowded, there was plenty of room to accomodate this large crowd. The bed was very comfortable with enough pillows to satisfy anyone and the bathroom nice and spacious, and all very clean. Ate at the Trellis restaurant for both breakfast and lunch, prices were a bit high but the food was excellent and well worth the price. 
I would stay here again if in Jacksonville.

Kitchen includes dishes, a large refrigerator, microwave, toaster oven, coffee maker, and table-chairs. Except for the Cafe on Park (which was closed on the day we arrived) there are no restaurants within a reasonable walking distance. However, San Diego has so many places with great restaurants like the Gaslamp Quarter and Old Town that we sampled a different spot each night.

Upon arrival, it was pouring down with rain & we thanked the gentleman who worked there, who helped us in to the hotel from the cab. The hotel receptionist were busy when we got there, with a long line of people checking in, however they did a fantastic job & were extremely welcoming & friendship to us. In addition to the free wifi, another perk is complimentary beverage service delivered in the morning. Both of these were very important to me. Location, Location, Location. It near Union Square and if you are planning to rent a car. Most of car rental and parking is just across the street. The hotel is quite old. The complimentary breakfast was great. It is a excellent value and I would recommend it to other travelers.

From the moment I arrived I was greeted by a very polite gentleman that took my luggage and escoted me to the front desk. The check in was quick and courteous. When I arrived at my studio suite and noticed that I did not have a shower curtain, I made a trip back to the front desk to ask for one and to get a city map and suggestions for dinner. By the time I returned to my suite the shower curtain was already put up. The restaurant recommendations were excellent. I went to the small store in the front of the hotel and the gentlemen in the store were also very friendly.
I attended the conference at another hotel during my stay and was driven to and from the conference by the nice gentlemen at the Magnolia Hotel. Every night for dinner we were driven in very clean luxury SUV's to our destination and picked up. The hotel staff went out of their way to make us feel special every time we saw someone.
The happy hour is nice and comfortable with very courteous service. I was pleased that I could get a late light snack of cookies and milk from the lounge when I had some late night work to do.
I will only stay at this Hotel when I visit Houston.
