Upon entering the room on the -th floor, we found that the room had not been used in quite some time. The bathroom was not clean, although it had nice amenities (soap, shampoo, etc), but we had to clean the shower before using it. It was awful. The room also had a musky smell to it. It stormed that night, and I assume they use a satellite dish, because once it started storming, the tv programming went completely out.
The next morning, we stepped outside our room to find everyone on our floor had received the Dallas Morning News except us. Whether this was an oversight, or the fact we got such a great rate that we didn’t matter, we do not know. As we gathered our belongings to head downstairs and ask about breakfast, we were told it was not included. Had I known that, we would have stayed at the Marriott down the street where I have a rewards card and would have received a great breakfast.
I have stayed at the Omni Park West in the past and was very pleased, and was actually looking forward to my stay this time. But, unfortunately, it did not meet my expectations and we will probably not be going back.

My son and I stayed for several days as I was in-town for a business matter. Wonderful historic hotel with class and especially great if you are into western decor. Walking distance to good dining and entertainment. Really nice rooms with great comfort. Just an all around nice experience.
My son loved as much as I did!

The very nice valet parked our car and we took the Metro for the - days we were in DC. The hotel is located one block from the subway. Neighborhood is safe and clean. You can walk to many good restaurants. Try Founding Farmers on Pennsylvania, just before the circle. The room is good sized and sound proof. Plenty of hot water and good water pressure. Windows open for a spring breeze. Housekeeping was attentive and room was always cleaned up nice. You are also close enough to Lincoln Memorial, White House, and the mall to walk. Our family walked downtown in the evenings to see the monuments all lit up. Our kids (-- and --) had no problem with the walk and it is very safe. There are actually cops and security guards everywhere.

We spent four days at the Bahia and loved it! Our patio opened onto the private beach so I had a water view whenever I wanted (I'm from the desert), it was close to all the amenities, and the staff was wonderful! I am slightly handicapped so accessibility was important, and I only wish they had had higher toilets :-)! The rooms are old, but clean and comfortable. This is a terrific place for kids -- I loved watching them on the paddle boards. Kayaks and bicycles are also available for rent. We had breakfast in the dining room and from room service and it was always excellent. Unfortunately we were other places for dinner.

We just stayed at this hotel last weekend, and I was SHOCKED with joy at how wonderful it was. 
Mark Hopkins is a Grande old Dame... perched on top of Nob Hill. Easy walk to Union Square, and the cable car. 
Our room was on the --th floor with a great view. The room was large, and extremely well appointed. The bathroom was large with really nice amenities and the large shelf above the sink was great to put toiletries on. The water pressure in the shower was a wonderful surprise too. See... I have extremely thick and longer hair and without good pressure I cannot get the shampoo out. Nice shower. 
The bed was heavenly too. We prefer our beds to be rock hard and ultra firm. This one would satisfy all customers -- those like us who like a firm one, and the others that like soft. The pillows were perfect too (which never happens in a hotel either!). 
Our room also was stocked with coffee and CoffeeMate which totally excited me. I know...I know... silly but true! 
The Concierge, George became our best friend. He was so helpful and scored great dinner reservations for us. 
We called for allergy free bedding upon first arrival and within - minutes they appeared. Same thing the next day when my husband needed shaving cream. LESS THAN - MINUTES? Wow. 
The service was impeccable. 
Top of the Mark chocolate Martinis come very highly recommended too :) 
LOVED THIS HOTEL. 
Plus... we got our room (and they upgraded it free) for $-- a night. NOt too shabby

My wife and I stayed at the W for two nights last week. The hotel feels hip and the main registration floor had many of the aspects of a private club. The registration staff person was very efficient and friendly. The hotel is located in the heart of the theater district and is convenient to all of Midtown. 
I found the room to be very well insulated from street noise, which can be a problem in NY. The bed was very comfortable and the linens were bordering on the luxurious. While the room is rather small, I didn't not feel cramped. It had a very modern, but comfortable feel.
Our big problem was the bathroom. There simply is no counter space and I became concerned that if I didn't position the glass I use for incidental medications perfectly, I would risk having it crash onto the floor. Everything about the bathroom was poorly designed. No place to hang used towels, a tiny basin, and no shelves or space for toiletries. I wound up using the top of the toilet as my primary space for bathroom stuff.
For a place as polished as the W, the bathroom felt like an irrelevant after-thought.

we had a quick one night stopover in seattle on our way to vancouver. we chose this hotel as it was recommended in lonely planet. GOD NO! the rooms were TINY, and the walls paper thin, with lots of strange characters coming and going at all hours. we asked to be moved from our initial room (with a great view of car park) as there was the constant sound of a baby crying. our second room (same size, even better view of car park) was even noisier, and we were kept up all night by people in the room next door having very loud and vocal sex. if you want to sleep in seattle, this is not the place for you.

We loved our stay in NYC as a result of this hotel. Location is excellent. We could walk to Broadway and to the Amtrak station (a few blocks away). It's a real neighborhood with juice bars, and hole-in-the-wall breakfast places, amazing pizza & salad places. It rained hard while we were there, and we were directed to a street vendor who stands at a certain corner selling umbrellas whenever it rains! We got two for $-. I got a different look at NYC this time--a community in action sort of look.
Staff is friendly and professional. Downstairs automatic coffee machine is amazingly versatile. Laundry room is v. efficient. There is one computer downstairs, but the place has wireless. There's an Indian place that serves lunch, a Dunken Donuts-Subway fast food place (yes, they are together!) as well as a high end chocolate and wine restaurant next door; there's also a whole neighborhood of fancy Korean restaurants around the corner. We saw lots of German tourists in our hotel this time. Made conversations fun.
Did I mention the place is lovely in a tasteful and determinedly non-chain hotel kind of way? We got sick the second day there and just wanted to stay in our rooms and nest, which we did. It was v. comforting to have the drugstore, and an acupuncturist (at the Pacific College of Oriental Medicine on Broadway), and juice stand so close.
We would stay there again anytime we're in NYC. No wonder this place won their city's award for best hotel value.

After a long haul flight, it took -- minutes to check in, while I was the only person at the desk. I had to ask - times for a power adapter, which at the end I bought at Radio Shak in front. The Club Sandwich by room service was cold. Going to bed, the linen was not changed, yerk! For that price, unbelievable.

This hotel is an excellent choice if you're attending a convention and don't mind a ten-minute walk to save a few dollars.
The hotel is on the Riverwalk, but it's more direct to walk a few blocks to the Convention Center. It's a quick, easy and pleasant walk.
The hotel is great -- rooms are fairly new and very clean, and it's always nice to have the extra room of a suite, and the convenience of a refrigerator.
The staff is very nice, but there is not enough of them. Often a call to the front desk went unanswered, and sometimes you couldn't find a person at the front desk for help.
Nevertheless, this hotel offers a pleasant experience and a good value relative to other hotels in the area.

I made a booking for a last-minute stay at this hotel last week through an online booking site - the date processed wrong. I made the booking at -am for that night since we did not want to have to drive anywhere after an unexpectedly late night out with friends, instead of that night the room got booked for the next night - i'm assuming because they can't process a booking that late? Anyway, it wasn't the end of the world I figured I could just talk to someone & sort it out........
The booking site didn't give any numbers that put you through to a person & listed the number of the hotel so I tried calling them to figure out what I could do-was there any room for that night instead-did I need to cancel the booking etc. The first time I called I got hung up on, the second time the lady I got through to was very abrupt, wouldn't even let me explain the situation before cutting me off & saying that she couldn't help - so I asked if there was a night manager I could speak with. She replied that she was the night manager and with an 'overly exaggerated sigh' (I could almost feel her rolling her eyes kind of sigh) said all she could do was cancel the booking because they were already full for that night. Silence for a minute or two then she came back on the line & rattled off a cancellation number so quickly I didn't even have time to grab a pen & paper. I asked her to repeat the number because I'd only managed to get the first few digits down and, Verbatim she said 'I'm busy right now, just check your bank account in a few days, it'll be credited back to you' then hung up on me. Now a week later lo-and behold, my account is still being charged & when I spoke with the booking company the next day they said they she could not cancel the booking & now it was too late to change it. Also they didn't know why she would have told me that she did. So either she is, as a manager, ignorant of the policies of the hotel & the companies they work with OR she just outright lied about cancelling the booking because she was busy & I was taking up her time. Neither of these are great qualities for managerial staff of a -* hotel. 
There are so many great hotels in this city with truly educated, caring staff & in a similar price range that I wouldn't waste my time with this one.

My husband and I stayed here May ---, and took in our first Baltimore Orioles game on Tuesday, May -.
The Pros: It's right across the street from Oriole Park at Camden Yards and only about a -- minute walk to the Inner Harbor and sights like the National Aquarium. For what we wanted to do, we never had to use our car while we were there. We had a terrific king """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""corner"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" suite overlooking the stadium on the top (-th) floor. Unlike other people, we didn't have any problem with noise (but on Monday night's game, the Orioles were losing badly, and there wasn't much of a crowd, so maybe that's why we didn't hear much). The daily breakfast has plenty of healthy options, including oatmeal, fresh fruit, and yogurt, as well as make-your-own waffles, bagels, cereals, pastries, and rotating hot items such as omelets and hash browns. Coffee and an assortment of teas are available in the lobby -- hours a day, with popcorn and cookies available in the late afternoon. The afternoon staff was very accommodating - they let us have a couple of Cokes from their store for free while we were waiting for the room we wanted to become available. The baseball decor in the lobby is a nice touch. We didn't use the fitness center or pool, but we did check them out, and the fitness center in particular seemed well-equipped with everything you'd need for a good workout. The business center was small but seemed adequately equipped. Most staff members we encountered were very friendly, with everyone from valets to housekeeping staff greeting us whenever they saw us. There are a number of nearby restaurants within easy walking distance - if you want to avoid the noisy pubs next door, go around the corner to Potbelly Sandwich Works for made-to-order sandwiches and cookies-to-die-for.
The Cons: I'm a Hilton HHonors member, and I was supposed to get a free newspaper delivered to my room on the weekdays. Of the - days, I only received a paper on the first day (Monday). I had to call down to the front desk to have someone deliver a paper on the other two days, and the morning staff seemed irritated that I would want this. Yes, it's a little thing, but it's a perk that comes with being a member of Hilton's frequent traveler program - if the paper doesn't get delivered like it's supposed to, then it shouldn't be a problem to have someone bring one up. Also, I had booked under the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Wheel-Inn"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" deal, where valet parking is included in the nightly cost (this saves a few bucks per night over getting a cheaper rate and paying $-- for parking), and I pointed this out when I checked in. When I got my bill, though, they charged me another $---night extra for valet parking. I called down to the front desk, which re-ran the bill with the correct amount. So make sure you check your bill when you get ready to leave.

Bathroom could have been cleaner but otherwise a nice hotel. Our room was --- and all night you heard some motor come on and off. Great location for all kinds of restaurants and shopping. Movie theater nearby. We will stay here again.

RPRS treated us like royalty on our -st south-western trip. The RPRS staff went above and beyond our expectations to make us feel very welcome and that our stay was comfortable. Room --- was in a part of the resort that was quiet with a view of Camelback mountain. I do have to say the resort was smaller than we thought which made it more intimate for my wife and I. FYI while there, spend time looking at the little things that aren't in the obvious like paintings, statues, and the landscape with fountains. 
The room was clean and bed comfortable. The parking attendants were great. I tried to tip them but they reminded me tipping was not required. They also like sprinkles cupcakes...check that our at the fashion square mall. 
The resort is so nicely located not far from the airport, which btw no plane traffic over the resort. The pool is refreshing at -- degrees in the --- sun heat. Jose at poolside hustles like nobody you've ever seen. I was sweating watching him go from - side to the other to make sure we're okay. 
The spa is very clean and they were so nice to make sure we got what we wanted. Lisa, Carol and Dell were very attentive and good at what they do. 
T.Cooks...awesome! I hate to call it food because everything we ordered was so flavorful
and delicious. For our anniversary dinner which they remembered made our night so very special and romantic. 
Thank you RPRS...we'll be back.
To conclude our anniversary stay was fulfilled by the staff at RPRS. Thank you!!!!
Check out some of our pics.

Got stuck here by an unnamed airline with lots of Charlotte flights after they bumped us a full day. It's the one thing the airline got right that day. Nice hotel, rooms were reasonably quiet and suite style, so lots of room. Exercise facility was in great working order, pool and hot tub were good. The main problem with this place is that it's in the middle of a business park, there's absolutely nothing around it. As such, the prices in the restaurant and bar are atrocious. Also, no free wifi - c'mon Renaissance, get with the times. Free airport shuttle.

the name of the hotel really attracted me, i knew it's super close to the downtown and Chinatown, but a room was too small, a view from windows ( well were it windows:-) was on some courtyard from which we could hear ( from - a.m) some cleaning work, garbages thrown down and the noise was indeed very irritating. hotel is great due to bar and the barmans:-) oh such lovely guys:-) and a music, live jazz.
besides the reception and service is ok. the flavour spread deeply is just amazing like in A&F stores.

This was probably the best Hotel we've ever stayed at. We also had a AAA special that included breakfast and WOW, what a breakfast!!!! The restaurant is excellent and the ambiance couldn't be better. Location is magnificent and our price couldn't be beat. To me this was a - star hotel.

Stayed at the ES on State Street for summer vacation. Check in was easy, but staff was not very """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""welcoming"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" especially being that I am a Hilton Honors Member. I did receive a couple of complimentary bottles of water as a HH member about -- minutes of being in the room. The room was decent size, and we had a corner room, so had window in both rooms of the suite that overlooked the streets below. A corner room was tucked away, so not much noise and foot traffic, which helped. Everything in the room seemed to work fine except the TV remote. Took many attempts to turn on the TV. 
Breakfast was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""free-for-all""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""' with huge lines, not much organization, and many dirty tables. We had to push dirty plates from others to edge of table just to find a seat, and then it took about -- minutes for someone to ask if we needed those plates cleared. I said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""yes since they had been sitting here before we sat down"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The buffet was the same each day...eggs, greasy bacon, sausage, overcooked rubbery pancakes, and an omelet station. The omelet station was right in the middle of the - sides of the buffet, which made it confusing as to which lines people were in, and the wait even longer in line. Perhaps they move the omelet station elsewhere to helpnline-crowd control of the main buffet lines. I would also suggest changing up the selection every few days. I know it's """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""free"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but it got old after a few days. The unorganized lines, dirty tables, and lack of selection made it not such a great experience.
The managers reception consisted of free beer, wine, and some mixed drinks. Had snacks (veggies and dip, Hummous and pita chips), etc. 
Good location of hotel on State Street with just a short walk - block south to the Red Line on the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""EL"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", and - or so block to Michigan Avenue. You can buy CTA passes across the street at the Market. The Concierge was VERY helpful and friendly with directions, recommendations, etc. 
Would I stay here again...maybe. If I did, I would venture out for breakfast instead of eating at hotel.

Wow; huge selection at the free breakfast with hit and cold foods, a free shuttle to the main city attractions and a great room with Aveda toiletries. We saved a bundle of cash and aggravation. Great front desk staff and shuttle drivers made our stay very enjoyable. Will recommend this stay to all our friends and family!

As wonderful as the facility is , and it is first class, from the quality of the linens and furnishings to the appearance and large size of the rooms, the staff genuinely demonstartes concern and care for their guests' well-being. This is reflected in their responsiveness, concern and friendliness in every encounter we had from check-in to room service, doorman and the spa. Their competency in doing things correctly and on-time is also noted. The no tipping policy does not leave service to be desired in this unique facility. This place works like a top-tier hotel should work. I wish they all did that!

Just returned from first visit to America - New York is a fantastic city to visit and our stay was made even better by this great hotel. Accommodation is as featured on the website and the staff were efficient and friendly. The breakfast is great to set you up before a day of sightseeing and the complementary glass of wine rounds the day off nicely. Would have no hesitation in recommending this hotel

Pacific Shores has the nearby beach going for it. That said, if you want to be more centrally located to the main San Diego area you may be disappointed here. It is just off of Pacifc Beach which is directly North of Mission beach. They are both just North of Mission Bay and Sea World. That means they are also well North of the San Diego harvour area, the downtown and Blaboa Park. We found the drive to Sea World to be easy with routes to Mission Bay right down Mission Boulvard or over Grand Street to Ingrahm Ave. We tried the beach both off of the motel at pacific beach and down near Belmont Park on Mission beach. The Mission beach area is a little better for kids. Both are well patroled by lifeguards and the ocean surf is warm and fun to play in. We spent three nights at Pacific Shores. The motel is going through some """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""growing"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" pains with upgrading going on. One afternoon after returnign from the beach we were kept oput of returnign to our room while maintenance was replacing a light switch with sensor switch. This was late in the afternoon at a time when they should expect the guests may want to return to thier rooms. The timing was bad. The last night we spent the smoke alarm batery gave out around midnight and the device began emitting loud alarms. A call to thew dsk brought someont tot eh room aroun -:--AM, We had to small boys with us trying to sleep. The man replaced the bsattery in the smoke dector and wehn away. A hald horu later it began letting off a short blast every hour or so for the rest of the night! We has a restless night and the kids were not happy. Complaining to the manager lead to the expalnation that the battery was probably not put in properly, sorry about that. No adjustment was offered on our rate but he did say if we come back again to call him and he would give us a better rate next time. Overall while the location may be out of the way to some we enjoyed the proximity of the beaches, the overall casual atmosphere of the area. The motel manager also mentioned that upgrades are planned to replace the pool area and improve the overall motel. The cost is reasonable, the weather is always great and if that darn smoke alarm goes off put the battery in yourself!

We have enjoyed the Four Seasons in many locations. Chicago is no exception. This hotel boasts a new restaurant, which is actually where the old restaurant used to be, but the menu is new and the atmosphere is great. You can't beat the location...very nice upscale mall on the first - floors of the building. You can step right out the front door onto Michigan Ave. and find even more fabulous shoppinig. The rooms are beautifully decorated and so well kept. The service is top shelf and the staff will bend over backwards to please you. This is my idea of a - star rating and I have compared other hotels to the quality of the Four Seasons when I reviewed them.

A couple of people we knew had stayed here and recommended it and when we read the reviews on Trip Advisor we decided to go for it. In New York you just want a clean place to sleep and shower and this place was perfect! Rooms were spotlessly cleaned, new towels were left every day and the chamberperson even used to tidy our clothes putting them into neat piles. my dressing table and the bathroom sink area was also tidied for me! (I am very messy!) The rooms had TV with cable I assume, ideal for putting on and dozing to before going out in the evening! Tribeca is a great area, fab neigbourhood feel to it, especially when you see all the yummy mummies with babies, families, workers and everyday New Yorkers going about their business, it really made the trip seem real insead of just crowds of tourists everywhere. We ate in Tribeca almost every night. Mexican next door to Cosmo is delicious. There is also good nightlife around Tribeca, we used to go to the Reade Street Pub most nights and everyone was so friendly which not exactly what I had been told about New Yorkers. The Subway is right outside the hotel, we bought weekly Metrocards for $-- and they were worrth every cent. You can also walk to alot of places from the hotel which is definitly worth it as you get the real feel for New York just walking round. But as far as this hotel goes I would deffo stay there again and have recommended it to my friend who is going in July. It is real value for money, we paid just over $---- for - nights and most places in the touristy bits of New York charge double that price. It was clean, staff were friendly and obliging , we asked for a room off the street and we got it. Above all I had a fab time and it snowed which made the trip perfect if not very cold!!!!

I have stayed here twice in the last - months. It is in a GREAT location just - block away from Macy's and about a -- minute walk to Times Square. There is a subway stop right on the corner and about a - minute walk to Penn station and Madison Square Garden. The front desk staff is friendly and helpful and they have a fantastic concierge named Matthew who is extremely knowledgeable and always offering up suggestions. During my first stay we had a room right near the elevator and this proved to be quite noisy. Our second stay we got a room further down the hallway, in the corner, and it was much quieter. My only complaint is with the water temperature in the shower. No matter what time of day you use the shower the temperature continuously goes from ice cold to boiling hot. I did ask about this at the front desk and they are aware of the issue and unfortunately there is nothing they can do. I will definitely be staying at this hotel again on future trips to NYC!

I would highly recommend this hotel. The staff was wonderful, the beds were extremely comfortable and the location is perfect. Of special note is the hotel restaurant (Coast). I chose their """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Superfood"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" breakfast and was treated to Orange-Blueberry Granola Pancakes. They were delicious and full of anti-oxidants. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Superfood"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" menu included many other healthy choices which is really great because it's so hard to eat healthy when on the road. My server at Coast was Nathan Nichols and he did an outstanding job. I generally don't take the time to write reviews but my stay at this hotel was so good, I really wanted to give the Westin a pat on the back.

We have just returned from a visit to USA taking in San Francisco. We chose the Palace Hotel after reading the reveiws on tripadvisor.
This is a wonderful hotel with very helpful and curtious staff, luxury accomodation and fantastic food. The bedrooms were very large and comfortable the location is good. We would return here again and would have no hesitation in recommending this hotel. Well worth a stay.

This hotel seems to be a place where long-term people stay. There was a party outside our door at -:--, our room was not ready AFTER the posted check-in time so we had to leave and come back, the highway noise was annoying, and last but not least a bum approached us in the parking lot. Fair warning.. DON'T stay here. Plenty of other better, cheaper options.

This hotel was booked as part of a package from the Uk and was great value. We only had two nights in New York and as it was our first visit, it was important to us that we were near to the main places. The hotel is just round the corner from the Rockafella centre and from here you can take the hop on hop off buses. We went to see Cirque du Soleil at the Radio City Hall which is - minutes walk from the hotel. Taxis run past the hotel all the time so are easy to catch if you need one. 
As for the hotel itself,our first impressions were good. The staff were very helpful and efficient. West Club is an old building which I personally found enchanting. Our room was spacious, clean and comfortable. However I do agree with the previous review that the air conditioning is old and noisy. It didn't bother me as it drowned out any traffic noise.however this could be a problem for light sleepers.
There is a lovely restaurant ,ballroom and jazz nights were held every Wednesday when we were there. to sum it up,this was a great value small hotel in a superb location. Would I stay there again? Definitely!

Courteous staff, but not recommended for the business traveler. Free internet, but no printing facility. Old, musty, dirty feel of an old aprtment building that had been converted into a hotel. Rooms were passable, but dirty in places. Carpet worn. Lack of attention to detail.
If you're traveling for business, you can do much better.

We chose to stay at the Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf Hotel as it appeared to be in the best location in town and following on from some of the previous reviews offered clean and comfortable beds. It was a good decision.
The hotel rooms are a good size (we had a King Bed) with flat screen tv, tea-coffee maker, individual controlled air con-heating (although old style) a chair, coffee table - we were on the third floor with a view over the entrance but were not disturbed by any traffic noise. The bathroom is rather on the small size (you have to almost stand on the toilet to close the door) and the sink-vanity unit is in a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hallway"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" shared with the wardrobe. (There is an iron-ironing board, hairdryer and safety deposit box as well).
Disappointed to find that the hotel charges for internet access in the room whilst anyone who walks in off the street can have free access in the lobby. - 
Staff were very friendly and knowledgeable - they answered any questions we had with a smile and we never got the feeling we were just another one in the queue.
The hotel is located just a few minutes walk from Pier --, Cable Powell & Hyde Cable Car stop and in easy reach of the ferry for Alcatraz.
The hotel offers an outdoor swimming pool with a couple of sunbeds around so useful for a quick dip after a busy day out. The seating area by the main door with the firepits are an interesting feature.
The hotel offers a basic snack bar in the lobby area however it is very expensive - (almost -$ for a herbal tea !!!!) so more cost effective to have breakfast out in any of the local restaurants)
One major thing to take into account when holidaying in San Francisco is the changeable weather....as Mark Twain is quoted as saying..""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The coldest winter I ever spent was summer in San Francisco"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" ! Whilst the sun is warm as soon as you go into the shade (or on a bus or ferry) the wind can be freezing cold so make sure you take a warm fleece jacket - cardigan to use when needed.

We were very pleased with the accommodations at the Baymont Inn & Suites. The shuttle service was a bit of a challenge but given the circumstances at the airport, I thought the staff at the Baymont did an outstanding job.

Stayed one night to go to a baseball game, front desk said it was a -- minute walk to park, took us about -- minutes to get out of park and walk home. Hotel was clean and fresh. Had booked a panoramic view room, but when we got here, there were not any. Front desk gave us another room without the view with a discount. Breakfast was ok, garden inn next door, looked better. The hotel is hooked to a health club, that is very nice!

I travelled here in April ---- mainly because it was a -- minute walk to the arena as we were headed to a Stars game. The continental breakfast was upscale and they had a free happy hour with chicken, guacamole, chip and salsa, beer, wine etc. Booking here really saved the food bill. This hotel is also close to the freeway (not that you can hear though) and very close to downtown Dallas. The staff was freindly, the hotel clean, parking was secure (and $-.-- per day). Being from Canada, the type of beds were abit odd, they dont have a room with two queens, we stayed in one with a king and csofa sleeper, Perhaps they just werent avaialble at the price we booked at. 
I would reccomend this property highly, also we were told that many families of Satrs and Mavericks players stay here so it cant be bad, right?

Downtown Indianapolis is architecturally elegant and JW Marriott is the keystone.
When we entered the lobby last Friday afternoon, waitstaff were offering on their trays, pasta in tiny glasses. Unusual offering, I thought. The mini-marathon was the next morning, so of course!
Everything at JW Marriott, from the service to the cuisine to the rooms is wonderful. JW Marriott is conveniently adjacent to Museums, where we visited on foot. However, the hotel itself could be the destination. It's a hotel that's effectively doubles as a resort. 
 Usually, this reviewer would seek """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""mom and pop"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" small places to cast light upon; not so, in this case.

This hotel seems great at first because of the great location and great service and the cute hotel dog that everyone can touch but when you are trying to sleep you nearly feel like if the people in the next room are speaking right next to you. The hotel was built in ---- so I'm not very surprised. Apart from that everything at this hotel is great.

I stayed during a recent conference at the hotel and upgraded to a suite. Not cheap by any means, but the upgrade was only an extra $--, which we found well worth it. 
The property is first rate. Our only complaint was that the housekeeper, who was apparently trained to pick up after guests, put suitcases on the luggage rack, etc., actually took our bags out of the closet and piled them on the luggage rack. We found that a bit odd and intrusive.

Our family stayed at the Omni at Independence Park at the end of July. If you are visiting the historic sights, this is the best location in the city. We were pleased with the friendly staff (from the doormen to the concierge). The pool is small, but very nice (the fitness room and pool were recently renovated). The room was clean and the bathroom area large. The only downside was the noise from the street at night (there isn't much going on outside, but the windows needed to be more soundproof). We would definitely stay here again if we return to Philadelphia. You are only a block away from Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell. If you are traveling with children, don't miss the storytelling benches located throughout the city at different historic areas. The stories are brief, but interesting, and often include participation from the children.

This was a very good stay at a reasonable price. Every person I interacted with was knowledgeable, efficient, and friendly. Breakfast was very good, with a large selection of items: bacon, eggs, biscuits and gravy, cereal, variety of pastries, and cinnamon rolls. The entire facility is clean, comfortable, and in great shape. There was fresh fruit and bottled water available at check-in as well. And even though we were less than a mile away from the airport, you couldn't hear the planes from inside the building. Things I didn't take advantage of but were available were a free shuttle to and from the airport, fitness center, and business center (including a printer). I even lost my cell phone in my room, and housekeeping found it, and a relative was promptly alerted that they had retrieved it. Because I had already left, they said they would ship my phone through FedEx overnight to my residence in Indiana (which I had to pay for, but I understand that.)

I took my family including my parents to DC for the weekend & stayed here for - nights. We loved our stay. We got an upgrade to the presidential suite thanks to the excellent floor manager Gene Polhamus. I used most of my points being a Hilton Honors member for so long but I felt that it was worth because the - bedroom - bath and large living room area was such a treat and my family really liked it. Breakfast & managers reception were good. Breakfast was really nice and they had great choices. Managers reception included great alcoholic drinks, the line was a little long. The soft drinks seem not to work that well. The staff was really friendly and really accommodating. The hotel is very conveniently located and the pool and hot tub were great. I plan to stay here again while my kids are in school in DC.

My husband and I travel to San Antonio often and stay at Omni La Mansion del Rio. We always have the most amazing stay at this hotel. Our last visit was our honeymoon August ----. We arrived late and the staff brought us chocolate covered strawberries and champagne!!! 
The staff are freindly and have a service attitude. They are always willing to accomodate us on anything we need.
I can never say enough about this hotel. The rooms , staff and service are the best around!!
I rave about this hotel to anyone who will listen!!!
The hotel resturant is also amazing!! Food, staff and service is excellent!!
We are planning our -st anniversary trip and we are staying at this hotel.

Stayed here for a few days last month and everything was top notch. I had an especially nice experience in the fitness center because of a very nice man by the name of Robert who went out of his way to help me...highly recommended!

I was in San Diego for a conference and my company booked at Pacific Terrace. I was greeted by friendly and welcoming front desk staff and found out I was upgraded to a junior suite with partial view of the ocean. Check in was quick and the person that checked me in was informative and resourceful about the hotel amenities and where to eat nearby, etc. 
My room was large, clean and stocked. That partial view was amazing, not sure why they call it a partial view! The front desk called me to make sure all was well in my room. The room is nicely appointed with free and reliable wireless (important item for me when traveling for business). 
They do not have a restaurant at the hotel, but have a few options: (-) they have participating restaurants that deliver food, and (-) they provide a food card and if you eat at the participating restaurants of that plan they just bill your room. 
Also, they do have a breakfast buffet in the morning which is nice and pretty reasonable in cost. 
Location, it is walking distance to lots of dining options and a Starbucks. The hotel is very close to Interstate -, literally --- minutes straight shot to La Jolla, and many other areas. 
Downside, public parking is hard to get, but there is valet option of $---per day. Not an issue for me, but those on a budget, this is a good thing to know. 
Otherwise, the stay was amazing and I will certainly return to stay at Pacific.

Visited NYC Memorial Day Weekend ------ - stayed at the West --th Street Hampton Inn - I began to wonder if there is a tier system in the Hampton Inn chain - were some Hampton Inns """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""better"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" than others because this one was a disappointment - it was just OK but I would not go there again - The Hampton Inn on -th Ave & --st St. is much nicer.

I was skeptical. We usually stayed at one of the big chain hotels in NYC, often using points because the city can be so expensive. But this time we were traveling with another couple and they balked at the big price tag of our usual hotel. My brother has stayed numerous times at the Roger Smith Hotel and has always been satisfied, so I reluctantly agreed to give it a try. Well, I have to admit that we've found a new hotel in the city! The Roger Smith is quiet, charming, nicely appointed and conveniently located. We found the front desk staff friendly and willing to offer travel advice. Yes, the decor is older and a bit worn, but that just adds to the charm ~ as long as it's clean. And yes, it was clean throughout. The bed was comfortable and the room was quiet. NYC has so much to offer that a visitor is rarely in the room anyhow. Why pay upwards of three times as much for a different hotel? We're trying the Roger Smith again this December and hope to have the same wonderful experience.

Positives were that the Hotel is close to the --th street Broadway subway, the staff were friendly and helpful and the room was clean. Negatives were the worn carpet in the room and a need for some sprucing up. Also, the immediate neighbourhood is not great but there are lots of restaurants there and it is relatively close to Central Park. I suppose one is not in the room much while visiting and its rates are generally lower and for those willing to ignore the negatives it is probably not a bad option.

This hotel has some of the best service I have ever experienced. The staff excels in service, upon arrival, my room was not ready but was able to check in. They stored my luggage while I attended a session of my work conference the staff took my luggage to my room then found me in the conference room and handed me the keys. Still don't know how they remembered me because there were several checking in at the same time and we all received the same service. Job well done Westin.

I frequently stay at Homewood Suites for business. I've had some mediocre experiences and some very good ones. This particular one was not up to par with some of the others. The facilities and rooms are clean, and the rooms quiet...no complaints there. Mostly minor stuff. Iron was missing from room. Only one TV remote, but it did control both TVs, so just a minor annoyance in having to carry it back and forth between the room and living area. No wine or beer in the evening reception (they say they are """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""close"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to getting their license). They have a TV in the reception area, but might as well not as their """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""mood music"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" drowns it out. As a Silver Hilton Honors member (not very high up, I know), it still miffed me that they wouldn't allow me a late checkout (-pm) even though I offered to pay half the daily rate. The hotel wasn't packed out, so it doesn't make much business sense to let a room go vacant when you could at least realize a partial payment AND satisfy a loyal customer.
I think with a little more attention to the little things, this facility could be one of the better ones, but if I was going back again in the near future I might try a different Homewood.

After a bad experience at another hotel we escaped to this hotel and were pleasantly surprised with place and the staff- especially the guy who checked us in. The rooms were clean and the location was great and the history of the place and connection with Hollywood made the stay even more memorable. I think that the girls at reception in the morning shift could be a bit more friendly but overall they did not detract from the overall positive experience we had there. Perhaps at check-in the staff could explain some of the services and amenities on offer. Overall a great Hollywood experience! Would definitely stay here again.

I just returned from a long weekend for Easter in San Fran. While I had a fantastic time touring this amazing city, the hotel experience was AWFUL. First, I'm not one of those picky travelers who complains about anything and everything. I travel frequently, US, Europe, Africa, Carribbean but I've NEVER had this bad of an experience and rarely ever felt the need to get online to write a bad review. But this, I had to let people know.
First, just as the reviewer below me said - I also arrived late, and the hotel was dead. I had to wait a few minutes to see one front desk person show up finally. No bell person, nothing. As a single traveler, it definitely was the least welcoming hotel I've been to. I head up, and get into the room, it was just very plain and very dated. I was locked in from the inside!!! I couldn't believe it. I tried and tried, nothing. So I called the desk, they sent a bell guy up and I had to SLIDE the card through the door for him to open door!!
I'll make it short, because it really was incredulous. So they gave me another room: Change -.

So the guy says he has a great room with a better view of Union Square for me, and that the next morning, I should go up and get complimentary breakfast and ask for the manager, because he (the front desk guy) arranged for it personally. I just couldn't believe that all they offered me was lame breakfast!!!! for making me move three times in - days!!!!
UNBELIEVABLE. 
So, left with NO choice I moved AGAIN. The next morning, I decided to collect on my """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""complimentary breakfast"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I was impressed with the views from the restaurant and waited for the manager. She came, and after I told her the story, she had NO CLUE what I was on about!!!!! She said, do you remember the name fo the front desk person who told you you could have free breakfast??
I couldn't believe it. She had to make calls - and still no one at the front desk that morning knew what I was on about. No complaint note on my room, NOTHING.
So she says taht she's sorry, but she will have to put the breakfast on my tab until she can clear the story. !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Enough said. I was so humiliated and furious!!! The breakfast, btw was awful (found a hair on the french toast and pointed it out to the manager, she didnt even apologize or offer me anythign in exchange) and I got billed $-- for the buffet. I headed back downstairs and told front desk to find the guy who said I could have the free breakfast, and that this was really just absurd. They said they would, looking at me like I was crazy instead of apologizing for putting me through that.
I came back very late (because frankly I never wanted to even stay in my room, the rooms are SO dated and dreary). I went back to the front desk, and the actual assistant manager who had handled my complaint was there, and told another front desk guy to delete the charge from breakfast from my bill. BUT AT NO POINT did he even identify himself (I recognized him from the name tag), or apologize for NOT having told the breakfast manager, or ANYTHING. Just gave me such a snobby go-away look. And then they have the gall to ask if I wanted additional breakfast coupons!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
I'm going to end here. But suffice it to say, I will never ever ever stay at this hotel, or any other Grand Hyatt ever again. I am sure that if I were older and probably of another color, I would have received better treatment and definitely more than a free bkfast. At the very least, I should've been credited one night off my stay, for making me change rooms THREE times in - days and making me pay for a breakfast until they could figure out whether I had """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lied"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" about it. And this is a four star hotel???? I had to CHASE them down to take the bfast off my bil!!!! The only positive was the location, but as the other reviewer said, there were MANY hotels with that convenience. I had a fantastic time in the bay area, but the hotel DID put a damper on my stay - truly cold staff and cold dated rooms. Never ever again.

This was a pretty nice hotel for the price. The location (off of Sugar Creek) appeared to be in an unsafe area, but it was actually very quiet and I DID in fact feel safe. The staff was very nice and helpful. We were late checking out and they didn't even hassle us about leaving nor did they charge us for late check-out. The cleaning staff returned my boyfriend's cell phone to the office after he'd left it in the room once we'd left.

Stayed here for cinco de mayo weekend, the room was pretty pricey for what we got, the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Suite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" we got was one room and pretty small. All the furnishings looked (and smelled) old. The sink and vanity mirror was located in the bedroom which i found really strange. The bathroom had a sliding door which was fine except for the fact that it didn't close all the way and would slide open a little bit on its own. The tvs were very very small; had cable but half the channels didn't work and the ones that did were fuzzy and hard to see. Had free WiFi but the signal was too weak to use from our room. None of the windows opened so there is no way of getting fresh air. A few of the lights wouldn't turn on and the room was very dark after the sun went down. Its an alright hotel but maybe for an older crowd. We were there for a weekend of partying and didn't feel like that hotel offered what we were there for. Would have rather stayed at the Hilton or The Solamar; which both have nice pools.... The Sofia does not have a pool. Will not stay here again.

I made my mother a reservation to stay here a month ago based on the price and Tripadvisor reviews. She loved it. So when my husband and I needed a room on our way Indy, I made a reservation. Everything was great from the friendly check in to the great food at kick back and the pulsating shower heads. I will definitely stay here again when passing through.

We stayed here for two nights to see the Moto GP race at IMS. There were three of us, so we booked a two-room suite which was nothing glamourous, but certainly spacious, clean and comfortable. Lots of things were happening that weekend -- the race, the state fair, and the Gencon gamers convention so the hotel was completely sold out. Even full, we found it to be quiet and the staff working breakfast and happy hour were efficient and helpful.
The only thing that might stop me from choosing the Drury Inn again is it's location on the far northeast end of town. Downtown was a half hour, $--+ cab rideaway, and the Brickyard was just as far.

It took longer than expected to get on the road after a long ski trip, so we decided to find a hotel near Denver to spend the night. Since I'm a Hilton Gold member and had points to use, I found a Homewood Suites listed near the Denver airport. I used the website to book the room with my points, or so I thought. When I arrived at the hotel they told me that the rate was $--- per night for a - bedroom. I asked if they could simply change the reservation to points and the told me I'd need to go online to book it that way - was not happy. I mean really, do you not want me to use your loyalty program! I travel with business and stay mostly at Hilton properties. Over the last couple of years I've simply received no benifit from the Hilton Honors program. This property was a prime example. Avoid.

I chose the Sofitel for my recent stay in New York, based on its Trip Advisor popularity.
The hotel is new and the accomodations are pretty good. The staff was always pleasant, but not THAT efficient.
But several things were not as good as I would have expected.
Even though the bathroom was beautiful, the sink was cracked and THE SHOWER DID NOT DRAIN PROPERLY.
Their TV e-mail was slow and not user-friendly.
But the really unforgivable part was their phone system. They charged me $--,-- for a one minute call to Argentina (probably several hundred times their cost) and they also tried to charge me for several calls that had not been completed.
To make things worse, their phone system is set up so that I was unable to use a toll-free phone card I had. I got a busy signal every time I tried and wasted a lot of time trying. I stepped outside to a pay phone and got through immediately.
That is why my review is titled """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Highway robbery"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".
If I go to New York again, I will try another hotel.

I recently returned from another trip to New York City where I was treated as a visiting family member by Manager Jay Dean and his delightful staff. In particular, Ms. Patricia and Mr Jose at the Front Desk greeted me warmly and courteously. Without them I wouldn't have returned (I have been housing there for some ten years now). It was a great discovery--wonderful location, attentive staff, great management, clean, efficient, and interesting guests! The entire hotel (lobby, rooms, restaurants) have been remodeled. It is clean and well functioning. I met people in the hotel lobby which only increased my enjoyment of being in New York. The two new Asian restaurants flanking both sides of the hotel are a great treat and offer discounts to hotel guests. I enjoyed having the breakfast buffet at the hotel each morning, too. The concierge was cheerful and friendly. She assisted me to get around the city and its suburbs as well as provided me with great advice about where to go and what to do. As you may know, it is centrally located close to the theater district and restaurants. Taxis are plentiful and there is no better place to get on a subway in NY than where the hotel is located at W--th and Broadway. I travel often but this is the only hotel I look forward to returning each year. Great place, great people. I recommend it to everyone. It's a fantastic place to visit!

The view of the Bromo Selltzer Tower alone was worth the price of the room,but the wide screen TV,comfy bed,great shower presure and water temperature took care of the rest.The room heater - AC unit worked rather well and the elevator to an -th floor room did not keep me waiting for a long time.
Lobby was clean,business room was well equipped with computers for immediate use.
Parking area was safe,but $-- per night for a guest does have it's drawbacks.Close to the -st Mariner Arena,Camden Yards,Babe Ruth Museum and the Inner Harbor.
Gift Shop food and drink item pricing were fairly priced.
Front desk staff was very personable and helpful.Great suggestions for dining arrangements.
Housekeeping member on this floor was very obliging and a real pleasure to meet.

My wife and I stayed in a condo. Clearly, it was more room than we ever would need for the two of us, but it was a gift.
The hotel was amazing. Chicago is a great city, and you really can experience it while staying at the Trump, starting with a terrific view.
The rooms were large and open. The kitchen had all of the amenities, down to every utensil you can imagine. Beds were very comfortable, and you were offered every pillow imaginable.
Were given a tour of the rooms. We should have asked more about the lights, but otherwise he was very helpful.
All of the workers were very cordial, and constantly asking if we needed anything.
The health club was terrific, and the pool was very nice.
The location of the Trump is ideal for shopping on Michigan Avenue and State Street, and is surrounded by many terrific restaurants.
No real negatives. They probably could have had a whirlpool bath and bigger shower instead of three full baths in our condo. Also, though the living room furniture in contemporary, I really didn't find it overly comfortable, though I'm probably nitpicking.
I suggest parking across the street in the garage above the Dunkin' Donuts. It's convenient, and way cheaper than at the hotel itself.

This was our first trip to DC, and we didn't know where to stay, but based on other reviews, we thought this was a good choice, and we were right. 
The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was spacious enough for a --yo, --yo, plus Mom and Dad. Two tvs are always a plus. The free breakfast and evening snack-meals were always good (nothing spectacular), but very crowded. We used the washer and dryer to catch up on some laundry, but we had to wait a few times as there are only - of each. The hotel itself is nothing spectacular, but it's not old or ugly either. The beds were comfy and they provided plenty of pillows. Houeskeeping did a great job everyday cleaning up our mess. Nothing bad to say really, they exceeded my expectations. However, if you're visiting the sites in DC, use the bus, or Metro rail, your feet will thank you, as the hotel is - or - blocks away from everything.

I could not have been happier with my room in the North Tower on a high floor overlooking the beautiful marina. The weather was perfect while I was there. This was for a conference. It is adjacent to the conference center. It is walkable to many restaurants and sights. I would not hesitate to stay there again. The staff was excellent. Do not miss Cafe ---, a few blocks away for a wonderful breakfast! Also there is a Roy's Restaurant within the hotel which was a pleasant surprise.

My grown daughters and I stayed at the Renaissance from April -- thru April --,----. We loved it!! Perfect location if you want to be right in the middle of Times Square activities. The restaurant has an awesome view of Times Square and the food was very good. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Rooms were a nice size for New York with nice decor and very nice beds and linens.

My boyfriend and I stayed at The Mosser earlier this month and it was FANTASTIC! Yes the rooms are small but it has everything you need! We splurged for a room with a private bathroom but as we walked down the hall towards the elevator, we didn't see a huge line of people waitiing for the bathrooms so maybe next time we'll save a few bucks and share facilities. Adela the front desk clerk was friendly and answered all of our questions. We luckily had a great view of the Metreon and the fact that's it's close to great shopping--you just can't beat it! We'll gladly stay at The Mosser hotel again!

I just returned home after spending - nights at Hotel Five in Seattle. I loved the bright colors & funky decor, as well as the hardwood floors. The bathroom was spacious, with a rainhead shower & upgraded toiletries. I enjoyed the Keurig coffee-tea service & the bottled water replaced daily. The bed was just HEAVEN, with very nice linens. There is also a safe. The wi-fi worked perfectly during my visit. Housekeeping was very thorough. I had breakfast twice at Cafe Max downstairs & both meals were excellent. As others have mentioned, it's an easy walk down -th Ave. to go to the Westlake Center & the light rail to the airport, even with luggage. I had a room with the monorail outside my window and it didn't bother me, but others may want to ask for a room away from -th Ave. and the elevators. I will DEFINITELY return here on my next visit. =^..^=

We stayed at The Madison for two nights on a room on the --th floor. The room seemed newly redecorated and was lovely. The beds are soft with a large amount of pillows, so that you can really lay back in bed enjoying a good book. The coffee maker was really fancy (and the coffee tasted very nice). There were large, good mirrors and a nice work place with enough space for your laptop and for papers. The bathroom was delicate with thick, wonderful towells. There's a fitness room on the second floor which is open ---- and you get the Washington Post delivered outside your door each morning. A very good place to stay.

I have stayed at several hotels in San Diego and this is the only one I have stayed in that I have bothered to review. The rooms are a little small I think but very clean. The views are spectacular and the staff is great. I would definitely choose this hotel again. LOVE the pool!!!!

I'm not writing about a stay at the hotel but their """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""bait-n-switch"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" marketing tactics. What I'm talking about is their published """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Unlimited Golf Experience for Two from $---"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that has been in Golf Week Magazine for the past two months or so. Whenever I call to obtain that rate they are """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""always booked"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I get bogus replies from the operator staying that they """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""just booked -- reservations"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and that the $--- rate is no longer available but they can do this date at $--- (in the middle of August) or dates in Oct, Nov and Dec for $---. My question... when are the $--- dates available? Classic example of get the customer on the phone and try to get them to book at a much higher price. The $--- price is just not available. They minus well just say the rooms are free. Don't advertise something that is just not available.

Stay there for a night. Got a great deal on Hotwire. Check in was fast and the front desk people were very professional and very helpful. The room was spacious, well lit and clean; it was decorated in a modern style, and it had a separate area with a desk, great for working in the room. Two very comfortable beds, I would have rather had a king size, but I did not even try to ask for a change, since I was just there for the night. Very large bathroom with lots of handle bars for people with disabilities. However to get to the elevators you have to claim a few steps and I did not see a ramp or a different elevator, but I am sure there is access for wheelchairs, etc.
One strange thing, in the bathroom there is something like a closet and you will find there some hangers with night garments for sale (for males and females), which are animal print inspired, and some socks... I thought it was strange, but nothing wrong with that, just not what I expected to see in a hotel bathroom.
Did not check out the restaurant, but it seem quite busy even after -- pm. The hotel does not have big lobby. 
My room faced the inside (as in towards where the air conditioners units were located), which was fine with me, since I imagine you may get some street noise if your room faces the street. Dupont Circle Metro station is less than - minutes walk. So Location, Location, Location.
There was a mini bar, for which I did not asked for the key. And when I came home at night after going out, there was a jar of cookies, Oreo like, in the lobby which I thought it was a nice touch. I guess my only disappointing comment would be the fact that I would have liked a little coffee maker in the room. I believe they do have coffee in the lobby, I just did not check it out, since I was in a rush to leave the next morning. 
I liked this place, I recommend it and I would come back if I have a chance.

I recently had to travel to Baltimore to look at a boat I was planning to purchase. After looking at the available lodging, it appeared the Pier - hotel was the best location for my needs. As it turned out, I believe it is the best spot anywhere on the Inner Harbor. It is situated on the water next to the National Aquarium, and has two of the best places to eat right in the hotel.
The staff is very helpful and attentive, and the rooms are very nice. Security is very good and there is ample room in the lobby to work if you are traveling on business. Valet parking is reasonable and all the Inner Harbor attactions are a short walk away.

I stayed here -- years ago as a teenager and went back for the first time in June ----. We stayed for a week arriving on --------- and leaving on ---------. This hotel is old and has not had many updates however it did not bother me at all. To tell you the truth it would bother me if they gutted it and changed it. The place was built in ---- and the rooms are a bit small but it was no problem. There is a certain charm to this place. They still have the old skeleton key locks on the closet doors!!! The room doors are very good however and use the newest RFID cards to open them. You don't even need to insert the card. Inside the rooms, they are dated but just as clean as any other hotel I've been in. Loads of hot water. The staff at the front desk was very nice and gave me good advice about sightseeing. I used the WIFI every day and it always worked and worked very well. They had free post cards at the desk. Most important to me was that they are VERY bicycle friendly. They had no problem with us keeping our bikes in our room and moving through the lobby every morning and night with them. They even let us keep them in the lobby while we ate at their restaurant. This place is the cheapest you will find in downtown DC. You will never find a place in this price range as close to the monuments. At --th and E street you will be right in the heart of it all for a very low price. When I go back to DC it will be right here.

This was a Hampton Inn and I had stayed here before. Now is is filthy and disgusting!
Need I say more.

This hotel was the first hotel we stayed in on our - week holiday travelling down the coast of California & a - night stop in Las Vegas & it was perfect. Lovely room, great atmosphere & very helpful staff. Just round the corner from the old tram that takes you to the centre of San Francisco, walking distance of excellent restaurants (try the one just opposite, lovely food & staff) & hop on, hop off bus. San Francisco hotels are quite expensive but best price we found was with Hotels.com & also found a --% off voucher on the internet. Next stop was Monterey where we stayed at the Hotel Portola which was also very good & central & EVERYONE must go to Las Vegas once. It was amazing!!!!

I specifically chose this hotel because it was a Hilton and because of the location. I work out in the valley and normally stay in Valencia however I have come to like this hotel. It is close by the Universal City Walk (so so), and has the most excellent breakfast which if you are Hilton Gold or Diamond it is a great value.
