The bed was most comfortable and it hurts that we had to wake up early the next day to do some last minute shopping before going to the airport to catch our flight home. We could laze in the bed alllllll day!
Hotel is located in the shopping district and we were able to go shopping and come back to dropped our purchases before heading out again.
Although we had no issue on security nor see anyone loitering on our floor, I noticed there were no security guards posted on the side doors that can lead to the elevators so i may feel insecure if I am entering the hotel on my own late at night
Overall we had a good stay and my dad has already hinted that if we were to return to Seattle again (not likely in the near future given we had to fly for nearly - day to reach Seattle), he will like us to stay there again.

I stayed at this hotel for three nights with my Mother, and two daughters, four girls in the room with two double beds. We ended up on the --th floor which had a nice city view. I had booked another hotel, and switched at the last minute because the price difference was $---+. I am glad we switched because it was a huge savings and paid for all of our meals for three days. If you are sightseeing in NY, most likely you will not be spending any time in your room at all. We have two young children and were never back at the hotel before --:-- pm, then went straight to bed. The room is good-sized, bigger than most I would say, fit all four of us nicely. It was not state-of-the art, or plush. It was average, but substantial, clean and served its purpose. The bathroom vanity area was small, my biggest complaint. The carpets could use some updating. I usually like a fairly nice hotel (at least --- stars) but went with this one based on price. If you want a good deal, good location, and don't mind if it's not a plushy or trendy hotel, then this is a good place to stay. 
Also, we did the CitySightsNY Double-decker bus tour and loved it. It is a hop-on hop-off bus tour, and you have two days to use the bus. We saw almost all of the major sites in the city atop the bus, stopped at the places we wanted to see, and then hopped on the next bus. I would highly recommend that tour. Great way to see the city in a short amount of time.
We loved NY, can't wait to go back!

As an owner of a Hyatt vacation club property (Beaver Creek), I'm surprised at the quality of the service we received while at this resort since usually the HVC properties are superior.
There are many good things about this resort such as the lazy river, the hammocks by the river, the volleyball, lunch by the pool, etc. so it is a shame that the service level is so poor and can cause me to rate them so low.
Everything from staff shuffling furniture above my room (don't stay in ----), to the staff talking on their cell phones at the store (about his car problems to a friend, while ringing me up), to the cash register being proken at the store (can't buy anything), the staff at JB's restaurant took -- minutes to wait on us and there were only - people in the restaurant to the cleaning crew rolling the very noisey towel cart past my room every day at - am. There are a dozen other small things, but they all add up to poor service and I chalk that up to poor management. The staff is not adequate for the level of service you would expect from a resort, nor were they properly trained in """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hospitality"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".
If you are an owner, be prepared to lower your standard relative to what you get elsewhere at HVC, and if you are paying to stay here, I suggest the Hyatt Hill Country Resort down the street for a better experience and all the same amenities.

The size of the rooms can't be matched - the suites are huge. The location is terrific as the hotel is in the middle of the financial district. However, the rooms are getting quite worn and could do with some repairs.
Some other caveats:
- the fitness room was small and contained mostly broken equipment,
- the two guest elevators are tiny and slow beyond the worst that you can imagine (the situation is exacerbated when school groups are staying at the hotel and children are riding the elevators for fun, stopping at every floor),
- the TGIF can get rowdy after --pm, not the best place to take the kids if you arrive late.
The staff was friendly and the service was surprisingly good. A phone call for extra towels resulted in the towels being delivered less than -- minutes later. 
The mini-kitchen with microwave (popcorn included) was a nice surprise.
Definitely not a romantic getaway spot, but the roominess of the suites at the low price makes it a great choice for any other type of visit.

Enjoyed our - night stay at the Westin...even though the fire alarm went off during the night and the staff seemed disorganized. 
Room & bath, nicely appointed. Weather was nice while we were there, so really enjoyed the pool area. Also appreciated that the windows opened in the Room. You don't see that much now. 
Very convenient to Pedestrian area of downtown with many restaurants & shops. Had a great meal at Vesta's.
Parking lot is a bit cramped & dark and elevators to Westin hard to find..plus$-- a night extra.

Great location...steps from walk of fame, kodack theatre, etc. Very close and convenient to travel from here via subway to places such as Universal Studios-City. Free snack bar --hrs.... I think that amazingness speaks for itself. Very friendly staff who really know the area and what they are talking about. Heated pool...didn't test out the waters but enjoyed the portable heaters in the courtyard.

Stayed at Radisson for daughter's wedding weekend. Desk staff were very accommodating. Requested a room relocation after being located near service elevator due to noise and were moved immediately. Requested lake view room which is highly recommended. Great location in Austin on Cesar Chavez and Congress near many restaurants and hiking trail.

We selected the hotel largely based on tripadvisor reviews - it scores well. And it did not disappoint. High scores for location, easy valet and parking, excellent and friendly front desk and concierge team and a great vibe which was unexpected for a pretty large property. Check in had a boutique feel. Lower scores for a concierge who didn't know some of the cool places around town that tripadvisor as well as some basic google searches would come up with - but very friendly. Still i think a great concierge is one of the most valuable assets to the front desk especially in a foody town like SFO. Extras are expensive. Almost $- for a bottle of water in your room, $-- for wifi and it is per device so $-- for your laptop and phone for -- hours. Thay's just wrong! 
But let's go back to location. San Francisco is a great city - and with the hills and streets some places are just naturally better starting points than others. This hotel is exactly where you would want to be. BART outside, you are right at the key point for shopping and Union Square and the trolleys are at your doorstep. As a home base and you want really (absolutely) nice sheets but happy with something fairly basic but truly well run and rather hip, this is a great place. Advice to get a higher room because of street noise was absolutely accurate. It's a buzzing part of town - so go higher. You'll love the view too.

Stayed here for a pre-flight overnight. The rooms are modern and clean - no complaints about the quality of the room, friendliness of the staff, etc. The doors to the rooms are nasty brown painted old steel doors that speak of a by-gone days but the rooms beyond are nice. There are just a few things that could be addressed. Firstly, the smoking area should be moved to a side entrance or somewhere other than directly in front of the hotel. To enter one must pass an army of lounging smokers and the smoke enters the lobby through the automatic doors. Then... lose the ---- style ATM that is right next to the front desk. For the price this is a decent, clean place to stay for a night or two.

Good hotel, good location. Tough to find street parking but possible. Don't park right across from hotel where homeless village set up.
Hotel charges $-- for parking. Big rip off!

The Mayfair Hotel is a great hotel. Very good location. Right in the heart of times square. The bathroom is ok. Not as good as most hotels in the city. Bathrooms are old. The shower can only really fit one person not two. If your there for your hunnemoon, I would not recomened it. If your there as a tourist looking for a good hotel buy to check out NYC, and have a good holiday weekends. Sure buy this hotel. The bathrooms are not dirty at all, there very clean. Ask for a room in the back of the hotel, facing into the alley. Very quiet. If you a room in the front it faces Times Square , noisy for most people. 
The best broadway show is always at the theatre next door. It changes monthy. Tickets are pretty easy to get. I got mine cheap out side. Before the show. I had nothing to do so I saw the show. Its one of the best places to see a broadway show the theatre is pretty big. I go to NYC all the time. my uncle lives in the Village. I would highly recomend this to tourists, for a hotel, good for weekends, not for couples.
Hilton, Millamum down near the convention center is ausome. Hilton honors gets you alot of discounts. That's my number two hotel.
This would not be the hotel for a family of four just for two people. Most of the beds are single, no doubles.

Friendly staff greeted us at the door. Pleasant staff everywhere. Bell boys are very helpful. Room was spotless and comfortable and roomy. I'm sure we got an upgrade because I mentioned (when I called the morning of our arrival from hours away) it was our anniversary. Good location - close to lots of downtown (Loop, Near North) hot spots. The El might be annoying, but you can ask when you call the hotel to see if your room can be located away from the front of the building. We would definitely stay here again.

Great location. Front desk staff were helpful. Other staff appeared bored, uninterested or irritated. The room smelled like it must have been a smoking room in the past. They need to either paint or change the carpet or the hvac system to get rid of the lingering smell. The room temp was ok but it was very humid. All of our clothes and bedding were just damp all the time. Not a fan of the rain shower as it didn't provide much water pressure. We were only in the city for - nights and the location was what we needed so we tolerated the hotel. I probably won't recommend it to others.

This was my first visit to San Diego and enjoyed it very much. We chose the embassy suites because of it's location and good reviews. This hotel is in the perfect location if you really want to see the city. Gas lamp, Horton Mall, USS Midway and just about all city attractions are with in minutes walk. The hotel room did show some wear but found it to be ultra clean, the bed was extremely comfortable and the breakfast was very good as well with many choices to choose from. The service was good and concierge went above and beyond to help us through the city. The only thing to be aware of is a room on the north east corner of this hotel, at --:--, --:--, -:--, and -:-- AM the Coaster and Amtrak start blasting horns at a crossing street level behind this section of the building. I know this is not the hotels problem but unfortunately these are the cheaper city view rooms, guess you get what you pay for ! Do not let this scare you away from this hotel because the trolley and trains run throughout the city, just be aware when booking a room and where these lines run. I did not complain and I'm sure they would have moved us if I did, good thing I packed my earplugs !

Stayed for - nights and from arrival to departure we couldn't have asked for more. The hotel is located in a beautiful building and has a very welcoming and relaxing vibe with nothing too much trouble for any of the friendly & courteous staff. The hotel decor is contemporary and the lounge areas have a warm ambience and are perfect to sit back and watch the world go by. We have stayed in many areas of New York and would regard this hotel and location as the best hands down and wouldn't stay anywhere else when visiting New York. I had mentioned it was our anniversary and some cute cupcakes accompanied by a card were left in our room and I must say a huge thank-you to Gerald Telliz the W Hotels Guest Services Coach who really made our stay a special one.

First of all, the hotel itself is beautifully decorated. The eclectic decor is vibrant, fun, and interesting which lends the entire property an the air of an adventurous hideaway. The hotel staff is kind, helpful, attentive, efficient, and generally great. The rooms are spacious, clean, modern, well-decorated, and incredibly comfortable. I cannot say enough about what a great stay we had. This will be my go-to hotel in San Francisco from now on.

My husband and I live in NY and were without power during Hurricane Sandy and discovered that the Westin was offering free Wifi, power strips to access outlets to recharge and movies to entertain kids in a couple of their conference rooms. And access to their always clean bathrooms! The hotel didn't have any vacancies but this was the next best thing. They made a very hard situation much more tolerable and we were incredibly thankful for their generosity.

I recently stayed with Ace Hotel and had a AWESOME experience. The location was very convenient, only a couple blocks to the subway. The hotel was absolute perfection. The staff was very friendly and the the decor of the hotel was brand new, trendy, and so intriguing down to the very last detail. The rooms were very spacious and spotless. Each room was outfitted with flat screen tv's and decorative items that sparked conversation and down right jealousy of its modern appeal. I would love to have the interior designing crew who decorated this hotel to come to my house. They also have a hip bar on the first floor where the local socialites mingle with the common folk like me visiting for the weekend. I hear a new coffee bar is opening up this week I am sad I missed it, but am planning on coming back for a stay when their new restaurant opens up.

I liked almost everything about this modern, immaculate hotel. The room was spacious and clean. Service was fantastic, the staff was friendly and responsive. When I arrived, there was no ironing board- I think one was delivered within - minutes of my call! 
Affordable breakfast could be found in their little coffee shop off the lobby area, a terrific breakfast buffet was available if you had the time and interest.
 A beautiful roof-top pool is available for those so inclined. The fitness center was large and very well equipped. 
Best of all, it's a pleasant walk along the River Walk to the restaurant district. 
Only downside: they could have installed better windows- the sound proofing not so great. I was on the --th floor and could hear street traffic fairly clearly.

As other reviews have noted, this hotel is in an odd location, wedged between buildings fronting Market Street. The exterior of the building itself is uninspiring. But while auto access is somewhat awkward, the hotel is perfectly located for pedestrians to get to Union Square, the Financial District, and Yerba Buena Gardens, all within just a few feet of the hotel's front door. I stay in the city often on business, and the views from the lower floors of this hotel are not as good as those from The Ritz Carlton, The Fairmont or The Mandarin Oriental, all in the same class of hotel. Despite this drawback, which to me is minor but may be important to others, The Four Seasons is without doubt one of the top - best hotels in the city. The service is fabulous, the food terrific, and the location for walking where most travelers want to go can't be beat. It is without doubt on the pricey side (for instance: - beers, a glass of red wine and one small filet mignon (a la carte) was $--- -- reminds me of Tokyo, but I suppose Tokyo would be even more expensive). However, in this class the room rate itself is quite reasonable, and unlike other hotels, guests may use the four story Sports Club-LA (in the same building, with its own entrance for hotel guests) for free. Other hotels have no such amenity attached, and if they send you to one of the upper end health clubs, there is a day pass charge. So, bottom line, stay there, work out at Sports Club, have a drink, but eat elsewhere and I think you will enjoy your stay.

The Westin Market Street is a very nice 'upmarket' hotel in an excellent location in San Francisco - a quick walk to Union Square and public transport on Mraket Street to just about anywhere
We ( family of - adults + - kids, - and --) had a large, bright and very clean room - on the -th floor I think - and the beds were wonderfully comfortable. Bathroom was a little dark, but spotless and we had a bath , which was nice for the little one.
Check-in was smooth and the girl at the desk who dealt with us was extremely pleasant, as were all of the staff we met there, including in the restaurant. This was a pleasant surprise given some of the remarks made on this site.
We didn't have breakfast at the hotel - Starbucks is just up the street if all you want is a coffee and pastry- but we did have a very good , if rather expensive, meal at """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Ducca"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".
My only complaint would be that our room was right next to the service elevators that rumbled noisily up and down late at night and early in the morning. I presume that our room allocation was due to the fact that we had got an absolutely fantastic rate on Expedia, which I imagine gives the hotel some scope to allocate better -placed rooms to those paying the full whack.
All in all our stay was very pleasant, and if we're ever back in SF ( it's a long way from France!) and get a similar deal, then I'd stay there again.

I live in L.A. so I stay at the standard a few times a year.
I usually rent a room there because I know I'm going to end up drinking on the rooftop bar (which is superb, especially on a warm summer night!) 
The crowd is always cool, international and local.
The music is great, the dance floor is small but perfect, and I just love the atmosphere at the standard.
No complaints!!
The rooms are spacious, contemporary, and clean.
you will definitely get a good night sleep if you rent a room at the standard..
Highly recommend...

Attended a conference at Squaw Peak. Room was adequate but not the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""awesome"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" place other reviews indicated. There was no wireless internet avaialbe in the rooms and wired internet was pricy - totally absurd for ----! There was also a charge to use the business center. The room was nice but not worth the price. Dust was on everything in the room. The balcony was a joke and barely large enough for the - chairs and small table - not enough room to comfortably sit. Use of the on-site fitness center was an additional charge ($---visit). Staff at Rico's restaurant on site was rude and non-accomodating. Glad I was not paying.

the best western hotel is a good hotel cause when i was away me and my family were just a couple of minutes from a good place for macys parade.
the hotel is good the staff are nice and the staff at reception are very helpful and it would be good if they had a food bit were u got food. 
the room i was in u could see a little of time square and u dont get a good sleep but apart from that thats it.
AND A BIG THANKS TO THE BAG PERSON HE WAS SO HELPFUL TO LOAD OF PEOPLE THANKS YOUR THE BEST...

The breakfast staff at this hotel was phenomenal! When I asked whether there were gluten-free breakfast options for my teen daughter who has Celiac Disease, Martyn, Iris, Dennis, and Steven kicked into high gear and actually shopped off-site to provide her with gluten-free waffles. They researched whether the bacon they had on site was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""safe"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for her, and had her piping hot breakfast waiting each morning. The hotel concierge was also incredibly helpful -- he researched local restaurants to find gluten-free options that weren't already on my list. We visit Manhattan once or twice a year and will definitely stay at Hampton Inn Manhattan Times Square North again.

We booked this hotel because it was about $-- cheaper than the hotels closer to Times Square. It was clean and the rooms were very comfortable. Not much, if any, view. Everything from internet to the fridge had prices attached, so we didn't touch anything. I would probably stay there again, but liked the NYC Hilton better.

Stayed at the Bryant Park for a week as a tourist and thought this was one of the best hotels I've ever stayed in. The staff were incredibly helpful and welcoming, the front rooms are spacious and have a phenomenal view of Bryant Park and the location is perfect for visiting Manhattan.
The nice touches really made the stay, from the luxurious bath and shower to the incredibly helpful concierge - entertainment planners (thanks Marco!) who recommended genuinely great places to go every day.
The only thing I didn't like was the internet in the room - the in-built browser is a bit old so to check emails we had to use a kiosk a couple of doors down.
I doubt the feel of the hotel would suit all - it feels like a very trendy bar - but as a young couple staying in NYC for the first time it was perfect and next time I'm in New York (business or pleasure) I'll definitely stay here.

What struck me most about our recent stay at this fine hotel was how accommodating and friendly the staff were. While calling to confirm our reservations and inform the front desk of a late-night check-in, we were offered a complimentary upgrade to an Executive King corner room. When we declined the offer for a rollaway bed for our -- year old, they offered us complimentary parking for - nights. When we requested assistance, we were met with prompt and courteous service. The location is great, the property is nicely maintained, and the room was excellent.

Great location, just a few doors down from Chinatown entrance and a short walk to Union Square. Nice and quiet rooms, very comfortable beds, nice furniture and appliances. Tea-coffee maker included. Staff was very friendly and relaxed. Great price for what you're getting! Would return!

We stayed here for four night on vacation. The hotel is beautiful, and the service is great. Yes, the rooms are a little small, but I love historical buildings and I love what they have done to preserve this amazing building. The Polar Bar was awesome, and the lounge is beautiful. Juno the restaurant in the hotel was pretty good as well, especially for breakfast. The bar menu is very good. We will definitely go back. The only problem we had was the heater in our room was quite noisy. We didn't say anything because we didn't want to change rooms. I'm sure if we would have we would have been accomadated.

I came over to Chicago for a mother-daughter week-end with my daughter. My husband is a Diamond Hilton member, and staying at a Hilton property is a high priority when I choose a hotel property. The Conrad appeared to meet all my requirements prior to staying there, such as location, breakfast, work out facitilty, and parking. 
We parked directly across the street which saved a money. I fell in love with the location of the Conrad being on North Michigan, mere steps away from Nordstrom, plus other shopping retailers. We had a incredible amount of resturants to choose from for dinner. 
Upon check-in we were upgraded into a Junior Suite with a view. The living room was large including a dining room table. The bathroom was unbelievable. I think my daughter took three baths in two days. The hotel will bring up special oils and salts to make your bath more relaxing. There is a menu of services provided for taking a bath. The bed was comfortable and the bedding was inviting. The best part of bed time was being able to order a special pillow that would allow your night's sleep to be the comfortable as possible. My daughter ordered the body pillow and still would like one to this day. 
We did not bring our dogs to the Conrad; we loved the fact the Conrad allows dogs. The Conrad makes your dog's stay at the Conrad as memorable as his or her owners. Offering services such as dog walking, dog day care, dog beds, dog """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""special"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" food, dog spa. 
Since we ate a late lunch we opted for room service later in the evening. It took about -- minutes, which I thought was slow. We were not hungry and time was not an issue. The cruisine looked as if a pastry chef had made it and sent it right up to our room. It was expensive, but I was excepting a high tab. For one coffee, one hot tea, and two cheesecakes the tab was $--.--. 
I didn't mind the expensive room service bill since I was able to look out and see excitment of the city, the beauty of Lake Michigan and grandure of Navy Pier. We wanted to enjoy the luxury of our suite, the view, the relaxing baths, and a perfect night sleep with our """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""special"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" pillows. It was like we had a vacation within our vacation at the Conrad. I would strongly encourage if staying in the city over the week end or a period of time to spend the extra money and upgrade into a suite. I stayed at the Hilton on South Michigan and would choose the Conrad not for the locations, but the amenties, and the staff.
The only down side, which happens at every hotel you stay at downtown if it be in Chicago or New York is the noise of the city. I have found no matter the price of a room, it is unavoidable that one will hear the noise from the city below.
The Conrad exceeded my expectation from the staff treating us like royalty, to the extra touches of the pillows to the best location on Michigan Avenue. Without a doubt or hestitation I will stay at the Conrad again.

We used this hotel and location for our honeymoon. We couldn't of asked for a nicer hotel and location if we had tried. 
It's situated - blocks from Central Park on --th Street and literally - - -- minutes walk away from the hustle and bustle of Time Square. There is a also a subway station at both ends of the block for easy access to Lower Manhattan. This is an easy and cheap way of getting around - $-.-- for unlimited travel a day!
The hotel itself if served by pleasant and helpful staff who attend to your every need should you ask, the rooms are immaculate - every day and the breakfast provided for $- each ample for the New York explorer. 
Things you must do while in New York:
Liberty
Rockefeller Building
Empire State 
Toys R Us - Time Square - jaw dropping!!!
Broadway
Macy's for your shopping and don't forget to ask for a discount card to get --% off!
Ground Zero and Financial district
Staten Island Ferry - Its free and great views of Liberty and Manhattan. 
Central Park on a Sunday - with the New Yorkers.
Overall a fantastic hotel in a fantastic city. Enjoy!

I stayed at this property for - nights during a business meeeting. As a lifetime platinum member, I was given an upgraded room in the south tower with a terrific view of the harbor. 
The concierge lounge is located on the --th floor of the south tower. The lounge has terrific views of SD harbor and is a nice place to sit and watch the boats go by! Lounge has a Starbucks coffee machine so you can make your own, fresh, high test which is great for the jet lagged. Breakfast in the lounge is very nice and eggs-sausage-bacon are always offered along with the usual continental fare. Evening snacks in the lounge are pretty sparse compared to other Marriotts. When I was there, it was usually soup and a salad.
The rooms are newly renovated, very clean, and very accomodating for a business traveller. Mattress is very comfortable and there was a refrigerator built in to the dresser. The walk in shower was huge. 
This hotel is directly connected to the convention center and if you stay here, you can expect to be with at least one group. There are - Starbucks, a shipping facility, and a gift shop in the lobby area. The new Market Marina restaurant is excellent and I had lunch there twice - what a refreshing change for a hotel restaurant! 
Outside pool-whirlpool are beautiful but I did not have time to enjoy these due to business meetings.
The location is very convenient to downtown and to the seaport area which is accessed from the back of the property along a very nice walking path
This hotel offers less perks than most to Marriott Platinum members. I was given a coupon for --% off a Starbucks beverage and while I appreciate this, it seems the hotel could do a bit more for someone who stays -- nites-year at Marriotts and is a Lifetime Platinum member.
Nice hotel, but too many kids for a 'spa' feel. Would have been nice if the lap pool was not a kiddie play area. The rooms are nice and very modern.

We stayed in a bunk room for - nights. The room was small (as expected) but very clean, there was a small basin in the room for shaving-washing and there was always a shared bathroom available. The shared bathrooms were generally very clean, and all had very good showers. I did on one occasion see a cockroach in one of the bathrooms, but i think this was an isolated thing. There was no way to make tea or coffee in the room (guess to keep cost down) but there is a coke machine in the lobby. There was also a cool roof garden. They also provide free wifi which is a nice bonus and an Ipod docking stereo.
The hotel was in a very good location, we could easily walk to times square and there was a subway station about - blocks away.
Downsides to the hotel, one of the lifts was out of service and the remaining two lifts were very slow to respond. There didn't seem to be a freight lift, so in the morning the staff use one of the lifts to move the linen up and down, so it can take a while to get out if you are on a higher floor!

We stayed at the Affinia Chicago for a special girls only trip to Chicago (with my mom, me and my daughter). What a fantastic hotel! The location is GREAT - just off of Michigan Avenue - and within walking distance to many attractions (the American Girl Store, Hancock Tower, Watertower, etc.) The staff was so helpful - giving tips on what to do (despite not ideal weather) and ideas on how to best get around town. In addition, the hotel has a free shuttle to-from Navy Pier. Our stay there far exceeded my expectations. I'd stay there again in a heartbeat! We had a junior suite - and it had more room than I've ever had at a hotel. I give Affinia Chicago a big two thumbs up!

This was my first trip to Seattle and I was traveling alone after a conference in Portland, Or. I found the hotel's location perfect for my purposes...very close to shopping areas and main attractions yet in a quiet, neighborhood section. The hotel's decor was understated elegance, comfortable, and very clean. The staff was excellent, always helpful and polite. One staff member, Mary, who was at the front desk and concierge desk went out of her way to be thoughtful and considerate. How nice to have someone remember your name and ask how your day's adventure went when you returned in the evening. Finally, what I loved was the mix of guests staying there at that time from families with young children to couples of all ages. I wouldn't want to stay anywhere else next time I return to Seattle.

I liked everything about this hotel. The staff were friendly and well-presented and professional.
I didn't eat at the restaurant, but I ate a nice breakfast to start each day in the restaurant area. I truly appreciated the Hi-speed wif-fi in my room, and the nice pool area. 
Nice rooms, and I also loved the dishwasher, cook top and full-sized refridgerator.
Everything about this hotel made my business stay easy and efficient.
Definitely stay there again, and recommend it for business or pleasure.

I have to say I've never felt more at home like the way I felt at Park South Hotel. The hotel as the business is perfect, exactly what you would like on a hotel. But you have to mention the staff. They make the hotel a great place to be. Demian, Rachel, Cat, Diana and everyone else. Thank you for making New York better than it already is.

The best feature was being literally across the street from Minute Maid Park. We were in town to see the Dodgers play the Astros for a weekend series, and this hotel was ideal for this purpose. Room was big and comfortable. The room service breakfast was quite good and not terribly overpriced. Only downside, and this is relatively minor, is that there was no """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sleep"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" button on the remote control.

The doubletree offered us a special deal including drinks, breakfast, and fourteen days of parking when we used it the night before our fourteen day cruise to Hawaii. They also had a free shuttle service to and from the port, but make sure you put your name in for it as soon as you get there, it books up fast. The breakfast was not very good, I have gotten better breakfasts at Best Westerns than here, but you can't beat the location, view, or ambiance of this hotel.

Wow!! What an incredible experience..Arrived Thursday the hotel was already jumpin'. After a very efficient check in we took a quick swim in the rooftop pool and enjoyed a steam in the spa before we headed to Ono, the restaurant situated within the hotel. I just recently returned from a weekend trip to Chicago with a few buddies of mine. We stayed at the Marriott Chicago-Magnificent Mile. It was a - day, - night trip:
Rooms: I have done a bunch of travel in the last couple of years and have stayed at many different types of hotels-resorts and different chains. At this Marriott, I thought that the beds in the rooms were some of the most comfortable that I have ever slept on. The pillows were extremely comfortable as well as the bed itself and the light featherbed that was on it. I have been told my other people that all Marriott beds are like this, but all I know is that the beds at this Marriott were extremely comfortable. The rooms contained an ironing board, Iron, Bath and Body Works Shampoo and Conditioner, plenty of towels, with a flat screen TV, small table and chairs, and high speed internet (available for a small fee). The room itself was not extremely big but had a decent view of the city. (I heard some rooms, the view is not so good!) The carpets and bathroom was clean which is always nice. The hallways were also quiet at night which was a plus.
Lobby: We stayed at this Marriott over the weekend and the lobby and lobby bar were extremely busy. The lobby is an open space with lots of tables and couches for you to sit on, relax, and have a cocktail before heading out to the city for the night. The prices were reasonable for service at the bar. It was a very nice lobby experience. Also in the lobby was the bell desk, front desk, and the concierge which was very helpful in finding nearby restaurants and bars.
Location: This hotel I believe is in a great location. It is right on Michigan Avenue in the heart of the “loop.” (I hope that is what the immediate downtown is called.) It is very close to “ Rush St. ” and all of the hotspots of downtown. There is great shopping close as well as many great restaurants within walking distance. At the hotel, we valet parked our car with the hotel and never once removed it from the garage as we could walk anywhere we wanted to go or just take a short cab ride.
Service: Check in was extremely quick. All we needed to do was give our last name and our reservation was pulled up. The staff was quick to have our bags brought upstairs and tell us where all of the amenities of the hotel were such as gift-sundry shop, pool, coffee bar, lobby bar etc.. The concierge located in the lobby was very helpful with making reservations and providing lists of nearby restaurants broken down by type of food and location. Finally, the valet and bellmen at the front entrance were very quick to hail us a cab, or to help us go in any direction that we needed.
Pool: There is a pool located on the -th floor (I think) but we did see or go in it.
Overall, Our stay at the Marriott was great and provided a great “home base” to go and do whatever we wanted to do that night in Chicago . I would recommend this hotel to friends and family and would stay there again if I was to once again, visit the Windy City .

The hotel website mentions that the hotel had been refurbished however they must have forgot to do the bathroom, it was smelly, looked like it hadn't been refurbed since ----'s. Sanitary ware was stained and cracked however the water was always hot. The corridors smelt of food! I found like other reviewers that the housekeeping carts and wastebins were always in the corridor close to the lift and fire exit (I saw this on at least - floors) - could this be a hazard if an emergency evacuation were required? 
Unlike other hotels there did not appear to be any literature in the room explaining about the hotel or it's services. Other than location I would not recommend this hotel.

The hotel is in a great location, rooms are definitely ready at -pm, not earlier. The staff was courteous. We were travelling with our -- and -- year old daughters, we stayed in a - bedroom suite, primarily because it had to full bathrooms. We decided it was more economical to stay in the - bedroom suite with a pull out couch for our daughters than to rent two rooms. The space was fine but the sofa bed was really uncomfortable. I'd probably stay at this hotel again but would not subject our daughters to the sofa bed. The only issue I had with our room was that it always felt a little too warm, and VERY humid. In fairness to the hotel, I never called them to complain, we just weren't in the room that much. Having the kitchenette area was handy, grocery store close by so we were able to eat breakfast in our room each morning. We avoided the slow elevators by using the service elevators which were not fancy but were quick! We also did not have any view whatsoever, our windows faced the interior of the building, brick walls, so there was no natural light in our room at all.

My partner and I had an opportunity to visit NYC for a weekend of play and leisure and the W Union Square was a perfect place for us. From the moment we stepped up to the Welcome Desk, Temara greeted with a sense of professional playfulness that is signature to the brand. Our room was bright and beautifully appointed. The bar was fun, concierge super helpful, and room service fantastic. I can't wait to return!

After travelling in from San Francisco, and delayed by a few hours, it wasn't until just gone midnight that I got to the Hotel on Rivington. The party scene was downstairs, but a doorman spotted me straight away, took my luggage for me and then up to the lobby on the second floor. 
Check in was smooth and problem free, and I was given a room on the --th Floor. With floor to ceiling windows, looking south, I had an amazing view, which only got better the next morning when the weather cleared up. 
A huge king bed with a Tempur Mattress was in the bedroom area, and there was a well stocked mini bar, desk, sofa and table, and plenty of closet space. I couldn't have asked for more!
The bathroom was huge, and in all my years travelling, I've never had the bonus of a bathroom with a window, so an opening window next to the shower, and being able to admire the view was just out of this world.
Cookies on turndown are a nice touch, and also not having to request the turndown service, it is automatic is even better. Free Wireless internet really makes a difference, I still don't get why some hotels charge! 
So, onto the bed. First time I've slept on a Tempur Mattress, and it was just amazing. First morning I woke up, I didn't want to leave. Onto that mini bar. Not really overpriced when compared to a bar price, but over priced if you compare it to a store. Plenty of space to put your own things in the mini bar too, so you can buy things locally to stock it up a bit more. The bathroom had both the shower with a view, and a huge japanese style soaking tub. Yeah, it takes a long time to fill up, but it's worth it just for the relaxation after a long day pounding the Manhattan streets. 
The floor to ceiling windows were amazing, and also I had a small balcony to walk out onto, maybe not the best in March, but perfect for taking some amazing photos of the view. The only annoyance with the room, (which I did get used to within a day), was that even though you had a black out curtain to block out the light from the main window, there was a frosted window in the bedroom to the shower area, which then, when it hit morning, let light into the room from the bathroom windows. The first night it annoyed me, and I found it bizarre, but then the second night it didn't bother me in the slightest.
The hotel itself is great, the location in the Lower East Side is great for exploring the nearby area, East Village, Greenwich Village, and up to Union Square, all really within walking distance, plus you have a few subway lines around the corner to hop on and get you into Midtown for the normal NYC sightseeing. If you're thinking this hotel is too far away from the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""centre"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" you must remember that NYC isn't a theme park, and the Subway will take you where you need to be, cheaply, and quickly. 
I can wholeheartedly recommend this hotel for a stay in NYC, especially if you can get a bargain rate, which then makes it more worthwhile.

After trawling through countless hotels when arranging our trip to New York I stumbled upon the Elysee and boy am I glad I did. Taking advantage of the pre-pay offer I booked three nights for under £---! Ok, so this only buys a slightly noisy low-floor room – use earplugs – but man what a room.
By New York standards the room was huge, featuring a lobby area with the bedroom off to one side and the bathroom the other. All were spotless and furnished in keeping wit the hotel's aim of seeming like a country b&b in the city.
On top of this a continental buffet breakfast was included and free cheese and wine between -pm--pm on weekdays!
The staff also deserve a mention, always ready to help and incredibly polite without been overbearing. A credit to the hotel.
When we return to New York we will be staying at the Elysee.

I was worried when I """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""won"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" a room at this hotel on Hotwire; however, the hotel surpassed my expectations. I stayed on the -th floor and my room was clean, quiet and updated. As others have attested, the location is great. You can easily walk to Beacon Hill, the North End, Faneuil Hall, the Public Gardens, the Esplanade at the Charles River and many other places. The MBTA (red line) is also close by, which will take you almost anywhere in Boston. For the price I paid, I was satisfied. The hotel really deserves a higher rating on Trip Advisor. It is not on par with The Liberty by any means but it is a solid - star hotel.

The hotel is worth the rooftop pool experience. This wouldn't keep me coming back (pool is a little underwhelming) but the view was great. Frida nights after an Astros home game is perfect. You'll have the best seat in the city for the fireworks display. 
The rooms were nice and comfortable but nothing spectacular. You're also in a downtown setting so the area around the hotel can be somewhat sketchy after dark. The hotel only offers valet so you don't have to worry about walking to your vehicle in a secluded area which is nice. 
My only watch out would be the hidden fees. Expect an additional fifty bucks in taxes and parking.

This was my second visit from UK to New York with my wife and did a fair amount of research prior to our visit. The Hampton Inn Soho had favorable reviews and after staying there I can see why. 
The most commendable aspect of the hotel was the endearing and friendly nature of all the hotel staff, we arrived early prior to -pm but lobby staff allowed us to bag drop whilst my wife and I explored the immediate area which is profoundly different from mid-town where we stayed last time in New York. The area is quieter less in your face and very chic. There is an abundance of bars and restaurants to suit every taste and budget. When we arrived back in the hotel the room was ready as promised, when in the room it was spacious, airy and very clean.
 The size of the room was bigger than expected and compared well to Flatotel where we stayed on our previous visit. The wifi signal was good and allowed us to stay in touch with our daughter back in UK (who declined to come due to the extensive walking that she may have to endure!), and this made a huge contribution to enjoying our stay.
Every time we entered or left the hotel the staff were courteous and always willing to assist. On our last day of our visit lobby staff allowed us to store our luggage whilst we made the most of our remaining hours, they also arranged for a private cab to the airport which arrived bang on time - I would highly recommend this service as opposed to hailing a cab and only $- more to JFK. My wife's main impression was the quality of the bed and bedding as she is a fussy sleeper - she said it was the best sleep she had had in a long while - so much so she wanted to change the pillows in our own bed to replicate the ones in the Hampton Inn!
I'd like to take this opportunity to thank ALL the Hampton Inn staff for making our stay a trip to remember and keep up the excellent service!

My husband & I completely enjoyed this hotel as it met with what was expected.
Yes as other reviews and the person that recommended this hotel to me said - the rooms are small and the bathrooms are really small. It is an old building. If I am recalling correctly it was a bathhouse at one point in its history.
The location is fantastic. A few blocks off of Union Square and cable car lines. Buses right out front that are -- to -- minutes to the Ferry Building. It was very easy to get anywhere we planned to go. It is in a slightly noisy area which doesn't bother us but may be a it much for some.
Cleanliness - Mostly very clean but it is about time for a deep cleaning. Dust build up here & there and the building has the distinct old building smell. 
Staff - Friendly and helpful. Sometimes they didn't give us the correct info though.(ie: sending us to a Tix place on Union Square to buy our transit passes on a Monday and it is closed on Mondays). Lots of maps and guidebook-tour info available. 
The sum of this being: For the price you cant beat it if you can let a few little things go.

I never write reviews but my experince at Hotel Palomar was so good I had to write about it. The staff at the front desk was extremely helpful, especially Nika. She gave me advice on what to do during my stay and even sent wine and chocolates up to our room. I will definitely be visiting again!

Looks old on the outside but rooms are tidy and clean, even modern for the age of the building. Great location. Close to shops, drug store, walk of fame. Car parking out back. BUT. forget the breakfast, its a twinkie and a glass of Tang..but still, good value for money.

My husband and I celebrated our -- year anniversary at the Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers. 
Danita Harth-Bates, CEO, was wonderful wonderful wonderful! I received a confirmation email before our trip, asking if they needed to know anything before we arrived. I emailed Ms. Harth-Bates telling her it was our -- year anniversary. We had champagne and strawberries (each dipped in a different coating) delivered to our room. I can't say a single thing that was wrong with our stay. Our room was great. Our view was great. 
I highly recommend staying at this hotel. Everyone was pleasant. The check in lady wished a happy anniversary. The food was great. The service was impeccable. 
Thank you Ms. Harth-Bates for making our stay memorable.

I found the Westin Indianapolis to be pretty much down the middle Westin quality. Nothing extrordinary, nothing awful either. Just normal. Checkin was efficient, I got a room of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""preferred floor"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which was fairly large and clean. Broadband worked. Bathroom wasn't top-notch but was clean and I didn't see any of the problems others have reported. Some idiot spent -- minutes trying to get his key to work in my door at midnight, but I can't blame the hotel for that. Housekeeping was really agressive the morning of my departure. I was surprised that the hotel doesn't print lists of which rooms to clean in which order. Usually hotles like Westin wait to clean the rooms of departing guests until they've checked out. Dinner at Schula's, by myself and a bit late, was fine. I didn't have any problems with smoke, and was happy to find a nice half bottle of Pinot Noir, which was just what I needed. Avoid the valet parking and pull into the public lot that's right next door. There is a direct connection to the hotel.

Stayed at the Doubletree with husband and two adult kids. Great location, right on times square. Room was perfect. Son slept on pull out couch and we had two beds in bedroom. Staff was very helpful and courteous. Highly recommend.
Fre WIFI in lobby, but would have been nice to have in the room for free. There was a fee and we didn't bother. Perfect location for the two Broadway shows we saw. Memphis and Mary Poppins were fantastic!! We also took the subway which was convenient to the hotel and went to a Yankees Game. The hotel was a little pricey, but its New York!

I went to the RSNA medical congress last December and stayed at the Allerton for about - nights. 
The hotel was disappointing on arrival, nothing at all like a --star hotel.
All my colleagues were complaining about the size of their rooms, I was ok since I was alone.
On the first night, the hair dryer blew up the first time I turned it on. I had to call four times for it to finally be replaced. It took well over an hour.
On the first day, the bathroom had one tiny soap (for the bathtub and the sink) and one set of shampoo-conditioner little bottles. Naturally, I was expecting that these toiletries would be substituted every day, little did I imagine that they would NEVER be replaced, for an entire week. Luckily for me there was a drugstore just a block away. I didn't even bother to complain. They weren't worth my time. I had never seen anything like this at any hotel. Anywhere in the world. The location is excellent. The view was nice (I was above the --th floor).

The business center consists of two computers and two very dirty mouse pads. How about changing them once a year, guys??? Maybe, huh? Or is that too much to ask?
I might stay there again (I'll try to remember to take my own computer) , only because of the location, but I will probably prefer to try another hotel in the area, if available.

Stayed five nights on a business trip because space was not available at the larger hotels. Historic nature of the hotel gives it a unique flavor. Location next to Alamo is central, though better is possible for Henry B. Gonzalez Convention Center. Room was slightly run down. Shower had great water pressure, but no shower wand. Air conditioning in room was easily controlled to maintain a comfortable setting (average temps in high --s during my stay). WiFi in room was mediocre relative to higher end hotels. One afternoon I put a DND sign on the door to catch up on sleep and room service called the room phone to let me know I could ask for towels - while I was trying to sleep with the DND on the door! When I asked to check out the night prior to an early departure, I was told that the new system would not allow it - I might get charged twice - but they could close out the next day and e-mail me the receipt. Not ideal for an early morning departure in a hurry or business traveler who wants to leave with all receipts in hand. Over-all, left me with a disappointed, tepid impression of what I had thought would be a stellar hotel.

Booked into the Beacon, after reading favourable reviews. What a find. Beautiful suite, with full kitchen. excellent staff, nothing was too much trouble. The best location, opposite the Fairway grocery store, subway a short walk away. Felt very safe in the area, with lots of excellent shopping and restaurants nearby.
The Beacon and New York the best part of our trip!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!..We'll be back.

We stayed four nights at the Chambers Hotel and had a great stay. The standard queen room was plenty of space for us, and the bathroom was modern and bright with a nice """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""rain"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" showerhead. We did have a slight issue when they seemed to think only one person was in the room, only leaving one bottle of water for a couple of nights, and removing one of our robes, but this was resolved easily when I spoke to the staff.

The lobby is comfortable and cozy and we enjoyed the second floor """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Mezzanine"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for drinks. Overall the hotel was very quiet. I just got back from a dental convention in Chicago and decided to stay at this Hilton Garden Inn. Let me start by saying this hotel is perfectly located in the heart of downtown, close to the red line train, shopping and numerous great places to eat. The check in was polite and fast. I got up to my room and was surprised how clean and modern the room was. Flat screen T.V. king size foam bed, comfortable enough for me but if you like a bed that is on the firm side you may not like this one. The room also had a fridge and microwave which was nice! I agree with the reviewers who talk about the hotel being right in the middle of everything. If you don't want to walk, one of the many mass transit or tour bus options are available close by. The rooms and bathrooms are comfortably sized for an urban hotel. The bathroom products are one of the few I have taken with me from a hotel chain. Also, the staff is extremely helpful - holding doors and elevators for me when my hands were full of coffee. (Their titles - intuition specialists - are a bit pretentious.) I did think the room amenities were slim - namely no refrigerator. I have no problem with no snacks or minibar in the room, but the prices to have them delivered were ridiculous. The food in the hotel was good enough - try one of the many other options in the area instead. The water delivered to the room, printed sheet of tips from the staff, and managers wine reception are all nice touches.
I had this for two nights on the front end of a business trip. I wish I had been there the whole trip.

Took my wife overnight on a Birthday Special the hotel was promoting. We had a Junior Suite which was comfortable but even being on the fifth floor the noise from the street was noticable. King sized bed was comfortable and the dinner served in our room was better than expected. Bathroom was very small and no exhaust fan so got pretty steamy with the shower on. The front desk attendant Wendall was extremely pleasant and helpful. The hostess at the lobby restaurant was less than helpful, borderline rude which took me by surprise and kept the rating from being above average.

Had a great smooth stay. great for the price and close to downtown and high way. Great pool, nice, clean, somewhat spacious rooms. complimentary washer-dryer comes in handy when you have extended stay w-kids!!! Will stay there again!!

Lovely hotel with beautiful grounds, great pools-lazy river. Restaurants were very nice with happy hour drinks and appetizers in the afternoon. The room was very comfortable, It had a large bathroom with separate tub and shower. I would reccommend this hotel.

We were here several days for a U.S. Navy ship reunion and could not believe how well we were treated from check in to check out. Scott Villareal was super in helping us make the plans and was constantly checking to see if we needed anything during our stay. If we needed it, he found it. Melanie was the event coordinator that made sure things ran smoothly as well. She was outstanding -- very personable. When we needed two ice chests we were told it was no problem -- later we found out that Scott and Melanie had brought us their own ice chests. That was truly going above the call of duty. Melanie, the food manager, and all the catering-kitchen staff did a superb job in catering our banquet. We were basically expecting a meal in our hospitality room after a day of sightseeing. What we returned to was a beautifully decorated room with ambiance. The food was excellent and the staff was so attentative and friendly. The food was delicious and there was plenty of it. You could tell the tables had been set with pride and the desserts were so carefully decorated on each plate for visual appeal. I walked in and found the ladies drizzlling the sauce on the cheesecake as if each one were to be their masterpiece. The rooms are quite spacious and the beds so comfortable. I heard one of the guests saying he wants those same sheets, pillows and comforters on his bed at home -- and that is from someone who does not sleep that well in hotels. The housekeeping staff were friendly and actuallly initiated conversations with us in the hallways. I appreciated the good job they did in cleaning our room each day. The parking attendant was friendly and efficient, and the gentleman that helped us with - carts of luggage and boxes the first day was so helpful and so careful with our things. The front desk was always willing to answer my questions, and volunteered to fax papers back to my office. I am sorry I cannot think of the names of the ladies at the front desk, but you were really helpful to me at all times with directions and suggestions. Our conference room was not set up exactly as we needed, and within minutes of our comments, someone was in the room taking down and moving tables. The tables had different colored table cloths than what we wanted, and without any complaints, the lady came back and changed the cloths. She said it would be the next day, but in just a few hours she was back with table skirting and busily put things in order. We had our group photo made out by the pool and it provided the perfect backdrop. The trolley stops very close to the hotel, so it was easy to move about the Riverwalk area. The breakfast was part of our package and it was wonderful each morning -- something new added each day. Loved the fresh water dispenser with apples and fruits in the lobby. I am sure I have overlooked something or someone, but I am trying to convey the idea that we were really treated well. I would definitely recommend this hotel for conferences and reunions.

The hotel looks nice, but the fold-out sofabed was broken and a TV remote did not work. Couldn't get a towel in the pool area despite begging.
Other beds were comfortable and the breakfast was good.
Very convenient if flying at LAX. Pretty convenient to other sights in LA area.
If you're planning a vacation and are not familiar with LA, it's in kind of a rough neighborhood. Not a place to walk around in, especially at night.
If you come by car, there's a $-- parking fee, but spaces appear plentiful.

When I arrived at St Mark's Hotel, a woman stopped me on the street to ask if I had the time. Not thinking, I told her I wasn't wearing my watch. It was a DUH moment, as I realized she really wasn't looking for the time. Thus began my weekend stay at St. Mark's Hotel, a simple place with high steps that only accepts cash and traveler's cheques. A few of the questionable amenities: there is no door to buzz you in, you just walk up the steps and to your room. I had the dickens of a time adjusting the shower handles to make the water not hot. Also, the two complementary porno stations on the television were startling. However, I was equally surprised to see parents at the hotel with their children, the staff was always helpful and friendly, and my small dorm like room was cleaned and cared for each day. There was no room slippers provided and I sort of missed that. 
There was nothing in the little fridge under the TV. If you want snacks and drinks stocked, you have to order them in the morning and they'll be in by evening. Might as well buy your own. 
Housekeeping did a great job daily cleaning up and straightening up my mess. 
All in, nothing fancy, but clean, quite convenient, and the subway station is nearby.

I have stayed over a couple times mid-week for work, but in my last visit I discovered when I actually read the employee’s badges – that the Harbor Court had civic-mindedness happening! Everyone has a favorite city thing they either do for fun or volunteer at. It is part of the hotel’s “community” feel for guests. If you want to know how the locals live and what they do, this is the place for you. Everyone is very helpful and very friendly. The location is great if you’re a tourist or love walking along the Bay. The hotel also provides running maps of the city, and you get complimentary access to the YMCA that is actually part of the building. Cocktail hour has non-alcoholic warmed spiced cider if you don’t drink, and hot chocolate in the morning with coffee. Very good! I had a very nice stay.

This property had a great blend of character and comfort. The room had a historic feel but not old or dirty. The lobby was fantastic. I did not really get into the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""ducks"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in the lobby but the fact that people were lined up three deep to see them made for quite an event. I would not describe it as overly luxurious but certainly nice and a place that I would stay at again.

We stayed for - nights with our - yr old baby. -* for value for money. Very clean and quiet room with an amazing view from the --th floor! Room was very clean and staff all very helpful. The kitchinette was very useful for the baby and there were several convenience stores close by for milk etc. Breakfast was good and the baby eats for free!
Location location location with this hotel. We would definately stay again and have been telling our friends!

NASTY! Sheets had stains and hair on them, hair all over bathroom, cigarette butts and dead roaches everywhere. Staff did not want to clean and said that it was clean. decided to check out after being there less than -- minutes instead of staying the night and they refused to give us our money back for the - nights we booked! With my partner I have just returned from an eleven night stay at the Hollywood Hills Hotel, beginning on --th September ---- and can say with all sincerity both of us were more than happy with all aspects of the hotel and its service.
Believe me, I am the type of person who tells of a situation exactly as it is and if I wasn't happy about an issue would speak out but in the case of the Hollywood Hills I had nothing at all to be unhappy over.
Check-in for the Hollywood Hills is at the Magic Castle Hotel and from the second we arrived to the second we left the front desk staff couldn't do enough to assist us and made us feel completely welcome. The Hollywood Hills is located (obviously) on a hill behind the Magic Castle. The distance to the Hollywood Hills is perfectly walkable and although a little steep is pleasant, taking around only ----- mins at a steady pace. We walked most days, without any problems and found the walk great for excercise, but for anyone unwilling or unable to make the walk the Magic Castle staff are always more than happy to drive guests the distance - at any time of day or night. A drive can be requested to or from the hotel just by asking at the foyer or picking up the phone in your room.
As for the hotel itself, let me firstly point out the amazing views of LA it has to offer. We took a studio city room (room ---) and it had the most fantastic, extensive view over the city, right to downtown. It also had a gorgeous view of the Hollywood Hills (see my pics). Sitting on the balcony watching the sun rise and fall over LA is something I will always remember.
The room itself was a decent size, clean, tidy and perfectly acceptable. There was a good size private bathroom, with the bath, sink area and toilet kept in pristine condition. The shower was powerful, a good tonic after a long day. 
**Please note - the TV worked fine and had more than enough channels for someone taking a vacation**
The bed was the most comfortable of any I have ever stayed in at any hotel. It was huge! No chance of my partner kicking me in his sleep - he wouldn't make contact!
The kitchen area was also clean and well stocked with cooker, fridge, microwave, grill, pots, pans and even washing up liquid. 
The location of the hotel is very quiet, away from the citys' noise but is ideally located for Hollywood Boulevard. The walk from the Hollywood Hills to street level is much shorter and attractions such as Graumann's Chinese Theater and the Hollywood and Highlands shopping mall are minutes away. The hotel is also ideal for travelling elsewhere in LA. Bus services run from Hollywood Boulevard to pretty much everywhere and the fare is just $- for an all day pass. Also, the Metro tube is at the side of the Hollywood and Highlands Mall, running directly to Universal Studios and so forth.
Each morning, a complimentary breakfast is provided at the Magic Castle between - and --am, consisting of fresh pastries, cereals, yoghurts, bread, juice and teas-coffees - all are delicious. 
During our stay we were also given bottles of water, chocolate and other goodies, free of charge, given with a smile! The staff are so genuinely friendly and helpful. Any queries are dealt with instantly, they even printed off directions and bus times to local attractions for us as well as checking in on line for our flights home and printing our boarding passes.
The hotel also has a laundry room open until late, where wash powder can be purchased for a small price.
The Magic Castle offers use of its' pool and sun loungers at any time and staying at either hotel gives access to the Magicians' club just next door. 
At the side of the Hollywood Hills is the Yamashiro restaurant. From the restaurant there are the most spectacular panoramic views of the city, well worth walking the two minutes to photograph.
All in all I do not have a bad word to say about this hotel. If you are looking for great value ($--- per night for a studio city room) a stunning view, comfortable, clean accomodation, friendly service and close proximity to Hollywood Boulevard, this hotel has it all. 
If you expect pure J Lo style luxury and ---% modern and expensive fixtures and fittings or are upset at the thought of a daily walk up and down a moderately steep hill you may need to look elsewhere. For everyone who does book, you should not be disappointed.

After a long drive through LA and a full day of Legoland we were ready to relax. As I walked through the doors and you know immediately that we will be well taken care of.
The location of the hotel is perfect for being able to bounce from attraction to attraction with little traffic and easy routes. I especially liked being removed from downtown where we could go for a great morning walk along the bay. There was even a small park for the kids across the street, which the kids loved.
Our two room suite was excellent. It had a small kitchen, couch and a patio facing the marina. My son (-) was in heaven with his adjoining room all to himself. As he put it, “I have a bed to watch TV, and a bed to sleep in!” The staff was incredible; everyone we passed had a great smile and warm hello. We ordered up a crib and it was delivered promptly and was quickly asked if everything was in order and if we needed anything else.
The restaurant was very nice for our morning breakfasts and the kids loved it. For our last dinner my little girl was obsessed with pancakes and my wife asked if the chef would be able to make pancakes for her. She quickly came back and said that the chef would be more than happy. Our (outstanding) waitress came back with four small pancakes, fresh made whipped cream, and strawberries. She was in heaven. My wife referred to her diver scallops as the best she has ever had. 
This hotel was perfect for us, close to the zoo, waterfront, restaurants, pool, view, and the staff. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone!
for the businesss traveller it has all you need, efficient, quiet, well appointed, brilliant staff etc

I did not stay in the Holiday Inn. As a native of Philadelphia, I frequent many hotels for Sunday breakfast. I had a terrible experience at the HOliday INn Old City. Here is a letter that I wrote to the manager.
Dear Mr. Hall:
I am a Philadelphia native who frequented your hotel restaurant on a weekly basis about -- years ago. I finally had to leave because of the deteriorating quality of the restaurant. 
On Sunday, I wanted to take an out-of-town guest to the historical area of Philadelphia, starting with a nice breakfast. I thought that I would, once again, give your hotel a try. I was shocked at the quality of the restaurant and would like to make you aware of the following:
-. My friend and I were excited to see that there was a buffet, but when we approached it and saw the way it looked, we were shocked. My friend opened the food trays and got burned from the steam table door to the eggs. The hot cereal appeared to have a film on it, as if it were not stirred since -am. The thing that surprised me the most was that the buffet cost $--.-- with no omelet station. I frequent all of the hotels and buffets on Sunday and I have never encountered this price without a prepared omelet.
-. In spite of everything, my friend decided to try the buffet. He was extremely 
disappointed at the quality and taste of the food. He said that the pancakes were rubbery and appeared to have been there for several hours.
-. The presentation of the buffet was shocking. I have never seen one in such a state. It was not appetizing at all.
