Mr. Frank Raffa
frankraffa@aol.com

For the several hundred high school students who came for a model UN convention, the Palmer House was wonderful. It's the ideal place for a young person to experience a classic E-shaped building, three separate banks of elevators, turn of the twentieth century lobby, and street level arcade. I will remember that the atmosphere and faded grandeur of the hotel seemed to help the young people feel appropriately dressed in their suits. 
Now for the rest of us: 
location
- --- blocks from the Monroe Street CTA blue line
three blocks from the Architectural Foundation
two blocks from the Art Institute
two blocks from the Symphony Hall
technically walkable, but also a very quick cab to the Lyric Opera.
one block to the loop train
If you are traveling for a --- day stay that includes the above, you may be willing to trade the advantages of this terrific location with the very faded quality of the lower floor rooms. The room was clean, but worn, and the bathroom had been renovated and was excellent. The next time we travel, we will ask for an upgrade to the top floors that have been remodeled.
Also, for those of you who really like the old-fashioned ability to open a window, you can do so, safely - the window tilts open.
The streets outside are not the North Michigan miracle mile - and late at night the business area is sufficiently deserted to make walking alone unwise. 
Hope that this is helpful.

My husband and I stayed here in July ---- and we had a great time in the city. The hotel is small, but clean, and the service is fine. There is a Starbucks right there, so very easy to grab breakfast and run. I have to say the negative (as with most stays) is the parking. We paid an enormous price to park down the street and not do so again. Unfortunately we had to have a car for this trip, so we could not avoid the cost. I would recommend it again, and would consider their other properties as well.

My wife and I had originally booked a room at the Hyatt, but due to issues outside of the Hyatt's control they reserved a room for us at the Blackstone. We were very pleasanty surprised. 
The rooms have all been nicely updated and are very modern. The location lends itself well to anyone wanting to visit the Grant or Millenium Park, the Museum Campus, or Navy Pier. If you were up for a little exercise you could walk to shopping on the Miracle Mile or take a short cab ride.
We had our two small children along, but the hotel is probably best suited for couples. We'd love to come back for a weekend without the kids.

We admired the effort taken by the owners to convert an ordinary motel into something a little more interesting. But it should be remembered that it is a motel and in a town like LA it is not within easy access to many of the attractions or fast public transit. While the Farmer's Market and Pacific Grove, across the road, has some interest, they are much of a reason to stay in the location. Of course, if you are a going to the Price is Right, you can't ask for a better spot!
I would not consider the Farmer's Daughter unless you have access to a vehicle for your stay. LA is quite easy for a tourist (even from the other side of the world and on the other side of the road) to drive around. If you are not interested in driving then I would suggest try somewhere else, perhaps near one of the train lines.
In terms of the facilities, there was nothing wrong it was well presented and clean. But at above $US---, it is not as good value for money compared to some other properties we visited in the US.

We are a family of four and spent two nights at the Morris House Hotel. It is in an excellent location to visit the historic sites of Philadelphia (and buy jewelry - apparently this is jeweler's row!). It was pouring rain so we were grateful to the proximity to these sites! I found the staff to be very helpful except for the person at the desk when we left - we asked for help with the bags (as others have mentioned, it is a bit of a schlep up the steep stairs) and he ignored the request. The other staff people were fantastic - we got to know all of them as we could not operate the television with the two remotes (and we have teenagers!). The breakfast was fine...continental so we didn't expect hot food. Good coffee, excellent bagels and constantly cleaned up and replenished. The best part was sitting in the library surrounded by books and the old plank floors and antiques - it truly felt like old Philadelphia - so much more fun than a modern hotel chain. Our room was huge...we got a two room suite and could have had a football game in the bathroom....very nice for my husband who had to share with three girls. Spotless and spacious - much more than expected. So my only picky complaints are the gentleman who checked us out and the inoperable remote controls...all in all two very minor details! If you can, stay here. Another tip - they will reduce the rate to fill the hotel so if you need to make a last minute reservation you may get a very good deal. And the final tip...by the advice of a local friend we ate at Mercato about five blocks away - absolutely perfect Italian....bring your own bottle of vino - they don't have a liquor license...gets crowded with locals who love the olive oil and salt selection and incredible pastas!

Stayed there earlier this month for a business trip. It's a lovely hotel. The harbor view alone almost makes it worth staying there.
I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone who has meetings in the Wall Street area, and whose bill is being paid by a corporate expense account. This hotel won't work for families on vacation or tourists, especially given the distance to any of the major attractions in NYC. 
The hotel is far from everything except the Financial District. If you plan to do any shopping or dining outside of the area, realize that it's a $-- taxi ride to anywhere in midtown - one way. Even getting around Lower Manhattan was dicey because the cabbies weren't always familiar with the Byzantine layout of the streets. You can certainly try the subway, but the station is several blocks away and the streets are not in a grid pattern (easy to get lost). The walk back to the hotel late at night can be scary.
Try to get a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""higher"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" floor to avoid noise from the street. The hotel part of the Ritz Carlton only goes to the --th floor. The remainder of the tower is residential and has a separate entrance. The hotel has great windows, but the hotel sits directly above the exit ramp for the Battery Tunnel and the West Side Highway. It's noisy.

My husband & I stayed for - night (a Friday) the first weekend in June. We checked in around - pm and didn’t have any problems or wait. The staff was very friendly and helpful in showing us how to get to our room. We had a king suite on the ground floor. The location was perfect, not to close to the river ranch, but not too far. The room and bed was comfortable and the couch in the living area was great for lounging. The property itself is older and could use a good power washing on the outside but it was not run-down or dirty and our room was fine. 
The night we were there the hotel was having its “dive-in-movie”, which I think is great and we would have enjoyed watching but decided to float in the lazy river instead. There was a ton of teenagers staying not just younger kids and most of them were in the lazy river while movie was on. It looks like a great place to take your kids to enjoy so we decided we would go again next year and take our son who will be old enough to enjoy it then. 
We chose to eat dinner at Hole-in-the-wall on the outdoor patio. I felt the meal was overpriced, one beer, one mixed drink, a burger & pork sandwich for $--.--! Next time I’ll eat dinner off-site. We chose to eat breakfast offsite and found a cute little place a few miles away called Scramble. Food was good and it was kid and pet friendly.
My only gripe is that I think they should have at least - complimentary bottles of water in each room. It is Arizona after all! I wouldn’t normally be bugged by this except that the Rodeo Drive store closes at -:--, the bar at Hole-in-the-wall didn’t have any bottles to sell me & - vending machines that I checked were out of water. I ended up having to walk to the lobby & run into the store there as they were closing just to get a bottle. 
We did go back to the river ranch area around --:-- Saturday morning and it was not overcrowded yet. We tried to lounge up by the lazy river, which had cushions on the chairs, but my husband kept getting bitten by mosquitos. So if you’re like him and attract mosquitos bring DEET. We moved from the loungers & got in the pool until it was time to check out. 
I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a relatively inexpensive overnight or weekend getaway with family.

Has everything you would like in a city hotel. Must be the best choice in Baltimore. If you want a luxury hotel, here it is. Especially nice location on the harbor. the staff, especially at the front desk, were incredibly friendly and helpful.

The bathtub needs culking. Bathroom smells dirty (pee). Towels smells paint.
I am glad i arrived late at night and left very early in the morning.

My wife and i stayed in Essex house sept.-- for - nights , we got a super deal on an expedia --hr sale so decided to upgrade our room to an central park queen , the room was worth every extra penny
we had an an amazing view of central park from the --th floor , the service in this hotel is second to none , right down to the security staff telling you how good you looked on your way out the door. 
The rooms are quite big and finished to a very high standard 
there are two subway stations very close to the hotel one at --th&-th and the other at --&-th these two lines take you to most of the attractions or very close to them .
I would stay here again without a second thought only thing stopping me is the price as i have not been able to get a deal like that again

I stayed at the this hotel purely because I could not get in anywhere else. It was a great surprise in that the room was a fabulous size. I had a king corner suite with a huge deep bath, and amazing views. I thought it was new, but realized it wasn't from the paint and badly patched up 'bit's'...BUT it wasn't a problem. It was very private, and in a great location. A completely different part of NYC..I enjoyed the diverse restaurants, and the very comfortable bed. I would stay there again, even though the price was more than I wanted to pay...oh, and the evening cookies at night were much appreciated.

We stayed at this hotel for - nights,there were - ladies to - room so we found the room abit small but we didn't spend too much time in our room.We were on the --th floor and never had any problems with the lifts apart from a short wait of - minutes at the most.Breakfast was lovely lots of choice and as we arrived down quite early never had to wait for a table,breakfast staff always happy and polite and ready to help with anything.This was our first time in New York and we had a lovely time,we found the hotel very central and we walked around quite late at night and felt safe walking back,we would be very happy to stay here again if we could afford to come to New York again!

Needed a place to stay for a business trip. My meetings were on the west side of Lake Union, so this location seemed convenient. Checked reviews on TA after finding a sale price of $---night on Hotels.com. At that price, I can't imagine a better hotel for what I needed.
Reaching the hotel was simple, taking the light rail from the airport to downtown for $-.--, then a bus transfer to the hotel. Bus stops are only a block away from hotel, and I used public transit to get most anyplace. If you prefer taxis, there are always one or two at the hotel.
The neighborhood was nice. Grabbed a burger at Dick's right outside the front door, and a hearty breakfast at Cafe Mecca less than a block away. Starbucks in the lobby is nice, and if you prefer to brew your own in the room they also have Starbucks for you there, along with free bottled H-- and microwave popcorn.
Room was comfortable, nothing lavish but totally nice. Staff was friendly and helpful. Took in the views from the rooftop patio on a nice night, and got to see the Seattle skyline lit up nicely.
I'll definitely stay here again when business brings me to Seattle.

Just returned from a quick one night stay at this hotel on the Sunday of Labor Day weekend. We are just a short drive away from San Diego, as we live in Orange County - but love to come downtown and enjoy the night.
We got this hotel Sunday morning at $-- a night (AAA Rate) - and I was sold! While it is a few steps further than the hotels IN the gaslamp quarter, this hotel was absolutely beautiful.
We checked in, got a room with two queen beds, and went to OdySea (the bar) and enjoyed great drinks with a beautiful view of the Bay.
The room was great, people complain about parking - but it is in downtown San Diego, $-- for the night is not much more than you would pay anywhere else down there. I loved that there is a Starbucks downstairs - I walked down in the morning to get some coffee.
The beds are SO comfortable...nice flat screen LG TV...I have no complaints.
For the price and the location - it can't be beat. It's much better than the more trendier hotels that can run you ---+ a night.
Also, we didn't get a chance to enjoy the pool, but it is absolutely beautiful! We have already booked our stay to come back in - weeks.

We have been in a couple of hotels that belongs to the Small Luxury Hotels and we have been really pleased with them, but Andra wasn't for us up to those standards. It is well located downtown Seattle, if you don't have a car. There are a lot of places you can walk to, even the Speace Needle isn't really far and you can take the monorail to come back. Restaurants like The serious Pie are just a block away. The bed was good, however our bedroom was very small, and the bathroom too but with modern finishes. It's not really a room to relax, just to go to sleep after a day of exploring the City. Our bedroom was at the end of the corridor, above of the restaurant's kitchen so we get the food smell (it was good) but the fans were noisy if you open the windows. They charge for wifi and parking is really expensive. We didn't have any incident but the service was not outstanding how it has been in the other Small Luxury Hotels we have stayed before.

Within good distances from everywhere due the --st subway station, a couple of block from the central park. Very good food market across the street, fridge and coffee machine in the room. Safetybox. Helpful personnel. Just in case take your ear plugs with you.
Visit the Pinkberry, ultimate frozen youghurt experience near --St. station.

We stayed here for the second year in a row for our annual Spring Training trip and I can't understand all the people giving it such harsh reviews. We look forward to staying here and have found everyone we encountered to be very friendly and helpful. Pua, at the front desk, helped us check in and out and was extremely nice and gave us great information. This hotel is centrally located and it makes it easy to get to all of the ballparks. The rooms are large, comfortable and very nicely decorated. Everything is exceptionally clean. We had a great experience here and hope to be back next spring. Thank you to everyone at the Crescent for such a wonderul stay!

I travel very frequently for work, and both domestic and international trips. I typically stay in Hyatt or Starwood hotels. This was my first time staying at the Andaz San Diego and it will certainly not be my last time. I look forward to traveling to San Diego in the future to stay at this hotel. The rooms were well appointed with hardwood floors, ceramic tile showers that made it appear you were standing among rocks in a waterfall, modern fixtures throughout. The bed was very comfortable and the layout of the room was excellent. The room included a working desk and a sitting area with couch and table. I was very surprised upon arriving to find out that the room included some free amenities; water and iced tea and some snacks for free every day. The rooftop restaurant-bar, pool and deck area was very nice as well, comfortable and inviting, and made you want to sit back with an iced cold beverage and relax.

What a terrific place to stay next time you visit Chelsea, meat packing district, SoHo, etc! It was a joy to simply walk out the door and experience the High Line, Chelsea Market, the Hudson River Park, and everything else that this particularly cool neighborhood offers. I stayed in the Captain's room, which was really well appointed. The private patio right off the room was delightful. The staff was so professional, knowledgeable, and accommodating. For example, they cheerfully printed out my boarding pass and had it ready at my convenience. Also, if you go uptown, it is really easy and quick to get there.

We had our wedding here on April --, ----, and it was amazing. The staff was very accommodating and friendly. There was always someone there when we had questions. Our suite that came with our wedding package was just as nice. It had a tub that could fit two people comfortably, and the suite was big enough for -- people to get ready in without getting in each other's way. Apparently, the entire hotel was booked the weekend of our wedding, so when several of our wedding guests checked into their regular rooms, they ended up with suites even bigger than ours because Hotel Valencia ran out of rooms. It was basically a free upgrade for them, which made everyone happy. The soaps and shampoos offered smell nice, and there is free breakfast for all hotel guests from ---- AM. There were so many breakfast options: pancakes, chocolate croissants, sausages, eggs, variety of healthy non-sugared cereals, orange juice, grapefruit juice, coffees, teas, toast with different types of jams, mixed fruits (pineapple, watermelon, blackberries, raspberries), and the list goes on. Hotel Valencia gets an A+ in my book.
Don't let the strange elevator lobby deter you. Once you go up the elevators, you are in another world; it is amazing.

I took my three older teenagers (- boys-- girl) to New York for their first time to celebrate a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""white"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Christmas. We're from Orange County, California so we don't get to experience snow unless we head up to the mountains. Well, it didn't snow much while we were there but we had the best time ever in New York, and this hotel was a big part of it. Our room had an awesome view of Times Square which made it very festive. We bought a little pre-lit Christmas tree and placed it in the window. The maid service was excellent. Our room was perfectly cleaned daily and we were never disturbed too early. The food was excellent in the restaurants and the location of this hotel can't be beat. It's in the center of EVERYTHING!! We never had to take a cab; we were able to walk everywhere, including Rockefeller Center where we ice-skated on Christmas Day. It was magical. We will DEFINITELY stay at this hotel again. The only negative comment I could make is that we couldn't access The View Restaurant one evening because the girl """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""guarding"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" the elevators had a little too much attitude and insisted that we stand in line and wait. We didn't see a line and instead went to our room and filed a complaint about her. I received a call back from the manager of the restaurant who personally apologized and invited us up to the restaurant at any time during our stay. He said to personally ask for him. lSo even our complaint was dealt with in a professional and efficient manner. We will definitely be back!

Great views , great service! I had my doubts about bringing our German Shepherd on her first hotel stay but I could not have asked for a more lovely experience. All the staff were flexible and kind. We stayed two nights and on night two , noisier people moved into the room next to us and I knew our dog might bark so they quickly moved us to a beautiful more remote room, not an upgrade but just as equally as nice a room as we had before.
 THe views are spectacular from the high floors. The beds are super comfy and the elevators were super fast unlike what I had read in others reviews. 
 The food was great, better than I expected.
It was a perfect stay and I will definetly be going back for more trips since my son lives nearby. I would recommend trying for the rooms on the upper floors if you appreciate the good views. The room we had facing west had a bit of jet fuel smell since the jets take off with their tails aimed right at the hotel sliders. The view was so nice though , shutting the door stopped the smell from coming in and subsequently all jet noise as well. The room facing East had no residual jet fuel smell. It was fun watching the jets take off and land.
I would recommend this hotel to couples and couples with kids , people of all ages and people with friendly , well behaved dogs.

We stayed at Ink-- for - nights in September ----, and as the first guests we were given the most amazing welcome!!
On arrival, there were about -- members of staff to greet us, we were presented with a beautiful gift of guide books, biscuits, a beautiful vase of flowers, and an upgrade to two connecting room!
The hotel is gorgeous, very funky and trendy, as said before the restaurant, gym and bar areas were not yet finished, but this did not detract from how fabulous our stay here was. Our rooms were spacious, huge light airy windows, with the most amazing views of NYC!! Just perfect for our first time visit. The bathrooms were big, very clean, and the shower was fantastic. Also very appreciated was the complimentary L'Occitane toiletries, which were replenished every day. 
The maid service was brilliant, the rooms were cleaned everyday, and were left spotlessly clean.
The staff at the hotel were beyond doubt the friendliest and most helpful staff I have ever encountered - especially Sam, Suzanne, and all of the concierges. The first morning we missed breakfast, and this was brought down to us in the lobby, even thought it had finished over half and hour before! Any advice or information we needed was attended to straight away.
As previous people have said, the hotel is situated about -- minutes walk to Times Square, and its no problem to hail a taxi outside. We never felt unsafe walking about at night, however we stuck to main roads, as we would do in any area at night. Yes there is noise from the street - taxis, car horns, fire engines, but your in NYC, it all just added to the experience for us!!
We cannot wait to return, hoping to book again for next September!

For the folks complaining about noise I'm guessing they live somewhere where there's no public transportation, neighbors, cars... Unless we were extremely lucky aside from the normal 'noise' of a city we did not find it to be noisy at all (and we were on the ground level). If you're looking for the kind of amenities and accommodations the Ritz would provide then save up the dough and stay there. If you're looking to have a nice trip but don't want to empty the bank this is a perfectly fine choice. It was clean, reasonably priced, in a safe neighborhood and easy to get to via public transportation.
We did have a car because we were visiting friends outside of the city but even though the hotel was full we did get lucky with parking. We weren't there in peak season which might have helped.
If you want cons the only one I can provide is: their complimentary breakfast can be skipped.

My husband and I were here for a small meeting for two days. Never having stayed at a Kimpton Hotel property, we really didn't have any specific expectations. We were pleasantly surprised by our experience. From the welcome by the bellman, to the front desk staff, to cleanliness and the restaurant, Hotel Monaco exceeded our expectations! We ate dinner at the restaurant the first night having arrived after -:-- p.m. and not wanting to venture far. The restaurant on property was excellent and Terry was a great server! 
When I arrived home, I promptly completed a survey that Hotel Monaco emailed me and within a couple of hours, I received a thank you from management. Now, that is real service and a desire to continue to improve upon a guest's experiences!
I would definitely recommend this property to anyone staying in downtown Chicago!

Stayed at the Boston Park Plaza for three nights. Loved the historic story of the building and the vision of Mr Statler. Love the patterned carpet in the foyer and wonder how long it has been there and what a carpet to withstand all the traffic it takes. Pairings wonderful breakfasts with excellent service. A very homely, quiet, excellent location Boston historic and comfortable hotel.
Great hotel. Clean nice rooms and good concept. I got the motion room and enjoyed the in room bike and Gigi bath every day. I recomend this place.

We stayed at the Warwick in October - we had been there before and like the ambiance. I went to bed one night feeling fine and woke up with bites all up and down one arm. My natural assumption was bed bugs. The hotel said they would inspect the room. When they called to say there were no bugs found, that was not the worst. The biggest problem was that they had the security manager call me who was quite abrupt and rude - pretty much implying that I was lying and trying to cheat the hotel.

I wrote to the customer service managers and to the Warwick International Hotels. No-one has had the courtesy of even responding. Why would anyone want to stay in a hotel where they clearly don't care about their customers.

As usual, breakfast and hotel ambience outside the suite is good. Enjoyed the waterfalls views and fish feeding. ALos it has good swimning pool and gymnasium.
Only problem is with the suites are there curtains and couches in living room are not clean and reason from the hotel management that because of old property and according to them they are planning for remodelling of Suites sometime next year.
ALso microwave is very old and als oit might be beacause of old property anf might be the part of planned remodelliing .

From the minute we walked in the service was excellent. We wanted to be on Michigan Ave. and this was south of the shopping but only a brief walk. Room was very good with wonderful lake view. Old charm in the hotel but updated throughout. I would stay again.

The reception was very friendly, but at the breakfast there was not much left already at -:--. Paper plates and plastik silverware.
Nice view from the roof top pool.

This is one of the most difficult hotels I’ve ever tried to navigate to. It is next to a Hilton and the Hilton is on the road, but there is no way to get to the Best Western without going through a maze of stops, turns, merges and then a drag race before attempting to make a high-speed turn into the only enrty-exit of the hotel – miss it and you have to go through all the turns, stops, races again.
The hotel is relatively new – maybe - years old. All inside access rooms with parking in front or in back only. The rooms feature the new Best Western branding – multiple pillows, blanket on the foot of the bead, flash screen TV and the standard mini-fridge and microwave. The rooms are nice and the breakfast was good for self-serve style. 
A negative, the pool is in the back and the back parking lot has a high fence. The fence acts like a megaphone for the noise from the pool. Around --:pm I complained about the high level of kid noise, the clerk said he would talk to the manager when she came in the next morning. Around midnight I and another guest took care of the noise. 
I forgot about the manager. The next morning she came in around noon and starting telling an unsuspecting guest that they shouldn’t be complaining to her about the noise. When I said it had been me I got an earful too. I tried twice to tell her the situation and twice she repeated that it was not her problem and that I should not bother her with such matters. I’m sure she was having a bad morning, but next time I need to stay in north San Antonio I know where to find a Hilton – a Hilton with easy access and I think an indoor pool.
Great rooms, strange manager.

I have nothing bad to say about this place. Evertything was great.
Got a good rate on Hotwire. We got there early, the room wasn't ready. They took our bags and called us -- minutes later to let us know the room was now ready.
I have to agree with some of the earlier comments, the sliding window between the bathroom and the bed is a little weird. The room was very comfortable and quiet... no problem with outside noise. the staff was very helpful.
the pool area and gym were nice. with a great view... the parking was a little pricey (--$), but I stayed a couple of times at the Boston Harbor Hotel and the parking there is a lot more expensive. if you don't want to pay that much to park, just leave your car at the wellington station parking (-.---day) and take the T to your hotel...
I wouldn't pay ---$ a night for the Intercontinental, but I don't think I would pay that much for any hotel in boston. so if you get a good rate, don't hesitate, this place is great !!

Booked this hotel through Victoria Clipper.com! Absolutely gorgeous room! Waterside room! Cruise ships only -- feet away from room window! Fireplace was wonderful! Bathroom is nice, shower is a little different, as its an overhead shower, but we loved the room! Beds were cozy and so comfortable! Pike Place is -- minute walk, loved it! Would absolutely recommend this hotel to everyone! Courteous service, clean rooms, quiet, and a wonderful lobby!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

We had a quick - day stay in Washington just after Christmas and really enjoyed the Holiday Inn Capitol. The location of it is fantastic, being one of very few hotels so close to the Capitol and the National Mall. It's very close to the Metro line and plenty of fast food outlets, however other than the restaurants in the hotel, there are none within close (walking) distance. 
The facilities were very good - we had a large corner room with plenty of space and a fridge and microwave. The staff were very friendly and helpful, and there is free internet access from their business centre, which was a huge bonus.
If you have limited time in Washington, this hotel is a great choice because of its convenience to the major tourist attractions.

When yoiu need help, Sheila the operator, makes it happen. The HVAC unit in my room was not working, my internet connection would not go through, and the toilet seat was loose. Sheila came to my rescue and all were fixed in record time. The unit was replaced and Sheila helped me get on the internet.
Kudos to the Sheraton's great teamwork!

We stayed at the Palace last month for a --day long weekend trip. The hotel was beautiful however our room was very small. We were told it was a Courtyard room, however our - window was overlooking what looked like a roof. The room was very cramped with no built in closet (I admit I overpack but this armouire was tiny & housed the extra pillows, the ironing board and needed to fit our clothing as well.) We were so tired Thursday night after a long flight that we decided to just suck it up. The mini-fridge in the room was so noisy that I made my boyfriend unplug for the duration of our stay.
The hotel itself is very close to many attractions and we felt like we were in the center of the action, so the location of the hotel is great. Also, the Pied Piper bar in the hotel was awesome, we ate here on Thursday night after we landed & also stopped in for a drink on both Friday and Saturday. Its very convenient to have in the hotel. 
My only other complaint about this hotel is that I did not realize it was pet-friendly. Part of this is my own fault for not doing enough research, however I wanted to jump out my window after listening to the dog parking in the room next to me for - hours straight on Saturday. I called the front desk who said they would send someone up to check it out, however I never saw anyone come up. It sort of ruined out relaxing long weekend. Also, there was a dog show of some sort in the Lobby on Friday night which we also we not told about up front either. You can imagine our surprise when we came back from a long day of sighseeing on Friday afternoon only to be surronded by ---- dogs and thier owners in the hotel lobby. Not exactly what I was I looking for in a hotel. I think they should have made all of their guests aware at check-in if they were hosting this type of event during the guests stay - especially since it was just out in the lobby-main enterance, not in a private room.

I wasn't sure about this hotel given some of the previous reviews that I have read but I am a Platinum Priority Club member and wanted to give it a try. I was so pleased!! Not only did I stay here but our larger team used the facilities for a --day meeting. All of the meeting space was just perfect. We used several rooms in the Plaza section. My room and the entire hotel decor was lovely. I really enjoyed the lobby area as well. The location was great and there were many fabulous places to eat and shop nearby. The staff went out of the way to be super kind and helpful. I am very grateful to Dale with IT-Audio for his expert help and to Ingrid for making my check-out experience top notch. The room was a little warm for me but given the time of year and the heat, I simply closed the curtains and that helped. The -th floor, outdoor pool was WONDERFUL, especially at night. The view is spectacular and it is just fun to be on a roof-top pool!!

check in- We had no issues checking in although I wouldn't characterize the staff as particularly friendly. They seemed busy, rushed, and like you were the ----th person they delt with that day. However they were not rude, either.
Lobby-common area- Big disapointment with the cramped tiny lobby, which is under construction, making it even more cramped. People rushing to a fro. Lots of yelling across the room as cabs are arranged, etc.
Location- Excellent. Located close to many attractions, places to dine, shopping, and a safe part of the city.
Rooms- I have good and bad things to say about the room. I will start with the good: it was clean, and we had a room in the corner, which was larger than most. Beds were extremely comfortable and I slept like a baby all night, despite the street noise, which I will get to in a minute.We had a long hall way to the bathroom, which added space and privacy, with marble countertops and an updated feel, plus an area for our closet that was generous. One other thing that always scores high points for me is the mini fridge, apparently in all rooms. Wireless worked great and is free for rewards members. Otherwise it was $--.
Ok, the bad. The air conditioner was an old wall unit and it sucked. It worked good as far as producing cold air, but it was VERY annoying because it whined and rattled really loudly. So we had to shut it off at night to sleep, of course making the room stuffy. We called maintainence and he came while we were gone, but I saw little to no improvenent. Also I could hear the people next to us through the walls. Especially in the bathroom. The street noise can be loud...we faced Lexington and we were on the --th floor. At times it was quite loud. So ask for an interior or high floor room and I'll bet you will be ok.
Other than that...we had no issues. We were using reward points to pay, but if it was on my own dime, I would try one of the many other hotels in the area.

We really enjoyed our two-night stay. Perfect service, nothing ever amiss, absolutely clean. Chose the Executive King, which was very spacious. Every detail of the room was just-so. 
The location was great for hitting the theaters, all the new and old Tenderloin restaurants, shopping. Starbucks right there, essentially in the hotel. No view from the room, but that wasn't a surprise. Quiet room -- ours was in the back, windows looking on another part of the building. But the fun, racy designer window shades made up for it.
There are numerous common-area lounges in addition to the business center. Cool artifacts to be found in all of them. One lounge was full of high-concept designer lamps.
It's definitely urban, but didn't have any worries about the folks we encountered on the sidewalks. Nice restaurants in both directions, and the American Conservatory Theater right across the street.
Would definitely stay again.
excellent hotel in a great location for all attractions. in walking distance of most

Transit stopover. Nice quiet, clean room, with great bed. Used gym as well, and it's very good. Overall, enjoyed the stopover, and as they say """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I felt better when I left than when I arrived"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".

Just got back from a quick trip to chicago to celebrate my sister's --th birthday with friends. The Marriott Residence Inn was above our expectations. The room was appointed very nicely and extremely clean. The location of the hotel was perfect - would definitely recommend highly if you just want to walk to various trendy sections. Just a few blocks from Rush Street, walked back from Old town, Buck -- great great great location. The staff was very accomodating but I will mention that the girls who work breakfast really stood out -- they were so pleasant with a ready smile and always had nice thing to say to us. I wish I got names so management would know but I didn't. The one bedroom suite was very roomy, the efficiency kitchen appointed well - we thought we would us it but never had the chance. Definitely go the the Drake Hotel bar for a fun time, the bartenders at Knickerbockers next door were great, James Hotel fun, as well.

This hotel is located in the heart of the Inner Harbor in Baltimore. Located one block from 'Little Italy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" where you can find authentic Italian cuisine to experiencing professional baseball several walking blocks away in Camden Yards. In between these two points are historic ships, quality museums, shops, and entertainment. This upscale hotel is affordable. That feature is always at the top of my list, but this time it is coupled with great service from a professional staff and transportation offered at the front door. From my hotel window I could see the Coast Guard ship, beautiful landscaping, National Aquarium, and the shops in the Hard Rock Cafe building. This hotel is located at the end point of Interstate --. So if you are traveling from the north, locating this hotel is very easy. I was amazed at the opportunities offered in Baltimore and completely satisfied with the Pier - Hotel. Check out their website; the rooms offer amply square footage and colorful upscale appointments.

My company just had a large group stay at the Dana and everyone in our group commented about the great location of the hotel and the amenities and great service that they all received. All of the employees from front desk to valet and bellman were very polite, helpful and nice!! It was very much appreciated! I want to comment you all on a great time that was had by all at your hotel.
A member of the reservation staff - Mary - was extremely prompt with confirmations and helping out with any changes we had to make for my groups stay! It made my job so much easier!
The rooms are very nice and comfortable - clean - and had just the right amenities. The beds are extremely comfortable - didn't want to get out in the morning to go to work! Views of the city are great! Awesome Hotel!! Cannot comment enough about the great location of this hotel!! Near a lot of great restaurants, night clubs and other venues - within walking distance!
Thank you again and “cheers” to everyone on your team at the hotel!!
Keep up the great work!

Great hotel, enjoyed staying there for - nights! Many pros about the hotel (service is friendly, very clean, location is very good), the only cons is the room size, which is quite small! If i have the chance, I would stay once again there!

We stopped here for our first night stay in US after flying into Sky Harbour Airport.
This was our first taste of American hotel rooms, huge, spotlessly clean, and superbly equipped. There were also mini doughnuts to help yourself to in the morning.

Due to a an unexpected death in our family, we needed accomodations near the family and this hotel fit the bill perfectly. According to my Mother, she and the other family members were well taken care of by the wonderful staff at the Loop South. I highly reccomend this hotel to all travelers.

We stayed at the Affinia in February ---- for - nights and it truly was excellent. It is located about -- minute walk from Times Square which was fine (even though it was very cold!) The hotel staff were all very helpful, a massive thank you to the doorman (I really wish I had his name to hand) who helped us with getting tickets for our train journey back to Newark Airport from Penn Station. The complimentary Tea and Coffee in reception each morning was a lovely warm start to the cold days. In all, no negatives only pluses. Oh and the rooms were VERY large (in New York terms from what I gather most are some box rooms.)

I stayed at the Yotel in June, just days after it opened, and I was really impressed to see how the staff had hit the ground running in the early days of business. The porters were excellent and helpful, they had a great manner. 
The room was small (no surprises though, it's Manhattan), but cleverly designed; it was just right. I loved the decor, and the shower fitting was so good we put a rain shower in our bathroom at home - how's that for an advertisement!
The breakfast was ok, just a muffin and tea or coffee, but better than nothing. I wasn't too fussed. I would have appreciated though, if the coffee machines in the galleys were maintained more regularly asthey were out of service for the duration of my, albeit short, stay.
While not my all time favourite location in Manhattan, is was close to Times Square, and was reasonably priced. It had a great feel, and I would stay here again.

Awesome staff, concierge and parking attendants are - star for directions, things to do and places to stay away from.
I was at first peeved about the ---nt parking and valet, until i was out that night and saw a homeless guy take a crap beside someone's car in the next hotel's parking lot.
Dont bother thinking about going to starbucks in the morning.
Will definitely stay here next time in SF

Upon arrival, having a truck to park in their parking spaces felt a little bit iffy. Their parking spaces are a tad on the smaller side, but we adapted by just parking in one of the designated parking spaces on the side of one bottom floor walls - not in an actual parking stall. Parking was free, albeit, limited. (& made us a bit scared to come back late and not have a spot). Checking in was a breeze, the front desk young male was very pleasant and cheerful. We walked to our room to find that the room door was already propped open & the heater was on full blast with the window open (other rooms around it were the same). They were cleaning the carpets to the rooms, which was a plus, but our carpet was still a bit damp when we arrived. 
The room was comfortable and had a fridge, a microwave, and a coffee maker. I was happy to see that the light in the bathroom was bright and not dim at first (like some other hotels I've stayed at). The hotel was in close proximity to a lot of things you could do, so that was a plus. Free wireless internet in the room - but our connection was really in and out so it was kind of hard to watch something on the laptop.
The cons of this hotel would probably be that it was designed more like a motel, so the hallways are not closed, they are open and you can hear the traffic and everybody who walks by, especially if they just came back from going out all day-night. The air conditioner-heater was particularly loud when it was bringing the temp. back up-down, but quiet when it was in-between those cycles. Also, the TV was a bit weird, it was a flat screen Samsung but it had lines that would run across it while you were watching - it reminded me of those old TVs. I already mentioned the parking spaces, so beware if you have a large car, if you can't get one of the more easily to back out of spots in the back. The parking area could probably maybe fit ----- cars at most.

This property is an awesome find. Its a uniquely renovated furniture showroom and warehouse. The architecture style embraces what once was into a cool place to stay. The rooms and public areas are clean and the beds are comfortable. The staff is superb and very helpful. My husband has been staying there while working on a project nearby. Its a quick walk to the inner harbor and little Italy. Stay here, you'll be glad you did!

The Ritz is very nice and certainly reminds one of times gone by. I stayed for business and will stay again in the future. Service is top notch. The experience is a bit dated - not a bad thing if that is what you seek! At the room prices charged internet should be free!

We stayed at the Marriott Union Square for - days and it was fabulous. From the minute we walked in we were greeted by friendly doormen who on a daily basis were always curteous and extremely pleasant. Robert at the front desk, who checked us in was just the nicest person and went out of his way to accommodate us. We immediately asked him questions about areas of interest and he was patient and kind and took a map out to get us acclimated. The Conceiere Kathy always had a friendly smile and again was patient in helping us navigate our trip. Our room which was a jr suite was huge and we had a beautiful view almost panoramic. Everyday we came back to a very clean room. the hotel was perfectly located and in the heart of exactly where we love to stay. Fabulous shopping and restaurants. I can't see anyone ever staying anywhere else. We will definitely return. It was a fantastic trip!!

I selected Hotel W Lakeshore in Chicago as a place to relax before returning on an - hour flight to Europe after touring some states in the US. I expected a chill down at the shores of Lake Michigan would be perfect. And it was... 
The location of Hotel W Lakeshore is perfect: it sits right at Lakeshore Drive North and as I booked a double double with lakeview we had the best view ever. Also from there it is not far to the Magnificent Mile (Michigan Avenue) on which you find every kind of shop you can imagine.
The hotel itself has a loungy feel to it and can be qualified as a boutique hotel but one withlots of rooms. Breakfast was good but expensive. 
The rooms are nicely decorated and well-kept. Room service is good too.
On a trip to Chicago I would stay there again.

this was a great hotel, very nice, room was fairly large even though it was a single (especailly when compared to other rooms we stayed in in the USA) we had a microwave, fridge, tea-coffee facilities, phone, tv in our room. the ensuite was small but very clean and reasonably new looking. the bed was great. the room was nicely done, and the housekeeping service was fantastic. laundry service was very expensive though. the complimentary bottled water on each floor was great. also they have a guest cuboard on each floor where we could help ourselves to more linen, and tea-coffee supplies. the club room was great, free computer- internet use was available which was really good because thats usually a rarity in the states. they also have a fitness room (very small though) the staff were friendly and helpful. room service was reasonably priced and efficient. we got a good rate through hotels.com of 
$--- US a night inclusive of taxes which was fantastic because it was at least $--- a night cheaper than anything else available . the location of the hotel was very conveniant to the metro station and to various sightseeing options like the white house. its also in a very safe area. we would highly recommend this hotel to others.

Last year in January, I stayed at this hotel and I vowed never to stay again. Although the staff was okay, the hotel itself was horrible. My secretary booked me at this hotel because other area hotels refused my state rate. I must say I was not very pleased until I arrived there. From the moment I walked in, it was obvious something was different. The hotel has changed and looks great! I am especially fond of the colors, decor and restaurant! Most impressed was that there is actually a putting green on property! My room was nice, clean and quiet and the staff was very very friendly. I reviewed this hotel last year after they put me in an exterior room, and it was not a very positive review, but this time around, I must say, I am quite pleased at the changes, I like that they no longer have exterior access rooms and that they have actually taken the time and invested into bringing this stunning building up to par. Hats off to your staff.
JD

This hotel was a huge disappointment - waiting in long lines every time to talk to someone at the front desks, waiting for over -- mins. to be seated for breakfast - not because there weren't empty tables - but because they were short on staff- there's a beautiful outside dining area but we were told we wouldn't be served there- on a Saturday morning with a full hotel, no less -due to a lack of staff. We had made our reservations online, but because we wanted to be assured we had adjoining rooms, also called to speak in person to assure that this need would be met, only to discover when we checked in that the hotel was full and our - rooms were on different floors. After much discussion, I was told there were - adjoining , but they had yet to be cleaned - this was at -pm! I was told housekeeping would call me when these rooms were ready -and waited for over -- min. Having heard nothing and then waiting in line again at the front desk - I was told that the rooms we'd been promised on the --th floor and paid extra for the better view- were not available and should not have been offered us due to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""an incident"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in them, but there were - adjoining rooms on the -th floor that had been cleaned - this said in a tone that suggested I should have known this, We finally got into our rooms around -:-- pm after trying to find someone 
to unlock the baggage storage room so we could retrieve our luggage. Only after expressing extreme frustration was I offered a complimentary buffet breakfast and a refund of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""upgraded room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" fee (only to discover while checking out electronically that those fees were still on the bill - which meant having to wait in line AGAIN at the front desk to have them removed. ) We travel frequently and have stayed at many Hilton's-but I can assure anyone that we never will again.

The roooms have all recently been renovated and look very nice if a bit odd. They are large in size and have great comfy beds. The bathrooms are huge and fairly well appointed although water from the shower typically soaks the bathroom floor. 
I was ill during my stay and the staff was very accomodating in calling ---. I was very grateful for their help. 
The lobby is very small and uninviting. They are currently renovating the restaurant and therefore the lobby area is quite a mess.

A great location-- within blocks of several subway lines, a short walk to Brooklyn Bridge and other great sites. Great price on a decent-sized room over a holiday weekend. Clean rooms, no problems with the staff. Great deli a few blocks away, coffee and groceries are very accessible. I can't wait to stay here again! A great place to call home base while exploring a wonderful city!

I was nervous about booking online, sight unseen, but the reviews of this hotel were all extremely accurate. The hotel is clean and the staff is friendly. Our room was a large two room suite on the -th floor overlooking -rd Avenue, providing hours of entertainment during a huge snowstorm. The subway was close, but we walked to most tourist destinations, even during the snow. There are several decent restarants nearby. We especially enjoyed the bagels at Ess-a-bagel every morning. 
Don't expect fancy decor or the amenities of a large hotel, but do expect room to stretch out, kitchen facilities, a pleasant staff, and a decent rate.

This is an average hotel,but a great value. The room was average and rather small,but, this NYC. It is an excellent location and can easily walk to the attractions. The staff was friendly and I will return if I am in the area again.

Our overall stay was quite pleasant. I did notice the water pressure in the shower was real low and there was a smear or something on the picture glass over the couch. The condiments were a bit skimpy, but all else was fine for the money. We will probably be back.

Upon entering our room, we booked a junior executive suite, we realized our room was handicap accessible (not per our request). We called the front desk to see if another room was available, mainly due to the shower in this room. We were told no, all junior suites are handicap accessible. Ok. We unpacked, went downstairs where, Sean, the conceirge, asked how everything was. Also asked him about the junior suites, not true, they are not all handicap accessible. He offered to have our stuff moved, but we chose to do it ourselves. Upstairs, repack, move, back downstairs. All of this could have been avoided if the front desk person would have be more properly informed. 
The rooms have taken some abuse in the last year. Furniture rather beat up, stained fabric, etc. The couch in the room is not comfortable at all. We had dual TV's, which proved to be interesting. Turn on one, the other one came on, manually turn one off, try to turn the other off while in bed, the other on turns on. The bathrooms are very cold and the shower caddy is useless as the amenities fall out through the slots.
Sean, the conceirge, was very helpful as was Jonah, our bellhop. The front desk staff seemed to be otherwise busy whenever we came or went. The staff at State and Lake is hit or miss. 
Personally, I'd like to see them offer free WiFi, in your room, especially if you pay for an upgraded room.
The hotel is okay, but unfortunately, nothing special. I feel like with a little tweaking they could be great.

The room was very large-- living room and bedroom. The bed was huge and very comfortable. It had a large flatscreen TV with lots of channels. They have a free laundry room which was very clean. The staff was very helpful. The lobby-restaurant area is very large and interesting. Highly recommended.

I never expect much from any airport hotel. So, since I had to attend a conference at this hotel I was stuck. I did not have much hope.
Boy was I wrong! Check in was perfect and quick. The rooms are truly beautiful. The beds and bedding were luxurious. And they were nice and spacious rooms too. The view was not great, but I was there to sleep and work. The lobby is gorgeous and elegant and the staff worked hard to make this Expo successful. I was very pleased.
Incredibly, the restaurants were really good and so was room service. I ordered breakfast every morning and tried the restaurant twice. Sometimes the service was slow but the food was very good.
I would definitely choose to stay here when flying in and out of LAX. 
OH! The one real downer here is their parking structure. What a mess. We had to go down - floors to get to any parking. Now, I know this is because of the Expo, but it was really inconvenient. Otherwise it was a very nice hotel.

We got a great deal on two rooms at the Hotel Mela on hotwire.com. To be honest, we just weren't sure what we were getting, but thought it was worth a chance.. we are so glad that we took that chance! The hotel is one block from Times Square, near the Toys R Us. When we checked in, we were immediately offered a room upgrade, and were allowed to check-in at --:-- since the rooms were ready. One room was small, but just fine for our two girls. The rooms are clean and elegant, the beds are comfortable. They gave us a late checkout, then gladly held our bags until we needed to leave for the train station. We loved the service at this hotel, they asked what they could do for us each time we entered the lobby, helped us with getting a cab, made recommendations of places to go.. the service was impeccable.

Had booked two rooms with two double beds, months in advance of trip. When we arrived had two rooms with king bed in each room. Extremely rude manager said no other rooms available. We asked for rollaway beds were told by someone at front desk that our request could not be accommodated. Cleaning staff employee got us a cot, but asked us no to tell management. Manager told us that if we had made reservation directly through Hyatt instead of Expedia we would have gotten the rooms we requested. I am originally from NYC and had friends from SC with me for a long weekend, our weekend was basically ruined, with three people in one room and four in the other sleeping on rollaways, all the time paying for two double beds we didn't have. The rooms were also very hot, and we couldn't see out the window because of the mold.

Our group of - college friends had a reunion here and were very happy with the hotel. It is in a great location--easy walking distance to both the Loop and North Michigan Avenue shopping and restaurants; the staff was extremely pleasant and accommodating; complementary breakfasts were elaborate and delicious; rooms had full kitchens. They gave us three rooms in our own """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""wing"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", which was great. It appears that they also offer complementary dinners during the week, although we didn't experience them. We definitely plan on returning for our next reunion!

The Omni is not just for staying when in town for a convention...it's a great place for most any reason you're staying in Dallas. There is so much to enjoy, and so many surprises, in the hotel. While the outside of the hotel might seem a bit imposing by day, the evening lighting transforms it into an colorful oasis at night. 
The standard room is outstanding with most every detail thought of. Upscale decor. Artwork you actually want to look at. Electrical outlets all over and just where you need it. Super comfortable bed. Massive bathoom and glassed-in shower area. Seating and workspace arranged in a way that you could stay one night or over a week.
Bob's Steak & Chop House is first class. The Owner's Box sports bar and grill is upscale with a great vibe. The seating areas in the lobby and tucked throughout are generous and conducive for just hanging and visting-meeting.
The biggest surprise and amenity most enjoyed was the rooftop infiniti pool and hot tub. A must experience...it's worth delaying your flight home for half a day just to hang out. Expansive views of Dallas looking both west and north. Covered area with misters for the hot Dallas summer days. And a pool bar & grill that you would only expect at a resort.
When we travel back to Dallas, we plan to stay at the Omni again and hope to schedule an extra day or two just to enjoy it more.

It is Sept --, ---- and I want to let people know that if they are going to be coming to Indianapolis (north east side) and they need a great hotel, this is it!!! My daughter and I have been in this hotel for - days, and it has been a very pleasant experience. My daughter has a life threatening medical condition and we drove from Columbus, Ohio for an (approx -- day medical treatment at the Community hospital of Indianapolis). I was very nervous about coming to a city (I've never been to before) and having to stay for -- days.

I talked to various people at the hospital, about where we should stay for the month... everyone had a different opinion of where to stay. I researched the local hotels (I wanted one that was close to the hospial and it also had to be easily accessible to the freeway.) Well, I am very happy with the accomodations (studio with stovetop, frig, microwave, toaster, toaster oven along with pots and pans, silverwear, towels, and dishsoap too!) Free parking, free hot breakfasts, - free dinners at the hotel per week, free laudry room, free fitness center, free internet-business center with computers, faxes and printers.
