P.S. Three of the staff members have been extremely kind and helpful (Pam, Charles, and Kenny) 
Penny and Gabi (Columbus, Ohio)

We stayed here for a short stopover on our way home from the carribean. We were very pleasantly surprised. The front desk was more than helpful, quick and efficent. Room was clean and bed was comfy. it was just around the corner from Times Square and the Subway. Would definately recommend.

I was pleasantly surprised by my studio suite at the Beekman Towers. Although usually rated at three stars, it was still a very comfortable hotel. The rooms are very clean and spacious. Yes, they are a bit dated and worn, so if that is a problem, you should look elsewhere. The queen bed was quite comfortable and the sheets were reasonably new. I did not try the pull out bed. Having a kitchenette was very convenient. The staff were warm and friendly. We did not eat in the hotel restaurant, but the view from its rooftop location is wonderful. The United Nations Cafe across the street is a good place to go for breakfast. The hotel was not close to the subway, so we took cabs a lot. The neighborhood is worth wandering around. Just to the north there are many consulates and we found Irving Berlin's house just a couple of blocks from the hotel. I would definitely stay at his hotel again.

Just returned from a business trip to NYC and stayed at the Iroquois. Could not have been better. Was upgraded to a --bedroom suite (a pleasant surprise) and the rooms were spacious, clean, lovely and quiet - a premium in NYC. The location is superb, near everything and we walked to everything. Would highly recommend the hotel. The staff could not have been more helpful.

The hotel is just east of the WH and a very short walk to the Mall and monuments. Great location! Rooms are nice, clean and reasonably roomy. We have stayed at the Willard several times in the past and the service and atmosphere remain elegant yet comfortable. Always look forward to our return.

We stayed at the Ritz for one evening before departing for our cruise out of NYC. I have nothing but good things to say about the hotel and its employees. Upon arrival, we were greeted by two doormen, then greeted again in the lobby by our bellman, who immediately offered our two small children new teddy bears, apples and cider. Check-in took about one minute then we were off to our room, which had the best view of the Statue of Liberty. We stayed on the club level, so we had evening desserts and snacks as well as a nice breakfast in the morning. 
Throughout our stay, I was pleasantly surprised at the friendly faces of the staff. The kids had a blast and were content to stare at the view for long stretches of time (for our - and - year-olds, this is not normal). They also got to know some employees well, and were excited to see them. We avoided the crazy long lines to see the Statue of Liberty up close because with our telescope in the room, it felt like we had already been there. 
The other amazing thing was how quiet it is. I hadn't been to NYC in a very long time, and I had never been to Battery Park, but it seems removed from the sounds and the crowds of the city. The only bad part of that is not being able to find a place to have an early lunch directly around the hotel. 
Overall, this is a great hotel. The employees make it worth the slightly expensive price tag.

Good location, pleasant room, reasonable prices. Breakfast and front of house service ok but nothing special. Small bar and lounge area on ground floor pleasant enough. - minute walk to Georgetown which gives plenty of eating, drinking and shopping options.

From the hotel's website, we expected a much more luxurious experience for the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""club floor"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" reservation we paid extra for...still can't figure out where the floor to ceiling windows are in the hotel, having seen nothing that resembled the pictures on the hotel's website. Biggest disappointment was with the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""complimentary"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" appetizer-happy hour. Food selection was minimal--far below what is normally offered at a boutique hotel or B&B--and there was a charge for wine, which was not apparent either from the website or when making reservations. The staff in the continental breakfast """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""club room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" wasn't overly friendly and began putting items away before the end of the posted hours of availability. While our room was nice, it wasn't anything special. However, the location of the hotel was GREAT! One final note...We were somewhat uncomfortable with the fact that anyone could enter the hotel and directly access the elevators, and thus room floors, without a card key.

We needed a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""home base"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for our family of four while visiting Chicago as tourists. We weren't too picky and didn't want to pay the extra --.-- a night some of the nicer hotels were charging for parking. This hotel worked out well, friendly staff, clean, and they gave us a room with a million dollar view. The room was small and the building is dated but you get what you pay for. We were within walking distance of tons of great places to eat, Marshall Field's (Macey's), the Field museum and the Art Institute.

This is the perfect location on the river walk. I spent - night there for a conference and it was great.
The room were nice but worn, room service was very slow nearly close to an hour.
Had a room overlooking the Alamo which was cool

We only stayed here one night while on our way to Lake Tahoe. We loved San Fran. We probably won't stay here again. Would prefer Fisherman's Wharf location. Not much to do around Union Square. Hotel was OK. Check in was simple, pretty good rate. You must valet park. The room was small and I was surprised to find it had no Central A-C. We had to open the windows, which was OK for early May. Rather old building converted to a hotel. Was OK, but wouldn't stay again.

We reserved four rooms this past weekend. We were celebrating my mom's --th birthday in the city so we really wanted everything to be perfect, and it was! When I reserved the rooms in May, Kerri noted that it was a special occasion and made sure we had rooms with city views. The first night, my mom came back to her room to find a wonderful dessert and a balloon from the staff. Thanks Kerri!
Ryan also made sure that all our needs were met during the entire weekend and he ALWAYS had a smile on his face. There were many people in our party with lots of requests and questions. He was amazing and came through every time.
I wish I knew the names of the three women behind the reservation counter who were so nice when we checked in. But thanks also to them. The concierge who was there when we checked in and also on Sunday when we left was extremely helpful and pleasant. Seriously, EVERYONE who works here is HAPPY! 
The rooms were spotless (and I am very picky!) and nicely appointed. The beds and bedding were comfortable. The location was great, but that would have meant nothing without the wonderful staff and the comfortable rooms at this hotel. I found the hotel through Tripadvisor and as usual, the reviews were very accurate.

In Sept ----, we booked four nights at the Marina Motel in San Francisco. The hotel was recommended by a neighbor who stayed here. Our hotel reservations were from Oct --th through November -rd, ----. Unfortunately, hurricane Sandy changed our plans and along with thousands of other folks from the east coast, the airline cancelled our flight. The policy of the hotel is if the reservations are cancelled or modified with less than seven days of arrival or in case of a no-show, ---% of the first night would be charged and in cases of special events or holidays, if the room cannot be rented the full amount would be charged. We called the hotel to tell them about this natural disaster, which we felt was totally out of our control. I spoke to the manager. The manager basically did not care about our troubles, stating that everyone “has an excuse” and that they were charging the entire stay to our credit card, which they wasted no time doing. I asked her if she saw the news, reiterating that thousands of folks cannot fly out from the east coast because of hurricane Sandy. I also reiterate their policy, which stated that we would only be responsible for the first night, noting that I did not book during a holiday or special event. The manager stated that all the hotels up and down Lombard Street were booked and every day is a special event in San Francisco. They were a small hotel and if they could not rebook, we were responsible for the whole bill. Our plans for California were suppose to be for -- nights. All the other hotels and resorts we booked with, having their own cancellation policies, were very understanding of our plight and without hesitation stated they would refund our money. All except the Marina Motel. I will never book at this location again. I felt this is a blatant misrepresentation of the hotel’s policies.

This place is wonderful, i think they must have been apartments at one time. My friend and I met in Sf ( me from Wa, her from Az) with our kids( - kids)the hotel we had booked tried to double our rate, so we left, and found this little jem! It's private, quiet, clean and we had a little kitchen and a garage!! The rooms are on the second floor and the balconies are dripping with flowers! Just lovely! Reminded me of melrose place( I know I know). I am a cheap skate, but I'd definitely stay here again!

My sister and I visited SF Jan ----- to celebrate my birthday. She had originally booked us at another hotel a couple of blocks down the street after doing alot of online research. When we got there however, that room was dark, small, and they had the windows open airing it out because it had a terrible odor in it. Ugh. Fortunately I had brought along information for a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""just-in-case"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" option for us -- The Coventry Motor Inn -- we just walked in the office and asked for a room. Older but clean and fresh-smelling, big room, comfortable beds, huge bathroom, knowledgeable staff and free, although tight, parking. No breakfast but there's coffee in the room and apples in the office. Plenty of restaurants around. Walking distance to another good find -- the Pacific Catch Restaurant on Chestnut St. -- amazing food at a good price -- the fish tacos and sweet potato fries are awesome and the staff are great. We also took a tour of wine country with Tower Tours -- fantastic -- thanks Will! I'd have no problem staying at the Coventry again.

The rooms are nice--a bit on the small side. The bathroom is absolutely tiny. The bed is very comfortable, but is also really high atop a really high boxspring, I guess. It's a bit uncomfortable getting in and out of the bed. Overall, it's a solid Hyatt property, but nothing extraordinary in my opinion.

The only redeeming factor of this hotel is its location and the nice door man. I am BEYOND disappointed in my stay at Affinia Chicago and I would never recommend this hotel. 
My incredible boyfriend booked a stay-cation for my birthday this past weekend at Affinia Chicago. It was my first stay-cation and I was ecstatic. We stayed Saturday July -rd through Tuesday July -th. Upon arrival were greeted by the friendly door man and made our way to our room on the --th floor. The suite was cute, nothing to write home about. I'd say the comfy bed was the highlight of the room. Here's where the trouble began. 
I started to write in detail what made my stay at Affinia Chicago so horrible but I had to stop when the summary turned into a short novel. Instead, I will list what happened. 
Sunday July -rd - My Birthday 
-. The elevators are painfully slow. 
-. No ice machines. Called the front desk for ice, waited an hour before it arrived and by that time we were leaving for the night.
-. That evening attempted to go to C-View. The outdoor deck was closed even though it was early on a holiday weekend. The inside portion of the bar was dark and dingy so we left right away.
-. My boyfriend had arranged to have rose petals on the bed as part of my bday surprise. We returned to our room and there were no roses to be had. The kicker? He had already been charged for it. 
Monday - July -th 
-. Before leaving for the day I put my presents, cards and my bday dinner champagne cork (signed by all my friends) proudly on display on the desk. I returned later that day to find all of my gifts and cards haphazardly shoved into a pile on the corner of the desk by the cleaning staff. What was even worse was that they threw away my signed champagne cork. I was so unbelievably crushed. Oh but the empty Starbucks cup on the coffee table? That was still there. 
-. Our towels were fraying and shedding all over us and our clothing. 
-. That evening we had a few drinks at C-View outside on the roof and the service was horrible. They were slow and kept on getting our orders wrong. Not to mention everything was extremely overpriced. 
-. The Grand Finale: My boyfriend had talked to the front desk about how the flowers he had arranged for the night prior were never delivered despite him being charged. The front desk promised it would be fixed that night. The flowers were never delivered. 
What a truly disappointing experience. It put a damper on my whole birthday.

The appearance of the hotel throughout is nice. It has the look of a small resort. Pool and patio area were very clean and relaxing. We had a great breakfast. I thought the food was great and prices were fair. However my biggest complaint and disappointment was the uncleanliness of both beds in our room and the noise coming from the room next door. There was a large group of college students and the noise was out of control. The noise I understand is not the fault of the hotel. However we should of been placed in a room away from this group. Both issues made our stay very unpleasant. The hotel mgr was professional and very considerate and he did adjust our room rate due to our unfortunate experience.

I am a very particular and travel to DC frequently for work, so I have stayed at many, many properties. The Hampton Inn was wonderful. The feel is much more cosmpolitan than most hotels of that class and this property worked hard to be friendly and welcoming. The room was great and the bed is a very nice new touch from the Hampton Inn chain. I would stay here again as the location is good and the experience was positive.

This place is very busy. It is attached via walkway to two very nice malls. It is close to attractions and universities. The valet parking service was very quick to get your car. The rooms and amenities were very nice. Althouhg the beds were a little soft for me. The staff was plesant and helpful. Our only complaints were that the halways were very cold and there was no free wi-fi in the rooms.

i don't the room was poor. we had a problem with the heat. we called management they came to the room and did nothing. we repeated told the front desk the room was cold. we decided to leave, so we checked out.

The room was nothing fancy but was a good price and very clean. They had free parking a real plus in SF. Walking distance to pier -- area.The people who ran the motel were very helpful. Across from Home Plate (very good breakfasts) and next to Ihop.

Very friendly staff. A very nice hotel ambience with a Concierge ( a bit smug). Softly lighted hallways. Wine tasting every night at -:--. Easy walk to the Wharf area where there are souvenirs to be found with open air vendors and shops. There are hamburger chains nearby and restaurants near the boats. Good short walk. Not many street people asking for handouts. Easy walk to the historic cable car turnaround. Hotel bed was very comfortable and there was a nice comfy couch for late TV shows. The name of the hotel did not bring to mind the quality of this hotel, great choice for a home base while in San Francisco. Valet parking was $-- a day but with a rental car there were few options. There is a parking garage across the street for $-- a day. Safeway and other shops found on groud floor of the garage across the street. Very convienient.

I booked El Gaucho on the back of this site and was not disappointed. I couldnt think of a better place to arrive after a long haul from London. One of the most comfortable beds and duvets Ive ever had the pleasure to fall into, stylish decor and room layout, very usable flat screen and bose system.
A traquil oasis of harmony right in the heart of bussling Belltown. Make your visit to Seattle complete and book it!

I stayed at the Inner Harbor Days Inn when I attended an EMS conference in March. I had attended this conference previously, and had stayed at the Hyatt (*bleagh*) and the Sheraton (not bad). This year I was planning the trip on a budget, and that left the Days Inn.
Wow.
Was I surprised. 
On my arrival the staff was friendly and accommodating. Check-in was a breeze, the lobby was intimate and immaculate. The entire hotel is NON-SMOKING...yes!! $--- a day fee if you're caught pollut...er....smoking in your room. There are only - elevators, but compared to the sloth-like lifts at the Hyatt, these were bullet trains. The room was small but spotless and inviting. Two full beds, newish mattress sets that were quite comfortable to sleep on, and no questionable stains on the quilts. Bathroom was smallish, with a commode and tub...sink and mirror were in the room in another niche next to the closet alcove. The shower was great; good pressure and you didn't have to wait a year for hot water. The room included a small fridge and a microwave; the Sheraton and Hyatt did not. Nice touch, if you ask me. The closet was an alcove without a door for your hanging items, the iron and ironing board, but hey...didn't bother me. Typical TV-armoire setup, with typical hotel channel choices, and pay-per-view movies (no I didn't watch any porn!) One of the nicest perks is FREE in-room wireless Internet access.
That's right....FREE! 
Costs $-- a day at the other, more expensive places, and the free service was much faster! There is a nice desk to surf the Web from. The in-hotel restaurant was good too; typical hotel-inflated prices but the food was yummy. Free USA Today if you want to get dressed and go down to the front desk and grab one. In-room pod coffee maker worked great, and the coffee didn't suck either. The pool was covered due to winter, but the workout room was nicely appointed. Self park for $-- a day (cheaper than the other places by $--day); bring your ticket to the front counter to get it activated so you can come and go as you please by inserting it into the gate machines in the garage. ATM in the hotel lobby too. Easy walking distance to Camden Yards, Metro Station, the Convention Center, and Inner Harbor attractions, even for a chubby chum like me. Street noise isn't too bad, although there must be a Fire Station near, as sirens were audible quite often. 
Minuses: ice machine on my floor was broken initially; fixed in a day. Candy machine ate another guest's money-it was also fixed quickly. Prices for the vending items were the same as you'd find at the local CVS...not inflated like the other hotels. Also, one wall outlet in my room was dead, but only a minor inconvenience. 
I highly recommend this hotel especially if you're just looking for a comfortable place to sleep while you visit the Inner Harbor area. Save money by not staying at the other, higher priced locales.
The hotel was very clean. Most guests were staying there for a relative's wedding and the hotel staff was very nice to our party. The building was very nice and kid-friendly.

I had a great time here, it was quite, clean, and close to everything I needed. I did have a hard time trying to get out on the freeway. I talked to the hotel clerk and he told me how to save time and distance to get on the freeway and to go to the mall across the freeway. He drew me a map which was great. It was a lot faster. You just went around the block. No big deal. Everything I needed is close by. The staff went out of their way to make sure my stay was a great one. The freeway right by the hotel never heard the traffic or cars close by. I would definitely stay there again. The room was big and clean the beds were very comfortable.

The Millennium UN Plaza Hotel is a great place to stay in NYC. Right in Midtown East, close to Grand Central Station, the Empire State Building, the Chrysler Building, and so much more. This is the second time I have stayed at this hotel and I was impressed the first time. The hotel staff was wonderful, we got to the hotel around --:-- am and check in isn't until -:--pm, but our room was ready- which was great!!! They also made reservations for us at a restaurant close by, and made sure we were treated well. The bellhops are always willing to help to get cabs, and any transportation issues.The rooms are very modern and have a cool New York feel to them. The bed was very comfortable and the room was always clean. Our view was spectacular- we could see the Empire State Building, the UN Buidling and the Chrysler Building. At night the city comes alive and our view was great!!! We had Sunday brunch at the Ambassador's Grill (the restaurant in the hotel) which was a little pricey, but very good. I would recommend this hotel to anyone who wants a great deal and a cool place to stay.

We stay at the Alexis for our trips to Seattle. We participated in the Quadzilla series of marathons for Thanksgiving. The staff and accommodations are amazing, We traveled with our dachshunds and the hotel is pet friendly. The hotel is convenient to the SAM, Pike Market and the Pier-wharf.
We recommend this hotel and we plan to stay here again.
The hotel parking is expensive, but there are few options for affordable parking in downtown Seattle

We are a couple in our early --'s that booked through Hotwire on a friend's recommendation and Hotel Fusion is what we got. After booking, we read reviews and instantly regretted using Hotwire but we didn't have a choice so we rolled with it and hoped for the best. 
We stayed at Fusion Jan --, -- & --. This was our first trip to SF and this was also our -- year anniversary. We had let the hotel know ahead of time that we'd prefer a -th or -th floor room (based on reviews) and that we'd be arriving late (--pm-ish). We were assured our request would be honoured. Upon arrival, we were told our room on the -th floor was given away (despite the room was already paid in full a month in advance) so we were given a room on the -rd floor with a room with a king size bed and plenty of room, which was nice. But seeing as the room was on the -rd floor, overlooked Ellis Street and the nightclub below, we were subjected to being woken up --- times a night because of street noise from the nightclub - and we were there mid-week (Tues, Wed, Thurs)!!! We are really easy going but when you just want to sleep due to a busy day of sight-seeing and jet jag, the noise was excessive and we were relieved we only booked this hotel - nights. I can't imagine staying there on a Fri & Sat. 
The positives are that it's an ideal location for shopping, public transportation, restaurants, landmarks, etc. The room was clean and a decent size. There is a continental breakfast that is just okay so we didn't bother. I did see instant oatmeal, oranges, apples, lots of pastries and coffee-tea-orange juice-apple juice.
We didn't use the fitness centre but there really isn't much in there.
I wouldn't recommend this hotel to couples, families or for business - it's just too loud. Possibly a student break crowd?
We loved SF but would look somewhere else to stay.

I stayed at the Houstonian this past weekend for a wedding. The property is beautiful and they have - awesome pools. My son loved the water slide. I loved the award winning gym! It was amazing! 
A few negatives:
ATM machine in lobby was broken.
First floor hallways smelled like musty old wet dogs!
Housekeeping left old cups and plates of old food in our room after """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cleaning""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""

We spent - nights at the Ritz and had a very nice stay. We had an executive suite which had plenty of room for us (- adults, - young children). The room was clean and had decent fixtures (tv's were dated). We also had club privlages, even though we were not on the club floor. The service was excellent during our stay. Everybody was friendly and professional. The hotel is in a central Phoenix location and access to main roads is a breeze. The hotel was clean, except for the pool area which had cigarette butts all around it (hard to criticize the hotel and not the disgusting, thoughtless cigarette smokers). The pool was odd in that it was so small. You would think they would expand it ? The misters were nice, when they were on. One note on the club level - it was mediocre compared to other Ritz club levels in terms of presentation and decor (not bad, just not the best).

The front desk clerk was amazingly friendly both when I checked in and when I checked out the next morning. I was worried about my room, which was the last one on the first floor. It was by vending machines! But I didn't hear much noise except for the sound of the ice dumping, but that cannot be prevented. The rooms were very clean...although outside my room the cleaning crew left two large bags of trash and mopping gear! Other than that my stay was great considering the price! Thanks!

Stayed four nights with out any issues. This HI Express is a little better than most HIE's, within walking distance to Walk of Fame, Kodak Theatre, Hollywood Bowl. Hotel is located a few blocks south of the --- which provides quick access to Warner Bros, Studios, Universal, Dodger Stadium, etc. Entire staff was polite, courteous and accomodating. Only problem that I found was that Highland Ave is busy and left turns in and out of the hotel can be an adventure and due to the street lay out, it is not practical to drive around the block.

We stayed at this place for four nights in April, ----.
The first room we were given was quite large but had two tiny windows facing a court yard. It was very dark and uninviting.
When I called the desk to ask for a more cheerful room I was greeted by an extremely unpleasant woman who told me that I booked the room and I am stuck with it. When I asked to speak to the manager, she told me she was the manager.
The next day I learned she was not the manager, and we were moved to a better room.
Rooms come with a big breakfast, but the breakfast room is understaffed. On a Monday morning one woman was doing all the cooking, all the serving, and all the cleaning. Needless to say tables were piled high with dirty dishes and food was hard to find.
This hotel is not located near restaurants.
The best thing about this place is excellent valet service.
I have added Residence Inn to my list of places to avoid.

When I need to stay in downtown Seattle, I only stay in one of two places, the Mayflower and the Red Lion (-th Ave). This location is the best---Westlake Center is in the same block (and Westlake Center is really """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""ground zero"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for downtown Seatte). The light rail stop is very close (and that is the best and cheapest way downtown from the airport).
But the best thing about the Mayflower is the staff. Five stars isn't high enough for them. When you ask the staff how long they have worked there it's usually decades not years. It's hard to find someone who has been there less than - years---in many other hotels it's hard to find someone who has been there there - years. It's not like working in a hotel is a glanorous job, so the owners and management must be doing something right and it shows. They are loyal to the hotel and guests. 
If you're looking for a place to stay in downtown Seattle, quit looking and book here.

We stayed for a quick weekend at the Days Inn in Lincoln Park. It is at a busy intersection, but we used the fan in the room and it drowned out all the street noise. The rooms were clean; the beds and pillows very comfortable. The staff was very friendly. The complimentary breakfast was one of the nicest we've seen with a pleasant area to sit. Their coffee is very good! We definitely plan to stay there again.

This is a cute little hotel in the Japantown area of Frisco. The staff were super helpful. The decor in the rooms might be a little overpowering for some but the four of us ( all in our --'s & --'s) didn't have a problem with it. The Hotel is on the bus route into the Frisco CBD and it was so convenient to be able to just jump on a bus to get into town. No need for a car in this town, the public transport system is great.
The room was a little small but it had all we needed. There was a balcony that allowed us to gaze over the rooftops and sometimes catch a glimpse of blue sky through the fog.
We loved this little hotel and its atmosphere. We will certainly book here again.

An attractive hotel. Nice rooms. Marina views were enjoyable. All staff - top notch.
However, if you are in for a cruise and without a car it is difficult to enjoy the restaurants,
museums and shopping of the San Pedro waterfront. There are hotels close to these features. The Doubletree offers complementary van transport to close-by attractions but during my stay there was only one driver and the van was often busy. Buffet breakfast was very good but a little high in price. A light breakfast eater would not be pleased.
Again, I would like to complement the management for putting together a great staff.

We had all the space we needed. It was great. The frosted glass bathroom door can make it a little awkward if you aren't with someone you are completely comfortable with though. The roof top view is incredible. It is close to everything and lots of yummy places to eat and drink at close by.

Great hotel, great service, great location, only one shortcoming. No free wifi in the rooms!!!!! hard to believe a hotel of this caliber has no free wifi for the guests . Other than that it was superb!

We read the reviews and were influenced by them and were not disappointed. The hotel is in a great location, near enough to everything but away from the madness of Times Square. Don't come for romance, quaint surroundings, upscale treatment, or relaxation. However, if you have a convention here or a great deal from an onine travel site, don't hesitate.

I stayed here for a few days with business in Shelton. The service was superb (check in, bell hop, car service). The room was huge and immaculately clean. Although I didn't use many of their services the ones I did use were top notch. I will definitely stay there again.

A very good hotel, very cozy, clean and friendly atmosphere! The staff at the front desk was very helpful when we asked directions or were in need for some ideas to explore the area.
The hotel's location is very good to explore all of Seattle, public transport or a taxi can get you everywhere in a short time..
It was also fun to enjoy the free cupcakes and coffee they served in the afternoon.

This hotel is really not close to the Riverwalk. You can find a nicer hotel DIRECTLY on the Riverwalk for the same price. The breakfast featured frozen potatoes, as in they were NOT cooked. The US Grant was one of the nicest hotels that we have ever stayed in. Everything was perfect from the room to the staff and don't have a single complaint. Great hotel we booked on hotwire so I felt it was a great value for what we paid! Wish the WiFi had been free...that would be my only recommendation for this hotel.

(-). The staff - all of whom were extremely friendly and helpful. and (-). The quality and comfort of the beds was exceptional. I slept so well every night.

This hotel has the privilege to be located at the center of Times Square. Hence you are near many opitions of restaurants, stores, museums and art galleries. The modernity of W branch is very well recognized at this hotel. The service is good and the room amenities are very clean. Some could find the hotel pricy.

The hotel was in a great location. The staff were friendly and attentive. Our room was very small, but it was clean and quiet with spectacular views. My husband and I travelled from Australia and having done a lot of research chose to stay in the W Times Square first and then the Bowery. What a difference. The w staff were nice but stiff. I traveled to Washington DC for two nights to attend a meeting at the Ritz Carlton in February ----. Overall, the hotel was very nice--attentive staff, large and luxurious room, and great meeting facilities. 
I arrived late in the evening. I took the Metro to get to the hotel. The Foggy Bottom Metro stop is very close to the Ritz, maybe about - blocks. I must applaud them for their meeting set-up. We had a medium sized group and took up one smaller ballroom. The service provided for the meeting (food, facility, coffee, snacks, etc) was outstanding. The lunch and breakfasts were delicious and more than I normally expect.
The hotel is only about a mile away from the Lincoln Memorial. There are numerous restaurants very close by to choose from. As I mentioned, the Foggy Bottom Metro stop is very near as well. After my meeting adjourned, I walked to the Lincoln Memorial, then through the Mall to the Holocaust museum, then took the Metro back to Foggy Bottom. While it was a good long walk, it was totally doable.
At the time of departure, my check-out was very fast. The door and bell staff were so helpful, and I was quickly on my way by taxi to Reagan airport, which was only a $--.-- cab fee away!
I would definitely stay here again if I return to Washington DC. The rate was actually lower than many other """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""luxury hotels"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in the area, but I still felt well taken-care-of and quite pampered. Overall, I think this hotel is a great value--you pay a little less, and still get the outstanding Ritz-Carlton service.

I tried to make a reservation under a block of rooms for an upcoming conference. The website for the conference said that the hotel still had rooms open as of today. We were looking forward to a --star hotel stay here- as has been rated misleadingly by many here but this is simply a contemporary hotel incorporating high technology like water features and dramatic lighting to add a theatrical appeal to its otherwise obviously tourist class category.

Because of the early mornings for work, there was still a lot of food available at their continental breakfast around - - -:-- am.

Very nice hotel with perfect location, you cannot be wrong about this when booking the Baldwin. The rooms are so clean that you definitely feel cozy there. The room was a bit small and furniture a little old, but as a group of friends traveling, it was the best bang for our buck. I highly recommend for groups of - or - to stay downtown and enjoy SF for a few days.

Hi, just returned from visit to San Francisco, staying at the Radisson, Fishermans Wharf, what a place! Nothing to complain about at all!!

We stayed here for two nights in early August family of four we had a room with kitchenette which was perfect for our family with -- and - year olds the rooms and all public areas were spotless I've stayed in hundreds of hotels throughout the USA and Europe this was at the top for clean well maintained rooms. Just got home from a - night stay at the Embassy Suites Downtown Chicago - Lakefront (Mar -----). Stayed here for a week and it was ok until after - nights new guests moved in next door. Woken up at -a.m. by the smell of cigarette smoke and loud voices coming from next door. We chose this hotel for its location and the fact that it had recently been renovated. We were not disappointed. 
We were told that we should have stayed at the Palace, but we disagree.
And a very good Ceasar Salad in the restaurant.

Looking for a really inexpensive hotel near to all the great sights? If you aren't worried about not having a walking friendly location or aren't expecting more than basic accommodation, then this is for you. We basically slept there, and it was comfortable enough. Did not appreciate the very loud and somewhat alarming neighbors on our floor at -am in the hallway, but that is not the hotels fault. Wallpaper peeling in our room, but it had all the basics and nice TV. Did not try the restaurant so we can't comment. The shuttle service to get you to your location was good, a big plus if you needed to get somewhere at night. Underground parking was also good.

Booked one night at this hotel via Priceline and called the Hyatt - weeks and also two days before my arrival to note room preferences. Feels very much like the old Days Inn it used to be. The lobby has certainly been cleaned up (isn't it always?), but the rest leaves a lot to be desired. Beat-up parking lot and stairs, gross pool area, generally dingy feeling from the moment you exit your car till you enter your room.

The room was very nice - we had a corner room on the --th floor and the views were great. The bathroom was a little small and there was little counter space. Otherwise its a great value for the location.

Do stay here it is a great hotel in a great location walking distance to Time Square and Central Park. Friendly Service and very good staff. The Resturant located in the lobby is a very good place for breakfast we travel with children and they enjoyed every minute of their stay the personal in the resturant are very knowegeable about the city we had two wonderful staff people a young man by the name of John Williams Bus Attendant and a lady which name i dont remember but she was a joy also thank you for making our stay a very enjoyable one for Me and my Family. Looking forward to the next time we vacation in New York City.

Wonderful room with very comfortable bed. Clean and calm. Good aircondition, low noise. Nice view on from hotel window. Hudge fitness center with free access, good workout possibilities.
No free internet connection, -- USD per day is very expensive.
Located perfectly for enjoying nightlife around time square.

For some reason I found the standard room much nicer than the apartment, not sure if it was refurbished, because the furniture was a little used but I felt comfortable in this room. The room was clean, the only problem was the bed, it was quite narrow for me and my partner. Otherwise the room is very good value for money, because it is apartmentlike with very good location and also cheaper then most of the hotels in this area. The front desk staff is always very professional and housekeeping does an outstanding job with the rooms-suites, public areas, and the breakfast room. You can't ask for more---one block from a metro station, within walking distance of museums and government buildings, and a very good continental breakfast to start the day. Can't wait to go back!

The staff and I mean all of the staff were friendly, considerate and attentive. In addition I was really impressed with the cleanliness of the entire hotel which included our room and extended to the car park. 
I will definitely stay at the Inn at Venice Beach should I be traveling to LA again.

The quality of this hotel has really gone done hill in the last few years. Room service trays from our next door neighbor stayed on the hallway floor for entire days. We battled gnats daily in our room. This was the middle of January!! I don't have any clue what all the fuss is about this hotel. We will never stay there again!!

Overall, I would once again try the other two Hilton properties before this.

Arrived late on a Wednesday night to be told that our room of two double beds was not available and that they only had one with a King. I told them that was completely unacceptable and to keep looking. I looked her straight in the eye and held eye contact until she said she would go talk to a manager and I told her that was probably a good idea. My children saw the look and walked to the other end of the lobby :) Miraculously, the gentleman playing the role of manager for that moment came out and found us a room with two double beds - I also had to ensure that it was a club level floor because I booked that hotel based on the amenities that come with the club level (breakfast bar, snacks and appetizers). The room was right across from the elevators but we did not hear them at all. After we got into our room and saw the two beds and checked our keycard to make sure it got us onto the club floor, I was happy. The rooms are well appointed, not very large but the location cannot be beat. You can access Grand Central Terminal without even going outside and the shuttle to Times Square is perfect. The breakfast bar, snacks and appetizers were an incredible deal, especially for two teenagers who eat nonstop! I would stay again but only with the upgrade to the club level.

The hotel is in an old bank. It's a cool building. It would have been nice if Marriott decided to embrace the uniqueness of the bank versus using numerous modern colors that frankly clash.
But!!! The Front Desk staff and people who serve breakfast are AWESOME! They were so friendly and helpful with any question we asked. They went the extra mile. 
The studio room is just right for a couple. Families would benefit from getting the two bedroom suite. We did a family weekend so I was able to see both set-ups. Both were very nice. The studio has a stove-top, refrigerator, dishwasher, microwave. The - bedroom had a full size oven along with the other items.
Valet attendants friendly and $-- not bad, we took the cars in and out and it didn't cost anything extra.
The breakfast was very tasty and a large variety of items. Definitely a place I'd stay again.

I spent - nights at this hotel and LOVED every second. The staff are extremely nice, helpful, and genuine; the decor and rooms are very comfortable and refreshing; and the location is perfect. I will definitely stay here every time I visit.

This is a beautiful place to stay. Very tropical with updated rooms and amenities. Best part---the parking. Nothing better than getting back to your room late and parking right at your door! The bungalow style rooms really are the way to go. No elevators or people walking in front of your window...and the patio in back with your own chairs and mini """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""yard"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" truly is enjoyable!

A truely lovely boutique hotel this is. I've stayed in other hotels and B&Bs in this city. Yet, despite the lack of a couple things, I put this one in the top -% for so many reason. I will absolutely stay here again. 
My daughter and I went San Fran to visit The Academy of Art University in January. Not normally a good time of year in SF, but we lucked out and had warm, sunny weather, while yet another snow storm raged in Colorado and other parts of the US.
The Art Academy has a relationship with The York Hotel just a few blocks away. However, we wanted to be just a little closer to the shopping and the Academy, and the York's twin beds just didn't really fit our needs. We also didn't want to share a bed. The Rex offers - dbl beds in a room, which was perfect for us.
Excellent location in the Union Sq area. Beautifully decorated, very comfortable beds, lots of power outles in good locations, clean (tho the carpet looked a bit worn, but not too badly). Wonderful, intimate restaurant where we were able to have a late night dinner our -st night there. Good thing too as we checked in late and were dead tired. 
There's A-C in the rooms if you need it, which we didn't of course. The control for the heater was a bit hard to locate, but actually, I didn't even know it was in the room until the -nd day. I just happen to notice it by accident. Good thing I did too as the room was chilly at night. 
All rooms have FREE WiFi, a well stocked mini fridge, gourmet snacks (expensive, but handy if you don't feel up to going out), and excellent cell phone reception. The bathroom was a bit small, but well appointed. The water pressure was great and there was plenty of hot water, even at - am. Our room was on one side of the hotel with not a very nice view, but to be honest, I didn't care. It was quiet. I'd rather have little view and a peaceful room as I'm a light sleeper. 
The elevator was small and slow, as I'd read in other reviews, but it's an old hotel so I didn't mind. It's part of the charm when you are staying in historic style places. There was a note about it being replaced very soon anyway. When I was tired of waiting, I just walked up or down the stairs and stopped to check out each floor if I needed a rest. Best of all were the very friendly and helpful staff. I really appreciated all the help they gave me. They were warm, friendly, knowledgable and professionable too.
I chose this hotel based on location, on reviews I had seen here, on their website and - other review sites, for the Friday evening Jazz performance. However, our plane was delayed, so we were unable to attend the entertainment.
Funny thing was I discovered several of the employees attend the Art Academy. We talked extensively with the female bartender who was one student we met. Everyone was exceptional, even the housekeepers (of course tipping well helps too). Bravo!
The only things I could complain about are the lack of a swim pool and hot tub, which would be nice to soak in after a long day walking, site seeing, shopping, beach going, etc. Also, the restaurant was closed for remodeling on the weekend, but there was a small continental breakfast put out for the guests. However, the food went quickly. And anyway, there are pleanty of good restaurants to go out to very nearby for any sort of meal you might want. So, who cares?
I especially liked the intimate bar-library- lounge area. Very homey and comfortable. Free glass of wine each evening for adults and juice or soda for the kids too. Might be nice to see a little snack for children, such as cookies, or cheese, crackers and fruit. Good selection of top shelf liquors. I might suggest they have out a few games perhaps to keep people entertained and staying in the bar to drink and order more snacks, especially children. Plenty of books to borrow tho in there. And be sure to check out the drawings on the walls.
One last thing... This hotel is about a half block away from the Powell St. Trolley. I suggest you get a multi-day Muni pass and take full advantage of riding the trolleys and buses as walking up and down hills get difficult when loaded down with luggage and shopping bags. You can buy them at the airport, train and bus stations and a few other locations. Well worth it if you are in town for a few days. Beats paying $- per ride on the trolleys. Also beats driving, paying very high gas prices, and paying high rates for parking.
The Hotel Rex is part of a small group of boutiques hotels. Check out their website: http:--www.jdvhospitality.com-hotels-hotel--- . I have yet to stay in the others, but am thinking of trying another for my next trip out there in June. But I may just come back to Hotel Rex as it's pretty hard to beat them. I so love smaller establishments.

Stayed a night in an executive room (which they upgraded us to at check in, free). By far one of the most spacious hotels I've been in while staying in SF, probably since it's newer than all the rest and located in the FiDi. Clean room, comfortable beds, modern amenities, quick and friendly service, there's really nothing to complain about. The room we stayed in on the --th floor facing North had a large unimpeded view of the piers, North Beach area with Coit Tower, and you could see well into the north when it wasn't cloudy.
I wasn't here as a tourist but if you are one, the only thing really close is the Ferry Building, everything else is a decent walk or drive so keep that in mind. The area is the financial district therefore at night its a complete ghost town and you'll be hard pressed to find anything open.

My husband and two grown up sons and l stayed here in a one bedroom apartment for - nights. We found it to be very clean and spacious, the bathroom was nice, the shower was good, always lots of hot water. We had a lovely kitchen, fully equipped. The bedroom was very big, lots of storage and comfy bed (firm ). 
The location of the apartment was not ideal, but we managed, it is so easy to get a taxi (which is economical when there are four of you). 
On the downside, the sofa bed in the lounge where our sons slept was awful, a very thin mattress, not comfortable at all. We asked reception if we could pay to upgrade to a two bedroom apartment after the first night, they told us we couldn't because we were not staying long enough. Then we asked for a rollaway bed, they never seemed to be able to find us one. I don't think they could be bothered. We ended up having to buy an airbed and one son slept on it on the floor.
There was construction noise going on day and night which also made it difficult to sleep. We have since found out this happens in lots of places in Manhattan. 
Nevertheless we had a great holiday and we loved New York we will definitely be going back, maybe stay midtown next time.

I stayed at the Belvedere this past weekend based mostly on reviews from this website. They were absolutely right! It is in a great location, close to everything with a subway stop right around the corner and Times Square - blocks away. Clean, reasonably priced hotel. 
I would stay here again.

...unfortunately, it's located on Bunker Hill, which my friends and I renamed Homeless Hill, due to the HUGE number of homeless people who spend all day and night there. I stayed at the Omni over Labor Day weekend this year (---- to ---). I had a corner room with a king bed. The room was fantastic--bed was very comfy, it was clean, and quiet. The bathroom was very large, but the tiles were a little outdated--no big deal, as it was very clean and had everything you could ask for (hair dryer, shampoo, conditioner, body wash, soaps, mouthwash, cotton balls and swabs). The hotel is adjacent to California Plaza, which was very convenient as there was a small convenience shop (Farmiga, I think?) which was open very early to late at night, and it had all sorts of beverages, snacks, breakfast sandwiches, and beer-wine. I think I went there every day for something to drink and snack on. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Angel's Flight"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" funicular is also adjacent to the hotel, so we took that down the hill and went to the market, which was very interesting, but the large number of homeless people milling about left us a little uneasy. I never felt unsafe near or in the hotel, but I also would not choose to go walking around the hotel after --p or so. The hotel staff was very accommodating and quick to help, which was wonderful. Sign up for their frequent guest program (do this when you check in, if you haven't already!) and they bring you a LARGE bottle of water every evening with turn-down service! I was staying at the hotel with a sports team, so I didn't choose the location, but after my pleasant stay, I'd definitely stay here again and recommend it to anyone who was traveling to L.A. (downtown area).

If you want - star luxury then the Astor is probably not for you but if you want a clean comfortable room, with friendly helpful staff with a subway opposite then it is ideal.
We used the hotel as a base and although it is a bit off the beaten track the subway was cheap and easy to use and ran --hours- a daily ticket is $--buses also run past the hotel.
There is nothing flashy about the Astor- it does not pretend to be a luxury hotel but we really enjoyed our stay and had more money to spend on christmas shopping,shows and meals as it was a cheap break.
A delightful surprise was the view from our room. The blinds were down on the window and I decided to raise them to get some light in the room and WOW- what a spectatular view!! The entire Manhattan Skyline-- you wont get a better view from a - star hotel!!!! Check out photo!!! I spent a lot of time at that window- it was great by day but breathtaking at night- that alone makes me recommend the Astor-- a little Gem on the park

This was a great hotel for an overnight stay in order to catch a flight at the airport. Rooom was comfortable, although the view wasn't the greatest. I especially liked the gym, all the equipment was in working order and was adequate to get in a quick workout. Wifi worked beautifully, it was free since I am a AT&T wireless subscriber. Parking rate is on the high side, however, if you don't need in-out privileges, there are less expensive parking lots available within walking distance. Transit to downtown is next door, and takes about -- minutes. Transit fare to downtown was more than reasonable. I would definitely stay here again..

Stayed two nights over President's Day weekend. Rooms were a little on the small side but very clean. Bed was very comfortable. Service was great - valets and doormen all very helpful and offered unsoliticed advice on nearby dining options. Front desk took immediate action when an adjacent room had alarm clock going off at midnight - guests weren't in the room but the staff took care of it.
Great shops and restaurants all around, and this hotel is an easy -- block stroll to all the wonderful historical sights. Considering the Latham is basically across the street from the much-more expensive Sofitel, my Orbitz rate of $--- per night made this even better. Have already recommended it to others.

This Ho-Jos is dirty, and very old and smelly. I would not every stay there. I was very disappointed. I took my son their for a game at Fenway and we just wanted a place to put our heads after the game. However, the place was so gross that we decided to drive -.- hours home in the middle of the night then to stay in the FLEE BAG HOTEL. Also, it was -- degrees that day and the POOL IS CLOSED FOREVER!! This is my first FLEE BAG HOTEL. Do not stay here.

Short and simple, Christine the general manager, Tina, her assistant and RENE the best valet in the entire city are picture perfect. I will spare you the saga of horrible Chicago trip, but these three people turned a nightmare into a cake walk. They will never understand the gratitude of our family. Tip RENE well please!! He is wonderful!!!
Perfect for trains, subway, shops (Macys) & Tick Tock Diner is FAB. Room great - only slept in it anyway!

There are several hotels within walking distance of this hotel. Choose one of those. The list of negatives are numerous. First: The room was dirty. The floor not vacuumed. The shower moldy. The fixtures in need of repair. A dirty wash cloth in the shower. etc. Second: The air conditioning never cooled the room. So we just sweat all night. Third: Only one """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""partial"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" roll of toilet paper. Fourth: There were at least ----- unsupervised kids and teenagers in a -ft deep dirty pool from the time we checked in until the pool closed. Fifth: The elevators were very slow, taking as long as -- minutes to go up or down. We were on the --th floor. Sixth: The parking was way to far away from the hotel and way too dark at night. Seventh: The staff was less than helpful, with the exception of the housekeeping staff member who had to bring us a roll of toilet paper late in the evening. Bottom line... you would expect far better from a Hilton. We were scheduled to staty at this Hotel again this week when coming back through Memphis... No Thank you. We'll choose another...

This hotel was excellent! One of the best I've every stayed in. Friendly staff, spotless room, and very comfortable, as well. We were visiting our son in college; and this is the first time we tried the Roundhouse. It will be the only place we stay from now on. Reasonably priced; and no complaints!

The Roosevelt Hotel is located about -.- blocks from Grand Central Station in Manhattan. It is central to so many well known sites. The hotel has character and class. Our room was confortable with great beds The rooms are smaller than the newer hotels but they are big enough. We had - adult family members in one room. I would not recommend a room next to the elevator. It could get noisy. The was not noise from next rooms or hallway. We did eat there or use the bar. .The hotel is old but that is part of the charm. It is well maintained , clean , good service. Everyone is willing to answer questions and help first time visitors to New York. I give it a high recomendation for comfort, location and service.

Make no mistake this hotel is older and is a budget hotel. Once you get over those two facts its an excellent hotel for those with realistic expectations. The rooms are clean and functional with free wireless internet. Union Square and Fisherman's Wharf are both a quick bus ride away with a MUNI stop right on the corner. Yes, there are homeless around, but there are homeless everywhere in SF and no more here than on the blocks with $--- plus a night hotel rooms. Great restaurants on the same block Mel's and Tommy's Joynt (recently featured on Food Network). The ice machine is in the basement and there is a porn store across the street, but if you aren't into experiencing a little character then why are you in San Francisco? Overall this hotel was great especially for the price and we'd stay there again.

I stayed for the weekend with family and friends at The Muse. The stay was wonderful. The rooms were spacious and very clean. The service was excellant and the staff were friendly and very helpful. This was our third trip to New York in the last two years and our stay at The Muse was by far the best. We have stayed each trip in Time Square. The location was also great.

Planned a trip to Sea World, booked online at the Heritage Inn. Was a horrible place we were in then out in - mins, I noticed the Holiday Inn Express as we were driving to the Heritage Inn and decided to see if they had any rooms available. Very friendly staff, felt safe. The room was very clean and spacious recently done up. No complaints at all except there is not alotta good tv channels, lol. There is a fridge and microwave in room. Stayed with my two small children. Arrived at night and area around hotels was not desireable looking but I felt good in my room. Dennys and CVS right across the st, Will recommend spending a lil extra for the comforts and securities especially with kids!

I went to Travaasa not really knowing what to expect. It was so much more lovely than I'd imagined it would be. The grounds in the hills of the lake country above Austin (near Lake Travis) were wonderful--they looked just like the gorgeous Texas Hill Country summer camp in Kerrville where I'd worked as a counselor in college. This is very much like a five-star, exculsive, summer camp for grown ups. There are trails and places to sit quietly and meditate. There is a big exercise-fitness center, horesbackriding, yoga, and other activities. Best of all, there's a glorious spa with a pool that has arresting views. I had the Willie Nelson-inspired """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""On the Road Again"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" massage (Rhianna was great--I asked for a real deep-tissue massage). They played soft Willie Nelson ballads and massaged me with hemp oils! Very clever and very nice. Soooo Austin. The pool and hot tub were nice after all that. There's an infinity edge pool on the hillside. You can see for miles--all the way across the (all too low this season!) lake. And the rooms are outstanding. Each has it's own balcony or patio overlooking miles and miles of hill country. Everything in the room was new and very tastefully done. The bathroom was enormous. There was no tub in my room, but the shower had great pressure. There were wine tasing classes while we were there, and mealtimes in the dining area (with its vaulted ceiling) were nice. Sitting outside in the morning to have coffee was lovely, too. The staff was gracious and helpful, and they were quick to stop and ask if I wanted a lift when they'd come by with a golf cart to go from one end of the sprawling property to the next. The GM turned out to be someone I'd met at another five-star resort property a few years back--Travaasa is lucky to have Tim here now. Travaasa is truly a destination experience-driven resort. I made the big mistake of having set up plans in downtown Austin for the first night I was there. The moment I got to the property, I didn't want to leave it for a minute the whole weekend. Go there and plan to leave the world outside the gate. It's so restful and serene. I really can't say enough about how nice it was, and I'm pretty picky.

I don't understand why this hotel has gotten some less than flattering reviews. I had a big corner room on the --th floor with unbelievable water and city views from glass walls. The room was terrific - with a huge comfortable bed, a great bathroom (with large mirrors and lighted makeup mirror) and comfortable desk with internet access. The front desk staff was courteous and helpful, the room service food was great - and delivered when promised - and there was no noise from adjacent rooms (a previous reviewer had warned about paper thin walls). Don't be scared off by the other review - this place is great. I'll definitely be back.
Expensive, Terrible valet parking situation. Many maintenance issues. Poor service at front desk. Food situation poor.

I'm sure at one time the Lord Baltimore was the place to go. They don't build hotels like this anymore. Unfortunately they have not kept up with the maintainence. The carpets were shoddy, the rooms were outdated. They didn't even have a light by the bed. No clock. A TV from the ---- with reception to match. Not a place I would go back to

My husband and I stayed at the Omni for a business meeting. The location was great! LOVED the sports bar food. The lobby was set up with comfy sofas and chairs, creatively positioned to provide an intimate setting for friends to gather. Had our happy hour there. Enjoyed my morning coffee at the rooftop pool area. Very relaxing and visually beautiful. The workout facility is located close to the spa and pool area. Towels and earphones are provided...great facility. Our room was huge and very luxurious. Lots of pillows!!! Loved the TV in the bathroom as well as the lighted makeup mirror! The toiletries were definate keepers. My favorite thing was the hidden nitelight (under the nightstand) that comes on should you need to get up during the night. The vibe of the hotel was perfect....not so fancy that you felt uncomfortable, but very, very lovely. Lots of neat shops to grab a snack or purchase upsale gifts. I hope to return next year!

I stayed here years ago, it felt small, cramped and like I was in another country. And yet, my husband and I often talk about Foley's Inn and what a unique experience we had. I don't even remember any of our other hotels!

The rooms are very nice, large, comfortable, tasteful. Denny's is across the street if you need your dose of Denny's. We stayed in the leftmost wing (I believe it is wing -) and some of those rooms have a view over a pond which is very nice. the workout room was just at the end of the hall, and had all the machines you might want in it (I really appreciate this). the chocolate chip cookies were very lovely. The price was not the most lovely thing about it, but it certainly is convenient for the airport!

I stayed for the President's day weekend in a double bed """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""suite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", which is really nothing more than a large room. Not even a room divider. It came with a mini fridge and microwave. It had a small couch and two double beds. New --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" flat panel HDTV, but only a very limited selection of HD channels.
The room was certainly large enough to accommodate two queen beds, but they only put in doubles. 
It does have an indoor pool, hot tub and work out room which are adequate, but nothing spectacular.
The self serve free breakfast was okay and included waffle maker, sausage patties, hot eggs, cereal, breads, but the coffee was awful.
Other than a business office park not much else around in the immediate area besides a gas station and fast food joints.

Stayed here to visit friends and its updated over last year in the front lounge area with a modern bistro style restaurant with healthy food choices and a gym with free weights. Rooms are atill a bit dated. Small resort style pool area.

I would stay here again... Its a great location, has plenty of restaurants-bars-etc nearby, has a Starbucks and a great sports bar in the hotel. I valet parked my car, which they charged $-- for, a total rip off, since basically I parked it, and they just let it sit there in front of the hotel, then handed me my keys back. The Valet guys were all --yr old D-Bags, but the hotel is pretty cool. Its both a Residence Inn and a Courtyard, so they offered me a suite with a kitchenette for the same price as a regular room. The area isn't exactly quiet, especially on a saturday night. The area is full of young beautiful people and the local restaurants and bars are very hip. Its a safe part of town...

Really enjoyed our stay at the Rittenhouse. Very nice rooms and service. A central location that allows you to walk to everything - Liberty Bell, convention center, universities and restaurants. Will definitely stay here again when in Philly.

Stayed here for two nights on business. Made reservations calling directly to the hotel and got one night (two rooms) at a very good rate and the next night at standard rate. However, at checkout the lower rate was not applied and I had to show the email confirmations to the desk personnel. Even with that, he had to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""check with the manager"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Also, one of the two room keys did not open the door... I took it back to the front desk and the staffer told me that I was mistaken, that it was coded correctly and it did work. Really?? Glad I had a second key is all I can say. On a positive, the beds were quite comfortable and the room darkening curtains help make a good atmosphere for sleeping. The bathroom was an adequate size with good, heavy towels and Molton Brown shampoo (the best!!). Internet is an additional charge and the room service menu is varied but expensive. TV remote would not power on-off, only change channels which was a little annoying. You have to request your bed to be made up if you stay more than a night and there is no turn down service. The present in hotel restaurant is VERY good but small portions and it has not done enough to create a niche. According to the doorman, it will be replaced soon with a more main stream menu-price point place. Speaking of the doormen... wow are they great at information, directions, finding the right transporation mode for you! Kudos to them. Concierge desk was polite, efficient and knowledgeable. Maid service personnel were very pleasant.

All I can say is, SCARY!!!! DO NOT STAY HERE unless you're completely desperate!! Room was musty smelling, tub had sinking floorboard so water couldn't drain out, the bathroom door was screwed together in pieces, you could hear every footstep above you, heater-AC didn't work for more than - minutes, no outlets to plug your wall chargers into; only - plug outlet that was bolted to a table, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""breakfast"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" consisted of a small dried out muffin, and parking was a joke! They would double-park people behind you, but not get their information as whose car it belonged to, so if you wanted to leave, like we did, they didn't have the information to know who to tell to move it! They want you to give them your keys so they could move it, but no one did. Some lady was late for work because the desk clerk didn't want to wake someone up at -:-- in the morning to have them move their car! There was a party on the second story balcony, but they didn't ask them to quiet down at --:-- at night and beyond. The staff was friendly, but spend the extra money and find a place with a nicer room and a real breakfast; it will save you money in the long run! Unless you're homeless, don't stay here! The pictures they post on their website is not what the rooms look like; trust me!

A quirky, unusual hotel. The rooms are small, but this is New York. We had the bunk beds and the stairs to the top bunk were very uncomfortable on bare feet (metal bars). There was nowhere to store clothes, just a couple of hangars on a hook. But it was workable. The shower was nice, although the water did not drain very well. The sink was in the sleeping area. The beds were very comfortable and the room was quiet.
We had to wait over an hour past the check in time to get our room. Upon returning to the room later that evening, there was a note on the chair apologizing for the delay with a gift of two of their soaps on a rope.
The staff were very friendly and helpful.
There was always a large lineup for the Stumptown coffee.
The lobby bar was very dark and by the afternoon was very, very crowded and very, very noisy. I would never want to sit there and have a drink, even assuming that one could find a seat.
The location of the hotel was very good with a subway stop around the corner.
I am not sure if I would stay there again. I do prefer a slightly larger room, a quieter, brighter lobby and it is nice to at least get coffee in the lobby in the morning and a light breakfast would be nice too. I definitely see the appeal of this hotel, but maybe not for everyone! And having The Breslin and John Dory right there is a real plus.

We ended up at this hotel after a home stay with a friend didn't turn out. 
Anyhow, the hotel is perfectly located for people wanting to look around Hollywood. The room was a good size and very clean. The beds were super comfortable. Staff were friendly and helpful. 
Tip...get to breakfast early as seats are limited (we managed to share with other people though)
Only two slight negatives -) the wifi connection was free but a little unreliable in our room. -) our room was non-smoking but it smelled somewhat like it was a smoking room in a former life. Neither of these issues were deal breakers (despite my aversion to cigarette smells) we enjoyed our stay and would recommend the hotel.

Hotel Angeleno was a great choice for our annual girls only mini vacay. From the complimentay valet parking to the warm greetings by the front desk reps. Hotel Angeleno was the perfect choice for us. Sunset Blvd is footsteps away and everything that we wanted to do was easily accessible from the hotel. I enjoyed the delicious apples that were offered to the hotel guest daily and the peaceful, sound-proof room that we stayed in. Even though we were right off the --- HWY, overlooking the beautiful mountains of California, the sound of the traffic was more invigorating than annoying.
The customer service offered at Hotel Angeleno was awesome. It made us smile each time we arrived and one of the hotel reps said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Welcome back ladies,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and we'd reply """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Heeeeyyy!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" LOL!!! One down side is that the room was kinda small BUT we made the best of it.
 I would definitely save at the Hotel Angeleno again.

We booked the hotel last minute on our trip toAlaska. The staff was efficient, the room clean and an excellent value for the money. The Torchlight parade took place in front of the hotel the night we stayed for an added bonus!

Check you room out carefully before you accept it!
We were allocated a room on the --th Floor which was filthy - dirty carpet that was ruffled up - dirty bathroom - dirty mirrors, these had not been cleaned for ages - overall it felt 'creepy'
Were moved to a room on the -th floor which was fine, it seemed to have been recently refurbished.
The lobby was very attractive and staff helpful.
Position could not be bettered.
Just check you rooms!

Stunning resort, beautiful landscaping, gardens-pools-beach. Excellent service, private bungalows. Very central location - rent a car and get to Balboa Park (Zoo), Sea World, Coronado Island, Gaslamp area and Little Italy, Mission Bay and the Ocean Walk and La Jolla very easily. Favourite thing to do: catch breakfast at the 'Best Breakfast on the Beach' restaurant just behind the RollerCoaster at Belmont Park, right on the beach next to the Ocean walk. From -am in the morning, everything from omelettes to waffles to fruit bowls - watch the surfers catch a wave, relax and enjoy the food and the view.

We enjoyed our - nights here. The first room we were given was pretty worn out. They moved us to a better room. It is an old hotel so shows signs of wear but still has a nice feeling to it. The common areas and hallways are redone and nice too. We enjoyed the evening happy hours and they have a good selection of complimentary beer and wine. Location excellent to transportation. Took BART to and from airport so did not need a car. Public transportation in the city is great. Morning breakfast is very light and coffee not hot, better to make coffee in your room. People who work there are nice. Little coffee shop in the lobby makes good soup.

The W is lovely, but you have to want to be """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cool"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to stay there. It has a hip, edgy style, so don't plan on coming through in your jeans and sneakers while site seeing. 
 There's a great bar in the hotel on the second floor - although it gets very crowded weekend night.

My husband and I stayed for - nights at the Normandy Hotel in Washington, D.C. and had a wonderful experience. We have stayed at their sister hotel (The Dupont Circle Hotel) in the past, and enjoyed our stay there as well. Basically, the Normandy Hotel is a boutique hotel which is located on Embassy Row, just up the hill from Dupont Circle. The location is perfect for visiting many areas of D.C. Within a mile's walk, you can visit Georgetown, Dupont Circle, Adams Morgan, the U Street Corridor, as well as the National Zoo. Upon check-in, we were told our room wasn't ready (we were about -- minutes early), so we asked if we could enjoy a glass of wine on the patio out front while we waited. We were given - wine glasses and told to make ourselves at home. They honored my request of wanting to be on the top floor and they alerted us when our room was ready. Our room was on the top floor and super cozy and quaint. Our view was pretty awful (looking out on an alley way), but at least the room was extremely clean, tastefully decorated, and the use of the small space was well done. Our room had a mini-fridge, a super comfy queen bed, free WiFi, and a modern bathroom. I fell in love with the Nespresso maker and plan to buy one of my own! The lack of sink space was one small problem, but overall - everything was perfect.
In the evenings between - and -pm, the hotel staff offer a wine and cheese hour. This was so much fun! My husband and I relaxed in the parlor with a glass of wine and some yummy nibbles. You don't find many hotels that offer this type of service. Every staff member we ran into was polite and considerate, and they seemed to really care about the quality of service.
We slept very well, and had no obnoxious noises coming from our neighbors. We enjoyed walking along the beautiful streets to see all the Embassies and large residences. We were close to everything we wanted to do and parking on the street on the weekends was free. The Normandy was a great place to return to at the end of the day. We will be back!

Booked a room on hotwire after reading some reviews here and, based on those, was pleasantly surrpised. This hotel is a typical Hyatt, clean and uncluttered with extremely nice staff. This hotel met all of our needs for a quick out of town overnight and we had very few complaints. I should note that our view was pretty bad but who goes to DC and looks out the window?

Arriving at the Trump Soho is a warm and friendly experience from the doorman to the reception. Eugene at reception handled all our needs expertly. As a matter of fact, all of the staff seemed to be on happy pills because of their commitment to making our stay a memorable one. That being said, the hotel seems to have some identity issues. First and formost, it is filled with luxury. Rooms are spectacular, baths are huge and well fitted out but the vibe from the bar, cocktail lounge and restaurant seems to set a party mood which is out of place with the remainder of the hotel. However, the views from those rooms was so spectacular that you forgot that you could not use the phone. Wireless should also be provided free of charge at those rates. I'd definately go again just to be around such happy staff in a terrific location.

Stayed at the Harborside Inn in late March as flooding in Rhode Island cancelled all Amtrak trains out of Boston. One problem - concierge said hotel was - blocks away from station and along the harbor. He called and I spoke w- hotel - they had a room that faced the harbor and was reasonable. I said fine. Pushed my rolling bag and brief case for at least --- of a mile to find the hotel across a main thoroughfare from hotels blocking the view of the harbor (Marriott). Free wifi and computers in the lobby. Free coffee in the lobby. No restaurant, though hotel surrounded by bars and restaurants in both sides. Convenience store two doors down. No obvious parking, though parking was available down the street. Hotel was very nice and in excellent location if I was sightseeing. Surrounded by bars, on the weekend the noise from the street might be a problem. Went less than a block and I found Faneuil Hall and found a take-out dinner there. Didn't walk across the main road to check out the harbor. From my room, if I looked closely I could see a bit of the docks where a few boats were tied up next to the Marriott - that was the harbor view. 
Overall, a nice emergency hotel, close to the train station at an affordable price. Excellent location if you wanted to see the local tourist attractions. I checked and no room had two queen bed setups, if you wanted to bring a family of four for example. However, my sofa opened up to a sleeper sofa. Might bring my family back to this hidden gem - probably save a good $------- from the rates at the Marriott or other chain hotels.

On our -nd night there were - major fires in the city, and we at one point while we were still awake heard the fire trucks, but were otherwise not bothered by outside noise. What an owesome place. We stayed here for four nights and loved every minute of our stay.
