Best Western Inn & Suites Fort Worth Review
My wife and I stayed here while in Fort Worth for vacation. We had already made reservations online. We arrived at the hotel around -am and the lady that was working was very nice and friendly. She got me checked in quickly and we were in our room in short time.
We had a room on the first floor. I think it was an accessible room as it had wider doors and there was a grab bar in the shower. Everything else seemed normal and the room itself was okay. The size of the room was huge. You could have easily fit two king beds in there (ours had just one). There was a desk and chair, a recliner with side table, a decent size mini-fridge with microwave on top and coffee maker. You also had a hair dryer, iron and ironing board.
The TV was a flat screen and had several channels. The TV seemed fine what little we watched it.
After we got there and got settled in our room we noticed that we did not have a floor towel for the bathroom so I called the front desk and in a few minutes the desk clerk brought me two fresh towels. That’s what I call fast service.
A little while later I called back to the front desk for a wake up call and the lady got that setup no problem. The next morning the phone rang at the time I had scheduled however after picking up there was no recording or person on the other end. It just rang at the time scheduled.
The A-C in the room worked great. It took a few minutes but did cool the entire room such that we had to turn the temp. up a little since it got too cold, but at least you could control it. Since the temperature was --+ at night and --+ during the day I was glad we had a great working A-C. 
The bed and pillows slept well and were very clean. 
The sink is separate from the bathroom. The bathroom just had the tub-shower and the toilet. The shower worked well. The water pressure was decent, the shower head was adjustable and the temperature stayed fairly constant while taking a shower.
Parking was good. Most of the time we were able to park right near the side door which was just a short walk down to our room. The lot got a little full at night, but there was still ample parking available. 
This hotel has a swimming pool (outdoors), a fitness center, and a conference room. We did not use any of these so can’t comment. The pool did look nice and in good condition.
We did make use of the business center. It was locked when we checked it around midnight one night but the front-desk clerk just said let me know when you want to use it and I’ll unlock it. She said it was open -- hours you just had to let them know when you wanted to use it. It worked well for being able to print out some documents we needed.
This hotel did have continental breakfast, but we did not partake since we are on a special diet. 
The wireless internet worked flawlessly and was fairly fast. The couple of times I used it I didn’t have any problems at all. 
This hotel was right off the --- loop and it was easy to get just about anywhere. One tip, when driving to the hotel for the first time we found out you had to turn into the Waffle House parking lot to get to the hotel. The road off of the interstate is one way so you can see the hotel but can’t get to it (unless you come from the other direction). If you turn into the waffle house then you can drive straight through their lot into the hotel lot. Another note, when using Google Navigation on my smart phone it didn’t have the location right of this hotel. It was a little off in that when we came off the interstate it was telling me to turn left when in fact we could see the hotel on the right. So if you are using a GPS be careful to make sure it is taking you to the right place. 
Checkout was at --am. I called front desk to see if we could have more time to checkout and the gentleman told me we had until --:--am or the system would automatically charge us an extra night. I was packing up and carrying stuff out and the general manager, Hermet, who was working the front desk asked my room number so he could get my bill ready. When I finished loading up the car he had me all ready to checkout. He asked me how my stay was and I told him everything was great and all of the staff I interacted with were so nice and friendly. He joked with me and said the only one that could be """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""mean"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" around here was him. He was very greatful for my comments and thanked me for coming.
The biggest thing about this hotel was the friendly staff and their quickness to respond. Everyone I interacted with was nice, friendly, and seemed to really want to do whatever they could to make your stay as best as it could be. I would certainly recommend it and if ever back in the area will consider staying here again.

I stayed with one of my friends for a week at this hotel. We chose it due to the cost. Most of the hotels in and around this location are extremely expensive. In fact pretty much every hotel in Chicago is expensive. With the exception of staying a Youth Hostel, which we didn't want to do.
If you want cheaper alternatives with hotels you have to stay outside of Chicago. This wasn't a viable option for us given we were going to rely on walking and using public transit and the occasional cab to get around and sight see.
When we first arrived at the Red Roof Inn my instant thought was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I'm not going to like this"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Unfortunately I was thinking this even more when we went up to our room on the --th floor. The entire hotel needs some serious updating. From my perspective it looks far better from the outside than it does on the inside.
Our room was small and relatively clean. However, it wasn't to the standard of other hotels we had stayed while in the United States. The bathrooms should be updated and there was a smell of mould on the shower curtain. The whole room-bathroom wasn't anything special at all. It certainly didn't look like it did on their website.
The first impressions of this place weren't good ones, to the point of me wanting to go across the street to the Marriott, pay whatever they were asking and staying there for the week. However we decided to be brave and stick it out with the Red Roof Inn.
We had a few problems. We couldn't get the fridge in the room to work and one of the lights over the bed was flickering on and off. The towel rack in the bathroom came off the wall as well. I reported these things to the front desk and they sent someone straight up. The issues were rectified, but not really to an appropriate standard. Never the less we were able to manage.
It's not all negative feed back that I have to offer. What I will say about this hotel is if you can handle the fact that you would be staying in a totally NO FRILLS, BUDGET hotel and if you want somewhere that's central to all the shopping, sightseeing and within walking distance to downtown Chicago, Millenium Park and Navy Pier then this is the hotel for you. 
The location is one of the main factors that made me enjoy my stay at the Red Roof Inn. I found it extremely easy to walk around and sightsee. I really loved it. If you needed them, cabs were always readily available at the front door to the hotel and there was very easy access to the public transit systems, trains and buses. Which we found great to use. There are also plenty of great places to eat to suit all budgets and places like Walgreens, Traders Joes and ---- to purchase food items and other things you might need during your stay. There are some really great Irish pubs - bars within walking distance of this hotel as well. Plus you are within absolute minutes of all the fabulous shopping along the Magnificent Mile on Michigan Avenue, all the designer stores and Macy's, which is absolutely great.
It's worth mentioning that the beds in our particular room were very comfortable, which was a blessing, especially when you are staying in a hotel for a week. Plus walking around every day. A comfortable bed to sleep in makes the world of difference. Our room was cleaned each day as well by a really nice staff member, this really helped make our stay a little more comfortable and easier.
There was some degree of street noise, like sirens and things like that.. But lets face it MOST cities have that kind of noise. You can't expect to stay in a city and not have noise. I personally didn't find it a problem, others may do so.
The main great experience we had staying at this particular hotel was the staff. Two in particular. Tammy at the front desk and one of the staff that cleaned our room. Tammy couldn't do more for us. She was great with offering advice on where to eat, how to use the public transit system and just information in general. She is a complete asset to the hotel. In fact she gave better service to us than some of the - and - star hotels we had already stayed in while in the United States.
The fact our initial feelings about the hotel where """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Oh My God, what are we doing here?"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". We ended up making the most of and enjoying our Red Roof Inn Chicago experience.
The staff that we interacted with were a credit to the Red Roof Company and basically saved the day for us. Would I stay at this particular Red Roof Inn hotel while in Chicago again. I do have to be honest and say probably not, but that's basically just due to the actual hotel accommodation. However if my budget didn't allow for something that was located more downtown, then I would definitely stay at the Red Roof Inn again, I'd just probably pay the extra fee and stay in one of their Deluxe rooms. Just to have that extra space in the room would be worth it.
I don't want to tell people not to stay here, but just to be aware that it's nothing overly special, so you don't get a shock if you do choose to stay at this hotel. 
My friend and I just made the most of it all. I totally loved Chicago and it far exceed any expectation that I had. It was my favorite part of my United States vacation. In fact I'm already planning to take my next vacation there.
I know that this is a lengthy review, however I wanted to be as comprehensive and honest and I could be. I hope that my review helps anyone that is considering staying at the Red Roof Inn. Don't be scared to stay here, just be fully aware that it's a VERY BUDGET Hotel and remember it's fantastic location.

Check-in was quick and friendly. Gift bag since we are Priority Club members. King bed was very comfortable.  Breakfast in the morning was help yourself style with typical fare. I got there just before it ended for the day but I was told to take my time.
 The only problem we had was when we arrived, the outside entry lights were all out. I thought maybe there was another entrance. We told the desk staff and they seemed to be aware of the problem.  One nice note, Tina, at check-in, sent us to get some great BBQ at A&R BBQ. We brought the food back and she gave us extra plates and napkins. YUMMY!!

Observations: My wife, infant daughter, and I stayed here for a weekend in May. We arrived before the normal check-in time, but the front desk was extremely accomodating. Our front desk agent, Alexandra (?) was very friendly and made us feel very welcome. Our room was clean and nicely furnished. We had requested a crib, and this was brought fairly promptly. My wife wanted some ice, and as I was wandering down the hall with the bucket, a housekeeping staff person went way out of her way to direct me to the ice machine and to give me an extra bag to get some more ice, as the bucket was on the small side. Once I arrived back at the room, we received a phone call from downstairs asking if everything in the room was ok. I definitely appreciated the effort the staff seemed to put in to making sure we were taken care of. Lastly, on the day of our check-out, the bellmen (their names were Luis and Reginald) were very helpful in arranging a car service to the airport for us at a reasonable price. 
Location: This is in a great location, literally right above the - train and a short walk to the E also.

- Concierge desk: went to ask for restaurant recommendations and they did not seem caring, nor did they really want to take the time to describe anything, give me a map, offer to make a reservation, etc. And there was no line behind me either. I found them rather snooty. 
- Minibar: snack items on the desk were dusty. I didn't indulge in any items and was charged for one. However, the charge was promptly removed (no questions asked) when I brought it up to the front desk.

The first impression of this hotel is that it is well kept and nicely designed. The service at the front desk was excellent. I felt that I was in good hands while there alone. The rooms were clean and well appointed. Towels were white as could be, no stains or tears. The bed was comfortable with plenty of covers. I had a little trouble getting the thermostat to respond and my call to the desk resulted in a maintainence person coming to my rescue immediately. The shuttle service was timely. One evening I requested transportation to a restaurant not on their list of regular stops. The driver went with me to the business center and looked up the restaurant chain that I had requested. He determined which one was best as far as travel time, and most kindly took me there never making me feel that it was an imposition. This was most important since there are few restaurants within easy walking distance. 
The location is excellent if you are coming in by car since it is just off of a highway with easy access. Also convenient to the medical center and that area of town. 
The only negatives that I could see were the TV and the restaurant.
Because I was there alone, I depended on the TV more than I would have at home. The sound was not the best, and closed captioning was not available. For lunch and dinner, the menu at the restaurant was heavy on the spicy side and more greasy than I appreciate. I did have breakfast there, but not the buffet. The service was excellent and just a bowl of oatmeal was available from the menu. Everything was properly served with """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""real"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" table ware and linen.

Did not have a reservation so I called and they not only gave me a good rate, but picked me up at the airport. Got a nice, clean room and free cookies and tea. Arranged a special pick up to go back to airport so I made my flght. For the money, this hotel is a fine deal.

Once you enter the hotel, you see a small lobby packed with lot of tourist brochures, booklets, magazines. Folks at front desk are nice and friendly. My room was on third floor. the walk-way is well lit and you can hear sounds coming out from other rooms. Now coming to the best part of the hotel. This hotel is located at a walking distance from Brooklyn bridge, Wall Street, Ground Zero and battery park (Statue of Liberty cruise). Nearest Subway station (Fulton Street) is also a short walk away although while coming back at around - AM, it was deserted and we saw few not so friendly people. Its better to take a cab if returning from Times Square - anywhere else after -- in night. cab from Times Square charged me about $-- in night. 
All in all, the hotel is an average one with an excellent location.

Hotel is currently going through renovation but does not affect the suites. They are nicely renovated with seperate living room and kitchenette area. Pool is just getting opened so hopefully it is nice. Breakfast that comes with diamond membership is very skimpy and I dont even use free breakfast vouchers. All the good stuff, like eggs and french toast are additional cost. But for the rate, you cant beat it, and location is right in middle of Southpark, right next to mall.

After reading several reviews citing problems, I was concerned but determined to try the hotel. My king suite was the nicest room I have ever stayed in. The staff is top notch and extremely accomodating with late check-out. Rooms are immaculate and large. Fitness club is free and possibly the best I have ever seen. It is very safe with a -th floor lobby requiring an elevator change to insure scrutiny of guests. Concierge and bell desk took care of everything I asked for, including reservations at top notch restaurants on short notice. Location is perfect for shopping, walking, and seeing SF without getting trampled. I felt I was treated better here than at the Ritz in Paris. Special rates can be obtained. Much better than the Clift House.

If location is your number one priority, than Empire Hotel is a great hotel. It is located across the street from Lincoln Center and a subway terminal. There is a Starbucks next door along with a pharmacy and is a couple of blocks from Central Park.
I found the hotel staff to be nice, however somewhat aloof. Checking in went smoothly and I was able to stow our luggage until we could officially get into our room. The room was fine - bigger than I anticipated since the reviews stated how small the room was. Our view was horrible - air conditioning vents outside the window. But the room was so quiet, I did not want to ask for a change. The shower needed a manual to work and the shower door was stationary and only went halfway - water hit the floor due to the open space.
The only complaint I had was that whoever cleaned our room kept forgetting to replace the towels, bath mat, etc. I would understand this if it was a one time event. However, four out of five nights, I had to call the front desk and ask for wash clothes and a bath mat, then wait between twenty and thirty minutes for someone to bring it. For a four star hotel, I thought this was a major oversight that was a big pain.
By the way, if you plan on using the internet, the business center is available to use. Bring dollars or a credit card as it is -- cents a minute.

When I checked out Yotel online, I was a little hesitant about booking it as It came across as a little gimmicky and with little substance. I was so wrong. Stayed there for - nights recently, May ----, and loved it. Check in was so easy and straight forward. We were brought to our room via control (reception in other languages), toured the restaurant and taken to the room. Compact, perfectly laid out, good bed. Great complementary muffins in the morning although, the coffee from the Galley on each floor is much better than the drip coffee served for breakfast. Great concierge team at the front door. Always on hand to help with cabs. 
Perfect location for midtown. Got a deal at the time for about €--- for - nights. Worth it and would stay there again!!!

I liked staying at the Helmsley Park Lane and my room was absolutely fine, not dilapidated at all as some others have said . I suppose rooms in these big hotels get refurbed in batches and so getting a good room is a bit hit and miss. 
Liked the dining room with view of Central Park .Nice breakfast buffet, but also lots of nearby places to have breakfast too e.g.: SaraBeths.
Was a bit miffed to be charged $-- a day for using the internet on my iPhone ( very briefly) - there was no warning if the charge - it just asked you for your room number.
Mentioned it to the receptionist on checkout and the charge was removed .
They have an IT room where you can check in online for your flight and get your plane e-ticket printed out, but you have to pay for that.
Overall, the location does it for me. Hotels in New York are pricey and I usually stay at The Wellington , but got a good price on the Helmsley .

Arriving at the Ritz-Carlton after a terrible journey (cancelled flights, awful weather, lost luggage) was a treat. We thoroughly enjoyed all the privileges that came with booking a club room. In our opinion, the Ritz-Carlton features one of the best clubs. The food presentations were fantastic, and the atmosphere elegant and relaxed at the same time. Staff at the club lounge was excellent and extremely friendly. Needless to say that we were overjoyed when the receptionist, who went to lots of trouble and spent hours on the phone insisting that she talk to someone in charge, managed to get our luggage back. We'll definitely go back to this wonderful hotel.

So I thought that there's no way people could say bad things about this hotel...it looked so great on the web! Boy, was I wrong.
We arrived in New York around -pm after a hellish drive in from Newark, and were greeted by a very nice girl at the check in desk. We got our keys and went up to our room with no issues. We walk into the room...it was small, as I had imagined, but I never thought it would be DIRTY AND SHABBY. My first clue should have been the elevators...tiny, rundown, and slow.
In our room, our carpet was extremely dirty, and the room had a musty smell. When I went into the bathroom, I found the shower tiles MOLDY. Okay, if you're going to commit to tiling an entire shower, you need to commit yourself to the maintenance. I was not happy.
I went down to the front desk and inquired about moving to a bigger room. They were booked up that night (Thursday), but we would be able to move the next night into a king bedded room for an extra sixty dollars a night.
The new room was spacious, but the bathroom still had mold issues. The sheets kept slipping off the bed because the featherbed was too big and the sheets too small. The worst thing, however, was the air conditioning...it made an awful banging noise about every -- seconds all night. We eventually turned the air off and slept in a hot, stuffy room for the rest of the night. I complained immediately the next morning, and was assured that it was going to be fixed. It was not fixed. Finally, on our last night there, my husband took the vent off the air conditioner, and guess what he found? DIRTY TOWELS, shoved up into the air conditioning vent. It was disgusting. When I told the front desk about this, we received --- dollars off our total bill.
On Friday night it was raining, and the front desk and concierge flat out refused to get a taxi for us. They said there was no way we'd get a taxi in the rain. Finally I went to the corner of --th and Broadway and hailed my own taxi. The desk people were rude, dismissive, and unhelpful.
Please, please, do not give this hotel your business. They try so hard to be trendy and fun, but just ended up being dirty and rude. Don't waste your money.

We have been staying here for several years for an annual San Diego conference. Its good location, modern decor, nice pool, hip bar and fitness room are still its best attributes. Rooms and hallways are looking dated (and rooms are still small) and haven't changed in the last six or eight years. Staff is OK, and as others have noted, parking, breakfast, and internet charges add considerably to the price of the room. We are usually here for a week, and I find it only nice stay for a couple of days. After a week, we are more than ready to leave.

I hesitated to book this property because of the negative reviews related to the noise level. I will address that issue first. Yes, this hotel is located near GWU Emergency Services and there are ambulance sirens at unpredictable times. Frankly, it was no worse than any other urban setting; we were on the first floor and were not kept awake by sirens. The neighborhood is otherwise remarkably quiet in the evenings.
I believe the more recent reviews of this hotel are a more accurate reflection of its desirability as a place to stay in this part of DC. The hotel management has clearly made an effort to correct any problems that may have existed in the past. The staff, for example, were commendably courteous and helpful
I had never stayed in this part of town before, but it is an excellent location for dining (the hotel will provide a list of recommended venues as well as make other suggestions for specific dietary needs) without having to drive or take public transportation. We enjoyed quick service at Roti Mediterranean Grill and Mehran Pakistani and Indian Cuisine, both about -.- blocks away.
The room was spacious, comfortable, clean and COOL! I say that because we were there during the blistering heat of early July and the room remained comfortably cool at night. The availability of in-suite kitchen facilities made breakfast so easy without leaving the hotel. Whole Foods is located about - blocks away for provisions.
Speaking of convenience, the Foggy Bottom - GWU Metro stop, serviced by both the Orange and Blue lines is just -.- blocks away.
All in all, One Washington Circle is recommendable and affordable.
Very clean rooms and lobby. Super friendly staff. Christine was awesome! Only concern was the location. We were fine and had no problems but someone told us we shouldn't have been staying on Ramona.

Our Grannies on the Go group chose to stay at this loacation for our trip to San Antonio and we could have not had a better place to stay. The staff was so helpful to us for our stay. They provided a shuttle service when ever we wanted to go to the Riverwalk or to the Mexican Marker area. They had the van driver stay late on eevening while we went to dinner at the Tower of the Americas so that we had transportation back to the hotel. On one occasion our driver took packages back to our hotel room while we continued to shop. On two evening the manager Ray provided a wine and cheese party for our group as for the other travelers in the early eveing. The staff that helped us were Augi, Ray, Roseido, Jhon, Georgia, and Melissa. The ladies that cleaned our room did a great job also but I did not get their names. Breakfast was great everyday and this was a great place to stay.

What a nice surprise. This little hotel lived up to reviews. Stayed one Saturday night for some R&R after surgery.We are born and raised New Yorkers,now living on Long Island. If you are looking for great location in Times Square, this hotel is in the middle of everything.We arrived around noon,desk clerk very pleasant .Found a very nice room for us with about a -- minute wait.
Room new very clean and nice appointed. Small kitchenette(sink ,fridge microwave and coffee maker). Wine tasting a free continental breakfast nice touch.Room even had windows that opened partially. Note this hotel across from theater so street noise until about midnight.We go the the city once or twice a year would stay here again- although rate a bit pricey.

You couldn't have a better location really! Its about - blocks (- minute walk) from Times Square, but far enough away to be away from the noise & bustle of all the tourists, its a - minute walk to -th Avenue shopping paradise, and a - minute walk to Central Park. There are lots of cafe's and restaurants near the hotel, as well as a subway station. Perfect location! 
In terms of the hotel itself, it was gorgeous, a huge lovely reception area with a fairly helpful concierge. The room was huge and spotlessly clean. All the amenities you could need - mini bar, huge TV, air con, good hairdryer. The beds were so comfortable...we had a queen bed each!
I loved it and would definitely stay there next time I go back to New York. My one, and only one, complaint was that on the day we checked out we wanted to leave our cases at the hotel between --pm and -pm, and we were charged $-.-- per item, which we thought was a bit of a rip off...I've never been charged to leave my case at the hotel before, and I would have expected better service after paying quite a lot to stay there. 
But thats just a small point - overall, superb location, fab hotel...I'd be surprised if you could find better for the same price.

A lifelong friend and I stayed - nights at Casablanca and will return. Everyone very helpful, especially the doorman whose name is Al, I believe.
Location superb, at Times Square but oh so quiet. We walked to theatres.
Great to get continental breakfast and wine and cheese every day.

Our flight arrived early, but our room was not ready. They took my cell phone # and called me in less than - hrs. to say we could check in. But we stayed out after -pm-normal check in time! Had to call to get our luggage delivered so I could change my shoes to go back out to Times Square which is VERY close.. hotel is in great location. We did not have a view of Times Square but did have the Empire State Bldg. side. We had no problems with the jackhammer-not even aware there was construction going on so maybe ask for the Empire side if you are going soon. Close to McDonalds for a cheaper breakfast than the hotel. Close to just about everything. I would definitely stay here again and have recommended it to several friends already. Beds were super... bathroom good too-nice water pressure and all free toiletries if you left something at home. Room was bigger than ones I have stayed at in past visits at other hotels. Desk help nice, welcomed us back everytime we passed the desk. Got a little tired of tipping the bellhops-doorman for doing their job.. one to store your luggage, one to bring your luggage, one to call you a cab... always someone with a hand out.. but overall---no complaints about the hotel. We had a wonderful king bed, flat screen TV, safe, and a small frig. Everything was in excellent condition, and very clean. We would have liked a nicer tub-shower arrangement in the large bathroom. It kind of cried out for a marble tub overlooking the river.
Hotel Dining - We never dined in the hotel, as the menu prices were a little more than what interested us much. $-- for pancakes (plus the usual huge upcharges for room service)? Nah. We did purchase some breakfast items from """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Perks"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" coffee bar in the lobby, reasonably priced.

Every request was handled better that we might have hoped, and he always remembered our name, and our special needs. He never made us feel as if he always had his hand out for a tip, which made it important to us to seek him out for a special tip on our departure. Jerry, you should probably be running your own hotel, brother.
Thanks to the Hyatt. We stayed for nights, and your hotel was a big part of an excellent trip.

Based on reviews here, I originally asked for a room away from the stairs. We were given ---, I believe. It had a view of the interior of the building - essentially a black brick wall. Sure, there's one by the TV, but it's - feet of the floor, better hope your little charger doesn't fall out. Would a courtesy outlet be so wrong?....
In a nutshell:
Nice decor, Nice neighborhood - (Pick-a-Bagel - blocks south was awesome) quiet, plenty of amenities nearby, #- train - blocks east.

Would I stay again? if the price dropped $---, yes.
Take a look at my review for the WalkNYC (.com) private walking tour we did. Highly Recommended.

This hotel was chosen because the room rate was less than other similarly rated hotels on the Miracle Mile. We had low expectations and we were pleasantly surprised. The street level lobby was under construction, which was not a good first impression, but it explained the lower room rate. We were very happy with the size and cleanliness of the room, the friendliness of the staff, and the location. We did not eat in the restaurants. There is a Corner Bakery nearby that has a very good, inexpensive breakfast menu.

Great hotel to stay if flying to or from LAX. I will difinately return and stay there.The staff and service can't be beat.Great food at the restuarant.Walking distance to other eateries and shopping.Great value for the price.*Pets are welcomed.*The personal attention the guest recieve cant be beat.

This hotel is in a great spot -- within walking distance of the convention center, great restaurants, JFK museum, and even the arts district if you don't mind a little longer walk. That said, the immediate neighborhood doesn't feel too safe after dark; I'd advise a taxi if you're travelling solo. For a hotel that averaged over $----night with taxes & parking fees, we were disappointed in the quality of service. Bellhops & front desk staff were hard to come by. The cleaning crew was more like what you'd expect to find in a cheaper hotel -- room service trays left in the hallways for hours, alongside piles of housekeeping's dirty towels. The hotel bartender was the worst of it all -- she completely ignored anyone who didn't look like a single guy. Wear your fake moustache if you're a girl, hide your ring if you're a guy!

We moved to the Milano after a very disapointing one night stay elsewhere. For the same price we got a clean, quiet, spacious room and excellent help from the staff. The difference was like night and day.

We recently took the family to Houston for a baseball game. I usually prefer staying at Embassy Suites when I travel for work, specifically for the perks of the free breakfast and happy hour, but often find that the hotels are in need of some updating. Not this hotel! It was a treat!!!

We have just returned from a - night trip to NY. Trying to find a hotel initially was difficult from reading some reviews, but the Shelburne Affinia's reviews were definitely accurate. Its in a great location as well as being clean and friendly. Would definitely recommend this to others.

Very close to Grand Central Station which is useful for the Airport coaches- shuttles. Also walking distance to many of the other main sights. Close enough to drop off shopping bags and head out again. 
Only briefly had a drink in the hotel bar, but it has a nice relaxed atmosphere. 
Overall, nice hotel and everything you need for a hassle free trip to NY.

We stayed here when on our honeymoon and the rooms were small but clean & sufficient.
The bar was a little bit expensive but they did have a drink reception at -pm every evening that was free for guests, which was nice!
This hotel is in the theatre district and is about a -- minute walk from the magnificent mile, when all the shops are and all where Millenium park is. It is about -- minutes to Navy Pier.

One of the good examples in NY that a first class boutique hotel can be a lot of fun with at a reasonable level in a top spot location. The hotel has an excellent location by a - min walk to Times Square but offers you the calm during the night and after long excursions in NY to benefit from a well decorated entrance hall, lounge and bar. The rooms are very nice, clean and well equipped.
Will be not the last time!

We stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn over the Thanksgiving weekend. It is a very concenient location to the Empire State Building, Macy's, Penn Station, the subway, and Times Square. The rooms were a good size for NYC and clean. We had a room with two queen beds and a good sized bathroom. I would definitely stay here again on another trip to NYC.

I write this review hoping the staff of the Bryant will see it. We drove from Montreal in the worst conditions. Arrived in New York during rush hour in the middle of a rain storm. Can't tell you what a relief it was to arrive at the Bryant, give my keys to someone and let them take care of it (insert big smile here). I have only nice things to say about the valets and the people at the desk. Charming and helpful people.

I really like this hotel especially when I am traveling for business. My employer is just a block away. Staff was very courteous. Room was great (with a great view!) Room service was good. My only complaint was they do not have complimentary WIFI-internet. The fitness area was great also!

We stayed here one night at the end of our stay in Boston. The view harborside is as advertised, very impressive.
Check in was fine although the service by the doormen throughout clearly over shadowed the front desk staff in our interaction with them.

The T is very convenient, we took the it - stops into Boston (on the blue line) and walked around Faneuil Hall- Quincy Market and the North End grabbing some pastries at Mikes. 
We did have an (overpriced) beer from the hotel bar in the evening and the service was good.

Although this is an airport hotel, depending on the price compared to hotels in town I’d consider staying here even for an extended stay in Boston as the subway system is very easy and economical to get around on.

Major plus was the responsiveness of every person who works at this hotel. I felt appreciated and moreover like a friend. By the -th night most staff that I encountered called me by name. Very nice way to end a day of sightseeing.

From the time I spoke with the Operator LaTanya Bell until the time I checked out with Aundia Sumner my stay with Greek Town was very very nice. I would not recommend this place for families or those looking for a romantic getaway; it definitely is a fun-party hotel. In regards to the rooms they were quite """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""minimalist""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""; the matress was inside some sort of bed frame that was built into the floor. Basically the bed-matress is on the floor, which is okay except we're not in college anymore and have become used living like adults. The other semi-complaint I have is the walls or lack there of. First, we could literally hear everything that was going on in the rooms next to us, awkward. Second, the restroom walls are exactly as described on their website...glass. Which is fine, since my husband and I are very comfortable with one another...except for one thing the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""heavy-duty RR"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". So be prepared to: either exit the room or just pull the sheer curtains over and giggle.

The security (with the exception of the pot odor) made us feel safe; showing their presence for those entering and exiting guests elevators made everyone feel comfortable with the stay. The cleaning staff did their best to please us; as I previously stated the rooms are bare and not filled with many items, the staff brought additional towels and pillows very quickly and made sure to ask if we needed anything else.
All in all, I would recommend this hotel, but note that it isn't for a romantic getaway or a place you'd want to take your kids. It's somewhere to let your hair down and have fun, just be ready for the glass restroom and very-very low beds! (LOL!!)

I stayed at Hotel Chandler for a long weekend in March. The hotel front and lobby was under construction making going in and out a bit dusty but inside was fine. The free breakfast (which I understand is no longer free) was not worth the money. Yes, I know, I didn't pay for it but I also didn't bother going to it after the -st day. Lots of tourist attractions are within walking distance, and the subway station is near the hotel.
The hotel is very clean and spacious, as was our room on the --th floor. Pay attention to what elevators you take, as they all don't go to the same floors. Their staff who helped us, Raquel and Leo, were very helpful, and Raquel even recognized us while walking around the hotel the next day and asked how we were doing! 
The only cons are that our bathtub in the room was scratched and outdated, the drain didn't close properly, and there was no hot water initially. Also, even though you can leave your bags with the bellman when you check out, you still need a room key to access their visitor bathrooms, which I can understand the need to secure their public bathrooms (as does everyone in the city), but it's still a hassle to deal with.
I highly recommend staying here, as it's close to everything, very clean, and their staff was very professional!

ROOM: The rooms are standard, though the bed was exceptionally comfortable and the bathroom was spacious. PROPERTY-SERVICE: The hotel is very pretty, with a clean gym and indoor pool. We enjoyed the cafe on the first floor, which serves delicious Illy coffee. The front desk and bellhops were extremely helpful with checking in-out, holding bags, etc. The housekeeping knocked on our door promptly at noon the day we checked out as we were running a few minutes late, though we were not charged extra or really bothered about it again.
LOCATION: The location cannot be beat if you're exploring Baltimore, as you're walking distance to the Harbor, the American Visionary Art Museum, the restaurants and bars of Federal Hill and the theaters. You're also a quick cab ride from Fell's Point.
Overall, it was a great stay and I'd be happy to stay here again!

was not treated by the one desk receptionist properly. very snooty, and it left a terrible feeling about staying there. did not feel at all like there was any focus on good customer service. don't feel they were honest about things either. i'm shocked this is so high on the list of hotels in dc. it definitely doesn't deserve it even if you look at room quality alone. it's average at best.

The first week of December two of us stayed - days at Gild Hall. The location was close to the Financial District and Seaport Village along with easy access to subways. The location was quiet, clean and large rooms. The breakfast of coffee, juice and danish was good but should have been free instead of $-.-- per person.

I stayed at Boston Park Plaza Hotel for a week, in an upgrade Tower Room. For over $--- a day, I couldn’t even get hot water for shower in the morning. I also experienced billing error and loss of item at my room. The staff was trying to help, but the hotel is so overwhelmed with problems that they either couldn’t do anything or did not care. I checked out with an erroneous invoice, and the security manager (service manage was not in on duty) promised that a fax copy of the revised invoice will be faxed to me. As of today (more than one week later), I am still waiting for the correct invoice. I emailed the security manager; she did not reply. I called the security manager and the hotel, and nobody picked up the phone at the front desk, or at the accounting. Apparently, nobody cares in the hotel once you leave. 
The lesson I learned from spending more than $-k? Stay away from Boston Park Plaza Hotel!

We found great rates on Hotwire and ended up here. We couldn't have picked a better spot. We were in easy walking distance of most of the things we wanted to do. The evening wine reception was a wonderful touch. The decore was fun and the staff welcoming. I was also impressed with the fact the hotel is very pet friendly. While not a dog person myself, I was amazed at the number of guests who brought theirs. During our stay, I heard no barking and there was no pet odor. Only people enjoying being able to travel with their friend. The only two compaints I have were #- there was no hair dryer in the room. For the first time in my life I decided to pack light and leave out the hair dryer. (We ended up buying a travel size at the local drug store) and #- the hors deHoevres (sp?) served with the wine reception were not good. Greasy little fowl of some sort - duck maybe? Maybe another night would have had better food. The thought was nice though!

I, like a prior reviewer, was unable to access my room until -:-- p.m. despite a stated check-in time of -:-- p.m. and repeated inquiries. No explanation was provided to me, but I would presume they are understaffed. The staff at the front desk were not particularly helpful or apologetic. Also, no effort was made to assist me with my luggage upon arrival at the hotel. Once I was able to access the room, the rest of the stay went well. The facilities are what you would expect, and the other staff were pleasant and helpful.
First impressions mean a lot, and a five star hotel should function better in this regard.
The room was clean and sufficiently comfortable. The in-room safe never worked. I was moved from the -st room I was allocated and the safe in the -nd room never worked!!!

Overall my hotel stay was what I expected for a Hyatt. Rooms were clean and staff was very helpful. Location was nice, as it was a short walk to the --th street pedistrian mall. However, hotel was a little on the expensive side - especially the hotel's restaurant. Dinner and breakfast buffet were way overpriced for what you get. And the water pressure in the bathroom was equivlant to a trickle. Also I could have sworn I heard a dog whimpering in the room above me around -am. Given other options nearby I probably wouldn't stay here again.

I really enjoyed my stay here. Everything is new and super clean. I was really impressed by the hotel staff. They let us check out later than usual and we had no problems. Also found a great deal for the stay. Would highly recommend if you have a car or need to be in that area.

Just spent a week in this hotel with my wife and - young daughters (-- & -) and will be recommending it to family- friends and also staying here again when I next visit NYC. The hotel's location is its standout feature - in West --th street it's literally yards away from Broadway-Times Square and is just one block away from the Rockefeller Centre. Close to a subway station and - minutes from -th Avenue- St Patrick's Cathedral & Radio City Music Hall this hotel really couldn't have been situated anywhere more convenient for all the big attractions. The hotel was clean, the staff were extremely helpful and friendly - especially the porter and Anthoni (from Poland) who worked in the breakfast area. The room was more than big enough for the - of us and being located on the -th floor and at the back of the hotel we could not hear any noise from the streets below. The bathroom was basic but adequate. The eat what you like buffet style continental breakfast was a sure-fire winner - the choice was excellent cereals, yoghurts, fruit, bagels, doughnuts, toast, fruit juices, tea, coffee etc basically anything you wanted and as much as you wanted - definitely sets you up for the day ahead. Downsides - none at all - having read previous reviews yes there may only be one lift in the hotel but our longest wait was --- mins and we were on the -th floor (there are - floors) - but when you're on holiday who is rushing, and yes you may have to wait on a table for breakfast (our longest wait was <- minutes) but for the centre of Midtown Manhattan this was a perfect choice at a perfect price. Great wee hotel.

If you are visiting San Francisco for a weekend, this is a great hotel to stay in. You have access to the whole city from Market &-th. You are right next to BART stations, bus lines, muni, MOMA, union square, shopping. 
The rooms are very small, but clean and tasteful. I was in a courtyard room during the weekend of the Chinese New Year Parade. I could hear the drums practicing from my hotel room, but for the rest of my stay, and all through the night, my room was very quiet. 
I didn't spend much time in the hotel-they had a restaurant and bar. I was not impressed with their business center-- computers which you had to pay for internet service on. 
All in all-this is a good place.

Stayed at the Westin St. Francis in San Francisco for - days (- business-- leisure) during the holiday season. My recommendation is that you ASK for a TOWER room that is NOT by the stairs or elevator! Elevators are slow and noisy. Took over -- minutes just to get the elevator up to my room. The stairs were near my room and the walls are very thin. I could hear clicks of heels and people talking at all hours. Also, there is traffic noise loud enough to keep you up at night. 
At check in I was assigned a room in the main building. After the long hike up to the room I found it to be dirty, smelled like mildew, and very very small. I lugged all my luggage back down to the main desk and asked to be moved (I'm a Starwood member). I was put into a much nicer room in the tower. The room had more room and newer carpet but still wasn't very clean. The food in the minibar is actually DUSTY and the juice expired in -.- months ago. There is mold in the shower and along the vanity in the bathroom. There is dust on all the main surfaces (I don't mean a little bit, I mean dust!). 
Bottom line, this area has many hotels as it's in Union Square. Try the Marriott instead of the Westin. Also, a word for tourists, this area has LOTS of homeless people and panhandlers in the shopping district. I highly suggest you stay in a different area of San Francisco.

This hotel is unbelievable. I just went for one night. They were very friendly when I checked in and gave me a bag full of goodies. Since I checked in late I got the Asian Suite. It was a beautiful room with a four-post bed with mosquito-like netting over it. There was a huge television. The entire place was immaculate. They called me after a few minutes to check on me. It was the best stay I've had anywhere in a long time.

From the doorman to the cleaning service this hotel can only be described as perfect. Their location is perfect, the rooms and beds were immaculate, fantastic bathrooms and decor. The proximity to the nightlife and the staff's knowledge of it was amazing....I will never stay at another hotel in Chicago again. I would rather pay to stay at Sutton Place then a free stay anywhere else in Chicago.

All that money and the king bed room doesn't even come with a fridge and not even a mini fridge. The room was pathetic and small. No complimentary breakfast, so the only thing you are paying at this hotel was for the name and location. I wasted my money on this room and never will stay here again and will only give bad reviews of this hotel. Such a shame.

My wife & I spent - nights at the Warwick which was recommended by our travel agent, through the Qantas Holidays accommodation guide. It wasn't cheap, but in New York, if you want 'nice' accommodation, you have to pay $ for it.
Quality: we could not fault our room for comfort or cleanliness. We requested a quiet location and we got it, away from lifts & traffic noise. 
Comfort: They advertised large rooms for New York standards and we were pleasantly surprised - after - weeks of travelling we were thankful for the space for luggage and for the two of us to lounge around - aircon. did the job & beds were firm but comfortable.
Location: We love walking - Central Park (where we spent - hours) was only - blocks north. The Rockefeller Centre was only a few blocks south & it was an easy -- min to Times Square. Plenty of eateries nearby!
WiFi: Had to pay to use own laptop in room - I was TravelBlogging, so needed it. Free for -- min. was available in 'Business Centre' for printing boarding passes or checking mail.

The hotel has a great location. We literally walked from the airport to the hotel within - minutes (once we knew our location). We had some dinner at the hotel which was good. The hotel was clean but the room smelled a bit (probably from the past when they allowed smoking). It definitely needs some refurbishment but overall value for us was good. On our second night we went next door to the Red Lion hotel for dinner and karaoke which was really cool. The drinks were a bit expensive at the Red Lion.

Just tried to get into this place again. I have tried numerous times this year, but it is always full. 
Want to stay just one night??? Pay the $--.-- fee to 'clean the room'. I paid all of this money for this? Really? Again, i will just stat at the Andaz....
The rooms are clean, and well designed. Great beds, nice linens...all that is fine.
Service? Sorry, but this staff does NOT compare to the staff at the old club in the Hilton Hotel in anyway. They don't have the sincerity, or the warm passion. I miss John and the old club staff. This place has a typical """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""NYC"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" attitude, and that is not a compliment!
If you want to BUY something here...they all jump! They are great at reminding you that you can buy more points. They are great at sending little cards, and setting up sales appointments. THey are great at bothering you with phone calls under the pretense of welcoming you to West --th, and then trying to schedule an appt. to 'review' your membership (sell you more). Unfortunately, they are NOT great at being able to fulfill your reservation needs. OVERSOLD!!
I am very sorry i ever bought here. This is without a doubt, the WORST investment i have ever made. I would love to debate their sales staff on this now...after the fact. It all looks great on paper...during the sales process, but it is NOT!
I have tried repeatedly to use my ownership investment to stay here. I cannot get in. If you have - months to -- months to plan your trip, you might be 'ok'. If you need to plan with less than - weeks notice, and stay on a weekend.... Forget it. Not going to happen.
They try to get you to use your points to stay at a hilton hotel....HORRIBLE value for your points.
The only good thing i have to say about this is that the breakfast and evening cocktail service in the owners lounge in lovely. The staff is great, the food is nice...great job. It also has nothing to do with Hilton...these folks are 'third party'....from a fabulous restaurant down the street. Great job, team. You are the best that the west --th has to offer! I have the same advise for staying here. Do what West --th has done with their food offerings....and 'GO DOWN THE STREET'. 
DONT BUY. RUN LIKE HELL.
CONTACT ME, I would be HAPPY to supply specifics.

Booked into MGM for a one night stay, also made spa reservations during our stay. We arrived early due to the spa appointments in the morning and were able to check in right away, well before the set check in time. Front desk staff were very friendly and seemed genuinely interested in making our stay as enjoyable as possible, I also inquired about late check out and was given a -pm check out time without issue.
I had booked us into an executive King room and was amazed by how well designed the room was, separate sitting area with writing desk and sofa led into the bedroom which was very spacious. King size bed with a gorgeous window behind, power black out curtains were also a nice touch. Bathroom was equally as nice with a massive shower, separate bath & toilets. Very beautifully done with overall.
The spa area was quite well done, felt very much like a vegas hotel both male & female changing rooms with sauna, steam and hot tub. Showers featured the rain shower head and were very large. We both had --min calm massages and were very impressed with the level of professionalism by the staff.
We did eat breakfast the next morning at Palet, all the food was fresh and well prepared, not an overly large buffet but had everything you could want for breakfast. 
A great trip away that I would gladly repeat!

Cool hotel! Great amenities, Pool, whirlpool, sauna, fitness room, and Fantastic breakfast! WOW the best we have ever had at any hotel with a free breakfast. Excellent and fast check in and out, great location, and parking was a bit tight, but we succeeded!
We would definitly stay here again!

The Whitcomb is not your average hotel but a historic building. As soon as you step into the lobby you have a huge crystal chandelier, marble floors, tiffany domes at the front desk; you feel the charm of the place. 
No matter what the purpose of my trip is, business or pleasure, I stay at the Whitcomb. Being away from home weeks at a time makes me cherish the quality and comfort of the Whitcomb. Even if -some- rooms are a bit smaller (it's a historical building!) the beds are heavenly comfortable. The staff is very friendly, I enjoy the food at the restaurant sitting at the window and looking out. There are also several eateries across the street, a Walgreens, a bank nearby and the Bart at the corner. The Whitcomb is conveniently located in downtown San Fransisco.

We stayed at this hotel for a night upon landing in USA. Hotel is nice and comfy. However for one who is used to the pampering in Indian Hotels, this is a self service hotel like any other US Hotel. Breakfast is highly limited for Vegetarians. People are friendly. Very close to the Airport and hence ideal for those waiting to catch a flight.
The hotel is clean and renovated. The only inconvenience is noise coming from passing next to the window train. I also did not like the additional fee for luggage storage (-$).

We stayed at the Chicago Airport Hilton in December in a prepaid room. The room was large, clean, comfortable and quiet. Even though we had prepaid, we were treated well and given a room on the Hilton Honors floor. It is so convenient to just walk to the check in counters. We did go to the bar for a snack and were shocked at the price of one beer, two glasses of wine and two bowls of soup in the bar! It is worth it though for the great location, and they must know it.

We stayed in the Residence Inn overlooking the Boston Harbor for - nights in September ----. Checking in, I was a little worried that we were on the opposite side of the bridge from the main part of the Downtown Area were all the action is. 
We'd later thank ourselves for this. #-, it kept the noise of the city down considerably. #- it gave us a reason to get in a morning walk or an after dinner cool down walk after we'd eat at one of the restaurants in town.
The Freedom Walk Trail is right in front of the motel and you have both Bunker Hill and the USS Ironsides within view of the front of the motel
The room was more like a small apartment with a king bedroom that had a huge television in front of the very comfortable bed. Pillows and Sheets were both top notch!
The living room had a fold out couch, a computer table, a small kitchen table, another huge TV and a small kitchen with a full sized refrigerator that saved us from having to eat every meal out at a restaurant.
We didn't really interact with the staff other than having to check in and out so I cant really comment on them, but when ever we saw them in passing, they were always cordial.
Our view out the window was stellar. It overlooks a nice marina with beautiful boats to gawk at. One night was a full moon and watching it rise over the Boston Harbor was pretty unforgettable. 
One word to guests checking in. If you're room faces the USS Ironsides, keep your curtains closed in the morning for the rising sun will blind you or wake you up if you want to sleep in
Parking in the Marina parking will also save you some money. Valet should have been $-- per night, but parking in the Marina for - days only costs us $-- total.

no help with bags. no breakfast that i could eat. not one gluten free item even when telling them beforehand. noisy from subway trains.the ac did not work and the windows did not open. the only good thing i can say was the location it was good.

On the plus side, the room was clean and the staff were friendly. On the down side, we had to change rooms since the toilet would not work. We were switched from a room with a river view to a room with a view of the parking lot. the next day we left the room at -AM and returned about ----. The room was not cleaned and the bed still unmade. When I called the desk they said they would send someone up as soon as she came back from her lunch break. An hour later the room was cleaned. Later that night I went to get ice but the lights in the room where the ice machine was located did not work. Again called the desk. By the way they don't tell you until check in but parking is -- dollars a day. Also the mattress was a killer. Big hollow in the middle. Not what you expect from a hotel rated this high.
Just an average hotel. Nice that it was close to Galleria, but pool disappointing.

We stayed at La Qunita Inn in downtown Chicago this January. The hotel was newly remodeled and we found the room very clean and comfortable. The bathroom was large, clean and the shower was great. The free breakfast was outstanding. Staff was very friendly and helpful. The location is about - blocks from Union Station and a short walk form the lakeshore. We walked to the Art Institute of Chicago in -- degree weather with no problem. As we came in by train, the locaton was perfect, a $- cab ride away. No resturant in the hotel (except for breakfast) , but several in vacinity. Only down side is minor noise from the EL train, ask for the quiet side of the hotel if this is a problem . I fully recommend this hotel.

I go to Charlotte, N.C. fairly often and have stayed at a couple of places. On the night I stayed here, there was a party in progress in a first floor meeting room. While the party remained inside, I did not hear it. Around --:--pm, the party goers began to move to the parking lot. I could hear them from my third floor room. After a couple of calls to the front desk, the noise finally stopped after --:--pm.

We found this hotel when looking for a hotel package for the King Tut exhibit. This property had a lot of great reviews so we thought we'd give it a try. I booked a lux suite for my husband, son and me and was pleasantly surprised.
The room was a very decent size, the sofa bed was super comfortable (I think it was one of the American Leather sofa beds which are really well built and have a great mattress). The bedroom was a decent size, and the sheets were very comfortable. I thought that the mattress on the sofa bed was actually more comfortable than the bed (they should upgrade that a bit).
I thought the bathroom was cute (which means it was well decorated but very small, especially for sharing). 
This hotel is located in the city, so yes, you can hear street noises, but not all night and we did not hear anything once we got settled in the room.
Everything was clean, the staff was SUPER nice and friendly. Wish we could have stayed another night. BTW, the King Tut exhibit was fun too.

I was very impressed with the quality of service I received for my one night stay. My room was in the tower and was nice and quiet. I ordered room service breakfast which was excellent and right on time. Was provided a wake up call and a paper at my door in the morning. Also a warm cookie greeted me a check in as well as a friendly accommodating staff member. I was able to use a computer to do web check in for my early morning flight. Starbucks was waiting for me in the lobby as I left to take my free shuttle. I am a happy camper and will definitely stay again as travel thru Seattle quite often.

I was on a business trip to DC and the Washington Court hotel was recommended to me due to it's proximity to my meeting. I was travelling and temporarily without internet at the time, so I called the hotel to make my reservation. It was a nightmare. I was cut off three times, put on hold for --+ minutes, belittled, etc. I didn't have high expectations going into my stay but I didn't have time or energy to search for another hotel. That said, from the moment I arrived at the hotel the service was spot on. The room was spacious and extremely comfortable and all amenities were provided for. I would choose the hotel again at any time.

Room was nice and modern and comfortable. They have a nice free gym and jacuzzi, and free internet and breakfast. Easy access to transit; walk to Wrigley field. Two complaints: -. the air conditioner was very loud. When I complained, they asked me to call during the day when the maintenance guy was in, but of course I was out and about during the day so it never got addressed. -. One of the desk clerks was very unfriendly (others were OK)

Co-workers and I spent a weekend off while working in the area at this hotel. We had gotten a remarkable price on priceline and it was worth every dime, I highly doubt I would pay the full going rate. The bar and breakfast area were very nice, but also very overpriced. However, the bartender had a rather heavy pour, which somehow makes the price bearable. The rooms were nicely remodeled and clean. Some parts of the building are showing their age but it seems as though it is a work in progress, and the completed areas are looking good. Their greatest asset is their concierge staff (I wish I could remember his name), he made excellent recommendations and was definitely full service. His attention alone was worth our room rate. The biggest opportunities for improvement include better heating in the lobby (the above mentioned bar is in the large open lobby area and a winter coat is basically required, even some of the bar staff were wearing them). As other people have mentioned, the elevators seems to need a little fine tuning. And finally, the entrances had very loud music being played, which during the day is fun, but even throughout the night, from my -th floor room, it was still audible. All around not a bad stay, generally meets or exceeds expectations for a Sheraton with superior concierge service.

A lovely hotel and a beautiful building. We stayed for three nights and were upgraded to a roomy suite. Given that we were celebrating a special ocassion we were also given a bottle of champagne which we thought was a great touch and made us feel very welcome.
The hotel is in a great location, close to the Horton Plaza shopping centre, a short walk to the Gaslamp Quarter and the sea.
Our only criticism was that the reception staff were a tad aloof at first and didn't really give us that warm feeling. However, in contrast, the concierge were very warm, helpful and very knowledgeable.
All in all a great stay.
Clean, Tidy and all that you need when in NYC for - days!!!!

The staff at this hotel is very helpful and friendly. It is very close to the airport, but we had trouble getting to the hotel due to all of the construction in the area. The breakfast was very good and they let us eat even though we were early (we left for the airport on the -:-- shuttle.) The rooms were very clean and well kept. The beds were extremely comfortable. The hot tub was small but not too crowded.

My Husband myself and our - young children stayed only last week and loved it !!! 
loved it was right in the middle of Times Square !! couldn't had been any closer !! 
cookies were soooo yummy , no line ups at the reception counter straight in help was always at hand , the door men were gr- with helping with the baby pram, Rooms were fantastic very CLEAN & TIDY ! NO BED BUGGS !! 
we stayed on the -- floor loved the buzz of the city not to noisy considering we were in NYC after all ... 
will recommend the hotel to anyone !!!

We loved this hotel and will definitely make it our base in SF when we return. Based on other reviews I asked for a room on a higher floor and for a pillow top (I read that the matresses were quite hard). The hotel was very accommodating of our requests. We asked for a very early check in and this was no problem - our room was ready when we arrived from the airport. Our room was very spacious with a huge bathroom and everything very clean. With the pillow top the bed was really comfortable so if you like a softer bed ask them to put a pillow top on for you. It was very quiet in our room. Reception people, housekeeping and concierge were excellent. Breakfast was great. Lots of choice and very comfortable dining area. I highly recommend this hotel. It is very convenient for Union Square and Nob Hill.
We really liked the free wireless and free DVD library.

The location is great for exploring San Francisco but the parking is expensive if you have a car. The rooms (we stayed in the Historic rooms) are shabby and seiously need redecoration. There are stains on the carpet and soft furnishings. Our bathroom was small and the lock on the door did not work. The view from our room was a wall. We requested an upgrade to a room in the Club section but were told there were none available. If I were travelling to San Francisco again I wouldn't choose to stay here.

I frequently stay at the Courtyard by Marriott Denver Downtown when I travel to Denver on business. The Hotel is centrally located on the --th Street Mall with restaurants & shopping within easy walking distance. The hotel is located centrally with easy access to the Convention Center as well as the Capitol. The best thing about this hotel though is Kathleen Bates and her top notch staff. The staff is always friendly and very helpful. You are greeted when you arrive by a staff that clearly enjoys their work and this shows in how the guests are treated. The staff is knowledgeable and never fail to give excellent recommendations for dining and entertainment. The fitness center is second to none with top quality equipment. I have a choice where I stay when I travel and never hesitate to book a room at the Courtyard. You will enjoy your stay.

From the front desk to the restaurant, everyone we met was helpful, friendly and engaging.
We thought the rooms were amazing. Good sized rooms with great bedding, comfortable chairs, nice lighting, great coffee maker, wonderful computer station and ipod docking station, great big windows, good sized bathroom and on and on and on.... We LOVED the frosted bathroom door in the corner king room.
Urbane has a nice happy hour and a wonderful breakfast !!
We will definitely be back and will share our experience with all of our friends...

My partner and I spent - nights in this hotel last April. We were a little bit afraid about the shared bathroom, but since we've read good reviews about Hotel --, we decided to take a chance. We're glad we did. 
The location is perfect. In the heart of Manhattan and only two blocks away from subway, which is essential in NYC.
The hotel staff was always helpful and nice. They let us check-in earlier, since we got the at --am. They booked a shuttle on the last day to pick-us up to go to the airport. And they even kept our luggage during the last afternoon, after we check-out, so we could spent the rest of the day walking around the city, enjoying the last few moments, instead of having to go to the airport too early.
The room was no that big, but we could manage even with - pieces of baggage. We had a sink in our room, a small tv and an a-c that seemed not to be working, but the temperature was good, so we didn't care about it. Our room was cleaned everyday and towels were changed.
They have two shared bathrooms on the floor and they were always clean and available almost every time we needed it. During the peak time, like early in the morning, it got kind busy, but nothing that bother us.
One thing I know for sure: a hotel with this great location and with this price in Manhattan is hard to get. I'm sure when I get back in NYC, this is gonna be the place I'll look to stay again.

This hotel is charming on the outside and the food is pretty good but I didn't enjoy our room. It had an outside balcony with a nice view. However, the outside balcony ran across the length of the wing so it was actually a walkway that was used by guests and the staff to deliver luggage. That meant that if we wanted any privacy, we had to keep our drapes closed all the time. Ugh. The room was decorated in browns: brown swirled carpet, dark brown wood, dark brownish draperies, not very bright lamps. Think - days in a cave. The bathroom was adequate but the calking around the tub was dirty-peeling. I should have asked to have a different room. Do consider this hotel but if you don't like having to keep your drapes closed all the time to have privacy, be sure to get a room without a shared balcony. Then you'll be very likely to have more than a - star stay.

this really is an excellent location. that is the one thing we couldnt fault. the only time we needed to get somewhere not on foot was when we went to the yankee game or to staten island ferry terminal (but the subway is very close by anyway). we couldnt believe our luck! 
the hotel itself is surprising small inside and does give you the air of school dorms. the breakfast is very cheap and very worth it (but get there early, we only managed to go once because of the queue - but we were there the same week as a school trip!) the lift is slow, i found some of the staff unhelpful and a bit stand offish, but a lovely woman was very happy to help.
the room was a good size, there were - of us sharing the room. the kitchenette was very basic and there could have been some instructions with the coffee maker - no kettle either, we had to make our tea by heating the water in the microwave. 
if you read any of the reviews about the hotel you'll be overwhelmed by the response that its the location that makes this hotel. 
plus there was a gorgeous takeaway pizza shop just a couple of doors down from the hotel - so nice

We had four good nights in the Serrano. It is a great old building with lots of history, and Kimpton is doing a nice job keeping the character of the old Serrano while they modernize. Yes, you have to get coffee in the lobby, but the stacks of New York Times and Wall Street Journals are there as well. The in-house restaurant does a good job with breakfast. The staff in the lobby were terrific - it felt like coming home after a busy day or evening in the city. The room cleaning crews were fast and professional. It all went great until checkout at - in the morning. The night front desk guy mistook us for another couple, refused to give us a receipt and was rude to my wife. Would we stay there again? Yes, but we'd have to hope that the night guy is either retrained or replaced.
One hint - if you are driving in the next few months, you'll recognize the hotel by its external scaffolding. The Serrano sign is hard to see.

I went to NYC to attend a friend's wedding and she'd booked a block of rooms at the Courtyard Marriott. It was a great deal on the room - I see that the usual rate is $--- but I believe the rate we got was $---, so for me, it was a great value.
The location was perfect for a geeky tourist like me - just a few blocks from Times Square, Bryant Park, easy access to the subway, etc. 
The staff were very friendly and welcoming - everyone I dealt with was very helpful, from the front desk, to the restaurant staff to the concierges. 
I wasn't there to work, so I didn't really try out the desk or the chair in the room. But the room itself was very modern and clean. Loved the big bathroom and walk-in shower and the king bed was really, really comfortable. I didn't have any trouble with noise - I was on the --st floor, right by the elevator.
My only criticism would be that the wifi was a little weak. Don't know if that was hotel-wide or just my room. I only had my smartphone with me and was keen to avoid using my -G (I was travelling from Canada) but I found the wifi crapped out quite a bit. 
There's no room service at the hotel, as they only serve breakfast, but that's okay - there are plenty of places to eat in the area and if you just want to get a snack in your pj's, they have a little snack nook by the front desk. 
I had the breakfast buffet at the hotel a couple of times. When I stay at my usual Marriott in Toronto, that same breakfast buffet is included in the price of your room - not in NYC! But I did enjoy the made-to-order omelette and excellent coffee.
All in all, I'd definitely stay there again - I was travelling alone and found it a very welcoming, comfortable place to stay.
New, nice, wifi works although air con was a tad noisy.

Loved the decor and the roomy room. The staff were helpful and didn't laugh too hard when I called down with my broken tv which was just not plugged in!! I knew the magic summer word thanks to following Kimpton on twitter and received free breakfast. Also was given a complimentary glass of champagne when I ordered room service one night. Its really all the small things that make staying at a hotel like this so pleasant. Not far from dupont circle and other downtown. Had a great time!!

My husuband booked this hotel for my --th b'day weekend. It is a nice hotel. I agree with a previous review, I think I expected more, the hotel itself was a bit dated. When visiting NYC again, we most likely would not stay at the Waldorf; I think for the price there are other options we would explore. For wonderful NY bagels, walk down to Ess-a-Bagel ... so good (ask at the front desk, they gave us directions).

Staff at hotel are a bunch of crooks! Smile in your face while stabbing you in the back! Pool was dirty and breakfast buffet not worth wasting your time. Not to mention after spending $---.-- per night, they have the nerve to charge you $-- per day for parking (valet or not, parking should be included in the price of the room).

I stayed at the hotel for a few months for business purposes and I was very disappointed that my high dollar clothing was slowly coming up missing. Not the cheap clothing, just the expensive stuff. On two occasions, the theft was reported, but no response except I must be mistaken. I found two enormous spiders in my room, one in my blanket while I was looking for the remote control, one under teh bathroom sink.
