Okay, let's get the good out of the way right off the bat: this hotel is in just about the best location there is. If you are taking a cruise out of San Diego, you'll be able to basically walk out of your hotel room and on to the ship. I think this is where this hotel gets a lot of its business.
Moreover, the hotel is within walking distance to some great things to do. The Midway aircraft carrier, Seaport Village, the old sailing ships, not too far from the Gaslamp Quarter. And, you're only a few miles from Old Town.
Now for the bad. I'm no snob, but this hotel needs some serious updating. We rec'd a room on the second floor, right next to the elevator and ice machine. Needless to say, some in our family didn't get a very good night's sleep. There was a bunch of young kids across the hall partying it up into the wee hours, yelling and carrying on. Did the hotel staff just not care?
The two beds in our room were small. I thought it would be two queens but it was more like two fulls or doubles. The room itself was very small. I also have little doubt that we rec'd such a poor location due to the fact that we booked on priceline. I've heard that this is common. 
Finally, be prepared to pay $-- to park your car. That's right! $--!! Amazing. This is somewhat common in this part of San Diego as you're basically in the city. But, given that I only paid $-- for the room, what can you expect?
Next time, I'll just spend a few more bucks and go the the Marriott or the Hilton. In this case, I booked at the last minute and took what I could get.

Stayed for two nights to visit our son at OSU. Location is perfect, right on the campus so you can walk to almost every activity that occurs on the campus (including football games). Also easy drive to short north and all sorts of good restaurants. This is not a fancy hotel, but staff is friendly and rooms are large. WiFi is free. Price is great. For anything OSU related, this is the place to stay.

Our family of - stayed for - nights for a family vacation. The room was pretty typical except for an added dressing area. This proved very useful with - people getting ready at once. Everything was nearly new. No views from our room but I do not know if other rooms had views. We got the continental breakfast add on for $- and that was a great deal. Also had the complimentary glass of wine in the evenings. The service was very good, expect for the housekeeper which was a little forgetful. The staff very quickly brought up what we needed. There were many restaurants and some shops within a few minutes walk. The subway station was several blocks away. It was quite a hike to any museums and attractions. So in the winter or summer you will find yourself using taxis. We found the room rate can vary greatly, think factor of -, depending on what is happening in the city. And it can change quickly, so check the internet often even while you are there. All in all a good stay and pretty good value.
Nice hotel located just off of Westheimer. Very convenient to shopping and restaurants. Staff was helpful. Room was spacious (king bed suite). Would definitely recommend this hotel to others.

I stayed at this hotel for - nights from Thursday night to Saturday and it was a good stay. The room was clean and the hotel was quiet. I flew in from San Diego for an interview in Jamaica Plain and the staff was helpful in detailing how to get to my destination. Some of the staff was not very animated nor genuinely friendly but they helped nonetheless. Two staff in particular were very nice and very helpful in terms of recommending food and fun places to visit in a short amount of time. Check in was easy as was checkout and the continental breakfast was good. I booked through Travel Zoo and paid $-- a day which was very reasonable compared to the other hotels in the area. The location is great, its within walking distance of pretty much any amenities you may need like food and transportation. I would really recommend this hotel. The only downside was that the tub in the shower was kinda outdated and not very nice looking kinda yellowish in color but aside from that the rest was great.

We booked last minute and the price was ok. We arrived at -pm and found check in empty and modern , no problem. Stepping out of the lift was like going back in time, paint peeling old carpet and plaster falling off the walls. The doors are original ---- but been fitted with modern card readers, stepping thru the door reveals a dated tired room in desperate need of a revamp.The room was small and so were the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""double""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""beds.On the up side we had clean sheets and the beds were made each day,the towels were clean each day and there was always hot water . The location is fantastic and the staff were very helpful. With a lick of paint it could be so much betterbut you do get what you pay for. Last point walls are thin and New york is loud all night-

I stayed in the Hotel Belleclaire for - nights in Nov-Dec ----. There were - of us in the group and having priced many hotels in New York we opted to stay in a suite as this appeared to be more cost effective. The Hotel Belleclaire had previously been recommended to me and having checked their website - I was impressed. We booked a two bedroom suite with private bathroom. The hotel is on West --th Street, in between two 'Tube' stations (--nd---th Street). These are really handy - literally - mins to Times Square. Like most hotels in NYC, the room was on a 'Room Only' basis but there was a great diner across the street - Manhatten Diner. It was busy, good food and good value. You need a good brekkie when setting out on some serious sightseeing and shopping! Most of the Diner's are the same - we tried to find somewhere different one day and ended up walking miles! My tip - Just use the one across the street!!
Hotel was clean, service was great. Rooms were cleaned every day. My only concern was the layout of the room. The first suite I was shown had two bedrooms but no door in between the rooms. I spoke with reception and was taken to a smaller room with dividing doors. Much better for two young couples. However the bathroom was situated off one of the bedrooms. It wasn't too bad for - days and for our close group - but please check with the hotel if you choose this option. I think we paid about £---- GBP between the - of us for - nights. It worked out about £-- a night, which was nearly half the cost of other hotels. This hotel may not be as central as some others but I think in NYC something has to give - Price or location. We decided to save money on the hotel and spend more on presents for ourselves!

I thought the Hotel Gansevoort was an ideal combination of location and hotel. As a first time visitor to NYC, I really enjoyed the trendy neighborhood (ie., great restaurants, shopping, and clubs). The Chelsea food market, Magnolia's bakery, STK - to name a few. It makes me salivate just thinking of these culinary delights! 
The hotel is modern and tastefully appointed. The room was very comfortable and offered a spacious bathroom. I certainly appreciated many of the little details that had been included in the room. 
Some hotels promise - Hotel Gansevoort delivers. The staff were extremely helpful in assisting us with our local destinations - suggesting great night spots, transportation routes, and other miscellaneous details. It made our vacation the best trip of our lives!

I stayed at Wyndham Jacksonville Riverwalk for one night for business, and chose this hotel because of the location and because we got a good rate. But I'll never stay here again, no matter how cheap the rate. Everything about the hotel is depressing, dumpy and dated, from the overly dim lighting in the hallways and lobby to the worn carpet and furniture in the rooms to the tiny, old bathroom. Avoid this hotel. What more can I say?

My husband, son and I stayed here for a couple of days in December. We arrived before check-in time and we were able to use their bag check facilities and sight-see until we were able to check-in. It gave us more time to enjoy the city without having to drag our luggage with us. The rooms were large,clean, and comfortable. Breakfast is included and there were many fresh pastries and bagels from the area as well as juice, hot beverages, hard-boiled eggs, fresh fruit, yogurt, waffles and a few other things. The hotel itself is located close to the historic Pier -- where there are many shops and restaurants as well as the Seaport Museum. There are interesting places to visit in the area (Battery Park, Trinity Church, the Financial District,etc,)which are all in walking distance of the hotel. Also, the Brooklyn Bridge and City Hall are close to this area as well. We took advantage of the convenient subway stops close to the hotel (about an --minute walk) (Fulton St.and City Hall). We will definitely return to this hotel on our next visit.

The hotel is a big nice-ish marriott convention hotel. The rooms were nice. The carpet on the way to get to them wasn't. The lobby is always packed with ---- tourists, prom attendees, and convention attenders. If those are your expectations, you will be fine.

I would gladly recommend this hotel. It is very nice not just on the outside, but as soon as you get in the service is wonderful. All the staff were very friendly and helpful. The room was very clean and comfortable. We had our son's wedding reception in this hotel and everything went smoothly. All our family had a great time.

We stayed for just one night and will be back again. Rooms are much larger than most NYC hotel rooms. Very clean. Staff was very friendly and helpful. We booked the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""executive room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and when we checked in, they upgraded us to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""studio"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Great location for theaters.

I stayed at the Chancellor for - nights in mid January ----, on the basis of reviews on Tripadvisor. Initially I booked for $--- a night on the hotel website, but a couple of months out I found a better rate ($-- a night plus taxes) on Expedia, so I took that rate with a smile. I arrived at -pm but my room was not available until -pm, no problem - they took my bags and I went for a walk. They gave me a room on the --th floor in the corner looking out over Union Square. It's a small room but it has a walk in closet, and its very well furbished. The bed was a little hard the first night (I have a princess and the pea back) but the next day they put a egg-crate foam topper on the bed and that made it incredibly comfy. There is the full complement of toiletries - shampoo, conditioner, lotion, soaps, plus cotton buds and tips, shower cap - and your own take-home rubber duckie. Mine came with a mobile phone and filofax! There is no mini bar but when I realised this, I asked if it was possible to have a bar fridge brought up and it was delivered within the hour. There is a Walgreens on the corner to buy milk etc - I prefer to have cereal in my PJs - can't handle company before breakfast!
The room has a desk, chest of drawers with a big flat screen tv, table and chairs, and lots of lamps. Nice heavy curtains keep out the neon lights from the Square. I only realised it on day - but my window was open about an inch which was why it was so noisy - when pulling the curtains on the morning of day - I noticed curtain billowing outside and followed it back to the source; once I closed the window it was really quiet and peaceful! Nice carpet, nice soft towels and flannels etc. There is a pillow menu with -- different types of pillows but I just stuck to the down pillows. 
The location could not be better; a - minute walk down Powell takes you to Market St, and the cable car stops just outside the hotel so you can shoot up to the tourist sites without having to queue down on Market. Get a Muni Pass if you are visiting - - days for $-- compared to $- per trip on the cable car; I estimate I would have 'spent' $-- a day on local transport without the pass. 
Tea and coffee are available all day in the foyer, along with REALLY yummy cookies and fresh apples. There is a tour desk down there too - the woman behind the counter has a lot of zeal! They can book you on the airport shuttle for $--. The front desk staff are incredibly helpful and friendly - even with my extra demands (fridge, bed) they didn't blink - and they lent me packing tape and scissors when I decided to see how much stuff I could pack into one of those flat-rate boxes the USPS the sells ($-- to Australia, up to --lbs - I managed to get --.- pounds in there!).
The rooms and the foyer are all wireless - and its pretty high-speed for wireless too. Plenty of power points throughout the room and the bathroom - and the light switches are night lights which is cool because the bathroom is a step-up and the light always reminded me. 
There is a restaurant downstairs for breakfast and lunch, and room service is available until -pm. I had breakfast there on my last day, using the discount voucher they provided on check in and it was absolutely fine.
I would definitely stay here again - it was really good value.

Their website had a slogan that reads """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""More than you expect."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" That is truly an understatement. This place is convniently located, which is what attracted us to begin with. More importantly, the accomodations were so spacious- - -like having your own apartment (comlete kitchen!) and clean, well appointed with all the comforts of home. Best of all was the service- - -the helpfulness and desire to please on the part of the staff is unsurpassed!! We'll always choose this sweet little spot over a traditional hotel when we come to LA!!!!

There was no window shade on one window in our room. The front desk person said he would give us a sheet to hang on the window! The walls were thin. We could hear the person next door sneezing like he was in our room. The shower temperature had a mind of it's own and exposed heating pipes in the bathroom could've burned our skin! We ended up leaving a day earlier and staying at a four start hotel for only $-- more.

My wife and I stayed in the New Yorker in May for - nights and found it dissappointing.The lobby area looked good as most New York Hotels do . But after getting the elevator (which creaked and groaned!)the corridoor was while not dirty, shabby , not smelling well and the decor was very very poor as was the lighting.The rooms were fairly small , apparently we had a master bed (yeah right!),they were poorly decorated ,musty smell, just generally a very poor hotel room.We have stayed in New York on - other occasions so we were no strangers to NY.I definitely would not recommend this hotel to anyone.The location of the hotel is very central in Manhatten with good shopping,food and pubs very nearby.
My verdict ? a poor hotel which is not cheap and I wont be back there.

Stayed here for the third (-rd) time the forth (-th) of July week. I will only say that it appeared under a different Management then previous visits. This is obvious in the service, throughout the facility. Mainly in the restaurant area. Ate there the first (-st) night and opted for other options the remainder of the trip. The food was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""DEAD"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (i.e. without any love) on arrival to the table. 
I hope the new management gets it's hands around this area, quickly.. Love the location but, the optics of the lack of Service Concerns with management, troubles me in this economy.

This was my third time to stay at the Worthington. We were here for the Cowtown Marathon, so obviously the hotel was booked full of runners. The Worthington is in a great location to everything in Sundance Square. The rooms are nice, fairly average size and clean. The bathrooms are nice, but small with very little vanity space. Check in was quick and valet parking was fairly easy, but expensive at $---day. We got a group rate for this stay. If I had to pay the regular rate, I would probably shop around. There are - or - other great options in Sundance Square.
My only big complaint was the hallway noise when trying to sleep.

This hotel is clean, afforable for chicago, and has smoking rooms. Yes I said smoking rooms for those of you who also smoke in the Illinois anti smoke state. You can catch the blue line from ohare airport and ride it downtown or relax in the hot tub. Would recommend this hotel for couples and singles. We stayed there and attended a Disney on Ice show at the allstate arena. Delightful stay overall.

The Country Inn & Suites near the Houston Hobby Airport was an exceptional find. The rooms were large, tastefully decorated and the foyer had a very welcoming vibe. The receptionist that night - Jessica - was gracious and professional. The shuttle driver courtesy of the hotel (very early in the AM) was courteous and punctual. Do not hesitate to stay at this location - you'll be well-rested for your travels!

Rooms facing Bryan Steet contend with train noise deep into the night (at least ours did on the -th floor). Hotel is older, but remodeled. King rooms are small. Parking garage across Olive could use some attention, particularly the elevator area (dingy and dirty, not a good first impression).
""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Draft"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" bar pleasant - plenty of TVs for Monday Night Football and decent prices.
The best thing about the hotel from my perspective is the large gym which has clearly undergone a complete renovation - almost Vegas resort quality.

The Fairmont is a full service hotel within a grand architecture. The property is about - to - blocks from Pike Place making it a pleasant walk. Also, there are several restaurants within walking distance. If you want an old style hotel in downtown to allow you to explore downtown Seattle, I would recommend this hotel.
This hotel is used by Holland America for cruise passengers arriving early. Transfer from the hotel to Pier --, Holland's pier, is easy and fairly quick. Pier -- is about - miles from the hotel. As a Holland passenger, I stayed here and it was a wonderful start to the cruise. I was able to enjoy discovering downtown the day before and the day of the cruise due to the hotel's location.
This can be an expensive property. Be sure to shop for deals if you want to stay here. I got a decent rate as a Holland passenger.

Day -
After flying from the West Coast and checking into the hotel, I had to visit the reception desk three times before I received an electronic card key that worked. The two elevators fit a maximum of - people and take ---- minutes to summon to your floor so this was a lengthy process.
Once I was finally able to get a working key after multiple and time consuming trips to reception, I discovered the room was just large enough to fit the bed and provide a walkway around the edge of the bed. I’ve been to NYC a number of times but this was truly incredible. I asked to be moved to a larger room; that was not possible until the next day.
Day -
I was finally able to move to a slightly larger room and a member of the hotel staff arrived at the room to personally let me know. I was told to go down to reception and get a new key. I was about to pick up my bags and move them to the new room however, the staff member said my bags would be moved and taken care of and not to worry.
I moved to my new room and waited for over an hour for my bags. They did not appear and I decided to head out to my next meeting without changing my shoes which had been soaked through by an afternoon rainstorm. I also had to call for a TV repair person for this new room; fortunately that service was turned around quickly.
I returned to the hotel after my meeting and while in the lobby bar, thought I would pick up some ice for cold water in my room. There are no ice machines on individual floors’ a call to room service for delivered ice is the only way to get ice. I thought since I was already in the lobby bar where there should be ice this would be much easier than going up to the room and waiting for room service. I asked a waiter and was told I had to go to my room and call for room service and wait. There were a handful of people in the bar and this waiter wasn't helping anyone, I believe he was arranging the fake candles that go on the tables. Fortunately, I found another waiter who was willing to provide me with a glass of ice.
I returned to the new room; by this time I had been moved to the new room for over - hours. Still no bags. I spoke to reception and was told that my bags had been moved. Clearly this was not the case and at this point reception said they had no idea where my bags were.
Edwin at the front desk left his post and looked for my bags himself. He was able to locate them, in the old room, and moved them himself. He went out of his way to make sure I finally had my bags.
Day -
After a day of meetings and late dinner, I returned to my room to find that a shirt which had been left on the bed was no longer there. I called down and spoke to Nelson the night manager who explained that it likely was wrapped up in the bed linens when they were changed but unfortunately housekeeping was closed for the night. He offered to look in lost & found and would call back. I did not receive a call back that night.
The next morning I called reception who knew nothing about this. I spoke to housekeeping, who also had not been informed, and they could not locate the shirt.
Day -
Upon check out, I asked again about my missing shirt and nothing. There seemed to be very little concern about this, just an offer for a free breakfast which incidentally my room rate already came with this free breakfast. My phone number was taken and I have not heard from the hotel since.
This is a great hotel in the middle of where you want to be: shopping, food, culture. The rooms are stylish and comfy. The staff is personable, accommodating and friendly. Great bar scene, too.

My night started at check in. Linda at the front desk was fantastic, from her welcoming smile to her knowledge of not just the hotel but also the attractions of the general area. My room was clean, quiet, and comfortable. At -:--a.m. I ordered room service, (prime rib medium and it was perfect). This is definitely a five star hotel. Management has something to be proud of here, their staff. Thank you Linda for starting my stay off right. I will be back.

First let me say that this is one of those rare hotels that does everything well. First the location. You can't do better than literally - minutes from Radio City adn three minutes from MOMA. The hotel is in an older building which has been remodeled without loosing its charm. My room was spotless. The king pillowtop bed was comfortable. I had a kitchette with microwave, small fridge and Koureg coffee maker. (Gormet coffee was free for the machine as was tea.) I had great Air Conditioning which is individually controlled. My wireless internet was fast and was free. The room had a flat screen TV DVD-CD player. Even the room lighting was state of the art with dimmers on the main lighting. There was a desk and a comfortable wing-back chair with ottoman. The bathroom had a deep tub, tons of granite and marble and a nice selection of premium bath products. I even had a robe which is a nice touch. The room was the kind of room that experienced travelers revel in.
Yes the elevators were small but I did not wait long for them. The staff was friendly and very helpful. At the end of my conference they even shipped some equipment for me at no additional charge. Very nice people. 
The restaurant is good. Free breakfast. Dinner there was fine though I had a steak and can't pass judgment on the Italion fare. My two dinner guests said it was very good. 
A review is supposed to talk about the good and the bad. I have nothing bad to say about this hotel. Choosing a New York hotel can be frightening. It is very easy to get very little for your money. I have paid much more for much less. I frequently have the feeling in hotels that everything is designed to get another twenty bucks from me. Not so here. Everything I wanted was included and done well.
I highly recommend this hotel. It is a business travelers dream. For vacationers the kitchen and free breakfast make it a downright bargain. It is not cheap but for the area offers a great value. Stay there. You will like it.

This hotel was our home base for a long weekend. 
I was attracted by the get the -rd night free deal. We were very happy with the value you get for the space and comfort of the rooms. It's in Queen Anne so centrally located without being trapped in downtown traffic. 
The staff was always helpful and polite. The parking and wifi were free. That's a huge plus in Seattle. 
We would stay there again.

We stayed at the hotel for two days during our hmoon trip and felt that was the best experience ever. We got a free upgrade with amazing city view. Also got a free champagne and brownies. Great rooftop bar not to be missed. Will reconmend this to all my friends.

This hotel smells like my great grandma's house. I know it's super old and some might say it has charm (which is what I kept telling myself because we had no other choice but to stay there), but if you prefer newer hotels stay away from this one. We complained - times before we got a nice room, with tall ceilings, good view, and a bay like window. If you settle you are likely to end up in a room that looks like it's half way through being renovated. During our stay a man went crazy in our hallway with the fire extinguisher and was using it to bang on our wall-door at -:--am. There were holes and blood splatter on the wall, and the entire hallway was covered in the white spray from the extinguisher. The man was on the wrong floor trying to get in the wrong room and it set him off. There were fire trucks and police cars that showed up within minutes of us calling ---. The hotel never reached out to us to comp our room for the night or to apologize. I'm - months pregnant, really didn't need this kind of stress. There are so many other choices, there is no reason to stay at this hotel. If cost is a reason, you'll be glad you spent the extra money to stay somewhere else.

I would stay here again and I was actually really impressed with the layout. I really liked how spacious it was, the modern furniture, the television, and two washrooms (one with bath). The lobby is also very nice. I didn't have a lot of time and only stayed one night here, but the price was good and the quality was high. One of my more memorable stays.

I had the pleasure of staying at the Raffaello hotel in October ----. The location is great, the room was very comfortable, spacious and clean. I liked the convenience of the mini-fridge, microwave and Keurig for in-room breakfast before adventuring out for the day.
I am returning to Chicago this coming October, and have already booked my accommodations at the Raffaello. I trust my future stay will be as good as my previous stay!

The Hotel Monaco is located in a beautiful vintage bank building. Everyone was friendly and accommadating from Campbell the bellman to Brian at the front desk. The room was lovely, comfortable and clean. The amenities were first class, from the Aveda bath products to the terry robes in the closet. We enjoyed the chocolate chip cookies with milk shots at -pm and then at -pm enjoyed a glass of wine before going out for dinner. 
The hotel is located in the business district but not too far from the Harborside tourist area. I would definately stay here again.
p.s. wi fi is free if you are a member of the Kimpton program.

Upon check-in the very gracious Palomar staff upgraded me to a pretty nice suite. I don't know what I did to deserve that but I wasn't asking. The suite was very clean and spacious, the bed was super comfortable and the jacuzzi was a blessing after a long day. 
My only complaint was that the WiFi was pretty horrible and my plan to put in a few hours of work before an event went down the drain. Even after signing up for the Kimpton membership for free WiFi, it was just a nightmare. I ended up working on my BB which was very time consuming.
As a business traveler, Wifi is super important. I'm not sure if I could stay here again.
Perfect location! Very clean! No Bedbugs! European restuarant next door is fabulous!!!

I had to travel on business to Austin. The conference was at the down town Austin Hilton. I had to stay - nights and so I decided to pay for the Executive Floor on my own dime. Greeted by a fellow coworker they walked with me up to my room. I was informed the only difference in my room was I had a headboard. BIG whoop. The room was super small and felt cramped. I decided later to let he Hilton redeem itself by stopping by the executive lounge for a glass of vino. What? The wine is not comped? Why did I pay extra? The wine was at least at a discounted price from the lobby bar but the quality was also less. Basically I was feeling pretty ripped off by the whole “upgrade”. 
I ordered room service for Breakfast one morning and sipped my drink from bed by the light of the TV. When I was finally ready to rise I turned on the lights to learn that the water glass I was sipping from was covered in cemented on Orange juice pulp (I had no OJ). Disgusted when I left for the day I took said glass to the front desk. The only response was that she would let room service know. Not in the mood to argue I can only assume she herself did not find it disgusting to drink from a filthy glass? 
I later learned that for whatever reason I was not booked to stay as long as I needed for the conference. I needed an additional night. Hilton was not able to extend to me the conference rate. I was more than willing to move off the executive floor however the rate was still astronomically higher than the conference rate. I decided to call it a stay and move to a hotel closer to the airport since my flight let earlier any way. If you are on Foursquare you can check in and get free tater tots. There isn't a kids menu, but they did have chicken tenders and sliders and what kid doesn't love tater tots? My husband also recommends the Strip Club which which is a restaurant where you pick out your own steaks and cook the steaks on a grill. We did not do this on this trip, but he was there a few months ago and said it was neat experience and the food was good. We also found a great breakfast-brunch place called Mary Janes. We loved it. I had a great breakfast burrito and the kids enjoyed the bottomless bowl of cereal and Mickey Mouse shaped pancakes.
We would definitely stay there again!

One last note: this hotel is about five minutes away from the epic La Madeline French restaurant. A MUST for your dining list while you're here :)

I went to the Spa Terre for my sister's bachelorette party--it was amazing! the entire place is beautiful, and you feel so removed and secluded from the busy San Diego area. The grounds are gorgeous, very clean and well maintained. The staff was so nice--we have -- women who all changed their reservations and spa treatements many times, and the Spa staff (Erin the manager is so sweet) completely accommodated all our requests. I reccommend reserving the private area--they served us with fresh fruit and vegetables, and we spent the day in our own private wood spa filled with flowers. I also reccommend the Chococlate Ice Cream pedicure and a facial with Melodie. We sat in the spa, layed out by the pool, and spent time in both the wet and dry saunas. But be warned: it IS really expensive, the entire resort is not cheap, but completely worth it (and I LIVE in San Diego). My boyfriend and I are going for a weekend just to be pampered and get away from life. If you're stressed, it is totally worth every penny. I can't wait to go again.

We recently rented a suite at the St Gregory for a special weekend. We were pleasently surprised by the lovely decor and many amenities provided at an affordable price. The open kitchen had a full-sized refrigerator and dishwasher. The living room had a flat-screen TV, CD player, decorative pillows and accessories. The bath was large and generously supplied with bath essentials and towels. The bedroom had another flat-screen TV, a clock radio with iPod dock and - mirrored closets. And most importantly, everthing was clean and modern. The hotel had a convenient bar-restaurant off the lobby that offered $- cocktails and appetizers each day at -pm. Plus they had inexpensive lunch specials that were quite good.

Stayed here for - days when attending a conference at the convention centre. The hotel itself wa very trendy with massive rooms that were nice and quiet in the evening. The location was also good - within the gaslamp quarter and only a nice and easy -- min walk to the convention centre. Staff were very friendly and super helpful - this is a great place to stay in San Diego.

Just got back from a wonderful - day stay at the Warwick. Couldn`t have been better and I`ve stayed in some great hotels around the world. Booked for my husbands birthday and we were upgraded to room --- The Warwick Suite. Hallway, big lounge with three large windows, on the corner, giving a view right down -th avenue and across --th street. Huge bedroom . TV`s in both rooms. The bedroom also had a large window and cupboards everywhere.
Perfect location. Easy to walk everywhere and the bar was very lively, with a great atmosphere.
Staff were brilliant - friendly and polite. We had trouble with our phone charger and help arrived immediately - problem turned out to be with our charger, but the hotel sent up alternatives and even when we gave up, Frank, who`d come to help, practically ran away rather than accept a tip for all of his help. Then another staff member popped up - minutes later, to see if he could do anything. He even offered to send the doorman off in search of another charger. Absolutely charming. They also let my husband check his emails in their office for no charge. as the surprise birthday visit meant that he hadn`t brought his laptop. The whole stay went completely smoothly, in large part, thanks to the hotel Never want to stay anywhere else in New York..

My wife and I were guests at the Ritz-Carlton Philadelphia for four nights last week. Overall, we had a great experience and will recommend this property to friends.
You cannot beat the location of the Ritz. Across from City Hall and within two blocks of Rittenhouse Row (Walnut Street, etc.), also known as Restaurant Row, you can easily reach all of the major sites and attractions on foot. Even the Philadelphia Museum of Art is an easy ---minute walk.
The standard rooms are on the small size, but they contain all of the accroutrements you expect from a property such as this. The public areas are wonderful. This hotel is in a historic building, so please do not expect all of the modern touches.
The only area that needs immediate attention is the health club. Although nice and well maintained, it is very small and has few equipment options.
The service was outstanding. From the front door staff to housekeeping, we had a great experience and were treated as you want to be when you are paying the Ritz rates. You really get what you pay for. 
The concierges were particularly impressive. Each restaurant and club recommendation was perfect. They even helped us with arranging a private tour of Independence National Park.

This is a fabulous resort. Excellent location right on the bay, beautiful pool, well appointed rooms, etc BUT I am writing to comment on their customer service. I attended a conference at this property last week and a container I had prepared for outbound shipping on Friday was misplaced. Miguel Hernandez and Billy Metzger provided extraordinary customer service working with complete commitment to my desperation to find my property. Miguel eventually located the container and secured it for shipment. Billy took the time to prepare a revised shipping label and agreed to meet with FedEx to ensure proper handling.
This level of customer dedication was so appreciated and provided me with complete peace of mind. These two individuals set a high bar for customer satisfaction and the Hilton Mission Bay Resort and Spa is fortunate to have them on staff.

A nice friendly welcome even though it was close to midnight when we arrived. Very clean room and I'm convinced the sheets were changed daily, as were all the towels. For under $--- a night for the two of us this hotel represents very good value for money. Complimentary coffee, tea and Danish pastries for breakfast included.

If I had to review this hotel in one word, it would be AMAZING! From the awesome location and tranquil surroundings to the extremely clean rooms, amazing staff and wonderfully delicious breakfast, this place is more than perfect! The beds were comfortable and cozy. No noise issues at all and it was pretty busy. We checked in on July -th and the gentleman at the front desk was very nice and welcoming. We can't wait to go back!

This is a great place for families. We had - rooms next to each other. The grandkids all had a blast. Swimming, pool time, just lots of fun. However, it's very expensive! When you're spending over $-,--- per day (for all four rooms), and that they call themselves a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""resort"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", it seems that they are really missing some resort items. For example....no bathrobes, no slippers, no turndown service in the evening, poor (even bad) housekeeping, no lotions, shower cap, soaps, and other bath amenities. 
Housekeeping is very disorganized. Watched supervisors and all they did was reassign staff to rooms that were screaming the loudest for service. They should have spent their time checking on the quality of the work - which is spotty and not consistent. One day, they even forgot to leave clean towels. Disappointing, to say the least!
Will we come again? Probably. But, the management needs to focus on improving so that more value is seen for the huge cost.

Well, my stay started off all right; I was to be here for - nights total under - reservations (- for - night and the other for - nights - Unfortunately, Hilton books each type of reservation (ie. award, paid, etc,) separately. When I checked in and the clerk stated it was - night, I explained that there was another """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""linked"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" reservation for - additional nights. """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Oh yeah!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" she found it. I asked will I need to go to the front desk and get a new key and she said no. 
Well, she was correct - my key worked. However, upon returning to my room (-pm), everything was gone. I immediately called down in a panic (wouldn't you?). I spoke to the manager and the housekeeping manager. I asked WHY? no one bothered to call me? Didn't they find it strange that ALL of my belongings would be left in the room. """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Oh yeah we were gonna do that shortly"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" They said I was making a scene - perhaps I was. Perhaps I had a right to be upset. Well, they finally bring up the luggage and I go through it. Well, first of all, the water, sodas, and wine I left in the fridge were gone. My razor was gone. As far as the rest of property is concerned: nice accommodations, free wi-fi, free breakfast (Get there BEFORE the end time as they start taking stuff away ----- early), free evening snacks (only Mon-Thr - there is a menu so they do not repeat often), clean rooms, spacious, and full kitchens to make your own dishes.
I seriously tempered myself not to give them a single star. If this horrific mix up had not occurred, I would have probably given them - or - stars. I hope they read this and see that a single phone call could have changed a guest's experience in a very big way!

Was a good price for SF, however, was quite a distance from the wharf and downtown (near the zoo), even though there is a muni that leaves from outside the hotel. Rooms were more like a bed and breakfast than a hotel. They were clean, but outdated. The rooms were fairly noisy. Check in was easy and efficient, although, there was no early express check out, which made it slightly difficult. Would be good for a family with a car on a budget. For singles or couples, pay the extra and stay near the wharf.

I was on a work's conference and had a fantastic time. There were --- of us and I think the overall consensus was great. Our rooms were good, not great, and the bed-linin made for a fantastic sleep. Great location and friendly, helpful staff.

Stayed twice during our celebration trip.
Don't know where to start - the beds are fantastic - L'Occitane toiletries- the staff great - the morning coffee - opposite the fantastic Potenza (chose your wine from their shop) - the stroll to the White House every evening. What more to ask for....

The bellman was polite and waiting upon our --:-- PM arrival. The pool area was nice and the hot tub was good too. The hotel had a little bit of an odd smell that was a little annoying. The drinks at the pool bar were weak and expensive. Also the restaurant was over priced And the food was mediocre at best. Internet was terrible through out the hotel and it didn't work in my room. Also I had no cell phone service in my room either. The location was nice. Overall, the hotel was just average and it really needs some updating and sprucing up and it could be a great place to stay.

I wouldn't listen to the people whining about this hotel. It is CHEAP and in a GREAT location. Is it luxury? No. But it's fine. Lobby is huge and nice, lots of international travelers. Our room was large, spare and clean. I have to laugh at some of the whining: cobwebs, shabby rugs, dings on the walls. OMG! First of all, our room wasn't like this. But secondly, it's at BARGAIN prices. What part of cheap do you not understand? And thirdly, if your room is truly gross, change the room. Not rocket science. Fourth, it's NEW YORK. You'll be out of your room almost the entire time you're there.

The rooms were clean and relatively sound proof. The check in process was quick and simple. My main complaint is that the business computer has - PCs and - or more of them had no internet access for my entire - day stay. Each time I called they said they were sending their IT manager or he had just fixed it. I didn't want to pay the $---day to use the Wireless in my room as I'd heard it was very very slow. Also, we the hotel staff didn't refill our coffee station and placed a plastic cover OVER a glass that still had some water in it from the night before. This worried me about their attention to detail. The highlight was the feather soft beds and pillows and the wonderful air conditioning in the hotel.

First time stay. What a great place the location is excellent and the view is great of the Bay Bridge. Easy to get around the BART station is only one block away which makes airport transfers easy. All the staff was excellent from the bell staff out front to the General Manager. All make you feel welcome. It was a pleasure returning after a day of business in the city. Seems the bar is the hot spot with an outdoor patio for happy hour and the food in the restaurant is superb! The spa is serene and try the head to toe treatment.

I did a lot of research before choosing this hotel and the main complaints i found were -) the rooms are small and -) the staff are rude.
-) yes the rooms are small but if you are a tourist you won't be spending much time in the room anyway. My partner and I stayed at the hotel for a week and never found the room size to be a problem. -) I found the staff to be very helpful and polite. The only reason i could think that people complain about the service is if they are used to the yes sir-madam, - star treatment you might find at upmarket hotels. The staff are quite young (in the mid to late --'s) but very friendly and the overall hotel vibe is trendy soho rather than upper east side. 
I loved this hotel and would definitely stay here again. It's the kind of place people walk into from the street just to take pictures. We dined in the Isola restaurant and the food and service was great. It's the most beautiful restaurant I have been too. Food portions are quite small but delicious. 
The only complaint I had was that there is not much bathroom privacy which might kill the mood on a romantic weekend away. 
Overall, great place to stay and great location. I would highly recommend it.

While the location is great, this hotel is difficult to navigate due to the two towers that only connect on certain floors. Room service was awful. Food was cold, there was a hair on my tray and the $-- lamb chops had to be chewed off the bone because only a butter knife was provided. The hotel was also not as clean as I expected. 
Some rooms have a beautiful view of the river, but they are hard to come by even when booking in advance. I had requested one two months before my trip and assured of one at the time of my reservation only to be told upon arrival that it was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no longer available"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". For a business trip it is OK, not great. For a pleasure trip, I would not recommend it. Stay at the Omni Suites instead.

This hotel is in a superb location, with the Gaslamp District literally outside your door. It's steps away from a multitude of choices in fine dining, clubs, bars, coffee houses, ice cream shops and so forth. 
Our room had concrete floors, which we liked just fine. The shower is frosted glass, with no door and in the corner of the room. If you're shy, this might not be your first choice. The room comes stocked with a high end CD player, an iPod player, a flat screen TV and so forth, none of which we used.
It also has a simple to use espresso maker. Loved that feature and used it daily. 
The staff is fabulous. They're happy and caring. 
We'd definitely stay again.

This could be a good hotel if it had an update. It has single glazing so every police-fire-ambulance in San Francisco can be heard through the night. The fridge had to be switched off as it was noisy. The room was a decent size and clean but just looked dated. The positives are that it is next to a cable car route and the bus stops outside. There are a lot of homeless people in the area but they do not cause a problem or risk - feel sorry not fear. There are good bars and restaurants nearby if you do not want to go far to eat.

We came out for the annual Tiki Oasis weekend with a group of friends. Everyone had a total blast. Hotel staff was super helpful, friendly and knowledgable. The hotel was clean, the rooms big and pretty nice overall. The hotel shuttle was a very helpful feature. The only downside was one of teh two queen beds in our room was at the end of its life, not too bad but not great at all. The other bed was fine. The location of the hotel was really nice too, - minutes to old town and just a few miles to Sea World and other great San Diego attractions. At the end of the trip I picked up on a discrepancy on our bill, they handled the issue right away, professionally and courteously. We'll be back next year.

Just checked out of the Renaissance Mayflower June --, ----, and all I can say is WOW!
From before our trip began , 'til we were leaving for the airport the service at this wonderful landmark was fantasitc. 
Two days before our arrival we got an email reminder from Renaissance hotels with the option of requesting 'feather or foam' pillows etc. I made my request. I certainly expected a canned response and was blown away when a real person , Christine Haag Customer Service Manager emailed me back to make sure I knew my request would be taken care of. That was just a glimpse into the service and attitude of all the Mayflower Staff. From the smiling faces of the front house staff (the doormen, bellhops and front desk) to the great room and up scale amenities - everything was perfect.
I'd especially like to commend not only Christine for her prompt attention to detail (my room was exactly as requested) but also the staff of the Town and Country Lounge. We so enjoyed our late supper on Friday, we stopped by on Saturday for lunch. Each time we experienced expert, professional service with a smile. The most amazing thing, during the lunch hour, the bartender was literally the only staff in the bar. But, you would never know it. My husband and I marveled at how the gentleman behind the bar was able to make drinks, wait and bus tables and still make sure every customer felt special. 
We'll definitely be back.

This was my second time staying at the Andaz. I went back because I remembered being comfortable, the hotel being classy and in a perfect location. I arrived late, --pm and was greeted quickly by the valet. I walked inside and I was greeted warmly and put in a great room. The bed was so comfortable, that I was deep asleep in a matter of minutes.
The amenties were top notch, the bathroom a great size with a large shower was just what I needed. This visit I did not use the pool but knew it was there and remembered it was great! I plan on staying back at the Andaz at the end of next month and look forward to some good shut-eye, walking the gas lamp district, and going for a late night swim. I have stayed at other San Diego Hotels like the W, Hyatt, Hilton, and Embassy Suites... this hotel ranks up with the W and above the others.
Andaz pulls of the botique type feeling with all the modern amenties business travelers are looking for. I woke up early the next day, my car was waiting, the free coffee was hot, and I was on my way after a great nights sleep.

We usually try and stay almost exclusively at Marriott properties because they are universally excellent and we liike to collect their points, but we're glad we made this exception. This is a teriffic property with lovely rooms and exceptional staff.

I was part of a party of - that stayed at The Edison last week during the hurricane that hit NY. The hotel was very clean, and the staff were very helpful and polite. Gloria, from guest services was particularly helpful.
The rooms very adequate, very clean, always with fresh towels and a good maid service. The furniture was outdated, but with new flat screen TV's. 
The cafe was very reasonable with very fast service and tasty breakfasts - very busy at times.
The hotel is within -- yds of Times Square, absolutely fabulous location. I would certainly recommend this hotel.

Cool place to stay. The decor is modern, sleek (think upscale IKEA) and clean with nice details. Fully furnished kitchens, DVD player, plenty of places to charge phones-laptops. Rooms have the heavenly beds (code for lots of pillows) and shower heads that are huge. It adjoins the Vintage Park retail area which has great restaurant options (but not much shopping). The Element is a relaxing atmosphere that feels like an urban retreat instead of a north Houston suburb. Outside by the pool is several fountains and a fire pit. Also a grill is available if you want to cook your own dinner. Even has two bedroom suites for families traveling together. We will definately return.

The Rancho Bernardo Inn is one of those resorts at which you need to stay for several days to unwind and enjoy the amenities. Unfortunately I was there for only one night, and that on business. From my brief stay, though, I saw that it is a warm, inviting resort consisting of a cluster of smallish buildings connected by winding garden paths. There are numerous small fountains and tranquil gardens scattered throughout. The lobby is an upscale rustic Southwestern decor, with an open fireplace. Very inviting and comfortable. The property is reached by driving to the far end of a residential area, meaning that there is no street traffic or noise. The rooms are extremely comfortable and are well equipped for business travelers. The inn automatically charges an all inclusive fee, so you don't have to pay extra for wireless internet access in the room or throughout the property. The hotel's business center was not all that well equipped, but the Rancho Bernardo town center (with a Kinkos) is nearby. It was a great location for our small business meeting, and I can see where a few days here could be very relaxing.

This hotel was in need of a renovation and they really did a nice job.
The property is easy to reach via public transportation and-or driving, though be advised that sometimes GPS signals are very weak in cities. Parking is expensive, but that's the issue when you're in a city.
The hotel is located in a great area and is connected to the Convention Center, across the street from the Reading Terminal Market and about - blocks from the Broad Street Line subway to get to the Sports Complex. Additionally, below the convention center is the SEPTA Market East station, giving you easy access to the suburbs, airport and NJ-Delaware.
I generally get rooms on the Concierge floor or """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""junior suites"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Some of these, located on the highest floors (meaning the junior suites) are below the A-C for the property so they are very noisy. Most of the other rooms are fine. I've also gotten a couple nice upgrades to full suites! You get very spoiled.
Unless you book a package including parking and-or breakfast, these items are not included. There is a Starbucks in the lobby, a Dunkin Donuts, ---- and WaWa within a couple blocks walk, and the aforementioned Reading Terminal Market as alternate options for quick food. The restaurant is fine though I have often had poor service. Not sure if this is due to being a solo female, staff ineptitude or bad training, but I prefer to dine at the bar. That said, the restaurant manager has taken care of this situation.
My major complaint is that in the evening, the music in the lobby-lobby lounge is WAY too loud. This may not bother some people, but on occasion, it's even too loud in the restaurant.
Service is generally very good although I really don't ask for much other than a nice room and early check in. This is a VERY large hotel and can get very busy so be prepared in case there is a long line to check in.
For touring, the hotel is great as there are a few tour buses that stop out front or on the side, AND for those who like to gamble, there is a free shuttle to the Sugar House casino several times each day-again, this is free and is located out the side entrance to the property (on the Hard Rock Cafe side.)
The beds are very comfortable, the new color scheme is pleasing and the rooms are very clean. TVs were all changed to flat screens, and the channel selection is very good. WiFi is not free (unless you are a Marriott Rewards Elite Member) but it is pretty quick. You can get 'free' WiFi in the lobby-picking up the signal from either Starbucks or the FedEx Kinkos location. Also, if you need to rent a car, Hertz has a lobby location.
All in all, the hotel is a great place to stay for any Phila activities.

I've stayed at many --- star hotels and very few if them were as kind and personaly accomodating as the Roosevelt. They exceeded our expectations. Worked their best to work with our unpredictable schedules. Usually when my husband and I travel nothing ever goes as planned except when we stayed at the Roosevelt!

This is a pretty consistent hotel, but odd things happen even to the best of hotels. Boxes not delivered to meeting space, fire alarm in the stairways only going off early in the morning until - am, arguments about the contract for the meeting amenities, etc. Rooms are much bigger facing the courtyard and much, much quieter, but no view. It's a trade off. The heating systems are oddly designed. The transformation of this hotel from ritz-like to the new edgy Renaissance is fun to watch. Front desk staff are well trained, but follow through on promises with them is lacking. Ups and downs aside, it's a good location for everything inner harbor you need - central.

We stayed at Dream - nights for a business meeting. Rooms are big, specially for NYC. Staff has and attitude. Not sure why, maybe its a NYC thing. Location is great, just a few blocks away from Times Square, but not right on Times Square. Which is great as its not noisy. 
Incidentals can get very costly. We asked for a bottle of water, got charged $-.-- just to take it up to the room and then of course, tip and tax , which made it for a very expensive little bottle of good old H-O. $-- is a lot for water - I think-. Also, we asked for a taxi to go to the airport, and the bellman said, they had a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""car"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" right outside that will be the same rate as for the taxi. It was NOT! Total cost was more than --% than the taxi....
In general its a good place, but I will not stay there again next time Im in NYC

A lovely small hotel within easy reach of all local attractions on Manhattan.
 Breakfast at hotel very tasty but basic and resonably priced.
 Rare restaurant served excellent value for money food and the burgers are to die for. Only had to wait any length of time once but it is a very popular venue for socialising.
 Room very comfortable and quiet for New York.
 Went to this hotel on an exchange with Disney Timeshare and they do not use rubbish or want their name associated with rubbish.
Wonderful view from the roof shame the bar did not open until -st May ----
 Will certainly use again in - years when Freedom Tower is complete.
 Stayed ---------- ----------

This hotel is located near the San Jose International airport , close to all destinations in San Jose, comfy beds and well appointed rooms.

Really liked this place and will return. Concierge and doormen helpful. Desk helped with a late checkout. It was a relaxing place to come into at night after full days and evenings in the cacophony of New York.

I don't know who trained these employees , but they were all nice and helpful. I was very impressed with the service and value of the hotel! You will feel very welcome here! And kids are very welcome too. The location is great if you want to do anything in or near West Hollywood. Please take advantage of the pass to get into the Magic Castle. You will love it! I can't say enough about the helpful staff- they will help you with anything you need! You can just be yourself here and enjoy your trip!

Everything about this hotel is amazing! I stayed here for a wedding and was initially a little taken aback by the price of the room, but it was worth every penny. The service is excellent (I got complimentary champagne because my room was not quite ready at check-in. I was also upgraded to a small suite. The room was wonderful. It was very spacious and clean. The bed was so comfortable and I loved having a robe and slippers to wear while in the room. I also loved the George- the system where you can plug your ipod into the speakers and control it from your bed. I had breakfast at Eastern Standard and it was delicious. The hotel is in a great location and it's so easy to get anywhere you need to go from it. I would stay here again anytime I'm in Boston.

We booked a double in order to share rooms. When checking in however, we were given a queen and had to go down to the lobby again to complain for getting what we had ordered. The staff was not particularly helpful (asking why we could not sleep together in the queen) but in the end gave us a double. Just a side note: they did not mention the --$ surcharge for the second person until we checked out. The room was pretty standard, nice but a little small. We had a very nice view over the river. What was particularly cool is that they offer filtered water on each floor.
Service however was really poor. Towels were not replaced, soap and shower gel had to be ordered on the phone because not even empty bottles were replaced by the staff. There is a complimentary laundry (washing machine and dryer) in the basement. However, there was no detergent. After calling the reception and asking for some, the promised it right away. It took us about an hour to get the detergent in the end.
The last thing was the internet. There is wifi in the rooms but it is so incredibly slow and unreliable that we could not really use it at all. A plus though is the fact that it is possible to print documents from your laptop for free.

Wow, what a fantastic view! Truly fantastic. Night + day, I refused to close the drapes on it. No wonder people are always being caught with their pants down through these famous windows. 
The Meat Packing District isn't our favorite area of NY (too many gaudily clad, out of town revelers), but I'd been asking to stay at The Standard ever since I laid eyes on the view from the Highline. Plus, the building's architecture and lobby design are pretty fabulous. 
The room itself was cosy and very well designed. By cosy, I mean both comfy and very small. It's a little like a high end ship's cabin, except with one entire wall being a giant window onto Lower Manhattan, the Hudson, Jersey City and the Statue of Liberty. I watched the sun rise and set. The queen-sized bed was extremely comfortable, there was a small table and sofa, enough closet space, a deep soaking tub, and interesting toiletries.
One thing that some people might have a problem with is that the bed is in a corner.
We stayed - nights, thought housekeeping was good, the bar okay (only tried restaurant bar), the beer garden fun, and the reception staff un-attentive.
