Stayed here largely based on TripAdvisor reviews. Okay at best. A bit worn, and a bit noisy (even on the side street). Breakfast? Most motel continental breakfast offerings exceed this fare.

This is the hotel to choose if you want to mix and mingle. Lots of people and much going on. The cocktail reception is nice, but was quite crowded, as was the breakfast buffet. Our room was average and rather small and dark, since the walls were a dark grey-green and the furniture black, which I did not find appealing. We attended a wedding and reception that was nicely handled and the food and beverages served were tasty. Overall the service was adequate, but not overly friendly, which I simply attribute to the vast number of guests. This was especially true of the valet. After pulling into the queue and waiting, we had to exit our vehicle and ask for assistance and when we picked up, there was no assistance offered with doors or luggage loading. We received a wedding room block discount, so that made it easier to overlook some things, but I would have been somewhat disappointed if I had paid full price. I have had bigger, better appointed rooms and better service at other hotels in this price range, although perhaps this is more typical of a large downtown hotel.

I loved it...it was a flawless stay from a perfect front desk check-in to a beautifully appointed room. Although I got this room on Hotwire and it was supposed to be a ---- star hotel...I believe it is closer to - --- stars and for that reason I will never use hotwire again.

Stayed overnight at this hotel for the Sailabration event at the Harbor - my family frequently visits the harbor area but this was the first time at this hotel - hotel was OK, food definitely overpriced but what got to me the most was extra charges to my credit card. As per the hotel, they charge a $--- incidental fee, which I can understand, but they fail to tell you this at check in! On top of that, the hotel 'made a mistake' as per management and OVERCHARGED my credit card THREE TIMES!!! Yep, as in $---.--!!! on top of the $---.-- incidental fee and the usual room charges!!! As of today, I am still waiting for my bank to release the credit! When I contacted the hotel, all I got was 'lip service' and basically a 'who cares' attitude - NEVER will stay here again - I intend to spend my hard earned money on a hotel who does care!!!

With this """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""prestigious"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel when you pay for a room you literally ONLY GET A ROOM. ALL OTHER AMENITIES MUST BE PAID FOR, well I guess surprisingly the toilet paper in your room you do not have to pay extra for, but everything else you do. You have to pay just to use their really poor gym, you have to pay to park, the internet costs $--!!!
The staff was unfriendly and flat rude when called for basic hotel items, like why the in room 'concierge' computer did not work, where the gym was, etc.. Staff tried to use me to get other staff in trouble which I absolutely HATE. At the end of my stay there were a ton of surprise charges from a mini bar I never used, that I had to argue with the clerk about. He was extremely rude.
I was here for a conference and then for pleasure. During the conference, the food served by the hotel was poor quality and cheap. Navigating the hotel is frustrating because parts of the building is not connected so you have to go all over just to get to where you want to go. 
As far as room service, there is NOTHING reasonably priced on the menu AT ALL! And the food I got was NOT WORTH WHAT I HAD TO PAY FOR IT, and the dessert I ordered was burnt.
We also went to the Michael Jordan steakhouse in the hotel, but were disappointed. The menu was very basic with a limited selection, and nothing special about the very expensive food. 
The only good thing about this hotel is the location, it is easy to get to a lot of shopping on mag mile, but it is still definitely not worth the stay.

Checked in today with Eddie Rayas at the Sheraton Gateway LA. He was exceptionally helpful and very quick. Multi-tasking request while doing my check in. A great first impression for the hotel. He also managed to be courteous while still being friendly and having a little joke. Just what you need after a long flight.

Hotel is situated in a decent location however was very noisy! The parking was overly expensive. You can avoid paying an extra $-- valet fee by parking opposite the hotel yourself. 
We could hear the traffic all night. Staff were good but concierge was a mixed bag. Room service was a little slow but accomodating. 
The one thing I would avoid here at all costs is the rental desk. Possibly the worst rental service you can imagine. Under staffed, long queues and I ended up running around San Fran to pick up a Sat Nav and baby seat because they didnt have even after reserving. Totally useless. 
Rooms were a reasonable size, in fact quite large. Hotel was overall well kept, modern and comfortable. Not sure I would stay again but was still very good.

We spend - days at the hotel for a little stop-by from Germany . Basically the hotel is quite ok because the location is so central that you can reach everything within -- min in Manhattan by using subway. 
Unless you are not stying at the --th floor next to the ice-machine you also will be able to have a good night. So avoid the --th floor - or even all equal numbered floors where ice-machines are located - as i heared (but maybe I am wrong). 
Breakfast was quite moderate, kind of coffee-to-go atmosphere but very convenient.
The cleanliness was also good, maids made a good job.
But now the little shady side: we got a little subtenant in our room: a mouse. This one entered the trash box and also the handbag of my girlfriend because there were some almonds located. We were disturbed in sleeping during the last night because of the action of this animal. Perhaps they will do sth. about it - at least we gave the hint at the reception and to the maid.
Nevertheless we would recommend this hotel even because of this little discomfort - it was quite avarage and compared to european standards between -* and -*.

The staff was friendly and helpful. It was -pm when we arrived, and we wanted to relax with a glass of wine before our dinner reservation at the hotel's restaurant Ovations. The front desk staff provided us with a full page list of other restaurants that were rated by price that we could go to within the area for drinks and food. We went at the Blue Muse which was only a couple of blocks away from the hotel for a glass of wine. The bartenders and the locals at Blue Muse were great. We had another glass of wine at the bar at Ovations when they opened at -pm, and our dinner was amazing. Our room was quaint, and comfortable. The staff gave us a map to find our way around the city, and the access to public transportation was easy to get to from the hotel. We had a great trip.

You cannot beat the price and location when looking for a place to stay in San Francisco. It has free parking and the rooms are clean and quiet. You can get anywhere by bus in a short time. When we first arrived we were greeted by Raymond who is extremely pleasant and helpful (as was the other staff). Basic continental breakfast was fine considering the price of the room. We enjoyed our jogs through the Presidio which is right next to the hotel.

The Monaco is in a beautiful old building which used to be a Post Office so it has long wide corridors which give a great sense of space. The room was very spacious and the bed so comfortable. But it is the wonderful staff who make the place. Every staff member was friendly and helpful, always smiling and saying hello. The concierge gave us great tips for restaurants which were all spot on, and directions for good shops in Georgetown. The quality of the staff combined with the happy hour in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""living room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and the fresh cookies each afternoon really transform the Monaco from a nice hotel to a wonderful hotel. The happy hour means that guests spend time enjoying the hotel instead of just passing through on the way to their room. The hotel is also in a perfect location - easy walk to the Washington Convention Centre or the Mall with all the museums, across the road from the National Portrait Gallery, beside the Spy Museum, along the road from the Ford Theatre and surrounded by incredible restaurants. You certainly won't need a taxi but if you want to take a train the station is across the road. This is a perfect hotel if you like small-medium hotels that are not boring. Thanks to all the staff for making our Washington stay so enjoyable. Stay here.

If i were to travel for any reason to NYC, this would be my first choice for accomodation. Its only - and half stars but thats only a number! The rooms are huge, the kitchenette basic but has fridge, sink, microwave, plates cups, microwave, coffee maker etc. 
The hotel is not shiney-new and there was no breakfast room but its on a par with hotels costing double in the area. The hotel clean, functional, big for NYC and v central. A couple of blocks from Chrysler and across the road from Hertz rental station, whihc can be hand for leaving the city.
The staff were v friendly and discreet...dare I say even hands-off.

My family and I visited New York City in June and stated at the Hilton Times Square. We were welcomed by a great service staff upon arrival. We had an early flight and arrived around --:-- am. Richard was our Guest Service Agent and he was fantastic. He told us our reserved rooms were not ready, but he had rooms available that were upgrades from our original reservation. He was extremely helpful and gave us great advice on several great places to grab lunch. Just a great way to start an incredible visit to the city. The rooms were very large and had a great view of the city. We stayed for four days and everyone in the hotel went out of their way to help us have a great time. Thanks!!

We spent two weeks last year in NYC and decided to choose this hotel for its location, ans its good rating on Tripadvisor. We booked directly with the hotel and chose a junior suite facing the park, room ----. The room next to us was used during the day for interviewing models so it was a bit noisy. The room was ok.
There are not so many facilities in the hotel (decent lobby where you can rest, restaurant, etc...) and sometimes it feels like being in a giant disco, but our stay was overall fairly good. We do recommend this hotel for couples wanting to have a central location in NYC.

Days Inn Camelback is a very typical motel, yet clean, not expensive and with all the facilities one would ask for. I was there with my husband and two children but at the same time I had to arrange few business meetings. That's why I chose it really and I paid ( through Easy Click web site) for a non smoking room with - queen beds, high speed internet access and a refrigerator less than --$ a night. Although usually I try not to do it, that way I could perfectly mix business with pleasure for an absurd price.

I stayed at the Mosser for - nights, and was very happy with the hotel and service. The location is terrific; I took the BART train from the airport (no need for a cab or rental car; save your money!), and the Powell station is about a block away; very convenient!! I liked the area that the hotel was in; lots of shopping around there, and it was easy to get on a cable car to go to Fisherman's Wharf, Alcatraz Ferry, etc.
I stayed in an economy room, so it had a sink, but no bathroom-shower-toilet; those were all down the hall (same as in my house), which was fine by me. The rate was cheapest for such rooms, and I was very happy to stay at the Mosser. I would definitely stay there again, no question; next time I go to San Fran, I doubt that I'll even look at other hotels, if I can get the same deal as I did at the Mosser this past trip.

Unfortunately this was the host hotel for our show at the LA Convention Center. I do hope to change that for next year and find a more worthy alternative.
What can one possibly say about the historic Biltmore Hotel without sounding like you are insulting your disheveled grandmother after too many martini’s. While it may indeed have the finest lobby of any downtown Los Angeles hotel, there is simply a complete lack of attention to the details that would make this place really great. I felt like I was in a bad B-Movie the entire weekend, often wondering if the Black Dahlia's limbs would actually appear floating in the pool. 
Although the fitness equipment is great and the pool refreshing the showers are filthy. The entire area needs a good scrubbing preferably with a commercial cleaner that will remove all the tinea pedis lurking in every crevice. Bring your sandals if you plan on using these facilities. The same goes for the co-ed steam room where the smell of mold and decomposing rubber mats while knock you out before the steam.
My room was extremely dusty particularly along the wall moldings, under the bed and behind all the furniture. Moving the flat screen TV slightly to the left (to make room for my computer) revealed numerous empty sugar packets, used plastic coffee stirrers and splatters of weeks old artificial creamer. Similar artifacts from previous inhabitants were found behind the bathroom door. A used Q-Tip, tampon wrapper, beer bottle cap and a false eyelash clinging to the tile. (I am not kidding!) Clearly signs of a murder mystery that I needed to head down to the bar to investigate. 
While sipping on my $-- Negroni I secretly scanned the room with one eye for an aging starlet missing an eyelash. When my $-- Sliders arrived I sat shocked at the silver dollar sized pieces of dry beef on a bland bun rather confused by the author of the eloquent description on the menu. The Tacos were equally dreadful making me wonder wether the Food Truck parked on Pershing Square was actually servicing the hotel. My suspicions were put to rest after dining at the truck the next day. The food was fantastic making the Biltmore Bar food seem like nothing more than an expensive Denny's.
The following night I had no choice but to meet clients in the bar again. I decided to give the place another chance. Service is pretty nonexistent to say the least so expect to wait about --- an hour to order and another --- an hour to get your cocktail. I went to the bar to get a round of drinks and this really pissed off the confused server. I did end up sending back - dishes that were cold, politely maintaining my patience in the company of potential future clients. A few hours later I paid the bill and retired to my room.
The phone rang about -- minutes later and the waiter from the bar began ranting about me not paying my bill. Clearly he was not aware that I closed out my check with the bartender. Somehow a second bill surfaced with the items I had sent back. I was getting nowhere so I hung up the phone and explained they could charge it to my room. - minutes later there was a loud knock on my door. - Hotel Managers stood there with the mystery bill in hand questioning me about what happened and why I skipped out on the bill. It was almost -:-- in the morning. 
I spent the next -- minutes in my skivvies standing in the hall and lecturing the managers on hospitality basics ---. I had never been so blatantly accused of intentionally ripping off a hotel and was clearly frustrated at that point. They finally apologized, thanked me for the feedback and offered me a free cocktail the next day. Huh? A free cocktail? I promptly cancelled the next - nights of my stay, checked out the following morning and walked across the street to Hilton Checkers. A far superior choice.
Do visit the Millennium Biltmore Hotel when staying in downtown LA as it is a remarkable trip down Old Hollywood memory lane. Dress up like your favorite Silent Film Star and wander the halls looking for Mr. DeMille. Perhaps if you sip on enough Martini's you might actually see the woman with the missing eyelash or the Black Dahlia herself.

My sister and I stayed at the Pod -- for - nights in late August this year. We got an unbeatable price for the bunk bed room and decided to overlook the fact that the hotel would perhaps be not quite finished at the time of our stay, as well as the small rooms, for the savings we would make. We stayed at the hotel Giraffe for the later part of our -- night trip to NYC (see separate review).
The first room we were sent to, after a quick checkin, was uninhabitable. By that I mean that it was so tight spacewise that we could not get our two suitcases in the room and hope to shut the door. We went back down to reception and asked for a room with a better layout. Although the attitude was frosty we were given another room which was adequate. There is no getting around the fact that the rooms are tiny. However, I think that the room we had was quite well designed and made good use of the space available. We pretty much had to sit on our beds when in the room, although there was a desk and chair. But the beds were very comfortable, the room was spotless and thoroughly cleaned each day. 
The bathroom was spacious, relatively speaking, and the shower nice and hot although I would have liked a bit more water pressure. I liked the toiletries provided, and replenished daily. Others have commented on the privacy issues of the glass-walled bathroom, so I'll just second that there is really no place to hide!
A major negative for me was that the room faced into an internal light shaft and so the room was gloomy. However, it must be said that we had asked for a quiet room at the time of booking and so I imagine these are deemed the quiet ones. And they were; we slept well. Except for one night when maybe the lifts weren't working or there was a big queue for them coming down from the rooftop bar, and we were disturbed by the sound of high heels clattering down - flights of stairs! 
The hotel is well located: subway-Grand Central nearby and we walked everywhere Midtown (Fifth Ave-Madison Ave shopping, Rockefeller Centre, Library, Central park etc). There is not a huge amount of options for eating at night in the vicinity, although the upscale market at Grand Central was good, as was the Oyster bar. It is a fairly quiet area at night.
We had drinks one night on the rooftop and it is a lovely spot with quite breathtaking views. However it was very crowded and on a couple of nights, upon returning to the hotel, there was a line outside the hotel for the bar.
The two main negatives for me: the staff had pretty high opinions of themselves and the WiFi was abysmal.
Overall, I was pleasantly surprised by the rooms in terms of the design quirks, functionality and cleanliness. And while the price could not be beat, I would probably only stay here again if I was solo and I could get a room with a bit more natural light.

Just returned from a - night stay at the chelsea star hotel with my husband, we had a hotel room with private bathroom. The room was a good size and bathroom also ok size, little dated but very clean, no facilities like fridge etc but due to not spending much time in your room and somewhere to just sleep, it was adequate for our needs. Bed wasn't great and we kept rolling into middle and a little noisy outside but when air conditioning is on you can't hear anything from the outside.
The location is brilliant!! pretty much central and access to the subway on your doorstep, I definately recommend using the subway, its so easy and cheap.
The staff where pleasant and happy to help when asked anything.
After reading the negative reviews on this site I was very wary about coming here but our experience was nothing but positive, yes in the evening there are a few undesirables around but isn't that the case in any town or city in the world! These people are all around New York even in the day!! Just keep yourself to yourself and go where your going. Always look like you know what your doing even if you don't ha ha!
We cannot comment on the hostel side of the hotel, as we had a private room but we had no problems at all. 
If you want a clean, no frills, central hotel on a budget this is a great option.
For the price we paid and the great location I would definately recommend this hotel.

We stayed at the Farmer's Daughter for one night while visiting LA. Location is great... steps away from Farmers Market, Grove and short walk to West Hollywood. The concept is kitchy-country hip. 
The concept of the place is cool and fun but they fail to deliver on a few fundamental areas: -. Beds are hard as a rock. This will eliminate guests from making a return visit to this hotel. -. Staff at hotel eatery Tart is non-responsive and needs training in customer service and cleanliness Examples: Wait staff were chatting at bar for close to -- minutes before anyone even greeted us... the place is not that big, so this was weird. One wait person cleared crumbs off next table onto bench seat and left it there... gross! I ordered a Mule drink and it was nearly undrinkable... pretty easy cocktail to make so not sure what that was about. Then wait person short changed me.... when I pointed it out he had a vacant look in his eyes and didn't seem to get it nor did he apologize. -. The icing on the cake is the price... I know that it is not cheap for a decent place in LA, but when all was said and done with room and parking (not including drinks at Tart or any other food) total bill was $---. This is outrageous! 
I hope the hotel owner reads this and at least -. Adds memory foam to mattresses and -. trains and adequately gives feedback to Tart wait staff... cleaning house of a few may be necessary. 
Sad to say I recommend staying somewhere else... If for no other reason the Best Western has beds more comfortable than Farmer's Daughter!

We were attending a family wedding and this hotel is great for families.  The suite was spacious and there was a good breakfast with a nice selection.  The hotel was also in good condition and the staff was very friendly.  I have to knock off - star from the rating though because there was a stain on a pillowcase in my room (the staff brought me a new pillow promptly) and because it is bit pricier than what I am used to paying for hotels.

I stayed in this hotel for a conference for - nights in Oct. ----. It's a high-rise and one of the older hotels downtown. The location was great - right near the --th Mall that has shops, food, and a lot of interesting crazies. Unfortunately, it wasn't a great hotel, and didn't meet my expectations as a frequent Marriott guest. 
Wifi is $---night. Make sure you don't try to use it one time plugged in and another time wireless b-c you'll get in a big mess, have to talk to tech support, be told it will come off the bill, then checkout the next day and fight with the lady about it still being on the bill (even though I had a confirmation # from tech support). I mean, who doesn't offer free Wifi these days? There's no free breakfast, either.
The rooms were clean, good views, and everyone else had great customer service with the exception of one person. The gym was nice. But, for $----night, it definitely was not worth that! I wouldn't stay here again. Go to the brand new Spring Hill Suites on Auraria that's maybe a mile away. I stayed there - nights after this place and what a world of difference!

Again we stayed here in October. Very nice hotel. Staff was very friendly. The rooms were clean and quiet. We had a king bed (very comfortable) They have a shuttle to Beale. Which we took advantage of it. We had a gentleman at breakfast tell us about some of the history in the area. If we ever go back, we would stay here again.

I've been hotel hopping in DC for work the for past few months and was really happy to finally find a place with free parking and a small kitchen with a two-burner stove. Most hotels in the District charge a lot to valet park and street parking can be a pain to find, but Carlyle Suites has a small lot behind it (it's first come, first served, and I was told it gets full a lot faster in the summer). The rooms are nice and spacious, with very comfortable beds. The location's quiet, with a decent bar-restaurant downstairs, and the staff was very friendly and helpful. They also have laptops you can borrow to use downstairs, and although there's no gym on premise, you can get free passes to a nice fitness center nearby.

This was a great hotel. At the time of staying however there was a industrial dispute which meant there was protest out the front of the hotel from very early in the morning till late at night. The front desk was more than accomodating and even upgraded our room when I jokingly inquired about it. We were on the --th floor (but could still hear the noisy pickerters downstairs). 
We also got - free breakfast vouchers to use. Wasnt sure if the desk guy was just being friendly or trying to make our stay more comfortable because of the noisy protesters. Unfortunatley the breakfast was quite sub standard. I wouldnt have paid to eat there. Lots of variety, but the eggs and bacon were very cold. 
Apart from that, great location. Great size rooms. Very happy with the accom. Would def recommend it. Oh and there is an internet cafe accroos the road. very handy. Dont forget to see the Sea Lions at Fishermans Wharf !!

My husband and I were extremely disappointed in this hotel. We had planned a romantic weekend getaway, and after finding a great rate, selected this supposed --star hotel. We found most of the staff to be snooty and our room was extremely small and had a badly stained carpet and drapery and a large burn hole in the curtain. If I hadn't known where we were staying, the size and condition of our room would have led me to believe we were staying in some dive that charged by the hour. Also, incidental prices were absurd, including nearly $-- a day for parking (on a weekend!) and $-.-- for a soda from the mini bar. The hotel did have a good location, but that is truly the only positive comment I can offer. The experience left us very disappointed, and we will not be staying at an Inter-Continental hotel again.

My husband & I stay @ The Dolce Hayes Mansion along with our - grandchildren age --. Upon our arrival to the day we left the staff were so attentive to our every need ,you couldn't asked for a more pleasant experince & more professional staff.. The morning breakfast buffet was top notch.& our waitress Maria was fantantic ! . She knew what we liked in the morning & was already for us very morning The kids enjoyed the wonderful pool . We all just can't stop talking about how woderful the Dolce Hayes Mansion is !!! Don't want to forget to mention the wonderful greeting we had from Alan & Adam & how they were there to meet every need . Look forward to returning on our next trip to the west coast .
What can I say...it's a Hilton and you know what to expect! The hotel is perfectly located to walk to Central Park, Radio City Music Hall, and Times Square! Hotel room was clean and comfortable.

The Fairmont is just exactly what are expecting if you are in the market for a high-end, business-traveler-oriented hotel. The common areas are mostly gleaming marble, the rooms feature large desks equipped for quick access to the internet and on the mezzanine the business center competes with the fitness center for space. Similar to other business-oriented hotels the DC Fairmont keeps its meeting rooms in the basement. Why people are made to fly to often distant cities only to meet with others in the basements of large hotels is a huge mystery to me. But I digress, in short this hotel is expensive (daily internet access is $--, the sprawling breakfast buffet is $-- and even with my firm’s substantial discount the room was $---) but you are unlikely to receive any serious complaints from conference invitees or colleagues to whom you recommend it.

I stay at this hotel for work and I have stayed at other hotels in the area and this is one of my faves. The location is great; a great walk down to the wharf or union square. Lots of great restaurants one block behind hotel on Polk St. The staff is nice and they have breakfast in the morning which isn't too bad at all. The rooms are old but very eclectic; the beds are very comfy but the bathrooms are pretty small and have great water pressure! I have always found it to be very quiet. The hotel is attached to Mels diner which makes it nice since it is open -- hrs. There are some homeless people that hang around but if you can find a place in San Francisco that doesn't have a few hanging around then let me know! I just love this city and would definately recommend The Opal!

The location was good.
Check-in was ok. Asked for non smoking room, given floor with half smoking half non smoking. We could smell the smoke as soon as the elevator doors opened. We asked for and recieved a room on a non-smoking floor. They did not bring up the key, we had to go down to the lobby to get it.
Breakfast could have had some healthy choices, the sweet rolls and danish were not fresh. Bananas not ripe.
Room only had ONE wash cloth, had to call down for more.
Housekeeping NEVER showed up at our room. Not for turndown service , not for the morning clean -up. Called down upon our arrival back to our room after being gone all day and we were accused of putting our the Do Not Disturb sign. They said they would come up and they never came when they said they would. We finally told them not to come because of the time. We wanted to get ready to go out for dinner.
Never greeted by anyone as we came and went.
I have stayed at the Peninsula and the Burnham. The Burnham was booked during our stay or I would have stayed there.I will NEVER stay at this hotel again, Not worth ---.-- a night

This property was a surprise to me. Starwood classifies this property as a category -, when it should be at least a -. The Gunter hotel is an historical property that is very well maintained. The customer service was - star and Roy at the front desk made it extra special for my wife and daughter. Having a tired - year old, we decided to stay in and order food from Barrons (the Hotel restaurant). The prices were very reasonable and the food was great. The only disappointment was that the website advertised a heated pool. So having a - year old, we suited up only to have a whirlpool that was to hot and a swimming pool fit for a polar bear. So we packed up our toys and headed for the bathtub. The Gunter hotel is a hotel that is defintely worth it's price and is great for families that are on a budget.

Stayed here for a nearby wedding and was really pleased with this place. Very easy to walk into town in -- minutes, large rooms, good reception service and there was internet and a computer in reception to check in on your flight from!

The hotel is ideally placed. The rooms were very nice, but sometimes an individual employee can make a very good hotel a great one.
The Concierge, Kat Bride, was without doubt the most efficient and helpful hotel member of staff I have ever met.
I would recommend this hotel as the ideal place to stay on a New York visit

We were very disappointed. This once was a great hotel, but is so no longer, based upon our experience. We stayed here primarily because of location and the fact that most of the other near-by hotels had no rooms available that day . Location is great, but check-in was a problem. Entrance to hotel often was partially blocked by strikers (an - year old situation the strikers claimed). After a -- minute wait in check-in line (only one clerk available, not many people in line), the front desk clerk was unable to find our reservation in her system…even though I showed her an e-mail with reservation number and date on it. After about another -- minutes (and a trip to the manager’s office) she “found” our reservation. Apparently the reservation system and the front desk computers do not always communicate well. She admitted that this happens occasionally, but is not the norm- an old computer system was blamed. She was very nice though (as were most of the staff) and gave us a (presumably upgraded) room with a view of Grant Park ( which was a great view!). The room was large with a very high ceiling, tastefully decorated and looked clean and well-maintained. There was a wall mounted flat panel TV that seemed a bit too small (--”?) for this large of a room. There was no desk, but there was a small table that could make do….if one did not mind running internet cable from TV and unplugging coffee maker to plug in computer. The room looked to be recently remodeled, but had not quite been completed , leaving an ancient banged up air conditioning cabinet ( covering a window unit that had a fan control, but no obvious thermostat) and at least one part of trim painted a different color. There was a large walk-in closet with surprisingly little space to hang anything. There were no collapsible luggage racks – just a permanent one built into closet & reducing usable hanger space. The beds were OK, but nowhere near as comfortable those found in Starwood hotels as well as in most Hiltons and Marriotts. There was plenty of hot water and great water pressure. Amenities (soap, shampoo) were minimal and brand-less. There was very little flat space to put anything in the bathroom. It took -- minutes to get car mid-day even though no one else seemed to be using valet service at the time. I would not recommend staying here unless you can tolerate strike lines, erratic check in and slow car-valet service…. and you could get room for less than about $----night.
Staff was very welcoming after a terrible experience at the hotel next door. Room was very clean and breakfast was delicious! I would stay here many times again!!!!

This was our first trip to NYC and choosing the hotel was difficult. Glad to say we chose the Hampton Inn Times Sq North. it is in a fab location, perfect for all the attractions but nicely away from the busy Times Square. Inside is a very clean and calm environment, away from the hustle and bustle of the city. We stayed on the -th floor and had a good view. Excellent staff and housekeeping. Room was stocked up with toiletries and fresh towels every day and I made sure I went back to find them on our last day to tip the lady on duty. The breakfast is a must, plenty of fresh food, hot & cold, fruit etc. Very helpful staff in reception, the concierge was very helpful in finding out how to get about (and sorted our transfer to JFK when it went wrong).

I have never written a bad review for a hotel, but this will be my first time. This was my second stay at the Kimberly Hotel. My first visit was okay. The location was fine, staff friendly and the room spacious and fairly clean (I stayed in a one room suite). My second stay was pretty terrible. I stayed in a one bedroom suite once again, but the room was worn and dingy. It just looked and felt dirty. The room's windows were stuck open. The reason for this is that the heat won't shut off automatically. You have two choices: heat on and blazing, or heat off. Consequently, the delightful sound of street noice and horns fills the room all night. There was little water pressure. I spent crazy amounts of time wating for the elevator. In fact, one time I waited so long I simply chose to walk down nine flights of stairs. The morning I was there, a group of people actually got stuck in one of the elevators. They had a convention meeting in the building which meant the very small lobby was often jammed. Both times I needed the doorman, he was nowhere to be found. I found upon arrival I had been assigned a smoking room. Apparently a non-smoking room is a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""special request"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on their reservation website. You are not asked your preference when making the reservation. I requested a different room but was told that they could not move me (despite the fact that I was checking in early). Sure, the location is great, but that is about it. And the cost is reasonable, but I'm not sure you even get what you pay for at the Kimberly. I won't be staying here again.

We at Hotel Pennsylvania from June --th to June --th in a room with three beds. We gladly checked out this morning.
This hotel is in a prime location, with easy access to many of New York's most famous attractions. That being said, it has so much potential to be a top notch hotel. But boy it couldn't be any more opposite. I don't know if we just got a bad room or what, but it was absolutely terrible.
The beautiful lobby is very deceiving, making you believe that the rest of the hotel is just as picturesque. That all changes the minute you step onto your floor. The hallways are worn and drab; half the time you think a ghost is following behind you. The Stephen King corridors eventually lead to your room, which is guarded by a heavy door with outdated decor on it. 
The prison-like gate swoops open to reveal the most trashy room I've ever seen. The bathroom is to the immediate right, filled with peeling white paint and walls that are scratched and clawed, dogged with a hideous door that doesn't even shut. Further into the room is the outdated television, three lumpy beds with flat pillows, and two miserable looking tables; nothing else, not even a mini fridge. The only trash can is a pathetically tiny one in the equally pathetic bathroom. The neglected windows are impossible to open and close without the aid of a maintenance man. The TV remote barely even works, paired with an ancient set that doesn't even show what volume it's at. Finally, there is a walk-in closet shared by the adjacent room, but it's just as tacky and tired as the rest of the room, if not actually better.
So to sum it all up, don't waste your time and money at this travesty of a hotel. Fork out a little more and get much better accommodations at a different one.

We arrived in the middle of the night and the Kimpton employees made us feel right at home. I stay at boring hotels all the time so when I get the chance to stay at a Kimpton, it's always a pleasure. I didn't want to check out the next day!

I was traveling with a group that booked several rooms in this hotel so I'm not sure on what price we paid for the rooms (sign outside was advertising $--.---room). I noticed a few narrow places where it looked like they couldn't get the vacuum in very well but the bathroom was great and the sheets and bedding were clean. Service was excellent and the front desk got us settled very quickly and even offered to provide us with shuttle service to a restaurant if we needed it (we decided to walk).
I slept fairly well (although others in our group did not). The bed was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""firm"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and had the feel of being a solid budget mattress (no pillow top here but not sagging either). My only complaint would be the sheets and blankets - the sheets seemed pretty thin and had a worn feel to them, the blankets were obviously fairly low quality polyester. But for the price wasn't expecting more - for an overnight budget trip or a night before a flight they were fine. Room was cold when we arrived (heat not on) but warmed up pretty quick. No problem with noise from other rooms or flights.
Bathroom looked like it had had a basic Bathfitter's reno with a few extra touches. My only complaint was the complimentary soap and shampoo - really didn't smell too good, kind of a Dollar Store feel and smell to it. Make sure to bring your own!
Wireless was excellent - had no problem connecting with my MacBook. Great signal and good bandwidth. Other facilities like the business lounge (?) and the fitness room were pretty basic. Don't book this hotel solely for the fitness room as you'll be very disappointed : ). Coffee only in the morning, no continental breakfast.
Several restaurants nearby within walking distance. We ate breakfast at the Denny's a couple of blocks down and had dinner at pub further down.
Overall this was good value for the money - basic overnighter hotel. If I was flying out of Seatac and needed a place to crash I'd probably book again.

Great location; beautiful room with a view of Washington Monument and Capitol Building. Surprised my wife and I with a birthday bottle of wine and chocolate covered strawberries (we share the same birthday).

The Bryant Park Hotel has the ideal midtown Manhattan location, everyone is friendly and helpful, and the rooms are clean and modern. You can't go wrong when all of the important points are so well covered. Of course, you pay for it. We were there during the -th of July week and we got what they call a junior suite for $----night. Not much light (natural or otherwise) meant that it was difficult to work in the room and wifi connection was a little intermittent.
The site itself is strange. I like to think I have a reasonable sense of direction, so didn't get too lost. There were a couple of points where I ended up walking down a road only to find I couldn't get through to where I was aiming though. 
Staff were all very helpful and well turned out, rooms seemed clean, though I did find a previous occupant's sweet wrapper under the corner of the TV cabinet.
Overall it's far from the worst place that I've stayed, but hardly stood out as a fantastic hotel. A resounding 'meh'.

We stayed here with group rates for a convention, but found there were much lower rates available through the internet, the week before we arrived. We were unable to change our booked reservation, so had to pay the higher amount. A few days, we had no cold water. It made no sense to me, but it's an issue they had dealt withbefore. They offered us free bottled water for our inconvenience. Honestly, it wasn't a big deal. The rooms were nice, with enough space. There was a small refrigerator, which was nice for restaurant leftovers. Not enough drawers for clothing. A decent amount of outlets for allof our powered devices, even by the bedside. The pool area was a little spartan, notvery well decorated, but workable. The worst part was the pavement around the pool. It got terribly hot, made worse by the dark slate-like tiles on the pool surround. You really need to be careful getting in and out. The pool was wonderful relief from the triple digit heat. The poolside beverages were very nice, particularly the mango daiquiri! Since the sun doesn't hit the pool until after noon, it would be nice to have a few lounges or chairs on the opposite side of the exercise room, where there is a nice space, but no furniture. The staff was great. The beds were comfortable. There were multiple lounges and restaurants in or off the lobby. Nice hotel.

The positives about this hotel are location on hotel circle in San Diego, a serviceable restaurant on the property, good internet access, as well as a nice lounge. The negatives are the limitations on cable channels on the TV, which is an important aspect for many guest. The only news-business station available is CNN; and otherwise most of the other stations are local sports and network stations. Rooms are comfortable, and it is worth it to pay the extra few dollars for a balcony over the pool.

Honestly the worst hotel I've ever stayed at. It took -- minutes waiting in line to get checked in.. and there were - people behind the desk and only - guests being helped.. slowly. The rooms are tiny, the paint is peeling, there are holes in the carpet and walls, it looks like a motel - room rather than a hotel room basically. Now onto the holding fee.. when we checked in the girl said after our check out it will take """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no more than -- hours"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to go back onto the card if there's no charges. I had to attend a conference over at the Adams Mark Hotel. This hotel is a good two blocks away but a world away in service and room amenties. Hot water was always available, no matter what time of day or night. The internet worked every time I tried to log on. The business center with two computers was available when I needed to print something. There was not an extra charge for using the printer nor the internet. The room was crammed with furniture but it was nice to have a sofa and a chair to sit on instead of only the bed. The decor was bright and cheery. The bed was perfect and the blanket was encased in sheets. The shower had a choice in spray type--hard, pulsing, or gentle. 
The staff was super friendly. I flew in early for the conference and dropped off my luggage at Hotel Indigo without a hitch. The East downtown transfer station is only one block away if you want to take the bus anywhere. I took the local bus from the airport to the hotel door for only $-.--. It sure beat waiting for the Super Shuttle to come or riding the van around and around the airport waiting on more customers before it left for downtown Dallas. 
Downside: I walked the two blocks from the Adams Mark to this hotel every time I wanted to go back to my room for something. The shuttle was available if I needed it which I did when I got caught in a downpour. There is only one restaurant in close proxiity for breakfast. At night, you need to take the bus or tram down to the West End to find food. Most everything closes at -pm in this area for food. 
Make sure that you bring your walking shoes if you are going to attend a conference over at the Adams Mark. The distance from rooms to conference to food or bar is huge. Some people in my group had problems getting around because of their fitness level.
Clean and updated rooms. Friendly and helpful staff. Perfect location to enjoy several parts of the city.

Huge room, free parking, outstanding customer service from the front desk, to the cleaning staff, to the parking attendants. It really is an unbelievable value....our room was huge and the parking, in downtown chicago, was free. We would definately stay here again.

My daughter and I spent - very happy days in Boston , staying at the Back Bay Hotel.The hotel is very well located to be within walking distance of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""must see"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" items on our list. It is - or -- minutes walk from underground stations. The staff at the hotel were warm and friendly, nothing was ever too much trouble.The concierge was painstakingly helpful in helping us to plan our sight seeing. The beds and rooms were very comfortable ;and we experienced very good room service for the evening meal ,the first evening. We ate from the good and varied breakfast menu, but chose to dine and the plentiful nearby restaurants. In all a very pleasant experience.

Great resort style vacationing with friendly staff catering to families of many different shapes and sizes.
If your a business traveler however you should be advised that this Hilton does NOT offer wireless internet service. but rather offers for $---day internet connection using an Ethernet cord (connection speed was rather slow).

We became fans of Element after staying at the one in Vegas.  When we learned that Starwood's """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""green"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel brand -- complete with signature """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hybrid only"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" parking spaces -- had a location  here in the oil and gas capital of the world, the irony of it all was more than we could resist.  After all, the element that feeds families in this town is Carbon!

We found the property clean and well maintained.  The location has some restaurants and retail within a short drive.  Moreover, it is far enough from the --- Freeway to provide a peaceful and quiet atmosphere.  Parking areas are well lit and the hotel has some nice common areas for relaxation both inside and out.
There were a few gaffes during our stay; however, the managers were gracious and responsive to our concerns and the staff appeared to find their game before we left.
Before you go, keep in mind that instead of little individual bottles, Element properties have """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""locking"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" shower gel dispensers that aren't always locked.  We recommend bringing your own shower soap as we do.  I won't go into what some perverts have been caught putting in shower gel dispensers, but if you want to be sure that is soap you are lathering up with, bring your own!
Overall, we recommend this property and we would stay here again.
They advsed us on restaurants, sightseeing, always good, and offered their assistance in any way wewanted. Would defintely stay again.

Initial confusion (on our part ) sent us to the Palomar in Arlington - a beautiful hotel and as they told us newer tahn the one we were booked into!
Arriving at the right hotel we were met with a slightly frosty reception and the black drapes hiding the renovation work by the elevators didn't make us feel great about our choice. 
Entering our room all this vanished! Our room was very quiet (overlooking the small outdoor pool) but was very well proportioned with ample closet space, a good sized bathroom and two large and very comfortable beds. 
After we had settled in for a short while (a friendlier) reception rang to check that everything was satisfactory - a nice touch. 
Our reservation included vouchers for complementary continental breakfast but after a mix-up on the first morning where no one knew what we were entitled to and we were directed to a buffet and (almost) charged. The next morning the same hostess was unable to answer the same questions about the vouchers. When eventually the issue was resolved we decided not to bother as the vouchers provide very little. Instead we relied on the free urn of coffee in the foyer to wake us up before heading downtown. 
A small problem with the sink (hand basin) was fixed immediately. The in-room safe was big enough to take a laptop and the ironing board and iron were useful as we had traveled down from New York. 
We never got back in time to sample the complimentary wine in the evenings so I know we'll want to return - and maybe try out others in the group.
in summary a good hotel that was good value, classy but not stuffy.

We stayed for four nights, and it was a lovely stay. The Riverwalk runs right beside the hotel, you can even dine outside along the water. The room was comfortable, two televisions, two full beds plus a pull out bed. The hotel had a nice restaurant with a yummy buffet.
The staff was helpful, kind, and attentive. The hotel lobby and lounge were beautifully decorated.
Being that the hotel was on the Riverwalk, it was easy walking distance to restaurants and shops.

As a traveling consultant, I've sampled the hotels in the Baltimore area, and none match the service received at the Sheraton IH. They were remembering my name after my second week, and I received a personalized note and gift basket during one of my longer stays. The staff take great care of their clients, and the location can't be beat (particularly in summer - right next to the harbor itself!). For business or pleasure, this hotel provides great value for the Baltimore traveler.

From the moment we arrived we were treated like royalty! It was easy to access the hotel from the highway and the parking garage was easily accessed for self parking. Check in went smoothly, we had reserved as part of a Summer Package and received a room w- a city-lake view on the top floor! Also as part of the package was free self park and free wireless internet. The concierge was very helpful and recommended a place for dinner. We did see a show, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The Color Purple"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" at the Arie Crown Center in McCormick Place and getting to and from the show was extremely easy and completely indoors. Taxi to the Mile depending on where you are going is $----- each way. The room was a fair size and clean. The decor was slightly older but in good shape. Our view from ---- was AMAZING! We could see Navy Pier, the marina and several of downtowns buildings. The beds at the Hyatt hotels are wonderful and we never have a hard time sleeping:) I did use the Fitness Center and it was very nice and accessible -- hours. The only downside of this hotel for me is that it is a little out of the way for what I am usually doing in Chicago. I would definetely stay here again though!

I stayed here for the third time with my teenage children and my wife. Every time I stay here, it seems to get worse. This was definately my last time at this hotel. We used PriceLine and they always put us in this hotel as a -.- star. It is definately not worthy of a -.- star.
While the hotel is convenient to the San Jose airport, the rooms are very worn and badly in need of refurbishing. The staff are very friendly and there are always the welcome cookies at DoubleTree. The common areas are still well kept and the pool is decent. The damp floor (actually wet carpet) in our room with mildew smell was disgusting. Paint is chipping off the bottoms of the doors to the outside and bathroom. Lots of people with pets stay here (probably a reaon for the wet carpet) so perhaps if you travel with pets, it could be an option. We will definately not stay here again. If we use PriceLine, we will exclude the San Jose area where this hotel is located.
I was quite busy this trip, so sorry I didn't take any photos.

Stayed for - night in a bay window view room. The rooms are excellent, best bedding by far during our - week USA holiday. Location excellent with walking distance to many attractions, shopping & dinning. Breakfast was perfect, eggs and also fruit & oats. This was the second most expensive property we stayed at, NYC was the most, well worth the price. Highly recommended & would stay again if in Boston.

Stayed here with my elderly father and wife. Great location, service and staff. We had no issues at all with noise from the railway or anything else. Great place to stay, and easy to get too. Would stay and recommend to my friends without question.

My partner and I recently stayed at this hotel for - nights. This was our first time at this hotel and we were very pleased. The location is great-- Tribeca ( which stands for the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Triangle Below Canal (Street)"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" has great restaurants, shops, and is near the West Village, Chelsea, Chinatown and Soho. The rooms were clean and up to typical Hilton standards. We had a small refrigerator and a microwave in the room. Although we faced -th Avenue, we did not find the street noise a disturbance. Staff was also helpful. 
There's no concierge or fancy hotel lobby, but if you are looking for basic, clean, comfortable accommodations for your NYC stay, consider the Hilton Garden Inn-Tribeca. You'll be very satisfied.

I stayed at The Standard recently for my birthday and had a great time! We arrived late in the evening and the front desk was very helpful, check in was a breeze. I think our front desk agent's name was Terrell, he was super nice and helped us find a great room. 
The room was fantastic, but nothing can compare to the views!! We were only on the -th floor, but you’d be hard pressed to find a cooler view in the entire city! Aside from the rooms, both the Grill and the bars were worth the trip. I couldn’t get enough of the Biergarten (it’s enclosed during the cold weather) and my girlfriend loved Le Bain. 
Between the views, the food and the party, I will absolutely be back!

Thanks to the other TripAdvisor reviewers who recommended this hotel. We found it a clean, convenient and affordable place to stay in Chicago and a great base of operations for exploring attractions in the Loop and Navy Pier. 
The front desk told me the hotel was built three years ago on redeveloped land that had once been """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""projects"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and the area around the property is clearly gentrifying. I never felt unsafe, but was very glad that parking for guests was secured by a key-card accessed gate and tall fence.
We appreciated that the hotel was right on --th and State Streets so that we could catch the #-- CTA bus to the Loop and later take the same bus back from Navy Pier in the evening. All in all, a safe and wise choice for a budget-minded traveler.
The only downside was that our queen bed was a bit too soft so my wife and I ended up sliding into the center of the bed instead of having support on each side. A little extra togetherness wasn't hard to put up with, though.

Stayed four days and found the location to be perfect. The room was clean and comfortable and fairly large. The lobby restaurant was superior to most hotel offerings, and there were many more within a ver short walk.
I would definitely stay again.

We booked and paid a little extra for a corner room, and on check in asked for a room on an upper floor. It was Sunday to Tuesday so maybe there were plenty of rooms available...anyway..the room (----) on the --nd floor, had the most wonderful panoramic view of San Francisco..you could lie in bed looking out on two sides of the room, through huge windows, at the whole of SF. The room was very clean, with a huge comfortable bed, a fridge, flat TV, reasonable bathroom. The staff were very friendly and helpful. Public transport in SF is excellent and the hotel's location, although not in the very centre of town, is near enough, and located on Van Ness Ave and California, which have frequent buses, meant an easy bus ride to Fisherman's Wharf and downtown. It was reasonably priced. I don't understand British people complaining about only coffee sachets in the room and not 'tea'. This is trivial..there are small grocery stores on Polk St just behind the hotel.The only thing was the business centre was a bit small, with only one computer working at the time and the very small health club has hardly any equipment in it....but there was a great outdoor swimming pool with more views of SF. It was an enjoyable stay.
Arrived on a Friday tea time, sun shining and bar packed to the rafters. Hotel was spotless and perfectly located but did pay more than at any other previously visited US hotels.

On a trip to Rockies. Stayed at the JW Marriott in Cherry Creek, got a Junior Suite and it was costly! Loved the Cherry Creek location! Several great restaurants were within walking distance, along with lots of museums, art galleries and shopping.

I only stayed at the Serrano hotel for a night. It is located adjacent to Union Square and the Cable Car main stop. You can get there from airport by taxi or BART (with some walking). 
The staff at check-in was very courteious and helpful. They responded to my request and questions with proper manner and professionalism. 
The room was a bit small but still bigger than the hotel rooms in Europe and Japan. The mini bar has quite a collection. If you join their InTouch loyality program (free), you will get $-- towards the mini ba plus free internet. 
Overall, a nice little hotel.

My biggest issue were the meals here. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""kids eat free"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" concept was one item that drew us to this hotel. I had read complaints about the train. There IS a train that you can hear, but it didn't keep us awake, or wake us up. The rooms are pretty well insulated I think. We had a corner room, and it was very quite.

With so many hotel choices, I'm not sure why one would choose to stay here. A family member booked our stay otherwise I would not have. The rooms are very dark and dated so they don't feel very clean which is a big deal to me And the only reason I would not go back. The staff was nice, the pool was big (though the pool towels were tiny and scratchy), the grounds we grassy and well maintained and the hot breakfast included was a hit. I just really did not like the old look ad feel of the rooms.

I stayed here for a week with my boyfriend. It's a nice hotel, rooms a little smaller and older than the photo's but we got a great deal on travelocity. It's in a really good location, close to public transport and really easy to get to and from the airport using BART. Go for cocktaisl in The Westin St. Francis on Union Square they are great and if you get a chance to see a gig at Greek Theatre in Berkerly do it do it do it. We saw Ray La Montange and David Gray and it was one of the best concerts i've ever been to.
Sarah

Stayed at this hotel-conference center this week while attending a conference. Have been here many times before as they are consistent for cleaniess, helpful staff, and a spacious and nicely appointed room. The room appeared to have been renovated recently. Our room overlooked Lake Michigan which was a very nice part of the stay. This hotel is always very busy with group meetings, conferences, family events on the weekends, etc. You can grab a cab in a few minutes. You do have to walk to get anywhere or cab it as it's off the beaten path a couple of blocks. It is a challenge to grab a bite in one of the hotel's restaurants when it's busy as they are limited on seating. The bar is great with good bar food. The whole place is packed when there is a large group there, especially if the weather is bad outside. I had to settle for pretzel chips and hummus for a late lunch as all the places were closed for a couple of hours during the day. (at -:-- pm). Wouldn't be my first choice to stay in Chicago as I like a more intimate setting or more amenities. This Hyatt is really positioned for large group settings.

We 'bought' a weekend at Pointe Hilton Tapatio Cliffs Resort at a silent auction for a charity, that included a Presidential Suite. Don't be fooled by that. They have -- or more Presidential Suites and I don't think that is an appropriate name for the room. We were reassigned when I mentioned our voucher was THE Presidential Suite and told that they had multiple suites of this catagory. The lady at the desk who was very pleasant, told us this was one of their favorite rooms because of it's view. Well, if we stood leaning over our balcony, looked through buildings and a bit around our balcony, we could see a pool and a bit of the city and by gosh, a parking lot. It was a nice corner room that had another view of a building, and the last view was a mound that had a road on top of it, so we heard both cars going up and down and people on the stairs. (And stairs from the parking lot do not have rails, not for the faint of heart). 
Once in the room it was quite nice, however NOT presidential. The first thing I always look at is the tub, and this was NOT a tub that I wanted to sit in. It was an old ordinary tub-shower combination, similar to a rental apartment set up. There were - bathrooms which was a nice feature, too bad someone didn't take the time to put one of the sinks in properly, poor workmanship (husband's a general contractor) and one of the toilets ran every -- minutes. Mike, Dave, the pro shop gentleman, the snack cart lady and everyone else were wonderful even if the Marshall did seem a bit clueless about driving his cart around just as I was ready to hit. Best part of the trip. Would have been helpful to have a map of the course since we had never played there. We ate at the Pointe in Tyme and had a snack by a pool. I'll review the restaurant separately and Cascades Cafe was good but once again, 'too bad' they didn't get my order right. (Beef or chicken was the choice, I asked for beef, I got chicken). Kind of a hap-hazard operation in a lovely setting. Nice enough, but too many 'too bad'.

Pleased and surprised with everything from the time we checked in until we left. Our hotel was close to the airport and featured amenities that allowed us to enjoy ourselves all weekend. Even though we were on the frontage road next to the expressway, we were able to walk to area restaurants on the sidewalk. We were in walking distance of North Star Mall, as well.
We ate dinner in our hotel and the snacks and dinner with dessert were truly delicious. 
Our room, on the -th floor, was clean, spacious and quiet.
The staff was friendly and very accommodating at all times and due to their friendliness we plan to return.
We were - miles from downtown, but the drive was easy and we found our way around to the AT& T Center-Freeman Coliseum and The Market Square for shopping and delicious Mexican Food at Mi Tierra restaurant. 
Great get away!!

My husband and my self went to Chicago for a - day getaway and were so happy that we opted to stay here. We took the train- subway from the airport to the hotel and it took about an hour. 
From the moment we arrived we found that the front desk staff and concierge were attentive and helpful. The room was very clean (passed our bed bug check) and the amenities in the bathroom (soap, shampoo, body lotion) were of a very good quality. The hotel's location made it very easy for us to get oriented and made it a great spot for us to base our different day tours and visits. We never ate in the cafe or bar so can't comment on it. 
The bed was very soft, suspected that the pillows and comforter were down and were worried as my husband has allergies- but he didn't react. We were so impressed with how quiet the hotel was- we were by the elevator and it looked as though the hotel was quite full, but we didn't hear anything and slept very peacefully.
Hoping that the next time we can bring the kids and take advantage of any future promotions- discounts as it was a great experience staying here.

we were very please with our stay at the hotel. the staff was great especially matt. He seemed to answer the phone quite a few times. I would even call the hotel when i was out, for help with taxi service, locations, they all gladly helped. The rooms were beautiful, my husband is very picky and he loved it as well. we will come back.

I booked due to the cheaper cost and excellent location. Until my stay, I was surprised at it's ranking as a --star hotel, but it most certainly is. Basically, you get what you pay for. Common areas of the hotel need work. It is a very old historic hotel, but the upkeep has been sloppy. Picketers stand outside the valet entrance. We used a self-park about - block away due to the bad reviews on the valet service (also saved us around $--.) As far as the room itself, we were in the north tower, -th floor. The furniture, tv and bedding were all new and clean. Lighting in the bathroom was terrible. Noise level in the room was louder than newer hotels in the area (other guests as well as traffic noise outside). I enjoyed receiving excellent service. The room I was in was not to my expectation, the front night auditor suggested another room and I decided to keep the one assigned and waited for my request. Not bad location, but I´ve been much better located in NY for less than the USD----day paid here. I´ve only accepted this hotel because I booked my trip a few days earlier, so the hotels I like were all booked already.

We stayed over the weekend for a leisure trip to the City. The construction is loud thought not very disruptive. More than anything was the issue that the hotel is located directly at Ground Zero. I knew this going in, and was fine with it in theory, but actually being there was a bit unnerving. Also, the location is apparently (I've discovered since returning home) the hotel's primary marketing strategy, which seems a little crass.
The hotel itself was nice. As noted, it is currently under construction. To compensate, they are offering a breakfast each day (baked goods, oatmeal, juices, cereal) and a Happy Hour each night (wine and beer selection, various cheeses and meats, and a veggie tray). Very much appreciated, and welcomed. We booked the cheapest option room, and it was surprisingly outfitted with a mini-frig, convection over and dishes. Really a nice surprise. Also, there are water bottles on each floor, which was a nice treat. Combined, these two things were a large cost savings. Finally, there is a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Guests Needs"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Closet on each floor where you'll find extra blankets, extra pillows, irons and iron boards and a variety of other needs. On the downsides, the showers stink. If you need a nice long shower with even decent water pressure, this is not the place for you. 
The hotel staff was very friendly, though not very helpful. They were frequently unable to provide restaurant suggestions and-or directions (the one night they did provide help they sent us to a restaurant that was not open on Saturdays), and discouraged travel by any means other than taxi cab. If you're looking for the NYC experience, complete with mass transit, do some research before you arrive. However, our room was very clean each day, and any time we ran into a staff member in the building they were incredibly kind. I think they'll become more helpful the longer the hotel is open and as they become more familiar. 
All things considered I would recommend the hotel, but with a strong caution about its proximity to Ground Zero.

Staffed by a lovely bunch of folks, the Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers is coming apart at the seams. The yet to be completed renovations cannot be finished soon enough.
If you're sensitive to mold, then do yourself a favour and check your bathroom carefully for mold upon entering your guestroom for the first time. The first guestroom that I was put in had a bad black mold problem in addition to it being in a state of disrepair. The guestroom to which I was subsequently moved also had a mold issue and was similarly less than ideal, but I was too busy to move again. I did let a woman on the reception desk know about the second mold problem upon check out, however. It seems likely that renovated guestrooms are handed out only by special request and even then they are necessarily subject to availability unless you've got some kind of status with Sheraton or you've paid a top rate. Both of the rooms that I saw were dated and a bit tatty.
Cleanliness also seems to be a problem. I found a few glaring cleanliness issues during my stay at the hotel, but I discussed only three of them with hotel associates. How hair finds itself smeared on to a bathroom ceiling is beyond me! It could have gotten there by the hand of a guest as easily as it did a dirty housekeeping or maintenance rag, but the point is that it shouldn't be on the ceiling at all. 
Look, I know that it has to be very difficult to keep guestrooms clean and I take care to leave a couple of bucks for housekeeping cleaners every day, but hair on the ceiling? In my many decades of travelling, that's a first for me. It was a bit of a shock in a hotel of this calibre.

Empty your car of any valuables and provided it isn't a fancier late model vehicle, it should be safe enough on the streets of Streeterville over night. Street parking is available on the ramp descending from reception or on the streets below the elevated reception level of the hotel, which streets can be accessed from the reception level by a set of stairs at the end of East North Water Street. Parking in this manner saved me anywhere from $-- to $--- during my stay.

We were looking for an inexpensive place to stay. I found this by chance by googling """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hotels in san diego."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" It was a great find.
This place is NOT the WINN!! It's a budget hotel. It's location is within ---- minutes of anything you'd want to see in SD (except the Wild Animal Park, which is not in SD). The rooms are spotless. The staff was friendly. I thought the breakfast was more than mediocre. My husband and I eat cereal or instant oatmeal and hot tea-coffee for breakfast each morning on a typical day. This breakfast offered assorted danishes, fresh fruit, yogurt, - or - kinds of cereal, toast, butter, jams, syrup for your waffles made fresh on these wonderful waffle irons, coffee, tea, milk, orange, apple, papaya juice. I didn't taste the sausage, as this was the one thing that did not look too great.
I do agree with other reviewers about the size of the rooms. We did not even get a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""suite."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" See my posted pictures with this review. Our room was a postage stamp just large enough for a king bed, small entertainment center, and a small table and - chairs, with NO room to spare. The bathroom, however, was quite spacious, immaculately clean, and had all necessities, including - fresh bath towels every day...and we were only two people in the room!

This hotel was fine for business travel. The rooms are a little dated but comfortable.

I agree with the last few reviewers. Thoroughly enjoyed my recent - night stay. Great location, friendly and hospitable staff, clean and comfortable room, nice happy hour and breakfast. I'll stay here next time I visit Charlotte.

This hotel is a great value! Staff was extremely friendly and helpful. While the rooms are small, they are clean and the marble bathrooms are fresh and new. The restaurant was incredible! Tapas and great martinis. Very modern and great vibe. Highly recommend for the traveling business person. I would even bring my family back. Close to the TD Garden and Quincy Market. Loved it. also recommended us to an amazing spa - Melt.

I stayed here for - nights. The hotel really needs some refurbishing, hardly a - star hotel for European standards. The staff are nice, but not genuinely interested in helping. Also, paid wi-fi on a hotel like this, when even Starbucks offers it for free is really bad.

Also, some gifts I bought disappeared from my luggage, probably stolen. So, better use the safe.
Not bad, but if it's up to me, won't stay here again.

Stayed here for the -th time last December. You know what your getting before you go and as for location, well you couldn't ask for more.
 Firstly the downside, of which there aren't many. If you get a room to the rear of the hotrel the odds are that your 'view' will consist of a brick wall. That said you ae very rarely in your room during daylight hours and the rear rooms are quieter than those at the front on West --th Street.

This place is a good choice for those visiting New York City on a budget.
I stayed for three nights in a two bed dorm room. Rooms are basic, come with a sink, lockers and heating. The staff downstairs were pretty awesome, I was traveling by myself and they told me of an --'s party-club happening that night.
