The shared bathrooms, three or four of them to each floor were the best quality. One had a rain shower head and would have fit four people in it, haha.
I wasnt a fan of the Upper West Side, catching the metro was a bit of a drag and it felt a bit removed. However paying $-- per night for a clean, warm bed in what was an extremely expensive city (for hostel-shared accom), who could complain?

The lobby is the best part of this hotel. The rooms are really shabby and nothing works. No hot water during the day and the staff are not at all friendly. They were too busy talking to each other than help guest. The location of this hotel is great but that the only good thing I can say about it. Have stayed in better hotels in New York and won't be going back here again. The room even smelt of must. The prices at the bar are very expensive even dearer than on Time Square and forget the lifts they are never working.

Just back from - nights at On the Avenue. We had a penthouse loft room - do book one of these. For not much more you get a great sized room and a balcony with fantastic views. (Superior rooms are v small). Great beds - very comfy and large. Fridge. Small but perfectly formed bathrooms. No room service - food on site - you are paying for just a room - but opening a linked restaurant soon. Free business centre. - internet - printing etc...
Brilliant, communual large open air terraces up high to enjoy views, drinks with friends etc...
In the Upper west side, its - mins walk to a subway station that is on a line that runs the entire length of Manhattan - great for Battery park and ferry trips. So quick and cheap - but quick is the main reason - cabs are fantastic and you should take many - but sometimes you don't want to spend -- mins in a cab to get to things.
Try Viand - blocks away for breakfast - great food. Also Fatty crabs round the corner for dinner - pricey ish (its an expensive city) - but great cocktails and food. Follow the advice here and try many dishes and share.
If you do - thing - go to Ellis Island - spectacular building - interesting history very well done - even children seemed engrossed
It feels like you are staying in a real NY residential area - but not quiet and boring. Easy to get to Central park walking etc...Having stayed many times in mid town near Times square etc... this feels less touristy - Give it a try

Stayed here with a friend over the easter long weekend. It is well situated in the DT area, which is close to all the museums and not far of a walk to magnificent mile and other tourisy locations. We got free upgrades to - bathroom suites and honestly, it was amazing !! I was very impressed (actually surprised) to see how many elevators this place has.... However, there still a bit of wait in the morning despite they probably have -- elevators in the hotel. Staffs are very friendly and helpful - provides lots of great tips and recommendations for the tourists. I would definitely stay at this hotel again if I visit the wind city again :)
Rooms very clean. Service was great. Wish they had movies to order on cable.

Perfect location just off the Boston Common and so close to great shopping. This is an old hotel that has been tastefully and efficiently updated with every amenity. My king-bedded room (---) was not spacious, but had everything I needed or wanted, including pristine linens, a comfortable mattress, a sumptuous bathroom and all the efficiencies that allowed me to work effectively. A great stay in a great hotel.

My flight with AA was cancelled and they send us to this hotel for the night. Its about -- minutes ride from Dallas-Forth Worth.
The hotel is very outdated, rugged carpets and curtains. Seemed like a cheap motel. very uncorfortable pillows. Big bathroom with a coffee machine hard to operate. Very noisy.
The hotel has a restaurant where we could pay with the AA vouchers, basic food.

I stayed here for a week while attending a conference. It's right on the Riverwalk and there is so much to see and do within walking distance that I didn't bother to rent a car. You can walk to the Alamo, the Rivercenter mall, and so many different restaurants, you won't run out of things to do.
The hotel is in a building that was previously the Alamo National Bank. The lobby and common areas are just beautiful - like out of an old movie! Be sure to walk downstairs and check out all the old photos of the bank and surrounding area. 
We got a suite with a balcony on the --th floor of the new tower and it was like having our own small apartment - including a microwave, mini fridge and small sink. Despite all the sights and activities nearby, our room was really quiet and it was easy to get a great night's sleep. There's also a full hot breakfast every morning, happy hour from -:-- - - with appetizers and snacks. My husband loved the - cocktails-beers he got each evening. 
Free, reliable wifi made it easy for me to keep up with my email and work while being away. I was also able to stream movies on Netflix using my iPad. 
Overall, I can't say enough good things about the Drury Plaza. Don't miss staying here when you're in San Antonio.

I have to confess I was a little nervous about staying here, having read some of the other reviews. I got what looked like a great deal on Travelzoo for a king sized room for $--- a night and grabbed it for my husband and I to spend a weekend in SD tagging it on to a business trip he was taking.
Our trip to SD was a heck of a lot longer and more frustrating than it should have been, due to a flight delay and the people at the car rental company who took an inordinately long time to get us in a car and on our way. As a result when we arrived at the hotel we were several hours later than planned, and tired, hungry (had pushed back our dinner reservation TWICE) and cranky. The valet guys were super nice, and when we got inside the guy at the front desk was also incredibly sympathetic and would have upgraded us to a better room had there been any available. When he was telling us about the wine hour hosted in the lobby every afternoon, we sighed and said we should have been there for that if it hadn't been for our delays. And so he went and fetched us a bottle from the back, handed it to us and hoped that our weekend would only get better from here on out.
That evening we had dinner at JSix restaurant (attached to the hotel). The food, service and wine were all very good and the staff incredibly attentive and friendly. 
We had to pay $-- a night parking fees - which is I suppose par for the course for any downtown hotel these days. Other than that, I had no complaints at all about our service, and considering the price I paid for the room, was all in all extremely impressed.
And the decor is beautiful. Sometimes the beauty doesn't quite work as functionally as one might like (e.g. the lovely looking sinks in which it's virtually impossible to wash!) The locationis fantastic (Gaslamp quarter) and SD is a clean, neat, friendly and accessible city.
We also ate dinner at Buon Appetito in Little Italy (took the city tramline to get there, incredibly easy). Brunch on Sunday at Hash House A Go Go in Hillcrest (don't eat for -- hours before you go, or SHARE), and dinner Sunday night at George's by the Cove Terrace in La Jolla. Would recommend all of them.

My family had an overnight layover in Seattle at the end of a holiday. We booked the Cedarbrook lodge because of the great reviews on trip advisor as well as the close proximity to the airport. We LOVED this place! The service was fabulous, the rooms were clean and comfortable, the bathrooms very big with an oversized tub, the snacks in the lounge were fantastic, and we all enjoyed the breakfast the next morning. The shuttle service is ---- with no long waits......they come as soon as you call. Although we didn't use the fitness facilities, they looked very good. My husband and sons ate in the restaurant and said it was very good.
We would definately stay here again. I think the value for the money is very good, and the airport is minutes away. The only thing that would make it better is a pool.

My daughter and I spent two nights-three days at this hotel, and I can't say enough great things about the staff and attention to detail! We were there to celebrate her birthday, and when we went to our room (which they upgraded in honor of the occasion!) there were birthday balloons and a box of mini-cupcakes waiting for us. We arrived at noon, and the staff ticketed our bags and held them until check-in time so we could go about our day. The front desk always spoke to us by name as we came and left, and asked if there was anything they could do to make our stay more comfortable. One night, I called down for an extra blanket, and two minutes later, we had not only a blanket, but two extra pillows as well. The complimentary breakfast was very good and replenished often. It was very crowded, but the staff did all they could to help us find a seat or carry our food to our room. The only complaint I had was the elevator wait, but I feel certain that this is the norm in high-rise hotels all over the city. I would absolutely stay here again and recommend this property to anyone staying near Times Square. It was within walking distance of most of the things we wanted to see, and very close to the hop-on, hop-off bus stop. A special thank you to Alex, who was especially attentive!

I checked in last week and was put into the south tower. The tower will prove a lot to do with this review. I was walked through a decent lobby and escorted to my room. We stayed here to attend a few Mariner games and, while it wasn't the closest hotel to the stadium, it was wonderfully quiet and comfortable. I slept like a rock since the room was well insulated and I really didn't hear much. My only (very small) compliant is that I could here the toilet flushing in the other room, but it didn't wake me so I was fine with it. Another bonus is the Dhalia Lounge and Bakery are right across the street. They do a wonderful brunch or you could grab one of their spectacular pastries at the bakery. I would definitely stay here again and highly recommend it to others.

On our reservations it clearly stated that we were honeymooners, but when we arrived we were given what must be their worst room - at the ground floor at the back with a view of the parking lot and very noisy due to cars passing by all the time. The room itself was claustrophobic and really ugly. The furniture, the bathroom and general outlook were just ugly. We then asked for another room, and they gave us a room on the -th floor that was supposed to be better, but it looked exactly the same except that this was a smoking room where the corridor leading to it and the room itself stunk of cigarettes so much that we could not sleep there even with the window open and with the cooling system on. We could hear the guy next door coughing the smokers cough throughout the night. At least the outer noise level there was lower since it was higher up.
They also tried to charge us for the parking --.-- USD per night whilst we then just parked our car across the road in the parking area there for -- USD per night!

After reading all the positive reviews on the Chancellor we decided to try it. We signed up for the family suite package as we were traveling with a child. Our one main criticism that actually made us leave was that there were no appropriate channels on the tv for kids, no vcr and no way to hook one up. I realize other people may not care about this but after a busy day of sightseeing, we like to relax and watch TV and we couldn't. I was surprised that there was no Disney channel or Nick or Cartoon network or any child friendly channel when they called it a family suite. It was also a bit too noisy for us as there was a street performer just under our window. We also had requested a refrigerator which was confirmed at least twice but when we got there we never got it. We moved to the Hyatt Embarcadero which all around was a better fit for us.

I stayed here for a bachelorette party weekend. We had great adjoining rooms. The front desk staff was super helpful and the rooms were beautiful. The Langham is a lovely old Boston hotel. Parking was actually really convenient and cheap -- $-- in the garage a half block away (that is dirt cheap for Boston!).
The beds were comfortable and the room was clean. My only complaint is the location. Being in the Financial District, it was tough to wake up on Sunday morning and not be able to get a quick cup of coffee without paying a fortune. In Boston, it's tough to go a block without somewhere for coffee, but the nearest place other than the pricey hotel restaurant was five blocks away, according to the bellman. That's the only downside to this place. I'm guessing this hotel is fabulous if you're in town for business travel. Overall, though, good experience.

The Casablanca is a peaceful haven away from the hustle and bustle of Times Square (Brits - think Oxford Street x -).
It is small with friendly staff and none of the excesses of the large Manhatten hotels. 
The rooms are bit on the small side but the beds were extremely comfortable, the shower worked, the continental style buffet and other complimentary offerings during the evening were very good.
Couldn't fault it - would definitely return if in New York.

I drove to the hospital before checking in and Boston traffic is tough so I am avoiding that with the shuttle and the train.
Breakfast is decent and loved the waffles.
WiFi worked great, I am using it right now in fact.
The biggest negative is trying to find the hotel. If you do not have a GPS good luck.
Some complained of cleanliness issues but there is no problem here for me but I did not get under the bed or search for mice poops. I might after reading one review.
The rate is the best in Boston. You can find upscale hotels but be prepared to drop another hundred bucks a night at least. 
If things go down hill I will revise my comments but soon I will be off to make my own waffles.

This Hotel was exactly what I expected. It is very old and certain areas could do with a bit of refurbishment but I suppose that all adds to the character. The room was very spacious by New York standards and very clean although the decor leaves a lot to be desired. 
The location is great, we could see the empire state building from our room and everything we wanted was in walking distance or a short taxi ride. 
On the whole a reasonably priced hotel with clean and spacious rooms which is all you need when you're staying in New York as you don't really spend much time there.

I would have given it - stars for cleanliness, as it appeared spotless, but one night I saw a roach in the bathroom. Eeek! Maybe that's normal for hot climates, but not for a northern city girl. It's hard to find anything to complain about at the Kitano but very little to get excited about either. It's location is great, its rates reasonable and the rooms are a decent size, but the Kitano offers neither the charm and unique touches of a boutique nor the facilities of a larger 'brand name' hotel. We stayed - nights in late May-early June. The location is primo. The property is just a little bit away from the most busy part of the Riverwalk, but you walk only five minutes along the water to reach the heart of it. Perfect for getting away from the crowds and enjoying the sculpted, landscaped pathways.
Because they had availability, we were upgraded upon check-in to a riverfront room, though from the -th floor the view was more onto the top of a parking deck across the water (the river is very narrow). Check-in was pleasant, and the lobby has inviting places to sit inside and out and enjoy the afternoon refreshments. A pleasant pool (modestly sized) is on the rooftop of part of the building.
There is an attractive restaurant on the Riverwalk itself, though we did not partake. There is also a bakery counter, an exercise room, a large bar, and hotel-wide wireless internet.
Because this is a Westin, of course the beds and showers are """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""heavenly"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (registered trademark!). The decor in the room is contemporary but bland.
But because this is a Westin, I would have hoped for better, more organized housekeeping. We returned to our room to find bottles of bathroom cleaner on the counter. No replacement toilet paper. The neighbors' room service breakfast leftovers in the hall until late bedtime. And the carpet in our room had various big, black stains.
So I'd say that while we enjoyed the hotel, for this price I will consider shopping around among other properties when we return to San Antonio.
We went to a Mariners game, and the hotel is an easy walk, which takes out the parking worries around Safeco field. It is also close to Pike Place market and downtown shops.

Stayed at the Town and Country for -- days last month, slected the hotel based on location. Did not want to have a car so here we could ride the trolley or the Old Town trolley. To go to Old Town the bellman dropped us off twice. Terry S. upgraded us to a pool room, gave us tips on where to go in la Jolla and places to go shopping, she was like our own tour guide.
We love San Diego and will be back

Our family usually spends a night in Denver around the holiday season, and this is our first choice of hotel. It's in a great location on the --th Street Mall, located right by the Light Rail Station. The free --th Street Mall bus can get you up and down --th Street as you like, or you can walk to take in more of the atmosphere. The food at the onsite Rialto Cafe is good also. One parking tip: If you don't want to pay the hotel parking fee (approx $--?), there is an in-door parking garage that charges ~$-- near California and --th St or so, just a ---- minute walk away. My girlfriend and I stayed in room --- for - nights this past weekend. We chose this hotel based on A) price and B) the reviews from this very site - which I must say, are too generous! See below for more details on WHY it doesn't deserve great reviews: 
Pros:
-Great location! The hotel is located in a pretty convenient spot for those that are traveling with vehicles. It is a ~-- minute drive to all of the monuments and is also a ---- minute walk to a TON of nice restaurants and bars. We didn't utilize public transport because we had a car but I believe there is a bus stop right on the corner near the hotel.
-Very cheap. Compared to the other hotels that are in the area this one (coming in around $----night for Friday and Saturday ) was very reasonable.
-Staff was nice. The staff mostly consisted of sub--- year olds that were very friendly. 
-A-C worked well
Cons:
-The building is very old and has seen better days. It feels like staying in your Grandmothers --- year old house - it has that musty smell everywhere. 
-The room was tiny. I've stayed in European hotels and it even puts those to shame. The whole room is just a bed with a foot on either side - no extra space.
-The room was not cleaned well. Stains here and there, dirt and crumbs, giant hair ball growing out of the sink, shower had that brown scummy stuff everywhere you stepped and the shower curtain was covered in mold.
-They don't have enough towels for the hotel. They give you - towels and you have to make due until the next morning. I actually had to delay leaving the hotel for over an hour because they didnt have any clean towels. When they finally did send one up - it was damp and smelled musty.
-Walls are thin
-No coffee in the room, no ice bucket in the room, no pen or paper in the room.
-Wireless internet did not work in room and barely worked in lobby.
-They use physical keys instead of key cards - which would be fine, but they apparently charge you $-- for losing your key - which is silly.
-You have to be buzzed into the hotel by the front desk every time you enter. This wasn't a problem for us but I imagine if you were a smoker this would be annoying.
I could go on but I think this will give you a good picture of the place. Even with all of the negative things I have to say about this hotel - for ~$---night and the location it isn't a bad deal if you plan on spending most of your time outside of the room. I definitely do NOT recommend this hotel to anyone used to - star and up hotels - it doesn't make the cut.

It's OK, but the rooms are incredibly dark. Also maintenance wasn't great. For whatever reason, they put very dim lights in the lamp. Thus, the bedside lamp provided insufficient light to see my watch. The shower leaked and the switch on the bedside lamp fell off. It's convenient to Grand Central Terminal though and the rooms are quite large. This is yet another hotel that pipes analog signals into digital TV's. This results in a distorted, grainy picture.

I was on the -th floor, the top floor, and though I don't suffer from vertigo, I didn't feel the most comfortable on those balconies. Could be dangerous if you stagger.
Rooms were fine, good internet connection and good air-con. Overall pretty happy with the choice of hotel and wouldn't feel unhappy about staying here again.

We stayed here because of the price and were a little weary of what it would be like. I could not have been happier. It was very clean and any thing we needed they gave. Great job. The front desk clerk Robert I think his name was great and more than helpful. I will stay again if I am in San Antonio any time soon.

I traveled to the Westin in Los Angeles for a small weekend getaway with my significant other. The hotel was nice - It felt very loungy, and welcoming. It had a very modern and updated feel to it.
The check-in was very fast, and the service was wonderful.
The view could have been a little better, but given the location and its proximity to the LAX airport, it wasn't too bad.
The bar in the lobby area is great. They serve wonderful appetizer food, desserts, and drinks. Although a little pricey, I wouldnt say it is too bad. 
The only negative aspect I would have to say would be parking, and wireless internet.
Parking is quite expensive, at around $-- a day for self-park in their structure. And wireless internet was around $---- a day. However if it is your first time staying with the Westin, you get complimentary internet for your stay. (You have to pay for it, and then it is credited to your room at check-out).
The Westin was a wonderful hotel that offered exactly what I was looking for. Its design was great, service excellent, and location superb.

I was on a business trip and decided to stay at the JW Marriott. Immediately, while I was checking in, the staff was quite friendly and helpful. I had a king size bed type of room. It was very clean and quiet. The location of the hotel is amazing. It is a very central location to many businesses as well as sites. In addition, it is walking distance to the metro. I loved the fitness center and it provided a ton of different options. The center is quite large and I did not have to wait for any machines. I think the customer service was awesome and well worth staying at the JW Marriott.

This hotel should be condemned. paint and plaster peeling off walls and ceilings, threadbare sheets, views over;looking a derilict building, no public transport, breakfast ran out daily by -.--am not even any bread and no restaurants nearby. Hotel provided shuttle into Beal Street and airport but charged. One room was sealed by police for being used as illegal drug lab! Add not too pleasant staff. It was the worst place we have even stayed in anywhere in the World!

After having read the reviews of the Iroquois I decided to give it a try. The room was comfortable, the linens top-of-the line and the afternoon iced-tea a lovely extra touch. But it was the service of the staff that made this stay exceptional. I will definitely visit again.

We enjoyed our stay at the Omni. The staff was very nice. Room service was very good.
The only problem with the location is that the few restaurants near by do not stay open late and some are not open on the weekend.
We were able to walk to all of the local attractions and when we got back the room it was always clean and the towels and toiletries were stocked daily.

This is a fine looking hotel, convenient to The Henry Ford Museum and Greenfield Village in Dearborn, MI. It is also convenient to Fairlane Shopping Center, the Henry Ford Fairlane estate, and Ford Motor Company World headquarters. The hallways inside feature pictures from automotive history and are quite nice.
The problems that I see with this hotel are all staff-related; at times this hotel doesn't really appear to be open for business. Here are some examples from my last business trip there in late December:
-) Arriving at -PM in the evening, there was no one at all at the front desk. By the time someone decided to check the front desk about -- minutes later there were two of us waiting to check-in.
-) Morning breakfast in the Grille--, the hotel's restaurant, can be a hit for miss affair. The restaurant will be open, but there won't be anyone to receive customers or even be present in the dining area. This has happened to me on this business trip - I walked around the restaurant for - minutes without meeting anyone or seeing any sign of the usual breakfast buffet at - am. I finally left and found a different restaurant to breakfast in. I have had this happen to me at this hotel twice before.
In summary, I feel that the management of this hotel needs to emphasize with their staff the importance of be availble for the guest at any time. I base this opinion on the fact that I stay in other Doubletree hotels regularly and have always enjoyed the high level of personal service in those hotels that seems to be sadly lacking in this one.

This hotel has everything you need...starbucks, good food, a late night sports bar, and clean rooms. I was disappointed by the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cold tub"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" outside. Several guests had complained about the hot tub not being warm enough and nothing was done about it. I waited, to no avail. All I wanted was a hot tub as I was running the marathon the next day.........:( The other complaint: you can't schedule a late check out until the day of after - a.m. Really? What kind of policy is that? I'm going to be running for - hours with -- thousand people and might not get back in time to shower and check out by --. I wish they had been more understanding....other hotels have been more accommodating when there are races in town (which bring in people from all over who pay lots of money to stay at the hotels...).... Sigh! REally, I just want my hot tub to be above -- degrees!!!!

My five-night stay at the French Quarters was simply awesome. My room was comfortable, very clean, with a street view, and I was really surprised it wasn't that noisy, as I was expecting, due the location - a great location, by the way. Everyone working there was friendly and helpful. Breakfast was excellent too. Everything worked perfectly, and I think It was worth every cent. I will certainly be back!

Just returned from a - day trip to New York and we stayed in the Waldorf Towers . This is the upper floors of the Astoria, our room was a reasonable size for a city hotel with a very smart and clean bathroom with bath and shower cubical. The unstocked fridge was a bit grubby & there was no tea or coffee making facilities which we did miss as it's nice to make a coffee when you first wake up. Access to the astoria lounge was included with this room, it was nice to have a complementary coffee or cold drink but it closed at -pm so after a days sightseeing you were too late to use the lounge. Food in the restaurants was top class but as expected very expensive. Over all a very nice experience and money well spent.

Do you like old style, close to so many things........ this is the place to go.
The breakfast is lovely. The wine and cheese in the afternoon is fantastic. You have a chance to mingle with other guests and find out where they have been, exchange ideas, find out about the best places in Town.
There are some wonderful restaurants within walking distance, and you are just a block from the cable car.

My husband and I stayed at the Intercontinental for one evening for our -- year anniversary. Upon check-in we received the most wonderful service from Emmanuel. There was an error with our Hotels.com reservation and our reservation could not be located at first. In the meantime Emmanuel booked us a new reservation at the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""walk-in"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" rate which was a great savings. He then spent about -- minutes with us calling Hotels.com and helping us cancel our prior reservation and insuring that we got our refund. He was pleasant and smiling at all times, and never got frustrated. He also upgraded us to a room with a spectacular view. We mentioned during check-in that it was our anniversary and when we arriving back in our room after dinner there was champagne and chocolate strawberries waiting. It was such a lovely touch. The room was clean and gorgeous and the bathroom very luxurious, but this kind of service really has to be commended. Thank you Emmanuel for all of your help and for making our anniversary so memorable.

My Wife and I travelled from Edinburgh, Scotland to NYC for - days Birthday celebrations and to see the George Michael Concert at the Garden and did a lot of research on where to stay (including through Tripadvisor). We looked at St Regis, Plaza, Trump, Gansevoort, Manderin etc but liked the look and size and reviews of the Peninsula.
We were not disappointed. In fact had found a heavenly oasis.
The Hotel exudes a quiet understated sophistication and calm. Staff are there for you if you need them and very attentive, but never intrusive and always extremely polite and friendly.
The room was beautiful. High ceilings and elegant layout, with lovely equipped bathroom and massive comfortable bed. Best of all the Hotel and Room were impeccably clean (I'm bit Howard Hughes about that stuff)
A trip to the rooftop bar was great, although very busy, We knew that the Spa was closed for refurbishment, but this didn't spoil the enjoyment for us and we will have that to look forward to next time we go - we most certainly will be returning.

We spent three days at the Benjamin and could not have been more pleased. Our room on the --th floor was quiet, well-appointed and comfortable. The linens were fabulous and the choice of pillows was a particularly nice touch. The hotel is convenient to public transportation and a short walk from most of the places we wanted to go. The bathroom was a tad small but the bathrobes were wonderful. The staff was accommodating and pleasant. We had a great stay!

I've stayed at many Seattle hotels, and this one is absolutely the best...great staff, unbeatable central location, perfect ambiance. The lounge (Oliver's) is deliciously relaxing whether I'm there with friends or my husband. And you won't find nicer, more efficient people at any hotel; the staff really makes this hotel the outstanding place it is. Try it; you'll love it.

I've stayed at several Joie de Vivre properties and typically find them to be chic with comfortable beds and moderately priced. Hotel Erwin in Venice has a nice location and a nice rooftop deck with great views of Venice Beach. The hallways and feeling of the hotel are modern and swanky, but the rooms definitely leave something to be desired. The decor in the rooms is tired with old worn furniture. Bathrooms are nice, but overall there are better options for similarly priced hotels. If you're just looking for somewhere to lay your head this may be a good option, but it's not a great hotel for a destination vacation.

Had to pay for suite since Chicago was jammed but really nice room and decent hotel. Suite was well decorated with very well designed bathroom. Fitness center (temporarily relo'ed to a ballroom) was well equipped. Service was great and Sheraton Link to print a doc at last minute was very helPful. Not typically a Sheraton fan (SPG Platinum. Prefer Westin) but would revisit this one

The location was good for staying out of touristy Times Square area, but with easy access to the square, and other sites via a quick subway ride or a leisurely stroll down Broadway. The staff was very friendly and professional, from the doormen to the housekeeping staff. The rooms were modern and quiet. I have stayed in New York many times and I could always hear street noise, but even though I was on the fifth floor the only street noise I heard was at -:-- a.m. when a garbage truck pulled up. The bed was ultra comfortable with a variety of pillow choices. I had a few issues with the room, and they are minor. No channel information was available for the television, and the TV, even though it was large and placed on the wall, had substandard picture quality. That could be because at home I'm used to high definition. I also had to pay almost $-- a day for wireless in my room. I should point out wireless is available in the lobby where there was comfortable seating, but not much privacy. I also missed having two bed lamps. The alarm clock was on the nightstand without the lamp, so I had to creep across the bed in the dark after turning off the light on the opposite side. The switch on the wall by the alarm clock didn't operate anything, and I have a feeling that it was supposed to operate an overhead light. Anyone staying there should note a second set of elevators off the right side of the lobby. The elevators to the left of the lobby are smaller than those elevators on the opposite side of the lobby, and they run slowly. Two terrific guest balcony areas offer private seating and a place to enjoy city views, although not spectacular views. I would stay here again as the room was modern, clean and quiet. This is a good value for New York.

I read the mixed reviews, but we found the hotel convenient and the room fine with comfortable beds--very convenient to LAX. Like others, got it on a Priceline very reasonable bid. Entrance area does need updating, but the room was decent--we just wanted to get to sleep after our plane arrived after -- PM.

Literally five minutes from airport. The taxi shuttle was quick and convenient. Laurene, the manager, was very friendly and helpful. Room was very nice. Looking forward to staying there again on all my trips to San Jose.
We were there for DARS-BET Annual Training Session. Everything was very good, except the mattress - it was old and compacted - too hard - otherwise, all was good.

We just moved to the San Antonio area and needed a place to stay for a couple of weeks before we closed on our new house. We stayed at the La Quinta in the Dominion. Very nice area of town, the hotel was clean, the pool was refreshing. They had a work-out room and a laundry room which was so convient. My kids loved the Texas shaped waffles in the morning, there was a really good continental breakfast very day. The housekeepers did an excellent job everyday. The best part, was Karen, she always had a smile on her face, had great ideas of where to go, and was very helpful. I'd defiently go back. Plus, it's close enough to get to all the fun areas of San Antonio, without being in the hussle and bussle of the city.

- Good in and out business travel hotel
- Ok gym and indoor outdoor pool
- Starbucks on site
- Across from mall. Food places like PF Chang and Ruby Tuesday across. 
- Free valet parking but .....
- The valet service dinged my car at back. Only found out about it after I left hotel and saw my car at a gas stop

This hotel was out of this world, my wife and I spent our honeymoon here for - nights. when we arrived we were informed of an upgrade to a corner suite on the --th floor. WHAT A VIEW!!!! the staff were very courteous and helpful when asked anything. The room was spotless and very well appointed. Wouldn't hesitate to recommend to anyone.

Stayed there for - nights, location was great and super close to cable cars-transit and shopping nearby. Check in was easy, they even had a parking in the front just to park the car temporarily and unload. Room was decent, with only the bathrooms smaller than expected, but it is an older hotel. When we first arrived in the room, there was a musty smell but after we got the fan going it was fine. Did not get a chance to try their pillow menu, but the choices were interesting. We were on one of the higher floors facing the back of the hotel, so luckily we didn't hear too much noice as other reviewers had mentioned. Had breakfast mainly next door at Sears Restaurant- really reasonable and good food. Overall for the great location and price would definitely go back again!

We enjoyed our stay at the Best Western Tuscan Inn. The location is perfect for a day or two at Fisherman's Wharf. Within walking distance of all of the attractions. Room was very clean and bathrooms were nice. The price was also reasonable. The only thing missing was a workout area.

Recently, I stayed for - nights at the Holiday Inn Express Washington DC-Northeast. It was a good stay--the room was spacious and clean and the morning breakfast buffet has a decent selection of hot and cold items.
I found the hotel staff particularly friendly and helpful. I needed directions and meal recommendations, and helped with both. 
This hotel is not right in the middle of town, but does run a regular shuttle service to Union Station. I didn't take advantage of the shuttle, but observed it running on a regular morning and evening schedule.
I particularly appreciated how clean the hotel was. Both my room and the common areas (hallways, lobby, breakfast area, fitness center) were spotless and smelled nice.
I definitely will stay here again if I am in the area for work.

I have just returned from a fanatastic - night stay in the astor hotel with my friend for a girlie weekend.
Rooms were a good size,we had room ---, with everything you need eg a comfortable bed and good shower.There was a complimentary coffee machine and internet access which we found useful for booking our empire state building tickets.
Reception staff helpful and so were the door men. The hotel is about - blocks from Broadway overlooking central park so about a -- minute walk from restaurants, bars and shops.Mama mexican can be highly recommended as amazing food.The Tavern bar was really nice and full of lovely people and cheap!! broadway bagels for breakfasts again excellent!
Would definatly stay at this hotel again!

I stayed at this place for almost - weeks while on a business trip. It is located right in between the Intercon and Sheraton, within a walking distance to the Galleria. Location was excellent and had geat restaurents and shopping places nearby. I'd say good value for this price (I paid $ -- + taxes); though I'd go to one of the hotels nearby spending a few more dollars to have the breakfast included. The only dampener in the room was the a-c which was very noisy.. had to turn it off a few times to get some sleep.

For convenience we stayed here one night prior to a US-Canada tour as the first night of the tour was here also. This hotel is pretty old and the rooms at the front where we were look it. There was a funny smell in the hallway and our room was very musty. The air conditioning worked fine but is very noisy. You could use it to block out the traffic sounds I guess. All in all the part we stayed in was not nice at all and maybe these are rooms assigned to tour groups although that is no excuse. 
I went to their fitness centre and found that there is a rear part to the hotel that looks much more inviting if better carpet and furnishings are anything to go by.
The location is ok. A short walk to the river and less than -- minutes to Times Square. There are plenty of deli's and restaurants close by but overall when we left the Skyline I was pleased to be leaving.

We were in town for the MAKEr Faire at the city fairgrounds. It was about a -- minute drive up the highway, but nothing unmanageable.
We found the hotel according to Tripadvisor, and they were a good deal. Fair price, clean room, nice breakfast. Wish it had a pool, but oh well.
Only minor complaint is that it's adjacent to the freeway, and in a bit of a lower-side of town, so we heard the kids cruising by with their """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""thumpa thumpa"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" cars.
Had no problems with front-desk staff; on the contrary, we had a good repore with them. Not sure what troubles other reviewers had, but we did just fine.
We booked the Asian suite (I think - the one with the swinging chair). Surprisingly enough, the swing actually is quite relaxing to sit on!

this hotel is on the Mag mile and close to the redline L train that can get you all over the city; the room was small but so was the price I paid to right on the Mag mile ; the beds were comfy and room super clean; close to Hancock tower, great resturants, and shopping; I love staying at this hotel and stay there alot!

Parking garage was a pain in the butt. Very narrow, but right underneath-beside hotel. Rooms were ok in size and decor. Liked the club floor for breakfast. When checking in, ask questions because front desk doesn't volunteer any information. Last day, key didn't work, and it was only -:-- am.

We recently stayed at this hotel August ---- for - nights. It was okay. I asked for a non-smoking room, but, was placed in a smoking room - which luckily did not smell of smoke. The room was dark and small. The room with the pull out couch did not have a remote. One was found and placed in the room in a timely manner. When the pull out couch was pulled out, there was no space to move around in that room. The bathroom was clean. One of the sheets was torn. Parking was adequate. Limited breakfast buffet.

Traveled to NYC for a family vacation and this """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""suite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel made Manhattan quite accessible. Walked to most of the must-do touristy places but returned to this oasis where terrific restaurants were plentiful. Staff helpful, rooms spacious and beds quite comfy. Highly recommend......

I stayed at this La Quinta a few years ago and had a great experience and was looking forward to a return visit. Unfortunately, the property has gone downhill a bit in the past few years. The mattresses we got were very worn and hard to sleep on. The breakfast was ok. The property is very close to good shopping and restaurants, but so are many others. This is a fine place to stay, but we will try someplace different next time.

The Orchard Garden Hotel is a beautiful hotel set in one of the most convenient San Francisco locations. I was able to walk everywhere; the the Ferry Building on the Embarcadero, the BART, Union Square, the Mission, and even Fisherman's Wharf and the Marina. Comfortable guestrooms. Loved the fact that all lights, air, etc. is powered off when I leave the room. So """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""green."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Had a nice view of outside from my room. Staff was very helpful and friendly. Extremely pleasant experience. I would stay here again for sure. I would like to see more vegan items on their menu, but their restaurant does include almost all local and organic items, so that is wonderful!

A very comfortable stay. Close to everything you want to see and do. Helpful and friendly staff. Good food. HVAC units work great and the beds are great. Very clean and spacious. Parking is a little bit high but worth it.

Stayed at the Milford Plaza for - nights and probably best described as adequate. A great location so as a first time visitor to NY was what we required. A large hotel so inevitably very busy. The room was quite small but clean. Would maybe try a different hotel next time

The Inn on Ferry Street is a truly wonderful establishment. The historic group of homes have been masterfully restored and decorated, the staff is courteous, and the amenities are a-plenty. There are so many nice details, it's hard to even remember them all: great breakfast, complete with fresh fruit, make-for-yourself waffles, Starbucks coffee and Tazo tea; very comfortable beds and linens; a music selection in each room; and lots of extra local-info reading, magazines, and books. The grounds are well landscaped, and the parking was clean and well lit at night. I’m sure work is continuing, but it would be nice if the back alley behind the parking lot was better masked by trees and vines. 
We stayed in the John R carriage house, which is simply designed in the Arts and Crafts style, and our room was quiet and comfortable. The night security fella made a not-so-tasteful comment about needing sunglasses to look at the bed covering in our particular room, but we thought the multi-colored velvet Pottery Barn comforter was wonderful. Next time I'll try to see if we can get the other carriage house, which looks incredibly charming! I especially like how the individual homes are decorated slightly differently, from Victorian to Arts and Crafts, depending on the architecture of the house—but all keeping with style of the era in which they were built. 
For those not familiar with the area, this Midtown, Cultural Center of Detroit is experiencing a renaissance. This block of beautiful homes that is the Inn on Ferry is located just down the street from some of the most impressive mansions around. You must explore the area! (There are still a good number of vacant lots and dilapidated homes spotting the area as well, and I wouldn’t recommend walking too far north or east from this particular street late at night.) The restoration work and new projects transforming the area are exciting and inspiring. 
Right now (summer ----) there is much construction in the immediate vicinity, but overall the Inn is located in a terrific area--the cultural center of Detroit—and will be especially appreciated by lovers of culture and history! Within walking distance are the Detroit Institute of Arts, The Detroit Science Center, the Museum of African American History, Detroit Historical Museum, and the main branch of the Detroit Public Library. There are also a good number of nearby restaurants, bars, and activities for families. The Hard Rock Café and Comerica Park are also within a longer walk or short drive. 
This place comes very highly recommended!

My husband and I stayed at The Michelangelo for - nights. We came to NYC for the Westminster Dog Show. The hotel was about a mile from Madison Square Garden, a short cab ride averaging about $- one way. The bellman will hail a cab for you in front of the hotel...very easy. We didn't eat at the hotel but did try Ruth's Chris just a few steps down the street and it was very good.
The hotel is clean, very quiet, and comfortable. The location is wonderful. Too cold to walk in February for us, but will definitely come back in the summer and do out sightseeing by foot.
We didn't partake of the morning coffee that everyone seems to be complaining about. Honestly I don't understand that since there's a Starbucks virtually every few feet you walk on the block. 
Every hotel employee we communicated with was very professional and helpful. I think this is the place for us when we visit NYC!

I got to the hotel a little after --pm, the hotel had left out my reservation paperwork and room keys on the counter in the lobby(yes the front door was locked, but the others in the lobby had no problem letting people in through the locked door). I got to my room(non smoking) that smelled like smoke. The people above me were very loud and you can hear doors all the way down the hallway being slammed shut! The room was not what I would consider clean at all and the quality of bedding is very poor. 
There is silverware, but only one spoon total! Plus it was not clean, along with all of the other silverware. I have stayed here one other time and had the same problems which were not really taken care of. 
The police drive through the parking lot a couple times per night. This should make me feel safe, but it is religously not at random.... The outside of the hotel is deceiving, it does not look too bad until you get inside.

This was our first stay at a Le Meridien. It felt like a true boutique hotel experience and I am looking forward to experiencing other Le Meridien properties. I would return to this hotel if I find myself needing to stay in Philadelphia again.
HIGHLIGHTS:
- Architectural detail and design that was integrated across the public spaces and the guest rooms.
- Comfortable bed with luxurious linens on par with the Luxury Collection properties.
- SPG Platinum upgrade from the standard room booked to a suite with separate living room and bedroom.
- Central location.
- Intimate feel in the lobby without much separation between the bar, check-in, and restaurant.
- Front desk and restaurant staff were first-rate. Every request was met without hesitation (including SPG Platinum -pm checkout).
GOOD TO KNOW:
- The valet area gets a big chaotic since you must simply pull over on the street. There's not always a valet immediately present. Car retrieval takes ----- min on average, but guest expectations are set accordingly.
- Parking is $--- night.
- There are no bath tubs in the standard suites.
- The bedroom area is separated from the living area by a partial wall, but there is no door.
- The windows do not open.

The W San Diego was nice enough but certainly not a four-star hotel. The overall problem was the desperate trendiness of the establishment. The hotel is relatively new, yet the decor is already looking dated. Though my room was clean, the lucite dresser-desk was chipped in places, and the custom shower curtain hanging mechanism (or whatever) was also worn. Some of the staff was helpful, whereas others couldn't be bothered, as when I tried to figure out how to connect to the wireless Internet in the lobby. Also, I understand exorbitant prices for cute in-room tchotchkes like teddy bears, candy and hats, but charging for an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""intimacy kit,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which included condoms, seems ridiculously irresponsible. And the W certainly could afford to offer free Internet in its rooms. I've stayed in Best Westerns that offer that amenity free of charge. Come on. The worst part of the stay, for me, was the hotel's clientele, a mixture of Eurotrash, buisinessmen, and Americans with a little extra money. Ew. If you're going to San Diego and you have money to spend on a hotel room, stay somewhere closer to the harbor or water in a place far less eager to be fashionable.

My sister and I visited this hotel on our girls trip to NYC. I was a little unsure because it was not one of the usual hotel chains I use. What a wonderful surprise. The hotel is well situated close to Grand Central Station and many NYC attractions. The rooms are much larger than other NYC hotel rooms. The service is wonderful and the staff are so nice and helpful. Take a few minutes to talk to Shane who works at the front desk in the afternoon and evenings or Maritza who works at the breakfast cafe in the mornings. Both were extremely nice and helpful to those of us who are obviously not """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""New Yorkers"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" 
I enjoyed this small boutique hotel and will be back again the next time I am in NYC. Our room was very spacious and the housekeeping staff was excellent. It is worth trying something new to stay here while visiting NYC.

I was not expecting much but was greatly surprised upon arriving at the Westin Columbus. The lobby is elegant and historically huge. The front desk is helpful and the rooms are all updated, very tasteful and spotless. Of course the Heavenly bed never disappoints. We went to the theater that was only a few walking blocks away and then had drinks afterwards in the bar. The hotel just has a classy feel and a friendly staff. I would highly recommend this property even if it is for a weekend to see and experience Ohio's Capitol city. Oh and one more thing - we did not know - but you could bring your pet - No EXTRA CHARGE. The outside front door has a water bowl and food bowl to let visitors know it is pet friendly. This by no means, takes away from the elegance and grandness of this historic property.

I've booked this hotel because of a price offer, so the value for me was good. 
Overall: acceptable 
The hotel staff were really helpful and friendly and I think they are doing an excellent job creating a home-like atmosphere in the hotel. I also liked the eco-friendly touches like filtered water, recycled paper cups and organic food in the Saha restaurant. 
The lobby is kind of nice and cozy but the rooms are really tired. They are a bit smelly, with old wallpaper and floor carpets, old TV and even holes in the linen. I was lucky I had decent looking bathroom and I also liked the nice organic toileteries. 
I would greatly welcome the idea of renovating this hotel, the building is great and I would even preserve some furniture but definitely change the wallpaper and carpets and do something about the noise insulation (I could hear my neighbours very well).
If you are going to stay in the hotel be also prepared to walk a lot and wait a lot for the public transport to explore the city or get to your destination in the city centre.

The stay would have been better if -) the ONE elevator would have been in working order. -) The TV in the frontroom would have worked (an excellent maintence man had to come late at night to fix it...he was great) -) the overhead lights in the vanity area would have worked. We went down to San Diego for a weekend getaway...we wanted to have some feedback from the hotel workers behind the desk...but they either were not knowledgable enough with how to direct to different places or were not interested in helping us.

Our first visit to Boston, rooms small clean and cosy. Staff friendly and helpful no problems at all. Easy walking to all the sights and not far from the Trolley tour stop. All in all for a few days stop over, could'nt be better.
Regards Greg & Margaret

Stay away from this falsely claiming --Star Jewel of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The Loop"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" area!
It's --Star at best!!!
The rooms are tiny, the beds even smaller, so that a -'--"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" person can't even keep the feet under the blanket. As soon as you enter the elevator you are being hit by a bad odor coming from some cheap chemical they must use to keep the place """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""clean"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". My room and the corridor leading to it on the fifth floor smelled even worse. The ceiling in my room had water stains and the vent in the bathroom looked like it was mold paradise!!
The TV had mostly snow storm picture quality on all channels except for the P-P-V channels. The bed only consisted of a duvet wrapped in a sheet to keep you warm at night, unless you went outside to search for an extra blanket in a special closet available to every guest. I only learnd about this option the next day after almost freezing to death my first night in --F degree wheather. Fortunately, the HVAC worked well, so I had to crank up the heat in the room instead. My room was not cleaned for - days in a row, which - I guess - can happen. What WAS bad about it, though, was that the night clerk tried to make me believe that all rooms usually only get cleaned after check-out. That topped just about everything I experienced during my stay! I have worked in hotels before myself, so I do understand what it takes to upset a guest and make him look for better options next time. In October ----, we visited New York City with a family of five. After doing a lot of internet searching, we ended up at the Hotel St James. Finally, there is a free transfer ferry called the Staten Island Ferry, which will give you a great view of Manhattan as well as get you close to the Statue of Liberty.
In conclusion, the Hotel St James is an outstandingly located, cheap and basic hotel that has all the important things just right.

I always check tripadvisor.com and other trusted sources for info before going to any destination, but I try to stay open-minded since the needs of each traveler are different. Still, I was interested to find several less-than-stellar reviews of the LA Westin Bonaventure. I knew the hotel had been around for a long time...my mother (who was in the travel business at the time) dragged me to its grand opening when I was still a kid in the '--'s. Some years later I even worked for a short while for a business that rented space from the Bonaventure (and had even spent the night in a --story suite we had rented for our own grand opening). Judging from many of the comments, you'd have thought the hotel had done little or nothing to update it. Well, I was so pleasantly surprised. I am a consummate business traveler, spending sometimes over --- days per year on the road, and I consider myself hard-to-please. But the hotel had everything I needed and more. My first concern was that the air conditioning would be ineffective in a hotel made of glass...how many times have I gone into a room with the curtains open and the air off only to BAKE for hours while the air tries to catch up??! Happily, the room I got cooled down in a matter of minutes. Secondly - the beds. Well, what could be better than the Westin chain's Heavenly beds? (I may ask Santa to bring me one this year!) Next I was concerned about noise. There were all sorts of comments about that. The only noise I noted was the rush of traffic on the freeways and surface streets, but being a veteran of stays in big cities around the world, I would characterize the noise as minor """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""white noise"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". It's voices and banging walls, etc., that disturbs me, and I had none of that. By the way, LA drivers, unlike those in New York and other eastern cities, do not drive with their horns on, so steet noise is far tamer to begin with. After that I considered the hotel amenities and facilities...you'd think to read the reviews that you have to hike somewere to eat or drink. Hello!?! I guess those people did not explore the several floors of sit-down & walk-up restaurants and snack places. There was plenty of variety right there in the hotel. I had arrived late, and the lobby bar was still buzzing with happy people, and the food looked great (if I hadn't been so tired I'd have joined them). I had a hot, delicious breakfast with a cappuccino at one of the little walk-ups at -:--am then next morning. The in-room amenities were great...the usual wonderful Westin stuff (nice quality soaps, shampoo, conditioner, lotion...and let's not forget the Starbucks coffee, real cream, and in-room coffee brewer). I really appreciated the generous bathroom countertops so I can spread my stuff out while getting ready...great bathroom lighting and a magnified mirror highly appreciated. My one and ONLY critique is that I had no place to plug in my ped's...it's not just Westin that needs improvement on that. In fact my room had only one exposed wall plug, and that was across the wall from the foot of the bed, where no furniture was present, so I had no place but the floor to put my phone, ipad, and computer. There was one surge protector on the floor between the bed and bedstand, but all the plugs were full! C'mon, Westin, get with the program.......! But, that notwithstanding, it was a wonderful stay and I WILL be back.

This type of decor, (contemporary), may not appeal to most but it was a refreshing change for us and what I believe to be very """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""New York style"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The beds are fantastic! Just a little bit of advice, it helps to have a separate bag to keep all your toiletries in as there is not much counter space in the very cool bathroom.

Stayed at the JW for Neocon in June. I had a regular room, which was lovely. The bathroom was generously sized with a large marble shower and double sink granite vanity. No tub, but I didn't miss it. The hotel underwent a total renovation recently, and the money shows. Definitely up there with the better hotels in Chicago. Not quite a Peninsula or Park Hyatt...but close! My colleague upgraded to a suite, and I tell you, that's where the rubber meets the road. The bathroom was as big as the bedroom, and it had a big Wow factor. There was a freestanding tub clad in marble mosaic tile, big marble shower, and a toilet in it's own room. The vanities were separate, so no leaning over your spouse to reach the toothpaste. But the big WOW factor was the mirrors. They were both large, with the lighting seamlessly integrated into the mirror in a clean band of white light. The best part - when you turn on the tv, the picture appears in the mirror facing the tub. Way cool.
I liked the fact that the hotel is next to an L stop, since I was way over the taxi cab drivers who floor it between stoplights for their own entertainment. One MAJOR drawback was the $-- a day charge for Wifi. Really??? These days, in my opinion that's like charging you extra for soap. All the major low and medium chains offer free Wifi, and for a high end hotel to charge for it is a major irritant to the business traveler. 
Other than that, a great stay.

This was our -st trip to San Diego, and we were not disappointed with the hotel. Except for an oops when we checked in (we were accidentally given a room that was already occupied) we had a great time. The rooms are very comfortable and the view did not disappoint. Easy walking distance across the street to the gaslamp quarter. The hotel itself is reasonably priced but parking is pricey, though probably about average for SD, we paid $---night for self parking.

We were in L.A. from Dallas for my wife's medical tests at Cedars-Sinai Hospital. We decided not to rent a car for the week, partly because of the $-- daily parking fee at the hotel and partly because we would not be doing any extracirricular activities. Due to construction in the lobby, the normal in and out of the hotel was somewhat inconvenient. Check-in was a makeshift lobby just off the garage. Then you walk down one flight of stairs to another """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lobby"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" where you catch the elevator to your floor. The staff was extremely helpful to us - each time my wife and I arrived or departed, they sent a driver with a golf cart to the lower lobby to bring us to the upper lobby. They also provided a wheelchair so my wife could more easily get from the elevator to our room.
Since we had opted not to rent a car, we needed a taxi to the hospital each day for three days. The hotel staff referred us to a limo service (Turbo Limos - Mr. Harry Kim)that took us back and forth for less than the cost of a taxi (confimed, as we did use a taxi once). Harry also drove us to the airport to go home for a lower price than we had paid another limo the day we arrived. I highly recommend the limo service. 
The location is good as far as being on a main artery. If you don't have your own transportation, it is not so hot for stuff nearby (i.e. restaurants). There is a nice supermarket across the street, though. No swimming pool, but there is a whirlpool and an indoor-outdoor gym with some nice cardio machines, a bench, and a full rack of dumbbells.

We stayed at the Red Roof Inn, July -----, ----. We used the trip advisor review to help pick the place. My wife and I with two -- year old kids stayed in a two double bed room. It's not big but very comfortable and very clean. The continental breakfast of bagels, donut's, juice and coffee was a great way to get going early in the morning. It is located one block from the Empire State building. When you walk out the front door look up, it's framed by the two buildings across the street. Macy's is two blocks away and is a must see even if you don't like to shop. A cab to Times Square was $-.--. It's a great deal for $--.-- a night, I booked through the Red Roof website and confirmed with the hotel, parking the car was $--.-- a night with the ticket validated by the hotel. Parking was just down the block. The bellman was very friendly and helped unload the car on the narrow street and even brought the luggage to the carpark to make it easier to load up when we checked out. We would definately stay there again!!!!!!

From the outside this hotel is very nice, but beware. The rooms not renovated and my bathroom was not cleaned correctly on several occasions. I would not recommend this hotel until they renovate. The hotel is probably fine if you are not a seasoned traveler but my group (who is) did care for the facility. I would not recommend until they make some changes.

Free parking and good location for the price. It's a -- minute walk to the Wharf and a few hills to travel. Good exercise so you can burn more calories for a nice dinner out. Irene our desk clerk was so sweet and helpful. We had a newly renovated room and a wonderful bed and slept well. Yes BRING EARPLUGS because the traffic is noisy at night but ear plugs work great. I was happy to save on lodging and spend the $ on shopping.....I would return again

We were unfortunate enough to be in San Diego staying at this hotel when the power out happened on -th September. This affected Southern California, North Mexico and Nevada. While this was obviously an unexpected event, the manager was nowhere to be found and my husband ended up lending the staff a torch. The place was in total confusion and the staff were no help at all.The airport closed and we asked about staying on at the hotel until we knew our night flight the following day was going ahead but you would have thought we'd asked the impossible. In the end we left.
Apart from that - the room we had was fine, old but clean enough with plenty of room. There is no real breakfast but the location is great. However as another reviewer has written there are plenty of these motels on this stretch of road.

We've stayed here over - times in the last decade. The experience has always been positive and consistent. We booked a room on the --th floor, where drinks and snacks are available throughout the day for free -- even Starbucks coffee. The hotel is located right over the Central Metro Station which is unbelievably convenient in Washington DC. Our room was quiet, and housekeeping is above average, but not perfect (my little guys found some trash under the furniture -- I don't know what they were doing under there to begin with.) Breakfast was weak-ish, and I wouldn't pay extra for it. It's clearly a convention - wedding type place, so you've got to know that going in. But, for conveninence in DC, it's the best.
We had the most fantastic time in NY last year, it was made possible by the lovely Sam who works there and all the other lovely staff, thankyou so much and see you August ----!! xx

I will echo a lot of the comments previously posted. My wife and I stayed for four nights in the standard one bed room. It is very small, but we only spent a small portion of our waking hours in the room anyways. The subway is just a few steps from the front door as well as Starbucks just below. 
It was cleaned everyday and we had fresh towels and washcloths. The staff at the hotel had no problem with holding our luggage on our checkout day until we were ready to actually leave.
The Mexican Restaurant right next to the hotel was actually very good. The Margaritas were expensive ($-- for a pitcher)... but they put you where you wanted to be!
The only recommendation I'll make is that you bring your own pillow... Unless you like the big lumpy type of pillows. Ours felt like they were once foam pillows that had been chopped into little pieces and stuffed back in the case.
Good times were had while NYC... Get a map of the Subways and actually study them before you go... It will help you tremendously!
FYI... IF you want to get to Penn Station or Times Sq faster from Chambers St, take the - or - train! It only makes one stop before Penn... while the - makes several... The same is true going back to Chambers St form those locations.
You really can't go wrong staying at the Cosmo... Just a great little place to stay in a great location...

I sent in a review in May and the rating is not showing up properly for this hotel . The rating should have been excellent and only showed as a - vs a -. 
Please correct this error on my review and repost. Thanks Dale Nelson

The parking is Ridiculous and...oh yeah...you must valet at $-- per day. Then the off site parking is like two blocks for $--+ a day but there is no in and out priviledges. The hotel is old and need updating. It was my husband and I -st wedding anniversary and our room was not a view of the riverwalk it was not what we expected for our first time on the Riverwalk.

A few years back bad things happened to the Algonquin. The prices went up and the service went down. The free bottled water was withdrawn from the rooms and the chaotic but friendly desk staff were replaced by chaotic but unfriendly desk staff. After a couple of bad stays, we tried elsewhere (ten trip to NYC, three different hotels)
This Fall we thought we'd try again as the lobby bar is great and the hotel is next to the Red Flame Diner, one of the best in the city (and we'd been travelling uptown from Meatpacking to --th just to use the diner anyway!) 
Desk friendly, but not excessively so. Hotel cleaner than it was a few years back. The old familiar and friendly faces on the door. Prices still steep for what's on offer (even for NYC) but you do get a great location and use of the lobby. That said, it would be nice to be warned about the building work which woke us every morning at the crack of dawn.

The room was clean and the staff was truly friendly. They all acted as if they really enjoy working at this hotel. The hot breakfast was the best part and included pancakes, pastries, sausage, bacon, scrambled eggs, hash browns, milk, juice, coffee, and much more all in a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""free"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" buffet - cafeteria style layout. I never did find the omelets I was hoping for. I kept getting pointed in the direction of the fountain. In the evening there were free drinks from an entertaining bar tender, and free snacks.
House keeping was very friendly, and showed they were trying very hard to make us comfortable.
There were no real problems, but a few negatives:
I had ordered a cheese tray and a fruit tray to be in our room upon check-in. It was supposed to come with two bottles of water, which it did not. I had to call down twice before the water was brought up.
The mattress was a little too soft and the room always seemed a little warm, even though we turned the thermostat in the room all the way down to --.
The line at the front desk was very long, so long I gave up a couple times. They did have a full house that night, but should have added more staff to the front desk to handle the crowd. Upon check-in I had to ask for a third key, even though they saw we had three people in the room.
The wi-fi requires an authentication code to login. The one we were given did not work. I had to find another way to get online to retrieve some of my HHonors information before I could login to the hotels wi-fi.

no real complaints except the mugs i used kept showing up rinsed and back in place as if i thought they were fresh new clean ones. That was weird. I knew because there was a piece of gunk on one that i would use to hold my used tea bags in . Still there every day! Otherwise i had a nice stay and the room was clean.

Although our kids are grown, we still enjoy Residence Inns and have had good experiences. In this case, the room was very good and there are no complaints there - the rating would have been better if the room was the only thing being rated.
But the breakfast quality and size of the breakfast area felt less than some other Residence Inns and the staff was less experienced and informed based upon my interactions and inquiries. It is not really the fault of the property there is no public transportation method for getting downtown without driving at least five miles - say to a ballgame or to the Gaslamp - but it still cost it in this rating. Finally, although mid-stay rate increases do happen and it might not be the fault of the hotel, receiving one during a routine middle-of-the-week stay also impacted our rating.

It was a tiny room - but it was fine for just me. The benefit of my room was that it was super quiet! 
The staff were also very accommodating with me extending my stay, and leaving my luggage while I was out of town for a day.
I would definitely stay there again - I'd probably just ask for a slightly larger room.

We adored the Beacon hotel. Stayed there for two nights recently and could not have been more pleased. A wonderful, friendly staff who knows what to do.. Both the person who took our reservation, Francesca and the receptionist Maria, when we arrived were very helpful. A great spot in the city to stay, can walk to it all. It felt like a small European hotel to us, wonderful beds with down comforters, nicely appointed rooms. So well cared for, very clean and chic. Omar , a manager, met us in the lobby and inquired about our stay and if things were as we wished. I even spotted the general manager opening the door for patrons. Personal touch. It was an oasis in a busteling city. We liked everything about it and look forward to returning many times.

This place is so cool, it's kind of trying a bit too hard. Although saying that, I loved it. It's all modern art and modern floral arrangments, all the stuff I'm a complete sucker for. We had a pretty standard room but it comes kitted out to the last. They can get you anything you want - forget your hair straightners, they'll get one for you. 
Didn't sample the food at the hotel so can't give an opinion on that.
The hotel has a pool but I didn't have my swimmers so didn't want to torture myself, as it was sickeningly hot on the days we were in Washington. 
Hotel is in a really nice location, just off Dupont Circle. It's quite a residential area so there are loads of really nice places to eat and it's just a lovely area to take a wander around. I would go back to this hotel tomorrow because it's my kind of hotel but if slightly more traditional is your style, this isn't the hotel for you. But if you like hip, then you'll love it!

We stayed for four nights April -- to --, ----. The hotel is located in great location, close to everything. San Diego is so easy to get around. I would highly recommend renting a vehicle. The hotel has a big name to live up to. The room was a nice size, but awkwardly set up. The bed was really comfortable. The room lacked amenities like enough towels, no bathrobes, no dresser to unpack my clothes. The valet parking was $-- a night, which is a little outrageous. However, the service was good and our car was always brought to us quickly when we needed it.
The Georgetown Inn is gracious, beautifully run, in an ideal location. A pleasure!

The weekend of September -- - --, ---- was a great weekend at the Wyndham. The staff was fantastic and met and supplied all of our needs at the conference. Will return again when in the Jacksonville area.

We asked for a room with a sea view and were given one with a patio that lead right out on to the beach! It was very relaxing. The hotel could do with a spruce up but it had a lot of charm. Also, we were given free tickets to a cute little bay cruise that went from right outside our room.
Liked: the price, location, free parking, private beach and two rescued seals that we watched being fed. And the harbour cruise.
Didn't like: the hotel itself is a bit old and dingy, but for me the location made up for that. Also, all staff were very polite.

My husband and I cant believe the Four Points can provide such an fabulous Hotel at such a cheap rate. The place looks - star, and the Airport Shuttle delivers you right to the door fast and efficiently.
Our room was spacious with fridge, coffee pot and full cable channels
Room service gets top marks for its service and meals too.
We arrived at --a.m. (way before standard check-in time) exhausted from our flight from New Zealand, and were handled swiftly and courteously and permitted into our room right away.
We had two queen beds, both marvellously comfortable with huge fluffy pillows, sooo quiet and peaceful with blackout curtains so we were able to recover from our jetlag extra quick.
and the price??? Thats our secret, but It was unbelievably cheap!!!!
Thanks so much Four Points,
We stayed here last year too, and we'll be back again ----, God willing.
K.C and wife N.Z.

Not one to criticise budget hotels which I regularly stay in, I genuinely found the Lone Star Inn disgusting and uncomfortable with burn marks from an iron and stains on the carpet, a little insect found crawling about on the bathroom sink, a feeling of insecurity and a smell of stale cigarette smoke in what was supposed to be a non-smoking room. I came here as my preferred hotel next door didn't have a room, and I took the room without asking to check what they were like. All the furniture was antequated and looked heavily worn out, as if the hotel had got it all in a yard sale. It looked as if no money has been spent on the rooms since the ----s, such was the general condition of delapidation. Do as I did, and spend a few extra dollars on a decent room at the Motel - hotel right across the road. I'd never consider returning to this dump.

This hotel is lovely and elegant. We had a wonderful stay. The room was beautiful, and the staff was helpful and friendly. Enjoyed a fabulous dinner in the French Room. The meal was exquisite, and we left with huge smiles on our faces. Can't wait to return for another weekend getaway!

I had business in the Seattle are that required me to stay down at the airport. In baggage claim, I found the hotel contact kiosk and called the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Ramada Limited"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" at SEA-TAC. I assumed (since there wasn't an address listed), that it was the Ramada that was located adjacent to the airport property. Since the hotel wouldn't send the hotel van until I gave them a credit card, I gave them my credit card number and was told to call when I got to the hotel pick up point (outside of baggage claim). When I got to the hotel pick up point, I noticed, with some surprise, that the hotel was actually located north of the airport in Tukwilla. When I called the Ramada Limited, I immediately tried to cancel my reservation (The hotel is located in a not too savory neighborhood that caters to prostitution, hourly motels, strip clubs etc.) The Ramada limited wouldn't cancel my reservation.
