Just returned from a business trip to the Hyatt Regency La Jolla. I agree completely with other reviewers - a very good hotel made excellent by the staff. I loved nearly everything about the property - clean, safe, comfortable accommodations, excellent service from all aspects of the hotel and overall a great option in La Jolla for business. The only thing I would change is the lack of dining outlets. While the - places across the parking lot are lovely, a place for a quick lunch (aside from the bar) would be a great addition. Also, there is no place in the hotel (again, aside from the bar) that serves dinner, leaving you with the choice of pricy specialty restaurants across the street, or bar food. 
Be that as it may, the HRLJ is a great hotel in a great location. Loved my stay!

The Magnolia lives up to the reviews. Used the shuttle service to attend a wedding and reception which worked out perfectly. Room was beautiful and functional and the location couldn't be beat. Would love to visit again.

I am a big fan of Andaz hotels (Hollywood and NY -th ave specially). The Andaz SD has an excellent service but the rooms were not what I expected: wood floor and furniture looking old and no view at all (both of my rooms). The roof pool is nice but the overall experience is so so.
Will not come back.

I recently stayed at the Inn on Ferry while in Detroit on business. The Inn is delightful, spread over three historic buildings on a quiet residential street. Each room is unique, and each building has beautifully decorated common areas, as well. The rooms are charming with antique decor, nice toiletries, plush towels, iron and ironing board, plenty of space to move around, ample storage, and a coffee maker with Starbucks coffee and Tazo tea. Guests can also expect a complimentary gourmet cookie every night. I especially enjoyed the bedding--divine mattress and delicious sheets! I stayed in Pugh House and, unlike a poster below, did not meet any ghosts and slept like a log. 
This is a B&B, not a hotel, so you won't find certain hotel amenities here, but you will find a lot more character and greater personalized attention. There is no gym, no restaurant (although the breakfast is quite nice with a waffle bar, a large selection of cereals and breads, fruit, juices, coffee, and tea in a cozy room off the lobby), no porters, and no vending machines. The rooms (at least in the building I was in) are also not the most soundproof. I don't know if they allow children, but I would not stay here with kids under -- as they would likely disturb other guests. All rooms and interior spaces are also non-smoking due to local firecodes. Management should set up some ashtrays outside as there were a lot of cigarette butts on the building porches as there is nowhere else to dispose of cigarettes. 
I think the Inn on Ferry is great alternative to chain hotels. The Inn has tremendous charm, and would be great for a romantic get-away. Service was friendly and helpful at every turn. I would definitely stay here again.

Perfect location to walk from. Rooms are nice, spacious and comfortable. Somewhat lengthy wait for check in, lobby is combined with bar area which makes it noisy if you are relaxing --r trying to- with a glass of wine and friends. There is a nice deck area on the --st floor which is a great spot to enjoy if the weather permits.

Viewed the fireworks on the -rd from the room, walked across the street for the big ones on the -th. We'd recommend this for anyone needing to drive around while in San Antonio - but not if you want to get the flavor of downtown sights.

my biggest complain was that the AC sounded like a helicopter landing every time it turned off. We really enjoyed our stay here, clean and comfortable room, amazing restaurant, convenient location, helpful staff, what more could you ask for?
It was just fantastic, we stayed as a family with - children and found everything to be comfortable and clean, we didn't get our room serviced every day but when they did come in they did a good job.

It's not the sort of place my husband and I would stay if we were on our own, however, our daughter enjoyed it very much. I would say it appeals more to a younger demographic. It is in a good location.
One of the problems with so much glass is the retained heat and at night it is necessary to have the air conditioning running constantly. When it shuts off the room heats up within - minutes and it has to come back on again. So, we had the AC shutting off and on all night long which can wake you up if you're a light sleeper. This hotel was a wonderful surprise. We live in a suburb of Seattle and like to stay in the city when going to late night events, so we have stayed in all the - star downtown hotels. We will be staying here again. Wonderful, friendly service and a great room service breakfast included. Just steps to the best downtown shopping, and theaters.

Business hotel, with nothing special. 
It's very big and honestly very sad, the furniture is old, it remembers the --'s. 
The breakfast is close to the reception, in an open area, but is too big and too many people have to wait to take some hot dishes or a juice...
If you have to stay few days is ok, also because you are close the typical area of the Fisherman Wharf and also to the center of the city.

Husband and I stayed one night here while we were in Dallas. Great hotel, great location. Walked to the Iron Cactus for dinner. Neiman Marcus is a block away. Every night they offer free drinks and milk and cookies and also breakfast in the morning. The bar set up is great. Lots of seating and very comfy. We stayed in a suite. Plenty of room. Small kitchen dining and living area. Great hotel and would stay here again.

This hotel was in central San Fran easy walking access to everywhere. We got a taxi from airport - reasonable cost too. The room was large and clean, pool heated and clean also. The breakfast large and filling. Overall an excellent choice as a base for touring the city.

I can recommend this hotel but not strongly. The location in Kenmore Square was next to the T. The location is perfect and the cost of the hotel for downtown boston was quite good. However the shower was industrial and not very nice. The decor is nice and boutique like but the floor is disgusting looking with large stains.It was unbelievably hot when i was going to bed and I woke up in a sweat. Also the generator outside my window made it impossible to open a window because of the noise. And the temperature could not be adjusted without damaging the heating unit according to an old hand written not taped above the thermometer. That was a nice surprise at - in the morning when i was looking forward to a good nights sleep after a night on the town. If a few updates are made this would be a beautiful hotel. Also , the the staff in the morning were some rather obnoxious women, not friendly and rather bothersome. The fellows working at night were quite kind and inviting, a stark difference between these two teams of workers. Also you only get -- minutes of WIFI a day in your room, and its incredibly slow.

I booked this hotel through Reservation Services International because of the wholesale rate I received. There were few complaints listed...mainly about the valet prices...which I agree are a little high. But otherwise, I am very appreciative of the staff and service I received while staying here. I lost my credit card at the roof top bar (which is amazing, by the way) and I was afraid there might be fraud charges, however, the next morning a staff member whom found out, brought it to my room. I will def return based on the service alone.

The Omni is our choice when we visit our son in San Francisco. The higher floors are so wonderfully quite. The location is perfect for us on lower California Street. The Omni has never been a disappointment.

This was our second stay at this hotel pre flight. We live in Cincinnati area, but will fly from different airports depending on price.
While some areas of the hotel my be a little dated, the hotel is clean, the staff is excellent, food is great. Parking and free shuttle to and from airport big plus.
Never had any problems that some other reviewers have run into. 
Overall, this is a great hotel for the price.

Loved other Kimpton's so we tried this one. Great place all around, from the Bellmen to housekeeping. We were upgraded and the room was fabulous. So glad we tried it. Can't wait to go back. Thanks to all of you for making our stay great!

I've stayed at this hotel - times over the last year and absolutely love it. The location is great (midtown) and very close to most things. The staff is very professional, helpful, and knowledgable....they will recommend a Broadway play, or set you up with dinner reservations around town.
The accomodations are nice. Plus, they have a great continental breakfast, as well as, a nice wine and cheese """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""happy hour"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".
The Monkey Bar is really cool and has a lot of history. If you love Italian food, definitely go to Cellini's across the street.

I recently stayed at the Holiday Inn during a business trip. My wife came along. Our room was big and fresh looking. The furniture was comfortable. We had a view of the city. The hotel has a wonderful restaurant and bar. We ate all three of our breakfasts there, as well as one dinner. It is reasonably priced with great tasting food. I am a member of The Priority Club and we got coupons for breakfast or drinks which gave us a discount. Housekeeping does an efficient job. Our room was spotless. We needed more hangers, at one point, and they arrived within ten minutes of our request. The front desk manager, Yudith was helpful and friendly. Thanks for a good stay!!

I had a great stay for two nights in NY. Business. Rooms are spacey and nice. The location is great. good value for money.
Nice location next to Grand Central and midtown events. We walked to Central Park, it wasn't that bad of a walk.

This Crown Plaza is nothing to get excited over. Overpriced based on the location and quality. I stayed here for a business meeting in SEA and my company picked the hotel. I can honestly say I will not use this hotel again for business or personel needs. Overall not the worst hotel but rooms are a bit dated. Flat screen TVs are nice but internet is slow, walls are damaged and abused, and worst is the bathroom. Very low water pressure and hot water that is lukewarm at best. Floors look as if the room was used by a barber with all the hairs the housekeeping syaff failed to clean up. Workout room has much to be desired and is hard to find. The bar has a nice happy hour M-TH but the free food is nasty. Better off buying off the menu. Checked in around ----pm and the girl working the desk was rude and not helpful to each guest checking in or out.

I have stayed at the Omni South Park before this trip. I can comment that the level of service and expectations remains high. The Omni South Park has a resort like environment with a pool that is both indoors and outdoor, sauna room, dressing rooms, fitness center, pool side patio with cabanas, towels in each pool chair, floaty noodles in the pool, croquet set up, tether ball and basketball court. We used all of these things in my off hours. The length of this very large pool is great for swimming fitness. There is no complimentary food service. An onsite restaurant is available. This is not your travel motel. The guest rooms are clean, comfortable and better quality. This Omni is not downtown so you have to drive to get there. This Omni provides a complimentary shuttle service to and from the airport that runs on a schedule. I would always stay here, but price and location can be a factor.

My husband and I stayed - nights at the Surrey's in June. We were absolutely thrilled! As we spent - nights in NY, we decided to stay - nights in the Lower east side and - nights in the Upper East Side. the Surrey was heaven: already upon checking in, the reception staff succeeded to make us feel immediately most welcome. The girl at reception, I believe she was called Sabrina, is a natural talent. We had (if I'm not mistaken) a superior room which was on the -st floor and facing the street (right above the entrance). The room had beautiful baywindows with comfy cushions inviting you to settle down and watch the streetlife. Not that there was much going on: to our great surprise the street turned out to be very quiet and it was no problem at all to leave the windows open at night (can you believe it, this being steps away from -th Av?). All furniture in the room was very tasteful, with plenty of cushions, beautiful fabrics, a few picture books on the coffee table, etc. The bed was majestic: large, with a fantastic mattress, great duvet cushions and whatever you could possibly wish for for a good night's sleep. The bathroom left nothing to desire, the toiletries were excellent. There is one thing (or better two) I should mention just to confirm the thesis that perfection is not of this world: there were only - hangers in the closet and we had to call - or - times before they brought more. But I am also mentioning this to illustrate how difficult it is to fine fault with the Surrey. Breakfast did not fully meet our expectations, but I have to admit that by this time they had gone over the top, being spoiled by the room and anything. For breakfast simply turn right when exiting the hotel and then right again (is this Madison av?) and go to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Two brothers"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""": they serve wholesome traditional meals all day round. You cannot stay at the Surrey without going to the rooftop bar: it is really the cérise sur le gateau. It is very relaxing (try the lemonade), offers stunning views and is the ideal place to recuperate after a day of exploring. The best experience is however yet to come: on our last day, we asked to have a late check-out, since we had a very late flight back home that night. The hotel was however fully booked and we were left with the idea of boarding the plane with sweaty clothes after yet another day of NY streetcombing. No worries though: when we came back, one of the spa rooms was waiting for us and we could take a refreshing shower again with the same luxury toiletries and smooth towels as those provided in the room. The very last thing to mention is the professionalism of the concierge: he must have thought we were some kind of secret inspectors testing him, asking for a different kind of cuisine every night. But of course he succeeded and our dinners were top. The Surrey is that kind of place where you return to and get the feeling of coming home.

Just returned from a five night stay over Xmas Holiday period - no complaints of the hotel at all. Staff were freindly and all of our needs were met. Room size was perfectly spacious, although decor a little on the tired side. Fantastic location. Booked through Tradewinds (UK) and feel the hotel meets it's three star rating, and offered good value for money. We would certainly return to the hotel.

We booked the Charlesmark on what was available on the web. It's a nice looking hotel, with nice wood touches and accents. I also understand that in Boston's back bay area, particularly, rooms tend to be small and pricey.
These rooms are very cramped and the beds are small. Staying with another person in the smaller rooms with a double bed, had us tripping over each other constantly. They are very poorly laid out and nothing is really all that ergonomic. Very illogical. Everything looked nice, but the experience of staying there was far from pleasant.
Since I was in Boston to run the marathon, sleep was important. The walls and ceiling were very poorly soundproofed and every time someone above us walked around the joists creaked like crazy. Light music or TV in adjoining rooms was very audible and normal level talking out in the tiny hallway came through the door loud and clear.
You have satellite TV, but in the smaller rooms it was - feet up in the air to your side so you had to wrench your head to watch it. There wasn't a particularly good selection of movies or sports that came by default and ordering PPV was not allowed. I've never experienced that before. The DVD player in our room only played CDs. So we couldn't rent movies or order them.
Lastly, they actually billed our credit card in the morning prior to our checking out and before we could sign and confirm the charges. A very poor customer service practice in my opinion.

Stayed here for a convention this past weekend. It was overall a fantastic experience, the only complaint I'd make was the beds were a bit uncomfortable and the room tended to get really really dry during the night (woke up parched every morning), but every other aspect of this hotel far out-shined these minor issues. I will be staying here next time I'm in Boston for sure!
I wasn't able to get an appointment at my RMT before I left, but the attached spa was able to accommodate me and the massage was fantastic, completely relaxed me and got me ready for the rest of the convention!

We stayed at Hawthorn Suites the night before our early morning flight. The hotel is just a few blocks from Love Field. Very helpful staff. Rooms are dated, but clean, comfortable, and quiet. Apartment feel. Would recommend. Lowest price in the area...they have a senior discount too!

I have stayed here and my parents have stayed here. It is in a great location. It is a chic, understated boutique hotel. It is LA's """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""in-the-know"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" secret boutique hotel.
Service was excellent. Nicole at the front desk was very friendly. I like the design and the restaurant has --- orders of pasta. It is down the street from Joan's on Third (which is a paparazzi-looking-to-snap-a-celebrity photo), which is one of LA's best cafes. It is also close to Robertson Blvd, Beverly Hills, Beverly Center Shopping Mall and other chic destinations. 
I wish I could have a permanent room here.

My husband and I enjoyed a wonderful week at this hotel. We stayed in a RockStar suite - which was located on the Petco Park side. Whilst some street noise was heard during early hours of the morning, for us it just added to the excitement of living at the entrance of the Gaslamp Quarter. 
The suite was spacious, modern and very clean. The room service and Mary Janes Cafe had a wide variety of delicious food and drinks which we really enjoyed. Mini bar had a large range to choose from, however it was not replenished for our entire stay! This was disappointing but instead we tried several of the bars on -th Ave.
The staff were all really friendly and accommodating which was great to experience.
Unfortunately we didn't have time to try the rooftop pool bar as we ran out of time.
My overall experience was awesome, we would definitely stay again!!

We stayed here for four nights while visiting NYC.The Hotel is in a great location and the service is outstanding.We had three rooms and all were immaculate and very spacious and comftable.The Bathroom was very luxurious.
Its ideally situated for visiting the financial district and Statue of Liberty,but getting anywhere in Manhattan is easy with in the Taxis which are always outside.
The cost to eat in the hotel are crazy,but with so many good restaraunts in the city why bother ?
The only negative for us was that they forgot to put an extra bed in my kids room until we reminded them on the second night,and after being told that the bill was settled it was a bit of an unexplained surprise to find that some extras had been added when I received my credit card statement !!!
The Staff are very polite and nothing is too much trouble so I guess some negative comments by other Trip Advisor reviewers about the service are from people who are never satisfied or think they are far more important than they actually are !!!!

I love the location of the Time - very convenient when visiting for work in Times Square. I enjoy the clean, modern feel of the entry and lobby, and the restaurant Serafina downstairs is good. 
The room I stayed in wasn't as nice as I'd hoped, though. I appreciated when I entered the room, it was lit and lively, as if they were expecting me - but oddly the radio was on very loud to a popular music station (not very soothing), and the room was absolutely freezing - just above -- degrees. I actually thought for a minute that someone was still in there cleaning.
The decor of the room was fine, but certain aspects of the place looked old and worn. There was dark mildew in the edges of the shower tile (places very visible when in the shower, but probably not to the maid cleaning from the other direction.) 
The television-minibar unit looked like someone had fashioned it on an episode of Trading Spaces out of plywood, and it served as a bulk piece of furniture to hide a huge mess of cords that went to the internet, fridge, tv, cable, and who knows what else. It kind of looked like elements of the room had been put together after the fact - like they didn't think ahead to get a TV stand-minibar, and they had to retrofit one into the design of the room and shove it in the corner.
The room had no real closet, but an ironing board and iron in room (not always a given in NYC) and a nice bathrobe. 
Another nice touch was the turn down service, though the radio was turned on rather loud to an obnoxious station again (I wish they'd go for a classical station, just loud enough to be heard when you walk in - that would be so much more soothing.)

Here's the thing, I'm a born and bred Texan so I will admit that every now and then a little exaggeration may fall from the lips of one of my fellow Texans - This must be the case with the phrase touted in the Barton Creek brochure and on their website, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""the ultimate in a relaxing getaway nestled in -,--- secluded acres of rolling hills"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Yes, it's nestled, and yes, there are rolling hills, but secluded? I don't think so. 
Pictures on the website show the Resort either FROM the view of the golf course or looking TO the view of the golf course giving the Resort a secluded LOOK. Folks, this is just not the case. Courtesy of Austin's population explosion, housing additions line the road leading to the Resort - granted they are multi-million dollar digs, but I was expecting the countryside. From the tiny balcony in our room, the view was pretty, but I was looking at lots of homes dotting those rolling hills. If I wanted to stay in a hotel IN A CROWDED CITY, I would have remained in Houston and stayed at the Houstionian. And that is my major beef with the Resort - the exaggeration of a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""relaxing getaway nestled in ---- secluded acres of rolling hills"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". They should tell it like it is!
That said, there were a few good things about the Resort. Our room was large and beautiful. The food and service in the main dining room was excellent and the staff at the Resort were helpful and friendly. The exception was the valet parking boys - Upon leaving I came outside to our waiting vehicle with my hands full and not one of the three guys standing there even made a move to open my passenger side door. 
The Resort in general struck me as a bunch of hallways with little open areas stuck here and there. No big pretty lobby - just a small one with a lobby hallway that looked toward the golf course. Amazingly, a huge metal roofed pavilion obscured the view. You travel down long interior hallways to get to the rooms, spa area, pool, dining and meeting rooms. Nothing to write home about as far as decor. Although the Resort was crowded with wedding receptions and Christmas parties, it was at least relatively quiet. 
All in all, if you want to stay at a nice hotel on the outskirts of Austin that has a spa and golf course, this would be a good choice. Just don't expect wide open spaces.

The hotel has gotten a LOT nicer since I first started at USC, but there are so many nicer hotels for the same price in Downtown Los Angeles that are only a short drive (- minutes down Fig you'll find the Marriott and the Sheridan) to campus and closer to LA Live that I would recommend... It gets the job done for those who want to be as close to campus as possible, but it is not that clean and the rooms are just average.

Have to say we had a great stay thanks to the great service we got from the staff and a special thanks for George. Hotel suite was spacious and provided all the amenities (microwave, fridge, cutlery) which worked out great with the staff recommended late night pizza! 
The hotel has a roof top lounge which is a nice place to relax and have a drink.
Location was quite central to the places we were going and we were able to walk everywhere we needed to go.
The only negatives were the decor which could use an update. Also, the washroom door which did not have a lock, saying that, it seems the washroom was built to be barrier free and likely was a feature. If you have mobility issues, this suite would have worked well for you.
Overall- yeah for the Beacon!

Has great location, close to Freeways, highways and Hollywood Blvd. The correct classification should be -.- stars. There is room for improvement but the price is right, and
also has free parking.

My daughter and I were very pleased with our stay at Super -. I had made the reservation online and was charged at checkin, the amount stated on the confirmation email I had received.
We arrived in town early and went directly to the Motel so we knew where it was in relation to the Riverwalk area. The person at the front desk was very helpful and gave us a map and information on the area. 
The room was very clean. There was a problem with the toliet and someone came immediately to fix it after a call to the front desk. 
We were very pleased with our stay and will stay at this Super - on our next trip to San Antonio.

This Hilton is a nice airport hotel with lots of meeting space. Stayed here - days for a conference. Easy to walk to from Logan. Has an executive lounge for Hilton elite members. Room was spacious, and I didn't lose sleep from the sound of airplanes. Staff was very gracious and helpful.

I had a very good experience at the hotel. The rooms were clean, and the property is located right next to the metro rail which was perfect. You just walk right over there and catch the train or bus. We didn't need a car and we went all over San Diego. Breakfast buffet was adequate. Pillows were a bit hard to me but my boyfriend and our friend didn't mind them, so it's all relative.
Yes some of the pictures are a bit weird in the rooms and halls, but they're just pictures! I found it to be a nice stay and would recommend it. Would stay there again while in San Diego.

The hotel staff was not accommodating. Although I arrived -- minutes prior to check-in, and the hotel parking lot was nearly empty, I was told that the only thing available was a smoking room because, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""That's how it is when you go through Priceline or Hotwire.""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""
The smoking room was awful. No ventilation, smokey, stuffy, etc. I went back downstairs because it was unacceptable. Again, I was told that everything else was booked for other guests. The manager overheard and suggested that the staff member check again. The staff member complains to the manager that we are Priceline guests, and reiterates that """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""that's how it is with Priceline."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" However, thanks to the manager's intervention, we were moved to one of the many available non-smoking rooms. But by that time, my impression was set.
Because of my experience here, I'm not sure that the money saved with Priceline is worth it for the stepchild-like treatment I'll receive.

You can't beat the location, right by Union Square. This is a boutique hotel. The service was very good as the front desk staff always was attentive and informative. The room is very small but nicely appointed and modern.

The Royalton is a glamorous modern hotel nestled into a beautiful old building in the heart of midtown New York City. Within a few easily-walked blocks you'll find the New York Public Library-Bryant Park, Grand Central Station, the UN, Times Square, etc. The Bryant Park, Times Sq, & Port Authority subway stops are all easily accessible. In the evenings, the hotel lobby is a popular gathering place for cocktails: the music's pumping & the lights are low. So low you might need to stop for a moment to let your eyes adjust! The elevators are a bit small, as are the hallways. It did take me a day to get comfortable with that. Our room was on the --th floor, very quiet. We were able to have them replace the feather pillows, etc, with hypoallergenic—wonderful! Our windows were somewhat covered over by the building's carved stonework. I wasn't wild about not being able to see the sky, but that won't bother everyone. I believe most floors don't have this issue and the windows are clear. The room itself was clean and sleek—not nearly enough storage room, but that’s not an unusual complaint for a hotel room, especially in NYC! The bed was very comfortable and there was an iPad available for use during our stay. WiFi was reliable and just $---day. We did have some issues with hot water in the mornings: It came on after we ran the tap for a few minutes. The staff was consistently friendly and helpful. I would definitely recommend this hotel and would absolutely stay here again.

Normally before I book a room I read the reviews. Actually this hotel was a little better than the reviews. For financial security I did not book online but went in and checked out the room prior to booking. It was a little smelly, but housekeeping sprayed air freshner and that took care of that. If I had to complain about anything it would be the bathroom having no window. Otherwise not bad for the money. Ryan was great!

Wait for an elevator ranged anywhere from - minutes to as much as -- minutes. No exaggeration, I assure you. The staff must tire from hearing all the complaints about them as there is nothing they can do. I realize it's busy but it is always busy except the few hours before check in and after check out.. With this in mind, I will never stay at this Hyatt again. All the nice things everyone before me said are true: Location, restaurants, mall etc. This one thing is something that can't be changed and won't be so I will stay somewhere else next time. My advice if you choose this hotel: when the door opens, get in, even if it isn't going the direction you are.

We stayed here for - months because of soot damage in our home. We loved it. We stayed in one of the two story two bedroom suites. It had a full kitchen and small living room area. The staff is extremely helpful and friendly. They really took care of us. On site laundry is clean and less expensive than a laundermat. Free breakfast is great and M-Th they have free snacks-dinner. We have two dogs and I would highly recommend this hotel for anyone travelling with a pet. Not just pet friendly, but pet welcoming. Plenty of grass area surrounding to walk the dogs. We were able to leave the dogs in the room, not crated, when we went to work or wherever. Great freeway access to anywhere you want to go in San Diego.

We were in San Antonio to celebrate a family wedding and we were very pleased with our choice to stay at this Red Roof Inn. At the front desk we were greeted with a smile by the manager, Sung, and checked in to our rooms quickly and efficiently. The rooms were large, immaculately clean and well-cared for with all the necessary amenities.
During our - night stay we had several opportunities to interact with the staff and they were consistently cordial, capable and professional-Chantae at the front desk was especially helpful and went out of her way to make us feel like """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""family"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".
I highly recommend this Inn for anyone staying in San Antonio for it's cleanliness and value for your dollar.

i have actually stayed at this hotel -times and everytime that i have stayed there i have enjoyed my visit the front desk are always friendly everytime i have went. they are located in a good location. for those who said bad remarks im sorry for you. you must have picked a wrong time to go. like ive said before i have stayed at this hotel three times and i have enjoyed it all three times. nice swimming pool, spa, elevator, clear everytime ive been there. yes its not good about the deposit for the remote control nor the telephone but you do get ur deposit back however i have no need for those things so it doesnt bother me

We recently stayed at the Rodeway Inn PCH on a west coast road trip and it was definitely worth the money we paid to stay there. While it isn't right in Los Angeles, it is close enough to so many major highways that you can really get anywhere in the metropolitan area quickly enough (assuming you're not needing to travel during rush hour). We were able to travel to Malibu, downtown LA, and Hollywood from here without any real traffic delays, which we did not expect going in. 
As far as the room itself, it was basically what you expect from a Rodeway. This certainly isn't a five-star resort, but the rooms were very clean and mostly quiet. The bed was very comfortable and that is much appreciated given the low quality beds at many similarly priced hotels. Overall, this hotel was definitely worth the money and it was a great spot for us leaving for our next destination in San Diego. The owner was very nice and accommodating as well, which added to the positive experience.

If you are on a budget and want to stay at a clean, quiet, friendly motel, with free covered parking in a nice neighborhood, call Varsa at the Castle Inn to make your resos. Even if you're not on a budget, this is a great little motel.
My mom, sister, -- year old niece and I stayed here for four nights over the Thanksgiving holiday and were very pleased. Varsa is so helpful and was able to grant every request that I threw at her...cork screw, dinner reservations, which bus to catch, even directions to the METALLICA concert!!!! You rock Varsa.

We stayed here Mar -th thru' Mar --th this year (just missed St. Patrick's day -d'oh!), and here's my thoughts...

*Price - a very reasonable GBP--- for four nights, including taxes.

*Maid service - efficient and unobtrusive, exactly what you want from a maid service.
Cons :
*No coffee-making facilities in the room (although some fab wee deli's across the road to fill that void, if required.)
*No hanging-space in the room - tonnes of room and not one little rail to hang our clothes! We didn't really unpack for the five days we were there, just dug deeper into the suitcases!
*Banging doors - this was the one thing about this hotel that I found hard to live with. We happened to be sharing a corridor with some kind of school-club gathering, hence every other room in our corridor seemed to have at least three teenagers resident. As you might imagine, there was a lot of room-hopping at odd hours of the day and night (...ahem...), and a remarkable lack of stealth and subtlety involved in said hopping. Basically, the room doors will bang unless you close them over softly. The teenagers in our corridor clearly hadn't mastered the art of soft door closing (a truly complicated task, after all...) and whoever was supposed to be supervising them had clearly drank themselves into oblivion in the bar, or some other such coping mechanism, so they went unchecked. Yes folks, there was a lot of banging going on in the Skyline that weekend...
*Pool opening hours - not great. I would have much prefered early morning swimming, but the pool hours are late afternoon to evening.
There has been quite a bit said on T-A about surly staff at the Skyline, but in general, I found the reception staff and porters to be okay - nothing to write home about, but certainly not rude. The same could be said of the breakfast room personnel.
Will I go back? Absolutely, but I may have to begin a petition for soft-close doors before I go...

Even so, the garbage trucks come by at -:-- am, so you're not going to sleep through the night (but that's true of most places in Manhattan). On each floor they had near the elevators an electric shoe shiner, which makes this place feel like a hotel for salesmen catering to the local stores--it has a Willy Loman feel to it. For under $--- this is about what you can expect in New York.

My wife and I spent two nights at the Belvedere in August. We found it to be a great value for the money. It was easy to drive to, valet parking cost $---day, the staff was friendly and tried to be helpful, and the room was fine. It was larger than we expected and clean but not fancy. The mattress was quite firm. There were - TV's, one in the bedroom and one in the small sitting room with a fridge and a microwave and an ugly but otherwise usable sofa. The elevators were often packed but it really wasn't a problem. The bellstaff was helpful and offered some recommendations for restaurants (but their recommendations seemed to be for places they had special relationships with). We would definitely stay here again though we would definitely prefer the W but can't afford it! Also the location about - blocks from Times square and the subway was great. The neighborhood seemed very safe also.

I stayed here for - nights in June for a business trip. The room and was very nice and comfortable. There was a nice chair to relax in at the end of the day. Very busy area. There are some nice places to check out nearby like the Reading Terminal Market, Hard Rock Cafe and the Liberty Bell. The neighborhood is a little iffy...a lot of major stores (like Macy's nearby) close at - or -pm. There's also a pharmacy nearby on Market street where you can pick up some items if need be. I liked the restaurant for breakfast as well as having the option of a starbucks in the lobby.
My only complaint would be the internet charges - at --.-- plus tax per day that seemed a bit steep to me. Other Marriott properties I've stayed at don't charge at all.
Overall a good option if you need to be in that area for business.

Hi. We stayed at the Omni on a Saturday night night in August ----. We were doing the tourist thing in DC on Sat-Sun, so really just needed someplace nice and clean to crash at night. Although we wanted a place closer to Dupont Circle, we got the Omni on priceline for $--, which was less than half of the going rate! I also thought I'd get this hotel, so didn't mind being about - mile away from Dupont Circle.
One to the hotel...nice grand lobby! Kept very very clean. The hotel was build I think in the ----'s or --'s so definitely not your Hyatt-Hilton cookie cutter type place. There were banners up all over the place about the historic Wash DC events that took place here. We arrived around --:--am and the were nice enough to let us check in early. Got up to the room...decent size. Bathroom looked more like one you'd see in a condo or rental apartment than a hotel. Comfortable bed, along with a chair or two and desk.
Parking...they wanted $-- for every -- hrs parking (valet only)! So if I checked in --:--am and left at -pm...more than -- hrs. If you drive maybe --- to --- mile from the hotel, there is residential parking available. During the weekdays it's a - hr limit, but no limit weekends, so we were set. Also looked like a safe area to park. So if you're here on weekend...save your $--. 
The hotel is about a - - - min walk to the Metro, and from there you can be in DC in -- mins. Also right by the Metro is a street filled of restaurants. We tried one of the Mediterranean places...a Lebanese place..was just ok but close. Also the National Zoo is a -- min walk from the hotel.
Overall, good location as a base on DC, but could be better with a place closer to Dupont Circle. If it's a place you're looking for just to crash, and want someplace clean, comfortable, and safe, the Omni is perfect. If you plan to go in and out of the hotel many times a day while visiting DC, look for something closer.

This was a great choice for us. Traveling with three kids, I wanted a clean, nice place to stay in a good location. This was it! Visiting from a small town, I wanted every detail of our Chicago trip planned for fun and safety. I asked the hotel staff many, many questions before and after our arrival, and each person was friendly and helpful. Not once did I get the feeling that they were too busy to help, or uninterested in what we needed. From the front desk to the restaurant staff, they all did an excellent job.

It was a very nice hotel, but unfortunately a couple was in the room the next to us and it was fairly obvious what they were up to - if you get my meaning. Better soundproofing would have been beneficial. I'd definitely recommend asking for a room that doesn't have an adjoining door to a suite with unknown guests.

Robbed in the hotel lobby!!! Was informed by police that the suspect was involved in other robberies around the neighborhood. Security was less than helpful, and was told management was not available. 
To further point out the dangers of this hotel, people known to the local police department are allowed to roam all floors of the hotel and loiter in the lobby. After bringing this to the attention of the front desk, their response is that it is a public building accessible to everyone. Strange because I have stayed in many hotels where entrances are locked and only the front entrance can be used and security is actively aware of people coming and going. I am not sure about the rest of the people out there, but I know I don't feel comfortable having vagrants and apparently in this case criminals entering the hotel. To make it worse anyone can enter thru the parking garage ending up on the sixth floor where guest rooms are. Where is the security and safety for guests????
Yes the hotel is large but shouldn't there be some sense of safety and security as we walk down the hallway to the elevator. Do you really want to be asked for change as you open the door of your hotel and walk down the hall??? It's not like we are taking a stroll down the street!!! We haven't even left the hotel yet!!!!
Staying here was like a nightmare. This is supposed to be a Hilton property and as such, one expects certain standards to be in place. One would expect management to address the situation and provide some kind of assistance after going through such a traumatic situation. You would probably be safer pitching a tent in Union Square than staying in this hotel.

After reviewing tons of hotels on TripAdvisor in an attempt to save money on a trip to NYC last summer (midtown hotels were crazy expensive compared to past trips), the Newton came recommended and at a great price. I wasn't expecting much because of the reasonable rates, but the room was spectacular. HUGE, a flat screen, wall-mounted TV, a sitting area that included a sink and refrigerator, a gigantic, Euro-style bathroom (completely tiled room, shower is half the room when curtain is pulled) with great water pressure.
It's true that the elevator is slow and small, but the hotel itself is exceptionally clean, the staff was super friendly, the room was (as previously stated) spotless and huge for the money, and the hotel is only about a half block from the subway. The express train gets you to Times Square in no time and at the end of the day you get to return to a relatively quiet NYC neighborhood (there's a great Thai restaurant just down the street, too).
In short, the Hotel Newton is a great hotel not only for the budget-conscious traveler, but for ANY traveler. I'm staying there again next month and looking forward to another great experience!

The Radisson near San Jose Airport is an OK match for the brand name, but nothing exceptional. Comparatively well situated, airport noise is not heard. Nicely close to freeway ---, easy access to drive north or south. Enough parking space. 
The building and some furniture seem a bit tired, but well maintained. The room was very clean, has a comfortable bed and safe locker. Bathroom was fine, with nice toiletries, but a bit small. The TV was strangely old, with their typical menu system that doesn't function well or simply I never figured out how to use. 
Didn't try the business class rooms they have, got an ordinary room and it was just fine for me. Didn't try the pool and the gym either. 
The staff is friendly and helpful. The restaurant RSVP-- (and especially the bar) are totally enjoyable, happy hour until - pm, good menu, very nice staff!! 
It was a pity that breakfast was not included for me. It's possible though to order breakfast in the room, but it seems expensive. 
Can be recommended for both business and leisure travelers, good enough value for money. However, I guess that some folks might be expecting more from this hotel.

Once you figure out how to navigate your way into the driveway without being slammed by turning traffic, it's pretty much downhill. You then need to find someone to park your car and forget about help with your bags. There is a look of relief on the attendant's face when you say you'll handle it yourself. There is a continual line at the registration desk where - people try to help you while answering phones. Our room was average size. I turned down the comforter to crawl into bed and the sheets were dirty with what I can only describe as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""body fluids"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I went down to the lobby to talk to someone about it and there was a woman there demanding to see a manager about the filthy comforter on her bed. tried to do laundry. - washers don't work. I have to carry laundry to washer in adjoining hotel. No apologies - no assistance. Breakfast buffet so-so. Coffee earns always empty! Hotel is in great location to inner harbor sites and restaurants. The attached gym is THE best I've ever seen in a hotel

We just stayed here for four nights. Our room was very spaceous and clean and everything worked. Breakfast wasn't included in our deal, but there was a cheap option to take this as an extra - it was good value, but get there early to avoid the queue. Staff were helpful whenever we needed them (extra towel arrived in minutes). Only slight negatives are that there can be a long wait for the lifts and the decor is a bit tired.
I should also mention that the Italian restaurant a few doors along (Alfredo's ?) was really nice and good value.

Had a great stay at The Pearl Hotel. I didn't feel like I was in NYC because of the room size. The hotel seems brand brand new and smells so nice and is extremely clean.
The ONLY downside of my stay was that my cell phone (AT&T) did not work in the hotel. I had to go into the lobby to get any sort of signal. Not okay if one is on a business trip or needs to use their cell phone.
Other than that, it is a gorgeous hotel and I will for sure consider it next time I need a hotel in the city.

I like the location of this hotel and the beds. We always ask for a room facing away from the street, so normally it is very quiet at night, also.
However, and this is a big however, the last two times I have stayed in this hotel, I have had to address the management about not being given what the reservation stated. In one case it was to be a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""full breakfast,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for which they gave me a voucher for a continental breakfast when I arrived, saying, that's all we ever have (not true). Fortunately I had the print-out of my reservation with me that stated that the room came with a full breakfast.
That was minor in comparison with the last experience I had there. I had reserved a deluxe queen suite, and when I checked with the reservations manager upon arrival, I said, this has two queen beds, correct? He said, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""two beds....yes."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" When I saw the room, I realized that they were double beds (the suite was also very small). I had to address the front desk with my printed reservation, and was then given the deluxe queen suite I had reserved. I had to move the coffee maker from the wrong room to the new room, which didn't have one, even though there is supposed to be one in every room.
The hotel's outgoing message (as you are on hold waiting to reach someone) describes the hotel as being """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""a ten minute walk from Times Square."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Since the hotel is -- blocks from Times Square (-.-- miles), this can't possibly be true. Another part of the outgoing message praises a restaurant in the hotel which is no longer in business.
They also have themselves listed as a free wifi spot on the web, which is also not the case, not even in the lobby, as some hotels are. (For example, the Marriott in Brooklyn charges for wifi in the room, but it is free in the public areas of the hotel on the first floor.)
The maids shouted to one another in the hall outside the door to our room - which was otherwise quiet when guests were passing through the hall. We seldom let them in to clean the room, only asking for clean towels, but on the one occasion they were there to clean, they did not vacuum the floor - we found the same bits of debris on the floor as before they were there.
One of our worst experiences with the hotel involved their refusal to take any responsibility for the car service (across the street from the hotel) from which they got a car to take us to JFK. (Incidentally, this was after the doorman claimed that he couldn't find a taxi - now that I think of it, I have never been unable to find a taxi from that hotel or in that neighborhood - where I used to live!) After asking us several times what airline we were going to, the driver left us off at the wrong terminal and drove away, causing problems that resulted in our almost missing our plane. We had to get a taxi to take us to the correct terminal, which was quite far away.
When I took this up with the hotel, the hotel representative said, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""well, the driver said he asked you several times to show him your boarding pass."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I replied that this was totally impossible, because we did not have boarding passes at that point, so if had asked us, that is what we would have told him. Etc, etc., one excuse after another, with no assumption of responsibility.
Fortunately (or unfortunately, depending on how you look at it), the driver or his company also submitted a charge to our credit card company that was more than what I had signed for, and I had the receipt, so I was able to put the charge into dispute with my credit card company.
Altogether a most unpleasant experience. The hotel sent me standard several requests for an evaluation via email, which I finally replied to. I received a bland, generic form response which did not address any of the specific complaints in my evaluation, and from what I've seen on the hotel's other recent reviews on TripAdvisor, I expect that a form response will follow this review, also.

I recently stayed at Heartbreak Hotel in Memphis. What a huge disappointment....the hotel is in need of repairs the rooms are worn looking in fact the whole hotel need a face lift. The shuttle system consists of one shuttle on a Saturday night you can get to Beale st but getting back is a problem and a cab is $ --.-- dollars...PEOPLE LEFT BEHIND WERE VERY UPSET.....
The breakfast left a lot to desired. My advice is to stay in a hotel that cares about the comfort of its guests...
 Naples Fl

Stayed at the Salisbury for - nights on a girlie shopping trip with a friend. Having requested a quiet room by email we were both upgraded to a suite each which was huge. The suites are extremely large and comfortable. Decor could be more modern but the beds are comfortable with a coffee machine, fridge and microwave provided as well. The front desk staff are friendly and efficient. We ordered a car via the hotel to take us to the airport and instead we had a limo ferry us there in style! Overall I would stay here again and do not hesitate in recommending it to other NYC travellers.

The accomodations and aminities associated with this facility is second to none. The cooperation of the staff is excellent. We will choose the accomodations every time we come to Houston for business. I will recommend this Hotel to all of our teams traveling to Houston.
The morning breakfast is tops. My student-athletes thinks this is the best hotel we use all year.
Thank you Robert Caltabiano for you hospitality.
Carson Fields - Golf Coach 
UAPB

My husband and I are Kimpton Hotel fans and have stayed with them in San Francisco, Boston and in DC. We were looking forward to our stay at the Muse in NYC and were not disappointed. Our stay was perfect. Here are the details:
Location: Less than a block off of Times Square. Very easy to grab cabs or just walk block and half to subway stop. Easy walk to shopping and Central Park. 
Staff: Very friendly and welcoming. That's what we love about Kimpton Hotels...staff is always great! We are members of their In Touch program and there was a personal note, bottle of water and Godiva chocolate in our room when we arrived. Such a nice touch.
Room: Amazing! We had an executive king and it was huge...super comfy king size bed, chaise sofa to lounge on plus desk and flat screen tv. Nice bathroom with plenty of room for travel stuff. Huge closet with hangers and bathrobes. Our room faced the back side of the hotel and was very quiet.
Amenities: Complimentary wine hour every night and coffee and tea in morning plus newspapers delivered to door and FREE wi-fi.
What can I say, Kimpton Hotels is the best hotel chain and they truely understand travelers today. They are always our first choice. We will definitely be back to the Muse hotel.

We were a little worried because of the cost of this hotel compared to other nearby hotels, but the location right between Time's Square and Central Park was just too good to pass up. We had a great room, a great view and the hotel helped me get Broadway show tickets and even brought us complimentary chocolate covered strawberries after the show in our room. My wife is still convinced that I paid someone to do that, but they were just in our room with a little note from the front desk. Seriously, I am not a paid commentator, just a couple visiting from the South and we would book this place again in a heartbeat. It is a little crowded, but I assume all hotels in NYC are at this time of year. Also, there is a great Halal vendor across the street that is unbelievable. you got to try it!
Great stay. Would stay here again. Beautiful view from our room. Very helpful staff.

A friend and I stayed here for - nights over spring break. We checked in on a Wednesday and there was no wait. The girl at the front desk had us down for a one bed room, but I asked if she had any rooms available with two beds and she said yes. Very surprising to us, we got a corner room with - windows on the --st floor (second to the top)...the views were amazing! The room was decently sized (big enough for us) and very clean. 
The best thing about the Best Western Inn of Chicago is that it is located literally in the middle of everything. It is a short half block walk to Michigan Avenue, across from the Virgin Record Store and between the Gap and Guess. Walking to north and south Michigan Avenue is a quick short stroll. Everything is nearby, I wouldn't stay anywhere else as far as location goes. We walked everywhere, and if we didn't feel like walking...we definately made use of the CTA public busses (they were so convenient)...(If you are going to use busses, which you probably will because walking does get tiresome...go to any place around that says """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Checks Cashed here"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and you can get the CTA bus and subway pass, it will definately save you a lot of money rather than paying the $- each way on busses. Make sure to ask the person what each card holds, so you can find the right one for your trip depending on how much you will use it.) Also, the subway (or the 'L') is about - blocks up from the hotel, which we used to do shopping in Wicker and Lincoln park. The L is really a lot easier to figure out than we thought. 
Overall, this hotel's location was amazing. It was so convenient to be able to walk everywhere, literally. Whether it was up and down Michigan Ave. or to Navy Pier, walking wasn't too far for us to handle. With our hotel being so close, it was nice because we could stop at our hotel for a few minutes between things we were doing. And, walking at night was fine...we felt so safe because there were a lot of people out on the street (even at like -- or -- p.m.).

You get what you pay for and whilst the Greenwich isn't cheap you get something other hotels need to aspire to - ultra quiet luxurious rooms with truly excellent service and a touch of class. 
So you know our type of hotel, our other NYC visits have included the Soho Grand (nice but moody staff), Tribeca Grand (nice but noisy), -- Thompson (average) and the Hudson (cool but tiny tiny rooms).
Our stay started with a swift paperless check-in and personal escort to the room. Fast Wi-Fi, snacks (sweets, crisps etc) and all mini-bar soft drinks are included in the rate - a nice touch and takes away the feeling of being ripped off or worried about using the facilities. We were upgraded too - from a superior to a deluxe - not quite sure why :-).
The room itself was -th floor facing North Moore St. Big comfy bed, soft pillows (harder ones were provided on request), plenty of space, deep bath, big telly, robes and an extra door to keep corridor noise out. I can't emphasise how quiet this hotel was. House keeping were ultra discreet and never seen (in fact we saw them actually hiding at one point!).
A DVD player and movies were available, the pool was breath taking, the breakfast was delicious and room service was excellent with orders arriving within minutes for easy things and on time for larger orders.
Location is great if you like the quiet side of New York. Tribeca is like a different country compared to Time Square etc.
The photo's on the site don't overstate what you get - lovely design and all really comfy and cosy.
The only downsides are (and these are aimed at hotel management really as quite picky)...
- With the room being hard to leave it would be nice to have tea making facilities
- The restaurant temperature was either really cold (to the point of having to wear a coat on two occasions) to really stuffy
- Soft close toilet seats - every hotel needs em!
All round top class and will go again.

We stayed here over the Memorial Day Weekend. We picked the Resident Inn becaue we were traveling with - teenagers. We used a combination of points and paying. We were upgraded to a two bedroom suite, which is perfect with kids. The room was ok, nothing fancy, but clean and lots of room. We were on the top floor, nothing special about the view, and elevators ran fast.
Breafast is always a nice touch, I did not find it crowded as I am an early riser. There was always a place to sit. We went to Sea World one day.....very easy to get to, go early as it does get crowded but we were able to ride everything and see all the shows with no problems.
Tubing on the Guadalupe another day, about a -- minute drive, but so worth it. I forgot how much fun it its. Lots of drunk people so not for the very young.
Short walk to the river walk and mall. I found it easier to stay up on the street to get to some locations to eat like the Hard Rock, but a stroll along the river walk on the way back is nice.
Also took the trolley to a Mexican Restaurant in the Market Area, worked out perfect as did not have to worry about drinking margaritas and driving.
The dance club next door did have some of the most interesting characters......kinda fun to people watch as some of the outfits they were wearing were rather flimsey. It did make me uncomfortable when my teenagers were walking alone back from the riverwalk. I made sure they called and I went out to watch for them....thus the people watching.
Overall a great location, management very helpful.

I’m giving only - stars because it’s not a five star experience, but I would definitely stay here again and have no real complaints about the hotel. The location is terrific and the staff friendly. It’s in a quiet, mainly residential area a couple of blocks from UCLA. The botanical garden is only a block away. Across the street from the hotel is fabulous and expensive W Hotel. Within a short walking distance, there are restaurants, shops, and movies. ALSO free parking! That’s a rare thing in L.A.
The Hilgard House is a older hotel. It seems to me that it may have been built in the ---- or possibly a bit earlier. I read a review saying it was similar to some old, small European hotel, and I agree with that assessment. There is a lot of dark wood veneer that is a bit shabby. The rooms have been updated but they are not completely modern. This is both good and bad. The room I was in had a window seat and a view onto the grounds of the church next door. The view was green and very pretty. However, the outside of the windows were dusty and that spoiled the view a little. 
The room decor could use some updating with a new bedspread and furniture. However, the bed was comfortable, and the pillows were too — not too soft and not too hard. The TV looked great. It’s a wall mounted flat screen. I didn’t watch it, but it looked as if it would be nice.
The bathroom is small and has a low shower head. I’m -’-” and it was low for me. The tub appeared to be new and it was a spacious oval shape. There are double sinks so someone could be outside the bathroom and still be getting ready. There was also a refrigerator in the foyer area of the room. 
So, to sum it up, the hotel is not “luxe,” but it is in and near a “luxe” and “deluxe” area of L.A. Everything is very convenient. I was visiting the Getty Museum, and it was an easy -- or -- minute drive away. 
I do need to add that I visited during a university holiday, so the area may be busier with traffic when school is in session. As it was, I could sleep with the window open and not be disturbed by the noise. That’s a rare thing for me in a city like Los Angeles.

I was nervous when booking here because of all the complaints about construction but I went ahead and booked because of location. What a great surprise to find the construction is mostly complete. The area it's in has some great litte local restaurants within a couple of blocks. You have to try the Flying Fish. The experience was great starting with the valets to checking in and everyone bending over backward to make sure everything is great. I can't think of anything that could have been better. We don't usually stay in hotel for the bars or the restaurants so those not being open yet wasn't a big deal especially with all the great places to eat in Dallas. The rooms were overly nice. Not just another Hilton property. Great decor, Bathroom amenities desk area and TV's. 
Are you getting the picture stay here and enjoy.

I am just back from three nights at The Carlton on Madison. I was disappointed in the hotel given the many very positive reviews on this site. Other than the beautiful lobby, the excellent Country restaurant and a reasonably good location, I thought the hotel was average at best and there were certainly some below average features which I have listed below. All of the staff that I interacted with were very pleasant.
-) The rooms and bathrooms are very small - yes, even for NY. The bathroom door cleared the sink by a millimeter at most. The shower curtain (as another reviewer noted) had an industrial look and had noticelable mold on it. The closet was small enough that the hangers did not hang in it properly - they bumped into the back wall and had to be turned at an angle. I was alone and that made the size workable but I would hesitate to recommend it for two people.
-) The free Wi-FI was a case of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""you get what you pay for"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". My signal fluctuated between """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Low"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Very Low"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and was essentially useless most of the time.
-) My -th floor room which was on the north (the --th Street) side of the building was very loud at night and there is construction going on immediately across the street (they start at -:-- AM). They sold this to me as an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Empire State Building view"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" at check-in (but did not mention the construction), and from the right angle, there was a view of the ESB. 
-) Although I had booked a non-smoking room, the room smelled heavily of smoke upon check in.
-) For a recently remodeled hotel, the room carpet looked worn and dirty. There was also a stain on my desk chair. The comforter was nice enough but the sheets were of very low quality for a hotel charging these kinds of rates.
-) The room safe was inoperable the duration of my stay.
-) This is one of those hotels where you have to call room service to get ice.
Overall, I didn't think the hotel was terrible but I can't see staying here again when there are so many other alternatives at this price point.

Stayed here during a quick business trip to San Antonio. I found this Courtyard to be a step down from the normal Courtyard. It does have free parking, which makes getting in and out easier than around the Riverwalk. But there just isn't anything special about this place. It obviously wasn't originally a Marriott and shows signs of aging. The bathroom needs to be redone. The tub is older, and the caulking is coming off. The bed was a bit uncomfortable. The mattress was on its last legs and needs to be replaced. I didn't sleep well either night. There is a small sofa in the room, which is nice, but it really needs to be replaced. There were major tears in the fabric, and much of the fabric has been worn off at the corners. It is stained and is not a good impression of Courtyard's normal quality. As for housekeeping, the room was clean; however, there were two empty beer bottles left outside the room when I checked in. They were still there when I checked out. I was working from my room one of the days, and despite the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""privacy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sign on the door, a housekeeper used her key and let herself in without knocking. Thankfully I was just working at the desk and was fully clothed! I need to be in San Antonio at least once a year. I will not be back to this hotel.

My husband and I stayed here for - nights in mid-November. The hotel has a very cool decor and is brilliantly located right in the heart of the meatpacking district, short walk to the high line, Chelsea market and multiple subways. The service was very friendly and went beyond the call every chance they could. However if you are looking for a quiet place this might not be the place for you. Dont be surprised if you come down from your room on a Saturday night and discover that the lobby has turned into a club with a long line out the door. That said the noise level did not reach the room at all.

I spent - nights at Hotel Frank. The first night, was fine until I got up in the morning to use the bathroom. It smelled HORRIBLE. It was overwhelming. A smell that it's impossible anyone else could have missed. I spoke to the front desk and they were able to move me to another room, however expressed zero concern with fixing the smell. The second room didn't included the fragrant bathroom. 
Overall the rooms are clean and kept up. The facilities in general had a very dated feel. I was traveling for business and there were limited options in the location I needed, so I stayed. Not sure I would return to the Hotel Frank for a second visit.

I had a very good experience at this hotel. Avez in the front office was very helpful. My - sisters and I traveled all night from Los Angeles to San Jose for my nephews graduation and were desperate to get some rest, since we had to drive back to Santa Cruz. Avez made it possible to get our room ready earlier than regular check in time. We were very pleased with the room. It was spacious and clean. Also, its close to the freeway, which is always nice. The price was not too bad, considering what other hotels around the area were charging. I would definately recommend this hotel.

Considering the prices of hotels in DC, the Georgetown Holiday Inn is a bargain! Walking distance to all of Georgetown (down hill from the hotel, catch the $- Circulator bus to come back up!), it's perfectly located. Very helpful front desk staff, very nice rooms (nothing fancy but nothing negative), good housekeeping, and plenty of bargain priced in and out parking make the Holiday Inn a good value. Even though the bar closes too early, the restaurant was fine for breakfast and we even had a brush with fame...meeting a Presidential candidate! All in all, a good deal!

Could not say enough good things about my stay. The bed was very comfortable, linens were soft and top quality. The personal assistants were very helpful, informative and friendly. Service was top notch, rooms were amazing, Food was excellent. I highly recommend this hotel if you are big in receiving the best service your money could buy.
