It took us to Space Needle-Chihuly Garden of Glass, and EMP Museum. We probably didn't need to rent the car at the airport while we were there but at the end of our stay when we proceeded to Portland, OR. There was an Avis Car Rental a block away. The wireless internet worked fine. The only complaint is the bathroom. It is an old hotel. The toilet is so close to the wall that the toilet paper holder was under my armpit!!! The towel rack was on the back wall above the bathtub, so there was no where to hang your towel. I hung my hand towel over the make-up mirror. My hubby just left his on the edge of the sink. We just left the bath towels on the floor. There was a wall where they could have put a towel rack. 
The weather was both rainy and sunny. The temperature was in the --s. We could change the temperature in the room but couldn't turn off the fan. It was high, low, or automatic. It kept turning on and off through the night which kept waking me up.
When we checked out, the front desk person said no incidentals and gave us our bill in an envelope. I just assumed it was correct. After we left I checked the statement. It seemed higher than what I thought. When we reached our next hotel, I checked the confirmation email. I was charged $-- more per night. When we returned home, I scanned the statement and attached it to the confirmation email and sent it to Craig of the Mayflower Hotel. He responded the same day adjusting our bill and advising I will be receiving a credit for the difference. I will have to check my account in a few days.
All in all, it is a very nice hotel and would stay there again.

My boyfriend and I stayed downtown at the Moore Hotel (just up the street from the market!) for two nights while we visited Seattle. Many eating and shopping opportunities around, and very central to many attractions in area. Affordable room rates, GREAT customer service, and inexpensive parking- the hotel gives you a voucher to park in a garage just down the block, $-- for -- hours. We checked out but were planning to stay in the area for a couple hours and didn't want to move our car from the garage or put our belongings in the car. I called the front desk and before I could finish my question the lady said they had a large storage area and that we could leave our luggage there the whole day if we wanted! So we left our car in the garage and only had to pay -- for half a day of parking downtown (as opposed to parking in a lot close to the market which would cost $--+!). I really liked the front desk attendents, very polite and wanting to accommodate our needs. Our room was clean and comfy. It was actually very nice for an older hotel. You can't beat the price, location, and charm of the Moore!

Actually stayed in April but option not there. Great place, love the service, the easy am coffee and newspaper the balcony rooms are super but not on Friday and Saturday night and they warn you. Unless you are into club scene ask for a quiet room

Stayed here for one night on business. The location was great, close to convention center, nightlife, and dining.
Beautiful hotel with high ceilings, exposed beams, cherry cabinets, and stainless appliances. All for a price that was less than many surrounding hotels. Would definately stay here again.

Yes, we were right in the heart of busy Time Square. It was easy to walk to various sights & to take the Hop on Hop Off Bus that was available at the corner of our hotel. There were several theatres next door & near by this hotel.
The Marriott itself was beautiful & clean. The helpful staff made our - night stay very enjoyable. As suggested by others on this Tripadvisor site, we ask for an upper floor room overlooking Time Square. It was quiet & large. I have to sing the praises of this Marriott --- we could not have had a better stay !

Nice layout, clean, comfortable, good room sizes, good locale, affordable. Went in the winter, so some parts were quite cold, including the breakfast area, and the wind was heard howling throughout the building. Staff were courteous and easily helped us move rooms when we wanted to be adjacent to our friends.

Worst 'English Breakfast' I've ever had- think it had been left on the side for a day. Lady who served was quite abrupt and made me split my table of - whilst waiting for my other - colleagues to join me, for imaginary waiting people who never showed. 
Service overall - the bar-serving staff were moody and blunt, reception staff were great. 
Room was ok, however I noticed stains on the outer cover. Slept in one day and the maids never came back- room remained uncleaned- never experienced that before.
Location was good- quiet, away from the tourists and a short walk to Soho. 
White noise in the rooms threw me at first- a simple explanation when checking-in would be nice, instead of me having to call back down and ask what it was.
And last bear bug- a host of great draught beers on the bar menu- oh wait, none available.
Not normally a massive moaner on here but this hotel disappointed 
more than impressed

I have just arrived home this morning from washington dc. The capitol hill suites are ok. The staff are very good. We arrived Saturday to be told that the heating was not working. The reason they gave was that it wasnt cold for -- days in a row. Yep we were surprised too. It was very cold outside. Anyway we were lucky we got a space heater for our stay. But there were alot of very upset guests wanting the heaters. In the end alot of them moved to the holiday in. We were travelling with a person in a wheel chair. I would say dont stay here if u dont like being push up capitol hill everyday, its a steep hill. Free breakfast was good. Big problem for us was lack of shops. No big supermarkets and record stores in the area that we couldnt fine.

I stayed at several hotels during this visit to Phoenix and I found that the Holiday Inn Airport North was a very pleasant hotel to stay in. The staff was helpful and pleasant to deal with. The hotel room, which was a suite with a kitchen, was very modern, clean and comfortable. The pool was very clean and a great area to relax. The pool is located in a courtyard and the hotel is a four story complex that looks onto the pool. My only negative comment is that when relaxing in the pool area, you can hear the housecleaning and maintenance staff yelling at each other in the hallways-walkways that overlook the pool.

This is a typical hotel designed for people who talk about the vibe of a hotel rather than its comfort or pleasantness. The staff is right in line with this philosophy: nice, friendly people who don't really know how to work in a hotel. The bartender forgot about my order then got it wrong. When you walk into the room your first challenge is to find the lights because there aren't any switches near the doors. You have to go to each individual fixture and figure out how to turn it on. The bathroom doors require constant movement to gain access to the toilet or the sink. The drapes don't close all the way. I would at least expect a place that caters to undiscriminating hipsters to facilitate the charging of electronic devices but this place is no better than your usual hotel in that regard. The plugs are inconveniently placed behind the bed or by the sink. On the plus side it is clean.

I don't have tons to say about this hotel, as we were there for only -- hours or so... but we loved everything we saw.
the hotel is very beautiful and chic. decor is top notch. and the staff are exceedingly helpful and friendly.
the room we stayed in was a large corner suite with a view of the city and partial view of the water. 
the bed was one of the nicest i've ever slept in, complete with a pillow menu.
really nice spa quality shampoo, conditioner, lotion and face wash in the bathrooms.
the only """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""issues"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" we encountered was our room being a bit delayed for check in. we were sent to the hotel bar with a $-- gift certificate to kill the time. very nice gesture, however the bar is VERY expensive, so that only bought two drinks. the next day when we checked out, they comp'd our valet parking as well for our inconvenience. that was great since valet was $-- a day (yikes)
we would for sure stay here again, but it's not for people watching their pennies. it's a splurge, but worth it for a nice night away.

We celebrated our anniversary with a three night stay in a lovely, spacious and well-appointed suite at The London NYC. We knew from the moment we walked in the door that we had made a great choice. The entire staff was so kind, helpful and professional, and the accommodations couldn't have been better. Though we travel to NYC often for theater, this was our first stay at this hotel. It's perfectly located for most of the Broadway theaters and pre-theater restaurants, so I'm sure it will not be our last. And I'll definitely be recommending it to friends and family, for whom I seem to be the go-to person for all sorts of information about New York.

We stayed in several hotels during our vacation in California and the Pacific Terrace was our favourite! Everything was perfect! The rooms, the view, the location and the staff. Our only quibble would be the complimentary breakfast. We disliked the cramped breakfast room and also how the breakfast was served. At any other hotel you are free to help yourself but here, you have to ask for each item (bagel, muffin etc.) You are allowed one choice along with cereal, fruit and yogurt. It was just o.k. You can purchase a regular breakfast but the price was exhorbitant. We enjoyed our stay so much that I am hesitant to complain about this, but this is the only hotel where we didn't enjoy the breakfast routine and would prefer eating breakfast elsewhere.

We booked through hotwire - as a - star hotel in Japan town. When we first arrived we got a smoking room accessed outside, - star motel room. Travelling with a young child, we insisted on a non smoking room. They couldn't accommodate as the hotel is full - but provided a air purifier. The next day, I requested again for a non smoking room, and luck was with us, we were upgraded to a non smoking suite. It is fantastic. 
The lesson learnt re Opal 
- they have different standard rooms depending on your luck - the suite is fantastic, but the other room is shocking.
- don't book through hotwire for Opal rooms as you will get a cheap, budget, - star room.
Convenient location, you can basically walk to anywhere in downtown. Had breakfast on the second floor, excellent service and the food is great.

This was my second time staying at this hotel. Very close to Comcast, IBC and other businesses. The rooms are large and each contain a fridge, microwave and sink. Just like any other embassy suites. Room overlooked the museums and was a nice contrast to overlooking the - seasons on the other side. Room service can be a little spotty. They are serviced by TGI Fridays which is attached to the hotel. tried calling for about -- minutes but never got an answer. Finally just sucked it up and went down to eat. There are a few other places nearby to eat but it was freezing and it was late. My only other complaint is the low shower head. Head only came to my chest and i had to duck to get complete shower. Will go back.

As always the stay here at the Arboretum location was great. We choose Hyatt Place for our travels due to the price, modern style, and great with a little one. The pool area was great, no towels though so bring yours down from the room. This hotel location was different from others with a walk in shower rather than a tub which we liked even more. We managed to get this hotel for $-- with tax on Priceline so that made this deal even better. 
Located Nearby
-. The Domain for upscale shopping
-. Amy's Ice Cream for the best dessert in Austin 
-. The Arboretum Shops
-. Just a couple of miles down the road great hiking
-. Right by --- and MoPac so easy on and off

Hotel Zaza is a fun centralized hot spot however I didn't expect the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""patrolling"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" when hotel staff came to our rooms. I'm assuming that due to their strict """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""No outside alcohol"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" rule, they are paid to inspect rooms and poke their heads into ajoining rooms in order to discover """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""non-zaza"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" alcohol . This made my guests and I very uncomfortable! We would order room service and instead of place the food where asked they would poke their heads into ajoining rooms and instead of looking at you they scope the room. In addition, we were bumped from our semi-private dinner area because someone with more money decided to go to Dragon Fly for dinner. After complaining management comp'd a few things like dessert and class of wine however for what you pay to stay here, I would have expected to be treated as a GUEST and not a a student in a dorm!

I really enjoyed my stay at Monticello. Rooms were clean, staff extremely courteous and excellent service. If visiting DC do not hesitate to chose this hotel.
Jenny
I enjoyed my stay at this hotel - Haile, the doorman, was a special treat!

My husband and I just got back from a trip to Scottsdale and we stayed at one location for the first few night of our trip because it was a time share as was free to us, but it did not cover our whole trip so we stayed at the Royal Palms Resort and had the best time! It was so romantic and they thought of every detail. We had turn down service and had Champaign; Chocolate covered strawberries and rose petals laid on the bed shaped in a heart. The staff was helpful and even got us in our room early! The pool was great we were in a cabana and was so relaxing looking up at the mountain. We would go back in a heartbeat, what a great way to renew your relationship!

We have absolutely no complaints about this hotel. After a rather chilly walk from the subway to the hotel we arrived to a beautiful, modern lobby and were greeted by very friendly and professional staff. When we got to our room it was chic, pristine and quite spacious, especially for such a central location. The bed was luxuriously comfortable and the mod cons left us wanting for nothing.
The complimentary breakfast was great with a selection of bagels, cereal, fruit, bread, pastries, eggs, ham and cheese. All you need really. Their main restaurant isn't open for dinner but you won't be struggling for food in NYC!
The rooftop bar is a bonus and provides excellent views towards the Empire State Building, especially at night. There is also what looks to be a very nice fitness centre but we were too busy eating and exploring to make use of it!
Overall I cannot fault this hotel and highly recommend as a reasonably priced but stylish base in midtown Manhatten.

We just returned on Monday from New York. We had a great time. We paid a bit more for a King Size room with City view - it was so worth it! Our view had been that we would not be in the room much but it was worth it to wake up and go to sleep everynight viewing the landscape and Emplire State Building.
Breakfast was included which was great and the staff could not do more to help us.
I agree with others about the lift but would equaly say that there is nothing they can do about this - it is a towe block with three other hotels and we never had to wait more than - minutes.
The hotel was very central and if you have been out for a long day there is a little restaurant and bar across the road that does great food and cocktails.

One staff member was really nice. Our vehicle was broken into on the premises and the hotel is saying they are not resposible for the damages. The main company has told me they are not responsible for personal property being stolen out of a car in the parking lot, but how do you take out a radio and GPS out of your vehicle. I will never stay there again.

This is a standard Hilton property. It is next to the Austin Convention Center so it was fully booked during my stay. Weekends seemed to be full of tourists. My only complaint was that the hotel was so full, that if you tried to get on the elevator at the wrong time, you could wait -- minutes for a car. It is a typical downtown hotel, so parking was expensive, but I found that my company negotiated very reasonable room rates, so that made up for the parking. The hotel seems to be recently remodeled. The only flaw with our room was that a previous customer broke into the mini bar, not really a problem. Plenty of good restaraunts within walking distance, so we didn't bother with room service. The fitness facility was very good, but was an extra $-.-- charge.

I stayed with a group of women for a Girls' Weekend. We had - rooms booked through a deal prepaid on a travel website. We were a little upset that we did not get adjoining rooms as requested, but the hotel was very accomodating to get us as close together as possible. We checked in and within -- mins, the people in the room between us complained to security about how """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""loud"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" we were (it was -pm on a Thursday). So we went down to the front desk and explained the situation, and they not only happily moved our rooms, but upgraded us to higher floor and larger rooms.
PROS
Excellent location. Easy walk to Central Park, Times Square, Shopping on -th Ave, Rockerfeller Center.
Bar service was friendly and fast. Try the Long Island Mojito at the lobby bar. And complimentary yummy chips that the waiter kept refilling.
Our -nd room was spacious (corner) with a great view. Beds were comfy.
Starbucks in the hotel was nice, although there is nearly one on every corner anyway!
CONS
Bathrooms in every room were TINY. Hardly any counter space.
Elevators were a little slow. Not horribly. But a little.
Starbucks employees (inside the hotel) were grouchy & rude.
WIFI not free...nor was it cheap.
Note: We did not use the workout facilities or eat at the hotel since we were out and about a lot so I cannot comment on those.
OVERALL - I'd stay there again in a heartbeat. It was a great stay.
I'll review the restaurants we ate at separately, but here they are in summary:
The Eatery, Tao, Otto's Pizzeria & Enoteca. We also did the Today Show (Kenny Chesney concert) and it was really worth getting up at -am. You do need to be there before -am if you want a view, but if you don't, they also film from the back platform, so we got on TV anyway :)

We loved the luxurious and centrally-located Hyatt at Olive -. As the first LEED certified hotel in Seattle, Olive - offers chic, modern rooms with iPod docking stations, an indoor-pool and eco-friendly spa and restaurant. We highly recommend this property! arrivalstravel.com

Well I stayed in this hotel and my mother, Elizabeth Whitman clogged the toilet. It was about -- inches and very circumstantial. We did not get a plunger up to our room for - hours and the whole room smelled like rotten eggs. But nice hotel definitely come

I loved my stay. The staff was friendly and swift. The room was quite small but well designed. I wished there was more variety for breakfast, but there is a supermarket across the street. The terrasse is superb (in summer). 
A great place for couples who wants to be in a hip place!
The rooms are clean (changing sheets and towel daily) but the commons spaces would need more attention (washrooms, common kitchens on each floor).

I was disappointed. Tile in bath was dirty looked like it hadn't been cleaned in a long time. Grout in the bath is really dry and cracks are in it everywhere. Room smelled really musty. Insulation in room isn't good at all and you can hear people above you and outside really well even with the air on. Corners are cut everywhere to save cost. water seemed really hard they provide you with a very small shampoo-condition combination but that doesn't do anything for long hair that tangles in wash with hard water. So no conditioner to really help reduce tangles. Coffee in the room they only provide you with - small packet of creamer and - small packet of sugar. Only two towels were provided in room. You can ask for more and it will be provided. Breakfast wasn't up to other La Quinta standards. Just not use to asking for everything that should already be provided. Extra creamer and sugar request ok i can understand that but the room should be equiped with enough for two people. in a double room towels should accommodate - people without having to request. Shampoo should be enough for two people without having to request more. I have never stayed in a room La Quinta or other hotel that didn't have conditioner. I will not visit this La Quinta again. Pool area was clean.

Stayed here with some friends for Columbis Day weekend. Found this to be a cheaper alternative to staying in Midtown. Hotel was very nice, room was a bit larger than average because we had two double beds, found room to be very clean. We walked the few blocks to Little Italy each night, and being three woman we felt very safe. 
My only complaint was the hotel restaurant, we did eat breakfast there on the day we checked out. The service was horrible as was the food, not at all what the menu described it to be. 
However, I would definitely stay here again, but only as an alternative to Midtown simply due tot he long cab rides and traffic.

Not only was it the typical W experience (which is always good), I left my iPod at the pool, it was turned in, and they were able to send it to me. THAT wouldn't happen at most hotels!! Way to go the extra mile for a good customer. THANKS!

Travelling to Washington DC in weekends is always better for tourists as the room rates are drastically lower than during weekdays.
What you see is what you get. A good Hotel on a good location, close to China Town and the Convention Center. 
The Rooms where spacious and very clean. We only stayed for two nights, and did not make use of Room service. So we are not able to comment on that.
The complimentary breakfast came with a wide arrangement of choices and it all tasted as it should. All in all a good place to stay.

This hotel was just ok, but the price was right for a Manhattan hotel. The rooms are tiny as at least one other reviewer noted, but most rooms in Manhattan are. The size wasn't much different from other Manhattan hotels I've stayed at.
The neighborhood is very quiet. There are a couple of delis and restaurants nearby for breakfast and late night snacks so that was good.
The hotel staff were very friendly and accommodating and maid service was also exceptional. We had a problem with our window closing and maintenance promptly arrived to handle the problem. 
Two main subway lines have stops just two blocks from the hotel- one on sixth and one on seventh. From these two lines we could easily get just about anywhere in the city, which is why we stayed here.
It's definitely an ok place to stay, but not party central or some place you would want to hang out. It's a good place to rest your head and shower and then spend the day out exploring the city.
There is a restaurant-nightclub behind the lobby, but it was very quiet when we were there. Free coffee in the lobby in the morning is a plus.

Super-comfy bed with luxurious bedding, very clean & quiet room. Attentive staff, always smiling and ready to help. Great bathroom with all the amenities. Classy hotel in a great location. We'll be back!

We went to New York to get married and booked to stay here for - nights. What can I say?!! This has got to be the worst hotel I have ever stayed in (and I have stayed in some crumby ones in Europe)
The 'suite' had old interiors with an old air con system, the view was into the other hotel rooms (we didnt see day light), we asked if we could have a room with a view and we told we could only that room would be tiny!
This place is probably ok if you are over with a gang of friends who just want somewhere to lay your head, but for us, it was horrible. We wanted something to enjoy and relax in and this wasnt it. The staff are rude, the lifts are slow and the rooms are so clastrophobic that you cant relax in them.

My family and I stayed at this hotel over the Memorial Day weekend. Overall, we were very pleased. Hotel staff was pleasant, room was ready when we arrived and we had no problems with any type of noise. The room was very nice, beds were really comfortable and the pool and fitness center were also very enjoyable. It was close to the sights and we had a great weekend. I would definitely stay here again.

From the minute we arrive in the Valet Parking area, we are always greeted as though we are part of a family. Actually, my family doesn't greet me as spontaneously as these folks do ...but I digress. Upon registering the family inclusion continues, with check-in being exceptionally smooth.
The front desk staff is ALWAYS amazingly accommodating and the concierge is VERY knowledgeable about """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""goings on"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" around town and always knows the best places to suggest for entertainment, shopping or """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""just being a tourist.""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""
The waitstaff in the Cork Bar and Las Rambulas are among the most efficient and courteous I have ever seen (and Texas is KNOWN for its generous hospitality). The food is prepared to perfection and the bar tenders REALLY KNOW what they are doing, able to prepare even the most exotic drinks you can imagine.
The rooms are exceedingly comfortable and livable ... spacious, clean, sanitized and inviting. If you are fortunate to have a lower floor (-rd or -th floor) River View Room, the sights and sounds are exciting and beautiful. But, of course, it is set up for ultimate, intimate privacy.
Finally, some of the most inviting, comfortable and soothing aspects of The Hotel are the Spa, Swimming Pool, Hot Tub and Exercise facilities. Clean, modern, up-to-date equipment for exercise and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Spic and Span"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" cleanliness of the entire area are hallmarks of this hotel.
If we sound like travel agents or part owners of the facility WE ARE NOT! But we'd be proud to be. When we say that this is our Downtown San Antonio Home, we mean it. We have stayed at MANY of the boutique hotels in the downtown area. Although many of them are nice, THIS ONE STANDS HEAD AND SHOULDERS ABOVE THE REST. It will remain our downtown San Antonio home for years to come. Come on down! You'll be impressed!

We stayed at the LAAC Hotel during our wedding weekend; we got married around the corner at Cicada Restaurant. Elegant hotel-club with lots of history, cool vibes and pleasant atmosphere.
It's not the Biltmore, but for many reasons this is a good thing. While Biltmore has beautiful common areas, their rooms are disappointing. LAAC Hotel has a very unassuming lobby, but rooms have a lot of character and -rd floor dining room and bar are very cool and make for great wedding pictures (so does their rooftop terrace). They offer excellent breakfast (included in your room charge) and VERY reasonably priced rooms. 
I booked my rooms with Teri and she was very prompt and accommodating, allowing us to check out a couple of different suites before we booked our bridal suite. Each suite has a different theme and some have larger bedroom, but smaller sitting room and others - larger sitting room and smaller bedroom. We chose the Social Suite, where Charlie Chaplin used to stay... so said the caption under his portrait:)
We booked - rooms at the hotel and all rooms were very nice. Our suite was beautiful and roomy, enough to accommodate - people I had there while getting ready on my wedding day. The room my husband's parent stayed at was also roomy and very nice. If I could change anything about the rooms... that would be the bathrooms. They are clean but VERY plain. Just feels odd, since the rooms are so nice.
Hotel staff was nice and accommodating. Overall, we really enjoyed our stay and would definitely come back.
As far as the area goes... it's Downtown LA. If you live in the city, you know there are scores of homeless people on the streets and in the adjacent Pershing Square. During day time it's no big deal, LA homeless are not aggressive. But at night time it could be a bit uncomfortable, especially if you are travelling alone.
Even though the hotel occupies top - floors (-----), you still hear quite a bit of street noise... could be an issue if you plan to sleep in; buses get going early and often on weekends.
$-- self-parking in the garage off Olive Street is a good deal for Downtown LA. No valet parking. Great health club facilities, which I believe you get full access to if you stay there. Make sure to check out -th floor swimming pool, the first suspended pool in Los Angeles. Also the pool where Don Draper (Mad Men) swam in season four's """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The Summer Man"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""":)

We were greeted by friendly attendants even late in the evening. The room was not terribly stylist - out of date, but quite clean. The bathroom was very nice, big tub - we did wish they had provided some soaps-shampoos seeing as we were out, but we had a really enjoyable bath. We stayed just for the night to be closer to BART in the morning to get to the airport. This is a very convenient location - BART (and Starbucks) are right around the corner.

I was told by a former resident that San Antonio is the easiest large city to get around in by interstate. Well, I am here to tell you, we looped many times because of missed turns and we did not find SA easy to traverse!!! Pleasant stay at the HIE near SeaWorld. Staff friendly, courteous, and helpful. We stayed at the HIE near SeaWorld because of its high ratings. The downtown area HIE hotels (where we intended to do most of our sightseeing) were not rated well. This one did live up to its rating. Ate at the Saltgrass Restaurant which was walking distance across the parking lot from the HIE (excellent food and servers). As an aside, Shamu greets you at the elevator doors! Highly recommend this HIE! If you plan to visit the Alamo and are traveling by car, there is a nice parking facility behind the Crockett Hotel which allows for daily parking for those who are not staying at the Menger or Crockett. It costs $--, but was convenient to the Alamo and River Walk, and was a safe place to park. The attendant told us a little secret. If you park fairly close to the Crockett, the afternoon sun will be blocked by the hotel and your car will be a little cooler in the ---+ degree summer heat.

I can highly recommend the Donatello, from the minute i walked in the door, the Front desk managed to find me a room at -am because i was not feeling the best, they went out of their way every day to ask how i was and to ensure that I was comfortable. The overall Service was excellent, the rooms were very comfortable, clean and housekeeping was more than efficient.The Location is excellent especially for a solo traveller.
The complimentary Tea and Coffee in the club lounge was great to come back to from a busy day in San Fran and the Internet is complementary another bonus.

As one who is on the road at least -- weeks each year, staying at an historic hotel like the Palmer House is a real treat. I was traveling with three couples. We were looking for a good location and room for all of us without being cramped. We shared two rooms on the Executive Level and enjoyed all the amenities! Each room had two double beds, two closets, and TWO BATHROOMS! It was wonderful sharing space (two lovely chairs, too) and having a modicum of privacy as well. Our traveling companions had a touch better room with a small sofa that was ideal. The breakfast each morning was excellent. There were European items (meats and cheeses) along with yogurt, granola, toppings for your yogurt, and pastries. The evening cocktail hour was pricey on drinks but the food was superb. Between the two nights, we had pierogi, wings, ravioli, and other items that made for a full meal if you wanted it to be. Soft drinks were included. The location was ideal for the Art Institute (-.- blocks away) and the park, Michigan Avenue, and State Street. It’s also ideal for commuting from the rail station (via bus) or the two airports (via the “L”). All transportation drops you off right at the hotel! What a wonderful place!

The drive from Denver International Airport is easy - important if you are new to driving in the USA. The lobby is welcoming and elegant - loved the Bonsai tree! Breakfast was excellent and the staff helpful and friendly - so I forgave them no whitener on the coffee tray and a remote control that didn't work.

I expected a - star hotel and what I got was a - star lobby and a - star room. Needless to say, I was very disappointed. 
The lobby and public areas were very nice and a couple of rooms I peeked into while they were being cleaned looked nice too. But my room (---) was horrible. On the headboard, there was a very sharp screw sticking out where the façade had broken off. The bathtub was stained. The ceiling in the bathroom was peeling all over. There was a chunk of wood broken off of the bedside table. The dresser pulls were missing so you couldn’t open many of the drawers. We stayed at the Palmer House Hilton while in town to meet up with friends from Los Angeles for a Cubs vs. Red Sox baseball game. Since hotel rooms were hard to come by and we had seen The Palmer House recently featured on the Travel Channel series “Great Hotels” we felt fairly confident about booking a reservation. We read the TripAdvisor comments mentioning Hilton HHonors members may have a good chance to get the best rooms so we made sure to check in at the HHonors desk. After waiting for what seemed like an eternity for a woman with some sort of fruit punch drink to go through a laundry list of dazed and confused questions which included wanting to know if each and every one of her friends had checked in yet, it was our turn. My husband mentioned he was a Silver level rewards member and inquired as to the possibility of a room upgrade. Supremely annoyed, the front desk girl scanned her computer screen and informed us that since we had booked through Expedia there would be no upgrade for us. I immediately had flashbacks to the Seinfeld “soup nazi” episode - NO SOUP FOR YOU! She then tersely added, “You have a great room”. Turns out Hilton has a very unique definition of GREAT. Apparently a “great room” is one the size of a closet that was last updated perhaps when the Brady Bunch was a hot TV show? A great room also includes a spectacular view of a brick wall, banging wall pipes that give off some kind of random, maniacal Morse code at any given hour and you get the pleasure of listening to your neighbors debate the current state of their marriage because the walls are about as thick as paper mache. And the Great Room piece de resistance – you get your very own, I guess you could call it a “room pet” – a petrified giant dead moth hanging out in our bathroom light fixture. We really appreciated a bathroom so clean dead bugs decided to make it their final resting place. The place is not all gloom and doom though. What others have written about the magnificent lobby – it’s totally true - it is beautiful and definitely something to take in and see. From what we experienced during our stay, just make sure you do not book your room through expedia unless you want to experience one of the very special “great rooms” and better yet, do everything possible to sleep in the lobby because it is, without a doubt, the best part of the hotel.

The hotel itself was very well maintained - good elevators, clean public spaces, very attentive staff. We checked in early, and after we asked about a place to grab a glass of wine with lunch, the concierge offered us free wine at the hotel restaurant (in lieu of the wine service they offer in the evenings). 
The room was very well insulated and in general noise wasn't a problem, except the last night we were there (labor day) when the irish pub behind the hotel played loud, raucous music into the wee hours... To their credit, the hotel offered us a room discount when we mentioned the problem. 
I would highly recommend the hotel itself, but the area of Fisherman's Wharf is a bit of a mixed bag. It looks like every other touristy ocean-front town in America: Ripley's Believe it or Not, a billion gift shops selling the same stuff, a couple ridiculously overpriced art galleries, hordes of tourists who seem to forget the traffic laws once they hit a critical mass, and kamikaze cab drivers honking like mad, trying to get through the masses. If that's your thing, then by all means stay here, or if you're prepared to hit the hotel and then hide out in your room, you'll be fine. If crowds aren't your thing, San Francisco in general might be a bad call, and the wharf in particular. Otherwise, it's a fun place and probably good for families who need to keep the kids entertained and don't mind paying to do so.

I anticipate future business trips to Philadelphia, and I anticipate that I will be staying elsewhere.

My two sisters and I recently stayed at the Wingate for - nights. We were very happy with our stay, and we found the staff to be very friendly and accommodating. Unlike a few of the other reviewers, we thought the staff was very friendly, from the people at the front desk to the sweet little housekeeper polishing the wood in the elevator who greeted us with a smile and told us to enjoy the day.The room was cozy for the three of us (- double beds), but we understand that hotel space in NYC is at a premium, so we were prepared. The decor was updated and appealing, the granite bathroom counter was generously sized for all our stuff, the room and bathroom were clean, and the beds were comfortable. The shower was strong, the water was hot, the towels were thick and fluffy. Even the toilet was an upscale brand--Toto,which is one of the best on the market. The microwave and refrigerator came in quite handy. 
I will admit that the bathroom fan is loud, but it works well, and the room air conditioner is noisy also (many hotel A-Cs are like that). We discovered a curious thing about it --we realized it wasn't just a coincidence that the A-C came on whenever we entered the room after a long day of sightseeing. It shuts off during the day as an energy saving measure, and as soon as a warm body comes back in the room, the A-C starts up again.
 The manager explained that there was an infrared sensor that was responsible for this curiosity. This wasn't a problem (cudos to the hotel for conservation), and we were fascinated by it. The breakfast was good, though I personally didn't care for the scrambled eggs--on the dry side. There were lots of other things to choose from--sausage, bacon, pastries, bagels, waffles, cereals, fresh fruit, yogurt, etc. The location is convenient, and the hotel is easily accessible to several different subway lines (--- blocks away, depending on the line you want.) It is - block from Macy's, and is close to Penn Station and Madison Square Garden.
Now for the downside. The hotel isn't perfect, and if you are looking for a - Star hotel, this isn't it. It is on a dingy side street, and the view from our room was looking at a warehouse- type building. The housekeeping was hit and miss, but this could have been due to our particular housekeeper. On a few occasions, we didn't get fresh mugs and glasses; toiletries weren't replaced during our stay even though the manager said they should have been; and one day, the housekeeper forgot to leave us any towels. We found ourselves calling down for stuff like this more than we should have had to. However, the management and front desk always cheerfully and apologetically took care of the requests, so I can't complain too much. All in all, I rated it a -, mainly because of the good value compared to other NYC hotels.

Enjoyed the bar, but thought the restaurant was a little overrated - though if you sit outside near the sidewalk, you have a great view of the Capitol dome. The West Wing Cafe across the street is great for breakfast and lunch.

Hotel Mela is very good located next to Times Square and Fifth Avenue. Very nice hotel with friendly staff and nice, but not very big rooms (typical for NYC). Hotel would be a very good choice, but there are problems with noise - at the street side due to traffic, at the backside due to air condition, even in higher floors. There are quieter rooms at another side.

Secluded, not much to do at resort. Very spread out and LOTS of walking to get anywhere. If you have mobility issues, very challenging. Our maid service was very poor - had to come back - times in - day. Very few places to eat, but food was VERY good. Grounds were stunningly beautiful!

I stayed for a conference for a few days. The staff was excellent, they never got tired of smiling, the hotel has everything you need and more. Thhe food was excellent especially for banquets, I would go again on leisure

The Blackstone (So. Mich. Ave. @ Balbo next to the Hilton Chicago) has been beautifully rehabbed and updated by Marriott as a Renaissance property. Having stayed there in '-- when it was independently managed, the improvement is impressive indeed. Friends and I booked - separate rooms and all of us were more than satisfied - especially given we had senior rates. Like all the prior reviews I read of the great location and general consensus of hotel-room condition, I do agree. I was okay with everything until walking into the dark bathroom, flipping on the light and seeing a bug scuttle across the counter! I did not sleep well even tho I didn't see any others or evidence of others, but doubt we will stay there again. I recently stayed at the St Gregory over the Columbus Weekend. We visit the area often and like to try different hotels. The St Gregory met all my expectations and more. The - bedroom suite was well decorated ,large and very comfortable. 
The hotel staff was very cordial and helpful. The St Gregory is very close to all the Georgetown shops and restaurants and is within a short walking distance to the Dupont Circle Metro. Had dinner in the hotel restaurant and the food exceeded our expectations. For those visiting the landmarks of DC this hotel is a good find.
We will definitely stay at the St Gregory the next time we return to DC.

off the lobby at the Holiday Inn express, so we know the wi-fi, which is fast and free, is up and running. I just finished a delicious and complimentary breakfast and I'm relaxing with a cup of coffee waiting for my travel companion wake and join me for a day of sight seeing in Houston and the surrounding area. The facility is up to if not exceeding the high standards I'm used to when staying at Holiday Inns. My friend and I enjoyed a evening at Discovery Green and dinner at the Grove last night and had no issues walking the two, maybe two and a half blocks back to the hotel at -:--P.M. Typical large Marriott property. Relatively new with standard Marriott decor. Very convenient to the convention center, the Riverwalk, and the River Center Mall. Friendly staff; clean, modern facility. Good stay for convention or a Riverwalk vacation.

The Morris House Hotel is really a jewel. My husband and I, along with our very best friends take an annual trip together to celebrate our wedding anniversaries. The location was supurb and within walking distance of so many of the wonderful historic sites in Philly. We found the noise level very quiet, even though our room faced a busy street. It never bothered us at all. We had the two rooms available on the third floor and were very pleased. Our only """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""complaint"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" would be the Continental Breakfast. It lacked any variety and offered very little, which was mostly cold pastries and only one kind of cereal and some fruit. Adding something warm, or even the availability of a microwave would be an improvement. The tea and cookies in the afternoon was a wonderful touch. We have traveled throughout the US and this Inn was very comfortable and very clean and we would reccommend it to others.

Good location for fishermans wharf and alcatraz only downside was windows were not double glazed so room noisy at times from traffic, had to pay for internet as well unless you had a laptop or wifi phone. Hotel and rooms were clean and staff very helpful.

nice place if your on vacation maybe, rooms are VERY small, internet is not complimentary, no coffee available in the rooms and the desk area has your back to the TV and windows, I would not recommend for anyone on a business trip. Lobby is on second floor which means tyou have to get in and out of eleveators too many times to naviage the hotel.

My best friend and I hit the road - we wanted to escape from home and visit Chicago! By pure chance we booked our stay here the day of our stay through a referral service - and we were in awe! It was my friends first time in Chicago and my -th time. the location is AMAZING - within walking distance of major attractions and shopping! If you cant walk there you can get on the bus or train and get to it!
 Outstanding service, friendly treatment, clean rooms with a GREAT view! We lucked out and got a room on the corner and fell asleep with the curtain open enjoying the view of downtown Chicago. I would recommend this place to everyone I know!
 There is a pool on the rooftop that is open based on the season. There is a restaurant on the ground and top floors as well.

Older hotel, but it has full kitchen with refrig, stove, microwave, dishes and a few pots-pans. We had - double beds and a sleeper sofa for - people. Bathroom is only accessible through bedroom. Compact room. Bathroom was adequate and robes are provided. Our problem: we had a drunken noisy party beneath us. We called the front desk - times, before anything happened and then it may just have been that the party ended. On the plus side, the pool was nice and the breakfast was generous. Cleaning and maintenance staff were friendly.
Pleasant staff; newer hotel; nice office-work area; clean; safe; work out area; indoor pool; easy parking; nearby gas, eating, shopping; hot breakfast; just a great choice.

We had a wonderful time in San Francisco. The city is truly magnificant! We stayed in a very large suite which was great. The breakfast was wonderful the food generally was superb. The pool was fabulous if not a bit too crowded and it was in the best location possible. It was well decorated especially the dinning room, and the building was very opulant. If you are going to New York City for the first time, this hotel is for you. Ideal location right ON Times Square and less than a block away from Broadway shows. Both our kids enjoyed all the wonderful sites and shopping without having to go far; just next door. Shopping until -am every day. We were on the --th floor and our friends-families came to visit US so they can enjoy the view. Love, love, love this hotel, its location and NYC. Definitely will return soon.

I recently took a solo vacation to San Francisco and stayed at Hotel Carlton. Not knowing anything about the city, I wanted a hotel where I would feel comfortable and could get my questions answered. The concierges were friendly, helpful, and made me feel right at home from the minute I checked in. They told me what areas of the city I should avoid after dark for safety, and offered a ton of information about things to do from standard tourist attractions to off the beaten path activities to hidden coffee shops and breakfast joints. I would ABSOLUTELY recommend the Hotel Carlton to ANYONE visiting San Francisco!!

Stayed at the new Yotel Aug ----. Room was small (as us the norm in NYC) but very well designed - glass bathroom and bed that retracted into a sofa at the touch of a button made the room feel more spacious. Glass wall bathroom with curtain for privacy - only share a room with someone you know well!! Free muffins were good for breakfast. No frills, but very comfortable, clean, nice design. Fast and easy check in-out. Location wasn't amazing but was fine... Nice view from rooms. Would stay again!

The hotel has a great location, right on the boardwalk in Venice, literally -- meters from the beach, and the owner is extremely nice!
The hotel could have been in slightly better shape - in our bathhroom the roof was leaking when the guests upstairs from our room where showering-taking a bath. And I would also have wanted the cleaning lady to have come more than just once during our -- day stay.
But otherwise a very cute hotel!

I slept better at Seaport than any other hotel I've ever stayed at, and I've stayed in some great hotels! First off, the bedding was immaculate, it was feather,which is great except that I'm allergic to feathers. Housekeeping promptly and graciously changed my comforter and pillows to down alternative and also brought the extra coffee I requested. There is a pillow menu, you can chose from a wide selection of pillow types to suit you. We were on the -th floor, overlooking the harbor. The room was well insulated and quiet, however, if you are a light sleeper request a room away from the ice maker; when I went to fill my stainless steel ice bucket it was very loud!

Complaints: I didn't like the toiletries because they were heavily perfumed! There was dirty carpet in the hallway by the elevators and there were no fans in the bathroom. That's it! It's a great hotel and I would stay there again.

Nice clean hotel, nice location. Showing some signs of age but very well kept up. The beds were VERY comfortable - nice and plush comfortors! Excellent breakfast - wide assortment. The only problem was that the heating-cooling system in the pool area was broken and it was a hot and HUMID -- degrees! Couldn't let my daughter swim too long because it was too overwhelming. They were very nice about it and called someone but it couldn't be fixed until the next day and we were gone by then. Very nice and friendly front desk service. We would stay here again.

We stayed here during the Rose Bowl, and it was a great spot for us! The neighborhood around the hotel isn't the best, but it is NOT bad! Plus, it's literally within steps of the subway, which was awesome! The staff was very friendly and breakfast was stocked each morning. Our room was clean and spacious, as was the bathroom. Would definitely recommend!

I stayed here for a conference in January. I really like this hotel. The lobby, restaurant and bar are just beautiful and the staff are excellent. I stay here about four times a year on business and with my wife to take in Orioles games. 
When I arrived in my room I saw that there was an adjoining doors. This is just me, but I do not like adjoining doors. They give me the creeps. Then on my last night I woke up at -.-- am to the sound of a man talking on the phone. At first it sounded as if he were in the room. I heard everything he said as if he were next to me. Needless to say, I could not get back to sleep.
I will stay here again, but I will never stay in a room with an adjoining door.

If you need metro access and have business on Capitol hill this location is ideal. The staff was super helpful - happy to give late checkout and very pleasant. The rooms were tiny - and I was told I had a nice room. But the price was reasonable and for a work trip it was fine.

Location was great, within walking distance to a lot of the major sights and shopping areas.
Room was basic enough, but clean and had everything we needed.
We asked for a -pm checkout and were told no, even though the hotel seemed very quiet all weekend.
The menu in the bar was disappointing, very limited choice.
Overall, it was fine but I probably wont stay here again!

I've stayed here every year, since ----, for The Chicago Marathon. The location is extremely close to the start and finish line and that's the main reason we stay here. 
The hotel is is a bit older and some of the rooms could use an upgrade (stained wallpaper, old carpeting, outdated bathrooms and not enough electrical outlets in the room). All of the staff that I encountered have been extremely friendly. Some cons of the hotel are that there's no free wi-fi (Who doesn't have free wi-fi in this day and age?) and that they usually charge $-- for an early check-in. 
Overall, we've been pleased with this hotel and will stay there for the marathon in ----. I would also recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Chicago.

We absolutely love the Inn at the Market. We've stayed here before, back when it was done in a somewhat French decor style. It's been modernized and is so comfortable and attractive. We booked city view room, but were upgraded to room on front of building with view of Puget Sound. It was delightful. You just can't beat this location. Wake up early and get to the market before it gets crowded. The restaurant Bacco serves a great breakfast and is located on ground floor. Service is terrific. This is just a great place to stay in Seattle.

Stayed here for - nights because we had to adapt to jet lack. Now looking back I would stay less nights here and go to Vegas, where you get cheap and good accommodation.

I am not sure about value for money. It was rather expensive (--- USD incl. tax) compared to other places we've stayed in the States, but we haven't tried other accommodations in LA, so I cannot compare.
Having said that I could recommend this hotel, if you don't have too high expectations and are looking for some simple place with great location.

Stayed here while attending a conference (in east harlem). Before my partner and I visisted the bahia, i was really worried after reading many of the bad reports on this website. It turns out I was worrying over nothing.

When we got to our room I was very surprised. They was no smell WHATSOEVER. The bathroom was very clean - mainly white tiled with a powerful shower. The room, to my surprise also had a small kitchen in the corner which we loved. It meant we didn't have to eat out every lunch and dinner time. The room also had a table and chairs and a comfy settee so it was sorf of self catering (much cheeper). We found it really good when we were just lying round the beach and we just had to nip back to the room for food.
The only problem I really had about the room was that we were on the ground floor and facing the car park. Being on the ground meant that we didn't really have a private space outside as anyone could walk on-off it. A balcony would have been nice but we were out and about the majority of the time so it wasn't really that much of an issue. 
Also by being on the ground floor we had to constantly leave our curtains closed so no-one could see in. They was no nets-blinds so anyone passing would be able to see your posessions.
There are parking spaces right around the hotel and we always found it easy to get a space near to our room. At night they lock the back gates at the hotel so its totally private which was re-assuring as our room was near to this area. No-one could walk through that wasn't meant to.
The private beach was lovely. We bathed on this a few times and really loved it. Its such a beautiful setting and very clean. It was never very busy either. I think the most people i ever saw on there was about --. The sun loungers weren't the cleanest so you would need your towels to cover them.
Overall I would definately recommend this hotel and would definately stay here again (but maybe ask for a room with a balcony and a bit of a view). The decor was slightly oldfashioned and the carpets were a tad shabby but if you can look past this, this is an excellent hotel in a beautiful location.

This place is amazing. The staff are fabulous, the rooms and facilities are superb. A must stay for anyone travelling to Universal Studios - there is a free shuttle bus on the hour and is a five minute trip to Universal studios. There is a laundry, pool, gym, sauna, restaurant (very reasonably priced) and much more.

I had to open my suitcase half way under the desk, after putting the desk chair on top of the club chair. What an awful stay in that hotel. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

We stayed at the Hilton Universal City for - nights for our visit to the LA area. A very convenient shuttle runs every ----- minutes between the hotel and City Walk-Universal. I've stayed at this hotel in the past and stay at Laquinta's frequently. This by far was one of my worst experiences. This is my scond stay. I stayed for seven nights at Double Tree Metropolitan (----- october). The hotel, itself, is good. Rooms are clean and confortable. The Hotel is very conveniently located right next to the UN. Safety is excellent. No restaurant currently, but then when you have such an excellent concierge who would want to stay in the Hotel? May be able to spot a celebrity here, just make sure you know them, because the staff is very discreet!

Stayed here for a medical conference .Spent three nights and very happy with the hotel and its location.Paid under $--- which is great for Boston.We had several meals in the Grill and Bar ,all were very good the menu was varied and great Martini.
 Free wireless in the room and a free workstation and printer in the lobby.The room was decent size ,clean and and in good working order. Staff was friendly .One elevator was down for repair but I was told this was planned ?

Staying at The Fairmont Olympic is always a special event... at least they always make it feel that way. From the valet to the check in I feel I am receiving special treatment. The staff is always attentive, professional, and very accomodating.
The hotel decor is traditional but not stuffy. The rooms are spacious, relaxing and have a special charm.
I always order room service during my stay, not only because the food is good but because it adds to the whole experience of the stay. 
The Fairmont Olympic is great for out of towners because of its location, service and classic charm BUT it is also great if you live in the Seattle area for a romantic get-away, a family weekend """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""downtown"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" or just a relaxing stay-cation.

With the Hyatt chain one usually expects to pay a little more but get more in the way of amenities and service. 
Well, I'd say it was a toss up with this hotel.
I'm currently staying here as I write this review. My wife is attending a convention and have to admit that being connected to the convention center is VERY convenient. For those that complain about the bad location, the hotel is here mainly to accommodate the traveler that is attending conventions NOT for those that want convenience to downtown. There are the Park and Regency Hyatt's for that.
The room is actually quite nice. Double sinks and nice beds. But here's my first gripe, while some may love the beds, for me, they are incredibly too soft! There's a pillow top and I get up in the morning with a back ache. Not sure if they have other types of bed. My wife is sleeping on the ground for the past few days. (I don't think it's because of me! LOL!)
Second gripe is that the concierge staff is pretty useless. They're okay for simple things but they are definitely not up to snuff for really complicated things. 
Third gripe and a major one to me, the shuttle runs once an hour. That's fine, they'll stop at the Museum Campus (GREAT MUSEUMS! Get the City Pass and you're set for several days worth of entertainment!), Navy Pier and WaterTower. But here's the glitch, they don't pick up! What's up with that? How much of a hassle is it to stop on the way out to pick folks up? Geez! Such a small thing that can make the stay here much more pleasant. To me, it's almost illogical to offer the pick up. Oh well...
Fourth gripe, the wait help in the restaurant Shor is terrible. We ate at the breakfast buffet for three days and every single day we had to rely on the assistants to serve us. And the only time we'd see the waiter is when the bill came! How's that??? Decided to give the tip directly to the assistant than leave anything with the bill.
Here's the good stuff:
House cleaning folks are very nice. Bring them a little something from your hometown and they'll great care of you. I think that means more to them than the standard tip (but don't forget that too!)
Front desk is fairly efficient and cordial.
Rooms are clean and fairly nice.
Only costs about $---$-- to town for a cab.
Check out how much you'll be paying for a shuttle, the cab may be cheaper from Midway at least.
In conclusion, for the price one pays for this hotel, there may be better deals to be had but if you're coming for a conference, it's kinda hard to beat the convenience of being right here.

I'm developing a love affair with independent hotels. This is a small, independent property in the Back Bay area only a block away from the convention center hotels charging a heck of a lot more. We arrived way early but they had a room available and checked us in at --:-- AM! Rooms are smallish but this is a big city, so what else is new? They must use a hiring profile that emphasizes youth and enthusiasm because everyone we encountered from check in to check out was young, positive, competent and engaged.

Arrived with -- friends, for - day stay. Beds and rooms too small to accomodate families, ( one of our families a group of - was given - single bed for all - on first night!!!) No wardrobe space, in fact, did I say, no space full stop! One families case was tampered with and our personal belongings (toiletries) were removed. The hotel staff were not concerned and although they claimed to involve security, we waited for security but they didnt turn up. Even though they knew we had a flight to catch!
Generally a nice modern hotel from a foyer perspective but the rooms and service let it down.

We have never stayed in downtown DC. Even though we looked at the hotel location on-line, getting from the Metro to the hotel entrance was a small challenge the first time due the the Metro exit being closed that was directly below the hotel. The hotel location was great for walking to the water front or the the National Mall and the sights around the area. The Metro does run right beneath the hotel. Given that it was a holiday weekend, I was not surprised that the shower never was repaired while we were there. Some of the recepticals need to be replaced due to age and use. The pool was nice but the life guard takes a break for an hour or more during the early afternoon, so the pool is closed at the heat of the day when we wanted to swim. Over all, with other things I observed, the front desk was always curtious and helpful. As for the facility, my opinion is that it is an old hotel that needs attention. I do not know what other hotels are priced at, but to me, the hotel was not worth price.

Clean rooms, quiet, friendly good service and great location if you want to be on a walk about downtown. Only stayed one night but was very satisfied. i believe they could give wi-fi without hurting the bottom line too much and the bartenders could have been little more professional instead giggly little girls but it was a very slow sunday night.

This was a great hotel!! The location was perfect! Within walking distance from the White House, National mall, Smithsonian etc. The rooms were very spacious and clean. Not one person had any complaints!

I will tell you why- -) the suite was perfect for a family of -. Plenty of sleeping space with a sofa bed and - window seat beds. You could have - kids and stay in the suite with room for everyone. I will definitely stay here again.

If a modest price and an attractive locale are very important to you, you will probably enjoy this hotel. If a high level of service and top notch facilities are your main consideration, you may want to look at a more expensive hotel

Stayed at the Palomar for - nights last week..It was great!! Gym is on the -rd floor and is very basic with a couple pieces of cardio equipment, a bench and some light weights. Closes at -:-- pm so hours are limited. Restaurant on the bottom floor is more of a bar - to your left after you walk in the front door open early for breakfast ($--.-- continental breakfast offers coffee, scrambled eggs with choice of bacon-sausage, and trips to the cereal-pastry-fruit-luncheon meat bar), and adjacent. Lounge with business centre, large screen TV and sofas adjacent to the reception area, except on the opposite side.
I can only speak to the penthouse hallways - however they seem as if they were updated in the past -- years or so, but the natural dingyness of the hotel was obvious in the obvious age of the exposed ductwork, the peeling and grime on corners of peeling wallpaper.

Again -- this hotel's best feature is location, and it was an important determiner for us. But if you're looking for luxurious surroundings and amenities, you won't find them here.
