Since my traveling companions and I were only there for one night, we didn't seek out a goldfish, but it is a cute Kimpton touch. Our room had a lovely view overlooking the river, with two nice cushioned window seats to enjoy the view. Several bars and restaurants were within walking distance along with a -- hour convenience store across the street. The reviewer who mentioned """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""beware of train noise"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is correct, but it doesn't bother me--it's just a sound of the city that I kind of like, so not an issue here. The bed was very comfortable. I asked for a wakeup call in the morning and behold! A real live human called. It's been years since that's happened to me. Free wi-fi if you join the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""In Touch"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Klimpton loyalty program.
A couple of things that I didn't like so much: There weren't enough outlets to charge phones, computers etc. There was no IPod dock which I do expect in these more contemporily styled hotels. The coffee in the lobby was wonderful, but there are people like me who just don't feel ready for primetime unless I have had my morning dose. Even a small one cup coffee maker would do the trick. I know most hotels feel they must have bathtubs for their guests, and I guess for those guests who have kids, or consider a leisurely soak in a bathroom some sort of luxury, they would get complaints if a room had no tub. But I really like a walk in shower with a real door instead of the bath-shower-shower curtain set up. The decor was fine, but not really stylish to me.
I'd definitely consider returning to this hotel or the Klimpton's Hotel Allegro again when staying in Chicago.

I searched and searched and read and read review after review after review here on tripadvisor trying to find a great hotel for my recent stay for the Marine Graduation this past weekend, and after searching high and searching low, i settled on this Marriott because of the countless great reviews and location. It's close to the airport but not too close, and it's close to the MCRD (Marine Base), and it's close to Rosecrans which is a popular street with tons of food options etc. This hotel lives up to it's high ranking #- out of --- hotels in the San Diego area. The rooms are excellent, spacious, well appointed with a flat screen tv, mini refrigerator, A-V hookups to watch videos if you have your camcorder or laptop with you and want to watch footage on the TV, cable including HBO, very spacious bathroom, granite counters, and even granite window sills. The staff is SUPER friendly, the lobby and main areas are immaculate, the fitness center has -- hour access, unlike many hotels that limit access, the jacuzzi was awesome as was the pool, the location has the harbor to the rear, a huge open park and trails, plus a beach area, and it's in a very upscale looking neighborhood. The business center is free to use, ie free internet access and a printer, plus free wi-fi in the rooms. There's a market attached to it that has starbucks plus other sandwich type deli items, plus a little store for knick knacks if you've forgotten something or need a little something extra (protein drinks, candy bars, chips, batteries, etc). Parking is FREE!! Which is impossible to find at a hotel in this class. So i basically had no complaints whatsoever and really can't imagine how anyone could complain on this hotel. Sure you hear planes, you're near an airport. They stop flying around --p and they start around ---am, but again it's not anything major. The planes aren't directly over head so it isn't super loud. I've decided that each time i return back to san diego, unless i'm renting some beach condo with a ton of friends, i will definitely be staying at this hotel again and again and would recommend it to any and everyone. Excellent. :) I stayed two nights (dec - - -, ----).

The public spaces and our room were very well maintained. The room was clean and a good size. Bathroom didn't have quite as much counterspace as other hotels we have stayed in but was adequate. We didn't notice any street noise or noise in the hallways even though there were at least two high school groups in the hotel. We had a great stay and would gladly stay at this hotel again.

We reserved through top secret hotels and there was a mix-up with our reservation so the Clift upgraded us to a loft suite which was spacious and beautiful! The door staff were very helpful in recommending restaurants, directions, etc. Location was excellent as well, walking distance to Union Square and many other places! Asia SF restaurant is a definite MUST!!

This hotel was AWFUL. We would NEVER stay there again. We booked through ParkSleepFly, and we called for a pickup after we got our bags. We were told the shuttle would arrive in -- minutes. We waited a full -- minutes in the freezing cold, after calling the hotel three times. Clearly, they were intentionally misleading us. The hotel was seedy and felt dirty, and was not a good value at all. As well, it is not convenient to Logan Airport. Never again!

The Westin Seattle is located - block from the shuttle to the Space Needle, - blocks to Pikes Place, and is across the street from tons of shopping options! The rooms are clean and updated. An upper floor features great views of Seattle. The features were great during our stay but the service was below average. We had trouble with requests of our reservation that had been confirmed prior to arrival. When asked about parking the front desk agents did not mention the $-- parking garage connected to the hotel to their $-- parking option. On the second night of our stay our room had a strong smoke odor, when we called to see about a room move they said they would send someone to deoderize the room. After -- minutes when no one had come, we cancelled the request so that we could go to bed
Great location and rooms - bad service.

I have stayed at the London hotel several times. It is conveniently located within walking distance to Time Square and Central Park, yet it is on a side street that is away from the main traffic flow. The rooms are a nice size and very clean. The staff is friendly and make you feel at home. I feel relaxed from the moment I step out of the cab until I leave for the airport. Definitely worth the price and my favorite place to stay in NYC.

This is a fairly average Holiday Inn Express, maybe even a notch below, but mainly because of the noise factor. The room was clean and the beds were very comfortable with soft and cozy linens, but the constant door slamming made relaxing and getting a good nights sleep nearly impossible. Why oh why can't hotels come up with a door closing system that will avoid the loud BANG when inconsiderate hotel guests let the door slam? I've always been mystified by that. Also there were children running up and down the hallway, but there's not a whole lot the hotel can do about rude parents who can't or won't control their children.
The room had a small fridge and a microwave, and we used the former but not the latter and the fridge actually kept things cold, which seems to be not a consistent feature with hotel fridges. We had one hotel (not this one) tell us that the fridges in the room were actually """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cooler boxes"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and so weren't expected to keep the items cold. What? That's just ridiculous.
Dolly at the front desk was very sweet and helpful, and there were great """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""welcome"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" cookies by the registration desk that were a nice perk. She also presented me with a gift bag of snacks for being a HIE Priority Customer when I checked into the hotel. 
Parking is tight but there seemed to be plenty of spaces, at least there were at the times we needed to park. There's a shopping center across the street with several restaurants and a pharmacy (if memory serves it was a CVS) so good places to eat are withing walking distance. You just take your life into your hands if you attempt to jaywalk across Sports Arena Blvd. Play it safe and walk a bit to use the signal just a short ways down the street. Oh, lots of street noise and police-fire sirens as well. Windows are not what I would call soundproof by any means. If I were to stay here again I'd ask for a room on the other side of the building, facing away from Sports Arena Blvd. Again, very, very noisy making for a not very peaceful sleep. I slept with earplugs all three nights we were there.

I stayed at the JW just before Thanksgiving, a veeeery quiet period for the hotel. The room was not remodeled, and will benefit from an updating, but it was clean, well maintained and very comfortable -- particularly the bed and desk chair (and how unusual is that!) The bathroom is marvelous. Unlike some reviewers, I found the service attentive. I don't use hotel services much, but when I asked for assistance, it was prompt and courteous. Did not use the restaurants; the bar was nice, but pricey -- hey, it's SF. Location is great. I usually stay at the SF Marriott on -th. This is clearly a grade up in style and attention, but both are terrific properties, with wonderful locations. If a first time visitor or someone still doing mostly touristy stuff, I might actually give the edge to the hotel on -th because of the very close proximity to the Fl ine! If you've been to SF before, choose this one for a touch more luxury.

Used my points this time, Stayed on the fourth floor(outdoor pool-Dining area for Breakfast is on the same floor), within walking distance to the Hollywood-Highland Center where the Kodak Theater is located, and of course the walk of fame, HUGE ROOMS( i have pictures) for public transport, MTA Red line subway is nearby as well as a few buses(--- i believe) has fridge and Microwave as well, Hot Breakfast, bacon & eggs or sausage sometimes, always a winner compared to other hotels' Continental breakfast, only thing was the pool wasnt heated and wasnt indoor, for a holiday inn express i didnt expect that.

This hotel is stuck way back in time. We didn't feel comfortable at all... Floor layout was confusing, everything felt old and musty. Only one elevator was working in the tower we were in. 
Very out dated. We'll never stay here ever again.

Travelled alone and the location of this hotel was perfect. I felt safe walking to it. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The room was small but for one person it was perfect, but if I was travelling with someone I would certainly book a bigger room. Everything was spotlessly clean. Library room was lovely. I didn't get to eat in the hotel but the food looked good. Internet room was also very handy.

We enjoyed our time at this Hilton property in San Antonio. The staff at all levels were friendly, proficient and made our stay memorable. While we were at the hotel the street was under construction, as well as some of the floors of the hotel, so there was a fair amount of noise during the day. But it didn't impact any of the operations of the hotel. We were especially impressed with three outstanding employees. On the housekeeping staff - Sandra A was the most pleasant and efficient housekeeper we have ever had, apart from being on a cruise ship. In the dining room Susana was very attentive as our waitress, also David was the most cordial and efficient omelette cook, I have encountered. We enjoyed our stay, please stop by if you are in San Antonio!.

My husband and I checked into the Hilton Garden Inn on ------- and stayed until ------- and we had a marvelous trip to the Chicago. We saw a taping of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The Jerry Springer Show"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (bizarre and sureal), went to see the musical """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Wicked"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" at the Oriental Theater (highly recommended) and went to see the Black Hawks defeat the St. Louis Blues in overtime (!) at the United Center. We ate excellent meals at both Heaven on Seven and Redfish (see my seperate review for Redfish). We also ate at Mother Hubbards which seemed more like a drinking establishment and not a dinner place (I would not recommend the ostrich burger). The HGI was an excellent base for our stay and was within walking distance for virtually everything we did (although we did take an express bus to and from the hockey game which is highly recommended at $-.-- per person each way). The Sears Tower was quite a hike from the HGI but it was a lovely day so we did walk back AND forth (but hey it gave us license for eating a great dinner with no guilt)!
After taking a cab from Union Station we checked into the HGI on Monday but our key card did not open the door properly and took many tries (typically -) to get the door to open. This problem happened virtually each and every time we tried to get into our room. Frustrating yes, but we learned to laugh about it and took bets on how many times it would take! Once inside our room we instantly noticed there were no pillows -- bizarre but we phoned down to request some and we were told they were to be sent up. Later while unpacking we noticed there was not an iron, only an ironing board. When we went out to grocery-snack-wine shop at the Jewel-Osco store (how nice to have a full service grocery store so close by) across the street later that afternoon we asked the front desk to send us an iron and also mentioned the room was still without pillows. They apologized and assured us everything would be taken care of. When we returned -- minutes later there was a knock on the door and an iron appeared but still NO pillows. It was only after a phone call from the front desk checking on the iron, that we reminded them that we still had no pillows. The pillows were then quickly dispatched. I hate to sound like a complainer as these were certainly minor issues but they seemed odd as a cleaning person would certainly notice the absence of pillows and probably notice the missing iron. By the way -- the rest of the week the cleaning service was excellent so this could have been just a strange occurrance.
I would definately stay at the HGI again and the rate of $--- per night was VERY reasonable. We are not needy nor demanding people so the king bed non-smoking room we requested (and received) suited our needs just fine (really it was GREAT)! We also loved the business center where we could check our email, and I was able to get more info regarding the express bus to the United Center saving us tons of money on a cab. We also appreciated the mini-refrigerator but did not use the coffee maker nor the microwave. Unfortunately we were too lazy or too tired after some late nights -- that's our story and we are sticking too it -- to use the pool or the exercise center but they looked great. Also kudos for the blackout curtains at the HGI and they should be standard at every hotel as they overlap in the center so there is not a large ray of light streaming into the room each morning.
All in all we had a FABULOUS trip to Chicago and the location and ammenities of the Hilton Garden Inn really allowed us to enjoy our stay. I would highly recommend this hotel and will certainly attempt to use it again when we return!!

We stayed for - nights over the Thanksgiving holiday to sightsee. Very glad we gambled and got this on Priceline for a steal $-- a night! Parking is an additional $-- per night, but that was a deal too. Nearby hotels were charging $---$--.
We really like the modern decor, huge flat screen tv, full kitchen & super comfy bed. Nice and clean overall. We stayed on the -th floor on the Vermont side of the building, noise was not an issue. Free wifi in the room made researching our next adventure a breeze. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Free breakfast was yummy and saved us time and $.
Occupy DC protesters and tons of tents are currently located down the street. We walked by a few times and all was peaceful, no one bothered us. 
In the other direction, we walked up to P street a few blocks away for dinner. Stoney's is a great casual place to grab a beer & burger that won't break the bank. Overall we really liked this property and neighboorhood and would stay again.

Wow! Nicely furnished room (Granite), clean and neat, free breakfast, super fast wi-fi, I had a couch, a small and a big table, a very comfortable chair (leather) to sit while working on my computer, fridge, micro-wave, manager-owner is really nice and will do his very best to please you. There is a big Wallmart and a nice dollar store just across the street. Don't hesitate to come there if you need to be near the Hobby airport and are on a budget but still want to stay at a very good place.

My wife and I stayed at the Travel Inn from May ----. It is located in a rather quiet neighborhood (for New York!), about a -- minute walk from Times Square. My wife and I felt very safe in the neighborhood, though there are many transients in the area (the bus depot is nearby, as well as a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""home"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for transients). The rooms are sparse, but pleasantly decorated. The bed was rather hard, but after walking all day, sleep was not a problem. We found the hotel staff to be very pleasant and helpful.
The hotel rates are a bargain for the location; and since we drove down from Boston, the free parking was a HUGE advantage.
I would definitely stay there again, and recommend the hotel to budget conscious travellers who want to be close to all of the action.

A great location made this this ideal venue, but the hotel itself was a little tired. The rooms were dark and the whole place felt old-fashioned. The executive club was closed at the weekend, but when it was open had a good selection for breakfast. Overall an okay experience, but not a five-star experience.

I thought everything was wonderful! The staff was great, they all knew my name. The room was great, I recomend getting the Hard Rock room. The room service was way cheaper than I would expect to pay at a hotel like this. All was great until I got the bill in the morning and realized I had to pay for parking!! They had even told me it was included, I guess they ment included in your final bill!! So I recomend finding parking on the street and risk getting a ticket. It will be cheaper than parking!

This was our -th or -th time staying at the Dolphin Motel, and our best experience yet! 
We live in Arizona and try to get out of the heat every summer by spending a week in nearby San Diego (a -.- hour drive for us). 
When we called the Dolphin to make our reservations this year, we asked if they got new mattresses, as we found them to be hard and uncomfortable in past years. We were assured that all mattresses had been replaced.
We have not been able to make it for a couple of years, but found during our week-long stay last month, that much of this quaint motel remained unchanged from years' past. (which is a GOOD thing!) 
What has stayed consistent over the years is the ever-friendly faces of Holly, Alan and Steve! They are always available to chat, to give info, to ask how your stay is going, to ask if you need anything, to hand you a bottle of water, or just to offer a friendly smile.
We also noticed some welcome changes: New, flat-screen TVs, mounted on the wall and freeing up the corner above the mini fridge for other stuff; new windows (much quieter inside the room now!); new chairs outside the rooms; a small round mirror mounted on the wall by the fridge (yay!); a small wire basket in the bathroom to place toiletries; and freshly painted A-C units.
One thing we did not notice was a new mattress. Our first night's stay was uncomfortable on the hard bed, necessitating us to get lots of extra pillows from the office and placing them under the mattress cover, creating our own """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""pillow-top"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" mattress, so to speak. The next morning, when Steve asked us how we'd slept, we casually mentioned to him that, upon booking the room, we were told that the mattresses were all new, and apparently they overlooked our room when changing out the mattresses. We left for the day and upon returning to our room, were surprised and delighted to learn that they had moved the old, hard mattress out of our room and hauled a new, pillow-top mattress up the stairs to replace it!!!! NO OTHER lodging establishment would do that for a guest! And at the Dolphin Motel, you do feel like a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""guest"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and not just a customer.
As others have stated, the rooms are small and simple, yet very clean and accommodating. The room has a double bed with crisp, white linens, blanket and bedspread; a wooden cubby holder on each side of the bed as night stands; a lamp on each cubby; a substantial sized closet with shelf and hangers; - folding luggage racks; a folding wooden TV tray; a chair, a mini fridge; a small round mirror; a corner shelf above the TV; and a wall-mounted flat screen TV with remote. (The TV volume is pre-set to a maximum level, and it can be difficult to hear the TV with the A-C running). The bathrooms contain a sink; a shower; a toilet; a wall cubby; and a small wire basket above the toilet. There is a large window in the room, and a smaller window in the bathroom. The rooms have air conditioners. Parking is plentiful. 
They offer bananas, yogurt, muffins, coffee and tea, which is a substantial breakfast. It is set up outside on the patio and is self-serve. Muffin choices were blueberry and chocolate the entire week we were there. Other flavors of muffin or even donuts would have been a nice change for the taste buds. They might also consider offering de-caf on a trial basis as many people can't drink caffeine or enjoy a cup of de-caf before retiring for the night. (We would walk to Winchell's every morning and evening to get our de-caf). 
We would like to suggest to the Murdock's a few other inexpensive additions: Hooks on both sides of the inside of the closet to hang belts, hats, purses, etc.; Another hook in the bathroom to hang clothes, towels, robes, etc. (there is currently one hook on the back of the bathroom door, the only hook in the room); A small shelf or hook near the sink to place or hang a blow-dryer, shaver, toiletries, etc.; A doorstop to keep the bathroom door open if desired (the door kept hitting me in the butt as I was drying my hair, applying make-up, etc. I finally stuffed a plastic bag under it to keep it open); And de-caf coffee.
The location is the best in San Diego, in my opinion! It is central to EVERYTHING! The fisherman's landing and marina are right across the street. There is a restaurant there where you can sit outside and watch the fishing boats, yachts, gulls, pelicans, and seals. Tradition for us is to walk over there after we settle into our room at the Dolphin and order the Fish Taco Plate and a couple of cold brews. Their clam chowder is also very good! We sit at the long bar facing the marina and the ocean beyond, pitying the poor people back in Arizona suffering the --- degree heat! 
Cabrillo National Monument, Seaport Village, Sea World, Downtown San Diego, Mission and Pacific beaches, Hotel Circle and the airport are all about a -- to -- minute drive from the Dolphin Motel. Walk to Hector's Mexican and Seafood restaurant on Rosecrans if you are pining for a fish burrito, or to Uma Sushi on Shelter Island Dr. if you feel more like a California Roll. There are many good, inexpensive places to eat in San Diego.
I defy anyone to find a motel in San Diego comparable to this one at this price! And they haven't raised their rates in the -- years I've been staying here. I just hope Holly and Allen NEVER sell this gem!
We will be calling you again in January to make our reservation for next summer! Can hardly wait! :o)

Never been a fan of the Ramada but hotels in San Fran are expensive and this one suited our budget ($--- a night)
The location was not great - especially since we did not have a car with us on the trip. Quite a walk to get anywhere interesting.
The hotel itself was quite outdated and run down. Very much had a cheap motel feel - not what you hope for when paying $--- a night. The room was clean but the sheets were pink, thin and seemed very old. The breakfast was in the 'lobby' - cramped and confined and right beside the front desk - we didn't try it - better to go down the street and grab something. 
The hotel was loud and we could hear doors slamming-people talking all the time. 
Overall it was decent for the price since everything else in San Fran is more expensive but if you are looking to have a comfortable stay you may want to spend a bit more $$$.

We loved this little gem on the cliff. This old school --'s motor lodge looks like it has been plucked off of Route -- or out of the Palm Springs desert and landed near downtown Dallas. The staff is comprised of Dallas hipsters (very nice, helpful, beautiful ones) with style and flair. We felt right at home right away. We were there for a casting call for a network television show and when the staff found out, they treated us like mini celebrities...even though we are just restaurateurs from Texas. Our standard room was very nice with a great view of downtown Dallas. Love the decor, mid century mixed with ultra mod. The bar is like a cozy den of some fabulous, creative interior decorator. The drinks are done to perfection and the bar appetizers and food available fits the surroundings (brie quesadillas, hummus, potstickers, anti pasta plates etc..). We were lucky enough to get a surprise call back and ended up having to stay another night even though we had already checked out. I called the Belmont as Dallas was under a heavy ice storm and asked if we could get another room and this time it even had a more spectacular view!! We recommended the hotel to another couple we had met during the casting and they ended up staying there too. The weather was terrible, it was a Sunday evening but the staff showed us a good time. Michael (?) grabbed the hotel vehicle (nice Escolade) and drove us over to the Mission district for a lovely dinner at a tiny tucked away Mexican restaurant. Vera Cruz has only - tables and it feels as if you are inside a tiny, beautiful jewel box. The food was good and the hotel hospitality was awesome. We plan to make this our place to stay on business or pleasure trips to Dallas! Thanks Belmont!

We stayed - nights, a family of -. The hotel is well located and clean but really needs updating. Our room was very small. The clean pool was appreciated after hot days of visiting. The parking was free with the room.
Direct access to the riverwalk, though you do have to walk a little ways to get to the bars and restaurants.

My wife and I spent - nights in this beautiful hotel. Room was plenty big enough with excellent views of the city. I recommend requesting a tower room - if you can get a corner room you will have views from two sides of the building. The building is very large with a beautiful lobby. Location is very convenient with a cable car stop right outside hotel. I recommend buying a - day transportation pass, which includes cable cars, trolleys, buses, etc.

Spent Labour Day weekend at this hotel, and found it to be everything we wanted - nearby to all the action, but very quiet ,comfortable, sizable room with all mod cons, helpful staff & a celebrity spot staying across the hall. We did have a deluxe room on the -th floor, but booked this direct with the hotel having found a really good rate elsewhere, which the hotel matched. Will definitely stay here again. Hot tip - there are better places to have breakfast than Sears - very over-rated.

Nice view, stayed on --th floor. Very accommodating staff, and the shuttle was a great plus! Stayed for - days to attend Ron White show at the Majestic Theatre. Great location if you like to visit restaurants, shops, and bars in downtown Dallas.

I stayed at the Sheraton Denver Downtown Hotel for a conference recently and was very impressed. Although the outside building looks a bit rough, the inside is tastefully decorated with modern touches. There was an additional conference on site at the same time, but the hotel had plenty of staff available for check-in-out. The conference banquet staff was phenomenal and food tasty. My room was very large and the only real negative was a lack of view...I saw only more hotel rooms. Bed and pillows very comfortable and I'm picky! I had read that the hotel lay out can be a hike, but I did not experience any distance issues. Perhaps request a room in the plaza building (but you may forgo any view).
The hotel gym is nicer than some private gyms with plenty of high-end equipment - cardio and strength training. 
The location of the hotel is right on the --th street mall, so plenty of restaurants and shopping nearby. I would definetly recommend this hotel for future conference attendees.

Was lucky to get room ---- which is a superior room with city view and an access to a large balcony. Amazing hotel room, could not be better.
All staff was very friendly and helpfull.
Great location.
Highly recommended

Great place and all you need to know about hotels in Manhattan. Large quiet rooms, great staff and service. Well located in the West Village near a subway stop. Staff is very friendly and go out of their way to help. Took care of theater tickets and pointed me in the right direction for food and entertainment. Great location to visit the best Jazz clubs in NYC. Don't miss Smalls Jazz Club walking distance from the hotel.
Great breakfast with even an outdoor area and there's always coffee and snacks available. Thanks Jay!!

The last two nights of our vacation we stayed at Ocean Beach. The first five were spent at a high end Hotel near the Marina (which we got for a really good price) so it was a rather stark contrast. 
 We checked in around - PM and right away walked down the street to look for something to eat and were struck by the number of tattoo-body piercing parlors (and the many people who apparently frequent them) and bars with a smattering of tacky souvenir shops...That was our first impression of the area, and we were a little disappointed (and nervous) but then reminded ourselves that it was all part of beach town culture and decided to embrace it and enjoy this very different side of life we were experiencing. 
 The people who run Ocean Beach Hotel are really friendly, and our room was neat and clean with a great view of the ocean and cute center courtyard. 
 The bed was queen size and pretty comfortable, with a fridge, microwave and little table and two chairs. The floor is a hardwood veneer (probably easier to clean after beach goers) Only a couple of minuses: The headboard banged against the wall every time we moved, and we could hear the TV really well from the room next door, as well as the conversations of everyone who walked by our room late into the night. The cooler was kind of loud, and yes the bathroom had a couple of missing tiles and a little peeling paint as mentioned in other reviews but its a beach hotel and we thought it was well maintained and cared for. 
 If you are looking for a spa-type resort with indoor access to rooms and a fancy lobby, this isn't for you, but if you want a clean nice place to stay at a fun beach with great staff, this is a great choice. 
There were a couple of great places to eat (Hodad's and Newport Pizza) and the business owners in the area were very friendly. We even got some great deals on shells and souvenirs at some of the tacky little gift shops!

My work collegues and I had saved for -- months for this trip to New York, and decided to splash out on the accommodation. The Waldorf Astoria has a reputation as an iconic New York hotel, and we hoped it would be a luxurious experience. We didn't wait very long to check in, our rooms were not ready on arrival, but we had arrived before -pm. Our party had - rooms. We had various issues during our stay, none of which were resolved. Room -, ran hot, the air con did not work. Room -, the safe and air con did not work, the windows did not open. During our stay the hotel hairdryers blew the fuse and we were without electricity in any of the rooms for over an hour. We did notify the front desk about the problems we were experiencing. They did give $--- dollars credit to each of the rooms with faults, to use at Oscars for breakfast. We really enjoyed breakfast, which we had on our last day. We were squeezed into a corner of the restaurant, but the food was lovely and the choices plentiful.
The main problem that we experienced with this hotel is the unauthorised use of our credit cards after we had settled our bill and checked out. I was charged $--- - days after I got home, for breakfast for - people. I had used the credit awarded by the hotel and settled the rest in cash. I then rang billing and was told I would be phoned back, which never happened. I emailed Hilton Group customer services and got no acknowledgement. In the end we both contacted our Banks to investigate and try to get the money back. Eventually, after -- days, we both got an email from billing saying they had no idea what we were disputing. Another few furious emails ensued and I have now had my account credited at a worse exchange rate!! My collegue is still waiting. There was no apology from billing until I demanded one. The customer service at this hotel is atrocious.

We were booked at the Sheraton for - nights over Easter weekend but they gave away our rooms and sent us on to the Colonnade. Their loss was our gain as we had a wonderful experience in a hotel we have obviously overlooked during the many times we have visited Boston. Now we know exactly where to book in the future!
We arrived quite late on Friday evening, We had the extreme pleasure of being checked in by the lovely Nuala Creedon. Her professionalism showed while she dealt with fairly disgruntled clients. Yes, us!! Nothing flustered her as she found us - rooms on the --th floor - until we mentioned that one room was to be for three people. They had no doubles left (something the Sheraton KNEW when they sent us there) but Nuala promised to have housekeeping bring us everything they had to make our son comfortable...albeit on the floor. She also offered to have us moved to a double room the next morning and made notes so the morning staff would be prepared.
Housekeeping brought up extra blankets, duvets, sheets and pillows - not to mention extra bath robes and our son did sleep on the floor that night but may not have suffered too much.
After settling in we went down to the restaurant, Brasserie Jo, for a bite to eat and a night cap. They had a small late night menu and while I really wanted clam chowder it was not on the menu. I merely asked and yes, it was available. It may have been the best CHOWDAH I've ever had! It was served with a delicious loaf of warm French bread. (See separate review of restaurant.)
The next morning we were able to secure a double room and how lovely it was. Also larger than our previous King room. The bathroom was also much bigger. The room was very modern and comfortable with lovely bedding. I will also mention that I loved the Colonnade for the fact the windows open! We are fresh air freaks and while the outside temp wasn't very warm it made the room comfortable for sleeping.
Loved the Keurig in the room and the hotel offered a nice selection of coffee.
The room was immaculate and included a good sized safe in the closet. We consider that a must when traveling.
The staff was very warm and accommodating and always friendly to chat with. We really felt they could not have done more to make our stay so pleasant.
A special shout out to Norman at the door - he called and arranged for a van cab for - of us (and all our luggage!) to get to South Station for our train home. He was very warm and personable.
So, the Sheraton's loss was definitely our gain! The people who work there could not have been nicer and we totally look forward to visiting them again in the future.

This is a modestly priced hotel that delivers outstanding value. It is a ---% nonsmoking property, which my husband and I appreciated. The front desk staff readily accommodated our request for early check-in. Housekeeping service was excellent. Our room was spotless every day of our stay. We had a king suite which offered plenty of space. The fitness center was decent, with free weights in addition to the usual treadmills and bikes. The breakfast buffet was surprisingly good.
The hotel was full when we stayed due to the Texas-Oklahoma game, but the staff and management did a great job maintaining a quiet and family-friendly environment throughout the weekend. I noticed that on Sunday morning the breakfast area got very crowded, so the management opened up a banquet room for additional seating. Again with the good customer service!
While there isn't much to do near the hotel, the area seemed safe and quiet. Our only complaint, which is very minor, was that our room was behind the hotel's front facade which blocked our window view completely. But we were there to visit family and didn't spend much time in the room anyway. The hotel is a little hard to find at first, It is on a frontage road off the freeway and is easy to pass by the first time, and thanks to a lot of one-way streets is hard to get back to. My best advice, when you get on the frontage road, look for the Enterprise Commercial Rental place and be ready to make a quick right turn into the next parking lot.
Bottom line, this hotel is a great value for the money and we will stay there again.

The hotel is a little run down, the rooms aren't the cleanest either. The shuttle service took quite a long time even though we called twice so we ended up having to take a taxi. The employees were very friendly though.

Last time we stayed at the Dupont Circle hotel we were moved to the Level Nine Presidential Suite because of an unfixable issue in our original Level Nine Studio Room. When we decided to visit Washington DC again this past May, we booked the Presidential Suite because we wanted every inch of that great room and the fabulous balcony.
You will notice a difference in reviews from people because in my view there really is two separate experiences within the one hotel. If you are willing to pay for a room on Level Nine, then you will get a different experience. 
Having said that, I did not like the Studio room - it was way too small. I have no seen the - Bedroom Suite - but I'm told that the size difference between that room and the Presidential Suite is minimal, but the balcony is larger.
Since we had already done all of the sight seeing on our last trip - we really used this trip to chill out, relax, in the room, on the balcony, we went out to different neighbourhoods, bars and restaurants. This hotel and the room really worked for us given our needs.
The option of having light snacks-drinks and alcohol in the Level Nine lounge (and the open bar in the room) was also great for us --- we didn't have to leave or rush just for a quick bite.
Service, for us, was great - from housekeeping to maintenance (we had an issue with the TVs) to John Paul and Cole at the Front Desk. We were treated wonderfully. There was a great note from John Paul welcoming us back and Cole called to check in on us. I didn't regret choosing this hotel again, and will choose it again in the future unless another hotel with a similar inclusive 'club level' experience comes along with great rooms and fabulous balconies. All of that is hard to come by in Washington -- I tried, I searched for months. The rate on the Presidential Suite goes from $----ish to $----ish a nite - it's not cheap, but for everything it provided for us, it worked.
I will continue to complain about having to pay for parking -- another $---$-- a night just to leave my car in spot is ridiculous, especially when I'm dishing out several hundreds of dollars for a room. I'm told that the parking lot is not operated by the hotel, but I hope that in the near future the hotel and the lot operator work out something for Level Nine guests.
I will add pics to this site as soon as I can -- I think that the pics on the hotel website could be better and labelled more clearly so that you can see what you're getting. But if you have any questions about the rooms-hotel, I can certainly try to answer them.

I'm not a fan of the dispenser in the shower for shampoo, conditioner and shower gel but I suppose it does help keep expenses low. The neighborhood can be scary at night but there are safe pockets for you to walk if you want.
The only problem I had was with the two different parties who were in the adjoining room. On Friday night, the first group decided to stay up and talk all night and I finally had to call the front desk after -:-- a.m. to see if they could do something about it. Saturday night was fine, but on Sunday morning the second party decided to get up extremely early and carry on a loud conversation where one member kept laughing loudly every few seconds. Since I couldn't sleep any more, I just checked out early. The front desk suggested that next time I ask for a room that does not have an adjoining room.
All in all, a great hotel.

I was recently in Chicago for business and needed a quick reservation. The Congress Plaza on Michigan Ave was available within - week of my trip. The room was small, but extremely clean and comfortable. I enjoyed the location as I had to walk to my conference on Monroe Street, about a mile away. As a woman traveling alone, I never felt worried about walking around that area at night. I brought my own air card, but I heard the clerk tell another guest that they were being charged for each device (ipad, iphone etc) that they accessed the internet on in their room. That doesn't seem right. The bed was even more comfortable than my own at home and the selection of pillows also was perfect. No fridge in my room, but that didn't matter to me. Great for someone traveling alone. Close to the Art Institute - too bad I didn't have time to visit!
close to all the great NYC gems. staff very polite and wanting to help. close to Penn station, sub-way. rooms clean and neat. felt safe. children enjoyed. was not too noisy.

Yes, the rooms and bathrooms are small—but more than big enough. I found the rooms well appointed, very clean and perfect for a business stay. I stayed - nights and had a wonderful experience. The staff can't be beat...they went out of their way to help me with my needs that had nothing to do with the room. If you are looking for a resort style place, this is not it. If you are looking for a great place at an affordable rate—stay here. I'll be back next trip to Boston.

Great location, friendly service, complementary wifi, complementary wine and cheese hour, complementary breakfast, and coffee and tea throughout the day. Couldn't of asked for more. The rooms were a bit small and the bathrooms were even smaller–but hey, what can you ask for when real estate is a premium in NYC.

We were there for - nights in early July ----. This Hotel is in the financial district and has a lovely Japanese Garden on the -rd or -th level which is just amazing. Dont miss it . The view of La city from there is beautiful. Hotel has a huge lobby, great rooms with adequate airon, spacious and comfortable beds. What more can you ask for .It is a no smoking hotel . Excellent buffet breakfast.We did not eat in the restaurants as our tour operator had arranged for our dinner elsewhere but overall ambience of the hotel was great.

My son and I stayed for - nights at the Hilton Garden Inn in N.Y..C.This was our first time in this hotel. The service was excellent from the front desk, to the maid,to the breakfast buffet. The room was well-appointed with all the amenities to make our stay as comfortable as possible.We will definitely stay at another Hilton Garden Inn when we travel again.Very quiet and also very clean!!!

We've stayed at several hotels in New York. This is by far the best one we've stayed at. It was terrific. The location was perfect...central to so many things. The beds were comfortable and the room was clean. The bathroom was very clean (after reading reviews here before we left I was worried...no need...the bathroom we had was the best I've had in New York City). The room wasn't huge, of course...but this is New York City (if you want a big room you need to stay in New Jersey or pay through the nose!). The lobby was lovely. The rooms seemed almost sound-proof...we heard no noise in our three nights there...and we had a room with a lot of people walking by. Our hair dryer didn't work, so we called the desk and they sent up a new one right away. I really have nothing bad to say about this hotel. My family and I will be back...often.

My girlfriend and I stayed at this hotel for about five days at around $--- per night for the first weekend in August. The Lollapalooza festival was that weekend and the hotel is about as close as you can get to the gates, even though it's still a bit of a hike.
The hotel staff we quite friendly and helpful and we had no problems checking in, or at all during our stay. The rooms are no frills, but then again we just needed a place to rest our heads. We actually used the hotel more than we expected, as the -nd floor rooftop pool and fitness center were quite nice for the price of the hotel. The shower-bathroom was nice and there was plenty of space to store all of our goods. Service staff was excellent.
There are plenty of options nearby for food, even a nice grocery store just a few blocks away. We were able to stock up on some cheap eats, beer, etc. to keep us company in the room. There is a diner around the corner that's really hip and the food was incredible, I've gotta think of the name and come back here to post.
As far as the location goes, you simply can't beat this place for the price. When you're in Chicago you should really be seeing Chicago, and this hotel provides a comfy space and a decently clean environment.

There was a mix up with my reservations and the front desk would not even help me fix the problem. They just gave me an --- number to call and the number I called could not help be the hotel was individually own. The room had a strong odor of smoke, was old and needed updated and a good cleaning. It was not worth the ---.-- they charged me for it. That was the first time I had stayed at a Best Western in some time and now I remember why I don't stay at them. There are a lot of better Hotels out there to pick from.

Stayed here for the second time. 
Now a little expensive compered to the standard, but good situated. 
Nice, spacy room but a little dark though we definitely had one of the best in the back on the third floor. 
Breakfast was only served until nine o'clock , and that is not ok. As last time there is no bread and juice - only coffee, yoghurt, muffins and apples. Should have been better. 
The bed is fine and the bathroom is vell functioning. 
Perhaps we will stay here again next time visiting SF.

New York Palace Hotel is an outstanding immaculate hotel. The lobby is elegant and staff is extremely courteous and helpful. Free wi-fi internet is available in the lobby and the best part of this hotel is by far the room size. I travel to NYC weekly for business and have had numerous hotel rooms half the size of the Palace's. The Palace room size trumps NY Hilton's executive suites and their Hilton Club apartments. The rooms are definitely older and more traditional in style however . Nonetheless, definitely worth the money if you can find a good deal. (~ $---) On busy weeks I've seen the prices jump two-fold which has forced me to other hotels - but I will always stay at the Palace whenever possible.
For general comparison - I've stayed in Midtown at Hilton New York, Astoria Waldorf, Millenium Broadway, The Muse and The Royalton for a min. of - week each.

First off, I have stayed at several Hilton Hotels, and this one is the worst. This hotel charges for every single thing! They have ample self parking and it's $-- per day or $-- for valet. If you want a fridge (shouldn't it be standard at """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Hilton"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel?) it is $-- per day. If you have small children, be prepared to pay for a refigerator to keep their formula- milk cold. There is free wifi in the lobby, but if you want to use the Internet at the convenience in your own room, there is also a charge for that. The night staff was appropriate, but they weren't accommodating enough to provide customer satisfaction. So after spending three nights here, my total alone for the extra amenities without tax was $--(not including wifi and tax). One would assume that if you're paying $--- plus tax a night for a three in a half or four star hotel, parking, refrigerator, and wifi in the room would be included. I guess not for this Hilton. Next time I'll be sure to read the fine print of amenities included, but for sure, I will not be returning to this hotel.

I wanted to make sure that someone knows about Diana Lugg, She is the very best person I have ever encountered in a hotel visit, She is the friendliest and most courteous person at your hotel. Truly I cannot say enough about her, She is awesome.
Then there is Andy and Fernando Mendoza, amazing, Two of the politest young men I have ever encountered. They went out of their way to ensure that we all had rides to where we needed to go, Especially me, I felt that they catered to me, Maybe they didn't but they sure made me feel that way. I really appreciated the services that they provided. Not one time even with the hard time that I gave them (Joking around) did they ever step out of line or anything. 
I have the utmost respect for all three of these people And I would pray that would get recognized and rewarded for their dedication and professionalism that they obviously take pride in. Thank you for a wonderful trip

This property has something for everyone, families and couples alike. 
The rooms with the view of the bay are absolutely wonderful! Check in was easy and the staff was very friendly and accommodating. 
We LOVE staying here and will most definitely be back.

Stayed there with two other girlfriends, there were three of us in the room and we had plenty of space! The beds were very comfortable and it was so quiet and clean.
Very close to everything, we walked everywhere China town, the Pier where you can catch buses to Fisherman's Wharf or other attractions. Very close to famous cable cars turnabout! Lots of good shopping near hotel if don't want to go to the premier discount malls. 
On our trip back to the airport we asked doorman to arrange for a Taxi, he asked if we were celebrating anything said all our --th, so he arranged for a limo ride to the airport wonderful way to end a fantastic stay!!

We began with a negative experience at breakfast but this was resolved, the staff need to realise that many of their clients have travelled long journeys and a warm smile and a kind word can make a big difference.
Riley Woods at the front desk was very helpful always as well as Deming and Santos who served us breakfast and the Restaurant manager Dennis Kudos to him. he came every day to make sure we were suitably served.
The hotel was in need of a renovation we expected more for such a high price of services.
Thank you!

We visited Baltimore for - days prior to going to DC. The hotel staff was very friendly and was very helpful with questions. Dion was great, helped us find the stops for the the free bus. (It's a little confusing at first) 
 The room was clean and has a micro & fridge which was nice. They provide free granola bars, popcorn and water! It was an easy walk to Camden Yards, the inner harbor, and the light rail.
 All in all, a really good experience.

This hotel is what Omni is all about. The management at this hotel has to be top notch, there was not a single person that we met at any hour that was unhappy. This energy immediately is contagious to its guests. The restaurant onsite was wonderful, live piano music each night, and the indoor and out door pools were very refreshing. The management informed us during our stay that the carpets on our floor were going to be cleaned and it would be very load, they offered to relocate us and we took them up on their offer. Everyone in this process was extremely apologetic, we relocated to a room with great views and a surprise of champagne - chocolate covered strawberries - treats for the kids. I would definitely stay here when I am in San Antonio with its great location, close to downtown, and excellent security surrounding the parking lot at all times.

I've stayed at the Rouge a few times, and finally felt compelled to write a review. The Rouge is one of my all-time favorite hotels. It's in a great location, the ambience is definitely not your standard 'hotel' atmosphere, and the service is consistently excellent.
When we called for more towels, we had them in just a few minutes, and when we asked for another pillow it was there promptly.
I'm a big fan of Kimpton Hotels generally, but the Rouge is particularly excellent!

To start with the good point - the breakfast is good, and the rooms are relatively well appointed.
Unfortunately, there are too many problems. Not having a car, we went to the hotel on the promise of a shuttle service from the subway services. This was immensely unreliable and invariably full. Every time we used it, we waited for between -- and -- minutes as successive shuttles don't turn up when they say they will, and you have to fight your fellow guests for a seat on it. When I complained to the driver, he was polite, but clearly not in a position to do anything about it. I complained to the hotel, after standing in the dark and the pouring rain for -- minutes in what my guide book said was the most dangerous part of Boston, the reception staff member I spoke to was rude, disinterested, did not apologise, said 'don't know' and walked straight into the office to hide. 
When we stayed, we had a reasonable amount of rain, which somehow splashed under the roof guttering, and soaked the carpets. The a-c is useful and effective, but sleeping with it on would be rather similar to sleeping next to the runway at Boston Logan airport.
The door lock on our room didn't really work properly (although the staff assured us that it did), and the hotel has any number of external doors that anyone could walk through.
It's a pity, because it could be a nice hotel.

After extensive research on trip advisor I decided to book our reservation at the Hampton Inn Times Square North - I would stay there again and again. Kids were happy, I was happy. Very clean room, smoke free building meant a fresh smelling hotel. The free breakfast had a very wide variety and I could not say enough nice things about everyone who works there, from the front desk to the bellman to the maids. The concierge desk was very knowledgeable and friendly and gave us great advice. After all the craziness of shopping and touring around the city it was heaven to come back to our room and it was silent, no outside noise, no inside noise.
Good hotel with a simple but okay breakfast. Bed is a bit too hard and the room is very small, but with a vacation you are only in the room to sleep. Bathroom perfect. Nice people working there.

We recently stayed here for a very good price using Priceline.com. The hotel is right next to the Oriole's field and close to the football field as well. There are several little bars just across the street that cater to the sports fans and visitors. The hotel itself was pleasant. The rooms were clean and the bed was VERY comfortable! The gym was super cool as you can do cardio while literally overlooking a ball game! There was also a small lap pool and hot tub but there were too many children inside. We ate in the restaurant one evening which was good (food and service) but a bit pricey. Just a note, parking is rather expensive here, as it is anywhere in this city, but at least you can have in and out privileges. Also, it's not advisable to go out walking at night much further than the bars across the street as there's nothing else to do or see in the immediate area except for beggars...

I spent a bunch of time looking for a hotel in DC and more or less ended up settling on Madera. Overall, I was very pleased. Check in was easy, service was very friendly. The room was good sized and we had a balcony. Even with the glass door open was pretty quiet overall. I'd say this hotel aspires to be in a category with a W hotel, and offers a lot of kitschy and somewhat charming perks, although they are not in the same class. Hybrid cars I was told valeted for free(yeah environment!), the animal print robes were kind of a riot and the coffee-tea selection and wine receptions were nice touches that made you feel welcome. They were running a $--.-- for a second night special on Sundays so we stayed an extra night (but I had to ask for any specials to be told about this). Overall, this is a safe, pleasant hotel, they do allow pets, but I wouldn't have known that if there hadn't been dog biscuits also available at welcome. I would stay here again, especially for $--.-- in this location!

For the price the hotel wasnt bad. 
I really expected much worse
well first off let me tell you I was in town to see a Tool concert, there were - of us and i needed a convient place to stay bc most of us hadnt been to DC before. I didnt need much, and didnt expect much out of this hotel but it was good.
it was older but clean, the elevators are freakishly small, and the hotel was laid out funny. there were not loud trafic noises, and it was nice and quite. The hotel staff was pretty nice. Parking was expensive, but convenient. And we were less than two blocks fromt he metro. I got a dicount through work and it was --- tax parking and all for two rooms for two nights. Not bad. I felt very safe because a room key was needed to get in the hotel after a certain time, and it was needed at all times to use the elevator. I was extreamly happy with this hotel, it was very conveitly loacated, and safe and clean.

I booked a room for - people (- full beds) - extremely small! it was really a small double room with - beds squeezed in there. Other than that, it's a nice hotel - very clean, friendly, comfortable beds, discounded parted ($-- per day), free breakfast. Great if you need to spend a night after an event at Madison Sq Garden.

I stayed at the Shoreham shortly after it opened a few years back. I was really looking forward to this return visit, but unfortunately I was left slightly disappointed.
Everything was 'fine' but it wasn't the treat that it was back then. 
On the plus side, it's got a handy Midtown location. It still feels a bit more individualistic than the bland chain hotels. The bed was super comfy. Free wifi is a good bonus.
The downsides were the lack of any kind of view, and the general level of service. Queues seemed to be the norm at reception, and the staff weren't especially friendly. On Sunday housekeeping started tapping on adjacent doors from -am. The printer wasn't working for boarding passes.
In all these things were more annoyances than things that were bad per se, but I left somewhat disappointed on this particular occasion.

This has to be one of the best hotels. From the check in with Maya, Concierge Marc, and the best bartender ever at Rumba. It may be pricey but worth every penny. Check out Miel as we had a wonderful meal there also.

We picked this hotel for location and price and it didn't disappoint.
Double,double room was a good size,.bathroom a bit small,but so what?
Beds were a bit creaky and on the firm side,but pillows were wonderful.
(We have bought new pillows since we came home!)
Room was very clean,except for cobweb in corner of celing.
Towels changed every day.Refrigerator in room was great for water-drinks-snacks.
Didn't use microwave,but handy if you need it.
We were at the back of hotel and it was pretty quiet.Just round from gym-ice machine.
Wi-fi at $- a day was good,considering the room-rate.
Thanks for the last """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""vitamin"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" free!
Yes,we would stay here again.
P.S. great hotel to reach from airport express bus

This was a kinda a “spur of the moment” trip for the family to San Antonio (SA). We used a travel website that rhymes with “buybak” to start looking for hotel rates in the Riverwalk area of downtown SA.
The Marriott Plaza San Antonio had the best rates and looked to be fairly close to downtown - Riverwalk area.
Location – 
It’s within - – - blocks walk to the Riverwalk. There are stairs down to the Riverwalk behind the Hiton Del Rio (?). The hotel is - – - block walk to The Alamo. It’s an easy walk, and our family walked to the Alamo twice. We took the River Boat Tour also ($-.---pp) – the ticket stand is right behind the Hilton (again, - – - blocks from the Marriott). Another poster wrote that the bus stop is right outside the Marriott – this is correct. The published rates were $-.-- per person to get on the bus, and I think the bus goes most everywhere in the downtown SA area.
Staff – 
The staff at the check-in desk was nice. They had incorrect information regarding the hours at The Alamo, though. The valet - bell stand guys were really nice. The restaurant staff was the best – one guy even brought my daughter and me a muffin from the restaurant while we were waiting in the lobby for my wife and son. Just because he saw us sitting there by ourselves.
Breakfast –
Get the buffet breakfast – even better, if you’re offered the option of “adding breakfast” at the hotel for a $--.-- or so upcharge – take it. It’s a steal, and the buffet is really good. Made to order Belgium waffles and made to order omlettes. Hot food selections were bacon, sausage, fried potatoes, and hot oatmeal. Then your selection of cold meats and chesses including salmon and capers. Fresh cut fruit, cold cereals, and muffins, toast, etc were also available. 
By far the best value on the trip, and I urge couples and families with children less than -- to take advantage of the “add breakfast for $--” option if it’s given to you on one of the travel booking websites.
Room – 
Nice enough – two double beds, rather than two queen size beds. Room looked like it had been refurbed within the last - – - years, but the hotel was definitely an “older” hotel. The pool was nice, but there were quite a few mosquitoes about. Our children enjoyed it, though. We asked for more towels, but they were sent to the wrong room. One MAJOR issue I had with the room was that Marriott wanted to charge you $-- per day for internet service in the room. Internet (Wi-Fi) was free in the lobby. This is simply unacceptable in ---- to charge for internet in a hotel room – especially when it was available in the hotel. The room had a mini fridge, but it didn’t get real cold. If you have ice packs or you are carrying things that have to be kept frozen, do not rely on this fridge to do this.

Great options for families.... however, when placing the safety side rails on my kids' bed, the mattress pad came up to reveal bed bugs. There were only a few dead ones, but that was enough for me. Inspect your mattresses. Bed bugs come home with you and are very difficult to get rid of. The hotel did replace the mattress and linens, but I am not sure if that was really enough. I am still scratching!!!!

We’ve been holding our company's conferences at upscale hotels throughout the region for many years, and throughout that time have often been impressed by excellent service… however, I really do have to say that the quality of service (and food!) at the Hilton Charlotte University Place hotel is truly of the very highest caliber.

The front desk person, Alex, at Club Quarters Houston made my week long business trip here wonderful. There were a few bumps in the road during my stay at CQ Houston. However, Alex's consistently pleasant attitude and ability to make even the smallest problems disappear swayed me to give the property an excellent rating.

The hotel is obviously dedicated to ensuring that you enjoy your time while staying there. The wine hour was a great way to relax and experience a sense of community during your stay. The staff is very helpful. I left wondering how I paid so little for such a great hotel.
Beautiful loft-style rooms with modern decor, warm lighting and very comfortable bed. Love this hotel, will definitely stay here again when we are in Indy.

This La Quinta Inn is great. We stayed there twice - so far - and are very happy with it. The rooms are clean and the beds comfortable. All the staff are very friendly and helpful and the breakfast is quite nice. Yes, it's not the bacon and eggs type, but for the price, it was delicious. The coffee is strong -- and I mean STRONG, not that watered down stuff one gets other places, and they have real milk, not that fake creamer stuff. The breakfast area is clean and friendly looking. Wasn't able to enjoy the pool because we got in late that night and had an appointment early next morning, but the water looked really crystal clear and some people enjoyed the hot tub. You know all the talk about hotels with bed bugs! Well, I checked really good to make sure that there were none. No Bed Bugs anywhere! You can't beat that peace of mind. The rooms are a little on the small side but you only sleep in there and not have a party - right. 
When I made the reservation online I put on there that I needed a room on the ground floor because I have problems walking. Many other places do not pay much attention to those statements but this La Quinta Inn did. I was called and asked if they could upgrade me to a king bed from two standard because there were no more standard ones available on the ground floor. The upgrade even had a fridge and microwave in the room! The bathroom was old but clean and had sufficient towels in it. 
When I have to go to my next appointment I will definetely book a room at this La Quinta Inn again and again.

I stayed here any way after I saw the ratings. Now I know why they are so poor. The front desk staff was less than friendly. When I checked out the front desk person would not even mutter a sound. It was unbelievable! The room was clean, could have been nice however, they put me over the main lobby so I heard the noise of the elevator and front doors all night long. Would I sty here again? Doubtful.

We stayed at the Waldorf Astoria for one night and have to say that the experience was a bit dissapointing. 
The first room they gave us was pretty big for NY and pretty, but there was a low, thudding noise coming from the hotels huge airconditioning unit or something which was outside just on the same level as the room. I knew I would not be able to sleep in that noise so we asked for another room. I could not help thinking that this was the room they automatically offer to first-timers who don’t know about the noise problem in that room. The next room was in the Astoria Tower and it smelled like tobacco smoke. As we had been confirmed a non-smoking room we asked for a -rd room.. The -rd one did not smell of tobacco and was otherwise ok too. It just took a lot of time and energy to get a proper room. And I have never had to ask for another room before, despite loads of travelling around the world.
As I have seen in another hotel with a prestigeous past the staff can be a bit snooty. And they seem to pop into your room rather often. We had put some bread and cheese in the minibar and were """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""scolded"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" by someone whose job seemed to be just popping in to your room to have a look at the minibar, in the evening of your --day stay.. Why not at the end of your stay? 
Another snooty example from the breakfast restaurant where we were rushed to the table and hastily asked """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""have you been here before?"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in the meaning that do you know how this works. So they have many options for breakfast which come with their do's and don'ts, so the first thing in the morning (before your morning coffee ;-) ! ) you have to be sharp, focused and fast and absorb the rules. Why don't they just simplify things?! One breakfast type in one buffet table etc. It seems to be that """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""this is the way we have always done things"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and you just need to read through the hotel manual so that you know what to do and where.
I would not recommend this hotel to friends or family. It would be nice to tour it for the history, but staying there is not so nice.

Stayed here over the weekend of --------. Awesome hotel with a great location - but out of the rush. The rooms were so quiet with a flat screen TV. They were also clean and a great size for a NYC hotel. I have stayed at the W Times Sq and the Grand Hyatt - this was much better! Would stay again!
This hotel is located across from San Diego Airport. It has great view of the bay and marina. It is clean with comfortable beds and friendly staff.

Just one night. Quick check-in, though a little trouble over check-out time. My reservation was of a kind that included -pm check-out, but the desk clerk treated it as a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""request"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". We compromised on -pm, but I'm not sure what didn't get through from the reservation.
Quiet (mostly) room - odd banging outside(?) in the night. A-C was not easy to manage. Iron leaked more than steamed. 
Had a meal as part of a conference banquet - very good food and excellent waiters.
Also had a business meeting in one of their """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Board Rooms"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" - excellent facility & service.

We recently held a convention with around --- people here. As one of the convention staff, I'm used to working my tail off and you come to expect the staff at the hotel to behave a certain way. Often they are friendly and willing to help you but at the same time distant and getting complete cooperation from them can be a difficult task. Not at the Hilton Charlotte University Place. The team there was amazing! They made every attempt to insure that we had everything we needed. Constantly checking in with us while still allowing us to run our own event. I can not say enough about the staff here. They helped make our show the best we've had to date. Thanks Hilton folk :)

Let me first start by saying that I will never use Priceline.com again. I had never used it before and thought.....what the heck, I'll try anything once! I put in a price of $--- and Hotel Edgewater came back as the hotel that accepted my bid. Well after the taxes and parking ($--) our total room cost was about $---.... 
The hotel has great views.... but thats it! The rooms are cute, but super small. So small our suitcase had no place to even rest. The balcony, which looked to the south over the ocean was old and looked unsafe. All balconys are connected so you dont have your own, just a little privacy half wall that seperates yours from your neighbors, which means you cant keep your balcony door open all night because it would not be safe.
The check in went smooth and they were gracious and nice. Parking was outragous..... 
Overall, so-so. When I go to Seattle next time I would rather choose my hotel and know exactly what I am getting.

I stayed at this hotel during a last-minute business trip because it was the only hotel available in the Seattle area (Manchester United was playing so all hotels were full). The hotel is basic at best. Location is - minutes from SeaTac International airport, easy access to I-- to downtown. The staff is friendly and helpful, but one can't help but get the sense that manning the front desk is their """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""side job"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (everyone was dressed differently like they just rolled in from the nearest coffee house and their demeanor was friendly but nonchalant). There is a Chinese restaurant in the lobby which is not affiliated with the hotel, the food is not good - but I ate there anyway because it was late and I had an early start the next day. The rooms are your basic Ramada rooms. A bit dated, comforters, sheets, and towels were a bit worn and stiff from too much washing in bleach (hey, at least they bleached them!!). The bathroom was clean. Free internet was good. Microwave & ironing board in the room. Coffee maker didn't work. What bothered me most, and the reason for the low rating, was that the carpets in my room felt dirty, which made me feel that the entire room was dirty. It's one of those places that I just didn't feel comfortable walking barefoot.
All in all it was OK since I didn't have any other choice, but I would not come back if other options were available.

This hotel is in the best location on --th and Lexington. We were within walking distance of all the great shopping (after Christmas sales!), sights and restaurants. There is no need to stray more than a few blocks for great dinners at some of the best restaurants NYC has to offer. The Rockerfeller Center is - blocks away, Central Park and Times Square are just a bit further. We hardly needed to use any transportation because we were able to walk almost everywhere we wanted to go. There is a subway station conveniently located on the corner.
We stayed in a - bedroom apartment on the --th floor. The space was perfect for our family of four. It was clean, nicely decorated and roomy for NYC. The kids slept on the sofa bed in the living area. The kitchenette was helpful for snacks (we had jet lag, having traveled from Asia) and the continental breakfast downstairs was perfect for our light breakfast eaters. 
The only downside of our stay was having to be moved to another room on our last night because our bath was leaking into the room below (we had no idea). The staff was very apologetic and did their best to make the move easy for us. The new room on the --th floor had a lower ceiling and was a bit darker than our previous room.

It is true that it is not located in a good area of San Diego, but I felt safe and the parking lot was well lit. There are some parking spaces that are way too small, but others that are fine. Our heater-air conditioner did not turn off so it was unplugged when we got in the room. I quickly found the problem and pluged it in. The TV was set on a low dresser so I put it up on the table. The room had a small microwave and a fridge. There were signs of rust and abit of mildew in the bathroom, but overall it was clean. It did have a strong cleaning solution smell when we entered but it wasn't overwhelming and you quickly got used to it. The room we were in had a couch, so that was nice. The toilet didn't flush that great, but we just held the handle down and it was fine. I am glad that we didn't do the timeshare upgrade of -- bucks to a holiday inn. I would recommend this place for a cheap place to stay.

My husband and I stayed at the Belvedere in mid March for - nights. This was our first trip to NYC, and we will definately be back!
The Bevedere was a pleasant part of our stay. While we typically stay in slightly nicer hotels, this property was recommended to us as being reasonably priced, and with a great location. We were not disapointed. 
The positives:
- amazing location. Within walking distance of several subway lines, times square, a plethora of restaurants, and most Broadway theaters.
- Clean, well kept rooms. Ours was right next to the elevators, and we were initially quite concerned. I think this resulted in a slightly smaller room, but it was functional, and surprisingly quiet.
- an included buffet breakfast (book through the hotel website, and it is one of their 'deals'). Although not exactly gourmet, and they didn't change a single item in a week, the food was fine, quick, and a convenient way to start the day.
- kitchenette in all rooms. Handy if you have leftovers etc. or would like to keep drinks in the room.
The negatives:
- the room temperature seems to be an issue in this hotel. It is an older property, and has correspondingly older HVAC. Our room was pretty warm, but tolerable if we left the window open an inch or two.
- the elevators are terribly slow. We were on the --th floor, and you really had to allow 'elevator time' in anywhere you were going. A little secret...there are elevators at the opposite ends of the hallways that can be a bit more responsive, and have fewer stops along the way. They do, however, take them out of commission occasionally.
- make sure you bring some physical documentation of your reservation. There was a problem with our room rate when we first checked in. To their credit, the front desk staff were polite and dealt with it relatively quickly. I had confirmation numbers, screen prints, and was able to pull up their confirmation email on my black berry. If not though, we may have ended up paying a higher rate.
Overall, I was happy with the Belvedere. I consider it good value, and wouldn't hesitate to stay there again.

We stayed for three nights over a weekend and were delighted with every aspect of the hotel. The welcome is warm and professional, with a front desk team that will do everything they can to assist their guests. 
The rooms are extremely comfortable; perhaps the only observation would be that it is impossible to open the external-facing windows, leaving one reliant on air conditioning. That said, the rooms are spacious and well presented. 
I would highly recommend and would stay again. The hotel is ideally located, with most of the attractions of the centre of the town being in easy walking distance.

The rooms are clean, hotel is convenient but what really makes this hotel special is the Club Lounge! Connie keeps warm cookies and treats out all day! She does her best to make it a home away from home and always welcomes me with a big smile. You might gain a little weight but it’s well worth it!
