Context: This was my first visit to a Swissotel but not my first visit to a - or --star property in Chicago or any other major US city. I was staying at the hotel for a conference that was being held in the hotel, the negotiated conference price was very good for downtown Chicago.
The Good:
* The rooms: I stayed in just a King Standard room on the --th floor. The room was spotless, it was so clean that all the finishes and surfaces looked as though they might be brand-new. The room was spacious for a downtown setting and all the furniture was very comfortable, beautiful and in great repair. The bathroom felt luxurious for not being a suite including a separate tub and shower. I absolutely adore the Kohler plumbing fixtures, particularly including the shower head.
* Water pressure was great for a high floor and I had no problem keeping it hot (it seems that issue may have been resolved as reported recently by other reviewers)
* The in-room entertainment system is top-notch. I also loved the advanced array of hook-ups built into a discrete but very accessible side of the desk next to the TV where I could connect my laptop (or many other devices) to the large wide-screen LCD TV if desired. I really enjoyed it.
* I had a great view of the lake and the park next to the building, mostly unobstructed. Beautiful, clean and large windows. Great """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""staged"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" drapery system for just the right amount of light or none at all.
* Service: The service I experienced by the kitchen-room service staff was the only great service I experienced during the entire stay. Something is different about that segment of this hotel's staff, something excellent.

I heard mixed reviews with my peers at the sessions I was attending but as a technology geek, I personally loved them. I felt they were a great improvement to the efficiency of a busy downtown high-rise hotel and I found myself waiting for elevators for shorter periods of time than I remember ever waiting before, plus the cars were very fast-moving and quiet. Great investment!
The Bad:
* Construction: I understand that every property has to be renovated, but the current check-in system seated firmly in the event center lobby, well there's got to be a better way. Crowds conflicting constantly between events, guests trying to check-in or check-out, the concierge desk, luggage laying around everywhere - and no where at all to sit, unfold a laptop and do some business. Front desk agents are standing at tiny little podiums with laptops and attempting to communicate with hotel staff via a radio system.
The just plain Ugly:
* Front Desk-Check-in Service: How these people were given the job of being the first face that a new customer sees at a service-class hotel such as Swissotel is astounding to me. I observed as they were curt if not downright obnoxious to nearly every customer waiting in line to check-in for --+ minutes only to be told that their room wasn't ready (at -pm in the afternoon) and they would need to come back """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""at least"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" until after -. I arrived at the hotel exhausted and hungry from a long and early day of traveling and naturally I received the same response with no offer at all for help... just """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""come back after - and we'll see if we have a room ready for you"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". This is NOT --star service.
After I wandered around in the main floor for - minutes just looking for a place to sit and use my laptop - I actually found myself aggressively cornered by the doorman and a member of the front desk staff asking what I was looking for. They were clearly not attempting to help but trying to assess if I belonged there. That was humiliating and incredibly rude. I'm a guest at this hotel, I just told you that! Unbelievable.
Fortunately I was attending a conference at the hotel and the staff working for the conference organization were FAR more helpful in finding me a place to work on my computer and a place to just eat and rest for a while - while I waited for my room and attended some early sessions.
That's not the even end of my service story!
On the second day of my stay I was in my room resting between sessions when at about -:-- in the afternoon someone rang the door bell. It was some random member of staff literally asking why I was still in the room and if I had planned to stay over another night. I double-checked on my computer, my reservations were clear... I had reserved two nights. I informed the staffer of her misunderstanding and she told me someone would be in touch to work-out the confusion. Nobody ever called to apologize or explain. Why didn't someone call-up in the first place instead of making an in-person visit? Can you imagine how it feels to be standing at your doorway by a surprise visitor feeling like you're being asked to leave?
I successfully ordered room service that evening and my TV and room key was still working so I assumed that everything must be ok.
When I went to check-out on my final day, they weren't able to check me out of the hotel and give me a receipt because the computer informed them that I had already checked-out the previous day even though there was a room service charge on there for the day that I supposedly hadn't stayed. At this point the confusion was just laughable. This should be embarrassing for what's supposed to be a high-class hotel, that the employees can't even handle using the reservation system properly. I was later emailed a correct receipt by an office manager (as promised).
All-in-all, the next time I go to Chicago (later this year) I will stay just about anywhere but the Swissotel. The room was magnificent, but that's about the only thing they got right. Fortunately Chicago is a great city and has no shortage of great places to stay!

This hotel met my needs. Close to everything, so I got lots of walking in. Lots of things to see around the hotel. My room was on the park side and had large windows. Perfect to sit and enjoy. Only downfall is there is no fridge in the room, which would have been handy.

We declined since we had the extra set on us but we had the keys in our possession in a few days. You can see why this is my favorite hotel.

Reception is clean and quite elegant, with a pianist in the evenings which I personally just found very loud. Use internet access in small shop across the road, it is way cheaper than the one offered in the hotel and have a look from the --th floor public access roof balcony that is great. I cannot fault service, a lovely clean room each night and the NY Times each morning. Although I cannot really complain I found the whole place somewhat impersonal, I have stayed at grubbier places that were more homely and overall friendly, but I will give it another go more so because I really liked the area. Next time though I will definately go for a room at the front of the hotel with a view.

The beautiful lobby and great service is somewhat offset by the small, older rooms. The location is at the top of Nob Hill, which means it's just two (VERY steep) blocks from Chinatown, and two of the main trolly lines pass just outside.
There's not much within walking distance because of the steep hills, and the on-site restaurant prices are very high ($-- pp for breakfast).

We really enjoyed our short stay in San Diego - everyone had told us we would have fun in San Diego and we did! The Hotel Solamar is in a good central location very close to the convention centre, Petco park and close to lots of shops and restaurants. Our room was very nice overlooking the swimming pool - we stayed midweek and it was very quiet. We had cocktails at the pool bar which were very nice and we took advantage of the very popular -pm wine! We asked the staff for advice on where to go and what to do in San Diego, and also what restaurants to go to and they were incredibly helpful! I was showered with tourist leaflets and information and we ate in a great Mexican on the staff's advice.

We recently stayed at the BW Seven Seas hotel on our first trip to San Diego. We had never been there before so I'd booked strictly off of online research. Location ended up being good - centrally located when driving to zoo, sea world, beach, down town, old town (thank god for GPS). The look of the outside pool area was what attracted me to the place and ended up being my favorite part. Was so pretty and peaceful (quiet even though its close to freeway). Rooms were quiet too. Beautiful setting. Nice to have the restaurant there. Hotel was clean. Only downside was that the room was really small. We had - dbl beds for family of - and the room was so crowded. No extra room for suitcases, etc. Tiny bathroom. My mom stayed in a single and it seemed fine, but for more than - people, the room was way too small for long stay. Not much they can do to improve upon that. But San Diego had so many fun things to do we didn't spend much time in the room at anyway. Having a room that overlooked the pool and having the great relaxation time at the pool was worth it. Workout room, hot tub, ping pong table were all nice. Not sure we would have liked our stay as much had we been in one of the back buildings farther away.

The rooms were clean and comfortable. Location was great, you can walk to just about anywhere. We had a group of people celebrating a birthday during Memphis in May. We were able to walk to the Music Festival and Beale Street. The staff was the best part of the stay. They were extremely helpful and friendly, even taking some of our group to local stores.

I enjoyed my time here at this hotel. It's location is perfect, it's opposite Madison Square Garden and just across the street from Macys and only a short walk from all the other main attractions of NYC. The hotel is beautiful, very nicely decorated and lovely. Our room was really big with a bathroom, kitchen, wall length desk, tv and - double beds. The beds were so comfy and the room was clean which was the most important. There were - slight things wrong with the room. One being a gap next to the air con machine meaning cold air was coming in through the room (it was November so not warm!). We also accidently pulled the curtains down (as in the whole thing, pole and everything) and again upon returning to our room later on it had been fixed without us asking and with no charges made. We really appreciated this. The staff were all lovely. We didn't use any of the hotels services so can't comment on them, but i would definately consider using this hotel again.
Room was clean, spacious, and well appointed. Staff was extremely friendly made us feel welcome everytime we returned """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""home"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".

Very good stay. We stayed during the week so maybe less traffic, but was a good find.It is located in a safe area & right on the bus-tram route. That's the best way to go,, it's @ $-.-- - person to go downtown,plus you don't have to find a parking spot!!.The River Walk is a must do, so the bus saves time & money.
Back at the Hotel , the Pool is very nice & the landscaping is very well taken care of.The service is very helpful. The breakfast has plenty. Our neighbors were a little loud (@ -:--am to -am ) , getting ready for the day, they finally left. The rooms are comfortable , ours was arranged unusual, but worked . This hotel was great, very clean, great customer service. The only downfall was they have a dress code for the lobby after -:--pm (thats difficult for tourists walking around all day sweating) and no free internet in your room. I like the hospitality and friendliness of the staff of the hotel. Enjoyed our dinner at S Dynasty with its excellence food and romantic ambience. It's within walking distance to - Ave for shopping!

We thoroughly enjoyed our stay in this NYC icon. Although the price was quite high the location and comfort of this hotel more than made up for it. The rooms were really clean and tidy and the service was outstanding. We would return here next time in NYC just for the experience.

We booked through goPhila.com and got a great price for a --day stay. We chose this hotel for its location (near relatives we were visiting) and because we prefer smaller, non-chain hotels.
Overall, we were pleased with our accommodations. Service was pleasant and unobtrusive. We stayed on the fifth floor and found the room sufficiently bright and very clean. The hardwood floor was immaculate and the decor (lamps, table, desk) funky and not cookie cutter. We never did figure out the electronic system for lights, heat and wake up through the phone, but there were switches for all those functions so we didn't bother to ask. The dimmer didn't work on the clock, which was inconvenient because it was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""stuck"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on too dark to read from a distance. The mattress was very comfortable, but the bottom sheet was pilled and scratchy. Again, we didn't make a big deal of it; we slept on the top sheet covered by a fluffy duvet. It would have been nice to have a second chair in the room, since the only other place to sit was the bed- inconvenient at breakfast.
The bathroom was spacious and the dual headed shower delightful with plenty of hot water. The toiletries came in those annoying bottles with small necks that make hair washing like trying to pour ketchup. The towels were thick and luxurious as were the two robes. 
Continental breakfast was brought to the room at -, -, and - AM. We were able to choose from a short menu the day before (cereal, juice, fruit, muffin or yogurt.) The hotel has wireless and wired internet service (the cable was tucked into the desk) but again, we did not make use of this.

Stayed two nights on business. From the forecourt greeting onwards, the people who work at this hotel were amazing. Went out of their way, nothing was any trouble, even the boss introduced himself. Rooms are big, extremely well appointed, a Nespresso machine was a nice touch, as well as the TV screen in the middle of the bathroom mirror!!

My first time staying at a Howard Johnson property. I cannot give it higher marks. I checked it at ---- am. I was given a room for an early check-in. The front desk agent was extremely well spoken, while providing me with the highest posssible level of customer service and courtesy. The room was very clean and well equipped as was the entire facility for a hotel in the two star category. The management staff was equally approachable and receptive to input and discussion. Keep in mind this was all delivered with this hotel being one of the lowest rates in this part of the city. Finally, it seems as if this high standard was normal operating procedure. I highly recommend the HOJO Express Inn S.A. to anyone and will be returning in the future myself.

Very pleasant, fancy and well kept hotel near Union Station and Capitol Hill (great when we celebrated -th July there). The only thing I have to complain about was one of the women that worked in the bar. She was so rude that my mother and I acctually refrained from ordering drinks and a bite to eat.

Lovely, safe neighborhood where we have watched neighbors helping neighbors and strangers alike. There is a $---day parking garage available. I hope that they make no alterations to this property...as it is truly charming, just as it is... and a rare treat ...!

We were disappointed by this hotel. Our family of four stayed in this hotel for one night, at the end of our long weekend. It was convenient and the room was cramped, but the beds were comfortable and the room was clean. 
The bathroom was a problem. It seemed to be recently remodeled. They used a counter that seemed oversized for this small bathroom. Then, they stuck towel racks out from the counter, so you were jammed by the towel racks when you were sitting on the toilet. Additionally, the towel racks made it hard to close the door.
Service was a problem too. We were given only three bath towels and NO SOAP. We called down for soap and waited -- minutes. No one brought these items to our room. Upon check out, they asked if we had any issues during our stay. We provided the above comments. Management seemed uninterested.
The one bright note was the bar. We ended our one evening here and ordered drinks for the adults and dessert for the kids. the staff was very attentive, friendly and ended the evening on a very positive note. Kudos to the bar staff.

My recent stay here was a very pleasant one, found
no faults. Staff were very friendly and helpful, they
couldn't do enough for us. Good continental breakfast .
Excellent shuttle service to airport.

I stayed here with my daughter, who was in NYC for the summer, under the impression that this was one of New York's best hotels. Perhaps it once was but that is no longer the case. The rooms are tired and in dire need of renovation. A flat screen does not make a room - star if the bathroom was installed in the --s! The bar is fine but the dining area, which is part of the lobby, leaves much to be desired. Overall my impression was that too many cut price deals and cheap room rates brings down the reputation of this hotel. By choosing good hotels I rarely have the need to write bad reviews so this is a rare exception. I will not be visiting it again.

Super fantastic hotel. Great location. Great amenities. The king suites are huge and have a full kitchen in them!! Would be a great place to stay for a long stay in Charlotte. Be sure to check the Time Warner Arena schedule before booking. We made our reservations months ago, upon arrival we were surprised to find the hotel taken over by screaming girls going to see the One Direction concert next door. It made for long lines for the elevators and large crowds in the lobby. The hotel staff kept the chaos to a minimum and we never heard a peep in our room. We would definatley stay here again!!

We booked one night in a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""city view"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room. This was our first trip to Seattle. Hotel is in great location if you're visiting Pike Market. Fabulous customer service and roof deck. Clean, well-appointed room with great bed and pillows. The window air conditioning and street noise are unbelievably loud. Louder than New York City. If you're looking for a quiet, peaceful stay, this is definitely not your place. We didn't get much sleep.

My husband, son and I stayed at the Wilshire Crest recently for three nights and were extremely happy. We were part of a group of -- who stayed at the hotel in order to attend my nephew's wedding, which was held nearby. The attention we received, the management's willingness to accommodate us and the general atmosphere of this boutique hotel all made for a wonderful weekend in LA. Mr. Tomaszewski and his staff went out of their way to make sure we had everything we needed. The rooms were spacious and clean with a full bathroom as well as an extra vanity outside the bathroom, super comfy beds with an extra rollaway for my son, a mini-fridge, massive closet, coffee maker and a guide to LA. Everything was sparkling and one of our group checked for bed bugs and pronounced the beds ---% fine. Breakfast was ample (coffee, milk, juice, bagels, jam, butter, cream cheese, cold and hot cereal, fruit, cut up vegetables, assorted cake) and the staff came frequently to replenish the bagels and to clean any stray cereal that spilled. The lobby was inviting (they even provide a computer for the use of the guests-we printed our boarding passes) with plush chairs and sofas, the outside terrace area, peaceful and the location to many places of interest, perfect.
The night after the wedding we stayed at the LAX Hilton, to be closer to the airport for a very early AM flight. The Hilton had nothing in the room that was any different from what the Wilshire Crest provided and it was not as reasonable or as homey.
I would gladly return to this hotel and recommend it highly. Large chains can't give that same personal attention. I thank Mr. Tomaszewski, on behalf of our entire group, for a wonderful weekend that we will long remember.

So many Residence Inn's are run of the mill, no differentiation, no charm. Not this one. Fantastic, room guest rooms. Excellent on site restaurant, complimentary breakfast and Wi-Fi. I love trying new properties when I visit cities but I do not think I will when I stay in Baltimore.

I got really lucky finding this hotel at the price I did. It's a very nice hotel in a great location. The staff is friendly and helpful. The rooms are modern and clean. I wouldn't recommend paying for the breakfast at the hotel. Save the money for a better place. The best thing about the hotel is that it's across the street from the Space Needle and the monorail that takes you to Pike's Place.

Steps from the subway line, this hotel is built for people wanting to go see the city. While not in Times Square proper, this location offers all the perks with none of the annoyances. Ask for a high level floor, and you'll sleep in one of the quietest rooms in Manhattan. Even being next to a fire station, you'd never know it. Front end staff can be a bit harried at times, but the bellman are first rate. I'd stay here again in a heartbeat.

Near Soldier Field, Grant Park, museums and attractions. 
Great value for location.
Rooms are just average.
Skip the hotel breakfast and go to Yolk, just around the corner on S. Michigan ave. Don't miss it

After a long flight to Newark and transfer to Manhattan arrived at the Westin New York Times Square. As a Starwood Platinum Member normally get upgrades to standard suites, but not at this hotel. The rates are way to high for the too small rooms in this hotel.
As well as the executive lounge which had almost nothing to offer. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""breakfast"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was nothing more than in a - star motel. The service was also not worth more than - stars, even in New York. 
The only good thing about the hotel is its location.

a beautiful elegant hotel-that is luxurious to stay. service was impeccable friendly and warm.
the maids were always ready to be of service. Valet extremely knowledagle and honest with recommendations. which was very surprising to hear.

The Hotel had a great art deco feel to it, the room-property was clean & presentable, the manager was very nice & helpful with complimentary cookies at check-in , the location is a little further from Pier -- & china Town than I prefer but it was centrally located to almost everywhere in the city. All & all a nice stay.

I recommend this hotel to anyone visiting San Francisco. I stayed there with my girlfriend from May --th to June -rd.
Its located about ----- mins from the centre and the bus stop is - block away. 
The local area has a few bars and restaurants to keep you entertained if you want things within walking distance.
Im from the UK & the room was larger than you would find in a simirlarly priced hotel in the UK. Lots of TV channels to choose from if you relax in your room, and nicely refurbished bathrooom - bedroom. Good size bed as well.

We got a great price and stayed here for four nights! We would have walked more if not for the heat during this week and could have seen more of Chicago's beautiful buildings. Still, we were able to walk to Michigan Ave. which is just a block away, Chicago River, Millenium Park and Navy Pier. Holy Name Cathedral is also a few blocks away. It's also very close to restaurants and food shops so we were able to sample the deep dish pizza and Garrett's popcorn. Food can be more expensive though compared with other areas. (McDonalds' sausage McMuffin is around -- cents more expensive.) 
Being in the pool, although small, is still a refreshing place to be. We picked odd hours so it was never full. Staff always greets the guests and was always happy to give directions. There were coffee and tea every morning at the lobby so people can just grab a cup if they didn't have time to brew in their rooms. We will definitely come back to this hotel.

Great little place! Clean, old, but nice for the price! We will go back! 
Took the Red Line to Addison and the Cubs game and then on to Bryn Mar. There is a bus that runs right by the Motel if you get there before -- p.m. but they start back up at - am! This is how to enjoy Chicago on a budget! We stayed to late at the game and walked to the motel. Not too bad of a neighborhood, nor too long of a walk.

This hotel is centrally located to everything. Five blocks to almost everything downtown has to offer. The prices are very cheap compared to other hotels, almost $--- less then the other hotels in the same area.

If you don't have transportation (and who wants to pay $------night to park their car!), this hotel is very convenient to Chinatown, Alcatraz, Fisherman's Wharf, and other tourist sites.
The only negative is that the free Wifi is available only in the lobby. It will cost you to log on in your room. I found this fact very annoying!

Stayed - nights earlier this month. Entrance to a hotel is a small lobby with a lift to the hotel recpetion. Reception very informal but pleasant. Room was average size - the biggest bathroom we had on our trip to - US cities with a great shower although no bath to have a soak in! Corridors a bit bashed where luggage has scuffed the walls and could have benefitted from a lick of paint, the windows in the room needed a good dust and clean. Air conditioning and fridge in room very noisy; we switched both off at night. Breakfast basket was delivered to room - basic and oatmeal was to cook in the microwave yourself. Choice of croissant or bagel would have been nice. As a tea drinker it didnt quite taste the same warming the water in the microwave or putting it through the coffee machine without a coffee bag. Our breakfast was late both mornings, the second morning us having to go and ask for it so we could eat before leaving. Ipod dock in room was good, large TV with good choice of channels. No inroom safe. Central location; wouldnt like to walk back late at night as a single woman but was fine as a couple.

Great location within walking distance of Times Square. Spacious King room, very clean although bathroom small but functional. Staff helpful with tea and coffee available ---- in the Lobby area,
Plentiful self serve breakfast and free Internet. Highly recommend this Hotel for the location and value for money as it is New York afterall.

We stayed at the paramount hotel for - nights at the end of march. The rooms were clean, the beds were surprisingly comfortable and the linens were quite soft and modern. The location is close to everything from Pike Place Market, to the department stores, to the monorail to whisk you off to the Space Needle and the EMP music museum. Friendly staff, the only drawback was the parking fees, but I found them to be comparable to those in Vancouver.

We enjoy taking the subway when we are in New York so the location is great. They have wonderful buffet breakfast ( a little pricey) but worth it. We typically stay on the club level, so you receive a continental breakfast with your room rate, they also have lite snacks (very lite) during the afternoon. We have not been there in the evening to enjoy the desserts, so I have no comment on that. The staff is very friendly and helpful. The hotel is just a short train ride from time square. My husband and I enjoy going into Grand Central having a coffee and just watching everyone. Great place to stay. Very easy to find and get back to when you have been out walking around.(Everyone knows where Grand Central is)remember it is right next door.

The first night we stayed we had a room that was impossible to sleep in. When the air conditioning turned on it made an incredible loud banging sound. We went to the front desk the next day to request a different room and share our concern. We were assigned a different room. While we were there waiting to talk to the concierge ( a very helpful gentleman) we met Keith Jones, the Director of Rooms. We shared our problem w-him and he indicated that an adjustment could be made to our bill. We gave him our name and room number. On the day we checked out I called the front desk to see if this had been done. It wasn't. I talked to - different people and they both stated that our bill had been prepaid so they didn't have the authority to make an adjustment. I told them about the conversation w-Keith Jones. They said he did have the ability to make an adjustment. Took our home phone number and told us he would call. It's been - days. Haven't received a call. Not happy w-the way we were treated.

stayed here on the first and last day of our two week holiday in september.

a easy walk to the major car hire firms, so you can have a good nights sleep then go and pick your car up without having to lug your cases with you.a decent hotel for the price
with breakfast included.

My wife and I styaed at this Super - on the --st May for two nights.We found the room very comfortable,I had booked this after changing from staying at Torrance thinking it would be closer to Universal Studios which we wished to visit.

The hotel itself was,as I have said very comfortable and the breakfast was more than sufficient with cereal, orange juice ,coffee and all manner of bagels, danish pastries and cakes (fresh this morning from baker) and more than enough to start the day.

Just down the road we visited Sizzlers and ate two Rib Eye steaks that just melted in the mouth,salad bar,grilled onions a Heineken and Merlot total bill $--.-- and at todays rate works out at £--.-- what a bargain.All in all a very pleasant location and well worth vsiting this motel

Stayed overnight with my husband and daughter for our annual """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Christmas in NY"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" celebration. The Palace, particularly at this time of year, is a beautiful oasis in a wonderful location. Rockefeller Center, Radio City, American Girl, FAO Schwarz, Saks, etc. are all a very short walk. 
We were uprgraded to a higher floor with a view directly across from St. Patrick's Cathedral all the way across town and the Hudson which was truly striking both day and night (room ----). They provided our six year old daughter with her very own NY Palace teddy bear. The parking, check in and bag service was all very smooth and rapid. Both Istana and Gilt had great service and offered much to see. The hotel is great because you don't feel overwhelmed--it's almost cozy. 
The original fireplaces and mouldings, etc. from the mansion are impresisive and provide a dramatic backdrop for holiday photos. The tasteful holiday decorations, including a beautifully lit tree in the courtyard are lovely. 
While The Palace is not quite as luxurious as a Mandarin or Four Seasons, it is perfect understated elegance. I found it to be considerably nicer than the Waldorf. The rooms are very generous size for NY. The staff, the decor, the gym, the beds, turndown and personal service are all wonderful. 
Everyone is willing to help or assist whenever needed--highly recommend, particularly during holidays with family. Cannot beat location!!

Ive been traveling a lot and stayed in many different hotels since my job is a flight attendent and I can tell this hotel was definitely one of my favorite hotels!
I traveled with husband and our -months old daughter. Room was very clean and especially the bathroom was. We got a room with kingsize bed and a little crib for our daughter(I think it would be better if you could bring your own crib sheet and bumper since they just cover the crib mattress with normal adult mattress sheet). We stayed there for - nights.
First day we decided to take the free ride hotel was providing and walk back to the hotel from downtown. That was little too much for us because the hotel is on high hill and we had to carry baby stuff and the baby. But if we were traveling by ourselves, we wouldve enjoyed walking even though we are not the best walkers. The neighborhood is really peaceful, nice, and well taken care.
Service was really great. We didn't have much time to plan about our tirp before we went there, but the first day we got there, the staff showed our room explained about the city and recommended places to go and that helped out a lot. Very small details about their service impressed us.
Paking around the hotel wasn't hard at all and we didn't pay anything for parking(compare to the hotels in downtowny that you need to pay about $----- for parking per day, it wonderful). Free internet access was pleasant as well. Iron board, iron that they had in the roon were clean, too(it doesnt happen with every hotel in my experience). Also complementary continental breakfast was really wonderful. Fresh baked bread was prepared everymorning and great staff delivers you freshly brewed latte or cappucinno. Usually I don't expect much with complementary breakfast(especially when it's continental) but it nicely filled us up every morning. We enjoyed good price room service sandwiches very much as well.
I really think it was great choice and would go back to this one when we go back to visit San Francisco.

A friend and I stayed at this hotel for a recent professional conference and had a very bad experience. The first night, a drunken man started banging on our door at -:-- AM and constantly knocked on our door and window for several minutes. We were two women alone in a hotel room in an unfamiliar city and didn't want to try to deal with it ourselves, so we called the front desk to have the manager chase him off. The desk worker on duty hung up on my roommate when she told him our problem. She immediately called back and asked if they could do something about it and was told, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Just tell him to go away,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" before she was hung up on a second time. The knocking man wandered off on his own shortly afterwards, though we had been seriously considering calling the police since the management obviously didn't care about the safety of their guests. We thought this was incredibly unprofessional. The next day, our room was very cold and we couldn't get the heater in our room working. We called the front desk to ask about it and were told they couldn't do anything about it. They didn't even offer to move us to a different room, despite the fact there were several empty rooms we could have moved into. We asked for extra blankets and were told they didn't have any - again, there were several empty rooms. We spent - days freezing in our room before they were able to find a single spare blanket - not that helpful considering we had - beds - and it didn't look clean enough to use anyway. The next to last day of our trip, I wanted to call home and couldn't get the phone in our room to work. I called the front desk and was told that I had to pay a $-- phone deposit to have the phone line in our room turned on. I was making a single toll-free call with a calling card and thought this was a little ridiculous. Still, I went down to the office and payed the deposit and asked again about getting our heater fixed because our room was barely warmer than it was outside. This time, the desk worker told me that to get the heater working, we had to turn the temperature dial all the way to the cold side and then turn it on. Though completely counterintuitive, this worked when I tried it. We turned the heater off while we were out for conference activities that evening. When we turned it on after we returned, sparks started shooting out of the heater and the room was immediately filled with an acrid burning smell strong enough we had to open the door to air out the room, thus driving out what little heat we had managed to trap in the room. We spent our last night in a frigid room.
This was probably the worst hotel I've ever stayed in, and I'm pretty cheap when it comes to these things. I've never been to a hotel that obviously cared so little about their guests. It would have expected this sort of service if the room was $-- a night in San Diego, but the hotel wasn't cheap. It was certainly not worth the money we paid. This hotel could have been so much better with just a little effort and caring from management and staff.

I went downstairs to inquire if I could get some and was told they no longer supply it to guest as they took a survey and guests have said they never use it, and that most hotel no longer give out hair conditioner. I find this hard to believe as I travel quite a bit on business and every hotel I have stayed at supplies hair conditioner, or atleast a - in - product, talk about cheap.
There was no information about the hotel services in the room, I found out on the -rd night they have a movie theater by the bar area in the lobby with free popcorn. I also found out later in my stay that they had bikes for guest to use, again no mention of this from the staff or in the room . Wore white socks around the room the first night and couldn't see anything on the bottoms. The tub-toilet area of the bathroom is not fancy. Just a simple tub and toilet. If you are expecting glass shower surrounds and seperate tub and shower area, you might want to look elsewhere. Our room was on the ground floor of a two-storied building and was SUPER quiet. We could only hear our neighbors when they were coming in their door from the outside. We could hear our upstairs neighbors walking around occassionally, but overall...probably one of the quietest we have ever stayed in. Room was a great size for our family of -. Our littlest slept on a toddler cot we brought from home. We requested a microwave and with that and the refrigerator, we were able to make several light meals in our room.
Location, location, location! Seriously, it can't be beat. Loved being on the bay and one block from the beach. It was our son's -th birthday the day we arrived and upon checking in, the gal helping us out, made it a point to wish me happy birthday for him and gave us a nice little perk...free parking for our stay. That was awesome!!! Our kids used the pool every day and had a blast. It was never overly busy in the pool area and was very family-friendly. 
Mission Beach is a beachy, down-to-earth community. If you are expecting more glitz and glamour, perhaps you should try La Jolla Shores area. I have spent many summers (in my youth) at Mission and PB and I love that it is so casual, comfortable and not overly-pretentious. The restaurants are small and there really aren't any big chains in the area (unless you count Subway?). 
We ate a couple times at the little Mexican restaurant right next to the hotel and it was super yummy (and very afforadable). We also ate at World Famous...beach-ocean view and it is a nice, family restaurant. When eating there with small children, we actually prefer to sit in the bar area over the regular restaurant because there are more kid-friendly meal options (plus, it's cheaper). 
The Catamaran was very easy to find and very close to Sea World and other touristy areas. 
Only recommendation for the hotel...self-laundry service. The hotel laundry is too expensive and if you are staying for an extended time, it would be nice to have laundry facilties on-sight.

I appreciated the philosophy and the decor of the hotel; however, I was disappointed by three things:
(-) Despite their assertion that lowest rates are always found on their website, I was able to find a significantly lower rate via online resource (in this case, Hotels.com). Of note, I had even directly emailed the manager regarding rates, but was simply directed back to their website.
(-) I had trouble picking up the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""free"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" wireless in my room, and found my connection to be exceedingly slow.
(-) Upon checkout, a charge for a minibar beer appeared on my bill although I never even opened the minibar; while this was ultimately removed, it should never have been there in the first place.
I hope the hotel can improve these small annoyances, because it has the potential to be a really nice place.
Was a great hotel. Staff were friendly and helpful. Great location. Had a free wine hour down in the Restaurant. Clean rooms.Would stay again

Stayed here two nights and had no problems. Good location in a safe area and close to the airport. Resturants were close by. Mamagement was very nice. I stayat sleep inns al the time and this was a little better than the average Sleep Inn.

Room was small but clean, the bathroom was a good size for New Yor. air con was great, the staff were friendly and helpful. The breakfast had a nice selection but get there earlier so as to not miss out. Had free wifi in room good speed didnt drop out. Location is fantastic the buzz of times square is a -min walk up the street!

I have stayed a couple of times at the Four Points Shearton in Indianaplois - Carmel. I always have a good stay. The staff is great about remembering your likes and preferences. Supporting quick reservations and service. The bartender and grill is great with the bartender, Kyle, remembering the wine I drink without even a reminder. The value for the price is great!!! I would highly recommend the Four Points at Carmel.

We had two rooms for three nights over New Years. Location is great for walking to so many things - restaurants, Independence Hall, and the museums up on Ben Franklin Pkwy. It is a shame they get you on parking -- there is no way around it. We self parked at the garage behind the hotel (this is where the valet parking is anyway....I don't know why folks use the valet parking, frankly). With kids, I normally like complimentary breakfast, which this hotel does not have; however, with Reading Terminal Market, Dunkin Donuts, and ---- so very close, we simply made sure we had food in our room for breakfast each day the night before. There is a refrigerator in each room. The pool and fitness room are very nice and both of these were priorities for us. Housekeeping fine, but nothing spectacular. My husband and son had a little trouble with the wifi cutting out if you were on for a while.

We stayed over Easter weekend ---- as we were in town for a wedding. We had a king bed room with a roll-away. Though the rooms are smaller, the beds were comfortable, the room was very clean, the staff could not have been more helpful. Everything within walking distance, museums, restaurants, churches, Central Park, and cabs to to be had on either corner. We would definitely stay again!!

In January ---- I stayed - nights and in August ----, - nights. Both were for a class that was being held on the property. I slept there, studied there, ate there...lived there. This review will cover both trips, since the review is the same with one exception.
The facility is excellent. Very clean and well maintained. The location is within walking distance of most of downtown Denver.
The staff is professional and genuinely care. The only staff issue I encountered was in August when a certain waitress refused to serve us...I have no reason why. She wouldn't even look over at our table. I requested a different server and discussed the incident with the restaurant and hotel manager. The next day, I was seated in her section and she got someone else to serve my table. Later that week, she was very unprofessional to one of my colleagues. I don't think she's a bad person, but perhaps food-service doesn't leverage her strengths. Other than that, everyone was awesome. 
The meeting rooms were a good size and had everything you needed. Well done.
Definitely will recommend. I'll be back in January and August ---- and January ----.

We were a group of five girls from Northern Ireland travelling to Boston for a Christmas shopping trip. We had booked a triple and double room. On arrival we were shown to - identical rooms each with - double beds (queen sized for the UK readers, huge for single sleepers but tiny for - adults sharing); we mentioned to the wonderful bell boy we'd booked a triple and a double and we (the - sharing) were easily upgraded to a king suite with sofa bed. The rooms were well kept, clean and with adequate space, with lovely crabtree and Evelyn toilettries The staff we fantastic in the hotel; I had problems using a $--- travellers cheque in one shop (not accepted in most of Boston due to a freud problem), yet the conceierge went totally out of his way to find a store who would cash it for me, he was amazing, thanks Charles. The reception was welcoming with wood panneling and seasonal Christmas decor, enhanced by complementary hot chocolate or mulled apple available from mid afternoon onwards. The restaurant provided lovely food, but it was was pricey: there is an excellent Irish pub for evening meals and deli's for breakfast on the door step though. The location was great, the city is so walkable, Quincys Markets is - minutes walk away, yet the hotel was quiet- some of us who had previously stayed in NewYork for shopping trips were amazed at how silent the rooms were at night, and how quiet the streets were. We were so happy, we're already booked again for Dec ---- which says it all!

I decided to give this Sheraton property another chance being that it is one of my least favorite Starwood properties mostly because as a Platinum guest, this hotel has NEVER tried to earn my business nor even recognize my status. First, parking is still $--.-- for self park in an outdoor lot. The hotel has an outdoor pool and has two towers or wings. I drove up to the main wing where the club lounge is and was told that my reservation was for the other tower and when I arrived at the other tower I was told that I had a room reserved at the other tower and this would have continued if I did not end it and ask both towers to just assign me a room. Needless to say, they put me in the tower that does not have a club lounge nor did they want to compensate with a drink coupon. They did not seem to care and the checkin desk did not have a gold-platinum desk so there are no perks for being platinum. When I got to my room, I had a wonderful view of Harbor Drive and the airport. The other side overlooks N. Island and downtown. I guess that these rooms are still unavailable for platinum guests. The rooms are nicely redone but very small. The rooms all have electronic minibars and I did find one bottle of water was free as per the tag on the bottle. Typically, folks do not open the minibar for fears of being charged up to $-.-- for a bottle of water. Here, the complimentary bottle is free so I recommend getting it. The decor is nautical in nature and colors and they did a good job redecorating the room. The bathroom was also updated and the sink has a white marble top with porcelain sink. The rooms all have motion sensors that tie the cooking and lights together and when you leave, they will shutoff the power as a means of conserving energy. The rooms are dark due to low power energy efficient bulbs.

I recently brought a group of teenagers there for the National FFA Convention. The staff was most courteous and helpful. There are several restaurants within walking distance and access to downtown was quick. The rooms were not fancy but they were clean and smelled fresh. We will stay there again.

The woman who issued me tag for three pieces of luggage, where the most valuable one (including easily pawned items) conveniently disappeared, now she claims that my missing piece is a different color than it was, so her boss says """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Sue us"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".
They are fine until a problem emerges. Then if you can't stick around San Diego for weeks to fight them in Small Claims Court, you're out of luck and this untrustworthy staff knows that!
Don't have anything of value any where near this den of thieves!

I went on line reading reviews and expected a great experience at the Omni, but recieved quite the opposite. The staff was unfriendly. We pre-purchased dinner and breakfast but the hotel did not have correct when we checked in, this provided extra work on our part since the Fireside was curt when we presented the voucher. Room view was horrible, we looked out at nothing but brick wall. The front desk was not accomendating nor where the bellman. It must have been an off weekend because this was not what I expected. I would not stay there again. The location was okay but quite a distance away from time square, need great walking shoes or take a cab. Very bad experience and it was a surprise for my husband birthday. We made the best of it.

My husband and I stayed at the Bristol Hotel for two nights in May. The best part of this hotel is definitely the service - we received excellent service from the valet, front desk personnel, maid, bellman and restaurant host (even though we weren't eating at the restaurant.) We stayed on the -th floor (the dog friendly floor since we had our dog with us) and our room's window faced away from the street, so we didn't experience any of the street noise that some other reviewers complained about. The location of the hotel is right downtown, so you will have to deal with a cast of vagrants, transients, homeless people and drunks, but that's what you'd get at pretty much any mid to large city's downtown area. 
Our room was clean, the amenities were nice, the mattress was a little softer than I normally like and the bathroom was too dark, but overall this hotel was worth the money. It's in walking distance of the Gaslamp area as well as most of the things you'd want to do downtown, so the location is great. 
Finally, the only downside was the nearest grassy areas to take the dog. One is on the street where the train-tram runs and a lot of homeless people hang out, so I was a little uncomfortable taking the dog out late at night - I instead sent my husband. The other grassy area is near the mall, so it's a nicer area, but it's a couple of blocks away, so not as convenient for a quick bathroom break.

The hotel is perfectly situated between two metro stations and there are also bus stops nearby,making it easy to get around.The hotel itself has a comfortable and relaxed atmosphere and the reception staff were always friendly and willing to help with any queries.The free breakfast was a bonus,served in a clean dining room with no feeling of being rushed.Although the restaurant was closed for refurbishment during my stay it was easy to order takeout or book tables at local eateries.The laundry was good,although rather than use the dryer I hung the clothes in the room and they dried quickly.The room was well equipped with a fridge,microwave,alarm clock,hairdryer,coffee maker,iron and board and the bed was VERY comfortable.
My only quibbles were the small towels,the lack of an overhead light in the room and the extremely slow elevator!Overall,it was good value and I would recommend it.

Absolutely loved this place and would definitely stay there again. Would recommend it to anyone. Only - blocks from the beach. Loads of restaurants on the same street - check out the Italian C&O up the road. Great bar right next door. Gorgeous rooms. The best thing about it was the staff. They were so friendly and helpful. A real gem.

My family and I stayed at the AKA for over -- months as our house was being repaired. Everything about the AKA is excellent. The staff is extremely helpful and accomodating. The rooms are spacious and modern. The hotel is perfectly located in a great part of Center City. We highly recommend for a short or long term stay.

Great location near trolly line and lots of resturants. The employees were great and very helpful, even housekeeping. This was a small older hotel, but very clean and comfortable. We had a refridgerator, coffee pot, sink, and a microwave, but there were many places to eat near by. We also walked to the mall and shopped at union square. Only one place to eat in the hotel, but the food was good there also.

I had a --night stay at this hotel during a business trip. During my stay I was interviewing people in my room and the suite part came in handy. The King suite I had was smaller than other Suite hotels but nonetheless, charming. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful, especially Laura at the front desk. She always greeted me by my name each time she saw me. The lobby is very cozy and well decorated and you can enjoy their coffee bar there ---- as well. The breakfast was well stocked and there was plenty of space inside as well as on the patio.
My only complaint was that the air conditioner had a funny smell to it, which didn't bother me all that much since I was there in November. This hotel is in a busy area, with nearby restaurants that you can walk to but any of the outside noise didn't bother me, and I was towards the front of the hotel. I had a great experience at this hotel and I would recommend it and stay there again.

My boyfriend and I stayed while apartment hunting in DC. The hotel was great and top notch. Breakfast was super packed inside everyday because of the heat wave, but service was great and the staff was pleasant all the time. Not to mention the hotel was down right beautiful.
We've stayed here numerous times and always found the staff friendly, helpful and willing to do whatever it took to make our stay comfortable.
You will love this place, stay if you have the chance. It's right on the ocean and plenty to do and eat. Just a lot of fun.

We stayed for - nights, safe did not work after - times of reporting it and - times of taking our valuables to the holel safe. The hotel told us - times they had fixed it and had not. Room was old, very old. The bathroom was small, very small and the shower was weak and slow to say the least. We were """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""upgraded"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to the towers but in reality they had run out of useable rooms (so the receptionist told us """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""off the record""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""). The continental breakfast was so inadquate we had to eat again outside the hotel straight afterwards. Would I use this hotel again??? Not ever.

I stayed at the Doubletree for - nights, at a priceline price of $-- per night.
This was my second time staying at the hotel, so I knew what to expect, and everything was as expected.
I remembered from my last stay that (especially when booking through priceline?) there was a very long walk to the room. At check-in I was offered a handicapped room closer to the lobby, but after looking at the room, I decided that it wasn't really an appropriate room for a non-handicapped person (shower hose was about waist high, closet rails were also low).
So I was given a room in the wing farthest from the lobby. On my first walk to the room, I got lost, and ended up outside, then back inside, and walking up and down stairs several times. On later excursions back and forth, I figured out a more efficient route.
The room was spacious, clean and comfortable. Good assortment of TV channels. Comfortable bed. Room service was available late, but the after --PM options weren't very tasty. A nice touch is that the hotel has several exercise rooms, so there's one nearby when you want to work out. Nice equipment too.
The hotel is close to the airport, and the light rail system that runs to the city means that you can get into the city for less than $-.
The biggest negative is that they don't award Hilton Honors points if you're staying through priceline, even for things like room service.
I'd definitely stay there again, especially with the priceline rate.

I recently stayed in this hotel four - nights this past April due to it's high ratings on TripAdvisor. I frequent San Francisco a few times every couple of years, so I enjoy being able to stay at different hotels, but this to me was an overall disappointment. 
I will start by saying that yes, the location of the hotel is great, but there are a lot of other """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""true"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" - star hotels that have great locations as well. 
The rooms themselves are quite small and had I been staying any longer, or travelling with luggage (I just had carry-on) I would have found the space to have been much too cramped. The room I received was facing the inside courtyard, so there was no obvious street noise which was nice, BUT, the rooms are not sound proofed at all! You can clearly hear doors shutting to other rooms, TV's in adjacent rooms, conversations as people passed by your door...If you're a light sleeper, good luck. 
The overall quality of the room wasn't much better either. It looked more like a cover up job, than a remodelling job. The door to the bathroom had chips and scratches all over it, the baseboards were cracked and had visible marks all over them, they had forgot to sand before patching something in the ceiling, the window sills were filthy and showing their age...Like I said before, not a - star. 
The front desk staff were pleasant, but had there issues as well. It is difficult to hail a cab from this particular hotel. The bellman-front desk agent actually gave up when I was trying to get a cab to go to AT&T park and referred me to the hotel across the road. I also requested a wake-up call on my last morning, and they completely forgot. 
When I return to San Francisco, I won't be returning to the Hotel Abri.

I usually go to Marriott but the local one was full. The sherayon ended up being cheaper, had a much nicer pool and jacuzzi, gound my prefered status (i was not even aware i had one with chain). Decent and reasonably priced restautant and bar. Outside of that low end hotel circle that I find depressing. I still don't like the mission valley area in general, but if you stay there because of your budget, the Sheraton is a good pick.

Stayed at The Belvedere for - nights and overall thought the hotel was really good value. Room was clean and well decorated and was larger than we expected given what we had read about New York hotels. The location is really good (took under - mins to walk to Times Sq). Also, on the final day they held our bags until the evening after we checked out without any problems which was really useful. Only real gripe was the unhelpful concierge. Basically, it seems that they have contracts for transport (obviously not the cheapest!) and will not help to arrange alternatives. That said, we did book Shuttle Bus to JFK through them and the driver couldn't have been more helpful.

I stayed at this hotel over several days during NYE in Dec ---- - Jan ---- and really enjoyed my stay. The front desk staff were very friendly and the bellhop took extra time to go over everything in the room so we would know how to work everything. 
The location was perfect! We were able to walk to many shops, restaurants, bars and the meatpacking district is also within walking distance. If you are going any further, there is a subway station just up the block and the doormen will also help you find a cab. 
As some of the other reviews said, the place is pretty dark inside and feels like a club. It definitely made me want to dress and look nice while walking through the lobby so I wouldn't feel out of place. This hotel is more for people looking for a modern and trendy hotel and not for families with children (though I did see a few kids). I stayed in a regular room and it was small but that is too be expected in NYC so no complains there. The room was clean though so that is a huge plus to me. I get grossed out easily by hotels and want the room to feel clean enough for me to be comfortable staying. Also, the bathroom has a (peep)hole where the knob would normally be so you can see right into the bathroom. Just an FYI if you are staying with anyone else in the room.
I ate downstairs for a late lunch-early dinner and remember enjoying the food. I can't remember anything about room service, so to me that means the food-service wasn't bad but wasn't anything special that would cause me to remember it. 
The view from the club upstairs (PH-D) is very nice! I would recommend going up early to have a drink-apps and check it out. The club itself is not owned by the hotel (similar to how Vegas clubs work) so entry after -pm I think? is up to the bouncers, whether or not you are a hotel guest. I know some people would not be happy with that policy but I didn't mind. Yeah, it would be nice if you could get in just for being a hotel guest, but they don't own it so it is what it is. 
The only that happened during my stay that could be negatives for other people (weren't a big deal to me): Since it was NYE, they had really loud music pumping for an extremely long time. I assumed it was just for that weekend but some of the other reviewers seem to mention club noise as well on other weekends. I am a heavy sleeper so once I fall asleep, I can sleep through noise like that. Another thing was one of my hall neighbors came back around ---am and started making a lot of noise outside her door (bf passed out inside-lost her key-can't remember). I didn't care so I didn't call downstairs or ask her to quiet down, but it could potentially be an issue for some people on weekends when drunk people come back. 
I would definitely go back and stay at this hotel again. They also have an outdoor pool, so it would be a nice place to stay when it's warmer out.

After reading the reviews on Tripadvisor I was quite skeptical about staying at here, but I'm really glad I did! 
The location is insanely convenient, and if you look up hotels in and around that area you'll realize just how much better the value for money is here. A decent breakfast is included, and if your on the run it's actually pretty convenient. As for the sheets on the windows, they actually told us beforehand that they were renovating and they didn't have curtains yet. I stayed during the President's Day-Valentine's day long weekend, and in spite of it being sold out I didn't think noise was a problem. 
The bottom line is, you get what you pay for. If you don't want to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""rough it out"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (and trust me, it's not that bad) in central San Francisco, than stay somewhere else, otherwise this is really a great bargain.

It was not cheap, but the rooms are great, breakfast excellent, the service from everyone from housekeeping, to front desk, to the restaurant was about as good as it could get. If you have a car, you will pay $-- to park. But this is a very good place. Rooms spotlessly clean.

Modern, clean and bright rooms. Warm and welcoming staff. Easy and pleasant place to stay. Handy for Dupont Circle area but not walking distance to international financial insitutions - taxi is only $- each way. Restaurant menu limited - could have some vegetarian options for example. Well set up for business travellers including power points and high speed internet - though if you've paid for secured access, watch you don't end up using hotel's free wireless system as some of the tech staff don't understand the difference.

Very pleasant hotel in many ways, but our last stay here was spoiled by the three hour wait to check in. It's one thing to say """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The room's not ready,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" another to say """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""It'll be ready in -- minutes,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and then, an hour later, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""It'll be ready in - minutes,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and then, and hour later, to still leave your guests waiting. Meanwhile we had to wait in the lobby, where the wireless was so slow as to be barely functional. It's so easy to fix something like this, and so odd to find this kind of service in a hotel of this caliber.

Everything was terrific at the hotel, and for a business trip, they provided all the needed services and more. We ended up renting one of the meeting rooms on the third floor, and they took care of all our needs. My only regret was not taking advantage of the ---hour gym.

Checked into room and there was pee in the toilet. Dirt on the bed sheets. Received no room service. As we checked out, they told us the room we stayed in was vacant in their system. They said we were booked for another room. Our belongings could have gotten stolen or possibly another couple could have walked in. This would explain the no room service and pee. We got nothing in return. This is the worst place I have stayed at. I have children as well. I woul not recommend this hotel to anyone. How embarrassing that a -star can do better than a Hyatt!!

Just spent two nights at this disaster of a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Resort"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I do extensive traveling for business and am normally very easy to please, but this place compelled me to write this review. I was traveling with my wife and -.- year old twin boys. When we made the reservation (knowing we would be arriving late), we asked that two cribs be put in the room. While this was confirmed during our midnight check in, no cribs were in the room. We had to wait an eternity for cribs to be delivered because """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""all the housekeeping people had gone home"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Not a good start.
The next morning in the restaurant, we met up with family (who luckily for them were staying elsewhere). After we were seated in the restaurant NO ONE would wait on us. We waited and waited. After asking THREE times for some help, we were told by the only server present that it was not his table, that he had asked someone to help us, and to get any service, we would need to speak to the manager! After speaking with the manager, someone finally showed up, but by then it was beyond annoying.
We were gone for most of the day and got back to the room at about - pm. The room had not been made up. Because the twins needed a nap, we put them down with the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Do not Disturb"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sign on the door. Right after the kids fell asleep THE PHONE RINGS - waking up the kids- and the staff person asks when they can clean our room. They had ALL DAY to clean it but wait till the evening and then ignore the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Do not disturb"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sign. Incredible.
The $-- dollar parking fee is high, but it would be better if you actually got a space to park in. When we got back to the room at -- pm the last night, there were no spaces in the entire resort. I drove around for -- minutes looking for a place to park (with a bunch of other guests). I eventually had to park on the street and hoof it back to the room (a ten minute walk). 
There is much much more, but I have already wasted too much of my time on a place (like any other Hilton) that I will never stay at again.
STAY AWAY!

I brought my teenage granddaughter to NYC for two nights to see shows and shop. The St. James has an odd system. They dispense one physical key to the room and you have to hand it back in to the front desk every time you leave the place. They re-issue it when you return. On the day we were to check out, we left at -:-- in the morning to go shopping and handed in our key. The desk clerk never reminded us that checkout was noon. I had forgotten this detail, and we returned at -:--. The desk clerk chastised us for coming back late and said we'd have to pay another night. I asked why he had not reminded us when we left in the morning. He sassed back, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""because you didn't ask."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Our things were in the room and he would not give us the key to go gather our stuff until I gave him my credit card. After some arguing, the blond woman boss-type told the desk guy that he could charge me $--- instead of the full night. He added all kinds of taxes to that - occupancy tax when we were not even occupying - and came out with $---. 
The only good things about the place are its location and the fact that it does not have bed bugs. The room was dark to the point that we could not see to write postcards, the bathroom ran out of toilet paper and there was no spare roll, the bathroom has no shelf or countertop to put things like contact lens supplies and such (we had to use the windowsill), the two elevators are so small and slow that we walked up the three flights to be faster every time we came and went, and with the exception of one nice guy at the front desk, the rest were abrupt. All in all I'd never stay here again. Oh, I forgot to say that when we did get the key and go to our room on that check out day, an Asian maid was in there finishing up her housekeeping duties and she was angry with us. She grouched something to the effect that we made her work late. I said I'd use the bathroom and leave immediately. She said, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no, no. all clean for next guest. no can use."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Well, I respected her wishes and did not use it, deferring instead to the one off the lobby as we left. But it is interesting how they had another guest coming in and had already extorted $--- from me for that same room.

I stayed with my wife for - nights. The hotel was average. The location is very convenient. Staff is helpful, no problems with reservations. The room was not that big, but it had a nice big bathroom though. All in all, a not so bad experience, but I was expecting more from Conrad.

Great deal. Free parking. No breakfast but a Mel's drive In down the street where the pancakes and french toast are simply delicious (also an International House of pancakes nearby).
Well located: near the --, -- and -- buses. Not in the city center but quite convenient to get to places.
Great room. Clean but noisy, even with earplugs so ask for a room on the quiet street.

I checked into my room on Saturday, received two side by side rooms. The desk clerk asked if I would like the key to my second room, I declined and left a list of names at the front desk for my potential guest and instructions to issue a key to either room as I would be out for the night. The next day I saw someone I didnt know leaving the adjoining room and inquired at the front desk, the hotel informed me since my guest had not arrived they treated the room as a no show and rented if for the full rate. It was explained to me that since my room was prepaid at a discount and my guest had not picked up their keys the hotel was entitled to resale the room and keep my payment, essentially selling the room twice. This was my second stay at the Hotel Monaco because I loved staying there so much the first time. It is hard staying here with someone with whom you do not want to share a bed if you want a superior room, i.e. two beds in a killer room. Let me point out: the amenities are wonderful, the staff is excellent, the adjoining restaurant is delicious, the location is good, and the price is right. We stayed - nights at the Marriott Custom House in Downtown Boston, I would thoroughly recommend staying at this hotel - even though it is quite expensive. The Good
Excellent, clean Hotel. We stayed in room ----, they must have turned the fans off for us as we did not experience the louder than TV noise from previous review!
Restaurant-Bar next door, great food and great staff. They were able to explain to us what the protesters where complaining about

We stayed for - nights, the protesters were there on Thursday and Friday, then came back for an hour at -am on Sat morning. No sign of them when we checked out on Sunday morning.
With a bit of customer service, the - could have been a - with an acceptance of peoples right to protest

This was not my favorite Marriott Hotel. On the plus side, It has a great mid-town location on the corner of Lexington and --, walking distance from major tourist attractions. The zen bathroom with double-size stall shower was fabulous. The bed and the linens were quite nice, which is standard for the Marriott. Now for the negative. My visit to the restaurant was a disaster. The service was both arrogant and incompetent - a particularly horrible combination. When I complained to Marriott management, they distanced themselves, telling me that they just leased the space to the restaurant and that they have had other complaints. Due to my complaint the restaurant manager called me and offered me a coupon for another visit. I declined, because who wants to waste a meal in NYC at a substandard restaurant? She insisted, took my address, and several months later has yet to send me the coupon. Adding insult to injury, as they say. The concierge lounge takes the minimalist approach to food, with a small plate of sliced fruit, a few muffins here, tiny pitchers of milk. A lady helping herself to some of the fruit worried there wouldn't be enough for other guests.
The decor may strike some as wacky. The hotel isn't consistent and doesn't have a decent restaurant, so it isn't great for business travel where you may arrive late and just want service. If you're staying here as a tourist it may be a better bet because of the proximity to the attractions and because you are less likely to use the restaurant or concierge lounge. For business travel I prefer the Marriott Eastside a few blocks away.

Long weekend to celebrate our --th anniversary with friends. Staff was great - very friendly and helpful. Thanks to Igor, Bill and Nick! Loved the location. Very close to Grand Central Station. Rooms clean, nicely appointed and comfortable. Plenty of room plus nice bath with plenty of space, as well. Location great, street noise a non-factor. Second floor reading room provided perfect start to day with great coffee of your choice, beautiful bowls of fresh fruit, plates of assorted pastries, yogurts, cereals - a little something for everyone to get their day started. Great spot for respite after long day of walking and shopping. Coffees and teas always available. Roof top bar and patio another great escape!

Spend more money and stay somewhere else!
It was our first day in the US and we had to stay at the Herbert Hotel in SF. The hotel was horrible. The bath was full of hair. They did not tidy up the room the next morning (we stayed - nights in total). There was no remote control for the TV. 
The sheets were full of holes and blood.

So, stay away and go elsewhere. Only positive point about the hotel is the area. It is walking distance to Union Square and the Powell&Hyde cable car.

I'm a Priority Club member and I paid for part of my stay and used Priority rewards for the rest of my stay. Well, the Front Desk somehow is not equipped to handle a transaction like this. Room, bed, pillows and stay was comfortable.

Great location - a short walk to Lady Bird Lake. They have a computer room & a nice bar.
While I was staying here, they decided to block off the main entrance and begin paving of a section of the entrance. It was inconvenient to get inside the hotel.

Let me start by saying this hotel is very cheap for the location. Very close to Time Square (about - or - blocks) The rooms are clean but nothing fancy. I would say average noise level for a NYC hotel. My biggest complaint would be the beds being a little hard and the rooms didn't have a coffee maker but there was a deli close by that had a nice little breakfast. I would recommend this hotel to anyone staying in NYC. 
Other recomendations while in NYC: 
Broadway - Wicked and Chicago were both great

Bars - House of Brews II (--st street), Langan's Irish Pub (--th street) (Kristina is a great bartender!) Both have great service and aren't as rowdy as some of the other bars in the city

We stayed at this hotel easter weekend and had a wonderful experience. The hotel is just beautiful. we had a king room with a balcony, which I highly recommend. The room was spacious and the bed amazing. We had enough room to set up an air bed for our - year old. The staff were very friendly and helpful. There is a valet parking at the hotel for $--, but we ended up parking at the parking lot across the street which offers complimentary self parking for hotel guests. I highly recommend this hotel.

I spent three days at Peninsula. The district is perfect, Everything is AROUND THE HOTEL.
It was my first time in a Peninsula hotel and I must say I would go again.
The decoration is old but nice, the bathroom is huge bathtub and shower. The view from my room was not amazing but once in the gym one can work out with a view all over the city and the lake which is very pleasant.
The Asian restaurant is good, service perfect but the atmosphere quite boring.
The bar is really nice at night better to reserve on friday night because it is very crowed.
Note: If you order breakfast in your room it always take more time than promised -- mns sometimes. They always call to apologize but...the water used for the tea tastes really bad by the way.

This place continues to amaze.

We were treated like royalty the whole time we were there. Granted we spent a considerable amount of money (we ate at least -- meals at the hotel) and the concierge secured great tables for us at prime time at three restaurants that are typically difficult to get into.
The staff could not have been more gracious or friendly. They repeatedly stopped to speak with us and allowed themselves to be drawn into lengthy conversations if we were so inclined.

It was Pretty Good Ecomomy Motel with good value, less than $--.

Also friendly staffs in the evening when I checked in and check out in the morning.
But no refrigerator or micro wave in the room. Some light in the room is still not working.
Overall it's good motel in the $-- range!!

I stayed at the Courtyard New York Manhattan - Midtown East September ---. This hotel is in a great location. We walked all over. There is no need to take a subway or taxi. After reading the reviews on here, I did double check to see if we had sheets on the sofa bed, and we did not. I was able to ask the bell man before he left our room. We were supposed to stay there our entire stay and ended up staying one night - we teuly regret we didn't stay four nights, it was the best hotel of our San Francisco stay!
This historical property is amazing. It is truly a living part of the history - so if you are not the kind of person who appreciates that - Stay away.
We had a lovely room, truly unique, spacious, lots of furniture, a lovely fireplace, and a hot shower. We loved it.
They offer a lovely tea and coffee setup all day long, an AMAZING continental breakfast, and a delightful sherry and cookies inthe afternoon. The staff is courteous, friendly, and truly there to help you.
Highly recommended!

I was in New York for - days (- nights) before flying off to St Louis for Thanksgiving. Having never been to the City before (or even to the US!) I was careful in picking a hotel not too far out. I almost stayed in China Town until this Gem became affordable due to booking last minute.
