A luggage rack, huge wardrobe, bath and shower, extra large double bed, comfy armchair and a view overlooking the street. Okay so the view wasn't amazing but I was glad to have this view rather than none at all.
The location was perfect for an NYC virign like me, about a - minute walk to Times Square, -- minute walk to Central Park and the nearest subway was about a block away - all ESSENTIALS for your first trip.
I was on a pretty tight schedule trying to see everything I wanted to in only three days so I didn't have breakfast in the hotel at all although there was a little queue each morning so I would assume it was good.
I couldn't reccomend this hotel more. Although I admit, I wouldn't necessarily stay so close to Times Square again and probaly not in this hotel because:

-) I got such a good deal on this hotel, I doubt I'd be that lucky to find it again.

I was very impressed with the service at this hotel. The staff is very friendly and helpful. The location of the Wingate was great! We were within walking distance to a lot of things we wanted to see. I highly recommend this hotel!!

We just got back from a weekend trip to San Diego. We took our - year old son to Sea World and chose the Hyatt because of it's location. Excellent accomodations, outstanding restaurant, helpful concierge, and perfectly located for all travel desires. A touch of Europe in the USA. We will always return to the Sofitel Chicago Water Tower.

We had a great time in New York and enjoyed the hotel very much. Friendly staff at the desk and in the morning folks helping out with breakfast. The rooms were spotless and very well designed. Loved the lights and the ability to gradually darken-lighten them. Wifi was strong and free.

The only down side which has been mentioned numerous times is the packed elevators at peak times. Only three elevators makes for long waits at times, wish there was way to add a couple more.
We'll be back and we'll stay at the Staybridge! Thanks.

I had read many Trip Advisor reviews before booking this hotel, and I have to say that the good reviews given to this hotel were correct. I stayed in the Golden Gate Bridge Room, which is a queen, premier deluxe room, so can't really attest to a cheaper standard room, but for the price ($---+tax) it was a deal for San Francisco. The room was large and clean, with a great view looking south over the city. That said, I suppose that the view may be the main difference in price compared to a standard room; the higher floor and opposite side of the building from the street probably helped with noise, as I had no problem with garbage trucks or other street noise. The kitchenette was adequate, although not as well stocked as I had hoped. There was a refrigerator and microwave, but there were just two sets of large and small plates, bowls, coffee cups, wine glasses, drinking glasses, forks, spoons, and knives. No bottle or wine opener, so bring or buy your own. The one thing missing was any way to wash the kitchen items after use; neither soap nor sponge were present. Also, there were no tissues or paper towels, so really no way to clean up afterwards. I noticed that and bought my own tissues while shopping, so along with the fact that the housekeeping staff washed the dishes when they cleaned the room it was really not a big deal. Breakfast was free and plentiful: scones, muffins, coffeecake, bread, hardboiled eggs, oatmeal, apples, orange juice, coffee. A colleague who stayed in another (more expensive) hotel did not have breakfast included, so I don't think anybody could complain. I should also mention that I rented a car and used the free parking. As others stated, the entrance is very narrow, so insist on a small car (my rental company kept trying to give me a Jeep or a Mustang convertible...), preferably one with folding mirrors. I was attending a conference at the Moscone Convention Center, and the walk took about ----- minutes.

First, the nearly impenetrable crowds of Times Square tourists make entrance to this hotel an exhausting challenge. (If you were always hoping to see Times Square, you should know that it has become little more than a gigantic outdoor mall - a Sunglass Hut here, Gap across the street, Olive Garden down on the corner). But you've got the energy and the nerve (hey, this is NY!), and you've made it inside! You wait with a dozen other guests (now --, now --) for the elevators to your room, or to the check-in desk which is on the eighth floor. The wait is as much as -- minutes, since the computer system that controls the elevators tends to crash when it gets busy. And it's ALWAYS busy here - there were three conferences going on simultaneously when we were here, and that was less than usual. You're grateful when """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""John"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" shows up in his red double-breasted jacket to excort the now highly impatient crowd to the freight elevators - past the stacked chairs and dusty cases of hotel water bottles. John's nice enough (everyone's nice enough here), and he says simply that this is what happens here when it's busy. That's what the waitress said when she tried to deliver our breakfast -- minutes late. But don't worry, they'll comp it when it's late. They're used to it. Things here are ALWAYS late. Now you're ready to check out. You stand on the --rd or --st floor for -- minutes, -- minutes, as the crowd grows, bags in tow, waiting for an elevator to stop at your floor. Slowly the awkward banter goes silent, the humor is gone, and someone goes to call from the nearby emergency phone. They'll send someone soon. They're VERY nice - they're used to it here. The crowd grows. On a floor above, the alarm rings. Uh oh. Someone's having a worse time than you. But at last an elevator stops at the floor, ten of the more ambitious of you squeeze on (hope that alarm doesn't have to ring), and soon you're downstairs, thankful to have made it out alive. Wait on the -- person line for a cab? No thanks, we'll just walk up to Eighth Ave and hail one ourselves. 
But the room was nice. 
Good Luck.

We stayed here from ----- to -----. We booked with QuickBook for a rate of $--- for the weekend nights and $--- for the Thursday and Sunday nights. I had never used OuickBook before and liked the fact that there were no fees for booking through them.

The location and price for me earn this hotel an above average mark. - of the - Metro lines stop at this station. One stop and - minutes to DCA on the Yellow line.

We stayed at the Doubletree for one night the last weekend of July ----, and let me just say this place was AWESOME. Did I mention the cookies? I ate mine shortly after getting into the room and told my boyfriend that I was going to eat his. He taunted me with that cookie the rest of the stay. He finally ate it on the drive BACK HOME! haha.
We were going out to a birthday party on -th street that night and had inquired about the shuttle. - miles radius from the hotel. For free. The next day after we checked out, we ate at the attached restaurant (and watched some Olympics on the TV). It did take a while to receive our check and then also to pay said check. The food was good enough to overlook that small infraction. :)
Overall - I would definitely stay here. I booked through Hotwire sight unseen and was pleasantly surprised.

After significant research into fine accommodations in San Francisco for a best friends wedding, we opted to book a suite at San Francisco's famous Fairmont Hotel. OK, not for everybody maybe, but for this traveler, San Carlos is the place to stay in downtown Phoenix.  When we got into San Diego (Point Loma, to be precise), we headed down Rosecrans to find The Pearl. Upon arriving, the parking situation left much to be desired. Valet parking is $-- a night and I'm not one for unnecessary expenses so we parked a couple of blocks away and hoofed it.
 When we entered the hotel, I was blown away by the decor. The vibe is retro-beach-glam. Is that a real thing? No? Well, I just made it up, so HA.  The hotel provides H-O products for the standard shampoo-conditioner-lotion trio and I must say, the lotion made it's way into my purse in less than ten minutes and stayed there for weeks while I squeezed every last drop out of it.
 We also had our own little patio but the best part of the room? The beta fish! Every room has their own little beta fish in a bowl mounted on the wall. It was such an unexpected detail and I thought it was totally cute and original.
 Because it was such a short stay, we didn't have a whole lot of interaction with the staff.  All in all, we were really pleased with the experience. This was the most interesting, futuristic, exciting hotel my wife and I have ever stayed in. When I travel to San Diego, I always book with the Dana. The staff is very professional, and the rooms are very clean. Is this the best hotel in SD? No, of course not. Does it give you everything you need on a budget and then some? Yes. It is what the BW is known for. The rooms were a little on the small side but considering the age of the hotel, they were good. The noise level in the morning from traffic was high but the hotel can't control that.

My wife and I just stayed for two nights at the historic Phoenix Park Hotel and had an absolutely wonderful time celebrating our --th anniversary. This was one of our most wonderful romantic weekends ever. Our view of Elliot Bay was gorgeous. This hotel is very convenient off the interstate at exit --. The room was clean, the bathroom was clean, and it was very quiet. It was also nice to have the extras like the full breakfast in the morning, free drinks and snacks in the evening. I would stay here again.

Fantastic suite hotel. Great for families needing more than a hotel room without the usual high cost. We live in San Diego and love doing short little vacations in our home town! Stayed here a couple of days ago for an overnight getaway. Was sooo pleased with the accommodations, location and the professionalism of the staff. Hope to stay here again soon!

We stayed here for - nights over spring break. The room set-up was great with a separate bedroom. There were many cupboards and drawers for all our stuff. The maids did a great job of cleaning the room but the carpets were very much in need of cleaning and the cushions on the couch were stained.

I am a frequent traveler and was very impressed with the quality, location and service offered by the Chicago Renaissance.

Room was very clean with ample soap, towels etc. Room was quite small but that was to be expected in an historical venue. The pool (which we didn't use) was small but there were plenty of fresh towels and chairs around. The only negative about staying downtown is the high price of parking. Seems that the finite amount of parking should be considered by hotel management and a way worked out to benefit guests and staff alike. 
Would consider staying here again.

It's interesting to read that nothing has changed at this dump since I stayed there. I think I made the hastiest retreat in history. Indifferent service. Very indifferent service.

The bathrooms are divided into a room with toilet and sink and a room with sink and shower -- great when sharing with a family. There was a nice desk area that we used quite a bit. The exercise room and the pool were very nice. Although we didn't ask for one, I noticed that the rooms have the option to be connecting rooms which is great if you have a family that is larger than one room can accommodate. They offer a nice breakfast along with the room but you're also connected to the JW Marriott and the Courtyard if you want a different option. We love the Marriott chain but have never stayed at a SpringHill Suites. We would definitely stay at one again. Also, as a resident of the area, I don't often have the opportunity to see the city like this but we had a room that faced the JW Marriott and it was a beautiful view of the downtown area

My boyfriend and I stayed here over Thanksgiving for a week. The hotel is in a great location for shopping, Times Square, the subway is directly opposite so when we arrived we didn't have to wander around trying to find the hotel.

The slight downside was that the bathroom was on the small side so we had to brush our teeth one at a time and took us longer getting ready to go out each day. When our room got a bit cold in the night as the windows are thinner than what we're used we put the heater on as it is one you can control yourself as and when you want it which was really useful.
Although the room and bathroom clearly needed some work doing to it as bits of paintwork were flaking off, the bath and sink both had cracks in them and the whole room was rather dated including the bedding, we had everything we needed, especially since it's in New York so you don't want to spend too long in the hotel as there is so much to see and do.
We can't comment much on the staff as we didn't see them after checking in except the cleaners who were always polite. Our room was cleaned everyday to an adequate standard as the room was rather dusty from the start and the bed sheets often had holes in them.
We both agreed that if we go back to New York and want to stay in the same area we would stay here again, the hotel is reasonably priced especially for its location and with some much needed refurbishments it could be the ideal hotel.

I stayed at this Hampton Inn during the first week of June ----. I was by myself, - months pregnant and on a business trip. The Baldwin is unassuming, but very affordable, comfortable, and in a great location. The accomodations were very nice and attractive. Very comfortable bed and pillows. The desk area of the lobby is in the midst of a renovation project that looks like it will be a beautiful update to this old hotel. Amenities are minimal, but you shouldn't be spending much time indoors here anyway! (There is a Starbucks next door to hotel and across the street from the famous Chinatown gate)

I stayed with my family at the Residence Inn Indianapolis Airport in August ---- for a multi-day event in downtown Indy. We chose the hotel because of the price - about half as much as for the downtown hotels, which more than made up for the minor cost of driving to downtown and parking (never more than $-- for the day).
The price is the best thing going for this hotel, which is a pretty standard Residence Inn. The room was fine and clean. The breakfast area doesn't have much seating. The pool is getting old and outdated, with one of the ladders in the pool actually broken (is this not a safety hazard or code violation?). There are some family restaurants within walking distance (Waffle House, Dennys, etc.), but the neighborhood is not one of Indy's finest.
This is just an opinion, but I don't expect this property to improve much in the future or be given a lot of attention by Marriott. The Residence Inn is off the Sam Jones Expressway which used to be the main terminal access to the airport. A couple of years ago, the Indy Airport moved its main access to the southwest side of the airport off I---. Thus the RI (and some other hotels) now find themselves on the back side of the airport on what is almost an abandoned short stretch of freeway.
I think this RI can still be a bargain compared to the downtown hotels. However, the property is not worth paying more than a bargain price.

We were placed here by the airline to wait out the Volcano in Iceland.I have never stayed at a Crown Plaza nor will i do again.The room was ok but the restaurant is a joke and the staff there not much better.We sat down ordered our meal and waited after a while we asked where it was as other diners were served before us they said they would look into it. My husband & I stayed here for - nights, while in town for the Nike Marathon. At first glance, being used to the typical corporate chain hotels, we were both disappointed when we arrived to our room. However, the charm of this place becomes apparent rather quickly.
We too, had a corner room, just like a previous reviewer - room #--. It is immediately next to the elevator, and facing the street. The room is plenty big for - people with a fireplace, sofa, an upholstered chair and a desk with chair. I see no reason to avoid a room by the elevator - on the contrary, I found it quite convenient. The street noise is present, but either sleep with your windows shut or turn on the provided """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""noise machine"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and you'll be fine. 
The amenities are such that I've never experienced at any other hotel before. They keep a refrigerator fully stocked with bottled water & sodas, for you to take whenever you'd like. There is always a bowl of apples available, coffee & tea. Starting in the afternoons, and going straight through to after dinner, there is a cookie jar kept stocked with fresh baked cookies. A different type of cookie appeared every day, and often times we were at the jar while the cookies were still warm! When dropping off your parcels or running in to change clothes, having a bottle of water and a small snack is a welcome find.
The breakfast is adequate. It's enough to get you started on your day. I agree that the set up is a bit of a disaster, having the coffee-tea immediately outside of the elevator doors. I enjoyed my daily cup of coffee and croissant with jam!
We did not take full advantage of the wine-cheese reception. We did stop in, grab a few glasses of wine to take up to our room while getting ready for dinner, but the people who were down there were social and it was a friendly atmosphere.
Overall, I recommend this hotel, and if staying in the Union Square area again, I would love to stay here again.

This is one of the quietest hotels I have stayed at. The staff were very friendly and the free breakfast and happy hour were great.
However, I don't think I will ever book into any Embassy Suites hotel ever again. The reason, well I thought that I wasn't really bothered by heights. After - days I was almost crawling along the open balconies. I have developed a fear of heights at this hotel. The glass elevator seems to be partiularly cruel in the evil psychologist's (I mean architect's) designs.
I've stayed at dozens of US hotels in the past but hardly ever in downtown areas. I know what to enquire about now before I book another.
The attached photo is the view from my room door.
i don't know if it is caused by the philly marathon. the rate of a single room is $--- which is too far expensive for comfort inn. though the hotel itself is not bad.
What a fabulous hotel...ultra chic, ultra modern, ultra amenities! The Ink has become my home away from home in Manhattan.

If you want to stay in the heart of the tourist district in San Francisco on a budget, look no further. While the rooms are very small, you can't beat the location. I would not recommend this hotel if you have more than two people in a room, and even that is pushing it. The building is old but the remodel is nice. Good amenities.

We found this hotel at a great price on Getaroom, and we were pleasantly surprised at how wonderful our stay was! The staff were all very helpful and pleasant, the pool was very clean and never crowded, the room was spotless and roomy. Some reviews stated that the bathrooms were so small it was hard to close the door, but I can only see that being a problem if you are severely overweight. The internet worked wonderfully, the view was great, and the shuttle service was SO helpful!! We never had to wait more than -- minutes to be picked up or dropped off, and the driver Juan was extremely helpful and friendly and a very safe driver!
The restaurant was superb; we had both lunch and dinner there multiple times and everything tasted so fresh. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone and will definitely be staying here again!

Checked in at midnight after a very long -- hour day of working. Walked nearly a country mile to get to my room. Passed a wedding reception letting out, full of drunk obnoxious people crowding the hallways. Tried to shower and get some sleep, there was NO WATER PRESSURE! Tried to lay down, had sleep number beds, but I found - dirty socks in my bed!!! Horrible housekeeping! If I had not have been awake for -- hours already I would have just left. Had a terrible stay, not to mention the people in the rooms next to me were in and out all night long making all kinds of noise.

We have just returned from a trip of California, having stayed in many hotels during our visit this was by far the best. The location was perfect in everyway, the rooms were ideal (clean, well presented and amazingly comfortable beds!) and the atmosphere of the hotel was generally excellent. Probably our only complaint was with some of the front desk staff who we found at times were abrupt and unfriendly especially during check - in (at one point a member of staff found his mobile phone much more interesting than helping us out). However this is a trivial point in a generally brilliant hotel.. and a lovely staff member called Rory made up for what others lacked :-D

This used to be my go-to hotel for staying near downtown Austin without paying a fortune, but my last couple visits have grossed me out. Smelly rooms. Bugs in the bathroom. They never send a maid unless you beg them. Just run-down feeling and paying $--- a night for this place is just insane -- regardless of where it is.

After a horror trip from London and an awful night at The Standard, The James was a wonderful relief. We had stayed at The James in Chicago years ago, and were very happy there. But The James NYC was even better. A beautiful low-key environment with staff that could not have been more helpful (without being intrusive). Our room had everything we needed for a relaxing stay, plus great views. Can't recommend the hotel highly enough. And what a location! Perfect for anyone holidaying in the city.

Be careful if you reserve this hotel with a Priority Club reward...
At check-in, attendant confirmed that reservation was associated with a PC reward. However, express checkout showed $---+ charges -- so visited another attendant at check-out and was assured that the charge would not be put through to my credit card.
One day later, the $---+ charge appeared on my credit card anyway. Expect better (i.e. seemless) service from a supposedly --star property...

Not sure how long ago this hotel was taken over from Starwood, but the Jumeriah group turned this NYC historical property into something really fabulous. The guestrooms are beautifully appointed and the bathrooms are roomy. Love the amenities - lush towels, robes, slippers, ironing board, etc... I hear some of the queen rooms are smaller but when you are in NY, are you really ever in your room? Do you really need a view? I am sure Ducasse's restaurant is missed on the block, but South Gate makes a nice replacement. Bartenders are very personable, food excellent and the setting fantastic with a fireplace set in the back - great atmosphere. Yes New York is expensive, but we landed an amazing rate via the website and they upgraded us without us even asking. Yes, it was February. Still on a whole I was left with a wonderful impression and I will be back. Last note - being on Central Park is great no matter what time of year. Convenient to all subway lines.

This is - seriously - my favorite hotel in the world. If you need to be in the middle of Hollywood, the location is perfect. The rooms are all simple, gorgeous, funky charm. Bed linens are exquisite and the beds are firm and comfy, just the way I like them. But the best part is the service and staff. Beyond compare! I have never been treated so royally. Public Restaurant is an oasis of calm and creative cuisine (best burger on the planet) and the Tropicana pool is a fabulous spot to chill under a palm. I just love this hotel and will definitely return - again and again.

My husband and I stayed at the Doubletree for a night because of a wedding that we were attending nearby. It was not the hotel that the bride and groom chose for their guests but we got a great deal through priceline that was hard to pass up. 
The hotel really is in the middle of all the action in Philly. It is walking distance (across the street) to some theaters and surrounded by some great restaurants and local eateries. We decided to try to check in before the wedding ceremony (at -pm) eventhough we knew that the rooms probably wouldn't be ready yet. We arrived at the hotel at noon and the staff found a room on the -th floor for us! Ofcourse their signature warm chocolate chip cookies were another huge plus. The concierge also were happy to give us directions to the church where the wedding was to be held. 
The room is very traditional- not huge but definately more than enough room for two people. The windows for most of the rooms are very large with nice views of downtown. But best of all the beds are luxurious and comfy. I did not find the room to be dirty in any way but the decor may need some updating. 
The only problem we had during our stay was the parking garage. It was rather narrow and had a very strange and confusing floorplan. (We walked around for -- min trying to find or car) They also charge $-- to park in the garage- which I think it typical for Philly. 
We were very happy with our stay at the doubletree and wouldn't mind going back. We do prefer our previous stays at the Westin and Sofitel better but for the price- Doubletree was the best deal.

Centrally located in downtown Dallas. Owing to its period construction (early --th Century), the rooms-floors are incredibly quiet; could not hear any noises from adjacent guest rooms. The staff was extremely friendly & helpful. Nice touches: evening happy hour, and late-night cookies-milk-coffee set-up. Very relaxing with an upscale feel to it. A restaurant on-site would be nice, but there are plenty close by to choose from. The hotel offers an above average conference room facility right acorss the street for large meetings, and provides excellent catering service for morning & afternoon coffee-snack breaks. Great experience. Would be happy to return.

Just came back from - nights at this hotel with a group of -- friends and it was a prefect base for exploring NYC! Fantastic service and an allround comfortable experience.
I have written a more comprehensive review of the hotel earlier, just wanted to give my praise again.
Keep up the good work!

We had a very enjoyable stay at the Marriott Union Square. We had an easy check in, a late night snack at the bar-restaurant and they are very helpful in getting you around town as easily as possilbe. The location is great, we were sooooo glad we did not stay near the waterfront area(nice to visit, too noisey and busy to stay). It is very easy to get on a cable car or F line trolley($--person) from the hotel. The valet service was also great, we had to retrieve some items from our car and they were superb about helping us out, and when we needed the car it was there exactly when we requested. Our rooms were great, they gave our kids a corner room which was very spacious. Highly recommend this hotel.

We stayed here Labor Day weekend so our kids could go to Universal Studios and we could relax by the pool. 
Our room was spectacular. We were on the --nd floor and the view was awesome!!! Especially at night. The room was extremely spacious and clean.
With our room, we had vouchers for the breakfast buffet and I have never seen a more generous breakfast buffet!!! We headed down and I was expecting the usual coffee, juice, cereal and pastries. But this buffet had anything you could ever want!! I love breakfast and I thought I was in breakfast heaven!! In addition to the usual things I mentioned above, there were different stations like Jewish and Chinese for things like lox and bagles and dim sum and they had Nutella and fresh fruit and omlettes, and fresh squeezed orange juice.... I can just go on and on. It was in an airy, spacious space with tablecloths and cloth napkins and the servers were so gracious. So with a good nights sleep and this delicous breakfast under our belts we were ready to tackle the day! 
The kids headed out to the park and my husband and I headed to the pool area for some rest and relaxation. I went to the pool bar to put in my cocktail order and this is where things fell apart a little bit. They didn't have my brand of alcohol, which wasn't a big deal, but they seemed to be very confused back there and as I waited for my drink, one of the bartenders kind of snapped at me like """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""What are you still doing here? We'll bring it out to you"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of course that isn't what he said, but that was the jist. I didn't want to hear that and I felt sorry for him. He never returned again to see if I needed anything and I didn't order another drink. With that being said, later that afternoon, I met a couple at the pool and they placed their second drink order, as we were chatting in the pool and after about a half hour, they finally had to leave and he cancelled the order. So I wouldn't give a very good review on the pool bar, but the pool and area surrounding it is nice. There are private cabanas you can secure as well.
After we spent the day at the pool we took the free shuttle to the CityWalk and met our kids for dinner and after dinner, we all rode it back to the hotel. The shuttle runs every -- minutes, I believe, so it was really handy! I would definately recommend this hotel to anyone going to Universal Studios. It's easy to get on and off the freeway also.

Great view,very clean, nice pool area, staff was extremely helpful, other hotel visitors seemed as happy as my family and I were (everyone was friendly, guessing because they were relaxed and having a positive experience as well) amazing location, nice sheets-pillows-towels-robes etc., nothing unpleasant about my stay

Room was clean and staff was friendly and accomodating. Two king beds is a nice touch. Breakfast was standard """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Holiday Inn Express"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but was hot and fresh. Internet connection was OK. Liked the cable TV but wish some sort of guide was provided that would show what was subscribed and what isn't. I would recommend this Holiday Inn Express location.

We found this hotel last minute after an apartmen from VRBO cancelled on us. We were suprised at the great rates during Christmas season. The location was absolutely perfect. Macy's is literally around the corner. There was a subway station near and Penn Station was close too. Nothing fancy about the hotel but it was nice and clean which is all we needed. I would stay here again.

The service was slow in checking in, getting food, getting directions, and checking out. It was not slow because of lines, but because of disorganization. 
I will not stay here again.
Not many guests. Very quiet, Decent bed. Both down and down alternative pillows were given per bed, Nice perk.

Perhaps it was because I was on a layover from Orlando to Los Angeles. Perhaps it was just nearing midnight. NOT. This hotel was simply terrible. The room was sardine-can like, the toilet ran all night long, and the flourescent overhead lights throughout the room made it rather cold and uninviting. Just terrible. Even their courtesy shuttle vans were extremely worn down and unsafe feeling. I can't even say anything really good about the front desk service either. Do yourself a BIG favor. DON'T STAY AT THIS HOTEL AT ANY PRICE GREATER THAN $---night, unless of course you prefer window A-C, stained carpets, and dusty air. Then perhaps you'd like it there.

Stayed for - nights in early August and had a great time. The hotel is very clean and modern. Our room was a good size, we heard the fire station which is next door but in my opinion it wasn't too loud or bothersome. The pool area is nice as well.
The hotel is in a good location, close to shopping and restaurants, a couple minutes to the subway but not too bad. Concierge was helpful is directing us to where we wanted to go.
We ate breakfast at Filini every day and it was awesome, great food and service. I highly recommend getting the AAA-CAA rate that has breakfast included. Totally worth it! only about --$ a day more than the cheapest rate and you can choose what ever you want off the menu +coffee + juice
Had a couple extra charges upon checkout but this was taken care of. 
Definitely recommend this hotel to all groups of people

I stayed here last week for two nights after doing extensive research of where to stay in San Diego. I decided to follow other reviewers and asked for a front room. I was given a side room facing the courtyard. Yes, there are trains, but no matter where you stay downtown there are trains, and you can hear them no matter where you really are. The train tracks are directly behind the hotel, and there are several trains that go by, and yes they blow their horns. But, being only - window lengths away from the tracks, I can honestly say that the noise was not as bad as some people wrote about. That was the ONLY reason why I was not going to use it. But there was a special on expedia for a very good price so I grabbed it and hoped for the best.
First and foremost, my BIGGEST RAVE about this hotel is that due to scheduling I arrived at --:--am or so, check in is not until -pm. I expected to be told to leave my luggage secured and hopefully by -pm I could get a room . Once I went to the desk, the clerk, who was very friendly, informed me that my room was ready and gave me the keys. Not too many places would do that!
 The lobby is open, clean, there are - computers, - is strictly for boarding pass-airline info and the other was a general use one. I read someplace here that the elevator were slow, that I have to agree with, if your in a rush in the morning you can wait up to - min to get one, and there are - of them. I guess maybe the cleaning carts are blocking them or something, but once the afternoon rolls around they are fine. 
The room was clean, they wash all the bedding after each guest which is a plus, as I said my view was the courtyard, - windows away from the tracks, with the air on in the room we did not hear much at all. We are heavy sleepers, so that may have something to do with it, but you are given ear plugs everyday left on your pillows, we did not need or use them. I do have to add that the train was loud when we were awake in the room without the air on and the tv low, but that cannot be avoided, and most of the hotels in this area have that problem. 
The pool was clean as was the pool area, it was too cold for my liking, as it was chilly out there, but my son swam in it without a problem. There is also a little patio area outside of the gated pool where you can sit and enjoy a book, coffee, or just relax on a nice day. 
Breakfast, which is included is your typical Hampton Inn breakfast. cereal, muffins, eggs, Belgium waffles, coffee, juice, tea. We only had the waffles and muffins and they were good, and the food area was clean and constantly being cleaned by the staff working there. Coffee, tea and hot chocolate is available -- hrs. 
There is a shuttle that will take you places other than the airport or the scheduled zoo trip, those take priority but if they are free they will take you within a certain radius, we used it to go to a popular taco place about - miles away and picked back up again, all within a reasonable time, just make sure they have no airport trips scheduled or you will have to wait or take the trolley which is also right there. 
I cannot stress enough how great the staff was, friendly, professional, and were always on top of their game. They offered suggestions on where to go without even asking. Very great staff!
There is also an exercise room, again a typical hotel gym, nothing huge, treadmill, weights, bike, elliptical, and a TV. We checked it out and it was clean and had cleaning stuff for after using the machines. My son used it the days we were there and said it was good enough to keep up your routine.
Make sure you book your airport shuttle the day before, they ask for -- hrs notice, I just booked it when i got there so I wouldn't forget. The shuttle driver for the airport was prompt, and left on time. Once again, great service. 
The area around the hotel, and generally the whole seaport area does have a lot of homeless people around but they really do not bother you. I am a mother with - kids and went out at night walking around and felt safe. Another great deal is your a few blocks from Little Italy, and across the street you have the USS Midway, and Seaport. Great shops, food, and scenery. 
I would recommend giving this hotel a chance and put aside the train noise, it was worth the money, clean, helpful and just an overall greatly centered place.

This hotel was perfect! The staff was very helpful and polite. I called the day we were arriving to see what types of bed was in the room because one of my cousin's friends was coming for the night. I asked if they could switch it to a double bed and that was not a problem. The room was small, but it wasn't a problem as we just slept in there. The beds were okay. I don't sleep well in hotel beds, so that's just my opinion. Each bed comes with - pillows- - soft and - firm. Elevators were kind of slow, but it was a busy hotel so it was expected. Continental breakfast was very yummy! Eggs, bacon, cereal, juice, muffins, fruit, yogurt, cinnamon rolls, etc. DEFINITELY TRY THE CINNAMON ROLLS! Computers in the breakfast room were fast, high speed internet in the room was kind of slow. Location was PERFECT!! - blocks away from Michigan Avenue and - block away from State Street. Surrounded by good restaurants and Starbucks is right across the street! Didn't use valet parking so I can't review that part, but the staff was always willing to hail a taxi for you! The view was also pretty good! Easy and quick check-in and check-out. Hotel was very clean and trendy--didn't want to come back to Michigan. I will come back to this hotel!

My husband and I visited this hotel-city as a late Valentine's Day celebration. The hotel just opened a few months ago. Rooms are very nice-large and comfortable with large windows. Comfortable chairs, desk area, flat screen TV, large closet. Bathroom was large with nice amenities. We had an upper room with views of White River State Park and the White River. Service was wonderful-from the clerk at the front desk through everyone we ran into until check out. All were very helpful, asking how we liked our stay, smiles...very much appreciated. 
Location was near several attractions-Indiana State Museum was across the street and within walking distance. Indy Zoo, White River Gardens, & Victory Field are all very close.
We didn't use Internet or any other services. Valet-parking is available on site, but is $-- for regular parking-$-- for valet. There is a parking garage across the street connected to the hotel by a skywalk that is available for less than half the price that we utilized.
We had breakfast in the Osteria Pronto restaurant-also very nice. Lots of the regular breakfast fare plus a made to order omelet bar. Lots of fresh fruit, danish...great assortment all around. And again, service was great. Very attentive without being overbearing. 
My only complaint about this hotel was the bill....a $-- """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""incidental fee"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was tacked on to the bill when we checked in to cover damages or extras. No mention of this on the confirmation or at check in. Was assured it would be removed and credited to my card within a week. Suggested that they might want to mention this somewhere along the way so it's not a surprise when you check out.
I would definitely recommend this hotel for a downtown Indy visit.

We received a recommendation for this hotel, as very convenient and well situated.
The general aspect of the hotel is not so pleasant. It looks old, but not in a good way. Some of the members of the personnel are quite nice, but others showed little interest in being helpful.
The hotel had been recently fumigated, and it had a very strong smell of naphthaline! 
The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""continental breakfast"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that is included in the room price, is really shameful. First of all it is served with disposable dishes and cutlery. Second, the choice of food is very poor and low quality.
The room had good proportions. The bathroom was tiny. 
We had to go somewhere else to have a decent breakfast. In a word, disappointing. I don't recommend it.

If you are looking for an affordable room with a free shuttle - this is the place.
It may be a little run down, but what would you expect from a hotel with a bar and a shuttle driver who both know the happening places in the area to drink and be merry?!
this is the place if you need to lay your head while in the city of Brotherly Love and you are not looking for something posh and snobby.

During our stay we enjoyed service that was uber attentive and appropriately friendly from all staff. The luxurious accomodations were ultra clean with modern conveniences such as the ability to control lighting, climate control and shades-draperies with a user friendly-on screen (TV) interface with the remote control. The area boasts wonderful shopping and restaurants.

Though everything was not perfect here, I would recommend this hotel on location and cleanliness; which for me are the two most important things. Service was lacking but we are independent travelers so assistance from the employees is not a major concern.
The pros: Clean spacious suite-walking distance to Little Italy, Harbor Cruises, Quincy Market and many other attractions--- a short cab ride to the other major sites.
The cons: Though we prepaid for two suites neither was ready by -:--. After a long morning and a bumpy flight this was inconvenient. We decided to venture out asking only that extra towels be placed in our room. Upon our late return-no extra towels.
It was raining very hard on Saturday and the door man was overwhelmed so we asked the desk clerk to retrieve a phone number of a cab company. He said to go out the back door-walk down a ways and this """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""secret location"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is a great place to hail a cab. I pointed out to him the torrents of rain and repeated my request. He stared at me for a minute and I asked him if he did not have the ability to look up a phone number. He finally gave me a number.
As Hilton Gold Members, a continental breakfast was included with our room. We were supposed to get vouchers and for some reason, we could not get them at check in or when we retrieved our keys when our room was finally ready. Sometime during the night we received a partial number of our vouchers and a partial number for the other room. Consequently, when the other members of our party from the other room tried to get a cup of coffee-coffee only-they were rebuffed until they could get a voucher.
Also, we were given directions that were useless when we asked how to get to a few attractions. We ended up using our GPS.
Again, all the cons are minor but I mention for those who might like extra attention.
This Hilton is in the quieter part of downtown Boston - the Financial District -so some places like Panera Bread, Dunkin Donuts were not open early on Saturday or Sunday.
Again, the cons were a nuisance but nothing of any importance to our group. The important things make this hotel a worthwhile stay.

My mother, sister and I decided to visit New York for a long weekend and had heard great things about the Novotel from a friend so decided to book for - nights. The location is fantastic, basically right in Times Square and easy to get to. You enter the hotel from street level into a lift that takes you to the reception area which is nice and bright and despite undergoing rennovation work they have blended it in very nicely. In the reception area there are a number of desks for check in and a computer and telephone area. The computer in the lobby is free I think but if you wish to use wifi in your room there is a charge- I think it is around $- an hour or $-- a day (other options for a week i think are available) and we chose the day option which would have been a lot cheaper than browsing on our phones and coming home to a large bill! Spent a weekend with my staff to enjoy the best our city has to offer. The Dana Hotel has the best staff ever, the most comfortable beds, clean upsale and modern. This is a nice hotel in a great location; however, it is a high price point for the value. The check in process took a very long time. The restaurants were good, but the service in the lobby bar was horrible. I'd stay again for the location.

A complimentary courtesy car is offered on a first-come first-served base for rides in the immediate vicinity (+-- - miles), which comes in handy for restaurant visits in the area. Beautiful hotel and lovely staff, but this is more of a high style business stay type of place than somewhere to kick back and relax Hoping there was a jacuzzi and there was none. And no self-parking, the valet costs $-- a day. But it is a beautifully designed and comfortable place to stay more suited toward business travelers.

We stayed in a One-bedroom deluxe two beds room for - nights. It was in a great location across the road from Madisson Square Garen. It cost about the same as a regular room in New York and it was great to have the extra space of the living room to relax in after a day of sight seeing.

Dirty run-down dump north of downtown. Dingy-Stinky reception area. Old dirty sheets. Rust y shower with extra-low pressure. All in all a miserable experience.

We really enjoyed the space in this hotel and the very comfortable beds.The nearest subway stop was within easy walking distance and made it a pleasure to visit any tourisr sites. Would definately return to the Beacon for a further New York visit.

Have been stayed in Sheraton Denver for - nights for a conference. The hotel staff always provide advice to travellers as if they are all millionaires. I could have gone to Cherry Creek Mall by bus and was told that I should take a taxi. Paid more than $-- for a phone call I didn't get through, which was really a shame! They simply said yes you have to pay because you have dialed and you have asked for assistance from the operator! The plus side is that the rooms look nice although they are obviously overpriced. It is good location to travel around downtown area.

We stayed here for - nights in August, booking the hotel primarily through the strength of the reviews on TA. 
The hotel is excellently located and, using the underground, we were there -- minutes after leaving the airport. The room was spacious, had lovely big beds and floor to ceiling windows which made for a great view. We didn't use the hotel restaurant but it looked popular, and the rooftop pool is certainly a great addition. There's also a lovely little place for breakast just down the road called Thorntons.
So far so good and heading towards a - star TA rating...
...except that on the first full day of our stay we discovered a very soiled towel at the back of a bathroom unit (there are deep units in the bathroom which are used to store haridryers and towels etc). Not soiled as in it had been used by someone after leaving the shower, but soiled as in it had been used by someone after visiting the loo. Really not a nice thing to find in your hotel room! It being the first full day of our holiday neither me nor my girlfriend wanted to kick up too much of a fuss about this, though of course we were clearly pretty unhappy. 
Being the true brits that we are, we lined up at the reception desk and quietly explained to the lady on the desk what the situation was, before leaving for a day's sightseeing. When we got back to the room the towel had of course been taken away, but there was no message from the manager or any one else offering us an apology or an explanation of how this had happened. 
Clearly this was an unpleasant incident, and I was really surprised and dissapointed that at no time during the rest of our stay did anyone from the hotel seek to apologise or compensate us for what had happened. Granted, it's not the end of the world but when you find a filthy towel in your $--- a night hotel room I would expect some kind of recompense from the hotel operator. I can only put it down to the fact that when reporting the incident we didn't rant or rave, or create a scene in the hotel lobby, but I wouldn't expect this kind of behaviour to be necessary to get a response to an incident of this nature.
I am happy to accept that this was a one-time anamoly on behalf of an otherwise very good hotel, but it does of course serve to influence my view. We probably wouldn't stay here again as a result.

We booked a four day-- night package with airfare and hotel for about $--- on expedia. So maybe the room worked out to around $--- a night (pretty good!).
We did not know anything about the hotels in SF. We used this site and people seemed to say some good things about Parc --. I travel on Business and usually like to stay in Marriott’s. This Hotel is owned by Marriott so that ment it would meet a minimum acceptable standard for me.
 Some general thoughts about the hotel.
-) Star rating - the hotel is listed as a - star hotel. I think it is a little shy of that - maybe a -.-- star. Only a little better than a standard Marriot.
-) Room was good sized, clean, comfortable bed, and quiet.

-) Views - ask for a room on the --th floor or higher to get a decent view. They gave us a corner room on the --th which was pretty good.
-) Bums and Panhandlers - In general, SF has a lot of homeless people. Be prepared where ever you are walking around to be asked for money. They are not mean or aggressive - but they are every where - not just around this hotel.

Also this hotel is kind of on the edge of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Tenderloin district"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Know where you are going when you head out for a walk - talk with the bellmen. However, you are right next to an upscale mall, and the cable cars, shops and resturants.
Bottom line on this hotel? Good value for the money. Clean, comfortable, above average. Looking for something more upscale and willing to pay (double-triple) for it? Look to the Mandarin.
Also let me share quick thoughts on SF in general.
City is a little dirty - to much trash in the streets. To many bums. Commercial Architecture is a little boring.
Restaurants - If you can afford $-- per person - try Aqua and Boulevard. They were FANTASTIC.
Go on a NAPA valley wine tour. Bus will pick you up at Hotel. Loved it!
Go on a bus tour to Muir Woods and Sausalito. We went to the Muir woods in the morning but they were only going to let us spend -- min in Sausalito. Get off the bus in Sausalito and spend the afternoon there- take a ferry back to the pier warf.
Skip Fisherman’s Warf for site seeing. Sausalito is MUCH better.
One last thing - If you are looking for an alternative trip - instead of SF - come to Chicago ! You will LOVE IT!

We stayed - nights at the club level room, with the all day club room access and its wonderful selection of foods-treats-drinks all the long, we liked it and would have come back to here again. This is a top end type of hotel,however we think its money worth spend. Spacious room, beautiful decor.The Hotel location is at the top of the hill so i suggest all the ladies can forget about high heels, wear something comfortable when going downtown for shopping, its not far but the up hills are killers. The Valet Parking for the hotel is expensive $--.. go for the car park near by.

Check in and out was very easy and quick. staff are very friendly. Though some people had mentioned that this hotel was next to the parole office. I was traveling alone and felt very safe coming and going during any time of the day or night. Hotel was small and cozy.

Hotel ZaZa Houston is a hip, sophisticated independent hotel in the heart of Houston's museum district and a stone's throw from Rice University. The interior is arty, edgy and unique. The rooms are nicely appointed if a little on the small side. The gym is nice and well located on the second floor. As a smaller hotel, egress and ingress is easy with well staffed valet parking. The only minus is lobby music that is too loud.

WONDERFUL staff! Special kudos to Kevin the doorman!!! Clean, big rooms. This place was great for young kids. Feed the Koi in the fountain twice a day, Nightly movie, game time. Cool glass elevators. Happy Hour with free cocktails and snacks for Mom and Dad. Free delicious hot deluxe breakfast buffet. Indoor pool and hot tub, with grown-ups only hours too! Internet access in the lobby was a bit slow. Dinner at Nicola's was tasty, kids meals well priced. Walk to Lincoln memorial was not too far. We were going to take the Metro, but it there were service interruptions the weekend we were there. Had to pay for parking, not unexpected in the big city.

WOW! 
This is a true gem! Beautiful property, nice staff, great location, close to everything San deigo has to offer, really impressive. We were so happy with our newly redone room, almost did not want to leave and visit the sites, now that said, we did have a - bedroom balcony suite over looking Balboa Park on some very beautiful days, but our room was just the BOMB!
Only drawback was parking, but we never really needed the car except to and from the airport and could have used buses even for that, and next time would not even rent a car

I stayed here for a conference. The hotel seems to be able to handle a large number of guests; there were -,--- present at the conference and also some little league baseball teams. The lobby, business center, and fitness center never seemed crowded, but the Starbucks had long lines and the pub restaurant was busy, understaffed, and hot. I stayed in the Marina Tower. Check-in service was prompt, courteous, and friendly. I can say the same for the parking valet and concierage. My room was very clean and comfortable.The bed was great, and room service was reliable. Unfortunately I was unable to get a room with much of a view, but the -th floor was quiet and I was never bothered by noise from the airport or other quests. Also, the conference facilities were great with prompt attention from the tech team. So on the plus side--very nice room, clean and quiet, and overall wonderful service.
Now, the cons--as noted by other reviewers--the hotel is isolated. If you want to see San Diego, you will need to rent a car, and if you rent a car, you will have to pay the outrageous (in my view) parking fees--$-- per day for self park, $-- for valet. I would prefer to stay some place where I could walk to restaurants and shopping. Secondly, in-room internet is costly, although wi-fi is free in the lobby. Finally, the food and drinks in the on site restaurants were mediocre and way over priced, and the restaurants and bar always seemed to be understaffed. 
I spent two nights checking out restaurants in the Gaslight District. I would recommend taking a cab rather than driving, as parking was scarce and very $$$. Also, the evening scene there is not very family friendly. Try Fred's for Mexican or one of the reasonably priced Italian restaurants.

I read the reviews about rooms being small and dark prior to checking in. Nothing prepare me for just how accurate theose reviews are. I am currently staying in the hotel and writing under a single lap. It is the only light with the exception of a sliver of light at the top of the room. The lobby is nice and trendy but the room I am staying in feels like it is a dark, dingy room in a cheap hotel because it is so small and so terribly lit.
Great location! One block from convention center with a ton of restaurants nearby

This hotel is very good in all ways. The prices are very affordable for the kind of service and amenities at the hotel. Staff is very helpful. They have a wonderfule Park & Fly option which is very customer friendly. Will stay agai for sur and will recommend.

I found a weekend speacial deal starting at $---. This was a minor set back...and everyhing was super...from the staff, down to the details of the room. If you sign up for their loyalty program, you get free breakfast via room service, and free wi-fi as well.

We came for a two day conference to the resort. Not sure here to start really. The rooms were amazing. Balcony views of the hill country were amazing. The food was exemplary. We had lunch in the spa cafe the first day. The food was organic and they grow the veggies and herbs in the grounds. The chef visited with us about this in length. The restaurants are all very good. For the boys, the sports bar is ridiculous. Giant TVs everywhere! The lazy river was heated and open but we just sat by the infinity pool and didn't venture in.. Lots if other things, hiking trails, amazing golf course, fantastic waterfalls.. 
Now for the service... The only other time I have had service at this level was went we're vacationing out of the country. Anything I need was immediately taken care of. We will recommend this resort again and again. WELL DONE!

After having stayed at just about all of the hotels on Shelter Island (and unless this one has been recently upgraded)... I would rate it dead last. It doesn't have the charm or character of the Best Western or Humphries. The parking lot is tedious. My room had outdated decor, ugly color scheme and the architecture is fairly hideous. Kona Kai is sort of lame and uptight. Can't describe it really. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""view"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" from the rooms is obstructed partially. So I would try that or Best Western, then Humphries.

If you are looking with competitive rates in LA downtown area, this is the one.
The hotel's location is great and the service excellent.
Love this hotel! Suite park view second to none. The restaurant was easy and very comfortable for our extended family. Room very expensive, though.

I have to say when we check in and we were given a different room than book I complained a lot to the husband in private. It ended up that the room was perfect for us. Our - yr old stayed in the bedroom with us and our -- yr old had the sofa. We were able to shut the door and sleep, well he was up talking with his friends. It helped us not get on each others nerves after a long day of walking around which in turned made this one of our best vacations.
The room was clean though a dated.
It is locate so conviently to the metro and easily a -- minute walk to the White House and the Lincoln Memorial. 
We did not eat at the hotel, we went for the quick food. I would suggest Bobby's(Flay) Burger Palace. Best burger I have had.

I checked into the Holiday Inn and the front desk staff treated me like I owned the place. They were very welcoming and went over every aspect of the hotel. In the evening the hotel provided a happy hour where they served cheese and crackers, and beer-wine or soda. It was great to enjoy a snack and just relax with fellow guests. This hotel really knows how to take care of their guests and ensure they are happy. I loved that on my second night at the hotel, the front desk called me in the evening to just make sure everything was going alright and to see if I needed anything at all. That is the service level that I love from hotels that understand their customers and their needs. Thanks Holiday Inn for making this such a great trip. Look forward to returning many times in the future.

I stayed for one evening and enjoyed the accomodations. If you are an early riser, ask for a higher floor with a bay view and enjoy an incrediable sunrise. I didn't have time to check out any of the hotel's ammenities this time, but I'm sure everything is top notch.

My family and I stayed at the Talbott from ---------------, Room ---. The entire stay was great. We had a double queen room which was huge. I was concerned about room size since there was four of us in the room, but no problem what so ever. The staff was attentive and helpful. The location was great (you must go across the street for cupcakes at More - even better, just stand outside the place at night and smell the cupcakes baking). I would highly recommend this hotel.

Palmer House reputation as a Grande Dame is thrue. From the moment you enter, you feel a sense a history. In brief, Granbde Dame who is missing her heart. Something can definitely be done to show how warm service can be extended.

This was the first time I visited New York and the location could not have been more perfect! I was steps away from Times Square!!! The hotel was nice, clean and felt very homey. The rooms were a little small, but I expect that in NY. Great staff and very accommodating with all our requests. I have recommended this to everyone back at home and I can't wait to come back again soon!!

Having stayed in San Francisco over half a dozen times in the last -- months, I am excited when I find a hotel worth praising.

As is standard based on my last experience with Kimpton, the room was very well decorated and comfortable. Considerably spacious for a San Francisco hotel. The location is great and the staff is BEYOND friendly and helpful. I also enjoyed the wonderful restaurant Fifth Floor for a special occasion and was not dissapointed. 
My only very slight complaint is that the bathrooms are a bit small, though not cramped. Other than that, I couldn't be more satisfied with my experience.
I plan on staying at Hotel Palomar for my next visit to San Francisco.

For me, the location turned out to be perfect. As I arrived , the place looked decent. It was clean. I had a king bed , with a kitchenette. A two burner stove with a full size fridge, and a dishwasher. The dishwasher wasn't connected to the countertop like it should be, so a person would have to be carefull not to dump out the contents of the washer, or have it flip out from underneath the counter. Other than that the room was great. Cheesy furniture. Fourty somthing flat screen tv. Wireless internet that worked well. I used the exercise rooma couple of times. The seat on the bicycle was about to fall off, it had not been repaired by the time I left. Ex room could have used a freestanding fan. Because I was there for a week, I got a great rate!!! I'll stay there again.

I enjoyed this hotel very much. The best part about it was the location, right in the middle of Midtown sandwiched between Herald Square (The Fashion District) and Times Square. Were close to about - different subway lines and convenient to almost all major attractions.
Check in was easy and smooth. We arrived at --am and I expected to store our luggage and wait until at least -:-- for a room. To our surprise, since they had a room ready, they let us check in. The king room had a little more space and the bathroom was bigger.
The full breakfasts in the morning was an added bonus and was decent. The beds and pillows are great which is the case with most Hampton Inns. The furnishings were tasteful and the rooms very clean. The towels can stand to be a bit thicker but other than that everything was ok.
I would stay here again.

Stayed at the Westin for a week and found it to be only average. I did ask for a quiet room and I did get this, which was great. However, there was a distinct smell of smoke in the room - jetlag prevented me from asking for another. 
There was no shower gel provide. There was no proper breakfast facility - other than a cafe-type place that was pretty poor. Internet connection was not free - in this day and age, this is ridiculous.
On the positive side, the room was large and the view was great. But overall, it was not a great experience.

Stayed here as part of a group trip so can't comment on the service at reception as didn't personally check in or value as the hotel stay was included in an overall price, however we did find our room to be very modern, clean and comfortable. Shower was great. Toilet with its sink on top was neat! Wasn't the best area to be walking around at night but good location for getting to places in the day.
Very good price and comfortable room. The location is excellent, just some minutes walk from Times Square. The room was clean and the towels were changed everyday.

Stayed at this hotel for one night (July -----) with a couple of friends. Outstanding location, and very pleased with the room, which was spacious clean, comfortable and offered a nice view. Very nice bathroom as well - good water pressure. Parking's a bit pricey ($---night), but there's a public parking lot a half block south (on -th Ave, between K St and L St) that's a bit cheaper, and offers elevators for easy access to the street level. The front desk staff was pleasant. Altitude, the rooftop lounge located on the --nd floor, is a *must-see*. Going there for a drink around sunset highly recommended!

After two years I had the occasion to return to this hotel. My first disappointment was the lack of the nice Washington State apples on the front desk. The clerk informed me that that perk was taken away. My second disappointment was the fact that the parking fee had been raised from $--.-- per day to $--.--. The clerk said that the parking meters had gone up so the hotel had to increase their price, really? My third reason to mark them down is the removal of the Tully's lobby coffee and the replacement of the room coffee with a cheap brand (formally Tully's). These factors lead me to reduce my appraisal of the place. The rooms are still very nice but the atmosphere is cool, not sure if it is only me. I still recommend it if you need to be in that part of town. I'll be making more frequent trips to Seattle and now will consider other properties.

We stayed here in June, having booked it through the Sheraton website as we are SPG members. 
Yes, the rooms are small but what do you expect in NYC! The rooms have all the amenities you need and the heavenly bed which is worth the admission fee alone. A fridge would have been useful but there is ice available. 
The one thing that struck us about the room (we were on the --th floor) is how quiet it is. Despite being in a busy area of Manhattan is was really quiet so a good night's sleep was ensured.
The staff were very friendly and always helpful although we were out most of the day exploring.
For breakfast, we checked out the cafe recommended by others on the site but it was -- degrees so we didn't fancy many hot omelettes. We can recommend the Whole Foods Market just round the corner on -th Avenue which has an amazing array of hot and cold food for breakfast and lunch. There's another one at the bottom right-hand corner of Central Park as well - great for picnics.
For dinner, The Salaam Bombay (Greenwich Street, Lower Manhattan) was fantastic and for Italian, go for Pelegrino's in LIttle Italy which is a little pricier but fantastic food and service. Some of the other places in Little Italy offer below-average food and way-above-average prices.
One tip - if you're flying back from JFK allow at least an hour from the hotel because the traffic can be really bad.
Great hotel - would definitely go back if we revisit NYC - reasonable rate, clean rooms, friendly staff and very quiet!

The Courtyard staff is outstanding. We were greated every time we returned and they were always very helpful with directions. Location was perfect, close to Times Square but out of the rush. Room was quiet and nice, although the bed had a trench on one side. Coffee downstairs was very nice on a cold day and the breakfast was excellent. A great place for a quick weekend away.

Just returned from a weekend get a away at The Fairfax at Embassy Row. The hotel is great. It is located ideally within walking distance to Dupont Circle and the Metro. Dupont Circle is a lively beautiful area and if you do not want to go to far there a several dining options. The Hotel is located close to all DC attractions either by Metro or cab.
We took a tour in the Hop on Hop off bus which is close by and we had a blast - I highly recommend it.
The Hotel is fantastic, from bell man to Reception - everybody always welcomed us with a big smile! The rooms are great and the beds are very comfortable (loved the TV!!).
In Room Dining was great during a rainy day and the food was fabulous. We also enjoyed having a drink at the Fairfax Lounge.
The rooms were spottless clean and our Housekeeper knew our name ( I have never experienced that before).
I will definetely return to the Fairfax again!

Other than the horribly unfriendly attitude displayed by the front desk person named Kendra, the --th Century TV and the twin bed (really, it was a true twin size bed !), I thought the place was OK. It was very clean and well located. Aside from Kendra, the hotel staff were great. There are good restaurants in the neighborhood. The free continental breakfast was, well, quite Continental. I give the Buckminster a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""-.--"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".

I picked this hotel because of the location. The price was good for the room considering it was downtown DC. We were there for - nights and paid $--- total. We did not have a room with a fancy view. We just wanted a place to lay our heads at night. So, if you are looking for something economical with a great location this is the place for you. It was fairly close to a metro stop (- blocks, which rode several times). Althought, they really get you for parking, $-- a day. 
Overall, the room was clean. It was a very outdated hotel. The photos on the internet make this hotel look great and I would say that it really didn't look like that. I thought we would use the pool after long days of sightseeing, but we didn't and the one time that we were going to there were no chairs available.

I was pretty excited staying at the Hudson given the location and the funky website. I arrived very early for check-in but finished the paperwork with the front desk staff and was able to leave my bag on hold. The hotel reception area-restaurant has an amazing ambiance. Beautiful! 
The Room:
HATED IT! It definitely ONLY provides the bare basics. I believe I was in room ---. There was about --- inches (barely) of walking space between the bed and the surrounding wall. The view out the window was great but although I kept it closed, there was a distinct draft that kept me shivering at night and since its so close to the main streets, there was A LOT of street noise that was very disturbing. The mattress was hard and uncomfortable. The bathroom was cute but again - cramped! You literally have to sit on the toilet in an angle of to the side since there is not enough space between the wall and the toilet to sit straight. 
Decent for the location of the hotel but I like a good night's sleep and therefore, won't be staying here again and is why I am giving this hotel an average rating. 
The staff were excellent. I really want to recognize this aspect of the hotel because although I wasn't satisfied the room, the service was enough to keep me content without complaints.

The problem with hotels that try to be trendy is that the trend inevitably passes. Then you are left with staff wearing uniforms that look more at home in a cheap and cheerful burger joint, kitschy decor, unhappy staff providing bad customer service and the occasional mention by tour guides of what once was.

I can't imagine how frustrating it would have been if I had been staying there on business and needed to access my emails. I hope the hotel sees these reviews and does something about either their IS provider or their server. It turned out to be a major annoyance.

Amidst the expensive apartment towers and designer stores of downtown Chicago's Gold Coast sits the Hilton Suites, a very nice place to bed down after a day or night prowling the Windy City.
The hotel is in a relatively nondescript tower at Mies van der Rohe and Delaware, a block from N. Michigan Avenue and the John Hancock building. It features a relatively small, attractive and placid lobby. The front-desk staff is pleasant and efficient.
But the rooms are what make this place such a good value for the money. The standard room is not really a suite, but sort of a mini-suite. The cozy sleeping area is separated from the spacious sitting area, which features a couch, cocktail. lounger and work desk, as well as a bar area with a mini-fridge, microwave, sink and coffee service (which has Lavazza coffee and actual liquid creamer!).
My bedroom featured an uber-comfortable king bed that I didn't want to crawl out of on a cold Chicago morning. It also contained a vanity area. And though the rooms won't win any contests for edgy design, the soothing earth tones and comfortable furnishings will be a welcome sight for a tired traveler.
The spacious bathroom (with excellent shower pressure and Peter Thomas Roth bath products) could be accessed from the bedroom or the sitting room.
Both the bedroom and sitting room featured flat-screen TVs, though the channel selection was rather limited.
With so much good grub in Chicago, I didn't bother with the hotel restaurant or room service, which was typically overpriced. There's also a little lobby shop that serves Starbucks coffee.
As with most downtown chain hotels, just about any service in the hotel is a la carte, including wired and wireless internet service, as well as access to the business center. So when I needed to boot up, I found a nice little independent coffee house on the north side where the WiFi came free with a soy latte.
The Hilton Suites is a block from the north end of the Mag Mile, close to Bloomingdales and the Water Tower Place shopping center. Nearby restaurants include Gaylord India and the Cheesecake Factory.
Price-wise, you could spend a lot more and get a lot less than the Hilton Suites. I got a sensational rate of $-- per night via a Priceline bid, and even the rates on the Hilton website, or Orbitz, Expedia etc., compare favorably with other hotels of its quality.

This was one of the best days of my life and this hotel was a big reason for that. I cannot say enough about how wonderful this place is, and I highly recommend it. I will never stay anywhere else but here when I come to San Francisco. Thank you Hotel Drisco!

You will love the location--right out the back door of Union Square and there was not one place that I thought about going that I could walk to from this location. You will immediately love the service provided by this hotel. There is no doubt that this is the model and one that will make you feel special.
The overall concept is still old school elegance. You're not going to see anything amazingly interesting, but all the things you would expect from a high profile, nice hotel gets high ranks here.
I love the marble entry and I like the vantage that I get from the architecture in the main hall. I like the linens on the bed. However, I think the bath towels need to be changed out--I've had fluffier ones at the business-level hotels.
And, get ready to love the great bath robes and house shoes. They even put a little towel down with turn down service next to your bed.
Now, if only we could get a chocolate at night and ice upon check-in!

Stayed here for a college search trip for my daughter because it modest cost and was a five minute walk to the Boston T (mass transit system). Rooms were standard size with comfortable double beds. 
 There is a distinct lack of restaurants in the area. We found it necessary to take the T into downtown Boston to have a nice meal. (Though Amrheins is near by and is recommended for a very nice meal of classic American Cuisine.)
The staff was helpful and went out of their way to assist us when our luggage was lost by the airline. The hotel took us to a local shopping area to get """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""supplies"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The hotel has a shuttle that runs hourly to and from Logan International making your flights. There is a Au Bon Pain deli in the hotel lobby that is the hotel restaurant. A separate full bar is also off of the lobby with several TVs playing the local and national sports.

Booked a View Room with King Bed expecting a view of the city and the bay (as per the wording on the website) however only got a view of the city. In hotel's defence management was very understanding at my disappointment.
Overall the room was clean and comfortable and had recently been renovated but still showing its age. As a tourist would not recommend the location of this hotel as its close to the 'Tenderlion' area which is very unsavoury.

We are frequent travellers to NYC. And many hotels in NYC look a lot better on the photo's and the staff is most of the times not very interested in there guests.
But the brandnew Tryp hotel had a very friendly and helpfull staff. The rooms are spacious and clean and we like the walkin shower. The hotel is located near the subway. And free wifi!
The only thing, we maybe can complain about, are the soft pillows, so maybe a pillow menu would be nice. 
Excelent choice!

I booked a reservation for my daughter who's in the millitary. She had to stay - night in texas before going to Japan. When I booked on line I also called the hotel direct to get information on what was required for me to do since I was paying for her room, but she would be staying there.
