Nice way to send a girl all alone in Texas by herself off to Japan.

Wonderful hotel and everything you would expect an upper class Hyatt Hotel to be. Our room faced the runway but could barely hear the planes taking off and landing. Fitness room was large and had all the equipment you would need. The roof-top pool was probably the only negative experience since you are exposed to the sounds and smells of the jet engines. Food in the restaurant was great - suggest eating at the bar for a more relaxed atmosphere.

Pleasant surprise as this was booked through travel office for business. Had an early morning flight to catch so was put up for the night here. Very nice room and comfy bed. Easy to get to and easy to get back and forth from rental car agency to airport-hotel. No airport noise that I heard. Room service was very good, not quite as pricey as I'm used to, appetizer, meal, tip, tax, and service charge made it just over $--. Only complaint was crappy view but it being only one evening it was no big deal. Easy to get downtown on mass transit if you so desire. I'd stay again!

The Hilton Times square is an amazing hotel and has wonderful staff. We got upgraded to highest floor room when we mentioned we were in our honeymoon. It was the only hotel to provide us with special treatment. The staff is awesome and the hotel location is one of the best. It's in the heart of times square. I will never stay somewhere else in NYC. My special thanks go to front desk manager, Chad Nathan, and front desk agent Peter. Your professionalism, care and hospitality at its best made our stay perfect. Hilton is lucky to have you.

When we arrived the Bellman was wonderful! Gave my nephews each a bag with juice and granola bars. Ask for candy bars, we each got one, and it was great chocolate! And lots of literature on places in Georgetown and DC. Rooms are very small, especially for a family of -. They provide for FREE a small refrigerator, microwave and a cot for my one nephew. 
Parking is horrible! You have to park in the hospital parking garage at $-- a day! There is a FREE shuttle service to take you to the Metro Trains. You can go to either Dupont Circle or to Rosslyn. It's called the GUTS. Runs about every ----- minutes. That was a plus. 
There were free cookies (that were great!) and lemonade in the lobby all day long, and apples in the morning. Just down the hall is a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cafeteria"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" style restaurant, and breakfast was not too bad at all, depending on what you want to eat. They make omlets for you and have other warm items. The warm items are weighed by the pound. Don't get fruit, as it also is very expensive and by the pound! My husband and my self ate breakfast for about $--.--. Not bad! Stay away from donuts and danish as they want $-.-- for one donut and $-.-- for a danish! YIKES! 
We ate at Hoya's restaruant one night and food was excellent, a bit expensive, but worth it to us, as we had been eating pizza for two nights in a row, and it's not the best pizza. There also is another area that surves Subway-Taco Bell-KFC-Pizza Hut, but they close at -:-- and we would get back later than that. So we ordered take out. You can order pizza and other fast food to be delivered, just ask at the front desk. 
The kids were very disapointed to not be able to swim, as you have to use the college facilities, and it was $-- a person a day, even if you just wanted to watch the kids and not go in. We didn't do it. $-- is a lot to swim for about a --- hour. 
Over all, it was enjoyable. Oh, stay away from the National Aquarium, you see more fish at the local Petco for free as you have to pay $-.-- a person to go in and $-.-- for the kids. What a waste of time! Smithsonians are WONDERFUL and free! Wear really good walking shoes, you'll need them! Highly recommend Arlington Cemetary, and the changing of the guards. A must see! 
Take the GUTS to Dupont Circle and then the Metro to Cleavland stop. Walk to the Zoo is on flat ground about - blocks. Then you can walk down hill to Woodley Park Metro stop, which is a little shorter, about - blocks. But better to walk on flat ground then uphill. Zoo is fabulous and FREE! We didn't see it all! So much to do and see there! And very clean!
Hotel is very hard to find! Very small sign, you have to go into what looks like the hospital emergency, the first entrance. Go to way in the back. Very deciving. But we finally found it. Just wish swimming was free and that we had some sort of discount on parking as guest of the hotel. Beds were very, very comfy! Great toiletries also!

Since I'm a Hilton Gold member, I find the Metropolitan as an above average hotel for the the Midtown area. I'm not touting my horn, but I did receive bedside chocolates from turn-down service, check-in treats, daily water bottles, and access to the higher floors. So my review will be somewhat biased.
First of all, the hotel's fragrance or overall smell reminds me of MGM Grand in Vegas. I can't put a finger on it, but it reminds me of Vegas every night during my - night stay. The overly funky, hip lobby - bar area also reinforces this. The service was great, especially since I lost my key card one night and they helped resolved a business center issue (connectivity) for me another night as well. The bed were quite comfortable (King) and I think they actually had too many bathroom towels and amenities for me.
Overall, for the business rate, location to work, and the service, I would rate this as above average. During my stay there were a good mix of international and domestic leisure and business travelers, and all seem quite satisfied from the body language. Keep in mind I received double-points (on top of the bonus as Gold), so this hotel is a good benefit for us Hilton folks.

My boyfriend and I stayed here for the night for my birthday, using a voucher from RueLaLa and it was great! The only problem we found was that the hotel was pet friendly and there was a barking dog in the room next door! I saw that the hotel was pet friendly before hand, but figured it would be a separate part of the hotel. Other than the barking dog, we had a great time and the room was very very nice!

The hotel is very spacious for a new york accomodation. The service is in top and i would recomend this place to anyone traveling to the city. It is especially nice for an extended stay, as you have your own kitchen and the opportunity to have - or - bedroom appartments. A little wore down, but clean and best of all affordable - which is almost impossible to find in this city. Good location close to major attractions yet in pretty calm corner of town near the UN.

I have visited New York -- times and this is one of the best hotels I have stayed in. Housekeeping staff and reception staff were so very helpful and professional at all times. Loved the coffee and muffins first thing in the morning. No complaints at all. Will be back in the summer.

I stayed here four days on an impromptu visit to Charlotte. The Hotel is convenient to the airport, the City, the southern suburbs, and highway. The Management was superb and the staff were friendly and efficient. The room was clean and the mattress and bedding were terrific (for a change). The hotel offers smoking and non-smoking rooms, a full breakfast is included in the rate, and I was very satisfied with my experience. This hotel is a great value.

We stayed on the --th floor and has a fantastic view of Manhattan (Chrysler building v nearby, lovely view of the Empire state etc) and the East River - Queens etc. Friendly staff, lovely breakfasts and clean, comfortable rooms with a huge bed! We booked via hotels.com and chose the option with breakfast, however we weren't told on arrival that we needed a voucher for breakfast every morning, but this was sorted out for us fairly promptly. We were close enough to everything without being right on Times square (which was a bit of a mad house to be honest! We were glad to be away from all that). 
I searched for ages trying to find the 'right' hotel for us - I'm happy to say that we were very pleased with this hotel. We're in our late --s and it was just right for us, though some may feel the hotel is a little bit 'corporate' for their tastes and may want something with more character. But this is NYC and we wanted the whole sky scraper, fab room thing so it was perfect for us.

having stayed at this hotel for - nights, the staff from reception desk to handyman and restaurant staff and valet parking were exceptionally friendly. our room was nice and clean and even though it was at the front of the hotel we didnt find it noisy. we had one small problem with the toilet blocking and the handyman was there to fix it within -- minutes after reception had even offered to move us to another room. the breakfast was very nice, as was the food in the bar restaurant.
 travelling from the uk we were advised to hire a car, which we did, and strongly recommend, even though the valet parking may appear expensive, but a luxury we british dont usually get and were made to feel a million dollars. in fact my wife always expects me to open the car door for her now when she gets home. hope to come back to la again and will definitely stay here again when we do

Me and My Father stayed in The Penn for - nights from -- April to the --th and i read alot of bad reviews in the weeks leading up to the holiday and to be honest was dreading it. We arrived at -pm and had to wait until -pm to check in, not a problem as they are the rules as advertised. 
The Room, we stayed in a room on the -th floor (room ---A), room was basic but great, - twin beds, fairly big T.V, bathroom was very clean, window view of city and for the price what more can you ask for. 
The Staff, we found the staff to be very helpful, really couldnt do enough for you, rooms were cleaned every day, new towels and plenty of them, new sheets, everything was great. Only disgruntlement i had with the staff is when we checked out at -- on the last day, when they brought our room up on screen and found no charges, they couldnt wait to get rid of us.
The Location, what more could you ask for less than -- mins walk from Times Square, less than - mins to Empire State and for those who take thier wifes and girlfriends, MACY's almost next door. 
Getting food near the hotel, no problem, there were alot of places very close to the hotel, from Wendy's to Popeyes chicken, KFC, Dunkin Donuts and plenty of local food stores or DELI's where you can also buy all different kinds of foods, all within a minute walk.
I am actually going to the travel agent in the next few days to book NEW YORK for next year and will definatly be staying at the Penn. 
The funny thing is, people slate this hotel, when i went to book this hotel they advertised it as a - star hotel, with great location, I would agree but in NEW YORK, LOCATION IS EVERYTHING, when we were walking around we saw the Grand Hyatt near Grand Central Terminal, a - star hotel, and its location isnt as good as that of the Penn. 
And lets be honest in New York how long are you going to be in your hotel........
I would recommend this hotel to anyone, like i said i will definatly be staying there again.

Let me start by saying that I was expecting something nicer than the Westin since it's a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""boutique"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" SPG hotel. I found the hotel be be run down and dirty. Mold in the shower grout, peeling wallpaper and dingy dirty walls. For the price, I guess I shouldn't complain. I think my expectations may have just been too high. 
As for service, the front desk guy I spoke to (Eduardo) was curt and rude. I was asking when we could check in since I got in early and he spoke as if I didn't know that I was early. Hello? That's why I asked when I could check in. Anyway, maybe he was having a rough day... 
We also called once to the front desk to say that the ice machine was broken and asked if they could send up some ice. They said room service doesn't exist in that hotel. Again, i think my expectations were too high. 
One last gripe... There's no wifi in the room! The hotel description says wifi available for purchase but only if you have a jack to plug into. No ipods or phones can get on. Only place where wifi is available is in the lobby. Big minus in my book. I've stayed at the Hudson before and it's much much smaller but the experience was so much better.

Just got back from a - day trip to California. Based on a recommendation from a friend in LA, we chose the Hilton Universal City for our LA base---even though we never even went to Universal Studios (aside from CityWalk - nights).
Most of the things we needed to do were in the North Hollywood-Hollywood area and the hotel couldn't have been more convenient. It also provided very easy freeway access to Santa Monica and other side trips.
The hotel staff was notably friendly, courteous, and helpful. Special shout out to Stuart at the front desk, who was wonderful and handled a couple of minor issues promptly and professionally.
The hotel itself is beautiful and the guest rooms are very attractive, contemporary, and clean. The beds were amazingly comfortable! If it had been warmer, we would have used the pool. I did use the gym, which had everything I needed.
There are only two issues that prevented me from giving - stars: As noted by others, there are some real elevator problems. Surely, engineering can fix the issue. Waits were very long at times and sometimes the elevator would go down when the only button pushed had been for up. Also, on our check-out day when we were especially rushed, we had a problem with hot water. They sent someone to our room and it was more a matter of fiddling with the faucet handle than anything else, but it was annoying.
Still, I would highly recommend the hotel to anyone visiting LA looking for an attractive, quiet, safe location that's close to so many things. The positives far outweighed the minor flaws.

Its an old hotel and close to the metro train...so think twice if you are a light sleeper. but its clean and the staff are helpful. Also close to the attractions, eg. museum campus. Its worth the money in general. You cannot expect more at this price at the loop in Chicago I guess.

Room was fine, standard Hilton fare -- excluding the TV which hasn't been upgraded to an LCD yet. The only real issue I had was the noice level. Even with my windows shut up on the --th floor, I could hear everything on the streets. If they can make the Doubletree in Times Square soundproof, you think they could make a little effort and upgrade the windows in here. That said, I still haven't found a quiet hotel in SF.

The hotel room was a little smaller than other Hiltons but still with the same Hilton quality and standards. We were upgraded to a --th floor room overlooking the runways. The room was quiet and we were not disturbed by the air traffic. Decent buffet breakfast, superior exercise facility. I will stay here again if I have a morning flight out of O'Hare.

We checked in and upon arriving in room discovered that it had not been cleaned from previous occupants. After a long (- hour) flight, this was a great disappointment. Called down to desk to arrange another room and were told to wait for delivery of new key so we didn't have to lug bags back and forth. Never saw the key delivery after about -- minute wait in dirty room, and two phone calls to desk. Went down to desk with all of our bags, expecting immediate attention (luxury hotel better attend to something like this immediately) and was brushed off by receptionist. When finally attended to, apologies started. A bit late considering that we were now almost an hour from the first check in. We were give a room key that allowed access to the 'club' level which basically provided us with free continental breakfast. Since we were touring we could not have taken advantage of any other privileges. Room we were given was also an upgrade but that was also a minor comp since we really were hardly in the room. Remainder of experience was fine but I have to say I've never had a check in experience this bad before. As such, I have a difficult time recommending Parc-- in San Francisco as a place to stay that claims to be luxury and strong attention to clients.

I've been doing business on and off in SFO for over -- years and this is one of my favorite hotels. Completely remodeled just a few years ago when Hilton took it over, it feels very new and hip. The service level is quite good, but the two best things about this hotel are the location and the views. The location is on the border between the Financial District and Chinatown, and is easilty walkable to North Beach. I can't think of any hotel that has a better location if you have business in the Financial District but want to socialize in Chinatown and-or North Beach, two of my favorite parts of the city. As for views, be sure get an upgraded room facing north ----- floors up for the most amazing view of Coit Tower, Telegraph Hill and the Bay. It is really a magical view, either day or night.

My wife and I stayed at the Handlery for - nights and thoroughly enjoyed our visit. We'd been to the city about - years before but in a different hotel and were keen to come back. The original room we were offered was noisy (a union protest across the street) so the excellent desk staff found us another two to choose from and were very helpful as were all the others we dealt with. Breakfast in the adjoining Daily Grill was excellent and the closeness of Union Square for shops & eating and the cable-car stop only yards away were most convenient. We found the Handlery to be excellent and can happily recommend it to other travellers.

As other reviewers have noted, this hotel is in a great location. From here we were able to walk to musicals and plays on Broadway, go to Central Park, and eat at some great restaurants. The concierge was helpful in making recommendations for us based on the fact that we were a family with - young kids. The room was small, but tastefully decorated. The bathroom was ultra small- barely big enough for a tall person to sit on the toilet without kicking the sink. The view from our room was of the back of three other buildings- like being in a tunnel of concrete. The elevator is super small and often slow if you are checking out at a busy time. Definitely a tight fit for - people and - small suitcases. I am aware that this is New York, so the smallness of the hotel is outweighed by the great location.

I've been to NYC a couple times but this was my first stay in Greenwich Village. I had a wonderful time. Everyone on the staff here was friendly and helpful. The room was clean and pleasant. I would definitely stay here again.

I recently stayed at the Sheraton Seattle for a convention and everything about the stay was perfect. The check in process was smooth and painless, the concierge desk was well informed about everything around the city, the entire property was clean and well maintained, the rooms were spacious and comfortable, and housekeeping was efficient and prompt. I really enjoyed the art in the lobby especially the Chihuly piece located next to the gift shop. Plus, you can’t beat the location of the hotel! If there was one thing to complain about, it would be the bell desk. I almost felt like they were doing me a favor by assisting with my bags. Overall a great stay and will stay there for all future visits.

My room was small but elegantly furnished and clean - the size of a --x-- bedroom. But there was NO view (looked out onto an ugly wall a few yards away from the window, so that made it feel a little claustrophobic). But being a few blocks from Central Park, I had no intention of staying in my room for the one Spring day I was there, so I certainly wouldn't be writing a review to complain about a small room. But at night when I went to take a shower, I could not get the water to warm up. I was told to let it run awhile. It ran and ran and stayed cold. I called the front desk again and they sent a repair man down into the boiler room. I gave up and went to sleep. They said they were full and couldn't offer me a different room. The next morning, I tried to take a shower as I was told it had been fixed. Nope. A bellman came to the room and couldn't get the shower to work at all. The room also did not have a clock although I was told there was one in there. Not a big space to miss seeing a clock in, so I don't know where it was hiding. I was told it was on the charging dock, but there was no charging dock in the room either. Also, I'm glad I had my earplugs because the air conditioning was extremely noisy. I asked that they give a significant discount (or complete comp) to the non-profit that was paying for my room primarily due to not having a working shower, but I don't know if that ever happened.

This hotel is a GREAT value! If you are traveling with kids it can't be beat. Our room was huge! There were two comfortable king size beds in seperate bedrooms, two full baths, and a pull out sofa in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""family room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Our family of - was quite comfy there. The kitchenette is a bit dated but who cares? I was delighted that is was all clean and working! But by far my favorite thing about Habitat is the price. Our room including taxes but minus our Go Austin card discount was only ---.-- per night. If you take into account what the incredible hot breakfast would have set us back (--.-- easily) this is an amazing bargin. Thank you Habitat. We had a wonderful stay!

AS with Londoner---, I feel that The James needs to improve quickly in order to even stay in business. Yes, the bar has a great view. And yes, the location is excellent. But the staff is most unprofessional ( Save Michael who is a real gem ) and our room not only leaked during a rain storm, but seemed never quite clean. It was also SO noisy that we moved once ( the first day) to what they said was a quieter room, but it was very loud with noise from other rooms-door slamming, etc. Also, there was such a lack of attention to detail - only turn-down service one night of our - night stay, and no real knowledge from the concierge staff about the cool new restaurants in town. They pride themselves as being a luxury hotel, with luxury prices to boot, but don't follow through.

This is the -nd year my husband and I stayed here to see the Bruins play the Blue Jackets. It is obviously an older hotel but the rooms are huge and clean with a refridgerator and microwave. The staff is efficient, and pleasant enough. The parking is underground and secure, but if you have something larger than a compact car, getting into the parking spots may be a bit tricky.
My major complaint is the noise from the floors above. The first time we stayed in the hotel, they gave us a top floor room, which was fine. The next three times we were on a middle floor. I can't believe that we got """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""foot stompers"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" above us each time, so it must be in the construction It is very noisy and was loud enough to wake me up, even with using ear plugs. The restaurant is just okay as mentioned in other reviews, but the staff was nice and I did have a very good plate of biscuits and gravy for breakfast.

The Eventi was an absolute pleasure and I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a beautiful top-notch hotel in New York. Unbeatable location, wonderful views, gorgeous rooms, fantastic service. You really can't beat this place - it's amazing!

I really enjoyed staying at the Andaz. The staff was very helpful, the rooms were very nice, and the fitness center was very convenient. The quick check in with the roaming staff using I-pads was a nice touch. In a couple minutes I was already headed up to my room. The rooms are large with faux hardwood floors and a large shower. Super clean and comfortable. The king bed was comfortable and relaxing. I would stay here again for sure.

Checked in late at night. Bathroom was flooded and dirty, so had to get room switched. Small, dated, with faulty AC that seemed to turn off even though the room was still warm. The entire lobby, though attractive, was very hot. When I asked about it, the staff was dismissive. Then, my AC in the room did not work at all - and this was July!
The waiter at the restaurant was belligerent, nasty and took forever for simple requests. The only restaurant is in the basement and it is dark, cramped and depressing. I saw a gang of drunks stealing beer from the closed bar - and the night manager would not do anything about it. Even though I had paid for a week, I left after just a few days. Horrific!!!

First impressions of the hotel are amazing - very impressive from the outside and the lobby is breathtakingly beautiful. The rooms have outstanding views over San Diego however the money has definitely been spent in the lobby and bars and not in the rooms. The rooms are looking a little tired and not at the same standard of the public areas of the hotel. Location is great - the hotel backs onto the Seaport Village which is a lovely little area to potter around in and has a gorgeous marina to enjoy in the sunshine. Seal Tours and the Trolley Tour are also available from the Seaport Village - both are definitely worth doing! USS Midway Museum is about a -- minute walk and is a great day out also. Overall a gorgeous hotel in a great place, would highly recommend.

If you stay here you will be treated like DIRT from the desk clerks, you will get double billed on your credit card, and this hotel will charge an extra $-.-- as a destination fee which is not tax and is probably illegal. 
NEVER AGAIN.

I booked this hotel a week prior to my trip and the rates where really cheap compared to any other hotel Downtown. As soon as we walked in we were greeted and treated great! Our room was clean and spacious. The bed was really comfortable and the AC worked great! The shower had a great shower head and lots of towels were provided.

Really enjoyed our stay here. Walking distance to major attractions and easy to get on-off the subway. Rooms are immaculate and generously sized, though decor is a little dated. Only caution is no Wifi and it's expensive to buy access. Would absolutely stay here again.

I live in Dallas but stayed at the Magnolia as a small treat with my husband as we attended a reception nearby. 
Having lived in Dallas all my life, it was so fun to experience Dallas from a different perspective, as a visitor. Honestly, I love the impression the Magnolia gives of my city. The Magnolia has a historic feel but has been renovated with all kinds of modern comfort and decor. The price, location and accommodations were all excellent. If you are going to be in Dallas, I strongly recommend renting a car as that is the best way to navigate the city. The cost for parking is $-- for come and go valet or $-- for a one-time park. You have other options of where to stay that are new and right in the middle of action but I prefer staying somewhere just a few miles away for a better night's rest. The complimentary brunch on Sunday is exceptional, especially considering it is complimentary. There are some nicer restaurants nearby but if you want something more casual or more options, there are plenty of options within a few miles. You can use the - mile radius hotel shuttle or take a short drive to the Deep Ellum area for the Twisted Root or Cafe Brazil (kind of grungy in a good way part of Dallas). You can also go to McKinney Ave. where there are a variety of restaurants and pubs (The Gingerman has an unbelievable amount of beers on tap in a great old wooden house). If you want some higher end shopping and more food options, go north on -- to the North Park Mall area. For more nightlife- bars, clubs and indie music concerts, look up Lower Greenville. For events, you are seconds away from the American Airlines Center and surrounding area. For biking-walking, head to the Katy Trail or White Rock Lake. All of these things are within -- miles of the Magnolia. Having been downtown countless times, it was nice staying in a room on a higher floor and seeing the ornate work on the tops of the buildings I've only seen from street level. If I ever had a reason to get away again, this would be my choice. Enjoy!

We stayed here for - nights in ---- and it was ideal for our needs. It was my first trip to NY and the hubby had only been once before. All we really wanted was somewhere to crash after our days of sight seeing and this was perfect. En suite was fine. Room was cleaned and tidied daily if we wanted it. This also included our beer which was on the table, being put in front of the air con unit to keep it cool! The hotel was within walking distance of many attractions, and there is a fantastic Mexican restaurant across the road from the hotel which dis fantastic margaritas. The only downside is that there is not tea and coffee making facilities in the room, however, this seems to be a very British thing as have often found this to be the case inAmerican hotels.
This place isn't luxurious, but that is reflected in the price. The staff were helpful and recommended places to eat etc nearby.

My mother, sister, aunt and I went to New York for the first time and stayed in the Mariott Marquis. I have to say it was the best. I was skeptical at first because I read the posts here about the elevators and how long it took to get on one, but we never had a long wait for the elevators the entire time we were there. Actually I don't think we ever waited for more than a minute or two and we were on the --th floor. Our room had a perfect view of Times Square and the hotel staff was very friendly. During peak times the hotel kept an elevator offline which an employee would use to shuttle people up to their rooms so that you didn't have to wait. We also avoided leaving our rooms during the peak times which were between --:-- and noon for check out and -:----:-- pm for the shows. Overall I had a great experience and would highly recommend this hotel to anyone.

Overall, it was okay until I had to take a shower....NO HOT WATER! When I called the front desk, Amy told me they ran out of hot water and wait -- min. I informed her that I took a cold -- min shower, she then said wait because everyone else is taking a shower. I can suck it up and take a cold shower, but there is no way I will make my - year old do that!

Myself and two friends stayed at the Salisbury for - nights in March ---- and had a fantastic time! 
This was our first visit to the Big Apple and we had read plenty of reviews about the city and also the Salisbury. I agree that the hotel is a little dated, that the lifts can be a little slow and that if you are on a lower floor (we were on the -th floor) street noise can be a little intrusive (especially at -am in the morning! Earplugs are a must!). However all that being said we felt it only added to the experience. 
We had a one bedroom suite which had a very large lounge, bedroom with two double beds, plenty of closet space for all our goodies, kitchenette area with microwave, fridge and coffee maker (not being a coffee drinker I used the microwave to heat up water for a cup of tea) and a small but perfectly adequate bathroom. 
The only problems we encountered were the fuse box being tripped by something in the room which did plunge us into darkness on a few occasions. However, we reported the problem to Reception one morning and by the time we arrived back in the evening the problem was fixed. There was only one occasion when the water temps in the shower went a bit erratic. Other than that I can honestly say that the hotel is well maintained, very clean and is ideally located for sightseeing and shopping (both of which we did plenty !!).
We didn't use the subway when we were there, but definitely would if we went again, but we did use taxis and plenty of foot power (very, very comfortable shoes are a must!). We also used the Gray Line bus tour service which offers a hop on-off loops tour of downtown, uptown and Brooklyn. Tickets are readily available from representatives standing on the pavement down -th Avenue, heading down towards Times Square.
A taxi from JFK charges a standard rate of $-- to anywhere in Manhattan. However, make sure you confirm price of transport back to the airport as we had (wrongly) assumed the same rate applied and entered into a very heatedt arguement with our taxi driver as he was driving us away at speed down --th Street!! In the end though we agreed a price and had the quickest (albeit a little hairy) journey back to JFK!
I would recommed the Great American Health Bar between -th and -th just down from the hotel for a good breakfast. We also used the food delivery service from Angelo's next door on our second night for pizza and Ceasars Salad as we were far too tired to go out (both excellent!). If you like Indian food try the Bay Leaf restaurant on -- w --th street - very nice atmosphere, setting and excellent food. We also made sure we had the deli experience and found one just off Times Square, which was less busy and a little less expensive than those on the main strip. 
We hope to one day return to NYC and will definitely book into the Salisbury. If you are heading there yourself or are thinking of it, I know you will have a fantastic time.
Enjoy!

The Sheraton is a huge hotel and convention center. It is right in the heart of Back Bay. Once you are registered at the hotel you can use the internet area. There are free computers for use to surf the internet or check email. You are limited to -- minutes at a time. You can also connect your laptop in this area. If you want to connect in your room there is a charge. The reception area is nice and inviting. The rooms, at least in the North tower are older and not up to the Sheraton standard. I found it difficult to get the temperature of the room at a contant level. The Atlantis Fitness facility is well-equipt but there is a $-- per day charge. The swimming pool is free of charge.

My husband and I were attending a birthday party in Detroit (about -- minutes from our home) and decided to make it a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""date"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" by staying overnight at the Westin, which we had heard a lot of buzz about. We arrived to check in at about --:-- p.m. While checking in my husband asked for a bottle of water to take some pills. Alas, at """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""our level"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" there was not complimentary bottled water in the room and the gift shop was closed. Our tough luck. The room was comfortable and attractively decorated with the obligatory plump, plush bedding and an oversized well appointed bathroom. However, the foam pillows had a slightly odd odor and the pillowcases were pilled, not the nice smooth texture of the sheets. In short, the Westin isn't going out of its way to make you feel like a guest. The coffee bar in the room had no creamer, there was a charge for wi-fi (which is just crazy, when every coffee bar and auto repair shop is offering this for free now) and the front desk was so impersonal in thier approach to customer service. We have other choices in the area that would would consider before returning here, or recommending it to out of town guests. Too bad. Detroit could use something to boast about.

Avoid !
This is a grubby motel, dirt has gathered everywhere, there were huge cobwebs in the bedroom, closet and bathroom. These take weeks to grow.
The room just had that icky feel.....only high point was great Thai restaurant across the road, called Hoy Ka.
It cost us over $--- a night incl tax, total rip -off!!

I have read a few of the reviews, and just had to add mine, as I stay at the Congress every week for work, and have since last November (----).
I was initially drawn to this hotel (and btw, I'm sitting in the hotel as I type this) by the low price. Courtyard, and others of that ilk, run at least $-- a night higher in this area.
As a regular business traveler, I have stayed in many hotels, none as old as the Congress, and so none with as much of an excuse as the Congress. For every negative I read, I can point to a similar experience at a major chain hotel that should be delivering a better product.
The Congress is over --- years old, and yes, the building does show its age. Some reviewers complained of construction noise, and this is due to the continuous remodelling that is going on. A one-thousand room hotel doesn't get redone overnight - and certainly not when it has such a low occupancy rate due to the very issues they are working hard to correct.
Here are the pros and cons as I see them on my --th week here:
Cons:
-old carpeting
-sometimes stale, funky smells in the hallways
-inroom coffee is about the cheapest stuff they could find
-some fixtures have issues: jiggly handrails, loose trim, dresser drawers needing repair, etc.
-surprise closings of food service (makes sense when paid staff outnumber the guests)
-Low water pressure on some floors. Irritating if you like a bath as opposed to a shower. I find that the shower sprays fine, even in low pressure.
-If they tell you your room is in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Buckingham Wing"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", tell the clerk you're leaving if they don't put you in one of the towers. The BW is a small part of the hotel on the south side of the building that looks like it was added on in the ----'s. These rooms can really sour you on the Congress, but unless there's a convention going, they should be able to move you.
-Low occupancy on some weeks makes you feel like the place is abandoned. Sometimes I'd swear it's just me and two other guys in the whole place.
Pros:
-Best prices in Chicago Loop area
-Great bar. The bar has a reputation apart from the hotel.
-Different room every week (I'm on week --, and I've yet to have the same exact layout twice. Kind of nice when you have to put up with hotels all the time)
-Comfy beds. Someone upstream complained about a torn bedspread. I've seen sloppy housekeeping in the best of them.
-Friendly staff. Really. Someone complained about being ill-treated. Well, I've been working long enough to know that there are some folks that just don't quit until they've pressed every one of somebody's buttons.
-Tons of character. Rooms have -- or -- foot ceilings, never seen that before.
-Internet works great. It's wired instead of wireless, which in a hotel is better, I think. I've had some bad chain hotel experiences with the wireless stuff.
-The Lakeview rooms are beautiful. Nice view of Lake Michigan, worthy of snapping a few pics to impress your friends.
-Room service food is fast and excellent. Killer garlic mashed potatoes, prime rib bigger than your head (exaggerating a little here ;-), pizza is passable (It ain't Uno, but it's yummy), and the -- oz. burger is awesome. Order the Pecan Royale for dessert.
Someone commented that business travelers should stay away, but I would say just the opposite - it's perfect for the frequent guest (I say, speaking as one). The people I would warn away would be younger people seeking some """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""perfect experience"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" like in the movies. This ain't a movie - it's a place to flop your briefcase down, have a drink, watch a little TV and go to sleep. If you want experiences, hey, it's Chicago in every direction out the front door. And say if you're an older couple on a vacation weekend, and you want to do something with it besides sit around and gripe that the plumbing is fiddly, I'd say you'd be pleased too.
I was attracted to the place initially to save the company a buck, but now I stay here because I really and truly like it here. I'll be here until mid-May, and if my company sends me back to Chicago after that, I'll come right back.

We had a terrible experience. We had booked a double - double room, when we checked in, we asked for a cot for our son as the two teenagers sleeping in a double bed had not been successful so far on our trip. We asked if we could get either another room, or get a cot and were told that would be no problem giving us a cot. At -:-- when we got back into the hotel from dinner, there was no cot. Upon calling to see when it was to be delivered we were told that they had run out and they would send blankets up for one of our sons to sleep on the floor. I don't know what happened between the -pm check in and the -:-- phone call - and we never did get a satisfactory answer, even after going past the front desk to the night manager. 
Other than that, the hotel was purely mid road at high end prices. The location was fine, but nothing spectacular. The room was ok, but not exceptional. The pocket door to the bathroom offered very little privacy such that others in the room could hear everything! Everytime the houskeeping staff cleaned the room, they only left two towels, so we were constantly calling the desk to get tow more towels sent up as there were four of us staying in the room.
The Concierge was fantastic - he always had a great suggestion as to a fun place to eat or how to get around. He was the best part of the stay.
We would not stay at a Kimton hotel again, we will go back to Renasainnce or Fairmont where we are always treated well, and they seem to want our return business. Plus we don't have to sleep on the floor.

This hotel is as the name suggests situated in Downtown LA. The location is two blocks from the Blue Line metro station that connects to all lines so is ideal for those wishing to get around by public transport.
It is only a few blocks from the Walt Disney Concert Hall which is superb, in fact the whole artists hill area is worth a visit with time to spend taking in the features.
By day the hotel functions as a professional business hotel but by night it becomes a hip nightspot with the rooftop pool and bar, surrounded by waterbed pods and lounging sofas, attracting a trendy crowd. Excellent choice of drinks and good service.
The rooms are spacious and modern with glass cubicle bathrooms which are entirely open to those sharing the room!
A feel good stay for a city hotel.

This hotel is literally minutes from the Space Needle (I could see it from my balcony) and Pike Place and across the street from Lake Union. It was a great price for practically a downtown hotel. Parking and the shuttle were free, which saved us a lot of money. The morning shuttle driver is friendly, humorous, and very laid back. He provided us with Seattle trivia that was interesting. 
The rooms were comfortable. No problems with the temperature, bed, or water pressure. Rooms were clean (however, they were an environmentally friendly hotel and if I hung up a towel after using it, they replaced it anyway) and the staff was nice and helpful. 
Only a couple of minor complaints. On our second night there, the fire alarm went off at -:-- am. We stood out back, in the cold, waiting for the okay to go back inside and the solitary overwhelmed night clerk was unable to notify us when it was safe. The breakfast was tasty, but the toasters were slow and it was really crowded Monday morning and they ran out of some things.

I really liked how modern the hotel was and the location, but the rooms were small. The bathroom was even worse, cause when you showered everything in the bathroom got wet from the shower steam. 
The restaurant in the hotel was great. The day we were leaving they had complementary alcoholic beverages and non-alcoholic with hors d'oeuvre. Pool was a bit too small. A few people brought their kids to the pool and i felt like they didn't belong amongst the partiers. 
We ordered room service one night and put it on a credit card, but when we checked out it was also on our checkout bill. Double CHARGED!! :(

Have used the Westin several times in the past few years but my last visit was exceptional!! I had booked the stay and fly package and left my vehicle parked at the hotel for eight days. Upon returning from our trip, my vehicle would not start due to the extreme temperatures from the past week. The staff started my car and were so helpful despite the freezing temperatures...Stay here!!!

Check in was easy, and went smoothly. The manager, Susana, was very helpful and kind. Room service was prompt and accurate. The room was beautiful and clean, and the bed was very comfortable. Everything worked well. Front desk staff (a woman on the evening of ----), was rude when I called on one occasion (after being transferred - times and hung up on once), but did eventually get me what I needed.

Stayed for - nights in Feb ---- and got an excellent deal from Booking.com. Good things about the hotel were its central location (on --th between Lex and Park) with -- minute walk to Times Square and -- minute to central shopping area on -th and -th Ave. Breakfast was included at Audrey Cafe in the next door sister property. We had the courtyard king room which was massive for a NYC hotel, however, they could have used some of that space for a larger bathroom which was quite tiny. Staff was courteous but cold i.e. lacked the welcoming warmth. Also they should provide Free Wi-Fi in the room which is a fairly standard in most similar hotel nowadays.
Given its location and convinience and assuming the same price, I'll definitely stay there again.

Our Family of - booked a - night stay here between Christmas and New Year's for the Alamo Bowl game. What a great choice! The location is fantastic, walking distance to everything. - min to the riverwalk,----- min to Alamodome, -- min to the Alamo. The room itself is on the small side but has nicer finishes, large flat screen TV, free WiFi, marble bathroom, comfy triple sheeted beds. I booked a balcony room and we really enjoyed the unobstructed views of La Villita, Tower of the Americas and part of down town. Granted there is a parking lot below but it was still nice. Staff was always friendly and helpful. The breakfast was perfect and the Texas shape belgium waffles were tasty and unique! Overall would reccomend to all.

We stayed at The Salisbury for a week at the beginning of August, and approached the experience with some trepidation - while some reviews were very positive, many deplored the dinginess, etc of the hotel, the inadequacy of the air conditioning and the surliness of the staff. While it is true that the decor of the rooms is a little faded, and the corridors a little musty, the overall experience, for the price, is excellent. The rooms are huge and well appointed, the storage space is immense (one of the closets in our suite could have doubled as an extra room), the cooling, kitchen, ironing etc facilities were absolutely fine and the staff were very pleasant.
The location is, of course excellent, but we can honestly say that there is no need to see this as any kind of compensation for the shortcomings of the hotel. The salisbury isn't a hip boutique along the lines of the Hollywood Rennaisance, or a grandish place like the Wyndham in Boston, both of which we've stayed at, but it gives a great, spacious and reasonably priced base to explorre New York. We will certainly stay there again.

I stayed at this hotel after one day of being at a hotel closer to the heart of Times Square. I am sooo glad we switch to Hotel --. Hotel -- was sold out the first night we stayed in New York. The staff was great, professional, helpful. We had to switch hotels early in the morning because we had to get to a New York Jets game. We thought for sure we would have to store our luggage until we could get in our room, after the game. Much to our surprise they were able to get us into a room, we were so happy. I was also presently surprised to find out they had a free hot breakfast in the morning, bonus. Most things were within walking distance including Times Square. In my opinion a better location than Times Square. Rooms were newer, great beds, good decore, they are small but I have heard that is normal for Manhattan. The first hotel had bigger rooms but it was a dive compared to Hotel --. I'll take the smaller room any day. Bathrooms were spacious. I would definately recommend this hotel to anyone.

My wife and I went to Hotel Palomar for one day and night to celebrate our one-year wedding anniversary. They were able to accommodate an early check-in, and offered a complimentary upgrade to a larger room when we asked if it were possible. We took advantage of the valet as we werent planning on using the car until we left. The hotel is extremely nice looking once you get in the lobby and made us feel comfortable even though we had just stepped off the city streets.
Our room was clean and had lots of extra space. The decor was very creative but not over the top. We planned on being out for the day and the hotel is within a few blocks walk to the metro station and always had cabs out front. There are some small cafes nearby (Starbucks, a crepes place, pizza) and some other dinner places that we didnt get to check out. Seems like if you needed to stay there for a while you would be OK.
We made sure to make it back for the wine reception held every afternoon from ---PM. That was part of the reason we booked. We both thought it would be one glass and thats it, but they had Tony tending to about a dozen bottles of white and red each ready to fill you up. I thought that was fantastic.
During the wine reception we were speaking to one of the hotel reps (sorry I forgot your name) and he heard us say what we were celebrating. Later that night, the hotel had brought a bottle of champagne and a plate of chocolate covered strawberries for us! It was an amazing touch.
The front desk sent up a band-aid and antiseptic wipe fairly quickly when my wife had a small cut open up on her leg. That was helpful and much needed.
Check out was easy and we got our car fine from the valet. No issues whatsoever with the hotel except we wished we could have stayed longer. With great service and the added touch I would definitely consider staying here again on our next trip to DC.

We stayed here because of a Hotwire deal. We ended paying less than half the price that came up when we did an Expedia search for the same weekend, so it was a good deal. 
The hotel is very clean and pleasant. The service was good. I asked for a complimentary upgrade since we were there for a birthday, and they were able to accommodate this and we got a king size bed. Our room was simple, but clean and comfortable. The decor was very traditional, and it was nice and pleasant but nothing particularly memorable and seemed a bit dated. The bathroom was similarly basic and a bit dated, but very serviceable. We felt the location of the hotel wasn't as convenient for our needs as we would have liked, but that was our own issue. We booked a lot of broadway shows, and we often stay very close to Times Square or very close to Rockefeller centre, so usually our hotel is literally a block or two away from the theatres. In this case it was a slightly farther walk, but still close enough to walk. Other than the hotel's own restaurant, which we didn't try, there isn't very much directly around this hotel so there aren't crowds or bustle, which is nice if you like to get away from it all when you return to your hotel. A big plus for this location was that it was completely quiet when you wanted to sleep. All in all, a very pleasant stay.

I spent - nights here in Denver with my wife and kids aged - and - before heading to a conference in the Rockies. The hotel is easy and quick to get to from the airport and has ample parking. Its just off the freeway and the location is functional not beautiful - not a problem for us. Breakfast is plentiful - the room its served in is a bit small and on one morning it was chaos as half the hotel descended at the same time. The staff were very friendly and helpful though at all times and our room was clean and spacious with free wifi. In the evenings from -.---- you get free food and drink - not exactly imaginative fare but it would fill you up if need be. There's also free soft drinks at night and free popcorn - our kids loved both! There are plenty of restaurants nearby though, especially if like us you have a car and a GPS. We found it easy enough to commute to sights in Denver such as the zoo and natural sciences museum (both higjly recommended). The pool is quite small - half indoor and half outdoor and there's a spa bath too.
All in all fantastic value for the price we paid and we would stay here again no question.

EXCEPTIONAL SERVICE!

Besides those two items, stay and accommodations were top notch!
~Houston, Texas traveler

Central location, easy access to sites by walking or to buses-streetcars. Room was small but extremely clean and bed comfortable. Join the Kimpton rewards for free wifi, found out about it from literature in room not from staff at front desk. Booked the hotel through Hotwire but I found it expensive but San Francisco hotels are quite pricey.
Exceptional Mexican restaurant just up the street on Geary by the name of Colibri.
Also ate at the Grand Cafe corner of Taylor and Geary- excellent meal- try the kale salad.
Arrived on a late flight our first night so ate at Jaspers (hotel restauranat-bar)- friendly staff and bar food was good too.
We were in a room beside the elevator but it was very quiet b-c no other room beside us.
All the car rental places are just down the street on O'Farrell.
Lots of panhandlers-homeless people in area but felt completely safe and had no issues whatsoever.
Would stay here again.

We arrived after a long bus journey on Saturday night so were looking forward to getting into bed. On the front door there was a sign to say 'no more check ins' but we ignored this as we had a reservation. When we got to the desk the rude man said he couldnt check us in and hadnt we seen the signs?! We explained we had a reservation and had already paid for -nights online. If ONLY we had read the reviews before booking!! They are all true!!!! Worst hotel EVER!!! Cant believe its still open! Someone needs to shut the place down!! Sleeping in the hotel lobby was actually nicer than the room!!!!

Although the rooms here are extremely large they are a bit tired. However we were very glad to have some room to move around so the size of the room was a big asset. We liked the faded grandeur atmosphere overall, but we really found the breakfast room to be gloomy. The location is perfect and we happy to ride the cable car up and down those steep hills.

We stayed at the Westin in San Diego while in town visiting family over Thanksgiving weekend. We had an amazing stay. The hotel staff are wonderful: from the check-in staff member to the bartender, everyone was efficient and friendly. Our room was clean and up to date, and the view was amazing. The hotel is centrally-located; we walked to Horton Plaza nearby, and parked in the garage across the street from the hotel. I would highly recommend the Westin, and would stay here for business as well as personal trips. Very nice!

My husband and I went to Seattle for an anniversary long-weekend. I chose this hotel because I had airmiles gift cards for Best Western to use and the hotel was close to the Amtrak train station (less than $- taxi fare). 
It turned out to be a perfect choice. We were welcomed with a celebratory bottle of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""champagne"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for our anniversary, and two bottles of water and cookies after having signed up for Best Western Rewards. I asked for a quiet room and we were given a king sized room that overlooked the inside roof. No view, but very quiet and a lovely spacious room and nice bathroom. The bathtub was a small square with a bit of a seat in it. Good for showering (with the waterpik shower head), but not for taking a bath. The Neutrogena bath products were very nice (and they even had make up remover cloths).
Nice large flat screen tv, but we felt the bed was a little bit firmer than we would have liked (and my husband prefers firm beds). After the first night we asked if they had thinner pillows and were given new pillows and had a better sleep. But, oddly, housekeeping replaced them with the thicker puffy ones the third night and by the time we realised it was too late to call front desk (we were already in pajamas and sleepy and ready for bed). So the only downside was we didn't sleep very well for a couple of nights.
Complementary breakfast was lovely in a separate room with tables covered with tablecloths. Lots of good, individually boxed Kellog cereals, fresh fruit, yogurt, bagels, cream cheese, bread to make toast, and delicious make-your-own waffles (complete with strawberries and whipped cream!). The only downer was the doughy egg, cheese and bacon pockets.
The location is fantastic. Walking distance to several key sightseeing spots, lots of restaurants and pubs, and there is free transit within the downtown area. 
The front desk staff are really friendly and very helpful. We would not hesistate to stay here again!

The location was brilliant – - min walk to Hollywood Blvd & Highland Center http:--www.hollywoodandhighland.com- which includes the famous Grauman's Chinese Theatre, Kodak Theatre and plenty of places to eat and shop.. Of course it was also on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.
Metro station - min away for a quick trip to downtown LA or to Universal studios.
Rooms are well decked out. We had a family room which had a separate bedroom. Walls were a bit thin but not a big deal. Reasonable continental breakfast included but the location of this place is what stands out. The staff were very friendly and overall the experience was fantastic. This place is great value for money.

Stayed two nites at the Donatello and could have spent a week there.Just a short block away from public transport,union square,shopping and many restaurants.Many homeless and beggars on the street but felt very safe walking round,even at night.Hotel very comfortable with kitchenette,small lounge,very comfortable king bed and also large TV inbuilt in the bathroom mirror.Overall clean rooms and very friendly staff and next time in San Francisco will stay at the Donatello.

The rooms are MARGINAL at best. The bathroom is plain and has zero imagination. On Sunday the shower ran out of hot water. Someone must explain to me how a hotel runs out of hot water. The soaps, shampoos and towels are on par with any Holiday Inn Select. The entire reason for writing this post is to convey to future guests that even their large rooms are too small. I cannot image what the smaller rooms are like if our ---+ square foot room was this small. (note: ---+ sq ft my backside!) There was one dresser with three tiny drawers and a night stand that held a clock and barley the phone. 
The other item someone needs to explain to me is how housekeeping NEVER changed our drinking glasses. I can understand one night, but not multiple nights. If the glasses were not cleaned, what other short cuts are they taking? 
The lobby does not have any chairs and the chairs that are available are located within the lobby bar area. I don’t know about most guests, but I will not sit in a bar if I am not a paying customer of the bar. Additionally, we were surprised that the lobby barely changed its flowers to reflect it was Easter (or the height of Cherry Blossom Season). 
Very few amenities. (no spa, pool or lobby gift shop)

Had a great stay at The Nolitan. Their staff was great, very accommodating. Although we weren't traveling with pets, it's nice to know that the hotel is so pet-friendly. The Nolitan's great location and design touches made big impressions.

Bottom line first - Solid hotel, great location on a great looking NYC street, smaller size rooms & bathrooms. Would recommend for someone who hasn't stayed here before, but would probably stay somewhere else on my next trip.
Recently stayed at The Mainsfield for a holiday weekend in NYC. Location is the biggest selling point of this hotel being only very short walks to Grand Central, Bryant Park and Times Square.

Having been restored from it's rich history, the hotel's size is dictated by the original rooms and layouts. It is smaller than most hotels in both lobby and rooms, but and effort has been made to preserve some of the charm of the original.

This place is very nice! Everything about it is classy, for the price you really can't beat it. We will stay again!

Stayed only one night for a wedding, so didn't really get a chance to see what was around the area. There did look to be some restaurants within walking distance though. As I said before, this hotel is pet friendly with a refundable deposit and a nightly fee. They also do have onsite coin operated washers and dryers should you need to do some laundry.

The hotel room was okay. It wasn't great nor was it horrible. The strangeness of this hotel was the interior. Unfortunately, I wouldn't choose this hotel again. It isn't bad for the cost, but again, the inside is just too weird.

fab location, friendly staff, beautifully clean rooms and very good value. visited with - friends for a NYC reunion & shopfest. quirky rooms with hollywood themes, not huge but bigger than the Hudson!. generous extras such as free wifi, printers & computer access, cookies & drinks available all day and breakfast until --am. charlie the cat likes cuddles! This Westin is brand new with clean, modern rooms, comfy beds and other typical Westin amenities. Wow, we really enjoyed this hotel. After reading some of the negative reviews we were really concerned. The hotel is beautiful; listed in the National Register of Historic Hotels. This hotel is located very conveniently in downtown Chicago. Staff at front desk were also very helpful. But the bed was as hard as a rock and they are stingy with towels. Shower head was awful. No pay-per-view movies available.

Great hotel - older style - clean, comfortable and welcoming. Excellent location for all sight seeing and transport needs. I had been there with my colleague last year, the staff is nice and warm hearted, he replaced a larger room for us free of charge. There is a big yard, a lot of parking lots, very beautiful place to stay.

Was not very sure of staying in this hotel after my excellent stays in Algonquinn , Paramount and Omni Berkshire Hotels in NYC. I stayed in this hotel last May for - days. We booked a suite since I was traveling with a toddler. We requested a crib with our reservation. Very nice hotel me and my husband always stay there. Super close to sea world. An my husband loves there continental breakfast, because you can make your own waffles haha!! Definitely would stay again.

Staff excellent from the doorman to the concierge guy.
I wont get into detail just back up all the other reviews really.
The rooms in this hotel are very small - there's almost no place to walk around the bed. Location on -rd avenue is also problematic as the windows are not noise proof

We were working at a wedding, only about -- minutes from our home, but knew we'd be finishing quite late. So, as we've done before, we decided to book a hotel so we could just relax and specifically booked a hotel with a hot tub so we unwind on Memorial Day.

At this point, we decided we had to ask for at least a partial refund, which we have never done. wow! a big 'thank you' to mr. Rob DelliBovi, director of sales of the hotel, and the rest of the staff. the hotel is fantastic, from the design point of view. our room was located on --th floor: a wonderful suite with an incredible view over empire state building, chrysler building and many other famous skyscreapers. to take the shower was an experience itself (try and you will understand!). very lively area scattered with nice small restaurants.we will be back for sure...

We stayed at The Dana during our honeymoon. When you first arrive on the property, it doesn't seem like a three star hotel. The rooms are small, but very clean. The bathroom is huge, though. After the first night I had a chance to walk behind the property and see the marina rooms, which are more. The view is beautiful. Very blue water and hills in the distance. Looked like a post card. The two restaurants have wonderful food. I actually like the Blue Pearl better. It is more casual and the choice of food is better. The people working there could not be nicer. The front desk will tell you how to get to each place you want to go in the city and they have worked out deals with the Zoo and other destinations for a flat rate if you are taking a cab. The Dana is across the street from Sea World. It is a nice walk. We've decided to go back every year on our anniversary because the staff and the people make you feel like you're a part of the family.

Central location if you want to be in the middle of it all. International guests, so feels different - not too American. Super delicious coffee-capuccino in the very attractive bar. Modern, comfortable rooms with good bedding. Restaurant way overpriced for breakfast but delish as a special treat. We've been three times and had connecting rooms with our three kids - you cannot find a better overall in midtown.

We stayed in this hotel after arriving in Boston on a flight from London.
From the reviews I think I was probably expecting too much, and we were a little disappointed. I would rate the hotel as average - good, but went with average as the service was very slow and the hotel was looking quite tired.
Location was good however, and the rooms were clean so we would probably stay here again if the rate was good.

Caveat - we stayed on points so I can't comment on price-value, particularly since it was a December weekend visit. We were on the --th floor, overlooking Times Square. While I much prefer staying closer to the Park, the views were amazing for our - year old son! He loved watching the screens. The room was up to date, very clean, and really large by NYC standards. I recently stayed at the Doubletree in Chelsea, and the room at the Suites in Times Square was easily - times the size. The living room had a queen-sized pull out sofa bed, plus a mini bar area with a small fridge and microwave. The bathroom was big with lots of vanity space, which was nice. Main bedroom had plenty of space. Note that the mattress was quite soft, which didn't bother me, but might be an issue for some. 
Even overlooking Times Square, the noise wasn't too bad. You could hear the occasional siren, but it wasn't loud enough to wake you up. 
Only two negatives: everyone was exhausted after a great, but long day so we opted to eat at the hotel restaurant on evening. The food was fine (about what you'd expect), but the service was lacking. They just weren't staffed nearly well enough for a weekend evening. Our server was very nice and apologetic, but the management should review the staffing needs at peak times. Also, probably like most places in NYC, check-out time was a zoo. Do not plan to check your bags with the front desk unless you have to, and then I'd recommend checking them as early as possible in the day. Fortunately, we were heading to the train station by noon so it wasn't an issue for us, but the line in the lobby to check bags was insane!
All in all, a great room for a family who relished having the extra space in Manhattan. Would recommend!
Stayed there for - nights. Very nice and modern rooms, friendly service and good location.

After reading some of the reviews on Tripadvisor I was really worried I had booked a mistake. However, I was pleasantly surprised by my stay at the Allerton. 
Like other people who have left reviews, we were upgraded to a larger room upon arrival. You get the choice of a double bed with views, or a queen without views. As we were just there for - nights, I chose the queen and I would recommend anyone travelling with a partner to do the same, as a double would be way too small. 
The room itself was still cozy, but it was clean and comfortable. Nothing spectacular, but no real complaints other than it would be nice to have coffee in the room. 
The hotel is in a great location which really can't be beat. It's walking distance to Millennium Park and lots of great food and shops. I recommend renting bikes and riding along the path by the lake. 
For the price and location, I would certainly stay here again.

I stayed in the Chancellor for four nights in September. I really cannot say anything negative about my stay. The location was great, I was able to get to anywhere I wanted in the city with ease through public transportation or walking. The staff was friendly and it was a great value. My room was clean and comfortable, larger then what I thought it would be. If I visit the city again, I would stay at this hotel as well as recommend it to friends and family.

This is a good value hotel for the location. It is about ---m from the top end of Time Square where you find Hersheys and M&M stores. You absolutely cannotfault the location of the hotel. The only one down side this has to the hotel is noise, car horns and sirens go on at all hours through the main streets of New York. I wouldn't say it's something to put you off the hotel though as you'll probably find this with most. I would however request a room on a high floor. The hotel and rooms are of a good size for New York and were cleaned well. The rooms are not quite as bright as they look in the pictures but nice all the same.
The hotel offers free wifi which I'll be honest was my only real let down of this property. It was a big selling point for us but it was really not very good at all. The service was intermittent and we were lucky to get it working once a day. Or one of us could get it and the other couldn't. (you definitely cannot rely on it). Spent the weekend in Philadelphia for my wedding. Stayed in the VIP suite on the --nd floor and had about -- wedding guests from out of town staying at the hotel. Great stay!
First, I have very realistic views when staying at lodging properties. I travel quite a bit on business and pleasure. I am surprised there are so many negative reviews for this property after my recent stay. 
I would certainly stay here again. And, many of our wedding guests made it a point to mention to me that the hotel was a great choice for our “host” wedding hotel. I can stop there, however some specifics….
LOCATION – Some reviews complain about the location. I have no idea what these guests are talking about. Within minutes, you can walk to Old City and the Constitution Center. Personally, I thought the location was awesome, and if you needed to get beyond walking distance, it seemed that you were within a $-- cab ride from the entire city of Philadelphia.
PARKING – Yes it is expensive, but what do you expect??? You are parking in a covered, attached garage in one of the nicest areas of Philadelphia. Parking in any major metropolitan area is going to cost you, especially if it is gated and covered. If you aren’t happy with the daily parking fee, park on the street and see how well you sleep that night…..
SERVICE – I travel a lot for business and have the opportunity to stay in some pretty decent hotels from time to time. The service here was pretty decent. Prepare to tip, but the staff earns it. The Bellhop staff was especially helpful and courteous from the minute I pulled up. Again they are working for tips, but I thought they were very friendly. 
ROOMS – Clean and well appointed. Again I stayed in the VIP suite, and everything was obviously wonderful on the --nd floor. Beyond that, I heard nothing but positive comments from our wedding guests.
VIEW – Unbelievable! Try to get one of the upper floors if possible. Either way, you are pretty much guaranteed a great view no matter what room you get.
FOOD & BEVERAGE – The only meal I had at the hotel was breakfast the following morning with my family. It was very good. Perhaps a little pricy, but you have to remember you are having a meal within the hotel property and you have to expect to pay for this convenience. The breakfast was served hot and tasty and the service was decent as well.
ELEVATORS TO THE PARKING GARAGE – I think that it is funny that some reviewers are complaining that you have to take up to three elevators to get to the parking garage. Give me a break. Is it going to kill you that you have to walk an extra - minutes and take an additional elevator ride to get to your car, in a parking garage, attached to the rear of a major hotel property? As I stated earlier, if you are worried about elevators, you are focusing on the wrong things.
In the end, I would stay here again. It is a modern, business class hotel that will satisfy most every guests. The location is great, the service is friendly and the views are incredible.

 print outs for directions.

 The prospects for the hotel becoming a real Kimpton appear quite limited. The lobby would have to be completely done over and made to feel more spacious and inviting. The rooms are so small that the possibilities for improvement are limited.
