Not this time. 
But there is always pluses and I like to point them out.......the proximity to Union Square is ideal!
Many great restaurants within a short walking distance from the hotel. The executive room is very roomy for such an older hotel in a city and was well appreciated! The large full mirror on the outside of the bathroom door was great! Flat screen TV, so that was also a plus but we dont usually watch too much tv outside of the weather and a quick news report in the early am.
Most of the reviews here have been excellent and I am sorry that I was not one of those also. Things just didnt turn out as they should and the types of problems we had could of easily have been avoided in where the other problems would not have been magnified as it normally is when you are away. I truly believe that if a problem is resolved, we can all move along happily and I gave enough chances for this to be taken care of for - days with nothing in return.

The Crockett hotel was exactly what I was expecting. An average room for an average price. The room was clean, well made up and quite spacious for having two doubles. You didn't have to do the 'side shuffle' to get between the bed and the TV-dresser. The bathroom was actually huge. Shower decent with plenty of towels and the usual complementary soaps. The complementary breakfast was the usual fare. Pastries, bagels, scrambled eggs. and waffle makers. The food was good and sure makes it nice to get going in the morning without an extra stop. OK a couple of negatives. Firstly the a-c seemed unusually loud when it starts up. Maybe it was just my room? Also as usual, avoid the room across from the ice machine. It was running all night. So the two basic negs are pretty standard for all hotels. The location is great if you have anything to do in the DT San Antonio area. Walking distance to most and the area has what looks to be an excellent colour coded streetcar system. We were attending a convention at the convention center and it was close to that. The River Walk was great. Saturday night was busy full of action and lots of fun. I recommend """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The County Line"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in the river walk for real good BBQ dinner. Overall worth the price for a good, clean nice room with a good location.

I travel regularly and this hotel was one of the best I have stayed at. The location is great, plenty if things to do. The rooms are clean and cozy. The employees were very friendly and informative. With upcoming renovations I believe this will be the best hotel in the charlotte area.

We feel that The Dana is one of the best kept secrets on Mission Bay. My husband and I have been annual guests for the past -- plus years. Each year we have seen an expansion, improvement or both. It has been fun to watch them grow and we're excited to see what's in the future. They offer room rates to fit everyone's budget and all of the rooms we stayed in were immaculate and well maintained. We love it there. As for tips-Visit the little bait house on the marina for a fresh sandwich or go across the street to a little brown seafood restaurant. Ask where the Wave House is located (close by). It's located by the beach and has excellent breakfasts at reasonable prices. (Mission Beach is a - minute drive away)

A great location for airport access. Clean, comfortable hotel. Staff was very hospitable. Breakfast was very nice. Easy to find and good on-time reliable airport shuttle. 
The air conditioner cycled often and the room temp was hard to control. Well laid out king room included a refrigerator, sofa and good desk chair.

I booked a room last minute for a place to sleep after a long drive. I read the reviews and some were great and some were bad but decided to give it a try since it was just off the highway. Well..... the check in process was quick and the guy at the reception desk was very friendly. After a long drive, all we wanted to do was to get a good night sleep and boy! their beds are so comfortable we slept like a baby. We were going to leave to go grab breakfast somewhere until I took a peek at their breakfast buffet. They had scrambled eggs, bacon and sausage etc. everything you can get at an IHOP but better!. We saved -- bucks! The room was clean and smelled fresh. I will definately stay here again!

I booked the Sofitel on the strength of the Tripadvisor reviews. I have worked in and visited Manhattan as a tourist for -- years and this is the best stay I have in terms of value for the standard of accomodation, service and quality of the experience.
I stayed for - days and two nights, used the restaurant and the fitness centre and again both were well above the average. The broadband Internet service was fast and inexpensive. My first choice in New York from now on.
Im so pleased with the Tripadvisor recommendation that I have signed up.

I have just come back from San Francisco. I stayed at the Adante hotel for -- nights with my girlfriend and we don't have a single complaint about it. The hotel is clean, the rooms are cleaned everyday. The staff are friendly and helpful. Our toilet got blocked while we were there and we informed the front desk of this as we were leaving for a bite to eat. When we returned to our room the problem had been resolved. The hotel is is at the start of part of town called The tenderloin which has a lot of homeless people walking around. Although it could get a little bothersome being asked for change every - minutes walking around the area back to the hotel, not once did i have a problem with those people. They just ask and you walk on by. So i felt pretty safe there and didn't feel threatened at any time. I have read other reviews before i went where people have said the rooms smelled and what not. This is not my experience at all. Others said the decor of the rooms was bad. Well, why don't they stay at the Hilton then.
I don't know anyone who goes on holiday to stay in their hotel room. I went to see San Francisco, not - walls of a room. If you want to see the city, the Adante is great.

I was so lucky to find this place. I wanted to stay close to the Riverwalk. I had never been to San Antonio but heard the Riverwalk was a great place to go. The hotel was a mile or so away. You can either take a taxi ride (less then $- one way) or walk (-- min walk). 
The hotel was an excellent find. I named my own price on Priceline and this was the hotel that took my $-- a night offer. The hotel had a kitchen with full fridge and stove. Flat screen television. It was an excellent hote. The staff was very helpfull with all my questions. I did hear the train on Saturday morning around - am but did not mind. It was a one time wisel and I was already expecting it because there were ear plugs next to my bed. 
The continental breakfast was awesome. The pool is kind of small and there is no hot tub. It was so hot that weekend that a dip in the pool felt excellent. 
I would definelty stay in this hotel again. I thought it was an excellent find for the price I got.

This Intercontinental is less than a year old, and is what you'd expect in a new, five-star hotel in a major city. It does have a range of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""modern hotel problems"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", however.
I was upgraded to a nice, high-floor corner room due to my Ambassador Club status. Hotel was pretty empty, despite a major convention at Moscone Center (a block away). Rooms are tastefully appointed, clean and comfortable. A-C system is particularly good, very quiet. 
However, when I first checked in, I was warned that a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""maintenance issue"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" would require the hotel electricity to be turned off for an hour that afternoon. Fair enough. But during the late night hours, while I was working (phone and internet), the power again went out along with all communications - AND THE ELEVATORS. No warning at all. This pattern of electrical service continued for the next day as well. Apparently still-unresolved construction issues. The phones go down because of a too-small UPS system specified. 
My other """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""modern hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" pet peeve is the showers. Part of luxury hotel life is a good, powerful hot shower. Instead this hotel has barely enough water pressure to get wet. If this is due to some kind of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""green initiative"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", I object. If this is just due to bad water-saving shower heads, it should be fixed. 
Midline management was dismissive of the concerns I raised. I was able to finally raise the hotel manager with a call to IC head office about the electrical-communication issues. Management shouldn't be hiding from the customers.
One other note for potential visitors - much of SFO including the area adjacent to this hotel has become extremely street unsafe, even during the daytime. Factor in cab fares if you're planning on doing sightseeing.

A big thank you to the staff at the Hyatt Regency Century Plaza. We were visiting Hollywood to for my daughter's --th birthday. A snafu in booking with one of the online services, put us farther from where we wanted to stay. Erika Garcia-Lavyne was more than gracious to make our stay worthwhile. The rest of the staff was friendly, curtious and quick to help or answer a question. Only negative - ouch on the parking. Looks like my daughter is going to a State College.

I stayed here because my firm held an event in the conference facilities. The rooms were nice, but the service left a lot to be desired. The parking was the worst -- if the hotel manager reads this, here is my advice: get a new provider, this """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""service"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is ruining your reputation. They were disorganized. (gave me the wrong color ticket, then asked me why I had the wrong color. I am supposed to know...how?) They were abrupt. Their credit card machine was not working so they demanded cash. They charged more for hotel guests than non-guest conference attendees. Also, on the conference, the hotel nickel and dimed us to death, charging extra for every little thing. No internet access in the conference room. We rented a printer and projector -- a terrible mistake, as it cost about - times what it would be to actually buy them -- but apparently you are locked in to renting and paying for their setup technicians. I have stayed at other Intercontinentals and this one is pretty low on the list. I give this a three only for the rooms and for the conference food, which was good.

The location is handy, but be fair warned locating the lobby is awkward. You will not find much on the street level to indicate that you have a hotel nearby. The glass door has the Hilton Logo, the awning as well, but not much else. Having said that, once we found the place, it was a perfect spot for our trip.

We stayed in the Hilton for - days over the Easter Period and had high expectations after a stay here last year. We were certainly not disappointed and it was like returning to an old friend. The location is superb, and the free shuttle to Universal is a real life (leg) saver. Room was immaculate day in and day out with great attention to detail by the maid. The beds are just the best, so comfy its a real shock coming back home. Pool was great, never over crowded, always seating and loads of towels available. Try and stay in the executive floors as the breakfast sets you up nicely for the day. We booked early and paid in advance, in our opinion was worth every penny. Would definitely use this hotel again.

We stayed at the hotel sept - -, ----. The rooms were magnificent, the staff was so friendly and we certainly stay there again and again when we come to Seattle. The restaurant at the hotel is exceptional and I highly recommend the Thai french toast. YUM!

The hotel is simple, but very confortable, clean and tranquil. The breakfast is varied and the prices are very cheap: U$--.-- daily. The localization is excellent for purchase. He's close of the Best Buy, Macy's, Target, Krog's, DSW, Marshal""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""s, Walgreens ,and Starbuck's. 
Great!

We stayed her with my in-laws. It was recommended by their friend. maybe it's in an up and coming neighborhood, but I just thought it was sketchy and not a place I wanted to hang. There were a lot of aggressive homeless, graffiti and run down buildings. Not the best location for us, we were always leaving the neighborhood to enjoy the city. The - elevators were slow. Unfortunately, it was pretty warm when we were there so it got very uncomfortable in the room. The windows don't have screens, the ceiling fans weren't enough and the air conditioning unit was way too loud. The staff was extremely helpful but kind of snobby. We didn't eat in the restaurant but had drinks at the bar, which was nice but again snobby...

Stayed at this Ramada to attend graduation at Lackland AFB. This Ramada is very convenient to the base and not far from downtown. We got a great discount for staying - nights (--% off!). I was worried about the condition we might find becasue of some of the reviews here, but I am very pleased to say this hotel is in great shape. 
The lobby is very nice, very clean, nicely decorated, and Tony was very sweet and helpful and found my reservation in seconds and I was checked in very quickly. 
Our room was spotless and smelled good. Ramada is in the process of putting new furniture in all the rooms and ours had been replaced already with a very nice round table and chairs, new dresser, work table, and bedside tables. The bathroom was very clean and hot water was quick and plentiful. The shower also had a very nice massaging shower head which was great for my sore back. The bed was very comfortable and the carpet was very clean. I walked around in my socks and they were not a bit dirty. 
All of the lamps and outlets worked, the TV worked and we had a fridge and microwave, which was very nice. I also used the small room safe and that was nice to have.
The service was very good, we had plenty of towels everyday and the toiletries we used were replaced. The first night, our AC started making a noise so we turned it off and the next morning I reported it. When we returned that afternoon, it had been fixed and we had no more problems. It kept the room really cool and never had that musty smell that some do. 
The breakfast area was very clean and I even talked to the hotel manager one morning who was in there overseeing the breakfast. He was very nice and asked if we needed anything. He also had comment cards in the rooms and posted in the lobby that openly asked for opinions and feedback and provided contact numbers for himself. That is a first for me as you hardly ever know who's in charge in other places and never see or are able to contact them. This is a man who knows how to provide customer service and get return business!
Our toilet backed up the last night and unfortunately, they could not find a plunger. They offered for us to change rooms, but I was very tired and just didn't want to move all my stuff, so they offered us a room key to use the bathroom in another room, but I didn't want to do that either. So, I drove - minutes to WalMart and bought a plunger and had my toilet cleared in a few minutes. I was pleased that they discounted my room for that night even though I didn't take them up on another room. 
We ordered Chinese delivery from Sun Sun (menu in the room). They deliver to your room and it was delicious and convenient after a long day at Lackland. 
I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again and would recommend this Ramada to anyone looking for convenience, cleanliness, and an affordable stay.

I will define the stay at """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Homely"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" since it is a non-formal hotel with basic services in place. The rooms are spacious with full kitchen. 
What makes this hotel my favourite is the location. This is situated along side the river. On a sunny day, people having jog, families with cycle-rickshaws and pedal boats, with ducks floating in the water make it a very soothing and lively scence
Flip side - not all the staff memebers of the hotel are cooperative and sensitive theier patrons but good part is you have a very good ear in the form of its General Manager (Vicki) and she is all there to help whatever best way can be done
Proximity to the downtown shopping area, Lucas stadium, Childern's museum and the Zoo (in fact we walked to the zoo from the hotel, along the canal) makes it better to stay

I came to NYC for four nights and did not want to spend the fortune that most hotels cost here. The Morningside Inn is a part hostel-part hotel. I requested the Double Deluxe Room and it was really nice for what we paid for it, very affordable. Our room was behind the office right as you enter the building, which was odd, but the room had two double comfortable beds and a fairly spacious bathroom. The window air conditioner works great and kept the room very cool at all times. Also has two dressers and a closet for clothes, plus a mounted tv in the corner of the room. The only problem I had was that the shower water was luke warm at BEST and the shower leaked very slowly onto the carpet right in front of the bathroom.
I never saw anything in the hotel besides the entryway, front desk, and our room. 
This hotel is a bit north of the heart of NYC (it is located on ---th and Broadway), but that doesn't matter at all. The subway at ---rd and Broadway is easily accessible and can take you anywhere! There are great restaurants, shops, flower stands, etc. nearby everywhere!
I would definitely recommend this hotel for people who are trying to save money to spend elsewhere in NYC!

I recently stayed at a crowne plaza in center city on business. My room very, very, small, paid way too much money. Staff very friendly, Concierge gave great suggestions for dinner and breakfast. Check in and out very fast. Front office manager seemed kind of dense.

We stayed at this Homewood for one night in February and again over the Fourth of July weekend. Great stay. Decent breakfast although the last morning we decided to walk across the parking lot to the Cracker Barrel. We've stayed at all three Homewood's in Indianapolis on different occasions and all are nice. What I like about this one is it's location and ease of getting to and from the highway. And they have a better rate which is always a plus!

Embassy Suites is a great place to stay for families! Our daughter slept on the pull out bed in the front room and we had the king bed to ourselves in the back room. We appreciated the fridge and everything was very clean. Check in was easy and all the hotel employees were very friendly and courteous. 
Breakfast is a mixed bag. While I definitely appreciated the convenience and it is one of the reasons I chose Embassy Suites, I found the quality to be somewhat lacking. All the cereals were high in sugar. Cherrios was not an option which was sad because I think almost ALL kids love Cherrios. The yogurts were also high in sugar and had aspartame in them. A plain greek yogurt would have been nice. And be sure to get downstairs before -:-- a.m. My poor husband waited -- minutes for an omelet while I was trying to entertain a two year old. 
Parking though is outrageous at $-- a night and is your ONLY option. And of course you feel obligated to tip too! 
I still recommend it for families because of the suite experience.

Both the outside and inside of the hotel requires a facelift. Some of the furnishings were old and the lifts were slow. The rooms were also somewhat old but they were spacious and the beds were comfortable. The air-conditioning unit was loud but it did its job. There were various soaps and moisturisers on offer but there was no coffee or tea facilities. Neither was there a kettle or refrigerator in the room, which would have been useful. However, a fairly large safe was provided. Internet was also not complimentary and this was inconvenient. 
Check-in was efficient and the lobby was of an ample size. The location is conveniently located approximately -- minutes walk from Times Square. It is also of a walkable distance to other main attractions such as -th Avenue, the Rockefeller Centre and the Empire State Building. 
Breakfast was average. The restaurant service was good but the variety of food was quite poor - only cereal, eggs, bacon, sausages, pancakes and muffins - but after considering the price of the buffet ($--.--), it was good value for money.
Overall, it is a quite a nice hotel, albeit old. It is good value for money but it is fairly basic. I recommend it.

The first thing you notice is that the hotel is very anonymous. Which makes it difficult to notice. Perhaps that was due to scaffolding or something else but you need to keep your wits about you until you get your bearings. Entrance hall, great. Good reception area (with wifi) and excellent service from the receptionists. We were booked into a second floor room which proved (eventually) an ideal choice as we were there just after Hurricane Sandy and didn't have to worry about elevators (see other reviews). Didn't like the room at first as it had no views and was pretty hard to get our heads round the design - even though we had prepared ourselves for it after reading reviews here. Asked for a couple of alternative rooms but the place was very busy and we could either have a shoebox or something on the --th(?) floor. Decided to keep the one we had. Nothing was too much trouble helping us decide.
Ok, as my wife told me on numerous occasions, the room could only have been designed by a MAN. Have to agree. (Except a man would have at least put the TV in the right place (see pics) - it was off centre and really annoying.) See the pic showing the room location for an idea of the overall design. Windows? Forget it, these were pretty much for show as we didn't particularly like looking up or down on others and at the back of another building. Keep those blinds closed - besides, they keep the heat in. Necessary when some idiot designed the A-C outlet to be right above the end of the bed you lay your head. What I mean by this is that unless the A-C is ON a small flow of cold air continually dribbles out and drops straight on to you. Nice in the summer maybe but not in winter. You can't have the A-C on all the time either as it's too noisy.
Moving on - BRING coathangers or better still a coat rail.- there are only two stupidly small pegs on the wall as you enter to hang stuff on. The idea is you live out of a suitcase but it just doesn't work if you intend staying more than a day. This aspect could be easily improved. 
The bathroom area is special. You REALLY have to know who you're living with as there is absolutely no privacy - or soundproofing. No """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""first time together"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" holidays here - seriously. Glass sliding doors with big gaps??? Nah. No use. That will be a redesign sometime soon I bet. The sink was diabolical, there was not enough shelving to put toiletries on - a common hotel fault to be fair - and the toilet itself was designed for people with diminished stature (no offence intended). The drench shower was great, except when the electricity went out (thanks Sandy). And it leaked - no surprise there with the glasswork.
THE GOOD STUFF! - Love the Bar, the attention and the ambiance. The staff in general. Love the rooftop area - see photo taken from the Empire State Building(!) but they had closed the bar for the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""season"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" - what is that about? What the heck is a season when the place is open for business???.
The location is just about perfect to get to anywhere, we walked New York. Plenty of bars, food and tourist stuff nearby. Highly recommend Docks Restaurant - reviewed with other stuff elsewhere.
Summary - if you can put up with the strangeness of it all and are looking for a reasonably priced, clean and fairly new hotel then go for it. You probably won't last long but that's not the deal in NYC. 
(Stayed -- Nov to -- Nov ----.)

I recently stayed at the Embassy Suites with a co-worker to attend a conference at the Hilton Bayfront. The room was just right for us - spacious bathroom, plus two other sinks and plenty of counter space. We barely used the living room but it was nice to have. The beds and pillows were very comfortable. Our room was on the -th floor with a city view, and was quiet. Breakfast was a hit - plenty of hot and cold choices.
Location is excellent - right next to shops and restaurants at Seaport Village, and a very pleasant -- min. water front stroll to our conference hotel. Taxis were waiting right outside the hotel for longer trips.
Check in was friendly and efficient. We had asked for the room charges to be split between two credit cards and this was no problem. On the morning we left, we each got a receipt under the door for exactly half the charges, and we didn't need to check out in person.
I cant think of any negative things to report, so definitely a thumbs up for this hotel.

We searched high and low and found this place to be a standout in Manhattan value. Our standards weren't that high in just wanting a hotel for under $--- per night that did not have bedbugs and had our own bathroom. We found this at Newton! The added bonus was the convenient subway stop (right at --th street which was also serviced by express trains and as a late night stop on the red line) just a second away. We felt safe getting back and forth. The other plus was an in room air conditioner and microwave. Also, I forgot $--- in my drawer one day and the cleaning staff were trustworthy (I can't say as much for another much more expensive hotel midtown who stole a picture frame from my room) as when I returned, it was still there. 
There is shopping and convenient diners nearby, plus a starbucks on each side of the street as well as Tim Horton's, McDonalds, etc and much more little places on the periphery. Two bodega's where you can buy beer - etc and a drug store practically downstairs. 
The only downfall is the older elevator which broke twice when we were there and the -th floor was a long walk. However, they were prompt in getting it back in service.
The major plus was the convenience, bathroom and cleanliness. I'll stay there every time I return based on those three points. The most important being clean...just because you are on a budget, there is no reason anyone should have to deal with bugs of any sort...and the Newton definitely takes cleanliness as a high priority. 
The room was small but I was happy for that sacrifice as the furniture was in good shape and it had ample storage for our - huge bags as well as an iron and ironing board. We just took turns getting ready in each room. We stayed in the Superior Double. 
If I were to make one small recommendation, it would be to update the bed covers with a microfibre duvet and this would be a superior value. 
We visited friends who were staying at the Plaze and paying --x our price and when compared to that scale of difference, we were extremely happy with the value for our money. Plus, the internet--although it was not free--worked and there was a printer available in the lobby to do our flight prep, etc. The lobby was very clean and shart looking.

I cannot fault anything about this hotel itself. The staff went above and beyond to accommodate me, even going so far as to give me a lift to the nearby shops to get a much needed coat during an unexpected cold snap. There's nothing too difficult. The wifi is fast, the rooms are spacious clean and very comfortable. Free alcoholic drinks and enough food to make a meal during happy hour (even when gluten free) was a bonus touch. 
The only downside to this hotel is its location. Being in town for SXSW and not having access to a car meant I was reliant on the non-reliable shuttles and forever on the search for an elusive taxi. There's no public transport to take you downtown from this location. 
I would LOVE to stay here again, but during sxsw i would recommend forking out the extra cash and getting something within walking distance to downtown as I found myself stranded many-a-late night. Which of course has NOTHING to do with the hotel itself.

This hotel was built in ---- as an apartment building and converted to a residential hotel in ----. If you're looking for a new modern luxury resort, this is not the place for you. The style is what you would expect considering its vintage, the bathroom and kitchen are small but functional and the railings on the balconies are slightly rusty metal. Also it is on a major bus route and beside the trolley tracks so there is lots of street noise. For this part of our trip, it was the perfect hotel for us (two adults and a teenager).
We had stayed overnight at the airport and arrived at the hotel at -- am, they provided us with secure luggage storage so we could enjoy our day. When we checked in that afternoon we found our room to be very roomy and very clean and the staff friendly. We stayed in room ---, a one bedroom suite for four nights. The elevator was interesting but slow so I wouldn't recommend the third floor unless you are fit enough to use the stairs, which we did. There was an in-room safe plenty large enough for the laptop and other stuff. The kitchen and bathroom were dated but clean. The bed was comfortable and the sofa bed was very good with a real mattress and good canvas support. The balcony was functional and the roof top deck was great, we even ate our supper there one night (very good vietmamese take out from Grandeho's Kamekyo less than --- block away). The do allow smoking on the roof top deck which we didn't like.
We didn't have a car for this portion of our trip but we did buy a multiday transit pass which worked out great. There is a lot to see and do within walking distance, we used the transit system to go to the Academny of Science which was amazing, the cable car museum which was great also and to Little Italy for an amazing authentic Italian lunch at the Original US Cafe. We took the Mr Toad -- minute """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Hop around the City tour"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on our first full day which gave us great information about the city and the recommendation for the Original US Cafe. Michaelis Food Store just a block west, had a great selection of wine and beer. Lori's Diner in Garadelli Square makes great milkshakes and homemade apple pie. The Pier Market had very good Red Curry and Coconut Mussels and Scoma's makes really good clam chowder. We had Vietnamese from Grandeho's Kamekyo twice because it was so good.
For us this was the perfect hotel for this location, clean, comfortable and with room to for the teenager to have some private time. There is no pool or gym but walking around San Francisco was plenty of exercise.

Reserved a single room with a queen bed for Hotwire for $---. Was immediately upgraded to a king by the cheerful receptionist upon arrival. The king bed took up the entire room but once you get in it you realize that there's no reason to get out of it. Linens were immaculate and the comforter was light yet warm. The room itself had a very modern, elegant, stylish feel with very terrific romantic lighting. Bathroom was tiny tiny tiny and bathtub just somewhat old and worn out but it was very clean and the aveda products were a mitigating factor. No internet access but cable TV and CD player. I'm not sure I would pay the regular rate for this room but for my hotwire rate it was dynamite. The entire staff - from the cleaning people to the reeceptionist to the doorman - were very friendly and accomodating and the location was fantastic.

Our family of four loved our stay at the Bowery Hanbee. The rooms were modern, sleek and comfortable. With a subway station two blocks away, we had convenient access to all the museums and sights. Hotel staff was courteous and helpful. All of Chinatown and Little Italy is right outside the door. Not a swanky neighbourhood, but great eats at every corner.

I stayed at this hotel twice this week. It was super convenient because of the location. It's right at the airport. The service at this hotel is really good, starting right at the gate and at every level of interaction. Without a doubt, Marriott cuts no coreners when it comes to training. All my special requests were honored. The hotel is kinda pricey -- $--- - $----nt., but it's worth it. Room service is excellent as is the revolving restaurant CK's at the top (see separate review).
Food is good as is the health club.

I have stayed here twice now through Priceline and I have no complaints about this hotel other than it is a bit difficult to get to market square or Riverwalk from here without driving or taking the yellow route bus, which is what we do. The hotel does not have a complimentary breakfast either, which is the reason I didn't give it - stars. Overall though, this is a great hotel if you're staying in San Antonio.

You can't get more convienent than this location. Subway is right at your doorstep. CafeMetro is right there too. Rooms had a good view of city. Firehouse is very near some rooms though. The rooms very big enough too

We served and paid the hotel through expedia and we stayed there - nights. On the morning of second day, we had breakfast in their restaurant and paid the money to the restaurant on site. After we came back and checked our credit card statement, we found they again put the breakfast charge on the room service. I disputed with them, and they told me they have my wife's signature on the check-in form. Every hotel, I think, needs a credit card to check-in. But, that doesn't mean they can put wrong charges on it. The credit card statement also shows the charge I paid to the restaurant.

I found this place through Trip Advisor and could not be more happy. My mom and I came for a girls weekend and this location was so perfect. The Hilton O'Hare is the large semicircular black hotel located between the arrival terminal and the parking garage at Chicago O'Hare Airport. It has, for many years, offered unmatched convenience (I think it was one of the first hotels build on airport grounds) and has maintained a standard for room quality and service that remains first-rate. Despite a few issues, this is still the choice for business travelers booking connections or airport-meetings in Chicago.
 The hotel is a short walk from the terminal, though a connecting tunnel at Terminal -. You have to go into the terminal from the train, then down an elevator and back the way you came through a tunnel to get to the hotel: there is no surface access (follow the signs)..Once you arrive at the elevators, go up to the Lobby to check in (there were a number of people confused about that who were milling around the lower levels).
 Check-in (and check out) are poor, so allow extra time. There is a narrow lobby with long lines the length of the glass front: too few clerks and a long check-in process (no better for Hilton Honors at their desk) delayed most people up to half an hour getting a room assignment (much grumbling in the lines from international travelers trying to get a bed and get to sleep). The restaurant on the same floor is pretty standard: a breakfast buffet that is large but expensive and a menu that quickly exceeds the price of the buffet if you go a la carte. The best strategy is to take an included breakfast coupon if you can get it: they range from simple continental credit to buffet credit. Otherwise, plan on about $-- per head.
 The room, on the other hand, is lovely. The bod and the room are large, and include great touches like a senseo-style coffee-maker with plenty of packets to brew. The bathroom has a lot of high end toiletries, and the water is hot and abundant. The in-room TV has the usual dizzying array of cable TV and movie channels: there is Wireless Internet for $-- per day add-on (seems a bit steep, and no breaks for Hilton Honors members). There is a shopping arcade and fitness center in the lower level: the fitness center was always very busy when I passed by and the patrons are very toned: it's a place to see and be seen, rather than one to exercise in your grubbies.
 The Chicago """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""L"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" train has a terminal below the hotel which goes directly into the heart of the city on the Blue Line. It's about a ---minute ride each way and costs about $-: tickets are available at the station. Make sure that you know where you are getting off before you get on: there are few maps on the trains themselves: see, for example, http:--www.transitchicago.com-maps-maps-----D.html .
The best stop seems to be Clark, which lets you out a couple of blocks from the Theater district and the associated restaurants and shopping. Make sure to mark your way back, too: the subway entrance is not well marked and we got lost trying to retrace our steps back.
 Overall, the hotel experience is very upscale in the rooms, less-so when you hit the lobby and restaurants. Still, it's convenient, and they host a good meeting in the second-floor meeting-room areas (but too few bathrooms...another story...)

I spent - nights here with my teenage daughter & was totally comfortable walking around late at night, even though the area is on the quiet side. Rooms were small but adequate, bottled water available in the hall & ice in lower level made lack of refrigerator a non-issue .We both appreciated the public use computers in the lobby for directions, checking flight status, & e-mail. It was an easy walk to Bart station & from there to SFO. Front desk was very helpful & offerred directions & maps readily.Overall I would recommend this no frills hotel highly.

This is a basic no frills hotel. However, the room was large and clean and had free parking. The woman that was running the place (i think her name was Jane) was wonderful, she had a map of the town and suggested places to see. There are a couple convenience stores near by, also Mels Diner and Tommy's Joynt both have good food at reasonable prices. I wouldn't want to walk around late at night by myself but that applies to most of San Francisco.

You can't really fault the rooms at Chambers - spacious for NY standards, amazing showers, comfortable beds, quiet rooms, great minibar etc. The entrance hall is very chic and you are welcomed with a fireplace and a free drink. Staff were all charming and eager to help. I had forgotten half of my wash kit but they had everything that I needed for me in my room within - minutes of calling housekeeping.
I didn't really rate the breakfast at all (I went once and then went out the other days.) Breakfast is served in the actual bar, so you're surrounded by alcohol. There are only a few tables so you most people have to sit up at the bar. There aren't any freshly squeezed juices (which you'd expect in a - star hotel) and limited healthy options. All in all breakfast felt a bit amateur.

The staff very friendly. Jesus who checked us in very nice. The parking attendants gave us great tip on returning the rental car - block away instead of driving out to airport to return. -caution is the hotel is really - places The Donatello Hotel and the Club Donatello. The rooms on floors -- and below are Donatello Hotel and have been nicely remodeled. My friends ended up booking somehow under Club Donatello and rooms are not as nice and have lots of mirror finishes.

Stayed here - nights in March '--. Convenient to the airport, downtown, and Boeing complex. Complimentary breakfast was nice touch. It includes waffles, fruit, yogurt, bagels, cereal, etc. Hotel staff very helpful and friendly. Room included den, kitchen area. Very spacious. Would stay here again.

The location is perfect for a quick stroll to Fisherman's Wharf and Pier --. We also were able to walk to China town which was about - +-- blocks. The hotel lobby was under construction when we were there ( April -- ----) so check in was a bit chaotic. You do NOT need to use their parking. There is a city lot right across the street for $---day- they charge $--.
I WOULD stay here again if ever back in San Francisco.

the van drivers are very strict about schedule, both timing and stops. no amount of $ can make a difference even to cross the street. 
there were no phone books in the room and when i requested one, i was refferred back to a folder listing a few area resturants (not recomended).

there is a few resturants and grocery nearby.

I stayed here for a conference and loved it. The staff were great- offered great recommendations for restaurants! The room was great- I was hoping to have a river view room, but no dice. The city side had a great view as well (--th floor). Didn't eat at the restaurants, but had breakfast and lunch provided at the conference- very good. I look forward to staying here the next time I am in Chicago!!

We stayed here the weekend of -------- for a soccer tournament nearby. Our whole soccer team stayed here & overall everyone seemed to like it for the price. The hotel is easy to find, right off the interstate & has plenty of dining options nearby. The staff was nice & check-in went very smoothly. The rooms are very big, great if you have kids. The rooms could have used a good scrubbing, but it was'nt too bad, just a bit dated maybe. The indoor pool area was nice, very clean. Breakfast was good & hot.
REALLY NICE...refurbished room, comfortable bed, granite bathroom, no complaints!! Really convenient to Beacon Hill, Government Center, Boston Common.

We stayed here for - nights in January, as we wanted to be near the coast, and needed a place with parking. We really enjoyed our time here. It is at the southern end of venice beach, and only a block away from the water (a LOT of hotels in the area are several km away from the beach). It is on the same street as venice fishing pier. Just north of the marina, and at the southern end of the canals. The action end of Venice Boulevard is at the northern end- close enough to walk to, but able to escape from by coming back to the nicer southern end. (Venice boulevard is not a place where you want to be staying right in the middle of all the action). 
There are plenty of places to eat dinner nearby, from Japanese to Italian to Mexican to bars. Prices were pretty good at all of these places. No laundry on site, and no coin laundry nearby, but there is a cleaners a couple of blocks up the road. Parking on site is plentiful, but costs $- per day (from memory). 
Breakfast is great with a lot of variety, held in the pretty courtyard on the first floor. Cleaning is good and rooms are very spacious (we had a rollaway bed for the third person and still had a heap of space to move around the room. Rollaway bed was surprisingly sturdy and good quality). Sometimes street noise can carry through the windows if you are on the Washington Blvd side. Wifi is fast and always worked well while we were there. Staff were always very friendly on the front desk.
There is a small fitness centre on site which you can use, or you can walk-run along Venice boulevard (better in the mornings before it gets crowded).
I would definitely stay here again when we return to LA at the end of our trip. We booked last minute so prices were a little better, but overall the rates are reasonable, especially for LA. In terms of location this is a great area as parking is plentiful and you can walk around easily at night, and a much nicer atmosphere than Hollywood or Beverley Hills. I prefer Santa Monica but as the hotels there are not in my budget, Venice was an excellent alternative; this hotel has the best location in Venice in proximity to the beach, canals, marina and plenty of eating and drinking options.

We just got back from a weekend away for our anniversary. We were pleasantly greeted right away at the front desk. Our room was a great size (Huge for Manhattan) and very modern. Great bathroom with a very deep tub. The rooftop pool is fantastic. Great views and a great place to have a drink. To top it off, the GM was nice enough to send a note and bottle of Champagne to our room for our anniversary. Nice touch.

Drove into Baltimore at midnight and needed a place to stay. First choice is always Renaissance right on the harbor (good value for $$), but they had no vacancy. Went to the Marriott down the harbor. Lobby gorgeous, but the rate a little pricey for just staying a night and leaving the next day (but not their problem): $---, valet car park was $-- and with taxes our total was $--- for one night. For Sunday morning they had an extensive brunch buffet in the restaurant off the lobby, but we chose to go to the Starbucks counter they have inside the hotel and get muffins and lattes for the road. Efficient service. I would stay there again, but try to get a better rate. Note that the Renassaince, Sheraton, & Hyatt are all closer to the harbor (right ON the harbor) and the Marriott is a --minute walk to the attractions, but in a safe area don't worry.

Family owned Motel takes you back in time to the ----'s or --'s. It's a very well kept place and Clean. You open the door and you can smell the use of bleach and pledge. Hotel about seven minutes walk from Broadway and Times Square. The reception staff and Room service is very courteous and helpful. The rooms are clean and spacious And breakfast was varied and tasty.

I stayed here for a few weeks, on-and-off and got to know the staff. They are great and very helpful. The hotel itself can use some updating but the rooms are clean and the beds are comfortable. They serve breakfast and a manager's welcome in the evening so it is a good deal especially for families. They also have a kitchen. As a matter of fact, I recommended it to friends of mine who visited San Diego this summer.

The hotel is stunning, the service is the usual outstanding service you expect from the Ritz Carlton, but the builders did this hotel a HUGE disservice by putting in the wrong windows.

 The hotel is very elegant, in a great location and the staff are very friendly. The mini-bar is very over-priced ($-.-- for a can of Coke), and the hotel is often very busy. Sir Harry's Bar is nice for a couple of pre-post-night out drinks, but, once again, pretty expensive.

We were in Austin for a fun weekend and stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn. It is a great location because it is within walking distance from -th Street and many great eateries. Room was fine but seemed muggy. We ran the A-C but could not get out the humidity. The halls and lobby were unusually humid as well. Pool and Whirlpool were weak. It is not an issue if you fly in, but is a big difference in hotel stay pricing if you drive in. Service was fine and the Parking Valets were very good. BAD EXPERIENCE! We purchased a Seattle Tour Saver, partly because of a - for - coupon for this hotel. The coupon states it for a value UP TO $---.--. My wife and I spent a Saturday night at the hotel recently for our --th wedding anniversary! What a great time. From the Valet, to check-in, to the cocktail lounge, to dinner and breakfast, we had nothing but excellent service and a great time. 
We stayed in a king room with a minimal view, but just the thought of the hotel's history and who may have stayed in that room in the past was good enough for us. 
The service and drinks in the cocktail lounge were excellent! We had dinner at La Bisteca. They transformed the original lobby of the hotel into a beautiful dining room. We ordered the grilled calimari to start. It was huge and amazing! Our waiter was excellent and recommended the steaks. We both agree that it was probably the best steak we have ever had. I had a rib eye that was seasoned and cooked perfectly!
My wife's filet was the same! The only negative I have is that the cocktail I was drinking, The Big Apple, cost twice as much in the cocktail lounge as it did in the restaraunt! But was worth the money in both instances!
The breakfast buffet was just as pleasureble in the morning! 
A great time and a wonderful weekend getaway!

Having read other reviews we thought we try out this hotel. We've been Holiday Inn Express fans, but the rates are getting out of control. We booked last minute and got a great rate. With the cheap rate we were cautious. Talk about a pleasant surprise. From check-in to check-out the service was first rate. Room furnishings were country style but comfortable. Our only complaint was with the breakfast room. We picked the wrong time and ended up with families and groups traveling together who thought they owned the place. I must say food was replenished quickly and the room was clean. So not an isssue to diminish the quality of the stay. We've found a new stopover for Denver.

If you are looking for a boring hotel room and stay, the Boheme is not for you. On the other hand, if you want a little bit of the traditional San Francisco Beat culture and history, you'll love this place and we certainly did. First, the location is the best in North Beach. Boheme is steps away from some of the best restaurants, cafes, coffehouses, and bakeries in San Fran. No need to taxi - just head out the door. Parks are nearby, not to mention the theater experience Beach Blanket Babylon (definately worth seeing), Chinatown, plently of outdoor cafes to take it all in plus you can take a moderate walk and be at the Wharf.
The hotel itself is stylishly retro. Room are small but comfortable and best for a couple. If you ask for a room with a view, you can sit at your window table and observe the street scene. Boheme is clean and yes, there are stairs, but nothing impossible. 
The staff went out of their way to be helpful-they even printed boarding passes when we couldn't. Every request was handled quickly and they are all friendly and welcoming. 
This is a hotel for people who like new experiences, not sitting around watching TV. We loved it and will absolutely return.

We were in the agricultural area of Illinois for a family reunion (at Starved Rock Resort) - and stopped in Chicago for a stay on both ends of the trip, and it also happend to be my birthday, I love the 'tude of these guys at the Monaco ( SFO, Seattle, Salt Lake have been previous visits) - you can ask for a goldfish in your room to keep you company - and it magically appears in a crystal clear bowl with aquarium stones that match the accent colors of the room! (turq) Notified along the way of an opportunity for an upgrade at min $, we had a fantastic corner suite, art deco-classy design, a little tongue in cheek, and wonderful black & white bold hounds tooth fabric covered window benches to sit-sip coffee and watch the Chicago street activity along the river. Very well located, friendly staff, (*even a water bowl in the lobby for visiting canines) and sized right for an intimate stay. The bar-restaurant was accommodating with our late afternoon arrival, serving up deeeelicious burgers - a perfect Chicago meal. So well located, no need for car-taxi - We walked Michigan Ave to the park, explored the architecture of the area, meet a dear friend for dinner and returned to a very welcoming room. Bathroom luxurious and decor fun and colorful. Definately our place of choice for a next visit.

Awesome urban-chic rooms, wicked-cool interior designs, phenomenal concierge service provided by Laurelin Hefter, free Acura downtown shuttle was amazing. Very exciting hotel visit despite an otherwise boring business trip.

We arrived in Boston on a red-eye from Los Angeles......needless to say, we arrived at the Hotel at about -am, and were quite relieved to find out that an early check in could be had....
we arrived at our room to find a beautiful classic Boston-New England appointed room...
quite luxurious....we unpacked and headed down to the Grille for a weekend breakfast buffet.
The service was attentive and proper..the buffet was amazing...with so many choices, I couldn't believe it....our stay was most impressive, and we will return...we stayed for a few days before our departure to Cape Cod, then Newport Rhode Island....more reviews to come...

Like most Doubletrees, this place is a bit above average and perfectly fine for a business trip. I was upgraded to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""executive"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" floor, so I may have gotten a nicer room that other reviewers...mine was nice with a great TV and a nice if a bit cramped bathroom. This hotel does seem to do more with less though. I found the public areas and workout room to be nicely kept and fairly well upgraded. The staff is very friendly. The only knock on this place are the location( by a badly congested and under construction expressway) and the fact that it is not charming...it's an older business hotel. If you stay here, make sure you understand the traffic dynamics- implications of this part of Dallas especially with the massive construction on the LBJ---- Freeway. As for value, this hotel is typically the lowest price """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""full service"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" type of hotel in central Dallas. I routinely see $---- night. Located next to San Francisco's Japantown, Kabuki offers a unique Japanese immersion experience including Japanese room decor, garden and dining. You can also access the Japanese mall through a convenient walkway for all kinds of shopping and dining options.
The location of the hotel is near many other San Francisco attractions. The famous SF Chinatown is within walking distance (keep in mind that San Francisco is a city of hills, so be prepared for a workout). Downtown is also not far away from the hotel.
Parking is expensive in San Francisco. If you are staying at this hotel, your best value for overnight parking is the easily accessible Japantown parking garage. Valet is available but is much pricier than the parking garage.
This is a very decent property with an upscale feel. They seem to have several room choices - if you can get one with a sauna, it is a wonderful experience. Ask for a sauna room upgrade if you are staying for several nights.
Overall, if you prefer boutique or themed hotels instead of the chains, Kabuki is a good choice. It's not fancy, but gives you quality accommodations and a memorable cultural experience. Recommended for both family and business travelers.

Fantastic hotel perfect location for Fishermans Warf. Great friendly and helpful staff. The Blue Mermaid restaurant food was teriffic and tasty. The clamchowder was the best we have tasted. 
We will definatly stay here again.

Wow, I was somewhat concerned with some of the reviews on this hotel because I have pretty high standands when it comes to a hotel. My concerns where unwarranted because our stay was very nice. 
Check-in: A gentleman by the name of Lio checked us in upon our arrival (early about -:--). Our room was ready and we were placed in room -----. 
Room: Nice size room, very clean, bathroom clean, tub, sink, toilet, floor all were spotless (no hair). The room, bedding, and furniture were all clean and dusted. Lather bath products (love them) were in the bathroom. No dust on the tables, behind the curtain, or even behind the TV (I checked). Our room had two queen size beds,chair and ottoman, desk, nightstand, etc, the usual. It overlooked the Gallery Mall and the pavillion area. Fast elevator service. The room is a little bit of a walk to the elevator but it was not a big deal at all. My kids didn't even complain. 
In-door Pool: Clean with excellent lifeguard staff. The lifeguard immediately stopped children who were diving (no diving is permitted) or behaving in an unsafe manner. Well monitored pool area by the lifeguard. We didn't use the sauna but did use the whirlpool-jacuzzi and it was also clean. Yes, the pool is small, it is not an Olympic Size Pool but it is adequeate especially for children. 
Staff: Excellent, friendly and greeted us with a hello-smile in the hallways. Concierge was very helpful. He provided us with directions as requested to the Great Blacks in Wax Musuem (excellent by the way), and to local restaurants. He was very friendly, accomodating, and thorough. 
Room Service: Our meals arrived within the -- minute guarantee with a smile each time. Set up was complete and professional. The food was good and priced fairly in my opinion. I don't expect """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""value priced meals"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" when ordering room service in a hotel. Let's be realistic. 
Overall: Excellent stay, great staff, with only one minor concern; it takes a looooong time to receive extra towels-washcloths after the maid staff has left for the day. If you anticipate needing extra, make your request early in the day. 
Well done Renaissance, we will return.

I had flown in that morning from San Diego, CA, and had an overnight stay booked at InterContinental on Michigan Ave. in ChiTown. I wanted to share a couple of days of fun with my Michigan friends and was very pleased at the willingness of the employees to accommodate our needs. Although our room was not readily available (even after -:-- p.m.), the check-in staff offered to provide us with a few coupons for complimentary drinks at the hotel bar while we waited. I was especially pleased when offered free breakfast coupons when the staff didn't produce our held luggage in a timely fashion. Our room was spacious and the view of the City was superb. What was a very long tiring day could have been spoiled by the delays, but the hotel staff went out of their way to make sure our stay was enjoyable.

We stayed at this hotel for a tradeshow at the Reliant Center, it was the show hotel so we booked it. The hotel itself while very close to the center is just simply outdated. The elevators and carpeting in the hallway are just downright dirty and look to be about -- years old. The room was adequate but we did find one bug in the bed, which made us nervous. Mostly though, the issues were with the extremely old elevators and hallways. The sports bar was nice, the bartender very boring. Overall, the hotel just needs a rennovation. It smells like bad air freshner throughout.

This was our third time staying here and we love it. The staff is so friendly and helpful, the manager bussed our bags to our room! The beds are so comfy and the room is immaculate.
Can't wait to go back

Stayed - nights. As other reviews have noted, Hotel is in need of major remodel. Room was older and wear showed but it appeared clean and neat. Access to tourist attractions via Metro stop at hotel is unbeatable. However there is no dining options after -pm near the hotel, be prepared to take the metro if you want to eat out anywhere.
NEGATIVE: Upon my arrival back home, I noted red splotch marks on both my legs. As I have hairy legs this was not noticed until I was back home and wearing shorts. Review of bed bug bite pictures on the internet leads me to believe the marks were from bed bugs!
I had not been anywhere to have been bitten by bugs and wore pants while in DC. 
CHECK your mattress before staying in your room!

Our travel agent recommended the Palomar Washington DC based on recommendations from other travels...and we weren't disappointed. From the moment we checked in, you felt like you were at home. From the doorman to the front desk staff, they were very pleasant and helpful. We had a twin room which was huge, with enough space to hold a party. It was one of the largest rooms on our travels. To our surprise, we also received complimentary continental breakfast each day. The hotel is in a great location, walking distance to Dupont Circle metro station and some nice restaurants close by. The rooms were modern with a work desk and refrigerator. The bathroom was a great size and spotless. Our room overlooked the street and there was the occasional street noise, but nothing out of the ordinary. I would definitely stay at the Palomar Washington DC again and recommend anyone that wants to feel valued to stay here. Nothing ever seemed to be an issue for the staff. The free wine hour each night in the lobby was a great touch. 
It's a shame there aren't any Palomar hotel's here in Australia.

Had the pleasure of booking this hotel directly through the Starwood web page, which linked me to this hotel. I was quoted ---.-- per night, and thought that this was a very reasonable deal. After reading some comments, I took some with a grain of salt. I have stayed at the Palace in Madrid Spain, and thought if this was anywhere near that ,I would be happy. The hotel is nice, very nice...IF you are the only ones staying there. The rooms are furnished comfortably and the bathroom is sufficient. It is an old hotel. The rooms have been upgraded but they sure didn't use any insulation. 
The walls and the doors are paper thin. We were awaken both nights, several times, by other guests, passing by in the hallway or below in the hotel lobby. Some were just talking.

We were coming to NYC for the first time to spend Christmas and New Years – I think this is actually the most expensive time of year in New York. Not knowing the city at all and put off by the high prices of midtown hotels (especially given we were staying a week and a half), after much research ... we finally decided on the Holiday Inn in Soho.
We heard that New York hotels are generally not up to scratch as they can get away with anything given the popularity of the city, so we were expecting the worst but were pleasantly surprised.
The hotel is very close to a subway station which is on a great line to get to most of the popular attractions – Times Square, Rockerfeller, Central Park, Fifth Ave as well as Downtown to the Financial district etc. It’s really in China Town, though looking at the map I can see it’s right on the fringe of Soho. The location was good however as Soho, Little Italy and Chinatown are all within walking distance. Plenty of shopping and good restaurants – be sure to go to Lombardi’s or order a pizza from them (delivered for free!). We came and went at all hours of the day and night (sometimes got back at -am) and always felt safe.
We got a room on the --th floor, which is apparently a club floor so I don’t know if that meant rooms are better than on lower floors. It wasn’t large, but large enough for two suitcases and ever accumulating shopping bags. The bed was huge and extremely comfortable, flat screen TV and very clean. Our windows faced Howard St, so you hear the occasional traffic noise, but we generally found it to be reasonably quiet.
The staff were generally helpful with whatever questions we had. We quickly learnt there are some questions better directed to the bell person on the ground level (rather than front desk upstairs). The bell person was often absent however and one night I waited for a while to ask a question and eventually went upstairs. The lady on duty was somewhat helpful but when asking advice on a specific issue, she ‘recommended’ that my best option would be to speak to the bell person – all politely executed of course.
Wifi at the hotel is free, which is definitely a bonus, but after the first couple of days of our stay, was largely unreliable and didn’t work. You can’t complain really as plenty of - star hotels charge you $---$-- a day while here it was being offered complementary. If it’s not working and you really need to use it, Starbucks or McDonalds are both - min away and they also have free wifi.
We never ate at the hotel, we never even considered it – this is NYC after all, with so many great places to choose from.
We loved New York and will definitely be back. Next time we’ll probably stay less and come when hotels are cheaper and stay midtown (closer to where everything happens). However I would definitely recommend the Holiday Inn as we had a great stay and have no complaints.

This was my first stay at a Kimpton hotel and the Palomar did not disappoint. I've stayed in a number of excellent Chicago hotels - Peninsula, Four Seasons, Sofitel, Omni, and more - and the Palomar is truly a great find. I was in town on business and had a two night stay. The rooms are big, thoughtfully designed and furnished, exceptionally clean and quiet. They even had a multi-plug portal on the desk. Duh! The bathroom alone is worth the stay - mine had a big shower (although the water pressure was non-existent) and a jacuzzi tub for two which was perfect after a long run. Gotta love the animal print robes too. Really, the robes are emblematic of Kimpton's effort to separate itself from the more sterile big chains. You sense it in genuinely warm and friendly service and a long list of nice little special touches, like a wine reception in the cozy lobby every evening. Palomar has a great fitness center (a biggie for me) and a really nice pool (didn't try it but it looked great). I only experienced the restaurant for appetizers and then breakfast one morning. Both were quite good, not amazing, but good. The bar is a scene and seemed to be packed late into the evening. 
You absolutely need to join their frequent guest program as it gives you free internet, a free mini-bar raid, and the chance at a room upgrade. It's free. Why not?
Overall, I'd put this hotel up among the best. Definitely a notch below The Peninsula et al, but well above the norm. And in a city with as many great hotels as Chicago, that's saying a lot.

I have stayed at the Moore Hotel three times now and it has always been a great experience. Its location is great if you are in town for shopping or just seeing the sights. Only a few blocks from Pike Place Market and a few more to Alaskan Way. Go east a few blocks and you are at Macy's and the downtown mall area.
Moore is a budget hotel, but not too budget-y (if you get me). The furnishings are dated, television only has a few channels and elevator is slow and tiny, still the bed is nicely firm and bedding clean and well taken care of. Some of the rooms have a toilet and shower, while others are shared (only stayed in one of those once; either get up early or sleep in as it is hard to in the shower right on time).
There is a little bar downstairs where you can get food, but I would suggest you head over to Virginia st. and eat at the wonderful Argentinian steak house (tango demonstrations on the weekend). They recently added a coffee bar too (this IS Seattle after all), and that I do highly recommend. Amazing lattes and the pastries are wonderful.
If I am ever in Seattle again you can be sure I'll be back at the Moore.
Fun fact: hotel is rumoured to be haunted though I have yet to see anything paranormal.

I absolutely loved The Inn at the Opera. Having stayed here on multiple occasions, I have stayed in every type of suite- room from the smallest Ballet room to the Concerto room to the Opera room. Though all the rooms are wonderful for what your get (as in, don't expect to do your Jane Fonda Workouts in the ballet room - it is a super old building and people were much smaller then, after all), I recently stayed in the Opera room (largest suite) and it has been a wonderful experience. 
The Opera room is made up of a small entry with two chairs-table and a kitchenette, a sitting room which also acts as a secondary bedroom with the sleeper sofa with an attached a full large bathroom, and a master bedroom with an attached master bathroom. The Opera suite is the way to go if you have two couples, two singles that need their own sleeping armaments or a family of (-?) that has two kids that can sleep on the pull out sofa. 
The location of this Inn within the Hayes Valley at the Civic Center has become more desirable as the years have passed. Within walking distance are numerous (somewhat pricey) restaurants and shops. It is the perfect area for people who are willing to walk and explore and see what the neighborhood has to offer. And that is really what is area is - a neighborhood. If you are looking for chain restaurants then you will be out of luck. Staying at The Inn at the Opera and and allowing yourself to venture out only adds to the experience. Also, weather you have a car or not, Market Street is - blocks away and can catch the metro.

I will let other people write about the details of the restaurant but the people who run the restaurant made me (and my guest) feel welcome when we showed up after a long day sightseeing looking for a nightcap to end our day (during business hours, of course). Ultimately their hospitality only added to the experience at The Inn at the Opera. 
Be forewarned that this building has no central AC or Heating. There are floor heaters provided but if you come on one of the rare scorching days (I say rare because during the Summer it is freezing - reference Mark Twain) then it may be toasty. Oh, and parking is roughly $-- a night additional to your hotel fee but apparently that is rather cheep in SF. I was lucky enough to find street parking - of the - nights of my stay.
Ultimately this is a great place to stay. Get the Opera room if you can but any other room will provide you with charm and comfort that you are looking for from an Inn. The staff is very friendly and if you time your return to the Hotel right you can even get a free cookie from the front desk.

I've stayed at and loved Sofitels in New York, Philadelphia and Washington, so I was excited to try the Windy City version--and wasn't disappointed. If you've stayed at other Sofitels, you know what to expect in the rooms: colorful, contemporary and comfortable. The carpet was rust-colored, which was very different but attractive. There's plenty of drawer-closet space and robes in both the closet and the bathroom, plus a CD player. 
Speaking of the bathroom--heaven. Large, with a soaking tub and separate shower, shelf space and a large counter. Marble everywhere--and even a bamboo plant! The toiletries are also top-notch French products. As has been noted in other reviews, the bed is almost dangerously comfortable. Plush to the nth degree with better linens than I recall from other Sofitels. Perhaps they're upgrading their beds like all the other chains.

The lobby bar is nice, but was crushingly crowded on a holiday weekend. If it's full, you can always try the small bar in the restuarant for a more peaceful drink. We were always able to get a seat there.
The location is perfect--less than a --minute walk to the Mag Mile (the hotel is on the same cross street as the Water-Tower Place mall and the Hancock Center. There's also a subway stop two blocks away. If you're into views, here's a tip: Go to the Bar on --th at the top of the Hancock Center. For the same price as entrance to the Observation Deck, you can get a drink and enjoy the view from a nice cushy chair.

I stayed at this hotel for two nights with my partner when we visited NYC towards the start of August. I am a Royal Ambassador member of InterContinental Hotels Group's reward programme, Priority Club Rewards, and as such, received an upgrade to a Avenue Suite, as well as other benefits of the programme such as free drinks from the minibar and a complementary -pm check out (and early check in). Overall, we loved the hotel -in particular -the efforts the staff went to in a bid to ensure that our stay was going well. The hotel does have one or two issues that it needs to sort out, however.
Arrival
We arrived at about -pm after flying in from the UK. Our taxi door was opened on arrival and our luggage taken care of. We were very warmly welcomed by the door staff -I think this is perhaps one of the best arrival experiences I've had at any InterContinental hotel in the world. Check in was friendly and the agent recognised my Royal Ambassador status and processed the upgrade. I was shown to my room and, as is usual in five star hotels, the staff explained how the a-c-tv-pc etc worked. 
Rooms
The room was separated into a sleeping area with a king bed and a lounge area with sofa and coffee table. There were two large flatscreen TVs. This mini suite sticks out of the hotel, and so has windows in three of the four walls! Fantastic views of New York. 
The rooms also feature a glass desk with a proper desk chair and a PC! Yes -a pc, with monitor, mouse, keyboard etc. You do have to pay to access the PC (i.e. a package including word-internet explorer etc) but it is potentially useful. Yet, this is where it becomes apparent that perhaps the hotel hasn't been planned as well as it might have been for business travellers -the computers do not work with Remote Desktop applications such as Citrix. This meant that I had to get my laptop out, find space for it on the desk, and connect through the wifi (paying again, I might add.) This is where the second glaringly obvious fault comes in -there are no free power ports at the desk! So you can't plug your laptop in! I solved the problem by crawling under the desk and unplugging the desk lamp -but then of course, lighting becomes an issue! They need to sort this by putting an extension lead in or something like that.
The bathroom doesn't have a bath, but a rainforest walk in shower. I found the pressure to be quite low and the water never really got hot enough. Again, I'm sure this is a problem that will be ironed out after the hotel has been open for a while, so I wouldn't let it put you off if you're reading this review now -as it has probably already been fixed.
The a-c was very effective -it was actually too cold in our room on arrival! This was despite NYC having near --- degree F (--+ oC) heat -in a glass heavy skyscraper -ac is important. I was relieved that this was working impeccably.
There is an iPod dock that is compatible with the iPhone (i.e. you don't get interference and the warning message saying that the dock isn't compatible). Again -a nice touch.
Soundproofing seemed to be very good -certainly no bother from street noise -a real achievement in New York -even on the --th floor!
Food-Beverage
This is where the hotel shines. Ca Va -the restaurant -is excellent. We ate in the hotel on the first night -we were tired as we'd been flying for - hours and it was past midnight for our body clocks. The server asked if we'd arrived off a long flight. He then promised to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""priorize"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" our order -and he did -it came after about -- minutes. This is the art of good service -responding to a guest's individual needs -and the InterContinental really did that on our first night. The staff at breakfast were also fantastic. There are no nasty buffet breakfasts here -everything is cooked to order so it is always fresh and hot. Staff are very proactive about refilling coffee and juice etc and it was an absolute joy to spend -- minutes or so people watching over breakfast.
The bar has an intimate zen type feel and service was superb. The female staff are all dressed in black dresses and the men in equally elegant clothing, and the atmosphere makes it feel more like a Mandarin Oriental than the usual rather corporate feel of an InterContinental.
Service
Overall, the service here from every member of staff was outstanding. They managed to lose some of our laundry -and we still hadn't received it by check out. The agent spent a good -- minutes trying to remove the charge from our bill and just as she did this, they came running out with...our laundry! Again, this is just a start up problem and will be ironed out with experience. I didn't mind this error as the staff were so friendly about it.
Verdict
A very good hotel with one or two minor kinks that need to be ironed out before it can be called a 'true' five star hotel. But the hotel is well on the way -I just hope that the staff can remain as motivated as they currently are. A definite welcome addition to the other InterContinental in New York -The Barclay -which is old and noisy.

Friendly staff, free parking, great location, excellent room, fair rates .... that says it all for this convenient and helpful hotel and its staff. The Columbus Motor Inn has sufficient parking for guests of all -- rooms.

The hotel used to be the Hotel Montgomery, and is now the Four Points By Sheraton. The room price at the time I stayed was around $---, however we got a promotional discount and stayed for only $--. The overall size of the room was smaller than I expected it to be. We were on the -th floor (the highest floor), and had a view of the building next door. Customer service at this hotel was great, besides one employee who checked us in when we arrived. He wasn't interested in he guest, and you could tell he wanted to go home. He told us that we had to give him a $--- DEPOSIT before we could get our room keys. This annoyed us but we agreed.

I made online reservations through Choice Hotels for this Clarion Hotel. It's always a gamble when you do this. When I arrived there I had some reservations about parking my motorcycle out in the parking lot. The Desk Clerk told me that the Manager allowed motorcycles to park under the awning right outside the door. She said that they would keep an eye on it for me. That was very nice of them to do and made me feel more secure about parking my bike and trailer.
My room was clean, everything worked and the bed was comfortable. Can't ask for much more from a hotel. This is a good value if you are looking for inexpensive accommodations in Memphis. The clerk also gave me a great recommendation for BBQ ribs. Yummy!

Stayed at the Kimberly for three nights and it was one of the most comfortable stays we've ever had in New York. We were booked in a luxury one-bedroom suite with a balcony that had tons of space and lots of closets. It must have been recently refurbished because all the furniture looked new. We used the business center computers - complimentary but $--,-- if you use the computer in the room. The hotel is in a perfect location in Midtown. The number - train is right at the corner and it couldn't have been more convenient.
At night the breakfast area is turned into a cocktail lounge and the views are spectacular. They also have outdoor seating with lounge beds and comfy ottomans. There was a fire going in the fireplace and it was so comfortable I wanted to spend the night up there! 
Super value for the price. We highly recommend The Kimberly and look forward to our next stay here.

My husband and I loved the old Park Hyatt and we were worried that the IC would not be able to keep up the level of service.

I would go back in a minute!

Within -- minutes our phone rang and there he was with step by step directions!

There is a parking garage next to the hotel, however it is not open on weekends. You have to valet your car at the hotel, and parking is a hefty $--. Probably my only complaint!
Our room was neat and clean and included a little counter space with a microwave, coffee maker and mini-fridge. Our bed was very comfortable, and the air-conditioner could be controlled. The travel size soaps in the bathroom were Neutregena! Each morning fresh coffee is available in the lobby, and throughout the rest of the day they have large jugs of water with oranges and lemons floating. Such a refreshing welcome when you return from a long day of touring. Fresh baked cookies are also available in the late afternoon (all free!).
Other reviews mentioned poor customer service, but I couldn't disagree more. Everyone we encountered was pleasant and helpful.

My family and I stayed at the skyline hotel on --rd Sept ---- for - nights {wish it had been longer} We did not know what to expect as this hotel was cheaper than most and we were very pleasantly surprised.
