The Stay is a rather affordable address given the location and the level of service. 
The rooms are pretty small (at least mine was) and the decoration is quite minimal, be it the bedroom or the bathroom. It is clean, good grade for housekeeping. 
You will find bathrobes, iron board and safe in the room. And you can ask for a boiler (but it comes without mugs or spoons... you get ... a boiler) . 
What I liked : the bedding (confortable), the hall and the restaurant (very lively). The location (right on Times Square: theaters, food, bars...) 
On the downside: the elevators (only -) are very slow and you have to be ready to wait and wait ... appliances in bathroom are minimal. It is noisy when your neighbors could not care less about the world around them. The TV channels are few, and many do not work. 
I would probably prefer a more roomy, just a bit fancier place for a romantic stay, but for work, tourism, and shopping I need no more.

The hotel claims to be the oldest, continually operated hotel in the country. As such, rooms are tiny! The hotel recognized that I would be staying for a week, so they offered me a larger room. I never saw the smaller one, so I'll take their word that I got a larger one. The room was still small! 
However, given that, it was very nice. All the amenities are packaged and tucked away in accessible but out of the way locations. Minibar, flat-screen TV, bowed-out shower curtain, lots of pillows all made the stay nice. 
Internet access is free if you join their loyalty program - which is also free. Otherwise, it costs. The loyalty program also provides free morning beverage - I chose to receive both a cup of hot tea & a glass of orange juice every morning - that was nice. Finally, you get the newspaper. I would recommend joining the loyalty program online prior to arrival.
Food was very good. I attended several conference events where breakfast and lunch was served and everything was great. The bar is nice too. The hotel lobby seemed forever crowded with people coming and going or taking advantage of the free internet service. 
Service was excellent across the board - from the front desk (which I had to visit repeatedly when my room key would inexplicably stop working), to maintenance (who I had to call to get a cot when I had a guest one night), to the catering and waitstaff. 
As long as you keep in mind that the rooms will be small and adjust your expectations accordingly, I think anyone would enjoy this ornate, old-world hotel.

The reception is very pleasant with original artwork which is a nice touch. The staff were always charming and helpful.
Breakfast is included in the price and was a real treat. A great array of pastries and also some cereals, yogurts, juice, tea and coffee. A buffet where you can eat as much as you like.
The location is simply perfect. We walked everywhere and everything was in walking distance. Even if you are not a walker, the subway is located a mere - blocks away in either direction.
I cannot recommend this hotel highly enough. Superb value for money and really it merits more than the -.- stars it currently has. Thank you for such an enjoyable stay!

The hotel is very nice and clean, updated decor, and in a great location. The best part was the staff. The Comfort Inn Central Park West met my expectation for a reasonably priced NYC hotel. I was in town for three nights for my son's auditions to various NY music schools, so location and price were paramount. The room with two beds was small and the bathroom even smaller. A large person would find the shower stall more than adequate, but positioning oneself at the sink and toilet might feel cramped. The room was generally quiet. Although they say there is no wireless internet as part to the hotel, we were able to get a strong signal in the lobby and a slightly weaker one in our room facing the interior air shaft. The best points are location, location, location. West --st at Columbus Avenue is NY at its best. Central Park is right there and the local avenues within a short walk have wonderful places to eat at a variety of prices. Subways, buses, and taxis are right there. The staff was helpful and friendly. I would certainly come back. My positive impressions general confirm some of the earlier ones on this site.

Late at night, there security was checking for keys before entering the elevator banks and a key was needed to call elevator. There is a medium sized workout room with a large variety of weights and machines, but no locker facilities, showers, or pool.
The rooms are well furnished with comfortable mattresses with thick mattress pads and white duvet covers and comforters rather than bedspreads. I had two double beds in my room and there were four great quality pillows per bed! How great! Night stand had a clock radio to wich you could attach your ipod or ipod shuffle to listen to your music. I also had a nice lounge chair and comfortable rolling desk chair. The closet contained a safe and ironing board with iron. The bathroom toiletries are nice with great quality herbal shampoo, conditioner, soaps, and shower cap. Towels are fluffy. As noted in another review, the toilet looked a little instiutional, but I found it comforting to know it would flush powerfully for both me and the room's previous occupant. My brother had corner room which was a little bit smaller and oddly angled, but he had a great view of the Wrigley building from his bed. 
Wireless internet worked well for -- dollars and change for -- hours. 
I was pleased with my experience and would definitely return.

- windows that don't open - the standard claustrophobic box

If you want to feel like you are at work rather than on vacation, this is the place for you.

I arrived late after just getting back to the US from a European business trip. Hotel staff were extremely friendly and helpful. Reasonably priced rooms and food service. One of the best Four Points I have ever stayed at.

The hotel has good sized rooms that allowed a place to relax without feeling confined to a tiny hotel room. The only problem with this hotel was the tiny bathroom. However while the hotel did have laundry facilities, they only had - washers and - dryers for the whole hotel which seems ridiculous for the number of rooms they had. But it was a pleasant stay.

This place sits right on the beach (mission beach). This is a great place to stay if you want the beach experience. You can walk down mission beach and go to the boardwalk. Parking there is scarce so parking you vehicle at the hotel and walking up and down mission beach is the way to go.

I did however reserve a room with two twin beds and got a room with one king so we had to pay extra to have a cot wheeled in (and we didn't have it for our first night so my poor sister had to sleep on the floor). Similarly, our room had maybe only one or two towels which were not adequate for three people. 
We arrived at the hotel at about - p.m. on Friday and asked if we could check in early. They told us we couldn't check in until - p.m. which we understood but the way they said it was a little harsh. They did let us leave our bags with them so we could go to the concert. We also asked for a room with two twin beds (like we reserved) and they said no and we asked for a cot and were told no. I understand - it was busy - but that was it. No offer of extra pillows or blankets, just no.

There's a museum and cafe not too far away as well as an Original Pancake House. The bus was about -- minutes from Grant Park and downtown Chicago. There's also a shuttle but we didn't want to ask the staff for more info about it since they were already pretty unfriendly. 
Also, when we were getting ready Sunday morning, a housekeeper knocked on the door at about -:-- a.m. and asked if she could come in. We asked her to come back later. She knocked on our door again about an hour later. Now, sure, most people probably would have left by then, but this was Sunday morning. The actual room was fine. With the cot, it was a little tight for three people. The complimentary shampoo and conditioner were gross though. They made my hair feel terrible. I'm usually not at all picky about that type of thing but these were bad. 
In general, this experience could have been pretty solid if the staff had not been unpleasant for the whole weekend. I've stayed in cheap hotels before and been treated well. This was not that type of experience.

It seemed to me that every person that was working at the Lenox really wanted to be there. From housekeeping to bellhop,reservations to bartenders, a smile and a greeting. Let me tell you that's huge! Tom and Jason thanks for all your help and making our trip to Boston even more enjoyable!

We had a lovely stay in this hotel. They kindly upgraded us to a King Superior on the --st floor the views over Dallas were amazing. The room was spacious and clean. The bathroom was huge with a large bathtub. Walking distance to JFK sights and was close to many restaurants.

We viewed all of the sights around Hollywood and LA and thoroughly enjoyed our trip. There is a back entrance from the end of Orchid Ave that leads to the mall area, so it is a quick walk to Hollywood Blvd. Yes, the hotel is a little outdated and doesn't have an elevator, but the rooms are very clean and the staff is always there to help. We had a little street noise from Franklin Dr, but we slept through it easily. The free wifi only reaches to the lobby and patio area, so don't expect it in your room. The staff knows the area, metro routes, and anything else you need really well and are always willing to please. I will definitely recommend this hotel to others and would stay there again if I were to ever again.

Good hotel if- and only if- you are going to a convention in McCormick Place. The hotel is located a long distance from any other attractions, except Solider Field. It is on the northern edge of one of the worst south Chicago neighborhoods. Don't walk any where. Drive or taxi, even if only a short distance.
The hotel itself is clean and modern. The staff was adequate. Our room faced the lake and had a nice view of Navy Pier, which would have been good in the summer when they have the fireworks.
Despite the hotels features, we will never stay here again because it is simply too far south of the restaurants and activities we want and the surrounding neighborhood is a disaster.
The self-park garage was attached to the hotel and safe ($-- for -- hours). The hotel offers breakfast, but most of the dishes are $--+ which is pricey for eggs and toast, even in Chicago.

My husband and I wanted to stay on Riverwalk to view the annual Christmas parade. We DID have a balcony but it is only about -- inches wide - no chairs - no way to sit and be comfortable. Service at the front desk was very slow and somewhat gruding. The concierge was largely invisible. The food was buffet only during our stay - lots of employees standing around with very little actual service. We dropped in on other properties on the Riverwalk while there - lively lobbies, bars, etc. The bar at the Westin is very small, in the basement, and there was no service except bar walk-up. No view of the river. Overall, a huge disappointment, especially at the price. The website is not exactly dead on in their descriptions. I suppose there were welcoming chocolates somewhere but employees lacked the energy to point them out. Everything was prohibitively expensive (and that was not a surprise, based on the hotel's location,) but a staff meeting is in order with a presentation on courtesy and service. We loved the River Walk and San Antonio but the Westin, no. Too bad - we chose it based on prior experiences. All in all, a huge disappointment.

After changing my plans i was left wanting in San Fran,due to things out of my control i ended up hear. Not wanting to fork out $--- a night i ended up here @ $--- p-n double.my fault you get what you pay for, well usually $--- gets you a great room.

I stayed at On The Avenue hotel for a brief layover I had while in NYC. The price was absolutely amazing. I paid -- dollars for the night. Most hotels in NY go for at least double that. The hotel is a boutique hotel and is very very trendy and modern. The decor is absolutely unrivaled for the price, and the staff was extremely helpful. I travel a lot for work, and I have found this staff to be impeccable! Especially Joanna at the front desk. She welcomed me in such a genuine and friendly manner. Extra towels were offered without me having to ask. The hotel is conveniently located right on Broadway, close to major shops and still was very quiet. 
The room itself was gigantic compared to most NYC hotels... there was a king size bed along with a nicely designed bathroom, standup shower... very very very unexpected.
Come to NY... stay here , that's the motto.
Bravo, well done... and I look forward to staying here again... =)

We had traveled to LA to visit family and had not intended on staying at a hotel. At the last minute we decided that a get away from the kids deserved a mini romantic stay. We booked through their website and we're surprised to see a $----night rate on a Thurs. for the weekend! We immediately booked for - nights (Fri. and Sat.) 
 Upon arriving at the Bonaventure, we were immediately greeted by the Valet. VERY friendly and helpful. They opened my wife's door and took out our luggage before I even got out of the car. Robert was great! We preceded to check in and were agog (is that a word) at the view inside. Really felt outclassed. (HA! HA!) 
 We went up to our room and we met with a decent sized room with a spectacular view (see pics). The room might not have been the biggest but its not like we were gonna live there. The bathroom was small but elegant. 
 We changed and then immediate went on the hunt for a Starbucks. The only bad advise we got was being sent to the wrong SB's. Go to the one on Figueroa, alot friendlier staff and not pretentious. 
 After some coffee we preceded to the Bona Vista Lounge were we had great Martini's and a fantastic server. (Brandon I think?) The view was breathtaking especially at sunset. We also went the next day and after only one visit, Brandon already knew our drinks and got us a prime table along the window eventhough their was a wait.
 Though parking was expensive ($--) it was still worth it. We had a great time and were thouroughly spoiled by their staff. We highly recommend The Bonaventure and will be staying there again!!!!!

excellent location around the corner from Macey's, and a short walk from Times Square. The staff were all very helpful, late checkout was no problem and the room was a good size with two comfy queen size beds. Also a computer available to do online flight check in- boarding pass printing - very useful.
Overall, excellent place, would definately book again.

""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Its just one night - about anything will work,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I thought. WRONG. On arrival, the front desk couldn't find any trace of my reservation. I showed my printout, and the lady at the front desk flipped through some heavily highlighted computer printouts, finally coming up with the info that they had made my reservation for the wrong night. (It showed the correct date on the printout of my online reservation.) I was hit with a shock once I made it up to my room, after squeezing into the cramped elevator. The room had not been touched since the last guests - trash everywhere, all appliances left on-running - looked like a frat party had just occurred. After calling the front desk, had to lug everything back down for different room keys, then back up to a hopefully better room. Yes, the new one was made up, but I had serious doubts as to the cleanliness. Too many stains, spots, paint spatters, and overall shoddy construction. And the large floor to ceiling pasted-on graphic of a bikini clad ---year-old did nothing to help the poorly thought-out decor. Basically, nothing looked quite clean enough to touch, so it was like camping without the tent or sleeping bag. It was quiet while I slept, though I saw plenty of partiers on my way in. In the morning, windows out the front looked over the parking area in the atrium space at the hotel's center, and windows on the other side overlooked the street. On my way out, after tipping the gangster-looking valet (uniforms would've been good so you know he's not), a young couple also leaving accidentally dropped a couple cases of Bud light in the driveway in front of my car.
Kinda summed up the place. 
As a young graphic artist, I have no idea what the marketing team was thinking when they helped put this place together.This place feels like it's trying to be a trashy LA fashion boutique, marketing to the kind of young demographic whose parents never took them to nice hotels, so they never acquired the training on how to act at a hotel. And the rooms show the wear and tear from this.
Next time I'll be staying somewhere nicer - like a motel -.

Fantastic hotel, rooms are super clean and not tiny as I thought it would be. We had double room with private bath and it was perfect. Rooms were clean, linens fresh and great location.
We got a great deal on their website and paid about US$-- a night which is incredible for a hotel in New York City!

This is a beautiful, stylishly cool boutique hotel with a great cocktail bar and sidewalk dining area.
The rooms are very compact but have everything you need (unless you need a big desk) and the location is great.
The hotel provides a basic breakfast but it is worth crossing the street to sit and eat in the library courtyard
If this hotel is full, my next favorite is the Chandler

I honestly can not say enough about this hotel. I went on Priceline last minute and got it at a steal. I wasn't expecting very much, and it doesn't stand out as spectacular from the outside, but once you enter it's shocking! Starwood hotels has just taken over this property and totally renovated almost the entire hotel. I believe there are only a couple floors left in the renovation process. There is a beautiful open area that includes meeting rooms, sitting areas, restaurant and an area for the indoor pool and jacuzzi! For traveler's there is even a nice flat screen tv at the check in area for you to see all flights going out of Charlotte. I went up to the room and was surprised at how clean and amazing the room looked. The photo doesn't do it justice, it's really spectacular! There is also a free shuttle that leaves on the half hour throughout the day that will take you a few minutes away to the airport. I think this hotel is the first I've seen in quite a while that's suitable for a business person, their spouse, and children too all at the same time! The ONLY thing I would have liked would be free wireless in the rooms, but it's very inexpensive to buy hourly. I'm not sure the actual cost of this hotel, but if you're on priceline and want to give it a try, request a -star hotel in the Charlotte Airport area.

I understand that we are among the first guests to stay at the new Double Tree Mag Mile (after it was converted from the Chicago City Centre). I'd read the mediocre reviews of the CCC and decided to book anyway, for the proximity to my conference at the Navy Pier. I had no idea of the pending conversion but sometimes things just work out FINE!
Everything is new...carpeting, furniture, beds, bathroom fixtures, etc. The beds and bedding are fantastic. Extremely comfortable. The hotel looks nice: clean and sharp. It's probably a -.- star on """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""the scale"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". 
The staff are working very hard to get the operational systems and processes ironed out. Nothing major and every question is responded to politely, even if it takes a bit longer to get the right information.
We just enjoyed dinner at a great pub literally across the street, Timothy O'Tooles. It doesn't look like more than a ratty bar from the street but the restaurant dowstairs is spacious, well ventilated and the menu is terrific. Next door is a B-L restaurant called the West Egg Cafe...menu looks good but a bit pricey.
The free access to the adjoining health club is an awesome amenity. Excellent facility including sauna AND steam room. The indoor pool is nice for lap swimming and cold weather. The hotel also has a nice -th floor outdoor pool with room for sunning, etc.
I love this place for the location and the nearby restaurants (and even a grocery store). It's easy to walk anywhere including my conference at the Navy Pier. 
And of course, you get the warm Doubletree cookies upon check in...

I went here with a group of -- for the weekend. We were in town to visit the city and attend the Browns vs. Cowboys game. The hotel location is good. It is just a short cab ride to many of the great spots to visit. The hotel restaurant and bar is very nice. The rooms are very spacious and clean. Definitly recommend the Renaissance.

This is my second stay at this hotel - ended up there last year about the same time for a conference. Last year, the rooms were horrid. I took a chance this year based on the latest reviews and must note the refurb has much improved the place. It is now up to what I consider to be Hyatt standard. The service was lovely with exception of a couple of minor hiccups - airline """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lost"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" my luggage and when it arrived at --:-- pm the hotel neglected to inform me which made for a sleepless first night. However, all made an effort to make my visit a pleasant one. Within walking distance to many popular spots. Spacious rooms with lovely comfortable beds. If you make a request, it is taken care of in a timely fashion. They must have taken the mini bar incident to heart and they advise you of its nature upon arrival. If you need a separate fridge they will bring you one. Overall, a pleasant stay. Would recommend.

We live in Hollywood and wanted to celebrate our anniversary in a cool boutique hotel without giving up any amenities. Needless to say the Redbury is a true class act. Each room has a fully functioning kitchen and living room and balcony - making for very spacious accommodations. We dined in ordering Katsuya for dinner and breakfast from Cleo in the morning. Despite its looks, the hotel is brand new so everything is immaculate. We will definitely be back!

We stayed in Seattle as a stop-over on our way to Hawaii from the east coast. Since this wasn't the ultimate destination, we didn't want to pay top dollar to be in a fancy hotel. Unfortunately, the old adage is true... you get what you pay for. This seems to be a very old property and the rooms are aged. The lobby was recently remodeled and was very nice. The front desk also gets the highest of marks for being OUT OF THEIR WAY HELPFUL! They gave us coupons for free appetizers at local restaurants and called the free shuttle to take us there. They even changed us out of the first cramped room they gave us, which hardly had -- inches between the end of the bed and the dresser holding the TV. Although the room we changed into was larger, it faced the parking lot and if we weren't being woke up by the noises from outside, then it was the crazy ice machine running through its loud routine every -- minutes or so. The toilet seat was also old and cracked and didn't seem sanitary. I wish the rooms were as quality as the people were.

My wife and I booked a room mid week in July. When we arrived, we were pleasantly suprised. The hotel was intimate and right on the beach. The prices were very competitive and because the hotel was not booked to capacity, we were upgraded to and ocean view room at no extra chaged.
It is a small hotel without a bar or a restaurant but it is well within walking distance of shops and restaurants.
The owners are modernizing and renovating the hotel but that did not interfere with our stay.
The manager was top notch without a question and I firmly believe that he is their greatest asset. I give it a -+.

This ideally located hotel could not be better situated for taking advantage of Chicago's Magnificent Mile and for access to the must-do Architectural Foundation boat tours. The building's design is getting a lot of buzz. Staff is eager to please. Lots of innovative technology incorporated.

Just got back from a business trip and stayed at the Park Plaza. I travel often for business and have received better service from far less fancy places.
Problems:
- got to the hotel late after flying from the West Coast. No one at the front desk. Waited. Waited. Someone finally showed up.
- Get up to my room, it's late and I'm starving. Call down to room service. Phone rings...and rings...and rings...and no one picks up.
- Say OK, I'll wait till breakfast. Go into the bathroom -- about the size of a closet. 
- Lay down, turn on the TV -- can't get any channels (full of fuzz) -- mess with the wires in back to try to fix nothing helps. Then, after - mintues of barely watching the Olympics thru the fuzz, it cuts out completely.
- Go down to the concierge desk in the morning to report the TV problem. Leave for the day on meetings.
- Get back to my room at -pm. Try the TV -- still doesn't work. I call the front desk...phone rings...and rings...and rings...and no one picks up.
Never again. I paid over $--- for that room and will not be staying there again.

As a regular to retail type hotels I have had good luck with marriot branded hotels....until I needed a special request for a room from -am to -pm for a bus driver. Beth, the special events coordinator made it happen! I will always try for a Wyndham first now!

We had a great stay at the Courtyard! We were on the sixth floor which is the same as the pool so there was a bit of a chlorine smell when you first got off the elevator. We looked out into the alley but we didn't book it for the view :)
The hotel is in a great location. Just a few blocks from the magnificent mile. The staff was very, very friendly. Apparently they are going to be going through a renovation soon as our water was turned off each day. They let us know the times it would be off and tried to be as accommodating as possible.
We got a great deal from travelzoo which made it even better. Chicago is an amazing city even when it is -- degrees.

I booked this hotel for our recent stay in Boston after reading the reviews, so I had a good idea of what to expect out of it. The location is excellent: about a block from Trinity church, a few blocks from Newbury Street and a short walk to the nearest subway stop. The hotel staff we found to be very friendly and helpful in answering any questions that we had. 
Our room was tiny. Once we set our bags down there was little to no space to walk around the room and it would have been too small to spend any extended amount of time in. The bathroom was adequate however the fixtures are in great need of being updated-replaced. We felt the room was cleaned prior to our arrival however since the fixtures and carpet are so old they appeared very dingy and dirty. We also felt that when we were sleeping and early in the morning there was a lot of noise coming from doors being slammed shut nearby and the noisy elevator which we were very close to. The breakfast was fine, nothing out of the ordinary was served but we each had cereal and coffee each morning. I would have liked there to be a larger selection of fresh fruit but was satisfied with the cereal. I appreciated that the hotel offered a discounted rate for the parking garage which was next door, it saved us quite a bit of money during our stay. The discounted parking ($-- for -- hours) was one of the main reasons that we chose this hotel over - others that we were looking at. Overall our experience was ok.

A nice room on a Monday night in San Francisco is an expensive proposition. I did not want to stay in any of the Lombard Street motels - decent as many are - because I was alone in the city and don't always feel quite comfortable walking in that neighborhood. Anyway, even on Hotels.com the best rate I could find was $---.-- at Hotel Adagio, which I had never heard of, but booked as the lowest rate. It was a small and delightful place, an old building rehabbed into very nice rooms - no views here so don't expect it, one couple I met said they faced a brick wall - very clean and very comfortable. The pillows were exceptionally plush as were the bath sheets in the bathroom. The hotel is just a couple of blocks from Union Square so everything is there. I did not eat at the restaurant but the bar downstairs was a delight. Hand made specialty cocktails are a must-try and if you meet Tim the bartender he will be happy to show how it's done and inspire you to try one.

Great boutique hotel nestled on the upper east side. The staff is friendly and accommodating. The rooms are always clean and the bed and pillows are comfy. The rooms happen to be a nice size for Manhattan standards. They have a wonderful rooftop restaurant with beautiful views of the --th street bridge. Wonderful for dinner or just drinks and appetizers. I have stayed here several times this year and will continue to use this hotel as my base when I am in Manhattan.

I stayed at the Marriott Metro Center for a weekend in January and thoroughly enjoyed it. The hotel is within walking distance of the National Mall and three metro stations. In addition, there are many great restaurants nearby. The staff was friendly and very helpful. The rooms were clean and well-appointed. I was surprised at how quiet it was inside the hotel and the room, despite the fact that it is located on a busy street. The hotel has a bar, restaurant, and a Starbucks located inside. I can't say enough good things about this hotel and would definitely stay there again on my next visit to D.C.

Everyone I encountered at this hotel was very helpful and accommodating. The rooms are fine and clean. However, the walls are thin, and if you are facing Colorado Boulevard, you will definitely hear traffic, as well as other guests' doors banging all night. Make sure you ask for a room away from the traffic. The parking in the garage is very tight, which is nothing that can be helped, but be aware of it. 
A very good location, with lots of shopping, movie theatres, and restaurants all around, and Cherry Creek Shopping Center is a mile or so away, but not within walking distance.

Stayed here with my fiance for two nights last weekend. We got in late on Friday night, and the guy at the front desk was friendly and accomodating and recommened a few places that locals go for breakfast, which was very helpful. The lobby was beautiful and always filled with people are the bar or restaurant. We didn't eat here other than ordering chocolate cheesecake (which was amazing!!). Room had a modern decor and the bed was one of the most comfortable I've ever had in a hotel! Everything was very clean. Hotel is in a great location and we walked to many of the historic sites. Parking is expensive, but expected in a big city. If you want your car, make sure to call -- minutes ahead since it is parked about - blocks away. Will definitely stay here again!

I just spent - days in Boston at the Charlesmark. I was in town for a convention that was based at the Westin Copley Square (just about --- steps away). The hotel is stylish, friendly, modern and the location cannot be beat. The Green Line """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""T"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is about - doors down, Newberry Street, around the corner. They don't have a restaurant (coming in the spring), but they do offer a lovely continental breakfast on the -nd floor lobby. The hotel is quiet, the beds amazing, and the pillows even better. I will definitely stay there again.

The rooms are good -sized, spotless and recently updated, nicely furnished. Wireless internet iffy, but they do provide cords. There were no toiletries in the room on arrival, but the front desk took care of that immediately. Front desk was very friendly, and they immediately offered a courtyard room upon check-in so that we were not on the train track side.
However, unless you are a heavy sleeper, you probably will hear the trains going though several times during the night. I was also awakened both mornings at about -:-- am by loud banging noises that I assumed to be a trash truck emptying dumpsters. At -:-- the first morning we were again awakened by the alarm going off in the next room and persisting for about -- minutes until we realized what it was and called the front desk. They took care of it in about -- minutes. Apparently the previous guests had been unable to figure out how to turn the alarm on the clock radio off. We were unable to figure ours out as well. (No, the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""alarm off"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" button didn't do the trick. Even my electronically minded teenage couldn't figure it out. We unplugged ours.) 
The breakfast buffet is $-.-- per person for the hot and cold items, and $-.-- for just cold items. It was pretty much the standard fare that most hotels offer now for free. Definitely nothing special. 
So, all in all, nice clean hotel,close, but not too close to the highway, but not the ideal place for light sleepers.
I used priceline and wound up staying at the hyatt regency. I asked to stay in one of the renovated rooms, and it was very nice. I would stay here again.

My son and I visited this hotel for a long weekend. It was beautiful, right on the Riverwalk in San Antonio. We literally walked out the door onto the Riverwalk. The service was excellent, especially when we had breakfast Saturday morning at their restaurant, Zocca, with service by Angel. He was so warm and welcoming, made menu suggestions and engaged us in conversation. All the other staff was exceptional as well. The beds really are as comfortable as they advertised! Very nice experience.

Stayed here for - nights in September! Nice clean and modern touches! Front desk was very friendly and helpful! Large room and super big bathroom! Room service from the Domestic staff was just perfect! Enjoyed """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Cuffes Bar"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (The hotel was a former Police station!) Had a Gaelic flavor to the place, which was just great! Great location to the main shopping and commerce area of the City! """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Free coffee"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in your room in the morning, which was the perfect start to your day! Served up a great breakfast and the staff were excellent! A little pricey but worth it! Would definitely recommend this hotel for a stay!!

We loved the Distrikt - we picked this hotel based on the reviews on trip advisor and we certainly weren't dissappointed. the staff are really friendly and helpful and went out of their way to make you feel comfortable which really was lovely.
We felt the room size was more than adequate especially for NYC. 
The hotel is so close to Times Sq, restaurants and the subway so it is perfectly located. A lot of reviewers have commented on the area however we always felt safe and as there are a number of hotels in close proximity there's lots of people walking around. 
I understand some of the higher level rooms have spectacular views - we had a lower level room with limited view but really we weren't dissappointed - there is so much to do in NYC it would seem silly to want to spend too much time in your room admiring the view when you can be out there amongst it!! ;o) Yes we did hear the buses in the bus terminal from time to time, but hey it's NYC - there's bound to be a little bit of noise.
Thoroughly recommend the Distrikt - the rooms are clean, modern and well equipped, the staff are awesome and the location is ideal.

Let me start by saying we usually LOVE Hyatt properties. However, this hotel is a nightmare. We've stayed here twice, and hoped our first bad experience was only a fluke. The staff and managers were pleasant when we voiced our issues, but we will never stay here again. We travel to Chicago at least -+ times-year for pleasure, so we've stayed almost everywhere downtown. 
If you are traveling to Chicago it is a known fact you will pay A LOT to park your car (owned or rented). The valet parking at the Hyatt was an absolute NIGHTMARE when we checked out after a three day stay. We called down for our car and was told we had to go to the garage to pick up our car. When I went into the garage there must have been ---+ people either in line, or sitting on the floor of the reception area wondering if or when they would ever see their vehicle. Some people told me they'd been there an hour waiting for their car. Picture an airport that has canceled all of their flights, and that is what this lobby looked like. The hotel told us that they were just busy and everyone was checking out at once. I was also told this is a regular situation. My advice to the hotel is that you need MORE STAFF if you are making people wait an hour to get their car. If you know Sundays are your busiest day, HIRE MORE PEOPLE! 
There were other issues with our room, but I would end up writing a small essay listing those things. 
On a positive note the hotel is in a great location, but there are other hotels we've stayed at in Chicago for the same price and offering a much better experience. Be smart and check out various hotel websites before booking your stay in Chicago and you will be surprised at what cool places you can find. We loved our experiences both the Hard Rock and House of Blues Hotels. 
Based on two stays at this Hyatt we won't be returning for a third.

Stayed here for - nights. Rooms very clean and comfortable. Great view of the river from our room. Very good location for us, just off the freeway and easy to get back onto as well. Lots of food places and nightlife near hotel. Felt safe walking around food places near hotel. Parking free which was great, even Valet as well. Staff friendly and helpful. Buffet breakfast good and reasonably priced. Casino very busy.Would happily stay again

We were so pleased with our stay here. We mainly chose it as it had underground parking but it turns out this hotel is in a fantastic location in San Fran.
There are some great bars and restaurants very close by and just one or two blocks over is Union street which has excellent shopping and dining! 
It doesn't feel like a particually touristy area either, it's an area popular with young professionals. 
The site seeing tour bus stops right outside this hotel too which is very handy after a long day site seeing, you can just hop off right at your hotel!!
Room was spacious and we couldn't have wanted for any more.
It was a tad noisey on the Saturday night (when the bars kicked out) but this was easily fixed by ear plugs, wasn't an issue at all. 
At least the bars are on your door step so it's not far to stagger home! :o)

We chose this hotel based on a recommendation and it did not disappoint! Our room had two comfy queen beds, and a pull-out couch - very spacious and comfortable! Was also exceptionally clean and well made-up daily. Staff were excellent - always pleasant and helpful. Location is great - -- minute walk to -th avenue, -- to Times Square. Would definitely stay here again - with family or friends.

Stayed for four nights at this hotel while attending an International Convention at the nearby Convention Center which us within walking distance. The hotel room was average. The main restaurant was excellent with a decent buffet that had a wide range of great food choices. During conventions it is advisable to go down early for breakfast to avoid long lines or a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""waiting period"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which is virtually unheard of in my book for breakfast at a major hotel! Room service was very poor, both in terms of food quality and the waiter, who in my case, on two occasions, was not on the least polite. Front desk very helpful, as was the concierge for dinner suggestions and directions. Best feature is the downtown location in the SOMA area, with tons of decent food and recreational amenities.

Stayed here during our recent visit to San Diego. It was one of those times when the hotel was just as good as we hoped! We weren't expecting a five-star luxury resort, but we still thrilled with it. We got a two-room suite (well, a bedroom and a sitting room with a faux kitchen and a good-sized bathroom) and it covered our needs quite well (two parents and two girls so we wanted some separate space). Everything was very clean and comfortable, we had a fabulous balcony-deck looking towards Mission Bay, and the staff responded quickly the couple of times we had minor needs. Bear in mind that the hotel rooms open to the outside, not an enclosed hallway - not a problem, just thought you should know. We were very happy with it and will most likely stay there again next time we visit SAN (it is located about three minutes from Sea World).

I loved staying at The Hotel Wilshire! I can't say enough about how chic and impressive the decor is. The rooms are spacious, extremely clean (it's brand new) and the beds are so comfortable!
The rooftop bar was amazing and had a great view of the city. The rooftop drink menu is out of this world! I would highly recommend the Bourbon Smash!!!
The service was impeccable - the staff was friendly and accommodating. 
I will def plan on staying here again! I love everything about this place!
Hotel is in a great location - close to everything downtown - just a block or two from Beale Street. Hotel was very clean, and staff was very friendly.

I was visiting a friend who has a sailboat in the San Pedro-L.A. Harbor. I needed to be close-by but be on a serious budget. I looked at the other low-budget places in the area and decided on this one. Probably the best <$-- a night place in SoCal. Rooms are small to average, no-frills but clean...TV and nice sized bathroom. Some rooms have refrig. and microwave. Other comparably priced hotels are jokes compared to this one. I've stayed at -star hotels and resorts before (LaQuinta Resort, Fairmont, Westin, etc.) and I must say, the manager tries to live up to those standards, albeit <$--. Located in industrial area. Manager is a godsend, but when I tried to contact her to make a reservation, was tough to track down. Be persistent though, it's worth it.

Beautiful, winding, quaint property with flowers everywhere~
Attentive staff and excellent food!
We would definitely come back

This is one of the better Hamptons that we've stayed in. The place was very quiet and reasonably close in to downtown Memphis. The price was right and since we were heading east it was easy to head outbound in the morning.

I have stayed at this property - or - times during business trips into San Francisco. The hotel is clean and reception is always courteous and efficient. I stayed here on business last week, and chose the hotel because it was priced within my company's expense policy and seemed convenient for much of where I needed to go. The location is indeed convenient, being walking distance from downtown and close to lots of attractions, though the neighborhood seems a little sketchy at night.
This hotel seems to be trying to style itself as a chic downtown destination for travelers of all kinds. But despite its reasonable pricing, compared to other hotels, its marketing hype does not match reality.
On the good side, the service was very friendly. When I checked in, late on a Sunday night, the guy on the front desk was very helpful, and recommended some good restaurants to call for delivery that evening.
But the friendly service was really the only thing that lived up to the hype. Don't get me wrong, this is not a dump by any means, and the room overall was clean (though it is crying out for a proper deep clean, in my view). But it is not at the standard the hotel seems to want to hit. The biggest surprise for me in relation to the room was the heavy spotting of mold across the bottom of the shower curtain, extending all the way across and almost a foot up from the bottom edge of the fabric. When I mentioned this to reception they very promptly sent someone up to replace the curtain. This could have been a really positive experience, but the replacement turned out to have mold spots too, albeit on a much smaller scale. This kind of thing underscores the fact that this hotel struggles to meet its own marketing.
All of the above, though a little irritating, were no big deal for me, since I still felt the hotel was decent value for money. However, there was one experience which colored my overall stay and means I won't be back to the Bulfinch. One weeknight in the middle of my stay there was a live band playing downstairs in the restaurant attached to the hotel. Being directly above the restaurant on the next floor up I could hear, and feel, the music, especially the bass and drums, and was not able to sleep. Calling down to reception I discovered the band would not finish until midnight. On a weeknight, and for a hotel that says it's suitable for business clients, I really don't understand how they think it's okay to schedule something like that as there's obviously not adequate soundproofing to avoid disturbing the guests. If they must have live bands, at least give the guests on the second floor some warning of the gig, and perhaps offer them a different room for the night.
