The three level fitness center w- indoor - lane lap pool was great. We checked first to see if there were any lap swimmers and as the pool was empty we brought the kids down for about half an hour. 
For location, this hotel is on the eastern border of Georgetown so the Ritz Carlton Georgetown (which also has great service, wonderful hotel) is more convenient.
For getting around town, there is no metro in Georgetown, so you may consider Ritz Carlton Pentagon City or elsewhere for that convenience. But with a car or cab, you can get anywhere from this FS fairly quickly, especially to the National Mall which is about a ---- minute cab ride.
In comparison to other FS properties, I would say this one is okay. (FS's - stars is most other hotel's five star, so I say this with a grain of salt.) People love the FS for so many reasons and our top reason is the level of service, followed closely by its family friendly - star service. The service was excellent. At other FS properties in US, Canada, Mexico and Costa Rica, and Ritz Carlton properties in DC, I've grown accustomed to cookies and milk for the kids at bedtime. Additionally, the paper I requested for the morning was never delivered. Maybe bedtime cookies & milk are not this hotel's policy but for the price, these little details are the things that distinguish at hotel within this chain.

My husband and I recently stayed at the W Hotel in San Francisco in celebration of my birthday. From the moment we arrived in front of the Hotel and were greeted warmly and professionally by the Bellman to our departure the next afternoon, our entire experience at the W went far beyond our expectations. Our room was beautifully appointed, the view of the city breathtaking, room service friendly and top-notch, concierge extremely helpful, and Guest Services staff patient, professional, and very gracious. We believe that General Manager, Michael Pace, deserves to be very proud of the W, his staff, and himself for leading such a great team!

Stayed here for one night while visiting a friend in the hospital. We booked a King room, non-smoking. The room was clean with a cable tv, mini fridge and very large desk, which would be great if you are a business traveler. The bathroom was clean and the linens were as well. The room didn't smell like smoke, either. Sometimes a non-smoking room isn't really a non-smoking room. The room had just a slight musty smell but that is typical with a-c in high humidity locales. Our room was on the second floor on the backside of the hotel so we did hear some of the I--- noise but with the a-c running, you weren't kept awake. Lots of restaurants within a few miles and there are several other hotels in the immediate area as well as a Cracker Barrel within walking distance for a hardier breakfast. Front desk staff were cheery and helpful. There is a small pool but we did not use it. Would stay here again for the price when you need a reliable, no-fuss, bargain hotel.

The Hotel Edison is steps away from the half-price Broadway theatre ticket booth on Times Square and within a few blocks of all the major Broadway theatres. With the newly up-graded rooms, the hotel now has extremely comfortable beds with lovely bedding in their newly carpeted rooms. (ask for an upgraded room.) Nice lobby; helpful staff. Plenty of nice elevators. Can't beat the price for the location.

I came in on Christmas eve. Before I left I called the hotel to check on services and to make sure that they had my reservation and that it showed pre-paid. They said yes and the restaurant would be available for a continental breakfast the next day. I had been there the year before and it was closed Christmas day but was open Christmas eve.
When I got in everything was closed. I couldnt even get help to get me a cup of milk from the kitchen refrig for my coffee.
I wanted to leave. I asked the desk guy if he saw that my reservation was prepaid. He said yes everything was paid for but he just wanted to take an imprint for incidentals. I said what incidentals--there was no room service, no restaurant NOTHING. At the end I let him take a manual imprint of my card and staple it to my check in form. I needed to be someplace soon and it wasnt worth the aggravation--I just swore never to return.
Over night the guy ran my card for --- dollars and then someone made - charges on it using my number from Maryland. Close to --- was charged over night while I slept. These guys may still have my cc number.
When I checked out I asked for a receipt. The guy said he couldnt give me one since I didnt charge anything. I had to get to the airport so I left and didnt argue with this nonsense.
Two days later I saw all these charges run up on my Mastercard debit card...I called the River Inn and asked to speak to a manager.
He checked my account and said the --- was a mistake but refused to reverse the charge. He denyed knowing anything about the charges over night. He said the --- would go away by itself which Citibank thought was laughable. I argued with him but he refused so I asked him to put the statement that the --- was a mistake in writing--email, letter, fax i didnt care.
He refused. I told him I would take them to court and that there were uses of my credit from -in the morning showing on Christmas day from Maryland.while I was sleeping...and the only people who had my cc number were the crook at his front desk. He refused to put anything in writing including to send me a receipt for my stay. Then he hung up.
Citibank is now investigating the charges and the visitors bureau is opening on investigation on this fraud.
Stay away unless you want your credit cards to be scammed by their night people while you sleep==and then covered up by the day people.
Signed, ripped off at the River Inn

I have stayed at Rivington Apartment twice, for one night each time on business. Yet despite this, I was greeted like an old friend on my return, with a hand written card in my room to welcome me back. The staff on reception are always very helpful and the porters genuinely keen to help with luggage. Even my chambermaid was helpful, knowledgeable and friendly. I am happy to recommend this excellent hotel to family and friends and for me, it is a benchmark for what the service industry can achieve in customer service if it puts its mind to it.

Just returned from attending a - day conference and was looking forward to - days of Fairmont luxury and hospitality. Unfortunately, this hotel did not measure up. Although our stay was pleasant and comfortable, it felt more like a stay at a Marriott Courtyard (or similar) rather than a Fairmont. It's hard to be critical but this hotel is missing all the special touches that would make it a real four star hotel. Our room was nice, but nothing special. It seemed faded and tired and it's hard to ignore a sink that doesn't drain well, a toilet that doesn't flush well and a showerhead that's left over from the --'s. The bed and pillows were comfortable and the bed linens were very nice. However, there were stains on both the sofa and chair cushions. The room was quiet and there were working windows if you wanted fresh air. Although our room had all the amenities it was supposed to have, we heard from fellow conference goers that their rooms were missing such items as hair dryers, clock radios, coffee makers, extra pillows and even the TV remote. 
Our conference meals were taken in the hotel’s Pagoda Restaurant but the buffet food came into the room from another kitchen in the hotel. The food was no better than average and rather bland. The coffee was awful – tasting burnt in the morning and undrinkable in the afternoon. Tea was very hit or miss. Service was very good and several of the servers remembered our beverage preferences from meal to meal. That was a nice luxury touch. 
The huge lobby is quite eclectic in style with dozens of seating areas and several small flat screen TV’s. The chairs and sofas are tired and stained and the entire space desperately needs to be refurbished and cleaned up. The outdoor pool is nice but we were surprised to find no spa or hot tub. The Health Club had a couple dozen exercise machines but no sauna or masseuse. The hotel does not have any of these “luxury” offerings that you come to expect at a Fairmont property. 
Lastly, we were surprised at not having some sort of express check-out – via the TV or at least a bill under the door our last morning. Instead, we had to manually check out at the Front Desk. We left our luggage with the Bell Captain for the short time it took to finish our conference. When we asked if our luggage could be taken down to our car, we were advised that we would have to do that. That meant a walk (with all our bags) back through the lobby to the rear elevators, taking the elevator down to the garage level and walking another -- meters or more to claim our car. Don’t get me wrong, this is all more than acceptable at a Marriott, etc. but hardly what you’d expect at a Fairmont.

I'm a huge Hampton fan. That said, some can disappoint. This is one of my favorites. When you walk in, you have your choice of fresh lemon water, fresh orange water, and helpful folks at the front desk. It's easy walking distance to the River Walk, and easy access to interstates.

As stated, we found this to be a little older property, but its location is nice and close to the airport. We stayed only one night on our way back home. Its about ----- minutes from downtown depending on traffic.
Pros:
Free managers evening reception (Mon through Thur)
Complimentary breakfast (all days)
Free parking
Cons:
A little older hotel
We got a high-floor room and found that the floor would creak in certain areas
We would definitely consider staying here again, if we revisited Seattle.

Great front desk staff, the rest of the experience was dreadful. The room service staff have to be among the most poorly trained I have ever encountered. We had to ask FOUR times for the staff not to slam the supply closet, adjacent to our room (almost in the room itself). They do these random room checks for the minibar, as if the entire budget hinged on the sale of a can of $- peanuts. The roomservice is also equipped with walkie-talkies as loud as megaphones. If you like sleeping in on your vacation, don't stay here. Also, the hotel was under massive construction, a detail that was conveniently excluded from the website. SO we had to take the elevator with construction workers just about every time we used it. No discount because of the work and noise. I'd rather sleep in a box in the alley.

As I get older I am placing a higher value on quiet rooms. This hotel room I had was not quiet. The fan in the a-c would turn off and on even though I had it turn on high and not auto. I was put near the elevator and heard it arrive, depart, hear how much fun the occupants were going to have. I was also on the third floor and my view was nothing. Thank you Hilton for treating a diamond member like talc.

Friends and I were in town for Whiskey Festival held within walking distance - it was very clean, comfortable and the corner rooms are huge - ask for a higher floor with a view of City Hall and the towers - quiet and worth the money...
We walked to most of what we wanted to, including Reading Terminal Market for a helpful hangover breakfast (thank you Down Home Diner...)
Valet was helpful, as was housekeeping for extra towels...

Located in the middle of Times Square, across from the TKTS bleachers. Ground floor features a very nice-sized welcome area with a guard who checks room keys before you proceed to -rd floor. -rd floor fatures check-in, bar with tvs, etc. We NEVER had to wait for an elevator. Three elevators lead from ground to -rd floor, then upper floors accessible by at least - elevators. We had --th floor with a nice view of times square. We walked to Emipre State Bldg-Macy's, to Lion King (across the street - HELLO!), subways are VERY convenient (went to WTC and Yankees Stadium), walked to FAO, -th ave, Rockefeller Center, to Central Park, Radio City Music Hall, Daisy May's BBQ, etc.
The room itself is a bit cramped for - people, as the fold-out sofa takes up a large chunk of the living room area when opened up. Service personnel VERY friendly and helpful! Room seemed either too hot or too cold - hard to find the balance at times. Free wi-fi was adequate.
Very QUIET! Never heard the sounds of the city unless you opened the windows. We would stay here again in a heartbeat! McD's next door and easy access to stores, eateries, you name it.

We spent - nights at the Distrikt, arriving very late after a snowstorm got us diverted to Bangor, Maine before finally arriving in NY. The staff were charming, smiling and helpful. Good sized rooms for New York, well appointed (and a great view). Good shower, although would have loved a bath after walking for hours but I understand rooms with bath tubs are rare. Lovely toiletries, only tiny niggle would be that a shower cap (I know, very old fashioned) would have been useful as the shower head cannot really be moved from its high position.
Fabulous linen and comfortable bed. Breakfasts are served with a smile and relatively good value for NY hotels. We'd definitely go back.

I recently returned from a business trip to Dallas. My stay at this hotel could not have been better. Spacious, clean rooms (complete with chocolates on your pillow every night), an extremely friendly staff, and a location convenient to downtown. Plus, a free shuttle brings you anywhere you want to go AND picks you up (within a few mile radius). If I go back to Dallas, I will most definitely stay at this hotel again!! Thanks :)

I needed a room for a business trip to the downtown area (which was booked solid). Room was a surprise -- modern, clean, renovated bathroom. Fresh. Amazing bed -- really, one of the best I've ever been in -- soft, plump pillow, great linens. I took a shower at -pm, and the water temp wasn't hot enough. Free wifi, Aveda products. Would have appreciated a bottle of water in the room, but there are glasses and a kitchen down the hall. Be sure to get here by -pm -- their concierge closes then, and you don't want to be locked out. Concierge opens at --am, so there is a key drop.

On arriving at the Four Seasons we were met by pleasant and smiling staff - always a good start. We were upgraded to a superior room, a nice surpise, and Laura at the check-in desk could not have been more helpful!
A special thanks to Blanca at the concierge desk, whose help went above and beyond my expectations.
The room had a vast view of the city and made it easy to plan for whatever weather was coming our way! What can one say about the bed...was easily the most comfortable bed I've been in and the room and amenities were second to none. Attention to detail ranks high in my book, from the earplugs supplied at turn down to the toiletries-accesories provided in the fitness centre. 
While there were some renovation works going on, they made no impact to our stay - always plenty of hot water, room was quiet, and didn't see any workmen.
The location was ideal for shopping and sightseeing and will very much be planning another stay there in the future.

There was not one real big issue with this stay but a number of small ones. The location of the hotel is in a dissolute area ( I saw a group of homeless people hanging out across the street.) There were not any restaurants in the area. At the hotel there was a car with a broken out rear window parked in the parking lot all weekend. The carpet in the hallways was frayed and torn in several places and left as a tripping hazard. The room was okay however there was only one small trash bin in our room and the mattress needs to be thrown out. One of the selling points for us was the indoor pool however it was to cold to swim in and enjoy. The front desk was friendly but limited in helpfulness. Since we were using the sofa bed we needed extra pillows and a blanket, I was only able to attain one pillow because that is what they happened to have behind the desk. There had been free coffee when we checked in but apparently when the restaurant is open they do not offer it. On Sunday morning I waited at the desk to check-out and was informed that all I had to do was leave the keys in the room. This information would have saved a lot of time. Also I did not receive a final tally or receipt from my stay. I do not know what my final charge was.

Not even close to the Riverwalk. I got this hotel through Hotwire, and was really disappointed. Hotwire really needs to provide a safety rating and specify whether the hotel has interior or exterior corridors. We did not feel safe at this hotel. Arrived late and the manager had the lobby locked and we had to check in through a window outside while people were walking by on the street. When walking to the room, we had to go past two people arguing and cursing at each other on the steps. The room was ok. The plug in the bathroom did not work, so the hairdryer was unusable because it was attached to the wall. The hotel is near the freeway, and there is very little if any soundproofing. The cars were very loud. We would also hear the tv from the room below us. I would not recommend this hotel. If I had not prepaid for the room, I would have gone somewhere else.

The reviews I read prior to staying here made me hesitant about the visit and in terms of the area I would say to be careful and don't walk around at night unless you are in a group.
Having said that the room I stayed in was large and facing away from the street was quiet - bed was super comfortable but as noted in a few other reviews the decor is certainly dated. Check in earlier than -pm and you are charged a fee but being Thanksgiving weekend and very quiet the receptionist waived it which was appreciated.
In terms of location for access to downtown it was great - easy walk to the Civic Center (again only walk during the daylight hours) and in the evening there was a bus route that went directly past the hotel.
One thing I struggled with was the restaurant - there was a sign displaying the opening hours for each day (although arriving Thanksgiving Day I was unsuprised to find it closed) but then it randomly closed on the Sunday too when I got back late from a day tour and could really have done with eating in the hotel. However the pub across the road, suggested by the receptionist, was great. 
Generally speaking in fact the staff were very friendly and helpful.
Would recommend to anyone going to Denver on a budget but just take note of the neighbourhood concerns.

Here are the positive aspects first. The location is unbeatable and the park views are outstanding. The lobby, bar, breakfast, elevators, concierge, and staff were adequate. 
Our room had a flat screen tv and great internet connection, but no refrigerator.
Our room did not have a shower curtain, mattress pad, or bottom sheet. These were problems that could be corrected. The decor was dreadful. The furniture and carpet were very worn and stained. The bathroom needed updating (badly). So it just felt dirty whether it actually was or not.
However, some in our party had nicer rooms which had been somewhat updated. Their rooms were blue, and they had a city view. Our rooms were red, and there was not a view. The prices were the same.
The halls also need updating.
I've stayed at this hotel many times over the years because of the location and the price. I thought the decor was tacky and gaudy even when it was new, so it's just not my taste. But now it's just too worn out.
The location is so perfect that many things can be overlooked. But I won't be back until there is a renovation.

This was my first stay at Barton Creek resort. It was more beautiful than the pictures. I arrived late on my first night's stay & it was raining. Checkin was so quick & prompt, but I was the only one in line. Upon entering my room, I noticed that it was very cold inside & I just thought that the heat wasn't turned on. I walked over to my balcony & noticed that the door was standing open. I called the front desk to voice my concern & they sent up an attendant & a manager. I didn't want to stay in this particular for security reasons & within -- minutes the staff had moved me to another room. The rooms are absolutely gorgeous - interior design, furniture, etc. are so beyond comparision to any other hotel; not to mention all the live deer that are standing on both sides of the little lane that goes up to the hotel (I love animals).

Everyone was friendly at check in. Room was great! Nice and clean. Bed was very comfortable! Unfortunately, we had an emergency at home and had to leave at -:--pm the same night. Fully expecting to have to pay the full hotel rate, they very kindly charged us only half, no questions asked!! We have stayed at a different hotel, in a different state, and when we had to leave that same night due to our son being sick, they would not refund us a dime. 
Although our stay was VERY short, we had a wonderful experience. We would DEFINITELY stay here again!! (Hopefully for a full night next time). :)

This place is perfect for us, myself and - children -- and --. We had a - room suite which was huge, modern, clean, full kitchen, balcony overlooking the pool. So much better than a typical hotel room for several days. The staff is as advertised, friendly, attentive, helpful, and especially nice to the children. They came out with popsicles while sitting by the pool.They let us take towels to the beach, fresh cucumber water always in the lobby. How nice is that. As for the location for what we wanted to do it was perfect. The only locational drawback is that it is on a busy street and while we were not facing the street we were - room back on the side and road noise can be bothersome. They should install better windows which would curtail the problem. We had a great vacation. Thank you.

We stayed here recently for both Business and Pleasure. We checked in on Wednesday ( -----) and checked out on Friday (-----), We then checked back in on Friday (-----) and out Sunday morning (-----) keeping our business and personal stays separate. I heard the desk clerk tell the Housekeeper (Amanda) we were a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""stay over"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and to clean our room appropriately. The room was not cleaned until late in the afternoon after I called Housekeeping. Housekeeping said they had no record that I was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""stay over"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Also despite leaving out the empty tissue box on the bathroom counter for two days, I had to go to the front desk to re-plenish our tissue supply. Despite the number of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""suits"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" walking around (which is bothersome in itself since one always felt watched) these houskeeping problems are rather basic and could be handled with more effective oversight.
The breakfast and other amenities were fine, but overshadowed by bad basic housekeeping.

I stayed at this hotel recently because of the seven positive reviews and they were all correct. The hotel nice. I will refrain from restating the positive comments. My issues are these; the rooms are small. I had a one bedroom suite. It had a bedroom barely bigger than the king bed. Master bath was tiny. The sitting room was connected to the kitchen. Again, pretty small. The $--- a night that I paid is a premium in that market. The following week I decided to try something different. The brand new Cambria has similar rooms at $-- which doesn't include breakfast. Cambria is a full service hotel like a Marriott. Homewood is pretty close to an extended stay type operation at a full service hotel price.

We planned to stay for two nights, but left after one. The hotel was dated and dirty. Linens were old and dingy. The double beds were so old and worn that we rolled to the middle of the bed. They were VERY uncomfortable. The room was extremely small, with just room to walk around the beds. Road noise was high. The elevators are very old, and the sensors don't work properly. If you aren't careful, the door will hurt you. Watch out! The location is somewhat central, but it's ugly. All of the equipment in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""fitness center"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was broken in one way or another. On the bright side, most of the staff was nice, but the manager made up for it. She refused to take care of a parking ticket their hired service issued despite the fact that we were guests and parked legally in a space in their garage. She said she could take care of it, but that she wouldn't. (Huh??) It made no sense then and still doesn't. We went to another hotel, which was clean, bright, friendly and cheaper! There are MUCH better options!!!

We had a nice one-night stay at Hampton Inn. Location (SoHo) is convenient for sightseeing, although the closest subway station only serves local (-) trains, that might be obvious for New Yorkers, but for -st time visitors it's a bit confusing.
The hotel itself is really nice, housed in a relatively new tower building. Rooms are quite small, but that's NY standard. Our room was on the --th floor, comfortable with a nice bathroom, free wireless and cabled internet, big plasma TV. The bed comfortable, the only disturbing factor at night was the noise of the heating-AC, but you may turn it off if the outside temperature is comfortable.
Our breakfast was included, nice choice of bagels, eggs, bread, ham, juice and coffee-tea. Btw. coffee and tea are available round the clock.
The hotel has a small bar at the entrance with a discount for hotel guests.
Staff is very helpful, smiling all the time.

Just been on a two week holiday with the family and we stayed here for - nights.Firstly the hotel is in prime location for all downtown attractions, restaurents etc.It is a good -- min walk to the USS Midway and -- min walk to Petco Park the home of the Padres (depending on the traffic signals). Secondly the hotel has just had a makeover and it is very smart indeed. When we arrived, check-in was fast and efficient but when we found our room the beds were not made and we asked for a rollaway bed and unfortunately they don't supply rollaways in a double queen room. We reported the state of the room and the fact we didn't have a rollaway and the hotel manager couldn't do enough to help us feel comfortable and it was quickly resolved by giving us a room with a king size which slept - of us and they could supply a rollaway for our -- year old son. It wasn't ideal but we were happy with their efforts. On top of this they gave us a $-- credit to use in the bar or restaurant.The hotel pool was on the -rd floor and it was a great way to cool off after spending a day sightseeing. The charming concierge lady was extremely helpful and knowledgable about the area and pointed us in the right direction when needed. 
All in all I would recommend this hotel for a small family or couples.

We stayed here on a business trip. The hotel is on the -th floor, so you enter at the bellhop area, then have to take a ride in an elevator, then have to shlep down a marble hallway and turn left before you even see the check in desk. Other than that the hotel is very swanky.
The rooms are large and well appointed. The bathrooms are lovely. The price to stay there is astronomical. If a business wasn't paying for it I don't see how the normal person could justify the $----night cost.
If we were being put up again in Chicago and it was at this hotel, I would be a happy camper.

We stayed at the Hotel Pennsylvania (New York) for - nights. The room was big, but very old bathroom and not clean at all. This Hotel is very well located, downtown NY, just in front of MSG! You can reach every good place to visit by walk. But, they really need to fix-upgrade their bathrooms soon...

I was in NYC for New Years with - friends. We had actually booked a different Hotel (our -st choice) and they could not accomodate us for the full stay so we had to book -nights of our stay at the Belevedere. This was a blessing in desguise. The first hotel Sucked to make it brief. We walked fron the other hotel to the belvedere which was only - blocks away. Upon arrival to the Belvedere the bellman came to meet us almost --- way down the block when he saw us comming. I was very impressed as the previous hotel has hardly acknowleged our arrival. Even though it was - hours before check in and we were not able to get in to our room yet (we expected this) they got us started with check in the process and stored our luggage. The receptionis went out of her way to help us with reccomendations as to were we can go for breakfast. Upon return for Checkin mid day they atually recognized us coming in!!!! We were greeted and they had everything ready to go. Our room was great; clean, very comfortable and decently roomy for manhattan standards. The bellman delivered our lugagge and checked the heater for us and made sure we were comfortable and familiar with all the ammenities in the room including how to operate our heater. We quickly became familiar with all the staff and they greeted us by name. One morning as we were leaving they actually gave us very nice coffee thermoses to take with us. I still keep mine on my desk. 
We found on our trip that Customer service for some New Nork establishments is a far off westcoast hippie concept. It was a great relief to find that all the staff (reception, bellstaff, housekeeping, concirege, etc) at The Belvedere knows the true meaning of Customer service. We felt we were among friends. 
Also it was a short walk from times square (vital if you're there for NYE.) Broadway and the fashion district, and the a couple of blocks from the Metro. BTW if you like Cajun The Delta Grill is a must. Great recommendation by the staff. The concirege also helped us set up great tickets to hard to get shows. .
It was an epic trip only enhanced by our experience at this hotel. We will definately be staying here again when we visit.

This is a great, boutique hotel. Very small, with even a smaller pool area, but not lacking in entertainment. It seems to be a hot spot for young, single people. The restaurant; Dragon Fly was excellent, but for my money, I like a more subtle ambiance instead of a retro-scence for young hipsters & hipster wanna-be's. If you're with your spouse, you may want to try something down the street for a bit more R & R.

Very friendly hotel. The restaurant (Saha) is worth a mention as the food is outstanding - Middle Eastern food. The only downside is the room had a bath which needed a bleaching but overall the room was well equiped and cozy. Also, the daily wine tasting was a good touch.

Just arrived home from Edgewater. Many comments are as noted. Rooms are small but nicely appointed. Loved the fireplace to take the chill off. We stayed city side and YES there were trains all day and night. They never blew a whistle but you could hear the dinging of the guardrails. This did not bother us as much as a loud crowd yelling outside our last night. Rose and Hilda were our housekeepers and they attended to our every request. We did look at a waterview but decided it was not worth the extra $$$ as you could sit in the bar or lobby and have the same view. PARKING.........OMG wow OK so we knew it was $-- plus tax a night and only Valet parking is offerred. When I paid my bill, parking came out to be just under $-- night. There was a parking garage across the street for $-- and parking on the street is free from -p--a. Look around this was a big big suprise and I am glad we moved our after - nights. The Valet guys were great and offered a shuttle until - pm but it departs hourly on the hour. We just could not seem to make the hours! We were in the bar - restaurant nightly. If you go ask for Judy. She is fabulous and makes sure everything is up to speed! Beside the parking...... the hotel was remodeling and laying new carpet. A bit of inconvenience and workers left glue, unlaid carpet, and etc. on the floor just outside the elevator. It would have been nice if the hotel would have said we are remodeling and as a compensation for the inconvenience offer a better room or coupons for the bar or dinner. Then we would not have felt imposed upon so much. Overall the hotel was clean and has a nice NW atmosphere. The staff was courteous and friendly. There is a Starbucks in the giftshop and they offered free refills on coffee. The coffee in the room is aweful! The refrigerator in the room was well stocked but we emptied and placed our own leftovers and drinks inside. We did not know they had a pool until I just read other reviews. I would recommend this place. We did priceline and received a very good rate $--

Really don't want to rave about the Blue Moon too much as I'd like to be able to get a room next time I'm in New York, but in fairness I have to recommend this place. It is quirky and quaint, comfortable and homely, great staff, breakfast bagels that could fill you up to dinner let alone lunch and situated in a fantastic neighbourhood of little bars, restaurants and shops and within walking distance to lots of other fabulous neighbourhoods too. We had the smallest of their rooms, endearingly called 'Ella Fitzferald' but that was very generously sized, the shower was wonderful and the bed very comfortable. We loved this place and New York and will be doing our best to get back again soon. No need to spend weeks trying to find the right hotel this time, we know where we want to stay!

Location - Just off Times Square, funky & eclectic modern lobby and reception area. -th Ave to the west had plenty of cheaper Irish pubs, bars and restaurants than the ones around Times Square, all within walking distance and the neighbourhood felt safe.
Staff - Our tour operator managed to completely balls up our booking and misinform the hotel of our room requirements and duration. The guy on the front desk was happy to help and speak to them on the phone and sort it out so we could get to our rooms ASAP. There is always a doorman available, plus discreet (black turtleneck sweaters, black trousers) security at night checking everyone that entered to see whether they had a room keycard. Always a nice touch to keep out the riff-raff. 
Room - Average size for NYC, can't complain. Clean, comfortable beds with ample pillows and cushions, flat screen TV, small bathroom but good shower and plenty towels and bath-products. Our friends asked for extra towels and this caused no problems at all.
Facilities - Dean & Deluca Coffee Shop always handy for that wake up shot for weary travellers. If you want inferior cheaper coffee there's a small Italian deli food place next door. We never used the bar or restaurant as there's better & cheaper places in the city, get out and explore!

“S” stands for sorry because everyone working at this facility seems to be sorry or apologize for something. Having stayed at a few other W properties I had high expectations of this hotel.
As a Platinum member of the SPG program I expected a priority Check In line. Since there wasn´t any I approached a clerk and she said she could check me in right away. Other guest in line started complaining and because she couldn´t handle this guest I opted to make the line and wait for my turn.
When I asked the clerk about the priority check in for preferred guests she said that W hotels did not provide this benefit, something that is not true. She and the Welcome Desk manager were sorry for the inconveniences.
Imagine my surprise the following morning to see a priority check in sign up at the Welcome Desk.
Suite was big, nice view of the lake, very comfortable. Bathtub wasn´t properly cleaned and room amenities were incomplete for the duration of my stay and the AC worked at times. I contacted Welcome Desk to let them know about these and again they were sorry.
Lobby Bar and Whiskey Sky were great. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Drinks were quick to come. 
The whatever-whenever service was mixed. I asked the clerk on the first day to book dinner reservations and he simply didn´t call to confirm, I had to approach him on the lobby on my way out to find out he couldn´t book it, he was sorry. On the other hand, the guy that was “on duty” on the second day was extremely helpful, as he managed a way to get us a spot on the restaurant I wanted and provided me the service I expected from Whatever-whenever.
I also booked a car and the fee I was charged was way over what Whatever-whenever confirmed to me. It´s been over a month of my stay and I still have not been reimbursed that money. I contacted the hotel and one more time they were sorry but they simply didn´t do anything to try to make it right.

We have stayed here over many years - and the consistent good service, nice rooms etc are one of the main reasons we keep going back. We always go for the imperial floor where internet and snacks are included. That somehow makes the high price bearable :-) Breakfast has a lot of Japanese items that most people will not want after a first try... so the breakfast is now looking weak compared to other buffets available. Plus only the adults staying get breakfast included in the rate we get. Free breakfast in the imperial floor is OK as the view is amazing. Fridge is annoying (auto-charge). Bathrooms fantastic.

It has been over -- years since I last stayed in a Hilton. I avoided them because the rooms are tiny and the rates aren't. So, when work booked me into this hotel I thought it would be a good way to re-evaluate the chain without it coming out of my pocket.
The location is great. The lobby is big and active. Check in was OK - they had a computer malfunction that took a few minutes to rectify.
After a hike to my elevator, I arrived at my room - just steps from the elevator. The room was small. Two double beds - yes, double, not queen - pretty much fill the room. A tub chair filled the entire width between one bed and the window. And like a lot of modern hotels, the sound separation between rooms (and between the room and the passage way) is poor. I heard plumbing noises, TV, and conversations from other rooms, and lots of voices and elevator """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""dings"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" from the passage way.
The rooms were impeccably clean, and staff were always friendly.

Myself and wife stayed here from the --th - --th sept and overall we both really enjoyed our stay. I was apprehensive before arriving after reading some not so complimentary reviews, and after being showed to our room i thought oh no the reviews were correct. 
The room we got had no windows in it and was like a big store room, it was very clean and tidy and probably ok for staying a couple of nights but not for a week. I went to reception and explained this and to my delight was moved asap. The room we were moved to was very stylish, clean, had a window & was peaceful when you wanted to get away from the madness of times square.
Talking of times square it was right around the corner. The hotel could not be in a more central location, it has everything on its doorstep from broadway theatres to restaurants to subway stations that take you all over the city.
And a special mention has to go to the girls at reception and the door men who couldn't have been any more helpful, this hotel really has a personnel touch about it that most NYC hotels dont and i wouldnt hesitate in recommending to anyone.

Having booked through my travel agent I began to have reservations with regard to his assurances that it was not like the Hudson, which had I not thought was so terrible I would have thought its faux funkiness was laughable. hotel issuperb location. Staff at door most welcoming, reception smotth and courteous. Room was perfect for three of us. Lovely furnishings. No view.but compensated by ipad and free wi fi. Stayed on with no problem with transition. Staff most helpful.
Would most certainly stay there again.
Had a great one-night stay in a very large room with harbor views. Perhaps a little disappointed with the breakfast but otherwise highly recommended.

I was very disappointed with my experience at Affinia Dumont in mid-December. I had booked a Suite for one night to celebrate my mother's --th birthday. The manager did not come out from the back at all during this whole ordeal except to handle the paperwork to finally transfer us to Affinia Manhattan, a hotel of lower quality. This hotel is very well located, just a medium walk or short cab ride from Times Square, or Columbus Circle, and central enough that it is never too far from SoHo, Flatiron, or the Museum of Natural History.
The design is great, with great decor, and very comfortable furniture, especially the bed. The rooms are huge for NYC standards, with giant bathrooms, great views, and decent amenities. However, the shades are far from """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""blackout"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" so if you're a light sleeper, you may want to bring an eye mask. Didn't bother us though.
The rooftop lounge has great views and a neat design aesthetic as well, though there was a fair share of cheesballs hanging out there. The drinks and oysters were great, though a bit pricy, especially considering how inexpensive the hotel is. It was also a bit odd to need to take the elevator down to the lobby from our room in order to go up to the lounge. No direct access from hotel floors. 
As with all Kimpton properties, the wine hour is always nice, and they are very pet friendly. However, there were quite a few service missteps...
First, when we pulled up, no one helped us with our luggage or out of the car. Eventually, after a few minutes the valet came over to park our car (hint: there is a much less expensive self park lot a block before the hotel).
Second, we were assigned to a room that was already occupied. This was very awkward... to try to walk into someone else's room! The front desk gave us the correct room and keys, with an apology, but didn't seem to think it was a big deal.
Third, we called down to have our car brought around -- minutes before leaving, and were told it would take only --. After -- minutes of standing in -- degree heat, with our dogs, I asked the doorman how long it would take... turns out guest services never relayed the request to the valet. So another -- minutes of waiting. As compensation the hotel waived one day of parking charges. 
So, overall a good hotel, but three pretty serious (and un-kimpton-like) gaffes in the service department. Still, given the size of the rooms, and the very low price, I would go back.

Located almost on site to Universal Studios and Walk and its stores.
Taxi from LAX c $------ but the shuttles are chaeper but may take longer. In Theory, you could do it by subway if limited luggage is your - the subway is just at the bottom of the hill (-- min walk)
Weekends feel very different to weekdays due to families-visitors for the Studios.
Bit out of the way if not visiting Universal or local Burbank area.

Not somewhere I would stay again, pictures on website are not what we got. We stayed five nights, ugh, only because nothing else was available. Maid was re-using towels we had on the floor, hanging them back up like they were never used. Very small bathroom and bedroom area. Beds and pillows were very uncomfortable. We encountered a baseball team having a BBQ everynight in the parking lot, very loud and office did nothing. Pool and Jacuzzi area was dirty, never any towels to be found. Breakfast was ok. A few restaurants nearby and easy access to freeway was good.

I stay at this Holiday Inn Express two to three times a month for business in Memphis. The staff is always friendly, and they do a good job at breakfast. 
The location is good for me because many of my customers are within a short drive from the hotel.
My main complaint with this HIE location is the condition of the rooms and the hallways. It is time for some remodeling and general repairs. Little things are broken or in disrepair all over the hotel - from toilet paper holders and shower heads and shower curtain brackets in bathrooms, to doors on furniture. Also - many of the rooms in this hotel are VERY SMALL. 
The rate is generally well over $---.--. I am not sure why the information on tripadvisor says $--.-- rates. I have not paid less than $---.-- in several years at this hotel.
If you are looking for a good location for many of the tourist sites in Memphis TN this hotel may work well for you. 
Personally, in the last few months I have avoided staying here for business and have been choosing other Holiday Inn properties in Memphis ( I am a Platinum Priority member and like the points program) that are not quite as convenient because of the overall quality and costs. Although I miss the convenience of this location, there are a few other hotels that work out, and are about the same rate.

One of the nicer Choice Properties in the CLT area, Very Clean & Comfortable Rooms. Nice Spacious Breakfast Bar. Accomodating Staff. I have no complaints. Would definitely stay again & also recommend. Convenient to the highway, the mall & PF Changs:)
Party central right in the heart of downtown Austin. Nice place but BEWARE, they charge $-- per night for PARKING! I got a great deal on Hotwire but in the end it wasn't that great of a deal.

As a Diamond HHonors member, I have stayed at many of their brands around the world. This property is in a good location, close to the subway and friendly and attentive staff. Only downside was that they do not provide free breakfast like other HGIs I have stayed at. Rooms are small, but average size for NYC. With few rooms on each floor is it nice to be close to the elevator, but not have to hear any noise - was handy with a big suitcase. Would def consider staying again, if needed to be near Chelsea area of NYC.
Clean, quiet room, free wi-fi and breakfast plus a reasonable room rate, what else good a tried traveler desire.

This place is inexpensive & you get a lot for what you pay for. The restaurant downstairs has been refurbished & runs very efficiently now ( much improved from last year!) The amenities are pretty nice.. comfy bed, great TV, iPod dock on the alarm clock and just a generally pleasant place to stay and it won't ding your wallet like some of the comparable places nearby. I'd highly recommend it!

We stayed at the Affinia -- from --th---th Jan. and the hotel lived up to its high rating on this site. 
Rooms - were clean and big with a huge bed which was super comfy. Our first room (---) had a great view of -rd Ave but was a bit noisy with the traffic below however we were changed (---) without a problem but the view was also lost.
Staff - were always helpful and every question was answered even if it took a bit of research to establish the answer. Guys at the door were super friendly and helped us feel really welcome as did the reception staff.
This hotel really made our short stay even more enjoyable. This was our -rd trip to the city and we would recommend this hotel to anybody if they want somewhere to stay to enhance their trip.

My wife had stayed here before so we elected to stay here on layover while in transit from Paris to Minnesota. We booked the hotel on Hilton Honors points so cost was not a factor. Our room ( slight bay view on -th floor) was nice bu nothing special. My daughter told mevthe pool was quite good. However: room service was slow, and the food was a disgrace. Parking prices ($-- per night) are insane even for Boson. Finally, in world where free wifi is rapidly becoming expected by clients, at this hotel Internet is available for a fee. I have stayed at numerous Hiltons and sadly report that this is one of my least favorites. The only outstanding aspect of this hotel is it's proximity to Logan.

Great location - close to theaters, Times Square and Hudson River, and directly across the street from Port Authority bus station. Rooms are very comfortable and well-appointed. Most notably, all of the staff were extremely friendly and personable. Chris, manager in reservations, was fantastic.

I am in Jacksonville too often, but not often enough to justify the fact that I have probably tried three dozen hotels (Incuding Amelia and Ponte Vedra). Jacksonville is not heavy on the downtown hotel scene. Most properties are located along I--- south of the city with a cluster at the airport as well. I was a Hilton downtown waterfront loyalist until it became a Crown Plaza and the option then were a horrible radison, a out of the way Omni and the Adams Mark ugggh!
Hyatt took over the premium location that was the Adams Mark and although I could not bring myself back to that property for over a decade, I did recently return to the scene of the crime.
Hyatt has done a wonderful job with the property, not major renovations, but through a better staff including from desk, housekeeping and food. The valet is wonderful and not a bad view while you wait for your car, sometimes I have language barrier with the front desk staff, but they try to compensate, by alway being helpful and friendly. I recomend the side wing, with larger rooms, longer walk, but quiet and away from the hustle and bustle of the very busy lobby. The property has a rare treat too, in addition to a coffee shop, they have an attached Einstien Bagels attached to the back of the property. Outside restaurants are a walk, but a very pleasant one and you can even take a ferry to the Ruth's Chris or a entertainment area with bars and burger joints. Big improvement, I will look forward to staying again.

I'm not sure I understand some of the lesser reviews, before you stay at Yotel, you must have some idea of it's mission statement right? So If you plan to stay at Yotel NYC, you will have a great visit. Just spent a couple nights there and it is truly super. For a Hotel that provides human free kiosk check in and out, the staff is amazingly attentive. You are always greeted warmly, and the mission control staff is super helpful. Location is great, just blocks from times square, great restaurants in Hell's Kitchen etc. The hotel has cool fun spaces everywhere to hang out especially the roof deck. The rooms are smartly designed and comfortable, as if Apple designed a hotel room. Will stay here exclusively in the future...

Had lunch today with client. Very disappointing with shrimp salad, drowning
in mayo-catchup dressing. Small salad shrimp with no taste on iceberg lettuce
at $--.----pathetic. Client had Thai beef tenderloin (medallions)--oh so small.
Friendly waiters, empty restaurant on a Friday at noon. Guess the word is out.

We (- adults and - children) stayed in the hotel for a night catching an early flight. The room was clean and spacy and the beds comfortable. The breakfast very good. The shuttle service to the airport was convenient and efficient. The hotel is on the way from some rental car firms to the airport. The bus driver dropped us off the hotel after we return the car. We would stay here again.

Felt like an old warehouse on the floors rather than a nice hotel. Nice lobby but you don't stay in the lobby. Had to walk for years to get to my room and it was loud outside my door during part of the days.

Absolute luxury. The most comfortable bed I've ever slept in, a fantastic view facing NJ, a prime Times Square location (with no traffic noise) and outstanding service from the staff. Cannot recommend this hotel highly enough.

My husband and I have stayed at the Hotel Commonwealth several times in the past and have always enjoyed it. This past weekend was spent with our two young children and after our experience, we couldn't help but to write a review. Hotel Commonwealth is, without a doubt, the BEST hotel you will experience while staying in Boston. The accommodations are luxurious, the convenient location cant be beat, and the choices and quality of the restaurants and is fantastic. What prompted this review, however, is how friendly and helpful each and every employee is. From the housekeepers who set up the crib to the waitress in the restaurant....I even lost my cell phone only to have the doorman find it for me within - minutes (under the seat of my car!!!) Will most definitely be returning to our 'home away from home.""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""!!!!

We spent two nights (a Friday and Saturday) at the Hilton Hill Country in late June ----. We have three children; ages -, - and - months. We had a suite, number ---, and our overall experience was very good.
We checked in on Friday evening around -:-- p.m. This is one area where they could definitely use some improvement. I waited in a very long line. They did have every computer manned with an employee, and Aubrey was very friendly and helpful when I finally got to her, but this process took entirely too long. (When you’re tired from traveling and you have cranky kids, the last thing you want to do is stand in line in a hotel lobby.)
Our room was very nice. King bed – the most comfortable hotel bed I’ve slept on – and nice water pressure with plenty of hot water in both the walk-in shower and the jetted tub. I did notice that the hot water in the sinks did not appear to work, but it wasn’t a necessity for us so I didn’t call about it. Plenty of luxurious towels in the bathroom. Flat screen tv in both the bedroom and the living area. These two rooms are separated by a double door. One thing that my entire family noticed is how quiet and well insulated the rooms are. We never heard a sound from any of the other guests – no doors slamming, no traffic in the hall, etc. It was very, very quiet. We all slept very well. Room came with a mini frig, but no microwave. That would have been a nice feature for us to heat our baby’s bottles.
The free shuttle to Sea World is SO nice. It begins running at -:-- a.m. (or thirty minutes before Sea World opens) and they take you right up to the front gates. No walking a mile across the parking lot; no paying $---day in parking. They will also pick you back up from the front gates – the shuttle picks up on the hour. The drivers are all super friendly and very informative. They provide a lot of information about the local area and will also give you some “fun facts” about Sea World. You get to bypass a lot of the car traffic waiting to get in the Sea World parking lot as well.
We spent some time in the pool areas one evening. I agree with several other posts on here – the pool water was not as clean as I would prefer. However…I noticed a number of children who were not being well attended by their parents as well as several bar patrons bringing their beverages into the pool. These two factors almost inevitably increase the litter. The fire pits were very nice, and I saw a number of people roasting marshmallows. The “play area”-playground consists of one small climb-on playset with a slide.
Breakfast buffet was okay – nothing special – but they charge a whopping $--.-- per person. Unless you receive this as a comp for being a Hilton Honors member, I would definitely skip it. There are a number of restaurants nearby where you can eat equal or better food for MUCH less.
Local calls incur a service charge – it ends up being a little over a dollar with the taxes. We ordered a pizza one evening from a local pizza shop called Presto Pizza (their flier was in our room). I would also recommend skipping that. If I had known they were going to stick us for a buck plus on the phone calls, I would have used my cell phone. The pizza tasted like something served in a school cafeteria and took over an hour to get.
Housekeeping did a good job. Our room was clean and, when we left a note asking for extra blankets, they were there waiting on us when we got back from day one at Sea World. Our housekeeper (whose name I do not know, unfortunately) folded our two year old’s bedding and even “tucked in” his stuffed animal. We thought that was a very sweet thing to do.
I also agree with a few other posts that I would not necessarily refer to this place as a “resort”. We did not utilize the spa services, so I can’t attest to those, but this hotel was a bit smaller and did not offer the full array of services-amenities that I would refer to as a “resort”. However, if you’re going to Sea World, this is a convenient and nice place to stay. The shuttle is such a great time and money saver. If we return to Sea World in San Antonio, we will go back to the Hilton.
Pros: VERY comfortable bed, great shower and bath, extremely quiet rooms, free shuttle to and from Sea World, nice outdoor area with fire pits, free parking
Cons: VERY slow check in, expensive breakfast, charge for local calls, no free internet-WiFi in rooms, pool water could use improvement
Added tip: We found out after we checked out that there is a nice walking trail somewhere behind the hotel property.

We stayed here before flying out of IAH and it was perfect. The hotel is an updated La Quinta and had comfortable mattresses and the room was pretty spacious. The hotel provides a nice continental breakfast and complimentary shuttles to-from the airport. We will stay here again before flying out of IAH.

I satyed at the Sheraton on the Bay in San Diego for a week long business trip and decided to go downtown to get some groceries. When I returned with -- bags of groceries there were not more carts left at the concierge desk. When Claudio Arreola, the security guard, saw me standing on the curb waiting for a free cart he promptly asked if he could help me carry the bags to my room. Everyone at this hotel has been so friendly and helpful during the stay. Top notch!
Glen McDonald

This Farifield Inn at ---- Macon Cove, Memphis, TN is without a doubt, one of the WORST Hotels I have ever stated at and I am a World traveler.
The staff were INCREDIBLY RUDE, the parking lot is not lite up at night and is in a very dangerous neighbourhood.
STAY AWAY FROM THIS HOTEL AT ALL COST!!!

We stayed twice at the Westin - once the day we arrived into Detroit and once the day we were leaving. This hotel is brilliant for relieving the stress and weariness of air travel. The beds were the most comfortable I had ever slept in and the shower was brilliant. The first time we stayed we had a room looking out onto the airport and I much preferred that. There was no noise at all, an interesting view and some daylight! This was my only problem with this hotel - it was difficult to see daylight - everything was very dim and I think you could probably have a whole stay there without seeing the sky. The second time we stayed we had an inside room, looking over the lobby. The room and beds and shower were still all brilliant, but I much preferred the outside room. Service was very good and the food excellent, although expensive. Lesson - do not use your room phone to make even a short international call - I was charged about $-- for less than - minutes!

My wife and I recently spent five nights at this Hotel after reading all of the previous negative reviews, we decided that they were probably whiners and complainers. We were right. We chose this hotel for several reasons, close to airport, centrally located to downtown and the beaches, Ocean, Mission and Pacific. We also chose this hotel because we are Best Western points collectors and don't like to spend tons of $$ on rooms that you mostly just sleep and shower in. We were not disappointed on any of our requirements. The hotel (not apartment) has been obviously recently updated, clean, fresh, new furniture. We had a harbor view room, great view but in our late forties we had no problem standing (due to lack of furniture) to enjoy the view. The road noise is mostly in the peak rush hour times but did no bother us. At check in we were given a rate that was different than we booked, easily rectified with my confirmation print out, at no time did I feel that I was being ripped off, I put it down to initially booking with the National call center and then adding a night and taking part in a more recent --% off promo for Best Western Rewards members by calling the hotel directly. The front desk staff was always friendly, courteous and helpful. The hotel was very clean, our room as well, nice King with fridge and microwave, no water problems. The cleaning staff did use an air freshener in the rooms and hallways that I requested to not be used in our room and they honored this request with out a problem. The breakfast provided was up to Best Western standards, pastries, waffle makers, apples, oranges, toast, cereals, breakfast burritos, three kinds of juice, tea and coffee (Starbucks). We found it very easy to get to downtown and the beaches from here, get a proper street map the tourist ones are not detailed enough. We used the computer in the lobby for local information and to check email from our kids, possibly a sign limiting use would be helpful, some people don't seem to like to share. We used the hot tub, very clean and well maintained. We don't understand what some people expect for reasonably priced hotels, if they want a resort go to one and pay for it. We would recommend this hotel and will stay there again when we return to San Diego in the future.

Liked the hotel, staff and service. Restaurants and shops are within walking distance an it is safe to walk. The hotel has a cozy feel to it and the executive lounge has really good service. I enjoy HiltonHHonors Diamond status and was given a room away from the ice machine and elevator as requested. Little did I know that I was right above the loading dock for the restaurant and close to the garbage containers. At -:-- a.m the garbage truck came and picked up the garbage. Once the containers were empty they slammed them down on the ground. This took over -- minutes to empty all containers. Then at -:-- a.m. the deliveries for the hotel arrived. All I could hear was BEEEP BEEEP BEEEP when the trucks were backing into the loading dock that was - floors below my room.
Long story short: Please ask for a room that is not facing S Mendenhall Rd or in other words, ask for a room that is facing the pool. Those are the quiet rooms you want. 
I just wished the front desk staff was aware of these details.
Staff was friendly...rooms were clean and large. Great location for downtown and the parking was great. The only thing it seemed to be missing was a hot tub.

There is a bath room with bath and toilet but a washing basin is in the bedroom together with and queen size bed with still some space around it. There's a cupboard with a flat screenTV and there's no air-conditioning and with a noisy street it's no fun sleeping with a window open. Sheets and bathroom are cleaned every day, no complains about housekeeping- cleaning. The hotel is conveniently - blocks up from Union square. In the lobby you'll find a free coffee machine with excellent coffee and lots of sweet cakes in the morning. Two internet computers are available in the same lobby where the breakfast is served.
Let me put it this way: a simple but clean hotel.

We stayed at the Mercer after spending - nights at the Greenwich hotel (Tribeca – see my review). 
There’s no doubt about it, the Mercer is the place to stay and be seen if you’re in Soho however given the cost and the status of the hotel I think I expected more at times. One example was that I was contacted by concierge the day before via email asking me what time I was arriving. I asked if we could have an early check-in (- p.m.) to which the reply from Matthew Kranz was that the hotel would do their absolute best to try and accommodate us. We arrived at - p.m to be told it was not ready. No problems, we dumped our bags and went to explore Soho. We arrived back at -:-- p.m. and told it still wasn’t ready. Not very happy. 
Having said that the room was amazing - big double bath, walk in shower, massive bed etc, the guys on the door very friendly and helpful especially getting us in to the Submercer for a drink. This is definitely worth a visit trip – very cool. 
The hotel also accommodated a late check for us on the final day making up for the earlier lapse. 
Completely loved the stay but for us it’s the Greenwich everytime.

LIKES: Perfect location! Clean, very nice room facing the courtyard. Hotel staff was very kind and accomodating. Great tray of cheeses and wine...although they were missing crackers :)
We had breakfast brought to the room and everything was very good! Pancakes were tasty!Perfect place for a romantic getaway!
DISLIKES: There was some kind of event going on so a group of guests decided to continue their party at the courtyard which was extremely loud...but after a couple of other guests complained, they left and that was the end of the noise. Other than that nothing!
Valet is expensive, just like with any other hotel, but if you like to walk, then you will not really need a car since the hotel is in a perfect location. There were a couple of public parking garages very close to the hotel though.
We will be coming back to the Valencia hotel for another romantic weekend next year!

I have been coming to New York for a few years now and have always wanted to stay at the Sofitel, but never been able to afford it. Having stayed in the Sofitel in LA (through Hotwire), I decided to splash out and book four nights in (for the price of three) for my daughter and I to celebrate her --th birthday the weekend before Christmas. Our flight was delayed so we arrived in the middle of the night to be welcomed by charming members of staff. The hotel was warm, stylish and inviting and our (upgraded) room was absolutely lovely - very spacious and well equipped. It's true what they say about the beds - they are so comfortable you don't want to get up. The bathroom was large and it was a treat to have a separate shower cubicle. I had also seen on other reviews on TripAdvisor about the damages from Hurricane Ike and the renovation project at the hotel, so I asked for a non-damaged, renovated room. Just to be safe. :) Upon our arrival, the boyfriend and I were greeted by wonderfully attentive staff, who promptly took our bags and put them on a cart. Ah, the rooms. I know there were previous reviews that the rooms were """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""outdated"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", but let me tell you, they have since remedied that! Brand new EVERYTHING - carpet, bed, a very comfortable chaise lounge, an efficient and comfortable workstation area, an alarm clock with iPod docking station, a nice --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" LCD HDTV, wonderfully post-modern art on the walls. The showerhead was one of those rain type showerheads, and it was probably the best shower I've had at a hotel before. I loved it. :) There was a perfect amount of closet space with extra pillows and blankets, and of course an iron and ironing board (which I had to take advantage of, since I'm not the best packer!).

If I could have one complaint about the place, it would be that the hard wired Internet (listed as free on their website) was not available on the --th floor, so we ended up using the wireless for our needs. I don't consider this as much of a hiccup though - I work in the IT field and am very familiar with how the wiring gets done in a multi-story building for Internet access. 
Keep in mind, the Hyatt is very large, so it accomodates well for large groups. Considering that, you will most likely run into tons of people - it was very busy the entire time we were there, and you may have to wait a few minutes for an elevator.
The valet service was professional and efficient. It was so nice to simply pick up the phone and ask for my car, and for it to be brought to me with no issues. Wonderful staff!! 
I loved staying at the Hyatt, and I would definitely do so again. It was such a pleasant experience.

This hotel has a great location (near I---, subway stations, JFK Library) and free parking, but don't expect to spend a weekend in your room. GRAIN OF SALT: This is written from the perspective of a --+ couple that appreciates a little city grit, parties just enough to stay within cab range of concerts, requires a good night's sleep, always books the cheapest room in the joint, and can't pass up a novel vibe. 
Our one-night stay at The Redbury met our requirements with some caveats. We're glad we tried it. 
CITY GRIT: Accept that in this part of Hollywood, you're always within six giant steps of something grungy. Between The Redbury and scrumptious Juicy Burger or the Pantages, expect to step in a little pee and expect a couple of requests for a buck or a smoke, both within acceptable levels of city gritty. 
That said, even if you didn't book a view room (see CHEAPEST ROOM), you shouldn't have to expect in-your-face grit when you sit on your balcony. It felt like we could reach out and touch the adjacent Avalon, with its crumbling façade and stinky, noisy ally. Hey, Redbury - how about collaborating with the Avalon for a quick pressure wash and paint job? No? How about something well within your means to mitigate: (-) Add two more privacy panels to the two already hanging on the balcony and (-) clean up the pigeon poop on the balcony floor every now and again. 
CAB-RIDE CLOSE: This is a terrific base for concerts and theatre. The house ride was available when we were ready to head out to a concert at the Greek. Superior. 
GOOD NIGHT'S SLEEP: No complaints about the mattress or linens, nor did we experience the noise others did, possibly because we stayed on Sunday night. The too-low lighting and the bed's platform… not a match made in heaven, and I have the bruises to prove it. Redemption came in the form of superb quality blackout curtains on the windows and roller blind on the patio door. Nighty-night, sleep tight! 
CHEAPEST ROOM: Having booked the smallest size suite AND requesting super-early check-in the morning after a sell-out, I got exactly what I expected (thus the ugly balcony scene). 
The great thing for the budget-minded is that but for the balcony and square footage (ours was ---+ - who needs more?) the experience (amenities, service) is pretty even across the board. Queue up a little Dark Side of the Moon on the easy-to-use turntable, crank up the AC and the well-positioned ceiling fan, poke through the ample snack baskets, and settle in for some pre-event R&R. Every staff interaction - with valets, house car driver, front desk staff, barista - resulted in engaged, efficient service. 
NOVEL VIBE: With the exception of the front entry area and Cleo, this is a relentlessly dark space, with deep browns, reds, and blacks competing to dominate dimly-lit public spaces, and in so doing, hiding some really nice appointments and people (gosh, sorry, didn't see you sitting there in your black t-shirt on that brown couch under that ---watt bulb). And where was the genius hand that dressed Cleo when it came time to do the suites? You know your suite is dark when even the long expanse of butcher block, glossy white kitchen cabinets, and crisp white bed linens can't make a dent. Unmitigated murk is a novel vibe, and we enjoyed it for a little while. 
Try it for a night. It's the biggest and most unique bang for your buck in this neighborhood.

Typical semi full service suburban hotel that is a bit dated. The hotel was previously a Radisson, and prior to that, a Wyndham Garden Hotel. The rooms and public areas are clean, and sufficient. Nice lounge for an evening cocktail. Very attractive courtyard area. Just fine for a night or two.
Everything was exactly as advertised. Very European boutique hotel feel, yet predictable enough for a business traveler like me. Service was excellent. Very clean.

We stayed here in late October, arriving at -am on a Sunday morning where we greeted (for want of a better expression) by the rudest, grumpiest receptionist you could wish for. Having said that, she proved to be about par for courteousness in New York, I mean, a 'please' and a 'thank you' every now and again would be nice!
Thankfully the rest of our stay was superb. Lovely big room, comfy bed, big TV, broadband internet, beautiful bathroom and a location to die for, just seconds from Times Sq.
We'd also certainly recommend The Muse and it's neighbouring restaurants: 'District' and 'Rosie O'Gradys' - just avoid the receptionist from Hell.

When I checked in I was told I was upgraded to a deluxe room (that just means it's a bit bigger than a standard room). Lots of street noise out my window and a rattling heat-AC vent - even though I asked fir the quietest room they had when I checked in. 
Having said that, the bathroom was large and nicely appointed, and the rest of the room was nice. Roomy, too.

If you are tired of large chrome and glass hotel structures, if you yearn for the charm and quiet luxury of a small and intimate hotel, then The Sorrento is definitely what you are looking for. It is like stepping back in time from the moment you enter, with attentive staff, plenty of wood, and even a roaring fire! The on-site restaurant is elegant and features a wonderful selection. Rooms are comfortable and beautifully appointed. WHAT A DIFFERENCE !!

After a disappointing last trip away I needed luxury and ritz definitely delivered! Food, service, everything to the highest standard, Fantastic!!! If there was a sixth star the ritz would be the first to have it as it flew past the - star mark with ease!

My daughter and I have just returned from a - night stay in Hotel Penn, after reading some of the appalling reviews we were dreading what we might find. The lobby is impressive although very busy, the check in line was short and the desk clerk very helpful and polite. As we exited the elevator on the --th floor the hallway did remind us of 'The Shining'with a very musty smell but once in the room there was no smell at all. The window was stuck open but after a call to housekeeping this was rectified within -- mins. The bedding and towels were very clean and there was lots of hot water. The TV did not work but we had so much to do this didn't matter and the location is excellent, we were able to walk to Times Square in about -- mins and Macys is only one block down. We had a brilliant time and had no problem at all with staff, would reccommend to anyone because of excellent location!!

This La Quinta is wonderful! It looks really new-not sure how long it has been open, but we will definitely stay here again. It is a good price and pet friendly! The room isn't huge but it is comfortable and very clean. Great location with plenty of food options in walking distance or down the road at the mall. The bed was comfortable and breakfast was fine....maybe they could have a few more options,but that isn't really a big priority for me. Overall, very pleased!

The Arizona Grand Resort is an excellent getaway for any family or single couples. The water park has to be the best. Kid friendly and plenty of staff to assist your needs. The rooms are nice, however I would recommend staying in a Villa if you have more than - kids. Only downside would be the $--.-- daily rate for internet access. I can't think of a single hotel-motel that charges for internet access these days.

We stayed here for one night. - adults, - small children). We were lucky to find the last room available: the Presidential suite. The bullet points:

We are local to the area and have stayed here before. This time spent one night in a casita for my daughter's birthday. The interior is somewhat dated but it was clean. Parking was an issue: the casita comes with one covered spot but there is no other parking """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""spots"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" near the room short of parking on the street. To start, a large sign greeted us as we pulled into the parking lot """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" lock your car , remove your valuables """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Not exactly a way to make one feel safe, but moving on. The lobby and check in are next. The florescent lights flicker giving one the feeling that the power was ready to blink out at any moment, the """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" store """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""where you might pick up any small item you may have forgotten was dismal a few scattered items on dusty shelves.  Spacious Room was delightful with wonderful bed and beddings. HDTV a pleasant surprise. No air conditioning but was not a problem due to local climate
Breakfast very nice with plenty of fresh fruit. Don't expect eggs and bacon, a very nice continental buffet Nightly wine reception was wonderful way to wind down, 
Staff and Service Impeccable. Will Stay again on next visit.

Had other choices for our stay in San Diego prior to our cruise, but decided on this one due to the great location near cruise ship terminal. This hotel has a free direct shuttle to and from the airport every half hour which is very convenient. Attentative and courteous front desk staff at check-in, arrived at the hotel from the airport after a brief -- minute shuttle ride and was settling into a bay view room in just a few minutes after check-in. Hotel in within walking distance to practically everything such as downtown, Gaslamp quarters or just a short trolley ride away and if you're visiting for a few days I would recommend getting the all day or multi-day passes on local transit. Best perk of this hotel is the cruise ship terminal is right across the street from the hotel.

Having, sadly, just returned from New York after -nights staying at this Hotel I can say without a shadow of a doubt that the Chandler is in an ideal situation. It is spotlessly clean and the staff are friendly and helpful. We were - minutes from the Empire State Building and within walking distance of many tourist attractions. Can't wait to go back to the Big Apple and will defo stay here again.

The hotel was recently remodeled. The room was clean and the bed was great. The staff was extremely helpful and friendly. My wife and I are in Manhattan at least half a dozen times a year and would certainly consider staying here again.

We stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn --th Street weekend of Nov -----. The location was perfect, right off of Herald Square with a subway one door down from hotel entrance. Macy's just a block away. We had a great time. We were there for a wedding (which was lovely, great food and decor and service) and had a wonderful time. Our room was spacious and well outfitted. Service (one hour valet, shoeshine, newspapers, concierge making salon bookings) was great and check in and out was a breeze. Staff was very service oriented.

I arrived on saturday and when I asked for my reservation (without the reservation number) the attendant told me that there were no reservations at my name, no one already checked and no possibilities. I am a travel agent from Belfast and I stayed in this hotel on the --th May this year with - girlfriends for - nights . This was my second stay in New york and i was very impressed . my boyfriend and I came to this hotel for a week while attending a conference and it is just as fantastic as I remember. I usually stay at very good hotels, but we did not want to blow our budget.
