I can't say anything bad about our stay other than that... well done indeed!

First time in this hotel. I live locally in Denver but had some family coming in from Ohio and Iowa. We decided to get a couple of rooms and stay downtown instead of my place. The service was amazing. Sara the Afternoon Manager on Duty was very kind and helpful. The rooms were clean and the housekeepers were very nice. The only small glitch is the Valet, it is very difficult to get your car and the guys could smile a little more. Overall the stay was amazing!!!

We stayed at the Chancellor for - nights at the start of a two week trip along the East Coast. 
The rate I got through their website was a bargain, much cheaper than any other centrally located SF hotel, and it included a $-- room credit too.
The room was nicely refurbished, large TV, comfortable bed, walk-in wardrobe, small but clean bathroom - though overall small as advertised. We had a view of union square.
All in all a pleasant stay at the Chancellor. We had breakfast there once and it was nice, though portions were huge. Recommend trying at Cafe de la Presse and Limon in Mission.

This hotel just opened according to the sign. Lobby even smelled new. This was a rewards night for us. We've had mostly good experiences with rewards, but some bad. This was the BEST ever. Room was great, quiet (even near Hobby airport!), and breakfast was also great. Those hash browns with peppers and cheese omelets were top-notch. I was somewhat hesitant about the location on Airport Boulevard. But the parking lot was very well lighted and fenced. So wasn't an issue. Would definitely stay again.

I had to sleep with earplugs every night. The room was so poorly noise-insulated that I could hear the TV from the room on the right of mine and follow the conversation of the people in the room on the left of mine.
If you plan on working in your room or just want to rest peacefully, avoid this hotel!

This hotel is a ploy to extract money from unsuspecting out-of-towners. $-- internet, $-- parking: Those are just some of the fees that you will encounter if you stay here. You can't fight back once you're in town and have nowhere else to stay.
Hotels beware. If you nickel and dime customers, you are going to get scathing reviews. Why? Because putting in hidden fees, or """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""unbundling"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" the costs of basic necessities, deprives consumers of the right to know how much they are going to pay. The types of people who stay in a Hyatt regency are going to need internet access and the operators of this business are well aware of that. It does not necessarily have to be throughout the hotel, but there should be somewhere that people can access the internet for free, whether in the lobby or a business center. Internet is a necessity nowadays. This hotel has absolutely no areas with free internet access. I confirmed this with several employees. I was told that I would have to pay between $-- and $-- to have internet service during my - day stay. I have stayed at -- hotels over the past - months, from Econolodges to - star hotels, and every one of them has provided free internet access in at least one area of the hotel. Not here.
I brought up this issue with their manager -------- [name withheld]. I said I felt that I was being nickel and dimed because when I purchased the reservation at Hotwire, there was no mention of how much the additional cost would be for internet access. All she did was to say that this was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""my opinion"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", recite the internet charge policy, and make some smart comments that did not address the real issue. This included a suggestion that $-- was so little, why didn't I want to pay it? She kept treating me like I was trying to get something for free, when in fact I was trying to suggest a way for this hotel to improve the customer experience. I'm pretty tired of companies feeling that it is okay to nickel and dime customers, and then belittling them when they complain.
This hotel is far from Philadelphia's excellent subway system, so you have to take a taxi to travel into the city or bring your car. They charge $-- for self parking!
Send this hotel a message--do not book there!

We stayed at the Embassy Suites North Labor Day Weekend ---- and had an excellent trip. The hotel was great and the staff was very helpful. The made to order breakfast was out of this world. As a Hilton Diamond Club member I have stayed in many Hilton properties around the country and I would like to say that this Embassy Suites was one of the best. Please consider it on your next trip to Indianapolis.

We stayed in LA for - nights, hotel itself was lovely, clean, great service from valet to reception. I didn't like the area it was in, we found downtown LA dirty, intimidating and full of tramps gathering in mass in some areas. Just be careful which way you go out of the hotel.

I recently stayed at the Hilton City Center for a convention. Overall, level of customer service there is very high. The lobby guys are amazing, very helpful and incredibly nice. However, there were a few things that make it an average place for me, the frequent business traveler.

Also, the interior decorator of this place just went a little nuts with decorative glass and color in the lobby. The rooms are fine, but again, not in love with this place. How about you put money into the rooms instead of in your big fancy glass chandaliers? It was very close to the convention center, and they got me a car service to the airport, so all in all, it was a nice trip.

This is now my 'go to' hotel when I need to fly in and out of Houston. (Although I live in Colorado, I am in Texas for work on a semi-regular basis.) I love being able to drive in to Houston the night before a flight, get a good night's sleep, and then have the shuttle take me to the airport. The hotel is easy to access. This a is very special property that when you arrive can make you feel slightly over awed. The Spa is wonderful and the gold course is a really good test which I thoroughly enjoyed, special mention to my 'fore caddie' Coulton who was courteous, very knowledgeable and really cared about ensuring that I had the best experience possible thank you! The food in the restaurants is top quality, the Addison restaurant is superb and a really special experience but is a bit on the pricey side compared with other top worldwide restaurants. Overall a really special place to stay where we had a really good time thank you.

While I was in New York for a brief conference, I decided to actually stay at the hotel where most of the events were being held. This was a change for me. Usually I'll stay elsewhere and just make my way to the hotel. I don't have a problem with the subway, and in fact typically enjoy it, but since the rate at the Affinia was one of the better ones, I decided that it would be easier to just stay there.
In general, I'm glad that I did. But you need to take it with a grain of salt, and be ready for what you'll get when you check in. Make sure that you realize that this is an older property, and you'll probably be okay with what you get when you arrive in your room.
Notably, the rooms are reasonably well upholstered, but they are on the small side, and the plaster is aging, so you will see some cracks, and some of them might be on the large side. You aren't going to see central air, and in fact you won't see a thermostat of any kind.
Instead, you get what is essentially a steam-controlled radiator to handle the heat that is expelled into the room. You'll also have a window unit (air conditioner) for cooling the room, but in the winter, these units are taped shut to keep cold air from coming into the room - so hope that you don't hit a hot spell or you'll have to open the window to cool things down.
Finally, you may want to make sure that you don't get a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""--"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room (---, ---, etc). This is because the main steam pipe runs through the closet, and it makes the room absolutely bake. Even opening the outside window, with outside temperatures in the --s, kept the room a nice -- degrees, so it was bearable - but it meant that the outside noise increased quite a bit. And even when closed, those windows don't block a lot of noise.

Awesome and quiet room, awesome view!
I'll definitely stay there again, close to Times Square, room has all the amenities you'll need and it's very functional.
I didn't mind the size of the room, but might throw some visitors off.

We stayed at the James for two nights recently and decided that we had finally found """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""our hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in New York. Our stay was a pleasure.

Rick and Brendalee Harris

When searching for a hotel we were concerned with location to public transportation, an included breakfast and a quiet spacious room since we would be in San Fran for a week. The Monticello provided all of these things along with an evening wine reception, exceedingly friendly and accomodating staff who got to know us and regularly asked about our day or evening and whether we needed anything. We can't say enough about the location as we took BART (Bay Area Rapid Transit) from the airport for about $- each and came out - block from the hotel at the Powell Street station. The street cars, cable cars and buses are all within one block as well. We enjoyed the breakfast each morning which consisted of: coffee, tea, muffins, croissants, various other pastries, and fruit. The only thing missing was juice and-or water as there was nothing for non-coffee-tea drinkers. The complimentary evening wine was either red or white along with some type of bread. The room that we had was a Deluxe King facing a wall but was very quiet yet near the elevator. Since the hotel is on a busy street, I think that we benefited facing the wall. We still had three windows that let daylight in. The room itself was spacious and tastefully decorated with: a king bed, desk, two arm chairs and a small fridge. The bathroom was a decent size with a shower only. The free wireless internet and free lobby internet station allowed us to keep in touch and check-in for our return flight right from the hotel. Everything was super clean throughout the hotel including the lobby bathrooms. We laughed at how often we ran into a housekeeper sweeping the elevators. While here we have already recommended this property to several people who we ran into who were complaining about paying high rates at chain hotels. This was very affordable with their internet special combined with AAA. We would definitely stay at the Monticello again.
hotel was sound. was in town for Pistons and it is close enough to the central downtown area. The cities attractions are close by and a reasonable taxi fare away.

The car was twice as expensive as taking a cab, even though we specifically requested the most cost effecient mode of transportation. Don't get sucked in to this trap!!!!!

I had a great time during my first stay at the Bryant Park Hotel and recommend it to anyone looking for a stylish and comfortable (yet not outrageously expensive) hotel in Manhattan.
I stayed at the Bryant Park for one night at the end of May. The hotel is housed in a gorgeous black-and-gold ---- Art Deco tower overlooking the leafy park. The location is perfectly situated between the subway lines for both the east and west sides of Manhattan. It's a short walk to Penn Station and an even shorter walk to Grand Central Terminal.
I was warmly welcomed to the hotel by cheerful Anna at the reception desk. I had booked a Deluxe Queen View and was given room ----, which wraps around the northwest corner of the building. The park views are gorgeous and worth the higher room rate. The room itself was spotlessly clean, with oak floors and modern furniture. The bed was very comfortable. Best of all was the palatial marble bathroom, with a giant tub and a separate shower fitted with a marvelous, waterfall-generating showerhead. The high-quality soaps and shampoo smelled great. I found the room to be an oasis of calm in the middle of bustling Manhattan.
I did not visit the Cellar Bar or Koi, as I was meeting friends downtown the one night I was in NYC, but I did have breakfast and read part of the Sunday paper (provided by the hotel) in the beautiful park across from the hotel. It's like a little slice of Paris in Manhattan.
I have searched long and hard for a hotel in Manhattan that's not prohibitively expensive but that also has style and a distinctive personality. With its historic exterior, elegant interior, central location, spectacular views and courteous staff, the Bryant Park will be my new home-base for future visits to New York City!

My wife and I drove up to Philadelphia for an overnight stay to enjoy the city in late December and decided (after staying at the Ritz-Carlton two years ago) to check out the Four Seasons. After reading many reviews online, Trip Advisor, Frommers, etc. we decided to book and we were both excited about enjoying Philly and the Four Seasons experience.
Upon arrival we were warmly greeted by the very nice front door staff who never once let us touch the doors to open them. The level of service here is exactly what you know and expect from a Four Seasons: simply the best. The lobby is very stately and inviting and one thing you'll notice at any Four Seasons is how clean they keep the properties (both common areas and the rooms). The housekeepers are some of the best in the business. As we walked through the lobby and over to the front desk to check in early, we were warmly greeted again and told our room was actually ready (we were checking in well before noon). We proceeded to our room and got settled before heading out to walk around.
While the rooms are a nice size, with a comfortable bathroom, they are showing their age. Our room was incredibly clean, but lacking in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""up to date"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" feeling that you expect from a Four Seasons property. The first thing we noticed was how the walls felt somewhat barren and the décor was showing its age. The bathrooms still have standard bath tub showers that were an original part of the hotel and you could tell the woodwork has been painted over and over again in the room. The furniture had definitely been updated as well as the beds, tv, etc. The safe is not even large enough to put a full size camera in (think wallets and jewelry only), let alone a laptop. I believe the closet locks if you ask the desk for a key.
It's just the small things that you notice that start to make you realize this hotel was in need of a room renovation. While cosmetics are not important to everyone, when we stay at a Four Seasons property we expect to have the best service and accommodations that meet its high standards. When we are out in the city all day enjoying the sights and come back to our room, we want to feel like we’re truly on a getaway trip and the standard room here just didn’t meet that expectation. All of this is by no means a deal breaker and I would tell anyone going to Philly to stay at this property. The rooms were nice, just not at the level you would expect and that left us disappointed. It is worth noting that I was told the property should be going under a renovation in the next two years.
I walked up to the front desk in the early evening and happened to be greeted by the Assistant Director of Rooms, Ekrem Koroglu. Ekrem and I spoke for a few minutes and I told him what I needed. He could not have been more courteous or pleasant. Yet another example of the exemplary service we love at the Four Seasons! 
Overall, the hotel is a top pick in Philadelphia if you value impeccable service and housekeeping, a great location, including proximity to everything you need downtown and all the things Four Seasons provides! We look forward to seeing updated rooms in the future!

I booked this hotel after I read its reviews on Trip Advisor - believe them when they tell you the rooms are small. I discovered it coincidentally: I often travel with a very large, heavy suitcase. Thanks to the Americans with Disabilities Act, (ADA) I am confident that I will be able to roll this boulder into any hotel in the land, including an urban hotel like the Comfort Inn where the lobby is located about seven feet above street level up a set of steep steps. The ADA is a Federal law that mandates equal access to public facillities for everyone - including people who use wheelchairs. Apparently, it doesn't apply at this hotel...
BE WARNED: THRE IS NO ELEVATOR from the street level to the lobby! There is a concrete pad on the side of the building where the elevator may SOMEDAY be, but there's no sign of any construction going on around it. (I got the distinct impression that the concrete pad is there simply as a ruse, since I believe that the hotel is in violation of the ADA as things stand now.) Ironically, the agency charged with enforcing the provisions of the ADA are probably in a tall building just a few miles away! I'd love to report this hotel to them but I don't know whom to tell. If you know, do it. The owners deserve to be educated.
Oh, by the way: about my suitcase: the desk clerk called her son from the room behind the lobby desk and he hauled it up the stairs for me. I wonder how well he'd do with a ---year-old!

I don't often gush. I've been fortunate to have stayed at some wonderful hotels, but very rarely am I driven to write such a glowing review. I'm still here as part of an extended business trip with my wife, but wanted to write this review while everything is fresh in my mind. This is the nicest hotel I have ever had the pleasure to stay in.
The hotel rooms themselves are beautiful. Starting with the bathroom, with a glassed off shower-step in tub area, an electric mirror with built-in TV (cool for a gadget guy like me), fully automated-dimmable lighting, etc. The room (at least that I'm in) also has a mini-fridge, --burner flat surface stove top, microwave and is fully stocked with plates, glasses, cutlery and the like. While it's doubtful that you'd actually cook anything during your stay, the kitchen amenities come in handy if you visit Giordano's for a stuffed crust pizza, which really needs to be eaten with a knife and fork. There's also an espresso maker, but we haven't needed it given the coffee available throughout the hotel. Rounding out the room amenities are switch operated drapes (room can be pitch black in midday), Bose wave system, lit closet, flatscreen tv system, and an incredibly comfortable bed.
But, as nice as the room is, as my review title says, I think the service really sets this hotel apart. The room has robes, slippers, and numerous other little touches, including and an umbrella for free use, The hotel has a health club and pool on the --th floor. It has a locker room, with electronic lockers stocked with robes and towels. These are lockable with digital key codes for guests. Go into the health club, and every machine has a bottle of water and towel on it. In the pool area, towels are on every chair, there's water, apples, newspapers and a water punch available. There's also coffee available in the morning outside the locker rooms, and separate wet and dry saunas in them.
Service. Just one example. We asked the concierge for directions to a local camera store, because we forgot to bring our camera's battery charger. Instead, they checked their back area and, found that they had a fully compatible charger. They then took our camera upstairs, plugged in the battery to charge while we went out for a walk down Michigan Ave. But this is just a reflection of the continuous service excellence. Housekeeping is spectacular, loading and running the dishwasher every morning in the course of cleaning the room, assembling the numerous pillows, including specially spa pillows, during turndown service in the evening, welcome greetings from virtually every staff member you encounter on your walk into the hotel, and full-on smiles from everyone.
The location right on the Chicago river is awesome for walks down the newly developed Riverwalk and access to the numerous river tours and water taxis. To be balanced, I do take away a rating point for location since the hotel is somewhat isolated and it takes a minute to walk from the hotel doors to anywhere meaningful - but that is a little nit-picky.
There's lots more to add, which I might do later, but for now, wanted to express my thoughts on this wonderful hotel.

Other than the price of parking, if you take all the other Hiltons in the world and average them out, you'll get the Hilton Seattle Airport & Conference Center.

We were especially fortunate to stay here on very short notice during Mary Kay month in Dallas. 
 We had a room for under $---.--. In a perfect location for on and off the highway.
When there developed a damp carpet ( ac problem) in the room we were moved to a suite for the remaining time of our stay.
We make our own reservations using Hardin as the discount code. It is usually a good savings on price.

... so I picked this place. I should have kept looking. There was only one guy running the front desk. He was really rude. The reception area is nowhere near as clean as it looks online. I didn't want to use the mini fridge because it looked grimey.This place is acceptable if you need to stay in the area for one night and you aren't planning on doing anything else but sleeping in the room. I would not stay any longer than that. I almost lost the key because it was not attached to anything. It was not one of those card keys, but an electronic key that looks like you have to pay $-- if you lose it. The continental breakfast is pitiful. If you think about staying here because the pictures look nice, think again. The room I had looked nothing like the picture and it was even in the main building. Almost forgot about that, too. There's a separate annex building they use that sits in the middle of the parking lot. I don't think I'd stay again unless there were some MAJOR rennovations.

By far the best place that I've stayed while visiting San Francisco! The hotel's staff provided superior service and the restuarant, The Blue Mermaid, has one of the best waiters at dinner time that I've ever encountered. The room was also very clean and had a very comfortable bed. However, when I return to the Argonaut I'll spend a little more for the deluxe room as the window in the standard room didn't open so it got a little stuffy. The hotel is also in a prime location -- at the quiet end of Fisherman's Wharf but also within walking distance to many great places to eat and drink. I'm looking forward to my next visit to the Argonaut!!

We stayed at the Hotel Monaco over Fourth of July weekend. The staff was friendly and helpful. The room was clean and decorated in a very funky style that I would never in a million years copy for my own home, but was a fun departure from boring for the weekend. The hotel was centrally located downtown, quite close to the Market and the ferry terminals. It was a great value and we would definitely stay there again.

My wife and I recently stayed here for our ten year anniversary. The room we got on the -th floor with the balcony was great during the day and evening, however... Around -am the craziness started and all hell broke loose in the hallways until around -:--am. Outside we heard fighting, yelling, smashing and all kinds of trouble and no hint of security.
I still like this hotel and it was partly our fault for choosing a room on the same floor as the nightclub. If you do end up going to this hotel choose a room on one of the upper floors and away from the club if you want to get any sleep.

We stayed here for one night (October -, ----) and enjoyed our stay. We were in room #--- - The Executive Suite. Extra Large room with dining table for -, wet bar, two closets, living room, large bathroom and bedroom. Staff was nice and very helpful. Full buffet breakfast offered for less than $--.--. Room was clean. Great location right off of I--- and only --- minutes from Charlotte Douglas Airport. Only -- minutes from

I booked this hotel based on a co-worker staying here - years ago. When we pulled into the place the first thing I noticed was the parking lot was empty. The second thing was the musty smell of the lobby that hit you as you walked thru the door. We were given the room key ,and as we walked to the room the areas around the hotel the pool were filthy. Now the surprise, as we opened the door to the room, the pictures shown on the web site don't do it justice. I instructed my kids not to touch anything, the entire room needed to be over hauled, the chairs were ripped, the beds were worn and sagging, the furniture was missing doors, and handles, only - light worked in the room, and the shower and sink area's had mold all around. Save yourself the money and frustration stay else where.

I have stayed at this hotel countless times!The major attraction is the convenient location.The hotel is mere steps away from Times Square,opposite Bryant Park and sandwiched between - major subway lines.All the rooms newly refurbished,the staff are helpful and since it's a small hotel it doesn't take a long time to get to your room.The lobby is bit dated though and the restaurant doesn't open for dinner,but there are plenty of dining options nearby.

Dont stay here: Horrible neighbourhood, unfriendly staff, dated rooms, gross breakfast.
I wouldnt go outside after dark... it is a very rundown part of town, with questionable people walking around. We felt unsafe. The staff were good with giving directions, but that's the only good I can say. We found them very rude, monotone, and unwelcoming. Also, what kind of hotel does not allow split payment between - credit cards when there are - adults in a room. """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Hotel policy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is not what any customer wants to hear as a response: Customer service ---. And it's nice to have a free breakfast, but not when there are flies trapped in the cereal container! ...we paid to eat elsewhere, and got outta there asap!
Good price, but NOT worth it.

I've been traveling for over -- years and this is one of my favorite place to stay. In jacksonville I wouldn't stay anywhere else. Great staff from housekeeping to management. Being that its Summer I was able to bring my two kids with me and they have really enjoyed it. They allowed me to use their conference room to hold sales meetings and do interviews. Great hot breakfast. Great location, close to restaurants. Only -o minutes away from the beach. What else do you want? While in Jacksonville, I'm not staying anywhere else.

The Windsor Inn in Washington DC is one of the most charming hotels I have stayed at. From the lobby cat that greets you to the lovely young owners who are doing a wonderful job of renovating the rooms and the overall hotel, this is a great place to stay. The staff is happily ready to assist with all your needs. A good continental breakfast comes with your rate, which is a very reasonable rate given the neighborhood. Evening wine and snacks provided in the lobby. Lots of exceptional eating establishments and shopping nearby. Metro is just a short walk away, bus line on the same street, though most monuments and attractions are within walking distance. This will be my hotel of choice whenever I visit the Washington DC area in the future.

The Jane has the feel of --th Century NYC. The rooms are small, however, they have many retro touches and the decor is very suggestive. If the intention was to create the mood, they are succesful. The decoration is inticing. In addition, the rooms are sound-proof. Even the temperature was perfect.
I will return to The Jane for a short stay, it is worth it.

Stayed overnight at the Hyatt with some friends this past weekend. The hotel is definitely business oriented and huge. If you want warm and fuzzy do not book here. But they are fast, curteous and the staff does their job. The rooms were clean and the stay was enjoyable. We had a club level room booked and the girl at the reception desk upgraded us (without being asked)from a regular room to a suite. The club level is always a nice amenity especially after running around Manhattan, it's great to get some picky food and drinks before showering and running on to your next event. You know the city... go ... go ... go.
The hotel is conveniently located if you know how to use mass transportation and even if you don't there are many cabs always out front. If I could have changed anything, I would have made the sheets a little softer, but for one night - I could deal!

I have stayed in far better places in Seattle for less. Room was the size of a prison cell, with a window facing a outside wall. It was quiet until someone showered or flushed a toilet. 
On the plus side a Seattle Best Coffee is next to the lobby and it is right downtown. If you take the hotel's limo expect to pay at least --% more than a yellow cab. Hotel staff are helpful and friendly.

Let's start with the good points. The staff was fairly friendly. The look of the hotel is very cool. The sky terrace is very pleasant and a great place to unwind or have a drink in the evening. The location is excellent - a short walk to Columbus Circle and the subway, and there are taxis aplenty. 
The bad. This hotel is extremely loud on the weekends because of the bar and hosting of private parties. The hotel staff was less than honest with us about when the music would end, though they did give us ear plugs. The rooms were very small. Granted, you don't need alot of space for a bed, but we had trouble finding somewhere to put our suitcases. The bathrooms also were very, very small. I was several months pregnant and was frustrated that the tub did not have a ledge to sit on and there were no bars to hold on to in the shower. If you have a disability, consider those points or ask for a handicap accessible room. The bed also is very low to the ground. The hallway smelled like mildew. The room was less than clean. Some days housekeeping gave us new shampoos-conditioners and some days they didn't. You have to pay for internet access.
All in all, if you have kids, like to sleep, or have any type of disability, consider staying elsewhere.

When you pull up, the hotel is very impressive. The lobby looks great. The Greatness stops there. The bar food is terrible and the room service is worse than eating at Denny's. The rooms are in need of being remodeled. The floors had stains, the doors were filthy and the bathrooms had mold all over the tile. I would literly compare the rooms to a Motel -. They are in no way near the standards of a Hyatt Hotel. FIND ANOTHER HOTEL TO STAY AT!!!!!!!

We got a great deal through booking. We found it very nice, well located, clean, new, well designed and friendly stuff. Though -- dollars for a breakfast is a bit crazy hehehe.
The rooms aren't big but there'snt any new hotel in Manhattan with big rooms, same size than Mandarin Oriental ,, no same views though hehe, the Views are good but not as in Mandarin.

What a nice discovery...a lovely boutique hotel in a great part of town and it is QUIET! Just a short walk from the Civic Center, around the corner from the Opera and Ballet, a block from the city bus to the De Young Museum, delicious continental breakfast to start the day, very helpful and friendly staff, just a few of the finer points of Inn At The Opera. We found this hotel thru a timeshare trade and it is a real gem. And the added bonus is the Ovation Restaurant has great food in the evening. Will be recommending this hotel to all my friends. Thanks for a nice stay in a very special city.

Stayed one night to celebrate our anniversary and enjoyed the quiet, relaxed room overlooking Baltimore marina-harbor view. Room was first class with large King-sized bed, windows all-around, separate soaking tub and rain shower. Modestly decorated with bamboo accents on walls and bamboo floors.

I stayed in this hotel while I was visiting colleges in the Philadelphia area for graduate school. I was looking forward to staying here because of all of the good things that I had heard about the hotel. How wrong were those reviews. The staff at the hotel were rude and every time that I had a question for either the front desk or the concierge, I felt like I was interrupting and bothering them. Every time that I had asked how to get to a certain destination via public transportation, I was told to just take a taxi. As a broke AmeriCorps volunteer, taking a taxi everywhere is not an option. I had to explain this to them multiple times before getting my answer. On top of this, the hotel charged my credit card twice and trying to get a refund for the second charge was unbelievably frustrating. 
This hotel is in a good location, but I'm sure that there are other hotels in the area that have a much friendly and more helpful staff.

This hotel is just amazing. Several individuals made my stay perfect in every way. Bob remembered my name from a previous stay and made sure I had help with my luggage. Stefanie and Kelsey and others at the front desk were so wonderful. Their kindness made me feel so special and cared for. John greeted me by name and asked about my grand baby, remembering her from my last visit. The Acura service added a dimension of assistance that was wonderful. Last but not least, the Bliss was perfect.

Really nice hotel. Great fitness center - lots of treadmills. Nice pool with a fantastic rooftop location. The beds were incredibly comfortable. The rooms were really clean. Internet is not free - which I find ridiculous for a place like this. Close to lots of good restaurants (within walking distance). Beautiful waterfront location. I really enjoyed my stay and would go again in a heartbeat.

I picked this hotel for a weekend getaway for my husband and myself. I went to the site looked and the pictures and when I got there I had to take a second look. I went upstairs to my room and the elevator was out of service. They did offer someone to help take the bags but I had to go up - flights of stairs. I went to the bathroom and there was a roach crawling from the trash. I called my husband to come and take a look but he was right at the door ready to wash his hands from the sticky stuff that was on the remote. We had to stay one night in this place and we left the next morning. Do your research before staying here. This hotel gets - stars one star for the help bringing up the bags and the second star for an easy checkout

We got a great deal on the room through Travelocity and had a wonderful experience. The service was excellent from the moment we arrived. Terrance was accomodating and very helpful. The staff even stored our luggage for several hours after we checked out so that we could enjoy the rest of the day. We loved our room and all its finishing touches. We will definately return.

I stayed in this hotel with my friend in summer. 
This location is pretty convenient as subway is near by, 
Lots of restaurant, shopping area and attractions are
within walking distance. Simple breakfast is included also.
They have nice patio area by the entrance and we were
chilling at night chatting with cup cake from Magnolia bakery.
But if you open the window in the room, the next building is 
just right in front of your eyes and you could almost join
their yoga class...what can I say, this is New York!
Overall, I don't mind coming back to this hotel again!

Hotel is located in the Murray Hill neighborhood which is a really nice area to stay when in Manhattan: there are lots of good restaurants nearby, Empire State Building, Grand Central Station, Macy's etc. within walking distance.
Hotel itself was well maintained, room was spacious and comfy with excellent bed. Service was okay. The hotel is hard to fault although it lacks any wow factor.
The issue that really irritates is that if you are payng more than ---USD a night a free internet should be included in the room's price. Now you could only use free internet in the lobby of the hotel. Because of jet lag did not want to go there to answer my emails at -am!
All in all, I could stay again on this property especially because of its location.

I can thoroughly recommend the Orchard as an excellent base in San Francisco. It's in a great position - not too far from shops and theatres, but far enough to escape the noise of the downtown area. Very handy for the cable car stop too, and if you're tempted to take a Grayline tour, their shuttle bus will pick you up at the Orchard.
The breakfast menu is the best I've experienced in the US and the service and cleanliness are second to none. 
Overall, the hotel has STYLE - go for it!!!
VB from the UK

I have stayed in NYC plenty of times. It is our go to overnight trip. Most of the time we just priceline something around Times Square and hope for the best. This time we were lucky and go this hotel. My only complaint was once we found the enterence we had a bit of a hard time finding the elevator to the lobby. We were in no rush so we just wondered till we were pointed in the correct direction. But other then the nice man in the parking lot there was no one around.
The hotel lobby was amazing. It was huge. There was two bars, resteraunts, and shops. We were meeting people at the hotel so we walked right over to the bar and waited. We kept saying there was no reason to leave the hotel. The bar and resteraunt was so nice!
The room we had looked right over times square. Normally I am lucky to just get a bit of times square in the distance. But in this room I was right over it! The bed was extreamly comfy and the staff seemed very nice. We only stayed for night unfortunatly but I would haved loved to stay more. 
There was nothing bad about this hotel. I loved it.

I stay in starwood hotels all over the world and what I loved about this hotel was that they not only took care of me as a platinum member, but I was attending a course at the hotel and the bell staff were amazing. They were constantly offering to walk and take care of my husky. (of course she is an angel ;-)) Kidding aside, we have stayed at many Westins, Marriots, Sheratons, and too many other hotels to list and the staff here was exceptional, especially for an airport property. I have stayed here before and will stay again.

We spent - nights at the Westin Copley Place for a graduate school reunion. This was the chosen hotel for our class. It is very well located and there are several similar hotels within two blocks. 
This Westin was totally predictable. A - decade old structure with the style and layout of that period. Rectangular rooms with adequate space, except in the bathroom. Indeed, the bathroom was a true challenge with poor lighting and almost no room to move around. The room decor is simple but neat with adequate closet and drawer space for a short visit. Elevators are a little slow due to the size of the hotel. The service was polite and attentive, when you got noticed. Again, this is a big, convention style hotel that is not set-up for boutique hotel style service. We only had one breakfast in the hotel and it is clear, they strain serving a heavy load of guests. Have the buffet. 
All-in-all, the hotel is just what you would expect and met our expectations which were not high from the outset.

The Gem Hotel Chelsea, always be my first choice, when i go to New York. The hotel is execellent, because the hotel was in a great location with lots of good restaurants , bars and delis nearby. The neighbourhood are not very touristc area, and it's great to seems maybe for a few days a local. The room are smal, but if you are in New York, you problaby walk all day long, and doesn´t matter the size of the room. the only thing i didn't like is the mattress, not so good, can be like these one with memory foam mattress.
The rooftop deck was very, very cool. The shower was great and always when i come back to the room the cleanness was perfect. The staff are very helpfull. So i love this Hotel.

My first reviews were oddly all removed? Seems I am being stalked by someone I didn't give a glowing review to. 
Not quiting though. The GRANT was dynomite. I sure wish the Kimptons of this world would drop in and see how first class service including the housekeeping is and should be done. From the grand entry, to the second level where they have a magnificient art collection...on up to my room. It was pure magic. I think it was like it felt -- years ago to be at the grand old hotels. 
I noticed some celebrities in the bar-restaurant. The Grant's happy hour is a big draw for the locals. 
My only complaint...tiny complaint is certain members of the staff checking their cell phones while they should have their head ---% in the game. My pet peeve. It just looks bad. 
Easy to over look though. Management has done a great job training the team.
That was a worst hotel i ever seen before! Bugs, small dirty room, no elevator, strange smell...Never stay here! It's horrible!... and do not trust the pictures on the website, they are lie!

When staying in the Times Square area, we usually stay at one of our favorite hotels down the block and always wanted to try The Iroquois Hotel. I'm so glad we did. The staff is professional and polite. Upon checking in we were upgraded to the Presidential Suite. I like booking rooms with separate seating area, so I had originally booked a smaller suite. Well, I couldn't believe when we walked into this suite! It was absolutely wonderful! Living room, dining room, kitchen and bedroom. There was just one thing. The bathroom stall shower was tiny. But if you like to take a bath, it has jacuzzi. The decor is elegant and the bed very cozy. I don't sleep very well in hotel rooms, but I did in this bed. Until the morning when a jackhammer woke us up. They were opening up the street below the hotel. Even with the construction going on, we had a wonderful stay because the room was so nice.

I have stayed at the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""W hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in London and was beyond impressed with the rooms and service. However the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""W"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on the Lakeshore leaves a lot to be desired. When I first pulled in the - valet personell were fighting with each other over who had to take my car, pretty bad first impression. When I got to my room I found it was basically a comfort inn with a little paint slapped on the walls. I pulled back the duvet to sit on the bed and the white sheets were filthy!!! The furniture is what looks like Ikea, with scuff marks and damage, the bathrooms is tiny with dirty walls and the walls are so thin you can hear EVERYTHING!!! I definitely would not recommend staying here, for the same price you can definately find a much nicer room in the area.

While I travel to Chicago frequently, I had never previously stayed at the Hilton Suites. I got an excellent deal so thought to give it a try. The hotel is conveniently located just off of Michigan Avenue, and if you enjoy the shopping around the Hancock and Water Tower Place you'll find the location superb. The hotel is busy, but spacious, and check-in was a breeze. My husband and I were assigned a room at the end of the hallway behind the elevators. While other reviewers found the elevator noises bothersome, I did not really notice them (unless in the bath which was directly behind the elevators) - if this troubles you ask for a suite away from the elevators at check-in. The room itself was large and clean - bed was great - nice view of the Hancock building - no complaints! We parked elsewhere - the valet parking is over $-- a day, so you can definitely find a cheaper place to park if you drive around a bit. L is a few blocks down, along with TONS of restaurants and coffee places. It is also an easy walk down to the river and the Christkindl market if that strikes your fancy. All in all a great stay; I'd happily recommend this hotel to others, especially if you can find a discounted rate.

We wanted to stay near the Riverwalk but out of the crowds and at a reasonable price. This hotel fit the bill perfectly. The cost also included breakfast, parking and WI-FI all of which you often pay for at the higher end hotels! The bed and furniture were very comfortable. Our only complaint was that the room was dimly lit which made evening reading a challenge.

location location location: central park - min, line NQR to the side of the hotel. The room, if compared with the lobby which makes u some expectations, a bit disappointing. By the way it was cleaned, which means a lot to me. Never tried breakfast o the reastaurant. 
The consierge: super! Anthony: outstanding. Lisa Wood: very kind, but she could had spared 'your english is not so good'... I didn't undestand you only because partially deaf :) 
Many thanks also to the driver's the hotel hired for the trasfert to the jfk: Christopher Lucciani.
se vi capita di andare... non aspettatevi chissa cosa: c'è moquette ovunque, a parte nel bagno. Abbiamo pernottato per - notti, lasciato loro la belleza di ---- dollari... e non avrei mai creduto che per lasciare il bagaglio avrei dovuto pagare, ancora. lavoro anche io in un hotel e teniamo bagagli per tutta la durata del giorno gratuitamente.

The Omni Hotel at California Plaza in Los Angeles has many positive features. If you need to be downtown, the location is excellent, easy walking distance to the Disney Concert Hall, Ahmanson Theatre and Mark Taper Forum and the Los Angeles Museum of Contemporary Art. The hotel itself is lovely – beautiful lobby, restaurants, and newly redone rooms. The staff is outstanding – friendly and helpful. Only negatives – while the rooms were redone, the floor of the shower was not so the old pink tiles were somewhat grotty. Also, the second day we were there , black material appeared around the drain of the bathtub. I suspect that the renovations of an older hotel were either incomplete or something was wrong with the plumbing that day. The swimming pool while clean and pretty is situated near the ventilation system and was too noisy to sit around. The restaurant (Grand Café) food was very good and once again, the servers were excellent. We would stay there again.

Very enjoyable stay. 
Rooms were clean and confortable. Fine location. Service was great. Recommended.

This hotel was wonderful. We were there during for New Year's and LOVED IT. It wasn't very warm, but the pools were still heated and usable and our family swam every day (yes, Crazy Canadians). The decor is gorgeous and there a lots of little areas to sit and chat-cuddle-relax. There is a tiny arcade and pool table and a bar with a ---' (yes foot) tv. It wraps like a ribbon with alternating tvs and they are everywhere. Getting to play TPC San Antonio Golf Course was also a great perk of staying at this hotel. Our kids can't wait to go again!

I stayed at Hotel Monaco during my trip to Folsom Street Fair in September ----. This was my third or fourth time staying here as it is always consistent. Truth be told... the standard rooms here are rather small so I would suggest an upgrade. Luckily I am a Kimpton In-Touch member so typically my room is upgraded to a suite which is very accommodating (large room, enormous bathroom with tub-shower, extra seating area, two desk areas, etc...). 
Geary Street near Union Square is somewhat populated with many homeless but that's most of San Francisco so there's nothing you can really do about that. Fortunately, the location is walking distance to the Square and to many other tourist destinations. One drawback, however, is the difficult in finding a taxi... the bellman-valet certainly helps but there were moments when I waited +---- minutes because most taxis fill at the other hotels further before on the street. 
Overall the rooms here are nice, clean and comfortable. The restaurant is outstanding (can never understand why it isn't usually crowded) and unique. Staff is always friendly, polite and attentive. 
Great hotel.

I went to San Diego to celebrate an event in my life and unfortunately had to go alone as something came up for my traveling companion. I chose the Old Town Inn because of the Trip Advisor review and because it was very close to the trolleys at Old Town. I expected that would be very helpful to go everywhere I wanted to go without having to take a taxi. I was so right! Five minute walk to the trolley and the Coaster and everwhere was within my reach. The staff was really helpful and very friendly. There is a wonderful continental breakfast each morning and the pool is beautiful. Coffee, tea, and lemon water was available in the front lobby all day. No hot tub but that was the ONLY thing that was missing. Rooms were clean and bright. I would definitely recommend the Old Town Inn to anyone who wants a good vacation, great service and does not want to spend a fortune on accomodations. Thanks to all the staff for making my stay very memorable.
Good location. Clean property with helpful staff. Forget the breakfast.

STAYED --st October for a week.

Honestly, there's nothing really wrong as such with the hotel, except that what once passed as glamour is rapidly starting to look very tired as the years go by. Some people will love the chintz, the gold fittings, white-gloved attendants and the liberal use of barely readable fancy script on each and every sig - but it really wasn't for me.
As others have noted, the reception and lobby are often overwhelmingly busy. On my check-in in the late afternoon there were twelve desks and probably only four being manned, with a resulting queue sprawling across the lobby itself. Fortunately there were staff on hand to direct and keep things moving, but simply adding more staff on the desks would have helped better.
The rooms have been updated with a little bit of technology to drag them into the --st century - an alarm clock with an iPod dock, a decent size flat screen and an individual room based WiFi router. However, my experience of the internet connection was that it was exceptionally poor, especially for the $--.-- USD daily fee. Other oddities were a lack of a safe and an rather fancy, yet entirely empty, mini-bar.
Finally, I only ate here once for breakfast, in what seemed to be pitched as the more low-key buffet restaurant """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Oscar's"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that's tucked away downstairs. I think everyone knows that your average hotel breakfast price is way overpriced, but seriously for -- dollars (no, really) I'd expect something more than the tired looking array of hot and cold food on offer here, with coffee and juice served up by aging robot-like staff who seem to have lost the will to smile many years previously.

I booked this hotel last minute because the price was great. The location of the Wellington is awesome, near Central Park and Times Square. We arrived at the hotel well before check in. We were able to check in although our room wasn't ready. Our awesome bell hop, Mike, took us to our room and put our luggage in the closet! We spent - hours out and about. When we came back to the hotel, our room was ready. We stayed in room ---- which was newly renovated. Our room had - beds, tv, refrigerator, sink and microwave. It also had a small round table with two chairs. There was plenty of dresser drawers and closet space. Our view was of an alley, but that was not a big deal. The city was warm during December and our room was very stuffy. We called downstairs and asked if they could turn the heat off. -- minutes later someone came up and told us the heat was off. We opened the windows and the room was comfortable. We also had to call down twice for extra towels and both times we received them within -- minutes. For the amount of time we spent in our room, it was perfect. I cannot say enough about the friendliness and accommodating staff. The reviews about the water pressure are true! It is strong.

I had the best time of my life at the sleepless part of New York City--Time Square. Crown Plaza Hotel has wonderful accommodations and top notch customer service. Everyone made us feel so comfortable and special. I went with my two nieces that were visiting the US for the first time and I took them to visit this special part of New York City Time Square. The hotel has the convenient location to explore the intriguing and exciting Time Square and the main landmarks in NYC. I felt safe and this time of the year (Monday thru Wednesday) was a good time to go. Not too many turists and we are able to enjoy the main landmarks with no lines and not many people. 
Also, I wanted to give special thanks to Hector Isaza, Doorman, and bar attenders Martin Rojas and Marco de Leon. They were superb! Customer service at its best. 
Plus a great breakfast buffet (orange juice was so good). Nothing to complaint....no noise, comfortable rooms and exciting way to explore the area. All of these Priceless!
In summary, best time and wonderful memories spent at this place and of course New York City. Thank you for making my dream trip special and unforgettable.

Fab hotel with great staff. I was impressed with how clean the room was and the staff were very responsive, the beds were fantastic and so comfortable. Loved the coffee machines in the rooms, only disappointment was that you had to go to the lobby for fee WII Fi. First class location right across from the Prudential Centre, would book this hotel again.

We stayed at this hotel because my friend is part of their Kimpton In Touch program through which you can a night free every seven nights you spend at any Kimpton hotel (now, that's a real deal) and what a treat that was!
Wonderful marble lobby and more marble in the hotel, great paintings, flower arrangements, sofa, fire place and the staff: simply delightful, very friendly, helpful.
We had requested a double double and were upgraded to a double queen on the highest floor with a great view. Very large room, super comfy bed, loved the design of the bathroom, the size of the Etro amenities and.... The hotel had free hot chocolate in the lobby in the afternoon, followed by free happy hour from - to - pm and complimentary coffee from - to -am.
Although I don't have pets, I don't mind them and I thought the food and water bowls they had in the lobby was a very sweet gesture.
What more would you wish for? I immediately signed on to their Kimpton In Touch Program and would advise you to do the same. Enjoy!

We stayed here this past week after -- days of travel and hiking through UT and AZ. Chose it because it was new, close to the airport and great reviews. We were not disappointed. The hotel was luxurious from start to finish. We had the pool to ourselves with our kids and walked around the city that evening. The room was spectacular and the bathroom over the top - had a corner suite it was perfect.

I was pleasantly surprised by Rodeway Inn. After four days on the road all we wanted was a great night sleep and a bathroom where shower shoes were not necessary. We found it here! The staff was helpful and friendly. The rooms were recently renovated and spotless. Also, my cat Sebastian was welcome for a $-- fee. My only complaint is that I couldn't get the wifi to work on my laptop. I think the signal was just too weak.

This place is amazing! Water park for the family with a very impressive layout. We were able to enjoy it even in November as they heat the water. It is amazing how peaceful and quiet it is out here. Great retreat for the family. And yet not too far from Sea World and other great things San Antonio has to offer. We only went to SW and then enjoyed the resort the remainder of the week.

Room was very clean. Supposed at how large the rooms were for New York standards. Stayed there during hurricane sandy and the service was still incredible despite the hurricane. One the managers, Brett Caspi was incredibly helpful providing both hotel services and concierge services during a time when most of the city was in turmoil. Can't imagine how great the service would be under normal business conditions. Highly recommend!

This hotel is definitely geared more towards the business traveler than the vacationer and is located on a somewhat busy strip of Colorado Blvd. The rooms were very clean with comfortable beds and a cool modern vibe (like something out of a Crate and Barrel catalog). Close to Cherry Creek shopping and restaurants as well as downtown Denver. Staff was friendly and helpful. For a unique and delicious breakfast, we highly recommend Snooze (which is just down the road)!

Stayed one night here after coming in late, before leaving the next morning. Used points, so I don't know the regular room rate. Overall, it was OK - decent room, nice staff, convenient to airport. but had some issues too. Details...
GOOD:
--Rooms, in the tower where we stayed, are pretty decent. Plenty big, nicely kept bathrooms, bed was fairly comfy.
--Rooms have a small deck, but the view is of the airport - nothing spectacular.
--Staff was friendly, both at the desk and in the restaurant.
--Location is very convenient to the airport, and pretty quick access to I--.
--Cookies at check in were good. ;)
BAD:
--YOU HAVE TO PAY TO PARK HERE. This is a pet peave of mine - if you aren't in the middle of Manhattan or the Loop or somewhere that its ultra-crowded, there is NO good reason to have to pay for parking. This place had a gigantic parking lot. I think parking cost $-- or so. Ripoff.
--Restaurant staff seemed to be overwhelmed during breakfast, so they fell behind a bit. Food was good, but a bit overpriced.
--The doubletree is not just a hotel, its like a little village of condo buildings too, which makes it very crowded and hard to get around the property.
--Common areas could be kept up better and cleaner.
--The doors to the rooms have a huge gap at the bottom - allows a lot of light and sound in from the hallway.
If you are coming late and-or leaving early at Sea-Tac, this is not a bad choice. But you may want to consider other places as well, shop around a bit.

We booked this hotel on hotwire and when we arrived we felt we had gotten a steal. The hotel is beautiful, the area is lovely, and the staff are pleasant and helpful. The room was spotless and each room comes with an Ipad to use to request hotel services as well as navigate the area. The valet overnight parking was a bit steep at $-- but with how much we saved on the room we couldnt really complain.

I stayed at this hotel over New Year's with my husband and some friends. The rooms were very clean and spacious. Our room was right across from the elevators which was quite noisy, day and night. The happy hour was a nice bonus, and the breakfast each morning was quite good. The hotel's location is very close to Michigan Avenue, restaurants and shopping. I would definitely stay here again next time I'm in Chicago.

Made the mistake of checking out of the Peabody Court which was great, to check in here (the Plaza was the conference hotel). The restored Masonic Temple and Conference facility was exquisite and the service fabulous, the AV people were great and the catering staff were alwalys on top of the water and coffee. It is a beautiful unique setting which makes the hotel even more of a disappointment. The entrance from the hotel to conference center is awkward. The rooms were adequate, but it seems that not much thought went into the planning, never mind the lackluster decor. For example there was a definite lack of outlets, there was a huge walk-in closet with an ironing board in it, but no outlet to plug the iron into, so you had to drag it out into the room. In addition, a vanity in the closet rather than in the bath would've been nice. The wait for the elevators often lenghtly and the customer service average. I had problems with check out and splitting the bill and the staff was not terribly helpful. The small deli in the lobby is great. they have sandwhiches and coffee and a nice assortment of cheeses, crackers and other tasty treats. I can't comment on the pool, because the hours were so limited, I didn't get a chance to swim. After the Temple, the deli was the best part of the hotel. Not a terrible place but, not wonderful or unique either.

My husband and I have stayed at the Hotel George many times. It just gets better and better. The superb staff are kind, caring, and very helpful. This puts us at ease each time we visit. Very clean, good sized rooms with all necessary facilities. Service is excellent.

I recently stayed here for a business conference. No complaints other than the restaurant at the hotel was overpriced. The place was clean and the staff were professional. It is conveniently located. A little expensive but it's NYC.

This is a nice property that's a little dated but well maintained. The rooms are smallish but as a party if -, we were gone. The king bed we reserved was fine - maybe time to upgrade soon because it was a bit squishy.

Stayed at STAY for - nights. The location is ideal and right next to Times square. It is a nice boutique hotel. The hotel has a nice lobby with a bar-club at night. The breakfast was delicious, but as mentioned in other reviews the tables fill up quickly by -am. Elevators took a long time since there were so many people downstairs at breakfast. 
I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

I actually live very close to NYC so I don't usually stay in hotels but commute in and out when I need to. But, I decided to attend a conference taking place there and it seemed to make sense to stay at the hotel where the conference was being held. 
The room was beautiful and ready when I arrived. Although the check in line was long, it moved fast and the staff was helpful and quick. I was placed on the --th floor and was pleasantly surprised by how nice the room was. There was no fridge in the room but they did have a flatscreen TV, a couch, and an ottoman. The bathroom was nicely sized with a shower and a bathtub. The toilet broke my first day there and they fixed it immediately. 
The elevators, however, were a problem. The hotel is huge and in the middle of time square so it is always busy. To get to your floor, you cue in your floor on a pad and it tells you which elevator you can wait for. There are no buttons inside of the elevator to cue in a floor so you are entirely reliant on the elevator the keypad assigns you. Btu the keypad doesn't know how many people are getting on the elevator with you. Frequently, you have to let your assigned elevator pass you by because the elevator gets overcrowded. Late at night and early in the morning everything runs more smoothly. 
The bar and the restaurant are both good and there is an ATM in the lobby. 
I enjoyed myself and I would stay again if another conference was scheduled there

We stayed here for -nights before joining a cruise in mid-may, and it was wonderful. The reviews sold it to us, and they were all spot on - great hotel.
Doesnt look much from the outside and the area isnt as glitzy as say -th or something like that but it's right next to the subway and a - min walk to Times Square, Bryant Park etc.

We stayed here as a couple to get away. OVERALL LOVED IT!. The breakfast put the icing on the cake. From the cook to the fruit, excellent. The room was wonderful. My daughter and I loved this hotel and loved being ON the beach and all the shopping. The staff made us feel at home and I wouldn't stay anywhere else when I return to the area!

Not the prime spot for meetings. The downstairs had an odd scent that wasn't 'pleasant' at all. The breakfast was not hot and fairly spend at $--.-- for what they serve. Long walk to Beale Street as well. If you can, get a bit closer to Beale as there are better properties there.

This hotel has to be one of the finest in the world. It imposes itself onto fifth avenue, the rooms are magnificent and the service is excellent. However it is certanily not cheap, but you get what you pay for in life, and the Pierre is worth every penny!

This is the second time at the Pod. This tome I stayed in a suite type room....- queen bed and two twins....so my two daughters and I each had our own bed. It was a good arrangement for us!
The hotel is clean but the bathroom is a bit small.
The concergie's were very helpful and the location is great! Just about a block from two metro stations. Doubt you'll be disappointed if you're looking for a bit of economy and convenient location.

Just wanted to comment on the level of service at this hotel. Nothing but top notch. Specific credit goes to Sam who manages the fitness center. Sam goes way beyond what is expected in a hotel fitness center. He remembers my name each time I visit; offering complementary chair messages and expert advice on general fitness. It is simply very hard to find this level of personal service anymore...anywhere.

After insisting to our travelling companions that despite renos, the Carlton was the place we wanted to stay for our first time, - day adventure to New York. Yes, I had read the reviews that the lobby was under construction but was quite horrified to find a tiny drywalled space for checking in. However, we were very thrilled to hear that the brand new lobby would be opening the very next day. It was quite an improvement, to say the least! Elegant but understated, a cool (literally !) place to escape the heat of the New York pavement. The architecture books in the lobby were a nice touch. Unfortunately, the lobby bar and restaurant are a few months from completion, but will undoubtedly match the decor and ambience that the rest of the hotel has. 
Our room was small, but nicely appointed. No A-C troubles at all.My only complaint would be that the maid didn't vacuum daily. 
We also had a bit of difficulty finding local places to hang out for a drink at night, but would recommend Ixta (Mexican) down --th and Houston's on --th. Scopa (across the street) was handy but pricey. The --th street cafe was a handy place for breakfast and is actually open ----.
We loved NYC-what an exciting place! We were a bit worried about the location but many things were within walking distance and the subway was also very handy and not at all intimidating! (this coming from - --ish folks from the Fraser Valley area in British Columbia!) We would love to go back again!

Stayed here for - nights in September. The location is slightly random as it is just off a main freeway type road, but also very close to public transport and the old town area of the city. The staff in the hotel were very helpful and friendly. DVD's, books and games available in the lobby and we took advantage of this, and it was a great bonus. Breakfast was good, cereal, fruit, bread, waffles, tea, coffee - all that you could ask from an included in price buffet breakfast. The rooms were clean and spacious, although we did notice the that walls and floors seemed slightly thin, although thankfully are neighbors were quiet so noise was not an issue. We did not notice any noise from the road or airplanes.
There is a pool and also laundry facilities if you wish to do any washing. 
Great location to avail of local sights and public transport, and lovely hotel with great staff.

Once you pass the oh-so-shiny lobby, everything becomes mediocre. We had a standard double room and the only good thing was that we had two huge beds and a big TV. The furniture was a bit on the older side and no safe in the room (seriously?). There was an obviously old and very loud ventilation system which we had to turn off completely during the night because of the impossible noise and the air in the room would then get stuffy by morning. We had windows overlooking the lobby, so no help there for fresh air. The bathroom has a (rather weak) light in the middle of the ceiling and the shower curtains are very thick, so once you pull the curtain, you basically shower in complete darkness. Sounds like a silly thing but it gets irritating after a few nights. Be careful with rasors.
As regards the staff, I cannot say that something was very wrong there but again - not impressed. We arrived around --.-- and we were informed that our room was not yet ready and that it will be ready in a while. We had absolutely no problem with that but we wanted to know how long 'a while' is (is it ten minutes or two hours?) so that we can decide whether to leave the bags and go out or to wait in the lobby. We asked the question twice (adding the word 'approximately' the second time) and we got two 'I'm sorry, I really can't tell' answers. It was almost as if the lady was afraid we'd sue them if the room was not ready the minute we came back. I literally had to ask 'Ok, so, if for example we leave our bags and take a stroll around the neighbourhood, will our room be ready when we get back?' and then she said 'Yes, definitely.' And then we come back and our room is ready and she hand us the key, upon which I ask where the elevators are (because it is a gigantic lobby) and I get a quizzical look, as if I asked a really stupid and inappropriate question instead of dragging my suitcase around and discovering this myself. Excuse me for expecting the receptionist to say 'Here is your room key, you are in room No. so-and-so on such-and-such floor, the elevators are over there'. I have stayed in various dumps before and receptionists never had problems with that line. As I said - not a big problem, but c'mon. The concierge was helpful. The location is good, although at the time we stayed there (May ----), there was a massive and unattractive construction site right in front of the hotel. Starbucks in the lobby - useful for the first morning coffee.
Oh, and also - no free internet anywhere, not even in the lobby?! Nowadays you get free wi-fi in your room in budget hotels, so this is just downright absurd.
In any case, my first time in a Hyatt and, for ---$ a night, not worth it at all. It was a business trip so luckily it was not out of my pocket. If it were, I'd feel cheated.

The warmth of the staff at this hotel begins out on the sidewalk, with a man dressed in a sharp suit who helps with your car. Every step of the way, from concierge(one of the finest I have ever met--beyond helpful and wonderfully gracious, a woman who orchestrated my engagement to my fiance) to the front desk and then to room service and bartenders in the restaurant. There are a lot of reasons I won't forget my weekend there, but when you have a beautiful room and staff like this, your visit is automatically unforgettable.Thank you Abigail Raymond!
PS. How many hotels have you been to that serve free wine in the lobby for an hour every night?

My husband and I recently stayed at The Allerton for two nights. 
The location of this hotel is prime for shopping at The Magnificent Mile, and very close to public transportation. We were never more than a few blocks away for anything we needed!
The hotel is a landmark, and the rooms are very small. Our standard room was below average in size, and the bed was situated only a few feet from the doorway. It was fine for us, but definitely a little cramped.
Had no problems with customer service, infact all those we came in contact with were very friendly and knowledgable.

The Roger is beautiful! Charming & well decorated! Excellent Service! And I can't say enough about the bed...so comfortable! We stayed in one of the Penthouse rooms which had a terrace and a view to die for (the Empire State Bldg)! We wanted a hotel that was in the center of it all and we definitely got it! Walk a few blocks north and enjoy Grand Central Station, Times Sq, Empire State Bldg and the shops on --th St. Great bakeries just a block over on --nd St - Paris Baguette - in Koreatown! Walk down Madison Ave, Park Ave, Lexington, etc.

This hotel is right across from the back of the bus station. It is convenient for traveling. The staff is very friendly and helpful with directions and events in the city. The hotel is clean and comfortable. I stay here often when visiting the city.

We stayed here the night before checking into Disney, booked on Priceline for $--. It was a really nice hotel. The rooms were clean and staff friendly. Since I booked through Priceline, I had to request my room type, but the hotel honored my request. The pool was very nice. I'm not a huge fan of the sleep number beds (maybe I just haven't found my sleep number yet), so I would have preferred a pillowtop mattress to the Sleep Number.

The rooms are spacious and spotless.
The pool and spa were great.
The bedding was awesome. Very comfortable and relaxing.
The staff were great, couldn't do enough for us.
The hotel had a shuttle to-from the airport which we needed.
The hotel is a bit of a walk to any shops but not an impossible walk as we did it.
There is a Denny's a couple of blocks away with pretty good food.

got a best rate guarantee rate of ----night. the hotel is really nice and the room is sufficient. we had view of the city on the --th floor but this hotel is right on riverwalk..it's really nice to be able to stroll to the restaurants and back. it can be pretty romantic. it is situated right next to the contessa. the nights we stayed we saw the houston rockets in the lobby, they were playing the spurs that night. we also got a massage there, didn't really like it much and way overpriced. they serve a merienda in the late afternoons with drinks and little snacks. nice touch. you can even print your boarding passes at their little kiosk. the concierge was really nice too. the thing that really bugged me was the crazy -- dollar valet and the neverending trains at night. i think they were even working on the street i could hear the jack hammers. anyway, i wouldn't pay the regular rack rate. a note about san antonio- if you're only here for the downtown area you probably won't need a car once you get to downtown. it was easy to walk around.

Location - if u happen to be going on a cruise, this would be the hotel for you as the terminal is directly across (which for other travelers, when the ships are leaving, u will hear the loud horn)
The property is U-shaped but all rooms have a balcony. The view isnt that great as u r blocked by the terminal but if u r on the right side of the building, u get a view of the mountain.
There is a lift to bring u up - levels towards Pike Place Market. This lift is located outside the property (about a min. walk or so). Not that great of a walk back at night (wondering souls hang out at this landing). 
Check in - very professional looking staff, young and efficient though the concierge seemed to be very busy at all times (missing most of the time and usually a bit of a wait to see her). Lobby is of the new age Marriott, very hip and trendy (at night, this lobby bar area is very packed and noisy for the whole week we were staying)

Facilities - small city gym, small pool (half in and half out), if u hang out on the deck, those walking along the bridge or taking the lift to pike place will be watching as it is directly beside the elevator-link to Pike. There is a tiny room where u can use the internet (complimentary) but with only - units, it is always occupied

The location of the hotel was great, but the hotel lacked some of the excitement of a really great place to stay. It was typical hotel breakfast--nothing special. The rooms were clean and neat, but nothing special. The cookies were a nice treat. Go for the location--forget the ambiance!

The bottom line: I have stayed in a few dumps in NYC, and this hotel is NOT a dump. Yes, the rooms are very small like in most New York hotels. The renovations a few years ago were kind of slapdash in some ways with too much caulking around the sinks, etc. But to be fair, this is not a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""boutique"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel costing $----night. It's a budget hotel in an old building. 
The lobby area has a lively bar and a nice little lounge with free coffee and tea and an internet terminal (charge applies). During my two visits (Sept. ---- and March ----) I have found the front desk staff to be professional and polite. Speaking of which, I traveled this time with a colleague who was given a ground-floor room. She heard a lot of noise from the lobby and from the smoking terrace behind the hotel, so I would avoid a ground-floor room.
The furniture and bed linens look just like the photos on the hotel's website. The beds are very comfy and clean. I stayed once in a room facing --th St. and once in the back of the hotel. I slept like a baby in the back room, though I got a lot of street noise in the front room (mostly drowned out by running the window a-c unit). The neighborhood is safe. There are delis and a subway stop just footsteps away, and you can walk to the heart of Times Square in about - minutes. I had a rental car for my business trip and paid $---night to park across the street at a theatre's underground garage. Shocking? Yes, but that's the going rate for garage parking in midtown Manhattan.
If you're traveling with kids, just be aware that there is an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""adult novelty"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" shop on the same block. Frankly that is part of the history of the Times Square area, a holdover from the old seedy days before Disney came to the neighborhood. But the store is fairly low-key and you can't see much from the sidewalk. 
Overall this is a pleasant place to stay. I not only recommend it -- I was happy to return six months after my first stay. The Amsterdam Court ain't the Pierre or the Waldorf-Astoria, but it costs a fraction of what those hotels cost.

I spent - nights at the Stephen F. recently and it was a decent experience.
On the positive side, the staff was outstanding. Very attentive, respectful, pleasant and professional. I thought it reflected well on the management. They have close proximity to -th street and are blocks from the Capitol. There is easy access from the interstate system and generally an easy place to get around with a car.
