Prior to arriving, I was surprised by the high valet charge. I checked another site, and a public parking garage sits on the same block. Unfortunately there's no elevator and I had to park on the -th floor and lug bags up and down narrow stairwells. I believe the daily charge was about $--, so you save about $-- a day by carrying your bags. Worth it to me, but maybe not everyone. As an additional bonus, they opened the gates on the weekend, so I parked for almost - full days for free!
I thought the rooms were marginal. They were clean, but I'd take a Hampton Inn room over these rooms anytime. In my opinion, the layout was ineffecient and wasted some of the limited space. The TV was unusually high in the air and not well seen from the bed. If you sat in a chair in front of the TV, you'd be straining your neck over time as you looked up at the screen. The bathroom sink was my biggest complaint. No counter, just a bowl sink. A counter with a mirror was at the opposite end of the bathroom, completely worthless to me without a sink.
I got the impression from the website that free internet access was available in the rooms. I was wrong and am always annoyed at allegedly higher-end hotels that charge for this now-basic service. I was pleased that internet access was available in the lobby and banquet rooms, so they are partially vindicated!
I think the management is doing well with what they have to work with. However, I left the hotel with no desire to return.

My husband and I stayed here the last three nights of our NY stay and absolutely loved it. The room was more spacious than we thought and everything was well thought out -- we were welcomed with Hershey's kisses on the pillows and bus-subway maps were placed in the room for our convenience.
The room came with a tiny shower (a bonus) and there were more than enough toilets to share among rooms. Everything was very well maintained and clean.
A big shout out to Jose at the desk who was an absolute dear, even helping us with our luggage up the stairs.
The neighbourhood itself is charming with loads of cafes, little bookshops and art galleries. It's also close to Times Square (we walked home one night from there and were surprised that we could).
Very nice. Chelsea Lodge made our New York experience extra special.

My husband and I wanted something nice but affordable for our anniversary trip. This hotel was overall nice and it was in a great location. However, there were some fees that we weren't aware of when we booked, such as the valet parking for over $-- a day. That adds up when you stay for a week. And there were no other options, so you pretty much have to pay it. I couldn't believe you even had to pay for wireless. For such a nice hotel, you'd think that would be included...i mean you can even get free wireless at smaller-less attractive motels. The prices of the food and drinks were also outrageous. Definitely smarter to plan on eating out and not at the hotel if you stay there.

I just got back from a - night stay at the Salisbury. I will definitely stay there again. My friend and I took my daughter and her friend for my daughter's --th birthday trip. I wanted somewhere safe, quiet, great location within walking distance to area attractions, and clean but cheap. I wasn't there to stay in a five star hotel and spend all day in my room. So, the Salisbury definitely fit the bill. It is an older hotel, with older furnishings, but very clean and safe and reasonable. We had a standard room, and I requested a room at the back of the hotel for less noise. They accomodated me and it was very quiet. The room was clean, everything was in working order, and it was a big room in comparison with most NYC hotel rooms I thought. The linens were adequate. I thought the continental breakfast was very good being free. But, I am not a big breakfast eater. They had the standard muffins, croissants, bagels, donuts and assorted juices and coffee, cereals, and hard boiled eggs. I thought the staff was helpful, although not overly friendly..but Phil the doorman was sweet! One plus was that they store your luggage for a day, if you have a late flight, which we did. The elevator was slow at times, but not real bad. But, we were on the --th floor. Overall, if you have teenagers, kids, or just want a room that is in a great location, with no frills and very reasonable and clean..then the Salisbury is perfect. I would definitely stay there again without question. Also, it's a short walk to Times Square, Theater district, Central Park, -th Ave. shopping and area attractions. Everyone was right, try Angelo's Pizza two doors down for great inexpensive Italian food and pizza,and the Brooklyn Diner has great cheeseburgers..and it is right up the street from the hotel. There is also a Starbucks right across the street also. Because the hotel is owned by the church next door, there is no bar in the hotel..which didn't bother me, but thought it was good to note. But, there are plenty other bars around the area. Overall, I was very pleased with the Salisbury and the reviews here were very helpful and pretty accurate I think. I just think you can't beat the location for the price.

This hotel is NOT - --- stars. It is dirty, scuff marks everywhere, the maid looked through our things, but did not bother to give us clean towels, I guess she was too busy. They should be embarrassed that this hotel looks like this. Dirty carpets, bed bugs, etc.

This property sums up a lot of the problems with the Holiday Inn brand generally: inconsistency. I've stayed in some very nice Holiday Inns on my business travels...but I always hesitate to book a Holiday Inn because there's a pretty significant risk you'll end up in a Holiday Inn like this one. This is one of those hotels that was probably really nice back in ---- but just hasn't kept up with the times. 
I had hopes when Holiday Inn announced its rebranding campaign, because what I read said that any hotel that bore the new Holiday Inn signage was going to be subject to renovation and a rigorous standards evaluation. Well, this hotel has that new signage, and it is sore need of renovation. The only change from the old property, beyond the sign itself, seems to be that the bedding is new (thankfully, the floral bedspreads of yesteryear have been replaced by a crisp white duvet).
The hallways are disgusting. Harsh lighting, ugly decor, and DIRTY, worn carpet that's stained, unswept, and threadbare. The elevators are the same way. They actually have high-pile, house-like carpet in them, which only serves to collect dust. The lobby is pretty unwelcoming, just because it's SO dated. The room itself is dated, too -- thankfully, it didn't suffer from the cleanliness problems of the hallways, but the decor is in serious need of an upgrade, as is the furniture. Some of the patchwork choices that have been made along the way only exaggerate the old decor: for instance, in the shower, old tiles had been replaced with shiny white new ones -- accentuating the yellowish old ones. The window coverings need work too, both their style and their functionality. Our room in the first stay was overlooking the pool, and the window curtains didn't block out the very harsh lights illuminating the pool.
Service was mixed. On the first stay, check-in was slow, but friendly. On the second stay, check-in was highly disorganized (computers weren't working, etc.) and not very polite. On both stays, the parking lot was jammed with cars and very difficult to find a space in.
We ended up staying at this hotel because it was CHEAP (under $---) and our power -- and hence air conditioning -- was out for a very lengthy period of time. With DC's ---+ degree heat, even this Holiday Inn beat out an un-airconditioned apartment, and it was hard to beat the price, especially at the last minute. However, if you're traveling to Washington, there are many, many, many, many other hotels I'd look at first. This place isn't a complete dump -- my rating is average, not below. It met the test of a halfway comfortable bed with clean sheets and a tolerable room. But there's far better places to stay and, even with the great rates, comparison shopping is worth it.
I stayed here during a nurse practitioner conference. I would leave early and enjoy the lazy river with my husband while there. My experience was lovely! I would recommend!

My wife, our cat, and I have stayed at this La Quinta many times over the last --- months. We find that it is one of the best hotels we have stayed at. The rooms are always clean. The staff is very friendly and helpful. Check in-out is usually very fast. Prices are also very reasonable (even when booking last minute). 
It is in a safe area located with other hotels and a small duck pod with fountain nearby. All rooms have nice flat screen TV’s and free wifi.
This hotel has a nice pool and hot tub area. It is by the interstate, but still very quiet. The beds are so comfortable too!
It is located in a quiet area off of JT Butler Blvd and I---. Being set off the main road helps reduce the noise of the traffic. There are MANY fast food and gas stations located within .- to - mile drive of the hotel. There is a huge shopping complex about - miles drive away. 
Overall, I recommend this hotel for its friendly staff, quiet, comfortable, and clean rooms, and its central location and ease of getting in and out.
Don’t forget, if you bring your pet, they stay for free too!!!
Room was comfortable. Internet is wired only, a disadvantage for me. Restaurant was marginal and bar expensive and sparse. But the location is great for eating elsewhere. Value stay.

I recently stayed several days for a convention in late April. If you choose this hotel because of a convention you will be the envy of all your peers if they do not. The location is literally across the street. The staff was welcoming and knowledgeable of the surrounding area. Room was clean, bed was incredibly comfortable. Check in was fast and easy. I don’t think I could log a single gripe for anything during my stay other than the downtown trains constantly ringing their bells (not the hotel's fault). There is a sky bar up on one the --th floor (Peaks Lounge) that provides an excellent view to relax and unwind. Thumbs up to the restaurant on the first floor (Altitude) we had an excellent lunch there as well. I was very impressed by their fitness center, one of the best I have seen in a hotel. Plenty of space and equipment. I only wish I would have brought my swimming trunks. The pool looked inviting and I saw quite a few people enjoying the spa and sun deck.

We stayed here for one night for my daughter's -th birthday. While the package is rather pricey, you get your moneys worth and more. My child was spoiled with one thing after another and she was completely thrilled every minute we were there. Other packages will cost less but this was worth every penny spent. Our package included a welcome present, a travel bed for her doll, a visit from the candyman and his huge cart of candy, breakfast for - adults and valet parking. You don't even have to step outside to get to the American Girl store. I cannot say enough nice things about our visit to the Ritz Chicago.
Good value for money! Try this hotel if you are visiting San Francisco for the -st time and don't want to pay too much on high-end branded hotels. You won't regret it!

Excellent boutique hotel, not large by US standards but better because of that. Location is excellent close to all sights on -th and Madison. Very good continental breakfast and the complimentary cheese and wine early evening is very well received. Front of house staff were exemplary in their help. The books in the rooms add to an intimate ambiance. Strongly recommend this hotel to a discerning traveller.
Two and a half to three-star hotel that gives you a decent place to stay for the price, not many frills but clean and fairly comfortable.

We stayed for - nights. Our - interconnecting rooms are large, clean and modern. The staff are extremely helpful and when we had a problem with the room the staff did more than expected without being asked. The only complaint was getting to breakfast early as there is limited seating. We and been concerned having read previous reviews about traffic noise. Although aware of traffic in the morning it was not a problem. Great location easy walking for china town and wharfs, we would definitely use this hotel again.

Yolanda Holden, was very helpful & a pleasure to visit with each day. She made sure that we had several places of interest to visit & gave us directions & options for our destinations. Everyone at Spring Hill Suites made our visit enjoyable. Spring Hill Suites hires top notch employees; & is an excellent place to stay at.

Very nice, clean and comfortable rooms. Convenient location close to major attractions and bus transportaion. Friendly and helpfull staff especially Steve at the reception desk. Would be perfect with complimentary breakfeast.

My then---yr old son and I spent a long holiday weekend at this property early this year, and as we begin to plan our ---- visit, it is really the ONLY property we are considering! The hotel is perfectly located to get to anywhere and everywhere: walking back from the Zoo at Central Park via -th Avenue, hopping on the subway for ethnic eats in the Village, taking in a show just blocks away, great restaurants, shopping, and Times Square, Times Square, Times Square. 
The front desk staff are wonderfully attentive and knowledgeable, as are the concierge staff. Even long lines at check in-check out times were handled quickly. The suites are just right for us each to have our own sleeping area... most of the time we were out and about. I was concerned about street noise, but our room overlooking Times Square was absolutely quiet. Security on the ground floor was very attentive and never a problem.
For meals, the restaurant's osso bucco was excellent, and the breakfast buffet was very good, with an excellent wait staff.
Three words: Excellent. Hilton. Perfect.

Stayed in the Whitcomb Hotel in March this year for - nights with my daughter. A lovely historic hotel central to most places. Trolleys and BART on our doorstep.Our room was lovely and large if a little dated but that added to the charm of the place The shower was great and the beds were very comfortable. The room was spotless. 
We ate in the Market grill one night and had a fab meal there. A work of art came out on my plate, I had the chicken and my daughter says her seafood pasta was the best she had ever eaten. The food was delicious, the restaurant was very comfortable and there was a fire burning in the fire place which was lovely as we had a window seat and it was pouring out of the heavens outside and it made us feel really nice. 
There is a Starbucks attached to the hotel which opened really early and it was great to start the day with a nice coffee.
Yes there is a lot of homeless people in the area but at no time did I ever feel threatened by them. I spoke to a few of them, most were ex Vietenam Vets who were thrown on to the streets by Ronald Regan in his wisdom. It actually really upset me to see how these people were treated having fought for their country they were nothing but respectful of me.
Sams diner is across the road and does a really good breakfast.All in all I had a wonderful stay here and would definately stay here again when I next return to San Francisco.
Thank you Whitcomb

Stayed a total of - nights. For over $--- a night, i expected more. Room that i stayed in is showing signs of overuse. Could use some renovation. Furniture looks a little worn. At least it doesn't look-feel dirty. I can find similar conditions hotels for --- the price.

I would have given the Catamaran more than a - rating if the room were a bit more than average. The bed was not very comfortable but of course on - days during our stay we noticed new mattresses piled up for delivery. I'm sure the guests staying in our room after we departed received a new mattress! Oh well. However, most importantly, the room was immaculate. It also had a refrigerator which is always useful. The grounds were very lush, lots of exotic plants, flowers and trees from all around the world. There were ducks walking around which I also find to be a nice touch, and ponds with fish. A local bartender we chatted with at a restaurant on Pacific Beach called it an oasis and said that that is where he refers his visiting friends. I loved the location of the hotel. It was in the middle of the places we were visiting, the zoo, La Jolla, etc. I must say that after a day of being out and about I liked coming """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""home"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to a nice tranquil hotel. It was also nice to sit on our patio and look at all of the beautiful plantlife while ducks walked right past our room. However, I do not think the cost of the room is on par with the room itself. I would have liked a nicer room for what we were paying. I didn't use the heated pool but I did visit the free arcade in the pool area. We rented a car during our stay and had to pay $-- per night for self parking ($-- per night for valet). We were lucky that our room was on the side housing the parking garage. However, my husband pointed out to me that we could have parked right outside the hotel on the street for free b-c there were always spots available. This hotel is located on Mission Bay and one block from Pacific Beach. We appreciated this a lot and spent a lot of time walking along the bay as well as the beach. The bar inside the hotel hosted an excellent happy hour that we found accidentally. For some reason the hotel does not advertise this. There was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""guest appreciation night"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in which there was a wine tasting with cheeses and fresh fruit. That was a nice touch as well. I would return to this hotel but I probably would research a cheaper option first since this is not a typical resort vacation. All in all, a very pleasant stay at the Catamaran.

This hotel is situated right on Bryant Park with views on to the library with magnificent views.
Location wise it is in the heart of everything.
The rooms are spacious for NY standards, comfortable beds and very well appointed bathrooms and Molton Brown toiletries.) All the staff have been charming too from the reception desk, to room service to the kind man who calls the lift for you.
The big let down, which unfortunately will mean that I will not be returning is the noise. I had a room with a view but it sounded like I had trucks and road works and traffic and building work at the end of my bed and I didn't get a wink of sleep. The hotel leave earplugs for you to use but even with those you can hear al the noise. (I am not a light sleeper and usually sleep through everything) I have never experienced this in a NY hotel before who usually manage to successfully block out the outside city noises with heavy duty windows.
I was meant to be coming back to the Bryant Park in a few weeks time but unfortunately the noisy rooms mean that I will look for somewhere else to stay.

This was my second stay this month at the Courtyard at Easton, and it has become my first choice for business travel to Columbus. The hotel looks and feels new and the rooms are very immaculate. The beds are comfortable and there are at least five foam or feather pillows on the triple-sheeted king size beds. The room is roomy, with a large desk area and a pull-out sofa (if you need it). You'll need to use a ethernet cable (you'll find it hanging in your closet) for internet in your room, but I think wireless service might be available in the lobby. The sink and dressing area are separate from the toilet and tub, and both areas are spotless! Nice toiletries are provided.
The breakfast is very reasonable ($-.--) with lots of choices. The cooked-to-order omelettes are delicious. The service is excellent (and it's buffet style). There is a little convenience """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""store"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for snacks at times other than breakfast. 
If you need a small refrigerator, ask for one at check-in. They are complimentary and will be brought to your room quickly. Shop at Trader Joe's less than a block away and stock up on beverages and snacks for your room.
The hotel may be slightly more than usual for a Courtyard, but due to location at a fabulous shopping area, it's great if you can travel on business, and take time for shopping after work! There are MANY great restaurants at Easton. The airport is minutes away, and the hotel has a shuttle.
There are great (chewy) Otis Spunkmeyer cookies (also complimentary) at the reception desk. The entire staff is professional, friendly, and very helpful. I'll stay here again.

We were visiting friends and choose this hotel because of its location. We were very surprised that the room was so big, clean and quiet (except for the loud talkers walking down the hall one night). We had a great breakfast each morning that saved us $'s. The bed was very comfortable and the sheets were of nice quality. We always turn the fan on the AC to block any noises that may disturb us and it had a thermostat that offered a temp. so you could sleep very comfortable at night. The front desk staff was very nice on all shifts and the house keeper did her job very well. I could not find a single thing that disappointed me about the cleanliness of the room. We would recommend this business and would come here again.

The Houston JW Marriott is literally across the street from the Galleria shopping mall. You walk across the street and you are inside Macy's. This places it within an easy walk of an extraordinary range of stores and restaurants, but about - miles west of downtown Houston. Self-parking is available, but you will need to look for it (or ask the valet) because it is not immediately obvious and you may think you have no choice but to valet park. The hotel itself is nice, as are most JW Marriotts, but it is beginning to show some signs of wear and tear. Think of this as a really nice Marriott, or an average (or even slightly below average) JW Marriott in terms of the overall condition of the hotel, furnishings, service, etc. The upside is that I was able to get a rate far below what you would normally expect to pay for a JW Marriott (or even a really nice Marriott) so definitely check for specials.

My wife and I used to stay at this hotel when we would do business down in San Diego in late ----. The style of this building inside and out is just unbelieveable, how nice it is. The Fox Sports Grill is a great place to hang out, food is amazing, bar tenders are all very courteous. The location is great with the whole harbor or city in sight. They also are tolerant with larger dogs which was nice. We would love to return back down there, the only problem is the company stopped doing business with this hotel, and the rates went up with onlines sights signifacantly over the past year. Anything under $--- a night we always thought was to good to be true for a - star hotel like this not to mention the area.

Location in Thai Town about a mile from Hollywood walk of fame and free parking. My room door card key did not work, the door had half inch gaps, cracks in walls an the whole place needs total remodeling. I will not stay again.

I stayed at this hotel for a few nights recently because I was attending a conference at the convention center. If I had it to over I would stay elsewhere.. It was overpriced for what it is and what they give. If you need to be near the convention center, the options are limited and the hotel knows this. So, the charges are high. I think a more central hotel would be a better idea. After hours there is nothing around the hotel and you’ll need to take the T into Boston or end up with a boringish walk into town. After a screw up on their part they upgraded me to a better room and free breakfast in their lounge. Even my upgraded room wasn’t that great. The hotel is billed as water front but the hotel is really only facing the water on the short end not full on so the best you’ll get is partial view of the water. There aren’t all that many rooms that have even that. There is a whole wing of the hotel which faces the back and has no view whatsoever. The breakfast which I got for free because of their screw up was nice but should have come with all rooms at the rates they charge. Oddly, the hotel does not offer the breakfast on Saturday or Sunday. I am not sure why. So, the last morning of my stay there was no free breakfast. The walls of the hotel, like most, are super thin. I heard the tvs of both rooms next to mine and every word of the cell phone conversations of these rooms as well. Finally, here’s the most amazing thing, even though the hotel charged over --- a night, they still charged -- a day extra for internet access. Actually there is a -- a night plus tax for semi fast internet and -- plus tax for the faster internet. This to me is appalling. It brings new meaning to the term nickel and diming. All of the hotels near the convention center charged this extra rate for internet. The front desk clerk failed to tell me that the starbucks in the lobby gives their internet away for free. So if you stay here you can go to the lobby for free internet. They won’t tell you this. This place basically is a rip off. Too high priced, and then looking for extra money in things they should provide for free. Better value can be found in a more central location. If you must stay here make sure you try to get a room with a semi view or you’ll be stuck looking at the T sliver line tracks in a hotel that has water front in the name. Also, beware the not free internet. Lastly, the front desk will steer you to park at the apartment building next door for -- a night but there is public lot next to the hotel on the other side which charges -- a night. They will not tell you about that lot. Again, they are not helpful and probably get a cut from that higher priced parking. i'd stay somewhere else.

A+ !!! :) This hotel really made our vacation! The staff was very accommodating and friendly. You can set inside or outside and enjoy the beautiful view along the river. The bar is affordable and has an awesome drink call the Santa Fe Sunset~yum. The atmospher is relaxing and the pool is nice. The room was cozy and clean.My only complaint is that the toilet was not perfectly clean. 
I would highly reccomend The Eltropicano.I cant wait to go back:)

This may be a -.- star rated hotel, but the parking here is horrible. Our family has a disabled child and we clearly saw parking spaces designated for disabled persons. The valet here is $---night and they refused to let us park there without paying the ridiculous price. We ended up having to park in a separate lot that was a couple blocks away through some back streets, which can be dangerous especially when you come back at night. We have three children so this was a big concern. Although the attendants at the front desk were eager to help, they really need to change the parking policy here. We won't be coming back otherwise.

We found this Courtyard Marriott to be very comfortable and convenient to the Med Center. The rooms was very clean and attractive and the beds extremely comfortable. It is a fairly new hotel and has a nice fresh look about it with tasteful decor. We had a drink at the cafe-lounge area and found it a little expensive but the service was very good. We enjoyed our stay and will probably choose this hotel again.

I stayed at the hotel to explore it as an option for a convention of professional dancers and is simply ideal for its location, rooms, food and especially service quality. I am looking forward to do business with them.

I got this place for $--- a night through Travelzoo and for that price I was pretty satisfied. It is not worth their usual price of $---+.
The good things:
attractive, spacious room
great location with lots of nearby restaurants
very comfortable bed
great double shower head
The bad things:
A nightstand on only one side of the bed, very inconvenient
Ice maker in the mini-fridge didn't work well
There was a small couch but you couldn't see the TV when sitting there
Very little counter space in the bathroom
wi-fi didn't work the one time we tried it
Breakfast was very mediocre, coffee and warm juice were the only drinks
Ceiling in the bathroom wasn't installed correctly and looked really bad
Toilet paper holder wasn't correctly attached to wall and kept falling off
I might consider staying here again if I could get a deal but otherwise it wouldn't be worth it.

I stayed for two nights in this motel and to tell you the truth it was perfect for my kind of trip. It was my first time in L.A. And all I wanted to do in the motel was sleep, and for that it was great. The beads were realy confortable, it had a dual air conditioner and heater, wich was realy noisy, but for what I was paying I expected to freeze to death, and there is a --' flat screen TV on each room. The owner was very polite and helpfull. 
If you are looking for luxury, this is not your hotel, but if you just need a good, clean place to sleep, for very little money, this motel is exactly what you are looking for.

Clean, convenient. First time at a Hyatt Place.
Only some minor waiting for reception, not a big deal.
Good breakfast, a little more interesting than most free breakfasts.
Would definitely stay again.

I will be back. Attended this hotel for a --day conference. I had stayed a couple other times. Every visit was great. Recently remodeled, sleep number bed, quiet spacious rooms, very clean, great wi-fi, included breakfast was plenty and they have a great evening reception. Has a spacious workout room and the pool appeared very inviting. As for the conference, the hotel and staff went all out with facilities and refreshments. This hotel has been recently refurbished. There's not a lot of eating places within walking distance, however IH -- is flooded with restaurants within - minutes drive time. Their uniformed security helped feel my vehicle was secure.

I booked an evening stay for a night out with friends. The hotel itself was gorgeous, from the lobby to the bar-lounge, & finally to the room, I was definitely pleased. The desk attendant was very pleasant and although my stay was short, she took the time to explain all the features of the hotel. I booked a suite on the executive level and this room had excellent views of downtown. The room was well equipped and nicely (if minimally) furnished. It had a very lofty urban feel with all the floor to ceiling windows. Only thing was the AC was rather loud and it did wake me up at night (light sleeper though). 
The pool and lounge area we're great and I did get to use both. The lounge-bar is on its own floor and has great seating both for small intimidate parties and those wanting to meet up on a slightly larger scale. I did receive two complimentary drinks which were great and not something you'd get in many places. Again, the bar staff were pleasant, polite and very accommodating. Pool was awesome with even better views than the room. It's especially lovely if not romantic almost at night. Spa tub was great and I enjoyed an evening and early am swim. 
Overall, access to the hotel was great, service was excellent, and room was more than accommodating. Should I book downtown again I would definitely choose Magnolia over the other nearby similar class hotels. Great stay, thanks Magnolia!

This is a very busy hotel.. 
There should ne no surprise there, it's a large hotel with conference facilities that is centrally located in Manhattan.. it's going to be busy, isn't it..
The good news is that the staff and facilities seem up to the task.. (with a few exceptions)..
My room was on a renovated floor and, I had to say, I was impressed. The renovation certainly seems to have given the hotel some really nice rooms.. A little on the snug side, compared to some in other cities, but not small, and with good facilities.. I had a large bed and a nice sofa to relax on.. Other members of my family on the executive floor certainly considered my room to be superior to theirs (old style) on that floor.. This may have changed, now..
The breakfast room was busy, busy, busy.. but we never waited more than a minute or so to be seated and the buffet had plenty of variety.. hot and cold..
One niggle was that the elevators get very busy. There was a conference on when I was there and this seemed to mean that peak time traffic caused quite a considerable wait for an elevator..
Everything else just seems to work OK.. You will queue for a cab, for instance, but you'll get one..
Busy.. yes.. efficient.. yes..
The location is great for the mid town sights-attractions, most of which are within walking distance..

This is the dirtiest hotel I've ever stayed at in my whole entire life. All the negative reviews are dead on. At least most people who reviewed had a reduced rate through priceline. I paid the full rate of more than --- for the night while traveling for business. Carpets were not just stained, but down right filthy..you could see the dust piled around the edges of the carpet..stained comforter.. dirty and peeling wall paper. Behind the mattress there was a later of dust and random hair on the box spring..yes I was checking for bed bugs. I complained to the manager but all she kept doing is offering free parking..free drinks..all I wanted was a clean room. No matter how many drinks you feed me I will still know my room is a dump. I should have checked tripadvisor first but put too much faith in the crown plaza name. After I checked in I read the reviews on here and was floored to see the offered renovated rooms to some priceline guests for an extra -- bucks! Meanwhile I'm paying far more than that and that wasn't offered. I will be sure to warn all my coworkers and colleagues to never step foot in this hotel. We also ate in the hotel restaurant which was low quality and expensive. Are you seeing a trend?

We stayed for three nights before our Alaskan cruise in a studio room. We invited another family with four kids to join us, and they were upgraded to a larger suite. The hotel staff were very friendly and helpful in suggesting fun and inexpensive things for the family to do. Both the lobby and the hotel rooms were clean. We enjoyed the free full breakfast and weekday happy hour. The location was convenient. The pier for Norwegian and Celebrity cruise lines was closer to the hotel than the Princess and Holland America. It was a relatively short walk from the hotel to the trolley, which then would take you all over the city. Unfortunately, we didn't realize that Hempfest was going on in the park not far from the hotel. The kids really got an eyeful and actaully it was kind of scarty at times.
Overall, we had a wonderful time in Seattle. We enjoyed spending time in Pike's Place market, the International District, Pioneer's Square (and the underground tour), and the Seattle Center. The Pacific Science museum was lots of fun. The view from the Bank of America Tower was really nice.
On the advice of the hotel staff, we also walked up the hill a few blocks to see the view of the city - breathtaking. 
We would definitely recommend the hotel.

Elevators are extremely slow and small. Often waited over five minutes for an elevator to arrive only to find it full with other guests. Cue waiting another five minutes.
Guest rooms are extremely spartan for the price of the hotel and its location in a major urban center. Even though you are in a beautiful old building, expect nothing more - and probably less in many cases - than that which you would receive at a tired suburban Courtyard property. Furniture was worn and chipped throughout the room. Beds have that annoying Marriott assortment of pillows that includes fewer pillows you can actually use for sleeping than pillows to look pretty.
Sleeping was extremely difficult at this hotel due to its horrible plumbing. Every time that an individual next to us (or above or below us) flushed his or her toilet, I heard it in my room. Also, every five minutes or so, my room's toilet made a loud and obnoxious noise that was more than enough to wake me from a deep sleep.
Last but not least, WIFI was poor and unreliable. Unless you are willing to pay a significant charge, you receive internet that is best described as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""dial up."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Further, during my stay, I found that this slow internet was not even working correctly. It frequently """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""dropped"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for long periods of time. Good thing I wasn't visiting on business.

It had been years since I’d stayed at a Four Seasons, but this summer I wanted to treat the family to a higher caliber of service and accommodations on our yearly trip to Chicago.

The rooms are elegant, but not over-the-top in terms of style or design and the central focus is the amazing view out the window. The bathrooms are quite stylish, though and I did like the Occitane soap. The beds were extremely comfortable. In fact, I don’t think I’ve ever slept in a better one.
Amenities are fine. The pool is area is clean and fairly large and there were always one or two other families swimming. The lobby area was nice too. I noticed some other reviews noted how small it was and I don’t quite get that. While the check-in area is tiny, there’s a huge lobby off to the side with plenty of couches for waiting, gathering, talking or working quietly on a lap top. It wasn’t a “scene” to be sure, but that’s what I liked about it. 
Staff were excellent, concierge knew everything and was easy to access (we never had to wait in line) and room service was friendly and quick. We only ordered breakfast since it is quite expensive, but based on how good it was I’d probably budget for room service and do it again! Still, I did miss having a coffee pot in the room. 
As for how The Four Seasons treats kids, I’m quite sure my almost-- year old daughter wouldn’t want to stay anywhere else after this visit. Not only did they greet her by name, every time we returned to our room they’d left her a little treat – a toy, some sweets, popcorn, special bath items, and near the end of our stay they left her a dessert from the restaurant with a Happy Birthday greeting. She appreciated it so much. When we arrived back home, she said she was a little disappointed there weren’t any surprised waiting for her. 
So all in all, this was an amazing hotel. I didn’t use the spa services because that’s not my thing, but I’m quite sure they’d be fabulous yet non-pretentious.

AMENITIES: This hotel had a lot of extras that made our stay more pleasant. They provide a small coffee machine and free tea and coffee bags in rooms, which meant if we woke up late and missed breakfast we at least could make a coffee. There was a free hot and continental buffet breakfast every day downstairs, which meant we could fill up on that and not have to spend too much on lunch. There was complimentary high-speed wireless (we have a laptop) that we accessed from our room - and when we needed to print something we were able to use the free computers downstairs (and we didn't pay to print either). They have a fitness center, but we didn't use it. Room service is provided by a local restaurant between certain hours. We ordered in the first night and they delivered to our room door (just keep in mind that after --pm you would have to go downstairs to collect the food as they won't let people up).
SERVICE: The staff were always friendly and personable - from the doormen to the manager on desk. Every time we entered the hotel we were greeted cheerfully by the staff, which may seem like a small thing but it was really appreciated. The doorman also called a taxi for us on the day we left for the airport and negotiated a flat rate ($--) which would have been exactly what we paid for the shared shuttle - so make sure you ask if they can do that for you! One night our remote for the TV wasn't working; we called downstairs and they sent someone up within minutes with a new remote. The cleaning staff always did a nice job and the rooms were turned down daily and bathroom cleaned thoroughly as well. 
We travel on a budget, so if we could get this hotel again at such a great deal I would definitely stay here. One feels very safe here; after a certain time you need your key to enter the building and the elevator up to the rooms. Although the rooms are small (which doesn't matter if you are only sleeping there), the staff and the extras they throw in make the stay at Hotel Cass - Holiday Inn Express a wonderful place to stay. We really enjoyed our stay there.

Stayed in a suite on the ninth floor. The room was comfortable, but in need of updating (stained carpet, dated furnishings). Other than that, I have only positive comments about the hotel. I would rate the Embassy Suites-Love Field a little higher than this property, but if you need to be closer to downtown Dallas, this hotel is a perfectly good choice.

The Conrad is a modern hotel located in heart of Chicago's gold coast. Easy walking to the shops and attractions. Room was very large and great walk in shower

Budget hotels in Denver are not easy to find. This hotel is great, parking and wifi included is a rare perk in this city. The service was excellent. When we checked in the desk attendant noticed our room was an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""oddly shaped room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (I think near the elevators) and moved us to one further down the hall. The beds were very comfortable, shower was hot and had good pressure, tv was a little outdated but not terrible.
We went to Osaka sushi for dinner just down the street. Definitely a good locals place if you want to get away from the strip mall fast food that surrounds this hotel.
They call this """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Cherry Creek"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but I think that's a bit of a cheat, it's pretty far from the downtown Cherry Creek scene.

My husband and I traveled to Los Angeles to board a Mexican Riviera cruise, and decided to go a few days early to see the sights in LA. We booked our room online for $---night. Judging by the photos, it seemed like a great deal and close to some of the things we wanted to do and see. 
We arrived at about --:-- am on a Thursday morning, and the manager - owner was nice enough to let us check in early. Shelter has a gated parking garage underneath the hotel, which is great. It isn't staffed ----, but they'll give you the number for the night guy to call if you get in late, and he'll come down and open the gate for you. That worked out fine. 
Shelter is VERY conveniently located in the Koreatown section of Los Angeles. The neighborhood is very clean, quiet and safe, and we quickly discovered that the nearby W. -rd Street will take you virtually anywhere in the city you need to go while avoiding the dreaded freeways--sweet! 
Our room was on the -rd floor. The room itself was great. Shelter is NOT the corporate-business travel hotel you're used to. The room is a good size for two, with plenty of room for the king bed, the nightstands, the desk...and that's it. No chair, no dresser, not even any art on the walls. Minimalist, uncluttered. I like it. 
When you first get to Shelter, you realize right away that they are still doing some clean up work and renovations, as there is the occasional bundle of wires here, a hole in the stairwell where some pipes used to be there. And a lot of construction dust in our room. Now mind you, this is not a huge deal to us--we live with dogs, and are usually covered head-to-toe with dog hair, so a little dust doesn't bother us a bit. But the room was dusty, so dusty we could write our names in the layers on the nightstands. 
The only other minor gripe I had was with the cleanliness of the bathroom floor. There was a definitive 'muddy footprint trail' between the marble threshold (also muddy) and the bathtub, where you could see that the grout on the rest of the floor was white, but here was dark gray and black. My white socks turned black after one trip to the bathroom. Also, our bedsheets were very clean, but as we were packing on our last day I noticed a stain at the bottom of our comforter. Even though I knew that housekeeping came every day we were there, it just felt a little like they didn't pay attention to detail very well. 
All of the staff we encountered during our --day stay were fantastic: friendly, knowledgable about the area and had great recommendations for us tourists. The lobby had a little plate of donuts and fresh coffee each morning and stacks of local papers, which gave us a lot of great ideas for stuff to do. Oh, free wi-fi too, which is great. The hotel itself was VERY quiet, even though it was a packed house the last two nights we were there.

Very basic and clean rooms. Free parking. Service was excellent. Easy access to the highway to get to Balboa Park and downtown. - minute walk to the public transportation and to downtown Old Town. Complimentary breakfast served in the morning; pastries, fruit, hard boiled eggs, cereal, waffle maker etc. Best service I have ever had at a hotel and very affordable! I defiantly recommend this place if your looking for a basic, affordable place to stay on vacation.

The best thing about Parc -- is location location location. If you are coming to SF without a car, this is probably one of the best places to stay. It is next to the Powell Street Station so you can catch the MUNI or the BART without a problem. I was on this trip without a car, but parking each day is probably around $--, which seems outrageously expensive, but in all honestly, this is average for a SF hotel, especially in the Union Square area. There are parking lots within walking distance that are cheaper, but since I did not use any, I cannot recommend a specific one. If you're taking the BART in from SFO, it will cost you less than $- to get to the hotel.
Since it is close to this hub of public transportation (including the famous cable cars), and surrounded by the major shopping area of the city, you should be aware that there is a lot of city street noise through the night. If you are a light sleeper, you will need the highest floor possible to get away from the hustle & bustle. If you are used to it, or can sleep through anything, you probably wouldn't even notice the noises. However, the hotel does provide ear plugs if you need them.
Some people seem confused by the lobby being on the second floor, which is understandable, but don't forget this is SF and buildings are built into the hills. There are signs all over the place to direct you to the correct place to check in and elevators to get you to the second floor. There's also a great staff to assist you if you come in on the ground level, which is still under renovations. Or if you're feeling spry, you can always walk up the hill to another entrance and take a short flight of steps to the second level directly. 
Also, if you are on a lower level, do not expect a great view of the bay from your room like they feature on their website. You are, after all, surrounded by other tall buildings, block after block. If you really like the views, I would ask the front desk for the highest level possible upon checking in. 
The room we had was one of the recently renovated from floor to ceiling so everything looks great. For me, the bed was too firm, but I am used to sleeping on foam so all traditional beds are less than comfortable to me. The room featured flat screen tv's & a safe, but no fridges, unless you're willing to pay for it, and also no free Wi-fi. There is a business center and a -- hour fitness center, both of which I did not frequent.
The hotel features the cityhouse restaurant & bar, located on the -nd floor lobby, which I recommend, especially if you have a late arrival like I did and do not feel like finding a place to get a quick bite (fast food restaurants aside).

Although I was slightly nervous approaching the property from outside, once I hit the doors, was immediately taken aback by the cuteness of the hotel from inside. Kind of reminds me of an old embassy suites, with the mexican tile and decor inside, and the big atrium in the center. Rooms were clean, updated, what more to ask for? Only thing I will say, don't ask the hotel for food recommendations. Make sure to find your own. So much local food, and they give you a canned sheet with franchises that you can get anywhere in the country. Experience San Antonio, from the dive to the fancy, tons of GREAT alternatives, really, who wants TGIFridays after a long travel? Close to airport, great location, parking was ample. Although it was on the highway, I never was bothered by any noise.

My partner and I enjoyed three nights at the Oxford Hotel when we went to Denver for the Cubs-Orioles series in ----. The staff is friendly, helpful, and courteous, and frequently funny. Our room was elegant and comfortable. The hotel is three blocks from Coors Field, right around the corner from the Tattered Cover bookstore, and right smack in the middle of some great brew pubs. Beer, baseball, and books--I could live there! You won't need your car: the free tram is nearby to take you downtown, and you can walk to the ballpark. The Oxford is a great value!

Will go back to this hotel when I go back to Chicago. Actually I already booked my room for December! They staff is so professional they followed up with me on my complaint about the loud music so I suspect that will not happen again.

We stayed at this hotel for - days at the beginning of August. It's nothing spectacular but it served as a good, comfortable base whilst we were in Chicago. The hotel is very convenient for attractions in the Loop and those of the Museum Campus. Also easy access to the lakeside where there are spectacular views of the Chicago skyline. We ate breakfast in the restauarant one morning and there was nothing wrong with the build-your-own omelette but there are other options in Yolk next door. The Eleven City Diner round the corner on S Wabash is pretty much open all hours and is handy if you've had a hard days sightseeing. Another local option is The Exchequer pub and restaurant a little further North on S Wabash - really good food. There is also a Jewel-Osco for groceries further South on S Wabash although for some reason the area around it suddenly becomes a bit more edgy. 
The Lollapalooza festival was on in Grant Park when we were there which was interesting although it obviously meant access to the Park was restricted. The Art Institute of Chicago is -- minutes walk away as is the Crown fountain and the Cloud Gate (aka 'The Bean') and definitely make sure you take a ride on the actual 'Loop' itself.

It was memorial day weekend, and pretty full, but even though we had booked a long time in advance, we were only left with the scuzzy rooms to choose from, because they allocate on a first come first served basis, and we got there quite late in the afternoon.
There is no free wifi in the rooms, but the business centre in the lobby was good - I don't think I ever waited to get on a computer even though the hotel was busy. We enjoyed the Starbucks in the lobby, too.
The hotel is only a ten minute walk away from Whole Foods on Greenwich St (for anyone who cares about this).
Overall, I would stay here again - but only if the price was right.
This is a little gem. Great value and location. Staff was great too.

don't get a room anywhere near an elevator. You'll be up all night. Front desk helpful but the property seems very understaffed. Difficult to get assistance If needed. Arrived room - no soap, towels, ironing board. We had to move due to horrendously loud elevator noises.

Just returned from a four night stay at The Argonaut. The hotel is situated in the best bit of Fisherman's Wharf. On the whole the Wharf is tacky, but not as bad as I expected. The proximity to the cable car stop is a definate bonus (especially if you are on your own and worried about safety).
The staff were friendly at all times and always acknowledged you, and you always received a friendly welcome from the doorman. The decor, although wacky, is very tasteful and not at all overpowering.
I had a room facing the courtyard (a view would have been nice, but I was hardly in the room during daylight hours). It was totally spotless, you would honestly think that it had been furnished and renovated especially for your visit. Lots of extra touches that set the hotel apart, such as flat screen TV, DVD, Starbucks coffee, modern phone and clock radio. 
Free internet in the lobby was a huge benefit and was not abused. 
Ate breakfast in the hotel a few mornings and was impressed with the food and the service (unlike some other reviewers.)
I would definately return to The Argonaut on my next visit to San Francisco- during my time there I saw no other hotel that I would rather stay in. If you plan on staying at the Wharf, stay here. The other chain hotels (Holiday Inn, Radisson etc) look run down and dated from the outside.

As reported by another reviewer a couple of other travelers must have thought they were in a college dormitory as there was considerable noise in the hallway after midnight on two of the three nights I was there (and I had asked to be put in a quiet location!). On the morning I departed I had to report to the front desk screaming from the room two doors away from mine as I really was concerned that abuse might be happening. The receptionist thanked me for speaking up and said she would send someone to check right away.
While it is true that there is no free wi-fi in the business center, you are able to print your airline boarding passes at no charge. I found the staff to be very courteous. My room was clean, comfortable and the TV was easy to figure out! If I had to return to downtown Jacksonville I would consider staying here again.

I was put up in this hotel by the airlines after volunteering my seat to another traveler. I was very impressed. The hotel was great. There were many restaurants nearby. A person can easily walk there from the airport. I enjoyed it very much. The only downside is that guests have to pay for the internet.

what a wonderful place. Quirky in the best possible way and the two lovely owners leave fresh cakes for you every day. Just such a great find and really one the the best, no THE best, places we've stayed in NYC. We had the spa suite which was superb - biggest bath i've ever seen complete with a romantic fire in the bathroom and a sauna! Big rooms particularly for NYC.
fab!

I checked out both the Fairmont and Park Hyatt which are right across the street and both looked much nicer, at least as far as the lobbies are concerned.

The centrality of the location also made it a great place to stay as everything was in walking distance, and we did a lot of walking!!! 
I would definitey recommend this hotel and look forward to stay ing here again if we ever need to stay in Boston again!

The room was perfect and comfortable and the bathroom updated and spacious. The only thing missing is a hotel bar but there are plenty of those close by. You are able to buy beer and other drinks from the hotel lobby fridge which is a plus. 
Except for the -:-- unexpected wake up call by the fire alert system which directed us to please leave the room and take the stairs to the lobby to be met with Boston's finest fireman (mind you a false alarm) we highly recommend this hotel when visiting Boston. 
We definitely will be staying here again.

nice hotel but there was a baseball team and they were running in the halls and front desk did nothing to Stop IIIIIIIIIIIIIIIT, the hide a way bed the frame broke and I have a sore back. I wanted to like this hotel very badly, and in many ways it delivered. But in a few more overt ways, it failed completely. Previously we've stayed at the Park Central in midtown and the Embassy Suites downtown, but we decided to take a chance on this well-reviewed hotel on the Upper West Side. Largely a mistake.
At first, the hotel looks quite nice, with a modern lobby, decent reception staff and a great location just a few blocks west of Central Park. The room is also OK, on par with most three-star rooms in the city (ie. small, but modern enough, with a mini-fridge, flatscreen TV -- with wires hanging out -- and a big, comfy bed). 
The trouble started in the morning after our first night -- staff placed us in a room adjoining one of the noisiest families possible, with two small children screaming and waking us up at -. I understand families travel and kids are noisy, but the walls in the room were paper-thin, enough for us to hear pretty much the family's whole conversation, screams included. Luckily enough, the hotel switched us to a more quiet room after we requested. 
Everything else seemed fine until we returned to find a bag of clothing I had purchased went missing between the time we left for the day and returned in the evening. Extremely long story short: it turned out the cleaning staff had accidentally thrown it in the trash, despite it being full of new clothes -- including shirts, ties, etc. We only found this out, however, after much runaround by the security staff and front-desk personnel. And yes, we were compensated for the lost items. 
But, two thoughts: if your guests report a missing article, perhaps you should immediately move to satisfy them -- with some sort of token gesture, at least -- rather than say the investigation is ongoing and basically refusing to even apologize for the matter. And second, it takes a seriously neglectful room attendant to mistake a bag of new clothing for garbage, and to simply throw it away. Poor actions, and poor response on part of the hotel staff. 
Luckily, the security manager did manage to suss out the situation, was apologetic and compensated us on our last day there, but the whole mess hung over the trip, and I simply cannot recommend the hotel based on it. Great location, decent room and price, but overall I will be staying at another establishment next time, no doubt.

Our room was directly above the bar-lounge which had a band that played so loud that it literally vibrated the walls and floor. Fortunately they stop at - p..m. The hotel's breakfast buffet was excellent in both variety and quality.

Now I know what a fleabag is. Sure, the lobby was OK, and I mean not as bad as reviewers may have led me to expect. And there was possibly the only triangular floor in the dinky elevator I've ever seen. After making our way down the dingy, prison like hallway, I was prepared for the worst and was not surprised! The room was AWFUL. If it had been any smaller I'd have had to sleep sideways - I'm not kidding. I don't ever remember a hotel room painted bright yellow. The whole room reminded me of the Honeymooners, if you can remember that show. The curtains (a cheerful brown) were haphazardly hung on the rickety white curtain rods. I expected a train to go rattling by outside my window. The owner(s) are not ones to splurge on anything beyond the very basic. One towel was provided, perhaps to satisfy code requirements? We slept in our clothes, not trusting whether Detroit requires hotels to spray for bugs every couple of years. We will not be staying here again.

Narrow room, so skinny you have to twist your neck to watch tv that is mounted in the wall.....
Glass of wine in bar was WAY over priced! $-.-- for a half glass of house wine? Yikes!
No fridge, no microwave!
Never again Holiday Inn!
Same as I remember Holiday Inn's from years ago.

We met our son and his family at the Adolphus to spend the night and attend the Christmas
Parade. The service was excellent amid hundreds of families staying there to attend the 
Parade. The rooms were very comfortable and the food was very good considering all the food that was having to be prepared. 
We know that The French Room is wonderful, but did not have the opportunity to eat there,
but the two of us will return to have dinner later.

Stayed at Ritzs, The Bellevue in Phila, NY Hyatt, and many Marriots but nothing compares to The Affinia Dumont. My husband and I just stayed there last night. I mentioned via online reservation that we were celebrating our anniversary. We arrived to check in and was welcomed with """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Happy Anniversary"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" by front desk staff. We were immediately upgraded to a corner suite on the --th floor, a large room with amazing views of the city, Aveda bath products AND a dozen pink roses compliments of the hotel. This just doesn't happen to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""not rich and famous"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". From the moment we stepped in to the time we left, our stay was phenominal. The spa was great and breakfast at the Barking Dog was tasty. Andrey at the front desk was so helpful. He got us reservations to a great restaurant and hailed us a taxi. We were treated like royalty. Being a people watcher, I noticed the other guests were treated the same way. Many were referred to by name and one gentleman said he only stays at the Dumont when in NYC. The Sofitel is definitely a great place to stay in Chicago. The location near North Michigan Ave is very convenient. The building is visually stunning and the rooms were clean, spacious, and comfortable. My fiance and I stayed on the --nd floor and had a nice view of the city. Trying to grab a light bite or a drink at the restaurant or bar was a bit difficult, though. The bar seats were all occupied, but the restaurant was empty save for - tables. But they would not seat us for drinks and appetizers, which was very annoying, so we left for dinner early. Late night room service on the other hand was excellent. Overall, I would highly recommend the hotel - great facility at a great price...just the service needs a little more work.

As a member of JC Resorts, I have the opportunity to play a number of courses in the San Diego area. Although I live closer to several of the courses, my favorite destination is the Rancho Bernardo Inn. I have found the course a bit easier than some of the other JC courses. The outside dining is exceptional and overlooks the --th. Parking is tight.
I would recommend RBI to anyone.

We had a bay side bungalow which basically was a one bedroom suite with a couch bed. The kitchen had no stove or microwave. We initially thought we'd just cook in the room but that idea quickly faded so we had to eat on property and it got to be pretty expensive. One morning I ordered a children's oatmeal and an adult oatmeal with - milks and it was $--.--!!! just for oatmeal! I was shocked to say the least. If I had to do it again I'd just go by regular taxi and not get stuck having to wait for the water taxi to take you back to the hotel. Situated between the Meatpacking District and Chelsea, the location of Dream Downtown is ideal. From the outside it’s very unassuming, but then you walk into the lobby and it’s dark, modern, and sexy. The staff was very professional and accommodating. Upon checking-in I was immediately upgraded from a Gold King Room to a Platinum Suite. The room was dripping in chrome, leather and animal print. There was an integrated sound system throughout the entire suite, bathroom included. It also had two over-sized porthole windows leading to a balcony overlooking the pool, which is a major perk in Manhattan. If you venture upstairs to PH-D be prepared for spectacular views of the city. Dream Downtown certainly has it’s credentials. I have a feeling I’ll be back very soon.

I was at the Lowes for - days in late Oct and early Nov ----. The staff is great and could not have been nicer. I booked - rooms, both were suppose to be king suites, but were regular rooms with worn out double beds, there was no phone in my room and I had to chase down someone to get one, hall ways reeked of cigarette smoke(ohios smoke free..lol) room was dirty and other than main walkways wasn't vacuumed well.
