Stayed here a week while visiting Denver on business. I was originally given a double room but the front desk gave me a king room after I requested the change. The rooms were clean and the breakfast was good. The location was also close to several good restaurants.

I flew out to Boston in August ---- and spent time with my fiance. We stayed at the Hilton the first night in town and we only booked one night. I had seen Samatha Brown's """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Great Hotels"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on the Travel Channel and she stayed at Nine Zero and I had remembered this when we drove from the Hilton into downtown Boston. I got on my cell phone and called reservations and was able to get a room that night. My fiance and I were going to be going up to Maine the next day. Nine Zero was in the perfect location and we went sight seeing soon after checking in. It was fantastic. My fiance grew up in Massachusetts and spends a great deal of time in Cambridge, he has told everyone about the great service and the beautiful rooms. I was extremely impressed with all of it. Thanks for leaving such a beautiful and lovely lasting impression. In fact, ------- was two years ago and I remember that vacation and Nine Zero fondly. We plan to come back for one more visit.

My two girlfriends and I decided to stay at the Revere Hotel because of it's location, the parking garage that is attached, and the main reason, because it was just renovated and everything is pretty much new. Upon arriving, we were greeted with a huge smile from one of the bellman who offered assistance with our luggage and showed us to the lobby. During check in, we were offered a glass of champagne which was a nice way to start off our night, and everyone at the desk was really friendly and helpful, explaining all the amentities the hotel had to offer, like the free wi-fi, indoor heated pool and outdoor lounge area which we had no idea about! 
Our room was on the --th floor with a nice view of Boston, and a nice modern decor. After realizing I completely forgot to pack a toothbrush, toothpaste, and my most important things I can not sleep without since I am the lightest sleeper ever, were my eye mask and earplugs..so I called guest services and within -- minutes they had someone send up all the items I forgot and even sent me up a razor and deoderant as well! Neither myself nor my friends found the a-c to be too loud like some of the reviews on here say, but if you do find it too loud, just ask for some ear plugs! 
Before heading out, we stopped by the pool area which was awesome, especially the outside area which overlooks the city and there was a part set up for some kind of function which looked really nice. We then went to Emerald Lounge which is new to the hotel, and it was awesome..a wizard of oz theme, with amazing cocktails (we got a hot chili raz, a champagne drink with a popsicle in it, and a blueberry mojito).
The next morning we ordered room service and it arrived in a half hour like the girl that took my order had said it would, and had everything we ordered. My only complaint is that there wasnt that much room to eat which is why we will probably just get a suite next time we stay here. Oh I can't forget to mention the skoah products they have in the bathroom...the peppermint shampoo-conditioner made my scalp tingly and made me feel super clean! i bought them along with the bodywash at the front desk! 
Overall great experience, great location, great staff that were super friendly and so nice really made our girls night in the city extra special...can't wait to come back!

Would highly recommend this hotel. Can not beat the rate. I paid $--- per night, not including tax and parking($---day). The room was spotless, bed comfortable and nicely decorated. I would agree with some other posts that the city noise makes it hard to get sound sleep but what do you expect if you want to stay near Union Square and the Theater District. By the way, - block away Jersey Boys is playing thru September. If had known that I would have purchased tickets($-- for pretty good seats but sold out). The hotel is about - blocks from the gates of China Town and - blocks from Union Square. Wine and Cheese from ---pm but I did skip the tequilla shot at check in...maybe next time. Just be aware that the rooms are rather small so dont expect some sort of suite with desk, chair, minibar, etc.. I dont stay at too many fancy hotels when I travel. A hotel room is just a place to clean up or sleep before the next activity ,but I will say the Hotel California exceeded my expectation and based on the price and my taste, it might be the best hotel in the city from which to base out of.

The three greatest things about this hotel are -) staff, -) staff, and -) staff. And then everything else is pretty good, too. Quiet. Free parking. Exceptionally clean. Very good air conditioners, for a hotel. Comfortable (not extraordinary, but better than most) beds. Storage. Kitchenette (small fridge, microwave, sink). Wonderful shower! Loads of closet, drawer space. Wired in-room internet. Plenty of electrical outlets for recharging gadgets. Shuttle to med centers. And did I mention the stellar staff? They could write the book on customer service. Tell them what you need - no frowns, no blank stares, no tension... if they can't do it now, don;t be surprised if you get a call later with an unexpected solution. At least, that was our experience. When we return every quarter for the next two years, this will be our home away from home.

Having lived in the Richmond District in SF for - years, I like to stay in the Richmond-Sunset area when I visit so I can easily access all my favorite haunts. Easy parking, a kitchen, and good public transit are also things I look for in a hotel. And on my most recent trip, I had my dog, so a place that was dog friendly and near the beach was essential. I found all this and more wrapped up in a gorgeous little package at the Ocean Park Motel! 
The proprietor is as friendly and personable as can be. He and his wife have maintained this GORGEOUS art deco property impeccably, with its lovely gardens and courtyard, beautiful paint job, a great original neon sign (facing out to the street, so not a problem), and festive white lights framing the entryway. I got the sense that there is a wide variety of room setups, some with two rooms, some with one, so I can't speak to all the rooms. However, I was pleased with mine, #-, right at the head of the courtyard. The room was a little small, with just a bed, a dresser (with great cable TV including the digital guide, which you never find in a hotel!), one bedside table, and a small chair. I'd've liked another bedside table with another lamp. The mattress was divine and I slept really, really well. The kitchen was totally cute, and came with everything you'd need, though no mugs to go with the coffeemaker (just small disposable cup things). There was a table with two chairs in the kitchen. The bathroom was really big with a nice shower. No hairdryer, FYI. There was also a really big closet which was great for storing stuff, though it could use a light for finding stuff! The property also has a hottub, though I never had time to use it.
The location is, in my opinion, great. It's a block off Sloat, so it's really very quiet. It's just a block from the ocean, which is great. There's a great coffee shop a block away as well. The best part is that the L Taraval streetcar line picks up right by the hotel, so you wouldn't need to drive much at all! (But if you do, there's ample, easy parking.) The zoo is also right by the hotel, across Sloat. 
I would definitely stay here every time I come to SF. It's hard to find a place that has everything this place has to offer -- quiet, pretty, friendly, parking, kitchen, dog rooms, hot tub, streetcar, beach -- in SF. And it's clean and relatively cheap!

Inn at Queen Anne was a wonderful place to stay. The price was great, it was in a wonderful neighborhood with grocery stores and restaurants. 
The kitchen was wonderful to have so we didn't have to eat out for every single meal. There was a huge walk in closet to put our clothes and luggage. We were traveling with a baby and they provided us with a nice crib. The staff was extremely friendly. The breakfast was great and they had a very nice wine reception. The grounds were beautiful! We were just a short walk away from the Space Needle and the monorail. We would definately stay there again on our next trip to Seattle.

I have stayed at this property a couple of times to catch early am flights. What can I say? It's not the greatest place in the world, however, it is functional if you are not staying there for fun. The rates were not horrible the past two times I stayed there however, I could stay across the way at the four points for a bit cheaper and use it for the same purpose. The staff does need a bit of work because their attitude was a little upsetting to me. There is not much else to say except I think its good for travelers with families or people who are staying in south philly for a while.

Self-parking ( $-- per day) is on the south-west corner of the hotel. As you drive in, continue to the far side of the lot and you will be very close to the elevator to the lobby. Once you check in, your room key gives you access to the room floors. A good security feature. The room ( king) on the -th floor was basic. Comfortable bed, good size TV, comfortable air con. Great front staff - helpful and friendly. Go to the hotel website for best deals. We paid $--- per night.
 The Lincoln Memorial is just a few blocks south - a pleasant walk or $ - taxi. We really enjoyed seeing all the sites ( free ) as they are all enclosed in close proximity to one another. We saw the Lincoln, Viet Nam. Korean War, Roosevelt, Jefferson, and Washington monuments by lunch hour. The next morning, we visited Arlington Memorial Cemetery, Smithsonian, and the White house.
 Both afternoons we strolled through Georgetown, just a five minute walk down the street from the hotel. Lots of excellent restaurants and shopping. Lunch anywhere is $----- pp. One of our best restaurants was across the street from the Westin (literally) at the Blue Duck Tavern restaurant in the Hyatt Hotel. Wine, crabcake entrees, dessert 
( all fabulous) for $--pp. The next night at Kramer's BookStore and Restaurant at Dupont Circle ( $- taxi) had crabcake pasta ( excellent) and wine + dessert for $-- pp. 
 The Westin was good but basic - but the location, restaurants, and the amazing memorials were priceless ! Loved Washington, D.C. Will definately return. Enjoy !

Nice location in midtown, close to subway station. Smallest closet I've ever seen. Room is on the small side, but typical for NYC. My biggest gripe was that I had trouble getting the hotel to accept a tax exempt form from my employer (non profit) because they require I pay with a company credit card. I understand the policy, even though I provided documentation that I work at the non - profit and I was in town on business. All I wanted was a letter confirming they wouldn't honor the tax exempt form so I could submit it to my company, but the manager told me he couldn't do that but I could call the comptroller in the morning. When I said I didn't feel like they valued my business he agreed to have to comptroller call me in the morning. I really don't feel like a valued Hilton customer and don't think I'll be back.

When I enter this establishment, I feel like I am stepping into hallowed ground. The first obvious difference from any other hotel in this area are the displays commemorating the proud history of the US Marine Corps; if you are lucky, you may be greeted by two bulldogs wearing Marine uniforms, or the pup who has already outgrown his first uniform. The third floor hallways have extensive bios displayed for every commandant since the Revolutionary War. The --th floor has a memorial to all Marines who have given their lives defending the country. On every floor there are tributes to the sacrifices and accomplishments of the Marine Corps throughout their history. On this trip, a small plaque caught my attention; it had the names of six ----- year old Marines killed in action in several different wars. I increase my knowledge of and appreciation for the Marine Corps on every visit. There is a superb gym with every conceivable piece of workout equipment in the basement, including a serious three lane lap pool. The top floor houses the superb Leatherneck Grill with breathtaking views of San Francisco, great breakfast buffet, delicious dinners (had the rack of lamb this time), and outstanding service(!). I am not a Marine but I believe everyone should spend some time perusing the displays and increasing their awareness and appreciation for this great branch of the military. The arrangement of the rooms make you feel more like you are staying in someone's very comfortable home than in some kind of commercial property. I suspect that all of this great hospitality and service is attributable to a staff truly dedicated to the mission of maintaining this tribute to the Marine Corps and their members; it starts with the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""landlord"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", Major General Myatt, USMC (ret.) who served in two wars. I highly recommend this hotel experience!

Great location, close to times square but just far enough to not be busy right outside. Odd lobby system, you walk into an empty area and then must take an elevator -- floors up to main lobby. Great room.

First and foremost, our room was outstanding. We loved our room. The bed was perfect. The food quality of the in-room dining was excellent. The Mid-town location of the hotel is terrific. Most importantly, though, the service that everyone at W New York provided was exceptional. From the doorman, to the housekeeping, to the room service, every employee we encountered was professional, helpful, and friendly. My wife and I have stayed at many luxury hotels, and W New York set a new standard that will be difficult for other hotels to match, let alone beat. We are very impressed.

Perfect for seeing the city proper. Greeted by Ed at the entrance. Very friendly and helpful. Pointed us to a really good restaurant for dinner. Would definitely stay here again. Took a day trip to Salem utilizing the near by harbour boats. Very convenient to Fanuel Hall, the Freedom Trail, and the Commons.

The manager, Mr. Shah and Chris at the front desk provided us with information about places to eat, shop, and see, as well as directions and recomendations. Everyone was so friendly all the way to the cleaning staff who barely spoke English. We didnt expect much for the price but the room was clean and the area was safe to walk home to at night. Walking distance to the Riverwalk, Alamo, and Alamodome.
The beds were rock hard, the rooms had flies....lights flickered on and off in the rooms. The service was poor at best. Seemed like a shady place. Wouldn't recommend this flea trap to anyone.

This is by far the best hotel in Chicago. Excellent Service! Thank You Reservation for seeing to our """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Special Request"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Friendly-Professional-Courteous! Love, Love,Love the location...can walk anywhere. Beautiful upscale room decor. Clean, clean, clean....did I say CLEAN!
Thank You for letting us check in early & check out late!
Thank You! Our #- choice!

The bed was large and comfy, there was a CD player in the room, and the marble bathroom had a jacuzzi bath and nice sink area. Our separate lounge area had a sofa, a dresser, coffee table and lamps. There was a safe in the room, hairdryer and complimentary water. The lobby area of the hotel is a little dated but it's not horrible, like some reviews suggest. The location is two blocks from Grand Central station, so central enough but away from the buzz of Times Square. It's possible to walk to the Empire State Building in about -- minutes or so. I would recommend this hotel if you can get a good deal and secure one of the newly-refurbished rooms.

I had a - day stay at the Waldorf recently and was a little apprehensive having read other negative review. However, from our initial arrival at the front door to the doorman hailing our return taxi to the airport, we had a wonderful experience. The staff were very friendly and helpful at all times. Check in was prompt and friendly. 
Our room was on the --th floor and surpassed all our expectations. It was at least --'x--', two double beds, large flat screen tv and a great view of the Crylser Building. The room was really quiet too.
The hotel's location is superb. There is a great little diner for breakfast just a block away- 'Lunchette'. The hotel is walking distance of -th Avenue, Times Square, Central Station and Central Park. 
I have been raving about the hotel sinto all my friends and will definitely stay there again.

Room size - Small. The king size bed took up the entire room. There was not enough room for - people. The walls are also paper thin. I could hear everything including the nice conversation the people next door were having at -am.
Bathroom size - Tinny. A tall person could wash their hands and sit on the toilet at the same time. There was no room to get ready after you shower and there was no separate area where you could place your personal care products. 
The rooms are old because it is an old building but I will say that the housekeeping staff kept the rooms clean.
Service - No $-- credit was offered as part of the Kimpton membership. They said they didn't have a mini-bar in the room but that should not have stopped them from providing a certificate that I could have used in the hotel bar. They don't have water in the lobby throughout the day. They only put out cold water after -pm in the lobby. They don't offer a newspaper or all of the copies were always gone by -am every morning. 
I did not feel welcomed to the hotel. The few employees that I saw throughout the day never made eye contact or said hi to me even after I said hello to them. Even when we arrived they didn't offer us a map of the city or any help on how to get to the conference even thought they were a conference hotel. 
Fitness center - that was nice because they had enough machines and it was properly ventilated and they did have a water fountain, towels and headphones.
The location is convenient and there was always foot traffic around that area. I wish the employees had been nicer and for the price I would have liked to have some water available after a long day of walking.
Overall I was not impressed with the hotel or the staff.

We stayed at the Handlery Union Square Hotel for - nights in September-October. We had a nice room with - small double beds. The room was clean and in very good condition. There was a small fridge and a coffee maker. The hotel is in a great location, close to cable car and there are lots of great places to eat nearby. We went to Lori's more than once for breakfast. Didn't try the Daily Grill which is next door but it was always busy. The staff were all super friendly and very helpful with directions and suggestions. If you are driving in and returning your car, Hertz rental car has an office just around the corner. There is a coin operated laundrymat about a - minute walk away. We would definately recommend this hotel, we had a great time there.

The Westin Waterfront is a clean, modern hotel near downtown Boston. It is less than a -- minute ride to the airport and you can walk to downtown very easily. The room was clean and a good size. The bathroom was clean also and featured a cool double headed shower. We were on a floor they put SPG members on so we had a nice view also. The room was a decent price as well.

This was our last hotel of our vacation and after the terrible experience in New York.... This hotel is in good position, close to Michigan Avenue, the front desk have been very helpful and friendly.
Our room was very nice, very clean, and we felt really spoiled in this place...
we were interested in spending one night listening to blues music but we didn't find a place where we could go with our son who was underage.. we were suggested from the front desk staff the Kingston Mines with some discount ticket, and instruction to reach the place... and we enjoyed very much the evening!!

I only have good things to say about this hotel. Best location in Boston (Back Bay area, close to good stores, restaurants, cafe, besides being on a walking distance from Amtrak Station). With incredible rooms and excelent service, Back Bay hotel is well worth it. The building itself is very nice and hotel bar-restaurant is also a good option (specially on cold nights).

We have stayed in or near Boston a few times before, but this was our first time at the Long Wharf. We were able to get a decent rate as a Marriott Rewards members - $----night (although still a little hard to swallow with tax and daily parking fees but it was our five year anniversary). The location was by far one of the better places we have ever stayed in Boston. It was not even a five minute walk to Fanueil Hall-Quincy Market, and the North End was less than -- minutes away. It was right along the water, which we probably would have taken advantage of more had the weather been nicer, but it was still a beautiful area with plenty to do. We also took advantage of one of the trolley tours which in some ways was like door to door service because the main stop is on the side of the hotel.
I would definately return to the Marriott Long Wharf, and think it would be a fabulous place for the kids. Besides the aquarium, and other area attractions, there is a small park next to the hotel that has a small playscape and there is even a carousel just outside the back entrance. I cannot really comment on the service or amenities because we did not use any of the facilities or have a need to call the front desk or house keeping. The only somewhat of a downside is that the hotel does not have an area for free coffee and fruit (not a necessity, just a nice perk) although there was a Starbucks on the lower floor and there is the option to make it in your room. We were not expecting a free breakfast with our stay, so to keep the cost minimal (we splurged on lunch and dinner) we just grabbed bagels at Quincy Market in the morning. 
Overall, it was a very nice stay, and based on the location alone, I would definately recommend it to anyone with or without children. Our stay was pleasant, our room was clean, the beds were comfortable, there was a big screen TV in the room. In and out, our needs were met. Wish the price could have been slightly lower, but we knew that going into our stay that we could get a place with a lower price and free breakfast just outside of the mainstay. . . but then you lose the ambiance of staying in the city.

Stayed in this hotel for a week recently. Check in staff was very cooperative and helpful. Good location and close to a train station and public park. The items available for breakfast are excellent and available in sufficient quantities. Room was clean and well furnished. If I come to Boston, I will stay again in this hotel.

Many Many problems is what I would say...
Didn't get correct room service order, did not get promised benefits for being a Club Member, they did not clean the room, overcharged on breakfast, small room, no additional amenities (refrig-microwave) 
checked out early! Would NOT recommend!!

Dreadful, abysmal, dirty and unacceptable. This place is a total dump. booked this place through hotwire and it was big mistake. This place was awful and I would rate this a ZERO if i could. Terrible is not doing this justice. I waited over -- minutes for the manager to even make time to speak with me and when he did, he talked down to me and critisized me for not coming to them to make accommodation changes. I am sorry that blood stains (or what appeared to be) are unacceptable and that i dont want to stay at a place whose housekeeping things that it is ok to have that. The rooms were small, dark and dingy. The furnishings are --+ years old and look to have been rode hard and put up dirty...
DO NOT STAY HERE UNLESS YOU AND THE BABY JESUS HAVE NO ROOM EVEN IN THE STABLE.

We stayed - nights in this hotel & loved the location, clean room, comfortable bed & helpfull staff. We were on the -th floor and were not bothered at all by noise, except when the windows were open & you get the street noise. We enjoyed the shot of tequila when we checked in and the complimentary wine & cheese in the afternoons. We would definately stay here again.

Hotel is in a great location and staff is very helpful. When I asked for a recommendation for dinner in the area, one of the staff recommended a nice Italian restaurant down the street and actually walked us there. Room size was bigger than I expected for New York city. Hotel even has a car sercvice available. Down side - shower drain clogged after a shower and standing water stayed in tub all night. Toilet required two to three flushes to empty. Hotel did not offer a discount or anything to compensate when I reported it at checkout. Hopefully, this was an isolated incident. I would definitely give this hotel another chance if working in NYC again.

Our daughter is attending HBU. Not only is this hotel super close, its one of the best rooms we have ever stayed at...especially at $---.--. Our room was a two queen suite. Its like an apartment! A small living area...NICE, with a seperate bedroom. Way better than what we expected. Love the lay out of the room and the overall hotel. Friendly staff. If you're in the Houston Baptist University area, this should be your hotel.

Pleasantly surprised at the low price for the nicest, modern room with all the conveniences we needed including a nice breakfast prior to leaving for the airport. Conveniently located close to airport and restaurants.

Had to come to Seattle to visit a few friends. Had some starwood points so I tried out this hotel. 
Everyone was very nice and easy to deal with. I had a large dog with me and he was very well accepted in the hotel by all staff and others at the hotel. Hotel rooms was comfortable, clean and great bed. Really my only complaint is just the parking. It's -- bucks to park overnight and not a lot of options around but is an amazing location close to everything. Lot's of homeless people in the evening that didn't make walking around at night to fun. But over the hotel was great.

I came here with - friends (one a platinum member) for a girls trip to shop and see the sites of San Francisco. The hotel is very modern and cool. We were told we would receive an upgrade to our room and of course we were very excited. We get to the room and it is a normal standard room...... we then worry about what sort of room we would have been in to begin with. After a day of shopping we return to our room to find that it was not cleaned. We look at the room controller to see that we had accidentally left the do not disturb button on. Our bad. So one of the girls calls to have some fresh towels sent up and ask to just have our beds made. No one comes. The next day we ask the concierge to book us to see Alcatraz. She gives us the number so we could do it. Wait a second...... No we need you to do it..... So she does. We taxi down to that area early to go ahead to will call to get our tickets so we could have a nice lunch before Alcatraz. At will call we find out that only two tickets were purchased and we needed three. Of course it is now sold out. One of the girls calls the concierge to find out what happened....they say this is a normal occurrence that the Alcatraz tickets are mixed up (what?!?) but they apologized for our waisted time and said we would have a gift waiting for us in our room. That evening we come back to the room to find that yet again it has not been cleaned........with no gift. We have now had it. We talk to a manager about it he of course apologizes and sends a bottle of wine and a stress ball and candle. We brush the afternoon off and get ready for dinner. We have been so excited to use the house car (a bentley) for dinner so we go downstairs -- minutes before our reservation to let them know we would like to use the car. We over hear them ok-ing the couple in front of us to go out side the -mile radius the car is limited to. We wait for over --min. We start a new with the driver and he is amazing. We return and the valet now apologize for our wait and offer to buy breakfast. I feel like there were so many other smaller things that happened that really put a bad taste in our mouths about the St. Regis. The whole place is not horrible the restaurants, bars and of course the Remede Spa are top notch. I would NEVER stay here again but I would come back to the spa because they truly know how to make their guest feel special.

everything was good except (as usual with Marriott hotels) you have to pay about $-- per day for internet. which is unfair. the room costs enough, there is no need to squeeze as much as you can out of the customers.
Location was great.
I liked the American DIner Cafe next door..

The hotel has been updated nicely. Pros- location. You can walk or run along the lake. Garage parking.
 Cons- breaksfast buffet $--.-- per person. Soft and firm pillow choices- but we had four pillows two stating they were soft. Only thing we could not tell any differance between the soft and the firm. They were the same. All in all a nice stay and very quiet.

I read some of the reviews and was a little nervous as some people make the place seem like a rundown mess, but it was actually okay. For $--- per night on Priceline, it was a great place to drop my bags and explore NYC. The hotel staff is friendly, the room was a bit dated, but very clean. The bathroom actually had a lot of character and charm. Overall no complaints.
However, while we were out of the room, the maid came into the room and appeared to have smoked several cigarettes and a joint. She also appears to have had sex on our bed and left a giant love stain in the middle of it. She also took a giant dump in our toilet and left it there. Just kidding. I'm sure the manager who reads these reviews and responds to them had a momentary heart attack!
While the place could use some updating, this is a perfectly acceptable option for a very affordable and pleasant overnight stay in NYC. I strongly recommend it.

The hotel was very clean and well kept. The staff here was amazing and so helpful. The managers reception was a breeze and breakfast was hot and tasty. We ran off and left our sons bag there and called when we arrived home - hours later and they found the bag and mailed it to us no questions asked.
Love the vibe in this historic Houston landmark. The staff was amazing. We had a lovely dinner for two and enjoyed the surrounding area.

This properties layout reminds me of a college dorm. This is a large property by HGI standards and it doesn't fit the standard layout. It seems they try to utilze each square foot of space. The hallways are long and seem narrow. The rooms were very nice. I was in a king room with a sofa, oversized chair and large flat screen TV. There was a little area with a table-work station. Fridge and microwave in each room. The rooms were very clean, beds were comfortable, A-C was efficient and quiet. Internet service worked fine. Bathrooms were equipped with standard HGI amenities, shower had plenty of hot water and pressure. 
My collegue stayed down the street at the Courtyard and he said it was a dump. I would recommend staying at his location near the airport which is like --- minutes away. Shuttle service is provided also.

I will be back! I have been staying in San Fran for a while as i visit my college aged son. This hotel is the first i have felt totally comfortable in. The staff is friendly and the hotel itself is not what it appears from the outside. The Kimpton Group has taken it over and i believe, have given it a shakedown.....down comforters......gorgeous lobby and friendy restaurant and lounge. The food at the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Cafe"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is quite """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hotel-like"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but the service makes up for it.....plus SF is a food town! So many other places to explore other than your hotel!
This place geets major reccomendations from me. I will stay there again.
Just an update. You can get into the Casino now with a green card or foreign driver's license. Security was very nice and informative. Hotel and Salt Water was out of sight.

Universal Pricing would be honorable. Pleasant as can be, nice front lobby. Stuffy hallways but fresh room. Would not come back only based on over rated room prices and the difference from online to their billboard. High fluctuation in prices, refused to honor their own guidelines of price guarantee.

The rooms are not luxurious, but the place is clean, the free breakfast is good, and it is close to hospitals. The night-time staff were not as customer-focused as the day staff, and told us we could not have a late check-out. The day staff granted multiple late checkouts the next morning. Suggest walking for dinner to Le Central restaurant for dinner.

We first arrived to find the parking lot and all nearby parking lots completely packed and cars parked illegally all over the place - parked across corners of curbs, fire lanes, handicapped parking space slanted lines, etc. When we inquired inside about the parking situation they told us they let people pay to park there and take their shuttle van in to the airport while they were gone for days on end on their vacations elsewhere. So their hotel guests didn't have any places to park and had to walk with all their suitcases from way down the street because they let anyone pay to park and shuttle in to the airport from their lot. I asked if they had a permit for this and they claimed they did. When angry guests complained about the parking situation and asked if they could park in the fire lane they allowed them to - I didn't realize a hotel was above the law and fire safety to be able to make such decisions. The AC in our room did not work and I was hot all night despite putting the AC on high all night long. The soda machine was out of order when I wanted to go buy a water. The safety lock at the top of the door to my room didn't work. The toilet flusher didn't work properly either, it was jiggly and you had to push and hold down while twisting to the side at the same time if you wanted the toilet to flush completely. To top it all off we left very early in the morning for the airport and my husband left his sunglasses in our room by mistake. I called -- minutes later after arriving at the airport and asked them to go retrieve the sunglasses and mail them to us. I was very pleasantly surprised when they did go find them and said they would send them back if I got a FedEx return package sent to them myself. She said she would set the glasses aside with a note for the people who came in to the desk after her. I couldn't do this on a Sunday so waited a day, ordered the return package, paid for it, and just called them to confirm they still had my sunglasses a day later and the lady at the desk couldn't find them. This online review is only the first of many steps I will take to show this Super - as the horrible service that it is. No value for the customer at this place.

for a first timer to new york we wanted a nice hotel in a good area and was not disappointed at all. room was ok not best we have stayed in. The views were ok but not great. location was amazing but best of all was the staff, As from being from Australia never had to deal with tipping so gave what we thought was ok but some times missed giving as was never a issue. the rooms were always cleaned the staff was friendly and very very helpful and can not say enough about them and would stay here again any time.
only issue was WIFI in room was expensive as i found it very unreliable and when working very slow.
which caused me unknowingly to use up all my data on my ipad.

Love the rooms, and decor of the hotel. Very High-End! Hotel is No Smoking which is nice. The casino is the most upscale option in Detroit. The price for room is very high, but check out the website, they offer packages that can include gambling credit, dining credit, ect...
I am a travel agent who travels extensively, this is about an hour from my suburban home, and makes for a nice overnight couples or girlfriend getaway. Wolfgand Puck restaurant is awesome! Never any luck gambling in casino, but still fun. Dinner Buffet is pretty good, with a lot of options. Location is not really within what I would consider a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""safe"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" walking distance of other downtown attractions. Just take a cab, everything is very close by. Tigers and Lions Stadium, Fox Theater, Greektown, Restaurants, and other casinos all within a - minute cab ride. The hotel is actually one of my favorites as far as room design, very fine finishes and awesome bathrooms. Just be prepared to pay for it.

I was able to get a great rate for this hotel & I enjoyed my stay. 
Although...in my opinion, this is not a - star hotel (as other sites may suggest) Yet, it was still sufficient for my one night stay. The location of this hotel is great if you're looking for a hotel near the galleria mall. It's within walking distance to a Starbucks and has an onsite restaurant. However, I learned the hard way that room service is not -- hours.
Note: Valet parking is $--.-- & the mini refrigerator is not stocked for (pay per use). This is an older hotel, which the room furniture & decor will show. But, the room is clean & very spacious. I like that the room is separated from the sitting area & hallway (I slept well). Overall, the pros outweigh the cons. In closing..I would stay here again.

We have just arrived home after - nights at the Affinia Shelburne in NY. We were unsure about the location (--th and Lexington) when we were booking, but are very glad that we stayed there. It is close to Grand Central Station and easy walking distance to all areas of Manhattan.
The hotel is updated, with modern style furnishings and very clean, but what really stands out and make this a fabulous place to stay is the staff!! Each and everyone of them were wonderful, willing to help and very accommodating.We had an issue with elevator noise in our room and asked that we be moved,... no problem... it was taken care of while we were out touring. We were treated very well and always greeted with a smile when ever we approached the desk.We would gladly stay there again.

While I agree that the location for this hotel could not be better, I had major issues with noise during our recent stay (Memorial weekend). We got a good deal on the hotel's website ($--- per night for two double beds). However, upon check in, we were placed on the -th floor, facing Cyril Magnin Street. Even with the earplugs in place that were so thoughfully provided, we could hear street noise. Fire trucks, police cars, motorbikes, and yelling reached our rooms. Then, at -:-- a.m. on Saturday, we were awakened by a group of drunken guests making their way back to their rooms. Nice! No fault of the hotel, of course, but just added to our annoyance. On Saturday evening, we were entertained into the wee hours by a prom that was taking place in the -th flloor ballroom. Nice of the hotel to advise us that such an event was taking place. My husband had to call the front desk and ask when the thumping rap noise might cease. I would have gladly paid more for a higher floor had I been advised of the noise issues and the party. The room was OK. Decent size, clean, nice bedding, comfortable beds, good sized bathroom with very good water pressure, very prompt maid service. No fridge, lousy coffee maker, no key for the in-room safe. I would not stay at this hotel again. I prefer the quiet and super comfortable Orchard up on Bush. You pay more, but the rooms are a delight, breakfast is included and you get a really good night's sleep. Had dinner at R&G Lounge, a must in China Town (reservations advised) and also at Hyde Street Seafood Cafe, a very good place for fish. Good value, good service, on the -- bus line and the Hyde Street cable. Walk back down the hill after dinner for exercise!

Had an excellent stay at this Club Quarters. Very clean, newer room which was plenty big. Free in-room internet a plus. Very quiet location. I read some reviews about rude staff. I found them to be very friendly and helpful. It is just too far to walk to most attractions in the city. For the right price, I would definitely stay again.

We stayed at this hotel for my niece's wedding in August and it was just beautiful. The service staff is very attentive and the food is very good. Our room was on the harbor side making our view spectacular! The rooms are good size and the beds are so comfy. The only complaint I would have with the room was the air vent that blew on the bed. I wish there was a way to shift the vents so the blow would go towards the wall. It was also a little noisy because of the hallway noise but nothing too bad. All in all, a lovely hotel with an incredible harbor view, especially at night.

Recently myself and - friends visited the New Yorker for a - day weekend girls get away for my friend's --th birthday. The hotel was very inviting; we arrived from LaGuardia via New York Rides ( they were late, see that review); and were dropped off at the front door at - am. Our room wasn't ready at first but within -- minutes we were in. We were on the --th floor with a corner view so we had a great view of the city from two directions -- financial district, ESB and Madison Sq Garden. The room was clean, beds are great, relatively small room but expected in NYC; bathroom clean, towels fluffy; security on duty most of the time; conceirage useful; lower level gift shop great with good options, Overall perfect location, never ate at restaurant or used the fitness facility since we were barely there at all but I woud stay again.

I reserved a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Petite one full-bed room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and so was prepared for a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""petite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room with a brick wall view, which is what I got. There truly was just room for a double bed and one bed-side table. (Deep, built-in shelves gave you some storage space and also housed TV and CD player.) That being said, I loved the crisp modern design, and perversely, enjoyed the cosiness of the small but well-designed space. With the tans and beiges, as well as dark cork floors and dark brown marble in the bathroom, I felt like I was staying in a little chocolate box. The Italian sheets were THE most comfortable I have ever encountered in a hotel. The bathroom, too, was small, but had a nice marble shower (my partner admired a large fossilized shell) and Hermes toiletries. I think the lack of natural light would be a negative on a long stay, but for one night it was negligible. I did get a laugh out of seeing the New York Post outside my door in the morning. The lobby staff was friendly and unpretentious. I would have completely balked at the price last year, but that's what the prices are in NY right now. The block is nice and the location is very convenient to subways and most parts of the city.

We stayed here for a week. It was a wonderful stay, good continental breakfast, clean rooms, and it stays less then a square from Times Square, you can go to many attractions by foot (Central Park, Macys, Rockfeller Center, St. Patrick Cathedral, -th Av, Park Ave., Apple, Broadway, HB...), but if you preffer there are subway and bus station nearby. We'll certantly be staying here whenever we visit the city.

Upon arrival late last Friday night, Cedric tried to check us in, - persons; it took him what seemed like a longer than usual time since we were tired after driving from New York. The hotel's lobby is pleasant, but not particularly well decorated; once you reach the restaurant area or the elevators, all changes. It becomes coherent and much more attractive. Arriving at our room, we were pleasently surprised-it was spacious and also attractive, the furniture is not of quality, but it is nice. Also great beds, pillows and duvets. Great windows and a superb marble bathroom. We never got the ice and champagne glasses we called for on Friday night. On Saturday, champagne glasses were brought after a considerable wait. For the check out, Mr. Menz was most competent and friendly-I will definetely go back, but will like to check the Fairmont across the street that is very Frech and whose lobby is superbly decorated.

We had a large room by NYC standards. Bathroom was definitely more funky than functional. Staff were helpful when we needed some assistance. Very nice location between Park and -th, also close to Grand Central Station. I didn't see what all the fuss was about compared to other top rated Trip Advisor hotels I have stayed at, yet there was also nothing wrong with Morgans and the price was excellent.

This is hands down the absolute worst motel I have ever stayed at. My husband and I decided to stay there, because it was close to the stadium downtown. Now, I wish we had spent the extra $-- to stay somewhere decent. When we first arrived, they checked us into the wrong room. We had reserved a non-smoking king, and they checked us into a smoking room with two doubles. The first room smelt terrible, and there was some serious damage to the walls. We went back to the front desk, and they checked us into the correct room. This room also had some strange odors, and my husband sprayed some """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""smell good"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" stuff to try to improve the stench in the room. The first time we used the toilet, it backed up. Not to be crude or anything, but it was just urine. So, that was pretty ridiculous. We also noticed damage to the walls in that room as well, and the plastic lining that goes around the bottom of the walls was falling apart. Later on, we noticed cigarette burns in our sheets. I would honestly have to say the best part of that room was the water pressure in the shower. Other than that, it was a completely gross and unacceptable experience. Please don't waste your money here!

This hotel is in walking distance (several blocks) of the attractions in Dallas TX. If you don't want to walk, they will shuttle you just about anywhere near. There are places to eat a wonderful meal very close. You can eat steak and buffalo within a block! This hotel is comfortable. But most of all the service is out of this world. The employees here are a PERFECT example of the friendliness of Texas!

From the moment we checked in with our family at --:--PM things were bad. We booked an executive King mini-suite and all they claimed to have left were standard rooms with double beds. Then the bell hop didn't get my bags to the room for another - hours (the final duration may be much longer, I am still waiting). They cannot manage their rooms or even ensure that a customer they just affected with their own mistake gets taken care of expeditiously.

This was the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Official"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel for our recent convention. The staff couldn't have been friendlier. The rooms were well appointed, but not exceptionally large. The common areas were elegant. The bar was swanky & hopping. The pool wasn't anything special, but the fitness area was nice.
I sent myself a package there, to avoid a carry-on fee from the Airlines. They charged me $-- to sign for it. I suppose that's standard, but it seemed a tad high.
If you're going to the convention center often, this is the place to stay. If you're going for the River-walk....I'd stay closer to the action.

From the moment I called the Magic Castle Hotel to make our reservations I encounter a friendly and caring of staff. I told the person at the other end of the line, my husband and I were celebrating our --th Wedding Anniversary! That's FOUR DECADES, yikes! The young woman chuckled at my comment. I explained my husband is legally blind, and I am anticipating knee surgery within the near future. She said, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""No, problem. We have the perfect room for you."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" She was right! I asked her to please tell about the hotel ... describe it. She said the courtyard looks like a scene from the television program a few years ago called 'Melrose Place.' And that's exactly what we found ... we felt like we had walked into a movie set. The desk assistant that checked us in greeted us with a huge smile, helped me with our bags, explained some of the surround sites, and told us about the continental breakfast offered each morning. Our room was lovely. You could tell it was an older hotel that had been refurbished. But with great attention to detail! It was so clean. The bed was comfortable with a wonderful soft duvet. There was a refrigerator, a coffee maker, blow dryer, huge remote control television, makeup mirror, delicious smelling tangerine smelling soap, shampoo and cream rinse and abundance of wonderful fluffy towels. The staff surprised us with a small Anniversary cake and a card signed by each member of the staff. It was like having family help us celebrate! Additionally, the individual who made our hotel reservations, went one step further, and offered to make our dinner reservations at the Magic Castle Club for us as well. At the Club we received VIP treatment. If you are in the Hollywood area ... stay at the Magic Castle Hotel. We highly recommend it! Your stay will be magical!

We didn't like the fact that none of the ice machines were working in the middle of July. We had ice chest that we wanted to fill to cut down of the cost of buying beverages. We paid cash for our room once we arrived but the hotel still charged my credit card for the full amount too.

Great deal - not expensive, but a great service and nice room for the price. The breakfast is mediocre at best, but the staff are very helpful and friendly! I recommend this hotel if you are on a (small-medium) budget but still want a decent hotel room for the money.

The owner Randy and his family are friendly and helpful.They told you not to go to certain areas because those places are not safe enough for visitors.They gave you some warm feelings and make your stay in this hotel assembled being at home.
The room is clean and basically you got everything there.And so many channels of TV programs,not like some hotels only got handful to watch.The old-fashioned elevator,I like that to add some retro-style to this hotel.Glad Randy keeps that elevator.
There's only one thing not so pleasant,the noise on the street.But that's the way it is to live in a big city.Overall I think it is a nice experience to stay here.

My husband and I go to baltimore once a year. This hotel, was clean, safe, close to the inner harbor and comfortable. They even allow pets, although you would not know it, because it was so clean. It was also quiet. When we went there was a lacrosse tournment going on and we had about -- lacrossed players staying in the hotel and they were loud, but all we had to do was shut out door and we could not hear a thing. 
The only very very small complaint is the bathroom was small compared to the rest of the room. But functional and of course very clean.

The bed had Frette linens and was comfortable. The sheets had some stains and a hole. The room was large and the bath nice, but there was a constant noise all night long and I couldn't figure out what it was. We were on the top floor so I settled on it being noise from the roof. Other than that, it was a pleasant stay. No view on the back side but I was warned. I wanted a higher level and that was all that was left.

The Essex is a great hotel. My husband, me , and two of our friends decided to go to Chicago and used Priceline to do so. We booked a hotel called Econo Lodge. From the description on the internet it seemed fine,but when we got there it was under construction and was nasty. We called around for hours looking for another hotel when the hotel was not willing to work with us and refund our money. Thats when we finally found the Essex Inn. They were more than willing to help us and put us up for the remainder of our stay. We loved it there. The rooms were perfect.If we ever go back to Chicagowe will for sure stay at the Essex Inn.

This hotel has changed hands recently. Formerly it was a Choice Hotels property where we stayed many times. We have always liked it. The Sheraton four points facelift is attractive and they have added a restaurant that serves a sitdown order-from-the-menu breakfast that is free for the right rate (and maybe to all guests, I'm not sure). I think they are still getting the breakfast act together; communication between wait staff and kitchen seemed a little iffy,but fixable. On my comment card I advised them that for opera goers a full-length mirror is a necessity. Opera is walking distance. If you know anything about Seattle, you know that traffic in this area is a nightmare, and a sleepover is well worth the price to avoid driving in and out after the opera. We already have reservations for a week next year.

Our stay at this hotel was fantastic! We stayed - nights and - days, and we would definitely go back again. :) Everything at the hotel was kept clean and the grounds were beautiful. Our room was very clean and had a lot of space. Having a separate sink and mirror from the shower was very convenient. We spent a lot of time at the pool because the lounge chairs were so comfortable and it was very relaxing. The other pool area was also a good option for being more active (water slide, basketball hoop, and volleyball net). Everyone was very helpful and anything we needed was taken care of from the concierge, they were always available to help! We would definitely recommend this hotel!

The Oxford is exactly what you hope for when staying at a downtown boutique hotel. Great location in LoDo, close to Coors Field and lots of restaurants. Beautifully furnished lobby and guestroom, nice period furniture with modern electronics and bath. Extremely friendly, helpful staff - everyone from the front desk to the doorman and valet. Complimentary wifi worked well and we really appreciated the morning coffee service on each floor. We were traveling with our dog who was made to feel very welcome with treats and friendly greetings from all the staff and many other guests.
Our room was a Parlour Suite, which was a true suite with a living room area with sofa, desk, flatscreen TV and a separate bedroom with a king bed and another flatscreen TV, with a smallish bathroom with a very nice glass enclosed shower. A-C, controlled by a wall thermostat, was quiet and efficient. Our package rate included valet parking and the hotel does not charge a pet fee, so we thought it was quite a good value. No surprises on the bill at checkout, just the room rate and taxes, no previously undisclosed additional fees. Basically a perfect experience from beginning to end!

Although this isn't the Taj Mahal of Crowne Plazas, I will say that my stays have been pleasant. I frequent many of the major hotel chains throughout the year and I will say that the staff here really does care about the customer. The rooms are clean, the food- drinks are good, and valet service is prompt. Any issue I have experienced has been resolved-- always exceeding my expectations. The Night Manager Ms. Flemming is top notch when it comes to getting things done, as well as making my stays comfortable. If your not getting what you expected--see her! In this day and age, customer focus far surpasses customer service. Overall, I will continue to stay at this property when I visit Memphis--largely due to the staff.

This hotel is clean and comfortable. The staff is helpful. It is no frills, but the price is right. It is located within walking distance to the Van Ness Metro. Parking on-site is reasonable, as well. I have stayed here many times and would do so again. The only cons is that the walls are """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""thin"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and so at times it can be noisy.

This was my first time staying at an Omni Hotel, and I was very impressed. They are comparable to the Fairmont. The bed was comfortable but not plush. There were two very comfortable, cushy chairs by the window which looked out on a beautiful view of trees, an old building (now a gift shop), the Delaware River in the distance, a bridge, etc. We were on the -th floor. My view was much better than the one I got at a Fairmont recently, and I didn't have to pay extra for it! I could even see the view from the bed. Loved it!
When we returned at night, our t.v. looked like an aquarium, and soft music was playing. It was fun to just sit and watch the fish, listen to the music, and relax. Ice was in the ice bucket, and we hadn't even asked for it. The face mirror with the light on it was lit up in the bathroom. 
The bathroom had a large countertop with plenty of space. The shower had the curtain rod that arcs so that the curtain doesn't go toward you when you're taking a shower. I got a kick out of the fact that they have a phone on the wall right next to the toilet! The shower head was high up on the wall. It was one of those large heads which I think they call rain heads. I liked how they had the towels on a rack inside the shower area, but it wasn't so good for my short mother who couldn't reach them without my help. It would be nice if they put a lower bar in the shower for older people. 
The desk was set up for business. I appreciate how the light had two outlets on it so that I could recharge my camcorder and camera at the same time without having to crawl under the desk to get to an outlet. There was a very comfortable rolling chair to sit on at the desk.
The alarm was part of a Bose system. Nice!
The location of this hotel was perfect for my mom and me. We could walk to most of the major attractions or buses. Independence Hall is on the same street on the next block. The Liberty Bell is across from Independence Hall. There was always a taxi outside the door just waiting. The doormen were very helpful and opened doors for my mom. 
We ate in the lounge our first night there and had a delicious chicken cheesesteak sandwich. Yumm! The lounge looked very classy, as well as the lobby. I loved the chandelier and lights in the lobby.
I would definitely stay here again!

The main thing here is the location: it's a - minute walk from Hollywood walk of fame and up to -- minute drive to most of LA tourist attractions. It's very easy to find your way to popular attractions such as Universal studios, Beverly Hills, Venic Beach, Farmers market etc. It has free parking which is great and the manager is very nice. 
The only critict I have is that we had bugs in our room (not bedbugs so don't freak out) - Mosquitos and such. It wasn't too bed. When planning our annual trip to New York, I wanted to get away from the midtown hotels and stay more towards Greenwich Village. We have walked around the Village numerous times,, but have always gotten lost, what with its narrow streets intersecting this way and that, without the perfect grid system of midtown streets. We also have been following the High Line project--the redevelopment of an old elevated railroad platform into a lovingly and cleverly designed landscaped walkway-- as well as the construction of the Standard Hotel straddling it. So when we discovered the Standard would be open during our planned visit, we eagerly booked there. We were able to get a good web-only rate similar to the soft opening rate the hotel initially offered.
The Neighbourhood. 
 The hotel is located in the Meatpacking district just north of the West Village. It straddles the High Line and is quite an impressive sight, -- stories tall. We first visited this area when the boutique Jeffrey opened on --th St. a number of years ago . Back then the area truly did consist of mostly meatpacking facilities. A few of these still remain, but most have become designer shops, clubs, lounges and restaurants. The nightlife here is very active--weekdays and weekends we witnessed crowds at - am and later--people who require very little sleep and-or don't go to work until the afternoon, if at all. Over the course of our - day stay, we saw exactly - children in the area, all during daylight hours and none within the hotel itself. The hotel offers queen or king rooms only; - people maximum per room.
The nearest subway stop is about a - minute walk away.
The Hotel Public Rooms.
There is a large outdoor seating area in front of the lobby, which is smallish but stylish, a bit retro looking. The elevators all have - unique video screens playing a mesmerizing continuously scrolling presentation, with music. There are several lounge spaces on the ground floor, both indoors and out, with the largest being outdoors under (and protected by) the High Line--very popular. The restaurant The Standard Grill is adjacent, also with indoor and outdoor seating. Not yet opened is the top (--th) floor lounge-club, which apparently will have pool, and is certain to be a hot spot once it opens in about a month. It will surely be a velvet rope type of place, and I would expect there may be difficulty (or at least a wait) for guests just trying to return to their rooms. Even now, over the weekend there was security at the elevators, asking for room keys and checking guest names from a list. There is a large gym on the --th floor with fabulous views in - directions, including the Hudson River. There is no business center (but Wifi is free) or spa.
The Guestrooms.
Our web rate was for a Standard Queen, but we were upgraded to a south-facing Superior Queen, a slightly smaller room but with a better view. Apparently all the Standard rooms face north, where one gets a glimpse of the river. High Line and Empire State Building, but mostly one sees a large building being built one block north. From the south-facing rooms, there are virtually no buildings taller that the hotel, so one can clearly see Downtown, the southern tip of the High Line, much better views of the Hudson River, New Jersey and the Statue of Liberty. 
We were informed at check-in as well as via a letter delivered to the room that the floor-to-ceiling windows were non-reflective, so without your drapes drawn, people below can see EVERYTHING, and this apparently has been an issue, based on things we'd read online. Indeed, whenever we looked down at the High Line, there were always people staring up at the hotel.
The room was not large, but I've seen smaller in New York, and things were designed to maximize space--a built-in seating area, - sides of the bed placed flush against the wall (the person with the stronger bladder should sleep against the wall). The colour scheme is black, white and beige. The flat screen HD TV froze a lot.
The bathroom was tiled in black with a laboratory-like sink and counter fixture. The bath products were cleverly packaged. Very early TA reviews of the hotel mentioned the flooding situation involving the shower, and we bore witness to this in our room. The shower is not enclosed, with only a small glass partition between it and the sink. Only the water temperature can be controlled, not the volume (this is true of practically every hotel shower we've used for the past few years), so the water naturally flows out onto the floor, which is not sloped enough towards the drain. We learned quickly to form a dam using a towel (very large and fluffy by the way) to contain the water. Indeed, after showering, the driest place in the bathroom was in the bathtub, which was huge and open to the bedroom with shutters. The toilet was in a separate water closet.
The Staff and Service.
The staff was all quite young and stylish, courteous and helpful for the most part. Male staffers seem to outnumber the females. Our one exception was with an unfriendly room service attendant, but this was after midnight and he was doing double duty--taking an order on a mobile phone while delivering our order.
This was a fun hotel in a fun location. It's not a - star place, nor does it strive to be, but it delivered on most fronts. Again, it's not a place for families with small children or friends who are not intimate with each other. or for business. Coming from Los Angeles, we think this Standard has more to offer than either of the LA Standards.

This was my first time at the DoubleTree, and I was really amazed at the service I received. The staff at this location was outstanding, the hotel is top notch. I had to travel for business but I will now look for other doubletree for leisure as well. Thanks for a great experience and keep up the great work!

While the first room they offered us was tiny (corner room), since that was all that was available, we waited and got a larger room (queen size bed, though they admitted it was shorter than the average queen bed). After the high prices at a nearby Hyatt, we appreciated the refrigerator for our use (vs. the Hyatt Regency where a Pepsi cost $-.-- and a sign warned us that using the fridge for our own items could result in a $-- fine), and microwave and plates and utensils if we wanted to eat in. I decided to give this place another try since it changed from Wyndham to Crowne Plaza a couple of years ago. Experiences when it was a Wyndham were not good at all, because they had let it get pretty run down, cut corners on maintenance, and the staff was not very helpful back then. I was pleased to see that the renovations in ---- made it more pleasing, the bedding was upgraded, and they installed flat screen TVs. The front desk staff was efficient and polite at checkin and gladly answered any questions.
The only reason I didn't rate this Crowne Plaza higher is because it isn't as polished as some I've been to, and the bedding isn't as plush and comfortable as others. I didn't notice much noise from the adjacent rooms, but there is little soundproofing between the bathrooms (you can hear haridryers, coughing, and such through the exhaust vents) and you can hear everything that takes place in the hall. And, if you need the elevators during a busy time, the wait can be longer than I liked. I'd also recommend eating all your meals somewhere else (the breakfast is $--.--).
Yes, I will probably stay here again next year simply because it is so convenient to the Convention Center and way more affordable than the Marriott across the street.

The Hotel San Carlos is a hidden jewel in downtown Phoenix. It's one of the city's most historic buildings, rich in history, and staying there is a unique and wonderful experience.
In its heyday, the Hotel San Carlos was a favorite of the Hollywood set. You can stay in Marilyn Monroe's suite, Mae West's suite, or rooms where Clark Gable, Spencer Tracy and other icons stayed while in Phoenix. 
The owner of the hotel is a Phoenix history buff and published author; the hallways on all - floors are filled with old photographs and news clippings about the city and its history.
We got a kick out of the story about the hotel being haunted by the ghost of a girl who threw herself from the -th floor. 
I couldn't help but rave about this hotel to the manager as I left. She showed her appreciation by giving my son and I a tour of the entire place. Everything about this hotel makes you feel like you're living the life of luxury in the '--s, which is a fantastic experience. You won't get that at any of the more modern hotels in Phoenix. It's historic, but it's clean and well appointed and has all the conveniences of a modern hotel.
The only negatives about the Hotel San Carlos are parking (valet parking is $---day, but not easily discovered; but the parking problem is typical of all downtown hotels) and the restaurant, the Ghost Lounge, which is a separate leased operation - it doesn't fit the character of the rest of the hotel. There is an adjoining coffee shop, however, which serves breakfast and lunch.
I won't stay anywhere else when I'm in Phoenix.

I was a bit apprehensive about our stay after reading some of the postings -- my main concern was about noise, so I phoned ahead and requested a room on a high floor away from the pool.
The hotel was able to honor our request and we found the staff as a whole extremely friendly and helpful. The concierge even went so far as to recommend the lobby of a nearby rival for photo opportunities (i photograph architecture as a hobby).

We enjoy the modern decor and furnishings -- the Salomar's common spaces retain a warmth that other hotels lose in a cold sea of tragic hipness, and that frostiness sometimes makes its way into the attitude of the staff, which is not the case here.
Our room was quiet and very comfortable; and we did take advantage of the happy hour. Our only regret was that we did not have a chance to sample the food at J-Six, the hotel's restaurant, but we'll definitely stay there again and try it next time around.

We had the most wonderful time at the Pacific Terrace Hotel. We have two children ages -.- and - years so we stayed in a Family Suite (two rooms) the first two nights. The suite was well equipted and had a refrig, kitchen table, plates and utensils so we were able to eat fruit and cereal most days before heading out. We were thrilled with the location. You are right on Pacific Beach and it is beautiful. The boardwalk runs for -.- miles or so and it is just gorgeous.

turndown service at night with bottles of evian. 
someone always at the front door to welcome you and open the door. Once, there was no one at the door and one of the valets saw me coming and RAN to open it for me.

nice room, clean, good housekeeping, good breakfast, lots of restaurants nearby, close to metro, free newspaper, irish pub onsite. traveled w- handicapped friend who left his crutches in the room. called from airport, hotel put them in a taxi and we got them in time! one concierge was not much help but staff in general ok. small closet. nice handicap accessible rooms. requested refrigerator-no charge. bed-pillows good. area looked a little iffy but we never felt threatened or fearful. overall a good experience. would return.

Walking into the W, you immediatly notice that they're going for a cool, trendy, edgy vibe. It's very different from most hotels. The lobby area, or """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lving room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" as they call it, is --story, dark, with techno music and constant video displays on - walls. Yes, I'd rather stay at a Westin. We'd all rather stay at a Westin, but this property, for the price, is well above average.

Yes it's relatively cheap and the locations great for the East Village and Soho, but we had pigeons nesting on our air conditioner which is fine if you want to get up when they do ie. -am, but not so good if you want to sleep any later than that. The bathroom was large, with a glassed-in shower with rainforest shower head. Best of all, the toiletries were made by Fresh and were lovely. 
The hotel also has - roof decks for guest use and a fun restaurant in the lobby - it has an indoor lounge and outdoor terrace that seem to be extremely popular with young businesspeople. The restaurant isn't cheap, but it's worth checking out.

If you're not a walker, the hotel is about - blocks from one end of the cablecar line as well as the Embarcadero BART station, and the streetcars go past the hotel as well. We found it a convenient walk to Union Square, the SF Moma, etc., but we really like walking.
