What is there to dislike about the Tapatio? It is one of the best hotels in the Phoenix-Scottsdale area and you can get a room for $--.-- until Jan. -th (and around $------ after…good breaks for AAA members). We have stayed at the Phoenician, The Hyatt at Gainey Ranch, The Wigwam, etc. (Someone mentioned that they left the Tapatio because they thought it was not up to snuff, and they were going over to the Phoenician...just be aware that the Phoenician is about - times the cost of the Tapatio.) Of all those hotels, we often prefer to go to The Tapatio because: 
  -. Wonderfully friendly staff who go out of their way to say hello or to help you out. This includes the check-in staff, the hotel room-service delivery people, the gift shop people and the whole assortment of the people at the golf course. Someone commented in a post that “...the service people always had their hand out for a tip.” I have never felt pressured to give anyone a tip. However, at any resort tipping is just part of the deal. It is normal to tip: the bellboy, the waitresses, and anyone who does something special for you such as bring an extra pillow, etc. Also, at any golf course, it is proper to tip the person who cleans your clubs when you come in. 
-. The rooms are suites. The first is, of course, the living room. That is separated from the bedroom by an ingenious system of doors on either side of the bathroom (The bathroom has a pass-through from the living room to the bedroom…basin and mirror on one side, toilet and bath on the other with a door.) which is between the two rooms…one that closes between the living room and the bathroom and one that closes between the bathroom and the bedroom; this allows people in one room to close off the other room but to still use the bathroom. Also, the T.V. on in one room can’t be heard in the other. I see in a couple of posts that people though the place needs up-grading. Actually, the hotel did one of those hugely expensive “re-dos” two years ago. Unfortunately, the colors they picked are a bit drab which gives the rooms a less that bright appearance. The beds have feather pillows and feather quilts. There is a wet bar and refrigerator in the living room. - wide screen t.v.‘s., and adequate lighting by each side of the bed.
-. There are two main restaurants. One is paneled with mahogany and is very handsome. Good food, reasonably priced for a resort. Great bar and a friendly atmosphere. Then there is their very slick “A Point of View” restaurant with terrific views of Phoenix-Scottsdale, but we have not eaten there.
-. You want pools? They’ve got pools. A huge water-wonderland set up with slides, etc. Two smaller pools are near the main part of the hotel…rarely busy (one is adults only), and one on top of the hill. Fitness center. And here is something outstanding: the hotel does not charge the usual $---$-- a day “resort fee” which I have come to hate at all hotels. 
 -. GOLFERS! Listen up. The course is terrific. It is kept in first-class condition. The course has been called “the Phoenix areas best kept secret.” The staff was very accommodating. The course climbs up and up until the -th (at which point you are - miles from the clubhouse) where you can see for miles in either direction. There are some pretty tricky holes where doglegs, water and thick desert flora abound. Deep traps. Undulating greens, Fun. 
  I wasn’t paid to be this upbeat about the hotel! I just think it is great place. It isn’t going to all things to all people…but give it try. I think you will be pleased.
Rooms were clean, huge and nice. But too expensive for hotel near the airport. For that price, I rather stay in west Los Angeles or near downtown. They really should lower their price.

The Marina Motel was one of the best parts of my husband and my visit to San Francisco in early September. The motel courtyard, which our room looked out upon, was like something from times past, and made for peace and quiet in the evenings. Lombard is a busy street, but you wouldn't know it from how the rooms are situated. Our accomodations were modern, clean, cozy- just great. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The public transit system in SF is great, and we used the bus which had a stop very near to the motel. The neighborhood had excellent restaurants & shops of all sorts just a block or two away. When we return, we will definitely be booking at the Marina Motel.

My Mom, daughter and I stayed here for one week in September, and we booked it on Expedia. 
The overall experience was average, except for one outstanding employee....he is the evening Manager at Front desk, and his name starts witht the letter T'. He made our trip-he was so helpful in making reservations and getting us directions. His general attentiveness was very much appreciated. Thank you!!!
When you are booking this room, be sure to ask for the larger of the - double occupancy choices, because there are - sizes of rooms, and the one you see on the internet is the BIGGER room. You wouldn't have belived HOW SMALL our room was, In fact we requested a cot prior to our arrival, and it was in the room when we arrived.....I am not kidding, we COULD NOT open it up due to the small size of this room (see the photo I uploaded). Oh ya......ask for a room that faces --st street, not the back alley.
THE restaurant in the hotel is VERY PRICY.....our bill was $-- for three buffet breakfasts.....there is a neat cafe right beside the hotel called CAFE METRO (they are all over Manhatten too), but we could get breakfast there and late night snacks as well, so that was a good thing.
The room was cleaned adequately each day, but the decor and overall style of the rooms could use some updating. The beds and pillows are good, but we were so tired at the end of each day, we could have probably slept on the floor.
Coffeemakers are available ONLY BY request, so be sure to request one if you are a coffee drinker......ONE issue was the maid forget to provide us with coffee each day, so every night we had to call the front desk for more coffee, so we would have it ready to make in the morning. Finally on the last night, the restaurant manager brought our coffee up, and when he found out we didnt get coffee all week, he gave us - breakfast buffet coupons (remember, that's worth $--), so we really appreciated that and we enjoyed a buffert breakfast before leaving for a long day of traveling.
Location was good.......the blocks are long but depending on weather its nice to walk so you can see all the shops and cafes along the way. The 'all loops tours' bus stops right on --th and Lexington, so we used that lots to get back and fourth from Times Square and Broadway shows. Also, there is a subway station on the corner of --st and Lexington (right beside the hotel). The one on the same side of street as hotel goes all the way downtown (Brookyn Bridge, Canal Street, etc) and the one across the street goes uptown. My recommedation is to get a metrocard of you are using the subway or buses for transportation-you can buy them at each subway station.
Hope this was helpful-take care

My husband and I checked in late one night and then checked out (including return of room keys) almost immediately when we found we couldn't stay due to a family emergency. The dishonest hotel staff promised we wouldn't be billed -- then falsified their records to make it appear that we'd been there until the next morning! Speak to a manager? What manager? He's """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""in a meeting"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that lasts twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week. Enough said.

Stayed here for four nights at the end of May, had a few reservations after reading other reviews but was pleasantly suprised on arrival.
Room was adequately sized but clean, but it didnt really matter because we only really slept in there. The location is the best thing about this hotel, right in the heart of Times Square. 
Overall this hotel has such a good location for such a good price and I could not complain about anything. The staff were friendly and helpful and at the end of reading some (bad) reviews I would like to stipulate that you get what you pay for. I would definelty stay at this hotal again, it is reasonably priced, clean and has a great location, what more could you ask for a trip to NYC!

This motel is an excellent value and very close to to everything we wanted to do. The staff was very helpful with directions and dinner suggestions. Rooms were very clean and the property well groomed.

Booked the Sommerset suites after reading the reviews on Tripadvisor. Wanted a hotel near to Hillcrest as the hotel circle is too far out for nights out. Great location, - minutes walk to bars and restaurants. The rooms were a really god size, clean. Nice to have the separate living room. Pool area is clean although the pool could be heated! The breakfasts were good. Really liked the social hour every night, a nice touch. Martha the maid was extremely friendly and ws a really welcoming ouch to the hotel. Would definately stay there again. Recommended.

Our group of ten ladies from Ontario, Canada, returned yesterday from our weekend trip to New York City. The majority of those in attendance were mothers and daughters. We had two rooms of four and one of two. The Hilton Garden Inn was absolutely perfect for our needs: well not first class, certainly more than acceptable. The rooms were well sized with plenty of room for four (two queen sized beds). They were clean and well maintained. Each room had a small fridge, microwave, and coffee maker. Unfortunately when we arrived only one room was ready but it was wonderful that we could all put our suitcases in the one room and go exploring in Times Square. The front desk would not allow me to check in unless my room was ready but they did reserve and promise me the room across the hall from our friends. When I again attempted to check-in they informed me the guest who already had the room decided to stay another night. Meanwhile my firends were waiting for me outside the previously assigned room and spoke with the occupants. They said they had just checked in and were staying for three days. It is unfortunate that when a hotel messes up they don't make the choice to simply admit it and apologize, instead they decide to cover up with an excuse. Although frustrated my friends and I were not deterred. We enjoyed the wonderful location of the hotel. The play """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Spelling Bee"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (great fun!) is just a block down and around the corner, Times Square is a perfect -+ block walk, and taxis are always handy. Because of our disappointing check-in we were given a dozen free breakfast coupons which we shared with all our group. The restaurant is relaxed and our breakfasts were tasty and well served. The bottom line is that the Garden Inn more than satisfied our needs for first time visitors to New York city and we would without hesitation stay there again.

I stayed one night at the Charlesmark, which is located in the heart of the activity of Boston. Very close to the T, and surrounded by dining and shopping, and the ritzy Newberry Street. Close to Boston Common as well.
The room was very nicely appointed and comfortable, albeit somewhat small. I had a view of the alley behind the hotel, but I guess someone has to have that view. The hallways to my room were very narrow, making it difficult for me to pull my two pieces of luggage easily.
I found the staff to be friendly and helpful.

I can see why people have weddings or private party's here. The location is in beautiful hill country. The hotel is rather mediocre, for the price. We ate dinner down stairs at the restaurant and it was ok, for $--- it could have been better. The service was fantastic! Our waitor made the BEST Mexican Martinis. The spa was delightful. Breakfast in the morning was a fabulous treat. 
Not sure if I would stay here again?

Husband and I (mid --s) stayed here for - nights Sat Dec - and Sun Dec - to be close to Universal Studios (- metro stop away, though we didn't feel safe in the metro subway at -.--am on a Sunday morning - very quite and isolated and shady in-your-face characters try to get money from you for 'helping' you to use the automated ticket machines and 'kings of the metro' who harrass single and groups of women ... take a cab instead) and the Warner Bros Studio Tour (completely brilliant - just do it!). Hotel staff were extremely helpful and accommodated our request for a quiet room away from the pool area. Unfortunately on Morning One, our shower didn't work properly and water just spurted everywhere all over the bathroom floor. The conceirge came up and said there was a knob missing. He gave us a key to shower in a room on the next floor up. This was inconvenient, but our shower was fixed by the time we returned from Universal Studios later that day. The room upstairs was much nicer and better updated than our room, and while he offered us an exchange of rooms, we prefer not to move once we've settled as we're already staying in - hotels during a - week stay. Providing we can get some sleep, we can cope with any other little inconveniences. No breakfast was provided, but go to the Fresh and Easy supermarket a few blocks up the road for supplies to make your own breakfast - other meals (the frozen vegetarian selection is outstanding!) The best thing we did in Hollywood was take the Kodak Theatre tour which is right next door. When you are standing on the front steps of the Orchid Suites, look up on your immediate right and see a long glass corridor with yellow paint underneath. That's where the Oscar winners walk past the photos of previous winners after coming off stage to do their press interviews. This tour was the entertainment highlight of our whole - week trip to the US (especially walking out onto the stage itself, then taking Johnny Depp's front row centre seat while learning more about the theatre and Oscars ceremonies).This hotel is definitely not the Ritz, but you coudn't get any closer Grauman's Chinese Theatre (we missed the tour there but bought tickets to see a film inside), the sidewalk stars (not the dodgy fakes dressed up as stars who charge you to take their photos!) and the celebrity hand and footprints. The UWink restaurant in the Hollywood and Highlands centre is a bit of fun for a meal (except when -- drunk male and female 'Santas' arrive right after you've placed your order on the computer screen on your table and get even more drunk while you wait for your meal!) The Orchid Suites staff were happy to mind our luggage after check-out until our LuxBus came to take us to Anaheim. We can't imagine staying anywhere else during a short, low budget stay in Hollywood.

For the price and location, its a pretty good deal. We had # --- and the A-c was not working, so we got switched to #---. Its a pretty noisy part of town. All night I heard the metal from the trolley rail. Every time a car drove over the railing, it was obnoxious. The only thing offered is coffeetea in the morning for free and that was alright. Theres no pool or jacuzzi and the rooms were ok. Nothing great. I'm sure for the price, you can find something better.

If you like a lot of space and an ocean view, this is the place for you. Housekeeping here is excellent and the staff is helpful. Free parking is a definite plus. This is a great place for a family and the bus at the corner takes you right in to downtown. We've stayed here on two occasions and we'll definitely be back!

Excellent location for the mall and museums and not far from the Capitol and Library of Congress. I was here on business with the National Gallery a -- minute walk. Had stayed here several years ago and the location worked well for me. Room was fine and quiet (faced the inner courtyard). Lobby was large.
The metro is a short walk. No restaurants nearby. I ate in the hotel restaurant (Bistro) one night and thought it was good. For something quick there is a McDonalds a half block away. Also a Quiznos Subs and a Starbucks.. A CVS pharmacy next door. Always seemed to be cabsa round. Staff was friendly.
A good choice if you are touring the museums around the mall.
Good location, nice rooms, comfortable beds. Workout room a bit on the small size but service was good as usual from Kimpton.

My husband and I stayed here while visiting Chicago. The Conrad is a nice hotel and moderately priced for the area, but beware of package deals from Hilton. 
Let me start out by saying, overall we enjoyed our stay at the Conrad. Our room was very clean, the beds were appointed nicely and we had a nice large flat screen TV in our room. The hotel is in a very good location. Close and within walking distance to many attractions, but far enough away from everything that it is quiet and peaceful at night. 
We only had two main issues with the hotel…one moderate and one major issue. Moderate first, the air conditioning. Although, the air conditioner was on --, our room was warm. After calling the front desk, a maintenance technician came to our room. He informed us that the hotel had installed energy efficient motion sensors in each room. The sensor recognizes when someone has entered the room. When this occurs the air conditioner then comes on…great for saving the hotel money…bad if you are out all day and enter into a room that takes forever to cool down. The maintenance technician “fixed” it so that we could have cooler air all the time. Problem solved. 
Our biggest issue was our package deal. When we booked the Conrad through Hilton, we bought their package that included parking. The representative over the phone told us that the parking would include onsite self-parking. Sadly this was not the case. Although the hotel does have self-parking which is attached to the hotel and shared with Nordstrom’s, we were made to park two and a half blocks from the hotel. Upon check in we were told that the parking package was for a parking garage off-site. WHAT! 
Needless to say, this morning when we went to get the car at -am it was extremely scary. Please be forewarned, if you are driving, do not get this package. Not to mention, the parking that is attached to the hotel, was only a couple dollars more than the package. 
Other than the aforementioned, the hotel was nice AND if you stay over on a Sunday night, I highly recommend eating at the hotel restaurant located on the roof top. Every Sunday night, they show a movie while you are eating dinner. Very nice! Please feel free to email me if you have any questions.
Go to priceline and bid on something. This place is not where you want to die!

The hilton garden inn is located in a very convenient part of town. It in within a few miles of most anything you could need. There are a couple places within walking distance, but will most likely need a car to reach good food and shopping. 
The rooms were the great hilton standard, each includes a mini fridge and microwave. The breakfast is the best I have seen. It includes made to order waffles with all the toppings, oatmeal, eggs to order along with the buffet with all the trimmings. My favorite is they had a full variety even including cooked veggies on the buffet along with lots of fresh fruit. The buffet is $--. 
Complimentary each early evening they have fresh cookies and in the morning they had danish and coffee. Parking is $--.
This would be my hotel of choice when visiting the area again. I also attended a conference at the double tree suites - - blocks away when I was there. The hilton garden inn far exceeded the sister hotel. 
This hotel was great.

I should have turned right around and checked out when I walked up to my hotel room door and it looked like it had been kicked repeatedly. Black scuff marks coved the bottom of the door, which gives a very bad impression. The room itself appeared to be fine until I began to notice small things. There is no safe or make-up mirror in the room. Also the in-room coffee is horrible. There was a used dried up package of coffee left over in our coffee maker--yuck! 
The room felt dusty, there was a huge red stain in front of the little sofa. The hair dryer was broken, in pieces and put back in the little cloth bag and left for the next guest! The bed was very hard, and the shower drain was very slow. All in all, not a good stay. I am very disappointed in this Hilton property and will not be staying here again. 
They do have free breakfast, and wifi. And the rooms look nice but feel dirty. There are no elevators either so you have to lug your own bags up the stairs if you have a room on the -nd floor. Also, no bellmen or any help.

Found this hotel to be overated. We stayed in a renovated room on the -- floor. We had a great view of the River. The room is small. Poor lighting. Bathroom was weak. Stainless steel sink and counter. Very little room for storage. Service was weak. Althought there was a car show at the time. Not impressed with this Westin!

I'm really surprised at the negative comments about this hotel. No, it's not the Hilton. However, it only cost us $---night. For the price it was a great place to use as a base for visiting Sea World and the San Diego Zoo. 
I think the name is misleading as our room was not a suite, but it did have a separate kitchen area. Still, the room was clean, appeared to be well kept, and clean. There were several reasonably priced, idependently owned (ie non-franchised) restaurants within walking distance.
The staff was very helpful and friendly. Breakfast (cereal, oatmeal, bagels, donuts, toast, and fruit) was included. Our - year old loved the garden and fountain, the heated pool, and the hot tub. If you're ultra picky then go somewhere else. If you know a good value when you see it then this may be your place. If I were returning to San Diego I'd book another room here without hesitation.

The hotel aspires to be in the same class as luxury hotels likeThe Four Seasons, The Peninsula, the Ritz-Carlton, but I felt the service was far short of what I have experienced at those hotels. Although it was a very busy weekend (Chicago marathon, Notre Dame football game), a five star establishment should be able to handle the volume without any decline in service. From it taking over an hour to get our bags after check-in (and only then after a call to chase them) to failure to acquire tickets to a show by the concierge (again I had to repeatedly chase the status of my request), the Trump Chicago did not in anyway exemplify the type of service I would expect, particularly when paying top dollar for one of their largest suites. I would suggest choosing another - star establishment - the Trump Hotel is just not in the same league.

My husband and I stayed at the Crowne Plaza Metro for our first trip to Chicago. We had originally booked at a Hampton Inn on Travelocity, but it was overbooked and Travelocity recommended this hotel at the same pricepoint. I did a quick check of the Tripadvisor ratings before I committed, but then when I read the reviews, I started to have my doubts. 
Well, I shouldn't have worried at all. True, the hotel is many blocks away from tourist attractions, but if you don't mind walking a bit and-or using mass transit like us, you'd find it just fine. My husband and I, unfamiliar with the layout of Chicago, ended up getting off the Blue line at Monroe and walked about -- minutes to the hotel. Location-wise, while it is not near the metro, there's a bus stop across the street (in front of the Dominick's grocery store); the - will bring you up the street to Milwaukee-Grand to catch the Blue line, (which is what we did at the end of our trip to take us straight into O'Hare). The bus system in general is very well run...we bought at -day transit pass for $--pp, and that was the best deal, as we used it many many times. The best part of using mass transit on our trips is that it makes us feel not as touristy. (Remember...it's the journey, and not necessarily the destination...) 
Speaking of the Dominick's grocery store, we were happy to find it so convenient, even though we only used it to buy bottled water, and coffee from the Starbucks stand inside. There's also a Walgreens on the other side of the hotel. There are also hot food options inside (prepared foods, a sandwich stand, etc.) The proximity to Greektown allowed us to pick up a gyro at -AM after we came back from a late night comedy show at Second City as well!
As for the rooms, we got upgraded to a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Deluxe"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I don't know how my room was different from the other ones, but we were disappointed that we got two doubles instead of one king. The room had a nice color scheme of neutrals, but sort of dark. The light over one of the beds was not working, but we didn't bother to call downstairs. There was a flat screen TV. Beds were comfy, and were piled with four different pillows (firm, soft, flat, etc). Bathroom was very clean and I liked the fluffy towels. There was complimentary wireless internet service as well. The only thing that I would have really wanted was maybe a minifridge. 
Check out is at --pm. Since our flight was at -, we asked to have a late checkout, and they provided us with a -pm check out. Overall, we would definitely consider staying here again

We stayed here recently and were blown away by the wonderful hotel rooms, the superior service, and great location. Dwayne (spelling?) greeted us at the door and was very helpful, suggesting options for dinner and things to do around the neighborhood, as well as taking the time to show us the features of our room (including the heated floors in the bathroom). The rest of the staff was great and very friendly too. People who like what they do treat their guests right, and they clearly do this at this hotel. The location is outstanding - about a block from the John Hancock building - and close to Michigan Avenue, the Chicago Art Institute, the Loop, etc. The room itself was huge by Chicago standards, with plenty of room. The room rate was about $--- per night on a busy fall weekend and the parking was $-- per night (self park) and located just around the corner. Only drawback was being in a room next to an alley way where they seemed to load trucks loudly at odd hours. No matter though, it was a great time in Chicago and we would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a comfortable and affordable hotel option in a great location.

Avoid by all means this sheraton ho tel. It is old, impersonnal, run down. It is sad but there is nothing positive to say about this hotel, except may be the location, close to the theater district. Rooms are old, bathrooms too, hotel is noisy, breakfast area is a joke. It is amazing such an hotel can still be in business. I guess the good name of sheraton helps, but i doubt people would ever come back for a -nd time. Worse value for money is terrible.

If you’re looking for a good bargain hotel in downtown Seattle, this is the place for you. We just returned from a trip and spent - days in Seattle. We paid $----night plus $-.-- for parking. If you check around early enough you might be able to get the price down some. The rooms were clean even if the hallways are a little “used” looking. It’s weird that this hotel sits right across the alley from the regular Holiday Inn. I don’t know what the prices are there, but the hotels look exactly the same. The “regular” Holiday Inn has a restaurant on site, but we never ate there so no recommendation. The hotel features a very extensive continental breakfast…one of the better ones for my money. We got our fill every morning, even if we were showing up between ----. The hotel is in a good location, even with the panhandlers near by. In fact, a block away must be one of the best begging corners in Seattle, as every time we walked by there it was occupied, even at one in the morning. The Space Needle and EMP is about a -- minute walk (- blocks). From there you can catch the monorail (or in our case a shuttle as the monorail was closed due to a recent fire) to downtown. The monorail stop downtown leaves an easy walk to Pike’s Market, the underground tour, etc. Also, on the way to the Space Needle is the “Ride the Duck” tour. We highly recommend the amphibious tour. It was lot of fun. Near the hotel are several restaurants: a pizza parlor which was okay; Minnie’s café, about - blocks away, which we walked to at midnight for dessert. Don’t mind the way the staff looks, the food is good; and the Five Points Café, which looks like a real dive, but the food is very good. Minors are allowed in until -pm. Again, it looks like something you’d want to avoid, but good food at good prices. ***Now for the bad stuff about the hotel. First, the secure underground parking is horrible if you’ve got anything bigger than an economy car. It is very difficult maneuvering, and a limited number of spaces are available. If you don’t get a space before they fill up, they direct you to an outside lot, up near the panhandler. Not the ideal spot, especially of you’ve got a rental car and didn’t get all of the exorbitant insurance. Second, the rooms have free local calls, but when trying to connect to the internet with our laptop we kept getting disconnected by the phone system after about three minutes. I asked the staff to check the line, but don’t know if they ever did. It never did work right (the next hotel in a different city we connected fine). Finally, getting an early morning wake up call by the fire alarm was no fun. I read some of the other reviews, and this wasn’t the first report of this happening. Maybe it’s the hotels way of getting you out of the rooms early for housekeeping. All in all, if you’re on a budget, I’d recommend this place.

I stayed here --- - ---- for a meeting I was holding. I've avoided the Shoreham Park in the past because I usually like to stay at Starwood hotels. I booked a $--- AAA rate and was only able to book two double beds. I immediately joined their frequent guest program when I booked. My key packet was ready on arrival, and I went right to my room, having checked in online two days prior. When I checked in, I asked for a king, if available, and I received it - room --- - a nice corner room with balcony.
The hotel is at a tail end of a renovation, so everything was fresh and new. My room lacked a bedspread and headboard reading lights that I saw in other rooms, but a letter from management explained not all rooms had every detail yet. I usually cast off the bedspread anyway.
The bathroom was small but well appointed with good amenities. The sliding door to the balcony was original and had no latch, which might bother others but did not bother me. The desk phone did not work.
As a frequent guest, you can have two beverages of your choice delivered free of charge in the morning, which was quite. Free internet is also included.
The service at the hotel was impressive. All staff were very nice, and the catering staff in particular were very responsive to our needs. I will return to the Omni Shoreham Park.

From the moment we 'glided' through the revolving doors into the lobby, we were greeted and assisted by such a great and friendly concierge. The ease of self checking in, and being taken to our room. The amazing trendy elevators to our floor. Our premium cabin on the --th floor was beautiful. Everything you need. Great view out over manhattan and views of the river. Flat screen hd tv. Ipod dock. free usa phonecalls. Very comfy beds. Amazing shower cubicle. Free coffee and filtered water on galleys on each floor. Trendy -th floor terrace bar. Just the right level of music. Great for a pre cocktail. Cannot recommend this hotel enough. Compared to other NYC hotels, this trumps the lot!! Can't wait to go back!!
Great location to everything. We were able to walk to mostly everything.

Easy walk from New York's Penn Station with NJ Transit, LIRR, and Amtrak located there. NJ Transit offers an inexpensive connection from Newark Liberty Airport to Penn Station. Subway is at end of block from hotel. Super friendly and helpful staff from warm cookies and bottled water to help with restaurants and transportation. Breakfast is included and is more than adequate. WiFi is free. Bathroom is very small but modern with a walk-in shower and plenty of storage. Bedroom is more than roomy enough, especially by NYC standards. We had a very comfortable king-size bed with desk, large dresser, end tables, and desk chair. No extra seating except the desk chair. The closet was small but had plenty of hangers. We were on the front side and had a view of the Empire State Building. The street is very quiet. It is the 'Flower District' and by day all the sidewalks are bordered by trees, plants, and flowers.

We stayed at this hotel in early June. We found the hotel to be lack luster. The furniture and decor of the room was outdated. We had to switch rooms because of a very strong cleaning product smell and the second room didn't smell much better. We paid to be in the club level which came with free drinks and hors d'oeuvres and a very pleasant breakfast.

I used to stay in Chicago pretty often on business, so I've seen many of the downtown hotels. I really thought I had stayed at a --star hotel when I stayed at the Westin. 
The room was really really nice, much larger than the Intercontinental or the Marriott that are nearby.
I think I paid as much or more than I have at the Marriott or IC, but this time I thought I got more value for money. There really was nothing to complain about and my room had a wonderful view of the river. This place is still within very close distance of the theater district as well as the northern part of Michigan avenue.

Spent just one night while visiting my daughter in San Francisco. The staff got us right into a room even though we arrived at -- AM. It's a beautiful property and the service is excellent. We were upgraded to a Junior Suite and given free breakfast (that one was due to my Starwood status). The Pied Piper Bar is fantastic and the location of the hotel suited us perfectly.

We found this hotel through Trip Advisor and couldn't have been happier. We had one bed suite, roomy with kitchenette ideal with - children. Staff friendly especially Bobby. I've been coming to San Francisco frequently for two years and this is by far the best place I've stayed.

There is a restaurant in the hotel that serves breakfast and dinner and also room service. Food is very good. And, there are many nearby inexpensive options in close walking distance.
This is very comfortable for me for a long-term stay, as well as being the best price I could find.

Oh well can't have a perfect trip.

I stayed at the Madison while in DC for a conference. The location of the hotel is excellent, as it is within walking distance to the White House, museums and other historical attractions. I found the staff at the hotel to be extremely friendly and accommodating. The lobby and restaurant areas of the hotel are airy, and beautifully designed. Unfortunately, the positive points listed here did not make up for my disappointing room. My room was spacious; however, it was not particularly clean. The furnishings were worn and there were stains on the wall. My husband noticed on our second night that our bedsheets were also ripped. In addition, the toilet in our room was an industrial toilet that you would find in a public washroom. It was extraordinarily noisy when the toilet was flushed and I felt as though I were in a public bathroom stall. The rooms surrounding ours also had the same toilet and we were woken throughout the night to the sounds of the toilets flushing in the adjacent rooms on our floor. A number of other people who attended the conference with me and who stayed at this hotel indicated that they experienced similar issues.
Overall, the Madison is a decent hotel and it is a suitable place to stay if you are more interested in seeing the sights of DC. If you are a light sleeper, this is not a hotel for you. The Madison is in need of some TLC and decor upgrades to the rooms.

I spent two days at the hotel in the middle of January and was very pleased. The staff was outstanding and I saw them handle a couple of challenging situations with other customers very effectively. Overall good stay in San Diego though not without some disappointments. It is a grand hotel with beautiful decorations in the lobby. This hotel is in a convenient location across the Horton Plaza mall and near the Gaslamp District. We did not always feel safe walking the neighbourhood around early morning-late evening due to the homelessness surrounding the hotel. As this is a large hotel, it depends on which side of the hotel you are walking along. 
Reception
- Arrived early morning and immediately received early check-in from friendly reception staff.
- Reception staff were also quick to resolve while providing apologies when room key got de-activated part way through stay.
Cleanliness
- Cleaning staff were friendly and cheerful. One lady provided us with bottled water for our day out even though bottled water is supposed to be provided during turn-down. 
- Bed and bathroom was clean but the room was overall dusty.
- The television remote was quite dirty but this is often the case in hotels. 
- There was no consistent turn-down service. We received bottled water around -pm on the second night but this was not the case on the first night. 
Rooms
- Lots of windows for sunlight but views of a run-down, sketchy hotel-building. 
- There were constantly homeless people and garbage outside our side of the building. Although we live in the downtown core of a big city, we still felt a little uneasy keeping the blinds open. On the first day, we saw someone being arrested.
- At night, there were loud noises from people shouting in the streets, of doors slamming in the hallway (which in turn caused the mirror put up against our room wall to bang against the wall each time), and of the loud heating-cooling vent that turned on and off. 
- Interior decor requires certain taste. It is special and unique but may not be pleasing to the eye.
Concierge
- We approached two different concierge staff members on two occasions over our stay. They answered our questions straightforwardly but really did not show any interest or enthusiasm in helping us with our plans. We found them rather curt in their responses. 
- We had asked the concierge about taking the Old Trolley Tours the next morning. However, we found out the next day that this tour was being disrupted by the annual ---- Port of San Diego Big Bay Balloon Parade. We would have greatly appreciated this finding this out before taking the tour as the roads were closed and traffic greatly disrupted by this Parade. It would also have been fun to see the Parade, which was just a short walk from the hotel. Since this was such a large event that affected our plans, we would’ve appreciated the concierge mentioning it when we asked about our plans. 
Valet
- We only encountered the valet once after we checked out of the hotel. The reception directed us to the back to get a taxi. We stood waiting for a while before someone approached us. When we asked for a taxi, we only got an abrupt response telling us to wait while he shouted at another staff member to get a taxi. When the taxi came in a few minutes, we were again abruptly asked, “airport, right?? Airport?!” before we were boarded. Although this was not a terrible experience. It is really less than ideal to end our stay in a supposedly world-class hotel.

Recently stayed at the triton hotel in San Francisco, the location is very good, right on the door step of china town and only a short walk to union square. My only concern was that a double room meant a double bed, a little cramped and there was room for a queen size in the room with a little furniture adjustment. Other than that quite good. The French cafe next door is the best and the dinner menu is to die for. Had the duck confit, omg, simply scrumptious!

Myself and my significant other stayed here in April ----. We arrived in the hotel absolutely shattered tired after a long day of travelling and were asked to wait as our room wasn't ready. We took a seat and were treated to some pink champagne as we took in the surroundings. It's a beautiful building and very well decorated but the wait of well over an hour was a bit too long, all we wanted to do is get checked in and hit the bed for a few hours sleep. Eventually we were checked in and given our room card, unfortunately the room already had a person staying in it so we trekked back to the reception desk again and waited for another hour while a room was prepared for us. We were given a room at the front of the hotel, bit on the small side but that's not unexpected in New York. The housekeeping staff were still preparing it when we walked in but were soon finished and sent on their way. I wasn't too happy with the room to be honest, it was a bit shappily decorated, not very clean and a little bit noisy in the morning. It hadn't been a great experience so far. The following morning I went to reception desk and explained to the clerk that I wasn't pleased with the room, it wasn't clean (I found used q-tips on the floor) and would like another room. She offered to change my room when we left for the day Which I accepted. We were given a corner room on the -th floor which was absolutely fabulous, great view of the hustle and bustle below but without much traffic noise. I have to say that the clerk positively changed our experience of this hotel and made our trip to NYC a very enjoyable one. That is why I would recommend a stay in the Soho Grand. The hotel is in a fabulous area, nice bars and restaurants and is the perfect antidote to the usual shop till you drop NYC experience. I would recommend the hotel to anybody who wants to just chill and relax in a part of the city you would not normally visit. I wish I could remember the desk clerk's name and give her a big thank you.

 There is also too many pillows and cushions on the bed, a total of seven!

I tagged along with my wife on her business conference which was held at this hotel. During check-in we were told our reserved room did not have a king sized bed as we requested so after we asked if another room could be found we were given a free upgrade to a small suite (it helps that my wife is a Wyndham Rewards corporate traveller). Yes, this hotel has seen better days. The carpet was worn and some of the furniture was beat up. Hotel staff were friendly and helpful. The room was clean and comfortable. Great location to everything. Monorail close by provided convenient transportation to shopping and restaurants. Microwave and refrigerator worked well for our snacks and soft drinks.

Stayed here with my friends for a girls weekend. It was great! The staff was amasing! They were friendly, and truly went out of there way to make things as easy and comfortable as possible. There is a good little coffee shop that serves Starbucks and pastries in the lobby and there is a nice internet center with several computers and a printer available. The rooms are very clean and modern but have cool old pictures of NYC which I really liked. The beds were amasing!! So comfortable with big fluffy pillows and down comforters. Bathrooms were beautiful too and had everything you need including fog free mirrors which I thought was a nice touch. The rooms are a little tight but still very comfortable. Also, hotel had town cars available to guests, that are a little more expensive than cabs, but totally worth it if you need to get somewhere at dinner time on the weekend. We really had an enjoyable stay, and for a new hotel things really run very smooth.

Me and my wife love to stay at the Ritz when we are in town, I am a frequent Four Seasons customer and this hotel has been always on top of my list. Laurel and Jon helped us out with our dinner reservations and the show tickets(Million Dollar Quartet), they were both awesome as usual. The hotel is conveniently located by Michigan Avenue and very easy to access everywhere in the city. The Inn at the Market is the best hotel-inn I have ever stayed at. My husband and I were very happy staying here. The location is great, the staff was fantastic, our room was beautiful, we loved the entire place. I will stay there again no doubt! It is a GREAT place for romance!

This hotel was THE WORST hotel I have ever stepped foot in. It was absolutely disgusting. There are bed bugs, and no sheets on the bed. The rooms do not have a DVD player or a way to watch a movie (we wanted to relax one night and stay in) BUT in a city like that you don't need that anyway. The front desk was very helpful and kind and we will definitely stay there again when we go back to San Fran!

Stayed in the Hilton Times Square over Christmas. The hotel is OK, but a bit impersonal and cold in terms of atmosphere - we stayed in the Sofitel previously, which is much more welcoming and friendly in feel. The room was fine, comfortable big bed, and great views over the city from the --rd floor. Breakfast was pretty good, although I'm glad we got it free because of our HHonors membership - it's never worth $-- per person. The restaurant is small for the size of hotel - I guess everyone eats out - but that can mean queues at breakfast. The bar is also small and nothing special, parked in the middle of the reception area.
However, our major issue was the hotel's responsiveness to a problem. It does seem that the great American customer service only extends to a big smile and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""have a nice day"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", they do seem programmed to put up a brick wall at the merest hint of a problem. We were going to see friends on Christmas Day and had ordered some flowers (direct from the florist) to be delivered to our room on Christmas Eve. When the florist arrived, the hotel rejected the delivery, despite it having the room number on, because my fiancee had paid for them and her name was not on the hotel records.
When we finally established after Christmas what had happened, we went to talk to the lady manager, who decided to hear our complaint in the middle of the reception desk. We asked why nobody had thought it appropriate to call our room and at least leave a message to the effect that someone had tried to make a delivery but there was a problem with the name? Apparently they don't do this because of - wait for it - """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""security issues"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". She wouldn't budge on this, despite me asking her to explain how my security would be compromised by leaving a message on my phone.... Eventually, as we were getting absolutely nowhere with her, we agreed to differ and the matter's now with Hilton Customer Services. It was just disappointing that the reaction to a problem was just a brick wall and no imagination, common sense or customer service.

Have just come back from a - night stay in New York at the Salisbury Hotel. Loved it. Great location, close to Central Park, -th Ave and short walk from Times Square, Macys, Bloomingdales, Disney Store, Apple Store - the list goes on!! Excellent value for money and plenty to eat at the breakfast buffet on -rd floor. Very spacious - bedroom suite which had - large beds and a living room and kitchenette area. Lots of character too. Angelos Italian restaurant which is - doors away is definitely worth a visit. They do take-away as well.

I stayed here for a week. Staff are excellent; the room, or I should say suite, was great. Breakfast was ok (I am used to the full service restaurant at the Courtyard (CY) in Rancho Bernardo (RB) but, does cost $ for the meal there). I stayed here for two reasons - the CY in RB is showing its age, IMHO. Secondly, I've stayed at this hotels sister hotel, the Springhill Suites by Marriott several years ago (right next door) and it then was good (thought, has been recently renovated). I will be back in a week for two week duration then back in Nov for one more week since I liked this place and, feel safe and comfortable here.

I've stayed at this Doubletree several times over the last year for both business and leisure travel, and I cannot say enough good things about my experiences. The hotel is easily accessible to theatre, concert halls, sports stadiums, shopping, the historic sites, and transportation as well as downtown business complexes. There are a number of good restaurants in the surrounding blocks, and I've also had excellent meals and outstanding service in the two restaurants inside the hotel. I've always found my rooms to be extremely clean and well supplied thanks to a strong housekeeping staff, and the beds are very, very comfortable. The Fitness Center's fifth floor location includes a large outdoor seating area overlooking the Avenue of the Arts, not something typically found in hotel in the middle of a big city. The entire staff is consistently professional and welcoming, and goes to great lengths to ensure my needs are met. I've experienced the same excellent service and amenities during both busy and quiet times, which is the mark of any well-run business.

The Good
Our check-in was quick and painless. The person at the front desk was cheerful and gave us a warm welcome. He also provided driving directions without prompting when he discovered the reason for our visit.
The lobby of the hotel is gorgeous. The bar on the lobby level looks very nice though we did not eat or drink there. It has an outside patio with fire pits and HD televisions. 
The king-size bedroom is very clean and in great shape. The bed and linens are outstanding. Four lamps provide the light to the bedroom and one hall light lights the entry area. The bathroom is roomy. I appreciate the desk and the two additional chairs to sit in. I expect a room of this quality to contain a refrigerator but it does not. The TV and chest of drawers have a sharp appearance but the TV’s performance is lacking (discussed below).
The Bad
A non-HD analog line feeds the LG HD TV. If you are used to HD content you know that standard format content looks terrible on a HD TV. 
Worse though is the menu system to control the TV. I am unable to change between ESPN and The Discovery Channel without making this navigation process: 
Menu -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Channel Guide -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Down -> Select. ESPN is channel -- and The Discovery Channel is --. No, you cannot enter the channel number with the remote control or use the Up-Down buttons.
The Ugly
Wireless Internet access became standard -- years ago. The Hyatt Regency charges $---day for wifi. No, there is no other access point that you can connect to. Luckily I was on vacation for the purpose of unplugging from the world. Had this been a business trip I would either have to pay the bounty for Internet access or select a hotel that does not insist on nickel-and-diming its customers.
I read about parking on several travel websites but did not let it prevent me from booking this hotel. Valet parking is $--hour or $---night. Self-parking in the garage beneath the hotel is $--hour or $---night. My wife and I were able to cope with the parking situation but it was a major inconvenience. We elected to save our money by parking on the streets around the hotel. This was only possible because my wife and I are athletic and she was able to take our bags to our room while I parked the car when we arrived. If you are traveling by yourself or if long walks (including several flights of stairs or major inclines) tire you, I suggest planning on using the self-parking in the garage. My shortest walk from my car to the hotel lobby was --- yards and including crossing - lanes of traffic and - flights of stairs. My longest was a quarter mile, though it was traffic and stairs free. There are other businesses and apartments in the area that each has patrons that park along the streets, making finding a spot near the front of the hotel difficult.

We staid at the Hampton inn & Suites twice last month. We had originally booked it for the first night of a one month vacation in the western US and thanks to Delta and JFK airport we arrived at the hotel at - am in the morning
Even though the front door was locked and we had to ring the bell, the welcome was great. We got our room quickly and the night concierge even opened up the small lobby shop so we could get some water for the night. 
We were so impressed with the first stay that we booked a night for the final night of our vacation before flying home. Again the service was impressive. Check inn were quick and the front desk helped with boarding passes and supplied us with a card with directions to the airport.
We would highly recommend this hotel, and will probably chose to stay here when we come back next time. The location next to a shopping area with lots of restaurants were a plus as well.
The rooms
The rooms for both stays were identical, large and very, very clean. The beds were great, and small sofa section very nice. The bathrooms very clean and the hotel had supplied lots of good quality shampoo, lotion etc...
Breakfast. 
The hotel breakfast is nice, with different hot items every day. It also have lots of fruits and a good supply of cereals and breads. The breakfast hostess kept the breakfast area nice and tidy all the time.

I stayed here one night after I had a minor surgery done in a nearby medical office. My sister stayed with me. Check-in went smoothly (I was even able to check-in early). The room was spacious with - beds, TV reception was fine, and room ammenities were quality. The hotel was very convenient--my sister went shopping in the nearby Keystone Mall while I slept after my surgery. She also brought back a take-out dinner from a mall restaurant (there are several choices). The parking was a breeze--an attached garage with a covered -rd floor walkway. 
My only complaint is the fee for wifi. We didn't use it since there is a charge and we were there such a short time. We did notice there are several computers for use in the lobby--and saw several businessmen working there. I thought nowadays all hotels had complimentary wifi, but I guess not.
This is the first time I'd stayed in this hotel though I have been in it for conferences before. The hotel is nice, the workers seemed friendly and helpful, & the room was clean. I would certainly stay here again!

My husband and I recently took our son on a trip to San Diego and we stayed at this wonderful resort on Vacation Island. From the time we arrived, an employee met us and directed us on how to get to our room and provided us with all kinds of information about the resort and about sites to see in San Diego. Our only regret was that we only stayed - days, instead of a week or more! The resort has so much to offer that you really could spend a week only there, without needing to go explore San Diego (but you'd miss this beautiful city!). Our suite was very nice and spacious. The beds were very comfortable. The bathroom and shower room combination were a little odd, with the light switch for both in the dressing room half. This required you to have to walk through both """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""rooms"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to turn on the light, and then return to the showering room. The shower didn't have a ledge along the floor to prevent the water from covering part of the bathroom floor, so that made showering a little messy. (This was just a minor inconvenience.) We were just a short walk from a beautiful beach that was great for running along or just for a peaceful walk. The flowers and plants reminded me of Hawaii and the sea birds were so fun to watch. We had fun playing ping pong and croquet on the grounds and had a wonderful dinner at the Barefoot Bar, seated outdoors as we watched the sunset. It was such a lovely trip! I highly recommend it!

I could not have had a worse night on a business trip. Not only was the front desk lady icy cold at check-in (who wants this after a long day of business meetings?), she gave me a room off of the alley, with a dumpster (that apparently gets frequent activity) and next to the street. Needless to say, I looked and acted like a drugged-out zombie for my next day of business meetings. I love SF but I won't be back at this hotel any time soon. No wonder the rate was so good. 
The only consolation - free wireless intenet.

One of the prior reviewers may have said it best-----""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""What more do you want?"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" This is the best-run Ritz Carlton where I have stayed, and one of the best """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""city hotels"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" anywhere. Beautiful, spacious rooms that are classic in the traditional Ritz look, yet with modern amenities such as flat screen TVs and I-pod docking stations. Large marble bathrooms. We had an interior view room. In many city hotels this is the kiss of death, and you look out onto a dreary courtyard or """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""air shaft."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" At the Ritz SF I actually prefer the Courtyard view----its a really pretty landscaped courtyard with semi-permanent white party tent in the middle. 
 Wonderful, classic lobby. One of my favorite experiences at the Ritz SFwas having evening cocktails in the Lobby Lounge----very sophisticated room, well-mixed cocktails, perfectly elegant. 
Service is incredible. When you check in, after giving your name to bellhop in driveway, they greet you by name when you walk in the front door.One of the other reviewers found this a bit hokey or over-the-top. I did not. Employees uniformly greet you as you walk past. Very service-oriented. 
After touring around the city during the day, it was always a pleasure to return to this hotel, which seemed like an elegant and calm oasis in the middle of the city.

This is a nice hotel in a great location. The room was very large and great for a business traveler. The service was great, staff friendly, food and bar was awesome. Bed was great, hotel was quite, etc. Here is the deal with this property - it needs updating. In about a year, if left as is, it would get a - rating. Old school TV was interesting. There was some wear around the edges with this place. I am not overly picky but in full disclosure, they need to start renovating.

This is in a great location near lots of things to do. There is a drugstore right next door which was convenient with - children under -. Very family friendly, the swans and indoor pool were a hit. The decor in the rooms is dated, but clean. The breakfast buffet was included and was very convenient and good.

the standard room price was USD --- per night w-o breakfast, reservation was made via a bank who arranged a large conference. The list price is USD ---. 
I was on the --st floor, the view was nice. The room was tired, old deco, a refurbishment is pretty needed. Big screen TV but old equipment. Terrible service. I called min - times in the evening the front desk-concierge-room service-operator etc to have a wake-up call. Not succeeded. I also wanted to find out some basic info about the gym. No success again. The gym was average.
Breakfast: no variety of food, very crowded the Oscar, very unpolite staff
Limo service was reasonably priced and efficient arranged by the hotel to the JFK
To sum up: this might be a very stylish hotel -- years ago. Since then just prices went up....
Room was alright, nothing special, but the price was OK: $--- for - nights, weekend. Free parking. No wireless internet.

I stayed at the Edgewater on business--at a conference--the first week of January ----. I think it's a great place to stay: beautiful location right on the water, legendary ever since the Beatles stayed there and had their iconic photo op, really nice lobby area--very Northwest log lodge--to hang out and have a drink, and, I have to say, an outstanding restaurant on site. I had drinks there, dinner, breakfast, and lunch, and all were just spot on. Were I staying somewhere else in Seattle I would go there just to have a meal--with an incredible view over the water, by the way. The location is very convenient to the Market and the Aquarium, and if you're a runner, you can just get on Alaskan Way and head up past the Olympic Sculpture Park, very nearby, and keep going. Only two criticisms, really: they close down the bar too early on weeknights if you want to hang out in the lobby with a cozy drink, and the common spaces (hallways, etc.) are more beat up than you would expect. Rooms are just fine. Not big but plenty serviceable. If this is the location you want, excellent choice. If you want to be more downtown, I'd suggest the Alexis.

I would give this hotel a very good were it not for the noise. The hotel was just finishing renovations when I was there. The decor is beautiful. My room was on the -th floor facing K street. Nice view but way too much commotion. Let me preface this by saying I live in the city and my street can be loud, I am also a heavy sleeper so I usually don't have issues but I was woken up every night of my stay. The first night was a Saturday, teh street noise consisted of drunk people talking loudly and yelling, sirens, loud motorcycles, loud trucks and a lot of pounding. Every night was pretty much the same (sans drunk people). My other work colleagues with rooms off K street also had this same complaint. We were there for a conference so the hotel was booked and no way we could move. I decided to extend my stay and bunked with a friend that had a courtyard facing room and it made a world of difference, the first good night's sleep I got.
Ok, enough complaining about the noise. The hotel, as I said, was new and beautiful. We ate at the President's Grill two nights. The second night I got the steak which I was concerned about but it was delicious, perfectly cooked and juicy. Service at the restaurant and lobby bar were great and all the staff were very helpful and friendly. The hotel is also a block away from the convention center and a metro stop so you can't beat that.

We stayed two nights at the Milford and had one of the new renovated rooms. The room was beautiful, clean and and spacious (this might vary?) enough for two people. Nice design and with a view over the city and the Hudson River from our bed - pretty cool to stay at --th floor and enjoy the lights of the city from there in the evening. If youre a light-sleeper - remember earplugs, cause even youre staying at the --th floor, NYC is still a bit noisy at night ;) Kind and helpfull people in the reception. The hotel is placed only one block away from Times Square and all the theaters and if you come with the bus from Newark, it is only - min away by foot. We would definitely recomend this hotel and is looking forward to stay here again, probably after the big renavation of the hotel trough ----.

We really enjoyed this small, boutique hotel and not just because we got upgraded to a suite (although it was great!). This hotel was perfect for the purpose of our stay--to end our vacation in a relaxing and comfortable fashion. The staff were so eager to please and the special touches throughout the stay (fruit in our room upon arrival, cookies daily left in our room, upscale continental breakfast including lattes per request, etc...) really made this hotel stand out. We enjoyed exploring the parks, walking the hills and checking out the Fillmore Jazz Fest during our stay, but did need to take a cab downtown for most other activities (which we knew and was fine with us). A good vibe at this place, you can tell the management knows what it's visitors want and that the staff all works well together. Other than families, we were one of the younger visitors staying here (we are in our late --'s). Would highly recommend to others!

Booked room for - to share & got - double beds. Complained to reception re size of room and was changed immediately with little fuss. Excellent location on -th Ave & --th St. opposite Penn train station """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""underground to us blighties"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Get the train from JFK to the door for $- each (aiport shuttle $- from JFK to Jamaica Stn, change to Penn Stn direct $-.--). We were -- minutes walk to Time Square. -- minutes to Umpire St. - minutes Macey's. IF you go this time of year, pack little. Winter coats, jeans etc are cheap as chips in the sales at Macey's, Bloomingdales etc. We ate daily at the Tick Tock Diner... portions are BIG so best shared. Drinks are more costly than uk. $- wine glass $- lager. $- Pepsi. Remember Americans expect to be tipped... rule of thumb is to double the tax on your bill to get the tip expected. Definately going back. Definately staying at this Hotel (ask my husband, I AM FUSSY!) The rooms are renowned to be small in this hotel, & ours was. But they did change.

The location is outstanding and the lobby is nice, but the rooms are run-down and out of our party of six we had the following combinations in our January stay: 
 no heat-no hot water
 no heat-with hot water 
 heat never shut off-with hot water (- of us)
 one had proper heat and hot water (we decided to hate that person for the trip.) 
Maybe my expectations are unrealistic, but in this price range I do not expect to have to regulate the temperature with the window (if it opened, it didn't for one poor soul.) My sink also had issues and when I mentioned the problems with the room I was utterly ignored. The icing on the cake was with conference package we had all booked. Breakfast was included but they charged some of us anyway -- case is still pending.
Avoid this hotel. Terrible.

We stayed at this hotel for - nights last week. The hotel is old. Lobby and the hallways are way outdated. Room looked slightly better than the lobby. First of all, neither of us hardly slept all night. Walls are like paper and you can hear the exact conversations on the street even though we were on the -th floor. Air conditioning unit is the oldest I have ever seen. Every time it kicks in, it makes lots of noise. You could hear every door opened all the hallway all night long. On top of all this, we were charged for - nights parking when we only parked one night. They are refusing to reimburse us since they are saying when you check in they assume you will keep the car for - nights with valet unless you tell them otherwise. It is nonsense. They know when we took it out and we weren't told to notify them otherwise. First time we called they lied to me and said they did an inventory and know the car was there at - pm second night when we knew we took it out in the am. Second time I called and talked to the manager, he came up with a different story. I wouldn't suggest this hotel to anybody. Not only it is loud, old and dirty, their customer service is also not good.

Stayed at this location for a meeting. Had a wonderful time. The folks at the front desk were very helpful although this hotel is alway hopping. Be sure to tell them exactly what you want and be patient. The room was spotless and quiet. The housekeeping staff did not try to clean before - AM. The Reading Terminal is across the street and really interesting and local. Be sure to take a cab to Isgro's and have some wonderful Italian cookies. While you're in the neighborhood, stay for dinner at Dante's. It's like being in your grandmother's living room, if you should have been that lucky. 
There's an authentic ice cream parlor within another cab ride from the hotel but I can't remember the name! The young people who run it are passionate and serve up really good ice cream creations. Philly is a fun place.

I stayed here on business, off and on for several months. The rooms are smallish but clean. The service is very good, the location is great if you want to be close to Chinatown, Union Square, Financial district and the Embarcadero.
My favorite part of staying at the Galleria Park was the wine hour. They served complimentary red and white wine in the lobby every evening. It was a great way to unwind from a days work (or sightseeing). It was also a fun way to meet people from other cities and countries.
You have many options of hotels in this area for a similar price. If you like older style hotels with a somewhat European feel, this is a good choice.

This Inn has a great location, situated in Center City, walking distance from all the historic sights and is a really good value for the money. The staff is very friendly. The breakfast was very good - yogurt, eggs, much more than just continental and the breakfast staff was really on top of things. 
Parking is a little far and doesn't afford in and out privileges and is really designed so that if you drive in, you drop the car and don't use it until you leave. 
The neighborhood has great restaurants - Mixto (Columbian-Cuban) was outstanding and is right around the corner. 
One thing that could be improved is that they don't clean the bathroom completely until the -rd day of a visit which leaves hair and other stuff on the floor and a not so clean sink. I mentioned it to the manager and he said that was their policy but if you ask for it, they will clean the bathroom for you. Notwithstanding, the Inn is still a great value and this didn't spoil our visit at all.

Great location if you want to stay in Mid town. The staff are young but very efficient. We had a suite which was a reasonable size and a huge bathroom. Very very quiet room which is amazing for NY. All mini bar is included (except alcohol) and nespreso coffee machine. Ate in the hotel restaurant which was excellent. My only criticism was there is no real concierge. I asked about a restaurant before the theatre and was told about a place she had heard of which turned out to be the worst meal I have ever had in NY. I think because the staff are young, they could direct you to the hippest bars but not great restaurants. Overall a wonderful hotel and I look forward to staying there on my next visit to NY.

I am a captive of the Marriott Rewards program, so I find this hotel an excellent alternative to the Washington Hilton when attending a meeting or conference there. The Courtyard is a different tier of hotel, but if all you need is a clean, comfortable place to stay, at a comparatively good rate, while in this part it of DC, the Courtyard by Marriott Washington DC \ Dupont Circle will serve you well.
Restaurants are super abundant in this neighborhood. Plenty of choices, and lots of activity along Connecticut Avenue.

If you are a kind who uses the hotel room just for taking showers and sleeping, this is the right one for you. If I am visiting a city for touristic purposes, I expect the hotel I will stay to be close to major attractions or public transportation, safe (since I usually leave the room early and return late), and clean. The Gem Soho was really satisfactory for me, especially when I consider the price. 
Location is great, walking distance to Little Italy and Soho and close to two different subway stations. 
They do not offer breakfast but there are a lot of Deli's in the neighborhood, so it was not a major problem.
Bed was really comfortable with lots of pillows, sheets and towels were changed everyday, therefore it was clean. 
Staff was really helpful and concerned. Provided several maps for us, gave tips about the neighborhood, and arranged out transportation to the airport. They deserve great appreciation.
Windows were not open-able which was the only problem I got. If you want to have some fresh air, you have to leave your door open.

This continues to be our favorite place to stay.
the clean rooms, awesome location, and the people are the reason i will continue to stay here.
In particular Pamela Curtis, has always made sure not only myself but the Chairmen of the Board to the CEO are taken car of properly. It is this kind if service that makes the Mela my go to place...

We stayed here for a couple of weeks to take a break from the road. We got a single room, which is the same size as a regular motel - room just with a kitchenette in the corner. The pros: great rate for a clean room in good condition, kitchenette, WIFI, pets friendly, grocery store nearby, seemingly decent area of memphis, security and friendly staff. The cons: front desk is available only during business hrs, cleaning is available only weekly, WIFI wasn't always working, and our first room had a few bugs but we were immediately moved to another room that had none. If I am in Memphis again for more than a week, I would definitely return here, but instead get the two room suite.

My friends and I enjoyed our stay here while attending a show at the new ATT Performing Arts Center. The downtown location was perfect and easy to find from the major highways. I booked the room on Hotwire at about half-price, and was pleasantly surprised to be treated like a VIP at check-in. We were even upgraded to a very roomy and quiet suite. I loved the Starbucks coffee in the room! Only con was no wi-fi in the rooms. There is a restaurant and sports bar on site that were very nice, and a gift shop-convenience store. All of the staff we encountered were very friendly and helpful. I would stay here again.

My family and I had a great time at the W. What a first class operation this place truly is. We were in Austin for the first time, and chose the W based on the experience we had at the NYC one several years ago. I'll tell you there is no better hotel chain out there then W hotels. My wife and I feel a lot of this has to do with their amazing staff. Case and point - I was in the hotel bar area waiting on some friends. Our server was a blonde woman named Lauren, who could not have been nicer, and more professional. Then on top of that a screw from my eyeglasses popped out, and one of the arms came unhinged. Lauren took out a flash light and helped us locate the screw. Then she persoanlly took it over to the front counter, got a repair kit, and fixed it for me on the fly. All the while telling my wife and I about some great spots for us to check out in Los Angeles (where she is from), and where our next trip is. It's that going above and beyond the call of duty approach by people liek Lauren, and the entire W staff that will keep my family loyal W customers, and advocates for life.

The hotel is well located. Service was genuine and helpful. My room was spacious with a decent view. The rooftop bar featured panoromic views of D.C. Easy metro access. The hotel is next to one of my favorite D.C.'s institutions, The Old Ebbit Grill. The only negative is that rooms are not well insulated and I could hear conversations in the room next door and hallway activity. However, I would not hesitate to stay here again.

Really enjoyed this hotel. The management is relaxed and friendly. Comfortable, clean room. The hotel is right on a fantastic beach. Has a patio and informal roof terrace overlooking the beach. I would highly recommend this hotel.

On February --, we decided to stay at the Marriott Courtyard Property located on Tremont Street, downtown Boston MA. I am deeply sorry to write and state how terribly disappointed once again our visit with Marriott has been.
