I very recently returned from a week's stay at Hotel Erwin on Venice Beach. I'm so mixed about my stay there, as they had some great advantages, but too many annoyances to go along with it. I'll try listing the good stuff, then go into the bad.
For the entire week, the staff was fantastic. Front desk clerks were always super nice and helpful, maids in the hallways would always give a friendly """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""good morning"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" as you headed out for the day, and the front door was almost always opened for you if an attendant was standing there. I have absolutely no complaints about the staff as a whole.
The hotel was very clean as well. The carpet in the hallway on the -th floor was a bit spotty, but nothing major in my eyes. The room was very clean when we first arrived, and it was touched up every couple days by the staff, which we were pleased with. Linens were spotless, sheets-blanket was spotless, everything was great.
The location of the hotel was nice, but ONLY if you want direct access to the beach and the Venice Boardwalk, otherwise, there is nothing else around that you can easily walk to (Santa Monica Pier is a -- minute walk from the hotel). Directly behind the hotel are basketball courts, the bike path, the boardwalk, and the beach.
Here's where some of the annoyances come into play. We reserved a -th floor """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Ocean View King Bed"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", or as it states on the website, the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Premier Ocean View King"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". We got a room on the south-facing side of the building. The ocean view was fantastic from the -th floor, as there were no other buildings as tall as Hotel Erwin (on that side of the building, anyway). You could see a decent stretch of ocean down the coast towards Marina Del Ray. We were happy with the view.
However, the bed we had in our room was NOT a king size bed, but queen size. I have a queen size bed at home, and have slept on king size beds in other hotels, and I'm confident that what we had was not king size. The bed itself was very comfortable though, I never had any trouble sleeping. Also, it was of my opinion that the room was rather small overall for what we paid. However, that is said by someone who stayed a week. If I were to only stay a couple of days, it would've been fine.
Also, on their website, our room was described as having a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""private balcony"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", which is an absolute lie. Putting up - foot high glass panes to section off a building-long balcony does not make it private. If I wanted, I could've easily climbed over these short walls and entered someone's room if they didn't have their balcony door locked. If one were so inclined, they could make their way all the way down the building and back just on the balconies. We were saddened that we couldn't leave the door open at night for fear of someone coming into our room. A nice touch, however, were the lockable screen doors, but those wouldn't have held anyone back who wanted in. This was only on the sixth floor, however, I cannot speak for other floors.
Next, the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""complimentary high-speed wireless internet"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was basically non-existant. On my laptop, I could see the network, but the signal was so weak that it wouldn't connect (< --% signal). If I stood in the door to the room, it would get a little better (< --% signal) and let me connect (although still excruciatingly slow), but the fact that I was standing in the doorway (and for such a meager signal) made it pointless. Keep in mind that I stayed in the very middle of the sixth floor, next to the ice-soda machine, so it's not like I was staying on one extremity or the other. As soon as you walk into the room, the signal drops and your connection goes bye-bye. I contacted the front desk about it, and from what I gathered (without him saying it directly), the person I talked to knew this was already an issue, and handed me an ethernet cable and a phone number to call tech support so they could help me while I was in my room.
I initially tried the ethernet cable and plugged it into the jack next to the bed, and the ethernet port was dead. I called the number, a gentleman came about - minutes later, had a conversation with me in very broken english that I did not understand (he never came into the room, just stood in the door), and left (never saw or heard from him from again, but then again, I couldn't understand what he was saying to me, so I just nodded to everything until he left). The wireless was still non-usable later that night, and I stumbled upon another ethernet port behind the coffee-maker on the other side of the room, plugged in the cable, and I finally was able to get internet. Unfortunately, I then had an ethernet cable strung across the room for the entire rest of my stay there, but at least the internet was fast. My suggestion is to bring a cable with you if you stay at this hotel and want internet.
On to other things, we were pleased with the large --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" TV in the room. It was a plasma, if that matters to anyone. There were composite, s-video, and component hookups on the wall, but we didn't use them. It appears that certain channels were for those hookups. The selection of channels available was fine, around ----- in all, everything you'd want-need for a business-vacation trip.
Another annoyance was the overpriced parking (valet only, no self-parking). $---night is a bit steep in my opinion. Also, the long waits for valet service were bad. One night was a particular mess, as I waited for -- minutes in my car so I could even get into the very small driveway to the hotel. I literally was halfway into the street and barely giving enough room for people to walk on the sidewalk. Luckily there was enough room on the street for cars to easily get by, but waiting a full -- minutes is insane (it was right at -- minutes, I kept watching the clock as I was pulling my hair out). When I finally got my car in far enough to where I could leave it, there were a couple of people that were still waiting to get their cars, that had been standing there before I even arrived.
The in-house restaurant, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hash"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", was way too expensive in my opinion, so we never ate there nor did we order room service. It's almost like they know they are the only nice restaurant in that area, so they be sure to charge as such. We also didn't go to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""high"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", the rooftop lounge, because beer was $- and mixed drinks were $--+. Probably the most frustrating thing overall is the single elevator. During my stay, in the middle of the week, we noticed they taped a printed paper that strongly recommended people pay attention to the passenger-weight limits, probably due to the fact that the small lobby becomes crammed with people in the evenings during the multi-minute wait for the elevator.
I'll close my book now by listing the pros and cons:
Pros:
 - Great location for beach goers if that's all you want to do.
 - Very friendly staff.
 - Very clean hotel throughout.
 - Comfortable bed.
 - Great ocean view on the south side with the premium package.

Cons:
 - Bad location if you want to do anything other than the beach (Santa Monica looked to be a MUCH better option for vacationers like myself).
 - Wireless internet did not work, and they will do nothing to fix it.

 - Single elevator will make you curse during the evenings.
 - Expensive in-house eating options.

Rooms are nicely designed with copies of modern classic pieces and immaculate. Views are very nice on the Beverly Hills side. On the other hand, the entry to the hotel is on the Beverly Hills side, and if you're in the lower floors, be prepared to deal with noise and smoke from the entry area at night as party goers mill about there.
The hotel is supposed to be smoke-free. On the morning of our check-out, the smell of smoke infiltrated almost the entirety of our suite. The smoke was clearly coming from another room. We brought this up to the front desk and all they could do was apologize. Apparently they have a penalty for smoking, but this is clearly not well enforced and the policy is not brought to the guests' attention upon check-in. Rooms don't have much in terms of fabrics so smoke smells don't linger too long, but still very unpleasant to wake up to that.
Noise is also a potential problem. There are area rugs, but rooms have wooden floors. We were fortunate that our neighbors weren't walking around at all hours in shoes, but it was very easy to hear the clomping of shoes when someone was walking around. Also kids crying could be heard through the walls very clearly and we did not have any connecting doors.
Showers were low-flow. Jacuzzi tub wasn't working properly - kept going on and off by itself.
Service in the restaurant was questionable - they're trying to give you European -* service, but they're not quite getting it right. You might spend - minutes explaining what you want, and they'll say they understand, and even repeat what you asked for, but then you get exactly what you said you didn't want.
Also, inquire about events. On several days of our stay, the hotel was buzzing with event activity, which even closed off the pool to guests. When they cater to the events, individual guests might get short changed on service.
Overall, it was almost there - almost as if they were trying to give you that vibe of a visit to the Amalfi coast. However, if you're accustomed to impeccable service in luxury hotels, and won't tolerate anything less, these little potential hazards might be a dealbreaker.

The days when the Allerton was a premier hotel in Chicago are long gone. Today, she's showing her age and living off her former glory. The carpet in the hallway was even dingier and shabbier, and chest-high piles of bagged trash and dirty linens blocked the narrow passageways for the majority of the day and night - along with trays filled with half-eaten food. 
The -- inch TV with mostly SD fare was almost unwatchable, while the extra-cost basic net access had incredibly slow bandwidth. Rather than add $--+ per night for decent net access, I bought meals at various local sites providing free wifi access, such as Panera's. The room had no coffee maker or microwave, presumably to encourage you to order food and drink from the hotel.
On a more positive note, room service was very responsive and friendly, and the basic breakfasts and lunches we ordered were well prepared, tasty, and had generous portions. The prices were at typical Streeteville levels, so presumably food costs plus the $-- per night parking fees makes up for the discounted room rates that are often available.
It's hard to imagine a better location for shopping, eating, and access to the Northwestern University medical campus. Michigan Avenue is literally steps away and and the Apple Store is directly across the street. There is a great mix of modest and more upscale eating places within a few blocks in any direction. Walgreens and CVS were within easy walking distance to fill prescriptions and they have a good selection of basic food and beverages. There are also high quality food stores such as Treasure Island in the area, and their deli section, salad bars, and hot food selections are surprisingly nice and fairly reasonable in cost.
Bottom line: we'd always wanted to stay at the Allerton but were sufficiently unimpressed that we probably won't be back. For about the same net cost per night there are better-run properties and lower cost options are a few blocks away. Overall, we probably got what we paid for: mediocre accommodations and service at an average Streeterville price by the time you park a car and buy net access.

The staff on reception faffed around for nearly -- minutes, trying to decide what rooms they could allocate us. They settled for - rooms on the same floor, but at opposite ends of the building, meaning our children were not within shouting distance should there be any problem.

I'm a big fan of the Club Quarters hotels for business. I often stay at the one in Rockefeller Center, but this one is nice too. I was surprised at the large size of the room. Not your typical NYC postage stamp size place. The location is great-just between -th and -th Aves. So you are within walking distance of a number of sites and great shopping. 
The staff is very helpful and friendly too. It's clear they cater to business travelers so it was no problem to receive a package for my meeting or get cabs, etc. There was a problem with the AC in my room and they quickly sent someone to fix it. 
If you are looking for NYC posh, this isn't it. The rooms are pretty basic, but always clean and neat. The lobby lounge has newspapers, a very small bar and some nice room to unwind before or between meetings. Overall, this is a great business base if you are working in midtown.

I had the job to find myself and some family members a cheap but still decent hotel i New York City. For Easter. As you can imagine, that wasn't easy. Thanks to reviews here on TripAdvisor I finally went for it and booked Wolcott, telling my family they shouldn't expect the hotel to be very good.
What struck os first was the elegant lobby and the convienient location (we arrived by train to PennStation, a -- min walk away). We were also surprised to hear that a small coffee+muffin-breakfast was included in the price! The hotel had booked us on the ninth floor in two rooms next to each other, which was perfect.
The rooms were very basic but ok. To me the bathroom and the bed are the most important in a hotel room, and here the bed was good and the bathroom OK. The carpet on the floor was stained and old.
Don't hesitate to choose the Wolcott if basic is good enough for you. The location is excellent!

Stayed here for two nights with my husband, daughter and mother. Got the AAA rate. We were attending a family wedding on Martha's Vineyard and made a trip out of the event by spending time in New York city and Philadelphia. Enjoyed the vacation in all areas in the USA thoroughly . The room at this hotel was fine. Two double beds with nice linens. Nicely appointed. The room did not have a fridge but this could have been ordered at a charge. There was a swimming pool outdoors but it was closed. The internet access was free which was a nice added feature. Staff were pleasant consistently. The location was excellent. Had to pay for parking. Breakfast which was complimentary was very fine. Buffet style with an array of foods from omelettes which were great. Boiled eggs, fruit, pastries and beverages were available. The breakfast area was clean and pretty. There is a good convenient store opposite the hotel run by Koreans which was very handy. I would recommend this hotel to those who are not snobs and enjoy value for their dollar.

This old hotel (built in ----) would have been interesting if it were clean.
Not very expensive 
The hotel is located in the perfect spot! Close to the train station, subway....
The registration was a nightmare too. Around --- people in the check in queue and - cahiers to serve us... 
Fine for all those who don't care about cleanliness!

First, let me say that I am a Marriott employee. I love the company's hotels and accommodations. Every time I stay at a Marriott, the service is the same: friendly and helpful. Having said that, the Marriott Marquis Times Square New York lives up to the expected Marriott service level, but isn't really anything more than the typical Marriott property. In fact, there are more comfortable Marriott hotels around the country than the Marquis. What you get at this particular hotel, however, is the location. It is perfectly located in Times Square on Broadway between --th and --th.
It is expensive to stay at the Marquis, although I got a discount for being an employee. The first floor lobby isn't really the lobby. You have to go up to the -th floor to check in. Weird, huh? There are a bunch of high speed elevators in a circle that take you up through the hotel, but you might wait a while because there are so many people going up and down. The room was a typical king standard room. I had a partial view of Broadway and a lovely view of an office building. The bed was comfortable, but not nearly as much as some of the other Marriott properties I've stayed at . I don't think this room was equipped with the new Revive bedding that can be found at many other Marriott properties. The bed is why I love staying at Marriott's, and this one wasn't as good as the others. The plasma TV was very nice though, and the channel list included HD channels.
As I said, the location was great. It was wonderful coming back from seeing a broadway show and walking to our hotel, in the midst of the throngs of people. I always wanted to be one of those people who could just veer off the path and walk into the hotel. I must say, it was wonderful. The hotel was quiet, once you're in your room, and the accommodations were comfortable. The prices for everything were ridiculous, of course, since you're in Times Square, but what else do you expect? Overall, the hotel was a typical Marriott. Nice design, great location, comfortable room and friendly staff, but nothing spectacular. The best part was being in Times Square.

I've stayed here twice, first in June '--, and again in Jan '--. While this review is specifically for the Jan '-- stay, both stays were comparable, Fri+Sat nights, and both were at a nightly rate of $-- via an opaque, prepaid, online booking service (I named my own price). 
The hotel's own website states: """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Please note the hotel will be undergoing renovations from Nov. -, ---- until Mar. --, ----.""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""
My advice is: Do not pay rack rate here until after renovations are complete!
On the upside, the room was well-furnished, with two double beds, attractive wall coverings, TV, ironing board and steam iron, free wireless & wired internet (more important than TV!), a small desk, and adequate lighting. There were nice soaps and shampoo-conditioner-lotion in the bathroom, along with clean towels, washcloths, and a coffee maker. As noted by others, the elevators were functional and fast. Climate control in the room was adequate. I also appreciated ceramic coffee mugs and glass tumblers (rather than plastic). And there was a sliding-door closet, with hangars and plenty of storage for luggage, etc. I was annoyed that there was not a luggage rack, however.
On the downside... the bathroom ceiling was absolutely filthy with mould and peeling plaster, the grout was mouldy, and the floors stained. I'll stop there, because as noted by the many flyers, the hotel is undergoing renovations to replace all guest bathrooms """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""from the studs out"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The worn carpeting and shabby draperies are also set to be replaced. I can only hope that the hard and uncomfortable mattresses will be replaced too. As noted by others, the rooms facing the hospital do experience sirens and road noise all night long, and I don't think the renovations will fix that. And renovating the tiny bathrooms won't make them any larger.
I had little interaction with the desk clerk; however, I was pleased that my advance phone call at -- PM the day of check in was sufficient for them to hold my room until my very late arrival of --:-- AM. (Prepaid bookings are sometimes cancelled with no refund if you don't check in before midnight of the arrival date. Fortunately that did not happen to me.)
Aside from the items noted above which will be rectified by renovations, my stay was satsifactory, and the price was terrific. The outdoor pool was closed. Others seemed to be enjoying the restaurant, though I ate elsewhere. There isn't a lot of late-night dining in the immediate vicinity of the hotel, other than a pizzeria. There seemed to be a security guard out-and-about, so I always felt safe. Yes, there is a Red Line """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""T"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" subway station about two blocks away; the hotel has no self-parking and the adjacent garage charges $---day with no in-out. (So if you're going to park, use the hotel's valet parking, which is the same price but allows in-out). There is no on-street parking available. I would stay at this hotel again, though I'd really want to find a cheaper parking option. I'm sure that after the renovations, this will be a much more attractive property.

While visiting MD Anderson, this was a great place to stay. Hotel Service was very accomodating and breakfast in the morning was good. 
Price was very reasonable. Rooms were clean and internet service good also. 
If one thing they could do was offer a shuttle to MD Anderson even if you had to pay something like $- for trip there and back.

My sister and I stayed - nights here for a weekend in Boston and to see a show at the Wang Theater. Luckily, we were on a government rate because I would have been disappointed at the size of the room if I had paid full price.
Other than that, it was an excellent place to stay to see Boston-- centrally located and we could walk to everything we wanted to do. The front desk staff was exceptionally helpful in reccomending places to eat, calling a cab, and giving advice on when to depart for the airport, etc. I would stay here again because of that, but not if I had to pay $--- to $--- a night.
In the heart of Manhattan, you can not get better value for money! The only quibble: Internet in the room is priced too high!

Stayed here for a convention at McCormick Place. Not too far away and it is definitely not your average Fairfield. Almost """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""A-Lofty"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" if you will.

We stayed here for - nights this month and can highly recommend it. Perfect location for all transport - we used the BART from the airport to get here and was just a short walk from the station. Door staff and bell boys excellent, but the desk staff could do with being a bit more personable and attentive - we tried to use the airport check-in terminal next to the front desk, and were clearly struggling, but the man on the desk was too busy on his phone arranging a weekend with his girlfreind and booking his flights to help us!
Our room was perfect - we had a corner family room on --th floor with windows on - sides overlooking Macey's and Sutter Street - just fab!
The downside is that the bar is WAY too expensive - $- for a Gin and Tonic!!! Not every guest is loaded with money! MInd you, just down the street opposite Union Square is a GREAT bar - looks very seedy from the outside, but excellent inside called Gold Dust Lounge.
We got the - dat MUNI pass and used it many times over to get all over the city. As for car parking charges, you really don't need a car - we dropped out hire car back before we went into the city - and didn't miss it at all.

Nothing that was so bad you wanted to complain, and nothing so good I want to mention it here. Others have talked about the small bathrooms, and the lack of water pressure in the shower. All true. 
This is a huge bed factory, and conference centre. I was there for a conference and it was very easy to fally out of bed into a lift and straight to the conference.
The food in the bar was pretty basic - and whilst not cheap was well presented and served quickly.

Recently completed a stay at the Hilton Palacio del Rio and what stood out was the location. It is located on the riverwalk and directly across from the hotel’s riverwalk entrance is the dock for the river boat tours. It was great taking early morning walks on the riverwalk and it was so convenient to have so many nice restaurants nearby. Also, the Alamo is only a two block walk on the street level. However, the hotel itself was nothing special. The room had the comfortable Hilton bed which I have come to expect but the accommodations were dated. The bathroom was also on the small side. A plus was the balcony which overlooked the river walk. Thumbs down to the pool scene as the pool and deck are very small and there were not enough chairs to handle all of the guests. The fitness rooms have all new equipment and I thought were very nice. I received complementary breakfast at the hotel’s Ibiza Restaurant due to Diamond status but I would not have paid $--.-- for the buffet. All of the staff I encountered had a great attitude and were very helpful (I was surprised by those who found otherwise). If I return to San Antonio, I may stay again as I have heard from one of the staff that a hotel renovation has been scheduled.

Recently stayed in this hotel for one night. It was very clean and nice. The only problem would be that it is extremely small. Only a few steps around the bed on any side. Breakfast is also fairly meager for a Microtel. The staff was very nice.

The most impressive quality of this hotel is its service. The staff are very responsive and very attentive, an added bonus to just a great hotel. The rooms were decorated tastefully and are quiet. The bathrooms were large. And, the place was clean. The roof top pool and jacuzzi were quite enjoyable. My only complaint is that my king size bed was really a queen size as demonstrated by the difference in the headboard and mattress size. I chose not to take a different room. The location of the hotel is also nice. Not too close in the center of everything on the Riverwalk but not too far away either. I will definitely stay here again.

On a couple of incredibly hot July days, the Drake was an oasis of lodging, food and drink. The location is fabulous, the service was impeccable-- whether the front desk, housekeeping, the lounge, or the restaurant-- we were treated like royalty. The place is storied and deservedly ranked highly. Going to Chicago? Stay at the Drake, stay at Chicago's finest!

I recently stayed at the Curtis Hotel while attending a conference. What an awesome gem in the heart of downtown Denver! The friendly staff, well appointed room, business amenities and walking distance to the convention center and area restaurants was just perfect. I am a fussy traveler and often times hard to please. The hotel provided great dining recommendations for entertaining clients. I would highly recommend the Curtis Hotel if you want all the amenities and convenience yet a smaller, more intimate hotel experience. Be sure to check out the restaurant and trendy bar! Loved the themed floors and elevator that announces the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""floor-theme."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Will be back.

The Marriott Downtown is near the Reading Terminal Market. Fabulous prices at restaurants in the market. Cheap fresh fruits and veggies, and rare Amish made cheeses, fresh fish market, beef, and chicken. A Maggiano's is across the street as well as a Hardrock Cafe. The staff is friendly and security roams the halls. This is a great location to also view historic Philadelphia.

Our two-night stay in San Francisco could not have been better. The Nob Hill Motor Inn is 
not a big chain hotel like the Hilton or Hyatt, but rather a quiet little inn with a family-run atmosphere. Our room was clean, up-to-date. Staff was unendingly helpful in assisting us with our itinerary in seeing the city. And don't overlook the free parking-- other hotels charge $------day-- this was a bargain!!!! If you don't mind walking a short distance to catching public transport or just walking period, this is a great place to stay. Highly recommend!!!!

This a good hotel to stay in for a family with teens in New York. The location is great and central, most of visits can be made walking.
Rooms are ok for - persons. Nice view on Times Square.Walking distance to Central Park; Empire State Building; and most of New York attractions.
Times Square and Broadway area are a great placde to be in...
Good concierge service.
Internet is very expensive and should be free for the room price we pay!
Breakfast is ok but expensive more than $-- for Buffet formula.
Excellent Health Club.

I stay in mid range hotels and this is the best value I've been to. Great location and well priced room service. My room was a little small but adequate for my needs. I like the old fashioned decor. Would recommend.

My issues: Thirty minute wait at the aiport for the hotel shuttle pick-up. Only one night stay. Business purposes. The smiles were friendly but the customer service was unacceptable. No check in until after -pm. This would be understandable IF there were no rooms available but this wasn't the case. It seems that this was just a policy that couldn't be altered. Made no sense to sleep ole' me.
Was anything OK? Sure,the staff smiled a lot. The exterior-interior were clean. The equipment in the Business Center was operable. There are a handful of eateries within walking distance (next door).

From the moment you step into the fragrantly scented candle lit lobby you will be won over by this lovely hotel. The staff are professional, efficient and helpful. Our room we a reasonable size for NY with a great view over the Chrysler Building. The location is only a block and a bit from Times Square one way, a block from Grand central station and a block from -th Ave. Excellent location. The best thing was the L'Occitane products in the bathroom, just wonderful. We really enjoyed our stay here.

Very nice location at one block from Time Square. Don't hesitate to ask for a room on the top floors because the noise of the metro is very present!
Our room was just above the reception floor and it was for me impossible to fall in sleep without sleeping pill and earplugs...
However it was a good choice and you wi'll find the metro on the --th street and -th avenue.
Free internet access and a nice restaurant """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""à la française"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" give this hotel a very good price-value
Two queen beds with a good quality and that's it!

First off, this is a perfectly pleasant - star hotel in a great location. The room and bath were tiny, but fine. The beds were quite comfortable. The carpet was stained, there were shiny liquid spray droplets (?) dried on the bathroom walls and there was dirt in the corners of the bathroom floor. Not so nice. The place is looking a bit worn and shabby. The staff was very professional and helpful which we appreciated. When I booked the room I was told that wifi was part of the package, but once we got there were told it would cost $--.-- per day. So, my husband simply accessed the internet via bluetooth and his mobile phone. Oh yes, the desk phone didn't work though the bedside one did. 
The worst thing of all was the incredibly sleazy minibar setup. All the crappy junk food ----seriously, Pringles, Mini-Oreos, do people really eat that crap?) items were placed on sensors so that if they were moved an inch, the hotel guest was charged for the item whether or not they actually consumed the product. And charged ruinously exorbitant prices, I might add. We have stayed in - - - star hotels all over the US and Europe and I've never seen anything quite so tawdry. 
Needless to say, we won't stay here again. Manhattan is filled with fantastic hotels. Why waste time and money on places like this.

We booked into Smyth after checking out from another hotel in Midtown because of poor quality. We could not have been more happy with it - great location in Tribeca, really spacious and modern rooms, great bathrooms, very light and airy with good views onto Broadway. Stellar staff and beautiful design to the public areas. Moreover it was very reasonably priced considering we were walk-ins.
We no longer need to look elsewhere when coming to NYC, this will be our #- choice!
Only word of caution is to avoid breakfast - it is gorgeous but very expensive, there are plenty of options nearby!

This was our first time at this property and we would definitely return. The room was nice and the beds were very comfortable. The staff was great and the location is excellent. There are so many restaurants and great shopping, all within walking distance. 
There are many choices for continental breakfast and the food was always replenished.

The lobby is beautiful and looks very regal. They use Bath and Body Works for their shampoo, condition, lotion and soap. Pretty much you're paying for location, as it is walking distance to Times Square and a subway station is just - blocks away. The concierge can also help you out with making reservations at restaurants.
However don't expect anything grand with the bedroom. The rooms are very small and fits only a bed, desk and TV. Bathrooms are just as tiny and don't resemble the rest of the hotel. Also, I experienced slow service where we requested an iron and had to call - times before finally going down to the front desk to request it ourselves.
Overall a decent stay with great location.

We stayed at this place for one night. Was scheduled for two nights.The noise is really bad. Street noise till -:-- am. The closest parking place is a block away. We stayed in a Hugman suite paying $---.-- per night.We had crickets in the. For tis pric it was not acceptable. We could not stand two nights and I explained the problems to the manager. We lost our money for the second night.This place is way over priced for the location and room.They had white noise machines to cover up the street noise. Still very noisy

The Chestnut Hill Hotel is an extremely comfortable, incredibly well kept, small hotel in a charming section of Philadelphia. The service is top notch and professional with the focus of effort being simply to be of assistance.
The rooms are quiet, spotless, large, and extremely comfortable. There is complementary wifi and an excellent restaurant beneath the hotel. There are some charming restaurants and shops in the vicinity. Manayunk, the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""main line"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and Center City are all within a reasonable distance. 
The Westin chain advertises a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""heavenly bed."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" The Chestnut Hill Hotel has the real thing. We have travelled extensively, and stayed at some so-called """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""world class"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotels and the bedding here is the best ever in our experience. Seriously. 
Highest recommendation, from an admittedly critical and not easily pleased traveller.

I stayed on a street room and the upside was you are right nest to metro and the down side is you are right next to metro , the train is SUPER loud I can sleep through anything but if your bothered by noise don't stay in their street rooms . We really liked the room it was nice and homey . The staff was quite friendly , and polite and helpfull the only down side was we ran into a pummeling issue with our bathroom sink and they assured us it would be fixed but it never was , so no sink for - day. Overall a truly awsome location and I will stay again I'll just be sure to bring draino.

We booked a room with city view and at check in were told that they gave us an upgrade: the upgrade was a room on a lower floor and the view was that of the buildings a few metres from the hotel building making the room dark. But the personnel was helpful and changed our room to a city view room after we complained. All in all, nice experience though: great location just a short walk away from Quincy Market and the shops. Confortable beds, funky style and funcional rooms.

Just had a delightful stay for business at this downtown beauty. Hotel is new and fresh in all respects. Nabbed a King Suite on the -th floor. Everything was pristine. Bathroom was open and airy, bed and linens were INCREDIBLE, living room was spacious and comfortable. Only knock I can come up with was that the desk was literally right next to the door to the room, so I was a little conscious about my business phone calls with the housekeeping staff right outside the door. Check-in was efficient and courteous, workout room was very nice and new. The only criticisms I have was that room service order for dinner took closer to -- minutes to deliver versus the -- minutes I was advised at the time of the order. The restaurant on the ground floor was really busy and the smells coming out of there were delicious. It is on my list for next time. An excellent choice for the business traveler. Prices were high, so I'll give a slight deduction for value, but if you are on an expense account, I would highly recommend.

My husband and I just spent a weekend in New York. We chose this hotel because I had purchased it through a shopping site. From the moment we arrived, the staff treated us as if we were frequent guests. We had lunch in the Blue Bar where Henry took excellent care of us! His recommendation for the salmon carpaccio was incredible and definitely the best I've ever eaten! Both Henry and Otto were wonderful hosts and made sure that we had everything we needed. Germaine made sure that our car was brought to us promptly. The hotel lobby has so much character.....from Matilda, the resident cat in the lobby (who KNOWS she's a star) to the charm and attention placed on every detail, the lobby was a testament to the quality of the hotel and the pride they place in their history. We have stayed at a number of fine hotels in New York, but I would definitely recommend this one! Great location, beautiful space and incredible staff!

Pros: On the cheap side. Free shuttle service. Located a stone's throw from Seatac Airport. 
Cons: Extremely worn property. Heating-Cooling units in rooms smell of mold & mildew. Inconsistent service.
The Clarion Hotel Seattle Airport has seen better days. It is an extremely worn out property that lacks consistent maintenance and housekeeping (e.g. peeling paint, holes in walls, broken furniture, etc.). Having said that, it is also on the cheap side, so the old adage that """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""you get what you pay for"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" rings true here. Now, I've stayed in several different rooms on the property, including the suites. Unfortunately, everywhere you go there is a musty smell permeating. This is just one of those properties that has you thinking """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""ewww"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" everywhere you go. 
To make matters worse, the customer service here seems as tired and apathetic as the building. In fairness, it appears that the front desk is woefully short staffed for the amount of traffic they get from airport patrons. In the several trips I've made to this property, it appears there is only one employee per shift for check-ins, reservations, wake-up calls, phone lines and customer requests.
The bottom line is that if you only need to spend one night near the airport, this hotel is tolerable. However, with numerous other hotels lining International Blvd., there are certainly better options out there.

We arrived at the hotel at check in time (-PM) and was greeted at the door by the bell man. He was very polite and helped us with our bags to our room. 
Our room was great.. We had - rooms side by side.. The beds were to die for, nothing but comfortable.. 
We had room service in the morning, which was great, nothing beats waking up to coffee, muffins, danishes, and crossiants by your bed..
I have stayed at many hotels, but The Hilton Back Bay is by far the best hotel. Location is great close to many restaurants and shops..

I stayed at the Vintage Park recently with a friend and found it great value. Yes, the bathroom was cosy, but the whole point is that Kimpton know how to take a unique, historic downtown property, restore it beautifully and run it immaculately. If you want to throw a party in your bathroom, go to any cookie-cutter Sheraton you can find and enjoy yourself.
The beds were extremely comfortable. The room was very quiet, despite the fabulous downtown location. Tulio's restaurant was wonderful - even their continental breakfasts. Service was great. 
An all-round pleasure.

I normally don’t seek out large hotels, like the Hyatt Regency Chicago, that are frequented by conventions and other large groups. However, the deal I got on this hotel for three nights in May, using an Entertainment Card, was approximately $-- to $--- cheaper than if I had stayed at a comparable hotel. So, if I had been paying full price, I probably would have gone to a smaller place, but at the price I paid I was perfectly happy at the Hyatt and enjoyed my stay.
The hotel is large, but not anywhere near as large as the hotels in Vegas, where it can take -- minutes to get from your room to the main entrance. Rooms are very modern and comfortable; service is adequate. I didn’t eat at the hotel, so I don’t know what the restaurants are like. The fitness center is quite large and is better than most places I have stayed. Best of all, is the location – just a block from North Michigan Avenue with easy access to the Loop, Millenium Park and the Art Institute and the great shopping and restaurants of the Magnificent Mile and surrounding areas.
So, again, if you are paying full price, you probably could do better, but if you get a deal via Entertainment Card, AAA rates, Hotwire or Priceline, this is a fine place to stay.

Peoria Arizona- I stayed at this hotel June --th ---- and was not please with the room size. The hotel was in a great location, but the rooms were very small. The Hotel monitors the air conditon units so you cannot stay in your room during the day. The Hotel turns the air up about midnight, until then the room is very uncomfortable. The beds needs new mattresses and new comforters. The bathroom is small and the ceiling was peeling. 
I informed the front desk of theses problem and they stated that they would let maintenance know, but nothing changed. You have to pay seventeen dollars a day for valet parking when it should be free considering how much you must pay for this Hotel which is similiar to Motel - on a good day. I think this Hotel would be nice if they would shut it down and remodel the rooms. The staff is courteous , but the food is terrible, the potatoes were dry and they ran out of pastry all the time. This Hotel need to take a look at cutting their prices to eighty-nine dollars a night instead of a hundred and twenty a night. 
Also they would benefit from hiring new cooks. And the elevator did not work all the time.
I give this Hotel a rating of one. Will not stay here again unless they remodel because as I said earlier it is in a great location.

Our family of two adults and two children, ages - and --, stayed at this hotel for part of a Northern California family vacation for three nights, April - - -, ----. I booked it through Hotwire at a rate of $---.-- per night, and for that price we got a fabulous deal. The Hotwire listing stated """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""-.- Star Hotel, Union Square West, Moscone Center."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I was pretty sure we would get the InterContinental and we are so glad we did! I used a website called """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Better Bidding"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to help me predict we'd get the InterContinental - so helpful! 
It was my first experience using Hotwire, and I was expecting to be assigned to a low-level room by a noisy elevator. Upon check-in, we were thrilled to learn we had been upgraded to an --th floor bay-view room. Our room was spotlessly clean, quiet (with the occasional sound of a fire truck, but it was San Francisco we chose to stay in!), and the double beds were very comfortable. (The sheets and bedding were even more comfortable to me than that of the Ritz-Carlton Half Moon Bay, which was the hotel we went to after our stay here - so kuddos to the InterContinental!) My only wish was for queen beds, not doubles, in the rooms. (The Ritz had doubles, too, by the way.)
The location of this hotel met our needs quite well. Since we knew it would be about $--.-- to park a car we did not rent one. I would recommend to all families traveling in San Francisco to not rent a car, not only because of the expense, but it's very stressful to navigate around a busy city like SF with all of the bus lanes, speeding taxi cabs and people. It was a $--.-- cab fare to Pier -- to do Alcatraz, and about $--.-- to the Exploratorium. We definitely saved money and aggravation by not renting a car.
Because of expense, we only dined once at the hotel restaurant and it was for the breakfast buffet. We had met a very nice fellow guest at the pool one evening who gave us his two adult breakfast vouchers he wouldn't be using. Since the hotel breakfast buffet costs $--.-- per adult, this was another huge savings for us and we were so thankful! The cost for each of our children was $--.-- and we enjoyed a delicious buffet with fabulous service - a very special breakfast! On other mornings, we dined at a nearby Denny's, Starbucks and Mel's Diner - all within a block of the hotel. There are many, many restaurants within walking distance of this hotel. We walked to dinner one night at a great seafood restaurant called Anchor and Hope - wonderful food and very different from the seafood we get at home in Atlanta! =) We also dined in the food court of the mall one evening. I am typically NOT a food court fan, but this one was unique and upscale. 
One evening we were all so exhausted from our day of touring that we used hotel room service for dinner. We had great pasta dinners and the prices were reasonable, considering it was room service. We had taken our own bottled waters to the hotel with us and never consider using a hotel mini-bar.
We visited the hotel indoor pool and hot tub a couple of times. It is a smallish, two or three lane pool but served our purposes well as our --year-old is a competitive year-round swimmer and needed to keep up with his training. We very much appreciated that the hotel had goggles for loan at the pool - a nice touch of the hotel.
We had never stayed in an InterContinental before and were overall thrilled with our choice. I am SO GLAD that we stayed here and not at one of the hotels in the Fisherman's Wharf area. Though the Wharf area is where we spent much of our time, I found the InterContinental to be a quiet, restful place after full day of touring the city. There were very few other children in this business-oriented hotel. Because of this, we never encountered any screaming, ill-behaved children running up and down the hallways of this hotel or playing in elevators as we have in many other """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""family-oriented"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotels in which we've stayed. We were able to have a peaceful, enjoyable stay. I would definitely choose this hotel for a future San Francisco stay - Hotwire deal or not.

The main highlight of this hotel is it's location. Just about anywhere in """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""tourist"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Boston can be reached on foot from here, but it's also located close to two subway lines. The rooms feature the heavenly bed and shower. Don't expect the personnel touch.

I thought I have to write this review to advice folks to stay away from this hotel. It was a mistake to book this hotel. I stayed in NYC many times. Unfortunately, all my favorite hotels were overbooked due to the last minute booking. It started with -- min wait for the check in. The line was long. The room was horrible..dirty..pelling paint. Let´s hope there is not lead. The carpet in hall way was third world hotel. This hotel´s time is over. It might be good in the past but now it is just dirty. There was no hot water on my last day and the water pressure was so low that the water would not flow. PLEASE, do yourself a favor. Do not stay here. Book early and stay at other places.

Well, I wasn't sure about staying at the Sheraton at Fisherman's Wharf in San Francisco because I've known about that hotel for many years. It's been there for many years, and I was afraid it would be old and worn out. I traveled with a good friend, the woman who was my best friend in high school fifty years ago. It took a bit to figure out that you enter their driveway from a side street. The common areas are very nice and the personnel very helpful and friendly.
Our room overlooked the driveway where taxis enter to drop off people and where we left our car with valet. Now for the parking. Would you believe $-- per day! Parking in San Francisco is outrageous. The hotel was nice, but I'd be inclined to look around next time to see if I could find something with cheaper or free parking, possibly in the Van Ness area. It was a bit noisy in our room one night as people came into the lobby right below our window at all hours of the night.
The room was nicely appointed. New everything, except for the heater which worked just fine.
Now, for the beds. Fantastic! I don't know what they do to make those beds as comfy as they are, but I want to duplicate that feeling at home. I pulled back the sheets and found a tag saying the bed was a Serta P-S (which I assume stands for Serta Perfect Sleeper.) It didn't say if it was firm, soft, or whatever. I'd say it was somewhere between firm and medium firm. The sheets and pillowcases were smooth and tight weaved. I found that I could order those exact same sheets by going to Sheraton.com. Expensive but luxurious. And at only --- thread count, which I have given up getting in recent years. These have some polyester in them. Feel so rich and smooth. Then, the blanket and duvet were also luxurious. I think I've made my point; I all but purred when I rooched down into that bed. 
We did not try the hotel restaurants and instead walked to restaurants in the adjacent Fisherman's Wharf area. Be prepared for big time tourist attractions. Lots of junky shops and vendors but with really good seafood restaurants all over the place.
People with asthma and or-alergies might want to think about staying somewhere else; we both reacted to something. Don't have a clue what it was, but my eyes were bright red by the second day, and my friend was resorting to her inhaler for her asthma. We were both extremely uncomfortable.
Bottom line is we liked this property. Everything in San Francisco is outrageously expensive. For about $--- through Priceline, Hotwire, or other discount sites, you can get the room. Then, we added tax and parking and wound up paying about $--- a night.

Pros: Very clean. Front desk staff very nice. Parking and breakfast included. Good location for those visiting the Stockyards. 
Cons: On the pricey side. Was a bit noisy at --- am when the part goers returned to their rooms. Breakfast was really just okay. 
Overall, we would stay here again.

Stayed here with my family for one night in June. Very clean, great location, helpful staff, and gorgeous view. Nice running path along golf course in front of hotel and shopping mall across street. Great breakfast buffet. Very clean and well kept pool.
Hated to leave!

I'll start with the pros. The reviews on this site are, for the most part, accurate. It does have a cool retro vibe - decor is adorable. Location is excellent, and there is free parking, which is important. The diner downstairs is FANTASTIC - we ate there several times and loved every meal, and the prices were quite reasonable. We were really prepared to love everything about this place.
As long as everything in your room works, this hotel is great. So I assume that the majority of the reviews have been left by people whose rooms were functional, and probably the odds are in favor of that, so it may be worth the risk, particularly because LA hotels are so expensive. We would have been one of those reviews if we'd stayed in our first room, quite honestly. However, we had requested a king non-smoking and were given - doubles instead. We stayed there the first night, because we got in very late, and that room was nice, and everything worked. However, my husband is - foot -, and the beds were WAY too small for him, and we couldn't share one (they were tiny), and since it was a romantic weekend away, we asked for a room change in the morning, and got one. No problem.
This is when we discovered that if something in your room doesn't work, you're screwed. In the next room, the toilet was broken. We were told that maintenance couldn't come until THE NEXT DAY, so IF they could find one, we could have another room (like having a room with no toilet was a reasonable option!). In the room we were moved to, the shower was broken, and the answer was basically, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Tough, wait until maintenance comes tomorrow"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The attitude of both people we spoke to about the shower (the night it broke and the next morning) was that we were being unreasonably fussy by expecting our plumbing to work correctly; one said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I know about YOU people - you SAID your last room had problems too"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (as if we'd made it up) and the other said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""So in every room you have, the shower is broken?"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" We calmly reminded him that no, the toilet was broken in the first room. However, we were pretty angry that no apologies were given and we were blamed for the problems; the usual response for a hotel in this case would be to apologize for having things in the room that weren't working, inconveniencing the guests. And they were pretty MAJOR things - it's not like the remote control was broken or something.
Sadly, we had to agree that we wouldn't stay here again. Sure, we might get lucky and next time, our room might have no problems at all. Or we might have another broken toilet on a night that the entire hotel was booked - with this hotel's """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""we don't call maintenance until morning if only one room is having problems, no matter what"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" policy (this is what the front desk lady told us when we called about the shower), we could end up spending the night without a toilet, or having to pay for a room somewhere else just to get a room with a toilet that worked! That's not a chance we're willing to take.

My daughter left her ring on he floor in the bathroom with her pajamas. When we came back, it was gone. I reported it to the night shift, but when I checked back in the morning, the next shift knew nothing about the report. He said he would check with housekeeping. He acted bothered by the request when I came back after breakfast and told me housekeeping did not open until -- AM - as if I should know when they get there. He told my husband when we left that they would contact us - never did. This was a very special ring for my daughter, and she was pretty upset. We will not be staying with Homewood Suites again.

I have to say that while the hotel is in a fabulous location close to central park, the Metropolitan and Guggenheim and the neat places in the Upper west Side and Harlem, with lots of cafes and especially a great Bagel place called Tal Bagel, and the subway connections were great, we found the hotel a little rundown and definately our room let in all the considerable noise outside. In fact, because the air conditioner was put in the window and then tape was used to try and seal the space ( which had disappeared in one section , so the cold night air was blowing in - although the hotel staff did at least put more tape on the next day), we could hear conversations on the street below , as if the window was open. Add to that the fact that there were construction things on the street that made noise everytime a car went over them - i didn't sleep at all the first night and only slightly better the other nights. Now I know NYC is busy and people do stuff ----, but this was very noisy. The room itself was fair, although some of the slats for the blinds had been broken off, there were only sheers on - of the windows , so it was very bright, the toilet handle was cracked too. As I said, we did like being away from the hustle and bustle of the tourist area, but close enough to visit when we wanted. But no, won't stay at this hotel on our next visit.

Hotel rooms are nice and very quiet, the restaurant food was fantastic. However, I will not use this hotel again - there are just three elevators for over -- floors, and you will wait, and wait and wait. Over twenty minutes each time - pretty disappointing

The London NYC was the perfect location for a New York City trip. Almost EVERYTHING was in walking distance. Since this was my first trip to New York City, accessibility was key. This was a solo trip and I am a bit younger (--) and I think some of the staff wasn't sure on how to treat me. I'm a well educated young lady, and for the most part, everyone treated me with respect.
I didn't know about the free use of the General Manager's car, and I saw that the bell boy had offered it to another older couple as they were leaving. My only gripe was that I wish they had offered it once to me as I was standing around waiting for a taxi, since I was a girl by herself, from California.
The rooms were BEYOND comfortable and spacious. Hands down probably one of the best properties I've stayed at. I can't wait to come back and enjoy it.

If you or family are receiving treatment at one of the area hospitals, the location can not beat.
However, the hotel was a nightmare to deal with. Booked a stay of over a week while a family member was having surgery at Children's. We were advised to book based on our longest projection and that we could check out early if there was an early discharge. This was confirmed verbally when the reservation was made, at check-in, and at check-out, as well as in writing.
The hotel ended up booking us for nearly an extra week, despite advising the hotel - times that we were checking out both via phone and the front desk. They repeatedly refused to correct the problem and forced us to chargeback the additional nights.

My husband, son and I stayed one night at the Marriott as we were in town to see The Lion King.
We arrived an hour before check-in time and were able to check into our requested room ( Times Square view) right away. The room was very large for NYC and the furnishings were nice. The bathroom was well appointed, but a little on the small side. Would have liked a mini-bar or little refigerator in the room. 
We left the hotel several times and never had a problem with the elevators. Most of the time the elevator was available within seconds, and our longest wait was a couple of minutes. There did seem to be some people in the lobby having difficulty understanding how the elevators were assigned, but the process was very straightforward and my nine-year old had no problem grasping the concept.
There were plenty of places to eat and shop within blocks of the hotel. We have stayed at other hotels in the Times Square area, but we enjoyed the Marriott the most.

The grounds were beautiful. And our kids loved the pool. The food was very expensive, but really good. Our room, however, was tiny, outdated and musty smelling....more like a motel. Within -- minutes of being in the room our children's feet turned black. Absolutely disgusting. The shower curtain also had mold spots on it and the beds-pillows were horrible. The baby crib also had a terrible, musty smell. For the cost of the room (very expensive given it was a holiday weekend), I did expect a nicer room, but most of all I expected a clean one.

We stayed here for - nights in January ----. Obviously not a really popular time in NYC so we got a great price ($---night). Yes, the hotel is a bit dated. We were in an unrenovated room. However, for the price plus the convenience of the location this was a great hotel. the beds were very comfortable. The room was small but who goes to NYC to sit in a hotel room? The carpets were old too but the hotel is going through a renovation right now. I really thought this was one of the better places I have stayed at in New York. I don't think I would have paid $--- a night for this hotel but if you get a good deal take it. I would rate this as a -.- star hotel. The staff was also great. Very helpful. This trip was with my -- year old daughter. This was a perfect sized room for the - of us.

The experience here at the West Loop Marriott was great! Marriott provided a town car to take us out for our special dinner out in town. This service provided us to relax and enjoy our night out. The rooms were clean, modern and very warming. Breakfast had so many selections to choose from at the right temperature. I would highly recommend this hotel for any visiting Houston. It is a wonderful location and the associates are very nice.

I was going to NY on the train for a shopping trip. I chose this hotel based on location, reviews and price and I was pleasantly surprised. Although the rooms are very small, they are immaculately clean; the bed and pillows were the most comfortable I have ever experienced at a hotel. The view was nice of the Hudson River - the staff was friendly - I was travelling with my elderly mother, who was tired from the trip, and were able to check in early. The hotel felt safe, with staff near the elevator area. The Tick Tock Diner had good food at reasonable prices for NY hotel fare.The location was convenient and within walking distance of many attractions. The bathroom did need work - it was not renovated and it was hard to find a place for toiletries. However, on the whole this hotel is quite a value for NYC and I would recommend it without reservation. I will certainly return...

I stayed for a week at the Hyatt for a conference. Check in was smooth and easy. My room was clean and comfortable. No coffee maker in room (but Starbucks on ground floor!). Elevators were fast and not crowded. As a Platinum member, my internet was free and I got coffee coupons, which was a bonus. The hotel is right around the corner from a large mall with a good food court, but not much else around that I could tell. The X bar has some good Stella Artois beer! It was a little pricey for me, but it is a Hyatt near Beverly Hills! The large convention area was nice, but we had some items stolen from our workshop room on the last day.

I stayed with a friend for a girl's weekend away. The grounds and architecture of the Hacienda is lovely. There are several places where guests can sit outside to enjoy the beautiful weather on a patio amidst bougainvilleas. From a balcony above, you can see red-tiled roofs, rich foliage, and winding staircases. It is also right in Old Town, which I think I liked the most about the place. We didn't need to get into a car if we did not feel like it, and it's kind of nice to have a few drinks and know you can just walk home. The rooms were clean and large enough but a bit dark. It is not a luxury hotel in terms of the rooms. The shutters kept the room exceptionally dark at night--great!--but did not keep out noise much. We could hear movement upstairs, voices next door, and someone emptied trash or something early in the morning. Pool and jacuzzi nice. Free breakfast not worth it. Overall, if you plan to stay in the room a lot and you are a light sleeper, I don't recommend it. If you want to be able to hang out in a fun place without having to drive and a beautiful environment, it is great.

Just had - great nights at the San Carlos New York from the --th June. Excellent location. a little noisy across the road is a nightclub, but you are in New York & you have to get used to that. The rooms are large for New York, with Queen Size beds which is highly unusual for America, which were extremely comfortable. Great lounge area, with a small kitchenette, enough for us (microwave, fridge & sink). Staff couldn't do enough for us, everytime we came back from a long hard day pounding the streets we were always greeted and asked how our day was. Breakfast for a self serve is excellent, you really dont need the huge buffet everyday, they had a great choice for a continental breakfast, somedays it does get a little crowded though. Some fantastic local restaurants just two blocks away in a really local area, supermarket, pharmacy etc. Very safe area never felt unsafe. Great stay, thank you San Carlos. Highly recommended..

I've never written a review for this or any site. However, as a mother, I'm disturbed by the thought that any young ladies might get stuck here. Scary.
I normally like to use fairly nice hotels. But my husband and I were going to a reggae concert at the Majestic. This hotel is listed as the closest to that theater. We were just looking for a place to sleep after the concert and then heading straight home in the morning. So we wanted the closest and cheapest. We were warned, but thought it would be fine since we're not usually too skittish in the average situation. Another reviewer stated that it is not for the weak or easily scared - he is a brave brave man. 
The furniture is as pictured, old but okay. The walls are like cement with cracks that are painted white which gave it a creepy feel. The smell was not good. The window was duct taped at one time but it had come apart. As a result, you could push on the window from the outside with one finger and have your hand inside the room. The fan in the bathroom made a horrible noise - so loud that we had to shout over it. I expected a dump, but this was seedy and scary. After the concert we decided that our safety was worth more than $--, took the loss, and made the ---minute drive back home.

Stayed here when my first choice hotel was oversold. Paid $---, and couldn't sleep due to the noise - paper thin walls, slamming doors. The rooms are very tiny - when I opened the door I immediately thought """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Japan"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Ever ride a toilet side saddle? Tiny. However, very clever design, beautiful fixtures, clean. The heater was very loud (clanging, banging in middle of night). The little desk and metal chair wasn't very cozy for doing work. The restaurant had great food. The lobby was cool, fun atmosphere. Bouncers at the elevators waiting for you to produce your room key to pass. I would never choose to stay here again, because ultimately, I want a good night's sleep from a hotel.

This is a great hotel to stay in or plan an event. The staff helped me replan my entire wedding in less than a month and were there every step of the way.
I have to say the staff went above and beyond to make sure my wedding was nothing less than perfect. Words are still not enough to express the way I feel. I will recommend the Double-tree Hotel to everyone I know that is planning an event and to stay. The rooms were very nice and the entire staff service was excellent. 
I look forward to staying there again.

My friend and I stayed her las Saturday. We were looking for a location close to La Cantera Shopping and this hotel was right around the corner. Lobby and outside patio area were very nice as well as the rooms. We ate breakfast there in the morning. We had a bagel and coffee but they did have a nice breakfast buffet. Would definately stay here again!!

I've stayed in various hotels around Powell St BART Station (Palomar, Marriott Marquis, Pickwick). It's a great location for getting to places and there's a Walgreen's on every corner!
Hotel Monaco is a Kimpton hotel, and their hotels are always quirky and high-quality. Free Internet, cocktails (though always at a time I can never attend), nice toiletries, great beds. This certainly describes the Monaco. The hotel was extremely clean and well-appointed.
On the downside, the rooms are fairly small, especially when compared with the Palomar or Marriott. However, it's plenty for single travelers. My room faced the rear of the building and there was no noise.
The Monaco is two blocks west of Union Square and the area is quite lively at night. One block east is the American Conservatory Theatre, a beautiful building restored after the ---- earthquake. It's currently showing """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Tales of the City"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", a fun musical set in San Francisco in the --s. After the show, the area was filled with people streaming past the art galleries and nearby clubs and restaurants.

I cannot believe that Hotel.com would list The Milner Hotel in Detroit Michigan to choose from, to stay in Detroit....The WORST Hotel I have ever and probable will ever stay in. Unfortunatly I had to stay - night, worst night of my life!

The Marriott Suites is an excellent choice if visiting the Dallas area for three main reasons. 
-) Free shuttle service: parking can be expensive and they will drive you and pick you up from anywhere in a - mile radius. 
-) Great rooms: the extra living room space and color palate really increased the enjoyability factor of our stay. 
-) Free breakfast: make sure you book your room with a free breakfast. Not only was it delicious but the service was extravagant. 
Please note that internet does not come for free at the Marriott but that there is a business center with a printer attached as well.

The staff is very nice and proactive! Always ready to help. 
Breakfast is very limited but is okay!
My room was not fully cleaned as i found crackers-ships under the window! I stayed - nts an my room as not been cleaned at all during my stay.

Nice friendly little hotel in a great little neighborhood. Convenient to walk or take a cab to restaurants, shopping, etc. Very friendly reception and on-site personnel -- hours a day. Will definitely return on my next visit to San Francisco in a few months.
I cannot thank the staff here enough for extending warmth, kindness to me and my family in our time of grief. Thank for for making our stay pleasant and worry free. God bless you! <-
Stayed here from Friday --th March until Monday -nd April. Lovely room albeit slightly small. Excellent location, close to Fanueil Hall. Would most definitely recommend.

Stayed for - days in late August with husband and - teenage sons. Double-queen bed room was fairly large; small kitchen area with fridge and microwave was convenient. The room was well-appointed and very clean, and the only thing I could criticize is that the carpet was worn. Location was excellent, just a short walk to the Riverwalk and other attractions. Every single hotel employee we encountered was friendly. Breakfast included pancakes, biscuits & gravy, oatmeal, fruit, and yogurt, and real scrambled eggs. Also it was great to get snacks (that served as a meal on more than one occasion!) and drinks every night--it saved us a fortune, considering that my teenage sons do nothing but eat lately. The rooftop pool-hottub area was clean and enjoyable. This isn't a full-service hotel, but it perfectly met our needs for a very reasonable price. I wouldn't hesitate to stay there again and wholeheartedly agree with other reviewers who say this is a great place for families.

The Sheraton Dallas Galleria staff makes business travel a pleasure! They are extremely attentive to their guests' every need. The facility has been renovated beautifully. The pillows and comforters on the beds are ultra-comfortable. The workout facility is the best I have experienced in a hotel. The pool lounge chairs are inviting to say the least. As for the food, no need to go out in search of a better meal. However, the Galleria is a short walk from the hotel and has every possible food choice.

Copley Square Hotel is in a terrific location, the rooms are lovely, and the staff are incredibly nice. They offer complimentary coffee and hot chocolate all day, and a cocktail hour (free wine) in the evenings. It's a really nice touch, and people gather in the lounge and visit with each other while having a drink. I haven't had an experience like that in a US city before. I also had dinner via the bar, since the weather outside was terrible and the restaurant was closed for a private function. The food was terrific and the atmosphere in the bar was fun without being completely crazy.

With a family of five we can't be too picky on where we stay -- we needed a suite and Springhill had one. Room are not huge, but adequate for two parents, three kids. 
Pros: EXCELLENT location -- we easily walked everywhere for shopping, theater, dinner, etc. Really conveniently located -- definitely the biggest pro
--Front desk responds quickly to complaints (see below).
--I like that the sink is in a separate area from the toilet-shower room. 
--Great gym -- (but very small pool)
--Sofa with attached chaise lounge was very comfy
Cons: The BIG complaint -- This building is divided into two hotels: Springhill and a Residence Inn. The half of the building that the Springhill occupies is next to an extremely loud night club. We were originally on the -th floor and when the music started reverberating our suite at -- pm we called the front desk to ask how long we could expect to be feeling the bass. Their prompt answer was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""-:-- am -- we can call over to ask them to turn it down. We get this a lot."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" 
Needless to say their request to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""turn it down"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was apparently not met and we spent the evening with ear plugs in. We requested a room change to the front of the building, but the suites only occupy that side -- so we were moved up to the --th floor. The music was fainter and didn't interfere with sleep. If you stay here request a room as high as possible unless you and your traveling companions are very deep sleepers. If you are with kids as we were, it can be a nightmare.
Other con is just sort of odd and not something I've ever seen before. This place is AWESOME. The grounds are beautiful with native Texas landscaping. The pool area is worth the visit - the hotel has its own man made river to float on. I stayed in this hotel for a week on business and my room felt like a home away from home. Comfortable bed, large flat screen TV, large desk, adequate high speed internet, balcony with amazing view. If you want to venture out to San Antonio, the hotel is about -- minutes away from downtown and a bevy of restaurant choices. The hotel is besides the Metro station which is convenient but can get noisy in the night as the railway tracks also pass beside the metro's. My wife and I stayed at this property during a weekend in NYC. The property looks almost new, and is terrific condition. The rooms are a little small (as expected in NYC), but well appointed. The Monaco makes one feel like they've gone back in time and living a scene in a movie like the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Maltese Falcon"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". There's an old time elegance to it, though not in a seedy slightly rundown way. Everything is up to date,

The rooms are a bit small but well furnished and there is no A-C, but its rare one needs it in SF.
Being located on Geary St. has its pluses and minuses. Great Diners for breakfast and lunch, a few good restaurants, Sushi in particular and art galleries, but the street is a bit seedy. We have previously visit San Francisco and this time we decided to stay in a hotel closer to MArket st so I read a few reviews and decided for this one. I've stayed twice at this hotel for business reasons. As I was traveling alone, location was important. It's just a few steps from Times Square so there is no way of getting bored or feeling lonely and shops are open until - or - AM.

stayed here for - nights and hotel was brilliant - comfortable beds good shower clean and quiet. we enjoyed this stay as we were on honeymoon from scotland - we ate in papasitos on recommendation from hotel - BEST TEX MEX EVER!!!

This is not a luxury hotel--and it's not priced like one--but it is extremely comfortable and charming. If you're looking to stay in Union Square on a budget, this is the place to be.

In all, I would definitely stay at this hotel again for the price and the quality of the hotel.
