Hotel is clean, comfortable, and well placed for Penn Station, lots of Subway lines, MACY'S, Times Square and above all the Empire State Building which was outside our window with the Chrysler away to the right. Breakfast was a buffet of bagels, apples, bananas - kinds of bread to toast, Quaker oats, fruit juice coffee and tea and a free neswpaper. The staff efficient and friendly.
Although the price was sort of lowish, the additional taxes (x-) bumped up the final bill considerably. The street is in Korea Town, so all shops and commerce were Korean, including take away meals and grocery stores. Many stayed open until midnight, but there was a tendancy for large piles of slightly smelly rubbish waiting to be cleared each night. Generally a safe area for late night night strolls. One block in any direction and all the more usual eateries were in evidence.

I stayed at the Sommerset Suites for only - nights in mid October. They were very welcoming and the room was immaculate. I was worried from reading some of the reviews about the location since it seats between two hospital buildings but I was not bothered by any noise. The location is closer to the Hillcrest bar-restaurant scene than I had expected. I would definitely stay here the next time I travel to San Diego! I liked that they offered a pass to the fitness center although I did not take it up. The only thing I would have liked was an scrambled egg-omelet station in the morning continental breakfast.

Just returned from a four night stay. Had a wonderful time. Arrived around -:-- pm on Tuesday. Check-in was a breeze. Was given a very nice room in the north tower with views of the marina. Since I was on the end of the tower I actaully had two balconies, one with a view of the city and the other of the marina. The pool was great and not overcrowded at all. Pool service was excellent. Location is great with easy walk to Seaport Village, Gaslamp District and the Midway. Would definitely stay there again, in fact, planning another trip next month.

This hotel is located right in the city center with great views of the war memorial and just a few blocks from the City Center Mall - the perfect location for travelers without a rental car. Unlike other Sheratons, this Sheraton charges for in-room internet access, but wi-fi is free in the hotel lobby and there's a Starbuck located in the hotel lobby with free wi-fi.
As a basic SPG (frequent user-customer), I was greeted with a bag of goodies (bottle of water and a couple of sweet treats) upon check-in. 
Rooms are nice and big with all the amenities. Rates are very reasonable and a great value.

So we stayed at this hotel for -- nights at the start of June. The hotel itself is great. Comfortable beds, gorgeous lobby, comfortable rooms.. And free valet! Only downside is during check in they want $-- per night for incidentals which is fair enough.. And of course a credit card number and figure out the payment on check out.. This was all good until I noticed my credit card had been drawn for $---- in all separate transactions. This ment all my spending money was frozen and had been charged over drawn fees each time they went over. Which accrued to over $---aud. Certain people were sympathetic whereas the manager thought I was being dramatic. I stay at alot more boutique hotels across the world and never have I had a hotel charge the payment in small installments. People pay on checkout and a credit card number should be enough security until then.. Absolutely ridiculous. I was having a great trip until now and have now been turned completely off this hotel. Proberly due to the fact I can't even afford lunch until the money is released. Communication between management and staff here is shocking because one person said one thing, and another said something completely different..

I stayed here on a business trip for - nights. I was pleasantly surprised by almost every aspect of the hotel. Despite a somewhat bland curbside appearance, the rooms are updated and clean and it has everything you need at a reasonable price. My room was $----nt, which I assume was less than the Hilton Anatole just down the street. Ironing boards in room, free internet, marble baths, comfortable beds and linens. The exercise equipment in the fitness center was pretty new and certainly adequate to break a sweat after a day of meetings. They had aerobic machines and also some dumbbells with a bench. The bar and back porch were really great for team meetings and they were crowded every night I was there. The pool is outside and at the time the weather was too cool for my taste, but there were other who did use it. The restaurant and room service were good. Cabs in Dallas are expensive and I when learned that a DART station was a closeby, I used that a lot. It was a short walk but not an inviting stroll as you need to cross underneath a highway overpass. The hotel might offer a shuttle to the DART for downtown travelers who don't want to drop $-- on a -- minute cab ride. A great restaurant nearby is The Moth - not much else otherwise.

My girlfriend and I enjoyed one of the Deluxe Suites for a five night stay over the '-- New Years. The room was furnished with a fireplace, offering a pleasant atmosphere to the cold winter nights of Denver. A nice flat screen TV with plenty of channels - perfect for lazy mornings! A wonderful down comforter and decent room service. Overall the Inn was pleasant and the staff was engaging and hospitable. If given the opportunity, I would stay here again. 
BTW... The Inn at Cherry Creek may not carry the curb appeal of the Marriot Hotel (located one city block away) but, you will still have the comfort, cleaniliness, and local shopping experience at only a portion of the price of the Marriot. Consider staying here, it's worth it!

First time to the Big APple. Loved everything about this hotel. The location is outstanding , short walk to times square, but just far enough away its nice and quiet at night. Staff are professional , friendly and very helpful. Our room was so comfortable , very clean , nice and big by New York standards, and the bed was amazing!!! . We had a king suite on the --th floor, nice view. Felt safe walking home very late at night, which you can easily do from a Broadway show or the square. Subway close by, drugstore, food...you name it . SIMPLY PERFECT!!

The hotel is a stone's throw from the San Diego airport. If your room faces the marina, you will hear the planes taking off and the balcony is of not much use due to the constant noise. However, the sliding glass door does a good job of shielding the noise. The lobby decor is in the marine theme and is very inviting. But, the arms on the chairs look pretty dirty even though the fabric was dark blue. I changed my room because the bathroom smelled and the paint was peeling on the bathroom ceiling. The second room was better. Decor is in blues and white with a touch of red. I attended a meeting with work and the food supplied by the hotel was very good - everything they served was tasty. Front staff was friendly and helpful and what you'd expect. The location of this hotel is not the best. It's on Harbor Island and it is very isolated. There is nothing else around there that is interesting. You have to get in your car to really enjoy the San Diego experience. There are a couple of restaurants down the road. I went to one and it's just not very lively around the hotel area. If you're looking for isolation and want to stay on the property, this place is OK if you don't mind jet noise. I'd stay somewhere else in the future that has places to eat, drink, and shop within walking distance, like around Seaport Village. This hotel does the best with what it has, but it can't change its location.

Parking was very complicated: the stickers did not appear, you never know what to do and the staff in the parking is absolutely unfriendly. They act as if they were the maximum authority in the world, rude and unrespectful. The elevator was smelly and tremendously slow. We spent a lot of time waiting: one only elevator for all the Hotel. The room was very small, the bathroom was terrible, everything smelled old. It is for the first time in my life that a hotel has no breakfast (¡!) You must go elsewhere to have it. Friendly staff was probably the only positive thing we found.

Upon arrival, hotel is swave, and funky. Staff didnt seem too friendly, but it was busy so I initially didnt think much of it. Then, when we got to our floor, impressions faded, decorated nicely, but a moldy smell, attempted to hide behind tacky air fresheners. We had booked a deluxe queen, through hotels.com, now first of all hotels.com messed up our booking so that we were not even in the right month with the hotel, even though our confirmation has our dates on it, and the room we booked was described as having a sitting area, mini fridge and safe, none of those in our room, so we checked the booking online, and even though hotels.com listed a deluxe as that, it is not so on the best western site (needless to say, i wont use hotels.com again)! 
Back to hotel, - lights are not working, cant get hold of the front desk to fix it, shower head was rusty, and the bed is a small sized queen, if there is such a thing, bedding has pulled threads and is none to nice.
and we had to spend a half hour on the phone to get the internet to work

This was my second visit to this property, my reason for returning was due to location and a reasonable price. However, the online price direct with the hotel did not match the price I was charged on my credit card ... I was charged an additional $-- on my credit card. This was amended at check out, but I did try and email on - occasions before my arrival and never got a response.
My reason for booking direct with the hotel was to try and get a better view than my previous visit. My last view was a brick wall with no sunlight. I asked on the booking form for a view after my last experience. On check in a -.--pm there was no rooms ready, fair enough. The hotel offered to store our bags but we said we would wait in the lounge after a -hr flight. We were told the wait would be no more than an hr. No offer of a drink during our wait. By -.--pm I asked the desk was there a room available....yes there was! Don't know how long I would of sat there if I hadn't had asked. Ask the girl on check in did it have a view? she said she wasn't sure but there is a chance your might be able to see the chrysler building. However, if I was unhappy with the room I could swop it the following night.
We got a lovely size room and the pantry was handy. Bathroom was better and newer than my previous visit. But the view was terrible, I was - rooms away from previous visit, -nd floor and had - windows in total. I have included pictures so your have a realistic idea of your view, first window was full of pipes and air con units, second window was the back of another hotel with broken glass and window panes (I realise the hotel can't control this). And a few days later I discovered you can see the Chrysler building!!!! If you sit on the toilet with the blind up you can just see the tip of it! Didn't bother swopping rooms, too much of a pain, packing and unpacking and to be honest I think about --% of the hotel rooms have poor views. My view was made worst by the fact I was on the -nd floor and could see below.
I know whilst in the city you see the views on foot, but it was my mum's first visit and I wanted it special...I see very little point of asking for room requests when they are not considered. 
On a positive note, staff were friendly, fab housekeeping, great location and nice breakfast in rare.

Excellent value this. My wife and I stayed here in ---- and enjoyed it, and have just stayed again - with two kids this time.
Room was clean, comfy and very well equipped with fridge and microwave as well as the telly. Bathroom very clean, sheets changed daily. Friendly staff, other than those on reception.
For UK readers, the price worked out at £-- p.n for all four of us (mum, dad and two kids) which compares favourably with London hotels, for example - and you get breakfast here (bagels, doughnuts, fruit, coffee and juice, just fine.
But it's the location that is so great - easy walk to Empire State, Time Sq, Macy's, Madison Sq, Flatiron, loads of eats on Fifth Ave and surrounding streets. Subway at the end of the street, same with Post Office. Internet in the lobby. 
No complaints here, highly recommended.

We stayed at The Handlery for - nights from -st September, our first port of call on our - week honeymoon in the U.S. My parents had emailed the hotel to let them know that we were arriving and were on our honeymoon. When we arrived the man behind the desk was so welcoming and polite and congratulated us before we went off to our room, to find that they had upgraded our 'regular historic room' up to what can only be explained as a 'Suite'! Huge for a city hotel! We were welcomed to a bottle of sparkling wine on ice and a bag of snacks and water...perfect after our -- hour flight! Later on, getting back to our room after a day out, we found a message on the answerphone from the owner of the hotel, welcoming and congratulating us, and apologising that he wasn't available to welcome us when we arrived! Little things like this - that we really didn't expect, or need - made us really feel special and set our honeymoon apart from any other holiday.
The room, staff & The Daily Grill - All perfect, a brilliant start to our honeymoon! We hope to visit San Francisco again in the future, and would definitely consider staying at the Handlery again. The location of this hotel is great!

Perfect spot in Hollywood, just -min from Chinese Theatre, Kodak and walk of fame. Awesome rooms, huge with walk in wardrobe, big bathroom. Very good first impression. Well located with nice front terrace where are tables and sun umbrellas. One minus, limited parking, staff do what they can do to arrange cars in convenient order, didn’t had any problems, car was parked, but not an easy drive in and out. 
Still worth money. I think everybody will be satisfied as its very central location.
Definitely will come back.

I had been wanting to try this for a while, since it joined the Starwood Group. 
It is a great location, but expensive for a totally 'no-frills' hotel: basic, but adequate rooms (bigger than the neighbouring Sheraton and Towers), no charm or style, no room service, patchy Wi-fi only in the lobby, need t go round the corner for the Coffee Shop (the local Deli).
Despite these negatives, after a busy work week, it started to grow on me - a bit of a facelift and a facility or two, and this has good potential.

Their customer service is awful. I spent a week trying to resolve a cancellation issue and they were almost totally unresponsive. I gave up and paid the bill and found out that they overcharged me. I spent two weeks trying to get them to fix the bill without success. I finally had to get my credit card company involved and the threat of non-payment got them to correct the bill. I have never received any kind of apoolgy for the overbilling.

I went to SF for a tradeshow at the Moscone. It was a short walk to the convention center so that was a plus. I traveled with my wife and got another room for my employee and his wife. the place is really nicer than I thought it would be. The rooms are clean although the bathroom is quite small. The sheets are not the best quality but the beds are comfortable. Don't ask for a room with a view as you might get road noise. We got an inside quiet jr. suite and it was quite nice in deed. For a business trip to the moscone or to just be close to a few great places to eat and lots of shopping, this place is great. We will stay here again. It's very inexpensive for SF.

Just spent the past weekend at the Comfort Inn By The Bay. Found it to be a reasonably priced hotel in a convenient location made even better by the fact that the staff was not on strike like a lot of the downtown hotels. An easy safe walk to the Bay area attractions. Continental breakfast provided is a real plus. I had a top floor room and found the Bridge-Bay view to be fantastic. My only complaint would be the traffic noise which is understandable at the corner of Van Ness and Lombard. Overall I was very pleased and would stay there again.

My daughter and I stayed for one night at The Orchard Hotel on a quick trip to San Francisco. We had a great experience and would highly recommend it. 
Even though the building is older, everything was updated and very clean. The staff were friendly and professional with prompt service, including valet parking. The room was beautiful and very comfortable. After doing a lot of searching on-line, I know that the price was reasonable for the location and type of hotel. This is not a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""generic"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel; rather we felt it was upscale yet cozy.
We liked the location because it was right off the cable car line and only a couple of blocks away from Union Square. If you're a woman traveling alone, this would be a good choice. I would feel comfortable staying there on my own.

This hotel is Great. I stayed here for - nights. Had an excellent time! The check in process was simple. I was even able to view my suite prior to paying for it. I'm one real light sleeper so I had to make sure I'd get my sleep. I sure did. The clerk was real nice and respectful. The next day I ordered breakfast. My order wasn't correct but the kitchen then gave me one complimentary breakfast. That was also very appropriate customer service. On my -nd day I slept in due to my work and flight schedule from the day before. Housekeeping still came back to sort my room out that afternoon. That was greatly appreciated. I used their shuttle service for some work appointments I had. Their driver Mike is excellent. Always respectful. I tipped him accordingly. I took the shuttle to the nearby Rave theatre. Great location as I was able to get some dinner at the Sushi restaurant next door before the movie began. So overall this newer hotel is in an excellent location. It's an upper scale hotel in one very classy area. If you like the nicer, contemporary atmospheres stay here. It's WORTH your Time as well as your money. It's Money well spent!

I booked our stay with Expedia because they had a good deal with a saving of --%. I have requested a room with - king bed per room description and I left a comment requesting a room at the upper level because I read on other reviews that they are bigger than ground leveled rooms. When I got at the h(m)otel I was told that they do not have king beds only queen beds and the ones at the upper level have - queen beds therefore are more expensive and that they did not have any left. I was assigned room -- which is a detached unit by the pool. The room was much smaller, had a dampness smell and it was very noisy (you can hear the neighbours) and first night I could not even go to sleep until - am. In the morning there was some construction going on across the street, so, we had to wake up at - am. Also, in the room description it is said that there is an internet dial-up access which is not true so beware if you want to use your laptop. For the so-called """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""breakfast"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" you'll have just pastries, juice and coffee (small cups). There are no tables to sit to, so you'll have to carry the plate (we had to request for one) to your room. For the price and location the price was good, but I would try to book the hotel through their website and call in advance to make sure I can get a different room. The pool was out of order for the entire stay.

Stayed for three nights. Right in the heart of the Financial and Shopping areas, very short walk to Union Sq and Chinatown. Able to park right outside for free from Saturday afternoon until Monday morning. Don't forget free wine each evening.

Just got home from a visit at the Inn at Union Square. We were unsure of what to expect but it was one of our best hotel experiences ever! The Inn's staff is extremely helpful and friendly and will go out of their way to make sure you are happy. The wine and cheese was a nice addition and breakfast was simple but really good. The room was very, very comfortable and the bed was a dream to sleep on! We will definitely visit again!
-Brittany and Alton

Pros: Convenient location (--- blocks from Pike Place Market), very friendly staff, big room, reasonably priced guest parking, free internet.
Cons: Noisy within the hotel (doors are wafer-thin so make sure you don't get a room outside-near the lifts), minimal decoration, springy mattress.
If you are looking for a very basic, clean room in a fairly central location, this is a good choice. We were doing quite a bit of traveling to multiple destinations and didn't want to break the bank, so this was fine for the purposes we had in mind.

We had booked - nights at the Windsor Suites. But after a day of sightseeing all we wanted to do was check in and pass out. Unfortunately, we were told that they didn't have a room for us. There was a water pipe leak that had ruined a number of rooms. We were less than pleased, but thankfully they set us up with a room at the neighboring Sheraton. We were set up with a fine room there and when we returned to the Windsor Suites we were greeted with an upgraded room and a free breakfast. It wasn't the most ideal situation of switching hotels, but we were treated well.

The hotel is easily accessible off the highway and parking is free. They do have an outdoor pool which is good for families with children. Our rate included the buffet breakfast and we found it to be substantial and good. There is also a full service bar that is open during the evenings.This hotel is NOT on the riverwalk and across the highway from Market Square(restaurants, shops, and street vendors). The rooms were basic but updated. They had flat screen tvs, a sleep number bed, and free wifi. I would recommend this hotel to families for a short stop over in San Antonio.

Got our room the morning of our stay for $-- on Priceline (best online rate I could find was $---). The room was pleasantly comfortable and looked like it had been renovated in the previous year or so -- great beds, nice shower, good ---inch LCD with about -- channels. We had nice weather so the kids checked out the pool -- small, only ----- feet deep. Parking at the Hyatt was $-- plus tax, which is about standard for that block.
For those of you who've never stayed in Fisherman's Wharf, there are about six chain hotels right next to one another along North Point and Bay Streets. If traveling alone or just with my wife, I might have instead stayed at one of the two nearby Kimpton hotels (Argonaut, Tuscan Inn), but the Hyatt was terrific for a family stay.

I had a great experience at Hotel Monaco. The staff was very nice and accommodating, there was always someone in the front to welcome us or wish us a good day. The room was a bit small, but I was able to adjust, I guess I didn't need much space since we were exploring San Francisco. I really enjoyed their free wine and chair massage at -pm everyday. It is a special way to say thank you. I would definitely stay there again.

Spent - nights at this hotel with my husband. Room was average hotel room size. It was clean and bright. View of city was good. For the cost of the room internet access should be included. Location is good but need taxi to get to most points of interest.

Amazing views from hotel, very modern, stuff very helpful, near all attractions, millenium park, michigan Ave., the Navy Pier all within walking distance..
Will definetly go back again. The view from our room was stunning, could see the lake and the Chicago River.

Not sure if this was just a cursed visit (all was fine the other time I stayed there) but the place seems very poorly managed. Asked for early check in but didn't even get my room by -. They offered to downgrade me to a lesser room (saving the money but that made no sense fo rthem or for me. The room service menu was from - years ago and they took an hour to get the current one. THEY CHARGE FOR WIFI! despite the room charge of $--- per night. And they knocked - times between - AM and -- to see if we were gone yet. Constant wait at the front desk, just like Starbucks. Disappointing.

Too many issues to list but stayed at many different Ritz in other states and would NEVER ever recommend this one to anyone. The caliber of service from front desk, housekeeping and staff were on par with the motel -.

We booked this hotel based on its location as we wanted to be in the centre of all the action and it didn't disappoint. The service was just what you'd expect in a good hotel and everywhere was spotless and clean. We would definitely recommend staying here to anyone coming to the big apple.
good location. good service.walk to pike place market and art museum. walk distance to shop

This is the last time I will use Priceline. For $--- a night, I dont think its too much to expect a clean place. This is a dirty run down hotel with EXTREMELY cramped rooms and very worn everything. But worse is the location, in the middle of a block of buildings all at various stages of construction, and with trains, trucks etc. running all night and a very noisy mechanics place right opposite the entrance. There are no restaurants or shops nearby and one has to walk a couple of blocks even to find a taxi, which do not cruise past the hotel. Under no circumstances would I recommend staying here.

Our stay started out great but had problems after we left! Nice comfortable rooms and good value. However, the pool area was not clean over the two days we stayed there. We complained to the manager a day after we left and he was nice and gave us ---- extra Marriott points. Now for the interesting part. Two days after we stayed we noticed red spots all over my body, my son's body and my wife's body, but not on my infant daughter. Our pediatrician said they were spider bites! Could they have happened when we got home? Possibly, but not likelly. I can't prove it but I am sure we got them at the hotel. Overall a nice hotel, but with an experience like that, I wouldn't stay there again.

Hotel is a basic limited-frills place where one can stay closeby to most attractions for an affordable price and then spend money elsewhere. Staff are friendly and courteous and helpful in solving problems. There has been recent renovation to some of the rooms, with small refrigerator, coffee machine, safe in room. Wireless access in rooms is convenient. Can be a bit noisy due to location and hall noise by guests, but with earplugs is manageable. I am a repeat customer and plan to stay again.

My boyfriend and I arrived at the Holiday Inn Express in Detroit late Friday night (July --rd), and woke up the next morning to find bedbugs crawling on the sheets and the pillows. I was horrified and disgusted! Contacted the front desk and they came up with a cup and collected - of the bedbugs. My boyfriend was bitten as well, but his bites were not a severe. This has been the worst hotel experience I have ever had! Will not be staying there again, not even with the certificate for a free nights stay.

Always enjoy staying at Kimpton Hotels and Harbor Court was great. Very good location in San Francisco. Hotel staff was very friendly and helpful. Very clean and comfortable. The wine tasting-social is fun and you meet very interesting people and hotel staff.

Our son had a blast at the pool and met new friends while we enjoyed refreshments from the hotel's bar. We also got to enjoy the room of the newly renovated wing of the hotel. It still had the new smell. The room service was great!! ...This is a ---% smoke free hotel though. :(

Have just come back from - nights at the Affinia Dumont.
My first impression was that it was not as upmarket as I had hoped, and I too was a little disappointed, but they had our reservation and had met our request for a quiet room.
We had a one bedroom suite - and it was large - by any standard, and we paid $--- per night ( booked via the Affinia Website in January ).
However over the five nights I got to like it more and more. I was staying with my husband and two boys, who fought on the first night about sharing the double sofa bed in the sitting room. I mentioned it to reception, and they arranged for an extra rollaway bed to be brought to the room for the following four nights ( and didnt charge for this!! ). We requested extra pillows - and they were there within -- minutes ( and a call half an hour later to see if we had them and if we needed anything else ).
The room was very quiet, and I like the fact that there were only - rooms on a floor - so you dont get a lot of noise of people in the hallways. 
There was lots of hot water and the showers were good and everything was very clean.
The weather was awful when we were there, and they provide umbrellas, and go and stand in the rain to get you a taxi, whilst you wait in the warmth of the lobby. The Barking Dog next door did good breakfast and evening meals when the weather was so foul that we couldnt venture further.
It was clean, well located, quiet, comfortable, in a 'safe' neighbourhood and a good price. I would definately stay there again, and would recommend it to others.

I have stayed in several hotels throughout NYC and tend to always end up near Times Square, especially with most SPG brands, which I am not a fan of dealing with, especially during this time of the year. This W is a prime location in Midtown, convenient to everything but off the main drag to not always be insane to deal with.

I will be honest the rooms are not large, but it definitely worked for my needs. They have acknowledged the issues of how small some of their rooms are and have comped internet, which is worth it to me because very few hotels do. 
Overall great experience, it's my go to hotel in NYC.

Central location, great breakfast downstairs, but we felt as though we were sharing our room with a few strangers. - I upgraded my room and at - or - am heard a lot of noise on the --th floor.

Terrible hotel, I've stayed over --- hotels in different countries and the US, this has been the worse. But why the worse? basically because you pay as a luxury hotel and expect the best. Hotwire ranks this place as a -.- star hotel. I certainly will give it a - like Ramada or Holiday Inn. My upfront suggestion to a couple, young people and everybody that has a sense of reality, do not spend time or money in the Nine Zero Hotel in Boston. Give your money to charity and you will feel much better. That's what I did after I came home.

This hotel was great! I went with my boyfriend and we stayed one night. The room was really nice, very elegant and clean. They have valet service so you don't have to deal with parking downtown. And the location is unbeatable. I would stay here again in a heartbeat. It was a treat to crawl into their bed at night!

Spent a night here with my teenage daughter. I grew up in the area and it felt like coming home. If you want slick, this isn't for you. If you want easy comfort, a helpful staff, and great location, you can't beat the Melrose. Lots of great eateries within walking distance, from pubs to haute chic. A deli a few steps down Pennsylvania Avenue is a good bet for breakfast and snacks. I read so-so reviews on Expedia and found the Melrose undeserving. I highly recommend this DC classic.

The following are paraphrased excerpts taken from an email I sent to the hotel after experiencing a terrible stay:
· the hotel was not able to provide adequate hot water for bathing during the morning. 
· the bathtub spigot was not even attached to the wall. 
· the shower diverter valve channeled only some of the water to the shower head. 
· the bathtub did not drain properly resulting in showers taken in standing water. 
· soundproofing between adjoining bathrooms was poor. People in adjoining bathroom were audible in both actions and words. 
· bureau drawer space was totally inadequate because of the installation of a mini-bar in a guest clothing storage space. 
· Riverside Cafe staff inadequate to handle breakfast surge. Waiters and bus-boys harried, inattentive, and unavailable. 
· elevators usually had one form of trash or another on the floor. 
· Java Bar Starbucks coffee station was second rate, an inadequate afterthought.
 · unable-unwilling to switch my booking credit card for one which I would have preferre to use at check-in: 
· charging for toll-free calls just smacks of money-grubbing, as do the exorbitant local call charges. 
· ditto for the shameful wi-fi charges. 
· blatant, in-your-face, peddling of $-.-- bottled water used up most of the space on the tiny guest table.
On the positive side we did find your staff, for the most part, pleasant : we were well served by your housekeeping staff. We did enjoy the very comfortable bedding and the champagne acknowledging our anniversary. However, these minimal positive items are normally expected from a four star hotel and they did not serve to offset the negative issues. What a disappointment!!
Got a great deal on Hotels.com. It was as good as the Sofitel in NYC which cost me - times more!

I travel from out of state to work in this part of town once a month and have tried most of the budget hotels in this area. This is my favorite and if I get a good deal I stay here (price between the hotels fluctuate -- Travel Lodge Presidio, Greenwich Inn are also fine options). Rooms clean, staff helpful and it's in good location. Only drawback is that Lombard can be loud so try and get a room beyond the main court yard as traffic and loud passers by can be loud.

Staff not friendly. 
Long wait for check-in. 
Would rather be at the Garland Hotel 
Where they are much more considerate 
And friendly. 
Very long wait till check-in. 
Arrived a little early, about --:--am 
After driving all night. Customer service is poor.

The front desk staff was very helpful. They approached us to guide us through the automated check in. Our room was nice, plenty big for - people and our baggage. The linens were great. The room had a nice size closet. The bathrom had no tub but the shower was large, clean with nice tile and fixtures.

There was no room upgrade. The hotel is run down with paint coming off the wall. They are trying to fix up the property, during our stay the flooring was removed and relpaced. It is an old hotel in a cool,part of the city. As a platinum member I will not return.

My husband and I stayed the July long weekend for - nights. We chose to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""go green"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and forego housekeeping since we were there for only - nights. That meant we got - five dollar gift cards for Starbucks!! The hotel is in a fantastic location....just a block to union square with a great variety of restaurants and shops to visit nearby. It's just three blocks from the BART train, so we took the train from the airport and walked to the hotel and did the same for our return home. Took a lovely guided walking tour of Victorian Homes which began at Union Square where we met our guide, Jay, who was friendly and very knowledgeable. You can meet Jay at Union Square at --:--am every day and look for him holding the yellow sign. (victorianwalk.com). Get your tickets at least a week or two in advance if you want to see Alcatraz. We missed out because it was already sold out when we booked our trip a week before.
The only negative for the hotel is the street noise, but with the a-c on low, it helps to drown out the noise a bit.

We booked online and paid a very reasonable rate. On checking in we had made a mistake and the room that we had booked had only one bed. Given that we were two independent travelers this was certainly not what we wanted. Roberto on the front desk found us an alternative and couldn't have been more helpful. He also gave us complimentary breakfast vouchers to welcome us. Our room was immaculately clean and very smart indeed. It was in the old main building and the quiet was amazing to me - being more used to thin hotel room walls. Breakfast included a great range of fresh fruit. Thanks to the great service I would come back again for sure.

impersonal and over priced, not a - star hotel, more like a - star. $--.-- for internet access, no robes, no water glasses, no flat screen TV. Bedding? you'll find better at a - star hotel. The rooftop pool is pretty cool though, that lessened the pain of my one night there. Moved to another hotel for the rest of our NYC visit.

Stayed here for one night before an early flight. This hotel, although a Courtyard, actually had the feel of a full service Marriott. Restaurant and full bar serving decent food and individual TV screens in each booth. Several computers with printers in the lobby for boarding passes. Airport shuttle for your use. Free parking if you have a car, which I did. The surrounding neighborhood is fairly bleak, the closest gas a couple moles up the road and not much else around. But the rooms were large, very clean and the staff 
were very pleasant. The airport is 
about a - minute drive away. Overall I was impressed with the amenities here and the decent room rate. I wouldn't want to stay here as a base for a Boston trip but it's an excellent choice for the late arrivers or early departers to Logan.

As many have noted, this place still hasn't worked everything out. The restaurants? I stayed away from Sauciety based on other's reviews. Other than that there's not much close by, but it's not impossible. The walk to a restaurant was about the same as I usually take in other towns. The only difference is that in other towns I am usually passing other restaurants along the way. Other problems? They have no price list on the phone usage or the snacks in the refrigerator. When we called to ask the prices on the snacks, we were told that the value of the entire contents was $---. That didn't help us much in figuring out the price of a diet soda. After I checked out and verified my bill, I received a second charge for $--.-- on my credit card. I called back to ask about it, and I was told that it was for food taken from the refrigerator. I assured them we didn't take it, and they refunded my card. The Starbucks didn't seem prepared for large groups, because they ran out of food every morning. As a note, more restaurants are opening in the hotel next year. There were also some problems with the locks on the doors. I got locked out of my room twice. The second time I was getting a new entry card, they gave me - cards just in case there were more problems. So for the rest of the week, I had to carry - cards around and of course the card never stopped working after that. Other than that, I really liked the open airiness of the lobby and the proximity to the train.

Overall, was pleased with our choice of staying - nights at Riverwalk Vista. We had a room with a Riverwalk View, which was nice. I'm a pretty light sleeper, and it is noisy outside in the evening....it did definitely quiet down, but be aware that it's not just traffic, it's live music across the street and down the block...even with the AC and the sound machine running, it was still an issue. Maybe we would have been better off with a room on the other side of the property?? The staff was excellent and very helpful, the breakfasts were nice, and the cookies and lemonade were a welcome touch at the end of a long day. The RV offers something that most other places along or adjacent to the river don't....a bed and breakfast type feel in an impressive historic building.

Great hotel; my first time staying there. Great location, easy access from the highway and easy to get to the lightrail.
Staff was very friendly and helpful.
Room was clean and well attended. 
Lots of great pillows!

First time staying in NYC, so I expected prices to be high and rooms to be average for my price range.
With tax, I paid $--- for a corner room in this hotel...which is supposed to be a larger room. Room was very small. You could barely walk in the room..the two double beds, desk and tv-dresser were crammed together. Bathroom was tiny, and shockingly awful. There was a huge crack-hole in the tub which we didn't notice until late that night. We were only staying one night, so we sucked it up.
Upon showering in the morning, the tub became clogged and I pulled a huge wad of hair out of the drain. It was disgusting. 
Sheets were itchy. Bed was so-so in terms of comfort.
The only decent part about our room was the view of Times Square.
The hotel itself wasn't overly impressive. I did not get a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""wow"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" feeling when I walked in there. Pretty standard. Nothing fancy. 
In general the staff was very polite and friendly, however, when I mentioned that I was disappointed about the room and was shocked about the tub (upon checkout) they told me I should have called and asked for a different room.
That wasn't the point. I just felt the room and hotel was very overpriced!
And another shocker, they charge you $-- to use the gym-pool. I know it's the NYSC, and not the hotel's own gym-pool...but come on. Maybe that's typical for NYC, but it was a surprise for me.
I will do some better research next time I stay in NYC. 
I do not recommend this hotel.

Overall excellent place to stay if you are looking for somewhere nice on the Riverwalk. Friendly environment and great staff and bartender. The bartender Patrick is very talented and friendly, and went out of his way to find out exactly what we wanted. Over all great stay. Will definitely be coming back again soon.

The Westin at Times Square was a great location. It was my -st time to visit NY along with - girlfriends. I thought the room was a generous size (for NY) for - people-suitcases-purchases and stuff! The room was quiet at night and everyone enjoyed a comfortable sleep. We didn't eat at the hotel, but others said it was good (there were too many other places to eat at!). We didn't see much of the staff, but would definitely stay there again.

Room that I stayed in was basic at best. Lamps in the room worked part of the time. Outlets in the room were installed very poorly. Very pricey for a small room, basic cable and a bed to sleep in. Parking prices and WI-Fi fees are out of this world. Restaurant was very appetizing, but very expensive also.

Stayed at this hotel room for - nights and had a pleasant stay. This hotel has a superb location with loads of sight seeing and shopping trips within a short walk.
Slightly disappointed with the standard of the rooms but they were clean and the maid service was good. 
Staff were very helpful and friendly especially Rafael the bell boy and Juan Carlos who served me every morning at breakfast.

Great location, nice rooms (seemed larger than the other Manhattan hotel I stayed at and much quieter). Very friendly, helpful staff. The only thing that marred my stay here was an incident with a very rude woman from room service. However the hotel has addressed the issued and apologised. As I underand it, room service is operated by the Madison and Vine restaurant and not by the hotel. Skip the room service and find somewhere else to eat. Other than that I 
would highly recommend this hotel for anyone looking for a nice hotel close to all the main attractions.

This quaint inn with such helpful and friendly staff was our """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""home"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" when we visited Philadelphia recently. The staff made us feel as if we were guests to a family home and they were our hosts. The rooms were not that big but very clean and comfortable, and very nicely decorated. The breakfast was wonderful, with so many choices available, and there was even a bowl of fruit available all day long. There was internet access (although we didn't get to use it because we were out seeing all the great sites of Philadelphia all day long). When we arrived, we wondered where we would park our car. When we asked the front desk they very efficiently gave us a map to the special parking garage a short walk away. We didn't need our car till we were going to leave since the inn is located very conveniently and we could just walk to the dining places and even to the sites. I had a great time in this lovely place. Thank you to all the warm and wonderful people who run this inn.

We picked the hotel for the location. When we arrived in the afternoon I dropped my wife off with our luggage and I went to return our rental car. The front desk clerk (a man) refused to check her in because the reservation was in my name (even though we share the same last name as well as sharing the same credit card used to book the hotel.) Also, the bell hop helped with the luggage, and he was aware that I was leaving to return the car whilst my wife checked in.) The front desk clerk (a man) flatly refused to check her in, explaining that he worked in the hotel industry for -- years and he suspected my wife of using deceit to gain entrance to my hotel room (really). My wife called me and asked me to give my consent to have her check into the hotel (really). Oh, the clerk also asked me to physically describe my wife. We travel a lot and this was the worst hotel check in experience we've ever had. The front desk clerk is not qualified to work with the public.

a place that feels like home, but has the service of any - star hotel! Makes every effort to make this the best stay ever! The only thing lacking is space, but u can't fault the staff for that. One employee was exceptionally helpful, PATRICK I believe was his name. you would think he worked around the clock, because when ever i called, morning, noon or late at night, he was always there to bring what ever i need. Thank you for being such a devoted employee!
Thier breakfast is good. The room is clean and stuff is nice.

Whenever my husband and I visit El Paso (which is often), we always stay at this La Quinta. Comfortable beds, clean rooms, excellent price, and the location is great! It's very easy to get to and close to all the places we need to go. We have tried several other hotels in the area, but for all of the above reasons, we have settled on this one.

This hotel was super nice for the price. I got - days for $---- total including all taxes. I stayed in --- and my room was spacious for NY, very clean, updated with large flat screen, quiet, VERY comfortable bed and sheets (all down feather) superb location if you are seeing shows. Have breakfast at the deli about -- paces west on the street across the street....good food and can't beat the price.

Native New Yorkers, we visit a couple of times a year.If you are a theatre goer you can't get a much better location than THE LONDON..walkably close yet far enough away to be out of the fabulous mania that is Times Square. We've stayed there several times and enjoy the look, the space, the bar-tearoom-breakfastroom and the location. This time, however, the place is looking a bit tired and ready for renewal; worn carpets, upholstery were noticeable. The suite seemed very dark as if there was a downgrade in lightbulb strength. Also there were no magazines or NYC pr materials for the uninitiated NYC traveler.
We do like this hotel very much and its proximity to the things we like to do in the Apple but for the first time, while waiting to be picked up for our return flight home, noticed that there was not one place to sit in the lobby.
If there is a redo in the London's future I would like to suggest double paned windows to block out the inevitable truck and siren clatter that woke us every night. One expects noise in the city that never sleeps, but I, for one, would like to. One last thing, the price was astronomical this time, way higher than our last visit. We just might be priced out and didn't feel all the god things about the place balanced out the cost.

My husband and I stayed here while he was participating in a conference. When you walk in, you are struck by a lovely scent in the air signaling you are now in just as lovely of a hotel. Every member of the staff has a service-oriented attitude. The rooms are beautifully decorated and maintained, but in our room the mattress could use replacing. Also, the shower water pressure was skimpy. 
Jose the concierge was fantastic at recommending and arranging a tour to Muir Woods. Anyone, including the bellman and security, was willing to help make our stay easy by recommending restaurants, routes, etc. By the way, don't miss the restaurant - we had both an excellent steak dinner and a creative, hearty breakfast there.
Although the Omni is in the financial district (FiDi) you are centrally located to walk to Chinatown, Union Square, and the Ferry Terminal Marketplace.

I have stayed at the Marriott North on two different occasions. It is a nice, well-kept, typical Marriott. The rooms are average hotel rooms, nothing special, but comfortable. One thing that did stand out was the attentiveness of the staff. They are very friendly and constantly checking on you to make sure everything is okay. If anything is wrong, they will remedy it immediately. Service like that is lacking too many places these days.

Stayed here when i took my - eldest sons (--, -- and --) to new york. It was a last minuet choice after the other we booked cancelled on us. The hotel was okay, the staff were fairly friendly and helped when i asked for directions. The rooms were not fantastic, they are a bit outdated and were not that clean. That said, the room was comfy, the bed sheets were clean and the TV in the room was really useful for when we were waiting to do the next thing.
 It was also quite noisy from the road during the night as we had the window open but after a day shopping-sightseeing we would have slept through anything We also had problems with the toilet, which wouldn't flush, and the sink became blocked. The staff were very helpful and sent someone up within about -- mins to fix it on more than one occasion so that was okay.
Breakfast was good for us. None of my family are huge eaters in the morning which was good because while the food was nice it was a bit basic. There was toast and bagels, fruit, yogurt, doughnuts and cold boiled eggs. The only thing that got me was that we were eating off paper plates and using plastic cups and cutlery.
This all said, all the room was really used for was a base. When sightseeing-shopping in New York you barely use the hotel, it was literally just to sleep. For what we paid it was more than satisfactory and was also in a fantastic location. When you have been shopping for -- hours a day you don't really notice a bit of dirt on the celling, or some traffic noise from outside.

This was my third and last time I will ever stay at the Heartbreak Hotel (HH). Unfortunately my """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""instinct"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" told me not to stay there but because I was going with a friend who had never been to Memphis I thought the HH would be a fun experience. We arrived early and the staff would not allow us to check in prior to the - PM check in time. The clerk literally made us stand in line (We had tried to check in at -:--) until -:--. When we finally were able to get to our room it smelled like stale smoke, it was dirty and run down. Paint was peeling off bathroom door, an empty used cup was under the vanity and the floors were filthy. The HH is overpriced (I stay at Marriott Hotels all the time for less), under maintained and the staff could use some professional development training to say the least. The location is convenient for the Graceland tour and exhibits, but after you have done all that there is nothing in the immediate area. You can take an hourly shuttle to Beale Street and the downtown area, but again you are limited on things to do there as well. For the amount of money the owners are making there is NO excuse for the condition of the HH.

I booked this hotel on the strength of previous positive postings and I was not disappointed. You felt like an important guest from the moment of your arrival. The doormen (Special mention to Randy and William) who were very helpful.
Check-in was quick and painless and you didn't have to wait an age for the lift to arrive!
Usually rooms in NYC are relatively small (ie not much room to swing a cat) but its fair to say that my jaw dropped when I entered our room. It was huge!! And the bathroom was a decent size with both a shower cubicle and a bath (being - foot one I fitted in it perfectly!) The curtains were heavy and thick so it was easy to fall asleep at night. A fresh bottle of evian with a note on the following days weather forecast was also left every night.
I would disagree with previous comments about not going up the Empire State if you've never done it before. All I would say is go first thing in the morning or late at night to avoid the queues - the view is incredible. Other suggestions would be:-
Take the free Staten Island Ferry - the views of the Statue of Liberty and Manhattan are amazing on a clear day. The crossing takes roughly half an hour. Take the subway to Bowling Green then its just across the road.
Head to Strawberry Fields in Central Park - there's usually a good crowd with musicians so you can have a sing song.
I would also recommend the Monkey Bar which is on East --th Street between Madison and Park Avenue. For all you Sex and the City fans - this is where Carrie and Big decide to be friends after their affair. It's very chic and moody and the Cosmopolitans are to die for!

Location, decore and most important the staff were amazing. The bed however was painful. We had adjoining rooms and the kids beds on the double room were great. Ours sagged so bad I used a pillow to keep from falling out of the bed. Next day when I asked them to please do something I saw that under the mattress they were using a sheet of plywood so I guess I wasn't the first to experience this pain. The other disgusting part was the filth under the mattress pad, not sure when that was last changed or cleaned but not acceptable. The manager was very accomidating when I showed her the pictures. They did move a mattress from another room that was unfortunately in a similar condition. I do like everything at this hotel but a Holiday Inn would provide a better sleep. Too bad.

This hotel has a very modern, young vibe. Our room was large with a living room, bedroom and bathroom with a walk-in shower. The bathroom was all tile, - shower heads and - benches. We had - balconies with a great view of the city.
The night-club upstairs was hip and seemed to be the in-place to be.
Everything was within walking distance for us (we love to walk). Michigan Ave - blocks away. Lots of shopping, restaurants, all within a few minutes.

Dylan Hotel, Midtown, NYC
Date: February --, ----
Reviewer: Codymae
The Dylan is a European style hotel with a great central location. On average I stay in hotels ----- times per year. I found the Dylan to be very comfortable... Great value. Friendly staff. As a single woman, I felt very safe and comfortable. Great amenities... including bathrobe & slippers. Would definitely go back.

Older Embassy. They have updated here and there. Fairly clean. Housekeeping does a great job. Front desk staff seems bored and annoyed they are there. Free breakfast...quite the buffet. Light Rail public transportation close by...able to walk there and then ride to down town or anywhere really. Grocery store across the street and several restaurants which is nice change compared to the hotel offerings.

We stayed her because it was suggested by the wedding party. While the location was fine (we had a view of the river), the hotel was only """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""ok"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". This is a BIG hotel and the lobby was kept at around -- degrees (or so it felt) and it just wasn't that hot in Chicago. The rooms were nicely appointed but the bathroom was so poorly designed that it was impossible to get close to the mirror because the counter top was SO deep. We had to ask twice for additional blankets and towels (they provided only - for - people) and, when the room was cleaned the next day, they did not replace the extra towels so we had to ask again. I didn't find the staff to be overly friendly but the bartender was good and knowledgeable. With so many great hotels in Chicago, I wouldn't stay here again, especially with a $-- parking fee!!

Just returned from an over night at the Hyatt. I have been staying here for several years and have always been pleased with nlocation and the room itselfl. I do understand though why poeple that are paying full price complain. They used to deliver your paper to the door but now have stopped that. They also used to have complementary coffee for the early riser in the lobby but that was also discontinued.
The staff is responsive to your requests but most of mine have not been carried out. One time I needed a roll away bed and that took four phone calls. This trip I needed a tooth brush sent up and that never arrived. I arrived early and understood that a room was not ready at that time, but after walking around for an hour and a half and waiting for them to call I checked with them and they said they would """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""rush"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" a room for me. I waited another hour or so and no phone call, so I went back to the hotel and checked with the desk. A room was ready now. I put my stuff in and then left. About half an hour after this, the desk called and said my room was now ready.
On another stay, I requested a room with two beds and was given a king. Upon complaining, I was told I """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""requested"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" two beds, but """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""reserved"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" a king. 
Also some of the concierge staff is wonderful and knowledgeable. (all were polite) Some however have very little knowledge of Boston.

We stayed at the Salisbury from the -th to the --th Sept. --. On arrival the female receptionist was on the phone ,she continued talking on the phone as she booked us in, that's multi-tasking for you. So not a great first impression. We stayed on the -th floor the corridor of which had a constant smell of burnt toast,not great either. We had a room at the front, not much of a view and quite alot of traffic noise. The room was large with plenty of storage space. The main problem was the air con unit which was fitted in one of the windows, it was old and very noisey when turned up.
The location,however, could not be better with various subway and bus stops within a short walk and all the main attractions within strolling distance.
We had breakfast one morning which was a bit basic but only $- so what do you expect.
Staff were all OK and no problem leaving luggage after checkout before the flight home.
The stay cost less than £-- per night which for the location was very good.
Cheap and cheerful would be the best description of the Salisbury

Due to a mix up at check in, we were kept waiting in the lobby for about forty-five minutes. The front desk attendant was not concerned or helpful. When we finally opened the door to our room, a maintenance man was sitting in the room watching football. The carpet in the room was old, dirty and stained...or burned. The room was hot. The power strip at the desk was not working so the cell phone and iPad that had been plugged in the previous evening were not charged in the morning. The shower was dark and the water pressure was poor. Since it is an old hotel, the soundproofing is poor; you can clearly hear when your neighbor showers or flushes the toilet.
On the plus side, the location is great and the hotel has free internet. We paid $---.-- for Saturday evening. Parking was an additional $--.--.
If I got a great rate, I might return to the Radisson...but I really would not look forward to it.

We stayed for a long weekend in September ----.
As we went along the corridor to our room, we passed several drunk men in their --'s carrying bottles into their room and shouting... this was a good indication of how things were going to be...
The room we stayed in was a dump! The bedsheets had cigarette burns in them and were fraying around the edges. We complained that the room smelt damp- of cigarettes- was dirty- but were told that it was all that was available... so that was that!
We spent our Friday night listening to the blokes in the corridor shouting and going between rooms.
Saturday evening was great until we arrived back at the hotel...
BEWARE!!! The ---- Lounge downstairs can be rented out at weekends for private functions.
On this night, there was some sort of wedding reception which involved banging music until -am!!!
(If you have ever seen the scene in Jurassic Park where the glass of water ripples with the vibrations - that was our night)
We complained at -am and were told that we couldn't move rooms (ours was directly above the mayhem)
We complained again at -am, and were told that there was nothing the hotel staff could do. (Seems odd when you consider that they own the building!)
One couple actually checked-out at -am because they couldn't stand the noise anymore - and the hotel staff DIDN'T EVEN APOLOGISE!
We were promised that the Manager would speak to us before we checked-out the following Monday, but surprise, surprise... he was always """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""unavailable!""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""
The Sunday night was almost as bad with a pair of gay men in the next room screaming abuse at each other because one of them had slept with someone else. (Yes, the walls were really THAT thin... I lay in bed listening to this soap opera unfolding!)
This has the potential to be a fantastic hotel, but its staff are awful and let guests do whatever they want, the rooms stink and are dirty, it needs refurbishing and then it could be a great place to stay.
We chose the Skyline because of it's location... DON'T MAKE THE SAME MISTAKE!!!!!

As with most TA reviewers concur, the extremely affordable Doubletree Guest Suites in Times Square was a pleasant and welcome stay for part of our honeymoon. WE booked far enough in advance to get below $ --- and received a room on a high floor that was clean and about average size for a midtown Manhattan hotel. Separate sleeping quarters with a very comfortable bed (that was welcome from all the walking) makes the Doubletree a BEST DEAL considering more upscale hotels in the area charging twice our rate.

Enjoyed about a week at the Essex House. The new renovation is lovely with lots of interesting little touches including motion activitated night lights. Very comfortable rooms and a friendly staff. Great central location - perfect for business and for pleasure.

Pros: friendly, helpful hotel staff; clean rooms & very comfortable beds; good on-site breakfast; excellent appetizers & comfortable lounge.
Cons: just one, but a major pain - hotel advertises 'high speed internet access', and while I was able to access once, (only after consulting with the service provider), it became too frustrating with each subsequent attempt. My laptop is 'ready-to-go', and I have always been able to connect at other hotels with zero problems. This hotel needs to upgrade - and they should add wireless capabilities as well.

Our first night, the people above us made so much noise that sleep was impossible. I think the rooms are poorly insulated or something. It sounded like people were right outside our glass window. Numerous compaints to the front desk didnt do any good. The next day we were moved to another room. The people next to us were so loud we couldnt sleep for hours. Its not that they were so loud, the walls were just so thin or poorly sound proofed it seemed that way. As a business traveller I've been in a lot of hotel rooms, its not often I've had such a rotten stay.

In the end of Sex and The City Movie, the camera pans out to reveal the - stars of the show walking down the street in front of this hotel. The location of this scene aptly describes this hotel: stylish, attractive, and sexy.

My wife and I stayed here for a night on our way to the Outer Banks. We're big fans of Mandarin Oriental hotels, so we welcomed the opportunity to visit another one. Here are my impressions.
Location: A bit out of the way, and certainly not in a lively area, but there are some nice views, and having a CVS and Starbucks nearby makes it feel less isolated. 
Hotel: Nice enough, with quality fixtures, nice bar, and overall it exudes quality, though perhaps not as much as the MO hotels in Miami or NYC.
Service: I thought that the service was great, with everyone we spoke to being kind and polite. As with all MOs, they were very accommodating with our dogs.
Rooms: Nothing special, really. There's nothing wrong with them, but they just seemed bland. The bathroom was very nice, especially the shower. We were on the fourth floor, and could definitely hear the train every now and then.
In-room dining: Again, nothing special. We got there very late, so our only option was to order dinner from room service. My wife's pasta was nice, but my burger was dry, and the fries were soggy.
Overall: A very nice hotel, and considering that it is modestly priced for an MO property, I would likely stay here again. However, it is not quite as astounding as their hotels in Miami, New York, Boston, or even Munich.

The Westin is really a beautiful building in downtown Columbus, and it was quite convenient in terms of location. Overall, I would recommend the hotel if you're in town for a quick trip like I was, but definitely can't imagine staying in this hotel for any longer than a night or two because of how cramped the room was.

All in all, my wife and I loved this place. It was convenient to all the things we wanted to do, we got a great rate on Priceline, the concierge was very helpful and the front desk check-in staff put us on the --st (out of --) floor, so we had great views.

This hotel was very disappointing!! No free breakfast and a very expensive breakfast buffet. Pools were dirty, hot tub was way too hot, inside pool had very slippery surfaces all around. Small drawback were the slowness of the elevators, but there are fright elevators on either end of the hallways that are convenient and much faster.
There is a small Italian Restaurant, Patzeria, just a few doors down from the hotel that serves breakfast (much less expensive than the hotel) and great dinners. Recommend this highly.
We would definately stay at The Belvedere again!

If you're the type of person who enjoys the HI Express brand, then you'll be pleased with this hotel once you're inside. It is clean, and has amenities you want (wireless internet, complimentary breakfast.) The staff is knowledgeable about local restaurants, tourist sites, and how to get around in DC. On the negative side, this hotel is located in an area that is not the greatest. We didn't feel unsafe, but it's also not an area I would take chances in either. Other than that, this HI Express is consistent with the other hotels of this brand we have come to depend on.

It was the -st time for me and the family to stay in this hotel we usually go for other hotels, we stayed for - nights at the Seattle Pan Pacific and we were so impressed and pleased with the services provided to us since day one, and comparing to other - starts hotels in my openion i say this is the best service a guest can get not only from reception staff and room service but also from the restaurant and the bar at the ground floor as well.
Thank you Pan Pacific for the excellent service you had provided us during our stay and we sure love to repeat it again and spend our next vacation in one of Pan Pacific Hotels.

This was a nice hotel in a great location right near Union Square. We were able to walk to almost everything or catch the local transportation which was also nearby. The room was pretty big, the bed was comfy, and there were lots of windows! 
The only complaint is that we ordered a movie one night (it was expensive) and the picture quality was horrible and they weren't able to fix it. That was the only issue we had though.

I visited NYC with my fiancee in Nov -- and it was the first time either of us had been to the states - everything about the trip was amazing!
The hotel is located on the same street as the Empire State building and Macy's (takes about -- minutes to walk there) and is fairly central to the main attractions of time squre - Rockafella - but takes about -- minutes to walk there. There is a subway about - minutes walk that is very handy.
The hotel is excellent - huge room - massive bed - very friendly. Not a bad word to say about it. Try and get a high floor (room -- was excellent) You are right opposite from the Crystler building and have a fantastic view over the city.
Would definitely recommend it to anyone and NYC itslef is amazing - just make sure you go for long enough to get in all you want to see and do as - days was only just long enough for us and could have stayed much longer.

good stay, very convienent location outside airport, clean and quiet. I'd stay again.
Given a good rate. Breakfast was good, if a bit limited. Bathrooms were on the small side. I really like the window seat.

What a great find! We only stayed one night but if was perfect for our shopping getaway! Easy to find, staff was very helpful, kept our luggage for us before check-in and the next day also after check-out. Very clean which is what we were worried about, not huge rooms but sufficient and spotless! Involves a little bit more walking to places like Time Square and other attractions but still close enough to walk. Very pleased!!

I stay at a DC hotel at least once a month. This was my first stay at Topaz and everything was perfect. It's location is very convienent to K Street and the Golden Triangle areas. It is also located a half-a-block off of a main road, Connecticut Ave., which makes the hotel very quiet and peaceful without being far removed from the action. There are hundreds of great restaurants in close walking distance. Additionally, the restaurant in the hotel makes some really great """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Zodiac"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" cocktails and great bar food. I enjoyed my stay so much, I booked a room the next week for my parent's --th anniversary.

Recently stayed here with our kids during spring break. I thought the hotel was fine, but did not feel it was extraordinary in any way. Great midtown location - front reception staff were really friendly as were all the staff we encountered during our - nt stay. Adequate size rooms were clean & shower was fierce! Didn't eat at hotel but can recommend Astros for b-f and Ben Bensons for a great steak. Not all rooms have a safe but reception has safety deposit boxes. Would recommend hotel and would def go back.

In terms for value for money, I think the Courtyard brand takes some beating. This is one of the best courtyards.
While I really like the new receptions they have been standardizing on in other Courtyards, this one is different, in that it has a more traditional reception area, with a nice fireplace and seats in the reception area, which makes the place feel welcoming, and the reception staff were excellent.
The room was good, comfortable bed, though still with the relatively low quality sheets that you get at Courtyard (not really a criticism - when you're not paying top dollar, you shouldn't expect the high end luxuries). The bathroom was a little small and not well lit, but it wasn't too bad.
This hotel has one of the better hotel bars. Nice welcoming staff and a decent menu.
The gym and swimming pool are excellent. I actually couldn't get into the pool due to some sort of problem with the door card system, but the receptionists couldn't have been more helpful in getting it resolved so I could get my daily swim in.
All told, this is an excellent hotel.

As a Priceline customer I regularly get the Hilton and am always pleased. Airport pickup is prompt and friendly, I always ask for a room near the lobby and receive one with no problem. The rooms while not large are impecably clean, beds very comfortable, linens top notch. Nice easy chair and ottoman are appreciated. They've kicked up the bar menu a notch or two and have a good variety of items at reasonalbe prices and the food is excellent. Spencer's restaurant is as good as you get but can be spendy. (No worse than other fine restaurants.) A real plus is that they are located adjacent to the light rail station. You're just steps away from the train to downtown. Never a problem with airport noise. Hilton really does the job!

We only stayed one night and recieved a fantastic rate via Priceline. Checking in was quick and easy. The staff was very friendly and eager to help. They offered us either a king or - doubles. Our room was very clean and nicely decorated. Fluffy blankets and four feather pillows on each bed. The only thing that I would have liked would have been a refridg- microwave...but no big deal. There was plenty of parking. We did not use their restaurant but their selection looked good. I would definatly recommend this hotel.

I really don't understand how this hotel is ranked so high on TripAdvisor. My wife and I (we're in our late --'s) just stayed here at the end of July for - nights and were somewhat disappointed. Like other reviews mention, there is no elevator and TON of steps. If you're carrying up luggage, good luck! Check-in was fine, no issues.

Stayed there just not too long ago, for my conference. Found the hotel on lastminute.com and managed to booked us a room despite all the established hotels in town are fully booked.

However though, the bed is not clean at all as the few nights we were there, we were bitten by bed bugs. Woke up every morning with bug bite marks all over the body. Didn't dare complained as knowing full well that that is the only room available and there is nothing we can do about it. 
Told the receptionist when we checked and they actually apologized for it and will take note about it. 
All in all, the hotel is still a good and nice hotel to stay in, staff are all very very nice and friendly except the chap that checked us in when we arrived initially. He could do with some smiles though but hats off to Spencer and Filimon for making our stay enjoyable still. 
Oh yeah, the steakhouse across the hotel, VIc's and Anthony's...they serve the best steak in town! Absolutely wonderful and mouth watering steaks!!! 
We had a brilliant night at the Vic's then went across the ball park to watch a game between the Astros and Nationals. Absolutely brilliant!!
Makes our stay in Houston absolutely memorable despite being bitten by bugs.

I was a bit concerned about the hotel secondary to the reviews, but I'm glad we booked here as the hotel was just fine. Every other Hilton property in the core area was booked because of the Yankees-Red Sox game. 
We arrived after the red-eye to a full hotel. I was expecting to leave the bags and go do some walking around the city before checking in. Luckily, they were able to accomodate us with a room right away. Love the front desk for expediting it and letting us know that no one had booked that specific room for the previous night. Able to get some shut eye before the day at hand. The front desk was so friendly and helpful. 
During the day, the housekeeping staff was amazingly helpful and accomodating. The entire staff from beginning to end was helpful and gracious.
Admittedly, some of the furniture in our room was older, but it was tasteful. The room had one of the largest flat screen TVs I've ever seen in a hotel room. The sound-proofing was acutally excellent except for the teens next door trying to get into our room. Cleared that up straight-away :-)
It is in the Financial District, so during the days on the weekends, it's pretty empty, but the walkability to all the attractions was awesome! We were able to walk to the Aquarium, Quincy Market, the North End, Chinatown, Boston Commons, etc. At night, the area is packed with college kids blowing off steam. I've never seen so many lines to get into clubs. It can get noisy and the testosterone can flow with some noisy """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""arguments"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" occuring outside the hotel.
In any case, I would have no reservations in recommending this hotel to anyone visiting Boston.

A beautiful property, with a great staff. We stayed for several days in a two-room suite and had ample room (with a folding table and chairs) to host several family meals. The suites have the feel of a comfortable, up-scale apartment. The staff is very, very accomodating. The price is a bit high, but not out of line given the fantasic location and the quality of the property.

I read some of the reviews before writing my own. My husband and I had a completely different experience than some.
We stayed at the Driskill for our wedding night, and I cannot imagine a more perfect place for it. We had the Renaissance Bridal room, and it overlooked downtown Austin - on Memorial Day weekend, the party kept going until the late morning hours. 
It's a beautiful old hotel, the bridal room was breathtakingly gorgeous, and the bathroom was to die for. It had a jacuzzi tub and a multi-head, wall length marble shower. The bed was canopied and very comfortable. 
Our only complaint was that the traffic made a two block trip -- minutes long. However, that is not the Driskill's fault - if you book downtown, expect downtown traffic.

This hotel was perfect for a family of - visiting Sea World. We stayed in one of the suites with - queen beds and a pull out sofa. The sofa would not have been great for adults but worked fine for - small kids. Hotel was very clean, had a good selection of breakfast items and a good pool. The hotels location is near the freeway system and makes it easy to get to all the area attractions. There is a shopping area with many food choices across the overpass. Also a Denny's and Wendy's in walking distance. My only complaint was the old creaky elevator near the pool. Parking spaces are tight and it would be hard to fit a large SUV. Our minivan was a tight fit on weekend nights. I would stay here again.

Looking over some of the other reviews I am a little mystified. I have never had an issue with this hotel but don't know if that is because I am an elite Priority Club member or not. The rooms I get are usually very nice and extremely comfortable. The amenities are good for the price point. I usually eat in the steak house on the first floor and have never gotten poor service or yucky food. It is a little expensive but I'm dealing with Houston and traveling alone having that convenience of a decent place to eat is worth a little higher price tag. 
I do advise to toss into your suitcase an extension cord and a plug strip if you are a business traveler as the plugs are rare animals in some of the room since this hotel was build in the years before multiple electronics were a must for business. I'm in the area three or four times a year and stay here when the schedules allows.
