Like everyone else - the one issue is the parking. The ticket says complimentary and no-ne tells you ist going to be $-- per day added to your bill on departure.
TOP TIP - when you book in - don't take the car park ticket option. There is a free car park adjacent to the property that is well lit and very open - use that!
A reviewer on here said there was no Wi-Fi. This is wrong - there is Wi-Fi that covers the entire hotel and it is free. 
The bar closes far too early (--pm) something us Brits struggle with I'm afraid. Restaurants are ok - but you'd be better taking yourself into town for choice and value.
Pool is nicely sheltered behind glass screens to keep the cool breeze off and the Jacuzzi is super heated.
All in all - very good - but please sort the hidden $---day parking charge out as customers can'd help but feel screwed by it.

Good place, and some nice touches in the room. Toiletries-turndown service-clean and neat. A vibrant bar, and smart hotel generally. The best thing is the location, near the shops and Boston Common. Concierge slightly pushy, but always helpful - parking though is expensive, in my view at $-- per night. Generally though a good stay and happy with the place

I was here for a Wedding in Sept ----. 
Its an older classy hotel, and nicer than any of the other Intercontinental Hotels Ive been to. Most of the others seem to be --- star hotels that are a bit worn. Personally, I'm not a huge fan of the Intercontinental-IHG Hotel chain (which includes Holiday Inn), but this is a very nice place. I usually prefer startwood hotels like the W next door, but the wedding party was staying here.
The rooms are quiet, clean, and comfortable. The service was attentive and very good overall. I didnt spend much time using the hotel facilities. If you are getting a good rate, this is a great place to stay, albeit it may be a bit expensive.

The good: The location is great if you want to stay near the capital and the Central Station metro. The inhouse restaurant has a delicious buffet that is reasonably priced.
Disappointments: The room was very small. We received small double beds instead of the requested queen beds. I am tall so I did not sleep well. The gym and pool area were nice, but felt very cold. Fine for when you are working out, but not so great getting out of the pool. One day the pool was quite warm and one day is was very cold.

I've just returned from a five night stay at the Soho Grand Hotel. The hotel is well positioned to great eateries and shops in SoHO - a short walk to China Town and the trendy Tribeca area. The subway is also only a - minute walk away and taxis like the rest of the city are in abudance here. The rooms are small but that's nothing unusual where space is at a premium plus there's so much to do in New York you're not going to be spending much time in your room so this shouldn't put you off. The rooms are slightly dated, but clean the beds and pillows are amazing. They were so plush and comfortable I'm sure my I fell asleep as my head hit my pillow. A Bose iPod speaker dock which is stated on the hotel website as one of the room amenties is only availble on request from reception for small deposit. But because of the problems I had with returning the item (you have to call for someone to collect on check-out) its probably not worth the trouble. I never bothered requesting the gold fish.
Breakfast is available at the hotel at an extra cost and you are expected to have it in your room. I couldn't imagine anyting worse considering the size. Luckily the hotel is close to so many great eateries, that we ate out every morning. Balthazar is only a -- minute walk away on Spring Street , and was a great place to sit and people watch.
The staff at the hotel are extremly polite and knowledgeable. We experienced no problems that other reviewers have reported in the bar. But word of advice if you do intend to sit and drink in the bar is that it's worth smartening up - I've learnt that you can never be over dressed in this city.
All in all I enjoyed my stay at the Grand and would definitely go back. I would recommend the hotel to second-time visitors who've already done all the sights, and just want to experience New York as New Yorkers do.

This is our second stay at Hotel Cass-Holiday Inn Express. We stayed for the weekend over the air and water show weekend and just as the first visit - it was pleasant. We traveled with our - yr old daughter and needless to say, she just loved going downstairs for breakfast. Breakfast is your typical fare, but there is plenty to chose from and the staff was quite helpful. However, do ge there early as it does get busy and the dining area is very small. Speaking of small....the rooms are not suites and are pretty small. Decent hairdryer and toiletries. However in a city like Chicago, why do you need a big room? Great location, very close to many attractions and in between two red line stops. 
Overall another great stay!

This was our first stay at the Driskill. This is a historic hotel, the original part was built in the late ----s. The Driskill has historic charme and splendor. In the original building walls are --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" thick stone and extra thick floors and ceilings for fire protection. Our room was very quiet towards the hotel noise, but we did have some street noise from -th Street. That is however the trade off for being in an excellent location right where all the Austin action takes place. We were in walking distance to the Capitol and downtown area. Our room included --$ coupons for welcome drinks at the bar and --$ for breakfast. Service and food were excellent. This is a Texas tradition! Lots of history and some old world ambiance!

We had stayed at this motel about - years ago also for medical reasons and it has deteriorated horribly since. This visit we were unable to find another hotel to stay in, therefore, we ended up here by default for - nights. The first night we were on the first floor. This room had a very moldy smell and the room was very old. I immediately went to the drugstore next door to buy a candle to attempt to mask the odors. 
We had to use the hotel shuttle back from the hospital the first night. The desk had informed us the last shuttle had to be called in by -:-- and back to the hotel by --:-- pm. Just returned from a GREAT - night trip to the Marriott Long Wharf, Boston, MA. Immediately upon arrival, Mike (one of the most accomodating door men) welcomed us and assisted us with our check in. From this first greeting, everyone we came in contact with, was exceptionally helpful and interested in our having a wonderful stay. We had cool weather, with scattered showers one day and were delighted to find complimentary umbrellas waiting for us as we exited the hotel, to sight see. The hotel was impeccably clean. All our special requests were handled immediately, with a cheerful attitude. Extra coffee and a whopping amount of extra half n half creamers were provided. One night my daughter left her IPad in the car, which was already valet parked, and Bob, (another of the door men) gladly, searched the vehicle and brought the ipad to us on the -th floor. What a wonderful, very well run, hotel. In addition, the hotel is perfectly located across from the aquarium, Quincy Market and Fenuil Hall. Great food and shopping! On our last day, upon check out, we learned that our car could stay complimentary at the hotel till -pm. What a great perk! The (terrific) valet guys brought us the car and re-parked it - times that day, for our convenience. Overall, our introduction to Boston was delightful, and left us wanting to go back!!

I was a little worried given some earlier reviews of this hotel, but my stay was fine. I spent three weeknights while my mother was recovering from surgery at nearby Kernan hospital. The room was clean and well furnished with pretty recent stuff; the fridge, microwave, TV and everything all worked just fine. The bed was pretty comfy and the shower was hot in the morning. I wish the cable selection included more channels like Bravo and SciFi, but it was ok. 
I had a room overlooking the pool, and so I didn't hear much traffic noise. It was midweek and there didn't seem to be many people, so I didn't hear any external or neighbor noise. I can see how if there were people outside in a party mood (on the weekend maybe) the voices would carry. I used the fitness room which was ok, though the counter on the elliptical was a little fritzy. I stopped in for breakfast one morning, which was just bagels and sweet rolls etc but was ok, too. 
For free high-speed internet, they'll give you a cable at the front desk since they don't have wireless. It was really convenient to Kernan, down the road from fast food restaurants, and just across the street from a mall with a grocery store where I got some food to heat up. The property itself is back from the main business area, up a side road, so there's not much local traffic.
I'm a single middle-aged woman and I felt pretty safe. There was a delay the night I checked in when nobody was at the desk, but the security guard was there and was very nice and went to find a desk clerk. Overall, it was pretty standard motel fare: maybe not quite worth the price given that it's still just really a motel, but comparable to what else is in the area. And it does seem like they're trying to get their act together and provide good service to their customers.
Dirty.. Dont bother. The only reason we stayed was the two king beds in one room.

Castle Inn was pretty easy to find and seemed to be in a good area - free parking another bonus. Thankfully the hotel had an elevator so we didn't have to drag our bags up to the -nd floor (rooms have outside entrances). We didn't really try to walk anywhere from the hotel, so I can't say if it was conveniently located to things like the cable car etc. Our only complaint was the internet was terrible here, was really patchy and barely worked. We told the front desk but nothing really happened to fix it - being that other reviewers have commented on this, it was a little disappointing that this was still an issue. Other than some very rude guests calling loudly to each other back and forth outside at -am (don't know why management didn't hear them?!) which due to the shape of the hotel facing the wall seemed to echo, we had a good stay and I would stay there again.

Definition: (A hotel near the airport. The hotel does not have to be connected to the airport (although some are) or even adjacent to it; it could be located up to five miles away. Most airport hotels have a shuttle to and from the terminals.)
Well, reading the definition above, this place is for SURE an airport hotel. Nothing more actually.
The person who checked me in was not very friendly. Seemed bored with his job. Bummer. 
My room was on the -rd floor overlooking McDonald's. The hallways were in pretty bad shape. Did not feel much like a hotel hallway, felt more like an old, creepy, condominium hallway. 
The smell. Ahhh the smell. Almost all Holiday Inn's smell the same. Not bad, but not good. Just Holiday Inn """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""ish"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".

Free WiFi.
Tried for -.- hours to get a wake up call. The phone just rang off the hook for over - hours straight. Sometimes it would go to a strange voice mail. There was a clock in the room, but it was flashing some incorrect time since my arrival and I refused to set it.
I grabbed one of those """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Do Not Disturb"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" things from the door to place on the knob and it was NASTY! I mean, gum or something on it and some disgusting looking stains.
Bathroom is small, but WAY more updated than the halls. Tub looks pretty worn out. Had ZERO washcloths in the bathroom. Love the light sensors that turn the light on for you as you approach. GREAT shower head, really nice flow. And of course, skinny, wimpy towels.
McDonald's really IS -- steps away from the lobby if you are into that kinda thing. Egg McMuffin, MMmmmmm.
If you can get a room here for $---night or less, go for it, for the convenience. Most airport hotels I have stayed at are never great and that is unfortunate. But this place will do the job, and nothing more.

My first impression was a very sterile lobby. We walked through the parking garage to check in. We were on the --th floor - and the room was very very small which was OK because we did not spend a lot of time there - but very small. I had a hard time getting out of my side of the bed because there was not much room between the bed and wall. We had one bath towel and called and asked for a second towel - but it never came. They cleaned the room at -:-- the next day at which time we got two towels. There was nothing in the refrigerator - even to pay for and no machines to buy a drink anywhere. For a - Star hotel I think I expected a little more. It was not as nice as hotels that I have stayed in in the past. It was centrally located though and I liked that. If i was to go back to San Francisco I would not stay in this hotel.

I arrived in San Diego early and no rooms were available, but I was put on a waiting list and was called immediately when my room was ready (approx - hour later). The only bad thing about that was I was tired and there wasn't really any indoor lounge area where I could sit down and wait for my room to be ready except up by the pool, so we just walked around downtown. But overall the check in, check out and valet services were very quick and easy. The hotel is very unique and the room was really nice - the room was a bit pricey, but it was nicer than a regular hotel. The pool was small, but the lounge area around the pool was super nice! I stayed with my bf and we both had a fantastic time. I would definitely recommend for adults (I wouldn't stay here with kids)!

My husband and I loved this hotel! We were a bit wary about staying in a courtyard but this exceeded my expectations. The rooms were absolutely beautiful and very comfortable...one of the best rooms I’ve ever stayed in! Everything was spotless. Bathrooms were very clean and modern. The view was spectacular. We were on a higher level floor with a terrace facing the riverwalk. Very quiet and a helpful staff that was very eager to please. The only issues I had was with parking, the pool (way too small but I don't swim) and the long walk from the elevator to our specific room (which I didn't mind but for some people, it's kind of far). Just to warn you, parking is valet only (unless you want to pay for a parking garage but no in-and-out privileges) I believe it was $-- a day. But do call -- min ahead before leaving the hotel or you will be waiting in lobby awhile for your car. Other than that loved everything! San Antonio is a great place to visit.

I checked into this place early on a Friday, well before the stated check in time. The desk clerk was more than accommodating in calling housekeeping to find me a room. Upon gathering my things and riding the elevator to the top of the building I found everything was in order. The television was up to date, the bedding and towels were in perfect condition, and the room was sparkling clean.
I was there for a two-day stay, which precipitate usage of the shower. Immediately I noticed a very slow drain, which is a pet peeve of mine. When I got out of the shower and got dressed, I called the desk to have the building engineer come look at the problem. Within two minutes he was at my door, much to my surprise. He eliminated the problem in very short order, which I was very pleased with.
Houston in the summer is so muggy you cannot ever get to a cool dry place. The air conditioners were plenty adequate, but they were overwhelmed by the fact it was raining outside. For the bulk of my visit, I was plenty cool enough yet still sweating underneath my shirt.
This hotel offers a full restaurant open for breakfast and dinner, but not lunch. They have a small bar adjacent to the restaurant for your evening cocktail needs. They offer a buffet style breakfast, or cooked to order. Some rates get a free breakfast with their room price; some discounted rates do not. The hotel also offers a flower shop and a separate gift shop with sundries. It’s across the street from Houston’s entire medical district, thus there are a lot of patients coming and going.
Ty on the front desk was particularly helpful and completely in control. I asked him if he was the GM, and he indicated most devoutly no. Still, when he was on duty he ran the place with the authority of a GM, and no guest request wasn’t immediately taken care of.
This place charges a self-parking fee, and it’s my guess that it’s a result of the hospitals across the street. If they didn’t, they would be over-run with freeloaders trying to skip out on paying for parking in one of the hospital garages. The fee was nominal. They also have - different shuttle busses to ferry passengers to-from medical appointments or the airport. They also have a well informed concierge desk. 
The business center was fitted with badly obsolete computers, so slow you could hardly read e-mail. They took forever to connect, appearing to be almost as slow as dial-up. Also, the printer did not work on the one I used. Still, the machines are WAY obsolete running Windows-XP, and they are running about like a pig on stilts. It’s time to throw them out and buy new ones, or just abandon the business center all together. What is offered is hardly useful for any normal activity.
I didn’t use the fitness center or the pool, but I did view them and they were in fine shape, clean, and appealing.
This is a property Kemmons Wilson could be proud of. It felt like a Holiday Inn should have. The property and the staff both were up to standards. I would indeed stay here again, and I would recommend it to anybody.

I stayed here because of it's location, reasonable prices and a website(very tacky showcasing a half naked woman in bed by the way!!) that made the hotel look very nice. Also, while attempting to checkout at noon there was but - person behind the desk and at least - others waiting to either check in or out. This is my goto place whenever I'm in town visiting family. The rooms are very clean and a good size and updated. The staff are friendly and helpful. They have the best breakfast buffet of any hotel I've ever stayed. It is well located in the White Marsh area - close to shopping and restaurants but tucked back from the main road and therefore very quiet.

Located in the heart of Seattle the Hotel Monaco is always a favorite of our traveling crew. From it's location to the staff to being a pet friendly hotel the Hotel Monaco is always a treat. Your never alone in the hotel as you'll have one their trademark Goldfish w-name in your room when you arrive. Just a great environment and pleasant place to stay.

The good- the people are generally nice and it offers the perks of an Embassy Suites (Breakfast, - room suite and reception), the location is not too far from a metro stop.
The not so good: the hotel has been remodeled, but is still showing its age, the “snacks” during the reception are weird (its limited to goldfish crackers and hummus), the price (---.-- a night) is on the high side and the bell staff service is pretty limited (don’t expect luggage help. They recently did some work on the pool, but I can’t see any difference.

It saddens me to see such structures of once beauty- left to degrade. I had hopes that perhaps her room would be in better shape. When I stepped out of the lift, I was wondering through the Roosevelt's vast, rather creepy hallway, searching for the correct room. A group of kind housekeepers pointed the way. She had tears in her eyes when she opened her door! Long story short- She was freaked out, and did not want to be there. As she imagined her trip to New York quite different! I went into her bathroom to inspect the spotted """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""shower curtain"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that clearly had things only a scientist would know the correct names for, and also had the misfortune of seeing a rusted pipe leaking the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""wrong kind"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of mineral water under her sink! Needed a place to stay in Philly for one night. We were traveling for pleasure and primarily focused on location. The Warwick is in a great spot. Good neighborhood, walking distance to anything City Center, a stumble away from Rittenhouse square. The hotel was fine, the people were incredibly nice and the room was mediocre (leaky toilet, sleep number bed didn't really work). It's certainly a fine place to stay, and given that we got a great price we were happy. Again, the staff was great. But I wouldn't spend a ton to stay here.

The hotel was very convenient for the hop on-off trolley tour, walking to Seaport Village, the Midway and some other places. The interior decor was a little tired but the staff was very nice and helpful. Several places to eat in and around the hotel. Beware of some rooms that overlook the roof and ugly pipes unless you don't care what you see when you're on your balcony.

Visited our friends who moved to Chicago and stayed down the street from them at the Drake for the weekend. The location of the hotel is fantastic - near great shopping, the lake, and wonderful restaurants. 
We were able to book a great rate ($---). When we arrived early after our flight, we were allowed to check in early, but for a price (additional $--). It was worth it to unpack and regroup. We had a handicapped room, which was very spacious. The shower-tub combo was not ideal for us, and had only a hand held shower head. 
While the room was very elegantly appointed, it was showing signs of age - old floors and carpet, window casings, drapes, etc. The bedding and towels were nice and pretty new. The furniture was nice, and the tv was rather large and flat screened. 
The bar area of the Palm Court is just beautiful - had tea there on Friday afternoon, and drinks later that evening. 
We had only one complaint - one afternoon after a long day walking around town, we returned to our room and discovered both of our key cards would not work. We had to return to the front desk to get replacements, and it was right as most folks were checking in. All we wanted to do was get inside and relax!
There are so many aspects of the Drake which reminded me of the Ritz in Paris, including the shopping areas on the ground floor. 
If you are wanting a new and hip hotel, this is not it. If you are traveling with children, this isn't your place either. No pool, no activities - really not a great place for kids. If you want to have a great weekend of shopping, dining and exploring Chicago with another adult, this would be a good choice.

Loved how close the inn was to the Prudential Center subway. Neighborhood atmosphere. Large room and bathroom. Stayed in Studio Suite. Only con was we could here people upstairs walking, talking, etc. Great view onto street. Breakfast was a light, typical continental... coffee, bagels, cup of oatmeal. Staff was very friendly and helpful. If we come back to Boston we will definitely consider staying here again... Just on the top floor,

Stayed at this hotel in December ---- and returned. Stayed on -rd floor this trip. When first entering the room the smell of cleaning products was overwhelming. But the window opens so the room could be aired out. If not for this option, myself and companions probably could not have stayed. The residual of the cleaning products burned our eyes and throat. But opening the window corrected the situation to the point where we decided we could stay. Other than that, the room was a very good value. The room was clean. The beds were comfortable. There was no issue with noise. The hallway a little smell of stale cigarette smoke. The staff was friendly and accommodating.

My kid is still traumatized.
I had never seen bed bugs up close in my life. It was a disgusting experience to wake up itching with bites all over and a bug still feeding on me. 
There was also a huge stain on the ripped comforter and lots of traffic coming in and out of the rooms around me.
The staff acts as if you're a Burden and even with a dnd sign up, housekeeping came banging on my door at -- am.
Rooms look ok, but only get cleaned very superficially.

This was our third stay at the Conrad Indianapolis. We are amazed at the level of service we receive every time we stay. We have stayed at other Hilton properties and this one by far blows the others out of the water. The staff is very helpful no matter what time of day. Our room was spotless. They really care about the guests! We find it is always difficult to leave because by the end of our stay we feel like we are home. The location is top notch! We couldn't have asked for more luxury. We will only stay at the Conrad Indianapolis!
good clean hotel friendly helpfull staff near to times square and broadway plenty of resaurants nearby also near to the subway

However, it was quite possibly the most uncomfortable bed-pillow situation I've ever encountered. The pillows were quite firm and thick, bending my neck at a very uncomfortable angle. The first night I ended up with a cramp all the way from my neck to my hip. The second night, I gave up and slept without a pillow. 
The staff was average. After recently staying in a hotel where the staff was superb, I noticed the little things, like the doors not being opened for us and not being greeted when we entered the hotel. Also housekeeping didn't show up until late afternoon, after I had already called the front desk to request fresh towels because I thought we'd been skipped.

I wanted to rate this hotel more highly, because I slept really well (and needed it after a long drive). Beds are great, mattress is comfortable and pillows are awesome, The hotel lobby is very nice as well. A lot was lacking, although I imagine that if you know what to ask for, your experience could be much better than mine.
First, the noise is maddening. I had a fourth floor room facing the lobby (first four floors on one side of the hotel face into the lobby's atrium). There is a partially indoor pool along with a restaurant in the lobby area, so kids' screams, diners' loud voices and people talking loudly on cell phones are all very audible. Also the walls are paper thin - heard the neighbor's wake-up call at -am as if it were in our room and could hear doors slamming and people at the vending machine at all hours. This may have been their policy for a while (I asked the front desk) but I've not experienced this at any other hotel. I was able to get the duplicate charges removed. 
I am heartened by the fact that I got the room at more than half off regular rates through the negotiation website, however if I had paid full price, I would be at the front desk complaining about the stay. Hopefully you'll know what to ask for and have a better experience than I did.

If you value honesty, integrity, and your time, avoid this hotel! The local owners of this hotel have no qualms at all about overbooking you well in advance, lying to you about it on the day you arrive, and trying to shuttle you out to their cheaper motel across town. If that sounds like a travel nightmare to you, beware...it could become your reality if you book a room here.
I booked at Rodeway Inn Mid Town about a week prior to my visit to Baltimore by calling the hotel directly. I got a great rate at $-- per room per night. I got a room for myself and another room for my business colleague. I chose this hotel because of decent reviews here and its location close to the train station & where we were conducting a business seminar. The day I was to arrive in Baltimore to check into the Rodeway Mid Town, I checked my reservations online and they were good. However, I received a phone call at about -:-- PM from the hotel's desk clerk, explaining that there was a problem with the internet in the rooms I had booked. He asked if I would mind staying at the Rodeway Inn on Pulaski Highway, about - --- miles away, with a free shuttle from the train station and to my business meeting venue. I told him I wanted to stay in the room I booked. I asked him to call the other hotel to confirm whether that would actually be possible, but made it clear that I was not committing to his offer. He said he'd check and call me back.
About - or - hours passed with no phone call from the hotel. I called them back and again explained that I didn't care about the internet problems and would just rather stay at the Rodeway Mid Town. The clerk changed his story and told me that actually, they were having problems with the toilets in both of the rooms and that it would not be possible for us to stay there. He again offered the rooms at Pulaski Hwy. I told him I'd look into some other options.
I called Rodeway corporate (Choice Hotels customer service) to complain. They confirmed that Rodeway Mid Town had overbooked me, that both Rodeway Inns had the same local owner, and that I was welcome to file a formal complaint. Since returning from my trip, I have come across other similar reviews online for this hotel from customers who experienced the exact same problem (including the bogus stories about plumbing problems). My advice: avoid both Rodeway Inn Mid Town *and* Rodeway Inn Pulaski Hwy. They do not deserve your business!

i recently stayed at the gansevoort and frankly it was one of the best hotels i've ever stayed at. Personally we felt there was not enough time to digest the large amount of information they supplied, but signed up based on the time and questions we did get answered. After returning home, we took a closer look and determined that it is not a great deal. In fact it is not really a deal at all. There are a lot of details you will not learn while you are there and most likely not find out before the - days cancellation time in up. There are too many to go into, but the biggest problem thus far has been canceling. We called and discussed the process with several people at the Club. Do not sign up because you think time is against you. It is not. If something seems too good. It probably is. We don't dislike the people there. In fact they were very kind, but they lose interest when you learn the facts.

As this is an all suite hotel, the room is spacious with a living room. Although i do think that the living room can be more private without the windows that allows other guest to see what you are doing when they walk pass your room! The toilet looks a bit dated and do not have a walk in shower.
The hotel provides free wifi at the lobby area, otherwise its -.--USD per -- hours and they charge by IP Address, which i thought is ridiculous.

I had dinner in the hotel one night and i have to wait -- to -- mins for a plate of spaghetti, there seem to be only one server and one bartender. 
Checkout was a nightmare!! No one came to help us with the bags and we had to do it on our own and get our own taxi. There was no service of any sort, be prepared to put up with it when you stay at Doubletree.

My - month old and I stayed at this hotel while my husband was in Houston on business and it was a GREAT place! The pool is super warm so it was great to take her swimming and she never got cold. The rooms are very nice with updated bathrooms and home touches - Hooks where you would have them in your home, comfy mattresses and fluffy duvets and pillows. NO scratchy sheets or """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sex"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" blanket covers. After a few days, I attempted to process my travel claim when I noticed a discrepency in my bill and credit card statements. Dean made our stay amazingly comfortable and made us feel very welcome! It was like a home away from home! Thanks Dean! Rooms are very clean and tidy! Room service was amazing, provided us with all necessities we asked for and made it an all around great experience!

We booked two nights at the La Quinta Seatac via internet, got good rates, the hotel was way above our expectations, the staff was exceptionally helpful - they allowed us to check in way before check in time and thus we gained many hours of enjoyment of the lovely city of Seattle. What the staff doesn't ell you is that there is an express bus across the street which takes you to downtown Seattle and there is no reason to take a taxi as they suggested; this was a big saving for us(we are a retired couple). Would certainly go there again.

We stayed at this fabulous small hotel for three nights at the end of April. It is in a great location just off -th Avenue and within walking distance of many of New York's main attractions.
The service from the reservations team when we were booking the hotel was excellent and this service continued when we arrived at the hotel with attentive, friendly and helpful staff. The rooms are very clean and tidy with comfortable beds and were ideal for us. The staff knowledge of New York and where to eat was invaluable and having coffee and tea available in the hotel lobby -- hours was also a benefit.
My wife had an accident on -th Avenue just before we were due to leave on our journey home and we returned to the hotel where the staff couldn't do enough to help. My thanks go to Millie and the team for their care and support and ongoing assistance which is much appreciated and shows the high level of customer service.
We would certainly return to this hotel on our next visit to New York and would highly recommend it.

My experience at the Waldorf was horrible. The check-in was slow but the place is busy so I had no issue. I had to wait about -- minutes. 
I believe I was given a room which should have been offline and since I booked through Priceline they decided to give me one of their not so nice rooms. I called the front desk to find out if they could change my room but I was told they had no other rooms available so then I just sucked it up.
After my stay on August -th I sent an email with the photos attached to their guest relations email but have yet to hear back from anyone. 
I would have expected better from the Waldorf.

Recently spent one night at the Sheraton for a quick in and out business trip, and can't think of one negative experience. Beautiful and warm, which is tough to do with such a large hotel, all the staff I encountered were pleasant and helpful, I didn't need much, but if I did I got the feeling people would trip over themselves to deliver. The standout was the breakfast buffet at the second floor restaurant, served daily but so incredible you get the feeling it should be served as a holiday Sunday brunch. Service was impeccable, George our server was very pleasant, and his back server Matt was a joy. Both true ambassadors of hospitality. Matt went above and beyond to make sure I had everything I needed, and spent a few extra moments with me chatting about the area and answering my questions about the buffet, even though the restaurant was incredibly busy. i watched him assist with several tables at the same time, quietly and efficently making sure everyones needs were met, and the above and beyond service he provided me made me feel very comfortable, particuraly seeing that i was dining alone. Would highly recommend this hotel over others in the area, regardless of size, you do not get lost in the crowd, made to feel special throughout the entire stay.

Borders on a really seedy neighborhood. When the cabby drove me there, he rolled up my window as were were driving near the hotel.
Also the hotel is in dire need of a makeover!! I'm used to staying at Hiltons all over the world where I'm treated with high respect with room upgrades and a full hot breakfast. This hotel offered me a cramped out of date room, charged me for items that were missing from the mini-bar before I arrived and gave me a coupon for a coffee and danish from Starbucks as my Gold benefit and said I could pay $-- more if I wanted a full breakfast. I was supposed to stay for - nights, but checked out after - to move to the Hilton Financial Dist because I was so turned off by the property. The Hilton Financial Dist was much nicer, cleaner and worth the move. They are too lacking an Executive Lounge, but because it's under renovation.
They clearly are not up to regular Hilton standards. I travel to SF every week and was giving your property a try. Sorry to say, it missed the cut.

My mom and I planned a trip to SF and after looking through MANY hotels we decided to take a chance on this one through others reviews. Let me tell you, this hotel is fantastic. Very quiet, the staff is absolutely awesome, great price, awesome updated rooms, FREE PARKING. We had to park around back and they had survallence all over. It was great to feel so secure. The staff was so friendly and very knowledgable. They told us how to get to certain bus stops, best places to eat, best places to visit, and even printed out a list of tours for us!. The only problem for me personally was that it wasn't as close to the Wharf and Pier as I had hoped, which isn't that big of a deal. I will DEFINITELY stay here again. It's like staying in a - or - star hotel for a lot cheaper. Thank you guys for making our vacation so great!!

The look of the place was great, though much of that which was supposed to be slick was not functioning...auto check in kiosk was not functional, desk clerk was chipper but clueless...he chatted up a visiting staff member for over - minutes as guests lined up to check in...I really couldn't believe what I was seeing. The bartender in the lounge did a serviceable job of keeping the clientele happy but was painfully slow.
As others have attested, the housekeeping was substandard. On the first night the sconce lights in my room were not working. I asked for maintenance to come to room to fix. The guy spent -- minutes turning the light switches on and off, barely hiding his real intention of watching the - st game of the world series with no intention of fixing the lights. He was unable to get them to work and promised to have the day shift fix them as I needed them the following evening. When I returned the next day they still didn't work and yet no note, message or anything from the desk. I called and they said, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""oh ya, here's a message that says the lights don't work"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Then I insisted on some sort of light be sent to the room. They sent the sorriest excuse for a lamp I've ever seen...the shade was not affixed to the base and it rocked when moved.
The desk clerk on my departure, a young woman was the only bright light in the place. She was both knowlegable and helpful.
With the many hotels I stay in for my work I really enjoyed the cleanliness and wonderful staff that made this stay one that makes you first asking is there a Staybridge Suites were I am going.

The location was very good, with a -- min walk to Time Square. The street the hotel was on was fine (as compared to what other people say). Its a typical new york side street. 
The hotel is close to the subway.
The hotel itself is clean and basic. Free coffee in the lobby, little store to buy basics at (but we mostly bought our stuff in small stores along -th). 
Staff was great, very helpful and friendly.
For the price, you cant get much better than this.

The location is excellent, The rooms are spotless, exceptionally comfortable and well appointed and the staff were very friendly. The problem is we got no rest at all. The construction wasn't the problem ironically, the problem was the room doors have absolutely no sound proofing and the housekeeping staff were literally letting the doors behind them slam all morning from - am to check out it was a continual stream of slamming doors, knocks, elevator bells and talking that could be heard clear as a bell from bed. I don't know how anyone can sleep here without ear plugs. I choose a hotel on the UWS and on the side facing a brick wall for some silence, but I got the loudest and inconsiderate hotel experience ever. I would have extended my stay, but in the AM I realized there was no rest to be had. The front desk was very nice about my complaint and apologized, but they couldn't do anything as I prepaid on hotels.com. I can't recommend thia hotel, because all I use my hotel in NYC for is sleep and that need was not met here, it's sad too, because otherwise it's a great hotel.

The Eventi Hotel is quite new (I think they opened up in April ----) and therefore when we booked in June we were able to take advantage of their special Grand Opening offer! 
The premises are just beautiful: the lobby is not big but features distinctive and stylish pieces of furniture; the front desk staff was friendly and professional (special thanks to Victoria); the bedroom was not very spacious either but nicely furnished, with the most confy and largest bed ever and a great view! We were offered complimentary tee & coffee in the morning, wine reception at -pm (we just adored their veranda!), wi-fi connection at all time and a $-- voucher for the in-room minibar!! Everything was spotless clean and every single person of the staff was always nice and smiling! Last but not least, a subway station is only - minutes walking from there.
During our vacation in the US we stayed at - different hotels and we realized that their standards are somehow lower than the European ones, but the Eventi was no disappointment!
To be very very picky, although in the heart of Manhattan, its immediate surroundings are quite ugly and dirty.

My boyfriend booked me a surprise holiday to NYC for my --th birthday at Christmas and it was the best ever as he also proposed. We went over new year ---------. 
Hotel - Situated in downtown NY, we were on the --th floor so had a very touching and memorable view of ground zero. The ongoing work on the WTC site is --hr so prepare for a bit of noise although the windows muffle the sound a little, it's still audible. The hotel is very clean and the staff are very friendly, the hotel has a concierge so use this service when you can i.e reservations for restaurants etc. The pool looked lovely but we never used it as we were too busy doing the touristy things. The menu looked appertising although we never ate in the hotel and the room service charge was high. The room was big with a bed to die for - very comfy and cosy.
Out & About - You definitely need to get the subway (E train) from WTC subway or a taxi to midtown ($-) per ride, it is not within walking distance. Downtown Broadway (the road) becomes very dark and quite at night as the shops close so try to avoid walking here.
If you are planning to go on the Staten Island Ferry to pass the Stat of Lib I would advise getting to Battery Park for one of the first crossings of the day as the queue gets very long.
I recommend a Broadway show to complete your stay tickets can be booked via the concierge or by turning up to the theatre & booking direct - Mary Poppins was $-- each (£-- at the time) much more expensive through your tour op.
Overall - I loved every second of NY and found the people v.friendly. I would go back tomorrow and I would stay in this hotel again but as we spent a lot of time Midtown I may book a hotel nearer there.
Thank you for making my stay (& birthday) very special.

I had a very good experience at this hotel. My check-in went smoothly and the person who checked me in was very pleasant. The lobby was very nice, clean, stylish and inviting, though I didn't spend much time in it. My room was pretty much perfect upon first inspection. It was clean, on a non-smoking floor as I had requested and it smelled good. The rooms looked better than what the traveler pictures portray on this site. Some of the towels had seen better days - but that was not most of them. The lotion, soap and toiletries provided in the bathroom were of good quality. I stayed here after a business trip in Austin turned into more of a leisure trip. My main purpose was to find a hotel conveniently located near a conference that was happening at my former church. The Omni was in a perfect location for me - less than -- minutes from the church - so it was an easy drive late at night after the conference. There was plenty of parking even though I came back late two nights in a row.
I spent a little time at the pool and it was nice. I ate breakfast at the restaurant there two mornings in a row and had a good experience each time. I had no problems with this hotel and would absolutely stay here again. In fact, I imagine I will try to stay here every time I go back to visit my church.

I am hesitant to spread the word, for fear I wont be able to get a reservation when I want one! We love this small hotel for the warmth of its staff and cozy rooms. The neighborhood is safe, pleasant and convenient! Its a great find and bargain! Enjoy!

Bargain for NYC. This hotel had a very European flare; small rooms but knew what to expect from reading these reviews. The bed was comfortable and the A-C worked great; in fact at times it was pretty down right cold...which I love! The only problem I had were the feather pillows, as my daughter and I are allergic to them. We asked the staff for different pillows; but that was all they had. We """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""made do"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" by putting bath towels over them. Nice and friendly staff. Whenever we needed anything, the staff was quick to accomodate. Very convenient to Times Square and there is a great deli two blocks to the right in which we had breakfast every morning. Would stay there again.

This hotel is not too spendy. It has smaller room and we had issues with the airconditioning-heater and management moved us to a bigger room up in the new wing. I suggest when you book in this hotel make sure you are placed on the new building as it has a lot bigger rooms and better furniture. The hotel is walk away from good restaurants and is about -- min walk to Jacob Javits center where my convention was held. 
I would not stay here if not place on the newer building with better rooms.

The Doubletree has a reputation of being a warm and friendly place to stay. This San Diego hotel meets all of these requirements. The staff is friendly and helpful and the cookies (choco-chip) are to die for!! The room was spacious and a balcony overlooking the pool area provided us with a place to dry out our scuba gear!! 
Access is easy and straigh-forward, but beware of the garage ceiling - we have a --- ton pickup that did not fit and parking it became a bit of a hassle. Still, there was adequate parking for all guests.
The bartenders were friendly, the beer cold, and the service more than adequate!
In the morning we had the buffet breakfast and it was wonderful, fresh, and a great start to a day of scuba diving the wrecks of San Diego!
I heartily recommend this hotel and plan on staying there again!!

This was our second time to stay in this hotel. We have a - yr old so the play ground is perfect. The pool was great! Even though it was a little cold outside, part of the pool is heated. I mean really heated! It was so nice to get in and relax and let my daughter play! The only not so good things are ..... It was kinda hard to find and they ran out of irons. My thought was go buy some! We had to walk around all weekend wrinkled. But other that it was a great stay!

Stayed here @ start of - week tour of California-Nevada & New York following reviews on Tripadvisor. Great location, free parking available, though we didn't pick up our rental car til leaving LA. Good clean accommodation, complimentary breakfast but basis, bagels-muffins-crossants, need to bring back to your room (table & chairs provided & fridge) as no room to sit in lobby. Room a bit on dark side. Next door to Kodak Theatre, walk of fame etc.

A hotel with a big name but without much character. Dark and small lobby area, inattentive staff. Rooms and bathrooms are in need of renovation . The service is average and the breakfast was not what one could expect from a - star property.The location is great though, but there are better options in NY.

Absaloutley loved this hotel, great location! I was a bit nervous as never been to America before but the staff at Candlewood Suites were so helpfull and really nice! Very understanding and accomodating to any request! only - minute walk from Times Square, in same street there is Starbucks and everything you need in a - minute walk! Room was great, amazing Lazy Boy chair and the bed was SOOO COMFY!!! you get free cookies and they have a free gym and when you leave to go home they hold on to your bags all day and dont make you feel pressured to tip or anything like that! Great hotel and would recommend anyone to go there, if your thinking about going, just book it, you wont regret it! ALMOST FORGOT, Free Wireless internet in the rooms!! WOW!!!! i was doing face time with my family back in england on my iphone - for free!

Stayed at the Westin as a part of a package deal with the Colorado Ballet. The overall atmosphere is nice, and the rooms have great furnishings, but you could tell the building's age in the bathroom and elevator, especially.
Everything was clean and comfortable, but the best part were the people. The front desk workers were so helpful about any of our needs. Sometimes helpful people make the stay just right.

The staff is attentive and fast, they are very friendly people and seem knowledgable. The location is great, just down the road from the bus center and the epicenter - walk able to everywhere downtown. Loved my stay!

If you want a good downtown location, do not want to break the bank, and do not plan to spend much time in your hotel room, this hotel is a great choice for you. But if you want something a little more, I would stay elsewhere. The room I stayed in (which was across the street in the tower) felt damp and dated, and the air conditioning was extremely noisy. I do not think this hotel was worth the price, even at the $-- rate I got through priceline. I expect more from Sheraton and will likely not return to this hotel next time I am in Denver.

The check-in process was fine, staff is nice, but the quality of room I recieved was poor. The leather-like headboard to the bed looked as though it had been all scratched up along with the recliner that was in the room. It was old and weathered, looked as though it could've come from the dump. The bathroom faucet had a roach come out of it, I washed it down and plugged the sink only to find in the morning when I opened the stopper back up that the roach was still there! I was there on -------- and believed I stayed in room ---.

The Westing downtown Charlotte is the best! I have been staying here since it opened. Rooms are great, the staff is very interested in making your stay a good one.
Close to everything downtown. I work generally in the Wachovia or Bank of America buildings when in town on business. Rooms are plenty big, weight room is great. 
Bar -- is good some nights. During BBALL season you will see Jordan here often. Many of the visiting teams playing the BOBCATS stay here. Not a big fan of EMBER Grille but to each his own.
I am a Platinum Starwood member. My only complaint is I never have water in my room.

Stayed here on -------, the room was a standard size, very spacious, very clean. Great placement off of Times Square, super convenient to theater area. Our room shared a wall with a bank of elevators and we never heard the sounds of the elevators EVER! Our view faced downtown, we could see the Empire State bldg to our left, and New Jersey to our right. I'd stay here again!

Stayed with my friends for two nights in June ----.I'm very pleased with the service and the room.My friends and I stayed at the Executive Suite.The room with two double beds is spacious
and has a dining table and a kitchen.It is clean and the bed is not infested with bed bugs.The receptionist and the lady who serves breakfast are very helpful and friendly.,The location of the hotel is just behind Kodak Theater and from the hotel,it is easy to go to Hollywood Boulevard,where all the action is.If I go to Hollywood again,I would definitely stay at this hotel .

My husband and I stayed here for a week over Christmas - we both loved the hotel. On arrival, we were greeted by friendly reception staff who informed us that we had been upgraded as it was my birthday! We had a lovely room on the --th floor with an amazing view of the Crysler building. The room was perfect - gorgeous bathroom, comfortable bed and linen, flatscreen tv, safe, mini bar etc. It was serviced thoroughly everyday and we also had a turn down service in the evening. We did not eat in the restaurant, although had booked to on Christmas Day. However, we changed our minds when we saw the menu was not the one we were shown the day before. Gaby's is great for evening cocktails and yes, it is probably expensive, but we were on a holiday (and birthday treat) of a lifetime so didn't worry! I would definitely stay at this hotel again if I visited NYC. The only thing that bugged us a bit was that you could hear the lifts continually going up and down all the time from our room but this was a minor concern.

My husband & I stayed at the Drake hotel for an anniversary get away this past weekend. We booked and paid for a king room two weeks before our arrival. We received a free upgrade to an executive suite upon checkin. Our room (number ---, the Churchill Suite) was enormous with great views of both the lake and the city. The room was clean & the bed was comfortable. The bathroom was spacious with an ok bathtub & a nice seperate shower. We had no complaints with the room & would highly recommend spending the extra $$ to get a suite at this hotel. 
The hotel itself is beautiful. The hotel staff was courteous & helpful from check in to check out. 
Valet was very prompt upon check in but a little unorganized when we checked out. 
Things to definitly do at this hotel: 
Sunday brunch at the Drake Bros. restaurant. Pricey but well worth the $$. 
Entertainment in the Palm Court on Saturday evening. They had a jazz group there the night we stayed & they were very good. 
Check out the shops on the lower level of the hotel before heading out to Michigan Ave. 
Things to skip:
If you don't like tight crowded spaces...skip dining in the Cape Cod restaurant.
The Saturday night lines can be long waiting for the hotel staff to get a cab for you. Take the - minute walk to the end of the block & you will be in a cab much quicker than waiting in front of the hotel. 
If you do have access to the Executive Lounge don't bother. This was the only thing we were dissapointed with. It had the exact same view that we had in our suite. There was a very small bar with a bartender that was not as friendly as the bartenders in other parts of the hotel. They have a free breakfast in the lounge but we opted for room service after our experience in there the evening before.

We stayed at the Hard Rock Hotel for a week in the beginning of June. We had arrived several hours before check-in, but we still were able to get our room right away. The cleanliness of the hotel and our room was excellent. We had a great view and were able to see part of Lake Michigan. The location was also very convenient to several bus -subway stations, shops, and restaurants (our favorite was the Sweetwater Tavern and Grille right across from the side entrance of the building). The lobby and elevators were very ornate, and the building itself is historic. The only reason that we rated this a - instead of a - is because we were just expecting more. There was nothing wrong with our room, it just wasn't anything spectacular for the price. The hallways and lobby area were very well decorated and inviting. Our room lacked this sort of atmosphere and almost felt cold. If we were to return to Chicago, we would most likely stay here again for the location and because we did have a good overall experience.

Overall, this was one of the best hotels we have stayed at, especially for the price. The location could not possibly have been better. And the price of $-- a night (with -th night free) including tax that we found at a discount website was unbelievable for an inner city Chicago hotel. Some of the reviews I read that spoke of the staff being discourteous concerned me, but everyone we dealt with could not have been nicer or more eager to please. The hotel is not one of the new, sterile ones but it has old-world charm that we love and of course the room-bathroom were not big, but the one we stayed in at the Plaza in NYC was possibly even smaller. The maid did a wonderful job cleaning it and fluffing up the sumptuous quilt every day. We asked for a top floor and were given the --st floor out of -- although there is no view due to Chicago being a city of huge skyscrapers. And do not miss the roof top on the --nd floor. Only disappointment was the charge of $-- daily to access the internet although it was free in the spacious lobby.

What a great hotel and a great location. Right from check in we were made to feel very welcome. We had a standard guest room which was very comfortable with a king size bed. The room and bathroom were spacious and tastefully decorated and most importantly clean.
All the staff are very friendly and helpful, especially Monique on the concierge desk. The hotel is very close to the Chrysler Building and Empire State Building and there is quite a few good places to eat and drink close by. The rooftop bar was a fantastic place to kick off the evening. I would definatley go back.

Location was terrific, close to all the sights. The hotel room on the -th floor was very dated. The bedding looked as though it could do with laundering. Very noisy air conditioner and very noisy toilet cistern. Old fashioned. Kitchenette was hopeless. Not enough paper cups, no cutlery. Only two lifts, and in the morning often had to wait -- mins or more and the stairs was not an option.

Our third stay at the Indigo hotel. The rooms are nice and modern, have free WIFI and are pretty spacious for New York standard. Location very good. Close to public transport, shops, restaurants or whatever you are looking for. Roof top bar (happy hour not during weekend, although mentioned daily between - and - pm) with lovely views. Best of the hotel is the staff. They make the difference!!!

I stayed here for - nights in May and was very pleased with the results and am glad that I trusted the reviews on this site. Everything was great... location, cleanliness, staff, continental breakfast and for a great AAA price that you can't beat. If you are not looking for anything fancy and just want a clean, decent place to sleep and shower... this is your place. I would definitely stay here again.

Clean, friendly hotel close to main areas and attractions.
Good breakfast and free evening reception on - nights included.
Includes a Kitchenette for those inclined to do some cooking; but not us, too much to do and see! Use the 'open top' buses to get above the hustle and bustle of the street traffic and have a guided tour of New York.

I like this hotel i was there many times and i was happy there ..nice pool nice fitness and the rooms are clean and modern...but this hotel is not good for people who dont have car becouse hotel is not in centrum...

We stumbled upon this hotel when trying to find a hotel to stay so that we could check in our son to UCSF early the next morning. They were offering half price, so we decided to take a chance. We were pleasantly surprised. The staff was extremely helpful at the front desk, our rooms were very clean (important to us), and the computer they have available for use was in a good location and very handy. We decided to dine in their restaurant, and were so glad we did. It was one of the best meals I have had. It's pricey, so be prepared. Within walking distance to Union Square. The parking is the only issue here. You have to park in a pay-for-parking garage, so factor in that cost (we paid $-- for overnight). Our son had a room next to the street, so he did not get as much sleep as we did. Overall, a pleasant experience.

My friend and I stayed here for a week in mid December. The service and communication were great, the staff combined two bookings for us (we extended our stay and booked on Expedia and the hotel website). Very competant and efficient. Staff were all helpful and pleasant. The room was great- very clean and the beds and pillows were really comfortable. It is a great location, most hotels in the area require walking but this was close to the white house (-- mins walk) which was great. Expedia booking was great value (one night free). I have nothing bad to say about this hotel, would definately stay here again.

I booked a superior room online though a discout travel site and was upgraded to the slightly larger deluxe. I'm really glad we had the upgrade, because the room was not particularly large. It was a good size though with plenty of room for the queen bed and a desk. The room itself was nicely decorated. I loved the large flat-screen tv. The bathroom was ample size with tub-shower and large sink-vanity. The location was nothing spectacular, but it was definitaly convenient for getting to most parts of the city. Subway was just a few blocks away.

I was in town for a conference of an organization I belong to. I bought my room-airline ticket and rental car through another online search engine for $--- total. My stay was three nights. While I was lucky to get such a good deal, I was really surprised that parking, wifi, the gym-pool cost additional. Enough that it was the equivalent of another nights stay. Now compare that to the fact I stayed the previous night at a Super - that cost me $-- total. That room had the same sized bed, free breakfast (a hot one not just donuts and coffee) free wifi and the pool and weight room were free too. 
While I signed up for Hilton Honors, I am almost certain that I go out of my way to avoid this chain again. It was just very expensive

Asked for a high, quiet room with a view and had a room on the --th floor with a fantastic view of the Chrysler Building.Our only complaint was that we could still hear the very noisy sirens and horns on the quite busy street below,although to be fair to the Hotel,we didn't complain or ask to be moved!The whole area was busier than we expected given that this hotel is in a predominantly residential area.Easy walking distance to shops and Metro and staff friendly and efficient.

I stayed here twice during stop over's in and out of Chicago and i found the hotel to be perfectly adequate. Yes the rooms are quite small but then so are most airport hotels. The beds were very comfy and the room was nice an quiet. The bath rooms could have done with a smartening up but that was it really. Its a shame that they dont have an Exec Lounge like most Hilton airport hotels as this would have made the stay even better, although the sports bar was good, a nice atmosphere, friendly bar staff and good food. I will stay there again, the only negative aspect was the price increase from $--- on the saturday i stayed to $--- for the same room type just because it was mid-week. But hey you get more Hilton base points to maintain that all important Diamond card.

We had a great weekend getaway at the Back Bay Hotel. It's located right in downtown (just off Copley Square), so it's perfect for getting anywhere in the city and is surrounded by great restaurants and shopping. 
The service at the hotel was excellent--they had a terrific staff that was completely accommodating of all our needs and ready to help right away. It's the sort of service you'd expect at a hotel that cost twice as much. The rooms were clean, modern, and spacious with nice amenities, as well.

I was attending the auto fair at the speedway and all hotels were booked. I found this one on expedia and took it after reading the reviews. This place is definately top notch. I travel a lot and this was all around a great deal from start to finish!

I'm by no means a hotel snob, clean, friendly and comfortable is pretty much all I need in a short break. the Affinia Manhattan ticks all these boxes with a couple of proviso's.
The location is one block down from Penn Station on -th Ave, this makes for a much easier, quicker and cheaper arrival than by cab from JFK (about $- pp and --mins, depending on time of day). Check-in was very friendly and prompt and the lobby is quite nice too.
