I realize that this is a small hotel, but I don’t like eating my breakfast in a bar. Call me old fashioned. The bar area itself is too cramped to use comfortably, doubling as entrance from the hotel and the street. And the bar is poorly stocked. The Mixologist, while VERY nice, does not know how to make a proper Mint Julep or a proper Grasshopper. I ordered two martinis, and both glasses literally arrived more than half empty. When I asked (earnestly) where the rest of our martinis were (I actually thought the barkeep was going to bring a separate decanter as some bars do), she seemed confused.
The lovely two-story reception area is largely underutilized and the bar-dining area is far too mean. There is something wrong with a small hotel with such a large and well appointed registration lobby, and such a tiny bar and dining area. The second floor balcony overlooking the lobby is outfitted with tables and chairs that seemed perfunctory. I’d much rather have breakfast there, in quiet, overlooking the lobby.
The elevators are a bit of a mess as well. There are only two. They are heavily used by the very affable housekeeping staff to the point that it took us more than -- minutes several times to move from the first floor to the --th. We have stayed in many boutique hotels in which the staff must use the guest elevators, which is understandable. But this was by far the worst problem I have encountered. 
Our room was not made up one day when we returned at -:-- in the afternoon. When I called to request that it be serviced, I was told that housekeeping had until -pm to service rooms. When paying $--- a day, a client expects to hear an apology and promise for prompt service, not to be read the rules and regulations.
The turn down service did not properly service the bathroom. We consistently needed to call for towels, washcloths, soap, etc. Simply placing two chocolates on the bed stand is not turn down service for a pricey suite in boutique hotel. 
Add a large retractable awning to the roof deck to make it more appealing on hot summer days and evenings. We baked during the Thursday night music, which in itself was delightful. The Hotel Washington in DC has (or had) a great rooftop bar that looks onto the Treasury Building and the White House. In hot weather, water pours continuously over the canopy helping to cool the hot humid evenings. But a simple awning (or even tables with umbrellas) would be a good start. And the surface of the small bar that services the roof is stainless steel, which is red hot on a typically hot June day. It should be sealed wood.
I was really looking forward to staying at the Madison. My wife and I are no strangers to expensive and exclusive hotels. We are willing to pay, and have paid, far more than $----night for an excellent suite in an excellent hotel – sometimes triple the cost of the Madison. The Madison raises one's expectations, but can't even keep one's coffee cup filled at breakfast.
Some of these issues are easily fixed and I suspect will be. Others are more long term or systemic issues that may take time to address.

Wrapped up a weekend in NY, we stayed at the Yotel. The presentation and interior designs are pretty impressive. Its a pretty new property so the rooms felt new and clean. We stayed in a Queen two bunk room. The layout was comfortable and the view was impressive.
My annoyances with the room were mostly cosmetic but worth mentioning.
curtain controls are kind of hidden and not really obvious. 
The shower was large but there is no real division between the shower and bathroom floor so water gets out on the floor eventually. I always am annoyed with hotels that use this type of shower design, Its such a nuissance. Like even a small lip or drain along the edge would be great. Nothing is more annoying than going into the bathroom with socks and stepping on a puddle. Same sort of deal for the sink. Its a flat box basin, takes awhile for the water to find itself down the drain. Its mostly due to the design of the sink really. I'm sure the drain is just fine. 
I didnt like not having body lotion within the toiletries, there's two types of soaps to choose from but not one body lotion? Seems strange.
Also the bathroom doesnt lock. Not sure if that's just particular for this room but it would probably be an issue if i was bunking with a coworker or something. 
The highlights are, easy checking-in, you dont have to stand in line or deal with anyone, you just punch up your reservation on the self service kiosk and youre done, im a big fan of self check-in at airports so I love hotels that let you do that to check-in also, the rooftop area bar is great, the drinks are pretty good, pricey. But the view is fantastic, you get a feel for being in the big city.
I'd probably stay again if there was a good deal.

Overall, it's not bad but it's far from great.
Check-in was painfully slow. Thank God we got there before the -- airline employees behind us, but it still took -- minutes of standing in line. 
Immediately upon going up to our room, - young men who clearly walked in off the street were begging guests to let them into the locked indoor swimming pool. And they were behaving oddly, one standing at one end of the hall, and the other standing at the opposite end...I honestly felt like I was about to be robbed on the -th floor of the hotel. I reported it to security, who immediately responded, but the whole thing did not leave me feeling very safe and secure.
The room was nice enough, again nothing amazing. I did not feel like the maid did the best job...she clearly did not vacuum every day, and at least one day she forgot to empty our trash can. 
The air conditioning was miserably inconsistent, making it very difficult to sleep through the night.
I needed a postcard stamp one day, so went to concierge. For some reason, one of the women working behind the counter could not be bothered to look up and even acknowledge me, so I had to wait for the other to finish helping a guest. When she did help me, she was wonderful and pleasant, and simply gave me the postcard stamp at no charge. Little things like that do mean a lot to me, and I greatly appreciated it.
The location is fantastic for access to the BART, shopping, restaurants, etc. Everything else was standard for a Marriott. So in that sense, I can say it was --stars """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""average,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which is not necessarily a bad thing. But at $----night, it was nothing special.

Although we booked a suite for thre people they made us paying for an third bed.
We asked for additional bath products, they gave us the second choice quality.
Internet in our room is an extra!!! C'm on, even Mc donald's gives you free wi-fi!!!!
At night time the street isn't that attractive.

I travel constantly and am deliriously sick of the standard Marriott wallpaper, carpets, etc. I was so happy when I came to the Carlton in NYC, an Autograph property of Marriott, and discovered that Autograph hotels are really distinct. The service at the Carlton is great, the rooms and hallways beautiful, as are the lobby and the hotel bar. Very old fashioned. The rooms are not large, but they are nicely furnished, with a safe and very large screen flat tv. For Marriott Platinum and Gold members, the breakfast has few choices, but with AMAZING croissants, marmalade, and best of all fresh yogurt with fresh berries and granola brought to you from the kitchen. This is now my choice hotel in NYC, and the location gives you great access to different subway lines. My only complaint - no coffee maker in the room. But the coffee maker in the hotel business center made up for this!

My boyfriend and I stayed - nights over Columbus Day weekend. The view of Boston and the harbor is gorgeous. The room was clean, spacious, comfortable love seat, bed and desk. Although it's close to the airport, we heard very little plane or airport noise. 
Our room had an interior door connecting to the next room. We could hear the next door guests quite clearly (not so with the guests on the other side of us where there was no interior connecting door) and also room doors slamming and guests talking in the hallway while we were trying to sleep. We recently stayed at a Hyatt Summerfield Suites, where they have a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""quiet"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" policy, asking guests to be a bit quieter after -pm while talking in their rooms or in the hallway. Hyatt should consider a similar policy at all of its hotels.
We had breakfast Saturday morning. The food was good, but unfortunately the service was terrible. Our waiter was disorganized, he kept hanging out in the buffet area, we had to beg for a coffee refill. When our food arrived, we asked the food server for coffee, but he referred us to our waiter, saying he just delivered food. A waitress from a nearby table refilled our coffee, she was very friendly, and I think she felt sorry for us. 
The lobby staff were helpful and friendly, I appreciated that we got a late checkout when I asked for it, since our flight left in the late afternoon. Since we didn't have a car, we used the free shuttle to the subway and to the airport. Drivers were friendly, helpful, and the shuttle came within minutes, even to pick us up at the subway station to bring us back to the hotel.

One Washington Circle is a nice hotel. It has a good location, as the Georgetown is in the walking distance from the place. Also it's possible to walk to many places and to easily reach the most Must see of DC.
The hotel staff is friendly.The rooms are spatiouse, and have all facilities needed. The free internet is availbale in every room. The hotel cleaning ladies leave some surprises after cleaning the room, like chocholate etc. The breakfast in Circle Bistro is very good, one of the best I've seen in the hotels of middle price.
The hotel makes your stay at DC more pleasant.

My husband and I stayed here for a night while my parents watched our kids. The staff was very professional and helpful. We enjoyed the evening happy hour, having some wine before we left for dinner. We ate at Sambucas, which was an easy walk, but it was very cold. The free shuttle took us there, and we called to be picked up. Breakfast was pretty good as far as free ones go - one of the better ones I've had. The service was hands down the best though - the staff came and refilled my juice more than once for me!
The room was not very big - but as it was just me and my husband we didn't need a lot of space. The room was very nice and comfortable. The big garden tub was a nice touch too!

this place is awesome. walking distance to everything!!! small rooms but what do you expect, it is NY!! at least they tell you the square footage, so you are prepared. clean, friendly staff, perfect!!

We have stayed at the Chicago Trump a few times and have never been less than ---% thrilled with everything from our service and beautiful rooms to the fabulous food and tasty martinis. The rooms are spotless and oh so comfortable from the bedding (I am sheet snob), to the furnishing to sit back and enjoy the view. Pricier but if you are looking for truly spectacular, this is it.

Brand new JW Marriott in Indy. Stayed for busines and it was really nice. I expected it to be much nicer than a standard metropolitan Marriott. To me there was very little difference. 
I have no complaints, just wasn't blown away. Very nice, clean and good staff.
Higher Floors feature views of Statue of Liberty. Non-connecting rooms and rooms away from the elevator and ice machine are the quietest.

Just returned from a girls weekend in NYC. This hotel was perfect. We booked two King Rooms. Room #---- was really nice. Corner room with lots of windows. Room #---- was fine, with the exception of being near the elevator. Room was large for NY. Bathrooms are small but nice. Beds are really comfortable. In fact, the location of the hotel is extremely quiet at night. We hardly heard any sirens etc... Very different from the San Carlos Hotel we stayed at last year. Nice wine reception in the evening. Water and apples in the lobby area all day. Bellman were very nice and helpful. Grand Central is a couple of blocks up, very convenient for subway. Easy walk to Rock.Center area. Conceirge seemed a little rude, which I did think was odd! Only complaint, was one of the elevators was not working and the lines-wait times for elevator were extremely long and also that one of our rooms was not ready until -:-- or after. It was disappointing since we arrived at the hotel at --:-- that morning and were told to come back around -:--. 
Ate dinner before the show (Grease) at Trattoria Trecolori on --th Street. Dinner was really good and prices extremely reasonable. The restaurant is adjacent to Brooks Atkins Theatre, so it is the perfect location. Moonstruck is a small diner type restaurant around the corner from the hotel. Reasonable priced breakfast and lunch. Also ate at Bar American on --nd (Bobby Flay Restaurant). It was just okay. I wouldn't eat there again or recommend it to friends.
I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone and would stay here again. Location was perfect!

I have nothing to complain about except I wanted more 'glamour' for my families' vacation. The room was very nicely appointed, albeit small for a family of - (why do so many hotels think that - double beds are good for - people, why not have queens?) The service was excellent, and mostly friendly or neutral, never bad. The location was good. It was just not special in any way, considering the money paid. Just felt like a very nice business hotel..... maybe that is all it is supposed to be.... where I would have preferred a destination luxury hotel.

Although the hotel is a little run down, overall the room was clean and comfortable with all the necessary accoutrements. The location, close to the Wilshire Theatre, Metro train and bus services is great. Plenty of options for dining, especially if you like Korean. Because of its location It is a great base to explore Los Angeles with the La Brea Tar Pits just down the road and a myriad of other attractions easily accessible by public transport. A liitle TLC to the hotel would definitely make it even better.

We stayed here one night. It's a fantastic location. We stayed in a room with two queen sized beds. The room was big and the beds were so comfortable. Parking was --.-- per night, which was very reasonable. The only problem was there was a group of partyers on our floor. Security was good in quieting them down quickly. They broke one of the two elevators. If you are afraid of elevators, these aren't the ones for you. Get a room on the first or second floor. It's a convenient location with great service. We didn't try the restaurant, but it looked clean and it was busy.

It's the Waldorf and an iconic NYC landmark. Yes, it's a bit outdated, but the rooms are a little larger than most of the other hotel rooms that I've stayed in. Bed was very comfortable, lots of big fluffy pillows. Our bathroom was fine. The bathroom cabinets are outdated, but no issues whatsoever. The only downside for us was that it was hard to regulate the temperature and we felt a little stuffy.
I thought the hotel staff was very friendly. There was a NYC buzz about it with tons of people milling about. We also had a drink at The Bull and Bear, which was really nice. 
And finally, extremely convenient to all of the major stuff you want to see.

I found this hotel to be a brilliant stopover on our way from New Zealand to the UK. The staff were very helpful and lovely. The rooms were clean and tidy if a little worn and dated. The pool was clean with lots of towels and the kids spent a good couple of hours getting rid of pent up energy. The restaurant The Daily Grill was great - family friendly, nice food and reasonably quick.
Definitely recommend

Everytime I am in San Francisco, I'll never miss a visit to Scala and Starlight at Sir Francis Drake. The service at both places had been excellent, until my last visit between August -----, ----.
It was an unplanned visit and therefore I didn't bring along my exclusive dresses, only jeans, skirts and sneakers...but I thought that shouldn't stop me from enjoying myself.
On one of the nights, I handed over my jeans jacket and a handbag to the Hostess at the Cloak Room to keep as I wanted to dance. When I went back to collect them, I saw the Hostess kept my things on the floor, where there were plenty of hangers available, while my companion's jacket was kept nicely hang up. I was rather upset and cross and just refused to give her any tips, although my companion offered the tips on my behalf. 
I don't know what was the reason for her to treat me with such a manner, but I thought that was very disgraceful for a reputable hotel like Sir Francis Drake, and I should let everyone know about it. 
I will still visit the Scala and Starlight when I visit San Francisco, but surely will not consider staying at Sir Francis Drake Hotel.

In a word - NOISY. 
A new hotel is being constructed out back. They start at - a.m. sharp and don't end until late at night. Every Day. 
I'd wait until it's done before staying there. If you only need one bed, they can move your room to the front of the hotel where it's not as bad. If you need more than one bed, though, you're out of luck.
The hotel is nice, restaurant has very good food and otherwise the stay was fine.

Had a one night stay here in mid-October on a layover.
The room was expensive - over $--- US-night, and I guess I expected a little more from it. Indeed I've stayed at the airport Hilton for much less, and have gotten much more.
\But - having said that, there were few surprises, the room was comfortable, large (although a bit awkward in terms of the TV placement, and served its purpose.
We did check out the hotel-exercise area, but it was packed with kids so we gave it a miss. Likewise, the business centre was packed as well, and extremely hot (as noted in another review). I waited so long for one page to load that I just gave up - not worth my time. It appears to be a common problem - they really should do something about it. An early check-out saw us quickly on our way.
I have few expectations for places like this, and I guess this hotel met most, if not all of them. It would be nice to have a surprise on occasion, however - just something that makes me want to come back to places like these.
Would I stay here again? Sadly no, I will choose the airport Hilton or another brand next time.

We just returned from a -- day vacation where we flew out of San Jose, California. After searching the internet for a hotel we could park our car with shuttle to and from the airport, we settled on the Sleep Inn on Harris Way in San Jose. We stayed there the night before our flight out and were taken to the airport. 
When I made the reservation I specifically asked if it was necessary for us to stay a night on our return in order to be picked up at the airport and taken to our car, which was left parked at the Sleep Inn. I was assured that this was not necessary. We made arrangments with the hoitel for the pick up at the airport -- days later. We were told to call the hotel after we picked up our baggage and they would send someone to get us. 
We called immediately upon picking up our baggage and we told at that time they would NOT send someone to pick us up as we did not have a reservation to stay the night on our return, even though I had specifically addressed this before our departure. There we were, stranded at the airpot, tired and our car many miles away. Luckily we were able to contact a friend in the area who picked us up and took us to our car, but I am still pretty steaming about this situation. The Sleep Inn charges extra for this hotel shuttle-parking service, which we paid and then not to received the service you paid and arranged for is unforgiveable. Beware of being ripped off and stranded by this hotel.

I booked the Chancellor Hotel after reading the many many good reviews on this site. Originally I wanted to stay in Fishermans Wharf which is where I had stayed on a previous visit quite a few years ago. I am so glad I changed my mind. I much preferred Union Square. When we were walking back to the cable cars from the Alcatraz trip at night I noticed how quiet Fishermans Wharf got.
The Chancellor is great value for money. I didn't find the rooms small. Maybe they were for American standards but they were a normal size compared to European standards.
The beds were super comfortable. I loved being able to open the window too. I prefer fresh air to air conditioning where possible.
The bathroom was nicely stocked and I thought the rubber duck was a great touch. The deep bath was fantastic and not something I have found much in hotels.
We had breakfast at the hotel most mornings and it was great everytime. 
The coffee and cookies were also a great touch. 
Finally, the staff in the hotel were always friendly and helpful. A few times we asked for directions to places and they were very happy to help.
Next time I stay in San Francisco I will most definately stay here.

Checking in we were told our room wasn't ready. We asked again at the next counter and they gave us our room. Staff isn't well trained and depending upon who you speak with you get different answers. The room was dirty and dusty with hair in the shower. The hallway didn't looknlike it had seen a vacuum in days. It took -- minutes to get down to the lobby via the elevator . This happened on several occasions. The day we left there was an inflatable rat -- ft. tall outside the hotel protesting the hotel for having bed bugs and for being greedy. The inflatable pretty much sums up our stay.

As other reviewers have mentioned, rooms are tiny, but ours was fine for an overnight stay. Most important to us was the quick walk from Grand Central to the hotel. We arrived very early and were able to store our luggage until check in time. When we checked out we were able to store our luggage until we were ready to leave the city. Breakfast was fine. If you don't go for the complimentary breakfast scene, there are a couple of breakfast places within a few steps. There's a twenty four hour pharmacy nearby on Fifth Avenue. This came in handy for toothbrushes. Although the little card in the room said that common toiletries were available from the front desk, when I asked for a toothbrush the desk clerk said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""we don't have any."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" At check in time the young woman on the desk was very helpful when I came back after checking out because I had left something in the room. There were lots of channels on the TV, including TCM, so if you need to rest before going out for the night you can watch a classic movie,

We reserved and pre-paid for - non-smoking rooms. When we arrived we were told they only had smoking rooms available-even though we pre-paid for non-smoking rooms. The rooms were so small we couldn't even open the door completely and they reeked of cigarette smoke. One of the rooms had water pouring from the bathroom ceiling through the light fixture. When we complained to the front desk clerk she said there was nothing she could do. We moved to another hotel. The web site picture are very misleading and the hotel personnel service is very poor.

The room was very clean and spacious. It looked like it should have been double the price considering the custom touches to our room and the lobby's decor. It was very quiet at night considering the downtown location and the amount of people staying around us. The pool on top of the building is cool for checking out the views. The breakfast (in the bar) was excellent and free is always great. However, the bar area needs more tables and chairs during the breakfast and free drinks time.

Stayed at the Embassy Suites Riverwalk for - nights and would definitely stay there again if returning to San Antonio. The room was huge, clean and quiet. I was at the very end of the hall on the --th floor and couldn't hear any of my neighbors. There was a large living room area that included: the sink, microwave, fridge, table, couch, and flat screen TV. It was such a nicely laid out space that made you feel at home and gave you some room to work and sit and not feel like you are constantly in your bedroom. Plus, I never heard the refrigerator making noise during the night because I was able to close the bedroom door. The bedroom was very large and had a small desk and another flat screen TV and ample drawer-closet space. The bathroom was clean, well lit and had a great walk in shower. The free breakfast at the hotel is wonderful. They have an excellent selection of hot, made to order food as well as cereals, bagels and fruit. Plus they have really good coffee which is rare at most complimentary breakfasts. 
The front desk staff were extremely friendly and were very enthusiastic about helping with directions. A staff member even walked out of the hotel with me to show me where to pick up the trolley. After a few days in San Antonio, you may get tired of tex mex and BBQ so think about eating at Luke's, the restaurant attached to the hotel. It serves amazing German food. I had one of the best meals of my entire trip there. Wonderful spatzle and schnitzel. 
The hotel is very convenient to all things San Antonio. The Riverwalk is right outside, Houston street has lovely shops and restaurants and leads you straight to the Alamo or to the Mercado depending in which way you go. Plus, you can hop on one of the city trolleys right outside of the hotel if you are tired from walking. Parking is the only downside to the hotel. Parking is always a bit pricey the closer you get to the Riverwalk, but you only have the option to valet park at the Embassy Suites. You do get in and out privileges and my car was always ready when I needed it and in great condition so no complaints there. 
Overall, I really enjoyed my stay. It was comfortable, convenient, clean and relaxing. I would definitely suggest it to anyone headed to San Antonio.

I loved staying at this hotel because it's downtown and walking distance to Pike Market (a must see and where the original Starbucks is located that hasn't changed since the '--s!). It's right on the water so the balcony views are incredible. Having a walk-on balcony makes the place feel more like home than a hotel. The hotel has a good restaurant and a Starbucks is just across the street. 
This is the first hotel whose shampoo, conditioner, and lotion I've used because it's all from BATH & BODY WORKS. How cool is that? You know it's good stuff then. :) The hotel was very clean and quiet. At home I have to sleep with a loud fan on to block out noise (I'm a light sleeper), but I never heard any voices or loud noises that woke me up. That's rare for me at hotels! 
Negatives: 
- There is no wireless internet, so you have to plug into an ethernet card on the wall to access internet, so you must sit at the desk where the cord is- no internet surfing or working on the bed! Internet is $--.-- a day, just fyi.
- The bed was a little too firm for me, but the bedding and pillows were incredibly comfortable, so that helped tremendously.
- There is no mini fridge in the room to store drinks or food. 
Even though there were a few negatives, they weren't deal breakers, and I would stay here again! A great place to stay for your first time in Seattle like it was for me!

Stayed one night and got the heck out! Dirty rooms, rugs not cleaned, poor TV reception and the staff seemed liked they could literally 'care less'
about most all complaints! Cheap price, but this place is not even on a par with a poor Motel -. Avoid this dump!!!

The room was ideal for a family of three. The hotel was able to provide accommodation that can be hard to find in NY- a spacious room, a kitchenette, a great Gym, a good restaurant, comfortable beds and no noisy corridors. All combined with friendly staff and a reasonable rate. So we will definitely be back

We booked the Affinia after finding a great deal on Travelzoo and were very impressed by the value for money. The service provided by the hotel was very friendly. The reception and lounge area was quite nice. It was our first trip to NYC and the hotel provided a great base. I would book room ---- again.
PROS:
- enormous comfortable bed
- kitchen in the room
- located right in the heart of Manhattan just by Penn Station-Madison Square Garden
- fitness centre
- newspapers in the lobby
CONS: 
- $-- per day for Wifi
- The shower was tiny; only had room for one person with no turning.
- Old tv
This is a very nice classy old hotel. It is in a accessible part of town. The services are very good. But, it is very pricey, frankly over proced for what is provided.
Stayed here last weekend...everything was perfect! If you're looking for a quiet, very clean hotel at a great price...this is it. The one bedroom suite was wonderful.

Stayed there in a king size single room ----. Top floor in the corner. Never heard a peep from anyone. Nice size, clean bathroom. The tv channel selections were the only downfall but hopefully you are not there for that. DVD player was also included. Attentive staff. Good room service. Across the street to a line of great asian restaurants.

My wife and I stayed for - nights in September this year for our Honeymoon. It was our first time in New York so we needed to be central to all the sights. 
The position of the hotel was perfect. Close to Time Square and Central park and walking distance to most places of interest.
The staff were all helpful and freindly and the breafast was great. 
The room was very clean and spacious, the bathroom door has seen better days but I read elsewhere that changes will be taking place. 
We would definately return to this hotel.

Great hotel in a great location in Austin - the Sixth St bar district is right behind the hotel, with great restaurant-bar options, although there is definitely a younger crowd there. About an ---- minute walk from Colorado--th area with great places for the young professionals and the more mature clientel. The hotel itself is really nice, with a small outdoor wading pool-lounging area with stone staircases and walkways. It has a pretty nice gym with windows for natural light, and the staff were very helpful, and really seemed like they wanted to make the stay easier and pleasant for you. The valet service is great too, if you call just before you go down, your car will be waiting for you. Would definitely stay there again.

Nicely redone and clean hotel but that is the extent of the positive comments 
Young family for an early flight Sunday morning and found out the quiet time started at midnight. Rowdy drunk ----- year old crowd having a good time but at others expense, not a good idea for an airpot hotel .
Had a large room at the back of the hotel ground floor by the main a-c unit and could not sleep all night as I could hear it start up through the single pane windows about every -- minutes
Seemed like there was a gang element at the hotel (ie clean shaven , muscle bound tatoo'd young men driving tinted out sports car in and out of the hotel all night) Police showed up at about midnight on force to deal with some problem.

This is my second time to stay in the Pod. I was very pleased with my first stay back in December ----. This time, they booked me in a corner room with spotty wireless signal so I called the front desk a couple of times to get it fixed. When it was apparent that it could not be fixed, the very efficient gentleman at the front desk, (his name is Mikee) was very kind to transfer me to another room as quickly as he could. Even if I was disappointed with my first room, Kudos to Mikee for resolving the issue quickly and efficiently. He has shown a great service of retaining a customer. I will always have the Pod in mind whenever I visit New York. Highly recommended!
Suggestions: I suggest to put a floor length mirror behind the door. I don't think it will take up any space. A small fridge in the room will be nice to have. Other than that, I give this hotel a thumbs up!

I was in San Diego in the past month for a trip to visit a friend and I chose to stay at the maina inn and suites for - days. I should say that the place is really well maintained and the staff is very friendly and helpful. My flight reached at -- in the morning and Dhiman who was at the front desk was kind enough to give me an early check in. And if that wasn’t enough he also let me have the continental breakfast they serve every morning. I was really impressed by the customer service he provided. The room was in great condition as well. They had a fridge and a microwave in there as well. Marina Inn is located in a very convenient location. Little Italy is close by, there’s a ---- right next door, a rite aid and several restaurants as well. The Gaslamp district is just a - min drive. Overall I had a great experience and hope this review helps tourists looking for great hotel experience.

We stayed at the Palomar when it first opened, having first discovered the Kimpton chain in Salt Lake City, and have stayed three times since -- we wouldn't think of staying anywhere else in Chicago. The location can't be beat -- easy walk to museums, Magnificent Mile, gallery district and best eats (don't overlook Sable, the hotel's restaurant, great for pre-theater or late night). Smartly appointed rooms. You can't help but see a great sense of pride in the quality of service and facility from everyone on the staff, from the bellhops to the restaurant waiters to the able desk attendants. No hotel or chain is more LGBT-friendly. Be sure to sign up for Kimpton's InTouch Program.

This was my first trip to San Fran and I am so very glad that I choose Inn at the Opera. I had an interview in the area and attended SF Opera...it was perfect for everything that I needed it to be. Walking distance to the opera, shops, restaurants, etc...location was perfect for me. The hotel was very nice, my room was clean, cozy and comfortable, and the continental breakfast was great too. I don't have a gripe only this...be aware that there is only one elevator in the hotel and it does not run fast, but it's charming...so just something to be aware of. Otherwise, great stay and highly recommended.

I was traveling with my brother on this trip. We booked this hotel knowing how poorly it was rated in tripadvisor; we were looking for a reasonably-priced downtown hotel for just one night.

The hot water worked fine in my bathroom, but my brother's bathroom could muster only a trickle.

The three tiny elevators were not nearly sufficient, especially during peak times, like - or - a.m., when everyone was heading out for the day.
We had breakfast in the restaurant off the lobby; it was actually just fine, which is to say, it appeared to be unassociated with the Travelodge itself.
The bellman did have the ability to check your bags for you, and could even give you claim tickets for them. We were amused and a bit concerned to find that he didn't seem to check the claim ticket numbers when giving back bags. One lady asked for hers, which she described as a pink bag with a red ribbon on it; the bellman brought out a maroon bag, sans ribbon, for her consideration, but I guess she was kind of attached to her own luggage. He finally asked her to go into the storage room and show him the one she was after.

Some reviewer mentioned that the wooden shades didn't block the light. I guess their shades must have been broken, because I found that they worked great, and I like my hotel rooms very dark. 
I also ordered room service one morning and it was brought up in about ----- minutes and was very good. Yeah, it's expensive...it's hotel room service, so what. 
The pool and workout area are also very nicely done. I wish that the outside patio that extends from the pool were on a higher floor rather than just the -rd, but then again it was raining most of the time, so it wouldn't have mattered for my stay anyway.
The only piece of advice I have is this. If you're getting to the hotel by cab instead of your own vehicle, don't drag all your luggage in through the main enterance at the corner of -rd and Howard. Instead, go down Howard about --- feet to where it says """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Wheels"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and go in that way. If you go in the main enterance and it's after -pm, you will feel like an idiot b-c you'll be dragging your luggage through a mob of people and probably try to check in at the bar. The hotel is a great retreat and you'll have fun as long as you like the hip-trendy type of hotel. Check out their website and know what you're getting into...if you're older and don't want to be around a bunch of young professionals, probably better off at a Union Square hotel, which is really only a few blocks away.

When you arrive at any hotel and they ask you if you want to sign up for a hotel points card, make sure you do it. I just stayed at this wonderful hotel for - nites using my club carlson points and I didn't have to pay a dime! The hotel is right in the heart of midtown on --nd and broadway. From the moment you walk in, the staff is very nice, very informative and always willing to lend a helping hand or advice, The room is huge for a hotel in manhattan with complimentary bottled waters, a firm bed and nice clean room and bathroom. When you stay in manhattan and if you love shopping like my fiancee does, you come and drop your bags off in the room and head out again. Macy's and manhattan mall are yards away - and if you have the willingness to walk, take the initiative and walk. We walked all the way to central park east on park ave and all the way north to wall street. In conclusion, a very nice stay at the Radisson.

We stayed at this hotel -- years ago, and had an incredible experience - all the good things we'd ever heard about the Ritz experience. The facility is the same great location and old European style (refreshed in - years ago), but the service has changed. The valet-bellman was efficient but not welcoming. No more staff these days to open the front doors and greet you. Dining area used for breakfast was too small and couldn't accommodate all the guests, and the staff seemed somewhat disorganized. Food remains very expensive ($-- for an omelette at breakfast). Internet is a separate charge, which doesn't seem like a luxury experience. I still give it - stars for the room and the location, which are both very good relative to other options in the city - but it's a low - stars relative to price and not meeting the expectation of service that the Ritz Carlton promises.

This is our second visit to Philadelphia in a couple of months (see my review for Windsor Suites) as we liked it so much the first time we wanted to come back for our Anniversary. 
I chose Club Quarters based on location and price. When I booked, I noticed that for a bit more money you can get a Superior room, so I booked it. I'm glad I did! Room was bigger than what the standard would be, had really high ceilings (almost --'!) and a big beautiful window. Now, some amenities might not be to everyone's liking, but this is what we got.
Queen Bed
Table-Desk
LCD TV
Kitchenette with coffee maker, microwave, refrigerator, sink, cabinets with utensils and plates.
Bathroom is small with a shower - no tub.
Yes, as some reviewers noticed that the check-in process is different because you have kiosks and less """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""member services"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" staff, but it works. Another unique feature is that all room items are located in closets on selected floors so if you need linens, coffee, creamer, irons, etc. you can just go to the closets.
Fitness room is average, but I saw a sign on the elevator that indicates you can request an eliptical machine or stairclimber for your room!
In house restaurant is a bit more upscale (in pricing), but if you are a guest and have the bill charged to your room they'll give you a --% discount.
And, all of this is housed in an historic building on a nice street corner.
I'm glad I chose the room I did at a price less than the major chains. But, if you are used to - or - star hotels, this might not be for you.

My mother and I wanted to take a quick mini vacation in Chicago on a tight budget. We booked this hotel at a GREAT price. Hotel Staff is Super friendly. Hotel is very trendy and hip and well decorated w a beach theme. It has a small restaurant w a great selection and great prices for a hotel. The also have a nice mid size bar right down in the lobby. Our room had a great view, Comfy bed, clean room. I liked that the hotel had plenty of reading material of attractions in the area, if you ask the staff as to where to go and eat, they will be more than happy to direct you and they also have some coupons for restaurants in the area. They also offer Free Wifi which many hotels in Chicago do not and right next to the hotel there is a parking garage where you can pay to leave your car overnight. It is within walking distance to Many places to eat and several pharmacies, supermarket. Super convenient location and there is a train stop about --- blocks from hotel. Will def stay in this hotel again.

I really enjoyed staying at the Amalfi. The decor is beautifully done and brought back wonderful memories of my travels to the Amalfi coast and Capri. The breakfast was great. You could get a plate full of food and coffee and take it back to your room. The location is nice for shopping on the Magnificent Mile or going to the park. I found the staff to be very friendly and accommodating.

We stayed at the Salisbury from -- to -- May ----. We booked it through Thomas Cook and chose the Salisbury due to its excellent location. I did read the reviews on the site regarding the noise, showers and lifts so I was a bit dubious. When we checked in to the hotel, we asked for rooms at the back which they provided with no problem. The room was spacious and the beds is a great size and just what you need after a day of sight seeing. There were times when you did have to wait for the lifts which is usually around breakfast time but it certainly was not an excessive wait. With regards to the showers, we had no problem with temperature and it was a lovely size of bathroom. 
The breakfast was great value and for $-, you had cereals, donuts, bagels, toast, fruit salad and as much tea, coffee, fruit juices you can have. It is served on paper plates but this was no problem at all and did not affect the taste of the food or drink at all. In fact, it was quite nice not to have waiters keep coming to collect items from your table and you could eat at your leisure and go whenever you please. 
The location of the hotel was great, and Times Square is a few blocks down the road. I would recommend going on a bus tour. We went on the Citysights Tour (people in bright yellow jackets!) and we found it enjoyable, interesting and so convenient. We used the bus for two days and boarded at Time Sq, left the bus at the Empire State, boarded it again to visit Ground Zero and board again to come home. We never waited more than - minutes for a bus. I would recommend doing the Uptown and Downtown Tour. I would warn people though that when walking up to Times Square, representatives from tour companies will try and stop you and sell the tours to you. We learned quickly to just say 'We have already done it' (which was before we booked our tour) and they will leave you alone. They do work on commission so they will try their hardest to stop you. 
When going to Bloomingdales, I would recommend eating at the -- Carrots which is on the -th floor. The food was absolutely delicious and their frozen yogurts are legendry!! Red Eye Dinner, which is on the way to Times Square is lovely also and is perfect for a evening meal.
Al in all, it was an enjoyable holiday and would certainly recommend this hotel to everyone.

I travel often to Chicago, and this is my preferred hotel. I typically love it. This time, I was given (two!) unlovely rooms - the first overlooking a roof and walls, the second a parking garage. Ok, can't have a great room every time. The hallway was dank, the sounds from inside the hotel were incredibly loud even in the room and the toilet literally did not flush. They did send someone right away for that, but he didn't fix the shower that did not drain (my tolerance limit for this is above the ankles - I don't call under the water creeps up my legs, which is just gross. It did the entire five days I was there). There were no toiletries in the room where I did eventually stay - ok, sometimes these too get overlooked - but the front desk staffer I asked for some was downright rude. I almost complained to the management, but who has time for that? The workout room's water dispenser was a leaking mess, but he wasn't interested in hearing about that either. Guess this was a wake up call that even our favorite hotels aren't always on their best game. I'll give these guys one more shot, then move on. Again, this place is generally the bee's knees. Maybe it's just the comparison that made it seem so slovenly.

This past weekend I had my first (and last) visit to the Omni Shoreham. I've stayed at Omnis in a number of other cities and have had some wonderful treatment, so I assumed I would have a similar experience at the Shoreham. Unfortunately, that's not the case. I made my reservations over a week in advance, and having read other reviews here, decided to request a garden view room. The day before my trip I called to confirm that request was noted. The room was not ready at check in time. I was told I would have to wait to get a garden view and that they were preparing one on the -th floor. It was -:-- (check in is -:--) when I finally got a call that the room was ready. I returned to the hotel and was slightly confused when they gave me a keycard for a room on the -th floor. When I got to the room, the view did not face a garden, but rather, a series of ventilation shafts on a roof and the opposite interior side of the building. I returned to the front desk and was first told that no other rooms were available, in spite of overhearing another guest next to me checking in who had just asked for, and been given, an upgrade to a garden view with balcony while I was standing there. I asked to see the manager and she also said there were no other rooms available in the entire hotel, then when I mentioned what I had just heard, she somehow found a room open on the same floor but the other side of the building (no balcony). I asked for an upgrade for the inconvenience since she didn't offer any, but she said the best she could do would be a breakfast voucher. When I got to that room, the bathroom door didn't shut. I was sick of dealing with the front desk at that point and just asked for maintenance to please come and fix it, which they did. I also wondered why I never got my beverage or newspaper selection card since I have been a Select Guest member for - years and this is the first time that perk was neglected, nor did the turn down service you normally get with that program happen. To end the visit, check out also provided a surprise. The desk staff tried to charge me a fee for using the treadmill in the fitness center. That fee is a.)not posted in the fitness center, b.)on any reservation confirmation or hotel information, or c.)the bill that is placed beneath your door on the morning you are checking out. It's charged to you as you are about to leave, so check your final bill if you stay here. I won't need to since I will stay elsewhere on future visits.

I read the five stellar reviews and have to disagree strongly with the glowing reviews of this hotel. Yes, it is new and with that come lots of problems. The worst is the air conditioning vent., It blows all the time, and you CANNOT turn it off. That's for supposedly green reasons. How can that be? The thing blows in every room ----. That's insane. So you have generally cold air blowing on your face all night long. Not fun. and doesn't exactly make for restful sleep. The restaurant is horrible. The food is well below average and quite expensive. We had breakfast and it was barely edible. The pool deck is closed and not slated for opening for several more months. The stairwell is locked from the inside, so if you get in, you can't get out anywhere but the bottom floor but there's no notice of that. They try to not make up the room or bring you towels unless you specifically ask for clean towels. 
On the good side, the staff is polite and generally helpful. They try hard to rectify the myriad problems, but ultimately there's only so much they can do. the gym is well maintained and the free bottled water is a nice touch. I think what was most disappointing is that the hotel looks really nice but below the surface there lay hidden a lot of problems and they really interfere with a pleasant stay. Wish I could have been more positive.

The rooms were nice- clean, spacious, and a good value. However, that is the only nice thing I can say about the place. All four of the people I dealt with were either incompetent or just unhelpful. They didn't reserve the type of rooms that we wanted. As a result, we had small children in the room above us running around at -am making enough racket to wake up my parents. After the first night, we tried to switch rooms but couldn't. They also locked us out of our rooms after the first night because they had our rooms reserved for only one night instead of two we had actually made the reservation for. When my father spoke with the people at the front desk, they were unhelpful and wouldn't take any responsibility. The manager was out of the weekend and so we couldn't speak with him because we were checking out on Sunday. We were offered no discount or compensation for the inconveniences they had caused.
The Dolphin is family owned and operated with a friendly staff. It is clean, quiet, centrally located to downtown, to tourist attractions and restaurants. It is very low priced.

Having two sisters living in the Austin area means I come here often. As soon as I stayed here I knew I found my home away from home. The staff is excellent, rooms comfortable and clean. The free breakfast is great too. 
My family has stayed here multiple times and each visit keeps us coming back again and again.
Thanks for making my visits so comfortable
Billy

Yes the rooms are small, the stairs are steep and the toilets are down the hall, but if you stay at the Chelsea Lodge, you're in a great neighbourhood, you're not paying an arm and a leg, and you're minutes from a subway stop. The place is charming, central, clean and great value. What more do you want in New York?!!
Tip: For great coffee, turn right as you exit the hotel, cross over -th and walk half a block and you'll find Cafe Grumpy. A quick coffee and muffin-pastry and you're good to go for the day.

We stayed here for one night using Marriott Rewards Points. The hotel is, as stated by others, an oasis in Times Square. We were upgraded to a beautiful suite on the --th floor (room ----). The furnishings are very hip and modern. Check-in is right off the street and very convenient. The elevator takes you to the lobby level which is beautifully furnished. There is a bar, a comfortable seating area and the R Lounge, which sits overlooking Times Square. The Lounge also serves as the breakfast area for concierge level guests. Another elevator in the lobby takes you to your room floor. Our upgraded room wasn't ready when we arrived at - p.m., so we were given coupons for lunch in the R Lounge. The suite itself was very spacious with - bathrooms, a king bed and a separate living area with sofa bed. We had a great view of -th avenue and all the billboards. Even though you are in Times Square, we never heard any noise. The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom had a large walk-in shower. All the room amenities were great. Right after we arrived, a maid knocked on our door and brought us ice and chocolates. Never had that happen before in any hotel. We had room service after the show at Radio City (the Rockettes are fabulous, don't miss it). The food was okay. We have stayed at several Marriott properties in New York City (Marquis, Courtyard, Hotel --), but this one is the BEST. There is something to be said for the smaller, boutique style hotel. If you are used to larger, more impersonal hotels, you may not like this one. For our money or points, this is where we will stay again. The staff is friendly 
and accommodating. You absolutely cannot beat the location, and the view from the R Lounge is spectacular. The best thing about this hotel is the calm you experience when returning from a hectic environment. Try to get the best rate available and always ask for an upgrade at check-in. Better yet, join Marriott Rewards and stay for points.

This is one of the classiest Renaissance that I have ever stayed at (stark contrast with the one in Northbrook IL). I was extremely pleased with my stay. The hotel is ideally situated in the bustling South Michigan district across from Grant park but once inside, it is very quiet and peaceful. The room was a decent size and came in with some very fancy amenities - a massage lounger, Bose wave radio and in-built TV in the bath. I would take off --- of a point for the odd shape of the concierge lounge which does not have enough seats but all in all a great stay and would stay here again in a heartbeat when in Chicago.

Stayed here for two nights with my fiancee and staff were fantastic, rooms were extremely clean and comfortable and can't help to feel that we had a great location in the city!
A wonderful city is complemented by a wonderful hotel and for once it is nice to see a huge chain hotel pay attention to the important bits; customer service and satisfaction.
Only disadvantage is that there is no free parking, but hey show me a city which has free overnight parking!

Stayed - nights on business. Nothing really bad, but not so great either, which is disappointing for $--- a night. Details...
GOOD:
--Location is excellent if you want to be near Times Square, its right there.
--Staff was very friendly and helpful
--Free high speed internet (lots of places in the area charge for it now)
--Rooms are clean and decent
--Bed was comfortable
BAD:
--Rooms are smallish, old outdated and in some cases broken furniture
--Lots of noise from outside the room
--Poor value for the price
--Workout room is small, equipment not in great shape
Everything in the area is pricey of course, but honestly, you can go $--- cheaper and stay at a similar star-level property like the Holiday Inn, and get a room just as good or even a little better. So unless they are running a deal, I can't really recommend this property.

We made our reservations through priceline, and so we were happily surprised to be at a holiday inn! the room was huge, the bed was WONDERFULLY comfortable, and the service at the front desk was great. There was some kind of conference going on at the same time we were staying there, but we didnt notice anything at all! We did have a maid start to open our door and come in while we were still sleeping.... which was a bit jarring, but didnt spoil the experience!

This property is a block or two south of the National Mall, a block from the Metro, surrounded by office buildings. The hotel is an older Holiday Inn, but the lobby appears to be renovated. My room was large, bright, facing the north side, so was fairly quiet (south side faces railroad tracks, so can be noisier). While the room was pretty dated, the room was clean, had a small fridge, flat screen TV; as others have noted, the shower pressure was terrific (probably old-style showerheads, so will be gone when renovated) Wireless internet is free, worked well. The fitness center is adequate-bright, but with some pretty dated equipment. There is a CVS and a couple of fast food places down the block.
Overall, this is a perfectly fine place to stay in DC-it's convenient, old but kept up, and has what you need. I would stay here again.

Stayed just one night but the staff was great in all aspects. We arrived too early to check in but they kept our luggage so we didn't have to drag it with us around Seattle. The shuttle service was quick and easy and they would take you or pick you up anywhere within their radius. Only problem was that I had made the reservation a couple months in advance so the six of us could share a two-bedroom suite and that didn't happen. We ended up with a one-bedroom suite and another room. They had overbooked their large suites. That was disappointing. The facility was clean and well kept and, like I said, the staff was very friendly and apologetic about the room not being what we had reserved and tried hard to make up for the mistake someone made. Breakfast was pretty good, better than most. We would stay again.

March - - --
-- yo well travelled mom and -- yo daughter, looking to see as much as possible and visit a few colleges.
We reserved via a third party online service and got a variable rate from --- to ---, total taxes-service included came out to ----.--. What we got was two double beds in a room on the --st floor. Nothing extra. The veiw included was to the north, --st street I believe. 
This is an excellant choice for location, the subway at rockerfeller is just past St. Patricks (about - minute walk) and the Grand Central is an easy stroll south. We walked to Central Park, a bit distant but doable, and to Time Square frequently during the stay. In the mornings we were across the block from a star bucks and-or bakery. The concierge was very good, no problems with asking for a double room and no hidden charges.
I had expected a small room, but it was roomy, large sink-vanity, tub and toilet. The dresser was large enough to accomodate both our wardrobe and the two large suitcases we brought were stashed out of the way without any problem.
Except for the first night, we never ran into the maid who had our rooms clean each afternoon and again turned down when we returned from a show. The bellmen were the most friendly I have encountered in this city. The main entrance is beautiful and a very nice place to meet friends. We did not dine at the hotel but would love to do so in the future. 
Internet service was great, the maid remembered my preferences for type of chocolate and ice everyday. 
I would definitly return to this hotel.
Cons: The price of room service-snacks is rather ridiculous compared to the room fee but going out was very easy.

You might find an inexpensive room here, but make sure you include breakfast ($--) and parking ($--). Not even internet was included in my stay ($--)... it get's expensive!
Everything is clean and works well, but the hotel is somehow dark and seems worn down. I did not get the same feeling as I got at Doubletree in Amsterdam where everything seemed new and modern. 
You get the cookie when you check in, but a smile is not included.

We stayed here three nights in suite with terrace. The room (----) and it's fittings were great the only problem was the noise due to the fact that the extractor vents for the whole hotel seemed to be located directly outside our window - the noise made the terrace unusable.
You might think that would have been enough to put me off but the hotel is so nice in other ways that I'd still recommend it - just make sure you don't get that room.

The only good thing whit this hotel - is the location.
We ordered big family room whit large (Queen) beds, but got - small rooms whit standard bed. Very small beds and we slept very badly all - days. This totally spoiled the holiday.
The room we ordered though Hotels.com does not exist at Wellington Hotel.
My dotters bag was stolen from a lock hotel room, and the Hotel never contacted us afterwards.
The aircondition was very noicy.

The staff at the hotel was extremely friendly and helpful. We had no hot water on our -nd day and we were immediately moved to another room. River-side rooms provide a wonderful view of the Ben Franklin Bridge. On several occasions the staff provided directions or assistance in finding restaurants or other locations. The complimentary breakfast buffet is an added highlight. The location was great - just blocks from the historic area. We were easily within walking distance to most Center City locations, but the hotel also has a courtesy shuttle service to many areas. We would definitely stay here again!

I recently went to this Hotel recently with a few buddies for a relaxing weekend in a suit overlooking the pool. I had stayed at the Hard Rock in Chicago and had a good experience with that property, so I though the San Diego property would be similar.
At first blush, I liked the modern design of the hotel. But I can see how people would be turned off by the design. The valets and front desk clerks were great, but that's about the end of the positive comments.
At night, getting back into the hotel was like getting into a prison. They set up a velvet rope at both entrances and make you display a key card to get into the lobby (even though you need a key card to get the elevators to work). I can see some safety logic to this, although the hotel is in a safe area. But the problem I had was the doorman refusing to accept my key card on multiple occasions. 
As others have noted, there is the Sweetwater Saloon on the ground floor, which might be popular at some time. During the weekend I was there, it was not busy. Regardless, the bouncers are incredibly rude to the hotel guests. We went to have a drink after dinner and were told that we couldn't go inside, even though we had put our names on the stupid guest list you have to use just to get a drink. The bar was less than half full and the bouncer let another group in while we were arguing. After I asked why the new group was allowed in, he told me that I had to leave the lobby or I would be arrested for trespassing. I'm not sure how I could be trespassing in a hotel that I had paid to stay in, but that was his threat. At the same time, I was soon surrounded by a bunch of bouncer-thugs who """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""insisted"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that I leave the lobby. I went back to my room, but it seems like a weird way to treat your customers.
The next night, we hung out on the bar by the pool. We met a few new people who had rented out a cabana and had purchased some bottles of vodka. Last call came and another bouncer stuck his nose in the cabana and told me I (and just me) had to leave. I showed him my key card and he accused me of having a fake card. He played with the card and talked on his walkie talkie. He eventually gave me my room key back, but then said that I """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""had a lot of balls"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to be sitting in there. I don't think anyone should have to be insulted by the hotel's staff, especially in front of someone you just met.
The whole thing left a bad taste in my mouth. What made it worse is that I've stayed at the Omni, which is basically across the street, and had a wonderful time. I would suggest anyone who is not wedded to the Hard Rock to stay at the Omni, unless you don't like being treated like a valued human being.
Also, the rooms are fairly small and the tv remotes suck. There's no lock on either the toilet or the shower, and the both have frosted glass walls. 
Mary Janes' was pretty good for a diner. The location is great, but as I've said before, there are a ton of hotels nearby and the Hard Rock's location is not better than any other.

This property has rooms that are a bit on the small side, but they are decorated in a delightful way and they have pleasing and unusual bathrooms.
We like the Japantown location and our room, on the --st floor facing Geary Street, had a spectacular view.

Excellent location in Union Square. For unknown reason we were upgraded to the Penthouse. Can't complain about that. Definitely would stay there again. Room service is thru Max's Restaurant on street level (which is great). Not sure if they are related. An old building so the elevators aren't all that fast. Lot better price than the Hilton and Westin that border it. Much nicer than the King George in the same block.

One of the worst hotel i have been at. First of all when you pay over $--- you expect a room with comfort. The room looks like its fitted for a Motel - chain...Plus there is no air conditioning in the room. YEA thats right no air condiotiong at the best western that charges more than $--- a room. Better off across the street at the Howard Johnson there rate is lower and they have air conditioning.

Nice location with easy access to everything by foot or by car. I was most intrigued by their unique mini pineapple cupcakes that welcomed you in the lobby. They were a whimsical way to reinforce their brand.
The bathroom was my favorite - spacious and sleek. The rooms were very clean and the bed was full of pillows you could sink into, prop your feet on or just squish as you sleep the night away. I'll say we didn't spend much time here but we used it as our book end for our trip from Seattle, to Victoria, to Vancouver and back to Seattle. We were easily able to walk from here to the Space Needle, Pike Place, the piers and even uphill to Queen Anne. 
I will say, their reservations process was not as smooth as the stay - my friend experienced multiple charges and phone calls required to correct it. However, they did correct it and our stay was comfortable.

I stayed at this hotel for one night for my medical board exam (because of which, I received a discounted rate). For this purpose, the hotel was excellent. It was only --- blocks away from the exam site. The room was nice, comfortable, and clean. I enjoyed and had a nice dinner and breakfast at the hotel restauraunt. I also liked their express checkout. The beds were very comfortable. My stay definitely was not cheap, but was reasonably priced with the discount. The only problem was there was a lot of traffic noise, even from my --th floor room. I was also located near the elevators which were pretty noisy.
The only time I got a hello was when i checked in, and it's not in the best area of San Francisco alot of homeless people around sleeping on the streets outside

Met all of our needs and aimed to cater to us. We paid around $--- for - adjoining rooms and valet parking. The hotel was gorgeous and absolutely great service at every corner. I would recommend taking a walk around the area to see all of the great attractions and restaurants. We walked to Millenium Park with - small children and they played in the water, and Jersey Boys was playing a block away from the hotel. Room service even brought us up placesettings for us to eat carry out in our room at no charge. The rooms were luxurious and spacious. There was even a Starbucks in the hotel. I would love to stay there again, everyone was so nice and helpful! The best hotel we've stayed in.
Very nice place , doesn't feel that you are in the airport, very handy, lots of room for meetings. Excellent attention from the staff.

I recently stayed at the Hampton while in town for a national competition with students. It is directly across the street from Camden Yards! Even though we were there for competition, the crowds were really mellow, even after winning the game. The fireworks woke me up one night, but were over quickly. There are many attractions within walking distance and lots of choices for dining - from the hot dogs on the street to more expensive steaks and seafood. Everyone was so friendly. They even allowed our group to check out in the morning, compete all day, and come back to get our luggage from storage that night. I would definitely stay there again, and the next time, I hope I actually get to see a game!

I always enjoy my stays here, and I find it perfect for the business traveler (though if I was looking for a location close to Times Square, Central Park, etc. I would stay here for leisure too). The hotel is very boutique-y and roomy for NYC standards. I've always found the staff to be ridiculously accommodating, and surprisingly I've been able to check in early every time I've stayed there (though I never assume it will happen!). While waiting in line to check in early, the doorman always offers to check my bag if it doesn't work out--super thoughtful. 
Located - minute away from Times Square, the location for sightseeing can't be beat! Though in a touristy area, you wouldn't know it at this hotel. It's just the perfect distance from all the sights and sounds of the city. I've had rooms low and higher up, front and back of the hotel and I've never been disturbed by the city that never sleeps. I don't think there's a room with a view at this hotel, but that doesn't matter to me since I'm rarely in my room during the day.
I had recently signed up for Kimpton rewards since I seem to stay at their hotels a lot, and there was a note and $-- mini bar comp card. Fabulous! Not sure if this happens every time, or only the first time after sign up, but still...a nice touch--so sign up! They also have a free happy hour too--a nice way to start your evening.
I also appreciate all the channel offerings--Bravo, MTV, HBO, etc...it may sound weird, but I hate staying in a hotel and being confined to - channels. All rooms also have the ipod alarm docking stations which always makes me happy too!

Sir Francis Drake is a nice hotel located in a good & convenient section of Downtown San Francisco. It's only a block away from Union Square, and a short cab ride from embarcadero. Our room was very clean and unexpectedly large. There was plenty of space for the couple that we were traveling in to come to our room and comfortably hang out. The furniture was older but in nice condition, and I expected the bathroom to be a little more recently renovated. However, the bathroom and the room itself were indeed very clean!
If you're looking for a ride on the San Francisco Trolly while in the city, Sir Francis Drake is perfect because the trolly goes right up Powell Street, and the hotel's main entrance is on Powell Street. Another great thing about this place is Scala's Bistro, the restaurant in the hotel. The food here is amazing! I'll be writing a separate review for that, though. Be sure to eat here at least once if you stay at Sir Francis Drake. Actually, eat there even if you don't pick SFD.
The staff is very friendly at Sir Francis Drake. They are also very accomodating. There's a nice bar in the main lobby, and the bartenders are really cool. The jester that hangs outside the front entrance to flag you a cab and help with your luggage is really cool as well. My only complaint is that they charge you (I believe it was $-) to use the computer lounge. Most hotels offer a shared computer-printer complimentary these days.

Words cannot express the sheer luxury associated with Four Seasons Chicago. I stayed there in June with my wife, for my birthday, and the stay was absolutely magnificient. in today's economy (or any economy) you think they would be grateful that people are still coming to this hotel and spending $----night, what a dissapointment. The pool was dirty, it was not heated, no music as advertised, the bar was closed and no drink-bar-food service available at the pool. If you are not a model on a photo shoot, you are treated like a second class citizen. Their spa is -rd rate, the day I went they only had - person working and she was terrible. I would not stay here again if I was compted!!!!!!

We stayed overnight for a layover and it is an adequate airport hotel. Its lobby is way better than its rooms which cries out for renovation. Everything in the bedroom looks old and shabby. The same goes to the bathroom. They actually look better in my pictures. What is going on with this ripped chair that has been in many reviewers’ pictures? It is a shame to the Westin brand. The only good thing about the hotel? The heavenly bed is still as comfortable as advertised.

The Phillips Club is first rate in every respect. I had to laugh when I read the above review. That """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Italian grocery store"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is Balducci's.

This hotel represents the meeting between luxury and urban chic that is taking over New York City. The decor is beautiful. The rooms are spacious and very clean. Service is by far the most accommodating i've experienced so far in the city, the front lobby clerk Mrs. Batista was a sweetheart, had no problem going the extra mile for our comfort.

I stayed two nights at the Sheraton San Diego Hotel and Marina. They should rename this hotel to the Airport Sheraton because you are RIGHT NEXT TO THE AIRPORT. Don't get me wrong, the hotel was nice inside, but if you are outside by the pool or restaurant, you hear the planes taking off every couple of minutes. I mean LOUD! And if you have your balacony door open (which I like to sleep with the door open at night instead of air conditioning), then expect the noise from the airplanes. The hotel lobby was nice, the bed was very comfortable and the concierge level was nice too. Not excellent but just nice. 
I wouldn't stay here again. It would work more as a business hotel close to the airport but definitely not a weekend pleasure trip.

The ultra cheap Jetsetter rate is what swayed me to try this new hotel and I wasn't disappointed. This hotel is cool. The Small but well appointed rooms are more than adequate after a hardcore day of shopping. The staff were friendly, helpful and were more than happy to provide any recommendations for restaurants and bars. I'd have no hesitation staying here again.

Love the hotel and Love the People!A Very Big Thank you to Devon,Ceicle,Giselle,Michael and the rest of the staff whose names I've forgotten,but should also be Thanked for your very kind and generous hospitality,which was above and beyond the call of duty.I had such an amazing stay at The Hollywood Hotel,that to be quite honest I didn't want to leave LA.The customer service was excellent and I have no complaints whatsoever about staying there! For the first time ever I made my hotel reservation through hotwire and did not know what hotel I was getting until after the purchase occurred. I needed a hotel in the LAX area for a weekend conference. There were - possibilities that matched the offer for - ½ stars for $-- a night and after researching online reviews I was really hoping I would not get the Crowne Plaza for my reservation, but I did. I dreaded my stay and pre-requested a quiet, clean room with a king bed. Upon my arrival, I was surprised to find the staff to be friendly and helpful and my requests noted in my reservation were granted. They gave me a room in the “quiet zone” with a king bed and a small pull out sofa. The carpet was stained, the outside of the windows were muddy and the tv & furniture was outdated as mentioned in other online reviews, however the room was QUIET and the bed was definitely comfortable. The room was clean other than the carpet and the daily cleaning service was efficient. I personally would not take a bath in the small tub, but the shower had a massaging head and the curtain was curved out a bit as to make it less confining. I parked in the self parking lot (a reasonable $-- a day or something like that) and was able to walk to my conference at the Hilton in -- minutes each way. The breakfast buffet was a good deal with the --% off coupon given to me at check-in and seemed to be a popular choice. The outdoor pool was the smallest pool I have ever seen and the chairs did not have cushions on them but the sun was shining down on the woman taking advantage of the facilities where-as the rest of the area was still overcast. I did not use the pool, hot tub, fitness room, sauna or steam room but it was nice to know they were there just in case. I did try to get a drink from the drink machine that only takes credit cards. After the machine on my floor did not work, I went to the next floor. It took my credit card but did not give me a drink (twice). There is a number to call and get a refund but I have not called. I did get a drink coupon from the lobby when I reported my issue. There is a convenient trolley that loops from the LAX hotel area to Manhattan Beach regularly for $- round trip. Buy the tickets at the front desk and enjoy. I felt safe and relatively comfortable during my stay and they allowed me to have a late check out. I would rate this hotel at - ½ stars max because it really needs an update in furniture, carpet and pool. I would recommend this hotel as long as you are not looking for a - star glamorous resort-type get-away.

The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""new"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Sheraton Gateway, after an extensive lobby overhaul, the addition of the overpriced but above-average Shula's, and room renovation (but not the bathrooms) is a pleasant place to stay. Like many reviewers state, it's a bit cold - check the pics - greys, blues, and black. close to the runways (only the Radisson sits closer), but you won't hear much noise from the room. The Sheraton's the newest remodel in the area at the - star level, far nicer than the Westin, Marriot, or Crowne Plaza.

So I am only a Gold Starwood since I switched to Hilton as my main hotel of choice.
This property is nice but for you out of shape people don't get put into the Lani section of the hotel unless you drive your car over to that wing.i don't have a car and from the lobby I could not believe the distance for my room.easiest way to know if you are being thrown into the labyrinth is the desk clerk pulling out a map that resembles the outcry of Italy.
