Let's be upfront - I was thrilled to be booked into the Waldorf Astoria, even though anticipating that it would be a faded and worn shadow of its Thirties glory. And it was, but I would still go again with the family just to share with them a New York landmark.
Stayed in three rooms over - nights. The first room was tiny with two double beds lacking any form of back support. Was moved to a quirky mini-suite overlooking the front entrance. This is the sort of room which makes staying in an old hotel so memorable. It had an entrance foyer, bedroom, a huge dressing room (large enough for a small couch, dressing table and two armoires) and an art deco bathroom on a raised platform. Incredible. The third room was a nicer version of the first.
All the rooms were worn and in need of repainting, new furniture and carpets. But it was all well worth staying for the fireplaces in the halls, lobby area and the ability to say that you stayed at the Waldorf=Astoria.

After a long flight from Australia, the last thing we wanted was to be delayed at check in. As Hilton Honors members we thought this would be a quick procedure - wrong. The Hilton Honors counter was not attended and the check in line was very long. When we finally got to our room it faced a Fire Station which kept us awake all night with sirens going off. The room was in need of a complete overhaul. We left early in the morning and left a letter of complaint for the Manager but never had a reply. This was the worst nights sleep we have ever experienced at a Hotel anywhere in the World.

Excellent place, almost brand new, great staff and good location. Rooms a bit small but take it for granted you will have a nice stay if you do not have a lot of stuff to place in.
Congrat to the manager, your people are great.

I stayed in this hotel for only one night. I was pleased with the room, and the cleaning ladies were really kind, however the hotels pool is really tiny, the gym had flies flying around in it, and the hot tub was shallow and just for two people. I'm am not too sure how up to date it was either. The hotels lobby looks nice, but if you are planning to enjoy the hotels amenities then you'll be dissapointed. Also, you have to use your room key to go to a floor on the elevator. Alot of times it doesn't work or the elevator starts moving, and it passes your floor, etc. Alot of people on the elevator were annoyed by this. Mine didn't work at all and I was on the way to the gym, and got stuck going to the lobby. I just went ahead and asked them to fix my card instead of taking the stairs, but I didn't have my id on me. The woman at the front desk then said she would call a security guard to escort me to my room to get my id. I was really upset by this. She then changed her mind, probably because she could see how unhappy I was, and just called the room to talk to my boyfriend to verify that I was who I said I was. This is not a nice enough hotel to be so up tight. I didn't complain, because I'm sure that's she was just doing her job and that's just thier policy, but it's a bad policy to have. It is DEFINITELY NOT worth paying the full price, especially after they nickle and dime you for everything. Internet is $--, but they have another type of internet they offer that, if you exceed a certain bandwidth, they will dissconnect you for $--. Parking is $--. Also, Instead of giving you a fridge they give you a mini bar. Don't plan on keeping any leftovers. Luckily, I used hotwire and payed little to stay here. I stayed at the aloft (three star) in the bwi hotel district before and the staff was way friendlier, everything was much more updated, and their internet was free.
Basically, this hotel is not worth paying full price for. --- at the most. It doesn't feel like a four star hotel. If you want to stay in a hotel in the inner harbor, I'd recomend the Marriott waterfront. It was nicer.

Giving this Motel three stars is a bit unfair but at the same time there are things it can not better simply because of what it inherently is which is an old fashioned Motel but with an updated image. Built in I think the ----`s the rooms are all facing out to a pool - garden with them all sharing a set of inner walkways which can cause noise when being walked on or if dragging suitcases along. 
So saying, this was not generally what kept us awake at night, that was down to young red neck guests who thought it funny to use the place as a play pen at -.-- am.....The -- hour concierge should have sorted this out however.
The interior of our room ( a standard king next to the stairwell on the first floor ) was nice enough with plenty of room, a good sized walk in wardrobe and table - chairs, T.V cabinet and draws. 
The room gave almost no view to the Street ( Webster ) due to a tree growing outside and no front view to the pool - garden so was also quite dark.. The bathroom was small and very basic with a shower only, no bath. 
There were dispensers in the shower cubicle for soaps, good idea.
However, the room was clean-ed every day and had no glaring faults that made occupation distasteful and we actually found it reasonably pleasant, I can only assume that the nicer - larger rooms looking out over the courtyard would be slightly better and more pleasant still.
Couples or families on a budget should find all this acceptable however, the funky interior paintings and wall colours brighten things up and gives a sunny `holiday` feel to the rooms and certainly is better than acres of beige- white which i`m sure it would have been a few years ago. 
The big drawback was that there was no coffee maker, fridge or microwave in the room, no DVD or C.D player either. A clock alarm and a T.V were the only `extras` . Shame, but if you know thats what youre going to get...
Breakfast was very basic as is usual in America, muffins and bagels with some jams, cheese spreads, packet jogurt ( urgh), juice and coffee. I think some cereal as well. Okay but not gourmet by any stretch.Trays are provided if you wish to breakfast in your room ( we did, the only seating is outside which at -.-- A.M in San Fran can be damn chilly!)
Parking, it should be noted is on the ground floor under the rooms with an overflow car park next door in a lot. There is also plenty of parking on the streets.
The best part of this though is the location, down near Marina, close to Chrissy fields, the Forts, Pier --, Golden Gate and facing the other way a -- minute walk into the City for Union Square and shopping. The Del Sol ineighbourhood is pleasant and busy, upmarket with many shops, cafes and bars with some good restaurants of all types and budgets catered for. We had Thai, Mexican and fusion fish all within about --- yards of Del Sol and all were fine and well priced. 
I cannot really comment on the staff, at Del Sol, booking in and out was about my only contact but that was fine and friendly enough.
In summarisation I would say that this was a fine enough place for most to stay, its quite cheap ( for San Fran, we stayed at the Rex last visit and that has trebled in price in just - years), its location is superb, its quite fun and funky, it has a swimming pool ( not heated I don`t think and a bit open next to the street ), its on a quiet street and it`s safe. It is really a Motel still not a Hotel and does have comfort limitations but if you go with all this mind you should not be dissapointed. We would not rush back but we certainly wouldn`t boycottt the place either, especially if we were to return to be in that part of town.
A final reminder is that State tax and Room tax is additional to prices quoted even on Booking.com! Be aware, it adds quite a bit to a longer stay! WE paid about $--- per night plus tax.

The room itself is clean, the beds are comfy, and I like the flat screen tv's. But this room has its quirks! 
This morning, at -am, they were testing the fire alarms. Inside the room at full blast volume, they announce, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""WWEEERRRPP!!!! Also, if you're a light sleeper, be warned. From my room at night, there's a constant generator noise. It's not the ventilation for this room b-c the heater already kicked off. Ear plugs don't really help because it's a low pitched hum, so my cheap ear plugs won't block that frequency out.
I didn't bother to ask for a room change because I talked to some of my co-workers on different floors, and they complained about the same generator noise.
Too bad for the annoyances because I thought it was a beautiful room.

We had a fantastic view from the --th floor of Manhattan including the Empire State Building. The location is a few blocks from all of the attractions on Fifth Avenue, ESB, Grand Central and Times Square, but also a few minutes' walk from the Flat Iron District to the South East of the hotel. With flat shoes we walked north to and from Central Park (as far as the Natural History Museum and Strawberry Fields) although it takes a while. The subway station to get to South Manhattan is only minutes' away too and takes about -- minutes to get to Battery Park. 
Service at reception was faultless. Room was small but very comfortable and clean with a big TV, security box, floor to ceiling windows and the great view. You don't need a big room when staying in New York. 
The price was good when I visited in May ---- as the hotel was relatively new, but I think the prices have gone up since then.

I honestly would not suggest to anyone to stay at this hotel. The location is descrete and in the middle of a business park, and one subway directly across the way from it. My experience here was not very good. I had to wait -- mins to an hour for the airport shuttle, while I saw other hotels come and go constantly picking up guests from the airport. Once I made it to the hotel the front desk clerk was no where to be found, it was night time so I was very tired and anxious to get to my room. The next day I found that the breakfast they serve was out of date and highly overpriced. The up side to it was the young lady who was my server was very nice and gave me other options to go with. Most of the front desk clerks I dealt with were very rude and heartless, especially the young lady who wore the wig, which I thought was so tacky! The housekeepers were very nice and kind and the night driver was very nice and helpful with my bags. Will I believe his name was. Overall I would rate this hotel a -.

We stayed at this hotel for one week in early July ----. We were able to get a good deal for the hotel room from Expedia. We were very pleased with the location and services at this hotel. This high-rise hotel was refurbished a few years ago from its original apartment residence and there are still a few longterm apartment tenants but you would never know it. Our room accomodated two adults and two teenagers without it feeling too cramped for a Manhattan hotel. The washroom and beds were clean and fresh daily. The lobby, surroundings and indoor environment were well maintained, bright and inviting. It has a central location (two blocks from Times Square, near a couple of subway entrances) that allows easy access to all that Manhattan has to offer. Surrounding restaurants within walking distance were plentiful and reasonably priced. The staff were all friendly, pleasant and accomodating. Definitely a real hotel jewel for families in Midtown and we will be back here the next time we visit New York City.

I stayed here with some girl friends as a mini reunion. We all went to school downtown- we love and are familiar with the area. The hotel is easy to get to- lots of subways within a few blocks.
The room was really clean. Everything was sleek and modern. If you don't want to be naked in front of who you are traveling with, let the shower steam up first. We had a room where the glass shower wall was the only wall for the bathroom...even though it's not clear glass, you see everything! 
Hotel staff was really nice and helpful. Toiletries are Bliss brand and I loooooved them. There is still a lot of construction going on in WTC- hearing that noise in the morning was obnoxious. 
The bed was soooo comfortable. I slept like a baby until a jackhammer woke me up.
Bar had good drinks- kind of expensive. 
Overall, If you're into the modern look, this place is probably for you. Im not...but I didn't dislike it- I'd come back.
room need to be clean and fix up.carpet was dirty door at bottom have a big space.tv guide was incorrect. park lot was bad

Hotel is centrally located near the Mall. Good location for the business traveler and tourists. Hotel is located at Metro Center (subway) and this provides easy transit to all points in DC. There are several restaurants on the property from deli to sports bar to upscale. Prices were very reasonable for the weekend - $--- per night - given it's downtown location.

Stayed here for - nights during October. The hotel has a great location across the road from Grand Central Station. It is also very near to major shopping areas and restaurants. The staff are very friendly and the rooms are nice. The bathrooms definitely need some renovating. The one big downside is the price of the internet. It was about $-- per device per day, that is ridiculous !!!! I am from South Africa and we don't even pay that much for internet. Overall good hotel.

Terrible hotel. Better prices and facilities at any major chain in the LAX area. Apparently they got a bargain for military surplus battleship grey paint so that combined with the dim lighting the hallways have the charm of a tomb. They also apparently got a bargain by buying liquidated clothing racks when Montgomery Ward went out of business, putting them into the rooms instead of closets. No self-park although there is plenty of space available, and $-- valet parking is not fully revealed in the website.

My wife and I stayed for a three day holiday in Chicago over the Labour Day long weekend. The hotel was near perfect. We had booked a deluxe room and were upgraded to a deluxe corner suite. Very nice touch. The room was unbelievable, with stunning views of the Hancock Tower and Lake Michigan. The staff were all very friendly and helpful, especially the concierge. The location was perfect; walking distance to the Magnificent Mile, the beach, Rush street at night and a Red Line subway station. The atmosphere was perfect; vibrant and busy, but not like a larger convention type hotel. We have travelled the world and stayed in many places and wouldn't hesitate to highly recomment this hotel for anyone taking a visit to Chicago.

This is the hotel we stay in whenever we visit San Diego. Our most recent stay was June --th and --th, ----. The hotel is close to the beaches, Sea World, The Zoo, Old Town, The Airport and not too far from the inland cities. We usually get the King Suite with the sofa sleeper. We have always found it to be a clean, well appointed room. While there are more expensive and finer establishments within this area, we have found this to be a mid range, family friendly hotel that we like to provides comfort and great service.
The staff is always courteous and knowledgable and are always willing to let us check in early, if there are rooms available. We have frequented the available breakfast options, but usually prefer a more substantial breakfast when we vacation. The breakfast is the standard fare like some fruit selections, waffles, hard boiled eggs, cereal, muffins, toast, etc..

My husband and I recently stayed at The Ballantyne Hotel and Lodge as part of a wedding group. My first impression was that the hotel reminded me of luxury hotels I've stayed at in New York and Boston. That is both a good comparison and a not-so-good one. On the good side, the room was very nice, the bed more than comfortable, the bathroom luxurious. On the not-so-good side are the fact that you have to pay extra for WiFi. I mean, come on! Motel - doesn't even charge for WiFi! Plus, if you want to use a PC in the Business Center, there is a charge for that as well. Also, the way they have the minibar set up, you cannot put ANYTHING of your own in the fridge to stay cool or else you will be charged when you take it out. Not exactly sure how this works, but a sign on the fridge says that you are charged by weight, any time something is removed from the fridge. Again, I stay at much less expensive hotels all the time, and I can ALWAYS use the fridge! Next is the difficulty I had finding the outdoor pool. The indoor pool and fitness center were very easy to find, right off the elevator on the lower level. But I had to go outside and wander around on a very small sidewalk in order to reach the outdoor pool. Then trying to get back into the hotel, you kind of have to go through the Spa, which they don't want you doing. (One note on the fitness center, it was great except they need to get an elliptical machine!) 
My final comment concerns the electronic locking system on the guest room doors. From the minute we checked in and first tried to use our key, it took five or six tries before the green light came on and we could open the door. My husband went back to the front desk to see if they could give us better keys. The desk clerk told him there was nothing wrong with the keys, he just must be doing it wrong. When my husband pushed back on that (we are not idiots and we travel a LOT) the clerk acknowledged that you kind of have to jiggle them and try them several times, but new keys would not resolve that. We muddled through with the slightly defective keys, but then found out that other guests were having the same problem, which makes me think the problem is the locks!
Bottom line: I'm glad i had the experience of staying at The Ballantyne Hotel, but when I make future trips to Charlotte, which I do with some frequency, I will not stay there again.

My company's office is across the street and I was in town for training and stayed at the Dream for ---nights. The location can't be beat for me and the very friendly staff and clean rooms made this hotel a perfect fit. It is a very fun hotel with a roof bar, the pool area, lobby bar and a basement club. No shortage of places for music & drinks.

This Hampton Inn lives up to the reputation we have come to appreciate. Excellent accomodation. The location is the best, within easy walking distance of Central Park, Times Square and great access to the subway. Buffet breakfast was busy but very well stocked and staffed. As previously mentioned by others, too bad about all the disposables. Especially the trays!! Wonderful to have hot drinks all day long especially at this time of year. Parking adjacent at $-- a day was reasonable. Did you know you can park for free on the street on Sunday? We parked the day we arrived and saved some money. I definitely recommend this place, we were a family of - and had two adjacent bedrooms.

We checked numerous hotels in the San Fran area prior to booking, the major difficulty was finding anything completely objective and that gave a good overview of the area. The location for the Adagio is super, close to Union Square (- blocks-- minute walk) however, you are on the border of the Tenderloin district which is a little on the rough side with many panhandlers on the street, although to be fair they didn't really bother us. There are reasonable eateries locally for breakfast-dinner, but, they do all serve much the same fare. Now back to the hotel! Its a nice, clean hotel only losing marks for it's location, hence the - stars, but don't let this put you off as many higher graded hotels are close by. Overall if I were to return to SF I would probably stay again as we got a good deal and reasonably happy with our value for money.

Its not the biggest hotel room but most American hotels have small rooms so don't be mislead by that! We were on the --th floor and heard nothing from the streets outside!! It was fab! Nice businesshotel, well situated and very good staff specially at the bar. Lounge also serviced nicely, although breakfast buffet at the lounge could be better - definitely too few choices. Support from concierge a bit slow and room was made after --:-- the first day, which is very late

The hotel is just a block or two off of Michigan Ave where we spent a day walking around shopping, eating, etc. There are several bars, places to eat in the immediate vicinity, and tons within a short walking distance. Ryan, the concierge, was always there and very helpful with directions, and he made reservations for us for dinner a couple times. The bell staff was quick with getting cabs whenever we need them. The hotel is situated about - blocks from the train which we took to and from the airport. $-.-- vs. $----- cab fare. (and quicker) Our room was nice and clean although the view was of a roof and the side of another building. What can you expect by using priceline? We saved alot of money by using priceline! Every night the hotel put on a wine party with free wine and there was coffee in the morning from Starbucks in the lobby. We got room service for breakfast one morning and it wasn't very good. We had some friends who walked across the street to the Emerald Loop for a breakfast buffet, we should have gone there. The hotel had free wi-fi, which is always nice. Morton's of Chicago is right next door, we had dinner there one night and it was one of the best meals we have had in a long time. Make sure to check the website before going there for a really great special! 
There are so many hotels in downtown Chicago we are not sure we would pick this one again, not because we didn't like it, but because we like to try new ones all the time, but if priceline chose this one again we wouldn't be dissapointed.

 When we got home I started to wash our clothes when I found a pair of men socks and underware in the laundry I knew they were not my husband, when I asked about them my daughter said she picked them up from the closet. I would say the maid didnt check or clean the shelve from the last guest.
 The beds had the linen pulled up the second nite. They were not remain, I could tell because the one corner had come undone the nite before and was still undone when we got in bed that night.
 There is no refigerator or microwave in the room, however there is a cofeemaker, iron, iron board, and blow dryer. The TV are being upgraded. (so we were told).

We arrived before advertised check-in time, and were advised rooms not yet available and we should come back later. The receptionist wasn't particularly friendly or welcoming - more interested in chatting in Spanish with her colleague. The cocktail hour was held on the rooftop pool area and the skies opened up to sunshine just before the event. The atmosphere, the staff, and the appetizers were great. The following dinner and the dinner service was also top notch.
Thanks to Kristyn and the staff, Jerry, and Chef Nick.

We came from las vegas to san francisco and stayed in the handlery for - nights.Upon checking in the receptionist offered us a room upgrade for $-- a night.This i was unwilling to pay.When we got to our room i could not beleve the size of it ?!?! it was tiny and old with a close up veiw of a wall outside.I am not a moaner as you can see from my other reveiws but the room in need of a make-over it looked like something from 'the waltons' the room came with a fridge which did not work, i rang in a wake up call for -am which never happened {this call could easily have been to catch a flight }.I was waiting for the lift one day and noticed the fire escape floorplan-map on the wall you could see the size of all the rooms on this ,their was our room --- the smallest on the floor.Not a great hotel at all.

I stayed at the Independent for four nights and was surprised that this place is rated so highly on TripAdvisor. On the plus side, the bed was very comfortable, the room was artful and hip and had high ceilings, and the bathroom was pretty large. And, it was relatively inexpensive ($----nt on a Travelzoo special which included a small continental room service breakfast). 
The location is both positive and negative. Yes, it is convenient to everything. However, this neighborhood has a pretty busy street scene - lots of clubs and restaurants. So if your room is on the street, it can be pretty noisy. The single-pane glass windows don't do anything to keep the noise out.
There are plenty of negatives too. The air conditioning functioned only sporadically, despite a request for maintenance. Nevertheless, the unit was really loud.
A red light (maybe part of the fire alarm?) mounted high on the wall by the front door kept flashing on and off my last night there. The recessed lights over the bed would not stay lit either (despite a maintenance request, this was never fixed). 
Security is lax. I came back to my room mid-afternoon to find the housekeeper there. I asked her if I could duck in to change and then I'd be leaving in -- minutes. She let me in to my room without asking me to use my key or see ID. I complained to the front desk. Same thing happened again - days later. Also, the door has no peephole, so if someone knocks, you can't see who it is until you open the door.
Bottom line, this is a -.- - - star hotel. If you can get it at a good price and don't mind the lax security and the potential for street noise, you may love it.

Stayed - nights at this Marriott for a conference - had hoped for a room in the beautiful old tower but all were full. While the hallways in the newer section were a little dingy and dark (low ceilings), the room was very comfortable and appeared clean. Used the work out facilities twice and they were very nice. Location of this hotel was fabulous - went walking each night to catch dinner and some exercise, couldn't have been better. Amenities at conference left a bit to be desired but I believe that was more the conference organizers issue than the hotel. Would stay there again.

I was requested to use my credit card to reserve a room for our business customer on Aug -, ---- - Aug -, ----. The Hotel representative re-assured me that they would charge the cost of staying on my customer when he checked in; my credit card was only needed to reserve the room on that paticular day.
Later, I found out that my credit card has been charged for the day of staying. I called Hotel Sorella on Thursday, Aug --, the person, in charge of this matter, was on vacation, so I left a message to her assistant manager, Tuan. 
I missed Tuan's call on Friday morning, but I called back right away and left a message. Ever since Friday moring, I have not heard any word from them. I called and left a message with the A-R of Hotel Sorella - Town Center, once every day , but no one seems to be interested to return my call.

My husband and I recently spent - nights at the Hampton Inn at South Park for a business trip and found it to be the nicest Hampton in which we have ever stayed. It was very clean, comfortable, great free continental breakfast, free Otis Spunkmeyer cookies in the afternoon, and the customer service and hospitality were superb! We would absolutely recommend this hotel!

We enjoyed our recent stay at the Parc --. The location is ideal for first time travelers to San Francisco. It is close to all forms of public transportation. And, there are food options at every price level in proximity to the hotel. We got a terrific deal on our room through Priceline.
Though we paid little for our room, we got great service from the hotel staff. The room was a good size and the bathroom was very spacious and VERY clean.

I concur with the positive reviews. Indeed, the only negative note is lack of space for breakfast, but you are free to grab and go. The lobby also offers many items that may help: tylenols, free coffee ----, some grocery items to cook (rooms have a full kitchen). Very quiet sleep. Staff indeed is very friendly: they do their very best. No problem with cleanliness. I will go back whenever I go back to Denver, for sure.

We stayed at the Westin at the Domain in Austin several weeks ago and it was great. The room was comfortable and the staff was more than helpful. We utilized the golf cart shuttle to access the large shopping area across the street and it was very much a plus to have. Would definitely stay there again!!

Don't be fooled by the pretty pictures of the rooms on this hotel's website like I was. Paid $--- per night for a room that felt more like one that should be rented by the hour.
I do have to say the room was clean, but very tiny. The bathroom was decent, but tiny. The floor this room was on must be one of the permanent residents floors as many there cooked in rooms and smoked. Adjoining rooms and hallways very noisy and there was NO ac, even though it was the end of Dec. Room hated by radiator and was so hot upon arrival I had to open the window which had no real view. Drapes were coming off the hooks also. 
Sent a complaining email to the concierge inquiring to the difference in the my room and those shown on the website. Never received any reply.
The only good thing about this hotel is the location with two subway lines on either corner and pretty close to much of the sites.

We spent - nights Mid-August, booked with a mainstream Travel Company and got a very nice room in the old building facing the marina. This is an excellent family location with nice pools, kids activities, rentals, and very close to everything.
The hotel,(motel section) is old but clean, and was a bit noisy with the - pools open late and the wooden balconies. The staff could bone up on the local attractions but were as helpfull as they could be. The hotel has only - shuttle to Seaworld and had no tour or bus arrangements. (they suggested the local transit bus). The gift shop is WAY too small and carries very few ammenities.
All in all, I reccomend the property if you are travelling with kids or just want a nice casual place to stay close to some very beautiful sights. For more upscale visits, I suggest buck up and stay in the new building for aa bit more money.
Very nice spot.

Stayed there for Natural Products Expo East
The location is excellent, the service is really good and eventhough it is a big, business oriented hotel it offers enough tranquility as for one to relax while not working

I stayed at the hotel july ----, there were numerous types of bugs in the room, and I came home with numerous bug bites on my legs, and around my feet. I saw one bug crawling under the bed one night, and the bed felt like the springs were broken. They need to clean the hotel more carefully and caulk up the holes that allow bugs into the rooms, that being said, the prices are good, and the staff was very friendly and helpful. The location is okay, a cab ride is close to everything and so is the subway.

This hotel has a great history and its one-time elegance is visible in the grand hall. But an interesting past does not make up for indifferent service, bland, boring food and rather dated rooms.
The restaurant looks very nice but the first morning were there the hostess was MIA. After ---- minutes, we seated ourselves. They offered a buffet which was more than we really wanted to eat but the wait staff told us that if we ordered off the menu, it would take a long time to be served. So we browsed the buffet. They had eggs benedict but the tray was empty. We wandered around the other offerings, waited in a medium line for an omelet but never saw the eggs benedict replaced. Hot tea seemed like a nice idea but no lemon was available - would we like lime? The next morning they did have eggs benedict but we regretted the choice. The hollandaise was bland and scanty which turned out to be an apt description for all the meals we had there.
One of my new pet peeves is hotels that post those nice little cards in the bathroom suggesting we help them save water by reusing our towels. The Menger, along with all the others we've stayed at this year, seem to have neglected to tell the maids about this policy. We dutifully hung up our towels and what did we find when we returned? Fresh towels. 
San Antonio, we heard, was experiencing a drought and water shortage. Surely even historic register hotels can update their plumbing, can't they? The shower blasted out water with no way to adjust the flow or the volume. The toilet roared when flushed apparently because there's too much water pressure? 
And so on. Management and staff seem to be bored and disinterested in making this a really fine hotel. It just feels old and dated. The best thing it has going for it is its location and its history. But it takes more than history to make it worth a return visit.

We stayed here Dec. --th - Dec. --th and loved every minute of it. The rooms are decorated beautifully, the bar was hopping and a perfect atmosphere to kick back and relax, awesome food and great staff. We booked the room for $--- a night, too -- what a steal!

I spent one night at the Millennium Hotel Broadway with young son to see hockey game at Madison Square Garden. Room was clean ready before scheduled check in time of -PM. Internet access was said to be free but turned out it was not. Beds comfortable but pillows hard as cement. Good location right in Times Square. No complaints but nothing overly exciting about this hotel.

Suite was fine, but the room was noisy and cold-drafty (our stay was in late October) . . . the location is good, but if you're planning on spending lots of time in your room, and resting peacefully for a good night's sleep, think about other options.

was in nyc to attend a wedding in soho; had not heard of this hotel; someone who lived on the west side told me of the convenience; nice hotel; room was comfortable; reception staff and doorman helpful; did not use concierge
would stay there again. walked to park on westend avenue; great river views; walked to the lincoln center. zabar's around the corner; found a great foot massage on --th newyouagain; a fun weekend especially with great weather; $-- cab ride to soho

We stayed there as an overnight stay before catching our morning flight, rooms were not clean and very outdated through out the hotel, did not have the rooms available that we booked and was offered an alternative on the smoking floor, which was unacceptable when you have children but did nothing to rectify their booking error. would not use or recommend this hotel to anyone. very disappointed.

This is our favorite hotel if we have a flight to catch or activities downtown Phoenix. We love the divided room to make a homey feel a TV in each room, one the bedroom and the other living area with pull out couch bed. Their is a refrig and microwave. Free wireless internet (or wired too). Their pool is heated nice on those cool nights. open -am - --pm. With a hot tub too. Love being greeted with their famous chocolate chip cookies. And their breakfast, fruit, eggs, bacon, ham, juice, coffee. Is all included!! It is the best way to start off the day. Breakfast is -am to --am, so sometimes we miss it do to early flights out. They have a free shuttle to the airport that runs every half-hour. On our latest trip we went to the zoo which is about - blocks going East. The light rail is also right out front if you want to explore the city, go to a baseball game, etc... It is not a resort hotel like some others, but for the price, they are the BEST bargin out there. Always friendly staff as well. A place we always recommend fellow travelers. Good for family and business. Plus we always get a good nice rest -- love their beds.

I used some of my starwood points for my recent stay at the chicago lakeshore w and was extremely disappointed. By far my worst w experience. The attention to detail and service was not up to the level of expectation for a w let alone a Sheraton or lower level brand name. 
Just a few examples:
-. The staff: We arrived and no one was around to offer taking our bags. Every staff member except the room service delivery person seemed disinterested in even being there. This included the bartender, service staff in two bars, reception desk, and concierges. We ordered a bottle of wine to go. It took ten minutes to get it when no one was patronizing the bar. And that was after waiting -- minutes in a dead bar before I got up and tracked down a menu myself. 
-. Attention to detail: the mats in the elevators that said good morning, good evening, etc. were always thrown in the elevators crooked with corners riding the walls. The iron in the room had its labels were completely worn off so I didn't know what settings were what. The bar on the top floor was layed out in a way that - people could enjoy the space so we left immediately.
It just did not feel like a w to me and I was upset I wasted my points staying there.

A nice clean location in the heart of NYC. Plenty of dining options around. The room was nicely set up and clean. Breakfast buffet was very nice. The dining are provided ample seating. One criticism would be the on-site parking. At $-- per day you can do better getting yourself an on-line pre-parking coupon. I forgot mine from a nearby location that would have saved about $-- for the stay.

Across the street from Ruth's Chris and MccCormick and Schmicks. Around the corner one way from the Mint an Harvey Gant Center. Go the other way and - blocks from Epicenter and Bobcats Arena. - blocks from Panthers stadium. Great front desk personnel also.

We spent - nights at this hotel just after Easter. We had booked - rooms, one for our grown up daughters and one for my husband and myself. It turns out that theoretically we could have stayed in one room as the rooms are very spacious and ours had a King Size bed as well as a sofa which was a sofabed. But all - of us in one room would probably have been a bit of a squash!
Having read some reviews about the cost of the breakfast in the hotel, we decided to go to a diner. There is a very good place called the Oxford Cafe two minutes away (turn right out of the hotel and take the first turning right). They also do home made pizzas later in the day, which are really good and reasonable. However, on our final morning we decided that we would have breakfast in the hotel and to be honest, it didn't cost any more than the diner. If you look at the menu, they quote various set breakfasts, but you can have whatever you want and they charge for the items individually, and that way it doesn't work out so expensive - and it was the only place where we had china cups and plates and tea in a teapot!!
The hotel is very convenient for many of the attractions of NY - Fifth Ave and Central Park are quite close. We didn't find the concierge very helpful, but all other staff were very friendly. On our final day we put our luggage in the store room until it was time to go to the airport and the hotel arranged a car to take us there, which did cost slightly more than a taxi, but meant that we knew for certain that we would leave on time and we didn't have to hail a cab.
I would certainly stay at this hotel again and would recommend it.

This is THE ideal hotel for budget travelers in a very good location. It amazes me how many reviewers have complained about the size of the rooms and the lack of hotel amenities. At this price, with such a great location in a big city like San Francisco, you're not going to get a luxury suite for $--- a night. That's just the way it goes. With the Metro as with everything else, you get what you pay for. Who comes to San Francisco and wastes time that could be spent exploring this wonderful city sitting in a hotel room anyway? We booked for value and location; just a place to come back to at the end of the day and get a restful night's sleep. 
My girlfriend and I stayed here for three nights as part of a short vacation. I've been to SF half a dozen times and It was her first time in the city. We planned to spend a lot of time shopping, eating, and exploring in the Haight and take in a concert in Golden Gate Park so for us it was the perfect location; walking distance to Haight-Ashbury and Golden Gate and Buena Vista parks with a MUNI stop just a block away if you want to go """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""furthur."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" We also went to the symphony at Davies Hall which was just a $- cab ride away. Some tips: if you need minimal noise to get a comfortable night's sleep, request an interior room as the hotel faces a very busy lower-haight thoroughfare. This was an issue for my girlfriend, so we made sure to call ahead and they accommodated us with a room facing the very lovely garden patio. If you're from a very hot climate, as we are, I would advise that you request a space heater from the front desk. The central heating was not adequate to keep us warm at night; it was about -- degrees outside and felt even colder in our room on the first night. We slept very comfortably on our second and third nights. A great experience overall!

Was in a room with an adjoining door, but didn't know those guests - could hear every word of their conversation. Could hear their shower running. 
At --:--AM, while I was asleep, a man enters my room. He apologizes and says he has the wrong room. Front desk calls up in three minutes and asks when I checked in. Not only did they wake me up by sending a man into my room, they call me and wake me up again to ask when I checked in, as if accusing me of squatting there!
I'd stay there again, if it were the only option around.

There was nothing horrible about this hotel, but nothing fabulous either. Got a deal online, so that was good, but the phone in the room didn't work right, the shower did alternating blasts of freezing and scalding water, the bed was very creaky, and there was a weird beeping noise outside the room during the night. Good location, friendly, if ineffective service, clean but uninspiring room.

This hotel is always my choice when staing in the Dallas area for several reasons. Proximity to my customer at Love Field, and the amazing staff, make it the place to stay for me. I've been coming here for years and with the recent room upgrades, the hotel is by far the best value in the area. The staff knows me by my first name and truly makes me feel at home when I'm on the road. In all my travels this hotel is certainly at the top of my list for value and friendliness!!

I was intrigued by all the positive so I thought I'd stray from my usual downtown hotels and check this one out. It didn't take long to work out where the high scores were coming from: the rooms are modest--typical travelodge stuff-- but the staff are what make this a great value spot in SF. They really, really know the neighborhood (and the city) and they really want their guests to enjoy it. I needed a quick food reco, I got a map and the menu so I could decide what to eat before going. I asked about walking in the nearby park, I was give trail maps so I wouldn't get lost. When I enquired about visiting the submarine at Fisherman'a Wharf I was shown photos of the ship and provided with very clear bus instructions to save me walking in the rain.

The Palmer House Hilton is like everyone says, a grand looking hotel located conviently in The Loop and close to almost everything. Situated along Whabash and Monroe, it's within a block from the Art Institute of Chicago and Millenium Park. Walking distance from Target and CVS is right across the street. State street is next to the hotel so you're walking distance from the Redline train. Not to mention that if you're coming from O'Hare airport you can take the Blue Line train for about $- all the way to Dearborn-Monroe and walk - minutes to the hotel. A bit of advice: take the train everywhere instead of a Taxi. It will save you tons of money during your trip and help you bypass all the traffic that everyone else and taxis are all stuck in. 
Now back to the review of the hotel. Great place for conferences and meetings with a business area for guests and lost of lounge areas and tables. The entrance and lobby really is grand, but like the other guests mentioned were a bit dated. The hallways are like a maze and easy to get lost in. The walls are pretty thin so expect to hear people next door if you are in the bathroom or if they are talking loud. If you get a room on the Whabash side of the roadm expect to hear the rumble of the train passing by every hour or so. The staff and maintenance crew were friendly, sincere, and great. The only issue I had were with the front desk people, whom I felt were a bit incompetent. I caught one girl at the front desk in a lie when she told me that all their non-smoking rooms were booked as we checked in. However, when I told her that I had a respiratory problem with cigarette smoke, a non-smoking room magically appeared on their computer screen. The front desk also gave someone else our room key, and those people almost entered our room while we were still in there. The people would have barged into our room if it weren't for us having the deadbolt on. 
I did like how there were two bathrooms in the room with our two queen size beds. Very convenient for those travelling in groups of ---. Roomy and lots of space. Would recommend just for the convenience and location, but the hotel could use an update on the room decor.

My husband has wanted to stay at this hotel for quite some time now as we visit Boston often. I'm glad we have now checked this off of the list. You can tell the staff truly care about your experience and needs. It was a busy weekend for them so we were not able to be upgraded. The standard room was pretty small and luckily we were out and about enjoying the perfect September weather. We will probably stick with Wesin Copley in the future due to location.

LaQuinta hotels have always been known for their great services, etc. I find out another great service they offer at my last stay. We stayed at the one across from the San Antonio, TX airport. We knew they offered free shuttle to the airport, which is great. But, they also let us leave our vehicle in their parking lot while we went on vacation. We did not have to worry about finding a parking spot at the airport or some where else. This great service cost us only $--.-- and you can leave your vehicle for up to -- days. Other hotels might do the same, but I have never asked up until now. Just remember to let them know you are picking up your vehicle when leaving, they might report it stolen, etc.

As a regular at tourist hotels in America and Britain, I liked this place. Most hotels frown on a family of five and make us feel like we had """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""one too many."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Here, our spacious room was set up for five. It was quiet. We slept all night. We walked to all the attractions. The price was half that of its neighbors. But like any old tourist hotel, it has character and you need it too. Roll with the quirks, and both your feet and pocketbook will thank you.

Great hotel in a great location. Stayed here for the weekend - the service was excellent and this location was great for everyone in our group to walk to all the Broadway plays we had tickets for. I also found a great rate on Travelzoo.

I spent one night at Hotel Rouge and thought it was funky & fun. The decor has tons of red in it, and it's certainly not your typical chain hotel. It's a converted apartment building and it shows. I liked the decor and the free wireless internet access. What didn't I like? The bed was a little soft. The room was somewhat dark (to enhance the funky feeling, I'm sure), and that made it hard for me to work going through papers and using my laptop. I would have liked more overhead light. I forgot a toothbrush, and they did not offer complementary ones ... they were $-.-- from the minibar! Finally, the bar on the ground floor of hotel allows smoking, so when you walk in, you are assaulted by a blast of nasty cigarette smoke. The hotel is very similar to the other nearby Kimpton Hotel, Hotel Madera, at least in terms of funky decore. But Hotel Madera has a better location and no nasty smoke pit on the first floor. But all in all this was a fine place to stay and I would do so again, although it wouldn't be my first choice.

Me and my husband stayed for our Honeymoon at Yotel for - days. The first thing that comes to my mind when I think about our stay at Yotel is the crew, I have never in my life met a nicer and more professional crew. Even though you think that nobody is going to greet you because everything is computerized, you are met by people that greets you and helps you. Yotel is fresh, futuristic, modern and special. The rooms are fresh and clean, always clean when you are back from a day spent in NYC. eve if you have a smaller room you dont feel it is so small because the windows are big and the class doors to the bathroom and toilet makes everything much bigger. The complementary breakfast was not my cup of tea, since you only get coffee and muffins. the al la carte breakfast is expensive, you can get much more for less money just across the street. The food however, the lunches and the dinners are awesome and fully price worthy. The tapas inspired food is awesome, I loved the food, it is fresh and delusions.
We will definitely come back to Yotel, and Yotel made our holiday worth wild.

If you need ready access to the stadium or the convention center and don't mind your fellow convention goer crowds, this is a great choice. Easy access to both make the stay a snap. Dinner in the gaslamp (touristy, but hey, it's easy) is a short walk away. Opt for a bayfront view--well worth it. The night we were there, the symphony was playing, so in addition to the lovely lights of the city-bay, we saw the fireworks from a quiet viewing point. The hotel is clean, the hot tub and pool a nice size. The gym is small but adequate, and nice little touches like cool lavender washcloths wipe the sweat away. Or take a nice run down to the airport and back, winding through Seaport Village, etc. For families, the location is mixed: if the crew wants to see a ball game, it's great. But for the price, it may not be the best choice--there's no beach to romp around. Overall, I really enjoy this hotel every time we stay at it--this is the third time for us.

This was our second Christmas Eve dinner at the Ritz. Last time our friend couldn't get us in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""main"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" dining room so we had dinner in the lower dining room for a fixed price meal at $----person. The food was mediocre and the service abysmal. 
Somehow we were talked into dining at the Ritz again this year. We balked but said if we could be assured we'd be in the main dining room, we'd do it.
Our friend got the reservations and away we went.
I can't say the food was bad and I must say the service was very good. I can say that I had been led to believe that the room was beautiful and we'd have a lovely room to dine in. Somehow our party was placed in a corner with a much-too-large table where you had to strain to hear your table companions. There was a tiny (and I do mean tiny) vase of little white tulips sitting in the middle of the large table, looking very forlorn. Oh, the tiny portions were very good, I must say. When it came time for the palate cleanser, though, our group completely lost it. The waiters came out with huge white charger-like bowls and in the exact center of each was half a teaspoon of sorbet along with three pomegranate seeds artfully placed alongside! They ceremoniously placed them in front of each of us. We howled with laughter. My husband yanked out our digital camera and took a picture. We have subsequently shown it to many friends. The photo always draws screams of laughter.
Next came the dessert, followed by a huge bill. Believe me, we have no problem enjoying and paying for an expensive meal. This, however, was a comical insult that we will not repeat.
Thank you,
L Russell (Photo attached)

I've stayed here a couple of times for business. The first time, my room was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""slightly used"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" -- a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""head print"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on the pillow and an opened condom wrapper on the floor. Excellent view from the --th floor. Much quieter than anticipated and the most comfortable hotel bed I have ever slept in. It was our first time to New York, but we felt part of the city. Broadway, Central Park, Museums, Macy's and Time Square are all a short subway ride away. The subways were much cleaner and safer than we would have thought and new Yorkers were always ready to lend a hand with directions.

Greeted warmly by Gabby in the lobby (so good to see her again!) and received room upgrade from Liz! Our room was on the --th floor (city view) and immaculate! The housekeeping staff deserves -*****!
This is OUR PLACE TO STAY when visiting in Chicago!!!

This hotel?Timeshare is close to everything. Great restaurants and subway outside the door which takes you to museums, theatre district and china town. Microwave and small refrig in unit. Rooms were small, old and dirty. Towels were changed infrequently. Staff were very rude and arrogant. This place needs to be shut down.

This place is great! It is an amazing location. Be sure to check into possible upgrades. For $---night, I was able to get a BEAUTIFUL Victorian style room with LOTS of space. I LOVE the art deco style of this hotel. We had - rooms for our group, and all of them were awesome.

This is the second time my family is staying at this homewood suites and will definitely NOT be the last since we visit Colorado every year. We love to travel and we love homewood suites so we have stayed in so many homewood suites in at least - states, non of them compares to this. This is the best!!! The employees are very friendly and helpful, the hotel is always very clean, breakfast and manager's specials are simply awesome!
Best of all, HONEST EMPLOYEES!!!. We just checked out of the hotel this morning and in the rush to catch our flight back to Ohio, my son forgot his hat and wallet with a $--- bill inside. Guess what? The hotel manager called my cell phone to let us know, we forgot some items in the room and a black wallet, I had to describe the wallet and let her know how much was inside. She will be sending the items to us by FEDEX today! How awesome is that?!!!
I am going to be calling the Hilton hotels to let them know how satisfied we are with this Homewood suites. If you are ever in the Denver area or even in Boulder or Colorado Springs, look no further for a hotel. This is absolutely the best hotel ever!!!

Everything was perfect from the time I made my reservations until the day we left. We made reservations to celebrate our anniversary and do a quick in-town getaway. The resort is a really good place to bring kids. The facility caters to kids' every need. My kids loved it. The lazy river and main pool were very, very cool. The water is as warm as bathwater. Very nice, since I get tired of jumping into freezing cold pools. The other pools also had kids.

The grounds were very clean and very nice. The only thing that prevented this from being a perfect -- was the --- degree heat outside. I am from San Diego and have low tolerance for heat. Stayed at this Holiday Inn for four nights in late July ----. First off: do not confuse this Holiday Inn for the Holiday Inn Express nearby which ALSO has LAX or Los Angeles Airport in its title. This Holiday Inn is on La Cienega Blvd, (corner of Century Blvd.)
Reviewers are correct, recently renovated this year, and it shows. Not all aspects were renovated, but the most important things in our room felt new. No mishaps at all, hotel is not that loud, we slept soundly every night. Only thing I would mention -- and it's not really that big a deal -- is the water temp. in the shower. Never seen anything like it, when the water flows from the bottom, hotter than hell, and steady heat. When you slide the switch to shower from up top, the heat fluctuates from lukewarm to damn hot every five seconds or so. Unexplainable, but am mentioining it because another reivewer reported the same.
All in all, GREAT CHEAP option, and worth the $--- or so per night. Book through Expedia or Travelocity and check both just to make sure one is not ripping you off.

My mom and I stayed here for - nights on our trip to attend a taping of The Price is Right. The hotel is directly across from CBS Studios, which was perfect. Our lock broke and the staff worked really hard to fix it, but we had to exchange rooms in the end. We received a breakfast voucher for the restaurant there, Tart, which has DELICIOUS breakfast! Only complaint was the noise at night and that the beds are extremely hard, but other than that, very clean and cozy.

We booked this hotel by calling it directly which resulted in a lower price than through the online websites. We liked this hotel, it was a good basic hotel and it was a very good value for the price. It is in the heart of Chinatown only about - blocks from the Red Line so is just a few stops from downtown and in what seems like a safe area. The staff was friendly and spoke English well. It is on - floors, no elevator. The room was small but large enough for us and contained a queen bed, desk, - side tables at the bed, a chair and a stool and had a small closet. There was a shower in the bathroom. The room was clean and was cleaned every day of our - night stay. It was quiet and the individual air conditioner worked well. There was a kitchen room on the lower floor with coffee, a microwave, refrigerator and free internet. We would stay there again.

We stayed here for - nights back in Nov '--. Read about it in this website. We were able to get a room the day of our stay, they were able to accomodate our late check in time (after --pm). 
Nice room. Nothing fancy. Clean. The decor could use a little updating but I'm not there to stare at the room. The bed was comfortable. We had a nice little balcony facing the marina. We stayed on the bottom floor. The one problem I had with the place, which I didn't mention to the staff, was I think the ceilings are thin. There must have been a family which had small children in the room above us that kept running back and forth. It was loud. Word to the wise, tread lightly if staying on the top floor, or stay on the top if you don't want to hear people walking above you. 
The continental breakfast sufficed. It wasn't excellent but it wasn't terrible. The staff treat you well there. They help serve you, set the tables for you, get your drinks. I was a little surprised when they handed me a receipt to sign, so we included a tip. i've not had that done at any other continental breakfasts in other hotels, but they do serve you more than at another place. 
Decently located. Easy to find. Nice area across the way to just walk along the water. The fee was good. I was able to get a lower price calling the hotel directly than the fees I saw on travel websites. 
I would stay there again, if I was in that area again, but I probably wouldn't just because I'd like to try something different. But it was a good, decent hotel.

We live in San Diego, but have always been intrigued by this inn. I decided to surprise my husband with a night's stay for his birthday. Everything was perfect! We stayed in the Aesthetic room which was gorgeous and the bed was very comfortable. The wine-cheese in the afternoon is such a nice perk and the breakfast was amazing. We hope to stay again!

We stayed with three other couples because we were seeing a show down in the theatre district and wanted to make a night of it. The people here are so nice and the rooms are cozy and offer the best night's sleep I've had in awhile. Would highly recommend

Besides that, the pluses are:
Beautiful workout room. Holy cow, working out with a view and a very new machines is amazing. Rooms are decent, nothing to write home about but yet nothing to complain about. The location is nice, it's in a very busy area of Seattle if you like that. Plenty of shopping right next to you.
Still, great hotel, I just think the Westin is superior even though it's much older.

Spent - nights here last week and the rooms are masive! - king size beds, huge dresser with flat screen TV. The kitchen was a bit poor but did not go to Washington to cook. Short walk to the White House so in a very good neighbourhood! Lincoln Memorial in the other direction. There is a lot of walking in Washington but well worth it to see all the sights.

I suppose it's not like we needed much more to make that day unforgettable...

So when we make our rainy trek to the Four Seasons, to find that we had been upgraded to the Presidential Suite...it sort of blew our minds.

The TV could ahve done with on demand films-tv but it was more than big enough though.
The reception staff and concierge staff were first class every time.
The Burger Joint sell the best burgers ever and Normas comes a very close second.
Would recommend this hotel to anyone and everyone

I had difficult time finding the right hotel in SF. We decided on Abri based on the reviews. Turned out the location was perfect! Our first room was facing the street so it was noisy, they changed us to the inner facing room which was perfect. Bedding, ammenities was up to - star standard. Front desk service was excellent too! Overall a great experience. I would certainly recommend and come back here

Such a nice place to stay, near to the monuments, safe place, with a store next...where you can get anything -- hours....definetly good place...not expensive...

We just returned from a business trip to LA and stayed at the Omni for four nights. While my husband was attending meetings, I was able to take advantage of some wonderful sights thanks to excellent advice from Amy, the concierge on duty! She was especially helpful in making suggestions for tours and restaurants that we would like and was so friendly whenever she saw me in the hotel! All of the staff went out of their way to be of service from the bellman to the housekeeping staff. I would highly recommend this hotel and its location in downtown LA. We appreciated the services of the Omni driver when going to restaurants that were a bit too far to walk.

For some reason, all the smoking rooms are on the second floor and due to saftey issues the windows in these rooms do NOT open! Who would have thought that a smoker enjoys fresh air as well...Not only did the windows not open, but the smoking rooms are definately NOT as nice or as clean as non-smoking rooms. Perks - Expresso machine broke the day after we got there....no lattes :(

great way to star a vacation. Ony one issue, they forgot the wakeup call. Luckily I woke in time and the shuttle had us to the airport in plenty of time.
will definately do it again

They are trying hard and the room was clean but VERY dated with the sink in the bedroom and the toilet and tub shower in a separate tiny room. The lounge on the top floor was dark and dingy, the breakfast was cooked to order by a chef with an open grill that needed a good cleaning.

We stayed at the Crosby St Hotel for a week in November ----. Unbeatable location, lovely quirky decor, comfortable rooms (I particularly liked the floor to ceiling windows that you can open), cool bar and restaurant, good food, loved the guest lounge with honour system drinks - great place to relax after a hard day's shopping. But what sets this hotel apart is the amazing staff, particularly the Reception and Concierge guys who were so helpful with restaurant bookings, sightseeing advice ... they even found us a dentist who was open on a public holiday ! I would recommend this hotel to anyone, and have already done so, and can't wait to come back.

A hotel with a very good location. Stayed there for a week during a convention and, although downtown San Francisco is pretty small, it was close to pretty much everything.
Rooms not above what you could expect but clean and well kept, and friendly staff.
The one downside was the smell of chinese food froom the nearby restaurant that seemed to penetrate into the hotel. You get used to it, but notice it every time you return from outside.

The W Times Square is my absolute favorite place to stay in NYC. (My last stay was March ----.) It is *the* place to stay. It's hip and trendy, but not snobby. Service is excellent, as is the location. Entrance to the hotel is via an elevator from a ground-floor room with a neon-lit, cascading waterfall on the wall. The hotel bar, which is an open area next to reception, can be a very happening place. Try a mojito or sour apple martini from the bar. (The drinks ain't cheap, but they're mighty tasty!) One recommendation I make is to request a room *not* overlooking Times Square if noise bothers you. I always request a room on the opposite side and don't hear a pip. The W Times Square is for the traveler who values comfort and style more than a bargain.

Okay, so it's not the Hilton. One should figure that out when the room is under $--- in NYC. I must say though that most people don't come to New York to stay in the hotel room. Yes, it is located at the beginning of Koreantown but on the other side of the hotel is Broadway. And never once did I feel unsafe. Except when I opened the large window to check out the view and realized there was no screen and we were on the --th floor. So be careful with children. We had a room with two twin beds (perfect for a girls weekend) and it looked exactly like the photos on the website. The walls were a bit thin, we heard some rowdy neighbors during the night but I called the front desk and they immediately sent someone up and we had no more problems. 
I wouldn't recommend it for honeymooners, but for people wanting to spend their money on SEEING New York but don't want the hotel to compromise on service, this is the place for you.

While there were other hotels that were closer, they were all twice as much or more! As it was, we were only about - blocks from the convention center. If you don't want to walk, the trolly stop is about --- block from the motel. I found the staff to be polite and helpful. its on the bay, the tropical landscaping is lush and beautiful, it has a quiet and clean, but older, dated exterior. and the hallway to our room was a little too dark.

We love this hotel. We have stayed in the marina suites twice (other trip Aug. --) and have thoroughly enjoyed it. While my husband checked in, I steped out the back door to see the renovations completed that we're underway during our last visit. There is a courtyard of cabana like lounging areas etc - it's especially impressive at night with great landscape lighting. The pool looked smaller but nice and I didn't go into the area myself , just looked through the iron fence.
The hotel is the perfect blend of elegance and comfort esp. since we've traveled with an infant each time. It is down the street from the Mission Bay board walk and amusement park and the bellman told me there is a trail-path-sidewalk I could stroll the baby from the hotel to mission bay. The afternoon I went to Mission Bay boardwalk, the beach was beautiful blue - a perfect day at the beach. Though we're used to Dallas traffic and commuting, this hotel is close to the airport and not too far a drive to all the places we want to visit. We never have trouble with traffic. As my husband comes to San Diego for business often, we'll be back!

Everything perfect during our last trip. Club lounge excellent and have to give special mention to Laza- a real character and great fun.. But all were staff excellent, friendly and elcoming without being in any way over th top. I wouldnt stay anywhere else in NYC

Outmoded and worn furnishings combine with some poor original design choices to produce a drab place to stay. This hotel's five-star rating needs a downgrade!

Was in Houston for the Final Four. Hotel was sold out and obviously busy. Its a nice hotel, nothing spectacular. The rooms are all suites and nice. Great space.

It's a newer hotel, so rooms and amenities were wonderful but was a nightmare during peak times and the Starbucks kept a line of about -- ppl at any given time.
