The wi-fi worked well all the time, on my Mac and iPod.
I would had stayed the extra two days, since I felt comfortable at this place, but I had made reservations elsewhere.

We booked this hotel on priceline for $--- a night by naming our own price. Granted this was in ----, but I'm sure you could still get a good price today. The hotel was in a great location near subways, Radio City Music Hall & Rockefeller Center. The room was very nice and clean and roomy. Our view of course was sensational. The lobby was very nice and so were any employees we ran into. I would definitely stay here again.

The hotel looks fine from the outside and is located a couple of miles from Downtown San Diego. The bay doesn't smell particularly nice, so next time I will probably stay downtown. The hotel was clean enough, but the stairwells were filthy and smelled terrible. The hotel has ----s decor. The room was spacious, but there was no air conditioning and although the day was cool it felt quiet muggy in the room. The sink area-hallway is located directly opposite the closet, making it quiet narrow and cramped. It seems that the hotel is mainly geared towards retired guests, because they have shuffleboard and billiards, the location of which remained unknown to us. We wanted to play pool, but the sign marking the location just led to a sad putting green and lawn in front of peoples rooms. But the linens were all clean and we got the hotel at a good price, so you could do worse.

My party visited LaCantera for a long-planned special occasion. When we arrived in the afternoon, for some reason the resort wasn't ready for us and our requested suite was not available. The resort immediately went into correction mode, and as a result we had an unforgettable stay. Our rooms did not include the suite but they were nice, with stunning views all around. Staffers Marques and Chelsea quickly fulfilled our every request and gave us tips about the resort that enhanced our stay. I'm looking for an excuse to return to La Cantera as soon as possible.

I stayed at Gramercy Park Hotel this past February while in town for business. I lived in NYC for years and had always wanted to check out the GPH, so was happy to stay there while back in town for work. GPH is certainly a great hotel for people on vacation or a special event, but perhaps not the right pick for business. For example, I was upgraded to a beautiful suite, but the desk was positioned in the middle of the room with no electrical connection. (Separately, I find the whole purple velvet-brown leather design to a bit Russian prostitute-ish) But on the other hand the staff was able to get me a reservation at Maialino (which was delicious), and the lobby bar is a great place to catch up with friends. All in all, great hotel for someone looking to relax, not a great hotel for someone looking to do business.

I am a Hilton Honors guy. This is in a decent location, but besides that, this is the worst Hilton experience I have had in the city. Stay somewhere else. I think the Garden Inn on --th is a much better option.

Fully renovated older Hilton and typically small rooms for Manhattan yet nicely situated for quiet nights. There was an interesting view of the top floors of the Empire State building from the window. Staff at front desk were accomodating. My only complaint: I still don't understand why these major brands still charge for internet - it is almost like charging for a shower in the morning. Perhaps it is about losing revenues by not using the telephones in the room.

The Renaissance O'Hare offered a very pleasant experience - the hotel is very clean and the staff was extremely friendly and helpful (every staff member I ran into said hello!)!! Beds are comfortable, and I especially liked that you got five pillows on each bed! The fitness center is clean and well equipped, and while I did not use the pool, it was large for a hotel pool and looked very nice. It is a short walk to the train, which is perfect when traveling to Downtown Chicago to eat or sightsee. The train ride is about -- minutes, though, to get downtown, which was a little longer than I was expecting. Beware, too, that unless you want to eat in the hotel's restaurant (which was very good), there were no restaurants that were easy to get to, it is in the middle of a bunch of office buildings. Overall was very pleased with the stay!

Trent and Cathy help make your visit to San Diego a wonderful experience. I can not express enough how wonderful everyone is at this hotel. I have stayed here many times and it always a wonderful experience.

The Good: Great midtown location, nice clean, new rooms and bathrooms. Great beds, soft sheets, adequate-sized rooms (even get a desk!) Very helpful staff. Our room had a nice view of the Rockefeller Center Plaza Park and the Christmas Tree. Overall a wonderful place for my wife and I to stay during our first trip to NYC. Relative to the other hotels in the price range we paid ($---), we were supremely satisfied with the hotel. The exercise room is suprisinlgy well equipped. Loved the bottled water on every floor.
The Bad: Funky check-in system, but the clerk was very helpful navigating us through the process. When we inquired about calling a taxi to take us to the airport (- day in advance), they suggested a car service for only $-- more. We agreed and set a time - but the car never showed!! We waited -- minutes and then hailed a cab and left. Obviously, we weren't charged, but still - it was nerve racking! So, when you go to the airport, don't rely on the hotel to get a car for you - it is actually easier to just walk outside and hail a cab.
Bottom Line: Great hotel, this is where I will stay next time I go to NYC.

I stayed at the Madera for a business trip -- had a dinner meeting at the Ritz Carlton, which is only --- blocks away.
The location (aside from my meeting) was perfect. The area is lovely for a leisurely walk (felt very safe at night), and plenty of bistros, coffee shops, and wonderful bookstores. 
And it's just a few steps from the Dupont Circle stop on the Metro. I decided to take the Metro to the hotel from National Airport (DCA) and it was a breeze -- and less than $-.--, ha! I simply took the Metro from the airport and got off at the Galleries-Chinatown stop, and then took the next train to the Dupont Circle. The hotel was - short blocks away. An easy stroll. The entire trip from the airport took perhaps twenty minutes from the moment I picked up my bag at the luggage carousel.
And the welcome I received at the hotel? It knocked my socks off. Gracious, warm, charming, polished, efficient. You'd have sworn I was a long lost relative. Or a royal duchess who'd deigned to visit them. Seriously, I was nonplussed at how lovely they were, especially Victor at the front desk.
I arrived just in time for the free wine, which was delicious. I took a glass into the little business center and sipped while I checked my email and printed off some background info on the potential client we were wooing.
This is a boutique hotel -- tiny lobby, tiny business center (closet-sized room with computer and printer, free internet), no room service, etc.
But the service and atmosphere were extraordinary. I can't say I've EVER had better service. When I called and asked for a clothes steamer and a bigger hair dryer -- these items not only arrived promptly but I got a telephone call asking if the items had been delivered (they had). When I called and asked for another robe -- it arrived in seconds.
The room (I was on the --th floor, I think it was ----, no balcony, not facing the White House or Capitol) was lovely. Very pleasing contemporary decor, free wi-fi, great portable telephone, great bed, nice sound system (wonderful music was playing when I entered the room), fabulous fabrics on the chairs, windows, and bed. Tres cool lamps and artwork. Impressive and stylish. 
The wash basin and counter are in an alcove separate from the bathroom, which is very European in size. (In other words, quite small: if you have an ensuite bath in most continental hotels, there's just enough room for the bathtub and toilet.) But I'd rather have the large airy room than a spacious bathroom, and I'm accustomed to small bathrooms in France and Italy.
Victor at the front desk took very good care of me. Recommendations, directions, taxis, cookies and milk when I came back """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""home"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" at night. I felt like a V.I.P. and I wasn't -- just an ordinary business traveler.
Breakfast at the adjoining restaurant was fine - pasties, bagels, juices, coffee-tea, jams, muffins, yogurt, cereals and milk. Not a big buffet but perfectly adequate.
But the best thing was the staff and the lovely room. I would stay here again in a heartbeat.
The nearby metro station is sooooo convenient -- you can get to the Smithsonian or Capitol Hill in a flash.
(I previously stayed at the Grand Hyatt, which has a truly spectacular,massive lobby and is great if you need multiple restaurants-bars, big conference rooms, etc. But the personal welcome and impeccable service at the Madera were second to none.)

This is my second stay at this property. Rates are great and even better if you are in the Armed Forces. The fact that I am a Reserve Officer, in the Canadian Forces, makes no difference to them - I am given the same rates as an American service member.
What makes this place so wonderful - the staff. Attentive, genuinely concerned about the well being of the guests and very helpful. 
One of the best breakfasts that I have had in a North American hotel. Happy hour is a great way to end the work day and the opportunity is there to interact with other guests if one is so inclined.
The library is awesome and a place to relax. A well equipped public gym in the basement.
I'll be back!!!

We loved this hotel! A great location, near Fenway, the Art Museum, Newbury Street etc. The staff were really perfect and the room was clean and beautiful. I have never written a review before and DON'T want this hotel to be busy the next time I want to go there but they deserve accolades. Thanks!

A nice hotel, great location close to Michigan Avenue, nice cafe and coffee shop in the main level. Service was nice and accommodating, but I slept horribly when placed in a room next to a bank of elevators. They were so loud running up and down all night that I slept between the hours of - and - a.m....made for very long days at the conference!

They want you to feel """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""home away from home"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but if you were encountering people as indifferent as the staff at this hotel at your home, you would probably pack your bags! The location is good but quite noisy if your room overlooks --th Street, the rooms are quite dark due to the colors of the furniture and the wallpaper, the elevators are a big problem (too few, as usual) and the public spaces (a little lobby) are in need of a renovation. The staff is pseudo helpful but cannot get things done. And if you add up all the various taxes and fees NY gets out of your pocket, then I ended up paying USD --- per night for one person in a relatively small room. A room which just did not give me a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""kick"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of any sorts. And their pillow-menu is a nice marketing gimmick but completely useless - as are - pillows on your bed when you just need one of them! Customers are mostly mid-westerners or foreign tourists on shopping trips, hardly any business people.

We spent the night in this boutique hotel while attending an event in San Francisco. I found them through the Joie de Vivre hotel network online. I am a big fan of small, historic hotels and this did not disappoint.
The hotel is just a few blocks from Union Square and so is very convenient to a lot of shopping, etc, but since it is a wee bit away from the Square, it's much quieter than you would expect. 
Loved the little touches such as free soda or bottled water (down near the kitchen), home-baked cookies and free internet. The buffet breakfast in the morning was WONDERFUL! Definitely miles above what is often offered for breakfast when it is included in the cost of the room at other places. The staff was also very helpful and friendly. 
If I were to stay here again (and I probably will) I would be sure to upgrade to a larger room with a larger bed. We got the double bed in their smallest room and it felt a bit tight. 
The only complaint I could possibly make (and what kept me from giving them an Excellent rating) was that the mattress in our room seemed old and worn out. Not the most comfortable I've ever slept on with obvious signs that it had seen better days. 
Other than that--I'd recommend this hotel wholeheartedly!

In the last few months I've logged roughly --,--- mi. In an effort to save money I tried staying at Motel -'s along the way.
As far as Motel - is concerned, they suck... However, this is a diamond in the VERY rough. It was very clean, quiet (something I surely can't say for any others I've stayed at).
This morning I awoke to find my TV remote wasn't working. A call to the front desk had the manager in my room in less than - min with a new one. I know, just a TV remote, but I firmly believe if you can't be trusted with the small stuff, you damn well can't be trusted with the big stuff. I WILL stay again
Fantastic hotel. Beautiful grounds, very nice rooms,super location, quiet, exceptional service and fantastic restaurant.

We attended a regional convention and were gifted by staying at the Hilton Austin Airport. From the time we drove up, with the porter and valet; to the front desk and valet to the room, we were very happy. The luggage valet told us the history of the hotel (was part of the old airport terminal). The room service was awesome and food was extraordinary. I would highly recommend use of this hotel. Easy to get around and very easy to get to if coming in on hwy -- from Houston area.

Traveled to Denver on business and will definitely stay here again, whether for work or pleasure. Room was outstanding with large desk, fast Internet, iPhone-compatible alarm clock, and a whirlpool bathtub. The staff was really accommodating and helpful, too, with questions and special requests. The hot breakfast was fairly good (complimentary national newspapers available, not just US News), the milk and cookies in the evening were a nice surprise, and the concierge had some great recommendations for activities: only a couple of blocks from the pedestrian mall and a fifteen-minute walk to the Capitol, Denver Art Museum, and public library (an architectural gem). Public transportation is also a block or two away in any direction.

A competent hotel not far from the air and space museum, Capitol, and the central sites of Washington. Also adjacent to the L'Enfant Metro station.
The room was large with a king size bed offerring a comfortable night's sleep.
All the staff were very helpful and keen to assist wherever possible.
I ate dinner and breakfast at the hotel which were OK but did not excite the palate. The food was typical US style strong on presentation, fats and sugars but lacking taste and quality.

Both from the City view room and the rooftop bar """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Print"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". We like to walk and enjoyed going to the theatre district which is only a couple of blocks away. There are plenty of small restaurants nearby and we even got caught in the middle of the filming of the NY tv series """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Smash"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The Hell's Kitchen area has plenty of character as it is very multicultural. There is some similarity to London's East End, such as Hoxton now also modernised with little bars. At the same time that you are away from the main turist spots, some of these are also not too far and within easy walking distance. Good place for those who like to walk to feel the atmosphere of New York. The view from the rooftop bar was astonishing. One of the most dramatic sunsets that I have ever seen, even on a rainy evening. Fantastic!

I loved this quaint hotel! The staff was very friendly and helpful, especially Maria at the front desk. The location was great, but it was a little bit noisy (which I totally expected - it is the city after all). If you don't mind a little noise, this hotel is for you. 
The price, location, and staff were great!

I stay at a lot of Four Seasons and this was by far the biggest disappointment.
Most -* hotels have a grand lobby, someplace where guests are welcomed and can hang out. But the Chicago Four Seasons doesn’t have that, it has an elevator bank to the main lobby. Once you’re in the main lobby, the ceilings are low, the color scheme is bland, there aren’t any windows to speak of; it feels like an old-fashioned Vegas casino. Not the kind of place you want to spend any time.
The room (an executive suite) wasn’t any better, despite a terrific view up Michigan Avenue. Very dull and old-fashioned. I thought that maybe we were in one of the un-renovated rooms, so I asked to be moved, but was told that that was a new-style room. How disappointing!!
I suppose that the hotel would have been fine for a business man… but I certainly wouldn’t bother justifying the Chicago Four Seasons to my finance department; better off at a Hilton for all the generic BLAH of the place. It was a sad and depressing place to be. Stayed for a week and regretted it every day. Big waste of money for what should have been a special part of our trip.
I’ll never ever stay here again. I’ve seen what Four Seasons can do at their properties in Istanbul, Budapest, New York, London and, of course, the George V. But this was not up to snuff.

I just got back from a trip to San Francisco for business. Booked my room on Hotwire for $---. a night. 
Checked in very late on Wednesday evening and checked out Saturday morning. 
My room was small but functional. Bed was very comfortable(love the heavenly bed). The bathroom was big enough and the shower pressure and dual head was great. They have really good bath products at Westin. The TV had about -- channels. The room has two phones (which actually seemed silly given its size). There was an iron and ironing board in the closet, as well as removable hangers and an in-room safe. 
I ordered room service and it came within about -- minutes. The food was good. The hotel lobby has large seating areas and the concierge was very helpful. They also have an ATM machine in the lobby and a small conveniece store that had food and souvenirs(store was bigger then most other hotel stores). 
The location cannot be beat. It is on Powell Street and the cross street is Geary. Very convenient for shopping and transportation. I also ate breakfast one morning at Max's in the Maxwell hotel which is right next door if you go down Geary. I reccomend their breakfasts! Very good.

After reading several positive reviews of the Hotel Beacon my family and I rented a room for - nights this fall. We enjoyed the Upper West setting with the easy access to Central Park. Although it was a bit noisy at night (we had a room facing the street) our overall experience was just fine. The staff are friendly and helpful. Although their prices are high ($--- per night), for NYC this was a bargain compared to other options we found. I would recommend this hotel to others and return to stay there myself.

I recently came to this hotel because a member of my family need care at the MD Anderson Medical Center. The room on the --th floor was dirty, dark and dingy. First, the sheet on the bed was tattered and had a blood stain! The bathroom toilet was filthy as was the vent over the bath tub. The small freezer was full of ice and could't be used. I did change rooms the second day of the trip. However the second room wasn't great either. The bathroom sink was stuffed up and the room wasn't cleaned until almost dinner time. My famllies room wasn't much better. They also had poor housekeeping service.
The business center's printer wasn't working either. The hotel has three elevators, and most times only one was working.
Clearly this hotel needs renovation and maintenance. Houskeeping should be checked by a manger after each room is cleaned. I will consider other options when I travel in the future.
We stayed at this hotel while traveling this summer. We were very impressed with the size if the suite for the price.

Trying to find a good, cheap hotel in New York is like trying to find a street corner at time square without some trying to get your money off you in one way or another.
I booked this place because it was cheap and I was visiting in December. Admittedly the airline losing my bags didn't help, but upon arriving I thought that the lobby looked ok. My room was shabby, the shared bathroom was disgusting and there appeared to be little more than cardboard between the rooms. Best of all, my door didn't actually lock, so I spent the night with my hand luggage blocking it.
This place would be far more accurately described as a youth hostel and not a particularly good one at that. 
It is quite handy for the subway and the upper west side is a nice quiet part of New York to stay in though.

My wife and I stayed there for a wedding in September ----, so really don't have that much to offer about the hotel, itself. But one thing we would want to point out is that they do have a complimentary car service to anywhere within - miles of the hotel. They don't make that especially well known, which is why I am writing this, so that Trip Advisor users know about it. Given the fact that the hotel is somewhat isolated, and it's a good half hour walk (in the heat) to the nearest commercial area (for eating, etc).,the car service is good to know about. I heard that the food prices are very expensive for breakfast at the hotel, so going to that commercial area is a nice diversion. There is a Rice Food Emporium in that area, which is a very nice and upscale gourmet market, as well as other restaurants. A positive of the hotel is that we found the rooms to be quiet.
This hotel is a little older, but it is very nice. Anat at the front desk is great!!! All of the staff does a nice job and I am very happy I picked this hotel.

The hotel is worn down. The hallways and rooms smell musty, like there was water damage at some point. The elevator made loud clunking sounds, which made me nervous every time I rode it. A train runs in front of the hotel, it makes the bed vibrate like it was coin operated. The breakfast offered is bland. I would never stay here again.

The rooms are lovely--you get your own little cabin, but what's truly fantastic is the privacy and the scenary. You feel like you on the edge of the world. It's just incredible. We had the honeymoon suite at the end of the pier and it was terrific. Neighborhood is cute--it's not fancy schmancy LaJolla, but Pacific Beach. A great breakfast cafe is walking distance, a downtown LaJolla is about a five minute drive. Would highly recommend.

On the face of it this is an awful hotel; no computerised records, small and poky rooms, pretty unclean, often falling apart, very noisy and looks as though its probably full of criminality. However, its ridiculously cheap, beds are comfy and rooms are secure, plus its about -- paces from Times Square. You really can't ask for more than that when on a tight budget, so i'd be more than happy to go again! If you are looking for class, comfort and style steer well clear.

First night of honeymoon - had been travelling for -- hours straight. Arrived at -am, having rung the hotel to warn them of late arrival due to to air delays. Receptionist ignored our presence for nearly - minutes whilst chatting on his mobile phone until I said 'excuse me' in a very direct manner. He informed us the hotel was full and that we would have to re-locate to another hotel in another area. We remonstrated about the number of months we had had this booked (-) and the response we got back was 'too bad'... My husband then informed him he had requested a bottle of champagne to be put in the room and, miraculously, the room became available... Had he not requested that bottle, we would have spent our first night of honeymoon wandering Time Square... 
The receptionist was discourteous and put us off staying here again. The room was nothing more than alright - glad we were only there for - nights. Great to be so close to Time Square and was excellent for travel around Manhatten.

Chose this hotel after much deliberation in Tripadvisor.
There was no choice but to use valet parking in this area as many others have pointed out,however as a member of the UK AA we got the AAA discount on the parking rate.
On arrival the desk staff were very friendly and efficient and when we got to the room we were very impressed.The room was large,well appointed and very clean.--mins afterwards we got a call from the desk to check if everything was to our liking;we've never had that before!!
We were given a quiet courtyard view room as requested on the top floor.Several people have remarked about the shower;we didnt really find it a problem during our - night stay.
Room service was fine;of particular note was the courteous attitude from all the hotel staff which made our stay so enjoyable.
We were able to print our boarding cards in the free --mins allowed online.
It was a real pleasure to stay at the Hyatt;it is very convenient for all Fishermans wharf attractions whilst being sufficiently far away from the piers and bay front shops to be an oasis of calm after a hard day pounding the streets!!
Recommended without hesitation.

The hotel looks decadent from the outside and the value for the money is even more disappointing. The room looks old, the bed is not comfortable, the restaurant is good quality but rather expensive. 
During my stay, the laundry took - days to be delivered, luckily I stayed long enough. The noise in the room was terrible because they had a wedding going all night long with music at high volume regardless my calling to the front desk - times. The corridor where often covered with rubbish and cleaned maybe once a day.

great downtown Chicago shopping location, nice, quiet, clean room, everyone on the staff was very friendly and very helpful, i would stay here again, only fault, free wi fi in the room would make this hotel A+++. recommend this hotel

The Affinia Manhattan is my favorite New York hotel. I couldn't wait to get back on a long-delayed vacation. The overall service was fine - not outstanding this time. Staff is always very friendly, but a few things happened that were annoying. My debit card was hit for $--- without any notice. My wife called from home asking why the money was taken from our account. It turned out it only appeared to be removed - a pre notice would have been nice. lt took two trips to the desk to clarify what happened. Beverage items were not replaced one day. Ice was never delivered as promised another night. Irritating.
The location is great - a primary reason I returned. The fitness center was also nice. 
The room was very nice, but lacked a microwave and ice. You've got to be kidding! Strange! I was alone this time and got a deluxe guest room through AARP. My wife and I had a suite last year. I was in town for six nights and the lack of a microwave and ice bucket became a real issue. The front desk offered to warm up any food for me. Yuk. For the price paid, this seemed punitive in the absence of a kitchen area. Wierd! 
My daughter stayed a few nights and the sofa bed was nice. Great bed and pillows. Nice decor. Again, remarkable remodeling job. Where is the microwave and ice????
The Niles restaurant is quite good. Excellent food creatively presented. Sea bass - WOW!
My flight home was cancelled and I ended up spending the night at the Lexington Marco in Flushing NY, seven minutes from Laguardia in Queens. Chinatown is nearby with easy access to subway and rail (-- min to Manhattan). Entered room and there is a microwave-refrigerator combination, an ice machine and ice bucket. Not as large as Affinia deluxe guest room, but very nice and comfortable. Shuttle service to Laguardia and shopping districts. Excellent authentic Italian restaurant - Magna Risorante. Might consider the Marco during my next stay in New York..

I booked this hotel for $----night off Priceline. Hotel is nicely situated on --th between -th & -th close to Times Square. I was hesitant about staying at this hotel once I found out there is a CAT that lives in the lobby. I was unable to get out of my reservation after several emails with Priceline for the cat reason. 
I was pleasantly surprised with my overall very satisfactory stay at this hotel. I arrived early around -:-- AM. Room was't ready but they took my bags. I asked for a large room. I received a complimentary upgrade to a King size room. Usually this is a $---night upgrade. Room was very small for NYC standards, but still worked out ok. Bathroom is small, but shower pressure was great. Bathroom has a pedestal sink. Room had everything I needed. Even though the website said there were bathrobes, I didn't see any in the closet. No coffee-tea in the room. Free bottle of water in room which was replaced everyday. Bed is very, very comfortable. Flatscreen tv with good selection of channels.
Employees are extremely nice. Lobby has a wonderful evening ambiance. Hung out one evening with friends and had tea-coffee service. Did not try restaurant. Plenty of taxis outside.
If you book this hotel, you will be fine.

We really enjoyed our stay at The Westin in Seattle. We were able to walk nearly everywhere we wanted to go like Pike's Market and the Harbor Front. We were also near the monorail and that was an easy way to get over to the Space Needle and the fun museums in that area. Our hotel concierge was great. We made several reservations that included transportation and everything went smoothly. The rooms were very spacious and comfortable and the view from our room over the Olympic mountains was incredible. Down side was the very low water pressure in both our sink and shower.

The Stanford Court, with its motor court, exudes a contemporary San Francisco feeling. Atop Nob Hill, it provides views of the city that are lasting. The rooms are well furnished and have plenty of space. On our visit there were a number of business travelers so it must have that appeal. The advantage is being on Nob Hill which is literally above the city. The downside is the distance to other areas of the city. While the hills can obviously be walked, for some people cabs will be needed. The Powell Street street car line goes by the hotel. So, if your room faces Powell, expect to hear the clang clang early in the morning. But, all in all this is a very nice hotel.

I'm always happy to stay there, and the friends that I've recommended it to have enjoyed it too. The check-in is very friendly, maybe because they are sitting down at desks instead of standing on aching feet all day. The front desk also provides helpful and knowledgeable concierge service. The highlight of the hotel for me is its nightly happy hour, which features an excellent antipasto bar and a variety of beers and wines. The complimentary breakfast is also quite nice, since it is set up on each floor, although I would appreciate some more lower-carb options, like a wider variety of unsweetened cereals. Personally, during four separate stays, my room has always been quiet and comfortable, but reading the other reviews, I suppose you have to be careful about the garbage truck and alley noises. Again, I've never run it that problem myself. The location is ideal, within walking distance of quite a few destination restaurants. No pool, but the exercise room is great.

Stayed here a few times over the years, sometimes for part of a day intransit. Great front desk staff, very efficient and helpful, just OK restaurants but there's lots of place in the airport, and nice comfortable rooms with everything you could need. Lots of electrical outlets, and a nice big flat screen TV to unwind with.
Enjoy!

Am writing because I could find no other guest reviews, just Fodors and Washington Post. We did not know quite what to expect, because BW Clarmont is not in the AAA Ohio Tourbook. So we did seriously consider elsewhere but now are glad we stayed at the Clarmont. It was very nice, remodeled and clean. Good bathroom. We had one of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""suite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" rooms with microwave and fridge, which was nice. Actually, all rooms are the same size, but the suite ones have a sitting area with foldout couch instead of a second queen bed. We were concerned about the area, but it was OK, and the German Village, just adjacent, was quaint and interesting. Also, breakfast at the adjacent Clarmont restaurant is very good and reasonably priced (tho' dinner meals are expensive and a la carte). All in all, it was a very good experience.

We had to change our plans while we were in Washington D.C. and ended up staying at this beautiful Marriott. The location is outstanding with easy access to the Metro and it is close to many of the attractions of D.C.. Our room was clean and comfortable and the staff was helpful. The area surrounding has several nice places to eat. It was a wonderful change from the beginning of our trip and we are thankful we found it.

We arrived on a Tuesday and stayed on the Elvis floor room ----. The bathroom had used dental floss on it which leads me to believe the bathroom wasn't even cleaned. The bed had stains all over the comforter, someone elses hair and a bottle of eye solution fell out of the sheets. I WILL NEVER RECOMMEND NOR STAY AT THIS PLACE AGAIN!!!!! There are a lot of other places to choose from. PLEASE STAY AWAY!!!!!

This is my first time to stay in this hotel and I must say that it is probably the nicest hotel I've ever stayed in; especially for the price. It is located in a very nice area of Houston. It is located right in the middle of The City Centre plaza and there are plenty of great restaurants and bars, all within steps of the hotel. The hotel staff were all very cordial. The W is located in a great tourist location, in the heart of Times Square. It is close to all of the Broadway shows, as well as most of the off-Broadways. Decent dining options abound in the area, and they are all reachable on foot.

The second room was better, with reasonable lighting in the bathroom. The living area also suffered from a lack of sufficient lighting. We turned-on every light and kept the window fully open to take advantage of the daylight, but after sunset the room was dark and dreary due to the taupes and browns used decorate. The bathroom had a great rain-shower (no tub), and also had a cool frosted-glass wall which helped a bit with lighting. Sound proofing was good, and we had a quiet stay. Overall our experience was good, and since all we do is sleep at the hotel, the small nits are not as critical in this case. I don't know too much about NYC so can't really compare to others, but all in all the room was decent for the price. Had a few issues which weren't addressed very promptly, but in the end they gave us a credit for our troubles. I agree with others that charging for internet access is a bit ridiculous.

I've stayed at the Commonwealth maybe a half-dozen times over the past five years. It's always a joy. Clean, convenient, and the staff are incredibly helpful and professional. Not only is wi-fi included, but on this latest trip, I found they had a charger on the desk in the room for iPhones, Androids, etc. Very, very thoughtful and helpful. This is a great hotel: Professional, convenient, reliable.

Late at night (and I walked back home most nights after -AM by myself and felt ok) the area south of the hotel is deserted, but the block north on Polk is a little active with druggies but they keep to themselves. Seems the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""activity"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" starts at Geary where the hotel is and goes north. The staff at the hotel were not unfriendly to us (as some here complained) and were quite polite. We asked for a quiet room and they gave us one looking out over the back alley - which is weird as it looks to a blank wall of the AMC Theater building. Nice big California shutters on the windows, decent finishings and comfortable beds.
One complaint: one glass in the room. When we asked for more, we were directed to the table in the lobby that always has complimentary coffee and a stack of paper cups there. A little cheap.
The hotel seems to cater to young European toursts (ie: college students-backpackers) so if you get them above you or beside it can be noisy.
There's not much right around this hotel. City Hall is a few blocks south (as is Market Street & the subway). Union Square is about a -- minute walk to the east down Geary. There is a Whole Foods just up the street. That was good.
Our room had a safe, but you have to rent the key for $-.---day.
All in all, better than expected - but not plush.

Location was great, couple of blocks from time square, food and shopping. I can't say enough about the hotel staff -helpful,kind & they cleaned the room very.well. The door man was a nice touch. We were greated with smiles by the whole staff.. The concierge was out standing and really helped plan our time with many suggestions. Rooms are not large but it is well laid out. They have a mini kitchen area and a little grocery stores around the corner to stock up. I suggest taking the tour bus approx. $-- per person. It takes you all over the hot spots. And you can get off the bus and take as much time as needed to sight see (bus runs every -- min) Take extra cash as eating is not cheap. We kept things to munch on in our little kitchen area and ate one good meal out.

I stayed at The Intercontinental Century City during my trip to LA in January ----. It was a pleasant experience - since I booked the hotel by calling them up, the staff was cordial enough to provide me with the best room possible - booking for smooth and easy, check in was equally smooth - they knew of my arrival in advance and my room was neat and clean. I was on the -th floor and my room gave me a great view of the city. The service at the hotel was quick, the food was good whereas I found the bar to be bit more expensive than normal standards - however the hotel's proximity to the Westfield Shopping Place (I hope I am remembering the correct name) is a blessing - you get everything there from food to drinks and even grocery and other shopping needs. I had a complimentary internet service at my room, which was a blessing for me.

I booked a short trip to NYC on a whim and needed somewhere cheap to stay in Manhattan and came across The Jane. I was nervous about the bathrooms being shared but they were immaculately clean and I never had to wait for a shower or the toilet. The rooms are as small as advertised, but there was still plenty of storage space for my luggage. If you're the type of person who needs alot of bells and whistles in your room or who plans on spending alot of time in the room, this is not the place for you. The rooms were comfortable, and the flatscreen tv, wall outlets, and free wifi were nice. But really you should only stay at the Jane if you view your hotel room just as a place to lay your head. With the cheap rates and incredible location, this is perfect for travelers looking for a place they can drop their bags, explore the city, come back for sleep, and then head back out again. Can't wait to try it again on my next visit.

I must say that the people here are lovely, and everyone is very nice. We stayed a week, and the place was clean and kept clean, and overall a great value for the price. But I only had one complaint. 
We were booked for - days, and on the -th day my girlfriend and I decided to try to book an extra night. We were on our way out for the day and stopped by the reservation desk to do so. I really wanted to give this hotel a good review. We even took nice pictures of the room to post after our trip, but this problem caused me way too much grief on my last day. I would never stay here again. Next time I will stay somewhere that doesn't think they can get away with such things.
I stayed for business for a week; the rooms were well furnished, I had room service which was fine; lots of local places to eat. Great location for business-shopping-jogging!

The lobby and hallways are in desperate need of a facelift, and finding your room through the winding maze of corridors can be a bit challenging, but the room was decent and had cable TV, a mini fridge and a sink. An added bonus was that because this hotel is located on the end of a street, it was pretty quiet for New York. Not a lot of street traffic going by at - in the morning. The shared bathroom was ok, but I'd bring shower shoes next time.

The Hard Rock Rocks! This is my second stay at a Hard Rock and they keep out doing themselves. Its a very cool, comfortable hotel in the heart of San Diego central to EVERYTHING. Try MaryJanes for breakfast best Cheese Blintz's I've ever had.

My son and I stayed here for a weekend to attend the NMCA World Street Finals and LSX Shootout. The hotel is conveniently located less than five minutes from the raceway and there are lots of places to eat nearby. The only downside is there are no places to park a trailer at the hotel. The staff is very friendly and accommodating.

I was setting up a trip for one of my best friends for her and her significant other for a romantic get-a-way, i recommended The St. Regis, Washington DC. I have stayed there in the past and always have had a great stay. The staff was very attentive, especially the concierge staff (Lida and Alex) that were following up on transportation that had been set up for an airport pick-up. They made sure the room was ready upon their arrival and that all the details of their stay was flawless. They are truly professional concierge! Thank you so much for making their stay impeccable!

I just got my credit card bill to find they charged me for using the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""refreshment center"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I never touched. I was also charged another $-- that the woman on phone could not even explain (already paid for parking). The lotion in bathroom was open with a long dark curly hair attached. The bartenders were too busy talking to each other and watching NBA Finals to help. The breakfast server (male) was very unprofessional (coming from an ex-Starwood breakfast server).

My pal and I just needed a one night stay and the hubby let go of a few """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Reward"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" points so our stay was FREE! That isn't actually true, they rape you with the parking, $-- for overnight parking, glad it was only one night. One would think if you are staying at their hotel, the parking would be FREE!
Less than -- from the airport, nice free breakfast, very new, still very clean.
The thing I found the most fascinating was that all of the Marriott properties were connected in this complex and yes it is like a complex.
Accessible and comfortable smoking area for you smokers.
Check in was easy, the guy at the desk failed to tell us we would need to use the room key to get us up to the --th floor. Now I realize if we had just read the sign when we got into the elevator we would have known, but we were dead tired after - hours on the road......just a thot!
Every Marriott property I stay at my only complaint are the beds. With their buying power one would think that they could put DECENT, COMFORTABLE beds in their properties and I don't mean the linens, I mean the actual mattress!
The room was very well lite, including the bathrooms. Plenty of room, large work-desk area with a comfortable chair, even our view from the room was great.
For those of you looking for a place to stay for the ---- Super Bowl, this is a good location and the rooms are huge, even had a sofa sleeper, just be prepared for the parking fees.

Outstanding hotel! The room that we were allocated was stunning - very clean, bed was the best bed I have ever slept in, lots of quirky design - although not over designed.
We stayed over Christmas, the staff made us feel so welcome - my husband and I have worked in hotels for years - I would hire all of the reception staff in a heart beat to work in our hotel, bright, fun, friendly, knowledgeable - overall fantastic! 
Morgans thank you for making our stay in New York unforgettable, we will be back!

great place to stay if you are in New York for a mini break. Whilst the rooms are small.. how big do they need to be when you should be out exploring the city. the complimentary toiletries were lovely and the fluffy robe made having a bath after a long day exploring lovely. location by central park is great for shopping on -th avenue, and strolling through the park... and you are conveniently a short distance from the subway to go downtown. staff were friendly, and this is a buzzy hotel. whilst this may have been more of a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""scene"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" a few years ago, with the deals available this is a very trendy good value for money place to stay.

I was here for one night for business. Found the hotel to be quite nice. The location was good for me and I walked there from Penn Station.
The lobby is very nice and looked like it had a cool bar, but was unfortunately closed for renovations.
The room itself was nice. I liked the look of it, very modern. Very comfortable bed. It was tiny, but that's NYC. I was fine there for a night and I was alone. Probably would have wanted something bigger if I was staying for an extended trip.

The television had five ESPN channels and five other channels. Most had static in the picture and none of them were NBC? What gives?
Also, the telephone in the room had so much static on it that it was unusable.

Amazing Stay. Great location, great staff, awesome housekeeping, very
comfortable bed & linens. Very Cool hotel.

Although eventually we were happy with our room, we did have to ask to be moved from the original one allocated. We had booked a king size room also requesting a quiet location (after reading reviews on Trip Advisor). We got a good sized room, but everything seemed a little tired.
Pleased with the front desk for not hesitating to change our room. Well located hotel and helpful conciege recommended a good Thai restuarant for us to try. We ended up eating there twice.

We stayed for - nights to visit DC and have a little fun. The Hotel in my oppion was very luxirous but for the price of the room and the customer service the value is not worth it. In turn if you are going to DC do not stay here!!!!

A friend and I stayed here as part of a Contiki tour in May ----.
We found the rooms to be very small and the bathroom you could barely move around it it was so tiny. 
The beds were comfortable and the lobby was very grand looking. As we were only here on a tour we didn't speak to any staff other than the door man who was always very polite and helpful.
The hotel was within very easy walking distance to Westfield Mall and the main shopping area. Also very easy to catch a tram down to the Wharfs to visit Pier -- and Alcatraz. 
I wouldn't choose to stay here again simply because of the size of the rooms.

Just got through with a three-night stay there. The staff was supurb....VERY friendly and eager to please. Unfortunately it is in a bad location. It's about a ----- minute walk to Times Square. The closest attraction is the Empire State Building, about - blocks away. The decor is tired and old. Perhaps there are nicer rooms there, but ours was pretty lame. The highly touted spa and work out room were also small, dated, and shabby. Sorry to say I wouldn't stay there again, in spite of the great staff.

I attempted to stay here overnight in Feb ---- for a birthday celebration-long week-end. Everything the other reviews say is true: the rude staff who speak no english (we had to wait --- hour for somebody to show up at the desk to check us in), the squalid conditions, the brick wall view, the bare lightbulb in the ceiling, the mis-representation on-line. The attitude of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""you get what you pay for"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" should not really apply here, because I've stayed in boutique hotels for the same price, and this is just a disgrace. Fortunately, Orbitz (I think that's where I booked it) gave me a full refund after a phone conversation, and told me they've received complaints about it before, and that they would alter the hotel's profile on the site (which had since been done.)

My friend and I were on a two day getaway to enjoy Seattle. We booked this hotel off of Hotwire not entirely knowing where we would be staying only knowing that it was a four star or better. We ended up getting Hotel Monaco. We were extremely excited after reading many great reviews from trip advisor. I find trip advisor to be most helpful in booking a hotel since it's real people booking hotels and their experiences. This hotel did not disappoint; I absolutely loved the modern decor in the foyer all the way up to our room. Super funky and the beds were most comfortable. This hotel had an awesome location. Just enough off the beaten path to be quite but only a few blocks from all the fun. The ocean was about four blocks down the street and transit was super easy to figure out for any other part like the Sky Needle. This brings me to our awesome service we received from Jesse Patterson (not sure on the last name) All I know is he was extremely helpful and managed to get us booked into the Sky Needle restaurant and directed us to any place we needed. After making us laugh and letting us know about their complimentary wine hour we then head out four our boat cruise. The cruise was awesome and the weather was perfect. Only problem is we missed our wine hour; which was too bad since we loved the quick witted Jesse. After our cruise managed to get a little more shopping in and then headed to dinner. The views were amazing and the food was just as good and at the end of our meal Jesse called in and had a desert sent to our table (btw thank you Jesse!!!). The customer service from this hotel was amazing and can make a real difference on your stay. All the hotel staff were great and I look forward to coming here again; next time with my family! 
Also friendly warning that I don't think reflects too bad on the hotel but just a warning for other guests is I did have to make a long distance call to Vancouver, BC because I forgot my phone and I found the charge was pretty large. I knew it would be expensive but just beware it is about - dollars a minute and a - - - min call home cost -- dollars. Not a huge deal but good to know so there are no surprises. Also the parking was expensive at -- dollars a night but that is also to be expected down town Seattle.

we arrived at the New Yorker Hotel after travelling -- hours from Sydney. My partner and I had paid for a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""deluxe city view room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" so upon checking in we were quite upset to see that our city view was in fact a view into someone's office about - metre away, and the deluxe room was not so deluxe. in fact, there were no working power points in the room, and I have no idea how the hotel expected - people plus luggage to fit into the space. I know that NYC rooms are small, but this was ridiculous. we couldn't even walk past the edge of the bed.

I could understand if they gave this room to a local staying for - night on business, but not to overseas guests for - nights. They explained that they could change our room in the morning and we were happy with this result.
The next day we changed rooms and were very happy with the outcome. It was actually what we had paid for! Great views of Empire State and Madison Square Garden.
After this incident though I felt that Reception staff were rude to us (because we complained?) and weren't very keen at all to make our stay enjoyable. The lady at Concierge was generally helpful but would sometimes let out a frustrated noise when asked to do something that she may have felt was too hard. The diner was great value and you could easily have breakfast in there without needing lunch as well, the meals were huge.
Great location for first time visitors to NYC but unfortunately don't think I'd stay again after a few not-so-good experiences during our stay.

My husband and I stayed here for - night while attending the AFI Film Festival in LA.. As out of towners, we were a bit unsure of the hotel, as it is in an okay, but a little rough around the edges, part of town. Anyway, the hotel has a gated parking lot, which really helps add to the security, and it has a cute little interior courtyard overlooking a swimming pool. It isn't a luxury hotel by any means, but it was clean, quiet, and I felt quite safe the whole trip. It is a family run hotel and the staff was very helpful to us. Overall, I definitely recommend it!

I was at SLS for a bachelorette party. We had - rooms booked. First, if you book a room with - doubles, know that the beds are """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""full"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" NOT """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""queen"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" - and the pillows are XL-King pillows, so it's impossible for - people to sleep in the bed with their own pillows.
