I will say that the Hotel Gym was one of the nicest I have been to, so maybe hang out in there - there is plenty of light! I would still recommend the Viceroy over SLS and now that the new W Hollywood opened, I will try to stay there.
The W is a nice hotel with a great location. The staff is warm and friendly. Although the rooms are small they are definitely upscale.

The hotel has a great staff and definitely is turning around with the new manager, she is always running around taking care of things. Everyone is about new, but great smiles and friendly attitude, that goes a long way. Some rooms have been renovated , others haven't but they keep them very clean! Also they will have new TV's in a few months. great location off ---.

I had the pleasure of staying at the Maritime hotel for my anniversary. We were lucky enough to stay in the penthouse at the top of the hotel. Needless to say my wife and I were ready to move in! Spacious, clean and cool with a rooftop terrace and a view of the entire city. The decor followed the theme of the rest of the hotel and the double fire places were a real bonus! The wet bar-snack bar was ridiculous with its over the top offerings. There was enough alcohol there to throw a party for -- people! The suite offered a great living area as well as a small table to eat, though we chose to eat our room service selections on the long coffee table in front of the big flat screen. I highly recommend the french toast for a morning after pick me up. 
Service throughout the hotel was friendly and attentive. The bar area was great as were the cocktails. The only small inconvenience I could think of, if I must be nit picky, is that to reach the very top floor where our suite was, you had to go up a short flight of stairs. Overall our stay was amazing and the location was great.
The location is great! Price is reasonable as well. Front desk staff is friendly, especially Elizabeth! Shes patient, professional, and very approachable. Strongly recommend this place

I travel a lot for work and stay at many different hotels (Ritz, Hilton, Marriott, etc.) but when i go to NYC at least - weeks a year and I always book the Trump Soho for a number of reasons. The staff is wonderful, I always get greeted and welcomed back, asked if they can do anything to make my stay better, to simply put it, they go the extra mile without me feeling that they are trying too hard (like other nicer hotels do). The rooms are large, clean, luxurious and have all the amenities that you could ask for. (Tip: if you need an iron & ironing board, call the desk they will bring one up to you, I spent more time then I would like to admit looking for it!) I like to workout while traveling and they have a great gym that has everything you need. I would recommend this to everyone and anyone that wants to have a great stay in NYC.

I stayed two nights at this hotel during a conference in Mountain View. It is ultra convenient to the airport and the shuttle runs on demand which is great. It is less than - minutes from airport to the hotel. Check-in was quick and courteous. My room was a little outdated in terms of decor but was very, very clean. Bed was comfortable and there were plenty of pillows. There was a large flat-screen TV with an abundance of channels. Also, my bathroom had the standard weak hair dryer, but there was a stronger """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""real"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hair dryer hanging in a bag on the bathroom door. I pre-ordered breakfast room service for one morning and the room-service arrived on time, warm and tasty. I also needed the bellman's help in getting a cab on a rainy morning and the guys out the front of the hotel did everything they could to get me a cab when there were none anywhere! I also ate in the sushi restaurant. Food was ok, but service was excellent. In sum, the location, cleanliness and service of this hotel far make-up for any shortcomings in terms of being a little older and not as hip. I would recommend this hotel and would definitely stay there again.

We stayed at this hotel due to the great reviews. Indeed, the numerous amenities (e.g., evening snacks, in-room computer, bathrobes) were a nice touch and contributed to our overall nice stay. However, the hotel lost major points when the manager’s wife (who checked us in) placed us in a second floor room. Almost a month earlier when we made reservations, we requested the third floor because we needed quiet and didn’t want anyone above us. 
When I reminded the woman at the front desk that we really needed a quiet room, she insisted repeatedly that it was. Nope, within hours, we heard someone stomping around, dropping things, etc. overhead. When I went back to the front desk, a couple who had just walked in with no reservations was given a third-floor room. I spoke to the same woman who checked us in and explained the situation (and why we had even requested a quiet room in the first place) and was told the third floor was completely booked and that the reason we were given a second floor was because a group was on the top floor and she didn’t want us to be disturbed (!!). I didn’t understand that logic because members of that large group were also placed in several rooms on our floor. We tried to make the best of it since we were only staying two nights, but being awakened several times between midnight and -:--am made me regret booking this hotel.
We just wanted to be able to sleep peacefully and didn’t get it. That staff member had an opportunity to: a) fulfill our request – made weeks in advance – upon check-in, as they clearly had availability on the top floor at that time; and b) just move us and forget the lame excuse of not wanting to disturb us by sticking us in the middle of a large group, which we were anyway.
We actually planned to stay at this hotel for several other visits in the coming months, but we will definitely book elsewhere. (The manager himself and a young woman at the front desk were awesome, though. Wish they happened to be the ones who checked us in, in the first place.)

David and Tiffany were amazing ...they set the tone for my entire stay at this gorgeous property. You would never know you are only - minutes from SeaTac. The service, the rooms, the ambiance, the food and the location made me feel like I was in Telluride Colorado. Five stars for this property ... a must stay if you need to prepare and unwind for that important business appointment in Seattle. FIVE Stars !!
The best location, staff, facilities, view. Don't bother to look at any other hotels in Seattle. Stay here.

My boyfriend and I stayed in a standard guest room, but, at any other hotel I've stayed in, this room would have been a suite. I usually stay at B & B's or smaller boutique hotels so this was quite a different experience, one I'm sorry I put off for so long. The hotel itself is so beautiful and the service was top notch. Our room was totally pristine and the staff was really knowledgeable and professional. I often feel when a staff is too professional, it can convey a certain iciness, however, at the The Grand Del Mar, it never felt this way. The views are gorgeous and they have the best pool I’ve ever been seen.
There are so many amazing features and free amenities, like shoe shines and turndown service, it really is the lap of luxury. I usually don't spend that much on hotel rooms, but I felt it was worth every penny. I would recommend this hotel to anyone who wants to splurge a little or, if this is the sort of place you are used to, I can't imagine you'd be disappointed. It was a really romantic getaway and I can’t wait to go back!

I had a brief stat at the Marquis Marriott for two nights and found it to be an adequate hotel. The room was appointed nicely and generally clean however the vent above the tub-shower was filthy. 
The fitness center is surprisingly small for a hotel of this size but again well-appointed and very accessible. 
While not necessarily warm the staff were professional and helpful with all questions.
Clearly the best attribute of the Marquis is the fact it's in the heart of Times Square and the Theater District which is why they can charge the outrageous room rates they do. 
Overall nothing remarkable although given the room price in any other US city this should have been a penthouse experience.

I've stayed at the Marriott Marquis on several occasions when visiting the Theater district. Its a great place to stay as far as logistics are concerned- whether you plan on staying in the immediate area or if you plan to venture out to other areas via cab or subway. As far as rates are concerned, if you book early enough, the rates are great for the value of the stay. Since the area typically generates higher fares, if you get in early the rates are very valuable. 
A quick note when booking at the Marriott, request a room on the south east corridor, this will give you a fantastic view of Times Square South. See the attached picture.
For accommodations, the check-in-check-out, valet, in-room dining, etc. is seamless.

Stayed for - nights in April (room ----) and highly recommend it. Spring break with my teenage son and adjoining room with relatives. Adjoining rooms were located right off the elevator lobby and ice machine but it wasn't loud at all. Really heard nothing. Walls were very soundproof. This hotel is in a great location very close to Times Square (on -th Ave between --th and --th). Lots of places very close by on -th Avenue (Starbucks, Food Emporium, liquor store, bodega). Restaurant nextdoor, Pigalle, was very good. Breakfast for - (eggs, homefries, toast, juice, coffee) was $---. I went to Food Emporium the next morning for breakfast sandwiches. Great beds, pillows and down blanket. Fridge, microwave. Flat screen. Safe. Free wifi. Bathroom was small but spacious countertop (many hotels in NYC have little to no bathroom counter space). Good shower. Excellent service. The rooftop bar is not accessible from the hotel; have to go around the corner to a special door. Couldn't go due to a private party but pics looked nice. Would definitely return.

The hostel bathrooms were quite dirty. Housekeeping no longer makes beds and you must ask to have them made. The reservation staff is wonderful though. However, you will not pay what you reserved at all because they will cheat you and you will pay around -- and up more than what you reserved. This is not recommended for people traveling on a budget because you will need to pay more than you budgeted. It is actually a nice hostel, with the exception of the bathroom, making beds thing, and the price scam. Other hostels charge what you booked. Everything is in cash....

Our family stayed here in July. the location was great. close to the metros and in walking distance to most things. The staff was friendly and the hotel clean. The rooms however are very very small. we had a room with - double beds and there were four of us. There was very little space around the bed and the bathroom was even worse interms of space. The pool was very disappointing. There was mold along the walls of the pool and hot tub. After a long day of walking and sight seeing the hot tub sounded good but it was not something we wanted to get in to.

I have had the pleasure of staying at the Grand Hyatt Washington twice already; and, will no-doubt return... sigh. It is the destination hotel for an annual conference that I attend. Check-in is always crowded; and, on this visit it seemed that no rooms were ready. As such, everyone was checking their bags with the valet. Of course, these guys had their hands out quicker for a tip than they did the luggage tag. But, this is fairly typical of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""luxury"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" brands that feel it is all right to charge for every little convenience. The kicker here, is the $-- a day you have to pay for the fitness center -- WOW, I get that for free at Holiday Inn Express and Hampton Inn. I paid it on my last visit; but, just didn't feel it was worth it on this trip -- I just skipped the shuttle to the convention center and walked every day. I specifically asked for decaf coffee in my room; and, evey day I had to go down and get some from either the front-desk or housekeeping. The first time the front desk person asked, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""well, you are welcome to try our Starbucks."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Yeah, free coffee in the room vs. $-.-- for an Americano decaf -- no thanks, I can do the math on that one. I attended a few functions at the hotel; and, the food was outstanding (mostly appetizers). These were either fundraising events or educational; and, the service was fine. I am a member of Hyatt Gold Passport; and, I have to point out that when I expressed my dissatisfaction, they did """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""reward"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" me with extra stay points, which is the reason this review is higher than I would normally apply.

My wife and my second stay here. We like AAA rated hotels and they are -D. It is a clean, pleasant, well-maintained conveniently located hotel, with all amenities close to the airport and tourist attractions. The lobby which gave us a welcome to the hotel. The area feels safe and is extremely easy to get to if you are flying in and renting a car (they do have comp airport shuttle service). It appears to attract many business people, and we were allowed check-in with no hesitation when we arrived early. The desk was quick and efficient. The hotel is easy to find and only minutes from the Rental Car Pickup Points. The hotel has plenty of parking space which is convenient to the entrance. 
The room was clean and good size and in nice condition. Like they offer fee internet access. The morning continental breakfast is an added value we like very much but there is also a Denny’s next door.
We would stay again as it’s a nice property and the location is great. l’d recommend this hotel to anyone.

This is a hotel that with a bit of work would be much better. Stayed for - days but had a dollar store plastic garden chair instead of a handicap shower chair, had no soap dish in the shower, no method of securing the shower head, and the floor flooded with use of the shower. All of these conditions require quite easy and inexpensive fixes but it appears they don't care. Many instances of deferred maintenance including old construction materials standing beside one entrance door-just looks bad and allows bugs to accumulate. My husband killed - small bugs in our bed the first night, they moved us to another room but I found a bug there and in the dining room. Just poorly kept!

This is the third time my girlfriends and I have treated ourselves to a stay at the Lenox Hotel for an annual get-together. From the moment you reach the curb to the moment you step off to say goodbye the staff makes you feel like a special guest. The bellmen are friendly and helpful and you will find the front desk staff also very friendly, attentive and professional. As you turn to go up to the rooms, the fireplace in the lobby will becon you to sit and relax. Our two rooms were beautifully decorated and exceptionally clean with a postcard view of the city (don't forget to look out at dark as well to see the city lights). The updated bathrooms are spa-like with Aveda bath products, fluffy towels and even guest robes to use during your stay. The Lenox is also in a great location near Newbury St. and other fun shopping, many fine restaurants and tourist attractions. You will not be disappointed in choosing this hotel for your stay in Boston and I suspect your first stay will not be your last!

Have stayed here several time and considerit a good value. Package deals can make it even better..We walk to most venues and enjoy the city. Consider the package deals.
David and Jean Baskin

In terms of amneties, and all the services of the hotel, I found it excellent, including the building and a very professional staff. Location for downtown in not good because in the the subway you have to change twice, however for the airport is most convenient.

I stayed at this hotel whilst on business. Initial impressions were a little disappointing - it doesn't look much like a hotel and there was no restaurant or bar to speak of. As it was pouring outside, I resorted to ordering off the in-house dining menu - which extended about as far as a toasted panini. To be fair to the hotel however there is some refurbishment being undertaken with a restaurant-lounge to be opened in a couple of months. Staff seemed very friendly and attentive and whilst the complimentary continental breakfast might not suit all, I found it pretty good. It was served in there penthouse room which is very nice on sunny morning. My room was clean and modern however the bathroom was pretty small and without a bath (fine for me but don't think the wife would have been too impressed by it!). However what can't be overlooked is the price, which given its location is very good value - especially compared to some of the other luxury hotels in the area. This hotel might not be everyone's cup of tea however, depending on circumstance it is somewhere I would consider staying again.

Everything about the Ace Hotel just adds to your enjoyment. The excellent bar - where the tip is included in the price, a great thing for a non American like me - which doubles as a club or gig venue hosting very exciting acts. The vibe is open and friendly but also very trendy, without being pretentious. The staff were incredibly helpful. The rooms: the bed sent me to sleep almost instantly and the touches of having lovely products in the bathroom and a beautiful tapestry on the wall made the whole experience just that bit extra above what I expected. My fridge was contained within a box that roadies keep live music gig equipment in.

Great place huge clean room , - tv`s ,private bedroom , nice cafe with a buffet meals and room service the pool was awesome clean in the morning , great price and a very friendly front desk i had a very nice stay thank you ramada keep up the good work !!!!

I enjoyed a double-hitter when I visited Boston for the Boston Book events in October and this property and its people took top marks with this """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Book Mark"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I know I'm on a winner when the doorman lets me know he takes owership of his curb-front, the front desk darlings smile like Cheshire cats with cheerful service and the bell-hop hops-to with gusto matching a Red Sox fan with season-long dug-out passes. The bifockled old fella at the informtion desk could have easily filled a book with local information I needed to tick all the boxes, and when I was all done at the end of the day, I had no fewer than three in-house watering holes to enjoy a cleansing ale or two. Its not just the location, location location that's great about this place... I love a wide-beamed corridor, and old-time elevators that can still manage to hold a baby-grand piano or two to slip into the Judy Garland sized sweet-heart suites... any room in this bit of Beantown history is a keeper in my book...
My top-hat's off to the owners, whom I can only guess take great pride in the team... I left the hotel with the suggestion that my floor maid is a solid candidate for cloning. And to think of it, I might have sadly picked a property on the outskirts, been condemmed to cabfares and conjested intersections... I was in this one property, under the skin of one of America's best cities to take-on by foot!
I can count on one hand, the number of hotels that tick all the boxes of this Beantown property. My next visit from Australia, will be with my family troops in tow, and I know where we'll be resting our heads!
Mark Sheehan, Sydney Australia
Author of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The Scent of a Dollar"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" by New Holland Publishing
Access to Grand Central Terminal is about the only thing great about this hotel. There are so many better, unique hotels in NYC for about the same price.

Too expensive for what we received. The room was small, not very clean. The place had no restaurants for moderate to high prices and nothing in walking range. That Disney recommends this hotel is puzzling. It is not """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""child friendly"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" nor is it convenient to the historic places in the city. I was not happy here.

I ran into a major headache with this Hyatt over a Priceline booking that went missing, but the hotel people were so very nice about getting it straightened out for me after the fact that I'm writing my first ever online review. The hotel is only perhaps two years old and is exceptionally clean. Like all Hyatts, it has comfortable beds and nicely appointed rooms. I saw one review wrote that the room was too small. I had just a regular room but found it to be huge by big-city downtown hotel standards. I really like the architecture and interior design elements of this Hyatt, too. Its location could not be any better if you're in Denver for a convention or a downtown vacation as it is super close to the Denver Center for Performing Arts, the --th Street Pedestrian Mall, and other attractions. It is no more than a -- minute walk to LoDo. The hotel does not have a vaction-y feel, however. It has a super busy lobby and just a real downtown business feel to it. Because I prefer a super clean room that is new over a charming historic room that feels a little dirty, to me it is the perfect spot for a downtown weekend get away. Note that parking is pricey at something like $---day. Also, Priceline seems to have a GREAT prices on Hyatts in general and this one in particular if you're willing to play the Priceline game and accept the risks that come along with that.

On trips to L.A. it's a continuing challenge to find moderately priced hotels that are conveniently located. The Palomar fits the bill nicely with discounts for corportions, AAA, and AARP. It's located a short walk from UCLA on Wilshire Blvd and the staff is very helpful. There is a weird policy regarding pets that leads to a wide variety of dogs in the lobby, some of whom inevitably fight with other pets. The animal motif is continued with leopard skin designs on robes and throws. I have no idea what the notion is here but overall it's immaterial. The fitness center is large and well equipped and the rooms are comfortable. The restaurant is mediocre and over-priced, a bad combination, but otherwise we found this an attractive alternative to hotels in which we've stayed before. Recommended.

We stayed at this hotel for one night. When we got there, we checked in before we parked in the self park garage. Check in was a breeze and the front desk was very friendly. She asked if I booked a corner room and I did. I asked her if we could take our car in and out of the garage and she gave me a pass so we could do that. I am not sure if you can do that if you just get a ticket at the garage. Parking was steep at $-- for -- hours. There doesn’t appear to be any other “deals” nearby so we parked there. We are Omni select members (DO THIS if you stay at an Omni-it is free and you get little perks) so she gave us a card to select our preferences and one to select our free morning beverages. The lobby was pretty. The doormen held the door for you. No one hassled you to take your bags or anything. The lobby has a restaurant, a bar, the concierge, and a few shops. There was fruit and fruity water there also which was a nice touch. As other reviews have mentioned, when you go up the elevator, you are looking over the lobby and people's offices. The other side of the building-atrium are offices. It is kind of neat seeing all of those people working while you are on vacation. Our room was at the end of the hallway and was a corner room. I think the corner room was maybe smaller than a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""regular"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room so I am not sure why I asked for it. It wasn't small, just oddly shaped. When we got there, the door was open and a hotel worker was in there checking the mini bar. He asked if he could come back and return with a missing soda and he came back promptly to replace it. It was a nice room with a big, comfy bed. There was a chair and a cool foot stool made of cow hair. The bathroom was ok. It had floor to ceiling windows on two walls (with shades). The shower was pretty but there was no bathtub and it was completely dark! There was no light in or near the shower. It also was built so water leaked out of the door so no matter what, make sure you have a towel down. The water pressure was massive. There was a flat screen tv in the room and a desk but NO free internet. It was some ridiculously high charge. I would expect more from this hotel at the prices we were paying. The view was ok. We could see Sixth Street a little (nothing much to see) and the highway and the vicinity. I don't know if anyone has a better view because the offices are on the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""good"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" view side of the city. We did not hear any noise outside as I read on other reviews except fire trucks. No drunks from -th Street. We were on a high floor (-- I think) so it was no problem. I asked that room service in the morning did not knock when we placed our order and just to leave it at the door but they did knock. Not a big deal. There is a pool on the top floor of the hotel outside. Part of the reason I liked this hotel was the pool but it was SO windy up there, we didn't even swim. It was way too cold. It was a cool view and the pool looked neat. The hot tub was very nice. The concierge was very helpful and friendly. They printed driving directions for us and gave us food recommendations. They had menus for local restaurants too. The location of the hotel was good. It was - blocks from -th Street which is where the Visitors Center is and a lot of the restaurants and bars. It was within walking distance to most everything downtown. We walked to the bat viewing (fun) and felt very safe walking at night. However, there are a lot of homeless people there it seems. No one really talked to us but we were surprised. We took a great tour. We picked it up at the Visitor's Center and it was a -- minute tour that took you outside of the city in a van which was totally worth it. We were going to take the Duck Tour but this was longer and took you to many other sites and the driver was funny and nice. I preferred the outskirts of the city to downtown. It was beautiful. It was not hop on, hop off though. 
I did not really see a better hotel or a better area so I would stay at the Omni again.

Stayed for three days and would certainly return again. Rooms are large and amenities are generous. Free parking and convenient location. Manager John Cassidy was especially helpful arranging an important accommodation. Great location and convenient to many restaurants. Clean fitness center with many machines.

This hotel is quite nice, but at around $--- p-n it should be better. Rooms are clean and well decorated, but it lacks simple details that are not expensive and can make for a more comfortable stay... drinking water in the room- tea and coffee facility in room-cotton pads, decent branded toileteries etc. There is obviously a premium to pay for a central NY location but small things make the difference.
My superior double room was small but still with enough room to open my case, other colleagues with the same room class had much less space.
There was also some confusion over our reservation, as - of my colleagues didn't arrive with us on day - of the trip (they were always planning to arrive later) the hotel gave their rooms away, without calling to check with them or even checking with the rest of the group who were already at the hotel. It was eventually resolved but not without some stress.
Restaurant is currently closed for refurbishment (Oct --) and there is limited room service and breakfast services available.

Perfect location! This hotel is modern and clean and the staff are helpful and friendly. Its right on the boardwalk, walking distance to everything. We had a full ocean view which was spectacular and our room was spacious and perfect for just us two. My mom was woken up a few times by people drinking and partying on the deck, you would only hear them if you had a full ocean view and I slept through it. The restaurant is wonderful, but really expensive, movies are $-- and water is $-. We spent $--- on breakfast, because their wasn't prices attached. If you are splurging this place is so worth it.

Have traveled to Chicago over the Thanksgiving for the past -- years have stayed about every hotel in the area of Greater Michigan Ave(from the river north to Oak St.). We booked on Hotwire for $--- per night per room(- rooms). We arrived early at --:-- pm and got right into our rooms, check-in was easy and went right to our rooms, ---- and ---- both corner rooms. Within - minutes we had our bags and shortly after that room service came with a plate of small fruit and chocolate overed strawberries, that was a surprise! Yes, The Whitehall is a smaller older hotel, but our room was large, nice view, CLEAN with a good bed, you can not ask for more. 
I parked our car in the Private ramp across the street from the hotel and payed the going rate($--- for three days). What was nice I could go to the car and drop stuff off so it was in our room. We could walk to everything we need to do.....shop, shop and more shopping. Check out was as easy as checking in. I guess what I am saying is if the Whitehall comes up and you are not sure.......stay there! If you are looking for a - star go someplace else, but if you looking for a hotel with a great location, clean, good staff the Whitehall Hotel on East Delaware will fit our needs.

I booked the Omni because of the location (conference hotel near by was sold out). While I have stayed in many hotels before for business and pleasure my only experience with the Omni was in Chicago.
The warm welcome of Christmas soon disappeared when I entered my room. I've experienced small bathrooms before, but this was one for the record. The tile was broken and there was mold in the shower. I could barely fit between the tub and sink. I immediately requested another room. The hotel staff was responsive and I was moved to another room. This time, the bath was larger, but the blinds looked liked someone painted over them to coverup the mold! There is no room to use any items on the sink and store anything. There was also a note in the room that said some items were missing because the hotel is undergoing renovations. I was expecting more at $--- for Friday and Saturday and $--- for Sunday-Tuesday nites.
While the staff generally was helpful and the hotel location is close to a Metro station, I wouldn't rank this hotel high on my list of places to stay in the DC area.

We arrvied for a one nighter in Indianapolis and were pleasantly surprised at the charm of this historic hotel and its proximity to many cool things in town. Great staff, large rooms, and all of the old school charm on the outside, with great modern amenities inside. Nice restaurant and great little convenience pantry with food and drink choices.

Excellent location, just half a block away from Times Square and right in the middle of Theater District. Despite the central location, the street-noise was non-existent in our room (eventhough we had windows facing the --th street). Furthermore, lobby provided a cool but yet laid-back feeling upon entering the hotel from the crowded streets.
The staff of the hotel were friendly and customer service-oriented - all our requests and questions were handled effectively with smiles. Free wi-fi and adequate breakfast were included in the price.
The only negative matter to mention was the loudness of the heating in the room. Due to the time (mid-January) and a quite poor insulation of the windows, the heating went on a couple times during each night with a rather loud humming-like propeller noise. Our room was large enough to serve two people and luggage, and it was very clean and really nicely decorated.
Overall, really nice experience!

Steeped with history this charming hotel is set on Union square, a perfect location for exploring SF.
From our window we could see SAKs and Maceys, lit my Girlfriends eyes up! 
Friendly staff, good sized rooms, great customer service and free cookies on reception.
If its modern all glass hotels yoou are looking for then you will be dissapointed by the Chancellor, if its charming, small, boutique hotel in a great loaction then you WONT be dissapoinnted! 
Thansk to all the staff at the Chancellor for making our stay so nice :-)

Clean and spacious room, with typically comfortable Marriott quality bed. Also very convenient location...at least for my purpose. BUT the hot water in the shower was barely adequate and had paroxysms of freezing cold. In addition, the flow restrictor on the bathroom sink faucet limited the pressure so severly that it barely cleansed the razor or toothbrush.

Room and bathroom were very clean, very comfortable bed, and friendly service. My rating is based on the value I received which was excellent. I've rated """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""fancier"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotels lower because they did not live up to their promise or standards. This hotel lives up to it's standard by providing a very nice room at a great price. Breakfast is free and adequate. Coffee is served all day long. Internet is free.

The Wyndham Garden offers simple accommodations with a minimum of frills.
The lobby is small and congested, so if there are several people coming-going-checking in--as there was when I checked in--it can be a bit of a mob scene. And for those of you who might need a business center--or even just a station to print out a airline boarding pass--there's a small computer shoehorned into the corner of the lobby as well.
Such """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""busyness"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" also lends itself to some frustration. The two elevators are routinely in service (often by cleaning staff), resulting in long waits up and down. If your room is on a lower floor, you'd be better off taking the stairs. Also, housekeeping tends to work well into the afternoon and early evening, leaving towels-sheets stacked or piled in the hallways and stairs throughout the day. Normally this wouldn't be a big deal, but when exiting the elevator, there isn't a lot of room in the hallways to maneuver.
The room itself was fine. The flat screen TV was a nice feature, and the work area well lighted and comfortable. The only downside (and one to be aware of) is that my room--on the -th floor--faced out to the street. It was very noisy at night, and especially late at night when garbage trucks were making their noisy rounds. You may want to ask in advance how removed (or not) your room is relative to such activity.

Wow.....we had expected great views but when we got there they were fab! Staff were great, concierge very friendly and helpful. Gym could do with some updating especially the free weights, but again views were excellent.
Breakfast food was great and of a good quality.

This is a great place to stay at a reasonable price. Everything was clean, comfy and spacious rooms. Breakfast was great and the desk staff were very pleasant and helpful. There is no reason to give this the highest rating for a --star non-luxurious type of accommodation. Convenient location from the airport and city and a Starbucks nearby. If I had to say what was the worst thing I would say that it was because we were there in --- degree weather and had to have the noisy a-c on all night.

We stayed a week at the Ramada Plaza. We chose this hotel for two reasons. We wanted to be in the hotel circle area, which is close to all attractions with easy freeway acess. We had stayed in the hotel circle area about - years ago, at a different hotel. The second was price. We went through a travel agent and the package price was under $-- per night with two queen beds. Ramada has a good reputation, and we were banking on it. Rather than trying a hotel we have never heard of. The hotel staff were very good and freindly. The room was a good size, with a fridge and micro, and a very sm. one cup coffee maker. The bathroom area had two sinks, one in the bath with the tiolet and nice shower with full sized tub. The other in a dressing area, which made it much easier for two people to be getting ready at once in the morning. Very nice comfy beds, comforters and four fluffy pillows to each bed. Just right for watching TV in bed and proping your back up. Free parking was good, most of the time we parked right by the door. The restaurant on property was too exspencive, and had very limited menu items. We did buy dessert one night to take up to our room. Big mistake...two cups of ice cream, and one piece of chocolate cake, $--.--+ tax. There is a little store down the street that has just about all you need, at resonable prices. There are two great restaurants we found on hotel circle. Adam's and Abbie's just to the east of the hotel same side of the street and Hunter steak house, just on the otherside of the freeway both are very close by. Great food, and excellent service at both. They have a nice laundry there. We had to wash clothes half way through our stay. The desk has soap for $-.--, the washers and dryers are new and commercial grade. They only cost a $-.-- each. Very reasionable, and efficeint. I happend to do laundry on Wed. night, and was surprised to find a extra special treat. They have a food and beverage reception every Wed. night. They have wine and beer, sodas, cheeses, friut and vegies, crakers. We were dissapointed with the pool and jaccuzzi(sp?) area. On the web sight you see a lg. pool lots of chase lounge chairs, and nice surroundings. The reality is a very small area, even smaller pool which only goes from -ft. to -.-ft. , the jaccuzzi's bubbles were sad, lots of noise and not much power. Only --- chase loung chairs, two umbrella tables one with benches and one only had one chair. Not much vegitation, a few tall trees on one side. Pluses for the pool area were that both were clean, warm, and hot. Plenty of pool towles, and a phone to call for more if they run out. They do have a computer in the lobby area you can use. Don't plan on being able to use it unless you like to wait. The sign says -- min. limit, and is not inforced. If you have a laptop bring it, they do have internet in the rooms. We just don't have a laptop, and needed directions from time to time. Over all we had a very nice stay. We had a room in the back (ask, if you want one that is quiet, and closest to the pool) if you want a fridge and micro you have to ask for that as well as a no smoking room. I would recomend this hotel for the most part, would really be nice if the pool area was better. If you don't care much about swimming and such, it is a great place to stay.

It's an old-style boutique hotel, so the rooms are small, the layout is non-standard, and you open a window to cool off from the radiator heat. But the bed was excellent and furnishings well-maintained, staff friendly and eager to help, and building has character. It was what I expected and a good value.

My husband and I were helping his daughter move to San Diego, and stayed - nights at the Hilton Garden Inn. We requested a room away from the freeway, and were accomodated with a nice king bed with new duvets & mattress toppers. 
The room was clean, the free high speed internet worked great. We used the pool and found lots of underground secured parking for free. 
There were a few local quick resturants, a small market and a great taco shop in the same block. Yes, this hotel is in the 'burbs of San Diego, but worked great for us...short drive to town, Balboa Park and LaJolla. 
Housekeeping requests were quick and responsive. I would use this hotel in the future.

We based our DC hotel selection on other trip advisor reviews, which proved to be really useful.
We loved the area where the hotel was located, that is, just off Dupont Circle with a wide choice of restaurants and bars on our doorstep.
The hotel gave us a further room upgrade (we'd already paid for one) and we were provided with a massive room, which was great, though the view wasn't all that (the main road outside of the hotel). The room was however, somewhat functional for us as we'd come to Washington DC to see the sights. We didn't take advantage of any of the range of facilities that were on offer, even the complimentary wine tasting that was available each evening, which appeared to be very popular. 
That said, the hotel staff were very helpful, the room was spotless, we liked the somewhat quirky vibe of the place and the breakfast-cocktail option for an additional $-.-- per night was a really good offer.
We had a really fun night out at what used to be the Brickskeller (can't remember the new name) just round the corner from the hotel. It's in need of a little tlc (which is ongoing), but the staff, Tim and Jeff were great and there was a brilliant atmosphere in there, plus they did a decent cottage pie. What was originally planned as a quick drink turned out as a full night out.
I would highly recommend this hotel as a great place to stay.

If you want to go somewhere where you will enjoy simple elegance done excellently, take a trip here! I've been here about --- times over the last few years. The consistent attention to detail is always present. The linens are lovely, the beds comfortable. When you arrive there's a glass of champagne to start your get-away. The bath is amazing and fills from the ceiling...the rubber duckie is a novel addition. It's close to Pike Market and the centre of Seattle. All the staff are polite and attentive without being overbearing. I checked out the gym, looks really quite decent. I like the Starbucks coffee too. I've been to Boka for breakfast on my last few trips and it's been excellent...dinner was also superb and we enjoyed the trout and salmon....both very good. On leaving, bottled water is placed in the car...a nice classy touch. Friends and family alike have enjoyed this hotel...it's not cheap but it's a real treat! On a special birthday, the management of the hotel send up a special dessert...once again...well thought out....keep up the great work at the hotel ----....a real credit to the staff and management :)

The staff of the Skyline Hotel at --- --th Ave. are very courteous and helpful. They made our event so much easier. Everyone, including security were right there to help us. I would recommend this hotel to everyone. Thank you staff of Skyline

Great location, staff helpful re. a-c that didn't work. Okay, first off, I arrived in San Diego a day early, we drove from Northern California and we did not think we would make it the entire way. But we did. We had reservations at the Radisson in Downtown San Diego but for an extra night it would be almost $---. My family and I decided to stay somewhere out of town outside of the main area. Bad decision.
The hotel itself is worse than a Motel -. I would have been better off staying in Hotel Circle. The manager is hard to understand but polite and we had no problems getting a room without reservations.
When I checked into the room the overall first impression was OK, nothing more. Standard crappy little motel for the night. Understandable. The beds were OK for a motel, very soft. The television worked without any problems.
One major problem was the incredibly disgusting stench that was inside the room, luckily we ha a Glade Plugin, it was bearable for a night but it definitely smelled. 
The bathroom had serious issues, more specifically the toilet. It looked like someone tried to pull it from the ground, when being used it felt like you were rattling around on a rollercoaster. By all means I would say without a doubt that it is a safety hazard.
During our stay we discovered that someone at one time tried to break into the room because the door frame was pulled away. 
The so called continental breakfast is an even bigger joke, it consisted of milk, coffee, tea, and stale cereal and even older donuts that looked like they were from --Eleven. 
All in all the motel provided us with a one night stay, we tried to stay out of the room as much as possible and left as early as we could. I would recommend staying at a Motel - (and there is one near by).

Our room was perfect. One of the best we've stayed in. Although it was only a standard king, the room was broken up very nicely and felt like a full suite. We will definitely consider a Renaissance property in the future.

A nice hotel at a great location, but for the money you can do much better in midtown. For this money I would expect better service, a larger room, a nicer interior (plain, boring lobby), and a view (window tucked back in the corner). Even the bed didn't live up to the hype. My waiter Teresa at the Hotel restaurant was absolutelly amazing. I travel weekly to different destinations across the United States and she was the best I have seen in - years of travel. Just returned home from a -N stay. Hotel is well located - a few minutes walk from a subway station ( with many lines running thru making for easy transfer ), minutes walk from Times Square yet quiet enough for a good rest at the end of the day.

There is a downside to Tripadvisor that shows its face occasionally - a self fulfilling prophecy, here's how it works.......................
An average hotel - service - (whatever) gets some good reviews and the Manager responds to the reviews with kind words to the reviewer and more follow, the hotel climbs the popularity ladder and then people start to choose it because its near the top. To get in on the 'love fest' action they then also write good reviews and get fawned on by the management etc etc etc even though its in relaity no better than other similar products.
Suprisingly the one """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I don't get it"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" review gets no management response - so this perfectly adequate hotel becomes the -th best in Houston - really ????? This is a sub-brand chain hotel in office central, how can that be ?
I have stayed here quite a few times as well as the Courtyard Marriot just across the way - I like the HGI slightly more, the Courtyard is marginally less nice overall but it is --- in the ranking which would make this HGI just above that so here's and honest review of this hotel - stayed here - nights this week.
Check-in - friendly enough but nothing special no welcome back etc, interestingly some colleagues didn't get the free breakfast coupons that come with our company rate here - arguements ensued and end result they didn't get them apparently because they had booked through an agent ...........just as I had and received them - get it sorted guys !
Rooms - nice enough but a bit dated, really think these chains should have central air con, hate the noisy wall - window units
Cleanliness - had a good look round as others have waxed lyrical, clean enough I suppose but lots of corners not vacumed, same in bathroom so pretty average.
Bed - really like these adjustable ones
Toiletries replaced sometimes
Wireless - really slow in higher rooms, spoke to reception to see if anything could be done and the answer was its working ok
Food - absolutley average, really nothing great to write home about, usually choose to eat out for that reason
Breakfast - didn't bother to use my vouchers as last time cooked was very greasy so has put me off
Check-in staff general - always felt I was breaking in on some gossip as I passed and it went quiet a couple of times, no friendly hello's etc - pretty poor really.
So, all in all a really average hotel that thinks its one of the top ones in Houston and clearly isn't - can we have some more honest and realistic reviews on here please to stop this kind of thing from happening and maybe some consideration of what can actually be done better by management so they actually try.

Waldorf Astoria was the choice of hotel for a special weekend in New York for myself and my fiancee, we had high expectations but were sadly let down, the room etire was tired and in need of enhancement, the heating system was not in working order unless you required cold air, tea and coffee was not as standard in the room unless ordered via room service at extra cost. I had a long travel day and had to be up at the crack of dawn for a meeting. Check in was smooth. The room was clean and cozy. Room service valet was polite and accommodating. I slept like a baby! The meeting facilities were professional and comfortable.

Huge Money for tiny room. I mean tiny. I paid a ridiculous fee to stay in a ity bity room. The staff was nice, and so were the restaurants, but it was so tiny. Everything else was fine. Staff fine, but rooms just so tiny. The bed took up the entire room.

I came into town for an overnight trip and had flown in on the red-eye early in the morning. By the time my meetings were done it was -pm and I just wanted to relax. Once I checked in I went down to the lounge and enjoyed a glass of wine while listening to the fabolous piano player. After reading the paper I headed off to the Ships Tavern to have a meal. I enjoyed their fabolous prime rib, and some of the best whiskey in town. My stomach full, I headed up to bed for a much needed night's rest. The room was extremely clean and inviting and the bed was very comfortable. The service and staff were nothing but helpful and friendly and go out of their way to make you feel welcome. I will come back every time I'm in downtown Denver!

This is a great little property, that follows the mold of many of the Comfort Suites properties. A nice comfortable, well equiped suite with a sitting area. What makes this property stand out is the exceptional staff, all of them that I have encountered have gone our of their way to be friendly and helpful. There are several good restaurants within walking distance, inlcuding a very good little Outback.

It was centrally located so I had access to the Metro (Red, Orange and Blue Lines), and was in walking distance to many places that I needed to go. The room was clean, modern and very spacious. I do not expect a management response as I no longer have a computer to send it to since it was stolen from a locked room at the hotel and they will not take responsibility for it or the other contents that was stolen.

STayed at the Omni in Chartown on Aug --- ----. Check in was great. Overly friendly and professional staff. Housekeepers were very friendly and loved doing their job. Enjoyed our stay here. Far enough away from all the hustle & bustle but close enough
to get to the main area of the Riverwalk in a few minutes. Rooms were nice but watch out for the bed frame. Easy to catch your leg on as you round the bottom of the bed. Put a cover across the heavy wooden bed frame to protect our legs from injury. The mattress was one of the best we've ever slept on. Also stay on the non slip strips in the tub or else be ready to slip & slide. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Would stay here again.

My two daughters and I stayed here in Aguust ---- and overall found it to be a positive experience. The hotel is centrally located and very close to the Medical Center T station (walk one building and a parking lot south to get to hotel). It was close enough that we should have taken the T to get there after our flight got in-- but at - PM, we were worried about security and took a cab instead (do not believe those airport transit, a cab is $-- not $--). The Theater District area is challenged on security and available child-friendly and reasonably priced restaurants, but several restaurants will deliver, or just eat elsewhere before returning to the hotel for the night. In the daytime, we set off walking using standard big-city common sense. The room was well appointed and clean. Hotel consists of several buildings linked together, so our room was quite a walk from the front entrance. Access to the adjacent YMCA pool and a pool lane resevered for hotel guests is a nice ammenity, though facility is old and the locker rooms undergoing contruction left much to be desired (be aware you must walk outside across a rooftop to get there). One big thing to know if you are visiting Boston to sightsee-- do very thorough homework on the T system. Originally we were going to stay in Cambridge at the end of the T Green line, but it was only by accident we figured out in advance that line has been demolished. Thank goodness we moved! For going to the Science Center, get on a bus at Haymarket or even earlier because the buses are always full by the time they get to Fleet Center-Science Park area.

The Four Seasons Boston is my favorite Boston hotel and I'll tell you why. Unlike the Mandarin Oriental (too contemporary and lacking classic features) or the Boston Harbor Hotel (finishes remind me of a cookie cutter chain with no personality), The Four Seasons Boston maintains a classic ambiance and a very high, professional level of service. Although, I will admit that the exterior leaves much to the imagination - but I hear a renovation is under way.
Location can't be beat - diagonally across the street from The Taj (which has location as its best asset).
Rooms are traditional with every modern amenity.
I miss the classic French restaurant, but the Bristol Lounge is a great spot for lunch or dinner - I just wish it was a little less casual.

I took my wife here for her birthday last June to get away and have some private adult time away from the kids for a couple nights. We booked it through Jetsetter, and from the pictures it looked phenomenal. And the lobby and common areas were, but the rooms were pretty mediocre, and the bathrooms were extremely small. Small bathrooms are huge problem when you have a wife who uses a million products and likes to throw clothes all over the place. So that was a negative for us. We couldn't both be in there at the same time it was that small. Size wise, the bedroom was big but the furnishings were a little tired. The halls of the guest room floors were interesting, like you were walking through someone's home. Not as luxurious as I would have liked, but not terrible. 
The lobby was really great and had a lot of interesting furniture, including a giant chair that my wife got a great photo in. The lounge was a lot of fun, we went there for a few drinks Saturday night and the crowd was really energetic. They had these really neat """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""paintings"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which were actually videos of the models standing still. Every once in a while you can catch them blink. 
So overall I would say it's a great place for young people to come for the weekend, but I think for a romantic getaway with my wife we would have preferred a hotel with more luxurious rooms and more amenities.

The rooms here are pretty basic, but if you come to NYC and spend any more than the minimum amount of time in your room then you may as well stay at home. I was really worried about the shared bathroom issue, but they were absolutely spotless and I never saw another guest on my floor. The room itself wasn't all that comfortable, but if you want to be really central (which this is) and are on a budget, you have to accept that it won't be luxurious. It is spotlessly clean though.

La Luna is located toward the west end of Lombard Street. This was the -rd time I have stayed here. The rooms are a nice size with cozy beds, continental breakfast and treasured parking spaces. However, staying in a room facing the street requires the luck of being a heavy sleeper or having some good ear plugs. Request a room away from the street and on the top floor to minimize noise. Literally, it feels like the street noise is cutting right through the room and it goes on allllllll night.

We stayed at this hotel for one night as a stop over on our way home from Florida. We got a very good rate on priceline, and were pleasantly surprised when we arrived at how beautiful the hotel was and how big our room was. There was a living area with nice size desk and a LCD TV. There was also a wet bar with microwave and minifridge along with a coffee maker. The bathroom was very nice with beautiful tile and amenities. The bedroom had two double beds with another nice size desk and another LCD TV. The kids loved having their own TV to watch their shows.....the parents loved this too! Although this hotel is not located exactly off of I---, it is just an easy three mile drive to reach. It is in a very quiet location away from all of the congestion of the Interstate. I would definitely stay here again.

Absolutely delightful, boutique hotel with outstanding front desk & concierge (Chris S., Tim and Lauren went all out for us). (Management did immediately resolve this and sent up a bottle of wine.) Our extra towel request (wash & hand) ended up being taken care of by the front desk each evening. First of all, this hotel is like staying in a living beat writers museum. It's got a great central location in North Beach, and you feel like you are genuinely a part of the beat scene while staying there. The room was decent- the mattress was acceptable, but not much more than that. The bathroom was tiny but did the trick. It did have what I would refer to as a museum quality picture of the great beat writers of the day- Kerouac, Ferlinghetti, Cassady, Corso, Orlovsky... with a handwritten note about the picture from Allen Ginsberg. How freaking cool is that??? It was absolutely amazing, and it made the hotel worthwhile for me. 
That said, if you want to sleep- especially on a weekend night- DO NOT GET A ROOM FACING COLUMBUS AVE. When I tell you that it sounded like a riot was taking place outside our room, I am not exaggerating. At various times during the night (and I'd taken a sleeping pill to counteract potential street noise), my girl and I heard shouting, fighting, ambulances, police cars, sounds like bombs going off, screams, laughter, singing, more bomb sounds... I swear to you, no one could have been more surprised to look out the window the next morning and see... a street. Just a quiet, calm street. Amazing. 
Anyway, if you love character, this is the hotel for you. If you really want to be in North Beach, it's the place for you. However, if you are into pampering or quiet solitude, Boheme is probably not a fit. That said, I would go back- I'd just bring ear plugs next time.

My family and I (- children) stayed in this hotel during a one-night stop-over in DC. It is a wonderful location, just minutes' walk from the Foggy Bottom-GWU metro station, and about -- minutes walk to the Lincoln Memorial-Mall. My only complaint would be that it is difficult to approach upon arrival. When we pulled up, all the spots in front of the hotel were taken. So I had to jump out to check in while my wife circled. It seems like some kind of check-in waiting area would be helpful. 
But a good place to stay.
Nice size rooms; good location if walking, although somewhat far from the metro; decent breakfast. Lots of families with children on weekends. Overall, a good value.
Newly renovated and excellent price for the location. It was clean, quiet and comfortable. It's within walking distance of Little Italy, Gas Lamp district and the harbor.

I know that the pricier rooms were much nicer. The other people staying there were happy. I was happy with the price. I saved my money. Would I choose that room again? NO! Would I stay at the hotel again...absolutely.

Wanted to cut a cake at the rooftop bar. Denied entrance because of the cake. My husband and I just returned from a long weekend we'll treasure forever. As former New Yorkers, we usually don't stay in hotels when we're 'back home'. This weekend, though, we wanted some alone time for our anniversary--and were sold on the Library's Web site description of its many amenities. That blurb is understated and humble. From the moment we crossed the threshold, we felt genuinely welcomed and planned for--a surprise bottle of Prosecco in our room with a thoughtful anniversary note; complimentary slippers and a soft robe for relaxing; no-additional-charge wine, cheese, crackers, and fruit in the lounge overlooking Madison Avenue before dinner; heavenly scented toiletries tubside; fresh eggs, bagels, and to-order, self-service espresso in the morning--again, all included in the room price. And above all--the books everywhere! New, old, classic, modern--categorized according to the Dewey Decimal System, what a hoot! You can pick them up and read 'em, or just leaf through--as many folks do while munching on ---hour cookies, coffee, cocoa, etc. in the lounge. The hotel draws an international crowd of curious and educated guests (adults of all ages) who are congenial yet respect your privacy. With two restaurants--one ground floor, the other up top (great views of midtown!)--featuring reasonably priced, broad ranges of food options, The Library Hotel is the perfect base for all your NYC explorations. We're already planning our next trip. Seriously. I'm addicted. I like being pampered--without having to remortgage our house to do so. Enjoy!

The Hotel was very inviting and the staff was great. The room had an amazing view of the city. My only complaint about the hotel was there was no refrigerator or microwave in the room. There was an additional charge to have one brought to the room. 
The room also featured a mini bar, and a fee for storing personal items in it, that contained sensors under each item. Upon leaving I was present with a bill for things that I didn't purchase. The staff was very accommodating and quickly removed all of the charges.

The hotel is stunningly beautiful, the ceilings are amazing. I would highly recommend going for drinks and to look around.....but I would NOT recommend staying there. Check in was incredibly slow - but it gave us plenty of time to see the video of how beautiful the rooms were going to be. They were obviously streaming ones that were upgraded and refurbished because we actually laughed at our room when we got there. Yes, I get it, it's an old historic hotel, I should have expected the rooms to be teeny tiny, and the bathroom teeny tinier. The bad.....well after you get over that """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""old man"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" smell that permeates the entire hotel, the room was dark and in need of a thorough cleaning. The TV has about -- channels - - of which are dedicated to the ammenities of the hotel.
