As a single mature woman travelling to New York on my own for the first time, I could not have made a better choice. Yotel is funky, friendly, modern, clean, great service, great atmosphere, close to Times Square, great bars and food. You HAVE to stay at Yotel just for the experience.

I stayed for four nights in a standard room with an eastern view. The service was excellent, the room was very nice. I particularly liked the electronic shades and curtains. The tub does fill in -- seconds 
The location is excellent. An easy walk to the park and shopping. I don't think you can go wrong with this one.

Decided to stay here for a few days in Mid October based on other reviews. Just wanted to confirm all the good things are indeed true. Front desk was very exceptional. The big guy behind the counter is a customer service guru. Super quick checkin and checkout. Housekeeping did an excellent job. Hotel appears to have been renovated recently. Room was very clean. Parking and internet are free. Ok, Internet isn't the fastest but the price is great. Cable TV but no HD tv's. Pool was not used as heater was out per note posted. Hot breakfast (toast-links-waffles-eggs-juice-coffee-cereal-etc) is good and included at no additional charge. Only consideration is lack of noise shielding? In All a great value for your money if you're not looking for a high end hotel.

My friend and I stayed there in September to visit Boston on a girl's trip. We were there for about a week. The stay was great. Our room was very clean and the staff was friendly. I was worried that it would be hard to get around because it looks so far away from downtown on the map. It turned out to be not far at all. We are not from the city whatsoever, so we took cab's everywhere. For the price, we had an enjoyable stay.

Just back from a stay at the Doubletree..It is a very nice hotel - blocks from Michigan Ave...close to major sites ...very good public transit system to get around...Rooms are a good size..comfortable beds and a large bathroom...towels are fine!(unlike a previous reviewers opinion!!!)....have breakfast across the street at the West Egg Cafe.....very good but crowded on the weekends(skip the bagel at Einstein!)..the best part....$-- a nite on HotWire!!!..would surely stay again.

Great location - just three blocks from Grand Central Station and many choices for ground transportation throughout the city and to airports. Room was adequate, very clean. Staff was courteous and provided an early check in.

The hotel is situated two blocks from Times Square. It has a subway station next doors and a reasonable price parking lot in front, if you are driving. There is a shakeshack on the corner, with its delicious burgers, and plenty of nice restaurants nearby (Hells Kitchens). It's a walking distance from a bunch of broadway theaters. The rooms are spacious, with brand new furniture and the rain forrest shower is just amazing. It was the best bed I ever slept on. The bar of the hotel is very nice, but closes early (around -- pm). The staff was very helpful. I can not complain about anything. Pure luxury and the best location in New York!

OK, let me warn you--this is a bit of a rant. 
I am a Starwood Platinum member who travels a lot. Typically I stay at W's, Westins and Sheratons. Geographically, this hotel is well-located and some of the rooms have nice views of the river. However , I digress . . . 
Usually, when in Chicago, I stay at the W Lakeshore, but I tried out the Westin Chicago River North because of the high ratings on this site as well as its proximity to the Chicago office of the company I joined a couple of months ago. Upon arrival, the person who was checking me in at reception answered the phone and, after a moment, actually rolled his eyes (not to me in a wink-wink conspiratorial way, just in general pissed off) while he was speaking to the guest who was calling. (I figured my front desk friend was just having a bad day.) Later, I found out that my flustered friend only programmed one of my two cardkeys, so I had to go back to reception after going to dinner. Since I was there, I thought I would do the hotel a favor and mention the incident that occurred earlier, as I'd think most hotels would want their staff members to be polite when working the front desk. Thus, I waited for the on-duty front desk manager, William, to end a phone call he was on. The call seemed to go on for a bit, and it became apparent that the guest on the other end was clearly not happy with his-her accommodations for some reason.
I was pretty surprised when I heard William raise his voice to almost shouting level and say to the guest, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""No, I will *not* reduce your rate!!!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" His outrage was quite obvious to all of us waiting for service, as he flailed his free hand and scrunched up his face. Upon hanging up, he turned to his staff and said quite dramatically, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Send housekeeping to Room [insert room number here]."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" One of them asked """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Is he checking out early?"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" William retorted """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Yes!!!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Then, he turned to we waiting guests and said very pointedly and loudly """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""And if any of *you* are thinking about checking out early, let me just tell you there is not one room left in the city tonight!!!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I realized then where the guy who checked me in got his training. I told William that I found his behavior to be quite unprofessional, especially as a manager, and he said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""How dare you--you don't even *know* me!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I replied """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Of course I don't know you; it's merely my impression as a guest in this hotel who observed you shouting at someone on the phone from behind the front desk where everyone could see and hear you. And then to be brought into it!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" He just rolled his eyes at me and crossed his arms and said something like """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Whatever!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" 
I finally got back to my room and called Starwood Preferred Guest hoping I could switch hotels, but William was right about things being booked up. Suffice it to say, I will never stay at that hotel again, and I'll warn anyone who broaches the idea away from it.

Pros: 
- Yes, the mattresses do indeed rock the casbah. I can understand why some people actually purchase W Hotel mattresses for their home bedrooms. 
- Bliss products 'aint bad. 
- Unexpected: the windows in the room opened -- we like that. 
- *Most staff we dealt with were pretty friendly and we got zero attitude.
- Nice modern, contemporary decor, great location.
Cons:
- Breathtakingly expensive for the basics -- which is, essentially, just a room for the night. Sorry, but the complimentary glass of cheap champagne in plastic cup served at check in isn't that much of a value-add.
- No free Wi-Fi? Really? At these rates and in this modern day and age, I think you could freakin' swing that for your guests, W Hotel. Come ON.
- I know how dear real estate is in NYC and the many challenges of parking in the city, but....$-- for overnight valet parking?? Again -- really, W? With the prices you charge? You couldn't give us a little break there?
- Purportedly we were entitled to the fabled FREE Lexis car service as part of our room fee (as we were advised by the check in clerk), but when we strolled over to the blond behind the Lexis appt table to arrange for a ride to the theater she told us there wasn't anything available. * And she wasn't exactly friendly about it. 
- No breakfast options included with the very expensive room price, and the on site breakfast option truly broke the bank. It should not cost $-- for two people to have a breakfast that doesn't include any alcoholic beverages.
- Prices at the bar in the lobby were equally astonishing, even for NYC.
Would I stay at the W again? No. Not unless they send me a half off coupon.

The (OVER PRICED) room was very small, not like the photos on their website. I found the carpeting on the floor was ripped away from the wall and just laying there, the shower curtain was worn and frayed, TV Remote was not working (probably needed a new battery) and the wall electricial oulet in the bathroom (where you would plug something into) was loose and shifting back and forth in the wall. The ($-.-- breakfast that was included in the $---.-- room price was about half the size of a KID'S HAPPY MEAL. There was a charge to use their in house computer & NO FREE PARKING, VALET ONLY $--.-- a day. There was a parking stucture attached to the hotel that had a sign that said PARKING $-. & VALET PARKING $-- @ day. I asked if I could use the $- @ day parking and the desk clerk told me the hotel guest are REQUIED to use the Valet Parking Only @ $--. I have requested a TOTAL REFUND.
 """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""NOT A HAPPY CAMPER""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""

We arrived early on a Saturday while the hotel was busy there was a wedding and some sort of a party going on. With all that going on Glenn was very helpful. Although our room was not ready he did everything possible to make it an easy check in for us. He had our luggage taken care of, and later when we were able to get to our room our luggage was there waiting for us.
There was someone always upfront and outside to help us with what ever we needed. It seemed everyone really cared a great deal about making our stay pleasant.
When we needed a taxi or directions the staff was there to help us.

I came to visit my brother for a weekend in August and we stayed - night at this hotel because we went to the Orioles vs. Rangers game. It was a perfect location! We arrived and were able to get an early check-in. My brother has a big truck that wouldn't fit in the garage, so we had to pay $---overnight to park in the parking lot across the street. The valet guys were very helpful! We checked in early and walked around the Inner Harbor for a little bit, then the valet guys hailed us a cab to go eat at Obrycki's before the game. We had to get a cab to take us from the resturaunt to the ballpark as well. After the game, we were able to walk back to our hotel. There were plenty of people out and about so I never really felt unsafe. The room was quiet for us getting in late that night....my only complaint would probably be that the A-C didn't seem to cool off for the temp that it was set at. Everything else was clean and comfortable. I am also allergic to feathers and forgot to get the bedding switched out that afternoon but housekeeping was willing to come up around -am to bring me foam pillows and a blanket. Great stay!

I like 'Boutique Hotels"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I don't like old, smelly , cramped and poor mattresses with elevators barely two of us plus our carry on luggage could barely fit. The hotel although well located was just old and tired. The lobby was nice but that is where it ended. After less than -- hours we checked out and moved to the Marriott up the street..Villa Florence needs a complete makeover and the web pictures are not indicative of the how it really looks.

THANK you Magnolia for a great stay. we came to celebrate our --th anniversary and knew we wanted to stay there. they have great emmenities. service and staff are very friendly and helpful. my wife is a nurse in an ER, and is in a stressful job. so we love to go and relax downtown at the Magnolia, with its ambiance and quaint rooms we have never been disappointed. we Belong to the Winery next door and enjoy being able to go to both places and enjoy life. thanks Magnolia.

I recently stayed at The Pierre Hotel for work. While the entrance and lobby area of the hotel are average the rooms and service are well above. My room was big by New York Standards with a king size bed, flat screen TV, work desk and large washroom (humungous walk in shower), which included some of the largest bathing towels I have ever seen. Another bonus was the minibar where they had left space so you could put your own stuff - I wish more hotels would do this.
The service was incredible. From the concierge to the elevator operator (yes they had someone push the buttons in the elevator for you). The location is also great - right across from central park and one -th avenue, so if you are into shopping this is a great place to be.

We stayed at the Hotel Metro for a week in January ---- for our honeymoon and to be honest, there wasn't another hotel we'd have rather stayed at unless we had a bottomless pit of money, then the Plaza or Waldorf would've been nice.
We had a penthouse suite on the top floor which was comfortable and warm, but not quite what I would consider a suite. It did have the advantage of being down the corridor from the roof terrace, which has a fantastic view of the Empire State Building and overlooks Macy's.
A 'help yourself' bagel, pastry and muffin breakfast included in the price is good and coffee on tap ---- was a blessing. We didn't use the restaurant or bar so I couldn't comment on them other than they looked nice. The other facility we bypassed was the gym - just too exhausted after all the sightseeing.
Renovations on the lower floors and, at the end of our stay, the lounge, didn't really cause us any problems as we were out most of the time. The only real problem we did encounter was a blocked toilet, but this was fixed immediately and efficiently. We found the staff a little abrupt but again, we were out so much this didn't really bother us.
What really makes this hotel is it's location. Situated on West --th between -th Avenue and Broadway it's within touching distance of Macy's (which has a fantastic restaurant in the basement) and Herald Square, a - minute walk to the Empire State Building and a -- minute amble to Madison Square Gardens, the Flatiron, the Chrysler Building and Times Square, to name but a few. We walked pretty much everywhere due to it's location. Central Park is a -- minute walk up -th Ave, taking in the Rockefeller Centre and some fantastic shops on the way. A bus from Herald Square will take you down Broadway to Battery Park via Union Square, Greenwich Village, Noho, Soho, Little Italy and the Financial District. For swifter travel there's a subway station at Herald Square, and Penn Station and Grand Central are both a short walk away.
For those wanting luxury and finesse this hotel wouldn't be a good choice, but if you want a fantastic location and an inclusive breakfast for not a lot of money, Hotel Metro is ideal.

We love this hotel because it is a five-minute walk to the Denver Performing Arts complex. Most people in the audience are still trying to get their cars out of the tall circular parking garage when we are back at the hotel bar enjoying ourselves. Breakfast is wonderful and the service in the little restuarant is both warm and professional. They got our reservations all wrong, but their email alert let us know and they fixed everything right away. One major complaint because we are enthusiastic readers: The lighting in the room is not at all adequate. We always return to this hotel each time we go to an event at the Performing Arts complex. Valet parking takes your car away and then you can walk everywhere in LoDo.

We bring a group once a year to eat and party and thank our clients. This was our first stay at this property. We got a special pre-paid internet rate of $----night. WHAT a bargain! The location is fabulous. We joined the Starwood club upon check-in and were given corner rooms on the top floors. There was free water and Starbucks coffee in the rooms. The room had GREAT views and was quiet. The bed was very comfortable. The reason I give it four stars is because we had terrible reception on CBS; couldn't get it at all. Also, the free wireless in the room never worked after many attempts. We had to pay to access the internet. Also, there's a $-- fee to use the exercise facility and pool. I think that's high, although they did have very good machines and an excellent facility. We found the staff to be over the top friendly and helpful. Though the decor is a bit dated, it is warm and spacious with beautiful views from the lobby and bar areas. The ceilings are lower than some hotels, so the noise level never bothered us. I hope to stay here in the future- we were very impressed!

We couldn't have been more pleased with the Cassa. Everything from the location, room, & friendly staff combined for a great week in the Big Apple. We didn't use any public transportation, walked to the theatres, restaurants and shopping. The staff is very friendly and went out of their way to please us. The room was small but, hey, it's NYC! The bed was comfortable and the linens were cozy. We loved the shower and the flatscreen TV was a nice treat. I would definitely recommend it and will stay there again.

We stayed there twice this summer and our experience is mixed at best. The rooms are nicely appointed but rather small and the side towards Kraemer books gets a lot of sun. Unfortunately, the staff does not always keep the aircon running at the necessary temp-fan speed and so when we occupied our room the temp inside was upwards of -- degree. Even after - hour that had not changed much. It took many calls and staff was not responsive at all until I got really upset and threatened to leave and find another place to stay. Finally a technician (very nice guy) turned up and had to perform a fix. Breakfast is normally not included, only a la carte and pricy for the selection and quality offered.
On our second stay a couple of weeks later we had a problem with our reservation. Again, the fron desk staff was overwhelmed by this issue and referred us to the Guest Relation Manager. The way we were approached and the way our issue was handled was poor at best and unprofessional at worst. I was made feel as if I was pretending to have a reservation (and was told they were fully booked), then - after I showed them my confirmed booking on my cell phone- I was told that my travel agent had not send the reservation, when I called my agent, they told me that the reservation had gone through and was confirmed and the guest relation manager kept disappearing w-o communicating to us - just interrupting my phone call with the travel agent that she refused to call herself. Instead of helping to solve the problem and staying with us, she attended to other front desk business etc. It was rather uncomfortable to be in that lobby and having to fix this. When fixed an apology was not forthcoming right away! Later that day we got a nice note and were offered a sign of good will for the inconvenience. Check-out in both stays took for ever, so allow extra time! But this booking incident together with the experience the first time have me believe that the hotel is badly managed and staff is not really customer focused but company and self-interst focused.
If you are young the bar is hoping at night and you might like that, but for older folks like me it is much too loud (having horrible accoustics with noise dampening materials) and does not allow for a pleasant environment.
If you are not used to city living, beware of the early morning noise from the garbage trucks that takes over from -am onwards...
The saving grace is that the rates are ok and that the hotel is truly centally located (being close to the red line metro) and the availability of concierge parking (pricy!).

This is my first time at this location even though I've stayed at other Staybridge hotels before. I stayed for - nights for leisure and used points to book this place so I didn't pay the quoted rate (which I thought was high). I was surprised by the modern look-feel, cleanliness and service of this location. Service was good overall from checkin desk to the bellman. Concierge service was more spotty, depending on who's at the desk. I love the free wifi and kitchen in the room and the free breakfast (everyday) and predinner horsdourves-wine (only Tues to Thurs) although it was usually crowded and hard to find seats in the dining-lounge room and the food area set up was not so good and there's usually a line and people were hustling which I didn't like the feel of that. The room and bathroom is spacious for nyc and clean, so I love that. Location is not bad, it's about - blocks from subway and -- minutes walk to -th Ave. Only negative is I had loud neighbors so I could hear their talkings and tv on and also the cleaning service in the morning, although outside street noise was not a problem, didn't hear much. So they have good soundproof for outside noise, but not for indoor noise. So I would come back if I could use points to book here cuz it's good value for nyc but I would not if I have to book at the rate of $--- to $----night.

I stayed at this hotel for - weeks on business and I do travel for a living, so believe me when I tell you there staff was rude and snotty! The front desk and concierge acted like they were the guests and that you were bothering them when ever you asked them something. In one instance I was at the front desk just standing there texting a colleague when the front desk girl came by and said in a snotty tone, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""may I help you with something"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", obviousoly I was texting someone and should not have looked like I was in need of any help!, so I said """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is there a problem with me standing here texting someone?"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and she pointed to seats accross from the desk and said """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" there are seats over there"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", so I said back again, so I cannot stand here and text someone?, and she said once more in a snotty tone and pointed """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" there are seats overthere"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Whatever, this hotel for the amount of money it cost, forget it! Down the street is the Marriot Waterfront, I should have stayed there, they would never treat anyone like that. 
Signed, One pissed and insulted business traveler!!

I stayed here for a week in May as a solo traveller. It was a week of contemplation and decision making for me so I wasn't overly concerned with the strengths and weaknesses of the hotel. I was lucky to have sufficient Marriott points to cover most of my stay, but paid usual hotel rates for the last - nights. Check-in was smooth and swift, and my room was spacious with a nice bathroom. I didn't eat at the hotel, nor did I use the leisure - fitness facilities so can't comment on those - too busy out exploring this wonderful city :-) It has a very good location on the corner of Post - Mason within easy walking distance of all transport links and up-market shopping and entertainment.

Nice hotel, it was a great place to stay at. Very good locations.
Their is bus coming to pick up, but the rooms is not so big and i am not sure if pets are allowed or not. I am also not sure if their is connecting rooms. It was a really nice trip.

Hotel is nicely located and very close to all attractions. The rooms are big and nicely decorated! 
Breakfast is also good, but the manager has to do somehing with the crowd and also needs to have better variety for everyday selection. Manager's reception was however definitely a plus. What I really found a bit unusual was the front desk unfriendliness, which is very uncommon for a Hilton hotel! Concierge was good, but front desk could be a little friendlier. That was a bit disappointing especially since I had to wait - hours to get a room.

This is a good - not great - Four Seasons hotel. For those who customarily frequent these types of hotels (Mandarin, Peninsula, Four Seasons, etc.) you will leave satisfied but not awed.
Rooms: The rooms are generous in size (especially for downtown San Francisco), if a bit dated. There is one sink in the bath of the King bedroom, and the carpets are beginning to fray. However, my wife and I shared the room for three nights and I worked in the room for two days and it was sufficient for these purposes. It would be in the middle of my Four Seasons experiences with regard to furniture and design. For those who watch television, the room did have a very nice flat screet televesion.
Restaurant and Bar: The bar is one of my favorites (and this feature matters to me!). The setting is comfortable and the service is very good. The wine list is above average and there is always a bit of activity. For the restaurant, it is good but not great. . .on the lower end of nice hotel restaurants in this city.
Physical facility: This hotel shares a fitness-spa with a large major chain. The positive is that all work-out equipment one could want to use is available; however, the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""intimate"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" spa experience is non-existent. If someone wants the more traditional nice, small, intimate work-out or spa experience stay somewhere else!
Location: It really is a good, centrally located part of town. One is very close to the SOMA area of town, the financial district, Union Square, and a short walk to North Beach and the tourist areas of the Embarcadero and environs. Location is a positive for this hotel.
Overall: We have stayed here several time and I do not quite recall being so underwhelmed? It has been a couple of years and, with all things American, we continue to take things to an ever-increasing level. Maybe it's expectations but I think this hotel has slipped a bit. If I came back I would try the Mandarin. Oh, and by the way, this is becoming a common Four Seasons issue. . .you pay for EVERYTHING here. Wireless - check. Printing in business center - check. USING the business center - check. Perhaps I am in the minority (I'm sure they've done the market study), but I'd rather pay --, --, --. . .whatever more per night but just stop nickel and diming me!
Value: The hotel is not expensive for San Francisco or compared ot other Four Seasons properties. Perhaps it is because of my comments above?

We stayed at the Magnolia Apr ---, with our - month old daughter. The hotel service was superb. From the town car service from-to the airport, hospitality of the front desk and food service staff, bell hops opening doors for us and driving us around in the complimentary shuttle, everyone had a smile on their faces and seemed too happy to take care of us. We received a $-- per night upgrade to a signature suite, and in addition to the free breakfast and late night cookies, we couldn't believe what a great deal this was! Too bad we didn't manage to make it to the free happy hour. There's always next time. Will certainly stay here again!

I stayed at the MOSSER in March for - days. I absolutely loved it. It is perfectly located in the middle of everything about a block from Union square. On one corner, you have Yerba Gardens. On the other, you are on Market Street and you have access to public transportation. You are about - - minute walk to Chinatown. The hotel itself is great. The rooms are small but really clean and really boutiquey. I like the charm of the hotel. All the staff is wonderful. You might feel a little crammed in te room, but it gives you the feel of the city. I need to go back in December and I am definitely staying at this place. Also, I was lucky to find a deal for under --- by booking through otel.com.

When traveling for business I often give less thought to the hotel because of how little time I spent in the hotel itself.
The checkin was fantastic, staff were great, got a fantastic room with a great view on a high floor. Could not have asked for better.
The starbucks in the lobby was a great touch and the location allowed for easy walks to a number of bars and restaurants. There were only - negatives I had for this hotel.
Taxis - when asking for a cab, we were told to wait and maybe one would come by. I could not believe that they doorman would actually let my business partners go out in the rain trying to flag their own cabs. He actually recommended for him to do so.
The only other negative I had was the very slow service at the hotel bar. We were trying to get a customer a little more drunk before talking business and honestly with ----- minutes between drinks it just was not possible.
I cannot honestly comment on prices because I have no clue what things cost when we travel on business.

This is a very solid hotel and in general up to Hilton standards. Not spectacular but clean, nicely appointed, and recently remodeled. Staff is effecient. One complaint is that the neighborhood can be somewhat noisy at night and the walls-windows did little to buffer the sound

I visit New York frequently but usually stay in midtown for business reasons or close to Central Park out of habit. I decided to try a new neighborhood on a weekend trip and am glad we landed at the Tribeca Grand. The hotel has an interesting location and unusual layout, being more or less triangular in shape. The staff (mostly in their --s, I'd guess) couldn't have been friendlier or less snooty. Our room, a Grand King, was spacious enough for two people, although there wasn't a lot of space for luggage (small closet). We thought the modern decor was pleasant and never had any problem with noise from the lobby (we were on the -th floor). Although the room did not have a coffee maker, we were happy to discover a good quality free coffee machine next to the ice machine very close to our room (I believe there is one on each floor). 
The neighborhood is quiet but there are excellent restaurants in walking distance. We didn't try the hotel restaurant. Subway access is very convenient for multiple lines. What's not to like?

This is a contiuation from my prior week story when we stayed at the Marriot courtyard in Lynnwood. The subsequent week we stayed at the Homewood suites on Western (Elliot), North of down down and due West from the Space needle. What a pleasant difference from our prior weeks stay. The main difference was having two -- inch TVs with HD that worked. Some may not see this as a big deal, but we find it important during football season (my wife more so than I).
The other amenities included an extensive free morning breakfast, news paper and dinner and drinks if you stay Monday through Thursday. The Marriot added on the cost of the breakfast and the quality of service and food available do not compare to Homewood suites.
Air conditioning was built in, not something hanging out or by the window and was much quieter than Mariott's.
Would definately stay here again, and would even consider purchasing a unit if it was available as part ownership (timeshare-part time simple title ownership).

A really good hotel. Awesome bed and a good sized room. Watts Street is though always busy as it goes to a car tunnel. Our room faced the street but earplugs erased all noice, so no problem. Very close to the subway and the nice streets of Soho. Plus the hotel offers breakfast which most hotels in NYC don't, so money is saved there. Really nice personnel too, ask them for restaurant tips. We went to a great Mexican restaurant. We will definitely stay at this Hampton again next time.

My husband booked the NY trip as a surprise for our -th wedding anniversary, so once I found out where we were staying, I trawled through the reviews. 
I chose to keep an open mind and was glad I did. 
The lobby is spectacular and the staff are very friendly. 
We upgraded our room on arrival, at a nominal cost per night but what I hadn't banked on was that it was the size of the bed that was being upgraded and I of course expected a larger room too. The room was cosy but sufficient, that was until day -, once the cases were spilling over with washing and the shopping bags had been accumulated. The room suddenly became oppresive. 
Kyrstal at reception did take on board my concerns and kindly offered a change of room on a lower floor. 
We travelled with another couple who had a much larger room on a lower floor, so guys I guess the lower the floor,the bigger the room.
I would reccommend the Paramount and would stay there again without a shadow of a doubt and I am a pretty picky traveller. 
Overall, the room was very clean, sufficient for a few nights and the staff were very accommodating.
Thenonly downside, not enough wardrobe space.

I was there for four days and there were many problems, including:
-. Plumbing problems, i.e. no hot water. There was lukewarm water in the shower and the bathroom sink. Management sent someone up to fix it, but the water was still lukewarm the next night. In desperation, I crouched down under the sink and saw a water valve and turned it all the way open. That fixed the problem. I didn't know I needed basic plumbing skills to stay in a four-star hotel. I was so demoralized by two days of no hot water that I didn't even bother mentioning that the shower didn't drain. I just stood in water up over my ankles every morning.
-. Extra blanket problems. I called the front desk around --PM to ask for two extra blankets. After a long pause, the night manager said he would check with Housekeeping to see if there were any (?) and that he would call back in -- minutes if there was a problem. A --- hour later, no call, no blankets, so I called again and finally got the blankets. How gauche of me to expect a hotel to have blankets!
-. The layout. The bathroom has a separate room for toilet and tub, with a sink and vanity area outside of it. Unfortunately, this area is opposite to the bed. There are no sliding doors to close it off, so you both better have the same sleeping schedule.
-. Everyone has their hand out for a tip. It is really obnoxious, especially in a place that doesn't really have a doorman. We were there for - days and - nights and except for our arrival and departure, where the doorman knew he was going to get a tip, we opened the heavy doors ourselves.

We often did not want to get out of bed in the mornings and just snuggle in. 
A great gem in Boston.

I reserved a room at the Allerton for a romatic weekend in downtown Chicago. I reserved a king junior suite and that is not what I got. The room did not match the discription of the room at all, It was so off we took our luggage back down stairs to let the hotel staff know that they gave us the wrong room. The staff told me that the room was correct and that it was a good room. I have never been more dissapointed in hotel in my untire life. Two of the three mornings there was a bug in the shower and when we checked in there was a dirty towel on the floor in the bathroom. The location was great and within walking distance of everything you could want, but that does not make up for the $--- it cost to park for three nights. So to recape, the hotel is in a good location but it is not the cleanest or do you get what you pay for.
Back to texas in another trip and back to Austin Plaza.....Clean, safe, great location, nice service...maids...mananger.....just great! I will stay there always when im in Austin-TX....

Despite the ridiculous $-- + tax fee for parking (every hotel in San Francisco charges outrageous parking fees) our two day stay (Saturday and Sunday) was fairly reasonable as San Francisco rates go. The hotel is very conveniently located - just a couple of blocks to Fisherman's Wharf, another few blocks to the cable car turnaround and easy walking to quite a few other spots. Across the street was a Safeway which also was very convenient and just a few steps away from that was the bus service.The rooms were spacious and modern in decor - they were clean, the beds comfy, and the staff very helpful and friendly. We enjoyed sitting outside in the casual firepit seatings the hotel has despite the wind and cold. Unfortunately, a homeless soul would wonder in occasionally and ask for money (something the hotel is trying to stop but hasn't succeeded in - these people are all over the place - you literally trip over them). Despite the high parking fee, valet parking was included in the price, so we said goodbye to the car for two days and didn't worry about it one bit. We got a very decent AAA for our stay and I would recommend this hotel to anyone. Sometimes I just wonder from some reviews if people actually stayed in the same hotel I stayed in..and I consider myself fairly picky.

The hotel is so convenient to the historical district as well as being right across the street from the Reading Terminal Market. We used the Phlash Bus which was in back of the hotel on Market Street. This bus takes you to all the major sites for Philly. You really don't need to use your car once you check in. Taxis are very convenient after hours and usually about $-- for a trip to most places from the hotel.
The room was clean and very close to Sea World. The only thing that I didn't like was that the beds were very uncomfortable. Other wise the room was good

i loved this hotel, the staff were friendly, the room was lovely and the bed very comfortable. the japanese bath was brilliant. toiletries supplied [especially the soaps] were of excellent quality and there was an abundance of towels. i'll be back.

We stayed at the Edison for - nights and had a great time. We got a renovated room (thanks to a recommendation on Trip Advisor, I phoned ahead and requested a renovated room - and I got one)
The room was beautiful. Very small bathroom. My one concern was that this pipe in the bathroom got extremely hot (I burnt myself on it) ...and I had - kids with me. There should have been some sort of warning sign around that pipe. Other than that, the staff very friendly, room was clean, great location

I had a blast staying here! But the rooms are the extreme form of retro. They are funky and colorful. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""old seventies chair"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in the corner really is an old seventies chair. If you prefer the ---- version of the old Dodge Challenger, don't stay here. If you like the original muscle car, and don't mind a little rust in the floorboards, you'll have a great time. Be sure and log on to their website. They have photos of each individual room, so you can choose your flavor of funk. Location among the clubs and vintage shops is awesome. If you ever wanted David Lynch to design your Valentine Getaway, choose that bright pink one by the pool...

Have stayed here a couple of times. Good hotel. Nice rooms with a large sitting room and a large bedroom, well equipped with fridge and microwave, good breakfast spread, free drinks in the evening. Undergoing renovation - part of the lobby was cordoned off and carpeting was being changed when i was there. Good shuttle service to nearby offices and malls. Prompt check in and out.

We stayed here for one night to catch an early morning flight to Kauai. It is not worth the money we paid (about $--- including tax and fee).
Our room is small and old. We waited more than -- minutes for their shuttle to pick us up at the airport.
We don’t recommend this hotel to anyone.

Stayed at the Intercontiental for - nights while visiting LA. -st off this hotel is in a excellent location. Right next store to the FOX studios and a short drive to LAX. Also for the shoppers out there, a shopping mall within walking distance. Easy excess to Beverly Hills, Hollywood and Santa Monica. The hotel entrance and lobby is very beautiful. Trendy with fresh flowers everywhere! 
The staff was excellent!!! Every single staff memeber from the valet, front desk, bellman, room service, housekeeping, restuarant and bar staff were all friendly and happy and always asking how our stay was going.
The room was very nice with windows and balcony that wrapped around. 
The spa was nice and the staff member were friendly and educated. I recommend getting a massage if you stay at hotel. I am a frequent spa goer and I definitely rank this massage up there. 
I would stay at this hotel again and recommend to anyone looking for a very nice hotel, in super location that is affordable.

Check-in was somewhat chaotic as they were renovating the lobby area and construction work was going on at the front desk. Nevertheless, the receptionist was helpful and friendly. Junior Suite Room was located on the -th floor. Spacious with - different rooms and far enough from the noisy street. The room was clean and the décor was fairly basic and slightly old - sufficient but nothing very glamorous. Minibar was empty as often seems to be the case. Amenities were standard with no frills (e.g. no bathrobe or slippers). Nevertheless, the room served its function well. The hotel restaurant is ordinary and I didn’t have time to try the breakfast. The hotel bar is small but freshly renovated with a great bartender. It seems that at least the lobby level of the hotel is undergoing renovations at the moment. All in all, a fairly good price to quality value and location.

We spent a week at the Custom House in Boston. Initially we were a bit worried about whether there was enough space for - adults and - kids but as there is so much to do in Boston, we spent very little time in our rooms. When we did we just watched movies or slept so we had more than enough space. The staff were really nice and helpful - we had many good recommendations for restaurants or shops from reception staff. The location is fantastic - very close to Quincy Market which has great shops, and near the harbour which has so many great restaurants as well as great views and tours. If you visit the Custom House, it's worth going up the top floor for a view of the city - beautiful. There are also laundry facilities up on (I think) the --th floor and a games room which we made use of. Just a warning that if you take or hire a car, there is a -- dollar charge per night for valet parking - and the car sat right outside the front door! Overall though we had a great stay and we would definitely go back or recommend it.

I spent the night (Sept -, Labor Day) at the Hotel Monaco in Denver. Arrival and check-in were very nice. The pleasant Front Desk agent was friendly, recognized me as a Kimpton in Touch guest, and upgraded me to a King room on the -th floor.
I was stunned when I opened the door to my room to see how small it was. I have added pictures to this review to illustrate. In two of the pictures, I am standing with my back to the door.
Because of the small room size, the furniture within is very cramped - note that the living room chair is wedged underneath the desk. I had to pull the desk several feet to the right in order to extract the chair and use it. In a room this small, they probably should have just skipped this chair altogether.
Because it was Labor Day, the hotel's restaurant was closed. That turned out to be a good thing, because it forced me to make the - block walk to the --th St. outdoor mall area. There was a lot of activity there and plenty of restaurants to choose from.
The exercise room in the Monaco is OK. A treadmill, a pair of elliptical machines, and a stationary bike. Two racks of hand weights are wedged between the treadmill and the door. The room does, however, afford a nice view of the street outside.
All in all, the Hotel Monaco is a nice enough place and conveniently located - though I suspect that the rooms in the Residence Inn next door are much, much larger.

Following the very good Tripadvisor reviews, I forgot all the things that are being associated with a motel and stayed here for a few days with a friend. You really get top value for your money and this isn't anything like the normal motel you know. 
It starts with the service, which is amazing and very friendly and continues with the breakfast and the very clean and comfortable rooms.
The facilities (pool and a tiny gym) were also unexpected.
The only con about this place is the location. It isn't loud at all (as you might expect because of its proximity to the highway), but it is just far out of the center of Austin. There really isn't anything around and without a car you would be lost.

Stayed here to celebrate a special day together. I was disappointed in the room overall. Chose the suite but really shouldn't have. The suite gives you a strangely shaped room addition (about -' by --') that really is more of an afterthought. There is a couch and a TV but the couch is so close your neck will be sore from looking up at it. The tiny TV was nothing to write home about either. The bed was comfortable, the bathroom adequate, but there really was nothing else worth noting.
Some nice touches here, nice people, but not enough to be that costly. If you want to splurge, go for the Elysian. That hotel is beautiful and really will WOW you.

I stayed there in april ---- for a conference at the convention center which is practically across the street. the room was neat and clean. the room has a tv set, microwave oven, ref and a phone. just behind the inn is the gaslamp area. the area is safe.

Anybody who is considering staying at the Milner Hotel should think twice.

In Boston for college tour. Only stayed one night. The room appeared clean on the surface. However when I opened the bedroom curtain the entire window frame and on the outside window sill was covered with rust and mold!!. The room was freezing because the air conditioner was on. I turned the air conditioner off but was unable to warm the room up inspite of the fact that the control indicated three settings-cold, normal and warm. The temperature control cover came off in my hand. The bath tub drain dislodged from the pressure of the water.

I stayed here when attending a conference up the street at the Omni. The Normandy was less expensive and ten-fold as nice. The rooms are thoughtfully and elegantly appointed, the beds are comfortable, the bathrooms large. Many boutique hotels tend to be heavy on the attitude but light on the amenities and comfort... not here. One complaint: The staff, while polite and attentive, was very slow to answer my emails, and I had to ask three or four times and wait five days for a confirmation to be sent to my email address.

This was the cheapest place I found in San Francisco that still had availability when looking to stay Valentine's weekend. Because it was so cheap compared to other places, I wasn't expecting much. I was pleasantly surprised by our room. It was very clean and there were unexpected amenities - free Wi-fi, mini-fridge, coffee maker, iron, blowdryer, skylight (not sure if every room has this...we had an upstairs corner room).
It wasn't exceptionally noisy as it's at the end of the block away from --- and is centrally located to all of the places we planned to visit. The person who checked us in was very friendly.
My only complaint - I am -'--"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" tall and the shower head came to about my neck. I've always vowed never to stay in motels that think every customer is an Oompa Loompa, but I'll probably make an exception for this place.

We just returned from a - night stay at the Hotel Metro following a Canada-New England cruise. We wanted a nice hotel from which we could easily explore the City during our few days we had set aside to see New York. Everything was great. We had a room in the corner on the --th floor with a view of Herald Square and Macys. It was one of the renovated family suites, so it felt new and fresh and I loved that my kids each had their own bed in one room and my husband and I had our own room. The beds were super comfortable and it was quiet at night. We slept like babies after long days of touring. The breakfast in the morning was very appreciated with delicious bagels and big yummy muffins along with fruit, cereal, juice and coffee. It was a perfect carb loading meal to get us revved up for walking the City. And there is so much to see within reasonable walking distance from Hotel Metro. It really is an ideal location. We saw three Broadway shows during our stay and walked to all of them. We also took advantage of the subway station that is at the end of the block for some of our longer treks.
The staff was very friendly and helpful. We arrived early on our first day after disembarking from our ship and they stored our luggage for us until check-in time. On our departure day, we didn't need to catch a taxi back to the airport until early afternoon and once again they stored our luggage and got us a cab when we were ready to leave. The concierge was helpful with all of my questions and gave us great directions for using the subway. I loved the Hotel Metro and it is the place I will return whenever we come back to New York.

The marina tower has the outdoor firepits, large pool and outdoor bar. The pool in the bay tower is very shallow. Also, we were booked on the second floor, which was really ground level, when asked if we could all be moved to a higher floor was told it would be another $-- per night, per room. Not worth it. Staff was friendly and when I lost my phone in Quinns the first night was relieved when it was returned to me the next day!

The rooms were very poorly cleaned. There were many black marks all over the walls and drawers as well as black stains on the pillows and sheets. Also, the showerhead and faucet head are caked with rust. 
However the location was great, right in the middle of Manhattan (within walking distance to Times Square). The rooms were small, the bathtub-shower a bit outdated, and the furnishings of the room were old and battered. It was more like a motel or inn than a three-star hotel.
I would definitely not stay here again. A better hotel choice would be the SHeraton which is less than a block away.

I spent two nights during the week in August at this hotel. Very good service. Comfy bed and nice room. The only drawback is the soundproofing. Conversation from room next door and hallway could be easily heard. Also in the bathroom I could hear through the vent system conversation coming either from upstairs or downstairs bathroom. 
Roof deck is great and lunch food was very good also by the pool.
I just did not feel totally secluded in my room.

My boyfriend and I loved this hotel. Just a short walk to metro and in a gorgeous quiet neighborhood. room was spacious with clean and comfy linens. If we visit dc again we will return. parking is limited but expected in a city.

This Hampton in was awesome. Very spacious rooms. Clean and well cared for. Breakfast was very good. GM Victor and his staff were very welcoming and their service was top notch. Old Town San Diego is a -- min walk. It would take longer to find a parking spot if you drive. I cant wait to visit again.

Stayed here with my grown up son, the main reason we chose it was we could get a room with two decent beds - we weren't going to share a double bed and two rooms would double the price.
The room was OK, yes I agree it was a bit tired but it was large with two king size comfy beds, no fridge, no safe but good aircon and although we were on the road side (--th floor) traffic noise not a problem. Good location, easy walk to Central Park, Times Square, -th Ave and port area for boat trips. The staff we experienced were friendly, efficient and couldn't be more helpful.
So it was cost effective and served our purpose well - we were enjoying New York, shopping, watching the Giants and the Yankees -having a ball, not skulking around in the hotel thinking about the bad review we would write when we got home!!

It's not bad but not as clean as I would have liked. The bath mat was dirty and their were random hairs in the bathroom and on the sheets. There are lots of hotels in this area so I probably would not suggest this one.

I went to an academic conference at the nearby Marriot but found, through Expedia, a very reasonable deal on a four-night stay at the Dana. It was very good value for money. Free WiFi, good food, nice room (packed with electronics, such as iPhone dock and large flat screen), really excellent location, friendly and helpful staff. Never used the spa, but I suppose for many that would be an added bonus. Breakfast service was prompt and convenient, no problems at all. Would definitely stay there again when travellling to downtown Chicago.

The Radisson Suites was a great hotel. I just got back from a three night stay and I couldn't have been more pleased. The room was large and kept very clean, the restaurant was comfortable and had good food. But, the best part of my stay at Radisson Suites was the customer service. It was five star service from start to finish. Every employee I came in contact with was personable and helpful beyond belief. I usually stay in fancier hotels; I chose this hotel because it was close to my niece. I have never encountered service of this quality anywhere. I couldn't have been more pleased.

If you imagine a classic, high-quality city hotel - imagine the Sofitel Lafayette in DC. Professional service and friendly, polite, helpful staff (though the emphasis on constant French greetings may seem a bit odd, it does contribute to its disctintive personality). Our room was not big, but adequate, soft carpets, good storage space, a bright clean and efficiently spaced bathroom - and the most comfortable bed ever. Really ever. The location is simply perfect, right in the heart of downtown Washington. The restaurant-breakfast-bar are all very satisfactory. The main criticism would be that it seems a bit old-fashioned to charge for internet connection - no longer justifiable, in my opinion. 
If I have the choice, I hope that on future business trips I will be able to stay here again.

Needed an affordable overnight stay for a college visit. Was very pleased with the clean conditions of the room. Our room came equipped with a microwave and a small refrigerator, which was very handy. I asked for a non-smoking room, and was pleased that it did in fact smell like a non-smoking room. The decor and TV were a little dated, but for the price and the fact that everything was clean, I could easily overlook that. If you are looking for a clean and comfortable no frills stay, I am happy to give it a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""thumbs up"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".

Great location and our room was surprisingly quiet even though it was in the center of Midtown. Just a few blocks from Times Square on one side and St Patricks Cathedral on -th on the other side. Room was smaller than others I've stayed at in NYC but had flat screen TV and coffee maker. 
The shower in the bathroom was not separated from the rest of the floor so the whole floor was soaked after a shower, which I did not like. Lots of business people in the hotel - not much of a tourist hotel - no concierge to help us plan our time in NYC. 
Would recommend for location and value ($--- per night when booked and paid for in full in advance).

The Marina Motel has a great location and is within walking distance of some great restaurants, shops, cinema. -- minutes by bus to Fisherman's Wharf, free parking..... all as per the Motel spiel.
However, unless you are used to traffic noise, I implore you to book a room off Lombard Street in the courtyard. 
We took sleeping pills to help us get an hour or two of rest, but still found it difficult. We tried to change our room, but the Motel was fully booked, so we decided it was easier to stay for our remaining three nights than to pack up and try again. 
It did mean we spent every waking moment away from our room. We crammed a lot into our - days in San Francisco!!

This hotel has an excellent location - walk to the Art Institute, M Park, Concert, etc. It offers decent rooms; check-in counter staff are very friendly and helpful; restaurants are good, too. Everything there meets expectations of a --star hotel. Downside is lack of swimming pool and parking is very expensive (>$---night).

This hotel is beautiful. The staff is very accommodating. The rooms have kitchen facilities hidden behind beautiful wall units. Great to have your own bottle of Champagne. Great views of the East River and Chrysler Building.

I went here with my son who loves all things Japanese. The location is right in Japantown, so it was perfect. If you love Japanese pop culture, you'll appreciate the design. Beyond that, it is simply a great place to stay. The beds were very comfortable and the linens were fresh and clean. All the furniture seemed new. The bathroom was fine. Nice towels. The hotel staff was very helpful in giving directions. There are quite a few bus lines right outside the hotel, so it was very easy for us to go all around San Francisco without a car. Also an easy walk to Fillmore Street, where there's shops and dining. A great value.

This Holiday Inn was very comfortable and quiet, had a king suite, with nice additional space for working and watching TV. The restaurant was quite clean and had a nice selection of local favorites, although they would run out of the sausage by mid week. Service was friendly, rooms were kept clean, and the personell at the front desk were helpful. Good location just outside of the downtown area, good access to the major highways. Parking below the hotel was tight, made for small vehicles.

My family & I visited the Bay Area to attend a Giants game & stayed at the Homewood Suites San Jose. Great covenient location to HWY --- and into SF. Clean rooms & grounds, great breakfast. You can tell that the rooms had a recent upgrade completed, as they are fresh and modern. Will most definitely stay here again!
This is a wonderful hotel with superb service-the rate is fair . The breakfast is good and I will be back in April

No doubt the location sells this hotel. Fantastically close to all the right spots in NY - - th avenue ,Carnegie hall, Times square, Broadway etc. Easy to get to the --th st subway for the NRQ lines. The rooms are spacious, but looking tired. The bed was really comfortable, and now that the restoration of the New York Centre next door is complete -a lot quieter. So the good points -location, beds and Jose and the team at the front -concierge services. The worst aspect by far is the breakfast - positively below average. Suggestion: ditch the included breakfast in rate. Great breakfast spots around the corner - including the Carnegie deli.

I loved the Inn at Queen Ann so much that I was very sad to leave my room in the morning and happy to come back at night. The rooms are very basic but very, very comfortable and very, very, very clean. I am very particular when it comes to cleanliness and the Queen Ann met and exceeded my standards. The rooms have a kitchenette that comes in handy, and there's a ---hour nice supermarket one block away. The building is very old. It looks nice but it's by no means fancy. The location is very close to some of the most famous sights in Seattle, such as the Space Needle and Kerry Park. The neighborhood has a ton of good restaurants and (dive) bars that make for an authentic Seattle experience. It is, however, a bit far from downtown. Only ten minutes if you take the Monorail but half hour walking. A cab ride is about $-.
I will definitely stay here again next time I visit Seattle. I would also recommend the Queen Ann to anyone traveling on a budget who still enjoys a comfortable and clean room.

My stay at this Hilton Garden Inn was exactly what I was looking for. The staff was always helpful and i was centrally located to everywhere I had to go in the city. Several times i asked for a recommendation and directions and the staff was always spot on. The room was clean and the temperature control worked very well. I plan on making a personal trip to NYC and this will be my first choice.
Had reservations for my best friends wedding. The front desk staff was very rude and when I called him out on it he threatened me telling me to leave and he was calling the police.

The bathroom was very dated and only one person could get ready, it was the smallest hotel bathroom I have ever seen. The carpet was torn and dirty, it was like going back -- years in time minus the oppulence. I would never recommend this hotel. The hallway always smelled like a horse stable, not impressed.
