Property is located steps from Ghirardelli Square, a block from Fisherman's Wharf and on a cable car line, but is quiet and peaceful. Our suite included a bedroom, a large living room and a small, fully-equipped kitchen. This hotel was a great find!

This hotel hit all the right notes!!! It was a great location in Beverly Hills.The staff went out of their way to welcome and please, and the decor was classy-cool. I definitely recommend...extremely good value for money spent!!!

My daughter and I stayed at the Hilton San Diego Resort and Spa last week for - days. It was a wonderful experience. We visited Whitney, the 'Guest Experience Coordinator' when we first arrived. She recommended wonderful restaurants, helped us find our way around, suggested things for us to do, booked our kayak trip and was just a lovely young lady. The Hilton itself is a lovely Hotel. Rooms are spacious, beds are wonderful. The restaurant is superior and overlooks the Bay. Each meal we had was excellent. We saved time to enjoy the many immenities at the Hotel and the beautiful pool area. It's a family friendly casual beautiful resort. We hope to return some day. And a special thank you to Whitney!

Room was adequate size considering it was NYC! Entire facility was spotless. Maintenance man was constantly tweaking little things in the building to keep it nice. Breakfast was typical Holiday Inn Express, which was fine. The location was wonderful. We easily walked to Times Square and back for three Broadway shows, but doorman will hail you a cab if you prefer. Wonderful small ethnic restaurants right around the corner on -th Avenue. Had a room on the --th floor with a wonderful view. Shower was fine. Yes, the elevators were a little bit crowded at """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""peak"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" times, but in no way unmanageable or intolerable.
What pushes this hotel from very good into the excellent category is the staff. All friendly from the moment we arrived. There is a concierge in the lobby, but if you want the real scoop on anything all you have to do is ask Alex at the desk. Alex was genuinely enthusiastic about the city and made some terrific recommendations about places to eat. We had Indian,Turkish and Pakistani around the corner on -th Avenue. He was full of insider tips that saved us much time (and the aggravation that sometimes comes with staying in such a big city). I can't tell you how impressed my husband and I were with Alex.
I hope to visit NYC again within the next couple of years. I will recommend this hotel to my friends. I would not consider staying anywhere else in NYC!!

We stopped here for four nights on our honeymoon.
This a small hotel but presented well. The front desk staff were very welcoming and made an effort to treat us as valued customers. As it was our honeymoon they had allocated us a very nice room, quite high up and freshly decorated. The style of the room was very nice and the finish was excellent. Looking at the floor plan it was one of the biggest on the floor, however, had we been stopping any longer it may have started to feel too small but for a short stay it was fine.
In the room we were greeted with sparkling wine and a souvenir photo frame which was a really nice surprise. The rubber duck was a great quirky touch in the bathroom. The free Wi-fi was also a bonus and very useful.
The location of this hotel is fantastic. Opposite Sak's, two minutes from Macy's and next to Borders Book shop (great for a late night coffee and cake).
We could hear very little street noise but we were quite high up. There was no air con but the ceiling fan was fine.
I would definitely use this hotel again.

After a lengthy flight and arriving in Denver for the first time, the
prospect of Grand Hyatt hospitality was far too tempting ... and not really realised after check-in. The welcome at front desk was unrivalled, but once the elevator it's all downhill as you travel uphill in this downtown business hotel.
Rooms - disappointing. Tired and in need of a spruce-up, if not a multi-million $$$ rennovation from top to bottom of all ---plus floors! The air-con was more like central heating and every bit of the room needed cosmetic overhaul. That said, the bed was very comfortable and the linens superbly laundered, there has to be a positive somewhere. Don't expect - star accommodation, but if here for a meeting or convention you're sure to sleep quite comfortably. Views? Not really. Pool? Indoor and heated - but could do with draining and re-modelling. The best feature undoubtedly the service of the hotel's exceptional personnel and the Starbucks coffee shop right under the portico at the entrance - convenient coffee when you want to escape the drabness of your room.
Come on Hyatt, you know your can spend a few bucks and do this one up
to your usual luxury standard!! Coincidentally, the Denver Hyatt just
the other side of --th Street looks much more chic and glamorous
... although The Westin is undoubtedly Denver's best hotel address judging by it's glossy facade
Lastly, 'Max' on Concierge Desk ... we thought you're a star! :-)
Very comfortable and relaxing. Great staff. Excellent location. Good value. The suites are very large with lots of room. Feels like an apartment more than hotel room.

Stayed here a while ago, but forgot to put up a review at the time. 
Don't come here expecting the same standard as say, a Grand Hyatt in Asia (e.g. Shanghai or Hong Kong), because it's completely different. Apart from the size of the place, there's nothing grand about it. 
Tried to check in at -pm, but the room wasn't ready, so had to hang around one of the cafes in Grand Central. When we got to the actual room, it was a bit underwhelming - dingy. The walls, as many other people have said, are paper thin. Hard to sleep if your neighbour is watching TV. The bathroom was a decent sixe, but there wasn't much hot water on the first night I was there.
Service alright, but nothing special. Overall, give it a miss. it seems unfortunate that this is the only Hyatt offering in New York City.
Yes, New York hotels are expensive, and what do you expect $--- per night etc, but this place is poor.
We booked the hotel as we were driving through Hollywood and were not disappointed. The hotel is quaint but the staff is awesome!! I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone.

My husband and I stayed here - nights while touring DC with our - year old daughter. The location cannot be beat! An entrance to the Metro is directly across the street, cafe's and restaurants are abundant in this vicinity, and the historic sites are within - blocks or a short ride on the Metro. Service was friendly and good. The business center was easily accessible. Very clean. 
The only issue we had was that the parking garage cost $-- per day in addition to the room cost of $--- +. Then a tax was added to the charge. For - nights of parking our car in the underground valet-only garage, we spent $--. Then we felt obliged to tip the valet. All total, we spent over $-- in parking-related expenses. 
The indoor pool was VERY small, and the water was cold, so my - year old was disappointed at the end of the day when she planned to swim after a day of sight-seeing.
I do not recommend this hotel to anyone with babies who don't sleep well through noise. Because of it's location, sirens (fire, police, and ambulance) can be heard at all hours of the night.

Arrived here from another hotel during the travel disruptions from the volcano. Very helpful and pleasant staff. While rooms are a teeny little bit dated, overall a really great stay. Ate in the restaurant and the staff here were brilliant, and the food just delicious Very close to Central Park. Would definitely stay here again.

Upon arriving in San Antonio for business, I arrived at the Hotel Valencia. I was informed that the night before their building had been hit by lightning and they were going to be without power until later that night or possibly later. Everyone from the valet people to the front desk were apologetic, even though I knew it wasn't their fault. They had already made arrangements for me to stay across the street (at another nice hotel I might add), pay for the room and my valet parking. The next day I came back and checked into a quaint and comfortable hotel overlooking the Riverwalk with a staff who were exceptional. In addition, when I got back to my room that evening, there was a plate of fruit and a half bottle of wine as an apology. As far as I was concerned, none of this was necessary to apologize for a lightning strike, but they certainly went out of their way to make it a delightful experience and I would not stay anywhere else the next time I am in San Antonio. Top marks!

just arrived home after a week in the holiday express on --th st . great location just - blokes from times square and --nd st. friendly staff very helpful and a good breakfast to start you off on your day , yes its busy but you are in NY what do you expect it all adds to the fun. while we were there we were hit by hurricane sandy , the hotel keep us informed and ran as smoothley as possible the staff really did there best in a bad situation .

Our family of - had - flights cancelled due to Hurricane Sandy and were delayed from flying home for a week.
We appreciate that rates are subject to change , however the Hotel, despite being aware of our predicament, saw fit to increase the price of our room from $--- per night to $--- per night. 
We feel exploited and deeply saddened that they chose to take advantage of stranded guests and are appalled at the poor treatment we received. This flies in the face of ordinary New Yorkers pulling together to help each other out in times of tragedy. A little compassion and understanding would have gone a long way.
We have stayed at the Double Tree on previous visits to New York but won't be doing so again.
It is a pity that this appalling treatment has tainted our view of New York and we know from
speaking to other guests that they feel the same way.
We were forced to move to alternative accomodation after - nights and had to rely on family and friends to support us financially until we were able to return home.
An unforgettable experience for all the wrong reasons - shame on you DoubleTree

This is an extremely clean hotel and a great location for a price that is unmatched.
Excellent facilities, very clean and very quiet. Great location - - only five blocks from the Phoenix Conference Center. It has free parking and very safe neighborhood.
Ask for a first floor room if you are elderly and do not wish to haul your luggage through the stairs since it does not have elevators. But it is worthwhile in every other aspect!

I have always enjoyed staying at Holiday Inn Express and looked forward to our stay at this one. Our reservation was made -- days prior to arrival and we expected we would have two beds for myself and grandaughter, age --. When we checked in, however, we were told that the only room left was one with just one double bed! Sure enough, my confirmation stated that while """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""all rooms are guaranteed to sleep the number of guests you provided during your search"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", they cannot guarantee the number of beds. Beware! Both of us had a very poor night's sleep as a result, and I will be extremely wary of booking Holiday Inn Express next time.

For a very low price, you get a perfectly clean room and a spotless shared bathroom (- per floor for about -- rooms, some lines in am but not awful). The elevator is tiny and there's only -, so it takes forever; we took the stairs from the -th floor to get out in the am rush. There are no frills, but there is internet on the -st floor for $- for -- min, a lifesaver to get those addresses I forgot to write down. Remember to take your soap and towel to the bathroom to wash your hands! Front desk even monitors who comes and goes and if you look confused or suspicious asks if you're a guest. Quiet neighborhood - blocks W of the --th st Metro (exit at the --th st exit).

My husband and I were married here and have returned recently to celebrate our anniversary. We were greated by a friendly valet staff and doorman, who remembered our names and greated us with a warm handshake. Just one of the small differences that make this a first class hotel, truely the finest I have ever stayed in. 
We have stayed in three room types, standard harbor view, deluxe city view and a center harbor view suite. All of the rooms are spacious, clean and comfortable. The beds are plush, clean, luxious and down right heavenly. The city view is just as wonderful as the harbor view, but watching the sun rise over Boston Harbor is absolutley priceless. 
The food at Meritage is unforgettable, offering both small and large plates, we were able to dine on Lobster, Kobe Beef and Fillet Mignon with wine perfectly paired for our meals. The service was unparalled. 
The Boston Harbor Hotel is everything you would expect from a --star hotel, but what make this hotel different is the warm service and friendly staff whom I can not say enough kind things about.

Upon entering the lobby, my cousin and I were somehow intimated by the grandeur of the hotel, however, this was instantly changed with the warm welcome of MS. MARICHU ALVAREZ at the lobby! We felt at home with the holiday spirit (christmas decors and beautiful gingerbread castle) because we were treated as if we were good old friends! If you need a place like home, then, do stay at this hotel!

The room was scary and not remodeled. I stayed because it was cheap, in a great location and I had no plans to do anything but put my things down and lay my head there. I will never stay there again.
The owner was kind however.
I got what PRICELINE paid for...last time I let them 'negotiate' for me.

From the minute I drove up, the staff was courteous, helpful and on top of things. The Desk staff, charming, and the lobby, beautiful. My room, clean, quiet and very well appointed. The bed, super comfortable. I stayed in a Lux suite, and was surprised that the bathroom, was quite small. Shower only, which was a disappointment, as I had an cold during my travels and really wanted a soak. Otherwise, really, really great stay. Great location. An easy walk to most attractions. And Lola, amazing!

My husband and I stayed at the Argonaut for one night on our return from Napa valley. He had never spent time in SF, so we decided to spend a day and a night here before heading to the airport. Depending on what you want to see in the city, this can be a really great location. You are steps from Giardelli Square, which, although touristy, does have a few good shops and restaurants. You are also literally one block from the cable car line on Hyde and you are practically on Fisherman's Wharf itself. Here is what we did in our short stay, which hopefully gives you an idea of the possibilities:
We had a bit of trouble finding the hotel; the traffic and crowds on Jefferson, where the front of the hotel is located, are pretty crazy on a Saturday! You pretty much have to valet your car for $-- per night, because there is no parking close by. Check-in was prompt and friendly and our room was small but clean and cutely decorated with a nautical theme. 
We quickly made our way to Fisherman's Wharf, which starts just a few steps outside the hotel. We had lunch at the Fog Harbor Fish House. The atmosphere, food and service were great, however the portions are HUGE! Way too much for a lunch when you plan to be walking around! After lunch, we walked The Embarcadero and up Telegraph Hill via the Filbert steps, then made our way down the Greenwich steps. This is quite a hike, but I highly recommend it. After lunch, we did some souvenir shopping along Jefferson and back to the hotel for a nap. The hotel was quiet.
We then walked to Ghiradelli Square for dinner at McCormick and Kuleto's. Although this is a chain restaurant, the service and food were good and we had amazing views of the bay. The next morning, I walked up Hyde to Lombard and down the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""curvy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" section of Lombard, which is another popular tourist activity, then stopped at the Starbucks on the block behind the Argonaut to pick up coffee and bagels.
All in all, the hotel was very sufficient for our needs of an overnight stay. There seemed to be a wedding going on that night and there was some loudness in the hallway near our room late at night, but it only lasted a few minutes until the revelers returned to their own rooms. This is a very cute hotel and better than most in the neighborhood. The location allows you to experience a lot of what SF has to offer. One last peice of advice; the boat trips to Alcatraz leave from the Wharf. I highly recommend touring Alcatraz, but you must purchase tickets days in advance, as they sell out. I have been to Alcatraz in the past, but my husband wanted to go and even with the concierge's help, we were unable to obtain and tickets the day-of.

We stayed at the WSH for a week earlier this month and were very pleased. We did change rooms at the start of our stay as the Queen Deluxe we were first assigned, was very, very small! I know hotel rooms in NYC are tight and I am not hugely fussy but to be honest, I would not have been comfortable in that first room for a week (esp. after all our shopping LOL). However, a quick visit to the main desk, a new room was assigned, we just had to wait one day - so all was well. 
Second room wasn't huge either but was a good deal bigger than the first and was very comfortable. A little road noise can be heard, but that's shouldn't be be an issue to most visitors to NYC - I hope. The hotel is very clean, the staff courteous and helpful and the main plus - is location. I have stayed in mid town on - previous visits and we were ready for a change, so glad we did - it made for a completely different NY experience. 
There is a subway right at the end of the street and we got to all locations we wanted to without having to change trains, you get either one or the other of the - lines and they take you to most of the main attractions - excellent! 
We didn't try the restaurant - too many choices elsewhere. The complimentary breakfast is a nice touch and there was plenty of the usual continental items available.
All in all, the WSH does exactly what is says on their website and I would recommend. Don't think I'll go back there though but only because I have the upper West Side in my head for next time...........................

Stayed for - nights from the day after Labour Day which meant the pool and bar were closed, whiich was a shame as the weather was very hot and I was looking forward to a cocktail and seeing evening views. However, that was the only disappointment. On check in the receptionist saw we had requested a king room if one became available and we were given it without having to ask.
Our room was quite large, with flat screen tv and the bed was superb, also liked the number-selection of pillows. We were on the top floor and had no noise problems.
Pastries, coffee, fruit etc were provided each morning and the restaurant was nearly complete - it looked good!
We ate at Union Station most nights and were -- minutes walk from Capitol which meant it was easy to queue for tickets.

This hotel is very well located . You are walking distance to the most attractions.
For this trip, I was looking for a hotel in a good location and this hotel has it....
I trully recommend this hotel if you have the same interesting.
Rooms and service were fine and no complaints at all. 
Beautiful lobby and bar.
You can have fast meals at Fox and Obel and breakfast at Starbucks.
We had the main meals at Cheesecake factory restaurant.

Went during spring break with my family on SPG points. Staff not very friendly, and front desk never smiled or was really helpful (except doormen were nice). Requested king w-rollaway, and were placed in a TINY room...no way a rollaway could fit. I requested a larger room, and after was teased by the housekeeping supervisor that a much larger corner room was available on the floor, moved to a regular room on the west side of the building. It was small, but mammoth compared to the first room. Reviews are right about the minibar, but one fact is that beer is cheaper there (if you don't mind cans) than a bottle plus tip at the dark and quiet bar downstairs. There is a liquor-beer store about - blks away, just north of CVS in a market-grocery. I was not aware of it until near the end of the stay. Only challenge for vacationers and kids is that it is about -.- blocks away from the Circulator bus route, which is perfect to see DC cheaply and get to the sites. Surprisingly, limited restaurants in the area unfortunately. To do it again, I might have stayed at the Washington DC Westin downtown, even though reviews say few restaurants, I found most the eateries to be on that side of town, and very very close to public transportation. To do it again w-kids, I'd pick the Embassy Suites (one of the -) for lots of reasons...including space and location. Also, BEWARE...pool is outdoors even though the pictures appear it's inside (much of the reason we picked this hotel was the indoor pool).

Spent - nights here, a family group of - people. Having read the previous reviews about the hotel having a fun vibe at weekends I contacted the hotel direct and requested rooms on a quiet floor. This request was not a problem and there was a lovely touch left in my room (thanks Jim!) which shows that customer care is paramount to the running of this hotel. From check in to check out the staff were nothing but friendly, courteous and helpful. The rooms were fabulous and the bed luxurious. The lights could be adjusted and dimmed to suit your mood accordingly. The quality and cleaning of the room couldn't have been better. The weather wasn't the best during our stay but we did pop up to the pool to take a look and I can imagine it on a lovely sunny day. I'm not the right age group to go to a club so I gave it a miss, but judging from the beautiful people in the lobby of the hotel on a weekend night I imagine it to be the place to go and be seen. Other reviews have mentioned the area where the hotel is. There is a metro station just outside and as far as I'm concerned it was a godsend as we relied on public transport to get back and forth from the airport (Flyaway bus to Union Station and red line metro direct to the hotel). Yes, there were a few homeless people there at night but they did not cause any problems or make us feel at any risk. It is at the end of Hollywood Blvd and there are some cheap underwear shops there, but there are equally as many fast food places and bars so you have to put it into perspective. It's only a short walk to Hollywood Highlands (or one metro stop) where you'll find plenty of places to eat, drink and better shop. All in all, I think this is a Wonderful hotel, far exceeded the quality of the other -* hotels we stayed in during our -- day trip to the USA. If I ever return to LA then this is where I'll stay.

With sleek decor in the lobby and some of the trappings of a nice boutique hotel, it gives a good first impression. As time goes on, the hotel begins to feel as though it is part of a movie set and is not actually run by trained employees. The rooms are decent, but small. A narrow armoire serves as a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""closet,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" so storage space was limited. The bathroom was divided oddly into two sections, sink area and toilet-shower. But the door to the toilet-shower area is glass and very see-through. There is no door between the bedroom and the bathroom entry where the sink is. Therefore, there is no privacy at all. Among the - of us staying at the Angeleno that weekend, we all agreed that was a very strange design choice and made things awkward. Not everyone sharing rooms is on such an intimate level with their travel partner that using the toilet behind glass should feel natural. We called for room service and it rang indefinitely. Many menu items were not available. Pool towels were mysteriously missing one day, and no one was around to fetch them. The poor woman in the coffee shop was our go-to person for everything, and she barely knew how to run the coffee shop. Many coffee items on the menu seemed beyond her capability. Ingredients had run out or were not available. The smoothie mixer was broken, or required mix that they didn't have on hand. 
The one place where things work well is the valet station. Those guys run a good operation, which can be tricky at the intersection of Sunset, the --- and Church Street under repair. Bravo to those guys who bring the cars up and down. They are always there, always friendly.
If you stay there, ask for a room on the side facing away from the highway. The noise is very loud. Staying higher up in the building might help also, but then you contend with the super slow elevators. We tended to use the stairs since we were on Level -.
The beds are comfortable, with nice clean linens. That is worth a lot in my book! In general the room was clean.
The location is convenient to Westwood, Brentwood, Palisades, and parts of Santa Monica. Beverly Hills is not too far, although traffic made it slow. Despite all of my observations being pretty critical, I have hope that the kinks can be worked out. I hope the Joie de Vivre company reads guest reviews. For the reasonable rate, I would be willing to try it again. It is hard to find - adjoining rooms in LA for under $----night, and that's what we had.

Stayed here on business with a corporate rate of $----night which seems very reasonable for a big city like Boston.
Hotel is generally filled with business travelers. It is located across the street from the train station and has direct access to a large shopping center.
The room was large with a nice city view of Boston.
The bathrooms are small and awkardly configured. The toilet is too close to the door.
They need to be remodeled completely!
Also, housecleaning needs to do a better job. My bathroom had significant amounts of hair in the sink and some in the tub.
Currently, they are doing construction in the lobby area, so its dusty and messy. Also, they were checking the elevators and they were not functioning at certain times of the day for fire alarm inspections. All of it was very annoying.
Took a taxi to eat near the sights and every cab ride was on average about $------one way
Me and my brother stayed in this hotel due to the Hotel Fusion being a dump but this hotel was great, big rooms, big gym would def go back and the location for the shops was ideal

Stayed here while in San Francisco for - days. 
Hotel was very good. We were placed on the --nd floor which offered a great view.
The location is excellent. You can easily travel to parts of SF with Bus stops right outside the hotel and a Cable car stop on California Street (which is next to the hotel). Buy a Muni Pass and travel the buses and cable cars as single trips on a cable car are $- one way, but a - day pass is only $--. You can buy these from the Hotel's gift shop.
Breakfast was good. Offering Continental as well as hot (though - days of Scarmbled eggs got boring). 
There is a pool on the -th floor, but we never used it.
Rooms were well sized and clean. Beds were comfortable.

Our son convinced us to join a frequent stayer program and so we picked Choice Hotels which is a good mid-range bet. The staff here are excellent and very helpful. Rooms are big and the bed was good. This hotel also offers a great bang for the buck.
Recommended.

I am a loyal Starwood traveler, and typically have great experiences at their hotels - but this one was different. The main reason is the service was well below an acceptable level, which manifested itself in several ways;
- - I had a two night reservation which they switched without my permission to two one-night stays b-c they had me on a floor that was being shut down for a remodel. This meant my wife and I had to pack everything up, check-out, and then check-in again to a new room. It also meant I was billed seperatley for the two nights.
- - Service at the resteraunt and room service were below an acceptable level. We dined in the resteraunt each morning for breakfast, and it consistently took over -- minuets for the food to arrive. When we ordered room service, not only was it slow, but they took the order wrong and did not deliver what we had asked for.
- - Front-desk service - again, below an acceptable standard. As already mentioned, they did not inform us of the situation that they would need to check us out of our room due to remodel, and then when we called the next morning they were fairly unaccomodating. Uon check out they had also mis--billed sveral items (i.e. internet which is supposed to be free for platinum members), and whne I pointed it out the lady practically accused me of trying to cheat or steal. 
Overall it was a very poor experience. It is a shame b-c the room we were in the second night was great, but it isnt worth having to go back and deal with substandard service at every level of this hotel.,

We booked for - double twin rooms, but the reception staff said there were no double twin room left. We then given two Queen bedrooms with fold away beds, which were no way fitting in such small rooms. We make a complained, but this staff didn't not bordered at all, her attitude was really bad!! 
We been treated with this attitude ever since we checking in. At the end the manager involed and arraged - double twin rooms. 
We didn't understand why she said there were no rooms at the first place, and suddenly there WERE rooms!??!?!!!! 
Since we been treated with such an impolite staff, we decided to check out earlier (originally we planed to stay for - nights). We ended up staying at the Hiton Hotel next door, aparently they offered excetly the same price and much better services!!!
We will never go back!

I frequently stay at the Jumeirah in NY for business.
Always a pleasant place to be. Rooms are clean, service is great, spa is well equipped despite small (dont always have much time).
The location is the best thing in the hotel. Located in Central Park South, in the heart of mid-town its walking distance to most offices and restaurants in mid-town. Also, great for shopping.
Breakfast and the restaurant are pleasant but nothing outside of the ordinary in a -* hotel.
The large suites are very comfortable. Too much space (no complaints), but would be better used if need to host for dinner or for work meetings.
There is a large sitting room, guest bathroom, meeting table, fireplace and bar.

What can I say - great location! Right next to everything you'd want to see - walking distance of Pike's Market, great restaurants, good attractions. We upgraded to Club level, and it was totally worth it. We didn't even end up going to dinner some nights because we just ate the delicious food at the hotel!
We got a view of the Space Needle and the north side of the city, which was pretty awesome, too.

The hotel is located near the Alamo and just a short walk away from the Riverwalk. As with other Residence Inn's, we appreciate the apartment like atmosphere. We were in the middle of our cross country driving trip and the fact that this hotel had two different laundry rooms with multiple washers and dryers, made our chore must less time consuming. As with most summer days in San Antonio, the weather was hot and sunny. The locked shaded parking garage was a huge plus!

Other reviews speak to the location - it is fine and convenient. You are very close to the useful and free shuttles that run up and down the --th street mall. We travel a lot and use Choice Hotels a fair bit (that is the chain that Comfort Inn as a part of). This is one of the worst in the chain bar none. We stayed six days and had our room cleaned once and that was at - a.m. Want to sleep in to -, you are out of luck. I had to find our own replacement towels, soap, dump our own garbage. The dust was so thick on the dresser that I wrote """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""dust me"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on it )(see the picture below) it was still there when we checked out. Food from room service lingered in the hall for more than -- hours - you get to watch the sausage rot in this hotel. We requested a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Do Not Disturb"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sign from the front desk, none was ever provided despite the promise to have one brought to the room. I could go on, but you get the point. A decent property that suffers from neglect. Where is the manager of this place? Send in Gordon Ramsay, please.

Great location and we were VERY impressed with the staff, cleanliness, huge room!, very comfortable bed and it was very quiet despite being less than - minutes from the airport. It would have been nice to have a Continental breakfast, but we came prepared, and the pluses far out-weighed this. There was always coffee available in the lobby and our shuttle driver was prompt and very nice. We would absolutely stay here the next time we fly out of Seatac!! We are from Vancouver Island and flying to the Middle East, so it was wonderful to have such a lovely relaxing stay the the night before.

My family and I just returned from a terrific two-night stay at the Beacon. I don't need to repeat all the favorable comments on TripAdvisor regarding this clean, spacious, fabulously-located hotel. You can read the comments yourself, and the comments are all true. 
My aim here is to inform future guests of the odoriferous resident pets on the fourth floor. The Beacon used to be an apartment building prior to transitioning to a hotel. A few people and their smelly pets apparently remain. I'm not allergic to pets but being alerted of their presence by the hallway odor was unexpected. This is a very old building with no AC in the corridors. NYC summer heat, oppressive humidity, pet odors and no ventilation are a lethal combination. Blech!
Be that as it may -- we loved it here and will definitely return. Next time I'll try to get one of the corner rooms on a higher floor as recommended by previous reviewers.

This is coming alittle late but I had not realized I had not written a review on it sooner.......We went as a family in June and booked through priceline.com and got a great deal on this hotel!!! But when booking through priceline I seem to think they do not offer all the extras that you get when booking through themselves.....no mention of breakfast vouchers etc.......but the money we saved bought me breakfast, lunch and dinner for a few days lol.....so no big deal.....I get it.......The lobby and facade of the Holel is so old world Hollywood-Business feel to it.....The history is fantastic and Matilda the cat terrific....Rooms are trendy but way to small for more then two,....but this is New YORK!......old Iron stairs were real cool.....elevator very slow at times but again this is a old Hotel so we have to take the good with the bad........Locations was perfect few blocks away from it all!!! Have fun!

I stayed - nights for a June weekend. @ $--- a night including taxes I thought I was given a small, tired-looking & really poor value room. The bed was, I has to say, superbly comfortable. The bathroom pokey & old fashioned. It was a charmless room. 
The view across to Telegraph Hill & the bay was awesome, of would have been had it not been marred by just the filthiest hotel windows I've witnessed in my life. They were so dirty it was almost comic: I Tweeted about it & management Tweeted back they acknowledged windows are an issue & they're 'on track' to clean them this year. Hmm...
I ordered room service dinner on arrival: a filet mignon was well-cooked but the side mash and gravy was cold & potato not properly cooked; crab cakes were also cold & tasteless. 
Service levels are good - especially check-in--out, but I was hassled by the concierge to take a hotel car, over a taxi, which irritated me.

I was required to attend a conference and meeting at this hotel for work. I used the complimentary shuttle service from the airport. Although the vehicle was rather small for the number of passengers (Toyota Sienna for - adults, some of whom were tall, some of whom were portly) we made the short trek without incident. My overall first impression was that this was a fairly nice property. When I approached the front desk the attendant asked what she could do for me. No smile, no warm greetinge; she simply wanted to get to business. It was early in the morning, so I knew there was a good chance my room wouldn't be ready - and it wasn't. She instructed me to come back at a certain time when she would assign my room. I returned at the time she instructed, she said a room was not available and that I should come back in an hour. Once again I followed her instruction. This time when I arrived, she looked at me as though she'd never seen me and asked what I needed. I explained to her that she told me to come back to check in... At this point she said the room still wasn't ready, but she would go ahead and get the paperwork done so that I could come back in an hour and get my key. I agreed, and an hour later I received the key for my guest room.
Upon entering my room I found it to be quite dated, with worn furnishings and stained cushions and carpet. The mirrors in the room were obviously not cleaned, evidenced by something smeared on them. When I phoned home, I sat on the bed and happened to look behind the nightstand where there was a dirty tissue from a previous guest, I assume. When I opened the closet I was pleased to find a mini refrigerator; a bit unexpected, but it was a good thing. Clothing is intended for the armoire-dresser. San Diego can be a bit warm, and this place does not offer central air. There is an old fashioned, rather loud, wall-unit air conditioner that protrudes out onto the lanai; which by the way is very nice with its patio table and chairs. 
The lighting in the bathroom is awful, as is the condition of the tub-shower, with its chips, stains, and mildew. There is a hairdryer and coffee maker, along with plenty of soap, shampoo, and lotion. Somehow my toothbrush didn't make it into my bag. I called the front desk to inquire as to where I could get one after -:-- p.m. They said they would send one right over to my room. In less than ten minutes there was a knock on my door, and I had a colgate toothbrush and toothpaste. Now that's some good customer service! (I guess it's hit and miss depending upon who is working what shift.)
The actual geography around the hotel is great. It's situated right on the water, so the immediate surroundings are lovely. The only way I would return would be for a conference or meeting; unless of course the property underwent a major renovation.

Bang in the middle of downtown LA where there really is nothing to do. Around the corner was a Starbucks and few other small sandwich shops but nothing spectacular or interesting.
It's close enough to all the freeways if you need to drive and in that sense it's very convenient. We hired a car and it took us maybe -- mins to drive from the airport. They were charging US$-- a night for parking which you can take the car in and out as you please - usual tips to the drivers. There is parking a plenty around the hotel and prices were about US$-- but I never could be bothered to park and walk to the hotel.
I think GRAND is the word you can use to describe the hotel. It's got a nice entrance, lobby, bar and restaurant. Very acceptable. The gym is quite old as is the equipment - feels like you're working out in an old turkish bath area.
Rooms are OK... big and spacious but the beds are way too soft. It can get quite noisy being downtown (the occasional fire engine or police car screaming past). There's no kettle in the room so you have to use the coffee machine to boil your water.
I paid about US$--- per night, staying for - nights. Not bad overall... but I'd prob want to try another hotel next time I'm in LA. Didn't do enough to convince me to stay again.

Our family enjoyed our stay at Off Soho. The suite was clean and roomy enough for four adults. 
The staff was exceptionally friendly,pleasant and helpful. 
The hotel was convenient to Chinatown, Little Italy,Soho and St. Marks place and an easy subway ride to other areas of the city. 
My only """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""complaint"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was the mattress on the pull out sofa bed. This was a bit thin and lumpy and could use an upgrade. The kitchenette could have used a coffeemaker too.

We had a nice stay at the Hilton Garden. It isn't the most exciting property out there, but there was little to complain about. The staff were very friendly at the front desk and elsewhere. Everything in our room worked well and the tv was modern. Given that I had to work one day in the room, a bonus was the ergonomically friendly desk chair. It was good to have a microwave and large fridge, and free wifi. Our north facing room had a decent view as well. Our bathroom was average size but one small issue is that the plumbing was somewhat noisy.
The fitness room was acceptable and it looked like there is an adjacent pool area. There is a Weber Grill onsite - there was an hour wait so we ended up carrying back to our room. Location is excellent - many nearby restaurants, bars, shops and a Trader Joe's and Jewel within a block. The Grand Red Line Station is directly below the property.
We received a great value for our room and were pleased with our stay.

Rooms are small but have been recently remodeled and my room had a plasma TV. Everything was very clean and the front desk was helpful and pleasant. The only noise I heard was one ambulance go by but when don't you hear that in a big city.
Downsides - small room, no bath tub (not that I needed it) and breakfast wasn't complimentary.

For the price i paid $--- a night i thought i would stay in a top hotel in beverly hills, the rooms are not quite taken care of, the towels in the room are very small and old, thy should change for new ones, no pillow selection, the housekeeping was awful, they always left garbage in the room, take too long to bring an extra towel, the restaurant is very nice but the rest of the hotel looks kind of old, the carpet in the hall had stains, and many of the halls smelled like marihuana, generally too much money for such poor benefits i rather next time stay at other hotel for that price.

Stayed at the Hotel Burnham during a recent business trip, and was so impressed by the staff. Our group was greeted warmly on arrival and given a run down of the offerings (including coffee in the AM and a number of items available if you forgot to pack them). Once in my room, I realized I needed some toothpaste and called the front desk. I was amazed to hear a knock on the door with the item seconds after the phone call ended!
Every employee, from Ben at the front desk to Linda in security treated us fabulously. They even continued to provide above and beyond service after I checked out - we needed to check out via phone and have a colleague drop off the keys later (no problem!). I called for a copy of the folio the following week and Ben had it in my email box in minutes.
The cafe attached to the lobby has fabulous food and a nice atmosphere to unwind - I especially loved the grown up mac and cheese!
The regular rooms are a little on the small side, but I was so pleased with the service that I didn't mind at all.

We stayed for - nights - staff was terrific - very helpful and always smiling. The parking structure is definitely different - but we parked our car and walked and cabbed and used the trolley. Close to Petco - Balboa Park - an the Gaslamp. Hotel was clean and the beds are great. Would stay there again. Cost was comparable to other hotels we looked at in the same area.

Room

 facilities

We used this hotel before and after an Eastern Discovery Tour in America. The first night we were in a room overlooking the financial district with fabulous views, on our return we were put in a smaller room at the side of the hotel next to an office building - not so good. There is an excellent coffee bar and comfortable lounge-bar area, also internet facilities in the reception area. Did not eat in the restaurant which looked a bit deserted. The reception and portering staff were very helpful. Not the best of locations if you want to visit the miain attractions (Midtown) but perhaps a little quieter.

The hotel has a fantastic location just seconds from Times Square. But that's where the positives end.
During my stay one of my group got - severe electric shocks whilst using the shower. They couldn't have been static shocks since she got two shocks in quick succession, and her hand was still numb several days later. The must have been an earthign fault leading to ---V reaching the shower.
My friend made a complaint and they were changed rooms. However we feared the safety of anyone else using the original room. What if a child or some one with a pace maker used it and got an electric shock, it could prove fatal. So we wanted to know they were going to get it investigated and sorted.
We spoke to the owner whose initial repsonse was they would send the maid to test it. When we pushed how dangerous it was and that they were risking people's lives she offered us a free night next time we came. One of the receptionists agreed with us that it needed investigating properly but the owner refused to accept the risk. It was only as we were leaving she said she'd send a general maintenance man to check it out, not a professional electrician.
Since returning to the UK my friend has reported the matter to the New York council for them to investigate.
On another note the elevators were a fiasco. When we were checking out it took -- minutes to get back to the ground floor. We eventuay discovered one of the elevators was out of order and the other wasn't exactly working properly. We got stuck on every floor and at one point the doors wouldn't open and some of my group started to panic.
So as long as you don't take a shower and are happy using the stairs this is the perfect New York hotel.

Took my son to college this weekend and stayed at the Hyatt. Figured this would be a great place to spend the night before he hits the dorm. The rooms are so outdated, hotel is dark, beds were so uncomfortable, even my -- year old who usually can sleep anywhere indicated how bad the bed was. My wife & I stayed for three nights in August. I had booked a deluxe king room and it was superb. -th floor on corner overlooking --th St NW. The bathroom had a separate large bath. Plenty of space in the bedroom and the bed was very comfortable. The first night we had a light meal at Urban Bistro - good enough for weary travellers. The hotel staff were always there if needed, suggesting restaurants & sights, etc. Frist day on the hop-on hop-off bus to get our bearings, second day very hot so spent it in the Air & Space Museum and Natural History. Only negitive is small bathroom, and no healthy breakfast options. No yogurt or bananas.
Waffles and biscuits and gravy though...and honey for tea.
Also when we arrived the coffee in the lobby was hot. It is cold in most places!

This hotel is in a lovely leafy street just off -th Avenue, is is close to the --rd Street Subway which is useful for the E line which connects direct to JFK plus all the other lines.
The area feels safe day and night and has some good bars and resutrants nearby although some do close early compared to NYC standards. There is a supermarket on the corner and a couple of Starbucks nearby.
The hotel is very nice although I did feel the rooms were a little small once you opened up the large suticase it was all a little tight, a light over the mirror by the sink would also be useful. However we did not spend much time in the hotel and the bed was comfy, a reminder to other guests that closing doors can be done quietly!
It is within walking distance of several of the main attractions or areas.

My family, friends and I all had a very pleasant stay at The Hotel Contessa. In addition to being a beautiful facility with comfortable, large suites, and large open lounge areas to gather with friends (the river level seating area and the roof top pool and hot tub area); the hotel's real value is in some of it's key personnel. My first and last contact at the hotel was with Eddie Gomez, the best bellman ever. Eddie's smile and genuine heart for service is remarkable. I wish I knew the names of the other bellmen on duty during our stay; they were fabulous as well.
I must also commend Erin Luther, in the catering department. Erin and the catering staff helped us host a party during our stay. The food was delicious and beautifully displayed, and the people who set everything in place were a joy to work with. 
During our stay we had the need of the maintenance man for a plumbing issue, we requested that a few burnt out light bulbs be replaced, and we requested a refrigerator for our room. After a call down to the bellmen, all our requests were quickly attended and with pleasant attitudes. In addition to this the woman in charge of housekeeping on our floor was also very pleasant, and helpful.
One other area of great service was at the Las Rambles restaurant. On our last morning at the hotel a group of about -- of us showed up un-announced for the the breakfast buffet. The gentleman who greeted me in the restaurant did everything he could to seat our group together and he and his crew took excellent care of our group.
Over all, we had a wonderful stay at the hotel. The only area that was a disappointment was contact with the front desk staff. Thankfully, Eddie G. and all the rest of the staff more than made up for the disparity of the service and attitude of the front desk personnel. If you need anything during your stay, call the bellmen first.

Choosing a place to stay for a trip to NYC can be bamboozling when there is so much choice and the prices are so high. I would not hesitate to recommend the Staybridge for several reasons:
-. Location - - blocks west of Times Square with many subway lines a short walk away. Far enough away from the hub-bub to get a good night's rest but not so far west that you end up in the seedier parts. Times Square is generally a great location to get to any other part of Manhattan, or even further afield.
-. Room quality - modern comfortable rooms complete with kitchenette; this can be a real money-saver if you don't want to eat out every night. There are several deli's close by and the Duane Reade drug store on the corner has a fairly comprehensive selection of food-drink items. Daily maid service who clean everything, even load the dishwasher.
-. Free breakfast - comprehensive selection of cooked and continental. Yes, breakfast room can get full. But you can either be sociable and share a table or take your breakfast back to your room.
-. Other free facilities - internet, gym and laundry. I don't recall having a problem with internet speed but I wouldn't expect lightning speed with a free service. The gym is small but reasonably comprehensive. Equipment in good condition. 
The only slight drawback that others have commented on is the number of lifts (elevators). At busy times you may need to wait quite a few minutes to get one. However, the lifts move fast, like everything else in NYC.

Yes, they can drop you at the Zoo but only at -:-- or --:-- and then they will only pick up at -:-- or -:-- - or something like that - Since we had - kids with us, we decided to rent a car - i am soooooo glad I did!

The Hotel Elysee staff has a great plan for making your stay comfortable...they anticipate your every need. The best part is the -nd floor tea and cookie room...always a comfortable respite after a day of touring NYC!

We recommend strongly Broadway Plaza Hotel for:
Top quality service, top quality cleaning, top willing to help staff
Deserves a great A Sanitary Level.

- Columbus is located right in Midtown Manhattan with easy access to restaurants, subway and a mall just accross the street. The staff and service was excellent from arrival to departure. I definitely recommend booking this hotel for your next trip to NYC.

My wife and I wanted to stay near theaters we would visit during our three day stay. The Hilton Times Square definitely met the location requirement. Prior to our visit, I called the Reservation Manager, Jill, to discuss some booking issues. Jill was extremely pleasant and responsive, which was a good omen for things to come. Upon arrival, check-in was quick and efficient and our corner room on the --nd (highest) floor gave us magnificent views of Times Square, Empire State Building and Hudson River. We had a flat screen tv and the bathroom was more than adequate. The bed was very comfortable with lots of pillows. We asked for maid service early in the moring and it was done when we returned from breakfast. The elevators wisked us up and down quickly and efficiently. Overall, we greatly enjoyed our stay at the hotel.

Based on the other reviews, I would recommend staying in the newer tower if you ever stay there. The best thing the St. Francis has going for it is the location.
My family and I had two rooms there on December --th. Although I had been excited to stay there based on the location and having been in the lobby, I was less than thrilled with the room. We ate breakfast at the coffee bar - okay, but Starbucks is only a block away. And, dinner right across the street at the Daily Grill which is always good. I might consider staying here again in the new tower if the room rate is reasonable. Oh, and you're not going to get away from the exhorbitant parking charges at any comparable hotel.

He was ever so nice and polite, check in did seem to be a bit long winded, seeing as most people have already booked and pre-paid on-line. 
When we got to the room it had just been cleaned and although the decor and the furniture was a little worn and tired there was nothing essentially wrong with the room. We wanted a couple of extra pillows and as the cleaners were in the corridor we went and asked them if they were able to get us a couple and they brought them to us about -- minutes later.
The location of the hotel is fab, easy to reach everywhere. We got the airtrain to and from JFK which arrives into Penn Station directly opposite the Pennsylvania, much easier and quicker than getting a cab if there is only - of you (usd -- per person)

The hotel is located in a beautiful and convenient area. The beds are very comfortable. Clio, the main restaurant is a must. However, the washroom is tiny and the rooms are not as clean and maintained as expected for a hotel of this category. The service and amenties are also very average.

The idea that you walk in the street level and there is a huge fountain you have to circle, then go up one floor, circle back around the fountain to check in is dumb. I dont know who laid this hotel out but it was not thought through well.
The hallways and rooms are DARK, I have a hard time seeing in the hallway. The rooms have no light switches, so you have to walk to each lamp to light the room which is a burden. The rooms are also very loud at night. I have stayed here --- times and each time the rooms are loud no matter which sie of the hotel I stay on. The property also isnt on the riverwalk, from --- corner rooms you can see the river, but to actually get to the riverwalk you have to walk a ways.

We just spent an agonizing night at the Hotel Americano. We'd planned to stay for two nights, but couldn't wait to escape this morning. Now comfortably ensconced elsewhere.
Where do I begin to describe the horrible experience we had -- four of us, in two adjacent rooms?
Our experience was similar to that described earlier by MaureenColorado. She wrote, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The hotel's designer seemed to mistake cheap, sparse decor for good design."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Please don't let the photos of the rooms on the hotel's website -- or elsewhere -- fool you. A bare concrete floor looks quite nice in a photo, but actually living in a room with a concrete floor is a bit like sleeping in Costco.
There are (essentially) no chairs in the room. The stool beneath the teeny, tiny desk is impractical -- nobody could actually sit on it. And the beanbag chair isn't soft, and doesn't envelop you. You sort of sit against it, rather than in it. Totally useless.
So your choice is to sit on the bed -- on the floor. There was a peculiar lamp hanging over one side of the bed, with probably a -- watt bulb. But the switch for the lamp was on the other side of the bed. The other choice was the florescent light bulbs behind the bed -- but they were incredibly bright, and could not be dimmed. The bed -- essentially on the floor -- was surprisingly comfortable, but the sheets were too small and instantly became untucked.
The bathroom was awful. It reminded me of a concrete version of a bathroom on an Amtrak train. Tiny shower cubicle, tiny sink, tiny shelf -- and very weak lighting. The towels were on a shelf at least (and I mean this) seven feet above the ground. I'm -'-"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and almost couldn't reach the towels. Her Ladyship is -'-"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and couldn't reach them at all. With so little light in the bathroom there's no way to put on make-up.
Although we booked two double rooms, each only had one robe, and one pair of slippers. (Remember the floors are cold, bare concrete.) We had an iPad in our room -- chained to the wall -- but someone had apparently left with the device that charges it, so the battery was all but dead. There was no battery in the clock in my sister's room.
We could not control the air conditioning or heating. The rooms had one temperature -- hot.
In his reply to MaureeenColorado, Will Jordan wrote, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""should you come back this way again at some point in the future, we will have the stool in your room replaced with a chair from our office."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" That's exactly what they finally did for us -- they brought us two desk chairs, vintage Staples. They were comfortable, but hardly gemütlichkeit. 
The hotel does not have parking. You need to go two blocks downtown -- yourself -- and park your car in a parking lot. This was explained to me ahead of time.
Dinner was actually very good, and our waitress was very friendly and efficient. It was the only nice part of our short stay. But we then found we didn't have any hot water in either of the rooms, and at breakfast the next morning we encountered the snooty waitress from hell. Burnt croissants, no cream cheese (I had to send them out to buy some -- which they did, without much grace).
The lack of hot water, hotel-wide, put us way, way over the tipping point -- and we checked out a day early. The hotel did not charge us for our stay -- which was gracious of them. Too bad they couldn't give me back a day of my life.
Her Ladyship and I have stayed at the Adam & Eve Hotel in Turkey. It, too, has concrete floors and low-down beds -- but somehow it seems to (generally) work at the Adam & Eve, and doesn't work at all here. This hotel is definitely, absolutely NOT for people like us -- in our early --'s. It's not for families. This is a hotel for young couples -- it looks like it's the perfect place for an out-of-the-way assignation. (Who will know you on West --th Street? I've lived in Manhattan for years, and have never set foot on this block of West --th Street until yesterday.)
But if you're planning an assignation here -- you'd better hope that the lady likes showers rather than baths, likes sleeping on the floor, and doesn't need light in the bathroom to put on her make-up.
When we were checking out, the bellman said he was from a Third World Country and the problems we experienced were """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""nothing in my country."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Hey, guy -- I've been to many Third World Countries, too -- but I made a reservation for a hotel in Manhattan, not Guatemala.

The best service and most helpful staff of any hotel I have stayed, period. From the concierge, to the desk clerks to the parking valets, everyone was friendly and generously helpful. Location is great, adjacent to the MOCA museum and close to Little Tokyo and Chinatown.

I had the most wonderful stay at InterContinental the Barclay! Besides the history of the building from ----, and all the important celebrities who have stayed there, this hotel has outstanding service and it is located at the heart of New York.

The honey made there is also delicious!
Not to mention the bed... The best I have ever tried!
The comfort and glamour of InterContinental the Braclay make you feel part of a movie... In New York City!

This was a very pleasant hotel to stay at in New York. It was quite, spacious - by NY standards - and the price was not bad for NY. Although the caveat is that it's crazy expensive to stay in New York - especially certain times of the year.
But it was clean, modern and the staff was friendly. The location was good too. - blocks from the subway. A -- minute walk to Times Square.
I would recommend it.

We arrived in New York for a --th birthday celebration and the staff at The Benjamin couldn't have given us a warmer welcome, starting with the bellman. Christine at the front desk was also so nice. She told us the history of the hotel and some fun facts about the new restaurant--perfect for foodies like us. My husband, ---month old son, and I just stayed nine nights at this Residence Inn. 
Our son has a rare metabolic disorder which requires us to prepare special foods for him, some of which require the use of either a conventional oven or a toaster oven. Just prior to our arrival, my husband inquired about whether the one-bedroom suite we had reserved has one or both, but unfortunately, it has only a microwave oven (which was a big help for other food we had to prepare) and a toaster. When my husband then explained the reason for our inquiry and asked whether there was a Target or Wal-Mart nearby where we could buy a toaster oven, they amazingly offered to go out and buy a toaster oven for us to use. Upon our arrival, we received a warm welcome from the front desk staff, who said they were waiting for us - a new toaster oven-convection oven was already in our room, and a Graco pack-n-play was all set up for our son - both at no extra charge. We then went to their Thursday evening barbeque where the manager asked us if the oven and everything was OK. I cannot believe what personal assistance and attention we received! The front desk staff was always very helpful and friendly.
The suite and property were very well maintained and clean. The carpeting in the suite looked brand new, and the bed was very comfortable. We were very pleased with the amount of space we had and the kitchen facility. The suite was much bigger than conventional hotel rooms. There was plenty of room to move around in the living area even with the pack-n-play. The kitchen area had a full-sized fridge with a freezer, dishwasher (which we didn’t use), and a small sink, and the cabinets were filled with dishes, a toaster, pots and pans, utensils, etc. - just about everything you would need. Even paper towels were provided. Adjacent to the kitchen was a small dining table and two chairs, and that room also had a desk, sofa, chair, coffee table, and TV (but no DVD player - we brought our own portable player). The bedroom also had a TV. The furniture isn’t fancy, but that isn’t a priority for us. The housekeeping staff thoroughly cleaned our suite early each morning after we left, and they were very friendly and polite and very kind to our son. 
Our suite overlooked the pool and basketball-tennis court, but our rooms were still quiet enough for our son to fall asleep in the early evening when children and adults were outside playing and swimming. Our suite was next to the elevator - I wish they could turn down the volume of the “ding ding” that plays every time the elevator arrives. We slept so soundly though that it did not wake us up. The air conditioner is located in the bedroom and was a bit loud, although it too did not keep us awake. The parking spaces are a bit tight, but unlike other Residence Inns in the area, there was no separate parking charge.
The breakfast buffet was free and much more extensive than I had expected. It certainly filled us up and saved us a lot of time and money each day. My husband enjoyed making the two of us Belgian waffles each morning - they sometimes even had blueberry or chocolate batter. Also available were muffins, donuts, bread, bagels, fruit (which was also available throughout the day), yogurt, scrambled eggs, potatoes, several types of cereal, three juices, coffee, skim and reduced-fat milk, and another hot selection such as biscuits and gravy, taco shells, pancakes, french toast, etc. Three high chairs were available for little ones. The staff members working in the “Gatehouse” during meal times were very friendly and kept the food replenished and the tables quickly cleared and cleaned.
Light meals were available Monday through Thursday evenings. We particularly enjoyed the Thursday barbeques which included grilled burgers, veggie burgers, and hot dogs, potato salad, watermelon, chips, soft drinks, beer, and wine. Music was playing outside; the volume could be reduced so that it isn’t so loud for those who are napping or working in their rooms. Another night there were french bread pizzas, which weren’t the best - they could be baked longer, and salad. The next night they had meatball sandwiches and salad, which were fine after a long day at the Zoo and the beach (although rolls other than hamburger buns would be an improvement). After a long day it was nice to just grab something quick (and free) to eat.
We went to the San Diego Zoo several times, having purchased a membership on-line a few weeks before, which is good for -- months and is also good at the Wild Animal Park. Membership more than paid for itself with just those few visits. Given our son’s young age and the heat and humidity, we weren’t able to stay at the Zoo or Animal Park all day, so it was great to have the membership card to come and go as we pleased. It took us only -- minutes to drive to the Zoo each morning between -:-- and -:--. The Animal Park was just a ---minute drive. Torrey Pines State Park beach was just -- or -- minutes away, except during evening rush hour when it could take about -- minutes just to drive the short distance from the hotel to the highway, which was a bit frustrating. La Jolla beach was about a ---minute drive. Beautiful Coronado beach was about -- minutes away. The front desk gave us cards with directions to each destination, which was a big help. 
While I wish there was a kiddie pool, our son absolutely loved swimming in the fair-sized pool, which was never very crowded despite a soccer tournament group and other groups being there during our stay. Towels were available pool-side.
The property is located in an office-commercial area, but it is not far off of the --- and is centrally located to the various attractions and nice beaches. Two grocery stores (Vons and Ralphs) and a Target are a short drive away, and there are numerous restaurants and fast-food places within a short driving distance. I was at the hotel when only --- of it was open. I meet Luis Diaz and call him every time, I'm coming up or any of my friends. He always takes care of everything. I call Embassy Suites Denver IAP my """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""eye of the storm"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". It's the place I look forward to staying at because it provides quiet, comfortable accomodations and a welcome break from the rigors of travel and the chaos that surrounds it.

I guess we got lucky-no noise from teenage drunks or elevators. Location was great. I hate valet parking but there is little choice in downtown Denver and the car retrieval times were actually prompt, not the usual eternity which makes you wonder what the $-- was for. Breakfast was good, not the usual bun passed off as a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""continental"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" breakfast.
The room and bath were small but comfortable.
My only complaint (which generally applies to Choice Hotels) is that despite Choice Hotels statement that airline milage is available if you ask, the hotel refuses to give it. Choice points are pretty worthless to me and calling to argue with the Choice people is more trouble than it is worth. As an incentive their rewards system is a negative in my book so they have to beat the competition's price badly to get my business. I wish they would drop the whole program and stop bombarding me with spam about the wonders of their program I know I am paying for it.

My kids and I stayed one night and I was fairly happy with the room. First, the positive aspects: the room and bathroon were clean, the beds were extremely comfortable with soft linens, plenty of towels were provided and the staff was friendly and helpful. The room was updated with nice furniture and had a large flat screen TV with plenty of channels. Free parking is always a plus, too. I also have to mention the convenience and delicious food at the restaurant, Bunz, which was right across the parking lot from the front entrance. Their prices were very reasonable as well. Okay, now for the negatives: the room had a slightly weird smell that must have been some kind of cleaning product or carpet shampoo. I couldn't quite figure it out. Our room was on the third floor, which could be pretty inconvenient if you have a lot of luggage. Finally, the exterior was dingy and could use a fresh coat of paint. All in all, I would recommend this hotel, but not for a lengthy stay - one or two nights at the most.

The Coventry Inn was easy to find, the staff was very friendly and helpful during our stay. The rooms were spacious and clean. We were able to walk to many attractions along the bay. We wouldn't hesitate to recommend the Coventry to any travelers.

This is my second visit to this hotel, the first being in July ----. The standards of the rooms are the same, as is the novel and rather stunning internal architecture, particularly the elevators. However, it is just this open plan atrium style that causes huge amounts of noise to rise from the bar area on the ground floor to the bedrooms. The hotel is a victim of its own avant garde styling. Perhaps the architect who thought of this should stay for several days particularly when there are sports fixtures in the area.
The bedroom was well appointed, but dated. It had a desk and a large, rather bouncy bed with a large array of pillows and cushions. The bathroom lacked shower gel, but it did supply body lotion, a bar of soap, shampoo and conditioner. 
Breakfast in the hotel was fairly standard fare, and based on that, we decided to eat elsewhere for all other meals.
The hotel charges about $-- for -- hours access to the internet. Why? Not many other hotels do that these days.
And finally, when I booked my four days, I was promised over the phone that $--- was the figure for accommodation. Not so. No-one bothered to explain the two taxes that would be added, bringing the total to well over $---.

I stayed that this hotel for three nights. Everything was pretty good when I got there. When I first checked in I asked if they had any rooms on a higher level and they had one. When we got to our room we found out that it was a handicap room. Neither my girlfriend or I was comfortable with that. It would have been nice if he had told us that before he gave us the room. I called front desk and they switched it. We got a room that was on a lower floor but that was ok.
The last night we stayed we decided to order room service. I saw on the menu that they were going to close pretty soon. And yes I do have pictures
The next morning when I went to check out the lady there did not seem really sorry about what had happened.
