For the hotel manager: If you have any questions please feel free to ask

I stay here often for the opera. I love it for the responsiveness of the management. When the hotel began using perfumed sprays during cleaning I had a problem sleeping in the perfumed room. I spoke with management in the morning. They asked me to call ahead next time and a room would be unsprayed for my next visit. I called and they delivered an unperformed room. I had a great night sleep. The rooms can feel tight but they have large windows that open for some fresh air.

The Gansevoort could be a decent place; nice location, ok rooms, but unfortunately most of the staff have ideas above their stations which inhibits the job they are paid to do; for instance, I simply want friendly receptionists and baggage men to help me with my bags, rather than mince about trying to look cool! So therefore the service, if it wasn't so embarrassingly hilarious to behold, was terrible. I'm not sure how hard any of these jobs are to do, but judging by the painful expressions and self righteous attitudes of the staff, they are obviously akin to rocket science....;o)

This review is for the South Tower, bay view room. I briefly visited a North Tower room, and it seemed to have a slightly more modern styling.
Pros - Excellent location right on the water; Star of India museum (tall ship) and Midway aircraft carrier are just a short walk away. Free WiFi (not super-fact, but servicable). Bike rentals available right outside the hotel. Both restaurants - an Elephant & Castle pub and a Ruth's Chris Steakhouse - are good, if a bit pricey. Service is decent. Bed was comfortable and bath towels were decent if not luxurious. Free airport shuttle, and free shuttle service to area attractions (but not to Petco Park, for some reason.)
Cons - Hotel is well-worn and in serious need of a freshening and modernizing. We had a room near the elevator, which is never a good thing, but in this case the noise was worse than I've encountered before. The elevator's """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""ding"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sounded like it was being piped directly into a speaker over the bed; on more than one occasion I was wakened out of a dead sleep by """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""DING DING"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" as the elevator arrived. Ice machine is out in the open, too, so the infernal rattle of ice cubes in plastic buckets reverberates down the hall. Voices from neighboring rooms are audible (understandable, if they're talking in normal volume), and bed is squeaky. You can put two-and-two together on that. Setting the room fan to high provides enough white noise to help mask the sounds from outside. Room furniture is dated and well-worn like the hotel itself, but serviceable. Water pressure in sink is negligible; tub-shower is better. There is no mini-fridge, safe, or closet (there is an open hanger area opposite the sink.) Bathroom lighting is not good and there is no makeup mirror. Balconies have no privacy from neighbor and there is no screen door to keep out bugs if you want to let fresh sea air into the room (we got eaten alive by mosquitoes, which I didn't expect in San Diego!)
Overall - I expected more for $--------night. The bay view from our --th floor balcony was excellent, but it couldn't quite make up for the intrusive elevator and ice machine noise or the somewhat rundown room. If Holiday Inn renovates the South Tower to quiet the elevators, add sound proofing to the rooms, move the ice-vending into a room or the stairwell, and updates the room interiors, I would gladly stay here again. As it is, I'd rather pay $-- extra a night and look into the Hyatt or Marriott. If you can get a deal in the $--- range, this is not a bad option. Try for a room as far away from the elevators as possible.

This hotel would have been fine -- years ago, but now almost everything looks incredibly dated, with the exception of the lobby which is fine, and tricks you into thinking you're staying somewhere nice!
I was only there for one night, and found the check-in staff decent enough, in that, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""we're being paid to be friendly"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" manner that you expect from a big hotel. To get to the room, you walk through the most dingy, dirty looking hallways (it's not actually dirty, just really needs re-decorating), with low ceilings and poor lighting. It really didn't inspire confidence.
When I got to the room, like the corridors, everything was clean, but worn out, with the exception of the bed linens, which seemed brand new. The bathroom especially looked like it really needed replacing. When I got to the room there was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""welcome"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" card addressed to someone else (the sort I used to get when I was a Platinum member of Marriott!), which turned out to have been left after the intended occupant cancelled. Not really a big deal, but a hotel on their game wouldn't have let that happen.
When I left my room to goto the fitness centre (which was, by the way, excellent), there was a tray with empty plates on it outside the room next to mine (which had been there when I got to the room), and was also there when I got back from exercising. For some reason a hotel employee came to my room to give me a razor (?) so he must have noticed the empty tray sitting in the corridor, but when I left my room to go for food, it was still there, and when I got back from eating about an hour later, it was still there.
It seems trivial, but again, it's just an example of a hotel that isn't top notch, and when you're being charged $--- a night, you expect better.
One of Marriots problems now is that with the refurbishment of their Courtyard chain, the cheaper option is now often better than their """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""full service"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotels.

The Beach Cottages are AWESOME. I didn't stay in one of the cottages, but in a room on the third floor of the main building. We had a balcony with a beautiful view. It was spotlessly clean. I figured being right on the beach it would have a sandy, grimy feel, but it didn't. The cleaners even sweep and mop the sand off of the sidewalks. Our room had a sliding glass door that we could open and look right at the ocean from the comfort of the bed. It was awesome. The hotel is completely fenced in, with doors that open right to the beach. It's a great place for kids, with ping-pong and shuffle board and they can play on the property. It's within walking distance of many restaurants and shops.

I needed a place to stay for one night before my flight so the Courtyard sufficed. It's not a bad place--rooms are clean and comfortable, bathroom is fine but both are quite small. The exercise room hardly lives up to its name however the pool is actually large and usually empty. Pretty much, only stay here in a pinch given the five minute drive to LAX. I took a video of the hotel room, lobby and amenities so if you want to see for yourself, you can watch here: http:--www.tripfilms.com-Travel_Video-v------Los_Angeles-The_Courtyard_Marriott-Video.html

I really enjoyed my stay at this hotel. I went to the Queens City to see a basketball game and I loved that this hotel has a shuttle that took us to the game and we were able to take the shuttle back. They also have an excellent hot breakfast buffet. The room was spacious and it was very clean and kept very well. The location of this hotel is great because it is right uptown close to the Time Warner Arena and all sorts of dining and social arenas. I would definitely stay here again.

The lounge on the second floor provides a very nice oppor-tunity for relaxing during the day, enjoying an early evening drink (free!) and break-fast in a relaxing atmosphere. The hotel has free wireless internet and in the lounge you will also find a computer for your use.

Very nice hotel, friendly staff, and great location. Again...OUTSTANDING staff.

We stayed at the London for - nights. The location was great: near Times Square, Carnegie Deli, Central Park. We did not eat at the restaurant, it looked a little intimidating and pricey. The room had an entryway, living room, big bedroom, and a huge gorgeous white marble bathroom with a double shower. Very modern and luxurious! It is in a busy spot, so it can be loud at night, but that is to be expected.

The renovated rooms are nice, with a flat screen TV, and lighted vanity mirror in the bathroom. The decor in the renovated rooms is much nicer. The hotel staff really made an effort to please. I called the front desk when my coffee maker didn't work. After a second call, and no replacement, Ella, the rep from Guest Services gave my Wife and I a complimentary breakfast buffet in their restaurant. While waiting for the replacement coffee maker, I tried to call room service for a pot of coffee. Ella really went out of her way to make sure we were happy. The hotel is very nice, and the parking is free. The room rate was competitive with other hotels in the area. There is a --Eleven, and a Japanese Steak House just across the street. Hope this review, and our pictures have helped you.

There are no ice machines on any of the floors because they are being replaced, so you need to go to the front desk and someone will get ice from the kitchen for you. The best thing about this hotel is the location. If you can put up with tiny rooms, even smaller bathrooms, and an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Executive Level Lounge"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that has certainly seen better days, than you may be able to stand a few nights here.

I asked for a map to Enterprise so my husband could go drop off the rental car, and she called Enterprise and arranged for them to pick up the car for no charge. The room was comfortable and clean. The bathroom is small, but we were only at this property for one night. Airport shuttle was easy and complimentary. Great value if you book online and prepay.

The front desk staff was very helpful in allowing me to check in very early. The free breakfast is one the best I have seen. I didn't attend the manager's reception, so I don't know about that. You can park in Circle Center for less than the valet parking.

Staff was friendly and helpful and the room was clean. Great area for restaurants and walking.

In its class, this Springhill Suites (by Marriott) may be the BEST hotel I've ever visited.
LOCATION: Centrally located for all events in and around the Ohio State campus. Along Olentangy River Rd, which has plenty of shopping and restaurants. About a -- minute drive to the airport. Free parking on-site, but NO complimentary airport shuttle.
LOBBY: You're instantly amazed at how incredibly nice, new, and modern the lobby is. Artwork, lamp fixtures, and design was clearly researched by interior decorators. Huge spacious lobby, including tall tables with outlets for laptops. Spacious breakfast area, with a hot breakfast. Also, a large inviting bar is staffed every night. On top of all that, there's a patio just outside of the bar area. The patio has a huge rectangular firepit along with a large waterfall along the back wall. Plenty of comfortable outdoor seating for our group to hang out in the evening, with the warmth of the fire, and the sounds of the waterfall. Fantastic.
ROOMS: The rooms are modern, beautifully arranged, large, and have a touch of european influcence. All suites come with a fridge and microwave. Front half of the room has a sitting area with an upscale desk unit for your laptop. There's a frosted glass wall on the back side of the deskunit, which keeps the other side of the room with the bed dark. So it's easy for someone to be sleeping while someone else is using the computer. Bathrooms have sliding doors, which take up less room than normal doors which swing open. Plus, there are TWO bathrooms: - has a walk-in shower along with a large sink. The other bathroom has the toilet with an additional smaller sink. Plenty of closet space. And the bed? Maybe the most comfortable bed I've ever slept on.
SUMMARY: Modern, new, interesting layout, lobby patio with firepit and waterall, breakfast included. Simply stunning. We all had a great time.

It's hard to review the Harrington without sounding really negative, as the only outstanding feature of the hotel is its location. The air-con was really really noisy, and thankfully it cooled down enough at night to not need to switch it on. The bathrooms needed to be redone as well, the water pressure was inconsistent and they were old enough that they never really look clean (even though they probably were).
The location was great. Walking distance to all of the popular sights so no complaints there. Metro stops were nearby, and it's close to the Verizon Center for sporting & music events.
In summary, would I stay at the hotel again? Yes, it wasn't so bad that I'd refuse to stay there. But I'd look hard for a better deal nearby. Great hotel, elegant, modern room, perfect location. Stayed at the Conrad with - other girls. We got two adjoining rooms. Last minute trip to SanFran, got this hotel via HotWire. We LOVED it! The location could not be better. We had room #--- and it was in the center of the hotel, super quiet and super cool. Me and my GF stayed here for - nights from ----- January ---- and loved every minute. We changed hotels at the beginning of January due to a worry about the hotel we had booked regarding bed-bugs. We stayed in a standard room and although it was not huge in size, it was more than adequate for our stay. The room was small and look old-fashioned,and little bit noisy but location was great,and very cheap. Staff was nice and effective.

There were a lot of positives to this hotel. First, it's - blocks from the subway in a very safe neighborhood. The room I has was very large by New York standards. I particularly like the quirky decor of the lobby, guest rooms and common areas. I think by far, the best part of this hotel is it's staff. To a person, everyone was super friendly and helpful. I felt less like I was staying in a hotel and more like I was staying in some private club. The staff just made me feel welcome. If you go to a larger midtown hotel, I promise you, that's hard to find. Before I forget, I loved the prosecco at check in -- it was a really nice touch.
That said, there were some negatives, but just a few. First, the guest room was super dark. I mean, there was no natural light. Part of that is the Financial District location, but most of that is the hotel's design. If that's important to you, don't stay here.

I honestly don't think you can be considered a - star hotel if you don't serve breakfast, but somehow, Gild Hall pulls it off. If a weekend breakfast is important to you, don't stay here. I also had a technical glitch with my TV -- something about the cable connection meant the audio wasn't quite right. It wasn't enough to complain about, but that and a few housekeeping details -- like a missing bar of soap -- made me think that the very pleasant team needed a bit of work.
Despite these hiccups, I would return, mainly because of the friendly staff, the good price and a convenient to the subway location.

I love staying at Westin's! It feels luxiourious and comfortable. It smells wonderful, and I alway sleep WELL.

When I opened the door to our room at the Loews Regency I was shocked at how big it was. We had - very nice sized closets, a dining table and comfy chair. We booked - nights in a - bedroom, - bathroom suite. We were in San Antonio to attend our son's graduation from Air Force basic training. Because we were flying in very late at night and would be leaving on a very early morning flight we chose to stay near the airport. We had our other son with us and also our graduating son's girlfriend with us, so the - bedrooms and - bathrooms plus sofabed were exactly what we needed.
The staff at this hotel could not have been nicer or more helpful. The rooms was clean and the furnishings newly updated. 
The pool was clean and inviting. The lounge chairs were comfortable with nice cushions and the tables with umbrellas came in handy to avoid the hot sun.
Breakfast was great and plentiful. 
The one and only negative was that the air conditioning seemed to be on some sort of timer and would go off during the night so we would go to sleep cold and wake up hot.But it wasn't that bad...just annoying.
Overall we felt we got way more than we expected and for a very reasonable price!

Ok....so when you call their toll-free line, you get no answer from the reservation people. Despite that, I showed up and booked a room. The first thing we noticed were the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""secure all valuables from your car"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" signs, the cameras, and the stench of urine in the hallways. Then the Strip Club that sits less than -- yards from the Hotel added to the lustre. We stayed for - hours - we checked in, went out to dinner, and decided to go elsewhere. Another thing about this hotel is that it appears to be used for housing, possibly by a social services agency or other organization. Not a great experience. If you desire space and a home-like feel, come to the Marmara! We stayed in Room -----a one bedroom suite--for two nights in early December ----. Although raining the entire time, the suite was bright and clean. There is one full bath in the bedroom and a convenient half-bath in the foyer. Shampoo, conditioner and other bath accessories were abundant. A hairdryer is stashed under the master bath sink. I was pleased with the white kitchen and all utensils-appliances one would need to cook. The coffee maker was welcome, as was the complimentary coffee and tea. The comfortable living room had a large flat-screen tv (Turkish station offered!), a desk, wi-fi, and dining area off to the side aided by a pass-through from the kitchen. The temperature is not themostatically controlled, but the manual switch is easy to use. With a lot of square footage and creature comforts, it truly felt like home. Because it's a suite hotel, it does not offer the usual hotel amenities like a restaurant or porter service. But the lobby staff are personable and helpful. The center lobby table offers guests free NY Times daily and other local magazines and guides. Stepping outside the hotel, SOMEDAY the new subway construction will offer quick rides downtown. However, the present subway stop is not far away (I took #- Lex & --th St). There are restaurants, delis, and a great drug store in the hotel vicinity and a good bakery where I ate breakfasts. A suite hotel is the perfect place to order in (especially when tired or inclement weather) and Chef Ho's delivers it's good Peking duck. The suite was very quiet, although we were there in rain with subway construction halted. I will stay here again. What the Marmara Manhattan affords is a break from the intense city frenzy--allowing one to recoup and start fresh the next day--at a very reasonable price. Value for money. Yes, I'd recommend it to a friend!

I had an extended stay at the Quality Inn, MiraMar and I can say the customer service I received was of the highest quality. The front desk staff, Rocky, (GM) Diane, Rea, Jimmy and the two young ladies were always so helpful and were there for me when I needed extra help since I am disabled. 
The rooms was quiet, clean and the beds were the most comfortable I have ever slept on. The color scheme is calming and destressing and with the nice Flat screen TV and extended cable, the combination helped with my recouperation and they even walked my dog for me when I could not do it. 
My stay included time over the holidays and they had festivities for the hotel stays and one of the workers, Jose, sang for us and has a wonderful voice. To make it more like a home away from home, Rocky decorated beautifully for the holiday with a tree.
The lobby is stocked with coffee and tea and nicely decorated. 
Rocky keeps the place running smoothly and looking great both inside and out. I never saw anything out of place and when you drive up you are greeted by beautiful flowers and a clean driveway. 
The weight room has the latest in equipment and in perfect working order. 
You can tell how a place is managed by how happy the staff is and I found everyone right down to housekeeping to be the nicest, most helpful, happy staff I have ever encountered at a motel-hotel environment. Rocky, thank you for the wonderful experience and I am referring my traveling friends to stay at this Quality Inn location.

Amanda at the front desk started my stay with exceptional customer service. She turned what could have been a terrible hotel stay into a great experience. We were too late to book rooms at the conference hotels and booked a stay at a downtown hotel that was less than acceptable. Amanda worked with me to get a room for four nights. Amanda was helpful in every way. I am so glad she was on duty that night. I must comment though that everyone we had interactions with at the hotel went out of their way to be helpful, friendly and courteous, always willing to go the extra mile for a guest. The room was truly beautiful, wonderful ammenities - check out the rain forest shower! The hotel is quite clean and the view from the spacious windows is lovely.
The food in the hotel dining room is very good. The service in the dining room is a bit spotty and sometimes there is a wait for food, drinks or checks. This would not stop me from staying at this Westin again. The total experience was amazing!

We felt the upkeep of this historical inn could be better. For example, the furniture-fixtures were run down, the carpet and drapes were stained, and the tub did not drain. Also, the bed was unchanged when we checked in.
On the upside, the hotel has a good location in Fell's Point, which has quaint shops, several coffee shops-restaurants, a nice waterfront, and a lively night scene. Also, the hotel has a free shuttle that travels to Johns Hopkins-Kennedy Krieger.
Tips: Ask for a room away from the street -- they will be quieter. Ask about the free shuttle if you need to travel to Johns Hopkins Hospital or Kennedy Krieger.

The Sheraton San Diego, met all of my wishes. Not only is the location - PRIME, but the staff is superb, making sure my every need was taken care of. I honestly did not want to return back to my home town, after such a relaxing stay,

Pleasant and helpful staff. Associated restaurant is very expensive but had excellent service. Manhattan is very expensive, so I cannot fairly judge this hotels pricing other than to note that it is less expensive than other hotels in the area we checked.
Clean, with pleasant cleaning staff and management. 
Two pieces of exercise equipment in the basement but you are unlikely to use it as this is close to tourist attractions.
Referred by staff to Eataly, an unusual Italian warehouse size with multiple restaurants and grocery stores in the same street that is excellent, and has food and deserts to carry out.
Whole Foods grocery store is walking distance away.
One negative is that the sound of doors opening and closing and voices in the hallway can be hear from within the small room, but that is to be expected in most hotels in this price range. You should be out of your room seeing the sites of NY, and not worried about sleeping late.

We booked - rooms, as we were traveling with teens, and we were pleasantly surprised at the size of the room, and its overall comfort. Having stayed at a number of midtown Manhattan hotels over the years, I know how tiny they usually are (real estate being at such a premium there). This was not a large room, by any means, but it was definitely roomy enough. Two drawbacks: elevators are teeny and slow; water temperature in our shower was extremely hot (and couldn't be turned down at all, even the cold water was too hot). Decent choice for anyone who wants to stay right in (technically, about --- ft away from) Times Square.

I stayed here recently with my partner who was on business in New York. My first impression of the room wasn't that great - they do feel a little stark and functional, but as our stay went on we really warmed to the decor and 'got' the thinking behind it. 
We had room -- which looked over the street and gave a good view of some of the skyscrapers nearby. The hotel is located literally just off Fifth Avenue giving easy access to Times Sqaure, Central Park and of course some fantastic shopping (if arriving onto Fifth by the Subway as I did then use Abercrombie and Fitch as your turning reference as the hotel is right past the side of their -th Ave store).
Despite my initial dislike of the room it has to be said that for a standard room in New York (or any city for that matter) it was a fantastic size. It was also spotlessly clean with lots of storage and a very comfy queen bed. Our bathroom had just the rainhead shower, which was the best I've ever used - spacious with great water pressure and you could be easily tempted to stay in all day.
We had room service breakfast a couple of times during the stay. The oatmeal with fruit was absolutely delicious, however the hot traditional breakfast items were just okay. The first day I ordered expresso with brekafast to stave off the jet lag and by the time it arrived it was stone cold. Simple things like butter were forgotten on another occassion, and the toast per slice was tiny, simple mistakes and downfalls but let me tell you this doesn't come cheap! By the time they've added everybody's cut on and all the different percentage charges our breakfast came to near on $-- so watch out for that. With Starbucks at the end of the street and so many other options I think it might be worth eating breakfast out.
Another disappointment for us was the hotel's dry cleaning facility. I didn't opt for the same day option for a jacket I needed to be cleaned so paid for the lesser priced overnight option - however the jacket was back within five hours. Great you might say, under promise and over deliver; the jacket however felt slightly damp (dry clean?!) smelt strongly of a fishy smell that just wouldn't budge and not only was it ironed really badly but we've snce realised that it has shrunk! All for the bargain price of $--.
All encounters with the staff were friendly, and a problem with our in-room safe was dealt with speedily. Take time to find all of your light switches before settling down for the night as they're not all controlled by the switches beside the bed which is a little frsutrating.
One final thing to watch out for - my partner asked for a cab to JFK to be organised for our last day, however when it showed up it was infact a car with a driver. Nice touch until you relaise that it's over $-- more expensive than a cab ($--!). Also as the journey was on company expenses we had to pay by card - to say that the driver was less than impressed is an undertstement as he said that the hotel had told him that it would be a cash fare.
Over all, despite the negatives I did feel relaxed and at home at the hotel. A few small issues need tidying up to make what is a good hotel now, an excellent one in the future. Would I long to return to Chambers or choose it for a break to NY? Probably not.

Stayed here for five nights, April ---May -. Absolutely fabulous, beautiful furnishings and immaculate. The rooms were large and, I understand, huge by New York standards. The service was impeccable, friendly but not pushy. They served a nice complimentary pastry-coffee breakfast in the morning. The only complaint I can come up with about the place is the surly waiter tending to the breakfast. Just one, the others were nice. I saw this guy snap at a couple of guests on different occasions. But who cares, the place was nearly flawless.

I think there may be some staff and management that may not handle complaints well, UNLESS the complaints are presented in a calm and undemanding manner. Presentation of a problem is very important. 
Yet, I do get the impression that management pays very close attention to where you purchase your room and how much you pay. And this does determines the quality of room you receive. But that is true of all hotels.

I was impressed with the way they handled my NEAR disasterous stay. turning it into a POSITIVE experience. Thank you! 
I look forward to staying at Stanford Court again, in the near future.

The only thing that I would warn about this hotel, like stated in serveral other reviews, is the A-C - Heat, It was a very hot August day and the A-C seemed to have done nothing, well it moved the air so it wasnt terrible. Breakfast was AMAZING steak and eggs were cooked perfect, French Pressed coffee. Service was so-so. Can't remember much about Check in and Check out but I think it was ok. I came back later and took advantage of no lines to ask another desk clerk a question or two about nearby attractions. He was full of suggestions and helped me with airport transportation the next day as well.

Outstanding property. Great location. Excellent service. Sincere and helpful staff. What more can I say.

Cons

We stayed for - nights and the hotel held $---- on our credit card for incidentals. We called the front desk and had this amount lowered to $---.--, but it was a struggle. 
Loud, but the city is loud in general. You can hear people in the hall, but then you hear car alarms and cars-trucks-people outside too. I think it will be loud no matter where you stay in the city. 
Overall, none of the “cons” are enough to keep us from coming back. When bidding for a room through Priceline (and paying under $---.-- per night), we realize we are not going to get the most premium room in the hotel. This hotel met my expectations and I would recommend it to others.

The whole hotel is very weird. It seems like you always owe something to the staff. I would say that half of personnel do their job worse than employees in Burger King. The position of this hotel couldn't have been better placed - we walked everywhere. The hotel staff were great and couldn't have been more helpful. We would definately use this hotel again and would highly recommend it to anyone else.

Can't say enough great things about this hotel. Love the location (only hotel that has a front entrance on Michigan Ave) and the architecture is beautiful. Love the gym on business travel and my kids love the pool on family travel. Best of all though is the people and serivce. Briscieda Medrano ALWAYS goes out of her way to make sure my stay is flawless. She is is the best Hotel Manager I have ever worked with and I travel a lot. Will (Bell man), Anthony, Malcomb, and Ursula always go out of thier way to make sure I am well taken care of. Whatever they are prescribing to in terms of customer serivce is working. My -- year old daughter and I recently took a fun mother-daughter trip to NYC. We booked a - day stay at the Chelsea Pines Inn, mostly because of the great reviews here. We had THE BEST time there! I have told everyone I know that this is the place to stay.... 
Here's why:
#-: If like us, you've never stayed in a 'small hotel' before, you'll notice an entirely different ambiance. It was so calm and relaxing to wake up here, and to return here at the end of a long day seeing the city. A completely different start and end to our days than I had ever experienced.
#-: The extras: The room was soooo much more spacious than the large hotel we stayed at in Times Square a few years ago. We stayed in the Paul Newman room, and loved the decor, bed linens, bathroom, everything. We hooked into the free wi-fi our first day to help with things in the City, and thereafter we were connected. No annoying finding the server each time, etc. Just like being at home. Did I mention it was F-R-E-E? Chelsea is a GREAT neighborhood, and there is a subway stop just --- a block away -it is an incredibly convenient location.
#-: The cleanliness...I'll admit, like things cleaner than most people worrry about, and the level of cleanliness everywhere here is incredible. This is clean the way a well-kept house is clean. The rooms, the hall, the stairs, the lobby, the breakfast area.... all fastidiously clean.
#-: The breakfast ohmygosh, blueberry tea cake, fresh fruit, a ham and cheese plate, muffins, bagels, an amazing make-your-own espresso machine.... all graciously presented on pretty dishes. A really, really terrific start to the day for us. And all included as part of the bill. 
#-: The staff -very, very special. Instead of hordes of stressed out staff bustling about, Chelsea Pines seems to runs smoothly almost invisibly. Everyone appears happy to be there, thrilled to help, and gracious way beyond the norm. Rumel is one of the most impressive young men I have met in a long time. He kept our room spotless (way beyond expectations), presented an impeccable breakfast every morning... I could go on and on. All we had to do was mention something, and he and others there jumped in as if they were our personal assistants, to help us with subway info, show tickets, etc.
#-: Charlie! ...If you like cats, look for Charlie -a wonderful, tuxedo kitty, who much to my daughter's delight, spent almost every night in our room!
We absolutely LOVED the Chelsea Pines Inn, and cannot wait to stay there again.

I just checked out of this hotel and it was not a good experience at all. Rooms are way outdated with grimy furniture and dirty carpets. The tv's were at least -- years old. My --rd floor lakeview room featured a luxurious shower - a deluge from above! A perfect weekend that could have been spent at a regular, boring, chain turned into an adventure to remember. Absolutely, stay at the W Lakeshore.

And it is still a well run and charming hotel, with a couple of glitches. The rooms (or at least my room) had no way to change the temperature. Second, I didn't see a place to get coffee and run - the only choice was Norma, which was slow and very expensive, albeit quite good. The food at the restaurant was adequate, far from being the best on Fisherman's wharf. If it wasn't for the fact that we had free breakfast included with our room, we wouldn't have eaten there past the first morning (in fact on a few occasions we chose to pay to have breakfast elsewhere rather than endure the free breakfast offered at the hotel).. My partner and I had to decide which one would have the butter and which one would have the jam as there was simply not enough for both of us. The coffee was stewed.
Would we go there again? Dear god no.
The one saving grace is the location though.

Stayed for one night. I had an interview the next day, which was just down the street from the hotel. Easy access to the interstate. Had a great night's sleep. The breakfast buffet, which was very good, had eggs, pancakes, meat, cereal, yogurt, pastries, instant oatmeal, and drinks. The usual things you would find at a Holiday Inn Express buffet.

The location was good for us, since we were visiting a grandparent in the area. The room was clean. Nice --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" tv. Renovation paid off. Pros: clean room, breakfast included, plenty of hot water, good price, gated parking, free internet. Cons: noisy hallway, not enough towels in room, bagel toaster was broken on one side, creating an inconvenience if more than one person wanted a bagel.

Just returned from the most wonderful family vacation at the JW Marriott Desert Ridge Resort & Spa!
We travelled with extended family...six adults and three younger children. 
First, the hotel is physically spectacular and immaculate. The grounds are absolutely beautiful with unbelievable landscaping and attention to detail. I cannot express how well cared for the property is. Our room (deluxe view room...standard with a nice view) was very well appointed. It was plenty large enough for two adults and a child (or two). We requested a roll-away and a refrigerator...which was worth doing. The furnishings were very high quality and the cleaning service was excellent. The bathroom was an excellent size and with equally impressive high quality materials and design.
As many write about, the pool complex with lazy river and water slide was outstanding! The Best! The water temperature was terrific and the cleanliness of the pool area and water was tops. Our kids loved their days here. The only problem we had was trying to pry them out of the water and sun before being too badly sunburnt.
Also, our kids loved the Nickolodeon Kids Activities that the hotel sponsored. We did a Nickolodeon Breakfast with Dora and Spongebob that they really enjoyed. Also, the Kids Club was fantastic. They did a pajama party one night while the adults had a great dinner...and then wanted to go back a day later for a half a day at the Kids Club...always a good sign when they want to go back.
Nickolodeon also sponsored several poolside events and arts and crafts which was terrific as well.
The restaurants and service at the hotel were all equally great. We have a wheat-gluten allergy in the family and were blown away by the excellence and awareness of the hotel and its staff. Every restaurant had a dedicated and extensive gluten free menu! This is an extreme rarity...which we really appreciated. The only other hotel that was this excellent on this front happened to also be a JW Marriott...(JW Marriott Grande Lakes Orlando). Marriott really is outstanding in this area.
Breakfast in the morning at Blue Sage was always a treat...very high quality and diverse...whether you do the buffet or off the menu.
Dinners at Tuscana (Italian and our favorite), steaks at Meritage, or pacific fusion at Roys were all excellent with great ambiance, quality food, and service to boot. You will be very happy with the offerings.
My wife enjoyed a massage at the spa and said it was beautiful, high quality, and very professional...
The front desk and concierge were also outstanding. Anything we required was handled with excellence and professionalism.
In short, if you are looking for a casual yet very high quality vacation without any snobbery...than I could not more highly reccomned the JW Marriott Desert Ridge...try it!

After much research, I chose this hotel as it was nearby to where one of our sons was living. We used it as a base of operations on either side of a road trip to the San Francisco area. Because our other son was traveling with us, we opted for the suite to begin with. We booked another suite (one floor higher) on our return to Hollywood. Then, when our son flew home before us, downsized to a smaller room. So, we got a good sampling of what they offer.
Customer service is a priority with this hotel, and everyone I dealt with . . . from initial booking, to the front desk, to the air conditioning mechanic, to the shuttle driver were all very pleasant and helpful.
Being separated from the Magic Castle Hotel, at the foot of the hill, was not a problem. Although we had our own rental car, we often used the shuttle for breakfast, or when we walked into the heart of Hollywood. The shuttle was ready when we were.
The swimming pool was a plus . . . located in a remote section of this hillside retreat, it was gated as was the entire hillside compound. Well-maintained, it provided relief from the hot temperatures.
My major gripe, was the level of building maintenance common to all rooms. Windows that didn't lock . . . same with a slider. Domestic water temperatures that were excessively hot, and were reported but not sure if they were fixed because of our short time in each room. Areas that needed caulking and painting.
Overall, we would stay here again as the viewpoint of the city from the hillside gave us a feeling of place. From our balcony, we could see the Griffith Observatory, downtown L.A., the Capitol Records building, and a good portion of Hollywood. From our third floor suite we could see half of the Hollywood sign. We were in good company, at that altitude, as we were on the same level as many of our Hollywood Hill neighbors . . .beautiful homes perched on the hillside.

Right next to the mall!!! Good shopping and easy access to the highway. The rooms are very nice more like suites with the two rooms. A bit tough to find since there really wasn't a big sign outside or on the building, so make sure you have the address. The pool is a bit small but it has a workout room. 
They will run you around within - miles so don't worry about getting to someplace close by. That was a nice touch. Don't forget to tip the van driver, it'll make him happy, plus he will look forward to taking you again in the future. 
Bathrooms are very nice and so is the ironing board. They didn't get this one from the dollar store. 
The only complaint I had, and believe me it was a small one, was the desk chair was just that a chair. It's sometimes nicer to have one of those office chairs you can adjust up and down. 
if you liked this please make sure you check it off.
Thanks

Nice rooms with a very helpful staff. The parking charge was excessive at $---day self park and $-- valet. The business center was small and expensive for internet access.

The best thing about this hotel is the location, it is a block away from the street with all the nightlife that Austin is known for. 
As far as the hotel, it is ok but a little worn around the edges. Rooms are of average size with a decor that was dark and what I guess is best described as western. Room service food was pretty good. Staff was very friendly and helpful. I would stay here again when in Austin.

I stayed at the Sofitel in Philadelphia with my wife and toddler for several nights. I could not have been more excited about staying at this hotel based on the reviews on this site. While this was a nice hotel, it was certainly not amazing. It is currently #- of all hotels in Philadelphia on this website, and my experience at this hotel did not reflect such a high rating. There were too many little annoyances and problems, that admittedly were minor, but when you think of the #- hotel in a large city with so many lodging establishments, you expect a flawless experience, and this was NO Ritz-Carlton-Four Seasons-W. Starting with check-in, the hotel occupies a very small footprint on a small city block in Philadelphia. While the location is very central, the amount of drive-up space is miniscule. Once you get more than two people driving up to check-in, chaos ensues and the street is backed up. Upon checking into my room, it was clear that I was given a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lemon"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room (and I wonder if all hotels have them?). It's just cosmetic blemishes, but it made a bad first impression, and after the delayed check-in due to the choked entryway, I was too tired to change rooms. There was free coffee in the lobby every morning, but for some reason, if you wanted decaf, the waiter had to go on a mission to Timbuktu in the back of the kitchen (some waiters told me point blank decaf was not offered at the hotel), and eventually we found it easier to go down the street and pay for it at a coffee shop. There was a free computer station in the lobby, but when I was staying there the printer was broken, and I suppose I could have the concierge print my documents for me, but I could never find him-her when they were needed. The bed was comfortable and my wife was impressed with the quality of the bed linens and bath products. You certainly wont go wrong staying at this hotel, it has some nice features and a great location- I just felt that it was a long way from """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""#- hotel in Philadelphia"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and while most of the contributors appear to have had an amazing stay, there were some inconvenient quirks associated with mine.

I cannot rate this hotel highly enough absolutely one of the best Hilton Chains we have stayed in from the apartment which we could not fault, to the location Friendship Heights is a very upmarket area with lots of designer shops, to the shopping centre this hotel sits atop of with some great places to shop & dine loved The Cheesecake Factory can't understand why some people do not like this place our meals were fantastic & the service excellent, there is a Coffee shop, Subway, Maccas, Pharmacy & other specialy shops to the Metro below no walking out in the cold, wind rain etc & only --mins x very fast train to Union Stn $-.--ea one way .Breakfast was all you could want for the start of a day & the managers reception freebies is worth while & who could complain as it is FREE. Just returned from a - night stay at the Cosmopolitan. For our first visit to NY it turned out to be an excellent choice. Try breakfast in the Soda Shop next door (to the left) and an afternoon coffee & cake in the Cosmopolitan Cafe next door (to the right). We will return!!

We stayed at the Sheraton from August --th through the --th, and while we didn’t have a terrible stay we didn’t find a lot to recommend the place, either. Here are our pros and cons.
Pros: As many have mentioned, great location, central to just about everything one would want to do in downtown Chicago. Great views, too – if you get a room facing the river and lake. We got to lie in bed on Saturday night and watch the fireworks at Navy Pier. And the river traffic below was always interesting. The riverwalk is a nice touch (especially if you remember “old” Chicago) and provided a pleasant escape from the crowds on Michigan Avenue above. And, despite the cons listed below, we had a quite nicely appointed room.
Cons: As another reviewer has mentioned, the common areas of the hotel were freezing cold. Much too cold to sit and relax in the lobby-bar. But who would want to anyway, what with the music blaring full blast -- hours a day? If we weren’t looking around for a sweater (despite the heat in the street) we were shouting at each other to be heard over drinks. It was also way too cold in the club level lounge where we feared our morning coffee would ice over if we lingered too long. Note to management: It’s a hotel, not a meat locker.
As was also mentioned previously, making the bed is an apparently lost art at the Sheraton. The sheets were simply draped over the mattress and I woke with my feet twisted up in them on more than one occasion. That one I just plain old won’t ever understand. 
Again, as already mentioned, there were long lines everywhere – from the front desk to the concierge to the bar – just about every time we walked through the lobby. That should really be forgiven, though. It was the height of summer vacation after all. But the savvy traveler will recognize that as one indication of a big, crowded, and somewhat noisy hotel.
Finally, front desk staff botched our move from a lower level room to the club level, leaving our luggage unattended all day, and leaving us in our new room to wait for it when we got back from our day’s business. And then they left it to a beleaguered bellman to apologize for the mix-up.
I imagine staying at the Sheraton might be an altogether different , and much more pleasant, experience in the off season. Perhaps in winter – they’re likely to have turned off the AC by then…

I got a very reasonable rate directly from the hotel's website and a simple upgrade request at the front-desk at check in scored us a room with a fun view and little balcony. The hotel is elegantly appointed and has true historic charm. There is a nightly manager's reception with wine and a lovely dining room with full lengths mirrors and a cozy fireplace by which you can enjoy what appeared to be an outstanding menu. (We didn't eat at the hotel, but wouldn't hesitate to do so on a future visit.) All hotel staff were extremely friendly, gracious, and helpful. Our room was small, but nicely appointed with antiques and tapestries. The bed had a nice down comforter, but was, unfortunately, a bit hard for our tastes. The vanity sink """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""gurgled"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" at us once in a while, but that added to the older charm of the hotel. Formerly two private residences eventually combined to provide affordable rooms for soldiers, the hotel has a rich history that's worth reading. There's a tiny business center and workout space downstairs. The front steps are a bit steep, so watch your footing, but definately give this place a try next time your're in DC.

I was on a business trip with some colleagues, and we selected this place because it was walking distance from our conference location. It was very different (to say the least) from our normal experiences with business hotels, and I checked it out on Tripadvisor afterwards out of sheer curiosity. I was quite amused to see the wide variation in feedback, and figured it might help to put out a balanced review. 
So here are the various things that stand out:
- History: It was a temporary City Hall a century ago, and the structure- decor has its own charm (I don't think it has changed much since then). I liked the elevators with external mirrors. Fine if you are there for a day, but for a longer stay amenities may matter more than looks.
- Location: depending on the reviews, this is either great or terrible and for fairly obvious reasons. Great because of its proximity to the city centre. Terrible becuase it lies on a stretch of road that has a high concentration of homeless people. Personally, I felt the homeless were quite polite when they did intrude to ask a passerby for coffee, cigarette or a handout, and did not have a nuisance value. I could see they made some people nervous, though. I didn't feel the street was unsafe when it was dark. 
- The bathroom: Aaaarghhhh!!! I come from a city known for small bathrooms, but this was crazy! The shower cubicle was approx -ftx-.-ft with cold marble walls that you can't avoid touching while having a hot shower. And I am fairly sure my butt was never really made it into the bathroom when I used the wash basin.
- Amenities: It has one restaurant, and an attached Starbucks. Period.
- Restaurant: had some pretty good food here, so no complaints. Limited menu, though.
- Rooms: room size is ok, but lighting is dim and the TV and AC are probably antiques
- Staff: friendly, courteous, helpful.
- Price: we had a company negotiated rate for the conference, so wouldn't be fair to comment. I think all hotels in the area were overpriced during that period.
In sum: fine for a one-day stay, when the quaintness and the history make up for other shortcomings. Beyond that, it may be tough to take. Avoidable for business travelers.

The hotel was taken over by Hyatt last year (was Swisshotel) and an extensive renovation will begin in the fall (according to front desk staff). I got my room at a very low rate from Priceline, but wouldn't have been upset even if I had paid more. My room was fairly spacious, had a decent view (--th floor facing toward Boston Common), had an easy chair in addition to desk-chair area, and a bathrobe. The furniture is a little worn, but still fine, and the beds are very comfortable (thick down overlay on top of mattress that feels great to sink into, in addition to comforter on top, and triple-sheeted with quality linens). Front desk person said that all formerly twin-bedded rooms have been replaced with - doubles--which takes care of the complaints by some other reviewers. The hallway areas are attractive with large windows at each end. Lobby is fine (on third floor, which in a large city is a safer arrangement--fewer non-guests wandering in from the street). Construction of hotel is solid--not much hallway noise or noise between rooms. Location is only a few blocks from shopping, Boston Common, South Station, Chinatown--but bear in mind that no location in Boston is near everywhere you'll want to go. I had a very pleasant stay, and when Hyatt renovates, the hotel should be even better. In the meantime, if you get a good rate at this hotel, it's a very good value. There are some dreadful (and tiny) rooms in Boston at very high rates, but mine at the Hyatt was, thankfully, not one of them.

We just came back from a girl's weekend in New York and were SO pleased with The Pearl. The amenities are outstanding (continental breakfast, wine hour, free wi-fi) and the staff was helpful and friendly. In addition, the location was great and close to many nice restaurants.

Otherwise, combination of rude & unhelpful reception staff and unacceptable cleaning standards plus lack of basics like a fridge in room (we stayed for a week and requested fridge several times) or ice maker in lobby (it was broken), coffee in room (never replenished) mean that I could not recommend anyone to stay here.
