The hotel does have a free shuttle to take you back and forth to the convention center if you like.
Near the property: The hotel is in a fairly under-developed area of downtown Phoenix. Current maps of Phoenix show the hotel as being immediately adjacent to I--- but those are misleading as the highway is underground in this part of the city (this meant there was less traffic noise and pollution than I expected). The hotel has a restaurant on the property (the Capital Grille) and there is a Fair-Trade coffee shop and Portland's Restaurant in the building next to the hotel. About - blocks further north is Cheuvront's Wine Bar. I ate at all three of these places during my time at the hotel and was happy with all three of them (note these restaurants are more fancy 'wine bar' types of places than family friendly chain restaurants). 
My stay: I was given a room on the -rd floor (I think it was ---)with - double beds and work area-desk. I thought the room was fairly spacious (ex it could have fit a rollaway bed into the work area without too much trouble). The housekeeping was fine, the cable tv worked, the bathroom was clean. The towels were thin and worn. My biggest issue with the room is that the air conditioning didn't work. No matter what temp I set the ac to, or how high I turned the fan, it blew warm air. I went down to the front desk to ask about it and was told that 'we haven't switched over the a-c yet'....this had a major impact on my comfort level during my stay. Fortunately the room has a window that you can open to allow for some air circulation otherwise I would not have been able to sleep comfortably. 
This room had a view over the outdoors pool. I did not use the pool or the exercise room so I cannot comment on these facilities.
The hotel offers a complimentary breakfast each morning, served in the Capital Grille Restaurant. This consists of a selection of cold cereals and instant oatmeal, fruit, some pastries and 'make your own waffles', along with the standard tea and coffee. 
This hotel also offers free wireless. This worked just fine for me, acceptable speeds and no problems with signal strength.
Overall it was an acceptable hotel for - nights but I wouldn't recommend it unless you need to stay there (for example the hotels near the convention center are full). It think it was a bit overpriced (my corporate rate was ~$----night) and for that I would expect a better variety of foods at breakfast, better towels and working ac.
Also, the hotel was full when I stayed and I noticed the front desk staff seemed a bit inexperienced. They were having problems with doubly occupied rooms (giving out room keys to new guests who were finding the rooms already occupied). They were also unsure how to handle my enquiries about the ac. They weren't rude, just a bit unsure of what to say.
So in summary a two-three star hotel, definately not four.
Great one night the thing we got to leave our car at the hotel for two week for free!

We booked a night at the Silver Cloud Inn because they offered a free shuttle after our cruise arrived back in Seattle. It was a bonus to learn the shuttle was available for other destinations as well. Hotel staff recommended that our grandchildren -- ages -, - & --, would enjoy the Pacific Science Center rather than the Children's Museum and they were right! The shuttle brought us to the Science Center and then picked us up. We were able to walk to Duke's Chowder House for a delicious dinner and enjoyed a very nice hot and cold Continental breakfast the next morning. The room was very comfortable and it was a pleasure to have two sinks in separate areas. After a week of cruising without access to a computer, it was also nice to find their business center offered internet access and free printing. The Lake Union area is beautiful!

We stayed for one night on our way from Madera Canyon Az. to San Antonio and then for - nights on our way from San Antonio to Santa Fe. We selected this motel because of it's proximity to the freeway and indeed, access was quite easy. While not impressed with the general layout (kind of reminded me of a maze) the rooms themselves were very clean and quite adequate , the beds were quite comfortable and at no time did we feel insecure (we never leave valuables in the car). Freeway noise was not a problem (the dog barking next door could have been but was not) and we had no problem keeping the drapes closed. As mentioned in other reviews, we found a problem with the shower taps but this was quickly resolved. Access to a bar was greatly appreciated after a long drive and there are some great restaurants on the other side of the freeway (Barrigas on Sunland Park Drive is one). I have to agree with other reviewers that having internet access in the bar area is rather distracting. We did appreciate the Managers Happy Hour Thursday evening. The staff, from Liz on were fantastic. The only negative comment I can make is about the grounds. Someone needs to walk around once in a while and make sure that the odd bits of garbage are picked up.

The room was great and the bed was very comfortable. Nearby were great restaurants, stores, and only a ---- minutes drive to downtown SA. 
Also, a great view of the hill country and an average fitness room.
The only negative comment would have to be the pillows. The pillows were very small, lumpy, and uncomfortable with no support.
This property is in the perfect location for a Chicago getaway. Close to shopping, dining, and the waterfront. Nicely appointed rooms and professional staff.

I know the staff tries hard here, but this is clearly a Hampton Inn that is missing on a couple marks. Don't get me wrong, the price is cheap, so you don't expect a lot - but I expected a little bit more. The room is clean, and the bed is 'okay' at best (it's hard as a rock). There are no amenities here - a small gym, and no on-site restaurant. The breakfast that Hampton is so proud of was poor at best. Old eggs, and dry Canadian bacon - does not a hot breakfast make.

I have stayed at this hotel several times with work and every time i stay here i make a mental note to myself never to stay here again!
The rooms are tiny, particulary the en-suite where your knees are pressed up against the door when you sit on the toilet. Although the rooms have had a slight make over recently, they are still below standard for the min nightly rate of $--- per night, with old faded carpets, dripping taps, tempremental air conditioning....
The hotel itself is extremely noisy, main culprits being the traffic outside which cant be helped in central Manhattan but aside from the outside noise the house keeping staff are incredibly noisy, slamming doors, bashiong servicing trollies up aginst the walls, and talking to each other from oppostie ends of the hallway, ---- times ive stayed here ive had to ask the house keeping staff to keep the noise down as they seem to work through the night here.The walls in the rooms are also very thin so if youre not being kept awake by the outside noise or the house keeping staff then chances are you'll probably be kept up by your neighbours TV.
The hotel bar is very dark and dingy and doesnt stay open very late so if you arrive into NY on a late flight and fancy a drink when you get to the hotel chances are you wont get one from the hotel bar, wine list is mediocre as is the food and very much over priced.

From start to finish just friendly and helpful..to the front desk people to the shuttle driver...I will always stay here when I need to be close to the airport.the free breakfast was even better than expected..

Centrally located and right at a metro station makes this a handy downtown hotel. The staff was extremely helpful and attended at once to one small defect in our room at check in. Everything about our two night stay was perfect. The hotel also has several breakfast place options so no need to spend a lot on breakfast. Alternate breakfast and snack options in the hotel provided healthy and reasonable choices.

the location of this hotel is the best part of it the rooms are very small,dated and very very poor
even we stayed there for - nights they gave us a noisy room (because of the aircondition outside units) the breakfast restaurant menu is worthless the price

The overall hotel is modern with a cool vibe. The rooms are clean and have Bliss spa products. The gym is small but well appointed with the newer fitness machines.
Room service was very prompt, but overall food quality was adequate. Oatmeal for breakfast touted sour cherries, but was served with marachino ones. Roasted tomatoes were barely touched by oven heat, and the sausages were sliced in half and dried out. For the price of the menu items, the chefs in the kitchen need to step-it-up.
If you're looking to be near the Gaslamp district...look for a closer hotel, this one's a mile walk away.

I booked the Excelsior Hotel as part of a New York Christmas trip for my two sons and their fiancees, my husband and myself. I wanted a place to stay that would give us privacy and a common room to visit. The two bedroom suite that I booked was great. We had one bedroom with a bath for my husband and me and another bedroom with two queen sized beds and a bath for the boys and girls. The couch in the sitting room also made out into a queen size bed but we did not need it. The layout was similar to a small apartment and gave us plenty of room. 
The location of the hotel is great. It is very residential and such a relaxing place after a busy day of sightseeing. There is a subway station about a half a block away and another two blocks down on --th street. We traveled all over Manhattan as well as the Bronx, Harlem, and Brooklyn and had no trouble at all because of the location of the subway routes. There are many deli's, coffee shops, and small restaurants within two or three blocks that are very reasonably priced. 
The staff of the hotel was very helpful when we needed them. The front desk staff was not overly friendly but they were attentive to any need that we had. The doorman and the other guys were extremely helpful with luggage storage on our last day and with booking a car and calling a cab to get us all to the airport. 
Central Park is less than a block away and the East Side is a very comfortable walk across Central Park. The Museum of Natural History is right across the street 
On our last trip we stayed in Midtown and it was not a bad experience but I really love the upper West Side and would stay at the Excelsior again.

This is a great hotel if you are going to be in the downtown area and don't mind walking a bit. You can always take a cab, but Chicago is a great walking city if you are able to do so. The hotel is also in walking distance to Michigan Ave. shopping and restaurants. The Red Line is a couple of blocks away which makes it ideal to ride the train up to Lincoln Park and Wrigleyville. The room was quite nice and spacious. Upon moving to Chicago from Texas, I stayed in this particular hotel for a week before moving into an apartment. The hotel staff were very helpful in giving me directions and suggestions. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Chicago. The rooms are much bigger than most hotels in the area, and the price is pretty reasonable. Further, free breakfast and happy hour are great bonuses.

The owners were nice enough, but this motel is a dump. They advertise the rooms as being newly renovated. All they did was paint the walls. The bathroom was not cleaned! There was soap scum and dirt in the bathtub and the toilet has urine stains on the base of it. Not worth the cheap rate! Spend a few bucks more at another motel or hotel.
stayed at chandler inn for one night only. the rooms were very very small and it is an old hotel. the staff however was very nice and helpful ,especially Zach!!

After several nights of combing the internet for reasonalbe hotels in Manhattan I decided to book CQ again. I have stayed there twice in the past - years. My sister and I had the most wonderful time. The room may have been small but very adequate for - people. The rooms were better than I remember them, they may have renovated. The bed was the best I have ever slept in and the linen felt like Egyptian cotton. CQ is convenient to all theaters and subway stations. We felt safe walking from the theater to the hotel even past midnight. Front desk staff was friendly and informative. The housekeeping lady was specially nice it felt like my mom was taking care of us during our stay. I definitely recommend this hotel and they deserve an excellent mark.

Check in was the best part of the experience. Motel was in the skid road area of Point Loma. Lots of Homeless. Place has made an attempt to keep clean but the pics lie about the pool. Pool area is somewhat run down and not the best for looks. Our room heater did not work at all so we had to request a blanket for the bed which was ratty and torn in two places. Water pressure in the room was real low. Promised room coffee was nonexistent. When we checked out I had to wait and be insulted for -- minutes while cleaning staff checked our room for damage and missing items. When I voiced the opinion of being insulted by this treatment I was shouted down by the Asst. General manager that this was policy. I def. won't be back and will pay a bit more next time for a better Motel

When we arrived at -pm, they found a room ready for us. Fred was very friendly and super helpful. We found out that there was a bus stop ---m up the road an cost $- to get to Santa Monica Pier. Bus arrives quite frequently and easy to catch, takes about -----minutes to reach the -rd street promanade.
The room was nice with an extra seating area, which is nice when you have a child. That means no fighting over the TV as there were -. Bathroom was very small but adaquate for what was needed as the rest of the room was large. Nice thing was when you did laundry you got the key so no-one else could get to your clothes. Pool was nice but fencing could do with up dating. The only down side was that the aircon smelt a bit but we left our windows open while out to get fresh air.
Fred and Denise were very nice and letting us check-out at -pm as our flight was not until midnight so it gave us time to shop and then freshen up before going to the airport.
Would stay again if I am in LA.

This motel does not deserve the - star rating it displays. Although the carpet, wallpaper and mattresses were obviously replaced since the last reviewer in ----, the place was just shabby. The sheets did not fit the mattress and kept slipping off all night, the pillows needed to be replaced. The commode was cracked and the vanity had peeling paint. 
There was an ashtray and burn marks on the bedspead even though the room was labeled as non-smoking. We were asked if we wanted the phone """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""turned on"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". And the office was not open after midnight...in fact, we had to ring the doorbell to check out at -:--am. Bypass this one!

I've stayed here in the past and was extremely satisfied with the value, location and amenities. This time we stayed in their basic suite which was anything but basic. The beds were very comfortable pillow top mattresses with premium bedding (feather duvets, triple sheeting). Needless to say, I had a very good sleep! Bathroom was quite large and totally gutted and re-done. The shower head was amazing and the pressure very good. They one of those two headed showers which cover your entire body. There were three of us and even though we stayed only one night, we actually had probably - or three showers each just because it was that good! Service was excellent too. I initially called their main call centre and received excellent guest service, but since I work in the industry I thought I would call the hotel directly. I managed to speak to a young lady at the front desk and she was very pleasant and gave us a great rate. The lady at check-in was nice too and she called us a cab later that night to take us out on the town. She actually called - or - companies because the initial one was taking too long so we were really impressed with her going out of her way to help us out. The room itself was nicely decorated. Big Flat screen tv and included HBO- movie channels it was great! Also fridge and microwave as well as popcorn for the late night craving. Breakfast was HUGE and included. I was very surprised but the large selection which we didn't have a chance to see last time! They gave us a late check-out and let us park our car for a bit later while we walked around. Location wise was ideal. Only -- minute walk to city centre. Can see the space needle as well which seemed pretty close too. Parking and internet were also included. Love not being nickel and dimed. I don't know what the previous reviewers problems were, but this hotel is very nice and the service exceptional. I've stayed in many - to - star hotels, and this one is definitely top of my list. There is no question, we will be back and looking forward to it!

We stayed for - nights, mid-week and it was a great choice for our family of - adults and - pre-teens. Room was clean, - queens, --th floor, quite (no traffic noise as some reported), hallway was bit warm but room very cool and comfy, ice machine at end of hall was more noisey than most but we couldn't hear it in our room - doors down, beds and pillows very comfortable, chair w- ottoman, desk with ergo chair. No wireless in room but free in lobby. I used the -nd floor cafe area which is closed for food service at night but is much quieter than the active lobby. The bellman was extremely nice and helpful. The front desk was ok but forgot to give us our breakfast coupons at checkin. This was quickly fixed the next morning. Breakfast was quite tasty and enjoyed by everyone. Great tasting fresh fruit , assorted pastries, hot eggs, bacon, sausage, potatoes, quiche, make-your-own hot waffles, plenty of beverage choices, and more. Septa station entrance directly next to hotel. On the express line to all stadiums (we did a Phillies game). Easy to walk to many sites. Took a taxi from historical area for $-. Phlash for whole family just $-- for day. Franklin Institute is a must for children. Parking $--. Pool small but clean, great exercise equip, free raquetball. Would stay again.

The Dupont at the Circle worked out great for me. It was close to the business I had to do. The room was comfortable, free internet, nice bar down stairs.
The bathroom was clean and quite stylish, European feel. It had a great walking in stone shower but no bath tub.
My only regret is that I was there alone. I would have been a lot more fun if my wife had been able to join me.

I will start off by saying that I am a Hilton Honors Diamond Member and have stayed at other Conrads and so I review this Conrad from that perspective. 
The Conrad in Chicago used to be a Le Meridian and they have changed nothing from those days it seems. They are in the process of remodeling but at present it is still the same.
The rooms, bits and pieces are a bit tired, the shower had a couple of cracked tiles and seemed quite frankly a bit dirty. 
The service is OK, the concierge is the best part of the hotels service, quick attentive, knowledgeable. 
Many of these small things you would forgive if it were just a Hilton, but not a Conrad and the prices they charge. The staff at this hotel need to go and spend a few days at the Singapore Conrad and learn how a Conrad should be run. Until then it is a tarted up Hilton.

Let's begin to say that San Francisco is a very, very expensive city when it comes to hotel rooms.....So whatever I paid for this hotel room, was a true bargain considering the crazy hotel prices in this city. The place looks nicer outside than it does inside. It has a very small lobby, and a true Youth Hostel feeling to it. It has no areas to sit around to socialize with other travelers, except an adjacent Bar that it seemed to be very popular in the evenings with the locals. It appeared that the Front Desk is run by friendly, but alas non professional desk clerks as far as local knowledge is considered. My room was pretty gloomy with a very small bathroom which had a tub-shower combination, with good water pressure. The room did have a small fridge and a microwave. The best thing about the room was the very strong WIFI signal provided free of charge. However, if you need to print anything from the Lobby's computer, you are out of luck because there is no printer connected to the Customer's computer. Also, the hotel is not rally centrally located, and it took me -- fast walking minutes to get from the hotel room to the center of Market Street were the Cable Cars turn around is located. So if you do not like to walk or it would be too tiring for you....Then this would not be a good location for you. The area is a little on the seedy side but felt not danger of any kind.....It is full of bars and small restaurants and as I menitoned, quite a walk from the touristy points of interest.

Hotel worthy of its - star rating. Good staff, clean rooms, nice furnishing, comfortable bed, comfy bath robes, and good temperature control. Close to lots of restaurants, Movie Theater, and even ice skating next door. One drawback was the $-- valet parking but that was taken care of by parking a block away in a city parking lot. The other was that annoying thing some upper end hotels like to do which is to charge you for internet connection. That was taken care of by the staff to sign me up for the frequent guest program – the Presidents Club which made it no cost. Over all a great stay and would definitely stay here again especially for low price I got on Hotwire.

Hotel was nice. Staff was fantastic. Great location - close to Union Station and the hotel is on the double decker bus tour route. My bathroom was very small and there was only a small glass shelf above sink to put toiletries which was really annoying. We had a double room and beds were doubles - not queen. We booked through hotwire, so I think we got one of their lesser rooms. Overall though, not bad.

Staffs were warm and welcome us as soon as we arrived. We were recommended a city tour which we should had taken. Room is big, clean and comfortable. The bed side even has a reading light. Extended desk provides lots of desktop as mentioned on their web site. We were lucky that we have a quiet room away from the street and facing the pool. Closet (with sliding doors) may be a bit small for - of us in a double bed room. Supplies were adequate, got refilled each day when the room was cleaned. 
We had a room service that arrived half hour after we ordered and the food was good.
Location is excellent, just walk to Hollywood blvd where actions and attractions are. Metro stop is just there for going to Universal Studio (only one stop). Easy access to downtown by metro. The traffic on the street was terrible and that is the same everywhere in LA. I don't recommend driving in LA. The metro is fast and easy and not expansive.

The Chandler Inn has been our place to stay in Boston for as long as -- years now! It has allways been very pleasant and service was excellent but now they have redone all the rooms and it is magnificent. The best value you can get in Boston. It has no restaurant but you can get a discount for the small and cute bakery just around the corner if you ask at the reception.

In October, we went to San Francisco for a couple's weekend and stayed at the Hotel Monaco.
As soon as we entered the lobby, we could tell this was a unique place, with some art Noveau elements and great ambiance, without being stuffy. 
The staff was very friendly and informed us we should come back downstairs for the daily free wine tasting the hotel has every evening. What a treat! Guests would gather on an other room with comfortable seating and have their choice of white or red wine. 
They were willing to help us in anything we needed, offering to book shows for us, giving us the detailed maps of Chinatown with restaurant suggestions, and so on. 
The location is great, right in the theater district, about three blocks away from the Central Station (where you can catch the double decker tour buses that take you by every major attraction in the city) and couple more to Chinatown. It is near several cool art galleries for art lovers delight, selling original Miró, Chagall and Picasso lithographs, even some selling Doctor Seuss' works. It also has a lot of bars and pubs nearby that seem to attract a lot of theater goers before-after plays, besides people that come into the neighborhood for that purpose. 
For our meals, we could either go to the hotel's French restaurant, in the same beautiful style and ambiance, or find great options nearby. 
There are a lot of breakfast restaurants, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""diner style"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to choose from nearby, if you prefer not to eat at the hotel. 
The rooms are good and the toiletries provided for guests were high quality. Notice the funky zebra robes for the guests use hanging in the closets, a nice change from the white ones usually offered at other places, but totally fitting this hotel experience. 
The hotel also has a gym and spa, but we were too busy exploring the city and had short time there, however if we go back to San Fran we would gladly come back to the same hotel and maybe then check the spa out.
Highly recommended for couples and people that want something unique and tasteful combined with comfort and good service.

This hotel has everything!
Location cannot be beaten,friendly staff,gorgeous rooms and views, delicious breakfast and a comfortable lobby.Definitely the best choice for a New York vacation!

Shared a special night there with a lot of my great friends, and we stayed in a terrace suite....It was amazing. Every detail was perfect....from the friendly valet parking staff to the lush amenities in the room. I loved being within walking distance of the fun of downtown Ft. Worth. I am getting married on July --th, and my fiancee' and I are staying here on our honeymoon night....nothing but the best for such a special night! Thank you!

Stayed her for - night (- and - september '--) and had a room on the --th floor on the 'backside' of the building but that was no problem; still had great views! Checkin was very swift and friendly staff explained everything very good. 
Room was very good, lots of space, a superb bed and nice cosy relaxchair to view the tv when coming back late in my room. The mag mile with shops is closeby as are several other interesting things (navy pear, millenium park, arts museum) and letts be honest these kind of cities you need to walk trough it to enjoy even more. Subway (El, red and blue line) you need to walk a bit for but overall that wasn't a problem for me...
Bathroom in my room was very spacious with a seperate bath and shower. It was spot on clean!
Had a very good stay here; even more so if the room only cost me -- dollars a night (got it trough booking.com).

I live and work very close to this hotel and have stayed there on and off due to some work on our home, and found it to be a cool, comfortable hotel. The decor is pretty nice, arty but tasteful. The location is good, especially if you have business-friends in Lincoln Park or want to go to Wrigley. Really convenient to get to the Mag Mile by bus right in front of hotel, but still not ideal location for a shopping trip or somebody who needs to be downtown for business. It's a new hotel, so some kinks are still being worked out: some trouble with the phones; one room we tried had a partially broken headboard on the bed; and the rooftop bar is still under construction, but overall things went very smoothly for a hotel that's only been open for a few weeks. Other downsides: room A-C were window units, not a thermostat, and the elevators are super slow and creaky. Upsides: very comfortable bed; we had drinks at the restaurant downstairs and it has a great atmosphere and delicious drinks (and the food looked awesome); staff was very young but extra friendly and helpful; very stylish. If you're looking for a quieter, only slightly off-the-beaten-path alternative to the Mag Mile hotels, this is a great choice.

This was our first stay in a New York City hotel. The location was just what we needed, away from the Time Square crowd, yet close enough to things when walking, taking the subway, etc. The room was large by NY standards (I had been in town on business), the decor was fun, the staff attentive. The lobby was great with breakfast in the morning, all-hours espresso machine, wine-cheese-piano in the late afternoon. We had an issue with a too-soft bed that was resolved quickly. The only negatives were the spotty internet availability and that the staff could have been a bit more knowledgable about simple issues like the subway, tourist attractions, etc. Since it was too small to have a concierge, the people at the desk should have known a bit more. We would definitely stay there the next time.

The Blackwell hotel is great. The amenities are wonderful. There is a Keurig coffee maker in the room which is very nice. The beds are very comfortable and the room is very clean. The desk area is more than adequate if you're spending a lot of time working on a laptop like I was. They provide free shuttle service to and from the airport. Little or no noise can be heard from the neighboring rooms.
The rooms were very clean, beautifully appointed, and amazingly quiet. The daily breakfast and afternoon teas were very nicely done, and the service was first rate.

I am frequently in Washington DC for business and occasionally for pleasure and I always return to the Hotel George. The service is unmatched, the location is convenient to the Capitol, Union Station, and multiple government offices. An added bonus -- the restaurant is excellent.

i've been coming to austin for -- years . i have seen many changes.I can alway find crestwood suites. and it is in a good location to get to the places I need to go.This place is priced right for these hard times.every time I stay under the new managment it seem to be getting better.there is always room for improvement in any place I stay. Glade that they r still here.

Stayed here one night. We had a great room, great service and paid a great price through priceline. Bed was comfortable but was queen size and only bed in room. Make sure you ask for king bed if that is what you are used to. Had great service at check-in. Quick and friendly valet(expensive $--) but had received such a great rate that we could not complain. Chatted with various staff (while riding elevator) asking us if we were enjoying ourselves and San Diego. All were friendly and professional. Pool small but lounge beds wonderful (if you can snag one). Would highly recommend. Decor is contemporary, art deco and tasteful.

Arrival experience: Arrived around -:-- p.m. Efficient check-in. 
Room (general): Spacious room with many architectural details such as excellent crown molding and trim, nice tucked away mini-bar, and more. The quality of materials in the room exceeds your typical Marriott room. Large LG flat screen TV, good carpets, good drapes, fixtures, etc. all of nice quality. Great - cup coffee maker.
Bathroom: Good size, nice granite counters, huge Jacuzzi tub, huge shower with the best water pressure I have ever experienced. Tub and shower were clean, but Jacuzzi was very hard to activate; a maintenance man showed us how to turn it on by repeatedly using shallow pushes to the start button. Also, several jets came off while using the tub. It’s a nice feature but was not maintained. 
Bed: Very good bed. 
Houskeeping: Average. We left a tip requested extra bath towels. Housekeeping took the tip but did not leave towels. 
Restaurants: We cannot recommend the hotel restaurant. We had the full breakfast buffet on Thanksgiving morning. Both the food and staff were sub-par. The buffet was not restocked, and we had to scavenge the dregs of what remained. Several core items were out of stock on the buffet including jam and fruit. The bacon was swimming in grease. We finally asked the staff to bring us fruit, and they did. However, the staff’s attitude was lackadaisical at best. We even had to get up to get our own water after waiting an extended period of time. This was probably our worst dining experience at any Marriott owned hotel. 
Bar: The bar in the lobby looked very nice, but we did not patronize it. 
Grounds: This is a downtown hotel. So there are no real “grounds.” Great gym in the basement. 
Pool: we didn’t see one
Staff attitude-service: The front desk was good, but the restaurant staff was bad. 
Perks for status: Platinum gift-points offered at check-in. Upgraded room also provided. 
Parking: Valet only. The valets were very efficient and helpful. 
Misc: This is a quaint, historic hotel. We loved the lobby. And the valets were very knowledgeable about downtown and restaurants. Use caution at night downtown. There are many bums in this part of downtown. I worked nearby at Pennzoil Place (about - blocks away) in the late --s, and never noticed bums during the day. But they are everywhere at night, even urinating in public. Although the Houston Police Department is also downtown, we saw no police patrolling this part of downtown at night. 
Photos are of room ----.

It was so nice to walk - minutes to the check-in counter from our room. From the lower level of the hotel you can walk through a hall and right over to the airport and take the elevator up to the ticket counter in terminal - for Delta airlines. For another terminal just take the O’Hare monorail. This hotel is great for an early morning flight.
The room was a little tight for a family of -, but clean, and comfortable with nice beds and pillows. Windows were very sound-proof. I never heard anything from the airport! If you’re a light sleeper you might hear noise from the hallway, but I only heard one group with a fussy child, most other guests were politely quiet. 
Our kids had fun in the pool. We enjoyed our fish & chips in the restaurant.
No complaints. I will stay here again when flying out early in the morning.
We got a very good rate by booking early.

Shuttle bus was super- driver was very courteous and helpful- staff were great throughout check in, porters, bar staff etc. We had an excellent sleep- then powerful shower- very pleased overall- thank you Radisson LAX!

All right, Let's get this out of the way up front. Like most moderately priced hotels in San Francisco, the Handlery is an old property. In one or two places, the carpet looks a little bit shabby. However, in all the ways that count, this is a nice comfortable, full-service hotel that may be one of the best values in this very expensive city. 
Accommodations
On my latest trip, I had room ---, spacious and nicely furnished. It was larger than the room I had last year, perhaps because I mentioned that I had reviewed them for Tripadvisor. On the other hand, the bath was not quite as spacious. There was a desk with lamps, desk-top plugs, and a great chair, In addition to the desk, there was a large dining table. Under the large flat-screen TV there was a small refrigerator. 
I liked the interface on the TV. On the power on screen, there is a scroll that shows the available channels and their numbers. This saved me from having to scroll to find the channel that I wanted. Since I now watch movies on my iPad, I did not notice the movie selection or the prices but I would expect them to be good.. I almost forgot that there was a safe in my room. 
There was a coffee bar in the room, but since the weather was good, I just went across the street to one of the three Starbucks in the block. (Lest you think that is a lot of Starbucks, there is a spot on Market street from which one can count five Starbucks. There are another two closer than the furthest of the five but which one cannot see.)
One of the advantages of an older property was the large walk-in closet. [I hate those tiny presses that pass for closets in """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""modern"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotels. ] The clock radio had a line-in connector for mobile computers. As an iPhone user, I might have liked an iPhone adapter but this arrangement accommodates my iPad, laptop, and your Android or Windows device. 
The king-size bed had a very comfortable mattress, plenty of big fluffy pillows and a bolster. There was a room service breakfast menu and order form on the bed. 
Okay, there was no scale in the bathroom. That is by way of saying that is the only thing I missed. All of the permanent and consumable amenities were there, including my favorite, the curved shower curtain bar that makes the shower seem more roomy. There was a generous supply of generous sized towels and was clothes. The modern plumbing delivered plenty of hot water.
Amenities
The Handlery offers all the amenities one would hope for, from a knowledgeable, polite, and helpful concierge to shampoo in the bath. There is a very nice pool in a large atrium, a barber-shop, a business center, and an exercise facility. While I did not avail myself of any of these things, they were all pleasant, well-equipped, and popular. While this is not a convention hotel, there is a small number of meeting rooms. 
Wireless Internet is $-.-- per day or $--- per week (per device). While free would be nice, this is cheaper than most commercial hotels. These think nothing of charging $-- per day on top of much higher room rates. (In the US, economy hotels include free Internet but luxury properties charge extra.) Last year, when I mentioned that I had three computers, they gave me a code.)
There is a vending machine and an ice machine across from the elevator on all floors. Unlike most hotels, where one finds the vending machine by the noise, these are silent (Silent!) and out in the open. 
Dining is in the Daily Grill. For world travelers, the Grill is a very popular pub. You can find the menu on the web. I like it so well that I try to eat there at least once on any trip to San Francisco. 
Transportation
The Handlery is at Union Square, the heart of San Francisco. The garage entrance is two blocks up Cyril Magnin from the Powell Street BART station, -- minutes and $-.-- from SFO. One can spit from the front entrance to the Powell Street Cable Car. There is always a taxi queue at the door. (I shared a cab to the airport with a colleague; the fare was $--- before tip) San Francisco has world class public transportation and Google and the BART app, make it easy to use. However if you choose to drive, guest parking in the Handlery garage is $--.-- per day, a discount from the daily rate for those who are not guests. 
Other
The Handlery is a no-smoking property and one must agree to a $---- cleaning charge if one violates this policy. Of course, many Americans prefer smoke-free properties. The result is fresh and pleasant atmosphere throughout. (I did notice an ash tray by the pool.)
I hope that this review has helped you decide whether the Handlery is for you and that, if you choose it, you will have a pleasant stay.

This is a grand hotel. Not because of its size by current standard, but because of it’s high up location and the resulting view it provides. This hotel hosted all US presidents from Hoover to Ford, earned her the status of top hotel in San Francisco for ~-- years.
The hotel maintained its classical elegance, kept a good balance between older look and modem functionality. The unbeatable feature of this hotel is its view of the beautiful San Francisco city. A major part of the enjoyment of staying in Mark Hopkins is a visit to the Top of the Mark restaurant and bar, and, only if the ever-changing San Francisco weather is cooperating.
