We wanted to save a little money when we came back to Boston from Bar Harbor, Maine, so we choose the Buckminster, which was very reasonably priced. We weren't expecting much, but were pleasantly surprised with our room, the staff, and the hotel in general. Our room was freshly painted, spacious enough, closet and furniture, nice bathroom, comfortable beds, and quiet. What more could a traveller ask for? The hallways were also freshly painted and carpeted, making for a good vibe. The people at the front desk were extremely helpful and curtious, despite being quite swamped with guests, they never showed any sign of impatience. The only thing we didn't particularly like was the room were the complementary buffet-style breakfast was served. It's pretty """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""bare bones"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" student cafeteria style furnishings, and a little dank. Still, for the price, I can't complain.

We had a very enjoyable stay at the Magnolia Hotel. The staff are very responsive and helpful. The hotel has character and a fun buzz. We'll be back!
To tripadvisor: I don't appreciate having to say more than I want i.e. meet your designated --- character minimum.

Nice hotel in a great location. Walking distance from Penn Station. Service is excellent as well as restaurant. Rooms and bathrooms are VERY small as well as hallways and lobby...but it is NYC after all!
I will definitely stay at this hotel again.

Our room was very shabby -- not charming, just old. The water dripped in the bathroom, the paint was peeling, the heat didn't work, and the management didn't seem to care. We left early. Perhaps they've renovated some parts of the hotel, but not where we stayed!

Arriving at the Biltmore and entering the lobby is impressive indeed. It is spacious and rather grand. A long hallway runs behind the lobby and contains restaurants, shops and convention room. The hotel has a good business location and is near the Dorothy Chandler Pavillion. 
When I went to check in, I had to wait for about -- minutes because the entire computer system had crashed. However, after, that there way no wait and I was on my way to my room. It was unacceptable.
First, the room looked like something out of the ----s -- an older looking, low-level queen bed complete with a ----s-----s style cream bedspread and dust ruffle that didn't match, didn't fit, and was torn. There's good retro and bad retro; this was bad.
The carpet was stained. The room was very, very small and very dark. The view was of a wall. The bathroom was tiny and poorly remodeled. There was one wing-back chair that looked incredibly uncomfortable. Also, the room was so small that you couldn't possibly sit in the chair and watch TV. TV was on the dresser. There was a desk with a desk chair. However, the desk was the only table in the room. There was no nightstand -- some weird heavy box-like object (like an overturned computer box) was lying on the floor right next to the bed with various wires attached to it. Not sure what it was or what it was for. But no bed light, no place to put anything if you lay in bed. I didn't see a clock. The only phone was on the desk -- not reachable from the bed.
The worst part, however, was that there were huge stains on the cream-colored bedspread. At that point, I demanded a new room.
I was upgraded to a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""junior suite."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Very large with separate sitting room, but the furniture was still somewhat dated and I couldn't fairly describe the suite as attractive or luxurious. The carpet was stained. Tiles were missing from the dressing area counter. The TVs (there were -) were only --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" at best. The bathroom was ok but small and also a bit dated. 
Also, no mini-bar and no bottled water, coffee or tea. Not sure if there were vending machines but, other than tap water, nothing in the room to drink. 
Service was unremarkable -- neither great nor bad. Concierge was helpful. Checkout was slow -- there were - people in line and only one person to provide assistance. 
Room service (breakfast) was fine -- prompt and tasty. Had dinner in the Japanese restaurant; it was good as was the service there. Didn't make use of other hotel facilities.
I get the impression that what room you end up with could mean the difference between a decent stay and an unsatisfactory one but am not sure what room or type of room you need to request. There is a club level -- didn't stay there but maybe it's better.
Overall, my experience was merely okay (once I was in the second room). I've stayed in many nicer hotels for the same price and thus will probably look elsewhere when I return.

Very trendy hotel near everything. It's a bit pricey and the Marvelous suite on the --th has a weird lay out (IMO). Next time we'll opt for a lower priced room. 
The bar was happening on Friday & Saturday nights. 
Conceirge - Jennifer and Josh were amazing...great recommendations and if you needed anything, they were there to help!

Two words...false advertising. This is not a luxury or sophisticated property as the hotel claims. The pictures on the inn's website are highly misleading. The property and its accommodations are rustic, not elegant. The outdoor walkways to the rooms are disgusting. Dirty, carpet full of stains, and also some graffiti on the walls. The room had a nice view of the gulf course but was the quality of a Holiday Inn. Plain and simple, if you're looking for an elegant hotel experience (such as The Four Seasons, Ritz, etc.), do not stay here. My husband and I were so turned off and disappointed in the Rancho Bernardo Inn, we checked out immediately after seeing the room. The only positive thing about this brief """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""stay"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was the customer service. The front desk and bell staff were extremely friendly, accommodating, and professional. In fact, they referred us to The Grand Del Mar. We ended up staying there and it exceeded our expectations.

just wanted to comment on how much help Darryl Hulon was. He was very friendly, helpful and professional. he definately made my stay at crown plaza very pleasant. thanks Darryl. The gym needs a lot of work though, everything was broke and the ceiling tiles above the treadmills had to be removed so you didn't hit your head when you ran; really!!
low costs, breackfast included and good location next to the river, very close to the touristic area. Nice attention and disposition to solve your stay requirements.

Me and my son stayed at the LaQuinta Inn on our recent trip to San Antonio. The hotel is in a good location, close to interstate access which came in handy while we were out and about in the city going to the outlet in San Marcos, the AT&T center for the Spurs game. It's about - blocks from the Riverwalk and many of the sights downtown. We also went to the Alamo Bowl for the Baylor-Washington game and the shuttle bus to get to the Alamo Dome was right in front of the hotel. If your looking for a hotel for a good value, this is a good place to stay.

Cant complain about a thing with this hotel. it was our first time in new york and we couldn't ask much more from the staff. we got there early and they didn't have a room ready so we went for a mooch about and half an hour later i had a voicemail telling us to return and for our inconvenience, they had upgraded us from a queen to a king room!! the rooms are very spacious and the beds are the comfiest!! the hotel is within walking distance to time square, all the shopping and central park but if you are feeling lazy there is a subway - streets up that goes north to central park or south to the statue of liberty.
we really enjoyed our stay here and we will definitely return!!
thanks again Fashion--!!

Ok, let me just say that I researched hotels to death before our trip since I started planning our trip in December...we travel with our teenagers, so there were some considerations there. For instance, we wanted two rooms, and that's mainly why I ended up booking the Hyatt, we got a nice Family Rate where the -nd room was --% off! That was a huge plus for us! The rooms were connecting.
First of all, we got there with Amtrak from Anaheim (flew into Anaheim from Alaska, originally I didn't plan on us going to San Diego first, but it worked out nicely!) When we arrived at the beautiful downtown Santa Fe station, it was a gorgeous sunny day, perfect for our first day on vacation! My husband noticed the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""twin towers"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of the Hyatt from the station and had the brilliant idea for us to walk. Mind you, I don't mind normally, but lugging our heavy suitcases (we were on vacation for two weeks) from the train station to the hotel was a bit much, although it gave us a chance to see our surroundings, so I guess it was a good thing! 
Once we got to the hotel, we were impressed with the massive lobby, the huge paintings, and all the hustle and bustle going on in the area! There are a lot of business travelers that stay there, so you'll see a lot of dressed up people. The lady that checked us in was very personable and helpful, and she put us in the Seaport tower, which according to her is -- years newer than the main tower. The elevator system is a little confusing at first, but basically the tower we were in had two different elevator areas, one for the lower levels and one for the upper ones. I'm trying to remember, I think we were on the --th floor, I know we were high up! 
We had a beautiful view, I especially liked it at night with all the lights twinkling in the harbor! Our room faced the Maritime Museum ship, Embassy Suites and of course the water! The only thing that wasn't very aesthetic was the original, now abandoned Seaport Village that was directly below our window, but didn't really notice it after a while. 
We didn't take advantage of the pool area, although I checked it out one evening, it looks very nice. I would have liked to have used the spa services also, but just didn't have time! We walked to two restaurants in the area for dinner, one was a Mexican place (La Fiesta?) and the other was a chain called The Melting Pot, which we really enjoyed. Both were spendy, but very good food and service! It's really nice being downtown, you can get around easily by walking or taking the public trolley, we even took it to the Fashion Valley mall one day, and on the way home stopped at Old Town for dinner then took the trolley back downtown again! When we went to Seaworld and the Zoo, we took a taxi, and it worked out great. We don't like driving in large cities, so we opted not to rent a car, and with gas prices & parking fees, just as well.
I would recommend this hotel, and my understanding is that they have started renovating the rooms, so by next year, it should even more fabulous! 
Pros: Great downtown waterfront location, walk to Gaslamp-restaurants, close to trolley, Seaport Village, water taxi to Coronado, Maritime Museum, great restaurants, spacious room, comfortable beds, great views, huge flat screen with HD, refrigerator, makeup mirror in bathroom, nice big closet, good A-C, clean, good water pressure
Cons: Expense-lots of extra fees (internet, printing in business room downstairs) no free breakfast like some less expensive hotels, no fan in bathroom, no liners in trash cans, low flow sink water (but shower had good pressure..go figure!) housekeeping forgot to clean our room the first day, but after that it was no problem!

The Wit is a very cool brand-new chic boutique in the Chicago Loop. I visited June ---, a week after the hotel opened.
The lobby, all modern minimalism, is small and very busy. The front-desk staff was friendly, but clearly don't have the operation down-pat just yet. It's a new hotel, and you expect things not to be quite perfect, and they seemed a bit overwhelmed at times when guests called down with problems.
The rooms are dark, elegantly modern and comfortable. They're about average in size, but the minimalist furnishings make them seem bigger. The desk, wardrobe and dressers are very handsome, and the big ---inch flat screen TV rocks. (Lots of cable channels, but there were no in-room movies available to order on my visit).
My king sized bed was plush and comfortable, kind of like sleeping on a cloud. 
The bathrooms have walk-in showers only (which I much prefer) with the very European removable hand nozzle. Water pressure was great. I agree with a previous reviewer about the flat sinks - cool to look at but the standing water gets marooned on them - which can be kinda gross.
I ordered room service the first night - very, very good. And the Roof, the popular rooftop nightclub - rules!
The location is great. Yes, the Loop is kinda dead at night and on weekends, but it's at the north end of it, with easy access to N. Michigan Avenue and the River North area. As far as mass-transit access, it doesn't get any better. The State-Lake El station (Brown-Orange-Pink-Green lines) is right outside the front door, and the Lake red line stop is just past it.
My only gripes were with issues which I'm sure are related to the hotel's newness. The front desk staff were all friendly and went out of their way to help, but are still a bit clueless. Check-in was a little more chaotic than it needed to be.
Also, housekeeping was abysmally slow. I returned to my room at - p.m. and it still hadn't been made up. And when they did come, they didn't replenish the Neutrogena toiletries.
Also, the in-room coffeemakers included good Wolfgang Puck coffees, but no creamer. (The front desk staff had some cream sent right up to me, tho). And the bird sounds piped through the hallways really didn't do anything for me.
Despite these minor gripes, I had a great weekend at the Wit. I liked it much better than the W Hotel on the other side of the loop - it's far less self-consciously hip. Once the new-hotel issues are resolved, this place will be a real gem.
And did I mention that the Roof rocks?!?

Overall I enjoyed this Motel but there was no soap to speak of in the bathroom. The internet in the room might as well have been --k in my opinion. Also they didn't inform us their parking garage was under construction so we had to park - blocks away and haul our stuff back...not fun. Restaurant was very decent and our room was rather nice. Overall a decent motel with just a few minor inconveniences..

Stayed here for three nights in September --.
Room was a good size, good safe in the room, bathroom clean but toilet blocked a couple of times through no fault of mine, (honest)
Hotel had a decent enough gym, one of the reasons I booked it, good weights and a couple of good machines.
Pool was warm but Sunday afternoon was a party like MTV pool party with hipsters standing around, girls in heels and bikinis dancing and a crowd much younger than my -- years made us leave after observing the scene for ten minutes. Not a place to take the impressionable kids. Or the missus:-)
Location was great, ideal for Hollywood, Chinese theatre.
Burgers were ok, not the best I've had but not bad. Fantastic sweet potato fries though, amazing in fact.
Parking was a little expensive but everywhere was.
Worth the cost for the history and the ex guests, the location , the gym.

I stayed in this hotel for two nights while traveling for business in January. As with other Kimpton properties, it was a nice place and there are amenities for those who sign up for the Kimpton InTouch rewards program (e.g., a $-- credit for the mini bar and a free wine hour in the lobby each evening).
The location was good - an easy walk to Mission and Market Streets, Union Square, Chinatown, the Cable Car Museum, and much more. The neighborhood is a bit varied, with ritzy shopping in one direction and some run down buildings in the other, but just the typical big city stuff - it seems very safe all around the hotel. It's also an easy walk to the Powell Street BART station, which will take you directly to the airport.
The staff was friendly and the room was very comfortable and clean. The bathroom was spacious and clean. The room was very quiet at night despite being in a busy area.
I recommend this hotel highly and would have no reservations about staying here again.

Although not central it is the same distance to both the Needle and Westlake Center from the hotel. They are both in walking distance but if you aren't inclined than the hotel offers a shuttle service every hour to these two attractions plus the Convention Centre. 
The room wasn't particular modern but it was very clean, spacious and homely. There was a small kitchenette with a microwave, a desk and couch-tv area. Very comfortable.
The staff were excellent. Well informed and friendly.
The biggest let down was the breakfast. There was no real food. The eggs were powered, the waffles tasted of bitter chemicals from the spray you needed to use on the waffle maker. No real milk and powered tang instead of orange juice. The apples were rotten on the inside even though they looked perfect on the outside. The bananas were under ripe and crunchy even though again they were perfect on the outside. Go to Wholefoods instead for your meals which is on the way back to Westlake Center.
The cheapest way to and from the airport is definitely the train. It's only $-.-- per person to Westlake Center. From there a taxi is only $--- or a --- min walk. After checking out book the free shuttle to take you back to Westlake Center train station.

The Grand Hyatt was in a great location, right at the edge of Union Square. It’s about a block away from a cable car stop, which is very convenient. You can walk to some of the popular tourist spots, but it would be a long walk, especially with the all the hills in San Francisco. The hotel was clean and nice, but not overly luxurious. It was definitely a little dated, but still comfortable. The service from everyone we encountered was very friendly and helpful.

This hotel is an old building with a makeover. It looks nice at a first glance but when your laying in your bed trying to sleep and the floor above you is non stop squeaking because instead of updating anything real they just put down new carpet and paint. But a lot of the cuteness of this hotel is how old the building is. So you get what you are thinking. I would stay here again if no newer hotels are available. Internet is painfully slow and the elevator only holds two people at a time.

The hotel was lovely, but if you're going there to lap swim, don't bet on it. The water level in the pool was too low. Probably down - foot from where it should be. My fingers scraped the bottom at one end. I asked for them to fill it up, but only stayed one night so don't know if they responded.
Very nice. Clean rooms with a modern vibe. Breakfast was nice they had a good selection to choose from. Great location next to office park and lots of restaraunts and shops.

We stayed here on the first leg of our honeymoon. As soon as we arrived the staff were very friendly and helpful and were quickly shown to our room. The rooms are STUNNING and enormous, there is every possible convenience. There was a card congratulating us in our room and champagne and strawberries.
Huge Bed
Beautiful Bathroom
Great Kitchen
Huge Balcony
The concierge and driver were lovely and very helpful, we weren't often able to get the house car but the time we did he was really friendly. It is definitely best not to rely on this service as we managed to use it once in a four night stay I think. 
Breakfast was fine, only continental and nothing particularly special so if you like a big american breakfast you might want to grab breakfast elsewhere. Still, you can always cook in your room!
The hotel is situated in a lovely area with fantastic views, however I would say there isn't much atmosphere, either in the hotel or outside it in the evenings. Because it is apartment based and there is no restaurant it can feel a little 'cold'. However this really is a slight issue as we love cooking and that's why we chose it! Although the place was fantastic, being someone that likes to explore by walking and doesn't tend to take cabs, I might choose a hotel nearer the centre of San Francisco next time, however it really depends on how you travel. There are buses to all the main attractions which we enjoyed figuring out!
One of our only niggles was the fact that the air conditioning, lighting and television set up was a little overwhelming (and I'm a technology lover!). Being an fan of saving energy, I like to keep lighting and air conditioning to a minimum but everytime we went out the cleaner would have switched everything back on again and erased our settings so that was a little frustrating. 
Although I have mentioned very minor things (it is simply a matter of taste, not a criticism) overall we had a lovely relaxing stay, just what we needed to start off our honeymoon.

We just got done spending the weekend at the Barclays in NYC on --th. It was fantastic. After I booked the hotel I emailed to let them know I was coming for my anniversary and within -- hours Marie-Emilie had contacted me! We were there early, before our room was ready and they made sure to call us when it was done. Later that afternoon we got to our room and not more than - minutes later, our bags, champagne, and strawberries arrived. After a few hours a wonderful cake too. My wife loved it (for breakfast). The cake came with a card from Marie and the staff wishing us a happy anniversary.
The bed was great, the size of the hotel is manageable, and the staff was fantastic. Service was TOP-NOTCH. 
Once again . . . Thanks Marie-Emilie!

I stayed at the Park Savoy for - nights in May ----.
I paid US$--- per night, which I thought was a reasonable price to pay for accommodation in the heart of NY, close to central park, -th Ave and the subways stations to get you all around town. For a tourist visiting NY, especially for the first time, it is the ideal location if you are planning to travel all around the city, both uptown and downtown.
The downside is the standard of the rooms. They are very small, plain and certainly not a place to hang out. The bathrooms are tiny. I treated the room as a place to keep my luggage, crash after a night out on the town, and somewhere to leave fairly early in the morning to head out for breakfast. The rooms are clean and there is a daily maid service.
If you are looking for a relaxing holiday staying in a comfy room, I suggest this is not the hotel you are looking for. But if you're taking a short shopping trip, or visiting for a few days of partying, or you want to keep your accommodation costs down and don't mind spending minimal time at your hotel, this hotel could be just right for you. 
It suited my needs. Would I stay there again? I think for next time I travel to NYC I would prefer to stay at hotel which has a few more creature comforts than the Park Savoy, and therefore I'll probably have to pay more.

Had to stay in Columbus for a business meeting; based on reviews of Hyatt's on Tripadvisor I switched to Westin. Tried to ignore posting by the marathon runner's reviews ($-- per night - he shouldn't expect much) so I booked a more expensive room (over $---). Talk about a terrible first impression - this hotel is surrounded by a ton of construction (many streets blocked off) plus it is by a courthouse; so lots of derelicts awaiting their sentencing -trials across the street plus surrounded by a ton of bail bond offices; didn't feel safe walking around after dark. Owners obviously paid a lot to renovate the lobby (a former bank building?) plus a bar (very dark & hopping) but skimped on rooms - halls for hotel guests. My bathroom was huge but tub - shower curtain not great; room dimensions very odd; bed had queen sheets on a king bed so could see sides of mattress(definitely unappealing) ; tv good but lighting in room terrible and a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""green bulb' didn't turn on; carpet was worn & ugly. Halls very depressing; very few elevators for size of hotel. Barely slept; would never stay there again. FYI, Hyatt's also very tired; I'd skip downtown Columbus & stay in a Dublin suburb; even a discount chain hotel would be better than any of these pitiful attempts. Save your $.

Like all the previous reviews, I booked this hotel based on the reviews. We were not disappointed. The staff were friendly, professional and extremely helpful. Our room was clean, comfortable and even though we were right by the elevator, quiet. The only noise was from outside and the street sirens. Breakfast was good although on the weekend, it got extremely busy and some of the food had run out when we were there. When we came back a little later, the food was restocked. We had already eaten though. Internet service was sketchy in the evening. At times, I could not log on and gave up. The lobby had two brand new computers with mega screens. If we really needed internet, we could log on for free in the lobby so the minor inconvenience of not getting it in our room was no big deal.
When I come back to Seattle, this will be my hotel of choice. It is a short walk to the Space Needle and a bit further to Pike and downtown but not too far. We parked our car (free parking) for the entire time and walked everywhere. What a great bonus!! Loved, loved the La Quinta and will be back with my family!!!!

I really like this Marriott, I have stayed here a few times the past few months. Pros- It is in a great location, the service is phenomenal, the club lounge is spacious and well appointed, the lobby is large and updated and the fitness center is well equipped. Cons- the upper floors smell like food, the front desk mentioned it is because they are surrounded by lots of restaurants and their ventilation system sucks in the fumes. The hotel room bath area is also extremely small. Really no complaints. I Am looking forward to my return stay

Beds are very comfortable. For old hotel pretty nice. good location. Great staff. nice lobby. some rooms nicer than others but all nice enough...a good bed with nice linens is the most important part. We always stay here when we visit family who live close to Wrigley. I don't like the rule where you have to stay Friday and Saturday night during certain times of the year.
room was dirty, and I ordered a wake up call but was never awaken. The hotel doesn't even have a vending machine in case you want to drink something cold

We stayed here on our way out of the north east to make sure we were near the airport for a flight the following morning. Quiet and clean standard Hilton room. The only problems are lack of any neighboring restaurants (fixed by a quick cab ride) and poor or lacking bell hop services.

We stayed at this hotel mid september ---- after getting a good room rate online. We have a large room with two double beds. very comfortable and plenty of room for our luggage. There was a slight leak with the toilet in the bathroom but the room was very clean. The hotel is located just off hollywood bld and you can walk from the hotel directly to Hollywood & Highland shopping centre. There is a mini mart just up the road (opposite the Holiday Inn) to stock up on bottled water and there was a bar fridge in our room with a small amount of space to place our water bottles. The staff were very helpful. No free wifi in the rooms but you could buy it for a fee. We purchased the wifi and had no problems. All in all a good hotel for the price we received.

After our recent wonderful experience here, I almost want to give a bad (ha ha) review to the hotel to keep it open for myself!
Seriously, here's what happened. We checked in very late. At the desk, I mentioned that I read (on this website) that rooms in one tower had been refurbished, and could we please have one of those. The night manager said of course, but after looking told me that there were none available, but instead he would give us a free upgrade to a suite (we had only booked a room with two beds.) Naturally I said great. The rate would be unchanged -- $--- a night.
But I had no idea what a luxurious set of rooms the suite would be! Yes, it was a tad shabby around the edges (after all, it WAS in the tower where rooms hadn't been remodeled yet), but when you get a suite with TWO beautiful views (one toward the U.N. tower and the East River, the other toward the Chrysler and Empire State Building), two full baths, a kitchen, about -- mirrors, -- drawers, - television sets, - telephones, - refrigerators (including the minibar) etc. etc. etc., one can only be overwhelmed! 
Also, the artwork, which consisted of the most beautiful framed samples of silks and other types of embroidery and other fabrics from around the world.
The neighborhood is, of course, wonderfully interesting and safe. The hotel personnel were helpful and very courteous. World class!
I don't think we will ever stay in a nicer """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in New York. We were in #----.
(P.S. We only had dial-up Internet service. This """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""old"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" tower is wired for Ethernet, but it was not working. There were several notices posted at the desk and in the room that the problem would be solved soon. The local call was not free -- it worked out to about $- an hour. Also, the breakfast buffet in the restaurant was pretty pricey -- about $--)

I swear, the only reason I didn't give this motel - """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""stars"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is that the night before we stayed here, we were in a swanky Ritz-Carlton in New Orleans. If that Ritz is the gold """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""--star"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" standard, this one deserved -. Zero complaints from us.
We selected this motel because it was so inexpensive, but it delivered like the pricy motels. The room was lovely, the bed linens looked new, the mattress was perfectly comfortable, the bath area was well appointed, and the continental breakfast was abundant. It was quiet, the staff were respectful and helpful, and the location was great for our purposes.
Unlike our room in the Ritz, this motel's """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""non-smoking"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room had never been smoked in!

Our family usually stays at one of the bigger hotel chains downtown in Seattle and we walk ourselves to exhaustion, but this trip we decided to try an older and closer hotel to the Market and boardwalk areas. When we arrived we were checked in right away and Bob our Concierge was really super friendly and an all around cool guy! Our room was much bigger than some of the older hotels we've stayed at in Vancouver, so we were happy with the size right away and the bathroom was pretty large as well. I enjoyed walking the halls and looking at old photos and each floor is decorated uniquely. My only two complaints are the hot water nearly scalding me to death in the shower with no warning, and no little coffee pot in the room, but hey its Seattle there are coffee places at every corner. All in all we enjoyed our stay and look forward to returning. Thanks for having a little fan in the room as well!

We stayed here twice during our recent visit to SFO and after reading all the positive reviews and getting a personal recommendation were a little underwhelmed. For the first one night stay on arriving at -pm we had to wait around -- minutes for the room to be available. The room was on the -nd floor and faced the street. Street noise was bearable but the ice machine in the hallway did get a bit annoying during the night. The second time we arrived back by car around -pm and scored the last spot in the street level carpark. We had a first floor (handicapped) room at the back with a nice view of a wall and not much character. It also seemed rather noisy and we expected a visit at any time from the returning revellers in the early hours of the morning. Lots of door banging etc. Reception seemed a bit grumpy at times - long hours maybe? Watch out for the lights over the table or better still move the table.
Price seemed reasonable for this part of town (although the most expensive on our trip) but I guess you get what you pay for. Parking is free which is a bonus.

Went to Boston for a long weekend """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""get-away"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and decided to try out the Ritz. The hotel did not seem to be very busy - and they were nice enough to upgrade us to a luxury suite. The suite was definitely well named as it was so luxurious that my husband and son did not want to leave the room! 
The room was huge, beautifully furnished and immaculate! The bathroom was beautiful and immaculate. 
(The weather was not co-operating with our plans - rain and snow and wind all weekend). Luckily there were plenty of places to eat and things to do within walking distance. When we did order room service, it was ready amazingly quickly and the food was very good.
My husband enjoyed working out in the adjoining sports club as well. We look forward to going back!

We stayed in the hotel for - nights and found it to be a most convenient location to get to business meetings, the convention centre as well as interesting spots for dinner and tourism.
The rooms are quite spacious, and in good condition. 
I found the service excellent - the main guy at the front desk is hilarious but helpful. Also in the restaurant and bar they are great. The conceirge can be a little annoying especially one of them who on arrival kept asking us about our departure so he could book a car for us to the airport - I kept telling him that I dont want to think about my departure when I just arrived after a -- hour flight but he wouldnt listen! Too pushy!
Breakfast was excellent considering this was a Garden Inn, better than some more expensive hotels.
Had dinner there once, it was OK.

We absolutely thought this hotel was the best - the decor was interesting and fun - the service was excellent - everyone from the manager to the maids were pleasant and friendly - the location was great - right in the middle of everything - 
This was a really great place to come back to after a long day of sightseeing and walking...
When we come to DC again, we'll definitely stay here!
Excellent rooms and facilities minutes from the main terminal.

We had one night to stay in New York and having been there before a few times staying at average hotels wanted to splash out for something a bit different. The W in Times Square couldn't be closer to the action and it offers a modernist, colourful environment in all areas, with top service and friendliness. We were upgraded (which always helps admittedly) to a suite on the --st Floor overlooking Times Square on one side and looking up Broadway to Central Park on the other. The room(s) were more than spacious with all the facilities you would expect in a well-designed space. Room service breakfast was top quality and despite the hubbub and -- hour action on the street, we had a peaceful nights sleep. We had lunch in the bar-restaurant on the ground floor - OK but nothing too special and drinks in the bar late evening - nice environment but not much atmosphere. Only slight disappointment was the charge for wi-fi, so we couldn't use the web for free.

I really liked this place. Flew in for a quick business turn around and this was perfect for my needs. The front desk staff is so nice and helpful. They let me know what was around and the best place to eat. The room was quiet and the bed was comfortable. I saw the manager in the moring and they too were very pleasant. No wonder why their staff is great. Starts from the top and trickles down. I would recomend this place for anyone needing a great deal and has to be close to the airport.

I made a reservation at the Hotel Felix through Priceline and I'm not even going to stay at the hotel because the service, prior to my arrival, has been so terrible. Like others, I need a room with two beds. When I called the first time with my request for a room with two beds I was told that my request would be put in the system. I called again to arrange an early check-in, which costs $-- but I thought would be worth the money considering how early my flight arrives in Chicago. I was told that they couldn't guarentee an early check-in but, if I was able to get an early check-in, there was no way for them to know when I would be able to check-in. Thus, I could end up paying $-- for a -am check-in or a -pm check-in (regular check-in is at -pm.) I decided to go without the early check-in but didn't want to get off the phone before I had confirmed that my room has two beds. When I asked they they told me there were no rooms with two beds available. I hung up the phone and got online to see if the hotel's website showed availability for a room with two beds. It did. I then called the hotel again, under the guise of booking a new reservation, to see if there were any rooms available with two beds. A room with two beds was available and they said they'd be happy to make a reservation for me. I then asked if I could just make sure my current reservation could be changed to a room with two beds, since there was availability, and they told me that was not possible. I volunteered to pay an extra fee per night for a room with two beds and I was also told that was not possible.
It seemed pretty clear to me that if I was paying full price for the room they would have been happy to accomodate me but, since I booked my room through Priceline there was nothing they could do. I've used Priceline to book rooms all over the country and have never been treated like this. If they don't want people purchasing rooms through Priceline then they shouldn't sell rooms through Priceline. I'm so frustrated I've booked a room in a different hotel. I'm a fan of getting a deal but I'd rather be treated with respect. Of course, now I don't want to use Priceline to book a room in Chicago again because I might end up with Hotel Felix. I'd rather pay full price anywhere else than step one foot in their lobby.

We stayed for - nights and found it very nice, very clean, great breakfast, good beds, and very friendly staff. Highly recommend it. We got the special AARP weekend discount and that is the main reason we stayed here. We had never been to Houston so everything including the motel was hard to find at first but it was very easy the second day after we got used to things. Would highly recommend this motel.
Great boutique hotel. Charming bar. Friendly staff.

The location of this hotel is very good! I have stayed there for at least - times during my trip to San Francisco.
The location is just beside union square and - min walk to Chinatown.
I ususally din include breakfast with the booking, I prefer to eat tim sum in the Chinatown.
The room is clean but a little bit old. TV is normal CRT.

I stayed in this hotel for - nights (---- to ---------), service was Ok.. Room service were so so. Only thing that I did not like is They did not have WiFi. They were keep telling me about different crap. No wifi access.. had to buy special deal from Verizon. Not really happy with it. I was there on business trip but got stuck.

My wife and I enjoyed the design and style of our room. Liked the spaciousness and the elevated ceilings. The price is reasonable especially based on the location near the Alamo. Service was average. The restaurant is a different story. Understaffed, unorganized for breakfast. Elected to get coffee only after -- minute wait for breakfast. Where is Tabitha when you need her.

This hotel is convenient, the staff polite, and the room very clean; however, it's not designed for sleeping. First of all, the window curtains do not shut. All our room had was a sheer curtain which kept out NO light. We tried in vain to find a way to block out the light but couldn't. It felt as if we were sleeping on a stage due to the light pouring in from the brightly lit parking lot. Eventually I safety pinned towels to it to try to block it out. 
The comforters: while comfy they are crinkly and every time someone moves, it sounds like paper rustling. This all sounds nitpicky, I know...but not at midnight when you're desperate for sleep.

The Chancellor Hotel comes highly recommended. The staff were friendly and approachable. The location can't be beaten- close to train, tram, bus and of course the cable car.
The room was very similar to that on their website. It was clean, comfortable and quiet considering the location.
It made an excellent base for exploring SF. Would definitely use again if lucky enough to return to SF.

Stayed at the ALoft for two nights on a business trip. Large (for New York), comfortable room with personality. The staff were very attentive, polite and welcoming. Many good restaurants within easy walking distance.
Wonderful place to stay. The location, the staff, and the service are excellent and the price very reasonable. We were so pleased with our stay there and would definitely go back again.

We stayed here for - nights and had a pleasant stay The hotel was very close to the Bart,cable cars, local bus and shops. We did notice people sleeping on the street near the hotel. But we had noticed this in other cities too on this trip to the USA a sign of the times.
The room was comfortable but does need an update and believe this is starting soon. The breakfast was good with plenty of choice. Was surprised there was no executive room for Hilton Honours members.

Stayed for - nights on December ----. Good location near center and the mall. Just slept at the hotel so no experience on the other facilities.
Staff was very kind and helpful.

Very very simple and basic. Right across the street from busy fire station. Seedy part of town. Breakfast was a box of donuts and coffee. Bed was very very firm and pillows had seen better days. Next stay will pay more to get more.

i was at this hotel for a conference. found the staff, rooms and service excellent. the walking trail was a nice treat, steep walking in places, but enjoyable.
the only disappointment was if you opted to go green and didn't have your bedding changed, then they didn't do anything in the room at all. there was a $- coupon under your door that could be used in the restaurant only while you were there, and if you needed towels, you had to call for them. a misunderstanding possibly on my part. i would have thought they would at least come in ,empty the garbage cans and pick up the wet towels. this did not happen. so i would not do that again. other than that, great

I stayed in this hotel and was very pleased with the service we requested a refrigerator and a smoking room which we got. I was not pleased that there was no hot water, we had to let it run for quite some time to get it to where we could use it. not much for water conservation. The breakfast was very good and the staff was very courteous. We did have a problem with the key card deactivating and although ElPaso is not a city i wish to return to if needed I would stay there again. The other negative was there was no HBO and the channels we could get were fuzzy.

This was a great hotel to park the car and walk or take the transit. The area was safe and we had no problems, walking to Fishermens Warf or to the movie theater. As far as the parking goes, it is very tight fit and we had a small car. However, the cost to park, $-- US a night was the best value for any hotel parking that I could see, so no complaints there. I would definatly stay here again.

Pros:
Room clean (but I did go over it with clorox wipes and spray for bedding)
WiFi worked but slow
Microwave clean worked
Breakfast (Fresh Fruit, waffles, yogurt, danishes, cereal, toast,instant oatmeal etc.)
Good water pressure in shower
AC excellent
we received a brand new flat screen TV as did all the rooms I believe
Customer Service A+
Cons I didn't use the pool as I did not smell any colorine and I had to exchange my key - times becuase it just wouldn't work. I will stay here again.

We were attending our eldest sons wedding in West Haven CT. We decided to extend this into our annual holiday by staying in Chicago at the beginning and Boston at the end of the trip.
We arrived in Chicago on Saturday -th April but our luggage did not arrive till Monday night and there was much uncertainty as to where our luggage actually was. A mixture of poorly trained Aer Lingus personnel and US Immigration bureaucracy and lack of common sense.
Apart from no change of clothes, our luggage included wedding outfits and small presents-cards etc. Our first point of contact in The Conrad was Jonathan and he was both extremely helpful and understanding . He requested some of the basics from Housekeeping and advised us of nearest Walgreens etc. During the - days without luggage, Conrad staff offered help and assistance and Jonathan was especially helpful.
In addition, the facilities and location were first class. 
This lessened the anxiety and concern until our luggage eventually arrived.
Will definitely return to this hotel when next in Chicago (hopefully in the near future).

i stayed there - nites and i mean everything went well with this hotel,,, it was calm and the best was the customer service. when im around that area again im gonna stay there again!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! PERFECT!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

This hotel is wonderful. Stayed for two nights and wished we stayed longer! Service is excellant. When you arrive there are at least - guys to help you out of your car. Same goes when you leave. Concierge is extreamly helpful. They go above and beyond. Outdoor pool area is fab! Breakfast was just awesome! Location is perfect. Right across from Beverly Center to do shopping plus other shops near by. Would totally stay here again upon return to LA! Just Fab!

How awesome was it to come from Kentucky and be greeted by the nices Coloradians!!! This hotel was soooooo clean. They gave us top floor with Mountain Views. It was sooooo super quiet. The food in the restaurant was so good. The breakfast? Best Buffet with omelet station EVER. I am sooo happy we started our week long trip off by staying here. I will definately go back when I come back to visit. Everyone was so nice!!!! Did I mention Clean rooms? CLEAN!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

We stayed here for - nights during September. It is a good location being in Murray Hill and only takes -- minutes to walk to Times Square and - minutes to the nearest Metro. The hotel does not have a traditional reception and bar - restaurant area. As you walk in the front you are faced with the reception desk and then the lifts to the rooms are behind that. In place of a standard bar and breakfast-dining area there is a bar and cafe adjoining the hotel called the """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Barking Dog """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which you can use for breakfast etc and charge to the hotel via your room card. The staff are friendly enough there and it is reasonable value, but for anybody who likes a draught beer in the evening there are only bottles.I would suggest you insist on a high floor floor room as we were stuck on floor - with only a view of a brick wall. The rooms are spacious enough with a kitchen area for those who require that sort of thing. We didn't use ours as we were in New York to get about not sit in the room and cook.
All in all not a bad place to stay but if I were going to New York again I might think again about something more traditional in its layout.

We were unable to make our usual spring trip to Vegas, so we opted for a gambling mini-holiday in Detroit. I booked Greektown for two reasons: comparable price and location.
Price: Greektown was $-- a night less than Caesars Windsor and $--- a night less than Motorcity (MGM Grand had no availablity) on the various hotel discount sites that you access through Tripadvisor.
Location: On the plus side, you can walk out the hotel doors and roam a couple of streets of restaurants and bars. On the negative side, the restaurants at which we dined were not worth the trip from the hotel. We did walk to the Detroit Institute of Arts (which is beyond amazing) one afternoon, a half hour walk, but the routes did leave us feeling uneasy at times (and we are two adult men).
Rooms: Although small by Vegas standards, the room was lovely: clean, bright, stylish and very pleasing to the eye. The carpeting and furnishings looked new and the bathroom was spotless. We both found the bed to be very comfortable and we both slept very well.
Casino: The layout of the casino is quite wonderful: a warren of rooms, both large and small on different levels. The smoke in the casino was not wonderful; I am not certain why this casino was so much smokier than casinos in Vegas, but we could not gamble in any of the smaller rooms (the smoke in the air was visible) and could only barely tolerate the smoke in the larger rooms. As for the gambling, we did not have a pay-out of more than $-- in three days (!!!). Admittedly, we do not play the high stakes machines, but we do bet from fifty cents to $-.-- at at time. We stopped gambling at Greektown when we finally hit a bonus giving us eleven free spins: our total payout on the -- free spins was thirty-eight cents. God as my witness, thirty-eight cents on an eleven spin """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""bonus"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". We did much better at the MGM Grand (we lost money, but at least we had fun losing it).
I would recommend staying at the Greektown for the hotel. I would not recommend Greektown as a destination to gamble: if you are like us, you work too hard for your money to lose it without at least being entertained while it is being taken from you.

It was our first time in New York and we went at Thanksgiving. It was a great hotel, the lobby and restaurants are beautiful. The room was a good size and the bed was really comfortable. The only thing that didn't work was the Internet on the TV but that was a very minor thing. I fully recommend this hotel!

Oh dear. So at one time this place must have been majestic. The foyer is wonderful and some of the staff were excellent, but I guess it stops there. There are two key issues: i) under-investment and ii) unions. Its a real shame - this place has so many inherent positives: location, grandeur, history. Feels like she's being milked based on past glory.
Unions: this is a union hotel. Staff often cannot peform basic functions that a hotel of this alleged status should offer without blinking (but don't blame all staff - some are awesome, some definitely """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""union""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""). Need a conference room at short notice with a speaker-phone? No dice - """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""IT"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" have to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""set it up"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (err...set up a phone?). Need coffee-water in the business centre at -am? Actually, its a mail room, and nope - you can get room service up ---floors at $-- and then carry it down though...or walk down the street a block and sort yourself out. Need your - bags left with the Bell Captain for a few hours? No, carry them down to the storage room.
Underinvested
Outside of the Reception areas (amazing), rooms are proper vintage...and not in a good way. Ours smelt of wet, stale carpet; leaving the window open sorted it out, but the noise levels go up. Small shallow bath, shower curtain set-up, loose taps-missing fixtures. There's adequate room on the desk to work. Internet setup was fine. Mobile reception fine. 
Worth seeing once, but never again. Suppose thats what milking the brand is actually all about though.

For a three star hotel, Hilton offered many little touches that are often found in a five star hotel. I was very pleased that there was an ironing board (and iron) in the cupboard and a hair dryer in the bathroom. The hotel also had a very comprehensive write up on services available in the hotel, which included free access to a computer and to the Internet (although you have to limit your use if another guest is waiting). The concierge service was also very pleasant and knowledgeable. The only thing which was irritating was the auto sensor in the fridge. This is so sensitive that even if you just open the fridge, it thinks you have removed a food item! Also, unlike other hotels whose mini bar fridge has some empty space, hilton's fridge is so tightly packed that you can't put anything in the fridge and it costs quite a bit to hire a fridge.

I know NYC hotel rooms are typically small, but the Maritime's rooms were the smallest I have ever seen. The design of the room was well done as it's very streamlined, but I felt claustrophic at times. The location is great as it's close to Pastis, Spice Market and other hot restaurants, clubs and shops. The hotel restaurant, Matsuri, was just OK to us, and the hotel club, Hiro, was cool on Thursday night (intimate space, good DJ), but terrible on Friday night (large open space with ear splitting music). I would recommend the hotel if you want to be near the MeatPacking area and don't plan to spend any time in the room (or if you like cozy spaces). If you want a more spacious room, I would stay somewhere else like the Gansevoort.

My husband was taking a course in this hotel for a week and we decided to tag along for a couple of days in the beginning and in the end. We were very impressed with the hotel. It was beautiful and very modern looking. The staff was great. There was a January sale going on where you pay for the room and get a free breakfast buffet at the Diamond Tavern. When we got to the Diamond Tavern, there wasn't a breakfast buffet. Instead, we got to pick anything we wanted from the menu. Breakfast was great! 
Bath and soap products in the room were Crabtree and Evelyn. Coffee was Lavazza in the room. TV reception was great.
The rooms were clean. On the first night we were there, I found a couple of hand towels that were dirty. But, we had it switched the next day and everything was fine after that. Beds were great.
We had some minor problems with the safety deposit box but the management came quickly and fixed it a couple of times.
If we are ever back in the area, we would definitely be going back to the hotel again!

We had a great week in Boston staying at the Colonnade. It was very clean and comfortable and the bathroom was excellent. The hotel staff were very helpful and polite, especially Norman.
If I visited Boston again, I would definately stay at the Colonnade Hotel and would recommend it to my friends.

As previous reviewers have commented, this hotel is in a working train station. Our room was quite near to where the trains pass through the rear part of the hotel and the most we felt was some low rumblings throughout the night. This was very minor and only woke my wife and I once the first night of our three night stay. I think this unique aspect of the hotel is something to be enjoyed as it did not seem to be a nuisance at all. As this hotel has been built around the station, the rooms kind of weave around the architecture in place prior. This does make getting to your room take a little longer than usual but we were not in our room but to sleep. Most of the day we were out exploring Indy. We found the service to very top notch and not once did anyone mention that we booked through Priceline. I always appreciate that in a hotel. The maid service was very nice and friendly when we requested extra items. Overall, a very nice hotel and well located in the city for any events you may want to attend.

This hotel was clean, and the location in close to DIA if you're coming in late or leaving early. They offer shuttles to the airport too, which is nice. The walls are a bit thin, but that seems to be typical for these airport hotels. The rooms were fine, and the breakfast was just ok, but it's a fairly priced stay for one night.

Right off Hotel Palomar got points for having our room ready for us when we arrived at --:-- a.m. We had a king luxury suite which was wonderful. It had a nice sized living room, connecting hallway (where the bathroom was) and a huge bedroom. The living room had a pull out couch where my daughter slept - she wasn't too thrilled with the mattress (you could feel the springs in the mattress). In hindsight, we should have requested a roll away bed (just a heads up to anyone utilizing the pull out couch). The bathroom was very large with a big walk-in shower and a jacuzzi. We were supplied with shampoo, conditioner and body lotion, as well as some animal print robes. The bathroom had plenty of counter space and the living room and bedroom had drawer space and there were closets in the living room and the hallway. There was plenty of room to store all your things so there was no need to be tripping over suitcases, etc. Everything was immaculately clean and in good condition. One very small picky complaint would be that they could have left more soap for the shower once they saw how thin it had gotten - however, my daughter tells me I always have that complaint so maybe it's just my pet peeve.
Enough about the room - the staff was wonderful. Front desk always smiled and greeted you. Employees at the door were always there to hold the door and ask if you needed directions, a cab or advice on where to go - a great group of guys! Every evening at -:--, there's a free cocktail hour in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Living Room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" where they serve wine, sangria and a sampling of their War of the Roses cocktail as well as flat bread pizza. In the morning, there's free coffe and tea (both hot and iced); and there was always a supply of lemon infused water in the afternoon (which was great since it was very hot while we were there). Gym and pool are on the --th floor along with a terrace where you can just sit and be amazed at the buildings all around you - Chicago has some great architecture (take an architecture cruise to really appreciate it all - we did one at night and it was spectacular). We're from New York City and were still in awe of the buildings in Chicago.
Location is perfect - there are restaurants and stores all over. We were - blocks from Michigan Avenue; around the corner from the free Navy Pier shuttle, a few blocks from the theater district and about a -- minute walk to Millenium Park. The red line train station is on the corner and it was only - stops to the Willis Building where you can go to the observatory and stand on the glass enclosed ledges of the Sky Deck -- very cool! There's also a very good grocery store on the next block across the street. Good to buy some things to keep in the room - liquor, cold drinks, snacks - even bought fresh rolls and pastries in the morning for breakfast in the room. It's also very easy to get to and from the airport. Since this was our first time in Chicago, we were hesitant to take the train from the airport since we didn't know the area yet and didn't want the hassle of figuring it out. We took a taxi which cost $-- ($-- with tip for three of us). After getting familiar with the train during our stay, we decided to take it to the airport and it was no problem. You need to take the Blue Line but can transfer from the Red Line very easily ($-.-- per person so $-.-- vs. $-- - next time we'll take the train to the hotel also).
Since we had an evening flight, we checked out and the hotel stored our bags until we left. Upon leaving, I noticed the concierge was checking a flight for someone and printed her boarding passes for the next day, so I asked for the same service and he happily obliged -- checked us in for our flight and printed our boarding passes -- loved that service -- saved us time at the airport.
Great job Hotel Palomar - we love Chicago and will defintely be back to stay here again.

We came for a long weekend and the location was excellent for midtown Manhattan. It is located literally right across the street from the Rockefeller centre, and at the end of the street to the left is -th avenue, and to the right is Radio City Music Hall. It seems many of the rooms are corner rooms, because of the design of the building. We had a corner room on the top floor. From our window we could see the flags of Rockefeller centre and St. Patrick's cathedral on -th. Everyday it was very easy to get around to anywhere, as we were very close to a subway station as well. Central Park was a short walk north, and all the theatres were walking distance as well. There is not much of a lobby to speak of, because its a business hotel, but the staff is efficient, and they have computer stations to check yourself in which is really handy. The room is very clean, and was in dark greys, blue and green. I thought it looked very crisp and modern and pretty masculine, all of which appealed to me. The bathroom was also clean. There was a coffeemaker in the room. Iron and ironing board were available down the hall. It was a great base from which to see the city and I would definitely stay there again if I wanted to be in midtown.

I stayed in this hotel in June ----. 
I had to review it despite the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""passage of time"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" because it was a gem that I discovered thanks to Trip Advisor reviews.
Location: If you want to be in the thick of things or you're a first time visitor to NYC then this is a great place to stay. It's located on Times Square so it couldn't be more central or knee deep in the action. The subway station entrance is literally on the hotel's doorstep so it's super easy to get around. If you're looking for something quieter then I'd avoid Times Square and stay near Central Park or the financial district. The hotel restaurant has the most fantastic view of Time's Square. 
Rooms: Very comfortable. I was traveling with a friend who snores so it was imperative that I'd have my own bed. Our room had two super comfy double beds. By NYC standards the room was cavernous. Very comfortable after a long day of shopping and to recover from jet lag. It also had a nice sized flat-screen TV and a modern bathroom. And if I stuck my nose to the window I could even catch some of the action down on -th avenue. (We stayed higher up to avoid the noise.) In fact we watched them filming scenes from the Scorer's Apprentice on -th avenue down below. Very cool for star struck tourists. The room was also very clean. 
The price was reasonable and it was great value for money.
Never ate at the hotel but had cocktails in the bar. Service was great. 
The concierge service was great. They booked us personal shopping at Bloomingdales and recommended awesome Jazz Bars. 
The only thing that brought the hotel service down a notch or two were the doormen. They damaged the pull-out handle on my suitcase with the result that I couldn't wheel my case, but had to lug it around for the rest of my trip. While I guess these things happen they really blew it by ripping us off. The doorman arranged a car to take us to Brooklyn which cost a whopping """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I KID YOU NOT $-- with a tip"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Considering it costs $-- from the airport I believe we seriously got ripped off. 
Bottom line: Ask the concierge to arrange transport with a reputable company. 
I would definitely recommend this hotel.

Wow we loved this place! Super kid friendly, they loved it all especially the cookies and milk in the evenings. The rest of us loved the neighborhood, nice and quiet but still close to lots of great places to eat and shop. Union Street is two blocks away, the Marina district is a quick bus ride one way, North Beach the other way. Fisherman's wharf is pretty close, but not really worth it when you have so many other better places to see. W e loved just walking up and down the streets admiring the shops and houses. We will definitely be back!

Nice hotel with an inviting lobby, bar and dining area. Rooms were OK. Marriott-sized and -styled. Clean and efficient. Given the convention rate of $---.---night, not a bad deal. Staff was great - friendly and helpful. Really liked the informal and large bar-dining area. Limited menu but the food was very good, just not too many choices. Observations (as opposed to complaints): Internet was expensive but you did get one small bottle of water per day. No in-room refrigerator, which is a shame as you are right across the street from a Super K. No in-room safe. Closet was OK but you had to close the bathroom door to get into the closet. Meeting space is excellent with a number of options. Parking fees were way out of line ($----- self-valet) given the hotel is in the middle of nowhere - as in - you have to drive to do anything include eat outside the hotel. However, as the hotel is a mile from virtually all of San Diego's auto dealers, you could hitchhike down the freeway and get the transportation you need. Wouldn't stay there if you want to see San Diego's tourist sights, would stay there if, as it was in my case, the conference was being held there. Lastly, it is at least worth the trip to the hotel to hear your GPS pronounce """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Qualcomm Way.""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""

We found this hotel to be very conveniently located and apparently quite a local hang out. Each night, way into the morning, people were lined up to get into the hotel bar. The bowling alley-bar next door was also quite popular. Despite all the traffic, our hallway was relatively quiet until Saturday night when someone down the hallway was having a party and one person only made it home as far as the hallway where we found him asleep early the next morning. The hotel did promptly remove him and sent him on his way! The staff were cordial and even gave us a very early check-in on our arrival day. The hotel's decor was very modern and classy. Our room was a very nice size and the shower head was great. The bed was very comfortable. The House of Blues was right next door, but we weren't able to work this into our busy schedule.

Very few properties, including other hotels owned or operated under the Marriott Brand have less personality than Marriott Marquis. The whole property looks and feels like a borderline comical tourist circus, with really random individuals roaming around the lobby floor (some who definitely do not appear to be hotel guests). Not very hospitable atmosphere, and any guest who requires more than cruise line experience should avoid.
The rooms while spacious are very tired and dated, and the staff was overall friendly but a slightly cold and impersonal. 
The rack rate in July ---- was approximately $--- including tax which is a complete joke and reflects how the hotel owners milk clueless tourists of their hard earned dollars.

I wasn't sure I could find a good, not-so pricey hotel in midtown, during spring break, but I did... Rooms are small but neat, breakfast is plentiful, and the location is fantastic. Two blocks from Penn station, easy walking to Times Square, theaters, Central Park...Now I have a hotel to go to when I visit New York again!

You couldn't get a better location at this price! Very nice hotel. The room was a bit on the small side but didn't present any problem for us. The bed also seemed small for a Queen bed.
