There are some great reasonably priced restaurants in the area (including the imaginatively named Thai Place (!) which is fab! ) . It is also only about -- minutes walk to beautiful Georgetown. There is a ---- corner shop nearby and a Whole Foods and a Trader Joe's. The room itself (smallest suite they do, think its called corporate suite?) was HUGE! It was really lovely with a big bathroom, dressing table area, big bed, comfy seating area, big flatscreen tv and separate kitchen area which was well stocked with implements. We were very impressed with the level of decor and cleanliness and have no complaints at all as regards the room. Ok is is not a - star property but it is really really good. The only downside of the hotel was the snotty staff member at check-in. Yes they were busy but we had been travelling for -- hours when we arrived and were exhausted. He was not very understanding or welcoming towards us. The girl at check-out however was so lovely. 
A quick tip as regards days to visit. As with all of Washington hotels it is WAY more expensive to stay midweek. Our rate was very low ($---) for friday and saturday and went up for sunday($---). Had we stayed for Mon-thurs the nightly rate was really high. So I'd advise visiting for the weekend! This was definately the very best value hotel I found in all my planning for our trip, and I am so so glad we ignored the bad reviews!

Stayed - mights for a convention in November, ----.
Location close to convention center was excellent.
Hotel is a little dated, though much of this is due to the design. The walk through the hallways with several turns to get to your room is telling and the atrium area feels old.
The rooms are fine and typical Marriott quality.
Fitness facility is okay. Adequate equipment but the lay out is terrible.
There was some maintenance being done on our floor and the workers were sloppy leaving junk in the hallway

Very clean, very reasonably priced considering how expensive everything else in SF is. Only slightly negative thing is Lombard, Fishermans Warf, Palace of Fine Arts are walkable, but its a good long walk. If you are elderly or have small children, it might be too long of a walk. Otherwise, it wasnt that big a deal. The window had a view of a white wall. Not that I'm there to stare out the window, but would have been nice to have a view of an alley at least! There are resturants and bars on the next street over. Seemed like a mid --'s---'s neighborhood.

This hotel is in a very convenient location. Just off of I--- and about - miles from downtown Dallas. I agree with the other reviews that the area just surrounding the hotel is quite shady, but then again, the street it's on always has traffic and you aren't veering too far off from the interstate, so it's not that bad. You do need a car if you stay at this hotel because you'll end up driving for almost everything. Dallas Uptown area is about - miles away and one of the best options for a night out in town or just some moderately upscale dining.
The hotel rooms are small, but the renovation has done a good job. Size doesn't bother me that much, because I'd much rather have a clean room and nice hotel staff any day over the size of the room. To think of it, this is probably a really old hotel and structurally it is not possible for the hotel to make the rooms or the bathrooms bigger. So can't ding them for that.
The bathroom uses Neutrogena amenities which are quite nice and the towels were clean and soft. Wolfgang Puck coffee machine is available in the room, so you don't have to deal with coffee pots and stuff. Just insert the coffee cartridge and voila! you have one cup of nice steaming coffee.
The beds were very comfortable and the airconditioning in the room is controlled through a thermostat and not a window unit. Thank lord for that. Set the temperature and forget about it :-)
The fitness center is on the -nd floor with all latest Precor fitness equipment. There are two treadmills, one elliptical, one cycle. All the precor equipment has a personal television, which is a nice bonus. Free weights are available and about - different weighted exercise balls. This is one area where I would say that they could have set themselves apart, but they chose not too. They can very easily convert an adjoining room into an extended fitness center and install a couple of those weight machines.
There is a shop downstairs which stocks your sundry items and is reasonably priced for hotel standards. The restaurant is also small, but has a decent menu and also excellent breakfast for a reasonable price. You get a full buffet for -.-- and that includes made to order eggs and waffles. Fruits were very fresh and the other preparations like breakfast potatoes were very good.
All in all, I travel for business and this hotel fits the bill just fine. For the price, I would highly recommend this hotel.

Totally agree with all the good reviews. Fantastic location for Theatre land, transport, China Town - you name it - it's not far. Clean, tidy, VERY friendly, helpful staff - nothing was too much for them. --th visit to Boston and having stayed in some of the 'big' hotels nearby I'll pick this one again next time.

We spent last night at the Greektown - it was awful! First the TV had terrible satellite reception and kept loosing sound. Had a meeting in the morning so went to bed fairly early... at midnight the alarm clock went off, OK no big deal I should have checked that. At -am we are woke up by a person yelling in the hallway, pounding on one of the doors down the hall. Opened the door and asked the gentleman if he thought he was the only guest at the hotel? Mr. Drunk-man apologized and went into the room. Less than an hour later same situation, Mr Drunk-man strikes again. This time I called security, as I am thinking to myself this is a secure floor that you need a key card for entry. I hear security giving him a warning... Less than an hour later AGAIN!!!! Called security again... they come up and I hear ANOTHER warning, this time I come out of the room to be told that the person is not even a registered guest, he is staying with his passed out buddy AND security are the people that let him up to the floor anyway!!!! Went to the front desk to check out and ask for some sort of compensation... offered us breakfast or $-- off the room. We will NEVER stay here again, they seriously need to change their policies. Stay anywhere else and take a taxi to gamble, you will be better off.

Great place with atmosphere and charm. Friendly staff. Ideally located for all the sights with lots of restaurants nearby. (We love The Cheesecake Factory a step away in the Prudential center!) Would wholeheartedly recommend...

The entire staff was warm, friendly and accommodating, going well above and beyond the level of service I've ever experienced from a hotel staff. When a business colleague was stranded at a local train station -- minutes away, the general manager personally drove me in his car to pick him up. My group of -- people stayed for a week and were treated with care and generosity from start to finish.
The rooms are enormous and clean, with all of the necessary conveniences. The amazing staff and spacious rooms make this a superb value in Baltimore. Highly recommend.

I travel a lot and I think the W group is doing exactly the right thing when it comes to re-thinking the way hotels are designed and presented.
The W in SF is extremely stylish - very unique and very different from what you are used to from the large hotel chains which all remsemble themselves so much that it does not really make a difference where you stay. 
The W has more of a european style, bright pastel colors and lights in the rooms simplicity and yet a lot of nice details like a lit buddha. The have a great bench by the windows with a perfect view of SF. The amendities are samples of the BLISS Spa products and a I only used the face wash (the first time I got that in a hotel) and the liquid sopa but they were great. The lobby is darker, with a turntable for lounge nights and psycadelic wall pictures. Valet parking is available with very nice staff ( they gave us water bottles for the drive home). Pretty pricey with $-- plus tax per night, but parking in SF is always quite a pain. This place probably does not appeal too much conservative travelers who enjoy the dark wood and fabric style, but it is ideal for those who want their eyes spoilt and like something special.
A few minor thins that could be improved:
We had reserved for two but there was only one bathrobe. Just a detail but one that should be taken care of.
Also, our rooms have not been cleaned when we returned around -:--pm and I called the lobby and asked them to send someone after - since we wanted to take a nap. --mins later we had the roommaid knock on our doors, of course while we were sleeping. Also the mini bar prices are ridiculous. $- for a small bottle of water and $- for - Oreo Cookies.
I cannot say much about whether the room pricing is reasonable because we did not pay the bill, but if your budget isn't tight, go for it.

I liked this hotel as it's in the middle of everything, very close to Penn Station and Times Square.
The team is extremely friendly, breakfast is great, the lift works well and the room was big and quiet. The best hotel I have found in the last - years in New York and I have been in a few.
Please go there, you will not regret it.
Terrific hotel and excellent valet staff. Room was beautifully appointed, elegant and relaxing. Best kept secret in Dallas.
it was the worst place I have had ever . Is it dirty , noisy, very, very old building and the beach also is very dirty nobody is take in care of it

Our second time at this hotel proved just as wise a choice as the first four years ago. Besides the perfect central midtown location we could not fault any of the staff, from the knowledgeable front desk staff to the very polite domestic staff. Rick's cafe is the perfect place to wind down after a day exploring the delights of Manhattan with the complimentary evening wine and nibbles offering. Don't expect great views of the skylines from here but you will be assured of a spotless room at the edge of vibrant Times Square. It felt like we were treated like VIPs here and felt very much at home. Would not hesitate to return here on our next trip to the Big Apple.

Great stay!
Only negative side was the shower. Water pressured seemed a bit low so didn't come out of the shower head with much force. Also, water temperature was always either just lukewarm or somewhat cold...making for not a very soothing shower.
Other than that....awesome location, very clean, asthetically pleasing, the back pillows for sitting on the beds are awesome too!
Modern and very clean rooms just steps from the subway and few blocks from the Rockefeller Center. The staff was very friendly and helpfull.

My wife and I live in El Paso but stayed overnight as the hotel is very close to the starting and finish line of the marathon that my wife ran in last weekend. While the location was convenient for the race, that was where the positives end. This used to be one of the nicest hotels in the city but now it is showing it's age. We checked in and
 the young girl at the front desk 
was polite but uninterested. The rooms are pretty big with a separate sitting area but were outdated and dirty. Repairs had been made to the walls but they had not been repainted, wallpaper was peeling off, the tv must have been -- years old, the bathroom faucet dripped all night and the sink was rusted. While the shower had good water pressure, the tub did not drain well. Plus, my wife and I were greeted by a cockroach in the tub. I called room service to order desert for my daughter and nobody answered after - tries. I finally called the front desk to tell them and the same cheerful (being sarcastic) front deck clerk did not apologize but just said, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hold on"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and transferred me to the on site restaurant. Once connected, the restaurant employee took turns telling me what they had left for dessert and having a personal conversation with somebody. I finally settled for a chocolate shake for $-.-- after all fees were added. It was just melted ice cream. I had the pleasure of checking out in the morning with the same bubbly (more sarcasm) clerk. She pulled up my account, asked me if I wanted a receipt and gave me my receipt. As I stood there for about -- seconds, I asked her if that was it and she said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""yes"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". No thank you, how was your stay or anything. This hotel reminded me of a low budget motel along the interstate in a bad part of town.

This hotel was a really great find. THe rooms are very nice and the view is awesome. THe staff was friendly and helpfull and resolved all problems quickly. only minues from the airport, seaworld and mission beach.

We stayed overnight for a campus tour at Johns Hopkins - can't beat the location - right across the street. 
The staff was wonderful and went above and beyond in all respects. The hotel is immaculate, and our suite was very pleasant. Great free wi-fi access in our room.
My only complaint - I wish they had a complimentary continental breakfast for guests or a discount for the Starbucks in the lobby. I would absolutely stay here again next time I visit Baltimore.

I really liked it here and -- dollars seemed a reasonable price to pay. The much commented on 'wine tasting' was actually more of a 'wine drinking' with plenty of people indulging in a couple of glasses. The wine is only ordinary but still nice; the white was well chilled (BA Lounges take note). It worked really well as a place to meet other tourists and compare notes.Our room was small but we weren't spending a lot of time in there. I see what other advisors mean about shabby. The hotel is definitely fraying around the edges. The shower, while reasonably powerful, was not in great order. Some of the rooms are noisy but I can't believe this is unique in a small city centre hotel.They have broadband internet access in the lobby which was convenient and not too expensive. Staff were pretty good I thought - Vincent especially was very helpful in helping us work out how our hire car worked! And Tara got us Alcatraz tickets. There was a relaxed vibe about the staff which I imagine does not go down too well if something is wrong.Location can't really be beaten. Handy for just about everywhere or, at least, transport to everywhere.They have been taken over by Executive Hotels now, let's hope they arrest the slide down the tripadvisor popularity poll!

Stayed for five nights for a conference. Room was very comfy. Staff was terrific and very helpful and friendly. Location is within walking distance of Beale Street and all the great restaurants and bars. Only comment was couple nights during the week very loud motorcycles - cars drove down -nd ave repeatedly. Not in hotels control.

Communal areas were as grand as expected however our room was tired. The shower just spurted water at you which was either hot or cold alternately (very annoying). Although the room was clean at the beginning of the week, by the end of the week it was really dusty despite tipping the maid $- each day. 
Be aware that there are no tea and coffee making facilities in the rooms, there is room service at $- for a coffee when you wake up. 
The well know Peacock Alley Bar staff were very aloof, bordering on rudeness with their inability to hold any small talk. Very expensive and like anywhere in New York children are not allowed anywhere that alcohol is served without eating and even then only between the hours of -- noon and -pm. This was very annoying and I was eager to sample the craft beer pubs that are quite famous. 
Be mindful that if you do like a decent cup of tea, the expensive breakfast does not serve a good cuppa (ask for two teabags). 
No WiFi in the rooms unless you pay for it and although a large TV the channels were very restricted to American news channels.
Thinking that the land of America was one of hospitality where people will do anything for you was not the case.
Generally we found that New Yorkers were rude and ignorant. Give me England anyday where people apologise for bumping into you in the street and open doors for you.

My family and I stayed here for one night. The check in was quick and efficient.The staff were very friendly and knowledgeable . The rooms were spacious and clean. We dined in the hotel where the food was excellent. We enjoyed it so much that we have booked another stay tomorrow night on our return journey to the Carolina's.
Staff friendly but rooms need to be updated soon. Shortage of outlets in room. Pool also currently closed to be redone

A tad quirky and a lot of fun, the Hotel Lincoln is a fresh breeze on the Chicago hotel scene.
The difference becomes apparent when you step into the cozy, cool lobby, which somehow manages to combine a wooden rustic look with contemporary furnishings, and does it well. The staff is friendly and check in quick and pleasant.
Off to the left of the front desk is a very inviting bar area, and the restaurant is to the right, past the elevators.
The rooms are boutique-hotel smallish, but not oppressively so. (They're larger than those at the Hotel Felix.) Like the lobby, they're modern and traditional at the same time - the quirky chairs at the small workdesks have slogans printed on their backs. The rooms make good use of space, but the coffee service tray is annoyingly tucked into the closet. My large king bed was a little firm for my taste, but I enjoyed a good sleep in it. A flat-screen TV with a decent channel selection is mounted on the wall.
Views aren't great (at least not from my fourth-floor room), but who stares out of the window for hours? And yes, the walls are on the thin side, and you can hear conversations and activity from neighboring rooms and the hallways.
Bathrooms are small but very nice, with excellent shampoos, lotions, soaps etc., and plenty of big, fluffy towels. The bath-shower features a raining shower head.
There's free wifi in the rooms and public areas, but the hotel does charge for use of the business center - a bit of a disappointment for a boutique hotel.
The Lincoln is located on N. Clark @ Lincoln and Wells in Lincoln Park, one of Chicago's most desirable neighborhoods. It's across from the actual park and the Lincoln Park Zoo, and - --- blocks from the restaurants, bars and shops of the Old Town district.
It's a good distance away from the N. Michigan Ave.-downtown core. The Clark, Broadway and Armitage bus routes (all of which run downtown OR to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""L"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" stations) stop right in front of the hotel, and the Sheridan and LaSalle bus routes are a block over.
I really like staying in a neighborhood like Lincoln Park as an alternative to the slow-footed tourists and badge-wearing convention people of the Mag Mile or the Loop. When you want to go to those areas, public transit will get you there with no problem. But there's plenty to enjoy in the blocks around the hotel.

Stayed here for a week while visiting family in San Antonio. The hotel is more like apartments with a separate bedroom, living room with pull out sofa, kitchenette with stove, microwave and full sized fridge. The place was extremely well kept and everything was very clean, especially the common areas, which was tough considering there were many families with children. There is free breakfast, which was really very good. My only complaint was that due to the families with kids, table space was extremely limited. There are - waffle makers available (making waffles looking like the state of Texas), but these were constantly in use by people making half a dozen waffles to take up to their rooms, which made breakfast slow. Aside from that, there was good variety, and the coffee was good. The staff was some of the nicest and friendliest people I have ever run into in any hotel I have ever stayed. No question was too dumb, and no request too burdensome. They could not have been any better than they were, and this includes everyone I ran into, from the desk staff to the dining area staff to the cleaning and maintenance staff. Everyone always greeted me, and was always cheerful. This added to the pleasure of the stay. I would highly recommend this place, and it would be my first choice upon returning to San Antonio again.

We arrived in San Francisco for the first time ever, but was treated like a familiar visitor to this hotel. Despite the small drop off area in front of the hotel, the valet and bell boys function so efficiently there was no congestion. There were occasional complaints from passers by but I think the hotel team is so experienced they handled everything seamlessly.
The concierge is worth mentioning. I have tasked them to book French Laundry for our family - months ahead of our dining date. The conciege stationed one person on the morning the booking was opened to call over and over to the restaurant, and they managed to get a reservation for us! When we told people we managed to book a table at the French Laundry, many Americans-Californians thought we were joking and they are so envious of us. We also had some problem with our car rental, when our car was towed away in front of Union Square, the concierge worked hard to help us tracked the car from the tow company and directed us to retrieve the car. The service is way beyond what a normal concierge is expected to do and i commend the concierge team for their effort.
The rooms are well cleaned, and this hotel honor all benefits of Ambassador Club. 
The main drawback is the lifts get congested sometimes due to the high volume of visitors to the Top Of The Mark, but the waiting time is normally not too long.
I will go back to San Francisco, just to stay in this hotel and enjoy the relaxing stay again and again, and of course enjoy the charm of San Francisco.
To the team in Mark Hopkins Hotel, Keep it up!

The ---$ weekend rate seemed like a great deal. The room was very spacious, all though the carpet had a bunch of burns in it, like someone neglected the party waiver, but everything else was fine. The balcony had a great view of the bf parkway and the museum, overall would definately stay there again.

This hotel is located in a nice location and very central. One big thing that I'd like to see improving before I recommend them to anyone is their services, Two staff that I interacted with were cold, short, and condescending in their responses even though the issue that we were talking about ended up with me paying extra money for the misinformation I received. Paying extra money was not the most annoying thing. It was how the two staff treated me and handled the situation. I didn't feel like I was being treated with respect. In my opinion, simple respect from their staff is what was missing from this hotel.

My husband and I've been there last May for three nights. One day we've spent in Napa Valley tasting good wines and the other one we stroll the Embarcadero and downtown San Francisco in the Cable Car.
San Francisco is a beautiful city, one of my favorites in the world and I think that it doesn't deserve a hotel like Holiday Inn Fisherman's Wharf. it's a pity, because the place is fantastic, near the Wharf with all the restaurants and stores and close to the Cable Car terminal.
But the hotel was much better years ago...
The service isn't warm as it should be. You feel as you are interrupting something very important , and the employees do you """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""the favor"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to answer your questions.
The breakfast is a disaster. Bad and expensive. Lucky you if you find a Denny's just around the corner: prices and food much better.
We are Priority Club members and I couldn't understand why they reserved an old floor, with old rooms for us. Our view was a big white wall, isn't it good?
We had a white cube in the middle of the room and we found out it was a mini fridge. Simply horrible!!!
When we need a taxi, the porter stayed at the door whistling and, obviously, missing every taxi passing by. We had to go to the street four blocks away to get one. Only because the Marriott's porter was doing correctly his job and Marriott is in front of Holiday Inn.
Next time, we'll try another one!!!

Comparable to Holiday Inn Express for --- the price. Updated decor. No good restaurants to walk to from there and the neighborhood is sleezy like most of Aurora. There are fast food places to walk to.

As a big fan of San Francisco, I have stayed all over the city. I had never stayed, nor explored much, over in the Sunset-Ocean Beach area. We wanted to take our - year old to the zoo and Golden Gate Park for his first trip to SF and found this little gem. We knew we didn't want to stay downtown as it is really overstimulating and the prices for anything on the Wharf were outrageous. We found Ocean Park Motel here on trip advisor and were not disappointed. For people who appreciate history, charm, character and older buildings....you will love this place. The landscaping is so lush and beautiful you forget you are in the middle of a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""concrete jungle."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" The grounds are meticulously kept by the owner himself. The rooms are basic, but EXTREMELY clean. The beds were more comfortable than your average place, which I appreciate as I am accustomed to a tempurpedic and motel-hotel beds usually kill me. The private hot tub was a nice escape after traveling down the state with a child.... In reading other reviews-complaints I wanted to add- the WiFi was never a problem for us and the streetcar was not a bother. We did stay in a room that was not directly not he street, but it wasn't that far from those that were and it never bothered any of us. I am a very light sleeper and it never woke me up. It is actually much quieter at Ocean Park than any hotel-motel I've stayed at in SF. Union Square is so loud with sirens, transportation, etc. 
Ocean Park was a little oasis, perfect for families or people who want to stay off the beaten path and experience a different part of San Francisco. We didn't mind driving to our destinations as driving through SF is also a great experience and we actually saw more than we ever have. It was also great not to pay ---+ a night. The--- (with tax) for TWO rooms was well worth it. The owners take pride in their establishment and it reflects by the grounds, cleanliness and advice-tips they give to their customers. We didn't even have to get on trip advisor, google, yelp etc because they provide a -+ page handout on all the close-nearby eateries and sights. I talked directly with Vicki, the owner, when booking and she took special care to place me in the right room for my family. She even placed us in a room that was over their storage-laundry so I never felt worried about my - year old running around....there was no one below to complain! I loved that! They truly know their customer base and cater to individuals. If you are expecting the Four Seasons or a modern place, this is not it. But if you are expecting a quiet, clean, beautiful, charming home away from home this is the only place like it in San Francisco! 
We will most definitely be back to Ocean Park! Frankly, I don't see any reason to say anywhere else!

We stayed one night for our Anniversary. This hotel had very friendly staff starting at the entrance. Never once did we have to open a door, they even watched our bags as we were checking out. Highly recommend valet parking. These guys are quick and friendly. Our king suite had a roomy little seating area and plasma tv. The decor is fresh and inviting. The bed was very, very comfortable. Can't beat the location, right off of Michigan Ave. Across the street from Trader Joes. And Jbar was very cool. The music was nice, and drinks are good too. The Pink Chocolate was delicious. Reasonably priced hotel with awesome service. Our stay of choice. Highly recommend.

Spent five wonderful nights at the Lenox, wished I had stayed longer. The hotel is elegant and classy with a warm friendly feel. The staff were professional, the breakfast enormous. We received a welcome gift on arrival which made our experience even more special. Thank you Boston.... Thank you Lenox.... A wonderful city and an exceptional hotel. Would love to visit again!!

I love this hotel, they accept pets with no fee, the breakfast is delicious, the staff is very friendly and understanding, it has pool, and the rooms are very clean!
I did have a minor problem only with the TV but I was told that it was the signal and that there was nothing they could do. This hotel is perfect for family because of the location.

We had a view to a wall directly from our window. There was a noisy AC outside the window and outside the door so we had to use earplugs every night. We expected to get a balcony, but found out during check-in that only about --- of the rooms have a balcony

Stayed here for one night at the beginning of December. Arrived at -:--, which is a half hour after check-ins start. They tell me that my room isn't available! I had to wait -- minutes for them to clean, which I'm sure just consisted of a quick vacuum. Once I entered the room, it was extremely cold. A huge draft of cold air came through both windows, and made the room unbearable when the HEAT wasn't working! YES, I was without heat the entire stay! Not to mention, I was also without hot water. Myself and many others complained about this and all management did was blame the customers for not making them aware?! They were made aware countless times and did nothing to remedy the situation, just said it was being fixed. My room was right next to their office so I had the pleasure of listening to everyone complaining about this every - minutes. This """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is nothing but a glorified apartment. The main entrance looks nice, but once you look beyond it you'll see a building that is very old and hasn't been taken care of.

We had so much fun at Magic Castle! We stayed - nights. The best part was the friendly and accomadating staff, who packed us a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""snack bag"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for our beach day, cleaned our room and organized it wonderfully even though we pretty much left it a sty every time we left, and accomadated our very large daily request for bottled water and snacks! The pool was fun and really suprisingly not very busy. We loved the breakfast and would go back to the Magic Castle in a heartbeat! The rooms are fun becuase they are not your typical hotel room, they are like mini apartments. The room could use a repaint and new furniture, but they are comfortable and fun, and unique! The place is smaller than what it looks on online pics, which I think is nice. Overall, Loved it!

This is a very nice apartment style hotel just one street over from the Hollywood Walk of Fame. The appartment we stayed in was bright and roomy with a balcony overlooking the pool, the whole place was clean, comfortable and nicely furnished. The kitchen has a gas stove and cooker, microwave and fridge freezer. There were only a couple of pans provided but it was nice to have the option of cooking our own meals rather than find eat every meal out and there's an excellent """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Fresh & Easy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" supermarket a couple of minutes walk away.
The hotel provides pretty much everything you could ask for, secure parking, free wi-fi, the room had a LCD TV and dvd player and there's a whole library of dvds you can borrow from reception free of charge should you not feel like going out. There's a continental breakfast provided in the morning and when we stayed there was an urn of hot apple cider in reception in the evening, again complimentary. And should you feel like a snack at any time of the day or night just go to reception, they have a whole list of free snacks such as cookies, chips (crisps) and candy (similar to chocolate but not quite right...) that they hand out on request.
The staff in this hotel are unmatched in any other place I have stayed. Every single member of staff I spoke to was polite, friendly and accommodating. I didn't test the theory but you feel that nothing would be too much to ask.
If I ever find myself in Hollywood again I won't even consider staying anywhere else.

We really struggled with choosing a hotel for San Francisco, but this is the perfect place for anyone traveling with a car. This is one of the few locations with free parking and great rates. It is a no frills place, but very roomy. We requested a remodeled room and it wasnt exactly stylish, but it had a great bed and lots of space in the room. We requested a top floor away from Lombard and had no noise issues. You have to make sure and turn the privacy nob on the door or housekeeping will walk in. Also, they start cleaning early so we put the privacy sign out if we were sleeping in. The hotel is a simple block walk up to the --Muni which you take most everywhere. It's an easy drive to the Golden Gate Bridge or to go down the crooked part of Lombard. A few blocks back from the hotel there's a great little restaurant for breakfast, La Boulange. We would definitely stay here again.

It is always refreshing when you stay at an upscale property and get exactly what you expect across the board with no unwanted surprises. This property delivered at every level across the board from check in to check out.
The front desk staff was highly trained, very efficiant, and super professional as was the resturaunt and bar staff. No request was was left unfulfilled.
Great -- hr work out facility with every ultra modern piece of equiptment you could ask for, nice large pool area with palm trees and pleanty of comfortable chairs to relax in and soak up the Texas rays.
They offered pleanty of free parking and a covered parking garage, free WI FI internet service for loyality club members.
A most rare and strikeing aspect of this hotel is a huge indoor - outdoor, koi pond that covers the entire property from the driveway entrance all the way through the hotel lobby and out the other side, this just polishes off what is already a great property and sets it apart, very impressive.
It would be hard to find anything adverse to say about this facility, very highly recomenced, you can't go wrong here...

The hotel is pretty good - nice rooms and I didn't hear much noise at night. The rooms do show some wear and tear - the plastic outlet covers in my room were broken in half on some of the outlets. The restaurant food was very good for the price (not too expensive) though the service was a little slow. Levi Schmidt, who was manager at the front desk as I was checking out, deserves special mention. He drove myself and my coworker to the airport so that we could make our flight when the shuttle service had some issue. Thanks for going above and beyond.

The Pros: Very authentic Victorian experience; the lobby is gorgeous and the front desk lady was nice. Cool-looking room (we got a junior suite) with the basic amenities. Decent amount of space. Bed was moderately comfy. We paid $--- for one night in a junior suite, so I considered it a decent room for the price. Good location too and very artfully decorated.
The Cons: I got the suite because it advertised a fireplace. Apparently that doesn't mean the fireplace has to WORK. The front desk lady said that none of them work; the city turned off the power to them or something. So it was kinda false advertising. Secondly, there is a bit of a musty smell to the rooms. Not overpowering, but definitely """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""authentically aged"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", haha. Thirdly, the rooms have blackout curtains, but they're literally NAILED to the walls to keep you from pulling them shut (I managed anyway, haha). Finally, the climate control in the room didn't work either, so it was probably in the mid --'s with no hope of making it warmer.
Overall: If you're not picky, the price is decent, but I guess you get what you pay for. For me, the cons tended to outweigh the pros. Decoration and theme is nice, but if you advertise a fireplace, it should work.

We used to stay at the Park Hyatt all the time but that became an Intercontinental ages ago and we wanted to be in Century City again so we thought we would try this one.
Check in great. King bed room facing downtown LA. 
Room was good. Bathroom was very dark especially the shower-Tub. Good closet. I loved the balcony. Room and halls looked very un-Hyatt. Looks more like a Westin or W. 
The Regency Club was very nice.
The bad was the hotel was hosting some Playboy function and all these ladies (and I do use the term loosely) and their drunken admires had taken over the penthouse, hotel, and much of the pool for our entire stay. They were hooting and hollering late at night. 
We were at the pool the next day when they decided to expand their turf and we refused to move as we were paying guests too. Our room was not made up until after -:--p that night.
The restaurant was good. 
Check out was quick even at -:--a. 
I think I will try the Intercontinental next time

This older Hilton is in need of a substantial renovation. The walls are paper-thin allowing you to hear bits of your neighbors conversation, the bathroom fixtures dripped all night, and the carpet felt wet upon arrival. Not a good stay and will not be back. I'm usually a loyal Hilton fan but I'm starting to look for a new hotel chain to patronize.

My husband and I stayed here for Valentine's Day this year. The first night we stayed in a Jr Suite which was very big. The decor was very modern which I liked! The bad thing about this night was that apparently the hotel had been robbed in the middle of the night and police officers went door to door banging on everyone's door in the middle of the night which scared us like crazy. It's was around ---am and being awoken by a banging on your door can really rattle you. I expected at least an apology from the front desk in the morning or something to say sorry for the awful night but no one even mentioned it, it was as if nothing happened. I know it wasn't their fault they were robbed but it did happen in their hotel so I just thought they'd want to assure their guest that this never has happened before and we're so sorry but didn't get anything out of them. The staff was nice enough but not at all what I would call warm and friendly. Did do a very good job at giving off a welcoming feeling. The second night we stay in an actual suite. It was a very nice room however it smelled like cigerette smoke badly (in this non smoking room). I called down to the front desk to let them know and was told house keeping would be up with an air purifier but they never came. We eventually left to start our day and didn't complain any further when we returned. The hotel itself is nice... I'd say a - star but with the staff I would take it down to maybe a ---.- star. I would stay again if I need a room in the area but to plan another trip to stay the specifically, not going to happen!

I stayed at this hotel for - nights as a single traveller and can recommend it. My room was massive with two double beds, lovely bathroom, tv, safe, fridge etc. It was very clean and cleaned daily with new towels and toilettires left everyday. The free internet was briliiant. The pool is lovely and was always quiet, the gym is smll but has everything you need. Breakfast was not majorley exciting but more than adequate, bagels, fruit, yoghurts, cereal and a small selection of different hot stuff each day. The hotel is close to hollywood boulevard and hollywood and highland centre with plenty of places to shop and eat are withing - mins walking distance. it is also near the main pick up for many many tours around LA, although they will pick you up at your hotel.

There are very limited choices for hotels in JAX - so the standards are low. If you don't expect too much then you will not be disappointed. The good - the beds are comfortable and the bar food isn't bad. The bad - thin walls and (very) loud heat - ac units. The workout equipment is minimal and why do they even bother with the concierge lounge?

Having read so many positive reveiws about the Pearl on TA, my partner and I decided to book here. We were in New York for - nights and the hotel is in a great location just off Broadway - very close to Times Square, theatres, restaurants and shops. 
I've never stayed in NY before but this hotel was fantastic - very stylish and clean reception area and the receptionists-concierge were very helpful-polite. Our room was large and included a terrace area with chairs and table. The bed was big and there was plenty of drawer-cupboard space for clothes. Safe, microwave, coffee maker, hairdryer, iron and board were also in the room. NY is constantly noisy but we were never disturbed during the night - the glass in the windows must be thick!
Breakfast was included in the price and we were really impressed with it - fresh fruit salad, yogurts, bread, variety of bagels, cereals and pastries - certainly enough to start off the day. Yes, we had to use plastic plates and cutlery but it didn't make it any less enjoyable.
I don't have any complaints about this hotel and would definitely stay here again if visiting NY.

Even if the hotel staff is quite cold and don't exceed in being friendly, we found two great plus in our recent stay.
The two bedroom suite is great for family. Rooms are a bit small, however compensated by a reasonable sized living room with kitchenette; and to have a chance to cook and enjoy a meal in your apartment in the --th floor facing the Chrisler tower is even better than the most sophisticated steak house in town!
In addition rooms and bathrooms very very clean

We enjoyed this place very much. Very good staff offer us good deal. We didn't make reservation and were able to give us a good price. The location was excellent close to Fiesta and Sea World. The rooms were nice and clean. I left my curling iron behind and I call the hotel and it was turn in. The Hotel Manager was honest, helpful and pack it and call UPS to pick up. The Hotel paid for postage. I appreciated her doing it going out of her way to return my curling iron. Honest and helpful people make this place want to stay there again.

Spent four nights here. The property is relatively new. Very neat and clean and the staff did a great job keeping it that way. We had a king suite which was very open and roomy. For our stay it was the same price as double queen rooms which were much smaller. The bed was very comfortable. The heating-cooling unit beneath the window was operated via a thermostat on the wall. One of my pet peeves is noisy AC units, but this one wasn't bad at all. We did find the temp alternated between slightly too cool or slightly too warm as the unit cycled on and off. The place was very busy during the week, but we seldom heard the noise of other guests. New hotels seem to be getting the idea of how to build to maintain quiet for guests. The breakfast room was large and comfortable. The food was pretty basic continental breakfast fare, but on the week days they did provide cooked sausage patties and scrambled eggs in addition to the proverbial waffle-making machines. Not sure why they didn't do that for the weekend guests as well. I would have rated this property """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""excellent,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but we have had much nicer breakfasts at other LaQuintas.

We read the reviews, we re-read the reviews, we said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no way"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" it could be that bad. The staff was polite, attentive, and accomodating. The room was worth the price, the parking was excellent, the access to everywhere we needed to go was easy. The nieghborhood was older, but we never felt unsafe. I'm not sure what the bad ratings stem from, but our experience was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""just what we needed!!!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Thanks.

location couldn´t be better, but the hotel is old and carpets smell bad...furniture, tv´s in bedroom very old..elevator service very slow, a lot of noise from the train outside, maide service very slow, i asked for toilette paper twice and never received it, i had to chase the maide with the cart on the aisle.

Pros: Location, in Belltown, walking-biking distance from lots of cool restaurants, Pikes Market, and the Seattle Center. Free bikes - and good ones too, not giant cruisers. Friendly staff. Free business center with computers and printing.
Cons: Location, in Belltown, with lots of sketchy people in the area. The place is also still a little old school. There's no A-C, which isn't actually a big deal because it's Seattle and never gets that hot. Also, the floor in our room was damp. 
The room had a kitchenette, was helpful for storing drinks and snacks on the go. But there are a lot of great places to eat close by, so probably won't need it too much.

Staff makes you welcome and provides you with the experience you expect. The lobby provides -- hours excitement in style ... You walk out of the elevator and feel NY excitement. No """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""stuffy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" people .. Just a fun friendly crowd. Every room is fun and fairly priced... the higher the floor the higher the price because of the view. Rooms are very spacious what is unusual for NY. No better location with subway and Madison park in walking distance.
In summary we will be back - a memorable experience for my wife and I for a quick - day weekend. Do not forget to taste the best coffee in town next to the lobby (independent store)

We stayed here on a trip headed back from South Carolina. I have a three-year old boy and the hotel is very new. Pool was great. Rooms was decent sized - not as big as the Embassy Suites, but nice. No door, however, dividing the room from the sitting area. Staff was nice and helpful. There's a great local Italian place in the strip mall next door.

We stayed here for - nights during our holiday in Boston. We ended up booking at short enough notice as we had been let down by another hotel. I was worried about the standard of the hotel as I expected it to be booked out. However I need not have worried. When we checked in they were very efficient and we stayed on the --th floor. There was some confusion as we went up to our rooms about not being able to use one of the elevators as they go straight to the --th floor for VIPS so it may have been helpful to know this beforehand. However our room when we got there was a decent enough size. Having stayed in New York in the city centre - years previously I was expecting it to be a shoe box like that hotel but it was big enough with a great view of Boston. Location was perfect to get to tourist attractions and the T Arlington was nearby. There were several bars and restaurants beside the hotel. I would recommend Finale and Davios as they were lovely. The only gripe I would have is that the buffett breakfast at $-- is overpriced so we tried to find alternative breakfast options. The lobby is really breath taking and even some tourists were coming in just to take a picture of it! All in all a great stay and would have no hesitation in staying here again.

Stayed here for a week and for a hotel that claims a - star rating the service needs some attention to back this claim up. Parking service is good but this is where it ends upon arrival. Rooms are clean but feel dated. The hotel Internet connection is extremely poor hence would be a bad choice for business travelers who rely on this for work. You will be unable to download MS email. The location is good with close proximity to the Galleria and a good selection of restaurants. Consider other hotels in the area as the choice is plentiful at this price range. I will not choose to stay at this hotel again.

This hotel has more than exceeded my expectations, and it hasn't even been a full -- hours! Because I signed up for their membership program when booking (do it--it's FREE), I was greeted with free door cards that treat members to free beverages in the morning, then not -- minutes after I'd been in the room, I was brought a complimentary bottle of spring water, nuts and fruit. There is a complimentary car service, which took me to my dinner destination after getting a recommendation and reservation from the friendly concierge, and I came back to find my turn-down service had been handled--my bed was remade, my ice bucket was filled, another bottle of spring water was left, and the bathroom was tidied. Oh, and I had a personalized note waiting for me on my bedside table. I couldn't be more pleased with this hotel. I've never felt compelled to rate a hotel, except when something's gone terribly wrong, but I had to share this excellent customer service. Thank you for making this rainy stay in LA as pleasurable as possible, Omni!
Was told they did a complete renovation of the property. It was decent. Our bath towels had holes in the and the hallway didn't smell good.

Back again as host of an evening event put on in this hotel. Though the conference area was under construction all round our meeting room, the staff worked around it very effectively and all came off successfully. Not even sure our attendees were aware of the construction the way it was decorated around in the one hallway just outside. Emily and other banquet staff were terrific! Attentive to every issue of a successful event. Bravo to them.
The guest room was wonderful! What is it about Marriott beds? Was clean, very quiet and exquisitely comfortable.
Will probably do it again right here next year.

After reading the reviews here, I was a little leery of what I was going to be checking in to, but my friend's dad reserved us a room as a birthday gift for her and I'm of the mindset that beggar's can't be choosers - and hey, it ain't the Tenderloin, right? But onward...
The front desk staff was very accommodating. We arrived at -am, and we stopped to check in. We fully expected to just valet the car and have to come back to check in later, but we were welcomed and checked into our room immediately and with no extra charge. The room itself was decent size, but like other reviewers mentioned the bathroom is a bit claustrophobic. The decor in our room was very mod. When we looked out the window, we were over the bus yard, so I was prepared to have a lot of noise, but I got lucky compared to the others in my situation and really didn't hear much noise at all. We also had a great view of Coit Tower and the Transamerica Pyramid from our window. It provided an excellent base of operations for us, as it was close to Muni lines and such.
The valet was quick with retrieving our car when we were ready to leave the hotel and great about letting us put our things in the car after we checked out, but weren't ready to take the car yet.
The lobby bar was tasty, but on the expensive side. - appetizers, - cocktails, and a desert ran us about $-- after tax and tip!
The only downside for us (other than the small bathroom and expensive bar) was the fact that the hotel is a giant maze! Our room was at the end of one hallway and it was quite the long distance of winding around to get there. I swear after a long day of exploring, it felt like we walked half a mile to get from the hotel's front door to our room!
Overall a positive experience!

On arrival the hotel has a very impressive foyer thats always buzzing with people ----. We stayed in a tower suite - room ----. This suite has a terrace with fantastic views of the Manhattan skyline including the empire state building and the chyrsler building. The suite is a decent size with seperate sitting and sleeping areas. The marble bathroom is nice with decent water pressure in the shower! My only gripes about this place is that some of the staff are a little on the rude side. Having travelled to the states before, I expected the warm ''have a nice day'' attitude I have previously experienced. Not so in this hotel!!! be warned. The staff in the Tick Tock diner arn't that great either. I was also dissapointed to discover that the sky lounge open to suite residents for breakfast on the --th floor was closed for two of the days were there, this is when we experienced the Tick Tock diner staff! When we did use the sky lounge the breakfast was nice - good bagels and coffee!! and a fab city skyline view make this a special affair. Aside to this the hotel is great with all the art deco elegance and charm I hoped for when I booked it. We had a great time in NYC easily filing the four days we stayed there.

I booked my stay to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Historic Hotel Menger"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" through hotels.com for the -th of July weekend. Even though check-in time is -pm,we didn't get into our room until -:--. The front desk staff could not have cared less. We even spoke to the manager, and all we got was a lukewarm apology and an offer of a complimentary ice cream in their ice cream shop.The hotel itself was lovely, but as far as I'm concerned the stay is only as good as the service you get. The pool is locked promptly at - pm, which I think is way too early. Taking a shower was an adventure: every time another guest would flush their toilet(which you could hear through the paper thin walls) the water would get scalding hot.There is no parking so you are forced to pay $-- daily for very inept valet parking. The hotel does not even offer complimentary coffee, which is usually a given at any hotel.On previous occasions to San Antonio we had walked through the lobby of this hotel and were charmed by the beautiful setting, but apparently it is just a facade. I just wish we had just kept our interaction with this hotel to just that walk through. Anyway this is a nice place to visit, but I wouldn't want to stay there ever again.

- Went with my inlaws to Chicago and stayed at the Palmer house. I had seen it on Great Hotels and was interested in seeing it in person, sadly, a lot of renovations were occuring at the time.
 + The location of the Hotel was very convenient to the Art Institute, subway-L, buses, Millenium Park, etc. Views from our window was nice, over looking parts of the city. 
 - Staff was nice and fairly quick, though there were some language problems at the desk. I woould suggest that the hotel keep a native english speaker at the front desk to handle possible language problems. The same problem also appeared at the concierge desk on the executive level. 
 - The room had a nice comfortable desk but the lack of easy clothing storage made unpacking problematic. If you are only spending a night or two, the drawers provided (little more than desk drawers) would be sufficent but wee stayed there - nights.
 - Food on the concierge level was ok to mediocre but relatively plentiful. Coffee was basically an embarassment, they should at least have fresh brewed on the concierge level and instead they had a liquid reconstitution device used. Go to the Cornor Cafe instead.

A group of us booked the Waldorf as for many it was their first time in New York so where better to stay than this iconic hotel?
On reaching check-in, we were immediately offered an alternate option, that being all of our hotel costs would be covered if we moved over the block to Days Inn, a - star hotel (a sister hotel to the Waldorf). This was because a conference had over-run. Now we did not book the Waldorf to stay in a - star sister hotel across the road, so not clear why we were asked. I am also a Hilton Gold Card holder, so they would have known my preferences.
However for refusing to move to Days Inn we were allocated a very small dingy room at the back of the hotel, with a tiny bathroom, which was many years old. Single glazed windows, so cold air blowing in. Not what we expected at all. 
The following morning my wife complained and we were offered a bigger room, on the corner of the hotel. Again the bathroom was very dated, the windows did not fit, and I know for the money we were paying we could have got much much better deal in New York (I had been to NYC a few times before). 
The hotel itself is prohibitively expensive to eat or drink in, you can cross the road and get the same cup of coffee at at one tenth of the price.
Sadly its a hotel that has a great lobby that really takes ones breath away when you enter, once you are past that, it is very much all down hill - which is such a shame. 
The hotel has seen better days and is need of a refurbishment and to make the rooms and the bathrooms much more up to date. Even though the rooms are small, I get that, it's an old hotel, so you can't magic up space, but care and attention to modernising the rooms would go a long long way. 
It can surely only trade off the tourist buck, or its history for so long?
Over all I wish I had booked somewhere else for my wife and our friends first time in New York.

I've read a lot, both good and bad, about the Custom hotel prior to my trip. The rooms, hotel, the staff is totally OK but the hotel is missing a few of the most important accommodations to be able to pass for a good airport hotel. 
-. Shuttle service forgot to pick us up. We booked shuttle - days prior to the trip (like the homepage said we could). We called, spoke to the front desk and sent en e-mail. When we arrived to LAX there was no shuttle there. Wohoo first time in US.. where to go? We had to call them again for them to pick us up. The explanation was that they had no booking from us. Come on! We are grown ups. Why even offer """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""the book before"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" service if it doesn't work? 
-. No coffee until - am. I mean people are jet lagged, they need coffee whenever during the day-night. Airport hotel means guests form all over the world. A coffee machine in the lobby could save lives. Luckily there was a coffee shop and food store where one can get coffee -.-- during weekdays. I've had few other guests expressing the same issue and asking me where they could get coffee.
-. The smoking area outside of the hotel is horrible. The hotel is a non smoking facility but guests arrive from all over the world. They do smoke. But all and all if you're a non smoking, non coffee drinking person who doesn't mind being stood up by booked shuttle service after a -- hrs flight be my guest.. or the guest of Custom hotel.
I can always count on this hotel. The staff is very responsive and helpful.

This little hotel has a great location in downtown Seattle. Around the corner from the -th Avenue Theater. The only entrance to the hotel from the street is on the corner of -th Avenue and University. There is a place in front of the door to park the car while you unload your luggage, etc. Unfortunately, the theater was getting out at the same time we arrived and the cars from the parking garage, attached o the hotel, were using the 'unloading' spot as a turning lane. We then tried to get into the parking garage and had to carry all of our bags to an elevator that took us to the --th floor to check in.... The room was very nice, great amenities but I doubt we will ever stay again. I would give this hotel a higher rating but still feel it's lacking in making it easier to access.

My wife and I recently stayed here on my --th birthday. We live about -- miles North of NYC, and I have been going to NYC for dining, concerts, sports, etc. regularly since I was a teenager. This was the nicest hotel I have ever stayed in. The front desk staff could not have been nicer, and the view from our --th floor room was beautiful, only to be outdone by the wiew from the top floor lounge. Room was clean and comfortable, and the kitchen was spotless. The furniture was not your standard cookie-cutter hotel furniture, it was really nice. 
 If you feel you must have that """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Big Chain Hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" feel,with waterfalls and fountains in the lobby, this hotel is not for you. But if you appreciate the attentive staff of a smaller hotel, you will enjoy your stay. Very nice art deco styling, and reasonably priced too!

Great location, right in the center of it all. Very close to metro. Nice rooms, nice view, nice staff. Only thing that kept the review from being - star was the $-- charge for a microwave and the lack of soda machines (there are $- sodas in the mini bar). We enjoyed ourselves and will definitely be back!

Hotel Teatro is one of the nicer hotels in Downtown Denver, stayed here in Denver briefly as part of larger vacation throughout the Southwest. The hotel was in nice condition, especially considering that the building dates back to ----. The room had high ceilings (which probably helped the small room look bigger) with a standard bed, good air conditioning system and a TV with lots of channels (no basic cable here). The bathroom however was really nice, with a rainbath shower, Aveda bath products (I'm not normally big on specific names but this stuff is great!) and a separate soaking tub. While some people praised the downtown location, I found it a bit isolated - it is across the street from a huge parking lot, and chances are you will be viewing that from your room as most of the hotel rooms face it. The Grand Hyatt and Westin, however, are right on --th Street. Nonetheless, I would probably still prefer to stay here when I'm in Denver because of the nice rooms. Service is professional, and the late check-out (-pm with no hesitations) was a nice touch. Valet service was prompt and friendly (they are hungry for tips!) but they work hard to get them. Would stay here again if I happen to visit Denver.

We were in New York for a wedding and thought it would be a great idea to extend our trip by a little bit and do some sight seeing. This hotel was in a great location it was quiet, felt very safe, and was in the middle of everything. The staff was nice and we were able to leave our luggage with the front desk since check out was at --am and our flight didn't leave until -pm. It was very close to central park and several subway stops. Wonderful hotel, an exception value for NYC. Would happily stay here again.

Immediately greeted by a front desk lady that was less than bored of me during our - second conversation. A conversation that consisted of: """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""name? here you go"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" then i was handed - keys. I was clueless as to which entrance was quickest to my room, parking, the location of my room, breakfast or anything. The bar takes up the majority of the lobby area, great for my kids to be exposed to drunk people watching football. Room was what I expected, nothing above and beyond, just plain. Breakfast was NOT included, I learned this as I had woken my family up and took my kids downstairs...$-- for breakfast...no thanks, I'd have been less mad if the front desk woman had told me the night before. Awful stay, poor nights sleep, not recommended.

I was surprised to read many positive review on the Waldorf. I have stayed there several times on business. Each time I was given a small room, frayed looking. The computers in the business center had filthy keyboards that had never been cleaned, ever. There is no coffee machine, nor room for any in small rooms. It seems the best reviews come from people who were upgraded to Suites. I suggest you try a Suite if you want to stay at the Waldorf, otherwise I can name you -- better places to stay.

Built in ---- as a hotel, I couldn't get over all the history of this hotel!
If these walls could talk! The Oxford Hotel in lower downtown (LoDo)Denver is a jewel. It is historic and lends a historic feel in the lobby and restaurant-bar. The rooms are modernized. We stayed in an art deco room in the interior (no view) of the hotel and while the room was small, it was cleverly designed to feel spacious. The location can't be beat since the renovation of this formerly trashy neighborhood. It's within walking distance of Coors field and the fun bars-microbrews that surround it. We also had no trouble navigating the --th Street Mall on foot although there is a hop on hop off shuttle that runs the length of --th St . Note: If you have a car, and it's baseball season, it's best to use the hotel's valet service at $-- a day.

I stayed here with some friends over a weekend and all I can say is stay FAR, FAR away. The towels probably had been washed, but they were so dingy and stained that it was hard to tell. The staff was rude, the floors were dirty and there was a room service tray that sat out in the hall for -- hours (it was still there when we checked out). In addition, our friends in another room had people partying in the room next door until -AM and the hotel staff did virtually nothing to quiet them down. For the same price, there are much better options downtown. Frankly, I'd sooner sleep in a cardboard box.
Big Sandy

Stayed here for - nights for St. Patrick's weekend. Room was good, front desk was good, concierge was good. Sales pitch was as expected. For the price we paid it was well worth it. Would I pay full price? Probably not. Would I buy and become an owner? Not at this property. But, that's not to say it's not a good property for people who want to visit NYC mulitiple times a year.....

A good choice when you travel to New York for leisure. It was my second time to New York City and the hotel was quite good. Almost new hotel, small but clean and modern rooms, poor breakfast, slow lifts but only steps from Macy's and Empire State Building. Many restaurants nearby and --m from subway.

I wanted to do something special for our wedding anniversary so I booked a room at the Crescent. The price was steeper than I would normally pay, but being a special occasion, I thought it would be worth it. Unfortunately, that was not the case.
I requested that flowers, a fruit basket, and a bottle of champagne be in our room at check in. I was assured that this was not an unusual request (all at my expense), and would be taken care of. When we arrived at the hotel, I asked the front desk if my special requests had been noted in the reservation and was told that nothing special had been noted. Told not to worry, that fresh flowers were placed in every room every day, and that the fruit basket and champagne would be on the way shortly.
Needless to say, none of the above materialized. We never did get flowers, not even the ones that are supposedly placed in every room every day. After about two hours I called room service and asked where were the fruit basket and champagne. They delivered a bowl of bananas and apples (yawn), and a bottle of domestic California champagne for over $--- per bottle. I would have happily paid for the items that I requested given the chance.

My husband and I wanted a romantic weekend in SF to enjoy dining and art exhibits. Hotel Vitale was recommended by several friends and now we know why. The hotel is beautiful, the amenities are perfect and the location could not be better. The view from our room was of the bustling Ferry Building and the Bay Bridge! We returned to On The Ave for another stay and were equally satisfied as our first time. The room was clean; we got a room off the street so it was quiet. I've already made reservations there for a future trip to NYC.

We stayed at the Maxwell for three nights and were very impressed by it's amenities. It is in a great location and the staff is very friendly. They have a shuttle which we took to the Woodland Zoo and Pikes Market. The free parking is another bonus. Rooms are nice size and very clean.
If returning to Seattle, I would definitely stay at the Maxwell Hotel.

Our fourth visit -- This hotel sets the standard in Washington for the very finest service – it compares favorably with the best in New York, and with exceptional European hotels as well. Walking distance to restaurants and shopping mall. Service was both welcoming and helpful. A lot of history seen and read throughout hotel. Room was a good size for a couple. I was impressed by the luxury though you can notice it is an older hotel.

We had a room on the -th floor whicch was very nice. I didn't find the room small. I found it very original.

This Marriott is in a nice location right beside the shopping mall and numerous restaurants. Rooms are adequate, nothing fancy, but comfortable. They seemed small to me.

Good location near Union Square this hotel would be a gem if it was updated. As a Kimpton hotel you expect it to be in better shape. HEADS UP, there is a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""club members"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" section of the hotel and see if you can get reservations there! My big beef was the headboard was loose and squeeky so you'd wake up in the middle of the night as you turned over. One benefit was the restaurant on the ground floor, great breakfasts and dinners. I'd only stay there if I was upgraded to the club level or they did a renovation of the rooms.

I stayed here a week after the hotel was reopened due to Hurricane Sandy. The best advantage of this hotel is the location, despite the Whitehall station (Yellow line) is still closed. The Bowling Green subway station is less than five minutes walking from the hotel, and the ----Green line runs frequently even during weekends. Perfect experience I had there and it is really impressive. Can't use few words to describe it. Just go visit there yourself and I I hope you can feel the same with me.

Great location with not so busy street compared to times square. Close to times square, macys, and -- minute walk to central park. Right next to Grand central which is very convenient. Very clean and the Service is very good.

Stayed at this hotel specifically because I liked responses from hotel general manager. I am returning because I liked the service, price, experience and location of the property. Having read the previous reviews I was a bit worried but my doubts were knocked out. The hotel staff were very welcoming on arrival, offering hot or cold drinks and Checking in was no problem. I don't know about: Any pool or spa. Any parking, or prices.

The Sheraton was a great hotel. First time I've stayed at this particular Sheraton. The hotel was extremely clean, guest services and concierge were friendly, helpful and quick. The Draft sports bar-lounge inside the hotel was much more than I expected, providing stadium seating, projection screen tvs and more than enough tv's around the place to catch whatever game you're looking for, plus pool tables and private karaoke lounge. The convenience store, coffee shop and Ice cream shop were also appreciated.

I really like this hotel. Stayed for - nights in late June, booked a deluxe room and was upgraded to a very nice and spacious studio king. On a previous stay there were problems with sound-proofing, but none this time. I'd recommend you ask for a quiet room, either at the end of a corridor, or on a corner. 
I'd definitely stay here again.

It´s location is fantastic. Very near from the Grand Central Station.
The room is very good and has everything you need.
The staff was great.

Sadly just returned from our first great trip to NY.

The obvious reason to stay here is the proximity to the airport which is a short ride away. The hotel appears to be doing some updates but like so many hotels these days, the lobby looks clean and new and the corridors and rooms do not. Most off-putting are the dark brown doors to the rooms which make it look like an old dorm. The rooms themselves are okay -- clean and no bedbugs (I thoroughly checked the mattress and cross-checked on the bedbugregistry.com). Make SURE you request a non-smoking room. We were originally given a smoking room -- we didn't even enter the room, just opening the door was like inhaling an ash tray. To their credit they immediately gave us another room and even ran the room keys upstairs to us so we didn't have to lug everything around. Also provided a free bottle of water in every room which was a nice change from the $-.-- bottle usually found.... Stayed here for a conference.
Pros: Awesome location (close to the Mall, Verizon Center, China Town, Metro, etc.), nice conference facilities, etc.

The rooms were nice but not """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Renaissance"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" quality. Felt nickle and dimed for everything here...

Stayed for a short business trip and I must say the staff was great. Far too many hotels have that very robotic professional staff that just say the words but could care less. The Lucerne has a staff that actually seems to care. Nice rooms, nice fitness center and super location.

We were very happy with our stay at the Best Western Plus Denver Hotel. This was our first time to Denver and had an AMAZING time. Our room was very clean & comfartable. The staff were very friendly..Front desk was very helpful with directions & information and having a shuttle was a great plus! The continental breakfast they have every morning is amazing lots to choose from. We will be visiting Denver again and we will definitely be satying at the Best Western Plus again!!
Thanks, JB

I guess you get what you pay for. This hotel was actually a very good deal in a great location. The rooms are small and old, but they do have a classic look. The hotel staff were kind, but not overly helpful. I had expected the stay to be much more pleasant--but I was disappointed. If someone is looking for a good deal and not super concerned with customer service, then this is a great place to go.

Very central Location. Reception Staff not very helpful could do with some customer training skills. Door and Conceirge Staff all very helpful and friendly. Rooms adequate small but clean. Night life very sparse as it is based in Theatre District so had to go looking for decent pubs restaurant in hotel ok if a bit overpriced. I would recommend the hotel for it's location.

Stayed at the Hotel in February on their Park and Fly program. The Hotel was fine and we had a drink at the bar and also ate at the restaurant. Bartender and waiter were very nice. Rooms were clean. When we returned however we called for a pick up and waited over -.- hours. Love staying in embassy suites .. - rooms are great .. Free breakfasts and drink at nite .. So convenient . Especially nice for familues with kids .. Kids-adults can each have their own t v and room . Also like the atrium entrance that's why we picked --nd st over --th st location . The atrium makes it a lovely open feeling.

I thought I was the fussiest person when it comes to hotels but in reading the reviews, I must say I was wrong! Any request was promptly fulfilled. The staff was gracious and not snooty. It was easy to go anywhere in all of Seattle. We stayed for - nights. We loved it. I have stayed in hotels all over the world and this little boutique hotel is a gem.

We got a decent rate on Expedia for a room at the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""luxurious"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Park Plaza Hotel. The entry of the hotel is quite nice, althought the restaurants were quite over priced. Our room however, was not so nice.

The light fixtures were rusting and a patch job had been done on over half the ceiling (they forgot to actually finish the patch job and paint it). It made me shudder to think of what the sheets were like!! The room itself was quite small, had peeling and chipped paint, the carpet was in need of replacement and the furniture was falling apart. The only reason this didn't get a one star was because the location was relatively safe and it had a decent workout room.

Arrogant staff, limited help with problem, followed """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""comany line"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", absolutely no effort beyond the company line to assist you.
Rooms are comfortable as are the beds, good location too.
