Another visit to Boston and another stay in the Long Wharf. Why? The answer is easy it is all about location,location. loaction. Long Wharf sits next to the bay, most rooms have a great view particulalry on the higher floors, and next to both the Aquarium and Fanueil Hall market place the center of Boston's tourism. It is an easy walk to most of the key tourist attractions and also the T the Boston MBTA. the nearest station being the Aquarium stop on the Blue line just next to the hotel and the more useful Government Center stop being a short walk away. The Blue line give a direct two stop connection to the airport.
The hotel itself is rtaher grand having undergone several rounds of renovation. The public spaces are great and there is a lively bar-restaurant for nights you dont want to venture far. Rooms are standard Marriott - clean, well furnished with a really comfortable bed. Downside is that the bathroom is rather smaller than usual -but how long do you spend in the bathroom? 
 Very friendly staff - this hotel is very good.

We loved our stay at the Catamaran! The location is perfect, the grounds are beautiful and everything was clean and well attended. The service was awesome. 
I will start with the service at this resort. When we arrived (quite early) our room was not ready but they offered to call our cell when the room was ready. I thought, ya, sure. Well they did call! Our deluxe king garden room was on the second floor very near the lobby, a great central location. The room was good size, well appointed and clean. Nice flat screen TV and a fridge. Large closet. Comfy bed. The next day we got a call in the morning that the water heater had broken in our building and we had to be moved. That was a bummer as we had unpacked everything, had gotten groceries etc. I asked where we were being moved to. They said they would give us an upgrade to a BAY FRONT room. We packed our stuff and got assistance will our move. The view from the bay front room was awesome. The room was bigger, the bath and sink area was huge (double sinks, yay!), there was an even bigger flat screen TV as well as a couch. The bed was still nice and comfy (there is nothing worse than a crappy hotel room bed!). We had a room with a second floor balcony maybe -- feet from the bay board walk and the white sand beach of Mission Bay. I was sooo happy that water heater broke and was very impressed with the management for taking such good care of us. But, it gets better. We left for the afternoon and when we returned to our room the management had provided us a wine and cheese tray as well as a card apologizing for any inconvenience! We have traveled to lots of hotels and have been on several cruises with various problems that have popped up and never, ever, have we been treated so well. After staying in both rooms I would recommend paying the extra cash to have a bay front room. I think it is well worth the view and the people watching. 
The location of the Catamaran is great. It is located on Mission Bay, which is a much quieter location than on the Pacific side of things. But, if you want to see the Pacific you just walk one block over and you are right there. There are great restaurants, shops and groceries within walking distance. We rented a car while in San Diego but your really don’t need one in this location with public transportation being what is and with everything being so close. (Parking can be a pain and you usually have to pay. Watch the parking signs on the street closely, we almost got a parking ticket!) Our favorite restaurant was just a few steps from the Catamaran. It is called “World Famous” and is right on the beach. Go at sunset for an incredible view! They have the best lobster bisque soup I have ever had. 
The grounds of the Catamaran were very tropical. Lots of palm trees and flowers. They keep ducks, geese and other birds on the property-- lots of fun to watch and photograph. The pool and the hot tub was clean and good size. The spa seemed very nice as well (a little spendy though). The lobby has a huge waterfall. 
We did not eat on the property but we were there on Mothers Day and there were lots of people paying $---person for the buffet. I guess it must be good. 
We would not hesitate to recommend the Catamaran. Everyone from the front desk staff to the maids to the gardeners were very friendly. We hope we can go back sometime very soon.

We stayed at this hotel for our sons graduation from BMT. It was very clean. The staff was very friendly and I would definitely stay here again. The pool was small but i wasn't' there for that and it served its purpose for a quick dip. My - year old loved it and your graduates aren't allowed to swim anyways so we didn't spend much time there. I found the breakfast to be very good. always hot coffee and many choices from fruit, yogurt, oatmeal, waffles, and eggs bacon and sausage. If I return to visit my son I wouldn't even research anywhere else I would just stay there.

Our experience at this hotel was as good as you would expect with the name and reputation that proceeds it ... fantastic! We have stayed at many hotels in the Boston area for various reasons and this was by far one of the best in all areas. The room itself was very spacious, the bed was comfortable, the room service was fast and delicious, the staff in the restaurant and bar were friendly, ... I could go on and on... definitely a great value (somewhat expensive but worth it to me)!

Less than - mins from my work place on Dir place. Great location. Good service. Rooms are spacious and well appointed. The bistromcloses at -pm however they have limited frozen entrees when bistro is vlosed. close to most places in La Jolla?

Please understand that I had read some bad reviews for this hotel on this very site. I wish I would have listened to the warnings. I thought that there is no way a Crowne Plaza could be this bad. The room was spacious and very clean, you could tell they have been upgraded recently. The free breakfast and free wi-fi also were a bonus. As has been noted before, there are many homeless people in the area and it can feel a little intimidating. So beware of needing US dollars during the weekend or public holidays. We didn't eat breakfast in the hotel, instead crossing the street to Sam's Diner. Stale pastries made the morning """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""continental breakfast"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" a joke so we ate at the Silver Cloud restaurant a block away (cheap and good!!).

Enjoyed our two stays at this hotel. We found every thing and the entire staff outstanding.

If the locations of Howard Johnson Inn is within our travel itenerary, we would not even consider another hotel.
Old, outdated, and overpriced. Never again.

I thought this hotel brand would be a bit downscale, but this place runs like butter. Very nice spacious lobby with a -- hr coffee bar and fruit. Our room was a double queen because the second night, our daughter flew home from a semester abroad and stayed over with us. Especially for NYC, the room was huge. It was decorated with nice B&W prints, the beds were done in crisp white duvets and were incredibly comfy including down pillows. 
A hotel can't make things right if they aren't informed, and when I told them about a few minor things like the sink pop-up and the shower head having little problems, they were fixed immediately. The staff were all very nice and friendly. A pretty nice breakfast buffet is included. It's not gourmet, but does the job quite nicely. Please add soymilk, Hampton Inn, for the milk allergic, vegan, etc.
The location is great, steps away from the subway and walking distance to many restaurants and some of the Broadway theaters.

If you are into design and are sick of the many so called designer hotels out there in the market that fail to deliver - then this one for you to try. The building and interiors are well thought out and there is obvious quality to the interiors and furnishings. I had a great room, with wonderful views of the city from the floor to ceiling windows. The bathroom also had plenty of natural light and a great walk in shower (no tub - but for me that was not a problem). There is a library theme to the hotel and a wonderful selection of books throughout (in the Lobby, as well as your room). A great distraction from the regular hotel pursuits of TV and Internet! They have moved away from the hotel experience, by getting rid of the Reception Desk and check in is more informal, in the Lobby Lounge. The restaurant and bar are hip and although I did not have time to enjoy them, looked popular. The location is good, but still up and coming as there seemed to be quite a lot of construction in the area. We were moved into a one bedroom suite. Large bedroom, large living room with office, large kitchen (fully kitted out) and large bathroom and as we were now on the --th floor a more amazing view onto the Empire State Building!!!
The first room we had was more than adequate but our FREE upgrade was amazing!
The hotel is situated in an ideal location. - Mins to Macys :@), across the road from Madison Square Gardens and -- mins casual walk to Times Square. 
Reception staff at the hotel were always courteous and helpful in every way.
We purchased a - day (hop on hop off) bus trip which got us around everywhere, up the Empire State, Staten Island Tour and the Statue of Liberty.
Woodbury Common is well worth the one hour journey by bus. Lots of bargains and fab shops. Much cheaper than Bloomingdales and Macys. 
A fantastic trip! Went with Virgin Atlantic (again fab! and make sure you prebook your flight seat -- hours in advance on their website!!) Enjoyed every minute especially as we had a day of snow there too :@).
Immediately upon arrival the staff was friendly, helpful and welcoming. Everything met or exceeded expectations (except the toilet which was weirdly uncomfortable). We'll be back.

Great location, large room, and friendly staff. As the others have said, the cable cars can be loud if you have a Hyde St. facing room as we did. However, we were not there to stay in the room but to enjoy the city.

Simply the worst hotel I have ever stayed in and this is New York not some oputpost. Booked in on the --th floor, so bad with paint peeling and shower not working that asked for a move. The -th floor is marginally better, shower pressure that would strip paint, carpet heavily stained and musty smell in the room. Key card would not work second day and after - trips to reception and an argument with security eventually got into my room after an hour. Consequently missed the start of a show. Cannot understand reviews that say you get what you pay for, in many other countries the hotel would be closed down by the authorities.....who monitors standards in New York? Even the most basic - star hotel anywhere in the world beats the socks of the Penn, a pity when you think of its location and history.

Our first stay at the FS Seattle and very impressed. The room we had (#---) was stunning and the bathroom had the very best views with floor to ceiling windows! Had a great time at the bar watching the ballgame and the staff was all extremely friendly and efficient. We will definitely be going back.

I recently stayed five nights at the Fairmont Copley Plaza while in Boston for a conference. We arrived very late at night due to airport delays, and our check-in was efficient. Sarah was the desk clerk working when we arrived, and she was very friendly and accomodating. 
When I got to my room, I was pleasantly surprised to see the size and decor. Unfortunately, I was given a handicapped accessible room with a big walk-in shower and no bathtub. I phoned downstairs to inquire about the possibility of switching rooms, and this was done within -- minutes. I was moved to a room that had a seperate sitting area and bedroom. It was nice enough, but the bedroom area felt a bit closed in, with the bed facing a wall. The rooms are clean and nicely decorated, but they are definitely not luxurious and show some signs of age. For example, the door frames in my room had some paint chipping off, and the carpeting in the bedroom area was showing signs of wear and tear.
The rooms do not have coffee pots, and I discovered the next morning that getting coffee in the hotel is not easy. They put out complimentary coffee near the restaurant, but that doesn't start until -:--. When I asked the desk clerk about getting a cup of coffee earlier, she told me that I could either wait until -:-- or I was welcome to walk across the street to Starbucks.
Most of the staff I encountered at this hotel were less than friendly. I noticed that if you engaged them and tried to start a conversation, they would respond. But, I feel that few, if any, went out of their way to be friendly first. The concierge, Jim, was one of the most unfriendly people I encountered during the stay. When I would ask him questions, I felt as if it was really bothering him to have to answer me. Another concierge (John, I believe?) was very nice and friendly. The doormen were nice, again if you spoke to them first, but none went out of their way to be friendly.
Overall, the hotel is beautiful on the exterior and quite pretty inside. It's centrally located and easy to get to most anything. The staff seem to feel that they are there for some other reason besides customer service, and I felt this was a serious flaw for an otherwise nice enough hotel. I would most likely choose another hotel if I were to go back to Boston. I guess I am a bit simpler and would rather stay somewhere with a friendly staff and easier access to coffe in the morning - yes, coffee is very important to me in the morning!! :)

The room was okay, nothing special. It seemed fairly clean but our trash was not taken out for the three nights we were there. Parking and internet were additional charges. This hotel is definitely over-priced. If you book yourself on-line, make sure to call the hotel and confirm the price. We were charged significantly more than the website quote. A high school marching band was staying-practicing in the hotel while were were there.

I have stayed at this hotel several times and the staff are what make it (or brake it in some cases). it seemed as though they were willing to help, but when it came down to it, the follow-thru was lacking.
Stephen Kelly, the Front Desk Manager was the shining star however. As soon as my message got to him about a specific problem that I had, it was resolved immediately and I appreciate his service in that regard. The hope for thr future, is that the staff that state they can and will help will resolve the problem and I will not have to call back several times to get to a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""manager"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for resolve. Work in progress, I understand. Good luck with the continuous road to improvement.

I picked this hotel for two reasons: proximity to my conference at the Washington State convention center, and the fact that it has a sauna. It's rare to get a sauna in the US, so if I can find one, I go for it. 
The sauna - and hot tub - did not disappoint. They were clean and fully operational. Towels were on hand and the space was relaxed and quiet. Three of us were enjoying it that evening. I called ahead to make sure that the sauna was working and the answer surprised me.. that they indeed do have issues with it but that it seemed to be fine these days. So call ahead if this matters to you.
The location of the hotel is excellent for proximity to downtown attractions as well as I-- access. It's on a busy street, but I did not notice the traffic as I selected the quiet (alley) side. This hotel is very close to the start of the Seattle ride free zone, so free bus transport is readily available from this location, a money-saving perk. The Space Needle and Seattle Center are walkable. In fact, I had a nice view of the Space Needle from my room.
The room was clean and attractively decorated. The beds were fine. The shower was fantastic. Water pressure the Sheratons and Hyatts I've stayed at recently cannot compare with. These are important features in a hotel room and they are all excellent for the price. 
Here's my little rant: One thing I notice in this hotel as well as most others nowadays is the abominable product that passes for in room coffee. Micro coffee maker with hyper plastic wrapped coffee inserts, and chemical """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cream"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sugar""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""... --% plastic unwrapping, --% coffee? I'd have to be an automaton to call this food. I am not buying the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""eco friendly"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room marketing on that note alone. Tea drinkers? Bring your own, and expect the coffee aftertaste from passing it through the same filter. In short, in room coffee has become a degenerate experience. To pass the eco friendly test, this whole concept has to be improved. Especially in Seattle where excellent coffee, high grade tea brands and eco-friendliness are a way of life. 
Luckily, this hotel includes breakfast and it is filling, with waffles, toast, cereal fruit, and yes, decent coffee and tea selection. The hours on breakfast service are generous. 
Though check-in was a bit chaotic, the staff is attentive and accommodating On the whole I'd say it was a real hotel for real people. Nothing pretentious, just reliable, safe and good value.

We stayed at this hotel twice within a ten day period. The first time was nice, but the second required a room change due to a broken toilet. Also, that room could have used more cleaning, as exemplified by a dirty telephone. It is also a pity that there is a charge for internet.

This hotel was one of the last options my group had for staying in NYC for - nights. The rooms were very tiny, which is to be expected in Manhattan; however, the walls were very thin and the doors shut very heavily. Additionally, the first - floors have a significant amount of noise from --th Avenue and the - (yes, -) bars right across the street. We were awoken several times by people yelling in the street in the middle of the night. With three people in my room (one Q bed with a cot, which we had to keep folded in the corner and just take out the mattress to sleep on) there was not enough room to walk. Being a somewhat larger person, I had difficulty entering the bathroom and closing the door, or opening it again once I got in there, as it was very small and the door opened inward. There is no soda or snack machine, and no bathroom in the lobby. The ice machine is in the basement. The elevator is VERY, VERY slow. We took the stairs to the -th floor and beat it, not even trying, when it only had to go from the lobby to -.
That being said, the hotel was a pretty nice place. The desk staff was friendly and helpful. They even gave us fresh cookies at check-in! There was a decent breakfast each morning, though we often ate in our rooms because of the limited seating. The location of the inn was FANASTIC--just a block and a half from Times Square, and right in the theater district. The beds were decent, though not superb, and each room had a coffee maker and hair dryer. Wired and wireless internet were free and readily available. I'd stay here again if I was on a tight budget, though I'd probably try for a room with - beds.

The Peabody is a classy hotel that is also more expensive than other's in the area. I did not see any specials on-line so I called to get a $--- a night rate. We stayed the first night of our stay just to experience it. When checking in they gave us the Concergie floor but we didn't find it extra special. The next nights we stayed at the Hampton Inn & Suites. The lobby, fountain, bar and decor are very nice. The employees treat you as a guest and are very quick to say Hello or Welcome. The rooms are ok, but the bed was Extremely comfortable. It was like sleeping on a cloud. At night we also returned to our room to find a surprise plate with chocolates next to our bed. If other hotels paid attention to just greeting you and the little things they would be just as nice. The newspaper was also delivered in a cloth bag on our door instead of just dropped. If you don't want to pay the price of the Peabody you would get just as much out of the visit by having a cockatail (or more) in the lobby bar and watching the ducks coming at --am or leaving at -pm. It is made into a show and is cute to see. Also, take the elevator to the floor where the ducks live. It is also a nice view. If we stayed again we would walk over for a visit and cocktails. We saved over $-- a night staying at the Hampton and even had a kitchen, livingroom, balcony, bedroom and bath. The Peabody is a nice hotel to visit!

We stayed at this Springhill Suites for one night in mid-March. We arrived via Amtrak and had the free shuttle pick us up at the station. The driver was very prompt on getting to the station but did not help load our bags and was not very friendly on the ride back to the hotel. It was like he was put out for having to pick us up. We arrived around --:-- a.m. and our room was not ready (which I expected since we were early) and the front desk staff graciously held our bags for us. By the time we arrived back to the hotel after walking around downtown awhile, the room was ready. The room was moderately sized for a suite and everything was clean. They had an evening reception with snacks and drinks (for whatever reason, no soda), which was OK, but not great. The bed was very comfortable. The room was somewhat quiet, but not totally noiseless. The next morning, we had the free breakfast, which included make-your-own waffles, scrambled eggs, sausage and yogurt, milk, juice and cereal. Again, it was OK, but nothing spectacular. Since our train did not leave until mid-afternoon, we had the front desk keep our bags for us, again. The location was great for where we wanted to go, but all-in-all, I would say the hotel was OK, but not great.

I stayed at this hotel for three days during an exhibition. The room I was given was small but very clean and the bed was one of the most comfortable I've ever experienced in a hotel. 
The location is fantastic. Once you step out of the back of the hotel you are on the riverwalk...with shopping and good restaurants a stroll away.
They charge for everything! $-- a day to park your car....$-- a day to use the internet....- levels of taxes or fees. The quote I had was $--- a night but when I received the bill it turned out to be $---. 
I had asked for a room with two queens when I booked. Once I arrived the attendant in the lobby asked if I would mind taking a king. I really didn't want to but I agreed. It was only later that I realized I had given up a room with a balcony that overlooked the riverwalk for a room with fixed windows overlooking the highway. 
If you have the opportunity I would definitely ask for a double queen. Same price with a balcony and a nice view.
The restaurant in the hotel was, of course, pricey and not good. With the riverwalk just outside your best bet is to not eat at the hotel. I was roped into it for business but otherwise would not have bothered.
The floor above mine was being worked on during the day so there was a constant sound of some sort of electric chisel but they were disciplined enough to confine that to daylight hours. If you are staying here I suggest you check to ensure they are not renovating the floor above you.
Overall an average hotel with a fantastic location. Beware the hidden costs!

I spent hours researching hotels in Boston. My son and I were doing college tours and taking a little extra time to see the city and surrounding area. I hadn't been to Boston since ---- so I was not familiar with the city at all. I read reviews. I went to every single hotel booking site. And then I went to Millennium's home page and found the best rate in the city for a well reviewed hotel. Room rate before taxes (and they are hefty) was ---. Parking was astronomical at -- per day. Wireless is less than posted - ONLY -.-- for -- hours. The hotel is right across the street from Faneuil Hall and there are places open for breakfast despite everything you read. It is a - block walk to Hayward Street and the fabulous Italian restaurants as well as Mike's Pastry and Modern Bake Shop. Our room was HUGE! It was clean. We did not have a quaint balcony, but we did have plenty of space to spread out, a huge, updated bathroom with tub-shower (note to hotel, put a circular shower curtain rod in and the guests will stay warmer and you won't have to worry about flooding the bathroom). There was a lovely vanity table in an alcove outside the bathroom which meant I could do my hair and makeup while my son showered (total privacy). Housekeeping was a tad iffy during our stay. The ice bucket was left full of water for tree days (we decided to see if the housekeeper would notice it before we left - she didn't.) Powder spilled on a table was still there when we left. The room was spotless when we arrived, however. The staff could not have been more helpful (even running to my car one AM to grab some paperwork I needed) or courteous, but I did get some of the WORST directions ever from a front desk employee. The street she directed us to did not intersect Congress and we walked forever before realizing that we were almost in Connecticut. The T can be picked up behind Faneuil Hall or take a very short walk to Government Center and pick it up there. It is a short walk or an easy subway ride to Copley Plaza. I will always price shop for hotels, but I would stay here again.

Awesome location but this hotel is worn out, customer service is limited but they try. Management is holding back, they could make this place better, but they would have to charge substantially more. Stay rather comfortably here, right on the pacific ocean, enjoy Pacific Beach where you can walk to everything including Mission Bay and Mission Beach, and don't expect luxury for less money. Great value!

For the price you pay, this is a clean and ideally located place to stay. The furniture and fittings are a bit tired-dated, but serve the purpose. Beds are very comfortable and rooms include safe-coffee-free Wi-Fi etc. The restaurant on the -nd floor serves good food at reasonable prices and all the staff are polite and cheerful.
If you're looking for a chique and very modern place to stay, this is not for you. If you just want to get your head down for the night (or more) and enjoy what Seattle has to offer on foot, you can't go wrong. Definitely recommended!

My wife and I stayed at the hotel in August ---- and we always meant to write a review of our stay and never got around to it until now. After all, it's never too late. 
Quite simply we loved our short three night stay on our one and only visit to the USA. We could not have had a better introduction to the country and its people. The staff were very friendly and helpful, the hotel itself was great and the evening wine tasting was an absolute delight. If we needed advice about where to visit we only had to ask. The hotel breakfasts were fabulous and one day when we return, as we will, to San Francisco, there is only one hotel we will book into. I just hope we get to make the trip in less time than it took for me to write this review.
Sorry for the delay!
Peter and Elizabeth from Poynton, UK

There never fails to be a time when i show up for the hotel and David Richardson hasn't already seen my reservation and made my stay the excellent experience that i have come accustom to in Phoenix. I cant wait to tell many of my travelers in business what a great hotel from the front desk to the lady in the gift shop that gets me my pecan sticky buns every morning ...this is first class service at its finest thanks Hilton!!!

Stayed at the hotel along my way to midwest. Service was excellent. The staff was great, friendly, and knowledgeable. The pool was very nice so I enjoyed using it unlike most places. I will be returning to stay at the hotel again if return.

Stayed at this hostel for - nights over new years. 
Pros: Excellent location- - mins walk to subway, and Broadway is fantastic street to walk along. Room was cleaned everyday, fresh linen and towels which was an unexpected surprise being a hostel. Free wifi in lobby, even if it is a bit slow, at least you can check your emails. 
Cons: stayed in a - bed dorm. The room was a shoebox, couldn't swing a cat in it. No heater so it was freezing, slept in thermals. There were some permanent residents who were very loud and noisy. Someone on our floor did not know how to use a toilet properly.... it was absolutely disgusting. I refused to use that bathroom, there were other bathrooms but the hot water wasn't that great. 
If your going to stay here, book the private rooms. From the reviews they sound much nicer (and more hygienic). Its not the sort of place where you would want to lounge about in your room.... but then again why would you when your in NYC??

I'll preface this by saying I got a great conference rate, so the value for the money was excellent. The rooms and lobby area as expected for a - star hotel and better than some of other older - stars I've stayed in. Every one of the staff I dealt with provided excellent customer service (friendly but not obsequious)-- special kudos to the woman in the business center. My room faced the marina and had a lovely view and was quiet-- probably best to request over a city view that might get you a peek of the Washington Monument and mall but more likely one of the office buildings next door.
For those unfamiliar with DC, the location is a bit off the beaten path, but easily navigable. It's just south of the mall off --th St., about a five minute walk from the Smithsonian Metro stop. The area is mostly governmental buildings that close up evenings and weekends but I felt safe walking in the evening-- late at night I'd probably cab it. The L'Enfant Plaza metro stop was equally close, but kind of a creepy walk under a highway that was okay in day time, but I avoided it on weekends and after -:--. It's easily accessible to the Mall and associate monuments (Jefferson, MLK, Washington, WW- all within walking distance)
Overall, my recommendation was great conference rate and easily accessible to the convention center via the Metro, but a bit away from things if you're planning to network with conference colleagues. For tourism, a great hub to get everywhere and as close as most other options to the major attractions with the plus of being a wonderful sanctuary to escape to at the end of a long day.

We stayed for one night in July after arriving from the UK having been travelling all day. The location was very convenient, within minutes of the airport car rental garage.
We thought that the parking was expensive (don’t they get their money from the room!), although it does seem to be a good price compared to other places in the area.
The room was okay (can’t say better than that) and likewise the pool – not very picturesque being surrounded by concrete walls. 
Perhaps we were put off by being hot and very tired, and finding a large woodlice on the bed when we arrived! But apart from this, for one night it was okay.

A very good, clean and centrally located hotel in the financial centre of the city. Easy to get to the local tourist sites. I can recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a central location to stay. Easy to get to and from the airport from the State """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""T"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" station. Internet access is available in the lounge for free.

It wasn't until I went to write this review that I learned this was the #- rated hotel in Chicago. This is the nicest hotel I have ever stayed in. The rooms are nothing short of spectacular. My suite was like a studio apartment with a fireplace, work area, huge bathroom (with TV embedded in the mirror so I could watch and shave), comfortable bed, and enough closet space if I wanted to move in. The service in the hotel was simply perfect. Great location near Michigan Ave and all of the shopping one could want. It would pain me to stay anywhere else on my next visit to Chicago.

A friend of mine and I stayed at the Palmer House for - nights in July. We loved it there! The lobby is beautiful and our room was beautiful and spacious. I thought the hotel was very clean and the staff friendly. We had a room with - bath and - double beds, so it was quite spacious with a sitting area around the TV. Now granted, it's expensive as far as internet, valet parking and the gym, but this is downtown Chicago so it's to be epected. We didn't eat or drink there, but by looking at the drink menu, they were quite expensive. As for location, it's great! Right by the theater district and Millenium Park. If you're interested in taking a tour with the Double Decker Trolley, there's a stop right outside the hotel. The Double Decker was very convenient and informative and we used it like a Taxi for the - days we were there. Overall, this is a beautiful hotel in a great location and I would definitely stay there again.

My friend and I stayed at the Chicago Ritz for a weekend in July, and it was wonderful. The location cannot be beat and the view from our was gorgeous - on one side was the water and Navy Pier, and on the other, the Chicago sideline. The service was fantastic, from the front desk who moved things around to get us into our room early to the concierge who got us to the top of the waiting list at a popular brunch spot nearby. If you're heading to Chicago, the Ritz is where you should be.

As other reviews stated, the hotel is ready to be updated....but don't let that deter you from staying here! The bedding is super clean and updated and the room and public areas are kept very clean. We had no issues with the elevators, wait time was short. Location is great to walk to Times Square and Central Park. Subway is - blocks away, short walk. The rooms are large, just like you would expect a normal hotel room to be. Most in NYC are tiny! Price is great too, hard to find a room under $----nt in NYC with a location this good. I am a travel agent and would have no problem recommending this hotel to my clients. I would definitely stay here again.

The Hotel Elan used to be in the Howard Johnson chain, but they parted ways about four months ago. It is about - mile south of the centre of San Jose, and definitely """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""on the wrong side of the tracks"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in a downbeat part of town. It's true that it is rather basic, as American motels go, and that the manager is taciturn and lacking in people skills. But you get what you pay for. My room was large and (relatively) well equipped. The bed was comfortable. The WiFi was free and fast. There was a (somewhat infrequent) bus service into town, and the breakfast was ample, given the minimal setting in the lobby. It could have been worse.

We have just returned from a - night stay at this hotel that I booked for my boyfriends --th Birthday.
The hotel is in a good location for sightseeing, shops and subway - we walked almost everywhere, only catching the subway once to go to the financial district. We tended to take cabs if we didnt want to walk as they were easy enough to get and cheap, if a bit hair raising at times! 
As this was a birthday present for my boyfriends --th, I had requested on booking through the hotel website, a high floor room if that was possible, we were to be staying in a Junior Suite. Upon arrival we were given a room on the -th floor which unsurprisingly had no view, we asked to be moved to a higher floor and were accomodated but had to take a smaller room and were not refunded the difference in price. 
I had also requested that some toiletries and pillows be in our room on arrival, all of which were confirmed but none of which arrived. I eventually had to phone the front desk and ask for them to be sent up.
I had also had tickets to Wicked delivered to the hotel. I asked for them on arrival but was told they had not arrived, I asked again the next day and still no sign, finally after numerous calls to the ticket agent, I eventually found out that the tickets were indeed with the front desk staff. I phoned to ask for them and miraculously they appeared. This is not what I expect from a hotel of this standard.
On my boyfriends birthday, I asked for balloons, cake and champagne to be left in the room, and it was there waiting on him after a long day at Woodbury Common. The cake was huge, chocolate and very nice, and the wine helped us along nicely as we got ready for dinner at the River Cafe in Brooklyn.
The hotel was comfortable, well located, the staff friendly - but I would not rave about it. It was a good base for what was otherwise a fantastic trip, but I couldnt help feeling a bit disappointed, like there was something missing. I felt that without the view, I simply could have been in a hotel in any city anywhere in the world. Having said that I probably would stay here again - the rooms were big, the view when we got it was amazing and the location was perfect, and at least if I do go again I know exactly what to expect...

Excellent for families, our room gave us plenty of space for the - of us, - bedrooms and a room with a large sofa bed. Its very central, only a couple of blocks from Times Square and one block from the greyline Bus tours.
Very good value!
I don't think I have one bad thing to say about the San Carlos.

We arrived at the Seal Rock Inn after a long day of driving. My first impression was that it definately did NOT remind me of a ----'s national park lodge as described in a travel book I had picked up. It is on a relatively busy street corner and the sound of city buses is prevalent. My second impression came to me as I looked out the window - yes, we could see the ocean from our third floor window- but in the foreground, I observed an apparent homeless drunk sleeping in the bushes across the street. After several minutes, he woke up, staggered several steps, urinated in the plants, stumbled several more steps and lay down to sleep again. As I looked around the fairly shabby room of questionable cleanliness, I thought """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Oh my God, I can't stay here with my family.""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""
 But, I tried to set a good example for my kids and roll with the punches. Amazingly we had a quiet night sleep. The buses stop running and the traffic outside dies down. We had a roomy third floor room with one queen and two twin beds, so the kids were happy to each have their own space. The next day we took the bus downtown. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""end of the line"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is right across the street from Seal Rock Inn. So the bus was empty when we first got on, and there was standing room only by the time we got off. But it was a great way to people watch and meet some of the locals who live by public transportation. Many were quite friendly. We did our sightseeing thing that day and returned tired once again by bus. It was nice to not have driven in the car for a day, but one day of bus riding was enough. 
 The next morning my husband and I got up and walked to a charming diner down the hill. We had breakfast and a spectacular view of the ocean and the Sutro bath ruins. The neighborhood was looking a little better. Later, we drove ourselves to Fishermans Wharf and found a parking garage for another round of tourist stuff, which worked fine too.
 Originally our reservations were for three nights, but we decided that two were more than enough. We cancelled our third night and opted to return to an airport hotel that we knew would be clean and reliable, we had an early flight in the morning anyway and we'd seen most of what we came to see for this trip.
 In summary, Seal Rock Inn has potential to be a very nice place in an interesting location, but it needs major updating. Most of the staff is friendly, but they reside behind glass in a small office off a non-existant lobby. It doesn't give the guest a very confident feeling about the neighborhood. Free parking is a definite plus. And the price of the room was looking pretty good after experiencing how expensive everything in and around San Francisco is. Still, if we ever find our way back to San Francisco, we will probably save our pennies and pay more for a hopefully nicer place.

The Marriott City Center gives you a great welcome upon check in and the Front Desk Personnel are most helpful. They are super knowledgeable about Charlotte, truly seem to love the city and their jobs. It was a great welcome. The hotel was very clean, well-appointed and sized rooms. A modern take on comfort.

Pros: It is very clean, modern decor. It is convenient to many of the office parks in the North Houston area.
Cons: Has window air units that are placed next to the beds. I awoke periodically to the compressor kicking on and off. 
The showers are tiny (about the width of a doorway). 
If you are like me and need the flat screen as a second monitor while you work, forget about it. The tvs are mounted to save space by tilting about -- degrees left of right to show the screen to either the bed area or the sitting area. The desk area is -- degrees from the TV, so do the math. You can't use the TV as a second monitor while working at the desk. 
The breakfast was disappointing. No eggs or meat are included in the breakfast. It is available, but it costs extra. The free selection is coffee, juice, milk, cereal, some breads, apples, oatmeal, one type of muffin, yogurt, and fruit from a can. 
The area is horrible. One of the guests had all four tires stolen off his rental car in the hotel parking lot.

We spent - nights at this hotel over Labor Day weekend. The location was fantastic, very close to Times Square and all the main sights in NYC. Also, many excellent restaurants within walking distance. Breakfast is included and had an excellent mix of hot and cold food every day. The breakfast area does get very busy after - AM, but we were always able to find a seat and they are great at refilling the food frequently. Also, there are only - elevators and in the morning they get very crowded with everyone trying to go down for breakfast and back up after breakfast. Something to watch out for is that they put a $- per day """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""optional"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" charity donation charge on your bill. Thanks to your reviews we knew it was outdated and a little bit dirty. If you like Trader Joe’s or Whole Foods, then Staybridge Suites is the hotel that you should stay at in Chatsworth. It’s only - minutes away from these markets! It’s also conveniently located just a few blocks from Hwy --- and Reseda Blvd where you’ll find all the shopping malls and restaurants. The --bedroom --bath suite is large and very comfortable, with nicely decorated livingroom and a fully equipped kitchen (flat top stoves, microwave, dishwasher, sink, cooking wares, dishes). The thick curtains keep the bedrooms in pitch-black darkness, great for sleeping! We also like the free high speed internet (you’ll need a passcode from the very helpful front desk staff to connect) and free parking. Reserved a junior suite and was simply told not available when I arrived. I was given a deluxe room instead. Later the hotel agreed to upgrade to a suite after a long conversation with the front desk. The suite did not have a robe and slippers, the newspaper was not delivered in the morning, there was no order form for in room breakfast, and the bathrooms in the suite were small and cramped.

A group of us are here for business and we all love Terry at the front desk and the staff! He remembers our names and is always cheerful. The rooms are new and very clean! The bar is nice and quiet and with a small menu. We appreciate all the staff and front desk for making us feel at home. We will continue to stay here...

great location, if you want to walk to georgetown; cool, modern lounge-tea room-bar with a great menu; very clean lines and minimalist look in lobby; service was average; dark, dank, damp, and smelly hallways to get to your room; loved the NO DOOR in the open-concept shower (best part of whole room) and the overhead rain shower head; we had a jr. suite that seemed dated even though it was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""modern concept""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""...room only had - flat screen tv that was not HD and very old looking, that you had to spin to see in the living area and then spin back to see in the bedroom with a cutout hole in the wall; no coffee machine in room; a lamp was on the floor like a table had been taken; bathroom counters were not that clean; bed was NOT comfortable or plush--just a single mattress w-o a box spring; lotion and soaps were nothing special; and even though we stayed in the hotel, we still couldnt get a reservation for dinner nor brunch at their famous Blue Duck tavern...so we had the tea room menu in the lounge which was very good; staff was not attentive nor friendly at the front desk...was looking for a hotel that was a little more hip and edgy than the usual Ritz......this hotel is more modern themed but lacks the luxury and cleanliness and attentiveness of the Ritz

Our first time in Point Loma and we're going back again in the summer. We loved this place, very nice room with roomy bathroom, comfy beds, lot of space for hanging clothes and storing our suitcases. We faced the Holiday Inn but could also see the harbor, so nice. They had a nice lobby to sit in, free warm cookies every afternoon plus constant free coffee and tea in the lobby. Breakfast room was usually busy but for a reason, lots of free food like yogurt, cereal, toast, waffles, coffee, four different juices, fruit, hard boiled eggs, etc. Free shuttle from -am to - pm and the day we left the van was down so they paid for a cab for us to the airport, nice. Lots of nice restaurants within walking distance, Pizza Nova, Jimmy's Famous, Point Break, Red Sails, Mitch's Seafood, etc and also within walking distance to Liberty Station with Trader Joe's, Panera Bread, Five Guys and beautiful grounds (it was the Naval Training Station before being renovated). Great staff especially Jason who always seemed to be there with a smile and friendly attitude. Other staff worked very hard to keep the place clean. The only complaint we have is that we could smell smoke when our patio door was open as they allow smoking on the sixth floor, we were on -rd floor so it may have come from the parking lot below us. All in all, we loved it and have reservations to return in the summer.

We stopped by to see if they had a room. When we asked if his price was the best he could do, he got mad. We asked to see a room (because of previous reviews we wanted to see a room.) He was too busy to show us. We ended up walking out to find another hotel. We refuse to spend our hard earned money with someone who treats us that way.

We stayed at the Radisson Los Angeles Airport for - nights, both which were pleasantly uneventful and comfortable. This hotel is the closest one to the airport, literally next door, so if you wanted to walk over, you could. The hotel also runs a shuttle every -- minutes to LAX, though ours ran late so you may want to allow a bit of extra time.
We were checked-in quickly, and without problems. This hotel was procured on Priceline and we were able to check-in at noon. We received our request for - beds, and much to my delight, they were *not* Sleep Number beds. The front desk made no mention of this at check-in, and I'm wondering if they are being removed from the chain's hotels? The keycard still prominently displays an ad for the Sleep Number...
The room was nicely furnished, in typical Radisson ways. The beds had nice mattresses and plenty of pillows, though I had to call down for a foam one. Our room also included a desk and TV stand. Bathrooms were also regularly furnished and designed. There was also free wireless internet in the room, which is always a great addition. Airport noise could sometimes be heard in the room, especially during the day though rarely at night.
We enjoyed the pool area on this trip, though it was a little hard to find (we had to ask). There is a sign pointing to a sitting area in the lobby with the words 'Pool' on it. We found out that you have to go through the door to the outside, walk to your left around stairs and a parking lot and you will see the white fence that encloses it. It was never busy and had lots of lounge chairs, though the second day we went down there were no towels until after --am, which was a bit inconvenient. 
Parking was available at the hotel under two different options - $-- for self or $-- for valet. We coughed up the extra $- to have them park it for the night, though it looked like self-parking was relatively close by. The hotel also contained a restaurant, which we did not sample.
Overall, our stay was good. I find the LAX area to be cheap and mildly central when it comes to going to different areas in Los Angeles. I never have a problem with any of the hotels here, and this is no exception. Another satisfied airport stay.

This is the second time we have stayed in this hotel. This time we stayed in the regular hotel room. I think everything could use an update, but as far as cleanliness and location this is a great place to unpack your suitcase. It is so close to Central Park and all the great shopping. There are lots of great places to eat within walking distance and the subway stop isn't far if you need it. Broadway is more of a cab ride for those dressing up and not wanting to walk that far. There is a ticket booth located in the hotel. We have purchased last minuite tickets there...you do pay about $-- more per ticket. It's pretty hassel free if you decide on something last minute. We just got back from our stay at the W union square. Our fourth visit this year and it keeps getting better. Wonderful location and staff. Can not wait for our next visit

The staff taking care of our bags litterally stole our money when we were getting our bags. The service in the Hilton Garden Inn Northwest restaurant is superb. Particularly noteworthy is the service and attention to detail by your server, Maria Ramirez. She is a credit to your hotel, without doubt. She is either just a natural, or your training is great, or both. 
We had a great experience here, and it was it large part due to the great service we received in your restaurant!
Jim Hudman

We picked the Embassy Suites Washington Convention Center since it's right next to the NYC-DC bus drop off. Location is very convenient. It's within walking distance to all of the museums, and also close to Metro station if you need to take the train somewhere. 
We have originally booked a non-smoking king bed suite through hotels.com. However, when we checked in, we were told that all of the non-smoking rooms were unavailable . Instead, we were asked to take a smoking room, and housekeeping would bring in a air purifier to help reduce the smell. Since it was already --pm, we didn't argue and agreed to take the room. The staff was nice enough to give us $-- certificate toward the hotel restaurant to compensate for the inconvenience. That made us feel a little better, and since we were only staying one night, we didn't mind it that much. 
The room itself was pretty nice. Very spacious with a separate sitting area outside of the bedroom. However, we discovered that instead of a king bed, there were - twin beds in the room. I went to check out the pool. Since I got that extra early (around -:--am on a Sunday), there was virtually nobody there. The water was nice and I had a good work out there.

We originally thought the hotel would be catered more to business crowd since it's close to the convention center. However, i guess the extra space and separate sitting around would be attractive to families as well, so be prepared if you are in town for a holiday weekend.

We stayed for a week at the Hotel Rouge. You can literally look down the street and see the White House. We rented a Prius and parked at the hotel, as they offer --- off parking if you rent a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""green"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" car. Only two things bothered me: when parking the car, you have to valet, and there's no good strategy for tipping the valet...should you tip each time? Although we were there for a week and saw the same people over and over, not one ever greeted us by name or asked us, for instance, if we'd had a nice day. I stayed here for one night with my girlfriend in August ---- after arriving at Seattle Airport after a flight from London Heathrow. This was a great base after a long flight and was only a - min drive in the free hotel shuttle from the airport.
The hotel is massive and it must have taken us five minutes to walk from the reception to our hotel room! We had a large room with two double beds, desk, dressing table, large TV with a balcony overlooking the car park. 
Everything in the room and bathroom was clean and modern so inline with what we expected (and the warm cookie was a nice touch!)
If we flew to Seattle again, we would stay here for our first night again.

I was intrigued to book a stay here after seeing the magnificent pics on this website and especially after getting an incredible discount on my stay thru Expedia. I am always attracted to romantic, historical hotels and always try to at least check them out when I'm in a given town. Upon arriving here, the valets treated me like royalty and helped me carry my bags and were only too happy to help, even when I didn't have any cash readily available for a tip. They seemed genuinely happy to make my two night stay as wonderful as possible. When I saw the gorgeous and super elegant lobby and common areas at check-in, I knew I had arrived! The front desk staff was as deferential and helpful as the valets and my check-in was problem free from the get-go. The room was meticulously clean and beautiful, not to mention huge, a whopping --- sq. feet and it was only the deluxe, not superior room. The bathroom was elegantly up to date and very tastefully decorated in a tuscany, Italian marble theme. The rooms are appointed with antique lamps that look like cloisonne-Asian vases and I couldn't have felt more comfortable. Though the hotel dates from ----, the electrical outlets work very well, unlike with some historic hotels and though I can't speak for the wi-fi or internet hook-up performance, everything worked!!! I ordered several room service items and they came promptly and the servers were very courteous and bent over backwards to please.
I have to be honest, I had some trepidation in booking this hotel, as I had read many neg. reviews regarding the thin walls and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lack of privacy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" due to poor insulation. Well, I am the original light sleeper and was prepared for hearing sounds of amourous couples, loud tvs and terrible street noise on Akard Street. I have to say that I spent two very quiet nights at the hotel, despite an apparent near full capacity. There was a girl's pre-wedding event going on and I thought, oh no, lots of partying into the night and noise. AGAIN, I didn't hear a thing from anyone, it seemed that no one else was even on my floor; though there appeared to be lots of cars in the garage. I have to say that this was a spectacular experience and you have to stay here at least once. Some nuttos who h ave reviewed this place, have said that it is dated and worn. Not only am I a light sleeper, I am also a hotel snob, and believe you me, this place is a tour de force; I have stayed in the world's best hotels and this one is near the top of the list. Elegance, courtesy, and an alluring history make this a wonderful place to stay. I got a tremendous deal on Expedia and would recommend that you check there for excellent package rates (I paid $--- for a three day car rental AND two nights at this hotel), you can't beat that. I was charged $-- for two days of parking my car ($-- per day), but they did NOT charge me extra hundreds of $ on my debit card, as others have said. There is an $-- per day """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""incidental expenses"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" charge which I didn't like, but apparently, since I prepaid the room, they did not actually charge me, go figure.
John, the concierge is a wonderful asset to the hotel and I just can't say enough about my experience here. If this place is good enough for Donald Trump and Queen Elizabeth, believe me, you won't feel any less special here! AWESOME EXPERIENCE.
P.S. I did not get a chance to dine at the French Room, as it was closed on the days I was there (closed on Sundays and Mondays). I will be sure to hit it up next trip. If anyone tries it, please let me know. What a knock-out that restaurant is, much like the hotel itself.

Very nice hotel, recently renovated. Apparently the old place was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""roach motel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", but was recently gutted and completely redone over a - year period. Opened like a month or two before I stayed there.

I'd stay here again!

The Hotel Vitale is a great place to stay for a trip to San Francisco. My best friend and I went there over the Canadian thanksgiving long weekend (early October) and we truly had a wonderful time. The rooms are gorgeous - with the most comfortable beds and pillows (not to mention down duvets)! The hotel also doesn't have that """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hotel-like"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" aroma that most hotels have - it smells like lavendar in the hallways. 
I would highly reccommend taking a trip to the rooftop terrace, at night and during the day. The views of SF Bay Bridge and the Ferry Building and all along the Embarcadero are amazing - and the lounge seating up there is very comfortable! A great place to sit and relax after a day of sightseeing.
The staff at this hotel was wonderful - they even have a car service (comparable to the price of taxis -and the driver was much less crazy!). The staff are willing to help novice SF visitors in everyway possible. 
Must sees in SF:
- Fisherman's Wharf (Pier --) - we spent an entire day here! Lots of restaurants (mostly seafood) - but the best thing to eat were the hot dogs from the food stands. The aquarium is very cool, and the sea lions are stinky, but are a must (just following the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""barking"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""").
- Alcatraz evening tour - seeing the sun set over the Golden Gate bridge from the ferry and the island was incredible. Also Alcatraz isn't as creepy as you may think it is - it's very interesting and full of history - and worth it just for the views of the city of SF.
- Chinatown - really neat shops with interesting finds.
- Union Square - all of the designer shops are located here - I was really impressed with Macy's!
- Ocean Beach - it's a long haul from the Hotel Vitale (on the MUNI - their subway-transit system) - but worth it just for the beautiful sounds, sights, and smells of the Pacific. Be aware though - there isn't too many places to eat around Ocean Beach - so eat before you go!

We stayed over one night and booked through Hotwire. We got a room with - full beds which is sort of odd. Though the room was comfortable and clean. 
 Parking is --$ in an overnight garage, but you can come and go as you please. Also, the parking is very tight. 
 What we liked was the close proximity to their train system. It was about - blocks away. 
Overall, it was a fine stay for one night.

I have become so addicted to Tripadvisor that I always check first before making reservations be it for business or leisure.

Amazing- if I go back to Dallas, I'm staying there.

Stayed here New Year's Eve and rented the penthouse and adjoining double room. Kimpton hotels are usually pretty good but this one was wonderful. Embarcadero location is great, hotel ambience & decor is very nice, rooms & hallways were spotless, service was very good (tough test on NYE weekend) but having the top room and fantastic SF Bay views was the reason we stayed here for NYE. Watching the fireworks on the Bay, felt like we were in the middle of the show and was spectacular. Prices are usually reasonable (for SF). Be warned though, the rooms are small, even the Penthouse was not huge, but all in all, a good hotel & if you get a view room - wonderful.
Nice hotel, clean rooms with a great beds. Wish the shuttle to Easton Center was available more often, but other than that no complaints.

Although the lobby area is in need of updating we had a refurbished room on the Executive Floor which was quiet, clean, spacious and well appointed. Because it was Labour Day weekend the Executive Lounge was not fully operational and we were advised of this at the time of booking. However, we weren't told the the restaurant would be closed except for the breakfast service.
The hotel is convenient for the White House and is within easy walking distance of - Metro stations and some good restaurants.
We'd certainly stay here again.

Driving to West Texas and stayed here. I was better than I expected. clean rooms. Staff was helpful ..good place to stay so you do not hit that wild traffic. I would stay here again, good value. Found the hotel on trip advisor while driving

For my work trip here in Round Rock I used Hotwire to find a room and this was the place that was selected and I'm pleased. The whole place feels clean and new. Everything in the room was neat and in good working condition including the free WiFi.

The neighborhood was fine and I felt completely safe at the hotel. Maybe if you're not used to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""urban"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" areas, you might it a bit of a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""shock"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", but it's completely fine.

You don't have to feel like you're Japanese or into Anime to really enjoy the main part of the experience. NEWLY REMODELED ROOMS AT A GREAT RATE... now in San Francisco, that means a lot. Quality hotel accomodations without having to shell out a fortune. Everything in the room is new, including the bathroom fixtures, tiles, floor, etc... 
The room (#---) had a great view (West) so we were able to appreciate a beautiful sunset over the hills. The hotel is just across the street from the main plaza in Japantown so """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""convenient"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is an understatement. It's close to restaurants, theater, the Kubuki bath house, parking, the center of the city, and just about all the main attractions in San Francisco. 
If I were wealthy and money were no object, I might stay somewhere else, perhaps with complete royalty treatment, spa included. But for me, the average traveler on a tight budget, I felt pampered. Perhaps even somewhat surprised that i had found this clean, beautiful room with a FANTASTIC view for only $----night. 
The staff is friendly.

I can consider myself now a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""regular"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" at the Hotel Tomo.

Ms. Alicia Olcese, a manager on duty, was especially helpful in providing extra necessities for my room and by providing a wealth of information about the city. She is definitely as asset to the company and a positive example for the employees on her shift.
The room was clean and welcoming, especially after touring the city all day! The cleaning crew did and excellent job of providing fresh towels and toiletries and were curteous.
Overall, I'd give my stay at Comfort Inn Downtown - stars for customer service, cleanliness, location, comfort and affordability. I will certainly recommend this hotel to anyone planning a trip to Philadelphia and indeed return there myself if ever in the city again!

Stayed here one night during a layover to ORD the next morning. Checkin was smooth and recognized my Platinum status even though I had reserved the room through a bidding site which allowed me free internet access. Room was clean and quiet. This was a last minute booking for a last minute trip. I booked an anonymous - ½ star at an attractive rate on Hotwire and was delighted to find it was the Madison. Out of curiosity, I went online later on the same day. The Madison website was offering rooms at a bit less than the Hotwire rate and the Marriott Wardman website offering rooms at $-- less than their “discounted” convention rate. The rooms at the Gansevoort are the hotel's best feature. I was on the -th floor and had a great Hudson river view, slight spoiled by the building of The Standard hotel but don't let it put you off! Colourwise, they're a neutral grey with olive, deep red and mustard accessories. Dark wooden furniture and comfy chairs in darker neutrals complete the look. The bathrooms are cool in marble and stainless steel, not too huge but large enough. The beds are LARGE and VERY comfortable. The rooms are well appointed with quality amenities and brands you'd recognise, unlike other hotels. We had a comfortable stay. I'm sure the smaller rooms are just as comfortable, if you keep yourself tidy! The Meatpacking District is a noisy neighbourhood but it wasn't a particular problem. However, I didn't stay on a Friday or Saturday night.
The rooftop pool is a great addition and it was lovely to be able to get into the pool in the New York heat. It was busy on an afternoon. The pool at Soho House across the road, that can be seen from The Gansevoort was very busy too so its probably a plus point that at The Gansevoort, only hotel guests can use the pool, whereas at Soho House, hotel guests and members are able to use their pool.
The rooftop bar, Plunge, however is looking a little tired and definitely in need of a refurb. There was a queue in the street every night of people wanting a taste of The Gansevoort without having to pay to stay. There is a great view of the Empire State Building, however, there are certainly many better looking bars in NYC.
The basement has a spa. The hydrotherapy pools are free for hotel guests to use and are a lovely way to end the day before getting ready for a night in NYC!
Its definitely worth a stay at The Gansevoort to explore the Meatpacking District. There are plenty of bars, restaurants, the newly opened High Line park and also surrounding areas with plenty of stuff to do before you've even headed further downtown or uptown! With regards to the other local hotel options, its Meatpacking, its all expensive, its not good value, but The Gansevoort is definitely good for the lovely comfortable rooms, the location and the pool, just hit and miss on the service.

I stayed at Hotel Whitcomb with my daughter in July of ----. The hotel is located just three blocks away from the edge of what I would call safe. There are just too many people with no where to go but up, hanging out in front of the hotel, begging, to feel completely safe. It is nice that the metro is directly outside the front door, but we found that the metro was not the most convenient way to travel, and used the bus instead. The Tenderloin district is only a few blocks away, and some of that traffic seems to cross too near Hotel Whitcomb. Ok, enough about the location. That was not the worst thing. The hotel is very tired. It desperately needs an overhaul. The lobby seems impressive at first, because it is vintage San Francisco, but upon closer inspection you see things falling apart and needing replacement. Our room was at the end of the hall, near a very loud stairway door that opened up a lot during the night - waking me up. The windows in our room were so thin, that I could literally hear the conversations going on three floors down on the sidewalk. There is a terrible echo effect in cities, where the buildings are close together, so the windows need to be soundproof. It sounded like people were yelling at each other all night, but it was just the combination of the echo and the thin windows. Our bed was not comfortable, and the pillows were flat. We were very cold the first night, and had to request additional blankets. The TV remote control only worked it you pressed the channel changing button in just the right way - sometimes taking upward of -- taps to change from one station to the next. All the appliances were very old and tired. 
Finally, I am very affected by color, and there was one thing that stands out to me over everything else when I think back to my experience at the Whitcomb. The royal blue trim in our room. Just the thought of someone spending hours staring at royal blue as they detailed the crown molding, chair rail molding, doors, and baseboards is nauseating. It sure was hard to look at.

The Hotel staff were very friendly. I booked a suite and requested a view. I got a suite but a view of a brick building. It was extremely hot and the hotel does not have vending machines. The restuarant does not sell bottled water.

That's not to say the room wasn't clean -- just that housekeeping was erratic and kind of unobservant. For instance, the clock in my room stopped working -- it was blinking back and forth from a blank screen to scrambled color bars -- so I took to turning it face-down on the table (you couldn't unplug it) and putting a newspaper over it. And every day housekeeping would come by and turn it upright again, yet apparently never seemed to notice that it was broken despite that being glaringly obvious. Now, in fairness, I never remembered to call about it, so I'm sure the hotel would've sent someone up to fix it, but it is also sort of indicative of my experience with housekeeping here that they repeatedly put the clock back in place and never did anything about it being so clearly broken. They also didn't regularly empty wastebaskets, and the room smelled like smoke when I arrived. It took two calls down to the front desk to get a remote fixed. Stuff like that. They just were kind of spacey.
However, the front-desk staff and the bellhops were super nice -- in fact, the housekeepers were nice too -- and the hotel is in a great location, right near both the red and blue lines on the subway and with tons of good eateries around, plus an all-night deli across the street that makes great sandwiches. The bed was comfortable, and if the pictures of the bathroom with the glass wall freak you out, it's okay: There is a motorized shade you can put down with the flip of a switch. The chair at the tiny table is ridiculously uncomfortable -- the pad they put it on it is not large enough, so the metal frame dug into my legs; classic example of choosing design over comfort -- but you can solve that by sitting on the leather banquette instead, which also has two drawers underneath it that were ideal for storing clothes. The closet size was fine, but there are never enough hangers in hotels, and this was no exception.
We will totally stay here again, though. All these are things that can be lived with or corrected.

I took my mom to NY to celebrate her --th birthday (June -----). I gave her the option of the Sofitel or a larger hotel. She looked at the online photos and selected the Sofitel because it was smaller and looked nice.

Considering the average size of a NY hotel room (very small) the room was large. The bathroom was well-appointed and we liked the updated style of separate shower and tub.
The staff was friendly and helpful. I liked the fact that there was a cubby hole in the lobby with three computers and a printer. Free of charge, you could access the Internet and print boarding passes. 
Although I had read other reviews that it would be difficult for the doorman to hail a cab, we did not find that to be the case. The staff was knowledgeable about the area and offered ideas on shopping areas where we could find bargains.
The one problem we had was with our room service the first night. We ordered the lobster bisque and did not like it. I was hesitant but decided to call room service to let them know we didn't like it. They sent someone to get the bowls and credited our bill without any hassle. 
Also, be aware that the minibar has a sensor on it. When something is removed your are charged but the sensor does not detect if you return something to the bar. I removed a diet Coke and changed my mind. I immediately returned it to the bar and selected a regular Coke. When I noticed that I was charged for two, I contacted the front desk and they told me about the sensor. They removed the second charge without any hassle.
I would recommend it to anyone and would stay there again. We got good value for your money.

For a good restaurant and 'San Diego' experience, try Casa Guadalajara in San Diego old town - it's very reasonably priced and you get a very good meal along with singing mariachis and strong frozen margaritas. Thoroughly recommended

THE BAD…
I'm a bit baffled by the other posted reviews... For my family, $---.-- per night included: unwashed sheets, cigarette burned comforters, sticky floors, broken amenities and dark, cramped and dingy rooms (see the pictures).
I can imagine when it was new this hotel was probably quite a gem. The atrium-style design and glass elevators were very popular in the --s and --s, but now it just seems DATED AND DIRTY. You can tell that they've attempted to “update” the actual rooms with darker wood, granite counter tops and newer furniture, but they missed the mark entirely by choosing pieces that were cheap, over-sized and ill-suited for travelers. And then, they FAILED to properly clean or maintain those updates (more on that later)…
FURNITURE--To be honest, I felt like I was in a furniture liquidation warehouse our entire stay- squeezing around unnecessary chairs, tables, stools, etc…There were THREE large sinks in the suite -one in the bathroom, one for the bar, and another randomly taking up space in the cramped bedroom. This was ironic because the lone tiny closet had four hangers and could probably only hold ten at most, (because when traveling, having multiple hand-washing options is more important than a place to put your clothes?)…
When the hideaway sofa was pulled out, there was barely enough room to squeeze your legs through to walk around to put the (dirty) sheets on it… There was a large desk-table with a desk chair on one side and two """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""waiting room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" style chairs on the other. This would be convenient for families to eat a quick snack or meal- that is, if there were room to sit down! We had to actually climb over and INTO the chairs to sit at the table squeezed between the wall and TV...Okay, okay, so you get it. The suites are either too small or just crammed with too much furniture. Either way, we were uncomfortable and tripping over everything and everyone the whole time. By the way, we (my husband, -- yr old daughter and I) are not large people. Overall, the suite was dark. The ceilings felt low. Blah!
MAINTENANCE—although you could tell that there were “updates”, the entire hotel and room needed a good scrubbing, carpet shampooing and general maintenance. The laminate wood floor near the bar area in our suite crackled and creaked when you walked on it. The carpets were sticky. I only dared to walk barefoot once! The floor near the elevator was sticky enough to make our shoes stick. (I told the front desk and they eventually mopped it. WHY would I have to report this?) The windows in our suite were SO dirty that you could not see out- see the pictures!
BATHROOMS—when I stay at a hotel, I expect the bathroom to be pristine. (Who doesn’t? I don’t want to touch other people’s funk!) The vanity shelving where they put the “clean” towels was dusty and dirty, and the finish was worn and peeling. The toilet paper holder was improperly installed, so that the roll would fall off every time you tried to unroll the tissue. The exhaust fan (six inches above your head when showering) was COVERED in clumps of dirty and dust- see the pictures! The multiple-stream massaging shower head could not be adjusted. I assume this is because it had not been cleaned-ever!
BEDDING—another thing I expect when checking into any hotel (especially for $---.-- per night) is CLEAN bedding… We arrived late in the evening, unpacked, and climbed into bed to find DIRTY SHEETS, covered in someone else’s makeup-see the pictures! ACK! (I called to the front desk any they apologized and politely brought me a pile of replacement bedding.) Imagine my surprise to unfold the new bedspread and find not one, not two, but THREE giant cigarette burns- see the pictures! It was close to midnight, so in desperation, I pulled the extra bedding from the top of the closet (-rd time’s a charm?) and found a nasty, cheap, flame-retardant blanket that was so sticky and stiff, it made NOISE when I tried to unfold it...Fortunately, we had brought an extra blanket along on our trip and used that to sleep that night. INSANE, UNNECESSARY, INEXCUSEABLE! At this point, I was ready to change hotels, but we had friends staying there as well and decided to stick it out. Who hasn’t stayed in a fleabag hotel at one time or another? We survived, but will NEVER return! 
OTHER IRRITATIONS TO NOTE—when we travel, we tend to have tons of electronics to charge- laptops, cell phones, camera batteries, etc. I attempted to slide the TV over on the bedroom credenza to reach one of the few plugs, and found that it was bolted down like a cheap motel. Ironically, the bedside lamps were NOT bolted down, so when we wanted to turn the light off before bed, I had to use two hands to push the sticky button and keep the lamp from sliding off the night table. Yes, I’m being picky now, but who wants to get IN bed and then realize you have to get OUT of bed to turn off the lamp? -just another example of thoughtless design…
THE GOOD?—
Unfortunately, there isn’t much good to report, other than the made to order breakfast was good, and the dining hostesses were polite. However, the largest cup available for drinks was a coffee cup. If you wanted juice or soda, you were stuck with a --oz Dixie-style cup. This is pretty standard for hotels that include breakfast, but I’d imagine three wasted tiny cups would cost MORE than one larger cup for juice. (I’m being picky again. I probably wouldn’t be if everything else were in order. It wasn’t and I’m a contributor on Tripadvisor. Soo…)
The desk clerk that checked us in was also very polite. The hotel was booked, but he still remembered to offer us the bottles of water afforded by our Silver Club Member status. (See? We stay in enough Hilton hotels to know when things are sub-par!)
Finally, the hotel is close to a Target, multiple dining options and highways, but there are many other options nearby. The flaws at this Embassy are MANY, but easily remedied. I think that’s why I was soo disappointed! We’re not talking about million-dollar fixes, just SOAP and EFFORT. Shame on Embassy Suites Memphis. $---.-- X - night for an experience worse than Motel -! Booo!

Great rooms, friendly staff, and not far from Foggy Bottom Metro stop and as close as you can get to Georgetown!
