Our first room had the worst plumbing I have ever seen. When we turned on 
the shower there was almost no pressure as the water continued to leak 
from the tub faucet as well as both the hand and fixed shower heads. 
The shower head was loose so it shook when the water came out and the 
tub didn't drain so I was standing in ankle deep water after about 
three minutes while the shower just sort of leaked on me. We called 
to complain and were told there was no other room that we could be 
given until the next night. They sent up maintenance and he said that 
many of the bathrooms had the same problem but he hadn't seen it quite 
that bad in other rooms. He said it couldn't be fixed and that it 
would involve taking the whole shower and bath apart to even try to 
fix it. He spoke to the manager and they put us in another room, 
which had miraculously come available. There were other minor
disappointments in the first room as well. The iPod connection cable 
was missing from the technology kit that they put in the rooms, the 
menu on the TV didn't respond to the remote - if you pressed the up 
button it would just start flying through the menu (not scrolling item 
by item) so you couldn't select the item you wanted.
Our new room is not a whole lot better. The bathroom is like 
something out of a cheap motel. The tub is chipped (the tub in the 
first room was chipped too!) and the shower pressure is pretty poor. 
The shower curtain is not long enough to stay in the tub, so the floor 
gets soaked. There is a vent over the shower so when you shower you 
have ice cold air blowing on you. The toilet keeps running because the 
flush mechanism doesn't spring back up after it's pressed down. The 
knobs on the sink appear broken - they don't line up and as soon as 
you turn them on there is a forceful stream of water that hits the 
back of the very poorly designed sink so that it splashes out and all 
over the back of the vanity and mirror - and our toiletries which we 
put on the vanity. The way the sink is designed, you have to reach 
into the basin to push a spring-loaded stopper to fill and drain the 
sink, which means that you have to reach into a sink of hot, dirty 
water after shaving to drain the water out. The way the faucet is 
designed, the water runs down the back of the sink so when you brush 
your teeth you end up with spit-out tooth paste on the stopper that 
you then have to rinse away with a glass of water because the water 
doesn't flow over the middle of the sink. You also can't fill the 
iron because the sides of the sink are too high and the iron doesn't 
fit under the faucet.
Also, the technology in the rooms doesn't work well at all. They 
lighting and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""moods"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" are controlled by the touch screens on the 
phone. The screens don't really respond, so to dim the lights you 
have to keep tapping repeatedly on each icon until it finally responds 
to the command. We tried using the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""moods"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on the TV which is a cool 
idea - it dims the lights and gives you a choice of music to set the 
mood in the room accordingly. There is only - mood...classical...and 
it doesn't dim all the lights in the room. You can hook your ipod or 
computer up to the room to play music, but instead of putting speakers 
in the room they have the music playing through the TV - the sound 
quality is awful! There is also an alarm clock with an ipod doc that 
has better sound quality than the TV, but it kept shorting out and 
restarting my ipod, so we ended up just dimming the lights manually 
and putting a classical album on through the speakers of the 
computer. It's like they had great ideas for the hotel and ran out of 
money implementing them. The lights and moods through a touch panel 
is a great idea, but it's like they skimped on the server so it 
doesn't respond to the commands. The little touches are missing that 
you would expect from a hotel of this type. They have greeters at the 
elevators (for security, I know) but they don't have anyone opening 
the doors to the hotel - even when we checked in with our luggage or 
came back with big shopping bags, we had to open the doors from the 
street to the lobby ourselves. There is no turn down service, etc. 
Personally, I would prefer to stay in a hotel that has a functional 
bathroom and lights (at TV and alarm clock) that work without all the 
complicated unresponsive menus than to have automatic footlights under 
the night tables and a computerised """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""do not disturb"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sign. I think 
they've put way too much emphasis on style (flashy technology and a 
grand lobby) and not a whole lot on functionality and substance. The 
beds are very comfortable and the room is clean, but you can say the 
same about most hotels in NYC that are much cheaper. Of course, the 
location is excellent, but I don't think I'd stay again. 
For the price we paid, which was well below the rack rate, it was fine, but I hate to think that there are people who saved up to stay here at full 
price on a dream NY holiday...if that were me I would be very 
disappointed and I probably would have tried to go elsewhere.

I stayed at this hotel on the nights of June - through - along with my quiz bowl team for the National Academic Championship. When our team arrived, our coaches got us checked in and distributed the room keys to us, and we proceeded to go upstairs to our designated rooms. (This ---story hotel has - pretty quick elevators, so we never had to wait too long to get from floor to floor.)
We got off the elevator on our floor, -, which we quickly found out was the hotel’s smoking floor. The smoke smell in the hallway was pretty overpowering. Luckily, our room, ---, was the first room on the right once you got off the elevator. The smell was still perceivable in the room, but it was definitely milder than it was in the hallway. The funny thing about the room was that it was a one-bedroom suite with one queen bed in the bedroom. Since we were already cramming - people in each room, we were expecting a room with two double beds. Our coaches talked to the desk staff and found out that it was being taken care of; they were sending a rollaway bed up. So now we had a queen bed, a sofa bed, and a rollaway bed – enough to sleep three of the four of us. Luckily, one of us didn’t mind sleeping on the floor (he said he actually sleeps better on the floor than in a bed or on a couch), so that kind of worked itself out. What I don’t understand is this: the reservations had been in the system for several months (they had probably already been made in late ’--), so how did they run out of non-smoking rooms with two double beds AND non-smoking one-bedroom suites? Did every guest in that hotel for those nights honestly have a reservation dating as far back as the National Academic Championship reservations? (I can only assume that the people in charge of our reservations would have booked us all non-smoking rooms; we’re high school students, after all.)
Besides the issue of cigarette smoke, the room itself wasn’t too bad. There was no wired internet access, but the wireless worked fine, despite being just a bit slow. The furniture was kind of beaten-up but still functional, and the carpet, though really dark and dated, appeared clean. The bathroom was pretty roomy, and the bathtub was perfectly clean. The one thing that grossed me out a little was this: one time when I used a tissue to dry off a drop of water I’d spilled on the bathroom floor, the tissue came up grayish-black, reflecting a poor cleaning job on the part of the hotel’s housekeeping people. The floor didn’t LOOK dirty, but I guess that was an illusion created by the type of tile they used. The moral: wear shoes when you walk into the bathroom. (The bathroom door also had some very weird-looking damage near the bottom of it [see photo], but that’s merely cosmetic and didn’t affect the cleanliness or functionality of the room, so I didn’t really see it as a huge negative.)
The hotel is located very close to the O’Hare airport, which can be really convenient for travelers... until you try to get to sleep. Planes flew right over the hotel frequently, ----. The hotel’s noisy, old, window-style air conditioning unit helped drown out some of the plane noise, so I got to sleep after a while. When I woke up, I found that despite the great selection of pillows, the bed itself hadn’t exactly been great on my back. They probably decided to use the same old mattresses that the hotel had been using as a Ramada, which probably date back to the days when it was a Clarion.
We had the only suite out of everyone from our school, so it was basically our meeting place whenever we needed to get together for breakfasts, practices, or just relaxation-downtime. The first two mornings, we had breakfast in the suite; our assistant coach went to Dominick’s (right across the interstate from the hotel) and got milk, juice, doughnuts, bagels, and other items so we could eat right in our room without paying the ungodly $--.-- per person for the basic breakfast buffet offered by the hotel. The in-room mini-fridge and microwave proved very useful for this; we could just store the milk and juice in there until breakfast the next day. The third morning, we did eat at the hotel’s breakfast buffet, which had a decent variety and tasted excellent. I don’t know if I’d call it $--.-- worth of food, as Holiday Inn Expresses offer a wider variety of similar-quality items for free every day, but it was definitely satisfying. We also ate at the lunch buffet at the hotel’s restaurant on the second day; the food was amazing. They offered salad with fresh, healthy-looking lettuce and a variety of dressings; pasta with alfredo and spicy marinara sauces available; delicious well-seasoned grilled chicken breasts that tasted like they just came off the grill; and bread and butter. (I’m probably forgetting something, but everything I had was incredibly good, and I can be kind of a picky eater sometimes.)
One night we thought about taking a swim in the hotel’s “heated” outdoor pool, but it didn’t seem very heated at all – way too cold to swim in, for sure. On the opposite end of the scale, though, were the hotel’s common areas near the meeting rooms on the second floor. I guess the A-C must not have been working or something, but it was ridiculously hot and humid outside the Ontario and Huron rooms. It was just as hot most of the time inside Ontario and Superior A. The other rooms we used (Superior B and C and Michigan) were fine. (We never used the Huron room, so I don’t know about the temperature of that room.) I also swung by the fitness center on the second floor just to check it out, and despite both window A-C units being on their coldest temperatures and highest fan settings, the room felt pretty warm.
Our assistant coach, a Priority Club member, mentioned to us that she wanted to see if she could get the Priority Club points for all of our rooms put on her account. (She wasn’t the one who had paid for the rooms, but the person who had paid for them wasn’t a Priority Club member or just had no interest in getting the points.) I mentioned that I was also a Priority Club member, and she agreed that I’d take the points for my suite and she’d take the points for our group’s other rooms. She managed to get the points put on her account by talking to the front desk. I tried to do so later on, but the woman at the front desk didn’t seem very informed. She told me that it was impossible to give the points to anyone except the person who paid for the rooms, which is obviously untrue, as our assistant coach was able to do that just fine. I feel like she was just trying to get rid of me because I’m “just a kid” (I’m -- years old, but I understand that some people mistakenly don’t view us as part of the adult community yet); she obviously wasn’t going to even try to do it, despite my telling her about how our assistant coach was able to do this with one quick visit to the front desk, so I had to walk away without the points.
Overall, our stay wasn’t too bad, but if I were choosing the hotel next time, I wouldn’t stay here again. The biggest problem is one that the hotel can’t really help – the location, right under the flight path of loud airplanes going to and coming from O’Hare – but besides that, there are so many little things (cold pool, unfriendly and-or uninformed desk staff, air conditioning problems, dirty bathroom floor, uncomfortable mattress, etc.) that would still keep me from returning.

-. Interesting to read the earlier reviews: my wife hated the place because it was ...

I would recommend this hotel for it's location, comfort and price and would stay here again. Wonderful hotel especially if you need to stay near Medical City Hospital.

Cold Water Problems:

We will definitely stay here again and dell our friends and family.

My wife and two young children concluded our week long get away by spending - nights at the Grand Del Mar (after spending the first - nights at the Ritz Carlton - Laguna Niguel). Where to start? The bedroom was not a bedroom. More like a loft. The only way to enjoy NYC. The staff are friendly, the food is excellent. The room service divine. I loved the Cow Shed Spa. Great steam room.

Great service and staff...we'll be back next April for the ---th Boston Marathon.

I stayed here while attending a conference. The overall appearance of the hotel was fine and my room was relatively comfortable. However, the poor service would keep me from returning. I stayed here recently when I had a job interview in Century City. I wanted a location that was close by. The Azul Inn is basically a renovated motel. The building's exterior isn't in great condition and it looks like a motel. This was a convenient home base from which I did a lot of prepping for my interview in the hotel room.
The Asian female hotel desk clerk at checkin was busy, stressed and not in a good mood. Guests did not receive a friendly welcome.
The free wi-fi was not working when I got to my room. I went downstairs to the lobby, they said they had recently reset the connection and to try it again in a few minutes. Then it worked fine. However, late that evening it stopped working again and wasn't working when I woke up the next morning. I asked them to restart the router again, waited, but it still didn't work. Fortunately, I was able to access the internet using my smartphone.
I requested a quiet room away from the street noise. They accommodated my request, however, a large building was being constructed behind the hotel. Due to this huge erection, enthusiastic jackhammering took place beginning at - am and they were still going at it strong when I checked out.
The mattress was a very comfortable and high quality Simmons Beautyrest WorldClass. I only know this because I accidentally yanked the sheet off the mattress during the middle of the night ;)
There were a number of eateries within a convenient distance. I walked ---- minutes to a healthy chicken - Indian restaurant near the corner of Westwood and Santa Monica Blvd. for dinner. I don't expect a free breakfast to be gourmet, and I was fine driving down to Westwood and Pico to Junior's where I ordered breakfast and lunch to go. 
The desk clerk at checkout was accommodating and agreed to let me to check out later than usual since I didn't need to be in Century City until - PM. 
I would recommend staying here for convenience and value, if you don't mind the temporary daytime construction noise. Don't count on the WI-FI working the entire time. Bring your smartphone if you need internet access.

Its not a bad place, its just averagely boring. Its clean, its cheap, and its located not too far from central Hollywood, and it has a nice pool area. Breakfast is included and consists of Homer Simpsons favorite doughnuts and coffee.
Just outside though... you might not want to walk very far, especially on your own, maybe a taxi could be your best option.

I stayed June ----- ----, and had booked a Priceline rate which (after taxes & fees) wound up being about $--- a night. (Not bad!)
I wanted to write this review because I had a really good experience. I booked this hotel, and then saw a mixed bag of reviews, several negative. It made me a little concerned, but I got there and had a very good time!
The Quick Version for the Attention-Span Impaired:
Very clean. Tastefully renovated. Slightly above basic comforts. Friendly staff. Awesome location.
The Long Version:
Location: 
Excellent! At the south end of the Mag Mile, about a block & a half north of the Wrigley Building. Great for shopping & dining. Cab from Union Station around $-, or the --- bus for $-. 
Lobby:
The bar takes up a good portion of the lobby. It's kind of cool-looking, with lots of seating. I did not patronize the bar, so can't review it. There is also a Starbucks, which I did frequent
and it was good.
Check In:
They had a lot of people working the front desk, so the wait was short. Although I had used Priceline, (and gotten a killer rate) I was not treated like a second rate or cheapo customer. I got a guy named Terrell or Terrence (can't remember) who seems to enjoy his job. He had a great smile and hooked me up with a nice lake-view room at my request. And, I was able to get right into my room - at noon, on a Friday, in the middle of tourist season, no less! My friend was coming in on another train and they added her name to the reservation, in case she got there while I was out shopping. Again, no hassle and happy to help. My front desk experience made me happy right off the bat, and from that moment, I expected the rest of my stay to be great. (And it was.)
Elevators: 
There are separate ones for lower & upper floors. Most of the time, the wait isn't anything significant. The only time I felt the wait was long-ish was Sunday morning, when you could see a lot of people were checking out. Even then, it wasn't ridiculous.
The Room, #----:
Was clean and pleasantly decorated. Air conditioning worked good. We had a lake-view and could see the sailboats on the water, as well as a view of the Tribune Tower. My friend and I both raved about the beds & pillows - so snuggly! We both slept like rocks. TV didn't have a lot of exciting options, but we didn't watch much other than the Weather Channel. (Who comes to Chicago to watch TV? Or hang out in their room for that matter...?) Was the room large? No. But it was not tiny, either. It was just fine for two people. It could probably could be a little tight for - people. 
Bathroom: Again, clean, tasteful, simple. Fine for two people, four would be tight. Nice hot water, water pressure a touch on the weak side, but not enough that I would complain. Bath & Body Works goodies - nice! Only complaint - wish it had a vent fan, in case anyone leaves the restroom smelling not so great. However, I think there is a fan when the shower runs, because it never fogged up in there, and there's a grate above the shower head.
Hallway - Walls:
Never heard much noise. 
Staff: 
Bellhop Michael """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""from Baltimore"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was a hoot. Concierges pretty nice, had good info. Front desk were all nice. Housekeeping efficient and quiet. 
Cannot comment on:
Bar, Restaurant, Gym, Pool, Internet. Didn't use 'em. 
So what's with all the complaints?
People complaining about valet parking, small hotel rooms - small bathrooms, slow elevators? Maybe they don't have a lot of experience traveling in big cities like Chicago or New York, where square footage costs money. Also, if you've ever been to a big Vegas hotel or a large convention, you understand how elevators work. This ain't NASA, and it does take a couple of minutes to make its way down from the --th floor. 
I will go back again.

This is a great boutique hotel. The price was right, the rooms are beautiful with high ceilings, nice linens, great service and perfect location. I'm looking forward to staying here on my next trip to NY.

We recently spent a weekend in Chicago and, through Trip Advisor reviews, found the Heart of Chicago Motel. The first attraction was the price, $-- for a one bed double, complimentary continental breakfast and FREE parking. What a bargain! Our room was clean and comfortable. For those with a longer stay--there is a grocery store just across the street (as well as a drugstore), along --nd. 
This was was very good and very reasonably priced hotel and I won't hesitate to go back to it if we ever get back to NYC. I would recommend it to anyone planning a visit to see a play or do sightseeing.

At least the very nice young lady working front desk Saturday morning gave us a voucher for $--.-- off the hotel buffet in apology for our circumstances when I complained. I stayed at the Hyatt Regency for two nights for a family trip to Chicago. We booked the hotel via phone with Hyatt central reservations. He further said that he would do us a great favor and take off the price of two of the four and also offer us two free the second day (which required us to purchase two more unless we let our kids watch us eat). Despite this, he would not comp all four for the first day. His attitude, as I perceived it, was not service oriented (unless the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I am gong to make you a great deal"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" [that costs you money] attitude is service), and he repeatedly said, only what is in writing matters. Essentially he was justifying lack of consistent verbal communication across Hyatt employees (though notably he would not admit our room came with comped internet, which we chose not to use based on the conversation with central reservations). The breakfast was not a small charge--$-- for four. It was nice but not that nice and we would have never purchased it if central reservations had not told us it was included (along with the local employee that said we would get four). This too, the manager simply did not understand (by his own words).
The short story is the negative reviews you read on TA are accurate. Hyatt (or at least this Hyatt) will gauge you such that you should have stayed elsewhere for a slightly higher rate and avoided the hassle (the Embassy Suites breakfast is comparable and all guests receive it). Also, the hotel may be technically a four star property but three stars would be more accurate so that should be considered when comparing rates. One bright spot was the excellent housekeeping. In sum, based on miscommunication, we were stuck with ~--.-- charge (half was comped) that was represented to us a free. Hopefully Hyatt will get their employees across offices-properties and email confirmations in sync for future guests. We will avoid Hyatt in the future based on this experience.

Reception staff are extremely friendly and helpful for all administration requirements, information and directions plus the offer of the hotel’s transport to local destinations. Next to the reception is a larder for drink and food snacks plus small travel items and along the corridor is an internet room. The Staybridge Suites are absolutely perfect for either an overnight stay or a longer visit to Memphis. Recommended.

Excellent place to stay when your traveling. They have a kitchen for your cooking needs etc. My family enjoyed it!

Brilliant thankyou Gustavano you made our stay memorable. All the best and I recommend this hotel to all as the location is great and the service was wonderful.

My goodness. It really surprises me that people feel that a - star hotel should be double its rating and also remain the price they paid.

Well done all you guys at the Hollywood Roosevelt from a very satisifed customer!!!!!

we stayed at this hotel from july -st thru the -th of ----. fairly close to everything we wanted to see. loved the free made to order breakfast , was a definite plus for this hotel. The room was a bit on the drab side and was'nt as clean as we would have liked it to be.

We stayed here because they accept pets, and it was in a convenient location. The hotel has plenty of parking, even on a busy holiday weekend. Fitness room equipment all worked, but it was old and very well-worn. We'd probably stay here again if we needed another pet-friendly hotel, but otherwise, it wouldn't be my first choice.

The location of this hotel is pretty good. It's close to the freeway and has a lot of food options in the area. They offer a daily breakfast that has more than bagels and muffins. Their cooks make tasty omelets with whatever you'd like. They'll also make other foods but it's not clearly indicated anywhere so you might think you can only order an omelet. In addition to the made to order food, they have fruits, oatmeal, cereal, bread for toast, muffins, bagels, coffee, various juices, and soda. All this is included, no additional fees! The attendants cleared dirty plates-glasses quickly and made sure the tables were wiped off right away to accommodate other diners.
The cons - the hotel itself is a little dated and the rooms still have tube televisions. The AC in our room was pretty loud and the people we traveled with had a loud clanking AC in their room. They contacted the front desk four times with no resolution. They also said their beds were like marshmallows, however, our bed was firm enough. The double beds are pretty small and could only be comfortable if used by one person (as opposed to a Queen bed). Parking was a little difficult to find most nights. 
I would recommend this hotel as it was still a good value, the breakfast was great, and they had a Managers Reception that offered free snacks and drinks. The bartender was very nice and attentive. There was a gift shop, the man there is really nice and helpful. The rooms were clean as was the rest of the public areas.

This Hotel Monaco, like others, is a unique hotel experience that surpasses your average, standard, nice hotel. If you like the large chain hotels (i.e. Hilton, Hyatt, etc.) and prefer that type of standard room and amenities, do not stay at the Monaco. In my opinion, those hotels, while nice, begin to all look the same after some time. However, if you prefer a smaller, boutique-type hotel with surprising, unique and whimisal rooms, you'll love it here.
The service at the front desk was excellent. The wine happy hour was very nice, serving local Snoqualamie wines. My room was wonderful with a wall of windows and window seats. I was happy to discover that windows also lined the wall of the bathroom - which I have never enjoyed in a hotel. (It is nice to have some natural light in a bathroom!)
The Monaco offers an easy walk to the waterfront, shopping and Pike Place Market. One point worth mention: if you are walking to the waterfront, do not walk down the street at the corner of the hotel - the sidewalk there is very steep downwards. Instead, walk down -th street towards the Market, and head down to the waterfront a few blocks down - the sidewalks are not so steep and scary there. 
And while you are staying at the Monaco, do not miss going inside the Seattle Public Library across the street. It is an architectual masterpiece and definitely not your average """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""library."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Tours are also given daily.
I've stayed at other Monaco hotels and thoroughly enjoyed this one, like the others. Any time I have the opportunity to stay at a Kimpton hotel, I will. I might also say, though, that the Kimpton Hotel Vintage Park, up the street from Monaco in Seattle, is not as impressive, but stays true to the unique hotel experience. If you have a choice, go Monaco.

I will evaluate this hotel with respect to the following: overall feeling of the hotel, location, quality of room and amenities. To give you perspective on the reason for our visit, my husband and I stayed here for a weekend visit to Chicago.
Overall feeling of the hotel – Like others have said, it’s a clubby, lounge type of atmosphere. The W hotel is intended to be trendy, so if you book this hotel, expect that type of atmosphere. The lobby itself is impressive, with extremely high ceilings and modern furniture. In the background you’ll hear lounge-club type music (no matter what time of day), and the entire lobby is dimly lit---just a little bit of light, the rest of the room is illuminated by candles. The lobby looks decently maintained, i.e., it is clean and everything seems to be in good shape (furniture, floor, walls, etc.). 
The people who work here all dress in black and have earphones to communicate with each other. I think the intended look here is “cool and trendy”—to match the furniture and lighting scheme, though to me it seemed a bit overdone and contrived. The guys out front sometimes open doors for you, sometimes do not, depending on how close they were to the door as you approached. The front desk staff and concierges seem to be friendly and courteous, interested in making sure you have a nice stay. 
So my first impression is that this hotel had a bit of attitude. Not anything to run away from, but something to keep in mind. 
Location – ‘The Loop’ is dead during the weekends, as my husband and I have come to find out. You are within walking distance to the elevated rail system (to Midway, which is convenient if you flew in from there), the Sears Tower, the Art Institute, and Millennium Park. That was about it though. If you wanted to go bar-hopping, window shopping, or have more than - or - choices as far as places to eat, you would have to either take the L, hop a cab, or walk. If you didn’t, you’d be bored out of your mind once evening hit. If you’re only in Chicago for a weekend AND want to explore the city at night (without having to take the L everywhere), I’d suggest booking elsewhere. The neighborhood is a ghost town on the weekends which actually was a bit scary when you factor in the numerous beggars floating through the streets.
Quality of Room – The hallways leading to the rooms were way too dark. If I were a vampire, this type of darkness would’ve been perfect. The rooms were tiny, though I was OK with the size—we’re in the city, after all. The room itself was worn down. You could see the paint on the radiator units chipping away and the walls were a bit dirty and worn. The hotel room seemed clean, though it felt dingy---almost like there was a coating of dirt and grime that had been left uncleaned for so long, it just became part of the place. Hard to explain. The lighting was barely adequate. Even with all the lights on (one of which did not work), you still yearned for a bit more light. The bed was extremely comfortable, probably the most comfortable of all hotels I’ve ever stayed at. We had an abundance of pillows too, which for me, was great. There is only one phone in the room, and it is on the desk, which is a walk away from the bed. It would’ve been nice to have a phone on the nightstand table. The walls were paper thin—and if you have a room that can be joined to another, request a different room. My husband and I could make out exact words and phrases of the people in the room next to us. 
The bathroom was a decent size (relatively speaking), as was the closet. Water pressure (shower) was weak, though that might’ve been because they had that rain spray shower head. The towels were really rough, but plentiful. You get a bathrobe (only -) to use while you’re there, which is a tad softer than the towels, but not much. 
Amenities – The coffee maker in the room had a coffee pot that liked to leak out coffee. They offered decaf-reg and various Tazo teas for your consumption, though if you used any of it, they did not replenish or provide you with clean cups, etc. Plus, the coffee maker was not plugged in the first night---and trying to squeeze behind the wall unit to plug it in was not fun though probably comical to watch.
The bath amenities were OK. Bliss products were OK, though the containers they came in were too hard for you to squeeze any of the product out. No real complaints there though, they refilled what you needed. 
Wireless was obnoxiously expensive at $--. We didn’t try room service, but saw the menu and noticed that it was too expensive for room service. We did not use the gym or any other facilities, so we can’t comment to their quality. OH, one more thing. If you buy ‘Hotel VIP’ tix for the Sears Tower from the concierge and are told that you don’t have to wait in line, be advised that the line they are referring to is the actual line to go up the Tower. You still have to wait in line to use the elevator to get up to the ticket booths AND you have to wait in line to get past security, which when we were there, was more than an hour wait. Just thought I’d mention that.
CONCLUSION: We booked this through Hotwire at a tremendously discounted rate. As a discount hotel, I’d say this place was barely adequate to OK. However, at the rates they normally charge, I would say steer away from this place. This W is totally undeserving of the higher level hotel classification---it just does not have the quality of rooms-facilities and service to warrant it.

My daughter and I were late getting into the city on Saturday eve. and had to get to our reservations at Red Eye Grill (ok food). A bellman offered to take our bags to our room for us and call ahead to the restaurant so we wouldn't be late. When we returned, a few hrs. later, our bags were not in the room and we had to hunt them down via-front desk-housekeeping. Needless to say, we were upset since we had tipped handsomely for this service. We got our bags within a reasonable time, but then realized one smaller one was still missing! That, too, was resolved but we did learn that this is not accepted hotel policy. The room itself could have been cleaned better; we found a man's belt and trash under the bed. A quick visit to the night concierge (Nicki) made all the difference and is why the Westin continues to stand out for service. She insisted on improving our experience and offered to have a dessert of our choice sent to the room as well as giving us complimentary breakfst buffet coupons for our next two days. The Botanicals Restaurant breakfast buffet is fabulous! Also, the location is wonderful and worked to our advantage during the beginning of the strike. We were nervous that we wouldn't get to LaGuardia in time. Never fear, the great bellstaff helped us into a lincoln towncar that was plush and a more reasonable price than our taxi coming in. Again, its all about the wonderful service that a Westin property has to offer. Granted, our room was nowhere near the size and interior beauty of the Westin St. Louis, but location and service during the xmas holidays was tops.

I have a great deal on my mind when I travel. To be able to rely on great accommodation and this terrific staff lifts a huge burden off of me and makes me much more effective at my job. My wife and I stayed here for two nights during a week-long trip up the CA coast. Got it for $--- per night through Priceline, which said it was four stars. Sorry, I've been in four-star hotels, and this isn't one of them. 
We heard parking is $-- (with tax) and decided to leave our car at friends in Berkeley and take the train in and out of the city. You might want to find a residential neighborhood in the city and leave your car there, and take a taxi to the hotel. 
The front desk was able to give us a room high in the hotel (it was a handicap-accessible room), so we had awesome views facing Union Square below and the bay in the distance. The location is great although, as someone else pointed out, it's a little challenging to find (it's not quite on Union Square). 
One incredibly annoying thing was that when our complimentary newspaper was delivered outside our hotel room each morning between - and - a.m., the person threw it down with a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""WHAP!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", instead of placing it quietly on the ground -- thoroughly startling us and awakening us for the morning. Not good. Also, we could hear people from up and down the hallway, opening and closing doors, engaging in conversation -- don't expect peace and quiet. 
Overall, the hotel does the trick, if you get it for a good price. But don't expect it to capture the character of San Francisco. It's just a regular old Hyatt. 
Also, if you want a truly first-class San Francisco experience, consider using Hotwire to find a four-star hotel on Nob Hill. There are four hotels there, each one world-class, so even though you can't pick the hotel, you'll be assured of receiving a great place at an amazing price. We've stayed at the Mark Hopkins Intercontinental (chosen by Hotwire) a few times, and it's never been less than extraordinary. This time, however, Hotwire was too expensive in that part of the city. 
Email me with any questions!

When you see a New York hotel at less than a King's ransom per night, what is your first thought? """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Surely must be a dump!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Well, be prepared to be very pleasantly surprised. The Pod offers excellent lodging for the price. It's not for the heavy in girth since beds are small as are the rooms; however, if you don't mind small spaces you'll be fine. Even though small, the room accommodated two comfortably when a friend came up while I finished dressing. The room is appointed in modern decor, down to the stainless steel sink, mod motif bed coverlet, and flat screen plasma TV on the wall. The twin sized bed was extremely comfortable and the pillow felt like sleeping on a cloud. The staff is friendly and efficient. Being from the south I was unaccustomed to room heat set to cycle every -- minutes, so I initially thought there was no heat. Upon reporting it to the front desk, it was explained how the heat worked, yet the receptionist offered to send someone up to make sure it was indeed working. Shortly thereafter, the heat came on and from that time forward kept the room very toasty. (As a matter of fact I actually opened the window a bit for ventilation.) Everything is kept very, very clean. The bathroom I used was splendid and a mere few steps from my door. Overhead shower head and jets! Modern sink, soft music, marble-slate tiled shower and floor. Though there isn't a restaurant in the hotel, around the corner is the Morning Star Cafe, an excellent selection for breakfast (eat-in or on the go)! I will stay at the Pod anytime I visit New York and will recommend it to everyone. I only hope it can stay as economical and unspoiled with all the great press I'm sure it gets.

This was our -rd stay at the Best Western Blue Sea Lodge. Great service...we asked to change to an ocean front room and they were able to accomodate us within the hour. Very friendly staff, clean rooms and the best location. Close to everything. We would recommend this hotel to anyone going to San Diego.

Stayed here in late December of '--... we were very satisfied with our stay. 
Very reasonable rates for tastefully-appointed, fully-wired rooms (albeit a bit on the smallish side, but very nice anyway). A great bargain for a hotel of this caliber. (I'm certain they are a lot more expensive on say, Buckeye football weekends in the fall, however). 
Desk staff was blisteringly efficient and cordial. Room service dinner was impeccable and delivered -- minutes early. Pool was well-kept and a welcome respite on a cold winter's night.
Bell staff was helpful, and check-out was a breeze for our early morning departure. 
The location, although not scenic (between I--- and tucked behind an industrial park), is convenient, only a few minutes' drive from campus and downtown. 
Finally, a few too many Ohio State items in the gift shop for my tastes, but then again, that's probably because I'm a big Badgers fan!
Seriously though, a great stay overall...

Friendly helpful staff, exceedingly clean room, unusually comfortable bed and pillows, and large thick soft towels. An elegant experience in this grand old hotel. I was in a king room on the quiet, interior court. Even hall noise was subdued, and the AC quiet and effective. The hotel is in a perfect location, very convenient to key L stations, the art museum, lots of restaurants and sights.
After reading other reviews I expected a tiny bathroom, but it was fine, and not tiny at all. The long shelf above the sink and toilet gave plenty of room for lotions and potions. My only complaint is that the light is not good for putting on makeup--too dark and yellowish. Brighter bulbs are needed. Consider the ladies, Palmer!
However I did have a poor experience late evening at the Lockwood bar. Three of us waited -- minutes for glasses of water to arrive after ordering them, and -- minutes for our drink orders to arrive, Many minutes later the food finally arrived. The bar had only a few guests and the restaurant was nearly empty. One member of our small group had to get up to go find the wait staff to ask about our order or I think we'd still be sitting there.. 
Then, after bringing the food, the waiter hung around and talked to us, on and on and on. We weren't in Chicago to have long conversations with waiters to hear about their home country! 
In contrast, drinks were served and the bill settled very quickly and professionally in the busy lobby bar area.
I highly recommend the Palmer, unless you have a thing about historic hotels and instead want one with a modern design and decor,

I spent four nights in the Holiday Inn-Capital while on a mini-vacation. The check-in was quick and easy and everyone I spoke to were very personable. The best thing about this hotel was the location. It was within walking distance to most of the sites that I wanted to see. Arlington National Cemetery was about - miles away and I took a cab there. On the way back I took the metro which I recommend highly. 
If I ever go back to the area again, I will definitely stay in this hotel.

The Monaco is just a great hotel. The room was a great size and we loved that we got to have a goldfish for our stay. First off, this review is partially based on my personal bias that I HATE historical hotels & properties (bed & breakfasts, etc). If I am away from home, I want modern amenities (work picked this hotel for me...so I was stuck). Not necessarily fancy amenities...but something at least updated in the last -- years. That being said...think of this hotel not as a Sheraton or Starwood property but instead as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Gunter Hotel...old & historic"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".
I could see someone who loves history and the Victorian or Civil War eras LOVING this property. To me (and many of my colleagues) it was just...old.
I stayed here for an entire week as part of a work conference.
In the room, carpeting was old, Toilet was old (and tankless! lol), Shower, sink and tile was ancient and the showerhead hit me at my shoulder level and could not be positioned higher. HVAC system old, room layout small & old.
Ok enough about the old. This place is old and it's not getting any younger! Here are some big cons about this property and why I would not recommend it:
-Black mold on several of the bathroom ceilings (yikes!).
-Noticeable """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hairs"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in the bathroom when I arrived
-Roomservice trays & glassware left in the hallways for HOURS (this is a small property compared to some Sheratons...inexcuseable)
-Used housekeeping linens piled up and put in a big ball in the hallway and LEFT THERE for hours. Sooooooo gross.
-Bags of garbage...same deal...left in the hallway for hours
-Hallway noise is awful (room doors very, very thin)
-That being said, the majority of the noise in the mornings was HOUSEKEEPING STAFF shooting the breeze and yelling down the halls to one another. Totally tasteless.
-Single pane windows so street noise is unavoidable and loud (near a hospital...so many sirens)
-Pool area was noticeably neglected
-Some rooms (guest and meeting) noticeably smelled of mildew
-Internet was only free in the lobby
-In-hotel bakery-deli was advertised as being a Starbucks but none of the staff knew how to make proper drinks and service was slow
All things aside, San Antonio is a fun city to hang out with colleagues (restaurants, bars) but I would stay ANYWHERE on the riverwalk besides the Gunter

I recently stayed here with a friend, having cancelled my own reservation and opting for a shared room. It's been done up and looks great inside yadda yadda no issues there. The reservation I had required -- hours notice or you would be charged a night. So a week in advance I emailed them, cancelled and they acknowledged back via email. Then I get a $--- something charge to my Visa. Write to them and tell them to immediately reverse the charge which happens three days later. The dollar has dropped and the conversion makes the amount they credited $--.-- less. So I am now out of pocket $--.-- for THEIR mistake. Not a lot of money but no one seems to now want to know about it. Be weary when dealing with this property and ensure you keep all correspondence. They will try it on!

A thorough renovation puts customary Hyatt luxury to the test. Results are mixed. As customary at Hyatt, the staff are wonderful. The beds are extraordinarily comfortable, the rooms quiet, the air system responsive and effective, the shower-tub design and materials accessible and secure, the elevators accessible and fast. This has the basic ingredients of a fine Hyatt hotel. Unfortunately, the excellence of this hotel is undermined by user unfriendly aspects of renovation design. Drawer space for clothes is insufficient, as are shelves and hooks in the bathroom. The toilet is dangerously close to other accoutrements. The hot water tap in the bathroom sink dribbled at best. The futuristic clock radio, while white, was an unusable black box. The light switches should come with a manual. The mattress foundation sticks out below the wonderful mattress and barks shins with its hard, pointed corners. The aesthetics of the renovation are dramatic and often interesting, but the predominance of white in rugs all over the hotel ends up displaying dirt as much as design. Although the hotel clearly offers alternatives to traditional check-in and check-out desks, the lineups for both were still enormous some times of day. The hotel solicited our use of internet check-in, which was then refused when we tried to use it. On manual check-in the room type confirmed was not available, leading to the need for housekeeping to provide alternative furnishings for the room allocated. The hotel location next to Grand Central Station on --nd Street and across the street from airport buses on Park Avenue is superb, but the interface of the hotel itself with cars and taxis is both confusing and nightmarish. Lots of good food in the hotel and its surroundings....
For these positive and less than positive attributes, the Grand Hyatt charges the high level of room rates typical of upscale Manhattan hotels. Hyatt is typically generous in its senior citizen discounts, but the base rate is rising quickly in the Grand Hyatt, as elsewhere. The question is whether the attributes of fine hotels are being delivered more fully elsewhere by the competition. Renovations addressing the eye more than many user needs undermine unbridled enthusiasm in the merits of this Hyatt.

I stayed at the Intercontinental for - nights whilst on business in August last year. The hotel is perfectly located for many offices around Park Avenue and within easy wlaking distance of Times Square and other main attractions.
My stay here was more than adequate. The room was large enough with a big bathroom that was always clean. Sure if you look close enough around the edges of the hotel rooms there are things that can be improved such as faulty plug sockets and some tired furniture, but overall this is a decent central New York hotel. 
One thing that I would say is avoid the buffet breakfast though and order something from the menu if you have time as there was a limited selection on the buffet and a lot of flies which was a tad offputting.

So, after reading what all the other reviews on TripAdvisor, I was very wary of what my hotel stay was going to be like this past weekend. However, I really enjoyed it! Sometimes, I don't know why people have the expectations that they do, before heading to a hotel. I also think some people to remember that this is a hotel in the middle of a city, that means things will be smaller. Okay, a pros and cons list:
Pros: wonder staff, the check-in process was great! The clerk could not have been more cordial upon our arrival at --:--pm, and when we had problems with our parking, she worked it out right away. Our room had plenty of room for the king sized bed and the water pressure in the shower was great! The room was clean, but not immaculate. The pool was quite large and we had a great time splashing around with family in the morning. When we came back to our room at -pm on Saturday night, the battery in our smoke detector was dying and beeping, but a quick phone call to the manager on duty and someone was up to our room in less than - minutes to change it out. It's located near a CVS, which made for some good cheap purchases for snacks! 
Cons: There is no refrigerator in the room (but I've never stayed in a mid-city hotel that had one), parking is $-- a night (but there are in-out privileges and for that, it's the cheapest in the area), there was some peeling wallpaper in the bathroom (approx - in square), we did priceline our room so we had an interior room (frankly, I didn't care about this, I don't go to a hotel for the view, I go to sleep at night) but I felt I should mention it. Also, the sheets were a little scratchy, I think they are just washed a lot!
All in all, I didn't care about --% of what other people found negative, but thought I should mention it for those who really care about those things.

There is eveything to like about this hotel. The location allows you to walk - take the metro (- block) to everywhere you would want to go and the rooms and service are exemplary.
Check in was pleasant and efficient and the room absolutely silent from any extraneous noise with all the facitlities you would expect from a top hotel.
What really nails the excellent rating is the helpfulness of the concierge and attitude of every single memeber of staff which was attentive and felt genuinely courteous.
To cap it all off look out for some excellent rates available particulalry at weekends.
We would absolutely no hesitation staying here again.

We were going to stay here for a couple of days, but our daughter came down with a fever and vomitting so we had to cancel. The hotel management was at first going to make us forfeit our entire $$, but after much hasseling back and forth on the phone (with threats of never staying there again in the future), they agreed to either give us a voucher or refund ONE of the - nights $$. I cannot say enough about the great staff at this property. They were pleasant, helpful and informative. The hotel is in a great spot for Michigan Avenue and Rush Street. Near to Lakeshore Drive. Navy Pier is a healthy walk away, and the Shedd, etc., are not walkable, but the amenities and staff make up for that.
The valet parking, while expensive (it is Chicago after all), was very responsive. The staff reminded us of free dinner on Thursday night when we arrived. The taco bar that night was just fine and well-stocked, as was breakfast each day.
The two bedroom suite was great for our family of five.
The frontdesk helped with restaurant recommendations and with a discount coupon for one of them. 
Very near to Michigan Avenue shopping and the Hancock tower.
Key recommendation: if you're hitting the museums, get the CityPass. It saves time and money. We avoided an hour wait at the Hancock and got rock star treatment in the fast line at each museum.
Great stay at an excellent Marriott property

My trips to New York City have been pleasure trips with lady friends. So, we are looking for a great location in Times Square and a clean hotel room! That's our main objectives when we visit NYC. We are not there to stay in the room; so, we're not concerned too much about a huge room; only that we have clean beds and clean bathrooms. The Edison is everything we've looked for in a NYC hotel! It's perfectly located; step out the door, turn right and you're in Times Square. We've stayed here - times. And will definitely stay here again. The staff is very courteous; there's security; there's a nice bar; two restaurants. Starbucks on both corners--perfect! There's also a nice lobby area; and, if you happen to arrive early (before check-in and the room is not ready), they will gladly store your luggage for you! Hotel Edison is our preferred place to stay in NYC!

This hotel is very different than most in NYC. It's small, quaint, a little bit elegant, and most of all... quiet! 
Although the Wall Street Inn is in the Financial District, the area is really a nice place to stay these days. 
The Hotel: It's a small, traditional building. It's elegant, private, and comfortable. The rooms are not large, but I had a corner room with several windows, a large bed, desk, and sitting area. The bathroom was small, but modern. The bed wasn't as soft as I like, but it was comfortable enough. A continental breakfast of muffins, coffee, etc was available all morning.
Staff: The staff was unobtrusive, but very responsive, professional, and friendly. Two different front desk associates gave me good recommendations for restaurants in the neighborhood.
Neighborhood: The downtown area has really emerged from ashes, and in my opinion, will be better than it ever was. Stone Street, just behind the hotel, is completely blocked from traffic and several restaurants and bars use the street for outdoor dining. There are many other restaurants and bars within a five-minute walk. Just a few blocks South is also Battery Park, with it's nice outdoor spaces.
Getting Around: The Wall Street subway station is two short blocks away. You can be in midtown in just a few minutes on the red line. Taxis are prevalent in the area. The Staten Island Ferry, and ferries to Ellis Island and the Stature of Liberty are right at Battery Park.
Price: This is the best part... the room rates are comparably much less than many hotels in NYC... especially the ones in Midtown.

I have the experience of many hotels in New York city,during -- years staying in a lot of hotels all around Manhattan ,and this Hampton really surprised me.The gentleness of all the staff was amazing,they are all ready to help you at all times.Besides that, a very good thing in Nyc,the rooms are all the same size ,large and with a huge window.The breafast is free and very good.

One thing I can say is the Staff is very nice and accomadating here. However, the pillows are lumpy and too soft. The beds in the unrenevated rooms are bouncy. No dresser for clothes, air conditioner way too loud and you can hear other people around you on the floor talking which kept one person in our party up all night long. Also there were no face clothes, coffee maker and no brochures on where to dine or what to see that you would usually find in a hotels room.

We stayed at the Canyon Villas for one week and had a great time. We didn't spend too much time at the hotel, but when we did it was very nice and relaxing. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Our room was a studio and was very nice. It had just a microwave and mini fridge but that was fine for us. The furnishings and everything was brand new and seemed barely-used.
The pool was great and never crowded. It was a bit dark at night, but still very nice. We ate at the pool bar one day for lunch, and that was great. It was also really nice that you could take a shuttle over to the JW Marriott. The bus comes twice an hour for the short ride over. You could walk, but it was too hot for us to do that. The pools at the JW were great including a lazy river and waterslide.
Overall, I would definitely go back and highly recommend the Canyon Villas.

Summary: This Hotel Indigo (it's a chain, part of IHG) came across as an overpriced Holiday Inn, rather than as a value-priced luxury hotel.
The decor is attractive, with (apparently) wood floors, cool earthy colors, and modern bath furnishings and electronics.
But a hotel room is first and foremost a place to sleep, and that's where this one fails to hit the mark. Noise, or rather, lack of adequate soundproofing between rooms appears to be the culprit. Every door closing, every conversation in the hallway was clearly audible (and I do mean clearly--we learned way too much about our floormates' personal lives). TVs in adjoining rooms were not as clearly audible, but the bass came thumping through. And those hardwood floors? It means any time some in the room above dropped something hard or walked across in a hard-soled shoe, we got to hear it. Street noise, even on a higher floor, was also quite strongly heard in the room.
Second problem: the bed was a reasonably firm one, but as a king-size, it still had four small and unpleasantly foamy pillows, the kind I'd expect at a Holiday Inn Express, instead of the large, cushy pillows I'd expect at an upscale hotel. No extra blankets or pillows in the closet.
The bathroom was attractive, but had no tub, just a walk-in shower, which I actually prefer but not all do. There were no washcloths when we checked in, and no floor mat the next day. Wet tile floors, whee! No robes provided, another common amenity for a true upscale hotel.
The much-advertised views of Petco park are oversold. The park is two full blocks away from the hotel, so one is looking between other buildings into the park. It's more interesting than looking at more high-rises, but don't think you'll really be watching a game from your room, at least not without serious magnification.
Lobby and bell staff were friendly when approached directly, but otherwise detached. Never a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""good evening"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" or """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""welcome back"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", even when they weren't otherwise occupied.
Someone in management is still thinking too down-scale. IHG needs to put some line staff from Intercontinental in place to touch up service. Even then, the main problems are structural. I'll be looking for somewhere else next time I need to be in San Diego.

Very welcoming stayed for our -st - nights in la ,very helpfull friendly staff booking meals in local restraunts etc then called again on our return to la you wont find a better place to stay than here.

The rooms are small and the bed is stiff, but overall very clean. Very basic, budget hotel. This is the place for you if you're just looking for a place to sleep at night and don't want to spend a lot of money...because that's all you'll get. A roof, a toilet, a shower, and a bed. Good if that's what you're looking for.

My family had a very nice stay at the Lucerne and I would stay there again without hesitation. We paid an excellent price (arranged through Westjet), had no problems with reservations, the staff was extremely helpful and pleasant, security in the hotel was excellent (always three or four staff members on duty in the lobby, no other way up to the rooms), the room was spotlessly clean, and the location is good (close to subway, walkable to Times Square if like me you like to walk a lot, a cab ride to the theatre district was about $--), it's in a completely safe area, surrounded by many great restaurants and nice pubs. There's a restaurant in the hotel that looked OK, but I never used it because there were so many more interesting restaurants in the vicinity. Any minuses? Well, the room was a bit small - but what hotel room in New York isn't? It took a while to get hot water in the afternoons, for some reason. There was plenty first thing in the morning and late at night. Go figure! But other than that, everything was fine - the beds were comfortable, the air conditioner worked great and the elevators were fast. What's not to like about this place?
I have no complaints,second time in - years my son and I have stayed here. Beds nice,Nice wide screen in room,bathrooms clean,treated great at desk,i'd come back again for sure.

I really enjoyed being so close to the Ocean. The room was clean but too small. The room was a bit out dated but the good thing was it was clean and near the beach! I would go again, but not stay so long after - days we were really crowded!

I have stayed here twice now and have had the most magnificent accommodations both times despite booking via a travel bid site. The first time we had a junior suite (that overlooked a gravel rooftop, but the room was so opulent we didn't care about what was going on outside) and the second time they gave us an upper floor double with a panoramic view. You really get the feeling of being wrapped in luxury here for the most part, although the age of the hotel does show in small ways, like the bath fixtures were less up to date than the rest of the room in some instances and the elevators don't seem in keeping with the newness elsewhere. I have to say we spent more time hanging out at the hotel than we normally would because we enjoyed our room and dug the general atmosphere. 
The big drawback, and the reason this is not a five-star review, is the parking -- it sucks. You pay a high daily rate for self-parking, and do not get the freedom of in-and-out access unless you pay the fees in advance or valet (the latter of which is just prohibitively expensive). There is a loophole however, in that the parking booth seems to be randomly staffed. Our first visit we agreed to just let them charge our bill in advance for the number of days in our stay, but then noticed that half the time the gate out was left open and no one was in the booth to charge anyone. When we complained about paying for parking when others were not being charged, after much wrangling we got $-- in parking fees refunded.. Our second visit we wised up and just paid at the booth as we went, and using the method we only ended up being charged one time during a three-day visit. But of course that's also a gamble, and mainly worked because when we left for the day we didn't come back till we were in for the night. Due to the parking cost and weirdness of that situation, I don't recommend this hotel for people who will be going back and forth to the hotel over the course of each day, as you can get charged anytime you take your car out if there happens to be someone working the parking booth. I would stay here much more frequently if parking weren't such an issue.

We had planned to go to NYC for my birthday in mid-June but could not find a rate under $--- for any decent hotel and were not going to pay $--- for a two-star hotel and pretty much cancelled our trip until a $--- room at a four-star hotel popped up on Hotwire. Check in and check out was a breeze. The rooms were spotless. The beds were extremely comfortable. Everyone that worked at the Argonaut seemed genuinely happy to be there and that was reflected in their smiles and willingness to help in any way they could.
A+++, Argonaut!
On a side note: the Argonaut Hotel allows pets, not just service animals. There is a great little park right across the street from the hotel where I walked Cleo each morning. There is also a little beach and a pier that was just perfect for an early morning stroll-jog. Pier -- is only - blocks away - an easy stroll past shops and food and fun!

It was a weekend to remember!
