You walk in the front door and the extremely hip lobby instantly puts you at ease - I was on the tenth floor and took the very slow elevator up and found yes my room was small, but it was so well designed it didn't seem to matter! That said i would not recommend putting more than one person into a single room, it really is designed for one! Other reviewers note they never had to wait for a bathroom, i kinda doubted it, but its so true, I never had to wait once! At most i think i saw the one bathroom being used on the floor at any one time.
The location is fantastic there are heaps of places to eat and drink in the area, a couple of grocery stores and its a short walk up the road to a couple of different subway stations. 
The only real downside i had was that like many other reviewers noted, the banging doors at night can be annoying. Its almost impossible to close a door without making alot of noise. That said it wasn't a huge issue.
If you are on a budget in New York then feel confident about booking the Pod, its the best value going around!

This hotel has a great location and is by far the cheapest option for the area. It was adequate for our needs. The bathroom floor was a bit disgusting around the edges, but overall the room was clean. The a-c worked, and with the white noise it provided, it was easy to get a good night's sleep. The front staff were friendly. We did overhear some guests complaining about """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hair in the bathroom"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but really, it's a cheap place to stay in downtown Chicago. You can't expect the quality to match the other hotels in the area with prices many times what we paid per night. I would stay here again if in Chicago.

I stayed for - night a few weeks ago and I have to say that I was impressed with the decoration and cleaniness of my room. 
I got a great deal through a search engine and based on some reviews here I was expecting the worst. But on the contrary my room was superb! Flat screen TV, small but cozy room, free wi-fi and brand new bath!
Location is fantastic, few blocks from Grand Central and right at midtown.
If I get the same deal again I will definetly stay at Algonquin on my next visit.

I am usually really terrible at picking hotels - no matter what the star rating -but this one was a winner!
A friend and I came here in November for a - night break and the hotel was just the perfect location to be in. we could walk to fifth ave - times square - central park and radio city music hall within -- minutes!
The hotel was beautiful and had a real feel of elegance to it - not just like a standard chain hotel.
Reception staff and all the concierges were nice - pleasant enough and helpful!
The only thing that I would say was not great were the prices of the food and drinks. As a result we did not eat or drink here but there are so many local places of good value near by it did not matter!
We did ask for a special room as I was going to celebrate my upcoming --th bday but we got a view of a brick wall ! At the end of the day we did not exactly mind tho as we did plenty of sightseeing in the day that looking out of the window was the last thing on our minds!
Rooms were clean - if not a little warm and there seemed to be no evidence of air con but we did manage to open a window so that was fine!
Overall this hotel is beautiful and elegant and well worth a visit!
Amber x
The lobby was very charming and the rooms were confortable. Not overly opulent but I would stay there again in a heart beat.

We really enjoyed our stay at the San Carlos. The staff were friendly and helpful, especially the doorstaff. Our room was clean and spacious with plenty of towels and tolietries. The microwave and coffee-maker were very useful. The continental breakfast was a nice touch, although the yogurt wasn't the best, it was good to start the day with some OJ, fruit and a bagel. The San Carlos is very central, we walked to most of our destinations. We would all stay there again.

Yes the front desk is very rude. Seems like they hate their life. Other than that the stay was decent... If I had the money Id definately stay somewhere else where they treat you right... But since Im on a budget Id probably come back. Its better than staying at a dirty motel. 
Also the blankets made my hair static all day during my stay... It was pretty annoying.. And the tv was fuzzy

I attended a conference in Chicago for four freezing days at the end of January. However, the employees at the Marriott Chicago Downtown hotel made the experience truly enjoyable. The hotel was quite full, but the service was always quick and pleasant. My room was also clean and comfortable. A wonderful business hotel!
Also, you can't beat the location of this hotel. It is within easy walking distance of excellent restaurants and shopping. Not to mention Starbuck's in the hotel lobby....!

I booked this hotel in October direct with the hotel at a rate that was pre-paid. Upon arrival at the hotel, there was a problem with checking in. Although I had booked - rooms, we think that they only had - for us. The receptionist disappeared for about -- minutes without any explanation. We were eventually given rooms on the --th floor. The rooms were nothing special. Our room didn't have a view at all. We were here for - nights. One day, our childrens room wasn't cleaned till - p.m. and that was after making - phone calls!! On leaving the hotel, we found that the hotel had charged us on booking for only - room and not both of them. We had specifically wanted to pay in advance due to the changing rate of exchange, and now find that we are worse off due to their mistake. Thye tried to tell me that our bank had obviously not allowed the charge to go through. Unfortunately, I onlly booked this hotel as we were meant to stay at the New York Palace, but thought that it would be too expensive because of the rate of exchange. In retrospect, I'm upset that we changed and would not recommend this hotel. The only thing going for it is the location. The concierge didn't seem to know anything when we asked about restaurants.

Good deal in a great location. Free continental breakfast and staff was helpful in recommending places to eat. Rooms were clean and the bed and pillows were surprisingly comfortable. Would recommend for budget travelers.

It was a toss up between the Westin San Francisco Market Street and the Grand Hyatt. The Westin had a guaranteed awesome view and a nicer room but was slightly more expensive, Hyatt had a AAA discount that included a breakfast buffet (Valued at $-- for - people). Opted for the Hyatt due to the price and breakfast. The breakfast buffet was a delicious and located on the --th floor of the hotel with an awesome view. The other plus was the location of the hotel directly next to Union Square. 
Unfortunately we got a room on a very low floor with a view of the air conditioning equipment on the building next door. The walls were paper thin and we could hear the very passionate couple next door like they were in our room. The room was clean, but the fridge is a touch sensor based minibar and there is no room in it for storing leftovers from restaurants. 
If you need a nice very clean and well made room for a couple days and don't plan to spend all your time in the hotel I would recommend this hotel, especially with the AAA discount. I probably won't come back to this hotel though.

I'd read some good reviews about this hotel but they are totally over rated. The hotel is mediocre. Beds are old and not really comfortable. Overall condition of the hotel, rooms, floors, etc., is not good. Colour scheme is erratic. Good for the location and proximity to the subway but a very high price for what you get. There must be better choices in the area. You also have to pay for leaving the luggage in the storage, and guess what, you have to pay again when you return in the afternoon to pick it up! I wouldn't recommend it to anyone.
We stayed only - night but the room was clean and comfortable. The restaurant was for breakfast only but there were some within walking distance.

My family and I stayed over night at the hotel on a trip to south florida during the july-th week. The hotel is kind of off the beaten path but it is located in a pretty nice shopping center if you are looking to shop or get something to eat. There's nothing spectacular about the property but I thought the room was clean and the breakfast decent for the money.

We travel a great deal in --- stars hotel. Having said that we were very pleased to experience great, polite and efficient service at the Boston Park Plaza. 
You may get a smaller, older room or a newly renovated <double room> (They took - small ones to make - big one with a King bed. All was very nice.
Warning: Fridges are NOT included but if you ask they usually will bring you one free of charge. LIke I said, the service is quick and polite. It took no more than -- min. to get. 
Second warning; check for cleaniness! I was unimpress by walking into our room to find the bathub dirty....I called and within -- min. the bellman brought a new key for me to check another room. The room was much bigger with a huge bathroom. 
All in all, nothing's perfect but at the Plaza, no fuss!
Comfortable rooms, delicious buffet breakfast, great dinner selections, clean.

We were quite impressed with the level of service we received during our - night stay this summer. Though there was really nothing special about the room itself (fact is, it was a bit tired), we were on the club level, and enjoyed it's use and food presentations throughout the day. The club concierges were very nice and couldn't do enough for us. The front desk, housekeeping and bell staff were also wonderful. I would stay here again without hesitation, but probably try to reserve a higher category rooom-suite next time.

Like others have stated the hotel IS located in a shady part of philadelphia. It is NOT reassuring to guests that every parking space has a sign that reminds them they are not responsible for stolen items. It also is not too reassuring that there IS a huge bullet proof glass that separates you from the clerks. I do have to say though that I did enjoy my stay there. 
Me and my friends books rooms there for the new years and we got there early to check in, I am glad we did. The first room we were told was our has a HORRIBLE vomit smell, like one that somebody got drunk and puked in. We walked in the room, and then walked out and requested a new room. The clerks and staff were very nice and immediatly gave us another room and showed it to us, and even asked if it was ok, and offered to show us other rooms if it was not satisfactory.
The room was clean, and I have no complaints. Our room did have an alarm clock, and i beleive it is standard that all of the rooms have one. The heater worked well and did not smell, and the bathroom was clean however I did not use the shower. 
I also recommend this because the clerks were very nice. Me and my date were going to a party and were supposed to have printed out our tickets at home. I did but she did not, so after we realized this we asked the clerks if we could use the internet. The clerk took us into their break room-office and let us print out our ticket. They were very nice with the limited english they spoke (maybe it was their accents, but very nice and receptive). 
They also hired a night time security guard since there is nothing keeping random people from walking in and going into the hotel.
All in all I recommend this place for business trips, but not pleasure or family outings. The hotel is also difficult to get to being that roosevelt blvd is a - lane strangely divided highway.

First trip to NYC and tried to pick the best place to stay...boy did we nail it! This hotel is excellent. Everything about it was fantastic, especially the bed. Absolutely, the best night sleep at a hotel ever. The rooms were beautiful and clean. The service was outstanding. Everyone was kind and gave great customer service. The location was spectacular. So close to so much. Easy check-in and out. (I did not want to check out.) They upgraded us, we were on the --th floor with a stunning view. We couldn't have been more pleased. The atrium continental breakfast was excellent. We will definitely stay here again. Thank you Westin for a very pleasurable stay.

What a GREAT hotel. Everyone should stay here when visiting San Fran and if you're a fan of the Fairmont chain. It's elegant, beautiful, classy, breathtaking, comfortable, and in such a great spot in San Francisco. Staff is so very helpful and will bend over backwards for you. Views abound from every room I feel like and it's easy to get to all the spots in the city from here. Great hotel bar and ambience in general. Definitely staying here again if I visit San Francisco.

My daughter and I stayed here in May for her senior trip. We enjoyed staying at the hotel and it was clean and comfortable. The staff was very helpful to us in many ways. The gentlemen at the front desk answered our questions if possible and when they were unsure they found out for us. They even called a cab for us to take us to the LA Zoo. Our rooms were cleaned in a timely manner and it was close to the Metro buses, therefore, it was easy for us to ride the buses to our destinations. The only thing that we didn't care for was the continental breakfast. The room was small and the selection was not very good. The only other thing that we didn't care for was there were quite a few loud people staying above and around us. Although this is really not under the hotel's control, it did seem that there were alot of young travelers that were a bit roudy, however, they did quiet down for the night. If you want a clean, comfortable hotel not far from the Hollywood Walk of Fame, then this is the place. But be ready to ride the bus because that is the easiest and cheapest way to get tothe middle of the action.
Fantastic location in Times Square, comfortable beds and nice bathrooms. But the staff let it down, didnt get much service with a smile. Innovative interiors, would stay again, ignore the staff!

I just stayed at this hotel for business. I had meetings near The Mint building and this hotel is not the best place if you are traveling for business. Let me discuss the good parts of this hotel. The staff was very friendly and they were good hosts. The room was spacious and clean. The workout room was nice sized and the mounted TV's were good quality. The pool area was very clean and although I did not swim I watched other adults swim while I was working out. FYI- there is a glass wall between the workout room and the pool area. The main breakfast-sitting area was clean and nice. The breakfast was the typical standard HIE that is at all locations. 
The bad parts of this property are that it is located a bit of a drive outside of all of the comings-goings. In addition, it is not near any Metro pickup so taking the subway -st thing in the morning is not an option. The hotel, however, does provide a morning shuttle bus that takes you to Union Square. From Union Square, you can get on the Metro and ride anywhere. The guys driving the shuttle bus were very friendly and helpful. I asked them all about the subway and places of interest and they were more than happy to help me out find my way around town. The down side is the shuttle ride is about --- an hour and finding the pickup is a bit of a challenge. 
Overall, I'm not sure I would stay here again for business as this location requires me to be up and out the door early to get the shuttle and then to get to the Metro so I can get to my meetings. 
If I were traveling for pleasure, this would be a nice option as it wouldn't matter if I took the later shuttle to Union Square. Another point to notice is the shuttle stops running at Noon and doesn't start again until -:--pm.

I've stayed here a few times on business. It's not a bad hotel by any means but doesn't really stand out in any particular way. Having said that, the rooms are comfortable and front desk staff are friendly. Free Wi-Fi is a big plus for guests. 
The best thing is the location - very close to Fishermans Wharf so it's ideal for tourists. I would recommend getting a cab if you're going downtown, as there are usually huge queues for the cable car. 
There are plenty of good restaurants in this area of SF, so I'd recommend going out for dinner. 
Can't comment on value as I don't pay for the room myself.

By the am the hotel upgraded us to the executive level but our - rd room for a two night stay. If you do stay here it is worth the money to either get the bigger rooms or the executive floors... I will also add I so irritated in the am do to repacking twice and getting to sleep at - am, the staff at the lockwood restaurant did not flinch at poor disposition and the excellent food renewed my attitude

My wife and I checked into the Philadelphia Marriott Downtown adjacent to the Pennsylvania Convention Center following a national conference that I attended. (Unfortunately, I was forced to stay at another DREADFUL hotel - Clarion Suites nearby -- run, don't walk away from this place! and anything would have been a drastic improvement from what we'd experienced earlier in the week). However, the staff and accommodations at the Marriott were splendid. Our room was stately decorated and very clean. All of the staff were very cordial and welcomed us to the hotel (even a janitor working in the hall stopped and wished us a good day!). I will always try to stay at the Marriott if I have business at the convention center or in the Central City of Philadelphia.

I stayed at the Sheraton for a last minute business trip to Austin. I
normally stay at the Hyatt, but it was booked for the week.
The carpet in my room was old,dirty and had multiple stains. The entire room had a dire need for a remodel. I will say that the beds were very comfortable and that is the most important factor for me when staying at a hotel. However, for $----night, I expected much nicer rooms - the Hyatt has flat screens and marble bathrooms.
The restaurant-roomservice food was very good. Roomservice was always
promt and the food was warm. The hotel gym was ok, but only had two treadmills and one was out of order during my stay.
Overall, I would probably not stay here again if I was paying the bill - but I can't really gripe because my company paid for this trip.
I will say that I saw pictures throughout the hotel of very nice room
plans for a remodel starting in the summer of ----. So if you are planning on staying here - you might want to ask for a remodeled room.

We picked this hotel based upon the high Trip Advisor rating and the fact that it was family-friendly. I always find it difficult to give a hotel a rating because the criterion are relative depending upon where you are, with wide variations in quality and amenities across both countries and continents. Make no mistake however, this is a good hotel. Equally, this is no five star hotel. 
The location, being within a few blocks of Bloomingdales, Saks, Tiffany and the Chrysler building is excellent. The hotel is a fantastic choice for families. The beds are comfortable and the rooms spotlessly clean, bathrooms are functional if not luxurious The views are good (although no sign of the Chrysler Buidling from room ---- where we were). As described previously, the staff are efficient although by no means exceptionally so.
So what is the problem? Well none really aside from the fact that I was paying $--- (£---) + tax per night for what is a mid-range chain hotel. Perhaps the comparison is unfair, particularly given the fact that we probably visited NYC on the busiest weekend of the year, but I couldn't help expecting more for the money. I have read gushing reviews but where people paid half of this rate or less for rooms here. That would be fair value but we could find nothing on Priceline, Hotwire etc that came close. Perhaps we have been spolied by what you get in Singapore or the Far East for £--- (true - star luxury).
We too got the hotel car back to JFK at $-- inclusive of toll but excluding tip and this was a good choice after the world's smelliest cab on arrival! Also, for breakfast, the hotel kindly recommended Maddison's which is two blocks away on -st Avenue. We ended up having breakfast there three times and it was a fantastic experience with great American breakfasts (bacon, two eggs and hash browns for $- with unlimited coffee) and a real '--'s ambiance.
All in all, I would return to the Courtyard. It's a good hotel and our family enjoyed it but I would not pay $--- plus tax per night for it. If you can get it for a more reasonable rate, do not hesitate to stay there - particularly if you are a family with children.

This was a very good hotel experience. The staff was friendly and the everything was clean. I felt very comfortable in the hotel and the services I needed were available. The rooms have high speed internet (that is actually high speed). Wireless is only in the lobby. The dining room overlooks the riverwalk and a corner of the street. It is a very relaxing view for breakfast in the morning.
I had one maintenance need (light switch didn't work) and it was taken care of immediately. 
You can walk from here to all kinds of San Antonio sites. You could spend days just visiting sites that are within easy walking distance. Public transportation is available right across the street and parking is in the same building.
Aside from the light switch not working the only other negative experience was that the water pressure in the shower was too high for my liking. I would definitely return and bring my family.

Our first trip to New York and the Belvedere was a great choice. The hotel is in a great location to get to all the 'action' of Times Square etc. with an easy walk - then very relaxing when you arrive back. We had a few minor issues - safe battery needed replacing, squeaky bathroom door and intermittent air conditioning - but when called all were fixed within a few minutes. The rooms were comfortable and very clean and the staff at front desk including the doormen were very friendly and polite - answering all our questions. There is an excellent map with subway stops in the room and-or front desk.
The Patzeria restaurant is a few doors down and we had excellent food, and service, at very reasonable price. If you want some refreshments for your fridge we seemed to hit the Rite Aid @ -th and --th. We used the Costco NewYorkCity pass and those paid for themselves. You will run out of time (and perhaps $) in a hurry - as there is so much to see and do - but a must is to make sure you have gr- walking shoes!

We booked this hotel for a next day flight and it was a good choice.
We had a rented car and the drop off was -- meters from the hotel, the check-in was fast and the staff was very helpful.
The rooms are very large, clean and modern, the bathroom is also large and we didn't have any problem with pressure or heat. 
We arrived late so we ordered the dinner through room service, the price was a bit high but the food was very good. 
The only downside it's the location: if you have to catch a flight it's perfect because there's even a free shuttle but if you plan to visit the city it's a bit too far from downtown Boston.

Stayed with the Cassa from the -th to --th of August . Sure it is under construction, but the value, location and the new spotless rooms by far outweigh the negatives of the stay at a hotel still under construction. Wifi, Star-bucks across the street and all the theaters nearby. Just do it. Book now before the rates go up. Walking distance to all the great reasonable restaurants in Hell""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""s Kitchen.

We stayed here for two nights --th & --th September - would highly recommend it. Beautiful room with everything you could possibly want. Very clean, quiet, comfortable and luxurious. Helpful and friendly staff including courtesy car. Downtown is a good area to be in with good bus and tube connections. Had no problems getting about day or night. Wouldn't hesitate to recommend this hotel and the area its in.

I have been meaning to write this for some weeks now but as per usual life got in the way!
We stayed here from the --rd December till --th December ----.
Our flight was badly delayed and we did not arrive in the hotel til -am in the morning. I had phoned the hotel from London gatwick to tell them of our late arival and was told all was ok. Anyway we arrived checked in, went to our rooms, just normal ones (not executive) on the -th floor, we had - rooms and our children were staying on the other side ot the corridor which was perfect.
Rooms very clean and the most comfy beds I have ever slept in away from home! We had booked to have breakfast included which we thought would be easier so we could just get going in the morning without worrying where to go and eat. The first morning we were late for breakfast about - am and there was a rather large queue (about -- minutes wait. But we got seated got our drinks and we were of to the buffet. Great buffet fresh fruit, bacon (no one does bacon like the americans do!), sausages, eggs in ayway you can imagine, cold meats, lots of pastries (heavenly) and bread, there was also salmon and stuff for the oriental market, they also had something called Birchers Muesli (this looked too much like vomit and therefor left it well alone!!)
When we left I was confused as we had paid for breakfast I thought that was it, but we had to pay a service charge of about $--.--, I was not happy with this as it was self service all they brought us was drinks and cleared the table.
When we returned in the evening the girls room had not ben made, a call to reception and the room was cleaned, the next day we had no towels, then they had no towels. When they used the hairdryer and the television was on they would loose all the electricity in their room. These were small things and they were very good at putting them straight more or less immediately but it was just a bit annoying. We also had no showergel, when we asked for this we got given more shampoo and conditioner (we are not very hairy people!!) so perhaps they do not use showergel, we have stayed in other Hiltons and we did get showergel anyway this is not very important. After the first morning we used to get down for breakfast by about - --.-- am and there was no queue then. Eventhough it is a very large hotel it does not feel that way, there were always people around but you never felt overcrowded.
The hotel is perfectly located for sight seeing, just a few blocks from Central Park, Times Square, subway stations and the main shopping areas. Lots of great delis around, go in to the pubs as the food is great and good value. We were in New York for Christmas, which was good fun, the skating rinks got very busy, everyone looking at the Rockefeller Tree you would not be able to move for the people, the shops obviously were very busy but it was a nice atmosphere. The Radio City show was mindblowing.
All in all we had a great time. When we were due to leave we got our bills under our doors, please check them very carefully as they tried to charge us nearly double, it was only because I had the print outs from the UK we got the rate we had booked for. They also tried to charge us for no show on our first night! They also take payment on your credit card straight away, so you may need to extend your limit before you leave the UK. Reception was very helpful , and took off the charges they had added. but had we not checked the bill we would have had a shock when our visa bill arrived. I even persuaded them to take of the service charge for breakfast!! All in all we had a nice stay but if we come back I will look at other hotels first.
I stayed at this hotel for my last - visits in San Antonio both the time I had a pleasant stay with great service.

I stayed at the Benjamin the night before an oral argument in the Second Circuit Court of Appeals. I absolutely loved it. First, Mohammed took wonderful care of me, just as other reviewers have said. He made me feel so at home and went way beyond his duties to be sure I knew where everything was, etc. The room was PALATIAL. I felt like I had my own condominium. Huge living room, great work area with desk and everything you need for electronics, beautiful dining room, charming little kitchen with full refrigerator, plates, glasses, etc., huge bedroom, beautiful bathroom. Ahhhh the shower -- best water pressure I have ever experienced EVER. The bed was so wonderful I had so much trouble getting out of it at - a.m. to go to oral argument! I could have stayed there all day. I give this hotel my highest rating.

We stayed for - nights at the Quality Inn & Suites. We had a newly renovated room with a complete kitchen - even a dishwasher. 
The room was huge with plenty of space for a family with - teenage children and the children loved the pool. 
Even if it is not right in the city center it is close enough to walk to Pike Place market and only a few minutes walk to the space needle. 
We found the hotel clean and the staff friendly.
The breakfast was good with fresh fruit and wafles, but the set up not very practical causing a long line from -.-- onwards. 
All in all very good value for the money.

Please keep in mind that I booked this hotel online with a site that was running a special, and paid $---night, including tax. 
The location was great - easy walking distance to central Union Square, Chinatown, BART-Muni, and even to the Ferry building if you're in the mood for a good stroll. The staff was professional and welcoming throughout the stay, including the very generous wine tasting (the attendant even came around with the bottles to offer refills! It's really more of a free wine happy hour!). Never waited more than a minute for the elevator and did not feel crowded, even though the hotel was at capacity.
Room: I could identify the musty smell other people had mentioned, but to be honest, it's just a damp smell that you can sense in every other old, non-highrise building in San Francisco. The windows or A-C can be used to help, and after a few minutes, I didn't notice it anymore. The room was a decent size for two people and luggage, with an enormous bed, sitting chair, desk, mini fridge, closet, and flatscreen tv. Bathroom was also a good size, and though very worn, was neat and clean. The room itself was a bit worn, but again, for the price, all I wanted was cleanliness and comfort, and the hotel exceeded my expectations. Did not hear a peep from adjacent rooms, except the occasional passage in the hallway.
The continental breakfast was just that - danishes, croissants, coffee and tea. We grabbed some tea on the way out in the mornings, and picked up yogurts and crackers at the deli across the street. No big deal. There are several small delis-bodegas within walking distance, and the fridge has enough room to store some food and beverage items of your own.
If you're used to chain-luxury hotels with amenities, I wouldn't recommend this one. But if you're a typical budget traveler and are looking for a comfortable, clean (even charming) place to sleep while exploring SF, this is a great place. If the price is right, I will definitely stay here again next time.

I planned a trip to the inner harbor for my boyfriends birthday and was not sure where to stay- the Renaissace Harborplace was perfect. It was clean, comfortable, centrally located -I have no negatives to report. We did stay in a harborview room which I would strongly recommend. I am not sure I would have enjoyed the room-view if I was facing the pool or another buliding, etc. The pictures on the hotel's website are exactly what the hotel-room looked liked like. Ask for an upgrade, the hotel was very accommodating!

This hotel has a great location. Surrounded by lots clubs and restuarants. Close to mueseums and theaters. There is something for everyone in this area. The hotel is great, love the evening reception and bedtime cookies. The breakfast buffet is ok. Now for the negative things the shower walls were dirty and there was no hot water. The elevator was slow. It is a bit overpriced too.

The thing that made this hotel stand out for us was the location. Downtown Boston and within easy walking distance to Quincy Market, North End , Wharf and Subway stop. Rooms are a tad on the small size, but have everything one needs and why stay in the room when your going to see Boston.

I had stayed at this hotel several years ago (when it was the Vance) and knew it was convenient for the Convention Center so I chose it again. Now as the Max it has been thoroughly updated and art-themed but retains an individual character that you don't get in larger 'chain' hotels.
The room I had was a little on the small side but perfectly adequate if you're spending most of your time out in the city as I was. The modernisation means that all the equipment is new and works efficiently.

Recently visited my daughter in NYC, and everytime I go, I try to stay at a different hotel.
Went on Priceline and found that my bid went to W New York on Lexington Ave.
It's located just a few blocks from Grand Central Station, so it's pretty much convenient to anywhere you need to go.
The lobby is very pleasant...and my check in went very smoothly. The staff was very accessible, and I was even given a flute of champagne. (I also enjoyed the green apples featured at the check in desk.)
My room was pretty small...but as I've said before, you don't come to New York to stay in your room. I did appreciate the comfort of the bed...and was so glad to see a door on the bathroom.
Recently my trips to N.Y. had me staying in hotels, where there was only a curtain, or screen separating the room from the water closet...great if you're staying by yourself..not so great if there's more than one of you.
When leaving, I found that the doormen were extremely helpful...and very friendly.
My only complaint with this property is housekeeping somehow forgot to clean my room on Saturday. (I arrived on a Friday.) I know it's a large hotel, but it would have been nice to have fresh towels...and after a long day of shopping, it would have been welcoming to see my bed made. But, such is life.
Overall, I would stay there again...

I stayed here November -----, ---- $-- per night on Priceline.com. Friendly staff upgraded my room for free. -th floor, great view of golf course. The room we finally got was ok - nothing to write home about - and a bit disappointing for a Hilton. Given the experience we got there and the great choices that Chicago offers, I doubt that we will ever go back there.

While located well away from downtown Philadelphia, this hotel is sited in a quaint area of Philadelphia that is rich in history of its own. It is very close to Morris Arboretum and Wyck Gardens, as well as numerous other historic sites, and it's in a very walkable neighborhood with many charming shops and restaurants. There aren't many hotels in the area, which is fine, since this one is a gem! The historic aspects of the hotel remain and add to its charm, but the inside has been completely renovated. Elegant, comfortable, clean rooms with one of the most comfortable beds I've ever slept in await the visitor. The rooms feature high-end toiletries that made a routine shower more like a spa experience. Wi-Fi throughout...and free! Each room features nice electronics, including a dock for an iPod and a widescreen TV. The lobby is an architectural and aesthetic knockout, as is the breakfast room. There is a very nice workout room and a well arrayed business center on the second floor landing. Throughout the property there are wonderful historic notes: old photographs and prints, and in one hall, an old bike hanging from the wall. Educational and fun! The hotel has a very high-end look and feel (think Kimpton!), but the price was quite reasonable. The staff is friendly and helpful...amazingly so. One manager offered me a ticket - and a ride - to the Morris Arboretum. They couldn't have been more helpful, fun, interesting or knowledgeable about the area (including restaurants, shops and other assets).
The included breakfast featured a wonderful, self-serve buffet that included fruit, yogurt, granola, baked delights, bagels, hardboiled eggs, juices, coffee-espresso, tea...and a wonderful waffle maker that served up the most delightful and light waffles. My wife and I frequently stop at many of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""new"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Holiday Inn Expresses throughout the country and we have rarely been disappointed. That certainly was true when we spent two nights at the HIE Southeast In Indianapolis recently. Conveniently located just off the I---- beltway that circles that city and only a mile or two from both the I--- or the I--- freeways, the Inn is immaculately clean, its rooms unusually large (every room contains two king-sized and quite comfortable beds), and its bathrooms well-designed. All the front-desk personnel were outgoing, efficient and very friendly. For travelers needing to find a location to stop in the Indianapolis area, especially in the south sections of the city, the HIE Southeast is well worth considering. 
There is probably no such thing as a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""typical"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" or """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""average"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Holiday Inn Express despite many seemingly outward physical similarities across the USA. Some are, however, better than others thanks to any number of intangibles; some are not. The HIE Southeast falls closer to the latter than the former. There are lots of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""problems"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that cause such a generalization. Each morning's breakfast, for instance, is, at best mediocre in light of today's expectations. Scrambled eggs, a few sausages (but no bacon), biscuits with, occasionally, sausage gravy, a few cold muffins or plain bagels, several cold cereals, and a few other low-end items such as Walmart's Great Value tea, the only available choice. The only fresh fruit when we visited the inn were several overly ripe bananas. Add to that the fact that the breakfast room is located on the east side of the motel so that each morning many of the tables are so heavily bathed in sunlight that they are impossible to be used (unless one wants to be uncomfortable through the entire meal). Though there are several small restaurants located nearby, anyone looking for a wide variety of eating possibilities needs to drive to nearby Greenwood more than five to six miles away, a clearly inconvenient nuisance. Shopping in the immediate area means either Walmart or, farther down the street, a Big K-Mart. Anyone wanting more also will need to go to Greenwood.
There are many other small, but quite irritating detractions at the HIE. No matter how hard we tried to be considerate of several sleeping neighbors, our door squeaked so loudly when we opened or closed it that we had the feeling we had been transported back to the old Inner Sanctum radio show. Though the housekeeping staff did a very nice job cleaning and freshing-up our room, they failed on both days that we were staying with them to replace a burned out light bulb which we reported almost immediately after checking in and then again the following day. For some reason, the elevators have heaters in them which seem to come on automatically even when the temperature outside is in the high --s. Though the bedrooms, as noted above, are large, if not truly spacious, there is barely room to put only one piece of luggage (unless one wishes to sweep everything off the desk and use it as a second luggage rack). And, even though it is, I suppose, a matter of personal choice, the inn has chosen to employ the same """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""weird"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" design of wallpaper virtually everywhere -- in all the hallways, in the front lobby, in the breakfast room, and elsewhere. It is a design that few could love. 
Room rates are fair (though the nearby equally large LaQuinta Inn was, on average, more than $-- cheaper per night). Whether the HIE is worth the added difference is a matter each person will have to decide for him- or herself. Still, despite all the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""things"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" noted above, we were in no way sorry we chose the inn when we were in Indianapolis. The HIE Southeast is a solid --star, maybe even three-and-a-half star place to stay. It offers a comfortable, restful night to sleep and, though there are drawbacks, many travelers will be as glad as we were if they decide to stop.

As its been a few days since I returned I probably would have forgot most of this things that erked me so much but I'll recall what still annoys me.
I found the houskeeping service very inconsistent. I got to the room in the late afternoon, no slippers. Nevermind, i thought, I won't use them right now anyway, they'll bring some in the morning. When did turn up? Night number -.

I just returned from a - night stay at the Hyatt McCormick Place. I was attending a conference at McCormick convention center so I opted for convenience over location. This place is a --$ cab ride from downtown so keep that in mind.

We recently went on a family vacation to San Francisco and stayed at this hotel for - days. Traveled with a - and -- yr old. This hotel is in a great location. Overall the noise was not a big deal, simple solutions for a great hotel. Would definitely stay here again. A few tips make sure to purchase the city pass, it has tickets to a few attractions and the unlimited Muni transportation pass is worth it alone. The pass is good for cable cars, trolleys, and buses. This saved us alot of money and we went all over town. Transportation from SFO to Sheraton, we tried both options. On arrival we took the BART to Embarcadero then picked up a cab the rest of the way, this saved us a little money but not much and was slower and more of a hassle. Do this ONLY if it is --- people to make it worth it because BART charges -.-- per person plus the cab ride is about another $--. Since it was - of us we paid almost the same price had we just taken a cab directly to the hotel. On departure we took a Cab from Sheraton to SFO which was about $----- it was fast and no hassle. Stayed four nights July ---. Staff were very friendly and helpful.Rooms are average for New York, with great beds and bedding. Nice touches: free wifi, bottled water, shampoo, conditioner & bath gel. Stayed here in early March ---- and couldn't recommend the hotel highly enough. Fabulous location, with breakfast a REAL bonus. Wonderful staff, especially Elena, who couldn't have been more friendly or attentive. We can't wait to go back and have recommended it to friends and family

I've stayed here - times. It's good. Can't complain, it's right in Hollywood. Nice pool, parking which has star's names, so you can decide if you want to be Will Smith or Julia Roberts from day to day.

 The staff are very friendly. The rooms and service at the hotel bar are also excellent.

I wouldn't recommend eating at the hotel's restaurant. Very expensive with mediocre food. Great hotel with friendly and helpful staff.

The Grand Hyatt is within about a mile of the major tourist attractions and the government offices and very convenient to the Metro.
The hotel is top notch, among the best I have seen in DC. The lobby is classy and not overwhelming. There is a large atrium area and a couple of restaurants surround it. The service throughout the hotel was fabulous.

I highly recommend this property.

I chose the Liaison Hotel because it's only - blocks from Union Station, where my friend and I came in on the Amtrak, and - blocks from the Capitol and National Gallery. They also gave out free beers and soda. Yeah, people said those things would have gone bad anyway (since the fridges wouldn't be working), but management could have still sold them and gotten some money out of it. We ended up having a great time eating and getting drunk on the hotel rooftop while talking to other guests! They really made sure everyone got whatever they needed and saved our day from being totally ruined.
Diane was the best!!! Helped us with everything we needed from directions to in room services! Really a top notch place to stay that is close to the airport. Just ask for Diane!

I loved the Hilton New York. We got a great deal on Priceline, but that wasn't the only great thing about my stay here. The lady at check in didn't mention Priceline and we even got a small upgrade! Although my room was only on the --th floor, I had a view of Central Park! There wasn't even a building outside my window! Taxis were always coming through for pick ups and drop offs. We never had more than a minute wait and didn't have to fight for them. And, we didn't have to unload and load our baggage on the side of the street, like so many other NYC hotels. I may be mistaken, but I think that the Hilton is the only Manhattan hotel like this. The location was wonderful. It was an easy walk to Central Park, Rockefeller Center, and a slightly longer walk to Times Square. I wanted to be in Times Square, but I am so glad that we weren't. The hustle and bustle there was overwhelming. I would imagine that you'd have to stay very high up to have a quiet evening in a hotel there. Not to mention the difficulty hailing a cab there. It was so easy to come and go at the Hilton. I would give this hotel - stars easily!

The Park Lane was a frequent stop of mine in the '--'s. The location and park views were, and remain, unmatched. I hadn't stayed there in twenty years when I came across a great price on TripAdvisor. But time was short and I decided to proceed. Some of the negative comments leave me baffled, for instance slow elevators and rude, indifferent staff. I was on the --th floor and never had to wait for an elevator and they were extremely fast. All staff were friendly and helpful, well above average. Some complain about turn down service. Well I'm not in NYC to be in my room in the evening and love to return to a turned down bed. Simply leave a Do Not Disturb sign on your door if you object. But the Park Lane's turn down service is the best: bedding, chocolates, trash emptied, towels replenished, room tidied. What's not to like? What I do have to agree with is that the rooms are very much in need of an update. The furniture and decor make it like entering a time warp; in fact, nothing has changed since I was last there in ----. It's sad that what should be one of the premier hotels in the city has been allowed to age so. Despite this, housekeeping did a superb job with what they have and my room and bathroom were immaculate. Also park rooms are quite spacious, although non park rooms are only average in size. So, if you want a super location, are fortunate to have a park view room, want a friendly, clean hotel and are willing to settle for out-of-date decor, then the Park Lane's a good choice. On balance, I'll definitely go back. But Leona, please spend a few of the billions Harry left you and bring the Park Lane back to its former glory.

The room we were assigned was a corner room on the --th floor that overlooked the Independence Hall on one side and the Delaware River on the other side. The view was absolutely stunning. For a single woman, I felt safe and really loved the location. CLose to all, restaurants, whole foods on -th and trader Joes on -th too. Macys and more within a few blocks. Staff great and helpful, room larger than expected for nyc. Loved the bed and granite bathroom and also the usa today at my room every morning. The King room was huge and very comfortable (desk to work at, - large lounge chairs & ottoman to relax & read on). Great sheets and a super comfortable bed. Bathroom is smaller, but was just fine (they could use those rounded shower curtains, though). Free wi-fi in the room worked great. Service was excellent here. We had a problem with the A-C unit - which I mentioned as we were heading out for dinner, saying they should put it on the list for the morning's repairs (it was cooling, but leaking a bit), but the front desk staff insisted on sending someone up right away (it was fixed when we returned). I can't think of any downsides, unless you were expecting one of the fancy hotels and came here. But thats not the target of Homewood. Definitely would come back here when we return to H Town.

We just got back from a fabulous stay at the Ritz Carlton. We were there for the weekend and pulled out all the stops for a -- year anniversary celebration. Still, I wanted to go somewhere that was already open to animals. When we arrived, tired, bedraggled, sweaty, we got a thorough grilling by a snappish desk clerk who wanted proof that Sofia is a service dog. Fortunately, I had her photo I.D. service card. I have stayed in this hotel in October, ----. 
First of all I had a very spacious room comparing with the other hotels in the area. I can recommend this hotel for a great for extended stay. Additionally you can find everything you need in the long term this hotel.

The beds are rock-hard; so hard, in fact, that I managed to eek out - hours of sleep on my side and awoke feeling bruised. And the walls are paper-thin. If you DO stay there, I recommend a corner unit on the upper level.
If you're looking for some fun and aren't so concerned about the sleep, this is the place for you. Beautiful golf course, huge pool with bar pumping fun music and a smaller children's pool, tennis courts, shuffleboard, children's play area and full spa services. But if sleep is important to you and you need to be in this same area of Phoenix, stay at the Pointe South Mountain Resort. Much of the same amenities, but luxuriously soft beds and nice, thick walls!

My husband and I love the Houstonian. We live in Houston and venture to the Houstonian (about a mile and a half from our house) about every two years. We spent our anniversary in a suite one weekend and loved it. The spa offers amazing services and I would recommend taking advantage of the steam room, sauna and lap pool when going to the spa. The pools are overcrowded so we don't even venture out to the pool. There is a track around the entire area and we love going for walks, either in the evening after dinner or for a little exercise. A suite or a regular room is well worth it. We love rolling food in and out for all meals. The bar is fun to hang out and watch sports on TV. We enjoy hanging out in the room and ordering movies we have missed. Room service will even bring up some popcorn. Being at the Houstonian is a great getaway for us without the long travel time. It's like being in the woods camping, with lots o'services and an incredible room.

Our suite with - beds and a sleeper sofa was perfect for our family of -. 
The bedroom was separate from the living room, so we had - TVs. There was a small bar with sink, microwave and fridge. Convenient.

A great choice in DC!

After the show we were tired, came straight back to the hotel. There's a good restaurant at the hotel, (Hong Kong Chinese food). It was open late, so we ordered food before bedtime. The food was great, (the prices are very reasonable too). We had our midnight snack and went to sleep happy, after a great day in Boston.
The internet access was fast and easy to use. The work space in our room was spacious and comfortable.
I forgot my bathroom bag back in Maine. The front desk had complimentary shaving kit, tooth brush and tooth paste, shampoo, conditioner, mouthwash, etc. 
The bathroom was large and clean.
The most important reason that I would recommend this hotel is the service.
The staff made our stay enjoyable. See you soon.

Located across the street from the Boston Public Library, on Boylston Street, this boutique hotel is, in my opinion, the best value in the Copley Square area. It is small and trendy with an art deco ambiance in the lobby-bar area and in the rooms. The furnishings are contemporary, the room has surround sound in both the bedroom and the bathroom and the bed is really comfortable. The bathrooms are really pretty with slate tiles on the floor, walls and into the shower. The queen size rooms are very spacious but the double room is very tight, so choose the queen size room if it is available. The front desk staff are very friendly and gracious. I have stayed here three times in the past year and, for the money, it just can't be beat! You can stay a block away in a bigger, fancier hotel with restaurants and bars and shops and pay almost twice as much. If you aren't interested in paying a premium for those """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""amenities"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", then stay at the Charlesmark. You won't regret it!

The hotel was conveniently located just round the corner from the Metro, which was easy to get to and from the airport and to downtown.
There was no queue at reception, and when we arrived the receptionist was very friendly, congratulating us on our wedding anniversary. He managed to get us upgraded to a corner room, which had windows on - sides of the room overlooking broadway, and there was a gift in our room of wine, chocolates, other tasty treats and a congratulations card. Didn't really have time to try out the bar and restaurant or other facilities, as too busy out and about experiencing this great city, but I am sure we will try to next time.

Unfriendly staff, sagging bed, poor continental breakfast, and building is not earthquake safe. Bartender refused to put on Raider game... In fact he lied that the bar did not receive the channel the game was on! Flood security light outside our room flooded our room through out the night.

great central hotel, good price, very close to macy's, empire state, madison square gardens, situated on lots of bus-subway routes which is a must when going shopping with lots of bags to carry. would stay here again............

No free internet in the rooms and even when using in the general areas, it's very slow and painful to use. 
The 'highlight' of the stay came one night when I had a long day of meetings and decided to order from the Draft pub in the hotel. Immediately I knew it was not hot (I didn't delay starting to eat) so I called the front desk to see if I could warm it up somewhere. They told me I could ... for $-- they would deliver a microwave! I told him the issue ... that I had JUST ordered from THEIR restaurant and it wasn't even luke warm. He said that was my only option unless I chose to return to the pub. I didn't return to my room with the food so that I would have to turn around and head back to the pub - not at all accommodating and slightly rude about it. 
Too expensive, they don't include breakfast or internet, refrigerators or microwaves. You can get a bottle of water for $- if you're thirsty ... but it's going to be warm. Would never stay here again. I would stay at the Marriott which is also in the Arts District.

Will definitely put ACME at the top of the list for return visits to Chicago.

Our room had a very comfortable king sized bed and also had a full kitchen w- fridge- freezer ( and icemaker) + microwave and dishes- utensils. Although we mainly ate out - it was nice to have plates- glasses and ice for the few times we brought pizza and soda back to the room. Our TV had a problem the final night and a very nice maintenance person came and repaired it within minutes! My wife and I stayed in this hotel from Mau -- till May --nd. We just got lost when we arrived in Time Square because we tried to use public transportation to get to the hotel, which I believed the best way to get to know about the way of life in the Big Apple. ( trains are numbered and lettered to identify which place you are heading.)
When we arrived at the hotel, the scent of the hotel was very striking. One can tell that this hotel is well-kept. The elevators are definitely quick due to it was organized in a way to avoid unnessary stops like control room and some floors that are not used by patrons.

Moreover, the restaurant located on the -th provides free muffins with different kinds of flavors. There is also coffee and milk. Whole milk, skim milk and half. The promptness of crew service, cleanliness of its hotel as well as the room price is very reasonable. More importantly, it is just - minutes away from Time Square and subway and train stations are accessible.
However this is not perfect. The shower room doesn't provide privacy. It only has curtains to separate the bed and restroom. Also, the window in the room 
doesn't have adequate blinds to cover the cracks so the building in the front could see you while taking a bath. It is truly embarrassing. 
Lets move on to the places that you needed to do to maximize your stay in New York.

Secondly, dine in in one of the prestigious hotels like Morimoto located on --th ave and between -- and -- street. The restaurant is hard to find because they did not properly label it. Fourthly, spend some time to take the subway by purchasing unlimited ticket for a week( if you plan to spend your stay for a week, otherwise choose the one day unlimited pass.)

So there you go, spend your holiday in New York and make the most out of it.

My recent stay at the Charlesmark was outstanding. The front desk staff was extremely helpful and friendly. The hotel has a wonderful design and atmosphere. Everything we asked for we received and the martini bar in the lobby was busy but comfortable. Thank you Charlesmark for making our stay so comfortable! We'll definitely be back and wouldn't stay anywhere else!

We stayed at this hotel while visiting the Maryland Zoo, the National aquarium and Port Discovery. The rooms were very comfortable and the location was very convenient. Great hotel, would definitely stay again.

Enough good things cannot be said about this property. From the time I called the Inn to book until my departure, the entire staff at this hotel was above and beyond excellence. I stayed one night pre-cruise on May - and was upgrade to a suite which overlooked the city-market area. The rooms were huge and the bed with the temp. mattress was to die for. If every hotel had this particular staff, rooms would be over booked. If you have time, definitely use the fifth floor terrace for a cocktail. It overlooks the market and has great sunsets.......all this while watching the ships come and go. Such a peaceful late afternoon cannot be beat! I was sad to go the next morning at check-out.....when in Seattle I will always stay at this property.

Stayed here for a national convention that was cancelled due to a transformer explosion that eventually shut down the power grid for the area. Upon check in on the Monday prior to the Tuesday night blackout, we were upgraded to a suite because they were unable to place a rollaway in the - double bed room which was very small. We paid $---night for access to the club lounge and internet access. I was disappointed I was unable to use my Starwood points to upgrade. The staff in the Club Lounge were extremely friendly and helpful. Breakfast was good. The evening club lounge was held in the lounge in the lobby where you could order $-- from the menu at no extra charge. We were on the --th floor in the Club Lounge when the explosion occurred and I got one picture of the event before going to the ground floor where they had not heard the explosion and were not aware of the event across the street. The hotel handled the crisis that extended over the next few days in stride...emergency lighting in the halls was adequate. Glow sticks were distributed for lighting in the rooms, continental breakfast, lunch and dinner box lunches were provided until the food in the kitchen ran out. The hotel provided several recharging stations on the -nd floor and lobby. There were - working elevators. Snacks, water and soda were available thru out our stay when we checked out Thursday night after the announcement the convention was cancelled. A few events were held at the Sheraton as well as many socials where food was provided. I was very impressed with the efforts of the staff and how pleasant they remained. Many customers were unhappy that no immediate discount was given upon check out, but a phone number was given to follow up for requests of discounts.
The standard rooms are small, the bathrooms are small...this seems to be a renovated older building. The suite was spacious and roomy with lots of light thru the windows.
Parking is expensive, but it is Boston where parking is at a premium everywhere. This hotel is a great location for getting around Boston. It is attached to the Hynes Convention Center and shopping.

Hotel Indigo is an understated, nice property. I came in town on a business trip and stayed there becaus the rate was within my company's budget. 
Overall Hotel: nice decor. Contemporary interior. Blonde hardwood floors in each room. Sizable bathrooms and vanity space. Fitness facility and restaurant onsite. Very clean!!! 
Staff: Valet could use some work. Front desk and restaurant staff (especially the breakfast crew) a great bunch. They are friendly and can get you moving if you are in a rush. 
Location: no need to stay anywhere else because this hotel is directly across the street from the Alamo and other higher priced (much older) hotels. San Antonio has a lot of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""historic"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" properties so be careful where you book. 
After my initial trip, I am happy to say I am - for - at this place now!!! Definitely a go!!

The hotel's laundy facilities (washer and dryer), are not listed on it's amenities list, are provided at no charge. A machine dispenses laundry detergent for $-.--. I was on a road trip from NY to North Carolina and decided to stop over in Washington D.C. since I hadn't been there in many years. I am so glad that I did and that I stayed here. We arrived twenty minutes before they started the daily wine reception in the lobby, so we went up and got situated and then went downstairs. We had a long drive due to road work and storms, so it was a nice surprise that we could check in and then enjoy a cocktail to take the edge off the day. 
The hotel is situated near many amazing restaurants, so you only have to walk a few blocks (if that) at night. During the day you can walk (if you like exercise like my companion and I do) or take the metro to all the sights. We ended up staying an extra night because we were so happy with the hotel and its staff. The rooms are comfortable and clean. The staff is so energetic and friendly that it's contagious. My boyfriend and I are planning another stay in the not so distant future and we will definitely be returning to the Palomar!!!

Fantatstic friendly hotel in a great neighbourhood area.
Service and cleanliness etc excellent.

Space is a commodity often not found in the hotels of NY. The rooms at the Tuscany were much larger than most NY hotels. My family and I stayed at this hotel for a few nights in June- July. This is the first time we'd looked to stay in a hotel in Hollywood as we normally are based in Anaheim when visiting Los Angeles. We were very pleased with this hotel from the outset. Very efficient and friendly staff, good hotel facilities, including the 'movie by the pool' nights which were very popular although we didn't get to do these as we were too busy at Universal.
The hotel has a free shuttle bus to Universal which is very very convenient and saves on parking at Universal which can be a right pain. The shuttle bus isn't the largest but it will return for guests who are unable to be facilitated immediately. It allows you to have a beer or two at Universal City walk.
The room was spacious and clean. 
Breakfast was efficient. However, I found the buffet a bit bland and not exactly inexpensive. Although kids eat free the menu for this is limited and we found we had to pay for breakfast our kids would eat.
The hotel is not far from the freeway although it is very easy to miss the turn-off if coming across from the Highway - and the Hollywood Freeway as you have to cut across very quickly once it merges with the ---. The hotel is within an easy drive of Warner Bros studios which I'd highly recommend.
The hotel wasn't the cheapest on our trip but represented good value given the comfort and location, The beds were very comfortable and we all slept soundly. Furthermore the carpark is secure and only accessible via a guest keycard.

Thoroughly enjoyed our - night stay at this hotel. The room was large and well appointed. The bed was comfortable and the linens good quality. The staff was very attentive and very friendly. The complementary nightly manager's reception was great. They offered a couple of appetizers (popcorn and nachos) and drinks (beer, wine, soft drinks, etc.). Very nice. The complementary breakfast was AMAZING! They had all the typical breakfast buffet items - eggs, meats, fruit, bagels, pastries, and hash browns... but they also had a cooked to order section, that offered pancakes and omelets, which were both delicious! Another location I use when traveling to NY on business. Great location, easy access and pleasant views. The staff is always amazing and the rooms clean and comfortable. Subway lines are about a --minute walk and cabs are always in the area.

Our room was a corner king-I'd have preferred to be up higher but since I was traveling with my little cat, we were on the pet floor, near the elevator which was fine! I didn't see other rooms but I believe that they may be somewhat different sizes and shapes. The room was pretty quiet-I really couldn't hear much street noise, and only minimal hall noise, (and well, the dog barking in an adjacent room!)
If you join the Loews YouFirst frequent guest program (which is free), you get free internet. Otherwise, it's $--.-- plus tax per day. The internet is WiFi in the hotel and it was pretty good speed. Also, there's a Keurig single cup coffee maker in the cabinet next to the TV-or a Starbucks across the street.
This property is right across from the Reading Terminal Market and PA Convention Center. It's only a couple blocks from City Hall and there's easy access to all the sites in town! I ran over to the Market to get some stuff for lunches and snacks and came back to settle in to do nothing.

There is only valet parking available-but the service getting my car was fast. The hotel was slow all weekend, but there was sufficient staff to handle the guests without long waits. All of the staff were very friendly. I needed engineering a couple times and they came quickly. Once, the bathroom was really hot.
