But do expect a smallish room (about the size of a typical American bedroom) with a very comfortable bed, a TV in an armoire, desk and chair, night tables, lamps, iron, blow dryer, phone, coffee maker, shampoos, several towels, etc. And a generous free breakfast is served on the lower level each morning. For the price, you could do a lot worse than this solidly middle class hotel! This was a safe and comfortable place. And there were absolutely no bugs! Believe me, I checked this out thoroughly after being terrified by reading reviews after I'd booked the room. The only complaint I had was that the ceramic tiles in the bathroom need to be regrouted as the grout looks kind of stained as years go by, which is not a big deal, just not appealing to look at. There is nowhere to put anything in the bathroom--any little shelf would have been nice. I couldn't put anything on top of the toilet tank because it was slanted, and the little pedestal sink had no room to put anything down. So the hotel management should consider adding a little shelves to the bathrooms. Other than that, this was a fine place to stay for the money.

We stayed at a two bedroom bungalow close to the end of the pier. We reserved the bungalow a year in advance. We were so disappointed because of the weather, but once we saw our view, even on the overcast day we had, it was fabulous! I can't say enough about the location of this hotel. Phenomenal. I wish it wasn't a rainy weekend or we would have been at the beach below all day every day. As it turned out, the kids wasted no time in going to the beach once the sun broke through the clouds on the evening before our departure and the morning of our departure. In any event, every wonderful review is spot on! While it is on the pricey side, they have a unique property and you never have to leave the neighborhood. We ordered Papa John's Pizza one evening and sat at the table outside on our patio. The kids loved it. It was fun watching the surfers every morning, too. At check out, they asked if we wanted to reserve for the following year. We tried to get something earlier to avoid the overcast weather. No chance. It was all booked. So, we'll be back the same time next year. To be critical, don't expect luxury. It's not that kind of hotel. And, the second bathroom's shower did have an RV feel to it, but as a whole, the cottage was clean and pretty. Also, the pier is open to the public during daylight hours, so it is not especially private. Still, the whole experience was great.

A relaxing trip to San Diego. 
The rooms were pleasing, the breakfast was good, bed comfy. The hotel is VERY family friendly.
The only minor complaint is the exorbitant parking fees and the atrium noises can be heard on the eigth floor.
It is also worth noting that the hotel is in a busy area, no where to take a leisurely family stroll.

The hotel was booked through a travel agent rather than directly but proved to be an excellent choice. The staff were very friendly, helpful and considerate. My luggage was left off my flight into New York and the hotel did everything in their power to assist me with resolving the problem. The room was very comfortable and reasonably large and the bathroom as one would wish. Situated opposite Grand Central Station on the corner of --th St and Lexington it is perfectly placed for Subway lines -, -, - & - and connections to -, -, - & N. R. Q lines at Times Sq & -th Avenue as well as being close to a number of attractions, all within walking distance.They have the Wheeltappers Pub adjacent where I enjoyed an excellent breakfast and there is access to a Gym, which I did not use. I would have no hesitation in recommending them and will definitely stay there again on my next visit to New York.

My family stayed at this Embassy Suites in Washington June -- thru June --. We loved this hotel. We have - people in our party, including our college age daughters. The suites were great. We shared on bathroom but that was no problem - even with girls because they were - other sinks with mirrors, lighting and plenty of outlets for blow dryers, straighteners, curing irons, etc. Or, if someone wanted to wash their face or brush their teeth. The suite was extremely comfortable. The free breakfast was great everyday. Plenty of seating for everyone and nice place to talk - not to loud. Many reviewers mentioned the kids. Yes, there were children, but the parents minded their children and there were no problems with the kids in this hotel. Happy Hour - we all enjoyed. Location of the hotel is perfect. Nice, clean, safe area. The entire staff was great at Embassy Suites. However, our favorite staff member and highlight of our stay? Hands down meeting Kevin. The gentlemen who greeted us when we first arrived. Kevin helped us with everything. He saved us so much time and money with his wise insightful tips on Washington. Thanks, Embassy Suites. Thanks Kevin. Hope to be back next year with the family.

We stayed here for our honeymoon and had a great, relaxing stay. The rooms are nicely decorated, had a very comfortable bed. The hotel is obviously older, the floors squeak when you walk. Everything was very clean. The continental breakfast that was included was very nice, and the evening wine and snacks were delicious. The hotel is close to Union Square, and it was very easy to get around the city from here.

we got there very tired and all I wanted was to get into the hotel room and get some rest. Instead, both of our rooms were dirty (pubic hair in the tub and on the restroom floor, urine on the toilet seat) they smelled dirty and like dog urine. Also the a-c barely worked in one of the rooms. I went to the front desk and Vincent was very polite and tried to help relocate us to different rooms. When we got to the other rooms, there was trash, the mirror was dirty and the tub as well. I went back to the front desk and demanded my money back to go to another hotel. After an hour and a half, Vincent convinced me to stay and give them one more chance. Finally the third time was a charm. But never again will I stay in this hotel. The only good thing that came out of this stay is the friendly service of Vincent! If they would have Vincent as housekeeping the hotel would be in better shape. Even though we were reimbursed for - night, that doesn't make up for the inconvenience and uncleanliness of the hotel.

I stayed here recently with my family and would highly recommend the Intercontinental to anyone staying in the Century City area. 
Service was top-notch from the valet on arrival to the desk staff at checkout.
We took advantage of the complimentary car and driver ( a beautiful Mercedes) to enjoy dinner at nearby Westfield Shopping Center.
The room and view from balcony was also well appointed and clean.

Was told this was the best hotel on the Bay. Was extremely disappointed within minutes of driving through. !-- to --- of the resort was under construction. Very little parking at all unless you want to park under ladders and construction crews. Room was very dated, carpet stained, a little smelly. Look like no updated since early --'s. Every time someone in hotel turns on water pipes make loud noises, all night long. Private beach is tiny. Does not feel like a - star hotel. The only thing good about the room was the view. But don't plan on your sliding door staying open, it's a constant fight!! This was supposed to be our anniversary trip, wow how sad!!

I was visiting Houston with two other family members. The staff was very helpful in getting us a room with a king-sized bed and a fold-out couch. The room was larger than an ordinary hotel room. The beds and pillows were very comfortable, the towels were thick and fluffy, and the extras things provided were good quality brands (eg. the coffee packets in the room were lavazza). It was generally quiet, one night we could hear someone's t.v. The hotel was in a convenient location, easy to get to Rice Village, Galleria, downtown, etc. The only negative is that when we called (twice) about a problem with the deadbolt we were told it would be repaired but it never was.

Decided to stay at the Beacon Hotel as it was close to Dupont Circle, other reviews were generally favourable and from its website it looked to be excellent. Our experience has been anything but excellent.
First the good things about the hotel. 
Its in a great location, although not as close to Metro as you might like. The check in was efficient if not overly friendly. We had to go find the doorman to help with our bags, it was raining and very cold standing outside and in the end the cab driver did this for us, gave him a good tip. 
The rooms are clean, but nothing to rave about. 
The bathroom is reasonably well appointed but the toilet is unnecessarily close to the wall and there is very limited shelf space to put toiletries on. There is plenty of hot water and the towels are ok. 
They have one guest coin washing machine and coin operated dryer, with luck reception will have washing powder. Thats about it for the good bits.
Here are the bad bits.
The airconditioning works in one part of the room only (we had a suite) so the other part has no air at all, its like sitting in a stuffy sauna with the heat on mild. The controls on the aircon dont work, and the fan makes it feel like you are sleeping in a wind tunnel. I had to manually adjust the vanes on the outlet so we didnt get blown out of bed, but it was fun watching the curtains get blown around. Called maintenance twice, in the end he said there was nothing he could do and we should have asked for a room with the new controls if only we knew.
Third night came back from a day out and the room was close to ---'. Called reception to be told that some guests had complained it was cold so the hotel had turned on the heating again and it was set centrally, nothing we could do! It was a very sweaty night inside while it was only -'c outside.
The television in the bedroom was on the blink, called maintenance, he said, oh you need to have it replaced. He left, I assumed to get a new one. Called down to see where he was, seems he was gone. Asked again the next day, and the next day, so far no new television!
Housekeeping alert! The housekeeping staff must be military trained. From just before -am you can hear them working their way down the hall, tap tap 'housekeeping' bang goes the door! If you dont leave the privacy tag on the door overnight your door will be thrust open as you are leaping out of bed to ask them to come back later. Really there is a split second between tap tap and bang the door opens.
Power outlets seem to have a mind of their own as to when they will and wont work. One of the outlets has a broken prong in it, mentioned to maintenance, nothing done about it.
Room service and breakfast menus are sparse. We had breakfast once only in the hotel. Didn't bother with the room service as there was nothing to entice one to eat it. More than $-- for a waffle and - pastries with some melon was enough for us, took the - minute walk to Starbucks, actually made New York look economical.
The hotel also promotes its roof top garden bar. Just don't expect it to be open before May! 
I really had much higher expectations of this hotel from the other reviews, it just does not live up to them. The staff are not at all friendly, and that goes from front door to housekeeping, with perhaps one or two exceptions.
I will not stay here again, it was not good value for money, the inconveniences far outweighed the conveniences and there was nothing that I could say that would encourage me to recommend it to anyone else.
I was very impressed with the penthouse suite, nice decor, very quiet, excellent staff, great breakfast, overall a perfect stay

Stayed for two weeks.
The things we feared:
Dirty rooms; theft of personal property; tenderloin beggars harassing us; tenderloin violence; poor service.
Things we looked forward to: location; cheap stay; convenient restaurant (Mel's Diner); convenient movie house (half block down).
The reality: Our room was clean and was kept clean, although there were - days when we had to request that the cleaning staff attend to our room at - p.m. None of the cleaning staff we spoke to were fluent in English.
Nothing stolen. from our room
Beggars had their territory and pretty much stuck to it.They were largely polite.
There were many (drunken?) nighttime yelling matches outside our hotel room (Geary and Vann Ness), but the double glazing shut out that noise. There was often garbage on Geary on the side of the hotel, and there is a persistent smell of urine in the same area, but this was not a problem in our -th floor room.
The immediate area down the hill on Van Ness is a little rough, but nothing to fear. The immediate area up the hill on Van Ness is more commercial and less tenderloiny.
Location generally is very good for buses etc. (We relied on public transport using a Muni pass, and we got everywhere we needed to get -- includng Muir Woods and the SF zoo -- very easily.)
The Golden Gate Transit buses to Marin County, Muir Woods etc stops one block up Van Ness (turn right out of the hotel) Buses to Muir Woods are limited, so call first.)
We booked a package through Travelocity about five months ahead of time and got the whole two weeks, accommodation and R-T air fare from Hartford CT for two for $-,---. The hotel portion was about $---, according to Travelocity's money-back gurantee, which separates the airfare from the hotel costs.
Overall, for the time of year (July -- ---), we thought that this was an excellent price.
Mel's DIner downstairs serves diner food. It screwed up a couple of orders that we took """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""to go"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to our room upstairs, but, generally, was an okay place to eat.
Tommy's Joynt across the road is overrated per its food quality. It serves cheap, institutional-type meat-and two-veg food.
Overall, we were perfectly content with the accommodation. We asked for, and received, a room with a little bit of a view of the city. Other rooms, we hear, face a brick wall. (Our room was (I think) ---). Our room wasn't very big, but we weren't planning on holding any conventions in it. We spent most of our in-house time sitting on the bed.
Coffee packets etc available but replenished in a very random fashion: sometimes none were replenished, other times there were three or four packets. None of the rooms have personal refrigerators. There is an excellent Whole Foods Market about five blocks up Van Ness and a half block up on California St.
The bathtub did have someone's hair in it when we arrived. The water did not drain very well after a shower. The toilet got blocked one day (nothing we did) and someone fixed it in short order.
The shower head was about a foot too low for me. (I'm - ft tall.) But the flow and temp were just fine.
The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""king"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" bed is actually two smaller beds pushed together. They did come apart slightly, but we really didn't notice that very much at all.
The bed itself was not an issue -- we slept just fine on it -- and there were five pillows, which was plenty for us.
Sheets and towels changed every day, if a little tardily at times.
Overall, we were releived that we didn't have to deal with any of the negative issues recorded by some other TripAdvisor reviewers.
A couple of the staff have a pretty aloof and arrogant demeanor, but that was not an issue. Other staff members were delightful.
Use of the hotel's computer is expensive for the budget traveler -- min. $- for -- minutes. But there is (apparently) free WiFi service.
The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""free"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" breakfast is a familiar selection of cheap fat, dough and sugar. We both do pretty well on a bagel or two and a coffee for breakfast, so it saved us a lot of breakfast expenses. But anyone who actually likes to eat real food in the morning might be better eating breakfast somewhere else.
We would consider staying at the Opal again, particularly if we got the same price. But we've stayed at better places in SF. (The Holiday Inn on Van Ness just up the street (Hotwire booking) was a much better deal.)
The Serrano, on the other hand, was a largely unpleasant experience, including a very troubling incident in which the clerk tried to withdraw $--- from our bank account when we booked in to account for an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""upgrade"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" we never asked for nor wanted. 
We've learned that we should only ever use credit cards that have barely a hundred dollars or so of credit available to secure the room, since places like the Serrano will charge undiscounted rates -- and add the difference -- to guests who prepay and book through discount brokers such as Tavelocity, Hotwire etc.
One final warning: The Opal stocks its rooms with a booklet of local businesses restaurants etc, which is probably very useful. However, the chicken and noodle meals that we ordered delivered from Brandy Hos, Hunan Food (--- Columbus Avenue), which is a recommended restaurant in the booklet, was absolutely disgusting. It was in parts gristle and raw. The soup tasted like urine and the rice nearly broke our teeth. The chicken tasted raw and like it was just retreived from the hold of a Spanish Galleon after three months of sitting in salt. 
One bite and I was gagging. at $-- for two meals (a treat we allowed ourselves), it was an expensive lesson for two budget travelers.
On the other hand, the Crepe Vine (Irving and --rd Streets) offers excellent food. The N-Judah goes right there from Market Street.)
Dottie's True Blue Cafe (--- Jones Street) is overrated per its food quality, but is an interesting dining experience per its reputation and intriguing menu offerings. Although, be prepared to line up outside and to be harrassed in line by local beggars etc.

I stayed at this hotel three years ago. I got a great price and didn't have to suffer for that. The room was spacious and seemed newly renovated and we had no problems either with the staff or the room.
I've stayed in several --star hotels, and of course these are better. But if you consider what you get for your money, this hotel is as good as it gets!
I'm going back to New York for a romanitc vacation in February, and we've booked - nights at the Park Central.
I can't wait to go back!

Great location. Small room but clean with modern decor. Great view. Very convenient. Concierge was eager to help and had great recommendations. Remodel was going on but was not disruptive. Bathroom is extremely small. Overall great trip and stay!

 First the good.

If this is the future of the Courtyard brand, then I""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""m out. I love Courtyards because of opening windows-balcony doors, quiet atmosphere, free parking, real glass and good value which means no parking fees.

I was petrified about going to this hotel after reading all then reports on here, from clean to bed bugs and creaky lifts. The staff were okay, i requested a low floor after hearing about the creaky lifts, and when we got there they had put me on --th floor, after arguing with a lady who said she had nothing else the manager came over and told me i could be on -nd floor - thank god, as my husbanc used the lifts and they were very scary - rickety, unreliable and very small! room was clean - no bed bugs but i did pull off the dodgy looking blanket, room had - queen beds which were very comfortbale. Stayed here in November, the hotel is clean and staff were very friendly and efficient.
The location of the hotel is excellent, couldnt ask for better, the rooms were nice and were big by new yoek standards! My only complaint is the lobby, its too small for a hotel this size and gets extremly busy with people coming and going, wifi is only available in the lobby so alot of people there. But its not a major thing!

I didn't know what to expect after I booked - nights through priceline. It seemed like a Loved it or hated it hotel.
First of all, the escalator on the arlington exit broke, so we had to lug - ---lb suitcases up a couple flights of stairs...not fun =| The Park Plaza has - exits, and the hotel was very easy to find (signs posted everywhere at the exit of the subway). We were able to check in early (at -pm) and although priceline booked us for a full-size room, they were able to change it to a queen. (the - doubles and kings were all booked because of a cheerleading competition..>(..) That upgrade was done w-o a hassle. Our room was on the -th floor (one of their newly remodeled floors) and the elevators were very fast (there were -) and the place was polished, clean and very nice.
Our doors were a little weird (kind of reminded me of a fridge), but the room was clean, the bed comfy, the sheets clean and the smell was pleasant. Our bathroom was definitely remodeled because the tile was white and the tub new. I LOVED the twin shower sprays! 
Anyway, I had no complaints whatsoever! When we checked out, we were able to leave our luggage w- the hotel while we continued to sight-see before our flight. The staff was friendly and very helpful.

First the pluses: The St. Regis is well located on Fifth Avenue near Tiffany's and other high end shops. It is a very short walk to Central Park and a five minute walk to Rockefeller Plaza. The beds are comfortable, the room size is quite good and it is a Grande Dame New York hotel property.
Now for the the mediocre to minuses:
Our two rooms looked out onto brick walls. One room had very little natural light and the other had virtually no natural light at any time of day. When booking the room, I noted to the St. Regis reservation clerk that I had seen an advisory on Trip Advisor that some rooms looked out on brick walls with no natural light. As this trip was a gift to my parents I told the agent that it was important to me that their room, at least, had some kind of view. I was assured that at $-,---.-- per night per room (and as a Starwood Preferred Guest) I was getting superior rooms with some sort of view. It was disappointing for me when that did not happen although some may not be concerned by that.
Also, the service was only """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""good"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and not the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""excellent"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I would expect paying the rack rate of $-,---.-- per night. For example, The St. Regis prides themselves on providing butler service. Personally (and this is another case where personal judgement comes in), I did not find having a butler terribly useful. For me they really just became someone else to tip (and the expected tip, as a per cent of room rate, was high). Our butler was polite but essentially just showed us around the room as a bus boy normally would do. They did offer to serve coffee or tea in the morning as part of our wake up call which is a nice idea. However, as I was travelling with my young daughter I asked if she could have a hot chocolate instead. The butler advised that I would have to make that arrangement through room service at a charge of something in excess of $--.--. At $-,---.-- per night, I think the hotel could have been flexible enough to offer hot chocolate for the wake up call. However, I will leave that up to the reader to decide. For me it was a niggly item that at this price point should not happen. Also, our room rate included a bowl of fresh fruit but on arrival we only had an empty bowl. Not a big problem especially since the butler said the bowl would be filled right away. However, it ended up taking two reminder calls and, even at that, the fruit did not arrive until the next afternoon. Again, just a niggly but one I don't expect at that price point. Butlers will also do a complimentary shoe shine overnight, and will iron up to two garments per day gratis. We did not need those services so there was not advantage to us there, but I recognize others may find that service useful (although with or without butlers most hotels at this price point offer at least the complimentary shoe shine and the expected butler tip at the end of the trip would have more than covered the cost of having a garment or two ironed).
Finally, the food at the hotel is mediocre and, with the exception of the bar which has a beautiful mural that is worth taking a look at, the central restaurant suffers from poor lighting and an overall bland feel. To those choosing to stay at the hotel I would recommend eating meals elsewhere (even the highly touted afternoon tea was uninspired). Thanks to the great location there is a variety of very good restaurants and eateries including several that offer high tea.
So there you have it. I have nothing terrible to say, it was just below expectations. On my next visit to New York, I will seek a hotel in the same locale but will forego the butler in favour of a room with a view and natural light.

I am really picky of where I stay at and thought that I would give this hotel a try because of it's location and my last minute decision to get a hotel.The location was awesome and very safe feeling- walking distance to everything you want to see in Chicago! The room was SUPER small... But It had a nice view of the John Hancock Tower and other buildings. The front desk people were always friendly and super nice. The valet was $-- dollars but for Chicago, that's not bad! The people who ran the valet were extremely nice and engaged us in conversations and helped us with directions, and where to eat, etc. I would stay here again.. Not for long periods of time but the one night I stayed here I enjoyed it. Comfy bed was a + and the large bathroom was great also. People staying here seemed happy in the restaurant and in the lobby. Good atmosphere.

The customer service at the lobby was terrible. One lady, Sonya, was incredibly rude. No one greeted me at the desk when I walked up the desk to check in on the first day. I really like this hotel. I often stay here when I go to Boston for business and it is in a great location, the rooms are nice and clean with a big bathroom and it is somewhat reasonably priced.

Chose this hotel based on Frommers Guidebook recommendation. Numerous gliches and unresolved airconditioning problem. Dirty robe with used tissue in pocket hanging in closet upon arrival - but arms of robe put into pockets & belt tied like it was fresh from laundry....Ewwwwwww. Just returned from our first visit to NY with husband and - children (inc - teens). Originally booked - nights at Pennsylvania Hotel but changed to Novotel after reading reviews on Tripadvisor! Our --night stay at the Hotel Elysee was all we had hoped for
and more! Our room (junior suite, no. ---) was perfect -- including THE most comfortable hotel bed we have ever slept in! The entire staff was attentive, gracious, courteous and helpful, from the concierge crew to the young women who delivered our room service breakfasts to the doormen and bellmen. The location is unbeatable -- close to all the shopping anyone could want, plus Rockefeller Center, Central Park, and many terrific restaurants.
An added bonus is the Monkey Bar restaurant downstairs -- we ordered room service dinner two nights we were there and marveled at the quality of the food. We are from California's Wine Country, a bastion of fine dining, but no meal we've had in Sonoma or Napa rivaled what Chef Christopher Cheung is turning out at the Monkey Bar. Bravo!
Having walked through the likes of the Waldorf-Astoria, the Palace and other grand hotels nearby, we would still opt for the boutique charms of the Elysee. Having such a lovely and comfortable place to return to after each day's adventure made our New York sojourn special indeed. Worth EVERY penny.
We look forward to our next trip to Manhattan, and will definitely plan to stay at the Elysee.

We traveled to Boston for a family member's wedding and the reception was being held at the Hotel Commonwealth. After careful consideration, we booked a room at the Commonwealth and we are very glad that we did! It was an excellent hotel. 
We arrived after having been traveling literally all day and we were exhausted. This hotel is in an excellent location, just a --- min walk from the Empire State Building. There is a great pizza place on the corner!! Our room was very clean and accomadation cleaned it every day and left us clean towels etc...we never had to wait to use the shared bathrooms and they also were very clean and the water was always hot!! there are sinks in the rooms which is very handy...the staff at the front desk were very helpful and also booked us a cab back to JFK....will stay here again on my next trip to New York!!

The hotel is in an old renovated building that was updated and very modern. We were initally put off by the $--.-- a night parking fee so we did not rent a car. Well , i looooooove this hotel, i went with my boyfriend for a couple of days in July it was awesome :) i mean our view was not the greatest because we had a horrible roof right next to the window but inside everything was lovely, we booked a junior suite that we really enjoyed ;) Ill recommend you that type of room, but try to request a high floor!

The hotel is in a great location and central to the library, short walk to Herald Square, and Time Square. We were able to access shops, restaurants, a great park without having to walk far. I met -- wonderful friends for our annual long weekend together, and the hotel was perfect for our group. The lobby felt like it was designed just for us. The breakfast was very good and well tended. The room was comfortable, and the rates were fantastic.

Fantastic hotel. When we arrived we thought we were miles away from all the glitz and glamour yet it was only a --mins ride on the bus, bus stop just outside the hotel door. I couldn't believe the pool area and that we were swimming at -pm and lying in the heated spa, watching the stars, then sitting next to the large poolside fire. This was fantastic. -- - -- for a city break hotel. Gorgeous room, huge bathroom and minutes from times square. Couldn't have asked for more. Love this hotel and will return whenever in New York.

My husband & I spent an overnight stay recently at the Hotel COmmonwealth, we were so impressed by the staff and the premises, the selection of restaurants was superb, all round we were made to feel that the Hotel would go bove and beyond to make our stay with them an amzing experience. BRAVO!!

Easy to find, within walking distance of most anything downtown. Nice rooms, very clean, bed was comfortable, staff was very nice. We did not here street noise, but we were on the top floor and it was a weekend.
The only negatives were:

We just returned from one night at the Custom House (July --th, ----) and were very pleased. Because we checked in later in the afternoon there were no rooms left on the upper floors so we stayed in a loft room on the second floor. The hotel staff were polite and knowledgeable about where to dine and shop. The observation deck on the --th floor affords spectacular views of Boston and the harbor. Noise was not an issue at all, we even commented on how quiet it was outside as compared to other hotels we have stayed in in other major cities, although we were there on a Sunday night. We stopped by the Westin Waterfront first, but after getting a quote of $---.-- less per night over the phone through central reservations which the front desk clerk said he couldn't match, even after checking with his manager, we went on to the Custom House which gladly honored the rate quoted by Marriott's central reservations. I do hope that someone reads this so far down on the mixed review list. I was in four suites in three days. Never accept the -- line of rooms, small and near the AC compressor (eg. ---, ---). Insist on seeing your room first although you will be told they are full and cannot change.

Just got back from a mini weekend vaca to NYC. Stayed at the Staybridge Suites Times Square, which is about - blocks from Times Square (TS). We also rode in style (hotel car service) for $-- flat fee to the LaGuardia airport, which we thought was convenient and reasonable. i just recco'd this place to friends...stayed there years ago, and it was OK....things have gone downhill dramatically...the hotel is filthy and old...the toilet seat was peeling paint, my friends had to step over homeless urine soaked people *on the hotel property* to get to their room...they left after one night. the location is good if you are an urbane hipster -- its close to the castro, hayes valley and the mission, but the massive influx of homeless and crazy people there has dramatically increased since the freeway came donw. go elsewhere. anywhere else.

Upon opening our room door the stench hit us, we walked in, debating whether we wanted to stay & promptly spotted -, -, ... - roaches. Running out of the room to the front desk, they refused to refund our money (fortunately Citibank saved us from the charge).

We stayed at this hotel - years ago and again this year. The rooms are clean and it is nice that there are two separate rooms where you can close the door between them. Overall the experience was okay but I would stay elsewhere if I had the choice next time as it was more expensive than other places close just as nice.

I am here for a training but sure has been taken care of by the staff of St. Gregory, especially the phenomenal professionalism manifested by one of your staff named Shadi. Again, I think the management of the Hotel and Suites is on the right track. Keep it up!

This was my first stay at the fairly new Ritz Carlton in Dallas. The rooms are nice and the common areas and restaurants are first-rate. It is definitely one of the best hotels in Dallas.
The hotel service was what you'd expect from a top end hotel. The employees were helpful, friendly, and out-going. 
The room was nice. I was in a junior suite with a good sitting area. (While it was spacious, I think the Stoneleigh down the street has a slightly better junior suite in terms of layout.) The bed was very comfortable. It had a goose-down mattress pad which was a bit soft for me, but I think most people would like.
The bathroom was very nice. It had two sinks, a separate commode, a bathtub and a stand up shower. The water pressure was acceptable and the towels were fresh and plentiful.
While at the hotel we had an excellent breakfast in the Fearings restaurant. It was pricey, but worth every penny. Some of the folks I was traveling with had dinner there and said it was also excellent. In the evening we had some drinks at the bar and it was very lively and had great service.
The hotel has good valet parking and the valets were helpful with directions, etc. 
If you have friends or colleagues coming to uptown or downtown Dallas, this is a very safe bet.

This hotel promises a lot but all it can deliver on is its location which it can't screw up.
Nothing is as it seems.
the bathrobes aren't in the rooms, the wireless internet isn't available IN THE ROOM!
The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""business center"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is a small room with a printer which does not work. The hotel staff knows it doesn't work but does nothing nor puts a sign on it so you can waste -- in. trying to make it work.

There is not even a guide to the few TV channels they get in the room. 
Do yourself a favor - spend a little more and get a hotel with decent, basic service.

Just returned from - day stay at Hotel Giraffe in NYC. Great location, handy to subway and since hotel in midtown, a relatively short distance to anything of interest. Our room was very clean and quiet , shower drained quickly, and the beds were fabulous. The breakfast in the lobby was more than adequate, and the coffee and cookies in the evening always welcome. The service was excellent--Jose, in particular was very helpful getting us started and pointed in right direction. I don't know when we will make it back to New York, but this is where we'd stay.

I stayed in this property while attending a large convention. It was further away from the Convention Center than the other properties, but I chose it because they offered a lower rate than the host hotels. I heard it referred to by a few attendees as the “Dreary Drury”, however the room was basic, but clean. I had events throughout the afternoon, so I was unable to participate in their afternoon break service. 
With respect to customer service, here is where it is a bit lacking. Many like to use this term, but will they actually live up to its meaning? Good customer service is saying hello to the guests, even calling to see if their room is ok. That they did. Exceptional customer service is going above and beyond the norm. I had left an item in my room and realized it after I returned home and unpacked my things. I called the hotel and wanted to pay to have them ship it back to me. Someone would call me back. Many calls back to hotel. No return call. I called one of the managers and he said he would check on it and call back. No return call. I guess maybe my request was insignificant to them and therefore, didn’t warrant much effort. I had checked out and was no longer staying in their property, so why bother. Putting extra effort forth to accommodate the guest, even after the they have left for example, would have said a lot. That is what separates good, basic service from exceptional guest service.
“Make it right for the customer every time, every visit”? Not really, but it sounds good.

We booked this last minute as a park and fly deal. The room was only $-- for the night which I thought with the shuttle and free parking was a steal. The rooms here are coming along. The ad makes is sound like select comfort sleep number beds, Thats not in every room. Ours sure didnt have one. We slept on a sheet of plywood that night. At least thats what it felt like. Other than that its all you should expect from a $--.-- stay.

Good for tourists who plan on spending most of their time sightseeing, not good for the business traveler looking to relax in the hotel room. The location is the only bonus of staying in this hotel.

The restaurant was a little disappointing - I probably wouldn't go back to it again. But we were tired of finding places around town. The best perk (of course you pay for it with the $-- parking fee) is the two Voss water bottles in the car every time we picked it up. We did a lot of driving during the day and this was a great perk. I plan on staying here again - at least untl the Mandarin Oriental opens next door - then I will have to pick the best one.

We have visited the Crowne Plaza Time Square probably - or - times so far. We recently stayed at the Hilton on East Market St. When we had a problem with the sleep system bed, the wonderful staff went above and beyond what we expected. Although the hotel was extremely busy, the hotel staff went out of their way to make us feel like we were their only guests. I will adopt this hotel as our corporate hotel in NYC.

Only problem was getting a cab in front of the hotel. It was in walking distance to the theater district and that helped. We did go to the Museum of Natural History one day and it was amazing.
We will return to Ink--.

Clean, quiet, centrally located, next to metro, food stores and restaurants right next to it, wall street a -- mins walk from it, great free cookies and coffee downstairs, and very polite staff. Everything was nice, functioning, clean and comfortable in the room. Highly recommended.

Had an excellent three-night stay in a clean, cozy room, staff were very polite-friendly. I plan to stay at The Orchard again on my next trip to San Fran. If possible, try to get a room on the front side (Bush Street) of the building.

It is literally right next to Reading Terminal Market and very easy access by foot or subway to the rest of the city. The Hotel staff were super-friendly and helpful. No problems dropping bags before game and then checking in after. Room was clean and comfortable.

The only complaint we had was one that probably would not bother most people, but is worth mentioning. Our room was on the second floor, overlooking the harbor - a pretty nice view. During the day we could watch the activity of the neighboring marina, the boats sailing on the harbor, and the planes taking off and landing at Logan Airport in the distance. But shortly after sunset, the hotel would turn on some VERY bright floodlights that were pointed right up at our windows to illuminate the building. Unfortunately, it completely wiped out all view from the window, so relaxing with a drink while overlooking the harbor in the late evenings and nights was out of the question.
Overall our stay was excellent, and we would not hesitate to stay there again.

I really enjoyed this hotel. Great pool and jacuzi, the view was magnificient, and not to mention the free breakfast was a great amenity. The flat screen was big and the small fridge came in very handy for beverages. The hotel employee's were more than helpful and made us feel very welcome. The font desk clerk was extremely amicable. However, the room smelled rancid, and the grounds were not clean. The gardens surrounding the pool were filled with stagnant water, and empty beer cans. four friends - we stayed January ---- for three nights; - queen beds; kitchenette; and living room area; it was great; would definitely recommend hotel; they were running a winter special at the time too, which was good; plus it included a free breakfast at Nice Matin downstairs, excellent; we had a blown fuse with the hairdryer situation; they fixed it immediately; and I mean immediately;

There were four of us in the room it was a little snug but what others have said in there reviews I didn't think it was bad at all. We had a new room on the --th floor had a wonderful view. Sure we had breakfast but it's like any other breakfast that you get at any other comfort inn. The subway is very close to the hotel walk around the corner and your there. However, if you like listening to the bathroom habits of complete strangers in the next room, or you like hearing every word of other guests conversations while youre lying in bed, or if you like being woken up every - minutes by slamming doors, TVs and children running around in the bedroom below, then this is definitely the place for you.
Having read other reviews saying this hotel should be a - star hotel, I can only assume that none of those reviewers have ever stayed in a decent - star hotel. The carpets were filthy, the kitchen was ill-equipped and we had a colony of spiders living on the living-room ceiling. Our toilet backed up and overflowed and when i contacted reception to ask for help, no one came. When I called again, I got told that the member of staff Id spoken to had forgotten about it.
There were one or two staff who were helpful but no more than I would expect from a hotel. My boyfriend was really unwell at the time and he needed peace, quiet and rest so I ended up spending a day searching for alternative accomodation in LA.
When we told the staff that the noise in the bedroom of our suite was intolerable, they couldnt understand as that was supposed to be the quite part of the hotel!! 
We would never stay there again. If youre a noisy person with noisy kids, maybe your own noise would drown out that of everyone else. If youre a quiet couple looking for a romantic get-away with privacy - forget it.

Location is excellent - I came for a convention at Moscone which is just a couple of blocks away. Stayed in King deluxe room - large, beautiful room very clean. Staff extermely helpful and friendly. Many free amenities -you can ask for a coffeee machine , there are copies of the NY times, etc.
There is only one elevator location - they are very swift, but if you ask for a room away from the elevators you may be in for a long walk .
My only gripe - the fitness room is minimal - one bike, one treadmill, one elliptical machine. If you are on a schedule, you may find none are available. They do offer discounted day passes for a gym, but it is three blocks away - not what you want to do at -am in the dark.
On the whole - great stay.

The hotel is located in an excellent location, central for walking everywhere. The front desk staff were pleasant, although not terribly knowledgable and we had to ask for information regarding the hotel rather than being offered information about internet access, gym, etc. 
The rooms are not the biggest, but they are clean and decently appointed. The bathrooms are spacious. The bed is very comfortable with fluffy duvet and plenty of pillows.

The location was great – close to Fanueil Hall, the Boston Common, the Freedom Trail, several T stations, all kinds of restaurants, etc. I was a bit worried, having read past reviews, but the size of the room was just fine and had plenty of room for the two of us. The bathroom was small but sufficient, had plenty of mirrors and hot water, although the walls could have used a coat of paint. 
The express check-in machine was a nice idea but it wasn't working properly so it was great to have a staff member available at the desk. The woman who checked us in was very personable. Unfortunately, I can't say the same for some of the other staff members, but all were efficient and knowledgeable.
The purified water station in the hall was great but the idea of a guest supply closet is just silly. We actually checked it several times each day for extra pillows and-or towels but found it empty every time. (Why not just have the extras in the room already?) Along the same lines, if you choose not to have your linens changed daily, remember that you'll probably run out of such things as shampoo and toilet paper!
If you get one of the –-- rooms (---, ---, etc.), I suggest you ask for a different room. These rooms are literally right off the elevators and you'll hear the foot traffic. It seems that even the most polite hotel guests will tend to talk loudly while waiting for the elevators, at all hours of the day or night, not realizing there's a guest room right there.
A word of warning – whatever you do, do not try to take the stairs to another floor or down to the lobby. Once you're in the stairwell, the door will lock behind you and you will have to walk all the way down, out onto the street and back in through the front door of the hotel. It's an interesting trip if you're wearing only pajamas and wooly socks.
The Elephant and Castle restaurant next door to the hotel is a bit expensive but the food, while nothing fancy, is not bad. It's obviously very popular, always crowded and you can charge your dinner to your hotel room. It's a great place to have a nightcap before heading up to bed.
While our stay at the Club Quarters was nice enough, I'm not sure we'll hurry back. If you're planning to see Boston, take tours, see shows or go out for dinners and all you need is a roof over your head and a pillow under it, this hotel will do just fine.

Estela Estrada and the Sheraton Gateway, Los Angeles conference team provided EXCELLENT service for our - day meeting. This is our -th time hosting this meeting at their property. If you are looking for a great venue for your next event with an award winning team consider the Sheraton Gateway Hotel, Los Angeles. It’s the experience that keeps us coming back!

My husband was having surgery at Mt. Sinai, so we chose the Marmara since hospital patients & their guests get a reduced rate. It was very clean and everyone in guest services was very accomodating. It had a lovely kitchenette which was helpful, since my husband needed the use of the refrigerator and microwave due to his restricted diet prior to his operation. If your in New York City for the weekend and you just need a place to crash that is in a convenient area, then the Broadway Plaza is fine. The hotel itself is nothing to sneeze at. However the rooms were clean and averageT size for a New York City hotel. The location is the best thing about it. So if you more like me and just need a clean, safe place to lay your head and you are more worried about location and going out. Then this is a good spot.

We had an excellent time! The room was clean and it looks new! We had a great dinner at Tickled Trout restaurant by the hotel and the room service was also superb! We will definitely use Ramada Hotel again for our future trip!

The general manager of the Bullfinch could not have been more accomodating online as I made my arrangements. I don't know how the housekeepers change the linens, which, by the way were very nice. The room appeared to be freshly painted, we had no problem with the carpet BUT the furniture looked like it came from a hotel surplus warehouse. On the third night, we rounded the little desk downstairs to find a note on the ONE elevator that it was out of service. The next morning, the door to the stairwell started slamming open and closed very early giving us the clue the elevator had not been repaired. Two very courteous bellmen helped us down to the lobby that morning. The same gentleman who was manning the desk the night before was still there, and holding up well, actually. He'd already removed the third night's taxes and fees, about $--, from the bill, a fair adjustment. Would I stay at the Bullfinch in Boston again? No. It's on the fringe of a neighborhood that is being renovated, but it's not terribly desirable yet. I've never, in Europe or NYC or anywhere, stayed in a room that was as small as ours was. To their credit, the staff could not have been nicer, more polite, or professional. A person who is fit and not terribly picky would probably find it a bargain.

This hotel is In a great location and an excellent value. Very clean and perfect for longer stays with stocked kitchenette and laundry right in the bedroom. Bathroom was a tad small but really there was nothing bad about this place. It was within walking distance of lots of places to see. Wish I could have stayed longer. Highly recommend!

Breakfast was not anything like the typical Embassy Suites breakfast. The cook was very friendly, but the food quality was average at best and they did not offer pancakes or french toast, which was what my son was asking for.
Overall, the hotel looks great, and should be much better.

Perfect stay in the city. We arrived early, and our room was not ready, but they could place us in a lower-class room immediately. You can walk from the lobby through a door and boom you are in the mall.. We checked out around -:-- the next day and that was a breeze as we only owed for the parking. The $--- for incidentals that was held initaly dropped off my credit card the next day (it took - weeks almost at the Sheraton in Philly!) and I was wished well and asked to return soon.
Overall my wife and I were happy with our stay and would do it again, especially at the price we received. We didn't feel treated any differently because we booked Priceline or any of that jazz. While it wasn't all that different than my stay at the Sheraton I will say that the location is beyond great and the mall connection is very cool. We will return to see some of things we missed during our short stay!

I booked this hotel with great expectations. I had family visiting from outside the country and wanted them to have a good experience in Chicago. Very good , quiet, easy location, checking in was verry easy and not troublesome. Beds were very good , air conditioner worked , easy access to elevator.
