We have travelled extensively over the years and stayed in several - star hotels around the world but this was our first visit to NYC and chose Trump based on its location and reputation. We visited NYC with family members in early September for - nights and had - Executive City View Suites on the --th floor with one of them being a corner suite. This was the best of the lot since it has better views. 
The rooms are nicely decorated (modern), in good condition and very well equipped (inc. two --inch flat screens, fully equipped kitchen, charger for all mobiles, ice machine, coffee machine, powerful air con etc..) and spacious. The equipment is easy to use and the staff are always willing to assist if need be. Bathroom is a bit small though. My wife and I stayed in the corner suite (no. ----) with our - kids and we loved it. The kids had their own Trump Kids goodie bags plus kids slippers, night gowns, DVDs and games. The only glitch was on the first day when the kids sofa bed had a stained sheet and missing pillow....although this was sorted within -- mins, it just shouldn't happen in this sort of hotel. 
The staff throughout the hotel are exceptional and they do their utmost to offer top notch service. They impressed us. 
In Room dining and service is good but a bit slow. Worth visiting the Whole Foods Market across the road. 
Daily complimentary bottles of water and chocolates are a nice touch although Wifi should be free when paying such room rates. 
We will return to Trump International Hotel & Tower.

My family and I spent a wonderful week here at the JW in San Antonio (husband, wife, -- year old son and - year old daughter). I am a Marriott Rewards platinum member and used points for our stay and I must say it was worth all of the time saving my points. My wife and I are already talking about how we can make it back here again soon. 
Check in - Got here on a Thursday evening and check in was fast and easy. They offer valet parking, but I went with self-parking to save the cost. It's a bit of an uphill walk, but was no more than a couple of minutes. I found parking pretty easy except one day when the resort was sold out. The lobby was big and beautiful. 
Staff - The staff throughout the stay were very accommodating and always helpful. We are pretty self-sufficient, but the concierge helped with a couple requests and the housekeeping staff were great throughout the stay. 
Room - We got very lucky with the best upgrade we could have ever asked for. I sent a note letting them know we had - people sharing a room with kids and would appreciate a room with extra space if at all possible. D reached out to us and took great care of us. We actually got a regular room with two beds and a connecting suite that included a king size bed and a sitting room with a pull out sofa. The extra space was incredible. The beds were very comfortable and the bathrooms were great. Great quality and plenty of space. 
Pool area - Wow is all I can say. The water slides were a big hit with the kids. The two bigger ones were definitely a lot of fun and the smaller one going into the lazy river was fun throughout the stay. The pool area is really laid out well and the padded lounges are a nice plus. It's great that there is a huge family pool, a lazy river, the slides and an adult only pool with great views. 
Restaurants - We enjoyed many meals at the sports bar, pool restaurant and main restaurant. A few nights were busy, but most times there was no wait and the service was great. The quality of the food was good and I was pleasantly surprised at the prices which I thought was pretty reasonable. Usually resorts like this really jack up prices for even basic meals, but could get sandwiches-burgers for like $----- and liked the kids meals were like $-. We didn't drink much so can't give any tips on that.
Location - There are great views in the Hill Country. It's only about -- minutes from the airport and easy to find, but you will need a car. There isn't much within -- minutes of the resort, but there is a lot around outside that -- minute loop. 
Other amenities - The resort grounds were beautiful and well taken care of. There was a kids club and workout facility which we didn't use. The kids loved the nightly s'mores near the pool. There were always activities and little games for the family going on. The JW is part of the TPC of San Antonio golf facilities (they say only members or JW guests can play there). There are two course. My son and I played on the Canyons course. It was pretty hot and there weren't many players. Course was nice, but greens weren't that great because of the lack of rain.
Keep up the great work JW.

An amazing hotel! Very clean, comfortable rooms with ample room for a hotel in New York. 
The room was more like a small apartment and contained two double beds, a bathroom and fully equipped kitchen. Given current exchange rates, should you wish to limit your budget whilst on holiday, the kitchen enables you to cook your own meals if you chose to. 
Hotel staff were very welcoming and friendly and were always on hand to offer advice on exploring New York. A selection of different novelty pillows were available and fun to try.
The hotel is excellently located within a short walking distance from the Empire State Building, some bars, restaurants and shops. Public transport links are close by so the hotel is in a perfect location for exploring other areas of New York.
If we have the chance to return to New York, we would return to this hotel as it really made our holiday a great one.

I was traveling solo and was not expecting so many families. No quiet time to be had by the pool. Close proximaty to beaches, so all was not lost. Very nicely kept rooms. Clean. Views of the bay. Nice place for family vacationers.

This very pleasant hotel is close to the Phoenix airport but you don't have a problem with airport noise. They do provide a -- hour airport shuttle. Efficient check in and free chocolate chip cookies. The rooms are true two room suites with a living area with couch, chair and large screen tv, a kitchen dining are with a small table, and a nice bedroom. Plenty of closet and drawer space. There is a very pleasant interior courtyard with outdoor pool, hot tub, fountains and tables. This Doubletree provides a complimentary buffet breakfast which was quite ample--fruit, cereals, pastries, eggs, juices, coffee, etc. It is served in their restaurant (we didn't actually eat any other meals there, so I can't speak to the restaurant-bar itself). They have a small business center with free internet access and free printing (very convenient for boarding passes, etc.) The hotel is in an office type area, but is within a couple of blocks of the Chinese Cultural Center of Phoenix, which includes several restaurants. We went to the Szechuan restaurant which was very good and quite inexpensive. There is also a very interesting Asian market there which was fun to browse.

We had a lovely time at a terrific little hotel in a great city.
It's in the thick of the business district so I'm sure there are more scenic ends of town to stay in for a longer holiday. For our purposes, however, it was perfect. The hotel is situated between the Gaslamp district where the nightlife and restaurants happen, Balboa Park for the cultural activities and zoo, and the shore with the USS Midway. 
Kristina on the desk looked after us very well indeed, cheerfully helping us solve a number of challenges. The in-house restaurant was great with friendly, efficient staff and tasty food. The beds were wonderfully comfortable and all in all, we had a fine time.

I absolutely loved this hotel with its suttle whimsical Beauty and the Beast style. The suite was very spacious though I've heard the regular rooms are a tight squeeze. By far the best feature was the huge window in the shower! Never had a view like that while in the shower before!! Actually the whole room was floor to ceiling windows and simply breathtaking! 
Another smart feature is the iPads they provide in all the rooms... much appreciated :)
The food was good... complimentary breakfast was basic continental but more than adequate and a good start to long days of walking the city. The same room for breakfast is a lounge-bar at night and is beautyfully decorated with stunnig chandeliers and a ceiling of windows... great room with an energetic vibe and many locals coming to hang out at the bar on any given night.
The service was stellar and the location perfect
I'd go back without hesitation :)
Enjoy your trip!

The Hilton America's Houston was perfect and I have to give it the best rating. The location was wonderful, my family and I stayed there for a convention and the hotel like others said is directly connected. Perfect. The green buses that run downtown are right there as well and I LOVED the Hilton Downtown Shuttle as well. We utilized both and found them very helpful. We also went to an Astro game which was within walking distance and it was fun you could see all the excitement from outside our room which had a gorgeous view of the park. 
The employees we encountered from Front Desk, Starbucks, Breakfast place, Bell Desk etc were all so nice, helpful and went above and beyond. A+ job to everyone!! I am huge on customer service, and I was really pleased. I am a Hilton Honors member as well and was very pleased with the service I received with that as well.
The room was typical, clean and I loved the pole in the shower so you could hang a towel or steam clothes. Used it every day!! I did encounter a problem (not the Hilton's fault, it was drunk people from a wedding being held there on that Saturday) and the Hilton took care of it. Wonderful time in Houston, so much to do and this Hilton made our trip so much better!!

My wife and I stayed here when we went to NYC for our Anniversary. We booked a king executive room. All of these types of rooms are in the back of the bulding, which doesn't do much for a view, but it does stay a little quieter since you're not right on the street. They do have two room family suites in the front of the bulding, which I understand if you get the right room, you can see the Chrystler Building. 
The hotel is in an AMAZING location. NYC is a very walkable city, but where this hotel is located took it beyond that. We were only a couple of blocks away from all the major sights. Times Square was extremely close, -th avenue was at the end of the street, numerous parks right down the street too. Not to mention a great selection and choice of fine quality, average Joe, and street food establishments. The hotel is also very closely located to all the major subway lines going up and down the island, as well as across the river to Queens. 
If subways aren't for you, central park and several of the museums are well within walking distance....it will take you a little while to get there (traffic, people, distance), but we made it from this hotel to central park in about ----- minutes. 
This should also help for the ladies...the hotel was close enough to the theater district, my wife and I went to see The Lion King, fully dressed (we had a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""fancy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" dinner before the show) in suit, dresses, and my wife in her high heels. She made the walk with much ease.
The staff was very friendly and helpful. Since this is a smaller boutique hotel they get to know their guests. The rooms are nicely furnished and provide an ample resting area for your many adventures you are sure to have in NYC.
My wife and I had a HUGE delay on our way to NYC due to weather, but the staff was ready and willing to help us get situated once we arrived. We didn't get in until almost --pm and I figured it would be a ghost town, we'd have to beg to get the room we requested, etc. Much to my surprise, they had our room we asked for, a staffed front desk, and a bellhop to help with our luggage. It might as well have been the middle of the day with the service we received.
We were very hungry after our long day of travel and we were able to order some room service right when we got to our room, and it was delivered VERY quickly. I have to say, though, that $-- for some crabcakes and a burger was a little much for my taste, but we were STARVING!!!
The next morning we decided to visit the little cafe in the hotel lobby for breakfast. Again, the food was good, but the price was way too much. This would be the last meal we had in our hotel. One, because of the price, but also because there were so many great places around the hotel to get less expenssive food. I recommend this diner right on the corner by the hotel....I beleive it was called the red flame diner or something like that. It's really good whatever it is called, haha! We had breakfast there every day and you could tell it was alocal place that real New Yorkers went to. The prices were outstanding and you got A LOT of food.
Overall, I think that this hotel provided an excellent place for my wife and I to enjoy our honeymoon and it was the cherry on top of our time in NYC.

The hotel was beautiful, the rooms pretty and clean and luxurious. Worked out great for family with kids. Hotel pool was great after visiting City sites. Staff was incredibly accommodating. Location good for walking to Mall. There is a CVS just across the street for snacks and drinks for kids and a starbucks for morning coffee. We will definitely stay there next time in DC.

One word to describe my stay at the this hotel would be disappointed.
I had high hopes, but was seriously shocked at the difference from their website pictures and what you actually get. Don't even think about booking the petite or classic room your be in for a shock. Even though I was travelling on my own i upgraded to the classic room so I had a little more comfort and what I thought would be a double bed, it wasn't, there is no way that two pillows could sit side by side on that bed as in the pictures on their website. It would certainly be interesting sleeping two, it would be difficult to get two suitcases in the room.
I would agree with others that the public spaces were fun and buzzing, maybe that had something to do with the $-- per day wifi charge in your room. Yes the location can't be beaten and having dean and deluca on site is a nice touch, but this hotel wasn't cheap at $--- per night. I've stayed in cheaper and had much more.
I also had an air conditioning unit out of the ----'s which was too noicy to use when sleeping, my room had no radio alarm clock and the overall feeling was shabby-passed its best. The bathroom was cute but I think their description of exquisite was taking it a little too far, it all needed redecorating.
On a plus point was traveling on my own and did feal completely safe in this hotel.
Stay in one of the bigger rooms and take their website pictures with a pinch of salt and you'll probably enjoy it.

I visit Chicago on a weekly basis for work, and I have had the opportunity to see many of the rooms, interact with the staff and eat the food on an ongoing basis- the level of quality is consistent and people learn your name and greet you personally. This is a home away from home for me and I'm grateful for the quality of the experience.
What's more, this hotel has done a great job at creating a glamorous environment that is warm and inviting, located so centrally in downtown Chicago I have not found a hotel comparable to the Ivy. My new Home away from Home.

I recently accompanied my husband to San Antonio for a conference he attended at the
Grand Hyatt. His conference was one of several held at the hotel during our stay. San Antonio itself seems to be a major convention site. I can't speak to the hotel's regular
room charges, as we received a conference rate. As Hyatt passport members, we
were upgraded to a corner room. The room itself was adequately sized, with a comfortable king bed, flat screen tv and generic furnishings. A make up mirror would
have been a nice addition to the bathroom. The hotel has an outdoor pool and fitness center, neither of which we used. The hotel's restaurant serves breakfast, lunch and dinner, and the food was good. We found the hotel staff uniformly gracious, attentive
and helpful. Location is great -- in a quieter area only minutes away from the hustle
and bustle heart of the Riverwalk. The Alamo and La Villita (quaint area with
art galleries, shops and restaurants) are both --- blocks away. While I would not
choose this hotel for a vacation (I prefer a little more pampering and character),
we greatly enjoyed our stay at the Grand Hyatt San Antonio.

I booked - rooms on booking.com for Hotel -- at NYC. Upon arrival, I was told only - room booking information was sent to them by booking.com. We traveled in - families with young children, fortunately, the hotel has extra room on that day, otherwise we wouldn't know how to find another room in such a short time. But the worse is yet to come: The hotel staff wanted my credit card upon checked in, as most hotels do for deposit-security purpose. What I was not aware of was that they already charged my credit card when i checked in (without telling me, nor issuing me any receipt). When we checked out from the hotel, we were told only one room was paid, the other room was not. (i was thinking at that time it could be the problem with booking.com, since they only sent booking information for - room, they probably charged my credit card for one room during my online booking. So we paid for one room fee upon check out. However, I got a big shock later to found out from my credit card bill that the hotel already charged me - room fees upon check in (without me knowing), and charged me one room upon check out. So all together we paid - room fees for - room!
We were also misled by the staff at the front desk regarding charges for valet parking. It was stated $-- per day. We checked in around noon time and checked out around --am the next day. We asked the person at the front desk whether we could collect our car around -pm, the answer was very assuring, but what he did not tell us, was that the parking charges is on a -- hours basis, not per day basis. So we were asked to pay $--- each instead of $-- when we collect our cars. We parked for total -- hours. If the person at the front desk had told us clearly on the -- hour policies, we could have collected our cars when we checked out at --am. It was really misleading. 
The bad experience at the hotel really spoilt our holiday.
Location makes this a good choice. Bedding was good but the towels need to be replaced.

The Sofitel Washington is inb a perfect location. If you can't stay at the White House, at least you can be a block away in a modern hotel with all amenities. The rooms are spacious with comfortable beds and large well appointed bathrooms.
Breakfast is tasty and the French press coffee is a good way to begin the day.
The staff is attentive and helpful and I will no doubt return next time I have occasion to be in our nation's capital.

Stayed at this hotel for three days and everything was great. The rooms are clean and have a microwave and refrigerator. The air conditioner-heating unit works well and is quiet--unusual for hotels of this level. Most important is every staff member is nice, and does everything possible to make the stay comfortable.

My wife and I stayed in the three days in the Holiday Inn and were happily supiorsed by the friendly and helpful staff. The room that we had was clean and for New York standards very large. The location of the hotel is ideal. You are in walking distance of the theatre district, Times Square and the Moma. The subway is just a few blocks away. We loved the pool, but were a little disappointed that it wasn""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""t open longer.
A very nice hotel, nicely updated. Reggie at the Mgr. Reception was fantastic. The hotel is hard to get to, yet close to the airport. Super value for the money. Very quiet.

Just got back from a quick - day trip to Boston. I booked - club level rooms. When we arrived early to hotel I checked in and we dropped our bags so we could start seeing the sights. The front desk person was very nice and said she would call when rooms were ready. We came back to hotel at -pm and only - of my - rooms were ready. An hour later we opted to downgrade - of the rooms from club floor to another do we could get in our rooms before we needed to get to sox game. No discount was given for downgrade. I did get wifi code that rarely worked though 
The hotel is beautiful and the rooms are very nice. The location is prime. 
The next day we went out for the day when we got back around --- my room wasn't made up. I called and spoke to a nice person who assured me it would be taken care while we were at dinner. When we got back at -- room was still not cleaned. Called again spoke to manager. She gave me a $-- break for the inconvenience. 
I held the Intercontinental brand to a tier near the Ritz Carlton. I lowered that opinion after we left.

It's located in a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""clubby"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" area which is cool if that's what you're into. But our rooms are very tiny and the walls are paper thin. My friends in the room over could hear us whispering and could recite our conversation verbatim... which was actually about the conversation the room across from us. Paper thin walls- unbelievable. And the club on the -rd floor was still loud and pounding on the -th floor where we stayed. If you are a crazy party type this is your spot but if you're not avoid this place like the plague.

We stayed at the Hotel Union Square because it was close to the start line for the Nike Womens Marathon. Our room was clean enough with a large king size bed and reasonable size bathroom. It overlooked the 'courtyard and thus was quieter than the outside rooms. This hotel is full of nostalgia having been built at the beginning of the --th century. It does show some signs of being old and tired however. Our room did not have air conditioning nor did it have a fridge or coffee maker. Not to worry, there was coffee in the lobby every morning and an endless supply of complimentary wine every evening. The staff was friendly and helpful and Tom the concierge went out of his way to ensure that our sightseeing adventures went well. Overall I would say this hotel was worth the money if you are willing to overlook the overall worn appearance of the place..

I was traveling with a group on business from Atlanta. The hotel is extremely convenient to the airport which was very good for the short duration of the stay. The hotel was booked for me by the group; I didn't have much choice. With that said, I am a Hilton Honors Gold Member, so I was a little disappointed when the Mariott was chosen as the place of stay. The hotel was very nice and is a typical Mariott with a couple of nice restauarants, a nice Starbucks shop, gift shops, spa-pool (I didn't use or look at), and concierge service (I also didn't use). All of the staff members were very helpful, courteous, and pleasant. As is typical with high-end Mariotts (and Hiltons for that matter), internet service in the room came at a price (very frustrating!), however, wireless service was available in the lobby for free. Breakfast was good, although VERY pricey. I chose to order a couple of scrambled eggs and toast with an orange juice and paid $-- after tip. Maybe I should expect differently, but I was sickened by the cost. The full buffet was $--, I might as well have gone that route (or gone to McDonald's). 
Overall, if you are on a business trip to LA and are using the airport, you really can't go wrong with this hotel. However, should I go back to LA for business, I'll look for a Hilton brand, not because this hotel was bad, but because I am loyal to Hilton. Should I go back for pleasure with the family, I'll definitely look elsewhere that provides a better family-vacation atmosphere and that is surrounded with tourist attractions.

Arrived Sunday evening and Superstorm Sandy arrived Monday. The hotal coped brilliantly with reduced staff and all of the other problems. We were given information without having to ask for it and Tony on the door was great securing taxis even when the fuel shortage struck and we needed to get to the airport.
Umbrellas for the asking if you wanted to brave the rain and wind, which we did.
The bathroom was dated but hot water and towels were plentiful and the hotel was nice and clean.
The bed was fab and if I could have put it in my suitcase to bring home I would have. I had my teenage daughter with me and despite Sandy doing her best to limit our fun we still managed to have a good trip. Thank you to the staff at the Roosevelt.

Got hotel on hotwire as -.- star offer with breakfast. Hotel lobby looked newly done and clean. Breakfast area was clean. Rooms were ok but a little worn. Coffeemaker looked like it hadn't been used and had some dust at the bottom of the water reservoir but otherwise linen, etc looked clean. Heating unit had a noisy fan.

My partner and I stayed at the skyline back in January before our cruise. Being cautious I investigated several places and chose this one. Needless to say We were very happy with our choice. The location is great, the rooms are big, clean and quiet. The beds were very comfortable and the staff was incredibly friendly. I have nothing but good things to say about the skyline. In walking distance are some great restaurants and we chose a greek place and we loved it too! If you want to stay at a clean place that is not overpriced I would consider staying here...
front desk staff member helpful and friendly ensured we were comfortable

Stayed here for - nights on business. I did not choose the hotel, and likely wouldn't have simply because while I love the neighborhood, the Hilton where I have points is right across the street. That being said, I was pleasantly surprised with how enjoyable my stay was.
The exterior and lobby harken back a few decades and seem somewhat dated. My room had been recently renovated and was spotless with nice furnishings, including a couch and coffee table. Only problem is that with the new multimedia panel built into the dresser under the --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" HDTV, there is very little in the way of drawer storage. I had to use the drawers in the two night stands - something I've never had to do before. As I'd read other reviews that indicated noise was an issue (I had absoluetly no problems during my stay), I found it interesting that the bathroom amenities included a pair of ear plugs!
Staff were friendly and helpful. I found the breakfast buffet to be over-priced for what it was - even in SF - but the coffee was delicious and the service outstanding.
Best part about this hotel is the location. Assuming you want to be in the Union Square area, it can't be beat for convenience to all transportation and shopping.

My stay consisted of - days for a business meeting in the area.
 I’ve never rated a hotel as “terrible” before, but my stay was awful at this property. 
Upon arriving, I found out that our bathtub had hair in it and our coffee maker had mold growing in it. I was given incorrect directions to restaurants by front desk staff.
 The concierge NEVER picked up the phone when I tried to call from my room.
 Food plates from room service were left in the halls the entire day. (It was around -pm when I noticed that the plates from breakfast were picked up).
 When I made my reservation I was promised high speed internet access - upon arriving I found out that this was only available to guests staying in suites.
 They advertised automatic checkout on the t.v. – I tried it; and it didn’t work.
 I would also make plans to eat OFF property, unless you want to pay about $--.-- for a chicken sandwhich.
 Overall, I can’t see myself staying at this property EVER again. Considering the cost, things should have been better. I saw signs for a Hyatt being built next door – they are getting my business next time. I suggest that you stay someplace else.

This was our first visit to this hotel. We have been in NY for many times and this time we wanted to experience a different hotel. The hotel is nicely located, near a subway. We had a corner room at the back so pretty quiet. Room had for NY standard a lot of space, bathroom on the other hand had not. It was old yet clean and if you took a shower the water in the bathtub took ages to flow away. Check in was decent and our safe was broken the first day and they replaced it immediately. So on average pretty decent but for the price they ask for the room per night it could be better

Inn at the Opera is ideally located just steps away from the opera, symphony, and the ballet. The staff at the hotel are gracious and committed to making your stay relaxing and enjoyable. The rooms are neat and clean. We slept so well I mentioned that to the manager. He said they just put new matresses in the rooms. We'll be back!

We loved the Langham! My partner and I stayed here last week during emergency construction on our condo and we were made to feel very welcome during a stressful time. We booked a room at $--- and were upgraded to a beautiful junior suite overlooking Post Office Square - a very nice surprise!
We found the hotel to be spotless and well-maintained. Our junior suite was nicely appointed and had a homely English feel. Internet connection was fast and reliable ($--.--(?) a day - pretty typical for a secure connection). Bathroom was spotless and smallish but the toiletries box with everything that one could have forgotten - priceless! Only complaint is that there was too much junk on the already small desk!
The bar... In a word, stunning! Possibly the best hotel bar we have ever visited. Huge crystal chandeliers, comfy loungy seating, stiff drinks (for a price) and polite bartenders - what more could one ask for?
The health spa is smallish but well done and designed. Pool area has lots of natural light and the workout rooms have brand new equipment and are again, spotless. Best of all, no access fee!
We easily recommend the Langham!

This hotel had a decent price, room was clean and comfortable. However, room had window to inside the hotel..so didn't get much sunlight in the room. But, thats just my bad luck of getting tat room. Breakfast was good ...had good selection with a good price. Room service was good and quick.
However, I was surprised with the lack of amenities. The hotel room didn't have fridge or microwave so you are at the mercy of the kitchen if you didn't want to leave the hotel. The hotel store had been closed for over a week, so very inconvenient to leave and get toiletries and snacks. The Starbucks closed early around noon. Also, i was shocked that the hotel bar was low class with really foul music.

Where do I begin? Just the facts . . . -. Staff friendly in general, but desk clerk was 'clever with an attitude'. -. Strange transition from elevator to our floor, having to go back outside to get to our wing, via rickety walkway with creepy carpeting; -. Interior of room: bathtub had bad skin disorder or something -- the finish was seriously decaying with big dark splotches all over the floor of the tub; very reluctant to even shower in there . . . and no bar soap, btw, and when I went downstairs and asked for some (how do you wash your hands in the sink???) the previously mentioned desk clerk said they provided misc. 'samples' in place of bar soap, i.e. 'body wash' and the like. Okay, there was a small sample of MEN'S body wash, infused with those pore-scrubbing bits of crystal sand or whatnot, and that was IT. All the other samples were either facial moisturizer, hand lotion, disposable razors, shampoo-conditioner. NO HAND SOAP. Okay, enuf about the pillows . . . this room was NOT economy-priced, either, at $--- for a Tuesday night, with no 'extras' like breakfast . . . and NO BAR SOAP. Also, the window shades did not work, and so were forever open so one had to find a dark corner to disrobe in. Lighting was strange and ineffective, as well as puzzling to figure how and where to turn it on. Each lamp-fixture had it's own bizarre personality, as well. All in all, it's just a creepy place, with that added roadside attraction of being where that news reporter was murdered back in the --s or something. It has a --'s motel-attempt-to-morph-into-upscale-boho-inn feel about it . . . I'm sorry, but I believe Trip Advisor was created to be a site one could go to for an honest, non-edited traveler's review, and that's what I always submit, good and-or bad. I trust the website, consult it ALWAYS, and hope it stays reliable. P.S. The female bartender was very pleasant, helpful, and efficient.

This is an excellent little boutique hotel with super-friendly and helpful staff in a great downtown location. Abundant continental breakfast included. If you love old B-movies, then you will be impressed by the tribute paid to old-school Hollywood stars. Each room is devoted to a star of yore, like Doris Day, Rock Hudson, Anne Francis, Leslie Caron, Ann- Margaret and more with vintage movie posters and memorabilia. You can even check your email in the Judy Garland Business Center! Free wi-fi. Our room was one of the larger rooms, and it had some odd angles and a few tight squeezes, but overall we were very comfortable at the end of a long day sightseeing, taking in shows and shopping. One caveat: There is no elevator and we had to climb up - flights of stairs! Glad we were in good shape, but if you think that would be a hardship, be sure to request a room on a lower floor.

The aLoft is a great, reasonably priced place to stay near the airport in Philly. The rooms are contemporary in decor which is refreshing. I'd read a few reviews of this hotel before travelling, so I confess to a certain level of trepidation regarding a number of issues, particularly the proximity to the apparently very noisy Manhattan Bridge flyover and the out-of-way location.
I was pleasantly surprised on both those fronts. Firstly, I had a room at the rear of the hotel, right next to the bridge on the second floor (the lowest occupied level) and the noise was almost non-existent - equivalent to the occasional, gentle rumbling of distant thunder. I don't know if this is worse on higher floors, but having heard so much about the trains going past, I was hugely relieved, and I slept like a baby every night on the immensely comfortable bed. IIt was certainly a LOT quieter than having to listen to the constant beeping of cab horns all night long when I stayed in a hotel in midtown.
Secondly, Chinatown was a brilliant location in which to stay. The hotel is a mere two blocks away from the subway station (F train - a few stops into the city) and a short walk away from the financial district, the East village, downtown etc. Also, Chinatown itself is a really fascinating, vibrant, colourful area of Manhattan - full of interesting sights, sounds and yes, smells. It is also home to dozens and dozens of excellent restaurants. Can recommend the Famous Sichuan, and Red Egg. If you really need some US style breakfast, walk for a few minutes, or get the subway uptown. Walked home a few nights at between -am and -am and it was very safe. 
The room was a decent size for Manhattan and extremely clean. Service was excellent, and the sheets and towels changed every night. Really impressed with the housekeeping. 
Staff at reception were very friendly and helpful, and there's free tea and coffee in a lobby area just down from reception. It's not the Ritz, sure, but it was really comfortable and great value for money.
Would definitely stay here again.

Stayed at King Spa suite for - days. The room was large with a sliding door separating the living and bedroom area. The bathroom was exceptionally large with a jetted tub that can easily accommodate - people. There is a separate shower and - sinks. Had a unobstructed view of LA which was nice. There are - separate thermostat controls for the bedroom and living room. There is an Ipod dock which is great and the wireless internet was reliable and fast.

Service was average. Room was always clean. However, there were a few inconsistencies. On our - day stay we only got the paper once. We only got wine glasses on our first day after that they never restocked them. We requested a coffee maker and mugs were restocked - out of - days. The coffee they provided for our coffee machines was terrible. It tasted quite acidic. We ordered coffee from Room Service to see if it will be better, it wasnt. Food is great. We ordered the chicken club (highly recommended) and the short ribs (really good also). However we try to order the chicken club again (its that good!) at ----am on our last day and Room Service said NO which was highly dissapointing. My friend also emailed the concierge several times before we arrived to see if they can do something for my birthday but he got no response at all. Don't expect them to go above and beyond. 
Payperview movie selections were good $-- each. We didnt know till after we made them but local calls are $-.-- each (no matter the duration) and apparently calls to Anaheim are considered long distance and they are $-. I stayed for one night at this hotel as part of a short trip down to San Antonio and the Hill Country. We wanted to stay in a Starwood hotel to ensure we requalify for Platinum status this year and so I took a look at this one and the Westin. The Westin overlooks The Riverwalk and although fabulous, was hugely expensive. The Gunter appeared to be a good alternative at a reasonable price (it was a Sunday night, which is often a cheap night for hotel stays).
The building is old and boasts an elegant pre war era style lobby with dark wood panelling and chandeliers. They have the old hotel switchboard on display there, which is interesting, and the old mail chutes are still on each floor.
The rooms have obviously been recently revamped and have the comforts of a modern hotel, and yet retain a period feel with dark wood and leather furniture. There was certainly nothing historic about the bed which was a super comfy King sweet sleeper.
I liked the bathroom. It was a little on the small side but not ridiculously so and had a nice marble free standing style sink. Two things to note though. There is barely any counter space so not enough room for two people's toiletries. Also, the shower head is at about eye level for a person of average height. I can forgive these quirks in an older hotel though.
There was one thing about the room that really irritated me and this was obviusly pure carelessness on the part of the decorators. There were very attractive wooden slatted shutters on the windows. However, the curtain rail had been attached so low, it prevented the shutters from opening. This was a shame because we were on the --th floor and I wanted to look at the view! I cannot say if this holds true for all rooms.
Being Platinum, we had access to the executive club lounge. It's a nicely appointed little lounge but I wasn't too impressed with the food selection or the fact you had to pay for Happy Hour drinks. I can't say how it compares to lounges in other US Starwood properties but it was poor in comparison to European and Asian properties which serve cooked buffet breakfast, great evening h'ordeuvres and free alcoholic beverage. It certainly isn't worth paying extra to be on the Executive floor to get lounge access.
In the lobby there is a computer area with a good number of terminals for free internet access.
The hotel is located about two blocks from The Riverwalk, so that is very convenient. We ate at Boudros (which I recommend) and then walked over to their sister Champagne and wine bar, Zinc, which has a lovely patio and very well priced champagne by the glass.
My tip is not to use the hotel parking. Only valet is available and it is $-- a night. The city garage is right across the street and only cost $- for overnight parking.

Stayed here for a quick weekend trip to NYC. You can't beat the location. Not even half a block to Broadway, breezeways to MOMA, restaurants like Le Bernardin and Bar Americain, etc...
Staff is friendly and helpful, especially the door men and housekeeping. No complaints there.
My biggest complaint is the room itself. Apparently I had one of the rooms that had only been partially updated if that. Needs further updating. Hole in the wall in the kitchenette. Many scuffs in the paint, especially around the closet. Outdated VCR and TV. Toilet looked like something circa ----s out the TV Show Dynasty. I will give them one thing though: it was very spacious by NYC standards.
Continental breakfast was pathetic even if it was free.
Rate versus location versus overall cleanliness is the winner here.

I was travelling alone for a conference and the location was superb. It was very convenient to the conference facility but even more importantly, was in a great location for exploring the city. I loved being near the market and got coffee and pastry at different places every day. Enjoyed the restaurant Bacco for awesome breakfast. Twice I went to Cafe Campagne and was welcomed by the staff as a single diner both for dinner once and for dessert and coffee another nite. Do your research, though because the front desk staff didn't know that much and a concierge wasn't really visible.

The hotel itself is absolutely OK - nice rooms, clean and tidy. 
Location is very good - ----mins walk to -th and -th ave, where most of the bars and restaurants are. Also a lot of shops are just next to the hotel - so you can buy pretty much everything from beer to lingerie.
Parking is something like $---day, which seems expensive to me, but maybe is OK for this location.
Recommended :)

Making a special effort to login and provide this review because this place sucks. I recently stayed at The Ashton for an overnight business trip. They have a small exercise room in the basement, but there is no way you'd know because there is no mention of it in the hotel guide. I did ask - but they failed to tell me that I could have gone to a full-service gym as well. It started to rain heavily while I was at breakfast. I asked if they had an umbrella to use to walk to my meeting and they seemed genuinely confused as to whether some might exist.

Very convenient location within walking distance of the inner harbor. Friendly team although the overall hotel is getting very worn and dated. Room has a very traditional older Sheraton look and feel which makes it look dark and less than inspiring. Nevertheless, the bed was very comfortable and the room was clean.
the Club lounge has a very limited selection and a bit on the cramped side. Have seen much better club lounges.

 The regular rooms were fairly small but well appointed without the extras.
 I called for my husbands' jacket to be pressed and James was there within - minutes to pick up the jacket. It was waiting for him in the closet when we returned from a walk.
Our first night there, we returned to our room to find a large bowl of fresh fruit, - bottles of Evian, a large plate with a solid chocolate replica of the hotel, - chocolate truffles & decadent cheescake with Happy Anniversary in chocolate.  A visit to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Top of the Mark"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" a lounge...at the top floor of the Mark Hopkins, with --- degree views of the city and excellent martini's..--- varieties, turned into dinner for our first night. Service was wonderful. We also had - delicious buffet breakfasts at Top of the Mark.

If you prefer a modern, minimalist hotel, this is not for you. If you prefer old world charm , high ceilings, excellent service, give it a try.

I was apprehensive of the hotel given the mixed bag of reviews on TA. However we had used air miles and had got a good price for the hotel. It is a big multi story hotel on the heights of Van Ness next to the Cable Car. The car park is very expensive but the hotel gives you a list of cheaper options. We had - separate one night bookings but they upgraded us and gave us one room for the - nights. The guy on reception was lovely. Our room on the --nd floor was great; it was spacious, clean and there were - very big beds with a variety of pillows. Downsides: firstly the laundry room had only - machine and dryer for a huge hotel - and the machine was not a youngster. Secondly there was no coffee in the lobby in the morning, probably because they have a restaurant which we didn't use. There were very few luggage trolleys.
There are buses stopping outside the hotel to downtown as well as the cable car. There are lots of moderately priced eateries on Polk behind the hotel. It was only a - minute drive to the best breakfast around - Homeplate on Lombard. Overall A good choice.

The W Union Square is a great hotel. It has a small lobby but there is some seating in the bar area adjacent to Olives Restaurant, which is also part of the hotel. We had lunch and a dinner at Olives (a Todd English restaurant- we actually saw him there the night we had dinner!) - cool design and the food was great. Because we were staying for a business meeting, we had a regular room which was on the small side but it was beautifully decorated. I would ask for a room with a window to the street. We had two windows that looked on to an alley and it always felt dark in the room- may not bother others but it bothered me. It's diagonally across the street from the Union Square Greenmarket which offers local produce & goodies several days a week in the pretty Union Square. This is also a great location. Great hotel.

The bar staff were very efficient and friendly especially Grace. 
It is just a quick walk to Times Square. Enjoyed the staff and the stay. Would recommend and will be returning next year.

The overall hotel experience was good. We stayed on the club level. The room was dated but clean. The happy hour was a nice perk, but the lobby had wine for all guests, so it wasn't a huge bonus over the standard. Everyone was friendly. Good location for Union Square.

We were pleasantly surpirsed at the great boutique hotel at a great price when we landed at the Hotel at Times Square in NYC. Breakfast included in the price, located near several excellent restaurants with attractive lobby and rooms. Our kids loved it and so did we.

The stay was great. This was an even good value hotel as well. I stayed there and got two carowinds tickets for $---.--. The staff was friendly and treated you with respect. I recommened this hotel to all types of travlers business, or fun

- friends and I went to NYC for a quick trip (just one night) and stayed at the Distrikt hotel. When we got there we found out that we were upgraded to a room on the --nd (top) floor. The customer service was fantastic - when we didn't answer the phone for our wake up call, someone came up to our room and knocked on our door to be sure we were awake!
I definitely recommend this hotel as a great place to stay!

I have read many of the reviews of the Arizona Biltmore and have been so surprised at some of the negative ones. If you are a lover of history and a lover of architecture, you MUST stay at this hotel. It is a true gem, a return to the ----s. It was designed in ---- by a student of Frank Lloyd Wright, and Wright served as the consulting architect. 
As you enter the main pool area (there are actually eight pools on the grounds) and view the Art Deco water slide and the shaded cabanas, you will feel like Clark Gable may walk out at any minute. It is a beautiful hotel, with lovely manicured grounds filled with palm, orange and kumquat trees. We stayed in a room in the main hotel (the original building) and the rooms were appointed with mission-style furniture and extremely comfortable beds. The service was excellent. We had an incredible view overlooking the mountain and the courtyard. In the interest of complete disclosure, I did have two complaints: the noisy groups who gathered around the fire pits late at night., which were on the main level right outside of our second story room. Had it not been for the earplugs I always carry, I would have found sleeping a problem. Also, the prices for amenities - drinks, dinner, spa, etc., were quite expensive. 
If you love history ,take the historical tour of the hotel offered from the concierge desk several times a week - it's fascinating. I highly recommend this hotel.

I used to love this hotel. Not just the location, which is still great (!), but the whole feel of the place - a cut above your usual chain hotel and a bit special. I have stayed here a number of times in the past few months and have noticed that things aren't what they used to be. The rooms are an excellent size for NYC and if you have a harbour view then they are amazing. Being located where it is, you get a great night's sleep even if you are on the road side as there is hardly any noise. Where it is missing the mark is: housekeeping, general upkeep and staff....hair left in the bathroom, torn sheet, no room service menu in room, stale smoke smell in no smoking room, change from L'Occitane toiletries to 'cheap' looking own brand ones, no body lotion, - shower gels and no shampoo, carpet looking stained etc Doormen who much prefer to stand and chat amongst themselves than open the door for you, very slow service in the bar, snippy receptionists (apart from Patrick, who is v. welcoming and helpful). I think my biggest gripe is that there is no effort to make the customer feel welcomed like there used to be. I am not asking for the red carpet to be rolled out, but would expect a 'Welcome Back' or a 'Good to see you again' when I am there for the third time in as many weeks, even the offer of a room upgrade wouldn't be too outrageous. All these things are details, but they are what make the difference between a good hotel and a great hotel. Step it up RC !

This is a beautiful resort especially if you have young children who love water parks. The water park is fabulous!! On our visit, however, we didn't get to enjoy it because it rained and the temperature was in the --'s--very cold for Arizona. The hotel should give a small compensation to guests when the temperature is in the --'s, and when it rains. Maybe give you back a portion of the cost of lodging, or at a minimum the $-- resort fee that they charge you. It was really a shame. We wouldn't have stayed here if we knew it was going to rain and be cold. I peeked in over the fence, and noticed a concession stand and saw hot dogs and french fries going for $- each. they don't allow outside food in the water park. 
We had a suite. It consisted of - rooms, one with - queens, and a sitting area, both with tvs. (Be aware that you got tax charged twice--once for getting a suite, which we weren't told about and only found out when we got our bill emailed to us. In an effort to be green, they don't give you a hard copy of your bill.) the room had a broken knob, hair on the bathroom floor that wasn't vacumed, and a dirty coffee cup that wasn't replaced. 
The breakfast offered was not gourmet. When staying at a resort, I like stuffed french toast, and other offerings, but nothing gourmet was offered. The waitress who took my order only offered me green or black tea, and never showed up with it until I was half way done with my meal, and after I had flagged down another worker who showed me a variety of teas, and immediately got me a cup. 
 The exercise facility was huge, but the individual ellipticals and bikes did not have their own tv. There were three huge tv's that you could watch--old fashion style. There was no where to plug in your head phones. You had to bring your own portable ipod or radio or something. 
The resort sent me a list of activities so I could plan my visit prior to arrival. I showed up for a -am Total Body workout only to find out that they didn't offer that class anymore. Why was it on the schedule sent to me? The person at the front desk of the exercise facility treated me as if I were imagining having received something about a class. Finally another worker told us both that a class used to exist at that time, but not in a long, long time. No one apologized to me. 
A nice little extra that they offer is free rides over to the outlet mall that is close by. It's nice for people who don't have cars. (We had a car.)
Please understand, I'm not a complainer. I liked the place, it was very pretty, but the price was steep compared to other places I have stayed. You really get charged for the waterpark whether you use it or not.

As previously mentioned the hotel is currently under renovation, which required us to enter through the underground parking garage. The staff was very quick to help with doors, etc. We used the concierge service a number of time and found them to be very helpful with directions (we walked to most locations) and activity-restaurant suggestions. This is the second Hyatt Regency that we've stayed in that required us to take an elevator from entrance up to another floor for check-in; and then another set of elevators to access our room. Given that we generally travel with carry-on luggage only, this isn't much of an inconvenience for us; however, if we were required to use a large luggage cart, it could be a hassle squeezing in a number of elevators. We stayed on the --th floor in a very nicely appointed room, with a very comfortable mattress. Even though there were - elevators to the rooms, we noticed that only - of them seemed to be in service, which at times made for quite a few stops and a tightly packed elevator before reaching the lobby. These inconveniences were small given the excellent location of the hotel and the friendly and helpful staff.

The innkeeper and staff were friendly and helpful. The parking area is free and seemed relatively secure. The room was clean although small. The Bathroom was nice, with plenty of consistent hot water for showers. Management is a little skimpy with the towels, soap and ice but you can ask for more. The TV worked great. 
The motel lies on the edge of the Tenderloin neighborhood to the east, which is very, shall we say: --colorful. The people here are very diverse and the streets are active. Yes, you may be approached and asked if you want sex or drugs. It is not particularly quiet at night. There are many restaurants, bars, stores and services nearby however, and this area is not a tourist trap so prices are reasonable. Immediately to the west, across Polk Street, are the Van Ness Auto Row and Civic Center areas which are much cleaner and tamer. Public Transit to any other part of the city is nearby. 
 We had no problems during our stay. If you are not ready to experience and accept a taste of the seamy side of urban life, or if you are a very light sleeper and cannot put up with a little noise at night, then this place is not for you. We were on a low budget, however, and this place satisfied our requirements quite well.

ShockIngly small room. Kind of like sleeping in a closet. However, super close to the Gershwin theater is you are going to see Wicked. Clean enough. Very loud- like the window is open due to window air conditioner. Rooftop has potential when it's done.

All in all, the Hampton Inn Del Mar has: an excellent location and nearby amenities. It has plateaued in a few areas, but after all, it's the attention to details that can make an average stay an excellent one.

I took a --day weekend getaway to San Francisco in April ----. Most of my time was spent sightseeing the central areas of the city, and happy hours in North Beach (Vesuvio is an absolute must).
Yes, my room was small and my window looked onto an alley - though I didn't spend much time in my room. I was visiting San Francisco to explore the wonderful city, not the insides of a hotel room. The afternoon wine reception was nice (and free), though the wines were, of course, not the best quality (read: free).
One complaint - the -nd day I was there, the maid did not replace my bath towels. I only had one towel out of - left. Not the end of the world, but I had rented the bike and needed to shower when I was done with riding for the day (riding up and down those hills can make a guy sweaty), so I had to use my last towel to shower that evening and then use the same one the next morning.
All-in-all, as a solo traveler-explorer, I would absolutely stay at the Triton Hotel again, given the price.

After staying two nights at the Royal Pagoda motel just a block or two away, we moved to this hotel because we couldn't get anymore nights at the other one. Also, the rates were very good thru Expedia. Our stay was great. I was traveling with two of my friends, so we were three guys just vacationing in L.A.
The check-in (and check-out) were the worst experiences of the whole trip. They're friendly enough, kind of quiet actually. But they are slow. Very slow. It took more than -- minutes for the person in front of me to finish and then it took them at least - full minutes to check me in. They would always disappear to the back office and not reappear for several minutes. The check-out was almost as slow at the end of our stay. At check-in, the guy didn't give us the complimentary breakfast tickets as he gave to the other guest he checked in. That might be because we had a low rate thru Expedia, I don't know. When I asked, he only gave us one ticket each when we really needed two each for each day of our stay. A couple days later, when I needed a ticket, I went to the front desk and told them we had only gotten one each at check-in, and the person there gave me another ticket right away, so it wasn't that big a deal in the end; it was just unsettling at check-in to only get the one ticket each.
Aside from the slow and slightly unprofessional (but not very bad) check-in the hotel was a great place to stay. The hotel is in a small complex of shops and it is organized around a courtyard where the shops are. I thought this was a great arrangement. One of the shops in the courtyard serves the complimentary breakfast. They had good coffee, a few danishes, bagels, english muffins, some fruit, and the person at the counter would offer you a waffle when you hand in the ticket for the free breakfast. The waffle was good, nothing spectacular, but good. Same goes for everything else. I saw nothing that was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""moldy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" as another reviewer experienced. Everything seemed very fresh.

The internet was no problem, I just started up my laptop and was on the internet - no codes or passwords or anything. Worked great, too, helped us find a restaurant for dinner and a couple bars to hit afterwards.
The beds were good, bathroom was very good, no problems with shower or water pressure, no problems with drainage in the tub, everything was fine. It was very, very clean also. We even used the in-room coffee maker and that was great also. The sink was just outside the bathroom but still in a separated area and this was convenient as others could use the sink while someone else was showering.
The maids were very accommodating and they did a great job with the room, it was very clean. They were very friendly also. This hotel has all exterior corridors as others have mentioned; however, in this case, I found it to be a positive. It was nice to step outside and get some air (or for those who smoke, to smoke). All exterior corridors overlooked the courtyard which was nice. And, even though the hallways are outdoors, the elevator (which needs to be taken for any room) has a slide so that you must swipe your valid key card or else it won't go to your floor, so that added a level of security and helped put me a little more at ease.
The neighborhood is Chinatown. Even though it is part of downtown it is a very safe area. We never felt threatened or in danger at all. The people are nice and it's an interesting area. You can sightsee right in that neighborhood and there are interesting shops to visit and there is GREAT food. I'm used to Chinatown in NYC where we have great Chinese food, but L.A.'s chinatown is definitely just as good, if not better.
The parking is a weird situation. There is a parking garage under the hotel. The hotel will charge you $- a night to park there, and from what I've heard they will require you """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""valet"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" park the car. My friends and I are not big on valets because we want to be able to just get in and go without waiting for some valet. So we didn't go with their parking. We parked on the street which was free and fine all weekend long. We parked overnight with no problems. During the day we were out and about so we didn't park there. The garage that does the valet parking is open to the public and charges a flat $- rate for the day, so I just moved the car there till we left later in the morning (no valet, it was self park).
Overall, it was a good stay. The room was much nicer than the Royal Pagoda nearby, and the rates were good but not as low as the Royal Pagoda.
Overall this is a simple hotel, and it's great for vacationers who aren't going to spend a ton of time in their hotel room.
If I traveled to L.A. on business I probably wouldn't stay here, at least not more than a night or two. I will definitely look to stay here again on my next vacation to L.A. though. Chinatown is a great location - it's safe, it's interesting, great food options (including bakeries that make awesome pastries for breakfast), and located near all the major freeways so you can easily get anywhere you want. Everywhere we wanted to go was only about -- minutes away - Hollywood, Pasadena, Venice, etc.
I'd recommend this place to any of my friends and I will hopefully stay there again. The only thing is that I've noticed their rates to get pretty high, and at that point I'd considering staying in a nicer hotel like a Hilton or something. But for under $-- a night it's worth it.

That said we had breakfast every morning in the hotel dinning room and the serving staff was wonderful. In short the hotel is nice, clean, and benefits from a nice location. If Hilton could find the time to conduct training sessions for the management on how cater to families this hotel will go from average to very good.
