It is not a fancy hotel...it is however more than adequate and fairly priced and I have not ever had a room that was not clean.
I have other choices but I keep going back because of how well I am treated.

I was looking for a place to stay for a long holiday weekend and needed to be close to the home of some friends in Saginaw. I forgot how close this hotel was to the Texas Motor Speedway and the Stockyards as well as how horrible the traffic is in the area of Loop --- and I---W. Most of the other guests were NASCAR types and had multiple kids, making use of the indoor pool or the morning breakfast buffet an impossibility. The parking situation is also not good, with the spaces being far too narrow for all of the duel-wheeled pickup trucks owned by the other guests. 
There are a number of nice restaurants nearby, many within walking distance. Waffle House, Joe's Crab Shack, Rosa's Cantina, Boston gourmet pizza, Starbucks, Whataburger, Popeyes, and McDonalds are all very close and on the opposite side of the freeway, within easy reach, are On the Border, Romano's Macaroni Grill, Chilis, Saltgrass steakhouse, MK's sushi, Braum's ice cream, Wendys, Genghis Mongolian Grill and several other Mexican restaurants. 
There are two nice public golf courses close by, The Club at Fossil Creek and Iron Horse, both of which are very highly rated and well-conditioned. Shopping is available at Northeast Mall in Hurst, about a five mile drive to the east.
The biggest negative for this hotel is the horrible traffic situation that exists due to its proximity to the Loop ----I---W interchange. This is the worst highway in Dallas-Fort Worth and traffic headed south on I---W is backed up for miles -- hours a day. Unless you are a native (as I am) or frequent visitor and know how to get around using city streets and avoiding the freeway, this makes getting the short distance into Fort Worth a nightmare. Be sure to check to see if there are events scheduled at the Speedway or Stockyards before booking this hotel as the infrastructure of the city cannot handle the additional traffic from major events at any of these venues. 
All-in-all, the hotel was acceptable, but it suffered in comparison to some of the other, much nicer places I stayed on this trip for the same or less money. It is not a bad hotel and the staff is alright, but the location is a detriment in terms of mobility and the parking situation is terrible. If you are a NASCAR fan, it is a great place to stay during race weekends; otherwise, find another option away from the crowds.

I have no complaints. The rooms were very clean. Nice decor, comfortable beds. Fun sports bar-restaurant. We had a package which included parking and breakfast. The breakfast buffet was excellent. The location was the best. Close to both of the cable car stops, Pier --, You can ride on any and all public transportation all day when you purchase their pass (approx. $--.-- per day). Cheaper then cabs and alot of fun. Alcatraz by Night was a great tour. Coit Tower, great views. Bring comfortable shoes. Loved San Francisco and our stay at the Hyatt.

My husband and I stayed at this hotel for our first trip to San Francisco and thought it was a great location for exploring the city. Only steps from the Chinatown gate and such a good value! Although the room was on the small side, it was well appointed and had everything we needed. (And besides, we came to San Francisco to see the sights and not sit in our room!) We also took advantage of the roof top patio one night and enjoyed being able to bring our own bottle of wine to sit and relax our tired feet.

Save your money! This is the smallest hotel room I have eve stayed in! It is extremely tiny by NYC standards! Queen size bed with -- inch tables on each side - that's it! Bathroom sink is so shallow a man's hands cannot fit under the facet! No clost - a very short rod with a curtain. Very noisy! No restaurants except McDonalds or Subway in immediate area.
Room Service has only - breakfast and - lunch selections! 
One of my worst hotel experiences ever! Staff portrays it as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""boutique Silver LEED hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".
What an excuse! You can have it!
we stayed at ramada to go on a cruise ship and they drove us to the cruise line great breakfast very nice staff have stayed same hotel many times allways nice .

Great value accommodation. Hotel has a bit of a funny smell to it. However the rooms are big, clean, and the bed is comfortable. 
Cute outdoor area for eating-having a drink. 
Basic continental breakfast each day which does the trick nicely. 
Very close to Hollywood Boulevard. Great Japanese restaurant nearby as well. 
The staff were friendly and extremely helpful. 
We weren't overly impressed with Hollywood, however if you want to be close to the action and like all of the celebrity stuff, then I would stay here.

We booked it for our wedding anniversary as a package deal with lastminute. Hotel seemed ideally located and photos of the hotel looked great. However, upon arrival we were eventually given keys to a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which in no way resembled the photographs on the website. With it being our first visit to NYC we were somewhat disappointed. It wasn't particularly cheap either, so we went back to reception and asked for an upgrade as it was our anniversary. The receptionist looked at us like we had just peed in her shoes and said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""er, there is no """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""upgrade"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", all rooms are like that"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" - and then turned away and dealt with the next person. Nice touch I thought.
The bed was filthy, wallpaper was peeling off and the room smelled disgusting, and as for the bathroom - eeeeugh. 
The missus wont let me book any more """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""surprise"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" trips away now because of the terrible experience and ALWAYS checks this site first before booking anything herself.

Lobby and bar area are nice. Location is great.
Rooms are tired and not very clean. Restaurant is small and just average food.
With all the great choices in downtown Chicago, it's hard to see why I would pay $----night to stay here again.

Hubby was on a business trip to Phoenix and we wanted to spend a few days together for our anniversary. We picked this hotel thanks to Trip Advisor and it was wonderful. 
The staff was attentive and charming, the property was intimate and private. Movie stars from the --'s and --'s used to escape Hollywood and stay at this very property. The atmosphere was old world hacienda with soft music playing, plenty of flowers and delicious iced tea in the lobby. 
 We attended a special James Beard gourmet dining experience that was as elegant as any NY restaurant. Our tablemates couldn't have been more charming, gracious and fun. 
 Our room was ample, offered a - person soaking tub, soft bed and plenty of air conditioning. Our biggest complaint was the hot weather, which wasn't the fault of the hotel. The property was conveniently located to major roads, not far from Scottsdale.
 We would definitely return to Royal Palms.

Attended a meeting. The hotel was expensive and charged -- dollars a night for wi-fi access in the room. Consequently, guests crammed into the lobby where wi-fi was supposedly free. But no one was able to access it. 
I talked to a lot of people and they were similarly frustrated. When I mentioned the wi-fi problem upon checkout, I was told that I should have spoken to the bell cap. That was not the answer I wanted to hear.

The Location of the W New York is fantastic. As a first rime tourist to New York this hotel was close enough to times square and rockerfellar centre and central park that you could walk to each, but also far enough away that it wasn't overbearing. The hotel is conveniently placed between two subway stations - each on different lines- so getting to downtown, meatpacking district, soho was fairly simple. One of the stations is also on the Jamaica line which connects with the airport train so we didn't have to change train lines to get to-from JFK.
When we arrived at about -pm (December --) there was a large line at reception and only two staff working on the desk. When we were assigned our room, we took our suit cases upstairs ourselves (I was surprised there was no luggage assistance- at both other W hotels our bags were taken to our room for us as soon as we arrived). Once upstairs, the key to our room didn't work. My partner waited upstairs while I went downstairs and had to join the -- minute long line at reception again. She sent me back up with new keys, but again they didn't work. I went down to reception again (this time skipping the line, thank god!) and she sent us to a new room on a different level. This time the key worked, but someone's things were already set up in this room!! She gave us access to a room already in use and if I wasn't a decent human being I could have easily gone through their things.
So I went to the desk a third time, and after an hour of going up and down the elevator we finally had our room. (all we got to compensate for the hassle was - drink cards for the bar).
The main part of the 'Wonderful' room was good- nice soft bed, good tv with lots of sports channels which my partner enjoyed. The bathroom was aged and worn- ugly shower curtain and pretty small, but knowing the building wasn't new andin new York everything is tiny, we had expected this. Don't go expecting a - star marble bathroom (as per my experience at the W hong Kong and Koh Samui, thailand).
The first concierge (male, --s, dark hair) was rude and when I asked when the Boom Boom Room at the standard hotel was open he said, without looking up from his computer, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Tonight is gay night, you probably won't get in if you're not on a guest list, you'll have to line up for about - hours, and you'll have to dress nicely""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""- as though I wasn't going to dress nicely? Turns out getting into that bar was easy anyway and nothing like he explained!
The concierge Lauren, however, was FANTASTIC- booked us a great restaurant - Illili - on Christmas eve and was happy to help with all my questions.
The free Acura car service was wonderful and we used it a few times- including to get to maddison square garden on Christmas day which was a huge help and money saver for cabs, just make sure you book a fee days in advance.
Didnt try room service but the bagels and pastries and juices downstairs were really good because we could get them in a take away bag and eat as we were exploring. About $- for a yummy juice and a bagel or croissant.
Slept really well, rooms nice and dark, cleaning service staff were very polite- even gave me some extra bliss products when I asked!
Love that the bar downstairs was always busy at night, always people around which I enjoyed but might not be to your taste.
All in all, the W New York was about what we expected, just don't go expecting a - star bathroom or - star service. I'd say it's more of a - star hotel.

Westin is generally a good brand to bank on. However, they sometimes feel a bit older and more tired than top-tier Westin. This is one of those. I'm guessing this is in need of a renovation in the near future.
That said, it delivers the things that Westin are good at. Clean rooms, great beds and a good place for a beer and a meal downstairs. The pool area was clean, although felt a little closed in. This is a good airport hotel but unless there is a good room rate available, there's plenty of choice in the LAX area. I wouldn't choose this over all others at any cost.
I'd stay again.

I have stayed at the Radisson a few times in the last five years, for both business and pleasure. With the construction of the light rail, staying near the airport is a cheaper and more convenient way to spend the night when attending a Seahawks or Mariners game. 
The hotel is located across the street from the airport...I mean literally across the street! The hotel does provide a shuttle, but I saw a number of pilots and flight attendants walking to work from the hotel. The hotel is also about - blocks from the Airport Light Rail station, which is the cheapest and sometimes fastest way to get to downtown Seattle.
The staff has always been friendly and helpful when I have stayed there. A few times they have only had one person working at the front desk, and I have had to wait in line for five minutes or so to check in.
The rooms at the Radisson are comfortable and well furnished. Some of the furnishings are a bit dated, but does that really matter? The rooms are equipped with large flat screen TVs, a desk and chair, sitting chair as well as a luggage table-rack. The bathroom has granite counter tops, and an adjustable """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""butterfly"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" shower head. 
There are a number of eating establishments within walking distance from the hotel...Subway, Mango (Thai), Jack-in-the-Box, Denny's, Sharp's Roaster, Gregory's Bar and Grill, Spencer's (at the Hilton), and a Seattle icon, -- Coins (-- hour dining) right next door.
Overall, I give the Radisson a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""thumbs up"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I will be back .

I had decided to stay at Comfort Inn because I had recently seen a commercial for Choice Hotels. After I was greeted by the staff, I had checked into my room and the cleanliness and the decor of the room was superb. I was later informed that they had recently renovated the motel. The breakfast was limited to coffee, tea, juice, cereal and pastries; however, san francisco had many different cuisines to offer us.

From my hotel window, I see the buses of the Port Authority Bus Terminal on -th Avenue. Times Square isn't close, but if I walk by five or six Adult DVD shops, two massage parlors, and a peep show booth, I think I'll get eventually get there.

My friend (visiting from UK) and I had a perfect stay at the Palomar. If you have never stayed at a Kimpton property you must give them a try. Everything from check-in to check-out was perfect including transportation arrangements, drinks in the bar, the spacious-modern-clean-comfortable room and morning coffee-tea in the reception area. We didn't partake in the evening wine reception (as we were never in on time) but I think it is a great perk. In the future the Palomar is the only hotel I will be booking when visiting Chicago.
Parc -- is a first class hotel. The room was nicely furnished, including a flatscreen HD television. Great location, too.

I stayed at the DoubleTree for - nights and I think it is a pretty good hotel. The staff is friendly and want to help, but have their mistakes from time to time. The rooms are spacious and clean but have some details that betray the fact is a renovated hotel (old TV, noisy AC, no safe in the rooms) but everything else (carpets, bathrooms, desk, beds) is new and very clean. The bed is super comfortable. The hotel’s location is very good for shopping and eating, if you are more into museums it is better to find something in the Loop.
Other reviews said the elevators were very slow, I didn’t have any problems there. What I didn’t like is that they charge the use of computers in the business center.

The earlier reviews give you a good taste of what the hotel is all about. Huge rooms. When I stayed there -rd week of April--- the rooms were really hot even with the heat turned off. The area did seem a bit seedy at times but it is undergoing change. Close to theatre district and Times square. Nearby --th St Dinner was great. I'd stay there again if it was for a short stay.

During a business trip, I was attempting to find a Hilton in closer proxy to my meeting venue and when there were no Hiltons available at either location I preferred on the dates I needed, the Hilton Rep directed me to this hotel for a close reference. There are several dining establishments and local attractions that are in walking distance, mostly past the freeway underpass. Check-in was easy and convenient, but they do not have room service or bellhop. The room was very nice and spacious with free internet access and such room amenities as a --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" HDTV, microwave, mini fridge, and coffee maker that made the week-long stay less taxing. The workout facility was not large (- x Ellipticals, - x Treadmill, a horizontal bike and free weights) but adequate. Perhaps the most impressive and accommodating part of the stay was their vast spread for breakfast in the morning; anything and everything is served and all was very good.

I gave The Curtis - stars because the front desk, valet, and management staff have been so friendly and accommodating. However, I had suspicions about its cleanliness when at check-in, I viewed the smudged elevator walls and carpet that had clearly not been vacuumed recently. I would not let my bare feet touch the floors in my room because it just didn't seem very clean. My suspicions were confirmed when I returned to my room after a conference and found that the beds had been made but my trash had not been emptied, my nightstand still had two glasses and melted ice in the bucket from the night before, the lid was next to the t.v. where I had left it, and the dresser that held the t.v. was dusty. 
I am an admitted hotel snob, and I only ended up here because I tried to save my company some money by using Hotwire. Still I was prepared to give The Curtis a great review based on the attentive service. I'm sorry, but no level of attentiveness makes an unclean room ok. I should add that a spot in the shower which I saw at check-in and believed to be a permanent mark was no longer there after cleaning. I can't begin to express how disturbing that is. I will never stay here again and I am strongly questioning whether I will ever use Hotwire again.

My parents and I stayed in the studio - queen room with the sofa bed for two nights. We were in town for a family wedding. Upon arrival, the front desk was courteous and welcoming. We were placed in an accessible room (although we had no need). We had breakfast at the hotel one morning. There was plenty of simple breakfast items available. I was very impressed at how clean this hotel is. Each morning, I entered the lobby to find someone cleaning in some way or another. We requested more pillows and blankets, and they were delivered in a timely manner. Parking was plentiful. This hotel is withing a few miles of Santana Row which is a great place to do some shopping and dining. Overall a great experience and good night's sleep.

Loved the location, it's just so convenient to Penn Station and accessible to everywhere-my husband and I love to walk everywhere so may not be as described as the same by others who don't walk much. There are - delis on the corners, the best cheesecake and amazing pizza within a - min walk-couldn't think of a better location anywhere.
The staff made some fantastic recommendations of places to visit and to eat (Joshua Tree and Starlight Diner). Staff are friendly, and will only engage with you if you go out of your way to engage with them- which suits us fine as we're pretty private people when we travel and keep to ourselves generally.
It's loud as mentioned, but you get that in NYC so nothing to complain about. 
Rooms are small and a shared bathroom but you get that with affordable hostels. We found the rooms and bathrooms to be very clean and tidy.
The only downside was that the free wifi was pretty slow and dropped out constantly. It's a hostel, if you've travelled before you'll get what you've booked :)
Have booked a stay in Dec-Jan so pretty happy.

Dont bother. The staff was very nice and friendly, but his place is not worth the money. we checked in late on Friday-had reservations for king room and they could not honor that reservation, so we got two double beds instead. We ordered room service. -- dollars for - turkey sandwiches and - bowls of ice cream. when the food came they were right out of the fridge. One of the sandwiches had moldy cheese on it. the shower head had pink mold all over it and light bulbs were burned out in the room. when reported all this, the staff acted quickly to address but for --- dollars a night I think they could have done a better job. it just kept missing missing the mark.

I stayed at the Hotel Mayflower in March ----, after reading all the excellent reviews on TripAdvisor about the hotel. Yes, I totally agree with all the good comments. Staff were friendly and attentive, even with her limited English the housekeeping staff took very good care of me. The location is fantastic, except Bush Street could be a problem if you are a light sleeper. Breakfast was complete (considering the room rate) The hotel is not of five-star class, but with basic necessities and great location. 
However, I believe hotel is a personal choice for everyone. I like the hotel, but it's not my cup of tea. I'm a regular to San Francisco and the reason for travelling is to socialise and get to know people, but this hotel didn't offer me the chance to do so, as much as the other hotels I've stayed during my previous visits.

I stayed here for - nights towards the end of November and had booked a room on their Club Floor because of the great rate I received and for all the extra's you receive. I had read many reviews and was a little hesistant but thought I would give it a try. The location is great, but it def. is a convention hotel. Nothing really impressed me with the upgraded room that you are supposed to have for staying on the Club Floor. The bathrooms need updating, the towels were worse than one's I've had at the Best Western! I've stayed at other hotels in Chicago (the Fairmont and the Hilton) and would not likely stay here again.

We stayed here in the end Oct ---- for - nights for a family vacation with my husband, myself and my - adult sons. The room had - queen size beds, a mini frig & microwave which was great. The hotel must have been recently renovated. The parking spaces are a little tight but we did not have any issues with it. They have - pillows to each bed but they are down pillows which can be thin. The breakfast was pentiful and good selection for a free breakfast. The location is great for sightseeing. We used the rental car during the day instead of public transporation. If driving around make sure to have plenty of coins for the parking meters but they do accept credit cards also. We did have to pay for parking everywhere even the bigger sights like the zoo. The only issue was about trying to drive the city which was not tourist friendly. Lots of no left turns especially near the waterfront or pike market. Also came across a couple of streets that we're closed but you only found out when you went half way down or all the way and could not get thru. We would recommend this hotel.

After spending a night at the Le Parker Meridian, The Benjamin was a welcome oasis! Very nice decor, wonderfully appointed bathrooms, comfortable beds, plenty of closet space, and a very nice wet bar area with an ice maker in the mini-fridge. The work desk was big and even had a fax machine-printer available. My favorite touch was the Pillow Menu, where you can choose from - or - pillow choices, everything from a down pillow to a Tempur-Pedic! Very friendly staff and a convenient location make this a business traveller's dream!

This hotel is conveniently located both to Logan and the Blue Line. The neighborhood is a bit dodgy looking and the fenced off street in front of the hotel a bit odd, but, the hotel itself is fine.
Had a room facing a wonderful concrete parking structure, but it was extremely spacious. I found the pool area to be a bit small, relative to the rest of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""complex"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", but, you do what you can, I suppose.
Overall, a satisfactory stay.

Aside from this hotel being located in Baltimore (yikes!) this hotel is just ok. Apparently the north tower was recently remodled and has more of a Sheraton feel but there is still no wireless internet, no bathtubs and the location doesn't feel safe at night. The south tower is run down and dirty - don't stay there. I thought the hotel staff service was pretty good though.

Whilst the Hotel & staff were friendly upon arrival and throughtout my - day stay, the room & Lockwood restruant were also fine, it wasn't until my arrival back home & after checking my bank balance found there was a ATM tansaction for $---.-- made - days after I had checked out and left the state. Five phone calls later I finally spoke to a Front Office Manager who attempted to assist me. The outcome was nothing they could or would do.
Advice is double check your bamnk statements.
An otherwise enjoyable visit ruined.

This hotel is quite well located in the financial district with easy walking distance from Quincy Market, the port or downtown. The building is very nice and important outside work were hiding part of the view of the room...The room itself was quite standard for a Hilton hotel. The bed is confortable, the bathroom is getting old. The problem of this hotel is that there is no service, no slippers, no attention from people working there. The breakfast during the week end was very average with no service AT ALL! People just ignore you but claim for tips at the end...Very disappointing for a Hilton!

We just got back from New York and it was a great stay. My fiance won tickets to a jazz concert at Lincoln Center, but we only had a week to make travel arrangements from DC. I used tripadvisor to choose a hotel to stay at (that was assoc. with Hilton - since I was going to use points for the first time). We've stayed in Times Square before, and didn't want to this time. Staying Downtown would be too far away, so I focused on midtown (but still on the west side). 
I really liked the reviews I read for this hotel. It was relatively new, good location and nice staff (and no knock on the door at - am to clean the room or check out like I've read for other places). Anyway, I agree with a lot of the comments posted on here. We were welcomed by staff as we entered the hotel and were able to check in pretty early. Painless check-in! Room was a little small, but cozy enough with a rather large bathroom (for NYC). Standing shower, which was great, and you could tell the amenities and the fixtures were top notch. TV was a little slow to start up, but that was explained in the room (on the placard).......flat screen with quite a few HD channels too. Went to the business center, and there is enough room to do some work on the computer (I think there are - in there). Internet is free in the room, but I didn't bring a computer for that trip (if you're there for leisure, the computers in the b center should suit you just fine). Only slight criticism is that the elevators took a while to actually go down. They all kept going up, and we had to get on and go up several flights (picking ppl up), before eventually going back down to the lobby. Interesting. Based on other reviews, we didn't even try the food. There are too many other places within walking distance to try out. 
Besides the room and the hotel, the location was great for us! Macy's is less than a - minute walk (less, but you have to cross the street). Good Christmas shopping! You can see it as you walk out the hotel, on the right. Empire State building is very close, as well as TImes Square. The subway stop is right there too, which was perfect for us because it was COLD the entire time we were up there, but we were able to quickly walk to that station (--th Street-Bryant Park, I think) and get out at --th St-Columbus Circle) and did the same thing coming back to the hotel. No need for a taxi this time around. 
All in all, the staff took care of us and answered all our questions, and based on everything stated above (and more), we would definitely stay there again..........and hopefully, it will be a little warmer next time.

- things which makes the hotel to be rated quite hight: perfect Location, easy advanced check in and check out. You can check in day before arrival, upon arrival no need to wait at reception - it can easily be done at electronic check-in counter - this saves time! Rooms need to be improved, maximum -*, but still quite and clean.

Recently stayed at this hotel for a business conference. Hotel staff was excellent. Logistics of the conference were great and the food was pretty good. Nice rooms with comfy beds. 
Removed one star due to no fridge in the room, iron was inconsistent with steam and front desk was not staffed too well in the evening. Otherwise, pretty decent experience.

The only good thing about this hotel is the location. And when I say location, I mean it's proxemity to the center across the street (Ralph's, Starbucks and so on) and the view of the Hollywood Hills. 
But everything else was a disaster. We'd stayed there once before in ---- but it didn't seem quite as bad the first time. We arrived late and were given the handicapped room. Upon entering, we experienced a foul smell and as we walked across the floor, there seemed to be a huge hole under the carpet infront of the bed. Then we were given a room on the back wall on the second floor. With - suitcases, it wasn't easy to load-unload the car. We instantly took the blanket off, curled it up and put it in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""closet"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for the entire duration of the stay. The reason... well how often are they cleaned really and the fact that there were huge stains on it. Yuk. The curtains seemed to have a matching stain pattern. The carpet was nasty and we spent our time in the hotel with either flip flops or socks... sock which basically were garbage upon departure. Breakfast was terrible... something that resembled vending machine bearclaws and plain toast. And as far as I can recall coffee was only available for an hour. The housekeeping staff didn't understand much english and the frontdesk staff were rude. The TV was terrible and only a few channels were watchable, though not totally clear. And the fixtures and counter in the bathroom looked like there were going to fall off the wall at any given time. The walls were paper thin and we could frequently hear our """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""neighbors"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" enjoying a little extra cirricular actviity. We experienced that on several nights there were guys hanging out in cars in the parking lot and found empty liquor bottles in the morning.
Honestly sometimes the money that you save staying at a place like this is NOT worth the time and headache that follows. This place could be a gem and would gladly pay $-- extra per night if everything was perfect because the location is pretty great (if you have a car that is).

Our first time of going to San Fransico was wonderful. My husband picked this quaint little hotel and we absolutely loved it!!! Everyone was friendly and very helpful. We were close enough to Fisherman's Wharf that we could walk to it. We looked for a place that would put us close yet we would have quiet when we wanted it. Marina Inn is definitely the place to stay. We would stay there again.

This place is a dump in the slum area of Hollywood, it is dangerous and the rooms are filthy and run down the rooms can be accessed by the gangs from the hood and the owner is a con artist that will take your cash at any opportunity. We were advised by the owner not to go outside alone, nor to let my child go outside, that speaks for itself just don't go is my advise. There seem to be much better places in more secure areas near Hollywood, spend the money and give this place a huge miss.

The best location in NYC, great service, friendly staff, average prices. The room was really small, the bed was big and the shower worked properly. I think It's an excellent choice at all. I'd definitely recommend it. We've been there for a week last june.

Despite reading the many negative reviews previously posted about this hotel we were pleasantly surprised.
Friendly and helpful staff
Great night's sleep
Compact but functional room layout
Good breakfast offering
Only negative was the towels that resemble something you might expect from a youth hostel

Four Seasons Quality with a double dose of Warmth, Charm and Personality. What I loved, was the feeling that this was really """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""my hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". At some hotels you feel like you are an intruder into an exclusive world... like staying at a friends vacation house and afraid to open the drawers for fear you're violating their space. Not so at the Hotel ----. You are treated like you have come home to a familiar place even though it might be your first time. The staff seems to be allowed to be who they are, and their personality comes through creating a sense of hospitality that some of the worlds best hotels could only dream of. Much different than say the Peninsula, where the staff seem more like servants fearing to interrupt you. 
Love the Decor and level of detail but anyone can duplicate that, but you can't duplicate the DNA (personality) that is distinctive to the Hotel ----. My time there was exceptional. Fantastic location. Can't wait to come back.

We stayed here at the end of a - week RV trip of North Carolina and Virginia. We were ready for a bit of luxury and Morgans certainly provided it. The staff were courteous and welcoming and our room was modern, spotless and comfortable.  We were particularly pleased by the little extras provided, such as the plentiful breakfast, the lounge where coffee and tea were always available and the free access to internet in the living room. Don't let the nice furnishings and art fool you, it's an average hotel when it comes to the room. Our room was pretty cramped considering there was only one bed in it. One of the best hotels I have ever stayed in. Not just the view and location, but the people are so friendly and helpful. We were upgraded to the --th floor and were able to watch the Blue Angels perform right out our window! 
We used their Mercedes town car to travel to a restaurant across town. The driver was wonderful. We didn't have to try to find a taxi to get home in the dark (SF is not like NY. To find a cab can be impossible).

I stayed at Rodeway INN Memphis in the first week of October with a mate of mine and it was great value for money .The room was a very spacious and clean it also had a small fridge which many of the upmarket hotels do not have unless you pay extra and the bathroom was a good size and the rooms were cleaned each day and new bath towels were supplied each day .The manager of the hotel was very helpful he printed out the time tables for the buses to go to downtown and Graceland and the location of the hotel was good as it was only a short bus ride either way .I asked the manager Harry if they had a computer you could use to check emails and he told me they didn't have one but he told me he had a spare lap top of his own and i could use it whenever i liked which was great .The breakfast in the morning is a help yourself and what they provide is good cereal toast cakes bagels jam coffee and tea and lots of fruit .I will certainly use this hotel when i come back next year .

My first of what I hope to be many stays at this hotel in Philadelphia. It completely outdoes The Four Seasons. The bed was unbelievably comfortable, the room was clean and spacious, the bathroom was huge and the location was perfect. Excellent service and amenities. Right in the center of everything in midtown. FABULOUS HOTEL!!!

This hotel is located in a run down area of the city. I definitely did not feel safe walking the streets at night.
Also, a young woman was running an illegal service in the room next to mine. A lacrosse team was staying at the hotel and I think the entire team was visiting this womans room. Not a family hotel.

I have to say that I was not looking forward to staying at an airport hotel, but it was a great experience. The room was very comfortable and the staff very helpful. The food provided for the meeting was very good and plentiful. 
The greatest thing was how convenient everything was. Having kiosks in the lobby for printing boarding tickets was great and getting through airport security was never so easy and quick.

Just arrived home from a - night stay in New York.Stayed at the New Yorker for the first time,will definitely go back.Rooms were clean,staff very helpful and friendly,location excellent.Our room had a view of the Hudson River,best hotel room window view I have ever had.

We stayed at the Sheraton Tribeca on our way home from Dublin Ireland. I am a SPG Gold Member but used HOTWIRE to secure a room at this location on Canal Street next to Chinatown, NYC.
We arrived by taxi and checked in immediately with no wait. There are bellhops at the front door who can assist you with baggage and flagging down taxis. The front desk clerk gave us an enhanced room with a view on the --th floor because they were out of double beds that I requested. I grabbed a free copy of the New York Times Sunday paper on our way up to the room.
The room was spectacular—big room for New York with luxury bed and linens and rainfall shower head in the bathroom. The HD Flat screen television had real HD programming to watch. Multiple outlets throughout the room for phones, laptops etc. And a grand window view of Canal Street and Chinatown!! It all made for a super night in Manhattan. I have to say again that Sheraton has the best beds in the industry for deep sleeps.
We walked east of the Hotel to Chinatown for some late night Asian food. And we strolled through Little Italy on Mulberry to see all the white linen tables waiting for customers. The entire area was flooded by Hurricane Sandy but we could see no sign of the disaster during our stay.
Before retiring for the night I used the free business center downstairs to print my flight itinerary. Use of the computers and printers is free for all guests and not just SPG Members. In the morning a free copy of USA TODAY was left at our door.
I would stay here again without hesitation.

Stayed -- days on business travel: Good access to transportation and restaurants; spacious and clean with the advantages of a small kitchen. It was basic: Mine had a rather loud window unit and a view of an alleyway. Staff was matter-of-fact but responsive. I would not hesitate to stay again.

When you exit the freeway just past chase stadium you will find this friendly Super -. Don't be dismayed by the miles of ghost motels some quite vintage that you see if you go too far. Just go back to the Super - pronto. It's a short walk to the center of town and the light rail and the airport near everything you need at a real price premium. swimming pool and laundry, fridges in room. free parking, ample, not fancy, breakfast but so friendly and helpful. We recommend this place for the budget conscious traveler

This hotel is very nice...sort of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""trendy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The thing that makes this such an enjoyable place to stay is the staff who were all excellent and polite and the service was impeccable. The room was very clean, the beds were comfortable but it was a little small and the water in the bathroom was not very hot. Other than that it was a great place to stay.

We stayed at The Midtown Hotel in Boston for a long weekend over the President's Day Holiday. We paid $-- a night for our room, we were touring Northeastern University and given this special rate when we made our reservation. Such a bargain! We arrived at -- Noon and although check-in is not until - pm we were very happy to learn that our room was ready. The room was spacious and clean. Furnishings were a bit outdated but not a big deal. I felt perfectly safe in the hotel. No restaurant, room service or mints on our pillows - so what. Don't go to a hotel like this with expectations of The Four Seasons. We were quite pleased with the great location of the hotel. We felt that the fee for parking our car was very reasonable for a city. We left the laptop at home, we came to tour the city and the school so wifi was not a concern. No complaints from me. We really just slept and showered in our room. Our bed was very comfortable. I could see how some claustrophobic guests might be uncomfortalbe in the small bathroom. I will say that the hallway was rather loud in the morning, it was not an issue for us as we were up and out early, but if you want to sleep late this may not be the hotel for you. If you have reasonable expectations you will not be disappointed.

When we arrived, we found out our room only had one bed. Since there was a wedding that night, they couldn't switch us, but switched us the following night. Both rooms were very nice and the beds very comfortable. We found the location to be excellent for catching the cable car or F-line or sightseeing buses. The day we were leaving we had to check out before we were done with our sightseeing, and the staff was very helpful and explained how we could leave our luggage and go finish our sightseeing and get the car when we were ready to go. We would definitely come back to this hotel.

I didn't experience any of the nightclub atmosphere explained by others. I thought that the property was perfect. It does cater to a younger, hipper crowd. This property isn't only embraced by repeat travelers but by the locals as well. The staff is helpful and attentative. Beautiful location. Excellent customer service. Thoroughly enjoyed our stay. Room service menu incredibly reasonable, beautiful views, water pressure and temperature excelllent, good insulation between rooms, we had a wonderful time. Definitely recommend.

We found the Maritime to be an oasis in the middle of bustling, cool Meatpacking district. The only down side is that it is located in the gaslamp district. And I say downside because to be among the excitement and entertainment, you will get the noise. We stayed in this hotel with my parents. When we pointed out the stains, she nodded and then took the whole thing out. When she brought it back, it looked much better, but a little later, we looked closely again and found more stains! 
Since it was a cool enough night, they left it alone and just didn't use it to sleep. But then the next day, they found a dead bug on the bed. Thinking, ok, this is just a one-off, its dead, maybe we brought it in from outside, they also ignored it. But then the next night, they found a LIVE bug in the bed. 
A couple of other things to make the experience less than desirable: We came into the room once to drop something off and the maid's cart was directly in front of the door. We moved it aside and tried to use the key, which didn't work immediately. After a couple of tries, it opened, and we were surprised to see the maid in the bathroom. This was odd, as I thought maids are supposed to leave the door open, or at least propped with the deadbolt while they are inside. She also didn't open the door when she heard us trying to get in. Not suggesting she was doing anything wrong (and there was no evidence of anything like that), but it was weird. On their last night in the hotel, my parents came back on their last night after a long day only to find the towels and toiletries hadn't been restocked. It was easily solved, but they shouldn't have had to call for something that's part of the regular service.
The rooms were comfortable, the location was great, and the concierge and desk staff downstairs were helpful. But dirty comforters and bugs in the bed just aren't acceptable; and perhaps the cleaning staff might need a little more training, too. Unfortunately, these issues are enough to make me never want to stay here again (or recommend it to anyone, either).
My company has used this hotel for multiple events and have always been impressed with their facility and the incredible service they provide. I would highly recommend them to anyone.

We arrived early in the AM from a red-eye flight and the terrific woman at the front desk (Eliva?)not only let us check in early but upgraded us to a newly renovated room. Of course, as is typical of the Four Seasons the bed was sublime. We have stayed at this property in the past and never been disappointed. Last year due to some of the negative reviews about Four Seasons Boston we stayed at Beacon XV- what a mistake! The service at Beacon XV is truly awful, does not even compare.

We stayed two nights. Our first night, the room got so hot that we could not sleep; we had to be moved to a new room the next night. The bigger issue is that i got bed bug bites while at the hotel. Yuck! I won't be back.

This hotel is closer to the South Mall than the airport, but they have a free shuttle which picks you up and drops off, so the extra - minute drive is really irrelevant. We do have to wait an extra ----- minutes for the pickup, but it is really worth it. 
We have stayed here - times recently and every time has been great. Each room is a suite with a living area, fold out couch, TV and small kitchen and a large bedroom with beautiful bathroom. Breakfast is buffet style with make-your-own waffles, fruits, cereals, yogurts, muffins, toast, scrambled eggs and meat and fresh juices. There is a fireplace and big-screen TV in the lobby which looks out on the pool and hot-tub (in a pretty little gazebo).
In the evening there are soft drinks in the breakfast area and on certain days there is a free happy hour with snacks, but we have not been there for that. The staff is really friendly and professional and the maid service has turned towel-folding into an origami artform. Rooms are immaculately clean and very quiet. Their soaps and shampoos are first class and we always look forward to popping the complimentary pop-corn in the microwave. Trying to find this place on your own is tricky, it cannot be seen from the main roads, so call for directions or use a map.

We got out of the subway station and started walking to the hotel and I can't help but wonder if I would get mugged. But Strangely enough..after that, it was perfectly safe! we took the subway back at midnight and walked back to the hotel and no one was on the streets... very quiet and safe! I would definitely recommend this hotel! It's a great bargain hotel and there are a lot of free perks that most hotels would charge a ton for!

My fiance and I stayed at the Hotel Boheme in October ---- for the Columbus Day weekend. The hotel is in an excellent location. We were walking distance to Chinatown, Fisherman's Wharf, the Alcatraz tour, and we even walked to the Golden Gate Bridge. Chinatown was a -- minute walk,Fisherman's Wharf was about ----- minutes, the Alcatraz tour was about -- minutes and the Golden Gate Bridge was about an hour long walk from Boheme. Now for the bad part. If you have a room facing Columbus Avenue, it will sound like a parade is going down the street at night. No joke. For some reason, the noise filters through the windows and is magnified by ---x in your room. Request a room on the opposite side of Columbus if you are a light sleeper. The only issue i had was the regular rooms are on the small side, but the out of this world comfy bed made up for it ! I highly reccomend this hotel. it is in a safe and nice area close to everything.

Absolutely loved it. The only problem - their web-site directions seemed wrong when you exit the Bay Bridge. Thanks to those handling luggage, opening the front door, parking our car, pouring wine each night from - - - pm, cleaning our room, etc. All wonderful. The beds and pillows were so comfortable I slept soundly each of the - nights we were there. On the plus side, the location was excellent, the price reasonable, the breakfast, which was included, we very good.
Very disappointed. Only time will tell if we bring the crawly creatures back home with us. Let's hope not!

Relaxed and comfortable, with the amenities you want, this hotel shines. My room-bath-closet were large and spotlessly clean. Everyone on the hotel staff is friendly and helpful. I can highly recommend a Concierge named Mark; he was knowledgeable and kind.

I too enjoy the reviews from Tripadvisor as I plan vacations to new destination. I again used this site in the planning of our trip to Chicago for the -th of July.

horrible room...dust on carpet.....front office people high attitute....no cust serv.....heater not working....they took -- mins to come and have a look what's the problem with heater....sunita front office terrible attitute....no blanket and outside it was freezing...

The first night someone from housekeeping knocked on our door and said “$--.
