We were able to walk to restaurants, Dupont Circle, Georgetown, the White House, etc. 
We were turned off when we first arrived because the service was poor, even though it wasn’t busy. When someone finally got around to helping us, our room wasn’t ready, even though it was after check in time. They hadn’t even started cleaning the room yet. They told us the day before had been very busy. (My thoughts – I was busy yesterday, too. My room should still be ready at the agreed upon time, however. ) After waiting a while, a manager offered us a drink in the bar – not a great concession for a family – and at -:-- in the afternoon! I asked if they would consider waiving the valet parking fee, so that we could leave our car and start exploring the area while our room was being cleaned. They agreed. We were happy with that.
Best thing about the hotel is location – which is EXCELLENT. If we had paid full price ($---+), however, I would have been very disappointed. Since we booked our room on Hotwire for $----night, I really can’t complain. We really appreciated the fact that they waived the $---night valet parking fee as well. We would go back.

We had been driving aroung looking for a hotel, it was a last minute decision to stay the night in San Antonio. Everywehere else we looked was booked and althought the sign was old and faded it said the Ramada limited. I have always heard good things about them so I figure it would be ok. My mistake!, we book the room and left, only to come back after a tour around the town and find the room that was given to us already occupied. We tried and tried the key, and were unable to open it and finally the door open and a man came out, I had my -year old son with me and he scared us, he said we had the wrong room and I immediatelly apoligize, shaken, and embarresed I went to the front desk. The desk clerk was nice but did not seem surprise, he provided us with a different room and apologize lightly by saying it was a mistake the owner had made, since he was the one that book us in. Their reputation is not at all a good one.

It doesn't get better than this! The Hotel Drisco is located in Pacific Heights with views that are breath-taking. My three children were with me (ages --, -- & --) & they agreed that the Hotel Drisco is the nicest hotel they've stayed in worldwide. The staff is at your beckon call! We will return to only the Hotel Drisco whenever we are in San Francisco.
The Admiral Fell Inn is a lovely place to stay in a great neighborhood and they allow dogs!

Pro's: attentive front desk, Georgetown location, kitchen
Con's: housekeeping, dated interior, slow elevators, no outlets near the bed, escort needed to unlock the gym
The housekeeping issues were pretty basic issues. There was no toilet paper on check-in and they failed to replace the removed towels. Each time a trip to the front desk was met with prompt, friendly service. Even when I needed an extra blanket for my son, the front desk went to the sixth floor to find one.
If a kitchen is an absolute must and you need to walk into Georgetown then this hotel will meet your needs.

I was very nervous to stay here after I read about the nightmares people experienced at the front desk upon checking in. To sum it all up, you are not getting a- star royal treatment stay at this hotel, so if you're looking to spend a lot of time in your room, look elsewhere. If you are looking for something basic while you explore the city...look no further. 
The staff was very friendly and let us check in early..(with the exception of the manager who was a little short with me one time when I asked a question) I personally did not have any problems, but did notice that there was an incident at the front desk when a staff member didn't show up for work so there was a line of people waiting to check in..the manager ended up showing up. 
Prices are excellent for location. I recommend booking through the official website, it's cheaper sometimes. 
Location is prime. Short walk from the subway, - stop away from --nd st (times square), brisk walk to Central Park, quieter than most neighborhoods, but it's beautiful. Located in the Upper West side with shops, restaurants and drugstores just around the corner. For this price, you can't get a better location. 
The rooms are small, the lighting is not the greatest. But functional. We got a private bath, modern and very clean, but very, very small. The shared bathrooms are also surprisingly very clean. The TV's in the room are also nice. 
They have fresh coffee in the lobby every morning and computers-you have to pay for wi fi.You can also store your bags for $- a bag in their storage room if you have a late or early flight. 
Affordable and basic. I would stay here again.

When we arrived at the Hotel Triton we had traveled all day and were extremely tired. The hotel serves wine and tea from -:----:--pm weekdays and we arrived at -:--pm. Erik checked us in and sent us a glass of wine to our room which we received as the porter was putting our bags up. Erik later called and asked if everything was o.k. in the room and if we'd gotten our wine. One day they had a plate of warm chocolate chip cookies at the front desk for guests. These special touches made this hotel our favorite out of a ---day trip. Our room was great also and it overlooked the gates to Chinatown. I will definitely recommend this hotel to friends and family who want to visit San Francisco.

I booked this hotel mainly because it looked like it would be less hectic than the other Shelter Island Hotels. I was worried after some of those reviews that I made a bad decision, I even had other hotels staked out incase. I did not have to worry. This was the perfect spot for what I was looking for. Though there was a mustiness to the hotel room, it did not smell BAD, opening the sliding glass wiindow onto the patio took care of that. The bathroom was small and yes a little worn, but it was clean. The pool was great but if you want some quiet, don't go on a weekend, too many teens and children. The room service was excellent, we ordered dinner twice and breakfast - it took -- to -- minutes just like they said and everything was hot. Their restaurant was very nice inside and out, I especially liked it outside as it overlooked the bay and felt private. Their bar was nice but it seems they only take your orders at poolside on Saturdays. However, a little cooler with drinks is perfect, the ice machine is close enough. We had initially booked the Marina View, that wasn't ready at time of check-in and received a room in the ------- portion above the lobby. This was great it was the closest to the Bay, laying on the bed we could see the water and a little patch of green. We had a great time sitting out on the porch watching everyone walking with their dogs and enjoying themselves. I looked around and a lot of the ocean views had too much parking lot as part of it. I recommend this part of the building highly. Because this hotel is at the end, it gets less car traffic. I spent a lot of time walking around the bay and marina - it is pretty enough that if you choose not to go anywhere you still get to be out of the hotel grounds and enjoy the scenery. I never once thought this place was noisy, I'm not sure if the people by the doors and ice machines felt the same way, so you may ask and be sure you are not in a traffic path. I was looking for a quiet and laid back place with no frills but clean, this was it.

Took my girlfriend to The Standard on Valentine's Day ---- for a romantic night away from home in NJ. We pulled up to this place, and the decor from the yellow chairs outside and the yellow doors is just amazing. I had to drive around the block once because I didn't know where to leave my car, but on the second time around - got so lucky and found a spot literally right next to the door. If you are just staying over on a weekend...you are allowed to park there and I recommend it as it saved me the $-- valet charge! The bellhop was nice as can be and took our bags for us as soon as I parked. We arrived at around -:--pm and our room was not ready yet, however they offered us each a free drink which we were glad to take. An hour later, our room still was not ready (I was starting to get a little upset) but another complimentary drink each saved that from happening!) Finally, our room was ready, just a normal queen room with an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Empire View"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" What a tremendous view of the empire state building from our floor to ceiling windows! At night it was lit up for Valentines day in white red and pink!...so romantic and so wonderful. The room was perfect. A typical smaller NYC room, however it was very roomy with the most comfortable bed I have slept in in years. There is a nice -- inch flat screen on the wall with a nice sitting area. One thing I would say about these rooms...dont go with someone you dont know very well! (and I mean very well!) The shower is completly see through. As you sit on the bed, you can see directly into the shower through the glass - very neat if your with your girlfried-wife..not so neat if your with a co-worker!! The bathroom is private, with a door. The tub is massive-and the shower was wonderful! There is no door on the shower so the floor can get a little wet! I had flowers waiting in the room for my girlfriend, which came out perfect from the conceirge! In the morning, just a phone call away was a commplimentary breakfast-brought straight to the room. Coffee, OJ, and pastries were perfect on a Sunday morning...and I didnt have to get out of bed! Overall a WONDERFUL hotel-with extremely accomodating (and good looking) staff!! Got a construction rate of $--- for a saturday night. Not a sound or look of construction on the weekends!! Would highly recommend!!!

This was only my second stay at a Kimpton property, the other being the Hotel Monaco, also in Chicago. The hotel Allegro was very nice and the staff was extremely accommodating and friendly! The hotel is very attractive on the inside and has several dining options attached, including ones that are open late in a otherwise desolate downtown area. The rooms are very small, but that's to be expected. If you're traveling with a family, I would go with the Monaco, but our romantic weekend getaway was perfect for the Hotel Allegro!

My family (including one teenager) stayed at the Casablanca Hotel for our spring break trip this year. What a great experience. What's not to like? The breakfast buffet was tasty, and we enjoyed the wine and cheese every afternoon. It was a great way to unwind after a day of sightseeing before going out to dinner and theater. We also enjoyed coming back for coffee and tea after our """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""night on the town."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" The staff was congenial and very helpful!
It is true that our room had no view, but it was clean and there was plenty of room for the three of us. (We had a two double beds and still room for suitcases). There was a window that actually opened to allow for cross ventilation if we wanted it. Our only complain was that our mattress was very soft and should be replaced. When we mentioned it to the management we were told that they had a schedule to do so. So it is something you might want to check on.

We stayed here for - days. The lobby was modern and nice. The rooms including bathrooms have been renovated with a modern polish. The bathroom is spacious. There was also a small refrigerator. It is not a huge hotel, so it is not too busy. This seems to make it more relaxing and a place to get away from the hustle and bustle of the city. The pool is beautiful with a wonderful view of the city. another plus, is that It is close to the theatre district. It is a great value.

We were in NYC at the end of October - got out of there right before the snow! Our experience with the hotel was awesome! The staff was super friendly and the atmosphere was comfortable and elegant. The concierge was fantastic!! We loved every place he recommended to us because he took the time to listen to what we liked and wanted. AND...after reading many reviews, I expected the beds to be rock hard but they were not - we thought they were very comfy! The rooms weren't huge but they were just fine. My only disappointment was that I expected a good view of Times Square but instead got the view of a building and a tiny part of one of a sign. I'm going with a group of girls and our daughters in the spring and might stay at Millenium Broadway again.

I have stayed at this property before and I love it. It is cute and funky. The rooms are small, but clean and the staff is always very friendly. They have wine tasting sometimes and a cozy lobby where travelers from all over the world connect.
This last time I stayed on the Everest floor (it is the top floor that has been deemed """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""GREEN""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""). I wanted to do something good for the environment and also wanted to check out the remodeled floor. Well, it looked EXACTLY like the other levels except for the cool water filter in the hall and mass pump shampoo and conditioner in the shower. I liked the lask of waste, but come on, the room was directed the exact same- no remodel and for a heftier price tag per night.
Next time I will save $-- a night and turn my lights off, use my own shampoo and stay in the same room for less while doing my part to chip in for the environment.

I booked this hotel at the last minute. Priceline actually picked it out for me and what a great result. The Marriott Waterfront on Baltimore's Inner Harbor was very very nice. It seemed brand new although I suspect it's been there a while. Throughout the hotel, everything was in great condition. Rooms clean, bright and well appointed including a big LCD tv. The carpeting in the rooms, hallways and public areas seemed brand new. The pool and healthclub were both modern and clean. 
The location is also a winner. Very close walk to all the Inner Harbor attractions. On top of all this, I found the staff very friendly, helpful and knowledgeable.
 My future stays in Baltimore will always be at this hotel and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it to anyone.

Stayed two days March ----.
Positive: - stories, very quiet rooms, great breakfast, very businessperson oriented, clean, free parking, helpful and pleasant staff, good if you have a generous expense account.
Negative: Wrong billing-twice, pricy, $-- per day for high speed Internet, in a business-industrial area so services are distant.

Well, as has been pointed out elsewhere, the rooms are small. Quite small. However, that's a fault you'll find in most mid-range hotels in NYC so I won't mark it down on that alone.
Now that's out of the way, the WJ isn't a bad hotel. The rooms were clean and comfortable, the staff were friendly and the location us unbeatable. The subway is around the corner, opening up NYC while the local area has tons of restaurants to choose for, along with being a short walk to Times Sq, Columbus Circle, Port Authority Bus station etc. 
As such, if you're looking for a nice, central location and reasonable comfort (if not space) and you can get this hotel at a reasonable price, I certainly wouldn't pass it up. My room had a nice walk in shower that was roomy and powerful - something I do like in a hotel!
Two negatives - small slow lifts (an old building, so not all that surprising) and the free wifi is very unreliable (great to have it, but not so great when the connection drops every minutes!).
If the price was right, I'd stay again however.

We booked a sky view room for a weekend trip to NYC. I would say the room was average size for NYC, and the view from the --th floor was great. Decoration and cleanliness were top notch. The only criticism I can think of is that there is no mirror in the room itself, only in the bathroom. I didn't really notice, but my wife and her female friends who stopped by all did.
The location was great for us. Close enough to Times Square, but not right in it, so it was quieter and less bright. Normally I don't eat at hotel restaurant's but I made an exception for Ca Va Brasserie by Todd English as I really wanted to try it. There are hundreds of excellent places to eat in New York, but I was not disappointed in the slightest that we ate here. Easily on par with the other places we dined that weekend. If we were in town longer I definitely would have gone back.

I am still at this hotel, I had chosen it because it belongs to the Marriott chain and the price was great (-- usd ++ per room). Wow it was a good choice - a lovely studio room on the second floor with all the amenities and nicely """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Marriott style"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" decorated, we also had a little kitchen which we haven't used but I like the concept. Wi-fi is free and powerful, staff is nice, breakfast buffet good but the breakfast room is little small - even though we found it full and had to wait only one day out of six. And finally, the hotel is located in a lovely area which seems in the countryside but it is only -- minutes drive from vibrant downtown. So, for the little price we paid, I could not immagine a bettet option. Well done Marriott!

heartbreak hotel staff very off handish had trouble to even smile. even though my daughter informed the hotel it was my birthday didnt get as much as a happy birthday. hotel had a few large photos but unless you stayed in specialised rooms you wouldnt know you were anywhere special.. the only person to make us smile was the lovely barman. breakfast simple. Friends stayed at the day hotel a short way away and had a much better experience.

I agree with the positive reviews here. Everything met or exceeded our expectations.
The check-in staff were especially helpful. Premised were clean, attractive, relaxing.

Stayed for one night while I was working Dallas Market. Very convenient location, and lots of great restaurants within walking distance. The staff is fantastic. Super friendly. The only bad thing was a hair in the bathroom.

I like kimpton hotels so far this has been my fav in DC. Reception is very cool looking and staff are very helpful. Hotel is quiet and clean.
Little bar area but nothing much seems to happen there. I really enjoyed our modern room, the bed had it's own little nook with nice lights that dim and a sheer that could cover it. There was plenty of room and a little sofa, which i think could turn into a bed. The only bad part of this room is the bathroom, it's soooo small, i could barely move in there.
Will stay here again

We were to spend five days here, but left after only two. The room was spacious, the bed comfy, the bathroom clean. We were literally driven nuts by the room air conditioner. There was no wall thermometer, so we were either shivering, or uncomfortably hot. There was no comfort there.
The hotel itself is located in a very, busy, very congested area, near the - freeway. The traffic was unrelenting no matter the time of day. Every time we left the hotel it was pure madness. The streets were always packed with a line of cars. Very unpleasant indeed.
We saw some unsavory characters strolling through the parking lot, walking around our car and other cars. That was disturbing. Further, there appeared to be several encampments of grizzly homeless people about the outside of the hotel. We just didn't feel safe there.
We checked out the hot tub. When we came back some ten hours later, the same group of rowdy drunk people were still where they were when we left. However, some -- or -- of their beer cans were carelessly strewn about. Nice that they had their own private hot tub with greenish yellow water! That was very poor of management not to keep an eye on the public areas.
Jasmine and Susan were very kind, very sweet people. We enjoyed them immensely. Susan took a liking to our little dog and gave him lots of attention and treats. He liked her too.
This hotel was recently renovated. They did a fine job. But, they can't change the location of the property. And that was the reason we chose to leave. 
The owner should promote Jasmine. She is one of the precious few people who truly understand hospitality. An amazing young lady.

Proximity to airport, walking distance to anywhere in the city, Little Italy around the corner, -- mins to DT, -- mins to water.
As far as hotel goes, we had all we needed during our --day stay in SD last summer.
Clean, neat, everything works, nice crowd, what else do you need.
Nothing fancy, but who need s that in a city with -major beaches and a great nightlife?
Def will consider staying there again

The Trump Soho is an amazing hotel. 
The hotel is beautiful, and has an amazing location in Soho. We walked everywhere, shopped until we dropped, and ate in lots of fun little cute restaurants in the neighborhood. Our rooms (we stayed in two different rooms) had an AMAZING view, of the water, and both the king bedded room and the suite we stayed in had great set ups, were well planned out, and comfortable to stay in with great beds and pillows, fluffy towels and even outlets that you could actually find and use without having to climb under the furniture
From our experience (five of us meet in NYC for a weekend every summer) a beautiful hotel and an amazing view does not always equal a great hotel. What makes the Trump Soho a great hotel is the staff. They are professional and knowledgeable, but it is obvious that their training goes beyond """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""skills training"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and somehow includes how to actually combine being real people and remain professionals simultaneously. A rare art form.
Just a few examples include the woman at the front desk who checked us in with charm and style and a smile that made us feel like she truly cared. She ensured that our room change went smoothly, looked into everything personally, and followed up when necessary. The door men and bell men always had a smile, and were very professional. One afternoon when the four of us left the hotel, the door man ran back to get water bottles for us. “It’s too hot for you to walk around, I am worried that you will dehydrate” he told us. The room attendant on our floor greeted me with a big smile and a “good morning” when I left the room. All of these employees helped to make our stay something special, but if we had to choose one “employee of the weekend” it would undoubtedly be the concierge, who was so professional, detail oriented but still sweet and so pleasant to talk to that we were actually sad to say good bye.
Run, don't walk, and make a reservation there now. You will not be sorry.

I recently spoke with the manager regarding our stay - Room ---- the week of July --, ----. I informed him that while the accommodations were comfortable (minus a lack of a bathroom fan), my daughter and son had been bitten by a type of bed bug on one of the first nights. We are not dirty people, nor did we think such a prestigious hotel would pose such a risk, however a doctor verified the kids were bitten then. Several hundred dollars in medication, doctor visits and after cleaning our home, car and laundry we feel like we have eradicated the bug. The manager (maybe his name was Michael) said he would contact me once he reviewed hotel policy, but never did. During our conversation, he continued to say the hotel had never had any bug problems before and dismissed my concerns saying the room was currently rented out to another guest. I’m not looking to take advantage of anyone, but I feel angry and embarrassed for your hotel that you obviously think so much of yourself that you cannot even take a charge like this seriously because “you change the sheets every three days.” Our vacation in Boston was a great time, but every time we think back the first thing that comes to mind is the bugs. It’s not the way we wanted to remember the trip we planed for over a year. Regardless of the eventual outcome I don’t foresee any more stays at Hilton-owned properties.

I have stayed here twice so far -- both times in July. I am very impressed by this hotel. The staff is super friendly. A shout out to Jonah, who worked at the front desk the first time I was there, and recognized me when I arrived back a year later! He was really exceptional.
-
The rooms are small, but that's to be expected in New York City. The hotel location is one block from Times Square but is so quiet, you don't realize how close you are. 
There is free wine and cheese from --- each day, and a complimentary breakfast each morning. The decor is warm and welcoming.
The only complaint is that the air conditioner is noisy, but that complaint pales in comparison to the compliments. This is an incredible place. Great for business trips and families.

I typically care about two things - location and the quality of rooms. Location wise, you can't beat this. It's a - minute walk from Union Sq and right by Market St as well as the Bart and the Trolley. It's always a toss up between the Marina versus Union Sq, and as a very frequent traveller, I think Union Sq is far more convenient.
The rooms seem to have been recently renovated. There is a fresh look about the decor and the finishes. The size of the rooms is VERY substantial by typical San Francisco standards. Also, request a high floor because the views are fantastic. 
Overall, I would highly recommend this hotel for great value to the upscale customer.
This has been the best hotel I have stayed at. The staff is extremely friendly, especially Anna. They know how to take care of the customers and I will definitely be back!!!!

My friend and I go to NYC for the theatre, Opera and museums, at least once a year. I picked the Millennium Broadway for its location, not realizing it had entrances on --th and --th Streets. This proved a happy surprise and made for an easy walk to all of the Broadway theatres, Sardi's, Orso and Joe Allen's, our favorite restaurants. Not having to allow time for flagging a taxi and inching through Times Square pre-theatre traffic made for a relatively carefree visit. Our room on the --th floor was handsome, well laid out and had a truly breathtaking view of Manhattan. The staff and chambermaids were pleasant and helpful, the public areas were immaculately maintained. My only complaint was the WiFi surcharge, which at a punative daily rate, I declined to use. With the room rate of $---. per day, the Millennium might considering comping WiFi.

This is my first trip advisor review. We were pleasantly surprised with the personal attention given from the time we arrived until the thank you email I just received at home. We arrived with a car and a -- ft U-Haul van. They graciously directed us to a lot for the truck less than a block away. Our belongings were safe there overnight. The room was spacious and nicely remodeled, with out of the way closet space, safe, and mini fridge. We ate dinner and breakfast there and both were above average and delicious. We intend to stay there often now, since our experience was trouble-free!

We chose this hotel due to its location, being only - blocks south from central park. We had a 'suite' - ie a bedroom with two big double beds, and a sitting room with a sofa bed, plasma tv and kitchenette. This arrangement allowed our baby to sleep in peace while we were still awake and watching tv etc in the other room. The kitchenette had a fridge, sink and microwave. But no crockery - we had to buy plastic plates etc from a nearby supermarket.
Negative points
Overall the hotel is a bit dated if that matters to you. In other words it's not a glitzy New York experience, just a functional, clean place to stay.
Bathroom was very small and dated. 
The air-conditioning units were very noisy which could be a problem when needed in the summer. 
Plus points
 The room was very spacious, so good for families with plenty of space for toddlers to run around. Room was kept very clean, with numerous closets for clothes. Lovely big, comfortable beds. 
 The hotel offers a toast-bagel type breakfast for four dollars but no other restaurant facilities. Local restaurants will do room service. There is a supermarket - mins away to buy milk, cereal etc. 
Overall it was pretty good value in an expensive city and a lot of attractions are in walking distance. I would most probably stay here again because of these plus points.

What a treasure! We've visited Baltimore many times, but stayed in the suburbs. I discovered the Admiral Fell Inn when researching Baltimore on line. Our first experience was with Dorian at the front desk who cheerfully took care of our bags, car, and showed us to our delightful room. We saw him throughout our stay, he remembered our names and continued to be very helpful. The Admiral Fell Inn is a wonderfully restored historic landmark. The rooms are beautifully appointed, ours had lovely canopy beds which were incredibly comfortable and deep set colonial style windows. The lovely cozy room was equipped with all the modern amenities, as well. Great room service, too. The area is historic and loaded with charming pubs, very good restaurants and unique original shops and galleries, (no chains, which was a nice change), all within an easy walk around the harbor area. Water taxis are available, also a free shuttle to take you around the harbor to a new entertainment venue, but who wants to leave Fells Point! It's completely captivating! We had hoped to find a ghost or two, but were unable to locate any! We'll definitely be back at the Admiral Fell Inn!

This hotel is nothing special. It's a fairly long hike from Harvard Square and the buses are not very frequent.
Make sure you are not located on the ice rink side or your sleep will be affected.
Generally the place is pretty rundown. It is close to a Shaws, a Kmart and a McDonalds (v. poor - even for this chain) but next time we'll stay nearer the centre of Boston and pick a better hotel.

Unfortunately this review ain't going to get me too many """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""was this review helpful"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" clicks because I'm going to briefly reiterate what others have said.
It's obviously a perfect location if your travel involves arriving at or from LAX. I make it a habit to stay at airport hotels when I'm flying east and have an early morning flight. Quite convenient ditching the rental car the night before and then hopping on the hotel shuttle bus.
From check-in to check-out this hotel was a delight. I was a solo dad traveling with a tired, cranky --year-old and they got us in and out perfectly. The pool at this hotel is great and for those of you who specifically seek out airport hotels to watch planes this place is amazing if you ask for an airport runway view and there are many. As for those of you don't don't like airport hotels because of the noise this place should not be an issue. I didn't notice any plane sound.
Rooms were newly renovated, there's a Starbucks in the lobby, parking is a ripoff (but that's the case at all LAX hotels...) and the restaurant was decent for breakfast.
I've stayed at the Embassy Suites across the street, that's a good bet too if you specifically need a suite hotel. 
The LAX Marriott is one of my personal favorites because of the runway views but that's just me

This place is disgustingly dirty: carpets are FILTHY, ceilings caving in, wall paneling falling off, sheets and mattresses old and dirty, exposed wiring, no working A-C, dirty bathroom, no functional smoke detector, decrepit room, door doesn't have deadbolt or chain...NO THANKS! I checked out the room and then CHECKED OUT! Not safe, not clean, not a bargain in the end. NO WAY!

Stayed here for just one night on my way to Anaheim. I was upgraded to a Suite that had a master bedroom and a separate living room. The room looked a little dated but it was OK otherwise. I found the location convenient and the hotel staff was very helpful and gave me information about the close by attractions, that way I was able to go to Manhattan Beach using the cute shuttle that you can take right up the street from the Westin LAX. Overall a very good experience. Nice restaurant, good food and they have a band that plays live some nights a week. The check in was fast and the service was what I expected from this property.

Denver is one of those cities that requires driving. I rented a car and drove from the airport to the hotel. As I continued to drive and drive, I came upon downtown Denver, which I eventually passed (?) and then finally saw the hotel. Given the location I would presume it was slightly outside of downtown or in a developing-or tired area.
Pros:
Great staff
Heated pool... did not use but saw others in the elevator coming from the pool
heard the PH deck and pool has a good view, but did not have time to use
Street parking is available
regular room was great size, came with a small bar area
good size bathroom
staff is helpful, received great parking tip (free during wkends) and good restaurant suggestions
quiet stay away from 'party areas'
relatively quiet room, could here some water pipes and elevator, but didnt mind
clean room 
pretty close to business district and highway access 
Cons:
dated interiors, its your parent's furniture!
dated patio (fake carpet-rug?) honestly just having cement alone is better!
mix and match artwork
Location, required -----min walk to --th """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Mall street"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (not much to see there)
Received view of parking lot - back of the hotel, perhaps worth inconvenience of requesting dif room
Compared to the barely four star hotels (e.g. ran by a socialite's father, name rhymes with milton); it seems to be lacking modern appeal... 
Warwick is a four star name, but I didnt get that four star feel.
Very clean & modern hotel. Staff were very friendly & helpful. No problem getting refund when we had to evacuate for Irene.

I stayed here for - nights on a mixture of business and travel. 
Overall, I would say it was a good experience.
Plus points: I really liked not being up in the hustle and bustle with all the tourist hoards, this is nearer Chelsea and the Garment district. I also found the free business centre a plus and the staff really helpful at all times. Going back to the location, you're close to the Fashion Museum-College so handy for that, there's a CVS down the street, Whole Foods a few blocks and various other stores around. Easily walkable to the Square Garden and --th St shops like Macys. 
Negatives: I might have been something to do with the hotel being relatively newly opened but on occasion there were some issues with the lifts being operational (altho only - out of action at a time) so sometimes it was painfully slow waiting for the lift. I was on the --nd floor, so after a long day didn't really fancy the walk!
Rooms: I had just the one bed, it was perfectly comfortable, choice of pillows. Flatscreen, two phones, tiny wardrobe and some drawers. Bathroom fairly compact, shower only though which suited me. There are only -- room rooms on each floor I think and altthough you could hear noise from doors closing I couldn't really hear the people around me. 
I had a high floor room at the back of the building. Now, I'm not sure where it's an upgraded room type but I had a great view across to the Empire State Building, so it might be worth asking as decent veiws can be hard to come by in NYC hotels. 
I did have room service, which was adequate and came in good time - but didn't try the restaurant. 
Overall, I would stay here again as it was in a good location and a budget hotel.

Check in was a breeze, lobby area is great offering starbucks and subway along with other restaurants and cafe and small bar. Hallways are open to the large building so there is not that stuffy feeling. Corner room was spacious, everything was neat and clean. Bed and pillows were most comfy. Conveniently located to everything in this fun little city. Had a great weekend, highly recommend this hotel!

My husband and I stayed overnight at Hotel Sorella, reserving the Big Easy Package for our anniversary. It was simply amazing: the decor, service, atmosphere, ambiance, proximity to other spots of interest. The jazz brunch was very charming: both food and entertainment. I would recommend this hotel to anyone wanting a departure from the ordinary. We absolutely loved it.

I will start with - positive point about the hotel since this is the only advantage it has: location and proximity. Yes it is - minute away from the main shopping street and faces the river.
Other than that, the hotel needs serious renovation. Rooms are tiny, the carpet smells so bad across the hotel and rooms. The hotel looks like it hasn't been renovated ever since it opened, maybe decades ago. 
The lobby is a joke, the bell boy was not there to help with bags and one of the staff was super rude, he is an Egyptian guy I believe, if the manager of this hotel is reading this review, then please do some serious training to this guy and make him learn to smile and be less pushy towards your customers, the rest of the staff is super helpful and nice!
Overall experience and according to the above, I don't recommend anyone to stay at this hotel. Chicago has plenty other decent hotels to offer.

Clean hotel with friendly staff right in the heart of San Francisco. The only reason I voted - star overall is because it doesn't have a bar or restaurant, but obviously this isn't too much of a problem in San Francisco! Don't think twice about booking this hotel if you want nice accommodation in a great location
What a friendly staff, room was very clean and spacious,close to what we wanted to see,would come back again,recommend staying here.

I am really enjoying my stay at the Washington Hilton. We got in yesterday morning and decided to try the breakfast buffet. It was so good. The Washington Hilton is a large hotel, but very clean. The employees are very friendly and courteous. Isabel was the person that checked us in and she was wonderful. The only thing that I miss is having a refrigerator, microwave, and free wi-fi. Queen size beds would be a plus a well. The hotel is about -- minutes ( walking distance) away from the metro subway station. I would definitely stay here again.

This hotel must survive on convention business, because without this the facility would die rather quickly. To their credit, staff members are all polite and efficient. Rooms are DARK and OLD. While colors and furniture have been updated, the walls in my room were in poor shape. The shower head is the worst of the low flow to be found. Bathroom was old with poor lighting as well. Unless you are in Chicago at a convention is this facility, you can do much better nearby at other hotels.

I stayed at the Broadway Plaza on business in April, usually I stay midtown but I wanted to stay closer to meeting location near battery park. For the price, you cannot beat this hotel. I've stayed in $--- rooms in NYC that aren't even close to the size and view that this hotel offers. I stayed on the top floor, awesome view of the Empire State Building. Location is just okay, but obviously that is why it is cheaper than midtown. Macy's is seven blocks north, Union Square is -- blocks south, subway very close to hotel. Had a few minor issues with the high speed internet, but other than that, I have only positive impressions and will definitely stay again.

Service was excellent, location was great. Upon arrival asked for - double beds, my wife and I and - kids --,--. We and them were falling out of the beds. When ask for a room change, the FD responded that those are the standard double beds. We have stay in dozens of hotels in the USA and Europe. Never a problem. For this reason alone I would give this hotel a ** star rating

My husband and I always stay at the Hotel Commonwealth when we visit Boston. The hotel is conveniently located to Fenway Park and is an excellent choice if you are attending a baseball game. The hotel and guest rooms are beautifully decorated! The hotel is very clean and the restaurants located in the hotel are both excellent! Great place for couples, families, or a fun weekend with friends.

I have worked for many years for a well know luxury hotel company and am particular when it comes to hotel rooms. I must say I was a little nervous about checking into to this boutique hotel as these type of hotels can go either way in NYC. This boutique hotel exceeded my expectations from the pleasant front desk agent to the concierge who we did not utilize though ever time we were in the lobby I could over hear him assisting guests in well educated pleasurable manner. We had an incredible nice size suite on the --th floor with hard wood floors in the living room (love that) and a beautiful bedroom with a king size bed with a surplus of pillows! The room was nice and clean!!! The bathrooms were all marble tiles with Molton Brown amenities (two thumbs up) and a plethora amount of Frette towels and luscious (-) Frette bathrobes. In Room Dinning provided timely service. All the employees were engaging and friendly. The only thing I was disappointed about was that I could not stay longer. Great hotel and I would highly recommend!!

The Majestic is small, tidy, charming, convenient to the lakefront and Wrigleyville, and staffed by very efficient, helpful people. Rates are very affordable, and some of the rooms are on the small side, so it's well worth spending a few extra dollars to enjoy one of the rooms with a separate sitting area - sunroom. But if you're looking for an intimate, neighborhood hotel with character rather than one of the chain hotels while visiting Chicago, this is a terrific option.

The Tabard Inn has a cosy, slightly shabby-chic atmosphere that makes you feel instantly at home. The staff were all polite and helpful and the inclusive breakfast was excellent.
When I checked in I was told that I had been upgraded to a room with private bath at no extra charge. The room (room - on ground floor, and a bit noisy) was very large with a lovely bath under a skylight (it made a loud noise when it rained though). 
I liked the art deco styling, the selection of books, and the bed was very comfortable. Sadly I visited in January, so couldn't take advantage of the lovely garden. Next time...
I like this place but they need more people, the pool is great and you can see the Boeing Company from your window.

We stayed in the Cooper Square hotel between the ----th August and just loved it. This was our first time in NYC, so picking the right hotel was really important. We had heard a lot of negative report about the standard of hotels in NYC either being quite run down, bad service and problems with bed bugs. Cooper Square does not fall into any of these categories. 
Before we booked we researched a lot of hotels, but kept coming back to cooper square as all the reviews were high and it seemed to be a better location for us.
After a very hot transfer via subway to the hotel, the comp glass of wine was a lovely touch. Check-in was very quick and as we where staying for - nights our room had been up graded to a cooper - (we had booked a cooper -) on floor -. It would have been nicer to be higher up for the views but beggers can't be choosers! We just really appreciated the upgrade in the first place. All staff very professional and friendly.
The room was a good size, massive TV, lovely floor to ceiling windows on one wall, decore was modern and well kept, large safe, mini bar, air con and I really like the up to date time out magazines. The bathroom was suprising big with a free standing bath and separate shower, toilet and wash basin, good hair dryer with plenty of power.
The best thing about the room was the bed, it was huge and the most comfortable bed i have ever slept in - it was hard to get up each morning it was so comfy.
The location of the hotel is brilliant, handy to the subway (Astor Place on the green line in the closest to the hotel), just a walk away to union square, Washington Square, Greenwich Village, West Village and Soho - Chinatown. Plenty of restaurants to choose from and because of this we didn't eat in the hotel restaurant at all (well only breakfast on the last day, which was a pricey and not great). Plenty of bars and music venues to choose from and some good happy hour's close to the hotel. Phebe's and the Swift nice for a drink near to the hotel. 
The hotel has a bar on the -nd floor which is lovely but the night we went there was an event on, so we didn't stay as it was so busy and we didn't really feel that we fitted in.
I would highly recommend the Cooper Square Hotel to anyone who wants to be away from the 'touristy New York', likes the ultra modern vibe, trendy location and a comfortable sleep!

I took my family for a weekend to Seattle and chose this hotel because of the location. I was not disappointed. Great rooms, great location, great amenities. I can get a bit busy but nothing we can't handle. The parking is a bit of a hassle since you have to either pay big bucks to the valet or park it yourself in a parking lot that is a block away, not great during the rain or snow.
Close to the Pika Market and other shopping areas. I would go back to this hotel.

The Mission Bay location of this hotel cannot be beat! We enjoyed being on the gentler waters of Mission Bay rather than the busy loud neighborhoods of some of the oceanfront hotel areas. On Saturday night we even got to see the fireworks from Sea World off our balcony! It was also a great spot to get around town from, with easy access to major roads and sights.
We were on the -th floor of the tower portion, and wished we were closer to the lower main hotel area. We had asked for a water view and it did qualify as that, and we were thankful not to be on the east side which faced Hwy -! We got in after a long day's travel so we were just thankful to get to bed that night. The tower was obviously an older section, redone nicely, but the room's ventilation system smelled old damp and musty. It was too cold out to leave the screen to the balcony open to get fresh air all night. That would be nice in the summer though. We would request a non-tower room for that reason and one other. The motor noise and exhaust from shuttles, buses, limos taxis and etc that were allowed to idle between the tower and the front entrance created more echo and smell than they realize! Even a beer truck pulled by and honked me out of bed one morning at - AM. Thanks, Bud Light. Yeah, I should have complained.
The restaurant was very nice, but maybe too nice. The whole family enjoyed the breakfast buffet, but it was too expensive for us to do every morning. It cost us almost $--- for a family of four each day with tip! That was a bit of a problem at dinner too. After tramping around the theme parks, zoos and etc. we would have loved a more casual option in the hotel for dinner. By then the restaurant was just much too formal for frazzled foot weary families to relax in. 
On the positive, everything we did mention to the staff, was promptly handled and things were clean and staff friendly. The breakfast was excellent and service very good. The pool was fun and the outside fire pits were great for cool spring evenings. Overall I would recommend it for those who want a way to get away from overcrowded beach areas and yet still be close to it all.

We caught the train to Washington as the last leg of our holiday on the East Coast having stayed in Boston and New York. The Holiday Inn was booked by our travel agent and as I had changed the hotels in Boston and New York before leaving the UK I wish I had changed this one also.!! Check in was ok and the receptionist was lovely although not totally sure what she was doing when we asked to pay for a late check out. I am a priority card member but didnt get any better service for this.
We had a room on the -th floor overlooking the rail road and with the noisiset air conditioning system right outside the door. My husband liked the trains I found them noisy and our son used ear plugs! The maid had a habit of knocking and walking in which wasnt good although at least she smiled which is more than can be said for the other staff. The room was an adequate size though very old fashioned and jaded with sections of wallpaper peeling and a computer chair with damaged arms from being forced under the table. We did have internet access although not WIFI but it still worked for us and was beneficial. Toiletries were not replaced daily and only consisted of shampoo and conditioner. Nice to have a coffee machine although strange to put it in the bathroom. We always left the maid a tip each day but the room was never serviced to the best of standards. We noticed that room service plates were not collectecd for hours on end and just left outside doors. One room had plates outside with food on for -- hours, when it was collected by the maid as we walked past she dropped it and it broke all over the floor!!!!! Hotel does have a laundry facility for guests to use for $- which was very useful.
We had room service our first night and the pizza was good if not pricey, we ate breakfast once and the food for the rpice was mediocre and barely warm. One evening meal and again it was mediocre and a bit of a pot mess. The lady concierge the first day was rude and unhelpful when I asked about tours and just thrust a map at us. When we went down next morning a really helpful concierge booked us tours and that night after -- hours on duty she even recommended an excellent place to eat for us, the DC Chophouse, excellent food and good prices. This lady was a credit to the Holiday Inn.
The location is superb for the sights as it is walking distance of the Capitol buldings and the National Mall, the NASM and Botanical Gardens, the Museum of the American Indians and the art museums and so much more. The open top tours were excellent value also. There is a McDonalds - minutes away and a deli, pharmacy and local food store, taxis are plentiful amd the Le Infant Metro station just across the road and a starbucks on the premises which did amazing coffee and muffins when the staff werent having domestics!
On our last day we asked about transport to Dulles to be told by the surly male concierge taxis would cost around $-- but we could catch a bus for $- each from around the corner. He was rude and indifferent but at least gave some advice. The bus did indeed go from around the corner to Dulles but....this bus is used by commuters going back to Virginia as it is so cheap, so it was very crowded and our luggage was blocking the door, but it did save us so much money.
All in all the worst of the - hotels we stayed in but it was a great location for us. Wouldnt stay here again though as we do like a bit of luxury.

We stayed at the Casablanca Hotel for four nights (---th June ----). The hotel was recommended by a work colleague's friend (who usually only stays at four-five star hotels) so on this basis and the fact that it was rated so highly on Trip Advisor we decided to give it a go. Well, what can I say, it was excellent! We stayed in room --- - a mini suite - it was great to have that extra space with a bedroom and a lounge area. It was a belated birthday trip, which I must have mentioned upon booking, as when we arrived in the room there were two helium balloons and a bottle of fizz to greet us! The Room had a flat screen TV, DVD player (with complimentary library of DVDs available from the Front Desk), fridge-mini bar, complementary bottles of water. The room was spotlessly clean, the bathroom was great with lovely, fluffy towels and the usual wash items; we also had complimentary bath robes and slippers (perhaps only in the suites?). Breakfast was a choice of bagels, pastries, toasts, cereals, variety coffees, fruits and yoghurts. Coffee and tea is available throughout the day (-- hours) with biscuits-pastries and between ---pm there is cheese and wine. This is all complimentary. The staff were excellent and bent over backwards to assist our every need, they genuinely cannot do enough for you and this boutique hotel has a really homely feel, unlike some of the bigger chains which can be rather impersonal. We really could not fault the hotel at all. One thing to be aware of is that the air con is audible when on so not everyone may be happy to sleep with this, if not then there are very effective ceiling fans (assuming you are visiting during summer months). The location is excellent; you are about -- paces from Time Square, with great subway links up and downtown. For a hotel located so centrally it is surprisingly quiet inside and we didn't hear any street noise. All in all an excellent stay and I cannot rate-recommend this hotel highly enough. For anyone who has not visited NYC before we used Dial- limousine transfer into Manhattan (you can Google them for details and book on line). The service was very good and highly competitive, circa -- mins travel time. We had a basic sedan car from Newark at $--: plus tolls and tip the total was $-- (tolls and tips explained on the Dial- site). We went back to JFK and this was $-- all in. So, if you want great service, attentive staff and a fabulous location then book into the Casablanca Hotel, you won't regret it! Happy travels :o)

A soccer tournament listed this as one of the preferred hotels. It's in a very sketchy part of town. On the night we stayed, swarmed the hotel, which is more like a motel, looking for a knife-welding suspect. The pool was dirty. It was very loud, being under the San Diego airport flight path. Lots of late night yelling from other rooms. We didn't stay the second night, even though we'd paid for the room.

Went up to -- degrees in our room. Waited till we were both so sick to call down and they fixed it. New hotel, they decided to polyurethane the floor in main lobby, eating dancing area on a Saturday night?? The fumes were unbelievable!!! They offered me -- dollars back to compensate???? Should have comped me the room. Sleepless in manhattan

Location is great for CHerry Creek, great shopping and dining. The rooms or at least mine was a bit small. Hotel had limited staff on hand- which were very helpful and were able to get the room ready slightly before that dreaded statement, """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Check in is not until -(insert hour of choice)"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" This is the most easliy translated hotel excuse for we are understaffed or poorly trained or simply are not concerned for the tired business traveler. Just my pet peeve! However after some push back on my part they were able to expedite the room cleaning.

We like old fashioned hotels like the Waldorf. There is something in the shabbiness that's attractive in a comfortable sort of way. The last time we came we found ourselves in an horrific room. But, after a rough night, we complained and in fairness we were moved - and to a better room to boot. And of course there is that wonderful Guerlain Spa.....As my grandmother used to say, its not whether one runs into problems, its what one does to solve them that counts! 
So we came back. We decided to stay in a suite this time. We booked a King suite but got a Queen. The room was nice enough. We did not complain. We were too tired to face the check in desk again! There had been a long wait for check in because there were only three or four unfortunate staff trying to check in a long long line of people when we arrived.
Then we discovered that even though we had sprung for a nice suite - not cheap - they were going to charge us extra for wi-fi access! When my husband called the main hotel line he was told it was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""corporate policy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and apparently corporate policy is inviolate. We were reminded that if we wanted to use free wi-fi we should go down to the lobby! (Did I mention we were too tired to go to the lobby? But of course one there is always the spa....Opps! I forgot to mention there is no Guerlain spa here at the moment - nobody seems to know whether it will re open.....
My husband complained to corporate headquarters about this - there is something unpleasant about being """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""nickle and dimed""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""..... Guess what? corporate headquarters referred us back to reception """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""downstairs"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" once again. We called again - this time mentioning about not getting the king suite - prominent in our reservation - and I suppose we had met the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hassle threshold"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and so the wi-fi access was now free. 
It did not end there! During the night we noticed the room was cold. We tried to sleep - early appointment the next morning....When we got up to take a shower we discovered the water would not get hot - after -- minutes.....At least the wake up call came on time - and came, and came and came: the thing would not stop ringing. The lady told us we had to actually listen to the recorded message or else it would keep ringing. I told her this was ridiculous and asked her to make it stop. She did. Apparently also they had known about the problem with the water: during the night something had happened and the steam that heated the water in the building had not yet heated all the water. I was advised to wait for my shower - out of luck, I had to leave.....finally, we mentioned the cold room - the first question was whether we had called the staff during the night. I explained we had been trying to get some sleep......
The hotel made a reasonable adjustment to the room rate at checkout. We stayed here to reduce the stress of a long commute and instead of starting the day refreshed and relaxed....well, at this point: 'nuff said!
Why do I continue to recommend this hotel? It huge, but its comfortable - overall. I like rooms - this is indeed an historic hotel. When there is a problem, staff do their best to resolve it. The staff make a big difference here. This matters. Its just a pity there are so many problems they have to deal with! 
I'm not sure if you will be seeing us again though.....

This particular Comfort Inn is one of my favorite in the country. It's got beautiful views of the Ben Franklin Bridge and within walking distance of many of the touristy type of things like Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell. The continental breakfast is always well stocked with a nice selection of times and the front desk staff has always been courteous. I will be back for sure.

This was a surprise. I booked at this location solely because of the price--after having experience less-than-deal Holiday Inns, I had no expectations. For less than $---, this was incredible.
The rooms were spacious and well-equipped, and I was relieved to find that I couldn't hear too much outside noise. The location of the hotel itself was fantastic--just a hop away from Hollywood Boulevard and near the metro and the ---. 
The staff were very nice, especially the helpful valets and the wonderful lady who runs the free (and bountiful) breakfast buffet (which includes eggs and bacon in addition to the usual continental stuff). Parking isn't free, but at $-- a day, it's a good deal. You do need to drive a lot in LA!
Overall, shockingly good find. Absolutely would recommend this to anyone desiring the most luxury that no-frills sort of places provide.

While I was checking into the Westin San Francisco Market St. I was trying to adjust the bag I was carrying. I unfortunately had the special bottle of wine I brought with us in the bag and dropped it and it shattered on the floor. I felt horrible because of the mess I made, but instead of making me feel bad for making a mess of the floor, the receptionist (believe her name was Salora) appologized to me and offered to have a bottle of red wine sent up to us. That made me feel so special and made a very embarrassing moment immediately change to an exeptionally pleasent experience.
That wasn't the end of the tremendous experience. When the bellman, Edwardo, rang he brought not only the wine but a tray with fruit and cheeze and cracckers. He was extremely polite and wished us a very pleasant evening. A few minutes later Edwardo called and aske how we were enjoying the wine. He said that chocolate was the perfect thing to enhance our enjoyment of that wine and that he would be bringing up some strawberries dipped in chocolate to make our wine night perfect.
I want to say that your staff at the Westin made our stay so special that we will most definitely be making it a point to stay there again again. We live in Santa Cruz and go to many Giant games and plays in the City, so we are able to enjoy San Francisco often. I would recomend the Westin on Market to anyone who enjoys comfortable surroundings and an exeptional staff to make sure every detail is perfect.
I had a fabulous stay at Jury's. Very welcoming and comfortable. Fantastic location. I loved Cuffs, it is a great restaurant.

Stayed in suite. Got a nice deal through AMEX platinum conceirge. Hotel service was excellent and on par with what you expcect from a first class hotel. The room seem slightly dated but were very clean and there was a great view from the living room. What I loved the most was the AWESOME restaurant in the hotel. The food was the best I've had and I've travelled all over the country and ate in many top restaurants but I can't wait to go back there! Oh, and we even sat near Steve Martin during breakfast :)

It was our first time in Chicago and decided to stay downtown and experience the windy city during Christmas. Since we decided to drive we needed a downtown location with valet parking and this hotel seemed to offer all that we needed. The hotel is on Ontario St close to all Chicago attractions, minutes from the Magnificent Mile and walking distance to all that Chicago has to offer.
The customer service is impeccable, very professional and stress free. The room is small, but again this is a downtown hotel and the view itself is so worth it. Bed is very comfy we got a king size bed and so worth it, all is very clean and modern contemporary style to the last detail.For those of us that consider ourselves ecologically friendly, good news, this hotel uses all natural shampoo and body lotions in case you forgot to bring yours! We have literally no complaints about anything regarding this hotel, cleanliness is a very big issue for us and this hotel surpassed our expectations.
We are definitely looking fwd spending some time here again and we will not be looking for any other hotel to stay in Chicago!

First stay at a swissotel. I will definitely stay at any of their properties in the future. Great service amazing views from corner suite, great location. My morning business meeting was a short walk down the street.

My husband went on a fishing trip out of Point Loma San Diego, so we stayed right across the street from the marina. The staff were very nice and the rooms were clean. The complimentry breakfast was great. We had a king size bed, flat screen tv, fridge and microwave. There was a small pool for the kids to swim in. 
The only thing bad was the room which overlooked the marina was a very busy street so the noise level was bad. Otherwise it was a great stay!!!!!

Enjoyed two nights in this wonderfully located hotel! Very nice lobby area and the staff were all very helpful and friendly. The room was comfortable, though a little older and worn. We did a lot of walking and shopping in this area. Staff was very accommodating when we asked for a later check out since our flight left later in the day, and they stored our luggage while we did last day shopping. A great experience at this hotel and I would return again!

My daughter and I just returned from a wonderful - days in New York City. I wanted to stay at a hotel that offered an American Girl Package and I did a lot of research about it. From the moment we entered the hotel to the moment we left, we were treated incredibly well. Everyone was very polite, helpful and friendly. The rooms were clean and very comfortable. The beds they have are the best. If you ever have the opportunity to get to NYC, stay at the Fitzpatrick.

Like everyone said, the lobby is beautiful, but...
the hotel itself & the rooms are pretty outdated. I'm not very picky when I am a staying in a location like the Embarcaderro, but for the price...i guess I expected a bit more.
Average business hotel near the ferry building. The balconies and elevators are maybe the best of this hotel. There is not much else to do in the hotel.The lobby is so big and vast that it lacks warmth and personality. Check in is fast enough, but nothing exciting. No smile, just business. Everything in the hotel is overpriced, Wi-fi costs extra ($-.---day for - Mbps and $--.---day for - Mbps).

I reserved this hotel for three nights at a special rate, was not given the rate when I got there. The hotel actually lost track of us and considered us a NO SHOW! Due to this we did not get housekeeping service the first two days! I must say that the size of the room was nice and spacious. view was to be as expected for the city. Staff was very rude and they just got worse, we did manage to find one front desk clerk that attempted to help us but however that ended up not working out as well. Every time we left our room we ended up going back down to the front desk and have our room key reset, and it was not due to us storing it next to a credit card. Several members of the staff spoke broken english to the point of not understanding our questions and concerns. I would not ever recommend this to anyone. I thought I was getting a great deal but it would have been worth paying a bit more to stay at a neighboring hotel, because the location was excellent.

If you've stayed at other W Hotels, you know that they are trendy. This one is a bit more interesting because the structure (old Hotel Washington I think) is very traditional. But it works and it is a very cool place.
Pros: Stylish, comfortable and clean rooms. Decent bathroom with cool shower. Amazing views (Monuments, memorials, White House) from the penthouse level lounge. Outstanding staff that manage to be friendly and professional at the same time. The proximity to the Metro was pretty good (couple of blocks).
Cons: The room is small. If you are looking for space, you might need to think about a different hotel. 
The location is both a positive and negative. It's centrally located, but the area itself is not the best DC neighborhood for dining or just getting a snack. 
Overall, if the smaller room size doesn't bother you, it's a great place to stay in DC.

Where do we start. It was a business trip so my other half tagged along and I know a pool would be perquisite. When we arrived we were in awe of the hotel entrance and sheer history..
The atrium where you have breakfast lunch or dinner is breathtaking. A bit expensive but well worth it, especially the buffet breakfast.
Rooms were very roomy and beds would make anyone sleep like they never slept before. Hotel had every detailed covered.
Service was exceptional.
The pool was indoor and was a long lap pool. The hotel itself is more for adults than kids. If there were four kids in the hotel, we met them all in the pool at -:-- at night!
Highly recommend!
PS, parking is expensive... more than to rent a car daily, I think $-- a day
enjoyed the stay even though the room I got was not the room I booked but I blame the booking company

Checked in very early at --am after a long intercontinental flight. My room was not ready but the friendly and efficient young man at reception found me a room with no trouble and checked me in there and then. Parking was plentiful and free. Throughout my stay I found the recption staff helpful, friendly and always smiling..
The room was large but the decor was dull and the energy-saver lighting was hopelessly inadequate for a room that size. This gave an overall dingy feel to the place which it did not really deserve being only a couple of years old. Very comfortable bed and nice flat screen TV let down by the very few entertainment channels available. Fridge and microwave were low-tech but functional. The A-C unit was, incredibly, window mounted and very noisy. It worked well though. Wireless Internet was free with several APs to choose from and a strong signal throughout the hotel.
Bathroom was large and had plenty of towels and amenities. The shower pressure was little more than a trickle and the water temperature no more than lukewarm at the best of times. This made my overall stay quite uncomfortable. This is my first review on TripAdvisor. I've stayed in hotels that were extremely nice to hotels that were less than stellar. However, none have compelled me to post a comment until now.
Customer service goes a long way. Situations happen and great businesses will understand that to the extent that they are happy to accommodate customers. This hotel, on the other hand, was very much concerned with their policies and bottom line revenue. Unbeknownst to them, customer service and revenue goes hand-in-hand. I would have been flexible with any other day of this coming week up until Thursday if they had an empty room that wouldn't have been taken up. The reservation manager explained that they were fully booked for the night I was supposed to stay and that they turned down business because they expected me to check in. So although it was not by choice that I did not show up for the room, it was my fault that they lost business from others who could have booked the hotel room.
I next asked to speak to his boss who turned out to be the general manager of the hotel. Same thing, inflexible. He also suggested that I """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""should have called the hotel and let them know when I found out my flight was delayed"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I quickly answered by saying I did. Not believing me, he asked who I spoke to. Luckily, I had taken down the name of the person who I spoke to the day before. He then proceeded to ask more detailed questions before coming to the conclusion that I am out of luck and they stick to their policy. 
By this time, I was appalled by the inflexibility and asked for his boss' information to comment about their customer service. I let him know that I was no longer pursuing the option to try and get a room for a different night but wanted to speak to someone just to comment. He then let me know that he was the person to talk to. I pressed further and he continued to say that I could leave my comments with him and to call his corporate number. I have never experienced that before. I would be essentially placing a complaint with the same person I am complaining about. That is not ideal. 
So at the end of the day, the lesson I learned is to stick with larger chain hotels.

Hotel provided timely transportation from Lovefield airport, easy check-in and staff was very friendly. We had booked king rooms which were very clean. Tony from NY-NJ

We really enjoyed our stay. The staff were all very friendly and helpful. The room was reasonably large and spotlessly clean. In the heart of the Gaslamp, this was the perfect place to stay! We live in North County San Diego and had a wedding at the Hard Rock. I really enjoyed my stay at the Embassy Suites Philadelphia Airport. Rooms were clean and very spacious and the hot cooked to order breakfast was great in the morning. Otherwise, I enjoy the Embassy suites chain and would choose this hotel again.

Nice, comfortable hotel on a quiet side street. We'd stay here again with another priceline deal - just be aware of the parking - over $-- a night - so you need to find other garages and there aren't any open on Sundays so we parked on the street and then set our alarm to feed the meter. The flavored waters were a treat to fill up our water bottles while heading out to walk around town for the day. For the price, we'd stay there again, we just have to figure out where to better park or just take the train to DC.

The staff was friendly and helpful and they gave us a very early check-in which we appreciated.The room was spacious and clean. The bed was comfortable. Overall, it was a comfortable place to stay overnight.

I don't get to my favourite city San Francisco very often (about once every - years) but I always now make a point of staying at the King George Hotel. I've stayed at Library and Casablanca; they are luxury. I'd give this - stars.
Stayed at Affinia as I got a SUPER deal via Priceline. The price was right and the location is very good. -.- blocks to subway and equidistant to Grand Central and Penn Station.

I did not have a chance to use the hotel spa or fitness center, but they are available. Restaurant and bar are next door. I had meals elsewhere due to other plans.

This is an old hotel which has been remodeled. All of the staff were excellent, from the front desk to the bellmen. Room was not quite as small as European room, but roomy enough and very clean and updated. Bathroom was well lit and modern. The desk set us up with maps and locations which were within walking distance of the hotel. We were there for vacation-sightseeing and you could not beat this location. Orange Line of the subway system is a half block from the hotel's front door. Definitely a good pick. One problem was emergency vehicles could be heard at times during the night.

Cedarbrook Lodge takes you back to a time when businesses truly put EXCEPTIONAL CUSTOMER SERVICE first! Courtesy shuttle service from-to airport & link light rail. Front desk is very POLITE and offers a delicious cup of iced tea upon arrival. The hotel & all its amenities are VERY CLEAN! The grounds are BEAUTIFUL...Lush & Green! Perfect for weddings...which we were able to see - of. The beds are sooo COMFORTABLE! The rooms are quaint & intimate but spacious. If you desire more space opt for the Deluxe Double Queen. The bathrooms have HUGE tubs that are great for RELAXING and large vanities! The windows are large with SERENE VIEWS and separate blackout shades make a late sleep-in possible. The best surprise was the common lounge area on each floor that provides guests with FREE bottled water, a variety of sweets, fruit, chips, yogurt, & ice-cream. Lounge also has library. The food available through room service or in the dining area was very tasty. My friends raved about the bacon cheeseburger. BEST VALUE for the PRICE!!! We are a group of - (- couples) who take @ least one trip a year together & it was UNANIMOUS...we loved Cedarbrook Lodge and it is now our hotel of choice when we return to Seattle! Cedarbrook Lodge take a bow for a JOB WELL DONE!

we found this on the Wyndham Rewards website-- it was in the location we desired, and the price seemed fair. We were very pleased with how nice the property was-- the advertisement saying """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""newly refurbished rooms"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was not overstated. I recently came to this location with my family and had a WONDERFUL Experience! I have to give special recognition to Lucianna and the rest of the staff. The pool was excellent for my grandmother who has difficulty walking, they were able to use a lift to get her in and out of the pool. The pipes leaked above our room and left us with no water for - hours and flooded carpet. For our inconvenience of being awakened at -:-- a.m. to check out the leak and then being left with no water pressure for the shower, toilet or bathroom sink until afternoon, Then the carpet was left wet with no provision for drying. Our stay at the Bristol was wonderful. The room was comfortable and cheerful. The decor fabulous. The staff was helpful and friendly. The lobby is beautiful, though we tend not to spend time in lobbies. It's a good first impression. The only thing we did not like is the food at the restaurant. There are plenty of restaurants in San Diego, so the lack of a great restaurant in the hotel does not hold us back.

We had read the reviews before we went to Hotel Carter, so we were prepared for the worst. We brought our own towels and cleaning rags, earplugs, slippers, and we needed them, exept for the towels. The bed was indeed big, good and there were clean sheets. The staff was not rude, just """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""normal"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". What a great place to stay. Clean super quite and very well located.
Within walking distance to Times Square. Comfortable bed and good price. The only thing is the valet parking is very expensive.

Our stay at the Hyatt Regency San Antonio was great in every way: customer service, cleanliness, value, comfort, location, etc. Two travel tips: check out their website under """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Guest Services"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for great San Antonio travel info from Frommer's,

AND be sure to stop by the concierge desk in the lobby for dining recommendations along the Riverwalk. You could not aske for a more perfectly situated hotel on Fisherman's Wharf in San Francisco. We we able to walk to a concert at Fort Mason, walk over to the SF cable cars and Ghiridelli Square. Perfect! The Blue Mermaid Cafe was really good as well which is right at the hotel.

This is standard motel-type accommodation with parking below the hotel. There are lifts-elevators at various points and a number of vending machines. The rooms are really comfortable. There is some noise as it is on a busy road, and when people talk outside your room at night it can be a bit noisy, but of course this could happen with most motels. The location is very good - a few minutes' walk to all the Hollywood sights e.g. Walk of Fame, Sunset Boulevard. I would definitely stay here again.

Good location about - mins from the gaslamp and close to the harbour. The only problem with the location is the close proximity of the greyhound bus terminal, which can have some slightly sketchy looking characters hanging around.
The hotel itself is clean and modern, with a decent gym. All nicely decorated too. The only problem is that the rooms are really, really small. As a result, the bathroom layout is a bit odd - our sink was in the room just by the door and then toilet and shower in the bathroom.
Overall, a good hotel as long as you get a good deal.

We stayed at the Milburn for - nights with - of our children, ages - & -. We loved the location, it was on a quiet street, very close to the subway and Central Park. The lobby was very nice. The room was pretty clean, the blinds needed a good dusting and the oldness of the bathroom-kitchen made them seem a bit dingy.
Having a free breakfast in the hotel was great. The breakfast area is small, so you have to wait in line for a table. We didn't realize this the first day and arrived downstairs about -- minutes before we had to leave the hotel to catch our ferry. If you want to eat in the breakfast room, allow some extra time in the morning. (Although since all rooms have tables in the room- you can easily eat there without a wait.)
The employees were great. We asked the housekeeper for extra towels with our tip each morning, and she always left more than our request.
We asked the front desk people about parking, and one of them came outside with us to give us advice.

One tip- check the parking on the street outside the hotel. When we arrived, there was a space across the street from the hotel. We parked there to check in, and it turned out to be a legal space.
