Location was excellent - just - block from --th street free ride bus. Staff was good and helpful. Had to call maintenance as soon as I walked in the room. Nice stay except I was made to wait too long during checkout. The staff at the desk made me wait while I stood at the counter while she processed the checkout for someone who had dropped off their key and did not wait but wen to their car.

The restaurants provide excellent food and service, the rooms are very nice and wonderful service.

We (group of three) stayed in this hotel for a week in June and enjoyed it.

Having said that the area around this area of -th Avenue is definitely a bit """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""seedier"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", so I would tend to come in-go out via -th Avenue which is far more attractive.
Getting back to the hotel itself, the location is great as you will have gathered. The rooms are somewhat small if you have two beds in them. The beds , by the way, are Doubles - not Queens. The clientelle seemed to be split between families on vacation and business people staying for short breaks.
The breakfast room is on the ground floor opposite reception, and for a complimentary self-service breakfast, is very extensive:
 - tea-coffee-juices
 - toast-bagels-muffins

 - pastries-doughnuts-muffins

The breakfast area tends to get busy between -am and -am but is good before and after this time. You can pick up refreshments anytime during the day. A nice cool juice drink is just what you need after a walk from the sub-way.
There is an Internet room in the basement and a small gym beside it. I also found the terrace out the back which is quite sizeable and well-laid out with tables, chairs, and parasols, but no-one seems to use it while I was there. The hotel could do more to advertise this nice little extra.
Having been there for a week probably puts me in a good position to see the positives and negatives about this hotel, but I have to say in all honestly that there are little or no down-sides in staying here. All-in-all I would recommend this to a group of --- people willing to share a double room that require a central and safe location to explore the city.

The entrance area is very small and the valet service was severely understaffed for this meeting. Jesse the bellman was very helpful and friendly, and the young lady who worked the lounge during the afternoons was very customer service oriented. The rooms are spacious and well appointed and the cable service adaquate. My constant complaint of this and other hotels in it's high priced range is the requirement to pay daily for wi-fi in the room. Conference rooms were good and the waitstaff attentive. The outdoor pool is very small but the workour area is large and very well equipped.

Ok, so it's a Kimpton. If you travel on a regular basis and stay at Kimptons, you'll know what I'm talking about. It is pure and simple a great hotel. Kudos to Jean Luc and Robbie at the front desk for being so helpful. Stay here, it's so convenient to everything. Looking for local nightlife, try TheWit rooftop and Public House, both only blocks away.

I recommend Supermac on -th just south of --th: multiple varieties of macaroni and cheese.

Flat-screen TV with many stations, about --- of which didn't come in. FREE INTERNET! (Wired or wireless--I went with wired--but be sure all the ethernet cables are connected properly.) All in all, I would recommend this place to a single traveler especially--but probably not families due to the size of the rooms. Maybe a couple. I don't know what the two-bedded rooms were like.

My girlfriend and I had a very enjoyable stay at the Doubletree over Easter. Easy and friendly check in after having to wait for -- minutes at JFK customs (doh - """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""easter kind of took us by surprise with all these people travelling""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""....) 
Location is fine, and though the street the hotel is in is a little dowdy the area of town seemed perfectly safe. Some complain about the walk to Times Square? it's a short walk. And the subway is just two blocks south for travelling further afield (though cross town travelling on NY subway is pretty hopeless - why does everything run uptown-downtown?!! I'm probably not the first person to think that the subway could have been planned a lot better, but it's extremely cheap ($-- for a week) and clean.
The hotel is two blocks from Madison Square Gardens, and after we booked we found that Springsteen had decided to play MSG - shortest walk ever to a concert.
The hotel staff were very friendly - always a smile (hint to others - treat people with common courtesy - it works wonders). We got - breakfasts for free on check in when I claimed that my girlfriend (who is a Hilton) was Paris' long lost British cousin. Not that they believed me, but a nice touch.
Room was small I guess, but perfectly fine, and the bed was large and very comfortable. Maids were good, a little late in doing the room one day, but it was done. The aircon was effective but noisy so mid summer may prove noisy to sleep to. The lifts do have a bit of a wait sometimes, but not really a problem. Free and fast wifi, internet access and a printer in the lobby.

Recently stayed - nights at this hotel. What a perfect location to be at in New York City. Just south of Central Park and close to just about everything. Hotel was clean, rooms were clean, neat and beds were very comfortable. Maid service was excellant. Our rooms were ready when we arrived at approx. -:--am. Staff were very friendly and professional. Elevators to the floors were quick. Would definately stay there again and again.

This is a high-end JW Marriott steps from the White House. I stay here at least twice per year on business. The lobby area is very updated and alive with activity. The rooms are a always very clean and well-maintained. Bathrooms can be small but pretty typical for DC hotels. The beds are very comfortable. The convention staff always does an outstanding job, and the convention food is not bad.

I am a Platinum SPG member, so I stay at lots and lots of Westin Hotels around the world. I stayed on the --th floor in the tower building on an SPG floor. Room was well decorated with a view of Union Square, the Bay , and Coit Tower. Elevators worked swiftly and are on the outside of the building which is cool. Was in town for work and everyone else was there to play! Several staffers at the front desk was not familiar enough with which room numbers were which type of room. Two days of the missing the melted ice in the ice bucket and one day with the housekeeper rag swirl marks inside the drinking glasses ( MY BIGGEST HOT SPOT).
Everyone hotel has it ups and downs when taxed to the Max. I will stay again but you have to raise the level.

We are New Yorkers who no longer live in New York. So we know the City extremely well and love coming to this Ritz every Christmas season. Let everyone else stay uptown at the over-priced properties and deal with the frenetic crowds. We come down to the peace and quiet of Christmas season Wall Street, when employees are few and the lower part of Manhattan is as quiet as it gets. We still go uptown to see shows, have dinner, etc - but this hotel also gives you quick access to the ever-improving Tribeca, for example.
We think this hotel has great value if you pick the right dates. We love the people there (so disagree with the assessments of others) and love having breakfast and taking a walk along the beautifully restored water-front. They try to upgrade you and some of the rooms that face the Statue of Liberty are just lovely. We always try to stay in the corner suites - great rooms.
This hotel is a five star oasis away from the crowds but perfectly accessible to everything New York City. The views are better than any New York hotel - with the possible exception of those that overlook Central Park. Give it a try - we have now for eight years.

My girlfriend and I recently stayed at the Redbury for - nights during a trip to LA and we had a great time. We were in one of the Vine flats and had a nice view of Hollywood & Vine from our balcony. The room had pretty much anything you would need, and included a kitchen (sink, stove, small refrigerator, Keurig, tea kettle), washer-dryer, old record player, TV, and the usual hotel accessories. The bed was also SUPER comfortable. The hotel in general has a funky retro-vintage Hollywood design with a classy but slightly creepy vibe (in a cool way), which I thought was awesome. The staff and valet were friendly and professional. 
The only thing I would mention is that on weekend nights it can get a little loud as there is an outdoor patio and bar in the center area on the second floor. Personally the noise did not bother me, but if you need *complete* silence on Friday or Saturday nights, this is something to keep in mind. Week nights were quiet. The other thing to be aware of is the $-- per night indoor covered parking fee (valet only). However, in the Redbury's defense, I think this is common for hotels in the area so maybe it just comes with the territory. 
I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a unique place to stay in LA and will definitely be back next time I'm in the area!

Price was different from when I reserved the hotel to when I checked in. The manager was very rude about the mix up. So if you are on a budget I would beware that the price could change on you, or make sure you reserve the hotel through another booking site to ensure your price.

Visited the Hilton property down the street that our friends were staying at which was very fancy-nice with attractive pool scene but considering the mandatory parking and no breakfast provided- the Holiday Inn Express is a much better value if you are site seeing and not planning alot of time to hang out around the hotel.

One nit pick would be the sound proofing; I was expecting that more could have been done on the windows to shield some of the strest noise (a big problem at the Ace) but found that from my second floor room, the sound-proofing was fairly mediocre.
+ The bar (especially the library) is fantastic. I worry that it will become too popular! Maison Kitsune is a wonderful addition (and expensive pit stop!) to the retail scene in the area; it's a perfect match for the vibe of the hotel.
+ The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""needs work""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""

Will definitely be returning. The lovely bathtub alone makes me swoon. But let's work on the spotty areas and I'll be an even happier camper.

This is the -th time we have stayed over as many years and this hotel and we love it. This new hotel opened in the Fall of ----, and it's fantastic overall. First, the staff (both in the hotel and the casino) is the friendliest of any place that I've ever stayed. Everyone from the desk clerk to housekeeping to security to the casino staff seemed genuinely excited to be working and wanting to be sure that I wanted for nothing.
The hotel would remind you of a cross between a W Hotel and a Westin--very comfortable and spacious rooms and a hip atmosphere. Incredibly comfortable beds and crisp linens, with a pillow menu to boot! The bathrooms include both a huge soaking tub and separate shower and great toiletries and fantastic large towels. It was very quiet, and we had no difficulties sleeping. We forgot toothpaste, and it took only about - minutes for a housekeeper to bring a full kit with toothbrush and paste to our room.
On the downside, there are no restaurants open in the hotel yet. There are - informal cafes in the casino and - formal restaurant, along with a full ---hour room service menu--all very reasonably priced. Also, there's not anything to do right around the hotel, but you're only a mile from downtown, Joe Louis Arena, Ford Field, and Comerica Park (not that you'd want to walk around Detroit at all).

My son and I just spent three days here. I could not have asked for more. Each level of service- from engineering (a light bulb went out), to front desk (we needed a favor), to valet (car service), to the concierge floor staff (Beri was outstanding), to housekeeping (I had a teenage son w me) to the wake up service, to the room service, to any other group I have neglected-was just perfect! It all worked so smoothly and with such a wonderful attitude, that it makes you wonder how other hotels almost never hit this mark!
I had just stayed in the Mandarin Oriental in DC for two nights the same week and the experience was like night and day.
Great job to the management and staff!! This is how it is supposed to work!

Not your traditional hotel. Hotel is on floors -- to -- of the Chicago-Sun Times building. Do a Google Images search on """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Chicago Sun Time Building"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Find the picture that says """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Chicago Sun Times"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on the side and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Holiday Inn"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on the rooftop. The hotel lobby is on floor --. You can see the larger windows on the -- floor. To get to the Chicago CTA, you have to walk thru the shopping mall part of the Merchandise Mart. The Merchandise Mart mall also has some fast food places, but some are closed on weekends. Furnishings showed some signs of age but they were clean and adequate. City views (if you get a city view room) are spectacular. Good pool, reliable internet connection, good exercise room. I'd stay there again.

We stayed at the James for - nights leading up to Labour Day weekend, and we loved it. The staff were friendly, the room was comfortable and large enough, and the facilities were kept spotlessly clean. As we were touring around Chicago the whole week we didn't hang out a whole lot in the room, but we slept well and the noise was minimal at night. We were offered umbrellas for our wet trip down to the White Sox game (came in very handy as it rained a lot that day) and we used the free computer in the lobby to check on things to do and check in to our flight for the way home. It was nice to have a Trader Joe's across the street for stocking up on a few snacks to have in the room too.
One downside - the free wi-fi is pretty terrible - signal strength is weak in many parts of the hotel.
To end on a VERY positive note, we ate at the James Burke Primehouse (in the hotel) because we didn't want to venture out into the rain to find another restaurant (we had wanted to try and wait for a table at Girl and the Goat). I'm so glad it was raining that day. The food, service and atmosphere were incredible. Our waiter was also a wonderful sommelier who made great recos, and we chatted throughout our meal about travelling, wine and great food. What a delight! We had heard that if you ask they'll show you the beef aging room (just wow) and they accommodated us. Do yourself a favour and try the Wagyu beef sashimi served on a Himalayan rock salt slab. Delicious!

Stayed over a weekend when the Horse Races were going on at Del Mar(Where the Turf meets the Surf) Horse Track. The Hotel is situated in a Canyon on a Golf Course a few miles from the Beach. The Hotel is beautiful and the employees are so friendly and the place has such a relaxing private atmosphere. Definitely one of the best and deserving of its top -- mention!

It's all been said before...!
Great location, especially for tourists like us. Everything in easy reach. 
Friendly,attentive staff and always cheerful.
Lovely façade and interior. The real flames were a welcome comfort on a cold winter day - a real treat to return to and just bask!! 
Great buzz in the evening, obviously a popular rendezvous for New Yorkers.
Could not fault our stay in any way.

This is worse that some seedy back woods motel! It was horrible! The first room we were given had ceiling tiles missing, stains on the floor and walls, broken lampshades, no toilet paper, no remote, one towel, and one pillow.....on a king sized bed,. When we asked for assistance the front desk was too busy to help. We had to walk back to the front desk to complain and get another room, which wasn't much better. If we weren't so tired we would have gone to a different hotel. Some friends of ours were also staying in the same hotel in a different room that also had no toilet paper or towels, missing ceiling tiles, and a piece of pipe was missing from under the sink so when the water was turned on it went all over the floor! The front desk was also too busy to help them and when they tried to get another room they were told nothing else was available! We also noticed several rooms with broken windows and all of the external doors were missing locks and it looked like someone had taken a crowbar to pry them open. On top of that, a week later they charged me twice! It was bad enough that I had to pay once for this dump but twice? Unacceptable! So, I repeat DO NOT STAY HERE!!!

We stayed here for two nights on a weekend and got a reasonable rate. The room we got overlooks Union Square and is lovely. The rooms have been recently renovated and have the sleek, modern, new """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Hyatt look"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The lobby is pretty much sealed off due to ongoing renovations, except for asmall area for check-in. I am sure it will be beautiful when its done. Staff very friendly and helpful and gave us complimentary late checkout. Large bathroom. The beds are comfortable and room was very quiet. Had great night of sleep! Walk to Union square, Westfield Mall, theaters and lots of restaurants in the area. Cable car stop also very closeby. There is a parking garage (valet) across the street on Sutter that offers a hotel parking special, and you are charged thru the hotel. Even though it is not the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""official"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" parking garage for Hyatt, It can't be any closer to the hotel and it probably costs a lot less.

I recently stayed at The Legacy for a business conference that was being held at a nearby resort, The Arizona Grand. I spent - or - days going back and forth between the two resorts. Of the two, The Legacy was far superior, in my humble opinion. But it didn't start out so well. To make a long story short, my only complaint during the week was with the front desk staff. Otherwise, the entire experience got better and better, from the immaculate grounds and facilities, to the pro shop, to the restaurant (several outstanding meals, including a $-- meal that tasted like a $-- meal), to the room, to the golf course, to the atmosphere, it was a very nice experience. I would rate it - to -.- stars.

My boyfriend and I stayed and Palomar San Francisco last summer.
Overall it is a nice hotel. Our room had a lovely street view. The layout of the room was great, lounge and the restaurant very enjoyable. Unfortunately, I had to bring down my overall rating of our stay due to the “screaming” incident.
One night we decided to tuck in early and were peacefully asleep before I was woken up by a sound of someone trying to open the room door with a key. Assuming it is a confused guest who would try a couple of times and be on his way, I quietly waited for him to go away. Then to my surprise door opens and a guy with a trolley luggage enters the room.
As I was still half asleep, and as this chain of events was rather unexpected, I decided (probably not the most rational decision, I agree) that the best reaction is to start screaming. So I did. My boyfriend wakes up (of my screaming I am sure) and in sudden awakening shock started screaming as well. I heard his screams and feeling that screaming is now fully justified started screaming louder. At this point our midnight intruder, that just entered a dark hotel room that I am sure he assumed empty, and was greeted by screaming started screaming back. After few minutes of all three of us screaming, he apologized and left the room.
We laughed it off, and were ready to fall back asleep, when someone knocked on the door. It was a security manager, who told us that front desk checked someone else into our room by mistake.
Next morning we went to get some coffee from the lounge and upon return we discovered that our keys no longer open the room door. I went to the front desk and asked to fix the keys. Front desk lady reactivated the keys and commented: “Next time keep your keys away from the credit cards so they don’t deactivate”. “Solid advice” I said “However, this particular time, I believe the key problem is caused by Front desk checking in another guest into our room by mistake in the middle of the night last night”. “Weird” was the response.
“Weird” indeed. I kind of expected and apology…. But oh well….
I generally like Kimpton, because of the boutique feel and nice amenities, but since the incident I tried to stay away. I guess “Weird” was not a reaction from the hotel staff I was expecting in this situation.

Enjoyed a weekend stay, Nice large room - non smoking - King.
I always enjoy the large bed due to my large frame.
There were sufficent electrical outlets available for my electronics.
The desk provided an attractive and functional work space.
This place is huge! 
Large open yet covered areas with unique artwork to enjoy reguardless of weather.
The hotel provided the meals for the event, all meals were enjoyed.
Location is close to the downtown area.

I booked Pod-- after a great stay in July just after they opened. After the storm, I realized that they were in an area of no power and this was confirmed by Thierry Facebook page. They had power for the common areas, and one lift, and they had wifi. I decided to go ahead and stay anyway. The reception staff were once again really helpful even though they were freezing cold. The Queen pod was again functional, clean and comfortable. Of course the rooms are small, that is part of the hotel design and function. The room had no power for the first night but was ok. The power came on early in the morning and the remainder of the stay was great. This hotel is in a great location and the service is fantastic, the staff are great. My only one criticism is that the bar is overpriced. I was charged $- for a can of beer, no glass and I can't recommend the bar because of that. The rooftop terrace was closed because of the storm and the fact that it is winter but it is a great location and I will return in the summer to try it

Booked the motel direct by calling from the UK and got the same deal as found online. The location was superb for a first time visitor to San Fran, the check-in staff friendly and the room luxurious - comfortable bed, large TV, large bathroom etc. Transport links were good as well (near to bike hire, trams etc). We had a room at the front (on the road) so it was quite noisy so I would recommend trying to get a room at the back. I would highly recommend this place as somewhere comfortable to stay in San Fran.

This hotel wants to be the best in Dallas, and it just might be - compared with elsewhere, they have a lot to learn.
On the whole, it's a great property, but the employees are still too wet behind the ears to get it right. Here are some notes from my stay.
-) hotel staff said Internet was free, it was charged to my room at $--
-) the picture ledge above my bed had enough dust that I could write my name on it.
-) the concierge was too interested in checking the gridr account on his phone to provide proper assistance. The second time I visited the concierge, one ignored me while the other appeared to want to leave more than anything.
-) morning room service forgot to bring the bill with him - he had to go back and get it which kept me from getting back into bed (that was just sad)
-) the on-property restaurants need work in service (I'll review those separately)
Given time and good management, the omni could be great - just don't have the highest of expectations when you go.
Nice small rooms, clean shared baths which were well available. Very excellent deal for New York!

Just returned from - night stay at the hotel, was really fantastic, the staff were more than accommodating and made the stay so memorable.
You cant get away from New York street noise but have a full and busy day and exhaustion takes over and the bed was superbly comfortable, there are ear plugs if you want them and the room was extreamly pleasant.
Definatly worth the money.

Your pretty standard midtown boutique hotel, there's nothing exceptionally unique about the place, but it is clean and the staff is very nice...which sort of does put you ahead of the pack in this market.
I stayed here on business last weekend and last minute found out a friend from Long Island was going to come in to visit. I asked for a two-bed room when I arrived to drop my bag. They were out, but lo and behold when I returned to check in I had been upgraded to a studio suite. Still just one bed, but plenty of room to sort of build a bed on the floor. Not sure if that was on purpose or just luck, but I appreciated it either way.
We also received free breakfast in the morning for booking with a visa and the restaurant in the building was pretty good and had very fast service.
Only downside is that as far as NYC goes, it's in a pretty boring part of town (though boring and NYC really don't belong in a sentence together). Convenient for business travel, though.
The rate was competitive without being outstanding, but given the room upgrade, I can't complain.

As you would expect from Starwood Hotels, this is a fine hotel. It has a very friendly and helpfull staff and the location is perfect for business as well as pleasure. 
Soho and Chinatown are a short walk away and the subway lines A,C & E stop right around the corner to bring you to the rest of Manhattan. 
The only downside is that this part of Canal street is crawling with street vendors selling counterfeit Gucci and Prada.
The rooms are luxureous; Good bed, large TV.
We had no breakfast in the hotel because it appeared better and cheaper outside and it was very crowded in the morning. 
There is a little bar in the lobby where you get Starbucks coffee and a snack.
But...: Internet is only free in the lobby (-- minutes a day), on your room it's $---day. This should be free of charge.
The rooms are reasonable quiet, but in this class of hotels you would expect better soundproofing - especially the doors. You can hear the doors slamming in the hallway all night and morning.
And: All this does not come cheap, we paid around $----night. With that in mind, the value is average.

It would be middling anywhere else, but it was quite a deal for New York. We go up to New York a lot, and frequently use Hotwire. For this trip, hotel prices seemed very high, so we decided on this place when we found it on Orbitz for under $---. 
It is definitely a three star hotel. The room was quite alright. The lobby area was a little less than ideal; the carpet in the breakfast area was pretty dirty, but other than that it was quite ornate. The location (just a few blocks from the Empire State Building) is ideal for our needs - we could walk everywhere. It's in a small Koreatown - we found a good Korean cafeteria.

Check in is fast. Elevator only accessible with a room key. The room is large, free internet, HBO, hair dryers, shampoo, conditioner and lotion. Clean and comfortable. Get for $-- through priceline. Room was very quiet. Located right off of FM ----.

Perfect spot to visit New Yorkfrom Not far from Times Square and siteseeing .Clean Quiet .Lovely Near restaurants Ideal location to visit NYC Will definitely use again in the heart of theatre district in Manhattan
This was my first stay at an Aloft and I must say it's fantastic! HOWEVER, I found the toilet to be dirty with urine and that's a big no no! Everything else including the staff was excellent.

My - year old's main passion in life is dinosaurs so my wife and I promised we would take him to the Natural History Museum in NYC. He almost turned inside out with excitement when he saw their collection and his mother and I were almost as pleased with the Beacon. It is a perfect home away from home for familties.
PROS:
 - Easy walk from Central Park and the Museum, even for a - year old, plus a very nice public playground along the way. Safe, tree-lined streets. 
 - $--- a night for a suite with a small kitchen. You can put the little one to bed, close the door, and the adults can have a drink or snack, or watch TV without disturbing him.
 - Fairway Market across the street. You can buy anything there ( I think they are open -- hr). You can save major money and avoid the hassle of eating in a restaurant with a toddler and prepare all you need in your own kitchen.
 - I went out to buy a bottle of wine and strolled around the neighborhood a little. As other reviewers have said you do feel like a local. There are newsstands, curbside book vendors (at least on Sunday), and many small shops, bars and restaurants. Many trees, too.
 - The hotel lobby is clean and inviting, the staff was polite and efficient, we requested wineglasses be brought to the room and they arrived quickly. 
CONS:
 - None to speak of, really. Some might find the decor and architecture a bit dated but it is an old building and I found it reminiscent of the classy old days of NYC. Everything was very clean and no bugs, bed or otherwise.
 - My son had one disapointment, though. We went to the museum first and when we were walking into the hotel later he asked in a loud voice """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""DO THEY HAVE DINOSAURS IN HERE TOO?"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" He now thinks all big buildings in NYC should have dinosaur skeletons in them. The Beacon does not have any dinosaurs but does have everything else you need to relax and explore NYC. Will return.

The hotel has been remodeled very nicely, the location is excellent, and the interior is as swank and stylish as you'd expect from an Italian auto manufacturer. While the hotel is quite old, none of its original charm was retained. Unfortunately local historical preservation requirements demanded that they retain San Diego's oldest operating elevator (seriously). We've stayed in lots of boutique hotels, and actually prefer older preserved-remodeled ones, but we have never had an experience like this. The steam-driven elevator mechanism positively roars and shudders the rooms, making sleep impossible. The hotel's solution -- complimentary earplugs and a white noise machine -- work well enough, but for these prices and the boutique hotel experience Keating aspires to, it's quite a disappointment. Add to that the malfunctioning toilet in our room that went unrepaired, despite our numerous requests, for our entire - day stay, plus a massive screw-up of our reservation by the otherwise charming and eager staff, and we can't possibly recommend this place. (I should note that as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""amends"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for our experience we were given a coupon for two slices of pizza somewhere, and the manager removed the historical preservation tax from our room charge.) To sum up, the hotel is superficially glitzy and swanky and fashionable, and the staff tries hard to please, but the guest experience leaves a lot to be desired. There are many lovely options in San Diego; go elsewhere.

The Website for the Ft. Worth Sheraton is misleading...This property used to be an older Hilton....with some renovations. The locks on the doors are questionable. There were mud-dirt stains on the carpet in our room. The bathtub needed repair..two rust spots showing through the pocelain in the middle of the tub. The swimming pool area was very large but the water was very COLD. I can't wait for the new OMNI hotel and convention center to open across the street.

We stayed for - nights and can only agree with other reviewers that this is an excellent example of how a hotel should be.
The area does not have many good restaurants but it is easy to get around so this was not a great problem.
Highly recommend this hotel for couples, short weekend getaways, close to all, and a great restaurant right downstairs. Staff was wonderful, helpful, and knowledgeable.

Scheduled a day in Seattle before our cruise with our flight arriving at -:-- in the morning. The Doubletree airport shuttle picked us up and took us to the hotel. We weren't sure how our luggage would work out since check in time was - pm. The bell man took our luggage and our traveling companions and stored it until we finished sight seeing which was about - pm that night. We caught the MT--- which took us to Pioneer Square for $-.-- and same back to the hotel (an added convenience which is right in front of the hotel). The concierre arranged a van to take us to the Cruise Terminal cheaper than all of our exhaustive research turned up. We didn't want to pay the $- for Wi-Fi for one night but they informed us that could pick it up for free in the lobby area which worked out nice. We checked emails while waiting for the rest of our party.

I got a pretty good deal on at the Dylan through ----hotels. After booking, I read some bad reviews on www.tripadvisor.com and tried to switch hotels. I glad I did not, I was pleased with the quality of the rooms and the hotel staff was very kind and accompanying. I through the rooms sizes were generous compared to other boutique hotels in the area. Upgraded to a king for the price of my queen rate. Free internet too. The location is great for Midtown. I would definitely stay at the Dylan Hotel again!

Great choice if you are attending a Padres game and looking for a clean, comfortable hotel. Yes, it's got a bit of the austere corporate convention center hotel feel to it but meets most of the checklist if you need something reliable and well located with good value. Only potential negative from a sleep quality perspective was the thumping electronica well past midnight at the rooftop bar a block north. Sounded like a great party but beware if you are a light sleeper and get a room facing north.

Stayed at the Bahia for a brief getaway, three nights. The room was very large and had kitchen facilities. The view was wonderful, Bay all around, and the location excellent. 
Unfortunately, there was something wrong with the pullout bed in the sofa and we had to stack couch and chair pillows underneath it to hold it up. When I picked up the chair pillow, I got old candy that was stuck between the pillow and the chair on my hands. Response from housekeeping was SLOW.
Based on what we paid for the room, this experience was surprising.
Otherwise, that aside, it is a beautiful location and the landscaping is excellent.

I booked a room online for this hotel after reading many online reviews of it. The hotel web site said that only singles were available with shared baths, but because I had a -am flight out of JFK, I thought I would be fine for that brief time. When I checked in, they gave me a room with a private bath for the same price, which was nice. The room safe is great, especially for a budget hotel. Since I was travelling with a laptop, the safe was important for me since I didn't want to lug it around with me. The room was very clean, including the bathroom. It was very small, but I imagine most people aren't hanging out in their hotels in NYC much until they want to sleep.
Ah, sleep...what I didn't get when I stayed at Herald Square. I didn't plan on getting much because of my early flight, but I didn't get any at all, thanks to a guest in a nearby room who was apparently using his room for some ...this review has to be family friendly, so let's call it audible alternative adult entertainment. Very unpleasant for me. I knew I wouldn't get much sleep, but I did want to get some shuteye and wasn't able to.
Without the noise from the neighbors, this hotel would've been great. However, I'm hesitant to wholeheartedly recommend it because I'm not sure if the hotel, being so affordable, is more susceptible to being used for such rendezvous. If you must stay in this price range, it's probably great since it was so clean. But I don't wish my experience on anyone.

Okay, so this a big and bland hotel, and once inside, you could be anywhere. The hotel may be generic, yet it is still on the Riverwalk, albeit a quiet section of it. It is a pleasant stroll to everywhere. Best of all, they gave us a great rate, which included a fantastic breakfast. Staff very friendly and helpful. Parking expensive, but this seems to be common to most hotels in this amazingly beautiful city.

Hotel claims to be non smoking property. When we entered our room we were assaulted with a wall of smoke stench. We were told it was the last room available. The -nd night was considerably better after the windows were left open all day, but the old embedded ashtray smell was still there. The first night was nearly intolerable, the second night merely disgusting and annoying. If you are at all sensitive to cigarettes don't stay here. Be warned!
Also, the double bed (why do hotels claim to have queens, but are really doubles?) was very broken down and saggy in the middle. It made us roll toward each other. Bad for any couple that needs their space.

Seriously, just stay away. This is kind of in a bad area, but that is nothing compared to the rooms and the staff. The front desk staff is so rude and obnoxious. The room we stayed in smelled like cat pee and throw up! Don't even think of complaining, the staff doesn't care and will tell you to go somewhere else if you don't like it. Several complaints and letters to the owner went unanswered. I filed with the Better Business Bureau, but the owners failed to reply to that s well.

My friend and I originally picked this hotel for its great location and the fact that it was a four star hotel. We were impressed at first, despite the construction (I don't go to Chicago to stare at the lobby wall!). But it soon turned into a nightmare when we went out for the evening, and came home to discover that our room had been broken into. Nothing in the room was upset and it was not forced entry, but the thief had carefully selected items from my purse, notably several electronics and cash, including my cell phone which was charging on the table (took the charger too!). My friend had her e-reader stolen. None of these items, aside from the cell phone, were visible. This makes us believe that it was an inside job.
When I went to the lobby downstairs, the young man behind the counter told us that there had been break-ins in the area, including the Four Seasons Hotel across the street and that the employees had received an email to warn them. Um...perhaps a heads up to your patrons might be a good idea, including reminders to check their doors and to use the safes in the room. Anyway, he asked me to write down what was stolen and said something about a police report, but I wasn't clear as to whether I made the call, or the hotel did, nor was a phone number to the Chicago police provided. I don't blame this young man, but management, please train your staff on how to deal with a situation such as this.
The next morning, we went down again to speak to security. It was then that we were told to call the police ourselves and a number was at that time presented, then the security guy came to investigate, asked us questions etc. He then said a report would be prepared. They were insistent on having the police report number and we provided that. After that, they seemed to forget about us. The next morning, we talked to security again and asked about the results of their investigation. We were told that it was an internal matter and that they couldn't discuss the results with us, and that head office would be contacting (it's been over a week and we are still waiting!). We finally asked to speak to the general manager. In this consultation, we were told that the only times that the room had been accessed were the times that we entered the room and that were we sure that we had locked our door? The door was sticky and hard to close, but I watched my friend pull hard on the door several times and she knew that the door was locked each time. (Miraculously, the stickiness on the door disappeared after the break in).
Also, our room safe did not work. We were originally going to put some of our things in the safe, but we couldn't get the safe to work. When we brought this up to the hotel manager, he put it back on us and asked if we had called the front desk for help?
The general manager offered to extend our stay on the house (why would we want to stay?), and then on our request, gave us a free night off of our current stay, which was OK, but not nearly enough, considering the amount of goods and cash taken (close to ---- dollars worth!). We didn't even get the two hundred and fifty dollar compensation according to the Innkeeper's Act, which the manager kindly pointed out to us on the back of our door. Another note is that the general manager had only been there for -- days and the room division manager had only been there a month. 
I get that unfortunate things happen when travelling, but I would have appreciated more openness and transparency. At the end of the day, we were violated and we felt that we had to push in order to get any information or compensation, paltry though it was. We will definitely not be staying there again....way too unsafe....will never know whether it was an inside job, or just a poor lack of security in the building.

I saw a living social deal for the Adolphus and thought it would be great for anniversary trip to Dallas. I didn't know much about the place before going, but saw that is was historic and knew that the boyfriend would love that aspect. The rooms were wonderfully spacious and everything was beautiful and in pristine condition. We had a lovely night stay and would love to go back and spend more time enjoying this hotel. Also, the bed provided a very relaxing night's sleep.

We had an opportunity to stay at this location for four nights while in Dallas for a recent SMU graduation. We found this location to be quite lovely, while still obviously in the process of renovation. In fact, new wallpaper was being installed on our hall while we were there. The complimentary breakfast was very nice, with many hot and cold choices. Our experiences with the staff were good on the three occasions we needed their help. Though costing $---day, the parking is gated, and the entries from the parking lot are all secure. We enjoyed the small shopping with grocery store nearby. With our kitchen, we were able to prepare small meals in our room. There are two things that need improvement to our way of thinking. Number one, the shower head flows so freely that the water stands in the tub above one's ankles. Number two, there wasn't a dresser in our bedroom with the only clothes storage being a small wardrobe in the closet. There was only one suitcase stand, so we asked for an extra one, which helped.

I stayed at the Congress last weekend and I realized their website is very misleading. The pictures on their site show, and are described as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""spacious rooms"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". This was NOT the case. The rooms were very old and cramped. Paint was peeling off the walls and doors. The bathroom door did not lock and had to be forced closed. The door was missing a hinge and had a large chunk of wood gouged out as well. The beds are not on boxsprings, only wooden crossboards in the bed frame. So, if you are looking for a good nights sleep, you might want to go elsewhere. The bathroom was awful! The shower curtain is actually held up by dollar store plastic rings on a lousy tension rod that would not stay up when the room was steamy from the shower. There is no fan in the bathroom either. Plus the air conditioning unit caused too much condensation and there was a puddle of water on top of it every morning when we woke up. Room Service was bad as well. We ordered four breakfast meals (one waffle, one french toast and two eggs with bacon meals), and after -- minutes only two were delivered. The woman who delivered the food insisted she would bring us the our missing meals asap. -- minutes later she returns with two more meals which weren't what we ordered. After speaking with someone in room service, they assured us they would adjust our $--.-- bill!! Needless to say, they didn't adjust the bill. This is the flagship Sheraton in downtown Chicago with great views over the Chicago river or the city (depending on both dimensions of your elevation). Stayed just overnight at the Radisson near LAX. The room was adequate-very standard features-and I frankly expected worse after reading other reviews. The hotel is simply worn and the places that are dirty looking (around the faucets, carpet pulling away from walls slightly) are I think because of age, not lack of attention. I stayed at this Embassy for a business trip (that I turned into a fun trip later). The rooms are spacious however, it's not the cleanest hotel I've stayed at. There is construction going on but I didn't hear any noise. The -.-- manager's reception was nice and a great way to catch up on action items from the day. The best part about this hotel was that is was in walking distance to my favorite restaurant in Chicago (Volare).

I'll post that review as well.

We stayed at this hotel for - nights in March and did enjoy our stay very much. 
The room (we booked a standard room) was fabulous - very spacious and luxurious. Everything is extremely comfortable and well designed and we could not fault the room at all. 
The main issue we had was with food service at the hotel. We got the impression that the restaurant was separately run and therefore it was not very flexible. For example, when we ate breakfast in the restaurant and tried to adjust some of the dishes slightly (bacon instead of sausage for example), staff said they had to check with the kitchen. We were also slightly disappointed with the location in that it is quite a long way from the main sights. It is a lovely area but a bit further out than we expected - probably our own fault for not having researched the location thoroughly enough - although we were surprised that the other reviews on this site didn't seem to mention this. 
Subject to these points we would recommend the Surrey, but if we were to return to New York ourselves we would probably look for somewhere a bit more central.

Location was perfect; turn right and you move into the middle of the tourist areas and bars-restaurants; turn left and you can walk on the beach around the harbour and up into Fort Mason park. Jet lag forced us out of bed early and walking in the morning sun round the harbour, watching the swimmers!, was just what we needed. Also right next to the cable car turn around for easy access to downtown. All in all, a top hotel, in a great location.
we could walk to the Broadway show and great restaurants. very nice staff & so very helpful. we were able to keep our car parked there most of the day we checked out. very convenient.

My fiancee and I stayed at the SOHO grand from ---- of March ---- and really enjoyed our stay. We read the mixed reviews on this site prior to booking, but made the decision to stay there anyway - and we were not disappointed. It's one of those hotels you either love or hate: with a real industrial chic feel - it's not for eveyone. Our room (a superior queen) was nice with fab toiletries, and we had no problems with the hotel staff, who were all pretty friendly. (If you want staff who are tripping over themselves to help you, then maybe you should try the Waldorf!). 
This place is for the young and young at heart and the conservative traditional type who their want every whim tended to. It's full of trendy people (albeit sometimes a little pretentious and noisy), but we had a blast. You can even have a fish for company during your stay. And we saw Ben Stiller (he's tiny!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""")
We spent very little time there and so for that reason only (and maybe the fact that I'd have liked black out blinds in the room), should we have considered staying somewhere cheaper. Soho itself is great - downtown Manhattan at its best, with endless boutiques, coffee bars, delis, restaurants etc to choose from. You need at least a week to get through them all! It's also spitting distance from other hip neighbourhoods like Tribeca, and Greenwich Village. Thumbs up for the SOHO grand. Would definitely return again and again!

The Fairmont is a grand old dame of a hotel. It’s all about grandeur and old-style opulence, which is fun if you’re up for it. They’ve got an impressive lobby, gracious service and manage to strike a healthy balance between warmth and ostentation. And the hotel keeps track of what room you were in on your last visit in case it might be available again, which is a nice plus.
We stayed here once before and had a lovely room with a panoramic view of the city. This time, though, it seemed that we caught the place on an off-night. 
Our room was alright, nothing remarkable given the price, but another dazzling view of the city compensated for that. The room seemed clean enough, but in the morning my wife found - pubic hairs on the bottom of their rather grand tub, which discouraged her from taking a bath. But I was eager for a long hot shower, so I jumped into theirs. No hot water. My cold shower was a quick one.
No doubt these things could have happened anywhere. On our last visit, our room was immaculate. And the Fairmont is, without a doubt, a lovely hotel. Next time, though, I think I’ll stick to the shower and hope they have hot water.

We spent - nights at the Affinia --. Great hotel in a great location. Rooms were very spacious and very clean. Would definitely stay there again.

Upon the recommendation of a client two years ago, I stayed at the Homewood Suites. Four business trips later, I continue to stay here whenever I travel to Indianapolis. Obviously the location is convenient if you have business on the north or northeast side of Indianapolis. The staff have always been friendly and polite. The rooms are spacious and clean; the breakfast is delicious; and things such as water pressure, temperature, and climate control have not been a problem. The location is convenient to the restaurants and bars of the Broad Ripple area. For joggers, the Monon Trail is a short drive away. Malls and stores abound. The only inconvenience is trying to make a left turn out of the hotel's parking lot onto --th Street during the morning rush hour. Have patience. Overall, this hotel offers all types of travelers a pleasant stay on the northside of Indy.

We stayed here for the convenience before our flight. Room was very small but ok. Exterior and pool really needs some work. Car was there on time to transport us to the airport. Don't think we'd stay again.

In the heart of Japantown with Japanese restaurants and shopping nearby. My room was very comfortable with king bed, easy chair with ottoman, desk, small fridge, safe, two phones (one cordless), flat screen TV, DVD player, iron and board and clock radio. The decor was very pleasant with Japanese touches and there was a great view of the Los Angeles skyline when standing at the window. The room was clean and the furnishings were very nice. The bathroom was small, but well appointed. It even had a combo toilet and bidet with heated seat and water. There were plenty of luxurious towels. The lobby has a marble floor and the feel of a Japanese hotel. There is a small gift shop and cafe and a Japanese-style restaurant with a buffet breakfast. Access from Los Angeles Union Station (Amtrak and Metrolink) is fast and easy (take the Gold Line Metro to the first stop: Japan Town Arts District and then walk one and one half block).

The Amalfi is located just a few blocks off Michigan Ave, across the street from the famous Harry Caray's Italian Steakhouse right in the middle of many great steakhouses. I was greeted warmly at reception and quickly checked-in. The receptionist informed me that there was a complimentary open-bar with """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""light finger food"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" each afternoon starting at -:--. There was even an umbrella in the room for me to use during my stay. I was greeted by name each time I returned to the hotel.

This hotel had a lot of charm. The rooms were a little small, but had a lot of character. The staff was amazing, and could not have been anymore helpful! The staff gave great advice on restaurants and great tips for getting around. The hotel is in a great location, there is so much to see, we walked all over the place. Loved this hotel, wish we could have stayed a little longer in San Fran!

The rudely clerk responded it was posted on the Hyatt website; I then told her I had booked through Expedia, and she said it was posted on their site also. It was not. My husband and I recently had to attend to a family emergency in San Diego, very unanticipated, so we chose the Travelodge just by chance but we are so glad we did. It was a very trying two weeks and it was so wonderful to get a dose of warmth and family friendliness every day from everyone from front desk people to housekeeping and laundry staff. We had breakfast every morning at Adam's Steak and Egg, the hotel restaurant, and without exception each morning all the staff were so friendly. There were some mornings when we felt terrible, but we got such a boost from Leoni and Hector and Alleandro and all the staff who were so kind and happy. We fed off that positive attitude and it really helped get us through the day. The family emergency all turned out okay, and we will never forget all the people at the Travelodge who made it a little easier for us. When we come back to San Diego, we will stay there again. Besides, the hot tub is great!

This is a great hotel for those looking to stay somewhere in the Union Square area. The hotel was clean, the staff friendly, and everything has been recently renovated. Before our arrival I had emailed the hotel with a few questions. The General Manager responded promptly and was so helpful and polite.
There is no air conditioning, but with the temperate weather it wasn't really a problem and the room had a ceiling fan and a portable fan in the closet that we used. Everything was very clean. We stopped by the continental breakfast once and there was bagels, fruit, toast, muffins, juice and coffee. 
We would definitely stay at this hotel again and I would reccomend it to friends. The hotel is right near Union Square, so I thought we would hear a lot of noise, but our room (which was on the -th floor) was very quiet.

After spending an evening in the room and finding trash on the floors, I felt like I was being bitten by something and had marks on my arms. I was concerned with possible bugs and spoke to management who stated they don't have bugs and I was having an allergic reaction to their cleaning supplies. I went back to my room and upon closer inspection, found it was infested by spiders (photos taken)! I showed management the problem and was moved to another room. Booked the Metro because of all the good reviews we have read over the last few years. Stayed --th March for - nights. This hotel is very nice. From the moment you walk in, it is very appealing. Very bright, fun, looks modern. 
Very nice bar in the lobby has great charm and trendy vibe to it. The prices are expensive, $- per beer.... But it is a very nice setting. Outside there is a nice looking pond, nice pool area(no indoor pool). There is a large convention center at this hotel as well. Bellman services too. 
The rooms were pretty nice. Modern bathroom, nicely decorated, nice toiletries provided too... Comfy bed, nice views, nice desk area for working.... Channel selection is good as well. 
Restaurant served a buffet breakfast that was good. Lots to choose from and taste was good, not great. Little pricey, but good. 
This hotel would be - star with a little updating. It is a huge high rise, but the elevators are scary. They have -- year old carpet in them and creak and pop as you are in them. Nice hotel, and with a few upgrades could be very nice. I never had any service problems. Great location, easy to get places in the city. Lots of places around to shop and eat...

If you need large rooms, don't stay here! But I have to say - it was perfectly located, and charming for us. We were there for a trade show and it was removed enough and yet still close enough. The service was wonderful - everyone there was so nice. Food was great! I would stay there again - being across from the park was wonderful and I hope to take the children there soon! No complaints: Loved the room, staff, amenities, location... I will be back. Love it!!!!!

The Harrington Hotel is an older hotel which shows some wear, but was clean and quiet. The location is excellent and the staff was friendly. The room itself was adequately sized, but the bathroom needed more shelf space. There was good water pressure and the hot water was adequate. We had a coupon for free parking which was honored, the parking deck is a quick - minute walk . We stayed in early August when the temperature was around --- degrees, the air conditioning was fine until the last day of our - day stay when it malfunctioned and the room got pretty warm, the front desk said they were working on it but we checked out before it was back in service. Overall it was a good experience and a good value ($--- night with coupon) compared to other D C hotel prices.

I didn't want to be one of the reviewers to pan a hotel just because there were a few faults, so let me start with the good. Excellent location right on Geary in a perfectly safe neighbourhood. Free internet access was also available and the fitness centre whilst small was very much appreciated. Now, the not so good.
If you have a room ending in --,-- or -- you will not sleep. These rooms overlook Geary and the hotel has done NOTHING to try and reduce noise. I am used to staying in city hotels, even in SF, but the street noise here was unbelievable. Please, if you are anything other than a very heavy sleeper get a room at the back. Next problem, housekeeping. Being woken up at ---am (when the do no disturb sign was clearly on the door) was not my idea of service, however it got even worse when the next day housekeeping left my door ajar all day. Not good enough - when I contacted the front desk they said they would record the matter and hung up on me. My final problem came when I tried to extend my stay. Whilst they were able to extend my stay one day the hotel was completely booked the next day. Fair enough - it was late notice. However it would have been nice if they had contacted another of the personality hotels and checked with them. 
all in all the hotel is ok but there are MANY better options in the city. Personally, for the mid range traveller, you should check out the Commodore on Sutter for a better all around hotel.

no working light switch at door(and lights were not left on). A bit of stumbling around in dark room found one that did work. A few cock roaches, but not too bad for Houston. They actually stapled a tripadvisor.com card to my receipt. Maybe that is why the check in clerk was so nice ---- typically the check in clerks at this location left you the impression they wished you'd go somewhere else.

It’s a “Sweet” deal for a large hotel room, small kitchen unit, complimentary continental breakfast, free internet, ideal location for Seattle Center and great walking opportunities along the piers. But, the housekeeping is slipping and the free continental breakfast is on sugar overload. 
Living Space: It is a huge room, which offers a sleeper sofa, coffee table, flat-screen TV, and a small table and chairs. The colors and décor are simple and are of the typical hotel style. Upon first glance it looks clean but with a closer look at the TV and it’s dresser-stand it all needed a good dusting. 
Bedroom: With the bedbug scare going around I didn’t waste any time doing a search with the bed. We rolled back the comforter, looked at the linens and pillows, and examined everything for small black specs. We didn’t see anything however maybe I just don’t know what to look for yet. But in the meantime after examining the headboard and nightstands we found them covered in dust. And we all know dust contains dust mites and other human skin. Yuck! Housekeeping is doing a quick job and not being thorough. See pictures that document our observation.
Bathroom: The bathroom seemed clean upon first glance, but it did not pass my washcloth test. I took a washcloth and soaked it with hot water and some soap. After wiping the floor in front of the toilet for just a little bit the washcloth turned black. *See photos. We initially thought the floor had been mopped because the tile grout was darker in the center of the floor and the cleaning service simply did not mop to the edges. Well, it never got lighter so that means it wasn’t wet and it was simply very dirty. 
We noticed with the toilet that when you held the handle to flush you needed to hold the handle longer than usual and it needed to be flushed twice. The water pressure must be very low. 
An area of the bathroom that seems to be missed way too often and shouldn’t be is the inside of the door. I saw filthy, smear marks left from someone’s hands and fingers. If someone is leaving a bathroom with unclean hands I don’t want to even imagine why they are dirty. This is a sanitary issue that really needs to be addressed with the house cleaning service. 
Kitchen space: The small kitchen unit is a great bonus for any extended stay where you can fix some of your own snacks. There was a refrigerator, microwave, dishwasher and a few dishes and utensils. It seemed clean at that angle, however, the floor had that darkened grout in the more central section and then the grout was light and clean closer to the wall. Again, I did my washcloth test and found the floor to be filthy! *See photos.
Continental Breakfast & Dining Room: 
“Homewood Sweets” has new meaning here. The Continental Breakfast is a deal if you are not picky and not concerned about having a sugar overload. We had breakfast there for a couple of different mornings. A few good choices included wheat bread, low-fat cream cheese, fresh fruit and water. I also tried the sausage patties, scrambled eggs and an omelet with cheddar cheese. The patty was cold, the eggs tasted fake and the cheddar cheese in the omelet was horrible. The food warmers were barely keeping the food luke-warm. It would be nice if the plates were warmed to keep the food warm just a little longer. For some healthy options it would be nice if the hotel offered low-fat cottage cheese for those of us that don’t want to eat meat or fake eggs. It’s great mixed with the fresh fruit. The juice offered was orange and apple, which are heavy with sugar. Cranberry juice could be offered for those patrons that would like to cut sugar calories. There were assorted muffins but none were a dark healthy grain option. Cereals offered were also heavy with sugar.
Coffee was offered around the clock and was fine for swigging down that high-sugar overload. But, for those Latte lovers it doesn’t substitute and you will have to go on a hike to get your fix. We would highly recommend a bottle of hand sanitizer at the coffee bar and a sign to suggest using it. Some people do not wash their hands. Some people eat with their hands and then return for a coffee refill. Everyone is touching the coffee pumps, cups, straws and counter. The garbage can should have an open top that you don’t have to touch. Hand sanitizer is good, please use it everywhere!
The tables and chairs seemed clean and taken care of. The staff was on top of that and kept everything organized. It was a large dining room ready for a large crowd. The upholstered over-sized chairs around the tables at the windows are great for those over-sized sugar lovers. However if you are of a healthy, normal size you will sink in and feel like a toddler because your feet can’t touch the floor. So they’re not that comfortable and hard to get out of. Some normal-sized upholstered chairs by the windows would be nice and be more practical. They would also fit around the tables better.
View & Location: Location is great with its proximity fairly close to the water, park and the walking and biking trails. As well, the walking distance is convenient to the boardwalk, piers, great restaurants and the Seattle Center.
Nice Bonus: Small store next to front desk is nice for small toiletries and goodies to eat.
Guest Services Suggestion: Provide dial-up movies or rent DVD movies.

I think this Hilton does live up to its name, we booked - rooms and both were in great condition,, even though we were close to the airport. there was no noise at all. nothing 
and the bed was super soft and big.. every night in that bed was amazing.. 
the food at the hotel was expensive but it was great. the parking i'm going to lie its a maze down there! but i'm from NY and used to having to battle it out for parking. the service was very friendly in the Hilton and the concierge knew his stuff recommenced a great club for us.

We travel to New York City many times during the year and always stay at the Algonquin. We have found the Algonquin to be our favorite hotel of all others that we have stayed. The lobby is a great extension of your room and you can relax there to have a drink or coffee in the morning. Perhaps the best quality of the hotel is the wonderful staff that always makes you feel at home. The hotel respects history and makes you feel part of the history of New York. We have stayed in other very nice hotels while the hotel is being renovated but none can come close to the Algonquin. Hurry back!

I used to stay here regularly about --- years ago. I was back for the first time since then. Great location but in need of some nips and tucks. Older, feeling a bit stuffy and gloomy. Nice people - very friendly. Independent hotel - not part of any chains.

A rather dingy, older motel in central Chicago. The good: great location, free Wi-Fi.The bad: -- parking spaces for -- rooms - you could be looking for parking at a neighborhood lot. My wife and I had an excellent experience at this hotel. I highly recommend asking for a room with the walk-in shower-tub. The architecture of the hotel and the rooms is superb. One complaint: we found some hairs in the bed linens. We did not bring it up to the attention of the staff since we were very tired and wanted to sleep.

In May, ---- we stayed three nights at the Orlando Hotel in West Hollywood, California. It was very clean, comfortable, and quiet. The hotel is conveniently located near the Beverly Mall and some very nice restaurants. An extra treat was having Wolfgang Puck coffee in our room, along with chocolates on the pillow. There is a little Italian restaurant off of the lobby with a wonderful daily """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""happy hour."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Drinks were half price and the food was exceptional. The hotel staff were very friendly and helpful with everything from driving directions to printing our boarding passes for the trip back to the Washington, D.C. area.

A four night stay during the wettest weather we’ve experienced for many years. The Elysee a marvellous port in the storm and conveniently central. Our bedroom spacious, comfortable, clean and quiet: The Club Lounge a meeting point for guests over a delicious breakfast. Our visit included opera at the Met as it was for other guests too we soon discovered! Great company! Self service tea, coffee, biscuits and fruit all day, and a selection of daily papers too. Staff more than helpful – even prepared to stand out in the pouring rain for several minutes to find taxis! Look at the photos on the website – they give a true picture. Wine and cheese each evening is convivial and a good ploy for relaxation between day and evening events. Access to the computer in The Library was useful. The laid back atmosphere belies all the care and organisation which makes The Elysee a most acceptable hotel in this fabulous city.

I was given the choice of a king or two doubles when we checked in, and chose the king which was on a lower floor, in hindsight I'd choose the two doubles on the higher floor as we stayed on the --th floor and only had a view of the monorail and surrounding buildings. The beds were incredibly comfortable, the furnishings were decent and the bathroom was clean. The gym was also well equipped, clean and had personal T.V's for the cardio machines with clean headsets. 
Cons - You could hear every little noise from the hallway, the sound didn't seem to be muffled at all.
