Good location for political meetings as well as for sightseeing - just a few steps from the Capitoal and Union Station. Friendly and cheerful staff. Comfortable and functional rooms, while some of the decor seems a bit dated - all clean and well maintained though! Creative and tasty breakfasts (I must mention the tasty quinoa granola), good bar with a few signature cocktails. During my stay the hotel seemed extremely busy, also with meetings and group functions going on.This may have led to some more noise and less attention than usual, but also despite the evidently busy days, the stay was comfortable and fully satisfactory. We came across it by chance and last-minute, and had a very pleasant experience.

I stayed here recently for a conference. I had stayed here previously (many years ago) and was amazed at the renovations and upgrades. This is a beautiful old hotel that had been let run down over time. I was so pleased that it has been restored! The check in process was easy with the clerk extremely helpful. My room was light, airy, comfortable and clean. I had a great view overlooking a park and the Lake. The conference rooms were fine though the hotel could have done a better job with the AV systems. Food was typical conference chicken and beef-just okay. The checkout process was simple as was retrieving my car. All in all, I'd stay there again in a heartbeat.

This was our -th or -th stay at the Kensington. Half a block from Union Square is it surprisingly quiet. Very efficient check-in and check-out. Bob the doorman has been there for years and is a wealth of information - he rarely cracks a smile, but will always have a joke or place to suggest to go see.
Our king room was a good size although the bathroom was a bit small - afterall it is an older building. 
They have a coffee-juice bar in the morning and sherry or tea in the afternoon in the lobby. One night they even had two musicians !
We will continue to book this hotel due to its location and value.

Overall this was a great hotel and appeared to be recently built. Everything on the grounds was very clean, the staff was very pleasant and helpful, and the room was comfortable albeit a little on the small side. The only problem (very minor) was that housekeeping didn't take all of the used towels and didn't provide full bottles of shampoo and conditioner for our second night. My only other suggestion would be that adding a shuttle service to Six Flags would be a huge plus since the park is close but not really in walking distance. Otherwise we were pleased with our stay and felt it was a good use of Marriott Rewards points.

my wife and i stayed at the mid town hotel for two nights, june -th &-th ---- on our first visit to boston. a little nervous having read some of the reports.
our opinion ?
ok it's not the ritz, but for the price, location and free car parking, couldn't fault it, would definitely stay again.

I booked this place through a Priceline bid and was pleasantly surprised! The hotel is within a sort of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Corporate Park"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" surrounded by other mid-price hotels such as Embassy Suites. The Front Desk guy was very helpful and the hallways were well-lit, super clean and quiet. The room I got was very big and had a pretty elaborate kitchen set-up with a huge refridgerator-microwave, coffee-maker (gotta supply your own coffee tho') and a new Flat-screen TV. It's an easy - block walk to the Train Station which is across from a ---hour Wawa Market (Philly's local --Eleven type place). This hotel above all is totally safe and totally clean, a big plus for a solo traveler! Big thanks to the sweet art student who works the Front Desk at night!

We chose the Carlton Inn Midway based on the Tripadvisor reviews, and the place lived up to what others had said about it. 
The staff were above and beyond friendly and helpful. When we arrived, the front desk had a package of brochures stapled to directions for all kinds of toddler-friendly Chicago sites (they knew we were traveling with a child). We were given really good recommendations for restaurants nearby. When we did have a problem with our room, the staff and management took care of it immediately and to our satisfaction. They offered us rides around the neighbourhood at every opportunity, but we found the walking distances to be very reasonable. 
The hotel is not right downtown. However, it is less than a five minute walk from the hotel to the Orange Train, and if you are not up for the walk, the staff will drive you. The Train is a very affordable transportation option and you can buy day passes at the front desk. To get right to the heart of Chicago's downtown and where all the attractions are takes less than -- minutes. The Chicago transit system is really easy to use and navigate, and the schedules are fine.
The hotel offers free parking, which is a rarity in Chicago and a real money saver. 
The room itself was totally fine. It was very clean. My only real complaint is that they seem to use a very strong, chemical-smelling air freshener when they clean and prepare the rooms. If you are like me and are sensitive to scents, I would recommend asking that they not use in your room, when you make your reservation. The continental breakfast is quite basic but fine. There isn't much space to eat in the lobby but the rooms have a nice table area. 
Overall, the Carlton Inn was perfect for us. Affordable, free parking, clean, excellent staff-management, and easy to get downtown. We would certainly stay there again!
Loved the proximity to --th Street Mall! Super comfy beds!

My husband and I stayed at Hotel Andra for two nights in May ---- before departing for a cruise to Alaska. Having never been to Seattle before, we were pleased to find that the location of the hotel was WONDERFUL! It was in a great part of town within walking distance of most of downtown. The King County light rail is only two and half blocks away, and many other metro bus stops are also close. The Westlake Shopping Center is only two blocks away, and a variety dining options are nearby. The restaurant at the hotel, Lola, was amazing. We ate dinner there the first day, and the food was the best we had in Seattle. The staff was also very helpful and had a cab waiting to pick us up Sunday morning to take us to the pier. We also got a great deal on our stay because we were able to get a discount for booking early. I will definitely stay at Hotel Andra again the next time we travel to Seattle. I highly recommend this hotel!!

Retraced steps of -- years past in San Francisco at the Cow Hollow Inn. The hotel was indeed as I remembered it, a quality hotel at a very reasonable price. It is very centrally located to shops on Union Street and to Fishermans Wharf. The restaraunts in the area are varied, and food in all was excellent. The lone complaint was the indifferent attitude that approached rudeness by desk clerk at the Cow Hollow. Any questions were met by blank stares and curt replies. With tourism waning throughout North America, it seemed to me they're attitudes required adjustment.

Hotel is beautiful with an old european ambience to it, rooms are spacious & very clean with very comfortable beds. Amazing view over harbor. Staff are very friendly and extremely helpful, always smiling and always very happy to help in any way they can! food both in room service and restaurants is very good! looking forward to staying there again!

My daughter and I stayed in the hotel for one night. It is very well located in a quiet street close to a lively neighborhood. Service was good. The room was neat and modern although a tad small. Modern bathroom, LCD screen and USB connections. A good touch was the dim light in the bathroom that turns on with movement. Very useful if you are trying to get there during the night and don’t want to wake up your travel companion. But then… the bathroom door has a glass section. Once inside the bathroom you have to turn on the main lights. The light will ‘escape’ through the glass and illuminate the room anyhow… so, I think, the whole thing doesn’t work. They have a happy hour with free wine in the main lobby, seemingly, in a daily basis. We opted for the breakfast in the hotel but I don’t recommend it. The reception staff is very attentive and helpful. Overall, I would recommend the hotel in spite of the minor flaws.

This was the perfect hotel for quiet retreat from the city's hassles, close to public transportation in a largely residential, business area. Polite staff. Clean. Nice bath. The shower had the perfect mixer even temperature. Breakfast was perfect. Not too dark, nor too white. The bed was comfortable and the internet reliable.

The rooms are VERY small. Just about ok for one, but would have been a squeeze with -. But well appointed, and comfortable. Staff also excellent. The roof terrace is fab but shame there are no drinks allowed up there. The other main minus with my room is that it had almost no natural light and was incredibly dark. The bathroom fan was also incredibly noisy as was the aircon. I think it would probably be impossible to sleep with the aircon on, which may be a problem in the summer. There's no breakfast available.
However the location is great, minutes from the metro and lots of nice restaurants and bars.

We stayed at the Blake Hotel this past weekend. It was beautiful...the room was nicely appointed and very clean, and the lobby was absolutely gorgeous. The staff were very friendly and helpful. Especially nice is their shuttle service - on Saturday morning they both took us to our destination and picked us up when we called for a ride back. The concierge Anthony was very helpful, providing us with excellent information and directions through the city. I would definitely stay here again!

The room we had overlooked some roofs, but I believe most of the other rooms have a view of the Baltimore Washington Monument. The monument was designed by the same person that designed the monument in Washington DC. The cathedral that Francis Scott Key died in is only a block away. We did not rent a car because of the cost of parking as well as Baltimore has good mass transportation. The hotel is located halfway between Penn Station and the Baltimore harbor. You will find lots to do as well as good food at the harbor. The Baltimore Orioles and Ravens stadiums are close to the harbor also. You can find free transportation within the downtown and harbor area. The Charm City Circulator is a free bus system that stops about a block from the hotel. We walked to Penn Station and caught a Marc train to Washington DC's Union Station for $-.--. The train from Penn Station to BWI airport is only $-.--.

Nothing.more than a crack motel.. The. Hotel has potential...great location! The manager there is horrible! She yells and curses the people that pay to live there. I hjave never seen a more serious case of mis management! As long as management remains the same it will never be a decent place to live much less visit!!

Overall we had a very good experience at the Westin Riverwalk. The location is excellent, on the quiet side of the Riverwalk with a great lobby with fruit, cheese, crackers, and a bar accompanied by a musician nightly from ---pm. Very nice ambiance. 
The rooms themselves are on par with other Westins we have stayed in - nice. Other amenities like the gym and pool were very good as well. The staff was very friendly and went out of their way to 
make you feel welcome. 
This would have been a - star stay but for a few dings. We had a couple issues with cleanliness (bath tub obviously not cleaned, and hairs(!) in our coffee maker) but the staff promptly addressed these issues. I didn't read any other complaints about the cleanliness of the rooms so I would not expect to have these issues on a future stay. In addition, our TV wasn't working half the time. 
Tip - before doing the overnight $-- valet parking (which though nuts is on par or even cheaper compared to other hotels in the area) check the lot right across the street - only $-- overnight.
Tip #- - during the middle of our stay we were upgraded (cool!) from a Studio Suite to a Corner Suite. The Corner Suites have a view of the river, but with it being so quiet where the property is there isn't much to see. We actually preferred the Studio Suite because it feels more open and spacious due to it not having a divider like the Corner Suites.

Just came back from SD. We stayed at the Omni for - nights, we loved it!! I got a rate of $--- per night through travelzoo.com, which is the same rate I paid for a night at Ramada in Carlsbad. I requested a room on the higher floor, I got --th, facing the bay and the train track. I could hear a bit of noise early in the morning but it didn't bother me since I woke up early every morning anyway. I registered on line on their web site as a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""selected guest"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (it is free), and upon checked in, my son received a back pack with toys and cooky & candies, also a Omni kid's cup with unlimited drink refill in their restaurant for the entire stay. As a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""selected guest"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", I also received - servings of beverages of my choice every morning, same as my son & my husband. Even though they don't have complimentary breakfast like others do, I had - glasses of V- juices every morning and that really filled my up! Besides that, my son had - big cookies and a glass of milk every evening.......isn't it great??
The room is very clean and comfortable, it even has a DVD player that my son could play his favorite movie that he didn't finish on the plane. The only compliant is the bathroom doesn't have any exhaust fan. 
The hotel is at a great location. The trolley station is right by. We only rent a car for - days to go to Legoland, La Jolla & the Zoo. The rest of the time we took the trolley. We purchased a - day pass ($-) and have unlimited rides on the trolley to the surrounding Downtown attractions. There is a public covered parking lot right across the street. The daily rate is $- and evening rate is $-. Fri & Sat is a few bucks more. There are many restaurants to choose along the Gaslamp Quarter area.
SD is a great place to visit, and Omni just make it even better.

Love this place. Like a European hotel, well appointed, clean, very reasonably priced. 
Only one suggestion, a coffee maker in the room would be a great touch. Sure there are places to get coffee downstairs, at any time of day or night (in fact, every food known to man is available within a ten minute walk), but I'm not a morning person. 
I wake up, I want coffee in the room. 
Small thing, though, everything else about this place is great!

We were delightfully impressed with our stay here. The rooms were clean & updated. We had a bay view that was breathtaking- there was construction going on next door, so if you are planning on working in the room during the day you might notice the workers & noise (but it was not enough to affect our stay, we just closed the blinds). 
All of our contact with staff were genuine & enthusiastic- I was impressed.
The location is great with restaurants & nightlife within blocks. 
The executive lounge breakfast is the best I have seen with fresh fruit, a variety of choices & a beautiful setting.
We got a great rate & will be returning on our next visit to the area.

First the positives. This is a great hotel with friendly staff, wonderful rooms, and great location. The positive reviews on Trip Advisor are accurate. The bed was the most comfortable in a hotel that I have ever found. The bathroom has both a tub and a shower. Extra perks like robes and bottled water are nice. That being said, this hotel does have a few minor quirks.
First, be prepared to pay $-- daily for in-room internet service. Secondly, and this is a small point, the cable stations are sub-par (no Food TV, no HGTV etc..). The final quirk is the resturant, Chez Colette. We walked in on a week night, and it was practically empty. Only - tables were filled. While the food was good (not great) and the service pleasant, it was hard to really enjoy it surrounded by such silence. The resturant has potential; but I would not go out of my way to eat there. The price tag was a bit steep too, at $--- for two. With so many great resturants in Philly, I would spend my food budget elsewhere.
Breakfast at Chez Colette is also pricey. If you want a quick bagel-muffin-coffee in the morning, check out Le Bus around the corner. They also have salads for a light lunch. 
Overall, this hotel deserves its high ratings. Do not hesitate to give the Philly Sofitel a try. We will definitely be back!

A great hotel, rooms a little noisey and old a-c had to be turned off whilst trying to sleep but otherwise very nice and we did not come to LA to stay in our room. Comfy double beds.
We used the restaurant every morning for breakfast, where there were - options where we could have the buffet or order off the breakfast menu, we also ate here a couple of evenings and the food was lovely and the staff were excellent.
We also booked our universal studio tour through the hotel as they had a free shuttle.
They also DO have a airport shuttle!!! we did not know this so we arrived via the fly bus and then a taxi which was long and expensive but used their shuttle service on the way back and for $-- it was excellent, even though we had a tyre blow out on the freeway we still arrived quickly, safely and right outside the terminal which we requested.

I want to start out by saying we never stay in Midtown. We've been to NY many times and find other parts of the city more desirable. That said, the Royalton is a good hotel choice for the area. It could be a great hotel with a just a few tweaks.
Here's what I liked:
The staff was friendly
We were in a king room, which was large. There was a long built-in couch for lounging or napping, the bed, a desk, a bar, and the bathroom. I have no complaints about the size.
The linens and pillows were great. It felt like sleeping in a cloud.
The location is centrally located to Times Square and the trains, but our room was quiet.
You can move stuff around in the fridge to put your own items inside.
The strength of the shower was superb. I want that shower head and water pressure in my house.
The bathroom products were very nice.
Here's what I didn't like (for a short stay, these are mostly minor):
The strength-speed of the Internet access was abysmal. I mean bad. Considering it is $-- per -- hours, it should work.
There are no accessible plugs by the head of the bed. (They exist because things are plugged in, but they are behind the furniture or under the bed and mostly impossible to reach.) This is a design fail.
The bed is set into a lovely piece of furniture that allows for these cute cut-outs next to each person's head. However, one of them has a telephone making one almost non-usable. If you want water or something larger next to your bed, you'll have to put it on the floor or pull up a chair.
If you use a C-Pap beware. Having no table next to the bed, nor any plugs, is a problem. We travel with extension cords and ran them across the floor for our phones and computers, but this isn't optimal.
There is only one reading light over the bed. Both sleepers have access to an on-off and dimmer switch, but if one person is reading the other might need eye shades.
The bathroom has a little vanity with a stool, which I liked but the light over it isn't bright enough. There is also a lighted makeup mirror, which was a nice touch but the light was very dim and was mounted too high to look in while seated at the stool.
There is only one small soap dish in the shower. I don't want all my shower stuff on the floor.
Beware the bellmen tipping off the cab drivers as to your knowledge about NY. They'll try to indicate to the cab drivers if you understand the difference between the bridge and the tunnel to LGA.
Here's what made no difference to me:
The TV is kinda small to watch from the bed. But, we didn't turn it on. It is easy to view from the couch.
The in-room iPad.
You get a candle and matches in the bathroom. We felt to guilty to light it knowing it would be thrown away after we used it and restocked for the next guest.

My family and i stayed her way back in april ----, what a fantastic hotel and the views are out of this world, and where it is, its great for getting up and down town. i would defo come back and stay here again if i was to get the chance to stay in new york again.

My husband stayed at this hotel for - week for a review course held there between nov ----. He raved about how nice and clean the hotel is, and how friendly hotel staff was. During this week, there was an incident that involved the hotel and denver airport, but everything was handled by the staff and hotel exceptionally well and handled very calmly. My husband was very impressed. My other reason for this comment is in regards to my husband forgetting approx --- of pieces of expensive clothing in the drawer of his hotel room. He only remembered that he forgot them when he arrived back in pittsburgh pa-morgantown wv. I called in the morning to see if someone could locate his clothing and left my name and number. Evening time came, and no one called me back with any info (our only disappointment), so i called again. I was connected to RYAN FODOR in the security-lost and found department. This guy could not have been any more helpful!!!.....and if any of you managers reading this, please acknowledge this employee and i say give him a bonus or a raise, and this is why: he checked his department and my husbands clothing was not there. He checked w- housekeeping, and the clothing was not there. He took my name and number and said he would look into this further and get back to me. He went out of his way to see if anyone had checked into that room for friday night and that sat night, as a vacant room, he personally went to the room to locate the clothing. He called me back to say he did not find them, but that he would continue to try and help. He did more investigating over the next hour to hour n half, somehow found all of my husbands belongings and called us with the good news! (he could have just said, sorry i cant find them and that be the end of it). He then was more than happy to ship the clothing back to us on monday, and he REFUSED any tip! I insisted he let us send him a tip, or add it to our credit card that i gave him to ship the clothing to us, and he stated he was more than happy to help and declined any money. I felt i should acknowledge him, and what better way than on trip advisor! We recieved the clothes by wednesday like he said, and we could not be more thankful! Thank you Ryan for doing what you did! My husband will for sure stay at this hotel again for this reason and many more!

The room was pleasant, clean and quiet with colorful bedspreads and paint. The hallways were somewhat dingy, perhaps they are in the process of redecorating? The staff is extremely pleasant and the common spaces of the hotel are very spacious and welcoming. There is a nice lobby bar and a full service Starbucks along with a separate sports bar and restaurant.
I stayed during a business meeting and received a highly discounted rate, so no comments as to value.

We stayed for - nights for our first trip to New York. When we arrived, first impressions were not quite what we expected. Decor is quite old and dated (while the lobby is nice the bedrooms are quite old and stuffy) and bathrooms are not the best - the shower trickles rather than actually showering! The service is not the best I've seen - staff are not rude but most look like they would rather be somewhere else and not very keen to help. 
The location however is brilliant! We could see the empire state building from our room, it is close to the subway, broadway and times square but not too much street noise so you can actually get some sleep! Absolutely great location. 
If, like us, you plan on being out all day sightseeing etc. and are just lookig for a place to rest your head and get some sleep, then this hotel was good value for money for us in terms of location.

Read some of the less positive reviews of this hotel prior to booking, but since most hotels were completely booked, and I got a good rate, decided to try it. Was very impressed. Room was spacious (king overlooking park), very quiet, and well appointed. Bath towels were very soft --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" bath sheets (not standard in hyatt or westin). Service was very good. Great location across street from Park. Only complaint is that the A-C was on too high when I checked in. There was a thermostat on wall, which I turned down, but it didnt have any temperature markings. Not easy to figure out how much to turn it down to get the temperature right. I didnt eat any meals in hotel, but noted that prices seemed high.

The Manchester Hyatt is a lovely Hotel. No complaints.
The service was excellent and the location was perfect. It was only a short ---- minute drive to Sea World and The San Diego Zoo.
The Hotel is also right next to Seaport Village which has many restaurants and shoppes. 
We had a corner room with great views of the bay and the city skyline. Awesome views!
We would definitely stay there again.

I traveled to Phoenix for a one night stay for business. I choose this location as I was coming in on an evening flight for an early appointment the next morning in Paradise Valley. I was greeted promptly upon arrival. My room was ready and received a gift of chips and salsa for Hilton Honors members. Room looked brand new and was spotless. Went down to the restaurant for a late dinner. Sat at a table for ten minutes but nobody came so I ordered at the bar. In all fairness it looked like the bartender was the only one there and he was doing the best he could do. Ordered the Mobley burger with fresh fruit instead of fries. Very good burger and some of the freshest fruit I have had in awhile. The bed was the most comfortable hotel bed I have ever slept in. Overall a great place to stay overnight if you have business in the area. The road to the hotel from the airport rental car center looks a little sketchy at times but the hotel is on the edge of a business-office district.

My wife and I along with our (-) pet dogs spent Christmas with our grandson who works at El Paso Airport. The hotel was walking distance from the airport and our grandson spent our time there with us in our King Suite when he wasn't working. Everyone at the hotel were very friendly and accomodating.... we made several requests of the housekeeping staff and they were very friendly and helpful. We were travelling with our - dogs and found out that about - families were there with pets. Our King ground floor suite was comfortable, clean and well maintained. We would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone travelling in the area.

This is a gorgeous property, sleek, spotlessly clean, on a great street for proximity to shopping and excellent bars, cafes, restaurants.
Check out the Uni Glo flagship store just down the road, fantastic.
The staff seemed a little snobby to my friends who were also staying there, I didn't mind them so much.
They had purchased on priceline and there were - of them, they were given a room with one queen bed and were told they could not get a room with - beds for that rate (we moved to the Grand Hyatt the next day and they offered us anything we wanted) anyway, they asked for a roll away and were charged FIFTY dollars for it! For one night! Ripped off.
The showers are all white tile, modern and super clean and have - shower heads, awesome!!

Super value for the money. We stayed here to be near the airport for an early flight after a cross-country car trip. The rooms are modern and comfortable with all you could need. The pool met the needs of my kids. The free shuttle to the airport leaves every half hour and was perfect. The staff was professional and friendly. There doesn't seem to be much immediately surrounding the hotel but since we weren't there to sightsee, it didn't make any difference to us.

We stayed at Nine Zero for - nights during our wonderful Fall trip up in New England. It was fairly pricey, but no more so than the other top hotels downtown. The location was excellent, right in the heart of the city. We walked pretty much everywhere: through nearby Boston Common, Faneuil Hall-Quincy Market, and the North End. And when we wanted to take the subway (to Fenway and other places), there's a stop a block away. Really no need to have a car... which is why we dropped off our rental car when we arrived in Boston. In fact, the only stressful moment we had was trying to temporarily park just to drop off our bags. There was virtually no room down the side road where the check-in was. After waiting about ten minutes, we got to a place where we could leave our car in their entrance... but then we got blocked in by other cars, so it took us another ten minutes to get out - with the very nice help of a bellman who actually blocked Tremont Street to allow me to escape by backing out the alley. Anyway, after we dropped the car off (and avoided the $-- parking-night), we were stress-free.
We had gotten a King room with a view and it did not disappoint. It was a corner window set-up similar to the one in the little picture above with a view of The Common and the Park Street Church with the rest of the city and water in the background. The room was nicely appointed with a comfortable work desk and chair and a nice armchair with ottoman. Most importantly, the bed was extremely comfortable. Really no complaints, a nice-sized room... and again, we loved all the windows. It was great waking up and seeing the whole city laid out in front of us.
We were pretty constantly on the go, so we didn't really take advantage of the happy hour or any of the other stuff the hotel offered... but, the service was very friendly and helpful. One night before bed, we wanted to watch a DVD on the portable player we had brought and we were having issues getting the TV to recognize the connection. Within two minutes of a call to the front desk, one of their maintenance guys had come up with the proper cord to get the job done. It was an excellent stay at Nine Zero and we would not hesitate to stay there again for a next visit to Boston.

It was a pleasant and comfortable stay at Super-. The price were reasonable for the amenities provided.Moreover, the staff was friendly and took care of the comfort. The motel needs a bIt renovation atleast in the economy class suites. It is close to downtowm and old town and situated in proximity to various eating and shopping arena. I would recommend to stay in it.

My husband and I stayed at the Posh Park Hyatt hotel in downtown Chicago. They have exceptional First Class service from the moment we pulled up for valet service. This is also a good place to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""spot"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" celebrities as well! We ran into Larry King and Martin Sheen in the lobby. The hotel itself was very beautiful and classy, everyone was very professional that you didn't even have to lift a finger for anything. We had a king size room with a beautiful view of downtown Michigan Ave! Very spacious room with desk-chair, huge flat screen TV, one side of our room was all windows with that gorgeous view of the courtyard off of Michigan Ave. The bathroom was spectacular, his and hers sinks, shower with double heads and a jacuzzi type tube that had double sliding doors that opened into the room to catch the view. My husband did check out the pool which was just a lap pool and they also had a hot tub too. This hotel was right in the heart of everything, great location to variety of restaurants and of course Miracle Mile for shopping! I would give this hotel - stars!

This hotel was filthy! It smelled awful. My sister-in-law's room next door smelled of toxic mold! The bathrooms were TINY and dirty. The shower had mildew and mold on the ceiling as well as in the grout lines. NOT to mention the mold in the bathroom that ran along where the wall and ceiling met and the wall and floor met. The paint was peeling off the walls and doors. My - yr old son could have put a better bead of caulk along the bathroom baseboards. My daughter dropped a toy off the head of the bed and when I reached down to get it I noticed that it hadn't been vacuumed in what appeared to be years! The carpet in the halls need to be cleaned and re-stretched.

I have stayed in this hotel several times over the past three years for business and it gets worse and worse with each visit. This stay was the worst of all - I was moved rooms three times and still wound up checking into another hotel! The first two moves were drainage related - the sink wouldn't drain in one and the shower would not drain in the other. All three rooms showed signs of age, with stains on the carpet, furniture, and even the comforter. The veneer on the furniture was peeling and the armoire wood was cracked. After my first (and only) night on this stay I began to develop a rash on my leg - similar to another outbreak I had on my first visit three years (which at the time they blamed on insects in the lobby). To top it all off, they were doing work on the facade of the building that caused noise - they should start with re-vamping the inside! 
Even though my week was paid for through work, I left and spent my own money at the Grand Hyatt Washington at Metro Center, which was a great hotel and an incredibly convenient location. Although I spend my time on the Mall at the museums for work (and L'Enfant's only appeal is that it is within walking distance to the Mall), it was just as easy to take two stops (about -- minutes altogether) on the Metro to Smithsonian station.

So, we didn't get the great treatment that it appears other reviewers received. The trolleys were always full and after buying a --day pass to use them, we were very upset that we ended up walking the majority of the time. Called to make a reservation. Paid to get a rollaway. Never got it. $-- a day parking, Cable sucked, $-- a day for internet, no fridge, no microwave and very expensive meals. You are paying for a name is all. It was a nice building and nice location but geez.... Do you have to bleed me dry for everything in the hotel??? Although it was next to the train station, I would have rather been closer to the center of town. Swimming pool was not clear, very murky, and very small. More for the kids. I believe they called it a lap pool. WHATEVER!!! The scenery from my window was of the top of the conference center, the highway and buildings in the distance. Only nice thing was NASCAR museum was next door.

stayed four nights during my business trip. The room was very spacious and clean and the bed was very comfortable. The hotel is very close to Quncy Market which allowed me to explore the area after work hours.
Wish they had pool though..and maybe allowing five free pages of printing from the business center...
And maybe it is probably me, but the front desk should be little more polite.

I feel sorry for those in charge of running this hotel. 
The location is very good, but can't so much more than that on the PROs side of things.
Plenty of CONs:

- infrastructure: in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""new"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" or second room, there was low water pressure and hardly hot water. The same room key problem remained with that roomlock too, however, at least it locked. The elevator was VERY slow.
- service: given the above we requested a reduction in room price. They were resistant, although I am quite sure that these issues and complaints repeat with every second visitor. - location is very good. BUT, watch where your room is located. If on the west side of the building the L-line will be going past you and it can be quite loud.

Started off with Rude check in. I come back the next day and theres a cleaning lady who tells me a manager and another person was in my room. Something I left right on the desk near the bed was straight stolen from me. The maid told me a manager and a few people

My boyfriend found this hotel for us when we traveled last year to NYC.
I was so surprised when we arrived. It was so cute and the staff was very friendly. The room was small but very stylish. And the location was perfect!
One night we went down to the bar for a drink and there was a young, hipster band playing jazz. They were awesome!
I'd definitely stay here again when I go back to NYC.

Firstly, there is no elevator. We had to lug our luggage up to the second floor. The girl at the desk didn't offer any help. She was cold and not a help. There was no computer available for our use. We asked for pool towels and she replied they had none; othyer guests at the pool HAD towels. A little boy was urinating by the pool. When we were walking out the door, not even a goodbye. I will never stay at thgis motel ever again.

After about a -- hour drive my family and I was anxious to get to the hotel. Right from the start the staff was excellent. They helped us unload our car and bring our bags to our room. At the check-in desk we received cold lemonade which was a relief from the heat. There was a mixup with our room but they fixed it immediately. The hotel was beautiful and large. We had a - double bed room. Our room was clean and nice. I wouldn't recommend it for - adults and - teens but we made it work. The lazy river was definitely lazy. I wished it was longer. Also be careful of the little kids i almost ran one straight over. We ate at the springhouse cafe while we were there during the Italian buffet night. The food was good but nothing was amazing. All in all i had an amazing stay it was always nice to get out of the heat after a long day of sightseeing.

Great location. Walking distance to Pikes Market. A must.
Very clean, check in was a breeze, Nice bar scene in the lobby after - pm. But with so many micro breweries... no real need to drink there.
Ask for a low floor room as the tower can take forever to catch an elevator for a higher +-- floor.

Close to everything. -th Floor roof pool was cool. Kids loved it. We had an adult beverage while they swam. Staff nice, no problems. Had breakfast in restaurant. Kids had the all you can eat buffet for $-.-- (off menu was $- for pancakes alone), I had an omelet skillet w-toast, hashbrowns. $--.--. Buffet would have been $--.-- for adults. Quick service, good food. Would stay again.

I found The Regency to be overrated on many levels. First, customer service. It is completely remiss. The doormen are the best part of the staff. From the manager to the front office staff they clustered in groups and ignored hotel guests. It happened during the entire duration of my stay. Bad service starts from the top so it came as no surprise when I met the manager. She was a non-problem solver. It was apparent this was the management style they were taught.
The rooms are large. If you have a family and that is your main objective then this is your hotel. If you are someone who prefers style, updated rooms and quiet this is NOT your place. The bathroom door was peeling with a messy quick paint cover up. GROSS. 
My room was $---. a night and had a small kitchen that I never used (I thought it was a closet the first day). As a business traveler who frequents NYC twice a month I prefer a stocked fridge and BOTTLED water. NONE. The kitchen was gross. I went to their hotel store and the Indian man talked on the phone the entire time I was there. I bought water and contact solution. For a -oz saline solution I was charged $--.--. This was not the Palace in Gstaad so no idea where these prices came from. I understand hotels upcharge but a $-.-- to $--.--???
Lastly, I asked if they provided a car service. MY EXACT WORDS. They said yes and would arrange for my arrival at JFK. The gentleman who met me was very nice. However, we waited -- minutes outside in the cold for the driver who showed up in an SUV. Fast forward to my bill and guess what they charged? $---.-- for a ONE WAY!!!!!! The car service was considered a limousine service (not disclosed to me) and instead of a normal car service of $--.---$--.-- I was charged $---.--! The hotel is RESPONSIBLE. I asked for a car service, not a limo service. AND I received a late SUV. 
The worst part was the management was very unprofessional about how they handled the booking. I repeated to them the facts but they took no responsibility. 
For a little more stay at the Mark, Pierre or Waldorf. Or for a great boutique hotel the Hotel Sofitel has beautiful rooms and excellent customer service. 
As I mentioned, if you are a family and space is key you can put up with these issues. However, business travelers and couples beware. There are better experiences to be had.

OK, this is one of those you can do it if your only expectation is a clean room and a free breakfast. They even have a wafflemaker, fruit, yogurt, pastries, hard cooked eggs.
The breakfast room holds about ten people, so get there early if you want a turn at the wafflemaker and a seat.
The pool is not heated and I do not think it is chlorinated, which is strange. The hot tub apparently only is available, heated, during certain hours. When I asked if they could go ahead and turn it on so I could use it they said, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Oh, it is broken.""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""
Half the hotel has interior rooms and half are motel style. So there is some serious noise from the outside and from your air conditioner. It is not broken it is just loud.
The manager did offer to take money off our stay when I suggested it strongly to him, but not until then.
There are so many hotels in the area to chose from next time we are in LA we will just choose another.

We stayed at Affinia Dumont in Dec '--, and was quite happy until we checked out. The room is spacious as a New York standard, and people were very friendly. But, we were surprised to find a mini-bar charge on our bill when we were going to check out. In general, my husband and I would never touch on anything from a mini-bar because we always get drinks and snakes from outside before we head back to the hotel. And that was the case for this stay as well. We told them we did not consume anything, and they checked with housekeeping and took out the charge from our bill. Well, a months later when we got our credit card bill, we found another attempted charge!! Of course, we insisted that it has to be mistake, but the person we spoke to said that she had to get back to us, so they have not yet cleared this charge. Be sure you check your hotel bill and the credit card! I would hope that this hotel is not trying to trick their customers, but it is wired that it happened twice for our one stay. Its a nice hotel, but only pay cash so they can't sneak charges to your credit card after you've left!.

We booked a three bedroom in the Flatotel. It was very luxurious; the living room was a good size with a huge wall mounted flatscreen t.v. The rooms were were spacious and the beds were very comfortable, the kind that you fall asleep in right away!! The fridge comes with bottled water.
There is air conditioning, hot and cold. The bathrooms were nicely laid out in marble and the showers were good. Bathrobes and slippers were in each bathroom (along with lots of towels!). The staff were polite, courteous and eager to help.
There is a good gym on the top floor of the hotel. We ate out every night so I apologize for not being able to comment on the restaurant, I'm sure it is nice!
There is a business centre downstairs where you can use the internet free of charge. The concierge were very helpful and knowledgeable about New York, especially about restaurants and the locations of clothing stores.
The hotel is in an excellent location and is very near Times Square and Central Park is only a short walk away. All the main stores are only a walk way and Chinatown is only a subway ride away (the subway is about a - minute walk away.)
Overall my stay was very pleasant at the Flat Hotel and I would definetely recommend it to anyone who wants to stay in New York. Thanks for reading and good luck!! If you found this review helpful please let me know.

The eight days at Indigo were a real pleasure. Although almost everything went wrong referring to the trip (lost luggage, missed plain), the staff at Indigo did their best to make our journey as pleasant as possible - and they really succeeded. In addition, the hotel offers room quite generously, be it at the restaurant, in the chamber or at the fitness site. All parts of the hotel are clean and the housekeeping service is excellent! 
At this point, me and my colleague want to sincerely thank Trina Cooper at the counter for her courtesy and both professional and prompt help in all matters at all times. Thank you very much!

I have stayed here several times after I moved away from DC. The room was great -- very spacious and reasonably priced. And the front desk staff was amazing -- Samuel really took care of us and he alone would be an incentive to return. Add to that the fact that all up and down Pennsylvania Ave down -th there are restaurants and bars. We had some great Salvadoran food at La Lomita on Penn Ave. We were able to get free parking on -nd Ave, but only b-c we were there on a weekend. Not so easy during the week. If you are interested in being near the monuments, the Capitol Hill Suites is only a couple of blocks from the Library of Congress which, of course, is across from the Capitol. There are two Metro stops in the area, as well. We were in town for the Redskins game. But Capitol Hill is largely a neighborhood where people live. I find it to be the most charming in DC. Not mobbed with tourists yet close enough to be easy for visitors. 
I will return to this hotel every time I visit DC.

We arrived tired from a long flight from Australia, to a warm welcome from the staff at the Harbor Court. Even though it was quite early our room was ready, and their welcome set us up for a great - night stay. Yes, the room was a little small, but we knew that beforehand, and everything else about the hotel made up for it.
We enjoyed the Happy Hour in the evenings, just the thing to relax us after a day of exploring all the many delights that San Francisco has to offer.The young,hip staff happily reconfirmed our bookings for a Sonoma Vallry Wine Tour with Terrific Tours, and a walk in the Muir Woods with Tom, both of which were wonderful. 
The location of the hotel so close to the Ferry Building was a great plus, and we enjoyed the restaurants and the Farmer's Market, also it was close to the Amtrak Building from where we departed from to start our journey accross the USA. 
The Harbor Court Hotel was a fantastic introduction to a wonderful trip to the USA, and we would love to stay there again, and have told our friends and family about it.

I had a nice day in Baltimore, and the hotel location really helped (near the hospital), as I had to attend a conference at JHU. The rooms are new, and the breakfast (free) is as advertised. Parking, differently from what Expedia had on their site, was extra ($-- for the day), but at least there were many spots available. The staff was not as well trained as I had hoped: not only they seemed to vacuum at all times (even as people were walking down the hallway to breakfast, and also in the evening?), but - worse than that - the person at the front desk told me my two credit cards were denied, when they had actually been charged. So I was on the phone with the credit card companies trying to figure this out, and the front desk attendant could not understand that my cards were charged. It took me many hours to untangle the problem...

Stayed here with my -- year old son and chose the Yotel specifically for his amusement. And it really worked. The whole experience, from check in to check out was entertaining and very pleasant.
First of all the location is great. A short walk to Times Square and about a -- minute brisk stride to Penn Station, if you are travelling elsewhere in New York State. 
Check in was a doddle - type in your reservation number and you're off. We had booked via a -rd party and had already made payment, so no need to swipe a bank card. The helpful staff on the door were on hand to answer any questions, and give directions to your cabin. We were on the --th floor which was accessed via two lifts. This was not a problem at all.
The cabin itself was small, but so much fun. The bed doubled as a sofa, but stretched out at the flick of a switch. Large flat-screen television, and a fabulous shower was an additional bonus, and the view was pretty good too. The bed was extremely comfortable (softer than my own firm mattress). Free coffees and hot chocolate drinks were very welcome, and there is a tray provided. There is also a fridge on each floor if you have brought your own food. The wifi connection was free and quick, requiring surname and cabin number as a log-in. The heating-aircon was very quiet - hardly noticed it at all in fact.
We ate at the bar and the food was OK, but not brilliant. It was also quite expensive, but luckily we were there at happy hour, so could enjoy a selection of small tapas-style dishes at $- each. The margaritas are fabulous though, and the terrace has amazing views. The entire hotel and terrace is non-smoking, but there is a small smoking area at ground level outside the hotel but under cover with patio heaters and ashtrays. 
Breakfast was reasonable. Fresh tea-coffee and a selection of sweet muffins, which might not be to everyone's taste, but a good stop-gap first thing in the morning.
My son and I had great fun using the Yobot to store our bags, and when we returned to pick up the luggage and take a taxi to the airport the door staff were extremely helpful, insisting we wait inside while they hailed the cab as it was raining. 
On the whole, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay and would definitely return.

My girlfriends and I stayed at Brookshire in early May ----. While we enjoying the city, we had items stolen from our room including a purse and a wallet. The manager on duty that day was nice and attentive but everyone else up to that point was incompetent and unresponsive. Their stories were not lining up and they weren't doing anything so we called in the Baltimore police to get a report. The police woman was great but was shocked at how the hotel was handling the situation (or not handling). 
Be careful if you want to take the risk in staying here- they admit that the doors do not lock correctly! We aren't sure if that is what happened but pretty sure it was an inside job.
We are still getting the run around from their unresponsive insurance agency as well.
Besides getting robbed, the bathrooms had mold all over the shower curtains and were disgusting. but that obviously was the least of our worries.
The manager working that day did comp one of our rooms but that came no where close to the amount of money that was lost during the trip or the headache of canceling credit cards, bank accounts, losing gift cards, etc. To date, they still have not made good on the troubles caused by us staying in their establishment.

This Holiday Inn has nice size rooms. Excellent price for the room. Our room with a king bed had a flat screen TV, granite counter tops and a nice love seat. The bed was firm, but comfortable. We requested a room away from the elevators due to reading previous comments. It was quiet. Also responding to other comments: There weren’t any homeless people right outside the door. They were mostly up on Market Street and they didn’t seem to be bothering anyone. There is a charge for parking of $-- but it was clearly stated. If you are coming from the airport, the BART is --- yards from the hotel, so consider not driving. Excellent location for the Orpheum and UN Plaza.

Family and I absolutely loved the Olympic hotel. From the swimming pool that was a good size for young kids (- yr old) and the cookies and milk they brought at night, it was a complete, comfy experience. We plan on heading back to Seattle soon and would make this place a must stay. Room service is pricey, so take the ----- min walk to the market (Lowell's has an awesome crab omelette) or run down to the French bakery on the first floor for some tartlettes and coffee for a nice change.

Could not get a room at Hyatt, so booked at this hotel instead. I was plesantly surprised at how great this hotel was. Very responsive staff, absolutely meticulous housekeeping, and great attention to detail. I highly recommend.

Stayed here on a quick vacation swing through San Diego. The room was great, the staff was friendly and very helpful, and my wife and I both feel this is the most exquisuite location we've ever stayed at. The view of the marina from our room was just spectacular, and the pool and jacuzzi were wonderful. MY wife and I can't wait to plan another trip to this wonderful resort -- it is the highlight of our trip!

We stayed at The Milburn for - nights and found it was everything we needed. The staff are polite and helpful, I had asked a --- questions via email before arrival and everyone was answered. The neighbourhood is great, not too many beeping taxi horns (you'll know what I mean when you get there!). Really easy to hail a cab, lots of shops, restaurants, etc in area. We stayed in a one bed suite with our two sons, we had a large bedroom and a large seperate lounge with a pull out double sofa bed, both rooms had a telly and video-dvd. Borrowed a playstation and games from reception. Has a small kitchenette with full sized fridge, microwave and you can ask for a hotplate so you can make a cup of tea. The bed in the bedroom was huge and very comfortable, the bathroom is small but adequate, lots of storage space in the hallway and bedroom. You may find a posher hotel, you won't find a more welcoming, unpretentious one then this, we weren't disappointed. Contact the hotel before booking as we got a good discount on the nightly rate because of the length of our stay. Would recommend highly.

Very disappointed with this property compared to other E. Suites I've stayed in. Lobby area looked okay & front desk clerk was very nice. Rooms have outdated furniture-curtains, peeling wallpaper borders & just felt dirty. Bathroom toilet seat had hair & urine stains on it. Bathroom floor looked dirty as well, just stood on a hand towel instead of bare footed on the floor. Don't expect the usual high standards of an Embassy Suites at this location. If I had seen the inside of a room before booking, would have chosen to stay elsewhere.

Double Tree Suites in Time Square is a excellent hotel in the heart of Time Square. The staff makes all the difference. 
 The hotel suites are spacious, clean and provide a family of four plenty of room. If staying brings you to NYC this is the hotel for you.

Like other reviewers, I was sent to this hotel by Continental Airlines after a missed connection. After a ----- minute wait, the shuttle bus showed up and lots of people crammed in. But the door wouldn't close, and the air conditioning was broken (think, Houston in June!). So it was an unpleasant ride--not a good introduction to the hotel. Then after obtaining a room key, I climbed to the -nd floor with my luggage, and the key would not work. So back to the desk I went, got a new key, and went back for a second try. Still no success, so when I went back to the desk for a -rd try, I asked for another room, and also for directions to the elevator. THERE IS NO ELEVATOR IN THIS HOTEL!!! What sort of a hotel doesn't have an elevator??? The front desk person, who was friendly enough, assigned me a different room and made - keys. Back again, up the stairs, and down the l-o-o-o-n-g hall to that room....and the key didn't work!! Fortunately the second key did, and so I was finally into the room. It seemed OK, but when I got ready for bed and went into the bathroom, the toilet had not been flushed!! DISGUSTING!!! I probably should have left the room at that point, but after all my problems getting a key, I stayed, and fortunately had a reasonably good sleep. 
There was a buffet breakfast, but since I had to be on the shuttle at - AM when it opened, I could only grab a roll and beverage. And to top it all off, the shuttle bus was the same one as the night before, with no air conditioning and a non-closing door!
Don't stay here unless you have no other choice!!

We went to NYC for a conference at the Marriot Marquis. We stayed at the Roger Smith because it was less expensive. During the blackout, we were very happy with the way the Roger Smith handled the emergency. 
They offered free drinks until they ran out. Then they handed us hand fulls of tea lights and glasses with instructions to put water in the bottom. They lined the staircase with tea lights so we could walk up to our rooms. When the power came back on, they went out of their way to make sure that toilets were cleared and guests were comfortable. By contrast, the Marriot evacuated all their guests and our professional organization's president and all our speakers had to sleep outside on the sidewalk in Times Square. Kudos to the small family run Roger Smith. They shined when the big corporate guy fizzled!
Great location, just a few blocks to -th Street. Room was very clean and I had a great view of the rooftop pool area. Cafe in lobby was a nice surprise - perfect for grabbing my morning coffee!

Stayed at the Redbury Hotel and was so amazed by the suite I didn't want to leave!! The property looks like and old one from the outside and is close to the freeway, but inside it's spectacular. All of the rooms are HUGE suites with incredibly beautiful finishes. A full living room and patio balcony. Full kitchen and two flat screen TVs--one in the living area and one in the large bedroom. Ample bathroom with huge closets and shower. Wish I could have stayed for more than one night! Highly recommend especially if you can find a deal!

We had noisy neighbors next to us. They went to bed around -am only to get up and make loud noise (laughing and talking, slamming doors) at -:-- the next morning. The hotel staff did not do anything to get these people to quiet down. They actually lied to the hotel staff saying they were asleep and they weren't making the noise. So after calling down a second time to the front desk, they said they did all they could do. The room was clean and nice, but customer service is seriously lacking. We'll never go back.

I stayed there once and liked it but they have changed. Dirty room (literally trash on the floor), mold growing on bathroom light and a completely soaking wet carpet caused me to request a room change at -:--am. The manager didn't seem to believe me, no apology and no offer to have someone help move my luggage. In addition, there was an issue with the reservation. Lastly, a yellow cab driver told me they are the only hotel in town that has a deal with drivers of the black sedans--they try to get guests to use them or more $$. I got my own cab so that
my driver wouldn't have to make a payout to the doorman. Won't be back ad encourage you to stay elsewhere too.

From the minute we walked into the hotel we could sense that the people in charge of our stay were on top of their game. Smiles, everyone called us by our name. No hassle, I always take note to how well the employees are trained, their appearance, smiles and natural upscale attitude about your stay. There are standards at this hotel that you don't see in many other fine places. And, we felt like guests not customers.

A Ritz Carlton this is not, nor are you expecting it to be. This is a fine no frills hotel when you're flying in and out of Indy and are looking for a place to crash close the airport. Lobby is kinda odd and you get a nice whiff of chlorine as the pool is open and in the back. Workout is pretty small but it exists. Staff is friendly. Restaurant leaves a little to be desired. Really, the hotel is closer to -.- stars in my book but again, it's clean and fine for a night.

I attended a convention at the Hilton Anatole Hotel, and wanted to watch my budget for the three-night stay. Rooms at the Garden Inn were about $---night cheaper than the Hilton Anatole, and the Garden Inn is across the street, so I figured that it would be a good compromise. I have stayed at other Garden Inn hotels, so I had an idea what to expect.
The Garden Inn is like other Garden Inns. The lobby is spacious, the room was large and clean. It's near the freeway, but outside noise was not a problem. My room did not face the highway. The room was also secure.
Walking across the street is not a major problem, but I had to cross the entire Hilton Anatole parking lot in a suit on a hot September day. I did not have to make trips to and from the Anatole and the Garden Inn, so it was not a problem for me, but plan accordingly if you are making the budget-minded move.
The staff was about the best I have ever experienced. They were all friendly, courteous, and ready to help; even with offering me a ride in the hotel van to the Post Office about a mile away.
Decent business value and top-notch staff make this a good hotel to return to. (CS)

I spent the night between flights and found the Westin to be very comfortable. Room was spotless and beds where fabulous with a great nights sleep.
Dining options worked well with lobby bar happy hour and restaurant.
A very easy return to the airport.

My husband was attending a conference at the Omni Hotel so he decided to splurge on the Ritz so I'd have somewhere nice to spend my days while he was at the conference. We had a parlor suite which was lovely. The staff were always friendly and courteous - especially the room service and turndown ladies - and Pia from the Urban Sip was delightful!
Unfortunately, all of the good was really tainted by this: We are from Canada and pay a ridiculous amount in duty for purchases in the US. I wanted to order some things online - avoiding the duty - and have them delivered to the hotel. I called the hotel to see if they would accept the parcel and they said as long as my husband's name was on the package it wasn't a problem. According to the tracking number on the parcel it had been delivered to the hotel but was no where to be found. The front desk staff were lack lustre in their effort to track down my package. I feel the Ritz-Carlton service vision was not in effect during this whole process. I never got annoyed with them - you know the old saying """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""you can attract more bees with honey than vinegar"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I wanted the communication between us to be positive. Yes, the front desk staff were """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sorry"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" about the parcel but I felt let down by their effort to find out what happened to it. Don't forget, I'm left with a bill for items I never received, so I'm very motivated to find out what happened to the parcel. Anyway, when I got home and started to investigate what happened, I found out from FedEx and the US Postal Service, that the hotel wouldn't accept the parcel when the USPS tried to deliver it. Thank goodness the parcel was returned to the sender and I wasn't charged for the contents. I spoke with the GM, David Rothwell, and let him know what had happened. He was perplexed as to why the parcel was rejected at the hotel. I feel that """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""good customer service"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" would require that he get back to me with some sort of explanation, but I've received no communication from him.
My husband and I have stayed in other Ritz-Carlton Hotels and have always had a very positive experience, so maybe this is just """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""one of those unfortunate situations"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Even so, it left a very bad taste in our mouths.

I stayed at this hotel after browsing through this website and expedia and the like. Some of the pictures showed the motel with very contemporary rooms. However, when I arrived at the hotel I was less than impressed.
It must be said that there are two sides to this hotel. On the one side, you have what are called """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""one-two bedroom suites"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". These are the the rooms you are going to see in the pictures when you are booking. However, the room I got was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""deluxe queen"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I believe. These rooms it seems are not yet renovated, and not at all up to the standards of what you pay for. My girlfriend and I checked in to what looked like a rennovated apartment building next to the magic castle. The location is convenient to downtown philadelphia with self and valet parking. The valet service levels are hit or miss depending on person working. The front desk staff is friendly and helpful. Visited Chicago for three nights following six days in New York.

The swimming pool on the --th floor was great to use on an evening and I had it to myself. Views over the city as you swim. There is an open air terrace beyond the pool which I suspect on a warm day would be a fantastic place to view the city from.
Hotel is very central for the main areas of Chicago. Once you get your directions sorted it was within easy walking distance of all key locations.
Chicago is a wonderful city to visit and it is hard to think that there is a better hotel to base yourself from.

Stayed at W Austin for a weekend getaway! Hotel location was perfect spot and always clean! The employees are very good and personable. Susan H. was very plesant and assisted us for most of our visit. We will be going back in a few weeks to bother her again poolside!!!

Previously, in past years we always stayed at the sister Hilton Americas. We had a room with a view of Discovery Green, which was pretty cool and a front row seat to runners coming in for the finish! Can't beat that! I would recommend this property.

We chose the hotel after lengthy deliberations and many visits to the TA website. We were not disappointed.
The hotel is ideally situated within walking, if you like walking, distance to all the major buildings and museums in central Washington. We even walked to Arlington cemetery (which is across the river) after visiting the Lincoln memorial, although we did take the metro back.
It is a lovely experience, well decorated and furnished. The bed is one of the nicest and most comfortable we have found on our travels. The room was spacious as was the bathroom. I have no complaints. A little pricey perhaps but this is in the heart of the business area. Maybe the price is right and it is me that doesn't usually pay that sort of rate.

To be honest I wouldn't have noticed but she pointed out that, whilst they appeared clean to me, they had a film on that does appear in showers and needs constant attention to keep under control. She is fastidious and I would suggest most wouldn't know what she was talking about.
Three very comfortable nights, restaurants close at hand, metro also but get the legs going and enjoy the visit. We arranged to pick up hire car after our DC visit so as not to incur hire - parking charges for three days - nights that were not necessary.

We chose the Time because of its location and reasonable price, and we were not disappointed. Our King Room was clean and had more than what we have expected range of supplies such as cotton buds and sewing kit - quite exceptional quality at this price. The staff are very friendly. We found the remote control not working and a staff arrived promptly on our request for help. Hoping to have a glass of red we arrived at the restaurant on the ground floor when it was about to close for the day but the staff there welcomed us nonetheless. The Merlot and the Baby Amarone we had were both lovely.

The hotel was great! There is a free shuttle to downtown and the stockyards which runs until ---- though downtown is only a -- minute walk along a busy road so it felt perfectly safe! There are lots of resteraunt and bar choices.
The journey to the hotel was a bit long (no fault of the hotel!) but if you're using public transport check the trinity rail time first, we waited over an hour for a train as they are infrequent, also it is not clear but at the airport you need to get a shuttle to the car park and then anothe to Centerport station. It was cheap and the T and P station and INC are close to the hotel, and if you phone them they will come in the shuttle to collect you. Be aware that the service does not run on Sundays! We also used this service to visit Dallas for the day which is very easy.
Breakfast at the hotel was great, full of hot and cold choices and the hotel also gave free cookies throughout the day (a lovely, unexpected touch). We ate enough that we didn't need lunch.
Rooms were good, as you would expect for a holiday inn, nice big bed and a bathroom and fridge etc. the maids did a great job every day and as a kind bonus the hotel would provide toiletries that you had forgotten.
I would certainly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting fort worth!

The entire hotel just seems in need of a renovation.

You can walk to time square easily enough, its great for a base. All in all good hotel, nice rooms and good location.

Loved this hotel. From the second I walked thru the ultra cool and warm lobby, I knew this was going to be a good experience and I was not let down. small rooms, tiny bathrooms, bar that won't let you take your drink to your room all located in the heart of mid town. i now have a love-hate thing for them.

I'm a light sleeper and was able to sleep every night without earplugs. Such luxury! They even have a turndown service--with chocolates and flowers on the pillows and towels. I wondered if I needed to tip them to get the flowers and chocolates, so I didn't tip housekeeping one day, and sure enough, no chocolates or flowers. Still, I felt like I was on a luxury cruise.
Although this hotel is ranked only --diamonds by AAA, I really felt like I was staying at a --star facility. The only lack of luxury was the pool and the lack of a grand lobby, but I wasn't really worrying about that on this trip, since I came for business. The distance to the Galleria is walkable in good weather, but I'm sure I wouldn't want to be doing it on a hot, steamy Houston summer day.

Other than the doormen, which I'll discuss later, the entire staff was gracious and attentive. A special note goes out to Concierge Jay, who landed us a reservation at Lamb's Club on a Friday evening and who tried everything to grab a last minute single ticket to La Traviata at the Met.
The room was enviable by NYC standards, but less than stellar compared to other Ritz properties we've had the good fortune to visit. The housekeeping staff was very accomodating, even having a dress pressed for me at the last minute, when an opera ticket materialized.
The restaurant has no ambience at all and really seems more like an open lobby. The lunch we had was good though, with a nice variety of soups, sandwiches, and other dishes on the menu.
The gym on the --th floor has a nice round-up of equipment and a great view. My husband's meetings were all on the --th floor as well, and he enjoyed the view of the Statue of Liberty each day. He remarked that the food brought in was better than your average hotel business luncheon rubber chicken.
Location wise, I would only recommend staying here if you have business in the financial district, otherwise you are a $-- cab ride or - block walk and -- minute subway ride from all that NYC has to offer.
Now...the big downfall. I hate to sound pretentious, but when you're shelling out a certain amount of money for a certain type of hotel you have a certain expectation. In NYC, where even the small properties have doormen to assist with luggage, hail a cab, and greet you when you arrive, we certainly expected as much at a Ritz Carlton. Not so. Yes, there were - or - doormen. Yes, they hailed a cab for me at one point. However, they were never AT THE DOOR, but instead hanging by the front desk (where they couldn't see who was coming up the steps until they were already inside) or huddling in the luggage hold area. In fact, as the weather deteriorated, they were no where to be found. It may sound like a small smear for an otherwise good review, but the front door staff needs training at this Ritz property.

We had such a great time at the Westin! The rooms were perfectly appointed with a spacious and modern bathroom that included a separate bath tub. As with all other Westin hotels, the bed was incredibly comfortable and the room amenities were great. From the hotel, you can walk to the near foggy-bottom metro station or just walk to most tourist destinations. GW and Georgetown university are within walking distance as well. In all, I would highly recommend this hotel. The staff was super welcoming, Jeffry from the concierge desk was very knowledgeable, and location could not have been better.
ps: if you drive to the hotel, use valet parking as they provide in-and-out privileges. It's only $- more but it's well worth it.

Would I stay here again, ahem, not sure, but not likely!

I had the pleasure of staying here with my husband, who was in town on a business trip. The hotel is very unassuming from the exterior but stepping inside, it is gorgeous. The staff we encountered were very friendly. Our room was beautiful, with very mod decor and a great view of the city & the Hudson. The bathrooms were quite beautiful and spacious, which I was not expecting. We had dinner at PRINT the first night and it was quite delicious. The location of the hotel is amazing, just across the street from Balthazar restaurant (SOHO). The staff was extremely friendly and helpful with no exception. The room was a little small for the price I paid even with the outstanding service the price was still high!
I would defenitly go back to this hotel! And btw the bar food was amazing especially the tuna tartar and the veal chop, amazing! Yeah, and even the breakfast was very good.

I had to attend a meeting in Philly and needed a room near the airport for one night. The on-site airport hotel wanted more than $---, which was much more than I wanted to pay. All I needed was a place to sleep and prepare for my meeting. I investigated the other nearby options, and learned that a Microtel was just off the airport grounds. I reserved a room for $---night through an online booking service.
I have stayed at other Microtel hotels, and had a pretty good idea what to expect. Other reviews at Tripadvisor raised some concerns for me, but I decided to give it a try. The Microtel Philadelphia Airport is actually more than I expected, and it's still a great value.
First, you need to know the Microtel way. The hotels are simple designs with basic decorations. The rooms tend to be just large enough for the basics. The rates being charged are modest, so don't expect a fitness room, lavish breakfast and room service at midnight. You can expect a clean, comfortable room and a hotel staff that is courteous and helpful.
The floor coverings and wallpaper -- in the room and in the common areas -- were all in very good condition. While simple and somewhat neutral, they were pleasing and did not look cheap or gaudy.
The building is an equal-length L shape. My room faced into the L and the parking lot. One out-of-the-L side faces Bertram Rd., which is a major road. It's possible that there could be some traffic noise, but I don't know personally. He lobby is small, but clean. There is a moderately sized breakfast area that also has a desk with a computer for Internet access. I did not use the machine because I brought my own laptop. The vending machines and ice machine are just off the lobby.
My room measured --' by --' for the bed area, and -' by -' for the bathroom. There is a short entrance area (about -' by -') as well. This sounds small, but it's not cramped with a queen bed. Microtel hotels tend to follow the European room size idea. It's not a suite or a place to host a crowd. It's a bedroom, which is all I need. The room has an armoire to hang clothes, a desk area, night stands, and a window seat. There are two drawers and the air conditioner below the window seat. Overall, it's a very efficient use of the space. The window seat was actually a nice spot to sit in while I watched TV for a bit.
My room was a non-smoking room. Each time I entered the room, I smelled some kind of air freshener aroma. It was sort of a sweet lemon scent. It was a somewhat odd scent, but it only took a minute to get used to it.
There is wireless Internet access throughout the hotel. My room was at the end of the hallway, and the signal strength was very low. The connection speed was slower than typical high-speed access, and while the data rate was shown to be --Mb-s, I think the combination of other users and the low signal resulted in the slower connection. For basic e-mail and a few small file transfers, it was fine.
The free continental breakfast is the typical style at a budget hotel: juice, cold and hot cereal, bagels, muffins, coffee. The breakfast area was kept clean, despite the sloppy ways of many of the guests.
The hotel provides a free shuttle to and from the airport. When I landed, I called the hotel to request a pickup. I waited for -- minutes and the shuttle never arrived, so I called again. I was told that the shuttle was on the way. It arrived -- minutes later. I asked the driver (Chris) about the delay, and he said that he was never told about my first call. That's one strike against the staff, but it's the only strike I experienced. Later, I was able to arrange a ride to Ft. Miflin with the shuttle, which made up for the pickup error.
There are a Hampton Inn and a Fairfield Inn next door. The only restaurant in walking distance is a Ruby Tuesday. There is a Metro stop (Eastwick Station) a very short walk (five minutes) away. If the shuttle service is not to your liking, take the Metro to the airport. You can also take the Metro into downtown Philly. The Metro stop is a huge convenience for this hotel.
This is a much longer review than I normally write, but I feel that this hotel is a great value in a pretty good location. Some other reviews gave this hotel low marks, but I disagree. I rarely give a full - rating (I save that for truly outstanding experiences), so don't confuse my - rating as being a problem. Great hotel for the busy Business person. Yes the rooms are on the small side and very European, very clean, comfortable queen bed, from my experiance vey well maintained and surprisingly quiet. Location, location, location. 
After i have read the reviews, i decided to reserve to the amalfi chicago. First we came from the airport (Ohare) with the train city (-- min and -.--$ which in not expansive).

Madeleine from Montreal

people so helpful .and rooms perfect. and near to all transport .and restaurants
