I booked this hotel for my parents for last Friday and Saturday nights. I should let everyone know that I live in NYC and am very familiar with everything I am about to discuss. The hotel is in an excellent location in Midtown East and is just blocks from the Grand Central station and the subway. Hotel is a historic building that appears to have been recently renovated. Very nice lobby and attentive front desk staff who rapidly conducted check in. Room itself was an adequate size for NYC. The room was a little musty however and smelled of cigarettes (not a major deal breaker).
The problem is the L Q nightclub which is attached to the hotel. When we arrived on Friday evening there was already loud music blaring and vibrating from the club. This music could be clearly heard throughout the lobby and the vibrating was heard from the room on the -th floor. On Saturday around --pm (St Patrick's Day) there was a line of people wrapping around the hotel waiting to get into the club. Throughout Saturday the club’s music could be hear. Music was blaring all night long and there were NYPD officers on scene to help manage the club by nightfall.
It is completely unacceptable to have a club blaring music this loud. Even though this is NYC the city has noise regulations. There are inspectors from the City's Department of Environmental Protection who are brought out to investigate noise complaints. The local Community Boards are also brought in to register complaints along with elected officials. Upon check-out I did let the front desk staff know of the problem. I was told that the hotel is working on it and they recently brought in the NYPD to help. I do not think this problem will be resolved anytime soon considering the hotel appears to own the space occupied by the nightclub.
I regularly frequent bars and clubs throughout Manhattan and Brooklyn and nowadays it is extremely rare to find clubs blasting music this loud. 
Overall, I would choose another hotel until the club is brought under control.

Small room no way! I have a -ft - boyfriend who accompanied me on my latest business trip. I was very worried after reading the reviews here and was pleasantly surprised. The room was larger than expected, very clean, very nicely designed. It was very quiet. The bed was very comfortable. And there was nice desk space to work. So, the room was beautiful. But the hit of this hotel was its front-desk staff and a tall smiling gentleman who literally walked into the middle of the street, down a block or so, just to hail a cab for us. It was raining, the traffic was light but steady, and right out there was this guy going all out for me and my kids, who he didn't know from Adam. My kids were amazed at how dedicated he was. A great hotel.

The location of this hotel is very far from old town ,and many major attractions ,the air condition makes the room either very hot or very cold.

one receptionist have a very bad attitude and was not helping at all ,will surely avoid this hotel in the future.

This is fine if you're on business but being supposedly """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""on holiday"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I found it created an oppressive and almost hostile atmosphere. The bar and restaurant prices were high but within - minutes walk in any direction you can find good local bars with lots of atmosphere charging at least --% less than the hotel.
The hotel also lacked the range of facilities that you'd expect - in particular it does not have a pool.
My advice for anyone travelling independently is to avoid this hotel. Despite its reputation its not - star quality (deluxe rooms might scrape - stars). Some staff were unhelpful and abrupt and the Waldorf clearly relies on past reputation rather than current standards as justification for its prices.
One last thing that really bugged me was that so many of the people buzzing around were so utterly pretentious.
Bob Baker 
Alnwick, Northumberland.

Despite being connceted to the convention center, it is actually quiet and very secure. Service is sometimes impersonal and seldom stellar, but I believe that most staff works hard to serve the guests. I am not a Marriott rewards member and am not loyal to any particular hotel chain, so I do not expect any preferential treatment when I check in or stay at a hotel. It's not a boutique hotel, and you won't pay the premium for that service, either, but it does offer a good overall value, and if you adjust your expections and demands accordingly, you will likely have a good stay.

As a proud resident of Orange County, I absolutely HATE having to fly out of LAX. But once or twice per year I have a transcon or international flight schedule that forces me to use LAX instead of John Wayne. LAX is dirty, dingy, decayed, ugly, overcrowded and unglamorous (the fabulous Theme Building its only saving grace). To deal with the nightmare of LAX travel, I stay at a hotel near LAX the night before my flight and then in the morning I plug my nose as I make the mad dash from the hotel lobby to the door of the plane. 
I found the Custom Hotel by accident while looking at the usual ----'s corporate megahotels that line Century Blvd. The Custom is not on Century, but sits in a surprisingly safe and attractive neighborhood a bit north of Century. The transportation to and from LAX by the Custom Hotel was excellent; their shiny black Mercedes van picked me up at Terminal - within -- minutes of my call, and was waiting outside the lobby in the morning to whisk me back to LAX for my flight. The van driver and bellmen were efficient, although rather aloof in that way that most young bellmen are nowadays (busy talking about ballgames and girls and pretending not to work in the service industry). 
The check-in went well and quickly, and the lobby was sleek and clean. The room was fantastic, although the aging bones of this hotel show through in the hallways and elevators. The bed was comfortable, the linens were crisp and perfect, and the bathroom was superclean and well stocked with nice amenities. The WiFi was strong and reasonably fast (and free!), and the wall TV and bedside radio were of great quality. 
I ate dinner in the restaurant attached to the hotel, and it too was a pleasant surprise. Stylish mod and busy, I was expecting the usual dollop of West LA attitude that you'd find in a similar restaurant if it was in West Hollywood. Instead I found efficient and friendly service without attitude on a busy Saturday evening, and the food was very good. The bartender made a perfect Manhattan served beautifully. It appeared that the restaurant crowd was a mix of hotel guests, and locals stopping in for dinner or drinks, which is a good sign. I didn't use the pool, but it looked nicely presented. The pool and restaurant complex appear to be in a new facility built a few years ago next to the much older hotel building. 
Nice thing; there's a -- hour Ralph's supermarket right next door to the hotel in case you forgot anything.
I slept in and skipped breakfast in the lobby, but it looked like a number of folks were enjoying that offering as I left. One minor quibble (and really the only one); the high quality coffee machine in the room had powdered creamer instead of liquid creamer. I have stayed in plenty of boutique hotels that stock little pots of the liquid creamer instead of the old packets of powder. 
I checked out in -- seconds and rolled my suitcase out to the curb, where a waiting van was pulled up, my bag was loaded, and I was being driven back to LAX within - minutes. The drive to the airport entry takes about - minutes, and then you're up to the whims of internal LAX traffic to get to your specific terminal. I was able get from the Custom lobby to Terminal - in a hair under -- minutes at --:-- AM on an October Sunday. Your mileage may vary with the seasons and traffic, but the Custom operates an efficient and pleasant free shuttle service to battle LAX with. 
I will use the Custom Hotel again when my travel plans force me to fly out of LAX. It's a much more stylish, friendly and efficient hotel compared to the giant aging corporate hotels on Century Blvd. Bravo Custom Hotel, you nailed it on what an LAX hotel should offer its guests!

Check in: When I arrived, there was a long line at the front desk. no one used the convenient self check in terminals. Not sure why. Bypass the line! You can get your key from the machine, request a king size bed and enter your Hyatt old Passport number right there. If you want to interact with a person, be prepared to wait.
Room: OK. Flat screen TV, nice bed, great view of the city. The bathroom was a letdown. I still don't know why a hotel will pay thousands of dollars to build out a room and neglect fixtures in the bathroom and the physical plant. It took a long time to get hot water in the shower and this was a lazy Saturday. Not sure how bad it would be on a business day when everyone is getting int he shower between -:-- and -:-- AM. The pull for the shower was very stiff. You may need help if you have arthritis. 
Amenities: This is a full-service hotel, so they have everything and you have to pay for everything. Internet in the business center is not cheap nor is the in-room internet. Breakfast from room service costs a fortune. Save yourself money. Go down the street to a nice deli for breakfast. Many of them have an internet cafe as well.
Overall, it was a nice place. The staff was very friendly and helpful. At what i paid on Priceline, this was definitely a good value. Not sure I would pay $---+ per night for this place. For those prices, I think you have better options.

We were very impressed with the friendliness and helpfullness of all staff here at the Embassy Suites, Logan Airport, in Boston. From the parking attendants and front desk, to house keeping and cafeteria people, we felt very much at home during our entire stay. Our room was very clean, comfortable, and equipped with everything we needed. Plus, the location is wonderful, close to public transportaion and easy to get to downtown Boston for all of the historic sights to see!
Great location, wonderful staff and unlimited colonial charm. If you are looking for authentic Philadelphia - this is where you should stay

My wife and I just had the five course chef sampling. Each of the courses from the beet salad to the boar chop was superb. Maybe a bit salty but that may just reflect my own limited salt diet. Every dish really was a work of art with a wonderful array of tastes to match. The evening went so well from the valet parking ($-) to an enlightening conversation with one of the three sommeliers. It really is an excellent place to dine for a special occasion.

Very very noisy hotel – if you can ask not to be near the stairwell or facing main road as there is a lot of guests moving around the hotel very early & the traffic from the main road is also noisey. Rooms are spacious & clean but you can hear the people in the room next to you. The free & secure parking is a bonus as is the free continental breakfast that you receive but it does tend to get eaten quite early. Overall an ok hotel in an ok location. Within walking distance of the main attractions if you don’t mind walking ----- mins.

Stayed at this hotel in March-April for spring break with my - & - year olds. On Priceline, I paid $---night for this hotel. I found this to be a great deal as it is a great location and a comfortable hotel. The hotel is a - minute walk from Union Square and several methods of transportation. Many restaurants and shops close by too. Fitness center costs $--, but it is worth it is you want a good workout. The outdoor pool is average. Note that the wind can blow very strong at the pool-hot tub. Beds are comfy; restroom is small but manageable. 
Note that Dollar, Thrifty and Avis car rental agencies are directly across the street from the hotel. You need to search under O'Farrell Street to find the location.

We had stayed at the Warwick mostly because of its central location (in the heart of downtown and close to Qwest field), and figured with its reasonable price and free shuttle - why not try it? Even before we had arrived at the hotel we received great customer service! Well, we were lost (google directions weren't very good) and it was dark, so we called the hotel and the lady who answered the phone stayed with us on the phone directing us to the hotel until we dropped our car off with the valet. The parking may be pricey, but the free shuttle service the hotel has, more than made up for the cost! Also, because we were in downtown we walked to Macy's, Bed Bath & Beyond and to the mall. The restaurant in the hotel was very good! But a tip - make reservations for Sunday brunch because it gets quite busy. The service was great, the rooms were very comfortable and clean. The water pressure was lacking but that was the only con during the whole trip. We had a paper delivered to our door every morning...what can I say except that we have already booked another trip to Seattle this November and we are of course staying at the Warwick again!

This hotel was like a cross between a nightclub and a college dorm. All of the lighting in the hotel was either fluorescent or neon, walls painted black, club music pumping ----- hence, the comparison to a nightclub. The actual room we stayed in truly looked like a dorm room w- a king sized bed. Furniture was sparse and not well made, with the exception of the bed which was quite comfortable. The bathroom was tiny w- a shower only, a shower which was not enclosed I might add, which led to a wet, messy bathroom floor. WIth the W, I expected minimalistic but serene luxury. Needless to say, I was quite disappointed w- this location.

I stayed in the tower and had a nice room with a view of the pool. The hotel was extremely busy with events in the conference center and parking was a bit of a challenge during the day, however, when we returned from Sea World at night we had no problem finding parking.
The hotel has numerous restaurants and pools which my family enjoyed. We enjoyed walking to the mall and golf course.

The Nine Zero has a great location, nice view, and an interesting contemporary decor. We got a clean and spacious corner room (---). They offer a happy hour with surprisingly pretty good wine @ -pm. The room temperature did not go lower than -- even though the thermostat would go down to --. My guess is that the a-c does not have the adequate capacity for the room. Bed and pillows are fine (could be better), perhaps is about time to get new ones. Not too bad but if you want a cool room to sleep this particular one would not do it. We had breakfast at their restaurant one morning and the food was simply ok. Spent $-- for breakfast for ONE person including tax and tip! We did not have a car so did not have to worry about parking. If you are thinking about renting a car in Boston, think again, it is almost impossible to find a parking spot without paying a fortune. I would definitely stay here again and skip their restaurant.

Our stay at the hotel was was enhanced by the friendly and knowledgeable staff.
Especially the concierge personnel. There help made our trip as comfortable and problem free for getting directions to the airport, to arranging rental cars, to finding museums, as you could ask. The hotel desk staff also gets a plus rating for their helpful service. They were quick on the assist to give me a training lesson on how to print my airline boarding pass(-) at the hotel kiosk. By doing so they saved me a bunch of time at the airport terminal to do shopping and reading and relaxing prior to my flight.

We stayed here on our way down to San Diego. The bed was literally - inches off the floor so it was hard to get out of. The TV was in an awkward place for watching unless you were laying across the bed. There was no in-room coffee maker which is standard in ANY other hotel we've stayed at in the past. There was no closet to hang our clothes, rather a clothes rack. The furnishings were scarce with only one uncomfortable chair and an ottoman available. The entry way was a dark dismal gray. The light switch to the bathroom was behind the door which is inconvenient as well as a possible danger since that means it was next to the shower. The sink backed up and leaked from the underside. Breakfast was available at a cost of $-- for an omlet and $- or so for coffee. We went down the street to a great little coffee shop and had breakfast. We also noticed that the Fire Alarms were out of order. A pool was available but it was very small. There was Valet only parking. The valet guys were very nice and helpful however, when we complained about not having a free breakfast which most any upper end hotels have as well as the coffee maker, the woman at the desk acted as though she had never heard of such a thing. We would NOT recommend this hotel to anyone. The people nice but beyond that, NOT!

I booked a stay here for a team I manage in July ----. We had quite a bit of trouble with the reservation, made worse by the manager barely speaking English. 
Upon check in, my company's card was declined. They refused to allow my athletes to check in. I was not physically present, and frantic to let my athletes check in, I gave them my personal card information. Even with that, they weren't going to let them check in until I faxed in the authorization paperwork, which I could not do because I was in the car on the way to the airport! 
Fortunately, one of the athletes just paid for it on his card and we reimbursed him. Problem solved. I thought. 
- months later, I am very surprised to check the online statement for my personal account and find a nearly $-,--- charge from this hotel dated January --!!
I call the hotel, and give them my info. They called me back about a half hour later and said it was all a mistake and that they would issue a refund. They said they are under new management and that when they were reviewing old paperwork, somehow my account got charged. 
Of course the refund takes time to process, so $-,--- of my money is tied up for at least a week, if not longer! 
I am very disturbed that they still had my personal account information, when authorization paperwork was never filled out for it, and that they would just put a giant charge on it - months later without even attempting to contact anyone from my organization first. 
I now have Days Inn headquarters and my bank's fraud division on the case, but the fact that this happened at all is extremely upsetting. 
The good news is that this hotel appears to have a new manager that appears to speak English. The bad news is that they appear to have no qualms about placing unauthorized charges on accounts from stays - months prior.

Make no mistake, although I am giving this hotel four stars, this is not a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""five-star"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" or """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""four-star"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel. But, this hotel is definitely a cut above other - and --star facilities. This hotel is the third or fourth oldest in Mission Valley, according to the manager. Built around ----, its decor is dated, but that is also what gives this venue its charm. More importantly, the rooms are very clean and the staff is exceptionally dedicated to providing its customers with friendly service. We were initially assigned a room in one of the attached buildings. However, the room had a musty odor (possibly due to recent flooding following unusually heavy rains) and was cramped for our family of three. For an additional $---night we were able to have a room in the main building, which one enters from the inside. (Rooms in the attached buildings are entered directly from outdoors.) This made a huge difference, particularly since it was cool and rainy during much of our stay. Due to special dietary needs, we did not eat in the restaurants, but, for an extra $--day, we were able to have a refrigerator in the room, which was larger than the usual cube-sized models. The beds were comfortably firm (no significant sagging) and the shower was outstanding. However, this is not a fancy hotel: there are few electrical outlets in the rooms; there is no counter in the bathrooms in the main building on which to place toiletries, and there is no elevator to the second floor. The toilet is an old-style, slow-flush, which often requires two or three flushes to remove paper. Still, for the price paid, these are minor inconveniences. Staff at the reservation desk offered to carry luggage up the steps for me (not needed) and were as knowledgeable as any concierge about how to get to local venues. If you are intent on finding a plush hotel you should look elsewhere; but if you would like to save your money for sightseeing and dining, a clean, comfortable hotel, with a friendly staff, without having to pay high rates, this hotel is the place to go. There is also free Wi-Fi in all of the rooms. Despite not being a true """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""four-star"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel, I rate the hotel at this level because of the great value for the price paid.

We chose this hotel because of its proximity to Seattle Center (where the Space Needle, Experience Music Project, and other attractions are located) and its very reasonable prices. For about $-- we had a first-floor room with a queen-sized bed and separate small kitchen complete with a stove, refrigerator, microwave, and sitting area. The hotel is on multiple bus lines, and lies within the commercial area of Lower Queen Anne with its numerous shops, restaurants, and two full-service supermarkets within easy walking distance.
Our room was a little worn, but clean and adequate for our purposes. We stayed just one night, but had we stayed longer we would have asked to be moved to another room farther from the front desk, which was only a few steps from our door, and seemed to have a steady stream of business all night, complete with loud voices and a slamming front door. Street noise wasn't really that noticeable.
I would recommend staying here even if your focus is on other parts of Seattle, given the great transit access and wide choice of restaurants in the area.

My partner and I stayed in a suite, which wasn't the greatest, and the service was horrible. The people working at the front desk were mean and rude. I thought that it might just be one person who was having a bad day, but it was every person I came across. I didn't ask for anything out of the ordinary, just questions over the phone when I arrived, but they reacted like they really were inconvenienced if they helped me, so you know how that came across. 
The last straw was when I asked them to actually do something, which was to fix the fireplace, well they simply wouldn't. At that point I finally got upset over their service and confronted them on it, which is when they were apologetic and accomodating and immediately sent someone to fix the fireplace. So they knew they were in the wrong the whole time, but wasn't going to do anything about it until someone said something.
As convenient as they are, I would rather stay somewhere further, than put up w- them. I've never experienced anything like it before at any place I've stayed.

Not super fancy, but just right. Great views, great location and great complimentary breakfast. Like others have said, not just your typical cereal and muffins. We had a wonderful time and really enjoyed our stay.

The only good thing I could say about this hotel was our check in and out was hassle free, plus the shuttle to the terminal is fast. The only reason we stayed here was for an early flight (check out my other review for preferred place to stay in LA). Opening the door to our room was going through a time warp into a tired motel from decades long gone. The bed (a small double not a queen!) was disappointing. The TV was ancient. Bathroom was small and poorly equipped (just two towels). The aircon-heater was incredibly noisy and I just ran it while showering before bed - it would have been impossible to sleep with it on. As we'd arrived late and only had about - hours to sleep before our flight I didn't want to waste time asking for a better room. The view from our upper-level room would have been good (of the runways) if it wasn't for a dodgy tinting film that was bubbling and peeling. No aircraft noise, external sound insulation good.

this hotel was amazing great location lots to do...great staff....the rooms were always cleaned..we had - guys for a trip to the yankees game and they gave us - cots for the room plus we had a doubble bed and pullout couch....also had our own kitchen. times square is just minutes away ...Hooters accross the street and oh ya the blue jays won.....YANKEES SUCK....

Just a few words to sum up our stay:
good service... quick check in... flavored waters available in lobby... good breakfast... Swans to entertain the children.... great location... can walk to the Galleria and a few restaurants.
One observation.
We've stayed a quite a few ES. This king suite is separated from the bathroom. Therefore, when the kids are sleeping in the living area you must open your door to get to the bathroom. This disturbed our daughter and she would wake up. Not a big deal and I'll stay at this location again but for parents with small kids just be prepared.

Please take my advice and stay away from this awful motel. Unpleasent neigbourhood and even worse motel. The staff steal whatever you forget out in the open in your room (I lost a piece of jewelry) and when trying to get some help from the manager with this matter he told me to get lost! You will be much better of at any other place in the area, there are many options nearby, closer to the airport.

We were having carpet put in our home, so my husband suggested I go to a hotel with our eight-yr-old daughter. We chose Aloft Ballantyne because of location, and I wanted to see what it was about. We got a great rate of $--, so I wasn't expecting much. However, I was pleasantly surprised! If you do your homework, you will see the hotel is a limited-service hotel, so there is no room service, valet parking, etc. However, they do what they do very well. We walked inat --:--pm and were promptly greeted by a gentleman named Trent working the front desk. He gave us our and told us the hotel had to offer: breakfast in the lobby from -am to --am (not included in the rate, but not expensive either), an indoor pool, ---hr lobby market, etc...and he gave us a list of local restaurants that would deliver if we so desired. Kudos to Trent for making a great first impression. When we got to our room, we discovered it wasn't particularly spacious, but it had all the basics. The bed was wonderfully comfortable, and the shower was great too. The towels were of good quality. In fact, we have no complaints! We went downstairs for the hot breakfast, and the pancakes and bacon were delicious. Props to Chef Craig on making my very picky --yr-old happy! We are accustomed to five-star hotels, but we were happy to stay at Aloft Ballantyne for the night! We were comfortable, safe and in a great location for the Ballantyne area. If you want to be near uptown or even Southpark, this is not the place for you, but if your focus is south Charlotte or Ballantyne, you will be comfortable here. If you want extra luxuries, go to the Ballantyne Hotel, but if you want value and comfort, the Aloft Ballantyne is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! Thanks to the management for running a comfortable hotel with a friendly, efficient staff.

This hotel is located closer to the garment district and Koreatown than it is to Chelsea, but nevertheless it's at a decent location - a couple of blocks away from a number of subway lines. For a Saturday check-in we were able to get an early check-in at -- in the morning. The front desk people were very polite and professional, the bellhops were also good. The size of the room was acceptable. There is a gym on the lower level which isn't huge but does the job. It's equipped with towels and water bottles.
We had breakfast there the next day, included in the reservation I made using my Hilton points. Omelettes, waffles, and a couple of other things were cooked to order. Service there was good too...so overall a good stay.

Helpful staff, good internet connection. Geat sized beds, nice bathroom except for faulty bath plug and couldnt have a bath only a shower. Breakfasts were light and adequate and parking was very handy indeed for Frisco. Great location, easy walk to Pier -- and some useful restaurants about. All in all a fab place and will be going back soon.

DO NOT STAY HERE! This place was the second worst hotel that I've been in my entire life. The place is filthy, unkempt, has cracking paint everywhere, por lighting and disgusting carpet in the lobby, elevators, hallways, and rooms!
I felt like I was in a Stephan King movie and was waiting for insects to be seen which I didn't. 
You would think that a place this big right accross from Madison Square Garden would be decent but it's really disgusting.
However, the staff were quite nice and the steak restaurant in the back of the hotel was pretty good.

We stayed here on a weekend trip with family. We needed three adjoining rooms (children in party) which they would not guarantee when we booked the rooms, but I found out that this is standard (if irritating) with virtually all chains. At check-in they were very accommodating and we got the rooms we needed. My family (two adults, two kids) had a suite which was great--plenty of room, clean and reasonable privacy. My in-laws had one double-double room and one king room and I thought they seemed a little cramped. For $----- more go for the suite! Amenities: Good a-c, it was a little iffy on maintaining a constant temperature, but was not noisy. Towels were too small, and rough and not very absorbent. Indoor pool was small but great for kids--pool area was very clean and always well-equipped with towels. Breakfast was fine: the usual waffles, yogurt, bagels, etc. They actually had protein which was a plus and very good coffee. Location is very convenient to -- and Sam Cooper. About ----- minutes to Beale St. area on Sam Cooper. The area was a little rundown in parts, but I did not feel unsafe. I like being downtown but you get more for your money here.

Cheap and cheerful but exceeded my expectations. The most important thing was that the room and bathroom were absolutely spotless. The bathroom was quite luxurious for a cheap hotel. Breakfast was included which amounted to croissants, rolls, muffins, tea-coffee. You had to get down early if you wanted a croissant; they disappeared fast. An unexpected bonus was a safe in the room and a fridge. There were two computers with free internet access. Staff were friendly and helpful. The only gripe I have was that the air conditioner was very noisy and we had to turn it off for sleeping. We also had a meal (at --% off for hotel guests) in the restaurant downstairs. No complaints about the food or service but it was VERY, VERY expensive. I would have no hesitation in using this hotel again and can thoroughly recommend it.

bar service was extremely slow, staff not too friendly, food was very good, room was nice but bathroom was dirty with hair on floor in several places...easy fixes! hotel was a very good hotel, wish the bed was taller, softer, bedding was very good.

Hotel is fine ... regular Hilton, there are a couple of delis somewhere around the street and a delicious restaurant next door, that's a plus. But If you want to get to know San Diego's best areas you have two options, one is take a cab, fare is high though, each way $---$--. The other option which I wish I thought about sooner, is to rent a bike so you can go back and forth strolling along San Diego bay. This is a very quiet hotel, is a safe and nice waterfront hotel.

Having just had a very disappointing stay at the Palomar in Chicago, we were expecting the worst and were pleasantly surprised. Staff attitudes were very friendly and helpful (unlike in Chicago) and even when very erratic housekeeping was reported, problems were always quickly and efficiently resolved. We loved the treats for guests - like a refreshing afternoon drink with pretzels and the wine receptions. The location couldn't have been better.

We found that booking through the hotel directly rather than using an online service worked the best. We needed handicap accessible room(s) and we were very pleased with what we were given. All the employees were very friendly and helpful to answer any questions we had. Our stay was a very enjoyable experience. We weren't right in the middle of downtown but it was a good location with plenty of free parking.

This was the most expensive place we stayed on our trip, and it was the least impressive. The fancy Marriotts that we stayed at in DC, in New Orleans, and in NC were cheaper and far, far nicer.
The staff here was friendly (well, not super friendly, but not rude either), the room was fairly clean, and the breakfast was so-so. I don't have any complaints except for the price for what you get. We would not stay here again.

I've stayed at Hawthorns before for extended periods. This time I was just in town for the weekend to see the Quarter Horse Congress, but the other Hawthorn I stayed at was nice. This one was average. The decor looked like somebody had a good idea and then cheaped out (frayed carpet & aged looking bedding). The web site really made it look nice but in the end I'm not sure it was the same hotel in the pictures. The staff didn't seem to genuinely care about us, and I understand how hard it is to fake enthusiasm for strangers, But still, at least try! For the price I paid, I feel ripped off. Next time I'll look around as there are quite a few other hotels in the area.

My daughter and I spent two nights in the hotel and would return in a heartbeat. The hotel is clean and the view of the Empire State building is outstanding! The staff is excellent. Especially, Irene at the front desk, who answered all of our questions, gave terrific suggestions and was friendly and helpful at all hours. Mikael worked hard to deliver our bags and anything else we requested. Thank you to both for making our stay stress-free!

My husband had to attend a seminar for work. The travel agency put him in this hotel. The pictures on the web look beautiful. What they don't tell you is they are remodeling and their working hours start at -am and don't stop sometimes until -pm. There is no need to set an alarm if you have to someplace by -am the noise will wake you up before your alarm. The bathroom in the room was terrible and our view of the grounds was over the dumpsters. I wouldn't plan on staying at this hotel for at least - to - months. What a nightmare.

This Hampton lives up to the brand. Clean, updated and had very friendly staff. It is conveniently located right off the interstate, near MANY restaurants and several shopping areas. Brenda at the front desk and Cara in the breakfast room were standouts for their friendliness, good humor and efficiency. Breakfast area was busy but was continually restocked and kept clean. The pool-hot tub area was nice and the equipment in the fitness center was in good working order. The street address for the property did not register with our gps but mapquest found it. It is located in a newish office complex, right off the interstate - look for the Polaris Road exit.

What a great stay!! The hotel was clean, friendly and in the perfect location.
The staff was very helpful and always ready to help. We traveled with our - children, - & -, and the staff made them feel like kings!!
We had a - bedroom king suite, and it was spacious so we could put the children to bed and enjoy quiet time. The only downside was the pullout sofa, it needs a better mattress, we put it on the floor. A European style breakfast was included and very good, but if you grew tired of it there were many restaurants within steps of the front door to satisfy you. The Orchard Hotel was a fantastic hotel in the perfect location to step on a cable car, get to work, sight see or go out on the town. Thank you!

This convention used to be held at the Hyatt Regency in Dallas and we liked the change. The room was a little more, but the parking was less. The rooms were tasteful and good sized. The bathroom had all the amenities, including a plush robe and towels. The pool area (we could see it from the room) was a basic rectangle, but had nice padded lounge chairs and - cabanas. The room had a great city view. The TV included a movie channel and hook-ups for peripherals. We only ate at Peets coffee in the afternoon, but it was a good deal for a drink, chips and a pretty stuffed sandwich (could barely get my mouth around it). We upgrade to the club level and were very pleased with the extra amenities and the helpful attendants. The check-in and out were speedy and the desk staff was pleasant. The hotel is in a good downtown location with Dart trains outside the door, restaurants and the arts district about - blocks away.

This hotel is old and our room could have been cleaner. The air conditioner didn't work the first two days and it was about --- outside. The hallway was cooler than our room! Our room also had a strong odor, which might have been from whatever cleaner was used. Whoever cleaned our room had long dark hair since I kept finding it in the bathtub and on the bathroom floor. 
Our room was small and looked out onto an alley. The wardrobe for clothing was very small and I wasn't able to hang dresses in it since there was a safe bolted to the bottom of the wardrobe. 
The hotel is close to many things and you can easily walk to the convention center, drug stores and places to eat. There's a metro stop near the convention center. I had to walk through a few blocks that didn't look so great to get to the convention center.
They offered breakfast every day, which was nice. They provided coffee-tea-hot water, hard boiled eggs, milk and yogurt, bread-bagels-muffins-doughnuts, milk, cereal and oatmeal. There was fruit only one day. There was always coffee in the lobby and fresh hot cookies were available in the evenings.
Their exercise room was two pieces of machinery right off the lobby--no privacy. 
The hotel provides free Internet access, which was easy to use and I had no problems. 
The entrance is up a flight of stairs, which isn't ideal when you're carrying luggage. No one from the hotel helped anyone carry their bags up or down the stairs. 
Most of the staff were friendly and helpful with a few exceptions. When I arrived, I was told I couldn't check in for a number of hours and was told to put my luggage in an unlocked closet in the lobby. The closet was near the entrance which is on a busy street. I also had to retrieve my luggage later. 
Most of the people at the desk in the lobby were friendly and helpful and gave good directions and suggestions. The person at the desk when I checked out was rude and not helpful. He gave me a receipt with my colleague's name on it and it showed her charge history, and he refused to change it to reflect the days I stayed there and the charges to my credit card. He was also in a dispute with another customer while I was trying to check out, and left my credit card on the counter! He didn't physically hand it back to me or even say anything. I could have easily lost my credit card since I was checking out and on my way to Union Station.

The Renaissance lobby was ok. After that there wasn't a lot very positive to say. The room was in bad shape. Everything looked as though the hotel has been used hard. Ok, it is an airport hotel, but I would still look somewhere else if you have a chance. The fitness center had decent machines, but they were all filled by -:--am.
I stayed there two long days. I won't stay there again. Please note that there was nothing all that hateful about the place. The service I did get was uninspired, but no one did a particularly bad job.

We had a corner room on a high floor. It is worth asking for an upgrade, as one of their customer service agents on property helped make sure we had the best room in the category we had reserved. I'm not sure if the whole property is suites, but we had a living room, with wet bar, and bedroom. This was great as while we spent most of our time out touring, with all the walking, it was nice to have a place to come back to relax that had more than a bed as an option. We had breakfast every morning, as part of our deal, which was great with plenty of options including made to order omelets, fresh fruit, cereal, numerous meats and cheeses, etc. We also had pre-ordered some sparkling wine and chocolate covered strawberries for our arrival. We ended up having to move them to the next night as our flight was very late. I appreciate the staff working with me to accomplish this when I called from the airport to say we would not make it in at our scheduled time.

Ok priced for location (nice enough -- min walk from Union Square) but let down by a poor view from the room we had (on inside of building overlooking room opposite). Well sized room though and decent bathroom. Hotel receptionists very friendly and helpful. Let down by a very poor self service buffet breakfast in a couple of very random conference rooms.

Myself, my wife, and -yr old son stayed - nights at the Crowne Plaza March --th and --th. The hotel staff were very nice and helpful with any questions we had. The hotel was very clean, as well was the room. The room we stayed in had two double beds and was more spacious than other chain hotels we have stayed at. We would have liked the hotel to have been closer to the Trolley line though, it was a short hike to the neighboring Marriot hotel for us to catch the Trolley to go downtown. By all means, use the Trolley, it only costs $- per person (have some dollar bills handy, the machine don't give change) , compared to other means it is a steal and is quite a nostalgic expierience. The hotel security was very sufficient, parking your car behind the hotel costs $-- per day w-unlimited access in-out , at night there is a guard shack at the entrance with a guard that patrols the lot all night. This is a - star hotel and I didn't feel pressured to have to tip anyone, although I didn't ask for help with anything, I was offered help but didn't need any. Check-in was fast and check-out was even faster. 
The only negatives I can say about our stay is; The lighting in the room- could have been more lights, it was very dim with all the lights on, The desk in the room needed some assistance with its legs, they needed tightening really bad, table wobbled around when using our laptop. Location to Trolley line access.

We stayed at the Millenium Hilton from July ---th.... Paid $--- with - free breakfast buffett coupons per day as a part of their BounceBack deal that I booked directly from their website. This hotel was great. We had access to all the major attractions. My daughter's group were treated fairly good during the trip. The only problem was that some of the businesses were closed for the Thanksgivihg holiday. We made up with shopping on Black Friday down the Magnificent Mile.

I booked this hotel for a - night stay on ---------- on the Sheraton website one month ahead. The reason I booked this hotel is the reviews about their comfortable beds. My wife and I just came back from our trip to New York to see our family. We have family on the Upper East Side and Soho, so we wanted to be somewhere in between and the Sheraton hit all of our wants. We checked in minutes after arriving around - pm on Sat. Nov. -- with Warren - he was extremely professional, yet accommodating. I had requested a nice room on a high floor and he said ---- was available. Best of all, he said that there were express elevators to floors ----- (I think it was these floors) which were one hallway away from the elevators to the other floors.
When we got to the room, the bed was folded up and the room looked like it would be appropriate for a business meeting, but was a good size. So, I thought the room size was probably on par, if not slightly bigger, than other rooms in Manhattan, so I was pleasantly surprised at the size once we had made the adjustments. Warren had mentioned that he wanted more space so he folded the bed up every day, but we just left it as is our whole trip and it was fine.
Our view was okay, not the best, but not like when we stayed at the Warwick (we basically faced a wall, so the view sucked). This time around, we had a decent view of Times Square - if we were - floors above, our view would've been great, as there was another building clipping the complete view. The view from the other side (corner unit, remember?) was decent as it wasn't directly facing a building, but the open street. 
The room was great as it was newly renovated - everything seemed new and even had that new smell. The bathroom was nicely done - the only complaint was that the shower head didn't have enough water pressure - I suspect it was a low flow shower head as the tub faucet's pressure was tremendous. The only other complaint in the room was that there was definitely a draft of cold air from the windows. I made sure that they were all shut properly (which they were), but there was still a slight cold breeze when the heat wasn't on. I called for maintenance and they came up rather quickly to fix it (another plus!), but it didn't seem to change anything... probably just a fact of life when you're on the -- floor in -- degree weather. Oh well, it wasn't a big deal as I blocked the wind from my wife when we were in bed.
All in all, I would rate this hotel a -, but I forgot to mention one other thing. Shortly after arriving in the room, someone knocked on the neighbor's door and then eventually ours. He said it was room service, but I insisted we hadn't ordered anything. Then he said it was service from the hotel and proceeded to place a wonderful cheese plate and complementary wine on the table. I'm guessing it was sent by Warren on behalf of the hotel for our -- year anniversary. Warren is the MAN! Anyway, that type of special service more than makes up for all of the little minor complaints I could bring up (oh yeah, Wi-fi was $---day - kinda sucks, but oh well). I say stay here as the price was great and the service was excellent!
One last thing: definitely order from Carnegie Deli down the street - they delivered their famous Pastrami Sandwich hot and ready to eat. Just don't order any chicken breast - too dry and not worth it.
The location is good, the price is good if you book this hotel earlier. The double room is a bit small but good quality. The staff are very friendly.

This hotel was PERFECT! My boyfriend and I stayed here for our first trip to Austin. The location could not have been any better. We found our stay at the Hotel Harrington to be surpisingly pleasant and convenient. Just realised by looking through reviews I had never left mine. Stayed here in March -- at the St Patricks weekend. My husband, my ---year old daughter and myself stayed at the Jewell for - nights and overall I think this is a great hotel, especially since we booked very early and got a fantastic price. The rooms are very modern and have nice touches such as an Iphone doc. There were a few little issues that I thought I would point out with the one-bedroom suite. One is that the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""bedroom"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is separated from the rest of the room but a sliding door that doesn't completely close off so there isn't total privacy (if that's an issue for you). Also, the door is make of an opaque glass as is the door to the bathroom so when my husband had to get up early for his meetings, this meant light went straight from the bathroom to the bedroom. My husband and I stayed at the Sherry for two weeks and I wanted this “hotel” to be excellent as per the ratings on TA. We had just come from two weeks at The Greenwich Hotel in Tribeca which was fantastic.
The ONLY reason this did not get a poorer rating is that the building is in a convenient location, this was a reason we choose not to move. You are right opposite Central Park with the horse and carriages and in short walking distance to all the main Fifth Avenue shops. Other positives were; spacious bedroom, heaps of wardrobe space, free wifi, free sodas that were refilled every day, comfy bed, plenty of bathroom amenities, choice of newspaper, heaps of TV channels and a coffee machine. Godiva chocolates were placed on our pillow at night, which you do not see often nowadays. There were a lot of old world touches.
Rather than give you two weeks of examples of the poor service we received, I will list just a few, remembering we are paying $---+ per night, it was $--- and then you add all the taxes. Before I start with the negatives, the reason for my heading is that Sherry lacks a lot of services that a hotel has, for example, there is no lounge to go sit in, read and watch the world go by. There is no casual area to have a coffee or snack, just a small lobby with a couple of chairs so if you are staying here for any length of time, you are stuck in your room. There is no pool to go sit by. A previous reviewer stated that their stay was “odd” and now I understand why. For two weeks I was able to watch how the staff treat the hotel guests versus the residents of the building and it is very different, in fact, we felt like we were imposing and intruding, we did not feel like hotel guests. The concierge’s were polite but they had this underlying tone and attitude. 
So we arrive at the Sherry and are greeted by Alvin who collects our bags. We are checked in by the concierge and given a nice welcome until she looks at my passport photo and tells me how much I have aged. Now I just laughed it off, however upon reflection, this lady did not know me and is that appropriate behaviour from a five star hotel? Or maybe it is not a five star hotel, it is a residential building and she became too familiar with us?
Alvin takes us up to our room and we step out to renovations occurring on the second floor, which is where our room is. The concierge forgot to inform us of this when checking in. Alvin points out that the Business Centre is closed for renovation and lucky for us they have relocated it right next door to our room. Alvin shows us our room, we tip him and he stated that he is a native New Yorker and if we need anything he is around – we never saw Alvin again until check out two weeks later when he picked up our bags. There was a box of Godiva chocolates and flowers welcoming us. There were also two notes from the management. Both notes had different and incorrect spellings of my name. My booking was made by my travel agent so they had all the details – oh and my surname, only has four letters and my Christian name is also very easy. 
I wondered about the renovations going on but at that time (it was about -pm in the afternoon on a weekday) we could not hear any noise, so unpacked and settled in. We were happy. In fact, during the whole two week stay we did not actually hear much of the renovation going on, it is what woke us up each morning. As stated above, there was board on the floor in the hall way stuck together by masking tape. Each night it was removed and every morning (weekday) it was re-laid. So between -.-- – -.--am you would hear the ripping of masking tape and while doing this the person laying the board would have a very loud conversation with the housekeeping staff or other tradesmen, right near our room. So rather than wake up naturally, without fail we were woken by the staff of the “hotel”. There were mornings on the weekend when I woke up to the housekeeping staff calling out to bring more towels or for a staff member calling for security on her walkie talkie. My tip to the Sherry, if your guest has the “do not disturb” sign up and the paper is still outside their door it indicates they are still asleep.
The bathroom – it was small. However, we had a bath, great I thought! Then I looked at the bottom of it, the non-slip surface was fifty shades of grey, there was no way I was sitting on that. It needed to be replaced or given a damn good bleach.
This leads me into housekeeping, extremely inconsistent. If a hotel is renovating and it expects its guests to stay within the area during this phase then the housekeeping needs to be vigilant with keeping building dust to a minimum. After about four days I noticed the build up of dust. It is important to note here that there was a lot of drawers and wardrobe space so we did not leave a lot of personal items out on the side cabinets or tables. The housekeeping did not have to move any personal items to dust. By day five I was able to write words into the dust, I wrote “hello” on the TV stand and it still did not get cleaned. Day seven it did, only because I happened to be in the room at the time. I am not sure if the bathroom got cleaned, as there was a pubic hair on the daddo by the toilet and stayed there for the full two weeks with all the dust.
Now there are plenty more examples to provide but the piece de resistance was room service. We had been eating in a lot of restaurants and decided to stay in one night. I said to my husband all I feel like is a toasted cheese sandwich. He rings room service and orders one each. We get our order – two plates with covers. First thing we notice, only one glass of water, we laugh. Then we lift the lid and were shocked. The toasted sandwich was that, a cheese toasted sandwich. Not what you expect from a five star kitchen: there was no parsley for decoration, no fries, no salad just plain crappy white bread with plastic cheese and the crusts cut off and it was very dry (took a photo of it). Now you are probably saying, yeah, that is what you wanted. Yes but guess what we paid when I asked my husband what the amount was on the bill - $--.-- for two toasted sandwiches and one glass of water. I would not have minded if we got some fries and salad with that. In all my travels and I have been travelling most of my life that would go down as the worst hotel dish I have seen and the biggest RIP OFF! By the way, based on this dish we did not even want to waste our time and money going to the restaurant. 
My tip if you are staying at the Sherry, go around corner to the deli we got beautiful sushi (spicy crab) for $-.--. Also for the international visitors who may not know, you can take your washing to a dry cleaner and they do it for you, usually one pound of clothing costs about $-.--. We had -- items of clothing washed and it cost $--.
BY the way I was happy to put all of this into a customer satisfaction feedback form but there was not one in our room. So with this experience in mind, go to a proper hotel, a place that provides the amenities a hotel of five star standard should. We certainly noticed the difference when we checked in at the Peninsula in Beverly Hills after staying at the Sherry – now there is a hotel! Oh and I checked what they charged for a toasted cheese sandwich - $-- but you got ham with that and tomato soup plus a bread basket and two glasses of water.
I will say that Fernando, the doorman was extremely polite and very helpful.

Got via Hotwire for around $--- so not too bad value. Once upon a time it would have been a fancy place, now it is somewhat faded and in need of a revamp. We will book here again for next year, but will try for a two queen size beds.

The place is old.Needs a new lift for sure.The rooms are ok but i had a noisy room facing the street.Disturbes your sleep.Its more planned for a group stay and hostel rather than a single private hotel room.Below average breakfast.Only advantage is if you visit union square its right there.

Wonderful surroundings, clean lobby, rooms and friendly staff. A GREAT value for your money. Love the new """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""quick check out"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Southern hospitality greets you as you enter the lobby. Everyone is cheerful and helpful.

This is a great hotel, provided you shop around for your rate! Through Booking.com I found great rate on a deluxe park view room, at a price that was more than --% cheaper than what the hotel's site was charging for a non-view room! The very best thing is the park view. It is well worth it! The windowsill is deep and you can actually sit up in the window and watch the world go by. The location of the hotel also can't be beat. It is mere minutes away from a lot of great shopping and dining. The walk to Lincoln Center is about twelve minutes. There are subway and bus connections practically on the doorstep. I know The Plaza is, for many, THE new york hotel. however, the Park Lane is right next door and rather than spend four times as much on a room at The Plaza, stay at the Park Lane and go over to The Plaza to gawk, shop and enjoy yummy food in the Food Hall by Todd English. 
Ultimately, this is a fantastic hotel, with friendly staff, and a great location. I will never stay anywhere else in Manhattan!

I spent one night at Ink-- while visiting family (dad's --th birthday). It was the perfect hotel for my stay. Upon first glance, I wasn't sure. We actually heard the baby too, and it was annoying us as well. But we didn't really know where it was coming from and so did not assume next door immediately or pick a random room number on our floor. It may have been on either neighbouring rooms- above and below- across the hall even.
I would, however, assume that it is rather simple for the front desk to check which rooms have checked in with children and which have not before calling a - adult - children room to calm down their - children?

My partner and I traveled to new york to see the broadway show Mamma Mia. We did a name your own price on priceline and it picked this hotel. What a perfect location, we were literally right across the street from the winter garden theatre where our show was at. The guest service staff was nice, the room was also very nice.
My only complaints is there is no complimentary breakfast or coffee in your room. You can have breakfast in their restaurant, but get ready to pay because its pretty pricey. They have a mini bar in the room which is also pretty pricey. There is no room in the fridge for any of your own personal beverages. There is a bar that serves coffee at - bucks a cup. Also, make sure you dont leave anything in your room. I left a pair of jeans in my room. I tried to call the hotel, transferred to house keeping, was told to hold and hung up on. I call back ,and then got the voicemail. I just gave up on it. So if you leave anythig in the room, good luck getting a hold of anyone to help you over the phone.

I have stayed at the Essex a number of times in years gone by and returned there recently under the new management. I found the front desk staff a little on the slow side but friendly. The room I received was a bit bizarre in how it was laid out - it seemed it have been built in a corridor. The bathroom was difficult to navigate with the door hitting the toilet (make sure you lock it or your knees will get it!). Checkout was a little protracted as well. The best thing is the location but I would find another hotel nearby the next tiem.

Just returned from a - day stay at the Talbott. I booked after reading the reviews on this site and after staying there I'm not sure how it rated as #- in the popularity rating for Chicago Hotels. The location in great - I had a meeting in the area and could have stayed at the Sofitel for the same rate that I paid at the Talbott - but I've stayed at the Sofitel before and wanted to try something different. I'm not sure that I'd make that choice again. The hotel is undergoing renovation which includes the main entrance, the lobby and some of the floors. I had a corner deluxe room which was large - it had a king bed, desk and two easy chairs. The room itself had plenty of room but it looked tired. The bathroom was great it had been recently remodeled - it had a double sink and great counter space - the only complaint is that the tub-shower lacked any kind of shelf or soap dish. There are only about -- rooms on each floor and the hallways were nothing special - once again it may be due to the renovation in progress but the floor I was on was extremely tired and dark. Other complaints included the heat-airconditioning and the room lighting. Since the seasons were beginning to change it was cool at night but warm during the day. Heat was supplied by an old iron radiator hidden under a radiatior cover - it's a good thing it was hidden - it was pretty nasty looking. To regulate the heat you had to lift the cover and turn the valve (not an easy thing to do in the middle of the night without getting burned). Once the heat started it never stopped. To cool the room there was a residential room type air conditioner mounted through the wall and a newer air conditioning unit with a thermostat that had a sign on it saying it was not yet operational - in any event I had all three going most days and nights and it was almost impossible to get the room to a comfortable temperature. I would assume once the new system with the thermostat is working - that things will improve. The lighting in the room was below average - it seemed that the lamps had been equipped with energy saving bulbs that didn't thrown off enought light. The staff was friendly - especially the doorman. Everything said I'd give the Talbott a B-

Following TripAdvisor reviews, I went for this hotel - and was not disappointed. Bedrooms are good size and in great condition. Lobby areas are quiet, yet stylish. Welcoming bar with good food (not cheap though). Best of all, front desk service was impeccable - I did not feel that I was 'another suit in another corporate hotel'.
Would gladly stay next time in LA - colleagues who stayed in similar LA hotels reported generally bad experiences, especially in regards to age of bedrooms

Attended a conference here, stayed in the executive suite. Ultra comfortable beds, great food, friendly employees. Only downside, one of the busiest convention nights, the bar closed at --:-- on a Thursday night which forced a bunch of people to go off property for libations. I would return on a family vacation the lazy river and pools are great.

Stayed at the Palomar April ---- with the family (kids -- & --). The hotel was very attentive to your request and just plain friendly! Pool on the --th floor was great, too bad it was too cold to sit outside and enjoy the scenery. Have to tell you the Happy Hour each night was a pleasant surprise and the manager on duty was great to talk to and very friendly. The rooms were very nice and modern. Kids really like them. The location of the hotel can't be better, close to Michigan Avenue which besides shopping also gives you close access to just about every bus line you would want to get to things like Shedds Acquarium, the Museum of Science and Industry and other like places. 
The restaurant onsite was a great appetizer place before we went out for the night, kid friendly and the food was very good. I would recommend this hotel for anyone who wants a fair value, great service, friendly staff and close proximity to just about everything! Try the Weber Grill Restaurant right across the street, it was very good!

This hotel is an old apartment building. The rooms look like my first apartment (you know, the kind you get when you are just starting off in life and don't have much). We ordered some room service and it didn't arrive at the time requested. Over an hour later, I called. They brought it up and give to to us for free - but it wasn't even good. They had the juice in a box with the hot stuff...so the juice was warm.

Simply put, this hotel was magical:
Room -Great Size, lovely decor, amazing bed (still the best I have ever experienced)

Service - Top draw - polite and professional
I would recommend the three guys cafe very close the the hotel. The best pancakes ever!
Overall - By far the best hotel I have ever stayed in, could not recommend more!

Stayed here last Saturday. A wedding party got out of control and hotel security was ineffective in controlling the problems. I had to call security about noise in our hallway three times...the last at -AM! Manager said the police were just leaving as she got in at -:--am. So, me and a friend took the mega bus to nyc from dc. side note- the bus drops you off about -- blks away from his hotel so its an easy walk or just get on the subway at like --th st or something and go to times sq. we got to the hotel at like -:--, so was hoping to have an early check in. but, since it was only -- min til check in, was not too hard up if they could not have a room ready. they did not, so we had a drink in the lounge. very warm, inviting type of lounge. the color scheme was charming and kind of felt like a living room, not stuffy at all. service from the waitress was slow. also, let me point out that i approached the bar and asked for a drink, to which the rude, obviously un educated bartender lady said she cannot help me, I have to wait for the waitress. last I checked, a bartender makes drinks. perhaps we do it differently in dc, but this lady needs to get checked. serious attitude problem brings bad karma! anyway, the room was not ready til about -:--. so, -- min after check in, and I found that really obnoxious. What has gone wrong with the service industry? seriously! anyway, now that that is out of the way, the location is great if you wanna kind of be near mid town, hells kitchen, and a close train ride to china town and chelsea.

Arrived on --th February in middle of snow and more snow. Hotel staff courteous and friendly. Room clean and comfortable and less noisy probably because we were on the --nd floor. Raffles was speedy, efficient and really great quality for service and food and price reasonable. Housekeeping in particular was first class. Our experience was an excellent oneand we would have no hesitation in returning when in New York.
Jim and Moira Fergie from Edinburgh

My boyfriend and I met another couple at this hotel to attend a party in the club on the top floor (The Sans Souci). The staff was very professional and pleasant in dealing with us. We live in the Dallas area and were just staying here because of the upstairs club and the convenience of having a room that we could walk to at the end of the night. Although we arrived hours before the other couple (they were driving in from Austin), the staff knew that we were waiting for them and called our room as soon as they arrived. The room was a newer room and very clean. As a Dallas resident, I can tell you that there are hotels closer to Downtown. But if you need a nice place to stay and want to be out of the immediate downtown area (or close to Texas Stadium for a Dallas Cowboys' game) this is a great hotel.

Me and my friend stayed at the Fairmont for a long weekend to celebrate her birthday. Service staff was accommodating, the only complaint we both had was that we were promised an iphone-ipod charging dock, and what it really was, was a lamp with an iphone- ipod dock built in. It did not charge our devices (we left them at home since we knew there was a charger in the room) and we had to have them switched twice because they were dead. A small inconvenience. Otherwise, terrific room, good space, great beds (so incredibly comfy) and great A-C control on one of the hottest weekends of August. Located a little ways away from subway (about a -- minute walk) but there is a nice view of Navy Pier from the hotel. Would stay here again.

You must understand what this hotel is! It is not a resort hotel, but it a good, clean, centrally located, friendly accommodations...at a fair price. Caters to a gay clientele, and the open minded. Attached is a nice friendly sports - neighborhood bar Fritz that welcomes everyone (Best bartender is Andrew - great sense of humor) Brunch every Saturday and Sunday--

Everything about our stay was excellent. The staff is very accomodating and friendly. Upon arrival my husband and I were told only smoking rooms were left...we informed the clerk that we both have severe allerigies and she immediately changed us to a nonsmoking corner suite with an incredible view of times square! This was much more than what we had asked for. The hotel is very clean, quiet, beds are comfortable, and it is one of the most reasonably priced hotels directly on times square. We had a late flight out so we checked out early in the morning and stored our bags at the hotel for free until we returned later in the evening.

Wonderful staff...very pleasant personalities and extremely helpful! Location is very convenient as it is next to the airport and the highway. Beware of the rumbling from the planes landing and taking off. The beds are super comfy so you might find it easy to sleep through it! The rooms had a mildew odor and I had to use air freshener. There are no mini fridges in the rooms but aside from those two drawbacks (one of which can be immediately corrected) LaQuinta is the place to stay. By the way, great rates!

My wife and I love to travel to Chicago for weekend trips. This is her current favorite hotel, and the single greatest factor is the window """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""seat"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", especially those overlooking the Chicago River. What a view. Lots of river traffic, people on the sidewalks far below, the skyscraper collection to the north... It's a great urban scene. Plus, the location, just west of Michigan Avenue, is prime. If you fancy this place, join the Kimpton InTouch loyalty program. You get free wifi, and can raid the mini-bar for a set amount of stuff. It's great to grab some goodies when heading home. Very nice staff, and the brunch at South Water was very good. The Chilaquiles were yummy.

Wanted to stay somewhere slighty quieter than last visit and hotel beacon was perfect. Subway less then - min walk. Central park -- min walk. Used the subway alot to get around. Food shops where great as our room had a small kitchen. 
Very residential area and not so many tourists so felt one of the locals.

Stayed here over the Air Show weekend & really enjoyed it. Getting to the hotel is very easy - the entrance is on Rush street, not a lot of traffic there, so no traffic hassles to pull in & drop off. The rooms are fine - big flat screen TV, fridge, comfortable bed, the room with the king bed has a separate shower & bath, toilet in its own room. The design is fresh.
I did not at all mind taking the elevator to the -th floor lobby then going to the street level...there's also an elevator that goes through a shopping mall to get to Michigan Avenue, but on a -- degree day who's going to mind that?? Nice mall too! I also didn't miss the coffee service in the room, it was easy enough to get to the lobby to caffeine up. Breakfast was very good, love the terrace bar.
Another side benefit is access to the red line subway - just two easy short blocks west of the hotel. Took the elevator to the Rush street entrance then just walked over. 
When we booked the Conrad we were looking for a luxury stay with a great location nearby the Magnificent Mile. There are a lot of choices, but we're very pleased with our decision to book here. Got a good rate on the Hilton web site, and all of the amenities added up to make this a very memorable stay.

My boyfriend and I stayed in this hotel during December, when New York's Christmas atmosphere is in full swing. We researched Tripadvisor extensively and chose to stay in this hotel for one night of our trip, staying at a cheaper hotel during part of the trip. The one night we stayed at this hotel was full-on fantastic. The staff treats you like a rockstar, no matter who you are, and they offer great concierge service. The beds are extremely comfortable, down to the soft, sumptuous bedding, and the bathroom was really nice, too. We had a fantastic time at The Bryant Park Hotel. 
The hotel is right across the street from Bryant Park, which was fantastic at Christmas. All we had to do was walk out the hotel and we could go ice skating and eat delicious food at the park. This hotel is within walking distance of tons of restaurants and shops. If you can't walk to something in the city, the subway is across the street, too.

stayed here june --rd to june --th. stayed in the large queen suite with - adults and - small kids. the suite had - very comfy queen beds and a pull out sleeper sofa double bed. the suite also had a mini fridge large enough for jucie boxes, milks, and bottle waters. 
what can i say the pool was AMAZING!!! pics dont do it justice.. it was salt water pool with small splash pad, great swim up bar, and --- of the pool was indoors.. there were - hot tubs.. one in the indoors partion, the other was outside....

the bistro served STARBUCKS..!! 
ask for extra towels u get them...

the location of the hotel is with in - mins of a freeway which has all the food locations... target - jc pennys ..HEB food store aswell..
