I enjoy staying at the hotel, have done so - times. The rooms are spacious and some have very good views. The locations is quite good, in the Theatre District but walking distance to a lot of good restaurants and attractions in the Back Bay, and - block away from the Boston Common. The service is quite good too - from the concierge to the room service to check-in, everyone has gone out of their way to be helpful and prompt.
It's sometimes been difficult to get a reservation here, I assume due to the popularity. But it's worth the effort. This is one of the better W's I have stayed at.

For anyone wanting to get a firsthand view of Seattle,this hotel makes it really easy.We booked a room on one of the upper levels and asked for a room with a view.We got a spectacular view of the Space Needle.On the ground you find yourself in easy walking distance from the aforementioned Space Needle as well as the EMP,Seattle Center and the Pacific Science Center.The Key Arena-home to basketball games and other entertainment events is close by as well.To access downtown shopping and the Pike's Place Market and Alaskan Way waterfront it is possible to walk.Those that want to save their legs can take the local bus or hop on the Monorail which is inside the Seattle Center.
The hotel itself on the outside is no example of great architecture.The giant concrete slabs on the exterior can only complement the concrete causeway close by.Having said that, once inside the hotel all is forgotten as the windows and walls let in no external noise. The room itself was very clean and the decor was very pleasing.The lobby staff were always very patient and helpful.The lobby has a very cozy lounge area with a fireplace.There's a small computer room behind the office open to the public where you have access to computers and a printer.Underground,secure parking is available -at $-- a day.Street parking outside the hotel is limited to a few hours-the parking police are vigilant.
There is a breakfast,dining lounge but that also is an extra cost.It's a full buffet breakfast not the usual Best Western express fare..There was a good selection of foods and the staff wait your tables to offer beverages.My only complaint was that the head of the dining room was a little too tense and he made us feel pressured if we hadn't left the dining room by the end of breakfast time.I am guessing that the reason being is that many conferences are held at the hotel due to it's central location and the dining room is in constant use during the day so the head is on a tight schedule.However if you miss breakfast at the hotel there are many alternatives close by.There's a Whole Foods about ten minutes walk away. Our favorite dinner spot was a late night pizza place called Bambino's.They are very low key and offer a select menu of wood-fired pizzas and fresh Italian salads at reasonable prices.
I would definitely recommend this Best Western.You can't fault the location and the efficiency of the staff and the neat presentation of the rooms are always appreciated.

We go to Washington every fall for a conference. I try to stay here as often as possible. The location is good and the management friendly. I really like the kitchenette. And the new restaurant is quie acceptable, too.

very nice place, good location. Only issues I had was that the AC vent blows directly on the pillow end of bed in a small room, but maybe there is something they can do about it. Housekeeping kept shorting us on washcloths (- for - people?) All in all, a nice place to stay. The reduced price due to the 'soft opening' is appropriate; no items in courtesy frig, no restaurant, no exercise facilities (they give you passes to some great health clubs that are close by). Overall, I would stay here again.
I look forward to returning.

Hidden in plain sight on Eighth Avenue is a gem of a hotel. The Hilton Garden Inn Times Square is an affordable, yet up-scale place to rest your head while visiting NYC. From friendly doormen to comfortable beds and linens to the delicious buffet breakfasts, you'll feel welcome. Within a couple blocks' walk are major theaters, city tours, subway entrances and, of course, Times Square. As well as an excellent on-site restaurant, Thalia's just half a block away, where you can enjoy fabulous dinners. This hotel may well be the best kept secret in Manhattan!

Except for the location I did not expect much from the hotel as Hiltons are not what they used to be. Check-in was fast and the person at the desk was helpful. Room was spacious, clean, and the bed was pretty standard but not very comfortable. Room service food was sub par in quality and overpriced. Not even close to be a luxury hotel.

Room was alright and breakfast leaves nothing to be desired. Location is relatively good, far enough from Tenderloin area to seem safe. However, too many other choices around San Francisco to settle Found it over-rated. Should be just average..
Even though the lobby is being remodeled, this location is very close to the airport. The staff is very helpful! There is a shuttle every half hour ---hrs a day.

From the minute we arrived the staff were always so friendly. The room was great. We requested a high floor and our room was on the --th floor.The Empire State Building and Macy's are right up --th Street (--- min walk). An MTA was right around the corner at Park and --rd St as well as Grand Central about a -- minute walk away. The room was very quite and the bed very comfortable. My only complaint was the bathroom was kind of small. Not alot of counter area to put stuff on.

My son and I were really looking forward to two days on this property. Due to the high temps during July, we spent each late afternoon and early evening in the waterpark (--- hours) and, truly, that was enough time. There really wasn't a whole lot to do if one wasn't golfing, playing tennis or working out at the gym. There are three slides, a lazy river and volleyball and basketball area. Regarding the volleyball and basketball area, there were only one or two balls for the whole resort to share. This doesn't make sense to me. Also, the lazy river was very long (nice) but not fully functional on either day. The rapids area did not work. A note for the resort: I would recommend that staff remove unmanned inner tubes from the river because they get in the way of the general flow of things. There were probably -- empty inner tubes for each guest during our visit and the tubes impeded our journey. 
The resort was probably at less than -- percent capacity but I had to really push for a complimentary upgrade to a room within --- yards (no kidding) of the water park. We loved the ping pong (only one table that we knew of) but had to seek out the paddles and balls. There was no sign indicated where and how to acquire them. 
The rooms were clean. 
We only at the Mexican restaurant on site and it was absolutely horrible. No kidding. 
I will definitely not stay at this resort again. It wasn't awful by any stretch of the imagination but it looked much nicer online than in person -- hence, the reason for my negative reaction.

We have used Copley House for years to house business colleagues for extended stays--many of them come back for just a couple nights and insist on staying there again! They have several apartment buildings located in Boston's vibrant South End, close to public transportation, shopping, restaurants, and sites. Each unit has a kitchenette, a must for those in the city for several weeks at a time. The owners are super friendly and always available to help out. Whenever I drop someone off, I wish I could live there all the time!

I was in town for a week for a science convention and I have to say that it was the best I've ever attended just because the hotel was great! The room was clean, the cleaning staff were friendly and always willing to accomendate me with whatever I needed. I have to give an extra special thanks though to the breakfast crew. I couldn't wait to get my day started just to go have breakfast. The omelette chef (Brian) was the best! He was a delightful way to start my day. My omelette was always perfect and even when he had a long line he always was sure to greet every guest like he has known them for years! You need to clone him and place him in all your hotels! Also Jrand(I hope I didnt butcher his name) was another person who stood out. Every morning he also greeted me with a small and made sure my beverage was always full. Thank you guys for making my trip memorable!

We planned a Mother's Day Trip to the American Girl Store and were very impressed with this hotel. The pool was very nice and from the pool area the view of Navy Pier was fantastic. Staff was friendly, rooms were nice, beds comfortable and they accomidated our request for joining rooms.

I recently spent - days at the Hilton Garden in downtown Detroit and It's not that nice! The staff is rather rude and they only cares to discuss their personal business while guests wait at the counter to check in. Rooms are dingy and the restaurant is a joke! I waited -- minutes to get my car and the valet brings up the wrong one?? If you have to stay downtown, I suggest the Courtyard on the river front.....

We were in LA for family reuninon. We chose this hotel because of the reviews and they weren't wrong. The hotel is in a great location and staff are friendly and very helpful.
Minibar service (free) is great.
We know where to go next time.

We have stayed at Warner Center Marriott many times over the years. Family lives in the area and this is the reason we stay here. 
I checked the reservation website several times and lowest rates ranged from $----$--- per night (not sure why it constantly changed). The last time a four night stay came up for $--- per night if you pre-paid. Couldn't pass that up. We knew nothing came with that rate and didn't expect anything more than a basic room. 
The room was comfortable. However, the weather was cool for LA and for some reason the air conditioning seemed to be on in the hall making cold air come under the door into the room. We just used a towel to block cold air and that worked. Housekeeping was wonderful. I always tip daily and being in the hospitality business I know that this is the best way to get good service. Try it, it works.
We ate in the restaurant once and it was good. Found Ruby's Diner across the street very affordable for breakfast and worth the short walk. Lots of great places to eat close by. I will say that when we ordered room service one night, it was very good. Fast service and food was great. 
We own a hotel & vacation rentals and you can not please everyone. I know how to read reviews. We had a very pleasant stay and the entire staff was always extremely nice and helpful.

Seems to be an aging hotel, the elevator was scary and slow and made clunking sounds at each floor. Basic rooms and lobby. It was supposed to be just an overnight stay near the airport but I schedule some business meetings without knowing what the hotel looked like. I was embarrassed to have customers meet me in this type of basic hotel. If you need just an overnight stay near the airport, this will suffice. Anything more, just booked a better hotel.
Shuttle service (free) but waiting time is long. Very frustrating if you arrive just after the bus leaves and you have an hour to wait. I was not happy. At all.

This was my -nd stay at the Austin Renaissance, Arboretum. The staff are friendly, the rooms clean and comfortable, the fitness center is well equipped and maintained, and the hotel is in a nice location.
In the Arboretum area, the Renaissance is comfortable walking distance to Z'Tejas and Eddie V's and the Arboretum shops, and only a few minutes drive from the Domain shopping area which boasts a number of nice restaurants and plenty of additional shopping. In addition, it's only a few minutes drive from some of Austin's finest barbecue at Rudy's.
The hotel is an open style with all rooms opening onto the walkway which is open to the atrium. It can be a little loud during the day as it has some meeting-convention rooms and sees a good bit of traffic through the Atrium, but I haven't had any issues with excess noise at night.
Overall this is a very nice property and I will definetly stay here in the future when convenient to my needs.

Stayed three nights in September ----. Staff is very professional and went far beyond expectation to make our stay pleasant. Location is really central if you want to be midtown. The hotel is on --th between -th and -th, just a half block from Times Square, the theatre district, minutes to Rockefeller Center and many subway lines, etc. 
Our room was very very dark. Windows, which did not face onto a street, were frosted for privacy, allowing for very little light. Even midday, it felt like we were in an underground bunker even though we were on the -th floor. Consequently, we spent little time in our room apart from sleeping.
The hallways as well are very dark. Even finding the slot into which you need to insert your room key card is a challenge. (I've never understood this trend for dark hallways, which seems to have taken hold in quite a few NYC hotels.)
The hotel has a great and busy rooftop bar and restaurant. We'll likely return there for a late afternoon drink and meal next time we're in town.

My sister and I stayed in a standard room, and it was very clean! It had a cute walk-in closet, rennovated bathroom, and two double beds. The hotel is within walking distance to many attractions. Since it is in the theatre district, we were able to walk to an off-broadway play that was amazing! We walked to Time Square that night and to Central Park the next day. There is a very good diner about a block and a half away. The staff was very nice and since our flight did not leave until later in the afternoon and check out is at --:--, they offer a safe place to keep your luggage until you have to leave for the airport later in the day, which I found to be very convenient! I saw complaints about the noise on other posts, but I never had any problems with noise, and besides, hello? You're in New York! What do you expect? I will definitely stay here again!

I booked this hotel through AAA at a great rate. It is conveniently located close to Times Square and Broadway. 
The room is small but served it's purpose. The bathroom had lots of mildew. Surprisingly, you could not hear any of the city traffic, but that is because it is drowned out by the sound of flushing toilets and showers running. You can literally hear every bit of plumbing that is going on. One morning I sneezed in the bathroom and heard someone say god bless you. If you plan to sleep past six AM do not stay here.
We arrived back at the room after a long day and found that it had not been cleaned. We needed to call the front desk twice to get clean towels. The location, rooms, etc., are nothing special.

I have stayed at several Ritz-Carlton's including, but not limited to those in Grand Cayman, Jamaica, New Orleans and St. Thomas. This one is not as nice as the one in Grand Cayman or New Orleans or St. Thomas. The facilities in those locations are nicer and the staff, believe it or not, are better there, particularly in Grand Cayman which is truly beyond belief. This is not to say the staff at Central Park Ritz are not nice and helpful. They are, but I rank the Central Park Ritz about an -.- on a -- scale. Examples of so-so service include the - calls it took just to reach someone at the front desk not at a busy time. It seems they just didn't want to answer their phone. And, in the club, it was clear that those who were regulars at this location rated better service as I was wholly ignored for long stretches while they conversed with them. The room was a king central park view which was nice, but small and nothing special in comparison to what you would see at other destinations, particularly for the $$$$ you spend for such a room. For example, in St. Thomas, you get more than twice the room quality and size for --- the money. All in all, a good choice for a clean comfortable hotel.

Last time I noted that the rooms seemed dated and they still seemed to be, especially the bathrooms. They smelled quite strange which was a bit alarming. The rooms are good sized and we managed to fit our family of four quite well despite having large luggage. One of the reasons we decided to come back here was because it is one of the few hotels in the area that include wifi service during your stay. All other places charge up to -- USD for the wifi. This time we did not use the concierge service but last time they were very helpful. The one thing that was extremely uncomfortable about our experience here is that at -:-- AM a drunken couple in a room next to us started having a shouting match that woke our whole family up and the kids had the opportunity (sarcasm) to listen to some wonderful vocabulary as we could hear their whole argument just fine. I called the front desk after -- minutes and finally, -- minutes or so, they quieted down. I don´t know if they intervened or not but it was not a nice thing to experience during a family vacation. All in all it was just OK this time around. The best thing, again, is the location.
Spent - nights while on a business trip. Friendly staff, more than adequate accommodations, free wi-fi & very fair pricing thanks to a Living Social discount.

I've stayed at this hotel many times....simply because of my Starwood status and the relative location of the hotel to business I have in the city. Here is what I will say:
-Twice I have arrived to find they have no rooms available and I have been sent to alternative hotels
-The elevators are extremely slow
-The staff can be very unhelpful and the service is very poor
-Not always is your reservation as you request (I have been quoted different rates during check-in than my reservation shows -- make sure you have your confirmation with you!!)
-The location is great
-The room service is pretty good
-The rooms vary, but in general are nice, clean and many have fantastic views
I now choose to stay at the W Hotel and prefer to book my rooms early to get a similar rate. Even the Sheraton next door has better service. That said, I have had good experiences at the Westin, but it seems to be hit or miss. A manager there once told me they are understaffed (the same manager that promised me ---- Starwood points for not having a room and those points never appeared).

We stayed at the Hyatt for a dental hygiene convention, the rooms were comfortable & updated. The conference areas were plentiful, accommodating, and convenient, but the rooms were VERY cold, be sure to bring a sweater-jacket. We did have a buffet lunch & dinner served & the food was very good. I enjoyed the -- hour fitness room, it was well equipped with plenty of treadmills, stairmasters & a few stationary bikes. The workout room was clean with towels, headphones & - large flat screened TV's.
We will stay @ the Hyatt again, but will be sure to have warmer clothing in the meeting rooms.

we have two teenagers. the king suite has a bedroom and a sitting room with a very large pull out bed. it worked out great for us and is more economical then getting two rooms and way more comfortable than getting one room with two double beds!
the hotel is in the middle of everything and windows look out into the street so noise maybe a problem. but you gotta expect that!
we have stayed at other san francisco hotels with family suites but the kids rooms tend to be geared toward very little kids (bunk beds, dress up toys, tiny chairs) so this was a real find for us.

I favorably reviewed this property in ---- but felt compelled to write another review due to some of the negative reviews. Perhaps some of the negative reviewers stayed in older rooms not renovated. However, my room was superb. it was immaculately clean, newer very comfortable bed, flat screen Hd TV with over -- channels, granite desk and night stands, new rain forest shower head and very clean bathroom, fridge, safe and iPod compatible upscale clock radio. Hallways were spotless as is the lobby. Fitness room has - treadmills with individual attached TV.
Yes, the pool is tiny so if you want to large pool don't stay here. Wifi was great but because of my Marriott status I did not have to pay. Also, because of my status I had access to the Concierge Lounge. Yes,, parking is expensive but this trip I listened to the reviewers who parked on the street and I did also. Breakfast buffet was excellent and at $-- is expensive but par for the course at a large hotel. All in all, I highly recommend.

It wasn't a bad place to stay, but nothing special. I thought it would be in a more boutique kind of neighborhood, but it wasn't really that close to anything. They charge for the wireless in the rooms and there is an additional charge for parking. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Some very loud, probably drunk, people came in around -:-- a.m. and didn't quiet down for about half an hour. It sounded like they were a ways down the hall from me, but the noise really traveled.

Spent a Saturday night in January at the Detroit Marriott Renaissance Center. It does not meet the standards of an upscale hotel but the stay was satisfactory. When arriving the valet parking and check-in was prompt and the staff were very helpful and friendly. Was given a room on an upper floor with a very nice river view. The room however is where the hotel did not meet expectations. The hotel room was rather small, it was clean but it is definitely showing its age. There were stains on the carpet, scuff marks on the walls and the furniture was nicked up. The bathroom is also very small which could be a problem if a couple is trying to get ready at the same time. The positives for the room are the very comfortable bed, the nice large desk, a comfortable chair and ottoman, and very large closet. The hotel has a very nice fitness center with great views while you are using the equipment. The hotel lobby was also very nice. The location makes it very convenient so for the right price I may stay there again.

We spent the weekend in this charming hotel and loved it. It has a European flair and all the staff are very nice and helpful. I arrived quite bedraggled and was allowed to check in early with no additional fee, as other hotels are prone to doing. We were given a quiet room on the backside and were not subject to the usual continuous street noise. Our room was quite spacious, especially for NYC, and even had a good closet. The location is excellent, near subway stops in either direction, good shopping, and walking to Central Park. There are also plenty of cabs whizzing by on Lexington Avenue to take you downtown if preferred. The hotel does have a restaurant and bar, but also, next door is a little take out food place with wonderful soup, fruit, coffee and breakfast things, etc., that we found very good and convenient for a quick stop. The only thing that needs improving is that the carpet in our room needed replaced. I have stayed in numerous hotels around Manhattan and would definitely recommend this one. We plan to stay there again on future trips.

My husband and I spent a few days of our honeymoon at the Mark Hopkins. The hotel itself is impressive and the staff helpful, but the room we were in was pretty bad. It lookes like it hadn't been renovated in quite a while. The location of the Mark Hopkins is also bad if you're spending most of your time on foot. By distance alone it is close to many of the attractions of the area, but since it's at the top of the hill, you must either get a good workout or travel the cable cars. 
I will say the Top of the Mark was excellent, however. And I later found out my dad actually took my mother there on their honeymoon.

The location of this hotel was convenient to my meeting, which is why it was selected. It appears to have been something other than a Crowne Plaza in a previous life. There were ongoing renovations in the atrium area. The room was a bit crowded; it included a small refrigerator and microwave. I am particularly aware of poor maintenance, especially of the bathrooms. The photo attached tells the story here and is a reason I would not stay here again.

I've stayed at this hotel at least four different time over the years so I am very familar with the place. Heck, my last couple of stays here have been via Priceline so maybe I should start booking direct?
Pros: Great location, airport shuttle, helpful staff, close to Phoenix Munical Stadium & Zoo
Cons: None really. I'm not a fan of the sleep number beds and would like to see the older ones replaced, but that's a minor quibble.

Staying at this hotel gave me the opportunity to explore Chelsea and the Meatpacking District. We timed our stay very well as it was the start of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hard opening"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of the hotel and we got an amazing opening special through Expedia, as it would otherwise have been very expensive to stay in the area.
We stayed on one of the lower floors so thankfully the nightclub didn't bother us, though it was amusing seeing the massive queues outside the hotel each night.
The King Size bed was amazingly comfortable and I loved the toiletries which were provided. I must say that the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""modern"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" bathroom (especially the metallic-looking toilet) probably aren't my design """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cup of tea"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", but everything functioned well.
The outdoor pool was a lot of fun, as was being able to order food and laze about on the lounge chairs.
The front desk staff were so helpful with tips about where to go shopping (a must in New York of course)!

My husband & I went to LA for - nights and stayed at this hotel on Sunday, September --th. We paid the manager special of $---nt., the free parking and the free breakfast was really good -- which makes this an overall great rate. We drove to Universal, it seemed too far to walk (like -----mins), plus the hotel is on a busy street, and the area seems just OK, I wouldn't wanna' walk around there at night alone. The rooms were fine, had a fridge in the room, which was nice. The pool is small, and in a small cement room -- don't stay here just for the pool! I wished we would have spent the extra $-- bucks and stayed at the Sheraton that was much closer and looked really nice!

Positive surprise after all the stories wa have heard about NY hotels.
Friendly and helpful staff. Big and clean room with good bed. OK breakfast included. Nice little restaurant just next to this hotel (door from reception, breakfast is offered here) with good happy hour and friendly staff.
Location is good, walking distance to many places and subway is near.
I think price is quite good what comes to NY standards.
Noise during night from --th street (garbage trucks, etc) is only minus. On the other hand we got ear plugs for next night without any request... :-)
Could easily recommend.

Ok so when I booked the doubletree I thought it was gonna be great. Not!!!! I got in late and got cookies which were amazing but then was told I had to pay for parking I have never had to do that at a hotel and I was never informed I had to do that. Now the gentleman at the front dest treated me ok but I didn't feel comfortable. He made it seem like he was surprised at how young I was and treated me like a little child. Now the room was great and the shower was amazing. Now the horrible I was woken up at -:-- am when I arrived at --:-- am the same day. I was woken up by housekeeping! They didn't knock or warn me and they turned on the first light in the room. This is crazy! I had an ok experience but that housekeeper waking me up ruined my view of the hotel.

We decided to stay here for our holiday to Los Angeles for - weeks.
Expedia say this place is In a good location to vist L.A. - The motel is situated right next to the No- Freeway and is so noisy that sleeping is almost impossible. We did complain about our room and was moved to a quieter room at the back of the hotel. Great! Erm... not so great as the walkways outside the room are often used as late night hangouts with people smoking and we heard a guy selling drugs outside our room one night. There are big gaps around the door so even with the door shut and towel shoved at the bottom of the door it still sounded like they were in our room. 
The location is ok if your visiting - Flags or Universal Studios but miles away from anything else! All that is in walking distance is a petrol station, a Dennys & a McDonalds. If you need to 'pop to the supermarket' (or anywhere else) expect at least a half an hour drive. 
Another reason why we booked this hotel was because it had a pool and 'spa'. We didnt use either once. Check out our pictures to see why! 
We were only in the room at night when we were completely exhausted after exploring L.A all day long but I would seriously recommend avoiding this place. At weekends it seems its a place where the locals come to party, play their music REAL loud until -am and deal drugs. Its ok for a few nights but if your staying in L.A for a while look for a good hotel near West Hollywood. This place felt really unsafe and the hotel room didnt even have a safe, neither did the hotel lobby (we ended up carrying around our valuable items all holiday).
AVOID!

We have recently stayed for a night at the Travel Inn Hotel on W --nd Street & --th Ave. 
We felt that it is over priced and has very poor service.

it's very good - everything works, the locations good, the room is comfortable, having a kitchen is really useful and it's lots of space for the price, but somehow it's very boring. and do the rooms have to be entirely green - walls, bed, dustbin, curtains, lamps.... bit home from homey, I'd look out for something funner on my next visit to NY.

ok so i booked the cheapest rate so probably got the smallest type of room and it is a city centre hotel so i'm not complaining. it's in a great area and has good facilities. i thought it felt pretty new although my wife didnt quite agree. 
unlike some other reviews, i got free wifi as a HHonors member. i wasnt using it for streaming or anything heavy like that so it was fine. 
we didnt eat at the hotel as prices were quite high but there's so many food options nearby that it didnt bother us. 
i'd certainly go back.

Spent a couple of nights here and had a very comfortable stay. I can't say much about the surrounding amenities (in terms of walking distance at least), but did find it a great base to see most things in LA by car. The rooms (which are spotlessly clean) feel like self contained little cottages, much more homely than a standard motel. Ample parking is provided. Seems like a nice neighbourhood too. Very friendly staff. My only gripe would be that its right next to an intersection and the traffic was quite heavy and a bit noisy, as a result I found myself waking earlier that anticipated each morning. Still, I'd very happily stay here again.

Checking was quick but elevators were always slow and crowded. We lost precious time between slow room service and trying get out of the hotel and get a cab. The breakfast service at the expensive restaurant. Arrogant and slow waiters. Our room seemed outdated. The location is great with nice view from all windows.

As soon as we entered the hotel we had this very welcomed feeling. We were greeted with a firendly smile. The staff were very accommodating, efficient and courteous. The hotel is situated in a great location. Shopping and restaurants are at the tip of your fingers. We spent - unforgetable stay at Diva. We will definitely go back to this hotel.

Extremely nice hotel in a perfect location, directly across the street from the Galleria Mall. It offers self parking as well as valet. The self parking lot is gated and accessible by your room key. The lobby alone is absolutely beautiful with its contemporary furniture and wide spaces. The hotel has an atrium design that allows you to see the entire lobby from the windows of your room. I had suite so I am not sure if this feature is in all guestrooms. The check-in process was simple thanks to Leah. The elevators feature sounds that influence your mood, even the songs of crickets! My suite was very functional and. spacious with enough room for entertaining a small group. It included a very nice sofa, and a high table that functioned as both for dining and as a work station for video presentations as it was stationed adjacent to the flat screen television.The queen size bed was very comfortable, I hated to leave it. The bathroom had a two way access which allowed you to get to it only a few steps from the bed. Le Meridien Dallas is my new home away from home when visiting Dallas.

Too bad service like this is so hard to find! Stayed here many times, last time here was in January. Check in was great, got an automatic upgrade from jr. suite to suite. Great room, clean, luxurious and great views. Very quiet. Bar was busy that night, but wait staff was still attentive and friendly. Just an all around pleasure to stay at this hotel. Many think its too expensive, but if you're already paying a few hundred dollars per night, its really worth paying a little more to stay at this hotel. This is what service and cleanliness should be.

This is by far the absolute nicest hotel we have ever stayed in. I had my -- year old child and my huband with me and we all enjoyed it immensley. By the way, for those who say it is not for children, my -- year old son loved it. The pool was a lot of fun for him, and there were other children there, as well. We did not have any problems with noise at all, either. I noticed that someone else wrote of a problem with people being loud in the halls. Hoever, it was so quiet that we almost felt like we should whisper in the halls. We were very impressed.
We had a huge bathroom with a glass enclosed shower and a deep sunken tub, which was great for relaxation! This was one of the best vacations we have ever had, and we didn't even use the spa or golf course! I would definitely reccomend this resort to anyone who is looking for a peaceful, comfortable stay.
Our room was very clean, and I am the world's worst critic on hotel cleanliness! The beds were extremely comfortable! The carpet was clean. I even walked barefoot in the room, and that is very unusual for me! 
All the staff, from the bellboy, to the front desk, to the cleaning staff were very helpful and friendly. The concierge was also very helpful. I can't say enough about the first class treatment you receive in this resort!
We will definitely return!
Jose Rosales at the front desk was very professional and helpful. Hotel is very clean and rooms very nice.

I am a top-tier Gold Passport member & it had been a few years since I had stayed at the Century Plaza. Now, I know why. The staff were warm & welcoming, but the rooms are showing some wear and tear. The bed was worn and clearly sagged on one side. Bathrooms were in fair condition with visible mold in the shower area and poor quality towels. On the plus side, the public spaces (Breeze restaurant & outdoor areas) are nice - but they don't make up for the outdated room. The value equation for this hotel is not very good - room rates are high & the hotel needs updating. There are better quality hotels in the area - but if you need to stay at a Hyatt, check out the Andaz in nearby West Hollywood - it has been renovated more recently.

Hard to beat location -- Four Seasons & Waldorf on same block you know you're in the action! Service top notch - arguably as good as a - star at --- the price. Rooms a tad dated but no doubt best overall bang for your buck in Chicago.

My boyfriend and I booked a room for a special occasion, and this hotel surpassed every expectation. We stayed in a suite and it was absolutely gorgeous. The bed was comfortable, and the room was very spacious. The jacuzzi was also HUGE, while it may be for """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""two,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" it was about - feet deep. We also enjoyed the hosted wine hour. Although we did not have a goldfish in our room (which was something I had been looking forward to after all the reviews), I'm wondering if that's usually for guests who stay more than one night. Also, we arrived in Chicago around - in the morning, and were able to actually check-in (- hours early!) when we went to drop off our bags. The staff couldn't have been more friendly or helpful. Overall, I really couldn't have asked for a better hotel.

I read the reviews and can't believe we stayed at the same hotel. I had a very clean room that was mostly updated but definitely no where near shabby which was given in a review, good food, very friendly and helpful service, etc. It's the only hotel in the inner city that had it's own parking and it was free. I give it Four Stars for Great Service, Very Comfortable, Very Clean and VERY Convenient!!! On my next trip to Philly, I'm staying there on --nd Street!!!!!!!!!!

I stayed here in November, ---- and it was a great value for the price I paid. Use the hotel's website and look for the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Name your own rate"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" promotion. For the price, you can't beat the location and the modest amenities. Don't expect the Hilton, but who wants to spend time in San Francisco at the hotel - hit the streets and see the sights!
I'm planning to stay here again on my next trip!

We stayed here for two awful nights!! The staff is poorly trained and for a relatively new hotel, it is not maintained well. When we arrived in our first room it was not what I had reserved. Informed front desk about this and were asked if I had really reserved an Executive King. I told them that I had the confirmation letter and then they remembered that yes, in fact, I had reserved that type of room, but it wasn't ready. We wasted the first few hours of our trip switching rooms and waiting for our luggage. Was a bottle of wine sent to our room or flowers to compensated for frustration and time wasted? NO!!!. What was sent to our room, which seemed quite shabby compared to the first room that they sent us to, were three -- count them -- - different engineers on separate times to fix the TV, a door that wouldn't lock and a smoke alarm that kept going off at --:-- p.m. and kept my young children awake for -- minutes. 
I have one positive thing to say about the hotel and that would be the location. It was quite handy to be next to the Whole Foods, Starbucks, and a great pizza place - Tutto Bella Neopolitano! Other than that don't bother with this hotel. Our last night in town was blissfully spent at the Four Seasons -- the smoke alarm thing did me in -- definitely worth every penny!!

I recently stayed at the LAX Hilton while attending a meeting there and found plenty of things to like, as well as a few minor complaints. My room was clean, up-to-date, and comfortable. The bathroom was on the small side, but that wasn't a big problem since it was just me in the room. The housekeepers seemed to take special care -- one day they made a little sleeping bag out of a washcloth and tucked my toothpaste inside. It made me laugh! The water pressure in the shower was great. Some of the amenities I found helpful included the hair dryer, coffee maker, and iron-board.
My room (----) had a direct view onto an active runway so I got to enjoy watching the planes land and take off. I could also hear the noise from the planes on the runway, and while it wasn't too loud for me, if you're very sensitive to that sort of thing you might want to request a different part of the hotel. 
Just a few nits to point out: (-) the elevators need a rehab -- some of the numbers are missing from the floor buttons, for instance; (-) the fitness room is in the basement (no windows) and can get crowded at times; (-) one night we had dinner in the bar and it was hard to get service (our meal was served without utensils or napkins, so we got up to get them ourselves rather than wait for help); and (-) I had to wait -- minutes for the shuttle when I arrived at LAX late at night -- annoying when I just wanted to get to the hotel and go to sleep.

The hotel offers great value compared to many hotels situated a few blocks uptown in SoHo. The train station just outside the door whisks you uptown in a flash and you feel like a local as you walk along the Hudson River in the Sunday morning sun.
The rooms are spacious for the price and the staff friendly,although I didn't really test them beyond a booking at a local restaurant. There is a great coffee shop run by Kiwis a block or so away in Greenwich street and an amazing bagel store for breakfast close by.
We spent - nights at the Benjamin. Centrally located, very nice and clean room. Staff was very friendly and helpful. I highly recommend it.

We recently took our first trip up to Seattle and stayed at the Sheraton. The hotel is located in a great location so you can walk to most things. (if walking isn't your thing, cabs are very easy to get)
The hotel itself must have been remodeled recently as it seemed to have that new carpet smell throughout the hallways and rooms.
The rooms were a pretty good size for being a hotel in a city. Pretty spacious, clean and bright. The bed was amazing!!
We would definitely visit Seattle again and when we do, we will stay here again.

We stayed at the Hampton Inn for our family reunion. We had eight rooms, a combination of suites and king bedrooms. The rooms were large and the suites were true suites with a door between the two rooms. The breakfast room is large and there was a hot breakfast, waffles, fruit, and pastries. The swimming pool was small but the children all enjoyed it and the hot tub. 
Parking was pricy but it is downtown Philly. We used the valet parking. When you needed the car, you texted the number on your chit and -- minutes later the car was out front.
The location is within walking distance to the Reading Terminal Market, the trolley and metro. 
The staff were great especially in helping us deal with a family reunion and all the challenges that presents. I would like to especially thank Alexis Butcher-Dahlin who was our contact throughout the weekend and make the stay even better.
Note that the address of the hotel is Race Street but there is no sign or door on Race. Just go along Race and turn left at --th and you'll find the hotel.

Conveniently located next to Petco Park and a leisurely walk to shopping at Seaport Village, but otherwise not very memorable. It was okay, but for the same price there are much nicer places to stay when in San Diego. Room was clean and comfortable. There is a Starbucks but you have to go outside of the building near the bus drop off and round the corner. Not a bad place for a conference, but would not stay here for any personal travel.

I did not get the polite help I would have liked. I called to ask about having a package delivered, and they said I could do that no problem. They did not inform me that there would be a charge, and when I asked about the charge, I was rudely informed that she could not change the charge. The person at the desk was also very rude when I asked about my rate- I had selected a rate with internet included, but did not need the internet because my conference supplied it. The worst was not these charges, but the rude way I was treated at reception.
Also, the room was super hot, and the small AC unit in the room did nothing to help.

We stayed at the Palace Hotel in San Francisco in May ----. The room was a good size, but it seemed austere for some reason. The public areas of the hotel are very elegant, particularly the Garden Court, where breakfast is served. The buffet breakfast was quite good. We enjoyed drinks at the Pied Piper Bar but not as much as we enjoyed the wasabi bar mix.
The location, at New Montgomery and Market, is perfect, and all manner of public transit is right outside (if you can figure out the multiple systems). We found it quite convenient when we arrived late at night after a connection in Newark,to take the BART directly to the Montgomery Street Station and walk to the hotel. We were also able to book the hotel at a very good price on the Starwood website. 
This is a very nice four-star hotel, but we found it a little ornate for our taste. We have also stayed at the nearby (though less conveniently located) W Hotel, which we preferred for being more modern. Neither of them is a wouldn’t-try-anywhere-else hotel, but neither would be off of the list of properties considered for our next visit.

This was our second stay at the Elysee. It is a great location for the MOMA, most shopping, and central park. Most other sites and restaurants are within a $-- cab ride. The room was very nice ( AND NO BED BUGS) and clean. It was my wife's birthday and I had arranged for flowers which they provided at prevailing cost and they also provided chocolate and a bottle of Proscotto for free. The breakfast is very nice at no cost and the afternoon buffet is not to be believed, also at no cost. You could easily make lunch or dinner at the buffet. In the evenings when calling for a cab, they sent one doorman up to the corner to secure the cab from the cross street. The service is really good. This is a great place and well worth the money. We also ate at the Monkey Bar and had a nice dinner on a day it snowed. We are definitely going to go back again.

The feeling you get entering this hotel is more like a youth hostel than a $--- a night hotel. 
Front desk staff were helpful and did their job, though ever so cool and laxed in their corner desk. I guess you should be carrying a surf board under your arm to feel part of the gang. 
Rooms (twin-bed, partial ocean view) where ok sized, but with a bizarre solution for the bathroom. You were to include all in the hotel room when going to the toilet, an open on the sides glass slide door.
The balcony had partial ocean view as promised, but also the slumish view of the back alleys, not making it actually very tempting to spend time out there.
The restaurant was small, but not that difficult to get a table. It turned out there were a reason for this. The staff seemed to be lacking basic training, so if you finally were lucky enough to place an order, you could wait ages to get it. The funny part was that there were not many guest and quite a lot of staff, that actually were running at times, meanwhile our food was getting cold ready to be picked up by the waiter. There also seemed to be no communication between waiters.
Finally, location: To me Venice beach was very much a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""in da hood"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" place, with a lot of mentally deranged people and pushers. There were actually an assault one morning, a raving mad woman screaming and attacking people. 
Conclusion: extremely overpriced.
Note to self: make better research next time.

Staycation! We live here in HOT Phoenix and escaped for -- hours with - other families to enjoy the water park. It was crowded but not overwhelming for us. The water park consists of a lazy river, wave pool and - big slides and has a large seating area, some of which is well shaded. The food served poolside is quite good and not total bust the bank prices. We stayed in a villa room with Queen bed and pull out sofa. Small but very nice and fantastic location by the entrance to the water park.

This is a great hotel, that provides excellent value. What impressed me most was the very personal service they manage to deliver. Despite the huge amount of guest I never had the 'train station' feeling that you get in some large hotels. The breakfast is great but otherwise the restaurant is not quite up to snuff ( dull food that's overpriced)

the hotel's location is fantastic! walking around is more than a pleasure! the design is fabulous and the staff very friendly! the food was also great! The rooms are nice with a wonderful view, a bit small, but is New York! I enjoyed very much my stay!

We stayed at the Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf for three nights in March. We got this hotel via priceline, which is a good thing because if I had paid the full price I would have been disgusted.
The hotel is very clean, the pool area is great - very warm. The room we had had two double beds, which suited us fine. It had one of the smallest bathrooms I've ever seen. And I've stayed in tiny hotels in Europe. It was impossible to shut the bathroom door without doing some kind of little dance and almost climbing into the shower. Half of the firepits weren't working, and they're located in the middle of the main driveway to the hotel. A good idea, but horrible location.
I could eal with all of this if it weren't for the thinest walls I've ever seen. Whenever our neighbours came home it felt like they were having a conversation in the room with us. That coupled with the elephants we had on the floor above us, and the traffic from the road outside...I've never been more thankful to have earplugs with me.

The Westin sure does look impressive from the outside but the whole feel changes once you step inside. It is dark, perhaps, a little too dark on the inside. Check-in was fast and efficient and the concierge was awesome, but you could really feel like you've stepped back in time. The elevators were perhaps the hotel's only saving grace - it felt new, and fast, and the views were gorgeous! The corridors on the guest room floors were new though and the colors were bright. Rooms were dated but well maintained nonetheless. All in all, it was an OK stay. I wouldn't return unless it was through Pricelines again.
Tiny rooms, but clean and the location of the hotel was perfect.breakfast was not great but you could not complain based on what we were paying.would definitely go back

Was in Chicago for a convention and had a limited budget. Found the Whitehall fit into that budget and was in a perfect location. I was concerned about some of the reviews on yelp and tripadvisor but, I thought I would give it a chance. Yes, it's old and small. Yes, it could use a makeover. But, for the price it's awesome. I did see the strings hanging of the chair in my room that someone photographed. Maybe I got the same room. But, come on, who cares. I wasn't hosting a social event. The place is clean. Things are worn but, not warn out. The bed is comfortable and they give you lots of fluffy pillows. I felt very comfortable leaving my personal items out on the bed or bathroom counter. The staff was extremely friendly and helped me quickly. The air conditioning was noisy and I had to use ear plugs. However I don't think it was any different then any other hotel in the area. The Four Seasons is directly across the street and at $--- per night they provide ear plugs for you. My friend stayed there for the same convention. The shower at the Whitehall gave me a warm shower everyday and the safe was large enough to hold my laptop. Bottom line if you want to pampered in a luxury hotel, go to a luxury hotel. If you want a great value go to the Whitehall.

Loved the location of this hotel. - blocks from the shops on Mich. Ave, - minutes to Ohio Street Beach and - minutes to the night life of Rush street. 
My room on the --th floor was large, clean and had a view of the lake.
My only complaint was the loudness of the A-C unit. I had to turn it of af night as it sounded like there was a train going through the room.

I booked at the Novotel based on the reviews I read on this website. I paid $----night for - double beds for - nights at the end of April (thru the website). While the hotel is passable, it is definitely not worth this much money, when for a bit more, you could get a --star hotel, or for a bit less, you could stay at the Comfort Inn or Super -, which includes a continental breakfast and an equally good location.

We are just back from three nights at this lovely little hotel on the Upper East Side and this is to say that we loved everything about it. The Franklin is comfortable, gleaming, quiet, lovely and clean. It combines the charming feel of another time with up-to-date features and amenities. The staff is extra helpful and friendly. If you are planning museum visits, the major UES museums are quite nearby; in general the location is only inconvenient if you are a person who won't take the subway: a -, -, and - line express stop is just one block away. Yes, the rooms are tiny - we had a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""superior queen,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which while small is not the smallest room in the hotel (that's the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Petite Queen,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which, seriously, is best for people of moderate stature traveling solo) but it suited us very well. If you need a lot of room, or come to New York to spend the days in your room, then don't stay here. Our family reunion was at this hotel July ----. The mosquitos and crickets were awful. The bathrooms contained much mold & mildew on the ceilings and cracks. Dead crickets were all in the lobby area. Overall, the hotel was not clean. The pool in located in the courtyard and debris from flowers-trees was in the pool.

My husband and I stayed at this hotel after our Philadelphia wedding and hosted a wedding brunch here the morning after our reception. I remember it being one of the easiest events to coordinate and the room, food and staff were spectacular.
Now, almost -- years and - kids later - we went back to philadelphia for a weekend and, of course, decided to stay at the Westin Philadelphia. We were not only not disappointed, our expectations were far exceeded during this stay. 
The room was amazing - the beds are just as heavenly as we remember them - so even -- years later that just goes to show that this hotel's management really takes care of it. The shower was great, the decor was beautiful and the TV and high speed internet were perfect. The channel lineup was great and, even with stormy weather, the satellite system didn't go out. The in room movies were a bit pricey at $-- each but they were all just-released out of the theatre and they even had older movies for $--$-- so something for everyone.
But, the best part had to be the warm, attentive and professional staff. They are incredible and we have to commend Ryan at the front desk for making this stay so relaxing and memorable for us. The location for this hotel is perfect - right in downtown and close to everything. The rooms are beautiful, the staff is friendly and the price is comparable to every other hotel - this place does not disappoint and we'll be back!
Thank you!

From the moment you walk in, you'll be taken aback by the impressive decor. The service that comes along with it creates a warm and welcoming feel. 
The room was spectacular and truly makes you feel like you've really travelled someplace wonderful, while still feeling """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""homey"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". 
I would certainly come back here again!

Called last minute after landing at Houston Hobby Airpot, and got a room for $-- with no discounts! Only minutes from the airport but without the street or airport noise. Very friendly front desk staff and, for the rate, a very reasonable free breakfast in the morning. Room was clean, king-size bed was comfortable, and the pool appeared better than most (although it was too chilly to jump in).

I saw some pretty variable reviews of the Dream but went for it anyway, primarily because we got a good deal and due to location. When we arrived, I asked for a room on the --th floor (as advised) and I have to stay that we had a really great experience. The room was small but really nice and perfect for what we needed.

We are early thirties with no children. We usually go for boutique style hotels and we really liked the Dream and would definitely recommend it to others in a similar position.

For a short, family trip, this hotel was in an good location in relation to most of the attractions (Riverwalk, zoo, Sea world). Staff was professional and gave us a positive guest service experience when we asked to move rooms because of pool noise. The staff moved us the next day to a room on the other side of the hotel, however, there was a bar across that side of the street so the road noise was also loud. This was nothing the staff could have avoided and it didn't ruin our experience. 
The only negative we experienced was that the one and only computer they hotel offered for guests to use did not have internet connection. The connection in the rooms with our laptop worked perfectly fine!
Breakfast was great and I was impressed with the manager who asked a guest without a shirt on to go back to his room to find one. I thought that was respectful for her to ask for the other guests eating.

This hotel is all about the location, close to some of Manhattan's main attractions, Central Park, Broadway, Time Square, etc. We would also recommend the Park Cafe, which is connected to the hotel. The food is great and the service is excellent. As for the Hotel, when you go past the lobby it all becomes a bit tired looking. Hallways and our room were shabby, and in definite need of a makeover ( not what you expect when you are paying $--- per night, even taking the excellent location into account). Photos of the guestrooms on their website were certainly not accurate in comparison to the standard of our accomodation. Would definately recommend this hotel for location but not for value for money.

Such a great experience! In the heart of downtown, easy access to everything, beautifully decorated room, great view of the Puget Sound, great comfy beds, AND huge plus for business travel, there's free wi-fi in the rooms and free printing in the business center. Couldn't ask for more and will be back.

Booking through Amex Platinum Concierge Service this was my first visit to a St. Regis (part of Starwood Luxury Collection so got my points too!). I usually stay at the Waldorf in NYC but wanted to try this historic property. The building itself is amazing and one of the best of its style in the city. The lobby is posh, albeit quite small and will not tolerate much of a crowd. Nevertheless the staff were very nice. I appreciated the personal touches of bringing the key around the desk to hand it to you in person, and the offer for assistance with not only luggage but unpacking as well.
While I declined the unpacking I did end up calling the butler for assistance with touching up a shirt for a concert that night. Ok - I did feel a bit odd the first time, but the service was so professional and helpful (I was brought some tea while I waited for the shirts - impeccably finished I might add, with tissue in the sleeves and silk links on the french cuffs!). I quickly became used to calling for my coffee first thing in the morning. My room deal (if you can call it that at that price) included a continental breakfast in the main restaurant, a beautiful space off the lobby. It was great, although I thought $-- was a touch steep! I used room service once and it was prompt, good food and beautiful presentation.
The room itself was beautiful and equipped as one would expect at this price point - bedding, bath amenities, etc. were superb. The turn down service was wonderful. No charge for small things like bottled water, coffee, etc. A small thing perhaps, but many expensive hotels still nickel and dime you on such things.
I used the spa for a facial and massage which were great. The gym is in the same facility - it is nice, but rather small. Additionally, if you are there after hours for the spa you must call the desk to gain access - this is unacceptable and access should be gained by your room key.
Overall I loved this property and hope I can stay there again!

I stayed as a Katrina evacuee. I checked in late Sept., --, and I was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""checked out"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" early Oct., --.

We stayed one night at the Hotel -- during a stopover in New York City. We deliberately chose to be in Chinatown as we wanted an authentic Chinese dinner in the evning. We knew in advance that the hotel is close to the Manhattan Bridge and you do hear the train at night, a sort of low thudding sound, although it didn't keep is awake. The beds were two queen sized, clean and comfortable although to get to the -nd bed you do need to shuffle past the -st one, there's not much room. When we checked out in the morning the hotel was kind enough to allow us to leave our bags with them until our transportation to the airport arrived, we also could wait in the lounge which has complimentary tea and coffee available. All in all this a good hotel, reasonably priced but you have to know about it's location, we'd be back for sure.

We stayed for - days in this hotel with our --moth old baby.
It was just perfect, especially if you consider the reasonable price. Great restaurants and shops just around the corner; not very noisy or touristic neighborhood, free parking, easy access (by car) to main city attractions.
Room was spacious and comfortable, and they had free internet acces (though it was not wireless). 
We highly recommend it.

We stayed at the Belvedere for three nights in September. It was the first stop of our Honeymoon. I booked the hotel on the basis of the comments posted here. We were not disappointed. This was our first time to New York and really had no idea where to book. The hotel was in an ideal location. It was off a busy street and therefore that bit quieter. The room was large with two king size beds, and it even had a decent view out the front of the hotel. The bathroom was new and clean and it was handy having the addition of the kitchenette, with tea and coffee making facilities and a fridge.
The first day we walked to the Empire State Building, Central Station, Macys etc and the hotel was ideally located. We managed to find a great Brazillian restaurant round the corner on the first night which meant we never had far to walk. The second night we dined in a French restaurant, again just round the corner, it was superb. It meant we never had far to go at the end of the night.
I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel, my husband and I both work in the hotel trade, and are probably that bit more critical! We are definitely going to return to New York soon and would not hesitate to book the Belvedere again.

I stayed here for a conference with my boyfriend for a combo business-pleasure vacation. The only reason we chose this hotel was for the conference room rates. We had never been to Chicago before. 
First, the great:
We booked an extra night beyond my conference dates and the hotel gave us the conference rate for the room.
Our front desk service was exceptional with Pablo. It was not only easy but he was so pleasant and welcoming, it put me at ease. He got us into our room -- minutes before check-in time.
The support we received with checking our bags in the lobby and getting taxis was very good.
The concierge helped us with choosing a great Italian restaurant.
Another front desk employee (I think Alfredo?) helped us with restaurant choices, going so far as to call to find out about vegetarian options. 
We had a sink issue in our room, and it was dealt with immediately while we were out to dinner.
The beds are super comfortable and the rooms with queen beds are spacious.
We got free wireless through the conference rate. Awesome. (But it would have turned me off if I had to pay $-- per night for wireless in the room. This is an unnecessary fee to charge.)
Next, the not so great:
Booking the rooms was very difficult - I had to call at least --- times to deal with pre-payment due to my conference reimbursement, and I received different information repeatedly from each person I talked to. This is exactly what turns me off from large hotel chains. 
The hotel has obviously worked to upgrade the rooms...to a point. We had a nice granite sink and large shower head and new tile. This is nice....except that all of the hooks for towels were either not in place (holes in walls) or falling off the wall (we used it anyway) which made functionality more difficult. I think we used more towels because of this. So, it is nice to have things look pretty but if it isn't functional, it doesn't matter how pretty the tile is....and the wallpaper and doors were peeling and chipping, so it really was a tile job and that is all. I'd rather have no tile but a well-maintained bathroom.
Our tub drain was weirdly sticking out and we couldn't put it down. 
We had a leaky sink...if we let the water run for more than -- seconds, the bottom of the vanity cabinet would start dripping water. 
The pool was impossible to use because of crowds of children running with noodles everywhere. I like kids....I really do....but one hour of adult swim at the end of the night would have been nice, especially with ---+ degree temps. 
Overall:
It was a decent stay, but I would not choose it for the regular rates. I'd prefer a smaller hotel with better maintained bathrooms and a pool we can use. But I did feel we had good service. Our thanks to Pablo and Alfredo.

The only decent thing about this hotel is the location, which is excellent, I've stayed in better value hostels.
The room was dirty, the ceiling plaster had a great chunk missing over the bed and the shower backing was falling off the wall The staff were just not interested. The decor dated from the ----'s and was all various shades of brown, grim and depressing 
Only stayed one night , then found somewhere else.
The staff was friendly, the value was good, the beds were comfortable, but the room and bathroom were very cramped. There also seemed to be a problem with the HVAC in the room - not functioning well.

The hotel was great, it was in a great location right near the OSU hospital. The reason for being in the area was the best but the Staff was very friendly and welcoming. They were very understanding due to the situation of my son being in the hospital. The rooms was very clean and the housekeeping staff took great care of us. Food place close by, as well as some shopping. This is are hotel when we come up to go to the hospital.

We recently spent a week at the Hyatt Islandia. The room was very clean and in very good repair. The view of the Harbour was wonderful. We had a sea lion outside our balcony on a couple of days. The service was wonderful. The concierge was extremely helpful in locating several amenities close by. The staff and managers at the hotel were also very helpful and courteous. I would come back to the Hyatt Islandia in a heartbeat.

This hotel was beautiful! The rooms have super comfortable down comforters, pillows, and a Sleep Number bed! The room was clean and comfortable. The staff members were very friendly and accomodating. The location is also excellent! There were many wonderful bars, restaurants and shops all within walking distance. We will definitely stay here again.

I might choose an apartment to cut costs next time, as I did feel I was paying a lot for such an old room.

Arriving in Denver for the first time, we decided to book a hotel close to the airport, after landing and picking up our hire car we headed off to the hotel which is very close by. First impressions the staff were very helpful and polite, one male member of staff reminded us of alan carr the comedian !!, the room was spacious, the bed comfy and the sheets clean, breakfast in the morning was good with several juices, cereal and toast, overall i would recommend to anyone travelling to Denver.

The staff is incredible. From the moment I pulled in front of the hotel the bell staff was taking the luggage and arranging to park the car. The front desk was excellent and accommodated a new request with a smile & efficiency. Everyone always greets you with a hello & a smile, holding elevator doors or eager to answer questions or help in every way. The rooms are fantastic, comfortable & efficient. Very clean. The pool is always great, my daughter can swim in there for hours. So convenient to all mid town manhattan areas and being adjacent to Central Park is a huge plus. I've stayed here a number of times and will do it again.
Highly recommended!!!!!
We were told that there would be construction when we made the reservation and we were actually given a choice to stay on the --th side vs the construction site on --th when we checked in. But, we wanted the park view and opted for the construction side. I would probably change that next time and take the --th street side. But, it's NYC and there's lots of noise. It's not the hotel's fault that there's construction going on next door.
I booked this hotel two months in advance via a Groupon offer. At present, two weeks after my stay, I am still trying to sort out how I got double billed. By Groupon and By the Yotel

We have recently experienced a very comfortable - night stay at the Hotel Metro. This was our second stay in NYC. 
From the moment we arrived we were well taken care of. All of the staff we met were friendly, professional and very helpful.
 We took an early morning flight from the UK to JFK which meant that we arrived at the hotel around -pm – as check in is -pm our room was not ready. We left our bags with the bell boy who stored them securely for us and set off to orientate ourselves in the city.
We were gifted with an upgrade to one of the two bed roomed suite rooms at the front of the hotel and on the -th floor. We could see the Empire Sate Building from the bedroom windows. The room was a little tired looking but very well appointed and very clean (the hotel is currently refurbishing its guest rooms). Other than from the expected street noises the suite was quiet and we slept very well. 
The suite had three “pillow top” beds with heavenly soft pillows and egyptian cotton bedding, two large flat screen TV’s, two iPod dock-radios, a fridge, dining table & chairs, safe, two individually controllable air conditioning units and more than ample storage space. The walk-in closet was a good size and contained an ample supply of coat hangers, an ice bucket, an iron & board and two good sized umbrellas. 
The bathroom was a little tired looking but very clean & fit for purpose and provided us with a over bath shower, wc, hand wash basin, vanity mirror, shaver points and a wall mounted hair drier. The main bedroom was appointed with a second vanity sink – useful when two of us were getting ready in the mornings.Note the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was given a average score purely as it was one of the rooms which is awaiting refurbishment. Once complete this room would be awesome!
 Our housekeeper was very efficient, changing beds and replenishing towels and toiletries as required. There was always a great supply of fluffy white hand and bath towels and face cloths. The Gilchrist & Soames complimentary toiletries were lovely!
We enjoyed the breakfasts and the ability to grab a hot drink ---- , The bagels, muffins, pastries & breads were always very fresh, there was additionally choice of fruit juices, hot beverages, cheese, preserves, butters, yoghurts, cereals and assorted fresh fruits to chose from. A PERFECT start to the day for us!
The hotel is very conveniently located and is in easy reach of Macys, the Empire State Building, Rockefeller Centre, Broadway, Madison Square, the Flatiron, Times Square & Herald Square & Penn stations.
The view from the roof terrace if the Empire State Building and the city at night is breath taking and should not be missed!
Will we return and-or recommend the Hotel Metro to fellow travellers? 
ABSOLUTELY YES!!!!

The front desk guy was curt and not friendly. He definitely had somewhere he'd rather be...I was handed keys and given no direction to the room or elevator, but a friendly gentleman in the restaurant was helpful in leading me to my room, which was perfectly nice with a very comfortable bed. Most unfortunate about the front desk attendant was that he saw that I was there with an organization and did not tell me about the breakfast that was included with my group. I had to talk to other coaches there for the tournament to find out about this, and paid for breakfast one morning at a Panera when there was a banquet breakfast set up for us. I got to enjoy the breakfast the next morning but was disappointed about this omission.
We had banquet breakfast and a large banquet dinner, the dinner food was extremely disappointing, salad, pasta on which you could put your own marinara, chicken fingers, and hard garlic bread that was almost inedible. I picked at my food and had to eat dinner after because I was still hungry.
Regarding my room, housekeeping bothered me many times throughout the first morning I woke up there, each time I yelled back that I would be out in about an hour...other than those aforementioned complaints of the staff, other members of the staff were quite friendly. Any housekeeper I met in the elevator, the bartenders, all were very nice and the bartender remembered me when I went back the second night! My grown daughter and I stayed at the Orchard Garden for several nights in Feb and were very pleased with our accommodations. I don’t think you get a great hotel but they are extremely convenient if you are visiting the Children’s hospital - if you call them by phone they will also do a CHB rate. Stayed here last year. Just a base for us to explore Hollywood from.

We were very disappointed with our stay at RBI. While the grounds are beautiful, the property is old and tired looking. Guestrooms have dated furnishings and are not well maintained. Had lunch at the Veranda restaurant which was below average. Wedge salad with pancetta had a few tiny crumbles of pancetta and was not that great. Fries were ice cold. I expeced more of a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Four Seasons"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" type staff based on the cost and other reviewers comments. We checked out of our first room b-c of the noise and A-C not working. There was a HUGE spider in our bed in the second room so we had to switch rooms again at -pm at night. I understand things like that happen, but it is still unpleasant. The front desk staff member who helped us find another room was very kind and helpful. She was the most accomdating staff member we met. 
When we advised the staff of our complaints, they were not eager to help. The check out staff member simply thanked us for our comments and said she would relay them to management so it could help the next guest. Well, that doesn't really help ME at all, does it? So we had to ask to be compensated for the inconveniences during our stay as she did not offer any solution. She acted like she had never addressed a guest compaint before and only offered to cover our breakfast from that morning. Most high end hotels would upgrade you if you had to check out of your room even once.... we had to change rooms twice and were not upgraded or offered compensation.
I would NEVER go back to this hotel and would not recommend it to anyone. I expected way more for $---+-night. I am surprised by the high reviews. We probably would have been better off at the courtyard marriott up the street. I've stated in Holiday Inns that were nicer.

First of all, the room was small and everything looked so old, but the worst was when we discovered that the air condition wasn't working at all on a hot and humid day! The hallway was cool of course but not our room...We asked them to have it fixed by the time we got back from dinner.
We got back later that night to find a fan in the corner, and you guessed it, no AC. When we complained they moved us into a larger room (handicapped). We had to move everything ourselves as their was no one available at that hour only to find once we got there that the sheets were dirty and the bathroom hadn't been cleaned!! I was disgusted... We would've checked out then and there if it hadn't been -am.
The third room they gave us was a suite, and that's where we stayed for the rest of our stay, but we were off to a horrible start needless to say, not the relaxing vacation we pictured but stressful and completely unnecessary. My husband and I enjoyed our beautiful, comfortable room, the view from our --th floor window and the exceptional location. I would happily recommend this hotel and plan to visit there again with my next visit to Chicago

As first time visitors to SanFransisco, the Hotel was ideally located for our purposes. Spent one night at The Argonaut and wish that we could have stayed longer. We even missed the free wine hour but what the heck, the staff was so pleasant and not in a superficial,' I don't mean it' kind of way. I rated very good given the price that we paid is really reasonable.

Location is just off I--. We park near the front desk, just to ensure the car is safe. Well, overall impression for my - night stay is quite safe. There is Java coffee store and petrol station nearby. Drving to town is about -- minutes.

We needed three rooms for three families to stay close to the UW as we were coming up to visit our niece at UW and attend a football game. We got a great advance purchase price. The staff was very helpful as we made numerous calls in the days - weeks in advance of our visit to ask questions re. transportation to the game, off street parking, directions to pubs - restaurants, etc.
The staff was so helpful. We had gorgeous, comfortable rooms on the same floor and could not have been happier.

Nice budget hotel with clean rooms. The toilet was about useless as it backed up every time I used it. The staff were nice enough to move me to another room but this one had the same problem so I'm guessing that there is a problem with the plumbing system, and that all of the toilets are like this. Wonderful hotel, convenient to the convention center, the art museum (if you take the free Mall bus), and various restaurants. Really comfortable beds, great fitness center. One of the best showers I've ever had in a hotel. Would definitely stay again and highly recommend it. Only downer was slow breakfast service, but there are Starbucks and other breakfast places nearby.

- Columbus is a trendy hotel in a great location next to the Time Warner Center and - th Ave subway. Staff is friendly and helpful. Rooms are small even for NY standards. I stayed there during a weekend, and the experience was great. I got an upgrade to a fantastic suite, in the corner of the building, that had all possible luxuries.
The location of the hotel is very good, close to Dallas downtown. Service is really professional and discreet. Lots of options to eat at the hotel and close to the hotel.

I cannot fault this property. The hotel is an exquisite luxury boutique and my personal preferred style- elegant but a mix of rustic European with stunning hardwood floors-beamed ceilings, colorful furnishings. Tribeca is also one of the best areas of NYC- cobblestone streets, great restaurants and shopping downtown. Laconda Verde is also one of my favorite restaurants in the city. If you can afford to stay here, do it! You will have a wonderful time.
