We came to San Antonio for a weekend at the end of March ---- for a Birthday celebration. We called the front desk to report that the room was significantly warmer than to what the thermostat was set. The front desk clerk told us that he would notify maintenance. When we arrived back to our room, there was one fan in the suite. I'm guessing this was their way of trying to make it cooler. I called the front desk again and spoke with the clerk, Adrian. Furthermore, shouldn't a popular hotel make certain that every room is as comfortable as each guest would like? Their guarantee says so. 
Suffice to say, I won't be staying at any of their locations in the future.

A disappointing, over-priced, one night stay here. The room was spacious and comfortable, but curiously many the fittings were generally loose: a person equipped with spanner and screwdriver is needed to tighten everything back up! The staff were dis-engaged, and the breakfast on the mezzanine, comprising pastries and coffee or tea was cramped and unappealing.

This was my first visit to LA and I was delighted with the location of this hotel. We were within a short walk of the main sites on Hollywood Boulevard and we used the nearby metro station to visit other attractions including universal studios. This is a great hotel to stay in if you're not planning on renting a car because of its central Hollywood location. We were in LA for - days and walked to all the local sites and used public transport to get around with very little difficulty.
The free hotel breakfast was good and there was a choice of juices, tea, coffee, bagels, pastries, cereal, fruit, etc. The vending machines in the hotel were very reasonably priced and had a good range of drinks and snacks. There are a few places to eat nearby, including the ihop across the road, the In n Out burger next door and a -- hour Subway a short walk away.
The room itself was excellent value. It was clean and comfortable and the free wifi was useful but a little inconsistent. Our room faced into the pool area so this was a little noisy sometimes during the day. Overall however we were delighted with this hotel and I would definitely recommend it to others.

I am actually staying at the hotel currently, and contrary to the review below, there IS internet access in the hotel rooms (I'm on my laptop right now!). There is only wireless on the second floor, however, all other floors require a cable to connect to the DSL (available at the front desk).
The hotel is just as advertised - clean, relatively large rooms, nice bathrooms, comfortable beds. The staff is friendly and the resturant was good (the room service guy was extremely helpful and cheerful). The doorman has given us some great recommendations, and everyone has been accomodating. Plus, we're only a short walk from the conference we're attending at the Moscone center. 
It's a great, business hotel. It doesn't, however, have any bells or whistles - I certainly wouldn't rank it with boutique hotels like Dominion ---- in Quebec. It just didn't seem to have any personality of its own. That being said, I don't have any complaints, either!
Also, I had originally booked at the to be opened Orchard Garden Hotel - but when the opening plans were delayed, they moved my reservations without question to the Orchard, honoring my original price.

As early reviewer stated, don't listen to THE WHINERS! I've stayed at this hotel two times and the second time for over three weeks. No, its not your $--- a night hotel, but my room was clean the availbility of the shared restrooms was fine. I didn't have to wait for anyone. Most people just don't understand the concept of NYC hotels. Most hotels under $--- a night have shared restrooms. If you want an expensive hotel then be ready to spend it, but if you're in the city to see the sights, shop and enjoy the nightlife then stay here. 
NO, not all the shared bathroom hotels are clean as this one, but I'm a very picky person and I wasn't grossed out at all here. Don't stay at the West Side INN next door that was gross!!

On a whole our stay at the Warwick was pretty nice. I think the best part of the hotel is the location (walking distance to most attractions downtown) and the fact that they are a little cheaper than most other hotels in the area. If you go, don't expect a large fancy hotel. Request a high floor (-th or higher) for a view. The food and room service aren't really that great but there are some eating options that are very close.

I stayed at this Hampton for one night while attending a business event at nearby Seattle Center. The first thing you will notice is that the property layout takes some getting used to. I had a king room on the suite side - not accessible from the lobby level. I got a very detailed explanation (from the very helpful staff!) of the layout but still got lost on my first attempt. Once you get used to it though, it does makes sense. Seems like an unfortunate side effect of fitting the property on that piece of land.
The second thing you will notice (especially if you are a business traveler) is that there are no accessible-practical electrical outlets to plug in a laptop-cell phone-etc. I had to plug in my cell phone and lay it on the floor and literally crawl under the desk and unplug a lamp to plug in my laptop. If there were any better outlets they eluded me during my exhaustive search.
The free internet worked great and the complimentary breakfast was pretty much the same you get from any other Hampton - the coffee was very good. There is also a very nice ---hour super market one block away that was a nice place to get a late night snack. 
This was not the best Hampton Inn that I have encountered but it was also far from the worst. An okay choice if you need to be close to the Seattle Center and need a reasonably priced option. But charge your cell phone first!

Room was average sized for a business traveler, but big enough for one night and two guests. It was very sumptuous, from the bed to the lighting to the decor. Very luxurious linens on bed. Liked having the Ipod dock. Hotel staff was very helpful, friendly. Location was close to everything you could need for a great night in Chicago. Parking across the street was $--, which was very reasonable.
Didn't eat in restaurant but it appeared very relaxing and inviting. Great atmosphere.
Got a great rate on hotel website and that made it even better. One issue noticed was that once floor in shower got wet, it was very slippery and there was no mat.

A bit pricey, but worth the money, as you stay close to all the attractions, - minutes walk from the subway. 
I would mostly recommend it to people coming here for business.
Rooms are clean, service professional, all a businessman would ever need in D.C.!

Three best things about this hotel? Location, location, location. Seriously though, you are walking distance to everything near Fisherman's wharf, Ghiradelli Square, the Powel St trolley, etc. We stayed here for - nights with our - year old and - month old and we loved it. The room was very clean, spacious, and comfortable. The decor and fixtures were very nice as well. Bed was very comfortable even for my wife who is very picky when it comes to beds. We would definitely stay here again next time we come to San Fran. We got a pretty good deal through priceline. The staff were moderately helpful but not the best I've ever had at a hotel.

Columbus Inn is only a ---- minute walk from Fisherman's Wharf, at the stop of the no. -- bus and about -- yards away from the Powell-Mason cable car route, which can take you to Union Square. Because of this prime location, the Inn is situated amongst various - and - star hotels. However, its rooms are priced more competitively than those premium chains, and is thus a great find in this expensive city. There is also a Walgreens nearby which opens till late, so you are set for a reasonably comfortable stay.
Our room had the necessary amenities, but was not what I would call luxurious. However, it served its purpose for our sightseeing family vacation as place to lay our heads down at night. Ours was a family room, which had - double beds, and faced a side street off the main Columbus Avenue, so it was very quiet. We were also treated to spectacular sunrises creeping above the city skyline.
There is free wifi available, and the front desk will check you in for your flight and print your boarding pass free of charge. Apart from that, I am not aware of any other business facilities available.
One incident that I must mention here, is the hold they put on your credit card to secure your booking. This is done one week before your stay, and is charged not in the name of the hotel but the owner's private company. This caused a few anxious moments, especially when the first staff member I telephoned had not even heard of the company! They also put a hold on my card a couple of months earlier - a clerical error no doubt - but my email to them requesting an explanation still remains unreplied to date. No damage was done and my card was only charged at check-out, but the hotel management would do well to step up their customer service in this regard.
When all is said and done, the Columbus Inn is a nice little hotel and a great find for its price, given its prime location.

My partner and I stayed for - nights at Phily, we were on vacation and this was the first time we both were on this lovely city and wanted to stay on a good hotel, well located and -most of all- according to our budget; I know it may sound like a commercial but we got all that on Crowne Plaza. The first contact we got with the hotel was when we called to confirm our reservation and they were very friendly (and patient since English is not our first language).

I was warmly greeted by staff....Room is clean and comfortable....
Unfortunately the property is surrounded by construction on both freeway and backside building.

The first night, a good sleep, normal traffic sounds.....However, - nd night was noisy with off site construction.....i know management cannot control off site public works ....once construction ends the hotel will be a nice place to relax.... Parking is well lit and plentiful. Internet works well. Love the Starbucks coffee in the room.....Thanks again for the good humor at check in!

The Parker House is one of the grand hotels living off their past glories. While the lobby is lovely and impressive, the rest of the hotel is severely lacking. I knew I was in trouble when I got off the elevator on the floor to my room and saw how worn and dirty the hallways were. To say the room was small is an understatement. It was so tiny you could barely walk around the bed. The sound proofing is non existent. I could hear every person walking down the hall, every conversation could be clearly heard, and every toilet flushing in every bathroom around me. It was like trying to sleep in a dormitory. The bathroom is so small you have to close to door to be able to access the toilet. And I am surprised a hotel charging the prices they charge doesn't have wifi. 
Come for a drink in the bar, or to take a look at the lovely lobby, but stay somewhere else.

Excellent service, design aesthetic, and location. Have visited Boston many times on business and prefer Beacon hands down to Four Seasons. 
Great car service. JR

We really liked Hotel Max - the look is different and fun and our stay was really very pleasant. I heard about how some of the rooms were smaller but I asked for a larger room if possible and I got one. At the same time when I called they offered to move our travelling companions to the same floor (if possible) and it was done. The doorman that first day was really nice and helpful. I'm from the south so I'm used to more open friendly types but I did notice Seattle was not exactly like that - nice, but not overly friendly so it may seem to some people that they are a bit cold - I think it is just a different culture. The only complaint I had was that when I called to ask them the best way to get to the airport they stated a cab or town car. I wish they had mentioned that there is a really reasonable Downtown-Airport bus as well - we could have saved some money as the cab drive was about $-- but the shuttle would have been $-- for two people. Other then that I would totally recommend this place - it was a good value in a very convenient location with a certain cool ambience.

Have stayed in Boston many times but usually stay at the Lenox. This time we booked this trip through a price comparison site as we were also going to Cape Cod for a week and this hotel was on as a special deal. I knew that it was in a great location and the reviews were quite good. When we booked we knew that it was just a standard room and expected it to be quite small. When we got there the receptionist told us that we had been upgraded to a king size room which was a great surprise. The room was huge with a big bathroom and one of the most comfortable beds I have ever slept in but the best thing about this hotel was the service which was excellent. Everyone was really friendly and nothing was a bother even when my husband locked us out of the bathroom at --.--pm. Plently restaurants nearby. Trinity Church on the door step.

This hotel was terrible. Broken elevators. Cold, drafty, heat didn't work. Was the coldest night I'd ever spent indoors. Called the front desk and asked for a space heater, but none ever arrived. Went down to the front desk at -am to speak to a manager, but none was on duty. Checked out after a terrible night and switched hotels. The hotel agreed to refund my charges for the night.

This is basically an old, budget hotel with fancy water taps and a nice bed installed. I switched to the Hotel Vintage Park, which, when you add in the free wireless internet, was basically the same price. Plus at the Vintage Park they had a free wine reception and a free port reception every night. Really saved on the mini bar bill. Most of all, it was comfortable, inviting, well run and WARM.
Bottom line on the Max: Sometimes a bargain is no bargain at all.

Perfect getaway location right in the middle of all the action! I flew in from Las Vegas and didn't even need to rent a car. Ocean Park Inn is definitely my favorite hotel to stay at when in Pacific Beach-San Diego!

Excellent front desk service. Clean. But - a little scary. Best rate I could find near the Galleria, but I was not comfortable with the location and did not feel ---% safe. I would not recommend to a friend, so I can't reccomend to you. Pay a little more and stay at another proprty nearby.

My husband and I came from Israel for a - day stay in San Francisco before a wedding. The hotel is clean, the staff is excellent-helpful with every detail needed. There is free coffee, cookies and apples -----just a small friendly part of the general friendly hospitality. The location is perfect- we really loved this hotel and the price was perfect.

The hotel has so many advantages over the other options in the area that it is a no contest. Best location, easy access, free parking. Very comfortable , ample, and clean rooms for it's category , good restaurant and not too expensive. But the best part is the quality of service and the knowledge the staff has about their work and of the Mayaguez area. They volunteered information that was very useful and all this with a smile. It is a comfort to notice that the hotel has more than adequate but not obtrusive security, you know there's someone watching what is happening in the property.

We stayed there when we brought our daughter to UPenn to start her undergraduate program. I find the hotel very tastefully decorated, a lot of attention to details, textured walls and ambient lighting. The staff was very friendly & helpful including our cleaning lady who told us where to buy household items for the dorm.

We stayed at the Red Lion during our Seattle-Vancouver family trip in April. The hotel is super nice with a lot of perks when we booked this straight through them. We got free breakfast and free parking which was super nice. The location is at the heart of downtown shopping district with a lot of coffee shops and stores nearby when you step out of the hotel. The room is clean and the beds comfortable. The concierge and hotel staff were very courteous and knowledgeable of the local scenes. Of course to top it off, we got a super deal from them, and overall it's a great hotel for a family with small kids.
Of course you get free internet and free coffee and free breakfast, what more can you ask??!!!

We had a great time here. Since we were flying back home from Denver, we added one night hotel stay after our Thanksgiving visit to friends and family. The staff were wonderful. We have two small boys and they were treated nicely too. It was lovely having a goldfish guest in our room.

We only were in San Fran for a night, and chose to stay at Hotel Frank. Hopefully anyone reading this is fairly web savvy because it will pay off. We did have to haul all our stuff to our room ourselves when we first got there, but service got better over the weekend, and we had better help when we were leaving the hotel. Honestly, for the deal we got, this hotel far surpassed my expectations, I would stay there again anytime. Just don't eat at the sushi place across the street.

I stayed at this hotel for - nights while conducting business at NYU. Clearly the location cannot be beat if you are visiting NYU or the West Village. The bathrooms had vintage black and white subway tile but modern amenities. The front desk staff was pleasant and seemed to remember each patron. My only challenge was that I experienced quite a bit of noise even after I told the front desk clear that I was a light sleeper and needed a low traffic area. My room was on the first floor and faced the street and full of the sounds of NY. As well, I could hear the sounds in the lobby and patrons passing my door on the way to breakfast. So if you are looking for old NY charm, with some noise and a great location- This may be the place for you.

My husband and I stayed here during a little mini vacation and must say we absolutely loved every minute of it, our room was lovely and comfortable, bed was comfy, carpets were noticeably clean as was the whole hotel. We ate at the grand restaurant several times, very good breakfasts, overall we have not one complaint about staff or anything else. The location is great and walking around is fun, even did Angels flight, the only thing I could say I was not crazy about was the $-- parking fee. The guys working at Valet were so friendly and nice tho. Liked the apples in the lobby that were for us too.
I recommend this hotel to everyone. The room we stayed in was very clean. The employees were nice and very friendly. I definitely stay to this hotel the next time I will be in town.

Great Location, Service was nice. Rooms were clean and the workout facilities were a plus. TV service was also nice. I didn't like the fact that they charge you $-- - day for the phone, when I didn't use it. Otherwise nice.
Area recommendations
City Tavern. Great Restaurant. It's amazing to feel the atmosphere where Ben Franklin and John Adams use to kick back and drink a cold one

The Hyatt Regency is just a sophisticated business hotel is the middle of downtown Boston that also caters to families.
Take advantage of the great room service, fitness center, incredibly comfortable beds and prime location close to shopping and restaurants.

Stayed at the Park Plaza recently and it was a pretty nice place. I found the room to be clean and comfortable. It's in a great location and is really close to a lot of fun, touristy things like the Public Gardens, Newbury Street, etc.
My only complaint is that the hotel staff were slow to deliver my luggage that had been lost by the airlines. It took them almost a day to get my luggage to me even though the airline had already delivered it.

We heard from another guest that this also happened Friday night. Police did nothing as it was not a priority. We will not be staying at this location again when coming to San Antonio in the future.

I work in the area and fly out often, this property allows you to leave your vehicle in the parking lot and they shuttle you to the airport. I like the little lobby restaurant for convenience and not having to drive anywhere. There is a BBQ place nearby that is a little pricey but not much else. They have a washer and dryer here too. I like the staff and Dannika Brock is always on top of things, she really makes a difference when I compare to other Hilton properties. I have stayed here six times in the past two months and have always enjoyed my stay.

Stayed two nights with our small children. Perfect location for visiting the zoo, which was our reason for being in Jacksonville. Staff was nice. Breakfast area was large, and we had lots to choose from. The pool and hot tub were clean and great for our family. Hotel is near the airport, but we never heard the planes. Several restaurants in elating distance, and a short drive to a very nice shopping center. As with most hotels, the fitness room was small.

My wife and I came to the Marriott on our first trip to NY and absolutely loved it! This place is super clean, the location is the best in NY. We walked everywhere from here: Broadway, Ground Zero, Empire State Building. At night the view of all the lights on Time Square was pure MAGIC!

My recent stay at the Candlewood Suites was very nice... plus reasonably priced. The hotel is located in an industrial area (a variety of corporations, small businesses, a community college, etc.), but there are plenty of other hotels surrounding it. Also, I was glad to grab a sandwich for a late dinner at McDonald's & coffee at Starbucks in the morning... both were across the street. Of course if you're staying longer than one night you can bring groceries into your suite. There's a full kitchen... cook top stove, microwave, full sized refrigerator, counter space & kitchen supplies. The hotel does have food for purchase available, which you can pay cash for on honor system or charge to your room number. The gym looked great, but I was in a time crunch & didn't get to utilize it. The hotel staff was pleasant & efficient. I've stayed here twice for conferences & felt safe both times. My room was very clean & everything was in great working order. I'd recommend the Candlewood Suites as an excellent value for your money.

If you have a business meeting near downtown San Francisco, I would highly recommend that you stay at the Hilton Union Square. The hotel is immacuately clean, the staff are extremely friendly, and the location is very convenient to downtown.

Have just returned from a fantastic five day trip to New York with my brother.
Although we loved everything about the experience, Affinia -- has to take some of the credit for making our visit so memorable
Our room was clean and specious and the beds were incredibly comfortable.
The bathroom was small but very clean and modern and the staff were always very friendly and helpful.
In terms of location, Affinia -- is well situtated just a few blocks from major attractions such as Grand Central Station and the main shopping areas. The nearest subway is just around the corner and there's a selection of bars, diners and restaurants to suit all tatses and pockets juts a short walk from the hotel.
All in all Affinia -- offers excellent value for money and I would have no hesitation in recommending it to anyone looking for a friendly, reasonably priced hotel near to all the action
I'll definitely stay there again

The hotel is above average, but what is up with the loud banging elevators?
The noise from the elevators was very loud. We noticed the unusual sounds when we were going up to our room, but never expected to hear it from our room. (All night long)
We were unfortunate to draw the room closest to the elevator landing on our floor. Wow! I spoke with others and they said they could hear it from their room as well.

The closeness to the Alamo and River Walk are a plus for this hotel. The - star review doesn't do it justice. The only problem that we had with the hotel was our door would not close on its own. Told them about it - or - times and nothing was done about it by the time we left. Was good for the money, and the proximity to the Alamo, River Walk, Tower of the Americas, & Rivercenter Mall!! If you've read enough of these reviews, you know to disregard the best reviews because they were probably written by the hotel and the worst reviews because they were written by the competition.  The rooms were roomy and the bed was comfortable. The heat and A-C worked, the TV worked, the room was reasonably clean and the staff was very friendly. The breakfast was OK and there is free internet (which I didn't get in the $--- room I stayed at in Orlando two weeks ago). The area wasn't scary, it's tucked in with a variety of other similar level hotels with places to eat and drink and watch a movie within walking distance. 
 There were a couple of cons, but keep in mind that you're choosing this hotel because its reasonable. The common areas are a little threadbare and the beds don't have fitted sheets so the sheets don't stay tucked in while you sleep. That's about as bad as it gets.
 I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this hotel to someone who needs a decent room at a good price.

I loved this hotel. The room set up is amazing. When you walk in there is a living room area
that contains a huge big screen tv and couches. Across is the bathroom and a separate area for a desk and bar for coffee. The other side of the living room is the bedroom area. The room was very clean, king bed comfortable and free wifi. The breakfast was very healthy. There was fresh fruit, hard boiled eggs, oatmeal, cereal, bagels and Starbucks coffee and several different teas! Their free shuttle took us to a mall and picked us back up. The Quarry mail is an outdoor shopping area. We ate dinner at J Alexanders which is wonderful. I have no complalnts about the hotel. My husband and I really enjoyed our --th wedding anniversary there.

We stayed for -- nights arriving on a Saturday evening. Check in was easy & pleasant and because we were staying -- nights we got a free upgrade to a mini suite with fridge and microwave on the -th floor.
Room was pleasant, - double beds( not the expected kingsize), possibly a little dated, clean and fairly quiet with very little traffic noise and only one Saturday night did we hear any noise near midnight from outside or inside.
Room had wired internet access and heating- A-C, and free breakfast although it was really busy so after using it once we opted for a long lie most mornings.
Exiting SFO we easily were directed to the taxi rank and got a cab straight to the hotel for about $-- plus tip. 
Taxi's are available outside the hotel across the road at the Hyatt, and we also used 'knuckles' at the Hyatt for meals when we had a long day sight seeing.
A few points are to pre book your Alcatraz trip from the UK to guarantee a place on your preferred day, and we also bought a CityPass online and exchanged the printed voucher at the Pier -- Aquarium. This gives you - days travel on the cable cars, buses, trolley cars that run down Embarcadero from Fisherman's Wharf to Market Street ( near Union Sq). Plus admission to - attractions.
We also got the open top double decker bus which gives you - days of hop on, hop off, around SF and worked out at $-- (£--) for - adults and a child although most tourist brochures-guides usually have money off vouchers to reduce the cost.
There a quite a lot of homeless people in SF and the Wharf but never had any trouble. Also watch out for the Bush Man.

We stayed at the Doubletree for a long weekend November ---. We stayed on the HHonors floor (-th floor). Friday night we went to the executive lounge on the -th floor and service was outstanding! We loved our bartender, Samantha! She gave us recommendations on where eat, have drinks, things to do...and she's an excellent bartender! She was a pleasure! Room was great, bed was comfy, all staff were very attentive. Couldn't have asked for better. We will definitely be back!

In the beginning of May we visited New York for the second time, after staying in the Pennsylvania Inn last year we were planning on finding a clean hotel with better beds.
That certainly worked out with staying in the Hotel Garden Inn at -- west --th, it's a very clean modern hotel on a great location with good staff.
The bed was very comfortable and the shower was clean, we had an amazing time in NYC and that certainly has a lot to do with the hotel!
Next time we'll definitely stay at the HGI -- west

I explained about the power cords but the rep had me go through all the system and setting checks on my laptop before he finally determined the routers at the hotel had no power cords. No work done for two days, sink would not drain, water dripping from the ceiling into the bed, and even though I informed the front desk of all of these issues, the only attempt at making it right was to move me to a different room. No discount. Still no Internet for the entire two days. They obviously could care less at this hotel, and their not afraid to show they don't care.

This was honestly the worst, most unsafe place I have ever stayed. The hotel staff was behind protective glass and the front desk employee told us the reason was the previous employee had been shot working there. The parking lot was poorly lit and we had to walk down an unsafe feeling alley to get to our room. When we arrived to our room it was beyond filthy. There were stains on the carpet, chairs and refrigerator; the towels were obviously unwashed, there was a drawer missing from the armoire, the phone was broken, and there was a strange odor to the room. After turning on the tv manually since the remote had no batteries we heard someone trying to get into our room with a key card for several minutes. We tried to call the front desk for assistance to find that the phone was broken. The person finally went away and we got a hold of the front desk. They claimed they had accidentally given someone the wrong room number. Either way we weren't sticking around to see what would happen to someone next so we checked out and got a reservation at another hotel. When we arrived at our new hotel they informed us that the American Inn was known around town for being extremely shady and unsafe. I would recommend staying anywhere else in Memphis. Although it was kind of cheesy, the Heartbreak Hotel up the street was reasonably priced and extremely clean and safe.

Have always liked this hotel and we got a high floor overlooking the bay and pool area.Dont eat in the hotel as notimpressed with the restaurants but like were it is as easy to walk to most places.Same as others about the walls being thin as cud hear the tv in the next room as if in our room.But will always book this if the price is right as like being next to the little market with its shops and qaint little food places.

Our stay at the U.S. Grant in San Diego was very memorable and we highly recommend a visit.
Only negatives were noise from outside fan and no t.v. in sitting area.
Otherwise...perfect!

I stayed at Hotel Andra in late October. I was very impressed by the hotel. First of all, the design is beautiful and modern. The staff is very professional and accommodating. Check in and out was a breeze. The room was slightly smaller than we expected (we stayed in a Superia) but that's to be expected in a downtown hotel. Speaking of which, the location was wonderful. The hotel is about three short blocks away from the busy downtown center but it's one street over from hustle and bustle. You must try the Dalia bakery, right across the street. Delicious! We didn't have a chance to try Lola, the restaurant attached to the hotel, but it was always humming. The beds were very comfortable. The bathroom was gorgeous, very clean, with a large shower. Lovely granite bartop and desk. The lighting was a bit dim but I appreciate it over harsh lighting. We had a walk in closet that was lovely. The wifi was very fast. One thing I didn't expect was the atmosphere in the lobby lounge. Each night, hotel guests would sit and chat by the fireplace downstairs. It was very cool to see. Overall, I was very impressed by the service and design of the hotel. I would definitely recommend it!

We stayed here for one night in June at the end of a road trip through New England with friends and couldn't have been more pleased with our lodging. First, we paid less than $--- for the room, which was a special on Hotwire. Second, the small-but-comfortable
renovated room was clean and quiet, had a great double bed that ensured a good night's sleep and was located on the --th floor of the North Tower with a wonderful view of the Charles River and Cambridge. It was magical to look out at the evening lights. Third, the elevators came quickly and we never had to wait longer than a few seconds.
In our travels worldwide, we have found that free use of computers for Internet service is generally only provided at B&Bs and budget hotels. Thus, we were delighted to discover that the Sheraton Boston has bucked this trend, offering many free computers for guests to use near reception. A Starbucks is also in this area.
The hotel's convenient location includes indoor walkways to the Prudential and Copley Place shops as well as the Hynes Convention Center. We walked inside the mall areas to Amtrak's Boston Back Bay Station for our morning train to New York City. The concierge alerted me to this option when I asked about taking the subway to Amtrak's Boston South Station. His suggestion saved us time and much hassle with our luggage. We found all hotel staff to be friendly and helpful.

Wish they had staff out front all the time ...every time I went out someone was asking me for money. One of my fellow travelers got a big blob of white shoe shine spray on his black shoes by a man while he was trying to pay his taxi fare.
 It is too bad because it is a pretty hotel, beautiful bar and nice staff. 
Maybe that is just Chicago ...who know ....

Second time at this motel. Room was clean and front desk was very nice. Just off --- at Shore Drive. McDonalds right on corner so it's convenient for lunch or breakfast on your way out. Pet friendly and nice property. It's an average to better stay for the night
location is perfest for business getaway and has great work center and weight room. Rooms clean and comfy-Breakfast bufffett needs some help or a new cook.Grounds clean as well as pool

Very nice hotel. Check in was very fast and efficient. I was offered a two queen room, but asked for a king and the clerk cheerfully fulfilled my request. Hi, a group of - girls stayed in the Boston Back Bay Hotel for a long weekend - - nights. It was absolutely fantastic. From the outside, the hotel does not look that great and is showing its ago...sixty plus years but inside is another matter entirely and I found the rooms to be very nice. The Moore is definitely old, but nicely kept, clean and comfortable. It's location can't be beat, just one block from Pike Place Market and the waterfront (you will really appreciate just how close and easily accessible it is). There aren't a lot of hotels in that area that are in the price range of the Moore, so I booked it because of the positive reviews on TripAdvisor. 
I was pleasantly surprised, the staff is great, the decor is cool, each floor having it's own unique design. I stayed on the fourth floor which was leopard-like in color, and I had a single queen room that included a bathroom. It was very simple, so for those of you who are used to the typical chain hotels (like I am) it's a different vibe and feel altogether. Let me reiterate: s-i-m-p-l-e. No big screen tvs, no big showers and tubs, no pool, just a no-frills place to stay that's near where you want to be. 
Some issues: In the single queen room, there was very little shelf space to put your brush, hair dryer, makeup bag, shampoo, etc., so I had to keep putting it on the closed toilet lid and bringing it back out to the luggage. There was a tiny shelf right below a small mirror in the bathroom that was big enough to hold the toothpaste and toothbrush. Also, there is no full size (or large size) mirror that you can see below your waist. I had to keep jumping up and down on the bed to see if I looked ok. 
The bed was uber comfy and the windows are large and can open wide to cool the room off some. (there's no screen, beware those with kiddos). There's wifi on every floor of the hotel now (each floor has it's own wifi router), they'll give you the password and you're good to go. 
There's a tiny-cute coffee shop adjacent to the hotel that's owned by the Moore, it has great coffee-tea, some baked items and fruit to choose from. You can get to it from the lobby or from the street. 
The neighborhood is not the best, but you're only two blocks away from the better areas (see pics below). Definitely grab one of the maps they have available of the downtown area, it shows all the restaurants and hotspots you'll want to see, all of which can be accessed by walking and using the free buses that are available. The Moore is easy to get to using the Link Light Rail from the airport, just get off at the Westlake station at -th and Pine, it's a quick walk (yes, with luggage), but for only $-.-- (each way), it's the cheapest way to-from the airport and is clean and easy to use.
Would I stay there again? Yes. Absolutely.

First impression upon check-in was favorable and positive. The room was clean and a good size. It had a mini fridge that was larger than most these days with a freezer area that was roomy and worked which is something most motels no longer offer. My concerns were mostly issues that would be easily remedied if the motel wanted to do so. There was not enough light in the room once the sun went down and the curtains needed to be closed. Extra lamps in the areas on the sides of the room could help this issue. Apparently the waterproofing or whatever usually makes the shower curtains keep the water within the shower area did not work as every time someone took a shower the floor outside the tube was quite wet and we had to use extra towels to soak that up and the shower pipes sang when the water was on. The issue that would be more complicated to fix was the lack of electrical outlets. Usually there are outlets on the side walls available for whatever you need. However this room had only the outlets in use for fridge and microwave, the lights and clock radio on bedside table, and the tv and one small lamp on a desk. This made use of all the outlets in the room meaning we had to unplug items to use our personal electrical items. That was a first for me. Breakfast was fine; no real hot items but several things you could toast or microwave. Also the usual cereal, waffles, pastries, and juices. Do wish there had been more fruit, only apples the four days I was there. The staff were all pleasant and helpful when asked for assistance. Did not use pool or exercise area.

My wife and I stayed at the Holiday Inn on the Bay as the last stop of a long road trip. What a disappointment! The layout of the hotel is bizarre (multiple buildings), parking is expensive, and worst of all, the customer service is terrible. Everyone, from the valet to the restaurant staff was unfriendly. After sitting down in the restaurant, we left because of the incompetent waiter, and then tried to order room service. Overall, this hotel was a tremendous let down. You can do much better for the price in San Diego.

This hotel is one of those hotels which looks great on a website, but proves itself wrong after a two-night stay. The staff will do anything to NOT go out of their way. We stayed at the Bowery Hanbee over the New Years holiday. I can't say we would stay here again. The price was right, and the location wasn't bad. Just two blocks walk to the subway, and then only minutes to get anywhere. Chinatown was busy, but we enjoyed that. The soundproofing could've been better. There was hardly any room to store your clothes. A dresser or small chest of drawers would've been nice. The breakfast was alright, but there wasn't much room in the dining area. We found ourselves taking our food back to our room. The worst part of staying at the Hanbee was the manager. So all in all, it was a decent hotel, in a good location. But thanks to the manager, we won't be staying there again, or recommending the place to our friends.

Look forward to visiting San Diego again as we loved the Zoo, Animal Park and of course Sea World, just won't be stopping here!

rooms are on the smaller size, although my room had two double size beds, all very clean and modern, very quiet, I was near the top floor, great bathroom products, staff very friendly and helpful, breakfast was average, not much choice and nothing seemed very healthy.

I recently spend three nights at the Colonnade for a business trip. The rooms are comfortable but perhaps not as well suited to business travelers as they might be. They are a bit dark and rather than a desk there is a round table. For it's location right off the freeway, the comfort and space, amenities and most importantly price... this is definitely a hotel we will seek out the next time we need to stay in the Columbus area!

I am a Georgetown native and have stayed in-observed this hotel through the decades. This used to be a really well-kept, elegant hotel with a warm and welcoming lobby, very nice but restrained (and appropriate) decor, and professional staff. It was a place people sometimes stayed for weeks or months. It was never cheap but was also never silly-expensive (posted room rates are $--- for a single occupancy?)and what you paid really did deliver the kind of value for money one used to expect. It was also a very Georgetown institution, one that knew and was part of the local landscape. Now it has the slap-dash feel of a corporate absentee owner, willing but not very professional staff (I don't fault them; they do the best they can but some have only been in the country for a few months) and a thread-bare, shoddy, jerry-rigged T.J Maxx-type """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""plush"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" interior of the kind that goes to pot in weeks or months, not decades. If you strip off this thin exterior, we could have been staying at a Fairfield Inn in any part of country. But the Fairfield Inn would have given us more space and been better designed. 
Our room had a beaten up table, way too much fat, cheaply brocaded furniture for the delicate scale of most historic Georgetown buildings, unbelievably cheap-o looking lamps (randomly slapped-on gold and silver paint - TJ MAxx is actually more tasteful), over-stuffed, enormous beds with gigantic mattresses upon which were stretched under sheets that slipped loose during the night. The bathroom was a joke, obviously jerry-rigged into the top floor with a ceiling height sufficient for a -- year old. It had all the signs of shoddy workmanship (thick and cracked caulking slapped over wallpaper, thin shower door that barely closed, shower that constantly leaked, etc.) I can get a better rate and get more usable room space at the GTown Holiday Inn up the street. Not to mention free internet access and a reasonably priced, on-premise restaurant for breakfast. There was little at the Georgetown Inn to pull me back other than location, which is not that important if you are mobile or like to walk. I am not sure there is much to be done when you get to this stage of big corporate alienation despite all the touchy-feely attempts. This is not a neighborhood, elegant hotel -- but could be. The usual rates indicate that it should be. Hopefully someone will eventually buy up this property and make a real Georgetown hotel out of it.

Nice, elegant building, good location to the shopping streets. Large room, comfortable bathroom. The bed was too soft. My wife and I thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Westgate. The staff is friendly and helpful, the room was beautiful, and the location is tough to beat. We took the train to San Diego, and the ~- block walk to the train station was quite nice. We didn't miss having a car at all.

I stayed at The Curtis for a conference and loved it. It is close to the Convention Center, Starbucks, and many restaurants. The staff was great - very friendly and helpful. The place is fun. Pros - Building, room and furniture all very attractive. Front desk very professional. Cons – A swarm of ants emerged around midnight and took over the bathroom vanity. We had not visited San Antonio before, and relied on the staff for advice regarding restaurants and transportation, and found the staff courteous and very helpful. I would happily stay at the O'brien again.
The staff was very friendly. The location is very Convenient to the Pier -- and the cable car.

We live in a rural village in England. We are not used to noise, therefore, and if anyone ever sounds their car horn where we live then people turn up at the run from up to half a mile away to find out what the emergency is. 
New York was interesting to visit and in some ways stimulating, but if I ever went back I would take a room at the Casablanca, bolt the door and refuse to come out again until it was time to go to the airport. The sheer unrelenting bloody-minded rudeness of almost everybody, the constant wail of sirens, the cars hooting, people pushing, shoving, walking around quite literally naked, arguing, fighting and making obscene gestures to each other all defied imagination and rendered our four days there more of a trial than any sort of pleasure. 
That said, we were able to walk -- yards off Times Square down W --rd Street and into the lovely peaceful classic haven of the Casablanca. We stayed for six nights here from March --th. We were initially booked in to a Deluxe Studio. I am extremely allergic to cats and dogs and earlier correspondence with the hotel assured me that we would be accommodated on a pet-free floor. We were checked-in to Room ----. A five hour delay on our flight from Edinburgh meant we got to the hotel a lot later than expected and so were pretty tired after an unusually long day.
A quick scan of the room revealed that our bedroom windows looked out on to a terrace access to which appeared to be split between the two rooms on each side of us. There were two chairs sitting on the terrace immediately in front of the window our bed looked out of and this struck me as odd. Surely that would allow someone to look in? We reasoned that perhaps the terrace was not in use as otherwise we would be obliged to keep the curtains closed for privacy. As I say we were tired and after a quick bite to eat in a local diner enjoyed a very comfy night's sleep with the assistance of some pillows from The Benjamin's extensive pillow menu. You really should try it!
Next afternoon we returned to our room to freshen up before going out to the theatre. On stepping out of the bathroom shower I noticed that there was a guy smoking a cigarette on the terrace and looking in to our room. 
On arrival we had been presented with a letter from the manager Mr Labetti's office saying to get in touch if anything could be done to improve our stay. I phoned and spoke with a very pleasant assistant who having listened to my concerns immediately arranged for us to be moved - we were in fact upgraded to a one bedroom suite facing Lexington Avenue which was an extemely kind and much appreciated gesture.
The rest of the stay passed in a very pleasant fashion and all in all we very much enjoyed our stay at The Benjamin. The Underground is right across the street with a further station a couple of streets further up Lexington. Getting around is very easy indeed and as we tend to enjoy walking found we could get to the Broadway Theatres in a relatively short time.
We did not have a lot of contact with the hotel staff but those we did speak with were unfailingly delightful.
We would certainly recommend The Benjamin but do bear in mind the peculiarity of Room ---- - I dare say there are others with a similar outlook throughout the hotel. We just don't expect to have someone looking through your bedroom window -- floors up. You should also note that the hotel windows open so a terrace from which someone could gain access to your room should a window inadvertently be left open seems too much of a security risk. Again there is the privacy issue arising from the occupants of the two adjoining rooms having access to the terrace. Were we to return to The Benjamin we would be forewarned and avoid that type of room.

It is also within easy walking distance to many attractions, cafes and restaurants, yet it's not in a noisy area. We didn't try the restaurant so I can't comment on that. The staff let us print up our e-tickets for the Alcatraz tour using the laptop and printer in the lobby at no charge which was much appreciated. They also were happy to give directions whenever asked. Having free Internet access was great as were able to get info on attractions and easily find out how to get around town using the MUNI web site. The free DVD library is also a nice touch though we ended up having no time to watch any movies.
One minor negative point is that if your room faces the back alley you will probably hear garbage trucks going by in the early morning if you are a light sleeper, but this is pretty normal for a downtown hotel. They're not extremely loud but are audible. Our minibar fridge seemed to buzz quite a bit the first night but the noise seemed to disappear after that. Another small thing that was somewhat annoying is that our card-keys for the room failed to work on more than one occasion. On two occasions we had to go back down to the lobby twice to remedy the situation (on each occasion they sent us back upstairs assuring us the key would now work and it still did not). Again, this is not the end of the world but something that I hope will be remedied.
In sum, I'd definitely stay at this hotel again provided the price stays reasonable, and would recommend it to travellers who appreciate quiet, comfort and courteous service.
