Don't be fooled by their """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""wireless"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" services for laptops. It does not work in all rooms of the hotel. On my next trip to Chicago, I will choose one of the many other hotels.

This is a brand new hotel, so I decided to give it a chance by booking when it went on sale. I stay at the Ames Hotel normally every month (great property) but it was sold out when I booked for September, so off to Hotel Revere. 
Bad decision. 
When I arrived, the hotel had overbooked, or had a maintenance issue that did not allow certain rooms to be booked. I was given no call or email to let me rebook somewhere else. Upon arrival, I was kept waiting for literally twenty minutes (standing in front of the desk, with three bags, with no other guests around) while the front desk fiddled around. When the time had elapsed, I was told I would not be able to stay at the hotel - they could send me across the street to an older property that I never would have booked on my own, no upgrade. I would have to lug my bags back over there the next night and there might be a room then. 
I was shocked and asked for the manager. I had booked three nights. I told him I would take a loss on the third night but please book two nights in a row at another property so I could get some work done. I asked to be transferred to the W, which was a more comparable property. No upgrade available, and after much more arguing I was given the (-) night at the W. The Revere would not make the transfer for two nights even though they would have made money off it, and we (myself and the other unlucky traveler who showed up after me) hauled our several bags each up the street on foot to get to the other property.
What 'great' staff were the clients in other reviews dealing with? In Boston alone I have stayed this year at the Ames, W Hotel, Fairmont, and One Beacon, and have only met polished professionals with great customer service. The manager and front desk staff I met trying to check into the hotel left me with a terrible taste in my mouth. If you are kicking a first-time client out of your hotel because you did not manage your room availability, make sure they leave feeling better off than they came. 
I will never book a room at a property this unprofessional again. Back to the Ames.

Nice location in Old Town section of San Diego, room was clean and had a small frig and microwave, breakfast in ;mornings, wireleess and short walk to commuter rail. Very good value. Would recommend highly.

Whether you like or dislike this hotel seems to hinge on what each reviewer's particular needs or pet peeves. We just spent one week at the Doubletree Downtown. We were looking for location, cleanliness, comfort, and value. The hotel more than met our needs and expectations. The location is excellent: steps away from the Little Italy entertainment district, close to the trolley stop, a quick walk to the bayfront, and about - short blocks to the Gaslamp District. We enjoy walking, and found that we could walk to Balboa Park and the Zoo in about a half hour (North on -st Street, turn right on Laurel which turns into El Prado, and there you are.)
Our room was bright, large, and spotlessly clean. The staff member that checked us in fulfilled our request to have the best view available (see attached photos). The balcony was really a bonus and we used it frequently. Housekeeping staff were pleasant and responsive. The room was always clean and made up before we returned in the afternoon. The plumbing does make some strange, and sometimes loud, sounds, but we found that if we kept the bathroom door shut, it didn't bother us. Some of the wood furniture is older but not in bad shape. Chairs were new and comfortable. We had a new flat screen tv. The beds and pillows were extremely comfortable. We didn't have any problems with noise although the other rooms around us were occupied.
We didn't find this neighborhood to be creepy, and felt comfortable walking around at night because so many people were out walking or eating at sidewalk cafes. The hotel staff were mostly very outgoing and helpful. The hotel van driver that came for us at the airport was very informative and oriented us to the neighborhood on the way to the hotel. We did not use the parking garage so i cannot comment on that aspect.
We got an excellent rate for our stay and feel that we got a great deal for our money. I definitely would recommend the Doubletree Downtown and will stay here again.

I was a wee bit nervous about my three night stay at the Sheraton Marina, based on some other reviews. At check-in, the woman behind the desk gave me keys to a room in the tower, which she said had two double beds. When I told her I had requested a king, she switched me to another room in the lanai section on the ground floor. The room was clean, spacious and comfortable. There was a patio with sliding glass door that faced the tennis courts. The TV was a large flat-screen. The shower had one of those fab shower heads with a million little jets (and great water pressure). Oh, and the bed was super comfy. 
Housekeeping was great. The bed was made every day, and any towels that were left on the floor were replaced with fresh ones. While it is true that the hotel will award a $- gift card to use on the premises for every night the housekeeping services are denied, it is by no means a requirement to accept this offer. 
Normally, I avoid eating in (chain) hotels like the plague. Usually the offerings are lame and overpriced. We ended up having a late dinner one night in the hotel bar, and it was actually just as good as if we had gone out somewhere, and not super expensive. There were some surprisingly decent beer selections, as well. 
The main reason for my stay was because of work, and I was a little skeptical when I saw that the exhibit room was actually a giant white tent outside the hotel. It was a little strange, but certainly better than the dungeon-like, subterranean exhibit areas of other hotels. Equally important, the boxed lunches were way above average, and the deli-style lunch on the last day of the exhibits was pretty tasty. 
With all these great things, I will say that there was a lack of customer service in some areas. I tried getting in touch with someone – anyone – about a shipment that was being held for me, and I had to call practically every number just to get someone to finally answer a phone (thank you, concierge-lady). Same thing when I called to make the reservation prior to the trip. I don’t know if they are short-staffed or what, but not being able to get in touch with the front-of-house is annoying. 
Those minor inconveniences aside, I was still very pleased with the hotel overall and wouldn’t think twice about returning. 
(Don’t forget to say hi to the cute fish in the giant tank in the lobby!)

We had two rooms at the TS Hilton during the period --st to --th December --. We were happy with just about everything. Even the smoking rooms didn't """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""smell"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" too bad. (We had one smoking room and one non-smoking room). Our rooms were on the higher-up floors so we had a good view also (towards the Hudson River). 
The front desk clerk on check-in was helpful and very welcoming and fixed up our request for smoking room without any problem. (He might have been called Alexander - I'm not sure - I had thought to remember his name on check-in because he was so nice to us!).
Because we left generous tips in our room (non-smoking one) every morning and every night, we got good room servicing and at night we got our bed turned down and a replacement of bottled water and towels etc. This was important to me as we were able to shower or bathe at will without regard to how the towels would hold out - unfortunately probably without regard to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""environment"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". This was better service than our hotels here in Australia (only two towels per room here!). However, the other room (smoking) didn't leave a tip for night-time turn-down and they didn't get any special treatment - although their room was pretty daunting what with all the clothes and things piled up!
The security on the street entrance was a good thing. We didn't eat at the hotel generally except for one meal - which was Christmas night dinner - we had thought it might be Christmas oriented so thought we might splash out and at least get a Christmassy-style meal - but it wasn't - it was just the ordinary menu.
There was a bit of noise coming from our next door neighbours - mainly I think through the inter-connecting door - and that might cause a problem if you had really noise neighbours.
Also, if you are planning on going to a Broadway show or the like, make plans early - as far as I could see you have no hope of getting tickets unless you book in advance.

While staying in Beverly Hills for a business trip, my partner and I experienced the ultimate value, which is that of a front desk that is overseen by a caring, helpful, intelligent staff member. 
The front office supervisor, Dennis Phillips, made my trip and the work I was attending to, feel effortless and filled with ease. His assistance and personal care made us consider kidnapping him and taking him home with us.
We truly appreciated his hospitality. Sincerity, warmth and efficiency are a winning combination worth recognizing and certainly employing. Bravo to the Crowne Plaza for hiring such fabulous staff. 
It is the people of a company that make all the difference. I consider this property a valuable resource because of it.

I read some of the reviews after I made the hotel reservation and almost canceled because of the comments on the noise at the hotel. I am a very finicky traveler and can't tolerate a lot of noise at night. I did not cancel and gave it a shot. We had a great time and the hotel was very quiet. Our room was very spacious, and had a good city view. The beds were so-so. Not out of this world and not terrible. Upon checking in I asked for the highest floor available. She gave us a room on the --th floor and on the corner. I believe the corner rooms are a lot bigger after looking at the fire escape plan on the back of the door, so ask for one at check in. Overall, very pleased with the hotel.

Stayed here March, ---- for - nights.
Upon checkin we were offered a room in the building near the freeway, although not facing the freeway. Or the option of a $-- upgrade to be in the taller building off the freeway with bigger rooms.
They let us look at the room ahead of time and it was acceptable to us. But it was very small. I'm sure these rooms all have only - bed and NO room for a rollaway or a portable crib, no desk to work at. You would need to upgrade to a bigger room. But it was pretty quiet and unless I needed the space, I wouldn't pay to upgrade. The only odd thing was that they had tile flooring on the walkway outside the rooms, so everything that rolled by had a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cla-clink, cla-clink"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sound as it went by. Didn't hear it during the night, though.
They are not really close to the mall or the trolley station, but for a tip they will take you to the mall (where there is a trolley stop), about - mile away. It is close enough to walk, but not a great walking route, lacking safe space to walk in some areas. The trolley goes to many locations in San Diego.
Room needs redecorating, just a little dark, with peeling wallpaper, not a great place, but clean. Not bad, just not great.
Didn't eat at any of the restaurants, but the Sushi place seemed quite popular with many locals on Friday night.
I have been here before and once again the room was great, quiet. I asked for a quiet room and non-connecting and got an end room.

I have overall been very pleased with the Holiday Inn chain over the years for my business travel, but this hotel is the one glaring exception. The staff is disorganized and less than friendly and I had a horrible issue with the thermostat in my room that was not resolved for the - nights I stayed. Was not even able to sleep because the room was HOT (about -- degrees) despite the fact that the a-c was turned on high. Lots of noise, no cool air. Nothing was done about this during my stay and unfortunately I was too busy during the week to move to another hotel.
Avoid this place if you can.

I travel a lot...and stay with Starwood brands most of the time, as I am a Platinum member, but all I have to say about this property, it is a bit tired.
The public areas are for the most part in good condition, but our room was in need of a thorough cleaning, which would include dusting of the furniture and vacuuming of the cold air return in the bath area...it was just gross!
Staff were OK, but to have their Club Lounge closed on weekends, especially with how busy the hotel was on Memorial Day weekend, defies logic...--+ people in line for the Starbucks kiosk...

My boyfriend and I went up to LA for a basketball game and picked this hotel since it wasn't far from the Staples Center and Ramada was also promoting a half off booking special. The hotel was in a decent location, nice and quiet neighborhood with lots of options for food within walking distance. They do charge a parking fee of $-- but it covers your whole stay. The rooms are a little old yet comfortable. The only big issue we had was an ant problem on our second night. We didn't realize they were there until - am, since they were walking along the crack in the bathroom door, and by then it was too impractical for us to move rooms. Big mistake on our part. My boyfriend had a drink on his bedside table, and by morning, it was swarming with ants. We quickly packed up to check out, and when we told the woman at the front desk about the infestation, she merely shrugged and said sorry, which is not very good costumer service if you ask me. I would like to say I would stay here again, but the negligence of the woman who was at the counter makes me second guess coming here again since I heavily rely on friendly service when traveling.
I have stayed at the Park Plaza Boston before and never been disappointed. It is a fine old hotel still projecting an aura of luxury and right in the heart of town.....I will be back..

The location is perfect with so much to do within walking distance. The rooms are very spacious and comfortable. As for the service, I really can't say enough about the staff, we stayed there for a week and were just amazed at the leves they would go to make our stay as pleasant as possible. Truely a great experiance.

I stayed here one night on a business trip. The hotel atrium is large and airy and contains the pool and the restaurant...a good first impression. Help at the desk was very pleasant. The carpet behind the desk was dirty and disgusting looking which seemed really strange considering the rest of the atrium space. No gift shop, just a window next to the registration desk that contained a few items. Per the front desk person, they only had some of the items in that window. Room was clean, but bed creaked a lot and seemed very old. I could hear everything in the hall and the adjoining room so sound was an issue. Stayed on the -th floor and had access to the club. Elevators seemed really old and just felt dirty. Club space looked brand new and service there seemed to be good. 
Ordering room service for dinner was an experience. Tried to order a chicken quesadilla and was told that they don't have any chicken quesadilla available. Ordered burger with fries instead. Do I want chips or breakfast potatoes with that? I want fries like it says on the menu. We don't have any fries. Um, okay, chips. Would also like a bottle of water...we don't have any bottled water. I said it sounds like maybe someone needs to do some shopping, I was told that the chef is new. Co-workers that I traveled with said that they ate in the restaurant that night and that only - or - of the -- or so offerings were available. When I went to the club to attempt to get some bottled water, the man working there said that they didn't have any. When I commented that they didn't seem to have any anywhere, he said that they usually ran out around the end of the month because that's when they do inventory and reorder stuff. Went down to visit the window at the front desk to get water, and they had none available there either. If it was earlier in the day, I probably would have walked over the nearby gas station to get some, but it was dark, so I just gave up and went to the ice machine instead (no vending).
Overall, the hotel was okay. I would probably not stay there again and was frustrated by the experience enough to post my first review on Trip Advisor.

We stayed here for a week in August attracted initially by the very professional and helpful receptionist on the phone when asking about availability. Our spacious room was beautifully decorated and furnished. Bed was extremely comfortable. Nice large plasma or LCD TV. The balcony overlooked the marina. (Ask for a room on this side of the hotel rather than the other side overlooking a car park). The hotel had a very warm swimming pool to relax around, with bonus of a happy hour from -.-- to -.-- pm. Superb Bloody Marys!! 
Breakfast was excellent, including fruit, cereal,bacon, sausage, scrambled eggs and different breads. No rush and plenty of fresh coffee. A great start to the day. 
One huge bonus is the hotel next door, not to stay - the Bay Club is best but because it has frequent open air concerts such as Seal, Buddy Guy and Tony Bennett. You can sit by the pool in the Bay Club with your beer and listed to superb sound from next door. Choose the right place and you get a good view of the stage too. Saving you some $-- at the same time. Also there are many very classy restaurants within easy walking distance of the Bay Club on Shelter Island and downtown San Diego is only some -- minutes drive away. 
Will definitely stay at the Bay Club when next in San Diego and have already recommended it to friends traveling to California.

Got to Memphis, no reservation, phone app recommended Hyatt Place. We stopped at one in the midst of a busy office park, and it was packed, no rooms. They sent us five miles down the highway to this one, in a big vacant area waiting for office park to grow around it. Never stayed at one before. Location was dullsville, but close to the highway and some main streets, so easy to get places. Room was quite nice, would have been $--- to $--- in better locations. BIG TV with actual HD content (not blurry pictures stretched out wide), swivels to view right in front of couch or at the foot of the bed. Jack panel allows easy hookup of almost any computer, audio or video to the TV. Very secure building, all doors locked all the time (except front). Front desk person can cook you a meal in a few minutes -- hours a day. Hot breakfast is decent. Staff is very friendly and helpful. For under ninety bucks a night, we couldn't find a thing to complain about.

I visit D.C. every two or three years to see family and friends. I used to live in the Dupont Circle neighborhood; it's a great place and it's where I always stay when I'm in the D.C. area.
I'm a light sleeper, so the the most important hotel """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""amenity"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for me is peace and quiet. I stayed in room ---, which was VERY quiet. The decor of the room, including the bathroom and kitchen area, was nice -- everything looked newish. The staff was pleasant and helpful. 
On the negative side, the parking was limited. I found a space on three days; on the fourth I had to park at the Washington Hilton. 
The worst part of my visit was the closure of streets near the hotel for a parade. When returning to the hotel that day, I spent an hour and a half stuck in hellish traffic jams. I don't know whether hotels and car rental companies get advance notice of street closures, but it sure would have been helpful to have that information.
Except for the car-related hassles, my stay at the Carlyle Suites was really quite satisfying. I definitely will stay at the hotel in the future.

My experience with this hotel was not all that great. I paid a lot of money only to listen to a party in the lounge (on the first floor) in my room on the -th floor. After a long day, I was exhausted and at midnight the party downstairs was still going strong. I felt sorry for the people who had rooms on floors -, - & -!! The hotel was clean and the staff was very friendly. Thank goodness the lounge manager was nice and quick with our drinks! The man at the front desk tried very hard for about -- minutes to get us reservations for dinner somewhere close, but he could not. We ended up walking about -- feet outside the hotel door and found a wonderful Italian resturant that was completely empty!! Yumm. The valet service that was included in my room price I thought would be great, except that the valet was nowhere to be found when I arrived. My car had to be double parked on the street for about -- minutes while the front desk checked me in - very slow. I finally convinced someone to call the valet to come and park the car and was then told that the hotel was very busy for the evening and the next day and that for the unlimited """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""in and out"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" service that I paid for I would need to be sure to give them at least --- hour each time. I could have gotten a decent hotel room for a lot less, but this hotel came recommended by a relative and the website looked fantastic. I guess I have learned my lesson.

I had never been to Charlotte before, and we were traveling from central Pennsylvania for my sister's wedding. This hotel experience was like nothing I've ever known before. We were treated like royalty just for coming in the door. Everything was pristine, the staff was phenomenal (everyone, from the desk to the doorman to the waitress at breakfast), and the wedding reception was glamorous and we were well treated by everyone. The room was beautiful, the setup was extremely nice, the housekeeping was great, the TV size and selection was great, I can't say enough things about how wonderful this experience was. If you're ever going anywhere near Charlotte, I cannot recommend the Renaissance of SouthPark enough. I have a weekly internet show and we thought so fondly of the hotel that we gave the place a plug in the end credits to encourage anyone to stay there.

We returned today from our spring break vacation in D.C. with two grown children. We picked Capitol Hill Suites based on the reviews we read on line. We were able to travel easily on the Metro, returning late each evening to a spacious, clean, and quiet accommodation. Even though we had four grown people in the room, it was just fine in size and comfort. The office staff were pleasant each time we stopped in to ask a question or use the computer. The breakfast was a wonderful extra. Thank you for a great stay!

I have stayed in this hotel twice with a friend. It is centrally located for shopping and getting to know Manhattan. Port authority is just around corner, with bus connection to the JFK. 
Convinient size room for -. It is nice not having to eat out every meal, when you have coffee maker, fridge and dishwasher in the room. I also enjoyed the free internet connection. Bed is comfortable. No bedbugs. I warmly recommend this hotel for couples and friends who don't mind sleeping in double bed.

This is my -nd stay at the Vintage Park. The location is excellent as it is within walking distance of everything down (ie. market, public transportation, shopping, Belltown) and around the corner from I--.
I was given a King premium room which was located near the elevator but I didn't hear any elevator or exterior noise for the duration of my stay. Room was very spacious and included a couch, coffee table, desk, great ego chair, spacious bathroom, and nice size closet. I did feel the room was slightly dark vs. my comfort but no major problem
Stocked mini-bar but you are probably best served walking to the drug store a block away to acquire any beverages.
The restaurant Tulio offers a great weekend brunch-breakfast and I would eat there again. I felt the service was slow but I wasn't in a rush.
The hotel beats its competition (as in the bigger -*):
. Free Wifi access (usually for a fee elsewhere)
. Free wine-tasting every evening between ---pm (why bother with Happy Hour elsewhere)
. Quick valet parking.
. Located between the W & Crowne Plz so finding a cab is never a problem.
The hotel lags behind competition in that is doesn't offer a fitness center. If not your interest, no lost!
Save yourself money and visit the Vintage Park.

This is a nice, reasonably priced hotel - it's clean, fairly modern, and has comfortable beds. The staff makes this place as they are very friendly and willing to accomodate. Location is ok, it's near Times Square but next to the Port Authority Bus Station - great for catching cabs as there is a cab line just around the corner, but somewhat sketchy. There is a small bar in the lobby and a fitness center. I'd stay again.

Pros--Helpful giving family members adjoining rooms. Check-in and check-out were simple. Beds were comfortable. Room very clean and had mini-fridge, coffee maker and microwave in attractive, modern style furniture. 
Cons--upon checkin all bellhops were busy and we received no help getting our luggage to our rooms. Usually this isn't a problem, but the luggage was in our car and our husbands had gone to a movie. We waited around a bit for a bellhop, but had to meet them for dinner reservations so we hauled all of our luggage from the car to our room. On the second load, through the lobby and up to our rooms, still no help. I saw other women in the lobby also overloaded with luggage. No one showed us to our room, explained where the ice machine, restaurants, or other services were. Parking valets were a necessity here, because there was very little parking space and I believe they had to take some of the cars offsite. Parking valets were nice, just seemed a little too busy. Maybe Marriott needs to hire a bit more staff.

We recently stayed at the Laquinta for a short weekend trip, and we absolutely loved it....wish we would have stayed longer. We are very picky when it comes to hotels and resorts...cleanliness and a nice appearance are very important to us. The hotel is brand new...only open for --- months. The rooms are very clean and look wonderful...the rooms look exactly like the pictures that are posted on the internet. The room is decorated in bright colors, with dark walnut colored wood furniture. The bed is very comfortable. The room even had a DVD player (plus microwave and fridge). The rooms are a good size...no complaints. The hotel lobby, rooms, and other areas are pretty upscale for a Laquinta. A short drive to the Riverwalk (-- minutes) and Seaworld (-- minutes). We've stayed in numerous hotels in the San Antonio area, and this hotel is the best....from now on, we will only stay at this hotel during our San Antonio Trips.
Tip: Get to the breakfast buffet before -:--am; the line gets very long.

We had - girls on this trip to NYC to shop for wedding dresses in November, ----. We stayed Thursday-Sunday. The service at the hotel was great, especially the bellmen, who were very helpful when it came to storing our luggage before and after checkout; but they also gave excellent recommendations for restaurants & even hooked us up with some deals! They were awesome! The hotel bar in the lobby area is great. The food was wonderful and the service was exceptional there, too. One of the best chicken quesedillas I've ever had! Our only complaint is that the TV connection in the room was bad and kept going in and out and making awful noises; but we were only watching at night & while getting ready, so it was not that big of a deal. Also, all of our room keys stopped working one evening and caused us to have to move our dinner reservation to later. While security was pretty efficient in getting up there and letting us in the room, they never sent us new keys. Instead, we had to stop by the front desk to get them when we got back from dinner. Overall it was a great experience. Great deal for the price. I would definitely stay there again.

This is my preferred hotel when I am in San Antonio, which is very often. The amenities, staff, location and food are Awesome!!!! It's great checking into a hotel where the staff know me by name and know exactly my room preference without even having to call prior to my arrival. It's a very clean and accommodating hotel, too. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone that is looking for a hotel that is going to give you A BANG FOR YOUR BUCK!!!!!! Oh yeah and the heated pool, basketball court and gas grills were A BONUS for our family!!!!!

Our - night stay was overall disappointing. The hotel is tired, with limited quality facilities. There was no hairdryer in our room, one of our telephones did not work, there was a smell from the basin drain pipe and, incredibly for a hotel of this standard, the bathroom had a shower curtain over the bath!! A small bottle of water in the room was $-, the TV reception was poor.Perhaps the low point in our stay came at ----hrs on the first night when suddenly our room lights flashed on and we had other people who had a key card, coming into our room. When I raised this with reception the next day, there was an apology, but no action to follow up, and no recording of the event.
The highlight of the stay was when we dined in at Breeze Restaurant on our first night, the quality of the food, value for money and service were excellent.
Plenty of other good hotel options in this area - would not stay here again.
Standard stay at a place like this. Staff was nice. No noise or cleanliness problems. No issues and close to TCU stff and Ft Worth zoo.

Stayed here for six nights in late February and early March ----. We booked the hotel as part of a package deal with ebookers which included return flights with Virgin Atlantic. 
The location is great, just off -th Avenue, two minutes walk from the tube station at --rd and -th (around -- minutes from JFK with one tube change). We were given room ---. A fantastic room with a huge bed looking out onto a courtyard at the back of the hotel. Cleanliness of the room was fantastic. 
Breakfast is served on the ground floor between ----am. This consists of hot items (two items per day on a rolling tots - scrambled egg and bacon; sausage patties and omelette; Spanish omelette and fried potatoes), fresh fruit, yoghurts, bread and pastries, juice and the highlight (for me as I had one each morning!), a make your own waffle machine. 
Service from the reception was exceptional from check in to check out. 
The only disappointment for us was after check out. We had left our bags to explore the city on our last day before our plane left at -pm. On return to the hotel, we used the reception toilet and found it in a dreadful state. What a shame as a last reminder for this excellent hotel. 
With this matter aside we would wholeheartedly recommend the hotel to others and on a return visit to NYC we will check this place out.

Stayed the weekend at the Hampton Inn Convention Center recently and really enjoyed the stay. The location is very convenient, only about two blocks from the subway and a block from the Verizon Centre. There are plenty of restaurants on -th Avenue and on the other side of New York Avenue, all within a -- minute walk. You're also less than a mile from Union Station (but watch out for cab fares!)
The rooms are spacious and comfortable and the front-desk and concierge staff members were all very friendly. Our room was clean and in good shape...no wear and tear.
It was in the --'s all weekend and coming back from sight-seeing on Saturday afternoon, the front desk staff was standing ready with small bottles of ice cold water for returning guests; that was a nice touch.
The breakfast buffet does get crowded and to watch some people attack the food, you might think they believe they'll never eat again, but the staff did a good job of replenishing the food even when some families attempted to eat all their meals for the day at breakfast. I guess because it's included in the price of the rooms, people want to get their money's worth.
The area north of the hotel looks a little sketchy, but I never felt unsafe coming back at night from the subway in Chinatown. There was always a lot of traffic on Mass Ave and plenty of people on -th Street, and I liked the location because I think something a block or two closer in would have been a bit noisier.
There were no negatives surrouding the stay. I would definitely stay here again.

Recently stayed with my sister. Had connecting room but with extremely large chairs the walk thru both rooms was hardly possible. Closet sliding doors were broke. Small pool area with lots of butts on ground. Poorly designed bathroom. Our first morning we woke up to no running water. Was told plumber was called. Came back to no HOT water in afternoon. Last day our rooms were not even cleaned! Food trays were left on floor in hallway for - day. Night time sleeping used ear plugs since too many loud partiers. Will never come back!

I agree with all of the previous positive reviews of this hotel.The main benefit was the great location-we could walk to the White House or the metro in - minutes-a great bonus when the weather was so uncomfortably hot.
We had rooms at the rear overlooking the service yard but that didnt matter as it was very quiet-a good nights sleep without any traffic noise .The staff were very helpful particularly the concierge in booking tours and recommending restaurants-we loved the Ebbitt Grill just down the street .
The hotel bar was very good .We didn't eat in the hotel and just had breakfast in the coffee shop across the street .

My second visit to the Crowne Plaza in Times Sq. Everything I remember it being from my first stay was still the case. Great location, good size modern room with view out to the Hudson, great facilities and staff. The bed was really comfy and I love that you can't hear any of the street noise during the night - a rare treat for a hotel room in NY. I have no reason to look anywhere else for my next visit as this hotel ticks all the boxes.
Hotel was average. Good clean rooms. Staff friendly. Location is outside of the city but easily reached via the T on the redline. Applebees nearby. Good food reccomendations by the staff.

I booked a room at Dunhill three weeks in advance (prepaid through Hotels.com) for a colleague. When he showed up this morning, he was told the hotel was full and they had no record of the reservation. Since Charlotte was completely booked, he was out of luck. Hotels.com called the hotel and was told the hotel was overbooked, but agreed we had a reservation and they would refund. RIDICULOUS! Of course, if I don't show up, I am charged the room rate, but if the hotel cancels on me, there is no penalty for the hotel. This hotel is unworthy of four stars.

We have stayed in other NY hotels. This for us is tops. The rooms are second only to the W in Times Square but about $--- a night cheaper!
You will not be disappointed. This is a cool place for discerning people.

I travel a lot of work, and the staff at this hotel is some of the best in the business. Since my first review the owners have put many upgrades in the hotel. While still an older property, the rooms are clean and spotless. The staff is willing to go the extra mile to be helpful. 
Parking is the biggest issue when the hotel is at or near capacity. If you cant find a spot, just ask the front desk, and generally they can work something out.
This place is conveniently located but it is such an awful old building that I can't believe it is a super -. They really should call it Sewer -, go somewhere else.

A hotel basically right on South Street Seaport!!! Can't get much better than that in NYC! Close to the water, shopping, sights, great food...not to mention the nautical themed rooms...super cute! They even supply good quality toiletries...see the pics & go!

I chose this hotel based on combination of price and trip advisor rating. Best thing about it was location, -nd best was the shower (good water pressure and hot). Room was very tired with peeling wall paper and dirty net curtains. Beds were comfy though. Bathroom was Ok but had damaged mirror and cracked basin. I have stayed in better places in New York for the same price. All a bit faded with European styling that needs updating.

This hotel stay was so awful. There where bums at the front door. The floors where really dirty. I got yelled at alot by the manager. In all of my past hotel stays that has never happened to me. I wanted to leave but I had a no refund policy. It was my sisters birthday. I wish I could get my money back from our very expensive and awful experiance. This is by far the worst hotel experiance I have had in my entire life. In order to enter the hotel you have to get the door opened for you and you have to have wait for someone to walk down and check your id. You may not have anyone visit you at all! I did do research before we went to the hotel and the pictures where beautiful. It was not like the pictures. There is NO PARKING! Do not trust the parking lot next door. I witnessed a couple of cars getting hit and the owner of the car asked the attendent what happened and he acted like he didn't know. I have so many more compliants, but I'm afraid they won't all fit.

This was our second time staying at the hotel and like the first time it was great experience. My daughter and I like all the Art Deco and the staff is very very helpful and friendly. We will most likely choice to stay there again and again.

My husband and I stayed here Memorial Day weekend for a long weekend. The hotel is in a great location on the water right by the harbor. 
We took a water taxi from the airport which was a lot of fun. The hotel has a dock right out back where you can request a water taxi to take you anywhere on the harbor.
We did not eat at any of the restaurants in the hotel but they did look rather classy, so bring something nice to wear. We walked across the bridge to the Barking Crab and had wonderful crab legs and lobster. We also had amazing cupcakes at Crumbs bakery just down the street. 
The concierge was very helpful when we asked what was the best way to get to Harvard. 
South Station is a - minute walk from the hotel which gives you access to the subway. 
The nice thing about Boston is that it is small enough that you can really walk anywhere, and you want to because there is so much to see. 
My only complaint about the hotel is the bed. It was horribly hard and fairly uncomfortable. For a high priced hotel like the InterContinental I expect a much better bed.
We did have a street view of the fire station but hardly ever heard the sirens, they rarely went off.

In Chicago on business, I stayed here as it was closest to client. The hotel needs work, for sure, and if you're finicky about every detail you will find plenty here to turn you off--old, slow elevator, spots of peeling wallpaper, banged-up moldings, aged furnishings, electrical tape on the remote control. But the room was huge and everything worked, so for $--, it was serviceable for one night. The on-site restaurant was surprisingly good.
The staff was cheerful and helpful. The alarm clock was going off in the room next to mine and the beeping was clearly audible in my room. On my way to eat, I told the clerk at the desk. He rang the room but, obviously, the guests were out (or unconscious). When I came back through lobby -- min later, the clerk told me he had gone up to the room and turned off the alarm.

Our party had three rooms this past weekend and essentially, other reviews posted were on target. The rooms were small, yet ours appeared to have new carpet and bathroom tile. They were clean and comfortable and fit the bill just to sleep and clean up, if you want more than that, I'd look elsewhere. I'd look for discounted rates through thrid party booking firms. $--- - --- seems about right for the facility. Indeed the elevators were small, yet we didn't experience long wait times as others had menitioned. Again, good location if you wanted to walk to shopping on Michigan Avenue and there mulitiple bars and eating establishments within a - - - block walk of the hotel.
The Breakfast time were different than what was published. Good stay people were nice.

Stayed here for a few nights. Pricing is good for the location, and there are a number of restaurant options nearby. Breakfast was VERY basic (even for a Continental), with hard-boiled eggs only being offered every OTHER day. They do have the waffles every day though, so I'll cut them a little slack!
As a few other posts have noted, the walls are pretty thin, so you may want to remember to bring your earplugs.
This hotel is a good option for people flying in, with the intent of Seaworld being their main excursion. If you have any other destinations in mind, or you have driven to San Diego in a vehicle, I would recommend staying in a different hotel, and saving yourself a few bucks. I saw one of the other Howard Johnsons in San Diego advertised for significantly less than this one (about an - min drive away)!
WiFi at this location could use some upgrading and consistency also.....very intermittent.

This review is fairly long, so if you just want the point, here it is: do all you can do to avoid this company. If you want to hear how an anniversary plan can be ruined by an unprofessional apartment rental company, please read on.
If you are unfamiliar with WooGo (and I wish I was), they rent apartments out in major cities in the same style as one would stay at a hotel--you rent them by the night. We had arrangements to rent out one of their midtown apartments for a night in New York, and called in advance to clarify that the pictures on the website were actually of the apartment, since the photos were the same for different apartments on the site (same apartment building, different number of rooms). We were assured that the apartment photos appeared that way because despite the number of rooms, all apartments shared the same style foyer because they were all in the same building. Over $--- spent and a trip to New York later, we found this company to be one of the worst we've ever had to deal with. 
Upon entering the apartment building, the reception looked oddly nothing like the pictures of it on the website. As it turned out, the reception for Woogo was not actually in the lobby, and was instead on the second floor of the building. So, keeping an open mind, we ventured to the second floor, which was exactly as you'd expect the second floor of an apartment building to be like--a hallway with doors leading to different peoples' apartments. We were walking down the hall when we realized that the one open door was actually the Woogo lobby, within a small apartment. The staff was highly unprofessional, and I've received better service at Dunkin Donuts. Needless to say, we were worried about the quality of the room, especially given the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lobby"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that they'd setup at a kitchen table in an apartment.
We took the elevator up to our room, and instead of the high ceilings, marble floors, and new furniture that we had not only seen in the photos but had also been told over the phone were in the apartment, they were instead: - foot ceilings with paint missing in spots, wooden floors with enough scratches that they could have once been used in a roller rink, and furniture that would have been outdated in ----, and had the wear and tear to prove it. The bed looked like it had been made by an --year old trying to impress his parents, and the paper WooGo flier they left on the bed looked as if it had been crumpled in a ball by the previous guests, and then the WooGo people uncrumpled it and put it back on the bed for us. The apartment also had a pungent odor, and so we phoned their customer service and told them we would not be staying there, but the customer service could not handle any refund requests, and let us know we'd have to call back when the London office was open, between ---, London time. 
At one point during the -- minute conversation with their customer service, a bellhop (who didn't actually carry bags or give us any information, so it was unclear what his real purpose was) entered our room as my wife was on the phone, and after I explained the situation to him, we simply waited in the room and listened to the phone conversation. Once we left the room to return to the converted """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lobby,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" he left without an apology and took the elevator before us going up. While usually not anything to find any major fault with, in the context of our situation, it added to the already unpleasant experience. 
We returned to the kitchen-table-in-the-apartment lobby, where there were the same four people who don't appear to do anything all day and fail to acknowledge customers who approach the lobby for a few minutes. We explained the situation and our conversation with customer service, and they informed us that because they had no other apartments in New York for the night (a Tuesday night in September), we were out of luck. They said that they never provide alternate accomodations or compensation for clients, and thus left us, in New York city on the night of our anniversary, without any place to stay. Also, they refused to reimburse the $-- roundtrip cab fare we had to spend to travel from the upper West Side to their midtown location. We ended up spending the anniversary sleeping on the floor of our friends' apartment.
As if all this were not enough, not only is WooGo not compensating us for any of the expenses incurred due to their false advertising (not to mention ruining an anniversary), they are also attempting to keep our $--- deposit. In subsequent conversations with their London-based company, they have actually refused to let either my wife or I speak to a supervisor, and usually put us on hold for a couple minutes and then act as if we are speaking to a new representative. Also, they will not take notes on our situation, and demand that in addition to the phone conversations, we write an e-mail detailing our dilemna.
We spent a couple weeks planning out our anniversary trip, with a focus on where to stay in New York for the night of our actual anniversary, and now are spending more hours on the phone arguing to simply get a deposit back for an apartment that we never stayed in. Because of WooGo, we've lost time and money, and spent our anniversary dealing with rude customer service reps and an unprofessional staff, and were forced to sleep on the floor of a friend's apartment.
This company will be reported to the Better Business Bureau for their poor business practice, and if there is any solace I can take in my experience, it's that no one else will be subject to WooGo. Please tell your friends or anyone who may be considering using their service: do not be tempted by the pictures on the website; you will not ever see one of those rooms. I have had single bad experiences at hotels, but acknowledge that it was primarily circumstance, and can imagine that under different conditions, one may have an excellent stay at that hotel. However, this was not one instance of my bad experience; this company falsely advertises and engages in fraudulent business practices. There is no circumstance I can imagine in which someone would have a good experience with WooGo. Do not use WooGo; it's just not worth it.

The room was beautiful! A-C wasn't working properly when we first checked in but they had someone up to take a look and everything was taken care of within an hour. Concierge was great! Wonderful Location!

Stayed here for - nights in the month of april and the stay was good. Rooms were actually bigger than what we expected, and very adequate. Shower was big, nice designer toiletries and free internet was a huge plus. Location of the hotel is superb really, just next to Houston Street station on train - line. We were in room --- and were facing the main road. It is noisy, though it didnt bother us and we slept through it. For those light sleepers, pls avoid rooms ending with --,-- and -- as all of them faces the main road. If you do get those rooms that ends with the above mentioned numbers, i would suggest going for higher floors, namely - and above. The gym was good, equipment was brand new, towels and water were provided though it was a tad too cold in there! In addition, the hotel was just on the outskirts of soho, and its great to just walk around. -- mins from little italy, - mins from soho literally and nice food all around! We paid USD $--- for it and it was well worth it, knowing that its in NYC. Would definitely stay here again for sure!
Very good for tourists, in the middle of everything

We had just stayed in this hotel from the --th to the --th after being upgraded from the Royal Park Hotel unexpectedly. What a deal! Anyway, we had a roomy -th floor room with a bathroom bigger than our apartment's in Florida with a huge frosted window and more than enough room to put our toiletries in the windowsill. Our beds were a little firm but comfortable. Definitely no bed begs, that is always the first thing I check for. The AC window unit worked great, and we had a flat screen TV. The front desk was helpful and sent us up ice whenever we asked for it, which was great after a long day of walking. There are some great places for breakfast just a block or two downtown- I suggest the Metro DIner and Broadway Bagel- both excellent. Our doormen carried our luggage up and down the stairs, and were always friendly. So were the housekeepers. All in all, a great stay. I just wish we didn't have to walk up five flights of stairs, but as long as you're not morbidly obese, it's a non-issue. =)

We stayed -- nights at this hotel and loved it. Although the rooms are really small, they are clean & well presented.
The staff at the hotel were always on hand to answer any questions and very friendly. Basic breakfast included which is handy.
The location was wonderful, right in the heart of The Village.
Highly recommend and would definitely stay there again.

The location of this hotel was great - one block from Water Tower Place - decent walk to Navy Pier, etc. 
I didn't think the front desk did a very good job - we were checking in to a room that a friend had reserved with reward points...since he wasn't getting in until later, he called ahead to clear us getting there first, and FAXed all the information they requested. We still had a problem checking in, and they never bothered to look for the FAX, 
The rooms are a decent size since you have a living area and a bedroom, but the sofa bed was disgusting and broken. Unfortunately, we didn't discover this until we pulled out the bed for the night and my son sat on the corner and fell right through! There were no springs on the left side, nothing was even attached to the frame. The extra blanket in the closet was also disgusting with black oil stains all over it. 
Never received room service the second day because they showed up at - PM when we were resting from a day out.

I booked through Booking.com on this nice small hotel.
Stayed there whit my Girlfriend and mom for - nights.
The hotel is located just half block away from Broadway. 
Hotel staff is really nice. I stayed the year before on another Comfort inn a few blocks away and it maintained the same great service, but this was better located.
The room was quiet and nice, but a little small. I think triple rooms are same as double but with one more bed, this makes the small a bit tiny.
The breakfast is good, but its really difficult to find hotels in New York with this service included.
I would totally recommend this place to spend some days.
The only problem I found is that some days there was cigarette smoke smell. 
The rest GREAT A++++

I stayed at the New yorker with my mum. The hotel rooms were small but very nicely decorated and an ok size bathroom with bath and shower. There is a -- hour diner in the hotel which we went to each morning. 
The hotel is in a fantastic locaion, we could see the empire state building from our room, maddison square gardens and macys was minutes away.
The only downer we had was that we didnt sleep too well due to the room opposite sitting ouitside their room and slamming the door in early hours, but on the third night we heard a security guard tell them to keep quiet and heard nothing since!
Would go back!

A very nice place. The living room was very roomy, and the bedroom with the - double beds was a large room, although the bathroom could have been made bigger. The evening reception was a nice set-up, serving drinks and snacks, then the morning breakfast was very nice with a cooked to order breakfast offered. There isn't anything to do within walking distance of the motel, but it is an easy drive to downtown.

The staff was friendly and the breakfast above average. Some of the common areas were beginning to show wear (elevator, stairs) but overall a nice looking and comfortable hotel. Great price and good location for all we wanted to see. It was a little noisy in the halls at times, but it was spring break and there were lots of families staying in the hotel.

We arrived at the hote early coming from Vegas on an early morning flight. The hotel had no rooms available as it was early and we happily accepted this. The neighbourhood, as others have pointed out was not the nicest, even at -am we were hounded by street beggars and unsavoury characters. It's such as shame about the location as the hotel is technically on the outskirts of the tenderloin district (San franciscos Bronx) however you are only a couple of blocks from Union Square and the designer boutiques. The staff were amazing, offering to help us out with tours and arranged a private car back to the airport. They were very friendly and were always smiling. The rooms were nice, however the carpet was in need of replacing and the portable air con unit was extremely noisy. It was very warm during our stay and the ceiling fan was not enough. Overall,the service was great, the location was dodgy and I did not feel safe walking back at night. However, if you were to walk briskly and ignore the panhandlers you will be fine.

The hotel has some significant bright spots, it is a beautiful building, it has an amazing atrium, an ok pool and several young women (Erika in particular) at the front counter who are marvelous. If you aren’t staying at the hotel, they have a neat tour where you can eat a good lunch in the atrium for --.--, a neat thing to do I’m sure. 
However. The wifi costs -- dollars. The rooms are tiny, and if you don’t upgrade to a market street view, you see nothing but the walls-roofs of other buildings. The soap they offer is awful; it is drying and the quality of a motel off the highway. Brunch is -- dollars, seriously. The windows allegedly open, but they weigh an absurd amount, and if you call the front desk to help, they respond that they don’t do that. The male staff is rude. Every one of them I interacted with was condescending and pretentious.
The worst part was the way I was treated when there was a mix-up on their part. I had booked twoconsecutive reservations, because my employer was a paying for a few days and I chose to extend my stay as a mini vacation. When they combined the reservations they asked for a card for the final two days. I obliged. They placed a hold on the card (it was a debit, not credit card) for the two nights stay, reducing my available balance. On the second afternoon, we returned to the hotel after dinner. Our keys would not work. We went to the front counter, where they told me they would have to run my card to guarantee the room, I obliged. They gave us keys. They called shortly after and asked for me to return to the front desk. They stated that my card had been declined. I called my bank; it showed three holds on my account from them, for a total of - nights. I explained this to them. They asked me to get a verbal authorization from the bank. I belong to a small community bank with no weekend hours, and I informed them that could be arranged on Monday (it was Saturday evening; I was to check out Monday morning). They said that was impossible, they had to guarantee payment. I explained to them that there was no more cash available in my account- because they had issued so many holds on it. I work for a federal government agency, and stated that I represented that agency in my travels, and obviously would do nothing to sully the name of that agency. The desk clerk stated, “you don’t look like you will pay the bill, I’m sorry”, and told me to go across the street to the ATM and get cash. I then suggested that he could simply put it on the account of my employer, and that I would straighten it out on Monday. He said this was fine. 
When I got to the room, someone else’s luggage was being brought in (my things were all still in the room). In addition, a gift basket had been left with a card on it for that person on our desk. The soap had not been refreshed, and the window I struggled so desperately to open had been closed. I returned the gift to the front desk, and was so stressed and frustrated that I decided to spend the evening in the room with my partner.
When we awoke, there was a note under the door stating that we needed to report immediately to the front desk to make payment. I went downstairs, and was greeted by another, but just as rude male desk clerk. He informed me that I would have to make payment immediately or leave the hotel. I gave him a different credit card, because he had maxed out my other one with all of the holds, I was stuck in San Francisco on vacation, with no available cash because the hotel has a total of - nights held on my cards, for a - night stay. They were not apologetic, they did not offer an upgrade or a free meal for my trouble, they were nothing but rude. 
The moral, visit this place to see the history, but don’t stay here, it isn’t worth the headache.

We flew into the city at the approach of Labor Day weekend. We love the US Open and were ready to indulge in the bounty of Manhattan as well. The hotel is well situated, within a stones throw of Central Park, Nobu --, and of course the famed shopping down Fifth Ave. However, this hotel is simply fair. The rooms are fine - kind of felt like a larger dormitory room, with furnishings much in keeping with college living. The bathroom is small. The shower head is powerful, but the water seeps out readily. I would not recommend this highly, nor do I plan on staying here again. I did not dine at the restaurant - but I do wonder, what happened to Chef Zakarian's """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Town"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Restaurant, which I had read about as being within the Chambers, and yet proved not to be...
Oh, if you love the Westin Heavenly Beds - this is not the place for fantastic mattress and sleep experience.

The Beacon is in a great location, close to everything and the rooms are large and clean.
My problem was with the hotel staff. We discovered a theft from our room and reported it to the front desk. They could not have cared less. They were loathe to take down details and it was only when we asked for the police to attend that they pulled their collective fingers out. They asked that they conduct an 'in house' investigation rather than get the rozzers in. We agreed but when we asked the next morning as to the progress of the investigation the front desk staff looked at us blankly and we discovered the details of the theft had not been passed on and zero investigation had been carried out. I have since contacted the manager and he promised me faithfully he would come back with an answer for me by guess what? Nothing.
If you are thinking of going to NY then by all means go, its great town but avoid the Beacon.

I stayed at the Bradford Homesuites for two nights on a business trip. I had a huge suite with two comfortable double beds, a full bath, an additional sink-vanity, a living room, a kitchen, and a desk. It was clean and quiet. They left complimentary snacks each day (microwave popcorn and breakfast bars).
Complimentary continental breakfast was good (muffins, toast, juice, coffee, fruit, several hot items). There is a small business center in the lobby with two computers, including free internet access and free use of the printer. There is also a free shuttle to downtown, a couple minutes away, although you need to reserve in advance. The hotel is walking distance to the arena, if you want to see a basketball game. Otherwise, there is nothing much in walking distance.
The hotel is very reasonably priced. I paid $---night.

I recently stayed at the Triton to attend a business seminar. The location was excellent two blocks from my class, across the street from China Town, a few blocks from Union Square, one block fromt the trolley line to Fisherman's Wharf, and a few blocks from Market Street. The room was small but I believe that was due to age of the hotel. The wine hour at -pm was great. I utilized the fitness room, well appointed. This is my first stay at a Kimpton property and it has generated an interest to continue to use this chain during my travels. The staff was very helpful with directions and very friendly. For a trip to a funky hotel with great service, I would recommend the Triton.

This hotel was built in ----, keep that in mind. If you need everything to be new and shiny, not the place for you. But if you like the charm of an old hotel, this place is in a great location. We walked to Wrigley to catch the RedSox vs the Cubs. Also walking distance (one mile) to Lincoln Park Zoo, Conservatory and Lake Michigan Beach Trail. The bed was comfy and the shower was fine. Our room was very small. There is a breakfast that is included but we did not participate. If you get a good price, give it a try.

Myself and - friends stayed at the Cosmopolitan Hotel from August -- - --. I had read all the reviews on Tripadvisor, and was only mildly concerned that our room would smell of cigarette smoke. However, when we checked in the woman at the reception desk asked if we wanted smoking or none, so obviously we took non. I didn't smell a hint of smoke the entire time we were there. We got the room with two queen beds and a pullout couch and it was HUGE! We had a full bathroom plus another countertop, mirror and sink outside so that - people could get ready at once. The television was huge, and we got lots of stations. There wasn't a fridge but we didn't need one. Ice was available upon request. We were on the inner courtyard so the view wasn't great but it was quiet at night. We didn't hear a thing from other guests. You could tell that it was newly renovated, but they kept the old feel with actual keys for the rooms instead of magnetic cards. We didn't fly out until -pm on the --th, so they stored our luggage for us at no extra cost, and called a car to take us to the airport. Slightly more than a cab, but it was much less of a hassle. (Too bad the flight was cancelled but that's no their fault :) ). The hitch was that when we got back to the room at --:-- one night, there were posters in the elevator saying that by order of the New York public works the water was shut off until -am. I think it was the whole block, so not the hotel's fault, but it was still an inconvenience. As far as location, we walked to Battery Park, South Street Seaport, and Ground Zero. The Subway to Times Square is literally right outside the front door, so that's easy. The Metrocard is $-- and good for a week. All in all, I would definitely recommend this hotel to my friends, and if I return I'll be staying here as well.

Pros: 
* Location, location, location. A couple of blocks away from Pike Market
* Beautiful historic building
* Lobby is inviting with comfortable leather couches and tastefully decorated
* Rooms are clean and spacious enough (considering the age of the hotel and downtown location)
* Bed and pillows were comfortable
* Parking is only $-- per night
* Tasteful decor in hallway on -th Floor
* My room had a claw-foot bathtub, which was unique! (some people may not like this--note, some rooms have a conventional shower)
* Price of hotel is reasonable considering location
Cons:
* Street noise given the downtown location (i.e., best to keep your windows closed)
* No A-C
* TV, altough perfectly functional, is an old tube-style so could be upgraded
* When you are told a - pm check-in, count on it! I went by the front desk three times until my room was ready right around - pm
* Only one service elevator so this can be awkward when checking in and out with luggage
* Parking is in parkade across the street. Not horrible but also not the most convenient.
Final Verdict: Considering the cost, location, and comfort of the room, I will be staying again. If you are a budget conscious traveller looking for a clean and comfortable room in a great location within a late Victorian building, then you won't o any better in downtown Seattle.
Found a great deal in the hotel's website for thanksgiving. Rooms were spacious, good amenities, great location! Would recommend and definetly go back.

The location of the hotel is about the only thing it has going for it. Valet parking at $-- per day is not worth it. One day we had to wait nearly -- minutes for them to get our vehicle because the valet never heard them call for him to get it. You would think for the inconvenience they would have offered us free parking or something for that day but they did nothing. Alex was probably the best person working there. I also had to make multiple trips to the front desk to get room keys that would work. No pool, and there were ants and other bugs in our room. Only reason we stayed there is because we did the name your own price on priceline and we were stuck with it.

I stayed at this hotel for one night with my husband and my -- month old son. The hotel is in a great location, easy walk to many destinations. Nightly parking was $--, a little pricey. The hotel is very trendy, rooms are super clean, bed was very comfortable.
The negative was that we were given a room off of the atrium where the music-nightclub started at - pm and went until -:--am. It was very loud...I couldn't get my son to sleep with the noise. I called the front desk and they said they were sold out and could not move us. Also, the room we were given had a see thru bathroom. the wall to the bathroom was glass, so when either of us went to the bathroom or shower...it was seen by the other. My son is young so he didn't get it...but toddler or older kids...I wouldnt have been happy about it.
If you are single and want to party this is the place for you, but for a family..I'd say check out other hotels.

This hotel is excellent for exploring all Boston has to offer. It is attached to a shopping center and has easy access to everything. The rooms are very modern and the staff were exceptional. I would not stay anywhere else.
Beautiful setting, spacious rooms, elegant restaurants with great food and, perhaps best of all, amazing pools. Even though I was there on business, I felt really relaxed after my stay here.

First of all, there is some confusion here. There is allegedly a Fairfield downtown near Market Square. No such place on Marriott's website, though Mapquest seems to know it. And if you click on Tripadvisor's title, it takes you to the one at the Airport.
Anyway, here's the thing. This place (near the airport) was built in ----. Pretty recent by most standards but ancient in hotel terms. So much has changed! When this place was built, hotels were just beginning to offer free breakfasts, didn't have guest laundry and there was no such thing as a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""business center"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". So all these features had to be retrofitted into older places like this.
The guest laundry is a washer and dryer in what was probably once a closet. Not even a place to sit down. The business center is a computer and printer in the lobby. And the breakfast area was probably once a meeting room.
The worst problem is the elevator. Just one to service - floors, including use by the cleaning and maintenance staff! This has become worse because of free breakfast: at one time, people would get dressed and leave and pick up breakfast somewhere. Now, they go down, get fed, return to the room and leave a little later - the load has been tripled! But what's made it even worse is that, even after a half century or so of self-serve elevators, people still haven't figured out how to use them. Almost every time we entered on the top floor there were morons who had pushed both buttons and ridden up. Then on the way down we'd stop on their floor for no reason.
Back to breakfast. It was the holidays and also the Alamo Bowl and the place was packed, including lots of kids. The breakfast area was a zoo. The manager stepped in and made waffles and marvelously kept his cool trying to get everyone fed. We also found the front desk staff very friendly and helpful in fulfilling some requests.
Overall, the staff is doing its best (cleaners were still working at - pm) but the building is not designed for hotel requirements of today. If you're thinking of staying here, avoid busy periods and get a room on a low floor so you can use the stairs.

My girlfriend and I stayed here back in Feb ----. The hotel has a food court which has a very good selections of different eats. I checked out the pool although I didn't swim since it was still winter. It's an outside pool and it looked real nice.

Where do I start ?
