We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Doubletree Chelsea! Staff was incredibly personable and accommodating. Our room was quite small, but that is to be expected in the heart of Manhattan. It was very clean and well designed, so we moved about effortlessly. Penn Station is a mere five minute walk away, making getting around the city much easier. Union Square was a fifteen minute walk away. Our only complaint was the A-C which would not consistently hold the temperature. We adjusted several times throughout the night, just to sleep comfortably.

I even tipped the front desk $--. For that, I guess I was lucky to have the west side, away from the interstate. The room furnishings were VERY tired: all marred, even with its cheap plastic veneer. It's been a long time since I had an old analog TV, no flat-screen. The heating-cooling unit was falling off the wall and was too loud to sleep with. The toilet would not flush: you had to hold the handle (gimme a break! This is -.- stars??) Structurally, the hotel is solid and capable of quiet isolation. Parking is very convenient. But the room I had was no less than a disaster. I ended up checking out a day early, losing the cost because I was there on Priceline.

My girlfriend and I stayed at Club Quarters WTC for a few nights at the end of April, at the start of a holiday in the US. It's in a prime location right over the site of the planned Freedom Tower - ---- memorial in Downtown Manhattan. 
We booked a studio suite through Hotelclub, but when we checked in the first room we were given was a standard room, so they moved us to a studio room. To be honest, there was very little difference between the two room types, and if anything their website is a bit misleading when it infers the studios are much bigger rooms - have a look at my photos to see what I mean. 
Despite the above our room was fine, definitely spacious enough for two people, and in addition to the Queen bed there was a separate desk, microwave, fridge, flatscreen TV etc. The bathroom was a decent size, though the toilet-roll holder fell off the wall on the first day! Decor, furnishings etc were very clean and modern. 
As others have mentioned the hotel is still under construction, though really you're only aware of this if you -) see the signs about this in the lobby or -) meet the workmen in the hallways. We bumped into some one morning and it turned out the room next to us was being """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""installed - built"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", but we really weren't disturbed at all by the work. The construction work means there's no hotel restaurant, so the hotel provides a free buffet breakfast in one of their meeting rooms - very good selection of muffins, cereal, fruit juice, coffee etc, and the inclusion of breakfast was what made this a super good deal in New York. They didn't do room service, but instead offered a delivery service from local takeaways to your room. 
The club """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""living room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" area of the hotel is very well appointed, and is a significant positive for this hotel. There are computers with colour printing, and a dedicated """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""boarding pass"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" computer-printer every morning to get your lastminute documents before heading for the airport. 
In terms of hotel location it's right in the heart of downtown, only a couple of minutes walk from Battery Park (and ferry to Statue of Liberty), not too far from the Subway, and being next to the WTC site makes it a good landmark for taxis, airport buses etc to aim at. 
I'd go back to this hotel, though next time I'd probably just book a standard room.

I went with my mom over the summer for just a girls night getaway and I swear I don't think I've ever experienced anything so amazing. The staff was incredible, only caring what I needed. The room was just pure luxury (and I definitely had the best sleep in the fluffy bed!). For breakfast we went down to the restaurant at the hotel and it was just more of a relaxation. Everything tasted amazing and the service was quick. Later, we got -- minute facials (which I highly recommend) but it felt like I spent a week in some warm exotic place it was just so relaxing. I was certainly relieved of any stress and had the best time ever. I just can't imagine staying anywhere else in Boston!

Super location - near the wharf and pier -- and also close to catch the tram car to the city centre - a real fun ride, a must do while you visit. Although the hotel is pricey it is worth a stay for a few nights. Modern and Clean. Staff were suitably friendly.
Staying right at the airport takes away all the pre trip anxiety. Even going through security is a more pleasant experience.

I loved the firendly and efficient service of the front of house staff. I felt very at welcome. The restaurant attached to the hotel had great food and service. The bedding was very comfortable..I trruly was like sleeping on a cloud after a busy day of work and sightseeing. The shower was strong and pleantly of heat The room was always cleaned to highest standard and the housemaid staff were also very friendly and efficient. The location is fantastic close to everything you need to enjoy a busienss and pleasure trip to New York.

I simply couldn't find fault with this Hotel. Just came back from a - night business trip to New York and took a chance with The Chatwal, which I had never actually heard of before. Now, I travel a lot particularly in the States and have stayed at some fabulous hotels but there is always something which tends to let you down. No so at The Chatwal - from my first greeting from the Doorman upon arrival to the farewell from the Desk upon departure, everything was absolutely perfect. The location was great, close enough to Times Square to be on top of everything, yet far enough to be quiet and discreet. The decor was beautiful, the service was impeccable, the staff (from cleaner to Manager) was faultless and the room, well, it was simply stunning. The 'Asprey's of London' toiletries symbolized the class of this place and the free wi-fi throughout the Hotel was a bonus - I wouldn't even have minded paying for it! I am desperate to think of some criticism, if only to prove that this review hasn't been placed by the managing director of Starwood, but I can't! When I return to New York later in the year, I will not even consider staying anywhere else!

COTTAGE B ..that's where we just left.This place has been on my """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""bucket list"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" it's all I thought it would be!the - end studios a and b ,I think are the nicest.they are studios that are pretty large.Bed was king size and comfortable.TV ,fridge,microwave etc.I would bring your own bar of soap..they are skimpy....the place is old...but clean There are binoculars in the room...the beach town itself is pretty DIRTY and if it was not for this place...there is NO WAY we would go.The surrounding restaurants are lousy and the streets are supper grimy...We thought we were in Venice Beach....BUT THE CRYTAL PIER ROCKS!!!!

We stayed here for a business trip. As of February --, ---- the hotel was in the middle of construction to renovate it. The work is being done in a way that will not interfere with your stay. I would suggest calling the hotel directly to ask if the construction is finished.
We stayed in one of the newly renovated rooms. Everything was quite comfortable. 
You can hear conversations in the next rooms but the noise level is not so bad. 
On one night there was a very loud party across the street (not at the hotel) that went until the early morning. The hotel of course is not responsible for that, and it seemed to be an exception (it only happened on one of the four nights we were there).
Breakfast buffet is great. Staff is great. I couldn't make the wine and cheese from --- pm but I imagine it is also quite nice.
Good location for a hotel. We had a GPS in our car, which made it quite easy to explore San Francisco.

We stayed here as a family of four on our first visit to New York and it was a perfect base from which to explore. OK it's not super luxurious, but all we wanted was a clean comfy base to return to at the end of a long day exploring!! That is exactly what we got...the room itself, well it was a bit rough around the edges in places, but the housekeeping staff did a great job, even changing the towels daily which a lot of hotels don't do any more. The beds were really comfortable and the shower was powerful and always hot...what more do you need??? OK there is just one thing that would be appreciated...tea and coffee making facilities!! 
Location was brilliant..a few minutes walk from the vast array of restaurants that Hell's Kitchen has to offer and only a -- minute walk to Time Square and the subway. Over the road was the Skyline Deli where there was always service with a smile and their European Flatbreads were gorgeous!!
All in all, no complaints..we just had a standard room and I could see no reason not to return and hopefully one day we will.

Stayed here last month. It was a Hotwire win. Room was large, high ceilings, very clean. Staff was very helpful. Probably the best La Quinta that we have ever stayed at and definately on of the best in it's class that we have ever stayed at. You cannot go wrong with this one.

I have never felt the need to write a reveiw about a hotel-motel before, but after our stay at this one, I feel that people should know what to expect when going there. We stayed at this motel a week ago. 
Upon arrival, we noticed: 
-The neighborhood was run down
-There was supposed to be free parking, but the lot was always full and we couldn’t park near the hotel.
-When we checked in they told us that they were “booked full, not to bother coming back to the front desk to complain and request a different room after we see our room as there is nothing they can do about it”. So we didn’t know what to expect. 
Going into our room:
First impression: """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""What a dump but surprisingly close to Golden Gate Bridge, never realized how close it was on maps""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""
-The only good thing I can say about the room is.. it was clean, no bed bugs.. thats it 
-It had a very stale, unpleasant odor 
-The room was so tiny we could barely fit both our suitcases and ourselves in it.
-The Bathroom had a shower, toilet, sink and that was it. There was no room for any kind of moving around. You couldn’t shower with the door closed and expect to be able to get dressed in the bathroom.
-The T.V. didnt work at all (even after fooling around with it for ten minutes, we were unsuccessful to get any type of a picture) 
-The toliet would not flush toliet paper, and by the end of our - night stay, it wouldnt flush at all. We had to use the public bathrooms when we went sightseeing around San Francisco, because we couldn’t use the one in our room.
-Our heater had no knob on it to adjust the temperature 
-Our walls were paper thin and our room looked onto Lombard Street so the entire night we were awakened by either people yelling on the street or traffic. 
-We were very digusted with this, and were very shocked because the pictures that were online were very deceiving, NOTHING what we paid for
-Upon check out we listed the above problems to the lady at the front desk and she showed zero concern at all, saying that is what we paid for
To sum it up: we would never stay here again.

We visited BW Blue Sea Lodge from a Tuesday-Saturday Morning and could not have been more pleased. 
 When we initially arrived we had booked just a standard room, which we had a partial view of the ocean and we were happy with it. One Queen bed, little kitchenette, and great bathroom. However our tv was broken. It was less than - minutes after i called the front desk until a maintence man arrived. After trying twice to fix it they ended up just moving us to a different room, which turned out to be a beach front view w- a flatscreen TV! If you have a little extra to spend I would definately suggest doing the upgrade to the ocean view...it was absolutely perfect! and next time i stay here I will absolutely get the ocean front. we fell asleep to the sound of the ocean and there was great people watching from our balcony.
 The pool & jacuzzi area were clean and well kept. there were a lot of kids there during the day, but at night my boyfriend & i were able to get in some pool time which was just fine for us since we were either at the beach or exploring SD during the day. 
 Some of the reviews mentioned that the walls were thin which i didnt notice, but we stayed mid-week for the most part so it wasnt too busy at the hotel. 
Another Plus was free internet in lobby where we were able to print out our boarding passes. Also, the lobby had a suprisingly good coffee shop w- tasty pastries.
Location is everything and all of the area attractions were about a -- min drive away. We had rented a car for the days we were there and a car is def a must have when visiting SD. Plus Pacific Beach is great in general w- plenty of bars, restaurants, and of course the board walk & ocean within walking distance of the hotel.
We loved the hotel and the accomadating staff and were sad to leave.
As long as you arent anticipating the Ritz when booking Blue Sea Lodge then you should be pleased. It was clean and comfortable and for the traveling family, friends, or couple who wants a great casual atmosphere with plenty to do nearby, then I would highly recommend.

On the surface, the hotel is very beautiful. It is in a great location and has nice amenities such as the spa and fitness center and a great pool. The restaurant (Robert's) has wonderful food and there are nice gift shops. However, my experience was not so pleasant as there was a rodent infestation at the time I was there in late summer. There was a mouse in my sleeping room, that fortunately was not discovered until the morning I was checking out. Otherwise, I would have not have been able to stay in that hotel another night. There was also a mouse in the main Regency ballroom. It was a tramatizing experience as I have never had a rodent or insect problem at ANY hotel I've stayed. The hotel staff was quite apologetic, but it was apparently a big problem. I will not stay there again and even if there were no rodents, I would not have recommended it.

Our stay here was over four nights at an average rate of $----night, including tax (booked direct on the Hotel's website). This was our --th hotel stay in around -- weeks of travel across North America.
Overall: A comfortable, modern room, close to Seattle restaurants in Belltown, with a little noise. Probably best for those wanting just a few nights in a good location from Sundays through Wednesdays.
What's good: Our room was brightly painted with new, modern decor including a leather foot stool, soft timber flooring, a renovated bathroom with a modern, large showerhead, and a keurig (coffee) machine with a selection of assorted coffees and tea. Towels were the fluffiest we’ve had at any hotel. An in-room safe was available.
Our king-size bed was really comfortable. Pillow comfort is quite personal though we didn’t really like ours – a heavy style that compress into a hard slope. Heating was good and quiet. 
Breakfast was not included in our rate and there’s no refrigerator or microwave in the room. A restaurant on the ground floor provides breakfast and lunch until -:--pm. We ate breakfast there one morning – tea-toast-juice ($-), and oatmeal ($-). Breakfast prices were reasonable, and service good. Free coffee and mini cupcakes were available in the hotel foyer after the restaurant closes each day (after -pm), and a free local newspaper was available at reception. If you don’t like packet creamer in your coffee, pick a few small tubs of liquid creamer from the coffee stand in reception for use with the machine in your room.
Minor annoyances: Some noise from what we assumed were hotel renovations in progress (black construction plastic on a few windows on the second floor and we were woken before -am on Saturday morning by intermittent hammering in the building for several hours), major building construction diagonally across Blanchard St (likely for at least the next - months), and hotel hallways. The hotel has a policy of putting a ‘hold’ of $---day on your credit card to allow for ‘contingencies’. We had no problem with the money being released against our debit card, but be aware of the practice.
Our room (#---) was on the fifth (and top) floor facing Blanchard Street, more towards the end of the corridor (third last room), away from lifts and a drink-snack machine. The timber floors reflect most hallway conversations, footsteps and slamming doors, and I’d recommend an ipod or earplugs if you want a peaceful night’s sleep. The weekend nights seemed noisier and busier, with party goers returning early in the morning, and a local football game and bus load of fans as hotel guests also made for a noisy Friday night stay. 
The building has two lifts which worked quickly, and drink-snack-ice machines are available. 
Nearby: Top Pot Doughnuts across the road on -th are a must. Ralph’s Grocery & Deli is a few blocks away for cheap and wholesome soups and sandwhiches. You’ll find plenty of restaurants within a few blocks of the hotel, in the Belltown area. Try Mama’s Mexican for grungy ambience, and good value large-sized mexican meals. Pike Place Market is a great walk of around - blocks (try the Russian Bakery and check out Starbuck’s first ever store), and city stores are a similar distance. The Space Needle is an easy, half mile walk. 
For something unusual-different: Wexley School for Girls is an advertising agency along -th – look through their windows; There’s colourful knitting around the trees in the park on -rd Avenue & Yesler Way-Jefferson St.
Transport: Seattle has free buses in the downtown area!

My husband and I recently stayed at this hotel and it was beautiful! The rooms were big and very modern. The bathroom was gorgeous! Our only complaint was that the A-C didn't work very well and it was stuffy. Otherwise, a great place.

I have been spoiled by staying at the - Seasons and The Plaza, so with the rate I received, I wasn't expecting much. Boy, was I wrong! First Class all the way around. My best friend and I stayed at the W City Center for a girls weekend get away. The location was fabulous! Within walking distance from the train station as well as some of the best shopping in the US. Our favorite part of our weekend trip was complimentary tickets to Kristin Chenoweth at the Cadillac Palace - (thanks to the Concierge Eden - she is the best!!). If it were not for these two small complaints I would have given the W City Center an Excellent versus a Very Good rating.
I got what i needed almost before i hung up the phone. Thanks for following up to make sure i was taken care of. You made my stay more enjoyable.

Old Hollywood, right there on Hollywood Blvd. My room was small and had a crappy view. But it was clean, decorated in a minimalist style with interesting B&W photography and had a lovely bathroom with lots of shelf space. The staff was great. My first room didn't have AC and they moved me almost immediately so I could still make the Dodger game at -:--. The concierge was very helpful with tours, dinner reservations, setting up my pedicure. My experience in the spa was great, too. Yes, there was a premiere party when I was there and it made access to the hotel difficult. But LA isn't the easiest city to get around anyway. If I'm in LA again, I'll try to get into this hotel again, too.

I booked my trip through Priceline and at first i was a bit apprehensive because the parking was so horribly expensive. I went for a weekend and thought from the other reviews that the area was abandoned at night. It was not. Parking is ample at night but you must pay the meters $-.-- per hour at -am, Although I like sleeping in, I got up and moved the car over - blocks to ample parking lots for $-.-- per day weekend if no events are going on. It was $-.-- although u must pay by credit card. It was great. The old town trolley stops near Anthony's pier which was easy walking distance to do the trolley ride. The Hotel is brand new and amazing. Very clean, nice tv's, excellent bar and restaurant and great staff. The trolley driver dropped us off in front of the hotel because Tropical Storm Hanna decided to pour down on us so for our benefit and some of the older passengers he made a special stop and avoided our need to walk - blks in the torrential rain. 
Hotel is near the waterfront, near the convention center and near the Fannueil Hall, (about a -- min walk) You can easily take the silver line from the Airport to the Hotel and it is on the next block that the train is there. I would have preferred not to have a vehicle because parking where all the clubs and bars are is awful and hard to find. I think you can take the silver line to South Station and transfer to the rest of the T, which I would definitely do next time. Airport by car is on the other side of the New Tunnel and it is a -- min drive. Very nice, quiet area. Starbucks is in the lobby for a morning coffee and danish. I would definitely recommend this hotel and stay again, so close to everything.

Like many people traveling through ORD in the wintertime, I missed a connection and ended up staying overnight in Chicago. I booked one of the Hilton's """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""allergy free"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" rooms and was overall happy with my stay. 
room: the room was quite impressive, for the allergic traveler. It had hardwood floors and no drapes. Instead of drapes it had sliding wood doors - two with opaque translucent panels to let in light and a second pair that were solid wood. These provided some sound protection in addition to privacy and blocking the light. My room overlooked the L and the U S Airways terminal. It was mostly quiet - with the exception of sirens that could be heard around -am and some alarm type sound shortly before that. The bed was made up with allergy free blankets and no feathers. My only complaint is that in the winter they really need more on the bed than one blanket. I suggest the hotel to add some allergy-free bedspreads or comforters to the room. I found a second blanket in the closet. Unfortunately it had a noticeable perfume smell - like air freshener. I happen to be allergic to that stuff so I could not make full use of the second blanket. However my room was not that cold and it has a thermostat. The room came with a large flat panel TV and also some kind of air purifier up on the wall. The last item was a bit overkill IMO but the other allergy-free things like the hardwood floors and no feathers were very welcome. Even the usual chair was upholstered in leather instead of fabric. The bathroom products were the same standard fare that Hilton uses. Nothing different there.
service: the staff were very helpful and prompt at responding. 
gym: the hotel has a full fitness center including pool. I spent about -- minutes in the gym and it was quite welcome after a long flight from the west coast, and dealing with a missed flight.
restaurant: the hotel restaurant is italian. Service is pretty good, the food was nice. Only drawback is that they do not get wifi in the restaurant - so as a solo traveler I often bring my laptop and could not really use it, although I did get a cell connection in the restaurant.
location: the hotel is right on the ORD property. You can get to it without going outside - nice in the winter. Although it is a fairly long walk from some of the terminals - including United T- where I flew into. The moving walk way, elevators, and escalators were not working on the underground connector from T- to the Hilton so I had to schlep my bag the whole way including carrying it up the broken escalator. I don't think this is the Hilton's fault however. 
price: I paid on the order of $--- - considerably more than non-airport properties that I pulled up on the web. But the convenience of staying right at the airport due to an unexpected overnight - and early morning flight - kept me there rather than trying to find another hotel that was cheaper. 
Overall it was a very good airport hotel and I plan to stay there again in a few months during a planned overnight stay in Chicago.

We booked this, considering it the best hotel in New York. Our doubts started increasing when we saw the lobby, which was quite pooorly restorated, if it was. 
Our rooms were very average. The fruits Compositions in the rooms were unacceptable for a luxury hotel. 
When we were shown to our rooms, the receptionist showed us only the double, saying that we will find the suite ourselves, because it's right behind this door. (We booked a double for iur dwith a connecting suite). 
So, when we, incredibly tired after the transatlantic flight, got to the suite, we were terrified by the noise coming in the room. It was impossible to speak there, without yelling. To sum up, I don't recommend this hotel to anyone. You will receive terrible service and terrible rooms.

We love the sheraton and return there whenever given the opportunity. It always exceeds our expectations from luxury and ammenaties, to service that goes beyond. This trip was no different. We were celebrating our --th anniversary and the staff (Mark H) found out the reason for our stay at the time we checked in. Later that night, after returning from an evening out, we were surprised by a beautiful, and delicious, anniversary cake in our room! What a treat and a wonderful surprise. Although my husband tried to take credit (haha), we knew it was Mark's kind efforts that made our evening even more special. We'll be back for sure!

I travel a lot-- all over the U.S. and worldwide. I've stayed in jungles and deserts, in dumps and palaces, in extreme luxury and in places that make Gilligan's Island look like the Ritz-Carlton... so I bring a little perspective here.
I've generally found Holiday Inn Express to be decent and clean, but this one in Chandler (a suburb of Phoenix, -- minutes from Sky Harbor Airport) was above and beyond in every respect. 
Earlier reviews (---- and prior) indicate it was in need of a remodel. Well it got one and it is fantastic. My king room was huge, high ceilings, beautiful furnishings including a great desk, nice sofa and chairs, refrigerator, and very nice bath with large tub-shower and great towels. The bed was extremely comfortable (wish mine was so nice), and the decor was very tasteful. Very clean too.
The lobby was also tastefully decorated and the complimentary breakfast was quite good and filling. Lots of choices: fresh scrambled eggs, bacon, biscuits and gravy, oatmeal, several cereals, many types of muffins and baked breads, several yogurts, milk, juices, coffee, tea, etc. And did I mention it was complimentary?
As if this isn't enough, there's a Cracker Barrel (my favorite) within walking distance.
The hotel was also quiet. My room faced the busy freeway but the windows were very well-insulated and I didn't hear a thing.
Free high-speed wireless internet was a very nice plus. Also USA Today every morning. Also free.
Staff was very friendly-- always said hello, good morning or evening as I walked through the lobby to my room.
I'd stay there again in a second (and will be back in the area soon-- looking forward to it.) What's not to like?
All that for only $----night.
A GREAT deal! Loved it.

The day we checked in to the hotel we waited in line and then walked up to the counter and stood there while the check in attendant was doing something with his computer. Then without looking up he grabs my credit card and types in my name into the computer. He hands me my room key and that was that. He never acknowledged us!
When we walked in to our room we got situated and unpacked our suitcases and got a chance to relax.
We rang down to housekeeping for additional towels and robes. The robes came with out any belts.
There was no light bulb in the desk lamp.
One of the bedside lamps was unplugged and we had to try to move the bed to get it plugged in.

We spoke to the bell desk about the shuttle to the airport and we were told that the shuttle ran every ½ hour and was free. He specifically stated that we didn’t need a reservation. When we got down to the lobby to check out and jump on the shuttle there was major confusion.

Our stay at the McCormick Place was a disappointment! We spoke to others on the shuttle bus drive to the airport and they had a terrible experience as well. I would not recommend this Hotel for any of our corporate meetings. The service was terrible! 
Outside of physically connected to the growing convention center the facility has nothing to offer. Access to any of the areas' attractions is cumbersome at best and could be dangerous for those that did not know the area at all.

We stayed at the Residence Inn last summer with plans for visiting Coors Field for three games. the rooms have far too many categories so unless you are a frequent traveller you won't really know what is a good room but I am sure there must be some. The hotel was put together very well. Everything was done very causual without being """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""to much."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Very welcoming, including the staff!
The roof top is what makes the hotel, it is a full rooftop with --- views. The ooms were spacious compared to some NYC hotels. The only complaint I have about the hotel is the doorman to the roof top. From my understanding he is not a part of the Kimpton staff, but that must change. He was very rude to my guest and myself. I would like to give thanks to - very special employees. They went out of their ways to make my stay as enjoyable as possible. Two of the front desk employees Ms. Naadei and Mrs. Ralhan (Jake). Stayed one night on a united airlines bump. Didn't pay for the room so I'm not sure what the cost was. Rooms were clean and comfortable. No complaints. Walking distance to walmart for beer and other supplies :-) . The restaurant was decent and i love any lounge that has colors banquet on tap. No hesitation recommending this hotel.

I stayed at the Metropolis Hotel April --th ---th, and everything was
perfect and your staff was really polite and professional at all times. I

I stayed at this classic hotel located in a very upscale, walkable neighborhood for a business seminar that was held across the street at the Hilton. Many of my colleagues stayed at the run-of-the-mill, --s-styled Hilton and each morning I smugly walked across the street to our meetings feeling superior and smart, especially since I paid the same price as they did ($---!) via Expedia. SPG.com didn't show any availability and the rate was $--- more. As an SPG platinum member, this is annoying.
The Fairfax is one of SPG's Luxury Collection and has a definite private club, non-chain feel. It sits on a corner surrounded by embassies and large homes complete with wrought iron fences and gates. One block away there were nice restaurants and bars and I especially recommend La Tiramisu. I didn't take the metro on this trip but the nearby station doesn't look too far away on a map.
The lobby, restaurant and bar are wood-paneled and look like an old-boy's social club. Even the name of the restaurant, The Jockey Club, smack of Ivy League ambiance and privilege. The halls feature chandeliers, brass and other old-school touches.
My room was a standard room (no upgrades available- a constant theme at many SPG locations. Who are they saving them for??) and it was very nice. The bed frame and furniture were solid wood, the bedspread and curtains were thick and the bathroom had antique-styled, but modern fixtures. Wallpaper and nice framed prints completed the mansion guest room look.
I didn't have interaction with the front desk, so I can't speak to the service there. The lounge has no vibe whatsoever but it is comfortable with upholstered furniture and a fire burning.
I plan to return to this hotel next month with my wife for tourist stay and I look forward it.

I recently stayed for the first time at the Hampton Inn New York City Empire State Building. The hotel is located right off --th St. in between -th and -th ave. The hotel is in a great location right near the Empire State Bldg, Macy's, Herald Square, and the New York City Library. It is right next door to the Hilton Garden Inn, and there are some good restaurants and plenty of parking lots near by. Keep in mind though that parking is between $-- and $-- a night. 
The hotel is fairly new and super clean. The rooms are sort of typical Hampton Inn with comfortable beds, nice bathrooms, and free wireless internet, which is a bonus in NYC. The big catch is the room size. The rooms are TINY, even by NYC standards. With a king size bed, dresser and desk, there was hardly any room to walk around. Since I was alone for one night, it was fine, but multiple nights or multiple people and I would go insane!
One other slightly annoying thing was that the front desk staff really wasn't able to help with food recommendations. First I asked about the - Korean restaurants next door, and they couldn't tell me anything about them, nor could they recommend a place to get bagels within walking distance of the hotel. Kinda odd??
For under $--- a night, if you must get your Hilton HHonors points, this is a decent choice for Midtown-East, but if you could care less about that stuff, stay somewhere else.

This hotel was lovely. The staff was all VERY approachable, helpful, & went out of their way to assist me on a number of occasions during my brief stay. I had several packages delivered to the hotel, I asked to ensure my room was bedbug free, & I asked for directions and dinner recommendations. They responded to each of my requests with a smile and were amazingly helpful. Amy & Ryan at the front desk obviously take a great deal of pride in their work. I would stay at Hotel Monaco in Chicago again in an instant.

This hotel is wonderful. I extended a business stay for - nights in downtown San Francisco and loved the Palomar. Whilst it's bang smack in the middle of the shopping precinct above the Old Navy store, on a very busy corner, the noise from the street was almost non existent. I was in room --- which was quite near the bar and restaurant but again, noise levels were fine, particularly as those services were not open late. The room had - double beds and was very spacious with - huge windows overlooking -th street with plenty of light. Beds were extremely comfy and the temp in the room was just right. I joined Kimpton and had free internet and a $-- mini bar voucher. Little touches make the place perfect including the wine hour and coffee and tea in the morning, and the decor which is very stylish. Sadly i didn't meet Maverick the doggie as he had been naughty. The staff were excellent. I come to SF quite often and would love to stay in the Palomar again.

Stayed in this hotel for one night, as a stop over on a three week road trip of the East coast. The hotel was relatively easy to find and parking was good, as long as you got there early, which we did. The parking fills up almost instantly once check-in time arrives. 
Our check-in was ok, can't say the desk staff were OVERLY friendly. The staff in general weren't very friendly or helpful. 
The room was lovely. We aimed for cheap and cheerful and that is what we got. Our room was clean and comfortable, exactly what we wanted! We had a room with a beautiful view of the Benjamin Franklin Bridge, it almost looked as if it was coming out of the room on top and to the side of ours, SPECTACULAR, especially at night!
Whilst the hotel wasn't in the heart of the historic district, it was a short walk away. A little bit awkward to figure out as you need to walk a short distance and use stairways to get onto one of the bridges in order to access the town, as the hotel is at a lower level to the rest of the town. Also, saying that, if you wish to take a 'stroll' down to the museum of art, which we did, you are probably better getting a taxi! That is quite a walk away. Something we hadn't counted on for our one night stay.
The breakfast wasn't anything to write home about but at least they were offering something, again not much! 
Overall, we were quite happy with our stay.

The hotel is located right next to union square, so very central for the downtown area. The room was average, had a TV, hairdryer, toiletries, coffee making facilities, a safe, access to the internet via the TV, fridge.
The hotel has its own bar-restaurant next door but didnt use it, but looked pleasant, there is also another bar next door where you can get drinks and food. At the back of the hotel is an Irish bar. There are a few restaurants around this area, but it is mainly shopping.
The powell-mason street cable car stop is just round the corner, this takes you all the way to Pier --. You can walk it in about -- minutes (be prepared for a couple of steep streets!).
At pier -- there are much more restaurants and a some bars-pubs etc, so if you are looking for evening entertainment you may be better staying in this area. However we did go to Pier -- on a couple of evenings and it is easy to get the cable car back or there is a direct bus (route --).
Hotel pool small but very quiet and nice. Staff average.
We paid $--- for seven nights (not a club room and no balcony), but apparently an upgrade from a basic room. booked direct with the hotel.

We stayed here because it was low priced and we were attending the San Francisco Macy's Christmas tree lighting. 
The room was small, very small. A full size bed, a tv, a desk chair and table. The small fridge was nice. The bathroom was clean, but they did not provide a towel for the floor, so the tiles were very cold and slippery. The hardwood floors are nice. 
The elevator is slow. The stairs are narrow, in is an old victorian style. It was nice. 
This place was very clean, the staff was not friendly but not rude either. Just business.
The restaurant and hotel lobby was loud when we returned. If you had a room in that area it would be noisey. We did not have that problem. The walls are thin though!
Parking is either valet ($-- plus --% tax) or find a local place for about -- plus the same tax.

We travel all over the world and finally we have found a true luxury hotel. The rooms are spacious and are beautifully decorated. The personal touches are fantastic; they will even send a staff member to draw a bath for you! This is a wonderful hotel with a fantastic location (the Denver Center for Performing is right across the street)! We highly recommend Hotel Teatro. We can’t wait to return.

Just returned from our first visit to Austin. Our choice of Summerfield Suites was perfect. Not too far from town, lots of good restaurants nearby, close enough to major roads that every destination was close at hand. 
Rooms were laid out nicely. Staff were attentive and did a great job. 
Hot breakfast daily was a real plus.

We had a quick two night stay in San Fran and managed to book the Westin St. Francis through Priceline. The room was on the smaller side (hey, it is an historic property) but clean and well appointed. The hotel and location were fabulous. There are some great restaurants and amazing shopping in this area. Also, there is a cable car stop right across from the hotel. I had read some reviews noting the area was a bit dodgy, but my daughter and I were out and about breakfast through dinner each day and did not find that to be the case. I would definitely stay here again.

Spent - nights at the Sofitel in Jan ----, and were cvertainly recommend it to anyone.
We arrived at about midday and was immediately given acesss to our room on the --th floor.
The room was bright, airy and very clean and the bed complete with light fluffy duvet was the most comfortable hotel bed I have ever slept in. Included in the room was a safe and a mini bar (we didn't use it as I suspect the prices were very high) and on our floor was an ice making machine. Bottels of water were regularly provided.
We had an evening flight out of NY and were allowed to delay checking out until -pm. The staff were almost apolgetic that they couldn't extend checkout later than that but explained that they were pretty full the following night.
We didn't make use of the restaurant but just a few steps along from the hotel was an excellent little diner (The Red Flame) that provided excellent breakfasts for about $-- that would keep you going until lunch and beyond. Drinks at the bar were a little expensive, but they always came with a wonderful bowl of olives and a bowl of nibbles that were regularly topped up.
There is a gym in the hotel, just in case you didn't get enough exercise walking Manhattan. Unfortunately there was no sauna that would have been very welcome to sooth sore feet.
An excellent location (--th Street between -th and -th Avenue) a few minutes walk from Times Square where you can get the subway to travel further afield.
I would look no further for a hotel if I was to return to NY

I booked three rooms at the hotel for my brothers wedding in the city. Since they were having a very low maintenance wedding to celebrate their --th anniversary this location seemed central. Reaching out prior to the hotel for recommendations, Taralyn had some really great ideas to share. I travel a lot, and my expectation is that the staff at the hotel will recommend something """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""local"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and unique. In many cases I am disappointed with what they come up with but not here. Taralyn listened to every word I said and offered thoughtful suggestions to meet our needs. My brother arrived Thursday before anyone else. The General Manager had personally upgraded their accomodations and sent a lovely amenity to welcome and congratulate them. He did not stop there, he had done the same for me! What a great way to begin my first trip to the Big Apple.
However, there are three elements that set this hotel appart and that have me wanting to return already...
First, the design. Both the architecture and the thoughtful touches in the hotel make you feel at home. The fireplace in the lobby between both front desk pods was a really nice focal point. The rooms were spacious compared to most in NYC. Keep in mind we were not in the Cozy Room category. The bathrooms were really well thought our and the beds are amazing.
Second, the roof top terrace. The hotel started opening the roof top lounge last year to test it out and had moderate success. This year the owners invested some money to put cool furniture and decor up there and this was the place my brother decided to get married -- hours before the vows. The best part was once they decided this the entire staff offered all they could to make it memorable. The space was great and I hear they filmed a portion of Sex and the City up there. Either way, if I lived in the city I would be up there weekly! Great cocktails and excellent service provided by Vinny.
Finally, it's all about the service here. Without a doubt this hotel has the best customer service I have ever recieved in NYC. Nicole and Chanel at the Front Desk in the evenings were TOP NOTCH. They recognized us everytime we walked in the hotel and offered assistance at every turn. These ladies truly get it. The part that amazed me the most is that even the bellmen knew that my brother was getting married in the hotel and asked because of my last name if I was in """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""the wedding party"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", that blew me away. Danny and Daniel were on point with everything from arranging cabs to delivering room service and even giving directions. They were friendly and engaging at every turn. The restaurant Opia threw together a pre-fixe menu with less than -- hours notice, placed us in a private room and even had custom linen, specially printed menus on the table with fresh cut flowers.
Bottom line, you can not go wrong at this hotel. Clearly they love their jobs and it shows!

-. Cheap- you get what you pay for.
-. Easy and convenient for a single individual traveling alone.
-. Internet service. 
-. Close proximity to University of Washington. Village Shopping Center.
-. Clean bathroom, room.

Outdated and not maintained to say the least..... This hotel has not be updated in at least --years and I am being nice at that. Meet family there from LA and MO to have a little weekend get together. Made me look like I didn't do my homework.. which I didn't and that was my fault. There were a number of items that I noticed that were either dirty (walls-doors), stained (carpet) or torn (couch cushions). I asked for more bedding and the blankets had holes in them. I will pass on this Embassy Suites when in Dallas next time. 
Plus there was some band playing or some sort of music playing until midnight that rang thru the hotel.....

We return here every year, and always receive excellent service. (I admit, the fact that we """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""help them"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" remember us makes a difference.) Rooms and facilities are what one would expect in a large convention hotel. Good business services. The key to a great stay is executive lounge access (by booking an executive level room or being HiltonHonors Gold or higher). This peaceful little oasis with a view offers free continental breakfast, late afternoon hors d'oeuvres, wireless Internet access and a couple large-screen TVs, usually set to a cable news channel. Wine and cocktails can be purchased. We've found it useful for hosting local guests (for an extra fee, of course) or for a quiet chat with other hotel guests. The District Line restaurant in the lobby offers spotty food and service. Bell staff can also be variable. Good location, between Dupont Circle and Adams-Morgan (think great Ethiopian food).

We just recently stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn and thought the facility was great. It is very convenient to everything. It's a short walk to the Historical district and the subways are very close. I didn't find the surrounding area to be a problem as some of the reviews that I read, having said that I did grow up just outside New York city and in comparison this area was no problem. The hotel seems to be adjacent to China Town and there are some great Chinese restaurants close to the hotel. We were there for a concert at the Tower theater and the subway was a very convenient ride ($-.-- round trip for - people)

Needed to get away from cold weather. Upon arriving in sunny San Diego, I gave the hotel a call (be sure to keep the phone number handy), and the free airport shuttle was dispatched. The driver was very courteous and knowledgable. The person running the front desk asked me about my room preference ... I wanted it quiet, so he gave me a room on the third floor away from the current street maintenance. I found my room and went to the pool ... well kept with plenty of lounges. Upon returning to my room, I asked for a room change to be closer to the pool and still on the quiet third floor. The front desk was very gracious and accommodating, and I had in the blink of an eye, a room to my liking ... far from the street and close to the pool. I didn't see any free popcorn, but there was coffee, TV (with HBO), microwave, refrigerator, hair dryer, iron w-board, beach towels, and a room safe. The office lobby also had free internet and WiFi. This was certainly nice when I checked out as I was able to download and print my boarding pass. I went to the zoo. A free shuttle to and from was provided. Actually, the hotel provides free to and from shuttle to all the local attractions. There is a bus stop just outside the hotel, but I walked the short distance (perhaps - - - blocks) to the trolley station and easily accessed downtown. In fact, the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Blue Line"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" goes all the way to Tijuana. The cost was $-.-- each ride, or $-.-- for an all day pass ...a great deal! The other review didn't care for Bunz (hamburger-hot dog restaurant on the property). I ate there twice. The prices were reasonable and the food was good. Although I had a late departure, they let me hang out in the room for two hours past check-out. I would most definitely stay here again.

I want to remind others that this is only a - diamond resort. I definitely feel they are charging - diamond prices, but I think the service and surroundings reflect the - star rating. We had a garden room that backed up to the miniature golf course and was only surrounded by - other rooms. It was peaceful and quiet and clean. The hotel was renovated about - yrs ago and I usually stay in a beachfront suite, but this time, due to the busy holiday, stayed in a - queen room. We had great service from the time we checked in, to the bellman that drove us on the cart to our room and called for more towels and our rollaway. The grounds are kept up well and we enjoy the beach. I agree, the sand is abit dirty and the main heated pool (yes, there ARE - heated pools) was really crowded this time of year (too cold to swim in unheated) and towels were not cleaned up while swimming late night, but we found the hotel to be most enjoyable. We had our own car, so we didnt eat at the resort and we went to a close grocery and got fire wood and marshmallows to roast on the beach. As far as ants, we did see a few (but I grew up in CA and there are alot of ants on the coast), but not a problem and the bathroom was beautiful marble and very clean. I think for a family resort this is the place to go!

The rooms were excellent, with good views, comfortable beds and a kitchen with all the needed dinnerware was supplied. The breakfasts were yummy and the dinners and drinks were great. I would recommend this hotel with great pleasure. The staff was friendly and helpful. Thank you for a great - day stay at your hotel.

Stayed here as part of the National Pop Warner Convention. As you can imagine, between that, some other large group booking, and it being Memorial Day Weekend the place was lively and bustling. But that really did not impact service too much. We were able to get our car quickly on two occasions, seats at the restaurant and bar, and the elevators came fairly quickly. This is an older, refurbished hotel where some of the age is visible but it's relatively nice for this type of hotel and size. I can't really complain about too much. The bathroom and room was not exactly sparkling clean upon check-in but that's really my only complaint. It's very conveniently located. Be aware the valet parking is very expensive. No wireless service.

We used to stay at another nearby hotel but their room costs are constantly going up so we decided for a little more money to try Copley Square Hotel. Glad we did. We used to stay here before the renovations and now the hotel is so much better. Every staff member is friendly and helpful. (Thanks Rene!) Our room was decorated very contemporary. It was clean and comfortable. The bathroom was a bit tight and their was no place to put toiletries. The complimentary wine hour was a special treat. The downstairs bar off the lobby was very busy and noisy. Overall our stay was excellent and we will definitely be staying here for every Boston trip.

I had once stayed before in a SpringHill Suites in a suburban location (VA). This one was much nicer, definitely had more of an in-town classic feel, particularly in the stately lobby. The valet parking (only option at the hotel) is pricey, but I guess that's to be expected. The location is EXCELLENT... just a couple blocks to the Inner Harbor (you can see it when you round the corner upon leaving the hotel), also close to the Mt. Vernon Cultural District. Also close to the Charles Center Metro Station, if you need that.
Free breakfast didn't have many options, but for free I suppose you could just be confronted with a continental breakfast, and this was better than that. Overall, a good choice.

My recent trip to San Francisco was not as pleasant as it should have been. Being a Diamond member with Hilton for many years and staying exclusively at Hilton properties around the world i have come to expect a level of service and quality of room that this hotel did not meet. The location can't be beat and it was well worth the cost of the stay. All of the staff, from the valet to the front desk, were amazingly friendly and helpful. There is a Gordon Biersch brew pub downstairs and several restaurants on the same block or nearby that offer all kinds of food choices at varying costs. When leaving, we saw that the restaurant next door served a breakfast panini and beverage for less than $-. There are two musuems right outside your door and the standard attractions (White House, monuments, etc.) are a quick walk away. Valet parking is the only option at the hotel, it comes to about $-- with tax, per -- hours but also allows in-and-out priveleges. 
The room has a fridge for actual use, great views with floor to ceiling windows and is very quiet. There is a nightclub across the street--my room was on the third floor and and had two windows that faced the club. Despite seeing a line of people waiting to get into the club, once in our room we heard nothing. Also, I arrived early and was able to check in early.
The were few downsides to the hotel. The tv signal actually took about -- minutes to come in clearly. Also, the bathtub is less than -- inches wide before it starts curving up--I wear a size -- shoe and when I turned my foot sideways in the tub, both my toes and my heel were on a curve of the tub. So, I found that out and don't know if it was just the layout of our room or if that was standard for the hotel. Also, I didn't know about the energy saving feature on the thermostat. Even if you are satisfied with the room temperature when you check in, read the sticker next to thermostat! It will tell you how to overrid the energy saver feature--if you don't override the feature, the thermostat will shut off if it does not detect motion in the room. This is fine if you're out and about for the day but not so fine at night when you're sleeping...I woke up to a super stuffy room.
Overall, this hotel is great and I would recommend it to anyone and stay here again myself.

I have stayed at the Mayflower for many years (at least -- times). The hotel was quiet and the staff incredibly polite. Now, you get a USA Today at best (a few other newspapers are downstairs in a room where you can also get coffee but you need to dress and it always chancey whether there are any left). When you call to request a specific part of the hotel to stay (advice :ask for the quiet side facing ABC news towards --th street), all the staff will do is say if when you check in if a room is still available they'll let you have it. Don't get me wrong it is still a nice hotel, but they have slowly but surely reduced their class from a - star to a -.- star...and for the price, it isn't worth it--try the Jefferson (after it is reopened) or Hay Adams (small rooms though) for top notch quality. for the small hotel experince try the Talbert Inn on N Street

I stayed at this hotel on a business trip and it was a great hotel. Clean, centrally located in downtown, and all of the service and amenities that you would expect from a full service Marriott. I would recommend this hotel for business or pleasure.

I stayed with a couple of friends at the Econo lodge for the labour day weekend and the hotel had no hot water for the weekend. The staff didn't apologize and the toilet in one of the rooms overflowed twice.

My wife and I have stayed here on a couple of occasions. First for our anniversary. Staff was great. Upgraded us to a higher floor and a Lake view. Magnificent. Our second stay was for New Year's Eve. What a great party at this hotel. And the convenience of stumbling to the elevator after a great night of dining, drinking and dancing was real nice.

Nice, new, and very clean hotel. Very friendly staff even on the late shift. Close and convenient to the airport. Large modern room and comfortable bed. I would definitely stay here again for business.

We liked the hotel but the service was horrible. Once we asked for a fork and a knife and waited for -- minutes. When i called the manager on duty her reply was that they are very busy. HOPEFULLY OTHER GUESTS WILL HAVE BETTER LUCK THAN I HAD!!!!

The Casablanca Hotel is in a great location and staffed by a lovely and caring group of employees. Our -th floor room was smallish but cozy and nicely decorated. My husband and I just got back from NYC and I must say that the experience was top notch because of the lovely hotel we stayed in. When we arrived we automatically got upgraded to a King room and the room was beautiful, very modern and very comfortable with a balcony over looking Park Avenue. Breakfast every morning was perfect, just small and simple and the lounge area to sit in and enjoy it was lovely and relaxing. Upstairs the rooftop patio was awesome, we enjoyed many glasses of wine at the end of a long day and overall the service was ten out of ten. I would recommend this hotel to any one visiting NYC as the area was great as well, close to everything and very central.

Stayed here recently for - nights, it was my first trip to NYC and we were just looking for an affordable base from which to see the city. The hotel is very clean, with good air conditioning but rooms are so tiny, the shower was hot and cold, and front desk staff (bar one guy, who was pleasant) are SO unfriendly. I've never stayed in a hotel where I didnt receive a warm welcome, I also used to work in hotels so I know how important these first impressions are! We used the hotel as a base for our sightseeing, and it served its purpose as that. The room was so small, but we didn't spend much time in it so we were not too bothered by it. The location is good with plenty restaurants-cafes nearby and central park, and natural history museum within walking distance, and a subway station literally round the corner. We didn't have a bad experience, but it could have been better.

This hostel is great - only - blocks (- minutes) walk south of the subway station (---rd st on red line - number -) and very easy to find. Cheap chain supermarket near the subway and a great kitchen with grill-oven, toaster and microwaves - very easy to eat in. The mixed dorm - person hostel rooms are bunk beds with sink and air conditioner. Spacious room but basic. The 'shared bathroom' was great - actually a private bathroom but shared - so it had a toilet sink and bath-shower in the one room - better than the standard shower room ones you usually find in hostels. Nobody was ever using the bathroom when we wanted to so it was great. The hostel plays films throughout the day if you are having a lazy day and give out free popcorn. There are lots of comfortable lounge areas and big flat screens. I really loved this hostel! Don't hesitate to stay here!
Be CAREFUL - although it is great that maids change your sheets daily - we are sure we had a metrocard stolen from our room - so don't leave anything worth stealing out.

One of the best things about this hotel is the location. We could virtually walk to everything we wanted to see (Times Square, the theatres, Radio City etc) and the subway was only seconds away. The bed was very comfortable and the room, though not large was beautifully clean & livable and the free wifi a bonus.The street it fronts is a little dingy but never at any time during our six night stay did we feel threatened or uncomfortable. A great place to stay.

This is a good hotel, very well located in Union Square, great to go shopping and eating. The rooms are clean, the staff is really polite, in general a good experience.
The hotel doesnt have a parking, so you have to first park in front unload your luggage and leave it with the bell boy at reception or bring it already to your room and then go and park the car. The garage is a public one that also serves the hotel, and is like a block away, so this might be a problem for some people, for us it was ok.
The rooms are tiny, really little, and as we had lots of luggage, that wasnt optimal, but we managed. The hotel is not new, but well kept and clean.
The hotel also doesnt have a restaurant, there is a restaurant there but doesnt belong to the hotel, so if you want, you can have breakfast there and they even will charge it to the room, but is a separate business. I will not recommend it though, because we had breakfast there twice and you have to wait FOREVER to get your food. So if you are staying here, I would recomend you to go the Cafe du Paris that is very close (great breakfast) or next door, there is a great place, a little expensive, but with a wide range of options, very nice food and efficient service.
All in all a good place to stay in San Francisco, not so expensive and central.

Great location just a short walk from times square and very modern and clean.
Would come back again any time. Perfect hotel for a five night stay in New York. 
Cabins were well laid out and thought through. Plenty of places to eat and drink nearby.

I stayed in the Pod Hotel for a week in order to do some research in New York City. As I was on a budget, this was ideal for me. The cost is very reasonable, and the accommodations are great. It makes me wonder what I really need all the extra hotel room space for! If travelling by yourself, this is the ideal place to stay. Bathrooms were spotless, and they have great warning lights above the doors to let you know when they are available.

We stayed at this stylish hotel for - nights in June and had a lovely pleasant stay!

We loved this hotel and its location, we highly recommend it and will definitely stay re-book next time we're in NYC.

Booked this as the relaxation break in between holidaying in Las Vegas and San Francisco. A delightful resort in an otherwise just-ok area. Set on Mission Boulevard on the bay (but with the open ocean just across the road from resort). The rooms are delightful, well appointed and large with equally generous balconies and terraces. Our room had a balcony overlooking a beautiful ornamental pond appointed with fish and ducks. Just around dusk a man arrives to light the gas flames on sticks around the pond so no one falls in. This is both practical and beautiful. Maid service was truly efficient and nicely late morning - into the afternoon. Free coffee making facilities and a huge television (TV set inside a carved unit. Took me - days to realise that once you've opened the doors to view TV you can then actually slide the doors back inside the unit so as not to have to duck and dive around them). The walls of these rooms are nicely thick. I didn't hear my fellow guests below or adjacent once in our - days here. This is a quiet resort hotel so don't book this if you like to think you're going to teach people how to have a lovely loud night in your room or balcony-terrace. It's very tranquil and any younger people who do check-in for the weekend (chiefly young Americans) know better than to continue their 'good time' vibe here after dark. They take themselves out of the hotel to the bars outside and return perhaps a little drunk but with due consideration. The hotel pool area is nice enough but rather cramped with sun loungers set side by side by side with barely an inch between them. It does however provide fresh beach-lounger towels for free (you sign your name and room number against the loan). There is also a poolside bar and hot-cold snack area. I would definitely return to this resort.

The hotel itself is stunning and the room was beautiful. However, there was no gift shop, only one restaurant with very limited room service and the menu was mostly sushi - which I do not eat. There were no shops or restaurants nearby and since I did not know the area well, was somewhat stranded. The CVS across the street was the highlight. I must say, that the staff was OUTSTANDING and very accommodating. Had the location been better, I would have recommended this hotel. One small thing - if you want ice, there are no machines - you have to call room service or housekeeping and then wait for them and tip them...
This hotel needs a serious over haul. The staff upon check needs a serious over haul as well, like remembering they are in the hospitality business. Never again.

I found the Chelsea Lodge using TripAdvisor. TripAvisor has earned its keep with this one!

The rooms have their own sink and shower, but you have to use the shared bathrooms. All the above are exceptionally clean. I have definitely paid more for a dirtier, but private, bathroom. Don't let this scare you off - the Chelsea Lodge is a great place.

First time in NYC. What a great location , walking distance to most everything you would want to see. Hotel staff very helpful . Greeted by Tom at the front desk who made us feel at home.
Would stay here again

A one night stay, got a great rate, especially for the size and content of the suite. THe suite includes a living area, kitchen, bedroom, and a nice size bathroom. The rooms appear to be recently decorated.

The Conrad was a refreshing change from the ordinary business class hotel. It was upscale without being stiflingly opulent, and the staff were professional without being curt; helpful without being overly friendly. The furniture and furnishings were modern, warm and inviting. The huge flat screen television that met me when I entered the room certainly was a nice touch. Even nicer touches included consistent turn down services from almost invisible and unobstrusive staff members, with niceties left. The Conrad doesnt come cheap, but that is to be expected with the class of service provided. Other colleagues of mine stayed at lesser offerings and complained about huge convention crowds, impersonal service and banal, usual business class rooms. I had the opportunity to sample what I have come to expect from Hilton hotels, and one of this category: true hospitality and comfort.

Just returned from a weeks stay at the Gaslamp Plaza Suites. Our suite was a mini on the -th floor and was tasteful, comfortable and clean. It suited our needs just fine because our trip was to experience San Diego and all that goes with it, not to stay in a hotel room. Housekeeping services was very good. and the staff was pleasant and helpful. We visited many areas of the City by walking or using public transportation. The weather was great and if your stay is to enjoy the City there is no necessity to rent a vehicle nor is there any need to worry about where to eat. There are plenty of restaurants of great variety. Places to visit are Coronado, Old Towne, Seaport Village, the San Diego Zoo and Balboa Park. Our next visit will include LaJolla. 
We enjoyed the view from the rooftop and took advantage of the continental breakfast served there every morning.

First, the location is quite good. Located on the northeast corner of the Loop district, the Hotel Monaco is just two blocks from the Magnificent Mile and one block from any of the public transit trains.

The staff, particularly the doormen were quite charming, though we felt they were overwhelmed at times. That's not their fault, but we felt a little sorry for them.
All-in-all, a good choice, but we'd likely explore another of Chicago's boutique options on our next trip.
