The room was clean, and although small, I have stayed in smaller in Europe and New York. To those complaining about size, well, dont go to Europe, Japan or other places. Any issue that was negative I have read on other reviews are all matters I have encountered at Comfort, and even Hampton. So those checking out this Hotel because you cant get in the Hyatt for your conference, it is within walking distance, and they provide a shuttle if you need it. Breakfast is standard fare but served on real plates with real flatware (the Hampton could take a clue from this), If you are a solo traveler, this is a good bet, if not, you may want a suite. I would stay here again in a heartbeat. Bon Voyage.
Fantastic location! Spotless room, good size, good breakfast. Staff v helpful. Use of computer-printer throughout stay. Highly recommended!

The bad first. Be ready to pay $-- for valet parking, not much choice in the city I guess and many of the other hotels I looked at were high also. It was Friday night and the hallway was loud, a couple rooms were back and forth doors slamming etc. 
The good. We were here for a college visit and stayed just one night. The room was average size with two beds. The bathroom was average also. No smells or anything in the room or bathroom. The bathroom contained the shower sink and toilet, I prefer the sink and mirror outside making it easier for two people to get ready. Shampoo and body wash in containers mounted to the shower wall. Just a pet peeve of mine but I hate the system they use for the TV channels, making you through menus and stuff before actually getting to the channels. 
Breakfast was just OK but it was free. Coffee was pretty good.

The staff at River North provided personal service that exceeded any of my expectations. I travel constantly for business throughout the US and rarely stay at a Marriott, unless forced, since they first adopted their ---% no smoking policy. They don't even provide an area that can shade you from the heat or protect you from storms in order to sit when you step outside to smoke. So, they've been on my """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""do not book"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" travel list for years. However, the conference booked our rooms and there I was.... Marriott Courtyard. My TV remote was dead and the hotel engineer (I called him the Fonz) tapped the TV with his hand and it worked... for a bit. To make things worse just three hours after checking in at the hotel I came down with a fever. Although the hotel is just a few blocks from the Red Line, that I planned to use to commute to the office on, and very near a number of good and great restaurants and shops, walking out even -- ft. in the --- degree weather with a fever was more than I could handle. I talked with the staff (Tabatha), who was sincere and empathetic, explaining that I felt I needed to move to hotel where I could easily walk to the office and get room service as necessary. She explained how I should address the situation with the manager and was willing to do whatever she could to help. The manager was sympathetic and willing to help me change hotels. However, I decided in the end that I just couldn't muster enough energy to even move to another hotel and headed up to bed. A few minutes later the manager, John O'Connor, came to my door. He had brought me chicken noodle soup, sourdough toast and water to help me feel better. Needless to say, it worked, in so many ways. A little love and some chicken soup comforts and heals like nothing else. When it comes from a hotel manager... it heals on a much deeper level. I was full of energy and feeling great the next day. The TV didn't come on the next morning The Fonz tapped it again and it worked...since he actually had a new remote hidden behind his back that we laughed about and he left for me. Marriott is no longer blocked on my travel list, my time in Chicago was fantastic, I will never forget the Fonz, and I will always cherish Tabatha and especially John for their love, compassion, and superior customer service.

Stayed overnight while visiting a client in littleton. 
Rooms were clean, spacious and comfortable.
Location was okay, a little ways from downtown Denver....however there are a several very nice bars and restaurants across the street from the tech centre.
Stay was just perfect for a business trip! Not sure if I would stay with the family.

We were a party of - adults who stayed at the Shelburne for a few days over Christmas ----. The room we pre-paid for was a one bedroom suite. When we arrived we were given a two-bedroom suite. We've been to New York many times in the past and this was by far the largest room - - queen beds, three televisions and two bathrooms. Our only complaints were that we asked for a quiet room and were instead put on the second floor - the traffic noise was horrible. The door lock on the room was a bit sticky - but with some pushing it would lock. The cleaning staff were lovely and even supplied extra towels when we asked. The location can't really be beat. You can walk to Macy's, the Empire State Building and Times Square. There are dozens of quaint places to eat in the neighborhood. Above all else, the staff was lovely and accomodating.

My husband and I decided to start off the New Year downtown with a nice dinner and hotel stay. What we had instead was a confusing, expensive, sleepless night. The person at check in was extremely rude, but we shrugged it off as post NYE work. We get to the -th floor and are met with carts of garbage from other rooms in the hall. It was -pm when we checked in-- why is that still there? Our room was completely blocked by a cleaning cart. We jumped over-- went inside to find a small cold room with faded outdated furniture. The chair's leather was peeling, the wallpaper was peeling, and the window screens had been slashed and not repaired. 
But that isn't the worst of it. The worst of it was the heating system. An old outdated system that took -- minutes to heat up a tiny room but did it with such loud banging and clanking that we were unable to sleep all night. My husband and I took turns turning it off-- sleeping for an hour-- freezing-- and then turning it back on again. By -am the cleaning crew had begun banging and slamming doors. We had no chance. This hotel was very expensive. No excuse. There are better hotels in the same location. We've been to the Conrad Hilton and had a great experience-- go there instead.

I had been by the Mayflower Hotel on numerous occasions, and actually attended several meetings over the years at the Mayflower, but this was my first time ever actually staying in the hotel, when recently I stayed there for a week. The history of the building is fascinating in and of itself, but the amenities; the service and the quality of everything is definitely - star.
I was on the --th Floor, and my room was where former Vice President Curtis's (Hoover Administration) apartment was located, and former Senator John Kennedy' maintained his love shack! 
As far as location, you can't do much better, the Mayflower is located off of Connecticut Avenue and L Street....There is a Metro Station right adjacent to the Hotel, and McPhearson Square, where the Occupy D.C. folks were gathered is only a block or so away, (On K Street). I ventured down to meet with my """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Peeps"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" at the the Occupy D.C. gathering, and although I chose the Mayflower versus the Occupy D.C. Peeps' accommodations, I was there, protesting whatever the Hell it is that these folks are protesting, and also offering free personal hygiene tips.

For the price, I thought our room was a bit cramped and only had a double bed. It was an incredibly comfortable bed though. The building was beautiful and filled with history but the stay was riddled with unexpected fees. Only parking option onsite is valet which was over $---night and seemed very slow. Also had to pay daily for wifi. Not bad for a night, but can really add up for a longer stay!
I particularly want to commend the helpfulness of Jack, the Bell Captain; and Ralph, a Security Guard. They went above and beyond in their helpfulness to me.

My wife and I had a wonderful stay at the Charlotte Marriott City Center in October ----. Great location. Very convenient self parking. We had a very nice room on the --th floor - above the noise of a busy downtown. Concierge lounge on --th floor provided one of the best concierge lounge breakfasts i've had at any Marriott or Hilton around the world. Very attentive and helpful staff. And the internet was fast and reliable.

I was a participant in the ---- International Sport & Cultural Festival which took place June -----, ---- in Ft. Worth. The Omni was designated as the hotel that most participants would stay in. It worked out great overall, because the hotel is directly across frpm the Forth Worth Convention Center, adjacent to which are the very impressive Water Gardens. Downtown Fort Worth has much to offer, including a free downtown shuttle. But since this is a review of the hotel, I will limit my comments to the accommodations. The hotel is new, opened only on Jan --, ----. The hotel employees were all super friendly and eager to assist. My room was spacious and luxuriously appointed. I was on the --th floor and had a fabulous view all the way to Dallas. I was pleased that there was a safe in the room, since during performances we had to leave all personal belongings and documents somewhere and the safe came in very handy. There was a refrigerator, a coffee maker, bottled water, hairdryer, and a robe. I had two queen beds that were comfortable, the only negative beeing a great surplus of pillows, so that the unused bed basically functioned as a storage for all those pillows. If both beds are being used, storing all of the decorative pillows might be a nuisance (there were - regular pillows plus - large decorative pillows, so a total of - pillows, per bed). The air conditioning worked well and was completely adjustable by the guest. The room was very quiet, no noise of any kind from neighboring rooms. I assume they have good sound insulation, since we had a lot of kids staying there and I know they tended to be noisy. Overall, the room was very comfortable. I didn't use any of the in-house amenities like pool, video game rooms, and the like. The festival had many children and youths and many were not accustomed to the extreme heat we were experiencing (around ---F during the day), so I overheard many adults say what a blessing it was they had some way to entertain the children during their free time. I did not eat in the on-premises restaurant, I only know it was there, also a gift shop which I did not visit. The entire hotel premises are non-smoking, which was great, but the hotel will need to find a better solution to accommodate its smoking guests. Currently all the smokers sit outside the front door where also arriving and departing guests are entering or leaving the building, plus the valets bring parked cars for their drivers, and the taxis are picking up or dropping off guests. This area is completely covered on top but open onto the street. With the car fumes and all the smokers, this makes for an upleasant atmosphere, especially for nonsmokers. The hotel should relocate the smokers to a designated area, probably indoors and with a separate ventilation system, but I am sure they will soon take care of this one negative. The hotel is trying extremely hard to meet the needs of their guests and I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone who needs to stay in the downtown Fort Worth area, and would recommend highly this location for any convention-type event. The convention participants do not need own transportation. The convention center is right across the street. The Water Gardens provide a welcome respite in an urban setting and are just steps away. Downtown Fort Worth is compact and can be crossed on foot in about -- minutes. For those who don't want to walk, there is the Molly the Trolley, a free shuttle service that runs continuously. Downtown FW has many shops and restaurants and is magical at night and completely safe for pedestrians. The Stockyards provide more entertainment and dining and shopping opportunities and there is city bus transportation that connects the downtown and the stockyards. One night we visited the Stockyards and went to a rodeo and then to Billy Bob's Texas. We had a great time. Overall, this is a great place to stay for a family or for a larger group.

I had a great stay at this hotel. Staff was excellent and I felt like I was right at home. I needed a ride to and from the aiport and they went out of their way to pick me up and take me back to get a rental car, but they were sold out, so they came back and picked me up. Great people, great hotel..

I recently stayed at this Doubletree for - weeks on my own. Everything about my stay was outstanding. Excellent rooms, great food in the restaurant and the hotel is so clean and nice. I saw every type of traveler staying at this property. I believe it is suitable for everyone. Barbara, Lindsay, and Cristina at the front desk are so helpful as is everyone who works there. Ask to meet Bill in sales just to say hi, he is one of the nicest fellows I ever met. The restaurant was very busy one day and he stepped in to serve the guests. I could go on naming all the great staff and I do so as I am so thankful to have chosen this hotel. 
The Del Mar area is very beautiful and not having a car I was able to use the hotel shuttle to take me to locations nearby. All of the shuttle drivers were excellent, Jose, Sean and Aj were all very consciences drivers. I felt very safe with all of them. The hotel calls upon a car service for other transportation including the airport and the fellow Alibaba is also a very reliable driver. He is always on time and also a good driver. 
It is unlikely I would stay anywhere else in San Diego after having found this hotel. There is a Vons mall a very short walk away if you don’t drive and need to pick up some essentials. If you are a gal, at this mall there is a small boutique shop called Ronda’s closet, check it out.
Thank you very much Doubletree, I will see you again in September.

Used Econolodge for Park 'n Fly services over the weekend to attend a funeral out of state. The rate charged me more than the guaranteed online rate for one. Were very rude to other costumers during my check in process. When I returned I found it very apparent that my car had been used by one of the employees for personal use and that items had been stolen from my locked glove box. Don't use these people......they are crooks!

We are a late --'s couple on a budget. We had a --night stay at the Monarch. Overall it was a good stay, but we weren't expecting anything fancy. Located in the Tenderloin area, the Monarch allows you to experience the sights and sounds this neighborhood has to offer (pleasant or not). Smaller rooms with the basics, windows to the street are thin so you hear everything. Seemed like one employee on duty at all times so it could be a short wait to get help. It's an old SF hotel with some renovations and has character. Moderate walk to buses-MUNI-BART, Union Square & Market St. We just needed a place to sleep and shower after touring the city and this worked just fine. If you want relaxation don’t stay here.

My husband and I recently stayed at the Sanctuary for a fun, birthday weekend of Broadway shows and we had a wonderful time! If you're in town to see shows, the location, just steps from Times Square, can't be beat! We stayed in a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sweet"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on the -th floor, and could still hear the cabs honking on --th, but overall the noise level wasn't bad. If you're a light sleeper, request a room that doesn't face the street though. The room itself was gorgeous! The suite is essentially twice the size of a regular room. It was so nice to have the extra space. The living room included a sleeper sofa, a coffee table, a big screen tv with a Bose sound system and a docking station. The sound system was such a treat and really added to the ambiance of the room. The decorating was so warm and inviting, but had a nice touch of elegance, including - chandeliers! Gorgeous! We both got a kick out of the Japanese toilet with different washing and drying functions. The bath area is separated from the bed area only by a curtain but that didn't bother us. The glass enclosed rain head shower was awesome! I didn't want to get out. The vanity and the shower were both finished with emperador marble which is a personal favorite of mine. The room was beautifully done. As far as the room goes, the only cons for me would be the toiletries (I liked that it was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""green"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" brand, but they didn't feel luxurious), the size and feel of the towels, and the fact that the sheets were a bit rougher than I'd like. The bed was very, very comfortable though. 
The best thing about the Sanctuary is the staff! I try to stay in boutique hotels because I prefer the personal service and the Sanctuary definitely delivered! My husband mentioned that it was my birthday and the concierge brought me a card signed by the whole staff and a cupcake from Magnolia Bakery. Nice touch! Brandon was ready to deliver with everything from restaurant recommendations and reservations, to helping us figure out where to shop for area rugs and mapping out the stores for us. Michael and Peter were also very helpful. I definitely got the feeling that there is no request that would have gone unfulfilled at the Sanctuary. Even when I mentioned that the bathroom in our room smelled a bit musty, they tried to get rid of the smell. When we return to NYC, we will definitely be returning to the Sanctuary because it lived up to it's name!

What a delightful surprise this hotel was! It was in a very nice location, easy access to the
BART and the cable cars and abounds with wonderful shopping and restaurants. We have
always stayed at The Palace, the W, or other very large hotels and this was a wonderful
surprise. The room was extremely clean, quiet, well appointed for the use of a laptop but
best of all, the bed was amazing!!! We went to Sears and Cafe de la Presse for breakfast.
Walking to all of the sites of San Francisco is easy from this location but hilly, as another
reviewer said. Don't miss the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art while visiting - amazing
to see! Also, there is a WWII submarine that you can actually go on in Fisherman's Wharf.

this place in located right on the bay, great room, underground parking garage(only $- a day) free breakfast buffet. allaround great service, very friendly and helpful staff. i will stay here again and again. thx guys for a great weekend.

The location is optimal and the hotel itself is very nice and clean. Our basic room was big for NYC - with a separate sitting area and a spacious bathroom. The hotel staff were very accommodating and knowledgable. We had one meal at Riingo, the hotel restaurant - not bad at all.
Overall, this is a good choice for a nice weekend in the city. The price we got on expedia was better than the hotel itself could offer.

A lot about the hotel, I loved. The area was great... just off -- and also by the Cumberland Blue Line stop, so easy to get to either by highway or the CTA, and there was also free parking, which is almost impossible to find in the Chicago area. They provide a shuttle to close locations, so they were more than willing to drop me off at the Donald E Stephens Convention Center. The rooms were decently sized, the bathrooms were large, and there was a coffee pot.
Downsides on the room: the channels on the TV were very limited, and didn't include a channel guide so I had no way of knowing what programs were on. The TV was also an older TV (not a flat panel) which is rare to see in - star or above hotels.... most hotels have switched over to flat panels. Also, the air conditioner was very very loud and it was difficult to control the temperature... it was either too warm or too cold, since you couldn't actually set a temperature, so I had to constantly fuss with the dial. There was also a strange smell that reminded me of diapers in the hallway.
I had - very big problems with the hotel, other than the minor things mentioned above. The first is that I was there from a Thursday through Sunday, prepaid, but they deactivated my keys on Friday. I had to leave my friends and my belongings in the hallway and go back downstairs to get a new key made. The hotel claimed that my key became deactivated by a credit card or my phone, but my boyfriend's key was also deactivated... he's local and had to work until -am, so when he showed up at my room to cuddle he had to wake me up so I could let him in.
Sunday was the worst. My boyfriend wasn't able to see me off to the train station, so he left flowers at the front desk for me. They didn't call to let me know. When I checked out, I did so by calling down to the front desk since I didn't have to pay, and I spoke with an actual person instead of leaving a message, but I wasn't told about the flowers. They should've had my number on file as well, but didn't call me to let me know even after I checked out. - hours after I checked out, my boyfriend let it slip that I shouldn't received a surprise... when I called the hotel, they told me """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Yeah, you have flowers."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" At that point, I was already boarding my train and had no way to go back.
While the hotel itself was nice, the lack of courtesy at the front desk would be enough to make me avoid the hotel. Unfortunately, I also have a room reserved there next weekend, and it's through priceline so I'm unfortunately stuck. So I guess I'll see what happens.
Everything was well except for a maid tried to come in the room unannounced at about --;-- pm because she had lost a phone and was looking for it.

We were visiting our son who is studying for a semester in LA for - nights. We had a beautiful large, very clean, king room with -- feet of windows looking out on to the Hollywood Hills, it was a fantastic view. The staff at the front desk were very friendly and eager to answer any question we had. The location is a quick walk to Universal Studios and City Walk where there is a variety of food options. It is also a short distance (although LA traffic is a nightmare) to all major attractions.
The parking rate is high but seems to be the norm in the areas we visited in Southern California, so just be resigned to fact there is not much you can do about it.
My husband and I are both in the hospitality business and it is very refreshing to go on vacation and receive the quality of customer care that we give while doing our jobs. The staff at the Universal Hilton was a delight.

We spent - nights at the Porto Vista and were absolutely satisfied. We had a very nice room on the -th floor, which was clean and big enough. The bathroom was pretty huge, too. The hotel is located in Little Italy, so there a lot of good restaurants there, and Downtown and the Gaslamp District are within walking distance. Negative about this hotel: the free WiFi is extremely slow and the bathroom as a huge glass door, so you don't have any privacy, whatever you're doing, literally.

This is a good quality hotel that I stay in regularly on business trips to NYC. The location is very convenient for my workplace. 
It is a large and busy hotel. Decor is rather gaudy for my taste but is generally clean. I have always found the staff to be courteous and friendly. 
The rooms are hit and miss. If you get one of the newly-refurbished rooms there is nothing to complain about. I recently stayed in a couple of the older rooms however and I wasn't impressed. The carpet in one was damp due to faulty a-c...not nice 
The restaurant is pleasant enough. Breakfasts are better than the evening meals. 
There is no minibar in the rooms so even for basics like a bottle of water you have to purchase from a small shop in the foyer. They have a good selection but this is not convenient given the room rates. 
Final point to make is on the gym. It's on the top floor. Clean and I've always found there to be plenty of room. I find the selection of equipment rather odd. There are several running machines and cross trainers but only - bike and no rowing machines. 
In summary, there are a few frustrations with this hotel. But for business trips in mid town it's hard to beat for convenience and service
Booked this hotel after reading reviews on this website and I was not disappointed. This is a lovely little hotel, the staff are very friendly and helpful and the rooms are spotless.

The location is great, and the staff is what you expect from a Kimpton Hotel (human, easy going and dog-loving). The lobby and bar area are really comfortable and visually stunning. T
Unlike a lot of other Kimpton hotels, this property is not a renovated old building turned into a hotel but rather an old hotel renovated into a boutique. The rooms are on the small side and the bathroom I had was one of the smallest I have ever seen...think old London B&B...no real shelf space. Closet was very small as well, but functional. Overall the value for money is good, and as a single male I am not that fussed...there is nothing really wrong with this place, it is just not as good as other Kimpton properties. Next time I will try the Monaco.

My husband and I stayed at the Windsor after attending a dinner in Philadelphia. As soon as we walked into the hotel, we were greeted by a friendly staff. We received a free upgrade - and we were blown away by our room. The hallway included a walk-in closet; the bedroom had its own closet, as well; the kitchen was clean and well-stocked with cooking and dining ware; the living room was comfortable and included a flat screen TV - even the bathroom was beautiful! We loved the balcony and its view of Saints Peter and Paul Cathedral, too. Everything was clean and comfortable, making us wish we could stay longer than over night!

My husband and I went to Chicago this past weekend and stayed at the Chicago Hilton for - nights. We got the room off Priceline for $--, which I thought was decent for peak summer season. At check-in I was able to easily and quickly request the type of room I wanted and they also were able to upgrade me to concierge - Executive level for $-- per night. We were there with another couple (shared a room) so that cost was pretty reasonable when you consider the free continental breakfast every morning.
The room: Since we got Executive level, it was quite nice. Large, with a pretty corner view of the museum campus and Soldier Field. The only complaint I have about the room is the bathroom was on the small side. The beds were very comfortable, although a bit on the soft side. Since we were up on the --th floor, we had minimal road noise and it was good for sleeping. The room was always cleaned nicely and there was a turn-down service with good chocolates every night. AC worked great - no complaints here!
The Executive Level perks: We were on the --th floor, which is the same floor that the Executive Lounge was on. The continental breakfast was adequate, although very busy! They had bagels, muffins, cereal, fruit, yogurt, etc. The usual for this type of breakfast. The one perk I did like was the room was open all day for guests to get coffee, water, or pop if you were thirsty. This was very nice since the rooms only had an already-full mini bar for a fridge. As I said earlier, the room was also quite large - which I know was an Executive perk since I had read many reviews of how small some rooms were.
Other amenities: We didn't use the parking as I think $-- - night is highway robbery! I did notice some surface lots in the area that were as low as $-- - night though, that seemed quite cheap. The pool and hot tub area were very nice although busy. There were plenty of towels and the outside deck was a nice touch.
Overall, I would stay here again if doing a primarily sightseeing trip to Chicago. This hotel is much closer to the museum campus and the Art Institute than it is to the Mag Mile shopping area. We walked a lot and used the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""El"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" system to good advantage - the closest subway stop is only - blocks or so from the hotel.

The bathrooms were nice but the rooms felt a little sterile. Maybe it was the lighting, maybe it was the furniture, but the rooms felt like ones you would get at a high-end drug rehab center. A rehab center for the stars, if you will. I think it was the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""green"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" initiative that the hotel had going which created this vibe. I never thought I'd care about hotel room lighting, yet here I am. The ground zero contruction was not that bad and our window was practically pressed against it. The construction outside was soothing compared to the what sounded like Santa Claus getting a head start on some furniture making for next year in one of the nearby rooms. Every morning around -:--am, bang, bang, bang, bang from within the hotel, not outside.
The housekeeping staff and folks in the restaurant were very pleasant.

This was our first trip to San Fran. We saw a special hotel deal for $-- a night at the Adante Hotel. The hotel was clean and fairly comfortable, the location was good, very close to Union Square and the cable cars. The hotel service was okay, one day we went back to the hotel to take a nap and there were no sheets on our bed, still not sure why. This is a good deal in a city that has very few, so if you don't mind the fairly tacky decorating ( the mural at the front desk is beautiful, but the painting-mural in our room looked like it was done by a - year old ) Also, there are some very loud and inconsiderate people living in the complex next door. They had poker games, and blasted music a ---am many nights... So if you are looking for quiet getaway, DO NOT STAY HERE!!!! Also, make sure to visit Sausalito, Miur woods and the wine country (bus-van tour is best) and make sure to buy a - day public transportation MUNI pass for $--. The cable car rides alone are worth it, as they are $- each way!!!
Also, it gets pretty cold at night, so bring some sweaters-jackets. Also, there are an abundance of homeless people-vagrants that live here. And the food is not very good, and is very expensive. Other than that, there are many beautiful views to be seen, but the entertainment-food will never be as good as our home town Chicago.

I bid on a - star hotel on priceline.com for $-- (it was Memorial Day so I think the prices were higher) and got this one. I was worried when I saw the reviews but tried to have an open mind. We got to the hotel and had to wait for a man who was living there to pay with all dollar bills he had stuffed in his hat. When we got to the counter the lady was medium nice and gave us our room key. We went to our room. The hallway smelled like smoke. We got nervous because my husband is allergic to smoke but we went into our room and it didn't smell like it anymore. The room was nice and pretty clean. Nothing really gross about it. (The garbage was taken out). The rooms needed updating badly but it wasn't awful. The room had small plates and big plates, glasses and coffee mugs (I didn't look at silver wear); it had a refrigerator, microwave, a stove and a dishwasher. My husband turned on the a-c and it worked great. We didn't hear anyone in other rooms but there is a lot of traffic noise because it's located right next to an interstate. We watched the cable TV and went to bed. The bed is a queen size and every time someone moves the other can feel it. We kept waking up because of the other person moving. Check out went smoothly.
Overall if you find a great deal on this hotel I would stay in the hotel if you are alone but with two people it's hard sleeping on the bed.

booked this hotel - days before we travelled for a - night wedding anniversary trip to san fran. initially we were going to stay in union square, but having arrived and walked around for a day fishermans wharf was definately the best location for us.
reasonably priced especially as the weekend we visited was the --TH anniversary fo the golden gate bridge which we did not know until we arrived.
Hotel was impeccably presented, staff very welcoming and attentive.
rooms were clean and tidy, no view from the room, but for the time we spent in there this was not a problem
The wine hour evening is a great idea, as this brought many guests down into the lobby-lounge area of a night time to sample free wine, and meet other guests and swap stories and best places to visit in san fran.
Location is fantastic as - minute walk from tram stop, although local tip was to walk up the hill from the main stop and by law the tram's have to leave spaces on each tram to pick up walking passengers. rather than queue -- minutes + at the main end stations, walk to next stop and you will probably get on the -st or -nd tram to go past.
Also very close to the main piers, and streets are littered with restaurants and bars for you to frequent.
every meal we ate was of good quality, and the clam chowder in sourdour bread is a must.
visit the bakery on the main street, and watch them making bread, and the bakers will talk to you through their microphone through the window. Outsourcing is a way of life for vacationers. Despite the brouhaha regarding the export of American jobs, most of us have come to accept it as a generally seamless way of trip planning. But my recent experience of making a simple change to hotel reservations demonstrates the old adage about sausage making: you don’t want to see what goes on behind the scenes. The following is completely true, except I’ll use only first name initials. 
My brother is preparing to get married in Memphis. His wedding planner funneled guests to the Hampton Inn Memphis (Shady Grove) for reservations. The rate and location were great. So great, in fact, that about a month after I originally booked my stay there, I decided to celebrate my own anniversary in Memphis and arrive a couple of days early and stay at the same hotel.
That’s when the seamlessness of outsourcing began to unravel. I called the Hampton Inn where we’ll be staying. T picked up and politely told me she was switching me over to reservations desk. I soon learned that the “desk” was in the Philippines, where E answered. E extended my stay two days as I wanted, but only after putting me on hold twice for a total of over -- minutes (my phone records bear this out). The only problem was that, in the process, he bumped my entire rate up about $-- per night.
Why the increased rate? E attributed the mistake to someone else whose name he eagerly volunteered: M. M is in Dallas, but E could not contact M again, due “system limitations,” so he did the next best thing. He transferred me to B, whom he said was in Memphis. B’s is the only name I’m suspect about, because I was told that no one at the Memphis hotel goes by the name of B.
 Who told me that? L. L is a housekeeper at the hotel, and she picked up the telephone “in order to help out the front desk” she informed. Ours was actually a pleasant conversation. L is a good listener, and sympathized with me after realizing that I had been on the telephone holding for -- minutes. But L could only put me in contact with someone else. T.
Remember her? T was the first person I had spoken with, over half an hour ago. T assured me of one thing. She was busy booking a large group and couldn’t speak with me. But, strangely enough, she breathlessly offered to put me in contact the staff person in charge of weddings. Fearing the advent of another trip through the maze, I fortunately remembered the name of an onsite manager, M. I asked for him.
To say M was pleasantly efficient is an understatement. He made excuses for being overworked. He did not claim that the mix-up in my rates was due to anyone in the Philippines, Dallas…or even at the Memphis hotel’s front desk. He made the booking change, locked me in at the original rate, and wished me a great day and safe arrival. In essence, M brought about a new concept that I’ll call “inn sourcing”. Just as my hour long globetrotting call made a ---˚ return to the front desk, perhaps the “seamless” outsourcing concept should be rethought. M was the best argument of “Inn Sourcing” I had seen in a long time. © ---------- D.

A really great hotel in a convenient location in downtown Columbus.

This hotel is such a gem in Philly. It is quaint and boutique but very high class and well maintained. The staff is warm and courteous. Great location as well.

This was my fourth or fifth stay at the Warwick. The staff are always friendly and professional. The location is close to the subway and major midtown sites. We were visiting Houston for a friends wedding and wanted to avoid the large, characterless hotels of downtown. The look of the place may be very cool and artsy, but the welcome and service is homely and personal. If you’re hung up on crisp “turn down” service, folded toilet paper and formal dining of a morning, then give this one a miss. If however you want to feel like you’re staying with a friend who happens to be a very good host, look no further, you won’t be disappointed.

The location of the hotel on Bush Street was very convenient, the cable car stop was only a couple of blocks away, and there were several nice restaurants in the area, especially our favourite Cheesecake Factory in Macy’s at Union Square!
It seemed pretty safe walking back to the hotel at night. We hired a car from O’Farrell Street which was a convenient place about a - minute walk downhill from the hotel.
We would highly recommend this hotel as location was great, with no minus points other than the view from the bedroom.

I was visiting one of my Navy sons who was deploying soon and ended up extending my stay in San Diego due to bad weather on the east coast. Our room was upgraded to a double queen suite which was huge and very comfortable. Our view was overlooking the bay which was nice and offered a walking-running path along the water. Staff was awesome, the restaurant was very good and exercise room adequate for my needs. Shelter Island is a wonderful off the beaten track kind of place to stay and my son and I loved it. I will tell you though that you are right across the bay from North Island Naval Air Station (where my sons are stationed) and I happened to be there a week before my sons ship was deploying so there were lots of preparations being made for that. Which meant an awesome view of several Naval ships passing through the causeway there across the hotel. Great view of all the ships! There were sounds of helicopters for several days and for most of the day. I am used to it as you can here jets and helicopters around most of San Diego, but Shelter Island faces the runways and such on the base so you heard them constantly except not at night while sleeping. Just a not in case someone would be disturbed by all the activity. It was just an all around nice experience and I would definitely come back to stay!

On the more negative side, and the most important, is that our air conditioning kicked off daily. We would wake up in the middle of the night to ----- degree temps in the room! Every morning I would tromp down to the front desk to report it, receive an apology, and be told that it would be fixed. While out for the day, we were happy to return in the late afternoon to find the AC back on. But then in the night, it would kick off again. Next day, repeat the previous day, and then the same result. The problem was that the sun would pour through the window (yea for nice sunny days) but with no AC, it would heat up so badly. One day (Friday) it was -- in the room when we got back. All this to find out when I was checking out Saturday morning, when the Front Desk Manager asked me how the stay was (and I told her about the continuing AC problem), that we could have fixed the problem ourselves had we only removed the room key card from the little sleeve by the bathroom that controls the power in the room. According to her, that would have re-set the thermostat, and allowed the AC to kick back in. Who knew?? No one had told us that previously. Now, I cannot vouch for whether or not that approach actually would have worked, since I learned this upon checking out. So, if YOU experience the same problem, you might try it!
Other things -- there are no ice machines in the hotel. You have to call to have ice sent up (so you are actually paying for ice via gratuity for the room service). The restaurant is indeed not connected to the hotel. Great view, but mediocre food, at best. It is a Kosher restaurant with a limited menu, and none of us found any of the food to be remarkable in any way. I would not go there again.
All in all, the Bentley was a good place location-wise for us and room-quality wise (apart from the AC issue).

Booked this Hotel through Priceline, and for the money ($----night), it wasn't bad...especially for New York standards. I always use Tripadvisor before planning a trip, and had read many reviews about the Envoy Club before I booked. That said, most of the reviews about this hotel are accurate.

Except for the occasional ambulance noise (the hotel is located accross the street from NYU Medical center), the neighborhood is extremely quiet and safe.
Now the bad:
The Envoy Suites Hotel isn't really a hotel at all. So basically, check-in consists of picking up your key at the front desk from someone unaffiliated with the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".
Once you get past the nice foyer, this hotel goes downhill fast. Exiting the elevator reminds one of an old college dorm, in desperate need of an overhaul. The lighting is dark and the carpeting is stained. Really a horrible first inmpression. Our suite (#---) was at the end of this dark hall, around the corner. My initial impression was that we had to leave...fast. But after a day of travelling, we were too tired to think about that option.

One of the curtain sheers was quite stained from water, and there was a glass stain on the table, but other than that, the room was pretty nice. Again, the carpet was in need of replacement. There were two safes in the closet. They were not operational, and were not bolted down...kind of odd. One of the two air-conditioners worked. I didn't bother to tell anyone because I knew from previous reviews that noone was around to help me anyway.
Given, that the weather was ---plus degrees and humid, this was a bit of a nuisance.
So for $----night in NYC, this traveller got a lot of space, in an inconvenient location, with no guest services, in accomodations equivalent to your typical roadside hotel-motel. A little rough around the edges and in need of an upgrade. Would not stay here again as some of the larger hotel chains have rooms with comparable prices in town. The difference being that at least there is someone around in case you need something.

Anticipation builds for french toast, or pancakes or eggs benedict, but after a while - and then a bit more of a while - is nudged out of the way by curioisity. Is there actually anybody behind the serving hatch? Is this some kind of elaborate hoax? Exploration around the back of the kitchen area reaveals a locked door and some banging. What is going on in there? Is it human? Smurf? Womble? No-one ever finds out, because food appears - eventually - served at your table with the same friendly smile that is shared by all the staff. I didn't know what to expect in terms of room size after booking the W based on the reviews found here. We were a couple staying for - nights and received a Queen bed cozy room. There was plenty of room to place luggage, use the work desk, the bathroom, closet space, and most of all sleep.
Here are the other amenities:
Bathroom:
Fairly large and deep pedestal sink, rainfall type showerhead with adjustable water flow control. Fairly long shelf to hold toiletries for - people. Plenty of towels for - people as well. Spare roll of toilet paper in the closet.Hair dryer can be found hung in a bag. Bathroom door slides rather than swings. Door is kept closed when the magnetic strip touches the door frame. If the door does not touch the frame completely, expect the door to slide back open.
Closet:
Plenty of hangars for two people. Closet rod lights up whenever the closet door is open. Plenty of floor space for shoes.
Mini Bar & Snack Bar:
They managed to squeeze in a mini bar and snack bar. Underneath are a few drawers for storage with the bottommost drawer reserved for the in-room safe, which was very easy to use and roomy enough to store a laptop.
Work desk:
Fairly roomy work desk with some complimentary reading materials. Behind it on the wall are - available electrical outlets, which I used to charge my electronics.
Bed:
Queen bed was quite comfortable. Headboard lights up if you trigger the correct switch.
Night stand:
On the nightstand is a Tivoli brand radio with superb sound. There is also an iPod dock which should charge your iPod (I didn't test it though).
TV:
Flat screen TV is mounted on a pole in front of the bed. There is also a stand that has a DVD player. Check out is also possible through the TV. About -- TV channels available.
Climate control:
Thermostat controlled room which may trigger the air conditioner which can be noisy during the night. Thankfully it only goes on for periods at a time while sleeping.
Exterior noise:
We got a room by --th street on the --th floor where street noise could still be heard but then again, this is Manhattan.
Complimentary car service:
The hotel offers complimentary one-way rides from the W to the destination of your choice within Manhattan but reservations are required. Came in handy as we were in town for a wedding, which allowed us to get transportation straight to the church.
Complimentary beverage:
If there is wait by the check-in, you will most likely get a bottle of water, which was appreciated. Also toward the elevators, there is a large water dispenser filled with ice and sliced citrus for additional thirst quenching. 
Wi-Fi:
Wi-fi on the street level and -nd floor is complimentary. There is a charge for using it in-room. Also, in-room wi-fi is available both wired and wireless.
Elevators:
There are - that go to the rooms. They are small (about - people can ride at a time). Be sure to have your room key to access your floor.
All in all, the W was a worthwhile stay if you don't mind occasional street noise. Room size was not a problem for me.

This is a pretty fancy hotel right in downtown San Francisco. The rooms are pretty small, but beautifully done in a the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""moderne"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" minimalist style. The flat screet TVs are a waste since they only have analog low res quality and only a handful of channels. Internet is not free, not even in the business center. No coffee maker or fridge. Good location right on the edge of Chinatown and close to everything.

This hotel has received great reviews in the past. I don't have any complaints about the room, breakfast and location. If you have business related to SDSU I highly recommend this hotel. It is clean, quiet and the breakfast offerings get you off to a great start ... but had I known I would not have internet access in my room for - days I would have booked elsewhere. After - days of being told the problem was being fixed (but wasn't) I highly recommend that if internet access is important to your stay, check first that the wi fi problem has been permanently fixed.

I'm a marriott snob (last year, I stayed over --- nights in marriott hotels) and am pairing down my travel considerably. Consequently, I'm even more picky about my hotel choices. I really like the Stanford Court, from the great fitness center to the classic style that comes out in little touches in the rooms. I loved everything about this experience. Didn't eat at the restaurants, so can't comment on that, but used the gym and pool, which were great. Staff were very friendly and accommodating and the room was large with a very comfortable bed. Location was good, but it is a steep climb from the waterfront.
had a beautiful corner room with a view of the park, staff was helpful and attentive

I stayed at the Orchard hotel with my wife and I can recommend it to anyone both for the size and style of the rooms and also the location close to the shopping on union square right next to the hotel is a stop for street car

Staying at a hotel in New York is always an adventure and even more so when you are trying to do it without breaking the bank.
The La Quinta Inn in Manhattan was both an adventure and a huge bargain for the city at the same time.
For convenience the hotel is hard to beat as it sits right in the heart of Koreatown and is only - blocks away from Penn Station and - block from the Empire State building.
The staff was friendly enough but not very helpful. I originally booked a room on the hotel web site Applecore and received a rate of $--- per night which isn't bad for NYC. However when I checked the LQ.com site at the behest of my wife the same room was available for $--- which is a screaming buy in my opinion. 
I was very disappointed to learn though that the only rooms available were smoking rooms (I didn't know those still existed) and that the only thing the hotel could do was spray it. The spray lasted about -- minutes then it smelled like smoke again. My wife bought a can of Febreeze which she used liberally in an effort t fend off the stink.
Despite knowing that I wanted a non-smoking room the hotel did nothing to help find a non-smoking room the next day.
By New York standards the room was small and even though there was free wi-fi there was no desk or table to work from so I used my lap or went to the lobby to find more space.
Despite the flaws I would stay here again based on location and price but if you find a similarly priced hotel in Manhattan, take it and avoid this one. I know I will.

Being an SPG Platinum member I naturally gravitated to this hotel a short distance from IAH. I arrived and was checked into a room the first had no AC I was moved to another but this room was like the other only with AC but had a moldy smell and definatly did not look the the new Sheraton branding inspite of their multi million renovation . You waited forever for the elevator, the restaurant food was of poor quality best to pass on by this hotel to the brand new hotel a mile away.

nice spacious room. Hotel seemed to be quite new. Friendly service. Breakfast nothing out of the ordinary but ok. Stayed here for - nights in a business trip. Nothing wrong with the room at all, would stay again for sure.Only thing that bothered me was that the noice from the freeway. So bring earplugs or ask for a room on the backside.

I stayed for - days there and it was very pleasant. I walked everyday to Times Square and Broadway, which is about ----- mins. Room was small and clean, but the bedskirt was ripped. Continental Breakfast was pretty good. This Hotel is really good for the people who are in NYC for sightseeing and spend most of the time outside their room.
Hotel has a security service which charges $- per bag to hold.

The hotel staff was accommodating for the duration of my stay. The facility was clean and fresh. The food was prepared fresh daily. The attitudes of the staff were pleasant. They made a smooth transition from one general manager to the next. The service did not suffer during the transition.

We had the pleasure of staying at the Fort Worth Hilton while attending an event at the Fort Worth Conference Center , just one short block away. We found this to be a beautiful, historic hotel, elegant and well maintained and was a real value with our """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""convention special rate"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Our room was spacious, very well decorated, the bed was perfect, the linens were luxurious. My only disappointment was that there was not a refrigerator in the room and the windows did not open for fresh air. But the very quiet fan and precision temperature control kept us very comforatable. The best thing about this hotel is the staff, the desk staff was fabulous and quickly attended to our every request and whim. The waiters at the resturant, were the best we have every had, anywhere, friendly Darryl, Napoeleon and Omed were the picture of professionalism, courtesy and elegance and also always made us smile. The only disappointment with the staff came with the valet parking guys, they brought our car around promptly but changed the time on my clock, twice, and cranked the radio up. All and all though, this was one of the our very best hotel stays ever, we highly recommend this place. JFK stayed here the last night of his life, there is a hallway full of photos of that event, very interesting.

We booked this hotel after reading recent reviews. We arrived late and I was immediately put off by the bullet-proof glass in the lobby. After a few minutes, I realized I wouldn't work there without it either. There was a party going on in the neighboring rooms and people were screaming and going from room to room slamming doors. The music was loud and they were definitely smoking something other than cigarettes. These weren't teenagers - they were all about -- years old. We had arrived after midnight after driving for a few hours but there were lots of people going from room to room. We turned the fan up to high and turned the tv on so that our son could go to sleep. i slept fully dressed so that if we needed to make a run for it, we could. The beds were nice and the sheets were clean. The tub was so gross that we put wash cloths in there to stand on. I sort of felt like I was in a old dorm that no one had cleaned.
The entire area around Hobby Airport is pretty shady. I would recommend spending a little more and staying in a higher end place. Sometimes you get lucky with a discount place - this wasn't one of them.

great experience, just in time for my birthday great opportunity to be able to stay with MGM Grand Detroit. Cleanliness was exceptional, staff was very attentive. I will recommend MGM Grand Detroit to all my friends and Family

We loved our stay. We received exceptional customer service from host(s) & other staff. The room was a little on the small size; but it was very clean and efficient and super modern. It had everything we needed in a hotel room. For Boston, it was a very good price-value.

In the business center they might try and locate the printer and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""printer control device"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" away from the p.c. so people can work on them separately.
If they had a hot tub, we'd have given it - stars.

My husband and I have stayed at the Hard Rock Hotel twice now and plan to come back at least once a year. The first time we stayed at the hotel was actually for our honeymoon in September ----. We had a gorgeous suite with great views on two sides. When we came back for my husband's birthday in February this year, we were just as impressed with the standard room we stayed in. The beds are comfortable; the rooms are inviting and relaxing. We love that the hotel is within walking distance (even in February) to just about everything we like to do while we're in town. We also love that we could stay in the hotel and never leave if we chose to! There's a great restaurant and a trendy and fun bar right in the building. 
All in all, we feel that this hotel is one of the best we've ever stayed in and we can't wait to go back!

I stayed here for a work conference and thought the hotel was very good. It is not very close to the downtown area of san diego, but there is a metro stop directly across the street from the hotel with easy access to all the San Diego attractions.

Spouse and I have stayed at this property in the past, and it is a good choice for a weekend visit to Inner Harbor area. Close enough to walk safely to aquarium, etc. Those in the know warn against wandering too far from tourist area, especially in evening. Building used to be bank-office space so public areas are interesting. Not generic. We were able to check in before noon. Nice after brief flight from JFK. 
 Room is perfectly decent. However, my body wasn't happy with the mattress. It felt fine, but lying on my side caused by hip to ache. (Age, I'm sure. Mine, not the mattress.) Also, these were a bit dingy and need some time in a bleach solution to whiten them up. 
Water was hot. Drains run fine. Plumbing is reasonably quiet. One new feature is the replacement of those tiny amenity containers of shampoo, etc., with gym club-spa dispensers on the wall. Much better. I solved that problem by squirting some product into a paper cup.
Room had flat screen television set, microwave, and fridge. Fridge is especially nice as it was really hot, and hotel has all-day coffee and tea. Nice to make iced coffee in room. All in all, decent. Visitors should be aware that parking is at a premium in Inner Harbor area. This property seems to be all valet. Pricey. Other, near-by hotels charge as much as $-- for self park, $-- for valet. These are NYC prices!

I stayed at this hotel with my family for the weekend in three rooms. Everything was perfect. I travel a lot and find it especially hard to find clean, quiet comfortable rooms in big cities. This hotel stay was seamless. The hotel staff even returned an item to my mother that she left in her room by accident along with a thoughtful letter. It's minutes from all the museums and galleries and many fine restaurants and shopping nearby, a great location. I will stay at this hotel every time I visit Houston from now on. They also offer senior discounts which my parents took advantage of. For comparably priced hotels in the area, this is by far the best one I've found. Definitely a good deal, great for business travelers.

We were in the first --- to buy into West --th and achieved remarkable value for money. A nice place to stay - in fact I'm off there again in the morning!

My husband and I had an unexpected -- hour layover in Seattle on our way to Cambodia. As my husband had never been to Seattle, we picked the Four Seasons for its proxemity to the waterfront and Pike's Market. The rooms were beautiful. Just like all Four Seasons stays, this one was fantastic. The only negative could happen anywhere...I left my jewelry pouch on the made bed. It had several irreplaceable items int it. I called within -- minutes of checking out but they didn't have any of their staff members report it.

Had a wonderful weekend at the Madison. The staff were approachable and friendly and appeared to show a lot of pride in their work. The hotel decor was beautiful; was told by one of the staff members that the hotel was recently renovated. The room we had was amazing! I wish we had a microwave and dvd player though. 
I definitely would recommend this hotel to others, and am looking forward to going back to the Madison in the future.

A friend and I stayed here on the nights of -------, ------- and -------. We each had a room and were very comfortable throughout our stay. The rooms were clean and the beds comfortable. We had free parking for our entire stay. The people in the front office are very helpful and the office is open -- hours. You can walk to Fisherman's Wharf from the motel. We discovered that you can travel anywhere in S.F. using public transport. We caught buses near the motel that connected with other buses or cable cars and we were spared the worry of driving in this busy city. The Hop On - Hop Off bus tours are a great way to get around the points of interest.

We stayed here for the second time this year. We belong to the Starwood Club so we stay for free because of our points. Last time, we got a normal room and it was fine. This time, I asked for a free upgrade and we got an AWESOME room on the --th floor with a view of the Golden Gate & Bay Bridges. Our room had a hall way and was very large. I can't say enough how great the Hotel Palomar is in Philadelphia. Ihave stayed at this hotel many times because you just could not ask for a better hotel experience. This was my second stay at the hotel. This time I came for a get-a-way weekend with my wife to celebrate our anniversary. The location was great and the room was excellent. Check in was quick and flawless. The front desk confirmed all of our dinner reservations booked via concierge (reservations were for both in and outside of the hotel). She was a little upset that they were not in the room upon arrival as she had requested and confirmed. 
The room was very comfortable. The bed was incredible - wxtremely comfortable!!! There was plenty of closet space and a large, well appointed bathroom. The room was service was excellent. Finally, the staff treated us like movie stars. Everyone remembered our names and always asked how our dinner reservations turned out the previous evening. We truly enjoyed our stay and would highly recommend the hotel to couples.

This place is in a convenient location. Near the art museum, state capitol and - blks to the --th st. mall. The staff was polite and helpful. I got a private room for about $---night. It had a basic bed, TV and sink in the room. There is no A-C in the building.

Be sure to ask for a no-smoking room.

The weather sucked during our visit, too, but we took advantage of the Inn's location adjacent to Balboa Park and hiked a four-mile loop that took us through the park and across Cabrillo Bridge. Very nice. This off-the-beaten-track B&B offers travelers the variety of themed rooms and an escape from the mundane SoCal experience. We are pretty conservative and liked it lots. If you're looking for a high-end breakfast, try the Coronado.

The rooms were as expected clean and neat, the sheets, pillowcases, towels, etc. were all the way they should be,,,,,,,very clean and comfortable. The pool area and the rest of the grounds were clean and manicured and maintained daily.
The complimentary breakfast was a delight and the coffee was on all the time.
What else can we say,,,,,,,WE WILL BE BACK!!!!!!

Thought the hotel was very stylish and very pricey, but wished I stayed for the entire weekend. Has a beautiful pool area, complete with a covered outdoor lounge and cabanas. I knew this was high end elegance, but the staff could loosen up, it won't disappoint the clients I promise. Overall, it was very expensive, but probably not to the type of guests they cater too. I stayed in this hotel for a week and was really pleased. Sure, the hotel could do with a lick of paint and new carpets but the rooms and bathrooms were clean and very comfortable. Only tip, avoid checking in during peak hours - i arrived at -pm and sailed through but did notice the queue could get quite long. However this only seemed to be when a huge coach trip had arrived which any hotel would struggle with.

On January -th ---- me and - of my buddies checked into Marriott Los Angeles property for the night. On first arrival everything seemed great, warm receptive employees, beautiful décor, clean atmosphere, everything I look for when checking into a new property. The check in process went rather fast, considering there was not much traffic in the lobby when we arrived. The hotel room was average, nothing to complain about. As me and my friends got settled in the room we realized how hungry we were from the long trip. We called room service to hope to fulfill our hunger, but instead had another coming. At -- p.m. on a Saturday night all room service had to offer us was a cold cut turkey sandwich. Not being in vegas we could not travel anywhere that was -- hours , so we decided to try the sandwich out. The mistake that we made was assuming that the $--.-- turkey sandwich would be enough for - of us to split, that was wrong. This average sandwich did nothing to our appetite except frustrate it. The next day when it came time to check out is where I had the real issue with the Marriott property. After checking out, I walked to valet to get my car, and that is where I was told that I owed $-- for my overnight valet service. I was shocked by this amount considering my car was only parked overnight, and most of all I was never told it cost anything to valet at Marriott. I then asked for the manager of valet, and asked him how are people are suppose to assume these costs. He replied by pointing at a small sign posted at the valet podium. I then told him that with so much traffic in the valet, the podium should be in a more visible spot, that way people are aware of the costs of valet, and have a chance to make a decision according to the cost. The manager then responded by saying “when you become a manager, you can make that decision, do you want your car or not?” I then followed by paying my $-- fee, and telling him that what could have been a descent experience, he had put a negative stamp on it. Hoping the manager would stop me on my way to my car and make a last attempt to right things, I slowly got in my car and left. Instead I got nothing more than a friendly wave from the valet podium. If up to me, that will be the last time I spend $ at a Marriott property. What a shame because I was looking forward to staying at LA Live Property, but now am to scared of what hidden fees may imply.

the san carlos hotel is wonderful. although a small hotel it has friendly staff, great rooms, very clean, comfortable beds, excellent service. the location is great too, on --th street, between lexington and -rd, it is a quiet street, so no trash cans being collected at night, just bliss in new york. although there is no restaurant the irish bar just across the road provides the best in room service and late night drinks. the rooms were spacious and warm with everything from microwave ovens to a flat screen tv. i would strongly recommend this hotel to anyone. we are definately going to return to this hotel. it has everything and more you could want. 
well done san carlos, you made our holiday great!!!!

My husband and I stayed in this hotel for one night during our recent trip to the USA. It is a very different style of hotel and although we did like it, it certaily wouldn't be everyones taste.
I would agree with previous reviews who commend the views from this hotel, they are incredible and our bedroom also faced onto the lake.

We stay at Hilton's most of the time as a Gold Hilton Member. I must say, the Hilton Union Square was not even up to the standards of the last DoubleTree we stayed at. The lobby definitely needs updating and cleaning. In our room there was mold on the ceiling in the shower, the sink handle came off in my hand and I had to screw it back on and there were black marks on our sheets. 
The peson who checked us in was very difficult to understand. He said I'm upgrading you. I asked what that meant and he said just a higher floor - so not a larger room, executive floor or anything, I asked? No, he said, just a higher floor. He proceeds to tell me It used to be the executive floor but we don't have the executive amenities anymore. I don't consider this to be much of an upgrade. Not to mention, he hands me some breakfast coupons (like they are gold) and says they are for complimentary continental breakfast. Then he tells me I have to take them to the StarBucks in the lobby for my continental breakfast which includes - drink, - pastry and some fruit. If you really want to sit and eat after getting your items, you have to use one of the - hi-top tables in the lobby - if they are available. Or, the desk person continues to tell me, I can upgrade by returning these coupons and paying $-- more every morning and eat in the Hilton restaurant. This is ridiculous!!!
Hopefully, the hotel manager will read this and make amends. One can hope!!

Normally I'd start with a big description of the hotel - but this time I may as well just say it: The only thing this hotel has going for it is its location right next door to Boston Children's Hospital. Other than that, there's nothing appealing about this place.
Check in was easy and pleasant but the reception area is unattractive simply because it has no windows. The hotel itself is attached to a shopping center food court and so many of the windows are situated over the food court rather than being external which makes for a gloomy room. Traveling for an appointment with the hospital, we were given a very decent sized room, but we were so tired all we wanted was to eat and sleep so I didn't notice the specifics of the room until later.
The hotel has a restaurant attached to it - between it and the food court - but the food is lousy and very much overpriced and the service was spotty without even a smile. How far wrong can you go with a burger and fries? (Pretty far, as I found out)! A far better option for eating is inside the hospital in one of their restaurants or going to somewhere else - lots of places in the vicinity.
Back up to the room and we soon realized it was an interconnecting room with paper thin walls. That was with thanks to the people in the next room. They weren't talking loudly but any talk was coming straight through the door-wall as though they were with us! We decided to have a hot bath and to bed. Well, we would have had a bath had there been a bath plug. It took a call to reception before a very grumpy member of housekeeping came and more or less shoved a bath plug at me. I got into the bath to see caulking that was years' out-of-date, grubby and moldy. There were long dark hairs on the bathroom floor (not ours) and other less mentionable hairs also. Again, not ours. No waste bin in the bathroom and it was generally a bit dingy with aging towels, the bare minimum of toiletries, etc.
Back out to the room and I am reading in bed. I look up and notice that something had been thrown (or spilt) onto the wallpaper to the left of me. A very large spill which looked a bit sticky. The piping for the room heating and sprinklers were actually in the room and exposed and covered in dust and dirt. They came down from the ceiling. I have asthma and was having a good old sneeze by the time I'd been in there an hour.
Now I could say it was really awful, but it wasn't. It was just a room that had seen a lot of action and had never been updated. I'm giving it three stars because the reception staff were really pleasant, the bed was comfortable and because of the location BUT if you are staying at the hotel with a sick child who has immune system issues - this won't be the place for you. This hotel desperately needs an upgrade in every department. Until then, I fear the reviews will continue to be poor. Why? It advertises itself as a Best Western """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Plus"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Unfortunately the few regular Best Western's I have been to have far better facilities.
Tip: If you are staying there because of a hospital matter, you can get the hospital rate at the hotel, but you will need to take proof of your hospital appointment for their records. If you have a car - do not park at the hotel which is expensive and time restricted. Have it valet parked at the hospital. The hospital desk will stamp your parking receipt and the parking is infinitely cheaper. Another plus is that they will bring your car down to you if you need to store luggage and will return it to its car park spot at no extra charge. They call this an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""down and up"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The hospital parking is a ---- facility and the valet aspect (which was minimal in cost) was a real bonus and was used by all those families that I could see who had children with mobility issues or wheelchair requirements.

I'm never disappointed in the physical appearance and stayability of a Ritz property, but what brings me back over and over is the consistency of the service. I almost never leave a Ritz without at least one """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""WOW"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" experience. Unfortunately, I never really got close to that at this property. 
Employees routinely called me by my first name, when they knew or remembered my name at all. The reservations were a challenge and much of my party did not get assigned proper rooms confirmed in the reservation. One of our party had someone's luggage in his room on the -rd day of our stay. (I bet the people who were without their luggage were especially disappointed). 
Club reservations generally insure a private, prepared check-in, but not at this property. And club only guarantees you access, NOT CLUB LEVEL. I was on the -th floor and the club was on -. The bell staff was totally uninspired and didn't even attempt to help when they saw members of our party wheeling luggage. If they happened to be near a door they opened it. No eye contact, no """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""welcome home"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The cigarette disposal's were overflowing and dirty out front. 
After one day in our meeting room, we were alerted that there was a security issue with another party that was government related holding a meeting. I am very impressed that an entire hotel is all two room suites. It's rare that u get this much room to spread out, relax and enjoy a hotel. The room was spotless. The front desk service was perfect. Just finished stay for - days and had a very good experience - David Horowitz, general manager, was very helpful in helping to arrange our rooms as we were traveling with - young children. We stayed at the Sorrento in Seattle for our -th wedding anniversary and wow what an amazing two nights. Talk about rolling out the red carpet, I could not have felt anymore pampered by a hotel. Such a beatiful accomodation. Wish we could have stayed a week! Can't wait to stay at the Sorrento again.

We stayed here on a weekend trip to D.C. and the hotel was wonderful. The desk staff and restaurant wait staff were very kind and helpful. Washington seems a bit like Canberra. All neat on the surface but with a lot of other personalities underneath.The Monticello presents a perfect glimpse into the historic side of Washington and is a lovely and charming place to stay. It is located in Georgetown so there are plenty of places to shop and eat including the waterfront at the end of the street. Our room was beautiful and very quiet, the staff are helpful and friendly and the Thai crab cakes down the road were worth going to Washington for. The Monticello is a definite step up from the many souless hotels on offer here.

Stayed here with a friend - nights. Second time (stayed for - nights with my son last summer) and got an excellent room rate I would think because of the work going on in the hotel and construction in nearby street. Location is perfect, being two minute walk to Broadway and -th and right by Macys and other well known stores. Subway to other areas is right on the street corner. Easy walking distance to Rockerfeller Centre, Empire State and other downtown locations. Good eating places around the corner, Pax for excellent sandwiches and fresh salads and it's handy having a fridge in the room to store snacks and drinks. Duane Reade drug store on the corner of the street too.
As previously, staff were friendly and very helpful but I imagine it's how you treat them if you have a bad experience! Received a much appreciated and unexpected room upgrade. 
Breakfast is good but if you're looking for full service then this isn't for you. It's help yourself but a good selection of muffins, pastries, bagels, bread for toast, cream cheese and jams, yoghurt, and always a fresh fruit salad and bowl of fruit. Plenty of fresh tea and coffee and juices. Never had a problem finding anywhere to sit! 
Business centre has free access and good internet speed. Paper provided for printing off your boarding card or other documentation where other hotels charge for internet and printing. 
All in all you can't go wrong. The hotel is clean and the maid service excellent with clean towels daily. Most bathrooms in Manhattan hotels are small by the way! Plenty of hot water and good water pressure in the shower.
Highly recommended by a fussy traveller!

I stayed here for - nights and it was perfect for me. Very central, modern, clean and helpful staff. Andre at registration was especially helpful - I asked for a room with a view and I certainly got one! --th floor corner room was fabulous. Only small criticism was that it was a bit noisy (from outside) but that is hard to avoid in such a busy, convenient downtown location. Definitely recommended!

Very big and spacious rooms...clean...near to Premium Outlet Malls and food outlets around...good breakfast spread...free wifi...good saundry stall...cheap last min toliteries...laundry room is fantastic...

The value of staying here with free breakfast and happy hour may outweigh the issues of the crowds and lines waiting for your food and drink and elevator. The staff was extremely friendly and welcoming. My only complaint would be more comfortable chairs or cushions at the pool.

My family and I went for a weekend getaway to Boston for the long weekend in May. It was our first time staying at this hotel. The best feature I have to say is the freindly and welcoming staff. Just got back from NY - stayed - nights at the Beekman Tower Hotel. No real problems at all. The rooms are basic but clean with a handy kitchen area. We had - chaps in one room and requested an extra bed which was provided. I was pleasantly surprised that you can stay in a nice hotel in this price range right in the center of SF. My room was small but adequate, the view from the window quite breathtaking, the breakfast was fine. All in all, a good place to stay for a budget-mindful tourist.

between our group we had - rooms. Were charged a LOT for the rooms because it was formula - weekend. I was skeptical because of previous reviews, but the price was right and it was in the city, close to where I needed to be. It was perfect for my needs, and I was pleasantly surprised. A simple continental breakfast is offered with fresh pastries, cereal, fruit, coffee, etc. My son is in school in DC and this will be my first choice for hotels when I return. The only hassle is parking is limited to on-street so you nmay have to cruise around for a spot. I had no problem finding a space though. Thumbs up from me.

I have stayed at Motel Capri a number of times over the past - years. During that time it seems to have changed ownership once or twice. Very Comfortable! Excellent quality! This hotel is almost like being at home. Very Comfortable Rooms! I almost never sleep well in a hotel the first night. I slept great!
Very Quiet even though my room overlooked the street. The staff is very friendly and they know the area! The complimentary breakfast is very high quality.

We really enjoyed our stay and the cleanliness of the hotel. The staff was wonderful and a special kudos to Jill Rudnicki as she was pleasant and polite from check-in to the happy hour that she hosted.

Very good location, since we were just down the street from the Intrepid Sea-Air-Space Museum and the CircleLine cruise docks. It was a pleasant walk to Times Square (- blocks east) & Rockefeller Center (about - blocks northeast). Less than half an hour walk to Empire State Building.
