Don't be afraid to stay here, its a great hotel to stay in.
Use priceline if you can to get the lowest rate and you will get a fantastic room for your price with free continental breakfast and free hot cookies after -pm. Only -- odd minutes from downtown by bus.

The room is very large and the beds are a little firm but not uncomfortable. The bathroom is very nice and there is coffee or tea that you can make in there as well. The shower is clean and very consistent in temperature. However the walls can be a little thin in the bathroom so you can hear the shower next door a little or the water draining from upstairs if your in the bed next to the bathroom. Room is cleaned daily in the later half of the morning.
Maintance issues are dealt with as soon as possible.

There was a small convention with Asians being held in the hotels conference room but that was about all we noticed different about the place.
Heres the great part of this hotel, desk staff bake fresh cookies after -pm and they are free for you to take on your way up to the room or while you relax in the lobby. Breakfast is huge, with fresh baked cinnamon rolls along with the usual continental breakfast.
Fresh coffee along with fresh juice and skim and -% milk for cereal or whatever. Theres bagels and bread and cereal in containers. Eat as much as you want and watch big screen morning television in the dinning room.

If you need to ride the bus they will make change for you.
The bus stop is a few minutes walk to the north. Buses run in and out of downtown into the late night.
Across the street and within a few minutes walking distance are a few restaurants ( Las Margaritas, a family chain of sit down mexican food and Taco Time a northwest chain of fast food mexican). If you go north into Shoreline on the bus a few stops you can find a McDonald's and Taco Bell as well as sit down restaurant for dinner and a smaller dinner called Shays which serves a big breakfast for a affordable price.
Safeway (---th and Aurora) is also in this area as is a Walgreen's on the corner of ---th and Aurora.
Just about everything you need for a short stay is in this neighborhood. Plenty of pizza places will deliver as well.
Check the front desk binder for restaurants that will deliver or that you can go to. Price varies from affordable to fancy. All are recommended by the various hotel mangers and staff.
Overall a nice place to stay and I would stay there again if priceline gave it to me.
Sorry no photos, but it's no different than the candids or the hotel photos.

On the whole, definitely a hotel to recommend.

I slept one night in this hotel, guy at the lobby was very nice, but few things were bad. First, i waited -- min for the shuttle at the airport, it's very long. Second, my room smells urine. But i slept well. 
I will never go back, i prefere pay a little bit more and have a clean bedroom.

We stayed at the Bowery to take in a little dining and shopping in the city before heading upstate for Lake Placid.
Found the Bowery online and was intrigued by the design and concept… simple design with an old British touch. As an architect, I was looking forward to see the rooms and overall design in practice. The lounge is cozy and comfortable, the bar new and stylish. We had some house specialty drinks and little snacks. Well blended and composed. As I recall, all was suggested by staff… 
Very pleased with the experience and will definitely return here.

Stayed at this hotel for business. It is close to the riverwalk and within walking distance of a lot of attractions. But the hotel is older and the rooms are small. Let's start with the bathroom - very tiny and it would be hard for a larger person to get in. The room was clean but it needs a lot of TLC, like newer carpet. The bed was nice and comfortable. The hotel smelled older too.
It's a very quiet hotel and no one was eating at the restaurant or lounging in the lobby. And they charge you for Internet access as well. The hotel has a bakery, which was nice. The breakfast buffet was good and had an omelette station. The staff was very nice at check-in. I would stay here again.

Stay a night before flight to Maui and also on the way back at the San Jose Airport hotel. 
Excellent choice for late or early flights. Hotel location is ideal except there are little choice for resturants after -.--pm at that area except for some pubs. Shuttle service is good to and from airport. 
Parking for stopover is great for a week. 
Upgraded room provided - large room for - adults.
Rooms cleanliness - average. Carpet seems much older. 
Overall, for a short stay is alright but no showstopper.

From Check in to check out and everything in between this hotel was number -! We travelled around the states for - weeks and stayed in - --- star hotels (some much more expensive than the Sofitel) and this was by far the best. The staff are the most friendly and professional I have come across in all my travels. The gym is great with all the equipment you need and in excellent condition. The location is perfect, a short walk to some major attractions. Will recommend this hotel to anyone heading to DC for either work or leisure.

We had a company Christmas party at this beautiful & historic hotel. We were offered a awesome rate to stay overnight, and we thought, hey why not. A chance to stay at the wonderful Adolphus. I could certainly tell they had crammed a lot of events into this hotel for one evening. People in every nook and cranny. Our room was very large. It had a couch, arm chair, coffee tables, desk and chair, king size bed. The view from the -th floor onto Main Street was decent. Downtown has become alive again after many years of nothing to do down there. We enjoyed watching people from our birds eye view. The bathroom was plenty big. The TV was kind of tiny, but we were not there to watch TV. We retired early, around --PM, and that's where the evening went downhill. The guests across the hall from us had evidently booked their room for a party. It started around --:--. People coming and going and loud music and noise. People banging on the metal door to gain entrance to the hoopla, metal door slamming shut very loudly, over and over and over again. Around midnight i could not stand it any longer so I called the front desk. No answer, no connection, out of order signals. I called every extension I could find on the phone, nothing worked. I stuffed some pillows up against the door. Turned the air to run constantly on the heater (which was actually pretty loud) it helped to drown out most of the noise. Be sure and check your CC the next few days after your stay. I was charged for the over priced minibar that I absolutely did not touch. I was told they would adjust this error. I realize that it is not the hotels fault for the inconsiderate guests across from our room, but I am more concerned that the phone systems was not working. What if we had a emergency ? Oh well and never again.

I love this hotel. It is one of the best that I have stayed in. The lobby was beautiful and the room was nice and comfortable. The made services was terrific. No matter what time we left the room it was made up when we came back. I asked the maid for a couple of extras and she was very nice and friendly. That is what I liked about the hotel the staff was so nice and friendly. I was there with my daughter for a girl's weekend from Thursday - Sunday. Everyone from the doorman to the concierge to the people at the desk etc. was wonderful. I can't say enough good about this hotel. Yes the bathroom was small, but I wasn't moving into the room. I was just staying there a few days and was hardly in the room anyway. I will definitely stay there again

It is a decent place. The location, in the theatre district is great and it is very close to just about all of city and state government. 
The hotel is fine but don't expect a typical Marriott courtyard this is much more like an older, classic downtown hotel.

We enjoy staying at the Marriott Airport in Phoenix once a year for the last five years. The last time we were there in April -- we learned to ask for a room on the opposite side of the hotel from the highway. Our room faced the highway and the airport in the distance. The traffic noise was loud and constant all night long. I have a hearing handicap and the noise was still enough to keep this otherwise sound sleeper tossing and turning. We'll stay there again but only on the other side of the building away from the noise of the highway. The staff, cleanliness, parking, and location are all excellent. Skip the restaurant for dinner. The menu is nice but the food was overdone. The restaurant is clean and has great service staff but the food preparation is not Marriott standard. Property

While I have no doubt that the Hudson passes its fire inspections, I would dread being in this place were a fire to occur. Poorly lit hallways, with drab and dreary colors on the walls and floors brought to mind soviet-era hotels.
The room was what used to be referred to as a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""box room""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""; it was barely big enough for a futon type bed, and a TV. The floors and walls were wood-panneled, the windows thin, and one wall had a mirror to give the impression the room was larger than it was. 
In fact, impression is the theme here. Clearly aimed at impressionable younger tourists who mistake trendiness for comfort, most of the fixtures seemed to come from designers who believe that changing traditional designs is an end in itself. Instead of understanding that there is a reason why fixtures with traditional designs survive, due to their utilitarianism, these new designers produce 'modern' items that are impractical and often flimsy. So the light switches are annoying - and, of course, inconsistent : long and narrow, some of them are intended to be pulled, others to be moved up or down. And why the ridiculous design ? Just to be different.
Similarly in the bathroom, the wash basis is the 'modern' bowl with a faucet suspended above it. Traditional washbasins evolved the way they did to prevent water splashing out on the floor when the faucet is turned on; clearly the designer doesn't understand that, or that bowls with elevated faucets are a primitive design, and so whenever you use a sink at the Hudson you risk being soaked.
The shower is an afterthought, with spray being retained by a vinyl shower curtain. The air-conditioning is right beside the head of the bed, perfectly placed to cause chills, although it is necessary to use the fan to drown out traffic noise - unfortunately, the traffic noise in the room was so loud that my silicone ear plugs were insufficient for this purpose.
The beds, the most important items of furniture in a hotel, are appalling. They are as comfortable as a box spring; I defy anyone to sleep comfortably in them. The sheets are cheap and tacky, feeling like wax paper, and the bath towels are also cheap, and in short supply.
Incidentally, you of course have to pay if you wish to use the hotel's wireless service for internet access. As for proving it gratis as compensation for a delayed check-in, the thought never occurred to the hapless check-in clerk.
In a nutshell, if you are young and more impressed with style than substance, and likely to return to your room drunk so that you could sleep through an earthquake, then this hotel is for you. If not, find somewhere else.

Anyway, after a while it seemed to stop and we were able to get back to sleep, but very odd all the same.
Great, spacious room (suite); great service; great midtown location to enjoy Christmas-time in NYC. Will definitely stay here again!

Stayed at ZaZa Houston over Labor Day weekend. We had stayed at the property several times when it was the Warwick, an historic Houston property. Where it was once an old money hotel, it's now targeting the young hipster, only not as effectively as say a W, the Standard, The Parker, Viceroy, etc.
NIce decor heavy on dark, muted tones. Photography of rock stars-models-celebs througout. Rooms have been nicely redone and bathrooms are considerably larger than their war-era predecessors in the orginal. They have also added a group of rooms around the pool, so there are plenty of balconies and cabanas to be pool-side. Bar packed with Houston's scenesters chugging $-- drinks.
However someting about it was just not right. Service was good but not great. Lobby and pool music was all wrong. Movies looping behind front desk tried way too hard (scenes from B'fast at Tiffany's and Moulin Rouge were supposed to make us feel hedonistic?). Bar had DJ and plenty of beauties but seemed off.
The one outright negative was the filthy bed shawl laid stain-up on our bed that was replaced after being inspected by housekeeping. Why not just replace it without question?

We visit Boston, quite regularly. Although, we typically stay outside the city. However, we opted to stay in Boston for my wifes birthday, which happened to fall during the Memorial Day weekend. I booked the trip through JetBlue, to include airfare and hotel. we arrived on a Thursday night and took a cab from Logan to the Nine Zero $--. When we checked in the staff were extremely pleasant and helpful. We received a quaint corner room overlooking the Commons. The room was very well appointed. In fact, we received a complimentary bottle of champagne for the birthday occasion. The hotel is within walking distance to the North end, Fanueil Hall, the Prudential, Copley Square, and ChinaTown. Also, there is a Legal Seafood closeby. There is a train access across the street, which allowed easy travel to Fenway Park for a great Saturday night game; food and drink at the Cask & Flagon and post-game at Boston Beerworks. Adjacent to the Nine Zero is the Beantown Pub, which is a great little corner pub for a cold beer and a sports highlights. 
I would highly recommend the Nine Zero. The accommodations are comfortable, clean, and well appointed. The room had a very comfortable king sized bed, large bathroom and great shower, as well as a small stereo and an LCD TV. Great location in central Boston, too.

I love this hotel, the friendly and extremely helpful staff, the quieter location, the beautiful rooms and view. Also now I can add that the restaurant Print, is also amazing! I had not previously had a chance to eat there. The food is wonderful, so fresh, they try to source local, which I love. 
Thank you to every individual at the hotel: Olga, Victor, America, Jose, Jesus.........you make my business travel almost a pleasure!

This property is only about a year old and the rooms were clean and comfortable. The restaurant in the lobby was priced right and the food is what you would expect from a bar. The breakfast buffet was $--.-- and had made to order omlettes, bacon, sausage, pancakes and french toast. The staff was friendly and although I checked in a little early my room was ready. It is very close to Fort Worth Alliance Airport. I got a great rate and it was everything was as expected from a Hilton property. I will stay again!

Andaz turns the check in process on it's head and focuses on personalized service. It starts when you pull up a the curb. A member of their staff greets you at your car, collects your bags, holds the door for you, checks you in, and then escorts you to your room and shows you how to use the various devices in the room. The room was contemporary, spacious and comfortable. Some nice touches include the free (nonalcoholic) refreshments and snacks in the room, the waterfall shower, and the complimentary happy hour(s) in the lobby. The conference center was perfect for our meeting and the staff was outstanding. Finally, it's hard to beat the location, being across the street form the NY Public Library, two blocks from Times Square, and of course, being located on -th Avenue.

This will be short sweet and simple. We recently stayed at the Omni Hotel in Austin, Texas. We were only there for one night for a football game, but our experience at the Omni will keep us comming back - even if it's just for one night. Upon arrival (we even got there two hours before check in), they already had us checked in and our key ready to go. We had a bellman waiting to take us up to our room - no wait, no hassle. The valet service downstairs was awesome - told us where to go, gave us directions, etc. We had our bed turned down with mints that night. The next day we didn't even have to check out - just leave our keys in the room. Can you imagine going to a hotel and not even have to sign in for check in?? Everything was awesome. Rooms were a decent size, but bonus was that we had robes! We loved our stay. Being a select guest member enabled us to receive two complimentary drinks and a complimentary paper in the morning delivered to the room. We will definitely be back to the Omni and hope that you will give it a chance too!

This hotel has several things going for it but they drop the ball when it comes to the details .
We stayed here for two nights at the end of October ---- to see if it would be a good choice for guests of our upcoming wedding. We stayed in a renovated room on the -th floor, which was decorated beautifully and was a comfortable size. The bed was exceptionally comfy and luxurious. The bathroom was small however, and had absolutely no shelf space so we had to pile up our toiletries on the floor by the sink. There was only one small mirror in the entire room - over the sink - which made getting dressed and ready a challenge for - people. I can't believe they didn't even bother to install a full length mirror somewhere. There was also no in-room safe, which meant I had to carry all my valuables in my handbag all weekend long.
Another disappointment was the staff - although most people at the front desk were friendly, they weren't very helpful. We called the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""concierge"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" one morning and asked for help in contacting a rental car company; we were told they couldn't help us, not even with getting a phone number. I know this isn't a - or - star hotel, but you would think they would help with a basic request like this.
Avoid Perry's - we went here for a quick bite and the food was not fresh and not even cooked all the way through. There are several other restaurants within walking distance that are much better.
I really wanted to love this hotel - the interiors are quite fashionable since the renovation, and the location can't be beat. But the nonchalant attitude of the staff and some oversights on the details tarnished our stay. Service and attention to detail are supposedly the hallmarks of boutique hotels, but they missed the mark on both counts. For the rate we paid ($--- a night) I think we got what we paid for, but I wouldnt' call this place an amazing deal.

I not only stayed at The Pearl, I threw my husband's --th Surprise Party there! Tons of friends gathered there for a swanky dinner--the meal was fantastic--and spent the evening in bliss drinking cocktails in the inner courtyard around the lit pool. The staff was so helpful in organizing the event, and even more gracious that night. We stayed at The Pearl and woke up late, drank really great coffee then rode bikes (The Pearl's !) off to explore. 
We've been back many times. Dinner and movie nights by the pool are a hoot. Great wine list and the cheese course represents the best in CA. Love the vibe here, the artwork, the shag rug in the game-reading lounge. Point Loma is a great destination and The Pearl is really a gem in a dynamite city.

I have some of the same complaints as others. The hotel is nice, staff was very friendly except for one valet person. The hotel is definitely boutique which is a different style. Our biggest complaint was $-- per night for parking and we did not have access to vehicle. Valet was rude and informed us that all - star hotels are similar and you're not allowed access to car. That is not true as we've stayed at other - star hotels in area. It was an inconvenience not being able to easily access car for items we needed. For - nights the price of the parking added up. I had requested a quiet room and received one of the rooms at the end of the hallway next to three other doors which were constantly slamming very loudly and you could hear people talking next door. This is truly upsetting when you're wanting to spend a special quiet anniversary weekend away. Would have been nice if TV was in front of bed. Housekeeping was good, but a hassle to get coffee as I was told that the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""mini-bar"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" person does that. Bed was very uncomfortable and caused back aches. Restaurant next door was superb!

The first thing you will notice arriving on this street are the ----'s Times Square seedy porn shops and accompanying ouside hustlers. The second thing you will notice is the side of the Port Authority Bus Teminal with busses lining up to get in.
Once you have made it past these eyesores and arrive to the lobby of The Staybridge you will be greeted by a modern yet sterile lobby. The front desk staff was professional and also a bit sterile.
The hotel is next to several other hotels that all look identical. They appear to have all been built at the same time under some sort of revitilization plan.
The room was very modern, clean and and the kitchen area was simply fantastic. There was no blackout curtain on the windows. If you walk around your room unclothed be aware it is very possible people in the surrounding buildings could get a free show. I hope Staybridge will correct this privacy issue.
The all glass shower is nice and the bathroom roomy. The breakfast buffet is outstanding, however some of the staff at the breakfast act aloof. Better take your breakfast up to your room to avoid the hustle and busstle of the small dining room.
If you plan on a late night out spring for a cab as it can save you from some very unpleasant ecounters.
As long as you take the necessary precautions and don't expect much pampering from the staff you will have a pleasant stay.

Stayed Jan - to Jan -. Booked through Quikbook at $----night for a - double bedded room. Arrived very early (--am) no room available and I did not expect one to be. Called around -:--pm room available (had asked for quiet room) but when we got to the hotel about -- mins later turns out they had given us a room by the elevators (the clerk indicated this might be noisey). So we waited for a different room which was available about -- mins later
I should note there was just - of us, me (more than middle aged), and my -- year old daughter. We have travelled a far bit, and this was our -rd trip to NYC in - --- years. previous stays were at the renaissance Times Square and the Michelangelo hotels. This time I wanted cheap, great location for shopping and clean.
Bell hop very pleassant and helpful. Lobby is very small and quite plain by NYC standards. I was told by bell hop that concierge had left for - month holdiay, so no concierge available.
Room was a normal size hotel room (which means big by NYC standards), and bathroom was smaller than expected and plain. Overall impressions were that hotel is dated, particularly common areas, hallways. Clearly used to be apartment units at one point (noticed doorbell buttons at each door to rooms, not working though).
I like a firm bed and it was. Pillows smallish, and definetely problems with soundproofing in areas (ie I could hear some of the bathroom noice to the room next door, could clearly hear noise from hallways, and the plumbing would make a large mooselike moaning sound at times (even in middle of night)
Elevators very very slow in morning breakfast peak hours.
The above are the negatives. However overall i would go back. The room and hotel were very clean. The maid service pleasant and accomodating. The location great (- --- blks to -th, right by subway, about - blks to park etc). The Italian restaurant was superb and so handy (reasonably priced, great fast service, very good food, including pizza, pasta and a great organic greens with beets salad). Starbucks across the street. did the breakfast which I was not a fan of but -- year old daughter loved. It was worth the $- charge each. We were not in the room more than a ccouple of hours each day ( - hr in morning maybe --- hrs at night, except to sleep and to drop off purchases). I am very particular re cleamliness and cannot fault the hotel at all on this.
If you want an upsacle NYC experience this is not it. We have stayed at the renasissance Times Square and the Michelangelo, bof of which had nicer common areas and rooms in terms of decor, but I don;t need that and for $--- - night I am very happy.
Parking was a great deal (special for the Salisbury ) at $---night, just - --- blks away.
The one thing that could have been a problem for me is the heat-. halls very very hot, and room too was too warm. But the windows open, and then it got very very cold our last - days in NYC, which cooled the room down too. I tried the A-C but it would not cool the room down enough!! Not sure what that would mean come the summer!!!!!!! so beware of that
Overall great value for the money

We spent two night at The Seaport. We loved walking to the Harpoon Brewery tour and the nearby restaurants. The hotel was convenient to the historic parts of the city and public transportation. We did have a car and my one negative comment would be that he hotel parking was mixed with the whole complex and poorly marked. We often found ourselves parked very far away from the hotel lobby. Concierge did a great job of finding us a last minute reservation on Saturday night...for a party of -. That's good service.

Stayed for a business trip but found out of a Norah Jones concert at Mud Island and the concierge got me tickets. Bar is great. Skip Beale st and go to the restaurants at Main st. for great BBQ go to Central BBQ. Great beds at the Westin. ask for a high floor, less noise.

There was a mistake in my booking made through an internet website (probably my own fault) and when I checked in my prepaid stay was for another day. The very helpful staff (especially Michelle Bennett) went of their way to ensure that the booking was transferred to that night at no additional cost to me. They were unfailingly pleasant and cooperative. As for the hotel, it's an oasis of calm and relaxation amidst the excitement of the Baltimore Inner Harbor and a great base for exploring the many attractions that the city has to offer.

We stayed only for one night at this small, intimate hotel in an excellent location in downtown Philly. I dropped off my wife and the luggage, checked-in and then had to drive around the block a few times to find an inconvenient public parking garage with reduced rate parking. The walk was more than - blocks back to the hotel in the frigid cold. 
Our corner Queen room was fairly small, but very nice, newly decorated with funky furniture, wooden blinds, nice drapery and a nice view. We had to call the front desk for soap and shampoo that had been overlooked by the maid. The platform bed was very comfortable and the room was very quiet. They allow children, but kids need to be quiet. 
I went down to the lobby, looking for the promised complimentary snacks, and was dissapointed when I found some old bagels and danish. 
The folks at the front desk were very nice and helpful. I stayed here instead of a deal at the Hyatt, but next time I might opt for a good deal at a different hotel.

What can I say that hasnt been said already.This is a basic - star hotel that is next to Graceland and full of Elvis fans.
The towels are small, the breakfast choice is not great, the rooms are a little worn and can I say so what ! If your coming to this Hotel your there for - main reason, to be close to Graceland . Yes they could do things better, the rooms could be more fancy , there could be more choice on the breakfast but this would pump the cost of the price up so it would be even more expensive for Elvis fans from around the world to make what is for many their trip of a lifetime.
Its safe, clean and has plenty of things to do for a short stay with a free shuttle to beale on an evening and other places to visit that the reception staff can help you arrange, so if you are an Elvis fan I recommend this hotel for the full expieriance and dont be put off by what I can only imagine as people who are expecting somthing a little more grand or just unlucky in their stay.
By the way new bigger towels is somthing that wouldnt cost to much money so mabey I am one of those people myself.

Thank God this was only a one night stopover before a cruise. Small cramped room overlooking an inner alley. The room was drab and tired although heaven knows how they could dress up that shoebox. The hight of the ceiling is greater than the width of the floor. Should have nailed the bed to the wall to give more room to walk around it.
I'm contacting the travel agent who put us up in there with my opinion of the place.
The only redeming feature is its location to Times Square)

The property was in a great location for the downtown area. The parking was a bit expensive but that is to be expected in this area. I had a nice check in with Andy and throughout my entire stay Jamie in guest services was amazing she truly made our stay here more enjoyable was just so helpful enough for me to write a review, which I never do. If I come back to the area I will be back. Thank you so much great service

I loved my stay at The Iroquois. It was convenient to lots of spots in New York City and the hotel staff was extremely nice and helpful. The elevator in the hotel is a little slow but we stayed on the -rd floor and took the stairs. They had the best complimentary coffee in the lobby in the morning and the best hot apple cider in the evening. We hung out in the lobby and the library sipping our apple cider in the evening. It was nice to sit and talk to other people staying at the hotel. The hotel had a very home like feel and I would definitely stay there again. New York City is an amazing place. I really wish I lived there.

The hotel is ideally located in mid-town, five minutes walk from Times Square and Broadway theatres. The rooms are clean and functional. They're small but it's adequate. I'd asked for a room off the street so it was very quiet except for the hum from the restaurant cooler on the ground floor - not enough to disturb my sleep.

We stopped here after reading the reviews and thought we would check it out. Well I have to say we did not have a good experience. We ended up getting a refund and leaving. I have recently been to a few red roofs that had been completely remodeled so I think I have become spoiled for the locations that have not been. The floor was really stained when we entered our room (which is really what turned me off right from the get go) the floors were not vacuumed, the chair was stained, and the cleaniness just wasn't there. The pool was dirty with old leaves hanging out all over the edges and really I just thought things were not well kept up. I think they would benefit from a remodel at this location. One positive thing to note, the front desk clerk was very accomodating, refunded our money and even tried to help our son find a lost watch he had left behind. This is definitely a housekeeping issue and a general management issue.

From the moment we arrived to the moment we checked out everything was exceptional absolutely perfect. Every single employee went beyond all expectations to make our stay absolutely wonderful the concierge were superb fulfilled any request that we had immediately without any hesitation whatsoever. Next visit to New York it will definitely be Trump International!!
Stylish looking - great location. DIRTY rooms - especially bathrooms. If they can fix their housekeeping standard and have one or two people replaced from the front desk - this hotel would be ideal.

I did a sister's retreat at this hotel and we had a blast! The rooms were spotless, the beds just divine to sleep in and there was even the convenience of a fridge. Only drawback was no free internet. Nevertheless the hotel is a historic masterpiece. I liked the architecture... actually downtown Philly is an history lover's dream!
This hotel is strategically placed near several restaurants and lots of shopping. Macy's is across the street. Access to Septa bus terminal is nearby and the main bus terminal is a short cab drive away.
The Reading Terminal Market is a must; check out the Amish stalls...the breakfast is an experience.

This hotel is located in a great place. Just next to the Metro Centre subway stop and a reasonable walking distance from some of the popular sites (especially during a time of year when the temperatures are not tipping --- degrees).
We got an upgraded suite since our room was not ready when we got there which was very nice for a family of four to have the extra room.
I read reviews before booking and noted that there were comments regarding the lack of sitting room in the lobby, etc. I would say they are unfounded. 
The pool area looked to be very nice and bright at first glance but being a clean nut; I would say on closer inspection that it is in need of a refurbishment quite soon. The fitness centre has a great deal of equipment in it.
The restaurant is quite reasonably priced. Being that we were with teens, we did not visit the bar.

Check in was not good. We booked on Hotwire, I think they look down on you for some reason. After waiting for an hour we got our room. Overlooked the city, view is ok from room ----. Even though its beside the elevator did not hear a thing. Lots of shops and restaurants around, all different prices. Before we went there I read a lot about it being a pricey area, but there are lots of places to eat on a budget. Walk to Fenway, walk downtown or anywhere. Jog along the river, great for that. Ask at the front desk for a Prudential Center Preferred shopping card. My wife got one, you can some deals at some of the shops and restaurants there. You can also get a $- dollar credit every night that you pass on room cleaning. We did it a few times, it translated into some smoothies at the Starbucks in the lobby.

This hotel was clean and adequate. It doesn't have great curb appeal, but is clean, free breakfast and -- hour front desk clerks that were helpful. Secured parking and courteous hosts. I will stay here again when in the area.

My wife and I celebrated her --th birthday at week-end at the Harbor Hotel. Being European ex-pats we have travelled the world and been to many a great - star hotel but the Harbor Hotel is in our opinion the best hotel we have been to in the US so far. The service is just outstanding but in a low key and not brash way. The critiques on this site speaks for itself and is very accurate. We can recommend this hotel for any couple wanting a romantic get-away-week-end. The food is very good but the view of the harbor and the servive level is magnificent. Try it!
Wellesley, MA

Hotel was nice, Nothing spectacular. The location was great however! Was originally given a room that looked out to a brick wall. they did give us a different room the next night upon request. hotel was clean and pleople were nice. But given the rave reviews I guess I was expecting a bit more. Seemed just plain average to me. Wasn't worth the expensive price.

We just stayed three nights at this hotel. Outside of its super location, we found little to recommend it. Both of the beds in our room sank toward the middle and when I sat at the end of one of them, the other end reared up. The curtains didn't close and the only way to ensure privacy was to pull down """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""--'s type shades"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and secure them with our shoes...otherwise they flew up. There was a quarter inch gap at the top of the door so light and sound from the hall had no trouble traveling into the room. We would have checked out after the first night, but, alas we had prepaid. Important lesson learned.

We were going to spend Christmas in NYC so we thought we would book a hotel that wasn't too expensive but would be conveniently situated in the heart of Manhattan. This hotel was certainly no wrong choice.
The service staff in the hotel are like none other. Not only do they greet you when you come back from a long day's sightseeing, the lady at the concierge desk even worked overtime just to ensure that we would get our taxi to the airport on the night we were departing. We certainly felt that all our needs were taken care of when we were at the hotel.
The rooms are well equipped with a buffet of pillows, such that I felt that they could have given less pillows. The beds were comfortable and the bathroom was well equipped with amenities. The complimentary WiFi access in every room made our stay even better for we could search information about the places we intended to visit before setting foot each day.
The hotel also has a coffee machine in the lobby that dispenses coffee-hot water all day long. The gym at the basement is sufficiently sized with treadmills and a few weights. Bring along your earpieces if you're going to run, for the treadmills are boosted with individual TV sets with access to all the TV channels the hotel has. 
Certainly a good choice!

We decided to come here after reading the reviews on this motel and looking at the rather slick website. Furthermore, it's got to be good to be ranked -th amongst all the hotels in Los Angeles, right? However, after a wonderful trip to Vegas at a cheaper-priced resort at a more convenient location, we were unsure how to make a true comparison.
On the bright side of things:The location was good with Universal Studios a freeway away, the reservation service was prompt and no fuss, the free parking - free wifi - flat-screen HD TV with multiple channels rocked. Though small, the room came complete with all the facilities of a standard motel room. When you check in, Jerry gives you a small bag with snacks and drinks (all my favourites!). The water pressure and pillows were quite satisfactory.
On the other hand: There isn't an elevator in the motel so if you bring heavy luggage, you'll have to get it up the stairs. The walls and floors feel flimsy as we could hear-feel our next door neighbours moving about their room. The motel is located near a hospital so we were awoken by sirens through the night. It is also located in between two taller buildings so the area feels hemmed in. The toilet is a little cramped and there isn't any light in the shower area so you either bathe in semi-darkness or wet the bathroom because you leave the shower curtain open to let the light in. There isn't a heater in the toilet as well, so if you shower too late, you can get quite cold during the winter months. 
The verdict: Considering the other hotels in the nearby vicinity were very much more expensive than Jerry's, I would say that Jerry's Motel is a good place to stay if -) you're on a budget -) only concerned if you have a place to sleep (and can sleep through loud noises). We saw the owner every morning about his chores and was always nice and polite but wasn't particularly very warm or friendly as the other reviewers mentioned. 
In the end, we're confused. We don't like giving bad reviews but we have to say, Jerry's Motel was an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""experience"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of a lifetime. Would we come back? Not likely. If you do decide to stay at Jerry's Motel, go in with an open mind and if you can survive the first night, it gets more bearable each night you stay.

..had a very pleasant - night stay at the Affinia. The room was quite nice, well appointed and comfortable. The staff was exceptionally nice and extremely helpful. They seemed content just to chit chat with us in the lobby--they were knowledgeable about the area and were genuinely interested in making our whole experience special.

I stayed here with a friend for -- days for a combination vacation-business trip. We had a two bedroom, two bath suite which allowed us each to have some privacy. We had - flat screen TVs- one in each bedroom and one in the living room area. Room was clean and well maintained. Kitchen was complete down to a wine-beer opener. Breakfast was ample with varied hot and cold choices including waffles in the shape of the state of Texas- we didn't make any of the evening socials but if they were anything like the breakfast I'm sure they were good. Only one morning when there were more people having breakfast than chairs. Very close to the Alamo and the big convention hotels, we were a -- minute walk away from our convention, paid less than we would have for a standard room and had much, much more space. Staff was friendly and helpful. The hotel was busy with a variety of guest including a college volleyball team, many military folks, folks with pets but was quiet. I'd certainly return there if I visit San Antonio again.
A couple of minor issues-We rented a car for part of our stay- $-- a night plus tax to park our rental car seemed excessive- it cost more to park the car than it did to rent it. There is only one control on the air conditioning-heating for the entire suite so if one person wanted it warmer-colder in their bedroom it was an issue. There were problems with the internet access in our room- turned out the wifi didn't like our choice of browser which took a couple of days and a couple of staff folks to figure out, luckily I didn't have any major deadlines or projects to complete during that time.

My hubby and I stayed here for - nights for his birthday weekend to see the city. The hotel's website was pretty deceiving, showing it to be a pretty upscale place, with very upscale prices, but it is more like an old motel. The rooms are accessed from the outside, which if given the choice, I never stay in. The bed was uncomfortable, but the room was clean and the breakfast was good. The thing that most annoyed me was when I booked the reservation, I let them know I would be bringing our dog with us (a very small lab-dachshund mix). However, when we showed up, the guy seemed very confused and asked if the dog would be staying with us. Obviously, otherwise why would we have brought him along? I'm not sure if we were in a pet-friendly room, as it was on the -rd floor, and the lady I made the reservation with said it would be on the -st floor. I was a little annoyed to find that there were no grassy areas for our dog to potty in, only mulch-dirt and rocks, but they claim to be a pet-friendly hotel, etc. The other thing I found very annoying was that they placed a $---day pre-charge on our credit card. When I called and asked about it, I was told that they do this mostly on holiday weekends, etc. This should have been made very clear before booking, or at time of check in. I don't understand the need for this pre-charge when their prices are already nearly $---+-night for a simple motel room. Needless to say, I was not overly impressed, and will not be staying here again.

I recently spent a week at the Palomar for a conference at Moscone Center. The hotel is an easy walk to Moscone and also perfectly situated for tourist activities (cable car line and Union Square are steps away). Don't stay here if you want """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""normal"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" business travel support (although there is high-speed internet access in most rooms), but do if you want to avoid larger hotels (the Marriott is across the street at the end of the block) and the rest of the conference crowd.
The staff was friendly, knowledgeable, very attentive and helpful. The room (king) was above average and amenities like a CD player in the room much appreciated. Ask for a room facing Market or -th Street. Yes, the workout room is far too small, but it is open -- hours (and I preferred to leave the building- San Francisco is a great walking-jogging city). All in all, I would stay here again, for either business or leisure travel.

Booked two rooms for a girls weekend. I feel very pleased with our choice of hotels.
Location, Location, Location is great. Two blocks from shopping and a few blocks from the pike place market. Many places to eat and drink right around us. Never needed to use the car. Parking a little stiff at -- plus tax a night.
Rooms very nice, clean and comfortable. Beds great and bathroom was normal size.
front desk staff were very helpful. If I am looking for a girls weekend or family weekend again in Seattle this would be the place to go!
(no connecting rooms)

Yes, the basic rooms are tiny. Yes, the decor is minimalistic. Yes, it's pricey. This is New York! Why would you stay in your room? I have been fortunate enough to have travelled around the world, and never have I been remembered by the bell staff. Beckham, you were wonderful. Exactly what I expect from the first person I see at a hotel. Warm, gracious, and dispensing helpful tips. He suggested that I ask to be moved to a larger room, and would come back to move me. The next morning, he stopped me in the lobby to ask if I had moved, then took me to the manager, introduced me, and arranged to have me moved to a suite with an enormous balcony. While settling in, the lovely housekeeping ladies checked in to see if they could get me anything, promptly returning with ice, and insisting on checking to see if everything was perfect.

We didn't spend much time in the hotel but I liked the Japanese style restaurant, & the breakfast was alright. However we found a nice diner round the corner for breakfast. The staff were all friendly & helpful. The galley offering free hot drinks on each floor was a nice touch.
All in all a great hotel for a sightseeing trip to New York, but I wouldn't stay here if I was planning on spending much time relaxing in my hotel room as it is small.

I end up paying extra $---.-- for a hotel stay , I still wait for a Manger to call me back about the extra fee, I have called the hotel and they send me to account voice mail.
