I selected this hotel after many, many, many hours of research, mainly because of the free parking and the good reviews on trip advisor. It also appealed because it meant that we didn't have to drive into the main part of the city. We stayed one night at the end of our -- day road trip round Washington, and were very happy with the choice. We arrived a bit early, frazzled because of the traffic on a Saturday afternoon, (having been in the mountains for days it was a shock to the system!) and they checked us in straight away, which was great. The room was spacious and very clean, overlooking Lake Union. We enjoyed watching the sea planes and boats coming and going. Later we walked down the road and had a meal at Dukes Chowder House, which we enjoyed very much. The free breakfast was very good.

We stayed at the Marriot Plaza for a weekend in August. What I liked about it was that the grounds were beautiful with roaming peacocks. The workout facility is located in a seperate building next to the pool area. In the facility it has sauna. There is also a nice hot tub next to the pool. The landscaping is done wonderfully. The hotel is smoke free which is very nice. The rooms were not anything special a bit dated but the bedding was very nice as were the pillows. The bathrooms were also very nicely done. Good toiletries as well. The hotel is not overly large and has a more quaint feeling than some of the large hotels on the riverwalk. This hotel is located at the very end of the riverwalk which is nice but it is in the downtown area so you do have street traffic noise. Each room has a small balcony with table and chairs. We had free water placed daily in our room and a turn down service with mints. The dining area was very nice and the food good. We did breakfast room service one morning which was excellent and not overly expensive. At that time we paid about $---.-- a night. I returned to San Antonio in November for business and was all ready to stay at this hotel again because I had such a good experience and loved it but saw that the rates have almost doubled. I am not sure why? Thus, on our return trip we stayed at a different hotel.

Una Atencion -- con mrs DARIO,,,amabilidad ,,respeto y total cubrimiento de nuestras preguntas,,, una estadia placentera ,,,, excelente ubicacion,,, recomendacion --. I had a wonderful stay at this hotel and would recommend and come back here again!

Location is the highlight of the hotel almost connected to the airport. Suggestion - if you in Terminal E then forget the shuttle and walk - much easier and faster.
Nice lobby with the coffee shops etc
Rooms are standard Hilton - nothing to complain about. Room rates are pricey but they do lots of advance deals that are fine.
Food options are the primary nit. Room service (while always expensive) is even more so here with the MA, facilities etc etc taxes - a ripoff...but then there are not many other places to go to :-(
If proximity to the airport (late incoming or early outgoing flight) is your driver, then this is a great place

First time I've stayed here. And I'm always a little leary of the cool NYC hotel.
The elevators are small and old. Considering that I would suggest staying on the -st floor ---- although its really the -nd floor. Why? So that after you've taken luggage up, you can use the stairs and bypass the elevators until check out.
Beds are incredible. Bathroom nice and livable. Not big by any means, but no complaints here. --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" plasma on the wall, adequate space around one side of the bed.
Didn't eat here --- but then its NYC, why would I?
Blue neon affect lighting and a -- degree temperature room greeted me. NICE.
I'll be back.

We arrived very late but the people behind the desk were very friendly. Our room was right by the elevator which I didn't like too much. It was room ---. We also didn't have a very nice view but that's ok we didn't spend a lot of time in the room anyway. It was nice that there was a fridge but without a microwave it is almost pointless since if we brought food back to the hotel we would not have been able to reheat it. Another is with this room was that the bathroom is very small. Not much moving around space. I did like the beds and they were comfortable. We had an issue with the TV remote but again we barely used it so not a big bother. The hotel is very close to the space center although we did not visit it. There are a few places to eat not too far away, most importantly there is a Starbucks close by across from the McDonalds. We were there for a conference so didn't have much time to explore the area or use other amenities in the hotel. The food provided by the hotel was pretty good, lots of fresh fruit. Over all it was a nice hotel and if we come for vacation here, I would definitely stay here.

A girl's weekend in Charlotte was made so special by the accent on service of every hotel and restaurant employee we met. A trip to the uptown Mint Museum, shopping at Ikea,and a wonderful morning in the hotel pools and whirlpool made our stay fun, relaxing, and memorable. I loved the decor and just being away from the look-alike hotel chains. I also appreciated being in an upscale developed area south of Charlotte...no issues with security or feeling safe here.

I travel to NYC every week for business. There are several of us that are frequent guests of this lovely hotel. The staff are all warm and welcoming. I am especially grateful to Domingo who helps me get back on the road at the end of each week. His pleasant demeanor is always welcome in the morning. I highly recommend this hotel without reservatin.

Great location, but pretty unspectacular rooms. The rooms are very small and the furnishings a bit run down, but not dirty. Staff was fine, although not as knowledgeable about the surrounding area as I would have expected. Overall, this is a very basic hotel and a bit expensive for what it is. I would likely stay elsewhere next time I'm in Philly.

My family and I stayed at this hotel and loved it. We had the great view from our room. The room is clean and fresh. Good size room. The staff are very helpful and great. It's great to wake up every morning and just watch the harbor view. And this is our first time visiting Boston and its a greate experience. Also if you are visiting for couple of days make sure inquire about Hop on and off All day. This is a great way to visit all sites. Also make sure go eat at Fire and Ice at Harvard Square

What a fabulous find. Have just spent - nights at the Hotel Rouge and could not fault the experience. Funky decor, friendly staff and really how could you go wrong at a hotel that offers you free red stripe beer or red wine between -pm and -pm Monday to Friday. I can tell you after spending a hot and humid day seeing the sights of Washington this refreshing beverage offer was too good to refuse - we were just disappointed that on the weekends the freebies were on offer at --am and we had already left for the day.
Being located on a main road it was a tad noisy on Saturday Night but at all other times not once were we woken by street noise - or any noise as a matter of fact.
If you are heading to Washington check out the rates for this hotel at Tablethotels.com - i'm sure you wont be disappointed - we couldn't have found a better hotel for the price.
Oh and if you are heading out to Dulles Airport by cab ask the front desk about their car service - travelling in a stretch Limo for the same price as a cab is a definate bonus.

I've had the pleasure of staying at this location twice since it's opening in early ---- and both visits have been wonderful. From the time you walk in you know you are in someplace special. The staff actually walks out from behind the individual desks to greet you and check you in, and the walks you to the elevators and directs you to your room and amenities. 
The rooms are beautiful and many feature views of White River park, the baseball field, and the local museums. The hotel is within walking distance of all the local attractions, and if it's a rainy day you can take the covered skywalks to Circle Center Mall. 
Be sure to check out the fitness center. The exercise bikes feature video screens that are similar to video games where you can track your progress, and the chilled towels (two temperatures are available!) are a great refresher at the end of your workout. The complimentary disposable earbuds are also a nice touch. 
I've stayed in many locations in Indianapolis including the Westin and the older Marriott, and this is the best by far.

We thoroughly enjoyed our stays at Bay Club - one in ---- and one in ----. The rooms are spacious and clean and the hotel staff were all very helpful. Both times we had marina view rooms with a balcony - relaxing out on the balcony with a hot cup of coffee is a great way to start the morning!
The hotel staff was great and ensured that we had what we needed and offered advice on sites to see and travel distances. The heated pool and hot tub were wonderful - and the later hours very convenient! Breakfast was delicious with different things each day.
I would highly recommend staying here - very nice and convenient access to a number of San Diego attractions.

I went to Dallas for - day and had to add an extra day. I have to say the price was actually reasonable for the event I went for. The Staff was great as well when I had to changes things around it was no problem. I was able to stay in the same room. The room was nice. coffee was decent in the room. Maid service great!! By the way there was a microwave and refrigerator in the room. I had no problems at all!!!!!!!!

My husband and I stayed two nights at the Kimberly during the Christmas holiday season. The room was very roomy and comfortable. The staff were extremely helpful. Easy walk to all the must see sites. If you are looking for a good less expensive breakfast there is a good little restaurant next door, very clean and have a large selection for breakfast.

We finally found the perfect Times Square hotel! We have stayed at many different hotels in the area and this one was the best. The room was well-appointed and included a bath tub--a rare treasure for an NYC hotel! The bed was exceptionally comfortable, service was just superb, atmosphere was elegant yet warm, and the turn-down service was such a delightful touch. Also nice was that the elevators were efficient so there wasn't a lot of waiting or being crammed in. Highly recommended.

We arrived earlier than check in, and although our room wasn't ready they stored our bags so we could get out and start enjoying the city. We were able to get into our room about an hour early. Room was beautiful, double queen suite on the -th flour, facing the Eugene O'Neil theatre. I was worried that noise would be a problem, they even provided ear plugs, but I sure didn't need them, didn't hear barely a sound either of the two nights we stayed! I didnt understand all the negative reviews on the complementary continental breakfast. We found it to be just perfect and satisfying! The front desk people and the door men were all great. I highly recommend The Pearl, and would definitely stay again!

This was the first time for me and my wife in New York, and we are really lucky to have found this hotel. It is very close to the main attractions, we barely used taxi or metro to reach several destinations, like broadway, empire state, -th avenue etc. 
The rooms are quite big and spacious, so that after a long day of walking, you can enjoy going back to your room and relax, get ready for the evening. We chose to have the breakfast at the hotel, as we found the price quite reasonable and also the choices were quite healthy, compared to pancakes, fried eggs and patatoes which you get in some other cafes. Only missing thing was a nice coffee... The staff was always kind and helpfull. Also the guests mostly tourists made the atmoshpere better compared to a business hotel, where you would only see business people.

We stayed here based largely on the stellar recommendations at tripadvisor (and the hotel's close proximity to USC). What a mistake. There was only one working elevator, and it was remarkably slow. (Plus, it's a huge pain in the neck to scan your room card and select your floor once you're in the elevator.) The rooms are large, which is the hotel's one redeeming quality, but the front desk staff is strangely impersonal and ineffective. We called for a bellhop only to have our request ignored.
On sunday am, we awoke to discover the streets outside the hotel were closed for the LA marathon. We were given no advance notice by the hotel, and when we attempted to return to the hotel later that morning, we were forced to pay to park in a lot three blocks away. The front desk staff refunded the hotel's parking fee for the nite ($--), but offered no apology for the inconvenience.
The breakfast is overpriced and the exercise room is small. Do yourself a favor and find a holiday inn express nearby. You may think you're saving time by staying close to USC and Staples Center here, but you're really just asking for frustration.

I am a frequent traveler to NYC, a preferred Starwood customer, and the person responsble for booking more than ---- room nights a year for my company. While the hotel location is perfect, the service provided by the bell staff really left a stale taste in my mouth and the mindset of -- I will never go back to this hotel nor recommend it to others. The service received is not the Starwood way -- and something I have never received at another hotel. The rooms are spectacular - not worth the money though -- as the walls are not thick and you can hear noise in the hallway, the water passing through the pipes, and some of the painting and caulking around the windows was not properly finished (quite scary). The one positive thing about the hotel: you have the ability to leave your hotel room and take in a movie, go shopping in Times Square, and-or take the train to any part of NYC cant beat -- however, it can be beaten by hotels that value their customers. 
 As I was departing from the hotel, their bell staff was highly rude and offensive. The bell staff is the first and last point for customers -- and should be the most welcoming. After my treatment -- it almost made me think - my money was not as important as the next customers.

This property is not a hotel. They are villas - not the same. My initial feelings were not so positive since the check-in process was troublesome. There was some mistake made during the reservation so the room type I had reserved wasn't available. In the end, though, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The rooms are beautiful and have everything you need for an extended stay. The grounds are gorgeous - we should have taken more time to enjoy. We had so many activities already scheduled in and around Phoenix and Carefree.
But the attribute that promoted me to write this review was the service and follow-up by Housekeeping. We had left two pieces of clothing behind when we checked out, and I only realized this after I had reached home. Housekeeping sent the clothes via FedEx! Great service! 
I'm not sure how frequently the villas are rented or used. Our villa had mosquitoes inside. These were a nuisance, but more so they were completely inappropriate and out of character for a property of this caliber.
My room and the location of the hotel is unbeatable, just try it

I stayed for one night at Hotel Mela (March----) and loved it. I picked this hotel over the many others in Times Square because of the very decent price and from the great reviews I read here on TripAdvisor. And I'm very glad I did! The room was very small (fit the double bed, but only about - feet more of room on either side of it) but it was extremely clean and pretty. The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom was sparkling clean and modern. I laughed my head off when I opened the curtain and looked out the window for the first time as there was a construction worker working on the building next to us only a few meters away (I waved and he waved back!! haha). So it was noisy! But the noise was over around -pm, so it wasn't a big deal. Besides, it's New York City in the centre of Times Square. It's always busy and noisy! But that's what NYC is all about.
Check in and out was immediate and everyone was very friendly and polite. The lobby always smelled like pineapple or something pleasant and tropical. 
I would definitely recommend Hotel Mela to anyone looking to go stay in the very centre of things, wants a nice, modern, clean, and comfortable stay but doesn't want to break the bank either.

I recently stayed at the Boston Harbor Hotel and just can't say enough about the hotel- absolutely stunning and every single staff member I interacted with were extremely friendly and professional! The room was absolutely gorgoues overlooking Boston Harbor- and Gary, the Director of Rooms, was so very helpful and kind in particular- treated me like pure royalty! I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone wishing to stay in the area and I cannot wait to go back!

This was a nice hotel. The rooms were nice and the staff was very professional. My only complaint was the price of the parking but I'm not sure that there was anyway around that. There was some noise from the street (I was on the -th floor) but it wasn't unbearable. The ice machines didn't work and that was bothersome since I had a sick grandmother in the room with me. Also the vending machines were out. All in all it wasn't a bad stay.

Spectacular location both for vistas and getting around SF. Attentive and very, friendly staff from doormen to the front desk - everyone was quite gracious. We parked our car at the hotel which is wildly expensive at $--+ but you don't want to park and walk in this city. Our car was retrieved quickly and on top of the overnight charge (with come and go access) you have to or rather you should tip the gents getting your vehicle and that adds up as well. The rooms are clean and have lovely, comfy bedding and fluffy towels and complimentary toiletries.Our tv was older but you don't go to SF to watch tv - it's just that the Olympics were on and it would have been nice to view on a nice set. I have to mention the wind-tunnel effect under the bedroom door. Once you close your door you will hear this howling noise that at first might sound like the A-C but it isn't...it's coming from the crevice at the bottom of the door. Easily solved - take the little coverlet (sorry housekeeping) blanket and simply fold it lengthwise and rest it at the base of the door and it will suddenly be very peaceful. That said, the guests seem to be early risers because all we heard were doors opening just past -:--am and you could hear each door open and close. The one modern installation is in the HVAC system panel which is where you program your """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""do not disturb"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" message. Odd, but it works. The famous Top of the Mark restaurant does offer sensational views and it's worth going up to look out the windows day or night. We were incredibly disappointed with the pricey breakfast buffet - boxed cereal, dried egg products, sweet rolls, greasy bacon, chewy pancakes, not fine pastries, fresh fruit was ok as was fresh juice but overall really, dull and shame on them for the price and the location. Tsk. Tsk. The Huntington located one block away offers a spectacular breakfast - sorry, it's true. There are fabulous restaurants all over town so get up and get dressed and go enjoy. Also missing...an in-hotel gift-toiletries, magazine shop. Grand location and reputation but pricey options that simply weren't worth it.

Stayed for ne night as wanted to explore the city. Hotel is - mins walk to water front and had lovel old charm entrance as is in old office buildings of old railway company. Amazing cocktails in the bar and food looked good too. Had king premier room which wad spacious and had jaquizze. Sparing sem dodgy car service that pounced on us a w elf hotel and charged twice taxis rate all good. Had excellent welcome when arrived at hotel which was nic touch. Check out the visionary art museum if u can.

We have stayed here a number of times, but something has changed there....We purchased a - night package that included - transit tickets....We asked for the tickets three different times, - different people. Each time they gave a flimsy excuse as to why they couldn't issue the tickets, (no one had the key to unlock them, couldn't find them, etc.)
A major disappointment that we never received everything we paid for, with no apologies from management.

This hotel looks & feels sparkling & new. According to several proud members of the staff, this new addition to the Kimpton family was renovated from a previous use & opened in Oct. ----. After a long & rainy drive on the NJ Turnpike, we were greeted by the doorman who swept us & our luggage inside. The short wait to check in (disappointing) was alleviated by the bellman who immediately offered us glasses of wine and ice water (surprising & delighting us). The next day we once again arrived in the lobby during the daily wine & cheese offering, which this day was augmented with a bowl of popcorn before the gas fireplace & several trays of tasty fried oysters. We joined the throng - families, couples, single travelers - in the lobby for a relaxing & pleasant half hour. Our room - two queen beds - was lovely, well appointed, and just big enough for two old friends. Beds were comfy! As a dog-lover, I'm delighted that Kimpton Hotel's enlightened policy is to welcome dogs. One small criticism: During August's hot weather, the lobby's ice water dispenser was empty upon my return from a long walk. The single desk clerk apologetically explained that they had inadequate personnel to keep it filled during the busy dinner hour. I know this is a cranky criticism, but the hotel does spoil its guests, and I was both disappointed & surprised. (At an April stay at the San Francisco Kimpton Palomar, the desk clerk - one of two - responded to my request for ice water - a vice of mine - by immediately & cheerfully refilling the dispenser.) A more serious criticism-warning: Valet parking, so welcome upon our arrival, was $-- @ day. I inquired before surrendering the keys, but had no energy to drive another foot. However, the friends whom we were visiting told us that garage parking near them - on the other side of Rittenhouse Sq. - was available for $-- @ day. Nonetheless, because of the laziness-convenience factor, we did not relocate the car during our short, --night stay. I'll probably valet park again on my next visit. Don't forget to use to use discount options in making a reservation. It helped.

Great room. You're on the --- Freeway, but Bel Air's celebrities tolerate it just across the way, plus the Getty is just above. The TV and TV connection are so good, they may be better than home, and the Wi-Fi is free.
My reservation was a little complicated, and the staff messed it up. Overall, the staff were all right but really didn't seem as in tune with things as at most fine hotels.
The Web site mentions a shuttle service, but it seems to be one very over-extended van. My first night I called for a pickup from Westwood Village, and they said it would be a --hour wait. Next morning I reserved a ride from the hotel, but so many others did we had to squeeze ultra-tight to fit in.

We stayed here in September ----. We arrived in Boston after a flight from the UK on Labour Day weekend and were staying for a week. When we arrrived, having booked and paid for a double room with Virgin Holidays, we were given a single room with a sink that did not hold any water, next to the air conditioning unit and facing a brick wall. This was at -pm on the Saturday night of Labour Day. They had given all of the double rooms to people staying just for the weekend - it seems that staying for a week meant nothing to them! Went to reception to be told that we would have to stay there until Monday when more rooms became available, even though people were still checking in and getting double rooms! Started off polite, reception staff were unprofessional and totally useless. Took threatening and public humiliation on the Sunday morning to get the room changed - along with -- other people at reception changing. Food trays stayed outside doors for days, cockroaches in the halls and some rooms apparently! I would not put my worst enemy in this hotel and would certainly wish to discourage anybody else to stay there! I am well travelled and would expect much better service and maintenance from such a hotel, especially in the USA, but have to say that their customer service stinks! Just hope that they read this one day and realise how many holidays they have ruined! Hardly the thing you want to deal with after a trans-atlantic flight!

There was so much about this hotel that we loved. Our double queen room was spacious, the beds were comfortable, the honor bar was well stocked with many items for $-.--! The internet was free and fast. They have a special button to call a taxi and one shows up in five minutes. There were two overhead ceiling fan lights in our room which were quiet and made us very comfortable in the evening. It is in a clean, walking neighborhood on the bus line. We were thrilled and are already planning a return visit.
Our only suggestions for improvement are the breakfast in the morning. There are only couches in the lobby so no place to eat and the selection could be better. But it is free! Also, there is about -- inches of small counter space in the bathroom.
We were here visiting a Chicago based friend and we strongly recommended the hotel to her for when she has visiting relatives.
Also, guests have privileges to the adjacent Bally Fitness Center

We were amazed when we pulled up to the Hotel after reading great reviews on Trip Advisor and other rating website. This Hotel is ADJACENT to the Greyhound Travel Plaza. A homeless beggar approached us even before we got out of the car and was begging for money and cigarettes and would not leave us alone. We went into the hotel that had dark grime on the walkway. The website for the hotel shows a modern designed lobby, however, the rest of the fixtures are dirty and old. We cancelled our reservation and went to the Inner Harbor for a Hotel. We got a great rate at the Sheraton!! I suggest you do the same.

We spent - nights here,from the -st of October.We had a late check in,but had to wait half an hour or so for our room.As we had spent the last -- hours travelling we could have done without that!
However,the room was lovely,very clean and a good size.The bathroom was huge,and had everything you needed.
The staff were extremley pleasant,and the entire stay was lovely.We would definately return to this hotel if we go back to S.F.
Big thanks

My experience at the Topaz was just excellent: This hotel is located at a great spot, the rooms are big, comfortable, very clean and have a very original decoration, the hotel staff was always willing to serve me and my boyfriend needs; These are all clear strengths of this hotel, but for me the best part of staying at the Topaz was that, in times when honest people are very hard to find, I happened to forget my wallet at the hotel, as soon as the staff found it they contacted me ASAP (Despite of me not living in the US, I live in Colombia) and they proceeded to send it to my country. All of my personal documents, credit cards, CASH (Both dollars and pesos) were intact, not a single coin was missing!! I have no words to express my gratitude towards the Topaz staff and I strongly recommend this hotel to anybody who wants to have a great experience at a very trendy hotel with the best service at the hottest spot of Washington DC.

This past weekend my daughter (--) and I spent the night in San Francisco - dinner & a show. I got a very good rate at the Omni for one night ($---). It is smack in the middle of the financial district so there wasn't much open after Friday evening but the locations was terrific. We were able to walk to North Beach for dinner & Beach Blanket Babylon and then Saturday morning we walked to the Ferry Building as their Farmer's Mkt was open. The hotel was clean, accomodations great and everyone there couldn't have been nicer. We had drinks @ their bar when we got back Friday evening and I have to say, they were delicious! a bit on the pricey side, but at least they were a fairly good size. I have stayed at several hotels throughout the city and I will return to the Omni. Great hotel centrally located.

The hotel is new, clean, modern and beautiful. Personnel is very friendly and helpful. Great location - only half a block from Times Square. Breakfast did not include hot entrees but still was very nice. Wonderful hotel for the price we paid.

Never stay at this hotel! I have stayed in hotels of a comparable price range in cities throughout North America, Europe and East Asia and have never had a bad experience like I did with this hotel. Not only did I find the staff rude and unhelpful from the moment of my arrival, I had a valuable possession stolen from my room while I was out at the theatre. After reporting the theft, I only received the most cursory, and I might add non-apologetic, visit from the hotel security. It felt like I was inconveniencing them by pointing out that someone on their staff had been blatantly rifling through my possessions. They casually promised to follow-up with me and never did. Not even a templated """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sorry we can't help you, but of course we appreciate your business, email"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Considering that they charge over $----per night and fashion themselves to be a high-end establishment, I was appalled. It really made me wonder about the general security and integrity of their hotel (women travellers beware). Worst hotel experience I've had in North America.

Stayed at The Benjamin for a long weekend with my family and had an excellent stay. 
The location is fantastic, providing easy access to everything in mid-town. Rockefeller Plaza is only a - minute walk and the theater district is only -- minutes past that. There is a subway stop across the street and you only need to walk a block or - to access other lines. It is only about -- minutes to Grand Central if you want access to other places. It is actually a pretty quiet area in the evenings, with not much going on in the immediate vicinity of the hotel.
Our suite was fairly large by NY standards and the little kitchen area came in handy for quick breakfasts and snacks. There is a full grocery store (Food Emporium) about - blocks away on --th and -nd. We rearranged the mini-bar fridge to handle the few items that needed to be cold and it worked out well Work station was pretty nice and I got free internet as part of the room package.
Front desk people and doormen were great. Very helpful and very friendly. One night we wanted to have a nightcap and just missed last call at the bar in the hotel. A doorman overheard us talking and handed us - unbrellas and told us to walk a half block to the W. They even started to greet us by name, which was a nice touch.
My only complaint was that the concierges were not used to dealing with tourists' questions and instead seemed more comfortable with businessman type concerns They had trouble booking our tickets for the Statue of Liberty-Ellis Island as well as the ---- Memorial-by the way, do both before you go and bring the tickets with you. ---- Memorial tickets are free, but you need to have them for a particular day and time. In addition, they gave us subway directions that did not work because the particular train did not run on a weekend. They were very nice and always apologetic, but as I said, I am not sure the tourist trade is their specialty.
Overall, an excellent stay and I look forward to returning to the Benjamin.

We stayed - nights at the end of a great tour of the USA, and it was a total anticlimax. The room we were first allocated had a nice view (double aspect) but was very tatty and dirty - the bathroom was appalling: chipped paint, filthy grouting, hairs in the bath and on the tiles.... ugh.
We refused the room and were given another, not double aspect and not overly spacious, but adequate. The room was still rather ----s, not spacious, and the bathrom, while much cleaner, was very far from immaculate. 
To close the blackout curtains fully in the room, there were plastic bulldog clips attached... unless that's a bit of designer chic fashion that I missed, it's not a good advert but I guess it solves the problem! 
The furnishings were barely boarding-house quality: a rickety fridge on a wobbly plastic-coated wire stand was next to a bright blue plastic recycling bin. The wardrobe door was damaged - a large chunk of the wood missing, as with much of the woodwork and paintwork in the room. There wasn't a lot of space - you wouldn't want to be there for a long stay, for all srts of reasons...
We were feeling very let down, and later when we returned from a look around town, tried to get a drink in the bar but it was shut, at least -- minutes before the advertised time, which left us feeling even more jaundiced. 
Our friends took breakfast in the hotel and were less than impressed by value or quality: we chose a 'characterful' - i.e. tatty - cafe round the corner and had the better deal!
Desk staff were not overly impressive: when we asked via our tour guide to change room there was no apology of any sort, and the second room was presented with a 'take it or leave it' shrug. If I'm honest, I felt slightly sorry for our tour guide or I would have made much more fuss. Had we been travelling independently I would have immediately looked for another hotel. Mea culpa, to some extent, I suppose.

Had I needed to stay for a longer stint for business, I likely would have preferred to stay at an alternative hotel with a more flexible connectivity solution.
Otherwise, the hotel was clean. Bathroom was nice and the product seemed also nice. As an aside, it was odd to see the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""together we can make a difference"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" environmental card on my bed and then see several small plastic bottles of $- water next to the bed. If you're trying to encourage environmental actions, maybe encourage your guests to drink the fantastic potable New York filtered water straight from the tap?
Anyway, if you stay here and some of the extra touches are important or necessary for you - I'd recommend another hotel. There are lots of fantastic boutique hotels in New York. The Distrikt Hotel being one of them (unbelievable beds there, by the way). However, for a decent, no-frills kind of standard room - it's good. It's also probably worth noting that for a cost, you can upgrade to a larger room with more beds - but also more space.

This was our first stay at the Arizona Biltmore for me and my wife traveling on business. We stayed two nights in the heat of mid-August. Despite that, we had a great time. We obtained a great room rate on the internet, but resort fees ($---nt), valet parking ($---nt), and overpriced food took a bite out of that good rate. Unfortunately, we did not visit the spa. 
Overall, I think this property is a solid -*. Parts of it are -*, but parts of it are -*.
-* = cool architecture of main building, furnishings in common areas, historical touches, grounds & patios
-* = Frank and Albert's (great, but overpriced), pools, staff service. Kids area looked great.
-* = The Valley wing (average room, worn carpet, musty smell, old elevator, paper thin walls and doors). Seems like the other wings (Octilla, for example) were higher quality. The cabana poolside rooms needed paint and updating. 
For the rate we got, I was perfectly satisfied. It's a great hotel in the middle of the city. An oasis in the desert. We'll be back again. Hope this was helpful!

My wife and I stayed here as a part of her birthday weekend in Chicago. We were put into a fifth floor room with a view to die for! The room had floor to ceiling windows that looked right down State St. The hotel is in the middle of it all, including a short walk to Michigan Ave and the Magnificent Mile. There is cocktail lounge located on the roof of the hotel which provides amazing views of the Chicago skyline, even in Februaury! The service was great and the staff seemed very attentive to the needs of the guests. The bathrooms are modern with a HUGE walk in shower that has an optional privacy curtain, meaning there is a see-through wall of glass betweeen the shower and the bedroom. Oh, and it is important to note that the floor to ceiling windows do have room darkening blinds for comfort and privacy. All in all, we really enjoyed our stay here and would definitely go back!

My wife and I spent the weekend at the Fairmont DC earlier this month. We had been there a couple years ago, had a nice experience, and were looking forward to our return. We were very disappointed. Both service and decor have gone downhill, especially taking into account the premium rates they still charge. 
Full credit to the check-in clerk, who was very nice and very helpful. But the furniture in the room (desk, chair, etc) was badly chipped and gouged, the room was sold as a large corner room but wasn't a corner at all, and the view looked across to a close-by office building. Nice beds. But the bathroom was mediocre -- no separate shower, small tub, and a shower head that a Hilton would be embarrassed by.
On Saturday morning, we went to the restaurant for breakfast -- but sorry, no room for us -- a graduation party the hostess said. No suggetions made for alternate arrangements.
That afternoon we tried to have a drink in the outdoor garden. Sorry, closed due to a wedding -- though no one was in the garden and the lobby-bar seating was so full of wedding guests that there was no room for a drink there either. Again, no effort was made to suggest another arrangement.
I travel a lot, mostly on business, and stay in hotels from midrange to top of the line. I'm sympathetic to the challenges of running a hotel and delivering good service day in and day out.
But in my view a hotel that 's charging $--- a night really must do much better than this to accomodate its guests. While the management might maintain that it was an odd bad day, truly good hotels don't have days like that, or if they do, they go the extra mile in trying to find a different way to satisfy their customers. I expect that their cavalier attitude toward us, along with the deteriorating quality of the rooms, is indicative of a hotel that is living on its reputation from the past and is no longer trying to deliver a quality experience.

Great location. A few blocks from The Empire State. A couple of blocks from subway. Clean. Modern feel. Quiet room. Close to shopping, and nightlife. Generally happy and it made sure we enjoyed our week in NYC. What we loved best was the convenience of being right in the heart of Times Square - fantastic!! Great facilities, fitness center Didn't have a chance to enjoy the hotels restaurants - too much on offer in Times Square. Broadway shows all nearby !

This place is amazing. I love the lobby and we had a room with a balcony on the like --nd or --th floor and we could go out on the balcony every day and see madison square garden. I could walk to macys and the subway was like right across the street I mean everything was like ---- min away very nice location...The only thing is that the fire station and police station were right around the corner also but the bright thing to that was that nothing was going to jump off.

I had been a little concerned that the rooms would be too small for the -- day stay we had planned, but it was spacious, comfortable and quiet. The air conditioner worked, it was clean and had been recently renovated, so the bathroom in particular didn't show the age of the building. The common areas are stunning, very deco and stylish. I never had the feeling that anyone was standing with their hand out for a tip, but just that they were doing their jobs, being helpful. The concierge desk staff was generally very helpful. I wouldn't bother with the cafe's breakfast, very expensive compared to what is right around the corner in any direction! I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone who wants to stay in midtown-theatre district. It is really pretty close to the geographical center of Manhattan, so you can get uptown to the museums and downtown to the financial district with equal facility. It was the total Manhattan experience, an older building - but beautifully renovated - with very helpful staff, about - blocks from Times Square. Check their website for specials - we paid less than half the rack rate, less we have paid for a motel style hotel in a much less exciting location in a much less exciting city.
Great experience!

VERY busy hotel... packed with tons of families
I have never seen a happy hour with so many families and children --- and long lines.
There were lots of children running around the hotel in the evening, and in the morning.
The hotel restaurant (food and service) were the highlight.

We are a family of - and were very happy of our stay at the Orchid Suites.
The staff was very helpfull, the location was absolutely perfect, safe area and the room we got was huge and perfect for - people! free parking, wifi and breakfast was something we really appreciated a lot.
For sure, next time we go to LA, we'll definitively stay again at the Orchid Suites!

My family and I checked in for - nights Aug. -th - Aug. --th. Upon arrival we had a issue with the upgrade charge being too much compared to what the website said. The front desk employee basically said he could not do anything. We called Hyatt corporate and they called the manager for us. The manager comped the upgrade charge for the entire stay. We also had some Amex gift certificates that we used. We lost them in transit, but were able to get the info from Amex who verified it with Hyatt. This type of service continued throughout our stay. Anything we had a problem with or anything we needed was handed very professionally. The staff throughout the hotel was always there with a smile and ready to help. We used the concierge to book a nice dinner at Azul in La Jolla. We had a table overlooking the ocean and the food was great. We also had a discount off our bill by going through the Hyatt. We had a --th floor ocean view overlooking the pool. Each night the sunset was incredible. We had smores by pool with our kids that the hotel did nightly. Fireworks could be seen nightly from Seaworld as well. I rented a paddle board and took it around the bay, it was a blast and I was -- ft from a group of seals. The gym overlooks the marina which was a great view in the morning. The restaurants on site are nice as well. The pool restaurant is casual and the red marlin more upscale. I was going to eat at the red marlin and they were about to close within - minutes and the manager had no problem seating us. I declined as I wanted something a bit more casual with my kids. We ended up at the pool restaurant and the food was great. Mission Bch and Pacific Bch are both located with - - -- minutes by car and have a ton of other food options as well. We went to the fish shop in pacific bch. A must if you get a chance. The lobster taco is awesome. My family had a great vacation and can't wait to visit again!

Bayside Bungalow was great, nice and comfortable, wonderful view of Mission Bay
Close to Old Town San Diego
Walking distance to Sea World
Lots of activities
Nice Pools
A Bit Pricey
Guests were nice
Thanksgiving Weekend

I've just returned from a five night stay at the Omni (Rm ----). A great corner room, with windows on two sides. Prior to that I was at the Omni for New Years (Rm----); again a decent room with sufficent space. I've stayed at the Omni several times before, so knew what to expect. 
The hotel is just a very short walk from Government Center T stop (on Blue line from Airport). 
On both occassions, great welcome from staff. And provided with good, clean rooms. My rooms were of good size, but I know some of the rooms are fairly small - beware if you travelling as a couple. 
I'm a member of the Omni select guest program which entitles you to complimentary beverage in the morning, and free wifi. (Definately sign up before your trip). 
The hotel is on the freedom trial, and walking decent to the majority of sights in Boston. 
I was in town for the hockey and basketball - a short walk to TD Garden. 
I will definately return to the hotel, and would throughly recommend.

This is a good location but unfortuneately we had a bed bug situation. The Hotel naturally denies they have any. My arms say otherwise. We also did not get the - double bed room we were supposed to get.. If I were looking for a place to stay I'd look elsewhere.

I was at the Elysian for an event and it was amazing. I didn't get to stay here overnight, but spent an evening in their Hemingway Room. It was a beautiful space with great staff. They were so friendly and helpful and really made you feel like nothing was too much trouble.
The food was FANTASTIC, too. I'd love to go back and spend a weekend. Beautiful spot.

We usually stay downtown when in the city, but decided to try the Inter in Times Square for a recent wedding. The location is perfect for theatre goers and, surprisingly, relaxing and quiet even though you're a block from the action. The staff is attentive and friendly. Although small, the rooms are well furnished. Ours had a fantastic bed and a rain forest shower. I would recommend this property to all types of travelers looking for a comfortable, convenient spot in Midtown.

We just got home from our - day stay at the Homewood Suites. I have been to Chicago several times before, but this was my first time staying in the Homewood Suites. The homewood suites was nicer and more affordable than hotels I have stayed in previously.
My family and I were really impressed with the Homewood Suites. We had a - bedroom King suite. As mentioned before there was a full sized fridge and freezer, with a really fast ice maker, a dishwasher, and dishes including pots and pans. I really liked that there was door to shut the bedroom off from the living room. 
The room was really clean, we were on the --th floor which is a non-smoking floor, so there were not any musty, old smoky smells that you can sometimes get at hotels.
The free breakfast was great, much better than any other free breakfast I have ever had at a hotel. Hot scrambled eggs, sausage, bacon, potatoes, corned beef hash, fresh fruit in addition to typical cold breakfast options like bagels, donuts, muffins, cereal and yogurt. I have to say being able to start our day with a hot breakfast each day was great.
The staff was friendly, especially the doormen and valet parkers. We mentioned where we were going one day and they gave us directions to the closest place to get a CTA pass and then told us which bus we would need. 
Overall our experience was great and we are planning on staying here again.

This was the first time staying in a hotel over the Christmas holiday! The staff was very welcoming and attentive. Everytime we passed a the hotel staff we were always greeted us with a smile and a how is your stay? or a Hi! My kids especially loved eating smores by the firepits and swimming in the pools. The couples massage was WONDERFUL! It also great to have a state of the art fitness room to use to keep up with our workout! Thanks for an awesome stay!

The Peninsula Chicago is one of the nicest hotel facilities this hotel snob has visited in --+ years of travel. The room service, maid service, health club, beds, HVAC & room lighting are outstanding & exceptional.That's why it's such a shame one can hear those in adjacent rooms sneeze, cough, flatulate, argue & engage in sex. (Although not necessarily in that order).It's also shameful that the front desk ignored my -st request to change rooms. On the final day of my visit, after being kept awake from -am by the room next door's ongoing alarm buzzer, I was moved...but not before security personel were sent to confirm my complaint! Furthermore, this (former) repeat customer has not heard from anyone representing the property regarding his complaints or concerns in the month since this incident.Notwithstanding the exquisite facility, I prefer sleep to luxury.

My wife and I stayed at the W Austin July - thru July -. From beginning to end we were treated kindly and quickly. We were upgraded to a Spectacular King room, had a bottle of Proseco waiting for us, and were met with all questions answered helpfully and promptly. Tip: eat at Parkside on -th... the best quality eatery in Austin without pretense. We didn't watch any TV the first few nights, but the last one we wanted to watch some before sleeping as we had an early checkout on Sunday. The TV didn't work though! I spoke to the front desk who called some engineers. Two minutes later Jeff and Noel, from Engineering, knocked on my door to help. They assessed the issue, nicely asked how my wife and my stay has been, and fixed the problem. They were excellent ambassadors for what the W strives to be: the absolutely best customer service hotel out there. This was our first time, and not our last after this experience.

We were in town for a friend's wedding and stayed at the Hotel Commonwealth for just one night. Though only one night, we would absolutely stay at the hotel again and recommend it to anyone headed to Boston. It was in a great location- close to Fenway, BU and only a short walk to Newbury, Prudential Center, etc. It is also literally across the street from the Kenmore T stop. There were a number of restaurants-bars in the surrounding area. The hotel itself was lovely- rooms were spacious, clean and very comfortable. Staff were friendly and eager to assist with questions, recommendations, etc. All in all, an excellent stay.

The Villa Florence is in an excellent location, really close to Union Square and cable car terminus. We found the hotel staff to be extremely helpful in giving advice regarding transport tickets, directions, etc. There are plenty of places to eat within easy walking distance of the hotel. The kingsize rooms are very good and, as suggested by someone else, we requested quieter rooms away from Market and Powell. Valet parking service was very good - I saw cheaper parking within a few blocks of the Villa Florence, but we liked the flexibility of no in-out restrictions that valet parking gave us. It was only on the first day of our trip that we encountered a problem stopping outside the hotel - drove around the block a couple of times until a space opened up - otherwise, absolutely fine.

Stayed at the hotel for a business conference. WOW it was really great. The only down sides were the noise of the HVAC system, it was loud, the second was it was great to be able to open the window however the spring were broken and would slam down, could be very dangerous if you had you fingers on the ledge.
The room was a good size for an older hotel. They really did not spare any expense when they renovated. Bed was extremely comfortable, bathroom good size, great shower and towels. A MOST important need at any hotel is water pressure; it was great for the shower. Flat screen TV was nice and a good selection of stations. 
Hotel is close to everything that you could want, shopping, food, and entertainment.
Hotel help was also great, very friendly and accommodating.
Will come back to visit Chicago and stay here again.

We stayed at the Palomar for - nights during our trip to LA. We'd been to LA before so had a reasonable idea of what to expect about the hotel's location and local amenities. We walked everyday into Westwood village. It was a pleasant five to ten minute walk, and our kids did it easily and without complaint. Westwood has everything you need. and we had good access with our car to all of LA. The hotel is stylish but without being overbearing. We felt comfortable there. Staff were friendly and helpful. Our room on the top floor overlooked Wilshire Blvd. There is some traffic noise but nothing unbearable. After all, it's LA. In room facilities were good. With kids in tow, we kept the mini bar locked. Restaurant prices were reasonable. The happy hour with free wine between - and -pm was a nice touch. The only downside is the valet parking charge. But as we got a really good nightly rate for our rooms, by the time we added valet we were still in front of other comparable properties in the area. The pool area is great. Some reviewers have commented that it is only big enough for 'five or six people'. Don't know how big those people were, but the pool was ample for our kids and others to have a great time.

Stayed at hotel on anniversary trip to DC. Very near Union Station so no need for cab. Front Desk person, Liz Mitchell heard it was anniversary and upgraded us to suite for a small fee. What a great room with kitchenette, dining room and fireplace living room. Staff gave great help on transport around DC, Dining and discounts. this will be our DC headquarters from now on.

My favorite in SF. I've enjoyed at least -- stays at the Palomar over - years. The only reason I ever stay elsewhere is if I can't get a good rate there. It's often not cheap, but it's worth it to keep checking for a low rate. To be fair, a big part of why I love it is the location--right at the BART station, and - blocks from our HQ. But it's also because they really go out of their way to take care of their guests.
On my most recent stay, my day had gotten off to an awful start. Woke up to find my flight to SF cancelled, and I had to be there for an annual departmental meeting at noon. I arranged a replacement flight, but my cab no-showed, and I missed it. Another taxi to another airport, bad traffic, not enough time to check in; but I managed somehow, only to end up in the very back row next to a woman with a coughing brat in her lap. I got to the Palomar at --:--am. I stopped in, figuring I'd at least drop my bag and use a men's room. 
The clerk at the front desk asked how she could help me, so I asked if it were possible to check in, explaining that I knew it was very early, etc. While she was checking, she asked how my morning was going--so I told her the story. Well the room they had set aside for me wasn't ready, so she upgraded me. And I had half an hour to relax in a deluxe room before going to the meeting. Now I hadn't been to the hotel in over a year, and I had booked my room on their website at the cheapest special rate they offer all year. But I was able to go to my meeting in a good frame of mind because the Palomar took care of me. Will I stay there again? You beat--every time I can get a rate that won't alarm our auditors.

We had a decent experience with this hotel the year before so we came back this summer to relax and enjoy Philadelphia. We got a room in the dark end of the hall with a freaky busted door nearby. The hallways are dark and it gets kind of scary at night.
More specifically on the service and room itself:
There were MANY MANY things missing from our room. 
The large white comforter was missing and we didn't even receive a menu for room service. When we called in to get one, it was a photocopied booklet. 
The bed itself was disgusting. Two of the four pillows were dirty and had dark stains. The bottom most cover on the mattress (the one touching the mattress) had someone's hair on it and light stains all over it. I was afraid to inspect the rest of the bed. 
The closet was missing a rack. 
The shower curtain had mold growing on it. 
Housekeeper was nice and promised to bring us a comforter but that never arrived. 
Housekeeping forgot to provide and replace numerous things. 
The door handle got stuck a couple times and was hard to open. 
We only had one glass cup instead of the usual two.
Two towels instead of the usual ---. 
Personal complaint: a fridge was $-- a day?!!! microwave at lobby 
Pros: Concierge was great. :D
Overall, the general services provided were fine. It's just that our room was grossly lacking and just plain....gross. I should have taken pictures to submit here but I didn't think it would have been that bad for a -.- star hotel.

Ive stayed at the Wolcott - times now and i'd stay there again if i went back to New York. Its spot on for both price and location, your on the doorstep of the empire state building, and just a short walk from Time Square. You have the hop on hop off tour busses going past all the time if you wanted a great way to get around and see everything. The hotel offers you the basics that you need so you dont need to splash the cash on hotel and have less money for the other things on your trip. They offer a clean and comfortable hotel in a good location for a good price. They have the conciege service in the hotel and also a little shop where you can pick up drinks, snacks, newspapers, small gifts, postcards and pens etc. I'd recommend it to anyone who goes.

We stayed at this property - years ago and the hotel has fallen in terms of maintenance, we asked for a light to be replaced and it did not happen. The room was poorly maintained and the breakfast was not up to a best western plus standard!

Beautiful hotel which has a nice bar - restaurant downstairs as well as is attached to the copley square mall. Comfortable accomodations, and got an upgrade to a nice -BR suite. Very close to the Pru, trinity, etc.

My sister and I stayed here in August ----. Great location! Close to Times Square and great restaurants. Neighborhood was very quite. Lots of corner grocery shops for a quick snack. A liquor store was across the street. The room was well furnished, tastefully decorated and clean. Front desk staff slow and not too interested in helping guests. Overall a great stay. I would recommend this hotel.
Comfy bed and spacious room! We spent a night across the street at the Hotel Nikko before switching for better accomodations at the Hilton. Would be nice if they didn't charge for the gym...

Stayed two nights on a recent business trip. As previous entries stated, make sure to join the Kimpton Hotel rewards club. I was able to get free wi-fi, breakfast, and $-- to use towards the mini bar. The room decor was very nice and they have Aveda products, which I absolutely love! The staff were very nice. The only issue is that I was staying there when the heat was -- plus degrees. When I arrived, my room was set at the normal -- degrees. I lowered it, but it didn't seem to cool off. I mentioned this to the front desk the following morning and was told that they would have engineering take a look. Well, that never happened! The next night was even worse! It was cooler in the hallway than it was in my room. I couldn't wait to leave the room to check out. While I'm sure this is not the norm, it needs to be addressed. While I would recommend the hotel, I would check the weather and call ahead to make sure the air conditioning is working properly. Oh, great happy hour reception for guests that's free!

Stayed - nights and had a room on the -th floor on the street side. Room was large with large balcony. Staff was friendly and rooms were excellent. There couldn't be a better hotel or location near Beale street. Only negative would be the loud music playing late but hey, we were there for the music.

My wife and I spent four nights at Barton Creek recently and we really enjoyed the resort and Austin. The pros: terrific grounds, large rooms, friendly service, great golf, and tremendous workout facilities. Cons: the golf courses are not always available to resort guests, the food is very expensive, and there are few food choices close to the resort. Downtown Austin and its neighborhoods (South Congress, -th Street, Warehouse District) are about -- minutes away and a very easy drive. We will stay at Barton Creek on our next visit to Austin!

This is a really nice hotel in a great location. The staff is outstanding and the hotel is neat and clean. They did lose a package that was never found but verified delivered. I was out of luck on that one as the staff called and were at a loss on what to do. They have a nice fitness center that does not open early enough in the morning for early birds. Shulas, the restaurant downstairs is really good with great vibe. Pricey but does have a happy hour. Rooms were clean and updated. Usual amenities, no free Internet.

Renita the desk clerk was very helpful and kind. I got in at -am on Friday and the desk clerk really wasn't very helpful. All she did was hand me my key and pointed me to the elevator. Where as Renita told me everything that I needed to know on Sunday, July --, ----.

We just stayed at The Liaison and we're blown away by the the service..Simone and Jessica at the front desk were the most polite, friendly and professiona hotel representatives. We checked in Friday evening and we're told there was a problem with our room but without skipping a beat other accomidations were made. We were really impressed in how well the employes of the Liaison provide customer service. The rooms were Great, Clean and Very Comfortable. The pool on the roof was an added bonus. The hotel was very busy and filled to capacity but the staff made you feel that you were the only ones staying at the hotel. I would strongly reccommend this hotel to anyone looking for a great value that is conveinently located near Capitol Hill.
Thanks again for a wonderful expereince.......

This was our first stay at the Magnolia in Dallas. We’ve stayed at the Magnolia in Houston several times and could not resist the opportunity to try the Dallas property while there celebrating a birthday in late August. We had a “Guest Room” on the --th floor (no. ----) facing to the west with a view of Reunion Tower. The room was very spacious as was the bathroom with its separate tub and shower arrangement. The mattress and bedding were extremely comfortable. We had the opportunity to enjoy the complimentary evening glass of wine as well as a hot breakfast the next morning. The Dallas Magnolia location in Downtown was perfect for our needs as it was only a bit over two blocks to the nearest DART (Dallas Area Rapid Transit) train stop located on Pacific Ave. Though a few blocks further; it was also convenient for catching the free trolley service to the Uptown area of Dallas. To sum it up, the Magnolia never lets us down.

We stayed for one night at the Bryant Park at the end of July, in a room with two queen beds with our five-year old son. At first glance, of course, the Bryant Park seems more like a place for the hip and stylish underfed-model types, but the staff could not have been more pleasant and helpful. Upon our arrival, the manager went next door and fetched a delicious cupcake for our son as a welcome gift. When we returned to our room after a long, hot day of sightseeing, we were greeted by a handwritten welcome note, a bag of popcorn and a Spiderman book for our son (the manager had noticed he was carrying his Spiderman doll when we checked in). Not to mention chocolates on each pillow. I mean, it was almost over the top! As for the room, we couldn't have been more pleased--spacious, comfortable, tastefully decorated, and what have to be the largest marble bathrooms you're likely to find in NYC! Everything was extremely clean and well-maintained, and the bathroom towels were thick and fluffy. We got all this at a very reasonable price via hotels.com. I can't recommend this hotel highly enough.

This hotel is clean, quiet and comfortable. It is in a great location. Nearby in walking distance is Portillo's Hot Dogs, Gino's East, Giordanos, Al's #- Italian Beef, Garrett's Popcorn, Navy Pier, Water Tower area, groceries, gourmet groceries, movie theater, bowling alley, and lots of shopping.
Parking is adjacent and $--- day with In-Out priviledges.
Did not eat at the hotel but the menu looked good.
Swimming pool and gym are onsite.

I will definitely seek out Homewood Suites at all my travel destinations from now on, even tho I think they are just getting started and are few and far between. This was the nicest, and most comfortable, and affordable suite I have ever stayed in. Nicer than the suites that say they have a kitchen but it's only a fridge and microwave. This suite had a seperate kitchen with stovetop, microwave, full size fridge, cooking utensils, plates, silverware. And the room was big and comfortable, lots of drawers and closet space and my favorite and wish more hotels would do this-cabinets and drawers in the bathroom. I read a negative in another review that the walls are thin and you can hear your neighbors and this is true. I had a crying baby on one side and a very loud man on the other, but the AC fan drowned them out. My only complaint would be the lighting in the seperate shower room, it was pretty dim. But over all it was a very pleasant stay-I could live in that room comfortably! Nice area too, isolated-you don't hear all the traffic. There are grocery stores within a few blocks, easy access to the freeways. OH, and the internet was DSL, not wireless, which was a bit of a pain.

We usually stay at one of the W Hotels in New York but we wanted to save some money and stayed at the Hampton Inn and we were pleasantly surprised! The staff was super friendly (especially compared to the hipper-than-thou staff at the W) and the room was huge (again, when compared to the W). The hotel was recently renovated and our room was very clean. We used priceline.com to book the room and paid about $--- less than the rack rate and so we feel like we got a fair price. The parking garage next door charges $-- a day, which is a good deal. The only downside was that the hotel was crowded with the fanny-pack wearing crowd but what do you expect for a hotel near Times Square?
I was in Houston for business and stayed at this hotel. It was good value for the money and was comfortable and clean. I liked the bed and the pool was nice and warm. i would stay again.

Located above a Metro stop, this was an excellent place to stay with easy access to the Smithsonian on foot or the Metro Rail to anywhere in the city. Our family of - traveled with my parents and we all had rooms on the --th floor where the pool is located. Our room had obviously been sufficiently used by families. The sliding glass door to the pool area did not slide and could only be fully opened and closed by my husband, but it granted us direct access to the pool. My parents were in a room on the opposite side of the floor and their door worked reasonably well. The drawers in our room no longer had functioning glides, but all the drawers in my parents' room worked well. Our AC fan was much louder than theirs. Overall, the staff was friendly and the accommodations comfortable, but I can certainly see why the reviews vary. One unusual thing for us was that the food court in the lower level near the Metro was only open M-F during commuter hours.

If your looking for a hotel for convience to shopping at Easton then this is a good pick. Somewhat pricey compared to properties outside the shopping zone but it's location and very hospitable staff make up for it. Payed $---.-- a night over a two day weekend. The Hilton (nice looking property) was much higher and the Residence (which is right next door and just a shade closer to shopping) was $--.-- cheaper a night but they didn't have a king bed. The only reason I can not give this property a perfect score was that the heating and air conditioning sysytem sounded like a cooling system for a -- wheeler milk truck running next to my bed. so we thru an extra blanket on the bed the following night to cure the noise problem. A very clean nice hotel, will return.

I stayed here from the --th of June to July -rd. I've got to say I was very impressed with this hotel. There was a rustic chic ambiance about the place. Though it is very dark, it carried the appropriate vibe that they were trying to sell. I personally don't think it's too family friendly. Very nice, clean Hotel! The staff was super friendly and helpful! Our room was roomy and comfy. We will stay here again!!

I was a bit hesitant when placing my booking due to some of the negative reviews here, but after our recent - night stay, I was glad I did. The Gotham comedy club is next door, the - subway is on the corner, with the E train a block away (perfect for subway trip from JFK) and the M-- bus station is right outside . Cnr -f --st and -th ave so a great location slap bang in the centre of Manhattan.

I stayed in the Pod Hotel for two weeks. It's a nice place, stylish interior design, good service, good price. The only disadvantage: the rooms are really, really small. But that's OK, given all the benefits of the location and price.

From the first phone call to the property we knew our stay wouldn't be all that great. The person answering didn't sound too friendly; he was gruff, short, and didn't seem to want to talk.

Final thought: you get what you pay for. Wished we would've paid more for better customer service and accommodations. We will NOT be coming back to the Town House again.

Spent a week on holiday at this hotel which has some terrific features but also some that need improving.
The positives
- great location, lovely part of Boston, - min walk to Prudential Centre, T line, shops and lovely streets to explore
- space of suites is a nice change from tiny hotel rooms, kitchen is well equipped, nice shower
- friendly and helpful staff
- windows that can be opened, even if it means more street noise
The negatives
- serious problem of lack of soundproofing between rooms. We could hear people in the adjacent suite - talking (not shouting), television, coughing, snoring, as well as thudding footsteps from the floor above. Can't image how you would survive with a crying baby or amorous activities next door.
-decor and furnishings which may seem stylish, were uncomfortable. Two-seater couch and hard armchair in lounge area were excruciatingly uncomfortable, and with the large screen TV mounted high on the wall, we had cricked sore necks in no time. Four poster bed in the small bedroom was ridiculous and a hazard - we had to be very vigilant to avoid colliding with the posts when negotiating around such a small room.
- heating-cooling fan was one speed only, and very noisy and breezy when on. We hardly used it as the weather was mild, but it would have been very unpleasant and impossible to escape the gale if we had needed to use it.
On balance, the positives probably outweigh the negatives, but be aware that you are at the mercy of noise from next door and above. Bring earplugs - they may help.

Bottom line, the Hotel Helix is visually interesting, but it's location and limited amenities probably would preclude me from recommending this hotel.

Coffee, a variety of teas, cold and hot water, as well as ice and a bowl of fruit are available ---- in the lobby. There are doorbells for each room, and the hotel can only be accessed after hours if you havea key card. Floors are acessible with a keycard as well, for extra protection. Staff is very polite: one of the few places where someone will actually say """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""good morning"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to you in the city. (NO, seriously). They're also extremely helpful. When I checked in the night before, the gentleman at the reservation desk called to make sure I had a cab waiting for me at -:-- the next morning so that I could make my speaking engagement on time. While I was gettingmy clothes ready, my iron was making more wrinkles than it was taking out, so I asked them for a new one and within -- seconds later I had a brand new one with all the bells and whistles.
I've read a few reviews talking about the noise level of this place. My room was closest to the reception desk and I never heard a peep. There were people out and about, but I didn't hear a thing. 
A few things to note:
Its location on a tight one way street can cause a little difficulty if you're traveling solo, but if you have one person to unload the car while someone else parks, you should be fine. The parking garage they use is about half a block from the hotel, but you have to drive in a big rectangle to get there. 
There's a stand-up shower instead of the traditional bathtub-shower combo. It fits one comfortably enough... provided that you're not too far from average height and build. (My boyfriend is -'- with a football player build and he made out okay.)
Don't expect much of a view. The view from our room was of the side of another building. But that's what the city is for... go out there and see something!
Overall, this was an excellent trip and a great find. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone.

I stayed at the Indigo Dallas Downtown on the last days of a holiday to the US, and was really happy I did. The establishment is modern, cheerful, and near enough to the centre of the Dallas downtown area. All staff I encountered were friendly, attentive and helpful, while my apartment was well appointed.
Very comfortable bed, quiet room, fantastic shower, LCD TVs in both rooms, and lavish (yet somehow calming) blueberry wallpaper behind the bed somehow added a nice touch. Complementary wi-fi came in very handy too! All in all, a very nice way to end a holiday in the USA.

My brother and I went on a mini vacation. We lived here in Queens. When I saw this new hotel I did not know much but after meeting the staff and seeing the rooms I was so happy. It was a home away from home. 
I had to get use to the thin walls and noise but the bathrooms, the dining area for breakfast and were so clean and nice. I loved it.
The door man and the security staff made my brother and I feel welcome. I want to especially single out Andy the nicest bellman I ever met so friendly and nice. Also Sunny a wonderful concierge who made me feel so happy. Also the lovely Ladies at concierge who helped with travel tips Thank you Ladies and finally I can not forget the wonderful young staff of helpers in the dining area what wonderful young people who work so hard.
You all do a great job. Especially Stephanie, Francesca and many more. Thank you all.
Great hotel and made me feel so special.
Thank you to the Security guy John what a nice person made me feel comfortable and safe.
Bravo to all.
Thank you.

I stayed at the Strand on ----------------. This is best described as an upscale boutique hotel. They allowed me to check in several hours early, gave a free upgrade, and the room was so nice.
