About - blocks from Bryant Park, - minute walk from Penn Station, and between -th and -th so a great location.

I am a tour operator based in Toronto. I have been using The Hollywood Hotel exclusively for my LA-bound clients for several years. Its location and value are incomparable in LA. What is especially good about this hotel, though, is its staff and management. Without going into detail, I give a special thanks to Nelson Garnero for going above and beyond. Two thumbs-up for The Hollywood Hotel.
Andrew L

Rooms are a bit dated, and the valet parking price is outrageous, but the staff is amazingly accommodating to any request. Every room has a balcony! Hilton is refurbishing this property and I look forward to future visits.

The food in Brasserie was excellent. I ate there for breakfast on June --, ----. BabbeHee Shade I thought she was outstanding. Griselda Gavino server was very professional. BabbeHee Shade had all her staff working as a team.

I am very surprised to see so many people writing """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""clean"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in the reviews. That was not my room. 
I had a room on the -rd floor, with musty, stained carpets, old paint and fixtures. It was not pleasant. 
No heat in the room - I used the built-in hairdryer to warm up enough so I could fall asleep. 
But the final insult was the gym. When I finally found it, it was a sad """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""check the box we have a gym"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" gym - tiny, stuffy, depressing room with - treadmills. Then neighborhood is not great for a run, very downtown urban, but that was all I had. I ran up to Knob HIll, and the view from California street was the best part of the stay. 
Come back to Mark Twain after they've renovated.

Stayed here for - nights during this year's Austin Marathon back in February...been meaning to write a review since. Location is great, rooms are decent. Though I have split feelings about the service. Housekeeping seemed to be completely disconnected from the folks at the front desk. Each day, housekeeping either did not leave behind shampoo-cond replacements and-or did not replace our bedding-sheets. There was one day, we left in the morning and came back early evening to find our room had not been attended to at all. When we complained or called down to the front desk, however, they were kind, apologetic and even compensated us with SPG points (helps to be a SPG member). Regardless, I expect more from a Starwood property and its hotel manager. I hope housekeeping has since gotten their act together with the proper oversight and management by the manager.
The room was not available when we checked in and there was no crib in the room as we had requested. The lobby is awfully tacky, the staff handled our concerns with casual disregard.

The hotel was crowded with several events going on at the same time. Check-in took a while and it was evident some of the staff felt overwhelmed. The rooms were nice with a great view of downtown. When we got to our room, there were no towels, and it took a while to get them to our room. There was no free internet service, which for a business hotel is very odd, and hopefully will be corrected soon. The hallways were loud, but there was a staff person who came up and controlled the situation in a timely manner. Comfort seemed to be a priority for the staff.

Taylor Hotel was just as many have described. I walked in the smallish lobby at midnight and was underwhelmed. However, the next day I realized that it is very close to everything I needed. It was clean and had some remodeling in the bathroom. It was exactly what I would expect out of a hotel this price in Downtown SF. There are much ritizier hotels, yes, but you will pay. The owners were nice and helpful, kids were nosy, and the place was safe. There were a couple of long term residents that were especially friendly but I enjoyed the free internet service when it was unoccupied and I liked the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""continental breakfast"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". But don't be fooled it is just prepackaged donuts and some coffee. It was a nice start to my morning and I took a couple for the trip to the airport so all in all I would recommend staying here if you are on a budget!

Staying at the Novatel was a pleasant surprise since it was the first time for us in NYC. We stayed there from March -- to March --. It has a convenient location and surprisingly quiet despite it's location near Times Square. We went to see Hairspray at the Neil Simon Theater which was so close that the line extended out the door of the hotel so as soon as we exited we were in line. Service was excellent. Only problem, unlike most hotels these days, coffee maker was not provided. We normally have to get a cup of coffee to warm up and get our engine running.

This hotel tends to get mixed reviews and I guess people ask the question, who's opinion is right? I think the answers is that they are probably all correct depending on how much you pay and what room you are assigned.
I'd like to start by saying that if it's a good location you want then you couldn't do better. Not only is this Hotel on Union Square it is in fact the finest building on Union Square so you feel you really are staying in a true piece of American history. The lobby area is very traditional and has a real feel of turn of the century style without being dated (If you're looking for straight lines and minimalism or Ikea styling then look elsewhere).
The luck of the draw comes with your room assignment as far as I can see. Myself and a friend both got rooms at the Westin St Francis, I upgraded to a traditional tower room and he got a standard in the old building. The room in the old building was tired and in real need of upgrading while I found the tower to be very comfortable and spacious. I think you'd have a right to feel let down if you paid full price and ended up with a standard room in the old building with a view of a wall.
With regard to descriptions like 'heavenly bed' I must say I find these descriptions to generally be over the top but I must say that it is one very comfortable bed so I wouldn't argue too much about that. The room also had a nice large lcd tv with high definition channels and very good air conditioning which unlike many other hotels keeps your room at the same temperature throughout the day rather than you returning to the room and waiting an age for it to become comfortable again.
 The staff were also excellent and could not be faulted so I find it a little disappointing that whenever anyone has anything negative to say about the hotel on this web site the hotel representative seems to cut and paste a paragraph out of a hotel brochure as a reply rather than address the issue. I found the staff on the ground to be far more attentive than this.
I would certainly recommend this hotel if you get the right room at the right price which I did so I'd like to thank the Westin st Francis for a very good stay.
The Anadaz has great rooms and very good service. staying just a day later in the Mark in NY, the comparison made the Andaz seem even better.

I have just returned from a wonderful stay at this hotel during my fall break. I must start by saying that I found my room to be a bit smaller than I am used to, but it was clean and nicely decorated. The staff is professional , helpful and friendly. I packed in a lot for the two days that I stayed, so I utilized room service for a couple meals. The meals are a bit pricey, but the portions were large enough for me to save for later. Pro: there is a refrigerator; con: there is no microwave. All in all, I found this hotel to be an excellent value for the prime location. I walked to almost all of the attractions (white house, capitol, Lincoln memorial, MLK memorial, Jefferson memorial and many museums). I took the metro to the National Zoo.An added plus is that they stored my bags after I checked out so that I could continue touring. Excellent service...I will be back!

My wife, - year old son and I stayed for - nights. The hotel lobby was nice and the people were friendly. 
The room (harborview) left something to be desired - peeling wallpaper and missing knobs on the dressers. Very noisy due to traffic and metal sheets on the road. The hotel provides a small breakfast buffet, which was a nice touch - especially considering that there didn't seem to be many alternatives in the area. No pool or gym onsite. Room service from a local restaurant but almost exclusively seafood. Parking was expensive, especially considering that the lot was empty.
I travel --- times a year, so I've stayed in a few hotels - many firsts at this one:
This was the first time I've seen maids come to make up the room at -:----pm - just when we were there resting and getting ready to go out for dinner. This happened every day except the day we checked out - on that day they were knocking on the door at -:-- am!!!
First time I've had to go to the desk to ask for bathroom tissue.
First time I've seen a line of - people-couples at a hotel front desk.
First time I've ever seen and paid a $-.-- daily """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""destination charge."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" This was a surprise when we checked in. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""destination charge"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" supposedly includes internet access, copies, etc. - none of which I used. Overall the trip was nice despite the hotel. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Waterfront Invasion"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" package is a great deal for a long weekend with kids. The location of the Wyndham in San Francisco is just fantastic. One block from the beginning of the cable car ride, and across the street from some fantastic shopping. The hotel itself is very appealing, clean and comfortable and the staff very helpful. We were travelling with my daughter and grandaughters and wanted rooms that were close by. When we arrived the first night, we were quite late and that was not possible. The next morning we were able to switch rooms and we were placed in a beautiful room right next to my daughter on the --th floor with a fantastic view of San Francisco by night. Because we were on the --th floor, this gave us access to the --th floor club which served a continental breakfast every monring, serve hors d<oeuvres at - p.m. and desert at l- p.m. We found this very appealing and was well worth the extra few dollars. 
There is a concierge on location who knew her stuff and was very very helpful in discussing with us the many things there are to see and do in San Francisco. Her tips were very useful for our stay. All in all staying at the Wyndham was a wonderful experience and I would definitely stay there again if I go back to San Fran. This experience has made me want to stay in other hotels owned by this Chain.

The location of this hotel is really brilliant...but beware...if you get a room with a window on --th street, you will be up all night because of traffic noise and horns honking. Try and ask for a room away from the noise and also ask for a renovated room. We asked to be moved after our first sleepless night. It took a few times to get a polite hotel receptionist but finally someone took pity on us and we moved to a nicer bigger and quieter room which we really appreciated

The hotel location to historic Phildelphia was fantastic as well as convenient. The area is filled with things to do, great restaurants, Penns Landing (boat cruises) and history filled attractions.
Prea, the front desk manager or June,the Hotel manager will be happy to help.

We planned to stay in this hotel for two nights in september but after checking in we soon changed our minds! Every hotel was booked out in New York for the nights we needed because George Bush was in town but even that didnt stop us demanding a refund and leaving the Carter hotel. When we checked in at -- pm we were allocated a room and told it may not be serviced but to go on up and it would be serviced as soon as possible. i work in a hotel, and to me this seemed crazy! checking somebody in to an unserviced rooms is madness, how do they know that there arnet dirty needlees or used condoms still in the room!. When we got to the room the bed had been slept in and the bathroom clearly had been used so we left our stuff in the corner, adivsed reception we wanted our room serviced asap and left to go out for the day. The more we looked around the hotel the worse it got, broken fire exit signs, rubbish strewn all over the place, live cables hanging out of plug sockets and -- + guests talking in recpetion about the rat problem! apart from that the whole hotel smelt like a dodgy kebab house and the manager was walikng around with his shoes off, drunk threatening to throw guests out who dared to complain! Attended Open House and Tour of facilities and very impressed with it's upgrades and improvements under new management. Will continue to recommend to family, friends and colleagues. Will consider for a holiday party or special event.

the rooms were very,veey nice. it is unfortunate that the staff was so rude and not helpful at all. for instance when we were checking in our bags the bell boy got upset because he thought we said to check in - bags when we said -. not a big deal right? well he was quite upset and was mad that he had to tag another bag. it was just funny because it was his job and not only that but we had to tip him for his rude services. i would recommend this to a friend because the rooms are so nice, but warn them of what to expect from the not so nice staff.

Myself and my wife travelled from the UK and this was our first visit to New York . I booked this hotel on reviews that I had read on Tripadvisor. We were not disappointed, this is an excellent choice.
The Affinia is in a fantastic location. Easy walking distance to Empire State, Macy’s, Grand Central Station. In fact you can comfortably walk to Times Square but it was so hot whilst we were there, this was like torture.
There are many Delis, Cafés & Restaurants nearby so you don’t have to stray far for food. The Murray Hill market is just next door and they make great hot & cold sandwiches ----. This shop is well stocked for just about everything – except wine. You need to travel a little further if you want a nice relaxing bottle for your room.
The check-in at Affinia was smooth and very friendly. We had reserved a Junior Suite and when I mentioned to the girl at the check in that we would like a good view of Manhattan she immediately swapped us to an end room, where you get a two sided view. This was no problem, and no extra cost. We were on floor -- so were above many of the buildings in the neighbourhood. 
On entry the room was very clean and had been well prepared. There are IMHO a couple of minor niggles with this type of room, but we will get to them later. The view of the Manhattan skyline was fantastic. The facilities of the room were excellent with a handy well equipped kitchen, big bathroom and comfortable King bed and living space. This all made for a very relaxing stay. However I thought that the room was set up more for a business traveller than a holiday stay. The wardrobe was tiny and nowhere near fitted our clothes. Bearing in mind that this stay was part of a - week North American trip we had a lot of stuff with us. I use hotels for business all the time and the space was quite adequate for a short business trip. The business theme is further enhanced by a large double desk and office chair. Again, this is fine for business but not much use for us. Just takes up room. I realise that the Affinia has to cater for both markets, that is why the room was set up like this. The only other niggle was a very efficient but noisy AC unit. Boy, did we use this as it was --F on some of the days. When the AC unit was on it was noisy and we left it on all night. This may have troubled a light sleeper, but not us.
The hotel staff are top notch. They are very friendly and knowledgeable and will offer help and advice on any matter that you care to ask. They do not fuss, which is also good. The doormen are so helpful and will flag down taxis or book you a town car at a moments notice. They have full internet access at a PC in the lobby – you have to pay. They also have internet available on the in room T.V.’s and also wireless connection.
The hotel is very clean and the cleaners are a real friendly bunch who always chat to you. The standard of room cleaning every day was first class.
As for food, we ate breakfast most days at Austin’s Café, which I can recommend. This is left out of the Affinia, across the street and then up , about a block and a half towards the Empire State. Lots of choice here, from breakfast sandwiches, omelettes to vegetarian and freshly sweezed juices. The staff here are pleasant and can understand an English accent, which we found was a rare skill in NYC. 
The Barking dog restaurant (next to Affinia) was another story. They employ pleasant young eastern European girls for FOH and waitress but they just do not understand enough English. We were all laughing trying to communicate. They understand the American accent and phrases fine but not English. When I ordered a draught beer, they were confused. When I mentioned “Starter” & “Main Course” they had no idea what I was talking about. They only know what it says on the menu. Appetizer and Entrees. We ate there on the first night and even with the language issue we had a nice meal. Our Russian waitress was very polite and eager to learn and we taught her a little English on the fly.The second occasion(our last night) was a different story. It was very busy, the Romanian waitress spoke poor English and did not write the order down. You can imagine what happened next. My starter (er Appetizer) arrived after -- mins wait and then the Main Course arrived straight after. I had to sit there and finish my starter looking at my steak going cold. The Main Course was only luke warm so it had been stood a while. I complained to the waitress saying that I had never before had a Main Course delivered whilst eating the starter. “Really?” she replied and smiled. Probably didn’t understand me. These issues could all be solved with decent staff training, which obviously doesn’t happen. An altogether unsatisfactory visit.
Room service is another story and we used this only once to eat and they were quick and efficient.
Another good help is that the Affinia will arrange a town car to pick you up at the airport. You pay the driver direct, either cash or card, and it is only around $-- more than a yellow cab. This worked great for us as the driver was at JFK to meet us and because all the town cars were out, we got a stretch limo for the same price. You can email the Affinia customer services to book this before you travel. They set it all up.
All in all a great trip and a great stay at the Affinia. We were sad to leave and will definitely return before too long.

Stayed here for a conference.
Very nice hotel, large rooms, great location. Rooms are clean and quite. Gym is excellent....pool is ok. They also have a small sundeck.
Service was excellent...even cleaning staff go out of their way to say hello.
On site resturants are average. Parking is a little stiff at $-- a day.
Lots of cabs to take you anywhere downtown.

My home-away-from-home, On The Ave is the best and only place I stay when visiting New York City. The staff are so friendly, rooms so clean, bed so comfortable with fresh fluffy down comforters and high thread-count sheets, sleeping soundly is a treat! I highly recommend On The Ave to anyone who wants a delightful stay in New York City.

My stay at this location was very good. Conveniently located to the convention center and other downtown restaurants - activities. The hotel staff were on top of their game with great services. My room's decor was very pleasant and relaxing. I will stay here again.

We stayed at the Affinia -- from July --, ---- through August -, ----. From the doorman as you entered to the front desk personnel, extremely friendly and they go out of their way to be helpful! I was put off by location at first since we have stayed on Broadway in past BUT it was a refreshing change to NOT have all the noise and commotion of Broadway every time you stepped out your door! You do have to walk approximately -- blocks to Times Square-Broadway area but again you are in NYC, you walk alot :-) The rooms were spacious and clean, the bed and bedding were perfect! A-C could have been a little colder, we were thankful that it wasn't unbearable outside. There was some noise from -rd St and from other rooms but not un-bearable. For the money we saved staying at the Affinia -- we were able to spend elsewhere AND the hotel, rooms and personnel were all awesome! Stay @ The Affinia --, we will again!

This is a magnificent, ornate hotel built in the grand days of the early --'s and frequented by Hollywood's elite. The interior architecture is fantastic, yet it is plenty modern. The room was big enough and was comfortable with space enough to work, but it sure could have used a mini fridge. The in-hotel restaurant was a little pricey, but common for that area. I was there for a convention and the facilities were spectacular. Seeing the historical pictures on the wall of Oscar ceremonies and balls was pretty interesting. The hotel was convenient to the subway and many downtown venues and restaurants.

This was my -rd time staying at this hotel, for a conference. The experience has been consistently very good. I'm maybe a bit spoiled, because with my Marriott status I can get free wireless and a top-floor room near the lounge. The view is wonderful and the lounge is pleasant with great food options including meats, cheeses, and fruits for breakfast, etc. The rooms are on the small side - I had a king, only for two people max, and two cozy people at that! - but very well appointed. The staff was courteous and helpful, going above and beyond to sort it out when there was an issue with my reservation. This is a wonderful area just - blocks down from Metro Center and with many restaurants and sights in walking distance, as well as the Warner theater. I recommend this hotel for business or pleasure, but, probably not for families.

I stayed here for one week and had a king room --th floor at the end of hallway. First I would say that the required $-- per night valet parking is outrageous and the outdated decor is a major turn off. My room was kinda cramped and the sheets were dirty so that wasn't what I signed up for. Also the doors are very loud and careless people have a tendency to constantly slam them which can be easily heard in your own room. The positive was that the bathroom was fairly big, the bed was comfortable, and the location is pretty close to all of the east -th street craziness but the bums are attracted to that area as well.
PS- The internet service comes & goes and the elevator is a hassle.

The Library Hotel is truly a unique hotel, an excellent idea that actually works. The idea of a library. For a person with literary inclinations it's the ideal hotel with impecable service and excellent staff. Although the internet made the library a lost paradise, New York shows ther can be a slice of paradise for any person that strives towards a world of culture. 
The rooms can feel a bit small, as the area is not known for massive and roomy accommodations, but the books in the rooms ( yes, there are books in the room, as you can choose which type of room you want according to the books in it ) give you a different perception of space. The bathrooms are great and, oddly enough, pretty large and uncrowded, as the hotel offers amenities galore, and whatever isn't in your room, the staff would gladly help with. While there the restaurant was closed, but the second floor reading room, a sort of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""club level lounge"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" found in luxury chain hotels, was a great little spot for snacks, or a light breakfast, always packed with goodies, both for the stomach and for the brain, as a piano sits in one corner of the room surrounded by books and magazines with a gorgeous view of the street. The staff at the desk and all around are more than happy to help you, and even to give you free stuff ( thanks for the coffee mugs guys ). There's no reason to talk about cleanliness because it goes without saying that it's a great boutique hotel. Maybe they need a better pencil provider because they tend to break easily. We had stayed at Morgan's and Affinia Dumont while on the same long trip, and both had been just as spectacular ( morgan's breakfast place Asia de Cuba is probably better than the second floor lounge here, but there's an assumption that they served it there because of the restaurant closing ; affinia dumont's rooms were huge compared to here ) but there was an extra something at the Library Hotel. Maybe it was the fact that a couple of the guys working at the front desk were originally from Romania, or maybe it was because of a bias towards books. But all three deserve - stars, with the Library hotel deserving a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""+"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" at the end.

It doesn't look very special from the outside and lacks a bit of charm in places, but I think that's to be expected from a chain hotel.
The rooms were lovely - spacious, clean, very comfortable and some nice touches.
The restaurant and bar were very nice too with really good food, a hawaaiian feel and great service - breakfast and dinner, and you might as well eat in as there isn't much else nearby unless you head into the Gaslamp Quarter which has a fabulous selection of restaurants and bars, catering for all tastes so definitely worth the trip. It isn't too far away, just not walking distance.
If you do stay in, the bar offers good cocktails but if you look anywhere under -- be prepared to be asked for ID, and they'll want passports as apparantely driving licenses are easy to fake in nearby Mexico!
(Note: if anyone tries to persuade you to go to Tijuana in Mexico - it took us hours to get there, we walked down one street full of tat, ate the worst food I have ever tasted and then took hours to get back - personally I wouldn't recommend it, other than to say you went to Mexico!)
The hotel shop wasn't up to much, it was about the size of a box and usuallly closed, but the heated pool and jacuzzi were pleasant - even in November!
Plenty of parking but you do have to pay $-- per night to do so which I wouldn't really expect if you were a paying guest.

Being a local Austinite, and having experienced most hotels in town (stay-cations); I have to say- this is THE BEST hotel in Austin. You get elite customer service from the minute you pull your car up to the valet, not to mention, the entire hotel is waiting to welcome your stay. The interior is stellar and stunning, not to mention comfortable yet chic. The W has a way of providing such psychical ease and class you can't find anywhere else, I swear its such a treat to stay there! 
Upon my most recent visit, I stayed in a suite with my (now) husband for our wedding weekend. We also recommended the W to all of our wedding guests. We had the BEST view in our plush cool corner suite. My bridesmaids and I were able to get our hair and makeup done, while hanging out and having fun in the luxury suite. The following day after our wedding, we had scheduled brunch at the Trace restaurant. WOW, what service, the staff in the restaurant was MORE than accommodating and welcomed our large party with open arms, as well as delicious roasted chickpeas (holy addiction!) This hotel is converted apartments. All have a kitchenette, sitting area and a comfortable bed. I would definately recommend this hotel. The staff was very accommodating (I came down a few minutes after the breakfast buffet ended but they were able to get me something). Can't say enough good things about the staff.

I stayed at the Homewood Suites Riverwalk a few weeks ago. I was in town for a conference, and this hotel was the closest one nearby that I could afford (my employer only reimburses up to $----night.

 Each suite has a full kitchen-living room, bathroom, and bedroom. They are very roomy and comfortable.

I do have one gripe, and that is that my room was apparently right above where the dumpsters are located. This was a beautiful hotel, the service was outstanding, and the room and views were spectacular. I woiuld highly recommend!!!

I saw many complaints on this hotel after I booked it, so naturally I was worried. However, when I got there the employees were very nice. 
Our room was ready immediatly, and extremely clean, and I am somewhat of a clean freek. It came with topsheets and all. Yes the rooms were small, and it was a little noisy, but hey its San Francisco. Anyhow, I would stay here again and do recommend it.

We stayed here for just under a week and didn't want to go back home! Although its a little bit dark inside, my wife and I both enjoyed the clean, urban, and quirky design of the Smyth. The rooms were immaculate and the staff was extremely attentive. From the moment we got out of our cab until we were settled in our room, we had the personal attention of a bellboy. Our only complaint would be with regards to the hotel restaurant-Plein Sud-the food was a bit on the bland side and generally overpriced. Nevertheless, we will certainly stay at the Smyth next time we're back in NYC

I booked this hotel from the rave reviews posted on tripadvisor. Upon arrival, the receptionist was quite abrupt and not friendly. But it seemed that new yorkers I have met there adopt this sort of nature. 
The room I was given was near the emergency fire exit stairs. And the room smelt like cigarettes. I requested a non-smoking room and told the staff but said that it was a non-smoking room. The room was very small. The toiletbowl was not clean properly when I came, but other than that it was quite clean. it had good cable TV which was good.

There was free internet but because there are so many people in the hotel, i had to wait for ages for it as there were only two computers. 
It was difficult to sleep because i was near the fire exit, so heard the door slam quite a bit and I was near the elevator so heard many noises. 
Because hotels are so expensive in New York, this would be the suitable alternative but I would not go there again for the price I paid which is --- dollars a night. I would try to find another hotel.

My partner and i stayed in this hotel for - week. When we arrived we were informed that the hotel was overbooked due to flight cancellations and that we had to stay in the Blakely hotel across the road for our first night only, due to the inconvenience caused they upgraded us to a queen room the next day.
I dread to think the size of the double rooms in this hotel, the queen was very small. Considering we were there for a week i expected to at least have a fridge and tea & coffee making facilities in the room, but i requested a fridge and it was brought to my room straight away at no extra charge.
The room was clean and serviced every day, although the room facilities were disappointing the bed was really comfortable and the location of the hotel is excellent. We didn't spend much time in the hotel so location was of more importance to us, - mins from Times Sq and - mins to Central Pk.

Our first stop on our tour of the South was in Chicago at the Red Roof Inn. I was a little surprised to find quiet a small room when I opened the door. The room was ok and seems clean enough. Stayed - nights here while at a conference for work. Location a block from Powell St. Station is ideal. My room was much bigger than most, yet the bathroom was extremely small. Room faced courtyard which is great in this part of the city since I'd gladly sacrifice view for quiet. Rooms are looking a little shabby from age but bedding is great. The Monticello is definitely a step down from other Kimpton Hotels and is also reflected in the staff which seem much less experienced than other Kimpton Hotels. Just returned from Seattle visit & --night stay at Hotel Andra. We had a --bed corner room on -th floor facing -th Ave (per request). The room & closet were both large. We easily walked to the Seattle Center & Space Needle, and to Myrtle Edwards Park & Sculpture Park on the waterfront. There were many restaurants & grocery stores within easy walking distance. Fortunately, we discovered nearby Top Pot Doughnuts on the last day or else we'd be several pounds heavier!

My husband and I stayed at the Hotel --- in early October. We were just in town for two nights to do a bit of sightseeing (and eating!). Neither of us had been to Boston before so we were looking for a nice, clean hotel that was convenient to everything we wanted to do, however, we didn't want to blow our budget. Hotel --- was a great compromise in the Back Bay area. The bathroom and shower were pretty small, but I wasn't expecting a luxury hotel, so we made do. The service was excellent and the staff were professional and courtious. I couldn't have asked for a better place to stay for the price and area!

This hotel is in an excellent location, within walking distance of the theater district, many restaurants, and great Chicago sites.
The management is exceptional.
The room was very, very clean and quiet.
I recommend this hotel to business persons traveling to Chicago and to couples.

Stayed here for NYE. Checked into the hotel and had to go outside to a different building to get to our room. There was no soap-shampoo-conditioner in the shower. Had to call the front desk twice. Finally housekeeping arrived with shampoo and conditioner only (no soap). Even though it did not seem like there were a lot of rooms on our floor, we heard constant banging doors all night. Upon check-out I questioned them multiple times on our room service charges - - breakfasts cost $--- (for a $-- and $-- breakfast). After the third time arguing with them they realized the waiter had put our room number (#----) as the tip! Then it took almost -- minutes for the valet to pull the car up. All in all, not a great experience

Hotel Icon is a very nice boutique hotel in downtown Houston. The building is beautiful, I believe it was a bank at one time, and you can still see the old vault behind the reception area. There are various room configurations, so make sure you know what you are getting when you book. They have accessible rooms, which is great if you require this access, but not so great if you don’t need it. There is no pool at this hotel, and they have no agreements with any local hotels for access to their pool. It would have been nice for a cool down after a hot day, but not a deal breaker, if you're there on business.
I found my room to be clean and the furnishings in excellent condition. I had a corner room, so I had lots of windows and light. The ceilings are nice and high, which adds to the feeling of space. There is a large desk, and Wi-Fi is free, so it’s great for business travelers. I had a very comfortable King bed in my room and the pillows were OK, but they did get a bit flat after a few hours, so I had to use two. 
The TV reception was sketchy – most of the lower channels were all snow, and there were not too many to choose from.
The bathroom was huge! My bathroom had a large walk-in shower, but no tub. The water pressure was good, and I never ran out of hot water. There was a standard shower head and a rain shower fixture. A colleague was also staying at this hotel, and she had a tub in her bathroom, so it sounds like there are multiple bathroom configurations, too. Shampoo, conditioner and body wash are in a dispenser, and a bar of soap is included for the sink area. Good sized vanity, with lots of space for toiletries, and a lighted makeup mirror. You can get a hair dryer on request.
I was here for a conference, and I found the hotel staff friendly and helpful, the room clean and well suited for my needs, and the location convenient for everything I needed to do. 
There is a restaurant at the hotel - The Line & Lariat. It is a really nice restaurant, and the food is very good. Breakfast is great and the service at breakfast was exemplary. Lunch service is at the bar, and was also excellent. I had the crab cakes for lunch and they were really good.
Diner service, however, leaves a lot to be desired. I was seated promptly by the hostess, who had a bright, beautiful smile, and served me my water right away. -- minutes later, I had lots of time to peruse the small menu, but I still hadn’t seen a server. While the menu is not large, it does have good variety, with some unusual dishes tossed in. The supervisor finally came over and took my order, apologizing for the waitress who was quite busy. I found this rather strange, as there was a large conference in town, and there were lots of attendees staying at the hotel. You would think they would have made sure their staffing levels were sufficient to properly serve guests. Anyway, I ordered the Bryan Farms chicken, which was delicious. About -- minutes after my order was taken, my server walked by an introduced herself on the way by. No apology for the slow service, just her name (which I promptly forgot) and that she would take care of me for the rest of the evening. That was the last time I saw her. It took about -- minutes for my food to arrive, not completely unreasonable, but I was never offered any bread, even though I saw bread baskets on most of the other tables. I was only drinking water, and I had to flag down a bus person and ask before I got my water refreshed. 
After dinner, I sat with an empty plate for about -- minutes before my empty dishes were cleared, again by the supervisor. The supervisor left my table with my dishes, then remembered to return and ask me if I wanted to order desert – which I did. Serving tables was obviously not this guy’s job, but I have to give him an A for effort – he really did try. I had some chocolate concoction which was really sweet and very yummy! I never did get a refill of my coffee, even though I sat with an empty cup for about -- minutes. I finally gave up and got up to leave. I had to ask the hostess to get my bill so I could pay it as I never did see anyone at my table again so I could to ask for it. 
All in all, food was great, service appears to be somewhat inconsistent.

Perfectly appropriate for the cost! Staff were fairly sluggish and unenthusiastic, but eventually they got the job done. Rooms we comfortable and clean, but you don't get the view unless you pay for it. Breakfast was budget all the way - orange juice, powdered scrambled eggs, yogurt and waffle makers. There's a ton to see in this vibrant city, and most of it is really close, so for the amount if time we spent in the hotel, we were adequately satisfied! No more than -- minutes to Fisherman's Wharf, the famous section of Lombard Street and the world famous Buena Vista cafe (go!), half hour walk, or - min cab ride to the beach facing the Golden Gate Bridge, and about -- min walk in the other direction to Union Square and Chinatown. 
WORD TO THE WISE... This is a busy street, and there seems to be a lot of cabs, but for longer journeys, book a cab at the front desk, and make sure they know you name and where you are going at the time of booking! They are easily stolen, and fussy about where they take you! It took us an hour or more to find cabs to take us to the football stadium and the airport, and missed tailgating and our flight home as a result.

I've been lucky enough to stay in many New York hotels in my career and I think it's hard to go past Essex House for location and value, as well as style. The hotel is a lovely old art deco building with lots of charm - the rooms are well sound proofed and elevators although small, run quite quickly. The park view rooms have a great outlook, but you get more space for Manhatten-city view, which basically means no view - but you're in New York, so you're hardly in your room! The bar is open later than usual hotel bars, till -am and has a nice ambience. Breakfast is very good too. It's great to be on Central Park and only -- minutes walk from Time Square, so if you can't afford the Plaza or Mandarin Oriental, then this is the place for you!

Stayed here December ---- for - days, having stayed there previously had really high expectations and The NewYorker lived up to everything we had imagined . . . Our room had a beautiful view of the Hudson River which we had requested. The room itself was nicely decorated and the bed was really comfy :) which was perfect after a long day shopping!
The trip to Woodbury Commons is a must do! Its filled with great bargains but remember if you love to shop bring an empty suitcase so you can fill it with all your purchases and dont have to buy an overpriced one there like I did!! For the best views of the city go to Top of the Rock (Rockefeller Center), views are brilliant and unrestricted from every angle absolutely FANTASTIC!!!
The hotel is located right in the middle of everything across the road from Madison Square Gardens, a block away from Macys and literally a - min stroll to the shops on Fifth Avenue. 
The Tick Tock Diner located within the hotel is great for a full breakfast and snacks throughout the day. The staff are really nice and friendly and work really hard as it does be quite busy! It is also really cheap and the food is good with a great selection for even the fussiest of eaters!
The staff in the hotel are really nice and courteous and the cleaners do a great job in the rooms! The only flaw I would have with this hotel is with the Safety Deposit Boxes . . They are located behind the front desk but you have to queue behind all the check in-check out guests which can be very frustrating at busy times of the day. . I think they should either have a staff member designated for this area with a seperate queue or put safes in the rooms!
All in all though the hotel is a fantastic place to stay, great location, very safe and would recommend it to all . . cant wait to go back :D!

The room was still pretty small but other than that it was excellent. Comfy bed, nice shower and complementary bathrobes. 
Two things you should know before arriving - there is only a very small sign on the street indicating there's a hotel at this location. So make sure you know exactly where you're supposed to go. Also, the elevators are kinda slow (there are only two) but unless you're riding them up and down all day long it shouldn't bother you as much.

I live in LA without a car. I looked for a hotel near the Metro station and Art Museum I was attending within walking distance. This place was a gem. Three blocks from the Metro station and two blocks from the Japanese American National Museum, right in the heart of LA's Little Tokyo. Formerly the New Otani Hotel, (It still has an Asian-Japanese theme) they have about a -- story tower complete with everything you need. A lobby bar which also serves food, the weekend bartender Roberto G. makes the best mojito you could ever have and also is so personable he shold have a tv show.. Also a lobby level restaurant (Azealia) for mainly american food. A couple floors up are the main eateries, a fine food venue with a sushi and shashimi area, a place with a lot of beef and asian inspired influences and a mainly nighttime bar with every drink you want, including every type of sake, as well as food items. Hours vary depending on the day but there's always something, including room service if it's that late. Plus you're in the heart of little Tokyo. Yeah it might not feel great at -- or -- at night but it's safe! And there's a ton of other places to eat as well as the in-house Starbuck's, but they close early.
For the hotel itself, easy and quick check-in and out, very competent staff, I never had a problem go unanswered. The room, I had a basic room, was everything you could expect, windows that open, variable A-C, bathroom toiletries, the tv even includes a few HBO channels.
My favorite feature was the authentic Japanese Garden, located on a terrace on the third floor, it is a several acre oasis garden of foliage, streams and a waterfall. In one corner there is a full bar and grill where you can walk-up or order food to your table. Grilled ribs and a cool drink while admiring the LA skyline in the middle of a Japanese Garden, how cool!
The hotel's staff was always there, not only for security but to make sure you had no problems. I never had one.

I've stayed at the Lumen about - times now, and I'm always pleased with the condition of the rooms, the friendly staff and the location. It's just across the street from SMU, but it's quiet at night. It's small enough so that the desk person and the doorman remember who you are, which is a very personal, nice touch. The rooms are always spacious, although I've found that some rooms are much better than others. The food in the restaurant is very tasty, and there's a full bar for all your drinking needs.
All in all, it's a great price for a nice hotel.

Service is very good, all the stuff is very pleasant

This hotel is ideal for anyone who is travelling on a budget. The hotel was roughly $---.-- each night. The rooms were clean and spacious. The staff were very helpful. The hotel is close to the Prudential Center which is a more high end mall, however there is a Galleria Mall in Cambrige which is only a ----- cab ride. The TD Gardens is also about a -- cab ride. Took the train from Anaheim. Short walk to ES from station. Had booked a king, but ended up with two beds,(it happens). ES did change us to a Bayview room for the inconvenience on the top floor. Beds were comfortable.

Easy walk to bay cruises and Gaslamp. There is also Shoreline village across the street. The Lions Share bar is just around the corner on Kettner. Good food and drink here with decent prices. They have a limited late night menu.
Parking is -- per night. Seemed like many of the guests were waiting a bit to have their car brought up. Happy I took the train. Enjoyed my weekend at ES, would stay again.

Great place to stay. Reports of highway noise in other reviews are exaggerated. I am sensitive to such things and it was simply not an issue.
We walked practically everywhere from this great location. Don't let the proximity to interstate - throw you. Pedestrian traffic is beautifully accommodated, and protected, in Seattle and there is a walkway-sidewalk straight down Pike. Coming back will be mostly uphill so it is a little harder if you aren't in shape.
The only problem we had was a need to leave, unexpectedly, a day early. Our room rate for our entire stay was impacted. Never had a Hilton brand do this to me before. :(
Overall though good suite hotel. Clean. Can't beat location.

The hotel itself just doesn't quite have it together. The rooms are definitely tiny and could use a refresh.The staff was friendly, but slightly inept. my second stay and will be back
the location the bar the burger, the rooftop has a great view

we had a ball , clean friendly and very good service. the russian tea room is next door for a night cap.

The bed was very comfortable and room was adequately sized. I liked the nesting work desk that allowed me to slide it out for a more comfortable email work session. Air Con. worked well. Bathroom was fairly small but not cramped. Water pressure was pretty good and no issues with hot water.
Front desk staff was pleasant, although not the fastest dealing with check in. The attached restaurant was good during happy hour and offered a good breakfast (ordered off the menu).
Location was pretty good, being just a block from Times Square.
