It was the perfect location for us. The room was a tad small but the view was amazing. The ambiance is fresh and new with amazing attention to details. We stayed in a Cooper - with one King room, on the --th floor with a view of the Empire State. The reservation specialist met all our needs. Make sure, if you are on a higher floor, that you get a room away from elevators. They rent out the Penthouse floor for special events which can get fairly loud. We didn’t have such problem, but when taking the elevator we could clearly hear the noise. Their restaurant is not open yet, but it should open in May, I think. The staff can arrange for food, however, from nearby eateries. Their -nd floor lounge-bar is now open; a nice spot to start your evening in the city. The staff does not get any better: extremely professional, friendly, and helpful. I was very pleased with my stay here. Other than the room being a little small for my taste and for the money, everything else was excellent. Oh, if you are just ready to get to your room as soon as you get there, it will not happen. Instead, you’ll have a glass of wine, champagne, martini, or whatever drink you want prior to. Very nice idea…so just relax and enjoy!

We stayed for - days in this hotel. During our stay, the majority of guests seemed to be business(wo)men, although some families with children were present too. Overall, it is a quiet hotel (at least end of February), although the proximity of the interstate causes some background noise. The hotel offers a small outside pool, as well as a fitness center. The room was clean, the staff friendly. Breakfast was included in our deal, but at check-in, they forgot to hand us the breakfast coupons. Ofcourse, that mistake was corrected next morning. The front desk adviced us about the best route to go directly to downtown San Diego. It was a great pleasure to be pampered by Manny, the breakfast cook, who came to our table -- minutes later to ask if the eggs, or pancakes, or wraps, or whatever, was okay, and the waiters (Sasha was one of our favorites) who every few minutes offered coffee or juice. For us, this hotel proved to be a perfect staring point for visits of San Diego, the Mission Trails Park, Ocean Beach. It is possible to have dinner in the hotel, and the quality is good, but it is served in the bar. Within walking distance there is a choice of restaurants.

Stayed there twice in December for work. I enjoyed the comfortable beds and the very quiet area. The hotel is spread out enough that even the parties that were held in the ballrooms on new years eve were far enough from my room so that I was able to sleep.

Several years ago a friend told me about his experience working for a construction company in California. They were building a large facility for the Air Force. They put thermostats throughout the building and even connected wires to them, but the wires from the thermostats dead-ended above the ceiling. The thermostats were merely there to entertain the occupants, not to actually control the temperature. 
The Hilton Los Angeles Airport seems to have employed this same construction company…. While the fan control in the room does indeed control the fan speed, the thermostat seems to have no effect on the temperature of the air coming out of the vent. The air is cold, regardless of whether you turn the knob all the way to left to -- degrees or turn the knob all the way to the right to -- degrees. 
I mentioned the problem to the front desk the morning of the second day and was assured that the problem would be fixed. However, the second night was just as cold as the first night. Be sure to bring your thermal underwear because they only provide a very thin foam blanket for the bed.
Other than that, this is a pretty functional and well maintained Hilton property that is convenient to the airport and reasonably priced. Here are some tips:
-. Parking – if you are going to drive a rental car, you can pay for your parking in advance on their website and get a slight discount. After that, your credit card functions as your entry and exit card. I found this feature very nice. (See https:--www.airportparkinglax.net- for details)
-. Breakfast on --th floor - If you are a Hilton HHonors Gold and above member, you can have a complimentary breakfast in the --th floor lounge. Breakfast was a simple continental type (toast, pastries, fruit, cereal, hard boiled eggs) but it was adequate and the view of airplanes taking off was really pretty. It does get a bit crowded, but if you are patient, you can get a table when someone gets up to leave. I ate at the lounge both mornings.
-. Nice CuisineArt single-double coffee maker in room with Lavazza coffee.
-. Free internet for Hilton HHonors Gold and above.
-. Local Area – if you are planning to drive around and look for local shops and restaurants, the areas to the east and south of the airport are scruffy and uncomfortable. However, the area just a few blocks north on Sepulveda Blvd is very nice with extensive, shiny new retail and nice, well maintained neighborhoods.
-. Dinner – I had a very entertaining dinner at the Buggy Whip Restaurant, about -- minutes north of the airport on surface streets. The address is ---- La Tijera Blvd and it is next to Interstate ---. This restaurant is an old establishment and is sort of a time-warp back to the ----s. The hostess was delightful and served me personally in the bar. I had two excellent martinis and a very nice steak dinner including a salad with Green Goddess salad dressing (their specialty) and a bowl of home-made split-pea soup. The atmosphere was very nice. As I walked out, I noticed that they had a display of several posters of movies that had been filmed there. Notably, the initial restaurant scene from the movie “Date Night” was filmed at this restaurant.

Outstanding hotel. We had a --room suite at a reasonable rate for Chicago. The rate was equivalent to or less than comparable one-room hotels. The bedroom is a completely separate room with its own large flat-screen TV. The living area includes a full kitchen with a full-size refrigerator, computer desk, eating table, couch, lounge chair, and large flat-screen TV. The kitchen is stocked with dishes, glasses, utensils, etc. The room was very clean and comfortable. The hotel staff was excellent. The maid would ask us when we wanted our room made up if she saw us in the mornings. The maid service was very responsive to my request for a new hair dryer when I had a problem with the one in the room. The breakfast buffet was average but since it's included in the price of the room, we can't complain. There was plenty to eat at breakfast and the hotel lady who worked the breakfast buffet each morning was super friendly and attentive. She couldn't have been nicer. They also offer complimentary beer-wine and lite fare in the evenings (at least during the week, not sure about weekends). The front desk staff was flexible about letting us check out late on our last day. 
We suggest that you ask for a room on the higher floors as your view will be much better the higher you go. We were on floor -- even though we had been offered the --th floor. We didn't realize the view on the --th floor would be partially blocked by a parking garage outside our window. Another tip is that if you take public transporation from the airport, take the CTA Blue Line to the Clark&Lake stop and it's a relatively easy walk to the hotel from there (about - blocks). Don't take a route that transfers from the blue line to the red line just to get a block closer because the walk to do the transfer from the blue to red line is very unpleasant - up and down stairs and through a smelly dirty tunnel.

City Center is a typical W in that the rooms are small but comfortable. City Center is in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""loop,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" i.e. business district so there is not a lot going on there after -pm on a weekday or weekends. I lived in Chicago for several years so I know how to get around, but if you've never been to Chicago or do not have friends there I wouldn't recommend City Center. As far as the hotel was concerned the service was ok. The thermostat in my room did not work so the room was quite stuffy and unfortunately it was the marathon weekend so they were booked and couldn't move me. The walls are thin so you can hear your neighbors as well as everyone in the hallway.
As always, great Bliss Spa products. Overall, the hotel is old, the rooms are small and the location isn't great although it is centrally located if you want to take a cab or walk -- blocks down to Michigan Ave. It's also close to the El.

I went on priceline put in a bid for a four star hotel for $----night. I really didn't think I would get anything, but this came in. I was pretty excited at first, until I read the reviews. I figured for what I paid a night it would be worth it. They put us in the marina tower, and just like the other reviews, this is a bit older tower and not as nice as the main one but it had great views! The beds are comfortable and clean. The only wierd thing is the towlets have the loudest flush I have ever heard. You can hear when other rooms flush them too. We had a little airplane noise, but not too bad. We ended up falling asleep on the balcony one night, it was very relaxing. We had a car and the location was perfect for us, since we spent alot of time cruising the bay. All in all, if you can pay $--- a night like we did, it is a great value.

The first night, I got a rather big room, but without view, and a mini bathroom that hasn't been renovated for at least ----- years. They were full so I was promised a nicer room for the -nd night - when they upgraded me to a suite. Massive living room, ok size bedroom, but again small bathroom that, while functioning and clean, looked really tired - the white floor tiles had bits of dark shine through from the usage. Just a toilet, wash baisin and bathtub, you could barely swing a cat.
The restaurant is actually very good, I enjoyed my dinner as well as breakfast. I think it't far too dark , however, but then we're in the US and in California, where posh means dark.
Would come back to The Huntington mainly because of location and steam room-sauna in the Spa's male locker room. Towels, ice water, it's all there.

I took a group of -- College Students to San Antonio for Thanksgiving and we spend - nights there. This hotel, while not on the River Walk, was wonderful. They were easy to work with. My wife and I took our - small children as well. We were located - short blocks from the closest Riverwalk entrance....not a problem at all. The Hotel is also located beside a Trolley stop so if you can't walk well the Trolley is just outside the door. The trolley will take you to all of the tourist areas....Market Square, Alama, La Villata, etc....for $ -.--.
The hotel breakfasts were tasty and they rotated offering daily. The indoor pool, while a bit small, is the only indoor pool in downtown.
As a note, the Childrens Museum was across the street and easy to access.
We had a wonderful time there and would reccomend this hotel to anyone.

The Omni is the best downtown LA hotel--not to be confused with the best hotels in LA which are near Beverly Hills. However, if you have a business meeting downtown I recommend staying here. The rooms are very nice and good value. If you are from the East Coast and wake up at -AM LA time you can walk to the adjacent plaza and get a latte at that time. I also found the room service to be very efficient. The hotel is very quiet and within a short walk to the Disney, which should not be missed. Also, there are some good restaurants within walking distance. So if you do not want to be sitting in LA traffic more than necessary, I recommend a night at the Omni and then a trip back to the airport.

Stayed here for our honeymoon, beautiful hotel, lovely rooms and very friendly and helpful staff. Continental breakfast got you off to a great start each day, and the wine and cheese reception got you in the mood for going out at night. 
Most main attractions are well within walking distance but for those that are not, there are subway stations very near by. 
Would highly recommend this hotel as a place to stay in New York.

Custom Hotel is the prefect hotel when you have a night or two stop-over in L.A. and can't be bothered to leave the airport area. As great a city as Los Angeles is, with a ton of stuff to see and do, the bottom line is that you need time to enjoy your stay here. So, if your stay is short, you're better off keeping close to the airport and just lounging in the hotel's pool area, in the restaurant or sipping a latte in one of the nearby cafés. There's also a bowling alley and a Ralph's supermarket next door. 
Custom Hotel offers guests a free shuttle to and from the airport (LAX) – more or less at your convenience. WiFi is also included in the room rate. Breakfast is not but can be bought in the lobby where a buffet is set up each morning. You can also purchase a toasted bagel and other breakfast items in the lobby café. 
Finally, Custom Hotel's staff are genuinely friendly, rooms are comfy and clean and even if the restaurant's offerings are a tad on the pricey side, the meals we ate were tasty and generously portioned.

this was by far the best service I have ever received at a hotel... anywhere. I have stayed in New York at high end hotels with poor service. By the end of the first day felt like i was at 'home'. Breakfast food and service are outstanding...front desk staff are awesome, location is fabulous! I live in the mid west, these people are just like my neighbors at home! travel ----- days a year for business. Best service ever in a hotel.I will be back for our annual convention and always stay here. close, convenient and safe. everyone is nice.

Front Street freeway off ramp ends right at the hotel great for giving directions not so good for sleeping like wise for the airport fly way. Be sure to get an even numbered room for a harbor-city light view. We were checked into a dirty room, the pipes made noise, the shower was a hand held and it did not hold its position, in room coffee maker did not work, breakfast service staff SLOWWWW, web site states .-miles to city center???but the bed was very comfortable.

I've stayed here about five times; most recently in a queen suite for four nights in May and two nights last weekend (June --)in a standard room. I have ried several of the UWS hotels and prefer this one. 
The queen suites are nice with two queen beds and spacious by NYC standards; Ours was overlooking --th so the street view was pleasant, and the windows were thick enough to avoid any street noise. I like that they have wood blinds as well as blackout drapes so that you can control the amount of lght in your room.
The standard- superior rooms are small, but all have been immaculate. 
All rooms have very posh beds with down mattress covers, down duvets and lots of fluffy pillows. I'm allergic to down, and even the replacement bedding was nice! Two TVs -- one on a stand that can be moved to face beds or the sitting area, and one on the wall in the bathroom. Huge marble walk-in shower walk-in with a wood bench at one end, several shower heads, and a big frosted window to the outside. 
I prefer rooms on the W. --th side, as they seem a bit bigger and don't look out into a brick wall or space between other buildings, as many of the standard rooms do. The hotel is right across the street from a Westside Market (lots of gourmet take out food) and there is a -- hour diner with great breakfasts on the other corner. The OTAH just got its own upscale seafood restaurant, but I've not tried it yet, as there are tons of good places to eat on Broadway and Amsterdam in the Area. 
The staff are not super friendly, but polite enough and have been good at what they do. The lobby is comfortable with lots of seating. Seem to be lots of return guests.
The subway station is a minute away on --th and Central Park is a short walk away on --th. Good taxi coverage and Hertz and Alamo rental cars are in the same block.

Great hotel for LAX. Has a shuttle service and great views of the runways for plane spotting. Generally the service is good. The valets I think are an outside company and are a total joke - incompetent, rude, slow, and that is using tripadvisor friendly terms. Took - requests and -- minutes to get a car at --:-- in the morning. Not peak time. The car finally was 'found' after - people got involved and that was after a lot of shrugging and passing the buck. My colleaague was told several times the car was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""on the way"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" when it was obvious they had no clue - especially since they found the key still sittin at the valet desk -- minutes in. The hotel staff in general is friendly and helpful. The elevators are VERY slow - plan well ahead if you have to meet people downstairs. The Club floor and rooms are nothing special, but decent and quiet. The hotel and rooms are somewhat dated, but a very decent airport hotel. Starbucks in lobby is nice and the gym is fairly good. Nice pool area for warmer LA days.

Wife and I stayed for eight nights to attend our sons USMC graduation. The Old Town is a first class establishment in every respect. The location is good. The rooms are very clean and have been updated throughout. Room was equipped with all the essentials and a nice closet with Iron and board. The queen mattress was very comfortable. Maid service was good and reliable. Now for the specifics of why it’s five stars. We arrived on an -:-- AM flight and thought we would at least drive by and ask when we might be able to check in. The typical experience when no advance early check in has been established is a curt statement of the check in time. Not here. She politely said, let me check and see if your room is ready and then smiled and said yes it is and within - minutes of walking in , we were in our room. One day in a passing conversation with one of the staff I mentioned that one of the electrical outlets was a little worn out and loose. The outlet was replaced later the same day I mentioned it. We had some bad luck with a day trip to Balboa Park, the power was out and most of the park was closed. We had purchased the tickets at front desk and we were able to get a hassle free refund of the tickets. Here’s a really good example: My daughter was changing from a Gas Lamp Hotel to one on the beach. We had planned for her to take a cab and drop her - pieces of luggage in our room for the day. Since she was late and we had left for the graduation, she just went to front desk and they took her luggage to store without asking any of the typical who, what, when or “why we can’t do that for you.” I could cite several other examples but here’s the bottom line. This is a very well run establishment that has an obvious tradition of delivering outstanding service with a smile. I can highly recommend the Old Town Inn and I will stay there again whenever I’m in SD!!

Me and my husband decided that we needed some time alone, ( we have a - --- year old...enough said....) so we decided we would go to Austin for one night. I did quite a bit of recearch on hotels in downtown Austin, because we wanted to be close to everything ( well, -th street ). This hotel was a little pricy, so I decided to try to save some money by booking it through priceline name your own price. Needless to say we got it. When we arrived everyone was very friendly. We actually upgraded to exec. level for $--.--. The hotel was very close to -th street, just a - minute walk or so.... I was a little disapointed about the beds, they were not what I thought they would be. They were pretty nice, just not the Westins """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""heavenly bed"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". :) Overall the trip was good... oh and the breakfast in the morning in the executive lounge is just fruit, cereal, bagels.. not hot... just so you are not disapointed... But overall it is very nice, and quiet.

We chose this hotel over others basically because of the price and the good reviews on tripadvisor. We were not disappointed. The hotel is located in Chinatown and near little Italy, just a couple of steps from the metro station Grand Street, which is a plus. The accomodation is just standard, with normal-sized rooms, shower only in the bathroom, and queen bed. You have coffee maker, tv and wi-fi in the room. GThey do offer breakfast, which consists mainly of sweet things like muffins, cereals and waffles.
The rooms are clean and there' s no carpet on the floors.
The price, slightly more than ---€ a night, would be inapproprate for the structure, was it not in NYC. As a matter of fact, I do suggest you stay at this hotel while in NYC because it is practically the best you can get from the city, if you do not want to pay -------€ a night.

It's sort of a standard issue midtown-renovated---- star hotel. White sheet covered duvet, plenty of pillows, unnecessary bolsters.
That said - some rooms are better than others, although I think all of the bathrooms are the same (would it kill any of these places to put in soaking tubs?). The upper floors have insane views! And depending on which floor and what way your facing, it can be loud at all of the bars in the area's closing time. They do offer ear plugs, so it's not like they're unaware of the issue. Just try to get as high up as you can.
The beds are comfortable, the food - breakfast at least, is good, the bar is alright and the staff is great. It sounds cheesy - but they really are awfully sweet. 
It's really well located - you can either walk or take any number of kinds of public transportation - including the cable car stop that's right there. 
Watch that they get rid of your CC info, however. Several months after our last stay there, they charged our card again. We had to cancel the card, replace it...you know how annoying all that can be.

stayed two nights over labor day weekend ----. cute, funky, fun hotel and very clean. didn't hear any street noise at all and when the shades were closed you couldn't even tell it was daylight...great for sleeping in! bathroom is small but it's to be expected when staying in nyc. we will definitely stay here again.

We spent a very enjoyable week in the Cassa Hotel, very well located to Time square and the Theatre district and many notable sight seeing attractions. The staff were very helpful and friendly. We were upgraded to an executive room on arrival and found the room to be a great deal more spacious than we expected in New York. It was clean and comfortable and very quiet considering its location in such a busy part of the city.we would gladly recommend it to any visitor. 
We would certainly stay there again.

I was really looking forward to staying at this property, given its historical significance (a Burnham design) and recent renovation. I was expecting a lobby with a soaring ceiling and gilded age trim. Instead, the hotel lobby ceiling was too low, and the lobby felt dark. It was a huge lost opportunity for shock and awe. My room had great finishes, but was quite small, even for one lone business traveler. My view was that of a large airshaft. The concierge lounge was adequate, since it was obviously an afterthought. It felt pinched. There were no grand vistas, just a small street view. The concierge staff nearly drove me crazy with their hovering and chatter. I really wanted to like the property more, but there are more attractive properties in the Marriott collection available for fewer Rewards points.
professional staff , hot breakfast , super clean, happy hour fresh cookies on chekin ,good location , the best thing about this hotel is staff is always around to help .. just love it ! good job guys

This hotel seems to have become the place in Hollywood to live out the fantasy of being a character in the HBO series Entourage. Or perhaps, to party like a rock star.
At - am the rooms are buzzing with activity. It seems like a whole lot of fun....except if you're trying to sleep at that hour.
Oh how I wish I had a chosen a different hotel.

I had a wonderful stay here at the Comfort Inn! They are the best that I have experienced in a long time! Their price makes them a steal! When you come to San Francisco, stay here! You won't regret it!!!

Spacious room kept immaculately neat and clean. Shower had bars on all three walls and the extended curtain rod All the extras provided (microwave, refrig, iron, etc). Decent little breakfast Silly, I know, but we were impressed with how the bed was made each day with fresh sheets tightly tucked. The only problem was the additional expense of having to leave a nice tip for them. :-)
I stayed at the hotel with my girlfriends for a special birthday celebration! We were so happy with the wonderful staff, gorgeous rooms and perfect location. We will be back for sure!!!

We planned Christmas and New Year's in New York City with our family, what could be better? Wanting to be near shopping, Rockefeller Center and Times Square on New Year's, we also had the challenge of finding a bigger space for a family of four. 
After some research, Flatotel arrived at the top of our list for location and that they had a larger suite with a kitchen that could accomodate us. We booked our trip, eventhough the price seemed rather high-but hoped it'd be worth it.
Let me say that the lobby is great, although small...however the elevators seem to have trouble accomodating the number of people that use them. The room was fair in appearance and cleanliness, but there were several days that we requested maid service more than once, and never got it. On one particular occasion, we had not left the room as of about -- am, my daughter was still alseep and I was in the bathroom getting dressed, when there was a knock at the bathroom door. I assumed it was my daughter waking up and opened it only to find the maid staring at me. I must've looked rather shocked by her appearance in our room as she insisted that I tell her when I would be out so she could clean! I was infuriated! I didn't know maids can enter a room and see people there, only to knock on the door when they're in the bathroom getting dressed!
There was another incident with another one of the staff that I will not go into detail, but they actually threw a pen when they got upset with our conversation. Not professional, to say the least.
While I will say it is centally located, and the larger room with a kitchen is not easy to find, unless we were desperate, we would not return to this hotel. Our experience in New York is that good service is easy to find...just not here, I'm sorry to say.

I've stayed at the Kona Kai twice, once in a water view room and once not. The room itself is dated, non-flat screen tv, dated decor, peeling paint etc, but the price is good compared to the other hotels on this street. I love this location as I come to San Diego for work and its nice to relax in a peaceful place right by the water. I probably will keep coming to stay, but might try the hotel just down the road next time for comparison.
Overall pros and cons
Balconies on the rooms
The irons in the rooms seem to be very good (surprisingly)
Bed is comfortable enough, pilllows could be a bit more varied
Wi-Fi, although the first time I stayed it kept dropping out, the second time it was fine
Restaurant on site if you want room service, I had the mango chicken and it was good.
The water wasn't heating up hot at all on my most recent stay, which meant a cold shower, I tried it again -- minutes later and it was working (a bit late)
Walls are quite thin, I was woken up at midnight by my neighbors who had the most annoying laugh (especially at that time of night!) My colleague had a similiar issue the first time
Parking is free if you have a AAA card
Poor lighting - I have issues with dim lighting, and they really need a few more lamps
I discovered a mini refrigerator too on my last visit behind what I thought was just a mirror, but there is a fridge and safe behind it.
The view of Lake Michigan was superb and the rooms were extremely comfortable and sleek. Stick with the mid to upper floors if possible to avoid the Lake Shore drive distractions.

The room was in very poor condition, tears in the furniture, stained carpet, bathroom had some mold and the HVAC was spewing dust. After complaining, housekeeping-maintenance did make it somewhat better, but still a very poor experience. The restaurant service was lousy, food quality was marginal and the prices extremely high. If you need to stay near the airport, try the Marriott within the Philadelphia Airport, much newer and nicer.

This is not a new hotel. It actually is an old Elks Lodge. We had some problems with the reservation and were given a renovated room on the --th floor- the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""royal court"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". It was newly renovated, but very small. The bathroom was not big enough for two people-not enough shelf space. The lobby is dark and the furniture old, dark, but comfortable. 
We did have some problems (the maid missed our room one day, the TV was out, cold air continually flowed from the vent in the bathroom). 
We reported each problem and the VERY attentive staff saw to it within the hour. I will give them points for that. the household staff goes out of their way to say """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hello"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". 
There are literally dozens of hotels in the Union Square area. This one has a great location, but I think next time in San Francisco, we might try another hotel.

Hallway noise was ridiculous, including the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Housekeeping"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" call at the adjoining room at --:--PM. Walls are paper thin. Bathtub would not drain. I now have the worst case of Athlete's Foot I have had in years. Road noise (from I----) was relentless. WORST Wyndham property I have ever experienced. Done!

Dirty rooms! I would advise all travelers to stay away from this hotel. Sure it is cheap, however spend more money and stay at another hotel. The rooms smell like a mixture of urine and mold. The carpet is so filthy. It looks like they can't afford to clean the carpets on a regular schedule. I went and checked into another hotel because I refused to stay there. I was out the $-- but I feel better since I refused to stay there.

This was my first time to visit a Conrad and I was a bit skeptical as to what it would be like. The service was a bit shy of a Four Seasons, Mandarin, etc. However, the shower, towels, bed, and room were on par.
The hotel lobby was very nice. However, the front desk staff was a bit confused by a basic question regarding laundry service.
The rooms were very nice and clean. The furnishings were new and a bit heavy for my taste. However, there was no question they spent a lot of money on build out with guest comfort in mind.
The shower had two heads with lots of water pressure. The towels were plentiful, plush, and fresh. They also had nice toiletries, including a disposable toothbrush and toothpaste. There was a television in the bathroom. It had a separate bathtub and shower.
The bedroom had a nice working area with a good chair. However, as nice as the furnishings were they still had that Hilton feel to them, versus what you might find at a Mandarin Oriental or Four Seasons.
The bed was very comfortable. It had lots of soft pillows and great sheets. It also featured two LED night reading lights. 
All in all, this was a clean comfortable place to stay at a competitive price. It has an area or two it could improve, but it's definitely in the top-tier of hotels in the area.

I would like to start by saying this is my first time staying at the Marriott New York Downtown and very impressed by the size of the rooms and the especially the bathroom! I am also very excited about their concierge lounge and the selections available at dinner, I am impressed! This is not finger food this is dinner with dessert and all the hospitality of being at home, someone else does the dishes!
I would recommend this property to anyone who travels for business and know that you are taken care of by the best managers and chefs in the city!
PS, also close to lots of sights, shopping and incredible NY resturants when you want something specific for yourself or your clients.

Michigan

Easy acess to and from the airport. Comfortable rooms. Loved the soaps and shampoo products. When I commented to the front desk how much I liked them, she immediately offered me extra to take with me. Great coffee and nice continental breakfast complimentary as well as a decent breakfast buffet to purchase. A great value for the price and a quick overnight stay.

I have just completed my -th multi night stay at The River Inn. I travel to Washington DC quite frequently and The River Inn is the hotel I keep returning to. I have stayed at several others in the same area, but find I always end up going back to The River. It is not a fancy hotel, but a very comfortable, convenient place to stay. The staff is always pleasant, and the location couldn't be better, the metro is close by as are a Whole Foods and Trader Joes. The rooms are the real treat as they are almost home like in the size they offer. There is a good workspace, full kitchen, and very spacious. The decor is not updated, but is adequate. They have replaced the head board on their beds which is a plus! I am hoping the carpeting is next as the carpet in my room was quite stained and tired looking. The breakfasts at Dish are quite good. I have just completed a three-night stay at the Sofitel New York. After staying at several other NYC hotels, I can truly give this hotel the award as my favorite NYC hotel. The hotel is very conveniently located and only a few blocks from Times Square. Since I was forced to attend meetings in a Times Square hotel, this property was a perfect blend of 'close enough' but not too close to the tourist masses. 
The hotel itself is very lovely. All of the common areas look recently updated but keeping the feel of a classic European decor. Check-in was smooth and friendly, and all of the staff members I encountered during my stay were very pleasant. The gym was also well equipped and large enough to be usable with multiple guests using the facilities. 
My room on the --th floor was surprisingly large for a NYC hotel. Luxuriously appointed in right browns, golds and reds, all of the now-standard amenities were present (Bose alarm, in room safe, LCD tv, sitting area). The queen bed was very comfortable and only made better by the excellent fabric fittings. In the bath, a glass walk-in shower, large tub, and marble floors and counter made the luxury experience complete. 
Again, this hotel holds the gold standard for NYC in my book. There may be bigger (hello, Waldorf) and more glamorous (W Hotel, can you hear me?) but the blend of luxury, relaxation and pampering here are unmatched!

As someone who tends to go the cheapest hotel-hostel I can find, often ending up with some absolute dives, I was pleasantly surprised with one of the cheapest rooms in NYC! He gave us an upgraded room on the executive floor. Full disclosure - I am a member of Hilton's frequent guest program, however upgrades are not always given as they should be. This was a nice surprise and the rest of the check-in process was quick and without incident.
The property is large and well-maintained. Unfortunately I did not have time to use the pool or gym, however they looked quite nice. The conference rooms we used were nice, nothing unique about them though. The catered food served at the conference was very good however. Plenty of elevators also helped with short wait times.
Our room was a corner room with a fabulous view of the Washington skyline. We were able to see the Washington Monument and Capitol from our room. The room size wasn't overly large, but it did not feel cramped either with two people.
My only complaint is the high price of food and drinks in the bar. I realize DC is an expensive city, and eating in a hotel bar doesn't help with cost, so it wsan't a huge deal nor very surprising.
Active tourists will do fine at the hotel. It is about a mile walk to the National Zoo, and about a half mile walk to the Dupont Circle Metro station.
I'd definitely stay here again for business. If I were in DC for sightseeing, I'd probably look for something a little closer to a Metro station.

Started off attending a conference at this Sheraton and ended up staying the rest of the weekend when my husband came to town when it ended. It's a great location - close to Navy Pier & Magnificent Mile and within walking distance of many other sites plus there are always cabs available. The room was very well appointed and comfortable. We stayed at this Sheraton while visiting Dallas for the King Tut Exhibition. Despite some of the other reviews, we had a fine experience at this hotel. We did not rent a car for this trip, and for what we were doing, did not need one. A DART station is right outside the hotel, so trips outside of downtown can be easily made using this form of mass transit. The Plaza of Americas was the only disappointment to us; we thought it was a bona-fide mall, but it really is only a hotel, with an ice-skating rink and an extensive food court attached. Our trip to this attraction took only ten minutes, but luckily, the museums in the area made up for the Plaza. The hotel is less than -- minutes from Love Field, with a taxi ride costing about $-- (not including tip). Overall, for the price, this hotel proved to be a good choice for us and made for a very pleasant stay. If we were to need a hotel in the Dallas downtown area again, we would choose this Sheraton again over some unknown experience somewhere else. We booked this hotel through American Express, not a discounter like Priceline, so the hotel room was pre-paid when we arrived, and we had no problems with our check-in; we got the exact room we asked for, and then check-out was a breeze.

One thing that puzzles me are the rates. They seem to have changed drastically since I booked and I was wondering if there is a reason for this. Thanks so much.

My wife and I thoroughly enjoyed our time at -- Thompson. We were made to feel right at home. The staff were very friendly and helpful. Dinner in the restaurant Kittichai was amazing. The place is in a great location and very close to Old Town. We didn't find it noisy and the rooms were very clean. The staff is very helpful and very attentive I can't say anything bad about them. An outstanding choice if you are here doing business in the area. It is conveniently located, especially if you have to go both downtown and up north, as was my case. What a disappointment!

My wife and I stayed at this Hilton for two nights earlier this month. The plan was to stay for four nights, but the blah and drab atmosphere turned us off, and we switched to the Manchester Grand Hyatt. We were glad we did, and I'll write another review shortly on that hotel.

We also heard noise from a very loud ice machine that had a low vibrating buzz that could not be blocked. Also, the room doors are on springs that cause them to slam hard. This is an annoyance as well as danger, and I accidently lost my grip on the door while entering the room one night which caused the door to swing hard into my wife who got a slight shoulder bruise! I can't fathom why designers of hotels in the ----'s (or whenever this was built) would have installed such difficult and noisy room doors.
The facility is very dull and drab, including a small dated lobby. The best thing I can say for this place is that the bed is quite comfy, and I slept well both nights here. Of course, I use earplugs, which are a must at this location. Also, the wireless internet worked quite well and is included in the room rate. However, breakfast was not included.
In sum, unless you are flying out of San Diego and need a nearby hotel, other hotels in downtown or elsewhere in San Diego would be a better experience with more ambience than this Hilton, nice views notwithstanding. You'll be able to sleep here, but won't enjoy it that much.

We decided to sit down and talk about our plan for the rest of the day and about - mins later, she walks up to us and tells us she pulled a few strings and got us a room ready!! We were so delighted that we could freshen up in our room and get ready for the day. I also have to give my compliments to Ric and Shah, two of the concierges at this hotel. Shah arranged rental cars for us, and helped us out weeks before we checked in by helping us out with transportation. Ric was extremely knowledgeable about the city and made many fantastic recommendations, and proved to be the biggest help when it came to determining what to see and do. 
All in all, this hotel is a four star property. Only minor factors make it fall short of a five star hotel, but in many ways it already is one. I highly recommend this hotel for couples, families, and travelers of all kinds!!!

This hotel is a great place to stay for value and bang for your buck. If you have kids its pool and suites are great. I have to say the fridge in the room might be the best part along with the suite room separation aspect so kids can sleep while adults can stay up a little longer without having kids awake. The staff here are very friendly and helpful. During spring break week, however, they are very busy and understaffed in the check in-out area. On a trip in October the staff were much more helpful, and able to do their jobs. Alex is a great help upon arrival!
The hotel is nice and the staff was polite. The rooms were comfortable and location was OK, but overall it was an average stay.

I was worried about staying here after reading some of the reviews on Trip Advisor, but I was pleasantly surprised.
The reception and lobby are nicely decorated and I found the staff to be friendly and helpful. 
I booked a junior suite as it didn't cost much more than a double room and I was very glad I did. The room was very spacious with a sofa and coffee table, desk and dining area, kitchen with microwave, coffee maker and fridge, walk in wardrobe and a large double bed which was very comfortable. The room was very clean with plenty of towels, complimentary toiletries and hairdryer in the bathroom. 
Housekeeping were excellent and when the do not disturb sign was used we were not bothered. They would always come back later in the day.
We took our laptop as the room had free wifi but the connection was intermittent at best. There were times you couldn't log on for hours which was irritating, but we weren't there to spend all day on the computer so it wasn't too much of a problem.
The buffet breakfast (which is included in the room rate) was excellent. There were sausages, eggs, fresh waffles, cereals, toast, bagels, juice etc and you could eat as much as you wanted.
Many people have complained about the lift being slow but I didn't think it was that bad. I was on holiday so I wasn't in a hurry anyway.
The gift shop on the first floor was very handy as it sold drinks and snacks which were much cheaper than the vending machines. There was also an ATM but it charged $- per transaction so we never used it. There is one over the road at a liquor store which only charged $-.--.
The location of the hotel isn't great but I think that's reflected in the rate. I simply couldn't afford to stay at a decent place in a good location and a nice hotel in a not so nice location was a fair compromise for me. 
I don't think the area around the hotel was particularly dodgy, there's just not much there for tourists and there's nothing nearby that's within walking distance. However, there is a bus stop right outside the hotel and the subway is less than - minutes walk away. The public transport in LA is excellent and I had no problem getting around. Its also very cheap with a day pass costing only $-.
This is a great hotel for people on a budget and its also ideal for anyone relying on public transport to get around.

Overall great hotel and service. We liked the no tipping policy (service included). Roomy, clean rooms. Location was ok, removed from most sites by a couple of
Miles, but still ok. We walked everywhere. Being next to the water was nice.

The Marriott in the Fianancial District was the best. We really wanted to stay uptown but the rates kept us downtown. My first New York experience was staying at the Marriott Marquis, but that was when I did not have to foot the bill!! Prime location, especially when you are -- and single (living off of mom and dad) was definately needed back then. And the Marquis was the best. But now travelling with children; security, cleanliness and budget comes first. We were pleasantly surprised by this hotel. We were in a great location! We could see the World Trade site from the hallway while awaiting the elevator. The HUGE discount department store -- was very near the hotel as were the subway stations! It was very easy to catch a cab by the help of the bellman. The conceirge helped us with finding Bubby's restaurant in Tribeca. And even when it was pouring down rain, the front desk gave us nice umbrellas!! Location is everything and surprisingly the Marriott was the best location to suit our needs. We left the hotel early every morning and returned after -- PM every evening. I felt very safe and secure. We shopped and dined all day and when it was time to retire, it was nice to return to a quiet uncrowded area to unwind. We ate the breakfast buffet in the morning, a bit pricey at $-- per person (children were half price). The spread was fantastic, though. Everything you would ever want, from fresh fruit to made to order omelets. The fitness center and pool were very nice also. The entire hotel was spotless. We stayed in the corner room with - queen beds and plenty of space to spread out.There was a nice bureau and a desk with a chair and a lounging chair. The beds were out of this world comfy!!! The bathroom was full sized and very euro chic. And most importantly, CLEAN!! All in all, I have not one bad thing to write about the Marriott Financial District!

Stayed for - nights in April. Features include big, clean rooms with comfy beds. Very good bathroom and shower. Very elegant inside and out. Very good location, --- blocks from bus routes. Breakfast was the highlight for this trip (really good omelette's). Dominick's located across the street, Walgreen's and wine store behind the hotel. Need to improve: remote control did not work and was never replaced (complaint submitted on day of arrival), and the sofa bed was truly designed for small kids (no adults should be allowed to sleep there). Otherwise, an excellent option for Chicago visitors.

This place is like a bad ----'s hotel. As a HH Gold member it is embarrassing that Hilton would own given motelish feel with remote buildings. Very dated carpets, cold hallways, and a goofy entrance with gates. Doubletree are feeling like the old Holidomes. Not as close to airport as other hotels.

This place for sure is located perfectly for a visit to DC. The rooms were clean. Check in, no problems. Expensive to park your care, but expected Also, if you need your car quick plan for about -- minute wait.

The sleeping rooms at this property are larger than average, I believe their web site calls them Texas-sized rooms. Sleeping room furnishings etc. were what I would expect of a hilton.
Had a meeting there, and the meeting room space and staff were excellent. No complaints.
One perk that you RARELY see at a hotel is FREE printing in the business center! That was a nice surprise. 
There is a jack in the box next door, but if you're there for lunch, I HIGHLY recommend going to the seedy looking strip mall behind the jack in the box to Central Texas BBQ, it is the best BBQ i've ever had, seriously. 
Other than jack in the box, there's a shell station a quarter mile down the road (where they sell decent wine!) that's next to all of the other airport hotels (hampton inn, holiday inn, etc, this hilton is set away from that cluster). Aside from that, a shuttle driver will take you to some nearby options for food or walgreens etc. 
FYI for elite HIlton HHonor guests, there is no concierge floor at this property. Instead you get a free breakfast voucher, which seemed nice until I discovered everyone else seemed to get a free voucher too! 
I would stay here again, especially if you're just flying out of Hobby in the morning.

We so thoroughly enjoyed our stay at The Hotel Drisco. Situated in Pacific Heights, this hidden jewel sits among many Heritage buildings-homes - well worth a stroll to see the stunning architecture. The rooms have been re-designed and updated in keeping with the age and character of the building. A complimentary breakfast is served each morning, as well there is a sitting room where you can enjoy reading a book-newspaper and tea & coffee is served all day. The hotel is quiet, comfortable and the staff are kind and helpful. I am looking forward to my next trip to San Francisco - The Hotel Drisco will be my hotel of choice.

We did get this stay on a sale but even then, our experience was not good. We stayed one night to attend events in NYC and this location was close to both sites. We arrived after check-in time and a few guests were waiting for their accommodations as did we. The staff was solicitous and the included continental breakfast was OK. Our room on the -th floor was very small; the closet & drawers were small. There was additional hooks to use for clothing. The bathroom was small and the water source was reversed...the hot water was obtained by selecting the cold water indicator. The basin was small and there was little storage space for toiletries. There was a table top ironing board but very little table space. I had to move the lamp, phone, magazines, menu, etc. to make enough space. These inconveniences compounded by the delayed access to our room made for a very stressful time for - adults to prepare for attending an event. One elevator is out of service to make improvements for ADA. The location of the hotel is convenient to public transportation which is good for touring the city sites & sights. Granted, I was only in one room and at a very reasonable cost for a midtown location but I won't use this hotel again. There are others in this neighborhood where I have stayed with better accommodations. We departed as soon as we awoke--I thought the mattress was so hard, I couldn't sleep. The shade did not fully cover the window and there was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sliver"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of hall light from the building across the way.

My husband and I stayed at the beautiful St. Gregory Hotel in Jan. --' and couldn't have had a more enjoyable stay. The staff was both accommodating and courteous and our room was very nice with all the necessary amenities. It was conveniently located to everything and I would highly recommend it to anyone who's planning a trip to D.C. We thought the prices were very reasonable and received service above and beyond what we paid for. Also, you can't beat their $-.-- martinis!

Preparing for a recent getaway weekend, my husband and I stumbled on the Hotel Helix online and were intrigued by the unique decor of this hotel. When we arrived we found it to be a very fun and unique property to be sure - tucked into a great row of brownstones a little away from the hubub of the mall area, but not very far from the sites...the room was great! The daily wine hour and the great value made this hotel a great choice....but what really put it over the top was the friendly, caring and accomodating staff. Would definitely go back and recommend it to friends.

This hotel has everything from amazingly friendly staff who just couldn't do enough for us, to the most comfortable beds and pillows I've ever slept in. Nothing was too much trouble, from going out and buying us coffee filters for our in room coffee machine, to lending us a laptop for -- minutes (FREE) so we could look up a few websites on things to do in New York. The rooms were extremely spacious and spotlessly clean and coming home from a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hard days shopping"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to find our room where the beds turned down, the lighting dimmed and soft music playing, was fabulous. Wouldn't stay anywhere else in New York again.

What a wonderful hotel! Only a few stories high, decorated nicely, and the staff were very friendly and helpful. Every room has a microwave and a refrigerator, along with an easy-to-use safe. My conference was a few blocks away ($- cab ride), but the Days Inn was half the price! I highly recommend this hotel, and I plan on using it again in the future.

I stayed at the Westin Domain in Austin for work in September. Overall, I had a great experience at the hotel. While it is not in the heart of Austin (quite far North), it is a nice property with a lot of services around it. It is right next to a large mall and has some quality food options itself (really enjoyed my dinner). Further, I was able to get an excellent rate so the value for money was quite high. If I need to return to North Austin, I would enjoy returning to the Westin Domain.

Drove in from Chicago and stayed here due to family member having surgery at Jefferson hospital. Positives, the staff was very accomodating and willing to help you. The --th floor restaurant was good. I thought the prices were reasonable for a hotel restaurant and the portions were big. I highly recommend the swordfish and the bone in ribeye. The rooms are average, but I think each of them comes with a small refrigerator and a microwave which was a nice feature. The hotel is next to the Reading Terminal Market which serves every type of food you can imagine and groceries, (produce, meats, fish, etc..) and the hotel is across from the convention center and Chinatown. Now the negatives, hotel charges around $-- a day to park, but you can come and go as many times as you want. The location of the hotel isn't the best. There is a greyhound bus station and another bus transportation company right across from the hotel, so there are alot of transients walking around. Overall a good hotel but questionable location. I would recommend this hotel but caution about the neighborhood. Was fine during the day, didn't really go out at night.
DO NOT EAT at Crown Fried Chicken restaurant around the corner. I had a cheesesteak and ended up with food poisoning.

Having stayed at other hotels in New York before I was pleasantly surprised by the size of our room! By comparison, it was huge! Great location - less than a block from Times Square, walkable to major sights and shopping. The staff was very friendly; they had no problem holding our bags before check in and after check out. I would definitely recommend this hotel and would stay here again.

This hotel was a real find for any budget-conscious traveler who wants to spend money on site-seeing and not on hotel floor space. I stayed in a single """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""pod"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which was a room about -' x --' - a twin-sized bed built into one side and a flat-screen TV mounted in the wall, a desk, an open closet, a wall safe and a stainless steel sink. There were drawers under the bed and hooks on the wall and the window had wooden slatted shutters. Room felt both clean and cozy and the bed was comfortable. Individual controls for heat-air con.
The shared baths were not a problem - the showers were really cool and I liked that there are indicator lights in your room to let you know if the bath is occupied. In the lobby, there was a cafe and two wall-mounted iPods (free) where you could check your email and etc. They also had a terrace where you could sit outside and have coffee-drinks. I didn't get up to the rooftop garden. 
I paid just over $--- for a private room and in NYC, this was an incredible bargain. I would stay here again.

This hotel I picked was based on reviews I had read from this website, I was pleasnalty suprised at how quiet the hotel was and when I did arrive I was dealt with promptly, the hotel reception was nice and helpful but the concierge- baggage handlers were a bit unhelpful and alwas trying to sell us tours, when a tour came to pickup a few people from the hotel I overheard the concierge asking for his cut (not nice to see or hear) and on the final day when we were going to the airport because we booked out own transfer they didnt tell me when they arrived and didnt open the doors or help with our luggage or anything like that.
good point was its location to universal studios and the free shuttle that it took us to daily if we wanted it

Wow! I stayed here for - nights in November for business, and was so glad I did! My room was large with a nice layout, big closet, desk, flat-screen TV, and pretty view. Incredibly clean, too! Most importantly, the bathroom had a huge walk-in shower, and also featured a make-up mirror and great lighting. (Thank you, Kimpton!!). The lobby, roof terrace and meeting rooms are must-see, (even if you don't have to attend a meeting). Also, my friend and I had drinks at the bar - restaurant, and had a fabulous time. Really impressive with friendly (no attitude) staff! Talk about cutting edge architecture! In addition, the hotel also is adjacent to a very modern """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cafe"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" style restaurant, that's very cool with an interesting atmosphere. As long as you like the Chelsea location, the hotel works just fine - it is also a few blocks from the subway and a few small deli - pizza places for cheap eats. Special thanks to the hotel's night manager, Adnan Ali, who was especially helpful!!

The restaurant in front of this hotel is excellent but the hotel itself falls down in many ways. The location right near Northgate Mall may be advantageous, however the hotel has dire technical problems and some infrastructure issues too. Internet is almost impossible, and allthough the staff were friendly and helpful, they themselves could do nothing about the contract with a lousy internet company which apparently runs through December. Definitely check how internet is running before you book. The outside walkways shake when people walk on them, which you can feel inside the rooms, and the breakfast room has meager offerings which stop exactly --am, without a second to spare. As a European guest I found this difficult. Parking sufficient and rooms clean enough.

Room is amazing, very large and comfortable. Staff was very friendly and welcoming. 
Close distance to main DC attractions.
Restaurant downstairs has GREAT food, not very kid friendly (toddler) since they don't have a real menu and the items which were offered were not the best choices.

Our stay at the Westin La Cantera was as great as the last visit! The bar staff at Steinheimers (Dennis, Josh, Yvette and Louie) are so welcoming and friendly! Our stay would not be the same without them. They also provided us with great places to eat and things to do in San Antonio for entertainment. Thank you all....we are looking forward to our next stay in San Antonio!

I stayed overnight for a weekend event and booked this hotel for its proximity. The location was perfect. It would be a good spot for a business traveler, but it is not some place I would choose otherwise for a relaxing getaway. My room was on the -th floor facing the street and there was street noise well into the night, including lots of horn honking that was not that muffled. I wanted to go up to the rooftop just to see what it was like and transferred elevators on the -th floor and met another guest whose room was on the -th floor. There was thumping bass you could hear in the hallway and she said the noise was bad in the room. Then I was thankful I """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""only"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" had street noise. I didn't stay on the roof because the entire area was full of people on a Saturday night and I wasn't in a party mood. Besides, it was outdoors and cold. 
When I arrived, the room window was wide open and I was surprised there were no screens on the windows. It was also an uncharacteristically cold day and even turning up the thermostat to about -- it took a couple hours to warm up. I also felt like there was cold air blowing toward the desk. I resorted to the extra blanket in the closet which was heavy like a bedspread and looked really unsanitary--spots all over it. Although there were a few lamps. one never came on, and I never felt like there was enough light in the room or the bathroom. The room descriptions offer accessibility features and if you have any issues at all, you might want to request a special room because the edge of the tub was not rounded as usual and seemed at least -"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" or more higher than the average tub. I get that it is supposed to be hip and modern, but I thought they sacrificed comfort. The design of the modern sink allowed the water to spill over onto the smallish counter and gets your stuff wet. 
I really had to hunt to find the in-room coffee and then there was only one pack of regular coffee. I heard another guest checking out ahead of me with a similar comment. 
Thankfully, the internet was free and easy to access. The parking, however, was $--.-- for less than -- hours overnight. Yes, it's L.A., but I think that is still on the high end. By the time I added in all the taxes and parking it was more than I wanted to spend just for a place to sleep for one night, even at a discounted rate.

I loved every minute of my stay at the Biltmore. I did not want to leave.
We scored a good deal on a two-queens room in one of the poolside villas. Finding the hotel was kind of a maze! If you feel lost, just keep circling the outer ring until you see a kind of drawbridge; get on it so you can get to the reception desk to check in. Even the difficulty getting inside was nice because the whole point of a spa is not to leave, right? It's supposed to be this otherworldly experience, not just a place to hit the hay for a night. If you want fail-safe convenience, go to a hotel off the interstate somewhere.
We were met by the most helpful valets I've ever worked with. Walking in the hotel, I could hardly contain my excitement at the striking decor--a kind of art deco Mayan plaza, if that makes sense. The yellow cockatiels were tweeting softly, water features were sparkling and twinkling as we walked to reception. Reception was so cavernous that we couldn't see the receptionist behind the desk; I had to ask the concierge if anyone was in. That was kind of annoying, but who knows why I couldn't see the receptionist at first. It's partly the grand scale of the lobby, which cast shadows everywhere--very scenic, but only practical when you already know where you're going!
I will say that the receptionist did not offer necessary information, such as where and when we could find breakfast, and what the pool hours were. This information was clearly marked inside our binder in our guestroom, but it would have been nice to know from the receptionist. She was, however, very nice and willing to give us some tips about how to get around the whole complex. As I hinted before, it really is more of a whole resort than a hotel. Some hotels try to get by saying they are resorts, when really they only have a massage table in some obscure corner of the hotel, but this one really is a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""complex"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in both senses of the world. You have to spend a moment getting to know your way around.
Our room was roomy and strikingly pretty, yet dated and on its last legs. For example, the bathroom sinks and tilework were cleaned to an inch of their lives, but still had a few cracks and areas where the calking seemed to be coming loose. The bedlinens and carpet were clean, yet there were some hints of old staining. Nothing too bad, but they should think about rehauling some of these poolside villa rooms. (They need a better TV, and they should ditch the old-fashioned ethernet cables.) It's why I can't really give them - stars.
The soaps and shampoos and whatnot were intoxicating and upmarket. They're all made with local botanicals--yucca, etc--and smell amazing. I made sure to take the bath gel and shampoo home with me, and I wish we'd had time to stop by their spa shop to buy some. If the grouting and sinks hadn't been so old, I wouldn't hesitate to say it's the best bathroom I've ever been in. It was so huge and sparkling everywhere. 
We enjoyed walking the grounds of the resort at night. The dramatic lighting and fountains highlighted Wright's designs in a way that made our walk seem magical, and a great prelude to our satisfying, fun meal in the casual restaurant (Frank and Somethings?). We took another walk at - am, and it was astonishingly quiet everywhere. We had an expensive breakfast at the cafe (two americanos and two croissants were almost twenty dollars, if I'm remembering right), but boy that view was worth it. 
Wish I could go again, but now I live in Phoenix, and there's no reason to. We also peeked in at the conference center and the jaw-droppingly beautiful ballroom (really, you should peek in too), and we joke that we're going to have an anniversary party or a christening party there just so we can enjoy the grounds again.

This is a brand new """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""designer"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel with UK ownership. It fits very nicely into the SoHo scene and offers a warmer and more appealing décor than bland competitors. However, it's also staffed by the usual -- somethings who think they offer service but more often than not miss the mark. When I checked into the Meadow Suite for two nights, I asked if I could extend my stay for a further night or two. The young man on reception said he could not confirm that, but he would speak to the Reservations Manager the next day who would call me. No call came. I also asked for a second key and was told one would be sent right up...No key arrived. This was the start of a pattern of very uneven service standards based on many promises but little delivery.
The Meadow suite is a standard two room suite with a faux fire place that exists purely for aesthetics...It's main attraction is a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""private"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" garden. However the back of the adjacent buildings all back onto the garden...so its neither private nor particularly attractive. At the time of my stay the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""meadow"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was just a rag tag bunch of newly planted shrubs...perhaps in a year or two it will justify the $---- price tag for the suite. However in the meantime, its just a big disappointment. There's a set of outdoor lights to at least create an aesthetic appeal in the evening. However, there was no switch in the room or on the patio. An enquiry on the first night about how to turn the lights on met with enthusiasm but no solution. I was told they would consult the engineer in the morning and get back to me....As you can imagine, I never heard anything more and the garden remained dark throughout my stay.
If the Crosby Street Hotel wants to compete in New York and charge their sky high prices they will need to try much harder...Needless to say I did not extend my stay and won't be returning to this confused little infant any time soon.

My wife and I stayed recently for a weekend away from our --yr old son (she stayed longer for business). Like many have said, the hotel is tiny (that's why I give the hotel - instead of - stars -- that, and the noise) -- tiny front desk, tiny hallways, tiny foyer (if you can call it a foyer), and of course tiny guest rooms (not really big enough for two -- at least not two people with two suitcases). I reserved a room there to share with my family, and they got us a room that smelled like someone was smoking there, and it was a non smoking room. The room looked so dirty and creepy. The door lock didn't worked and we had to wait - hours until we got another room. The service was awful and we couldn't sleep at all. The only good thing about this place is the location, otherwise it's a nightmare.

I came with a group of girls for a bachelorette weekend getaway. The service was excellent and the staff were very obliging despite us asking to change rooms twice. The location is excellent, right on the Riverwalk, and only a - minute walk to the dueling piano bar, Howl at the Moon, where the bachelorette party was. We had breakfast at the hotel restaurant, and sat outside right next to the river--the service was excellent. If you are driving or renting a car, park in the parking garage across the street. It only cost us $--day rather than the $--+ they charge at the hotel. Even the gentleman at the front desk recommended this! I would definitely stay here again.

Nice hotel. Front staff very friendly at check in. Rooms are clean. Sunken bedroom is a different touch. Boutique feel with modern furnishings. Roof top bar has nice views and indoor and outdoor seating. Room service breakfast was above average. Definitely worth a stay and will come again.

Really enjoyed my recent stay at this hotel. It's hard to find a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""new"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel in Boston, in looks and feel. There are some newer """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""boutique"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotels, but thier fit and finish will be dated before long. This was my first experience at a Fairmont property, and it was very, very positive. So much in fact that my wife and I booked a three night stay at the Fairmont Chateau Frontenac for our anniversary next month. 
The place - easy in and out for an urban hotel. GPS in car brought us right to the front door. For those who whine about the cost of valet parking ($--), it's comparable to any other hotel of this class in Boston.
