It is within walking distance of most main attractions, the Prudential building and Copley Square is literally a few minutes walk away. There is a trolley bus stop just up the street and tickets for the trolley bus are sold in the hotel. The only downsides to this hotel was the fact that there is no fridge in the room and the refuse disposal truck collected rubbish just under our window which was very noisy. Otherwise I'd have no problem recommending this hotel and would definately stay here again.

The good: good location for business in downtown Philly. Free managers reception with beer wine and cocktails. Free hot breakfast. Rooms are big. I mean studio apartment big. With microwave, minifridge and wetbar. The bad: the place badly needs a fresh coat of paint and some new furniture. Not to say it isn't clean, but it looks worn. Tip: if you need a beer or whatever after the manager's reception ends skip the on property TGI Fridays. There are several pubs very close by with more charm and better beer.

Lovely Hotel to stay in very clean & lovely modern rooms. Great location right off Michigan Avenue, only - blocks for the Water Tower place shopping centre, - blocks from my fav restaurant in America The Grand Lux Cafe (--- North Michigan Avenue at Ontario above Ann Taylor), Gino's East pizza right next door, close to beach – - blocks, John Hancock centre – - blocks. Would definitely stay here again. The only slight downside was the sirens we could hear even at - floors up in room ---, the back of the hotel may not be as bad though. That said it was not that bad, we did not ask to be moved or anything. Word of warning watch out when crossing the roads, Chicago drivers pay no attention to the red lights & continue to drive even when the green man is giving way to to pedestrians.

I enjoyed my stay at this hotel. The staff was friendly, efficient and helpful. The room though smaller than those at a typical Marriott or Hilton was very clean and comfortable. There was a light over the desk so reading at night was not difficult. The New York Times (including the Sunday Times) was delivered to my door everyday without additional charge. The Nikko, like many hotels, has stopped automatically delivering newspapers to every room but it does so, if requested. The hotel has a restaurant in it but the restaurant does not feature the menu that appears on the room service menu. Since Nikko is a Japanese chain, I expected to be able to order a rice based meal in the restaurant. The restaurant did not have a single dish that included rice. But not to worry. There are many restaurants, bakeries and coffee shops all around the hotel. I enjoyed a Japanese meal at a restaurant in the next block. Large department stores such as Macy's are a couple of blocks away. The famous San Franciso trolley, the subway (called Bart), street cars and buses are all close by. It is easy to reach Fisherman's Warf and other tourist destinations without a car. I would certainly stay at the Nikko again without hesitation.

One need only point to the attentiveness of the guest services staff, especially Raquel, to understand why it's easy to keep coming back time and time again. As much as I travel and as many travelers as a hotel staff see during the course of a day-month-year, having someone that gives that personal touch always is refreshing. This hotel is consistent.

Very friendly, modern, great sfuff...the food at the restaurant was good...nothing to complain...there are some rooms with a great view.
Just two blocks away from the main street where you can take the trolley, we will stay again.

For a vacation in New York we did'nt want a expensive hotel, when we knew we were going to be out discovering the city, only having a place to sleep and rest. A great value hotel with good rooms and a great diner. The lobby was helpfull with resturant tips and the hotel had a great location, especially if you are going to a consert in Madison Square Garden, as we did.

This HI was a nice little surprise! Booked online for a spontaneous but cheap - day weekend with my husband. 
First night we had one of the older rooms but we didn't check in until --PM so no surprise there. The next day we asked for a different room and got a poolside room. Wonderful space right on the putting green. 
The restaurant was good and the vouchers we received were an extra bonus. Restaurant staff is very friendly, as is the evening desk clerk. 
Pool is nice and wasn't that cold (even in March). Never went to the bar area but it looked clean and was rather busy. 
Had a wonderful stay and will be bringing the boys next time!

We got this room for around $-- a night including taxes. The location is great, just feet from Michigan Avenue, and convenient to transportation, and a great place to set out on walks. We walked to the Art Institute quite easily. 
Check in was good. We arrived early and the room we booked, a queen, as not available, so the very nice clerk arranged for us to have a king room instead. The room was not enormous by any stretch, but more than enough room to turn around and maybe even dance between the TV and the bed. The room was on a corner, with two windows, the main one overlooking Michigan Avenue.
I noticed they were gradually upgrading the rooms (on the mezzanine there were stacks of boxed plasma TVs, and the --nd floor--we were on the --th--was noticeably fresher than ours), but our unupgraded room was just fine. 
The bathroom as small, but not claustrophobic. For whatever reason the sink had obviously been recently replaced with one of those furniture-like models, and it was very handsome, but way out of scale to the rest of the bathroom.
Requests for extra pillows and towels were fulfilled by the cleaning staff without any trouble. The bar staff was super nice. The Lavazza coffee shop in the lobby was convenient although the gelato was mediocre.
The crowd here skews young. The lobby tries and generally succeeds at being hip and modern.

I planned out my vacation months in advance and wrote down all the hotels for my husband to book. Some how, he got mixed up and booked the wrong hotel for San Francisco and we ended up at the Courtyard Marriott. Initially, it was a big shock and I was a little disappointed. The Marriott is your basic chain hotel, with very basic rooms. We had a decent view of the city our first night. The rooms were very clean. The beds were adequate, but nothing special. Out the hallway window, we could see a partial view of the Bay Bridge, so my husband went to the front desk and asked if we could switch rooms for our second night and have a view of the Bay Bridge. The front desk staff was very accommodating and they switched us to a room with an amazing view of the bay, the Bay Bridge and the city! So, although the rooms were basic, the view was worth the stay! Rooms were very clean and staff very helpful. Wifi free. No complimentary breakfast. Parking was $---day, but you can park for $-- down the street or find free parking along the side streets. Good location. You can buy a day pass and use any form of transportation, bus, cable car, trolley cars, etc. I would recommend this hotel, if you request the beautiful views of the city or Bay Bridge.

I'm not too picky with accommodations but this was extremely disappointing. The location was good, but the rooms are very dated (old TV, no power outlets to charge your mobile devices). I ordered room service breakfast and it never came, and the worst of all - no hot water for my shower. I barely got an apology from the front desk at checkout. I would never stay here again!
wondeful accomdoiations, gracious service, and perefect location. Hotel feels new, beds very comfortable, valet service good, and staff helpful.

Nice town house with antique furnished rooms, beds are comfortable. The kitchenette (cutlery, plates etc. are provided) with a well stocked bar is a nice plus.
Service is friendly, yet minimal: hello & goodbye; someone on-site from - am to -- pm. The area itself isn't too quiet, mainly due to ongoing construction work. There is no bar nor restaurant attached to it, however, B next door serves good food (can be ordered in the rooms as well) and plenty of other venues are close by. Get a room with balcony or private terrace to unwind on or to invite some friends over. Price is on the upper side considering the services provided, thus the average price-value rating - But hey, it's NY and you get a way more individual experience than with similar priced hotels.
Would have been nice to learn more about the story of the house, but the guest folder doesn't give away anything - Anyway, we'll be back!

These are apartments probably built in the ----s that have been gutted out and remodeled with trendy furniture and the usual granite upgrades. The cabinets in the kitchen and bathroom look cheap. they have been painted to look like the natural wood colors of the table and headboards. faux wood floors in the mini kitchen and bathroom. Large granite bathroom counter space. bath and shower pretty basic, nothing spectacular. I stayed in the - bedroom suite -it is nice. took a peak at the studio and that was really cute smaller with a divider between bed and living room pretty true to pictures in regards to furniture and colors. ..Will probably stay in that one for future ( a little cheaper). The area is great!!! high end and close to everything you would need!!! Was here on business and plan to stay here or in the arboretum area again. Three buildings on grounds fitness room in middle building. no free weights just treadmill, bike and elipitcal machine. all machines have built in televisions. Rooms have flat screen tv in living area ceilings are the old popcorn ceiling quite dated but over all a good area and pleasant stay.

The Hilton Seattle Airport understands what it is: you are here for a night and then off on a plane. Unfortunately, its long-term business model is disasterous as one would not want to return, if given a choice. The rooms are expensive but look more like a Hampton property. Staff is indifferent and ineffective---the front desk person even repeated herself---as she was so disconnected from her job and any personalization that might come with it. The room service menu is bizarre and over priced (coffe-crusted NY strip! What a way to ruin a steak (or hide its flaws, maybe)! All in all, a very forgettable and frankly, tragic abuse of the Hilton name and standard.

Came for UCLA graduation! Got a fair price at the Hyatt Regency Century City w- Pricline """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""bid your own"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Parking was a pain! $-- valet but had in and out privl. Great mall next to hotel with free three hour parking. We used that during the day and then found a parking place in the near by neighborhood at night (after -pm. You had to move your car by -am and was quite a walk but we liked the exercise anyway. Hotel was very nice, clean and fancy! Expensive food and crowded Starbuck's. We brought in food from the mall and had a picnic! Pool area gets shaded early in the afternoon bummer! Public bus near by! Good breakfast place near by off of Santa Monica Blvd. Would I stay again???? Not unless I got a good price! (But,....enjoyed the hotel better than reviews I had read on TA) Glad I had a chance to stay there! Thanks for such a helpful website! (:

My job put me up at this hotel for - night. I was very impressed. Nice modern, hip boutique hotel. Free garage parking for guests...located underneath hotel. There is a shuttle to-from downtown, but from what I heard from my coworkers...wasn't very reliable. I had a car rental, but several bus lines stopped at or near the hotel...easily takes you to-from downtown. UW is around the corner, so lots to see & do in the area. The hotel itself is in a residential area, it was very quiet.

This was our first time in SF, and the Nikko helped make our week-long stay the most wonderful vacation we have ever had!
Decor of the hotel, built in ----, is classy and modern, and everything is kept sparkling. Hotel employees that we interacted with were very kind and helpful. The elevators were probably the fastest we have ever ridden in any building.
Our room, #----, although a bit small, was decorated nicely, and was very clean and sound-proof. Maid service was excellent. The bathroom was modern and larger than average, and featured ceramic floors and walls, black marble vanity top with basin sink, and a massage shower head.
Nikko's location is perfect: one block from Powell Street, two blocks via Ceril Magnin St. from the BART, and two blocks from Union Square. It also is walking distance from major bus stops, making it easy to travel all around town from there.
We will definitely stay there again, on our next trip!

I stayed in this hotel for a conference trip. The hosting hotel for conference is way too expensive for me so instead I bid on priceline and get this hotel. They have a mini-gym and a super-mini swimming pool whose water is not that clean. Everything is fine except that it's really difficult to find a restaurant nearby without driving. I also have the impression that the neighborhood is not so good at night.

Spent a week in the Ivy - found the room to be very modern, lovely furnishings and a stunning bathroom with an amazing shower. The bed was comfortable and on the whole I cannot really fault the room. 
The main issue with the hotel is that it is poorly insulated and there are real sound problems. The cleaning staff woke us up every morning at -.--am with constant door slamming and talking as they set about their daily duties. This was relentless even though we got out of bed to ask them to understand that we were trying to sleep. We also mentioned this to the staff on reception - nothing was done but I can appreciate they can't magically solve what is essentially an issue with the design of the building. There was a clear gap under our door, which was also very thin..... Which meant we weren't in total privacy within our room as we were always aware of a presence outside our doorway! When we were waiting for the lift we could hear other people's conversations very clearly - which really isn't normal or acceptable for a hotel of this standard.
We had drinks at the rooftop bar, which was lovely, but the music was awful. 
The Ivy nearly gets it spot on, but the noise issue really spoilt things for me as I want to enjoy a decent nights sleep on holiday and I didn't get that here. Also, this hotel is not cheap.

\if you want a good sleep try elsewhere the televison is on the adjacent wall to next room so people who are deaf or like lod music disturb everuone else especially until - in morning suggest go elsewhere

My wife and I planned a huge trip to New York and booked the Casablanca based on the TripAdvisor ranking. It was mostly a great experience, and I'd give this review five stars except for the major faux pas the hotel made one morning. 
We'd had a bit of a late night (easy to do, given the hotel's superb location in Times Square and the theatre district) and had planned a bit of a lie-in. Imagine our surprise when sometime between -:-- and -:--, there began continuous sounds of pounding, hammering, sawing, and other unidentifiable noises of construction. After about -- minutes, I opened the door to see the halls packed with furniture and workers strolling about, installing new carpeting in every room on the floor but ours (fortunately), It wasn't so much the disturbance as the fact that it all happened without any kind of warning -- even from the staff member who visited our room the night before to see if we were comfortable and satisfied (which we were -- at that time). When we finally went downstairs to start our day, we complained at the front desk, and the general manager made a perfunctory apology. He mentioned that the work wasn't supposed to have started until -- am, when they assumed most guests would be out of their rooms, but he offered no real compensation or satisfaction.
It's a shame that this incident so colored our stay. Everything else was great. The room was immaculate and (excepting the construction incident) quiet (especially surprising, given the hotel's location half a block from Times Square) -- though it was fairly dark (our room faced an airshaft-courtyard). The staff was almost unfailingly friendly and helpful. The wine and cheese happy hour provides a great respite after a busy day and before the theatre. The wifi is quick and free. The rooms are large. The beds are comfortable. The shower is mediocre, but you can't have everything.
I assume future visitors will benefit from the new carpets and, because of the recent installation, they won't have to deal with the construction noise, but the whole carpeting experience really left an impression our whole stay.

I really enjoyed my stay at this hotel. The service was great. My suite was beautiful. The staff is very attentive and very helpful. I would highly reccommend this hotel to anyone staying in the midtown area. Also reccommend their other hotel in Manhattan. Their location is a great one for the business or the leisure traveler.

This was a good hotel, fairly central location. A large room which had a fridge and microwave in it which was very handy. The breakfast was sufficient with plenty of choice. The bed was clean and comfortable. The staff were extrememly helpful and I would recommnd this hotel.

Great stay. In a city as hip and youthful as San Francisco, nightlife often functions as a means for gathering and meeting friends, but it’s not the requisite scene that some cities render it. That said, I love staing here especially downtown!
Bix wraps de rigueur martinis, elegant food and classy entertainment in a single, glamorous package, while more contemporary style finds a home in Suite one-one, where beautiful patrons groove to soul, house and funk just beyond the velvet rope. For get-down-and-bump-it dance action, head to The EndUp, whose theme nights have attracted a faithful, energetic following for years. And for one-of-a-kind Bay City color, check out Beach Blanket Babylon, a musical review whose topical humor is always spot-on and whose elaborate hats defy natural law. Another particularly local institution, Asia SF, serves food, drink and dance, along with stunning female performers who are much more than they seem to be.

The Fairmont San Francisco is, without doubt, one of the world's grand hotels. And it deserves this reputation. Some of the facilities (the ----s Tower extension) are a bit dated, but generally, it is a very good hotel
When we arrived at the hotel very late (around midnight), because our plane was delayed, we were no longer given a room in the historic part (as booked), but the tower. However, they upgraded us to a top floor, corner view deluxe room (we were actually on the same floor as the InterContinental's hotel bar 'Top of the Mark' opposite, which we could easily look into). The room facilities were excellent with grand interior design and a cosy, elegant atmosphere. The bathroom was spacious and clean - providing a separate shower, toilette and bath tub. 
The bed was very comfortable, the desk perfect for my business needs and we could generally not fault the hotel or its service with anything. 
We arrived back in San Fran so late that all restaurants were shut and we thus decided to use the room service. The drinks and sandwiches arrived on time and were of good quality. 
Checkout was very good. 
Quick summary:
Location: Very good
Facilities: Good
Rooms: Very good
Special factor: the entrance hall and the bar just look amazing. 
Service: Very good

we stayed in the Traditional room. the hotel is relatively new. rooms are small- but roomy for nyc hotel standards for - people. room was clean and relatively quiet considering you're in manhattan. reception staff was very nice and helpful. location is good--just a -min walk to bleecker. subway was only - blocks away. it has its usual stuff in the room - coffeemaker, safe, hairdryer, internet access. bed was comfortable and clean. i would definitely stay there again. there is a small fitness room but no dining room or restaurant inside the hotel. lot of eateries nearby though.

Summary of Pro-Cons (Full review below)
Pro:
Good location; close to Lexington Ave line (-) & Empire State Building
Bar fridge
Con:

Useless WiFi (only in Lobby)
Linen can cause itching (possibly due to laundry detergent-powder)

After having researched this hotel in depth through several online sources, we decided to book this hotel for our holiday trip in NYC. What appeared to be an excellent choice with reference to tripadvisor and other sources, turned out to be a holiday wrecker. Essentially, don't trust every review on this website.
Upon checking in, the hotel staff did not properly greet us nor did they offer us any assistance with the neighborhood. When actually getting to the room (located on upper floors) we were presented with a --'s decor room which was not renovated to appear 'modern' as advertised. The worst part about our stay was that the shower was approx --x--cm in company with a hot water system that took -mins+ for the first person to get a steady stream of hot water. Most of the time the temperature of the water was random, and was intermittent changing from extremely hot, to freezing cold.
In addition to this, the complimentary WiFi was almost close to useless as it was only available in the lobby which never worked. The server had continuously rejected the guests attempt to connect. When querying the staff about why it did not work, they would just provide a generic excuse and blow it off. It was evident from many of the guests attempting to use the WiFi that they were also at the point of snapping. When it did work, it was acceptable.
Although I would not recommend this hotel to anyone, some of the upsides were that it is close to the Lexington Ave line (-) and the Empire State Building (although you'll only visit this once).

We stayed at the Doubletree in Times Square and it was a great place to stay. We had a room on the --th floor so we were away from the sounds of the city but there was still some very minor noise. Certainly nothing that kept us awake at night. The windows had room darkening shades which were very good at blocking the lights of Times Square. I was exhausted after a day of shopping and sight seeing so I slept like a baby but I did find the bed very soft. I have to say though that my bed at home is memory foam so it's hard to find a bed I'm happy with. I don't feel it's the fault of Doubletree that I have an awesome bed at home that is hard to compete with! This area of the city is VERY crowded but I knew that going in and didn't mind it at all. TS is centrally located to several walkable areas and public transportation is nearby. Every staff member we came across was friendly and helpful. We were taking advantage of Hilton Honors points so we had complimentary breakfast. The dining area was attractive and clean, the wait staff was friendly and attentive, and the food was all very good. We would like to stay in other areas of NYC to experience them better but when we choose to stay in Times Square again we will certainly book at the Doubletree.

The hotel was lovely but you have to like """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Italian"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" modern. There is free coffee and tea in the morning, free wine in the late afternoon, and, for Kimpton members, a $---stay credit to use on the in-room minibar. Service was extremely friendly, courteous and prompt. The complimentary robes and umbrella to use during my stay came in handy. The restaurant in the hotel was excellent but there were also several other excellent restaurants within walking distance. For me, the location was great - - blocks to my business location. I would definitely stay here again.

My favorite courtyard that I've stayed in. The hotel obviously was some sort of department store-office building before because the windows are huge! I booked a standard king and it had a little mini-fridge area and a little living room-sitting area. A lot roomier than most other courtyards. We had a view of Qwest Field from our room and it was beautiful. It's right downtown so it can be a little bit noisy, but that stuff doesn't bother me all that much. We walked down across the street and took the Underground tour which was pretty interesting. We also walked a few blocks to the Pikes Place Market, so it's very convenient to a lot of the city's main attractions.
The hotel has valet parking only, but it wasn't that overpriced and the valets were very nice and friendly. They brewed fresh complimentary coffee in the lobby and there was a little coffee shop (starbucks? can't remember) attached to the lobby as well. I really liked hotel and highly recommend it for business or a romantic getaway.

We really don't understand how this motel is -- of --- hotels in San Francisco in popularity index. The room was small, stinky and fetid. The window in the bathroom was broken. As we arrived we found that the linens and pillows were full of hairs. We informed the Front Desk but he simply replied that they wash the linens everyday... nothing else... VERY BAD EXPERIENCE. We stayed there only - night. The day after we changed Motel.

We stayed here for - nights in a queen room, --th floor.
The room was comfortable, large, clean, well maintained and modern. Housekeeping was perfect.
We loved the food in teh ground floor restaurant, great service. We enjoyed a few drings and nibbles in the lobby bar, again, great service, great food.
When you book your stay, be mindful they charge $--- for car parking.
Overall, we'll go there again, we were very happy with teh experience.

We (me, hubby and - year old daughter) decided to leave the snow of Lake Tahoe for a weekend of culture in San Francisco, seeing a play and the Nutcracker ballet. We booked the Huntington as we are members of the Small Luxury Hotels of the World, and we knew anything closer to Uniion Square would be way too noisy. The location at the top of Nob Hill is great -- our room (----) was HUGE and had views over the city -- could even see a portion of the big tree in Union Square. They put a roll away bed in for our daughter and the room was still very spacious. It was fairly recently renovated, with plush linens (bed and bath), a large double sink area outside the toilet-tub room, a couch, coffe table - club chairs and a desk, as well as a miibar w- small sink. The TV in the armoir was dated (not a flat screen), but got good reception. 
Walking up and down Nob Hill is great exercise, but if the hills are too much for you, the California St. cable car line is literally right out the door and the Powell St line (the one that goes from Union Square down to Fisherman's Wharf) is only a few blocks away. We parked in a nerby garage for $---day and didn't move the car until we left - days later -- you can valet the car for the same price.
We did not use the conceirge to make any reservations -- since we were there over New Years I had previously booked via OpenTable.com -- but he was very helpful in looking up movie times (and trying to get us into a hot resaurant near the Metreon on about -- minutes notice, unsucessfully, but we did appreciate the attempt). He also directed us to nearby breakfast spots.
I love staying in older, more architecturally unique hotels and the Huntington fits the bill. I love the fact that the windows open, yet when closed the city noises are almost completly obliterated. Having a window opened on New Year's eve allowed me (hubby and - year old fell asleep about --!) to hear the festivities, and the location allowed a filtered view of the fireworks over the Bay, but when I was ready to go to sleep, all I had to do was pull the window shut and no more party sounds! We heard NO noises from outside our room, although I can't guarantee that the people in --- didn't hear our daughter jumping around.
The ony reasons I didn't give the Huntington a full five stars were minor: no coffee or tea in the lobby in the morning, although they do have hot apple cider in the afternoon; the doormen and bellmen were not as attentive as one would expect in a -* hotel
I'd definitely stay at theHuntignton again -- but next time I'm booking a spa treatment for the aching legs after walking all over San Francisco!

I liked the property, and would stay here again. -- minute wait for a free shuttle, five minutes from the hotel. Staff was consistently friendly and helpful. The room was spacious, clean and comfortable with in-room coffee and separate sink from bath-shower. The TV was old and should be updated. Dinner and breakfast both very good. I never heard a single airplane despite the proximity to LAX. Finally, if you have a little time on your hands, the $- roundtrip shuttle bus down to Manhattan Beach is a bargain - see the ocean, walk the pier, shopping and dining.
Excellent customer services from staff, front desk and shuttle Svs.

We stayed here in September as a --st gift for our son. This was his first time in New York and we wanted him to love it as much as we do.
First impressions, reception area was tidy but a bit shabby. Receptionist was very friendly and efficient. The rooms were a fair enough size and clean, bathroom the same so no problems so far.
The location was great, just off Madison and around the corner from Grand Central Station. Ideal base for a sightseeing trip.
The hotel does not have a breakfast service so you can use the bar next door - which is in fact part of the hotel building so I didn't really get that. The breakfast was a tad expensive but a fair selection, although we didn't find the staff overly welcoming. (For the same price I recommend you walk around the corner, opposite Grand Central Station Pershing Square, a fabulous place for a real New York Breakfast, the buzz in there is great.)
On the day we were leaving we left the bags to be locked up until it was time t leave, only issue we had really was the receptions reluctance to organise a cab to the airport. They told us to walk over to Grand Central They did however offer to book us a private limo with a set price. We did book it but I was worried all the way to the airport that we were about to get ripped off. Worry not, we had a lovely car, pleasant driver and he charged us the agreed fee.
So all in all it was a great trip and no problems with the hotel. That is until a week after our return I find the sum of £--- being held on my account , This was the amount they hold on your arrival in case you should run up a bill of any sorts. All our bills were paid in full, in cash on the day of our departure. It took me - days and several phone calls and e-mails, some of which the staff were rude, to get this money back. Never had this happen before, and it would put me off returning to this hotel.

We chose the Sheraton as it was in a great location - attached to the prudential center, so it was near the tube and many restaurants. Also, from looking at the website, the facilities provided seemed great! Unfortunately, they weren't as great as they came across as. In the photos the pool looked gorgeous and was put across as 'one of New England's largest indoor pools'. The pool was disappointingly a lot smaller than advertised as and was really a disgrace. Staff obviously spent very little time looking after it as there were filthy marks around the edge of the pool and swimming around you would find clumps of hair floating around and I dread to think what the other suspicious looking objects were. The gym was actually really great, just not in the best place, you have to walk through the pool area to get to the second fitness room - I witnessed many poor people slipping over! 
The worst experience I had regarding the facilities was the fact that during my stay they decided to close off the pool deck to us paying customers for a private event. This, I found very unacceptable. You chose a hotel for mainly its facilities, then you get them taken away from you?! It was a lovely day and all we wanted to do was spend the day out on the sun loungers. If they are going to do this, they should inform you before you arrive there or give you a discount, surely? Another issue was that half of the staff were unfriendly and unhelpful. We had a few days when we came back to a room that had not been cleaned - not very welcoming for a good nights sleep. 
So overall you can see it wasn't a great experience for a family vacation. The hotel definitely has a lot of potential, they just need to take more care of the building and their customers! Next time we visit Boston, I think we will find an alternative hotel.

My family and I recently stayed at the Westin while on vacation. The staff was friendly and polite. They were responsive and efficient. Internet access cost $---d ($---wk), which seemed excessive. Like most hotels in the area, there is a parking fee. 
Metered street parking is available nearby but read the signs carefully. The walls seemed a bit thin - we heard loud music from neighboring rooms occasionally. The gym was well equipped. One nice touch was the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Milk & Cookies"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" option for families. They brought up books and a snack for the kids.
The hotel restaurant was closed when we wanted to dine in on a Monday night, to our dismay. Fortunately, there were several good restaurants ---- minutes away by foot. Of note, there is a Whole Foods ---- minutes away and a ---hr CVS around the corner.
I expected free access (or at least, much lower cost) for a room at this rate. The location was so-so. There is little to do immediately around the hotel but the area seemed safe to walk around at night.

If you are looking for a nice clean place with great A-C to get some rest after a day of driving, do yourself a favor and scratch this place off your list. After driving in from the Florida panhandle we were awakened at --:-- by either an air chisel, hammer drill, or air hammer in and adjacent or nearby room. I called the front desk and they denied anything going on. Then I went to the front desk and heard more denials. The on-duty maintenance man walked by and said he had heard it on the -th floor....three floors up from us. Then the front desk worker made a call and the noise that she had no knowledge of mysteriously disappeared. I asked to speak to a manager and of course none were on duty.
