Stayed in the Wellington Hotel -------- for four nights.Agree with all the positive points from previous reviews,great location,very clean etc.Nothing negative to say about this hotel.
Found the Blue hop-on hop-off tour bus great value for money,especially the Uptown and Downtown loop to give your weary feet a well deserved rest.
If you want to try something different food wise in NY,give TOPAZ thai cuisine a visit just round the corner from the hotel on --th street,between-th and -th Ave.great food and very reasonably priced,followed by a cocktail at Le Parker Meridien Hotel on W --th Ave(opp Topaz),
very relaxing atmosphere after visiting Times Square.

My friends and I stayed there during a convention in August ----. We had - rooms and Super - customer service was very helpful in making sure we had adjoining rooms. 
The staff at the hotel was very professional and friendly. They were able to answer our many questions and gave helpful suggestions. Their shuttle service made it easy for our late-waking friend to join us at the convention.
The breakfast was great, we ate in the morning and didn't feel hungry until late afternoon, not bad for - large-sized guys!
The rooms and beds were clean and comfortable. I only have - complaints: -) The bathroom. Like others have said, the bathrooms need to be re-vamped. The low-flow toilet was...unexpected. -) The ice machines. When we stayed there, the upstairs machine was broken and the one downstairs was usually empty. Luckily, there's a Wal Mart & Target nearby, so no loss to us.
Overall, a nice, quiet place to stay. Will definitely return there.
The hotel was excellent and the staff were fantastic. I would stay in this hotel again if i go back NYC.

I am in the city often for business and leisure travel. Chose to stay here as we were needing an inexpensive place to crash following a concert. The Springhills have been upgrading their design concept - kind of modern funky - I like it - the rooms were very clean - breakfast is okay - but its the value and location that are primary here. No, its not the sofitel, but its very centrally located, excellant service and a great rate for the class of hotel it is. The breakfast is just okay to me- but it is complimentary. I am a loyal Marriott rewards member and try to stay in Marriotts when I can - this place is great for people bringing kids to the city - with its internet in the lobby, pool and fabulous location. For a romantic weekend - try the Sofitel!

The Hilton Hill Country Resort and Spa exceeded our expectations. We usually stay at the Westin La Cantera however because our plans included Sea World we decided to stay at the Hilton due to the proximity to the park and the shuttle service available. Have to say the customer service, childrens activities and rooms were better than at the Westin (which we have seen decline in the past - years). The room was very clean and the beds were comfortable, the bathrooms were very large which is great when traveling with kids. This is a perfect family resort. My children looked forward to returning to the hotel every evening to roast marshmallows and watch movies under the stars. This gave my husband some down time to have dinner and drinks out on the gardens and we could still keep an eye on our kids. We also had massages at the Spa and had a great experience with friendly service. Also note that we purchased through priceline at an amazing rate and were not charged an additional $-- for - queen room . Great vacation, would highly recommend .

Stayed here for - weeks in July. All i can say is that this is a very good, clean and pleasant hotel. From the doorman, bell hop, through to the front desk, barman. Everything is very simple, but behind that simplicity lies class and a wonderful quality that only the very best hotels possess, or can hope to possess. All my requests were met with, of course! Nothing seemed or was too much trouble. 
 All in all, this is a hotel well worth staying at. The location is a serious plus, just of Park Avenue, a short walk from Times Square, Rockefeller, Central Park and all of midtown Manhattan.

My spouse and I planned a special weekend in Manhattan and chose to stay at the Waldorf Astoria. The grande dame delivered an excellent experience. The front desk greet us cheerfully and got us promptly to our room, even though we had arrived several hours early. The lobby was immaculate and filled with guests waiting for friends or just relaxing in its ambiance. Our room was spacious, immaculate and well appointed, giving the appearance of a recent makeover. The bathroom was large, with the quality of fixtures one would expect from this property. The hotel's location in the middle of Manhattan makes it convenient to trains and any point on the island.

We stayed two nights at the Burnham on our first trip to Chicago. The hotel is beautiful... the renovation of this historic building was done very nicely. The staff was courteous. The location was great: a couple blocks from Millennium Park, a block away from the El and subway, theaters within a block or two. There's a Walgreens next door, very handy for munchies and whatnot. Also just up the street is Lazarra (?), an excellent espresso bar.
The restaurant (Atwater's) looked nice, but we didn't get around to patronizing it. It's a little pricey.
I was going to give this hotel a --star review, but I'm going to ding it a star because they added on a credit card charge after we checked out for (as I later found out) honor bar items. We didn't take anything from the honor bar, and they promptly credited us back, but it still bugs me.
Anyway, it's a nice hotel and we'd stay there again, especially if we could get a better rate (we paid about $----night).

For the money, there are better hotel experiences even in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""grand dame"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" category, such as the Palace around the corner.
We booked the St Francis because of its reputation and convenience to Michael Mina restaurant, which is off the lobby. Unfortunately, our room was tiny and had a view only of outside walls and windows. The room itself was extremely noisy, being near an old elevator shuttling back and forth all night. Housekeeping woke us up at - AM on a Saturday to ask when we could be vacating our room.
In general, the level of service and attention to detail seemed lacking in the staff we encountered. Looking for coffee to go, I happened into the Oak Room restaurant. Rather than directing me to an espresso bar around the corner in the hotel, the restaurant had me sit down and -- minutes while they confusingly created two to-go cups, then mistakenly billed me $-- for a buffet, then made me wait another -- minutes (coffee getting cold) while they corrected the bill.
This is one of those old hotels that rests on it laurels rather than stepping up to the challenge of delivering excellent service that should be synonymous with the Westin name.
Note that the parking is run by a third-party not associated with Westin and the rates can be astronomical. Also, validated parking from Michael Mina does not apply to overnight stays. You can save a few dollars by parking across the street in the Union Square underground parking.

This was my third visit to New York and it was amazing as usual!
I went with my mum and grandma and between them they had visit new york around -- times and this was the first time any of us had stayed in the Waldorf Astoria and we will ---% be going back!
It was such a classic, elegant hotel which is full of history!
The rooms where outstanding and also full of history in its decor which we loved. The beds were so comfy and no doubt you will have a great nights sleep there!
The staff were just amazing and helpfull, we had no problems whats so ever!
We did not experience the spa so i cant comment on that but after what i have heard, that is also very good!
It was also great to find out that there was free Wifi access in the lobby which was great for me to catch up on college work!

I stayed at the Jacksonville Riverfront Hyatt with my wife and son on Aug. -----, ----. We went to Jacksonville to tour Jacksonville University. The hotel is awesome. I paid $--.-- per night by booking on hotwire.com. The hotel is right on the St. Johns River. Plenty of places to eat close by. The hotel food is extremely expensive, $-.-- for a bowl of oatmeal or grits. There is an Einstein Brothers Bagel Shop behind the hotel which is resonable for breakfast. Nice pool. The Tampa Bay Buccanners checked in on the --th so we got to see some of the team members. You won't be disappointed.

Stayed here for --day weekend. Great location. Lots of attractions in walking distance. Beds were wonderful and room in historic tower was very nice. Great views and the windows open which was great for some fresh air. Changed from --st floor due to banging we kept hearing for -- hours (sounded like someone jumping on the floor above us). Hotel was gracious in moving us to --th floor, but had breakdown in communication as to why we were moving. In the morning, told us to leave our stuff and bellman would move it; just pick up key when returning at day's end. When we came back at -pm to pick up our new key, they then asked all sorts of questions which should have been noted already. So it was annoying to reiterate the whole banging noise, engineer you sent up heard it, never got back to us, etc. Both rooms we had were very nice. Bathrooms have a lot of marble, nice tub and separate shower. Nice toiletries too that smelled great! 
Amazing lap pool--one that must've been shown in movies. Interesting how you must shower first--you have to walk past the attendant to get to the pool from the showers; this rule is apparently enforced. Pool does not smell like chlorine which was great. Didn't eat there so can't comment on food. Check on internet access--some get billed and some don't. There's a Starbuck's on the ground floor too.
Took doubledecker bus tour first thing and saw the whole city. Next day went to Space & Invention museum (taxi cost $--) and then to Millennium Park. Walked around the City and shops, etc. Hancock Tower was cool at night. Fox & Obel store near hotel was great. Lobster club sandwich was so good I went back next day and got one to go for the plane ride back to NJ (United serves-sells NO food in flts < - hours). I'm sure the cupcake we ate on the plane was the envy of passengers around us. Nice upscale store with a great """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""to-go"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" selection too. 
Ditka's had good food for dinner. All within walking distance of the hotel. Hotel staff was very courteous.
Used Continental Van service from-to airport. Paid r-t at airport but next time would taxi back as the p-u was late and driver had attitude toward everyone. A LOT of traffic to and from airport. Leave about an hour to get there.
Overall a good experience.

We stayed at the Bedford the week of April --- and would highly recommend it. The location was tremendous - just around the corner from Grand Central Station. We took the N.Y. Airport Service bus from Laguardia and it drops off south of GC, so we just walked with our bags a few hundred yards. Could not have been more convenient.
Plenty of restaurants right around the hotel. The room was clean and pretty roomy considering what you get in NY -- also had a fridge, sink and even a stove. This is an older hotel so the fixtures ect. are not exactly modern and this is not a luxuary accommodation -- but to get that you pay through the nose. Staff was very friendly and maid service was efficient.
If you go to New York to see the city and need a handy and decent place to stay, you cannot find a better deal. Only those who want pampering and luxuary will be disappointed.

From the moment I checked in, I felt that the staff were more than willing to help in any way they could; greeted us, welcomed us. It actually felt like they knew us they were so warm with their welcomes and smiles.
The rooms were impeccably clean and had a simple Asian feel and elegance to them. What was nice that small refrigerators were also in the rooms tucked away out of sight.
We had buffet type eating and the food was superb. I am a vegetarian and I had many options available to me. I especially like the eggplant parmisan, the grilled vegetables and the wonderful desserts. I am also a tea drinker and there were multiple selections available. 
There was a nice sitting area in the bar, cozy to watch TV and a decent selection of drinks. I would suggest adding a couple of local Monterey wines to their list of wine options. They also have a great workout room and swimming pool, well worth using.
Beyond that, the location is just a couple of blocks from San Pedro village where there is a variety of good restaurants and clubs (if you prefer that) and on Friday afternoons, there is an open farmers' market, always a great place to get cut flowers for your room if you are on an extended stay or want fresh fruit to nibble on.

I stayed at the Triton hotel over a very busy weekend in February. The location is fantastic, the best. It's an easy hop over to the cable cars, and right across from the chinatown gate. The hotel restaurant is very good. It's a great boutique san fran hotel. If you want something unique, urban, funky and fun this place is for you! The hotel has a sense of humor, your room comes with rubber duckies. Some of the rooms are tiny though. But no worries, just ask for a different one. The staff was very accomodating. Great choice!

Since this hotel is in an historic building, it enjoys its own personality and atmosphere--particularly the delightful guest rooms, which are unlike any other Marriott we've ever stayed in. Very comfortable bed and top-notch bathroom. Good quality coffee in the room, which is how it ought to be in Seattle! The restaurant is a great place for watching pedestrians on the other side of the windows (esp. during happy hour), with good service and food. We were pleased with the personable, can-do attitude of the desk staff. It's a pleasant walk to the waterfront with a number of wonderful restaurants to choose from.

This was my first stay at this property and I probably won't choose to return. Overall it was adequate, but there were some issues that I consider to be important when finding lodging.
First, let me say that I was in one of the Bay wings (two story wings beside the tower). I'm not sure what the tower rooms are like and this review only reflects my experience with a room in the wings.
The room has been somewhat recently renovated. It's too bad, though, that the carpet was a bit stained in my room (----). It is also unfortunate that when they updated these rooms (and I think they did a pretty bang-up job on the overall renovation) that they didn't remove the popcorn texture from the ceilings. It makes it look dated. 
Overall positives: Great furnishings as part of the renovation, including LCD TV; comfy bed; lots of light from slider; interesting room design.
Issues: Noise was a big issue for me here and I'm generally not a light sleeper. I heard TVs on both sides of my room very clearly. I also had a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""heavy walker"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" above me and I was pretty amazed at how clearly I could hear that walking back and forth. Mission Bay is close to the flight path for SAN, too, so there was some aircraft noise. An additional noise source was the heating system. This, clearly, was not updated in the renovations. It looked ancient and made a big ker-bang every time it shut off. It jolted me awake a couple times. 
The location is great only if you have transportation of your own. I did ... and found the location to be fine.
The noise issues, alone, would probably steer me away from this property. If you're a light sleeper, take note!

We stayed here the weekend of ------- we did not have a good experience mainly due to lack of communication between hotel staff. Since this incident, the hotel has stepped up and made things right. The GM of the hotel Raja went above and beyond our expectations to try and make things right...for this we are extremely grateful. Rooms, are very clean and homey :) we would recommend this hotel for a comfortable stay. One of their shuttle drivers by the name of Josh, was awesome, and if you need a shuttle ride, I highly reccomended him. He's a great friendly guy :-)

The Marcel at Gramercy is now one of my favorite hotels. Great location, very comfortable rooms, very inexpensive, and AMAZING staff and customer service. The staff were as helpful and courteous as any I have ever experienced, and I have very high standards for that sort of thing. Lindsay at the front desk is really a sweetheart, but the whole staff is amazing. 
I loved the room too. Very nice modern decor, and a cool building. Before I booked, I saw some complaints about the rooms being too small, but I am guessing a lot of those are from folks who don't stay in Manhattan hotels much. I thought the room size was average. And again, everything else was well above average. Outstanding. I am definitely gong back.

Upon arrival at the hotel, you will be greeted by friendly staff members that will promptly escort you to the first available desk clerk. It was there the trip was ruined for me. I booked a double room (traveling with teenage son) with a view, for five nights for the price of $--- per night. Upon my arrival the desk clerk asked me if it was my first time to NYC, which I replied yes. At that point she informed me she had me in a single with no view. After haggling and telling my son we'd go somewhere else she said a double suddenly became available but it would cost me $--- for the first night and $--- per night thereafter. I took the room, demanded to see the manager, which didn't happen. Upon my return I have made several attempts to discuss with Marriott (corporate) with not even a return call or email. I will never use Marriott properties again, as it is clear to me I was ripped off and Marriott does not stand behind their confirmations. Go somewhere else, especially if your a woman traveling with children and new to NYC. Nothing special about this place anyway.

A basic motel close to the airport & port, but has a very welcoming atmosphere and you get the feeling you ARE welcome.
Small room, with a fridge and folding table, and a new LCD TV. There's really no need for anything else.
Small free breakfast, good wifi service and a scale that can help before heading to the airport...
All in all, it was a very good experience and I'll most definately return when I come to SD again.

Would not recommend this hotel for business travelers.
As soon as you enter the hotel, there is a stairway down to the checkin desk. There is NO escalater or elevator to help you with your luggage down to the lobby.
Each morning, I had to ask for a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""refill"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of the toiletries (shampoo, etc.). Housekeeping did not automatically replace the empty ones with full ones.
The restaurant in the hotel had terrible service. It was definitely not worth the price.
When checking out, I needed to leave my luggage with the bellhop until I returned later that day. It took at least -- minutes before I ever got my luggage. If I did not mention that I needed to catch a train, I might still be waiting!
I would not recommend this hotel.

I had booked two nights (the charges were unrefundable through a travel site) but forfeited the second night's charges and changed hotels, it was that bad. The staff was friendly and helpful, but that was the only bright spot. The beds were awful, you risked sliding off if you sat on the edge, there was no support left. Furnishings were very sparse, and very old. The grout in the bathroom was nasty, the whole place needed painting and new carpet. The room was large, but there was only one yucky armchair besides the beds and bedside table. And I would never have sat in that chair. We didn't want to touch anything in the room, and if it hadn't been so late we wouldn't have stayed the first night. We couldn't pack up and get of there fast enough in the morning.

My husband and I loved the Riverwalk, but not this hotel. Check-in was fast & the lady was nice, but our room didn't seem so clean. The furniture was dusty and when I moved the ottoman, a pill was lying on the carpet. This wasn't a Tylenol or aspirin either; but a prescription pill of some sort. I also noticed some dental floss on the carpet by the sink. My husband was busy looking for drawers to put his clothes in, but the only two in the room were connected to the sink and one held the blow dryer and the other the Bible. Also, there wasn't a safe in the room, which wasn't that big of a deal for me as I intended on taking my purse with me when we visited the Riverwalk. This is on the quiet end of the Riverwalk and about a ----- minute walk to where the action is. I felt fine walking it during the day, but now that the time has changed and it gets darker so much earlier, I wouldn't feel safe walking alone or if - women were alone -I can imagine that crime can be more of a factor there since it's so far away from the action. There is a free breakfast from ---- in the morning -they have yogurt, cereal, juice, milk, bagels and donuts. There is a Starbucks on the premises and for those wanting something hot for breakfast, you can order something and pay for it. I went down early and grabbed a donut & some yogurt and brought it back to the room to eat while I read a book & the hubby was still sleeping. There were a few crumbs left from the donut on the bedside table that I decided to leave there to see whether or not the maid would clean it up. Also, I dropped the coffee stir stick on the carpet to see if that would be taken care of. Well, that evening when we returned, the coffee stir stick & the crumbs were both still there - so they didn't bother to dust nor vacuum. The sink area was not wiped down either as you could still see where the water droplets had dried. I think all they bothered to do was make the bed and give us - new towels. I picked up & threw away the stir stick and got ready for bed. The next evening I cleaned up the crumbs (as they were still there) and then my husband asked if I had noticed the dirty mark around the inside of the toilet bowl. Gross! I had seen what I thought was just where the water line was at, but sure enough, when you flush the toilet, you can see this black line around the inside of the bowl. That is uncalled for. Thankfully we were leaving the next morning. I also did not want to walk on the carpet with my bare feet -it was old, stained & was becoming thread bare in spots. I brought my shoes into the bathroom with me & after I dried off my feet, my shoes went on and didn't come off until I was seated on the bed and ready to get under the covers. Also, the breakfast is supposed to be from ----, well at -:-- we were leaving and I wanted to get a donut for the road trip, but they had put everything away already; they didn't even have the coffee urns out. Their reasoning was because it was a slow morning. Whatever. We will be back to San Antonio, but won't stay here.

Our company recently held a conference at the Detriot Westin Metro Airport Hotel and the experience was nothing but excellent. From a convienent location for both air travelers along with those who travelled by car to the excellent accomondations and service provided by a fabulous staff. As someone who drove to the meeting, would recommend considering the location for a easy connection for spending the night before that early flight. The room was first-class as all Westin locations offer.

Main thing in hotels favour is location and have rated it very good on the basis of getting what you pay for. Walking distance to Soldier Field and Millennium Park including the Bean is very nearby as well as other touristy stuff. If it was down to cost I would stay here again, but hotel is a little outdated.
Positives were staff were helpful and said yes to various requests. There is a cafe for breakfast which was fine and although we didn't use it there was also an Asian restaurant. There was also a subway and dunkin doughnuts round the corner as well as ---- nearby.
Negatives was the slow lift as only one was working and room was too hot at times. 
Overall though the hotel did the job for us.

I've now stayed at this hotel twice, once in early November ---- and this past week in Dec ----. I chose to come back to the hotel because of the incredible value that it offers, considering the price and location. I've stayed in several other hotels in the Times Square area - and in the past had to choose between a large room with updated furnishings and a reasonable rate. This hotel claims to offer stylish accomodations at a reasonable price - and they deliver.
Both times, my room was like the picture in terms of the decor. The first room was larger than the second, but I think this is because it's an old building that has some odd corners and angles. Your room size will depend upon where exactly in the hotel you are staying.
Free wifi, free breakfast. Small fitness center with two treadmills. Very comfortable - and only a few blocks from Time Square, Fifth Avenue, St. Patrick's Cathedral, Rockefeller Center. Easy walk to Grand Central Station or a bit longer to Penn Station. I stayed here on business as this was close to my clients, but it would also be a good spot for tourists.
I will go back to NYC again for business in the coming months, and intend to stay here again.

This was my second stay here. I first stayed - years ago with my teen daughter as a mid-week getaway. This time I went with my spouse who had one day of business in SF so we decided to do a long weekend. We checked in on a Thursday and left (reluctantly) Sunday. I love the location -- easy walking distance to Chinatown, North Beach, Union Square, the Ferry building. Also easy to take the cable car back up California Street from Embarcadero. Only caveat is, on the weekend. most of the immediately local sandwich-soup shops are closed, catering as they do to local business lunchers. 
Our room was very nice, if a little quirky. It was on the top (--th) floor and was a suite with a separate living room. I say quirky only because the windows were all small and very high up so they let in the light but you could not really look out. We didn't care -- to us it was charming and comfortable The bathroom was nicely appointed with marble and an extra large shower and some fresh roses in a vase - a very nice touch. We splurged on a breakfast at Bob's -- the Eggs Benedict were (was?) among the best I've had. Our room service breakfast was very good as well. We are part of the free Omni loyalty program. In ---- this got you free internet, plus free continental breakfast. This year they cut out the breakfast, giving you only coffee and juice of your choice. Still nice. The lobby is beautiful and the staff always courteous and helpful. I also appreciated the hot cider they have in the afternoons.
We used the gym which has a nice view of California Street and the cablecar. It's clean and well-equipped if small, but I will say the treadmill I used (the one on the right as you enter the room) was very noisy and I remembered I used the same one in ---- and apparently it hadn't been fixed.
I would definitely stay at the Omni again - it was a great value for SF and made for a very nice getaway.

Wow, how things can change in the hotel business! The hotel staff who used to be friendly, warm and welcoming have become distant, cold and arrogant. I'm talking about the front desk staff. Not at all helpful. Not at all concerned about the quality of interaction or serving the customer. 
The room was not at all acceptable: slow drains in the both the sink and the tub. Uncomfortable bed. HVAC system not yet set to air-conditioning so even the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""coolest"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" setting pumped out heat. We had the windows open ---- during our visit but the room was STILL like a sauna. 
I stopped by the front desk the morning after checking in and asked if the drains could be snaked. I was assured this would be taken care of, but it was not. 
That evening, I asked if we could be moved to another room because of the standing water in the tub and the sink AND the sauna-like conditions of the room. """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""We'll get back to you"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was the reply. Never heard back. 
I avoided the restaurant completely as I remembered the $-- breakfast buffet from my last visit. Too many good breakfast options within two blocks to pay that kind of money.
Noise. I realize that NYC hotels must cater to groups in order to fill rooms, but the noise in the lobbies from the hundreds of kids swarming the place was just wrong. There was never an attempt to control this hysteria. 
On the way out this morning, one of the concierge staff members followed me across the lobby trying to get me to accept the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""offer"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of a car service to the airport. He kept insisting that $-- was the same price as a cab. Ha! I'm not some first-time tourist to NYC. Finally I said, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Does that include tip and tolls, and will the driver accept a credit card?"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""No, no and no"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was the reply. Yea, right. I ended up at LaGuardia with a $-- trip charge and $- toll charge. With tip: $--. I know that extra money is a great motivator, but having the concierge staff pimp for the car service drivers is an annoyance, not a service.
On the good side, the housekeepers are wonderful. 
I need to find a new Times Square hotel. As I say in the title, I felt like I had revisited an old friend-relative who had suddenly stepped over that line into a death spiral. I can't help but wonder if the Park Central is spiraling down. It had been such a reasonably priced hotel option with decent service and a good atmosphere. 
It's very disappointing.

The location is decent, but the hotel needs some MAJOR remodelling. Rooms are old, smokey, and dirty. Bedspreads look dated. Bathrooms tiny. During my last stay, a bunch of kids were living next door with their mother, and you could hear every word until -- PM when they went to sleep (finally). I was in a room with an adjoining door that was paper thin. Old dinner plates with caked and dried out food from room service stayed in the halls outside rooms for nearly all day. Very unsanitary. TONS of tour buses and tour groups use this hotel. (Think...kids on field trips going to see Mama Mia). The people who work here are great and friendly. You get the impression that they know the place is a dump, but it's cheap and it's in Midtown so why bother fixing it up. Also, the elevators are extremely SLOW , cramped, and stop on nearly every floor. They do have a very good fitness center. The restaurant is so-so. Toast was dry (? day old bread??). Coffee was decent. The gift shop was a joke. The cash register wasn't working so they had to call in maintenance to fix it.

My Mom and I and her dog stayed at this Hotel because is was close to my daughters place, and wow were we pleased with this Hotel. The staff was so welcoming to us and our dog. The rooms were very pleasant with a little kitchen and bar table. The hotel was in a nice area and easy to walk to the main attractions in DC. The reason I loved this place is because of the staff, they couldn't have been nicer. Medionizo(sorry if I spelled that wrong) and Bernadette at the front desk were extremely helpful and friendly..anything we asked for we got right away.
When we came back we were welcomed home by David, he made us feel like family. He is extremely good at what he does, and helps you with whatever you need.
We had a very good breakfast at the restaurant. I liked the made to order omelets and waffles, very tasty. I thought it was reasonably priced, less than $-- a piece for brunch.
I would definitely recommend this hotel to my family and friends, and to anyone who wants a great hotel that is very pet and people friendly.
Thanks to David, Medionizo and Bernadette for a great stay in DC.

Arrived early before our check in time. The staff went above and beyond to get our room ready for us. Kids suites are spacious and clean. The restaurant offers a great selection of food and wait staff were also very friendly.

Be wary of this Hotel, esp if u book thru Priceline.com! We are Australians & planning to visit Big Apple this Xmas. Aft saving our hard earn $, cost us USD--K in air tickets, I offer a bid of $--- per nite for a -star Hotel in NYC & was accepted by Radisson Lexington. Instead of offering us a decent size room, we were given the cheapest & smallest room, called """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""petite room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", which has a going rate of $---per nite if booked directly w Radisson! The deceitful thing is; Priceline.com ad ertised on its website a savings of -----% if we bid for a hotel room. In our case, we only save $-per nite & not the -----% as claimed. When I contacted Priceline, they asked me to contact Hotel directly. I did that & Radisson pushed the responsibility back to Priceline. After many emails later, Radisson said they are happy to upgrade us to bigger room w King bed but have to pay upgrade fee! When I ask how much is the upgrade fee, both Priceline & Radisson would not tell me! How dodgy! We feel very cheated by both Priceline & Radisson! So beware folks!

Great hotel for downtown Chicago visit. Close to shopping, restaurants, lake, and Navy Pier. Great views, upscale ambience, wonerful service, and great staff. Water tower place shopping just feet away.

I have stayed at the Omni Birkshire hotel probably a dozen times over the last - years and the hotel never disappoints. Make sure you sign up as a preferred cutomer and you'll get the free wifi, turndown service, newspapers and drink of choice delivered to your room in the morning. The staff is very friendly, the rooms are clean, the beds are good and the location is just perfect! The gym is fine as well, but if you are running, it is nicer to run to Central Park instead of staying inside. Also, the restaurant is way too expensive, just go opposite the street for your breakfast and buy a bottle of wine at the Duane Rade and you are good to go!

I recently stayed at the Mondrian with some friends and absolutely LOVED it! It is in the heart of Soho and the views from the hotel are amazing. I felt relaxed as soon as I entered the hotel because of its cleanliness and the beautiful blue and white color scheme! The people at the reception desk were extremely friendly and very helpful in answering any questions that we had so I would say that the staff and service are the best that I've come across in the City. The bar decor is chic and fabulous and the food at Imperial is impeccable! I will definitely look no further when booking a hotel in New York City...The Mondrian Soho is the way to go!

The hotel is magnificent and is in an excellent location for doing anything in Chicago. I was there for a conference and the facilities were excellent. Free Wi-Fi, which is always good! The room was clean and the view from the --th floor was fantastic. Friendly and helpful staff. Great lobby for having a drink and meeting people.
British family with two teenage sons stayed three nights. As everyone seems to be saying, this is a class act in the mid-price range. Helpful staff, great location, clean and well-equipped rooms.

I stayed just one night for a business meeting. It's a very good location for business in the Loop, the Merchandise Mart, and is a short walk to the Art Istitute of Chicago, theater, and the opera. Macy's in the grand olf Marshall Field's building is a short walk away. It's not a bad walk to the tony mega-shopping district of North Michigan Avenue, although some may prefer a cab. 
While there are glitzier hotels, you can often get a good rate here since it is so large. You can spend the savings on a good dinner. The room felt recently renovated and very fresh (deatils below.) The public rooms are beautiful in a turn-of-the-last-century grandeur. I have visited the hotel a number of times over the years, and the most recent lobby redo is very welcome. There is a convivial bar and lounge area that makes for a very sociable atmosphere - some past years, the lack of furnishings made the place feel less inviting. Now it's back to being a social venue.
Room ----- had only a double bed as requested (usually there's more floor space when I ask for a smaller bed when I am staying alone than if the bed were larger or with two beds.) Very comfy bed and an assortment of pillows.
The room does not set records for spaciousness, but it felt like a good size as a result. There is plenty of drawer and storage space, although the closet felt small with the retro-fit safe. The view of was of an alley and airshaft, but it was also quiet, if dark. The room ALMOST has all the typical business-class amenities (ironing board, hairdryer, toiletries, etc.) EXCEPT a coffee maker, which I miss having. Also: no minibar or fridge, which I don't miss. Spotless housekeeping throughout.
Annoying things: there is the situation of the duvet without a top sheet, but you can remove the inside comforter easily if you are too warm and use the wool blanket stored in the closet. Also: there is an internet charge approx. $--, which I always find annoying, but less so since the rate was good.
The bathroom is very small, although it also felt recently renovated. There is good counterspace to spread out. The tub doesn't fill as fast as I'd like, but at least there is a tub, contrary to the shower-only rooms that seem to be a renovation trend at other hotels.
Very professional and friendly service throughout.
The hotel had a nice promotion when I was there for guests: a $-- credit for any spa services at the on-site spa. Unfortunately, I was too busy to take advantage.
There is a Starbucks at street level, and a newsstand-gift shop.
Some complain about the high cost of parking at hotels and lots in downtown Chicago. Get used to it. It is approx. $-- self-park and $-- valet at this hotel, which is in line with many other hotels. The City of Chicago tries to discourage ANYONE from driving car in, and charges high rates even for city lots. There is the odd open lot here and there where you can get away with under $-- for an early-in or late-in rate, but its how it is downtown.
While this hotel often charges a higher rack rate that you expect to Hilton policies, they often have very good rates at the last minute since this is a BIG hotel to fill up.
This hotel is gorgeous! Our room was so stylish and luxurious that we did not want to leave. Friendly service and great restaurants on the premises. I highly recommend and would stay here again.
Havecstayed at this hotel before and when I come back to the area I usually stay here...comfortable, quiet, and with a lot of extras.

I have been a guest at this hotel many times over the years and have always found it to be a pleasurable stay with great value. The location is unbeatable. Just a block off Union Square, within walking distance of shopping, well-known restaurants, theater, Bart and cable cars.
The rooms on the eleventh floor are a little bit more expensive but come with extra amenities (like bathrobes, cd players and continental breakfast at a nearby cafe). Bob, the concierge is a character and always willing to help. Stay in the rooms at the back of the hotel where it is quieter and you get a fabulous view of the city. 
No, it is not the most modern hotel in the City, however, it is updated, clean, has a wonderful theater and the adjacent Farallon Restaurant is one of the best in SF.

Firstly the hotel is in a fantastic location, and for the money I paid for my trip to the big apple I shouldn't really complain but...
The rooms are tiny, the bathrooms were smaller. We unfortunately checked in just as they had started the running their heating system, two night of sweltering heat, and the second night the radiator valve started clunking and banging, constantly. Next morning they were kind enough to change rooms for us, we moved our bags to a nicer room, a little larger with access to both sides of the bed. The radiator was stuck on full, no way to turn it off, but thankfully we had two small windows to open, and the air con was left on full.. Saving the planet. Oh and I sat on the bed and the frame collapsed! Got this fixed by the hotel, they wedged the bed together with a towel. Then that night we had a roll together mattress, It was a struggle. At this stage we felt there was no point in complaining. 
The staff were very helpful, very nice. The breakfast room was very small for the amount of guests, so it was a bit of a fight for a table, but there was everything there to set you up for the day.
The rooms were clean, but maybe just not clean looking for a decor point of view. This hotel needs an update, especially if you pay the going rate on their web site! That aside we had a great holiday, we could only treat this as a place to sleep, there was no luxury here.

Stayed for birthday-shopping trip. The location was great and I found the lift system easy to manage. On arrival due to jetlag we went to bed early but were kept awake with what sounded like a heating system - reception moved us straight away with no trouble. As its so big we had very little interaction with staff for our entire stay and it felt very like staying in an apartment. Great to be right in the centre of Times Square but theres probably better value to be had a couple of blocks away.

I took a picture of this hotel two years ago while walking around So Co and have wanted to stay here ever since! On my last visit to Austin for work it was during South By Southwest (unbeknownst to me) and when I called for reservations they just chuckled and said they were booked. I made my reservations early this time and after the drive from Houston was happy to finally arrive. I somehow missed the parking lot that sits between Hotel San Jose and Joes coffee but found a spot on the street right in front and just stayed there. Check in was easy and I found my room easily. It was a corner room right on the street and at first I thought the noise might bother me but windows were thick and I liked having windows on two walls and the natural light that streamed in.
Yes, the decor is very """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""minimalist chic"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and may not be for everyone, personally I loved it...from the concrete floors to the Malin and Goetz toiletries. It's everything my country dream cottage would be! 
The pool is small and I didn't find it very inviting but that isn't what I was there for. 
Location is terrific and in the middle of everything...I highly recommend The Snack Bar two doors down (especially for the live entertainment al fresco on Wine Down Wednesday). Joes coffee the next morning was also a treat!
I will plan my trip far in advance again so that I have a chance to stay here!

I stayed at the Affinia -- in a - bedroom suite (- queen beds) with my wife and parents on a long weekend trip to New York.
We found the location to be excellent for seeing Manhattan - easy to walk to Central Park and the big shops around -th avenue, and also close to Grand Central station and Rockafella. The subway on Lexington & --st is great to get around most tourist routes.
The hotel staff were always friendly and helpful, and we were made to feel that no request was too much trouble. The doormen were well groomed and extremely cheerful, whatever time we saw them!
The suite itself was luxuriously large and very clean as well as comfortable, and the hotel provides beds with memory foam matresses and a choice of several types of pillows, which made sleeping there even more enjoyable.
We would thoroughly recommend this hotel to anyone wishing to stay in New York!

I will not stay at this hotel again. Upon arrival I was told that I was double-booked. I checked with Expedia and my bank and that was not true. The room was newly renovated but very small. The internet access turned out to be wired-only with a $-.---day surcharge. They provide awful brew-your-own coffee in the room and nothing in the hotel lobby. Parking is by valet only and they charge $-- a day. 
I probably could overlook the above but what occurred on checkout was an absolute disgrace. During my stay I noticed that my cell phone was not working well (it's a very reliable quad-band cell phone that i have used globally). The building is an old structure that is not suitable for cell communications. During the course of a conversation with an important customer, I was forced to terminate the call and quickly use the hotel landline for a US domestic call. The call lasted about -- minutes. When I got my bill at checkout they charged me over $-.-- per minute for the call. I was in a rush to get to the airport so I could not address this with the management staff in person. When I called back and talked to the manager (Christian) he agreed to only refund about $-- of the $-- phone charge. The fact that a company would think they could get away with such outrageous charges in today's world is simply unbelieveable.. It appears they haven't noticed that long distance is a commodity with fiercely competitve rates.
My advice is to stay away - take your business to a company that doesn't try to generate revenue through """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""gotcha"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" practices like this.

We recently had our wedding at the Sofitel Philadelphia. Most of our guests also stayed at the hotel after the wedding. We couldn't have picked a better place for the wedding and our guests. The rooms were well appointed and very comfortable. The hotel staff was very attentive and welcoming. The food at the wedding was delicious! The next morning we hosted a private brunch, which was very nicely set up. Not one detail was overlooked. I highly recommend this hotel!

Found the staff friendly and helpful. Location is great if you want to be near it all and are not shy a walking. Once you park in their underground garage (charge imposed) you can walk to most anything you may need. Full Ocean view room w-balcony was clean and functional. The view is fantastic. The boardwalk below is very busy with all sorts of peeps during the day. Our stay was everything we expected and maybe a bit more.

This is one very tired Sheraton. It is much drearier in person than it is in its website pictures. The facade is dingy, the lobby is outdated and worn, the elevators and hallways also very dingy. The room was clean, but it was beyond dated. The bathroom was the size of a broom closet. The popcorn ceiling in the bedroom was badly patched in a one or two places. 
The room contained a sofa - no way I was going to sit on that. It looked like it had been there for many years, who knows what it has seen! The bed was clean and comfortable, though. The carpet, while threadbare, was clean enough I suppose.
One positive is that the people at the front desk were polite and efficient, as were the airport shuttle drivers. 
The rates here are not exactly low, and Sheraton has spent hundreds of millions of dollars renovating other properties. So why don't they pressure this franchise's owners to do the same?
Also, I love how when the manager responds to comments on TripAdvisor, she conveniently calls each review positive while ignoring the very obvious criticisms that many reviewers (besides me) wrote about. Seriously, spend some money to fix this place up. It is dismal.

Overall a very good experience, with good service (welcoming glass of wine a nice touch after a long business day) and good facilities: free wi-fi, books by Kerouac and Ginsberg to read in room and so on. Adjacent Cafe de la Presse, a good French bistro, is used for room service food. My room was on floor - and with rather too much external clanging from adjacent store backlots in the very early morning to make this an entirely satisfactory stay in SF.
We stayed during the Christmas holiday. The front desk staff was pleasant as well as the bellman and doorman. Our room was okay. It was clean, well kept. Conveniently located. We would stay again.

We stayed a couple of nights here.
The rooms are okay, they are clean. The hotel is located just behind the Empire State, in the Korean street. It was pretty hard for me to find a hotel in Manhattan with a reduced budget. This is a good option, although next time I would search something closer to Times Square.

You'll be amazed by the semplicity and yet the surprise of the menu. rich pearls of flavours with an incredible balance between spices, herbs and vegetables. the pita bread comes warm to taste the dippings. hummus and yogurt dippings were very smooth and tasty.
cotkails are made of fresh fruits and they are the perfect combination to the food: the cucumber with a touch of chile is refreshing and tickling for the mouth while the blueberry one is amazingly well balanced in sweetness...could drink more than one easily.
all the senses are embraced in the decadend atmosphere, a little in the --´s mood, with soft light and art deco inspiration. 
I will definetly go back.

I stayed at the HoJo in Manhattan for the first week of a three-week stay required for business. I have to say that I was more than glad to move to a New Jersey hotel for the final two weeks. I booked my hotel on Travelocity, so I was stuck with my reservation for that week (I was already charged for the room in advance). It was definitely off the beaten path (way over on --th Avenue, further west than the ads had made me believe).
I arrived and had to make sure that the front desk attendant didn't charge my room AGAIN to my credit card (I had to do the same thing when I left at the end of the week as they were ready to charge my card again). The hotel has -- floors, yet I was given the room number """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""----."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Wondering what this meant, the clerk told me to press """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""B"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in the elevator. I made my way to the basement-breakfast room, where there was one door marked ---- with a piece of paper. I couldn't believe I had been sent to the basement, but tried my key -- low and behold, I made my way into a closet-sized hotel room. It was a good thing I was staying alone because two people could not have easily passed each other in the short hallway from door to bed. There was a (small) armoire for my clothes, the bed doubled as the desk chair, and the flat-screen TV on the wall had no remote (I finally managed to wrangle one from the front desk two days later). 
I had to get up early in the mornings, so I went to bed early, something that was a bit of a challenge since I was on the other side of the wall from the breakfast area, a place for people to congregate and be loud, apparently. The vending machines were right outside my door and during an incident of kicking and banging on a malfunctioning machine, I heard the front desk clerk say """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""boy, I hope that girl isn't in her room right now."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" No such luck.
I will say that it was clean and the bathroom was about normal size and I had no problems there. However, this hotel is on my list of places never to return to again.

The hotel was fine. The staff was fine. The parking was fine. What was not fine was the fact that guests cannot control the temperature in their guest rooms. My room was sweltering as there was nothing to be done about it... the best they can offer is """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cool air."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" And it wasn't cool.... 
Don't stay here if you care at all about the temp of your room.

We chose the Hotel Whitcomb due it's proximity to the theater district. I was traveling with my daughter and wanted a safe location central to our excusions (SF Ballet and Wicked at the Orpheum.) The staff was excellent at every contact. The rooms were clean and quiet. (Although I paid for $-- upgrade.) The room size was small but ample for two. It is after all, an older style hotel. Nighttime security was also very good and made two women feel quite safe. We enjoyed the hotel so much we added another night's stay!

We stayed at The Mark back in Dec. It was fabulous. The customer service was stellar. The staff knew and remembered our names almost instantly. I've never experienced that. We were upgraded to a suite just because which was awesome. It was spacious and very clean, the beds were really comfy. I appreciated the complimentary apples that were left daily. Great location, central park is right out the front door to the right a half block. The only thing I can think that was even inconvenient was that our bathtub plug stuck so the bath water was left for housekeeping and that wasnt an issue. It was an amazing stay in a beautiful hotel. Highly recommended.

Reception was friendly and cold at the same time. Elevators are slow and small , general apearence of hotel is used old and dirty. I would not advise business trbelers to use this hotel surely not if you want a restfull sleep you might be surprised by the garbage collectors who find it amusing while they are working infrint of hotel to shout and laugh very loud so the entire hotel would wake up. Note garbage collectors are infront of the hotel at -h-- in the morning.

Moved here from Marriott Marquis on Time Square. The service was night and day from the moment we checked in to the moment we checked out. The front desk staff (can't remember the name -- a black female) was very friendly. I was in such a bad mood from my check out at the other Marriott and she pretty much made my day. Room was small but typical for NYC - I got no complaint. It was clean and we also got a personal note from the cleaning staff -- nice touch. Business center has everything that we need. Didn't try their cafe or other amenities so I can't comment on them. H&M, Grand Central, and a bunch of shopping and eateries are just around the corner. This is my top choice for a NYC vacation.

I checked into the Gateway Sheraton hotel after being in several , Horrible hotels in the LAX area.......once I arrived , I was Greeted very warmly and checked into my room quickly. I had several questions about restaurants and other fun things to do in the area and called on the operator Dianne or help. I could not have asked for a warmer and kinder person. She was informative and made my stay here at the hotel very Special! If you ever check into the hotel , ask for Dianne , she will make your stay feel like Home!!!
This place won't knock your socks off but if you're looking for a decent place at a reasonable value within a stone's throw of the airport, this is it.

I visited Seattle for a --day convention, and was pleased by the overall boutique feel of this hotel, the friendly staff, and the awesome bellman Tom, who helped with anything and everything. Great, comfortable room. I had a few minor issues and the staff handled them quickly and appropriately. Very close to Washington State Convention Center. Walkable to the important sites in downtown Seattle. I would definitely stay here again.

Went for a business trip to LA and was accompanied by my wife on the trip. Found the hotel staff to be very friendly and welcoming on arrival. Took a large one bedroom suite with a full kitchen (fridge freezer, microwave, dishwasher, the works!), sitting area, bathroom and what felt to me like the most comfy bed in the world! The hotel has just been fully renovated and is spotlessly clean and tidy. It has a spacious lobby and bar area, and we had complementary breakfast. There is a big supermarket across the road which is useful for buying food to cook in your room, and at the bus stop accross the road (outside the Crowne Plaza) buses stop every hour running to Hollywood. We loved this hotel, it was perfect for us- comfortable and the perfect base for us in Beverly Hills. Just wished the hotel also had a pool, the only feature which i found lacking .

We went for my son's BMT graduation Aug ----. I arranged for late arrival since we were driving in. Our room was ready without any problems. It was nice and clean...love the beds with the nice fluffy comforters and pillows. The room was nice and cold. Temperatures were --- ---- outside when we visited so the cool room was nice to come back to everyday. My airman wanted to just come to the room and relax - cool down after spending the morning out in the hot weather in his full dress blues. We had clean towels every day. Beds were made everyday and our maid even folded up my daughters blanket and fluffed the pillow she brought from home. The hotel was nice and clean and everyone was friendly and helpful. They have maps of the local area and Lackland AFB and were knowledgeable about the graduation events, gate closers, and area attractions. Pool and patio were nice and clean. The decor now has a southwest flare not white like in the internet pictures. I didn't have any problems with my bill. It was the exact price as what I booked on the Internet. I did agree to the --%additional fee for incidentals if I used them (like room service) but was not charge this fee because I did not use them. Our room was located right by a stair well by the ice machine and vending machines so this was convenient for my kids. I was happy with everything at this hotel. We did not spend much time in the hotel since we were visiting with our airman, but it was always a pleasant experience to come back to a clean, cool room and friendly staff. It is within minutes from all the attractions - everything is easy to get too. If you're not sure where anything is just ask the staff or access internet on the computer located in the lobby. I was going to book a hotel on the Riverwalk in downtown San Antonio, but am glad I didn't. It cost half the money to stay at this Holiday Inn and it was only a few minutes from the base and that matters when you have to be there at -am for graduation events and your airman wants you to pick him up first thing in the morning when he has town pass. Local businesses & restaurants are just down the street.

Downfall for me was they allow smoking in the rooms. I used Febreze and candles but it never got the smell out of the room and I stayed for - days. No clock radio, no microwave but the mini fridge worked. Another thing is it's RIGHT next to the train tracks so it can be loud. It is walking distance to Old Town so that (in my opinion) was the best thing about this place. You can also catch the trolley to downtown a block away from the motel. Another thing is you have to pay for Wi-Fi or you can use it in the motel lobby for free on their internet kiosk.

I had the pleasure of getting a job assignment working for a lower Manhattan agency this past month. Our rooms were booked at the Holiday Inn on Layfette Street near Canal Street. Upon arriving we were excited as the Hotel is located in the heart of the Chinatown-Little Italy area and near a major subway route. The lobby is on a second floor and the bellboy staff is on the first floor. They have a small unattended bar area with some computer terminals for internet use. When we got to our room on the --th floor we noticed immediately the lack of drawer space. The beds were crammed near a closet and the bathroom was very small. Upon talking to some New Yorkers I learned the building was converted into a Hotel and that is why it was so cramped. The bed linens seemed cheap for even a Holiday Inn and constanly slipped off the bed during the night. There was some train noise because the -, N, R lines run below. 
The restaurant Pacifica is just as one of the above reviewer's described. Fake eggs, Lo Mein, small Danish type rolls, sausage and broccoli.....not your average breakfast fare? Take note that the management discourages you from ordering off the menu. I was told they """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""only had one cook"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" working on the weekend which makes no sense. The weekend would logically be the busiest time you would think and to be constantly short staffed is not a good impression to make. Also the vouchers rewards members get are good for - dollars off a breakfast buffet that costs $--.--. The restaurant actually makes money off the Holiday Inn. Take note that if there are - people to a room you get vouchers per couple not per person and this was a surprise to my co-workers. Although, the management was helpful I could tell there was definitely a division on how each business was run. In fact, when we were dining Pacifica sent a company representative to inspect the site and very was disappointed in the way the restaurant was run. We overheard this information and I am sure other customers did as well. 
On the plus side the neighborhood was nice and Little Italy and Chinatown was nearby. It was nice to have other options for dining in the immediate vicinity.

There is really nothing more that I can add to all of the positive reviews written by others. We try to go to The Peninsula once a year, and I always look forward to staying at the hotel. Yes, as others have stated, it is expensive, and if you want over the top glam for the money this is not the right place for you. If you want very comfortable, under stated luxury, then The Peninsula fits the bill.
Service is impeccable and the rooms are designed to anticipate your needs. I have not experienced a hotel room that is laid out as well as the rooms here. Also, we have never done the chocolate late night buffet, but I've heard many good things. We have had the Sunday brunch several times, and it is outstanding each time. Once again it is expensive, but it includes a wide range of options of extremely high quality. I'm looking forward to returning soon.

Rancho Bernardo is a master planned community about -- miles east of the coast in San Diego county. The Rancho Bernardo Inn is a lushly landscaped Spanish style resort with spa and golf course in the heart of the community and just a few minutes from Interstate --. We live nearby and go there frequently to play the course or go to the beautiful spa but until this week, we never stayed there. Our room was comfortable and fresh and had a wonderful balcony overlooking the golf course. We enjoyed lunch and dinner at the outdoor restaurant, The Veranda. The service was impeccable and we were always met with a smile. The spa and spa pool are newer and beautiful. We did not use any spa services so did not have access to those facilities. The hotel pool and spa are a bit dated but have the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""old California"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" feel. All in all, a wonderful place.

I stayed here at the beginning of December ---- and after reading some of the reports was very worried before I arrived but the stay was great.
My double double room was exactly as pictured. There was morning coffee available in the foyer every morning.
The reception staff were very friendly and the bellman helpful. Two lightbulbs blew when I was staying and they were changed within minutes of my call to reception.
Clean, comfortable and very convenient. Recommended.

This hotel was amazing! It exceeded all our expectations and the staff was more than helpful. The room was spacious, clean, smelled good and gave us a great view of chicago. The breakfast that was included was great and there was more than enough food for all of the guests. The front desk staff really made our stay special. They gave great advice on where to eat, how to use the transit system, and awesome suggestions for night life! I cannot wait to go back!

Stayed here for a convention. Great location directly across from the Convention Center and at the entrance to the historic gaslamp district. Free wireless internet a plus! Room was spacious and very comfortable. Great views over the harbour and out to the Pacific. Staff incredibly helpful at check-in and throughout the stay. Restaurant pricey and breakfast offernigs just OK but dozens of great cafe's and restaurants within a very short walking distance. Would definately stay here again.

If you don't have a car, I'm not sure how you could even get to this hotel. This is a new beautiful hotel, but you have to take back roads to get to it even though it sits near the freeway. The room is comfortable and roomy. Breakfast here is not free, but there is a cafe where you can purchase food, but we did not eat there. The hotel was very quiet while we were there.

Interesting combination of modern and old-fashioned. Enjoyable place to stay. Service-oriented and they try hard, but they don't quite have their act completely together. It took an extremely long time to get something delivered to the room. Room air-conditioning went out for a bit, and I was told by maintenance that I shouldn't turn it up too high and was then told by hotel staff to ignore that advice (it did work for the rest of my stay).

My daughter attends college in the Georgetown area, so I've stayed there several times. The rooms are adequate and the elevator is speedy. My complaint is the slamming doors. They will be the last thing you hear when you go to sleep and the first thing you'll hear on rising.

The hotel is tucked in the middle of a high tech industrial park - the majority of the hotel's clientele would be young high tech professionals.
The pool is not heated and is outdoors. The pool is located in the center atrium, so it's out of the sun for a good part of the day. I was expecting that in August, the pool temp was decent. However, my kids started to shiver within a short amount of time.
Hotel service was also very good.
Would certainly stay there again.

In the interest of full disclosure we stayed here on points so i have no idea if this place is worth what the going rate (incidentally we stayed here on points because every hotel in chicago was charging ---+ a night!)
The service was bad but i believe the hotel had just hosted some army convention and was booked solid so every hotel guest was in the process of checking out and none of the rooms were ready - granted we were probably early for our reservation.
I loved the beds! But they were really squishy and apparently they were not the sheraton sweet sleepers that people are used to.
We got a room with a river view, not sure what this would be classified as. I liked it, the hotel was very convenient for walking.

Hotel was booked via travel agent on there advice.
However this hotel is tired and needs updating, I was very unhappy about the building work noise. Kitchen area in room was old and out of date , bathroom just OK.
Main bedroom lounge areas were acceptable for a short stay.
Staff in general were very helpful. Good central location for New York, could have had some visitor guides on display for guests.
Would I stay in this hotel again possibly not as it is not great value for money.

Actually, they sold it as Holiday Inn, so it was quite hard to find.

I really don't have a bad thing to say about this hotel. It was very much like a standard Courtyard, except it's in a renovated midtown Manhattan office building. We had reserved two rooms and because of a reservation snafu that was remedied, were given a corner king room upgrade. The second room was a standard king with sofabed. Given the office building past, the windows were very large with nice views. One room had a view of the East River (just a slice of it) and the towers on the East Side, whereas the Corner King had sweeping views looking north on -rd Avenue and of the landmark Citicorp Building across the street.
Both rooms were very clean and the bathrooms spotless. The sofabed room lacked sheets, so a call to the front desk was made and while we were out, the sheets were delivered, but we still had to make the sofabed ourselves. Requests for additional shampoo and even toothpaste were fulfilled promptly. Our rooms ranged from ------- sq. feet, with the corner king especially spacious. The pillows were down feather and the mattresses low, but comfortable. The bathrooms were basic and were outfitted with some sort of Corian material. It wasn't marble, just functional.
Hallways were very private and with only -- rooms on our floor, very quiet. There was a little bit of city noise from -rd Ave. below--horns, an ambulance--but nothing too disturbing. One should expect some of that in the city.
The breakfast room and lounge, located on the --th floor, looked fine, but with a summer street fair on -rd Ave. out front, we chose to sample the local vendors. Several restaurants, including a Smith and Wollensky's steakhouse, are within a block or two away, and across the street is the Citigroup Center with a Barnes & Noble and other restaurants, shops and pubs.
Times Square is a bit of a walk away, but still easily accessible. We walked all over from Grand Central Station to Times Square to Central Park and liked that the Courtyard was a little away from all of the push and shove of the Times Square area. A subway station was right across from the hotel, good for heading down to Lower Manhattan or Chinatown.
While still big-city outrageous, the room rates were not bad for Manhattan standards. Parking is $-- and it took -- minutes for the staff to retrieve our car.
The staff was helpful throughout and the rooms clean and in good repair. A good top to bottom renovation would really make this an upscale place. As it stands, if you want a good place to crash in the city, and you are not expecting a mint on your pillow or a lavish spa, I would recommend this Courtyard.

We stayed for - nights in the Beresford Arms, was the last part of our three weeks' honeymoon in the U.S.
With a price of $--- per night, which is very reasonable for San Francisco standards, we were very happy. Although the website looks great, in all honesty, the rooms in real life are pretty old-fashioned. It all has a real --'s feel to it. 
Pro's:
- junior suite is very large, with old kitchen and bathroom but all works well
- very quiet, no noise from street
- location: we did not find the area bad at all! san francisco has a lot of homeless people, but virtually none in the area of the hotel. it is only a - minute walk to Union Square and there are a lot of restaurants in the area.
- extremely helpful, though slightly aloof front desk
- valet parking fast and not too expensive for city standards ($--)
Con's:
- no internet access in room, only in hotel lobby
- breakfast very simple
- no airconditioning (but did not need this either in mid-July)
Overall: great stay in central San Francisco, personally we did not mind the old-fashioned rooms. Everything works, is there if you need it. You're in SF to view the city anyway! We did have a car (roundtrip) and even though everybody says you don't need it in SF, we found it helpful and it certainly allowed us to see the city in under - days.
Would definitely stay again!

It was the least expensive (parking incl) accommodation just about in all of SF when I stayed there, due to the America's Cup Sailing Race. the location is just above the Galleria mall. You don't have to leave the hotel to enter the shopping mall. The rooms are nice and the hotel is very clean. The staff is very helpful and courteous. The parking is the only downturn because you have to park on the shopping mall parking lot unless you get the valet parking.

We just returned from a much-needed vacation to Chicago. We stayed at the Fitzpatrick Hotel and overall had a good experience there. Three of the great things about this hotel include location, comfort and service. This hotel is located one block off the Mag Mile and is right in the center of the shopping district, convenient access to both ends is within walking distance. The room was spacious and comfortable, bed was a dream. I honestly don't think I've ever had a better night's sleep in a hotel. No noises from other rooms so it must be well insulated. The hotel staff was ready and able to meet our needs, beginning with the bell hops-great guys! Very helpful. 
The down side of our stay would involve - things. We are American and weren't familiar with the Irish way. We ordered room service one morning and found some kind of white pepper served, which tasted wierd to us. Also, how can you not have grape or strawberry jam? Orange marmelade and raspberry jam might be okay for adults, but not my kids!! The other issue was the way the room was set up. We selected a Queen suite. The virtual tour online is somewhat deceiving. On the web it looks as though the bedroom area is separate from the living room, but beware, it is all one room. If you want any privacy, don't go that route. I saw someone else's post on Trip Advisor, but took the virtual tour and thought that person was just picky. Believe me, she was right! The TV just swivels from one area to the other, so you're all there in the same room. We made do, but it would have been nice to have some privacy.
Overall, we had a good experience at the Fitzpatrick. I would stay there again.

We just came back from a one week stay at the kitano in NYC. We had a wonderful time. This hotel is highly recommended. Great location and wonderful views to the Empire State. Every time we returned to the hotel, it just felt like home.
I will surely come back to this hotel.

Great price, we got an amazing deal for - nights!! Great location, great roof top bar! Rooms were small typical for NYC but spotless and the bed was super comfy! Great linens- robes & toiletries, no iPod doc tho :( . Most of the staff were great some didn't seem to notice guests unfortunately! All in I would deffinately stay again, great smell of insence in the lobby at night... Worth a visit!

We stayed there on our honeymoon trip through california.
The hotel is situated in the Fisherman's Wharf in SF, which is a calm and interesting part of the city near the Bay.
We reserved shortly before going on our trip and this was almost the last hotel which was available in SF. We only could get a room with two Queen Size beds. When we arrived, we talked with the very friendly lady at the desk and she gave us a free upgrade to a Hypo-Allergenic Room with a King Size Bed.
The room was quite big and very calm, with a huge marble bathroom. The view was not exceptional but the quality of the room was so good that we couldn't complain.
The breakfast is not included but for a few dollars you can eat in the Hyatt-Restaurant. The quality and choice of the food is exceptional.
Around the hotel you have a high choice of Restaurants and you are near many tourist-attractions.
Sadly you have to pay quite a lot for the car-parking but this is usual in SF, you can't park anywhere else.

Writing this for my husband who was beside himself with how bad this hotel was - even for a one-night last-minute stay. Place was dirty - hallway, rooms, bathroom in particular. Joke of a restaurant. To use his words """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Nasty!""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""

Was referred to this Hotel and could not have been happier with the choice. Two blocks from Times Square! Rooms were clean and tidy, beds were comfortable, daily breakfast was great and free access to the internet certainly made keeping up with news from home a breeze. Would have no hesitation in going back next time I visit the Big Apple.

Brought my -- year old daughter and a couple of her friends to the Az Grand for a sleepover-birthday party last weekend. Had heard the water park at this hotel was best in Phoenix. They did not disappoint.
Check-in was a breeze, valets and bell staff very accommodating to all our bags, snacks, and paraphernalia. Room was beautiful and was located in wing with other family staycationer families. Was a fun atmosphere and the kids had a blast.
Oasis Water Park was great, the lazy river loops around, very relaxing. There are little lounge areas all around park where you can relax and get away from the water park mayhem. I did not ride slides but kids liked them, said they were fast and fun.
Lobby marketplace was a great place to get morning coffee and sit and enjoy cool post-monsoon morning. Did not eat at Bar-Restaurant in Lobby but it smelled wonderful.
Highly recommend for a Summer retreat!

My Mom and I stayed here for Mother's Day. The King City View Room was HUGE and extremely comfortable and inviting, very warm. The beds were excellent. The bathtub was amazing with well designed hardware. The color palette was beautiful. I would highly reccomend the pool and fitness center. Some of the room service and spa menu items are outrageously expensive, even comical sometimes, but there was a great variety on the menu, which is great for people with special diets, or just someone feeling like a peanut butter banana panini is a more interesting choice for breakfast then your ususal coffee, muffin, eggs bacon...

I usually stay with my family while in Houston but I was with other people on a road trip and didn't want to bother anybody so we stayed here for one night. And we pretty much got what we paid for, just a place to shower and sleep basically. although i did find a dead roach under the sink in the bathroom and the parking spots being pretty small i have no complaints. my friend complained about not being able to watch B.E.T. but im not sure any Holiday Inns have that channel because i stayed at the Holiday Inn Centennial Park in Atlanta (which is where BET's headquarters is located) and that one didnt have BET either. but i dont watch that channel and the only reason i knew the one in ATL didn't have it was because she went with us there too haha. The staff was great, location is good for me, i didnt eat while i was there because when im in Houston i usually go to Wings N More or Timmy Chans so i have no idea on the food or bar, but overall the hotel is just like any average hotel.

We stayed at the Parker House Sunday and Monday night of Labor Day weekend. The room was small but very nice, and the staff were friendly and accommodating. 
The location was great - right in the middle of the city, near to everything that we wanted to do, and next to a bunch of T stops. The lobby was very pretty as well. 
Overall, a very nice experience, for not a lot of money.

Hotel was great. Staff very friendly, free internet handy, elevator ancient but great music and very quirky. Everything was quite old, but everything worked and was very clean. Great location to, can definitely recommend.

My husband and I stayed at this hate for the weekend of -th - -th Feb ----. I booked the hotel some time ago, before some of the negative comments so upon re-checking the website before I set off I was a little apprehensive about what to expect. 
We arrived late and were greeted by a rather unfriendly bellboy, not the end of the world but certainly a long way of a warm welcome. 
Our room was fine, we’d been upgraded to a king and it was fairly comfortable. In the morning however I noticed that the bathroom hadn’t really been cleaned all that well. I would stay the standard of cleanliness was debatable, not too bad though if you’re not fussy.
