On a positive the location was great. The hotel cost $-- a night (booked directly – no breakfast) although I did notice Expedia had rooms going for $-- a night. We didn’t’ spend an awful lot of time in the hotel, I do think you get what you pay for, nothing more nothing less.

Hotel has been recently remodeled with upscale contemporary decor. Rooms were extremely comfortable and electronic check-in-out is extremely quick and convenient. Rooms were very large and very comfortable. Location is great, right off the freeway, less than five minutes to the airport and right in the center of a major shopping district. The staff was very helpful. There is a free airport shuttle (limited hours) and we were able to leave our car there for an extended period of time while we were out of town. Freeway noise was very limited and not really an issue. Not necessarily the best location for romance, relaxation or sight seeing, but great for travel, business and shopping.
Great location, clean rooms, free Internet, new flat screen tv. Only downfall is the rooms are not that big, but we didn't spend a whole lot of time in it, so not an issue,

Hotel is clean and well-organized for the business traveler. Breakfast included hot items, pancakes, fresh fruit, juice, coffee, soda pop, etc. Free parking in covered garage was helpful in the rain. The only negative thing that I may mention is that there is no free wireless available. Hopefully, the chain will address this in the near future.

This was my favorite extended stay ever. How many good things can I say? I wanted to move in permanently!!! I stayed here for - weeks for work in October ----, and hated to leave. For the money, campared to other similar standard hotels i've stayed in, in other major cities (rome, paris etc) this hotel is very overpriced but maybe this is just NY. Bed was very small for a double but the room was clean. Best thing about this hotel is the location, just -- mins walk to Times sq. and close to metro stations. Quiet area as far as Manhatten goes.

The Tuscan Inn is typical of the city hotels we've stayed at in the past. That basically means it costs a lot more than a roadside-highway exit hotel but isn't quite as nice.
We heard numerous things about the Fisherman's Wharf area, and many of them were true. There is plenty to do during the day because of the endless shops and restaurants, and transportation is available to take you to all places in the city as well as other destinations like Alcatraz. At night the area takes on a different persona with homeless people hanging around the darkness, but at no point did we ever feel unsafe walking the streets. The weirdest thing was how everything seemed to close between - and -- at night when there seemed to be so many tourists lurking about.
The hotel, located a few blocks from Fisherman's Wharf as well as Ghiardelli Square, has a nice Italian theme that carries into the lobby as well as the uniforms for the parking valets. Speaking of parking, you're going to have to pay and it's going to have to be valet service, as there are no free-self park lots that are part of the hotel. Not only is it pricey at $---day, but having nothing but valet parking means you have no access to your car unless you have one of the valets fetch it from the lot for you.
Our hotel room was very small and felt absolutely cramped when we had our two suitcases opened on the floor. The bathroom containing the toilet and the shower was also very small, not to mention the sink and counter directly outside of it. The overall look was fairly bland and a bit dated, but all of the furniture was in excellent shape and nothing appeared worn, dirty or neglected. Two negatives: Turning the bathroom light on also turns the counter light on, meaning a middle-of-the-night trip to the bathroom means the whole side of the room gets illuminated; and the wooden shutters that were installed in place of traditional curtains to add to the hotel's theme do absolutely nothing to keep the room dark once the sun comes up.
I'm sure there are better hotels in the area but considering how expensive most are, the Tuscan Inn ends up being a relative bargain. If you're willing to accept a hotel that can best be described as clean and comfortable, this one will do you just fine.

We traveled to Boston the see the Sox and were looking for a place to stay and considered Priceline as we have many times as most rooms in Boston are expensive. I stayed at this hotel last weekend (June ----) and was met with no major surprises—--good or bad. The staff was courteous but not overly attentive, the room was clean but a little shabby, and the property itself had a worn, comfortable feel about it. I booked through Priceline and got a King smoking room for $-- a night. Not bad, considering the best Internet rate offered through Doubletree was $--. The nightly rates go up to about $---, but the rooms at the Doubletree are essentially the same...I don't believe Doubletree Austin features two-room suites. I wouldn't dream of paying $--- for one night's stay here simply because The Doubletree doesn't offer the service level or room accoutrements to make it worth my while. However, Austin hotel and motel prices can soar outrageously high due to a steady tourist flow, frequent conventions, and Austin's many family-friend visitors of UT students. Even a Motel - can easily set you back -- pops a night, so again, if booked directly through on online discount site the Doubltree may exceed the budget traveler's expectations. 
This location is not directly downtown, but is less than - minutes from the Capital and downtown attractions (Guadalupe, -th Street, etc.) The location was one of my favorite things about this hotel...closest to the action but not directly in it.
My check-in around -PM went quickly and smoothly. The desk clerk didn't explain any hotel policies or help familiarize me with the property. I asked all my questions up front and although he was courteous he wasn't exceptionally helpful unless I asked specific questions. Parking is $-.-- a day with in and out privileges. The garage is easy to navigate and thankfully I didn't have any nightmare experiences with bad keycards. You must use your keycard to access the garage and to maneuver around floors and gain hallway access from the (very beat up) elevators. The room smelled musty, but Austin can have high humidity and the odor was not overwhelming. The room was clean (to the eye) and the AC was on full blast. A good AC is important for an Austin summer day and my room managed to stay cool but still produced that danged drip, drip, drip from condensation (which seems to be the rule for motel ACs). The room showed signs of age and wear and the TV was set up in the worst possible location for any comfortable viewing from the bed. The bathroom had free coffee-tea, a hairdryer, and the standard features for this level of room.
Room service rates are typically outrageous, as is their PPV. Room service hours and menu are limited, but will do in a pinch. I didn't sample any of the Doubletree fare.
The room was quiet (even though they put me next to the ice maker vestibule) and I slept comfortably on a very, very firm mattress. (Might have been off-putting to some sleepers.)
Two nights later my check-out went as quickly as my check-in, even though a reservations clerk was squabbling with an unhappy guest at the next counter. (The unhappy guest was not reimbursed for her stay and no one agreed to take responsibility. A lot of buck-passing, but hey, it's not trying to be a - star hotel. But I was glad it wasn’t me with the complaints.) The clerk was not going to charge me for my parking (her oversight) so I did the honest thing and I told her I KNEW I owed her money. Austin folks, especially the natives, dance to the beat of a very specific drum....so expect some healthy doses of flakiness from the staff. And all of Austin for that matter. 
All in all I would give this property a - out of - and if I could ensure a similar rate on my next stay in Austin I would book there again. 
PROS: Clean, good location, quiet and safe.
CONS: Most rooms open to an outside hallway, musty odors through room and hotel, limited service

This is really really really convenient to everything inside the loop and very reasonable, and the staff is very nice. BUT... I stayed here one night and couldn't take any more ... the bed was like a rock and I might have gotten - hours sleep if that much. Very poor quality mattress, I have slept better in a Motel -. Other negatives were that hallways can be dim to the point of being downright creepy at night, and my recliner was broken (and didn't recline) but I don't care about that so much. I would suggest asking for a front view though, as almost half of the rooms face a parking garage.
Pros are price and location, and the fact that my the room was very clean and amenable otherwise. The kitchen in particular was *spotless* and you hardly ever see that in a home-away-from-home style place. If you do like an untra-firm mattress, this may well be the place for you.

Stayed there for - nights. It was my first time in NYC and I was afraid the hotel would be far from all the main areas for tourists, but it is actually a great location with several subway lines less than - minutes away. We were able to go anywhere very quickly.
The room was modern and clean, the bed very comfortable and the bathroom very well equiped! Didn't watch much TV but the big flat screen is probably great for lonely business travelers. The access to broadband for free was useful to plan our trip too.
Not much to say about the staff, they were polite and helpful.
I recommend this hotel, this is really great value for the price (less than ---$ for - nights)!!!

Upon arrival the staff was really rude - they mixed up our room reservation - and threatened to throw the three of us (mom and sister and I) out onto the street. The manager finally gave us a room with - twin beds. Sleeping in the crack of - twin beds pushed together was not fun, especially after long days in NYC.The room was very TINY. The bathroom was microscopic. - people could not stand in it at the same time.The room was very loud and we could hear everyone coming and going in the hallway all night long (- am - - am).Would not stay here again.... ever

We stayed here specifically because of the price and because of the pet-friendly quality. It was our first time traveling with this particular small dog, and we are very impressed. Staff loved him, and even offered to babysit him while we attended our concert, if he was too lonely while we were gone. The room was spacious and while the view was of the building next door, there was a small balcony, and we could see to the cross street. Noise control was pretty good--we were on the -th floor, and so that helped. The king-size bed was so comfortable, with plenty of pillows; there were plenty of towels, and a roomy dressing area just outside the bathroom-shower-tub. We will definitely stay here again. We loved how close this (as far as walking distance) was to everything we wanted to see.

I don't understand why someone would not think the Doubletree Metropolitan is centrally located! You are right on Lexington Avenue, with a subway literally underfoot. Of course, it's not Fifth Avenue and it's not Times Square, but it's a nice -- very nice -- and pricey neighborhood! Away from the tourist madness.
The room was spotless, great modern furnishings and wonderful bed. Not too small by NYC standards. The service was efficient and people friendly. Breakfast buffet left a little to be desired...no pancakes or waffles, only french toast. If you don't like eggs or meat there's only pastries and cereal.
The only negative thing I would have to say is that some of the sleek, modern furniture in the lobby needs a good cleaning. Orange swivel chairs...I'm looking at you!
This is a really nice hotel at a great price. Our room rate was around $---, which, when you consider it's about the same as the Red Roof, is a bargain for NYC.

This hotel was very nice -- no problems. It met every need for a weekend in Chicago. 
That said, I had a bit of a sense of lost potential -- the hotel could be, with a few tweaks, fantastic, and (even while being perfectly acceptable and, in some respects, lovely) that sense of missed potential affected my perception of the hotel.
The positives:
--Check-in service was spectacular. Just really, really good, including sensitivity to the construction happening next door while making room assignments, putting me in my room before check-in time, and being willing to move my original room assignment to a room on a much higher floor based on my preferences. So, the hotel set itself up to majorily impress based on the check-in experience.
--The rooms are large suites, so you can't complain about the space!
--If you are a member of SelectGuest, the hotel brings to your room complimentary coffee and juice in the morning. This is a service of Omni's I adore -- who can object to a piping hot pot of coffee sitting outside your door, free, at the designated time? Fantastic!
--Location is hard to beat -- right on Michigan Ave., easy access to buses and red line subway, etc.
A couple of negatives:
--The bedding needs a makeover ASAP. Sheets were a bit threadbare and the bedspread and pillows were tired and heavy. Many of the competitor hotels to Omni, with nearby locations (e.g., Marriott, Conrad, etc.) have amazing bedding, and the Omni seriously fell short on this one. It's depressing to stay in a hotel of this quality and have a bed look lumpy with only two flat pillows hiding under a bedspread.
--While service at check-in shined, bell service didn't shine quite as much. You enter the hotel through a street lobby and take a set of elevators to the main lobby. This street lobby was always full of staff, and they only bothered to say hello about half the time.
--Housekeeping service was uneven. Everything was clean and the room was properly stocked with toiletries and towels, but housekeeping service didn't go beyond this (i.e., toiletries were not arranged neatly on the basin, bedding was wrinkled in presentation, etc.). -- small details that don't make-or-break a stay, but doesn't compare well to other hotels nearby in the same price-service bracket.
Missed potential:
--While not in poor condition by any stretch of the imagination, the hotel could use a makeover. It feels very much like a hotel -- generic design with zero risks, muted colors, institutional furniture, starving-artist-sale paintings, boring (and sort of uninviting) lobby, etc.
--Some small service upgrades. Again, there were no service outages at all during my stay, but I kept wondering what I would have thought if every aspect of the service had been as impressive as the check-in service.
I'd certainly stay here again...but it's not the sort of place I'd instantly make a reservation at without evaluating other options. Again, if you're looking for a perfectly reliable hotel in a very good location, the Omni will please -- but with a few upgrades-improvements and a dash of design, it could be spectacular.

We chose this property for its proximity to the beach and because it looked a little funky. We were pleased with what we discovered here.
Situated at the southern end of Venice Beach, the Inn is located near a lot of restaurant choices and away from the craziness of the ocean front walk. 
The rooms (we booked several different rooms due to group size) were nicely appointed with seemingly newer furniture and the bathrooms were furnished with good quality toiletries.
The continental breakfast was also sufficient to meet our needs to begin the day.
The front desk staff is friendly, very helpful, and well-versed in area attractions, restaurants, and points of interest. 
We'll be staying here when we visit the area again!

The Washington Jefferson was overall a nice hotel.
A few of us had rooms that faced the street, those were obviously noisier, but turning on the fan (it was hot) helped drown out the trucks and horse-drawn carriage noise. 
The rooms are small, but clean and modern, with nice amenities like down comforters, slate bathroom & new fixtures, free wireless, and close to many restaurants and theaters.
My room had a full bed, nightstand, desk, and mini-wardrobe. The bathroom was slate tile and had a corner shower with glass enclosure. All very modern & clean, but small. Another colleague had no desk or wardrobe, and another got upgraded to a king room. All depends. Maria Pia across the street was good, and the crepe place was ok, but slow and maybe pick your own crepe filling, some was weird.

I stayed in the Fairmont this past weekend. This hotel is absolutey beautiful! From the architecture to the ornate details- it is a gorgeous hotel. The service was impeccable. Concierge and front desk are very helpful with anything you could want. The location is excellent! We walked to everything- restaurants, bars, and plenty of shopping is within blocks of the hotel. But- with all of that said, I would not stay there again for the simple fact that I did not get a good nights sleep either night. The first night I slept maybe --- hours. Second night was better because we requested a fan to drown all of the noise. The doors to each room close very loudly- i feel like the door was slamming every - minutes. And because the hotel is old- the walls are paper thin so you can hear everything going on in the hallways and the roads below (and we were on the top floor.) 
My sleep is precious to me, so if you are staying there i would recommend requesting a fan be delivered to your room- or you will not sleep well at all!

This Sheraton is a good if not terribly exciting option in Mission Valley. Rooms are a little on the small side but comfortable. Some have been renovated more recently than others. The staff were very friendly and accommodating. Parking was a bit of a trick - there are two key-carded lots, one of which is a bit of a walk and not as easily accessible, but there isn't an extra charge. We did have a FANTASTIC dinner and drinks downstairs in the restaurant - could have been a fluke, but it sure was good.

My wife and I stayed here three times within the past year and a half. The Inn was always well maintained both inside and outside. Our room was always clean and everything worked i.e. TV, alarm, water pressure, lights, WiFi, etc. Breakfast offered many food and drink choices and the hostesses kept the area well supplied and clean. The receptionists and cleaning staff were friendly and offered assistance.
 We would definitely be repeat guests.

The HJ is rather tired but perfectly ok for the price we paid which wasn't high compared with it's location. Room was clean, bed was comfortable and the desk staff were excellent, very helpful and informative. Breakfast in the cafe on site is well priced and agin the service was excellent. Easy to get to City Tour Bus and it is a short walk to the McD Rock and Roll Diner and a decent steak house. You need to watch out for the shoe cleaning scam if you are waiting for the Tour Bus. I recomend it highly.

Because we were lucky enough to score this room, we entertained a group of friends before dinner which was fun. The service was great - everyone we encountered was very helpful and super nice. Also, the bathroom sinks are very cool but totally useless. So hard to brush my teeth & wash my face. But I'll deal!! ;) All in all, we really enjoyed our stay at the US Grant!

We decided to avoid the $-- pizza, but did give in to a $-- plate of hummus. I must admit, it was pretty dang good hummus, though. We booked our room through PL and were still treated like Kings. I'd highly, highly recommend this hotel.

Stayed here while attending an exhibition at Seattle Art Museum (- blocks away). Pleasant, charming boutique hotel. Small enough for the staff to be very friendly & genuinely interested in our needs. Spacious & comfortable room. We reserved the steam room for an hour--total decadence. Breakfast in the Library Bistro was very good. The food at happy hour in the cozy Bookstore Bar was so good we kept ordering and cancelled our formal dinner plans. We were looking for a special get-away without breaking the bank--the Alexis exceeded our expectations. We'd definitely go back,

We stayed at the Elan for - days in April. What a wonderful hotel this is. We have stayed in hotels accross the world and this is one of the best - it rates highly for customer service. Every member of staff we encountered had a smile and cheeful greeting for us, the valets in particular were very friendly. The location on beverley Boulevard is perfect for getting around LA and has many good restaurants on the doorstep. We liked Jan's Coffee shop across the road and Swingers which was just up the road. The hotel room was lovely, really clean and comfortable with a coffee maker, robes, balcony and each day a chocolate and weather card was left in the room - a nice touch. If i had a minor criticism(and it is minor) the bathroom could do with some shelves to store your toilet bags, make up bags etc. The hotel provided a free continental breakfast which was good - muffins, juices, cereal, croissants and good coffee.But the icing on the cake(as well as the free wifi) was the evening wine and cheese reception - a lovely treat when we came in each evening. Good quality wine and cheeses served from - - -pm. Really enjoyable. All in all a fantastic stay with a really good atmosphere, wonderful customer service and a perfect location.

My boyfriend and I stayed for two nights in a Deluxe King City-View room at the Contessa to celebrate our one year anniversary. I requested a room at a higher level away from the elevator prior to arriving and that is exactly what we got. We absolutely love it here. Our room was larger than we expected it to be and the layout was fantastic. The view of downtown from the bedroom was great, it was so nice to sit up in the morning and wake up to such a view, very surprising seeing as I don't think of San Antonio being known for views. The bed was so comfy and was plenty stocked with extra pillows (also upon request). The hotel is situated in such a location that its close enough to the action of the riverwalk yet far enough away to keep the noise down. We actually enjoyed the short walk to and from the hotel. The front desk staff seemed to care less if we gave them our business or not, not friendly in the least. The valet however were quick to respond and extremely polite, made us feel welcome from the start. I think its odd that people are complaining about the size of the pool, its built on the roof, the building is only so big. It did get very crowded, especially at night. We swam one night and the next we were able to grab a table and chairs set away from the rowdiness to sit and enjoy the view. We can't wait to return very soon!

Beautiful, spotless, very large, room with comfortable bed, a slick bar set-up and space to entertain or simply chill. Bathroom had fine finishes, dual sink vanity, excellent lighting and enough space for a couple to comfortably get ready for an evening out. Staff was gracious, warm and genuinely interested in taking good care. Could tell in every interation that they really wanted and knew how to be involved. Restaurants were great. Nobu's was spot-on in terms of outstanding quality of food and attention to detail in service. Sushi and sashmi was super fresh, nicely portioned and expertly presented. The Black Cod with Miso was cooked to perfection and absolutely melted in the mouth. My favorite was the Brick Oven prepared -- oz. Bone-in Prime Ribeye. The slow roasting in the brick oven seemed to concentrate the flavor and accentuate the tenderness of the beef. The steak didn't need, but certainly worked incredibly well with the accompanying sauces. A quick breakfast in Mary Jane's included an attentive server with keen awareness of my need for coffee as well as a no fuss approach to my request for a breakfast not on the menu. Scrambled eggs were fresh, fluffy and piping hot. Couldn't have asked for a better launch to my day.
Hard Rock Hotel San Diego was great for my quick business trip. I'd go back for again for business or a fun get-away.

Easy access to all attractions at Fisherman's Wharf and more. Cable car stop at front door of resort very convenient. F-Line buses close by. Rooms clean and all staff were very helpful. Would like to return someday soon.

We had a lovely suite overlooking the Charles River with very nice views. The suite was spacious which made it easy to visit back and forth with our friends who were on the same floor (--th). The location of the hotel was very convenient to sight-see and walk around. Neighbourhood felt safe. Shopping mall connected to the hotel and restaurants too, so if it had been raining that would have been nice. Staff was very friendly. They had the most comfortable pillows I have ever slept on. Room was quiet

The lobby is a good place to read or people watch and the ducks in the fountain are cool. It is very classy. There are plenty of restaurants in the hotel and within walking distance too. The skyway top floor gives you a good view of downtown Memphis too. Make sure you go up there.

Our family of - decided to stay here for our - day DC adventure as we have had good success with the Sheraton product in the past and we wanted to be centrally located in DC, with the abundance of tourist sites in the City. We weren't diappointed! 
We arrived on a Sat afternoon after driving into DC - although a large convention was in DC that week, we were checked in quickly and the staff accommodated us to allow overnight parking, although they were clearly reasonably full. 
The room was spacious and well appointed, with a nice bathroom. Nice touch to provide complementary bottled water and snacks, which was welcomed after a - hour drive. Room service was prompt and professional. 
The kids wanted a swim after we arrived - the Hotel pool is located on the top floor, with an outside patio area to catch some rays after a relaxing swim. Given the pools location, the - times we went for a swim, we always found the pool area to be very reasonably quiet - a nice departure from the noisy kid-filled pools at most City hotels in the summer. 
The concierge and front desk staff were very helpful in recommending local restaurants and tour details, as well as travel info. All in all, a great mid-sized Hotel, smack in the heart of DC, yet a few short blocks away form the tourist bustle of The Mall area. On last day, we took a $-- taxi to Jefferson Memorial, then walked back thru Lincoln Memorial to the Smithsonian area, then back to the Hotel, with little problems. 
Would highly recommend this Hotel!

I Wished we could have stayed longer. We stayed over the Thanksgiving Holiday and it was a very good choice. The rooms comfortable and clean and we enjoyed having the breakfast available to us. It was very well put together and we enjoyed the high speed internet and nicely appointed reception area. If we go back to Jacksonville I would probably stay there again. The gardens and pool were nicely kept up!

We stayed at the Hotel Lombardy in August ---- and found the hotel to be extremely charming -it was like taking a trip to Europe. After reading some of the bad reviews, I called the hotel and requested a room towards the front of the building """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""with a view"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Room service is a bit unorganized - sometimes you get fresh towels, sometimes you don't. They'll pick up the dirty ones but don't leave new ones. Breakfast is good and the breakfast area is spacious and also makes a nice place to gather in the evenings with coworkers. Location is VERY convenient to local transportation, restaurants, and shopping on Michigan Ave. I felt safe walking by myself.

Stayed here for a weekend trip. Hotel's location was the best, - minutes out of the Lincoln Tunnel, valet took the car, rooms are over top a movie theatre complex on --nd street. Staff was very attentive and helpful. The room was furnished well, bed was huge and very comfortable. Couldn't hear a sound from down below. Bathrooms were top notch, loved having the shower that worked for tall people. From the hotel it was half a block in either direction for the subway, which put you any where in New York. Times Square and the theatre was a - minute walk. Fitness room had lots of good equipment.

After we left, I realized that I had left my phone charger in my room. I contacted the hotel and Mark Butler, the front office supervisor, immediately confirmed that they had the items and would happy to ship them to me asap. I was extremely pleased with the level of service - he offered and priced the various shipping methods and sent the items out within -- hours. Great hotel! We will definitely stay there again.

This has always been our favorite place to stay. We try to come 
Baltimore once or twice a year and for the price, location and cleaniness, we love coming here. The staff has always been very kind and helpful. Thanks so much.

Hotel is showing it's age, check in staff weren't the friendliest. Room was okay in size, remote for the tv didn't work and a light was out in the bathroom. Sleep number bed was twin size at best. We stayed at The Lenox on Exeter Street in Boston's Back Bay neighborhood over the July -th weekend. The staff was incredibly helpful and very friendly throughout our stay. The hotel is one block from Newbury Street, which is the main dining and shopping district in Boston, and there were many young people from the city's many colleges on this strip. The rooms are large, if not old-fashioned in their lay-out. Surprisingly, we were never disturbed by anyone in the hallways despite there not being any barriers between the bed and the door. There was a large walk-in closet with an ironing board, refrigerator and full-size window, so we actually felt like we were in a suite. The location is walking distance to good shopping and dining as well as the Museum of Fine Arts. It is minutes away on foot to the Boston Commons, gardens, and the historical trail through downtown. We walked to the aquarium on Long Warf in about half an hour.
We would certainly recommend this hotel for anyone receiving a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""deal"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" like we did on Orbitz, but if you are paying full price you might want to consider a newer hotel if you expect the most up-to-date amenities.
Modern, comfortable size and reasonable pricing for NYC accomodations with efficient staff
Quaint, small cozy rooms with little extras like ornate bathroom fixtures

Watch out for what you reserve. Do not assume you will get a nice city view or sky view. It could also be of a parking lot. You
May call them to say you wl arrive late. The person checking you in wlll not get the message. Drunk collegians will be in the lobby. You could be told they ate sold out and you wl be getting an upgrade. Then you will get a parking lot view. Enjoy this city view which you paid extra for.

The hotel is decent. We just needed a place to spend a couple of nights at while we go around San Francisco..touring. The location is wonderful..right on Lombard Street, at least - restaurant choices within - min walks from the hotel, Including a wonderful bakery if you are a coffee and donuts person! I have to share with you folks the real icing on the cake...the guy who runs the place is a bundle of information...even before we got to s.f ..on the phone he gave us a lot of money saving-safety tips that only a local would know...we had just - days to see the whole city, even though we took a tour .. we had some time on hand to see some sights on our own...and you know what.. the guy was extremely helpful with bus numbers..tram details.. where not to go in the night...he knew it all.. and shared all the info. proactively even!!
As all the other guests have mentioned, room has a microwave. and a fridge, very basic..free parking is also a plus. I would definitely recommend people to put up here.. for all of the above reasons..and I will stay @ the same place if I am back @ S.F. \m-

I know you get what you pay for but there was little choice in Austin the week I visited and someone in my office booked me into this HELL HOLE!
Dirty, Smelly, Falling apart, No facilities and staff who wish they were elsewhere. Me too!
And that was all before the massive cockroach that crawled across the wall and ceiling and scampered across the floor. I asked to be moved and was put into basically the exact same room across the corridor.

I'd rather stay further out of town than stay here again.
AVOID!
Central TN Church of God In Christ Ladies had a wonderful stay at the hotel.Our state workers meeting will be returning in May!! You will in joy all the hotel has to offer.

I have now stayed at the Andaz -th Avenue on - occassions, having stayed at the Andaz San Diego once, Anday West Hollywood once, and the Andaz Wall Street twice. This is my favorite of the Andaz properties simply because the location is perfectly situated in the center of Midtown. The Wall Street property is also quite nice but I would suggest staying there only if you have business in the financial district. The property itself is modern and stylish and the staff are tremendously helpful but not the slightest bit pretentious. The bed is incredibly comfortable, so much so that I ordered the bed for my home. The unexpected treat with this high end hotel is that the non-alcoholic beverages and snacks in the mini bar are free! The mini bar is stocked with high end sodas, juices etc. The other huge positive to consider is that the rooms are quite a bit larger than most other hotels that I would consider to be - or - star hotels in NYC. Last, but not least is the fact that internet is also free at Andaz and the price for a night's stay is usually significantly less than the Grand Hyatt New York, which I also happen to like very much.

As a regular NYC traveler, I decided to book a room close to Broadway, and found this hotel online at a great price. As a married couple in our thirties, I was also attracted to the chic and modern look, as every other hotel we've stayed at for the same price is typically dirty and small (and usually I don't get worked up, as we usually don't hang in the room anyway). Well, needless to say, the decor and lobby were beautiful, and the staff was great right away. We were even offered a nicer room (the room was perfect, hip, decorative, and extremely exeeded my expectations) at no cost. In retrospect, I actually wish we did the valet parking, as it wasn't much of a difference parking in a -- hour lot.
There's little touches of coolness scattered around the hotel, and the bar was nice with a great view of the broadway shows (my wife saw Jordin Sparks from the lobby bar and ran out to get a photo). All in all, we'll DEF. be back. Also, it's perfect walking distance to central park, many cool irish bars we found, times square (much better without the through traffic), Rock center, and of course, Broadway! Can't wait to go back!

Good location, with just - min walk to the Powell street-market street and -- min walk to the union square. Stayed here for a conference and it was close enough to walk to the Moscone center within -- min. Hotel staffs are friendly and greet you everyone when you come or leave. The free tea-coffee in the morning and the free wine session in the evening just add an additional touch for being welcome. Feel very comfortable to stay here! Also hv a --h small fitness centre with sauna room, and not many people were interested to use it which is nice as you can have more space to use it. Though the room is a bit old, but for the price you paid in downtown SF, this is definitely a highly recommended hotel. Not to forget to mention that the lobby is very nicely set out too!

We loved the Staybridge. It was spotless, well thought out, and a perfect place for a couple traveling with a child. The breakfast was above average and had a wide variety. All of the amenities were high quality. And if you call directly if there is plenty of room in the hotel you can get a better price than the ones published on the net. It would also be an excellent place for traveling athletic teams.

We stayed here for a few days after a stay at the Surrey on the Upper East Side, with a great rate from an invitation website. This was our first stay in this area of NYC. I liked the uptown vs. downtown diversity; the - hotels have totally different vibes in sync with their respective locations--sedate and posh vs. contemporary and youth-skewed.
To me, these lower Manhattan neighbourhoods kind of blend in with one another, but I think the hotel is located in NoHo. The East Village, the Bowery, Nolita, SoHo, and the Lower East Side are steps away, with Greenwich Village, West Village, Union Square, Tribeca and Chinatown walkable. Cooper Square really is a small square, with the Cooper Union Foundation Building (built in ----, a National Historic Landmark) to the north. This building and the new (Sept. '--)) exquisite -- Cooper Square building (Thom Mayne of Morphosis, architect) house the Cooper Union colleges of architecture, art and engineering. Astor Place, the nearest subway stop, is - blocks away from the hotel.
When arriving, be familiar beforehand of the hotel's address and appearance, as it has no signage in front (besides the -- address)--too cool for that. Just look for the tallest white glass tower in the area. Opened about a year ago, its exterior is a striking modern design (architect Carlos Zapata) that at first looks rectangular but actually has few -- degree angles and even looks curved from some perspectives. The design is a definite step up from the similar-looking Hotel on Rivington in the LES, which is older, less tall, less distinctive and already showing some age. An adjacent small, old - story building is actually incorporated into the hotel inside, with a huge mural painted on its exterior. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""we're too cool to have..."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" attitude extends to the reception desk--there isn't one. Rather, you pass from the high-ceilinged entrance room into a chic Library, where a standing staff member goes into a smaller room to check you in. These staff members also serve as quasi-concierges, while the doormen double as bellmen. While waiting, you are offered a drink (wine or iced tea, available throughout the day). The Library has a fireplace, and books to peruse or purchase (there are also books in the rooms). Walls of windows look out onto an outdoor dining area and small garden. There is no business center, but there is a free laptop in the Library, and free wireless throughout the hotel. On the second floor there is a bar-lounge with windows onto a nice outdoor patio. There is no fitness center, but guests can get free passes to the Athletic Club across the street. The interior total design concept is by Antonio Citterio.
The room we booked was a Cooper ---the smallest (--- square feet) offered, but with higher floor city views. The Cooper - is slightly larger and less expensive, but has lower floor courtyard views. There are rooms, studios and suites of many shapes and sizes, maxing out with the top floor penthouse that occupies the entire --st floor and has an expansive wrap-around deck--it is available for parties and photo shoots. The upper floors have ten or less rooms per floor, with four corner rooms each.
Our room was indeed small but very bright with a wall of windows looking north to the Cooper Union and Square, with glimpses of the Empire State and Chrysler Buildings. We were greeted with the faint smell of urine, which thankfully later dissipated. The desk and armoire housing the small closet, expansively supplied minibar and safe were not very durable-looking. We shoved things under and on top of the armoire--there was scant room for storage. There was an IPod dock, but no alarm clock. The drapes had no pulls, so you had to pull on the drapes themselves--future tears are inevitable The TV had many channels, some hi def, but no premium (HBO). The lighting at night was dark. The all black-tiled bathroom lighting was dark all the time--- spotlights over the sink and one in the shower. No tub, but the shower was large, the head decent. There were supposed to be - robes--terry, cotton and silk, but the silk one was missing. All movable items such as the robes, the umbrella and the cute satin bags available for laundry and what not all have tags that say how much you'll be charged if you take them. There was no ice bucket--a champagne bucket of ice is delivered upon request. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""do not disturb""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""-""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""housekeeping service needed"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sign was a small leather pillow--red on one side, green on the other. Housekeeping puts a small broom ornament on the doors of rooms being serviced. We encountered more noise from the hallway (lots of doors slamming) than from outside.
The hotel's restaurant, Faustino, is Italian and very popular, headed by Scott Conant, seen on several Food Network shows. We only breakfasted there, but some items are available in-room all day. The restaurant initially opened as Table -, with Govind Armstrong.
When checking out, you tell one of the standing staff members, who goes into the small room for awhile, then returns and says """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""you're all set"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Not everyone is given a checkout statement--too cool for that--so ask if you want one to review or keep.
We had a pleasant stay here, despite some style over substance issues. When we first arrived and were taking the elevator to the room, I asked a guest what he thought of the hotel. He said, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""it's great if your under --, party all night and sleep all day. I'm none of those things, so I wouldn't stay here again."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" We are none of those things either, but given a good rate, we would return--it's a great location. The Standard, where we stayed last year, probably has a better location and views, but is pricier. Both are targeted towards the same demographic. For this year's trip, the Surrey wins out, but you're only as old as you feel.

The hotel was in a great location, The historic charm of the building was great. It is the building with the red pegasus. Great service and lots of amenities, from the happy hour, the milk and cookie bar at night and the American breakfast in the morning.

The hotel is not customer freindly because you need to walk outside to get to the lobby and other hotel areas. The overall apperance was average and the service was ok. Highway noise is somewhat of an issue.

I gave this hotel an average rating because I liked some things about the Washington Plaza and disliked others. First...the price. It is on par with other DC hotels (over priced) but they did allow a decent AAA discount. The staff was good all over the hotel. They were all pretty friendly. They did not offer to help with our bags on arrival.
The restaurant is mediocre at best, but breakfast was ok. The restaurant staff were all good and attentive. 
The hotel location is pretty good. It is a nice walk to the White House and Washington Monument. There are plenty of food choices within walking distance as well as plenty of coffee shops. 
we did have a room that was above the street, so it got noisy a couple of nights. 
I would recommend the hotel especially for the price and clean rooms and comfy beds!

I spent a week at the hotel. The rooms are a little outdated. The service was good. The meeting rooms have all been updated, so very nice. Nice excercise room and pool. The lobby areas get a little hot during the day but rooms are nice and cool. The shuttle service to-from airport was also very handy (nice drivers :) ). Overall, I would stay again if on business or passing through. Not a vacation destination.

Stayed at the Madison Renaissance for - nights end of May ----. Staff were very friendly and concierge was especially helpful. Not located in the middle of downtown but still very convenient. It is at the top of a fairly steep incline from the waterfront but easily manageable especially if you go through the escalators of buildings. Rooms are clean and well maintained. For the price charged compared to other hotels in the vicinity, the Madison Renaissance offers very good value. 
Henry

Hotel has very nice doormen and service staff. Front desk people were mixed, about were excellent and the other half adequate. We were first given a room on the second floor that was very noisy. We called and they changed the room for us to a very quiet upper floor room. We tried the wine tasting on our third night there and it was nice. The location is superb for a first time visitor to Chicago. The hotel is right in the middle of the top attractions. The restaurant was horrible. We had breakfast on Memorial Day and they had one waitress in the whole place.
The hostess didn't help and the lady who might have been management was completely overwhelmed. Our breakfast was cold on delivery. My oatmeal would have been good if it was even warm. I arrived from London tired, dirty and braindead. I was in San Diego for a meeting and was booked into the nearby Omni for all but the first night. Lucky me that I had one night in the Solamar! Check in was easy-peasy and was upgraded to a luxury room (just because!). The room was wonderful - bedding comfortable, bathroom spacious, and the (free) wireless was superfast. The next morning I ordered breakfast from room service (egg white omelet with spinach and mushrooms) and it was quick and delicious. Check out was simple and they even pointed the way to the Omni down the street (the Omni was perfectly fine... but paled in comparison to the Solamar).

Went to Austin on a spur of the moment trip and stayed at the Intercontinental Hotel. The Location is Fantastic its a block away from sixth street, however the rooms are very tiny do not expect the grand accomadations of you four star hotel, Valet parking will set you back -- bucks a night. The Hotel Staff was a little on the stuck up side and I really hate that, The hotel is nice and well maintained the beds were not as nice as the westin beds but they did have feather pillows. All in All this hotel is priced high because of its location and not its grand accomadations. If you go on sixth street you have to hit Barcelona and Blind Pig Pub!

It's a little pricey. Although, very comfortable and well run.
My daily rate was $--- (it really feels like a $--- - $--- hotel). And, I had to extend one night and they upped the rate to $---. 
The one glitch was that there was a Bose clock radio in the room and it didn't work. The same thing happened for a business associate staying in another room.
All-in-all - I'd stay there again, but not at that rate.

Good choice for NYC, would stay here again. Short walk to Times square but far enough to be quieter. Close to subway. Small grocery store next door. Nice to have a small fridge.NO bedbugs. Staff friendly.
Only down was the bass from the music on roof on Friday night (--th floor)

Really enjoyed staying at the Hacienda - very conveniently located right in the midst of Old Town. While we did have a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""mini-suite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", it did have a tad bit more room, it seemed, than some of the other rooms; the first room was a TV, small """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""kitchenette-sink"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" area with fridge, microwave, cupboards (there was a toaster), etc. Didn't really use it much, but small loveseat and extra sitting room outside of the bedroom made it more usable. Sandwiched in the middle was the vanity area, mirrored-covered closet with ironing board located inside, and the bathroom with sliding pocket door. The rooms were clean, and housekeeping did a decent job. We were in the --- building on the -nd floor; was fairly quiet our entire stay (- days-- nights). According to the front desk, the front desk area of this Best Western used to be a restaurant; many of the buildings are somewhat disjointed and it took us about - minutes to figure out where the heck we were going each time we were learning a new part of the hotel; parking is tight, but at $-- day it's better than many of the the other hotels we were considering. After walking out of a nearby restaurant, ended up eating at Acapulo at the hotel; service and food were just what we needed.

Ovwerall great hotel and the chinatown is the added value; however they have a stupid ---- building construction near the hotel. I stayed on the --th floor and could not sleep. The windows are not sound proof. Stay away because of construction

I often fly from coast to coast and stay at numerous hotels....usually Marriots and Hiltons, but I thought I would take a chance on a local, rennovated hotel such as Hotel Brexton. The room and bathroom was extremely small and didn't look at all like the photographs on the website. The insulation is terrible.....so bad...that I heard every move that every guest made all through the night and didn't get any sleep. I woke up the next morning and couldn't take a shower because I had no water. When I called the front desk they told me to wait a while because other guests are probably showering at the same time preventing me from getting any water pressure. WHAT!!!! Then I contacted the front desk to get a cab and instead of a cab she said they use a contracted driver for their guests at a nominal fee. I reluctantly agreed and told her that I needed to be in a car within -- minutes to make an appointment. The driver came almost -- minutes later, making me late for my appointment. This hotel was in a great location, super close to Times Square! The only negative was that there was a VERY loud night club downstairs from our room. However, the front desk manager was very kind in helping to fix the situation. We will def. stay in this hotel again, however, with small children in tow...we'll request a room on a higher floor! Could have been a terrible situation, but management did what they could to fix it! Just make sure you call to request a room above floor -!!!

Best Staff we've ever met! We've traveled all over the U.S. but this was our first trip to NYC. The Wingate Inn Manhattan made the trip the enjoyable success it was. The room was great, the breakfast was wonderful, and the staff was the BEST. Thank you for a wonderful stay. We had plenty of room for a family of four and all the complimentary amenities were unbelievable. The only thing that might have made it absolutely perfect would have been an additional mirror over the desk instead of a picture. We had two teenage girls with us and sharing the bathroom was a little difficult with so much primping going on! :) :) Otherwise, everything was ideal.

We enjoyed a - bedroom suite which was generously sized for a family of -, with a large living room area. Plenty of restaurants and shopping very nearby including a couple of small markets. Easy walk to Michigan Avenue and Water Tower, a little farther to red line subway. Very slow elevators (apartment building conversion to RI?). Average RI breakfast. Front desk staff was very helpful, good suggestions. Parking is the only downside, expensive and lightly staffed valet service, sometimes a long wait for car. Overall great for families and walking visit to Magnificent Mile and Hicago.

The rooms in this hotel must surely be the largest in Manhattan. Couldn't get any closer to Times Square. The only downside we can think of was even though it was snowing outside, we had to set our airconditioning to -- degrees C as we were waking up in a sweat when setting it any higher. This meant it was quite noisy - but after a busy day it didn't really keep us awake.
Everything else was perfect - tea and coffee making facilities in the room with a kitchen area, wonderful housekeeping, awesome lobby barman, lots of smiles all around. Anyone looking for a friendly, clean, comfortable and well located hotel in Manhattan - this is it!

I went to this hotel for a Rave event they were holding and bought a four person room. I was told on the phone that you had to purchase a - person room to attend. I get there, and there is a general admission booth for non-hotel guests. So basically the hotel lied so that we'd buy an expensive room rather than just event passes. Got upstairs, amenities were alright but there were stains on towels and the drain for the tub was clogged! The fire alarm went off for a good half hour at -:-- a.m., and then again at -:-- a.m. The service we received from the bar was decent, but the staff all looked and acted pretty unprofessionally. They just looked frumpy and not in the mood to help you. They didn't bother telling us when the water park closed so we ended up not even being able to go. And there is now a mystery charge on my debit card that I'm still trying to figure out, but the voicemail inbox to leave a complaint message is full. Horrible place. Don't waste your money.

My husband and I made a quick trip to DC for one night, since we had a flight credit to use. We spent the day in DC and then stayed overnight at this hotel, since we had an early flight out of BWI. The hotel room was a good size, as was the bathroom. The service was quite good; there was no fridge in the room, and since I needed one to store breastmilk in, I went to the front desk and asked for one. Within - minutes, a fridge with freezer was delivered to our room, free of charge! Workout room was very small, with just - treadmill, - elliptical, - bike, and some free weights. Breakfast was free and awesome; nice buffet with cereal, breads, eggs, meats, waffles, and tons of fresh fruit and juice. Delicious!

I was shocked that all they have to offer is valet parking. $---night. This is Austin not NYC. There is nothing within walking distance of the hotel in spite of what management told me. I tried to find the local Starbucks but would not want to be walking around that area at night. 
The property itself is very nice. Beautiful pool area. The gym can use some work; all of the cardio machines either did not work (stationary bikes) or were very outdated. 
The food is very good. I ordered room service...Penne Rustica and a caesar salad. It was delicious. 
I would recommend this hotel for business travel. It is wihin walking distance of the convention center.
The staff at check in were very pleasant. The gentleman that brought my room service would only bring the food in part way. Very odd. Not an issue though.

The staff are extremely helpful in this hotel. The rooms are clean, comfortable and quiet. There is a lovely atmosphere and it is in a great location - across from Macy's, next to the subway with nice restaurants and bars nearby. We left some of our personal belongings behind us in our room and the hotel staff took great care to keep them safe for us, for this we are very grateful. If-when we go back to new york we will definately stay there again, I recommend it highly.
Very nice place to stay. Great location for traveling and or shopping in area. I would stay there again if need be.

This is the hotel you want to stay at if you are visiting Seattle!
Views: You are within walking distance of everything including: The space needle, the waterfront, pike st. market, souvenier shops, the argosy harbor cruise, museums, and so much more.
Room: Up-to-date paint, art, and amenities. The pictures from the website are exactly what your room looks like. I loved the edgy style of this room. Everything from the mirrors in the bathroom to the clever shades in the room which tell you the hotels address. NOTE: There is no bathtub, only a shower. The shower comes with 'soap dispensers' that hold shampoo, conditioner and body wash that smell amazing.
Cost: The price ($--.---day) was competitive when considering the proximity to entertainment and eating. Additionally, the parking cost was nominal at $-- dollars-day. We had no difficulty finding a spot to park and we didn't move our vehicle the whole time we were there.
Staff: Very friendly and welcoming.
Amenities: There is a cafe on-site that is a little pricey for me, but convenient nonetheless. They have a laundry service that picks up every morning. There is no pool or exercise facility, but there was so much to do it never mattered.
Cleanliness: Absolutely five stars!!! This is a big sell-point for me. The room smelled so good. (I kept looking for the source of this freshness). The floors were clean and I was comfortable walking in bare feet. The corners of the bathroom were spotless. Sometimes hotels have gunk that builds up in the crevices, but this place looked brand new. The shower had crystal clear glass, as did the windows. No musty, mildewy scent. The sheets and blankets were clean and the fabric was comfortable.
The next time I visit Seattle I know exactly where I will be staying, HOTEL FIVE! You will not be sorry staying here.

We enjoyed a light lunch at the Grant Grill which was delicious and very reasonably priced. They make their own potato chips which are excellent! The parking is a bit expensive, but I think it is pretty much on par with the other hotels in the area. We would definitely stay at this hotel again and recommend it to our friends. 
If you are looking for a nice dinner, we tried Suite & Tender at the new Se Hotel and thoroughly enjoyed it. It is not cheap but it was definitely worth it to us. Lobster and braised short ribs on the same plate. Need I say more?!

My wife and I had a great long weekend stay at the Conrad over the Easter weekend. As a Hilton Diamond member the hotel goes above expectations and provides a fantastic complementary hot breakfast.
Rooms are modern and very clean. The location is great for shopping and site seeing. 
This is my second stay at this property and is now my go-to hotel in Chicago. Free wi-fi is a plus

having arived fairley late on a delayed flight from heathrow we were quite supprised how quick and efficient the shuttle bus was in taking us to this hotel,the staff were curteous and very helpful.The highlight of the evening was dining in the rooftop resturant watching the planes landing allthough the waiters were very disorganised not knowing who had ordered what food and which table to deliver orders too.Next morning we walked to the budget car rental which is only two blocks away.We would certanly stay here again as we felt safe in this area

PLI was our base during our three weeks summer holiday stay in SD and surroundings. Very friendly, helpful and serviceminded manager! He did all the best for us, always with an honest smile! Our group of - (four adults, three teenagers, two under --) shared two rooms. Bathroom and kitchen ok, same with the cleaning.
All in all, we got what we payed for. The only thing we really missed was a couple of extra chairs round the balcony table in the evenings when socialising. Keep up the good work!
With kind regards

We had a very early flight out of San Francisco and requested a -:--am wake up call, but never got the wake up call, so if you're staying here, be sure to use the wake up call as a back up only.
The front desk clerk was very nice to us, which made up for the bell boy's bad attitude.

They are charging additional fees & with no regard for keeping future customers. We have contacted the general manger (Ram) & he does not seem to have any sympathy about the matter. I have heard scam hotels like this before & never experienced it until we stayed here. Make a good decision for you & your family & stay somewhere else!

My daughter and I went on a girl's vacation to CA. And had no idea where to book a hotel....we picked the Sheraton and were SO happy we did!!! This hotel was centrally located,walking distance to universal studios and city walk. It was clean, friendly staff that was more than helpful. The bartender named Jeff also made us feel right at home!!! Go see Jeff and tell him Jean and Jess sent ya!!! The restaurant food was great as well as the service..I suggest renting a car and having a GPS....we had a great time and now know where to stay when we visit California!!! You will not b disappointed.

This hotel is very different from most hotels, very modern feeling from the time you walk in till you check out. The rooms are very modern, straight lines and clean. Close to the cruise ship terminal, walkable if you do not have a lot of luggage and are in good shape. Cab ride is abbot --.-- to --.-- depending on the traffic. There is not much around the hotel mostly car dealerships and repair shops. It is about - blocks to the Hell's Kitchen area to get a good meal. We stayed at Ink -- forb- night prior to a cruise out of New York.

Went with my school in April ---- for - nights. First time to New York so expected big things.. For young travellers this place is perfect, bunk bed rooms with convenient sink and tv screen with a lush decor and just enough space for two to manoeuvre. Great location, just a few blocks from all the main sites, If I recall correctly we only got the subway a couple of times.
Absolutely breathtaking views can be experienced from the roof garden, which is open all night and perfect on those summers evenings where you can't get to sleep.
Only downside I'd give to this place is the cockroaches that I found in the toilets and showers. Being from the UK it was a bit of a scare as cockroaches are rarely found in residencies. 
I had an incredible time in NY whilst staying here, and would definitely come back if next time I was also on a budget.
We were called at -:-- a.m. by the night auditor to ask if we were going to check out that day. She said it was their procedure to do that. Don't expect a good night's sleep.

I came to Chicago with my Mom for the Oprah spectacular in May and we stayed at the Palmer house. I was the first to arrive in Chicago from Atlanta as my Mom was to join me later since she was flying in from Baltimore. I arrived much earlier than check-in time and thought I'd just take a chance on leaving my bags at the counter so that I could rush to the United Center and pick up my tickets to the show. Being that I am not from Chicago I wanted to leave plenty of time to get to and from where I needed to go. The gentleman at the front allowed me to check in early. I was able to request a top floor since I'd read to do so to prevent noise. I got on the --th floor I believe it was room ------ lovely room, two beds and two bathrooms (which came in handy so that Mom and I could get ready for the show at the same time). We had a great stay here. 
It took some getting used to for me at first because of the grandeur of the hotel. It's very opulent, but I get it, it's historic. I'm used to more modern, chic hotels, but the main lobby does offer this and I think it's cool that the downstairs is right off of main streets and you can not beat the accessibility to the best that Chicago has in the way of tourism. The staff gave good old fashion accommodating service. I came in not sure if I would stay again because at first I felt it was over the top, and I left not sure if I would ever be able to stay anywhere but here. It was a great time in Chicago, and a wonderful at the Palmer House. Excellent Staff! 
Warning, the Concierge desk does get pretty busy so leave enough time to wait and ask your questions. Also leave a night to eat at the restaurant adjacent to the lobby. Felicia the manager is awesome and a true value to hotel! I hope this was helpful enjoy your visit!

The room had a terrible smell based on - reasons: failure in tube plumbing and the matress have humidity. i will never stay that hotel again. the breakfast area was so dirty and nobody does nothing to clean it up.

Second time in two years staying here and would recommend it. I booked online and got a good rate but arrived one day earlier than booked and the reception were very good and gave a decent rate even just walking in off the street.
Staff were very helpful, room was spacious and clean, free Wi-Fi, free parking, good choice at breakfast. Did not use the fitness room but others were.
There are a couple of restaurants within walking distance and even more just five minutes driving away as well as shops. Close to the freeway but did not have a noise problem.
Distance from Downtown Houston by car is no more than -- minutes at the peak rush hour and even quicker outside of the peak times.
No problem recommending.

I'm sixteen and i found this hotel for my family. The website looks great and a ---- chairman suite two bedroom looks great but i'm concerned about the bedding. Some images show a dated kind of material as bedding and then some show a newer white bedding. Is there a way you request what type of bedding you want? or is it a luck of a draw. 
Well i hope we get a bedroom with newly furnished bedding

We picked this hotel for the price first and the location second. The rooms and even bathroom are specious for a NY hotel. The staff was wonderful and helpful where needed. 
Manhattan Diner was across the street and there are some wonderful restaurants around. Subway is super close and Central Park even closer. I see people complain about the elevator and yes it didn't always work but there was a second one that did work and stuff sometimes break down simple as that. 
We had a wonderful stay and will come back for sure.

My wife and I stayed here because it was the host hotel for a professional convention she was attending. I'm sorry that I made this call.

Secondly, the hotel provided a shuttle service to the convention at Cal State-Northridge, which was about -- minutes away. They had a schedule printed and distributed to convention guests. This shuttle was horribly unreliable. When I asked what compensation would be made to make up for the habitual tardiness, he said that the shuttle was being provided as a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""courtesy,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but he would ask the GM to contact me.
