Third, when I asked for more towels one evening, I had an extremely grumpy man deliver them to my door. When I said, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Thank you,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" he simply turned around and walked away. 
Even more frustrating was the fact that I could see the nearby Hilton hotel out of my window, almost mocking me for staying there. 
On a positive note, the valet parking service was the best I've seen in a long time. Also, one of the vendors held a reception in the patio area, and it was quite nice. 
My dad's college roommate at Notre Dame recently retired from Marriott where he was Vice-Chairman of the board. He always asks me why I stay at Hilton instead of Marriott...unfortunately, I have another story to tell him.

This hotel has everything you could possibly want or need. We stayed - nights and it was absolutely perfect. The Director of Front Office Operations, Alex, assisted with pre-stay details of our reservation. Mr. Lee, Front Desk Supervisor, checked us in. Both gentlemen were extremely helpful, polite and personable. 
The room was very clean and spacious. We had a fabulous view of both the Charles River and Fenway park.
There were always plenty of taxis waiting outside the hotel if we needed to go somewhere outside of walking distance.
The Sheraton is within walking distance to Fenway park, tons of shopping and amazing restaurants. It also has a fantastic restaurant inside the hotel. We had dinner in the bar one night and room service for breakfast on the day we left. Everything was hot, quick and delicious.
I’ll definitely be back.

I had to call this hotel at -:-- am because the hotel I was staying at around the corner was definitely not what I expected at all, and I could not stay there for one night! 
So, Natasha answered the phone and when I told her what was going on, she had a room left and booked it for me for the - nights and - days that I was visiting NYC with my sister. I am very grateful for her courtesy and hospitality. She also helped us out with finding different tour sites on the maps that she gave us and which subway routes to take to the sites and places we wanted to see.
The staff in general were all very helpful and friendly!
I would suggest this hotel to others because of the great location (times square- theatre district), the staff, the price of the hotel for being in Times Square, and the cleanliness of the hotel all around. :)

My husband and I just returned from San Antonio and stayed at the Hotel Valencia two nights. The staff was pleasant and helpful at all times. The hotel is very unique with sleek ultra-modern decor one would normally find in New York City or San Francisco. The rooms were well laid out with an extremely comfortable bed and leather lounge chair and ottoman. Our room overlooked the courtyard complete with a beautiful mosaic waterfall to drown out the city sounds. The inside of the hotel is darker than most, but there is enough lighting someone would not get lost. My husband and I thought the dim lighting added to the uniqueness of the hotel. The icing on the cake about this property is the restaurant Citrus and adjoining V Bar. We have travelled the country and this restaurant competes with any five star restaurant in the country. The presentation and quality of the food is fabulous. This restaurant should in highlighted in Gourmet magazine. We actually changed our plans so we could eat there a second night before we left. This is an outstanding hotel. The owners should be very proud of what they have accomplished in making San Antonio competitive with the best boutique hotels in the country.
Poor. Called Hotel manager - day after I left. Mentioned I was calling regarding bed bugs. I was attacked on my foot and ankle. They put me into voicemail and never returned my call. That said alot.

Stayed here over Columbus Day weekend when prices were high in Boston. Booked an unrenovated room for $----nite, which was much cheaper than anywhere else I could find. The room was on the third floor over the lobby, so we did not have any noise from the bar. Room had a comfortable queen bed and wardrobe for hanging clothes. Bathroom was small but it had a new sink and toilet and upscale bath products. The tub-shower was old, but in decent condition and the shower had really good water pressure. Room and bathroom were very, very clean. TV, although old style, had a great selection of cable channels. Room had a big window that opened. The location is great: just a couple blocks down Berkeley to Tremont St. and its plethora of restaurants and a few blocks up Berkeley in the other direction to Back Bay. Staff were extremely helpful. For the cleanliness, price and location, I would definitely stay here again on our next weekend trip.

We were there for -- nights. It was a disaster. Dirty carpets, didn't change the sheets when we asked. Was guaranteed a room with a fridge didn't get one until - days into the stay even though we paid extra for it. Not enough towels, pool was dirty. Desk employees seemed to not care about any problems.

This is a nice place with decent sized rooms in the middle of Manhattan! My husband and I took our - kids and stayed for one night for less than $---- we had a fridge, a counter with bar stools and complimentary snacks and drinks in the evening (as well as free hot breakfast). While the food was nothing to rave about, all of us were able to find something that we liked. (The kids had chocolate ice cream at the complimentary """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""happy hour"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" before we went out to dinner- a rare treat for them!) We also had a front row view of the Empire State Building. We would definitely stay here again.

My husband and I had to stay here for a business trip. Our room was dirty in some places and filthy in others. Black mold in the bathroom along with peeling and missing wallpaper. The bathroom door had so much just grossness (I can't explain) on it, I only touched it with a towel and not my bare hand. The end of the hallway had a huge head-shaped dent in it. As if someone had either ran head first into the wall or someone had rammed someone else's head into the wall. Very interesting. Our business luncheon and dinner were catered by the resort. The lunch was a basket of sliced bread and plates of deli meat and cheese type products. I'm not going to go on and on. Suffice to say that I would never stay in a place like that had the business meetings been on the grounds.

First time to Philly for a business meeting. Hotel is near a lot of goods and services. Hotel staff was VERY friendly, no complaints on service. Room was very clean and the room attendant did a great job. Bed linens were great, loved the comforter. Biggest complaints... The hotel shower head. I understand about water savings, but it took longer and I use more water trying to get the shampoo out of my hair. I don't like the fine shower heads. The desk lamp was centered on right side of desk, could not move it. Biggest complaint of all no Food Network channel. There must have been -- ESPN or sports channels. Huge disappointment for my husband and I. A-C went to -- and did not work great. Stupid complaint is the lotion stinks and smells like lemon, so bring your own.

My husband was in San Francisco for a conference and we stayed at the Inter-Continental SF for five nights. The hotel is modern, sleek and convenient located - right next to the Moscone Convention Centre, - blocks from the cable car terminal, - block from Bloomingdales and Nordstrom and a ---minute walk from Union Square, where more shops await. 
The room was spacious, clean and modern, equipped with flat-screen TV and i-pod dock. The only complaint is that the shower was very weak - it was one of those fixed ones (as opposed to a hand-held one) and there was no temperature control, which was rather surprising for a new hotel. Our package came with breakfast included so we enjoyed their buffet breakfast every day. The selection was limited and remained exactly the same for our entire stay. 
Staff were helpful and attentive, especially the concierge who provided us with excellent tips and recommendation.

We chose this hotel for its location and proximity to the --th Street Mall and in that respect it was very good. It was a nice hotel but I'd read several reviews that referred to the themed floors and was quite excited about it. However, if I hadn't read about it in advance I probably wouldn't have realised the floors were even themed! There were a couple of framed pictures in the corridor in keeping with the theme but nothing else and nothing inside our actual room. Not that there was anything wrong with that, but I had been expecting a bit more from all the reviews!
The valet parking was helpful and friendly and breakfast (which wasn't included in our room rate) wasn't too expensive and was fine, though not the best I've had. Overall it was a perfectly nice hotel which is good if you want a central location and friendly service.

I booked the W for my husband's --th birthday, he loves the W. We checked in three hours early with no problems and received an upgraded oceanview. It was nice room, a bit smaller than other W's we have stayed at. We had a king size bed, chaise lounge chair, desk and two night stands. The bathroom was a normal size for a hotel in the city. The one weird thing is that there were large wooden shutters that you could open so you could be in the bathroom to look into the bedroom (like a window almost) or close them for privacy. 
The bar on the --rd floor had a nice view, but it was SUPER smokey. So we opted to go back down to the bar in the lobby. We had good service, strong and expensive martinis. I guess what do you expect in the city. 
We didn't valet the car, but it is $-- a day for those of you who drive to the city. 
The hotel is about four easy blocks from Michigan Ave, which is a great location. There is a great little place for breakfast about two block west of the hotel...I believe it is called West Egg. Great food and MUCH cheaper than eating at the hotel.

Beware of false advertisement on Hilton's Website. These rooms are NOT soundproof as advertised. As a matter of fact, you can hear lots of noise from adjacent rooms, rooms above- below you, as well as noise in the halls quite easily.If you are a light sleeper, I would avoid this place.
Loved this hotel. Staff were wonderful and the hotel was very clean. I would definitely recommend this hotel to any of my friends.

We stayed at the Residence Inn over Labor Day week end, and although it was very busy, the hotel handled the traffic just fine. Opt for a room rather than a suite if you would like, as it is huge with a kitchenette, et al. It's a better value than the one bedroom, unless you have more than two people staying there. Breakfast is included and you are walking distance to shopping and the Inner Harbor.

Hiltons are usually consistent, and this one was above average, particularly the service and attitude. I was pleased with the location, near Union Square, many stores and restaurants, and the Powell St. BART station. My room seemed large and was very comfortable. On the --th floor, it offered a fine view. The breakfast buffet looked expensive, and there are many alternative spots nearby.

Great Staff, friendly and professional. Wonderful restaurants bith at the hotel (Campagn is great!) as well as nearby. We had several great meals at local recommended restaurants. Room was spacious including the bathroom. Valet car service was prompt and professional. Location is superb. Steps away from Pike's Market and only a few blocks from the Art museum. -th floor deck area with great views of the bay. We got the last room available in the hotel for one of the nights we stayed, so water view was not available, but we will choose it next time, it would be especially nice for a romantic getaway! 
My favorite hotel (of many) in Seattle, a town with several good hotels to choose from. My new #-...why stay anywhere else?

My husband and I stayed at this hotel July ----, this hotel is over priced for the accommodations. If you get a great rate, no more than $-- a night (it'll be worth what you get) but not for the price we paid of $--- a night. The - bed king is VERY small. We had to keep our a-c on to keep our room from smelling damp. We had gnats in our -st floor room, the maintenance guy did come and spray but they were back by the next morning, as if it were an infestation issue. The best thing about the room, the mini refrigerator, microwave and free wi-fi. The variety of choices weren't great for the complimentary breakfast, I've had better. The hotel seems as if it was once a Motel - inside and outside. Not a lot of parking in the front or back lots. FYI - if you can stay somewhere else, I would. I will not be back. Not a good hotel to stay at for a romantic get away or extended vacation. Overall, the location of the hotel is great, that's the best thing I can say about this hotel.

Recently had a - night stay in this hotel. We booked through the SPG website and got a lovely king room on the --th floor with fab view over Broadway. The room and bathroom were a great size compared with previous New York hotels in which we have stayed. Also the room was immaculate and the bed was so comfy. The hotel foyer is nice and welcoming, and there is a nice bar-restaurant called Russos, however I see from one report that it is shortly due to close which seems such a shame. Once we checked in and took the elevator up to our room we were a little concerned as the corriders are a little grubby and could definately do with some decoratng. We were originally given a room on the --th floor however when we went in, it had not been cleaned and I have to say I am glad as it did not look nearly as nice. The only complaint I have about the room is that the walls are paper thin and unfortunately we heard EVERYTHING from the room next door .
The location is absolutely perfect, the swimming pool on the -th floor was fantastic and we managed to have a swim most days. Had a few drinks in the hotel bar but did not have a meal or breakfast so not sure what the food was like. There are lots of nice bars and restaurants close by - Ellens Stardust diner across the street is good fun although the food is nothing special. If you are thinking of a broadway show, I would recommend Memphis, It was the highlight of my trip. I have seen lots of shows in the past and this one is definitely the best..

Would highly recommend this hotel. Very trendy, upscale boutique style NY hotel. Rooms are small, but very nice. You feel ultra modern and chic when you stay here. Great shower and stereo system was a plus. Staff were helpful, never rude but not especially friendly. Room service and maintenance were prompt. Comfortable bed. We were told our room was an upgrade due the view, which may have been nice had there not been a big crane hanging over the water. But still worth getting room with a view, it's fun to look down at the busy cobbled street below.
Great location for all of down town, especially meat packing district. A few nice bars close by and some fabulous restaurants. The Gansevoort's own roof top bar has people lining up to get in, many nights of the week. Bar has great views, nice for a cocktail or two, full of NY's young professionals and IT girls. Great people watching. Good luck getting into the pool up there though, everytime we went up it seemed to be closed for a photo shoot of some kind. (LeeAnn Rhimes was shooting one when we tried to get in one day, was cool to see her though)
Stay here if you want to feel very New York, you will have a great stay.

We stayed at the Houston Doubletree Hotel IAH for one night between flying into Houston Intercontinental (George Bush) Airport and driving down to Galveston for a one-week Caribbean cruise.
For a review of that cruise (Carnival Conquest), see my posting (using the same """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""T. Advisor King"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" screen name) for March, ---- at
http:--www.cruisecritic.com-memberreviews-memberreview.cfm?EntryID=-----
We gathered our baggage from IAH and walked outside to the shuttle bus pick-up area. The Doubletree shuttle was already there. Unfortunately it was full and we had to wait for the next one. However, we only had to wait maybe five (and certainly less than --) minutes for the next empty shuttle to arrive. The hotel was nearby, but I don't have any recollection of aircraft noise. Usually, when you stay at an airport hotel, you have to accept that you will hear planes taking off and landing all night. Perhaps it was the direction of the wind, or maybe I just don’t remember it. But I certainly wasn’t kept up by aircraft noise.
We (family of four, with children -- and -- years) had adjoining rooms. My only real complaint was that I had booked directly over the phone with Doubletree and been told that they could accommodate a reservation that specifically included a room with one queen adjoining a room with two twins. When we arrived, the check-in clerk informed me that all they had was adjoining twin rooms. I had pre-paid to get a favourable rate, so there shouldn’t have been an issue getting the room I had paid for.
That said, everything else at the hotel was good. The total cost, including all taxes, was $-- per room. The hotel is a conference-style airport hotel, so it is larger than typical economy-style airport hotels, has an outdoor pool (which we didn’t use) and restaurant facilities.
We had already had dinner before we arrived, so we didn’t need to find anywhere to eat. I understand that there is not much nearby, in terms of restaurants. There is fast food next door, as well as a gas station with a small grocery store. After we arrived, we walked down to the grocery store and bought some soda and liquor to take on the cruise. It was very convenient and the price was right.
The rooms were fairly basic – nothing special. But they were more than adequate – very clean and comfortable. Each room had a flat-panel LCD television (something in the --” range, I’d guess). However, I’ve yet to stay at a hotel with HD-capable TVs that actually provides HD programming. It’s sort of pointless to provide widescreen TVs without the widescreen, HD programming.
Other than the problem with room types on check-in, the hotel staff were excellent. They provided excellent information when we asked about nearby grocery and liquor stores. In addition, we checked out around --:-- and waited in the lobby for our hired car to pick us up at --:--. Even though we were early (the car wasn’t late), the bellman insisted on calling the car service to make sure the driver would arrive on time. The car did arrive on time and got us quickly to Galveston for a price that was far better than the competition. I highly recommend “Z-Limousine” if you are looking for Town Car service at taxi price in the Houston area. Trip Advisor's rules preclude me from including their phone number of email address in this review.
While I was thoroughly satisfied with the rooms and the price (except for the room-type issue), my review wouldn’t be accurate if I didn’t mention one thing I noticed literally as we were leaving the room to check out. As I was just about to drag my suitcases into the hallway, I stopped to toss some paper into the trash can in the bathroom and noticed a small line of ants working its way around the trash can.
Because I hadn’t noticed them during my stay, it really didn’t affect my impression of the room. I mentioned it to the registration staff at check-out and they seemed genuinely concerned. I got the sense that they would have refunded the room charge if I’d been a “difficult customer” (or would have reduced my charges if I hadn't prepaid), but I told them that I had only noticed it as I was leaving and it really wasn’t a problem for me at that point.
For the price I paid, I would definitely stay at the Doubletree Houston Intercontinental Airport Hotel again and I probably wouldn't bother looking around, hoping to find some place that might be better.

Room was lovely, carpet and all linens were clearly new. Bed was comfortable, towels were plush, carpet was plush. Yes, there were some picketers at front, but they ignored us, and we ignored them. Location was incredible, we walked to concert at Soldier Field, and many museums were within walking distance. Our hairdryer didn't work, they replaced it within moments of our call to front desk. The room next door lit up a cigarette, we called front desk, they immediately sent security. Our only complaint would be the lack of water pressure. It was pretty pathetic, but not so bad that I couldn't shower. I would definitely stay again.

First of all, this is huge hotel with - towers. As far as restaurants, the food was fair, but there was not alot to choose from for kids. My son did like the Starbucks that was downstairs, though. The hotel is pretty and the pools are nice. The hot tub was a little small. On one of the nights, they showed a kids' movie by the pool, so kids could swim and enjoy the show. 
The problem came upon our departure. When we left the hotel, we were homeward bound. Upon landing, my children and I remembered that we had left some souveniers in the hotel room. I immediately called the hotel to see if they had found them. The lady who answered the phone could not contact lost and found because they were already closed. After trying to contact the person who cleaned the room, she found that the room had been cleaned, but the person who did the trash was already gone and they did not have a contact number. The lady who anwered the phone was kind enough to go to the room herself to look for the items. She called me back to report the items had already been cleaned and removed, but that I could check back the next day to see if they were in lost and found.
When I called the next day, Marriot contact the man who did the trash for the room and after much conversation with Marriot, it was found that the items were indeed thrown away. To their credit, Marriot did have some people search through the trash as best they could, however the items could not be found.
I was very frustrated that a hotel such as the Marriot would so carelessly throw away souveniers. These souveniers were in a DISNEYLAND sack. Easily, if someone had bothered to look inside, they would have found that they were items that were not meant to be left behind.
It was totally my fault for leaving them, but I do believe the person who cleaned the room went the easy way out in order to not have to be bothered by taking items to lost and found. One of Marriot's reponses to this was that they are a convention hotel and people are always leaving items they don't want that have been give aways in their hotel rooms. The supervisor over housekeeping did acknowledge that the cleaners should be more observant to what they think is trash. 
Marriot did offer me and my family a - night stay at their hotel in San Diego in case we are back in that area. The sad thing is, the drawings that were lost are ones that cannot be recreated, and are not something I can just purchase online. 
I am largely responsible, but I would have expected more out of a high dollar hotel.

We have almost only stayed in budget motels (often Motel - chains) in our trip across the USA and the Motel - in El Paso is one of the lowest ranking for us. That said, the rooms were clean, the water was hot, everything worked and the view of the valley in the morning was amazing. The motel is well located near restaurants and shops but it is in need of a spruce-up.
The rooms were smaller than most Motel - rooms we have stayed in. The blankets were worn and the room in need of a re-paint and light fittings not attached to the wall with a chain might have made it more welcoming. At the time we stayed there was a small flood near the office which did not inconvenience us but added to the run-down atmosphere.
We felt safe there and the staff were friendly. I would normally recommend Motel - to anyone looking for budget accommodation in the USA but this one needs some investment.

We stayed here while in Baltimore for a baseball game at Camden Yards. It has a beautiful appearance from the lobby to the actual rooms. The location was great and it was a short walk to the inner harbor and not as busy as the downtown hotel area. The inner courtyard area was great as was the breakfast room. 
Our room a sudio suite was roomy, comfortable and modern. The beds were comfy and the free wi fi was great.
 The front desk staff was courteous and friendly. We arrived before the scheduled check in time on a busy baseball weekend and they were able to get us into our room early which was much appreciated!
We loved everything about this hotel and will definitely return here again.

We booked the Carlyle Suites for a --st birthday weeks in advance for - people. The reservation was for a grand double with sleep sofa. Check was at -PM. When we checked in at -:-- PM we were told our room was taken and they were going to upgrade. The upgrade turned out to be a double room, no sleep couch and no bathroom door just a curtain!!!! It was for a handicapped individual- perfect for a --st birthday!!! The manager, S.A., stated that the city was booked for the Caribbean festival, people who were supposed to leave didn't, and there was nothing he could do, except try to find another hotel. After we said we would like to leave he said he would try to find some other rooms in the hotel. This was not relayed until we decided to leave. The karma was very bad and we tried to salvage what was left of the evening. Fortunately we found another hotel and left.

Our check-in at the Dana Hotel went smoothly, via a friendly & helpful clerk. Be warned there may be overnight parking fees to contend with, ours were waived apparently after we checked our bill. The room was hard to find due to the way the buildings are marked but we were pleasantly delighted to find our room was on the top of a --floor building and our bedroom-balcony had a fantastic view of the Mission Bay just yards away. The entire wall is windowed, with movable shutter doors to block light or open to the panorama. The nightclub adjacent to the motel is closed and presented no problem. Morning continental breakfast was fine. Hint: Some GPS units do not seem to have the address of this motel in them, We were able to locate the motel by using an ATT cell phone with GPS, however. Is a budget priced property which is well maintained and service was good. Is less expensive than any other chain motel in the area. Free wireless internet worked great. Microwave and small fridge in the room were a nice touch.

I booked this hotel while sitting in the airport prior to leaving for NYC, based on reviews online. Believe me, this spot does NOT disappoint!
ROOMS: Our room was the cheapest available at booking. Upon check-in, we were given a free one-step upgrade. The room was small but well stocked. The iPads used to contact guest services were a GREAT feature....very easy to use! The bed was extremely comfortable and well-tended each day by the staff. The best feature of the room was the bathroom-vanity, which made every hygienic chore a pleasure to engage in! 
FACILITY: The hotel doesn't have, to my knowledge, a pool or business center or conference area. It definitely doesn't seem geared to business travelers or large families. For locals or couples, though, it's perfect. While we did not partake of any food at the restaurant on site, it was always crowded, as was the lounge & bar areas. The lobby was spectacular. Also, the hotel was QUIET - a luxury in downtown Manhattan! Our room was directly in front of the elevator doors and we never heard a bump, bedsprings, honking horns or street noise. Very serene. 
LOCATION: - blocks from Times Square, - from Grand Central station. --th Street was never super busy, which was nice when walking as tourists & street vendors weren't an annoyance. There are plenty of small restaurants in the area, and great shopping only a couple blocks to either side! Also, LOTS of taxis...the plethora of hotels on this row meant you never had to wait to grab a ride. 
STAFF: Super attentive, super friendly. Concierge services were knowledgeable and helpful, and the only problem we experienced our entire stay (iPad wasn't configured properly) was fixed in under - minutes directly from the front desk. You can't beat that. 
SUMMARY: If you're here with a bunch of kids or need business amenities on-site, this location won't be your best choice. For local travelers, couples or singles on vacation, this is a fantastic hotel with a great value!

Really enjoyed my stay in NYC but the hotel room was adequate and we spent very little time in it. It was really quiet at night but we got lucky with a room on the top floor. On the final day we noticed that some items had gone missing from one of our party's luggage and we mentioned this to the management who were sympathetic but ultimately unhelpful... very frustrating to think that your possessions aren't safe when you leave them secure in your hotel room.
Overall, the location was great - right next to Carnegie Hall & Times Square. Subway was really handy - literally on the street outside the hotel. 
Food in restaurant was good by New York standards, but I wouldn't rate this city highly in that regard so not much of a compliment. The waiting staff were really friendly and attentive though.

We stayed at the Burnham this past weekend and were really very pleased. The lobby area is quite lovely, as was our room. I must say the room was really very small, but it was very well appointed and the entire East wall was one huge window. We didn't feel cramped at all, but I could see how someone would.
Although there is no mistaking us more multi-millionaires, we received particularly good service from all of the staff, from the doormen to the concierge. 
We found a rate of $----night on the hotel's own website, and at this rate we feel we received a very good value.
Chicago is a fantastic city and I would definitely recommend considering this hotel.

We stayed here as a family of -, and we could not have been happier with our choice. We went to Washington to see the monuments, public buildings, Smithsonians and Arlington, and this extended stay style hotel allowed us to do alll of that in a relaxed way. Strong positives:

* spacious, well appointed rooms with a compact, full kitchen, washer-dryer in the apartment, -bathrooms, and - TVs (it stops a 'my turn argument'!)
* clean and neat, ith comfortable bedding

Apparently, the AKA White House can be hard to get into when lots of long term guests (--- weeks duration) move in, so if you get the opportunity to stay for a short term visit, grab it. The hotel deserves a higher Tripadvisor ranking.

Both nights it was very difficult to sleep due to the noise from the elevator floor bells and the elevator going up and down. It sounded like a truck running past the room every - to - minuets. The hotel was full and no other room available. I stayed the rest of the week at the Westin.

This had to be the worst hotel stay I have had in years. I was on a business trip, scheduled to stay elsewhere but was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""bounced"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to the Days Inn because of oversold rooms with a huge convention in town. Too bad the Days Inn can't keep up with its neighbors in standards and cleanliness.

OK..it's not a - star hotel...it is more of a budget Hilton...but the staff was extremely pleasant, polite, helpful and accomodating!
The location is excellent. Few blocks from FW, trolley, Ghiradelli square, etc. Also, after taking cable car up the hill, you can walk down the crooked street (Lombard & Hyde) and walk back to Hotel!

I would recommend this place, but next time we would stay in another location...but no complaints about the Hilton! A little outside of the Loop, but still conveniently located to all the main attractions. Typical of other La Quinta sites. Room was clean. Bed was comfortable. Breakfast was the usual...breads, pastries, juice, fruit, yogurt and the now ubiquitous self-made waffle stations. They also had some 'hot' items, but they never looked appealing. Can't go wrong.
Accommodating staff, safe, decent beds. Well kept and one of the cheapest rooms you'll find in SF. Vertigo is just round the corner for a fun filled night of music and dance.

I was apprehensive about staying in a hotel in Manhattan with such low rates ($--- per night + tax) but after reading the reviews and staying a night at the Red Roof Inn, I can say with no hesitation: STAY HERE!
Red Roof Inn is situated in the Koreatown area of Manhattan, which is close to just about everything. I felt very safe during my visit and definitely heard no noise from my thirteenth floor room. And what a room it was: for such a paltry sum (by New York City standards), I got a microwave, mini-fridge, flat screen tv, free high-speed wireless net, a continental breakfast, and the enjoyable iHome was included in the room. The shower pressure was awesome (we all have our 'particulars' and that's mine!) and the bathroom was well-appointed. 
The service was great and the staff was helpful--even allowing me to check my baggage following my checkout, until I was ready to leave the city. My one very minor complaint would be that the elevators do take some time; it didn't bother me much, but some fast-paced travelers might find that frustrating.
A wonderful location + a steal of a price makes this a wonderful choice for your stay in New York City. The subway is just a block away, and there is a delicious Red Mango yogurt store nearby, which I would highly recommend. I hope to make it back someday to both the store and the Red Roof Inn!

We loved this hotel. The entire staff was very friendly and attentive. The location couldn't be beat and we got a great price. The lounge service was good, the breakfast was fabulous. We will definately stay here again

We just returned from a - night stay at the Marriott Marquis and were very pleased in all areas. Upon arrival, I requested a room with a good view as this was our first time to New York. The clerk cheerfully gave us a room on the --th floor overlooking Times Square. The room was plenty spacious and very clean. A perfect alternative to branded hotels . Perfect location close to several nice restaurants and large shopping mall. Reception in hotel was very good and fast , rooms are big enough for - people ( - adults and - children ) and very nicely designed as is entire hotel including swimming pool. My compliments to the entire staff in this hotel everybody working in this hotel was always very friendly and was always ready to help. We will promote your hotel to our friends.

I had been to NYC on two different occasions and was looking for a place to stay on my honeymoon. I looked and looked with no luck when my travel agent suggested the Hotel Giraffe. My wife and I teach school for a living and are by no means wealthy, but for six nights we were treated like royalty. The people at this hotel were WONDERFUL!!!! I have NEVER stayed in a hotel that treated me as well as the folks at Hotel Giraffe. But the positives do not stop there. The rooms were very very clean. The rose petals on the bed and the wine and strawberries were a nice touch for this honeymoon couple. The only concern I had going in was there was not a hot breakfast, but the breakfast proved to be very very good, and I really enjoyed the free papers available to read at breakfast. The staff at breakfast was very nice as was all the staff, the cleaning crew, the maintenance crew ( I put my key by a credit card and couldn't get in my room the maintenance gentlemen went with me to the front desk to make sure I got another key) and the gentlemen working the door treat you like you are a kind. The view from my room, --- was wonderful, I enjoyed the big french doors and the view they offered. This hotel needs to be rated number one in my book.

Stayed a few days for a conference & really liked it! I hope to return. The hotel is beautiful with historical charm. My room was comfortable & clean. I was lucky enough to be on the -th floor & stumbled upon the lounge, which was a very nice surprise. The service was amazing in the lounge with them even making up a plate of amazing food after the dinner time period was done. My only complaint is that my room was near a service elevator & it was a bit noisy at times. Otherwise it was the perfect place for me.

This hotel always has great service, especially those who need access to the Medical Center. From the Valet to the Driscoll restaurant to the check in desk- all exceed expectation(s). Well done again!

We stayed at the Edison for the first time from --st January to -th February and were delighted with our stay. We normally go cheap and cheerful and book in to Milford Plaza when in NY but decided to change to the Edison a week before our stay as we had the option of taking a suite for a little more than what we were paying at the Milford. We were not disappointed with this decision. The Milford is currently a building site and would have meant for an awful stay in NY. In comparison, we found the Edison to be peaceful, relaxing, friendly, clean, and an ideal location. As one of our party has not been keeping great health recently, taking a suite was the ideal decision as it meant he was able to relax in much more comfort. Yes, the room was a little dated but you get what you pay for -if I wanted super luxurious, modern quality I would have gone elsewhere and paid three times the price. That said, the suite was clean, comfortable, the bed was soft, the bathroom well stocked and clean, and we really couldn't find fault. I have read reviews on here of construction work going on - I was not aware of any work going on in the hotel, maybe we were just lucky. Will we back? Oh yes. The Milford's loss is the Edison's gain and I look forward to our next stay with great anticipation.

If you want to explore Seattle's Pioneer Square district, there's no better hotel to do it from than the Best Western Pioneer Square located at the heart of this neighborhood. It's right across the street from the Seattle Underground tour (recommended!) and near restaurants and other amenities. This is a a small, old character hotel though, so you have to be prepared for what comes with that - a slow elevator, no fitness room or pool, no onsite dining other than the breakfast bar, minimal meeting or business facilities. This is not hotel to stay at on business or bring small children to. It reminds me of similar boutique hotels in San Francisco's Union Square, but quieter at night and with fewer other attractions nearby.
The front desk staff at the B-W Pioneer Square are top notch. Very friendly and accommodating. Returning there after a day of knocking around, you really felt like you were coming home. The staff next door at the breakfast bar were less warm, but not obnoxiously so.
The quest rooms are larger than you'd think in such an old property. This generosity of proportion does not extend to the bathrooms however, which are quite dinky. The room decor is in definite need of updating - you have mismatched bed and window coverings, both of which appear to date from the --'s, on top of old carpet. Our room was quite long, with perhaps eight feet of empty floor between the bed and and armoire in which perched a --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" CRT television. You practically needed opera glasses to watch it. Updating the rooms and in-room amenities would greatly improve the property.
These are minor complaints, and on the whole we really enjoyed our stay.

As written hundreds of times by others, the location is great, away from the heavy traffic but close enough to everything. We walked to Rockefellow Ctr, Grand Centra Terminal, and Madame Taussads Wax Museum with no problems subways, Broadway is a block away, and so is Times Square and NY sightseeing tour buses.

The elevators are small. the in room safe came in handy as well as the kichenette. Wake up calls were prompt, no alarm clock in the room. The Olympic Resturant around the corner is good and reasonably priced for breakfast. Doorman very nice about holding luggage after check-out for late departure visitors. Didnt have time to use hotel's other ammendities, too busy having fun on the town. Overall, the Belvedere is the right hotel choice for those who prefer clean, quiet, friendly,
not too lavish hotels at a decent price.
We enjoyed it!!!!

This was a recommendation from one of my work colleagues who was in Houston two weeks ago. The hotel is very well-located right behind the Galleria Mall area. They have shuttles to the Galleria Mall if you want to go shopping or grab some dinner. 
Very clean rooms, quiet and excellent breakfast buffet (additional $---). I would stay there again and recommend to others next time I am in Houston.

the hotel is in a great spot and lots of good eateries, bars and shopping nearby. the room, especially the bed, very comfy and the room service particularly good - prompt, friendly and worth using. try the seduction in soho package with the american breakfast delivered to your room every day! the bar has a top atmosphere - very cool with good lighting and music. table service very good. the concierge was very helpful at booking a restuarant for us and the doormen equally so at grabbing us cabs. the room heating-air con was faulty though and check in was surly - the only - small points in an otherwise excellent stay.
definitely recommend you go there without hesitation.

A relaxing atmosphere and most comfortable bed in the busy bustle of the downtown city life. Wish the spa was a little bigger, but the workout facilities are great!

Love this hotel! We were able to get a last minute room at the begining of December. The staff was so accommodating, and the rooms were gorgeous! We are coming to New York for a broadway show January ---th, and have already booked our reservations here again!!! This place is a STEAL!!!

This hotel was fabulous from the decor to the rooms but the most memorable was the bellman Tony Bennett (yes that is his real name), he was AMAZING! Tony is so full of life, spunk overall genuine kindness that you really don't find these days. Hats off to the supervisors for hiring such a wonderful employee!

We had the best time at Edison in New York!!! Special thanks to Ryan at Front desk, very professional and helpful! We liked our room ---- very much, and would definitely like to come back.

What a pleasure it was to stay at the Hotel Burnham last week. I travel a lot and usually stay at Hilton properties so to stay at a boutique hotel and experience the outstanding service was so rewarding. I would recommend this hotel to anyone!!

I was curious as to how any Ritz-Carlton property could NOT be rated in the top five in any city-resort location, but I now know why. I originally chose The Colonnade due to the convenience of its location to a top-flight Boston restaurant where my wife and I were attending a celebratory dinner. We parked conveniently right in the hotel building which is not always the case in Boston. We were checked in courteously and efficiently by a desk clerk who treated us as though we were weekly guests. As we opened our guestroom door, we were met by a friendly woman who had just turned down our bed. She did her best to refuse the tip I eventually had to force on her. Our room was spotless. We appreciate the security they provide. This guy added unexpected touches of personality and hospitality. We enjoyed very professional service at Brasserie Jo, the hotel restaurant, for breakfast. I'm not just talking the server, but the busboy whose duties apparently included serving water and coffee. The menu was French and fun. Everyone with whom we interacted at The Colonnade was professional in appearance, anxious to help and most knowledgeable. This is a hotel experience we will go out of our way to seek to repeat.
