I can't say the hotel lobby feels particularly luxurious or welcoming when compared to other high-end Marriott hotels. The decor is a bit of a mish-mash of old building features (like the checkerboard floor tiles) and new (like the CFL bulbs casting harsh, bright-white light into the lobby area). The small reception desk area can be very crowded at times. I didn't want to linger. I just wanted to get away from the crowd and go to my room right away.
Initial check-in was smooth, and I was impressed that the smiling front desk clerk had my keys ready for my arrival. I trekked up to my assigned room on the -th floor and found a do-not-disturb sign hanging on the knob. Assuming it was a housekeeping oversight, I opened the door to find clothes and used towels scattered across the room, so it clearly was an occupied. Annoying, but it does happen. Back downstairs again for a quick re-assignment and key exchange, and no further problems were encountered.
My room was what I call typical """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Marriott-style"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" with upgraded cotton linens and down-feather pillows on a comfy bed, a small computer work desk, and a small bathroom with tub and shower. The bathroom had two small double doors opening outward, which made things a bit awkward, since one would block the entrance door. A comfortable upholstered chair, ottoman, dresser, large-screen TV, small refrigerator, and safe completed the furnishings. My room had a nice view of Christopher Columbus Park on the north side of the building with partial views of the water and the North End. Wired and wireless internet is apparently available in rooms, although I wasn't traveling with a laptop to try either. (Note: Marriott's wired-for-business package runs $--.---day.)
The Oceana Restaurant just off the lobby serves seafood, and it is open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. I liked the modern nautical decor, and I had a couple of meals at the bar. Bar staff were universally friendly and efficient, even when busy. I can recommend fresh oysters on the half shell (six for $--) as well as the crab-crusted cod ($--), which was absolutely fantastic. I overheard other patrons raving about the lobster ravioli with a sherry cream sauce ($--). Despite the many excellent dining options near the hotel, Oceana is an outstanding choice if you should decide to stay in.
The Concierge Lounge on the -th floor is at the water-side end of the hallway with a kind of solarium feel. The large windows face the harbor, and the lounge offers a wonderful place to relax and watch the world go by. The continental breakfast selection is pretty standard. Evening snacks and desserts were better and more varied, so I suggest stopping by for a drink and hors d'oeuvres before, say, trekking to the North End for some fantastic Italian cuisine.
I can suggest to anyone thinking of visiting Boston to stay at the Marriott Long Wharf just based on location alone. My only dislikes were the feng shui of the lobby and rather dark and dreary hallways. I realize it's an old building which the designers-decorators have tried to re-package as a modern hotel with historical features, but the combination doesn't quite work. I cannot honestly describe it as luxurious like other hotels in the Marriott category - I have patronized. Comfortable? Yes. Convenient? Yes. Good staff? Yes. Recommended? Absolutely.

The best part of this hotel was the location. Pacific Beach was busy but incredibly beautiful. The partial ocean view room made our vacation. We slept with the patio door open and listened to the waves crash on the beach at night. (There were no mosquitoes, which, for a family from Ontario was a very welcome change.) There is lots to do in San Diego, and Bora (I think that is his name) from Blue Sea Transportation, drove us around in his very comfortable car, never missed a timing, and was an excellent tour guide (thanks Bora, you helped to make our vacation special). The only thing we did not like about the room was the shower, it was installed too low so okay for small kids but adults had to duck down to get there hair wet. Other than that I can’t say enough good, steps to the beach, great restaurants within walking distance, friendly staff. I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

Location is prime near the Farmer's Market, the Grove, and Television City. Fairfax is a busy commercial street that lacks warmth. Once you walk in the Farmer's Daughter you feel like a person again. The restaurant on premises -- Tart -- serves great fare all day. The rooms are comfortable and cleverly decorated. Nothing fancy, but quite welcoming. We had a sort of wacky assortment of needs in our party (me, my husband, a niece, a friend, my brother, his son...) and the front desk accomodated all of our little peculiarities with pleasant aplomb. I am always happy to get out of the bowels of LA. It's not my thing. But I would definitely stay here again! (parents of children ages - - -- might not want to expose their kids to some of the tackier jokes and sexist tart references, but that was not our party)

We'd heard a lot of good things about the Tuscan Inn from people who'd stayed there for a night or two before cruising out of the port of San Francisco. Normally we'd stay at the SF Hilton, or one of the Marriott properties, but we decided this time to try something else.
The Tuscan Inn room was quite nicely appointed, the bed was comfortable the chairs & TV adequate, the bathroom reasonably good. Street noise can be a problem in an outside room, though, and the window coverings (sliding Roman blinds that don't quite meet) left a lot to be desired if you don't want to get up with the sun.
Housekeeping service was very inadequate, though. We left the room at --:-- AM, placing the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""please make up room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" tag in the key slot. There were at least -, and maybe -, housekeeping carts between our room & the elevator. Yet when we returned at -:-- the room hadn't been touched! 
The attached restaurant (Cafe Pescadore) is open for breakfast with a fairly skimpy menu - but quite good coffee.
On balance, it was an OK place to stay but, perhaps, not to return to. It's fine if it's convenient to what you're doing in the city.

Was in New York at the beginning of August for - night and my employer booked me this hotel as it was next door pretty much to their office. Location was awesome and I thought it was a cozy little place, the lobby is very small and the - elevators are situated just in between the - counter desk... Room was nice and the bathrom was awesome, great big shower stall...I like...!!!
Complimentary breakfast was pretty good I must say and the room behind the lobby was also very nice...
It was a very pleasant stay

After reading the reviews at Tripadvisor scheduled a two night stay at this hotel. The rooms were well maintained and clean. The staff were especially helpful seeming to go out of their way to help. The complimentary breakfast included boiled eggs to satisfy those on a low-carb diets, plus fresh waffles for those requiring a sugar boost to last the day. Excellent value for money.

This is great hotel if you dont care about - star quality. the rooms are a good size and very comfortable beds. the only dwnside is it could have done with more plugs for phones, laptops etc. parking is great and good fast food around it. very handy for getting to Hollywood walk of fame (-mins). apart from a personal incident, i would ---% stay here again.

This small hotel is a little off the tourist track, so if you're expecting tourist attractions at the doorstep, look elsewhere, but is in a perfect location across from The Garden for NHL or NBL games, as well as North Station (for commuter rail and T-subway). It is within walking distance to North End (Italian village), Waterfront, Beacon Hill, Faneuil Hall, and for the energetic to Boston Common-Downtown Crossing. While it's a little quiet at night, I didn't feel unsafe. There are a few pubs-restaurants on the same street as the hotel (but better to go to North End), as well as Au Bon Pain and --Eleven. Free morning coffee-tea was no longer available while I was there, but they happily supplied me with a coffee percolator. The staff were friendly and helpful. The entrance is a bit crowded in the evening when there's free wine-cheese, but I didn't partake in this, nor use the bar or room service. My room was on a high floor, was bright, clean and of average size, and decent comfortable bed. I was initially a bit concerned about having pets as neighbours, but was reassured they're sequestered on allocated floors, and I didn't hear a peek out of any pet-neighbour during the stay. The CRT TVs were replaced by large screen LCD TVs while I was there. Overall, it's a decent convenient hotel.

My wife and I stayed here over Memorial Day Weekend to see the Cardinals vs Cubs at Wrigley Field. This was a great location! The Red Line stop was right outside the front door, and in -- minutes we were at Wrigley. It was great to have all kinds of dining options at night, but we were still able to get wherever we wanted on the El. Front desk service was outstanding and the rooms were quiet and clean. This is one of the best values in the city, and we will stay here every time we return to Chicago. Typical Hilton quality and service.

Just back from - days stay in New York with my partner and two teenage boys - we stayed in the Doble Tree Hotel Times Square it was an excellent hotel as long as you didn't use any of the facilities in the hotel as everything was wayyyyy over priced there. We just used it as a base and it was very comfortable and quiet (despite being in the middle of Time Square) maybe that was something to do with the fact we were on the --th floor. I woud definitely recomend this hotel if there is more than two people in your party as it had two queen beds and a pull out couch bed in the sitting room so plenty of room. Security great in hotel so felt safe. Loads of places nearby to have breakfast and Juniors accross the road for steak or burger and all the shows what more would you want in New York

We stayed in Chicago at the end of our route -- adventure. So we were really happy that we pre booked this hotel for a nice and relaxed days in Chicago. Hotel is nice & clean and really almost on Magnificent mile. But that great position in downtown Chicago, cost you extra money... we payed extra --$ for two days of parking our car. Hotel stuff are friendly & really quick. We check inn & out really in a couple of minutes. The only unpleasant thing was the position of our room. It was just over the hotel air - condition system and for that reason it was noisy. ut Chicago is noisy town otherwise. Really great place for sightseeing Chicago.

The hotel is located a few blocks away from Skid Row in downtown LA. The hotel itself tries to be very 'LA hip'. There is a salon, a bar, a restaurant, a rooftop pool. It might be a nice place to stay if you want to take someone for an authentic """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""LA hipster night out"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I would recommend this hotel to someone IF they HAD to be downtown for some reason or they wanted a hotel where they could party with wanna be socialites.
The beds are super comfy, the TV works and the bathrooms and big and clean. But the decor is kinda gross and it has an IKEA feel to it. 
PROS:
- Comfy beds
- Good food at the restaurant
- Nightlife hot spot for LA Hipsters
CONS:
- Location is horrible
- You have to valet your car
- Room decor needs an upgrade
- Expensive

I arrived late thursday night and was apreciative of the ease with which I checked in to my room. More importantly I was vey glad that when she asked for a card to hold my room she made sure to specify a credit card. I have in the past had vacations marred by the front desk swiping my debit card and leaving me with no cash for the rest of my vacation. After a long day of travel I would have surely handed her the wrong card had she not clarified, so I appreciated her clarity. 
Upon arriving to my room I found soft soothing music playing on my bedside table and the most luscious bed I have slept in of late. 
The washroom was spacious and well-lighted with great fixtures and a tub made for soaking, which I promptly took advantage of. The bed as I mentioned was terrific I have slept in so called """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""heavenly beds"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and the sheets on those always feels rough or synthetic. The beds at hotel vitale are smooth and soft and fluffy and made for restful sleep. And what a restful sleep I had (after indulging in the delicious ghirridelli chocolate that was waiting next to my bed.)
The next day I enjoyed some of the best coffee that I have had in SF downstairs in the attached restaurant and then strolled over to the irresistable Ferry Building when I found great breakfast, gorgeous views and some presents for people I was visiting. 
When it was time to leave I certainly did not want to go. I have been so thoroughly charmed by the hotel, by its sophisticated and natural style, warm and accomidating staff, fun and accessible location and of course the dreamy beds, I know now where I'll be staying whenever I have the pleasure of being in SF.

The London NYC is a superb little hotel. It's within walking distance of Broadway as well as Lincoln Center, not to mention the best shopping in New York on -th Avenue. The concierge service is without parallel.The service is superior, yet tasteful. I've always felt at home. The staff really does go the extra mile-even without the usual NYC style tipping. Immaculate rooms, a well equipped gym and restaurants by Gordon Ramsay-how can one go wrong!

i've stayed here twice, once in feb ---- and again feb ----. the first stay, we had a -bd suite, and i have no complaints about that stay. the rooms were very nice, we had fresh brand toiletries. it was excellent. the second time, we had a single room, and didn't have the nice toiletries (i am a huge fan of fresh), and the room just wasn't as clean as i wanted it to be. small stains here and there - needed a bit more attention to detail. it's a great location (though you have an uphill-downhill walk to-from the common), and the staff is very nice. i LOVE the working fireplaces in each room. we like the restaurant's breakfast.
going again in the next month, so we'll see if there are any differences!

It was wonderful to find a B&B in such a great location. The rooms are large and have gas fireplaces. Being able to eat breakfast every morning without having to go to a restaurant was the best way to start the day. The staff was very friendly and helpful. We have been to SF several times before but this is now our favorite place to stay.

All the staff had the right attitude and seemed genuine in their desire to do their best. The rooms were clean and comfortable and had all necessary and advertised amenities. The complimentary breakfast was good and convenient, but not great.
Parking is the main detractor. VERY expensive, with little curb space for check-in-out.
Overall, a solid - rating.

We booked this hotel through Hotwire for $----night for a family weekend trip. The location is great and within walking distance to many great restaurants and local venues as well as transportation. Parking was easy and having in-and-out access all day was nice. Cost -- bucks a day but par to better than most in the city. We loved the detail and charm of the hotel which makes you feel like you are back in the roaring --'s or something. Rooms are small but adequate, especially if you are basically just sleeping there. The walls were thin and lots of noise from pipes and all but not too bad. Concierge helped us find some great places to eat within a short walk, since we have two small children. We did not use room service, the restaurants, or pool while visiting so cannot comment on those. It is a neat historic hotel in a great location for any stay in Chicago but maybe not the most comfortable nights sleep. Definitely great value for price paid.

The first night here the mattress was so terrible, I thought I might fall out of the bed.
They did change my room but, to my surprise, the room was re rented the next day and 
I saw the maid in there and someone's bags, and the mattress was as it was the night I stayed in the room! No one really addressed it with me, I am a Platinum member of Hyatt! Most Hyatt places are all the same, some are newer than others, this was an older property, just saying.

Good location, and a clean well air conditioned room with a bathroom of fair size on the newer side and ease of a fridge and microwave in the room. The beds were comfortable and our main complaint is while the parking is free; you get what you pay for. The lot is miniscule (-- cars max) and usually full; not that we were thrilled about parking there and leaving with a damaged rental car, all spots are tight, and parking on the street in that area is not easy. We have had better luck parking further south in the Dupont circle area. Also, the restaurant is only fair, and the room service is limited in menu and time served, But if you do not have a car to park, and are not eating in the hotel, this was an OK choice. Free WIFI with hotel code.

Well positioned - near Central Park and within walking distance of Times Square. 
Handy for tube. Normas for breakfast is to be recommended and the French brasserie style bar is delightful. The burger bar seemed a strange addition to an upmarket hotel but an experience not to be missed.
Staff helpful - had to change rooms on arrival. Had requested a room with - double beds overlooking the park. Initially given a room without a view and with one of the beds a put you up settee!
Expensive with current sterling exchange rate. No tea-coffee making facilities in room.

Spent three nights at the new Intercontinental in May this year. We got a great rate as it had just opened. Generally I'm not keen on big impersonal hotels as I find that often you are treated as one of three hundred guests rather than getting great service - but I was thoroughly impressed by this hotel. The service was friendly and helpful, breakfasts fantastic and the rooms were gorgeous, with an amazing view whichever side you're on (try and get a high up room). We didn't have a bath in our room, but we didn't ask for one and I feel sure if requested you'd get one. But the bathroom was gorgeous with a massive walk-in shower. The hotel is about a - minute walk from the main shopping area, where the tram exchange is and about a ----- walk to union square - but we found the location great. It's hard to find a criticism, but if I had to I'd say the doormen seemed to be invisible - but hey I can open a door myself!

Are you checking because this is the cheapest Hilton and it seems to be in a good location? Well it is both. It is frequently the best price in the area and it is right off the Mile. So if price and location are your top priorities then stay here. If you are traveling with kids you are likely attracted to exactly those qualities - trust me you will not be alone the hotel is full of kids. I don't mind the kids - but I'd never stay here again.
When I booked I reserved a king suite. I did that because I wanted a king and a work area. I'm traveling for business and I needed to work in the room. I check the Hilton zip-in check in box so that I would not be delayed. I arrived to find the hotel was a disaster. The woman at the desk was pitiful.After -- minutes of typing into her computer she called the manager who pointed out that the system was locked up and her computer needed to be restarted. I asked about the zip in folders which at most hiltons let's you avoid this kind of issue. I was told """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""we don't do that here."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I don't know what that means - this one hotel in the Hilton chain is rebelling against efficiency? (and if that is what they intended they are a raving success). When I finally got a room key and went to the room it was a double. I called the desk and was told the hotel had nothing but doubles. Now if you understand how Hilton's zip in system works you know immediately that this hotel must be managed by middle school dropouts. 
I was then told that the double room was an upgrade and I was lucky not to be charged more (???). I was later able to talk to a day shift manager who agreed that his night clerk was an idiot and he adjusted my bill. so I guess I should be happy that I didn't have to pay the premium that I had agreed to pay for a king room since I didn't get one.
The room itself was a sad little affair. There were - double beds (not queens so if you're taller than -'-"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" enjoy the dangling feet experience) plus a sofa and a dresser and a desk and a coffee table and another table. Picture a garage sale - that's what the room looked like. The space was way too small for the amount of furniture stuffed in the room. Then there was the fridge. Since they advertise a fridge in the room I guess they figured they better stick one in there. Since the room was a junkyard anyway there wasn't much worry about where to put it. So it's by the door. I mean right by the door - as in when you enter the room be careful not to trip over the fridge. Seriously - this is a pigsty of a hotel.
The one bright spot was room service - the food was decent and the service was good (and since there is so much crap int he room there were lots of places to set the tray down.
When I left in the morning the day shift seemed pleasant - a lot more competent that the night shift. perhaps mine was an unusual experience - but I'll never stay here again. It's Chicago for goodness sake - there are hundreds of fantastic hotels here - why in the world would you ever take a chance on this place?

I was very excited to spend my birthday in the City and stay at the renowned, Waldor. Well, to keep this brief, I would have been more impressed and gotten better value for my money staying at the Holiday Inn. First off, check-in was confusing and took too long. The elevators malfunctioned (had to go down to go back up). And worst of all the room, was not what we was expect. I get the appeal of old charm, but our room was just OLD and had a weird, musty smell. The tub backed up and we had to space showers so that the water could drain completely. To make matters worse, I was over charged...We compensated for our accomadations by spending absolutely no time there, we returned late and left as soon as we awoke..

After traveling for several hours, from Europe I was glad to check in. Many were attempting to do that at the same time. There could have been more staff.
The TV wasn't connected for some reason, it was corrected.

The only plus of this hotel is the location and again l have stayed in better places in LA. 
We will not be back. The staff at the front desk were rude and unhelpful we watched them with other guests and there attitude was the same. Thinking we got them on a bad day we expected it to improve - nope.. We arrived at Midnight and had advised the hotel our room was gone so we were downgraded it was fine we were tired just wanted to sleep no bellman to help with luggage and no offers. We asked for directions a number of times and got better advice out on the street, The bathroom had mould in a number of spots and the hotel is in major need of a refurb. The lift jerks and one night the bell was ringing for half an hour as it was broken and you could hear it all throughout our level. 
All in all, don't do it there is much better to be had..

Stayed here for business April ----. Overall the hotel is an excellent value for the money. It is clean. Great for biz with Internet and spacious desk. Located close to restaurants and bars an many office buildings. I didn't need a car. Pleasant staff that offered a guests reception consisting of chili,chips, beer, salads. Nice touch. 
Only minor complaint is that the A-C unit was too close to the bed and didn't work that well. It was loud and kept me awake until I got up and turned it off. 
I will likely stay again the next time that I am in town.

First impressions not so good. Arrived after long flight from Europe - very tired. No one to meet the taxi and take the bags. Queue to check in. However, the staff were excellent- friendly and helpful. 
Room fine - just standard business room- no frills. 
Breakfast excellent. Lovely cooked breakfast that changed each day. 
Overall quite expensive and not really any different to any other business hotel.

I'll start with the good - the bed is really comfortable and the staff is kind. The rooms are pretty nice. I definitely had some issues, though. 
Noise: I originally was in a room on the -th floor overlooking the freeway. I went right back downstairs and asked for another room because it sounded like I was in the middle of the freeway. I got moved to a different room on a lower floor that faced the front of the hotel and away from the freeway, but I could still hear the traffic loud and clear throughout the day and the night. I also could hear my neighbors flushing their toilets and drying their hair, as well as the ice machine down the hall. I barely slept the first night, called downstairs to speak with a manager about changing rooms again, but the manager hadn't arrived yet. I asked to have the manager call upon arrival...five days later, I'm about to check out and still haven't heard anything. I would've checked out, but I got the hotel through Hotwire and ahd already paid for it. 
The Security: On my last night at the hotel, my keycard demagnetized. I went downstairs, and the person behind the desk just asked me what room I was in and gave me a new key. She did not ask for ID. I don't care if my mother were behind the desk, I would've wanted her to ask for ID. It made me a little nervous to think that anyone could go down there and say they were staying in any room and get a key to any room...
Rips in the Sheets: I couldn't believe it when I read about ripped sheets in another review before coming, especially at hotel that is almost $----night, but sure enough, there were rips in the duvet and in the fitted sheet. The rip in the fitted sheet extended from the foot of the bed to the middle of the bed.
The Cafe: A bagel and a small bottle of orange juice costs $-.--. And the bagel wasn't even that good.
It is a beat down hotel. Carpets are dirty, it is smelly. The pictures do not represent the reality. It is not worth the $---. per night even on high season.

I traveled to San Jose with my husband on a business trip. Check in was easy. The staff was great. We got a room with a paito to the pool. The pool was beautiful & clean. The room was great and very clean. We loved the location, right downtown. We could walk to restaurants and entertainment. We would stay here again.

Just spent four nights here and found it to be excellent value for money. I paid $----night plus tax, and was amazed at the quality of the rooms. We had a very comfortable king size bed, tastefully decorated room and a large flat screen TV. Location is just on the western edge of downtown at the top of Greektown so there's some handy restaurants nearby. (try Greek Isalnds restaurant) A trip into the Loop is about a ---- min ride on the #-- bus, and there is a supermarket and a Walgreens on either side - handy for those small purchases you need during a stay.
We had our infant son and a clean and comfy crib was provided free. While it is next to the expressway, I found the room to be relatively quiet and not a problem. Our son didn't wake up at all. (I was on the --th floor - perhaps it is worse on lower floors??)
Just a few small things - none of which should be permanent.
-. The restaurant is not finished - I never eat at hotel restaurants anyway because they are so $$$, and if you're in Chicago you *want* to go out to eat. But it did mean that the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""breakfast"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was restricted to a few muffins and coffee on a table in the lobby.
-. The city is doing some roadworks on on of the freeway ramps - and one night decided that --PM was a good time to start work - not sure how often this happens though. (When I first got to the room I noticed there were complimentary earplugs provided by the hotel. I thought """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""that's odd"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" - on the third night I found out why ) Didn't keep us awake though.
-. The web site we booked thru (an AMEX travel site) mentioned a free hotel shuttle available - but this doesn't exist.
All things considered a very enjoyable stay at a reasonable price. Would definately stay again - but suspect that rates may increase when the hotel is complete.

I was in town to see a show and stayed just one night. No bellman came out to the cab to assist with luggage upon arrival, but this was fine as I feel no need to pay someone to handle one bag. The lobby of the hotel is small but tasteful and check-in was quick and pleasant.
My room was on the fourth floor, facing --th Street and the Port Authority, and was fairly spacious by New York standards. It was very clean and all appointments were in good repair. The A-C was easy to operate and effective (although it had a tendency to rattle and I was unable to find the source of the noise). The king bed was extremely comfortable and the pillows-linens were of high quality. The room also included a fairly large flat-screen HDTV, a nice desk area, an armoire, an electronic safe, a coffee maker, and an armchair.
The bathroom was sleek and modern with a spacious, glass-doored, walk-in shower (no tub, if that matters). Mirror lighting was relatively good by hotel standards. The sink was stylish and functional but offered very little counter space for toiletries.
There is a small onsite restaurant that offers a few tables in a glass-roofed, atrium-style space, which was quite pleasant in the morning. I had booked a AAA offer that included a complementary breakfast served there, and the menu price for this meal would've been just under $--. The food was good and the service pleasant enough.
Just outside the restaurant is a guest computer terminal and printer, which allowed me to check-in with my airline online and print out my boarding pass. Use of this equipment was complementary.
The hotel is located about mid-block between -th and -th Avenues. While not the most attractive block in Manhattan, it was a very quick walk to the theater on --th Street and therefore ideal for my purposes. This street can be somewhat noisy, but that's true of most of the busier areas of the city, and I travel with a white noise machine that allowed me to sleep without any major disturbances.
I asked for a cab at check-out and the front desk summoned a doorman who took my one bag and walked me outside to a waiting towncar just a few steps down the block. I asked if this was a cab and the doorman said yes, but it clearly wasn't - New York taxis are not towncars and are never this clean and pleasant. Also unlike taxis, this vehicle was not metered and charged a flat rate of $-- to LaGuardia. Although not what I asked for, the experience was far superior to my taxi ride into the city and the difference in price was less than $--.

I got a great deal on a room at the Orchard for two nights in early April and I would stay there again in a heartbeat. The front desk staff were kind and professional, and the Bellmen were also wonderfully helpful. The room was very nice, everything was very clean and the bed linens were very high quality and I slept very well. There was some street noise, and some hallway noise from other guests but nothing unreasonable or unbearable.

I have stayed in many hotels in the Union Sq area over the years and this is one of the better ones available today. Its been renovated, I mean really done up well! Everything seems new and clean. The flat panel TV's are a nice touch. The rooms themselves are on the small side, buy laid out well and are extrea clean and well furnished. Depending upon which side you face, it can be a bit noisy, but considering the age of the building, no real problem. Get a room on the highest floor possible. Staff is very friendly and helpful. As everybody has already stated, the location one block off Powell is hard to beat. Very easy to grab a cab right outside the front entrance. Definitely a bargain in todays SFO hotel market!

This hotel was is in a great location to see the sights of Seattle Close to the market, downtown and the various types of public transport - The rooms were basic (I had one with a shared bathroom) - but theye were clean, as were the shared facilities. The staff were great on the fron desk, the most helpful I came across in my - weeks in the USA. (And yes, they really do wrap thier towels in the shape of an animal on arival!)

Perfect location (middle of the Embarcadero), superb customer service, clean & inviting hotel. This was out first stay at a Kimpton Hotel and we were impressed. We will definitely stay here again as well as look for other Kimpton hotels when we travel elsewhere.

I am very used to staying at Fairmont hotels while on business trips, but this time it was for pleasure. 
The hotel is impressive; it has the old aristocratic charm to it. I loved the lobby - marble, gold, mirrors, and amazing Christmas decorations; as well as the location – walking distance to all you’d like to see and visit.
Our room was at the -th Gold floor - signature. It was very nice but needed some renovations - chopped bath tub, lots of scratches on the walls here and there. Apparently they are aware of this as some major renovation work is going throughout the hotel. This said - I don't accept being awakened by construction workers whose voices were loudly audible through the AC. Also, the Gold lounge was under renovations and closed. They might have thought of adding some free drinks or something in the room instead. 
The not so impressive part was the room maintenance. The first they we were awaken by the cleaning lady at - (Christmas day) and I asked her to clean when we were out. When we went for a walk at -- and came back at - p.m. the room wasn’t made up at all. I had to call the reception to send somebody while we were away again. The tea and coffee was never replenished (- nights stay), neither was the mouth wash. I realize I am getting picky but small details reveal the class of the hotel.
Above being said, the reception staff was extremely friendly and efficient. I would definitely recommend the hotel while visiting Boston.

Thia was just a one night stop, selected by our agent. A very comfortable hotel, we had a standard room and the bed was brilliantly soft. All usual amenities, helpful staff. pleasant bar staff etc.
Only downer is the area, which seems a bit neglected and we couldn't see any restaurants (other than a few Chinese) in the area.

Hotel is in need of updating, but was clean and the staff friendly and helpful. We stayed here the night before heading out from the airport and on the way back in. Compared to other hotels it was reasonably priced. We used their shuttle to and from the airport and had no problems - they were efficient and on-time.

Great location- very close to Times Square!
Rooms were clean and well maintained and surprisingly big for NYC. Concierge was well versed in restaurants nearby and suggested a great steak house, made us reservations then drew us a walking map. Would definitely stay here again.

I stayed with my husband at the Sheraton Phoenix Downtown Hotel for a convention and we were both extremely dissapointed. The hotel had a TINY little pool and there were only a very few chairs-loungers for such a huge hotel. We had to pay to access internet in the rooms ($---day!), which really burns when you already have paid so much for the room. The rooms are absolutely nothing special - I might have been staying in a Holiday Inn for all the character the room had. Overall, I was really disappointed in the hotel. I do recommend the Copper Square Adventures for a personal, guided hike in the mountains, though! If I were to ever come back to Phoenix, I would definitely NOT stay here and would book a room at The Phoenician.

We stayed here because we found an excellent coupon in one of the traveler mags. The room was clean. You could tell that it was an older hotel but they were remodeling and replacing the carpet. We didn't do the breakfast as there wasn't much to it. Staff was very friendly and helpful.

The fish in the light fixture really sold it for us. Wish we'd been there in the summer for dive-in movies. Look, it's not the Hilton, but it was still awesome. We had a great, comfortable, incredibly affordable stay. Would go back in a heartbeat.

The hotel itself is cosy and clean and is located in a quiet area. We lived at the ninth floor and thank god for the elevator, even though is was very slow and we sometimes gave up waiting and went down the stairs.
The room was small and a bit dark - but it was clean and the housekeeping were very friendly. The hotel manager wasn't too friendly and outgoing - he could do a better job, for sure. Overall is was an awerage stay. The location (near -th ave and empire state building) was great and subway stations were very near.
If you can afford something better, then go somewhere else. If not, then this hotel is fine it you're planning a sightseeing trip to NYC and if you just need a place to sleep.

We stayed at the Chancellor in June having read the reviews on Trip Advisor. It is ideally located and I can see why it is rated so highly, although we had just arrived from Vegas and the Hotel isn't in the same league as those Hotels! Good check in, fast and efficient and a nice room overlooking Powell Street, even if a little small, but we were only there for two nights. If we returned to San Fran (which we probably wouldn't as once you've done Alcatraz, the Pier, Fisherman's Wharf, the City Bus tour and driven over the Bridge and down Lombard Street there isn't much else to do) I would return to this Hotel and would recommend it to anyone, although there are a lot of other Hotels nearby the tram stops right outside this one!

I liked the location of the hotel. It is close to Soho, Chinatown and Little Italy. Plenty of restaurants and shops. I was on the -th floor and saw the tip of the Empire State building. Get a higher floor if you want to get a better view of it. The room was very clean and bed was comfortable. The breakfast at the restaurant was good and the price was reasonable. I would stay here again.

My husband and I stayed at the Holiday Inn Town Lake three nights for a conference. 
Pluses: friendly staff, clean room and bathroom, refrigerator, microwave, cable TV, free shuttle to-from airport and to convention center, located near great jogging-walking trail (Lady Bird Trail), walking distance to convention center (<- mile), right around the corner from the cool up-and-coming Rainy Street neighborhood with its many restaurants-bars.
Minuses: carpet in room needs to be replaced, one of the two queen-size beds sags and should have been replaced a long time ago, the freeway noise is quite noticable on our floor (-th).
From what I noticed, the hotel is not wanting for guests. The day we checked out, there were lines of people waiting to check in, mostly families going to the UT game.

We just came back from our trip to California .We stayed - nights at the Sommerset Suites .It was great. It really was like having your own apt there.The area is fabulous. So many incredible restaurants.We went to the Bombay which was great for India cuisine.We also took the kids to the Corvette Diner and it was a blast.Both these restaurants are about - block away. Also there is a candy store called the Candy Depot right near Bombay the fellow that runs it was so nice ,the candy selections were fun .The shuttle sevice from the hotel worked very well for us .and was way cheaper than a cab.They will take you anywhere within - miles I believe and that is lots of places as the hotel is so central.We liked the hotel we payed $ --- per night and really this was a great deal.

All suite hotel very handy for business. Good free breakfast with decent coffee and handy business center with printers that work..a novelty in some smaller chains. No frills hotel but great staff and large rooms.Easy fre-wi-fi ---- nearby to gas up rental before returning to airport.

I used my reciprocal club arrangement to stay at the University Club prior to our trip to Napa valley. Located on Nob Hill across the street from the Fairmont Hotel, the club is nicely furnished with a beautiful library and outside balcony overlooking the bay. Although there are only about -- rooms, it was a thrill to stay in this quiet, tastefully decorated gem - don't miss it!

The Crosby Hotel is incredibly chic and much thought has obviously gone into the interior decoration. It is a wonderfully furnished hotel for an overnight stay.
However, the same thought has not gone into the practical matter of providing accommodation for travellers who are staying for several days.
We were in a Deluxe Room and our immediate impression on seeing the décor was very positive. 
But then, where were the cupboards in the bathroom for our possessions? 
The bathroom did not look nearly so chic with toothbrushes and other bathroom paraphernalia lining the ledges around it. There was nowhere for a spare toilet roll to be kept so we never got one and we had to continually request replenishments. We also had the same problem with paper tissues. Amazingly, the soap was not changed until the last day of our stay.
The bathroom has two very impressive sinks but they are of such size that it was very difficult to get within range of the mirror in order to shave or apply make-up. Despite having two sinks, only one bar of soap was provided and the soap in the shower was a sink soap rather than a shower soap.
The bed sheets were not changed until we requested it (we knew because the bottom sheet had a tear) and, yet, the same daily rate was charged as if we were new guests each day.
With regard to the rest of the accommodation, there are similar practical issues for the long-term traveller. There are no facilities to make tea or coffee in the room so you have to have room service or go down to the guest room each time you need a coffee or tea. 
Design triumphs over substance so there is no clock in the room.
Room service is not really a practical option in the Deluxe Room as it lacks anywhere for two people to comfortably eat.
The accommodation smacks of a designer who has never stayed a night in the room that he or she designed.
The bar and restaurant areas are good and the food is good.
Service in the hotel is not overly attentive and some of the breakfast staff, in particular, have the knack of avoiding your eye at all times so that one is often left surrounded by dishes and waiting for tea and coffee. 
That said, there are a couple of wait staff who are quite exceptional. 
The staff in the entrance area may or may not pay you attention. It seemed that the more staff there were hanging around the foyer (which could be as many as eight), the less likely that any of them would open the door or acknowledge your existence
The hotel is located in an exciting area of New York that is always gridlocked with traffic and where piles of rubbish litter the streets. However, the street in which the hotel is located is remarkably free of traffic and is relatively clean and quiet.
This is a hotel with great potential but it is very amateurish in its approach and lacks basic quality control.
We have marked the hotel as a long stay destination. The score may have been a little higher had we merely stayed overnight.

I thought this was an above average hotel in a fantastic location.
Room: Modern, clean, very comfortable and quiet rooms. They are slightly small but this is typical for hotels I have stayed in in SF. The discreet in-room recycling bins were a nice touch.
Hotel Facilities: Not much. There is a very small fitness room and 'business centre'. We didn't use the restaurant - there are excellent dinning options very near by. The staff were helpful. 
Location: Great location near Union Square and Chinatown. SF is a very easy city to explore - tip: buy a MUNI pass and use it hop on and off the regular busses and the cable cars, too!

Only - miles from San Diego International, and located at Liberty Station, this hotel is often booked, so plan ahead. If your booking on the gov-military rate, the hotel usually books out about --weeks in advance. It's not in the downtown core, but close (- miles), located across the street from the Point Loma FASWTC Naval base. Quiet location, standard (by which I mean good) Courtyard hot breakfast buffet, dinner (did not eat diner there), good open-layout bar with three TVs (and doesn't have that creepy business-traveller-bar feel), espresso cafe (brews Starbucks, but isn't an actual Starbucks) with cafe food (panini etc...), pool, hottub, private courtyard, plenty of free parking, free wireless, room service (-pm---pm only), dry-cleaning, coin-op laundry with free soap (ask at the desk), modern rooms with LCDs and iPod-iPhone docks on the alarm clocks. They also have the network-video-audio connection strip that allows you to connect your laptop to the TV to review presentations or watch DVDs. Liberty Station also has a Starbucks located in it, and an Oggi's (microbrews, good food, great pizzas) that are a --minute walk form the hotel (I usually eat at Oggi's). This hotel has an excellent combination of ammenities that any serious business traveller looking for a relaxing base-camp would want. This location is everything that the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Courtyard"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" concept was designed for. I've stayed there three times, and it is now the first San Diego lodging I check for when I travel.

We spent two nights here during a journey down the Pacific Coast Highway. We had considered a number of hotels in downtown San Diego but settled on Tower-- as the location looked good and prices were reasonable compared with downtown options. We weren't disappointed.
Although this hotel is few miles out of town, we found the location perfect. You're right on the beach, and there are lots of restaurants, bars and shops within just a few minutes' walk. We hired bikes to explore up and down the beachfront.
When we went into town, we took a cab (about $--). We hopped on the bus back and found it was quick, if you check the timetable so you don't have to hang around to catch one. You can also drive, which is what I imagine most people do.
We stayed in a Sky Pad which had a partial ocean view from the balcony. The room was clean, tidy and nicely decorated, if a little plain. It could've done with a few more pictures on the walls or the odd extra design flourish, like those evident in the hotel's communal areas.
Having said that, it was a good size, and it was great to have a balcony, from which we enjoyed drinks and breakfast.
Service was friendly and efficient. On check in we were offered a welcome cocktail (a nice touch). I think overnight parking is $-- a night, but we parked for free in a space right out front the hotel. It might be harder to find a spot in peak season, but I imagine you'd find one in the surrounding streets easily enough.
The bar and restaurant really made this hotel for us. An imaginative cocktail menu and superb food (including some excellent sliders) meant we spent more time in the hotel bar than we'd expected. There's also a happy hour which offers better value for money.
Overall, an excellent hotel.

This place is garbage. For the price you pay, you would expect some luxury or clean rooms.. Everything is old and outdated. Bathrooms are tiny. When i got to my room there were dirt smearings on the wall and i'n the bathroom, and an old dirty washcloth hanging i'n the shower. They need new cleaning staff who actually clean, and i found hair i'n my sheets that was not mine. They rip you off with every service, the only good thing about this place is the palm trees. This shouldn't be called a resort, it should be called a fat rip off enclosure you can sleep i'n. i wish i would have stayed at marriot!!!

We travel to Austin once or twice each year to visit our son and daughter-in-law. For the past -- years we have stayed at the Four Seasons. It is consistant in service and quality. Though expensive we feel they provide good value for the money. The location on Lady Bird Lake and close to shopping, resturants and entertainment could not be better. The staff is terrific, the lounge bar and Trio resturant are excellent and the whole understated high end experience makes for a wonderful weekend get away.
We really like this hotel, we are comming back in August. Cant wait

Booked this hotel through Hotwire so got a good rate, on arrival the receptionist said that if we would be happy to wait for an extra hour he would upgrade us to a room in the main tower. We got a room on the --st floor with amazing views of the river, empire state and chrysler. The bed was so big and comfortable found it hard to get out of! The staff were very nice and friendly, decent bar in the basement. Location of the hotel perfect as near to everything but on the edge. Hope to stay again when we go again in the spring!
One unexpected thing was the sniffer dogs on duty outside the hotel, but considering how near to the united nations the hotel is maybe this is a sign of the times. Lovely dogs by the way!

The location is perfect for various downtown activities with easy walking access to River North, Michigan Ave, and The Loop. I thought the decor and atmosphere were pretty fun. My only annoyance while staying there was that the ice machine did not work on several floors, though the front desk quickly sent someone to drop some off at the room when I called. I would definitely stay here again, but probably only for a special occasion or if I find another good deal online.

I stayed - nights in the Peninsula and had again a great peninsula experience. Last time in stayed in Four seasons and the Peninsula just has that little bit extra. Chocolates in your room, great breakfast, friendly staff and a very classy lobby. I had dinner in their gourmet restaurant the second night. --- us for a single couvert including wine and digestive. Not cheap but the best culinair experience I had so far in the US. They have a new chef so check it out. Especially the wagyu with cocos is heavenly. Peninsula, done manila and chicago, cant wait to experience the other seven

My advise to anyone on a limited budget - or anyone who would rather spend their cash on sightseeing and eating out in this wonderful city should definetly consider staying at Hotel Astoria.
The check in was fast and easy, the counter staff were helpful and polite. We checked into our room which although basic and the decor a little tired, was clean and quiet with a great powerful shower and a safe.
The breakfast was included in the exceptionally resonable room rates and was more than enough to keep you going until lunch. There are HUGE muffins and bagels - lots of different flavours, bread to make yourself toast and fresh orange juice, coffee and tea. I really dont know why anyone complains about it! We thought it was great.
The best thing about this hotel is the location - for the price it is brilliant. Right near the shops, union sqaure, chinatown. Everywhere downtown is easily within walking distance. Its also on the main road and felt completely safe - always people around. There is also a very handy corner store accross the road if you need any fruit-water-beer etc.
Stay at the Astoria - its great!
To all the people who are worried by the complaints on this hotel - if you are sensible (like we were!) you take in consideration the price you pay for the type of hotel you get. You wouldn't expect to pay for a McDonalds and get a - star silver service meal would you?! 
Clare & Mike - Manchester, England UK

I really liked this hotel. The room was clean, and modern with balcony to step out onto. When you book ask for a river view room because if you get a city view you will not get any sleep from the traffic and sirens below. the staff was excellent. 
The only drawback is that I went out walking alone to site see and found the surroundings to be dangerous. There were a lot of homeless people asking for money and a lot of groups of young adults standing around. I got the feeling I was going to be mugged by the groups of people standing around with no reason for being there. 
This hotel is within walking distance of the Alamo, a mission, the hard rock, and of course it is on the river walk. I thought the river walk would be nicer, it was more like a dirty canal and ended in odd places at the street above with no signage of how to continue on below.

just got back from weekend stay with - children. Excellent hotel- very nicely appointed and the room was enormous- was a total surprise to find something like that in Manhattan. One very large bedroom and bathroom- with separate bath and shower- and then a very large lounge with decent sofa bed for the children. Nice touch of a kids welcome pack.
Location was superb easy to walk to Rock, Central Park, lots of shops.
Staff helpful. Had dessert and drinks in the Fireside on Friday night- even though a fairly """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""grown up"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" ambience we were able to find a great, comfy alcove with sofas, out of the way, where our - and - year old happily toasted marshmallows over a little dish of charcoal, while we had cocktails.
Just fab.

I had a wonderfull stay at the Kensington with my friends for a couple of days. The staff is helpfull, the rooms are great, the beds are very nice and the location is great! It's just next to Union Square which is the centre of the city.
Great Hotel! Close to everything you will possibly need......fun bar in the hotel lounge!

The hotel itself was very nice, and the service was excellent, but the value wasn't all there. The rooms were smaller than expected for an American hotel, and was pricier than warranted. The location itself was very good, centrally located in Boston.
Leave your car parked and walk or take transit. Boston is a driver's nightmare. The hotel has great valet parking.

A good value in Union Square. Great location. Rooms are very small but decent. We live nearby on the Peninsula and come stay at this hotel for a weekend getaway. Cookies and fruit in the lobby is a nice touch.
Book early. This place fills up fast.

Much more of a business hotel, but it worked perfectly for my first trip to San Francisco. It's right in the middle of Union Square, which is close to Chinatown, North Beach, and is walkable to Fisherman's Wharf. The rooms are small, but the beds are nice. If you don't plan on spending much time in the hotel, but want a central and clean location, this is a good choice. The staff were very accommodating as well with early check-in and late check-out.

Always a comfortable stay, and I travel to Indianapolis every week coming from NYC. Anthony at the front desk is the best! The breakfast in the executive club lounge is an excellent spread, and the attendant is very friendly and always ready for a nice chat. Heavenly beds are always comfortable. Only recommendation I have is more accessible electrical outlets near the bed (for iPhone chargers, laptop...etc). Overall, I would recommend the Westin Indianapolis.

Took advantage of their stay - nights and get one night free program. The staff at the hotel was very helpful and friendly. The location was great for going to plays near Times Square and good shopping on -th avenue. We didn't try the dining facilities. Very comfortable bed and we didn't hear the typical New York street noises at night or early in the morning--a good plus.

being located in the heart of Fells Point Baltimore is the best thing the hotel has going for it. The rooms are clean and the beds comfortable, but the hotel could use some repair and the repairs that have been done seem cobbled together. They will give you a gift certificate for the hotel restaurant, it's a total rip off because the food is way overpriced. They also charged the total cost of the room to the credit card the night before we checked out. That was odd, normally you don't pay until checkout. That was very tacky. Anyway, I found this hotel to be over priced...also if your room is on the front of the hotel you will be kept up late at night with the noise of the party goers coming out of three nearby bars.

Wife and I just stayed at AllertonHotel Chicago on dec--, ----. The room was a special groupon rate and it was a good value for location. The room was a superior suite and it was plenty big for such a older classic Chicago hotel. The building is old and shows signs of wear . Carpets could use a good cleaning or replace. The service was adequate. Nothing to write home about. We stayed at the Hard Rock last year and were much more satisfied. But in the end I would stay again just for location.

My Husband and I stayed at the Riverwalk Vista when we were in town for the Eric Clapton concert. I loved the location...right on the Riverwalk and directly across from the RiverCenter mall. The rooms were extremely clean and the linens and towels were above par. The staff was very friendly and helpful. We also enjoyed checking out all the historical photos they had in the common areas. The only down side was the traffic noise at night. The hotel is located on a very busy corner and the noise was quite noticeable at night. However, we were very tired and it didn't keep us awake long. 
One other note regarding our trip to San Antonio, if you plan on taking a taxi to a concert at the AT&T center, make sure you pay the taxi driver to come back to get you. After the show there were at least --- people lined up for taxis and not a taxi in sight. It was at least -- minutes to an hour after the show ended before taxis started arriving. It wasn't a pretty sight!

Have recently enjoyed a - night break at the Omni Parker Boston. We were lucky to have had a corner room which was actually quite spacious for a standard dobule room and the bed well..!! you had to take a running jump at to get in, it was very comfy and cosy with lovely quality linen. The bathroom was a little tired, however it was very clean. 
The bars in the Omni were quite expensive and the food was perhaps above average. 
The highlight of our stay was the great location for the Whale Watching trip (spectacular) most certainly not to be missed. So very sad though that due to the pollution caused of us humans that they are in danger! 
We also took the ferry from the harbour to Provincetown which is so very beautiful with it's clapboard houses and quality ecclectic shops.. Would loved to have had our stay there and it's much cheaper, still the Omni is lovely and found the staff very willing and well mannered.

Staff was unhelpful and rude. I will never stay here again. I am a single female traveler and wanted some assistance getting to my business meetings. They did not give me any assistance or directions. I was frustrated and checked out. Don't bother coming here. Stayed at another hotel and was MUCH happier!!

There is a fabulous view of the capital at night from the street in front of the hotel, very easy to get around the Capital area from here. The lobby is small and crowded most of the time, only place for free wifi! The driveway in front is also crowded but the valet and bellmen do a great job of unloading and getting things moving. The front desk staff were pleasant and helpful, you don't feel rushed. Unlike the concierge who could not be bothered to give his attention to get good advice or recommendations. I know they get tired of answering the same questions all the time but that is the job! Often walked away from the desk with guest standing there. The room was clean spacious and nicely decorated in a modern tone. (no pen or paper though). The street outside is busy and there is a hospital in the area as the ambulances,with sirens, were pretty constant day or night. I would stay again because of the local. Oh more thing $--.-- Vodka tonics!! Went next door to the liquor store instead.

Came to this hotel for a conference. Although the hotel was clean and John, the parking valet was super nice and VERY helpful, we really weren't happy with the hotel.
For the prices they charge, they could add a few more simple things that the lower priced hotels include in their room rate.
Things like free WIFI would be helpful - instead of charging $--.-- a DAY !! I can get free WIFI at the McDonald's or the bar down the street for heaven's sake !!
No fridge in room - would be helpful to keep drinks cold.
Poor choice of television stations. Couldn't watch the hockey game in my room. I could watch it in the bar in the hotel, but not in my room ?? 
Maid service on the first day - found my sample size shampoos and soaps lying on the floor by my door - the bathroom is - feet away - but they were lying on the floor in my room ??
Oh - and don't forget the parking situation. Valet parking - you can't park your own car - they charge you $-- a day to have parking on the premises !! 
If it wasn't for the conference, I would not stay here and will never stay here again !
Get better value at MUCH less expensive hotels !!

I love to stay at the Hotel Monaco when I am in Chicago, but when SniqueAway had a special on the Hotel Burnham I jumped on it for our girls week out, since it is another Kimpton hotel I figured the hotel standard would be the same for this property. I was wrong. That's not to say it was a bad hotel, just not actually a four star property.
The plus side is that the building is in a wonderful location and has a fun history. The architectural detail has been well preserved through the whole building which is beautiful. And the hotel is very clean and tidy. The staff was friendly and outgoing but we had to ask at least - times over a day and a half to get the gold fish for our rooms, each time being told they would get one to me right away. Since the fish is something that is offered at all Kimptons I was a little surprised, when I asked the last time I was told that the hotel was completely booked and the fish were all being aerated before they were sent off to new rooms, I was fine with that answer, just wish someone had said that up front instead of telling me they would get me a fish. The next problem was that I did not receive my Kimpton In Touch welcome gift that I am supposed to receive as a member, its not that big of a deal, its usually a breakfast or cookies, but there was nothing. The second day in my friends asked the maid for extra towels and she only left them the one time, even though they clearly needed them each day. We also found that when we needed a larger piece of paper the folder that is supposed to have stationary and one wrinkled blank sheet and one envelope only, good thing we were not writting home. I left the folder out for the maid so she would see it and replenish it, but instead she just put back the wrinkled sheet and put the folder back in the drawer. Despite the fact that the web site says they offer turn down service upon request there actually is no turn down service. I put in a request and was told at the front desk that they don't offer that. The door man was always nice and we got to know him a little, but as nice as he was he also spent quite a bit of time on his phone. There is no Concierge either which is something I was used to with the Monaco, there is however a desk that says concierge that is stocked with some brochures on the area. I am glad we stayed here and got to see the property, but in the future I will be going back to the Monaco for the service I am used to from Kimpton. This hotel is in a great area, close to the park and the Art Institute, but do not pay the full price for a room!

For a short break in Manhattan you really can't go wrong with this hotel, short walk to all the subway stations, a view of the Empire State Building from the roof terrace and Macy's at the end of the block.
The room was modern and clean, we were at the back of the hotel and it was really quiet at night. We had - queen beds and the hotel have thought of so many little extras, umbrellas in the wardrobe, iron and ironing board, free WIFI and breakfast included. The breakfast is self service but sufficent and the additional extra of complimentary tea and coffee throughout the day is a wonderful welcome on your return.
Matthew, the doorman was an absolute gem, so helpful and full of information. The Irish bar-restaurant opposite the hotel had a great menu and reasonably priced. Definitely worth staying at the Metro, would recommend.

I would not recommend this hotel for anyone who is looking for a clean, comfortable place to stay. When we got there, the girl from the front desk was outside smoking and talking on her cell phone. We had some trouble checking in ( that was not the hotels fault though) and had to wait almost a half hour to be able to check in. We left to go get something to eat while we waited and when we got back, the girl was outside smoking and talking on her cell again. 
When we got up to the room, the air condition was not on and it was super hot in the room. The beds were rock hard. My friend tried to bounce on them and they barely even moved. There was what looked like a small blood stain on the bed sheet. After about four hours, the room was still really hot. The air condition was obviously not working right. I would like to point out though that when I woke up the next morning the room was freezing. So at one point during the night it seemed the air conditioning actually kicked in and started working. The room was overall clean though. There were a couple places that it seemed the workers were just too lazy to clean. For example, it looked like there was either a chocolate stain or brown nail polish on the heater. 
I had to run out to the car at one point and again the girl from the front desk was outside smoking and talking on her cell phone, while inside there was someone sitting in the lobby waiting for help. I just wouldn't recommend staying in this hotel, especially for more than one day. I have stayed in cheaper hotels that were more comfortable than this.

I made a reservation for - nights, hoping to connect with someone to stay with instead and cancel my second night. After I heard from her that I could stay, I called the Rodeway Inn, (around - PM Friday) asking to cancel for Saturday, if it wasn't too late to do so. She assured me it was fine and would make sure that my credit card wasn't charged. Then, when I went to check out on Saturday (after a terrible shower btw) I was told that the employee had made a mistake and I couldn't cancel. I was shocked that they would go back on what they said after I had made other plans. I spoke to the manager-co-owner Monica, who told me that employee was misinformed and had since been fired. I spoke with her for -- minutes, begging for my $-- on the grounds that I had been told I could cancel, no one ever contacted me to tell me otherwise until I checked out, and she needed to take responsibility for what her employee had told me. She was totally unsympathetic and refused to give me my money, even though at this point I couldn't even stay there that night because I had already made plans. I am a grad student who auditioned at the music school there and can barely afford groceries, much less an unfair charge for an overpriced room I couldn't even stay in. Avoid the Rodeway!

We stayed here for the Boston Marathon. The location was very convenient for walking to the bus pick up to Hopkinton and also not too bad to walk home from the finish line. With the expo at the Seaport trade center, it was a convenient walk there too. The rooms are a bit small, so with all of our running gear and cooler (we drove), it was a bit tight. That's the only drawback. The staff was friendly and helpful and everything else about the room was just fine. The best part? Please read this before you consider staying at the Boston Park Plaza Hotel. It takes a lot for me to sit down and spend time writing reviews, but this hotel was so horrendous that I actually took three hours out of my schedule to write this and create an account here so that I could hopefully save one person from booking a room at this joke of an historical hotel. 
My boyfriend had a meeting he had to attend in Boston, and had never stayed at this establishment. Not thinking to read the reviews, he booked the hotel for - nights. A little background about us: I am what I would consider an unconventional student. I attend a very prestigious school, and during my time off, I like to ‘road trip’ around the country, and do some storm chasing, which, more often than not, leads me into having to stay at roadside hotels and motels, from chains big and small. I’ve stayed in every type of establishment imaginable, from small mom and pop motels and Motel -’s, to midgrade Hilton Garden Inns and Hampton Inns, all the way to five star hotels such as select Hyatt and Hilton-branded properties. My boyfriend is long finished with his education, and has traveled all over the world and also has quite a bit of experience with hotels. I think that we can both honestly say that this was, hands down, one of the worst, most tacky hotels we’ve ever encountered, and definitely a poor value for the price. 
This hotel is sold as an “historic, ----’s era hotel”, and so of course, you’re expecting the charm of the ----’s days of excess combined with modern amenities. That is not the case. It’s as if this hotel strives to save as much money as possible while charging as much as possible to its customers. More on this below.
My boyfriend and I arrived and checked into our room. It was a standard double room, with two beds (probably tmi but he moves around too much while he’s asleep, so we often end up sleeping in separate beds). The first thing we noticed is that the ----’s era door to the room would not close all of the way, and he literally had to run into it to get it to close. The next thing we noticed was the bathrooms. The toilets and tile appear to be original (there is no toilet tank, just a handle and a seat). The bathtubs are original but have had a recast put over them, so that the hotel could forego the cost of replacement, giving the bathrooms that ‘mobile home’-esque quality that we all seek in these fine establishments. The next thing we noticed was that the wallpaper was peeling off next to the tub, and that the border tile was coming off as well. Next to the tub was an old radiator, and the dial had been replaced with a more modern thermostat. The wire leading from the thermostat to the radiator had been partially caulked into the edge between the shower tile and the thermostat, leaving about six inches of it exposed. Right on the edge of the bathtub. Let me explain two reasons why this is wrong. Depending on how the thermostat works, the wire either carries an electrical current, or is used more or less as a mobile ‘pull’ to adjust the temperature settings in the radiator (i.e., turning the dial one way or another tightens or loosens the wire, thereby changing the temperature of the radiator). So if this wire actually carries an electrical current, and is right on the edge of a bathtub… obvious electrocution hazard. If this wire is used simply as a mechanical feature, well, half of it was caulked into the edge, leaving it immobilized and unable to properly function. Please correct me if I’m wrong with these assumptions. 
Moving on, I filled the tub, and apparently the secondary drain wasn’t working, which led to the entire floor in the bathroom flooding with about a quarter inch of water. Nice for me, because my bag of clothing was on that floor, so now I would have to launder every piece of clothing I had.
The bathroom sinks are pedestal sinks (as was common in the ----’s), but were not original. There was virtually no counter space to set your toiletries, aside from a small area underneath the mirror.
The toiletries provided by this hotel are from a ‘concept brand’ (i.e., more or less an off- brand in its marketing test phase) and really are not any good. For the price we were paying for the room, we were expecting to have somewhat recognizable brands; however, I brought my own toiletries so this was not a huge issue.
The next thing we noticed was the furniture. Again, one of the hotel’s selling points is that it is an historical, ----’s era hotel. I understand that the furniture would probably not be original, but I was hoping at least that it would be somewhat of an imitation of ----’s styled furniture. It was not. All of the furniture is this somewhat hideous, somewhat mismatched particle board disasterpiece, and none of it even closely resembles pre-depression styles. 
The overall layout of the room was unique, but it had its own problems as well. Trim and crown molding was coming off of the wall (and in some places, was entirely absent), and there were large chunks of paint cracking and peeling off of the wall… Everywhere. The ceiling was also cracking. The walls were paper-thin (room service was ordered in the room next door, and we both kept checking our door because we thought we had heard a knock on ours), so we didn’t sleep well at all. The wall art consisted of framed photographs (something I’m sure wasn’t the decorating norm for the ----’s), probably because it’s cheaper to reproduce and frame photographs than to commission an artist to produce reproductions and place them in the rooms.
Housekeeping wasn’t ‘terrible’, but you can’t really fairly judge the housekeeping when the hotel room you’re paying a premium for in Boston would be better situated in a slum in Beirut. It’s kind of like finding the decomposing corpse of a prostitute in the forest, and complaining about how its eyeshadow looked. Honestly can’t think of a better analogy. We found a pretzel underneath the set of dressers upon which the television was situated. There was hair in the bathtub and the shower. 
And the fees with this hotel, dear God the fees. They will charge you for ANYTHING and EVERYTHING. Want a minifridge? Expect to pay $-- for this, and expect it to not be delivered for over an hour, and expect the deliveryman to BEAT DOWN YOUR DOOR to get you to take it (don’t worry though, the minifridge had plenty of its own beatings from the looks of it). Want internet service? $--.-- per device, per day. Have a computer and a phone you want to use wifi on? Doesn’t matter. $--.-- each. As an aside, don’t think about using your cell phone here, either- you will NOT get service, and you will have to use the room’s phone to make calls. Want to make a call? That will be $-.-- for each call, even toll-free calls, plus a premium for any minutes over -- minutes. Want to print something downstairs in their complimentary business center? That will be an additional charge. Want to bring home a gift to the wife? How about a gift set consisting of a full-size bottle each of our off-brand shampoo and conditioner for $-- (they *actually* advertise this in the room… t.a.c.k.y.)? I appreciate how this hotel tries to bill itself as a high-class establishment, but then has the audacity to attempt to sell you full-size bottles of its off-brand shampoo and conditioner for $--.--. 
Want to relax while you’re here and catch up on some TV? Don’t expect to have many of the advertised premium channels. No channels after --, even though they advertise somewhere around --. 
Want to actually be productive while you’re here? Don’t. I guess this hotel figures that since they didn’t have internet and fully functioning phone service in the ----’s, there’s no need to offer it now. That’s about the only thing this hotel keeps as a tribute to that era – obsolete technology. The internet costs extra and was of poor quality. If you want to make calls, that’ll be an additional charge, and don’t expect the phones to work either. The cordless phone was absolutely nonfunctioning, and the corded phone had a somewhat busted earpiece, so that I had to continuously ask the other party to repeat themselves. 
Overall, this establishment is pretty run-down, and will probably never realize its potential. Don’t let the appearance of the lobby mislead you- the rooms are disastrous and in need of true rehabilitation. I felt embarrassed for the original proprietors of this hotel after I stayed here. I would be willing to stay again, only if the hotel was sold to new owners and actually, legitimately restored. Otherwise, I wouldn’t stay here if I was paid to. I’d give this hotel negative stars, but you have to give at least one.

My husband and I came to the Days Hotel as recommended by my brother and sister in law who travel to San Diego often and use this facility. We came to enjoy - days of vacation time after a busy seminar in Los Angeles.

Overall, this hotel is quite old even though it boasts itself as being """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""the best Days hotel in San Diego"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which is probably untrue. The vegetarian entree for our big dinner was exceptionally good (which is surprising because I usually get a nasty bowl of pasta and veggies for a veg entree) and breakfast was nice also. As for the lobby, it was actually quite small and not over the top, but it served its purpose. I really enjoyed the location of the hotel. It is close to Georgetown and definitely within walking distance of the attractions. The area around the hotel is very business oriented, so lots of restaurants, but not bars, clubs etc.
I also heard Eric Ripert's restaurant downstair was top-notch, but didn't get there.
All in all, a very enjoyable stay (although I did not have to pay for the room and I probably would not pay the regular rate to stay here again,)
