I stayed at Amber Inn this summer with my husband, brother-in-law, and mother-in-law. When I made a few phone calls inquiring about rooms and eventually making a reservation, the staff was helpful, but I couldn't get all the information from just one person. I believe I have it figured out now though: they have two different kinds of rooms: hotel and motel. We stayed in the motel rooms (door opens to the parking lot), and they were pretty dingy. They say the hotel rooms are more spacious. Our rooms were good enough to stay in for a couple nights, but there were visible cobwebs all over the ceilings, and in general it felt very unkempt. 
Some people have commented on the area of town being """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""scary."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I don't think it was such a bad part of town, but if you come from a fairly homogeneous, upper-middle class neighborhood, this area of town might make you a little uncomfortable. Just remember, diversity doesn't mean dangerous. It certainly isn't located in a glamorous part of Chicago though. But the price is just right for where you're staying; anywhere else is going to cost you many times more. 
A great advantage is that the train is located just two blocks away. 
One last thing they could improve would be the knowledge of the staff. I asked about recommendations for restaurants, for example, and no one had an answer except for their own restaurant on the premises. It wasn't very helpful from a tourist's perspective.
Final verdict: stay here (try the hotel room) if you care more about the economical value of it and don't mind not having a fancy place to sleep, but be prepared that the location is not like the nicest parts of Chicago.

Aside from those damn doors, this would have been a four- or five-star review. But, as nice as everything else was, a hotel isn't a hotel if you can't sleep in it.

Next time any of you stay in a large Hotel just for fun time how long it takes from closing your door, traveling down a corridor, waiting for a lift, sharing it , making small talk, making your way to breakfast room, waiting for seat allocation.... get the picture?

The staff mind their own business until approached and then were most courteous and helpful. Special mention for Kevin, Cornelius and Mark.

Then poor Cornelius brought down our five suitcases and bags to rest room and subsequently to taxi and when I tipped him he insisted I take back half nor did he take no for an answer.
Good luck to the Mid Town; Excellent value for its location unless you're called Cleopatra.
Previously stayed in Hyatt Regency Cambridge.

There is nothing about this hotel that makes it an absolute standout, but for the money--we paid ---, all in--you would be hard pressed to find a better option.

We stayed at the MarQueen for five days in March '-- on a tourist trip to Seattle - we had every intention of hitting all the tourist sites, having traveled to Seattle on business several times before. The MarQueen's location is PERFECT for anything at Seattle Center - Space Needle, EMP, Sci Fi Museum, Children's Museum, the theaters (Intiman, Seattle Rep), McCaw Hall, and Key Arena. It's a charming neighborhood with good restaurants around (some great, some not so good, so the selection does wear thin after a few days).
The rooms are well appointed - having a kitchen is GREAT. We ate in the room often rather than going out and Larry's Market right near by made for some good, fresh meals.
The staff is the most friendly and helpful I've seen in awhile. Very knowledgeable and friendly without being fake. Quick with a recommendation or anything you need. Cannot say enough good things about the staff. Really made the stay worthwhile. The weekend staff, however, was not as friendly and helpful.
The drawbacks -- the bed was THE most uncomfortable we've ever slept in and the pillows were flat and hard. It does get loud if there's an event at Key Arena or some of the bars across the street, especially on the weekend; avoid a room on the first floor facing the street at all costs. If you don't like stairs, avoid a room on the third floor, too. There is no elevator, and after walking around all day that gets tiring. However, on a clear day the views from a third floor room facing the street are gorgeous.
You are not close enough to downtown - Pike Place or the waterfront. We did walk it a couple of times and it isn't terrible, but not advisable. We did use the shuttle several times, which is terrific, but if it's not available you're stuck. You can schedule from the hotel in advance, but you can't schedule a pick up from down town in advance, so you have to take your chances. The weekend staff was not at all helpful in that regard and kept recommending we take a bus. We got back to the hotel and found the shuttle available. The shuttle is a really nice addition, though, and does make getting around easier - if you're able to schedule it.
All in all, it's a very nice place to stay. It is showing its age a little bit, but it is charming and much better than a chain motel with bland rooms and decor. Would definitely recommend the MarQueen and would stay there again.

I had a corner King room, it had two tvs, lots of closet space and a very nice bathroom. Great night sleep. The leased out restaurant in the lobby is excellent as is the bar , The Japanese restaurant in the hotel has the conveyer style sushi delivery system, great food and if you are in a rush it is great also.

An amazing bed combined with a magnificent decor, great customer service, perfect location makes the Eliot one of my preferred hotels. I had one little problem as I was charged for something I did not consume, but they took care of it and adjusted my check.

The ONLY thing I could think of that I didn't like (and it's not the hotel's fault) is that --th street could be noisy at ANY time of night.....I happened to treat the noise as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""typical NYC sounds"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and did not have any problems sleeping.
The bed and shower were out of this world, stumptown coffee downstairs, great bar, this place is worth every penny.

I really enjoyed my recent stay at the Hyatt Regency Baltimore. I am a loyal Marriott customer and I got a great deal for this hotel on Expedia so I gave it a shot. Lets just say I booked my next stay in DC with a Hyatt as well! I arrived late and check in was easy. The Front desk clerk, Valet and Doormen were very nice. I arrived in my room and it was clean and nice, the only issue I saw was a spot on the bench which of course I avoided like the plague. Otherwise the room was very nice. A beautiful view of the Harbor with floor to ceiling windows. There were extra pillows which I requested which was a nice attention to detail. I had to hurry and get to the bar-restaurant before it closed at midnight as I my flight into Baltimore was very late. Even though it was -- minutes to close the wonderful bartender not only let me order food but stay and eat it while she was closing up. Thank you Debbie! Then I witnessed her serve another guest who showed up five minutes after closing. She even chatted with us both. This is great service at midnight! The housekeeper Chantay was very friendly and did a wonderful job refreshing my room while I was out at the Inner Harbor. She even wrote me a sweet note thanking me for the tip. The bed was very comfortable and the shower was nice.
There were only two issues I dealt with while I was there... first one is a preference, I like a hotel hairdryer attached to the wall for convenience and cleanliness. The other issue was that I put one of the large bottles of water in the fridge that was on the table and a flyer was left instructing me not to place things in the fridge. I called down to get a fridge so I could have my $- bottle of water cold but they never brought me one even though they said they would. Neither issues were a big deal just little things that I would fix if I were the manager. There should be room left in the fridge for a guests bottle of water or an additional guest fridge. If I am willing to pay $- for your bottle of water I should be able to keep it cold if I would like.
I would definitely stay there again. Baltimore is a great place to visit with so many fun things to do and the Hyatt Regency Baltimore is in a perfect location to see them all!

This hotel is on a quiet residential street a block from Dupont Circle, so shopping and fine dining are steps away, but the immediate area is peaceful. We didn't use the restaurants or children's pools, so we have no review of those. The staff that we met was courteous and pleasant. If we had one negative complaint, it is that a cigarette butt (not ours), was on a chair on our private balcony the entire time. That's it. Otherwise, it was a nice stay.

I would recommend Flemings Steakhouse for an excellent dinner. It is a few miles south of the resort but well worth the drive.

The spa was wonderful-I had a massage with Bonnie and she was excellent. I used the health club and also walked some of the trails. 
We really enjoyed our stay at the Arizona Grand despite the noise. We did tell management and they were very open to our suggestions. Our service was first class and the grounds were beautiful. We will return next year.

You can jump on the cable car across the street and head straight to Fisherman's Wharf or head down two blocks to Market street and pick up any-all city transportation. Perfect!

Was in town for a college bowl game and had two rooms on the club level. Found the staff to be very nice, public areas were clean and in good condition (although the restaurant was closed with a sign up saying “Closed due to low occupancy”…even if that is the reason do they want to advertise the fact?). Both rooms were very clean, kudos to the housekeepers, however there were multiple maintenance issues in both rooms and a few design flaws that should never have been allowed in the first place. 
Whatever company did their last renovation should never be used again. There were a large number of paint spots on the wallpaper from when they painted the ceilings, the wallpaper was peeling off in (no joke) -- places in one room alone, and worst of all when they sprayed the texture on the ceiling it got all over one of the sprinkler heads (see picture) and I doubt it would even work now. In addition the nightstand drawer was broken in one room, the safe was broken in another room, one room only had one robe (which I don’t care about but we better not be charged for taking one as there should have been two), and there was a lot of water damage on the ceiling of one of the bathrooms…which is concerning considering we were on the top floor.
In terms of the design flaws there were two very nice and stylish lamps on each nightstand which conveniently had electrical plugs built into them. Many hotels are doing this now as they realize most travelers use their phones as alarms and keep them plugged in at night. Only one issue with the lamps at THIS hotel…the outlets turn off then you turn the lamp off! This was discovered of course the following morning when both my wife and I had dead phones and was confirmed by a number of other guests at the breakfast that morning that were in the same boat. I can only immagine the number of people that miss meetings because their phones died and their alarms didn't go off. The coffee maker was placed on a wheeled table which was a great idea as the rooms are quite large and it allows the freedom to set it up wherever you would like. Unfortunately they plugged it into an outlet located behind a huge bureau with a TV on top and beyond reach so you can’t actually move the table! Lastly there was a pole lamp in one corner behind a stuffed chair which is great for reading however there are no outlets in that corner so they used an eight foot extension cord running along the floor to plug it in. Talk about a trip hazard!
Overall not a bad hotel but the maintenance work was so shoddy it really overshadowed everything else that was positive and was certainly not something befitting of the Hilton brand.
This hotel-hostel is a great place to stay on the upper west side convenient for everything. bit of chaos at reception at all times but aint no thang. Dino Carlucci

On the other hand, I did receive an e-mail during my stay from a manager asking if everything was up to my expectations and if I had any issues. I've never had a hotel do that and that was a nice touch! In short, if you are able to stay at this hotel for less than $---, worth the price; otherwise, look elsewhere.

The hotel has a really cool urban vibe that sits really comfortably with the historic nature of the property. The staff was always professional and friendly. The restaurant and lounge are simply stunning. Comfortable, funky and expensive feeling. Very easy to find a little area with a couch and a couple of chairs to hang out and people watch or meet up with friends. The charges for the room, parking, internet, etc are all acceptable for a property of this caliber. The central downtown location with the ease of getting around from here, mixed with the historic nature of the property and the top shelf modern amenities makes for an incredibly cool and understated experience.

Some tips: If you are going to use the subway and buses get a daily fun pass or - day metro card. Caruso's pizza place by Fulton and Broadway was really good and inexpensive. There are Chipotle (the one across from our hotel gave my daughter and I bathroom problems-we had the chicken burrito). But everything else there was reasonable. Check out American Eagle at times sq. They have a deal: if you purchase something, you get your pic on the jumbotron...it's really something (she also has A.E. times sq. top and others that you can't purchase anywhere else...that is cool for a -- year old : ). I think that was the best part of her trip even though she loved everything else. Before we left I borrowed from the library & read NYC for dummies and Eyewitness Travel NYC and Eyewitness Travel top -- NYC. I also borrowed a travel nyc dvd. They are all good books to read. They eyewitness ones have a lot of pics (the top -- doesn't have as many pics, but you can look them up on the internet). We also took Amtrak to nyc out of Clev. We used the subway as late as -:-- a.m. and no problems- There is an S subway train that goes into Times Square...Take it! We were waiting at the Concierge desk for just a few minutes behind a couple receiving directions, when the Concierge leaned over and said to us very rudely: """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I'm finishing with this group and then I have to go, can you see if the front desk can help you?"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I told her the line at the front desk was long and she seemingly rolled her eyes and said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I'll be right with you"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I stood there for a minute baffled that she would end her shift without helping us when Marriott is so big on customer service, and also why we would want to check with the front desk when the Concierge is supposed to be the knowledgable one in the hotel about this. A few minutes later, she leaned over again asking us what we needed. I told her and she rolled her eyes and sighed and said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""well there's eight restaurants on Lake Union where you can see fireworks"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I stopped her right there. I did not ask for restaurant recommendations and I certainly wasn't going to take quick recommendations to get rid of me while she was still helping the first people. She was useless. I went outside and asked the bellman who was about -- years old. Though he did not know much in regards to what I was asking, he was much more pleasant and helpful. At check-out, the front desk clerk gave us great directions to the airport avoiding the parade route, which contradicted the bellman's directions from the previous night which actually crossed the parade route. I was disgusted with this Concierge experience and thought that since this Lions club convention was staying there, perhaps they should have been more well staffed and prepared for questions like this. 
We did not get to use the pool but it was very nice with both indoor and outdoor features, and the workout room was a great size with nice offerings.
Regardless of my one bad experience, I would choose to stay here again if the price was right because of the location, amenities and decor.

Hotel, rooms and location was fine. Toward the back of the parking lot they have squeezed every inch of parking space so that most mid-size cars cannot easily fit. What happens is that people start taking two spaces and riding over the lines and it creates a situation where people park right on top of others. Lighten up Hyatt and create a few less spaces. $--.-- extra dollars a night and cramed in like fish in a pan makes you look alittle desperate and create some angry parkers. Thanks for the paint chips numb nuts.
Also, I like my staff with a little less San Diego attitude. The gay waiter and the Red Marlin was great but most of the staff was either hung over or pissy.
All in all we had a good time.

this hotel provides studio-like room, with full kitchen, complete with utensils, pots and pans. it is located on a quiet street but there are ample restaurants-pharmacy-grocery stores within - min driving. staff is friendly and helpful, though i think they need more than - person to tend the front desk.
room size is okay. kitchen is small but serviceable. there is a medium sized fridge, electric stove, sink, microwave, coffee maker and kitchen equipment (pot, pan, plates, cutting board even washing clothes). iron and ironing board is also provided. bed is comfortable. the overall facilities are not new, but well kept. the only complain that i have is there is no hairdryer provided and that i have to pay for internet (fortunately it's just one time fee for the duration of your stay).
this hotel definitely good value!

The W is a very nice, chic hotel. I enjoyed my three night stay there very much. I was there with three girlfriends in their cozy room (squeezing four people into this room is not recommended...three should be fine). The room was really nicely decorated and comfortable. Got the room for a steal on Priceline ($----night plus taxes and fees). Having gone to NYC three times this year, this hotel was the best by far (other two times we stayed at the Radisson and the Pod). The doormen were always helpful in hailing cabs and overall it's a gorgeous, modern hotel in a great location.

I made a list of a few pros and cons about this hotel:
Pro#-: Location, location, location. 
The hotel's location can't be beat for games or events at Fenway Park. You literally walk out of the hotel, walk half a block, turn the corner, walk another half block, and there's the Gate B entrance to Fenway Park. It's also convenient for meeting up with a particular trolley tour that I took that stops in front of Fenway Park and lets you board at any stop. My hotel room on the second floor (top floor) had a peek-a-boo view of Fenway Park and faced out onto the hotel courtyard where there was an outdoor swimming pool.
Pro#-: Great service. 
First example- I had a package delivered to the hotel. I thought it was going to be delivered during my stay at the hotel, but the package arrived a few days prior to my arrival. I called the hotel and was delighted when the lady at the desk said they would hold it until I arrived, no problem. Sure enough, when I checked in, they had it ready for me. 
Second example- I checked out early in the morning and was waiting in the lobby for an airport shuttle. When I had been waiting a while, the two men on duty offered to call the shuttle for me. When they couldn't get ahold of the shuttle, they offered to call me a taxi. The taxi pulled up a minute later. 
Third example- The cleaning service restocked the toiletries. (I stayed multiple nights.) It's something I took for granted until I stayed in a hotel that didn't!
Con#-: No breakfast offered in the hotel. 
In the Fenway Park neighborhood, there are lots of bars and lunch-dinner restaurants but no coffee shops or other places that serve breakfast (that I could find). I would've even paid for breakfast if the hotel had offered it. (The restaurant inside the hotel is Hong Kong Cafe, a Chinese restaurant that is open for lunch and dinner.) It looked like there used to be a McDonalds across the street from the hotel but it was no longer in business.
Con#-: Older hotel
Because this is an older hotel, there were a few problems. I couldn't adjust the temperature in my room. It was freezing cold inside the room the first two nights when it was cold outside, and stuffy when it was warmer outside on my last night. Along with that, there was no way to turn the fan on in the bathroom. 
Also, the room smelled faintly of cigarette smoke. The hotel is now ---% non-smoking, but until they replace the carpets, freshen up the paint inside the room, etc, it will always smell. To be fair, they are in the process of refurbishing the hotel. They were painting the halls when I was there.
I didn't have any trouble sleeping because of noise. Sure, I could hear people in the hall, faucets, the soundcheck at the concert across the street at Fenway Park. But maybe I am more used to noise than others since I live in an apartment building.
All in all, I would definitely recommend this hotel if you are looking for a hotel with great service very close to Fenway Park.

A wonderful hotel.great location but traffic is terrible.I am a diamond member used my awards points for - rooms stayed executive level beautiful view looking out over texas.Breakfast buffet $---- but worth it.Bring light bulbs rooms need better lighting,Valet parking $--.-- but you can get your car in minutes.Concierge level nice but closed friday night and monday morning ask for Miss Jackie she has lots of local gossip.Would definitely stay there again

I was very pleased with my stay. The front desk staff and shuttle drivers-bellman were wonderful. At tentative, pleasant and prompt even with the hotel being very busy. My room was clean and everything was in working order. The complimentary bottle of water and the size and quality of the toiletries were a nice touch. The on-site restaurant was excellent. The food was fresh and served hot and the wait staff was top notch. I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

This is supposed to be a grande luxe establishment, but the hallway between the elevator and our room reeked of cleaning chemicals and smelled like the footbath at a public swimming pool. Modest hotel chains charge nothing for wi-fi these days, but this pricey outfit rips you off for a daily charge (the card on the desk says it's $-- a day, but it turns out to be $--). I called the manager to inquire about this curious business practice and she treated me as if I were some cheap rube who didn't appreciate the splendor of her establishment.
We were there for two nights. There are three elevators. One of them was permanently out of service the whole time. That doesn't seem so splendid to me. I don't mind paying top dollar but I expect top grade performance for it.

My sister and I stayed at RRInn in November of ---- and again in May ----
We were very happy with our rooms. when we arrived in November we were upgraded to a King room as we were there for a weeks stay. That was very nice...we didn't ask for this. Also we joined their club and earned two nights free for our next trip. In May we returned for a three night stay. Paid for one night only. Our room was on the --th floor and was extremely clean during our visit. Bathroom, plenty hot water and lots of towels and etc. We had no problems at all. Breakfast was good. Have recommended RRInn to several friends. Will return...

I would strongly recommend against staying in this hotel. I have travelled a lot, and slept in all types of hostels, boarding houses, bed & breakfasts and hotels - this is the worst place I've ever had the misfortune to stay at. The lobby is completely open to the public (overfowing from people just out of Penn Station looking for a place to take a break), the staff is rude, check-in takes forever, you have to use pre-paid wifi in the lobby (the signal didn't make it to my -rd floor room). However the most unpleasant part of the stay has to do with the room itself. Windows can not be opened and haven't been washed in years, paint is chipped and peeling, rusty shower fixtures, the dark-brown carpet is scary, and there is a strange, musty, lingering smell that permeates everything. It's worth a visit downstairs to see the safety boxes - if I hadn't been travelling alone, I might have seen the humor in it all, but one look at the broken safe doors hanging on their hinges made me turn around, go back upstairs and hide my computer and passport in a drawer and hope for the best. The highlight of this horroric stay is a walk down the halls. The stained carpet and poor lighting are downright creepy (remember """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The Shining""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""?). There have got to be better places in the city for the money I paid. The location is the ONLY good thiing about it, however with the good subway system, what's the big deal about being right across the street from Penn Station?

I love staying here the night before we leave on a vacation. Pull up to the front give them the keys to your car if you do the park and fly option. Go in spend the night and check into delta right around the corner. Fast and easy. Then when you get back give them a call and your warm car is waiting when you get there. It cost alittle more but well worth it.

I stayed at the Hilton for a conference and experienced no major problems during my stay but would probably not stay here again during my next visit to New York. 
On the positive side, the location of the hotel is superb, the staff was forthcoming, and the room was excellent. 
However, probably due to the sheer size of this hotel, the place had quite an anonymous feel and the level of service provided was not what I would expect from a hotel in this category. My most important problems with this hotel during my stay were the following; 
-) The huge lobby was dirty with trash piling up around sofas and tables without these areas being cleaned. 
-) I had to wait way too long for elevators of which there are not enough. 
-) When it was raining outside, the hotel was not able to provide me with an umbrella, something, which has never happened to me before at a -*+ rated hotel. 
-) The wireless internet service is not only ridiculously expensive but also ridiculously slow.

Fairmont was an excellent choice. Staff very helpful, room was comfortable, clean and well appointed. Maintenance response to a small plumbing problem was quick and efficient.
Lounge prices a bit pricey, butrecommended overall.

When I got my credit card statement the month after my stay, I noticed an additional charge to my card. When I called, they said it was for a movie. 
I NEVER order hotel movies so I knew it wasn't mine.
When I called, they said they would remove the charge, but implied that it's not possible to be charged for a movie without ordering it. I completely understand this, but I didn't order it. Hearing this make me feel disrespected by the hotel after my visit, and now it's what I will remember most about their hotel.
If you stay here, pay attention to your credit card bill.

We required a hotel for an overnight stay while in transit to our destination. We booked this hotel on Hotwire not knowing the name until it was paid for. For a cost of $--.-- a night we weren't expecting much, however did not need much for a quick overnighter. However, we were very pleasantly surprised. When we arrived at the airport we called for the shuttle and within ----- minutes the free shuttle arrived. At the hotel our checkin was very speedy and we were given a small welcome package. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The restaurant onsite, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Great Eats"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was very good with excellent wait staff. The hotel has a pool and small gym which we didn't have time to use but it is there. They also offer a free shuttle to the mall and pick up was on time. Rooms were clean and well appointed if a bit small. In comparison, we paid $--- for a Holiday Inn in Nisku, Alberta when we were connecting and it wasn't even close to the level of service, friendliness and amenities as this Holiday Inn. We would definitely stay here again!

Booked a room for my relatives here last year. The receptionists were very nice and friendly. Room was clean with its own kitchen. Downstairs bar may have been a bit noisy, but this is NYC, after all haha.

WE LOVE THIS HOTEL! We are just wrapping up a - week stay. We are retired, travel full-time and visit Dallas often. The Residence Inn at Dallas Park Central has everything we are looking for. The Staff is quite good, especially Robert at the front desk...professional and helpful. Breakfast offerings provide something for everyone, fresh fruit, yogurt, waffles, eggs, bagels, muffins and more. Rooms are clean and quiet (especially at night,) comfortable beds, clean linens and nice pillows. Furnishings in the living area are great too...nice seating options, large flat panel TV, good TV programming, free Wi-Fi that is a breeze to access, comfortable desk and office chair if you need to work. Rate is a good value, especially with all the extras provided. We love staying here! As long as this locations keeps this level of cleanliness and staff, we'll be back!

I stayed here three nights for pleasure (followed by two nights in a different hotel for business) ... I would highly recommend this for someone who would like a stylish modern hotel with superior service in a convenient area (but it may be out of the way for someone who is looking for the Time Square-Broadway show type of experience).
Here is a summary
:
- Interesting check in experience; there is no front desk. It is done well and it is unique, as far as I know.
- All of the staff that I encountered was very helpful... they are doing a good job training them since every single person I encountered was quite young.
- Breakfast (complementary) was very nice.... self serve --- i usually pass by the hotel breakfast to go out to eat but in this case I ate granola and had fruit before going out to my more decadent breakfast --- but if I would have been more than content having my full breakfast at the hotel. (though some of the pastries appeared to be a little old) Btw, they had coffee (no espresso) but it was great for brewed coffee.
- Close to the subway. If you like exploring the city and are able to get around easily, it is conveniently located.
-Wonderfully designed rooms - modern. The bathrooms were a treat ---- if you are shy, don't worry, no one outside can view you from the bathroom windows even though there are no blinds. 
-One possible problem is that the rooms are fairly small (according to the layout I had one of the smaller rooms #----) --- Mine was a queen size room and with the two of us, there wasn't a lot of room to put our stuff. If I were there alone, however, there would have been plenty of space. I did not see any other rooms so this may not be an issue in a King size room.
- Quiet.... I did not hear any outside noise.

A big hotel near the airport with a regular shuttle bus. Check in was fast and efficient. Everyone is friendly and smiling. Great coffee maker and toiletries and everything was clean. But they forgot to remove a used ear bud left conspiciously on the table. Nice lounge and room overlooking the airport.The decor is old and the bathing shower switch was anti-logic. The ceiling is low and the big CRT TV hung around like a decor, much to my amusement. The lift cranks crazily up and down but I understand that an upgrading is underway. Some aircraft sounds still permeates into the hotel but is ok for me. The club lounge is so so and no free internet despite booking a Towers (club) room. They wanted $--.-- a day for that. Overall an ok hotel for its price but don't expect a sleek wait-on-you-hand-and-foot Asian style hotel.

Stayed here for one night going back home to the airport early AM. We were very pleased with our room, great king size bed, windows opened, wall TV and channel options terrific, easy walk to all downtown restaurants and short taxi ride to airport. Will stay again for a few nights next time and enjoy more of downtown San Diego. Great hotel with a reasonable rate!

I stayed for one night for $--.-- because of the AARP discount. The room was larger than many more expensive chains. The free breakfast was minimal. The room and environs were all clean and well appointed. Check-in and out were very quick and efficient. I would stay here again and recommend this hotel.

We just returned from a - night stay at The Surrey on the Upper East Side. It was a fabulous small hotel with great service. The rooms are in great shape and they are top notch with Duxiana beds and Pratesi linens. Unfortunately never ate at the hotel but I had a couple treatments at the Spa (loved Malika for nails). A bit pricey for sure but what quality hotel in NYC isn't......

Please, please, please do not stay here! I came home with scabies AND bedbug bites. I have attached pictures that show some of the bites. My body is covered in itchy bites. 
DO NOT GET FOOLED BY THEIR WEBSITE (like we did). I should have known to turn around and run for the front door when I saw that the front desk is a - metre by - metre room with one person behind fully protected bullet proof glass on the -nd floor. It looked nothing like their website depicts. A sign at the front desk says """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The hotel will not call the fire department in case of fire."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Are you serious? So if you are on the -rd or -th floor, you have to jump from the window because there is only one way out of the hotel. 
Now for the bugs. I have stayed in huts in -rd world countries with no running water or indoor plumbing and they are cleaner than the Mithila. Our bedsheets and pillow cases did not get changed for the first - days of our stay. We saw the same stains on the same spots after the -nd night. So we marked them with a pen to see if they were in fact not being changed. And sure enough, they were not! We had to ask for new bed sheets and pillow cases and change them ourselves. But that didn't help the bug bites. We actually checked out at --pm to get to the airport and chose to sleep on a bench at the airport (until -am) rather than stay the last night at the bug infested Mithila. 
We called the Mithila the same day we got home to inform them that we got bit by bugs and to evacuate anyone who may be staying in our room and spray it down first. Knowing what a shady place the Mithila is, I called them back - hours later and asked for the room we were staying in to see if they had in fact evacuated the room. Sure enough the front desk person put me through to the room and the poor people had not been evacuated. This was the first they had heard from anyone that the room had bugs. 
PAY THE EXTRA $-- PER NIGHT AND STAY SOMEWHERE ELSE!!!

Recently returned from four nights at the Casablanca and am looking forward to a return trip in the Fall.
Anything I could say would just be a reiteration of the reviews that have come before. All I can say is that I would heartily recommend this hotel to anyone that enjoys a European-type hotel experience.
Yes, the room was small, though accomodating enough. Bath, cleanliness, etc. all excellent. But, what really makes this hotel stand out is the staff, from the front desk, to the breakfast-bar workers to the housekeeping staff all were professional, courteous and (as in a five star hotel) always meet a request with a 'yes, that is possible'.
Thanks so much to all at the Casablana for making our trip truly a delight.

This is a lovely hotel, but I would not stay here again as a result of the rude and demeaning staff. The check-in agent was surly when we asked for a room away from the elevator (and it was a polite request). We called down twice with questions for staff members and both times were put on hold with nary a word of apology or concern for our time. Both times I was cut off in midsentance with one word, just 'hold'. 
When checking out, my husband discovered a billing error and brought it to the attention of the young man who spent five minutes arguing with my husband. He told us over and over that if it was on the bill it was correct. We finally asked for a manager, who was even less helpful. The manager insisted that we must have ordered $-- worth of room service if it was on the bill. We finally got the bill fixed, but the attitude of every staff member we encountered at this hotel seemed to be that the hotel is right and customers are wrong. 
Next time, we will take our business elsewhere.

We always stay close to the airport before traveling back to Europe. The hilton near seatac was a good choice. Nice room. Was booked on rewards points but service was good and transport to the airport very efficient.

My wife and I stayed at the Yotel this month. We picked it b-c it was one of the cheapest options in Manhattan and it looked pretty cool. We were not disappointed! The room was amazing--small, but we never felt squished or cramped. The features (t.v., shower, bed, etc.) were fantastic.
The location was excellent. In the - days that we stayed in Manhattan, we never once took a cab. We walked to Times Square, Central Park, a few shows, and everywhere else. The subway was cheap and we saved a ton on transportation costs b-c of the Yotel's location.
However, the best part of the hotel was the staff. I've never stayed at a hotel with such friendly, outgoing people. I had more conversation with staff people than ever before--I remember Jose, the always-smiling guy who helped with our luggage. He went out of his way to say hi to us (and it seemed all the staff did the same thing). They offered great tips on the neighborhood and were simply amazing.
If my wife and I ever go back to New York, we will definitely stay at the Yotel again. Don't miss it--for $----night, it was well worth it!
Generous two hour Happy Hour and cooked to order breakfast. Front desk people very friendly and helpful.

I have stayed at the Crowne Plaza Brookhollow for -- years. The management and staff have always met all my needs. In the rare circumstance of a problem, my needs were always met swiftly and courteously.
Manager Rizwan Marfani is a very attentive manager and exhibits care and concern.
His assistant, Henry shows the same concerns for the guest.
Although there are numerous restaurants in the area, the food in the restaurant is excellent and prices are reasonable. The Bar is lead by Andrew who takes excellent care of his customers.

We visit NYC at least once a year so we know our stuff. We usually stay in a little place on W--rd but this year we decided to stay more centrally and chose to stay at the Holiday Inn on W--th St instead. 
Ok, so the good things.....
Excellent location!!! Step out of the hotel and take the first left onto -th Ave and you will arrive at Port Authority which is great for subway links as well as other forms of travel. Walk another couple of blocks and turn right onto W--nd street and at the next block you will arrive at the entrance to TImes Square (so the hotel is not quite in Times Square....... but its only a - to -- minute walk). 
Staff are very friendly - ask for a high floor and chances are you will get a nice view - we could see the Empire State Building from the --th floor. 
Great value for money - give it a few years and the prices will double because of the location. The hotel is obviously very modern since it is new and the lobby and rooms reflect this. Good sized room and bathroom for NYC. Clean. Flat screen tv. 
Now for the not so great.....
The hotel is -- floors high and has - rooms on each floor....... and only TWO elevators (lifts). Its ok if you are using one of them late at night, but if you are leaving the hotel on a morning then expect to wait for at least -- minutes for the lift to arrive and then another -- minutes to make it to the lobby as everyone else is waiting on every floor too which means the lift will keep stopping even if there is no more room left in it! Not fun when you are checking out and have all your luggage with you - as does everyone else, hence why noone can fit in the lift! On a morning one of the two lifts is usually blocked off by the maids too!
There are only - computers in the lobby (though they do have free internet access). One guy hogged the same computer for over an hour the other morning when we were trying to check in online for our flights. Each room does have free wifi though but sometimes it hangs, hence why we needed the computer. 
Overall, its a really handy, clean hotel - I would recommend.

While HGI doesn't have all the luxuries-amenities of a great resort hotel, it gives you about everything you could expect for the price point. Very clean, comfortable, well appointed rooms. Friendly staff that was helpful in directing us to different locations in the area. The truly pleasant surprise, however, was their food. We came back for the happy hour at - pm at their somewhat small bar in the lobby and struck up a conversation with a local person who regularly comes by to order a dinner to take home. She said the food was very good, and recommended we try their fish taco appetizers. She was right. After downing those quickly another couple recommended their ceviche tacos and they were even better. Instead of going out for dinner, we took their recommendations and had a steak at the bar - it was great. The next morning, we had breakfast there and it was also very good. To say our stay exceeded expectations would be an understatement. Not sure if all HGIs set the bar this high - they might as we met one of their college grad trainees who served us breakfast. He said he was on a rotation program and this HGI was a great learning experience. The only one negative is the location - it's not on one of the main streets and about a mile or two from the freeway and a bit hard to find. It's in a suburban residential area so there are no other places in walking distance. But that was compensated by the fact that parking was a snap and it was free plus the fact that the food, drink and service at the hotel was so good that you didn't need to walk somewhere else.

My husband and I stayed here for three nights in July. Loved the modern trendy room, which was well equipped and clean. Breakfast was very good, though quite pricey - the restaurant was very classy and service was excellent. The best thing about the hotel was the location - right by Boston Common. It was very close to the start of the Freedom Trail. Also very easy to get to Boston's other sights (e.g. Harvard, aquarium etc) from the hotel - either on foot or on the T. We'd recommend this hotel.

This is a huge convention hotel, with all the pluses and minuses that brings.
Pluses: The location is absolutely perfect, with North Michigan Avenue and the Loop each a block away. The guest rooms are of a reasonable size, with drop-dead views of the lake and the river. The hotel is modern and clean. The Club Lounge is very nicely designed and offers a standard Continental breakfast -- nothing special.
Minuses: The beds are absolutely horrendous. Whatever the opposite of a Heavenly Bed is, that's what they've got here. The mattresses are so soft and mushy that when you lie down, you sink right in, with absolutely no support. (Apparently, the hotel installed these mattresses in the whole hotel just a few months ago thinking that softer is better, but according to the Guest Services representative, they've had so many complaints about the mattresses that the will be replacing the whole lot again soon.) Service is very impersonal, and there always seems to be a long line at the front desk. In-room internet is horrendously slow and not cheap.
The gym has a really nice lap pool and sundeck, which are free, but the workout area is surprisingly small (and expensive) for a hotel of this size.
The business center was staffed with nasty people. They misplaced my Fedex package for hours, and they were not at all apologetic about it (although the front desk clerk did apologize on their behalf).
In brief: If you don't intend to do anything in the hotel besides sleep and need to be in this location, then this is a fine place to stay -- once the hotel has done something about the mattresses. Otherwise, there are much more elegant and personal hotels in the area for the same price.

This hotel needs a company wide seminar on how to treat customers. Customer service does not exist. My husband had a business trip in New York and I tagged along for several days. He left very early Monday morning for work and I was in the hotel room by myself when I realized that the linens on the bed had a stain of poop! Grossed that I had slept on it, I called the front desk. They were neither apologetic nor sensed the grossness of the situation. The front desk notified me that they would be sending someone. They sent one male janitor who came into the room to change the sheets. Again, no apology or anything. About -- minutes later, still in my PJ's and about to get into the shower, the same male janitor knocked on my door. There had been no call from the front desk so I was wary of opening my door. I opened it and stood at the front door asking what he wanted. He claimed he left his master key inside my room. I told him I had not seen any key but he barged in the room and started searching for it himself. At this point, I was really uncomfortable. Our room was in the corner, I was by myself, and this strange man was basically looking through my stuff. Of course, he didn't find anything and left. I was late for an appointment and didn't stop by the front desk to tell what happened. I came back into the hotel in the late afternoon and asked to see the manager. When I told her of what happened, again, she wasn't very concerned, was condescending, and kept asking me what the big deal the situation was. She referred me to the housekeeping manager who sent me a small box of chocolates to ease the situation. We left the next day. Their valet policy is to call the front desk -- minutes in advance and they will have the car waiting in the front. (I think the place where they park is actually pretty far and that's how long it takes to walk and drive back). We called it in the next morning at -am. My flight was leaving at -:-- so we were cutting it close. We came downstairs after the allotted time to find the wrong car sitting in the front. We informed the front desk that it was the wrong car and they had to call over to the valet deck. Instead of hurrying and trying to get our car back to the hotel, the front desk was more concerned with whose fault they got the number wrong. We didn't care as long as the car got to the hotel ASAP. It took them another -- minutes to do so. The charge was $-- per night for valet, so my husband wanted to see if they could waiver the last night's valet charge for their mistakes. It has been horrible trying to talk to anyone. No manger has called back. The customer service is non-existent.

-. The lock on the sliding glass door was broken off and it was about --- of an inch sharp metal. Reported it two days in a row it NEVER got fixed!! I have a picture on my camera to prove it. 
-. The metal bar to lock sliding glass door was also broken that when My daughter went to open the door it fell on top of her head. My husband immediately called the front desk.

This hotel is right on the wharf, well the nearest. So its just a case of walking round the corner where you can take a trip to Alcatraz, a bay cruise or take in the not so wonderful stench of the sea lions! I booked the hotel on the internet and filled in the form to request a smoking room, not realising that California are totally against this bad habit, I consequently did not get a smoking room as the hotel has only - such rooms and they were already booked, so dont expect too much, all hotels which state they have both types of rooms probably dont have too many, as smoking is not encouraged in this part of the world not even in bars. The hotel is very clean and has large rooms but does not have a breakfast room, there is a cart selling coffee and pastries etc but its not cheap. A IHOP is located next door which always seemed popular, a whole airline crew came in there the morning I was there, complete with their luggage. Its pancakes with everything so if you dont like them you can go to Johney Rockets for a real American diner experience, you would believe you were back in the --'s, this is located out the door from reception past the very small pool and then you walk in the diner through its back door, when you leave, through the front door you are on the wharf! Round the corner from the right of reception is a ----, here you can pour your own coffee-around ----- different varieties, always piping hot, very good and inexpensive, they have a selection of cakes and pastries but its take away, also I dont think you could ask for anything they didnt have here in this shop, wine, sweets, chocolate, toiletries. We walked a few blocks to the Cannery and the trolleys leave for Union Square area a further block, the view from here of Golden Gate bridge is great. Travelled first weekend in May and never saw a cloud, photos are fab, blue skies for - days. It is easy to find a --star hotel that meets expectations. But, sometimes circumstances don't allow us to stay in luxury hotels! My wife and I stayed at the Affinia Manhattan on December -----, ----. We arrived at the hotel before --:--am and was able to check in at this time. The room service people were never seen yet every time we came back to our room, everything was cleaned and straightened up. My wife and I live in Charlotte and we stayed here one night after a wedding reception downtown so we did not have to go home. It was not a very comfortable bed. The temperature would not stay very steady either. The overall look and feel was fine but for a Marriott it really was a letdown.

My girlfriends and I (- of us total) stayed at the Affinia Dumon this previous week. At the front desk, I asked for a room with a view of the Chrysler Buidling. First time family holiday to New York made very enjoyable by super hotel accommodation. Service by front desk staff was faultless, nothing was too much trouble. Right in the center of Manhattan, this Boutique Hotel has everything you could need or ask for on a visit to New York City. Just wanted to let folks know about the excellent service I received from the front desk, specifically Gustavo Gomez, in resolving a room issue with noise. This hotel is very clean, and the staff is very friendly. Upon our arrival, we were briefed on the attractions of San Diego and also a map of how to get there by various means of transportation. This is a grand old hotel--the foyer is stunning and very attractive,. the rooms are not quite up to scratch,. there are so many rooms--some are in new extension at the back (these rooms are bigger but not as nice as the ones in poriginal part of building). Very hard to say something special about this hotel. It's clean, has big rooms vith quite nice view from the higher floors. It looks a little bit old-fashioned..

I had the opportunity to stay here for awhile and I had a wonderful time. The view from the hotel was amazing and I loved the location! What made this hotel so special was the great service! If you are looking for a hotel with a great location, atmoshpere, and quality service; you should stay here!
room was very large by NY standards. Clean, beautiful linens, comfortable bed, and wonderful staff.

My mom and I were going to the Columbus Zoo for a weekend trip and did not want to spend a lot of money on a hotel and found a coupon for this Travelodge hotel in one of those coupon booklets you pick up at rest areas. I plan to report and send my pictures to their corporate office because this place needs to be condemned and there is NO excuse for it. I wish there was a negative number or zero rating because even a rating of one circle for this hotel is too good for this den of eniquity.

We haven't tried any of the others as our first stay at the Giraffe was so good that was the first place we thought about booking when we went back, and we weren't disappointed.

It is away from the overly touristed areas such as Times Square and Central Park, but at the same time extremely well located to visit all of the areas. It is very close to the Metro and while in the centre of town, relatively quiet (by New York standards). The location makes for reasonably priced taxi rides when you are too tired for another metro ride. 
While the hotel is not in a hot spot, there are plenty of bars and restaurants within walking distance. Around the corner is a small area of Indian and East Asian restuarants, nice quality and reasonable prices and enough off the grid that you can wander in and get a table without reserving weeks in advance. We had a superb meal at one that was almost extremely reasonable. 
The rooms are very modern (this is not a traditional old school NYC hotel, but I guess the ame gives that away). We thought the rooms were actually a very good size for a popular big city, with a generous bathroom and shower room. A couple of nice perks are a reasonable breakfast in the morning and other offerings throughout the day. Staff were pretty good too, notwithstanding the never ending barrage of tourists. 
While we would probably like to try another hotel just for the experience, I have a feeling next time we will end up back at the Giraffe so that we are assured of another great NYC experiience. You won't go wroing staying here.

I would not stay here again...and I would never ask my family members to stay here, either. If we hadn't moved so much stuff in that first day, I would have hightailed it out of here!!

Excellent property and great location. Staff was terrific and very attentive during our stay. Parking rates go down on the weekend. The room was good size, the bed comfortable, everything was great! Near theatre, arts, complex.

From the time of our booking until our departure for New York (flying in from Paris and Copenhagen) the hotel changed owner, and transformed itself into a Holiday Inn.
With that they also completely mixed up all bookings leaving us with an email three days before arrival saying the hotel was now over-booked, but a room at another hotel at Times Square was booked for us.

The next day a new manager however provided us with a new room - for three - and with a few days of complementary breakfast. And a big excuse. And we did then have a somewhat agreeable stay...
But... only to come home and following find the hotel - with no warnings or explanation - had withdrawn $--- on our credit card. And only when we asked why, we were told it was a fine for smoking in our room. Which is quite interesting as none of us smoke - and never have...!
So right now we are in the process of talking to our lawyer to get the hotel refund the money, so no, I wouldn't really recommend Holiday Inn Wall Street...

This Travelodge is conveniently located just five blocks from the Alamo and Riverwalk and promises a very unique and memorable experience.

Great location for the theater, good food. Even walked to the Javitts Center where
I had business.

Parking was expensive but the price of the room made up for it. Got a nice deal through Priceline.com and the hotel was within walking distance of everything! It was an easy walk to the nearest Subway which took us right to the Phillies game! I loved the help yourself toiletry closet and COLD bottled water. Nice touch! Bed was comfy and it wasn't noisy on the floor that we stayed on as some others have complained about. Room was small but functional and had a great LCD tv. Overall, a great overnight getaway location.

I would like to say that I have been going to the Affinia Gardens since ----, when it was called Lyden Gardens, and I think it is a perfect place to stay in New York.
The location is the best; it is located in the Upper East Side, but totally equidistant from the residential area and the more commercial one. Four blocks to the Fifth Ave!!
The apartments are very spacious and comfortable. The hotel provides everything you can possibly need, and the reception staff is very polite, totally helpful in a very warm way.

I recommend this hotel because of location, comfort, and staff. Thanks’ to each and every one of the staff.

This is a GREAT four star hotel. I think it's important to clarify that -- it's a FOUR STAR hotel. It's totally not the Four Seasons or anything else that is five star, so I don't understand why people go there expecting it to be at that level. However, if you accept that it's a four star hotel, you'll probably find it's the BEST four star hotel in Manhattan.
Stayed there for a week during late March this year, and had an absolutely lovely time. Absolutely no dramas during our stay, and we found everything to be clean, efficient, well managed and friendly. I booked a King Suite via their website on the '- night getaway' rate, which was tremendously good value. The - full nights in this massive --- square foot suite was just ---- USD, which is remarkable value for a room this size in New York in my opinion. The suite itself was absolutely lovely. Plenty of room to relax in, which is vitally important if you are in New York for a blazing - day tourism extravaganza, and you come home heavily laden with shopping bags every day :) Rooms in NY tend to be a bit smaller than other cities around the world, so this wasn't the largest suite I'd ever been in, but it was an okay size. Of particular note is the bathroom, which had the most wonderful deep soaking bath tub that we made good use of almost every day.
Concierge was excellent -- we wandered down to Daniel and said we needed a nice restaurant to have dinner in on Saturday night before our Broadway show, and he very quickly got us into an award winning restaurant nearby. His efficiency and professionalism was quite amazing.
Reception was also fantastic, but it depended on who you spoke to. Brook - Brooke was absolutely sensational. She had so much enthusiasm and was so incredibly friendly, that we couldn't help but have a huge smile on our faces as we checked in. Every time I needed to come down to reception, if I saw Brook I would make a bee line for her because she was so lovely.
The bed -- oh my goodness. Yes, people rave about the Sofitel bed and I was always like """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sure, whatever"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", but then I got in this one and I totally understand what everyone is on about! They put this very VERY soft featherbed thingy on top of the mattress, and it turns the bed into an absolute slice of heaven. We were often thinking about it while we were out and about :) Great down pillows too.
Room service was good, although they did make a mistake once, but quickly rectified it without any hassle. The food was very nice.
The downstairs restaurant has been badly slated in past reviews, but we ate dinner there on our first night and found it to be very nice, although the service was a touch slow. We cannot comment on the breakfast because we never ate it there. For breakfast, as has been mentioned in previous reviews, head down the street to the Red Flame Restaurant. This is a kind of 'diner' with lovely big breakfasts, fast service, and a real cool New York street ambience. People come in and queue up at the take-out counter for bagels and coffee, while we sat in one of the numerous booths and just soaked it all up. The waitresses may not be Minnesota nice, but they are super fast and efficient, and ice cold water will be on your table just as you sit, with coffee not far behind it. We had breakfast there every morning, trying different specials and can recommend a stack of things! (great poached eggs, home fries, omelettes)
Okay, back to the hotel!
Niggles: the cupboard for hanging your clothes in was very small, especially for a suite. However, we managed to get by. We didn't get a fabulous view, even though we were on the top floor. The view was of some unrecognisable buildings, so if you want a view of Chrysler (which you can absolutely get from this hotel) please make sure you request precisely that well in advance.
The water pressure in the shower was perhaps below average.
On the whole, we had a wonderful stay here and I cannot give this hotel anything less than full marks. I would have paid two to three times the price at the Four Seasons, and I'm sure the experience would not have been that much more comfortable to warrant it. They have great staff at the Sofitel, it's in a fabulously convenient location, and our time there was hassle free and completely pampered. What more can you ask for? Get it on a good rate, and stay there!!!!

The Mosser Hotel is perfectly located in downtown San Francisco and provides one with an ideal starting point for sight seeing in the city. Located right next to Bart station, and minutes from California St., you can't beat the location and access to the entire city. The staff is courteous and helpful, and the rooms and overall decor is modern and stylish. The hotel is reasonably priced given that you are in an expensive city. Overall a hotel that should be booked anytime you come and visit San Francisco.

I have stayed at the W Hotel on Lakeshore several times, both for personal and work purposes. I have always had an amazing experience, both with the venue itself and with the staff at the hotel. The hotel itself is an an amazing location (right on lakeshore drive on Lake Michigan) and has a spa (spa products are provided to you in your room) and a fantastic and very updated exercise facility. There is a very hip and fun vibe to the hotel. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Whenever, Whatever"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" line you can call is fantastic - they will literally get you anything you need! From a microwave to an eyeglass repair kit, they will get it to your room asap. The staff was always very friendly and accommodating and was great at recommending a hair salon while I stayed for an extended time. The W Lakeshore is my first choice of hotel in Chicago and is the only place I choose to stay - not to mention the reasonable prices!

We stayed here only one night out of convenience. The price was right until..... i'll get to that later. The room was cozy but not extravagant. We had a king size bed that was actually quite comfortable. The shower, once you can lift you leg over the insert tub, was especially strong and hot. A plus! The strange item was the faucet in the bathroom - there wasn't enough room to put your hands underneath! The AC never did cool the room quite enough. All in all the room was very clean and comfortable with a TV, desk, bureau, etc. All the regular stuff. The Park Plaza is in a central location; easy to reach nearly everything in the city. So, the price was fine (as Boston goes) but the parking! OMG! We had to bring two cars into town and valet parking those was almost as expensive as the room! Park it yourself across the street and save at least a few bucks.

I stayed here for two nights for a business trip. My office is only - blocks away so it was convenient for work. It was in a good neighborhood but I had to walk several blocks to get to Michigan Ave. (next time I think cabbing is better) 
The hotel is very beautiful, modern and clean. It's got some good restaurants and bars near by. It is pricey but what do you expect with a W? I had a great night sleep and workout facilities were decent.

Had a great stay at the Westin Grand. Everything was amazing. And the gentleman that worked at the door, Alain Kenow, was a true gentleman and very helpful with our bags and getting a taxi. I'll be coming back.

The general outlook of the hotel was low class. The bed sheets smelled clean. The air conditioner, refrigerator and microwave worked well. Breakfast was excellent. Receptionists were cordial. The bed and the breakfast were the most impressive aspect of our stay. The price was affordable.
Thank you!

The JW is conveniently located across from the Galleria in Houston, as well as ----handy for excursions away from shopping. The staff in the entire property were attentive and pleasant, particularly in the restaurant. 
The rooms are in need of a rehab, as noted by other contributors, which is currently in progress. The furniture and fixtures are dated...finding an electrical outlet to charge more than one cell phone and use the iron at the same time was a challenge! The room was extremely stuffy, and no amount of A-C helped. Look for packages like the - for breakfast.
Overall, a decent property with a some opportunities to improve, which is already underway.

My friend and I visited LA for NBA All-Star weekend. I automatically assumed this was going to be a busy weekend and the hotel service was going to reflect that. I was absolutely wrong with my assumption. When we arrived, we were greeted by friendly hotel staff. The line to check in was moving at a rapid pace, we were able to get our room upgraded, and the hotel honored our AAA discount (--% off). We were upgraded to the --th floor (club level), which featured a lounge, where continental breakfast was served daily and drinks and appetizers were served in the evenings. The hotel was clean, the staff were very helpful, the decor was exquisite, the rooms were modern and comfortable, and the view was awesome. The hotel is located in the heart of downtown LA so getting around was very easy....unless you have a cab driver that refuses to drive in traffic!

This was our second visit to San Francisco and had previously stopped at Holiday Inn next door so we knew the location was excellent, we only changed to this one as it provided complimentary breakfast and this was adequate with plenty of choice. Our room was large with two double beds and a settee with small kitchen too, very nice and cleaned daily to a very good standard. Staff were excellent, nothing was too much trouble , internet access was great with teenagers who need to keep in touch with the world. Everything was nearby so provided an effortless break.

Excellent coffee for customers, friendly staff, very good beds and clean rooms! Poor windows because all possible city- and traffic noise from the street hammered your ears. I would use this hotel again though. Sohotel is renovated with style and taste - respecting the history of the building.
I.S. Jämsänkoski, Finland

My husband and I stayed here for only one night on our recent visit to NYC and were lucky to get the best rate in town ($---) by bidding on Priceline earlier that morning. Score! We knew that it was pretty far away from some of the sights we had planned to see that day but for a --star hotel at that price it was totally worth it to us. 
What we hadn't expected was how cute the area was. Murray-Hill is for sure the most charming part of NYC that we saw. It was clean, pretty and obviously very affluent. We felt very safe walking the streets at night. Furthermore, the room was amazing! We had no idea that we'd 'won' a suite. The living room had a pull-out couch and TV, there was a kitchen, full bath and large bedroom also with TV. It was like a regular suite in any other city. Unusually roomy for an inexpensive room in NYC. 
Things that visitors might want to know...(-) use Grand Central Station. It's the closest stop. (-) it was only a $-- cab to LaGuardia! 
Stay here. It's worth it. We WILL be back!

My first impression when I walked into the room was - this is it?? It was extremely small.

We stayed at the Wyndham La Cascada from ------------. This is a great place to stay. Everyone is very helpful and the location is great

This is the nicest SpringHill we have ever been to. Rooms are big and service excellent. We were able to check in early which increases the value. This is a great location with good food and OSU ver close.

We are newlyweds who stayed here as part of a - month trip around the states in May of ---- and thought this hotel was great - if you love the Hollywood area. 
We didn't particularly connect with the neighbourhood and found the whole place itself quite tacky and overdone, but that is nothing to do with the hotel.
Yes, the rooms aren't particularly modern and you can tell that this hotel was built some time ago but they are clean, spacious and have everything you could possibly need. We were surprised to have our own kitchen and coffee-tea making facilities.
The bed was big and comfortable and the proximity to the big shopping mall across the road was great. 
The front desk staff were lovely and the simple free breakfast in the morning was fab. 
Would stay here again if I am ever needed back in Hollywood :)
To keep track of the rest of our trip check out our website:
www.revelintheview.com.au

Exceptional, excellent, extraordinary! This hotel is outstanding. The area is easily accessible to the expressway. Several wonderful restaurants including their own on site. When in Columbus we ate at the Columbus Brewery Company. Yum! A must see in Columbus. The Columbus Zoo is top notch! And the Polaris Fashion Mall is a shopper's dream! Back to Weston, the staff is friendly, classy and professional. It was our anniversary! The staff made sure to make it memorable. We needed directions and the staff actually walked outside with us to point out streets. The rooms were cleaned and spacious. This was at one time a well known, but older resort called the Pointe at South Mountain. They have kept much of that facility intact, so despite the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""newness"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of some parts of the resort, you can see areas that are dated.

I have to compliment the staff, they did not push the purchase side of the resort on us at all despite the signs everywhere. There is also a large construction area that was quiet for the weekend, that separates the hotel into two parts, so if you are going to stay here, don't stay at the Camelback or Mountain units--you will have to do a lot of extra walking to get to the pool, the breakfast restaurant, the health club and spa. We stayed at Camelback and found everything to be kind of far away. They do have shuttles to get around if you request them. Staff was friendly and helpful.
Room was suite style with pull out queen sofa, desk area, wet bar, TV and separate bedroom with - queens, TV, closet cabinet and bathroom with combined shower-tub. Parking was kind of difficult, with nite time parking a search, ended up walking about a block back to our room, as parking in our lot was always full.
Lots of activities--Oasis water park, is only open to hotel guests, has an - story water slide, water tube area, large pool and a wave pool. Each unit also has a small pool and jacuzzi pool. A golf course and driving range were available. Tennis was available, but I did not see the courts. Gym was very large and spacious. 
Food for breakfast is available at the restaurant adjacent to the Health club--food was ok, nothing exciting. There are several restaurants on site, only went to the one for breakfast.
General atmosphere of the place is lots of families with small kids. Lots of screaming and running around, by the end of the day, the housestaff must have their hands full trying to keep the grounds clean, always lots of snack trails down the hallways and in the common areas. At the pool, they have a lifeguard about every - feet!
Ok place to stay, but if you do not plan on spending a lot of time at the water park, you could probably stay somewhere else for less money. My kids are teenagers and they thought the pools scene was ok, but overrun with smaller kids. If you have smaller kids, this is the place for you.

This is a really nice hotel but not of that scale. Oh, you will definitely need a car since it is a good distance from both IAH and HOU.

The location is excellent from a tourist point of view. A very interesting neighbourhood. Close to all kinds of bars, restaurants and shops.

Would I stay here, in this room, again? No!

My brother and sister flew into Seattle to celebrate the holidays, and we wanted a downtown venue. None of us had ever stayed at the Andra, but we all loved it. Incredible rooms, great service, and perfect location for getting out and walking around Seattle.

This hotel and its sisters deserve the very high ranking they have on the list of favourite hotels in New York. See also the reviews of Madison and Vine, their bistro - it's a good choice any time - but particularly if you want somewhere easy to fall into after an evening arrival!

This hotel was ideal for us for price & location. The room that we had No;--- was on the top level and there is a lift to access all levels. The Affinia Shelburne is my go-to hotel in NY for busness trips. My wife and I spent a night at Lakeway Resort and Spa in lieu of a late evening drive back to San Antonio. We were both very happy we did so. Lovely staff, - minutes away from my elderly parents in the suburbs, very comfy bed. That was the good stuff. The bad? I stayed at this hotel for three nights and was extremely pleased with my experience. The convenience of the location was a major draw to me as it is located next to the red line. I have not one complaint about my stay here and the next time I am in Chicago, I will book a room here.

Warm cookies on arrival, helpful staff, lovely decorated hotel.
Theres a view from the main lobby onto the Marina which is gorgeous and you can go for walks there too.
We got a room with a view and so worth it!Get a Marina view!

Stayed there for two nights. Room was clean, service terrific. Nerma at the front desk was VERY friendly and helpful! The bar had ORGANIC VODKA and GIN!!! Crop and Farmer's, that's a PLUS! Can't wait to go back!

Negatives: flowery air freshener used heavily throughout hotel was extremely annoying. Bed was dreadfully soft. We had backaches the entire stay. Liquid soap dispenser inside shower didn't work and housekeeping provided exactly one bar of soap and one bar only. No hand lotion. Generally, bathroom toiletries seemed a bit stingy for a so-called higher end property.

This hotel has an AMAZING location! The rooms are super tiny and dark. The hallways are dark and gloomy also! Great location, and close to subways. It was a rough start, with a great finish. We got there to be sent to a room we definitely did not sign up for. Amazing hotel, clean rooms, perfect location and most important of all the best service. Manager in charge Elizabeth was extremely helpful in facilitating my whole experience and really made my stay feel like home. The rest of the staff is also very friendly and helpful.

The Abri Hotel has a very good location near Union Square. It's easy to hop on and off buses and cable cars as well as the BART just within a block from the hotel. The room nice and clean. I don't expect a four star hotel with the Four Points chain, but do expect it to be clean and comfortable. We had more than a fabulous time! The hotel is everything we hoped for. Check in was a breeze (however, parking in the next door lot wasnt as easy and also cost us $--). Hotel lobby was cute and enjoyed the orange iced water.

My wife and I stayed for - nights in August and couldn't fault it for what we wanted.
Great location, the concierge guy was fantastic and there is a lovely restaurant attached to the hotel that does a great breakfast!

This is --s---s motel - motor hotel (- stories, exterior corridors) which has been updated somewhat (new front facade, secured, attractive courtyard, standard rooms divided into --room suites), is clean and well-maintained. 
The rooms are relatively small (cramped for our family of -), but clean and in good repair. The dresser - media cabinets included adequate LCD TV sets but not many cable channels. There was a mini-fridge and microwave inside the parlor cabinet as well, but no table and only a single side chair.

A hot buffet breakfast was included (sausage, eggs, biscuits & gravy, pastries, fruit, juices, make-your-own waffles, boiled eggs); the breakfast area - and adjacent courtyard seating was kept relatively clean and well-serviced, but was not spacious and became overloaded at times.
