The hotel is located just off the main """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Hotel Circle"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" area, with easy access from I-- & I--; there are many chain and fast-food restaurants within walking and short (- min.) driving distance. 
They charge $- per day for permitted onsite parking - unusual for this class of hotel, especially in San Diego - it's on the hotel's website, but not on the Choice listing page. This appears to be eithjer a measure to keep guests from the adjacent LaQuinta out, or just a semi-hidden fee to bolster profits.
At around $--- prepaid (plus the $- daily parking fee) for a --bed-plus-sofabed suite, this hotel is a fair value (typical for San Diego in summer) in a good location.

I was really excited to stay at this hotel because of the history the hotel has. When we got there and checked my heart sank - the room was disgusting. The bath tub had black mold, the empty soap dish was filthy, the wall paper was peeling off the wall, the plaster had chipped off the other wall (big spots of white in the paint), the ceiling was peeling and the roof was covered in water stains. My husband who is usually very chill was even appalled at the state of the room. When I complained to the front desk, we got a better room that didn't have all those things wrong, but overall the place still just felt dirty. There was definitely a smell about the entire place that made me ill the whole time. The decor was awful which was surprising because they were just supposed to have undergone a renovation. The only good thing about this hotel is that it was on the freedom trail. Internet was not free.

First note: this hotel is undergoing renovations. They are upgrading the rooms throughout Spring ----. The renovations did not impact me except that the contractors were using a number of parking spaces. The gym was closed during my stay, but they offer use of a nearby gym.
Location: Hotel Circle South is a strip of hotels-motels. There's nothing interesting within walking distance and there isn't much of a view. You will need a car. On the other hand, the freeway is very convenient and the area is a short drive to Sea World, Old Town, Balboa Park-Zoo, shopping, and the airport. Downtown and La Jolla are also quite close.
Check-in: Very quick; received early check-in without a problem (I arrived around - PM, not very early).
Rooms: the --queen --BR suite is a generous size. The bedroom is crowded, with - queen-sized beds, but there is room for luggage; with the living room area, the whole suite is comfortable. The room was clean although it showed a little age (I was in an unrenovated room). In-room wired internet was free. It didn't work when I first arrived, but they had it fixed fairly promptly. The big problem was sound isolation. Although the bedroom door does a good job of blocking hallway noise, you can hear neighbors above and through the shared wall. Even a simple phone conversation is pretty clear. I've stayed in hotels with thinner walls, but not many. Unfortunately, there's not much the hotel management can do. They can only ask people to quite down if security can hear them from the hall and you can hear through the the shared wall better than through the two doors between the hall and the bedroom. The bed was comfortable and there were plenty of pillows.
I can't report on the HVAC. I didn't need heat or AC while I was there (not unusual for San Diego).
The renovations will update the technology (TVs, clock radio), decor, and kitchens (the photos of new rooms look nice). I don't think they're going to fix the thin walls.
Breakfast: fairly standard fare: cereal, bagels, bread, eggs, breakfast meat, potatoes, make-your-own waffles. Hot food was mostly warm. I was pleasantly surprised by the selection of Tazo teas. 
Manager's Reception: I did not eat the snacks, but like with the teas, was pleasantly surprised by the selection of beer on tap. 
Parking: $---day as advertised. From what I found, this is standard in the area. I knew I was going to pay it, but it's fairly disingenuous to charge for it when it's not really an option. There is no public transportation within easy walking distance. I understand the need to make a profit, but this is akin to charging for sheets.
Pool: I did not try the pool or hot tub. 
Overall, this isn't a bad choice if you -) need space for family, -) have a car, and -) can sleep through anything. If you're a light sleeper (like me), traveling alone, I would recommend something else.

Well I was there in September from the UK with my -- year old mum who had never been to the USA before and she thought it was fine - and, no, that's not because we Brits are used to crappy places. For Manhatten it provided an excellent base for getting around in a clean, safe and extremely good value setting. My sister has also stayed there twice and I had stayed there once before and think it is 'characterful', even the food van that parks outside and the visiting social worker.
Yes, we could have paid more and stayed in the Holiday Inn, but there's plenty of those in London if we wanted a bland experience. The Big Cup cafe opposite and the lovely East of Eighth restaurant nearby are also great places.

The hotel was opened in Octorber ----. I stayed there for - nights a few weeks ago. First - nights I stayed at a 'x--' room, which was right by one of the elevator banks. My bed was literally - feet away from the - elevators with constant noises from guests coming and going, and the annoying chimes. Seriously, do they have to set the chimes so loud? It was non-stop 'ding' 'ding' 'ding' throughout the night! Finally I had to ask to be moved to another room. The receptionist was very accommodating and switched me to another room, which reeked of this strong and strange smell of smoke and cleaning solutions. There was an industrialized air freshening machine sitting on the floor when I got there. I immediately called them and explained the situation - I felt bad asking for another room but there was just no way I could stay in that room for another - nights. The smell was so bad I had to leave the room immediately and wait for a staff member who was bringing me a key to a -rd room. To the hotel's credit, they were extremely accommodating and put me in an upgraded room free of charge (hotel was fully booked). The -rd room was perfect and I am giving the hotel - stars for trying to rectify - bad situations for me, a first-time guest. The hotel is brand new and I loved the modern decor. The bed and pillows were very comfortable. Free wifi worked just fine. Will definitely stay again and hopefully by then they will have worked out the kinks that usually come with a new hotel.

We checked out all of the hotels that were close to a Metro station. We were able to get a room with a King sized bed for $--- a night through Priceline. We were impressed from the beginning that we were able to check in at --:-- pm with no problem and they took our car then as well. The staff was friendly, attentive and well organized. They gave us a map of the city, a document about what would happen if the government shut down, and recommendations about what to do and see. We didn't have a good view from our room but the room was very nice, very well maintained and the location was great. We really enjoyed the Corner Cafe Bakery for lunch or breakfast. Reasonably priced, good service and very good food. If you check out before -:-- pm they don't charge you for the overnight parking charge of $--. For such a central location, we didn't mind pay for two overnight parking charges. The Metro is DIRECTLY across the street from the hotel.

We stayed here in late August with - teenage boys. We stayed in a one bedroom suite. It was quite large , with closets , and a kitchenette. The beds were comfy. I did lots of research on hotels in NYC and compared to other places I was looking at, the price was very fair. Location was great!! The room was spotless. Would go here again.

Altho the hotel has a beautiful lobby, housekeeping is very lacking. When we arrived we only had one towel and no soap. I found housekeeping and was able to get some. The next day, the trash had not been emptied when we returned from an outing. The $-- fee for parking is far too much considering the price of the rooms. All staff was very friendly but housekeeping needs to be addressed.

Celebrated our two year anniversary here, they upgraded our room for free upon check-in with friendly service. Not as close to the TD Banknorth Garden as we would have liked but the entire staff was more than helpful in directing us on how to get around. Clean facilities, with a very beautiful (albeit a little small for families) pool and hot tub. Right down the street from Newbury Street and the Prudential Center if you're interested in some nice shopping and Bean-town sightseeing. The view from our room was amazing, it looked like we were pretty close to Fenway too, if you're looking for a good hotel for a sox game. Got a great rate through Priceline, really top-notch. Nice, quiet room, super-cozy bed. Mini-fridge was out of service but they put our food in their front desk customer fridge for safekeeping overnight.

When we first pulled up to the hotel, we saw a homeless man in the doorway of an abandoned building yelling at passers by about --- block away (the area was cleared of vagrants by the nest day). At that point, I was ready to make a run for it but we decided to check it out anyway, and I'm glad we did. The hotel is a renovated historic building, the lobby was beautiful, especially during our stay because it was decorated for Christmas with holiday music playing constantly. Our room was great, a little on the small side although the bathroom was huge. The room was nicely decorated in colonial style. The bathroom was very nice except that the sink and bathtub drains were very slow. The elevator was very slow, at one point I had to wait almost - minutes to get back to my room from the bottom floor. The breakfast was really good for a free hotel breakfast, good food and good selection. The staff was awesome, especially Stacy who works the afternoon-evening shift, she was very friendly and went out of her way to help us with everything, including lugging our bags up to our room. There is no parking for the hotel, there is a limit on street parking, where I wouldn't have parked anyway, so the only option is to use a commercial lot about - blocks away which is $-- a day (no special rate for hotel guests). On the up side, the hotel is only - blocks away from Independence Hall and within walking distance of the other historical attractions downtown. Although it is not part of the hotel, I strongly recommend dining at the City Tavern, which is across the street from the parking garage, it is a colonial style tavern with the servers in period dress. There were - for one coupons at the hotel when we were there which made it even more attractive. If we are ever in need of a hotel in Philadelphia again, we will definitly stay there.

I don't feel the hotel merits - stars, the rooms are a bit dark, drinks and food are overpriced, etc, but I would definitely give them -.- stars and would return. I just feel that, for the money, and based on the other - star ratings, this hotel should have a bit more umph.
The hotel's background-story is very interesting, the design is very cool, the lobby bar and upstairs bar are really well designed, the luxuries in the room are fantastic.

This hotel is excellent. Everything was perfect. 
The only bad part was the room service I ordered when I got there. Very lousy for $---. 
For food, go to the grove directly across the street. Casual and one of the best restaurants I've ever been to. Open late.

I stayed for two nights at Sofitel New York in February ----. Its an excellent hotel, of a quality on par with its price, and a great deal for location. I'm a native New Yorker (and staying here only because I'm too lazy to deal with weekend train schedules to attend a work conference that started at - AM) and can confidently say that its location is fantastic for a tourist. Located within a -- minute walk to Times Square, Grand Central, Rockefeller Center, and Herald Square, and most of the major subway lines. Its really right in the middle of Manhattan.
Doorman at hand, the concierge-bag check right when you enter, followed by small lobby area with comfy leather seating, a small room on the side (entrance visible when you leave, not when you enter) with three computer terminals offering free internet access, and at the end, the main counter to the left. Decor is classy and simple, leathers and warm woods.
Service was ubiquitous, friendly, and attentive; some spoke French and-or with a French accent, which was a pleasant touch if not really necessary. Check-in was efficient. Turn-down service in the evening was sweet, with ambient lighting and classical music playing as you enter.
I stayed in a -th floor king bed room, which was large, of similar decor theme as the rest of the hotel, with good quality furniture, fixtures, and linens. The set-up around the bed was beautifully designed, including the lighting, artwork above the bed, and side tables. Bed was firm and very comfortable. The bathroom has a double door entry without locks. There is a separate glass-enclosed shower stall in addition to a tub. Bathroom was roomy and good quality, with an adjustable magnifying mirror and large, frame-lit vanity mirror. L'Occitane bath products were a plus. Mirrored closet space with lights inside, flat screen television, chair with side table, and work desk completed the room. Wi-fi in the rooms is an extra cost per night; the lobby terminals help but that's an outdated method of providing internet access. My room had no view to speak of (the back of buildings) so I just kept the curtain closed, but that didn't matter much to me. There's a fitness center open -- hours but I didn't make use of it.
I enjoyed my stay here and would highly recommend it for out of town guests.

Unfortunately, it's one of the worse decision I made in my life to stay in and trust Comfort Suites. The mattress is sagged and my son (a -- years old) couldn't sleep on his side. When I found out it's due to the mattress sagness, that's -:--am. I didn't know how huge impact it was on my son's competition. I was very dissatisfied by the stay. This was our first stay at the Plaza Athenee . We booked their standard King room. I informed them when we made the reservation, that my partner & I would be staying for - nights, and that this was a special occasion. We were going to be in NYC for our wedding in Central Park. ( just - short blocks from the Hotel) When we arrived Nicole, the front office manger greeted us, and escorted us to a seat, to register. As we began, she welcomed us again, and said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""congratulations on your upcoming wedding"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Turndown service nightly was great, when we went out for dinner, or the theatre, I actually think that the bed wasn't only turned down, but we had fresh sheets, as I had taken a nap that afternoon and there wasn't a wrinkle to to found when we returned!! The hotel bar is beautiful, we had cocktails there twice during our stay & took some of our wedding photos in the bar & restaurant. On our wedding night we returned to the room to find a bottle of Champagne, chocolate covered strawberries and rose petals on the bed....all compliments of the hotel. The doorman were always quick to retrieve a cab, or help with a package. Every staff member we encountered was utmost professional. The Hotel was extremely clean, and well maintained. The location could not be beat, close to the Park, in a beautiful upscale neighborhood. I truly didn't want to leave...... I WILL BE BACK !!!!!!

A tremendous Best Western property in a great location. I have been staying there both on business and pleasure, or both, for -- years. Hotel is nice and rooms are very clean. The hotel staff was wonderful, from the minute you check-in to the minute you check out..The staff is extremely friendly. Had some food in the bar and it was ok. The coffee shop is not good at all. The hotel is baout -- minutes from West Hollywood and -- minutes from Warner bros. I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

The platform bed (or just the mattress) was very comfortable but it was covered with a flat sheet that was tucked in a way that exposes a third of the mattress. So when you lay down to sleep, your feet touch the bare mattress.
Did not hear noise from the roof or street. I had no problems with the wi-fi. All in all, it was very pleasant.

Price-quality for New York standards is good.
Breakfast served was fresh everyday with pastries, bagels, fresh fruit, toast, juice and coffee.
The only negative aspect was the noisy airconditioning.
I will definitely come back.

We booked a room at this hotel for a special birthday weekend. What a nightmare. First, the staff was so aloof and wound up in the trendiness of the hotel, that we actually had to laugh. The person at the reception desk was indifferent and unaccomodating. When they showed us to our room, we discovered we had booked a closet (no joke) that had no windows or ventilation and a window above the door that could not be covered- allowing light to shine into the room at all times. Stayed here in early November ---- for the fourth or fifth time, and once again, had a wonderful experience. Friendly and efficient staff, many of whom have long tenure at the property. Great gym. Location is great for Moscone events, but also SoMa dining and nightlife, Bloomingdale's and Nordstrom shopping, and easy access to BART and Muni. In reading other reviews, those who gave lower scores (unbelievably!) seemed to dislike the decor, which travelers can preview in advance and decide accordingly. If I HAD to cite a negative, the worst thing I could offer is that room service, breakfast, and cocktails are a little pricey (although not unusual for top hotel in SF). Thank you SF Intercon!

The hotel has an excellent location. It is within easy walking distance to Time Square and Central Park South. Metro to Brooklyn and the Financial District are also nearby. Refrigerator, microwave and sink is added value if traveling with small children. The rooms are small, but it is NY. Room service is normal. What made the stay so disappointing was the lobby service. The concierge was a total rip off. Don't book any tickets there. The information provided is misleading. Also, be prepared to throw huge tips out at the doorman as well as for any luggage service. I wouldn't stay there again, and try e.g. the Best Western on --th Street between -th and -th.

Avoid this hotel unless it is your last choice. Prices in the $--- and up range are outrageous for this Budget Motel type place. Six months after opening the items I encountered should not have happened.
-The room was cold (literally) and uninviting and I had to turn on the motel-type heater at the window to heat it up--a process which took a good -- hours. 
--It looks like the owners tried to renovate an old building but ran out of money at the end--and so they scrimped on the finishes and fit-up. 
--There is no hotel restaurant and no restaurants in the nearby (bad) neighbourhood. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""breakfast deli""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""--the only source of food in the place opened at -:-- am (the posted hour) with one employee--resulting in a line of -- people trying to get something to eat--there is no other option.--I instead went to the Convention center and ate there since I was going there anyway.
--Don't allow them to give you a room on the side of the hotel facing the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""El"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" train line--its really noisy with trains going by multiple times an hour.

There is a desk but no notepad or pen. 
Bottom line the place felt like a cheap motel room--but at extravagant prices. I have stayed in those motels and have nothing against them--but not at these rates and not at a hotel which mis-bills itself as a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""boutique experience"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".

This hotel was my longest stay within the US, and this hotel did not disappoint! The room rates are value for money and the hotels location is within easy walking distance of time square, close enough to walk but further enough to be away from the lights and the noise. I however am not sure the hotel lived up to its - star rating... The glass window on the bathroom door had grubby hand prints from a child all over it and it appeared to have not been cleaned for a while with numerous marks over the glass. Also the room service didn't update our toiletries supplies each clean. The room was small but something that we were easily able to cope with... And considering its normal for NY we weren't worried. Some pro's and cons for the hotel-guests to consider
Pros-
- Within walking distance to Hells Kitchen and Time Square, also across the road from the Port Authority bus terminal
- Fast lifts
- Value for money
- Complimentary bottle of water
- Free wifi
- beds and pillows are amazingly comfortable
Cons-
- wifi connection was poor... Not sure if that's just the room we were in but we struggled in areas in the room
- the lights in the floor near the lifts are extremely annoying, however thought that was a good idea clearly didn't think clearly 
- no fridge :( 
- - vending machine which kept running out of coke
- no water in vending machine, my recommendation is that the hotel has a vending machine for snacks and another for soda and water... Since there is no fridge I'd like to be able to obtain refrigerated water within the hotel
Overall I enjoyed my stay and I will stay here again and will recommend the hotel to friends and family.

This is a new and comprehensive facility with all the best views of the mountains, city and close to the perfoming arts centers, the sports venues and the variety of local eating establishments, all within walking distance. The amenities are very good, comforting spa services, and their resturant has an excellent Chef and menu. Adults and families with children will find this the best choice if coming to Denver, no matter to if you stay in the city or as a staging for visiting the close by mountain attractions.

If you are thinking about any other way than taxi of getting to this hotel from O’Hare don’t bother; $-- will cover it. It’s about half an hour without hold ups. Reception is huge and quite impressive, quick check in, staff were ok if not particularly friendly. I guess the high number of residents at the cheaper end of the price scale dictates this. Long walk (a full block) to the other end of the building to a small elevator that didn’t work half the time. Up to the floor, reasonable room overlooking a side street. Net curtains always closed! Slept well, shower was ok if not special, no issues, down to breakfast at the place next to the bar. Casual service, average food, high prices for what it was, poor surroundings wouldn’t eat there twice. In the evening the bar was ok, prices not bad, bar food looked ok but we chose to eat out after the “breakfast”. When the lift went down, I had to walk through the staff only areas, which were disgusting, to get up stairs to my room. A couple of times they opened a door up truly horrendously tricky stairs that could be used instead. 
The location is only good for the park and the concert hall, there’s nothing much nearby so everything is a cab or a long walk.
This hotel is huge, impersonal, dated – there’s no way I’d use it again.

From the moment you are greeted by multiple hosts at the front desk, to the quality and size of the rooms and restaurant-bar areas, this hotel is an exceptional place to attend a convention. Great location; great amenities, great people watching lobby. The only minor challenge was with internet access in the room. While free, the access was slow and not up to par.

Whenever the opportunity arises, my wife Sandra and I always mention to fellow travellers the many additional benefits they will receive if they decide to book a room on the Club Floor of any great hotel which offers its guests such a facility. On a recent visit to San Francisco, we took own advice when we stayed at the Ritz Carlton Hotel. The hotel is a low rise building, built in a U shape around a landscaped courtyard and was previously the West Coast headquarters of a New York based insurance company. 
After pulling up at the imposing entry and admiring the spacious foyer with its inviting lounge and bar areas, the registration formalities completed, we were shown to the Ritz-Carlton Club Level where our corner suite room was located. Because our accommodation was on the Club Level we had automatic access to all the facilities available in the Club Lounge, that offers guests a relaxed and comfortable haven, with plenty of sofas and armchairs to sit back and enjoy reading a magazine, have a coffee, a glass of wine or a cocktail. A very substantial complimentary breakfast was available each morning, followed by mid morning pastries and cakes before the lunch selection of salads, soup, sandwiches and cold meats is displayed to tempt one. It does not stop there. 
Afternoon tea with beautiful cakes accompanied by tea and coffee then the day is rounded off with wines and cocktails made to order, hors d’oeuvres, savoury treats and sweets. My goodness, My wife and I virtually spent the whole day in the Club Lounge trying all this fabulous food. If that isn’t enough, there is a round table displaying glass bottles of chocolate treats and meringues for guests to help themselves. All of this was included.
The Concierge, located at the entrance to the Club Lounge, was extremely helpful and was able to provide answers to all our questions on where to go in San Francisco. We were also able to complete our check out procedures there.
Our spacious room, with its traditional style décor and --- thread count Frette bed linens, had views of Coit Tower, San Francisco Bay and the Financial District. The large Italian marble bathroom, with its double sinks and Bulgari amenities made for easy sharing.
Located in a quiet residential neighbourhood in Stockton Street, overlooking the Financial District, near the corner of California Street, the hotel is just a short walk to Union Square with all its tempting shops and department stores, such as Neiman Marcus, Saks Fifth Avenue, Macy’s plus many other boutiques and restaurants.

This hotel certainly lived up to it’s - star rating and we would be happy to return for another wonderful stay. John Pond with Sandra T.

My husband and I booked a room at the Howard Johnson for a four-night summer weekend visit to Chicago. We were pleased with the experience--the friendly staff, convenient location and basic-but-adequate accommodations met our needs. 
There are certainly plenty of luxury full-service hotels in Chicago. HoJo is where you stay if you want a good place to sleep. This motel is fun and retro--two stories, no common area other than a tiny lobby, and a tasty and cheap diner (LaSalle Cafe Luna) with excellent service. Some of the furnishings looked a little dated and the wifi was slow in our room, but we had a comfortable bed, cold A-C and a good shower. I noticed our sink drained slowly the first two nights, but it was promptly fixed without us having to ask. 
We traveled with other friends, and our group booked four rooms in all. The place was a hit with everyone--it is close to the el train, offers one free (!) parking space per room and one larger group got a big room with two sinks. My room was pretty small, but it was fine for the two of us. 
Besides being close to public transportation and plenty of cabs, the motel is a short walk to the Magnificent Mile area and lots of touristy restaurants like Fogo de Chao, Ed Debeviks, Rainforest Cafe and the (formerly called?) rock 'n' roll McDonald's.
I was a little hesitant after reading some negative reviews, but if you manage your expectations you will be happy you stayed at the downtown HoJo.

One thing about NYC I can not stand is being in Time Square. It's full of people and tourist awed by feeling like being in the center of the Earth. However, I was one of those people awed by the lights and fast pace of Time Square. I try not to book any hotel near this area, but to my surprise my company booked it at the Time Hotel. Hoping it was a few blocks north of Time Square, when we arrived it was right next door to it. 
 NYC is full of hotels, but I would not reccomend staying at any chains like the W, Holiday Inn, Crowne Plaza, etc. It is best to venture out and try some of the great boutique hotel NYC offers, such as the Time Hotel. Although this hotel was next door to Time Square, it was actually away from the hustle and bustle of the city. The Time Hotel was suprisingly in a quiet street next to two broadway shows: Spring Awakening and Chicago. 
 Arriving in NYC, our shuttle driver dropped us off at the Crowne Plaza Hotel just to walk us a few feet to the street where the Time Hotel was located. Walking into the hotel felt like a high end boutique hotel. An elevator takes you up to the lobby where a friendly staff greeted you. We were early for check-in and could not get a room until - pm, as a rule with most hotels in NYC. However, we had to work that day so it wasn't an issue. 
 The lobby at the Time is really not a lobby at all, but a BAR-CLUB as returning to the hotel that night, the music was playing loud. This would be a surprise to anyone checking in at night, especially for those not keen to hip hop music. However, our room was on the --th floor so this was not an issue. I was amazed by the bed we ended up getting, which was a king size bed. We seem to have been upgraded free of charge or was it my Trip Advisor hat that made a difference :) Anyways, as with most boutique hotel the room was small. However, it was comfortable and clean. There was not much view, except for the room adjacent to yours where you can see everything that went on in the other room through the window (Corner Room). The bathroom was fully stock with necessities and clean. The use of storage space shaped as squares was a nice touch. They were trying GO GREEN by asking for guests to request for towels when needed and to re-use towles. However, it seem like we got new towels anyways without having to request for them. The mini-bar was expensive, as with most hotel, but well stocked. However, the fridge could only open halfway based on the layout of the room.
 The only negative thing I have to say about the Time Hotel is questioning how secure the room is when you are out in the city. When we left our room one morning, the cleaning lady was on our floor. Having left my umbrella in the room, I came back to find our room door open wide with no one in it. It worried me since anyone could have came in the room and stole all our belongings. However, the positive side to this story is that cameras are on each hallway to ensure safety and security of the guests. I still feel the room should have not been left alone with the door open for anyone to come in and steal something.
 The Time Hotel is another amazing boutique hotel offering access to all of NYC and centrally located where all the actions is happening. It is literally a few feet from Time Square where all the madness and mayhem happens. The location is definately worth it for first time visitors of NYC. Tour buses are next door and the subway (blue line) is only a block away. There is a great grocery store-deli-bakery adacent to the hotel where you can get anything and everything (The grocery store is downstair). Rockefeller Center and -th Avenue is - blocks away. 
 In conclusion, I would reccomend the hotel to any first time visitors in NYC only to be in a centralized area where all other tourist tend to meet at the point called Time Square. Don't be surprise at how small the rooms are since many boutiques hotel don't offer suites, but - or - penthouses. Be mindful that you are going for an experience and most of all just to sleep. When visiting NYC, you spend all day walking, hailing cabs, and hauling shopping bags around that by the time you get back to the hotel you are ready to go to sleep. BTW there is a restaurant downstair called Serafina, pricey, but good breakfast. I never had a glass of orange juice for $-. My friend enjoyed their bagel and lox and I enjoyed their waffle. 
I may have had issues with the location of this hotel, but I am glad to tell you that I did not hear one noise from the people visiting Time Square. BON VOYAGE!!!

The room was comfortable and fairly peaceful. I had rowdy neighbors my first night and a security person came up to get them to quiet down. The bathroom was spotless and featured full-sized soap, conditioner, and shampoo; you can't take them home with you, but it's great not to worry about running out. 
One note - there is no free breakfast. A breakfast spread is available for something like $--, but I didn't go for it and cannot review it.
I was ill while on this trip, and the front desk staff made sure I had everything I needed to be as comfortable as possible. They were stellar, and I'm planning to stay at the GWU Inn again on my next DC trip.
I frequent San Diego for business, the Hard Rock Hotel is a great place to stay & dine. The staff is fantastic and very accommodating.

I was at first apprehensive about finding such a new hotel in Chicago at such a great price! I thought, what's the catch? With the help of Expedia, we paid $---night for a - night stay. Great hotel and even better workout room. Right in downtown Fort Worth. Parking is pretty expensive, but one night we just parked down the street and walked and was not charged for that night. If you don't have a car, it is perfect.

Though this place doesn't have the charm of some of the older hotels in Chicago, it is very clean and comfortable. The best part is the pool on the --th floor. Hotel ZaZa has been my home away from home for months now and it is absolutely amazing! The staff is outstanding and the hotel thinks of all of the nice touches! Daily coffee and tea service on the floor with newspapers makes the day! I love the proximity to the museums and Rice Village! Keep it up ZaZa!

I love Adagio Hotel. My husband and I stayed at this hotel while we were visiting US for honeymoon. As we walked in, we were greeted by a nice cozy feel of the lobby and the very friendly receptionist. She inquired if we were celebrating anything special and we said that we're on our honeymoon. She immediately searched for another room on a higher floor and gave us an upgrade from our original Deluxe Junior Suite. The room was on the --th floor and was quite spacious, but most importantly, clean well maintained. The best thing about it was that we couldn't hear the busy traffic of the street underneath. We also had a nice surprise when someone delivered a bottle of champage & chocolate with a little note of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""congratulation from Adagio Staff"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for our honeymoon. I mean, this was beyond expectation. We stayed in - different hotels while we were visiting The West Coast and Adagio Hotel SF was definitely the one that left a wonderful impression. If you don't like the $-- parking rate, there's one parking garage just next door for $-- or around the corner for $--. I mean, really, there's no reason to not want to stay in this hotel. I give two thumbs up for the friendliness of the hotel staff. We had a very pleasant stay.

This hotel has steadily provided decreasing levels of service with repeated stays here. The convenience to the airport is nice but beyond that would recommend looking elsewhere unless absolutely necessary. For a large hotel with a full house they only have a front desk staff space for - and check-in times can be up to -- min. Parking is always a hassle to find a space so best just to drop the car at the front and deal with valet parking. Better to take the time and drive away from the airport to another Hilton property that has service that is adequate to the facilities they have.

It's such an amazing hotel. I've stayed in three hotels for my stay in NYC, all -* with high tripadvisor ratings. Roger Smith is definitely the best. It is the kind of place that I want to come back again and will let all my friends know when they plan to visit NYC. 
I cannot speak too highly of their staffs. Every single one of them is friendly, responsive, and efficient. Every single request that I had was addressed properly and immediately, and I have had quite several non-usual requests. 
The location is good too, which is three blocks away from Grand Central. It's actually right next to Marriott, W, Hyatt and other great hotels. So you know you can't go wrong with the location. 
The hotel really stands out as a unique NYC hotel. The hotel looks like an art gallery (and they actually own one). The staffs all wear their own T-shirt. I fell in love with the guest room at the first sight. It is beautifully decorated with the floral wallpaper and antique furnitures. I'm not saying that the hotel is flawless. The room is dated, as other comments have suggested. The shower water is slow and I can't find enough outlets to charge all my electronic appliances. But all the problems can be overcome and they by no means change the fact that I'm in love with this place. 
I highly recommend you to try this place. You won't regret!

I stayed at the Sheraton recently while attending a conference. The proximity to the Convention Center and to Pike Place Market was a plus. The hotel is currently undergoing some renovations so the lobby is small and there was construction noise downstairs - but I couldn't hear the noise from the room. The room itself was fine but smallish. For the price, I have stayed in bigger places but I guess Seattle is expensive. The staff was pleasant but not over friendly.

If you haven't had the good fortunate to stay at Staybridge Suites - anywhere, do give them a try. They are such good value for money. Chose this one as we have stayed at Staybridge before but not in Jacksonville and as always it was excellent from check in to check out. You are made to feel so welcome and are instantly inundated with freebies - newspaper, appetisers, drinks, breakfast, complimentary use of business centre (no charge for printing) free use of launderette - there really isn't anything to spend your money on when staying at Staybridge. The location was superb, across the road from lots of restaurants-fast food outlets and a Publix where you can purchase your groceries and prepare them in your room as there is a kitchen with hob and microwave. The bed was so comfortable as were the pillows. - flat screen tvs, wifi - the list goes on.
From our personal expereience, I cannot say enough good things about this chain of hotels and if you do stay at Jacksonville and Billy is on reception, he will make it even more special for you.

The area is not the BEST, but not the worst. It's right in between a nice neighborhood (Nob Hill) and a bad neighborhood (Tenderloin) - we were told by a local is called TenderNob. Overall, I can't complain - I paid less than $--- to be right in San Fran.

I recently stayed at the Fairmont for my cousin's wedding. I have never been to San Jose before so I had no idea what to expect. I was breath-taken from the moment I drove up to the hotel. The doormen were friendly and very helpful. The lobby is gorgeous with marble floors and a fabulous lounge that makes you feel like you are sitting in your own living room. I had a room in their new tower, and all I can say is """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Wow!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The rooms was oversized and had all the extras I would expect from a luxury hotel (bathrobes, slippers, CD Player, etc). I didn't want to leave my room!
I am very surprised by the previous reviews, they don't sound at all like the hotel I stayed at. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone staying in San Jose. Everything I experienced was worth way more than what I paid, an absolute deal!

The Grand Hyatt is right in Union Square so you can't get a better location for sightseeing and shopping. The only problem is the hotel appears to be severely understaffed. I arrived at - pm on a Wednesday evening and there was only one front desk clerk. A large family was right in front checking in with lots of questions and issues. Seems like they have problems staffing according to load. I really enjoyed my stay at the Hotel Max. The staff were friendly and it was like staying in an art museum.

Apart from the great location, there isn't anything special about the Tribeca Grand. The rooms are the cramped standard fare for NYC. The beds were comfortable, but the room failed both in being comfortable and trendy. It was fairly bland and something you'd expect to see in the suburbs of a minor city. However, the toiletries were great and the staff were exceptional, going beyond the call of duty. The public areas of the hotel are fine, but tired in places. At the weekends the atrium bar can by noisy and this can be heard in the rooms. Overall, I would say this place is good if you're just going to be using it to sleep, but don't expect to want to spend much time in the room or the public areas.

When our family browsed the Salisbury Hotel's website we were impressed by several things - location, rooms and prices! The prices were very reasonable - which attracted us at first but it is very closely located to several main attractions.

The only problem I could see is that there were not enough elevators (they only had -) so you have to be patient sometimes as they would take awhile! This was a nicely decorated and well kept inn! The room was comfortable, especially the bed. We really loved the rooftop terrace. It was a great place to relax as we overlooked the market and the bay! The location of the inn was it's best feature! Right at Pikes Market! (Although we thought that the market wasn't as nice as we expected!) We didn't venture out after dark, though, as there seemed to be lots of sketchy characters around!! During the day we enjoyed walking everywhere, from the market to the downtown shopping areas! We enjoyed all the choices of food alongside the market...especially Beechers cheese store's macaroni and cheese!!!!!! Try It!!!! It's WONDERFUL!! In all it was a great place to stay!

My girlfriend and I decided to surprise our ---year-old daughter with a trip to Seattle for her birthday this last weekend. She had never been and we knew she would love it. I actually went on a hotel discount site and was given this hotel. I had been in the Portland location once and remember it being beautiful and have stayed at other Kimpton hotels and had great experiences. After receiving notice of our reservation I emailed their staff and informed them this trip was for a birthday and requested a room with - beds, hopefully towards the top. The assistant manager promptly replied and said that he could accommodate that request but the --bed options were lower and didn't have the best views. That night the hotel staff also left a note in our room with a birthday card for our daughter which included a free in-room movie rental as well as an invitation to call down for a complimentary birthday cake. We called down and they brought up a delicious personal-sized chocolate cake with ice cream and a candle in it. She was very excited!
Throughout our --night stay the staff continued to be amazing. We spent a lot of our time checking out Seattle attractions but each time we came back we were greeted warmly. There was a wine tasting each night in the lobby and the staff always offered to get my daughter a soft drink from the restaurant. There were bowls of chocolates around that we all enjoyed as well. 
If I had anything to add to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""con"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" side it would be that the views from this hotel aren't as attractive as some others I've stayed at in Seattle. It's only an ---story building and there are taller buildings surrounding it. If you're expecting a full city view or one of the water you may be disappointed. We also thought the cost of valet parking was a little much, coming to nearly $-- per night with taxes. I am sure this is on-par with other --star hotels but is pretty hard to justify. We opted to valet on Friday night but found street parking on Saturday night since parking is free on Sundays. 
Overall though, it was a great experience and I would highly recommend staying there. Even with getting our reservation through a third party site we were never treated differently and that says a lot about a place.

My husband and I went to Philly for a quick weekend get-a-way, and the Club Quarters was a great hotel for our needs. Yes, the rooms are small, but not smaller than most city hotels we have stayed in NYC or Boston. Perfect size for a couple, in my opinion. The room was clean and fresh, nice decor, and unexpectedly quiet. The bed, (the most important aspect of a hotel in my opinion) was sooo comfortable, and I am very picky. Water stations near the elevator were a great bonus on these -- degree days. The staff were very friendly and accommodating, (very nice restaurant recommendation-Ly Michaels) and we asked an employee in the hallway for extra pillows, which he went and got for us right away. Check-in was a breeze, and the lobby was very welcoming. We appreciated the computers with Internet access to check out directions and help plan our days, and my husband used it for getting info on Geocaches around the area. On the airplane to Philly, I prepared him for the worst after reading the reviews, but we were very happy with the place. Affordable, safe, and perfect location, I cannot think of anything negative except slow elevators during busy times of the day. We will be staying here again.

As a mother with a teenage daughter,this hotel was very safe and with very welcoming staff.
The room was very good and very clean having all what we needed . The free internet was an added value to our stay, the room service was quick and great. The reception desk staff was assisting and provided help as soon as was needed. Both our check in and out were quick.
You have help from the minute you drop off the taxi and onward.
Real value for money
It is definitely my hotel of choice in my next trip to NY.

Getting there: Getting here in a taxi from DCA was about $-- with tip. 
Room: The suite was as we requested and big enough for us and our teenagers . It was VERY clean. Housekeeping did a great job each day. Beds were comfy with plenty of choices of firm or soft pillows.
You also have a nice size refigerator which can make ice (lift the metal bar up to start making ice) and a cooktop but no oven. They have a regular toaster you can use but I wished they would have a toaster oven for those nights you crave cookies. If you go, there is a Subway nearby and they sell cookies. They also provide cookware and limited silverware, salt and pepper, plate, cups, etc. There is a dishwasher in the room too. There are two, big tvs. They are not HD LCD ones but the display was fine. 
Food: The free breakfast is average. If they read this review, please get a better waffle recipe. The one in the Joy of Cooking is pretty good. The coffee and service also needs to be improved. On two separate days, they ran out of coffee during breakfast. I've never had that happen at any hotel and no, I don't think they ran out because the coffee was so fabulous because it wasn't. The free evening meal is okay. You can eat it but it's bland. Examples of menu items are mash potatoes and meatloaf, tacos, chicken and dumplings, lasanga, deli sandwiches, puled pork etc. If you plan to eat back at the hotel for dinner, I highly suggest you show up before - p.m. as the food goes fast. They will still feed you something, but it may not be the menu item. They ran out one night so that's how I know this. 
Location: I agree with another reviewer. While they advertise they are two or three blocks from the metro, those are some long blocks, especially when you're tired at the end of the day. Don't get me wrong. They are walkable and the - block stroll to the White House is nice and we even walked to the Washington Monument on two separate days but if you're not into a lot of walking, then you will want to stay near metro center or the Plaza area where you're closer to a metro or one is right outside your door. Homewood also sits on a little hill so again, after walking all day on the mall, etc. and then a three long block walk back to the hotel and then that little hill up, it gets a little tiring. 
There is a CVS two blocks away so that was nice. Whole Foods is also close by. Keep in mind while the hotel advertises they do complimentary grocery shopping for you, they don't do it on the weekends, so if you arrive on any weekend day, you will have to walk to Whole foods or CVS to get your bottled waters or sodas. 
Actually, it isn't painful at all. It was a pleasant walk and we felt safe in the area.
Internet: We could never get the wireless to work , but thanks to other reviewers here, we packed an ecord and plugged up our laptop and were surfing in no time so don't leave home without a cord. 
 TV: There are only approximately -- channels. You DO NOT get Disney, Nick, Food, Bravo, Lifetime, TV Land, etc. You DO get History, ABC Family, Fox, CNN and the local ABC, NBC, and CBS channels along with BET and ESPN. 
Phone: Local calls are -- cents each so use your cellphone if you have one. 
Touring: While the hotel will tell you to use the double decker tour bus, it doesn't get good reviews on trip advisor. My best advice to you is to use the metro. It's not hard. I asked the info booth lady how to and she explained it to me once and I had it the rest of our stay. It was fast and easy and we never waited more than - minutes for a train. To get from the metro that is close to the hotel and to the mall is - minutes on the train. You will never get there that fast on a tour bus. It cost $-.-- per person on the metro during peak hours while the tour bus will set you back $-- per person for two days touring, but here's the thing, if you're going to be in Air and Space all morning and maybe another museum in the afternoon, why do you need a hop on, hop off. Take the metro to the mall. Go to one musuem, then cross the mall (short cross) over to the other museum. Then metro it back to the hotel for again $-.-- per person. If you go to the capital, Homewood is perfect. Walk three blocks and take the orange or blue line to capital south. Again, it's $-.-- per person. Come out of Capital south, turn left (or follow the crowd) and walk straight until you see a guard shack in front of the captial building. Look down and you will see the entrance to the visitor center. If you do the tour buses, they will drop you off in front of the capital and then you have a nice walk UP HILL all the way around the building to the backside where the visitor center is. Never mind during the summer, those tour buses are often full so when one finally arrives to pick you up, there may not be enough seats for your entire family to get on.
If you visit the capital, you can take the tunnel (as long as it's before -:--) over to the Library of Congress. Then when you're done, you take a short walk back to the metro's orange and blue line and back to the hotel. 
Capital South also puts you on the side where the senator offices are so it's easy to pop in to get a pass so you can watch congress in action. 
Do use Tour Mobile for your Arlington Tour. It's worth it. 
I also highly recommend doing a night tour because the tour buses do not leave you. You get so many minutes at each monument and then they move on. However, you can also see some monuments on your own. Head to the Washington Monument. Walk around the back of it. Look to your left and you'll see the Jefferson Memorial. Look to your right and you'll see the back of the White House. Look in front of you and you will see the WWII memorial and the Lincoln memorial. There is a path down to the monuments. Once you pass the WWII one, you can easily get to the other ones because they sit right there on the left and right. You won't see the FDR one though from here that I know of. 
Again, we walked to the Washington Monument from the hotel twice. I'm not a walker and even I didn't find it difficult in the mornings. The weather was perfect so it was a pleasant walk. 
Recommend: Yes, I do recommend the hotel because it's clean, rooms are big enough for a family of - to - (Per my teen, the sleeper sofa was fine), two tvs, free internet, close to the grocery, able to cook in room.

The hotel is nice itself, however, the room could use some updating. We stayed over vacation in March and enjoyed ourselves. The staff was good. The location is a good location, however, the location is in a rough part of town. Next door are some dance places for men. 
Overall, it was a good experience.

We stayed in Philadelphia for my Brothers graduation in the Month of May ----. For the -st two days we stayed in Residence Inn Marriott and the next two days we stayed here. This Hotel by Hilton is at a beautiful location and the suites were large enough for - people. We had our room at the --th Floor, and the view from above was absolutely awesome. The whole square lit up at the night and the view from above is beautiful. The staff seemed a bit arrogant initially, but later on it was ok, may be bad day sort of things.
Hotel was lovely, bed was very comfortable, shower was very big, free cookies and breakfast were delicious. And the shuttle did a great job of getting us where we needed to go.

It was weekday, and there were plenty of free street parking, just by the hotel...when we asked if its safe-ok to park overnight on the street, they said: we cant provide any information.. u better park in our parking.. --$ vs. Free on the street. After checking with few locals, decided to park on the street and that was a good choice

Central to the stunning LA Union train station and one of LA's sprawling Chinatowns but an expensive ($--US) cab ride from the international airport. My room was upgraded and was large with two double beds, a small table and chairs, a tea and coffee making area, a bathroom with a shower over the bath and a toilet with the handbasin outside the bathroom area. Breakfast is included and is plentiful but unimaginative (e.g. cereals, fruits, muffins, toasts, cold hard boiled eggs, juice). Staff friendly and helpful. Exterior tiles along access balconies very slippery in wet weather. Short walk to cheap restaurants and the beautiful train station.

We visited Houston twice this year to attend two weddings and stayed at the JW both times. As I researced hotels the JW was the best! The hotel itself was clean, modern and had most of the amenities you would expect from a four star hotel. Location is great with the Galleria mall across the street. The hotel car service was also very convenient and the Walgreens across the street....super convenient. Roof top pool was awesome and the gym offered headsets, cool bottled water and a BIG smile from the gentleman working the fitness center! I can't say enough about this hotel as I am extremely picky about where I stay! Chocolates on our pillows everynight...need I say more.

I stayed at Club Quarters in October for three nights. You can't really beat the location for easy access to the sights of D.C. It is two blocks from the White House and a short walk to all of the museums and monuments on the Mall. As others have noted, it is right above the Farragut West Metrorail station. You can take the train from Reagan National to the hotel for under $- compared to a $-- or $-- cab or shuttle. Be sure and take the --th Street Exit (towards the front of the train) and the hotel is right there.
I stayed on the second floor where the Club Room is. There are computers to print out boarding passes and coffee and fruit available as well as filtered water and a refillable bottles. You can order drinks and snacks from the Club Room as well in the evening.
I stayed in a standard room with a double bed. The room was clean and comfortable, but very tiny (almost dorm room sized). The bathroom only had a shower. Other than that, the room has the basics: free wireless Internet access, basic cable with HBO, in room coffee and a clock radio you can plug your MP- player into.
The hotel offers room service from the restaurant on the first floor, but you can also order off menus from several neighborhood restaurants and have it delivered to your room for a nominal $-.-- charge. 
My room faced Farragut Square so there was a great deal of street noise. I even saw what I think was a Presidential motorcade zooming up --th towards the White House.
If you want ice, you need to take the elevator to the lower level (only one of the two elevators goes there however). It is also the same level as the workout room. Be forewarned, there are only three machines in the workout room: a treadmill, a stationary bike and a stair machine. The hotel offers to deliver machines to your room, but I never tried that service. I'm not sure where they would put the machines, however, since the rooms are so small.
All in all, Club Quarters seems a fair value for business travelers, especially for D.C.

The hotel lobby was pleasant, and that is about where it all ended.
The room was tired, the mattress flat and hard, with linens and towels thin and scratchy.
Spent the night in Jacksonville to be fresh for the next morning's meeting, but this hotel was a poor choice. The breakfast was a nice feature, but did not make up for the poor room and quality.

I attended a conference near the convention center and this hotel was accessible via a free shuttle service from the conference. My first time in NY I stayed in Pod -- and, since it was a great experience, I decided to try the new Pod. Another great choice. Booked this hotel to celebrate my special lady friend's birthday. Front desk staff got things off to a great start by being friendly and attentive. I stayed here for a business trip and received a discounted price through the show that were attending. I am glad that we received the discounted price since I would have been severely upset at paying the full price for this hotel.  While I am sure that these issues were coincidental, they caused me to have a somewhat unpleasant stay at this hotel.

I spent two nights at this wonderful Kimpton property for a romantic getaway weekend. The staff were extremely friendly.
