We received a great rate for this hotel through expedia. I had originally booked a hotel downtown and I am so glad I changed to Hotel Palomar. We came to Dallas to shop on our way back to Australia and we wanted to experience NorthPark Center. It was any easy - stops on the DART and then a shuttle bus to get to NorthPark. The rooms at this hotel are very nice and we were given a room away from the freeway overlooking the pool. Unfortunately we didn't get a chance to experience the evening wine reception.

I stayed one week in this hotel to visit New York. Its location is fantastic, very close to Central Park and Rockefeller Centre, Grand Central Station is also easily reachable. The view from the room is as good as you can get from a hotel in New York. I payed around ---USD per night and it was well worth the price. The rooms are clean and have enough space if you're traveling solo or in a couple. The common areas are also very spacious and stylish. Staff was always very professional and friendly. All amenities that you expect are to be found in this hotel. Breakfast is good and with a large variety of choice. Can't tell very much about lunch-dinner since I didn't eat there. This is a very recommendable hotel.

We stayed at this hotel because our -- year old loves everything Hard Rock! Worst decision we have ever made. We arrived at -:--am and we couldn't even hear the person who was booking us in because of the loud music from the night club. Ridiculous location for the front desk. Once we got to our room we were up all night because they booked us right next to the party tent... lovely! The next night we were up all night because of the noise from the partiers all around us. I realize it's the Hard Rock Hotel but come on, if you are booking in a family, don't put them next to the party tent, put the -- year old there! I spoke with the Manager before he left and he was apologetic but couldn't comp us a night because be book through Expedia... ridiculous! He offered to set us up really well for next time but there will NEVER be a next time!!

This was our first visit to SF. And hopefully will not be our last. We fell in love with the food, the cable cars, the many vistas and the Arganout Hotel. What a great location for a first time visiters.

Do NOT GO HERE! I checked in on --------. The room was filthy. The halls smelled of urine and mold. When I got into my room...it looked NOTHING like the clean, cozy room they have in the photo. I had a cream comforter with blood stains on it! When I asked the front desk to please replace it....they told me they didn't have any replacements and they would just take our comforter away! The front desk was not accomodating at all and seemed agitated by my request to replace the blood stained duvet. Needless to say....I checked out immediately and found another hotel!

My wife and I stayed here while in town for a Rangers game due to its impressive rating on Tripadvisor (and we are Priority members). I do have to say we enjoyed the stay overall. Nice hotel in a nice area. It would have been nice to come back to the hotel lounge after the game and relax and have a drink but Saturday nights are hip-hop nights. We were aware of this and understand the hotel wanting to increase revenue so it was no problem. The problem lies with one of the bartenders (who unfortunately I did not get the name of-younger guy-short hair). I suppose since we were obvious """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""out to towners"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" or weren't Saturday night regulars then he need not worry about treating us like he cared if we were there or not. I am not going to say he ruined our trip, because we weren't going to let that happen, but he did put a damper on it. We will be coming back to the area in a couple of weeks for another game but will probably look for another hotel to stay at. There are lots of other choices and lots of other bartenders happy you are there and without the cocky attitude.

We stayed here for - nights to go to a Seahawks game and explore Seattle. We were very happy with our choice.
The FREE shuttle service was fantastic. It leaves the hotel on the hour and half hour and you call up the hotel to ask to be picked up when you're ready. We were able to take the shuttle to the stadium on game day which was incredibly convenient. It was about a ---- minute ride from the hotel to downtown.
Our room overlooked Lake Union and had a view of the space needle. It was comfortable and new. We didn't have any complaints about the heat, water, etc. Breakfast was standard but a nice spread for a free breakfast. The free parking was a nice plus as well. There were a few restaurants across the street overlooking the lake. We tried Joey's and enjoyed it - it was crowded on a Friday night but we didn't have to wait.
We would definitely stay here again.

I booked Hotel Felix as a package deal on Expedia with my flight to Chicago. The pictures looked great but I did read through reviews about the small rooms...paid extra for double beds since I was not traveling alone.
Location: First of all, the location of the hotel was great for us. It's very close to State Street, Magnificent Mile, etc. without being in the thick of it. It's just outside of those areas so you still have the peace and quiet of a quaint neighborhood. The hotel is also located within walking distance of many great eateries, Trader Joes, Whole Foods, a U.S. Post Office, etc. 
Cleanliness: Well this is where it lacked quite a bit. The cleaning service they did was...almost non-existent. The first day we checked in at about -:--pm, we were trying to catch some rest but the maid service kept banging on our door. We just checked in, we do not need service. Secondly, it seems like they do not know what a duster is - our room was filled with dust every day. There was one day where our room was not cleaned - we got back to the hotel at about -pm - suddenly a woman just lets herself in the room (no knocking) and quickly apologizes and closes the door (to be fair – there is a privacy lock and a secondary lock which we forgot to activate this night). I'll assume that was the maid...at -:--pm. 
I found hairs around the room of different colors so I knew they didn't belong to me. Overall - it just felt...unclean. I did notice a slight improvement at the end of the week when another maid was working the floor.
Room: As other reviewers have mentioned - the rooms are small. There is basically no closet. I lived out of my suitcases, the beds include two drawers each if you want to use it. We had a double room so we were fit in pretty tight. We were also placed on the third floor which gave us a nice view of a cement wall outside our window.
The walls are a bit thin. I knew when my neighbor was coming-going, taking a shower, etc. Luckily we were placed in the corner so I didn't have to hear too much hallway noise.
Microwave-Mini Fridge: NONE
Air Conditioning: I guess as a green hotel, their air conditioning units only allow for automatic settings. Our AC unit kept kicking on and off during the night - it was loud and got really hot in between the kick-ons. 
Bathroom: The bathroom is actually a good size. There is a complete lack of counter space which made getting ready a bit of a headache. The shower head was pretty weak and I didn't like that there was no bottom water spout...and the shower head was not one of those removable heads. 
Staff: I didn't talk much to the staff. When I checked in - the staffer had a bit of a speech issue and I had to keep having to ask him to repeat his question...and he finally snapped his question out. Wonderful, thanks for the welcome. Greetings back to the hotel were scattered and my check-out staff was cold and short. 
Internet: Free Wi-fi! This is definitely a huge plus for me. I had almost no issues with the wifi during this trip. There was one day where I saw a huge crowd checking in and that day, the internet was much slower...but all in all - it worked great! Loved having the free wifi.
Would I stay here again? I would consider it...it really wasn't too bad and I thought we got a pretty good deal on our stay. I don't know if I would highly recommend it to others.
Tip: If you have an iPhone - it's a god-send. The Yelp application helped us find some of the best eats!!

I stayed at the Pearl for - nights and had an excellent stay. I was by myself but for some reason was upgraded to a room with - double beds. It was a spacious room with a large bathroom. There was no tub but that's normal in New York and the shower was roomy. The room was clean and in good shape. It was also quiet.
Staff was very friendly and I was happy to share the chocolate dipped strawberries my wife had sent for Valentine's Day. The included breakfast was not overwhelming but was completely fine and satisfying.
The gym is quite small. It's very clean and in good order and bright. But there's not any room to lie on the floor or stretch. The equipment was all in good shape.
The location is great. It's close to Times Square if you like that sort of thing but not too close to it if you don't.
The free wi-fi was a huge plus.
I would definitely stay here again.

We were so thrilled with our stay at the Arizona Grand - we said to each other over and over we didn't think the staff could do a better job taking care of us. We were shuttled to our room, to the Rustler's Roost restaurant at the top of the hill (highly recommend by the way) and our luggage was shuttled back to the lobby when we checked out. They really try to take care of every detail. Our room was spacious and clean. Yes, they have old style tv's but with so much to do outside - why sit there and watch tv? The only complaint about the room is the pullout bed was uncomfortable. Also, they only gave us one pillow and a sheet for it when they knew we had two children. I didn't realize they didn't have a blanket until the next morning when they complained about how cold they got. Not good. 
We found the entire resort easy to navigate and signs everywhere telling you which was to go. 
The waterpark was so much fun - there is no way anyone got """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""bored after -- minutes."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" We saw people lined up an hour before it even opened so they could claim a good seat - that's how much fun it is. There are people who take the rafts and they think they own them for the day - there aren't enough for everyone to do this and it leads to lines at the lazy river and the wave pool as people are hoping to score on a raft. Meanwhile, there are rafts all over the park laying beside people's chairs as they claim them for the day (and then don't use them - running off to go down a slide,etc.). We just took those rafts off the empty chairs and used them and then left them in the water for others and I would like to see the park staff implement rules about that kind of thing. Just annoying and I shouldn't have to risk confrontation to get a park raft. 
There was an incident between two guests with one threatening the other. She was crazed and using profane language and the staff was quick to respond. She took off to hide but somehow they found her and as I was walking to my spa appointment - I saw her being evicted from the park. Good to know they take security seriously - especially with so many children there. 
The spa staff were professional and my massage appointment was on time and sooo relaxing. My husband played golf and also had a great time - said the course was perfect!
We ate at the Vista buffet on Sunday and oh - was it ever good! Even the kids had so much fun ordering omelettes and trying new food. There's lots of food and something to keep everyone happy. 
This was our first visit to the Arizona Grand and on the drive home we talked about how much fun we had and how we plan to make this a yearly adventure. Counting the days til next year! :-)

We have stayed here many times, and it does have an old fashioned feel, but it is elegant and feels like Europe in NYC. The rooms are bigger than most in the city, and the beds are comfortable. The location is central to everything and there are tons of places to eat nearby. I only wish they would not charge for internet and make breakfast a little more reasonably priced and I wouldn't seek an outside place. It is quiet considering the location, from outside noise, as well as room to room noise with large carpeted hallways. The rooms do have Nespresso machines, so that's nice addition too. I always check availability here first when coming to NYC. The people who work there are very helpful and professional. When you check in, you may meet Annmara at the desk, she's very nice and eager to help you check in-out and fill your needs.

A great hotel located on --th Street with Lexington. From the moment we pulled up to the minute we left the staff were really helpful.
The rooms are huge and so are the beds.
I thought it was good value for money, considering we arrived on New Years Eve I didn't think the price was too horrendous. Although I'd wish I hadn't fallen asleep at -pm and woke up at -am completely missing the celebrations!!
Not much else to say really, just give it a go you won't be disappointed!!

This is a big old hotel only - blocks from the city centre, cable car and shops. The metro from the airport stops right outside at Montgomery Station and is much faster and cheaper than taxis. 
There is a nice but expensive courtyard restaurant but I only had breakfast there once (--usd). There are plenty of places to eat and drink nearby. There is a little convenience store over the road.
My room was small but comfortable and many rooms just face inwards onto shafts so no view.
The pied piper bar is OK but I felt it was a bit dark with no windows. Bar meals are served. Annoyingly, the bar closes at midnight so we had to move on to the W Hotel to carry on until -am.
Much cheaper to book on line even if you have a discount code for a conference.

I booked a room here based upon good reviews in certain guide books and nice looking rooms on the hotel web site.
However, on arrival I was shown to a room with a badly stained carpet, rusty taps, peeling paint, broken tv, and a view of a brick wall. This place is a dump and should be shut down.
Breakfast and dinner are included in the room rate but unless you want to risk delhi belly then I would advise you to steer well clear.
I admit that it's cheap and the free internet access is great but unless you're really desperate don't even think about checking in here!

This is a beautiful hotel. The beds are an absolute dream. One of the best nights sleep I have had in a long time. The staff seem like they are one big happy family but work in a professional and very friendly manner. I will definitely return on my next trip.

My husband and I were there on Saturday May -th and checked out on May -th. The valet was the first person to address us and two of them were helping with bags. Very impressive. The next person was the concierge (Jackie). She was wonderful. She helped get us a porter to handle our bags and visited with me while my husband get our room. Our room was very nice. This is a very old hotel but is remodeled and is very nice. Our room was large for a older hotel and everything was spotless. The next morning when I went down for coffee I saw Jackie and she called me by name and even asked how our dinner was the night before naming the restaurant. She is by far the best concierge I have ever been around and we do lots of traveling. Great experience and great hotel.

I was planning my boyfriend's birthday weekend and looked up a lot of hotels. When I came across the Palomar hotel in chicago and read all the reviews and looked at all the info I could about this hotel it just seemed to fit!!! I joined the Kimpton inTouch and got a email asking if I wanted to upgrade for $-- more, sure why not! When I checked us in the lobby smelled fantastic and the decor was very beautiful, and that was just the lobby!! The sweet young girl who checked me in, informed me that they upgraded us again to even bigger room! She explained where everything was and gave us directions to our resturant for dinner. Right away I felt welcomed! When we got out of the elavator even the halls were amazing! We found our room and when we opened the door we were blown away!!! This was by far the most beautiful room I have ever stayed!! They even had a bottle of wine with a note that said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""For the Birthday Boy""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""! That made him and I feel extra special, like the hotel cared that it was his birthday. Beds were very comfortable and our stay was worth every penny!! We are still talking about the hotel a week later and already have planned on staying for our Anniversary!! Oh and the breakfast, YUM!!!

First off, I stay in many Coast Hotels as a business traveler. I have found all of the Coast Hotels to have excellent value and very good customer service. I can't comment on the price of the room at this hotel as this - night stay was done via points. What I can say is this hotel offers modern rooms and excellent service with some of the best front desk staff I have ever seen. Check in was less than -- seconds a very polite, not to mention that we were put on the top floor in a king size room which was more than I was expecting. I would rate the decor of the room and the comfort to be better than alot of higher end hotels.You wouldn't notice the difference between a - star hotel and this one. It is expensive to park in downtown Seattle as this hotel only offers Valet parking at --.-- a night but is less expensive than the Westin at almost --.-- night. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone who is looking for excellent value and close to shopping Pike Place Market etc. Next time I'm in Seattle this hote will hands down be my first choice!

Most of the place and amenities were average, but the big plus for us was the use of the fitness center right next to the hotel. It was not crowded and the staff and people there were very friendly. The place is not as popular as it used to be, but that made it easy for us to do what we wanted. They have indoor and outdoor pools, treadmills and elliticals, many, many weight machines and free weights. Not enough time to spend there.
The motel is set up as a convention center so the corridors were long and a bit confusing at first.
We got a good deal online, so we were happy with the whole thing.

Great location, close to the action but still far enough that you don't hear any noise. Close to great restaurants, shopping or simple leisure walks. 
Hotel is classy very helpful staff not crowded at all.

When I think DoubleTree I don't automatically think it's going to be all that nice. I booked the room purely based upon the other trip-advisor reviews and the great deal I got for paying in advance. However, I was pleasantly surprised when we arrived and saw the hotel. It was extremely clean, very beautiful with old moldings etc and, given how old the building was, the room was very large and had a great bathroom. The only thing I'd change is the lighting in the bathroom. It was very dark and hard to put on makeup.

Stayed here for - days. Decided to get the business --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" TV and got a pretty spacious room. Suspect by paying a little extra got a slightly bigger room which was more than adequate for the price and well worth it.
Location is extremely good. The only down side was that the toilet was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""wedged"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" against the wall meaning it was uncomfortable to use. Not sure why this was done as there was plenty of space to move it out a little.
Would stay here again.

I was a little worried about the hotel once I read the reviews. I shouldn't have been. Our room and bath were both wonderfully nice and spacious. The hotel is also in a great location. We were able to get everywhere we wanted to go quickly and easliy.
I have to say the best part about our stay was the staff. Especially Thurston at the bell desk! He and his co-work (John, I think) were so helpful and friendly. They made great suggestions for places to eat and made sure we were taken care of with transportation also. I travel a lot for business and these gentlemen are probably the NICEST hotel staff I have ever dealt with. 
Overall, we really enjoyed our stay and would go back to the Sheraton Gunter.

We stayed at this Hotel through a vacation package we bought with Sea World..Hotel is new and is a no smoking hotel , offers free breakfast and is only - mile from Sea World and they have a free shuttle form the hotel to Sea World and when your ready to return to the hotel..just call them and they are there in about - minutes..saves on the parking at Sea World and the walk from your car to the entrance. The staff was VERY friendly and helpfull.

I travel to NYC often and have tried a lot of hotels. The key to business travel is getting rest so that you can be ready for the pack jammed meetings and dinners. This hotel certainly delivers that, a big comfy bed, not noisy (one place I went to had club music every night until -am!), walkable to most areas, safe, clean (my housekeeper was awesome, organizing my mess daily and making sure I had products), really nice bathroom (the shower - I still dream about it - yes a place that actually gives you water pressure).
Now I look forward to my business trips.

This is my second time staying here (last time Feb ----). Had no problems that time so decided to book again. My parents were also travelling with us. My parents got a room in the main part of the motel. wooden floorboards, updated bathroom and they were impressed.
We, (family of -- husband, - year old and - year old) were placed in the old building on the side. We immediately were concerned and the age of the building showed. Our room was huge, which was appreciated as there were - of us and needed the space for a portacot. But the main concern was the bathroom. Nothing like the bathroom my parents had. First issue was the toilet didn't flush. I told my husband, a plumber, who fixed it straight away. I could maybe understand if something happened to the toilet during our stay but surely some basic checks when someone checks out of a room and it is cleaned would have uncovered a toilet that didn't flush. Should they rely on their guests informing them what does and doesn't work? We later were telling my parents about it and there were staff that my husband thought overheard. -- minutes later the handyman arrives at the door to put a new part in the toilet......
But the remainder of the bathroom was also questionable. The majority of the tiles on the floor were loose and the bathroom was so old and patched up.
The walls were also terribly thin and when i woke during the night i could hear the person next door storing.
I am sure that if my stay was in the main building I would have no complaints, because for the price the hotel is very good value. No concerns of safety or anything in the area. free parking (no issue getting a spot and stayed on friday and saturday), the breakfast was fine, free wi-fi etc. 
Just concerned about the inconsistency between rooms in the main part and the old building. The space of the room didn't compensate for the completely outdated and dodgy bathroom. If you are charging the same price you should have the same standard across all rooms.

The property is elegant, beautifully restored, the staff were friendly and efficient, the room was not particularly large, but spacious and well-appointed. There is free internet (big on my list), coffee, and even a big bowl of Bit-o-Honey at registration. Not much bad I can say – except … 
I was offered, and opted for, a city-view room, which I was forewarned was a bit noisy due, in particular, to the trolley system that runs through town. Little did I know, that would be the least of it.
After a nice dinner with a colleague at the hotel restaurant, the Italian one (quite good for a chain), I removed the ---- pillows from the bed and tucked in. the noise was, indeed, sleep-disrupting, but it had nothing to do with the sounds o’ the city. The guy (I assume it was a guy, though I really can’t be sure) in the room next to me was snoring so audibly as to be heard through the walls, and, ultimately, through the pillows (thankfully there were plenty of them) that I piled on my head. To no avail … I could not get the din sufficiently muffled to induce slumber (and I am not a particularly light sleeper) - this was some kind of all-penetrating sound that the military might want to explore. 
I was surprised at first that walls of such an old well-constructed property would be so thin. But then as I reflected more (I had a lot of time for reflection, not sleeping and all …) I figured that this could not be the hotel’s fault. This guy was a world-champion snorer. He had the full gamut of sounds, gasps, wheezes, gulps, chainsaw, tuba, freight train … you get the idea. A breathe right nasal strip was not going to cut it for this guy … he was a serious candidate for laser-assisted uvulopalatoplasty (no, not a doctor, I googled that), which, I think, is like the rotor-rooter of the nasal passages. When he actually did stop for a minute or two, I became fearful that he had expired from obstructive sleep apnea. My fears were soon allayed as the orchestra began a-new. The passing trolleys provided enough of a respite for me to ultimately catch a wink or two. 
So, well, this is not an indictment on the hotel … it is fine. But I know from nearly -- years on-the-road that every once in a while there is an experience so ‘interesting’ it negates the comfort of even the most luxurious hotel. My employer is undoubtedly happy – I got a lot of work done in eight hours of not-sleeping.

We stayed here for three nights, during the middle of the week. We knew we wanted to be near the middle of the city-downtown area, and in walking distance to basically everything. To begin with, the parking structure is right next door; was very easy to self-park and bring the ticket with you to the counter. We had requested an early check-in (-:--), if at all possible, and only had to wait about -- minutes for them to finish preparing the room, which gave us time to walk around a bit in the neighborhood. Everyone at the front desk was friendly and helpful. Actually - all employees of the hotel are friendly and helpful, and are always available to answer any questions. The room was amazing! Corner room, with a view down Broad Street-Avenue of the Arts - directly towards City Hall! Two beds, with a sleeper sofa, desk area, dresser and TV; plenty of room for our family. Everything is very clean and kept up well. We had some appetizers in the bar area; great service (loved Jarrell a-k-a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Big Baby""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""!!). When we asked, the hotel recommended a few area places for breakfast; they do serve breakfast on the mezzanine level, but we also wanted to try local places also. Our family would stay here again, and would recommend this hotel to anyone and everyone. Trying to figure out a reason to visit Philly again so we can stay here!!
Hated the location. Hated the pseudo-hipster vibe (in New York? are they kidding?) Friends dropped off a package and I never got it. Nobody was polite at the front desk.

Fantastic location within walking distance to just about everything. Traveled out - miles by bus then walked back. Hotel concierge was very helpful in selecting dining locations and all were above expectations. Bedrooms were ample in size and comfort. Bed linens were fresh each day and the room tidy and restocked appropriately. Room service was fast and the food above average. Enjoyed the sitting area near the bar with the fireplace and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""table service"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" from the bartender. Friendly staff. Excellent breakfast bar but a bit pricey. My husband and I would happily stay here again and recommend it to any traveler. One drawback was the significant walk from the elevator to our room. If walking is a problem, travelers should specifically ask for rooms closer to the elevator. But, that's a nit when you are away from home for vacation. Great hotel.

This hotel has the standard amenities and decorations, layout, etc. consistent with the brand. In reviewing the increasingly standardized properties of international brands, many aspects of the usual reports are predictable or otherwise commonly known.
Some points particular to this property include staff, location, and those points stemming from such factors.
Staff: The staff members were each and all very friendly and efficient. The cleanliness of the room and upkeep of the interior are further evidence of capable and attentive staff. My bill, including tax free application, was correct and in order.
Location: Though the city is relatively small, and distance to downtown is not many miles, drive times are lengthened by traffic. Austin’s good economy has attracted job seekers, some of whom are from out of state—which means non-Texas drivers. Apparently, some states do not encourage slow drivers to move from the left lane and officers fail to ticket lane changes devoid of signal. Overall, traffic is the main detraction to this location. Grocery stores and restaurants are very close, but it seemed like nothing within walking distance was particular to Austin (chain restaurants and the general pub), and the ease of finding the hotel being due to proximity to the airport and highway meant walking anywhere in the area would not be easy.
If you are looking for a good deal and comfortable lodging for business, I would recommend this property. Low rates, clean facility, and competent staff make this a good choice when spending your company’s money. If you’re in the area for a family trip or for fun, I might seek something more closely situated to downtown and signature Austin restaurants and activities. Parking downtown is not difficult, but if you have to walk several blocks from parking to your destination, there are properties where you could do this without first driving downtown and paying for parking. Also, if you planned to bar hop, why not be able to walk or take a much cheaper cab ride? If you did stay at this hotel with family though, you would be pleased to find clean, working refrigerator and microwave appliances in the room. And the refrigerator is actually empty, allowing you to put things you bring into it.

I was a little hesitant to book a room here after reading the reviews, but decided that the location would make up for any problems. A year ago I stayed downtown and was very unimpressed with one of the five stars.
The reception I received was very nice. The staff at the desk were very helpful and answered all of my many questions pleasantly. They even did some investigation for me when I asked about a specific church (where my parents were married -- years ago). My blind father and I were given a rather nice room, and the bathroom was HUGE! We had a small coffee maker and a refrigerator. The room was clean. The decor is definitely old, but charming. The beds were comfortable and clean. I was very pleased not to have feathers in the room (allergy which I made note of on my reservation). We had many channels on the TV to choose from. We did not need to use the window air conditioner.
Breakfast was FREE . . . and, considering, not bad. It is a self-serve style buffet. If you want eggs, bacon, waffles, etc., they were available, but you had to microwave them yourself. Bagels, muffins, donuts, cereal, coffee, tea, juices, etc. were all there for you. The breakfast room was very pleasant and clean. The attending staff were pleasant. I accidentally dropped a whole cup of juice . . . they rushed over to clean up my spill and just would not hear of it when I tried to clean it up myself.
Fresh fruit was available in the lobby -- hours-day, along with coffee and tea. Cookies were available in the afternoon.
Internet access was available . . . free connection in the lobby, a free computer also available. I don't understand why internet access in the rooms incurred a charge.
All staff were aware that my dad was blind, and they were very kind and helpful when he was navigating the hotel alone.
Parking was right outside the lobby door, and a back-up garage was available if the parking lot was full. I did not need to use the garage. 
Sadly, this hotel is scheduled for demolition in three or four years and will probably be replaced with something outrageously expensive. 
Overall, this hotel was just what we needed. Not fancy, but nice people, clean surroundings, safe, and in an excellent location.
Customer service is so bad in a city with plenty of great hotels,

OK, so this isn't the Waldorf Astoria...it's not supposed to be. But the location is PERFECT for anyone heading out on one of the vessels at the Landings right there practically in the parking lot!
The rooms were clean, roomy and just perfect for the night! If you're heading out do do some deep sea fishing from H&M Landing...this is the place to be! 
I had called after making my reservation to change it to a handicapped room, as I had to bring my daughter at the last minute, and they were very accomodating. The hadicapp room was perfect for us!

Stayed at the Paramount in late July. While the hotel was clean and the staff friendly, I was disapppointed in the lack of amenities. Knowing NYC hotels, some offer more than others. This hotel does not offer any extras and the price is definitely high. It would have been nice to have a fridge-coffee maker available. Going out for coffee at seven AM over to the nearest Starbuks - - blocks away is not my idea of a relaxing AM and getting ready to go places. You could pay extra for the breakfast pkg, but adding $-- more to an already expensive room was a little much. Also, there was not much of a lobby and the lounge and bathrooms there are not much. -The alleged view was pretty much non-existent, our room, despite being on the -th floor, overlooked neighboring buildings that obstructed most of the view. 
-Mattresses are brand new (according to their tags) but both me and my friend found them uncomfortable due to firmness. This is more subjective though.
-I would disagree the location being good or great. The neighborhood was not re-assuring at night. I would not walk there alone and I'm a guy. Would I return to the Mayflower? Possibly If nothing else was available. Based on what I experienced, I can understand why people on a budget like it. If you're like us and like your comfort and convenience location-wise, they are wiser options.

This will be my hotel of choise for future trips to Dallas.

My family stayed at the Red Roof Inn from August -- - --, ----. The staff was very friendly and our room was very clean. Our room had two double beds, desk, two chairs, flatscreen TV, closet, in-room safe, in-room coffee, ironing board-iron, hair dryer and - drawer dresser - plenty of room to unpack our clothes and store in the dressers and put the luggage in the closet. We used the free internet in our room with our ITouch which was handy. When I needed to send a longer email, I would used the internet near the lobby for a nominal fee. The continental breakfast was basic (juice, coffee, bagels, pastries, bananas, apples, yogurt, oatmeal, cereal, toast) and the breakfast room can accommodate about -- - -- people at a time. A few mornings, I used the tray in the room and obtained breakfast for our family and we ate in the room. The location is excellent - --nd St (very close to -th Ave) in Koreatown which is a street full of Korean restaurants and is always busy. I returned by myself around midnight on Saturday night by bus (I'm female) and I felt very safe walking down --nd St to the hotel because of the activity. I would stay at this hotel again; however, I would also consider the Hampton Inn on --st St. My daughter and her three friends stayed there and this was also a great hotel - very tiny rooms (no dresser thus no place for clothes); better continental breakfast with hot buffet items and larger breakfast room; free internet in the lobby; and friendly staff. Their location was fine but their street was very quiet and as a Mom, I wouldn't feel comfortable if one of them was walking by themselves on the street - no activity on the street. Both the Red Roof Inn and the Hamption Inn offered excellent rates at $----night and are great places to stay.

We recently stayed here for a couple of nights and it was ok! It has a beautiful lobby and bars and it is in a perfect location. What I found a little odd was the breakfast was only available in the lobby area !! not what I was expecting at all. When we eventually got the attention of the waiter he was fine, only we waited over ten minutes for him to finish his conversation with other members of staff before coming to serve us!! not good . Another review commented that the staff always refered to them by name and went out of their way to help, I have to say no member of staff ever referred to us by name or were overly helpful , although they were polite which is way better then the last hotel we stayed in in new york.We paid $----.-- a night for our suite which , i think, in hindsight was way too much . We was expecting something amazing , we got something nice but certainly not amazing.

You will either love or hate this hotel....depending on your taste. If you like classic, flowery, Baroque style accommodation look elsewhere, if you are into minimalism, dark wood and white - then you'll appreciate it lots!
It is stunningly modern, has small but pristine rooms with many nice touches, a superb --th floor terrace and a tasty canteen style restaurant which serve great food.
This was our second stay in the Hudson and paid the extra to stay in a Superior room, this is really worth it, the room was on the corner with stunning views over NYC.
The location of of the hotel is perfect with many subway stops in close proximity, enabling you to go anywhere easily.
When in need of a hotel, I will always stay in the Hudson.

We stayed here last weekend and were given a nice room with a harbor view. We were on the pool floor (-th floor) and it was so convenient to the pool and the outside huge patio that also overlooked the harbor. When I stayed here with my husband in January ---- and it happened to also be my birthday they upgraded us to the Presidential Suite. It made that day the best birthday of my life!! It's a convenient walk to Camden Yards, Little Italy, and two Irish Pubs!!

If I had to sum it up in a sentence, I'd say this property is more like what I'd expect from a suburban Marriott, maybe near a hospital somewhere, not a metro business hotel. Nothing awful, just older style, outdated decor and small rooms with dark faux wood furniture and a generally tired feel. And, for other Platinum (or Gold) members out there, the tiniest concierge lounge I've ever seen in a full-service Marriott. Very nice - if slightly over-solicitous - concierge, but the poor thing must be bored rigid most of the time, as it's not a lounge guests are going to choose to linger in. I'd say they've done the best they can with the space they have.
The staff throughout the hotel are lovely and happy to help, but I wasn't inspired to use the hotel services much. I had a couple of room service dinners (adequate but pretty basic) but in the end I'd sum it up this way: This place is somewhere you sleep, not somewhere you live. Unlike other Marriotts, which are just more, well, inviting.
Everything was clean, but there were a few maintenance issues. The sink in my bathroom could not be plugged - the whole mechanism was loose. The towels - of which they only provide two instead of the usual four - were small and a bit harsh. Daggy drapes and older style wallpaper and carpet, but for a business trip it was perfectly adequate. Just not luxurious or 'lovely', as I'd describe many Marriotts.
If you want to go to the Galleria (the very upscale shopping mall near here) there is a hotel shuttle at prescribed times, every couple of hours. I chose to walk (about -- minutes along major roads), and it was do-able but not """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""closeby"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" as the website may lead you to believe. And if you need a taxi for a business meeting or other appointment, be aware that they do not hold cabs at the hotel. Allow an extra ---- minutes for a cab to be called and arrive.
In my experience and in reading other reviews on Trip Advisor, most of the major hotels in Houston don't do much better than this despite city prices (although my weekend nights were only $--, a fairer price I thought). It was perfectly adequate and I'd stay here again if I was only here for a few days, but any longer and I'd probably try another venue.

If square footage matters to you, then the Chancellor might not be your first choice. But if you are looking for a clean, comfortable room close to many attractions and transportation at an excellent rate then there is only one choice. From check-in to check-out the folks at the Chancellor were great. The room is modest in size, but really all you do is sleep, and queen beds are pretty much the same size no matter where you go. 
One simple thing they have are great windows. With them closed they block almost all street noise, the only noise that got through was heavy street grinding that was happening down the block. We might not have even noticed it, but we enjoyed leaving the window open at night (for safety it only opens a little) and listening to the sounds of San Francisco as we went to be each night.
This is a great place to stay if you want a good value close to everything, but not if you are after a cookie cutter room (for twice the price) of the big chains.

Price wise is the chepest you can get for this class in the downtown core. Staff wise, they are friendly enough to upgrade me to a better room after my complain. is clean, the location is excellent, price is reasonable, it got everything with the exception of free wifi.
Pros:
- Reasonable Price for the area
- excellent location (right next to --nd st subway station)
- friendly staffs (most of them)
- room clean and tidy
Cons:
- even on --th floor (where my room was located), street traffic can be very loud, loud enough to affect sleeping quality. Police Station is right next to it, you can hear cops cars go by every hour.
- I don't know who designed the doors, but whenever someone is closing the door, it creates a LOUD bang. very annoying.
- if you're staying at the lower floors, rooms are very small. (but i wasn't)
- lobby are often over crowded with people.
- terrible restaurant they have.
- lack of parking

Disappointed in my experience here - a hotel trying to compete with luxury chains that just doesn't get it.
-- Booked a room with a view on a high floor. Got a room on a low floor. They didn't bother to refund the difference ($---night) until I asked.
-- Booked a non-smoking room and it stinks of smoke.
-- Service is mediocre -- nobody answers at the front desk. Though some individuals try to be helpful.
Overall I would not recommend.

The Hotel was absolutely fabulous!! It was extremely clean & had a beautiful view of the City including the Historic District!! Was close to everything we needed to go to and I would definitely recommend this Hotel to anyone who has to stay in Philly!! Oh yea, right next to the Stadium too if you want to walk to the game!!

The rooms are separate from the reception-check-in area, as is the outdoor pool and exercise room. When we stayed there, the exercise room was dirty and in the back of the building; although it looks as though (from the website) that it's been remodeled. Our stay was comfortable, the bed was the comfiest bed (at a hotel) that I've ever slept in. The reception area is very comfortable with a fish tank, revolving colored lights in back of the desk, and plenty of chairs for the weekend overflow of guests at breakfast. The breakfast room is small and the chairs are uncomfortable, so aim for a nook. The continental breakfast is similar to other hotels, but in a confined space. We opted for the shuttle service one time on our stay and they were late going out (one other couple missed their dinner reservations and we missed a museum show) and late picking us up. Although if you want to explore Seattle more and get a glimpse of the city, it's a perfect idea.
The hotel is located near the highway, so location is nice and there's a mall nearby. Although the hotel is backed by apartment complexes and the outdoor pool is right next to a person's home.

For many this hotel may be a little out of the way. I prefer being out of the crazy part of any city but the Fairmont is still close enough to walk to Millennium Park, Navy Pier the Financial District as well as a variety of restaurants. Getting deep into the downtown area was a quick - dollar cab ride or a ----- minute walk. The view from my room was wonderful, I could see the lake from the --th floor and overlooked a meticulously groomed park, located between beautiful luxury high rise condos. The room was very clean and well decorated. The bathroom was big. The attention to detail, provided by the staff was top notch, I received - star service! The restaurant was good, there are many other restaurants that are better in the area but once again the service made eating in the hotel a very nice experience. Compared to most hotels the in room coffee was good and there was plenty, they provided a variety of tea as well. It seemed if I ran out of coffee, if I just walked out of the room and came back the coffee was replenished and the room was tidied up for me. Every day around -pm, I was visited by the staff that offered me water and ice. The bed was extremely comfortable! The only downfall is the lack of a pool to cool down with on hot summer days. 
I was on business, it was my birthday, the staff brought a wonderful cupcake that was beautifully decorated with chocolate drizzle and fresh berries, around the rim of the plate the chocolate drizzle spelled “Happy Birthday”, it was a wonderful small gift from the hotel.
The valet staff was very helpful, kind and pleasant to talk with. 
Many hotels are stuffy and overly arrogant, I found this to be a comfortable stay that was more like being home. I would definitely stay at the Fairmont again and would recommend it to anyone that would prefer to stay in a mature hotel full of helpful staff.
I have stayed in hotels from Beijing to NY, this was one of my favorite hotel visits.

Four friends had a special birthday reunion in DC and after much research decided to stay at Hotel George because of past great reviews and because it was perfectly located for sightseeing. It could not have been more perfect. Michael, the majordomo at the George, gave us a very warm welcome, made sure our rooms were exactly as we wanted and was a font of information. As a Kimpton Hotel, the decor was upbeat and the rooms were well furnished and very clean. Food and service at Bistro Bis, the hotel restaurant, were excellent. We stayed four nights and wish we could have stayed longer.

Alright, I'll just say it: its not the best hotel out there. ITs in a pretty good location however. ITs right on the boardwalk and the boardwalk goes everywhere! i was there in march and the weather was great so there were people everywhere, including the homeless men. our room was on the second floor, and right across from a public bathroom. 
it wasnt a nice welcome on saturday night when the drunk homeless men sat in there screaming for hours. it really made my mom angry. the room size is typical of that of a hotel. bathroom was fine, everything was very clean. if you stay here, you MUST go down to the little cafe in the lobby and order a chocolate chip muffin....they are the BEST i've ever tasted. im trying to figure out where they get them. for the price, the hotel's alright.

I have stayed at this hotel several times since it became a Hilton in ---- (the NY office of my company is nearby) I have always found it to be clean, comfortable with very good service each time I stay here. (Excellent, fast room service, a great cheeseburger and fries for nights when you are too tired to leave the room!)
Some rooms are on the small side so try and upgrade if you can, though since becoming an Honors Member, I've found they usually put me in a better room upon check in anyway. 
Hotel is very charming (not a mega Hotel as you may see elsewhere) and has a boutique, personal feel to it. I highly recommend it.
Note, this hotel is off -nd avenue, Midtown East is extremely quiet after business hours so you won't find many shops or activities open at night. However, it's a short walk to Grand Central and many subway lines. 
I've always had a very very pleasant experience at the hotel and it has become my hotel of choice when Im in Manhattan.

We just stayed on an overnight layover... but the property was beautiful... and the room was great... the coffee maker leaked and was crazy but other then that.. a nice property. They did though charge its guests $--.-- to use the gym.. and charged for wifi... I think that was really cheap of them..

I've stayed at several Garden Inns and this is one of the best. The rooms have high ceilings, which given them a more luxurious feeling, and are nicely decorated. The staff was great and very accommodating. The hotel is close to the airport and was convenient for my early morning departure.

We stayed - nights at the Dolphin Motel and we will definitely stay there again. Yes, the rooms are TINY but spotlessly clean. The staff is outstanding and went above and beyond to make sure we were comfortable and had everything we needed. The continental breakfast every morning was a plus and it was great to be able to go downstairs and bring coffee, fruit and yogurt back to the room. This place definitely earns it's rating as one of the best budget priced motels in San Diego!! BTW we got the recommendation from Trip Advisor. This website is very valuable.

I have taken a group here twice--once in April ---- and again in November ----. The hotel has made significant upgrades. The rooms are newly furnished in a simple, tasteful, and comfortable manner. They are small but quite adequate. Breakfast is very good with plenty of hot and cold options. Most of all, the staff is friendly and extremely accommodating and helpful. They took care of my group's special needs with good cheer. I can only say positive things about this hotel--great value in an excellent location. Why stay somewhere that charges almost double the rate? You won't be sorry if you have a group or are traveling alone or with family for business or pleasure.

My husband and I booked a room at the here after receiving many emails and snail mail publications advertising how fantastic the newly remodeled Public Hotel is; and the price was so reasonable we couldn't pass it up. We live in Chicago and were hoping to have a quiet night away from the kids. Upon arriving at the hotel it seemed pleasant, a bit hip on the style, but the crowd that was hanging out in the lobby was definitely carrying AARP cards. The rooms are very small and very stark. The heating system was extremely loud, but it came in handy when we were trying to go to sleep and needed to drown out the noise from the adult movies which seemed to be on continuous play all night long in the room next door. At - in the morning we were awoken by voices that sounded like they were in our room but they were coming from the adjoining room which we had a door to within our room and you could see light coming thru the room. We started talking ourselves and I think we shocked the new arrivals b-c they were a little quiter after that, but you definitely could hear everything thru the walls. I did call guest services to complain and they were helpful, but it was such a bad experience that by that time we were wishing we had just stayed at home. 
If you are looking for a quality hotel to relax in this is not your place. If you are looking for somewhere to stay so you can enjoy-party in Chicago's nightlife and don't care about luxury or noisy neighbors you would be fine to stay here. We won't be returning.

I stayed at this hotel for a business conference. I wanted to come in a day early so I could take a non-stop flight, so I had to by an extra night stay on my own dime. The hotel wanted $--- after taxes for one night. No way!!! Instead I paid $-- and stayed in a full suite at the country Inn & suites - which was a far better hotel & experience.
The Marriott is indeed right in the middle of the airport, so location is definitely a plus. Everything is dated. I brought my family along for the trip, so they tried to enjoy the amenities. The pool was disgusting when we arrived. I requested it be cleaned, and it was not cleaned until - days later! The hot tube smelled funny and had greasy hand prints all over it. They did clean the hand prints off with a towel, but it still stunk. Without a sanitary pool, my family resorted to riding the subway tram for entertainment. Surprisingly, it was actually pretty fun and relaxing to do at night when there weren't many people using it.
For conferences, the hotel was a logistical nightmare. The elevators are the only way to access the room floors or the upper level conference rooms. The staff locked out the elevators so they only went from ground to the upper level when our classes changed out. So if you happened to be on your room level, you were out of luck going anywhere because there were no elevators for the next -- minutes.
As for the beds, they were extremely cheap and I slept horribly. At least there weren't bed bugs though, if that counts as a plus. 
Other than the fact that the pool was not cleaned in a timely manner, the staff was very attentive and friendly.
I'll end my review with a positive note: the food here is very, very good. We had buffet meals at every meal time and one formal sit down dinner as part of the conference, along with full snack spreads at every break. I also ordered room service for my family one night while I was at the conference dinner. Simply put, the food was out of this world. I read a review here on tripadvisor that said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""eat here, but don't stay here"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I fully agree with this.
My overall recommendation is to NOT stay at this hotel unless you absolutely have to. There are tons of far cheaper and far nicer hotels very close by that offer prompt and free shuttle services.

We stayed for two nights. We were impressed by the size of the room and the modern decor. On closer inspection, you see it's an old property that has been nicely camouflaged with modern fixtures. The furniture is quite old but has been painted black to make it sleeker. The bathroom is functional but really basic. The heating- AC should be in a museum. We stayed during the week that it was really hot (--s) and it was impossible to sleep from the noise that infernal machine made, it was like having a drill going off every -- seconds. We finally had to shut it off and endure the heat just to get some shut eye. The room was pretty clean. Overall, it was fine and if we had gotten a better deal (less than ---$-night), we would have been pleased. Next we're in NYC, we will look for something that is better value.

I got the room at a fair price (under --.-- per night). It was a clean but very small room, with a horible view. It had a fridge, safe, microwave, coffee maker and an Iron. 
So while it wasn't fancy, it was a good value! My one complaint, the $--.-- charge for parking was a real ripoff!!

After much deliberation and internet research we decided on the Rivington and weren't disappointed. Theres so much choice, Gansevoort, Hudson, Mercer but the views are unbeatable at the Rivington, rooms are a good size and as a visitor you will get to experience the lower east side - very cool area. We always favoured the west village and meatpacking, but this has lots of hip quirky bars - restaurants which we wouldn't have found had we not stayed in a new area.
Its pricey but definitely worth paying more for a high floor. We had a corner suite so loads of space. (good wardrobe space too). Waking up to clear blue skies and Manhattan sky line is amazing and showering with a view of the empire state is awesome.
We would definitely stay again and will recommend to friends, but ask for the highest floor possible. 
Minor negative - the rubbish is collected at about -am and its pretty noisy (for about --mins). Its in a cool neighbourhood, in the early hours bars and clubs close so people are on the streets, which is noisy so could annoy some. 
Staff were really friendly and helpful, and a complimentary breakfast in an NYC hotel is always welcome for the mornings when Pastis is chocca!
Was clean, but when rooms were filled, internet was extremely slow. Rooms were quite small, too. The kitchenette was well furnished.

Got booked into the Whitcomb for a business meeting at the hotel. Obviously an historic hotel, all you have to do is look at it. Turned the a-c on in my room and thought the outside wall was going to crumble from the vibration. Funky smell all over the hotel. Food at b'fast was okay, though no choice for the American. Lunch was better. Service in the conference room was okay, though internet wifi was spotty. Staff tried hard, but the building was a challenge.
Neighborhood was pretty grim - lots of homeless folks and NOWHERE to eat except a subway and burger king outside the hotel.

Stayed - nights. Clean, basic accommodations. Twin bed (just me), flat screen TV, sink in the room, a basket of towels with soap and shampoo. Yes, the bathrooms are shared. For me, no problem because I was never in the room, instead, out exploring NYC. Would recommend for """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no frills"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" travelers. Convenient to everything!

Stayed November -,-,-, ----. I've stayed here before in ---- so I knew how to find it again and what to expect. Rooms are pretty plush and staff swift and attentive. It's certainly handy for the waterfront and Battery Park for statue of liberty. On a good day the view from the Concierge lounge is excellent. Parking is arranged just round the corner and getting forgotten items out of the car is no problem. The cocktail lounge provides excellent meals if you get stuck in a big queue for Roys rest at the rear of the hotel. Roys is first class cuisine and service, no need to step outside the hotel for anything, but Century -- is about - minutes walk away.
Subway at Rector Street about - minutes walk away, taxi rank ouside the hotel never seemed to be empty. Pricey I think by UK standards but service standards are soooo much better in NY Arrive Saturday of Sunday you may be able to negociate a weekend rate if your stay extends into the next week. Hard by the WTC site so overview of ground zero from upper floors with the repairs still taking place on adjacent buildings. Good view of the city by night from upper floors as well. Swimming pool on floor - a must! One annoying problem, if you book by Internet as a couple with different names, they divide the bill between the two of you with one bill each! Just how daft is that?

This property definitely needs an updated review, and I have it! 
My husband and I were nicely impressed by this motel. We arrived in Dallas early in the morning, and check-in was not until - PM, but, wanting to make sure we knew how to get to the motel, we went ahead and drove over there. 
The first thing we checked out was the neighborhood, since we saw a warning about it in a review from back in ----. Neighborhoods apparently change greatly over - years – it seemed like a nice place, with no “weird” people or happenings going on in the area. You might expect a lot of “seedier” people to be hanging around here, just because it is a much more inexpensive motel, but I did not see anyone or anything that would fit that description.
From the outside, the motel looked very nice and well-kept. This is definitely an older property, but it is obvious that La Quinta has gone a long way to keep it up. The pool was very small, but it looked clean (we never used it - too busy).
We wanted to go the Dallas Farmer’s Market, which we had directions to, but we needed directions to a bank first, so I went inside to ask for directions. The front desk clerk was immediately friendly and extremely helpful. She looked up directions for me on Google Maps and even printed them out for me. When I asked about check-in time, she informed me that she had rooms available right then, if I wanted to go ahead and check in! Of course, I did! The clerk gave me a nice, friendly welcome to this motel.
We nearly froze when we walked into our room – a nice surprise, since that meant the air conditioning definitely worked, although we made sure to warm it up quite a bit. The beds are smaller queen beds – but plenty roomy enough for everyone to fit. The -nd bed is right next to the a-c unit, but that is to be expected in a motel room. In other words, this is not the Hilton – don’t expect to have all the room of a house! That said, we found we had plenty of room, and we definitely had to take up room, what with our toddler’s play pen (plenty of room to open it up and not trip over it), the surprise refrigerator, and all of our clothing-suitcases. The vanity area is quite large by motel standards – there was more than enough room for me to set up the motel-provided ironing board with a walkway to the bathroom. There is even a closet with folding doors for your hanging clothes. That is where you will find the iron and ironing board.
The best thing about our room: Everything was Clean!!! I have stayed in many motels, and I often find dead bugs around the corners of the room (a hazard of having the door lead directly outside, I suppose, and a cleaning staff that doesn’t work so well). At the La Quinta Inn Dallas-East, however, I did not run into that problem! There were no bugs there for me to worry about my toddler picking up before I find them!
Yes, this motel is right off the highway (I---), so you will hear some highway noise, but it was very muted and did not bother us at all. Someone previously mentioned a train being nearby, but we never heard nor saw any evidence of that. Our room was very quiet.
Although on the map this motel seemed a bit “off-the-beaten path,” it is amazingly close (considering the size of Dallas) to most of the things we wanted to visit, like the Farmer’s Market and Fair Park. There are plenty of places to eat or get to supplies in the immediate vicinity, including a Denny’s and Exxon basically in the same parking lot, a McDonald’s, Walmart and Staples across the highway (easy to get to because of the set-up of the streets), etc.
If you want a nice, inexpensive place to stay, that’s fairly close to most tourist attractions, I would most definitely recommend this La Quinta Inn!

This is a very new and clean hotel with great amenities. The room was very nice; the fitness and business center were excellent; the breakfast and dinner were top notch.
However, what is most important is the professionalism of the staff. They are courteous, professional and dedicated to their guests. Hats off to April and Amanda who have gone out of their way to ensure my stay was an enjoyable one.
I will definitely return to this hotel for future trips.

This place can always be counted on for a cheap rate. Right near everything, but still on a quiet side street. Short walk to subway. Rooms a bit small, but who the hell sits in their room while in NYC?? Highly recommended.

I stayed here for three nights with my parents. The hotel staff are friendly and the lobby makes you feel like you are coming home. Our room was clean though smallish for three people. I liked the wine reception and complimentary tea and coffee in the morning. 
A short walk from Union Square on the edge of the Tenderloin district meaning it was easy to find reasonably priced breakfast options.

We stayed here for one night while visiting San Antonio. The staff was very helpful. The hotel is on the older side but very clean! Breakfast was one of the best we have had while on a - week trip. It is within walking distance of the Alamo and The Riverwalk. Free parking on site. The only downside was there were no restaurants close to the hotel (within a couple blocks). We didn't realize this or we would have chosen a restaurant while on the Riverwalk (@--- mile from the hotel).

Wonderful hotel with lots to do. Hotel lobby is located in between Copley Place and The Prudential, which means shoppers heaven!. We had a corner room and the view of Boston was spectacular. They also run very good deals at this hotel, especially for Marriott Rewards members. We got our corner room on the --rd floor for just $---! For sushi lovers, you must try the Philadelphia Roll at the sushi bar in the lobby. My husband is a sushi fanatic & he says it is some of the best he's ever had, anywhere! The Cheesecake Factory food was terrible, but the Banana Cream Cheesecake was fabulous. Skip the meal here and just go for dessert! Also, just a - minute walk to Copley Station Green Line. Trust me, that is the station you want to pick up the T. It is very safe to travel in Boston on the Green & Red Lines. Stay away from the Orange Line (on the MBTA). It's a little shady.

We enjoyed our stay at the Fairmont on Nob Hill. Getting to it was a haul as it is situated atop historic Nob Hill, but after gorging ourselves on Chinese in Chinatown and Italian in Little Italy, climbing a few hills wasn't a bad thing. The hotel is beautiful, and has an old style feel without the musty smells and creaking hallways like other establishments have. The ceilings are high and the room we had was quite spacious. The bathroom was the highlight of the stay, with lots of space and THE BEST water pressure in the shower. Will definitely stay here again.

Had a very good stay at the hotel,everything clean and modern,absolutely great location for all the tourist attractions.The staff at the desk very rarely welcomed you back from your day out sightseeing etc.Also heard people in elevator talking about getting discount vouchers for having an evening meal at the hotel but we weren,t offered anything,having said that ,still had a very good time in San Francisco.

Stayed here for three days in January ----. I was given a room on the -th floor upon check-in, but it was missing a curtain at the top of the window so I was moved to a new (upgraded) room next door which was much more spacious. The decor is modern and funky. The bathroom was tiny but functional. The a-c is a unti under the window so can be noisy. The conceirge arranged an early airport transfer for me, for a lower price than a taxi. Overall, I'd return to this hotel for it's value and location - the Starbucks on the ground floor is plus too!

This hotel is located in the midst of Boston's world-class medical facilities, and caters to people wanting to stay near the hospitals, either as patients or families. It's a tower with eight floors and hotel rooms are only on floors ---. (don't know what's on the rest). As a tourist hotel, I found it lacking. It was more like staying in an office building-there is little welcoming about the lobby, nor is there any gathering place. The lobby has one couch and four chairs. Amenities I've come to expect were also missing- no bar, no restaurant, no fitness center, no breakfast. There is a food court next door that has a restaurant (we did not try it). The room was fine, the staff were mostly helpful, but for about $----night I expected more. I also found their energy-saving maid service backwards- you could have a complete cleaning OR have the towels changed and trash removed, but you couldn't ask to have the bed made and NOT change the towels everyday. If you didn't ask for a complete cleaning they didn't replace the coffee you'd used up. If you don't need to be near the hospitals I don't know why you'd stay there.

My wife and I stayed at The Library Hotel for - nights. In that short period of time, the staff made us feel like we were family. The attention to detail and the exceptional warm and friendly staff made our stay the perfect experience. We were surprised with things such as a VIP desert being delivered to our table at Uncle Jacks Steakhouse compliments of the hotel when we didn't even think they knew where we were going to eat.
In summary, We both agree that travelling would be perfect if every city we travelled to had a Library Hotel!

Booked this hotel through Priceline. Never been to San Fran before so had no Idea what to expect. I figure the hotel was as easy to find as anything else in the city. Very helpful when we checked in. Garage right next door took care of the car. Bell hop was friendly and full of info. We asked for a double room because our son was unexpectedly with us. They were sold out of doubles and extra single rooms. He said he could upgrade us to a suite for what I felt was a reasonable up charge. The hotel was very charming and I loved the room. View was. Commanding and I enjoyed our stay here. We stayed two nights and the location was great.

We had a nice stay at the Hilton Suites Mag Mile to ring in ----. If you're into shopping on the Mag Mile, the Hilton Suites is at an excellent location. Navy Pier, Downtown, Millennium Park are all very long walks. Taxi's were readily available at the hotel doorstep though.
We drove into town, and parking at the hotel was $-- a night. Outrageous, but we knew it ahead of time and budgeted for it. The valet service was very nice and efficient though. 
The folks at the reception desk were very helpful and friendly. Service to check in and check out was quick. 
The room was nice, though a bit on the small side, in my opinion, being a suite. There was a living room area with a couch (with a horribly uncomfortable pull out bed), a chair, TV and desk. There was also a small sink and refridgerator. The fridge was contained in a cabinet and didn't work very well. The bathroom was really large. The bedroom was small, but it was spearated by french doors from the living area, which was nice for privacy. Decor was kind of blah and very standard. I expected more from a Hilton in Chicago. We were only given - towels each day, and the room attendants replaced our towels even though we had them hanging on the rack, indicating we'd use them again. There were several elevators, though only one or two seemed to be operational. 
This hotel was ok for our purposes, needing two sleeping areas and some privacy and a decent price for our quick, last minute trip. Though, I was the one """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sleeping"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on the pull out couch and didn't really sleep. So, yes, a nice stay, nice location for shopping. But, I woudn't really recommend this hotel because of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""suite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" factor. Just spring for a second room if you can afford it or be prepared to have a stiff back if you're the one sleeping on the couch. I probably wouldn't stay here on a return trip to Chicago, just because there's so many options and I'd like to try a different location for different activities.

I stayed at the King's Inn for several nights in January ---- as part of a business trip. I was attending a convention at the Town and Country Resort nearby, so I chose to stay at this hotel rather than pay the higher prices at the (overbooked) convention hotel.
THe hotel is located on Hotel Circle, which is a loop drive straddling I-- flanked with hotels and not much else. The selection of restaurants, stores, and other amenities in the immediate viscinity is limited, but a large shopping complex is easily accessed by driving east on the interstate, and Old Town is easily accessed by driving to the west. The close location to the interstate makes it relatively easy to start driving to other locations in town, although traffic is still a problem. The location was very noisy, as the interstate is located across the street from the hotel.
The hotel rooms were clean and decently decorated, although it seemed that the decor could use updating. The window latches were notably flimsy. Unfortunately, the rooms are exceptionally noisy because of the close location to the highway, and the building construction does little to dampen out the noise.
The desk staff were not particularly polite or attentive. The cleaning staff inexplicably left windows open but otherwise did a good job with cleaning.
The price was particularly good for the Hotel Circle area. I made reservations in advance, and received one night free. This kept costs very low.
The hotel does contain two restaurants. One is a Mexican bar and restaurant that I did not bother looking at too closely (especially with Old Town nearby). The other is a waffle shop which incorporated bizarre drawings of cartoon characters (anthropomorphic breakfast foods wearing medieval costumes that looked like they were drawn in the ----'s) into its theme. I never felt like eating breakfast there, but it did look tempting.
Ultimately, I would recommend this hotel for a budget traveler that needs to stay on Hotel Circle. For other travelers, I would recommend looking beyond Hotel Circle for better, quieter locations.

I stayed three days at this hotel for a conference, so it was not a choice. This is a new hotel on Hwy. ----. The location is fine, it is near many restaurants, shopping etc. Its about -- min. to downtown. The staff was friendly, the rooms nice and clean although small. Great TV, nice kitchen and a nice separate dressing area. Beds and bedding were nice. Overall a good place to stay in SA although I prefer being nearer to the Downtown or airport area.

Was very disappointed with our stay . On the second I saw a dead cockroach on the hallway and a few days later my wife notice her Granola Bars were eaten . Lots of Mice %#^%@ left behind . There's was a few droppings under the Coffee pot too .

A place we can only but recommend; very nice atmosphere; friendly and helpful staff; nice and clean room; free and fast Internet; good breakfast, free regular bus service to train station which was great; expensive parking;

We had a family of - and stayed in the queen loft suite. Plenty of beds with queen in loft and murphy bed and sofa bed in living room. Liked the decorating and amenities. The wine and cheese was lovely after seeing the sites. The friendly front desk man really made a mark on us. Breakfast items are prepackaged but still nice to have it at all. We're so glad we stayed in a neighborhood rather than in the mega hotels near Market St. Had tapas dinner at Valanni. Good food. Would love to come back to see more sites. Would stay at the Independent again. Our best price was linking from TA site.

We recently enjoyed a four night stay at The Chancellor Hotel at the end of a -- day road trip around California. The hotel is an older property with some period features particularly apparent in the lobby area, and certain parts of the hotel show signs of dating. But I am not saying that this was a cause for complaint as we received very helpful and friendly service from all members of staff, our rooms were very comfortable and clean and we were fortunate enough to have excellent views across Union Square. The location of the hotel is its strength as we found it was perfect for getting around San Francisco and having taken a tour bus around SF we were pleased that this was definitely in one of the safer areas. Most of the attractions are within walking distance and if you purchase the passes for the cable cars - trams - buses you can hop on and off wherever you like. My only suggestion to the hotel is that you should think about increasing the size and updating the image of the hotel bar. It seemed a popular meeting place but far too small to accommodate the clientele. We enjoyed our trip to San Francisco and our stay at the Chancellor but I didn't """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""leave my heart there"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" .... I am sure the city is trying to help the homeless and down and outs, but they appear to have a long way to go.

This is probably the strangest hotel I've ever stayed at....and although I thoroughly enjoyed the experience I probably wouldn't want to repeat the experience. Reception staff varied in friendliness. The room was a decent size for New York, with really nice pieces of furniture, and a lovely long sprig of fresh orchid in a vase on the writing table. Thankfully the bed which was massive and very comfortable was new! Bathroom was clean with nice toiletries and lots of fluffy white towels. The room was warm - but they do seem to have a major problem with their central heating plumbing as it made a huge knocking noise every half-hour or so (all day - all night). As I said - an interesting experience!

I normally don't write reivews on TripAdvisor, but I stayed at Carlyle Suites on business March -- - --, ---- and had a GREAT visit. The manager and the staff are super attentive and love to point you in the right direction for restaurants in the area, attractions, or even offered to help my fellow colleagues and I find our conference we were attending. Just returned after a - day trip .Chose this hotel as i have stayed in a few of the sofitels , and found them great .This was ... well ok. The staff here has always been very friendly and helpful and this time was no exception. Valet parking, bell staff, front desk check in, Networks Bar & Grill waitress; all great. We requested a room on the third floor by the pool which we got with no problems. My family and I stayed during the whole week of the Comic-con ---- and it was great. The service was wonderful, the valet and front desk assisted me with all my questions. I stayed at the Milford just a week ago in January. I had my car parked - valet was helpful and timely, I checked in asked for a room with a front view - got it immediately, the valet helped me with a few restaurants close by. The room was comfortable -very clean with a clean bed and bathroom. I wasnt in it much but was impressed with the cleanliness of the room in general. We were close to the river, close to a lot of great restaurants and close to Niketown, close to the L and the subway. One thing I wish this hotel had in our room was a bath tub, especially after the race. Our room only had a shower. The hotel provided breakfasts every morning which helped us save time and money.
