Location to the convention center was perfect. We ate at several restaurants at the hotel and they were all delicious. The amount of food at the sports bar was amazingly large and yummy. Lael's breakfast buffet was awesome. We also had dinner at Sally's right by the harbor where we had a wonderful server. Food, atmosphere, service..all top notch. I would recommend it!

My husband & I stayed here for - nights. It is a very small inn with very limited parking but ssince we had no car it wasn't a problem. Rooms are very clean, bed is very comfy. Each morning there is coffee, tea, juice, fresh fruit & pastries, although there is no place to eat except for in your room. No prob. Coffee and tea are still available throughout the day & evening. No restaurant on premises. This hotel is in a nice, quiet neighborhood and within walking distance of several bus lines to take you to Fisherman's Wharf or downtown. Plenty of eateries and a Walgreen's drugstore nearby as well. Staff are nice. They can arrange a shuttle van to take you to the airport for $-- per person. I would recommend this hotel if you are looking for a nice, clean, simple accomodation.

My recent stay at The Pod Hotel was booked ultra last-min. I was going to stay at one of the Gansevoort properties, and when that didn't work out at the --th moment, my sister reminded me the Pod could be an option, so I booked a room with double or queen bed and an included bathroom. I think this hotel is decent value if you're booking a room sans bathroom, but when you book a room with a bathroom, the price skyrockets. 
Overall, I was very pleased with my stay, though the $--- price tag was a little much for a simple bed and bath, even for NYC. The location is fantastic in Mid-Town East and the quiet street has a ton of different restaurants, including a Parisian wine bar.
The Rooms
The room was well designed and very clean, aside from the carpet. Though it looked clean, if you shut the window and left, upon your return, the entire room would smell like dirty feet, a smell that emanated from the carpet. To counteract the scent, we just kept the window open. I was thankful I brought slippers with me! {Note that I forgot to tell the hotel about the carpet smell when I checked out, so Pod if you're reading this, I should have said something, but left in a big hurry!}
The beds act like a couch by day {with the pillows stored in the closet} and a bed by night. The bathroom is mini like a cruise ship cabin's lavatory, but again, very smart design with nooks, hooks and crannies to store your toiletries. The white on stainless colour scheme was tasteful as well.
I didn't really have much interaction with staff other than the concierge and bellmen, who were both helpful and pleasant. 
The Hotel 
The hotel itself is thoughtfully done. What I like about The Pod vs other pod or budget-style hotels is it didn't feel cheap. Additions like a little pay-for breakfast, snack and drinks area in the lobby and terrace was great, and the roof-top deck is of course a huge asset in NYC. 
All in all, I'd suggest it to others who want a fun and budget stay option in NYC, but as for myself, with so many other hotels in NYC, I might like to try others on subsequent trips!
What to know
- free wifi
- some rooms have bathrooms, so don't {but have easily accessible shared facilitates}
- great location with a grocery-type store down the street, subway access - blocks away, and great restaurants nearby
- bring your own slippers
- if you like to sleep with the window open, request additional blankets
- note that anywhere in nyc, nightly taxes are huge. on our $--- nightly rate, we paid an additional $---night.

I recently stayed at the Benjamin for a business trip to NYC. Not only was the hotel in a great location but it was very elegant yet homey. We also tried out the hotel bar every night and were very pleased with the service. On my last morning I went to breakfast and the Manager helped us with our JFK arrangements. Great hotel!

Overall, it was a wonderful stay and a pleasant final experience in Philadelphia.

Went to San Antonio for a yearly reunion with my NAVY buddies from -- years ago. San Antonio is a bit on the touristy side,but I expected that. While there we stayed at the Menger Hotel. After filing a report with the police we learned that this hotel was on the news a couple nights before for having an excessive amount of cars being broke into and thefts. Would I stay here again? NO WAY!

I stayed here for business for a period of almost three months. I was put up in a one bedroom apartment and must add it was very comfortable.
The property is very clean, its centrally located for grocery shopping etc. The kitchen is functional and I mostly made my own food. The most attractive feature of this particular property is its closeness to Rice university and you can take a jog around the village and the university campus. One can also hang around the village, where you will find quite a crowd during weekends.
The property also has a fitness center, though I hardly used the same. The staff are very helpful and you can use a printer in case you have to.
As for food, the breakfast is the same everyday, so since I was staying longer, got repetitive towards the end. However, the choices are good and people staying short term would like it.
I had a great stay and would definitely return back to the same property when travelling on business.

The staff was wonderful from check-in to breakfast to room service. The room was generally clean and the bed was comfortable, but the carpeting was woefully in need of cleaning. It was stained and filthy (something the daily room cleaning could not be expected to take care of).

Working in the hotel industry it is always nice to experience hotels that stand out like Hotel Bijou where we stayed for - nights before going to Sonoma. All rooms are named after a San Francisco movie and we stayed in """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Sneakers"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". What also makes it unique is the small cinema where they feature free historic movies together with hot chocolate and pop corn.
The guy working in the evening time, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""JR"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was truly helpful and gave a - star service with a smile.
If you are looking for an inexpensive --- star hotel with a good sightseeing-shopping location in San Francisco with some uniqueness try Bijou.

I stayed here for - nights last November, and I must say the hotel is very modern and beautiful. While I generally like modern hotels, this one just seemed a little cold to me. Maybe it was the black everywhere (furniture, employee clothing) or the club line out of the door, but something about it annoyed me, though I can't put my finger on it. For someone who is single and looking for a fun night out on the town, the Sofitel is great, with a hot club on the bottom floor. It is right across from the Beverly Center for great shopping, and is just a short cab ride from all the main LA attractions, as well as Beverly Hills. The rooms were modern with very comfortable beds, amazing showers, and a great view of the Hollywood sign. Very nice hotel , but defnitely more for business or singles. Internet was not free, although from my room I was able to pick up a wireless signal from outside, so I never had to pay for internet. They also have a nice pool, although it was a little too cool for swimming in November. All around a nice hotel in a great location. If you have any questions please feel free to email me at yoshapman@hotmail.com

This was our -st trip to Indianapolis and our -st Sprint Cup race. We scoured many websites and read numerous reviews. Couldn't be happier we chose Homewood Suites at the Crossing. Initially asked for a -st flr room with a king bed, but instead got a -rd flr room in an elevator building. Problem solved. The room was great...never had a problem with noisy neighbors. Bedroom was separate from living area-kitchen. Shower was fantastic. Breakfast was excellent...both hot and cold items. During our stay breakfast seating area was never crowded. Staff was awesome. Only minor complaint was that I couldn't locate an ice machine, but never got around to asking. There is an ice cube tray in the freezer. Area had shopping and restaurants nearby. Check out Broad Ripple Village and the restaurants on Cornell Ave. Bottom line...we loved the hotel and Indianapolis. Would stay here again in a heartbeat.
We loved it! Great service! Extraordinary rooms! Amazing view! What else can I say!?

The only minus for this hotel is they do not provide the free morning coffee at all the other Kimpton hotels. It was a great place to stay for the theater but our rate did say morning coffee.
The robes were not in the room and it took a long time (hours) but other than that a great place. 
The concierge was excellent.

This is a really funky, interesting modern hotel in what was formerly a fairly nondescript older building. Their complimentary wine hour featured one of the tastiest snacks I've ever come across: truffle-buttered popcorn. Service was excellent. The rooms were not huge was adequate and nicely decorated. The location is ideal for all concerts-plays in Center City and with good access to public transit.

I stayed at the Hotel last week when I was in town on business. The lobby is very attractive and the front desk staff was very helpful. The room (basic) was large and the bed was very comfy. The location is great with lot's of restaurants close by. I was able to get all over town easily. The valet parking is a little on the expensive side.

Positive: Rooms are larger than most and comfortable, Staff is helpful and cheerful, Everything very clean from lobby restrooms to the room itself. We had a slight problem with the iron in the room - it was resolved in one minute! When looking for dinner ideas because of several severe food allergies, the concierge service was exemplary! The attendant found a location within a short walking distance!
""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Okay"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""": The hotel is older and dated; however, it does not affect your stay. There is a parking garage with an elevator access - but it is tight quarters and smaller vehicles are much easier to maneuver. Taxi cabs go right to the front door for drop off and pick up, however.

My husband and I stayed one night at the Elysian and if you are looking for a luxury hotel that puts the emphasis on service - this is the place to stay. The staff are all exceedingly pleasant and accomodating which, being from Chicago originally, is something you hope to see projected to visitors to the Midwest's biggest city. Ordered room service up to the spa and for breakfast and it was delicious and speedy. There was a delay in getting in to the room we had originally booked, so we were automatically upgraded to a gorgeous Gold Coast suite at no extra charge. Every little request we had was handled quickly and politely.

Good place to stay right in the middle of times square. Room was clean, modern, good bathroom and shower, and had a very comfy bed. Ask for a room on the Broadway side of the building as it was much quieter at night. Room was quiet at night with not much outside noise which was a pleasant supprise. Also our room had windows that could pop open at the bottom which was nice to get some fresh air in during the day. Great view from the resturant and the bar was nice but both had the worse service of our stay. The bar lady continously asked us if we were staying there and always had to confirm our room number on the computer system which we found quite rude, especially on the forth night of our stay. Breakfast in resturant was great but again lacking service. Conceirge was good and the housekeeping ladies extremely nice and helpful. So overall stay was good, but not great because of the bad service from check and bar and resturant staff. I would still recommend staying here because of the great modern rooms and location if you want to stay in the times square area. On our next stay we would definatley stay in a less busy area which had more resturants to choose from as Times Square mainly offered the touristy choices of Planet Hollywood, Hard Rock cafe etc. 
Four stars

I decided to go the Priceline route and see what my bid would get me. I guess you get what you pay for. I was looking for a hotel convenient to UTSA and also a variety of restaurants, and this locale didn't disappoint. Unfortunately, the hotel had a bit to be desired. Though hard to desribe, the hotel common areas had a 'cheap hotel' smell that may have been related to the garbage cans placed on each floor for the guests to dump their trash cans into. As the name suggests, the rooms are geared for longer stays and though the bed was comfortable enough, the balance of the furnishings and the condition of the bathroom were barely up to the --star rating I requested. The small TV was a good -- years old and was about --' away while laying in bed. At least the pool was refreshing, though bring an extra towel for the lounges. Though not advertised ,the hotel did offer a 'coffee bar' and some bagels in the morning. Not a standard continental breakfast, but better than nothing. Got a good night's sleep, but luckily my wife wasn't with me...especially when a couple crickets found their way into my third floor room. Probably wouldn't stay there again at any price.

I have nothing but superlatives to say about the Chicago Sofitel. The room and bed were very comfortable, with an exceptional bathroom having both a shower and bathtub. We had a wonderful view of the skyscrapers. The fitness center had lots of cardio machines. The location very close to the magnificant mile on N. Michigan Ave was perfect. My wife and I easily walked to the Chicago Art Institute, the Modern Art Museum, to the architectural cruise tour stop on the Chicago River, to Millenium Park... There were always numerous taxis at the side of the hotel for transport to sites further away. I also can't say enough about the service, professionalism, and easy access to the hotel staff. The lobby was elegant and comfortable. We loved Chicago and staying at the Sofitel significantly contributed to our pleasurable stay.

I stayed here with my family of - for - nights. The room was not huge but it was clean, updated and comfortable (---). We have a price that included breakfast which I thought was good. The location is walking distance to most major attractions in the are. Valet parking was a bit steep. I would stay the again for the same price.

We stayed here for - nights and it was ok. It's an older hotel, but the rooms were clean. We were in a king executive room which was HUGE but the bathroom was so tiny and there was no mini-fridge. We paid a little extra when we booked for this room assuming it would have some ugraded amenities, but that wasn't the case. We had to leave early on Sun morning to get back home and we were in a hurry so I just stopped downstairs on the way out to grab a cup of coffee and they didn't have anything because the breakfast place wasn't open. We had lunch there in the afternoon - very basic menu, but the food was decent. You can only get food during certain hours though. The fitness center is nice and the pool looked great, but no hot tub which was disappointing. Parking is $--.---day which is kind of crazy considering it's just a big open lot. 
The service here was amazing though - everyone from the front desk to the dining staff was so nice and helpful. They had a hotel shuttle that is free with in - miles of the hotel. We were able to check in early with no problems. 
Overall decent hotel - very basic, but clean and nice staff which is always important.
New , clean rooms. Great location. If you want to be close to Times Square, this is the place. Good value.

On Thursday April -, ---- we went to Columbus, where we met our Son for our Easter celebration. He came from Dayton. I had called in advance a few days before and spoke with a Lady named Betty who was very nice. She told me the pool was warm, at the time the hot tub was being serviced, but by the time we arrived it would be working. The hotel is still under renovation, but the rooms were nice, the breakfast was perfect, the managers reception was good. Most importantly the pool was very comfortable we spent two hours in the evening, and then another two hours in the morning floating around the pool talking and catching up. We plan next year to make this location a monthly meeting place, since it is exact an hour and half for our son and us. Thank you for being one of those locations that make your pool comfortable.

I came into the hotel with the understanding that is a no frills hotel, and I got what I paid for - to be in a great neighborhood out of downtown. The receptionist was nice and recommended spots to park my car. It's within close distance to some great restaurants, and a quick walk to the lower Haight, Castro and Hayes Valley where there's plenty more great bars and restaurants. Pay close attention to street signs because I ended up getting a $-- street sweeping ticket. After a certain hour, -pm, parking overnight is a pain to find but that's to be expected in that neighborhood. They have a loading zone right in front of the hotel, so take full advantage of it before you look for parking. The walls are very thin so I heard some guy talking I think in the next room, and people stumbling in at -am on the -st floor. There were some dirt marks on the carpet, and the heat wasn't very controlled when I first got there so I had to use the ceiling fan. The decor of the room is very outdated --'s motel like with a tube tv. The pillows were thin, and the blankets even thinner but there are spare blankets in the closet. 
It's a great place to go if you just need somewhere to crash. But I can't say I got a good night's sleep. I didn't really relax there, because I was out most of the day. I'm not sure if I'd stay there again.

I was pleasantly surprised by the Days Inn. I normally stay at higher quality hotels, but we needed a place for one night before flying out of Denver after a stay in Vail. The hotel was nicely decorated with good size rooms and had a mini fridge which was useful for the food we had brought with us from our condo stay. There was also a microwave and coffee pot in the room. Everything was clean and up to date. The check out time is fairly late (--:-- noon I think) which was great for us as we could lounge in the room as our flight was not until - pm. 
The free continental breakfast was basic but adequate.
The price that we got at the AARP rate on their website was very low. The only problem we had was that my husband said he heard noise of people coming and going during the night. I did not, but this frequently is the case at hotels near airports.
The staff was friendly and helpful. Adequate parking and lots of restaurants nearby. We did not use the pool, which looked decent at a glance through the door, or the airport shuttle, so I cannot comment on those.

If you're visiting New York then this has got to be the place to stay. Stayed for - nights in March - we booked on line and at the time there was an offer of stay for -nights, pay for - - made this hotel even better value for money. We booked a High Floor Corner Room. We were on the --th floor and the views from our room were amazing. You can still hear some street noise (car horns) even at this level, but nothing intrusive as the rooms have double glazing. Having a corner room gave us - huge panaromic windows which overlooked the city and hudson river - could see all the way down to Liberty! The room was much larger than most hotel rooms and featured a large lcd tv, coffee making facilities, a room safe, bath robe and not many rooms offer a view of the Empire State Building from your bathroom !! Whilst the name of this hotel gives the impression that it is in Times Sq, it is just off it on W--rd - which is ideal - location without the noise! As you enter the hotel you go up via escalators to reception where very friendly staff are waiting to assist. There is a large seating area, bar and steak restaurant. High speed lifts whizz you up to your floor (get ready for your ears to pop)! If you want to find a classic American diner for breakfast ask the concierge - he recommended a great one to us (think it was on -th) - great food and great value. Check-out is at noon, but there is no problem if you want to leave your baggage at the hotel until you're ready to leave. The door man will also arrange cabs etc for you - If you want a cab to JFK ask him to negotiate you a flat rate - that way, no matter how bad the traffic is you will know what you're paying. We didn't eat in the restaurant - a fellow guest suggested we shouldn't - read into that what you will! The bar staff were friendly and on hand with nibbles. This hotel was fab and I would have no hesitation in recommending it to anybody. We will definately stay there again - but worth upgrading to a corner room on a high floor.

The Hotel looks better in photo's than reality. Our room was quite dark & looked tired. The carpet was odd...wasn't nailed to floor & worn in places, curled up at the wall. Bathroom tiny with large concrete pillar in middle of it, quite a monouver to get into shower & definately only one person at a time in bathroom itself. Awoken first morning (-.--) by very loud hammering-banging in opposite room. Rang reception to be told there were no renovations happening in hotel, on informing them that the sink & various room items were in the corridor she agreed to investigate & call back. We are still waiting for the call. When we approached reception for a room change we were told the Hotel was full & no other rooms were avail. They said they would contact Manager to find a solution. That evening on our return we were informed that renovations would not start until -.-- next morning & none over the weekend. We agreed to that offer as it would have been too difficult to find another hotel at that stage. We did receive an apology from the receptionist & a small box of chocolates (- pieces) .
Air conditioning unit was hopeless, hardly made a difference in the room, big old fashioned type that sounds like a --- landing at all speed settings.
Overall the Hotel was OK, clean linen & towels, the room would have been quiet, it looked over gardens & there was no street noise. Positon is good if you are looking for a quiet area, on a bus route, walking to midtown about -- mins, very close to central park.
I think the Hotel is expensive for what it is offering, it looks more budget than medium range & i would not stay there again.

I recently had the opportunity to visit Denver and stayed at The Timbers Hotel. After my experiences with this property, I can easily say that this will be my hotel of choice whenever I return to Denver. The property and rooms are clean, well furnished, reasonably sound proofed and priced in a very reasonable range. The staff is polite, professional, and did everything in their power to not only accommodate me, but went out of their way on several occasions to assure that my visit here was excellent. I travel a great deal professionally and cannot think of a place that has done so much for me at such a reasonable price.

I have stayed at the Westin Columbus for almost three months now and wouldn't stay anywhere else in Columbus! Although the hotel is not as modern as other Westins I have stayed in, all the little touches that you expect from a Westin are there--the heavenly shower head, the heavenly bed, and friendly service. They have a mini snack bar in every room, but unlike most hotels, they won't charge you an arm and a leg for them! I've also gotten the room service a few times and the food was actually pretty good.
They have really impressed me with their customer service by going above and beyond. Not only do they help book my rooms out ahead of time, but they are always extremely helpful in making changes for me if my schedule changes. The doorman always greets me with a smile and one story in particular sticks out above the rest: I typically leave a bag at the hotel over the weekend and one time it was misplaced. The hotel staff did everything they could to find it, but when they couldn't, I found a bag in my hotel room the next week with items to replace the ones I lost, a thank you note, and a few extra little items to apologize for the inconvenience. Now that's service!
The one caveat to my recommendation is that if you are a traveler there for pleasure, you may want to ask about the size of your room because while their Starwood Preferred Guest rooms are great, the regular rooms can be a tad on the tiny side.
Overall though, it is a great hotel with friendly service and definitely one I would recommend to people traveling to Columbus, especially if you are there on business.

Very friendly staff! I got in late at night and had to be up very early. The man at the desk greeted me with a friendly smile each time which was very welcoming since - am is not fun for anyone. Room was very clean and bed very comfortable. I will always stay in a microtel as long as it is close to my vacation spot

We visited The Liaison for Spring Break. It was my Wife and I and our -- year old Daughter. We had booked a room with two double beds at a very reasonable rate under $--- per night. We arrived and my Wife and Daughter checked in while I parked the car at Union Station's Garage. At check in they were told our room was not available and they had a corner room for us instead with a King bed and a chase lounge. Because of the mix up they offered us a restaraunt credit to be used for a breakfast for each of us. The room was ok and my Daughter quite enjoyed sleeping on the chase lounge. The room itself was very nice and well appointed including a wonderful flat screen HD TV (the channel guide didn't include the HD stations available to view the HD stations simply go backwards and change channels they are in a higher sequence than the non HD stations), a clock radio that had a docking station for my Daughter's IPod, the pillow menu including a really cool sound pillow that worked in conjunction with her IPod and the bed was quite comfortable. The bathroom was small but very well appointed and the included toilatries were all Aveda products. The only problem we had with our room was the safe malfuntioned a couple times and getting the Manager up to our room took some time. The exercise area was quite extensive and nice especially for such a small hotel. I parked the car at Union Station's garage because it was only about a - minute walk and the rate was $-- per -- hours versus the Liaison's rate was $-- for -- hours the savings was well worth the extra effort of walking to Union Station and during our four day stay we never needed our car. We used the Metro for transportation and that was also located within Union Station and that got us anywhere we wanted to go at a minimal cost. The location of this hotel has to be among the best in the area especially taking into consideration the price. Make sure to visit the Hyatt across the street as a nice alternative for a drink or food and they also have an extensive convenience shop selling anything from toiletries to coffee and danishes. We ate in the restaraunt for breakfast one morning and only did so because of the credit we received it was quite pricey even for breakfast let alone dinner for a family on a budget. Wireless internet is available in the lobby at no charge however if you want to use it in your room there is a daily or weekly charge and because of that the lobby at times resembles an internet cafe with several people and their laptops. This is a great hotel to stay at for the location alone and factor in the very nice room and facilities and we would definitely go back. The only problem unfortunately was the mix up with the room at check in and the only other recommendations I have would be to include wireless internet access in the rooms at no charge and include the HD channels on the channel guide in the room.

I stayed at Alexander Inn for a week in early September. The room was clean and comfortable. The staff was very friendly and helpful with hints, help and directions. Breakfast was well done and well stocked. The location cannot be beat since it is within walking distance to anything you want to do - museums, historic, bars, clubs, restaurants - you name it. I will definetly be back as soon as I can.

We just stayed here recently for - nights. The location is convenient and close to all highways but the photos on the hotel's website are very misleading. The rooms are clean, but quite dated and the bathroom is so small that its hard to open-close the door with someone in it. 
On the second day, we had no housekeeping service. I called the desk at -pm and was assured that the housekeeping staff was not finished and they just didn't get to my room yet. We left for the evening and returned at --pm and the room was still not cleaned. I called the front desk to ask for some fresh towels and was told the staff could not leave the desk and if I wanted towels I had to go down to the desk to get them so I did and received no explanation or apology. 
The air conditioning unit in our room was the size of a couch and sounded like a helicopter was landing in our room. Also, it only had - dials (low, medium and high) and even on low it got really cold and when you turned it off for an hour it got really hot. In general, not a very comfortable stay. I'm not familiar with Columbus but I'm sure there are better options!

I stayed - nights in this hotel for a wedding. The first night we had a junior suite...which was amazing. The second night was a - bed regular room. Both were very clean and spacious! The free breakfast was wonderful....huge selection and great seating. The pool is a metal one, which I found weird and the water had a salty taste...but my daughter still loved it. Staff was very friendly and helpful.
The door lock was broken, mold around toliet, toliet seat dirty. soap scum and tub was stopped up with large masses of hair. Stains on Blankets

The Catamaran Resort is the best one in San Diego. It's right on Mission Bay with a nice beach and within a short walk to the Pacific Ocean. The rooms were clean and beautiful and the grounds were tropical and beautiful.

I really like this hotel, it's clean, comfortable and full of free amenities. When you compare it to most other hotels around the corner, the price is great and you get free wifi, breakfast and more. Most importantly for me, the bed was very comfortable. You can't beat the view of the room onto the Empire State Building and great location to everything else...

My boyfriend and I stayed at this hotel for four nights. We were nervous at first about our choice as we had never visted San Francisco and weren't sure which areas we should try to stay in. In the end we were very impressed with the character of this hotel. Our hotel room was small but very beautifully decorated, there was a big bathroom, closet, ironing board, fridge and the bedding and matresses were the most comfort I've ever experienced at a hotel. The wine and cheese was a very nice touch. The area was great, really close to shopping and many restaurants, there were quite a few homeless people around, but they did not bother us very much. San Francisco is such a beautiful city!

Checking inn was chaos here, we checked in at arounds --pm and the worker there was extrmely slow. there was about - people in the line in front and in took her half an hour each, when it got to us it was --mins, she had failed to tell us that we needed to get our passports and it took another -- minutes for her to scan them, then after all the paperwork was done, she forgot to register our keys, an awful start. the rooms were ok, they were nicely decorated, and cosy, though the bathroom had no locks !! the free breakfast consisted of waffles (you had to make them with the batter provided) sticky buns, cereals (fruit loops and cherios) and apple and orange juice, plus coffee. overall it was ok, the only downers were the service and no locks
Nice and very clean. The first hotel to give us a Thank You card upon departure. Nice touch!

Hi, we have just returned from a - week stay at this hotel. We were very pleased with the hotel. It is in a great location for all the major tourist attractions. We booked a King room and were upgraded to a twin queen room at no extra cost. The room was a good size but the bathroom was a little compact but perfectly functional. This hotel would suit all guests. The hotel is just behind the Yerba Buena gardens where there are open concerts it is also a great place to enjoy the weather. I booked through Expedia and got a good deal. Staff are generally helpful, especially the Concierges. Had a few language problems with the bellboys. Didn't try the restaurant.

Traditional Marrryot ( clean, big rooms, comfy beds) in great location., very close to the Independence Hall.
I reccomend it.

I have stayed at this hotel on business several times, each time staff is always helpful and willing to accomodate its guests. I belong to the Priority Club Program and currently hold the Royal Ambassador status, if you stay at this hotel you must join because the perks are fantastic!! I'm always upgraded to a a suite on the corner which faces -th avenue-lovely view. I also get unlimited mini bar access-drinks only, not dry snacks. They also have delicious chocolates that they give to all guests when they do turndown service in the evenings. The bedrooms and bathrooms are spacious and well designed. They provide Gilchrest and Soames bath products, which smells and feels great. Unfortunately the gym is a bit hard to find, its tucked away in a corner but when you find it its well worth it, lots of machines and very spacious. The best part of teh hotel is that its right across the street from from Theatre district. The A train is literally next door, so you have access to major transportation hub. This station is also ADA accessable-which is rare in NYC. They have elevators and ramps, so this hotel is perfect for the disabled or elderly.

Just got home from staying at the Doubletree Mission Valley. In town to take children to Sea World and Legoland. Would definitely return and recommend to friends! Hotel was terrific; comfortable, clean and friendly staff. We got a great rate and were thrilled with the service, proximity of Sea World, indoor and outdoor pools and overall presentation of the Doubletree name. We were NOT disappointed!

My husband and I stayed here at the last leg of our honeymoon trip. The location is very convenient b-c it is right at union square and by the cable car stop. The rooms are very very small and of course expensive because it is San Francisco so I guess that is to be expected. The cable in our room was not very good and had very limited channels. We did not spend a ton of time in the room but it is always nice to unwind and watch something but not here. Our room was always clean but overall our stay was very average.

Centrally located, very reasonably priced (by my standards at least), and well kept, this was ideal for an overnight business trip. Friendly staff. Good in-house restaurant (tad pricey for breakfast). Have recommended it to friends. Would stay again. Nice views from upper floors.

Only stayed in New York for - nights this time around so sleep and comfort were a priority and we were not disappointed at the Sofitel.
Our queen room was large for NY standards (much larger than I expected!), very nicely furnished (with big cupboards- iron- safe - full-length mirror - fluffy bathrobes), and delightfully quiet. The bathroom had both a bath and a shower and lots of lovely products + candles & fresh flower (and the towels are from Frette...). The bed is just amazingly comfortable with fresh crisp linen - we're thinking of writing to Sofitel to ask where they got their beds from and buy the same one for our home! 
Service was faultless, and both checking in and out was extremely quick. 
And of course the location is brilliant - minutes off Times Square and -th avenue. 
Price-wise, it is expensive but then again everything is expensive in NYC. We paid the same price for the Hudson hotel last year and had a very disappointing stay there. You can get the best rates on the internet, especially if you book the non-refundable option. Only drawback of the whole stay: the price of the breakfast which we did not know about until we signed the check (and it was too late!) - USD-- for - continental breakfast + - coffee... extortionate! Once bitten, twice shy - we went to a nearby diner for the rest of our stay. 
But we'll definitely be back at the Sofitel.

We travelled to NYC for Thanksgiving and made a two night reservation at this hotel. We checked in before noon and a room was available. At the same time we noticed a large group of girls in brightly color costumes and signs in several places referring to Spirit of America. It turned out that we were staying at the same hotel as ---- young ladies, their families and escorts who were performing in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. This hotel does not have enough elevators to service the number of guest rooms and the result was long wait to get to your room. The hotel location was great, and the guest rooms a nice size, although ours wash at the point where a little refreshing is in order. Next visit we would opt for a smaller hotel.

I recently stayed at the Roosevelt Hotel for - nights during a business trip. I have to say that I was pretty disappointed. I had problems when booking (as did many of my colleagues). I arrived at the hotel at midnight after a delayed flight. As I entered the front entrance, I saw several steps up to get to the registration desk. I did not see a ramp or elevator and inquired about this with a maintenance member who happened to be near the entrance. He said there wasn't a ramp or elevator and indicated that I would need to walk up the steps. I had heavy luggage and nobody offered to assist. I checked in with a rude staff member who argued that I had multiple reservations and the wrong number of days reserved. After straightening out that mess, I went to my room which was very average. If you're looking for luxury, this is not the place. The lobby was pretty but the rooms are a different story. My room was worn and the carpet was musty. The only good thing was the bed, which was comfortable and the linens were nice enough. The cleaning staff seemed pleasant but the rest of the staff seemed rude. The front desk, concierge, etc. were not very helpful and sometimes rude. I've stayed at many hotels for business and pleasure and would not recommend this one.

What a combination. The coolest, mellowest front desk staff always eager to help.
Rooms that were a tad small but totally functional, quite stylish, and beds more comfortable than I would've imagined for a hotel that is such a value.
I still am amazed by what a deal this place is. Literally steps from Union Square and right next to everything, including being right on the trolley line!

However, it seems to have been pulled straight out of a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""how to build and run a luxury hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" box - just follow the simple to use instructions! Ritz Carlton have a great formula, but here is an example that they are resting on their laurels. There is no attempt to up the game, or push boundaries.
The highlight of the hotel is Fearings. Dean is THE celebrity chef of Dallas. It was a real coup for the Ritz to lure him away from the Mansion on Turtle Creek. The menu reflects the hype and we ate there a number of times and were consistently impressed. The staff were also very friendly and efficient. My only critisim would be that breakfast is not as slick as lunch, or dinner - service was a little slow. The restaurant is split into three dining areas. An open plan kitchen style, a more formal dining room and a conservatory. The bar scene was very busy on Thursday and Friday nights. It is supposedly the place to be seen in Dallas. Maybe if you come from a small country town - but it did not rock my boat.
I had a lovely corner room. It certainly had everything you would expect from a luxury hotel. Stand out points were the oversized bathroom and HD TV. Decor was not my taste - a bit too old fashioned.
There is a large gym, with good equipment. The spa is also very good and extensive. I had one treatment and my therapist was excellent.
I would definitely recommend the Ritz Carlton. Especially if you are in Dallas on business and want efficient service and ammenities. I would not say it is a hotel that will last in your memories.

I recently stayed at this Hilton for the Boston Marathon. The hotel is both close to the airport and the starting and finish lines of the race. It is a close subway ride from the airport, and the start-finish lines are within walking distance. If you would prefer not to walk the half mile to get to those points, there is also subway transportation to those points. The hotel itself was nice, clean and the staff was friendly. It seems a little overpriced for the quality of the room, but that is typical in a big city. The fitness center is tiny and there are no showers, do not rely on this if you want to get a good workout in or if you hope to use it to clean up after running the marathon. If you are there just for the running, this is better done outside in the safe and scenic neigborhood. Do not rent a car if you are going to stay here, the public transportation is all you need to get around the city of Boston. The restaurant and bar at the hotel are great, nice atmosphere, good food. Happy running!

This is the -nd time we've stayed there and will return if ever in Seattle again. The location is perfect, close to everything but in a quiet mixed (residential and commercial) neighborhood. Everything was clean and working, the business center is a real boon if I don't want to lug around a laptop, and the on-site Starbucks is a convenient quick-food feature.
At the end of the day, if the rooms and public areas are clean and amenities are as advertised, the only distinguishing factor between one property and another is it's people. These people seem to 'get' that, and everyone we encountered, from the multiple front desk staff to the housekeeping staff was top notch: friendly, polite, dedicated to ensuring a comfortable stay....even made GREAT in-room dining delivery suggestions.
This is a great place to stay in Seattle, relatively inexpensively.

We stayed at the hotel on a Friday night as part of a group reservation block. The rate was great for Center City and it was the host hotel for the event we were part of. 
The experience was fine. I would not stay here again with so many comparable rates at higher quality hotels nearby. 
Room was okay, clean, but looked """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""worn."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Beds were comfy and even though out room was close to the elevator, we slept without interruption. 
The hotel was very busy, but service at the front desk was still prompt and friendly. If you do not have a choice, you will be FINE here, but if you do have a choice, take a look around for a comprarable rate at a better hotel. 
One big positive: valet was just $-- overnight! An amazing deal for Center City hotels in Philly!

We were staying for - nights in this hotel the week before Christmas ----.
To New York standards the room we had in Hotel Beacon was very big. We were located at the --th floor and had - queen sized beds. We had a small kitchen including a good microwave. The room was clean, that's what important to us. The room could be a bit more modern and we like a shower separated from the bath, but everything worked fine (like t.v., airconditioning, heater). The hotel is relatively cheap and well located (- minutes walk to Central Park, - minutes walk + - minutes underground and you're on --nd street). Free newspaper every morning. If we ever go back to New York City (oh yes, we will...) this will be our hotel again. Tip: """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Sushi all you can eat"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for -- Dollar at - minutes walking distance!

We stayed a night in March ----. The hotel was well located, adjacent to the International Spy Museum with the MCI Center and metro stop just diagonally across the street. Rooms were well appointed, spacious, very high ceilings and two beautiful full length windows (it's a restored old building). Bedlinen of excellent quality, and Aveda amenities, CD player, cordless phone etc. (No bath tub though, for those of you who want a soak.) But what I liked best were the corridors leading to the rooms, which were stunning and unforgettable -- you have to see it for yourself. Service at the front desk can't really be faulted but could have done with a bit more warmth and enthusiasm.

The worst Internet speeds I have seen anywhere, faster in Zimbabwe honestly. Sure, everyone is on n the evening, but that's o surprise, happens every evening. Get more bandwidth then!
Rooms are nice, great renovation, last time I stayed here was in ---- when still an ITT Sheraton, h own things have changed!

I must say that the night life in San Antonio has something to be desired!!! I wanted more of a quiet quant place to enjoy a glass of NOT so PRICEY wine. I went to the bar of my hotel and my bartender, Mike and my waitreaa- Benjamin were nothing but the most upbeat, positively, hilarious people I have ever shared a glass of wine with. We laughed and giggled the evening away. There was never a dull moment. I must say that when you travel, staying in a quiet, professional, entertaining, comfortable hotel is a MUST.........Well, this is the PLACE...!!! THIS ONE IS TOPS WITH ME!!!

Very clean, very classy. I had a suite on the --th floor (bedroom and sitting room connected) which was the largest hotel room I have ever been in in NYC. Staff was friendly. No complaints. (Please note that there is construction going on immediately next door where the Twin Towers stood. The construction seemed to end around -pm or so and start up again between -am and -am. So, if you are a light sleeper or particularly bothered by construction, I would avoid this hotel for a while.)

You know you like a property when you return year after year. This hotel is very convenient and is still very good. It has a generous breakfast, a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lodge"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", a wine reception every weekday, an AMAZING fitness facility and is in the right neighborhood. I do have to admit that the room has its battle scars and the management has not worked hard enough on fixing them. There are scuffs and blotches all over the room and it no longer seems new (only -- months have lapsed!). This can be fixed with a little more attention to detail. Don't get me wrong: This is still my choice for a spacious, generous, comfortable and convenient stay in Baltimore. Don't let it deteriorate anymore as this gem may be tarnished. Staff is attentive and nice. Location is unbeatable and amenities are adequate. Kudos for free internet!

Worst mattress ever. Nicely appointed rooms, great staff, building is updated. Whats with the beds? If you like high end cotton sheets on plywood this is the place for you. I wasn't expecting a tempurpedic, but really?

My fiance and I booked a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""babymoon"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and stayed at the Millennium Bostonian Hotel for - nights. We really liked the location of the hotel, as it was an easy cab ride from the airport (less than $--, including the airport tax-extra fee) it was across the street from Quincy Market and Faneuil Hall, which made for quick and easy breakfasts as well as late night lobster mac and cheese! It's within walking distance to the Aquarium and the host of other tourist attractions that are down by the water. It is also super close to the North part of the city, which is FULL of amazing Italian restaurants including the (in)famous Mike's Pastry! Here's a tip...the line up will be OUT the door (and occasionally down the block for a few kilometers) but just walk in and go to the left...you'll get served right away :)
The hotel itself is not huge, which appealed to us, as we didn't want to stay in a massive, chain hotel. The staff was always very friendly, and greeted us as we left in the morning and arrived back at night. A few of the small inconveniences was that there aren't any ice machines, so we had to call down to the front desk every time we needed it. They were usually very quick though, so not a huge issue. There was a fridge, but it was fully stocked with mini-bar items, and you were charged just for opening it, so we couldn't get anything of our own to keep cool...unless we put it on ice...and as already reported...ice wasn't the easiest thing to get!
Also, the last day that housecleaning was in our room (so the day before we left) they didn't replenish our coffee, so the morning that we checked out, we couldn't make anything in the room as we packed up. Again, not a deal-breaker, but it would have been nice. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone travelling to Boston, for work or pleasure.

My husband and I stayed here for one night after a cruise from Quebec City to Boston. It was a stylish, comfortable hotel in a great location opposite the Boston Common. Most of the historic sites were within walking distance. We were even able to check out the harbour and public gardens on foot. Pretty good for a couple of seniors! The staff at the hotel were very helpful and I had the the best breakfast ever in their restaurant. The granola with yoghurt and fresh fruit followed by French toast with bananas baked in maple syrup was to die for!

The hotel is right at Penn Station and only - block from Macy's. Very convenient. Can walk to Times Square in ----- minutes. We stayed at the Metro Room and it was super small. The bathroom (one of the smallest I have seen in a North American hotel) doesn't look like it was renovated. Bathroom needs improvement but the room was fine. The beds were super comfortable and the carpet was clean. Rate is cheaper than surrounding hotels.

This is the second time I have stayed at this Marriott in Chicago. The greatest thing about this hotel is the location, it is exactly where you want to be for shopping, entertainment, nightlife etc. On the other hand, there are things I put up with at this hotel for the location. The lobby is always packed with people, I compared it to a homeless shelter at one point. Kids running around, luggage everyone, etc. It is a very big and busy hotel is what it amounts to. The rooms are okay, pretty small, but decent, we didn't spend much time in them anyways. The bathroom is also tiny and has no ventilation, which is a little annoying. On the morning of our departure, which happened to be the day after -th of July, our maid was knocking on the door at -:--am! We told her to come back, and she continued to knock on all the doors around us. We had a long drive ahead of us and unfortunantely were not able to get back to sleep after this. 
The service was great, the conceirge was very helpful with restaurant recommendations and a boat tour we did. I did not use the other amenities, tried to use the pool but it was always so packed with kids and families. The bar was decent, although as usual, way over priced. Self Park was $-- a night, which is somewhat normal in a big city. Overall, I would stay here again because of the great location.

This hotel is truly - star from top to bottom. The entire staff goes out of their way to help and please you. The public areas are beautiful. The room was the best I have ever seen. Everything about it was top quality. I just love this hotel.
It is in a great location too.
I highly recommend staying here if you are in Boston.
Everything was wonderful. Good location. Rooms spacious with amenities. I recommend everyone to stay at this hotel. Very Clean

A very nice hotel and location! We love coming to Shelter Island and walking in the park along the water's edge. When we can stay there too it's even better! Trip Advisor offered a special lower price on Memorial Day weekend here and we took it. The check in staff were friendly. The room was listed as a non view but we looked out over the parking lot to the park and water so we thought it was great! The room was clean. The bed was comfortable. The maid forgot to clean out the coffee pot the first day but did it the next day. The breakfast at the restaurant was good and it has windows looking out at the marina. The hostess and wait staff were very good. It was a very enjoyable stay!

The hallways stink of smoke, and even if your room is non-smoking the smell inevitably seeps in. If they are going to allow smoking they should segregate by floor. 
The room was a little tired but ok, with a kitchenette, in-room coffee, comfortable bed, and good wifi. The hotel's address is on the interstate frontage road but it's actually set back quite a ways by a long access driveway so was pretty quiet. Breakfast was the usual waffles, bread, and yogurt. Nothing special but adequate. It's the cheapest option I found in this part of town, and ok for a couple of nights.

My daughter and her husband, travelled with my husband and me to attend her graduation at Johns Hopkins. The Inn was a cross between a great B&B and a small Inn. It actually was the best of both. The rooms were very large, the harbor view lovely...especially with the complimentay bottle of wine upon check-in! Everything was within a - mile radius...a perfect location. Very, very memorable. They know how to do it right. The value was exceptional as well.

If this property wasn't where it is, and we hadn't slept like babies (love black-out curtains that do their job!), I'd probably have just given it three stars. No big shakes, nothing to raise hell about really. Definitely have some suggestions, though...
A friend and I stayed four nights -- girls' weekend for NYEve. At check-in I was told we had a suite. But the suite had a king bed and we each wanted our own, so instead they put us in a top floor room on the back (river) side of the hotel w- two queen beds. (Couldn't complain about the view of the river and SoCo, and if it had been during the bat migration I don't think there could be a better spot!) It was your standard double room: rather small, less-than-stellar art on the walls, tiny coffee maker in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""dressing"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" area (just a well-lit counter beneath a mirror and wall-mounted hair dryer), flat-screen telly w- basic cable, and no fridge (you have to order one as you would a roll-away, and they charge for them). But it was plenty clean. The bathroom was small and dated, it could definitely use an overhaul and some cleaner-brighter lighting. The only truly below-average item in the room was the closet -- not even deep enough for the hangers to fit once you hang something on them! And it's behind the bathroom door, which you have to close every time you want to access the closet. Just... yeah, weirdest closet ever. We heard the person next door to us once, and housekeeping doing their thing loudly one morning, but it was a mostly quiet stay.
What a great location, though! Close enough to be on -th Street in a heartbeat but far enough away to avoid the noise, and easy walks to both the Capitol building and South Congress. We didn't do any jogging that weekend, but the running path along Town Lake is right at the foot of the property.
The lobby and gift shop are small, but there's a great fireplace for those waiting-lounging moments. Friday's and Starbucks were decent perks -- had two or three good lunches and coffee drinks over our five-day stay. That's a --% Starbucks, though -- they make most but not all drinks. Very friendly there and at Friday's. There's a large computer monitor (internet station) between the front desk and the gift shop where you can check your email or hit the web. There's a --min courtesy limit, but we were on there for -- mins at one point buying tickets online and nobody was waiting on us. Plenty flexible and fine for most people's needs.
The staff is definitely taciturn, and at times you're waiting on them. If you're the gregarious type, which we are, then they respond. But they're not inclined to offer the smiles first, especially at the front desk (concierge and bell staff were friendlier).
I was surprised to learn that there's no courtesy van to-from the airport. Not enough traffic-business to warrant it? It's those blasted CLOSETS! :-) SuperShuttle is $-- one way, and the Airport Express (bus) is only a buck with pickup-dropoff seven blocks away -- otherwise you're stuck with a $-- cab ride.
We agreed we'd stay here again, but only if we could snag a(nother) discounted rate.

This was a really nice hotel, the room and bathroom are both modern and clean. I stayed in a room with two double beds, and the beds were very comfortable. There was a fridge in the room, and free wi-fi internet access. There is subway entrance just meters from the front door of the hotel which was great. I stayed here for seven nights, and found the hotel to be a great base for exploring New York.

I stayed - days in Dec ----, I chose this hotel because of the positive reviews on Trip Advisor, and they were right. The rooms are just fine. The lobby is nice, the staff are friendly and helpful.
 There is a $-- per day charge for parking in their parkade. Also you have to go to the front desk and have your parking validated every time you leave the hotel, which is a real pain if there's a line up. 
 Be sure to try the buffet at 'The Proud Bird' - a warbird-themed restaraunt clos by on Aviation Blvd. very impressive!

I hadn't stayed at the Cow Hollow in several years. Returned here the other day during a brief stay in SF. As before, fairly priced, clean, convenient and reliable. One of the best things about the Cow Hollow is the clean FREE parking lot. The lodge is located in the trendy Marina District. Lots of good eating places within walking distance. Also, not far from the Exploratorium.

We went here for the Cherry Blossom festival in April ----. We picked the hotel because of it's location. It's right next to the Verizon Center and Chinatown. The room was clean, however the AC didnt work the night we stayed. We tried to turn on the AC, but somehow only hot air came out. Not a good night sleep for my boyfriend and I. We also pulled our car into the valet parking in front of the hotel but got rejected by their doorman. Luckily we saw a parking place across of the hotel and had to carry our luggage across the street. Other than that, the stay at the hotel was decent.

From top to bottom, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The staff was attentive, efficient and friendly. Our room was absolutely lovely ... better than expected. We only had a short stay, and would have loved to have extended it, but unfortunately we did not pack accordingly.
The room had a comfortable sitting area with a desk facing Oak Street Beach, a flat screen TV, and a convenient wet bar, microwave and mini refrigerator (all nicely concealed in beautiful cabinets.)
The bathroom was quite spacious and tastefully decorated. It was accessible from both the sitting area and the master bedroom. Between the master bedroom and bathroom was a nice vanity area.
The master bedroom was also tastefully decorated with a very comfortable bed and a view of the lake. The bedding was top notch and what you would expect of nicer hotels. The hotel was very quiet, so you could really get a good nights sleep.
We took advantage of the complimentary breakfest and was pleasantly surprised at the wide offerings, the helpful staff, and the views of city life bustling outside the window. They also had an outdoor cafe.
All in all, if you're popping into the city for a short stay or long, I think you'll enjoy the staff, accommodations and locations of this gem. A great value for the money.

My husband and I stayed at the Omni for All-Star Weekend ----. Overall, the hotel was great. Our room was comfortably sized and very clean and the staff was helpful and kind. Another plus was the hotel's breakfast, which was delicious and inexpensive. The only con about staying here is that it is a bit far from downtown Dallas. Unless you are renting a car, you will spend a lot of money getting to town and back.

We booked this hotel through Expedia.com for a one night special rate. When we arrived the young man who checked us in asked if it was our first time to stay with them and we said yes. He upgraded our Standard King to a Junior King Suite. How nice was that!!!
The room was great and everyone was so helpful and friendly. I would recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to San Francisco.

Although I had read good reviews on this site I was still taken aback by the excellent location of this hotel - it really was on Times Square.We had a bit of a search to find the entrance but it was worth hunting for. The next surprise was the lack of noise from the street as we had a wonderful view of Times Square. By New York standards the room was spacious and well equipped. The bed was very comfy and the shower was super. Would certainly stay at this hotel again.

Was there for four days for a conference. The property is very nice, clean and appears to be well maintained. The hotel has a subtle old school elegance to it. The rooms are adequately sized, a bit smaller than """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""newer"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Westins, but plenty of room. There was a large desk in my room, which was perfect for getting things done.
Only real downside for me, the gym was small. And small by even hotel standards. So if you are into working out, you will probably want to use a city gym nearby.

We stayed for one night after finishing a fantastic Holland America Line Mexico cruise, and it was a wonderful end to our vacation. The hotel is only a short cab ride from the cruise terminal. The setting on Shelter Island is gorgeous, relaxed, and very family-friendly. Our two-year-old loved the great playground right across the street from the hotel, where we flew a kite and had a picnic. Our teenager (and her dad) loved the free loaner bicycles offered by the hotel. While our two-year-old took his afternoon nap in the room, I sat on the balcony and got to look out at the beautiful harbor view, and watch my daughter and husband enjoy riding bikes together on the gorgeous biking-walking path (there are paths all over the hotel property and island). Perfection! Our room was a standard room with a balcony, but felt very luxurious and new. The pools and restaurant are fantastic and moderately priced. Best of all, the service is the friendliest I've experienced anywhere, EVER. Seriously! We stayed here once before (on a cruise - years ago) and it is still my favorite hotel, even one of my favorite places on earth. We can't wait for our next visit!

We stayed here last week and I booked it because I trusted the DoubleTree name and the fact that it appeared to be close to Penn Station (Subway should I choose to go around New York with my kids).
Quick Facts: 
-. The rooms are extremely small and so is the bathroom. However, since this Hotel is very new, everything looks clean and sparkling.
-. It took forever and multiple reminders to get anything from the Service staff - and I am talking about simple things such as refills for the coffeemaker after - days of stay (and no refills in between). They appear to be extremely understaffed.
-. The neighborhood is not great to walk around after dark - it is dark and smelly and there is construction on the same street....
-. Unless you get a great deal on the stay - I woudl not recommend this place.

The receptionist was rude and very unhelpful saying we would have to pay $--- for a camp bed, after a long argument we were given this free and told we would get a room with twin beds the next day! The room we got the following night was lovely, ery big and had everything you could need. This hotel is very noisy as it is right in the center of New York so if you like your sleep i would advise against this hotel. However if you are here to shop ten tis hotel is great as it is ery central! I would go back but only if the price was right i would definetly shop around more next time!

I traveled to Indianapolis for a meeting at the -M EAR facility. The hotel was very accomodating to all of the international guests that accompanied me. While the hotel is totally non smoking (a bit of a problem for the smokers in the group), the staff was very helpful in changing rooms so that the people that do smoke were able to have rooms on the first floor. The hotel was very clean, so compliments to the cleaning staff and the breakfast was nice (food offered was hot and filled frequently so there was a nice selection available during the entire breakfast time).

I would recommend this resort to anyone, especially couples and families. My spouse and I spent two nights at this resort. It completely met our expectations. We choose a bay view room in the tower building overlooking the bay and pool area. Although the room itself was a bit on the smaller side it was nice and perfect for the two of us. The room was very clean, had a private balcony, fridge, nice bathroom and tasty in room coffee. The staff was friendly and very accommodating. The pool area was gorgeous with private poolside cabanas. We had a perfect stay and can't wait to come back.

My Family and I stayed at the Omni Berkshire for - nights over the Thanksgiving weekend. This is an excellent hotel in an ideal location. You are a - minute or less walk from everything (Rockefeller Center, Times square, Fifth Avenue shops and Central park.) The hotel itself is very nice and for a fairly large hotel has a boutique feel to it. We had a standard King room which was more than nicely firnished and had a suprisingly large bathroom. The hotel staff was also very nice and we never had a problem getting our car out of the valet. Finally we booked the hotel on hotels.com for under $--- a night which was at least a $--- less than any other - or - star hotel in the city. so it was also a great value.

I stayed t this Sheraton - nights while on business in Dallas. I booked it through Priceline and I got a deal for under -- usd-night. I have to say I have been lucky.
The hotel is definitely great value for money. Rooms are new and with the typical Sheraton amenities you would expect. As every Sheraton in the US, the bathroom is rather small, hardly fitting two people at the same time. 
The whole hotel is new (or renovated) and the spacious lobby, very white and bright, is an elegant meeting point. Staff is efficient and courteous.
One of the main features of this hotel is the complimentary buffet breakfast - a first for a Sherton. Quality and choice is pretty good - certainly better than a Hampton Inn!
The hotel features a bar-restaurant that is open to the lobby and rather stylish and pleasant. I have not tried it so I cannot comment on the quality, but it was always full of people at night.
The outdoor pool is not big but it is big enough. Sun loungers are comfortable and they are perfect to chill out and relax while reading a book or listening to some music. The gym was new and very well appointed.
The hotel boasts also various conference rooms and an outdoor parking which comes at -- usd-night.
Wi-fi is not free in room but it is free in the lobby area. However, we got free wi-fi in our room from the lobby.
I was very positively surprised and happy with this hotel; at this rate, I could not have hoped for anything better!

We stayed at the Omni at South Park as part of a wedding and were very impressed with the beautiful, spacious rooms, the great guest service and the wonderful restaurants and bar. We had a very delightful stay.

The Channel Inn is in a really awesome location. It's right on the water and they have FREE parking, something unheard of in DC. We walked to the Smithsonian and to a show at the Warner Theater. Easy, fun walk. 
The rooms are old looking, but if you are like me, and have plans to do things all day, all you really need is a comfy bed to come back to.
Gripes include:
-. Unfriendly staff
-. Construction was being done while I was there, and the workers started around -:--, hammering away at the room next to us. They were also right outside of our room walking around on the roof
-. As soon as I get to any hotel I put the """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" DO NOT DISTURB"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sign out on the door handle. Will definitely return. Great price and location.
A great amenity they really need is mini fridges!

This hotel is excellently located very close to Times Square and Broadway and very well priced for this location. Although the rooms were a bit small, this is normal for mid-price New York hotels, and they were clean, well equipped and recently decorated. The staff were friendly and helpful. Our only problem was a mistake with the bill, but this was honourably and quickly sorted out once we were back in the UK and were able to feed back our original booking information. To avoid this, ask for an email confirmation of your rate when booking and take a copy of the email with you. Then ensure that the correct rate is shown on your registration card for all nights of your stay. However, this problem apart, we would thoroughly recommend the Washington Jefferson

Ok, the reviews are definitely right - this is a party hotel. On a saturday night the hallways smell like pot and the pre-parties are happening in the hall. The ratio of me:drunk girls would have been excited -- years ago but now i'm old and boring.
But contrary to some of the other reviews i found the staff to be helpful and as requested they put me in a quiet room. 
The room itself had its wear marks but overall was well appointed and easy to live in.

We stayed at the Hotel Chandler this past weekend, July --th & --th ----. From the time we arrived everything was better than expected. We received a very warm welcome from the front desk and even received an upgrade to a Deluxe Queen. 
The room furnishings were very nice and the bedding extra comfortable. The bathroom was surprisingly large and nicely outfitted. 
The staff was every bit as helpful as they could possibly be. We were on a tight schedule and they assisted with information about the theatre we were heading to. 
The weekend was extra special thanks to our experience at The Hotel Chandler. We will definitely be staying here again in the near future.

We stayed at this hotel primarily due to the very high ratings on Trip Advisor and the relative reasonable price.
On the good side:
Reasonable price for DC, especially considering the location.
Location is excellent. Near the White House and Metro stop. 
Nice, friendly concierge staff. Very helpful in finding excellent food.
Rooms very quiet.
On the bad side:
Restaurant very expensive with average food. At least there was a Starbucks at the next corner.
Very small. Other than the bar and the room, there is no where to sit and relax.
Biggest complaint is the bed was very uncomfortable. Mattress was old and very saggy.
We provided a helpful complaint upon check out by never heard anything.

My husband and I got the romance package a few weeks ago, and it was okay. First of all, I like to prepay for hotel stays - I have had problems in the past, and it makes me feel better. My husband and I travel every weekend, and the Library was the first hotel that wouldn't allow me to prepay. After weighing up boutique hotels downtown with high parking costs vs staying at the Argonaut. w decided on it for three nights-booked by phone and did the parking, breakfast, cable car ticket package. It was a bit of a splurge for us, but worth every penny! This place was so charming and enjoyable. From the minute we met Steve, the valet, we knew it was going to be a good experience! All the staff seemed really well chosen and went out of their way to help, but Steve really made it special! 
Our room was lovely! We loved the nautical theme and attention to detail - alot of thought has gone into the restoration of this old cannery building and the decorating. So clean and well maintained! Starbucks coffee and Aveda toiletries and a well stocked mini bar (right down to telescopes for the kids!) with prices we thought weren't too bad at all. 
We were lucky to have a window with a view to the lovely colors and liveliness of the courtyard and even had a bit of a city view with the Transamerica building right there. Yes, there was music playing throughout the day, but if you shut your windows you heard nothing. We did have a noisy baby crying for awhile the first night and it was pretty loud, but it stopped, which was the important thing! 
Not too keen on the large dogs trotting about with their owners, we must say, and I do suffer from allergies, but we had asked for a non pet room and I was fine. 
 The breakfast was excellent....one entree, juice coffee came with our package. We also dined in the restaurant and had a few drinks one evening....all good. I must say though that if they opened the room up without that double row of tables in the middle it would be better. If you end up on the non-bar side, it lacks ambience. 
Super location. Helpful staff - they had stamps to sell and mailed the postcards for me. A tip from the concierge to get over the the City Wide Tours around the corner for around ten-ish enabled us to score some Alcatraz tickets (with the purchase of their tours of course) - which was great, as they were sold out for the next few days.
It was for a late run out to the island which limited your time there, but it worked. 
The tours with these open double decker buses were great. We did the City tour, the park tour and the run to Sausalito and then we took the ferry back. 
The wine hour they lay on daily was very generous and we had fun getting to know other guests. Yes, there were lots of families and kids and we were a couple, but there were others like us too and everyone was very happy to be there, you could tell.
We would highly recomment the Hotel Argonaut!

Based on previous reviews I made a mental checklist on things to look for:
Isolated location? I didn't see any convenient places within walking distance. If you're going elsewhere to eat, be prepared to drive or make a substantial walk. It also seems like there are no other people around unless they're in their cars. 
Parking ? Yes, $-- out back, $-- valet. Thanks for the warning. I can understand why someone might be uncomfortable walking from the back lot (see above). I felt okay, but I'm sure my wife would have reservations if she were alone.
Staff? Check in and out was quick and convenient, the front desk staff I dealt with was friendly and informative and even the cleaning people acknowledged us and were friendly.
Elevator problems? We didn't have any problems, but we were amused at the warning signs and the printed explanation in the hotel information packet. Yes, it's a long term problem.
Chipped bathtub? Sure, there they are. It didn't affect the operation, but with the repairs and old tiles, it almost felt like you stepped into a different level of room to shower.
Hair in the drain? None, but I have a headful of my own, if needed. The bathroom, as well as the rest of the room, was very clean.
The location was convenient for us because it was just a few blocks from the rental car center and our plans to explore the coast to the north of town (Santa Barbara) as well as south (Orange Coast). We had a late arrival and early departure, so being near the airport helped with time. 
We got back fairly late one night and had appetizers in Shula's, which were very good. Also, our package included the breakfast buffet. Since it was included, I forgot to note the price, but we were very pleased with the quality, selection and attention of the staff.
The pool area was very nice and there were families using it most of the time that we were there. I didn't have a chance to check out the exercise facility. 
We were pleased with our experience as everything went off without a glitch. Based on this stay and, for a reasonable price, we'd stay here again and not discourage anyone from trying it.

We spent - nights at the Hotel George at the beginning of our trip up the coast to Boston. The hotel is very well presented, the staff as friendly and helpful as you could want (particularly Shana, who was the personification of charm and professionalism). 
The hotel is well-located for the Capitol, White House, etc. and also Penn Station, which was useful as we were heading to Baltimore and New York, which are on a direct train line from Penn - see Amtrak timetables. 
Be warned that it is quite a long way from Dulles airport to the centre of Washington, so if you have the time, take the train, as our taxi was pretty expensive.
We were in DC in the middle of a massive heatwave, and when we got back to the hotel they provided iced water etc to cool us down, and they do offer coffee and pastries to take to your room for breakfast if you don't want to pay for a full breakfast.
Dinner in the bistro attached to the hotel offers very good food (and is reputedly popular with the local politicians, senators, etc,) however it is very expensive, and we found our waitress to be over-attentive and intrusive; interrupting us when we were in the middle of a conversation, etc. which was pretty annoying.
If you walk out of the hotel and turn right, there is a liquor store on the opposite side of the road, so you can buy beers, soft drinks etc to store in the hotel minibars. Also, in the same direction there is a Starbucks on the corner of the next block. 
This is not a great neighbourhood, and there seemed to be quite a lot of homeless people around, so do be careful if you go out at night. Don't wear conspicuous amounts of jewellery. 
Whilst I don't have a problem with the hotel itself, which met my expectations, I have to say that next time I'm in Washington I'll stay in Georgetown-Foggy Bottom, which is more residential and peaceful, although a metro ride from the centre.
Overall, this is a welcoming hotel which offers good value for money.
