The location is great for shopping and you can walk to pretty much any major tourist attraction in the central area of Seattle. We chose to take taxis twice when we were too tired to walk ----- minutes at the end of the day. Most places are under a -- minute walk.
However, I was disappointed with this Westin. This is normally one of our favorite chain hotels. The carpet in our room was quite dirty and bore multiple large stains throughout the room. Yuk! The bed was the awesome beds Westin is well known for. The room was otherwise clean, but the bathroom was not what I would call large. It was adequate for two people as long as one was in the shower while the other got ready. 
A quick peek into another room while being cleaned showed that it too had an old, dirty carpet. I've never had to use slippers in a Westin hotel room before, but this time I did. Also, even though we were on one of the higher floors (even though we'd requested a low floor) we could hear sirens, honking and the traffic below. I wear earplugs so no bother for me at night, but my family could hear it.
Lastly, the two times we asked the valets or doormen for directions or information it was incorrect.

I enjoyed my stay at the Hyatt Harborside. The rooms were beautiful and comfortable, and the extra charge for the harbor view is worth it. I adore the pillows. Although I asked for a quiet room, I did have a lot of noise. There was a crying baby next door (nothing the hotel could fix, I realize) and the second night I was there, there was a loud and drunk couple across the hall. The woman locked herself out of her room and kept pounding on doors. Again, not sure what the hotel can do about foolishness.

So I wandered down to the restaurant, where it took nearly an hour to get a Pub Club Waffle and when it arrived it was cold. I could not catch my server's attention to send it back, and she did not check on me the entire time I was in the restaurant. The restaurant is incredibly expensive, even by Boston standards. The lack of fridge in the room is also a problem and for the cost of adding one to your room, you could buy a small one and leave it behind as a gift for the next customer.
In terms of the shuttle, once I figured out the system (you have to call every time you want or need a shuttle), it worked fine - quick and quite efficient to get me back and forth to the T. But I sat at the airport for a while, not realizing I needed to call. 
The biggest irritation to me was housekeeping on my last day. First, a housekeeper tried getting in my room at -:--. Recently renovated, the Ink-- is the perfect place to stay. Close to the Hudson River and Times Square. Beautiful terrace at the top with a great view of MidTown Manhattan. Conveniently located near -th avenue and its restaurants.
Our room (DeLuxe with a view) was very spacious and well equipped.

We stayed at the St. Gregory for one night while driving up to Canada. We got a fantastic deal + free parking - by booking online at their site. 
The hotel was very clean and luxurious with modern amenities (bedding, sheets etc...). We had a corner suite which offered a view of both streets. There were two televisions in our room, one in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""den"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" area with a pull out couch and the other in the bedroom area. The room was also equiped with a refridgerator & game system as well.
We did dine in the on site resturant. It was a nice atmosphere, but rather slow service. Beware of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""included """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" breakfast, it's not free. 
There was a nice little pub with an outdoor patio just down the street (on corner) and I believe there was a Subway sandwich resturant & drug store across the street.
We got up early to tour the sites so we checked out early. They allowed us to call up our car, put the luggage inside and keep our car in their parking garage at no charge until we departed that afternoon. I thought this was very nice. 
We had a brisk walk to all the monuments and sites and later ate a wonderful deli around the corner (wish I could remember the name).
We would definitely stay here again while in DC.

As others have said, Times Square it is not! However, it's only a couple of blocks out and it seems lots of other places do the same. Easy self-check in at the computers in the lobby. The room was clean, small, but perfectly OK for what we wanted. The moving bed was really good for making more room during the day. Sheets are a bit too small and untuck themselves completely everynight. Covers are two sheets with a duvet in between - a duvet cover would have been better but it was fine.
The bathroom set up is a little odd but I can't see how it would cause anybody problems. There is a sliding glass door across the front of the toilet-shower bit. This, coupled with the floor to ceiling curtains means you have complete privacy in the bathroom, unless one wants to use the sink while another is in the toilet or shower, and you would get that in any hotel with a regular bathroom. Floor to ceiling window so you can gaze out over the city while cleaning your teeth.
Complimentary hot drinks on each floor are really good. There's a microwave and fridge in case you want to be organised and get your food in advance. Housekeeping was good, we left our Do Not Disturb sign on the door the first day as the room was chaos. They left another one over the top to say they'd tried to come but had seen the sign and if we wanted fresh towels etc to give them a call, and they left us a voicemail too.
They have a Happy Hour at the bar, but the staff do look down their noses at you somewhat when you use it. We had a few beers, sparking wine for $- each, and they do food. The only catch is they expect you to keep presenting yourself at the bar to get your food as if you've got it on the happy hour deal, they don't tend to deliver it to your table! You can't sit at the bar so you have no choice but to sit down. Similar with the free breakfast - they offer it but when you take them up on it they look down their noses at you and make you sit at specific tables because the majority are reserved for those ordering breakfast from the menu (and paying at least $-- for the priveledge) which very few people were doing.
Free computer use and printing which is good. Free luggage storage with the Yobot. Nothing to stop non-residents turning up and using any of these facilities as there's no room key check to get up to Four where they are all located, but you need your key to get the lift to the rooms and into the galleys for the tea-coffee.

Definitely up to Kimpton standards; the Monaco was clean, service was excellent, the restaurant was quite good, and the bed was very comfortable.
Its somewhat funky as its an old building wrapping around a courtyard, but they have spruced up the room, and the high ceiling are a nice counterbalance to the smallish rooms.
Free wifi and a very good location are big plusses as well. I recommend it.

My husband and I took a day to ourselves and went to Columbus, Ohio to visit friends. While there it got late and we stayed. we drove by Comfort Inn & Suites. When we walked in we had notice a BIG change from past stays. The whole hotel has been remolded. Lobby is so comfortable with breakfast . We checked in with the Night Clerk (checked in around -a.m.)She was very nice and helpful. The rooms are wonderful. new beds, couch,refrig. and micowave. Very clean. The hotel is so close to downtown that we got to go to some of the clubs also.The price of the room was great. So if you are planning a trip to Columbus Ohio stop by and check out Comfort Inn. Although the room itself wasn't too big, it was very clean, with comfortable bed (Marriott speciality) and very nice complimentary toiletries. Lunch in the restaurant was fine - expensive for what it was, but hey what can you expect if you stay in the hotel. Breakfast the following morning was excellent - fantastic choice from the buffet.
Agree with comments about having to pay for internet in-room. For a hotel of this standard, its penny-pinching to charge guests for this. However, very much appreciated the shuttle bus to airport terminals.

I stayed in the Palmer House Hilton for - nights on business. When I made my reservation I specifically requested a room away from all the banging and drilling, which I didn't get...I was one floor above it. But as I was up early every morning it didn't effect my sleep too much.
My room was big and clean, and the cleaning staff did a great job cleaning my room every day. No complaints there. I found the concierge (male) extremely helpful on all times I needed his help. He even recommended a great little nail bar around the corner from the hotel.
I had a drink in the lobby one night, the atmosphere was good, but it's very dark and I've been in much nicer places so couldn't really see what all the hype was about! The service wasn't great and I was given my bill before I asked for it. I wasn't happy about that.
I'd no issue with checking out. My bill was in order and all I had to do was call a number and I was checked out automatically.
If I was going on a holiday I wouldn't stay here, but it was fine for business.

Check in and check out were fast and the staff was friendly. I had both a cocktail in the lounge and breakfast in the restaurant, and while typically expensive, both were good. 
The bathroom was large and very nice, albeit a bit cold. Robe, slippers and L'Occitane products are provided. The room was fine, although the door to the room was very squeaky. My room had no view but was pretty quiet, which is important to me. There was a nice Bose clock radio that you could actually figure out how to set the alarm.
My only complaint would be the bedding featured only a flat sheet over the mattress and a comforter -- no top sheet. This implies that the maid changes the comforter cover between each guest. At least I hope she does! I would have liked a top sheet between me and the comforter. I'm sure I could have asked for one but never thought about it until late at night.
I will stay there again, asking in advance for a top sheet.

I agree the Curtis is seemingly a good value for its overall quality, service, appearance, and location. However, I'll echo some of criticisms already made about noise. The doors for each room are apparently unable to be closed without a fairly thunderous slam. That, combined with a significant gap between the floor and door forces you to hear pretty much everything going on out in the hall. I usually rely on a fan setting on the AC to drown out things like this, but their units don't have a continuous fan setting. 
The quirky style, nice rooms, friendly staff, and ideal location would make it a great hotel in my book, if it weren't for some glaring basic noise problems.

Was very happy with this hotel. Stayed for business and would go back for any occasion. The room I had could've used only one bed though as - doubles made it a bit tight, but this was not a concern. The breakfast they have is amazing - make sure you stay for this meal in the morning - very high quality food. Staff was friendly and helpful. Location is great - within walking distance of all of my meetings and had plenty of restaurants and shops close by.

Nice room, good view, clean and comfortable chairs. I noted lots of mention of the showers. Ours was a simple hand held with less than adequate pressure which was a surprise considering some of the hydrants we'd experienced elsewhere on the trip. Locations is fine for the business district but as passing tourists with no interest in NASCAR, it lacked peripheral interest. If I find myself back in Charlotte, I'd be tempted to try the alternatives, but only because I'm curious.

This hotel rocks! Love it! Modern, sophisticated, wonderful ambience, great position and above all, the staff are fantastic! Health Club wasn't available due to refurbishment; an alternative was available around the corner, but we didn't use it, so can't comment.

Great location downtown Memphis on Union Avenue only a few blocks from world famous Beale Street. Nice clean rooms, polite staff and reasonable price.....across the street from the Peabody Hotel and Autozone Park.

Stayed here -------. It IS an older property w- not many luxury updates but I still like it for the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""charm"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". We seem to get a room w- a different layout everytime. Who knows how many times the rooms have been reconfigured over the years. What a magical place! Right in the heart of Times Square theater district, this place is outstanding, even if a bit pricey. It has a whimsical, yet classic decor and color scheme. The bed was the most comfortable I've ever encountered in my travels, and service throughout the hotel was first class. With a view of Broadway from high up, the best elevator system I've ever seen, staying at the Marquis was an unforgettable experience and worth the big splurge! I probably won't ever go back because it's expensive, but it's the perfect spot for a business trip or a romantic getaway!

I really liked this hotel. I arrived after checking out of another hotel early as I was unable to get any sleep due to the noise. I know NYC is a noisy place but this was unbelievable. Anyway told the check in staff I wanted a quiet room and was taken up to see - rooms. Decided on one and asked if the air conditioning in the room could be turned off. It can't be but they sent up the engineer to shut the vents off for me. They were unbelievably patient and kept saying it really was not any trouble, but I did feel a bit petulant about it all. Absolutely nothing was too much trouble. For staff attitude alone I would stay there again.
Rooms are small but have everything you need. Bed was super comfy and the bathroom while small too, was clean and had all amenities. Bonus for me was being able to open the window just a little for some fresh air
Complimentary coffee in the loby is a nice touch.
Ihad booked several Broadway shows and it was so convenient to walk a couple of blocks to the theatre. I would definately stay there again.

I stayed at The Alex for one night, Oct. --. I loved the location, so near to so much and close to the subway. However, as has been mentioned in a couple other reviews, the hotel is shabby. In my room , the wall paper was pealing, and the clock did not work. While for the most part the staff was quite friendly and helpful, on the day I left, I told the porters, who supposedly told the doormen the name of the car service I was waiting for. After I called the car service, I found out the car should have already arrived. Sure enough, when I walked outside, there it was. We had been waiting for each other for about -- minutes. The doormen did not even seem to have been aware. Last time I was in NYC, the hotel was better all around. Both times, the booking of the hotel was done by someone else-the previous time was with a tour group.

Having booked this hotel several months in advance I had become concerned and really wondered what to expect after reading some of the most recent reviews, but luckily my worst fears were not realised! This is an OK hotel offering what most people would expect given its pricing, location and 'raison d'etre'.
We arrived at -pm, - hours before official check in time, but we waited no more than -- minutes while staff worked to get our room ready. The room was spacious with a living area and small kitchenette including fridge and microwave. It was clean but to be honest in need of redecoration. Complimentary breakfast is basic.
Obviously its siting right by Gracelands is the hotel's main draw, but shuttles are available to Beale Street and Sun Studios -- - --mins away.
Don't be put off staying here, just have realistic expectations.

We stayed at the Fairmont in April. We booked two connecting rooms--one for my husband and three boys, the other, for my brother, a quadriplegic, who needed handicap accesibility. I found the valet staff upon arrival very curt and unfriendly, Neither the valet, or, his staff welcomed us with a smile, or a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Welcome, to the Fairmont"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I was instantly irritated with this considering my great experiences with other """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""higher end"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotels, and their courteous and accomodating staff. I was always under the impression, as far as hotels go, that you get what you pay for. This is not so at the Fairmont, strike number one. The amount we paid for each room went as follows:(first night $---, second night $---, third night $---). As we checked in, my husband asked if he could have the bill split two ways--one bill I would pay for my room, the other to my brother, for his room--The clerk replied with """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""We can't do that."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" strike number two. We wanted a hotel with a pool, so the boys could swim. We were charged $--.-- each day, for use of the pool and the fitness center. The children were not allowed into the fitness center, this was evident by the large red signs stating no one under the age of -- allowed. I understand this, but when my son, came into the fitness center to find me, and ask a question, he was hounded by a fitness staffer. It was obvious he was not supposed to be there. The children were designated to swim in a very small area of the pool, and not allowed into the whirlpool, which was two feet away from the pool, or, the sauna, which was three feet away--Not even the option """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""children allowed if accompanied by an adult"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The second day, I was to meet my neice and her boyfriend for lunch, I suggested eating outside in the open air atrium, where they have many table,chairs and umbrella's. My wife and I stayed here - night in late Sept. The hotel was extremely nice but the location was definitely not the best. While it is within walking distance of the Alamo and Riverwalk, it's not exactly in the safest part of the neighborhood. In fact, we decided to drive over instead of walk so that we would be a bit closer and wouldn't have to walk as far after dark. Also parking is very limited at the hotel. The staff told us there was an extra parking area around the side of the hotel across the street that we could use but I didn't feel comfortable leaving my car there. When we returned from the Riverwalk, the parking lot was full and we had to park on the side of the street in front of the hotel.
The hotel itself is very nice with large, spacious, clean rooms and a very friendly staff. Our room had an lcd television and the bed was VERY comfortable. The view from the room was pretty bad with one window looking right at an old billboard. The other window was a view of the bridge. We didn't mind though since we were out most of the evening anyways. It was also somewhat noisy due to being next to the interstate but it really didn't bother us as we had no problems sleeping that evening (likely because we had been driving all day and were very tired)
If you don't mind the location, it's a very nice hotel. It's only about a ----- minute walk to the Alamo and Riverwalk although might not feel quite as safe after dark.

I have the pleasure of staying here for just over a week. I had a great stay and wonderful service. The rooms are first rate with a very funky vibe. Beds are quite comfortable and the room service is great. Couple of gripes but only minor, the Wifi is very slow and my bathroom had some early onset mould appearing on the ceiling. 
I will gladly co e back here next time and recommend to all my friends that can afford it.

PROS
- Location! This is in the heart of midtown--perfect location for a first time trip
- Recently updated rooms & it shows A little girly but nice
- Great housekeeping, clean room each day
- Did I mention the great location?
CONS
- Don't expect directions or suggestions from the doormen or desk staff They didn't know the area & said we could """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""look up stuff in the phone book""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""
- Know that the on-site food options close early

This was our -th time to Chicago for St. Patrick's day weekend. (about -th overall). Never stayed here before but always wanted to. Got a great rate and was surprised how nice it was. We stayed on a floor that was just recently renovated. It was very clean and spacious. The hotel itself is conventent to everything. I think the only thing I was a little dispointed in was the lobby bar. It was nice, but very smaill. If you don't get there early, you will not get a seat. But there are many bars very close that you can go to for a night cap. I would stay there again.

The Harrington is steps away from everything worth seeing, this is the most important part (for my husband and I, anyway). If you are looking for a spa-like retreat, this hotel is not for you. 
The hotel is old and run-down (some might find this charming?), but the staff is cheerful and helpful. Because of its central location, book early - we stayed there at the end of May ---- and there were at least - large groups of teenagers staying there (we're talking ----- people per group) and the hotel was booked solid.
Our small queen room faced a brick wall (it was on the inside of the building, on the -th floor) but we did not hear a sound from the busy streets below (this was a common complaint we overheard from other guests - the hotel is at a very busy intersection in Washington DC's business district)
There is no parking on the premises, their parking garage is about two blocks away, a brisk - minute walk from the hotel; they charge $-- per day. It is best to park the car and walk, as almost everything you want is very close by, including shopping, restaurants, coffee shops and monuments.
There are two restaurants downstairs, one a breakfast place (which we did not visit) and sports bars with mediocre food, tired wait staff and $-- pitchers of beer.
We would definitely stay here again, you can't beat that location!

We had a King Suite so we had windows on - sides which offered us a great view of the stadium as well as a huge pile of what used to be the old RCA Dome. 
Pros - The bed was very comfy, the room was large enough for friends to come visit; the location was great for walking to see the history in the area as well as some great dining experiences. Valet service was extremely polite and very knowledgeable. Terry is awesome and gave us the best ideas on things to do! 
Cons - A tad on the pricey side, the valet is $-- per use, not per night, the bathroom is small with no fan. It could use a vanity area outside the bathroom.
Terry the parking valet gave us some places to see and we did as many as we could fit into our stay. We ate at St. Elmo's and Le Pepe, visited Memorial Circle and the surrounding areas as well as the Capital and the Union Station hotel across the street. All of these were in walking distance to the hotel so that is a huge bonus for us. 
The bed is by far the softest we've ever encountered in a hotel. We were given plenty of pillows and the down comforter was so warm that even with the balcony door open on a cool night we were hot! The King Suite has a nice living room area that was laid out very well along with a neat balcony.
Our last night there was before some Supercross Event at the stadium so some kids were running up & down the hallways and stairs at -- pm. We did call the front desk who did get security involved, although she seemed a little put out by our request. They called a short while later to confirm that things were quiet so that was a very nice touch.
Other than that and our extra $-- fee for valet (since we needed our car one day) we don't really have anything bad to say.

Stayed from -- to -- June ----. Great location for using Muni public transportation—bus, streetcar, and cable car near Powell - Market streets. It was a - minute walk from BART station at Powell. Wide variety of fast food, casual, fine dining restaurants, - movie theaters, and shopping within walking distance.
My single room on the -th floor was between the women’s toilet room and a storage closet. To the right of the storage closet was the men’s toilet room. Each toilet room was the size of a public restroom stall. A few doors away from each toilet room were - bath rooms. Each bath room consisted of a regular bath tub - shower. Entrance to the bath rooms (not toilets) required your hotel key card. There is a double lock on each bath door, one of the locks turned a vacant - occupied sign. There were -- rooms on the -th floor, and I did not have to wait to use the toilet or bath. 
Since I knew about the shared bath, I brought along shower shoes (flip flops). This made it easier when I need to visit the toilet or take a shower. Not necessary, just a recommendation. Water pressure was good, and there was plenty of hot water.
These rooms were retrofitted into an old building, so each room is probably different. My room was approximately --’ x --’, did not include its own bathroom, but it did have a sink. It has high ceilings and is very bright. It had a --” CRT TV mounted on an arm attached to the wall, high over the bed—perfect to lie in bed and watch TV. Small radiator for heating and a regular size ceiling fan with light to cool the room. Fan speed, light w- dimmer was controlled by wall switch.
Biggest change from previous reviews is FREE WiFi. It was slow, but stable. Speedtest showed it downloading below -Mbs—good enough for e-mail and casual surfing. Only constructive feedback is that the fancy Sony CD clock radio in my room was difficult to set because it had so many buttons and options. Actually had to download the instructions from the Internet, even then I did not set it correctly. 
Room, toilets, bath rooms, and all public areas were very clean. My - nights averaged out to be about $-- which is a great value for the location. Would stay here again and have no apprehension of recommending to my female relatives, friends, and co-workers.

Victorian B & B type quaint hotel, complete with continental breakfast and afternoon wine-cheese hour right in the midst of downtown SF. Very attentive and personable service from all, spacious room [we had a jr suite with full kitchen - great for traveling family]. The building is an older structure but we rather liked this to the more """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""modern"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotels around. Very accessible to all transportation so didn't need to bother with a car. Would definitely recommend - and go back!

The Marriott Marquis has a spectacular setting but equally spectacular were the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""added"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" costs, e.g.,an in-room movie rental is over $--; room service for two burgers & one ice-cream was $--.-- and daily WiFi rate is $--.--. On two of our four days here, I had to call to ask that the room be made up when it had not happened by early afternoon. And although we finally got the room I had requested on making the reservation (South Tower, high floor) and although the receptionist noted my request on our check-in, she nonetheless assigned us to a low level, rather """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""tired"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room in the North Tower.

I booked a room at the Adagio for a single night stay, so I wasn't too worried about it since I figured if it was bad, so what. I was pleasantly surprised by the hotel and the room. The hotel is modern, decorated in muted tones. The lobby area is nice if you have to wait and there is a great bar. I didn't eat at the restaurant, but it looked good. This is San Francisco, however, so I would suggest many other restaurants. Still in a pinch, it looked decent.
The room was large ( I had a two bed room). Nicely decorated, again in modern, muted tones. High speed connectivity (not wireless), good working desk, room to move around. For a hotel room in a city, this was really not bad. 
Fitness center was above average for a hotel. If you were visiting for business, the location might be a bit out of the way but it is very centrally located if you are a tourist.
Staff was great, efficient, friendly, helpful. I would definitely stay there again.

I've stayed at this hotel twice now and figure I should write a review. This is a nice looking hotel. The lobby is gorgeous with a grand front entrance. Although you are immediately faced with dragging your luggage down a set of stairs, neither time was I offered assistance, to get to check in. There may be an elevator somewhere but I have yet to see it and besides who wants to wait for an elevator to go down one flight? My biggest complaint with this hotel is the rooms are tiny. Even by NYC standards. Both stays I was in an extremely small room and could barely get around the bed. No bathtub but a tiny shower that actually made me a little claustrophobic. I'm only -'-"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" ---lb so I don't know how a bigger person could even fit in that shower. Both trips I was staying with coworkers who also complained about the size of their rooms. Obviously there is nothing the hotel can do about the size of the rooms, but I have to admit on that reason alone this hotel would not be my first choice for a night in NYC.
Perfect location, beautiful room, friendly and helpful staff. Will definitely stay again!

A friend and I traveled from Delaware to San Antonio for a few days for a 'spa vacation'. The Mokara Spa was located across the footbridge from the Omni and was top notch. Our hotel room opened with French doors onto a terrace overlooking the swimming pool in the central courtyard. Not only a gorgeous view, but it was very quiet at night, as the pool closed at --:-- pm. Our room was immaculate but had an 'old world' feel to it, making it feel very cozy and comfortable. Breakfast was included in our package; it was served buffet-style and there were lots of delicious items to choose from. The service here was outstanding and everyone was so friendly and genuinely warm and welcoming. James, the bartender in La Colegio Bar (located off of the hotel lobby), was funny and personable, and my friend and I enjoyed cocktails there with his good company several times. In all, it was a perfect getaway.

The Independent is located within convenient walking distance of public transportation, many attractions (museums, historic district, etc), great restaurants and shopping. We certainly did not miss having a car. The desk staff (especially Colin) was exceptionally gracious and helpful. The wine and hors d'oeuvres in the evening were abundant and it was fun meeting other guests - both Americans and international. Coffee and hot water-teas were provided throughout the day. Our room was generously sized, quiet and clean. The beds and pillows were very comfortable. Our bathroom was also very clean and good size although the toilet was a bit loud when flushed. For the first time in a long, long time, there were enough towels provided without asking for more. Warning to women, the toiletries provided do not include hair conditioner. We booked the pay in advance rate, which was a great value. We look forward to staying here again.

We spent - night at this hotel. Everything was great, very spacious accommodation - we had a sitting room with fridge, microwavem TV, Sofa, Desk + bedroom with another TV, - Queen size beds,etc. I thought it was a new hotel, but was told it was totally renovated when HI took it over...
The rate was good, a lot of great restaurants nearby. The only frustrating thing weas to find the hotel; probably Mapquest map & directions was a bit confusing...As you head North from Austin, the numbers show ----- block; so we thought we missed it. Actually, it is under the bridge, then going South again; in other words: on the other side..
The desk clerk was extremely helpful, gave us a lot of good information & maps of Austin as we were to do all the sightseeing the following day. The seafood restaurant Fish Daddy was also excellent. The rate included breakfast of pastries, cereals, eggs, coffee, yogurt & juice. We enjoyed our stay...

Hi, this is a great hotel. John at the Front Desk provided great service to our family (We parked in the wrong garage, he fixed that; we needed a larger room, he found us a suite with a view). I couldn't find my Starwood number, he let me stay in the line anyway:). The room was fabulous; soft beds; very nice lobby. Also, it was my first time using hotwire and the rate was fabulous. It was an emergency trip & I only booked - hours before arriving. I know technology provides integrated systems between all providers, but there are many horror stories about rates not being honored or other snafus. This wasn't the case. Tip: Our Navigation system didn't have the correct directions once we got to downtown Indy. We went around the 'very long block' a few times before finally finding the street that led us to the Westin. Everything else was fab: Thanks John at FD. Thanks: A.O. from chicago.

Liked the location - they call it the Doubletree Magnificent Mile, but you're actually a couple of blocks off the Mag Mile. Felt very safe in this area. We recommend the West Egg for breakfast and Indian Garden for dinner; both are within a block. Had dinner at the hotel restaurant - good food and great service. There's an Einstein Bros. Bagels in the hotel, but had very long lines in the morning! 
Hotel was very clean, beds were comfy and service was very good, especially at the front desk and bar. The rooftop pool area was adequate, but sort of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cold"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" feeling - didn't have that fun, pool atmosphere that made me want to hang out there all day.
Our only complaint was that there's no free wifi in the rooms, but there is in the lobby area, and therefore the lobby areas were very often FULL with people on their laptops! We found, however, that you could sign into wifi in the lobby, then take the elevator up to your room (we were on the -rd floor) while holding your laptop slightly open so that it doesn't go to sleep, and we were able to maintain the free connection in our room! :)
We booked this room at about $----nt., and for Chicago in summer, it was a good price for a very good room.

The room was comfy and very modern. I loved the cleanliness- a dirty room is a big no-no in my book. And the biggest plus was there were so many outlets for all of our gadgets! The location was great. It was far enough from Time Square proper to not be hassled by throngs of tourists, but it was only a short walk to just about anything. The staff was exceptional and very professional.

The draw here really is the newly hip restaurants off the lobby. The hotel itself leaves much to be desired. I enjoyed myself here only because of a discounted rate so another reviewer who compared it (negatively) to The Mercer or SoHo Grand is comparing - completely different price ranges. This is not, however, a --star hotel. The location is great with easy access to the Meat Packing District, the Village, Chelsea...but it's side street location is not ideal for doormen being there when you need them. (They're off getting taxis on -th Avenue!). The rooms themselves are small but very nicely designed but the single biggest drawback are abysmally dark hallways and a similarly dark lobby. Not chic, just cheap and creepy.

The Edison Hotel Is located in the Theatre District, steps away from Times Square and very close to all Broadway shows. If your driving, you are going to really like the valet parking (which is very resonable) , the Bell Staff are very pleasant as well as the Reservation Staff. Breakfast is very good at the Edison Cafe and dinner at Sofia's, located within the Hotel proper, is just great, you'll enjoy the friendly greeting from Mike and you'll also enjoy Nick at the Bar. The veal Marsala is excellant as well as the rest of the menu choices, the wait staff are very pleasant and eager to meet or exceed your dining experience. the rooms at the Edison are clean with comfortable beds. I know this is hard to believe but the rooms rates were very competative. They were priced at $--- and you actually should purchase your rooms from The Edison Hotel itself, Online ticket brokers are not going to be less the The Hotel itself. Check with reservations for special rates or check OnLine at www.edisonhotelnyc.com I hope you find this information helpful!! I really think you'll enjoy your stay at the Edison Hotel. Enjoy yourselves!!!!!!
Service was fantastic and the Bed was so plush to slumber in. Can't beat the location in Manhattan, can walk to most tourist destinations.

The room was delightful, the bathroom immaculate (plenty of towels and hot water). We enjoyed the afternoon tea and the complimentary breakfast, but it was the friendly service that was exceptional -- everyone was delightful and helpful. The food at the restaurant was very good too! We can't wait to return -- the location was perfect for the theatre and historical sites: we walked everywhere and took the train from the airport!
Good hotel. Had a car, so no problems to move about. No complaints. Will definitely stay here again.

Boutique hotel very cute...location is great safe to walk around and safe to walkto michigan ave, and the El....hotel has been redone with fresh""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""make up""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""....rooms and lobby are not terribly large ( I guess because its an older chicagoproperty...all in all good experience.

Now that I've seen L.A., I think I'd probably rather stay along the beach somewhere, but if you are coming for the Walk of Fame-tourist attractions, this is a good base to start from and will save you some money.

I stayed here in a business trip, so it was very good and I had no need to pay anything, otherwise I would have taken another option. You have to try the Eggs Benedict and the Chips from the room service.
Though everything is far from each other in L.A. You can stay here if you have a car and move round Beverly Hills. It's Walking Distance (if you DO like walking) from Rodeo Drive (--min) and Beverly Center (--min).
Mi room was in -th Floor and I could see beautiful sunshines from my balcony (yes! It has a beautiful balcony) and also I could see the Hollywood Sign in the distance.
The TV is big, the bed comfortable and the bathroom has like - rooms inside! - for the shower, wc and tina and another for mirror, pile and make up (if you're a fancy lady).
If you can afford this hotel, it's totally recommendable and also maybe you can see one or another movie star in the elevators.

Not at all impressed. We booked this place as friends coming to Chicago for the first time. Its location is excellent, but that is all I will give it. We had booked a room with two beds and got here and were told they had none of them left and we would have to share a bed. I like my friend, but not that much! when we told the guy at the front desk we had booked two beds and we also had it on our email confirmation he said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""oh those confirmations can be misleading."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Um, how so? If I book and pay for something then that is what I am expecting to get. The rooms are TINY and the bathroom is as well. There was hair on the bathroom floor when we got there as well as a massive one in the bathtub and the walls and doors desperately need a paint job. There is nowhere to store anything in the bathrooms. Our bed was VERY soft -so much so that our backs hurt in the morning. The biggest issue we had was the sheet on the bed. It did not fit! I only went to the end of the mattress but did not go over the end. We accepted this for night one and then night two complained. The manager was very nice and had it fixed for us for night two. Night three it was back to the short sheet (they dont use fitted sheets!) and the top sheet had dried blood on it and so for night four I complained again and got it fixed by a woman with no teeth who was shouting at me in spanish!
The elevator is TINY so you often have to wait for a few runs to get on one. Especially in the morning as we waited almost -- minutes for one with our luggage. There are no fridges in the room which I was annoyed about but I guess there is nowhere to put one! The in room iron left a mark on my friends new shirt. They are VERY skimpy on supplies. For two females staying there, they gave us one bar of soap (which we used for the handsink) as well as two small bath towels and a foot towel. This is what I would expect for one person staying, not two.
Outside of that, the location is excellent. It is within walking distance of everything you would want to see and do in downtown Chicago. You have to pay for internet in your room but you can use it for free in the lobby. I never had any issues with the speed as it always worked fine for us. the front desk staff in the day were helpful and polite but the evening ones we found to be extremely rude and unhelpful.
Overall, if I were to come to Chicago again, I would not stay here as I would want somewhere of a better quality.
Just opened, very clean, top breakfast, just over a metro station (direct subway to JFK and Brooklyn). Rooms are nice and stylish.

We stayed for a few days and was very impressed especially with the level of service at the Magic Castle. Nick and the rest of te staff were great! We've never spent much time in the Hollywood-Beverly Hils area and enjoyed our experience with both the hotel and surrounding area. The rooms are spacious and clean and it is within walking distance to the Hollywood atmosphere. If you're coming to this area and don't want to spend a fortune, consider this hotel
room very small but clean. You can not ask a palace for this price in New York City. Very good location. Recommended for small budgets and short stays.

We stayed in this Hotel in May ----. A great location, within easy walking distance of Central Park and Times Square. Also a short walk to Grand Central Station and all other noted attractions. The lifts were slow but this was not a real problem. Our room was clean and of a good size. My only concern was the outlook from the room. If you are allocated an outside room (facing the street) it could be noisy, but if you are allocated an inward facing room you will overlook an inner courtyard which when we were there had collected a lot of rubbish.
Overall its OK for a City Hotel with a great location.

Before arriving at the Jury's, I expected this hotel chain to uphold their mission statement and the quality setforth through their marketing.

Issues:

-) Continuous overheating iron, despite turning to the lowest settings. In turn, burned the backside of my dress shirt. I raised this issue to the management. -) Overall dirty and not courteous staff. 
-) Not worth this hasle find another hotel.

I doubt if this hotel is Hilton it's standard is below motel - or any ill kept inn. I along with my and one of friend's family booked two rooms for two nights and find out rooms were very small and stinky no ventilation, shower in friend's room was not working properli disspensing very little water. Coffee maker in my room stopped brewing coffee after few seconds and never worked there after. Bathrooms were short of soap i mean only one soap for handwashing and shower. Never ever stay there again and strongly recommend to stay away from this hotel if you are planning to visit beutiful sunny San diego this hotel will ruin your trip.I don't know how this hotel got - stars it should be half star in my opinion.

Arrived at -:--pm, booked through Expedia and unfortunately arrived on a day when the hotel was full so we ended up spending our first night in the last room available which was tiny - having booked a deluxe room - which is --m- in the brochure we ended up in a --' x --' nightmare of a room. Bing an Expedia client we were bottom of the barrel. We were upgraded to premier room the next day for another three nights but am afraid the damage has been done and after visiting The Carlyle a number of times I cannot face another experience like the one I just had. I missed a whole morning and lunchtime changing rooms or rather waiting to change rooms. Stupid front desk staff who tried to tell me that it had a lovely view in the room the size of a closet - when infact if you sit down you see nothing. Make sure you ring ahead a ask for a lower floor where rooms are much larger and have rooms over Madison Ave.

Extremely quiet and comfortable rooms, immaculate housekeeping, the best pillows and mattresses ever! The location is perfect if you are visiting Chicago as a tourist. Great views and close to everything. The hotel had every amenity we could have asked for... next time we will stay longer and use more of the hotel services. We especially liked sitting in the outdoor cafe on the riverfront.

In July this year we stayed and the Lenox for the second time having spend three nights there in ----. The reason we booked the Lenox was the good reviews and the enjoyable short stay we had in ----. Often when you revisit a place it disappoints but in this case it was the opposite, we enjoyed it even more. This time around we booked a superior room (something I would recommend) and were fortunate to get one with an excellent view, this did add to our enjoyment but this hotel knows how to look after it’s paying customers. The attention to detail was excellent, small things such as calling the room to ask if everything was ok shortly after you have settled in may not sound like much but it is touches like this that made the stay very enjoyable. 
The standard of accommodation, the location and the staff were all excellent, we would definitely recommend this hotel.

We stayed at the Queen Anne in May of ---- for two nights. Our room was clean, had a comfortable queen bed and a working fireplace (room ---). The bathroom was small but adequate, no shelf or counter area for makeup, etc. The breakfast was a basic continental breakfast with coffee, tea, juice, hard boiled eggs,sausage patties, cereals, breads and muffins. The hotel's location was quiet, within walking distance to restaurants on Filmore Street. The housekeeping staff was helpful in locating and shipping a personal item that I left behing in the room. The first floor lobby had nice sitting areas with fireplaces. If you like old Victorian hotels, I am sure you would enjoy a stay at the Queen Anne.

The hotel is amazing. Super clean, modern, and the location couldn't be better. The breakfast was great and the staff was friendly and helpful. I travel to the area frequently and this is where I will be staying for the future visits.

Positives:
Good location, good value, very friendly and helpful staff, clean beds and bathroom.
Negatives:
Old shoddy furniture, room too cramped. Room looked out over scruffy back yard (Room Number --- !!!). Thin walls, so noisy from other guests.
Overall it was okay as we went out early morning and just came back to sleep so didn't spend much time in the room.

This is our -nd trip to the Westin Seattle. I guess I feel it is getting a bit tired as the sheets are a bit pilly, the towels are slightly threadbare ~ you know...just showing a bit of age. However, the staff here is excellent and we have great service and love to come on our annual trip away from the kids. I suggest a room above floor -- to get away from the potential noise from the monorail. Housekeeping has been lacking in the recent hotels I have stayed in but here - they got it right! So impressed with the housekeeping. The TV is crummy and unless we were doing something wrong, all the channels are in analog, therefore it looks terrible. The -th Ave., Cafe in the lobby is actually really good and handy if you are needing something quick and tasty before heading out for the day - they have it all from oatmeal to omelets to eggs and cereal. Again, staff there is super friendly. The lounge was good for a couple drinks - DO try the Dungeness Crab Mac n' Cheese - REAL CRAB.... and tasty....skip the calamari - ick. This location is right around the corner from EVERYTHING downtown. We never bring a car and we hit all the major Seattle hotspots. There is an AMC movie theatre at the mall around the corner that sells $- Microbrew beer! There is a pizza joint a couple blocks away (Serious Pie) that will make you re-think your traditional pizza and come begging for more. The shops are all close, live theatre and Top Pot Donuts for warm fresh donuts! 
All in all, this is a good place and we will certainly come back ... it is like staying at your aunt's place in the spare room ... nice and clean, friendly but nothing outstanding or new. A little dated but comfortable and predictable.

My young daughter missed her connecting international flight due to weather and I had to find accomocations from Kansas late at night. This hotel was close to the airport and offered convenient shuttle service. Doris, the night clerk, was very patient and helpful with all my calling and they even sent Robert, the shuttle driver, back to the airport at midnight when I thought she'd missed the shuttle. My daughter said her room looked nice and was clean.
I did not see the hotel myself, but the staff's help was appreciated and the room price was very reasonable.
We really enjoyed our stay at the Marquis. The rooms were great and beds were very comfortable. The location right now Times Square was amazing!

Yes, the rooms are small. It's New York, after all. But the location could not be better, the service was good, the room was clean, and ... well, the pipes on the --th floor had an angry case of the growls. That's the technical term for excess air in water pipes that, when faucets are opened and closed, sounds like a Hilti drill in the wall behind the bed. OK, I should have mentioned this to the management before check-out, but the thought of plumbers probing pipes during Thanksgiving weekend was worse than the occasional noise. Which did not cause any lost sleep, so the bottom line on Cassa is that it's a convenient, clean, comfortable, but rather cramped hotel in midtown. The price was right, too, when booked on Priceline the Tuesday before Turkey Day.

Stayed at the Paramount with my daughter for - nights after XMas .The price was cheap--about $--- w- taxes--considering its great location right near Rockefeller Center & Times Square. The lobby was also very chic.The major downside was that our double room was one of the tiniest I've ever seen & slightly shabby.

We had two stays at this hotel in December, both were ok my me, reception was helpful both times.
Both times we ate at the tables at the bar, service there was good and the staff friendly. The food was good also. The bar area is a high open space and felt cold. (so consider taking a light jacket just in case).
Starbucks cafe in the foyer if you want wait for a coffee.
The hotel rooms are getting old and need bit of a refurbish as the fixtures have seen better days. 
Found the bed comfortable and slept really well.
It is a popular place for the airlines crews, so be considerate of them as you move about the hallways especially if you see 'please do not disturb' signs. (nothing worse than a grumpy, sleep deprived hostie on you next flight).
The wifi internet was free with the room, although you had to logon and agree as if you are going to have to pay. (you need you room number and last name to login).

My husband and I stayed here at the end of a week long trip to California. We were celebrating our five year anniversary, and the staff was very kind in recognizing this when we checked in. When we returned from the pool the first afternoon there was a bottle of champagne and a little dessert waiting for us, which we loved. Service was excellent all around, from the front desk to the restaurant, spa, and poolside attendants. We also used the car service to take us into town and the driver was great. The restaurant in La Jolla we visited (Truluck's) was excellent, and we found it through a recommendation from the hotel. I appreciated being contacted before my stay to make reservations, spa appointments, etc. I highly recommend visiting the spa, it was a great experience. All the food we tried on site was delicious, and the drinks by the pool were great, too. The rooms are gorgeous, pools are wonderful and relaxing even when crowded, and room service was very prompt, friendly and tasty when we ordered it for breakfast one morning.
We had high expectations after reading all the great reviews, and they were all met! We had a great and memorable anniversary celebration and would love to return here someday.

I recently visited this hotel for business purposes. The conference I attended was at the Los Angeles Conference Center which is not all that close to the hotel. The hotel had a shuttle pre-arranged for transfer to the conference center.
Upon arrival the hotel looks like an old, Hollywood hotel (in a good way). I was given my key and asked if I wanted my luggage brought to my room (I declined as I was able to carry it myself). My room was on the --th floor. The room is quite spacious but you can tell it is an old hotel. The room, despite newer paint, is obviously quite old and has seen better days. 
The rate for the room was heavily discounted for the conference participants (~$----night plus $-- in taxes and fees). At nearly $--- per night I did not find it to be a particularly good deal based on the quality of the room.
The staff was extremely pleasant and friendly and went out of their way to make sure the guests were happy and satisfied. Overall the staff was excellent.
The pool was closed for a private event on one of the nights I stayed and I didn't have time on the other nights to review it. The hotel was accommodating and notified me in advance that the pool would be closed but that the restaurant-bar would be open to accommodate guests.
If you wish to view the Beacher's Madhouse show the hotel can help you out. Be advised that the shows are only on Wed and Sat evenings and the costs are very high. One ticket for the show costs $---. This was more than I wanted to spend so I passed.
The location is ideal if you want to see Graumann's Theater and the walk of stars. You are literally in the middle of everything. There are a tremendous number of tourists, but that should be expected. Even on the --th floor you can hear some of the commotion from the main street but not enough to be a distraction.

Just returned from a - night stay. We arrived early and the only thing ready was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""tower room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" -two fights above where the elevators stop-which was a $---night upgrade. The clerk said it was really cool---so we schlepped our stuff up there-- but we both felt claustrophobic, because of tiny windows (plus the furnishings were pretty dated and worn)-so we schlepped our stuff back down, put our bags in storage and asked to be pre-planned into a regular riverview (spectacular) room. 
When we returned later in the day we were checked into such a room on the -th floor.
Room was quiet and clean, with a decent (not perfect) a-c system. All employees we encountered were very friendly and helpful. and the location is DYNAMITE!! 
They do things a little differently here - I was torn between a - and - star rating--would have given it a - --- if I could. but went on the high side because of the positives. 
The pros have already been described: clean, quiet, friendly, LOCATION. +Self park available right next door for $---day---an incredible bargain in downtown Chi.
The slight cons: ice machine available on only a couple of floors (out of like --!) - no ice bucket in room--they stock these in a rack next to machine. If you don't get one early in the weekend---forget it-they don't appear to re-stock them. Same with the water bottles next to the elevators-- a really nice touch-providing cold water on your way out for activities--too bad there were no bottles late Saturday and Sunday. The postage stamp size HDTV wasn't too bad, but the god-awful sound quality was-- annoying to the max---good thing we didn't rely much on it.
We weren't there to study the architecture-- but it is our understanding that Chicago is a MAJOR tourist destination for those who are so inclined. It is widely known as the birthplace of the skyscraper. This building, at least gives the appearance to the novice eye,as having some historical significance in that regard, yet no information as to the history of the building is provided to the guest (as far as we could find). Wethinks the hotel is missing th boat by not heavily promoting this.
Don't want to seem too negative --this was a very decent place. Would happily return.

I love to stay at the Langham as I did last Sunday,-- November.From the minute you stop the car until you leave you are treated like an honored relative by all the staff, made to feel at home and nothing I have ever asked for is too much trouble.Concierge desk is one of a kind,led by William,Lincoln ,the newset addition is very helpful and a worthy member of a fabulous team. Mentioned my shopping plans on the way to breakfast and while leaving the hotel they had telephoned to check the opening hours for me, never happened anywhere else. I am always sorry that I cant book my next stay immediately to have something to look forward to. Well done,Langham. The beds are the most comfortable beds I have ever slept in.

I was pleasantly surprised when checking in to this hotel. Eventhough we only stayed one night, the hotel was elegant and provided excellent service. We ordered room service, since we arrived late and the food was excellent, room service was fast and very courteous. I have nothing to say but wonderful comments about this hotel. Room was large with great view of the downtown area, comfortable beds with nice linens and great toiletries.

OMG, worst hotel I have ever stayed in!!! Mold on the walls, loose ceiling tiles, showers were either hot or cold, no in-between. Housekeeping bugged us numerous times and every morning and would just knock and walk right in. a thunderstorm one night brought down the ceilings in many rooms and in some of the walkways. The only decent things were that I didnt see any bugs and the pool was clean. I was so scared when we left there that we were going to come home with lice!! Only stayed here for the convenience to the base, but so not worth it. The owners should be ashamed for running such a dump!!!!!

The look & feel of this hotel is great, every single employee was friendly and service-oriented, they made us feel welcome. The free coffees in the lounge are a nice bonus. The room is lovely, rather spacious, modern, evrything available you need. Best stay ever in NY!

Would anyone nowadays think that a call within the U.S. would cost that much? Most landlines now consider any call in the U.S. to be local, so when I had to spend a lot of time setting up an iphone with our IS Dept., I didn't think anything of it. I'd love to know the hotel's cost for connecting that call.
In addition, I was charged for two internet connections ($--) to use my laptop and ipad, another $- for a dropped domestic call (<-min.), and it took several weeks just to get copies of my bill sent to me by email. 
Sure, downtown hotels are expensive, but charges like this are unconscionable.
Otherwise, the location is OK- several blocks walk to Market Street, not a tremendous amount very close to the hotel. The room was decent, but I'm not partial to the setup with an electronic shade that separates the bathroom from the main room- I find it's much louder than an actual wall when there's more than one person staying in the room.

Don't be fooled by the picture of the view from the terrace, unless you are attending an event on the terrace, you will never see it. Since the view from our room was of an L stop, we attempted to find the terrace to enjoy the view for just a minute. We were rudely told we were not allowed, the words were very close, if not actually, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""You can't go there"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The girl must have realized how that sounded and added that it is only open to private events.
Everything else at the hotel was excellent. Our room was very spacious, on the concierge level, but as mentioned, we looked down on the L. Noise was not a problem.
We did not eat in the restaurant, but we did have room service and the food was very good.
The hotel is conveniently located, but not knowing my way around downtown Chicago, I found it to be a little challenging to get to and from in our rental car. My guess is that it is easier to get to when the surrounding streets are not under construction.
I rated the service average due to the terrace comment, everyone else would be very good.
The room was great, except for the view.
Even with street construction, great location.

Got this hotel on a last minute deal for a very reasonable price! I was staying on my own as girlfriend was with family elsewhere in the city. Arrived very tired and I was greeted politely by the porter. All bags were taken and after a breeze of a check in the luggage was with me within minutes in room ---- on the -th floor. I then headed out to meet my girlfriend and see Times Square. The bed was very comfortable and despite the noise you would expect from 'the city that never sleeps' I got a good nights kip. However it would be impossible to see NY without being knackered at the end of the night! Bathroom was clean, air conditioning great. 
Digital TV in the room was great when learnt to avoid the PPV rubbish. Especially loved the ESPN sport channels!
Bar downstairs expensive ($-- for - bottles of Bud!), Starbucks in the lobby a big +!
Will use hotel again, as was very good value for money!

Maybe marginal is not the right word. Nothing about the hotel is WRONG, per se, which is why I give it - stars. It's conveniently located in the Gaslamp, the beds are very comfortable, the entryway to the hotel is a MAGNIFICENT oversized door, the staff is friendly and efficient, etc.
But...
I stayed there for two nights with my boyfriend and the whole time we thought, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Dang. We wish we had booked at Palomar's beachier themed sister, Solamar"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". For me, Palomar is like that girl in the club who tries a bit too hard. She has one too many accessories on, a bit too much eyeliner, and you know by the end of the night she's going to be DYING to take off those stilettos. Solamar is more like your super cool friend who is always going on fun adventures and wants to take you with.
Palomar has upscale styling, but it ends up looking like the upscale styling of every other upscale hotel. Solamar has a fresher approach to design, including very funky mirrors in the guest rooms. To me, Solamar feels effortless, approachable, and soothing. Palomar is very nice, but just not my speed. 
Note -: The pool wasn't open while I was there (or at least I couldn't find a way to unlock the door to it). That was a bummer, because I love going out on Solamar's pool deck in the early morning and curling up with a good book as the sun climbs.
Note -: The guest rooms have fab wooden floors, which help alleviate my bed bug paranoia, but their heavy wood beds scratch the floors to pieces.
Note -: I do LOVE Palomar's rolling ottomans. I rolled back and forth all over the room in a frenzy just for fun. They roll REALLY quickly and the rooms have somewhat of a corridor inside that's a perfect rolling tract.
I think a lot of travelers will prefer Palomar over Solamar, but if you're a more laid back beachier type of person with an eye for funkier design I suggest trying Solamar. In addition, their wine selection is always a bit more eclectic, which I like.

Its an ok location. We were just staying here one night before we left on a cruise, we wanted to stay in Houston since there is things to do here. I booked via Priceline. We valet parked the truck which is over $--.-- after check in we didnt even drive anywhere. There is a good pool area and gym. But in the area there is much to keep you, but a short light rail ride away it will take you downtown. The rooms had plenty of space for two and the a-c worked good. All and All and nice stay.

We stayed just one night at the Fairmont, as we were on our way to a reunion west of the city the next night. We booked the hotel using airline points, so I am unable to comment on value for the dollar. However, we really enjoyed our stay and would love to go back again the next time we have occasion to stay in Boston.
The check-in experience was excellent, with very cordial and efficient front desk staff and a friendly and helpful bellman to escort us to our room and see that our car was taken care of. 
The room was beautiful, with a king sized bed and lots of space and seating. The bed was very comfortable, and we slept very well. There is a --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" LCD TV on the wall with a good selection of channels available. The bathroom is well appointed, with a glassed-in walk-in shower and a separate toilet with translucent glass separating it from the rest of the bathroom. Lots of amenities.
Seating included a comfortable reclining chair and a couple of other chairs as well. There is a desk with a good bit of space. My one gripe is that they charge $--.-- for WiFi, but this is common nowadays. Seems like an unjustified money grab, given that a $---night Super - Motel gives you WiFi for free.
One oddity is the absence of ice machines on the floor. You have to call the front desk to get ice delivered, and of course that means a tip. However, they deliver ice and bottled water around -:-- in the evening, which is a nice touch.
Overnight parking is $--, which is highway robbery, except that it costs an arm and a leg everywhere in Boston. There are some parking garages within walking distance (meaning a mile or less) that are less expensive, but you have to decide if it's worth the hassle of finding them and going back and forth. 
If you are looking for good food, simply walk over to Hanover Street in the North End, about a two minute walk, and check out the gazillion fine Italian restaurants. The Quincy Market is about ten minutes away. The nearest T stop is Haymarket, also about ten minutes. 
Would definitely stay here again.

We only had one night here on our way back to NZ but the location in terms of access to Union Square was brilliant. I had read comments previously about this hotel and was not ---% sure what it would be like because we had heard about the protestors. To be honest we didn't see them when we were there but our room was towards the back of the hotel. But hey, this is San Francisco and it is the city that invented protestors, everybody protests!!
Easy access to the cable cars which I would thoroughly recommend if you want to get to Fisherman's Wharf. Catch it though further downtown or right on the main street to the pier which is Powell Street.
Recommend also doing a hop-on, hop-off bus tour of the city too, you get to see a lot in a short space of time, especially if you are limited for time like we were.
Loved San Francisio, the Hotel Frank is on Geary Street which has a number of very nice galleries on it, especially The Art of Dr Suess, worth a look.
Hotel staff were friendly, room was nice and comfortable and decor was very art deco which was very cool. Definitely would stay again next time we are in San Francisco

... at The Fairmont was wonderful! My husband and I were married at the hotel -- years ago and our experience this time was just as grand as we remembered. The hotel is simply breathe-taking, and yes, being a historic hotel, it has its minor quirks. Our bedroom was beautifully restored, spacious at Boston standards, and had a lovely view of Copley Square. Our experience at dinner in the Oak Room lived up to its reputation. Our server and wine steward were both knowledgeable, eager to assist and made us feel as though we were the only diners in the restaurant. The food was excellent and the wine list was top notch. We would highly recommend The Fairmont.

My husband and I stayed here for - nights on our first-ever visit to Washington. The location is excellent. The hotel has been renovated, the beds extremely comfortable, and the staff very helpful. The neighborhood is great as well. We did have a couple of issues though. The first room we were given had water damage on the ceiling above the bed. The damage was such that the paint had begun bubbling off, which gave the appearance of a large growth coming off of the ceiling and potentially falling on you while sleeping (room ---). The staff quickly checked us in to another room - with a little less water damage! Later that day, two of the light circuits blew so we had no power in the bathroom or the room, except for the nightstand lights. Apparently this was throughout the hotel. The issue still hadn't been resolved by the next day. At approx --:-- pm, all the power went off! Nothing like sitting in a dark hotel room; no air, no lights, nothing. Oh yeah - don't forget those magnetic keys; they don't work either. The power returned about -- minutes later.
I'd go back to this hotel despite the electrical issues. Be sure to ask for a room with a view on the Circle or one of the side streets as the alternative is in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""inner courtyard"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" with a great view of the adjoining wall and the air conditioning units. The hotel bar is hopping on Thursday - Saturday.

I am so upset to have to write this review as I am from Dallas and have always admired this hotel from afar. Unfortunately we picked this hotel to stay in the night of our wedding. Big mistake. We were married on a Saturday and this hotel was a ghost town. Not to mention all the amenities we were promised, free breakfast, possible upgrade, were not granted. Even when we showed up in a wedding gown and tux they could have cared less. Our room was decorated in beige and brown and the TV was the size of a computer monitor. The bathroom was small and our view was of an office building about --- ft away. Multiple times we tried to remind the staff we were newlyweds and that our reservation included breakfast, etc. and it fell on deaf ears. It was honestly so depressing to arrive at this hotel after the biggest night our life and quite frankly the biggest waste of our money. Upon learning our reservation was not honored (a few days later), they comp’d our bill $-- for the breakfast, and said they would look into the matter. Naturally we have not heard from them since. I do not recommend this hotel at all as there are plenty of updated, fun, reasonable hotels in the same area.

I have no idea where some of the reviewers on here stayed, but I'm certain it can't have been the Omni in downtown Austin! 
Before booking, the hotel and its manager helped me sort out a lot of details, right down to the kind of room we wanted. Which, by the way, they honoured, giving us an outward facing room as requested. When we were checking in, they even lowered the deposit for us because we were paying cash, leaving me the extra funds to replace some of my lost luggage.
From the moment we set foot in the hotel we were treated like people who mattered. Every employee we passed greeted us and engaged us in conversation, and did their best to do everything they could to improve the stay. This goes from the managers to the guys at the door. Everybody was so friendly and seemed to really care about the hotel and its guests. My airline lost my luggage and the hotel gave me a little pack of complimentary toiletries, which saved my skin (and my roomate's nose!)
The rooms were gorgeous, much bigger than they looked in images and plenty big enough for the number of guests. The TV reception was sometimes a bit patchy, but that is hardly important. The hotel's location is perfect; my friend and I walked everywhere and were never bored. The proximity to Sixth street was not troubling to us, even at night, and we are both light sleepers. We slept incredibly well every night. It was a lovely, quiet, comfortable hotel.
It's well worth signing up to the Select Guest program. We felt like royalty when we saw the size of the free drinks you get every morning. It was a wonderful touch which really made the mornings wonderful! 
The one negative I can think of is that one of the days, housekeeping didn't give us enough towels or empty the trash, which simply meant that the bins were extremely full when we checked out. We didn't mind, we just felt bad! 
They even have a 'cricket hunting' service! They say if you have a cricket, just call down and they'll get rid. We had to call down because we had a cricket (I am British and a wimp with any insects), and they sent somebody straight up to deal with it. And boy, was he cute! Certainly made my morning a little bit brighter, I'll tell you!
And to the last reviewer? If you didn't want housekeeping to knock, put the privacy sign on. It's pretty simple! We did that every other day and never got bothered.
So, thank you, Omni hotels and the staff at the downtown Austin property. You made my once-a-year visit to my best friend magical despite a lost suitcase. I can't praise you enough.

We chose the Parker House because of its location right on the Freedom Trail, and I'm so glad we did! We stayed in April when the prices were more reasonable, and the location allowed us to easily manage all our sightseeing without a rental car. Most of the popular tour trolleys stop a block or two away, and we were able to buy a pass at the hotel lobby, get on with our receipt, and get the actual ticket once the trolley made the loop to the main ticket offices. 
On top of that, the staff at the Parker were just amazing! We normally do not stay in upscale places, because I've found you often don't really get what you pay for (luxury places aren't any bigger in roomsizes, aren't any cleaner, and often nickel and dime you with fees compared to the more-competitive chains) but this was a genuine exception. 
I would strongly suggest becoming a (free) member of their loyalty program in advance, because the staff bent over backwards to make us feel welcome. 
Definitely worth spending more to stay here than a cheaper place that will only prove to be a hassle with sightseeing. I did a lot of homework in advance of picking this place, and it really paid off. It was quiet, it was convenient, and it was so cool to stay here and learn about all the famous things that happened here (such as JFK proposing to Jackie in the restaurant).

From the moment we stepped out our car we were given the VIP treatment. All staff went out of their way to make sure everything about our stay at the NIKKO SF was top notch. Rooms were very clean and the beds were quite comfortable. The welcome cheese and cracker plate was a great touch. We also really enjoyed the Sunday brunch in the ANZO restaurant. We will be coming back!

Stayed The First Weekend Of December and Found it to be an incredible surprise. Location, Facilitiess Service were the best I have had in A hotel in this category Our room was a corner suite, spacious new and clean. Decorated for the next generation of mid-priced hotels. Breakfast was average but the M-TH happy hour was a nice treat.

BALTIMORE is one of our favorite getaway towns in the east coast, this hotel made it special....We were very impressed after recently staying in a Fairfield Inn that was not to lovely, and the suite was sour :( ....This location is exceptional, from the moment we arrived the staff was attentive, professional, and extremely friendly. The valet staff ( Jospeh and others were great), front desk (Makeba and Santia) sweet as pie, even the maintenance guy Tony was very helpful. They assisted us in every way possible, and referred many places to eat and go....The room was amazing for this property, very clean, airy, and well decorated. We missed the breakfast but they referred us to a place that was incredible across the street ( Miss Shirleys- see review). 
The location was walking distance to most of our favorite restaurants and inner harbor attractions. The valet parking is a tad expensive yet worth it, for convenience. We decide we will probably only stay in this property going forward during our future Bmore visits.
 Wish we had more time to stay long but we'll be back...
Amazing in soooooo many ways. They had marshmallow roasting on a middle floor outside overlooking the water with a huge fireplace and pool. Do not forget the hot tub!!:-)
Stayed for three nights in February ----. Central location. Rooms are so tiny and wifi is terriblly poor. Staff was helpful and no complains about them. No noice on the --th floor room.

The Embassy Suites MC offered everything we needed for our large group. Great rooms with extra space for working, ammenities such as a mini fridge added an extra convience.
The breakfast was a great start to each day, and the managers reception was a perfect ending to a long day.
The location was close to downtown Dallas, big plus for us!
I would recommend the Embassy Suites MC for anyone traveling in Dallas, TX.

The room was clean and spacious with high ceilings. The bed was very comfortable and you could wash cattle with the shower. The location is great for Center City and a $- cab ride to the historic district.
The towels were thin. Internet access was $-- a day. We had a crappy view, and the buffet breakfast at XIX was awful. And there are no vending machines or convenience store in the hotel - if you need a late night beverage or snack, you're stuck with tap water or costly room service.

We stayed at the Orchard for three nights, July -----. You get a lot of hotel for the $ here; the rooms are nicely furnished and spacious and the staff is great. Plus free breakfast and only two blocks from Union Square. Free DVDs too!

I spent -- days in a kept clean room with a hot breakfast every morning, well prepared. Recently renovated, the hotel is first class and I plan to stay there on all my leisure trips to Houston. The staff is great and work very hard. Great stay at Days In Hobby.

My husband and I visited SF for two nights, took a road trip to Monterey for - nights, then returned for - more night. We stayed all - nights in SF at Villa Florence. This is absolutely my favorite hotel in San Diego.

Excellent rooms combiner to hospital we were having surgery!! Gave us a first floor room to accompany our next day surgery. Only drawback was the breakfast, not so good! Staff was friendly and helpful. Would stay here again.
