If u r a seasoned traveler this was a great stay right on the beach. A few great restaurants and bars, as well as grocery store within walking distance. This is a real surfers location and doesn't cater to resort travelers . We had - kids age - and - who loved the winter beach. I loved the lack of crowds and how clean the beach. I'm sure this is a scene on spring break. This was convenient comfortable safe and cheap. I would recommend this to friends who have backpacked and don't need everything on site. There were several bike and surf rentals nearby.

We just spent - nights at the Coventry Inn this past Thanksgiving weekend, this must be about the --th time we have stayed there dating back to the mid --’s. We booked a back facing room on the third floor room ---, it was nice to see the upgrade to the bed, TV, carpet etc. The staff as usually were friendly and accommodating, nice to see Vince there once again as we have met him a number of times over the years. If you are looking for a good reasonably priced hotel in SF with free parking then you can’t go wrong here, as we love to walk we find it no problem to leave the car there for the duration and walk all over the city. We were in town for a family function and picked this hotel for its proximity to the event and price. The rooms are very comfortable, restaurant and bar are very good -- even better than many more expensive hotels I have stayed in for work. It seems very well-maintained. Special thank yous to Joanne at check in and Chanda in the bar for making us feel so welcome.

We rented a Corner Suite room and it was amazing. Great view, two tvs (although we didn't have time to watch any). The customer service was phenominal. From the front desk person, bell boy, concierge, room service, etc., everyone was GREAT. Only complaint? You couldn't store anything in the mini-fridge.

I stayed at this hotel in December ----. For $----night, I was unimpressed. The room itself was OK, but the bathroom was terrible. It badly needed a makeover. There was mold in the shower, places where the wallpaper was nonexistent or pulled back & I could see the wall. There is a W a block away for about the same price -- stay there instead. The difference is night & day. On the positive side, it is a great location in midtown Manhattan and the lobby staff was helpful and kind.

We have just returned from New York.
The Hotel and room was wonderful, staff were very friendly and helpful.
We were celebrating our --th Wedding anniversary and received within moments of entering our hotel room a knock on the door with a member of staff, holding a bottle of champagne and a lovely card, what a surprise!
Location perfect for shopping, eating and sight seeing.
Once again I would like to thank the staff for making our first trip to New York very special.
Will certainly be returning to this hotel in the very near future

I had searched several websites for a downtown hotel as we wanted to do some shopping prior to attending the musical """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Wicked"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I was a little apprehensive about choosing the Homewood, but had a friend tell me I would be pleasantly surpised. I booked two King Suite rooms, one for myself and daughter, the other for a friend and her son. The rooms were very comfortable. The concierge, desk clerk, housekeeping were more than accomodating and welcoming. They appear to make every effort for your stay to be as perfect as possible. The hotel was very quiet in the hallways, even though it was busy. The free buffet breakfast was delicious and was more than expected. 
If you are looking for a centrally located hotel near Michigan Ave. and would like the best deal for the price, this hotel is it. It does not have the magnificient views of motels directly on Michigan Ave. but it truly is a hidden gem. I will choose this hotel for future use when staying downtown.

This hotel was about half price what I could find anywhere else. I wan't expecting much and was pleasantly surprised. Not a great location on a busy highway with lots of fast food places and other budget hotels, a bit out of the way, but free shuttles into Union Station. Very big room, cleaned and serviced every day of my five day stay, free to use computer with internet in the lobby. Not luxurious by any means, but quite comfortable.

My wife and I checked in at -PM and I had to leave at -AM attend some meetings the next day, but the twelve hours we spent there was truly excellent. All the fittings and furnishings are first class, with the bed being a haven of luxurious bedding atop a splendid mattress. 
As to be expected from a French hotel, the food was well prepared. We ordered the Philly TV Set for dinner plus onion soup. I recommend it, but not for a regular meal. It is clearly designed to be a very large snack or perhaps a dinner for someone allergic to vegetables, as it consists of a Philly Cheesesteak, french fries, a bag of popcorn and ice cream (or lava cake). One very brown meal.
Breakfast of French toast and a selection of pastries was very good, and cheaper than I expected.
Service is always served with a smile by all the staff. They are friendly, professional and unobtrusive.
As I say in the title, I wish I could have stayed longer so that I could write a more comprehensive review. But, if you want to stay in a great hotel near Market Street, then the Sofitel is a wise choice.

We have been visiting Boston for over - years now while our son attends BU. We ALWAYS try to stay at the Commonwealth. Nothing else nearby compares. We have had to stay elsewhere a couple of times and are always disappointed because everything about the Commonwealth is outstanding. We are so comfortable there, it is our home away from home.

What a beautiful hotel, with a warm inviting interior, the Hilton Garden Inn is one of the most impressive hotels I have visited in some time. It is not a luxury five star hotel but you will think it is. The linens are wonderful, light and fluffy duvets, the staff is personal and friendly. The pool area is made for kids but has an excellent and extra deep hot tub. The work out area features high quality machines, however going for a run away from the property could be a problem as there is construction going on all around the hotel (NONE of which was heard inside the hotel). The lobby is professional, attractive and has several seating areas that are perfect for gatherings out side of the guest rooms. There are several large meeting rooms as well. The office area is well designed, private and has two computers with free prints. There is dinner room service and a small restaurant downstairs. The menu is varied and should accomodate must people including vegetarians. The made to order breakfast is a little pricey but the a la carte breakfast fits the budget. The only potential problem is that the hotel is so new that google and gps' are not picking up the address on Northton yet. We used the corner address of ---- Rosedale to find the hotel, or just call the helpful staff. Hilton Garden Inn is awesome, you will not be disappointed!

We had a truly relaxing stay. The pool was great and the staff
was most helpful. We had a slight problem during checkin and
the Staff gave us comps for breakfasts (-). We will definitely
return.

I really like this hotel. It feels like it's in a little neighborhood in spite of being walking distance to everything. I was at the Convention center for - days and it's quite perfect. I had a nice breakfast daily, a cup of Starbucks to go, and hit the managers cocktail party most nights. Good view of the bay, and the window opens! Comfortable bed. It wAs my second stay and I look forward to next time
The hotel was very convenient to stay at as there was a full kitchen, which came in very handy during a long stay. The location is very good. People are very nice.

The valet and bellman were very helpful and friendly. The front desk greeted us nicely upon arrival and were fine until we needed help later.

One lampshade was broken. Another lampshade dented. 
There was a comment card on the TV stand that had been completed by someone else that had never been picked up.
Upon bringing these issues to the front desk staff's attention, their answer was to give us more Hilton Honors points!!! Really?!

Even sleeping in her clothes because she didn't feel the hotel was very safe either.
I can live with a little dust and understand an older hotel being worn looking, but dirty is an entirely different manner. Thankfully, we didn't encounter any bugs or vermin.
Do yourself a favor and spend a little extra to stay at the Peabody across the street.

I would have to say it is pretty difficult picking out a place to stay from the internet. I found Ocean Park Inn from a San Diego travel website and could not have been happier with my find. I was nervous for what to expect, but was so thrilled when I arrived. Wonderful location with beautiful views!...perfect walking distance to stores, restaurants, and most importantly the beach! Also great location for driving to popular attractions. This hotel had an amazing beach front view. Alexandra at the front desk did not hesitate and never asked questions about changing our room to the -nd floor with the ocean view to have a private balcony. For anyone who is considering this hotel for their next stay in the Big Apple- look no further!

The Biltmore is a beautiful historic deco hotel in downtown Los Angeles. I would DEFINITELY return if I was doing business in LA. I also recommend it to tourists who want to stay in the downtown area. 
It has gorgeous public spaces, and is a great hotel to get drinks in the lobby. It's fun to peek into ballrooms, and think of all the movie stars that have walked the halls.
My room was nothing fancy. The hotel hasn't been redone in ages, and there is nothing spectacular about the amenities beyond the actual building. Even so, the bathroom was small, but with a great old showerhead that had incredible water pressure. 
Our morning breakfast was wonderful, on the --th floor. It was some sort of corporate client perk, and it was one of the best continental breakfasts I've ever had. The fruit and yogurt cups were over the moon! Also a neat view from the top floor...
The best thing about the Biltmore: THICK WALLS. This is a pre-war building, and it has the quietest rooms I've ever stayed in. You can just tell the hardware and construction is superior.

Impressive stay.....
Clean rooms, very responsive to needs being met, polite staff. Newer property and it really shows! Laundry facilities, pool, and fitness center. Easy access to HEB supermarket and a small Whole Foods type market. There are tons of restaurants and eating places in walking distance as well as shopping opportunities.

The hotel is within a couple of minutes walk of Times Square where there are plenty restaurants, shops and theatres. Would stay here again despite the noisy air conditioning.

My husband and I just got back from a weekend trip to Chicago where we stayed at the Omni. The location of this hotel on the Magnificent Mile can't be beat. The restaurant in the hotel, ---, is good, albeit pretty expensive with small portions. We ate dinner there and still ended up going out for a snack a couple of hours later since we were still hungry. Overall, this hotel was a great experience and has a great location. I am a frequent business and leisure traveler and upon my first stay (and last stay) at the Peabody, I was quite let down. Upon check in, the valet was slammed and seemed to be very unorganized in checking in cars. In the room, furniture was worn, the room was lacking -* appeal, the bathroom was tiny and the street noise was loud. After a few hours, I discovered dirt behind the sink, toilet, anything on the wall (mirrors, pictures, etc) and the room was lacking cleanliness. It was a dance club type scene, which had people lined up (much like a club) out the lobby and into the street. The elevators were so overwhelmed by the rush (and people going to another floor to take a lift to party level), that it took a long time to get an elevator. The elevators were crammed with a club-like crowd, which as anyone who has been to Memphis knows, isn't a good scene. People on the elevators were rude, swearing and many belligerently drunk and almost confrontational. Once at the room, the music was rattling my windows, literally. I called to the front desk to ask how long the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""party"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" would last and I was told --:--PM. The music did tone down just after --:--PM, but kept going at a lower level until midnight. The lobby was slammed with a ton of people who were not staying at the hotel and were quite obnoxious. The elevators were slammed with people coming from the party until around midnight and there were people screaming outside my room until well after midnight (anyone from the party can jump off on any floor). 
Bottom line, do not stay here. I spend --- nights on average in a hotel and this was quite a bad experience. It is actually hard to recollect a more drab experience. I would steer clear!

This was a great hotel. It had alot of amenities. Very, very nice. Loved the valet parking since I was with my daughter, we felt more safe. This hotel was very close to Universal City which is why we chose it. Great service, rooms etc....
I would go back here anytime....

The hotel is nice enough. But beware, they will hit your credit card with charges you will know little to nothing about until you get your credit card bill.
We were at a function downtown and pre-paid for a room at this hotel. The hotel is nice as was the room. However, if you drive there and expect to park your car there please think twice.
When we arrived it was raining, the valet service had cars parked in every conceivable spot, include more than a dozen cars with only two wheels still on the pavement and the rest of the car up over the curb. As a result, we were greated near the street by the value and handed our claim ticket. We walked into the front entrance and directly to the front desk to check in.
No where did we see a sign advising of the parking charge for guests that park there. There is a sign, but it is way over on the side of the building next to the garage exit - not someplace we came anywhere close to. We were not informed by any staff of any charges for parking. I know some hotels do charge their guests for parking, but others do not.
We stayed the night and when we left I checked out at the front desk and they said everything was taken care of. So I dropped off the room keys and went to get our car. We were not offered nor given a receipt. I assumed there was no need since there was no reason to have additional charges other than what I already paid for when I booked the room.
Handing the car claim ticket to the valet service we then waited for the car to be brought out. And waited, and waited - we waited over -- minutes. Again the drive was completely packed with parked cars they had yet to relocate into the parking garage. So when our car finally came out they had only one place they could put it and that was out near the street again - at least this time it was not raining.
Having to check my credit card account for other reasons today I noticed several charges from the hotel. One was --.--, and the other was --.--. So I called, they had no idea what those charges were for - supposedly my card was to be charged $-- for parking and $-.-- for a bottle of water from the mini-bar that we never even opened.
Parking in downtown Chicago on a weekend for any overnight rarely costs more than $-- at any parking garage. Thus this charge, which they neither got my consent for nor did they inform me of it at any time while at the hotel, is very excessive.
After speaking with a manager at the hotel they agreed to remove the mini-bar charge, but refused to remove the parking charge.
I have a great deal of problem with any business that takes free license to charge your credit cards without first informing you of those charges and obtaining your consent for those charges. Because they seem to be able to do this and have no problem doing it I would strongly advise that you avoid this hotel.

I stayed at the Marriot Ren Cen during a conference. It was quite a delightful surprise. The hotel contacted me prior to my stay and asked if I had any requests (bed size, pillows, high-low floor, etc.). They honored all my requests. The room was on the --th floor and had an absolutely spectacular view of Detroit and Windsor, Ontario. It was a small but very comfortable room. The bed was excellent. Everything was clean and functioning properly. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The elevators were fast. The food was very good and not too expensive in the hotel's restaurants. The hotel was within easy walking distance to several area attractions and restaurants and right on the People Mover line (public transit system). The hotel's conference staff did a fantastic job with my conference. I had a great time and would love to come back again.
I pray that the hotel and Detroit can survive through this tough economy. Detroit seems to be making a valient effort to keep moving forward after so many years of tough times. I wish the city all the best and will definitely come back to visit.

We just got home from San Francisco yesterday & I couldn't wait to write a review of our wonderful stay at The Hotel California. This place is perfect if you are simple & in town to be a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""tourist"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". If you are in San Francisco for a spa retreat, then skip this place. The rooms are cute, comfortable & serve their purpose. Yes, they are small, but it is San Franscico. There are plenty of resturants, shopping & bars within blocks, if not steps from the front door. Ricky, the Concerige is AWESOME!!!!!!! If you aren't snotty & want an ice cold beer, walk across the street to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""High Spirt Cocktails"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" neat dive bar. The next morning, go around the corner to Jones & visit """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Dotties"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" best breakfest in San Franscico.

A wonderful hotel, very close to Union Square and all the main San Francisco attractions. This was our first time in San Fran - we were there for New Years Eve so we picked a room that allowed us some space to relax - a suite complete with designer furniture, decorated in pastel shades. Our room wasn't ready when we arrived, so we were offered a glass of wine in the lounge area while we waited. Mood lighting, a roaring fire and a HUGE rocking chair adorned the lobby area. Certainly not like any hotel I've stayed in before. Given the location and the bars and restaurants within the hotel, if you're not comfortable around 'beautiful people' then this isn't the place for you. The staff were great - very friendly and accommodating and the doormen were excellent - the front doors are super heavy and they were always there to open them for you! Overall a lovely hotel - and well worth the money for the experience!

Check in was quick. We were a little early but the hotel did call us within the hour with a ready room. Wonderful view on the --th floor. Beds were nice and clean and so comfortable. And it was very quiet and we were right across from the elevator. There was no continental breakfast and the Internet usage was extra. Geez! Gimme a break. Whats up with that yo? But the bathrooms were clean and the towels plentiful and of a good quality. Ah, I need a diet anyway and shutting out the world for -- hours was ok. I'd stay here again.

We intended to stay at the Peabody, but it was full. This was the perfect fallback hotel. We loved the impeccable modern decor of the lobby and rooms. Everything was clean. Our room was large and well appointed. We would stay there again (if the Peabody was full)...

I was very impressed with our stay at the Palomar, it was our -st stay at a Kimpton Hotel and we will definitely be coming back. The hotel itself is very stylish and our room was great, it had everything we needed for our stay and it was very clean and well appointed. All the staff we met were very helpful and the concierge offered some great suggestions for places to eat out. Plenty of people have already mentioned the free wine hour and also the tea - coffee in the morning, be sure to take advantage of these, but also complete the 'Kimpton in touch' registration online before your visit to get free wifi. The hotel is brilliantly placed for the Bars and restaurants around DuPont Circle and is also only a short walk from Georgetown which is worth a visit. You can easily get to the attractions around the Mall either on foot (about --mins) or on the subway from the centre of DuPont. Overall a great hotel.

Stayed for two nights on business. While work colleagues had told me the Courtyard (next door) would be better, I can clearly vouch that the Residence Inn was far superior. There are two reasons for this: the service (everyone is extremely friendly and helpful) and the breakfast (which was better than anticipated). The common space on the floor where the breakfast is served was quite large (for a city hotel), nicely decorated and well thought out (and TV's in the breakfast bar greatly appreciated so I could catch up on the news). The room had an odd layout to say the least, but had all the amenities one would expect from a Residence Inn (fridge, popcorn for first night, etc.) Great location within five minutes of Center Ciry offices, City Hall, Reading Terminal Market and top restaurants. Would definitely stay here again!

We booked two rooms at the DoubleTree to attend our daughter's graduation at UMASS Boston, which is also located near the Bayside Expo. 
The room was spacious, clean and the staff courteous. Our room consisted of a comfortable king-size bed, desk, and a comfortable chair. The bathroom was clean and spacious. The room was also equipped with a small refrigerator.
The downstairs lobby, included a small bar area with seating for about -- people. Adjacent to that was a seating for about -- people to eat from the small """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""self-service"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" cafe where you can purchase sandwiches from a limited menu. The staff here was slow and not very courteous.
There was a $-- daily charge to park and wifi was available for free in the lobby (if you asked), but only available for a fee in rooms.
The location is a bit out of the way, but there is a T-Stop nearby.
Overall we would stay here again.

My boyfriend and I stayed at this hotel for - nights in February for his --th birthday. The staff were very friendly and we were made to feel extremely welcome. We stayed on the --th floor and had a magnificent view. The location is fantastic only two blocks from Time Square and -th Avenue and the doorman was always ready to grab us a cab when we needed to go further. 
We treated ourselves on our first night to room service and although the food isn't cheap it was delicious, but if you like steak though you have to try Ben Benson's Steak House. My boyfriend is a chef and therefore not easy to please, but he couldn't rave about his food more. We were even given a tour of the kitchen!! But be prepared, it's pricey but worth every penny.
We both thoroughly enjoyed our time in New York, and would happily recommend this hotel to anyone planning a trip.

The hotel is quite beautiful inside. But I was directly across the street from a multistory construction site. The saw blade ran at -am!!! Wooden boards were slammed into the bin. Trucks came and left at all hours. For a business traveller the room was beautiful but awkward. Low lighting on desk, difficult to plug in electronics, desk filled with tray of expensive goodies. fridge taking up too much space for a small room. Don't stay here until after construction across the street is finished. I was quite sleepy for my meetings.

Stayed here as a treat for the last night of my trip. Arrived early so checked in and left my bag. Was given a room on the --st floor which was an unexpected bonus. Great view looking north, you could see the Rockerfella Centre. The room was spacious and very nicely furnished. The bathroom was also spacious and marble-clad.

Location is perfect for tourists - just off Times Square on --th street - a short walk to the theatres and shopping on -th Avenue.

""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""It's lucky I checked"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was all he said.
All in all a very nice comfortable hotel in a great location, in need of some staff training.

I always dreamed of visiting New York.. Always heard that the people were unfriendly and the hotel rooms were as big as a closet. Once I got there I met the friendliest people who went out of their way to give me directions. The Warwick is a beautiful hotel and their staff were excellent. -Location

Metro Stations: rector Street, or Fulton Street or Cortlandt Street; PATH at World Trade Centre
-Room
Very spacious room, Coffee machine
-Service
Professional, no more no less
High quality Buffet breakfast served at hotel ; alternatively Starbucks Coffeeshop on site

I am writing this from the hotel bedroom . I have travelled to many cities and in fact stayed in New York four times but we have never stayed in such a noisy hotel . The clue should have been the white noise machine that is on the desk . White noise is to drown out the drunks and screaming sirens and all night deliveries. We haven't slept for -nights . First time ever I have wanted to leave NY .

We stayed at this hotel en route home from Michigan. Great room service, great pool, comfy robes to go down to the pool, great new workout """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""reebook"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" facilities with individual flat screens on each treadmill -it's easier to work out when watching sex and the city for some-, heavenly beds. Will stay there when we return to Indinapolis.

We stayed here for - nights in August (- adults, - teenage children) and found it to be a very nice hotel. The main plus point being the location. The staff were very helpful and friendly. As for the lifts, we never waited more than -- seconds.

Hotel is well located in the River North district of Chicago. Staff is very friendly and helpful. Continental Breakfast is provided on each floor and evening reception with complimentary cocktails is also a plus. Room and appointments are very comfortable with plush towels and robes provided. Internet is free and business center includes printing. Room was very well priced for the location.
This is a low rise hotel in a high rise city, so views are very limited. I booked a corner room which was supposed to have better views. Most of my view was of brick wall of neighboring bar. The extra square footage was in the hallway in the room. Not worth the premium for the room. The southeast corner, where my room was located, is adjacent to a bar that was fairly noisy at closing time.
Hotel does not have a bar or restaurant, but Keefers and Harry Careys are within a half block. The Public House bar is next door.
Will probably stay at hotel again. Very good value for the money.

Positive: Location, rooms, decor, service.
Negative: No breakfast variety, parking fee, no designated outdoor smoking area.
Great Friendly Staff, Clean Rooms, and great Service. They also provide shuttle service Downtown, which is a very short ride.

Fort Rapids is great. I have been to Fort Rapids several times and have never encountered nothing that the negative reviews that are posted here says. This was a convenient hotel to stay at when flying out of LAX there is a free shuttle that runs every -- minutes. The rooms are about average. If you get a good deal I would stay there for the convenience and that would be about it.

My family and I are always stayed with hotels-resorts managed by Marriott. This was our first time to stay in a Residence Inn. I've found the room is small, has small kitchen, breakfast's choices don't have a huge selection, don't have a great facilities, noises from our next door's room could get through to our room, bathroom is small, etc. The two kids slept on the sofa bed - not recommendable.
Location is great - a walking distance to the metro, shopping mall, Bryant Park, Empire State, restaurants, pizza (across the hotel), has their own tour company at the hotel lobby, etc. 
This was our first visit in NYC.

My partner and I always stay here when in SF. We were recently there and as always the service was excellent and everything about the place is consistent. You will especially love having Wolfgang Puck's original Postrio downstairs from you! Staying on the Club level gets you cocktail hour with canapés from Postrio and an open bar! The concierge on that level is extremely helpful in all aspects of booking tours or checking in for flights or arranging anything. Great location just a short walk from Union Square and tons of shopping and other restaurants. Im very excited to return in June for another visit.
Great old hotel in the center of shopping, good resturants,not far from the lake. Very good service,I hope when I do priceline again I get this hotel. This hotel has charm.

This is a great location close to Sea World. The rooms are spacious, very modern and clean. Breakfast was lovely, we only tried the evening reception one night but it was nice too. There is not much within walking distance but it is a short drive to lots of shops and eating places. Staff were very friendly and helpful.

This hotel is a hidden gem. My experience was the opposite of the previous poster. My room was very clean. The bathroom was immaculate. The housekeeping staff even straightened my stuff on top of the dresser every day. One day I lost my room key and the front desk staff knew my room number and made me a new one instantly. Great location right next to the Grove and Farmer's Market.

When we are looking for a quick weekend getaway we stay here! The waterpark-pool area is great for the entire family! Our kids like Greatwolf Lodge but we don't really care for it. This is our compromise! Food at the restaurants is very good. Great for golf, however that really isn't our thing. Close enough to the Riverwalk or Six Flags, Sea World or even Schlitterbahn if you are looking for day trips. I would highly recommend!
Had a comfortable and relaxing stay at the Chatwal. This NYC luxury hotel truly exudes class and sophistication from its interior appointments to the quality of customer service.

My recent stay at the Sutton Place Hotel was fabulous. From the first minute I arrived, every staff member not only offered polite, professional service but genuinely seemed love their jobs. 
This is a pet friendly hotel in the heart of the Gold Coast. The location is great as it is located next to great dining and shopping.
My room had an awesome view, it was clean and had great amenities. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone travelling to Chicago.

I stayed here - days before the new year, this hotel is ideal for easy access to places in Times Square. However the rooms are tiny good if it's you alone. Well the service was really good no complaints there. I would call this a really good business vacation hotel not really group visits.
The restaurant is dark but has some sort of quaint charm, food is tasty.
The only negative I had, it was winter and the heater location is in a weird location for air distribution, did not like that.
It was fine, but not terribly memorable. Nice rooftop pool, but the rest of the hotel seemed in need of an update. I'm not likely to be a repeat customer.

The Days Inn is a budget motel. The room was what we expected, a clean bed and a shower. The room was only used for sleeping and showering, if you expect more then this is not for you. Reception staff were pretty rude. The location is great, one street over is plenty of great restaurants and Fisherman's wharf is a $- bus ride away.

They only offered a very expensive continental breakfast (no price breaks for small children) and and an even more expensive full breakfast. The hostess indicated very unpleasantly that cash just wouldn't do as a means of paying for it. We left disgusted and ate at the very friendly, inexpensive and delicious Manhattan Diner which is just a few blocks away on Broadway. Stay at the Excelsior; just don't eat there.
hotel was lovely, room was huge. we had a veiw of times square dat was fab coz we wer on a high floor. def stay der again. novotels r a good chain anyway, stayn in one in liverpool it was fab -

There is a Starbucks style shop in the lobby - they aren't Starbucks owned, but do serve Starbucks coffee. You can also get your sundries here. They have a display case for bakery items, but every time I went down in the morning, it was pretty much empty. They said that the deliveries are made at -am. So if you don't need to be up before then, you'd probably be alright.
There is no free parking at the hotel - there is only paid parking in the convention center lot ($---night) or valet (unknown cost). The elevators are very frustrating - four of them and you can expect to wait a while for any of them.

San Diego State University is about - blocks away and there is a large number of restaurants within walking distance. That being said, if you walk the wrong four blocks, it seems to be sketchy.

Rooms are clean although bathroom is a little dark. There is a refrigerator but not a microwave which I thought was odd for a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""suite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" property.

There is a parking garage adjacent to the hotel but it costs $--...valet is $--. In hindsight, after a really long travel day I should have just gone with the valet.... bringing in all the luggage and navigating a small elevator and doorways was not worth the $- difference!

The hotel is spotless throughout. Our room and bathroom were small, but nice and modern. Everything (TV, air con) worked. I would definitely stay there again, as it is a great location and very good value (by NY standards).
There were - negatives:
-. Our room did smell of smoke, but I think I forgot to specify a non-smoking room. A previous reviewer has said that they had the same problem and they don't have non-smoking rooms.
-. In our room the air conditioning unit had been fixed to the window in such a way that the room was no longer insulated from outside noise, (if that makes sense!) It was noisy throughout the night with cars beeping and general NY noise.

Crunch gym location is in the basement. There's also a great wine shop next door - be sure to visit it! Valet parking is overpriced - there are much less expensive parking options at street level. 
I was substantially overbilled & had a minor heart attack, but the staff personnel quickly resolved it. 
I did not visit the House of Blues, though I had initially intended to.

The staff (Michael, Dwight and the bell staff plus the guy at breakfast whose name I didnt get) were FABULOUS. Can't comment enough about how great they were (and I'm a Brit so I don't go in for hyperbole!).
 I found the room furnishings a little bland; I was expecting something with a hint of more luxury; its all grey and a bit over-designed; our one bed suite had white plastic chairs that probably cost a forune but were uncomfortable to sit on. The sofabed is only a bed in the sense that one person can lie lenghtways on it; it doesn't pull out into a double.
But this is a minor niggle; we loved the living room; we enjoyed the breakfast and we thought the hotel was in a great location. And once again I need to mention how awesome the staff were. Would I stay at Morgan's again? Would depend on the deal I could get compared to other hotels; all being equal then I would. But purely because of the customer service - not the rooms.

If you want good location, clean and spacious rooms, friendly staff and old world charm then the Salisbury is the hotel for you. For someone who wants a very New York experience (and don't mind not having a big room-view-balcony), the Ace offers a really good experience. It is also located next to some really nice boutiques, the best coffee in NYC and a great restaurant - the Breslin.

After being bumped at the airport, I called the Radisson Lexington directly and was greeted by the the most enthusiastic agent who confirmed a room in accordance with what I outlined. She was great and went further that was required.
I arrived late in the evening of St Patrick's Day ----, among the roving, street swarms in this most desireable of hotel locations. Wandering downstairs, there was a bit of noise from the attached nightclub but I think it was coming from through the open-late Starbucks. I ate in the Raffles restaurant and have never seen such a coordinated staff of young waiters - you asked on for something, and another would place it on your table like magic. Must have been ESP among these guys! And the food was more than good.
The room was cozy but everything worked for me, especially the high-speed internet, and the small but fully-functional bathroom. The bed was one of the most comfortable hotel beds I have slept on, and with the blankets (and a extra comforter brought with the blankets) and the great pillows I fell asleep to the normal sounds of Manhattan, brought to a comforting level by good shades and drapes.
After going out the next morning, I returned to a perfectly cleaned and straightened room. Housekeeping was great and unobtrusive.
I had some special needs that the front desk took care of immediately and it a pleasure to say that the management has managed to bring this venerable New York hotel to today's standards.
The last day, I ordered room service breakfast but woke up about - hours earlier that I had requested the breakfast. I called and asked if they could send up a pot of coffee that early and that I would wait for the breakfast as scheduled. It appeared fast with a smiling room service guy who was totally concerned that I had the coffee where I like it. He returned - hours later smiling with a great breakfast.
Make no mistake about it, this is a historic Manhattan hotel right in the middle of everything. It is a short walk to all the midtown sights you may want, and on bus and subway routes to get you further to. No wonder it is surrounded by the much, much, more expensive Inter-Continetnal and Hyatt hotels. 
I would recommend the Radisson Lexington to anyone visiting New York.

I have stayed at many Starwood properties including the St. Regis brand and this property was the best. The place feels more like an apartment building than a hotel, which was fine for us. There is another part of the hotel on the other side of the block, on --th, but we couldn't tell if it was the 'better' part. All in all my trip to New York and The Edison hotel was out of this world, can't wait to go back and will definately be staying at The Edison again when i do, for the money this hotel cannot be beaten. Would recommend it to all. - the staff was helpful and friendly

- The gym is relatively small. There are two ellipticals and two treadmills, plus some free weights, but no weight machine circuit like at the Sheraton downtown. There is an indoor pool that looked clean. The gym was never crowded.
Would I stay there again? For the price that was pretty much lower than the Fairfield Inn next door, I would. For a typical full service price, there are better choices.

The rooms were quite disappointing. I finally settled on the third one they showed me among the so-called """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Grand Deluxe"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" level of rooms. The dining room was also cold and sterile, and the entire hotel is without color, unless one consider white, brown, beige, black and other neutrals to be color. In short, though its certainly a good hotel, for $---+ per room, they are relatively small and the atmosphere is very corporate, so it lacks elegance. Seems to be a great mix of families, surfers, couples, youth, life guards, and others. The front desk staff have always been fantastic to work with. They are always willing to help with any situation. The parking garage is well worth the daily rate.
It is not the quietest, quaintest location. There is lots of action in the area, so if you are looking for quiet, solitude, this may not be the best location for you.

I had stayed at this property several years ago, and when I learned that Loews had purchased it, I had no hesitations about making a reservation. As You First gold members, we were upgraded to a lovely junior suite which was perfect since there were three of us. The fold out couch, unfortunately, gave my teenage daughter a terrible backache the next morning, so keep this in mind if you plan on putting anyone on it. The manager, Daniel I believe, came out to greet us and personally helped us upstairs with our bags. We were treated like royality the entire stay. I was told that Loews will begin renovations this January, so if I love it this much now, can't imagine it getting any better. Don't hesitate to book a stay here. You will love it!!

Perfect location! Close to shopping, the river, Soldier Field, Wrigley Field, etc...
We were impressed as soon as we walked in the door. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Room was huge and nicer than expected. Overall, great hotel, location, and staff.

This hotel is in a great location ! I feel the rooms are just average(need upgraded)! Most rooms had double beds instead of queens wich was a very unpleasant surprise! They were clean although! Restaurant food was very good!

With the exception of the front desk attendant who just hung upon me, twice actually, while i tried to confirm the spelling of the hotel managers name to send a thank you note my experience at Gansevoort Park Ave was great!
We stayed for a long weekend in late October and had a great experience. At check in our room was upgraded to a room with a fabulous walk out balcony with lots of seating and thanks to the warm weather on the weekend we stayed we were able to use & enjoy the outdoor space a lot! When we walked into our room we found champagne chilling along with a handwritten note from the staff welcoming and wishing us well- a great personal touch!
Our room (a Deluxe King) was extremely clean and the decor was fresh and bold. (The hallways were very striking as well.) The King bed was very comfortable and had an abundance of down pillows and down duvets.
Our five piece bathroom was very roomy and loaded with plenty of plush towels. The deep soaking tub was amazing and had a telephone style faucet so you could wash your hair & rinse off with ease. The closet was large and stocked with two plush robes that were very cozy and there was plenty of space for all of our garments & luggage, however we could have used more hangers.
The room was pretty quiet, although our room was next to the stairwell so a handful of times we heard the stairwell door slamming shut, but we never heard other hotel guests.
We did not use room service, but we did call the concierge a few times for ice or something and they responded promptly.
We only dined in the Asellina restaurant once and it was for breakfast-brunch but it was absolutely delicious and we would definitely return!
We used the Exhale spa for massages which were very nice. The spa provides robes and has private baths for changing & showering which was perfect b-c we had already checked out of our room prior to our massages. 
The staff, especially the doormen and bellhops (whom we probably interacted with the most) were all extremely polite and courteous and attentive.
The midtown location of the hotel was absolutely perfect! You're not far from anything and there is a subway entrance at the corner of --th & Park Ave. There is also a --hour bread & butter across from the hotel on park ave for midnight snacks and a Duane Reade drugstore just a few blocks away. Also the French restaurant next to bread & butter was very good!
Overall we had a great experience and we would definitely consider staying at the Gansevoort Park Avenue again :)

I chose this Hilton for the location but it had been the worst Hilton as far as service is. I had to wait a long time just to get my luggage brought up. it seems they have a shortage of help. Very old hotel that is in desperate need of renovations. While the room appeared clean, the bathroom had dark stains on the floor and the room had a damp musty smell. The door to the room and the window in the bathroom had large gaps, which allowed bugs(spiders) in the room and noise of passing cars and slamming doors. The suite we checked into had a balcony and looked out at GE Building and Rockefeller Center. Check and see if you can the Playbill rate. Great, clean workout room too.
This is one of my very favorite hotels in the world and it never disappoints. Amazing service, wonderful staff, beautiful, clean rooms - you can't ask for more. I only wish I could visit more often.

I stay at this Marriott Courtyard each Fall when I visit Washington, DC for an annual conference. I just love the location; just a block or so north of the Dupont Circle Metro station and on the edge of the interesting and trendy Adams Morgan district. There are some wonderful restaurants all within -- minutes walk from this hotel. All of the staff, from the gentleman who parks your car to the folks behind the front desk to the waitresses in the small lobby restaurant are consistently courteous, professional and attentive. The on-site restaurant serves a good breakfast. There's a choice of a well-stocked buffet or you can order several choices prepared by the kitchen. The rooms are a little on the small side but comfortable and immaculately maintained. The elevators are never too crowded and seemed to operate efficiently and reliably. Room service, when used, was delivered promptly but the choices are limited and are pretty basic fare. Besides, with all the surrounding dining choices there's little incentive to order in. The Courtyard is not a fancy, pretentious luxury facility. It's a reliable, comfortable, clean place to stay in a good location with a friendly staff for those not too concerned about staying close to the tourist filled Mall area.

The room was more like a studio apt than a hotel room. A separate alcove for business activities, small kitchen area, a large HDTV and a large couch. Could not have been more comfortable.

The location is difficult to get to off the I---. The hotel is north of downtown Austin. So, if you're going to Austin during rush hour leave plenty of time. The traffic in Austin is horrific, probably the worst I've seen including LA.

Stayed in the Iroquois in mid August. The location is perfect! The rooms were nice, the beds were very comfortable, and the bathroom had a great shower. Having stayed at both the Algonquin and Iroquois, I will go back to the Algonquin.
We had a very nice week in California. The hotel staff was on top of everything. Well worth the money. Great rooms and location.

After having to change the location of our Daughter's Wedding Reception four weeks before the wedding with the help of Earl Adams, Director of Sales, he and the staff of Ramada made my Daughter and now Son in Law's wedding a beautiful event. From the Food to the finest details..thank you.

When I was at the Bliss spa, I saw the same travel kit runs for about $-- if you purchase it there.

All in all, I would stay at this hotel again.

Brilliant location, just a quick walk to Times Square, and not far from from Central Park and the subway.
All the staff were so helpful and patient with us asking for directions and advice.
Very clean and modern
But we unfortunately had the standard double room, which was so tiny

Nowhere to sit, thank goodness the shower was great.
Great position as I said, but would never get a standard double room again, pay the extra and get more space.

Before going to New York I checked out some of the reviews on this hotel and to be honest I was a bit unsure of what to expect however when I got there I was reassured! It's in the perfect location, close to everything and in the heart of times sq. The room was clean, modern and the perfect size. The staff were helpful and very friendly. However the room was quite hot and the lift was slow. The maid service was ok but room for improvement as our room was not cleaned for - days and had to ask for clean towels. However would consider staying there again!

Recently returned from a business trip March ----. I go to this area often and usually stay at the Double Tree - Mission Valley. Was not able to get a room.
As a Diamond member, I secured and confirmed my room on the executive floor the day prior to my arrival. When I checked in, I presented my e-check in confirmation with the assigned room number on the executive floor. The agent presented my keys and proceeded up to my room. Half way up on the elevator; I looked in my package and noticed I was now on a room on another floor. My original room number had been crossed out (it was the confirmed room number from my e-check in). I went back down to the front desk to ask why my room had been changed, not to mention that the agent never informed me of this change when I checked in and proceeded up to the floor I thought I was on. The agent apologized and stated that the floor of my room number was also considered an executive floor. I stated that I understood, but as a benefit of being a Diamond member is to secure a room prior to check in only to have it changed, what is the purpose of this benefit. Room - Very average-basic - especially for a room on the executive floor. Very small, old out dated furniture. Other reviews are accurate about the state of the rooms. Just finished a three day stay at this property and it is among one of the best Hyatt properties I have stayed at.
The lobby was grand and the staff was excellent.Rooms were clean and staff was polite.
I feel comfortable recommending this hotel to business travelers and families.
Hotel is very well located and my room had a sensational view of the bay and Coronado island.

The room was probably too small to swing a cat, as they say, but I didn't bring my cats, so it didn't matter. Honestly, unless you're paying a fortune, you're going to get a small room in any New York hotel! 
Bottom line: clean room, friendly staff, down the block from a subway station, one block from a cross-town bus, lots of restaurants in the area. That's all you need.
My only complaint would be that the bathtub is small.

I found this hotel a couple of months ago and booked it right away. the price and location were just what I was looking for. After paying in full I started reading reviews. Had I done this first I would not have chosen this hotel. All the reviews about bedbugs scared me but I'm too cheap to change my reservation and I knew I wouldn't find a hotel on the upper west side for the same price, so I decided to risk getting bedbugs. Before my trip I spent many hours reading about bedbugs and I got really scared of bringing them home with me. When I got to the Belnord our room was on the fifth floor(no elevator) but that didn't bother me considering the price. Our room wasn't too small and It was fairly clean. I immediately looked behind headboards and in drawers for signs of bed bugs and all I found was a few black spots that could have been bed bug droppings (They looked exactly like pictures I've seen on the internet.) We slept with the lights on and kept our hard plastic suitcase (which is almost air tight) closed at all times. The first night as I was trying to sleep I noticed a blood stain on the wall right next to my bed which was the same size and shape as the stains I'd been warned about on the internet. During our one week stay we got a couple of bites that probably were from bed bugs but that's it. Bugs that aren't very hungry won't come out if it's light, or so I've read. I don't think we brought any bugs home with us and overall the hotel was great. But I felt worried about bed bugs for months so I'm still not sure if it was worth it. If you are deciding wheather or not to book this hotel read reviews on this site for a couple hours first. Then read about bed bugs. If you're not scared of bed bugs, this hotel is perfect for the budget traveller.

Ok, so this hotel is inexpensive for Seattle city centre, but we think that cleanliness should be included in the price! We switched rooms as the bathroom was definitely cruddy and the bed sheets looked and smelled like they had been slept in and just smoothed over. The front desk gave us another room with no qualms. Rooms are a bit pokey and ours had a view of the parking lot opposite, but for one night before our flight the next day, it sufficed. The hotel is well-located for seeing the sights if you don't mind walking, you can get the monorail to the Space Needle just down the street too. The airport shuttle drop-off is a convenient block away. Last word, the breakfast is fine if you're on the go, coffee and danish from Seattle's Best Coffee downstairs.

Thoroughly brilliant hotel on all counts. Every member of staff we encountered went out of their way to be helpful, including concierges, bellboys, household and reception staff. For a city hotel, the room was great and had everything we needed. We asked for a quiet room and that is what we got. This hotel was very keen to get feedback and ours was obviously read as we got a very pleasant letter from the owners on our return home. As far as we were concerned, the situation of the hotel was excellent; we gave up our car so public transport was very easy once we knew what we were doing. We were ‘warned’ about the Tenderloin area but had no trouble at all even though San Francisco was very busy due to a big concert weekend. The breakfast was very good and we didn’t mind the fact that we had to wait a short time at busy periods – the staff were very efficient indeed.

Location, location, location! Great that it is very close to michigan ave! Very modern and clean rooms. The only annoying part was the checkin process on a saturday afternoon. There were so many people and since the hotel is undergoing ,a renovation, they only had a temporary front desk with a few employees.

We called each night to schedule room service for the next morning; six times they were prompt or a bit early, one time they were fifteen minutes late. Everything else ran beautifully.
The location is perfect. There's a subway stop (- train) just north of the hotel, and it's walking distance to all of Midtown - we saw two Broadway shows and ate at some wonderful restaurants and never had to take a taxi once.
Everyone on the staff treated us well. The bellmen, the doormen, the front desk, housekeeping, everyone we came in contact with was friendly and polite.
The dress code for the lobby and having to use one's key to get to one's floor after -pm are minor inconveniences. They don't expect tuxedos and evening gowns, just collared shirts and long pants. If you're going to stay at a high-end hotel in Midtown Manhattan (and not in the Times Square area), don't dress like you're at Disney World.

The Good: 
Nestled among small embassies on picturesque N Street, the Inn is ideally located near Dupont Circle, providing easy access to the Metro, shopping and eating. (In fact, the restaurant on the premises is a huge draw for locals and tourists, too). The furnishings in the rooms and throughout the structure are an eclectic assortment of antiques, or in the shabby chic style. Interesting posters, paintings, and old photos adorn the walls of the two lounges, the hallways and the rooms, giving the whole environment a well-worn and welcoming feel (like an old, favorite leather coat). 
The complimentary breakfast is excellent.
The Bad:
Four floors (around -- stairs from lobby to the top) with no ability to designate the exact room you want. According to the website, you choose the category of room and they'll choose the room number. We got room #--, with two windows giving a view of the alley behind the Inn and the parking lots for associations, committees, embassies, etc. 
The bathroom had two features worth mentioning: First, the shower head that came directly out of the ceiling and the only thing to keep the water from splashing all over the bathroom was a curtain that did not reach to the floor. The result was a watery mess that necessitated the use of a squeegee to help the floor dry if you later needed to use the sink or the toilet; second, if you do need to use the toilet and are particular about privacy, then it might be uncomfortable since the bathroom walls do not reach the ceiling, and so the space is more of a small, fancy stall rather than a room (see pics).
After -pm, this Inn is constantly packed with locals and the meeting rooms are filled with groups who have reserved private parties. The lounges and the restaurant are big draws working hours, so if you want dessert in one of the lounges or dinner, get there early or make a reservation (dinner service begins at -pm). The food is worth the trouble. If you love constant company, then the crowd is not a bad thing, but if you are looking for solitude, this ain't the place.
The Ugly:
Our location at the back of the Inn meant that we heard the occasional garbage truck come to empty the dumpsters constantly being filled with bottles and trash from the very popular restaurant. Also, either very late Friday night or very early Saturday, we were awakened by an impromptu and premature Mardis Gras celebration in one of the lots below. I thought they might scream, shout and dance until Fat Tuesday, but after an hour or so they broke up and dissolved into the night. 
No television or coffee maker in the room.
All in all, the Inn is enjoyable and would be perfect if you can pick your room (I heard that the rooms over the small lounge are best for privacy).

Good point: spacious room, clean, excellent location
Bad points: too much street noise (we stayed on the -th floor), staff impersonal, no safe in the room, bathroom very cramped, tv was placed on the side of the room and not directly in front of the bed.

I was pleasantly surprised by how nice the front staff was and how clean the room was. I even dared to go barefoot in the room!
It's noisy because of the hotel's layout and it's location on a major street a couple of blocks off the Hollywood freeway but I'm a sound sleeper so wasn't bothered much by that. Parking is free which was great but spaces are narrow. I tried the on-site coffee shop which was WAY above all expectations! It offered a variety of breakfast items with a cappucino machine to boot.

Inept desk clerks, no responce for days to email questions, had to hunt down bell boys. Had to go to desk to request normal cleaning services, several phone calls for this were not responded to. While smoking is not allowed, evidently burning noxious substances in rooms is just fine. They are trying to get by on their name but instead are only damaging it. I will never stay in any Westin again.

My husband and I stayed here for - nights. It is a small hotel,very modern and clean. It is in a superb position being only seconds walk from Times Square. We were a little worried it would be noisy being so close to the hustle and bustle but it wasn't. The rooms are quite small but lovey and decorated very well. There is no tea or coffee making facilities and that's the only down side. The hotel staff were all very friendly and helpful ESPECIALLY the concierce, John-Paul and Thyrone (not sure that's the correct spelling). They were excellent at telling us where to go, where to eat, where the good night life was and helped us to get reservations at some lovely rsetaurants. These guys have loads of experience so use their knowledge and ask them to give you tips and ideas. Thanks for a very memorable holiday!!

I am a Denver resident and I made reservations for my wife and I to stay there New Year's Eve. Downtown Denver has a midnight fireworks display that night and we had theatre tickets for the evening. I made the reservations the end of May and I specifically asked for a room with a view of --th Street, which is where the fireworks display is. I followed up the request three weeks prior to my reservation by visiting the hotel in person to confirm my request. When we checked in and got to our room I was very dissappointed in the view, which consisted of the the other side of the hotel across the courtyard. There was a sliver of --th Street in a corner view. The only fireworks we saw were some reflections of the windows across from us. Considering that the room was $--- and the reservations were made seven months ahead I will never repeat that experience again.
We had a lovely time at The Magnolia--great room, great rate, free breakfast and happy hour!

Comfort Inn on --th street was great when we got there they told us they overbooked and my double wasn't available. So what did they do, they set us up with - king rooms instead. THAT is customer service ! Can't complain they accommodated us. The rooms are tight but we are in the city. The only problem I had was the tv channel were all messed up so we had like - channels to watch. They have a free breakfast that was good, the staff are all friendly from the front desk, cleaning staff to the young lady working the breakfast. I would stay here again, their price was a fraction of what the other hotels were charging and it was right in the middle of the festivities!

My husband and I stayed for - nights (visiting family nearby). The hotel was average - great for the price. Bathrooms need updating - room only had an electric socket next to one side of the bed. Service was great, very friendly staff. 
One thing we found odd was, one morning we ordered breakfast. As noted, we left our tray in the hall, and left for the rest of the day. When we returned, the tray was still in the hall. Our leftovers had sat there all day. 
Really the convenience of the location to where we needed to be was wonderful and saved us over $-k versus staying in the Gas Lamp district.

On the reservation sheet it said I would get a iron and ironing board, I had neither. I was on a business trip and planned to iron my clothes before I went to the meeting. I went to the desk and asked the man about it and he said that the rooms dont come with it but he has one. I then asked him what I should iron on and he said he had nothing good luck. That did nto start my trip off well.

I have to say I was always a bit skeptical of staying with any of the W Hotels. I always thought they'd be crawling with wannabe hipsters and wannabe """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cool-kids"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I was also afraid of not getting a good nights sleep, thinking the hotel would be packed full of partiers late at night. Boy, was I wrong. 
The first time I stayed at the W was in August of ---- with two of my girlfriends. From the moment we drove up, we were greated pleasantly by the valet staff and greeted kindly at check-in. They made us sign some kind of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sweet dreams"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" note that basically promised we wouldn't throw any parties that would disturb other guests, which was totally fine with us because we aren't those kind of people. 
We made it up to GhostBar one night, and that was...well...an interesting crowd. Not very """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""high-end"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Just a lot of wannabes it felt like. 
In April of ----, my boyfriend and I stayed at the W just for one night and had a great experience. Valet and the front desk were always extremely courteous and kind to us.
The rooms are very cool and modern, not a whole lot of decoration. The beds are wonderful and so comfortable, I always slept like a baby. The shower was really nice as well. We never really had much of a view of anything but the highway. But honestly, when I go to hotels in a big city, I could care less to be looking out the window. The pool would probably be my biggest complaint. It's a completely covered area so you get zero sun. There are a few parts on the far edge of the pool, meaning you'd have to swim to get to it, that has a little bit of sun and those spots I'm sure are hard to get unless you get out there early.
All-in-all, both of my experiences at the W were wonderful and I definitely will stay again!

We stayed here looking for a nice but affordable hotel near the heart of NYC. We found it to be a new, classy hotel with great service. The parking is a little difficult and not much area to unload a vehicle, but a great place to stay near the subway station or a reasonable walk to the Times Square area. Very pleased with this hidden gem.

Nothing special to say, it is not a luxury hotel, but it is clean. As everywhere in NYC small rooms. The location near times square is great. I had less expensive hotels which were much better. 
The fitness room is not bad, just a bit too small for such a big hotel.

We had a terrible visit at this hotel and will never stay there again. 
Pros: Close to UCLA; close to Manny's Pizzeria, which delivers, and has fabulous food. 
Con's: 
-. VERY NOISY. It is sandwiched between Sunset Blvd. and the --- freeway. If you want to open the window you have to listen to traffic. 
-. Customer service was inconsistent. When I called and asked for a feather free room, I was told it wasn't a problem at all. Booked the room. I requested to move rooms, got a slightly quieter room, but she would not have the feathers removed. -. The refrigerator in the room is jam packed with alcohol and drinks, leaving you no where to put your own refrigerated items.
