I really enjoy staying at the Langham hotels. Boston's Langham is very conveniently located in the historic district of the city. It is easy to walk to from South Station and is a $--.-- taxi ride from Logan airport. 
The service is good, I arrived late and they were able to check in my friend who was already at the hotel. It did take me -- minutes holding before reception took my call. 
The rooms were comfortable and the seating area made it feel like a junior suite. The bathroom is older and could do with a refurbishment initiative. 
Concierge was also busy and poor man was on multiple calls as well as helping customers. It took a while before we were helped.
Overall a nice stay and a nice hotel with nice facilities.

I was excited to book the Helix for a fun twist on my business trip, but right from the start things went badly. They did not honor the coupon for free parking despite the fact that on the coupon and on the website there were no specific instructions on rules of use. The room was nice at first glance, but under the top decorative tissue there was a used tampon in the tissue box! The top layer of the bed was dry, but then urine seeped up through the bed during the night requiring me to place my bedclothes into a plastic bag in order to take them home. The hamburger bun I was served was moldly, but that was the least of my concerns. Internet signal was very poor and spotty. The staff did not do anything after knowing these problems - they didn't even bring new tissues! I will stay at the stuffy conference hotel next time. At least it will be clean.

For our parent's --th we chose the Driskill & am so glad we did. We wanted to tour the city of Austin as well as the Capitol & some museums. Everything was within walking distance from our hotel! Every person on staff at the Driskill, really makes you feel welcome. Breakfast was great in the ---- cafe. Servers & bartenders were very attentive. Our rooms & beds were very comfortable & we had everything we needed. There are pieces of antique furniture through out the entire hotel. I wish I had taken more pictures to show how gorgeous & historic this hotel strives to be. If ever in the Austin city limits again we will definitely choose the Driskill!
I have stayed here often and have no complaints. Even though it is close to the airport, you do not hear a lot of noise. The front desk is very accomodating.

Stayed here over Easter. What a wonderful hotel, smiling helpful staff, a totally relaxing atmosphere, I revelled in the complete peace and quiet. I can only compare the comfort of the bed to a cloud. I'm a light sleeper and I know we werent the only guests but there was absolutely no noise, nothing at all. Tears from my teenage daughter were imminent when her hair straightners didnt work, within minutes staff sourced some from a nearby hair salon, I need these folks for trouble shooting back home! Do eat in the Dining Room mmmm definitely grownups food. I cant understand the previous poor review at all, staff at this hotel were genuinely charming and helpful and made my daughter feel like a princess. When asked on checking out if there was anything which could have made our stay more enjoyable I had to think for a moment and finally admit that I'd have liked to find George Clooney in my suite. Maybe next time.

I can imagine if you were -- and just needed a place to crash, the Hudson would be fine. I think there's a reason that everything from the lobby to the rooms is so dark. I get the sense that the place isn't terribly clean. The nasty polyester curtains hanging everywhere in the room only add to that impression. The hallways and doors look like a minimum security facility. I've stayed at hip New York hotels like the City Club, the Bowery and the Hotel on Rivington. Make no mistake, the Hudson is none of those. Being here on business is a disaster. The only lighting in the bathroom is a tiny flourescent bar around the mirror. Can't figure out how to really put on makeup and can't even imagine how a man could shave. There's some ridiculous, tiny excuse for an ironing board. And I'm staying in an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""upgraded"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room. Everything in the room is Liliputian. I'm only -'-"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". A tall man would feel like offing himself in this place. Just fundamentally wrong in way too many ways.

Booked the motel months in advance because it was near the Aquatic Park. Hotels were just too expensive and could not offer us a suite with a kitchen and plenty of space. Never stayed at a motel before so not sure what to expect - and then there was the bed bug incident! Greatly reassured by the managements response we arrived to find a clean and comfortable motel with excellent, helpful staff in an ideal location. The motel offers free internet access, free tea and coffee, clean towels every day, a lift, even a car park space had we needed it. We felt safe - from our balcony we could see - security cameras! The area struck us as safe unless out late - same as any city.
There is plenty to see and do on the doorstep - lots of places to eat, corner shops for groceries, Safeway a quick walk away. Recommend the hop on hop off bus nearby to see the sights. Lots of local places deliver - India Curry House www.kennedyscurry.com has a pub attached so you can study the menu while enjoying a pint then have your tea delivered later on!
Our only concern was that it wasn't very quiet - the motel was quite busy and if upstairs have big feet or loud voices you will notice! And there is traffic and fog horns most of the time - but it's San Francisco after all! 
The staff will also arrange an airport shuttle service at very reasonable rates.
All my email enquiries were answered quickly and efficiently.
 We'd certainly go again.

Location: a minute from Hollywood blvd, cut through the back of Lowe's for the fastest route to Hollywood blvd.
Room: We had a - double bed room. Spacious but very very dated. But we knew that going in. Two flat screens, huge kitchen that had fridge, microwave, stove, oven, and full range of cutlery. Basically a two room apartment.
Bathroom: Very old and dated. But clean and good house cleaning.
Amenities: Free wifi, breakfast buffet. Nothing special but a bagel and cream cheese for breakfast isn't bad.
Services: Conierge was helpful. To get into the hotel you have to go up a flight of steps, and there are no bellhops. 
This place has a great location, it's cheap and it's clean. If that what you need (like us) then the place is perfect. Just be realistic with the price you're paying for the location you're getting. Don't expect this to be a flashy hotel. We enjoyed our stay and would recommend it.

My wife and I stayed here on Monday, December --, ----. It was our first visit, but not our last. The building is beautiful, the rooms are spacious & clean, and the staff is attentive. The hotel is centrally located in downtown Baltimore, and we were able to easily walk up North Charles Street to dinner at Sotto Sopra. If you're driving, use the Edison Park Fast -- hour, indoor, underground garage at Fayette & Hanover, a short block and around the corner from the hotel's front door. We pulled in at -:-- p.m. Monday, pulled out at noon on Tuesday, $--.

This hotel was absolutely fantastic! The renovations made to the room created a modern and elegant ambiance. We were fortunate to get a corner room on the -th floor with an excellent view of the city. The staff was very pleasant, especially those working in valet. For one who is not too familiar with getting a cab, the hotel staff made obtaining a cab or directions a breeze. We were in town for the CBC Annual Leadership Conference which was hosted at the Convention Center. The hotel was in walking distance to the Convention Center and various landmarks and more. We received a great deal when booking this quality hotel. The only downside was the $-- parking rate. As a result of the price, we opted to park elsewhere. I would recommend this hotel to all planning a visit to the DC Area.

We had stayed at this hotel over -- yrs ago and stayed here again on our recent DC trip as my husband loved the view from the rooftop pool. But the view is now obstructed on one side due to new building developments so the view wasn't as spectacular as before. Hotel is old but they are trying to improve. Staff was very friendly and helpful. I had read reviews about roach trap under a table in the restaurant but didn't see any. We did eat breakfast there which was average. I had read a previous review about mouse traps in the stairwell but didn't see any during our stay. The neighborhood has improved and is --- blocks away from a very nice area with Whole Foods, shops and an established DC bar. This area is approximately - long blocks from the nearest Metro station and not close to the Mall or any DC landmarks to my knowledge. Cab ride from hotel to Reagan Natl Airport averaged $--. Elevators are slow and hold about - people comfortably. I hope they are replaced as the hotel continues to improve. We had asked for a room high up with a view but only saw the side of a building. I had read reviews from Priority Club members receiving free drinks and an upgrade to a suite but these were not offered to us as Priority members. Guess you have to ask for the perks.

Booked a king spa suite for a weekend getaway with the girlfriend, and it was about perfect. Valet and front desk staff were all smiles and very helpful. The room was better than expected. Big, very clean, full of amenities, stylish, super comfortable bed, and the fuji soak tub rocks! The hotel has a great feel and style to it. The location was just fine, not sure what some other reviewers were expecting? LA is a very spread out destination, and the Hotel Palomar provides a nice central location. Close to Hollywood, Santa Monica, Beverly Hills, Griffith park, UCLA, etc. Would absolutely stay here again.

My stay on Sat, April --, ---- was a last minute reservation due to a need for an extra night in San Diego, the extreme rate at the Marriott ($--- for an avg room) and a very early a.m. flight necessitating being at the airport at -am. I found the Sheraton online via Orbitz with same day availability under $----ni. 
Pros: The room was good size. The price was good in comparison to other options. The check-in was easy, fast and they had a room ready at upon early arrival at noon. There were a couple of decent onsite choices for meals (affordable). They have an onsite spa-fitness center - so I could squeeze in a no-frills massage. 
Cons: The room was musty smelling and showed plenty of signs of wear and tear. The 'view' was of the parking lot and on the -th floor it was too easy to hear traffic noise, people talking, etc. The Sheraton wanted to charge a daily rate for internet access (when will SPG group get with the program?? Priority - aka Intercontinentals and Holiday Inns - offer free wi-fi to guests. Great for biz travelers). 
Another pro: while it is 'across the street' from the airport - it's still a bit of a hike wheeling luggage. The Sheraton provides shuttle service every -- mins - even at - am. Very convenient for that.
Good, solid property if you aren't looking for anything too fancy and don't mind a little bit of noise.

I lucked out, got a room for $--.-- by bidding on Priceline. The bed was one of the most comfortable beds I have ever slept in. My only complaints were, internet in the room will cost you $-- but they have free wireless in the lobby. The restaurant was a disappointment I would have expected a LOT better for the money
It will cost you $-- plus tip to park your car for the night

Originally given room right outside the elevator door, we asked to change rooms. They were very accomodating! Good location if you are going to Union Square! Tiny rooms, stale smelling decorative pillows, over powering smell of clorox. Found - hairs in the bed, - hair on a towel. Shower was either freezing cold or burning hot. Must be when someone else used water. Staff were quick, friendly and helpful. Noisy but wore earplugs to sleep. For $---.-- NOT WORTH IT!

Great hotel for a relaxing few nights away from everything.. Nice, courteous, respectful staff. Clean, quiet.. I enjoyed my stay here a few weeks ago. NO BUGS, NO MOLD SMELL as some one was referring to.. Overall this hotel is my favorite.

My fiancee stayed in Seattle for a romantic three day two night stay. We looked for a hotel that was close enough to walk to our favorite spots within the city and decided to stay at the Best Western Pioneer Square Hotel. It is within walking distance from both the Seattle Aquarium, Pike place market, and many great restaurants.
Upon first arriving I had trouble working the card key lock but the bell hop was very friendly and assisted us getting into our room to relax. He finished showing us our room and quietly left us to start our night.
Our wake up call came in on the dot which, for my hotel experience was rare but preferred. The continental breakfast was served pipping hot! Fresh Belgian waffles with coffee for my fiancee and myself. They had fresh fruit, yogurt and much more which we couldn't stuff ourselves with. However, I did sneak some fruit for later in the day. The staff was very polite and the food was never empty nor cold.
After a day out we returned to a well turned down room. The front desk was more then happy to sneak a bottle of champagne into our room while we were out so I could surprise my fiancee per my request by phone. We relaxed in our room the remainder of the night. Our room had a balcony overseeing the front entrance which made it nice to watch the foot traffic of the city.
After spending weekends at other hotels in the past, their prices never were justified with what we received. All of the Amenities at Pioneer Square Hotel were more then adequate and my fiancee will most definitely return. The room was superb, the staff was more then helpful, friend and went well above and beyond. 
If you plan on going to Seattle ANYTIME soon, I would highly recommend sneaking into this wonderful hotel and staying awhile. You won't regret it!

I really liked this hotel for a number of reasons. First, the folks working there were nice, helpful, not phony, fun and real. Second, the room was terrific. Had everything we needed, a little more space then most rooms in hotels. They responded quickly and happily when asking for a few things above and beyond what was supplied. The lounge on the second floor, awesome. The fountain, very nice and inviting. Loved the price. Highly recommend this place. Could walk to shopping, theatre, St. Patricks and much more...Also, not on a loud street so street noises were not an issue.

I stayed there for two nights and was totally satisfied with the services and amenities. Clean and comfy room, good breakfast and a decent size pool made it really worth the bucks.
Tip for drivers: Free parking on nearby streets is available at night

We traveled from Florida ( me and my husband ) my sister and her husband traveled from Chile , it was our first time in the Big Apple , we were in New York , I can not explain how beautiful it was the hotel , beautiful views and clean ! free internet for - minutes at the lobby (enough for check emails) confortable bed , it was the best selection in Times Square ! Everything was right there ! Farmacy and convinient store just at the corner , many places to eat , subway is - block north , Central Park is -- minutes walking !!! Love it

We drove down from New York for - nights to attend a conference. Valet was efficient. We checked in at -pm and our room was ready (not always the case some of you will or have learned - though not at a Mandarin, I'm talking to you W South Beach). We paid a special rate for the conference so the value was indeed excellent, also it was after they upgraded us to a suite too. 
Room was so quiet, considering you are neer a train track, airport and highway. We didn't hear a thing and slept like babies. Breakfast was organized by the conference so it's typical banquet food, but good. We had drinks at the Empress lounge that were great and everywhere the staff was wonderful and helpful. 
Spent some time at the pool and gym which were well appointed. We did not order room service or had meals in other outlets beside the a snack at the empress lounge (apparently the same menu as room service). 
Loved that we were walking distance from the mall and nearby a capital bike pick up station (like Velib in Paris). Starbucks right across the street for those of you who can't live without it (sadly closed on Sundays). 
Would stay there again.

We checked in the room and the air was on but would not get cool,I removed filters and dirt was caked on .The room walls were dirty the bath room reeked of old urine and had blood on the door jam. set on bed for a few moments and was bitten several times by some kind of bugs. I went to front office and explaind to them about room they said they would move us. we moved then to another room bathroom was clean however the walls were filthy air condition was nasty dirty . The fridge was all rusted microwave looked liked was dropped off of the roof then put in room. The room had spiders in every corner it was not worth the $--.-- bucks and then they not sure charged me around $ -.-- on card when moved to next room without saying they were doing it or what for. Be advised Do not stay here and expect quality . Never again

Asa former pianist at San Francisco's Stanford Court Hotel for -- years, (the only Mobil five star hotel in the city), I am no stranger to recognizing excellence in service. If Jim Nassikas, the founder of the Stanford Court, had experienced what my wife and I experienced at the Griffon, he would have been proud indeed! In every aspect of service, convenience, and amenities, the Griffon is a hotel to be recognized and praised. Particular kudos go to Austin Phillips, but the staff in general is to be highly commended. We're already looking forward to our next romantic weekend in the city, staying at the Hotel Griffon.

I have stay at this hotel a few times when I come into San Antonio for work. I usually have to stay anywhere from ---- days. It never disappoints. To be consistantly good, everyday, on every visit, shows that the management staff for front desk, housekeeping, and the entire hotel is doing something right. My room has always been exceptionally clean, and the front desk staff is always very friendly, knowledgeable, and quick to respond to any questions that I may have. The breakfast is better than most other places i stay in, with a different variety every day. The fitness center is a Ballys gym, but it definitely will do. Yes, there are obviously bigger and more luxurious hotels out there, but thats not what is important to me. The staff of this hotel make you feel like you are at home, and it has a much warmer feel to it. The ammenities are just what I want and need, and the staff makes it over the top. Thank you to the Residence Inn for providing me a wonderful stay every time I come into for work!

Room was clean. Bathtub was more of a bathtub shower stall. You could hear the airplanes taking off. The pool was under renovation. The continental breakfast was a little better than most. Hotel staff brought a rollaway bed pretty quickly. I would stay here again. It was a good value.

The Boston Harbor Hotel is beautiful and everything about it is pristine and stylish. When we first walked in the front desk staff was falling all over himself to make us fell welcome it was really really amazing. At -:-- every day there was a Cookies and milk delivered to your room and apples and candies in the hall. 
Nightly during the summer there are concerts on the water. They are really really great the two nights that we were there both groups were excellent. Everything is walkable. The north end with the best Italian food that I have ever had was just - blocks down the water. There is a water taxi from Logan Airport that drops off right at the hotel. It's very very close to everything. Boston Common, Faneuil Hall, Quincy market and most things are very walkable.
The pool and spa are amazing! The tile needs replacing but everything is clean and well maintained.
Overall, An unbelievable experience in the very best location in Boston. You really can't go wrong!!
I welcome all your questions if you want to know anything specific just contact me!

Quick check in and excellent service. I will be staying there next week again. I have tried - hotels in the airport area, this is the best for your money. Nice restaurant in the parking lot. I liked the way the staff really were happy we picked thier hotel. Personal responsibility.

This hotel brought a lot of problems to me. The hotel staff automatically processed my check out by using my credit card while I did ask to pay in cash. They then said they canceled the transaction and I paid the bill by cash. However, when I returned home, my bank credit statement still include the amount I already paid. So, basically, I have to pay twice. I am making the complaint with the bank. I however, wrote to the hotel to seek their help but they simply ignore my emails and fax.
I cannot believe that this is actually happenning with a hotel in the center of DC!

My boyfriend and I stayed at the Chandler five nights in the beginning of september. We chose this hotel based on the location, tripadvisor reviews and the nice pictures on their website. It's very centrally located a block away from empire state and within walking distance to most parts of the city. East --st street might not win a prize for being the most charming street in town, but it's quiet and safe.
We were given a room on the second floor when we arrived, but having asked for a room higher up and being light sleepers (there's a bar on the first floor), we asked for another. We were given one on the seventh floor without question or attitude, which was nice. 
Our room was a decent size and was tastefully decorated, it looked just like the pictures, a rarity for most hotels. The bathroom was small, but we lacked nothing and thoroughly enjoyed the plush frette bathrobes, the complimentary aveda products and the 'rain'-shower. The aircondition was effective and we could control it ourselves. 
We loved that the bed had a comforter instead of just sheets (being scandinavians and all), but the bed itself was very hard and not too comfortable. The tv had lots of channels, including hbo, and the hotel has its own entertainment system with movies on demand and a dvd-library, as well as playstation. 
What impressed us the most were all the little details that helped make our stay comfortable. The complimentary New York Times outside our door in the morning, the turndown service in the afternoon, the chocolates on our pillows and the little card with tomorrows weather and temperature. So cute!
The staff and doormen were all very helpful and friendly and the rooms and public areas were spotlessly clean. We needed to store our luggage there on our last day and it was free of charge and no problem. 
The few negative remarks we had were that the breakfast was very expensive (spend less money on a better breakfast elsewhere instead), the bed was really hard, it felt like it didn't have springs at all and that our window faced the back alley which wasn't much to look at. We needed the little weather cards, because we had no way of telling what the weather was based on looking outside. The lighting in the room was also a little dim. These are all insignificant, though; we loved our stay and would definitely recommend this hotel!

I stayed at the Omni Colonnade for a business trip for four nights. The lobby and decor were alluring, but once I walked into my room I was disappointed. The room didn't look like the photographs on the website at all. I had booked a room with a suite and double beds, and when I asked the front desk if I was booked in the wrong room they said I wasn't. I didn't have a separate seating area, so in my experience with hotels this was not a suite. The bed linens were clean and the room smelled okay, but the tub had mildew on the tub floor and in the grout. There was a drainage problem each time I took a shower. I informed the front desk of the problem and they took care of it the same day. For the inconvenience, the front desk manager sent a plate of fruit, cheese, and crackers to me which was a thoughtful gesture. The workout room is small, but I worked with it. The food is pricey as with most four and five star hotels, but tasty. Would I stay there again? Maybe, because it is affordable compared to the hotels at the Riverwalk.

Decided to try something new and stayed at the Marriott Magnificent Mile. The hotel was very busy during our stay, but the service was still excellent; they really go out of the way to make sure you have what you need.
The rooms were much smaller than I am used to but the view was spectacular. The walls were on the thin side, so you may want to bring some ear plugs. Bed was comfortable and the room was very clean.

We booked a - night stay at this hotel. After check in, my husband and daughter punctured their feet on nails sticking up through the carpet by the bathroom threshold and I found hairs from another guest in the bathtub. Brought this to the attention of the employees at the front desk. I was given a $-- credit for the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""inconvenience"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and maintenance would be sent to the room to fix the nails. I recently booked a room for four nights at the Hotel California through Hotwire. Naturally, rooms booked through Hotwire are less desirable, which explains my second floor interior room facing the alley. I really didn't mind the fact that my room faced the alley -- in fact, I was glad as I assumed that would help cut down on the street noise. However, I digress. Let me point out the good points of the Hotel California:
Location -- you're less than three blocks from all the action of Union Square. Very centrally located and easily accessible to all other points of the city via public transportation. Some reviewers mentioned the safety of the neighborhood -- I thought the neighborhood was fine, even at night. I never felt threatened or fearful for my safety. However, you are just a few blocks away from the shady-seedy Tenderloin district of San Francisco. So be sure you're know where you're going, direction-wise.
Value -- a very good value, especially when booked through Hotwire or other off-price venue (Priceline). However, you have no idea what hotel you're booking until you pay. Compared to most hotel rates in San Francisco, I felt I snagged a real bargain.
The Bed! -- the bed in my room was by far one of the most comfortable beds I have ever slept in. They had more than enough pillows (six pillows for one queen size bed) and the sheets and down comforter were what you would typically find at more high end hotels.
Free Internet Access was available to guests in the hotel lobby -- a nice touch when you wanted to look up the weather, local restaurants, directions, etc.
Room Comfort-Amenities -- the room, although small (but perfectly standard for San Francisco), was cozy and well appointed with bright yellow walls, unique art prints and polished hardwood floors. The room was very clean and also boasted a decent closet with an iron and ironing board and in-room safe. The room also had a small writing desk as well as a dresser and the usual coffee maker, ice bucket, television, etc. The plantation shutter shades were a nice touch, however they do tend to let a good bit of light in (not good if you like the room nice and dark).
Clean and Functional Bathroom -- the bathroom was small, but perfectly functional. However, the bathroom does need to be updated (the lighting fixtures were rusting over and the toilet seat was chipped and worn).
Nice lobby and fairly friendly staff -- the lobby complemented the feel of the hotel. The staff for the most part were professional and courteous, however they were not overly friendly. The hotel staff's personality-attitude did not affect my stay, however, I thought I would point it out. I will say that if you had a question or a request, they did their best to answer-honor it.
Wine and Cheese -- every afternoon from -:-- - -:-- p.m., the hotel offered wine, cheese and fruit to guests. That was a nice touch.
Now for the bad of Hotel California:
Room Noise -- by far, the worst aspect of the hotel and rooms is the noise one experiences. Although the hardwood floors are pretty to look at, they do nothing to mask the noise of footsteps up above you. For some reason, the guests directly above me decided to walk around their room non-stop for two hours (from --:-- p.m. - -:-- a.m.) every night. They also enjoyed dropping shoes (or something heavy) on to the floor every ----- minutes. The walls of the rooms are very thin and you can hear every word of your next door neighbors' conversations (which did provide some entertainment). Same goes with the hallways; it sounds like the people in the hallway are walking right through your room. Apparently, there is very little or no insulation in the hotel.
Room Darkness -- due to my room's location (mine was an interior room on the second floor that was less than a foot from the hotel's skylight), the skylight that was directly beneath my window had a constant light on that totally lit up my room every night (it was like the bat-signal shining directly in your room). I had to go out and purchase an eye mask at Walgreen's down the street after the first night. The handsome plantation shutters, although pretty to look at, did little to filter the light from the skylight below. Also, whenever the neighbors directly across the alley turned on their bathroom light, my room would light up even more. Needless to say, between the light and sound situation, I found it very difficult to sleep. I think this also had to do with the room location. But that's what you get when you book through Hotwire (the less or least desirable rooms). Then again, it's hard to beat Hotwire's rates!
One final note, I was not offered the frosted tequila shot when I checked in. I was not bothered by this as I really don't care for tequila. I'm not sure if this was an oversight, but just thought I'd mention it as I noticed other reviewers mentioned the same thing.
Overall, the value and location of the hotel far outweigh the negatives of the Hotel California. Just be prepared to know what you're getting yourself in for. If you're looking for a charming, unique boutique hotel with tons of character and personality, this is the place for you. If you're a light sleeper, be sure to bring the earplugs and eye mask.
Finally, I will close my review by stating that I would stay at the Hotel California again, but only if I could be guaranteed a room on their top floor, which should eliminate the non-stop footstep noise from above.
Enjoy San Francisco -- it's a wonderful city!

Good luck finding a place to sit and relax if you are not there first thing in the morning when they open. The location of the hotel is excellent. The hotel itself was pretty nice. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was clean and had a nice bar. The rooms also have a small balcony which I liked very much. I liked the view of the freeway from the balcony at night. Oh... and parking is free. The only thing that I did not like about the hotel was the food. It simply wasn't that good for the money I paid. I ordered a sandwich, which came with fries which tasted like they were re-fried. I liked everything else about this hotel and will recommend this to other people.

If you need a clean, comfortable and reasonably priced hotel smack in the middle of all that San Diego has to offer, this is the place to stay. We recently stayed here two days before a cruise and one day upon returning from the cruise. The hotel is located directly across the street from the cruise ship terminal. If you get a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""bay view"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room (and I highly recommend that you pay the extra money for the bay view room), you will see the cruise ships docking and departing. While staying there we saw Holland American's Oosterdam (currently doing the Mexican Riviera cruises) and Holland American's Zaandam (currently doing rountrip Hawaii cruises) dock, discharge passengers, take on supplies and embark the new passengers. When we left the hotel to embark the Zaandam, we walked across the street with our suitcases, went through passport control, walked into the cruise terminal and entered our cruise cabin, all within -- minutes of walking out of the Holiday Inn.
In addition to being close to the cruise terminal, there are several Harbor Tour companies directly across the street from the hotel along with a stop for the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""tourist trolley"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that travels throughout the San Diego area. If you like to take public transportation, we saw several bus lines running directly in front of the hotel. In addition, the hotel runs a free shuttle to the Airport, the San Diego Zoo and the major shopping areas. The location truly cannot be beat.
We were somewhat concerned about staying at a Holiday Inn since our previous experience with the chain has been very hit and miss. This hotel did not disappoint. While you are paying more for the location and the view (around $--- per night with taxes), the rooms are very comfortable and clean. Check-in was painless with our room being ready in the mid-afternoon when we arrived. The room had a king size bed, a desk with a desk chair, one comfortable chair and footstool, large TV (not a flatscreen), coffee maker and large closet. In the first room that we had, the closet was in the bedroom. In the second room that we had, the closet was in the bathroom. We had two different types of bathrooms. The first room had an outside sink with a toilet and tub-shower in a separate room with a regular door. The bathroom in the second room had the sink, toilet and walk-in shower in one room with a sliding door. The glass on the sliding door is opaque. I do prefer a regular door on a bathroom but for one night, it was fine. The balcony has two chairs and a small table. While the balcony is not large, there is plenty of room for two adults to sit and watch the harbor activity. The beds are comfortable and the linens actually fit the bed (you won't be remaking the bed in the middle of the night). Unfortunately we did have to listen to our neighbors returning from a late night (at -:-- a.m. in the morning) so if you are bothered by hall and-or adjacent room noise, bring your earplugs. Generally speaking, the hotel is very quiet. Check-out is also painless. You will get a copy of your bill under your door the morning that you leave. To check out you call a number from your room phone, leave a message that you are checking out, close the door and go. There is no need to go to the front desk.
Each and every staff member that we encountered including the front desk staff, the concierge, the room maids, the restaurant staff and the deli staff were very professional and accommodating. We were frequently asked if there was anything that we needed to make our stay more pleasant. 
There are multiple food choices at the hotel including a wonderful and hospitable restaurant just off the lobby, a deli located a few steps away outside with both indoor and outdoor dining, and a Ruth's Chris Steakhouse just next door. For those of you that are turned away from Ruth's Chris by the prices, eat at the bar. The bar menu is very reasonable and the bartenders will keep you entertained while you eat. The shrimp on the Shrimp Caesar Salad are the same shrimp used in the Shrimp Cocktail at about the same price for a full salad. You don't need a reservation to go in and eat at the bar.
While the Holiday Inn On-The-Bay is not the Ritz, it is a very nice hotel given its location and views. It is obvious to me that Holiday Inn is trying to upgrade its image and get more consistency location to location. Before you stay here, join the Holiday Inn Priority Club (can be done on-line) and you will get some """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""extras"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" when you stay at the hotel (e.g., later check-out).

We were scared at first cause we didn't know if this place would off been good. We have had bad experience in super - in the pass, I can say that our stay in super - this time was great. The room was clean and the people were great as well. It just made it so comfortable staying there. A plus they also have room service, witch is great. The most important thing was the price. We will come back for sure. I forgot to say the parking is free! :)
Great property, wonderful location and walk to everything. Well done will visit again

I stayed at the Valencia for a seminar, and found the rooms looked attractive, but mine smelled like a cheap cigar. I called the desk and they sent an air filter, which ran the whole time but did little to clear up the air. When I left, I used the Express Check-out and had no balance. (The group I was with picked up the bill.) I just discovered that they charged me for the next night. I tried to call the hotel several times, finally finding out that I needed to speak with someone during the ---:-- hours. The hotel looks nice, but it is lacking in the Customer Service Department.

Stayed here for two nights due to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""managerial recommendation"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The hotel is one block away from our company offices, and a WHOLE lot less than the Hyatt down the street. 
If you don't mind a ----- minute stroll, it's close enough to Times Square that all those tourist attractions are accessible. And there is a subway stop right at the hotel, if you prefer to take it down to Times Square. (If coming from Penn Station, you will need to transfer at Times Square.)
So far, so good. However...
I really hate writing anything less than a positive review; but there were a few unforgivable attributes here.
On arrival I was assigned an upgraded room on the --th floor. The room itself was spacious, which in NYC can be a rare feature. No problem getting into it either, because the door was ajar. The bathroom had a dirty floor (ground in dirt) and mildew around the tub. Both of these should be easy to stay on top of, so chalk that up to a management issue. Bed had craters in the mattress that were deep enough to cause a backache. This is a pet peeve of mine, and the Park Central was way into negative territory at perhaps the second or third worst craters so far this year.
Would I stay here again? Not too likely.

The primary reason for our stay here was due to the fact that all hotels located in the downtown area were booked for Comic-Con (July -----). Seeing that this convention only happens once per year, the pros & cons listed below apply to all travellers.
Pros: 
- Free parking
- Friendly front desk & cleaning staff
- Free Wi-Fi, although it can be very slow at times
- Close to highways
- Nearby shopping (The Fashion Valley shops offered all the big name department stores, there was also a Target with a grocery store nearby for snacks and necessities)
Cons:
- Rooms are outdated, and have a very musty smell
- Website promotes that there are an abundance of television channels, however, the satellite feed was very poor for the - nights we were there
Stayed at this hotel at a cheap rate. Next to a strip club if you are into that.

We had a King bed room, with views over the reservoir. In one sense, this hotel could be rated - stars. Here are the pros - immaculate, professional, nicely appointed rooms, cool, spacious, clean. Cons - Our room had a door in the wall, apparently going into an adjoining room. We were able to hear all the conversations of the resident teens next door. I realize that this hotel is a 'business expense account' hotel, and who cares if they nickel and dime you with all the extras. I was in chicago to see the White Sox and the Cubs play.
I was a little nervous about this place, but once I checked in and saw my room, it was fine.
The guy that checked us in, was very friendly and funny. Made jokes with us the whole time. When we got to our room it was clean and comfortable. Fluffly pillows. No problems with noise or anything. 
The wifi worked fine, and so did the A-C. The only problem we had I believe was the tv, I think we only got like - channels. But I was asleep as soon as I got back so I didn't care, and my boyfriend was happy to watch whatever.

I had no problem getting to US Cellular Field, or Wrigley Field. I drove to both. Very easy to get to with a gps and a nice drive. Chicago is a beautiful city.
Would for sure come back and stay here again!

My wife and I stayed - nights at the Bullfinch. I booked it after reading a few reviews on tripadvisor and finding that it was one of the less expensive hotels in downtown Boston. We arrived to a courteous bellman who helped us with our baggage. Then, the desk attendant told us that they didn't have the room that I had booked! I was pissed! She told us that she would have to upgrade us to a room with a King Size bed. Yeah, right... I thought. Well, as it turned out, she DID upgrade us to a very nice room, one at the apex of the triangular hotel and the room was very nice. Crisp, clean, heavy sheets, very clean bathroom, etc.
One of the nicest things was some of the staff. The bellman was very friendly and helpful and got a map out and drew where we wanted to go and pointed out some other things (restaraunts,etc.) of where we might want to go.
Also the bar was nice for a drink of too. A little pricey but they also had some nice appetizer-type food. Try the little """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""slider"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (mini-burgers). They were really good! The bartender was really fun to talk with - knew a lot about the area, the local sports teams (Red Sox, Celtics, etc.) so we all had a great time. I would stay here again in a heartbeat.

This hotel has a great location, very close to every place we needed to be. It is a little bit older, the lobby doesn't really show it, but the rooms do. The beds were comfortable though, and like I said, the location was what will really do it for you.

Expansive lobby area which is clean and efficiently run. The bedroom I had was very small, with a very noisy A-C unit. The place could really do with a major refurbishment as my room and my friends room were """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""tired"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" with wallpaper peeling off the walls. The staff were friendly and helpful, but I wouldn't stay again.

This hotel is good if you are in NY for a fun weekend and are not planning to spend too much time in your room. However, if you are on business and want a hotel that offers rooms that are comfortable, faily spacious, practical and tastefully decorated to allow you to wind down and relax after a busy day at the office then do not stay at this hotel.
The only thing good about this hotel is the very comfortable bed. Everything else is a joke, especially the bathroom.
I have stayed at numerous --star hotels around the world while on business and this hotel was the worst experience.

I have stayed numerous times at the Court hotel when it was the W and now as part of the St Giles Hotel chain. The hotel is as good or better then when it was under the W name and at better rates then the W. The rooms are spacious and the service is excellent.
If your looking for a place to stay that is close to everything and at a affordable rate, this is the place to stay. I highly recommend it.
Booked this for a fun weekend outing with the hubby. We loved it. The hotel was newly renovated in a modern hipster decor and the service was great.

I have been to a few hotels in the Times Square area of New York. This is the first that I would ever go back to. They staff was helpful, the rooms were very nice and the location can't be beat!
We were able to catch the subway right across the street. There were several places to eat and shop at and Times Square, Rockafeller Center and Central Park were all walkable distances! The rooms were clean, appeared to be bedbug-free, and well stocked with towels. Our room had a coffee maker, fridge and microwave all of which made bringing leftovers back well worth it. 
I would call the rooms spacey considering the normal size in NYC. Three of us shared the room with no problems. The room could use a bit of updating, but was clean and perfect for our use. We were on the third floor and could sometimes hear the subway, which ran under the hotel, but the noise wasn't a bother at all. Any floors up probably wouldn't hear a thing. They had a - station computer-printer area that was secure and only available to room key holding guests with one hour of free internet. It was very helpful to print off out boarding pass for the next day.
The staff was very helpful in directing us to NYC attractions and provided a map with subway lines listed. We couldn't have found our way without it!
They held our bags at check out until we left for the airport hours later for free. There were security people who checked that we had room keys in the evening hours for safety reasons. I felt very safe.

The Joule is an amazing hotel. The rooms are beautiful, the pool is unique, the Charlie Palmer serves one of the best filets I've ever had, and the PM Lounge offers a classy, fun nightlife atmostphere. Nothing but good experiences at the Joule--highly recommended.

I hate to let others in on this best kept secret, but The Donatello and its wonderful staff deserve better, so here it is: if you are planning a trip to San Francisco (business or leisure) and you are looking for the most spacious and well designed rooms in town, central location (one block off Union Square), if you appreciate being treated like a guest (compared to the number treatment you get at most other hotels), and if you want the best value you can get The Donatello is the hotel for you. I usually stay at five star hotels, and have stayed at many hotels of that category in San Francisco before business brought me to The Donatello, and it will definitely be my hotel in San Francisco from now on - this is the best hotel in San Francisco!

A wonderful place, spacious and comfy rooms, great staff, and super location: nice park with a cable car stop on one corner, in the REAL Fisherman's Wharf area (not in so-called Fisherman's Wharf hotels many blocks away), one block walk to the swim beach (cooooold water), bike rentals very close for a ride to the Golden Gate Bridge (and over down into Sausalito if you like riding and a beautiful ferry boat ride back, a short cab or bicycle ride to Columbus area with wonderful cafes, Italian restaurants and, of course, the City Lights Book Store. Kids love it, parents love it, anyone would. Only catch is that since everyone loves it, the prices have gone up considerably over the last couple of years. But if the prices are OK with you....you will be very happy there. A real San Francisco gem

This was my second stay at your hotel. Again, the rooms were nice and clean with ample room ... And the pillow assortment rocked!
Management was professional and very helpful and full of smiles. They also rocked!
See y'all next year for my annual Arizona visit.

Doesn't look much from the outside but what a surprise inside. Beautifully restored hotel, elegant but definately not tired. In the public areas, including the restaurant, the furnishings were luxurious,and the chandeliers stunning. The bedroom was large and nicely decorated with plenty of storage space. Beautiful pool outside surrounded by colourful and well maintained gardens. A special mention must go to the concierge who organised chocolate dipped strawberries, grapes and wine to be left in our room when I mentioned it was my birthday.

Fortunately, the Sheraton is a few blocks away from great shopping and walking through the snow wasn't bad at all. In fact, we had to walk to all of our destinations because the Taxi's and Public Transportation system were not running at full capacity. We even walked to Pike's Place and the Aquarium one day and the Seattle Center another (yeah, the monorail was down also!). Still quite bearable from the Sheraton and my son thought running through all the snow was a blast.
A few interesting things I noticed, lots of people smoking, and it didn't seem that most folks walking around were very friendly or courteous at all. I got the feeling that if I didn't get out of someone's way they'd walk into me. Just across the street is a ChesseCake Factory which is a much better deal for nearly the same quality of food. Only problem is that the Factory doesn't open for breakfast. My suggestion would be to have a donut and coffee for breakfast, you're in Seattle after all! There really aren't too many simple places to eat in the near vicinity unless you go to the food courts in one of the shopping centers nearby. The ones we went to seemed to be quite upscale so even the food court can be a bit pricey given the type of food served. 
All in all a pleasant stay.

The club is located in the theater district and boasts old world beauty but with very comfortable, modern rooms. My room was a beautiful corner room with two queen sized beds. Both nights there, we had drinks at the Rendezvous bar on the -th floor. The service was attentive and friendly - lots of attention to detail but it didn't feel stuffy. Everyone from the wait staff to the front desk staff were incredibly friendly and personable.

After an upgrade we got the room on the --th floor. The view from our room was splendid. The location is the heart of the financial district and is extremely walkable to most of the downtown area. I stayed on the -th floor and while my little suite was definitely spacious, the hotel felt old and dirty to me. I could see where the space and little kitchenette might be appealing to families or extended stay travelers, but as a single traveler spending one night on the way to a business meeting, I didn't enjoy staying here.
