They are not a - star hotel, they don't have a hotel store or gift shop, there's no gym, and I wish there were a hot tub, but for a reasonably priced place to stay, they are excellent. The grounds and rooms are very clean and well maintained. Bedding smelled freshly laundered, and I loved the large vanity area. Staff is very friendly - from the employees at the front desk, to maids, and the people working breakfast. The free deluxe continental breakfast was great. The Inn is centrally located. It's worth walking under the freeway overpass to reach Old Town rather that try to find parking over there. We also stayed at an inn located on Hotel Circle, but ended up driving back towards Old Town because of the large selection of eateries and shops there. Just keep in mind that since it's so affordable, families with small children choose to stay there. Our children are older teens and everything was great. We stayed - nights.
The room was very clean, a little dated with some repairs need BUT nice and clean. The room we got was a little noisy at night (right next to the vending machine) overall we had a good stay.

I would recommend this hotel for people traveling to NYC for leisure. The location is great and the service makes Sanctuary stand out against most other hotels in NYC. We will definitively try this hotel again the next time we visit NYC.

We surprised our daughter for her -th birthday and decided to stay at the Baltimore Marriott for a couple of days. Best decision we could have made. As soon we got there to check in, three people came up to sing happy birthday to her. Then they upgraded our room for free, and when we went out to dinner that night they must have tried to sing happy b-day again because we got back there was a beautiful, obviously handmade cake with fondant icing and Happy Birthday written in chocolate around the plate. They even did it for her again the next morning at breakfast! Food was incredible--get the breakfast package--it's worth it. Food is a little pricey without it. The only possible things I could ding them for is no free wireless Internet access in the room--it's $--.-- per -- hours, and the taxes are outrageous (--% per night) but I would think that is the case anywhere you stay in the city. 
I would recommend the Marriott Waterfront without hesitation. Everyone we met was wonderful, kind and accommodating. They made us feel so special!

I just stayed at the Bahia Resort Hotel, and let me tell you I had the time of my life! I live to travel, and I am constantly visiting new hotels. I have stayed in San Diego several times, but it seems like the only area I am ever able to get a reasonable rate in is Mission Valley... which is not a desirable area to stay (no beach, and not at all what you think of when visiting San Diego). So when I took a little time to research rates for my recent weekend trip, I was pleasantly surprised to find that I could stay at the beach without paying a fortune!! I was able to enjoy my entire weekend without having to drive anywhere. There is a lot of great restaurants within walking distance, and we LOVED Cafe Bahia... so delicious. The hotels Mediterranean theme is absolutely charming, and the rooms were clean and had everything we needed. And the staff was so nice!! Smiles all around. I can't wait to tell all my friends about this great hotel... and I will definitely return!!!

I traveled here with a group of --+ coworkers for a meeting-sightseeing trip. This hotel was BEAUTIFUL! The second you walk in the door you know that the hotel is nice. It looks like it has newly been renovated. It is next door to the WTC and the ---- memorial site. Most of the rooms look over the ---- site which is really cool. There were other complaints of voice from the construction but I never noticed anything. The hotel staff was great. They helped me with directions to different locations that we were going. The only con was that the restaurant and bar closes really early. Other than that it was a great hit with all of my guests. I had one issues with a drunk guy following me to my room but I called security and they were there within minutes to take care of the situation. It was really reassuring that they were so quick to respond.

It's the typical Kimptom Monaco hotel with a stylish building, nice and artistic interior decorations, free wine reception daily from ---pm in the lobby, great spa products in the bathrooms (Occitane). Great location downtown Baltimore with nice views of the other skyline buildings. Valet parking is expensive --$-day and nearby garages run about -----$-day over the weekends. Also, as a negative I should mention the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""free breakfast"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is a bit of a joke if you got it in the package, since it includes only coffee-tea, pastries and fruits, but if you want eggs, you have to order off the menu. I am not clear why they played this little cheap thing as a welcoming package since it's not really a pleasure to find this out when you go there. A big plus, however, the B&O restaurant in the hotel have amaizing dinners; the chef makes some of the most delicious meals I had; we tried the beef and chicken and can tell you that different flavors just melt in your mouth; a definitely must if you plan to dine in the area....Otherwise, rooms are a bit small and the A-C seems quite noisy when it runs. The staff is incredible and very accomodating, a typical for Kimptom. Definitely a nice place to stay overall.

I stayed for a couple of days at the Pan pacific hotel and I have every reason to recommend it. I could walk to all places I wanted to go but if tired I could take advantage of the free lift they provided you with on most days to any place within a distance of a couple of miles from the hotel which I found great service . Beautiful big rooms with very good service. Very friendly, helpful staff and breakfast is also very good which is very important for me.

Wonderful hotel, we had a nice corner room on the --th floor. They have a very nice lounge, however with dinner reservations each night at the likes of Daniel and Per Se we never availed ourselves of the lounge (although seriously - it was as nice as anything overseas - this was not your standard US hotel executive floor lounge).
Room was nice, clean - staff was friendly, professional.
Hotel is perfect for either business or leisure (we've done both here). I love the place - it's a great deal (rooms for under $---). As nice as the W, IC, Hilton(s), etc...
Desk and Internet access are great for getting some work done (desk is large enough to work at (a real consideration in NYC)). The room is nice enough to enjoy spending a few moments in - overall - we loved it.
We enjoyed it and we'll go back.
-. I wish they had a large tub in addition to the shower.
-. I loved the shower - but the wife pointed out you could not turn it on without getting wet (awkaward placement of faucet handle).
-. The hotel main entrance is between the side streets - difficult to get a car there (even my dial - limo's were confused).

Great location with large modern rooms but let down by the slow service. It seems to have loads of staff to help you but they are not very quick to sort any problems or even serve you! We soon started to go elsewhere for our drinks as the staff seemed too busy talking to each other. However, the hotel was clean and ideal as a base to see and explore New York.

Room was very spacious with small, modern stainless steel kitchenette (refrigerator, sink, table-- chairs, etc), beautiful light, Frette linens, free (fast!) wireless or cable internet, dressing table, desk, extremely convenient - near subway, Whole Foods, many reasonably priced, restaurants, friendly, helpful staff (directed us to whatever we needed). I'd love to go back soon!

I specifically asked for a room without street noise, having read some yelps about this place and was assured I would be ok. I can sleep through noise, especially when I'm out of town, but damn...it was a lot.
other than that, this place is pretty nice. The staff are rather oblivious to customers...I saw this many times to others and us. It could do better, especially at those rates. Oh, and $---day parking? Welcome to San Francisco!

Stayed here for one night before international trip. It is still undergoing renovation and we got an old room. Small with poor temp control and outdated bath. It was clean but the wallpaper was bubbled. At - am the renovation crew started drilling into our outside wall with a jackhammer. It was deafening. We had to get up and out early. 
The front desk people were helpful but the lobby is almost non-existent with nowhere to relax. This is a bare bones place that is in transition. We have stayed here before and the real draw is the location and proximity to Times Square and Broadway. If you can get a good price and don't mind some hassles then it may be OK for you. Don't expect much.

Was in Austin for a meeting at this hotel. A historic landmark, updated into a very nice hotel. Just a couple of blocks away from the Texas State Capitol and a few more from the University of Texas. I found a Starbucks (always a nicety) two blocks down the road, along with a Ruth's Chris Steakhouse.
Would definitely stay here again.

I have to admit, I wasn't expecting much due to all of the negative reviews, but not only was I pleasantly surprised, I fell in love with the Inn! For all of you who are hesitant due to previous reviews and their lack of a fancy website, don't be put off and reserve yor room now. The Inn isn't your cookie-cutter Hilton, but a charming Parisian-like jewel in a trendy-fun neighborhood. It has the feel of a European hotel with a very friendly staff, a nice complimentary breakfast each morning, complimentary cookies & coffee in the lobby ---hours a day, and antique light fixtures throughout. We got the last room at the Inn and when I was making my reservation she warned me that the room was small, so I anticipated tiny, but it was just fine. There was a large closet for our bags and everything was clean, which is important. Some reviews said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""old and dirty"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" well it may be older but nowhere did I see dirty, and I am a clean fanatic. Some folks just mistake old for dirty, and I guess in that case old homes and old brownstones and old furniture are all dirty. If you don't like charming and prefer cold and bland then stay elsewhere, but if you want to feel comfort & quaintness, and be in an amazing location that's just a short walk to Wrigley Field, then this is the place to be!

Comfortable rooms with Very Nice Views of Seattle space needle.
Heavenly bed was good, but could use newer bedding.
The rooms were a bit small, but comfortable.
The Heavenly Shower was Great! - Thumbs up for the Double Shower heads.
The bathroom was a bit small, felt tight. You had to move out of the way to open the door.
Nice Central Location.
Pacific Place, Pike Market, are all nearby. An Easy monorail ride to the Space Needle as well.
Got a great deal from hotwire at $--. Plus got an upgrade to a Space Needle View Room. A really great deal. But next time, i'd rather book early and find the hotel i really want. (and not random from hotwire),
All in all a good stay.

Spent one night at Heartbreak Hotel and moved on to other accommodation nearer downtown and Beale Street. We had viewed the property on a previous visit to Memphis so expected it to be a little seedy. The bathroom was not clean. Had to ask twice to have the bath cleaned. It was covered in scum with a black ring around it. On second request they responded and sent someone in to clean it. Many of the fittings were old and rusty. It wouldn't take much to touch up the paint and and replace the rusty fittings. All looks old and tired and an over-priced hotel...but you're there for its proximity to Graceland and the Elvis experience - an easy walk - the hotel is adjacent to Graceland. Also it is quite a distance from the music on Beale Street.
The staff in the breakfast room were awesome, and very entertaining. They augmented the Elvis experience with their humor and antics. Loved that part.
Liked having stayed at """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Heartbreak Hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" ...but needs work to up-grade and maintain it. 
Last visit we did Graceland and found it very tacky and commercial. This time went to the Elvis sites in Tupelo. This is magnificently done.Really tasteful. A spiritual experience - I like the music, but am not an Eiivs fan-fanatic...but Tupelo was special. Really recommend it for those on an Elvis or music trip.

When you enter, you know immediately you are in a place where your senses can finally escape the dull, routine world outside. Every room you walk through is different and stimulating. We stayed in the John Lennon Room, which reminds you of his bed-in, while surrounded by unique, authentic memorabilia.
The Sunday Brunch was spectacular as was the entire experience. 
No other hotel experience can compare. 
TT

My wife and two daughters, one - and other --, had a great time! This was our third time back and we really enjoyed it. We were there from July -th to July -th. TC at the front desk was alot of help. Several of the conciereg's were also so friendly and helpful like Melanie and Whitney. Whitney even personally delivered an item we asked for to our front door. There was another very friendly and helpful person Malara sp? and she was great. So, overall I would tell anybody its a great place to visit. Great for families too being so close to Sea World. The pool is alot of fun and right on the ocean. The staff that serves drinks by the pool are also friendly and helpful. See you again San Diego Hilton!

I stayed here with my wife and was very pleased with the hotel overall. The room we stayed in was great, on the -th floor and had a nice view of the city. Having a priority rewards card got us free buffet breakfasts every day. It is located directly across from the Peabody hotel and within walking distance from Beal St. Another added bonus is that some of the carriages stop right in front of the hotel if you're up for a horse drawn tour of some interesting parts of the city.
The zoo was about - miles away, Graceland was a little farther but still a short drive. Sun studios and the Rock and Soul museum are walking distance, as well as any food or drinking worth going to.
The down sides were few: The bathroom was made for half a person; to do anything in there required the door to be closed. Next I would say that the parking garage is a joke, and $-- per day. We checked in on a Friday and had to circle the cramped - floor garage waiting for someone to leave. The parking spaces are extremely small (I wouldn't bring a SUV) Also of note would be the incredibly slow elevators. Lastly and most minor is that the table in our room had a lose leg on it.

My friend and I booked this place after doing our research and reading up on TripAdvisor. We weren't disappointed. It has an air of understated elegance about it and has got the most fantastic location - somehow both quiet and right in the middle of the action!
We thought that because it was a boutique hotel the staff might be a little snooty, but they went out of their way to help us. Our flight over was cancelled and we couldn't get to New York until the next day, but when we called up, they just made a note on the file and said they'd look forward to seeing us the next day. This was appreciated because they were fully within their rights to charge us for that night.
When we got to the hotel, they had put us in the wrong sort of room, but moved us with profuse apologies once we pointed this out. The concierge was happy to make recommendations and reservations for us.
The room was quite small, but it was beautiful. Candles and little postcards on brackets around the room and the most amazing beds with the best pillows ever. No surprise that we fell asleep the afternoon we arrived and slept through to the next day!
I agree with the comments made before about the 'atmospheric' lighting, and it was sometimes difficult to find our room in the dark corridor, but this IS a trendy hotel - not totally unexpected. I imagine this is why it's such a hit with celebrities - no-one would ever be able to make them out in the dark!
Overall an amazing stay - will rave on about this place to anyone who will listen (and lots who won't, as well!)

I also had this hotel assigned to me on Hotwire. Not the nicest accommodation no, but I was clean, no bugs. It could definitely use a remodel though the rooms are old in need of new carpet and wallpaper,bathrooms are old and need new tiles. I will say this though the location to everything is awesome and the staff are super nice and helpful. I left my cell phone there and they had it mailed to me very quickly after I sent them postage. In two days from the time I left, I had it back in my hands. I felt safe while I was there. If the they just renovated it, it would be a great find.

We enjoyed our stay at the Hilton Bayfront. Great views, quiet and relaxing. Great place to go for runs and get exercise. A bit of a walk to other restaurants in town but views made it worthwhile. Was very glad we purchased hotel package which included parking, breakfast and Internet as otherwise these are expensive add-ons. We had connecting rooms with our teenagers and worked well. Would stay again.

Had - nights in San Fran as a part of a larger road trip with a rental car so we were looking for a good value, comfortable hotel in a great location with undercover parking. A bit of research on Trip Advisor suggestged that Columbus Motor Inn would fit the bill and it did so perfectly. It is not the fanciest place we stayed in during the trip but the room was large, clean and warm. It is well positioned to walk to entertainment on Fishermans' Wharf. Cable car stop is a short stroll and MUNI bus stops right outside.

Partner and I stayed at St. Mark's one Saturday night in August. We chose it for its affordability and location in the East Village. We were given a room at the very top (there are four rooms up there, -P--P) because I requested a quiet room not facing the street. What we got as a consequence was a room that looked a good bit more tired than some of the ones shown in photos here. The issue could be that they are still in the process of renovating up there, not sure. But, aesthetically I found it to be a good bit more on the homely side than I expected. 
The room was very small but adequate. Mattress appeared new but on the cheap side -- not great support but for us just fine for just one night. The AC struggled to keep up with the warmth but provided adequate cooling. 
Staff were decent but then again we didn't make any big demands to test this further. They let you leave luggage there for the day -- they have a tagging system and put the bags in an unused guest room.
Overall, the place appeared to me to be decently clean and well-run. I wouldn't choose it over Ye Olde Carlton Arms, though, where for the same price but you get lots of character, and it's just nine blocks further up the street!

We stayed for a Friday and Saturday night to attend a concert at the Hollywood bowl and had an acceptable stay. It met our needs and expectations and we would stay here again. There were good points and some bad points that we could dwell on, but overall the place was fine. It is located in downtown which is great for businesses and conferences but not good for nightlife. Parking is expensive, but if you go - block past the hotel, you can park overnight in the garage for $-.--.
The good points: We bid on the hotel via priceline and received a good, low rate. It had a desk and a LCD TV. I’m not sure if this was one of the renovated rooms, but it seems to be somewhat updated. There is a gym, spa, several businesses and a mini-foodcourt in the hotel. We ate supper once and breakfast once at a couple of these places and the prices are reasonable. This works out really good if you don’t like paying the expensive hotel restaurant prices. The metro station is only two blocks away and we took it to Hollywood blvd and then caught a bus to the Hollywood bowl. Total trip time was about -- minutes. The elevators are fast and come quickly when you push the button. The bed were comfortable. We did not have any problems with the staff, but we never need them other than to change out our towels.
The bad points: Parking is expensive at the hotel-around $---$-- a day. The room was small. Barely enough room to move around comfortably, but we don’t spend a lot of time in our room when we travel so this didn’t matter to us. The room service was pricey, but it is comparable to the same hotel chain at all other cities I have been to. We were in the yellow tower and the elevators we had to use did not stop on the -nd or -th floor. So you had to get off on the -st or -rd floor and take the stairs or escalators. The hotel is a little dated and I guess most people categorize this as a bad point, but I usually see it as part of the atmosphere of the place-I’m not the type that likes to have the same exact room, hotel, carpet, food, etc. etc. no matter where I am visiting. 
Some other points to mention: We did not eat at any of the restaurants, but we did order room service late one night after the concert around -am. It was delivered within about -- minutes and the food was decent, nothing to rave over but it was ok. Overall for the price and the level of service we received, we were satisfied with our stay.
We would recommend this hotel if you got a decent rate around the $--- range, but not for much more than that.
This hotel was great, right on the lake in Austin. Rooms were very nice and clean. Wish we could have stayed longer. Would definitely go back next time I'm in Austin.
Been there - night. Not impressed for the service. No internet in the room. A little bit noisy.

We stayed there one Saturday night in October, ----. Room ---, looking straight at the highway (and the Camden skyline). You could hear the traffic noise only if you were real quiet and listened real hard. Our room had double windows (not a storm window over a real window, but a real window inside another real window) and heavy curtains. Noise was not an issue in the least. Honestly, I've been in a couple dozen hotels that were a lot noisier than this one. 
The hotel itself is right at Penn's Landing on the Delaware River, within walking distance of all the historical attractions and lots of places to eat and drink. It is understated, attractive, and well-maintained inside and out. Our room had a queen, a gas fireplace, and a jacuzzi. The staff was friendly and helpful. We didn't try the restaurant.
With tax, it came to $---. A good value.

I travel on business to the area quite frequently and I usually stay down the street from this particular hotel. I saw this hotel and its new affiliation with Wyndham and thought to give it a try. I was pleasantly suprised. The room was clean, well decorated and I could use my laptop in the room. Breakast was fantastic. I was offered eggs, sausage, hasbrowns, french toast-the works and it was free! I joined the membership program before I left and will continue using this particular hotel as well as Wingates when I travel outside of Jacksonville.

I booked The Beekman hotel after much searching and agonizing over price versus value.
I booked thru Travelocity and got a fantastic deal. On my way to the hotel, I phoned The Beekman to ensure that my reservation had been completed by Travelocity. The hotel informed me that Travelocity had, in fact, NOT made my reservation! BUT, the hotel assured me that... although Travelocity was unable to complete even the most basic of functions, The Beekman would look after my family and make sure we were taken care of. Well, I finally got Travelocity to complete the reservation and The Beekman called me less than -- seconds later to let me know I was all set.
When we arrived, - hours early, the hotel front desk (Michael) told me our room was ready and we could check in immediately. (WOW).
The room was spacious and clean as a whistle (why do people use that phrase? Are whistles REALLY the standard of clean?)
The carpet and furnishings were outdated and worn... but certainly not unclean or unusable. For the price we paid, we would stay there again tomorrow. The doorman (John... you the man), was friendly and helpful. He gave us alot of great advice on where to eat and how to get around. The room had an incredible view. We NEVER saw any type of vermin as has been accused here by others. We felt completely safe and the bed was ABSOLUTELY comfortable!
Overall, a good experience in a comfortable room. We look forward to returning.

Booked room on Priceline.com for $---night. Stayed - nights.
The staff I encountered were nice, despite the reviews. Check-in process was moderate. Stood in line about ----
 minutes or so, but no issues.
We stayed on -th floor... elevators were fast and in good repair.
Room was comfy, beds are a bit small but slept well. Some minor detail repairs needed (see photos) but it didn't affect my overall stay. Didn't hear any noise from airport or through the walls. Shower gets hot, bathroom was clean. 
WiFi is free!!!! 
Shuttle to airport runs every -- minutes. It only takes - minutes to get to the airport, which was convenient. 
You can order tasty food at the bar (see photos) for less than $--. Drinks were good. Price $$-$$$
Hotel restaurant has a good breakfast buffet, but it's about $--. You're better off eating in the bar area.

We just returned from our second stay at the Elysian. The hotel and rooms are very elegant and stunningly beautiful. Even though I am rating the hotel average, there is no denying how beautiful the property is. 
We arrived and check in was quick and easy. The staff was very nice and welcoming. They asked what newspaper we would like to receive each morning of our stay. We asked for USA Today and were told that they do not have it so we decided on the Tribune. We stayed in a Deluxe Suite (same as our last stay) very spacious and on the --st floor. 
I was going to pour us a cocktail from the mini bar and picked up a half empty bottle of tonic that was in the minibar. When I went to call the front desk to let them know, there was a partially eaten bar of chocolate that had """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""happy birthday"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" written all over it sitting next to the phone. 
After a night out on the town, (a very cold night) I decided I wanted to warm up and take a bath. I started to fill up the tub and noticed that it was filthy. There were little black hairs all over and it was dirty. The hotel itself is very clean but my room was not. 
We were also celebrating a birthday and I had let the hotel know prior to our arrival that it was a special occasion. It went completely ignored by the hotel. Considering there was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""happy birthday"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" chocolate bar in our room from the previous guests, I know that they do acknowledge guests birthdays. We never got a newspaper on either morning of our stay. 
 If I am staying at a luxury hotel and paying luxury hotel prices, these oversights are not acceptable. Even though the hotel is beautiful I will not be returning. There are better hotels in Chicago.

Stayed ----- Dec ----. Contrary to the previous reviewer, this is a delightful central hotel that exudes ambience and history and is personal and friendly. It's like being invited into someone's gracious old home. It was always nice to return to a clean, neat room that was warm, welcoming and quiet. Room --- to be precise. Small like most NYC hotel rooms but a comfortable bed and good night's sleep. Flat screen HD TV with plenty of channels to watch when you get in really late after tramping the streets. Highly recommend it. Also, recommend checking out the shows at BB Kings Bar and Grill in --nd St. $-- each for a two and half hour tribute to the Beatles in a cabaret environment. Fabulous. That would cost you over $-- in Las Vegas. Carmines is a good place to eat if you like HUGE meals and good drinks. The Red Flame next door to the hotel is ideal for the quick and cheap breakfasts.

The O'Brien is a small boutique style hotel. My husband and I stayed here while in San Antonio for the annual Christmas Riverboat Parade. It is in downtown, but a bit secluded, still near all the main downtown attractions. Nothing fancy about the hotel, but it's a nice place with it's own unique charms (old style bathtub, windows that raise with no screens). Staff was really nice and helpful, free continental breakfast included pastries, waffles, fruit, muffins, coffee, juice... nothing spectacular, but a bit above average. Only downside was they have few places to park, and parking is $--. Other than that we already have another stay booked.

I was in Boston to attend a conference. Seaport was only a short walk to the Boston Conference Center. The room was small but nice and clean. The staff was helpful but not really friendly. They weren't rude but not very enthuastic. The bellhops were the only ones who were friendly. The restaurant is expensive and I didn't care for the menu selections. But there are some restaurants that are within walking distance. The hotel is not located in an area where there are attractions. But you can catch a bus that will drop you off at Fanuil Hall. I also caught a tour bus that picks up in front of the hotel. The T is also across the street. The plumbing is quite loud but it didn't bother me. The wireless internet is a nice amenity. I enjoyed my stay and would visit this hotel again.

I stayed at the Marriott Marquis while at a conference in May ----. The location was excellent and the rooms were great. I have stayed at severaI hotels in NY; this one was the best. I would definitely stay here again.

My stay at Carlyle this past week (November ----) was, without question, the best I’ve experienced over hundreds of stays in Washington DC over the past decade. The staff consistently made a special effort to assure our stay (my wife accompanied me on this trip) was the best possible experience. I do not recall all of the names, but do remember that ‘Chris’ scrambled to find a cab for our trip back to the airport, and stayed with us until our luggage was loaded and we were seated in the cab. 
My guess is that the beds are 'memory foam' or something similar - just as comfortable as our Tempur-Pedic at home. 
The special effort made by the entire staff are very much appreciated by those staying at the hotel, even if guests are not always motivated to thank them.

We loved our stay at the Chelsea Inn. It really feels like you are renting a room in a home in circa ----'s New York. Our expectations weren't high as we knew this wasn't a Hilton, but we were pleasantly surprised with this little gem. The check-in was smooth and easy. The nice lady named Melissa offered to make us dinner reservations if we were hungry and gave us a free copy of Time Out New York magazine to help us plan our time there. We were way up on the fourth floor and since there is not an elevator...carrying our --lbs. bag up the stairs was not an easy task. Once we got to our room,,,we loved how homey it felt. Nice big window, tall ceilings and a quilted bed. There was also a sink and a mini refrigerator which was very nice to have. Free Wi-Fi was also a plus. Sharing a bathroom with another room was no problem at all. We never saw the other people and it was always very clean. 
In the morning, you are given coupons to the downstairs nook of a bakery called Nana's Treats. You get coffee, a pastry and a piece of fruit every day of your stay. (I recommend the cinnamon rolls) The little breakfast helped us save a few bucks each day.
The location was perfect. Only two blocks from Union Square. SO many restaurants on the hotel's street alone and only half a block from awesome shopping: H&M, Kate Spade, Zara etc.
There are two clubs near the Inn but from our room, we couldn't hear any noise. I also felt safer knowing there were always people hanging out or waiting in line to get into the clubs when we got back to the hotel late late in the evening.
Check-out was just as smooth and a very kind and patient woman named Rada answered our last minute questions.
All in all, I loved it here. But don't go in looking for a chain high-end hotel experience. It is for those adventurous travelers that don't like to feel simply like a tourist, but like you are living as a local for a short stay. We will certainly stay here again in the future.

The hotel staff was very helpful for directions around the area. In fact all of the staff seemed very friendly and helpful. The main downfall is the paper thin walls that allow you to hear everything from the adjoining rooms, the television, babies crying and ( use your imagination) everything else. The location is convienently located.

We booked a room for a busy July weekend but when we arrived there was no record of our reservation - even though I had a printed confirmation email. The entire city was sold out and the management did nothing to help us find a room. He basically hid in the back while we were left to call around. We were able to leave our bags and go to the Red Sox game we had ticketsfor but upon return the bell hop was snide at our predicament. We ended up paying $--- for the Marriott only because we are Platinum members and they had to have a room for us. We were not offered any kind of compensation and we were not the only ones in this predicament. At least - other guests showed up with reservations and did not have a room. Worst hotel experience we have ever had.

My -th stay at the London NYC because its unique style, excellent service, and prime location cannot be matched in the city. When I booked a room at this motel, I honestly wasn't expecting much. All I knew was that I was on a budget and it was affordable. However, my stay was much better than expected. If I could, I would actuall give the hotel - --- stars, but since I cannot, I went higher rather than lower because of the amazingly helpful staff that was great for a first-time visitor to the city.
Pros: -. Again, the staff was amazingly helpful. I was able to get around the city with ease because of their help, which I did not even need to ask for. It was offered freely.
-. The hotel is located within walking distance (approximately a quarter mile) of the orange line of the elevated train, which can take you from the Midway airport all the way to all the downtown attractions for very little money, and you can transfer to other trains to get to where the orange line does not go. Because of that, I ended up never needing my rental car.
-. Continental breakfast daily. I cannot give a full review of this because when I went to eat, it was almost time for it to end, but despite that, the food that was left still tasted fresh and there was a nice variety.
-. Free Internet. Of course, most hotels and motels have this nowadays, but it is still a perk and worth mentioning if you are staying here anyway.
Cons: -. The room was a bit on the small side, so depending on how much time you plan to spend in your room, you might find it is too small for your needs, though it does have all the basics in the room.
-. The exterior wall is apparently a bit thin and while the neighborhood isn't extremely noisy, when a loud noise does happen outside, it can be heard pretty clearly.
-. The bathtub, like the room itself, is a bit small and the water pressure is low.
And lastly, this could be a pro or a con depending on your preference, the beds have a pretty firm mattress, rather than the extremely soft ones you find in the big chain hotels.
Overall, though, the hotel well exceeded my expectations and I would have no complaints about staying there again.

He was incredibly polite and I got the feeling they wouldn't have left us stranded.

The beds and pillows were not great and the room was a bit cold with the heating off, but when we turned it on the room warmed right up.
The bathroom was small but clean and well maintained, however the shower was absolutely impossible to turn on to a reasonable temperature. It went from too cold to burning hot with the slightest hair of a turn.
My only other complaint was the hotel back faces a gentlemen's club and it was a bit noisy at night. Well to be honest I slept through the noise, but my friends complained.
The restaurant was fantastic. The servers were excellent, very friendly and helpful, and the food was good. The restaurant itself is really well maintained and nicely decorated.
Overall, the service, cleanliness, excellent location and cheap price brought all four of us to agree that it's a great hotel for downtown Seattle. If you are looking for something within walking distance of all of Seattle's attractions that won't break the bank, this is the place.

Introduction:
The Tuscan Inn is a Best Western property in the Fisherman’s Wharf area of San Francisco California. They also are related to the Kimpton hotel chain. The hotel has - levels with a variety of King, Double, King Suite and Double Suite rooms available. 
Experience:
We had arrived on a late flight and only made it to the hotel at about -- at night. The single front desk clerk told us they had given away our original room with - double beds. Instead they said they would give us a suite with - king sized bed and fold out couch. This was not what we wanted but there were no rooms with - regular beds and it was late at night. They agreed to change us to the next available room with - double beds. Upon returning to the desk in the morning we were given key cards for room --- with - double beds. This was much better as my son said a night on the fold away couch bed was awful. I can understand this as I lay down and could feel the springs of the bed. Although I understand it is first come first serve I think it was wrong to give away a guest’s room especially if they have notified you of their late check-in. 
Room:
I will not go into details about the first room we had (King Suite) as I did not pay much attention other than where the washroom, bed and TV were as it was late at night when we checked in and all we wanted to do was relax and go to sleep. 
Our actual room featured - double sized beds with TV, honor bar (we liked the extra room left to store our own store bought products), a work desk, chair, coffee maker and . The room itself, although “smaller” was not cramped but not nearly average hotel room sized. The washroom was not overly large but big enough to comfortable move around in the morning. There was also a small closet in the room. Our room had a court-yard view which means it faced in the inside of hotel. This was good because it was quiet. Do not worry about the view from you room as the best views are in Fisherman’s Wharf in one of the restaurants. I’ll write more on that later. The room is not (or at least should not) be very important to the tourist traveler in San Francisco’s Fisherman’s Wharf. The area is full of exciting things to do and places to eat. If I exclude time spent sleeping I think I only spent --- hours total time in the room during the week I was in the area. The only weak point of the room was that there was very little storage space for clothing and person articles. 
Services-Amenities:
In accordance with the Tuscan Inn’s Italian style-theme a coffee-tea-biscotti service was open from -am till -am in the mornings. In the evenings from -pm till -pm a wine, beer and sparkling water service was available. Guests have the opportunity to sample local Californian wines as well as Italian beer and water. The hotel does not feature any sort of pool or exercise facility which would have been convenient to have but not necessary but definitely good to have. The hotel offers free wifi (wireless high speed internet) to all guests who have a laptop. The signal was accessible throughout the hotel. This is a definite plus for any traveler with a laptop. I used it to keep in touch with people back home, find stores in SF as well as look up reviews and recommendations on area restaurants. Parking at the hotel was a hefty $-- per day with unlimited in and out privileges. We never called down in advance and once we informed the valet from the lobby our car was retrieved within - minutes. Very good!
Final Word:
The Tuscan Inn by Best Western is an excellent choice for tourists who want easy (and I mean really easy) access to the Fisherman’s Wharf area as well as business travelers doing to the financial district (there are - daily shuttles). The hotel is located near many restaurants in the Wharf area as well as an onsite restaurant called Café Pascatore serving tasty Italian food. For breakfast I recommend walking the --- blocks to the IHOP near the Radisson on the Wharf.

The service at Stay can not be faulted! The staff were always friendly and remembered you from previous times. Having stayed at many InterContinental hotels, I've developed certain expectations. This Boston property fell a bit short in many respects. Let me start with the positive before touching on the shortfalls:

Hungry and exhausted we arrived at the Sheraton Gateway at -:-- p.m. Our room was ready and the hotel clerk made a reservation at Paparazzi, the hotel Italian restaurant. We never expected to find the absolutely delicious Italian food at an airport hotel. In fact we enjoyed some of the most delicious Italian food we had eaten in years. My first course was a caprese salad but not the usual fresh mozzarella. This mozzarella tasted sweet and as if it had been made hours before. The tomatoes were not commercial, hard tasteless rocks but succulent slices of three different colors topped off by a balsamic reduction. My entree was the lasagna which was made with slowly-braised short ribs and was by far the best lasagna I had ever eaten anywhere. Our waitress was not the usual sullen, overworked airport restaurant staff but a charming, delightful warm young woman whose personality made the meal that much more enjoyable. Because this was our first time at Paparazzi's we were given a free homemade scrumptious dessert. 
Then the room---absolutely quiet. I could not believe that as I watched a plane come into the airport almost in reaching distance I could not here anything. This was a miracle in an airport hotel! The bed was comfortable, the bathroom clean and spacious, and the entire experience topnotch. When returning back through LAX I wished that we would be bumped from our flight just so I could stay at this hotel again. Then I could savor another unexpected gastronomic tonic for one's weary traveled soul.

I have stayed at many hotels in the past year and The Westin Charlotte was my worst experience out of all. We stayed at the Westin on our way back from Fiji. It was only one night. Noisy and the room was shabby. Not even a shower cap.

Excellent loaction, in the heart of everything that is New York. Great for walking around the area and to central park. Metro to take you anywhere. Empire State Building near by. My mother found this hotel online a couple of years ago so we decided to try it out. The rooms are very small as several other people have said in their reviews, but they really are very charming. Having stayed at some other hotels in Seatlle we were awed by the Marriott Waterfront. room had BUGS.. showed deskman and then manager locked us out of room and would not go in with us. he said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""his man"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" would LIE and deny that he saw anything. Crappy management. Would not compensate. Pet free, but do not tell you either on reader board or at check it. SMALL signs. Splash that it is smoke free, but allow cigar smoking in pool area. Spa is not a spa and was COLDEr than the pool.

Location location location, Just back from a wonderful stay at Eastgate Tower Hotel, all you need to know is, large rooms, clean, very good service all round, value for money, good all round, our favourites hotel in New York City, we will be back.

From what I had heard and the price I paid, I expected much more of the hotel. It is convenient to the National Mall and nice to have the Metro downstairs. Service at the restaurant bar was horrible. Thought I'd save time by ordering 'to-go' - took me -- minutes to get my order. Blamed it on a new machine. Rooms are ok but old especially the bathrooms. Could use a renovation. Wasn't impressed with staff especially the taxi attendant who mouthed something waving his arms as I drove away in a taxi. Guess, he thought that I should tip him more than $- for waving a taxi that was parked --' away. Overall, I would not like to experience the L'Enfant again.

When you drive up and have to be buzzed through the gates to enter the property, it's NOT a good feeling. Sadly, this first impression is on exactly on target. While the hotel has the normally nice Hyatt Place furnishings, big screen TV and granite countertop, it's still a very far cry from other airport hotels that are in fact much closer to the airport. 
The elevator and hallways reeked of pizza delivery, and their lack of air conditioning in common spaces is a crime for Houston and its hot, humid summers. 
On the positive side, I didn't see the roaches that other TripAdvisor reviewers warn about. Perhaps they're down the hall, munching on those pizza boxes that need to be picked up?

Rather like another reviewer whose opinions I read a moment ago, I consider this hotel to be adequate. 
Our check-in experience was a drawn-out-affair, with them being unable to locate our reservation for some minutes. It may seem like nothing, but after a long journey, this simple clerical error was very ill-timed. 
On our first night, we decided to make use of the rooftop bar. The drinks were very expensive, but we drank whilst enjoying the view. That is, of course, until a drunken member of the public, who introduced himself to us by drunkenly and repeatedly """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""giving us the finger"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", possibly because we are a gay couple, intruded on our evening. He was being watched by the security staff but clearly they thought his behaviour to be acceptable, or at least, not bad enough to remove him from the premises. We then decided to leave the rooftop bar, and judging that to be the average standard of customer, did not return for the rest of our stay. It is a shame that the security staff's reaction to his behaviour prevented us from enjoying the rooftop bar, further. In a further encounter with security staff from the rooftop bar, a ---something-chap with blond hair and an abrupt attitude very curtly told my partner and myself to vacate a lift he held, empty at ground level solely for use for the rooftop bar, with several groups of people waiting in the foyer area for the other lifts. His manner was abrupt, and his logic still escapes me.
The lack of complimentary WiFi was annoying, and since we were staying for ten nights, we saw the daily charge of $--.-- as rather excessive, particularly when other Hilton hotels in the city, and every Starbucks, provide this, gratis. We made limited use of the two computers available in the foyer, though this area has little or no privacy when performing tasks such as internet banking - indeed, on one occasion, I was forced to ask a hotel member of staff to leave so that I might continue.
On the plus side, the room was well appointed and clean. The air conditioning a little loud, but at least worked reliably during the hot spell which encompassed all of our stay. The hotel is a good base from which to join the subway, explore the city, and get to know NYC. But, and I say this as a frequent traveller - Hilton hotels, at one point, were about luxury and attention to detail. It's a shame that my abiding memory of this hotel, during this trip, is that it was normal, that is to say, nothing special, and that we came to treat it as the average room in which we slept, before leaving each morning to enjoy more of that amazing city. On balance of price and facilities, combined with the incidents detailed above, I'm afraid I cannot recommend this hotel.

I have traveled considerably over the years and one thing I know is the least you expect, the better the place (most of the time). This Comfort Inn has exceptional customer service and an exceptional free breakfast, considering it is not made to order. The room we stayed in had two double beds, a wonderful walk in closet and a good sized bathroom. We were not there much but we were definitely overall, impressed. The beds and pillows were comfy and the maid service was A--. This use to be a - star hotel called the Gregorian. Do not miss the fine details of this place. It is VERY obvious that it was a - star at one time. Lots of elegance, especially in the breakfast eating room. My husband and I loved this place. Friendly staff, great customer service, clean room and comfy bed. What else could one want. Oh, I forgot to mention, location, location, location!! A++++ all the way.

This Hampton is clean and spacious with courteous staff as most Hamptons are, but this hotel is unique because it sits right next to the train tracks with trains constantly coming by and BLARING their horns. This is the only hotel I have ever stayed in that provides ear plugs in each room for their guests. That should tell you something right there!
The on site parking garage has spaces that are SO narrow, you have to fold in your mirrors to fit your car in the space. If you are not back to the hotel by around -pm, you will not find parking and the aisles are so narrow that you cannot turn around to come back down to the exit. The only way down, if you are not lucky enough to find a spot, is to back down the ramps, as there is no room to maneuver turning around. People make up their own spaces against the walls, making it even harder to navigate the garage. One night, - cars literally parked in front of the elevators!
I always try to stay at a Hampton, as they are reliable, but I definitely do not recommend this particular one.

When you walk up to the front desk you are received with a polite smile and a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Welcome to the Hotel California"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". On the speakers in the reception area you hear Janis Joplin, Bob Dylan, The Byrds, Jimi Hendrix... The building is historic and well preserved, the place has loads of character, this isnt just a generic hotel, even though it is a Best Western. Rooms are on the small side (it is an old building in the downtown area) but are well equipped. Rates were not bad for a centric San Fran hotel (I paid $--- a night). I would definitely return.
This is probably the new place to be seen in LA. My favorite W is still the Hong Kong one.

We did not stay at the hotel - this is a brunch review. My sister made reservations for us for Easter Sunday brunch at the Ritz Carlton in Georgetown. I'll admit - I was taken aback by the price. I would have been fine having a picnic on the mall. But we were with our entire family - all -- of us and we have never spent Easter in DC. So we went...and it was wonderful.
The hostess greeted the kids with empty easter baskets for a egg hunt that took place about half way through our meal. Then she walked us to our table in a beautiful big room with brick walls - very beautiful. The dessert table was spectacular with a chocolate bunny and easter baskets with candy etc... The raw bar was a hit with everyone. Everything tasted amazing. We also enjoyed the bottomless mimosas. 
the easter egg hunt was in the garden with the easter bunny. It was very well done and worth every penny (which was a lot of pennies - lol!) I would definitely recommend brunch - and next time we want to stay here. it's a beautiful hotel and a great location.

Reception staff in this rather faded once glorious hotel need a wake up call. They ignore you and you get the feeling that you are well beneath them in the grand scheme of things. I was deliberately ignored and stood at the desk while two reception staff chatted. In the end I walked away disgusted. 
My friends had their room double booked and received a nocturnal visitor trying to get in to his room. Apologies were profuse and compensation given, - biscuits and two bottles of water!!!!
This hotel is past its best.

This hotel was perfect. We were in a great area. Minutes to Union Square and you're in the middle of lots of great eateries. The hotel was very clean and the staff were very courteous. And you have to try the restaurant downstairs. It's called Fish & Farm and the food was delicious. Definitely staying here again!

We were transferred to the Edison after a terrible problem with a WooGo reservation. We really didn't want to stay right in Times Square, but had no choice. The room was on the -th floor and we were awakened by construction noises as they are renovating the hallway. The room itself was very nice and clean, but there are no ammenities -- no small refrigerator, no microwave, no ice, no coffee -- the room is just for sleeping. This was a consideration as the place we had reserved had all those things and we were trying to save a little money by not eating out every meal -- this is not an option at the Edison.

My husband and I just completed a stay at the Taj Hotel to celebrate our --th wedding anniversary. We select a Jr. Suite with a separate living room and fireplace. I stay at a many hotels for business travel and also host conferences, especially in the Boston area. I have never had a such a disappointing experience. The room was very expensive -- and not worth it!
The carpets are old and stained. The room was freezing cold and the hotel staff said that the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""heat wasn't turned on yet for the season."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" They brought in a space heater to address the issue (at one point we had to leave the door open to let warm air in until the space heater arrived). The fireplace was also not working -- while the room description includes a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""fireplace butler,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" well the fireplaces aren't available in September. The bathroom smelled of smoke even though we had a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no smoking room.""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""
Room service, which I don't expect to be a fabulous meal, was also substandard. The fish I ordered was incredibly dried out.
To top it all off, our room was directly behind the elevator. We could hear it going up and down all evening. My husband did tell the concierge that this was our --th wedding anniversary - and this was the room we were given.
They have a reasonable work out room, but some equipment was not in service. On the plus side, they offer good headphones for the guests and elliptical equipment included a TV. The beds in the rooms are also comfortable.
The staff, while relatively pleasant, were not overly helpful and didn't always understand simple requests. I'm sure it's difficult to work in a hotel that is supposed to be """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""superior"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but is sorely lacking.
My advice - stay at the Westin, Marriott, Copley Plaza, if you want to be near the park or BackBay. Do not stay at the Taj.

This Hotel is a great choice. It is very comfortable, very european and is just plain fun. The hotel is only --- blocks from Union Square and the Embarcadero BART Station. They have a wine and beer hour ---PM. The Ponzu Restaraunt attached is great too. Next door is first class wine shop. The only down fall is that is right next to the Tenderloin District, but don't let that stop you. This place is a great value and awesome place to stay in the City. Also check out the lepoard print fun wear in the rooms.

The Marten House Hotel is awesome!! We stay there every year For the Brickyard weekend. Its clean, nice, and everyone is so friendly!! I recommend this hotel! Nice indoor pool, vending near by the pool. Friendly front desk staff, always with a smile. Maid service very nice. If you are going with friends or family they have suites for your convenience. Some Suites also have kitchens which is great!!

My stay at the Marriott was wonderful. They provided me with the best service possible and if the couldn't provide it for me they could find someone who could. The food was wonderful. Great Southern Style food at the Magnolia Grill. The workout room had top notch equipment and was only available for those whom had room key. That was a nice safety standard I felt. I would stay there again. Very Nice! Great Everything!!

I checked in very late last night and was checked in by two ladies at the desk. They seemed like a cheery young staff who enjoy interacting with their guests. I asked them where I could get a quick bite to eat around in the area and recommended a great sit down restaurant a few blocks down. When I returned, I was greeted by a 'welcome back'.
I agree that the rooms are very small but if your planning to stay for one evening like myself then it's acceptable. The hotel should consider switching from ethernet to wireless in the rooms for business-friendly purposes. I also received an appropriate rate through AX travel. As a frequent traveler from NY to Boston, I will consider staying here again.

We had a Penn ---- King suite on the --th floor. The room was old, yes, but it was clean. The bed was comfortable as well. We came in later in the evening so we didnt really have a huge wait to check in. We didnt come to New York to sit in our hotel room so the dated atmosphere of the hotel didnt bother us. I did have a slightly rude operator when I called down to the desk with a question but it was just the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""typical"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" New Yorker attitude! The little cafe downstairs has the best chai tea latte. The weird part is that they are cash only. Overall, I would stay in this hotel again if I were in the King Suite. Its about the same size as a small-ish regular sized hotel room so its not as cramped as the other rooms sound.

We pulled up in a cab at the hotel and was gestured by a doorman to use the front entrance - with swift gestures and shouting """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no!no!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Which was a wonderful greeting. 
We entered the lobby which felt slightly reminiscent of a hunting lodge and waited to check in. 
Check In staff very helpful and accomodating, we were back to being a bit more impressed. 
Room however small, pokey,and beds unusually high. Me being only around -ft found myself having to clamber on. For a twin room there is little room for moving around - packing-repacking- and with such high beds for a heavy suitcase I found it difficult to maneouvre. 
The shower dial in the bath was back to front - after -- mins of turning to hot and not getting hot water i turned to cold and miraculously hot water appeared - a silly and frustrating inconvienience. 
Window looked out onto someone's office in a close proximity which made me feel a little uncomfortable having only discovered this AFTER a bath and wondering round in a towel simultaneously watching someone make a call from their desk. 
Bath uncomfortable and small.
To top it off My friend was sure he'd lost his bank card in the hotel room , and had left it on the nightstand. We called and were told it was not there. Fair enough, we may be wrong. We asked if someone could just check behind the night stand for us just to be on the safe side and eliminate this as an option. They promised to do so and we arranged for a call back the following day which we did not receive - I might add we were still in the U.S.A so it was not a case of not being able to make long distance calls. 
 Despite giving our new hotel and room number and cell phone number nobody bothered. Although I accept fully that the lost bank card was not their fault- problem when a call back is agreed at a time by themselves, you'd expect them to honour it. 
We weren't bowled over by the hotel for the points above. I wouldn't stay again, and won't be recommending to my clients.

This is the second time we have stayed at the DC Palomar. If you want to stay here (and you should) be smart - join the Kimpton """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""In Touch"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" program (automatic $-- coupon to 'raid the minibar') and carefully, carefully look at specials and packages listed. Sometimes very similar packages can have different costs, and (as in our case) a $-- upgrade moved us from a King to a Superior Suite. This is not available all the time - but be smart and study the website. Also, make sure you are familiar with the list of amenities and take advantage of those you like.
Now, the hotel - wonderful clean room with great bed. Our view wasn't the best, but that wasn't important to us. Location of hotel is great. Easy walk to great restaurants on Conn Ave, and little bit longer to Georgetown - where everything is.
The best part about the hotel is the employees. As my husband said, 'you really get the feeling that these folks will do everything they can to make sure you're happy.' So to John (Bob Seger) and Kelly (Bruce!) Abe and Patrick, I send my hearfelt thanks. You helped me have one of the best birthday weekends ever. We will always try to stay at this fantastic property

Stayed with my husband a week in the Herald square hotel in the beginning of september. At first we were offered a very small room, but when the staff realised we were staying a week they came with a bigger one. All very clean and quiet.
positive: near a few metrostations, in a nice and central neighbourhood, quiet street, nice staff.
negative: free coffee- tea is nice, but why on certain times? We were allways to early or too late.
To take a shower was really a challenge: it is difficult to get the temperature you like, allways too hot . So like an other reviewer suggested before: I mostly took a bath.
But the price in relation to the quality is good, so I would certainly stay here again.

I've been a Hilton Diamond Member for years now and I normally stay in Hilton Garden Inns. However, things were booked so I stayed at this Hampton for the first time. I must say that the rooms and amenities were standard Hampton Inn fare, but the staff went above and beyond. I left my air card for my computer and they not only called me and informed me, but they also mailed it out to me. I have to say that out of the dozens of Hamptons I've ever stayed at, I've never encountered a staff as professional and helpful. Especially Michelle.

Just got back from a nice weekend in San Antonio for my husbands birthday. The girl at reception was friendly and asked us what floor we wanted our rooms on and pointed out where things were in the hotel. Told us how much breakfast cost and was very helpful. We didn't care where our room was so she gave us a nice room on the second floor with a balcony facing the building that exercise room is in and you could see the gazebo as well. 
The room was nice, and well it seems most hotels you can hear some noise from your neighbors, but ours apparently were pretty quiet compared to other reviewers. Anytime we needed anything it was brought up to us quickly. Our A-C was leaking and they came and fixed it while we were out which was about - hours that day so I thought that was pretty good.
Nice pool area that was relaxing. I had a good time watching the birds while sunning. The hotel I don't think is a true -star but it was a place I would stay again. We paid $--- on Priceline for it and would gladly pay that again to stay there. We didn't have a car, but parking at any - star is expensive. Even at the - stars in Kansas City if I remember correctly we had to pay $-- per day to park our car non valet.
In short, I would definately stay here again. But if you are wanting the best - star experience try a place like the Emily Morgan.

This is a new modern hotel near the Philadelphia International Airport on the same property as the Sheraton Suites and another hotel. There was a very convenient shuttle to the airport which also allows you to get on the SEPTA train system so you can get downtown quite easily.
The lobby is open plan with a island check-in desk and a bar and a separate area with a pool table. There were also two free computers for surfing the internet. There is also free Wi-fi in the lobby and in every room there is an internet connection. This area had quite loud music which we found a bit obtrusive.
There is no restaurant but you can buy food and drinks from a display like a cafeteria and pay at the check-in. We had to go to the Sheraton Suites at the receptionist's recommendation for an evening meal.
The room is not big, though it has high ceilings and two large windows. There was a large flat screen TV but nowhere to sit and watch it except the king size bed. There was only one chair in the room and a rather noisy in-room airconditioner-heater which seemed out of place in a room that tried to be modern and up to date.
There is no bath tub, though it has a large glass shower cubicle which was fine. There was a room safe and coffee maker, though with only one pack of each type of beverage (coffee, regular and decaf, and a couple of types of tea). 
Curiously there was very little room to put clothes away outside a suicase, no drawers and only a small hanging area. If you are staying more than a couple of days this is a bit inconvenient.

After attempts to get management's attention via email and snail mail to no success, here we go...is it a coincidence that our daughter experiences bites on her back the first night, then my wife, and finally me? Too bad, all I asked was that management check the room and inform me of their actions. No response, nada.
Very nice & warm people

I found this hotel via Trip Advisor and LOVED it!!! Right on the water and away from downtown. Great restaurants, beach and things to do within walking distiance. Staff was SUPER friendly. Continental breakfast and wifi were included with my buy - get - night free!!!! I will be back!!!

First the plus points, the Essex Inn has a great pool, and for the size of the hotel the gym (with Life Fitness equipment) is very good too. The WiFi works throughout the hotel so one can relax in say one of the sunloungers by the pool and still be connected.
The hotel is in a great location; everything seems to be walking distance.
Service was fine, but not great; for example, when another bed was requested, accompanying extra towels were not provided, and when these were requested they took ages to arrive.
I was less impressed with the rooms. The airconditioning is old and outdated and doesn't control the temperature very well. This is made worse by the fact that if you go at a particular time of year, you can only select heating (or cooling). In our case, as it was October, even though it was really pretty warm, we couldn't cool the room and had to open the window which made the room noisy.
For what the hotel is charging, the bathrooms really need updating. The bath surround in my room was a horrible linoleum-vinyl, and the temperature of the water could not be thermostatically controlled.
Overall, if you won't be using the pool or gym a lot, I would look elsewhere as other hotels in the area such as the Best Western provide larger and better equipped rooms. If you do want a nice pool and gym, this makes up for the shortcomings of the rooms.

We were staying at the Marriott Waterfront for a conference. Their staff was more than helpful and attentive the entire time, from the bellhop, to the concierge and even the servers at the banquets. We had a problem in our room with the smell of propane, the director of security was immediately up to address the issue and stayed to tell us some history about Baltimore and the view from the room. He took care of the issue (it was a minor problem), and went along our way. The views are amazing on the bayside. We were lucky enough to get a corner room and had a fantastic view of Little Italy and the harbor. 
Thank you Baltimore Marriott Waterfront for making our first visit to Baltimore an enjoyable one! Looking forward to returning.

We stayed here for a weekend and at first were extremely impressed with the place. After checking in we found out the resort had NO wifi. We found that rather strange. Our rooms were ok, but we expected more. We had connecting rooms and one night our teenager and friend had a disturbance and they phoned security at -am. We were asleep in our room and had no clue. At -am our teenager woke us up and we were surprised security would go into a room with two minors and never bother to wake up the parents next door to inform them of the disturbance. I thought that was very unprofessional of the staff. We also received a letter in our room telling us of a special rate we were being offered...which included free cans of soda. When we phoned about our cans of soda they told us they were on their way to our room. -- hours later we ohoned to remind them and they had no clue what we were talking about. It seemed there was no communication between any if the staff. The valet service was strange as well. The valet employees would just stand around and wait for you to approach them if you needed help. They seemed standoffish. We were celebrating a birthday and phoned to have forks and a knife brought over and after - calls to remind them and an hour later we finally received them. The breakfast was overpriced and not that great as well. This place is nice looking and has a great location, but definitely not worth the money.

We found this quant little place by chance while spending a day in town on our honeymoon, after a great cruise, two years ago. Since then have been back for our two anniversaries as well as our birthday (twice)(we have the same birthdate- go figure). Everyone who works there is super friendly and willing to assist you in anything short of taking the adventure for you (although I am sure they wish they could). There isn't much room for parties, but then who needs it when you have San Diego as the backdrop. The continental breakfast is great only to be outdone by the terrific view of the bay and morining sunrises.

We stayed at this hotel on Sunday, June --, ----. We actually got their """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""executive suite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which consists of - large rooms - one with a king sized bed, tv and chair, and the second being a very large living area with a dining table, desk area, tv, couch, chair and coffee table. there was also a mini fridge, sink and microwave tucked into a corner. The two rooms are separated by a big archway. This was a great hotel for us. We have - kids, ages - and -, and needed separation for the two kids to sleep.
* this hotel was SUPER clean - cleaner than the other hotels we stayed at during our trip. The bathroom was immaculate, no signs of grossness anywhere.
* they had a pretty nice continental breakfast + eggs and biscuits and gravy in the morning.
* we needed milk for our son that night and they actually gave us milk from the kitchen so we didn't have to run out to find some (there's not a lot around this hotel presently, as the freeway is under construction.
* less than - minutes to airport - great.
* the bed and linens were AWESOME = it rivaled Westin's Heavenly bed. They had really nice linens with some more plush pillows, a nice white heavy cotton duvet - very classy and comfortable.
* a nice touch - there was a little bar on the hotel's main floor, and a guest pantry where youc ould buy juice, ice cream, soup, and other basic food-sundry items.
I was really impressed with this hotel and would definitely stay there again with my family!

Stayed here the week of Thanksgiving. Great location as it is within walking distance of two Metro stops and plenty of restaurants. The property was clean and the parking was conveniently located in the basement. If you have kids, it is perfect as the hotel pool is probably the warmest I've come across while traveling. The breakfast is similar to that of the other Embassy Suites I've stayed at with one exception: the bacon is the worst that I have had - anywhere! Paper thin with no taste. For that, I give it - stars instead of -.

I travel to Columbus a few times a month, and always stay at this hotel. The staff is great, they always go out of their way to make you feel welcome and at home. The location is great, it's close too everything in Columbus, and the location makes it easy to get around the city in no time. Easton Mall up the road has great restaurants, bars and shopping. The rooms in this hotels are clean and well maintained. They have a great restaurant and bar, and every meeting we've ever done here has been exceptional. I would highly recommend this place. If you are looking for a safe, clean hotel to stay at when you are in Columbus-this is the perfect place.

Stayed here for - nights during our recent trip through New England and just loved it! This Residence Inn is conveniently located (North End and Downtown at walking distance), the rooms are very spacious, well-equipped (including fridge with freezer, microwave oven, dishwasher etc) and comfortable and we had a fantastic view over the waterfront which was wonderful.
The staff was very friendly and helpful, too, and the atmosphere in the hotel good and relaxed.
Price-wise, this hotel compares positively with others in expensive Boston, so quality-price relationship was very good. 
Breakfast was good and varied. The only thing which we did not like is the use of plastic plates and cutlery - not very classy and not environmentally friendly. 
The hotel has valet parking which is very convenient.
We will definitely consider staying again in this """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""home away from home"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" when in Boston the next time.

The valet parking is a great luxury and value. I got a deal of parking for ten days for a penny. When you think about staying at an airport, you probably imagine it will be loud. This hotel is soo quiet, it's wonderful. The restaurant is nice and reasonable priced. The entire stay is very relaxing.
The proximity to the terminal is so convenient. There just is no other choice if you want to start your trip out on a positive note.

Despite a few service blemishes, the hotel is historic, glamorous, the location is perfect and probably the best spot in the city for tourists wanting to visit the monuments and museums along The Mall each day. The public areas are over-the-top, decadently beautiful with custom-loomed carpets, marble pillars, gold moldings, red velvet, etc.
Especially given the discounted rate currently available, (about $----night prepaid on Expedia with buffet breakfast for - given as a $-- daily credit) we would absolutely choose this hotel again. 
Service was blissfully unpretentious. Front desk is efficient and courteous. They did make an error on checkout, did not see my $-,--- prepay. This was (with some difficulty figuring out on their part) corrected when I quesioned it. Bellhops expect tips when luggage brought into the lobby and then again when they bring it to the room. Unlike other --star hotels I have been in, bellhops blatantly push for tips. Housekeeping always greeted us and were eager to please.
Service is excellent but not impeccable. We did not have a nightly turn-down service, nor was a paper delivered to our room, it was kept in a stack near the elevator. I believe these may be available in a higher room stay level. Restaurant service friendly but again not top drawer (in the breakfast buffet, they take your dirty utensils off your plate and put it back on the table when you go for more food rather than give you a new one for instance). Phone service is excellent, they answer you promptly by name (pronounced correctly!).
We had a deluxe room #--- overlooking the courtyard. Room was very large, quiet, fairly clean, and the bathrooms wonderfully clean. Mattresses were good, but not of Westin-Four Seasons quality. Plenty of towels (including wash cloths!) were always provided. However, they never vacuumed under the beds or bureaus...we know this because on our last day, we checked under the beds to make sure we didn't miss anything; there were plenty of large dust balls and a pair of sandals from some previous guests! There were a few minor things not in working order...the tv speaker in the bathrooms was pulled out of the wall, and the clock-radio iPhone plug did not work. The digital tv is amazingly slow turning it on and froze once, but turning it off and back on fixed it.
We made almost no use of the concierge, as the recommended DC restaurants are consistent across Fodors, Frommers, Lonely Planet, etc so check these sites online. The Old Ebbitt Grill is one block in back of the hotel, across from the White House, was a great inexpensive place for a meal with decent quality food.
Note that the famous restaurant """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The Willard Room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is now closed, the room is available for business and party rentals only. Thank you so much Catmaran Resort Hotel for making our first trip to San Diego such a wonderful experience for everyone. We will be back and promise to highly recommend your property to others.

Straight in from SFO via the BART, I was pleasantly surprised as I stepped into the lobby of Hotel Whitcomb. The staff greeted me warmly and I had no problems registering quickly. Overall, I found that Hotel Whitcomb provides classic stylings and comfort, professional service from all the staff, and intangibles like the restaurants on the first floor and views of City Hall.

the rooms were small. we were not upgraded to a suite, so we had a standard room that wasn't much bigger than your average fairfield inn.

layout is completely stupid. you have to go underground to get to your room, just to pop up to the first floor. transporting bags back and forth to the room and the long walk for a small hotel made me wonder what the heck people were thinking when they designed the place.
our fancy bose stereo system in the room didn't work. 
the tv was a -- inch CRT that has probably been passed down from a marriott that has recently upgraded everything to flat screen HDTVs. the sound and picture were what you'd expect in a motel. 
the television service included about -- channels that worked, another -- that were in foreign languages. i have no problem with giving international travelers some access to their home networks. but please... the vast majority of the people there are americans and you can't even get channels like foodtv or comedy central.
the bathrooms were nicely appointed at first glance, but the reality is that the tub and shower are purely functional for one person. so much for romance.
the food service is exceptionally over-priced. i understand that hotels charge a premium for food service. however, there is a point where even the super rich have to shake their heads. the continental breakfast room service option was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""a basket of pastries, your choice of juice, and a carafe of coffee"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for (get this) $-- plus a $-.-- delivery charge. you'd get a better breakfast from the local market, a few steps away from the hotel, for about $-.
