We went on a crowded weekend; however, the hotel delivered that Drury quality that we expect. This is a newer hotel and so it looked nice with updated amenities. Great front desk staff, great dining room staff and our doggies were not disappointed either. There is even room off to the side of the hotel to walk them. :)

We went to Chicago for our sons --th birthday. We chose the Hard Rock Hotel Chicago. From the minute we arrived they were wonderful. Our room was wonderful and the staff was awesome. The staff was so helpful with places to eat, places to go, my husband needed a phone charger and they had one to us in seconds. They also made our son feel very special for his special weekend. They made his and our experience GREAT! We will be going back and we will definitely stay at the Hard Rock Chicago.

I had never stayed at a Club Quarters so I wasn't sure what to expect. I got a terrific rate (~$--- including all taxes) on Hotwire. Turns out that I had a wonderful experience and I would definitely stay at a Club Quarters again. This one is in a terrific location just off of Times Square - very close to everything but not in the immediate gridlock of people, traffic, and noise so it was a nice reprieve from the chaos outside. The lobby is basic but professional, and the rooms are clean and well-kept. The only negative commentary that I have is that there are only two (very tiny) elevators so it may take quite a bit of time to go up and down to your room. Also, I had left my bags earlier in the day since I arrived before check-in; someone was supposed to bring them up in a few minutes - and I had to call a half hour later to tell them that I needed the bags b-c I was going out for the evening. All and all, though, I would encourage people to stay here - it's definitely significantly cheaper (even at the full price rate) than many other hotels in the area and it is just as good (if not better) than most of them.

Location is Good, not Great. Clean. Average Service. Garage Parking is extra. Our party was five so we payed extra for the Suite. Large comfortable room. Not cheap, but a good value for this part of town.

We did not enjoy our stay at the Doubletree Hotel Chicago-Magnificent Mile. First the positives. This hotel is often less expensive than other hotels in Chicago. It is also near Navy Pier, which is useful for people wishing to visit Navy Pier. Now for the negatives. Our bed was uncomfortable and our room was noisy. The windows do not effectively block out street noise. This may be a function of the age of the building, which leads to another problem we experienced. Something is wrong with the elevators at this hotel. At times the elevators come right away. At other times, elevator wait time can exceed - minutes (we stayed at this hotel before it was a Doubletree and had similar problems with the elevators). This hotel also has a poor business center, so I would not recommend it for business travelers who might need access to a printer. The hotel does have wireless Internet access. However, we had significant problems with Internet access. The hotel has what looks like a large outdoor pool, but we were not able to use it because it was quite cold in Chicago during our stay.
Management is very nice! Need a little improvement on interior.
I was extremely satisfied with the atmosphere, staff, and location of the Magnolia Hotel. The baseball game we attended was within walking distance. Very enjoyable!

I stayed at this hotel for - days. Got in late, the restaurant was still open and the staff could not have been nicer. As I am on the road every week, I can say with confidence that this hotel is one of the best!

Had a lovely stay in this hotel for new years. Really conveniently located in the back bay of boston. Great value. Only annoyance was...checkout was noon. Housekeeping knocked on the door every half hour from a little before -am till we left at noon. Clearly when I told them to come back after -- it didn't register. Other than that which really put a sour taste at the end, this hotel and the staff were awesome.

The location is the best thing about this hotel - it's incredibly central, close to buses, subway, and walking distance from many things (eg Grand Central, Empire State).
The front of house staff are pleasant and helpful.
Room facilities OK - decent view, comfortable beds, coffeemaker. Rooms are not massive (and I'm English, so don't necessarily expect rooms to be huge by US standards!) but are adequate.
The servicing of the room is a bit haphazard - no bathrobe when I arrived, no bathmat the next day, and the minibar was never restocked.
Don't even THINK about having breakfast in house. It is ridiculously expensive, and there must be -- or so diners serving similar fare within a block of the hotel, at around a quarter of the hotel's prices.
Nothing significant against it - and had it been cheaper I would have given it a higher rating - I've just stayed in nicer hotels in other large US cities (and capital cities elsewhere) for significantly cheaper prices.

We were first timers to NYC so I'm not sure what is the norm for room size but in saying that although the rooms were quite stylish I did find them rather on the smallish size. The elevators are definitely quite small but this did not cause us any issues. When we checked in at --pm it was nearly impossible to even hear what the receptionist was saying as the booming music from the bar area was so loud. I imagine those staying on the lower floors would struggle getting to sleep with the noise. The carpet in the bar was heavily stained and looked filthy. We requested a non-smoking room but our room absolutely stank of smoke. A great location and pricing is ok but a bit disappointed overall.

Was staying at this hotel for - nights. It is a very basic hotel with nothing special. I was traveling in a larger group of family members and we had - different rooms. There was a great difference in the way the rooms were arranged, but all were very small.
The interior was old, and there was issues with all the bathrooms but these were fixed during our stay. The air conditioning is integrated in the window frame, and was very noisy. We had to turn it off during the night.
If you don't expect much but a place to sleep, this could be a good basic hotel for a sightseeing and shopping trip to New York. The service from the staff was friendly.

The motel is the nicest one in the area. (Keep reading) It's clean and there is a fridge and microwave. The staff was very nice and the housekeepers very quiet while they moved from room-to-room.
Okay, with that being said, the motel being the nicest in the area doesn't necessarily mean that it's an area you want to visit! Frankly, it was a little scary.
I could go on about the depressing way people live and their choices in life, but I'm not going to judge anyone. I just don't understand why I passed a few people walking down the street carrying -- packs of beer they purchased at -:-- in the morning. 
I also don't understand why a convenience store (the one south of the overpass of Interstate -- with the yellow logo) would not notice the hooker soliciting on their property. I watched the whole thing as I was pumping gas. ( If you see a guy in a bright royal blue Scion with graphics on the side who is in his mid---'s with dark hair, ask him how his hooker was.)
If you need a place to rest your weary head, it's clean here but that's about it. Just make sure you lock your car.

The hotel is nicely laid out with pool and contemporary furnishings and staff are more friendly than the other top-end hotels in Soho area we have stayed at such as Mercer and Thompson. However they made - pretty fundamnental mistakes - they tried to overcharge me $--- for the room, then blaming it on 'computer glitch', they were unable to honour the -pm check-in time despite the fact i phoned ahead to make sure as my wife was coming in from transatlantic flight and finally they were unable to locate my stored luggage for ages due to a mishap. Manager extended the minimum of aplologies when i pointed these issues out.

I had a wonderful experience at Hotel Giraffe. The staff were friendly and professional and accomodated all my requests no problem. 
I booked a room for a girls weekend with my sister. Upon arrival we were shown a dark, back room facing street construction. I asked to be moved and we were immediately switched to a room with a better view. 
The breakfast was a continental breakfast +. It's served in the lobby - it's a charming space to relax.
The movie selection is pretty bad. Don't depend on their movie libarary. Bring your own.
The hotel is expensive. But it's New York. At least the service lives up to the price. The location is great. Not as touristy as times square or midtown, but clean, safe and interesting.

Looking forward to good nights rest, guess what, desk attendant calls --:-- am to advise me they undercharged me for the room an additional .-- was needed? What^ are you kidding me I was sleeping. Next morning manager was unapologetic and very arrogant. Add insult to injury, the breakfast nook was filthy dirty.

The first time we stayed here, the stay was awful! We booked through Hotwire, and this was the hotel we ended up with. 
Second time around was loads better; however, there is still much more improvement they could make. While the hotel is old, the rooms are not very clean. There is soap scum buildup on the bathroom tiles, and there are cracks and holes in the tiles, where someone has done a really poor job fixing them. If they got a legitamate person to do maintenance- repairs this hotel could be spectacular.
Trish with the front desk was really nice and accomodating. The valets were great... although $-- a day for parking is ridiculous, when the lot behind them goes for $-- a day. Next time we know better. 
Room and bathroom are smaller than normal, but this is a historic hotel. It was adequate for my husband and I. Also, the walls are thin; when we got back to the hotel around midnight or one, we got in bed, and we could hear others

The stay at the Grant Hotel was very disappointing. The Hotel smelled like urin, also the rooms. My clothes smelled really badly after returning home. The Hotel was unbelievably noisy. We could here everything that was going on in the rooms next to us and in the hallway. We were woken up every morning EARLY because of other guests and housekeeping cleaning rooms. The guests who stayed next to us liked to watch television late at night and this kept us awake. I have never slept as little in any other Hotel. Also there was no information in the hotel room. We did not know the number to front desk or how to call room to room. 
The staff was not very help full, and they all seemed very indifferent. I find it very strange that the staff didn't say hello, or goodnight or whatever whenever we entered the Hotel. They didn't even look up from the computer, and there where no other guests there. One of the receptionists was acting unprofessional by being in a bad mood and clearly showed us that calling for a cab to the airport was a hassle. The only positive thing I can say about the Grant hotel is the location. Besides of this the Hotel was expensive compared to service and the product we received.
I will never stay in this Hotel again!

Good basic motel with a very good location to loop --- east. Basically one block off. No noise from freeway, free breakfast even included egg dishes and waffles. Nice pool and they have a computer on site that you can use. 
King room has small fridge and microwave. Would stay again.

I recently stayed at the Powell Hotel with some friends for the San Francisco Valentines day pillow fight. The hotel is in a great location, with the BART, Muni, Cable Cars, and shopping right outside the door. My friends and I were able to take the BART into San Francisco, pillow fight, party and crash conveniently. I plan on staying at the Powell Hotel next month when I go to see Killswitch Engage at the Warfield Theatre. It's only two blocks away!

I booked this hotel based on TripAdvisor reviews. I had stayed at the Four Seasons Seattle last year and loved that, too. When I reserved the room, I mentioned it was our wedding anniversary. When we checked in, they had upgraded us to a townhouse for no extra charge! And gave us this amazing dessert to split with a card signed by the staff. The place is so nice and right near everything. I liked it equally as much as the Four Seasons, and it was a much more affordable price. I would highly recommend this hotel to everyone I know travelling to Seattle.

Seriously, if I had been paying $-- a night, I MIGHT not have been so aghast. From non-functioning lights in the bathroom and closet-like cubicle to total lack of amenities to noise to ancient furniture to dark, dark, dark faux-finished walls (and painted a-c unit) to food smells from the restaurant below, it was hellish. When I checked out, I requested a taxi. The woman at the desk told me to sit and wait and the driver would come in for me. i should have known a buddy would show up, who then tried to charge me $-- for a ride. 
Horrible. Its only selling point is its proximity to the Convention Center.

I had a two day conference and stayed for one night, and that was enough! I was a vendor and had a lot of boxes to take to the Fitzgerald Ballroom right off the main lobby. When you enter on the main level there is only an up escalator and no elevator and the escalator was broken. I had to have two bellman carry everything up. What a hassle. Had same problem the next day. I asked the bellman what do you do if someone arrives in a wheelchair? He shrugged his shoulders. I had a small dirty room on the --th floor...carpet wasn't vacuumed very well and toilet was clogged. The handyman unclogged it but left a filthy mess in the bathroom. I ended up cleaning it up not what you want to do at midnight. Why did I pay $--- for this room? Also on the -nd bed too many stray hairs that weren't mine on the bedspread.

My boyfriend and I stayed here after spending - nights up in the Theater District at the Sheraton Towers. The two hotels were night and day. 
I was exhausted (and cold) from the previous - nights in Times Square (weather was in the low --s). The room was small, but had very nice finishes. The bedding was super soft and the bed itself was very comfortable. The bathroom and wet bar had everything we needed, including Kiehl's shampoo and conditioner, and an adult """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""pleasure package"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", which I had never seen offered in a hotel room. The room also had a flat screen TV. 
The only downside is the location, sort of in an alley-like street. There aren't many great restaurants within short walking distance, so we always took the subway to Chelsea to eat. We didn't eat in the restaurant located in the hotel, but it looked like people were enjoying it. 
Upon leaving we checked our bags, since our flight back to Seattle wasn't until -:--. The front desk staff was more than helpful accomodating us.

From the time we walked into the hotel and until the time we left, we were always greeted with kind, helpful, and courteous staff. Everyone made us feel really welcomed and comfortable at the Hotel Brexton. They did a great job of renovating the hotel and making it a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cozy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" atmosphere. Thank you so much for the bottle of wine. 
The first day we were there the weather was beautiful. That night my wife and I sat outside an enjoyed a good bottle of wine. The night air was perfect and made for very special time for my wife and I - Thank you for providing an outside patio for us to sit and relax on.
Parking was not an issue as the hotel had reserved spots for its guests. We were surprised that there was a bus (free of charge) that we could take to get to the inner harbor and other nearby attractions. 
A BIG thank you to everyone at the Hotel Brexton who made our stay a welcomed and enjoyable. We look forward to returning for another visit!

I stayed here on May ----, and I loved it. If its your first time in Boston, I highly recommend it, simply because its a great location. First of all, you can take the free shuttle to the hotel, right from Boston Logan Airport (save over $-- in taxi fare, roundtrip), It's only minutes away from the airport, so you can sleep in a little more before waking up to take that early flight home, and you never have to deal with traffic. Second, the views. Wow. if you like the Boston city skyline, you're going to love this place. Sit back and have a drink as you watch the sun set over Boston Harbor. Third, I took the Water Taxi nearby, which was $-- for a round trip from the hotel to downtown (its cheaper than taking a taxi over there). It will leave you in a perfect place for taking Old town trolley tour bus, and Ghost tour venues nearby. You can also eat some good seafood in the variety of local eateries on the bay, and walk off the calories by taking a nice stroll around the historic places of interest.

The hotel was nice and clean, the breakfast was not great most stuff was cold and the service was lacking. the worst was that we got a room on the side of the hotel that had the train line across the way from it so at -:-- am and again around -:--am the train seemed to stop on the line outside for about a half hour it sounded like a very loud a-c unit maybe there was a problem on the line and we just were unlucky but it ruined our nights sleep

A wall of windows overlooking the World Trade Center and NY harbor. Maybe not for everyone, but dazzling for anyone with ties to the city. The room and staff were way larger than most NY hotel rooms, clean and with everything working. It's a great base if you want to explore lower Manhattan and the transportation access is unbeatable.

I booked a room through Priceline for $-- and later read I might've gotten it for $--. Anyway we were happy with the room and had a great view of the river, water taxis, Hancock Center, part of the Wrigley Building, from the --rd floor -- beds and pillows were very comfortable, AC worked quite well. Restaurant over-priced -- go to nearby Corner Bakery and Cafe for breakfast. Great location if you want to use the Water Taxis and catch the architectural boat tours, both of which depart from right in front of the hotel. We were told the hotel is soon to undergo a complete remodel. Our room was nice but the toilet was a bit stained and sometimes didn't flush well. We could hear thumps and bumps from other rooms plus loud people in the hall one night.
Desk manager was not helpful-almost caused us to miss our cruise! Woke up with little bites (red marks) on our bodies. A real example of you get what you pay for! Stay away from this place!

We live near Seattle, but booked a one-night stay at Hotel ---- to spend my husband's birthday in the city. We arrived a bit early for our check-in time. Check-in was at -pm, and we got there are -:--pm. They informed us that the room would not be ready until four, so we left our bags and opted to walk around the city for a little while.
We returned at -:-- and our room was still not ready. The staff was very apologetic and offered us free drinks and an appetizer in the Boca Bar. We weren't hungry, but the weather had taken a turn, so we accepted the offer and went and sat in the bar. The staff said that they would come get us when our room was ready. 
We waited, and waited, and waited. Finally at -:--pm (two hours later), my husband went to check to see if our room was ready. The woman at the front desk looked mortified. """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""They didn't come to get you??"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" she said. Our room was actually ready, but nobody had bothered to tell us. We were finally escorted up to our room. It was a lovely, large room that looked out onto the sound (we booked an ocean-view room). 
The woman who escorted us up also personally brought up our baggage and apologized again, offering us free breakfast and late check-out which we were only too happy to accept. 
We generally had a nice stay in the hotel. The room was clean. The tub was cool, and the view was beautiful. We did order room service breakfast. It came quickly and was tasty.
When we checked out the next morning, our free breakfast and late check-in had been correctly noted in our file and there were no further mishaps. I do appreciate it when a business admits that they screwed up and goes the extra mile to try to make it right. Because of that, I recommend the hotel ---- to anybody staying in Seattle. The location is great, the rooms are lovely, and the service is very accommodating.

The lobby and outside condition seemed fine. The hallway did seem a little depressing. The room itself was mostly fine. Although the walls needed cleaning in some places. The problem was the bathroom. There was mold on the tile, the tub needed a good scrub, the paint in the ceiling was peeling, and the wallpaper needed cleaning. The wall paper job itself just looked shoddy. The bed and linen were comfortable and in good condition. The staff were nice and polite. Parking is six dollars a day. It was a comfortable stay but I'm not sure if I would stay again.

This was my first trip to New York and my expectations were exceeded by the hotel and its staff. The hotel is located in the pricey Upper East side of Manhattan -- a very safe location and close to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Museum Mile"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and Central Park. I travelled during a quiet time for the hotel and was given an upgraded room at no charge on request. 
The hotel is rather old, but was updated in the ----'s. My suite had lovely dark woodwork and a (nonworking) fireplace with a modern, attractive bath. My only complaint is that my room was rather noisy -- it faced the traffic (notably garbage trucks) of Madison avenue and the windows were rather thin -- especially in the bathroom, where duct tape was placed along the sides of the window. Complimentary breakfast is served from -:----:-- a.m. and -- hr. access to coffee-tea-hot chocolate was a nice touch...as were the Aveda bath products. There is a small exercise room with new-looking equipment and $-- day passes are available for the nearby YMHA. Staff were polite and professional. Valet parking is available for $---day.

This is a classic example of hotel mis-branding. No way is this a Crowne Plaza. At best it’s a Holiday Inn with a few superficial upgrades, but even then it still needs some work. Everything has a down-market feel – the rooms, the lobby, the staff, the pool, the guests (large group of Hispanics sitting in lobby talking very loudly wearing tank tops and drinking from a couple of brought-in cases of beer). Good value, though, since the room only cost $-- through Hotwire. But it’s still a pig with lipstick.

I stayed three nights at the US Grant for a conference and couldn't have been happier. The most impressive part other than the heavenly bed was the friendliness of the staff. The front desk was welcoming and helpful. I ordered room service and concierge set up a massage and a hair appt for me within - hours on a busy Saturday. I enjoyed the fitness center that was open -- hours a day and away from the rooms. It is located perfectly in the gas lamp with an easy walk to the convention center.

I was very happy with my stay at the Sheraton. My favorable impressions began when I called the night befor our arrival. The weather report for travel between home and Chicago included a travel advisory. I called to ask if I could cancel the morning we were to arrive in the event snow prvented us from reaching Chicago. The staff person was very helpful and said in the event of weather it would not be a problem.
The second event of note was,while attending conferences my wife was shopping in the area. A shallow coat of snow had covered the sidewalks and streets. She stepped in a snow filled chuck hole tripped and fell. My wife returned to our room. A staff person was in our room cleaning . Seeing my wife covered with slush and a bruised and bleeding knee. She offered to get her help and took a hand cloth from her cart to help her clean her knee.
The hotel the building is wonderful but the workers make it very special.

We stayed at the Sheraton Tibeca only as a convenience as our bus tour was departing from this hotel. The cost was excessive for the basic facilities that were on offer. We stayed one night prior to the tour and upon checkout our friends had a dispute with the female receptionist regarding some phone calls. The receptionist was extremely rude and when we asked to speak to the Manager she said he was not available. 
Only again because of convenience and we had prepaid we stayed at this hotel one night at the completion of our tour. We encountered the same receptionist as our first visit. She was difficult to begin with and then recognised us so her attitude changed immediately to being very helpful and friendly. All other staff we encountered were helpful.
I would not stay at this hotel again but for those that choose to it is close to China town, Little Italy for all the fabulous restaurants and Soho for shopping.

This was my first stay here. Room modern and large. Bed and linens great. Beautiful flat screen. Staff truly wonderful and there was nothing that they would not do.
The negatives: Walls are very thin, and could hear the people in the next room talking, and the TV sound apparent.
Parking, at $--, extremely expensive for this area. Another issue is location. Fine for me, but if someone wants a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""night on the town"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", too far to walk anywhere.
Would definitely stay again, primarily due to the wonderful staff.

I am an executive with Choice Hotel (road warrior). I recently needed to stay in El Paso Texas for a week. I looked all over Choice and booked at a newer property ( always seems cleaner). I landed at Sleep Inn University El Paso. Upon arrival the GM personally greeted me and made recommendations on restaurant and things to see. The staff made me feel like I was at home with anything I needed. I stayed in a suite that was large, very clean, nicely decorated and full of amenities. I have stayed in over --- Choice properties and this is is a diamond property to me.

Everything was great! Room was clean, modern, comfortable bed, no complaints at all! Pool area was very nice, the staff was very helpful, and polite! Would recommend this hotel to anyone. We had a great view of the city!

I have never written a review before, but it was a great experience so I want to leave a note.
The hotel is an easy - to -- minute walk to the harbor, Fells Point, and Little Italy. They had no problem with me parking my car in their lot a few hours before check in time so that we could get started with our day without having to move the car later. The service was great when we did eventually make it back to the room. Everyone was very nice and very polite, it was refreshing to feel that they were actually happy to see me in the hotel. Even with the hotel filled to capacity for a Ravins game, they still made time to cover the little details that make staying in a hotel enjoyable.

We've come before and we just reserved to return in April. A couple of blocks to good restaurants and the Venice boardwalk. Staff are always very professional and friendly. They have wi-fi now, and are almost finished some renovations. Clean, convenient, and priced for those of us who like small hotels but have small budgets too. Little details like cookies and fruit at the desk. Breakfast has many choices, and can be eaten in the outdoor Atrium on warm days. They charge $- a day additional for parking, but that's minor compared to others in this area.

The best thing to say about the Sheraton is that it is in a fantastic location. That being said, I think they aren't getting quite all of the value out of it. The hotel looks...used. It is pretty nice, but looks like it takes a lot of use. Everything about the hotel is like that... I will say that the pool has a fantastic view of Mt. Rainier, so check that out. Also, the sheets weren't soft or plush, they were so stiff they made noise when I laid down, which is nice to know they were clean, but uncomfortable at first.

Visiting NYC for the -rd time (but first time for New Year), we decided to stay in Midtown, near the shops, sales and sites. The Roosevelt is perfectly poistioned on East --th, so was great for hitting Times Square, the shops on -th Av and generally getting around NY. Walking from the hotel was ideal and avoided the numerous taxi rides I have taken on previous visits. The Roosevelt itself has an impressive foyer and bar, and the staff are typically helpful of the US. Bags are dealt with and taxis are called, and the concierge desk is very helpful. The rooms are quite dated, but serve a purpose as we simply wanted a comfy bed-room to use as a base for doing the city. If you're spending lots of time in your room then this isn't the right hotel for you, but then it's probably not the right city to visit either.

I stay here fairly often when working in Columbus. It never disappoints. The staff is very friendly and helpful. The rooms are clean. This is a basic business hotel. I know what to expect and they always deliver. The restaurant is good with cook to order breakfast. I am not a big fan of Lodgenet, the TV service used in the hotel.

My trip to Charlotte was for business and I was looking for a hotel near the courthouse. The Blake Hotel was one of the closest choices. After reading the mixed reviews of the hotel, I was a bit unsure as to whether I wanted to stay there or not. However, I was also able to secure a fairly reasonable room rate and so decided to try it. The Blake exceeded my expectations. My room was extremely comfortable, the air conditioner worked just fine and the yet-to-be remodeled bathroom was clean. There is a basic continental breakfast offered in the morning and a happy hour in the afternoon. Although their restaurant is not open, you can order some food items at the bar. They also offer a Snack to Go service with simple food items (sandwiches, salads, drinks, etc). The pool was not open while I was there. The remodeling project is quite expansive and it will take a little while before everything is completed. But if you're looking for a simple place to stay with attentive, conscientious staff, try the Blake Hotel.

I was booked into the Hotel Helix by someone handling my business arrangements, someone living in the area who said she thought I'd appreciate a hotel a little out of the ordinary and standard -- and I absolutely loved the Austin Powers retro look of the lobby and my room and the music playing in the lobby. A younger friend going to graduate school in DC came to visit, and he thought it was the perfect hotel for me, too: funky yet filled with all the comforts and amenities one would expect at a hotel -- comfy bed with a trompe l'oeil backdrop of a surfer on the entire wall, bright oranges and yellows and greens to the color scheme but somehow not disturbingly glaring, television midway on a kitchy pole stand with good reception and sound, good quality toiletries and water pressure and temperature in the bathroom area with a bright orange sink, coffee maker. I also appreciated and attended the free champagne """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""happy hour"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" each evening.
I appreciated not being in not just a carbon copy chain hotel where all the majority of the hotels and noise were. I enjoyed walking to the White House area, to the International Spy Museum, to the Smithsonian American Art Museum, etc. Not far, but not for those unaccustomed to walking. Great restaurant a block or so away, convenient corner store for buying snacks or soft drinks for the room. I didn't find the neighborhood overly sketchy as some other reviewers had, but then I'm a born-and-raised big-city person.

I actually transferred from another W hotel that was just way too noisy. In general, I love the Starwood chain and the W's, the design, high energy, young staff, great locations. I chose this location for its rate+availability, and it was truly the smallest hotel room I have ever stayed in (compared to some very over-sized W rooms in Union Square's W Hotel). Design=A Mini-Bar-TV-Bliss goodies=A, dusty...the maid needs to wipe down the most obvious surfaces...I found myself dusting my own room before settling in! Great location near Grand Central Terminal, east side subway...nice lobby cafe and lunch place.

we stayed here July ---- thought it was great! Got a really nice room in the main tower facing the pool and the front of the hotel. Very nice landscaping, very clean. Loved the fact that the mall is right behind at walking distance. We plan to visit again this June ---- for our annual Jehovah's Witness convention, and if possible stay every year here. No complaints whatsoever!
breakfeast is good, and the view of our room is excellent! you can enjoy the sunshine just a few steps from your room. very friendly stuff. parking is convenient.

In short, what more could you ask for? Other reviewers seemed not to have enjoyed their stay. I found the staff attentive and friendly. The room was spotless and didn't seem outdated to me. True, the TV was not a flat-screen, but that doesn't rate high on my list.
What does rate high for me are cleanliness, security, and good food. 
For dinner at --, I had a perfect filet mignon. The following morning, I had the fabulous lump crab eggs benedict.

We booked our hotel online and chose SpringHill Suites because the rooms were said to be larger than most hotel rooms. The pictures of the rooms looked nice and big, but we were fooled. I would recommend this hotel to anyone going Newyork.
The location was great not far from time square, the rooms are spacious with great views & ensuite and very comfortable beds. The Restraunt downstairs was great for morning breakfast as it was a buffet.

the staff were great. The concierge Kristin was the most friendly and helpful person i came across. she was always willing to help & go the extra mile.
Overall, if you get the opputunity to go NY, thsi hotel is a must to stay at!!!!!

This hotel is a solid, quality experience. The rooms are nice, quiet, and clean. The staff is helpful and knowledgeable. The bar is fun too. There are also several good places to eat and drink within a few blocks. This is one of my favorite places to stay including the Willard and W.

Quality survives at the Campton Place Hotel despite a change in ownership. I've stayed at the Campton Place Hotel - times previously and have loved each visit. This fall after making our reservations we had some less than ideal communications with the hotel (dinner reservation assistance, etc...). We couldn't believe it when our taxi arrived outside Doubletree - the location was incredible - right bang smack in the middle of Times Square and for those of us who'd never been to New York before this was a perfect base for a perfect stay to what has to be the best city in the world. By the way I come from Sydney so that's saying something!
If you assume such a location would be noisy you would be wrong. Once you go up in the lift to the very cool reception and bar area you could be anywhere. To have that much space in a hotel room in the middle of Manhattan was again incredible. An extra living area is worth its weight in gold when you have heaps of shopping bags to bring back at the end of each day! Comfy sofa, comfy bed and big bathroom - superb.
The only negative - the breakfast buffet. We are used to Asian breakfast buffets and this doesn't even try to compete. Pretty ordinary and expensive - no gluten-wheat free options unless you have the omelette which I'm not overly keen on. But you don't need to eat there when you're in the centre of everything anyway.

Inexpensive, and pretty good for the price. 
My only complaint was that the carpet was apparently pretty dirty because AFTER I showered, my feet left black footprints on the bath mat.

We checked in yesterday and spent today exploring Canyon Villas and the JW Marriott next door. Staff at both are very friendly and helpful. My husband and I have a one bedroom suite with kitchen - lots of room and two televisions. Great place for long walks. We don't want to leave!

We were recommended Paradise Point by a travel agent after the hotel we originally booked told us their pool would be under construction during our stay. (Ouch!) I stayed at this hotel for one night this past weekend. Although the location was good, the hotel is just tired. The hallways are dark and the carpet in the elevator vestibules is worn and bumpy.

The Hilton Garden Inn in New York was just a block off of the heart of times sqaure there was a huge continetal breakfest and the rooms were very clean, service was great too they told us were te good resturants are, the value was average and i would reccomend this hotel to anyone!

I stayed here with two colleagues for two nights. The food at the hotel restaurant is something to write home about. Really loved the food there. Have no problem recommending this hotel.

Hyatt has yet to disappoint us. Hyatt we love you!! :)

We had the pleasure of staying at the Renaissance Times Square Hotel for three days during a recent vacation to New York City. The room itself was tastefully appointed offering a work desk, reading chair and side table, two double beds, a large armoire, a flat screen television, a mini bar as well as a close up view of some of the neon signs adorning Times Square. The washroom was bright, clean and equipped with a speaker connected to the television so that you can hear the television while showering. The washroom also had complimentary Aveda soaps and creams which were great in order to relax at the end of the day.
The hotel is also very efficient in unloading your car and parking your vehicle. You just have to pull up in front of the hotel and the porters will take care of everything. Parking is extremely expensive in New York City and the average going rate for a -- hour period without in or out privileges is about $-- for an SUV in a public parking lot. The hotel offers valet parking for $-- for an SUV and parks the car for you making it a breeze to check in and less expensive than looking for your own parking.

The staff at the restaurant and concierge louge were extremley polite and efficient. The hotel was kept immaculately clean and we even saw hotel employees touching up paint during our stay in order to keep everything in tip top shape.
In conclusion, I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking to be right in the heart of the action or who is visiting New York City for the first time. The hotel is not a budget one so I would recommend booking it on discount sites or on Marriott’s site when promotional rates are available. Enjoy!

I stayed at this hotel for my --th birthday celebration with my partner. Went to Chicago for the first time on a guy's weekend getaway. I had anticipated going for a long time even though it was winter, we are all from the south, so it's a nice change. We have W Hotels in our city, and have always had a good reputation, so seeing that Chicago had one right on the lakeshore we were all in. Hotel decor lived up to it's boutique reputation and the staff seemed accomodating, even moved us to a room overlooking the lake and Navy Pier. The problems arose with the rooms itself- very small and the bathrooms have no privacy being that they have sliding bamboo slats for doors and louvered window doors on the oposite wall. If your by yourself or with a significant other then it may not be an issue, but with mixed company it was awkward. Our second night we were invaded by a cheerleading group who were there for a competition....needles to say they did not sapre the expense on insulation- heard every word, in fact their phone rang and I reached to pick up mine. Bars within the Hotel are very pricey $-- for a mixed drink?? What this Hotel has going for it is the view and the location relevant to downtown and Michigan avenue- There are better Hotels out there for the same price, do your research.

I always like to give a quick bit of background info and disclaimers to put the review in perspective, so here goes. After working for Hyatt Hotels for -- years I am a bit of a hotel """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""snob"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" so take some of my pickiness with a grain of salt. In addition, this was a buisness trip that didn't allow me to use, explore or appreciate all of the facitities at the hotel so my reivew will reflect that perspective.
Checked in arond -pm to a well staffed front desk in a beautiful lobby. The desk clerk was efficient and helpful and gave me all the information that I needed and I was on my way. There are two towers in the hotel, Harbor Tower (older tower) and the Sea[something] tower (newer tower). From comments that I heard from fellow meeting goers, the Sea[something] tower rooms were a bit nicer and more up-to-date. The room itself was very spacious with nice dark wood funiture that included a big desk (w-outlet) end tables, dresser and a chair ottoman combo. The dresser contained a room safe, fridge (no mini bar) and three drawers on the smaller side, two phones, iHome clock radio, wired and wireless internet connections. Both we complimentary for me but that could have been a meeting perk. Big --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" flat screen with usable computer monitor and HDMI connections. Hair dryer and magnifying mirror in the bathroom. The carpet looked relatively new. No balcony rooms from what I can see. My room had a decent view of the opposite tower, with downtown to my left and the harbor to my right. The bed was decent but not the most confortable I've ever been in. The pillows did not appear to be feather but seemed to stuffed with some kind of chunky synthetic filling. The conforter was a bit thin as well. The bed was well worn on one side but quite firm and more comfortable on the other side. General hotel bed tip - if you like a firmer mattress, always sleep on the side of the bed opposite the alarm clock. Most people will sleep on the alarm clock side and it will wear down quicker. 
The bathroom was simple but clean and in good shape. OK counter space. The tub-shower was a bit on the small side and did not have a bowed shower curtain as I've seen in other hotels. The shower pressure itself would make Karen Silkwood proud. Shower pressure is a real hot button of mine but I can say this is the first hotel where I would have liked to turn it down a bit. I did feel better though knowing I started each day here radiation free. :-)
Location, location, location. The hotel couldn't be better situated. About a ---- minute walk from the Gaslamp Quarter and Petco Park (Baseball-Padres). Tons of shopping and a restaurant for any type of food you can imagine. Nice place to just walk around as well. In addition, there is the Seaport Village directly behind the hotel. More shopping and restaurants that is literally two minutes from the building.
The train tracks are near by and you can hear the train whistle on a fairly regular basis from both the light rail and Amtrack style trains. It didn't bother me much but I could see how some folks could get a little bonkers from it although they do seem to stop running by --pm or midnight.
I didn't swim but the pool looked well kept but small. The do run three good sized fire pits at night in the pool area.
That's about all can speak to. Overall it was a very nice stay but did not live up to the image I had in my mine when I heard it was a Grand Hyatt (a title Hyatt usually reserves for their more spectacular hotels).
I would stay here again for business without hesitation but would at least investigate other options if I was bringing the family back for a vacation.
Happy Travels,
Sulu

The Pickwick was a decent hotel for the money. The location was good, right next door to a shopping centre and a couple of minutes away from the subway and cable car turnaround. We spent our evenings down at fishermans wharf which is about -- minutes by cable car. 
All in all - I couldn't complain about the hotel. I assume it must be excellent for staying on business due to it's central location, easy public transport access. If I were ever to go with the family, I think I would be more inclined to stay nearer fishermans wharf.

The hotel was very busy when I checked in but it didn’t took from me a lot of time to reach my room. I was upgraded as I am priority member to the --th floor.

A bar and restaurant on the ground floor but were busy when I was there. To summarize the hotel is good deal to LAX airport and around. If you are renting a car so it could be even a good deal for LA area.

I stayed at this very welcoming hotel while on extended travel for work. The staff was very friendly, and I think the best part was having a (free!) warm meal to come back to after each work day (Mon-Thurs). They have DirecTV and DVD players in the room, and the typical appliances (sans oven) you would expect in a suite - basically a mini apartment (with free cleaning service!). AAA members - take advantage of the discount! It's been a very good experience for a traveler far from home.

I stayed with the Hotel Mela during the July -th weekend. I am a hotel guy myself in Washington DC. Stayed a week in SF; loved the hotel. The room was large and clean, parking handy (I had to drive to Stanford daily) and the location great. The friendly service and good breakfast topped the experience. Superb value for the money!

Los Angeles is a huge city and everything is far from anything. So, we choose this hotel for being next to the airport and nearest the car rental stores. The room was big and clean and the staff is helpful.
If you're looking for a space just to take a bath and sleep, is a good option.
Unfortunatelly, there are no much space to park inside the hotel. If you came too late from your activities, there is a good chance to park outside. 
The wi-fi is fast and hotel is quiet, besides of location near the airport.

After reading reviews about this hotel, I was a bit skeptical to stay there but it turned out to be not as bad as I thought it would be. I would recommend considering La Quinta Inn Oltorf if you are on a tight budget but need a nice place to stay. It is not fancy though, but it's clean and the service is good. I usually go back really late in the evening and I saw security guards checking around, so I felt somehow safe. The fence is always open though. 
I don't know about the breakfast as I never had a chance to taste it. And I can't comment on the swimming pool because I've never been there, maybe next time!
The minor problem I didn't really enjoy was the internet because I was unable to connect in my room, I had to go to the hall to use it. Also, I don't know if the wall is really thin but I could hear the other person next door yelling or slamming the door, but I think not every guest would do that!!!

We spent four nights at Hotel Triton and will remember it for a long time. Excellent staff, great design and feel of the place. They have a grill and bar and the far end for your convienence. Valet parking is $-- a night. If you do not mind walking - minutes, you can park for free around the corner in the garage. If you need a car, try budget, Avis or dollar...one of the three usually has some deal in Houston. This hotel is highly recommended.

this is one of the nicest hotels in downtown Chicago - not just because of its location and ambience - but because the staff go above and beyond to help people.
great room and great exercise facility. bed was superb - and room was incredibly quiet.

We have just returned from - nights in New York staying at the Wellington Hotel. We were a bit worried when we arrived as it looked extremely run down and not very well maintained but when we entered the lobby we were surprised as it was in a lot better condition. The lobby can get very busy and packed - which means long queues to check in-out etc and it gets very hot. Also there are only a few lifts so expect to queue or share the lift to maximum capacity most of the time. Our room was on the --th floor and we were a bit worried when we got out of the lift as our corridor had seen better days, carpets need cleaning, there was a permanant nasty smell filling the air and we had to dodge huge trays of empty plates - leftover from room service to get to our room. Once inside our room it was a lot better although nothing spectacular. It was small but clean - with a maid service everyday for fresh towels etc. There is no air conditioning so even at the end of november the rooms were very hot which means you have to have the window open constantly which means noisy traffic outside. We didn't spend an awful lot of time in the room as there is so much to see and do and to be honest you couldn't get a better location than the Wellington. We basically walked everywhere as it is so handy for everything - Central Park, The Rockefeller Centre, Times Square and so much more are all in handy walking distance. If you need to get the subway anywhere, there is a stop right under the hotel. It couldn't be better. We defintely think we made the right choice staying here for our first visit to New York as the location is so good but i think if we went again we would stay somewhere a little nicer.

Amazing place! Great rate, and the service is equal to - star lodging I've stayed at elsewhere. Even the maintenance men in the hall wishing me a great day.

Check in was seamless and everything contained a smile from the moment I walked in until the moment I closed myself in my room...which by the way was completely adequate. King bed, comfy pillows, etc.
Could be an an average place with average everything. BUT, these folks care about what they do and my comfort. I'd definitely come back.

The room was great...very comfortable. The concierge was wonderful, and got us information that we needed to have a great trip. The staff at the front desk, the bar, and at breakfast were all friendly, and helpful.

Everything about this place looks worn out, even the bar. The hallways have that ---year old carpeting look and smell. 
The coup de grace for me: I checked in early and went downstairs for lunch and, when I came back, the key card wouldn't work to unlock the door. I had to wait well over an hour while maintenance first tried to reprogram the door lock and ultimately broke into the room by removing door hardware. If I'd have had a meeting to attend, I'd have been sunk, because everything -- including my computer -- was in the room.
Later in the evening, when we returned to the hotel to have a drink at the bar, all they had to eat were burnt popcorn crumbs and leftovers pre-made tuna sandwiches. 
This place is a dump. I would never go back.

This review is a bit late but none the less I must say something about my stay at the Giraffe, Christmas ----. This was a first time visit to NYC for my wife and myself and I chose the Giraffe because of the rave reviews from Tripadvisor.com. I was not disappointed right from the start. The folks at the front desk took good care of us and we were given a room that faced Park Avenue one floor from the top level. Room was clean and nicely decorated though the television seemed small-old for such a nice room. Room was fairly quiet as traffic from Park Avenue didn't seem too loud though if guests made noise in the hallway you could hear everything. Because of its location the hotel worked out great as a base of operations for our tour of NYC. Subway entrances are only a short walk away, there are a number of restaurants nearby (excellent Indian restaurant off Madison Ave at Madison Square Park) and decent small grocery stores-deli's near the FlatIron Building). As we ventured farther north I noted that most areas are busy and crowded with people. The location of the Giraffe was quiet and non-crowded which is something I preferred over the hustle and bustle of hotel areas around Time Square, etc. Breakfasts at the hotel were more than sufficient with bagels, juice, etc., in the hotel lobby and the cheese and wine in the late afternoon-early evening was perfect after a day of running around NYC. We were treated nicely by the hotel staff as they were always friendly and courteous. After spending four days in NYC and knowing what I know about the area I would most certainly stay at the Hotel Giraffe again, it was a wonderful Christmas time experience my wife and I will never forget. Much thanks to the hotel staff for taking such good care of us.

Brilliant.

My co-workers and I agreed that we would not stay here again and we much preferred the marriott a few blocks away.

Hotel Elysian was a perfect choice for our one-night romantic getaway from our teenagers. From the moment we entered the elegant courtyard, we felt like personal guests at a refined European manor. Great location, near to Times Square and within easy walking distance of shops and all the sights of New York. Ok.. now i've stayed in hotels all over the world (from $$$ to $) and I must say for the price you pay, this is the best hotel I've ever stayed at. 
Stayed there my -st & -nd times in NYC (both being a single female traveler). No microwave or refrigerator in room as was advertised. Breakfast items were average. Room was quiet. Cheap price.

I think they were flustered by the number of conference attendees. Some members of the conference couldn't get in their rooms until - pm. I did not ask for any special services and expected more, especially as a Hilton Honors gold member. The maintenance staff, concierge staff, housekeeping, and breakfast staff were friendly and helpful. The pool and gym facilities are located in the YMCA, in the next building. Even though it is connected via an indoor walkway, it still necessitates bringing a gym bag full of gear to take a swim.

After a long day of travelling we eventually arrived at the hotel around -pm. The hotel was perfectly air conditioned, and the reception staff were absolutely lovely. Willing to help with anything and everything! There were free apples and cookies available at the reception for all guests, everyday.
We had a King-size room with sofa bed and it was amazing, the bed was huge! Much larger than any 'kingsize' bed I've ever experienced! The towels were changed everyday and it was always super clean and tidy. The perfect place to come back to after a long day of walking and sight-seeing. If you wished for your bedding to be changed during your stay, you simply had to leave the card on the bed and they would change the sheets for you. 
The breakfast was always busy, as expected, but if you went early enough then you could miss the mad rush and eat as much as you like at your own leisurely pace. They also provided a breakfast bag to-go, for guests on the go. There was a large and varied selection for breakfast too and free coffee-tea etc available all day.
The only thing I could possibly moan about was the fact that one of the two lifts always seemed to be out of service....and being on the top floor, then stairs weren't really an option! But this really wasn't a problem at all as the rest of the hotel was just absolutely perfect! It was a very short walk to both Times Square-Broadway but not so central that it was continuously loud and noisy at night when trying to sleep.
I really couldn't recommend this hotel enough! We would definitely choose to stay here again if-when we visit again. 
There was free Wi-fi available in all the rooms and two computers with free internet, on the ground floor of the hotel.
We did speak to the concierge once- to ask for recommendation on local restaurants before we went to see The Lion King on Broadway. She was also really happy to help, and called the restaurant for us to reserve a table!
Overall, a really wonderful experience and we would ---% recommend this hotel!

Having stayed at multiple hotels in Chicago, I believe the Intercontinental to be one of the best for business travel. The rooms are moderately priced, the hotel is conveniently located, it has an excellent restaurant in Michael Jordan's Steakhouse and the business amenities are sufficient for any business traveler's needs. The staff was courteous and helpful. There is also an excellent refurbished pool to go with a sufficient gym.

We chose this hotel mainly because of the location and the reasonable price for a hotel in Washington. And on those two counts it definitely delivered. Good access to tourist sites and great restaurants around the corner. Wonderful atmosphere in this part of the city whether you walk along the historic canal or on the M street with bustling city life! For that reason I'd recommend it - with some qualifiers as the hotel itself was slightly disappointing though still acceptable.
Tavelling with our two teenaged kids we prefer suites with a seperate bedroom. However, when we arrived at Georgetown Suites we were placed in a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""junior suite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" with two doubles in one room. The hotel was fully booked that night and no change was possible. But for the following - nights we got a one-bedroom suite with a king bed and a sofa-bed in the living area. Lots of space which we liked even if the decor seemed a bit dated. However the kids complained that this was the worst sofa-bed they've ever slept in and in dire need for replacement.
Moreover, while the beds (the doubles the first night, the king the following nights) were furnished with warm duvets the pull-out had only a single thin blanket. We asked for a comforter but were told that their policy is not to give one out for pull-out beds. They did give us a second blanket but this was a pretty cold week and the kids still felt cold during the night. Didn't help that the the noisy heating-cooling system was difficult to regulate. Not to mention that all other hotels (-* in NY and Philadelphia and cheaper!) we stayed during this vacation actually gave us two seperate duvets on request for the kids so they wouldn't have to fight over the cover during the night.
Breakfast was ok - if you managed to get to the buffet in time before the crowds had emptied it. During the week this small area got very crowded with business travellers and all the healthy choices (fruit, fruit salad, yoghurt) were gone and not replaced. One morning I asked specifically for replacement: they brought a handful of oranges (great!) some inedible green bananas but no salad. Tables were not cleaned after guests had finished their breakfast and the next group wanted to use them. Guests are expected to clear their own dishes (which I don't mind doing) but with trash containers overflowing and not taken care of that was not easy to do.. On less busy days breakfast was a much better experience.

My mother and I were flying to NYC the following morning and we could not have asked for a better hotel! Not only was the staff very friendly and accommodating, but the suite was very clean and comfortable. We were also able to leave our cars in the hotel's parking lot for the weekend. The hotel's shuttle dropped us off and picked us back up on our return. Breakfast is included in morning that has a variety of hot and cold foods. The only concern is that since it is so close to the airport, there is a lot of traffic and that you hear airplanes arriving and departing all day and night! I would definitely recommend this trip hotel for travelers by themselves or with families

We got what we asked for. Two comfortable beds and lots of room (- flat screens!). No view of the river was requested, since I had read that even rooms with a view left a little to be desired at most hotels along the Riverwalk. We were a little disappointed to find a band and cheerleaders in the hotel which made it difficult to walk through our hotel. We would come back here again, but first would ask if """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""fans"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (NCAA Girl Volleyball) be part of the deal. Location is very convenient to everything one is here for. Coffee in our room and a locked bar. After dinner out this evening, we enjoyed a nice cocktail at the bar while all the fans are away.

This hotel is NOTHING better than OK. Anyone that write rave reviews about it must have been at another hotel...
Would I stay there again? YES....but only because when you are in NYC all you really need is a bed for a few hours.
Rooms about the size of a queen size bed, taps were backwards so the hot means cold and cold mean hot.
Location is the best part....one block from times square, couple from radio city, letterman, central park.
Overall, just a bed to sleep in and nothing more. If that's what you are looking for, book it....if you would rather a bit of glamour, DON'T STAY HERE!!!

This was an extremely nice hotel. Wonderful view of Columbus Circle-Central Park, great access to the trains. However, I guess I just didn't look like a Trump guest because I was harassed in the lobby every time I tried to return to my room. Basically the staff asked """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""what is your name"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" with a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""you don't belong here, and I know it"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" kind of look. Then once surprised to find my name was registered, the general response was a sort of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""very safe building, very safe building"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" apology - you would think after going through this a few times, someone might write down, hey there some young people staying here, so expect the unexpected. Or something! Anyway, the doorman also accosted me when I grabbed an umbrella during a rainy day. Gee thanks, definitely worth the money. Great place to stay if you look like you belong. If you look like you don?t belong however, spend your money somewhere else (I was in general left alone at the Four Seasons, for example).

We stayed here for - nights in club and although the rooms are on the small side and showers lack any real power it was Jean and Joyce,the concierge, that made our stay here more than comfortable. They arranged everything from reservations in the best restaurant in the South West (Binkley's) to a hot air balloon ride over the desert, they just could not do enough! The Club lounge is exactly as a lounge should be, full of great food and masses of free drinks all through the day and more information about the area than you can shake a library at. Would highly reccommend, but only in club.

This hotel is close to the metro and national zoo and a pleasant neighborhood, nestled by rock creek park. People unfamiliar with Dc should know that it is a pretty spread out city: the hotel is far from the downtown area with White House, Mall, etc... But given the convenience of DC metro it is definitely not a bad location.
I found the people who worked here to be nice and helpful. My room was big and the bed was comfortable. 
A couple of complaints: the hotel has wi-fi but it is definitely not hi-fi... it is really, really slow. If you are travelling on business or just want to use the internet it is very frustrating. Also, incredibly in this day and age, they charge an additional fee if you want to use the health club which is pretty small and dated.
Otherwise, the furnishings and amenities are standard, mid-range hotel caliber.

Just returned from a --night stay. First, I agree about the great location, tiny bathroom and small rooms. Our room were clean and comfortable.
Regarding customer service, it is abysmal. I called the hotel a month before our stay and asked for accomodations for my wife and I and our two adult children. She suggested two adjoining queen bed rooms. I agreed, and they confirmed the reservation.
When we checked in, we were assigned two rooms, but they were not adjoining. When we got to our rooms, we noticed that one of them had a door into the next room (locked from the other side, of course). I went back to the desk and asked to see the manager.
