If you know anything about San Fran, you know that everything is overpriced, there are lots of homeless people, and finding parking is a disaster. Those are all just things visitors should be prepared for. This hotel is on a less savory street, but none of the people gave us any trouble at all. Once inside, the owners and managers were all very friendly, and when I needed to switch rooms becuase we needed an extra bed, they were completely accomodating. The room was clean, and we had a bathroom that we didn't have to share. The parking situation is less than ideal here, and I wouldn't recomend it for a woman traveling alone (due to the dark garage aspect), but it is secure. If you are looking for a cheap place to spend a night in San Fran without any frills, this is a good bet. My fiance and I plan to go back there next time we're in the city.

great hotel except for your next door neighbor(s) you can hear them talking and the TV and the outside noise was horrible. 
please wear your eye plugs.

I had a wonderful experience staying at the James. My teenage daughter and I stayed here for - nights for some Spring Break fun in Chicago. The staff was wonderful and extremely helpful in getting us walking directions to all of the places we wanted to see. The doorman also gave us great restaurant recommendations. The rooms were cozy and the beds the most comfortable I've ever slept on in a hotel! We stayed on the -th floor and although the elevators are small they are also very quick. This did not pose a problem at all for us in having to wait long for one. The bar area did get hopping pretty good both nights although since I was with my teenager I didn't get a chance to check it out. I highly recommend the valet parking, it's only $-- more than public parking, you just pull up to the door and they take it from there.
I will definitely stay at The James Chicago again!

just had a lovely weekend at the Kimberly. One of the reasons we picked the hotel was because of the beautiful rooftop bar. We were very disappointed that - of our - nights at the hotel the bar was not open until after --:-- pm due to private functions. There should be some area left open in the bar for hotel guests.

initially i got off on the wrong foot with this hotel. we arrived early (- hours before check in) but were told no rooms were avaliable yet. i was so tired from jet lag and had an upset tummy that had been bothering me for days, i looked like death warmed up, all i wanted was a place to rest and a shower. in the end our room wasn't even ready at check in time. my husband went to the desk to repeatedly check on the room status and in the end the front desk lady had to go to find the cleaners herself to check if the room had been done. my husband said to them, give us any room please, we really just need to rest, meanwhile i'm just about asleep on the lobby lounge and asking to use their bathroom every half an hour (which requires a key pass) and other people checking in after us got rooms before us (and as far as i know, all the rooms are the same). now i KNOW that check in time means check in time, but many other times when we have travelled, if we have gotten there early, and the room is not ready, we get the response of 'the room allocated to you is not ready but if you would like the same type of room on a lower floor-different view-whatever we can give that to you'. i was REALLY hoping this was the case as i seriously just wanted to walk out in front of a bus at high speed i felt so crappy. but it was not to be! however, once in the room, the room was great. clean, fresh, housekeeping was great, internet adequate (sometimes very slow), view was nice (looking towards macy's) and as it was our wedding anniversary they left us a nice bottle of wine and some (wierd fruit) chocolates and a card, which was nice. we also got a $-- card for the in house restaurant which covered - of - meals for us, AWESOME! check in aside, this hotel was great. i would still stay here again. i think it was alot of bad timing and circumstance that we had an initial poor experience. any other time i would have been happy to dump luggage and toddle off to have a look around. by the end of the trip i felt much better though. and i fell in love with san franscisco. do mr toads tours (- hour tour) and check out the haight ashbury district for vintage shopping.

Ive stayed at the affinia - times now and both the staff and the rooms never disappoint. The beds are really comfy and the safe in the room, plus kitchenette are great to have. The rooms aren't as modern as some hotels but provide an old world charm, some could probably do with a slight refresh but they are all clean and tidy with no major maintenance issues. 
The location of the hotel is perfect, an easy walk to times square and Macy's straight across the street is penn station, a cab stop and Madison square gardens.
All in all never disappointed.

Sold on its location with quite good rooms. Friendly and very helpful staff. Breakfast a disappointment, though """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""included"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in room rate, plastic plates and cutlery at this price point! Food reasonable quality but limited variety. On tap coffee and tea in lobby ---- a nice touch. 
Opt for a rear facing room, very quiet, I imagine could be noisy facing -th Avenue. 
Overall good but overpriced or is that simply the price of NYC?

Just finished our Conference last weekend, and I have to commend Marriott for the the great personalized and professional service I was provided by the staff at the Renaissance in Seattle-...from the hospitable welcome from Chuck at check-in to the friendly faces cleaning the room or delivering freshly buffed shoes or a vase for my Pike St. flowers, to the efficient and unobtrusive servers of delicious meals throughout our conference and to Timothy for his gracious printing of boarding passes and maps. I reserve special accolades for Jean-Paul, the consummate Concierge, who arranged an impromtu dinner reunion for -- folks at a local restaurant, where we were all greeted warmly and then surprised with a special appetizer course, compliments of Jean-Paul! Now that's style and grace under pressure! Jean-Paul provided the icing on the cake....or on the Conference in this case....and made my visit to Seattle into a truly memorable experience. I felt as if I were staying at the Ritz Carlton (my highest accolade!).

Although an older hotel, we visited Baltimore to attend the Preakness. We loved the location, Hotel was neat, clean, staff was exceptional. It was a great experiance, one of the nicer Holiday Inns we have stayed at.

we stayed in this hotel april ----. it has since changed its name. they were in the middle of renovating this hotel whilst we were there, although this didn't cause any problems to us. there was no lift so you have to lug your bags upstairs to the lobby then up more stairs to your room.
 we were given a large room overlooking broadway. it had not been renovated so it looked a bit tired to say the least. - huge beds, not many wardrobes but i suppose this will be different now.
 the price we paid wasn't expensive so value for money was good. as it's on tthr upper west side , it's not central but has a subway right outside the hotel which gets you about easily.
 there are a few (very few) bars and restaurants nearby, plenty of deli's, cafes etc. we went to the local pub (the tavern i think) and we were the only tourists there. it was full of locals who were really friendly and you get a proper feel of a NY neighbourhood.
 the staff were ok but didn't put themselves out for you. the maids did an average job. all in all it was ok.

I work in the city often, and had to take a last minute trip this weekend. I generally stay at Hilton family hotels, just because they're reliable, but they were booked, so I checked TripAdvisor and saw the good reviews for GP...and I'm happy to add one! 
--The rates were comparable to a Hliton chain hotel
--The location was amazing (a few blocks from BART, Union Square, tons of coffee and restaurants) 
--Service was top notch--I called the front with a request, and it was delivered within five minutes
--Rooms are small, but modern and VERY comfortable
--Park on the third floor...random but quaint touch!
Thank you, GP. I'll be back ASAP!

We - Girls came from FLORIDA to enjoy ALCATRAZ and CHINA TOWN and we just had a Wonderful Experience! We visited most of the bars we foudn around the Warf in walking distance and then found our way back to the Hotel. The Employees we very kind courteous and respectful of our needs and wants. They went out of their way to make this stay GREAT!! The trolley cars, taxis and boat rides were awesome and so close to everything near the Warf. The Restaurant and Bar in the hotel was just awesome as well!! Again very friendly and helpful employees all the way around. 
WE MISS BEING ON OUR VACATION TO SAN FRAN AND WE ARE PLANNING TO RETURN BY YEARS END AND WE ARE GOING BACK TO THIS SAME HOTEL, CAUSE THEY WERE JUST AWESOME TO US. THE ROOMS WERE CLEAN, LARGE AND AMENITIES PLENTIFUL. WE WILL BE BACK!! THANKS!!

This hotel has rude staff, dirty rooms and if your room faces the Peabody hotel, lots of noise all night.
We didn't seem to have to wait long for a lift but I would recommend parking on level - and walking up to level - as suggested in other reviews.
The hotel needs complete modernisation. The rooms are dark and feel unclean, quite disgusting.
On the plus side the location is good for all the Beale Street attractions.
Would I stay in this hotel again?? NO WAY.

Stayed here just one night for business. It's everything you's expect from Hilton. The room was spacious and comfortable and very wuiet. I stayed on the --th floor and no issues with elevators (very quick and always available). The business center was convenient for printing boarding pass for return trip. The front desk staff was friendly and professional. The bar was crowded on a Monday night, so it was hard to get the server's attention. The breakfast buffet was average. If you're here for the room, this is a good choice.

If you book on the Fitzpatrick Hotel site, you are actually making a pay-in-advance, very difficult to cancel reservation on an offshore site called Easy to Book. At the Fitzpatrick, your reservation will be listed as having been made through Expedia, but it doesn't end there. You can't cancel with Expedia. The reservation lives on Easy to book. Never heard of this? Neither had I. Took two hours and many, many phone calls to resolve. Not recommended.

Great location. Close to the subway and the white house. 
Rooms are TINY, cramped but clean. It's like the regular rooms were chopped into thirds.
It's great if you just plan to use it as a place to sleep and nothing else.
Security is good. Views are mixed, if any.
I'd stay again since I don't stay in the room much.
It's basically a crash pad and when your eyes are closed, who cares how small the room is. 
Price was right for the location. It's gotta be the closest to the white house of any hotels unless you want to pay BIG bucks.

This hotel is across from the Drake Hotel, just past Water Tower Place. The location is great if you want to be near the Gold Coast and shopping. We had an early arrival in Chicago and were very pleased by the friendly staff and the news that we could check into our room at -:-- a.m.!! That rarely happens, if at all. The hotel is an older hotel, but the rooms have been totally updated. The beds are extremely comfortable and have down blankets and very soft down pillows as well. There was a flat screen tv, a fridge and nice art work (photos of Chicago area) on the wall. The bathrooms were updated as well. We didn't get to check out the hotel bar area because a huge wedding party was occupying that area. I was afraid we wouldn't get much sleep because of the noise, but I didn't hear a thing all night. Maybe the staff has placed all the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""wedding party"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in some other area. The price we paid was around $---.-- (that included all the taxes) for a room with two queen beds. I find Chicago pricey overall, but I was splitting the room, so it came within budget. Staff is very helpful and nice!

I booked this hotel, strictly for its location at Easton. We booked one room, Saturday ---- for a bridal shower-bachellorette night. We chose the Hilton at Easton strictly because of it's location. Booked online through a third party site for $--- w-taxes. We were able to check in at -:--, which is an hour and a half early. Check in was extremely easy - no wait, staff was very nice.
Room: The room rate was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""special"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and was discounted because we stayed in an accessible room. As such, the room was huge! Plenty of room for three women to spread out all of our stuff, run multiple hair dryers, curling irons and straighteners at the same time. We had more than enough space for both a gift table and a food area. The carpet had some stains, one big ugly red one under neath the table. I would imagine this room hadn't been stayed in for a while - or the cleaning staff wasn't very thorough. First, there was hair on the tray, glasses and ice bucket. Second, there was a layer of dust on the shelving unit in the bathroom - including the two extra towels stored there. Once we removed the two towels you could see the outine from where the dust had settled around them. Because the room was wheelchair accessible - water ran out of the shower into the bathroom floor - but there was no extra drain - so it was quite hazzardous. Two bath mats, and all the extra towels still couldn't sop up all the water - and we were careful with the shower head. I've stayed in plenty of rooms like this before and never had it be this bad. Beds were comfortable, linens were clean. 
Location: You are clearly paying for location and name. The hotel sits on the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""outside"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of the Easton Town Center - so you can walk to plenty of shopping, dining and entertainment. This is the only reason we chose this hotel - and I was willing to pay for the location and feeling of safety by being only a few steps from our dinner and desert restaurants and all of our entertainment as opposed to other areas in Columbus.
This is a good hotel if you are going to be in the Easton area for an event. The hotel ballrooms and common areas are beautiful - but the rooms are a bit of a disappointment considering the rest of the hotel. Overall, if you have the extra $ to spend for a special event it's a good choice.

The Grand Hyatt was the location of our meeting and that's the main reason we stayed here. I really don't understand why this is called a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Grand"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Hyatt. It just seems like a very typical hotel - but very big. A number of reviewers have summed up the less-than-positive aspects. Room was comfortable, but small. We took a glance at the room service menu. A pot of coffee (with menu stating """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""serves one"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""") was $--.--! The math is simple - coffee for - is $--.--! This property is so big, it's hard to evaluate service - because you really don't interact with that many employees. I found the valet parking staff to be very helpful - but valet parking was > $-- a day.
We've stayed at the Marriott Rivercenter and Marriott Riverwalk on prior visits to San Antonio. They are immediately across the street from the Hyatt and Convention Center. And, we were much happier with our stays at those hotels. We won't be going back to the Grand Hyatt, because there's really nothing Grand about it.

We are staying here until Friday. This has been a wonderful experience! We were married here on Monday. It was to be just us until a few friends found out. The owner of the hotel and his staff went above and beyond to make this special for us. I could not have asked for a better day. This place has so much character and charm. I love it! I will admit I usually stay at the five star level. I would take the kindness of the owner and staff over any five star hotel. When I commented about the owner to one of the staff they shared with me how much the staff respects and cares for him. I was told he was the best to work for. How often do you here that? When I come back to Downtown LA I will only stay here.

First, the pros....the hotel is very modern and nicely furnished. Rooms, beds comfortable. Bathrooms are marble with rainhead shower. The cons.....we didn't care for the location. It was too busy. We prefer the --s on the east side because it is quiter, more residential and still in walking distance to the theatre. The biggest con was that there is a club on the second floor of the hotel and we heard the music from midnight until -am up on the --th floor. When you stay in the city for one night so that you don't have to drive home after a Broadway play, you want to go to sleep before -am. We should have just driven home. Very disappointed in our experience at this """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""luxury"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Kimpton hotel. Luxuryhotel and club music just don't go together. Kimpton should figure out which market it wants...the people who want to go clubbing or the people willing to drop $----$--- per night on a room.

My husband and I ended our California Adventure in the City by the Bay with a four night stay at the White Swan Inn. This quaint boutique hotel offers an excelled location that is convenient to the famous cable cars and public transit. Before leaving home, we purchased the City Pass which was an excellent deal giving us unlimited transportation and entrance into many of the city museums including Alcatraz. The room was quite large for a big city and well-appointed. Our room was on the -th floor and we did not experience any significant street noise. We certainly enjoyed the fireplace and having a mini refrigerator stocked with free soda and water was a nice touch! The room includes cable TV, WIFI, and a coffee maker. The bathroom is older and probably could use some updating. The elevator is vintage and contributes to the old world charm of the hotel, There is no air conditioning and although it was warm in SF, the night temperatures were cool so it was not problematic. The staff was friendly and welcoming. The breakfast offering were standard buffet items but plentiful and satisfying. The evening wine and snacks provided an opportunity to meet many diverse individuals from the USA allowing us to enjoy stimulating conversation about a variety of topics. The decor is decidedly English country which is warming and home-like. I feel that the hotel was reasonably priced and with the breakfast and wine reception a pretty good deal.

Here for -week, usually stay at Hilton Garden Inn - blocks away.
Check in was about a hour late & were to have corner suite, they gave us a standard room,went down to front desk and showed our copy of reservation for suite & price that was less, got corner room after another hour wait. All - elevators smell like urine entire stay, so did our rooms bathroom. Room was very spacious but decorated like something a cross out of the --s and The Jettsons. Upon checkout was build higher rate than told ,will now have to go to front desk and shoe them reserved rate. Make sure you bring a copy of reservation 
If you don't want to get screwed. No more stays here, Hilton owns both, sure hope Garden Inn hasn't went down in care like this place.

This Homewood Suites location is a nice enough hotel with a very nice, cozy lobby (see-through fireplace and comfy seating), helpful and friendly staff and lots of nearby dining options. However, the rooms felt...outdated? Hard to put a finger on it, really. I thought the king-sized bed was comfortable and that the room was quiet despite having neighboring rooms occupied and traffic in the hallway later in the evening, but perhaps the wallpaper was just a tad aged and the televisions needed an upgrade to flat panel. The range seemed a bit old, though I didn't actually use it, but the dishes were plentiful and barely worn.
The pool area was nice - several steps outside of the lobby to the gated pool area - but in late December, if there's water in an outdoor pool, it darn-well better be heated! It was icy cold, as if it had just been filled from a hose! The fitness center wasn't horribly cramped as another review stated, but with only - cardio machines (- elliptical and - treadmills - all Precor brand) and one weight machine, I can see where it might become a challenge to get your workout in during a busy season at the hotel. All in all, I'd recommend staying here, but know that the property will """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""feel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" a bit outdated, though the nice staff and the deals that seem to be frequent on the rooms if you look-ask, more than make up for that!

My girlfriend and I decided to go to San Francisco, and after some investigation into the matter, we settled upon the Kensington Park. We tend to stay at hotels that are fairly priced for their location, such as Bill's in Vegas. I'm not a fan of super splurging on hotels, but then again, I'm not going to save a few bucks if it puts us in a rather unpleasant area. After our stay, I have to say it is --.-% positive with only a few minor issues.
Located just off the main intersection of Powell and Post, Kensington Park is in a great location. If you're a fan of The Cheesecake Factory, as my girlfriend is, you will absolutely adore this area of town, as the restaurant is on top of a Macy's building no more than - minutes walk away. There are many other restaurants within that area, and there is little doubt that if you do not find anything within the immediate area, you can find something just a few blocks away. 
The hotel is also a few minutes walk from many posh boutiques, Chinatown, the Financial District, as well as the famous Cable Cars. Public transit is also very accessible from this location, with Geary and Market St within walking distance as well, and was a very good base of operations for the time we spent in San Francisco, as we were mainly focusing on the Northern areas of the city (Bay-Golden Gate Bridge, Golden Gate Park, Ocean Beach, Chinatown, Japantown, Legion of Honor, Fisherman's Wharf, and Alcatraz).
Getting to the hotel was a breeze. We simply (well, simply after finding the station) hopped on the BART, got off at Powell, and headed North to Post St. Due to the popularity of the area however, actually navigating Powell and making it up the hill with luggage in tow can be a bit of a challenge. I can't even begin to imagine the difficulties one would encounter should they have children along with them as well. It should also be noted that there are several homeless people along this route. However, they do not do anything that would cause a nuisance or disturb the peace.
Once we arrived at the hotel, we were greeted by a very luxurious, old school classy, dark coloured lobby, completed with a piano, and several comfortable couches. Once check in was completed, we went to our room which was furnished with your typical hotel items, minus a fridge and cooking implements. Most important of all, the room was clean, which is something that is of importance to most people. In terms of the bed, it's difficult to quantify the level of comfort, as this is a person to person thing. I will say that the bed is a bit on the soft side, which may or may not be to your liking.
Naturally, being in such a great city, we didn't spend much time in the hotel room, other than to sleep at night. Each time we came back, the rooms were tidied professionally, with any minor messes we made taken care of. The front desk staff were equally friendly and approachable, and were accommodating to the strange requests that I made of them. 
One final item of note is that light sleepers may want a room away from Post St, or perhaps consider a hotel not in this area at all. As luck would have it, Post is a one-way street, and just up the street is a San Francisco Fire Department depot, and because of our room, we could hear-see the trucks whiz by every single night. Despite being - floors up, there is still quite a lot of noise. Similarly, I'm guessing there is a Police Department or something in the area, as we heard those noises every night as well.
All this boils down to the bottom line: would I stay here again?
If the rating didn't quite spell it out for you, the answer is yes, assuming I'm doing stuff in this part of town, and I don't want to rent a car. Given the prices of all the other hotels in this area, Kensington Park offers one of the best combinations of location and price around.

I have chosen this hotel because of its location, as I need proximity to Grand Station and Grand Hyatt was sold out. We have stayed at this hotel many times, the staff are always friendly & helpful. The suites are spacious & very comfortable with a small kitchen, living room, & bedroom with bathroom. I did a LOT of research to find the cheapest lodging in San Francisco that I could while still being in a safe, convenient location. We recognized we'd have to give up some amenities, but figured we wouldn't spend much time in our hotel anyway. The Astoria Hotel fit the bill and we were not disappointed.
We booked on their website, which got us the cheapest rate I could find on a double room (- beds) with a private bathroom ($---nt). The room was clean, had a large closet and a good sized bathroom. I've stayed here a couple of times when in Phoenix on business, the hotel is very clean, staff is professional and friendly, breakfast is what you'd expect.. very good value for your money.

She always talked about how hard it was to get a room here and yada yada yada. Well we booked it and I actually looked forward to it. Can't recommend this place highly enough. If I go back to NY for my --th birthday, this will be the first place I look up.

The spare, contemporary decor contributed to the sense of cleanliness. We saw no evidence of bedbugs. The bed was very firm, with very fluffy pillows and a down comforter, and the room was very quiet; my wife says it was the best night's sleep she has had in weeks (all the walking we did may have contributed to that). The bathroom was ultra-modern, with black tile and a translucent window in the shower looking into the bed area which let natural light into the bathroom. The shower was large enough for a party! The wife says the lighting wasn't too good for makeup, but to me it seemed fine for shaving. The soaps, shampoos, and free snacks and (non-alcoholic) drinks provided were very high quality. There was no iron, but we didn't need one or ask if one was available. We ate breakfast in the hotel's restaurant and it was very good, though pricey. Right around the corner on Saturday afternoon there was a farmers' market, complete with musicians (ain't New York neat?). There is a large drugstore right across the street, but we were visiting our daughter and never had time to look for other restaurants in the immediate vicinity. We highly recommend Andaz and hope to return. One more thing - the door is the one with the seating area just inside, on the left. You'll see it through the glass. Peace!

This little hotel is one that stands huge on quality,service, and everything else that a visitor to New York would need.

We recently spent five nights here while on a business trip and would stay here again. The hotel is in the heart of Little Tokyo, which was a busy and interesting area to explore.
Our room was the standard size double that one usually finds. The bathroom had one of those electronic toilets with all the buttons. There was a hair dryer, ironing board, iron, small fridge, safe, large plasma television and DVD player. A large round, immovable table provided a work space and there were two desk-type chairs, as well as an armchair. There was a smaller round table and the double-wide night stand had a pull-out flat surface. There were plenty of outlets in convenient locations around the room. The free WI-FI worked well.
We were there during a recent heat wave and appreciate the air-conditioning in the room, however we discovered that housekeeping shut off the A-C each day. Not a big deal once we figured that out- we'd simply turn it back on.
The hotel has a gift shop which sells snacks (including dried squid!), sundries and souvenirs. There's a cafe on the lobby floor with different coffees, teas and light meals. Next to this are two terminals and a printer and a DVD-rental kiosk. 
Upstairs is the main restaurant. The breakfast buffet was quite pricey at $-- each, but the dinners were very reasonable and both the food and ambience were quite nice. We ate there one night and requested various substitutions and side dishes, all of which were accommodated. A light dinner for two was under $--. 
There was a karaoke bar, which looked like fun. Despite the cover charge, we were able to stand inside and watch for a bit without paying. 
There's a spa and laundry room, neither of which we tried.
Right around the corner is a walking street filled with Japanese restaurants, a grocery and shops. While we were there, there was a karaoke contest and a one-man band playing. We bought our breakfasts at the bakery and grocery store and took advantage of the room's small fridge. There is a pizza restaurant and a small shop with hot dogs, chicken nuggets, etc. for a break from Japanese food. Another block away is a public transport station.
Little Tokyo stretches out for several blocks around the hotel and this area was busy and felt quite safe. It did not seem safe beyond this area.

I had - pieces of luggage. It was dark and drizzling rain. There was no doorman at the door to greet guests. I managed to make my way through the front doors on the wings of - young men who were apparently entering to the lobby to join the free wine hour. Upon entry into the small and trendy-chic lobby, I heard the low key music apparently playing during the social hour-wine hour. While I would have enjoyed this atmosphere on a less stressful evening, I had just returned from a long day of meetings and wanted only to relax. I made my way to the front desk where I was greeted by a pleasant young woman. She checked me in quickly and informed me about the hosted wine hour going on at the time. The check in process was quick (thank goodness), and I proceeded to my room on the -th floor. I had purchased a Spa Room on Hotels.com. I was assigned room ---. The room was quaint, stylish and very comfortable. Although I was on the -th floor, I did not hear any street noise. I ordered room service both nights of my stay. I ordered the Frisee salad, fish tostadas, turkey burger and goat cheese pasta. ALL were surprisingly delicious. I ate way too much. 
The bedding is plush and very comfy. The decor is stylish and comforting and made me feel very at home. The room included a fairly spacious desk area with power outlets. The room also included a stylish grey couch. However, the flat screen T.V. could not be seen from the couch. The lights in the room were dimming lights. This feature is perfect to create calm surroundings.
The mini bar provides wine, water and snacks, although they are pricey. The room is equipped with the usual Kimptom robes. These are GREAT! It's very nice to not have to bring your robe from home - more room your luggage.

But the only thing that detracted from our stay was the street noise. I would stay here again, but I offer a word of caution about the potential for noise. When the bars close, it can be loud.

I live in Houston and I have travelled to hotels all around the world and I must admit that comparatively speaking, Granduca can really hold its own. My husband and I decided to spend our -nd wedding anniversary in Boston. Being that my husband had never been to Boston, and I haven't been in many years, we both had high expectations.  In terms of location, this hotel cannot be beat. It was right on the Freedom Trail, and convenient to the T. We walked most places, but if that is not for you, the hotel is happy to call a cab. Anyone we encountered seemed truly interested in our stay, and if there was anything they could do for us. I cannot recommend this hotel highly enough, and if we are ever back in Boston, I can guarantee we will stay here!

Thanks to the staff of the Benjamin Hotel ... I stayed at the Prescott last year and found the Club Level room comfortable but small. Enjoyed the Club Level amenities and the friendly staff as well as how easy it was to meet other guests during breakfast and cocktail hour. Last week, I was excited when told we had been upgraded to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""penthouse suite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" instead of the Club Level room we booked. I stayed here on opening night and it was great. The lobby and bar and spectacular and well appointed. I ate at Urban as well and it was quite good. Cost was competitive with the rest of the restaurants in the Domain. High-speed was super fast (although not free). Rooms had the heavenly bed and shower as expected. My wife and I just got back from staying at The Bowery Hotel, and it's an understatement to say that this hotel is incredible. I've never written a review for anything before (I figure there's enough people reviewing already), but this hotel and staff exceeded all expectations and certainly deserves the praise. Our room was amazing! I read other reviews about the floor to ceiling windows and thought """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""O.k., I'm sure they're nice"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", but wow, they really are awesome and make for spectacular views of the city. The tub was luxurious and was a daily treat for my wife after being dragged around NYC all day long by her husband. The bed was very, VERY, comfortable......seriously, you'll fall asleep just looking at it! The housekeeping staff must have been magicians, I never saw them but everytime I left my room and returned shortly thereafter.....Bam! Clean room! After this hotel experience coupled with all the shops, restaurants, and atmosphere in the villages nearby (SoHo, NoHo, Greenwich, etc.) as well as convenient access to the nearby subway stations (Bleeker St., Broadway-Lafayette, -nd Ave), Midtown hotels won't even be considered again!!
Congratulations to the staff and managers of The Bowery Hotel. Job superbly done! Thanks for the great experience!

We were visiting family close to this location so decided to try it over much nicer hotels in Seattle. The first morning of our stay water started pouring through the light fixture in the bathroom. We called the front desk who suggested that we take a key for a dirty room and use the shower there. I was told that they did not want to give us a key to a room with a clean shower because they would have to re-clean the room. When they finally agreed to allow us to use a clean shower they told us that they did not know when they would be able to fix our room. We were considering checking out when the manager told us that if we stayed the next night that we had reserved she would make sure that we would be taken care of. Although the room was cleaned when we returned, taking care of us was a $-- discount on the room which frankly was less than we tipped the maid. The front desk staff was disinterested and somewhat rude, parking was difficult to find and although they said that the hotell was newly remodeled it still looked like a run of the mill Ramada Inn. It's near a hospital and you will hear sirens all night long. Good luck if you stay here.

Stayed two weeknights to go to Henry Ford museum and room layout was great, queen bed and bathroom in loft for hubby and I, then murphy bed in curtained off dining room for teenage#- and sofa bed for teenager#-. TV up and down and kitchenette was handy, although not very well stocked. Room was quiet, bed was comfy. No welcome book to tell you breakfast buffet hours or pool hours, or nearby stuff. Breakfast was good, pool was fine, but hot tub was closed.
Do not use directions from their website, they end before you get there and it's not a neighborhood you want to get lost in or ask directions. I told girl that when we checked in and she agreed they were terrible, but no apologies, not too professional at desk until next morning. The guy that had to check us in was outside talking to his questionable looking buddies, which I had to walk through, nervously. He was just too casual. There was security on the property.
There was a Chili's restaurant, and Doubletree restaurant walking distance. Mall just across the freeway.

The room and the lobby were quite adequate. As many noted before, the elevators were very slow and non-responsive. The best feature was the pool and jacuzzi in the back of the property with a view of an overlooking hillside. Everything kept up great there by the staff (towels and cleanliness) and it added a nice tranquility. The item that put a bee under my bonnet, metaphorically and in old-timey phrasalogy), was the additional cost of parking there. $--. Besides Crowne Plaza down the road, I'm not aware of any other hotels in that area that tack on such an additional charge. There were quite a number of Asian guests there, which it probably didn't bother as much as me, since that is the norm in their countries, and is to be expected. Thank goodness for other tripadvisor reviewers that shared the secret to park on the street in front of the AM-PM gas station. But that is half a block away, and has only three spaces in front of it, and two of them are usually taken up by gypsy cab companies. And yes, I'd proudly cheap enough for this to rankle me. It's not as if the Hilton family is hurting, and Heaven knows I'd hate to deny any of the Hiltons their multi-million dollar bonuses at the end of the year.

The road noise was terrible here- I don't know if the windows are gto thin, or its the angel of the building in relation to the street, but I could hardly sleep during my three night stay. Also, there are thin white window shades but no curtains. This means that I had to put up with street lamp light coming into my romm all night. 
The wfi-fi was of better speed than most other hotels Ive stayed at. 
I would never stay here again.

Absolutely loved this place. The location and the views from the lakeside rooms are spectacular. Rooms are nice and unusual. I thought the sliding door to the bathroom was neat. It is modern with old world sophistication - best of everything. The lounge on the club floor is so inviting, I could have stayed there all day. But with the museums and Buckingham Fountain just outside the door, who can stay in their awesome room?

I spent - days-- nights at the Magnolia Hotel in Dallas and I have nothing bad to say! The driver was ready and waiting when we arrived in Dallas and took us right to the hotel. The front desk service was fantastic and so helpful. The room was clean and the bed was comfortable!! Housekeeping kept my room clean and was always prompt with requests. The food service was great, the cocktail hour was lovely and the milk and cookies at night made me feel like a kid again! The entire staff was friendly and I will most certainly be back!

We travel to San Antonio a few couple of times a year and always enjoy staying on the riverwalk to be near nightlife and dining. We have stayed at several hotels all around the river, but this was the first time for us to stay at this Hyatt Regency....though it is somewhere that has been on our “list” for quite some time. We feel that the Hyatt has the absolute best location smack in the middle of the riverwalk and across the street from the Alamo. 
Knowing San Antonio well, we knew that there were better options for parking. Knowing that the hotel does not have a self park option, and the fact that their valet is $-- per night, and self park across the street is $-- we choose to use the convenient city garage two blocks away (E Houston) for $- per -- hours. (No in and out though...but we rarely leave once on the river) 
The lobby is in great condition and the staff was very welcoming and appears to have been recently remodeled. We skipped the automated check in kiosks (Come On Hyatt....get rid of these stupid things....cool at Hyatt Place limited service, but of Place at Hyatt Regency and Grand) They assigned us a nicely remodeled King room on a high floor so we had no noise from city traffic, and kindly coordinated our friends being on nearby on the same floor. I heard that the rooms facing the interior of the atrium can be noisy so we requested city view. They also have nice river view rooms, but since they do not have balconies, we did not feel it was worth the extra money. 
We were here over New Years and never had any issues with noise, and appreciated them checking room keys New Years Eve night to ensure that only registered guests were permitted in. 
There is also a nice outdoor swimming pool and nice sized fitness center, though we did not use them as they under renovation while we were there, which we knew at the time we made our reservation. (there was an alternate fitness center set up, and you had access to the Grand Hyatt pool) The pictures of them look like they will be very nice. 
The ground level lobby is small but does have some comfortable seating. The elevators are speedy. The restaurant and bar is located on the main lobby floor and has a wonderful view of downtown the riverwalk from the bar. The main lobby level exits to the street. There is a lower lobby level with some shops, and a neat feature, that I remember as a kid....there is a (clorinated) river from the walkway to the Alamo,through the lower lobby, and out to the riverwalk. The lower lobby level exits directly to the river. 
As with most Hyatt’s, the breakfast was very well done and the staff was very friendly. Though there is usually a fee for the breakfast, our AAA rate included breakfast, and it was very enjoyable. I do not recall the exact price, but if was not included in the room rate, we might have checked out other options we know well on the riverwalk. Other than breakfast we did not eat at the hotel because we have so many favorite options in San Antonio, for both dining and cocktails. 
The room we had was a typical King room with a nice work desk, chair, and desk. The rooms have nice HDTV’s. The room also had a refrigerator in the cabinet. The AC blower can be left on for white noise. The rooms were spotless, smelled fresh and had nice pillows. (Both foam and feather). The curtains do an nice job of blocking out light, and the rooms have a nice view with the floor to ceiling windows. There is a fee for wifi (per device) so we did not connect in the room, but wifi downstairs is free. 
The bathroom was nice size, and well appointed with plenty of fluffy towels and nice bath products. 
New Years evening, a young person was laying in the hall outside a room banging on the door for about -- minutes. (not the hotel’s fault) When we called the front desk they had someone up there in less than - minutes and took care of the situation right away. A+! We also enjoyed laughing at the young man who was dancing up a storm in his atrium view room....fully entertaining everyone waiting for (and inside) the glass elevators.
All of the staff at the Hyatt was very welcoming and made for a pleasant stay! It was also a special part of the holidays for us, to get our annual dose of Christmas Lights on the riverwalk. 
The area has every type of dining and entertainment option you could ask for all within easy walking distance. We would absolutely recommend this location and would stay here again if the room rate was comparable too to other nearby options. We have stayed at a full range of -.- – -.- star hotels in the area, and this one is one of the best, but can get pricy, compared, to many, thus the reason we have never had the opportunity to stay here before. All of these are very nice options and similar in their offerings and the prices seem to vary wildly from day to day.

This hotel continues to be one of our very favorites! Rooms are ultra clean, the service is very very good & personable and the food & drink are excellent.
The workout facility is very nice & open ---- and the employees treat you like valued guests.
The Best!!!

We just returned from a five night stay. Our check in was a breeze. They were able to accomodate our oversized van right at the hotel. Location is great with a Trader Joe's around the corner, & Starbucks. Literally minutes from Michigan Ave., I would definitely stay again if I could get the same price I initially purchased from priceline. Thumbs up to the staff for making our trip so great.

My husband and I have stayed here twice for special occasions and both times were treated like royalty by the Willard staff. The entire staff from bellman to valet to front desk were helpful, friendly and professional. For a sublime visit to DC, the Willard is the place to stay.

Great location, right in the center of town, near restaurants, entertainment, historic areas and public trans. The hotel has a relationship with the Philadelphia Fitness Center next door. Fitness Center has anything you might want to work off those fantastic DiBruno's hoagies. Rooms are tired with stained carpet, broken cabinetry, and bathrooms from another era. We could hear every word the maids said as they chatted in the hallway. Our door did not close (or open) very well and part of the lock was broken. Not impressed.

All the rooms have a small fridge and microwave and there is access to a business center that has computer terminals and printers. I highly recommend this hotel as a GREAT place to stay in downtown Chicago.
Everything at this hotel made me say wow!!! I really enjoyed my stay and we plan to return soon...

We were greeted warmly as we pulled up in front of the hotel. The check-in was speedy. We were just in time for the fun wine reception. The art and decor is wonderful. The other guests were friendly and laid back, just like the staff. The location is great - near lots of stores, restaurants and Rittenhouse Park. The room was so nice we decided to get takeout for dinner and room service for breakfast. We didn't want to leave. It was everything the other reviewers said and more! We had a fabulous night in Philadelphia!!!

We were happy to stay at this Fairfield Inn because of its location and access to the interstates and downtown, and because of the King Suite. We have a toddler and needed the extra room.

We left early the following morning (-AM) an returned and -PM to find a dangerous ozone room-shock air freshener machine in the middle of the floor AND our room had not yet been serviced! It's very noisy, but when you stay next to an interstate you have to expect this. There are no decent restaurants or shopping nearby. Whole Foods is twenty minutes, and downtown is fifteen. A reasonable commute in Indianapolis.
They do have a security presence in the parking lot (thankfully - it's a rough area), so I felt our car was safe.
I really don't know if we will stay at this hotel again when there are so many other options.

My daughter and I just returned from a six night stay at the Omni Parker House, and our trip couldn't have been better! The staff, amenities, and location are all superb - I much prefer this location to any in the downtown area. Close to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""T"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", the North End, and an easy breakfast at Starbucks - we will definitely book another stay when we return to this amazing city. We stayed at the new W as we are Starwood fans and gold members and were in town to visit family. The front office staff was terrible. We waited over -- minutes for a room that was small and looked onto a parking lot and apparently that was a better room. The staff was unresponsive to my requests and it was certainly a terrible hotel and location with kids. I do not recommend.

We are a young couple who came for our honeymoon. After hearing that most rooms are pretty small, we asked to upgrade our room and got the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""superb room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", which was excellent, although the bed was only a quin size, without anymore charge. The room is very cool and well designed, the stuff is very nice and there is a party in the lobby every weekend (but in the room it's quite). We enjoyed our stay!

The front desk management was very cordial. The room quality was better than other contemporaries. Good service for the money charged. This hotel has a good location and the rooms are spacious but...it is loud! You can hear everything and it felt like every door in the hallway slammed closed...nonstop. The elevators can be slow and if no one is there to organize the crowd then forget it. Prepare to wait or take the stairs. The breakfast buffet was ok but very crowded.

The only bad thing is that the Internet was so slow at times (probably too many users at the same time) but still I think they should be able to foreseen that and try to fix it.
Another thing I don't like and most hotels do it is they have limited channels on the TV, I presume so you can buy a movie.
Another improvement they can make is to put a safe, I was worried some expensive items will be """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lost"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" or even important papers like passport.
Another more are the beds, they are so thin and do not give enough compfort and support to me..

The room was small and quite noisy and the clean service was not good and one day the room had not been cleaned at all without any reasons. Hopefully the staff agreed to reimburse a part of the price for this inconvenience.

The hotel is in a convenient situation for one of the Boston convention centres, and is linked to the city centre by subway. Our room was acceptable in size, and comfortable.
The outstanding fault was the fact that the hotel has no dining room, merely a breakfast bar from which one chooses from a list of sandwiches and other breakfast food, and then carries into the lobby (or one's bedroom) to eat. The system leads to queues, and is generally primitive.s

My only - complaints were that the concierge got us tickets to a broadway show and the price we had to pay was double the tickets value. I can't speak poorly enough about this hotel. It is not clean or nice to look at. They don't care what kind of room you book, they will give it away and put you in a different room without an apology or any compensation. They also will not call you back when you call asking for a manager and leave a voicemail. They're much too busy to try to make things right for one of their guests. And don't do the airport shuttle service unless you want to wait -- min to be picked up from the airport. You couldn't pay me enough to stay here again.

We held a business meeting at this hotel and found it very accommodating for our needs. It was clean and in good repair overall. Nothing really pops out about it but the Harbor View is a good one albeit a bit noisy in the early morning hours

We stayed - nights and was glad to have chosen this Marriott location. There are many choices, but we think this was probably the best one for us. Firstly, location - it is right on East Ontario and North Michigan which is a very convenient location. It is walking distance to Navy Pier, to buses and shopping on Michigan and many restaurants. The place was clean, had a mini-fridge and was quiet, With - kids, our - queen beds was perfect. It was a bit larger so there was a small sofa, coffee table and separate chair. It felt roomy.

The staff were friendly. We used the business center and printed some tickets for free. We used their laundry and the detergent was complimentary which was nice. One other downside was the parking which is $-- per day which is something that people will need to budget for. But that is the normal daily rate of having a car in Chicago.
Overall, very happy. It's not a - or - star hotel, but very comfortable for the price.
Tip for coffee drinkers - Duncan Donuts is close by which is another choice to the Starbucks down in the lobby.

The Hilton Universal City has a nice location but needs to be renovated. 
The rooms are boring and the interior needs an upgrade. The bed is way to soft: I couldn't sleep at all. Hilton Vienna has way better beds. You cannot open the windows and the air-con is unpleasant. The elevators are painstakingly slow. Staff did help but rushed your requests. 
The only reason to stay here would be the location in the hills and the nearby Universal Studios. It's only a five minute walk.

This was a nice hotel with great amenities ... awesome breakfasts with lots of fruit, eggs, potatoes, sausages, etc. They offer light evening meals too, which I can't review because we weren't around to eat them. They have a full kitchen and are close to a Whole Foods if you want to stock your refrigerator with healthy meals. The only reason I might not stay here again was that the windows don't open.My guess is that this is because they are right next to a cluster of freeways and are trying to minimize noise pollution, and I have to say they do a good job at that, but I feel claustrophobic if I can't get fresh air.

the envoy club suites was recommended to us by friends . on arriving, it was a terrible disappointment!! our one bedroom self contained suite, was rather old. the carpet stained, windows dirty. bath plug broken.thankfully, however, to their credit, they fixed us a plug when requested on the second day. the springs in the sofa bed, stuck into my daughter's back, giving a very uncomfortable first night. the cleaning maid was very accommodating and put an extra comfort on top to improve things a little. the bathroom and kitchen, though old, was clean.
i had booked a few months early, and specially requested a rollaway to be added for when my -- year old son arrived, and confirmed this several times with reservations., and also on arrival. to which, no-one ever said, they were subject to the day!! so, we found, that the night my son was to arrive, there was no rollaway available!!
i definitely would not recommend this hotel, unless you desperately need to be next door to the hospital. this part of town is not as pleasant as staying on the west side, especially upper west. true, you are not far from centre of town and the -- bus is close by to catch to and from lower manhattan. however, if you are looking for somewhere with a nicer view and surroundings or pleasant area to walk, don't book here.
This is a great hotel! Quaint, beautiful rooms, great staff, wonderful food - couldn't ask for more!

After reading some of the reviews I was afraid to stay there alone with my two kids. I was so happy to see how safe the hotel feels, we had a room by the pool, my kyds love the waffle spot, the room was basic, however it was clean. the front desk was great giving me directions to the zoo and sea world, it was great staying there, I'm sure we will return soon.

A very good hotel for the price, with comp breakfast and internet. Rooms very modern, flat screen TV, recently refurbished, extremely clean. Great central location minutes from Times Square, Macy's etc. But what made it stand out for us was the helpfulness of the staff. I'd recommend it!

The best part about this hotel is it's location. It is near everything! The lobby-check in area is very contempory, beautiful and clean. There is also a restaurant and bar across from the check in area. We didn't eat there, but appeared to be nice. There were always people there. Check in was easy and fairly quick. The staff was friendly.
Like others have said, the elevators are very small and a little slow, but there are - of them. Our room was extremely small. At times we had to squeeze past each other. There were just two of us in a room with - beds. What bothered me the most was the musty smell in my room ----. It was most pronounced each time we entered the room.  This is a decent place to stay. Again, not a - star hotel as they claim to be. They should be made to lower their rating. No basic amenities like real - star hotels. I would only stay here again, if I got a super low rate.

Service was exceptional. Conveniently located on cable car line and within walking distance to Chinatown, North Beach areas. Rooms are nice and comfortable. No noise problems. This hotel is nothing short of incredible. Amongst a lot of snobby hotels surrounded by tourist traffic, this hotel is the best location for people who enjoy luxury without the hubbub. An overly friendly staff, and an emphasis on service will make your stay a wonderful experience.

its very good location was perfect. we ad to walk only -- minutes and have been then in the middle of hollywood. also the metro station """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hollywood Highland"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was there. few fast food restaurants close to the hotel. the hotel byitself was nice and cosy decorated and with a very friendly staff at the reception. good breakfast buffet and there was also a small swimmingpool back on the hotel.

Booked through Priceline for substantially less than hotel website price. Front desk, valet and shuttle driver were all friendly and helpful. Stayed in an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""island"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room. We stayed at The Langham in Boston for two nights. It's a very nice hotel with a great location right in the centre of downtown Boston. We are just about to leave after a - night stay at The Fairmont. We booked it based on its reputation as one of San Fransisco's finest. We have travelled a lot and stayed in a lot of - and - star hotels and we have got to say that we were pretty disappointed. On the subject of walking, the hotel is at the top of Nob Hill and therefore high heels are a no no !! Check in was very swift and formal and if you wanted to know anything, it was a case of you got the right answer from the Concierge if you asked the right question and they seemed more keen for you to leave them alone and we were given some pretty duff info, for example we were sent to a nice breakfast place that was closed !!!! We drank the water in the room and were billed $-- for - small bottles so watch out - Walgreens is just down the road. No tea and coffee making faciliites and coffee in the room was $-- !!!! We also decided to visit the bar in the Tonga Room and were faced with a queue that we either couldnt jump as residents or book in advance as residents and when we wanted to go out , there was a very long taxi line. As we walked the corridorsof the hotel, there were plenty of glasses and room service trays lying about that the staff felt happy to ignore and spray air freshener instead. In summary, for a younger ( we are in our early --'s ) traveller, we would recommend somewhere more trendy maybe in Union Square or North Beach. While the room (though cluttered) served its purpose as a base of operations - it's located perfectly for the White House, Washington Monument et al - the service for which the US is famed is sadly lacking. Not the worst place I've ever stayed by a long way, but I'd go elsewhere just for a smile and some assistance from the reception staff.

Leaky faucet reported upon checkin yet it was never fixed and we were never given a status update, offered another room, or discount. Terrible. Breakfast was good but horribly unorganized. Our first stay at Hotel Commonwealth left something to be desired. I wrote an email to the manager explaining, and we were invited back for a second night. The staff, especially the front of the house manager Jeff, were extremely attentive and friendly. Everything we requested, from a fridge to an extended checkout, was given to us quickly, efficiently and with kindness and warmth.
 We have tried both adjoining restaurants, loved them both. Island creek has a great ambiance, Eastern Standards' brunch is very very good.
We truly enjoyed our stay. We will absoutely be back and we recommend this hotel for any kind of stay, business or pleasure.

Location is great, just like what others have mentioned here - short walk to the subway stations, Times Square, Macy's, Broadway theaters. We were on the --nd floor, king studio. Breakfast was a good plus, but i must admit, you get tired of the selection after a few days. (Not a biggie, because just a few steps away is a Tim Hortons.) We would come down to the breakfast area between - and -am, and we didn't experience any lines, and we always found a table. The elevators also cooperated with us, we didn't have to wait long for one to arrive. Had drinks one time at the lounge, and it was a nice, with friendly bartenders.

Before I start, you should know that I stay at Ritz Carlton properties whenever I travel. Rarely are there exceptions. However, over the past few years I have noticed something that those of you who travel a lot should keep in mind: The bar areas become absolute bedlam on the weekends! From Dallas to New Orleans and waaaaay beyond, it's a full-on see-and-be-seen nightclub scenario packed with [often] rif-raf running all over the lobbies...inebriated. The Ritz properties appear to sanction - and even encourage - the behavior because the alcohol sales are through the roof. But as we all know, you can't have it both ways. You're either an exclusive Ritz-Carlton property or you're a nightclub. You have to choose. But it's obvious Ritz has opted for both, hence the three stars. I will tell you that everything else about this property is wonderful: the food, the service the decor -- all of it is first class. In fact, Ritz Dallas has one of the nicest lobby bars of any property in the country. In the end, if you want peace and quiet, stay at the Mansion on Turtle Creek. Otherwise, the Ritz offers intense nightlife for those who prefer not to leave the property. Eventually the entire city of Dallas ends up there, anyway.

This is a funky old valley institution. We stay here when we come to visit family in the area. Quite reasonable. It's quiet and safe. One often sees a celeb having coffee in the cafe. Rooms are large and clean, beds comfy. The breakfasts are delicious, and the waitstaff who have been there forever, are competent, and very friendly.HOWEVER: The hotel can really use a brush-up: the rooms are old and tired: last time we stayed in a room which looked like a repository for all the old hotel furniture they could find: table, desk, TV console, nightstands and coffee service table were different, ugly, and superfluous. The front desk staff needs a lesson in welcoming returning guests: we've been coming for -- years. Hello?

My girlfriend and I stayed at the Doubletree from Friday to Sunday, March --th to --th and we had a great time exploring Philly and also at the hotel! I was worried that we would have a hard time at check in because our flight was delayed and we showed up at the hotel at --:-- pm, but the desk was friendly and we went up to our room on the --th floor. We were dubious at first because our room was the one right beside the - elevators, but there was minimal noise and we slept well the two nights. The view was very nice and the room was neat and had all the usual hotel amenitites. 
Service at the hotel bar was a little long on a Friday night, but the weekend breakfast buffet at the hotel restaurant, the Academy Café, was excellent. The pool is slightly small but still enjoyable, the air-jet spa and steam room was also very clean. Didn't use the exercise room but they seemed to be very well equipped with all kinds of weight, running, biking, rowing machines. 
Location of the hotel was great. Walking distance to the Phlash stops, taxis passed by the hotel all the time, and near the subway also. Taxiing around the sights from the hotel would cost between $ - to $ -. No hassles with the payment at the desk, friendly bellhops and handy luggage hold option for guests with later flights.
Finally, the event that made me rate this top service, when we arrived late on Friday night and checked in, we did not receive our two complimentary chocolate chip cookies which we had heard so much about. So we were disappointed about that but didn't press the point then because we were both tired from the flight. However, when checking out on Sunday we spoke with Tracy at the desk who was very nice and mentioned that they didn't have any there that morning but to go to the hotel restaurant and ask them to give us some. She also gave us each two coupons redeemable for cookies at any Doubletree hotel for future use (which would have been worthless to us because there are no Doubletrees in eastern Canada). We got the cookies from the restaurant upstairs, a little hard but very good, and went out to enjoy the St-Paddy's Day parade and the city. When we came back later in the afternoon to pick up our luggage for our flight out, we decided to try our luck and redeemed the cookie coupons at the desk and received four more warm cookies! That made our day.
I would recommend the Doubletree for the cost-concious traveller who wants to enjoy the sights of Philly, by foot, bus, subway, or taxi. I would definitely go back.

The concierge staff was wonderful, but most people at the front desk seemed like they did not really want to be there. The only thing we ate at the hotel was the Boston Cream Pie, since it was invented there, but it actually was not very good. 
The room itself was small, but not cramped. The AC unit in my room kept the room cool, but was very loud, which did make it a little difficult to sleep before I got used to it.

Very nice rooms. Awesome hot breakfast, with omelettes made to order. If you are a light sleeper like me, remember to ask for an inside room. Covered parking under the hotel.

Overall, it was just not the experience I had hoped for when paying that kind of price and I will never stay at the Park Central again.

No problem with elevators being busy and having to wait on them and we didn't have any noise problems from the street. The staff was very helpful in letting us have a late checkout time. This hotel is in an excellent location with the red line about one block down from hotel; restaurants (Joes is great) and grocery store close by; within walking distance to Michigan Avenue (you can go across the road to Nordstrom Department Store and go up to the first floor and out the front door and you're on Michigan Avenue or you can go a few yards down from the hotel and up some stairs to Michigan Avenue). A liesure walk to Navy Pier takes about -- - -- minutes. Our cab ride from Union Station to hotel cost about $-.-- plus tip. Thanks to the wonderful staff who may our stay a great one. We will definitely stay here again and tell our friends about this hotel.

I spent a night in this hotel and was very happy with it, the service is very professional, the rooms are nice and clean, wifi is for free if you become a member of the club, fireplace in the lobby is cozy, the room had a very modern feel to it with a great view of the Bay Bridge. We got a promotion, so they greeted us with a free champagne in the room. I'd definitely stay here again.

The River Inn is OK as a hotel while in DC. We flew in from the Marlowe Hotel in Boston [part of the Kimpton Group] and on balance wish we had stayed one of their hotels in Washington. The room at The River Inn was OK: the small kitchen gives a bit of flexibility but the room was a little tired and not the largest. The metro is a --- minute walk [not - mins as some have said] and we were a little disappointed by Foggy Bottom itself – not the trendy Bohemian district we had been led to believe. Given the busy roads it is not very pleasant to walk to Georgetown [although it’s well worth a visit] and it is a good ----- mins to the National Mall if you choose to walk it. Overall the hotel is OK but we are sure there are better choices out there in DC.

The hotel is overbooked: instead of King Non Smoking we got Double-double Smoking, and Double beds are small. The toilet was filthy dirty. Parking is paid and complicated - nobody bothered to inform us that first of all we need to sign up for an access code.

The Hilton Hotel in San Francisco Union Square is a nice hotel located close to the Union Square and the cable car end station.
The hotel offers clean, nice rooms and several restaurants with nice selections.
The service is good and friendly. Prices are high but justified based on the service and environment you get.

This is one of the nicest hotels I've stayed at in the U.S. My husband and I stayed here over the New Years holiday and we really enjoyed our stay. We got a very reasonable rate on the hotel website.
The rooms are absolutely stunning with fantastic amenities. The location cannot possibly be better. My husband actually started not feeling well during the trip and spent one whole day in the hotel room sleeping but it was the most comfortable room if you have to stay in it for -- hours!
The only thing that kept me from rating it with a --star is its staff. I've had numerous problems with them. The shoes that were sent to be shined didn't return at the requested time (not even within HOURS!). Newspapers weren't delivered as promised. There were other issues I had with them but I think I blocked it out of my head and can't remember any right now. 
Despite that, i'd still stay here on my next visit to Chicago.

Like everyone else we booked this through the reviews on tripadvisor, and it was a really nice hotel. Position was spot on, and even though it was busy a couple of nights, we never really saw anyone or heard any noise, it had that sort of cool calmness about it. We stayed - nights.

The rooms are pretty spacious, I opted to not have the river veiw and saved a $---pn, and I think it was a good move, as the River view rooms are quiet high, and we tended to be out most of the time. I think the side rooms are quieter, or they were for us.
Service was perfect, the people were great, nothing was too much trouble. We found a great breakfast diner, which was like something out of Happy Days, and a fraction of the cost of the hotel breakfasts (which were nice, but at $-- average were a tad expensive)
San Antonio was a real surprise, in the weather was perfect, and we never tired of the walks along and around the river. Having peeked in some of the other hotels, ours (whilst a litlle pricier) was worth it.
This hotel may have a - star rating, but it does not have - star service with the exception of Dwight at the concierge who was a big help to me.

Will, the valet, is the first impression of this beautiful hotel! He is such a positive & helpful guy, we were so excited to stay after he helped us! When we talked to him the next day he recognized us & suggested things we might do. We listened to his ideas & followed through on them. He was right! Will is definitely an asset to the InterContinental.

I stayed at the Grand Hyatt during the week of July --, ----. The room was great and was decorated with modern yet comfortable furnishings. The bathroom had this really funky looking vessell sink. The only thing was the sink was a bit shallow and I would splash water everywhere when using it.
The hotel location was right in the midst of some really great shopping and was within about a mile to a mile and a half to the water front. We walked to the waterfront a couple of times. It was a good and easy walk but be prepared for it to be chilly in the evening.
The only drawback to the stay was on our arrival, the bellman was a bit aggressive in trying to set expectations about how long it takes to get a taxi. My co-worker and I had just arrived and was trying to pay our taxi driver, get our stuff out of the car and figure out how much time we had before our first meeting. I assume that the bellman was trying to be helpful and set expectations but he didn't allow us to get out of the cab good before he began bombarding us with the drawbacks of the taxi situation in San Francisco.
We were guests of the hotel when a pretty major union was picketing. Though I support the picketers, I do have to commend the hotel lobby and bellman staff for how they tried to make the hotel guests feel safe, secure and avoid the picket as much as possible. On the day of the picket, they were all organized, in large numbers and escorted guests from the curb to the elevators. They definitely took extra care noting the inconvenience to the guests but remained calm and in control.
I would definitely stay there again and would recommend this hotel. Good price and service.

Rooms are great! Housekeeping has many OCD personnel as all our cords were neatly wrapped & tied every day. Our things on the sink area were placed orderly on a washcloth for cleanliness & our things in the shower were lined up neatly on the ledge. The tub was a small swimming pool! Ha-ha! My shorter adult daughter was not allowed to go in without a lifeguard. Within several minutes walking to many sights & amenities. Florentine restaurant on site, with Iron Chef Todd Stein, has food to die for! Friendly and helpful staff at all times.

We stayed in this hotel the weekend of October --th. We were in town for a wedding at Union Station. We did not notice it was a Kimpton Hotel, but had stayed at a Kimpton hotel July -th weekend in Chicago. The Hotel George, was clean, modern, staff was helpful and efficient. The room was very nice (no view from -nd floor). The bathroom was quite large and well appointed. Could not fault the room for the three of us. Very large room with - double beds - very comfortable, firm mattress with a build-in topper. Didn't like the $- charge for the water. Tea-coffee making facilities and microwave.

Just returned from San Fransico. Argonaut stay was great! Location was great. Service was excellent. The hotel provides Aveda soaps, shampoo and conditioner. Very nice. Leaves a great aromal in the room. Entering the room was alway a nice treat. The room size was nice as well. I would stay at Argonaut again. Definately learned to ask if hotel is union and if so are they in negotiation process.

We stay here for business. The staff is always very professional, super friendly and efficient with wake up calls, letting us know the best restaurants and of course their restaurant is delicious. One of my favorite layovers!

My wife and I stayed at the Westin Michigan Ave. in December ----. As others have noted the location is outstanding. Across the street from the Hancock Bldg, and very close to all the outstanding shopping on Michigan Ave. The hotel itself is just average, the front desk staff was not overly friendly, but many of the other service staff were very accomodating. Although we are SPG members we were given the choice of only two rooms, a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""non-smoking"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room that was a complete smoke box, and a tiny --th floor room directly behind the elevator, which was incredibly noisy throughout the night. I stayed at this hotel, after trying - other hotels closer to the Greenbelt- College Park area. I must say, this was quite a pleasant experience. First off, they are renovating - or - floors and tell you this upon check-in. I heard not a peep but it was the end of the week so maybe they weren't working. The room was clean and in good condition, the beds were very comfortable w- extra pillows and the bathroom was clean and no mildew smell, a pet peeve of mine. This may make sense as I don't really understand the Marriott hotel line up and where each property is positioned. Is this supposed to be a little less expensive and nice than the Marriott or J.W. line? No matter, this hotel was easy to like.

Other than the waterpark, there is nothing special about this hotel. I have stayed at better hotels for less money. The staff was mediocre and unfriendly. The bathroom had issues. When taking a shower, the water turned cold for a couple of minutes, most likely due to another room's facilities being used. We purchased the Carribean Cove Waterpark package. For what the package costs, it claims that children eat free, but the caveat is that an adult must purchase an entree, so even at the Calypso Cafe inside the waterpark, you cannot get the kids meal free without ordering something yourself. Again, the food was nothing special and was overpriced. For the price of this package, you would at least expect a complimentary continental breakfast, but that is not the case.
