This hotel was a great find for us. We arrived early and were told that we had been upgraded to a parlor suite and that the room was ready. Our luggage was taken straight to the room and the porter came in and showed me where everything was at in the room and made sure I knew how to operate everything. The front desk staff was very friendly and very helpful. This is where I will stay whenever I can get to Seattle.

Stayed here one night for business. The location can't be beat, and the sky walk access to the Prudential Center and the shopping mall is great (especially when it's cold outside). That said the hotel needs a little sprucing up. There were signs of wear and tear in my room. The bed was quite heavenly, but the shower was nothing special. The bathroom was small but functional. The room could have been cleaned better too -- I found random hairs in the very white tub and mildew on the shower curtain. The gym is adequate, and there is an indoor pool, which I didn't use. Overall, the Westin is okay, but certainly not outstanding. I would consider another hotel the next time I'm in Boston.

Chose the Sofitel for a romantic getaway in NYC. Upon arriving, we were greeted by very friendly staff and the lobby area was decorated beautifully with tons of roses. This was a few days after Valentines day so I assume it doesn't always look like this but it was pretty impressive for sure. We arrived at the hotel around --:--am which was well before check-in time and they were able to accommodate us with a room right away. The room was very nicely appointed and the bathroom was beautiful. We didn't spend a ton of time in the room since we were out enjoying the city, but I couldn't have picked a nicer place for a romantic getaway. The only disappointing part was that we returned to the hotel around --:-- after our Broadway show and the hotel bar was closing and it was last call. No big deal though, just ordered some drinks and took them to our room. I will definitely be back again on my next trip to NYC.

We stayed in a suite at the Hampton for two nights at a fantastic weekend rate. Ir was very roomy and well-furnished. The living room had a sofa, coffee table, and flat-screen TV. There was an eating bar between the living room and kitchen area. There was no safe in the room, but safe-deposit boxes were available at reception for no extra charge.
The kitchen contained a full-size fridge, microwave, --burner stove and dishwasher, along with the necessary plates, utensils and cookware. The bedroom also had a TV, and an extremely comfortable king-size bed.
The bathroom was large and there was an ample supply of soft towels and toiletries.
The complimentary buffet breakfast included six! dry cereals, fresh fruit and several hot dishes, in addition to the usual pastries, breads and condiments.
The location is ideal if you're visiting the Tech Center, but is not near any points of interest or major shopping areas. There is a large supermarket in the vicinity, however.
We had some special needs, and the staff went out of their way to be helpful to us. They couldn't have been nicer.

Clean spacious rooms which were big enough to accommodate the four of us. The beds were really comfortable and the pillows were the best feather pillows I have ever slept on. Easy Walk to restaurants, shopping and attractions. Would definitely stay here again.

Originally I accidentally made our reservations on-line for a day before we were supposed to arrive. Called the front desk, and Lucas was very sweet and changed it with no problems. He was at the front desk when we arrived, greeted us by our name, and we were expeditiously checked in and in our room in minutes. No waiting, no hassle. The lobby has fireplaces and is very comfortably decorated. It was so relaxing, I wanted to sit in the 
Lobby-lounge area and listen to music and read instead of going out in the biting cold. Our room was beautifully decorated like a romantic boutique hotel, and immaculately clean. The continental breakfast was great. Healthy choices & great coffee. Staff attentive to everyone's needs. Freddy, the concierge helped me find a bagel & lox place Sunday as my husband was craving lox. We will definately be coming back. We love Broadway, and this hotel is perfectly located!

My wife and I visited the Houstonian this past Labor Day weekend. We very much enjoyed our stay in the hotel and use of the amenities (Pools-Gym). My wife found the room to be cozy and comfortable. The rooms are kept very clean and the staff comes through twice daily, with an evening turn down service. 
The location was also perfect for our trip to Houston. The Galleria was only a mile away and access to the paths at memorial park was right up the street.
Overall, I would recommend this to anyone traveling for both business or pleasure. I think families would really enjoy taking advantage of the - pools and water slide.
We had a last minute rate...-- for - night before return to Venezuela. Great location! Clean and Large room. No breakfast

My partner and I were on a - week tour of the West Coast of America and started in San Francisco. We wanted a hotel that was central to everything, as well as having a comfortable and relaxed stay. 
We were not disapointed, the hotel has some of the most helpful staff I have ever come across, the conceirge gave us many helpful tips as this was our first visit to the city and we weren't always sure where to go.
The room was a little tired but still very plush, as well as being very clean.
The hotel is also within walking distance from the popular Fishermans Wharf and Union Square is just around the corner.
The only downside was that the bar and restaurant weren't very busy and was quite expensive - but for us this didn't matter as there were plenty of other places to go nearby.

I stayed here on business for - nights. The Hyatt Regency's location is really convenient to the Muni-Bart-streetcars and also the ferries at the terminal across the street. Because it is right on Justin Herman plaza, there are really outstanding views of the bay and the Bay Bridge. If you walk along the Embarcadero there are also many other great views of the city. There are lots of places nearby to get great food (especially the Ferry Terminal) so it is easy to go out and grab a quick bite if you are on the run. Also, Fisherman's wharf is not far, as well as the SF MOMA. 
It is not cheap, but most similarly rated hotels are about the same price (or more expensive), and if your expenses are covered this will not be as much of an issue. Because of this, splurging on the internet access fee ( $-- for -- hrs) did not feel so bad. I also did not use the valet parking (which seems to be a downside for many folks) but the location made a car unnecessary.
The building is older and made of concrete, so the structure can seem a little cold. However, the central atrium decorated with lights make up for it, along with the glass elevators. After having stayed at so many generic hotels, it was a treat to ooh and ahh a little. Also, because of the layout and shape of the building, the rooms are a little strangely arranged. However, this is not bad-- it turned out that the room I was given was larger than normal, where it had a separate hallway or foyer, and being able to spread out was really nice. The other upside of an older hotel made of concrete is that you didn't hear any noise from the other rooms or the hallway, which was a rare treat. The bed was super comfortable so in combination with the quietness it made for a great night of sleep. I was on the -th floor facing the bay, so noise from traffic was negligible, but it seems like it is an issue for other folks.
The decor is tastefully done and very modern along with the furniture, and the room was very clean. The toiletries in the room even included toothpaste. True, there are some things that are a little outdated, like the faucet fixtures and the thermostat, but these are not things that really make a big difference. Because of the layout, the bathroom contains only the toilet and shower and is small, but I didn't mind this much, as the sink is outside the room and has a large counter.
My experience with service was outstanding--they were really polite at check-in and check-out and very efficient. They verbally verified the charges for me before charging me, which was nice. Afterwards, they even pointed me towards the printer where you can print out a boarding pass. I also used the web check-in before I arrived at the hotel--at first it wouldn't let me check in but after a few tries it worked. 
Overall, it was a really pleasant stay. I definitely will return!

It is a beautifull hotel with excellent location!
Personal is very kind and I want to specially distinguiss the service provided by Mr Nicholas Baez.
I had a problem with a package being delivered late (I had already left) and in five minutes over the phone he got the packages, prepared everything and sent them to my next destination!
I really appreciate this good service which is not usual to get.

As every other reviewer has pointed out, this hotel is in a prime location in the Gold Coast. You can walk to Michigan Ave plus the surrounding area and find a wide variety of shopping and restaurants.
Speaking of restaurants, the Hilton restaurant is closed for remodeling. They claim the new restaurant will open sometime in later November. You may wish to check with the hotel on that status if this is important to you. Since the restaurant was closed, so was the bar in the hotel. Next door is a Sushi place (looked and smelled great) the lobby has a coffee shop that is still open. There is also a temp breakfast location on second floor but I did not visit it.
I've stayed here many times in the past. This hotel can sometimes be a better value than similar hotels in the area. However there are some issues I noticed this time around. I stayed on floor -- and could not get a stable wireless network connection. After paying --.-- for wireless I called down to the desk and they said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""we'll look into that for you"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" The charge did not show up on my bill.
Secondly the standard room I was in was looking rather worn. Definitely a - star accommodation.
The thermostat is not accurate, even setting the room temp to -- degrees I was very cold.
I seem to remember larger and cleaner rooms on my last few stays back in ----.
So over all this is an acceptable hotel (except for the non existent wireless connectivity on higher floor) but would not wish to stay for an extended period. I will mention that I would prefer the Hilton Suites to the Millennium Knickerbocker around the corner if that helps you.

We stayed here for two nights on our return trip from San Francisco. Our room was a Studio King with a Sofa (pull out bed). The room was very nicely decorated, comfortable, and well appointed. The room had a full kitchen with a full-size refrigerator, small dishwasher, microwave, two burner stove, and sink with a garbage disposal. The kitchen was well stock with everything you could need to make a meal. The room had a nice size desk with a rolling chair. There was a full-size couch with a large flat screen tv and a small leather ottoman. There was a large comfortable king size bed with lots of pillows! The pull out bed was comfortable for the kids and myself, but my husband said that he could feel the bars when he laid on it. The bathroom was wonderful for a family. The sink was separate from the toliet and shower, so someone could still brush their teeth even if someone else was taking a shower. Also the shower was a very large walk in shower! The enitre hotel was nicely decorated and very new up-to-date decor! It has a cute little bar with plently of places to lounge, including outside by the pool and a full size pool table. The pool was heated and very nice, they even had some intertubes in the pool! The breakfast that was included was amazing! There was a hot made to order omelete station! There was plenty of fresh fruit, variety of bread for toast, nice variety of cold cereal, eggs, hasbrowns, pancakes... lots to chose from and starbucks coffee. The hotel is also located within a newly built shopping center which included Target, Panera Bread, Panda Express, Five Guys, Sweet Tomatoes and other restaurants all with in walking distance! This is a wonderful hotel and we will stay here again!

My husband and I stayed for five days in mid-October. We had a large room overlooking the Delaware River (and I---). Despite the proximity to the freeway, it was quiet, although I could hear muffled truck sounds early in the morning. We had a fireplace and jacuzzi tub. Much too warm for the fireplace but we used the tub once. Very nice upgraded bathroom and the queen bed comfortable. I didn't see the smaller rooms, but if we stay here again we would opt for one to save money. Clean rooms, helpful staff, although there was usually one person only at the small reception desk. If she (or he) was on the phone with a complicated reservation, whoever was standing there had to wait. We did not experience that problem, but I noticed others did as we passed thru the lobby. One large group came in on Friday night but there were two staffers then. About half the group cheerily went to the bar for a drink while the others got their room assignments. If you are expecting this hotel to have bell hops, room service, a game room and a pool, it is not the place for you. There is a decent workout room. The ice, sodas and candy machine are on the second floor. I must say breakfast was organized and fresh in a beautiful room. Dinner in the restaurant was worth the price. The wait staff was helpful with wine selections and food choices. Only one vegetarian option (they should work on that) so we just ate there once. The wine bar was amazing. Hotel is close to the historic area. We did not rent a car so walked everywhere and felt safe, even at night.

Very nice hotel, very friendly staff, great value for money $-- per night! Minutes walk from the glitz and glamour of Rodeo Drive & Other Bevely Hills attractions, - mins drive from The Strip! What more can you ask for?

Fantastic position, over the road from subway system, ----- mins walk to Top of the Rock, Times Square, Broadway, Empire State building, etc, etc. Reception and Concierge staff very friendly and helpful, and the beds (stayed on two occasions) are the most comfortable I've ever slept in!

My wife, daughter & I stayed there recently for three nights. While the hotel is not exactly what you'd call a charmer, the rooms were very nice, the nearby restaurants in the hotel circle are top-notch (we had a dinner at the hotel's Cafe Japengo, and it was not only super-stylish but the food was fine, whether salmon teriyaki or assorted sushi rolls), and the service was very good for the most part.
A few criticisms: the parking lot requires a bit of an outside walk to get back to the hotel, and at $---day, it's not too reasonable. The bed looked great, but wasn't particularly comfortable to sleep in. And the Barcino breakfast restaurant is located in a cavernous space in the lower lobby, which makes it feel drafty no matter what; the food there was quite good, but the service was rather slow and a bit disinterested.
Pluses: the front desk service was great -- friendly, quick, and helpful. The valets out front and the parking staff were especially helpful. And finally, I discovered this place through a deal I had not been familiar with on Travelocity: their Top Secret Hotels deal. Through it, you can get super discounts on various hotels; the only thing is, you only get a description and a vague location -- you have to reserve your room before you find out exactly where you're staying. I took a chance on this """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""--star hotel in La Jolla for $---night"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and wound up at the Hyatt. All in all, a great deal, despite a few quibbles.

Great location: Blocks from Time Square (close enough yet far enough), Right by empire state building and right on - main subway lines to get anywhere fast (Subway entrance literally less than -- ft from front door). 
Great Service: Very helpful and friendly employees (especially at the front desk and at restaurant).
Very clean and well kept up rooms with great views (Mine window framed the empire state building).

Basic accommodation for the price, i believe that the tourist tax on accommodation in San Fran is high so prices are elevated (ie, you get less for your money) the room was ok, a litle aged looking, the bolster cushions i immediatley removed from the beds - grubby! The staff we met were great, very informative and friendly. The breakfast was basic. Car parking available, andspace on the street if needed.

We have been to San Antonio a few times and like the river walk for walking and shopping , but there is so much more to the city than this. We stayed at the Pear Tree Inn for one night prior to an early morning flight. The room was clean and fairly sparse, but the location was exactly what we wanted. In cojunction with several other hotels, they run a shuttle to the airport starting at -:-- AM. Coffee is available in the lobby -- hours a day, so if you need a cuppa at anytime, it's there. My girlfriend and I, along with two of our friends stayed at the Ritz Carlton Battery Park December --, ---- over our college winter break.

This hotel even though it states that it is a Plush hotel left us disappointed. Nothing special about rooms. Our two bedroom suite had an awkward floor plan. For $--- a night you should at least get expeesso in your room. We got nothing. not worth the price.

Too bad I didn't bring my swimsuit to take advantage of the pool and hot tub up at the top of the hotel too!

Absolutely fantastic hotel, went there for Christmas and new year a couple of years ago. Staff are so friendly and polite. Hotel was spotless and rooms were amazing , like our own apartment. Would definitely recommend it!

My husband and I stayed in a room where the bathroom floor completely covered with hair! The shower walls were had mildew stains and the carpet was awful. We stayed at this establishment in September, we are not new to the Crowne Plaza brand and have stayed worldwide in their hotels and are platinum priority members. Unfortuately this one just doesn't meet the standard of a Crowne Plaza and is similar to a budget hotel but charging top dollar.
The plus point is the location it is perfect, right bang in the middle of Times Square and should have everything going for it - the sad part is the hotel, management and staff let it down big style. Our rooms were Conceirge Class and they were no different to a normal room elsewhere, so god knows what their standard rooms are like. On check out I let my concerns be know and was told this was helpful as they want to become once again one of the best hotels in Manhattan - I would say they have a lot work ahead of them and a long way to travel before this dream becomes a reality!!

We stayed at the hotel because of the location and the great rate. Everyone that we had contact was very friendly and helpful. The room was tired and a bit grubby and it was noisy both nights we stayed there. If you stay here make sure they give you a room on the first or second floor. The area this hotel is in isn't very nice either. San Francisco is a great place and if i return i would stay in a hotel in Fishermans Wharf which is near everything.

I had never heard of this hotel before, but in a crunch needed to find something fast. The driver for the car service I use when I come to NYC said this was a good hotel. New York is renowned for small, tired and outdated rooms at high prices in well known global chains. The Andaz is not well known, and in fact many drivers do not know how to get you there. It is a welcome change to the high volume global chains, and despite being a boutique part of the Hyatt Chain, the experience is incredibly different to that at the standard Hyatts, including its big brother at Grand Central in NY.
The rooms are new, spacious, and very very cool. It makes staying in the room a pleasurable experience, from the unlimited snacks-soft drinks, to the massive shower, to the fancy lights, the very comfortable bed and so forth. The food here is fantastic whether its room service, the restaurant in the lobby, or the cool cavernous tapas style bar-restaurant in the basement. The staff are great here, though there are still some teething problems with technology.
The price is often comparable to other chains, potentially a little bit more but I'd pay that everytime.
Inefficient service, no vegetarian choices on menu.

Upon being ok'd & finding out that we were staying at the Hotel Solamar (had never heard of it before), I was elated to do some research and find that it had been very highly reviewed on TripAdvisor.

Great location in San Francisco. Close to union square, the great shops, and excellent restaurants. The hotel reminds me of the Delano in Miami. Very trendy and with modern flow. I regularly stay at Park Central. The hotel is extremely comfortable, the staff is very accomodating and I would highly recommend it to others. It is centrally located and convenient for all locations.

Stayed here for a night Feb --, the hotel was clean and well staffed. Breakfast was great with a lot of people helping out. Nice bar in the lobby, great bartenders. We asked for a quite room and got it.

My husband, daughter and I had stayed here many years ago, so on a trip to Denver we decided to check it out. The location was great and the staff was friendly. The rooms were dated and not as well maintained as we had hoped. We will try another hotel on our future trips.
This hotel took my breath away when I walked into the entrance. Rooms was very clean with an amazing view.

Stayed for four days in August with our two girls, age - and -. Room was cramped but reading reviews should have asked for a larger room. Very clean, quiet and nicely updated, we would definitely stay again both for the hotel, the exceptionally friendly staff and the neighbourhood. Went for runs in Central park, had breakfast at nearby diners for very reasonable prices.

The Layne Hotel was adequate as a place to stay the night, but hardly enticing. I stayed four nights and was not at all sorry to leave.

If you have large dimensions or large luggage you might have trouble fitting through the elevator door. Small children definitely need physical restraining during the ride as serious injury is possible if you stick your hand through the bars. I wouldn't stay in the hotel with a small child just on principle.
The narrow spiral staircase was not a great alternative to the elevator.
And what is it with hotels and bedsheets? I like the sheet to cover the mattress and firmly tuck in, not to have an inch of mattress exposed at the bottom of the bed where my toes will touch it. Now, all mattresses at all hotels are not cleaned very often, but who wants to touch the same spot that other, perhaps unwashed feet have spent hundreds of nights touching? Yuck! Attempting repair of the sheet tucking revealed that the sheet was not long enough to tuck in both at the top and the bottom, so you have to choose one or the other. Also, the top sheet was tucked in so tightly and so far on the sides that pulling it out halfway dislodged the bottom sheet, too.
The bed also had a bonus spring sticking out of it which I was able to avoid as I was its only occupant. But the two deep body impressions made the night a somewhat bumpy and leaning """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""travelling"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" experience.
There is no air conditioning. Opening the unscreened window did cool the room, but once I was assaulted by cigar smoke and had to close the window right away.
Directly across from the hotel is a massage parlor and within one block are three more. I know for sure that at least one of these has a rather liberal definition of masseuse (that is, prostitute).
The front door is always locked and you have to be buzzed in every time you wish to enter. The staff was friendly and helpful.
There was only a single garbage can in the room (in the bathroom), no facial tissues so blow your nose on toilet paper, and no clock on the nightstand, although they do offer wake-up calls.
Pluses which I didn't really care about were a refrigerator and microwave.
For the price, the room was adequate, and I am not telling you not to stay there, as nothing was so bad that I couldn't deal with it. But when you stay at a --star hotel, you get --star accomodations.

So, for starters, this is a really interesting building to stay in. It's an old bank that they have converted, and it's been done well, with the exception of the entrance area, where a lot of the old teller counters have been left (you can't walk up to them though) and they look scruffy. The check-in area is off to the side of that, and is nice enough, but I feel they could have done more.
The rooms are all excellent though. Because it's converted from a different business, the rooms tend to be interesting configurations (I've not stayed in - rooms alike yet), though they are all spacious and useable. There is a fitness centre (actually just a room) that only really has cardio equipment. It really isn't well equipped, and while they have arrangements for you to be able to use a nearby gym for free, they clearly have the space in the building for a decent fitness centre, and I've marked them down a little for that.
I also mark them down a little for the fact that the staff just aren't that friendly. They all seem like they are just going through the motions.

This time, however, it came back wet, but with bits of dirt inside and outside. As we were heading out, we dropped them off at reception, and they sorted them quite quickly, but quite shocking to have had it happen in the first place. Would have been really upset if my baby ended up sick.

A-C does not work. Fridge does not work. Carpet dirty. No vending where the map shows. Called the front desk to complain no one answered the phone. Unused cars covered in the parking lot. Great hotel, wonderful amenities, restaurant & bar. Will visit again!

Otherwise, just steps to cable cars, trolleys, BART, so about as convenient as it gets. Even so, next time I will trade being in the center of a whirlpool of businessmen for a less convenient spot that offers a rhythm other than full speed.

I loved this hotel. Perfectly appointed room and bath. It is a charming place that you either love or hate at once.

I stayed at this hotel for two nights in December after a Carribean cruise. A reward after my retirement after -- years as a Police officer.

On being confronted with this she changed her tact by stating that i had got what had been ordered by my travel agent. Basically she put the blame on them. 
I stated that the room was not suitable, confirmed to her that it was a single room and a double room had been booked. She checked the system and stated that a twin room was available for an extra $-- per night. I reluctantly accepted this offer.
I returned to my partner who was still in the single room. Outside was what turned out to be one of the senior bell boys. I asked him what type of room i had been given. He could see my partner. He would not say what type of room it was.
On returning to the UK i spoke to my travel rep, who along with a New York agent confirmed a double room had been booked. Despite being contacted several times the Hotel have refused to reply. To me that says it all.
I can only assume that this was an attempt to extract more money from their visitors by the Hotel. In fact they only got $-- extra off me for the two nights as i made my feelings known to the staff who said i could have the room for £-- per night extra.

My travel agent has refunded my extra outlay at this hotel as gesture of good will.

Stayed here with family overnight for a weekend in the city. Chose location because most of the touring, shopping and theater we wanted was nearby and easy walks. Hotel -- offers everything you need for a visit to New York. I stayed for five nights in January, my first ever visit to New York and I did not expect to find such great hotel in such a superb location for the price paid.

We had a fantastic first trip to New York and we will recommend this hotel to all of our friends and hopefully visit again soon!!

A nice hotel for a meeting, but a bit to big and not very friendly. The swimming pool was closed for - out of our - days and this was one of the main reasons we chose the hotel. The iron, ironing board, hair dryer, extra blanket and pillows were in the closet. The bed was comfortable. The wake up call was a personal call and the staff was courteous on the phone. You may want to order a fridge for your room if you stay more than a couple days. A nice touch is that the hotel windows open for the late summer breezes. Window opened easily and closed securely.
There were two concerns. One, the in room TV was not receiving satellite (or cable) signal in the evening for CBS, ABC or PBS. NBC signal was received appropriately, and PBS received signal in the very early morning.The other, the cold water knob for the sink shut, but kept spinning after the water turned off. On street, free overnight parking is located around the side streets of the Hotel and saved the $---day parking fee. By -:--pm, I was hungry, the food was filling, and the menu items were appropriately prepared as gluten free. While the menu prices were about -.- times what other Midwestern premium hotel restaurants would charge, I tipped at a --% rate. 
Tired of paying high prices for so-so pseudo gourmet food? There is a large Whole Foods --- mile from this Hyatt, the Sheraton and Hilton hotels with a deluxe hot breakfast and hot foods bar and plentiful cold salad bar. Sandwiches are available made to order. Excellent quality, upscale meals featuring local flavors at grocery store pricing.
The major chain hotels, including this Hyatt, are located along La Jolla drive, but you need a car to get to the shopping area where the upscale, luxury retailers are located. La Jolla is somewhat close to other key points like the Torrey Pines Golf Course, Del Mar and Carlstad. The highways are free of advertising billboards, street lines are well marked and reflectors are embedded within the street to alert you. 
The vehicle attendants at the Hotel entry were very accommodating, even though I was not driving a super luxury car. Front Desk staff is best resource for directions and local information.

This hotel has the best location if you want to be in the middle of all of the action. We went there for a friend's birthday celebration and spent a large amount of our time nearby on -th street. I was very impressed with the condition of the hotel- it was very clean and nice!

All in all a great value for what you get as long as you understand that if you want to stay in your room and watch TV mtd. on a wall, you are either going to do it while laying on your bed or sitting in a desk chair.

When you check in be friendly, use the hotel employees names when talking to them (that's why they all wear nametags!) and if at all possible be amusing. We've received numerous upgrades just be being funny and friendly to the staff when we arrive. 
Being a corner unit the windows spanned two entire sides of the room which was very nice. The view was of the city not the harbor, but considering what we paid, no complaints. The sleeping area was large (king size bed, desk and chair) with another television and another refrigerator in the dresser unit. The bathroom was large and the shower had good pressure. Other Positives: the location is the best available (fantastically convenient to everything in the inner habor.) spacious clean rooms, room service food is good and sometimes great (try the jumbo lump crab omlette!) and food arrives when they say it will. Decor is modern and pleasing to the eye. 
Negatives: Our suite was very very far from the only set of elevators. If mobility is a concern specify a room close to the elevators. The lobby bar not open as much as the hotel literature said it would be. We had a drink there on Friday, but were not able to on other days when we posted hours stated the bar would be open. (We did not venture to the bar in the restaurant which was probably open at those times). 
Also the hotel conducted a test of the fire alarms at -:-- am on Monday. Guests were given no notice and most of us evacuated using the stairs when the announcements told us to. When we reached the outside and made our way to the front of the hotel a security apologized, to us it was a drill and said we could return to our rooms. Kind of irritating. I'm glad it wasn't raining. If you are there and the fire alarms go off at -:-- in the morning, you might want to try calling the front desk before you hike down -- flights. :) 
Overall a very positive experience. We would consider staying there even if we can't ge a Priceline discount in the future.

When I book this hotel again, I'll pay attention to the description given because the large suite I mentioned was described as a King Suite on the internet and I was expecting it to be the King room with the sofa. This was a really good hotel for the price. Clean, comfortable, and affordable. Great location right in the center of DC. Check-in staff was extremely friendly and helpful. Even though it had a thermostat, it would get really warm when the (loud) heater kicked on, and then cold quickly when it was off.

Good value - great staff - conveniently located - room is confortable and practicle - great for business travelers.

GREAT location to everything in the city, and very easy to walk from to everything. Rooms were great, and very clean. All the staff, other than front desk, was very helpful and prompt with service!

My husband and I stayed for one night and got a room for under $--- which for NYC it's a deal. The hotel is very chic and room was very nice. I especially loved the modern bathroom. Our room was incredible. We didn't have a view, but we weren't looking for one either but it was so spacious, to the point where we didn't even need the little desk side area of the room (but if you are a business person its great). The bathroom was huge and clean and there was a small hallway with a mirror and table that is wonderful if you have two people getting ready at the same time. Very comfortable clean bed as well.
The restaurant staff was very nice and accomodating when we showed up right before brunch was over. We said if it's over, we don't want to be a bother and will order the regular lunch menu, but they insisted we come in and the buffet was kept open for just the two of us.
We were very happy with our stay at Washington Court Hotel and would definitely stay there again when we are in DC again!
Very clean rooms. Staff was extremely friendly and helpful. We stayed twice in one week since our flights were late night and early morning. Will stay again!

When I have occasion to travel to San Francisco in the future, you can be sure that this is where I'll stay. I recommend it unreservedly.

I read most recent T-A reviews and quite frankly, after my - nite stay last week, I find some of them much too critical and others overly glowing. If you are looking for the classic business hotel franchise experience, or expanded resort luxury accoutrements, this venue will likely disappoint. But if you revel in historic decor with an Eduardian flair and at a reasonable price point, this Grand Dame should meet your expectations.
The hotel has interesting lineage as it served as City Hall from ---------. The location is primo for public transportation access-- BART-Muni is literally steps from the front door. And yes, the location sits on the Tenderloin-SOMA border, which does present some street folk to deal with, especially in the morning hours. But remember this IS San Francisco, and like any major city, it wil have its fair share of edgy challenges everywhere.
As I think about it, the arrival experience likely sets the dramatic differences in T-A review scoring. The lobby is decked to the nines with Austrian crystal chandeliers, Tiffany glass, polished Italian marble columns and floors, Janesero wood paneling, polished brass fixtures, and fresh flowers so I could see how some folks are immediately enthralled. The front desk experience is pleasant and very efficient, and I was actually able to check in almost - hours early.
On to my sixth floor room where the after-glow dramatically retracts, which I presume causes overly negative feedback as you note the deminished TLC. For example, the bedding is comfortable but sheets were worn and frayed; and the bath towels are well past their useful life. TV reception is good, but the set is a Zenith throwback, virtually unexcusable given flatscreens are so inexpensive these days. The room itself is spacious enough, with high ceilings and vertically striped wall coverings adding to an even larger feel; but the cramped bathroom is in fact an absolute, unqualified disaster with mismatched ceramic tile and shifting floor gaps, a completely rusted and pitted vanity mirror, extremely poor lighting, lousy water pressure in the shower, a toilet with decaying paint enamel and failing flushometer, and and exhaust fan that is so loud you can't hear the TV which is less than - feet away. The fan coil unit was functional and unobtrusive, and I give bonus points for actually being able to open an awning window for fresh air without any significant street noise. But there is no refrigerator nor coffee maker in the room, likely due to the presumably limited power supply outfitted in older hotels. 
On the plus side, lunch at the Market Street Grill was excellent.....try the Sicilian Pasta. And the Tavern Piano Bar was very good too, with more than reasonable happy hour tarrifs for good service and tasty libations.
Bottom-line: not for attention-to-detail business travelers nor resort-splendored folks, but this can be a viable option otherwise at a reasonable price point for the location, especially if they correct the deficiencies noted.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I was supposed to have - free breakfasts with my - room nights but I wasn't told anything about this upon check-in. Despite my trying to convince the restaurant staff not to put the breakfasts on the bill, they did, and I had to work that out again with the front desk staff when I checked out. This may not apply to the suites as the rooms are probably set back from the hall, but for most of the (very small) rooms, the beds are not far from the loud hallway, so if you are anything but a very, very deep sleeper, you will hear late night folks in the hall and returning to their rooms.

My husband and I stayed here, along with another couple, for a getaway weekend. Hotel is located in cute neighborhood with a convenient wine bar and other small restaurants nearby. If the things I have discussed above do not bother you, this hotel will be fine. It is very close to the metro, and there was good houskeeping and polite staff.

Never again, never, ever! 
The spin goes that the Hudson “was” a dormitory redesigned by Philippe Stark into a haven of high design for the hip and well heeled – “the next generation of Cheap Chic – stylish, democratic, young at heart and utterly cool”.. I’d say that the Hudson IS a dormitory-flop house where form definitely trumps substance. The problem with all these sharp, pristine design places is… what do you do when they are no longer neither sharp nor pristine? They start fraying at the edges and slip in clientele. 
I can get the Hudson as a fun hang out for -- something’s from the world over arriving in town and NYC being their oyster, I get the Cheap Chic, young at heart and cool references … but if it is the young uber cool tribe that they wish to attract then these walk in wardrobes of rooms should be at a lower price. USD --- for a tiny room with no mini-bar and minimal service is neither Cheap nor Chic to me.… I get the feeling that the Hudson is more filled more by Priceline than Facebook or the hip and well heeled. And this is why a generationally specific environment gets filled by other generations who will feel like fish out of water. People like me! …. people who do not want to deal with a blaring empty disco vibe in the lobby and every night and elevators all day and who may react weirdly to “Hey dude” from bar staff.
Apparently I was lucky, the nice Korean lady assigned to cleaning my room let me know that I had “one of the biggest rooms in the hotel” ..; I was neither feeling my luck nor the love of the Hudson. My room was very small and dark. No bath only a shower with a curtain that did a very bad job of containing the water – brought a whole new spin on the “wet bathroom” concept. It took the longest I have ever experienced for the water to heat up once I ran the shower. Very annoying sheer net curtains served as the doors to the closet and to hide acces to the bathroom as well as a thematic anchor for the décor. The got stuck constantly! Wifi worked well though the hotel web site was somewhat misleading in giving the impression it was free for my room category. Room service was sporadic with something forgotten or mistaken on each of the two times I used it for breakfast in four. On two occasions I had very important messages from business contacts not reach me from the concierge desk to the clear detriment of the organisation of my trip.
Yet .. I feel like a grouch .. I am in my forties and past it probably! (yet I shared this view with many I spoke with over the music in the elevators) ….I know many younger people in the creative or high tech fields who would have a blast here .. but not at the prices the Hudson demands. They need to rebuild the demographic of their clientele here and get with the hip rather than foisting the Hip on an unsuspecting past it clientele… like me.
