My wife, who just so happens to be named Dana, spent our first weekend alone since our first child was born eight weeks ago. I researched downtown Chicago hotels for weeks and finally decided on The Dana after reading so many wonderful reviews.
I called the hotel about a week ahead of our arrival and asked them for three small requests.
-. We wanted a king bed. This certainly didn’t seem like much to ask. It was just my wife and I, so that makes plenty of sense anyway.
-. We need a room with a refrigerator. Since my wife is breast feeding, she needed to keep the milk chilled for the weekend.
-. If possible, an upper level room with a view.
Upon arriving at the Dana, we were greeted very pleasantly by the door staff and escorted to the front desk on the second floor. After a very short wait, we were quickly given our room card and headed up to our room. The room was the complete opposite of what we requested: Two double beds, no refrigerator and a --th floor view of the side of a building. I immediately went back down to the desk and let them know we needed a new room and their response was basically “We’re booked, too bad”. When we explained we needed a refrigerator and we were already told by phone it wouldn’t be a problem, their response was again “Your room doesn’t come with a refrigerator, too bad.” I’ve never experienced a front desk that was so unhelpful. It wasn’t exactly the way I wanted to start our weekend.
Fortunately, the check-in was the lowlight of the trip. Despite the fact my wife and I slept in separate beds, had to make God knows how many trips to the ice machine (which is hidden in a closet on the fifth floor) and gazed out of our window into an office building, I slowly warmed up to The Dana and eventually left the hotel with a feeling that I might, just maybe, stay there once again.
POSITIVES
-. Location. You can’t beat staying right in the heart of downtown Chicago within walking distance of everything that makes this city so wonderful. Dining, shopping, beach, nightlife … You are right in the middle of all of it.
-. Vertigo. The hotel has one of the best rooftop lounges in Chicago. It was packed both nights we were there and the views from -- stories above were fantastic. The drinks were great. The staff was helpful. Good crowd. Great place.
-. Shower. It’s a one-of-a-kind with a rain head spout from the ceiling and glass on both sides separating the bedroom and the bathroom. It’s about as nice of a hotel bathroom as you’re going to find.
-. Complimentary breakfast. It was so nice to be able to walk downstairs and sit down and be served a perfectly, light meal. They brought a really good fruit bowl with the choice of pastry and quality coffee and juices. It was very simple and very good.
-. Door staff. The guys at the front door go out of their way to make you feel special. Any request was quickly answered and, unlike the front desk staff, they were very pleasant and genuine.
NEGATIVES
-. Front desk. I’ve already covered it all with them. You would think a hotel would employ its most helpful workers for this position, not the opposite. The front desk staff was a joke. Completely clueless and just flat out insulting.
-. Elevator. This might sound like I’m being picky, but I can’t tell you how many times I was in the elevator and another person was mumbling expletives as they battled with the elevator. In order to push the button of your floor, you have to very quickly insert your room card and then make your choice. This is much easier said than done because every single person on the elevator has to do it in order to select your floor. It’s almost like trying to feed a crumbled dollar bill into a vending machine under pressure. It’s incredibly annoying and if you don’t do it quickly, you miss your floor and have to ride the elevator down to the lobby again. I appreciate the security, but I truly believe this is the hotel’s way of trying to be hip and in turn just pissing a lot of people off.
-. Thin walls. I had the stereo playing at low volume and within minutes the hotel security was knocking. If you need to sleep, this isn’t the hotel for you.
-. Trying too hard. This hotel desperately wants to be young and hip. It’s not young by any means and it’s not really all that hip. This place is loaded with middle-agers (----- crowd) and all of their attempts at being cool kind of fall short. Example: To get into the rooftop club, you have to briefly stand behind a velvet rope even if the damn place is empty. I could probably give you -- examples of stuff like that. The ceilings in the room are unfinished cement. Trendy or an eye sore? I definitely thought the latter.
-. Ice machine. Call and ask guest services where the ice machine is located. They will tell you it’s on the fifth floor. If you can find it in less than -- minutes, I’ll be impressed. There are a lot of things at this hotel where you just scratch your head and think, what the @#$% were they thinking?

I recently stayed at this hotel to celebrate a romantic outing on New Year's eve. Our accomodations were made by a group that organize this annual event.There are approximately --- couples that attend this affair. I believe that this is the third year that it was hosted by University Hotel. Upon arrival, my husband and I was informed that the only rooms that were available were two double bed occupancy or - king size bed that had special accomadations for wheelchair accessibility. We decided on the latter. I was quite dissappointed when we entered the room and I realized that there was no bathtub, as I had been told the only difference was the rail in the bathroom. I contacted the manager who again explained to me that the only rooms that were available with a king size bed was the one we had or the option of going with the two double beds. We again opted to remain in the room, only to discover that when showering the water ran all over the floor and it was very slippery and dangerous.
The next day we encountered another issue with the hotel's ineffectiveness. Our credit card which we provided on check-in was charged the entire amount for the overnight event, over $---.--, which had already been paid in full. The only expenses that we were to incur was incidental charges. Upon writing this review our credit card has not been credited for the error. Needless to say, I am very dissapointed with this hotel, and I would never recommend it to a friend. 
 I think the staff and management has the worst customer service I have ever experience and they are totally ill-equipped in handling large groups. I would never recommend this hotel to a friend

We have just returned from five nights at this hotel - the hotel itself is great, great location - lots of restaurants around and very quiet at night - best of all is the mini bar and basket of goodies which are all free (except alcohol) and replenished daily. 
Unfortunately our stay was marred by unhelpful and rude front desk staff, we had a problem with our special travel mastercard which we had charged up with dollars - because you get a better rate - on arrival we gave the card, but what we did not know was that the hotel 'reserves' $--- a day on top of the room charge (so an additional $---- in our case) - the result was that all of the money on our card was in effect used up and the following day we tried to use it and it was declined - after talking to the card company we discovered what the hotel had done - completely without telling us - the hotel said it was a standard thing to do, we have travellled all over the world and have never come across this - i'd be interested to hear if anyone else has ? we would not have minded if we had been told but sorting out the result of this took - days as the money did not go back on the card so could not be used - anyway, the point is how the staff dealt with the situation - it is like dealing with robots, they were very fake and pretended to understand - it was very frustrating - as someone else said in a review, the particular person who dealt with us was confrontational and comletely unhelpful. Stay at this hotel but be wary of the front desk staff and dont excpect help if you have any problems.

I had an excellent couple of nights here, one on my way to the Rockies, and one on my return. The staff were friendly and helpful, the rooms clean and bright. Given the free transport to and from the airport, and the frre continental breakfast (starting at -:--am), I don't think one could do better for a stop-over. One warning- the airport shuttle leaves the airport almost all day, every hour on the half hour, but it's worth phoning the hotel when you arrive at the airport to confirm place and time of the shuttle's arrival, either by cell, or by using the land line phones available by the exit doors (phone #-- for Microtel, I believe)
James

We booked our hotel at the travel agent and had a choice of places to stay - after reading so many favourable reviews on this website about the Affinia--, I am extremely glad we decided to stay here!
The rooms were very spacious and clean, I loved the fact that there was a kitchen, so it really felt like home. There is plenty of space for suitcases (three females sharing one room, so luggage was plentiful!), and space to hang clothes, etc. The first night we came in, two light bulbs had blown, so we left a note for housekeeping and that was fixed promptly. 
I have to say the best thing about this hotel was its location- situated where it is, and for the reasonable price we paid. We walked to Times Square, where we got tour buses, did our shopping, watched our broadway show. It is also close to Rockefeller Centre, NBC Studios etc, which were both things on the New York Pass we used. Walking back to our hotel at night, we felt very safe and we never ran into any trouble or unsavoury characters!

We visit The Westin LaCantera in San Antonio, TX annually to celebrate our anniversary. The customer service is always good here but they found one person who really shines around people. Her name is Danielle aka Danny. You can find her down at the adult pool and she made our entire stay that day so welcoming and wonderful! She has a smile on her face even when overwhelmed by orders. She called me by my last name which most people dont care to do. She is a wonderful addition to the Westin family! Keep this one around guys, the great ones are hard to come by! Thanks 'Danny' for making our day at the pool so wonderful.
-Bethany Shaw

This hotel goes without a surprise. 
Outside it looks good, inside it's fine, rooms are not that large though it's convenient and well designed.
Staff is nice.
And it's really a great location in SF : close to Union Square and Chinatown.
I would simply not go for breakfast, not interesting. Especially considering every other places available around for breakfast or brunch, e.g. try Sears if you never did ;-)

Not a bad hotel, but there were some problems. We stayed here one busy Friday night, which was enough. I think we stayed on what was a pretty busy weekend for them. 
The hotel lobby was very stylish, and featured a trendy bar. Hotel was located right across from the Met, so it's a good location if that is of interest. My favorite part of the hotel was the pool bar that was on the roof. I had heard that the rooftop bar (separate from the pool bar, but just one floor down and easily visible from the pool bar-patio) had a dress requirement (no t-shirts-sneakers) but we saw lots of people in t-shirts, shorts and flip-flops who got in anyway.
By far the worst part of the stay was the door slams in the morning. Granted this happens with every hotel, but there is something with their doors that that causes them slam automatically. I tried to shut our door quietly, but it slams shut inevitably. They really should address this. We checked out around -- (after a late night out), but beginning around -:-- a.m. we continually heard loud door slamming from departing guests what seemed like every -- - -- minutes until about -- am. 
Our room was stylish, but beginning to see signs of wear. The furniture was badly scratched in some area. The bed was hard, but we slept well on it (at least until the slamming started in the morning.) Additionally, there was an ice bucket that was left outside of our room from the last guest and was never replaced. The ice bucket was there from the time we checked in (around -pm) until the time we left the next day at Noon.
Also, we were just getting ready to leave the room (it was -- Noon on the dot), and the maid opens the door without knocking to ask us if we were checking out soon - granted it was check out time, but it was --:-- exactly, and she opened the door despite the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""do not disturb"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sign on the door. 
We weren't lucky enough to have an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""outside"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room, so our room looked out onto the inside exhaust system of the hotel. However the room was fairly large for NYC standards.
It would have been a much nicer stay except for the door slams - I can't recomend staying at this hotel for that problem alone.

Stayed on our way back from trip to California. Daughter wanted to see Seattle the next morn. before going home to B.C. Had the dog with us so we decided to stay at the La Quinta. This was on Jan -, ----. The girl at the front desk was very nice. New at hotel traveling with a dog. Was happy to learn they did not charge extra for our - mo old pup. Charged $-- or more other places. The price was right but it is true the place is pretty run down. Needs new carpet especially in the halls. Windows real dirty could hardly see the airport. Bad lighting in the rooms. Standard breakfast. The area to let your dog go was covenient and there was bags provided. Come on people pick up after your dogs! I have to say though one reason might be that they put the pags as far away from the doors as possible and you have to walk across the grass to get one. Meanwhile trying to walk through the grass at night and stepping in stuff that others didn't bother to clean up after their dogs. might help to move the bags closer? Would only stay again because I had my dog and if the price was right.

I stayed two nights at the hotel, and was impressed when I entered the lobby, the ambiance felt like a W property. However, once you leave the lobby, there is no mistaking this is a cookie cutter Marriott property. The elevators are extremely crowded in the morning and afternoon, and they seem to stop at every floor, so a ride to or from the executive lounge on the --th floor is not a quick trip. 
The rooms are ok, but again nothing to get excited about. It is strange to go from the trendy lobby, complete with club type music, to your room which is the old school Marriott color scheme, complete with blue carpet and somewhat dated furnishings. My room had a small refrigerator setup in it (forgot to remove that request from my profile), however they never bothered to clean it out from the previous guests, and it was full of old food and drinks, pretty disgusting. 
The executive lounge has a nice view of downtown and the airport, and there is a patio to sit on which was nice in the morning. However, the patio was constantly in use by smokers during my visit, so unless you don't mind sitting in a cloud of smoke, it loses it's charm fast.
The service at the restaurant for breakfast was not too good, had to wait for -- minutes before being waited on and that was only after I went and found a waitress. I then had to listen to two waiters argue with each other about who is supposed to work certain sections. The service at Tanq was not much better, waited -- minutes there and never was asked if I wanted to order something so I left and went to Il Fornaio across the street. 
The final indignity for me was that even though I had wifi access paid for through my room, this access is not available on the conference room level. So unless the conference you are attending pays specifically for conference room wifi access, you have no internet - and if you use AT&T, there is no signal on the conference room floor, which means a day of no email access. The chairs in the conference rooms must be from the --'s, because they are so worn that you can barely sit on them.
My take on this hotel is that they get a guaranteed revenue stream from conference guests and convention center guests, so they don't have a lot of incentive to go out of their way.

As a Hilton Diamond member, I booked one night at this hotel for a race starting at the Art Museum. Although the location is terrific, the valet parking at $-- borders on insanity. Once I got inside, although there were three people behind the desk and only two customers in front of me, it took a full -- minutes for me to get checked in and to obtain keys to my room. The hotel is round and thus the rooms are oddly shaped with awkward doorways. My room was large, but not clean, as I found a razor in the bathroom, popcorn on the floor in the bedroom, and the ice bucket in the mini-kitchen was filthy. The super-slow elevator, which was right next to my room, was very loud and disturbed my sleep for the entire night. To top this off, I had ordered dinner from Hilton's Requests Upon Arrival service, but it didn't show up, and when I called room service, I was told that they had never received the order. Despite this, the order showed up in two plastic bags (strange) a half hour later. I didn't partake of the free breakfast but I was told by the front desk to go early since they often run out of food.
I won't be staying here again.

I stayed at the Four Seasons Philly for - days in September. The best thing about it is its location. It's close to the major office buildings and looks out over Logan Circle.
But that's where the luxury stops. The bathroom was a letdown: there was no division between the sink area and the rest of the room. It felt like it was last updated in ----. There weren't any glaring faults--it was clean and adequate but that was about it.
The same was true of the public spaces. They felt old. Not in a tired way but as if they had just been taken out of a time capsule. Along with an episode of Dynasty and a Diet Tab.
The most irritating thing about the hotel is that they charge for the use of their business center. I stayed at - other hotels on this trip (not in Philadelphia), - of which were similar in price and both of them offered free internet in their business center. It was ridiculous to be charged $-- for -- minutes.

Good location, just off Times Square, although about as far west as one would want to be.
Room was reasonable (well-equippped), however sound-proofing was NOT good, we were disturbed by noise - people on either side and also in the hallway. 
Westin's 'Heavenly Bed' was very comfortable however their 'Heavenly Bath' was just an ordinary bath - certainly nothing special.
Were on the --th floor, which had no views at all - go higher up if you want to look out on the city (probably above --rd floor).
Service was good and hotel - room very clean and tidy.

great desk staff, like family, very helpful with everything!
very clean, comfortable and close enough to where you want to be.
could not have picked a better place to stay for what we wanted to do,[eat,shop,what ever]. desk clerks- debra,jen and keith gave info, for everything we wanted to do or go and helped with the directions. ask them about parking, the best place,[quik park] right down the street and very reasonable, paul the attendent, the best!!! and if you need to get a hair cut , mario nico down the street, super,fabulous job!!!!!!!!!!

The location is the only selling point of this hotel. The customer service is nonexistent. The hotel itself has a very corporate feel to it and just isn't very nice to stay in. The carpets and elevators are pretty dirty and unappealing. We tried to stay here this past weekend. When we arrived our confirmed King room was now two double beds. They refused to honor the reservation (which was a confirmed King as stated in the rate details), and refused to help us with finding another Hyatt in the area. 
Andaz on the other hand, also part of the Hyatt portfolio, is amazing. We ended up at the Andaz on Wall-Street and it was honestly the best hotel i've stayed in, and I have stayed at Hyatt properties all over the world. 
There are better hotels in the viscidity but really, go out a little and stay at one of the Andaz hotels!

Completely recommend this hotel to anyone visiting LA. The location in Hollywood is perfect, it really is only - minutes from the Hollywood Blvd and yet absolutely quiet. The rooms are very spacious and comfortable, we paid a bit more for the view and it was well worth it. Decor is slightly faded, but the space made up for it (massive and comfy bed, by the way). Great pool, not heated but attractively landscaped and quiet. The short walk down to breakfast was no problem, and the choice of food available was good.

Cleanliness - I give my room a - because of the dark carpet stain in front of the closet. Looks like it needs a good steam clean or more.
Location - downtown Denver doesn't have much to offer after -. I went out for a walk to the art museum and capital and down the main drag, --th Street. Lots of teens who looked like they are homeless and others who looked like they were probably up to not much good. I live in SF so I am used to seeing homeless people but this had a different feel because it is so concentrated and so young. Hopefully for the city and these kids they can come up with a solution to get them off the streets..
Rooms - the rooms are high quality construction but lacked some amenities that I would expect at a Ritz. The toiletries were second tier at best. The bed was a bit of a sponge which to me is very uncomfortable, leading to my low score on sleep quality.
Service - Service was good and the people are very friendly (which is true for Denver generally speaking). So why a - and not a -? No one bothered to get my bags out of the taxi when I arrived and the service was a bit lacking in the restaurant. There were quite a few staff on hand, and it makes me wonder if there are too many people on staff - perhaps that leads to confusion as to who is helping who.
Value - I paid less than $--- for my stay, which I consider quite good. I would rate it higher if not for the cost of the restaurant (too expensive for the quality of food).
Sleep quality - The beds were simply uncomfortable and sag in the middle. The air quality was incredibly dry - not the fault of the hotel but something to consider if you are sensitive to dryness. 
So - my guess is that this is the best deal going in Denver for a business traveler's hotel. They will need to step up their game when the Four Seasons opens up. The FS is really in a different class to the Ritz and will take a big bite out of the customer base for this hotel.

Stayed here for a conference for several days. Service was excellent. Lobby was the best so far in Boston- big and stylish in a Danish modern way. Linens were excellent, mattress was very good, room was very large. Contemporary furnishings were stand-out quality for Boston. View was not that special, but still better than Jury's or the Lenox. So why the bad reviews? Maybe the high price of the food (quite steep), although in-room breakfast was good quality. Maybe the bathroom was not as clean-well detailed as others? Location is out of the way unless you're attending a nearby event (you can't get any closer to the convention center than this hotel). If the average price on here is accurate, hotel is a good deal to me. Internet was extra- always an annoyance.

Reserved here based on TripAdvisor recommendations, and boy am I glad I did. While the decor could use an upgrade and the service in the dining room was slow our last night there, everything else about the place was wonderful. The staff couldn't have been friendlier or more helpful. From the hotel, Seaworld and the Zoo are a stone's throw away, and the shuttle to the airport is quick and easy. The atmosphere is relaxed, and the water is all around you. Definitely would stay there again.

Highlights include the very deep bathtub, the paper panel window treatments and Japanese styling touches. Front desk staff are exceedingly gracious, which will make up for the lack of attention to the front door itself: I found the greeting there to be basically non-existent. The hotel is ostensibly recently refurbished -- but I suspect the makeover was, indeed, purely cosmetic. The hardware in the bathroom looks old, as does much of the rest of the hotel: couches seem worn, wallpaper a little old. It's a fascinating and interesting space, featuring the same heavy concrete style of the nearby Japantown mall; the architecture reminded me of ----s Japan: Godzilla, the bullet train, trans-Pacific flights on a Boeing ---. The garden is pretty, but lacks integration into the overall guest experience.
Had one relatively average burger through room service (the apologized in advance for the late delivery of the burger; it took two calls to get an answer at room service). The bartender at the lounge seemed a little odd or off in some way.
The clientele was mostly families and hipsters: either kids or dreadlocks, or else kids with dreadlocks.
Overall, however, this is basically a very nice hotel with lots of interesting details. A main advantage is its proximity to Fillmore and Japantown... off the beaten track of Union Square.

With limited room availability in SF when we arrived, we ended up picking the Clift and a 'studio suite' for about $---++ (=$--- nett not including breakfast) which was described on their site as a larger, more luxurious room. The room was indeed reasonably spacious, but decor was very sparse. The only item it seemed they had spent some money on where the curtains, everything else was very basic. The bathroom was small, with an institutional feel to it (not the good kind). 
The hotel's saving grace is the excellent location close to Union Square and a couple of great breakfast places (Taylor Street Coffee Shop, Dottie's), plus the concierge and front office staff is excellent. The bar is great also, and really gets hopping on the weekends. 
Would not stay here again, despite the pluses mentioned.

I attended a conference here (otherwise would have not selected this hotel). The rooms are large but overall the place has very little character. I have ordered room service late at night. The food vas really third class. The fruit plate had many different kind of fruits in large quantities but bad selection with no taste. When I arrived there was no bottle of water in the room. No minibar. No bath robe. Called down to to the front dresk and it took them several minutes to answer. For the price of $---+ it is a really bad deal.
Excellent Location and great staff. Hotel was by far the best value for condition of hotel we found in San Diego.

This is a great hotel for a business stay as well as personal -- it's attached to the nordstrom shopping center by skybridge, easy parking if you need it, and great staff. Rooms are well appointed and well maintained (loved the pillow menu but didn't try it). Front desk staff were very helpful with even the smallest requests.

I was in town to anual meeting in Nephrology. It´s a cleaner hotel, confy enough and placed a few minutes from convention center by taxi. A two blocks from McDonalds and others fast foods. Very cool for a short stay or a business stay. The hotel was in price range at location and didn´t expect so much. Shuttle service was good and reliable.

Smart workers are so hard to find. Very tired of dealing with dumb front desk clerks, very tired. This hotel needs to hire smarter people, but it would have to pay more. It's a catch -- situation, I know. HIre smarter people, the room rates go up.

I spent one night here at the Fairfield and it was a great experience! The front desk clerk was very nice and helpful. The bed was large and very comfy. The flat screen tv had a few good channels including USA, TBS and HBO. The location is great! It is two blocks from Chinatown so my boyfriend and I just walked up the street to Clyde's restaurant for dinner. I did not take advantage of the continental breakfast and we arrived too late to hear the live band that plays. Overall good hotel.

My husband and I have traveled from NYC to San Antonio for a wedding that was taking place at the St. Anthony Riverwalk. The wedding was nice, but the rooms were horrific. This is not our first time at the Riverwalk, but this is our first and last time at this run-down, old, dirty place. I am sorry, but this place needs some serious renovations. Our room had paint chipping away everywhere, the handles on the doors were all broken, there was mildew and mold everywhere in the bathroom and the room smelled terrible. Well, complaining did not do much as there is nothing anyone can do but to level this place out and start from scratch. The lobby downstairs was nice, but the carpeting was old and stained almost everywhere. I do realize that it's a historic location-hotel, but it's not worth it. There are so many NICER places where you can stay and enjoy your trip....this one happens to be a nightmare :-( STAY WAY!

Second visit and although the room did have a nice view on a WALL instead of the Empire State Building, it was clean and the location is great, close to metro and some of NYC's highlights without being noisy. Fast check in and check out, helpful staff, very nice cleaners. Bed was noisy and mattress not to our taste but would book again

Boutique hotel in the Flower District. New, clean, staff was great and the hotel small enough that desk staff and doorman recognize you. Great location for transit, several restaurants nearby. Enjoyed the outdoor rooftop lounge. It's small with loud music at the bar and much quieter in the back. Air conditioning was great (very hot and humid outide) and the rooms were very attractive, comfortable and clean. Internet free and fast. If you needed to print anything from the computer, they have a small business centre in the basement elevator lobby. Great value for the money and we'll stay there again.

Let me just say the entrance was beautiful glass front elevator to the main lobby, the check in was prompt, and concierge desk was extremely helpful with recommending near by location for entertainment. Awesome bar and The Serafina restaurant right next door. Across the street the parking garage gave me a discount for parking --$ overnight since I was a hotel guest and my friends and I loved the room, clean, with bose radio and a flat screen TV. We didn't hang in to long the location was a block from time square. The pubs were endless bartender stayed open a little late so we can finish the night off with a little nite cap. Oh they even granted me an late checkout with no issues. Definitely heading back to thei hotel frequently.
Thanks again to - """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The Time"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for an affordable place, in an incredible location

We stayed here as a family whilst one of the adults was attending a large conference in November ----. I don't think I saw any other children in the hotel for the four days we stayed, but we were never made to feel unwelcome. 
The hotel was what you'd expect from any of this class: comfy beds, fluffy bathrobes... And also over-priced in-room WiFi and nowhere to keep your leftover pizza because the fridge is full of minibar items and completely automated to charge you automatically when items are removed. These little """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Nickle and dime"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" things really bother me given the amount being paid for the room in the first place.
My only other complaint was the temperature of the pool! The pool itself was too small to be used for lap swimming, but much too cold to be enjoyed for leisure swimming.
We loved the location, an easy walk, even for a pre-schooler, to public transport. The staff were all helpful and friendly. The food in the restaurant was amazing, and, again, even though ours were the only children there, they were welcomed.
Just on principle, next time we are in Chicago, we would probably look for a hotel with free WiFi, but we wouldn't mind staying here again.

Everything at the Peabody was great except The Motorcycle Noise all night long! It was terrible on a Wednesday night and pretty bad on a Friday night. Motorcycles seemingly were racing around downtown, revving their engines to see who could make the most noise. The Peabody must work with the authorities to proactively eliminate this problem or they risk having their first class property turn into a second class hotel.

Spent the week of oct ----- first time visiting Chicago . we took the package with valet parking & restaurant package . Everything was done with world class service from checking in to the valet!!!! We also loved the restaurant at the Omni we had the buffet in the am . we had the hamburger & sweet potato fries during the afternoon (fantastic ) , they gave us $-- dollars per day per Guest to spend the menu is reasonably priced . Wait staff at the restaurant we're AWESOME you wanted for nothing !!!! Our room was a corner room it had lots of room with a Great view of Michigan Ave!!! City of Chicago Speaks for itself Show Up & Be Moved !!!

I don't stay in """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""fancy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotels that often (I'm more of a budget traveler)... so I have mixed feelings about my Marriott experience. I spent - nights in the Marriott... ALL the staff were wonderful (and I interacted with at least - of them), the hotel was very clean, the location was great...
My disappointments: 
-- $--.-- PER DAY for internet in my room - are you kidding me??? (I used the free wifi in the lobby)
-- The pillows are shockingly TINY (I should have asked if they had regular-sized pillows) and way too soft for me... 
-- The weight room is on the pool deck (way too hot and humid! Thankfully, the cardio machines are in a separate, regular-temperature room)
-- The room rate was too expensive for what you get.

During our housewares shows at McCormick, I flew in from London, England.
Just minutes away, could go back and forth if needed. I found out I was not far from downtown
Chicago; we also had a seminar scheduled to discuss upcoming events. It was also walking distance to the beach area. Excellent service. Clean rooms. Polite staff.

My husband and I booked four nights at the White Swan Inn in San Francisco to celebrate his birthday. A few days before our trip we both became ill with bad colds accompanied by horrible coughs. The White Swan staff was excellent, understanding and very patient with us as we tried to decide whether to cancel or not. When we did make the decision to cancel, they were very accommodating and wished us good health. A few days later we received a delightful, hand written get well note saying they hoped we were feeling better and that we could reschedule in the near future. We will definitely make the trip in ---- and plan on booking with The White Swan. In this day of impersonal E mail correspondence, we were so impressed with the extra care this establishment took to make us feel welcome. Good job, indeed!!! Kathryn Brown

We stayed at the Springhill Suites in Downtown Memphis this weekend, and it was very clean & comfortable. The rooms were a little narrow to classify as suites in my opinion, but they did have a separate kitchenette, and sitting area. I would highly recommend this hotel, especially for the location and the wonderful complimentary breakfast. We could walk to Beale St. in - minutes, and if you didn't feel like it, just hop on the trolley right outside the door.

We stayed in SOHO for - nights earlier and paid half the price at the Hampton Inn. They had free breakfast, free wifi, and room that was twice as clean and twice the size of the Roosevelt. The room has an old rusty air con, dirty walls, broken shower. room ----.

Just returned from a --day break in New York where we stayed at The Hotel Lucerne. Firstly, its ideally located. There was a subway station at the end of the street to take you straight downtown. It was only a - minute walk from Central Park which we found handy for running every morning. Its right on the corner of --th Street-Amsterdam Avenue where you are spoilt for choice with great places to eat and drink.
The hotel itself was great. Always spotlessly clean & our dealings with the staff were always friendly ones. You get a --% discount card for breakfast in Nice Matin, the adjoining restaurant but we never used it. We really enjoyed the Amsterdam Diner just up the street.
There's a bit of street noise, but its New York so I'm guessing this would be the same in most hotels?
A great place to stay and great value for money in New York. Would definately recommend it.

We had a marvelous stay in Hyatt Place Hotel.
Convenient location (airport, Sea world, supermarkets, restaurants etc.) Nice interiors, spotless room, very good service. Very well organized, attentive and kind staff. Check in and out very fast. Excellent breakfast!
The manager is very kind and you can see that he handles all situations in a way that keeps the hotel running smoothly.
I would highly recomend this place and would stay again.

I found the hotel easy to find - but I dont think there is a sign post... just check out the images from the website - if you can remember what it looks like you wont have any problems locating it, which is suggested in some reviews.
It is beautiful inside - the ivy covred lobby ceiling is really impressive. The staff at check in are polite, professional, friendly and helpful.
The rooms are small, but really clean, and the bed was very comfy. Housekeeping is really good.. the room was cleaned thoroughly every day.
there was a CD player in my room, so i sort of wished that i'd taken a couple of cds to listen to while i was getting ready.
the freebie toiletries are nice enough.
I stayed over a long weekend, and the hotel has a very buzzy atmosphere on friday and saturday nights.. i was returning from a long day of sight seeing, so it wasnt really the best place for me as I'd have liked to have proped myself somewhere for a quiet cup of coffee in the evening, just for half an hour before bed.. but maybe im getting a little old!! 
but - if you're away with the girls, then its really fabulous - be sure to book a table in the outside bar area if you're wanting to have drinks there.. its really pricey though, we paid $-- for a round consisting of an orange juice, lager, and a bellini, the drinks were lovely,and the service was ok. but i thought $-- was a bit steep.
check out was before --noon, and quick and easy, and you can store your luggage while you spend time in the city before going back to the airport... the doorman will collect your bags if you present the little ticket at the door on street level. thats nice and easy.
all in all - great hotel... absolutely fabulous location, and perfect if youre really going for it in terms of sight seeing.. also if you're with the girls, or part of a couple who likes the bar scene, then the bars are great. rooms clean, comfy.. all in all very very good!

Hotels in downtown Chicago are expensive and then, if you've driven in, you have to pay an additional parking fee. We were looking for a moderately priced hotel with access to one of the subway lines. We got a queen suite with a sleeper sofa bed for $----night. at this hotel. Note: we did not realize that the sleeper sofa was only a twin bed and we needed a double. I went to the front desk and they comp'd us a roll away cot. 
The blue line is within easy walking distance to this hotel. To get to the blue line you'll need to go through the parking garage that is located on the northwest corner of the same intersection that the hotel is located on (hotel is on southeast corner). Note: if you want to purchase a day pass, they do not sell them at the blue line station. My husband had to trek to a grocery store north of the station (@Higgins-Cumberland) to purchase the day passes. 
The hotel is a little tired looking but the room was decent. The room was clean, our sheets were crisp and the bed was comfortable. The water pressure was good and we had plenty of towels. Also, the air conditioner almost froze us out. So, all things considered, I think this was a really good deal.

We stayed three nights over Easter weekend (April -----, ----) and got their DC Weekend Getaway package that included room, parking, and breakfast for our family of three. The rooms were clean, standard hotel rooms with the nice addition of a small refrigerator and a microwave. Breakfast was serve-yourself and was quite good and had a variety of cold items, hot items, and a chef that would make custom omelets. There was also waitstaff that provided your drinks and did a nice job of keeping your table clean. We had one dinner at the hotel and the service that night was a bit slow and the food was quite cold on delivery. The hotel is very close to the White House and conveniently located to other restaurants. The parking garage was very efficient and did a great job of quickly bringing our car right to the front of the hotel and was very accomodating with in-and-out privileges. The sunrise Easter service was amazing down at the Lincoln Memorial. We enjoyed our stay and would go back again if we find ourselves in DC.

Stayed here a couple of nights. Nice, clean hotel. The rooms were large and we had - queen size beds. Very new looking and the beds were comfy. Free parking and wi-fi. Very uncommon in city hotels. Breakfast was good but pricy. About a -- min walk to the subway(T). Felt safe walking back to hotel after dark in a group. Would recommend this hotel especially for the price....

Had a really great stay at Grand Hyatt Seattle. Really convenient location, close to the light link rail station, only - block away. The train will bring us conveniently to airport in just -- minutes (and it only costs -.-- $ one way). The light link rail was really clean too! which is a nice surprise for a public transportation. When we checked in, we were given a corner room, which is a real nice surprise. It has its own living room and a bedroom. Very spacious! And the bathroom was really spacious too, it has a gigantic bath tub, and a shower room. Overall the stay was excellent, we get much more than we expected (and did I mention they provide toothpaste in the bathroom? usually hotels don't provide toothpaste, although soap and shampoo are always provided). The check-in staff was really great and helpful, when we checked out, but we ran into a little bit of a problem with some drinks that were listed in our bill (we didn't drink anything from the fridge). Apparently the fridge has a sensor, so when we move things around in the fridge (to make way for the delicious smoked salmon we bought from Pike's place - we were really careful about packaging the smoked salmon so it's practically odorless), it records the movement and thinks that we took some drinks out of the fridge. The matter was resolved by a very helpful lady at the check out (although the gentleman at the check-out desk was not very nice-helpful and gave me a bit of a sour face when we faced this issue at check-out). He looked pretty arrogant too, for that matter, which is unfortunate. But it's okay, cause the other lady was real great, and very helpful, and hopefully next time he won't be so arrogant or has that sour face when dealing with people.

Really enjoyed stay at the Gotham, it was my first time there and will go back. Convenient for mid-town and the beds are very comfortable. My only negative was the front of house staff changed daily and therefore there was no consistency in service - other than that - all good.

Our daughter had her wedding at the hotel. Many quests stayed at the hotel. All where happy with the accommodations as well as the delicious breakfast buffet and happy hour to meet everyone. The wedding was excellent. Everything was done very professionally. Our daughter lives in San Francisico. The wedding planner was very efficient and made everything easy for her. The staff was helpful to all our quests since we are from the East coast. They got cabs for us, gave his directions to restaurants, and shuttles to the airport.The hotel is centrally located to many attractions. If you went on Greyline Tours, they picked you up and back after the tour. We all enjoyed the Red and Line tour to see the Blue Angels and other planes. We had a buffet with sandwiches, salad desserts. There was plenty of food for everyone to enjoy. The movie tour of the movies filmed in San Francisco was also enjoyable. We will be back soon.

The room was so small, we couldn't move around our suitcases easely, but we did have a lot of luggage since this was only the beginning of our trip, we still had - weeks ahead of us...
I requested two dubble beds, but we got only twins. Didn't complain at the front desk, we left home -- hours earlier, were tired and wanted a shower and any bed to sleep.
There was a closet large enough to put away our luggage, which is a plus in case you have - large and two small suitcases.
There was a coffeemaker in the room, but complimentary coffee is served in the lobby every morning. The room has no AC, only a ceiling fan. I cannot imagine that an AC is needed in San Francisco...
The bathroom was also very tiny. There was no bath tub, only a real shower! I like this better then a bath tub with a shower curtain, it's much cleaner. There was also a hair drier and a little welcome gift :-)
As I mentioned earlier: coffee is served in the lobby every morning, as well as every afternoon (- - - pm) complimentary wine is served. I know a thing or two about wine and the ones they served (white chardonnay and red cabernet sauvignon) were not bad at all.
There a laptop computer in the lobby for guest use.
The staff was very friendly and helpfull.
But the best about this hotel is price-location. It's an affordable hotel on a top location. It's nearby a bart-station, near a turning platform for cable cars, accross the street there's a wallgreens, around the corner is an Irish Pub, the nextdoor Thai is also recommended (it looks kind of weard, but check it out!!!)
My general conclusion: don't expect the four seasons, you get what you pay for... plus a little extra in this case... a great location!

Great location in the heart of NYC, and just far enough away from Times Square to get away from the craziness and crowds! Easy access to subway and short walk to many attractions-shopping-restaurants. Our family of three had plenty of space in the room (it was larger than I expected!), with a wonderfully comfortable king size bed and surprisingly comfortable sofabed. While we didn't use the kitchen, it was great to have a microwave to make popcorn and a refrigerator to keep our bottled water cold! The HVAC system worked well - room temperature was good even in July! Very quiet, didn't hear anything from other rooms (just the honking of taxis outside!) Breakfast was fantastic - lots of options and very spacious so it didn't feel overly crowded. The staff was very friendly and helpful, especially the concierge, Judy, who arranged our transportation to JFK airport and was extremely pleasant and knowledgeable. Be warned, elevators can be hard to come by on weekend mornings - we waited quite a while for an elevator that three of us plus our luggage would fit on when we were headed down to check out. Just four elevators for --+ floors gets tricky - but the hotel is very aware of it, and even left us voice mail messages advising us to get to breakfast early and to expect to wait for the elevator. Good advice! Highly recommend this hotel, and will stay there again if the need arises.

Great location for China Town and unusual decor. Liked coffee and drinks in foyer.But... Very tiny rooms, water took ages to drain away from basin. 
Unhelpful staff when I was trrying to get the telephone line activated in my room. It took three trips in tiny lift to reception who eventually told me """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" the phone probably doesn't work in your room."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and that was that.
Our room was not cleaned until I asked at -.--pm- we had to leave and walk around for a bit. Again the reception seemed convinced that I had out a do not disturb sign on the door - which I hadn't. No apology. Very different service to that in L.A..
Not very clean. Breakfast basic but okay. Staff unhelpful and uninterested in helping guests. Overcharged for room and took forever to get handled by hotel staff.

What a fabulous hotel! Great food, great breakfast room, great dinner. Excellent location. Staff attentive and helpful. Would stay again in a heartbeat. One negative, bathroom is small, very small sink area. Oh, and the cheese cube on the floor when we first came to the room..... Housekeeping either missed it, or they feed the mice. We saw no mice so I assume it was housekeepings error.

This hotel gets - stars because my wife liked it so much and because we felt the Platinum member advantage (which does not happen at all Marriotts). Like the other U.S.-based Marriotts, which is completely different in Europe and Asia, there is no concierge lounge service on weekends, a relatively spartan hor's d'oeuvre offering in the evening, and a charge for alcohol (""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""honor bar"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""") including red wines that were not very good; however, I received a $-- coupon-day for the second floor Starbucks to compensate for no concierge lounge on weekends. Like most hotels, there is no lap pool although it was a larger pool than most; the gym was excellent, from the layout to the large range of aerobic equipment to an extensive weight and workout room. The hotel was very nice, well run, we received a super greeting when we checked in and felt appreciated during check out. Because of my status, we were upgraded to a very nice executive suited that looked out over Boston - at a government room rate! The suite was great; maid service was efficient and worked around us. The concierge lounge and the gym also had nice views of Boston. The concierge lounge provided a bit more choice and quality than the usual. There is one restaurant - a sportsbar - but this hotel has passageways that connect immediately into many other good eateries in and around Copley Square so it actually makes sense not to try to compete with a separate hotel restaurant. Self-parking was connected but not part of the hotel and was typically Boston expensive but very convenient. This would be a good hotel for business meetings and modest sized conferences. We will definitely return to this Marriott!
Near Sea World; not much around the hotel so you definitely need a car.
Excellent staff and very pleasant staff. The room was excellent as it has a microwave and room to work if need be. Thank you for a wonderful experience always. Greg

Just returned from a - night stay at the New Yorker. Had a great time. We had a view room which certainly lived up to its name, We had the most amazing view of the Empire State Buidling. Really it was more than we could have dreamt of on our first trip to the city. The room was plenty big enough for the - of us. The bathroom was quite large with a nice deep tub. Yes, the tile paint was chipped in places but to be honest we didn't spend enough time in there to stress over it. Everything was really clean. Every member of staff we dealt with was really helpful. I do recommend the car service to and from JFK. This was well worth it and the complimentary printing of the booking pass was an added bonus. Now that we have found the New Yorker we wouldn't dream of staying anywhere else! Also recommend the Tick Tock diner and the guy with the counter in the lobby selling coffee-tea and pastries etc - a great alternative to a full cooked breakfast in the diner.

I booked this hotel because I wanted to be within walking distance of Petco Park for the baseball game. Little did I know (by simply looking at the map) that the ballpark is right outside the doors of the hotel! 
The hotel was nice. The service was excellent. The restaurant in the hotel was good. There is a rooftop bar that is pretty neat. We could see the ballpark from there. The rooftop bar did get quite crowded & there was a long line of people waiting to get in. 
The room had a good layout. The mattress could use upgrading. The view was nice, but the window desparately needed cleaning. Other than the window, the room was clean.

this was a great hotel. we basically stayed here room only, which is all you need as there are that many small cafes and resteraunts open until the small hours very close by. we did have drinks in the hotel and fond them to be very expensive.
nearby there are bars resteraunts and any amount of different types of food to be enjoyed. 
the room was small, but this is the norm for new york, it was ideal as a base to explore though, comfortable, warm and the shower- bathroom was great.
all in all the location is the best aspect, it is literaally placed on top of times square and is within a minutes walk.
great stay

I selected this hotel because it was close to my daughters hospital room. This was mid-August ----. I couldn't have been more pleased. Clean, comfortable, pretty room. I felt safe leaving early and coming home late. Perks like breakfast, computer access ---- and evening cookies made me feel at home. They offered a few grocery items which was a nice touch I thought. I wish I'd had more time each day to use the other facilities they offer like exercise equipment and swimming pool. Saff were exceptionally friendly and caring. They accepted deliveries and pick ups for me. There wasn't anything I didn't like about this place. Unfortunately my daughter is still in the hospital - months later. After my first - days in Houston I knew her hospital stay would be a long one and so I had to make other less expensive long term arrangements. But I would stay at La Quinta Westchase again in a heartbeat. And the points I earned at the Westchase location, I was able to use another La Quinta in another state.

Stayed two nights the first of July ----. It met my needs when searching for a hotel close to LAX. Free airport shuttle, lobby bar, restaurant and walking distance to rental car companies. My wait to check-in was minimal and was greeted by a friendly staff person. I stayed on the --th floor but there were four elevators so my wait time for one was usually under a minute. I also walking about -- minutes for an In-N-Out burger for lunch.

Hotel was basic but good for what I needed. Lobby was shabby but had lovely old photographs of New York performers -- Josephine Baker, Fred Astaire, Lionel Barrymore etc. Room was small but Internet connection worked -- yay! Bed comfy, wish I'd brought earplugs but that's not their fault. I couldn't get the shower to work, so washed my hair in the sink. If you stay here, you may want to test your shower before you take off your clothes...

Just returned from a - night stay at this hotel paid an extra $-- per night for view of the Empire State Building could lie in bed at night and the view was fantastic. Not a big room but you are only sleeping in it. Wardrobe big enough to put two large cases in it and our clothes. Room clean, towels changed each day. Staff were very helpful on check-in, Assistance and transportation. Tick Tock Diner food very good and plenty of it. This is my second time at the New Yorker and would recommend this hotel and would stay there again if I went back to New York. Used the --hr free service for the internet and had no problems.

I visited the hotel ----th of November and based my choice of hotel on reviews from this site. I was not dissapointed. Paid $-- per nite extra - on an already fantastic rate, to secure a times square view room on --th floor. FANTASTIC. My only crticism of the room that it could have done with a little more drawer space - but thats it. Maid service fantastic, very efficient and chatty. Front desk very welcoming and always there to help. I will definately be returning to this hotel on my next visit to NYC in February.

We stayed during the -th of July weekend. This was a great place and we were very happy with the accommodations and service. There was a little something for all the family. The rooms were clean and roomy. We had a great view of the --th street mall. The kids were able to wander about on their own. There was plenty of security on the mall. We were surprised to find an outdoor movie viewing behind the clock tower. Families were sitting in lawn chairs and blankets watching a movie on a big TV screen. In the warm summer evening it was wonderful. There are plenty of restaurants and shops for whatever you may need or feel like enjoying. There was a small mall toward one end and a theater. Coors Field is within walking distance. All the other amenities mentioned by other reviews are there and very convenient. We will definitely stay here again when visiting Denver.

I stayed at Distrikt, Sept -----. Overall the experience was great.I requested a early check-in and when i arrived my room was ready. Soon as I entered my room there was a knock on the door and to my surprise I was welcomed with a gift of chocolate brownies. The room was average size for NYC. Not too big not too small. Enough space for two adults. The hotel halls were also nice. On my floor there were - other rooms, so didnt hear much noise. The bathroom was very clean. The overall apperance was modern and clean. I also like the fact that --hours a day you had to use your room key to ride the elevator. So if you are not staying there you can only go as far as the lobby. Also, each night I was welcomed with chocolate and a card showing me the weather for the following day. 
The location of the hotel was excellent. Not far from Time Square and other attractions. Overall, this hotel is a good choice. The price was right, the location is great, and the hotel was wonderful. I would definitely stay here again.

I stayed at the hotel last week for two nights. As a Diamond member, I was upgraded to the Lofts. Nice room with a balcony. Staff was helpful and the breakfasts were okay. Perfect location to explore the Gaslamp District. Only wish the Padres were playing at home. You are right near the stadium. 
The only problem was the train that came back a couple of times a day. I'm not talking about the trolleys that go by all the time. When the train goes by, it lets off a very LOUD, and long, whistle. It was after -pm when I heard the whistle, so I called the front desk and asked how often the train comes by. They said it also comes around -am. Maybe it was because of the direction my room faced, but I couldn't see how any room would have not heard it. So, if you happen to be staying here, just make sure your room doesn't face toward the Convention Center.

Trump is a beautiful hotel inside and out located on the Chicago River. I stayed in a one bedroom full kitchen suite. My room was extraordinary. View was nice. The bathroom has a walk in shower and separate toilet. Main distinction in bath area is the in mirror television. The suite has a full kitchen equip with dishes and pots and pans and a microwave oven. Living room has a sectional and a desk with wifi. Suite comes with a fireplace. I was impressed.
Issues I had: none of the televisions works throughout my stay, luckily I was not there to watch television.
Parking is -- dollars a day! The guys that parked my vehicle returned is covered in what looked like paint, but I was able to wash it off. No one acknowledged it!
When I went to complain that -- dollars a day should protect my vehicle from such things everyone looked as though I was crazy and hilucinating and imagined the whole thing. 
I called to have the televisions fixed to no avail. The televisions continued to shut on and off all night waking from my sleep and creeping me out.
Upon check out the service clerks were extremely snuddy and unapologetic for my stay. For someone who has recieved perfect service at places that I have spent less money the tower of Trumps is not worth it! ---+ dollars per night should include a few perks for the guest, and at the very least superb customer service. 
After I wrote a letter to the hotel about my stay I was compensated for - nights of parking.
But I gave this hotel an overall of average, because I will not patronize the hotel again! I would rather pay more money to a hotel I know will fully satisfy my needs. Anything more than average mean I would stay there again, and this is not the case for the Trump towers.

As the reviews say fantastic location so central to everything.
We were very lucky we contacted hotel before arriving to say a special occasion and the Concierge lady called Gloria was fantastic .We stayed on --th Floor Executive room great size and great room ammenites, we never had breakfast as wanted to eat out so cannot comment but for the Travelzoo rate the room was excellent no complaints large room and certainley very clean. All staff were lovely, would definatley stay there again if we went back to New York.
Got cheaper Theatre tickets from Theatre desk in Hotel and better seats than we did booking before we went
Found great restaurant Wolfganges Park Avenue best steak we have ever had (need to book) Elios Italian again need to book.

I was a bit dubious about staying at this hotel because nobody had heard of it! The reason for this, I found out, is that it just recently opened two months ago. I was traveling with my daughter (-- years) and my nephew (--) and we were in New York for a week. The room was very clean and for New York standards it was quite spacious. The bedding and linens are outstanding! I only stayed here for a night since we had already booked the rest of the trip in another hotel in Times Square, but I would happily return to this location instead.
The manager, a very nice lady, came out one day to greet us and gave us a very warm welcome, she made us feel at home. Please consider this hotel on your next visit to NYC....you won't regret it!

Located in the Marina District, away from the hustle of Union Square and high room rates, this delightful motor inn offers large, tastefully furnished rooms, all of which are non-smoking. It is only blocks to Union Street, home to numerous boutiques and restaurants. Two blocks toward the bay is Chestnut Street, also offering local shopping and restaurants. Believe it or not, the room rate also includes inside parking. Just - block away is the stop for the -- Stockton bus which takes one, in minutes, to Fisherman's Wharf, North Beach, China Town and Union Square. In the opposite direction, there is bus service to Golden Gate Park. I have been a guest there many times and have never been disappointed.

I've stayed at the Grant many times. A superb property.
The ONLY complaint is that they ALWAYS end up charging for something at the mini bar you didn't use, AFTER you leave.
This time I called the front desk, got transferred to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""accounting"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and went to voice mail.
I gave up, and that's what they count on! Cheap and Petty!!!!

We made our booking through Priceline, so we were not expecting the greatest room. You can sometimes get squeezed into the worse space they have, thanks to getting a cut price deal. Having said that, when we checked in, the front desk staff gave us a choice of two rooms. Although our window faced a brick wall, the room was spacious, clean, and comfortable. 
Concierge was fabulous.. The guy there helped us with dinner, brunch & show bookings every day. He gave recommendations and then even called our cell phone to advise of booking status. 
We didn't dine in the restaurant, so I can't comment on food, however I know they have a live jazz band in there on Sunday afternoons, which I could hear from the lobby, and it sounded wonderful. 
The hotel is a short walk to grand central station, which connects you to everywhere. Get a unlimited train pass for $-- if you're staying longer that three days. Otherwise, it's a -- minute walk to central park, and -- minutes in the opposite direction to walk to time square.

The hotel was nice but we stayed the wrong night because there were teenagers down the hall who were having a party of some sort. It was crazy for a little bit. However, the rooms are nice and big. There are - flat screen tv's in the suite. Did not eat there so I cannot comment about the food. However, it is very convenient if you have to go in and out of Philly. Despite the noise and security did finally put an end to it, I would stay here again. Staff is friendly too.

Fell in love with this hotel. Very close to the pier and restaurants. Enjoy the fireplaces outside the hotel after a long day to enjoy a glass of wine. The hotel staff was so friendly and helpful of where to go, but also will advise you of any safety concerns being a single person in their town.
Beautiful lobby, clean rooms, shuttle to the medical center. This surpassed my expectations for a three-star hotel. Very much enjoyed the stay and will be coming here again.

I have stayed in Yotels in international airports and in NYC. The price in NYC is not at all a bargain -- it is as expensive as any - start hotel (if not more) and yet the rooms are smaller. The mission of Yotel was, once upon a time, to provide innovative, compact rooms at an AFFORDABLE price (meaning, to most people, priced well below that of a --- start hotel). Yotel has strayed completely from its mission

You can feel the history from the exterior facade of the hotel and the gates to Gramercy Park in front of you. The hotel has embellished this with wonderful interior details, graceful furnishings and rooms with a period feel, but all the conveniences you would seek. The Terrace restaurant upstairs is an oasis. While you feel secluded by the Park, the hotel is so central that going anywhere, uptown or down is simple and quick. We walked everywhere, but short cab rides are always available. The staff was pleasant, efficient and always available. I would not stay anywhere else in Manhattan.

My assistant booked this hotel based on the beautiful pics on their site. Once we arrived in the hotel we were assigned a room (#----) which was just horrible; dirty, hair in the shower, sink not drainig, ac not working, - of the - light bulbs broken and just not a clean room... I has been a while since I stayed in such a horrible place. Don't go there unless you've checked it out. The place may have some history but that's about it...!!! Never ever again!!!

We were informed that the pool area converts back to a spa-only pool after Labor Day. If you are looking for a serene environment for a relaxing massage, you may not find what you seek on a summer weekend at the Kin Spa.

Very basic hotel but at least is clean.
good points: location, just a few blocks away from the Chinese theatre, area seems safe at least during the day, small grocery store around the corner. Free wi-fi (only good in the lobby). Clean Rooms.
Bad points: strong smell in the room, lack of ventilation, window wouldn't opened. Wi-fi in the room was terrible, had to go to the lobby to get a connection.

We (my wife and I and - kids aged -- to --) stayed four days at the Hyatt Wild Oak Ranch. We knew in August it would be hot and we weren't wrong - - days all over --- degrees! 
The Hyatt - bedroom we stayed in was very nice - clean , well-decorated in a Southwest theme, all the details you would want including fully-loaded kitchen, flat screen TV's and washer-dryer. Lots of room. for a family of -. My wife and I were in King Room, and kids were in other room with a full size bed and a pullout couch. The pull-out was fairly good quality as pullouts go, but we had expected two full size beds as per our stay in Hyatt Pinon Pointe (Sedona, AZ) a year earlier - we asked about that and were told that half the rooms have pullout couches and half have - beds - and that we should have asked ahead of time to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""request"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" the two beds. Live and learn. 
The pool is very nice, although it skews a little too young for the age of my kids - the depth is just - feet all-around, except at the zero -entry where it's even less. That said, the pool slides (one outside, one sheltered inside) are fun and very fast! One day the outside pool slide was closed due to a problem (bees, I heard). I thus asked to go to the Hyatt Hill Country Resort very nearby. I first asked the Wild Oak front desk, who told me """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but said that if I wanted I could call the other Hyatt myself and ask and explain the circumstances. I asked if they would make the call to their sister hotel, but they declined - which I thought was bothersome. They didn’t really seem to care. So I did call the Hill Country - their representative was extremely sympathetic, but said that they were sold out and their pool was just too overcrowded to let more people in . We swung by that Hyatt later in the day just to see it – and she was correct – their pool was extremely crowded. I gained a much greater appreciation for the small numbers at the Wild Oak pool, where we could play water volleyball over the net or go down the waterslide pretty much whenever we wanted. And the lazy river at the back of the property. So overall, very nice pools, especially for the toddler to --years old age range.
We also did the typical San Antonio events – the Alamo (one-hour including listening to the historian was about all it took), Sea World is - miles away (surprisingly uncrowded except the Lost Lagoon water park that was massively over-crowded), Schlitterbahns water park which was extremely crowded but worth it, and the Natural Bridge Caverns which was a fun walk under the earth, as well as the driving safari tour next door.

Want a cup of tea? Forget it. You either have to line up for -- minutes at the aforementioned Top of the Mark ( no priority is given to hotel guests) or order from the glacially slow room service. The staff happily suggest you use the facilities in a couple of nearby hotels - indeed, they give every impression of wishing there were no guests in the hotel at all, so they can get on with running a tourist attraction, which is sadly what this place has become. The rooms are tiny with very limited storage space (no drawers!) and dominated by a massive bed (v comfy) and huge TV (unfortunately providing the dreadful Lodgenet service). If you 're lucky enough to get hold of room service and they actually deliver your order, there is no space to sit and eat. On the upside, the room decor is recent, period-correct and stylish, with opening windows and smart marble bathrooms, and well looked after and clean. Noise from the cable cars might be an issue for some people but for the middle of a major city, the location is pretty quiet. There are the usual chain hotel corner-cutting annoyances - $---day for -mb wireless, a very mean allocation of threadbare towels and toiletries - and a general sense that, behind the scenes, things are not going well.

My husband and I had a great week-long stay on our first trip to Boston. The hotel was sold out due to a baseball game so it was crowded, but the staff handled everything well.

Some guests with children need to learn manners - it is never OK to for children to throw food on the floor and then pick it off the floor to eat it - but even given that, the hotel staff quickly tried to clean the mess and maintain order. Also, the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""to-go"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" breakfast bags were great for the two excursions we took to Cape Cod and the Maine Sea Coast.
We were there the week before Labor Day and there were two local shuttles in service. We used the shuttle every morning then walked Boston and took the sight-seeing trolley and subway during the day, finally returning on the shuttle every evening. Frankly, if you're not prepared to get out there and walk and take the subway, maybe you're not ready for Boston. You can't appreciate the city from a hotel shuttle. Boston is called """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""America's Walking City"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" because to experience it, you need to get out there. Don't criticize the hotel shuttle. No one except the taxi drivers are there waiting to haul your behind from sight to sight. 
The housekeeping was great and we had no maintenance issues. The hotel was by the Boston Medical Center but we had no problems with sirens or activity keeping us up at night. I'm normally a light sleeper in hotels and if my sleep had been interrupted, I'd be so cranky right now that this review would reflect that.
It would have been nice to have more restaurants nearby but the hotel was accomodating with take-out and delivery menus. But over the next few months the area will be much improved. There is a Ground Round being built on site and right next door a Quizno's and Dunkin' Doughnuts are going in. By the end of this year the area is going to be totally different. 
We enjoyed our first trip to Boston and look forward to returning. The Hampton Inn Crosstown Center was a great value and we would definitely stay there again. If you have any questions you can e-mail my husband and I at codiesparents@wmconnect.com

Location is the only reason to book at this hotel. The hotel is located in the middle of Ohare. Strolling from gate to hotel to gate without the hassles of traffic or the blue line is stress free. So close that you can hear the roar of the engines and smell the jet fuel. But hey! 
Now for the rest of the deal.....
The room was on the small side, with a huge flatscreen TV, comfortable bed, nice bath, no robe, good desk. My room was drafty and cold, even after turning the thermostat up. Not sure where the leak was, but I ended up putting on my winter coat as a robe when working at the desk. 
Amenities come with stiff extra charges, from exercise access to internet access. Do not open the toothbrush-toothpast kit unless you want to shell out - or - bucks.
Check in and check out counter was lightly staffed, but the automated system works well. The convenience of doing flight check in and boarding pass at the hotel was nice.
I bought a - buck day pass and took the blue line into Chicago. Ate at a great Italian place south of the loop instead of dining at the chains in the hotel and aiport.

The hotel has an excellent value for the money. It is well located in Soho, with a MTA station - blocks from it and it is very close to (by walk) the several fancy stores in the neighborhood. The staff was very helpful too. The only suggestion I would make is to improve the shower curtains, because it does not reach the ground what makes easy to wet the whole bathroom.
