I highly recommend this hotel if you want convenience, a well trained staff, upscale and moderate price.

Actually, I was pleasantly surprised with this room. Everyone in my group agreed the beds were so comfortable. The room, bathroom and bed was fresh and neat. However, like all of San Diego, the parking lot was small and unfriendly to large full size trucks. We will definitely stay here again.

You'll read those words on their internet website and I found them to be totally true. We have stayed here on - separate occasions and have always found them to be one of the best places to stay in San Diego. Great location, reasonable prices, excellent restaurant, and top-notch service. Shuttle service means you may not need a rental car if you are just planning on staying at the hotel for a short visit. We have always had a great marina view from our room, which by the way is very spacious and equipped with all the amenities you might need. Do yourself a favor and stay here the next time you are visiting San Diego

We got what we really wanted: an affordable room with a bed, a bathroom, and wireless internet at no extra charge, close to downtown and Union square. Everyone who needs anything else (a view, service, any kind of luxury, or even just a room where you can spend a day), should look elsewhere.
What hit us on our entry, and stayed with us pretty much until the end of our stay, is that this hotel reeks of decay. I read that the place was supposed to have been renovated a few years ago, and if it was, I'm glad we haven't gone there before that. The lobby is okay (it's run-down in an almost charming way), but our floor (the -th) smelled of urine. Fortunately, the smell did not creep much into our room. The only thing that looked new indeed was the tiny bathroom.
Our room was very small, and offered basically no amenities, but a coffee maker (which we had to clean ourselves -- not a big deal, but what are the stars given for?) We had no view whatsoever (we saw the opposite wall about six feet from our window), but on the positive side, we heard nothing of the street noise, which was pretty loud. Instead, we could generate our own loud noise with the heater, which had two settings: freeze-at-night and no-sleep-for-you.
We haven't tried room service or the fitness center, but we found the restaurant pretty good both for breakfast and dinner.

-- year old hotel shows its age. Excellent friendly staff. Good wifi. Usual Embassy Suite free breakfast with a bonus of excellent homemade green chili. Evening cocktail hour moves from bar to atrium, some days hors doeuvres, other days only pretzels or chips. Christmas parties held in the atrium are very noisy.

One night stay over the -th of July to see the fireworks. View from the room was very good (top floor bay side). Fireworks did not disappoint. Best part of the experience beyond the fireworks...the pillows...just great...wish I could take them home with me.
Worst part... the huge (tree inches long ...not counting the antennae) cockroach in the bathroom. As this room was on floor --, had to wonder about what the lower floor rooms must experience. 
Next morning showed up for the free breakfast at -:--AM and was told that they did not serve after -:--AM except on Saturdays and Sundays...not holidays. This is NOT the world-class-customer-is-right attitude I expected from a Best Western property. It wasn't the reality of the situation it was the surly demeanor of the employee that was offensive.

I stayed at this property for two days in town for business. I wish I could have been able to spend more time enjoying the hotel. Sadly, as business duties called, I was in my room for only when I needed to be to catch some sleep.
I flew in on September -th and the hotel staff was extremely gracious and accommodating. Check in process was seamless and my room was ready when I arrived. I have stayed at a few JW Marriott's before but this one was the most comfortable to date. The room was perfectly sized, the bathroom was very nice and comfortable - it was not too big; it had a great bathtub perfect for soaking my tired bones, and the lighting was ideal.
The bed was one of the most comfortable mattresses I have ever slept on. I slept so well for the time I was in there, wish I could have been in bed longer. The best part was the true blackout curtains. Pitch black even middle of the day. The hotel did this right - and I was very grateful for it. Also many times in hotels while you are in your room, other guests can be fairly loud. At this hotel, I barely heard anything when in my room, except for the person in the adjacent room leaving once and not being kind to catch the door before it slammed (really, people?).
I ate at the restaurant, and while pricey, the service was fast, and the food was good. However, I would probably only eat at Level III again if I was in a pinch, which I was when I returned from working an event and on my feet for -- hours straight. Food was essential - quickly - and they delivered.
I also received numerous packages for the event that required being loaded into my vehicle. The staff was extremely helpful to assist with this. When I returned from the event, I had even more boxes - perhaps double the amount - that needed to be shipped back to the office. The staff was outstanding in offering their assistance. Mike in particular at the bellstand literally stood in the entrance drive with me sorting through all of the boxes as I affixed shipping labels. He then kindly loaded them onto a cart to take to the back shipping area to await for the driver the next day. SO HELPFUL, and I truly appreciated his additional attention to my needs.
If I had to be picky about anything with this property, I would say it was the shower stall. It was pretty tight quarters, and there simply wasn't anywhere to put my stuff. The metal grate tray screwed into the wall was loose, thus it drooped at an angle. It wouldn't hold even my trial size toiletries without falling to the floor. It would be #- - helpful to repair this in room #----, and #- - I would recommend installing a small corner shelf in the back corner of the stall that would hold at least a few small bottles - - perhaps - so that they are in reach easily. That shelf could also be used for shaving, so that there is more of an angle for bending over.
My final recommendation to those staying at the hotel is to really consider if you need a rental car or not. The charge, with tax, for valet parking was $--.-- per night. I'm not joking! The public transportation in San Francisco is excellent, and if you must have a rental car, there are options like zipcar or gocar for hourly rentals, or there is even a rental facility a block away for Hertz and other major rental car companies. I'm just sayin'.....if you need a car for the day, rent it, return it, and avoid the valet fees. I only had a car because I was in town for business, but good gravy that is steep. And I can think of several different ways that I could spend $-- per day - and valet parking isn't one of them.
I hope that one day in the near future that work will bring me back to the JW Marriott San Francisco Union Square hotel....and that I have more time to enjoy one of my favorite cities - and to spend a little more time indulging myself in this lavish facility. Thanks for a great stay!

The best thing about this hotel is that it is within walking distance from Coors Field. It is more like a motel, with the hotel room door accessible on the outside. The room was clean, breakfast was good, and the desk staff helpful. I just my room door was only accessible on the inside of the hotel.

The Congress was a view to a bygone era. It is a lovely building with gorgeous architecture. The lobby is stunning, with a lot of marble, brass, and velvet. The staff was very pleasant and helpful. Our room was large, with a wonderful view of Grant Park. The beds were comfortable and the room was clean. The bathroom was roomy and clean. The location could not be better, as it is right on Michigan avenue with an amazing view of the park.

We arrived to the hotel and found that Expedia had not passed on the details of our reservation properly to the hotel so we found ourselves with the wrong type if room so be careful of booking with Expedia. Having said that the hotel did everything to out it right. The hotel is a great place to explore la however food and drinks and parking are too expensive, more even than the Mondrian which spoilt an otherwise great time. I would stay here again.

We stayed here for three nights while visiting Family and were pleasantly surprised at the pure comfort of this Hotel. There's always complimentary coffee & tea available at a --hr beverage station. intenet & printer service always available, and a --hr fitness room with free weights & a bench, treadmill, cardio elliptical machine, and stationary bike (all equipped with TV's). I can't wait to come back and visit. I will definitely be staying here again.

We picked the Chancellor for its location and it was by far one of the best positioned hotels in San Francisco. Union Square is such a handy location, with everything at your fingertips. 
The hotel itself is a nice, boutique hotel. The staff are very friendly and eager to help. The rooms, as per the other reviews, are small and the bathrooms need a bit of an update, but for the price, you can't complain - the water was always hot, the towels always fresh! The free wi-fi was great and the coffee in the lobby was lovely and always hot.
I wouldn't suggest you stay at this hotel if you are travelling with a baby, the walls are a little thin and each time our daughter woke up in the night we would worry she was waking up the whole floor. As the room wasn't that big, it was a bit of struggle to fit a portacot, but we knew that before we arrived.
We would, and have, suggested this hotel to others, especially couples travelling to San Fran that want a great location.

This is my first review, which is prompted because I had to say how wonderful Evelyn at the front desk treated us during our stay. Every request or problem we had was resolved by her to our satisfaction, and she was always so pleasant!
Our room had two double beds and it was still pretty roomy compared to rooms at other hotels. The location is pretty much perfect. A main subway is right around the corner, and you can walk to most of the big midtown attractions.
We did not eat breakfast in the hotel because it's just too crowded. The room was very clean but I was not crazy about housekeeping.
Since my daughter plans to attend college in New York, I am sure we will be staying here again many more times.

There is also a children's area where they can write and leave a letter for Santa. There is a wonderful Tiki Lounge with great food that is downstairs and you may not even realize it is there. The gift shop also has lovely jewelry at very reasonable prices. The staff is attentive and friendly, and I got a terrific rate online, so check for deals. The staff made sure I got a room with a view even though the rate was so reasonable. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay. We were upgraded. Beautiful classic room. Staff was courteous and helpful. Morning coffee in the lobby. The location is excellent - the is such a walkable town and The Lenox is in the middle of it all. Trains (the T), Prudential Center, Newbury Street, etc nearby.

The computer cart was great - we could surf the web about the places we were planning on visiting and the university. In addition to using the van, the hotel booked us a very reasonably priced towncar for transport to-from the airport. The Watertown is very new, clean, and has cool modern decor. In the area, the Himalyan Restaurant and the Portage Bay Cafe (- block away) were very good. We enjoyed Seattle and staying at the Watertown was a definite plus.

We arrived by bus to port authority and walked to hotel- only about - minutes or so walk across broadway. The breakfast buffet that's included for free was awesome. On my first morning I discovered I had no regular coffee and worse, a broken coffee maker. I reported it to the front desk and by the time I returned that afternoon, the maker was replaced and I had more regular coffee than I knew what to do with.

Breakfast each morning was OK. The hot buffet were the same items each morning I stayed. When I had to eat, the made-to-order egg station was still not open. That was at ---- through ----, generally. I am unsure when they opened.
The night time reception was nice and the drink selection was far larger than a typical Homewood Suites, who do a similar thing. The snacks were fine.
All in all, I will stay here again. The traffic in front of the hotel took some getting used to, especially running out for an evening meal. But by the time I left the hotel, three nights later, I had become more familiar with traffic patterns.

The front desk clerk told us at the end of our trip that we should have been given a card that has a taxi cab phone # on it. Get one to carry with you and call for a ride if you cannot get the shuttle. Wish we had known this.
Overall, the people at this hotel are very friendly. We did have a few problems as stated above but the management there went above and beyond the call of duty to ensure that everything was addressed and handled.
We would stay there if we visit again.

The only negative I would have for the Rivington is its location. A definite cab ride from the main attractions, on arrival after basically a day of travelling the hotel is anything but welcoming.
However, do not let that put you off. This place is ice cool, and surrounds with you every comfort to ensure you have an enjoyable stay. The piece de resistance is the view, the glass frontage providing some dramatic windows to the Manhattan skyline. We were upgraded to a suite for our first wedding anniversary, and I have rarely had a better night's sleep on the super-comfy bed.
The service was good, but not spectacular, although our general experience of NY courtesy was surprisingly disappointing, so the Rivington's service levels were above average in comparison.
If you are looking for a safe chain hotel in the heart of the city the Rivington is definitely not for you. However, if you're after something a little different and cutting edge, give the Rivington a go.

Terrific location in the Back Bay area. Old world charm, but with contemporary styled rooms. Stayed for several nights in a Deluxe room (but no """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""padded luggage bench"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in our room as stated on their website) and a night in King room. No coffee-tea making in the room, but available in the guest lounge - an opportunity to mingle with other guests. Free Wifi, but disappointingly slow. Both our rooms faced the back laneway and we got woke up at -am on a Thursday by a garbage truck, so maybe a room facing Newbury St would be better, but it's a lively street so maybe not any quieter. We were staying for only one night in San Antonio over Christmas and just needed something clean and comfortable. This Days Inn was cheaper but I would not stay there again. The carpet and bed covers were old and dusty and the decor was not inviting. The bathroom was clean, but fixtures were so cheap that the plastic curtain came unhinged easily, and the toilet was close to getting clogged. The hotel was full so when we went down for breakfast in the morning there was hardly anything left, but we could see there was not much choice to start with. Would not recommend.

Check in was a bit slow, but we arrived -- minutes before official check-in time, and some folks ahead of us in the line didn't have rooms ready yet, so the staff had to do some shuffuling to get them into a room, which slowed the process a bit. The room was small, but that is typical in Manhatten. It was very comfortable, with updated bathroom and very clean. The beds were fine, plenty of hot water in the shower and the heat was easily controlled in the room. Not sure what else you could want for the price this close to the Broadway theaters. We will be staying here on our next trip to NYC.

This is a wonderful resort, although expenside, steeped in old-world Mexican atmosphere in a very private setting. But the food is not commensurate with the hotel's alleged high standards. A Chicken Ceasar Salad at lunch, for example, was fit for a Perkin's Restaurant. Actually, Perkins might serve a better food. Don't expect outstanding cuise at the Royal Palms.

stayed at this hotel with my wife and son from -- to -- October ----. Had a fantastic time the rooms were bright and large the service was exceptional. Profesional staff.
Have breakfast by the pool which we enjoyed very much, however, a couple had a pair of dogs by the pool that we found a bit strange. We did not know that the hotel allowed people to bring pets in the eating area.

My sisters and I have returned to this hotel annually for shopping excursion-get-aways and each time we agree that it is IDEAL! The hotel location is perfect for shopping, entertainment, dining (the Daily Grill is hard to beat!), and how fun to have a Starbucks outside the back door. The rooms are large and clean and the pool is a bonus. The staff is attentive, friendly, helpful, and makes you feel like they are proud you have chosen their hotel for your stay.

We came to New York for a girl's weekend and to celebrate my friend's birthday. From the moment that we arrived at the hotel we were given the royal treatment. We arrived very early in the day and unfortunately could not get into our room despite the efforts of the guest service provider who was trying very hard to accommodate us and get us in early, there simply was nothing available. After picking up theater tickets and going to lunch we returned to the hotel to find our room ready to go. The room itself was spacious enough for four adults especially under New York standards. We were in our room for a short while when to our surprise champagne and chocolates were delivered from the hotel (thanks Kevin!!) for my friend's birthday. After leaving for the theater and dinner we returned to the hotel to find wine, chocolate covered strawberries, popcorn and a movie voucher, this time we believe from the bellman (thanks Jean!!). The hotel itself is in the financial district, a block from the Rector street subway line, across the street from the World Trade Center Memorial, and - blocks from Battery Park.
I would recommend this hotel to anyone that asked. Although not located in the hustle and bustle of Times Square the hospitality of the employees at this hotel made the location well worth it.

The hotel has an amazingly beautiful facade, but what lies within is not the deco reno I expected. It's a pretty standard Weston, nothing extraordinary. The layout was sort of choppy with check-in up a flight with just a few small desks, I imagine to look exclusive, but often only one desk was manned so not terribly efficient. The restaurant choices were good. The rooms again were standard, but one night I had a terrible allergic reaction to something, and in the morning learned that others had had allergy symptoms too (cleaning solution? dust mites? who knows). The proximity to Campus Martius Park and Hart Plaza was wonderful, and during the week it was busy and exciting. Detroit deserves a better rep, it's a beautiful city and this hotel is close to many of the attractions.

This hotel is your basic Sheraton, good service, reasonable rates, and the rooms are good.....nothing to brag about but, good. The airport does get loud but that's what you should expect from a hOtel in this area. Basically the hotel served my needs

We did a weekend stay-cation in Manhattan and chose Andaz Wall Street, mostly because it was at the other end of Manhattan from where we live. The hotel, in the Financial District, is in close proximity to TriBeCa, so there are great restaurant options. Also close to Brooklyn Bridge.
The service was friendly; the room was well appointed with good attention to detail, ie, iPod, docking stations and good sound, modern bathrooms, good pillows. 
There was also a cool farmers market and a beer garden in the plaza adjacent to the hotel. 
Check in was efficient, everything done quickly with iPads, instead of the usual reception desk set up. 
Overall it was a cool place and i would recommend it.

Loved it from the minute I walked in. Friendly service, modern furnishings, great location right off of Herald Square. Extremely clean and nice finishes in the decent sized guest room. Comfortable bed and the neatest pressed sheets I've ever seen. This hotel snob was impressed!

Great greeting with a glass of Champaigne. very helpful bell staff, and valet parking. clean. Beautiful view of the river. Room service and Parking are not cheap, but location is wonderful, and service was all I would ever ask for.

Hotel is old but in good shape. We stayed in one of the two room King suites on the third floor away from the freeway. Very easy to get on and off of the - freeway and to --- and --- north and south. Lots of restaurant and shopping options within a mile. Not sure if I will stay here again but if you need a decent hotel with breakfast, and don't need Internet, you could do worse.

The Hotel website was somewhat deceiving, really hyped it up. I was dissapointed it was not what I expected at all. The employees at desk were very helpful and tried to make us comfortable but I was alittle freaked out about the hotels surroundings, quite an eyeopener could be looked at as good for our kids or not.

This hotel is great because it is in the center of the city and downtown. It is so in the heart of the city every time we would walk to a new site we would pass it on the way. We were able to walk to every site and attraction you could ever want to see. The staff was nice. We didn't like the Heavenly Bed system that Westin is so proud of. My back and neck were so messed up we HAD to go to a spa the day we checked out and I am still hurting. Our TV didn't work and the staff was very helpful in promptly sending up a technician. Unfortunately he was in our room for quite a while and we were tired so I asked him to leave and just fix it the next day while we were out and he refused to leave. I stayed at the Intercontinental for one night in August during a business trip. The staff was extremely helpful and attentive and the rooms were clean and spacious. I would recommend this hotel to a friend and would return if in the area.

I stayed over the memorial day weekend and I enjoyed my stay. The staff was very friendly and helpful, the rooms were clean and I think this hotel is in a great location. It is minutes from the riverwalk, shopping and the best restaurants. I'm from Dallas and whenever I'm in San Antonio this is where i'm going to stay.
Sincerely,
Angela

Lovely hotel, stayed one night at the start of my trip before I met up with friends. Short walk from small beach, great if it's hot (which it was). Very close to Navy Pier. This La Quinta is a new build in an otherwise largely undeveloped part of North-West Austin. The hotel and its services were fine and the pool was an afternoon suntrap. We enjoyed my stay here. My sole purpose was to see the memorials and monuments and this was the perfect location. had a Starbucks - huge plus!

I booked a corner king room with a deep Japanese tub. This time I was only on the -th floor, so didn't have much of a view, but the room had big windows and a comfortable bed. 
 Included in my room package (booked at the hotel's website, jdv.com) was a $-- coupon for O-Izakaya, the newly-opened restaurant on the -st floor, where I sampled high grade sake and small dishes of Japanese fusion cuisine. I always enjoy the deep Japanese bath, but was puzzled to see that the shower just outside of the tub had been removed, making it difficult to wash before getting into the soaking tub. Just a small quibble for an otherwise perfect visit.

My wife and I stayed here during a huge snow storm. The entire staff was very helpful and accommodating around check-in and check-out times. The snow had most of the city shut down, including most taxis. Their staff arranged for a ride, chased the driver around a few blocks as he couldn't get down the snowy side streets, and called the driver as he was driving us to make sure we made it to the airport timely and safely. My hat is off to this top notch hotel!!!

I stayed here during a professional conference at a nearby hotel. The room itself was a little dated, but clean. After I unpacked that night I realized I left my deodorant at home. Hotels in New York City have become expensive - really, really expensive. The city has definitely bounced back from ---- and the hotel rates certainly reflect that. As I mentioned, the room was large for NYC and we had plenty of room in the - days we occupied it. What I first noticed about the hotel is how quiet it is! The subway for the - train is half a block away; there are plenty of good diners in the area; a newstand is right next door (so you can buy your copy of the New York Post and read it over a good cup of coffee and a bagel across the street at the Euro cafe!). Stayed in room ---. The first night there I was attacked by bed bugs. I've had bad experiences at Fairfield Inns in the past, see East Rutherford, but I was very happy with this hotel. It is newly renovated from a Holiday Inn Express, which is how my GPS still sees it, and it shows that they've done recent work. We stayed here bookend-ing the Labor Day weekend.
The reception area was standard for this brand of hotel. We were at first told our room wasn't ready when we arrived around --:--pm. We were offered a different room, facing the street, if we wanted one immediately, and they offered to hold our luggage. I declined this, but as we waited in the lobby devising our plan for the day, the front desk made a couple calls to have the room status verified. Happily the room was ready, and we could unload our luggage directly.
The rooms we had, --- and --- respectively, were identical two king rooms. They had mini-fridges, microwaves, and mini balconies. The balconies were not big enough for a chair, but they did give a good view of the pool, so we could see how busy it was before going down. The balconies also gave a good view of the fireworks over Seaworld (a Summer only event). The beds and pillows were nice, and the bathroom was clean (bathroom cleanliness is a big issue for me).
The pool was relatively small compared to the size of the hotel, but this was only a problem on Labor Day itself. I would imagine the place is packed on weekends, but we also used the pool on Tuesday and we were the only ones there.
The breakfast area was small compared to the size of the hotel, but again I imagine this is only a problem on weekends. Again on Labor Day, the breakfast area was packed, but on Tuesday there was ample space. The breakfast options were standard continental, with three waffle makers and frozen Jimmy Dean sandwiches (also a microwave to warm said Jimmy Dean sandwiches).
We used the garage each night we were here. There was available street parking each night on the blocks directly against the hotel. However, for ease of accessibility, the garage was our best option. The entrance to the garage has a peak in the driveway, so be sure to approach it at an angle if you're in a sedan. Also, the spaces in the middle are extremely tight. The spaces around the outside can be significantly larger, with the best spaces along the south wall. There were a few single spaces as well, protected by pillars, but these were generally full.
There is of course lots of places to eat in this area, and a happening night life. Generally, you shouldn't need a car once you arrive, if you don't want to leave the area. The hotel also offers a shuttle to Seaworld which covers the non-Summer park hours well. However, during the Summer you could easily miss the shuttle, which explains the number of taxis waiting around Seaworld.
Overall, this was a very good hotel for us. I was pleasantly surprised with the hotel and the staff. The hotel photos are very accurate.

This is, by far, the worst hotel I've ever stayed in. I couldn't be paid to stay here again. After only being in the room for one night, I cancelled the rest of my booked nights and made a reservation elsewhere. I REALLY should have taken note when a customer came in while I was checking in and told the front desk clerk that he was checking out several days early. I assumed he shortened his trip. -. Construction workers - I read the review from April that said there are construction workers staying here. I (incorrectly) assumed that they would be gone now that it was August. Unfortunately, they're not all together and there are so many of them that there's no way to be placed away from them. They cook on the sidewalk with several barbecue pits (seriously ghetto) and, while they cook, they talk to each other across the building. Yes, from one side to the other. Good luck having any quiet at all. When they're not yelling at each other, they're blaring a huge boombox out on the sidewalk on one end of the hotel and blaring music from a car with open doors on the other end of the hotel. Different songs, too, just in case you don't like one of the songs. Don't worry. You'll be able to hear both songs just fine from your room. 
-. Stains. Everywhere. On the carpet, the chair, the shower curtain, the walls. 
-. The carpet. My son had dark black feet after walking on the carpet for minutes. We all wore our shoes inside from that point on. I understand not cleaning the carpets after every guest...but you need to clean teh carpet once every ten years or so at least.
-. You can hear the water through the walls. So, every single time someone flushes, washes their hands or takes a shower, you'll know. When those amazing military men get up bright and early for weekend training, you'll know. They'll (unknowingly) wake you up, too, when they shower, use the bathroom and wash their hands. 
-. Cleanliness. The trash can wasn't even emptied out. In our trash? Used tissues and the previous guest's empty bottle of shampoo. It took up half the can, but I guess the cleaning lady figured there was at least another half a bag to be used so why not leave it? There were hairs on the toilet seat that didn't belong to my family. 
-. The neighborhood. Turn left after the hotel and you're in a place that you probably don't want to be after it turns dark. Although the air force base is minutes away, the area is not safe at all (the military personnel are plenty safe behind their guarded fences). I didn't feel safe at all when I made a wrong turn and was just thankful that it wasn't night and that I was able to navigate my way out.
Pros:
-. Price... but you get what you pay for here. 
-. It's close to Denny's (walking distance) ...but we never got the chance to eat there because we checked out as soon as we woke up the first morning we were there. 
-. The young man who works in the morning is extremely friendly. It sounded very obvious that he's aware of the noise issues with the construction workers. Unfortunately, I think they chose the nice chunk of money offered now by the construction workers versus the luxury of repeat business from other customers who may have overlooked other things if not for the noise from their construction workers. 
Red Roof has lost a customer for life because of this incident.

I just stayed here for New Years Eve because it is across the street from a party I was going to (Big Night Out San Diego--which I also recommend). My friends and I booked a deluxe double double room back in November because we knew that hotels in San Diego sell out for New Years Eve. However, when I checked in, I was told that I had a room with one king bed. I'm not a picky traveler, and I usually just go with the flow. But I had reserved two beds (for quite a bit of money) very far in advance and was not okay with being given a room different from what I reserved. After looking into our reservation, it was discovered that the booking company we had gone through was responsible for this mix-up--not the Hilton. 
It being New Years Eve, they were unable to provide us with a room with two double beds (as all rooms of that type were sold out). It was explained to us that since we had booked through a booking site, they couldn't refund us any money. It did take some time, but we were finally were told that there was a room available with a king size bed and a pull out couch bed. Obviously pull-out beds aren't very comfortable, but this was an upgraded room with a view and our options were limited. 
I was content at this point. However, Jason K. at the front desk went above and beyond to apologize for the inconvenience. After our new years' celebration, we returned to our hotel to find a complimentary bottle of wine, cheese plate, cracker plate, and hand written note from Jason (who had handled our situation earlier) apologizing for the inconvenience. 
The hotel was very nice, but it was Jason's extra effort that impressed me the most. If the rest of their staff is anything like him, I would recommend this hotel to anyone and everyone!

My sisters and I spent - nights here in October. New York is so much fun. We loved our double-double at the Radisson - there was plenty of room for - of us! We were a tiny bit cramped, but we fit. As the title says, Excellent location - decent hotel. Stayed here with my Wife on our first visit to New York. My extended family (four adults and three tots) spent a weekend at the Affinia Gardens Hotel. Although small, the hotel provided us with a suite and a wonderful staff. The suite itself contained a spacious living-room, a large bedroom, and a kitchen with full appliances and basic equipment. The decor was modern and well-maintained. In the lobby my family and I received much needed help with luggage, todder strollers and travel information. We were checked in by a very lovely lady (Mihela - not sure of spelling) who was very courteous and very quickly we had two great rooms on the --rd floor - one was a lovely corner room overlooking the Hudson which was very spacious and the other overlooking the great view of Times Sq. Both rooms were of a good size and at night were very peaceful with no noise. Great comfortable king size beds. The rooms had all the amenities you need for your stay and housekeeping was top notch every day.
The only minor thing we had a problem with in each room was the safe - neither worked and in fact ours was taken away as the problem could not be rectified but the Crowne Plaza did have a plan B in that they have a deposit box system which even though a little inconvenient if it was busy in the lobby was a very good option and completely out of the public eye and you needed to sign each time you used it for security purposes.
We eat in the hotel once and had the pre-theatre dinner at $-- and it was excellent. Drinks in the bar were a little pricey but this is New York - no different from the prices I pay in London where I work.
We found all the staff very helpful and very friendly - security was very good and the hotel is of course in a great location - subway on your doorstep as well as a stones throw from Macy's, central park and of course most of the broadway shows.
Finally thank you Emily in Customer Services who helped us with our reservation. Much appreciated in all you did - my parents had a great time.
As we love New York so much this is the only hotel that I will return to.

Wanting to save money, my husband and I booked with the Chelsea Lodge for our --day summer honeymoon in NYC, after reading many positive reviews on TripAdvisor.com. I can honestly say it's one of the best decisions we have ever made! 
We stayed in one of the deluxe suites downstairs (room D-, I believe), and we absolutely loved it. It was like having our own little apartment - we even started calling it """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""home"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in conversation, which just shows how comfortable we were! Unlike the more basic rooms, it had its separate bathroom, which was very nice! It also had an adjustable ceiling fan and window A-C unit, its own phone (with a direct line), free wifi, as well as a small TV with free cable (highly recommend channel ---, which is Cinemax On Demand and has free movies). The room was cleaned daily with the utmost care, and the staff is available as needed, but not in your face bothering you every five seconds like some other hotels.
In truth, you're not going to spend much time in your hotel room, since there is always so much to see and do in NYC, so why waste money on something more extravagant than you really need? The neighbourhood is terrific and very central - great for getting around the city! Everyone in Chelsea was very warm and friendly, which gave the neighbourhood a very calm, welcoming feel to it. There are a lot of wonderful restaurants in the area as well, so it was always easy to find something tasty to eat before heading off for the day or when returning in the evening. (Highly recommend Le Grainne Cafe for breakfast, as well as Roy's Pizza and La Bottega for dinner - the Chelsea Wine Cellar is also closeby and has a lot of delicious wines, good prices and will sell you a $- corkscrew if you're buying a corked bottle and need one. All of these places had excellent staff and service!)
Honestly, we have absolutely zero complaints about this hotel and can't wait to visit again!

Stayed one night in a - bedroom suite on the --nd floor.

The only negative thing is that the lounge is not extremely big and can't hold all guests at once. There was a queue for breakfast, but we waited only -- minutes so all in all I find that acceptable.
Did not dine in the hotel so can't comment on that.
All in all I'd rate my stay as good but not over the top.
Would probably stay here again cause the location is great and service is good. Not sure if I would book a suite again though.

We enjoyed our stay and would definitely return and recommend it to others.

Holiday Inn is convenient to Travis Heights as well as the Capitol are, -th St. But the location is awkward to navigate to and parking at the hotel is not the best. Fortunately we booked this hotel via a discount site that offered us the rooms for half the normal price. I would certainly not pay $--- a night to stay here.
Everything was just...mediocre and average. The room decor; pretty standard. Customer service; fine, nothing special. Cleanliness; pretty standard - spots here and there in the bathroom that could have done with a bit more attention, but nothing gross.
Four things that annoyed us somewhat were:
-. You had to pay for wifi. We completely understand that in these large, business hotels wifi is a moneymaking business, but I find it so frustrating, as a non-business person who doesn't want to make hour-long conference calls and send work-related emails throughout the night, to have to pay $-- for -- hours of wifi access when all I want to do is email my mum and nip onto facebook for a few minutes.
-. We chose this hotel over others as it has a pool, which advertises itself as having views over Lake Michigan. When we visited the pool, on two occasions, it was absolutely rammed full of kids. Kids jumping and splashing all over the pool - not just at one end. It was impossible to swim one length without kids shouting and splashing in front of you. So we thought we'd just spend our time in the jacuzzi...but then the kids came in there too, and were splashing around in there which is quite irritating when you're trying to relax in the bubbles. This wasn't just one family either, there were numerous and different children on each occasion. And the views over Lake Michigan? They don't really exist - one side is a wall, two sides look out over the other fitness facilities and the one side that has a window to the outside is covered up apart from - foot at the bottom.
-. Oh my god, the pillows. There were four different pillows on our bed; none matched. Different sizes, different thickness, different covers, which surprised me in a large hotel like this as normally everything is uniform. And they were god-awful-uncomfortable. There was a really odd long one which when laid on flattened down to the thickness of a mousemat. Another tiny small one, the size of a laptop, that flopped up round the side of your head. And they were all feather, no acrylic fibre ones, so no support offered to your head at all. We rang down to ask for more and they said they had no others. I did not sleep well either night.
-. The silliest complaint ever, but hey! The toilet paper was really, really cheap and thin. As mentioned, if I was paying $--- a night I'd expect something a bit more luxurious than what you'd find in a public loo!
The location of the hotel is great though - right on the river side, not far from Lake Michigan. Fab for Michigan Ave shopping, restaurants, short amble to Millenium Park. Great.
There was nothing fundamentally wrong with this place, but we just wouldn't stay there again, not even for the discounted rate we got.

-The neighboring underground lot along the same block charged $-- dollars nightly for parking.

Ok kind readers, its time for a reality check. 
Location: This hotel is located in the Northern part of Seattle near the U of W. If you have business with the school, or you are visiting your kid in college, this would be a good place to stay. But, if you are a tourist or businessperson, I don’t think this hotel is for you. 
I arrived in the evening and I must tell you that my first impression of the neighborhood was that it was kind of scary. The hotel has lots of security and management wants you to know that this place is locked down tight after dark. There are signs throughout the underground parking lot warning you not to leave anything in your car and that the hotel is not responsible for any losses you incur. Oh well, so much for warm, fuzzy-feeling first impressions.
Because this property is near the university, the restaurants around the hotel cater to student budgets, so you have lots of nondescript ethnic eateries from which to choose-Thai, Indian, Mexican, Chinese, Pizza, Subway. Typical other businesses you’ll find in the area are barrooms, piercing shops, bodegas, record stores, recycled clothing stores, smoke shops, second-run movie theaters, and hair stylists. Now you get the picture?
Rooms: Think dorm room decorated by Ikea. Even though they cleverly added a big mirror to give the illusion of space, I found the rooms to be small and Spartan, but very clean. While the beds are indeed very comfortable, there is no blanket between the sheets and bedspread, so you must use the bedspread to stay warm. Since we all know that hotel bedspreads rarely get washed, I found this to be pretty gross. 
I’m not particularly impressed by hotel toiletries because I bring my own stuff when I travel, but you might be charmed by little bottles of Aveda shampoos. 
There is some kind of gimmicky ala cart menu (not food related) that I have never seen before in a hotel. I really could not be bothered with it, so I cannot offer an opinion, or even tell you what it is.
This property offers free breakfast and free internet, both plusses, but overall, there is coldness to this hotel. It has a very pronounced industrial and institutional feel to it. What makes matters worse it that it is not affiliated with any chain, so you don’t even get travel points.
Call me old-fashioned, but whenever I come to Seattle on business, which is quite often, I usually stay downtown. This time, I’ve learned my lesson, I won’t stray again.

The desk staff were all polite, efficient, and knowledgeable, as were the waitresses and cleaning folks who we asked for lunch and shopping recommendations for our large group of teenagers. The hotel overall looks nice and is well maintained, the location is good, with the metro just outside and options to walk, there are really loud parties at night, room furniture poor quality, there are no coffee or tea making facilities in the room, but it would have been OK if the staff had even tried a little. It was as though any request was too much trouble.

After many hours of research before our trip we chose the Affinia Dumont. What a great choice we made. The hotel is situated perfectly in Murray Hill area, which is away from the noise of mid town, however located in a perfect area to get to all the major sites and great shopping.
Walking distance to mid town, metro station around the corner, close to Empire State, Macy's, Grand Central, you are really in an excellent location to explore the whole of manhattan. The accomodation was above our expectation and the staff were great. Our room attendant paid attention to detail and we felt spoilt. Studio Suites are a great size, plenty of room to spread out. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone travelling alone with a familly or with a friend. The Barking Dog bar next door had great bar staff and we were made to feel like locals very quickly. We would have to think hard to find something negitive to say about this hotel. Try it, you will love it and return. We are already planning our next trip back. Lastly Feb great time for shopping in NYC.

Stayed at The Muse for a girl's weekend to celebrate our big birthdays. We just mentioned it at check-in and staff sent special gifts to our room, with a personal note. How to make you feel special! Location was near Times Square yet the block was quiet. Room was large and bathroom was lovely. Some street noise so ask for a rear room. Happy hour is a perk but a bit crowded. Service was superb. They bent over backwards to be helpful.

I just returned from DC where I stayed in a first floor room in the Wardman Tower. As soon as I entered the room, I noticed that the sprinkler was covered in moldy dust. Then the a-c vent-heating vent came into view. It was black. Black with mold. UGH. I trekked back to the registration desk, informed a nice woman of the issue who offered assurance that housekeeping would be informed. I should have insisted on a new room, but I was just exhausted after a long day of driving and the idea of packing up and moving overwhelmed me. I went out for dinner expecting to see a cleaned vent when I returned around - or -:--. Nope, still black. 
Hmmm. One of the big issues with this vent is that it is located directly over the bed. Thus, it blows directly on the bed. I decided that I should clean it myself, so I stood on the bed with one of their lovely white washcloths and proceeded to turn it black. Big mistake. As I was cleaning it, large particles of mold blew all over the bed. It was obvious that there was a LOT of mold in and behind the vent. Now what to do. New room? I was so tired. It was one night. I made the bad decision to fold back the top cover of the bed and turn OFF the fan of the A-C, figuring if it wasn't blowing I would probably be okay. 
Wrong again. I woke up at - AM with a vile headache and facing a -- hour drive. It wasn't worth trying to get some more sleep. I packed up, headed to check out with the black washcloth. The gentleman listened to my story, but offered me nothing. Not a word of sympathy, let alone compensation. I couldn't even beg an aspirin. (I tried). 
To make matters worse, I had parked my vehicle in the parking garage. I was told to use my room card to exit, but wasn't informed to use it in the second machine. At - AM in total darkness, it wasn't obvious where to use my room card. I had to leave the vehicle, walk back into the lobby, and tearfully request some help. Response? Push a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""help"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" button on the machine. Really? I certainly would have pushed an obvious help button. 
It was a horrific experience from the moment I entered the room to the moment I finally got off the property. This is supposedly a - star hotel. That certainly was not my experience.

Great location right next to T station, very close to Boston Common and about -- mins walk to downtown. Rooms were very comfortable indeed - modern, clean and very spacious. Absolutely everything we wanted. Front dest staff were OK, but we asked them to mail a postcard for us (pre-stamped) and it never arrived. .Good restaurants nearby (had a lovely meal at McCormick & Schmick's Seafood restaurant). The breakfast buffet in the restaurant was a little pricey so we opted for the Starbucks inside the lobby (nice smoothies). New England Medical Center is just across the road but we only heard a medical helicopter once. Otherwise it was very quiet, with just the patter of rain outside. Would definitely stay again and recommend to others.

I booked this hotel as a surprise --th birthday for my girlfriend. We were both really I pressed with it.
The location was great a short walk to times square or close to the metro for further journeys. We headed to the opera house a few times and caught some of their free outdoor shows which is just a couple of minutes away.
The rooftop bar was amazing, not much atmosphere but really chilled and great to have a chat. Our room was small but perfectly formed, square ft in NYC is a premium so we didn't expect itto be huge, we had plenty of space to unpack all of our stuff, to be honest we only slept in the - there's so much to see and do why waste tome in the room?! Only one negative was the air con unit was a bit noisy but we had to keep in on as it was real hot.
We ate at the - of the attached restaurants as recommended by staff but found them overpriced and not that great quality - we found much better places ourselves.
Staff were friendly but to be honest other than check in and out we didn't need to contact them. Bar staff were attentive but drinks were overpriced (like most hotels).
All in all a great place

Huge bed, tidy room. Free wifi
No room service, no video on demand, slightly tired hotel, small rooms. Minute gym
There are much better hotels in NY

Found this place amazing the staff were all lovely, the place was great really clean with a great courtyard and the best view you could ask for. The location was the best thing about this place near everything restaurants, bars and beach with a sunset out your front door.Would definitely stay with Ocean Beach hotel on my next stay in San Diego.

Penny is the front desk supervisor, and is a very curt woman. Reminds me of a drill sergeant. Otherwise the room was okay and the room service was okay. Jennifer (front desk) was amazing!! Older, tall, slim, van driver was also fantastic. Slightly above average at best.

The Downtown Residence Inn by Marriott is two large open carparks away from the River Center shopping mall, with the Convention Center and Riverwalk beyond. On the other hand, the back of the Alamo itself is just a block away. The area around the Residence Inn is not greatly attractive, but seemed safe enough during the four nights that I spent there. (Can someone tell the train drivers who pass through San Antonio at night to stop blowing their horns?) The Residence Inn itself is comfortable and has pleasant staff. The bedroom-sitting room-kitchen set up would suit a small family group. The amenities are functional without being deluxe. If you are in town for a convention and don't want to overspend, this hotel is a good choice in my opinion.

i would just like to start this off with a very special thanks to andrew and todd.. from the moment i called to set up my reservation i could allready tell this was the right choice in hotel..i spoke with todd.. he was extremly helpfull and very friendly..i literally called everyday untill the day i arrived to make sure that things were in order and he was patient and nice through it all. as we arrived to chicago we had a little trouble finding the hotel. We booked a Monday night in March ---- via priceline for $-- (with tax it was only $--)!! Priceline only class it a --star hotel but it's definitely a --star.
The staff were really helpful and gave us an excellent room on the --rd floor, with floor to ceiling glass and a view back towards the city. The bedroom had very nice furnishings although there is no bar fridge and the basin is adjacent to the door rather than being in the bathroom proper.
The hotel was a little further out from the city than we expected and the roads are slightly confusing in the vicinity. But as it's the tallest building around, you can't really miss it. Ample free parking too.

Just stayed at The George for three nights while attending a conference. Congress is not in session, so perhaps the place would be busier if it were. There is a nice manager's reception in the lobby each evening. 
The room was nice and fairly spacious. There are robes and slipper socks provided - a nice touch. There was a tub and shower, another nice touch. 
There is some work being done so only one elevator worked. Didn't eat at the restaurant.
Tip: Join the Kimpton Loyalty program for free wifi and a credit on mini-bar items.

We found this hotel extremely convenient to the Convention Center. The staff was super friendly and helpful even before checkin and was accomodating throughout.
The lobby is beautiful and the public spaces are very nice. This said, the rooms are a bit dated and not remarkable. Worth a stay if the price is right, but if you are looking for luxury, this is not it.

I live on the California coast about - hours drive from San Francisco, and frequently go there to attend opera, ballet or theatrical performances, as well as to visit friends. The Inn at the Opera is one of the choices available to me through my time share ownership, and I always make it my first choice when going to the city. It's a smaller property, which creates a feeling of cozy intimacy. If I'm going to the opera, symphony or ballet, it's a perfect location--just cross the street and I'm there. Staff are unfailingly courteous, knowledgeable and welcoming. 
Breakfast is provided and, while not extensive, has everything I want to get my day started right. Valet parking is available for an additional daily fee, but with unlimited in and out privileges, it's well worth it. There's only one small elevator, so if many people are checking in or out at the same time you might experience a delay. I'm always happy to make this my 'home' in the city.

I have been an avid fan of the Microtel brand since I discovered it about ten years ago. It is a great stay for an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""easy on the wallet"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" rate. About a week ago, I flew into JAX on a business trip. I stayed in a very clean, modern, and comfortable room. I believe my rate was around -- dollars with my AAA card, but after seeing the room I would of paid twice as much. A large LCD tv, shuttle service to and from the airport, and a free continental breakfast were all all included in this rate. If I have ever have to do business in Jacksonville again, I know I have a great, reasonably priced place to stay.
A very clean and friendly hotel, but overall the best experience during my stay was the beds. They were extremely comfy and i would definitely come back!

this hotel shines when it comes to service. Rooms are small but well appointed. If you like traditional decor you are in the right place. Don't expect to find a pool. The parking is quite expensive @ $-- a day. The location is very good and there are lots of small affordable places to dine in the area.

We stayed at the Harbor Court a few times in the past and it was wonderful until our recent visit. It wasn't owned by Intercontinental at the time. Our second day there we were out all day and came back at -:-- to fi d our room hadn't been cleaned. enjoyed everything this hotel had to offer.a large family group enjoyed warm service and elegance.was great location to absorb this wonderful city. will saty again anytime

Beginning with the first class welcome from Monique until we departed - days letter it was a first class experience. Located a half a block from Union Station when you walk outside and see the Capitol - blocks up the street. What really separated the hotel was the friendly professionalism of the staff. They were most supportive( you need all the help you can when you travel with twin -- yr olds) and accomodating. We will definitely stay there again!!

This hotel is approximately two years old, and most of it still seems new. The public areas and guest rooms are clean. Rooms on the back of the hotel have a nice city view. The breakfast, included in the room rate, has improved since my last visit. The staff was fully helpful and kind. Note that the neighborhood is """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hip"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" although somewhat off the beaten path.

I was concerned about some of the negative reviews about this resort. We made reservations for - nights over -th of July and we had lots of fun. Oasis staff as well as resort staff were friendly and helpful. Room was clean with the exception of carpet appearing old and worn. Some posts made reference to chairs lacking at Oasis. I would agree somewhat but we didn't have any problems finding at least - for each day we were there. There is plenty of space to find shade to park your chairs as landscape has plenty of mature trees. Food at the resort and Oasis is expensive and you can't bring your own into the Oasis. Regarding $-- per night activity fee which includes - passes to Oasis, I'd say this is a bargain considering it can cost $-- per person at other water parks for the day. Spend an evening at the Oasis and enjoy movie on big screen poolside or in the water on provided rafts.

This was the location hotel for the San Francisco Whisky Fest, so I wanted a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""home base."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" It turned out to be a very nice hotel with an excellent staff. I accidentally left my credit card at the desk and it was returned promptly. Had a great, quiet corner room mid-level and I would recommend asking for same. Easy cab service. Walked to the Ferry Building each morning for breakfast. I would repeat this booking.

My husband was going to take a shower before retiring for the evening. There was no rubber bath mat nor was there a towel type mat in the bathroom. A set of towels for each of us was provided, with no extra towel. He looked at the bottom of the tub, and there were faint gray ovals on the bottom of the tub. He assumed that this meant that it was a non-slip surface by looking at it, especially since no mat was provided. He turned on the water, and then started to get into the shower. His foot slipped out from under him and he fell heavily to the floor, taking the shower curtain and its rings with him. He fell with such force that the mirror fell from the wall above the sink, broke against the edge of the sink, and then landed on top of him. (The mirror was attached to the wall with only two small flat clips.) Small pieces of the mirror cut his chest, legs, hands, and near his ear. These were all small cuts, nothing major, and I always pack band-aids just to be on the safe side. Luckily he was not badly hurt, especially when you are talking about a -- year old man falling in the manner that he did. 
I called the front desk and told them what had happened. A gentleman came up and tried to clean up the shards from the mirror, but there were small pieces that he was unable to get up with the broom. I called the front desk while he was in the room and asked if we could move to another room since the bathroom floor wasn’t safe to walk on without shoes, but I was told that no other room was available that evening. The man who came to help us got us a new shower curtain and brought up some ceiling tiles to put on the floor along with some extra towels. He couldn’t find any shower curtain rings, so he brought me some pieces of string for me to use to put the shower curtain up. I had cleaned up the blood with the wash cloth and he told me to just put that in the trash can, which I did. 
The next morning I went down to the front desk and asked to speak to the manager. I was told that he would not be in until Monday morning. Our phone number was taken down and I was given a card with the hotel information on it. I asked the man at the desk to please let housekeeping know that the floor really needed to be carefully mopped since there were still tiny pieces of mirror on the floor. This was done. No new shower curtain rings were put up; the mirror was not replaced. We were given a towel type bath mat.
On Sunday morning we went to the front desk to check out and were told that a $--- charge for the mirror and a $-- charge for the curtain rings were added to our bill since we broke them. Once again I went through the entire account, and the young woman then removed the charges, but we were told that they might be put back on our bill on Monday. I reiterated that we wanted the manager to call us. Our daughter noticed that the notes that were sitting on the front desk had highlighted the statement that we broke the mirror, not that there was a fall and the mirror fell off the wall and broke on top of my husband.. 
This entire ordeal has left us extremely disappointed with Best Western Hotels. To begin with, this event never should have occurred. You either provide your guests with a bath mat of some sort, or your tubs have non-slip surfaces. You should also mount your mirrors with a stronger type of anchoring system than what was used. If and when an unfortunate event like this does occur, you do not bill your guests for damages that occurred through no fault of their own. We were upset that this happened to him to begin with, and billing us for the mirror and shower curtain rings made matters a hundred times worse. All that my husband wanted to do was take a shower safely. That certainly is not too much to ask of a hotel.
The manager has yet to call us, and it is over a week since this happened. He told the Best Western people to say that he was sorry. They have also asked him repeatedly to call us. The charges were not added back on to the bill, and the owner did not make any other adjustment to our charges to compensate us for this. I can't imagine what would have happened if he had broken his hip when he fell.

We spent - nights here on an annual visit to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The City"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", having previously stayed at a less expensive hotel, so this was supposed to be a splurge. But it was not our mistake that our toilet would not flush away all the waste, even after ---- tries. We got a quick response when we reported the problem, but the house plumbers could not fix it to work on one flush every time.
The banks of elevators posed further problems. There were no signs externally showing which floors they served. And on the ground floor the doors remained opened for just about - seconds, so you had to be very quick on your feet to get to one before it closed - not easy when arriving with bags.
Our room lacked an ice bucket when we arrived; they did bring us one when we called.
The room did not have a coffee maker or a mini-fridge.
They charged high prices for local calls ($-.--), internet access ($---day), breakfast in the lobby (twice the price compared to outside the front door), and $--bag to store our bags for a few hours on the last day - these things were all free at our lesser priced hotel last year.
Privacy was an issue. We could not only hear the guy in the next room talking on the phone, but we could see his light under the connecting door. Also, there was only one curtain on the window, so we could block out the light, but we could not have light without opening the view into our room from the adjoining office building.
These were our main gripes. We just expected more from a Hyatt.

Whata great hotel!! Great and friendly sevrice and staff. hotel is very clean and well maintained. It is also convenient to many of the downtown attractions - --th st Mall, etc..
i love staying there and would hilghly recommend it to business folks!

One of the best four seasons I have stayed at! definitely more homely feel to it. Stayed there for work, and a short time, but the service was perfect, and their breakfast is great. Definitely will stay there next time.

Del mar is jewel of a location. So close to Torrey Pines gorgeous beach. This hotel was great - with a wonderful pool, plenty of parking, and a couch in the room. And a very convenient strip mall super close by. We really enjoyed it. The cons are that the rooms didnt have fridges and breakfast was not included which I expected of doubletree. Also the cleaning folks were a little stingy not leaving all new things every day. But the pool and hot tub made up for any issues, it was a fantastic pool.

My wife and I stayed two nights at this Comfort Inn location. Before I left, I asked for a fridge in the room, but I guess my note was not received or understood. The clerk told me that it was $-- and wheeled out a fridge from the front desk area. I had to wheel it to the elevator and plug it in myself. Not a complaint but little things like this matter to me and make all the difference to a stay for me. There was mold in the fridge but I didn't want to lug it all the way down again and I was tired. We cleaned it best we could. The rooms were comfortable and very clean, we got a king sized bed. The breakfast is the usual, waffles, cereals, coffee, eggs, bacon, bagels, toast and was always a good stock of items. Front desk staff were nice.
The hallways are loud, like most hotels. People can be quite loud and inconsiderate sometimes, especially late at night.
It is - minutes from Fort Harrison State Park, Walmart can be seen from the room window along with many restaurants. Applebees, Bob Evans, Marcos Pizza, Steak and Shake. There was a pool in the hotel that looked clean but small, looked sized for children. High speed internet is free and quite fast.

Room was very comfortable and very clean. Not sure why it was cheaper for me to get a room with - beds though, rather than one. Staff was very friendly and was always around if you needed info or help with something. There was a slight bit of noise coming from venting even with heater-ac off but not too distracting. I would only suggest that they install dual-pane windows for the rooms that face the streets as I could hear sirens. But again, the noises were far from overwhelming.

I stayed at the Night Hotel for two nights to celebrate an anniversary. I choose the hotel based on the reviews here. I was not disappointed at all. The hotel is steps from the heart of Times Square and all the Broadway shows, which is great. The hotel itself is a very small, clean and unique property with black and white motives throughout. The rooms are tiny, but unless you are planning to spend lots of awake hours locked in a room, who cares. The front desk staff are very nice and all helpful as well as the doorman that opens the doors for you each and every time you leave and enter. I emailed the hotel Manager Michelle that it was my anniversary. She responded back right away and left a nice note and a bottle of sparkling wine for us to enjoy upon our return one night. A real nice touch and thank you Michelle! The bottom line is: Would I send friends there and would I return again..... YES!

This is a great place to stay if you want to be near Times Square. It is affordable and the rooms and building are historical. That said, the rooms are small, the hot water runs to extremes (too hot, then cold, then too hot again), and there were some strange sounds that woke us at night (pings in the heat or plumbing). But, I would stay there again - those inconveniences are outweighed by the location, character of the building, a good customer service.
Loved everything from the amazing artwork in the hotel to the service, rooms, and restaurants.

We stayed at Library Hotel for - nights in July. The hotel is in a perfect location and close to many attractions (-mins from Grand Central Station, Times Sq, Bryant Park, Chrysler building and - mins Empire State. A great location for Broadway too.). On arrival we were greeted with champagne for our forth coming wedding and a thoughtful note from the hotel staff. Fantastic hotel, knowledgeable staff, lovely breakfasts and a really comfortable room. Just Perfect.
What a fabulous hotel with extremely helpful front desk staff – especially Billy who was a star. Really great service. We also must mention Michael as well, lots of great advice and tips for our stay. On a less positive note the manager who I believe is called Scott made me feel like a criminal after losing my credit card through no fault of my own. Scott was also responsible for giving my fiancé and I some really duff information regarding where to watch the Macey's fireworks display but this was the only negative occurrences that we encountered. Beautiful surroundings with a great roof top terrace and wonderfully decorated. The complimentary cheese and wine nights were great although very few guests mixed, lovely breakfasts and tranquil rooms. Very blissful. All our needs were accommodated for. 
We would not hesitate to recommend the hotel and would come back again.

Stayed here for a few nights due a conference being held at the hotel. Overall, the hotel was nice but a bit worn as others have commented. Check in was fine and workers appeared to be nice but did not have much interaction with them either.
Fitness room was very small - just a few machines. Of course, it is an older hotel in NYC so that is to be expected. 
It is in a good location and within walking distance to many sights. I think this hotel would be fine for most tourist purposes but would not pay an extreme amount for it.

I recently stayed for a couple nights at -- Thompson and was very pleased with the service I received. When checking-in, there was a mix-up where I was booked for a smaller room than I had reserved. Despite the confusion, the staff was very accomodating and helpful as they upgraded my room. The stay was great overall. I will definitely return to -- Thompson when doing business in Manhattan.

Only - minute from Times square and the theatre district makes this hotel an ideal location if you want to be in the heart of New York. We had a one bedroomed suite and the room was spacious and above all very quiet. Ask for a room on the upper floor. Although the outside entrance to the hotel is fairly small, the lobby and bar are very spacious and cetainly buzzing everynight. . The one thing we found strange was the lighting in this area, which was very dark, presumably to create atmosphere The staff were very attentive and polite and we would definitely stay here again if visiting this part of the Big Apple!

I have stayed in this hotel over - years every time I am here on business. The staff is super friendly and courteous . . . the updated lobby is contemporary elegance . . . and the restaurant can compete with the best of them!

Overall our experience was very good. Elissa arranged a change to a room that overlooked the river (rather than the parking lot). That being said, the bus noise is louder on this side, but the view is worth it. 
Michael Ruiz, chef, did a superb job in accommodating our needs for gluten free. A nice gentleman to talk to.
Thanks to our server, Raul and to Daniel, the restaurant supervisor. The dining experience is sincere and warm and lovely on the river.

I stayed at the santuary with my sister in May ---- as we visted from Australia on our first trip to NY, but it was our second hotel in NY on that trip (the previous one was in Chelsea and was great).
Sanctuary is a nice hotel, the lobby is very trendy and very dark- its kind of like walking into a nightclub actually. The staff are attentive, very attentive- from the receptionists to the star manager and even the door men, they aim to make your stay the best they can. 
The room we had was a king room which faced an office building. It was clean and nicely decorated, but like others have said small. Its hard to make use of a room that size we had trouble tripping over our bags and shopping majority of the time. The bathroom-shower area takes up too much of thr room space in my opinion. The room does have wifi, but its not incredibly fast, the room also doesnt have cable- being ---- cable and fast wifi is not just a perk but neccessary.
The breakfast was underwhelming, while the hotel focuses on a luxurious and trendy vibe, it doesnt follow ow this vibe in the breakfast room. The breakfast choices were very minimal but did the job. We were also dissapointed that there was no coin operated laundry on site (but you could have your laundry done at a hefty price by the hotel).
But the major draw to sanctuary besides being trendy is the location, its a very short walk right into the heart of times square and close to broadway shows. I recommend this hotel for shorter stays but no longer than a week as the lack of space and bland breakfast will put a dampen on your mood.

The hotel smelled when you first walked in and got worse when you went in the room. Was supposed to have had - queen beds but they were not!! Holes were brunt in blankest. Should had left and went to another hotel, one that was worth the money. Will not stay in any comfort inn again!!

I usually stay at the Omni Parker House or the Ames when visiting central Boston. However, being a Hilton Hhonors Gold Member, I thought that I would give this Hilton a try and spent two nights in a King suite.
