The bad:
-. No in room safes. For a Hilton, this is totally unacceptable. When I called down to ask where the in-room safe was, I was told that there weren't any because """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""there wasn't room for them"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". No room for them? Please .... my suite was quite large and there were at least half a dozen places where they could have installed an in-room safe.
-. The building is art deco and you get the feeling that they have tried to buy art deco style furniture for the rooms. In my opinion, it hasn't worked too well and the rooms appeared a bit cold.
-. I'm not a lush, but it's convenient to have a minibar in your room. It's certainly something that I would expect in a downtown Hilton. However, there wasn't one. Instead, there was a dirty looking empty fridge in the TV console, which wasn't working and which had a tired sticker on it saying something to the effect that it was more of a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""chiller"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and would not refrigerate properly.
-. Although Nix's Mate downstairs is a hip and cool looking bar-restaurant with decent food, it didn't seem right that this was the only offering in a downtown Hilton. It would have been nice to have had a slightly quieter (Nix Mate was very loud on the Saturday night), more dressy, place to eat as well.
I'm a fan of the Hilton chains, but this is one Hilton that I will probably not stay at again. For the money, it doesn't come close to comparing with the Omni Parkerhouse or the Ames in downtown Boston

I love the location. Close to Chinatown, Starbucks, and Bart. Union Square and the cable cars were just a short walk away. Our room was very clean. I was surprised at how quiet it was. We closed the windows at night and could hardly hear any outside noise. We were on the -th floor. The staff was very friendly and I loved the towel animals!
The only drawback - The clingy shower curtain. 
We will definately be back.

I just returned from a - night stay at the Milburn Hotel and to say I was terribly disappointed is an understatement. I am by no means a - star traveler so I am used to staying at moderate establishments. This isn't even close. Let me start with the positive, the staff is great as is the neighborhood. The Upper Westside has some great finds and Central Park is really close. They had great restaurant suggestions ( Both Citrus and Coppola's restaurant (--th and Broadway) were fantastic) and the staff from front desk to maid service were always polite (which in NYC is not always the case). This, however, is where the nice comments stop.
We made our reservations through their site over - months ago yet were put in a room right by the elevator on the second floor. They are doing construction which meant banging on the walls all day. Our view was of construction workers and all the garbage that goes along with that. The air conditioner is a windowbox so all the dust from their work blew directly into our room. We asked to move but were not accommodated. The plumbing in the bathroom backed up (gurgling from shower, sink and toilet), the towels were crunchy, we saw a cockroach and the decore is right out of ----. Clearly we were not in an updated room. For this, we paid over $--- a night.
They call it """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""European"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but in reality, I'd say it's more rent by the hour. Before choosing this place, I read all the reviews on Trip Advisor which overall were pretty good. Unfortunately, the experience I had totally contradicts what I read. If you are looking for a bed, by all means the Milburn Hotel will be fine but if you are looking for just a little more, LOOK ELSEWHERE!

We stayed at the Millennium post cruise. We had planned to stay only one night, and had the ---- Anniversary package which was a reduced price on a premium room which included champaign and breakfast. Well.... Hurricane Sandy extended our stay for - more nights. Not at the reduced rate of the first night but at a pretty good price considering the rack rate. 
The hotel is beautiful. The entire property is immaculate. The furnishing are very high end and the bed is very comfortable ( except the pillows). Our view was of Quincy Market and at night the lights were absolutely beautiful. They offer Starbucks coffee in the lobby in the morning and hot apple cider in the afternoon.
Because our flights were cancelled twice, we had to extend our stay and the staff especially the concierge were very pleasant and helpful. 
The door on our """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""balcony"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" kept popping open ( gusts of wind due to the storm I guess) and both times the response was quick and it was secured.
I wish that we had stayed here pre cruise instead of the hotel at the Harbor that was almost twice the price. That however, is another review.
I would definitely recommend staying here. It is a perfect starting point for sightseeing and there is no lacking for dining choices. 
The Wifi isn't complementary, but printing off boarding passes is.
Now... I just hope they correct the billing on our credit card as I have double charges pending and my husband has a double charge pending from the restaurant that we are hoping is taken care of soon.

This hotel is in a great location. Room was ok, everyone in here had me scared I was going to get fleas or some horrible disease from here - THIS IS NOT THE CASE! If travelling on a budget this is the place to go. We never stayed in the room other than to sleep (I mean, come on, why would you if you're in NYC??!!) Right across the road from Madison Square Gardens and a little walk from Times Square you're right in the middle of all the action. Financial District and Statue are a bit of a walk but we are quite health conscious and didn't mind the exercise (plus you seem to find so much more in that city if you just walk).The internet service was incredibly inconvenient though as I had to pay by the hour and try to have a conversation on Skype with my family at home (Wi-Fi only available in lobby and of course with a strong Australian accent everyone notices). Just prepare yourself for the worst and you will be fine. For the price it's in a good location and lets face it's a warm place to sleep (no issues with heating and we were there right in the middle of their winter).

We arrived to celebrate our first anniversary in this hotel.
The entrance hall was very stylish and the staff were very efficient and friendly. I had booked the slightly more expensive room to get a higher room and I booked it about - months in advance and asked for a room as high as possible and hopefully facing the Empire State building. I think we were given about the --th floor and the room was beautiful and had a lounge area (so was huge for NY!). The views were absolutely incredible that high up because there isn't a building nearby that is as tall so we could see from the Brooklyn Bridge all the way round to up town Manhattan. Stunning. 
They had even given us a free bottle of Champagne and rose petals on the bed.
we didn't eat in the hotel because we wanted to go out and experience various eating places around NY so can't comment on breakfast or other food.
On our last day we were due to travel back to the UK but the big snow arrived and our flights were cancelled. The staff at the hotel were incredibly kind and gave us some tea and tried to help as much as they could.
You can not fault anything about this hotel it is amazing and the staff were brilliant.

Firstly, the layout of the hotel is not very user friendly. Being a first-time guest here, we drove up to the lobby doors as usual only to find there is only valet parking at outrageous rates. After being directed to the parking garage below where we can self-park, we had to figure out how to get to the lobby to check in. Nothing was obvious. Not to make it too confusing, this hotel has two lobbies; so which lobby is it that we need? We drove nearly three hours to get here and now I'm cranky having to deal with somebody's idea of creative hotel architecture.
I'm finally in my hotel room. Really? It looks just like a Hampton Inn & Suites room without the price tag. The bathroom had no drawers in which to store my toiletries; the countertop was small so storing the toiletries there made everything too crowded. There is no vent system in the bathroom so showering created an even muggier environment than La Jolla already is. 
The pillows and bed were nice. I actually slept well which doesn't usually happen in a hotel. Even so, I'd rather stay somewhere else which costs less for the same or better.
Left a pair of sun glasses in my room - Called after two days and found it. Glasses were shipped to me very quickly - Thank you Mr. Tony. Very impressed with your professionalism.

We stayed at the Gansevoort over the Christmas period . The hotel staff are friendly and efficient. The hotel is situated in a good area for restaurants and bars. 
It's a lovely hotel in a great area.

After much research (I'm an engineer - trust me, MUCH research), I decided on the Michelangelo Hotel. I wanted something on the northern end of Theater District (close enough to Central Park that I could get there easily for a morning run), yet really nice, very clean, and not overly priced. I found it with this hotel. The staff was...fine. Not overly solicitous, but professional. The lobby-bar was great, the room was very clean, comfortable, quiet, and well appointed. They had a lovely continental breakfast set up every morning but I wasn't ever able to use it (too busy running to Zabar's). Anyway, I am always looking for value, but I tend to stay at the nicer hotels when travelling for leisure, have been to a dozen or more in NY, and I think I have found my new favorite. Enjoy. 
Oh - one last thing. There is a great store-deli on --st right next to the hotel. I ate at several fabulous resturants up and down -th, on --th, in the Village, etc. - but if I had found this place earlier in my trip, I may have stopped in for lunch simply due to the convenience and seemlingly great selection of food choices.

This hotel has a very smae entry way but the furnishings in your room are very lovely. The shampoo and various other bath products they given you are top notch. The hotel offers advice to any thing you may have a question about in NYC. It is quite a walk from the teather district but can be done if you wear comfortable shoes and are able to walk a good pace. I'd stay here again if the price was comparative to the other hotels in NYC. Anything below $--- is a deal. I have always gotten this hotel when I book it with the airfare attached and then later on find out what hotel I received using Priceline or other search engines.

This hotel is very central in Boston. Directly situated near the old town house. The rooms are furnished very modern and equipped with HD TV. Everything was clean and the stuff was helpful in all belongings. We can highly recommand this hotel for business as well as for holiday trips to Boston.

My friends and I just spent - nights at the Edison, I was lucky I had a refurbished room, my friends rooms were adequate but tired in need of upgrading. My room was at the front of the hotel and I found it noisy but you got used to it. The location was fantastic - minute to Times Square. The room was only used for sleeping but the flat screen tv on the wall was nice at the end of a long day. Pricewise it was good value for money and our party of eight 'shopping ladies' were certainly happy enough. Would use this hotel again.

We stayed here for two nights. We were a family of four, two adults and two kids, age --.
The positives:
Very close to Beale but not right there with all the noise. 
Great places to eat right around the corner. (Especially the Denny's for breakfast with the kids)
An easy walk to the downtown Trolley line. 
Very nice staff. We especially had great service from a bellman who helped us several times but quite a bit on Sunday, ----. I wish we would have gotten his name. Overall, anytime we needed anything and called the front desk it was quickly provided. 
The pool was very nice and well-maintained (with one exception, noted below).
It is also directly across the street from the Peabody. We went there to watch the Ducks, of course. We also took advantage of how close it was and did a family walk one night and went up to the roof of the Peabody and looked at the view and the Duck Palace. The girls really enjoyed this. 
We had a nice and clean room. We were on the fourth floor and we had a view of Union Avenue.
The put out cookies and lemonade in the afternoon, which was a pleasant surprise when we came back to the hotel in the afternoon. 
Negatives:
The things listed below are negatives, but have nothing to do with the actual hotel. They just come with the choice to stay downtown, 
Parking is $-- a day. This is average for downtown hotels and we already knew about it so we were not surprised. Also, parking is limited. There are other public decks, but the the actual hotel decks was very crowded and tough to navigate. When we found good spaces we just walked or took the trolley almost everywhere so we could keep our spots. 
The noise at this hotels is loud. They are on Union Avenue, which is not Beale, but people are on Union late too. So be prepared and if you do not want to sleep with earplugs and you can't sleep with some noise, do not stay at a downtown hotel. 
The pool was nice, but the pool light came out of the wall during our stay. This was kind of concerning because younger kids do tend to want to play with those, but we did not have any specific issues with it. 
Overall, a great location and we enjoyed our trip.

This hotel disappoints from start to finish. On entering the lobby the “stale aftershave” smell induces a gag reflex which doesn’t abate with the passage of time. The counter staff appear to be too busy “looking beautiful” to be able to contend with guests concerns – we had to ring reception FIVE times and wait -- hours before our request for additional blankets was acknowledged!! A request to repair a noisy fan in the bathroom was rectified by covering it in tape!! Priceless! We also paid an exorbitant price for pool-side rooms on the second floor to ensure we would be as far away from the nightclub noise as possible. However, on two nights out of our four nights stay, there was a party in the lobby and the noise in our overpriced rooms was simply insufferable. We ended up moving rooms - times before we finally got some sleep. The issue of tissue thin walls needs to be addressed - you could practically hear the people in the next room turning in their beds!! – (we were kept awake on another night by the person in the next room talking on their mobile phone). Everything about this hotel is artificial – an absolutely horrendous experience.
PS. It will be interesting to read the snide remarks hotel management rebuke with!

I enjoyed real, warm breakfast (not a continental breakfast) and manager's reception (though I ohms a chance to go to the manager's reception only one night). I loved using jaccuzi after we went jogging outside!

I stayed at The Orchard in July ---- and just loved it. Although the room we had seemed to have tiny little beds - I didn't mind it one bit. 
The linens and bedding were so comfortable - I didn't even mind being snuggled up with my husband. Beautiful hotel. Great location. Just top notch all the way. I loved it! Highly recommend.

This hotel was great for me, but I can easily see it not working for everyone. The room I was in was a bit of a cave with very little natural light. I didn't mind this, but by the looks of the building from the outside I assume a good portion of their rooms are similar. If you're a fan of natural light, this could be an issue.
The hotel itself seem very DIY-ish. There's a self service laundry, self service purified water bottles, and even a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""guest service closet"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in the halls with many common requests - extra blankets, towels, irons, etc. I imagine many calls to the front desk are answered with """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""here's how to help yourself"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", as mine was when I wanted an iron. I thought this was brilliant, but it's far from full service if that's what you're looking for. They even have a self-serve check-in-check-out computer that's very easy to use.
If, instead, you're looking for a hotel that assumes you can help yourself here and there, the hotel could not be in a better location in downtown Chicago - when they say """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""central loop"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", they mean that literally - a short walk in any direction will get to a loop station with lots of great retail and food nearby.
Future trips to Chicago will definitely be here, no question.
Great Hotel, great value and the best location. Simple, clean and all the little touches anyone could want.

My friend and I booked a suite for - nights, one of which was my birthday! We had theater tickets and dinner reservations at the Tower of Americas. The hotel is in walking distance to EVERYTHING!! We barely used the car. We ended up staying in a double bed suite (room #----) which was on the --st floor just under the pool and hot tub on the top of the building. You could see ALL of the city. It was amazing!! The breakfast was divine, and the happy hour was very happy! We paid the state rate and it ended up being hundreds of dollars cheaper! I give it - stars!!!

Great hotel within walking distance of the union square area (about -- min walk).
Very clean and very friendly staff.

My family stayed at this resort for - nights, - days. When we first arrived we cringed up because it was right near the highway. One member of the family thought that it was just a small motel but she was definitly wrong. It is a huge complex with many restuarants and - pools which are great. When we really got into the resort part it was amazing you couldnt even see the highway or hear it. It was like a little secluded place. The food was ok...not the greatest but a not horrible. There is a great spa which is very elegant inside. All the staff were very efficient. And worked in a fast manner to measure up to our needs. The grounds are beautiful with palms, bird houses and gorgeous gardens and gazebos. The only real turn off to me is that the trolley is right behind the hotel and just random people can get off the trolley and walk right into the hotel and use all their facielities. I thought there should be guards and key cards for you to get into the pools and buildings. Our san diego experience was very good....although it may be a little to much of a convension center it still made our vacation meet our expectations

This was my first time staying in Drury and I must say that it was an excellent experience. Couldn't ask for a better location and the extras the Drury provided were great. Enjoyed watching the fireworks from the roof-top. I highley recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to San Antonio. For a $---.-- a night, (give or take a few bucks) free breakfast , Internet and the managers special (- cocktails per adult) make this a must stay. From now on i will definitely stay look for drury's in which to stay. Happy Traveling!!

This is a great little hotel, but not without some minor negatives. I stayed for - nights. 
The breakfast buffet is just so-so. There were the instant type scrambled eggs, very greasy sausage links, cold cereal, instant oatmeal packages, toast, waffles, and packaged muffins. I think other hotels do the breakfast way better. Jalapenos, the little Mexican place next to Starbucks has excellent breakfast burritos. There isn't a washing machine and dryer on site. When I inquired I was told that guests are permitted to use the facilities at the Hampton Inn across the street. The lighting in our room was very harsh. No table lamps, only bright fluorescent wall lighting. So it is impossible to have lighting that doesn't disturb others who might want to sleep later than you. (I would turn on the light in the bathroom and keep the door half closed. A table lamp with - way bulb would be nice.)
The positives of this hotel are the price, the very friendly and attentive staff at the front desk, free parking, free internet, very clean, comfortable rooms and great housekeeping service. 
We came to Austin for my daughter to attend a volleyball camp at UT. We had rented a car and it was simple to get to campus from the Microtel and took less than -- min. It's a great location for getting anywhere, really. I really liked this little place and for the price (around $---night) I didn't mind eating breakfast elsewhere. I would definitely stay here again, but bring more clothing options (It was July!). I gave this hotel a - out of - on service because of no laundry facility on site.

My sister, my niece and myself stayed at The Peninsula last year. I love NY! I have visited - times. Each time I stay at a different hotel. The Peninsula sets the standard for - star hotels. Every aspect of the hotel was excellent. The roses on our breakfast tray. The friendly and professional staff. The location. The food. The price: worth every penny!

My stay at the Ritz was aweful! The staff does not smile and everyone was distracted. The Sunday buffet food was burnt and you could tell they let it sit way too long before being swapped out. I had got sick from the breakfast and worst of all I tried to order from the menu and was told that they were only running the buffet. I should have stayed elsewhere. I cannot wait until the W is open downtown.

Always love Embassy Suites - primarily because you get a great breakfast and the two rooms. Were attending a trade show at the convention center, and this place was only like -- miles away and a lot less than downtown rates. And then there was Lassandra - the cook of all cooks...who saved me two days in a row as I was trying to beat the buzzer for the end of breakfast. Great food - but more importantly, great attitude, great smile and I left her a great tip. Oh...and love the bird you guys have! Sweetie...definitely adds some life to the hotel.

We spent the weekend at the Hotel Teatro. We requested a quiet room and were told that our room was far from the elevator, which it was. However, the street noise was very audible. The configuration of the room was awkward with the toilet behind the bathroom door. Turn down service was sporadic. There was no full length mirror in the room. There is no closet but an armoire is provided that barely contains enough space to hang clothes, certainly nothing that is full length. Half of the armoire is filled with an ironing board, iron and luggage rack, all of which need to be removed so that clothes can be hung.
The staff is welcoming and the room decor simple and attractive. The location is excellent. We normally prefer boutique smaller hotels but were somewhat disappointed with this one.

This was my first time travelling to USA with my boyfriend and we stayed at Jerry's Motel for - days. Our stay was very comfortable. We had a really decent sized flatscreen TV, air-conditioning, free cable with lots of channels, a nice bed and clean sheets and clean towels everyday. While not the biggest room, it was definitely a more than enough for the two of us who spent most of the days out. 
I'm a bit of a neat freak and cleanliness is really important to me. I'm happy to say that the room and bathroom were clean and tidy and the linen and towels were of decent quality and nicely laundered. I was really impressed by the quality overall of the services and amenities given how affordable our stay was.
The location wasn't too bad, there's parking at the motel and I didn't feel unsafe. I definitely recommend driving though, as the motel is located kind of east of downtown and not that close to fast public transport. It's a relatively quick drive to major locations in LA.
The only down side is that the wifi dropped out every once in a while and it wasn't the fastest but I'm just nitpicking. Overall I really don't have a complaint. I'd definitely go back to Jerry's if I ever visit LA again.

The location is good as it is right down the street from time square but the rooms need remodeling. Air does not circulate well and the tub had holes in it. Cleanliness was good but again for cost would expect fluffier towels and beds.

Everything was great. The staff anticipated every need. The view was breathtaking. Totally worth it. No better view of the hudson or ground zero. The room was spotless and well maintained....inroom dining was pricy but good and quick.
I generally do not stay with hilton but I was pleasantly surprised. Great shopping in soho next to century --.
One thing...they start construction on ground zero really early so it may be too loud...but i actually enjoyed it...it reminded me to get up and enjoy New York.

$---night for a queen room plus free parking in an attached lot is pretty much unheard of anywhere in the city limits of Chicago. So, you have to be a little suspicious going into it. We kept our expectations low and ended up satisfied with what we got. For the price, we knew we weren't going to have lavish decor and plush linens. The rooms are spartan and no-frills, but they are clean and adequately sized. The bathrooms have small bars of soap but no other toiletries, so be prepared and bring your own. 
If you're a light sleeper, this may not be the place to stay. Street traffic can be heard at all hours, as well as the bass beat of the music playing at the club across the street. We brought a travel fan and it helped drown out a lot of the extraneous noise late at night.
For the location and the price, the Ohio House is hard to beat. Just be realistic about your expectations and remember that you get what you pay for.

I only paid $-- for one night so I wasn't expecting much. I got in at -:--AM so I had to call three times until I got someone on the phone for the airport shuttle. That was a bit frustrating but I just rolled with it because I was tired. The desk staff person was friendly and pointed out the breakfast and internet usage. I had a hard time finding my room because it was all the way in the back. I helped another woman try to find her room. It's a bit confusing. The room was just okay. The bathroom was very clean but it only had a shower. The bed was okay. There was an air-conditioner left running in the room which made the air stale. The really liked that there was a Denny's right next door though.

We stayed here overnight last night on family vacation and will not stay again.
In its favor, the hotel is clean and well maintained. It is in a pretty good location with interesting local restaurants nearby.
The hotel itself out of date in terms of the decor and the facilities. The restaurant is very poor with an extremely limited menu and uninspired cooking. Restaurant and hotel service were generally mediocre to poor, with one disastrous experience.
We decided to take advantage of the free shuttle service to go to the Nature & Science Museum. It departed at the arranged time. Fifteen minutes after the arranged pickup I called the hotel to be sure the shuttle was on the way and the clerk made excuses and told us to wait longer. Twenty minutes later (-- min late) I called again and pointed out that we were going to be late for an appointment and asked for clarification when we would be picked up. Again, excuses and no clarification. When I pressed the issue the clerk suggested I call a cab. I finally got her to agree to call the cab and pay for it. We then waited another -- minutes with neither a cab nor the shuttle showing up. We then had to cancel our evening appointment and walked back to the hotel (-- - -- min).
Not much to recommend here, unfortunately. It's a shame, as basic customer service would have made this a decent place to stay at no cost to the owners. Except, of course, the cost of putting effort into what you do.

Stayed - nights for business because other choices with a shuttle bus to my conference were sold out. I was glad I requested a high floor, away from elevator because I would have been extremely upset to be in a room near the noisy train. Room was clean and bedding was nice, although as others have pointed out, the tiny bathroom was annoying. I didn't mind having an old tv but the lack of available coffee and the rip-off fee for wired internet was more than disappointing. Who wants to sit at a hotel room desk after a long day at work? never again.

No regrets booking this hotel, really close to everything, if you're like us just want to have a comfortable place, but the priority is the location with a strict budget, then this hotel maybe for you.

We stayed at the Crowne Plaza for one night prior to a flight home in the morning. Having seen Crowne Plaza hotels in London (which are very high quality) this was very disapppointing.
For a start it took as a while to actually find the entrance to the hotel. There seems to be no clear entrance to the lobby....the door is very small and is next to a large entrance to the convention centre which seems to be part of the hotel. The lobby is OK and the staff seemed friendly upon arrival.
However, once you entre the lunge area you see that the hotel needs updating. The lifts are small, dirty and look almost industrial. The corridors look grubby. The room I initially was put into looked nice enough and the bed was comfy. The air conditioning unti was not on....it was a very very old unit by the window and once turned on took ages to even start cooling the room down.
On my bed I had a small pouch containing ear plugs, a sleep CD and some sleep spray....and I later discovered why. When i went to bed I turned the air conditioning unit off because it was so so noisy. I then discovered that the road noise was even louder! Upon closer inspection it turned out that the inner pane of the double glazing was missing, and the noise from the highway directly outside was so loud I couldnt sleep. 
I called down to reception who, to give them their due, were very helpful and arranged for a security guard to come up with a key to another room...which was much better. Although obviously moving rooms in the middle of the night when I had a morning flight was not the best situation!
Another point to note is the condition of the pool 'area'. There is a sign directing you to the 'pool, sauna and hot tub'. It seemed that the sauna no longer existed and has been boarded up for some reason - yet the staff still seemed to think it was there as I asked them! I am a keen swimmer, but the pool did not look very clean or inviting - it had a green murky colour to it. And the hot tub looked like it needed a good clean, with dark brown mouldy marks on the bottom.
On the plus side there is a computer in the main lounge area which offers free internet access (I thiink the business centre is not yet open), and the rooms with functioning double glazing are perfectly comfortable, if rather dated. 
The charges for this hotel are way overpriced.......we were luckily able to get a large reduction upon check out because of the problems we had. My advise is to stay elsewhere though!

I was really afraid of coming to this hotel - I booked it and then looked at the comments on this site.
THIS IS A FANTASTIC HOTEL - great location. It does not smell at all - the rooms are so comfy - the pillows are just right - great wine every evenings complimentary. This is a top hotel and could not have been better. We are really glad that we are spending - nights here - Keri and Dawson Harrhy

We were given a room where the air conditioner didn't work, nor did the phone, the room was not worth the price. We were told a tech would come to check but no one came. Will not recommend or stay here again.

Spent - nights here on our honeymoon. The room isnt massive but with what ive read, you have to pay over the odds for a decent size in NY.
This hotel is a great base, just off Times Square & up the road from where Good Morning America's filmed. Clean and modern- what more do you need?
We used Supershuttle.com as our transfers. I thoroughly recommend this especially if using Newark airport at any point, you're looking at about â¬-- each

The hotel was very nice, however, when I checked my luggage with the baggage valet, when I came back with my claim check, my luggage had mysteriously disappeared. I believe the hotel has a responsiblity for this loss, but their insurance does not go past limited liability.

HORRIBLE PLACE. Terrible service. Incompetent and rude staff. Long lines with no apologies or acknowledgement of problems. One small example: I Asked for non-smoking room and was put in smoking room. When I nicely explained to the one person working, she was irritated and angry that I did not accept the room. No sense of customer service whatsoever. The problems I had here are too long to write. Suffice to say, STAY AWAY. There are many other excellent choices for hotels in the area!

Housekeeping is the worst I have seen in all my years of traveling. Vaccuming of the rooms is not in their dictionary. Walls of the rooms are paper thing. When your neighbors shut the door of their rooms it shuts with a loud bang and shakes you up. Why can't the hotel have the door closers adjusted. 
If you want to stay awake half the night go ahead and stay in this dump.

Stayed at this hotel in early June and it was very good. The location is fantastic in new York, near many great restaurants in walking distaance. Very considerate staff as well. The rooms aren't huge but clean and updated. Recommended for those like me who want to stay in nyc but on a budget.

This was a very nice hotel and everything was very clean. We just would of liked a gift shop or free breakfast. We did have breakfast in the resturant one morning and the food was good but expensive. There was no resturants or shopping close.

From the flowers, chocolates, handwritten note of thanks from the manager, to porters bringing me some microwaved popcorn! This is old school service, I count the days for my next trip.

The hotel emits charm and grace with simple touches like real keys and a mini-bar filled with fun, creative alternatives to standard fare. As for service, it was sufficient but lackluster. The bed had two lousy pillows and I requested two more. Housekeeping left them on the floor outside my door. I'm a bit of a clean freak so that didn't fly with me, but it is to be expected (what do you think they do when you're not looking anyway?) The concierge made reservations at the Park Grill over in Millenium Park, a nice stroll away from the hotel. The restaurant was a bit of a disappointment, good enough but in that strictly generic, cheesecake factory sort of way. Breakfast at Atwood Cafe was worthwhile. I'll write off any lack of service to the holiday. The hotel was an incredible value for Chicago and its location, its charm, and its clean, comfortable rooms made for a memorable stay.

I was so excited to stay in a - star hotel as part of a time share deal for free! Thank god I didn't have to pay for it! it LOOKS pretty and fancy, but there were some problems which I would hate to have if I had to pay over $--- a nite. For example, self parking for $-- is really insane! And $-- a nite for internet is steep. It quickly adds up and for a young family(just hubby and me) it can turn a peaceful vacation-getaway to stress and frustration. We were bummed that there was no coffee maker. I wasn't feeling well and I wanted some tea, but we had no mircowave or coffee maker so tea was not a good idea. Also room service ends at -- pm so I was just bummed out! I can get a coffee maker, fridge, mircowave, free parking, AND free internet at other places for pretty inexpensive (ala ramanda). The room and space looks nice, but my husband was frustrated because nothing is close by....the gym...any restaurants,etc. The gym is located way off to a far corner. 
 Seriously, if I had to pay, I want to feel comfortable, relaxed....we felt really nickle and dimed. 
 The mini fridge didnt work and they told us to leave the door open...what's the point of the cupboard? The lady when we called it in seemed annoyed with us. She told us that it doesnt relly keep things cold....and a fridge is for what pupose then? They sent a man to fix it and basically told us our fridge was too full(drinks- including MILK and some fruit), to keep the doors of the cupboard open and it's not suppose to keep things cold. WTH?! 
 Also the bathroom and toletries were not what I told - stars was going to be like. It's small and not very pretty.
 I am pretty disappointed over all....there's many pluses, but I think if you're going to put that much money into a room...I expected more.

This """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""classic"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" property was likely once a happening spot located right in the center of Seattle. Alas, it's small European hotel-sized rooms are showing their age. Despite a few modern conveniences like rain shower heads and older model flat screen TVs the rooms feel tired and worn. The bathroom in my room, ---, was tiny with a sink the same size as an airplane bathroom and the toliet is so close to the wall it is almost unusable.
We paid $--- which is a bit much given the age of the place and size of the room.
On the positive side the girl at the front desk was happy and helpful as was the doorman.

For a - star hotel, this place is left much to be desired. Add an inattentive staff to the lackluster accomodations, and you've got the very medicocre Knickerbocker.
Any hotel you stay at on Chicago's Magnificent Mile is in a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""good location,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but this one is a short building tucked away on one of the back streets toward the end of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Mile"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", so views, accessibility, and scenery are not the best.
No one on the staff took the extra mile here - service was bare bone. At the front desk, at the conceirge (an aging, befuddling old man, who - while cute - did not know much about the city), at the restaurant, at the front door - nothing was spectacular. 
The rooms feature lithographed copies of oil paintings in peeling frames, as well as a few other amenities which had seen better days. The TV selection featured only a dozen channels (even every budget hotel these days has a larger selection). The tiny rooms have paper thin walls, which make the plumbing, the conversations, and the movement of all your neighboring guests sound like they are in the room with you. All night. The bathroom had a stand up shower but no bathtub.
At the Knickerbocker, the free internet is not free, the complimentary turn down service is not automatic, and the nostalgic charm this historic hotel COULD have, is muted under the management of the current owners. Among Chicago's grand lobbies and beautiful buildings, the Knickerbocker does not even compare.
If you pricelined this hotel, oh well, you could do worse while in Chicago. If you are planning on paying full price for this hotel, stay somewhere else and be much happier.

I recently stayed there for - days with my two teenaged daughters. It came highly recommended by a close friend and my brother. The Handlery did not disappoint. We stayed in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""premier"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" section and were delighted with the room and all the helpful and friendly employees. The Daily Grill restaurant is adjacent and has very good food. The location could not be better for shopping or just relaxing and people watching in Union Square. A cable car stop is right at the corner and Market St is a short two blocks away. A great place to stay in San Francisco.

Upon arriving at the hotel, we were booked in a panoramic deluxe room. It seemed a little pricey but we wanted a different location for my wife and I as we usually stay in the hustle and bustle of Times Square. I was looking for a discrete place to put my laptop as we checked in our room and were headed for a stroll to Central Park . We arrived early, at noon, and didn't expect to be checked in so early and were pleasantly surprized by the courtesy and prompt respinse from Maria! She was great! I opened a nightstand draw to place my laptop and saw marijuana sprinkled along the bottom of the draw! As a professional counselor I was taken back by the discovery not wanting to be reminded of work in the least. I called to front desk and informed Maria and within minutes Danny O'Brien the head of security and the manager of housekeeping arrived. Danny was also very professional and personable and after the marijuna was cleaned up, stated he would speak to the manager and see what he wanted to do about the situation. After waiting -- minutes we heaeded downstairs to head out to Central Park and saw Maria and another employee at the front desk. I informed Maria that I would leave my number for the manger if he wanted to call while I was out. The man next to her spoke up and stated he was the manager and stated, after some prompting, that he would have the room deep cleaned. I stated that if I could not be moved to another room that the cleaning would suffice. He stated that he would see what he could do. When we returned, our luggage was moved to a loft room, more spacious, and a nicer view. Also in our room was a gift of a bottle of wine, a box of chocolates, orchard petals, and an apology note from Maria and Danny O'Brien. The rest of the - day stay was great in a nice location easy to travel to other parts of Manhattan with an easy accessable subway - blocks away. The concierge's we spoke to were friendly and informative in planning some of our days. Upon checking out, we again ran into head of security Danny who again was quite personable and accomadating.
Overall we were quite pleased with our stay at this hotel.

As the other reviews have said, this hotel is in a great location, very stylish, very comfortable, amazing views, etc.
The service does have some major issues though. For example, my room keys stopped working after the first night mysteriously. Also, when I called to order room service, and when I got my wake up call, they called me by the wrong last name (after complaining several times, I eventually just got used to it). My dry cleaning which was picked up at -am was supposed to be back by -pm the same night, unfortunately they """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""forgot"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" about it and had to overnight it for me. A staff member showed up at my door with milk and coffee which I had supposedly ordered (I didn't).
When the service does fall through - they make a very vailiant effort to correct the problem, which I respect. But - there shouldn't be SO many problems. And, it's not just my dumb luck - I've talked to several other colleagues who have stayed at this hotel who have had issues.
In summary - it's a really great hotel, but they need to work out some operational kinks before it can even be considered as best in class.

Where can I begin stayed Thanksgiving night. Had artistic expectations and they were all met. This is one of the strangest places I've ever been. ANd I was alittle nervous staying here. Would suggest only stay for one night. Think you would only want to stay here if you were interested in its history and knew about the hotel ( we were ). 
Anyway ultimately I'd stay away nice to say you spent a night here but thats it. The place is living off its historical past and capitalising on it. DOWNSIDE : The staff were useless simple. We had only booked for - night. After an argument we were told we were booked for - nights and they wouldnt let us get out of the deal as they had taken our cash. So we let the night go as we had also booked the Giraffe ( amazing see my other review). We wanted a contrast of hotels and certainly got it. The owner of the Chelsea wouldnt back down and admit his error so we paid for a room we never stayed in which sadly totally soured our experience. Enter the hotel and walk round take in the amazing feel but don't waste your money. The hotel doesnt deserve it. Eat next door at the Mexican food is very good, bit pricey but worth it.

We booked in at -pm and by -pm we had booked out. It was appalling. The first room they gave us was dirty, smelly, wallpaper and paint was hanging off the walls and ceilings. In my opinion it was not fit for human habitation. I complained and they gave us another room that was not much better.
Stay well clear of this hotel.

Recently on a family trip to Seattle we stayed at the Holiday inn Express and suites. The place was still in the process in being renovated. The rooms had been finished but the lobby was not. The rooms were clean. The internet was terrible! Half the time it didn't work and when it did it kicked you off after about ten minutes. The Breakfast wasn't very good, everything was cold and we didn't ever get anything that was hot. I understand they were busy but come on. They only had one attendant at the breakfast bar and definetely need two. That one person could not keep up it was just too much! The pool and the hot tub were fine and worked good! We used the laundry room and it worked good! The parking lot was very small and crowded! All the employees that worked there were somewhat friendly, whenever we went in and out most of them didn't bother to look up and acknowledge you. I guess that's a Seattle thing as I didn run into a very rude man on the elevator that wanted to fight! Next time I go to Seattle for some baseball games I will probable go see what else is out there to stay at!

First stayed at the Standard in ----. As promised, it was cool and hip from lobby to room to rooftop pool-bar-club. Not the most comfortable, but stylish and fun.
Two years later, not much has changed -- and that's not a good thing. What was cool and hip is now tired and mundane. A property whose main attraction is modern style should strive to stay interesting, imaginative, and relevant. Without the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""wow"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" factor, the hotel's shortcomings and shortcuts on the basics start to stand out more.
No wireless Internet (ethernet connection is possible, although I couldn't get tech support to help make it work), and the phone could only work on speakerphone. Some superficial cleaning problems.
Parking is easy and relatively inexpensive for a downtown location, and the restaurant offers a good breakfast. Fitness center is modest but very adequate.
We really enjoyed the service and quality of everything about this hotel. It's definitely not low priced but for where it's located and how beautiful the property is, it was worth it.

The location of this hotel is ideal. The rooms are rather basic and there can be a lot of noise from water pipes and ACs from other rooms. However, the rooms are clean, comfortable and very pleasant. The free wi-fi is great!!
The best thing for us about this hotel was the staff. We arrived after midnight and a smiling face greeted us after our long journey. All the front desk staff and managers were friendly, helpful and extremely caring. This makes all the difference in the world wherever you stay.
We highly recommend this hotel for its location, cleanliness and most importantly the people that make it very special.

This hotel is in a great location, right of the --- and at the base of the mountain on which the Getty Center rests. It has a nice pool, small but nice exercise room, little extra amenities and clean, very satisfactory rooms. Was previously a Holiday Inn. Now upgraded and well maintained. The staff at the desk could be friendlier but the parking attendants were great! Very good restaurant and room service too! A small cafe in the lobby for coffee, pastries, etc. plus free wine every afternoon.

I checked with Residence Inn, Springwood Suites and Homewood Suites before deciding on Bradford Homesuites, based on a (much-) cheaper rate as well as the TripAdvisor recommendations.
We stayed at the Austin location from Aug. ----- at US$---nt, with practically no complaints (on prior visits we generally stayed at the -* downtown Hilton, but a new child is changing our lives in that and many other ways). The facilities were fine, not old as other reviewers have mentioned. Our one-bedroom deluxe suite was very clean and well-equipped, and the service we received from the staff was excellent. 
I liked that most guest services were fairly priced (free local calls and wired Internet access, cheap snacks and items from the Bradford Market ministore), although we found the breakfast rather sparse (basically we had instant oatmeal and hard-boiled eggs two days, and then decided to go up the street to the Whole Foods for a quick breakfast). The crib supplied by the hotel was small and made of metal, and our baby kept getting his leg caught between the bars, but it worked out ok. Curtains were awesome, allowing us to sleep in as they kept out all of the light. Although the hotel says that cleaning only takes place once or twice a week, we found our room tidied and the bed made every day of our stay, which was a nice surprise.
The hotel is well located, practically on the corner of Capital of Texas Highway and MOPAC, allowing easy access to US--- as well. There are many stores located in the vicinity, as well as the Whole Foods mentioned above. The Arboretum mall is a couple of blocks away.
We will definitely stay there again, as this was a very pleasant and economical surprise.
My husband and I stayed on April --th to go to the Red Sox game. We both woke up with welts on our legs and arms that itched like crazy. After some research we determined it had to be bed bugs. Yuck!

Had a very spacious room on the --th floor, which provided amazing views of the city. The room was clean and comfortable, with a large bed. The decor on the whole was modern, however the bathroom could do with a little TLC (there were holes in the wall under the sink - which admittedly I wouldn't have noticed if I hadn't dropped something and the vent in the bathroom was a little grubby). This is a minor point as my husband and I had a great stay here. The staff were very nice - welcoming, informative and helpful on arrival and throughout our visit. It is a large, busy hotel (there were lots of business people around), but this didn't impact our stay at all (we were here on holiday) and the room was very quiet. Breakfast can be busy and is a little pricey, however it was very nice and set us up for the day.
Free wifi is available in the lobby, but not in the room - this didn't cause any issues as we were happy to sit with a coffee from Starbucks (that is in the hotel) and catch up online.
The hotel is in a great location in the Back Bay area and is very convenient for restaurants, shopping and sightseeing.
Would definitely stay here again.

Never having stayed at a Candlewood Suites, I was disappointed. There was no one on duty after --:-- pm when we arrived, except a security guard in the parking lot. Admittedly, I dislike staying in hotels where no staff is on hand during the night. When a hotel uses """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""suite"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in their name, I think of something more expansive and comfortable than the room we encountered. For the money, I would not stay here again but would look to the nearby AmeriSuites, which is comparatively priced yet offers more space and amenities.

The Penn is fantastic value for the location. I stayed here with my fiancé for a week in march. Yes, the rooms are very basic, and could do with a refurb - but were clean. Towels and sheets changed every day after that. Bed was *really* comfy, and a powerful shower. The location cannot be faulted, across the road from Madison Sq and the subway. There is a real buzz around this hotel, and no matter what time you go to the lobby there are people around. 
Cons: Our TV was an old CRT, and didn't have a remote control (to be fair we didn't watch it, so we didn't ask for one). Rooms could do with a refurb. No extra pillows-blankets available in the room.

My daughter and I took a spring break trip to NYC with the express purpose of seeing as much Broadway theater as possible in - days with a little shopping and relaxing thrown in for good measure. 
The Hilton Garden Inn Times Square was the perfect location for us as it it easy walking distance to Broadway Theaters and Times Square. It is also an easy walk to Rockafeller Center and Central Park. There's a subway station just steps from the hotel, for longer trips. 
The hotel is clean, comfortable, quiet, nicely decorated and rooms are a decent size for NYC. There are - elevators so we didn't have long to wait for one, which we have found to be an issue at other large hotels. The staff is very friendly and more than happy to help when asked for directions or suggestions. 
We loved our stay at this hotel, and will return the first chance we get.

After travelling for -- hours I arrived at just after -pm to be told my room that had pre-paid for - weeks prior was not available and that the hotel was fully booked and they were moving me to a lesser Sheraton in Mission Valley. I chose the Sheraton Suites for its location close to the convention center and Mission Valley is a ----- minute cab ride.
They have since reimbursed my extra cab fares, refunded the cost of my stay and for my personal inconvenienece the best they could do was to give a miserly ---- Starwood points. 
I always seem to have some problems when I stay at a Sheraton on my global travels and they do seem to be a real weak link in the Starwood group. Needless to say I will not be stay at another Sheraton and I have posted my problems on our intercompany travel site and hope this will encourge some of our --,--- people to also give Sheraton a wide berth.

We stayed in the Dylan hotel for - nights in the end of August ----. I have chosen this hotel primarily because of its location. We needed to be close enough to both Penn Station and Grand Central. Dylan proved to be absolutely perfect for this.
Overall I would definitely recommend it. It was clean, staff was friendly, rooms were OK size, a bed was quite comfortable. They have free wireless Internet (I assume on each floor).
Three caveats I want to mention. The shower doesn't have a door and half of it is completely open. It presents two challenges: first, it's impossible to turn water on without getting into a shower, so you need to turn it on and jump away; second, everything around you gets wet. Second caveat is that shower is quite complicated to operate - my wife couldn't figure it out on her own and called me to help her. The third little problem is that our room was on the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""inside"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" wall. Windows do not open and there are heavy drapes on the windows. It's hard to tell whether it's day or night outside. I figured we'd wake up on our own and didn't set the alarm clock. Of course both my wife and I kept thinking it's still too early because it seemed completely dark outside but in fact it was - AM already. So next day we set the alarm.
Again, overall this hotel is very nice. I never stayed in New York before but if compare this hotel to other hotels in large cities around the world this one is a winner.

This hotel was amazing. The customer service help was great always aiming to please and ready to answer any questions. We stayed - nights with a one yr old and two yr old. Everyone whom we walked past would always greet them and ask them how their trip was going. The hotel was very clean and up to date. Several shopping and dining areas within walking distance. We were extremley pleased and will stay again.

This was our first time staying in New York and we wanted a reasonable quality hotel with good value for money. Were a little unsure about this one reading the mixed reviews however our own experience was very good. We had a 'superior' room with king size bed which was comfortable enough. I thought it quite roomy ['just' -th floor] compared with other hotels I've stayed in the past around the US and it was very clean and tidy plus quiet at night - I dread to think what the Times Square area must be like overnight!
Excellent location literaly just one block from the magnificent Central Station to catch the subway. We also used the Newark Express bus pickup there to return to the airport - very handy. Within easy walking distance of many of the usual 'attractions', Central Park, Times Square, Empire State, Chrysler, Rockerfeller buildings etc
Only quibbles [forewarned by these reviews] were the Evian water in room at $- a bottle [we bought our own] and the 'Starbucks' coffee from the bar which was 'only' made from their beans.
The first morning we got a wakeup call at -.--am which was obviously a mistake and when I asked at the reception just to ensure we wouldn't get one every day, not complaining at all, we were given a full complimentary breakfast 'for our trouble' :)
Found the staff all very friendly and helpful. Well recommended.

My experience at the Kimpton was overall an interesting one, as this was a hotel that provided elegance and decor more than worthy of the price. However, customer service by the front desk was below par, and I did have an experience not worthy of such a fine hotel. The room was super-sized to say the least, with a marble bath-shower decor to die for!! The hotel itself was built in what used to be THE Baltimore Train station dating back to the very early ----s, over a hundred years old, I believe. Remnants of the original architectural splendour remain and continue to fascinate...The Bellman was very helpful and polite..the near-bald nubian-looking young lady at the front desk dare I say was quite the opposite: cold, unwelcoming, and very matter-of-fact; again somewhat unbecoming of such a fine hotel. I was there to attend a company conference; the conference rooms did leave a little to be desired, I did not have the opportunity to avail myself of the much-hyped (apparently appropriately so) on-site restaurant, however room service was disappointing; I waited over an hour for an order that was supposed to have been delivered in -- minutes, and discovered that the person who took my order was going off shift and promptly left without passing it on! A complaint to the manager was greeted with a bottle of fine red wine, for which I was grateful. A few days after checkout, I realized I had been charged for use of the in-room bar, which I did not avail myself of. After a quick call to the hotel, the issue was resolved. All-in-all a novel and pleasant stay, but with some significant oopsadaisies! I'd recommend this hotel for the novel experience (inclduing the tiger-themed bath robes!), but caveat poor customer service at the fromt desk and incompetent room service staff.

I was intrigued by the hotel when I was looking for somewhere new and interesting to stay in NY in October. Although the hotel is not in the most convenient neighborhood, I still gave it a try to check out the rooms and decor.
The staff at check-in and at the front door were nice, although clearly not very experienced. My room had some very interesting features (heated floors), electric shades. For being only open a few months, however, the decor was already showing quite a bit of wear - dirty and worn carpets, scratched floor in the elevator, worn drapes, etc.
The big problem comes, however, when you try to get any help from the front desk. I tried to get some help booking dinner at Balthazar. The hotel advertises a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""special relationship"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" with the owners of Balthazar and Schiller's. When I had them try to book dinner, they could not. I asked what about the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""special relationship"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", I was told by the concierge that they don't really have one. I was a little surprised (given that they advertise it on their website) and asked for the manager. The manager basically got in an argument with me about how could I expect to get in at a hot restaurant on that night. I continued to explain to him that my problem was the false advertising not the failure to get a reservation. He proceeded to become belligerent and rude and yell at me and call me classless. After basically reducing me to tears, I asked him what hotel management school he possibly leared that this was the proper way to treat a customer and he said life. Life was where he had learned to do that - nice life to know to be yell and scream at a customer.
Don't waste your time or your money. This place needs to be bought by a company that knows how to run hotels and to clean and remodel it.

This was a very special trip for us to the USA OPEN GOLF tournamentJune --th---th ----.The hotel was a good location, excellent service from all staff, concierge were very helpfull assisting us with travel advice to and from the Opympic club .Rooms comfortable, breakfast very good. I would highly recommend this hotel to family and friends.Thank you all.
Michael, Mgt furlong, Kilkenny, Ireland.

Good location,staff are exceptional. I was upgrated to a suite, and no extra fee to it. Very lovely room, except the windown didnot closed all the way. You could feel the draft. I notify front desk, but seems that no one came to fix it. During Sandy storm (- night stay) I had a hell of time falling a sleep at night. The room was very cold. But I will still recommend this hotel to my friends.

we had a wonderful stay at sleep inn staff were great took us in when we did not have reservations we were there in oct ---- and just had a bad exper at qulaty inn and had to leave we recieved a great rate welcome and very good two days i cant say enough about this place a little bit out of way for graceland but well worthh it I really hope the employees read this and remembers us no tatto back in ky

We stayed here late August as the final leg of our tour of California honeymoon. The location of the hotel could not be better - easy access to shops and attractions as well as public transport (and therefore the airport). Our room was on the third floor overlooking the 'courtyard' and as such noise was not an issue at all. Although the room could be described as small I have found this to be typical of city centre hotels and therefore this didnt disappoint me. In any case this was compensated for by the stylish decor. 
Wine is served in the lobby for an hour each evening. This is provided at no additional fee. One day we arrived back at the hotel just a little too late so my husband asked if it was finished and the lady on reception called down and a couple of glasses were brought up to us. That was very nice of them, they didnt have to do this but it added to our overall experience. 
Whilst the staff were alway pleasant and helpful, this was especially the case when we realised that we had left without picking up our camera (at first we didnt realise it was at the hotel and thought it might have been lost). We only noticed on our stop-over in Vegas. As you can imagine, I was completely distraught, it was all of our honeymoon pictures. My husband called them and the matter was sorted out within minutes. The camera was posted back to us in the UK and we recieved it within a week. A big thank you to them for that. 
Just a little tip if you're hungry - the noodle bar next door is very reasonable and extremely tasty!

This hotel is located near the airport but within walking distance of the T line also they have a free shuttle that picks you up in the train station. The breakfast bar is excelent they offer something for everyone from omelets to fresh fruits. The employees are very friendly.

They were really super nice. Doing everything they can to help in every way. I never once had a problem there. Called cabs and willing to help with just about everything. I cant complain about anything other than i didnt find this place sooner. Thank you guys. You really made my trip enjoyable.

The hotel is very trendy and stylish. Their pool is awesome but the drinks-food are expenisve. The concierge was helpful in arranging dinner reservations and letting us know what the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hot spots"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" were for the night.

Love this hotel as a cool hangout - appreciate its not got great room sizes but you really feel like you are doing NY if you stay here. On my many visits to NY have stayed in the chains which are comfortable but anonymous. This place is staffed with beautiful people, has two great bars and a cool canteen. That's what you pay for - not for families!

We got this hotel on a Hotwire deal. It was classed as a - star hotel but I'm not too sure it was up to that standard, and a bit over priced. Rooms were small and felt old. However, we had free wifi, the bar downstairs was great for drinks before going out, they stored our luggage after we checked out while we explored NY more before our flight. It's a few blocks from grand central which made it real easy to get around.

Checked in on a Sunday Night. The Hotel is old in appearance. The Elevators have not been cleaned, or painted for some time. The room had old, dated carpet and the walls had texture that was common in the mid --'s. The room had a musty order that actually caused me to feel sick. I’m a frequent business traveler and this is hotel is pretty outdated as for the interior. The bed linens were old and did I mention the room was had a really bad order. 
I was under the impression that all Fairfield Inns were actually owned by the Marriot name but that’s not the case with this hotel. It is owned and operated by a local group and it’s obvious they need to either update the hotel or get out of the business.

We travel frequently to the Sheraton Prudential Center in Boston and absolutley love the Hotel and the location. I have been here both with Kids and without. Their spacious suites are great for traveling with children. I love being connected to everything inside during the winter. We have never had any problems and I am a General Manager of a hotel, so I tend to pick the rooms apart! We are SPG members and used to stay at the Westin Copley, but it doesn't compare to the Sheraton!

Without a doubt, this is one of the best hotels to be found anywhere.
I was warmly welcomed by the Valet, extended one of the fastest check-in experiences anywhere, escorted to the elevator, and whisked up to a luxury suite with panoramic windows on all sides overlooking the lake. 
A few minutes after arrival in the suite, while unpacking, a knock on the door brought a gentleman who set up a complimentary display of water, fruit, cheese, and crackers in the suite dining area. Classy!
The suite was immaculate, kept well stocked with amenities, and I slept like a baby the entire stay (three nights).
Concierge service was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""world-class"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" with many excellent suggestions regarding dining.
A tip ... travel down the elevator to the mall and try the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Mity Nice"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (that's the name) restaurant! Great food and extremely reasonable prices.
I can't wait for my next visit!

I had previously posted (Sept --) about a problem with a lost swimsuit that I was having trouble retrieving from this hotel. I have read some comments on here saying its a noisy hotel, well let me tell you, I never heard a thing. Beds really comfortable, clean rooms, great view of the Empire state from my room. My next trip to NYC I will certainly be staying at this hotel again.

We stayed here for - nights last July to check out the Mag mile and see the Cubbies. The hotel appeared to have a total rennovation and was very nice and clean. The check in staff was very friendly and helpful with suggestions on places to eat. You get a warm cookie upon check in!! Check in was very quick. Our room and bathroom were very clean and newly remodeled. The beds were very comfortable. The only thing I thought was silly was were requested a sofa bed because we were traveling with our teenage son and the room was too small for that. Once you opened up the sofa bed there was no room to walk. You had to crawl over the sofa bed to get to the bathroom. Overall though it was a great We had a good view even though we were not on Michigan Ave. Michigan Ave was about - blocks away. When we asked the concierge about dinner, they gave excellent suggestions and made all our reservations for us. We also ate breakfast at the hotel and it was pretty good. They offered us private transportation to the airport which was the same price as a cab. Their private transportation was a Lincoln Navigator which was much more comfortable than the taxi on the way in! Overall I thought for the price it was an excellent deal if you are ok with a little bit of a walk...

This hotel is located a block from Time Square. I arrived from JFK and took the Airporter shuttle bus ($--) which dropped me off on Port Authority terminal. Walking to the hotel took approximately -- minutes which - large suitcases. The area seemed very safe even at night due to the large police presence and tourists within the area.
I was given a room on the -th floor overlooking --th St. The room was very comfortable and clean. I was surprised the bath room was so big. The mattress was very comfortable with duvet covers. Wifi was available free of charge. Service was good with efficient staff that handled large amount of visitors within short period of time.
The only grip I had with the hotel was the amount of street noise that bothered me throughout the night. Due to the area's location, there will be more noise from pedestrians noise late at night.

Having stayed at this hotel approximately - and then - years ago for Christmas time trips, I thought I would try it again. Very mixed results. The GOOD: -. Easy walk to Rockefeller Center-great for the holidays; -. Lexington Ave. subway stop right there; -. Price; -.Breakfast included with room- very good breakfast and incredibly nice folks who work in the breakfast area; Comfortable beds. The BAD: -. Room (now being in New York City one should really only be in the room to sleep and shower however...)- this room reminded me of my road trip days travelling with friends and trying to find the cheapest room available- wallpaper pealing in main room and all over the bathroom (along with lots of rust, some mold) due to absolutely no ventilation; thermostat hanging off wall (room --- if management reads this and cares), but it didn't matter because it didn't seem to control anything as we had to open window to cool room down and get circulation and heating and a-c unit had obviously seen much better days; moldy smell in closet as it appeared water from shower had leaked into it at some point; Carpet had not been given good cleaning in quite some time; Each morning we had a towel shortage and had to call housekeeping to correct.
