I loved this hotel! The room was huge! We got a superior queen with two beds. We had two bathrooms which was extremely helpful since we also had out two kids. The pool on the roof was great! The bar has happy hour ---. The margarita's wernt that good, buy for $- you can't complain. I will be staying in this hotel again.

I visit New York City three times each year. This was my second stay at this Sofitel and I do not intend to seek different lodging on any trip to NYC. The hotel is in a convenient location for the business functions that I attend, a few blocks from Times Square and Grand Central, tons of great restaurants within a few blocks as well as good shopping - so location wise, for me, it is superb.
The front desk is extremely well staffed with from four to six desk agents throughout the day and evening. They are each extremely pleasant, well informed, meticulously attired, and peform the check in and check out process with precision. The lobby area has several seating areas conducive to simply relax, meet with friends, have an impromptu business chat or check e-mail on one of four computers in a private area off of the lobby. The lobby is always staffed by a uniformed employee keeping an eye on things and there to handle simple directions.
The rooms are average to mid-size, especially for a major city. The rooms that I, and colleagues, have had are exceptionally well maintained, have all amenities that you could possibly need and have nice small touches such as fresh flowers in the bathroom and a bed that is luxurious. Room service is prompt, very good quality and as pricey as you would expect. The cafe-bar is a great place to relax with a cocktail and is very well staffed and reasonably priced.
It is rare to find a hotel where everything is as you wish, but this is one of those rare finds - quality lodging, efficient service and good location. At almost $----night it is pricey - perhaps the only thing that I could fault.

We planned to stay there for - nights with our kids. Got there are noon to check in and the lady at the desk told us that check in was not until -:--. After asking if we could leave our bags behind the counter she hesitated at first but then agreed. The parking garage was - flights down and we did not want to drag them down again.
We came back at -:-- to check in and was greeted by a different person. He told us that they had overbooked and that we would have to move to the Star Motel - blocks down. He said it was a similar hotel and the cost would be the same. The manager was not available to talk to.
Since we had pre-bought tickets at Alcatraz for -:-- we had not time to complain and as it was we almost missed the ferry.
The room was not the same as the Buena Vista because the exterior doors were leading to outdoors and they charged us at a higher rate as to what we were getting at the Buena Vista.
Based on our experience, The Buena Vista Motor Inn does not value their customers and I would advise booking else where.

We stayed - days and we got an unfrogetable service. The front desk were such a great help that we will definitely return when we are in NYC. The hotel is close to the subway and major attracation. The rooms are clean and large enough even for - adults and - kids (----- years). The view in the --th floor was great. You can open the windows but the noise from the street is NYC :-) - with the air condition we had a good night

stayed here recently. nothing really wrong with it, but Hyatt by Convention center is better.
Food a bit pricey, but their starbucks is open at -:--am:)). Walls were relatively thin, could hear TV in next room.

Almost forgot we were in a hotel! No crowds, friendly, highly efficient staff, beautiful decor (explosions of fresh orchids everwhere). This small, sweet sactuary offered absolute silence in it's well appointed, clean, modern, peaceful, lovely room. Super comfortable beds (though I recommend asking for a flat pillow if that's your preference, these were a bit on the fluffy side) lighting in all the right places, cordless phone (not that we had to use it to call them to fix anything) and bonus: the fan doesn't come on when you turn on the bathroom light! Coffee pot for making tea (no leftover coffee flavor) great location, desk with outlets for the computer...everything perfect! Only drawback: being a small, almost boutique style hotel, room service closes at - pm. Less expensive than the dreaded Park --, it's the best deal I've come across in a long while. Thank-you Hotel Gods.

I was at the Omni for four nights and had a great time. The staff was very friendly and helpful. My major problem was the $---day parking, which is typical for the area anyway so it couldn't be avoided. It is a good location, a block and a half from the metro and easy access to the freeways. The room was clean and well maintained throughout our stay and I was generally pleased with the hotel as a whole.

We stayed at the Talbott last weekend for what was our first trip to Chicago. It did not disappoint in any way. The desk staff was welcoming, the room very spacious, clean and comfortable and the breakfast was scrumptious. Probably the best feature I found was Tim, the concierge. He was extremely knowledgeable and helpful. He gave us a number of options when we asked for reccomendations and was quick to secure reservations for us where needed. Directions were always on point and he seemed genuinely interested in making our stay very memorable. Absolutely personable and helpful! When we return to Chicago the Talbott will definitely be our hotel of choice!

My wife had to be at the hospital next door for brain surgery. We check in and although the hotel room was very nice, I was going to be there for over two weeks and wanted something a little bigger. I went back down to the front desk to ask for a bigger room, maybe one with a small kitchen. I met Mr. Davies at the front desk. Bill took me around to look at three or four other rooms in the hotel. Bill then asked me why I was in town and what was my concerns. I told him what was going on and that after the surgery we were going to have to stay close to hospital in case of complications for a while. Bill then said not to worry anymore and found me a much larger place to stay in the hotel apartment next door with the kitchen as well as two bedrooms. He made our stay at a hotel feel more like a stay at a second home. He may not be aware of the impact he made on my wife and I. If you need a place to stay while in this part of Boston I can not urge you enough to call Bill Davies and schedule a visit. The Longwood Grill as well as the Food Court is just downstairs so no real need for anything else.

We spent two nights in the hotel during our first stop on a ten day trip during the fall foliage season. Our flight was a red eye from Los Angeles which landed at -:--am. The Embassy Suites offers a special -- hour check in rate that allied us to be in our room by -:--. We were able to enjoy the afternoon and evening in the city. The hotel is located --- yards away from the T Station. If you are returning from the city after dark, the hotel shuttle will pick you up at the T station for added security. In the evening I needed assistance because of severe leg cramping. The night clerk helped me by going to the kitchen and bringing fresh bananas and juice which alleviated the problem. The concierge helped book sightseeing tours and made restaurant recommendations in the city. The hotel also provided shuttle service to the car rental office upon our departure. The rooms in the hotel provide the high quality of bedding and space that you expect from Embassy Suites, but it was the personal attention and services that made this hotel stand out.

This is one of the nicest hotels in the area, good service, I recomend to stay here, wi-fi internet.
good location, very clean, big parking lot, access to diferent places. We got tickets to tours easy from the office. and more...

We stayed here three nights at the start of our holiday. On arrival at Logan we called on the courtesy phone for the shuttle bus which came in around -- minutes and took us to the hotel. We arrived at the time the cookies are put out, so quickly dropped our bags in our room and grabbed a couple – fresh and warm. We missed them on our other days, but there was coffee available throughout our stay in the dining area. 
The hotel was as we expected – clean and to a reasonable standard. Compared with some the room was well lit, with a decent sized window and good in-room lighting. I can understand the table-availability at breakfast comments from previous posters – we shared a table on two of the three days. If you hit the peak time it is busy and items were not always promptly refilled or tables cleared (most guests did this but a few did not). The food was a fairly standard selection – a few cereals, muffins, pastries, yogurt etc and one or two hot items, plus apples and bananas. The reception staff were helpful, giving clear directions to the “T” station, which is somewhat hidden from road by Dunkin Donuts. It is a little under -- minute walk and from there about the same into the centre of Boston.
The hotel shares a site with the Marriott, with the South Bay Center accessible on foot to the rear. The nearest eating places open in the evening (Applebee and Olive Garden) are in this complex.
The location is close to a major highway which does mean traffic noise; to the front there is a warehouse and motor repair place, not the most “scenic” of situations, but fine if you just want a decent hotel to sleep at a price considerably lower than in the centre of Boston.

I met my parents here for quick --day vacation after their --th anniversary cruise to Alaska. They had also stayed here before their cruise. No major complaints- rooms were clean and large enough but no K in suites, Q-size only- :(
Complimentary (ha!) breakfast very good for what it was but often resembles a cattle call during peak hours (-:-- to -:--?). 
For some reason my room booked under my mother's name, hers booked under my name- ? Still trying to get that resolved and points credited to correct accounts.
All in all, a nice stay and would recommend it if you're satisfied with an average national chain that still gets most things right.

We returned yesterday from a weekend stay at the Skyline. The fact that I had never heard of it during all of my other many visits to NY, along with some of the reviews here, concerned me. However, my family did not experience the rudeness others did. 
The Asian receptionist (does she know this site is making her notorious?) did not smile, but she gave adequate service; then again, no one else was there when we checked in. 
I did not like having to pay to check my bags either for the day we checked out, but apparently free checking is only when you arrived early, not staying late. (Doesn't make sense to me, but like paying the toll only one way in the LIncoln Tunnel, it must make sense to them...)
I, too, found the concierge captain, Norm, and his female assistant pleasant and helpful, but unfortunately they gave incorrect info regarding Sunday service stops on a particular subway line, as well as incorrect Saturday bus information. No biggie, but it was annyoying; I would have simply walked back from my appointment and saved myself from wasting time waiting!
The room surpised me. It was larger than NY standards, clean, totally redone, and fully stocked with everything we needed. We had the deluxe for $---, which was worth it if one needed a refrigerator. (This room is on special during the week for $---, by the way.)
We used the pool both days; it was wonderful to be able to take a dip in the heated water after a day of walking, before getting ready for dinner. It actually is much nicer than the pool at the Sheraton, and outside of that and a hotel near the UN, I know of no other NYC hotel pools. 
It is a little out of the way, but if one does not mind walking or plans on taking cabs everywhere, it's still close to the major areas of midtown.
There were actually - things that bothered us...one, when we were cancelling earlier reservations, that receptionist kept transferring back to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Reservations"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" even when I tried to tell her no one was answering, on a workday. Nor did the manager or assistant manager answer, for almost - hours. Since you need to cancel by - pm or be charged, I started to worry. Finally someone answered in Reservations and said that she had called my number and had gotten a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no-service recording"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", which sounded made-up to me, since other people were able to reach me! So, if you need to cancel, start trying as soon as you know, just in case...Secondly, the water pressure in the shower is terrible! If one has thick or long hair, it will take about - times as long as usual to rinse shampoo out. I finally turned on the bath spigot and just knelt down, that's how bad it was!
Overall, our particular experience was not bad, and for one or two nights, it offers decent accomodations for the price.

I can't complain about this hostel at all! My sister & I shared a double room which was small but this is NY after all! And my sister (-nd time visitor to NY) said it was bigger than the - person dorm room she'd stayed at previously. The hostel is close to Penn Station & Times Square so navigating via subway or on feet is a breeze. Bearing that in mind, being close to the action does mean there are sirens and street sounds going (the city that never sleeps!) but we'd brought earplugs and eye masks anyway so problem solved. There's no kitchen or microwave but plenty of food options nearby to cater from budget to higher-end tastes. 
Reception was welcoming - always attentive and ready to offer local knowledge or assistance so thanks to Issa, John, Tyron and Waz. The rooms are a feature - whimsically painted homages to NYC - and we stayed in the Esther Williams room but can't wait to stay in the Orbit room for my next visit. There was an issue with plumbing but nothing in life is infallible! Once I'd notified reception, they got onto it straight away and I was able to shower -- mins later. Water pressure could be stronger but people should really relax and not complain about every little thing - you're on holiday and some things are out of anyone's control so you just gotta go with the flow. Overall, the hostel was clean and if anything needed attention it was promptly dealt with so couldn't ask for more. I'd recommend the Chelsea for the price, location and a quirky hostel with character.

I gave this place - stars because depending on what you are looking for this could either be a - star or a - star.
Location is great. Adjacent to Melrose and Fairfax District and The Grove-Farmer's Market and in the middle of LA between downtown and Santa Monica each of which are only about -- min away or less with no traffic.
Great price, there are some cheaper motels nearby but most are more $$.
Food: Swinger's diner is downstairs and is almost open -- hours, Canter's is almost waling distance and is open -- hours. Unlike my past experiences and despite several reviews here on Yelp, the Swinger's staff were actually very nice and helpful. Especially the two waitresses we had early Friday morning. Awesome health food market right across the street and huge Erewhon market three blocks away with full deli.
My room was conveniently located close to the stairs and elevator to parking basement and had good sun and view of the pool. We were in room ---.
The hotel looks nice and inviting, the room looks nice, but after living in it for a little while I realize that there are a few conveniences missing. And I,m not talking about extras like chocolates on the bed or free bottled water or ironing board and iron. I mean a HOT shower! How bout a coffee maker? How bout conditioner to go with the shampoo? Lotion would be nice. How bout a phone book, pen, clock!?!
Big plus was that the room has a fridge and a microwave, bummer is that there was no dinnerware or mugs so the microwave went unused.
Another big plus is the free hotel parking except that during prime dining hours @ Swingers the patrons use the hotel parking and apparently the hotel staff don,t enforce the Hotel Guests Only policy.
Hotel staff and cleaning staff are nice. Guests seemed nice and were a mix of young crowd, thirty somethings on a budget, and a few families. I am sure that at least one of my neighbors was having a really good time because he let everyone know by screaming and singing and yelling at the top of his lungs for about -- minutes at about -:-- in the morning (not sure what time it was cause there is no clock in the room!)
Rooms can be a little noisy when guests walk down the halls talking (or scream at the top of their lungs). The walls are thin.
If it were hot outside, which it often is in LA, the pool seems like it would be really fun. But it was -- degrees and the unheated pool was freezing.
Bed is hard, so are the pillows. So hard that I tossed and turned every night I spent there.
So, to recap:
What you get: Good location, good price, free parking, pool, microwave, fridge
What you don't get: good night's rest, hot shower

The Holiday Inn Fisherman's Wharf was everything we expected and more. The location is wonderful, within easy walking distance to the Wharf, Ghirardelli Square, Pier -- and the cable car turn-around.
The rooms are spacious and clean, although the walls are a bit thin and the outside traffic could be loud at times, the other aspects of this hotel made up for it.
We didn't eat at the hotel restaurant, instead we walked across the street to an amazing little diner named Joanie's which had great food, service and prices. We were able to sit outside and enjoy the view without losing the detail of service. This place is a gem!
I would definitely stay at this hotel again :O)

I was in town for a convention held at the HBGCC. Depending on your pace the hotel is about a -- --- minute stroll from the HBGCC. It's a beautiful walk as you can take the river walk all the way to the hotel. Pretty much door to door. This may not be an advantage however if it's -- degrees or more and humid. 
There is an attached parking garage that I did not need to use. 
The hotel itself is historic but not necessarily preserved. I would call the public areas clean and for the most part well maintained. Though clean the common areas felt dated and worn. There is a small business center for guests which was helpful when I needed to print my plane ticket. 
The staff was very friendly, helpful and versed in customer service. 
My hotel room, #---, was impressively clean and fairly large. The high ceiling gave the room a spacious feel. The room had a closet, small fridge and plenty of drawer space. Though I did not use them there was an in-room hair dryer, iron & board and unlike some hotels the wireless internet was easy to connect with. The view out the window wasn’t anything special but let in plenty of natural light.
I liked that the hotel chose to provide shampoo, conditioner and soap in a three bin container as opposed to individual bottles as that is much better for the environment. The shower pressure was strong and hot water was immediately available. Though right next to the ice bin and fairly close to the elevators the room was not excessively noisy. 
All in all I’d definitely stay there again.

We stayed in the hotel over Easter and throughly enjoyed our time there. It is superably located for exploring Seattle especially the Market and the rooms were of a good size.
The staff could not have been more friendly and helpful and the reception area is very welcoming.
Our only 'criticism' would be that our room was next to a fire exit stairwell and at night we could hear the rumbling of what I assume was something like the air conditioning pipes.

Rooms were clean , recently refurbished and inexpensive.
This was a pleasant ,safe ,place to stay where the parking was free and yet short walk to Canairie Wharf-cable cars.
The manager and staff were extremely helpful ,advising us where to go and what to do.
Highly recommended.

 cgarman@diamondpower.co.uk

Stayed at the Muse on two occasions over the last month. Have nothing but good things to say about this Hotel. From the moment we stepped out the cab into the hotel we were well looked after. We stayed on both the -th & -th floors in a king room. Rooms were large, extremely clean and the bed was one of the most comfy I've ever slept in. All the staff were wonderful and always ready to help with any query, especially Rolando who always greeted us with a smile Great location between -th & -th Ave. Time Square, Rockefeller, Subway only steps away. Nice touch with wine tasting in the evenings. As others reviews have mentioned NY is a noisy city so go with the flow and use the ear plugs provided if it's an issue.

Very good location. Decor is a bit design on a dime, but the important things were fairly nice-like the bed, little desk and chair, and shower. Pretty comfortable beds and linens. Clean. The layout of the hotel is a bit labrynth like. Don't forget to factor in the cost of parking ($---day which is a pretty good deal in san fran). I'd say for the price it was a pretty good bargain. The rooms were a bit small, but you are in the middle of a big city so this is pretty much the norm. The Sheraton right across the street looked like they were doing renovations so that may be something else to consider if planning a trip, but the Radisson has the best location.

After attending a conference in Anaheim me and my friend decided to venture into Los Angeles for a few days and found the Hotel Palomar right in the middle of everything we needed. The rooms where spacious and well kitted out and if there was anything you needed including a coffee maker, toothbrush, hair brush or anything else you might have forgotten their concierge team are always able to help out.
The one fault I found was that the Internet connection was very intermittent. As someone who was sat planning meetings with prospective sponsors for an event skyping was almost impossible. I did make the front desk aware a few times but the internet is dealt with by an outside company who made a log of the issue. Not the hotels fault but it did cause an inconvenience.
All in all it was a nice hotel and the staff where very good :)

On a recent stay I was upgraded to a room with a breathtakingview of the upper east side of New York. The room was modern and luxurious but the view out of two sides of the room was magnificent and could be enjoyed by opening the curtains with a touch of the button next to the bed. Service in the hotel was excellent, totally up to the usual Four Seasons standard and the location was perfect for shopping and restaurants and an easy taxi to the theatres. The concierge was very helpfull.

We were very impressed with the hotel. The room was MUCH larger than other SF hotels we've stayed in, and it is immaculately clean. Must say, we found the very heavy wood sliding bathroom door to be quite a hassle. The concierge Laura was tremendously helpful with info re: biking the Golden Gate and with finding a restaurant near the show we were going to. Embarcadero Center is great, and right across the street. We walked there every morning for breakfast at Breaking Bread. Amazing food, and the best value we found anywhere in SF. It was hard to pay the daily parking fee, even at Embarcadero (which is almost half as much, at $---day). Still, a lovely stay!

The Hotel George was in a great location just adjacent to the capital building with easy walking access to the mall, museums, and subway. We did not go to the restaurant but I've heard it receives great reviews. We were able to walk to most locations and taxi service in front of the hotel was readily available. Staff was very courteous and helpful. Room was adequate with a very comfortable bed. Good use of space. We would definitely stay again. We received a great deal with parking included for $- a day and the rate was very reasonable.

Room small and grimy, extremely dated and tiny bathroom. No minibar, dirty windows, grubby bedlinen.......horrendous. Totally overpriced. No room service after --pm. Checked out as fast as possible and stayed at the Omni up the road which was fantastic and much cheaper! Good location on Union Square is the only thing it had going for it.
The starlight bar was funny for it's cheesiness but pretty seedy altogether.

We stayed here over the summer for - nights and had a great time! A huge twin room with - bathrooms was perfect for me and my friend, and made our stay very comfortable.
The hotel is massive so prepare yourself to do some exploring, but the staff were always helpful in pointing you to your destination. Surprisingly for a large hotel, and part of a chain, they really make you feel welcome.
Location wise this was perfect for us right opposite Grant Park, and about a ----- minute walk from the main shoppin area.
As an added benefit there was a pretty good 'Irish Bar' downstairs where you could get a decent burger and a beer.

I stayed here on a business trip with a group. The staff are very friendly, make you feel welcome and always helpful. The room I had was not big but convenient. Nice large bed, nice bathroom. The closet is too small though when staying for six nights. Breakfast is great, everything is there. The bar has a nice choice of beers and other stuff. Great staff there also. There even was live music on Friday night. 
The location is excellent. Close to a subway station and with plenty of restaurants and bars around it.

Great place to stay if you are going to a concert at House of Blues or any other attraction in the area. Staff is very nice. Rooms smell good and are very clean. No problem with parking. Felt very safe and secure. The breakfast was good and had a nice selection. Good and easy wifi connection.

Stayed here once, found it a great hotel as it was close to the main shopping area, Navy Pier, Lakeshore Drive etc., the room was good no problems. Never tried the food but as everything else was fine assume the food was good. I would have no hesitation recommending the Essex

We chose a hotel that was not ultra expensive, yet close to Times Square so my -- year old mother would be close to the action. We were pleased to have stayed at the Holiday Inn Express. Not a lot of bells and whistles, but the accomodations were just what we needed...comfortable and clean. What we were most impressed by was the friendliness and helpfulness of the hotel staff. I fine place to stay if you want a great location, a clean room, and good service, but don't want to go into debt staying in NYC!

Booked this hotel as part of a package deal flying out of Madrid. Booked - rooms for - people (parents, - brothers and myself). We got given - rooms together which was a start. The hotel is right by Times Square which is brilliantly central for Manhattan. It is wedged between a bunch of Irish bars. 
My only issue with the location - and this is completely down to personal preference - is that it is way too touristy and if you come back in the evening from a long day walking, shopping and sight-seeing, you dont really want to go too far for a beer and some food but here you are limited to the option of an $- beer and a $-- burger which isn't so great when there are - hungry people staying there for a week.
Looking at the hotel website this is a spanish hotel chain - all the staff are spanish speaking (apart from the cleaning staff who are all Thai I think). Rooms are nice and all different. They're not as small as people mentioned though I was told we had been upgraded (aren't we always). TVs were quite small. Shower water pressure not great. The pool is in the lobby and is tiny -never used it or the sauna as didn't have time. There would occasionally be people in there posing. Downside to pool is that the lobby and the breakfast room stink of chlorine. Despite there being no hot options available, the choice of breakfast was extensive and delicious (bagels, donuts, fruit, jam, boiled eggs, ham).
Would stay again but there are nicer hotels out there and I would stay in a funkier part of town.

The front desk personnel were excellent. I loved the parking lot crew, especially Timmy. The room service crew was excellent except for the next to the last day, they didn't clean my room and I had to call guest services.
The breakfast mnenu could use a little tweaking but basically it was a great stay.

We spent six nights here in December - got their standard king guest room facing the parking lot, a little bit of road noise during the daytime, but quiet at night because the traffic to Shelter island drops off. The property is well-kept, nicely landscaped. Lovely pool and hot tub, waterfalls and koi pond in the garden interior. We had a refrigerator and microwave in the room and mixed up sangria and sat on the viewing platforms overlooking the interior Shelter Island harbor several evenings - very serene, beautiful sunsets (going down behind Point Loma). King bed was comfortable. Quite a few good restaurants in walking distance. Had a fantastic Christmas Day buffet at Humphrey's Restaurant onsite - best buffet we've ever eaten - many fresh seafood entrees and fresh-squeezed orange juice in the mimosas (included in meal price). Great location overall - easy to get to Cabrillo National Monument, Point Loma-Sunset Cliffs, Mission Bay; short drive to downtown,Coronado Island, Zoo and Old Town. Easy access to freeway to get up to La Jolla and Torrey Pines. Also lovely to stroll through Shelter Island park and walkway along marina and bay. They also offer free bikes for two-hour use.

Two blocks from the Montgomery train station and within walking distance of everything,including Giants stadium. Front desk was nice and gave pointers on everything we asked. The most comfortable bed I've slept on in a while and that surprised my roomate and I. Breakfast,shopping,bars,Chinatown, all within walking. I booked a couple months in advance so the price was great. I checked rates closer to the check-in date(memorial day wknd) and would have paid more if I didn't book so far out. Had a room overlooking the alley so noise was no problem. Small room but plenty for - people. Bathroom updated and clean.

If you can imagine a gigantic estate sale in an old house, with everything marke with prices, and then think you might want to sleep in one of those over-stuffed, over-the-top rooms, the Mansion on O Street is for you. 
We found it interesting, but far from restful and also potentially dangerous: with tight passageways, hidden doors and organized clutter everywhere, just walking around the place with all of the lights on was sometimes confusing. What it might be like at -:-- a.m. were a fire reported staggers the imagination, though there are windows and fire escapes. A musty smell was occasionally noticeable in the rooms and a pervasive and disturbing smell in the main kitchen was seriously off-putting and made us think of spoiled milk and infrequent cleanings. Neither of us could imagine sleeping or eating at the Masion.
High points: great location and there is a kind of western-themed, log walled bi-level suite in the Mansion that we liked a lot and we also liked the stone-walled wine cellar (with table and chairs) that is behind one of the secret doors. The wine cellar would be a great place for a wine-tasting, a wine and cheese or tapas party, etc.
Caveat emptor for the rest of the Mansion. Some people obviously like it, but know before you go.
Excellent hotel all around! Great service, comfortable rooms, free shuttle to airport, and great parking offers while your are gone, especially in comparison to surrounding hotel park and fly offer.

I recently stayed a week in New York City, but only two nights at The Waldorf=Astoria- due to bad reviews. I shouldnt have worried, as it's still first class in everyway. My only complaint was that I had requested a new bathroom (and been told by email it would be granted), however I still got an old one. It was ok and I quite liked the room, so I decided not to request a room change. I did however receive an upgrade (on check in) for an extra $--, which gave me access to the Astoria Lounge and its delicious buffet continental breakfast. The service in all areas of the hotel was extremely good.
I did a tour of the hotel- this was truly one of the highlights of my holiday. I got to see the kitchens, Ballroom, Starlight Room and Royal Suite. You dont get much of a meal in NYC for $--, but not only did I get the tour but also a fabulous three course lunch in Peacock Alley. Tours depend on whats available at the time and I struck it lucky. Im glad I stayed and ignored some of those reviews, yes it's a little worn but it's still great!

We spent one night at the Holiday Inn Fisherman's Wharf in order for the family to be within walking distance of the Wharf. The location is great- just a block away, the rooms were newly remodeled and very comfortable. A downside for a large group (we had - people in four rooms) is that breakfast was not included and was only available in the hotel for $--.-- per adult. Another was that parking was $-- per car (we had three). We later found a parking garage a block away for $--, so it is unclear why the hotel charges more than the market rate. When the additional costs are factored in, the hotel is not necessarily less expensive than more upscale hotels that do include breakfast and parking but in general we were satisfied. Staff were helpful.

I loved this hotel, the location is awesome, -- steps from Time Square, restaurants and bars. Within - blocks of every possible show... it just does not get any better then this! 
The staff are very friendly and helpful... if you want incredible service ask for Lauren, she makes miracles happen. 
The District Restaurant is wonderful, great feel and delicious menu... service was quick and fabulous.
The rooms are large by New York standards, dreamy beds with down duvets and down pillows.... very comfortable. Loved the nightly turn-down service. 
My co worker and I (both travel agents) loved this hotel so much we are taking a group of -- travelers here in October.
Can't wait to see the Muse in - months!

If you enjoy excellent service in a boutique hotel, the Rex is an excellent bet. I've stayed there twice now, two years apart, and was impressed to see many of the same staff on both visits - rather unusual in today's rapid churn service economy.
The hotel is pleasantly decorated with a European feel and in a good location to downtown sites and attractions. The restaurant serves a good breakfast, which was the only meal I ate in the hotel. The complimentary wine tasting each evening is a nice bonus.
What really stands out about the Rex, however, are the superb staff. These are people who really go out of the way to make you feel welcome and who really understand what service is about. Everyone is friendly and amazingly helpful. From obtaining last-minute dining reservations for a large party on a Saturday evening to arranging transportation to seamlessly managing the logistics for a small conference, the staff carried it all off flawlessly.
If you prefer a venue a bit out-of-the-ordinary or are tired of the large chain hotels and are looking for a change of pace, the Rex is great value for the money and an excellent experience.

Over the weekend we traveled to Chicago for my daughter's audition at the music conservatory at Roosevelt University CCPA for Jazz Voice.
We stayed at the Chicago Hilton which was - blocks south of the school and well within walking distance. The Hilton turned out to be a good choice. We had a room with two double beds and a nice marble bath on the --st floor. We loved the Crabtree & Evelyn bath products. The room had a view of Lake Michigan and Museum Campus from one of the three windows. 
The cost was about $--- per night, which I got from LastMinuteTravel.com but you might be able to do even better on PriceLine. 
For food we would recommend Yolk for breakfast - we went twice. Buddy Guy’s Legends was great for dinner and live blues music. We also liked Tamarind for Chinese, where the Hilton provided at --% off coupon. We had coffee and desert at Artist's down by Roosevelt.
Very nice trip. I would stay here again.

We stayed at the Super - Downtown Riverwalk the last night of our trip, because we couldn't get an extra night at our timeshare located at New Braunfels-Gruene.
The location of the hotel is depressive; the room was o.k. but not for approximate U$--- (including taxes, etc). The basic room rate should be U$--.--.
Anthony (I believe that was his name), the Manager on duty is a one man show...a great guy working in the wrong place.

The O'Brien Historic Hotel was in a great location, good price, and right around the corner form La Villita--a quaint set of shops and artisians, and within easy walking to the San Antonio Riverwalk and Convention Center. The room was new and clean--a tad too small. Maid service was prompt. And you can't beat a free breakfast--even if it's continental. 
Beware, though, if your room faces Navarro street (the front of the hotel), there are very loud black birds that hang out in the trees and that are up squawking at night and worst of all, every night between --:--am---:--am construction workers were loudly throwing debris in a dumpster across the street and it was annoyingly LOUD due to the original old windows of the hotel. I woke up several times and couldn't sleep. The next morning, the front desk claimed this construction noise was not their fault because it is not their dumpster--and that the construction crews work at night. Apparently, San Antonio has no noise ordinance!! There is also noise from the street-traffic. So if you can stand the noise of the street and nightly dumpster crashing, have fun. 
Perhaps requesting a room on the back of the hotel is a good idea to avoid the noise (although you'll be looking down at a parking lot). So if you need a cheaper stay, it is a nice hotel, but quirks like the unpredictable loud noise could keep you up at night.

This hotel is situated in a nice quiet location just a few minutes walk to Times Square. Staff were exceptionally pleasant, knowledgeable and attentive to guests' needs. The rooms are decorated nicely but lacking in amenities - there were no coffee machines in rooms (nor was coffee available in the lobby), no ice buckets or ice (unless ordered by room service), and the closets are poorly designed with little space to hang-store clothing. The showers are large but there are no shelves for toiletries, etc. The hallways are dark, dingy and not air-conditioned. The lobby is very small and unfinished. Beds were very comfortable. We got an exceptional rate by booking with hotwire but would have been very upset had we paid more.

its not as bad as reviews was said it was very basic but clean and friendly carpet an deco out dated but liveable mattresses were spotless and comfy i dreaded going to this hotel because of reviews but already booked it so i worried all the way there apart from outside looking a bit shabby your half a block from times square not far from attractions an public transport

My wife, daughter and I stayed at the Hitlon a few weeks ago. I had stayed here before when it was an Adams Mark. The hotel has been extensively renovated since then, and like a lot of renovations, some of the good went out with the bad.
The room we had was immaculate and spacious. The bed was particularly nice as was the spacious bathroom. The lobby had a Starbucks, which was most welcome the next morning.
However, the enormous bird cages had been removed from the lobby leaving it rather dull. Also, the location is in a very manicured office park which is clean and safe but lacks the fun and romance of downtown.
I would recomend the Hilton to business traveler, but not someone wanting the feel of Memphis, which is a fun and unique city.

Sweet, cozy boutique hotel in great location across the street from the Curran Theatre (which we could see from our window) and only two blocks from Union Square. The rooms were clean; staff friendly and helpful. It was the epitomy of a charming San Francisco hotel.

I was at the Amalfi for - nights. I was lucky that the tips i read here were correct. The hotel is on a good location, close to the Michigan Ave. Around the corner there are lot of shops, restaurants, coffees. 
The reception of the hotel works quite quick, dont know why, but also the check out was completely uncomplicated. 
The room had a good size, with a TV and DVD player, Iphone dock station... cosmetics from AVENA, bathrope, lot of towels, etc. Everything is very clean
The best was the happy hour: everyday at -.-- pm! This is only for hotel guests. I read some comments that the food is not good, but this is not the sense of this. I mean, there are snacks: like cheese, olives, salami.. I mean, just for the drinks. The drinks were free. The atmosphere was really nice. 
And: everymorning there is a breakfast buffett on each floor which contains: coffee, milk, juices, bread, fruits, etc. 
I was really surprise about in in an american hotel. 
Oh, the WIFI is also free. And the Fitness Center is not huge but has enough for training
I am sure that whenever I am coming next time to Chicago I will stay here.

This Hilton is actually on the airport property, so it would be really
convenient if you were flying

The room was also very quiet; we weren't able to hear toilets - showers from adjoining rooms. Overall I thought it was a very nice hotel & wonderful for the price!

This place is massive, and just walking around exploring all the grounds is an hour or two. We had no complaints, and would stay again if we had too. Service was good, and it is in a good location, but due to the ----'s of people staying it was too busy for the hotel to offer Great service. We would probably look for somewhere a lot smaller if possible, unless of course we got another good price...

The room we had was horrible, in my opinion. The space was super small. The room has - very small pull out drawers. We were glad we did not stay more than a day, or we would have been upset with how much space we had. Wallpaper peeling in the bathroom. Double bed was insanely small, but was somewhat comfortable. Tub drained very slowly after using, and toilet looked pretty gross. Not dirty...but just old. Carpet looked very old and somewhat dingy. We had a tv, but for the price of the room and - star room ratings, we were expecting to at least have an updated tv, not one that we assumed was -- years old. We could hear a cell phone ringing, several times, in the room next to us, and could always hear people opening and closing doors and walking down the hallway... walls were obviously thin. I felt like our room was a - star and not a - star. I have used hotwire for hotels several times, now, and have booked - & - star hotels where the rooms were much cleaner and more updated than this one. I know it's an older and historical hotel, but we were expecting so much more after seeing how nice the lobby was decorated. Can give credit to the beautiful ceilings in the lobby, but that's probably about it. The whole room's feel just felt so outdated and ugly compared to the pictures we've seen on the site and other hotels we've stayed at. My boyfriend and I felt that we mostly paid for the location of the hotel than for a comfortable room, but we wanted to be right in the middle of downtown Chicago, so we were happy about that. We just felt like we were cheated out of something that could have been so much more!

When I stayed at this hotel six months ago I was absolutely disgusted at how dirty and smelly it was. I am a moderate smoker and so had requested a smoking room, but even as a smoker I was totally TURNED OFF by the reek and stench of the room, it was as if the carpets and drapes had not been cleaned for YEARS! Secondly there was tomato sauce ( I hope ) on the kitchen wall, dirty bathroom with burn marks, dirty outside with filth stuck to the air conditioner and building, just unbelieveably unclean, and I am not a clean freak. Even the front desk person was dressed in a shirt which looked as if it had not been laundered in weeks. Maybe this hotel has pulled it together in the months since my stay, but if not RUN AWAY from this dump.

Awesome hotel! Bed and pillows wonderful and very friendly staff. We were late arriving because of flight delay and they were ready and waiting for us when we walked in the door. Especially enjoyed helpfulness and friendliness of doormen David and Cornell. Very clean beautiful hotel. Great location right outside Union Square for shopping and right next to cable car stop for travel to the rest of the city. Will definately return. I love that they will plant a tree for every tripadvisor comment!

The hotel is a glorified Motel. We stayed there for - days without a single nights sleep. The MOTEL sits right by commercial railroad tracks. All night you hear screatching tracks and train horns. We are not light sleepers, and this place was impossible.

This hotel did not disappoint us. We booked a room for $--- per night, the week after Fiesta using Drury's own website, which promises the lowest rates. Very friendly and helpful staff. Great central location close to everything. Traveling with - young children, the hot breakfast saved us from having to get everyone ready and find something to eat. The free drinks in the afternoon were a real bonus, as was the free wireless internet. Rosario's is a great (but very reasonably priced) restaurant about a -- minute walk south on St Mary's St. Across the street from there is King William BBQ, a no-frill stand, which served - excellent brisket sandwiches for only $-.

Just returned today. Hotel has a pleasant lobby area furnished with tables. There are - computers for guest use but they are very slow and the printer wasn't working. Coffee and tea are available most of the day but we found them to be lukewarm to cold after the breakfast rush. Warm cookies were yummy and went fast. Breakfast was good - make your own waffles, bagels, english & sweet muffins, yogurt, fresh fruit , sausage, eggs & dry biscuits. The rooms were tight and the AC seemed to lag during the night - had temp set to -- & we were still warm. Typical lower end hotel. The ceiling above our shower was damaged from a leak above but I'm not sure it had been addressed. Bath has a regular tub which may be an issue for sick people. Toiletries were bargain basement quality and skimpy. Room seemed clean as did hotel in general except for the pool. When I booked, I specifically asked if the pool had tables with umbrellas as we need shade due to medication. I was assured they did but upon arrival, there were none. The water also looked murky. We didn't use the pool because of these - issues which was disappointing especially in --- degree heat. If you need to use the shuttle service, be warned that it is run by an outside company and will not take you to a restaurant until after -:-- PM. It stops running at -:-- PM weekdays & -:-- PM on weekends. It will also only take you to a limited # of restaurants despite others on the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""exclusion"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" list being even closer - is it a kick-back issue? The shuttle services many area hotels so you ride around to numerous places before arriving at your destination. Also, the van is difficult to get in-out of if you have mobility issues which makes no sense since the main purpose is to transport sick people to-from the medical center. I would rent a car at the airport but use the shuttle to-from the hospital since parking is expensive.Overall, it was ok but I felt the staff did a very poor job of communicating the shuttle's limitations as well as the amenities by the pool. The manager was more concerned with guarding his red ferrari which he kept parked directly in front of the hotel's door all day - that speaks volumes about the safety of the area. Expensive when compared to others in area. I'd look at the Springhill Suites & Holiday Inn before booking here again.

I just returned from four nights at the Loews Philadelphia Hotel. Although the hotel is generally rated as four stars, I think this place only deserves three. Unlike some of the previous reviewers, I found the staff to be very courteous and helpful, especially at the front desk and at the concierge desk. However, the condition and cleanliness of the rooms left quite a bit to be desired. The rooms are quite worn and dated with stained carpets and cracked sinks and tiles. When I arrived in my room, I found massive quantities of someone else's hair all over the bathroom. The first night, I had three washcloths in my bathroom, but when I used one, it was not replaced, but simply disappeared so that on my last night, I had no washcloth at all. Looking behind the furniture or under the beds will give you a dustbunny fright (I looked behind my nightstand in an effort to repair a non-functioning phone and was pretty shocked by the level of grime). My bedspread had what appeared to be mulch on it, and there were crumbs on the settee. I was also frustrated that housekeeping only came very late in the afternoon, always long after I had returned to the room to freshen up for the evening. The only time they showed up in the morning was on my last morning, when they banged on the door three times before -am even though I was checking out and my room should not have been scheduled to be cleaned until after check-out time at noon. 
I had a nice corner room on a high floor with lovely views, but the windows were filthy, and I found it bothersome that the pale curtains barely blocked any light. I awoke at dawn every day during my stay because the room was so bright. At night, I had the opposite problem: I couldn't get enough light. The large room had only three table lights (two of which face the floor and cannot be adjusted upward) and the only overhead light fixture was in the hallway. I found it very difficult to work with this lighting. 
The bed and pillows were comfortable, but the flat sheet always slid off the bed and there was no mattress pad underneath, which I found unusual. 
As others have reported, the hotel is also quite loud. I was way at the end of a hallway, but was still disturbed by banging doors in the hall and by the sounds of footsteps, TVs, and running water from the rooms around me. Definitely make sure you ask for a room away from the elevator at this hotel. I would have gone nuts had I been in a room near the elevator. 
I had one meal at SoleFood with a business associate. We waited over ten minutes for a table, even though the restaurant appeared to be at least half empty. It then took a full FIFTY minutes for our food to arrive after we ordered. We think they went out to catch the shrimp. The meal was good, but not with that kind of wait. The restaurant management surely knew a convention was in town, and should have prepared with adeqaute staffing. 
On the plus side, the bathroom was very large (although two sinks and more vanity space and towel bars would be nice). I also found the lobby staff to be very helpful and pleasant. I was always addressed by name, and the staff seemed glad to help with reservations, directions, etc. When I had a problem in my room, a repair person came within -- minutes of my call and fixed the problem in no time. The lobby and public meeting areas of the hotel are quite nice, and are in much better condition than the guest rooms. 
A four star hotel needs to have better housekeeping, newer carpets and curtains, some soundproofing, nicer in-room amenities (including a stocked mini-bar), and shouldn't charge $-- for use of the pool and fitness center. With some updates and a service upgrade in the housekeeping department, this could be a very nice hotel, but as it is, I wouldn't recommend it to others or plan to stay there again myself.

This hotel was fantastic for our needs!! The rooms may be smaller,but it is New york!! The rooms were cozy and clean and were always made up when we returned to the hotel. The staff was always friendly and willing to help us out with questions that we had. For travellers trying to stay on a budget the free breakfast was a great addition to get started in a busy day of exploring the city. As far as location,there may not be a coffee shop outside the door but walk ten minutes and your on -th avenue surrounded with anything you want!! LOVE NEW YORK!!!!

We spent - days-Nights at the pointe hilton tapatio cliffs. The resort is very clean and in good repair.  The parking was terrible there was no where close to the room if you came back late (after -:--pm). A recent business trip required unexpected evening sessions. Stayed at the Blackstone for - nights for a family wedding. Staff was amazingly friendly and helpful. Hotel has a lot of old charm and character. Very comfy beds, roomy bathroom, spotlessly clean. Nice sitting area in lobby.
Easy to get to Chicago museums and Navy Pier (short cab ride or bus). Wonderful facilities for wedding. 
Definitely recommended.

This hotel couldn't be in a safer & more centrally located part of Manhattan. The hotel is absolutely beautiful. Our room was on the --th floor with a view of times square. I could sit at my window all day & just stare. I love to work out every morning so having access to the New York health club on our property was great! The machines were all modern & clean. Our room was clean & spacious (by NYC hotel standards). The lobby was gorgeous but always very crowded. There is a lobby bar that served really good drinks but can be expensive. Would stay here again in a heartbeat!

My husband and I recently stayed at the Orchard Hotel when we visited San Francisco. We have stayed at numerous hotels in S.F. over the years and decided to try the Orchard Hotel because of the great reviews we read about it. The rooms were very clean and spacious, and the bed comfortable. Although the hotel is just two blocks from the heart of Union Square the hotel is a quiet respite away from the noise of honking of cars and cable car bells. This hotel is a great value and I look forward to staying there again.

Great location, only - blocks from Penn Station and well situated for exploring Chelsea and Meat Packing as well as Kips Bay across town. Very clean with very comfortable beds. The Poor service rating is due to having to call the front desk every time you need ice and at least one elevator being out of service the whole weekend; the elevator card system was also quite annoying. But overall still highly recommended - would stay there again.

Stayed here on our way to Sedona. What a pleasant surprise for a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""road side"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" type hotel. The front desk was professional and so nice. Check in a breeze.
The room was so clean and modern and very roomy. They launder everything in the room after each customer.
The breakfast room was sunny and you could sit outside if you wanted to.
I am so picky, so if I tell you it is a nice place to stay, it really is.

Came for Mopar Monter weekend. Stayed at this Ramada last year and there is a reason I came back. The owner, Johnnie """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""B"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is great. Unfortunattely, it was a bad experience. They change our room from the one I have reserved. The room was dirty, like someone had just left and the hotel hadn't cleaned it. My enormous and clean room on the --th floor overlooked beautiful Central Park The beds are Westin's Heavenly Beds and are as wonderful as their name implies. Don't count on actually staying here, even if you have a confirmed reservation! Based on a previous review and our own recent experience, it appears this hotel regularly overbooks. What made this especially galling is that we had received a phone call from the Casablanca management the day before we arrived, to confirm that we would be coming for a four-night stay (---------------). Yet when we showed up at -:-- pm to check in, we were told we did not have a room and fed a ridiculous and obviously invented story about a roof leak causing our room to be unavailable. (Suspiciously enough, they insisted the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""roof leak"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" would be a problem only for Saturday and Sunday nights. Also, the Casablanca has free high-speed Internet access, while the substituted hotel charges $-- a night. Had we been on a tight budget, this experience would have been absolutely infuriating. Fortunately we could afford it. But we'll never book the Casablanca again.

The bathroom was very moden and the shower was retro. The beds as mentioned in other reviews left a lot to be desired. Like the fact that the hotel had bed bug protectors covers on their beds, made us feel at ease. The lobby was very Chic, and made you want to hang out. The rooftop VIEW was AMAZING. However, the pool is in the center of the rooftop restaurant. If you chose to lay out (in the - chaise chairs provided) you were the skeptacle of the restauarnt, better hope you're in shape. The location was central to Beverly HIlls and also the Grove. Made it easy to come and go. I would recommend this hotel to other people but they need to replace those mattresses and figure out a better setup for the pool.

My daughter and I just stayed at the Grand Hyatt for a weekend. Food way toooooo expensive for the quality. We ate elsewhere after one meal. The theatre staff on duty at the hotel were very helpful with booking the shows we wanted to see. All in all it was an ok place to stay. However, if I were to go again for theatre only I would stay in a hotel closer to the venues. Ohter staff not as helpful to us as the theatre people.

I was on a budget, which is really restraining when visiting NYC. I found this hotel randomly and got a guest room with king bed for $---. It was actually fairly spacious for two people. If you are into the bar scene, a few quant bars are right around the corner on -nd. This is less than a -- minute walk to Rockafeller Center. I would definitly stay here again. My recommendation is if you are driving, leave early and stay late. The Affinia holds your luggage and parks your car for you so you can get the most out of your trip without being inconvienced. I also recommend the Bryant Park Grill for brunch or dinner, its located right in Time Square in Bryant Park. Also they have cheaper ice skating there than at Rockafeller. ENJOY YOUR STAY!

My husband and I were delighted with the warm welcome we received. The staff and owner went out of their way to be helpful. The location is perfect, the rooms while tiny provide everything you could ask for, and the friendly hotel cat, charming garden and good free breakfasts make this small hotel a real find.

.i had read some of the reviews before we went over & we were greatly surprised how good everything was from the bedroom to the friendly staff.We will not thing twice of booking this hotel again when we return.Kevin De Largy Bangor N.Ireland

Maybe we were just snake bit this trip, since most of the reviews on this hotel were better than average. But overall I would suggest to find somewhere else to stay.
First of all, I have stayed at other Omni hotels and they were awesome. I expected the same here. Not the case.

We have stayed at both the Dallas and Houston ZAZA hotels. Several times, all for special occasions. I have absolutely zero complaints. The staff has always been courteous and eager to help. I just changed a reservation and asked for their best rate and was immediately given a special lower rate.
Last year during Valentines weekend, I called for a massage ( Dallas location) and got one within one hour. This was with no prior reservation. 
 Most downtown hotels in major cities charge a parking fee. Don't most people expect this? It seems naive to expect boutique hotel amenities at a motel rate. I am sure there are always MUCH less busy, no parking fee motels that would accomodate guests who cry foul at ZaZa rates and service. Heck, there are hotels that give a free breakfast buffet. 
I not only would recommend this hotel to friends and family, I have many times. 
Actually, I am glad I won't run into any cranky guests who are staying elsewhere due to their prior bad luck at the ZaZa. It's unfortunate for the hotel to lose the business, and I dislike that aspect because of the excellent experiences that I have had. But I think many travelers are going to find something to complain about no matter what. When I get away, I look for things to enjoy and don't sweat the small stuff. It makes for a better time!
Try the ZaZa, it is really worth it. The prices are quite reasonable and the hotels are in locations that are near shopping, restaurants and museums.

Whatever perceptions I had originally were quickly cast aside by the incredible service and amenities offered by the first class staff. Check-in was efficient and professional, and we were wisked up to the room on an upper floor, as I had requested.

Details: start with the oversized tub in the bathroom, continue to the Frette towels and bathrobes, and toiletries from a famous French line. The beds were some of the most comfortable I've slept in, with luxury sheets caressing my skin while the pillowtop mattress welcomed my weary body. I may have snored I slept so soundly - without any noise from other rooms nor from the street traffic below. The state of the art phones would appeal to techies; as would the flat screen TV and wireless internet access. 
But I digress: in between check-in and tucking myself in, dinner at the attached restaurant was mouthwatering. Great Bay has received great reviews locally but had not been subjected to this admitted food snob's discernment. I will review this separately, but one word describes my feeling: KUDOS! Ditto for the food and owner-operated (as in on the floor) East Standard, located on the opposite side of the building, which raises the bar. 
Do you adore Paris? The only Boston spot where you can relax in the true Parisian style (heated year-round outdoor patio) is attached to this hotel. Somehow the awnings made one feel like a voyeur, separated from the masses. 
In a nutshell -- go there to be pampered like royalty! It really ranks in the top five Boston luxury properties.

My Boyfriend and I stayed at the Westin Times Sqaure for - nights for my birthday which was the -th of July. I honestly do not know how anyone can say anything bad about this hotel. This is a very nice property in a perfect location. I lived in Boston for - years and this hotel and area makes a great base while visiting. This was my first stay at this hotel, but it definitely won't be the last: I've already booked - return trips. great location great views we were on the --th floor over looking city Wrigle building and chicago river . NYC hotel rooms are always small unless you have a big budget. If you accept this, this is a great hotel for coming and going all day. Across the road from Penn Station, Madison Square Gardens, -- blocks from Times Square and full of atmosphere. It isn't a sleepy quiet hotel, you can feel the atmosphere of NYC everywhere. I'd say - star, certainly not -, but great nonetheless for the price and location.

This hotel was very clean, Staff was courteous and helpful and I would not hesitate to stay here again. The Room was Clean, well decorated and the coffee pot in the room was stocked with Starbucks coffee. The only down side I found was that the view from our room was of an empty court yard and the room AC was a tad noisy . I guess if you asked and paid for a view you could get a view of the bay or city. Location on the wharf is Ideal, easy walk to pier --. While waiting for tour pickups in front of the hotel we were entertained by people walking their dogs up to the bell captains stand to get dog treats. My friend and I stayed in this hotel for - nights in September and thought it was really excellent. We had a really big room which had - comfy double beds and plenty of space to move around in. Everything was clean and the decor was good. The kitchen was a bonus and we were able to make our breakfast: tea and toast every morning. The fridge was big, plenty of room in it for supplies and there was even a full size cooker. However, a small table with chairs would have been good in the room but as we only had breakfast here it wasn't a problem. The location was ideal for the subway and also for the downtown hop on-off bus (at the Waldorf) which we used for - days a great way to see around the city. There were some grocery shops nearby as well as cafes and a choice of restaurant.s. The hotel is within walking distance of Central Park, -th Avenue and the 'Rock' and it felt safe to walk around the area at night. The staff in the hotel were very friendly and helpful and Rome and Manny get a special mention, two great guys. It is good when staff actually remember your name and acknowledge you as Rome did. We had a problem with our safe late one night and it was fixed very quickly for us. This is the only place we would stay in New York now.

The Nuts and Bolts:
Lots of mixed reviews in here, so thought I would share our experience which was very positive.
Check-in was as efficient as one could design - we were early but they accommodated us immediately. We were given an upgrade and a great corner room with multiple windows - the room was very bright - lots of eclectic furniture,etc - we loved it.
Much has been said of the small bathrooms, and fair enough - these rooms and the hotel are from a time when bathrooms were utility rooms, not the 'destination rooms' they have become. Nevertheless, the bathroom was functional - awesome water pressure for the shower, nice soap and shampoos, etc.
We loved the bed - they just replaced all the mattresses in the hotel with new 'pillow-top' models - very comfy - my wife and I both enjoyed some very solid rest.
Lots of neat furniture throughout the hotel - over-sized chairs, modern colours, different coloured lights in the elevators - all makes for an interesting stay. I will agree with some of the reviewers that the lobby is very dark - a bit too much so at times.
We had no issue with the bar area or popularity of the hotel at night - it is definitely a 'hotspot', but it was nothing that interfered with us in any way.
Outside of all of the above, the location of the hotel is awesome - we walked to all corners of the city from this spot, right close to Union Square and access to all forms of transit, shopping, etc. 
Some General Advice:
Try the Alcatraz at Night tour - very freaky to be on the Island at night. Don't miss the upstairs hospital tour - usually only open for a -- min window - very eerie up there.
You can walk just about anywhere in the city. The cable car is great, and you have to try it (make sure you grab an outside spot, at the front of the car, on the harbour side of the car - great views and good fun). But you can often walk faster than the streetcars and buses depending on the time of day, traffic, etc.
Fisherman's Wharf - definitely a tourist trap - you don't need much time here.
Some great Restaurants we tried: La Mar and The Plant Organic on the Embarcadero; Tony's Pizza in Little Italy.
Loved our visit and stay at The Clift - wouldn't hesitate to come back and stay there again.

The hotel itself is nice. Not the best but definitely not the worst. I scored an awesome deal so for me it was definitely worth the cost. When we checked in I asked for an upgrade to a view of Beale St so she changed our room from River view to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""city view."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" After being asked to wait -- minutes for housekeepers to finish cleaning. We still couldn't be moved! So, here we are watching traffic and in double beds. Disapointing.

Very good situated, near Times Square, satisfied with rooms space and equipment, nice bathroom, very nice staff,we have met the girl on the reception desk Monique, very kind young woman,helpfull with all our needs, good advices and what's important- she speaks français very good!We think to come back!

merci

I stayed here with my wife for our anniversary and we had no complaints. The rooms were clean and the views were spectacular. I normally don't stay in Manhattan when I'm in town, but this was a treat for us both. If you decide to stay in Manhattan, be prepared to pay double or triple for what you would pay in other places. Of course, there is no substitute for being in a nice hotel in the middle of Manhattan, and you should experience it at least once in your life. You can walk next door to Applebees and-or Dave and Buster's without ever leaving the building. Or, you can walk a few blocks and get a real taste of New York at hundreds of restaurants in the immediate vicinity. You are also a few blocks away from the Theatre District which turned out to be our destination for the evening. As they say in real estate, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Location, Location, Location""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""! This place definitely gets an A+ for location, and an A in all the other categories except valet parking. If you are going to Manhattan, please don't drive a car. This is a walking city with great public transportation. If you must drive a car, please plan well in advance to avoid paying high parking fees. I paid $-- a night plus tips with no in and out privileges. It cost me more in two days to park my car than I would normally pay for a hotel room. I needed a car because I had to drive to New Jersey and Connecticut well on my trip. However, I really encourage tourist to take shuttles, taxis, or public transportation. By the way, the Port Authority is only a block away!

Very good service apart from the fact that they had trouble finding our reservation.For an airport hotel it was located several miles from the terminals,however it was still the nearest.We used the free shuttle to take us to car hire the next day .It runs every half hour so if you don't mind the -- dollar taxi fare it's worth it on arrival after a long flight.We were checked in unpacked and in the bar before the shuttle arrived at the hotel.

Go figure... I would stay here again - the housekeeping staff was beyond friendly and helpful, and the views of the Charles River Basin allowed us to watch the crew races. The clam chowder in the restaurant was the best we had, and there was free internet in the room.
Price was right and the service was great. The rooms were clean and comfortable and the pillows were actually nice.

We've stayed at the Marriott in Detroit two years in a row for my boyfriend's holiday party. The party was for a very large group (I heard over -,--- people) and they handled check-in and out with ease. I was impressed with how efficient they were with hosting such a large group. The rooms were nice and clean with beautiful views of the city.

The pictures and some reviews make this hotel to be amazing. However when we came to our room it was next to the reception desk, was stuffy, small and was nothing like what was on the website. As we had paid over US$--- per night for a room we refused to stay there.
We ended up staying at the hotel next door also owned and run by this hotel. See review for that place (White Swan Inn).

We often stay at the Marriott Residence Inn at Lake Union when we spend the weekend with another couple in Seattle. It has suites with separte bedrooms and bathrooms and is well maintained, easy parking, Sunday breakfast in the Courtyard.
This hotel has been very well kept up over the years and is totally friendly to weekenders.

I spent a night on the way to Las Vegas. This hotel offers a free shuttle from the airport and takes about -- minutes (depending on traffic, I visited on Thanksgiving weekend, which meant enormous traffic jams). There was extensive renovation work being done in the hotel lobby, with a partition off to one side of the reception desk being off-limits to the guests, also the lift well was being re-tiled and it was a little dusty downstairs, but this didn't affect my stay at all. There was a pizza bar downstairs where I had a delicious pizza, didn't try the restaurant but it looked standard fare and there was also a bar for cocktails etc. I see from other reviewers that reception staff were off-hand. I didn't get poor service from anyone and can happily recommend this hotel. There are many hotels along the same road, all chain hotels of a similar standard, but I was there for one night only and would stay at this hotel again.

We enjoyed our stay in New York and the hotel we chose was adequate. There is absolutely nothing that you can fault this hotel on. The staff were courteous, friendly and helpful. The rooms were clean and had a modern(ish) feel about them. 
Location wise - well it was ok. Very close to the subway, a short walk to times square, rockerfeller centre, -th Avenue etc. So you are not right in amongst the action - some may like that. 
The room was a comfortable size - we had a double room for myself, my wife and our - year old daughter.
I thought the breakfast-eating was a bit ordinary, then again it was part of the room rate and when you're visiting New York there are a million places to go for breakfast. Needless to say, we only had breakfast in the hotel for one of the mornings we stayed there.
Very family friendly, quite a few tour groups through the hotel as well.
It wasn't the best hotel Ive ever stayed at, certainly not the worst. It was very practical.

Great location, beautiful building, comfy beds. The staff was polite and willing to help but at bit rattled at check-in time. We arrived at -:--ish and had to wait an hour and a half for our room to be ready.

OK, so the rooms are smallish with no aircon, the lift is 'unusual', the breakfast room has no tables and you can hear others and, in some rooms, street noise. But hey you are in the center of San Francisco, close to almost everywhere you want to visit, have easy access to transport systems, have hundreds of eating places just down the road and you are sleeping in an individually decorated room. We got our second choice of room and thought it was lovely. We thought the old building had been well renovated - in other words its original features and feel had been saved as far as possible and not destroyed just to make rooms a little bigger. For the center of San Francisco, we thought the price was pretty reasonable, especially considering we paid nearly as much one street away and had no breakfast at all. If you don't want breakfast on your knees (there are no tables) use one of the trays provided and take it back to your room. Much more romantic anyway! If you want a 'Travel Lodge' then we suggest you go to one. If you want something different, we hope you also enjoy this hotel.

We almost always stay at this Embassy Suites whenever we travel to Denver. It is a beautiful hotel and is always sparkling clean. The staff is friendly, helpful and terrific. Most have been employed there for several years and very knowledgable in their position. Complimentary breakfast is always delicious and the manager's reception is always enjoyable and fun. I highly recommend this hotel!!!

This room was fab - very large, two double beds, decent wardrobe space, huge bathroom, aircon and very comfortable. The hotel is very smart and the decor is modern and attractive. I felt like I was staying somewhere much more expensive. The corridors are a bit more dowdy, and the lifts are slow and clanky, but it's not like you spend much time in them. 
Location, just off Times Square, is very touristy, but hey, we were tourists, plus it is within two blocks of - subway lines, so you can't do better for getting around the city - you could be at Battery City in -- minutes if you were lucky.
I wouldn't hesitate to stay there again, or recommend it to others

My daughter was recently married at The Belmont near the pool with a breathtaking view of downtown Dallas. The entire hotel staff especially Mason (the event planner) went above and beyond my expectations from planning, setting up, serving, cleaning and packing up all decorations afterwards so I could sit, relax and enjoy the guests. I would very highly recommend The Belmont Hotel if you are looking for that unique place to have special outdoor event. It’s definitely not a chain style hotel. It’s a one of a kind hotel that has lots of character and architecture with some beautiful outdoor seating spots. Dallas may not have the ocean nor the mountains but we do have a spectacular downtown Dallas view and The Belmont is the only hotel that has this stunning view!

Without doubt the best hotel experience!. The staff are so friendly and helpful past the point of duty. The levels of service exceptional. We had assistance with trips, restaurants and babysitting and the staff were faultless. This hotel helped to make our trip one to remember.
This is a great hotel located in north Dallas. It is conveniently located near DFW. The rooms are comfortable and the staff is great.

I traveled to Sandiego from Tampa for a highschool girlfriend get together ( we were from Mi and FL) this hotel has an awesome staff, Mitch, Robert, Jerald, Rebecca, Mike(bartender) Nick ( bartender) and Taylor ( bartender) sorry if I left anyone out. We didn't have to line up for ages to check in - I think it took all of - minutes. We were on the --th Floor - great views of Central Park in the distance and quiet. Everything modern and clean. All in a clean, relaxed and quiet atmosphere perfect for familes with kids or toddlers. There is really no place to walk to from the motel, but if you are staying between flights or for a night, it really is a very nice place.

Instead myself and my Father had to share a king room, and they promised they would send up a rollaway bed (which never arrived). Genreally, the foyer is nice but the hotel needs complete overhaul, in fact it needs to be ripped down and a new building put in its place! The bathrooms are awful and the staff unhelpful and do not apologise when things go wrong.
Stay somewhere else!

The Grand Hyatt is your standard, big, large, conference hotel. It has all the amenities you would expect, but with some pleasant things you wouldn't expect. -. Security -- you need your room key to use the elevator. This made me feel more secure, but was a pain for some people who kept forgetting their key.
-. Running track available on the hotel. This is not your standard amenity and if you like to run but not on a treadmill, this is nice.
-. Indoor pool with lounge chairs available outdoors where you can soak up the sun.
