We have stayed at this hotel - times and absolutely love it. We have never had a problem with the staff, they are wonderful. We have recommended this hotel to all our friends. Old Town is a very interesting historical area. We enjoy the park area and all the local restaurants & stores. Very clean and friendly area, we have never felt nervous at any time.

You have to weigh the good and bad when a rating a hotel so here is my thoughts.
Pluses: spacious fitness center with mats, stability ball, free weights, and machines, although the machines are not the latest but they work, plus they have wet wipes to wipe down the equipment, water and towels provided as well as a guest phone. Location is great right across from Central Park. Although we didn't get a great view, we took the available room when we checked in early and it was roomy. Also there is the Green Cafe when you exit the rear entrance of the hotel one door to the left. Coffee is $-.-- for a large and $-.-- for a small. They have breakfast to go, bagels, muffins, and hot oatmeal to go.
Minuses: Although the hotel is dated, it has its charm but hotel room needs more ac outlets as you cannot plug in your laptop and have the tv on. Internet is $--.-- in the room, and if you want to use the business center to print out your boarding pass they charge $-.-- a page and -- cents a minute for internet. 
However, we got a good deal for a room for $---.-- a night on Labor Day weekend through http:--hotels.com so we can't complain.

I stayed here on business. It is surprisingly easy to get to by car but you will shell out $-- for parking. That is not surprising for DC. I thought the property's lobby was beautiful, the concierge and front staff wonderful. The room, although lush looking, was actually dusty. I mean, my clock radio had a film of dust on it! 
The morning I checked out I could not find my badge so looked under the bed. They have a sign under the bed that says """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""yes, we cleaned under here""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""...however you could clearly see dust bunnies. The bathroom was clean, however, and they had nice bath products (mint shampoos, verbena lotions and nice soaps). The first night, I ate at a Louisiana place directly kitty corner from the hotel. The food was very good and prices what you can expect in downtown DC. The next night, I tried to find another steak resturant within walking distance and I just didn't find something quiet so ended up in the President's Sports bar in the hotel which had typical food for a reasonable price. I would recommend that if you're on a budget. The starbucks in the hotel lobby is a regular starbucks - not only hotel guests use it and it was pretty crowded both mornings. All in all, I think this was okay, but I would really prefer a Courtyard or a regular Marriott.

This is a great place to stay if you are traveling out of Philadelphia airport. The staff was wonderful, the place is beautiful. Food was good and a great deal if you want to leave your car while on vacation. We normally fly out of Baltimore, but no more! The hotel is very close to the airport, the shuttle runs every -- minutes. A better hotel, closer and cheaper than where we normally stay in Baltimore.

My friends and I came to Austin for a big UT party in the summer, and this ended up being the perfect hotel. The hotel was less than a mile from the venue we were going to, so we walked the whole weekend. Wish the parking was underground and not down the street, but it wasn't a hassle at all, and the garage seemed new and well attended.
There were - of us in one room, and we weren't charged extra. It seems that we weren't the first to have this idea. The front desk and concierge were very friendly, simply chuckling at our ridiculous outfits and giving us tons of recommendations for restaurants and such. 
The rooms were brand new and very well decorated, with great bedding. Also really enjoyed the AT&T U-Verse HD service, it made our hangovers much more tolerable. The pool was great, wish it was on a higher floor. Also, no food or drink service available by the pool as far as we could tell. The bathrooms were just a tad small though, which was the only real complaint we had about the rooms. We were all Texas guys and fans, and really enjoyed the burnt orange decor. The lobby was beautiful, and we enjoyed having real glasses and water coolers around to hydrate ourselves. The hotel was quite large and definitely obvious that it was a conference center with all the signs and business travelers; they definitely enjoyed seeing us walk through in neon tank tops with coolers laden with beer. Overall it was a great experience, and I would recommend it to anyone...leisure traveler or not!

Very expensive. The bathroom vanity was very small with little space for personal items.
Rooms very clean and well stocked with coffee and teas.
The housecleaning staff were very friendly and helpful.
Enjoyed the whirlpool at the end of a busy day - would have liked to have a change area at the pool.

We were lucky to find a great deal on this hotel. It was worth it. Yes, the hotel can be expensive but welcome to New York. The rooms are clean and the location is central to everything. The Concierge desk will do anything they can to help you. They can get reservations and go beyond what you would normally find. I'd like to mention David Almada. He is the quintessential concierge who made Nobu happen when others said no, helped us get good deals all over town and just always made my partner and I feel welcome. He defines the nothing is impossible mantra. Thanks. By the way, the lobby is loud with music and it certainly is the place to be seen if that is what you want.

I was curious from all the listings and VERY happy that I picked the Inn. The location is fantastic down the street from Pike Place and the original Starbucks, many shops and restaurants to choose. The staff are extremely friendly and professional. They upgraded my room to water view and were very attentive. The high speed is included and works, but does kick you off from time to time. Watch out at night by the market as there are lots of homeless people hanging around.

We picked the Hotel Edison for its location and based on some reviews from trip advisor, I was never as disappointed in a hotel as with the Edison. The room was small, dated, smelly, and bathroom was a disgrace. The staff were unfriendly and seemed uninterested in hotel guests. As I said the room was extremely small. The bed was hard and bed sheets were very old maybe as old as the hotel itself!! The sockets are a disaster awaiting to happen. When plugging in a hair dryer sparks came from the socket. The bathroom is like something you expect to see in a low cost Motel. The bath sinks when you stand in it and there is mould all around it. 
The carpet was thread bare and dirty. People have mentioned the big advantage was its location on Time Square, however - days into our visit we could take it no more and we moved to a similary priced hotel also very close to Time Square and the difference was incredable, a bigger cleaner room and the staff were friendly. Thankfully we moved hotels as the thoughts of returning to the Hotel Edison after a days sightseeing was ruining our Holiday.

We stayed at the Hyatt Regency for a conference... it was very clean, nicely decorated, and the staff were all friendly and accomodating. Restaurants in the hotel were great for breakfast (Altitude) and there are great views of Denver at the Peaks Lounge. It is new, so very clean and quiet.

I think the hotel had been renovated to some type of cross between a mid-century modern and beach theme...very odd. In general, it appeared old and the hallways smelled musty. Our room was very clean, however. The valet parking is the way to go. There are outdoor areas with fireplaces that are very cozy. Location is excellent.

This is a very convenient location with a excellent restaurant and bar next door (Elephant Bar). This is now a Holiday Inn Express, no longer a Holiday Inn as of January ----, even though it is still listed as a Holiday Inn. 
The property has been recently remodeled and the breakfast only restaurant, has been converted to a HIE eating area. This is a new conversion so not everything is to HIE standards, namely there were no cinnamon rolls or the new pancake machine. 
The staff is good, and they made the effort to bring me a new room key when mine didn’t work. I didn’t have to slog up to the desk or wait long for the bell man arrival. 
The rooms are average, and the TV has poor reception on some stations, but they have been upgraded to flat screens so it was acceptable but not ideal. 
The bathroom had two lotions and shampoo instead of conditioner, shampoo, and lotion. I didn’t find this out till I was already in the shower. Just a little disappointment, but a easy oversight by the staff. 
Again I have found that the bathroom central exhaust is not functioning. It leads to steamy showers, and in wet climates mold. But in this area since it’s so dry the only downside is steamy showers. 
Good property and will improve after the complete transition.

This was my first trip to New York and I chose The London NYC because one of the attorneys I work with loved it. I have always heard about the closet-sized rooms in New York so when I saw that the least expensive suite was --- square feet I thought that was great - and the price I got was very good I thought for New York as well. We flew from L.A. on a redeye so got to New York around --:-- a.m. and we were allowed to check in early which was great! The room was absolutely beautiful! Very roomy - beautifully decorated with modern furniture. The bed was divine! We chose to stay on a higher floor because we didn't want to be bothered with noise. The hotel staff at check-in were great, the bellmen were great - as soon as we walked outside, they flagged a taxi for us. We needed our luggage held on our last day so we could go shopping before our flight - done. Anything we asked for - change for the bellman - done. Staying in this hotel just made the trip that much better. We only stayed for a weekend, but I am planning on coming back and this is the only hotel I will stay in.

I stayed at the Hyatt this weekend for a bachelorette and the hotel and it's location and hospitality made the weekend a huge success! We had a lovely view of the city, our rooms were impeccable and we were central to all of the city's hot spots. Any time we needed something (extra silverware, wine opener, extra towels, pillows, etc) room service was there within -- minutes and more than willing to answer to our odd requests. Overall a great weekend made even better with a great place to stay.

From the moment you walk into the Algonquin Hotel you feel like a New Yorker. Its established class can’t help but rub off on you, and when I mean class I don’t mean the fake snobbery NYC attitude. You feel like you’ve stepped back in time when living life meant enjoying a cocktail and the lively art of conversation. This hotel has history, a friendly staff and the most comfortable hotel beds I’ve ever slept on. True, the rooms are “cozy” but you’re in NYC so who wants to stay in the room? It’s beautifully appointed, great towels and robe in the bathroom and plenty of fluffy pillows. And they have Matilda. Could you imagine the Plaza having a friendly feline mascot? Puhlease. Don’t miss out staying at the Algonquin if you want to truly enhance your NYC experience. After staying there I get why New Yorkers love their city so much.

What a pleasant surprise! We live outside Austin and stay in town often when we have late or early meetings or when we have an early flight to catch. We have stayed at this hotel many times before and during its remarkable renovation because of its convenient location to all of downtown, central and south Austin. Plus, it's an easy -- minute commute to Bergstrom Airport. It used to be a drab, mostly unpleasant place to stay. It is now becoming state of the art and cutting edge in its decor. The beautiful new rooms are amazing; they even have leather recliners and granite and tile in the rooms and bathrooms. The beds, bedding, linens and carpet are brand new and the rooms are set up to accomodate even the most high-tech travelers. We were stunned to find decor you might find in a - or - star hotel. Every time we come here we are amzed at the changes. We understand it has new owners who are committed to upgrading all the facilities and staff to a higher standard. They have a ways to go, and they still have some issues to iron out, but, you can tell they are in the process of an impressive makeover. The restaurant is still iffy, but, they tell us this will soon be renovated and re-staffed as well. This major makeover will obviously take some time to complete, but, the newer staff and management are a vast improvement and it gets better every time we stay there. Don't overlook this diamond in the rough. When the building and staff renovations are finished, it will probably be hard to get a room here because it will get so popular and the rates will probably go up.

The Madison is a great hotel. We had a three night say which was extended by an extra night due to Hurricane Sandy. The hotel rooms are spacious, beds are comfortable, cable tv is good and the food is nice. The hotel was great as they were able to extend my stay in the same room with no fuss and help organize transport to the airport. However it has to be noted that the transport is not included in the hotel which would have been a nice to have.
Due to the bad weather we experienced both of the hotels restaurants and we were so happy with the postscript casual dining area. The Postscript restaurant presents diners with exceptional value for the quality of food, please see my blog for posts next week coving the food in more detail. 
The only areas we were not impressed with:
- the doors need some maintenance as they were not easy to close and walking around the floor we noticed several doors remained jarred open -so make sure your door closes
- the in room air conditioning-heating stages, is very noisy and does not maintain an accurate temperature

I spent many days browsing reviews on this site before I booked this hotel, and I was not disappointed. This hotel is wonderful. I took their most basic room, and it was large (esp. for NYC) and new and chic and spotlessly clean. I can't believe the size of the shower stalls (with two different kinds of shower heads, one on each end of a long stall). The suite was so spacious and had so many great features. Where do I begin ? Maybe just look at the photos I took. This hotel is close to all the great shopping (-th Avenue, Saks, Bloomingdales, Bergdorf's, Barneys), Rockefeller Centre, Broadway, Central Park, and so many more great places.
The hotel itself includes a Gordon Ramsay restaurant and a great cocktail bar. The bed was so comfortable I could have stayed in all weekend. The hotel staff were all very helpful.

First time staying at the Hyatt House and everything was just great. Loved having my car safe in a garage that no one can access except for the tenets. Home away from home with a price that that was well worth coming back. See you all again next week.
Jonathan

I decided to stay at this property after I stayed at the Marriott Courtyard next door on a previous visit. I'm glad I decided to try something different because I had a nice - day stay at this property. The room was nice, not the largest but nice. It was always clean and smelled fresh. I visited the free business center and everything was in working order. The -- hour pool and fitness center was a nice touch. I had a chance to visit the hot tub late one night and that offered a peaceful moment before bed.
Parking is free, wireless internet access & unlimited long distance is about $--.-- a day. 
I didn't visit any of the onsite restaurants or bars so I cannot comment, but there are several fast food restaurants in the vicinity. 
Less than - minutes from Houston Hobby Airport. I will defintiely stay here on a return visit to Houston.

I feel utterly ripped off by the Stay Hotel...Due to hurricane Sandy my husband and I are currently nomads and had the great misfortune of staying here.... This hotel has a beautiful lobby, good bar downstairs, and excellent location if you want to be in Times Square, but this is where the thrills end. The room is about the size of a decent size closet...the only place I remember having rooms this small in the city is the Hudson Hotel (but atleast those are gorgeous rooms). The Stay has dark and depressing rooms..very dark colors, which in my opinion was a horrible color choice for rooms of this size. My husband and I nearly wanted to forfit the $--- we spent on the night we were gauged into paying last week but there was no other place to stay. (Now we know why) The room seemed clean, the TV was nice and the bed was comfortable, but it was so dark and depressing that unless you get these rooms at a very good price I would not stay here. If you are ok with dark and small, then this is the place for you...

Our room was very small and had no view of the city at all. But it was very clean and the staff was friendly and helpful. It was located close to subway stations, but we were able to walk to many of the attractions that we went to see, i.e., Empire State Building,
Times Square. Tick Tock Diner in hotel was good, but not special. But there were several very fine restaurants within walking distance. I would probably stay here again if I return to NYC.

Breakfast and the pool were nice. Location close to Space Needle and transportation was also good. The bedding was very nice and comfortable. The size of the room was way too small for four people especially for the price. The condition of the hall carpeting was terrible. I'm sure it was relatively clean, but it was so old it felt dirty. If the cost of the room was less we would stay there again.

My feelings about this property are mixed. On one hand it is a good location and we got it at a decent price for NYC. Our rooms were clean and we didn't see any roaches (which other people mention in their posts).
On the other hand, when we made our reservation they told us that they have cots available. There was a large group of us staying at the hotel and some were planning on sleeping - to a room. I repeat that they told us that they could fit - in a room. When we arrived, they did not have cots and were NOT apologetic in the least. We ended up having to get another room to compensate for this. Also, when we returned home from the trip, they had charged one of my friends twice on her VISA. She spent hours upon hours on the phone with the Ramada Eastside staff trying to resolve the problem. They were extremely UNhelpful and RUDE. She finally got the problem resolved with the Ramada corporate HQ.
Despite all of this, I would probably consider staying there again because of the location and price in such an expensive city. Just watch your back and remember: they do not have cots!
The Best Hotel I have ever stayed. Excellent service, very curteous front desk. Hotel is clean and excellent room
Stayed at this hotel for - nights during a business trip. Very spacious suite. Bathroom was a bit small, but there were - in the suite!

place was a bit dated, but the staff was courteous and helpful. The location is terrific, a bit offf the beaten path, but - blocks from Grand Central which is magnificent in itself and can get you anywhere in the city. Also near NY public libray which was unbelievable, MUST SEE inside, near Empire State and stops on Grey bus line hop on-off.Great value for money in NYC, has a little kitchen was silverware, glasses bowls ect with a fridge, many little grocery store around to stock up.

I had a wonderful experience for my first time stay at this hotel. The room was clean and fresh, the lobby and hallways were warm and inviting and the staff could not be more accomodating. I was particularly impressed with a front desk staff person Tasha Soto who was courteous and sincere and went out of her way to see to it that I was completely satisfied with my room, the floor it was on, the view, etc. She smiled all the time we spoke and when I checked in, and when I went in and out of the hotel she waved as though we were long time friends. She really made me feel at home. The hotel is located on the Upper West Side of Manhattan near everything one could want....restaurants, the subways, movies, Lincoln Center and quick access to mid-town for my meetings. I've already booked a room for my next business trip next week.

This is a great little hotel. The room was quiet and a decent size, there is a heated swimming pool, lots of freebies (free newspaper, bottles of water and sweets, lemonade when you check in, etc), great location for Walk of Fame, Kodak Theatre and Universal Studios, next to the Magic Club and with secure parking. 
The staff was simply the most helpful we've seen in any of the hotels we've ever been at. They were very friendly and calmed us down when we arrived stressed after driving through busy LA for the first time! Helped us to find the best places for dinner or take-aways, etc. Would definitely recommend!

This was an amazing stay in DC and The Hotel George made it even better. My husband and I received excellent service from the moment we stepped inside The George. Our first greeting from the front desk was from Edgar, a charming and friendly host. Edgar quickly checked us in and informed us of the hosted wine hour (fabulous), as well as the top places to dine. The room was comfortable and bathroom was spacious. We had tapas and cocktails in Bistro Bis which was a great way to start the stay. Check out with just as pleasant as check in, as Edgar told us quick routes home and offered us bottled water upon exit. We would return to The George anytime and will recommend the Kimpton hotels.

My friend and I have just returned to England after the most wonderful two weeks touring California with my son. Our last two nights were spent at the White Swan Inn in San Francisco and we weren't disappointed. The first impression we had was of the friendliness of the reception staff. They were very helpful and gave us so much information and advice regarding restaurants, bars etc. We were very impressed with our room...lovely furnishings and lots of space which we don't seem to get in English hotels! Within minutes we had a knock on the door to enquire if we had everything we required...a very nice touch. The hotel has lots of character and we were very pleasantly surprised to find we could meet up with fellow guests late afternoons for a buffet and wine etc in the lounge...just what the doctor ordered after a hard day's sight seeing. The White Swan's location is very central and only a few minutes walk down hill to Union Square and China Town....we took the cable car back which dropped us off close to the hotel. All in all, a great end to a brilliant holiday and I would certainly recommend the White Swan to anyone wanting a central hotel with great value for money.

Very close to federal offices and close enough to visitor sites. Good for business Service is excellent. However, seems that wifi should be included in the cost of the room. Starbucks is a block away with free wifi. Large rooms and excellent amenities
A very nice, clean property in a perfect location in Times Square! The price was reasonable for a hotel in Manhattan. I would go back to the Doubletree in Times Square for sure,

we stay in the hotel for six nights in a two bedroom room. the room was nice, clean and very comfortable. the beds are also very comfortable. The hotel lobby is nice and modern but kind of sterile. The room had three tv's wich for a family of five is perfect. it has kitchen and washing and drying machines. however, housekeeping service was inconsistent an the desk clerks, especially Taho and the indian guy were unpleasant and rude. location is nice since it is one block from the white house. saturdays and specially sundays the area is dead. there is a very nice place to eat three blocks from the hotel named Founding Fathers. it is very popular so make reservations. No food in the hotel. au pain quotidiane and a new Paul Bakery also very close. it also very close to the Farragut Metro stations.

I chose the Belvedere hotel after reading the reviews on this website. 
I was expecting a small room, a tiny bathroom, and noisy nights if we were on a low floor. But we were pleasantly surprised. There were - of us sharing a room but it was big enough for -. The bathroom was fine, but it took a few minutes for the water to heat up in the mornings (before -am). Our room was on the -rd floor facing the back and we were never bothered by noise, day or night. The room was dark so we needed the lights on all the time but we were usually out all day so it wasnt a problem. The room and bathroom were very clean. The staff were friendly and helpful. Breakfast wasnt included but the diners on -th and -th avenues were fine. The location is great - less the - minutes walk to Times Square, subway and supermarkets. Plenty of places to eat nearby. I would definitely stay here again and would recommend it to anyone looking for a mid-range hotel.

Not a super great hotel, but not so bad either. The location is good, and the lobby is pretty cool, but that's about it. The rooms are fairly average and a little bit old, especially the bathroom. Still a good place to stay, but not my first choice.

Sister had her wedding here. Cake -done exclusively by the one and only Ron Ben Israel was the best! Food though was mediocre. At tasting food was spectacular but the day of the wedding I noticed many details were left out and food was just thrown on a plate and missing key ingredients i.e. Chocolates were missing from dessert plate. Guests were not asked how they wanted steak done. They didn't prepare enough food for each guest. I don't think the kitchen was capable of handling a big party. I wouldn't recommend anyone on having their wedding here unless it's a small party. We had about --- guests.and had informed planner weeks in advance. Guess it doesn't matter once they got your business.

We stayed overnight in a King room with a family of -, on the east side of the building (away from the freeway side). We have a teen & toddler who slept on the pull-out couch with no complaints. The room was super, so much space for all of us to move around. Loved that the toilet & shower were separate from the sink-vanity area. We had a kitchen table, sink, & refrigerator, too. The TV was HUGE, which of course my children loved. The pool was awesome, it was the perfect temperature for a late night swim.
The staff was great, Cade was very welcoming & informative upon our arrival. Alecia was super helpful, I'm pregnant & got hit with bad heartburn at -am and she helped me find a speedy remedy! She was also very friendly in the middle of the night & I appreciated her company. The free morning breakfast was well rounded, biscuits & gravy, donuts, bagels, yogurt, fruit, juices, etc. My husband also enjoyed the Starbucks coffee.
We advance purchased our room online and saved a great deal by doing it that way. I believe our total was under $--...well worth the money! Highly recommend this clean & quiet hotel.

Arriving at the Hudson on Saturday night I was prepared for a small hotel room, I had warned my husband multiple times that we were staying in one of the smallest hotel rooms on the planet. I had not envisioned this small. Picture a room with a queen sized bed and one foot of space on each side of the bed - I felt like I was in a walk-in closet. Luckily we did not spend alot of time there, as one person has to be sitting on the bed for the other to be able to move about the room. If you are taller than - feet you also will likely not be able to sit on the toilet as your knees will hit the wall in front of you. 
So aside from the small room here are my thoughts:
Pros:
- Very cool atmosphere, if you go be sure to check out the rooftop patio & courtyard bars
- Impressive lobby
- Decent price ($--- per night plus a $-- per day room credit to use in the hotel because of the package we selected)
- Modern & trendy decor
- Friendly concierge & front desk staff
- We did not see this until it was too late but appreantly there is a really hip nightclub in the hotel on certain evenings (would have been good to mention upon our arrival)
- Across the street from subway system, lots of stores and food options nearby, close to Central Park & within walking distance to Times Square
Cons:
- Price of food & drink (two mixed drinks cost $-- with tip and breakfast for two people was $-- daily)
- It is extermely dark throughout the hotel including the rooms
- Room was a bit noisy, we could hear doors slamming throughout the night & morning
- Room floors looked like they had not been cleaned in months
- Service slow at bars & restaurants
Overall our stay was fair, we luckily did not spend much time in our hotel room, it was cramped for two people especially after a few shopping bags were added to the room. If you can afford a larger room I would consider that option. If we had not had the $-- room credit I would not have eaten at the restaurant for breakfast every day, the food was good but not worth $-- per plate.

after arriving from a long flight it was good to be back,the airport bus service was very good,the front desk helpfull,and the room was very clean and a good size with comfortable beds.next light breakfast and then we took the bus back to pick up a car.
all round professtional operation,we stayed in -- hotels on this holiday and i wish the rest had been as good.

I loved this hotel!! My room was well appointed and the bed was comfy. Street noise was really bad though. Close walk to Public Market and other attractions. Room service was good! And the staff were just great! Wireless internet kept blinking on and off every -- minutes during the length of my stay. I can't say enough good things about this hotel. I was very sad to leave. You're very close to several food truck stops, be sure to check those out as well.

What is it with Washington DC hotels? Chains that are usually perfectly acceptable everywhere else seem to suck here. The Sheraton was no exception. The hotel is badly in need of renovation: shabby carpets, creaky fixtures, noisy climate systems. The lock on my door didn't work, so I got a new room. The toilet wouldn't quit running, so I went to call the front desk. Only to discover that the phone wasn't working (I used my cell). The room was small and I think the bed had been there since the hotel was built a century ago. The only bright spot was the excellent seared ahi I had in the restaurant. But for $---+ per night, I expect far better.

Stayed at the W over my birthday weekend and chose it because a) I've always wanted to stay at a W and b) for it's location. Furnishing-wise, it's a beautiful hotel. Very modern and trendy. As others have stated, the hallways leading to the rooms are dark, much darker than I expected. In fact I had to pretty much get my nose up to the room number to see if it was the correct one!
The location is fantastic! There's great restaurants all around the area (we went to the Purple Cafe a block away and was NOT disappointed). The monorail to Seattle Center is about a --ish minute walk, a brisk walker can do it quicker.
My pet peeve about the W is really about the staff. Pretty much everyone we encountered were not outright rude, but they all just seemed indifferent. Like they never really seemed to interact with the guests as I've encountered at other hotels. I can't compare my experience with other W's since this was my first stay, but I hope the other ones have a more upbeat and lively staff. The front desk staff seemed blah, the bartenders weren't very happy the way I'm used to bartenders being. Is it just Seattle and the gloomy weather? Or is it really that bad working at the W Seattle?
The bright spots were the valet parking attendants. They were always very friendly and happy and ready to help. We didn't eat at the restaurant, but when we went to look at the menu the hostess was very friendly and cheery. Nothing like the rest of the staff.
Anyway, the hotel is a decent place to stay if you don't care about staff interaction. But I'm not sure I'd stay at this location again.

Stayed here in early December for - nights and once again wasn't disappoined. The staff at the front dek are very helpful as is the concierge. The rooms are spacious, we were in room ---, although the bathroom was very small with no bath only a shower. The hotel couldn't be better placed being set between -th and -th avenues only a very short walk from Macy's. the breakfast is buffet stle and us more than ample to set u up for the day. There are a couple if bars to the left as you leave the hotel which are both very welcoming, oriellys and the playwright. Plenty of places to find something to eat nearby including the Oxford cafe on -th which does great soups and sandwiches. Nice hotel!! I felt then that it was well managed and well maintained, which is difficult for a hotel of this size and capacity.  The hotel itself seems very well maintained and has a lot of amenities (business center, a few restaurants, bars, great location on the river, pool, parking (although a rip off at $-- when you can go next door, literally, for $--) and nice views. This hotel has a GREAT fitness center overlooking the river! the pool is okay, I never understand why hotels have pools and not hot tubs...this hotel does NOT have a hot tub, that would be a nice addition if they did. 
Overall the hotel is nice, well kept and staff seemed friendly. The one complaint I have is that on a Sunday morning starting pretty early around - or - am, the cleaning staff were being particularly loud in our hallway. Lastly, I must mention, we ate Sunday Brunch in the hotel and it was seriously awesome, the chefs who made our omelets and crepes at the create your own bars were SO enthusiastic and fun, and the food was great, a ton to offer. Again have to say the staff were very friendly and went out of their way to be helpful here!

We stayed for - nights in November and the staff couldn't do enough for you. When we initially checked in they gave us a smoking room. We phoned the reception desk and they immediately sent someone up to show us a non-smoking room and moved us very quickly. They couldn't have done enough.
The hotel is in a excellent location and within easy walking distance of major attractions and excellent restaurants not to mention in the heart of magnificent mile.

We certainly wouldn't hesitate to recommend the James and would definitely return.

We stayed here for - nights mainly to do some sightseeing and visit universal studios hollywood .The hotel is - mins walk from hollywood walk of fame , chinese mann theatre , madame tussuards ,metro station ( - stop from universal studios ) and all tours to stars homes. The Onyx is a wonderful addition to the North Station area. Steps from the trains and North End and Quincy Market. My room was gorgeous and very quiet - didn't hear any noise from the hall during the night, bed was super comfortable and I was greeted with a glass of wine when I walked into the lobby to check in. We were first time in New York and stayed here. Staff was very friendly and helpful, hotel was cool, its easy to walk, take taxi or use subway from or to there. We love the place. If all the shops and stores near the hotel would be like the two which are in the hotel, I would give - to the location instead of -.

Stayed here on a priceline reservation for three nights at the end of a weeklong vacation trip.
Over the years, I have stayed at the other two Nob Hill """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""grande dame"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotels -- the Fairmont and the Mark Hopkins, and I would include the Stanford Court in the same category.
When I arrived, I was offered a queen room with a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""better view"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" than the king room that had been set aside for me. I assumed that this was a win-win, but as it turned out, it was a mixed blessing.
True, the room I ended up with had very nice views, and I assume that the room that I had been given was an interior room with no views at all, but the views came at a cost.
The Stanford Court faces Powell Street, which is the one that the two of the three cable cars run on. The room they gave me was right over the Powell Street side, and on a lower floor (-rd), so the cable cars going by, ringing their bells at every stop, were quite noticeable during their operating hours. For a city dweller, this was a minor annoyance, but for someone from more quiet surroundings might find this rather disturbing. Just a word of caution.
Otherwise, the room was very well furnished, with a very firm and comfortable bed, a large flat-screen TV and a writing desk and small chair and table. The room was small but not claustrophobic, and the bathroom-closet was laid out intelligently, allowing for two guests to be using different parts of the layout in succession.
The staff was extremely helpful and courteous. I was even able to save a little time and effort by purchasing my Transit Pass from the front desk, rather than from the Muni booth.
I will also caution those who choose to avail themselves of the valet parking at the hotel. While it was very convenient, I found that calling ahead for the car was not always successful. Most likely, the attendants were constantly out, moving the cars in and out, and were not there to answer the calls, so more often than not, I just had to head down and call for the car from the doorman and wait.
Personally, I prefer Nob Hill as a central location for stays in SF, and in that sense, the Stanford Court certainly fit the bill. Other than my concern over the street noise, I would definitely recommend the Stanford Court and would stay there again on future trips to SF.

Campus hotels are a little unpredictable, but this one is a star. The rooms look to have been recently redone, and are attractive and comfortable. I had dinner in the restaurant and service and food were flawless. Some renovation was ongoing in the area containing offices-meeting rooms, and our meeting room was nothing special, so maybe they are working to update that part of the hotel next. If you have business at or near the University of Houston, this is a very good place to stay. The hotel wireless didn't work well for me, but the University's wireless network was a perfect substitute. Both are free.

Staying at this hotel provided a wonderful experience. The staff were extremely professional and friendly. We were able to check in four hours early. The room and bathroom were beautiful. Stay at this hotel, and I promise that you will not regret it!

I would stay here again if the price was right again. Any more and I would explore other options.

Best Western Grant Park - only adequate. The front desk staff was very helpful. The outdoor pool was nice. The problem with this hotel is restaurant facilities. The only food was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""continental breakfast"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which is useless for people with kids. We ended up eating at another hotel down the block. The fun stuff ends there folks. The room was dank, dark, the lights worked at varying intervals that could only be attributed to the lunar cycle, the carpet was dirty. It started out as an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""OK"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on the cleanliness factor, and deteriorated to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Disgusting"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on the day we checked out. The bathtub did not drain - AT ALL. Trust me, I am not a whiner. I have stayed in some grotty hotels. This is the second grottiest. The only reason the other hotel in my grotty category wins first prize is that it had bullet holes in the door and no towels. But you would expect that in Detroit :)

Perfect location, close to Times Square, but in quiet street. Very Comfortable room and bed. Bathroom something special. Staff friendly and helpful. Wifi wouldn't work in our room on top floor, but good access to computers and printer in lobby. Walking distance to good restaurants

Upon arrival we mistook the young man in a hotel uniform as someone who would open the door or help with our luggage. Since this wasn’t the case we lugged our baggage to the unmanned front desk. When the staff member materialized we inquired about dining options. She noted the bar would be shutting down so we’d be better off to go elsewhere or order from the -- hour room service menu. Tired and hungry we asked if we could order now and have it sent up. No good, we’d have phone from our room. 
Minutes later the same woman took our order via phone for a sandwich and a couple of beers, and foam pillows. We were informed, “Dinner would be on the way shortly, however drinks should have been ordered ten minutes ago while the bartender was still on duty.” We decided to raid the mini bar and watch some TV during the wait. Strangely the remote was missing. 
The uniformed guy reappeared to deliver our sandwiches. When we inquired about the pillows, he performed an enthusiastic search of our empty closet. After concluding the closet was still bare, he helpfully suggested that pillows must have been removed to accommodate another guest since there were none left with housekeeping. 
Other things to know before you go:
-Upon request a special a special remote control that only makes the channel go down can be delivered to your room 
-Lingering over your first cup of coffee is frowned on; refills stop at -:--.
-Pinnacle King Rooms are average sized with miniature bathrooms
-Ice is a precious commodity and can only be distributed by room service
-Hailing a taxi is more reliable than counting on the concierge to remember to arrange transportation, even if you are standing right in front of him
-The business amenities are great as long as you brought your own machine and don’t need a business center
-Request and complaints are met with attitude and sarcasm by the front desk
Most importantly we learned walking away is sometimes the best option. For ten dollars more per night the Westin across the street had helpful staff, functional business center, spacious bath, and plenty of pillow options. As a special treat a fully functional remote is supplied with each room.

I travel to NYC for business once per month, and this is my new favorite. Great mid-Manhattan location, reasonable rates for NYC. Many casual dining options within -min walk, convenience store across the street.

I stayed here with a friend for - nights on a trip to the West Coast in September-October ----. We had a bit of a mishap at check-in. We just returned from a - night stay at the Drake. - nights were using Hilton Honors rewards points, and we added - night at our own expense. If you think the Drake loves their Hilton Honors member, you will be sadly disappointed. Upon check in, we learned we would have to move after the first - nights, because we had booked our extra night in a different category of room than the room booked using our Hilton Honors points (we politely asked if we might be assigned to one room for our entire stay but were told no). There was mold growing around the shower bar and soap dish, and the tile grout looked like it needed some scrubbing. The first evening, I hardly slept at all due to the air conditioner. It was a warm evening and every time the air conditioner fan turned off there was a loud Bang! At -am I called the front desk and asked for a new room or to have the maintenance people fix the AC. No offer for a new room, but maintenance did arrive within minutes and fixed the banging AC. Fresh towels arrived one evening long after we had requested them, and long after I had wandered the halls to find them myself. Believe me, we felt pretty invisible and ignored! There was no comparison between the rooms, in fact, at the moment we walked in to the -nd room we realized how truly awful the first room was. The maids were friendly and polite. The concierge was helpful and gave good directions and suggestions. But if you want to feel pampered and safe and valued as a customer, find another hotel.

Mary-Lu and Chris
Canada

After doing some online research, my wife and I decided to book our early November ---- stay in Manhattan at the Hotel Elysée - and we are very glad we did.

I'll admit, I'd been itching to stay at this place since the new terminal opened in ----. But I never had a layover long enough to justify it until last weekend. After finally staying here, I have to agree with the other reviews - if you need an airport hotel at DTW, this is your place.
Finding the check-in desk at first was a challenge - entering from the land side put me on the third level, and I had to go downstairs and wind my way past the restaurant. Once I got there, check-in and check out were a snap. Since my flight didn't leave until -, they agreed to extend my checkout until -:--pm. My room was well-lit and everything was functional. There were lots of outlets to plug in my gear. The furnishings were typical Westin save for the (really comfortable) chaise lounger in front of the window for those of us who like to watch the airplanes. 
This is an airport hotel, so don't expect much for free. There are several bottles of water, wine and a mini-bar in the room. Read the tags very carefully before you open anything, because some items are free and others will cost you. Internet is $---day (free in the lobby) and there's no free breakfast unless you have club access. Like other reviewers, I found the hotel to be very quiet, with what I would consider a normal level of noise from the hallways and other rooms. The airplane noise was very muted, but still present... especially when the larger jets took off, but still considerably quieter than most airport hotels I've stayed at. There is also a tunnel that runs under the hotel for airport vehicles, and even on the upper floors I could occasionally hear the clattering of those trucks.. presumably coming through the ductwork. 
The entire hotel was exceptionally clean and smelled great - probably the cleanest Westin I've stayed at. The furnishings in my room were showing a fair amount of wear, but everything was functional. Unfortunately, the housekeepers left some trash and wet towels in the room from a previous guest. A quick call to the desk fixed the problem, and they comped my breakfast in the restaurant the next morning as an apology. Now THAT'S customer service! In fact, all the staff I interacted with were incredibly friendly and helpful. When I needed an item delivered to my room, they were there within five minutes!
I only tried the restaurant for breakfast, and while good, it was over-the-top expensive, even for an airport hotel. $--+tax for cereal and coffee?? If you're flying Delta, I'd recommend going into the terminal for breakfast. You'll need a Delta boarding pass to get through the checkpoint as the hotel won't give you a pass on the day you check out, and TSA won't accept a non-Delta boarding pass at the hotel's security checkpoint. The hotel's TSA checkpoint was open from -:--am--pm and using it was easier than I expected. Even though they say to allow -- minutes for the process, I was through in less than five. Without a boarding pass, the Detroit Police must screen you first, verify you're a hotel guest, and give you a pass (which you then give to the TSA agent who's standing ten feet away.) If there's not an officer present the front desk will have to call one for you. You'll get the full pat-down unless you have a Delta boarding pass.

Overall an excellent stay, and I'd highly recommend it for an overnight at DTW.

Cons: Poor layout. Undesirable location if you want to walk anywhere interesting. Thin walls. Old TV's. Very skinny parking spots at $---day. No restaurant or bar. Definitely not a luxury feel even though it's pretty pricey.

Monarch was great considering how inexpensive the room was. There were clean sheets, good shower pressure and sealing high bathroom mirror. The staff was nice and accommodating. If you are not used to large cities, area around the hotel may seem iffy, but it is just fine – there are even Mercedes-Benz and Bentley dealerships around the corner. Definitely believe all the negative reviews you have read. I wish I did. The reason I chose this hotel was because of it's location. My two teenage daughters and their two friends were to attend Z---'s Jingle Ball at Madison Square Garden on December --. I knew the show would be over late so I decided to stay overnight. When checking in I was told that not only were the two rooms not next to each other, they were on completely opposite sides of the hotel. I was told that they were sold out. Now, there is -,--- rooms in this place and they couldn't find - together? So we go to our room and had a good laugh. The room was HUGE but barely had anything in it. My partner and I stayed at the Blakely between just after Christmas and the new year.
On arrival we were pleased to find the helpful concierge and hassle free check in service though were a little disappointed that our room didn't have a bath. To be honest, I'm sure that if we had said something at the time they would have switched us over but we weren't so fussed. There was a nice little minibar, microwave, fridge and coffee making facilities as well as the standard room amenities at an additional charge. We also had fresh linens and dressing gowns.
Nice points - the hotel is very lovely, the staff in the lobby are helpful and the maid service was always excellent. The housekeepers were also very friendly when you spotted them round and about the hotel. You get a free copy of the NY Times every morning which was useful and the bedroom was full of modern conveniences, i.e: easy to use air con-heating, soft pillows and TV services with lots of channels. Not so nice points - The hotel hallways and lobby seem to be kept at a very high heat; not sure if this was just me however I constantly felt I was far too hot in the hallways. The staff in the restaurant at breakfast were just plain rude. This is a traditional motel-style building with outside balcony corridors. On the first floor you may be bothered by headlights of parking cars. I found it impossible to darken my room completely because of gaps in the curtains and the outside lighting. The room was simple and clean, with a refrigerator, safe, coffee maker, ironing board, hair dryer, and minimal amenities. Shower worked well and there were adequate towels, nothing luxurious. Everything was clean and the bed was OK, not luxurious but not lumpy, either. Room showed a little wear and tear but nothing serious. No washcloths, for some reason. I arrived late at night with no reservation to catch an early morning flight. The girl at the desk was businesslike and efficient. They have a shuttle to the airport every half hour, -- h a day. A breakfast is provided but I did not sample it because my flight was too early. A McDonalds, Chinese and Mexican restaurants, and the light rail station are an easy walk from the hotel. When I was there the clientele seemed to be guys getting ready to ship out for Alaska fishing jobs. This place is perfectly adequate for the purpose of catching some Zs and a ride to the airport but it looks a little tough and some people would be put off by it. Manager and shuttle driver were very friendly.
Hotel had friendly service. Was located easy walking distance to the public transportation. Do not try to walk to Fisherman's Wharf... too far...uphill...oops.

Beds and bathroom o.k., but carpets made your feet look black after a few steps on the floor. Front desk staff friendly and heplful, e.g., when we asked for a refridgerator, because the one in the room wasn´t working. Pool was in a very bad condition when we arrived in the afternoon of Labor day. Perhaps an exception, but we never tried again, because it was really digusting the first day. Location is o.k., near many fastfood restaurants and shops.

This hotel is located in a great area for sightseeing in Manhatten. Hotel itself was very nice with nice decor. Lounge was excellent. restaruant far too expensive even for breakfast. Rooms were small and cramped and a bit old-run down for the price paid.

We were touring the USA and choose the James Hotel in Chicago as a special treat so were very disappointed to find it was just an average hotel. Very nice hotel, for being old. The amenities and service were top notch. The staff at the front desk were extremely helpful and answered all of our questions. They also gave us great suggestions for fun establishments to visit. The restaurant next door was very convenient for late night or early morning meals. The bar drinks were very good, as was the service.

Our family of - stayed at this hotel recently and it was great. From a very pleasant and efficient check in, to breakfast in the cafe, the concierge, and afternoon drinks in the bar this was a most pleasant experience. We particularly note one of the barmen, Clayton, who was efficient and fun. The only thing that was unfortunate was that the hotel rooms can only have - beds (we asked our travel agent to request a rollaway for one of our boys before we left), howevr city regulations don't allow more than - beds in each room. Top grade hotel with everything you need and plenty of restaurants in the area. Great staff,friendly and helpful. Can't say enough for our time there.

My Husband and I spent - nights at Humphreys. We had a great room overlooking the pool. Our room was very clean and the maid service was exceptional. The staff was very helpful and friendly. The pool and grounds were beautiful. I would definately stay here again.

My family and I stayed here(wife and - yr old girl) Aug ----- and had a great time. The grounds were gorgeous and it made you feel like you were in a tropical location. Stayed at the Dylan in October ---- for one night, our last one in NYC, which was supposed to be a special treat to me and my significant other. Room was extra clean and beds quite comfortable.... Liked that the vanity was not in the shower-toilet area. Pool area is pretty, and free breakfast was a nice touch. Recommend, but be careful, everything adds up.

Having read the reviews here and the eternal nagging about the elevators I was a bit afraid to go here.
So first off: the elevators aren't that bad, they are crowded and there is some waiting involved during rush hour, but - mins was the maximum I had to wait. The breakfast area was very crowded as well and sometimes we had to search a bit to find a spot to sit.

It is beyond me why a new hotel choose these units as they only provide two settings: very noisy and extremely noisy.Luckily it wasn't that hot and we could make it through the night with it switched off.
Location is very good, very close to a subway station and the area isn't shady at all. I have the impression some people freak out because there is an 'adult' bookstore nearby...

This is an older motel, much like you would see built in the --'s. The rooms are small and furnishings outdated: But what do you expect for $--.-- a night in Austin. If you are just looking for a place to lay your head and aren't going to spend alot of time in the room, this is an excellent choice to save some money. It has apool that looked fine and has a basic continental breakfast. There was free WiFi in the room. It is convenient to St. Edwards Univ. (about - mile), and about - miles from UT. It is -- miles to the San Maros outlet malls. Pets are allowed at no charge.

My daughter and I stayed there for - night in early April. I was a bit apprehensive because of the bad reviews I have read. Well, it wasn't so bad. Our room on the first floor facing the pool was acceptably clean just smelled old. Bathtub and showerhead did need some upgrading. Firstly we booked it online and had mentioned we needed two double beds. Fortunately we were able to switch it and the Front desk staff were great. It was close enough to walk everywhere which we enjoyed. Fabulous service and rooms. Amazing staff. Helena at the front desk was an expert in customer service!!! Yeah for Frette linens and amazing views.

Not only was the Affinia Chicago the most affordable luxary Hotel downtown Chicago, but Albert and the rest of the Staff were AMAZING and accomodating! Priced as NYC hotels are, you pay more than in other cities, but it is simply worth in for the location, and a little pricacy in the heart of the worlds greatest city.

The internet in the room was $- an hour, and would disconnect you after each hour to have you renew (very bad if you need to remote in to work).

Great location. Local transportation to everyplace we wanted to go in Seattle including the airport. It is walking distance to Pikes market, the waterfront and right in the middle of great shopping. The staff was friendly, and they must have fixed the ice machine on the --th floor. Room was spacious, and very clean. Nice terrace brunch, but closed for private party for dinner, but nice pub below the entrance. Adequate seating in lobby but as stated before, no area to chill.

My husband and I stayed at the Roosevelt Hotel for - nights and I can honestly not fault it at all. Its in such a great location being - block from -th Avenue and right on Madison Avenue. The room was spotless and quite spacious, contrary to what I have read previously about 'box rooms'! The staff were more than helpful especially as the hotel was extremely busy. Even at the government rate, the Hard Rock is hard to recommend for anything other than its location and excellent desk and concierge service. 
Our corner room on the fifth (Beatles) floor was spacious and clean, as one would expect. But the presumably trendy decor was a bit on the bizarre side, from the lizard-skin-like vinyl lounge chair with orange shag pillow to the tiger-striped bureau, grey walls and carpeting. I didn't mind John and Yoko peering over their shoulders in the bathroom, but the photo overlooking the bed, of Sting in full mouth-taped-shut, arms-strapped-to-his-sides bondage regalia, was a bit much. The bed itself was excellent, as one would expect at this level.
Wi-fi service was strong but unnecessarily complicated to access. Perhaps because we were attending a conference at the hotel, we received wireless access codes that allowed us premium speed access, at least in theory. My mobile devices (iPod touch, Nook Tablet) were difficult to connect to the premium service, however. In fact, it was only after a call to tech support that I understood the system and connnected my iPod. My Nook never made it to the premium level and staggered along at ---k with intermittent interruptions in service. (I consider myself a fairly sophisticated user, a bit of a geek in fact. My wife, who is not, would have had considerably greater difficulty in navigating the system.) 
The restaurant was closed for remodeling with the full menu being served in the bar. The incessantly loud music from the bar area, at all times of day, made me keep my distance. The music was equally loud in the lobby elevator area, though the fifth floor hallways were whisper quiet.
About the service: the folks at the concierge were bright, cheerful, knowledgeable and helpful. Our request for sugggestions for a Mediterranean restaurant gave us two within walking distance and the one we chose (Armenian) was very good and very reasonably priced (helpful when traveling on a government per diem). The baggage check for those who need to spend a few hours in town after checking out is very convenient and, again, operated by very friendly and helpful folks. If the Hard Rock has gotten anything right, it's staffing.
One more niggle: I don't like to see unrepaired water damage in a hotel bath, particularly damage that appears to have existed for some period of time. It makes me wonder what there may be that I'm not seeing. Yet, there it was.

A fabulous hotel in a great location if you prefer to be closer to the city rather than fisherman's wharf. Right opposite the shopping mall and next to the Powell Street Cable car terminal turntable. Public transport is great, I recommend the All day pass giving you unlimited use of bus-tram-cable car.
We were on the --nd floor and some evidence of city noise. Earplugs supplied :)
Can't recommend Alcatraz tour highly enough, DON'T miss it!
