I have stayed at Hyatt Hotels all over the United States. The Park Hyatt in Washington D.C. and the Grand Hyatt Kauai, Hawaii are probably the best the chain has to offer, however Hyatt has some pretty shabby hotels including the Hyatt Regency Miami, Hyatt Regency Atlanta Downtown, and the Grand Hyatt New York takes the cake, I don't even know how this hotel could be in the Hyatt chain. The lobby is out of the --s, with it's marble and mirrors, guest rooms are the absolute pits, rooms are dated and have a drab, dirty feel to them, most rooms have a queen or king size bed, but don't expect much bathroom space, you can't even turn around in the bathroom. I had a problem with mold and mildew in my shower, so I complained and received a credit on my bill. I would have rather had a clean room that didn't require flip flops to be worn in the shower and around the carpet, but since I was there only a few days I didn't make a fuss. I must say that in a city like New York, I would think that Hyatt would want to represent itself better than this, they should consider getting rid of this hotel. I got a significantly discounted rate of around $--- a night on priceline, normally that room sold for $---. I pity the person who spends $---+ a night on this dump.

Stay was OK. Untill woke up in morning to drive to airport. My SUV rental was broken into along with two others and all items stolen out of them. Front desk was no help to call police, had to do it myself. Police were no help, had to file a police report online, WOW. Frank in Management said there is nothing they could do about it and just the way it is now there. Terrible experience and I am sure glad I do not live in San Jose or CA for that matter. Also I believe pets were allowed, but I do not see that as a good thing.

Liked the hotel very much. The location couldn't be better, only a few blocks away from Times Square. The room was quite small even though it was a Superior Room but you have other things to do in NY than to stay in your room so it didn't bother us. The room was very clean anf had nice furniture and textils. The breakfast was okay, some cereal, bagels, juice and tea.

The hotel’s design is interesting in that there’s a roadway separating the east and west towers, which are connected by an enclosed breezeway over the road and a corridor beneath the road. As I checked in I asked if any of the upgrades which had been offered had in fact come through (a strange system poorly explained by the reservations person with whom I spoke when booking); the checklist of those possibilities for which I opted got somewhat mystified looks when I presented it. Nevertheless, I was offered a ‘room with a view’ for a $---night upgrade, and the view I got was superlative: from my west tower --th floor room I looked out along the Chicago River to the Navy Pier and the lake. I’ve never had a more impressive a downtown hotel scenic view.
 The room, on the other hand, was odd. Upon entering, the bathroom was on the right, a closet on the left; inside the closet was a small safe (big enough for a small camera bag) and a three-drawer piece of furniture about night-table sized. Continuing in, the king bed faced me, with a night table on either side, and immediately to my right was the cabinet which once housed the mini-fridge (now just an empty shell), with a flat screen TV on top. A small oddly shaped chair, low-backed, definitely not designed for comfortable lounging or reading, was in the corner beside the cabinet. Behind the bed, between it and the window, was the desk, facing the door Thus, whether one was sitting at the desk or sitting in bed, the magnificent view was behind you! The bathroom was comfortably sized, but the sink had essentially no room to set out personal toiletries (my toiletry bag just fit on the right hand side). With the extremely limited sink space and equally limited drawers for clothing, I cannot imagine a couple being comfortable in this room for more than a quick overnight stay. Done correctly, the king bed would have been on the wall to the right as you enter, with the desk on the other wall or, better, facing the window; the complete refusal to acknowledge the spectacular view is incomprehensible. I overheard comments from others in my tower that made it obvious these design flaws were not unique to my room, though my friend’s room in the east tower was far more ‘standard’ in its layout and furnishings (e.g., two chairs, bed facing the window, drawers where the mini-fridge once lurked, decent sink counter size). In summary – just be aware of the differences in room designs (east vs west towers?).
 I did not eat at the hotel restaurants, so I cannot comment on their quality, but they were typically big-name downtown hotel pricey; the breakfast buffet, for instance, was $-- (just a half block down from the hotel, in the same complex, Houlihans offered virtually the same buffet w-o the atmosphere for $--). In the maze of corridors beneath the hotel, in addition to Houlihans, there are numerous coffee and sandwich shops – but almost everything closes at -PM weekdays and on the weekend (thank goodness for a Dunkin Donuts along that winding trail which stayed open!). If you’re desperate for a sandwich, beverage or munchie, there’s Bockwinkels grocery store a block away, open every day until midnight. And as noted in other reviews, the hotel has no pool, only a small gym.
 My comments notwithstanding, I really like this hotel (I’ve stayed there on three previous occasions). The staff – front desk, bellmen, housekeeping, all – were friendly and courteous (and I was attending a large convention, so they had a lot to contend with). Some rooms are oddly laid out, and dining might be problematic, but fronting on the Chicago River and with Michigan Avenue and the ‘Magnificent Mile’ a very short walk away, the hotel is a great place for a scenic Chicago stay.

We booked -- rooms for a girls soccer team - -- year olds! Group total was -- individuals. Staff was very friendly and accommodating. Breakfast staff was helpful and opened early to accommodate our schedule. Great value for a large group.

My partner and I stayed at Eastgate Tower for our second week in of a two week holiday in New York City.
It was our first visit to the amazing Big Apple and we booked accommodation in New Jersey for one week and the second week in Manhattan. The stay in NJ was a good location and price, it was a six minute ferry trip from Lincoln Marina across the Hudson and only $--- per night. 
But the Eastgate Tower was impressive and overall better value. The tariff of about $--- per night was very competitive for NYC and was located not far from Grand Central, about a --min walk.
If you want to spend more time sight seeing and less time travelling and not blow the whole budget on an absolute centre of town hotel you should be pleased with Eastgate Towers. We took a day trip to Niagara Falls one day and needed to be picked up at -:--am - no problem with this location. The bus only picked up from mid town hotels so it picked us up and dropped us off from the front of the hotel. 
My partner smokes so she was happy that Eastgate Tower could accommodate her. We were able to check out late and store our bags with the friendly staff while we spent our last day doing some last minute shopping.
One highlight of the stay was the friendly and helpful staff. Plus the room was large and clean.
We booked our holiday from Sydney Australia over the internet, so we were a bit anxious about what to expect. We needn't have been. 
Time is precious with so much to experience in NYC, so I would be happy to stay there again.

My family and I stayed here for the color run in July and are very weary when it comes to staying in hotels but this hotel was wonderful. Though the room set up is a little weird its nothing that can't be over looked, and if you read the history of the building it will make more sense. If anything the way the rooms are set up give character to an otherwise square uniform hotel room. The room was very clean and since we were running in the morning they allowed us a late check out without any problems and stocked our room with extra towels as we needed them for all the crazy color from the run. Overall this was a very pleasant,friendly,and enjoyable stay. We will be back next year!

I stay in Marriott family hotels often - and one of my biggest pet-peeves is the inconsistency of hotels being updated. This Fairfield is not updated and feels dirty.
What I always love about Fairfield is the free breakfast, free wi-fi, and limited snack offering.
I was updated to a suite - which includes a couch, -nd TV, Microwave, and refrig - all of which I did not need. A more up to date environment would have been better.
This trip was for business at the convention center - I was less interested in the tourist aspect.

I was amazed by the extra effort that went into accomodating the marathon runners! Not only were the runners catered to and spoiled, but every customer got the same priviledged treatment.
Brown bag breakfasts, waffle irons, hot meal, varied options...... Simply amazing! And the coffee is fresh ----!
Thanks so much for a very satisfying stay!

From the looks of the hotel it seems OK. Lots of history. I love old buildings and thought this might be interesting. When we got inside to check in the fellow behind the desk was not really friendly. Just gave us our key and away we went up the STAIRS. - story building but I was lucky my husband could carry the bags to the room on the first floor. There was a very old elevator from years ago that is not used now. Once in the room at first glance it looks OK. We had a king bed. It was fairly comfortable. The closet was only about - foot wide but was enough for hanging clothes. It could not hold the luggage. There was a fridge and portable heater if it got cold. The curtains and bedspread are old so we took the bedspread off the bed and put it in the drawer. The skirt around the bottom of the bed was ripped and needed to be thrown out. The towles in the bathroom were old and small. They did supply the regular shampoo and soap. The tub was the original and had been resurfaced. The water pressure in the shower was fine. Very small bathroom but it worked. There was no electrical outlet in it. Back into the main part of the room I think there was only - electrical outlets total. One had a power cord and had the fridge and other things plugged into it. We plugged our laptop into it but had to be careful not to trip over the cord. The table you are suppose to put the laptop on was on the other side of the room and the cord did not reach. Actually the table was so close to the bed you could not put a chair at the table anyway. Oh yeah, did I mention there was not a chair anyway. There is no phone in the room. The only place to sit was on the bed. 
We used the place just to sleep anyway. We would walk up Melrose to Western and go right to Hollywood in about -- minutes. The area is very seedy but Very convenient. Since we found there were really no decent places to eat near the hotel we ate before returning to the hotel. 
It is not a place I would like to have a toddler crawling around on the carpets. Checkout was the same as checkin. No thank you given.
I think if we paid an extra $--.-- a night something else might have been better

Overall, my three-night stay at The Avenue Hotel Crowne Plaza was quite good, with no major complaints about the things that were most important to me. There were numerous quirky things though. I might call it the good, the bad and the weird.
THE GOOD
The location, just barely off North Michigan Avenue is in the real heart of things, especially for anyone visiting on leisure. Tons of great restaurants and shopping is all in walking distance. Other attractions and destinations are a longer but nice walk in pleasant weather, a short inexpensive cab ride way or accessibly by subway, the nearest station being just five short blocks away from the hotel.
I wouldn't call the room spacious, but it's not cramped either. There's adequate room for two. The firm beds with pillow-top mattresses and very comfy linens provide a great night's sleep. Having a window that opens enough to allow a decent amount of fresh air in is also a great feature of the room.
Giant kudos to this hotel for having free wireless Internet. Not only that, but the quality and connection is solid and doesn't even require having to continually sign on an agree to terms each day. I didn't have a single hiccup with it during my entire stay, which is a rarity for free or pay Internet access.
The minibar is not only appropriately stocked with useful-common-popular items (instead of some of the strange things that some hotels offer), but the pricing on it is very fair.
Housekeeping was prompt, thorough and very courteous.
The staff was generally very helpful with requests and directions.
THE BAD
My one major complaint was the heating-air-conditioning unit, which was controlled by an electronic thermostat, but curiously located on a side interior wall, though it looked like a wall unit that would typically face outside. (Note that it was set at -- when I arrived and it quickly became too cold, and I'm not a person who usually minds cooler air). Regardless of the setting, it seemed that the fan wanted to run nonstop. The temperatures during my September stay were moderate with cool nights and I felt like Goldilocks, because it seemed that it would either make the room too cold or too hot, but never just right. Turning the thermostat setting up just one degree, to -- or -- would cause it to start firing heat, which was completely unnecessary. Before the first night, I quickly learned that turning it off completely and opening the window for a while during the daytime made it perfect, not to mention quieter. I If this were brought to management's attention, they would probably say they would address it, but really, I think it's just a matter of the way the system is and not that it's malfunctioning. 'd be willing to bet that in hotter or colder months, the unit would do it's job better.
Speaking of air-conditioning, even on chilly nights, the central air in the hallway was blasting cold air at full throttle from the vents in front of the elevators.
Speaking of elevators, as others have pointed out, there's only three servicing -- floors of rooms plus the lobby and two other floors. For the most part, it wasn't a big problem, but if you happen to catch an elevator rush hour when several people are checking in or a lot of people attending a convention are returning to their rooms at about the same time, it can get rather interesting with long waits from the room floors and a line in the lobby.
THE SORT-OF BAD
Soundproofing wasn't a strong point. Thankfully, I couldn't hear anything from my neighbors' rooms sans one toilet that flushed at least once every half hour all day and all night, but even on the high floors with the windows closed, the windows don't keep out the sounds of frequent sirens, horns and some other street noise. It didn't bother me in the least, but some light sleepers may be annoyed,
While there was a newer desk lamp, newer duvets and and a newer flat screen television, most of the furniture was older including two lamps and the desk. I don't mind the mix of eras, but the desk, which was nice and large to work on, creaked when it got a little push. A new desk with some desk level electrical outlets would be a welcome addition.
The bellman was plenty polite, but I have no idea why he offered to get me a cab every time I came down. Even when I asked for DIRECTIONS to a restaurant that was barely a -- minute walk away (on a beautiful night, I might add), his response was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""It's about a $- cab ride. I'll get you a cab."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I had to ask again, specifying and stressing that I was walking. Do the bellmen get a kickback from cabdrivers or what?
THE WEIRD
The cab-happy bellman could certainly fit into this category too. All of the front desk-guest services staff (it seems to be all one in lobby) were plenty nice and professional. Some were quick and confident in giving fairly simple directions and others had to pull out maps and-or ask someone (which sometimes led to asking someone else). They weren't beyond suggesting cabs either. When it came to accommodating a special request there were some inconsistencies -- one attendant gave an apologetic """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" without any checking while another was pleasant and more than happy to accommodate.
The indoor pool and (outdoor) sundeck on the top floor seems like one of the hotel's treasures, and a secret treasure at that. The front desk staff never brought it up at check-in. On day - of my stay, I noticed it conservatively listed next to the --th floor button on the elevator and checked it out.
Another secret treasure is the breakfast (additional charge) available on the top floor, with a great view. Again, the front desk staff never mentioned it, but I noticed a very small sign for it somewhere in the hotel.
The biggest unanswered question: Why are all glasses and cups stored at the furthest possible point from the sink? Seriously, both glasses and coffee cups were on a little table by the window at the far corner. They're almost hidden. Something should be rethought here.
I've heard of water-saving shower-heads, but the fancy one in this room must hold the record -- at least for the minimal amount of water it puts out. I'm not sure that having to shower for twice as long ultimately saves anything. Personally, I'm of the opinion that they should save a little on energy with the nonstop AC and spend a little more on water. The fancy rod for the shower curtain, which curves out beyond the bathtub, requires users to really be sure to create good seal with the inner curtain. Amazingly, that meager amount of water can still flood the bathroom floor with the way the curtain is set up.
I would have never guessed that I would ever notice that a room has too much artwork, but this one does. The room is still quite pleasant, but five wall-hangings in the modest size room is a bit much. Three of them are stunning black-and-white nicely framed large photos of the Chicago skyline and various Chicago landmarks. One of the three is partially masked by an old lamp that sits in front of it (photo provided). The two that seem out of place are panoramic color photos of the Chicago skyline that hang at a high level above each of two beds, above the already high good-looking headboards of the beds. Even more odd is that the two pictures are exactly identical. Someone astonishing is that in my room one of them was not centered with the bed -- and it was off by a sizable amount (picture provided).

My husband and I stayed for - nights based on tripadvisors ratings. We required somewhere central but not too expensive which is quite difficult in New York. We used Hotels .com to book our room which was requested - weeks before our visit. We were gauranteed a full refund up to three days before our visit with no questions asked.We decided also to drive to New York and park the car, so we understood where the parking was beforehand and downloaded into the satnav. We found the hotel and car park (directly opposite in the Natural History museum) without getting lost albeit a few impatient taxi drivers hooting us for going too slow. Hotel has a deal for half price parking and you can access your car at all times. New York is an OK place to drive in town and much better than Rome or Thesalonika.
Arrived at the hotel for check in , the staff didnt crack a smile but the room was small but adequate andt clean, some things like the clock and desk light didnt work. Could have done with a higher floor as requested but got the fifth which meant a view of somebody`s scruffy back yard.
Curtains didnt close and were decorative only. Nobody explained blinds were in the casemeant. Please look for the chains. No tea making facilities in the room not good for us British.
For the money value could be improved by having tea making facilities and breakfast thrown in which is extra to the room charge.
The doorman was very helpful with directions.
Location to downtown was not walkable but subway nearby and central park within half a mile.
Breakfast was good self serve and not the usual twenty questions with anything here in the US.
IMPORTANT INFO FOR ALL READERS.....Not a bed bug in site.

My stay was much better than I expected based on the reviews here. The room layout was efficient, with good closet and drawer space. Everything was clean and bright. The window blackout shades worked well and I did not hear any street noise even though my window was open. The staff was helpful, and immediately responded to my request to open the room safe, left locked by the previous occupant. The beds were very comfortable. I had no problem with the elevator wait, or the color of the grey hallways, which were modern and clean. And, of course, the location was absolutely perfect. I highly recommend this hotel.

We stayed at Mokara Hotel in San Antonio for - days due to a conference. From the first moment, we were impressed by the hotel, its ammenities and its service. Whereas most of our colleagues stayed in nearby ----+ room hotels (such as grand hyatt and marriott) and were disappointed by both their size and their price-performance, we were extremely happy to stay in the much smaller and more luxurious Mokara. On top, many small things made a difference: e.g. in a city where (for us, as Europeans) it turned out to be hard to find good coffee and daily fresh fruit, we were both happy and envied to daily receive as complementary 'refills' for the nespresso coffee machine in our large and perfectly equipped room and fresh organic fruit - as much as we wanted! Other things not withstanding, the Mokara and its friendly, efficient, and discrete staff contributed enormously to our happy and successfull week in San Antonio. We thus recommend it to everyone without any reservation. Best regards from Switzerland.

Because of our flight time we arrived at LaQuinta around noon -- though official check-in time is - PM. We expected to drop our bags, go to lunch, then come back to check in later. Instead, the desk clerk was most welcoming and, since a room was available, said she would be delighted to check us in right away. 
We'll definitely stay again when we return to Jacksonville.

The room was great and just what I expected - clean and with a great view. 
The front desk provided less that usual Kimpton service. No one on the door, had to ask about valet parking, a seemingly disinterested desk person - poor social skills - not what I've come to expect at Kimpton.

We were in Chicago for the Chicago Marathon. We initially had a reservation closer to the start but it was over $--- more a night and at least $-- a day for parking. So I changed our reservation to the Chicago South Loop Hotel. We were pleasantly surprised! This hotel is an excellent value for the price. Front desk staff was very friendly. The room was larger than average, clean and quiet. Did I mention that parking was also free?? The only down side is that its - miles away from all the action but a cab was very easy to get. Overall a very good experience!

For those frequent business travelers who want to be acknowledged and receive fast checkin service and friendly but """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""we'll leave you be"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" service, this is a great hotel! Always a crowd in the lobby bar having fun.

We stay at Kimpton Hotels whenever possible and this one is a great example. It is very chic and urban. The location is great, walk to everything- The rooms were very comfortable. The staff are remarkable, you feel like one of the regulars from the minute you step in. We love the wine hour and the morning coffee. We will recommend to our friends and stay there again.

We found that the Luxe Hotel was conveniently located, quiet and very comfortable. The atmosphere is cosy, despite being located just off the highway in a major city. The service, especially at the pool and restaurant, was very good. The rooms were clean and spacious, and the decor was inviting. The gym, albeit too small, was kept clean and in good condition, and the pool area was lovely. I was thrilled to be able to get a rate of under $----night, although the rates seem to change daily. The management was very responsive to my post-trip review, which was very impressive. Overall, this was a great experience and we intend to return.

The big decision - Fishermans Wharf or Union Square - We choose Union Square and happy I did. First, the location is central to everything and the Inn was fantastic. The rooms were small but elegant (all windows face a brick wall though), There is a continental breakfast each morning and a wine-cheese reception each afternoon (-:----:--), the staff is knowledgable, helpful and San Francisco is a great city. Try to book shuttles to-from the Airport, taxis are expensive. Be sure to book in advance and early morning trip to Alcatraz, buy a munipass for unlimited cable, trolley and bus service since there are lots of hills in town, go to fishermans wharf: see the sea lions at pier --, eat Ghiardellis ice cream at Ghiardellis Sq, take the #-- bus to Haight-Ashbury and on to the Pacific Ocean, Check out the Golden Gate Bridge, Chinatown and on. Coming from NY, the thing that struck me as most odd was the large number of street people millling about. They really didn't present a threat, just noticable.

We live in the suburbs of Philadelphia and have a getaway every January to celebrate our anniversary and as a Christmas present to ourselves. Usually we book at the Downtown Marriott, but since they were sold out, we chose the Courtyard.
There's nothing negative to say about this hotel. We booked using our Marriott Rewards points and were given a very comfortable, quiet and clean room with a nice view of the city. The staff were pleasant and accommodating. I would recommend this hotel to anyone coming to Philadelphia.

My husband and I stayed here for three nights on our honeymoon in January. As soon as we arrived the guy on reception gave us a really warm welcome, congratulated us, and gave us an upgrade - a really great start! 
We stayed in one of the ground floor rooms looking out onto the courtyard. In January, this meant that it was super quiet, as many of the other rooms look out onto the road (-th avenue gets a bit lively as it's right opposite the Verizon Centre). The room was huge with a king size bed, desk and cosy armchair. The bathroom was also very spacious, with Aveda toiletries. We also loved the quirky leopard print dressing gowns in the wardrobe! 
Shortly after checking in, we were presented with a complementary bottle of sparkling wine and snacks, as a gift from the hotel - a really lovely touch! 
Another great feature is the complementary wine receptions they hold from -.--ish each night - you can just turn up for a glass of wine or a beer and snacks in the lounge, which is a great way to start the evening. Make sure you're on time though - they clear all the freebies pretty promptly at six! 
We found the location really convenient - it's only about a -- minute walk from the Mall (if that), and is also perfect for some of the brilliant local restaurants (we loved Zatinya, Ping Pong and Old Ebbitt Grill in particular - ooo, also don't miss the frozen yoghurt place on -th!). We also caught the metro for a trip to Georgetown (tip - you DON'T need to take a cab as suggested by the guy on reception - just go to Foggy Bottom and it's about a -- minute walk). 
The only small thing we missed at the hotel was coffee and tea making facilities in our room - perhaps it's a British thing, but it's something I expect. We did get a coffee machine which we could also use for tea, but they charged fresh milk to our bill, which I thought was a bit stingy. 
But overall, we had a fantastic time in Washington. It's a beautiful city, and the Monaco is a great place to base yourself to see all the sights.

Hotel Monaco is an excellent hotel! Spotlessly clean, the room was beautifully decorated, well appointed, the bed was very comfortable. The service was truly excelellent. I travel frequently, and I can say with confidence that the service here is among the best, from the bellmen, to the concierge, front desk, and housekeeping; all were exceptionally helpful and friendly. The front desk staff know the area well and gave great tips for entertainment and getting around town. It was our anniversary weekend, and the staff surprised us with a complimentary bottle of champagne chilling in our room. A truly wonderful weekend, and I would highly recommend the hotel. Oh, and if you wish, you can ask for a goldfish to keep you company in your room. A quirky, fun little extra that we enjoyed.

The Mandarin Oriental was fantastic. It is perfectly located, a quick ten minute walk and we were at the national mall, almost dead center between the capital and the Lincoln memorial. The front staff was attentive and quick to respond to our needs. The happy hour in the front lounge daily was a nice touch.
My only negative comment about this hotel are the beds. They are rock hard!

Overall it was a great stay and it's in a great location not too far from downtown Austin. What made me really give them an excellent rating was the fact that my girlfriend had forgotten her $--- digital camera in the room after we had checked out and the staff was very helpful in locating it for us. They immediately gave us a call and we were able to pick it up before we had left town that day. It was a relief and great to know there are honest-ethical employees working there. They have earned my business.

The Westin is not impressive from the outside; in fact you could quite easily miss it when walking past. Inside, there’s a small, busy, unassuming foyer with escalators that take you to the large reception area. Bellhops were quick to take our luggage – it’s just a pity they weren’t so quick delivering it to our room. The main reception area is very large and not in any way a relaxing place to be. There were continual queues for reception (although in fairness this was Easter weekend) and although there were some seats, it was busy, noisy and there was no lounge area in which to relax with coffee and biscuits.
We had booked a non-smoking, club-floor room but when we entered there was an overpowering stench of cigarettes; so off to reception to queue again, where we were told that no other rooms were available. We stood firm, and were eventually given another club room on the twelfth floor.
The room was actually very nice. It was large for a city hotel (--- square feet larger than standard) and had an extremely comfortable bed. The room was also well equipped, with Apple computer, trouser press, (expensive) mini-bar, coffee making facilities, iron, ironing board and a rather nice flat screen TV. However, there were some niggles. There were two phones, one fixed and one cordless. The cordless one didn’t work and the other phone’s preset numbers for guest services didn’t work. The internet connection on the Apple did not work and no-one seemed capable of fixing it. Also, although there were five lights in the room, there was no one single place to switch them off – minor point I know, but very frustrating at times.
One of the advantages of the club room is the complimentary breakfast of which we took full advantage. The breakfast consisted of bagels, toast, cereal, fresh fruit and tea and coffee. It was very good, although yoghurt would have been nice, but unless you got there before -am, it became extremely busy. One day, I counted -- people queuing to toast bagels in the ridiculously slow toaster. I accept that this was Easter weekend, but the breakfast facilities could not cope with the number of guests.
The hotel is superbly located on --rd and -th, being close to Times Square, --nd Street and the Port Authority. However, the surrounding area is manic and not for the faint-hearted. If you want something a little more sedate, look for somewhere closer to Central Park.
Overall, we enjoyed our stay and loved our room, but probably wouldn’t stay there again. Overall, a good corporate hotel for the business traveller and a great central location, but to impersonal and busy for our tastes.

I enjoyed my stay at the Magnolia; they offer many amentities. However, I did not use most of them, lol. The garden tub was awesome, as well as the bed, and customer service. The only thing I had and issue with is the length of time it took valet to bring your car.

booked this hotel for one week in July ---- on a - and a half week trip to the USA. Arrived the first night and knew within - minutes I had made a mistake. the room was simply unclean. The shower was broken and an antique. The carpets are simply filthy. The TV remote didn't work. The area is an attraction for gangs and we noticed two unsavoury undividuals taking drugs outside the premises. I have no idea what the previous reviewers are referring to when they were reviewing this hotel, but I Left after one night. I had booked it foolishly for the week and when I asked the manager re: refunding the days I didnt stay he said not a chance. Do yourself a favour and find a hotel where you feel you are not going to be mugged or shot any minute. I was nervous from the minute I entered this establishment. AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE.

In August ---- I stayed at The Mosser hotel in San Francisco. It's a very nice hotel in a very good location on walking distance from example Union Square and the baseball stadium of the SF Giants. 
I had a double room. A little small, but very modern furniture! The serive of the hotel was also superb. So for me: a big YES!

noisy

no breakfast included, and breakfast times very restrictive
so overall it was fine for a night if you need to catch a flight, or you've arrived late in LA but I wouldn't stay there for a holiday or even a business weekend.

We had a - night stay at this hotel, and it was conveniently placed to be able to walk anywhere in New York - we never used a taxi during our whole stay and only used the subway once. You walk around the corner and you are right in the heart of Times Square and the Theatre district, loads of Restaurants around, Central Park is no more than a -- minute walk away and if you're up for a good walk, its easy and safe to walk even as far as Battery Park to see the Statue of Liberty. 
The rooms are very small and there were no Molton Brown Toiletries but that didn't spoil our stay - the bed was very comfortable with a huge TV at the end of it - there isn't much place to hang stuff so I suspect most people only stay --- nights but the room is smart clean and has a contemporary theme so all in all very nice. 
What could they do better? Free wireless would be nice! Its available but its expensive.
One tip though there is an Italian Restaurant next to the hotel you will be grabbed by the very affable gentleman who will entice you downstairs to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""authentic"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Italian its very much a tourist trap and you will be automatically charged a service charge for bread, linen and toilets of all things! They also expect a tip! So buyer beware! (the Italian Restaurant in Hotel Lobby called Serafina is excellent)

Making things short: cheap hotel, regular rooms (old, smelly -old furniture- but seemed clean), not trustworthy clerks (altered the price the second time we asked). Complimentary breakfast (nothing from another planet and lacked of fresh fruits) and internet connection (that wasn't bad).
In general, you can easily find better hotels at the same distance from downtown...so just stay in case of emergency :) (ok, ok...it's not SO bad).

We arrived at the Marriott at --am, just to ask what time we could check-in. To our pleasant surprise, the room was ready and they gave us the keys right away! We took the elevator up to the --th floor, and were stunned by the view of the harbor. *Definately* request a harbor-view room!
The room was very nice but somewhat small (we were traveling with our - small children and all of the gear that goes along with that). For dinner, we ordered room service, and it was pretty fast and tasted OK, but was very expensive (as usual). The pool was warm enough for the kids, and they had fun splashing around. The exercise room looked very well-equipped, but we didn't use it.
The walk to the Inner Harbor shops and Aquarium was extremely convenient, even with - little kids. 
Value: we got a great rate ($---) plus $-- to park, so I think it was a steal. If we had paid the rack rate of $---+, I might not have been as thrilled! If you can get a good deal on a room, I'd definately recommend this hotel.

I have always enjoyed staying at the sheraton even when it was the Wyndham. This past weekend we were in town for the Yankees game. I gave my valet ticket to the person running the desk and he very rudely told me I had to wait -- minutes for my vehicle. After enquring about the guy I was shocked to learn that he was the parking manager. I do not think I will ever stay at this hotel again.

Terrible hotel. Very poor lobby, missing ceiling tiles in the hall, dirty wallpaper, floors felt uneven at best (in the halls). 
Rooms where clean. I was traveling late and there was no bar or even a gas station close or safe. So very disappointing. Even better staff smelled like Mary Jane...
We stayed here for - nights on business. Comfortable beds, nice linens. Nice pool and hot tub area!

Not only is the hotel still under construction, but there are construction projects to the left, right and front of the hotel. Then behind it is a noisy backyard of tenement buildings, complete with clotheslines and hanging dirty mops. Construction workers start yammering and banging outside at - am.

We were visiting NYC in may ---- with family . We had a family reunion in NYC . We chose this hotel because of the location and the kids wanted a swimming pool in the hotel .
The room had excellent views of the ground zero and Hudson river. Plus it's close proximity to century -- was also an added bonus ;-) did not had to carry those shopping bags for long distances . 
Did not had any meals so cannot comment on it but otherwise it was an excellent experience .

I know this is primarily a business hotel, but if you're traveling to Dallas with a family or a big group of friends, this place is perfect. I had -- family members come in for the Thanksgiving holiday and I booked - suites at the Magnolia. It couldn't have worked out better. The suites were HUGE - all had a living area with a pull-out sofa and a full kitchen complete with a full-size refrigerator, washing machine, oven, microwave, dishes the whole shebang. The Magnolia is smack dab in the middle of downtown in walking distance to Neimans, multiple restaurants and DART (Dallas' train-subway system) so you don't really need a car. Plus there's a free shuttle that will take you anywhere downtown. The absolute best feature was the second floor. It was basically a large living room with couches, tables and sitting areas everywhere. It also had a stunning fireplace and a billiards room with flat screen tv perfect for ordering pizza and playing pool. Like the rest of the hotel is was nicely decorated in a hip but comfortable modern style. Aside from the slow service at the bar (which is only open from -pm to --:--pm) the staff was incredibly helpful. Free breakfast in the morning, snacks and drinks in the evening, and cookies and milk at night were also a nice touch. The only drawback was the lack of an on-site restaurant and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""real"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" bar. (The upscale Adolphus next store or the down-home City Tavern around the corner are better bets.) Plus, room service stops at --:--pm which didn't work out too well for late-arriving guest. But overall it was a great hotel experience. I'm assuming rates can get high during the week. Since this was a holiday weekend (and not very crowded at the hotel) I found a $--- rate for the suite which has to be the absolute best deal in town.

This historic hotel is beautiful. The stay was great, and I only have a couple of issues. The rooms can be noisy: it sounds like the neighbors are in the room with you. The biggest issue we had was housekeeping. They are relentless about getting in your room! If you happen to be in your room when they are cleaning, they come back three or four times.

We originally booked our motel room with a competitor located two hotels down, online. We arrived at the hotel that we had booked online and were thoroughly disappointed. It had been completely misrepresented. We had noticed the Microtel on our way to our hotel, so we took a chance and dropped in to see if we could get a room. The host was outstanding,he took us and showed us a room (suite) so that we might make our decision to move based on an actual visual inspection. He then held the room long enough for us to get out of the awful hotel we were in. The room we then booked with the Microtel was clean and in good repair, the pool is small but clean and well maintained, the service was outstanding and the staff was extremely friendly and helpful. This hotel is a little ways from the Riverwalk, etc. but it was only a - minute drive and about half the price. I would definitely recommend this based on our experience with this business. We would stay there again with no reservations of any kind.

The hotel sits on Mission Bay and some rooms have a nice view of the bay. My husband, me and the kids spent a weekend there this month. The pool area is really nice and there are water slides for the kids. Sadly you need to get up and save your seats by about -:--am or you won't get any. We saw people walking around all day each day we were there trying to gets seats but could not. The food and drinks at the pool are way over priced and the cocktails are made very weak. You have a very limited choice for food as well. You can eat at the one restaurant for breakfast, lunch or dinner, but it is very expensive as is the room service. There is one small bagel shop, but get there early as they close at --:--pm and run out of bagels and other items early. The grounds are pretty and the staff was friendly. Our room on the other hand was a disappointment. For $---.-- a night the room was very small, with old out dated furniture with very few decorations. There was only one picture on the wall and one mirror in the entire room. The mattress was very old, you could feel the springs in it and we woke up with sore backs and necks. The bathroom wasn't much better, with a out dated shower and shower head. We expected much more for our money and a Hyatt Regency. The patio furniture was also very dirty and in poor condition. They really need to do a remodel at this hotel. It is very close to the beach and other tourist spots, but not worth the money! This is definitely not a four star hotel.

I loved the location and the hotel. The service was terrific. The only thing I did not like too much was the food at the main restaurant. I would definitely recommend this resort if you are in Austin.

We stayed for three nights in a king room on the --th floor and had privileges for the executive lounge. Overall the room was very nice and clean, the service people were very good, the bed was comfortable and the hotel was in a perfect location for attending a convention. 
Pros - 
 - Attached to convention center by skywalk
 - Room was very clean.
 - Shower head was good height for tall people, water pressure was OK, temp control was good. 
 - Staff was responsive and seemed to care (I saw an employee go out of his way to pick up a tiny piece of paper on the floor)
 - Executive lounge was included with my rate and had a nice view, good wifi, two mac computers for use, continental breakfast and reception at night (Tip: Breakfast was good enough for starting my day, but don't expect the evening reception to be your dinner.)
 - Easy in-out privileges with card key at self park garage for $-- per night (Tip: We went to the self park garage first, took a ticket and then went to check in, the desk then turned on my room key card to get in and out of garage)
 - Pool was an excellent place to take a couple laps and have a great view of the city. 
Cons:
 - Wifi in room was VERY spotty Executive level provides free wifi, so not a big deal for me. I walked to the sitting area just outside our room and had slightly better access. Executive lounge or hotel lobby have the best. (Tip: Consider what you need it for, before you pay)
 - Minor Con is we had a hard time figuring out the temperature control for the room. Seemed obvious, but didn't do what I wanted.
Did not have a chance to eat at any of the restaurants or use the spa or gym.
Had a great stay, great staff, hotel was still in remodel process but couldn't tell. Will stay here on future visits.

Stayed - nights, mid-week, on a quick getaway. Hotel staff friendly and helpful (let us check out - rooms and pick; had a bit of trouble with wi-fi connection, tech there in - min to fix). King room was comfy and clean, if a bit small (hey, its an old, historic hotel in a city!). Great location - - block from Gov Ctr """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""T"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sta and - blocks from State St sta. Easy walk to Aquarium, Quincy Mkt, & Boston Common to name a few. Hotel has JFK history and is on Freedom Trail. Lots of places with good food in the area - no need to spend $$$ in the hotel. Last Hurrah in the lobby is a great place to relax after a long day of sighseeing. Deals can be had on room rates. Free wireless in lobby, not room, unless you are a member of Omni Select (free & IMHO, worth it). Would definitely recommend and stay again.

Traveled for a business conference last week. Really nice property. Really high marks for service all around. Food and beverage options are definitely top end in terms of quality and variety. Rooms were very nice. Views are fairly impressive. just know that the area appears to be in the midst of growth, development, and or construction..I'll leave it at that. The layout of the hotel takes a little getting used to, but once you figure the grounds out....it sort of comes together nicely. Really impressed with hotel. Would consider holding a conference here. And the Spa received rave revies. The workout facilities...ummm...not so much. But most of your true road warriors are going to do what we did...take advantage of the weather and views...and run outside.

I arrived at Hotel Eventi to do a tour of their meetings rooms with the Catering Sales Manager Darian. He provided me a lovely tour. This hotel has only been opened for - years so everything still looks new and well maintained. The hotel looks very stylish, modern, and chic. I was pleasantly surprised by the beautiful decors and thoughtful layouts of the meeting rooms. It's definitely a great place to hold social and business events. I've been on a few tours for the last couple of months in NYC hotels and this has become my favorite. It's really a gorgeous property! The service was very friendly and accommodating.

Recently returned from Our Nation's Capitol in record heat (---) and stayed at this hotel, located across the street from a Hyatt near the Capitol. When I arrived at --, the lobby was packed with guests and their luggage and there was a line to check in. The girl at the front desk was very nice and told me about the free yoga (which I'd already read about) offered on the rooftop every morning at -:-- A.M. My sister found this hotel for a work trip and the nightly rate ($---) was much cheaper than most in D.C. The lobby is funky, urban chic with black and white portraits, bubble-like ceiling and droning techno music. Since my son and I were starving upon arrival, we headed to Art and Soul, the restaurant inside the hotel, for lunch. Apparently, this chef celeb was Oprah's former chef and his specialties are Southern Comfort Food with a twist. We had a very nice, although expensive, lunch there. A cheaper alternative, with fresh,healthy food is the West Wing Cafe across the street. At any rate, while my son went exploring with a friend, I visited the Postal Museum (Smithsonian) down the street, which was free. The hotel is located convieniently near the Capitol and Washington Monument and the red double decker off and on bus, stops there for pick-up. Our room was very nice, overlooking the street (preferred view), although I would have preferred the view of the Capitol instead. The rooms were recently redesigned, with tile that looks like wood and modern touches. The beds were very comfortable and you got a pillow menu, with different choices, you could order for your bed. I got the magnetic. There was a bath, hairdryer, coffee maker and safe in the room, although no fridge. Fiji water (at $- a pop) is available. The first night it was kind of noisy with sirens etc... outside our window, but the next two nights were fine. I had breakfast at Art and Soul ($-- egg white omlette) and then got a ticket for the sightseeing bus, while """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""the kid"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" slept. I found all the staff to be very friendly and accomodating. The yoga was a perfect way to start the day and we ended up on the roof our last night for drinks, which was fun (although they had no Pinot Grigio, my poison of choice). The exercise room is small (- treadmills, one elliptical and free weights) but has TV's and water. Overall, I would highly recommend this hotel, with the caveat you eat and drink elsewhere if you are trying to save $$$. Having said that, my dish- the skate with beurre blanc sauce, asparagus and almonds- at Art and Soul was my best meal of the trip.

We decided to stay overnight at the Sheraton homecoming weekend. The staff were all very helpful and the breakfast provided in the morning was very good. I would definitely recommwnd this hotel to anyone visiting Penn. Very convenient location. Close to everything.

It's close to the buslines for access anywhere in the city, within walking distance to Ghiradelli Square and Fisherman's Wharf. It's a busy hotel so expect breakfast to be full and the staff at the front desk sometimes have people waiting for a while. Mostly everyone was really helpful and polite. While we were there the morning people were much nicer than the evening people.

I booked this hotel via Marriott.com as a long-time Marriott rewards member usually staying --+ nights a year in Marriott properties. The pictures, amenities, and location on the website looked reasonable for the $---+ I paid. However, when I opened the door to the room, I was quite disappointed. I guess I'm looking for too much for $--- close to the Denver airport.
The hotel is very dated and the rooms are in need of serious update. The room was good sized with a king bed, but had old carpet (dark, but I think it was clean) and very dated furnishings. I felt like I was stepping back into the --s (or maybe --s). Everything from the --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" CRT TV, thin-uncomfortable mattress, wall heat-aircon unit without a thermostat, and absolutely cheap soap-shampoo screamed Motel -. I really wish I had booked the Courtyard.
I would've been okay with the room if the bed linens were not so thin and the towels not so old and scratchy. I can sleep almost anywhere as long as there are good linens and nice towels. No so here.
Parking is also quite limited for a hotel of this size. It was quite full when I arrived and I had difficulty fitting my large rental SUV into one of the few, tiny spots available.
The room did have a mini-fridge and a small microwave (neither of which I used) and it is in a good location just a few miles from the airport. They also have free wireless. Otherwise, there weren't really any other positives. Okay, one other positive was the staff - they were very professional and friendly.
I'll look elsewhere when flying out of Denver in the future. I'd like to stay with a Marriott property, but won't if this is the quality to be found in the area.

We stayed at the US Grant in San Diego after some research, as high end properties were hard to come by in the city due to the fact that most hotels of that category were located well outside San Diego proper, in La Jolla or Del Mar. We didn't find the Marina too appealing either since we wanted to be as close to the action (Gaslamp Quarter or Little Italy, Hillcrest was far off anyway) as possible. So, right before flying to the USA we came across The US Grant, which had very good reviews and a very nice appearance; to my surprise, room rates were incredibly affordable, so I immediately assumed there would be a catch.
Well, I was definitely wrong: right from our arrival we found the hotel to be sensational. A ---- building with an enormous lobby, featuring beautiful carpets and ballrooms as well as a nice Christmas decoration. Check-in was speedy, although as it is often the case with big hotels I found the staff to be corteous and efficient albeit a bit cold and impersonal. Our car was properly taken care of (for US$-- a night) and we were escorted (through beautiful corridors) to our room on a high floor which, to my surprise, not only had great views over the city but had been completely renovated in a classic-chic style, with an ample bathroom (shower was not well-maintained, though), very comfy bed, a huge closet and overall modern facilities. We particularly liked a full-figure mirror at the entrance. There was complimentary bottled water as well as chocolate provided by the turndown service.
Breakfast was superb, too. It was à la carte but with plenty to choose from, and the staff was professional and attentive. A great way to start the day.
Location: unlike some reviewers, I didn't find it to be dodgy or scary. Granted there are some homeless around, as everywhere in San Diego, but it looks as if some people are scared off by the presence of poor people around. Not to mention it is perfectly located, within walking distance to all the action at the Gaslamp Quarter, adjacent to two great breweries and not-too-far from Little Italy on foot. You can also leisurely walk to Labrea Park or the Marina during daytime hours, so its location is also perfect for exploring the city's attraction. You can do no wrong with this one.
Overall, I was pleasantly surprised with the hotel and the value for money turned out to be excellent. If you want a good property outside the major chains at the Marina area or the luxurious hotels well far off San Diego, do not think twice.

You can tell a lot about a place by the smell...this place stinks. The smell of mildew and stale air makes you want to turn around. Our toilet sounded like a rocket ship. My family and I were horrified but toughed out the trip because my wife was attending a conference and someone at her work booked this place. My son got a couple of bug bites. We left vowing never to come back. 
Unfortunately, my friends booked a weekend in San Diego the following weekend and I never asked about the place. To my dismay, I was once again back at the Best Western Seven Seas. The room in the --- wing smelled so much better than the ones in the --- wings. The toilet didn't shake and nobody was bitten by bugs. Maybe the --- wing just sucks...the location of this place is great though, as it is by everything. 
If I somehow go back to hotel row again, I will not take a chance on this hotel.

I spent three nights at this hotel in early March. This is not the typical four star Kimpton property I have become used to in other cities. This is definitely a three star hotel. The hotel retains some of the nicer options that four star Kimpton properties have such as free wine happy hour every day from - to -pm and free coffee and tea every morning. The location is perfect and most attractions can be explored by foot from the hotel. Things I did not like included a small room and an even smaller bathroom. Two people cannot be in the bathroom at the same time and the door has to be closed in order to use the toilet. The building has a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""funky"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" smell that comes along with old buildings. I did not have a problem with the cleaning service but I was annoyed that the maid would refold the used towels and move them so we would not know which towel was mine and which one was my husband's. The beds are comfortable. The rooms do have ugly air conditioner units. The view from the room was an alley so I did not waste too much time admiring it. Overall, this is a decent hotel in a great neighborhood.

My family and I went to Chicago last month as our annual summer vacation. We had a pretty hectic time trying to find a place to stay, at first. There were so many hotels, and so little time! Finally, we decided to stay at the Lombard Embassy Suites, about -- minutes from Downtown Chicago. However, when we found that this hotel was right in the middle of Downtown, we switched our reservations right away. We couldn't have had a better trip. Seriously folks, this is the place to stay in Chicago. 
Everything was very clean when we stayed. The beds were nicely made and the sheets were clean and soft, which many hotels have troubles with. You could tell that the carpet had been cleaned and vaccumed. The bathroom didn't shine, but it was clean as well. You could tell that the hotel tried hard to put its best foot forward as far as cleanliness goes. The lobby and atrium were spick-and-span.
The staff was the nicest hotel staff I've ever encountered. Everyone was all smiles all the time. By the end of our --day trip the staff knew our names and always greeted us on our visits to the parking garage. The parking is convienient as well, but costly ($-- a day). 
The location was the best part of our stay, and what makes the hotel most convienient. We walked most everywhere in Chicago, and this hotel is right smack-dab in the middle of downtown, only about a block and a half away from Michigan Avenue. We felt extremely safe and comfortable walking everywhere downtown, and the hotel was easily accessed when we forgot a water bottle or were caught in the rain.
In addition, the hotel has a pool for kids. The pool is small, but is enough for --- people to play comfortably. There is also a business lounge, which was a savior for checking e-mail and Facebook. Access to the lounge and pool is free with reservations. Also, hot breakfast is served every morning, and there is something down there to suit everyone. They have cereal, fruit, coffee, milk, hashbrowns, eggs, sausage, bacon, and custom-made omelets, plus other things. Every night there's a Manager's Reception that offers free appetizers to guests (while we were there, they had fried vegetables and salsa chips). I personally did not use the fitness center, but from what I could see, it was large enough.

I stayed at this hotel for four nights. Late check in went smoothly, there was no wait, the hotel is not that big, therefore, for all the days I was there I never noticed a line at the front desk. The hotel is very conveniently located in downtown San Jose, less than a -- minute walk to the HP Pavillion, and all very accessible to public transportation. The lobby and downstairs area are all very inviting, there seems to be some kind of Moroccan theme as decor. I never had to wait more than a minute for an elevator to my room. I stayed in a room with a king bed, the bed was very comfortable, the pillows a bit too high for my taste, but this is not a big deal, since most people prefer big, high pillows anyway. This did not prevent me from sleeping. 
 The room was cleaned every day, beds made, chocolates left, and the bathrooms were freshened. My one complaint is that the base of the taps at the sink looked like they needed more thorough attention, they were starting to get that pale orange grime that shows me that they were not being cleaned properly. This can be wiped away really easily with some bathroom product. Besides that, everything was clean, I personally like to travel with clorox wipes so I can wipe everything down before I use them. The bathtub was clean, I did not like the location of the place to put the soap because I clumsily managed to bump my elbow into it, ouch! Towels were replaced daily, I like to bring my own towel, so I did not have to use the hotel's. Robes were also available, but I did not use them. The mini TV in the bathroom is a nice touch. 
The hotel is right by the flight path of landing planes, I heard them sometimes, but this did not bother me at all, it really is not that loud to disturb anyone. If you are from a big city, San Jose may seem a bit sleepy to you, there was very little traffic noise, previous guests have complained about that, but I did not experience any of this and when I stayed it was a very busy weekend. I did not visit the hotel's restaurant, there are plenty of restaurants just minutes away in all directions including a Starbucks, just two blocks away. The air conditioning worked great, but I barely had to use it because most nights very cool enough. The flat screen TV was in good working order, no problems there. The hotel does provide hangers, as well as an iron, so do not worry to bring those. The ice and water on every floor is very convenient. I did not use the fridge or honor bar.
I have no opinion on the parking situation as I do not have a car.
There is no place to warm up food brought from outside, it would be nice to put a microwave oven on the pantry floor that guests can use. 
I believe there is a fee for wired internet, therefore I did not bring my laptop, I think this should be provided with the cost of the room. Overall, I was very happy with my stay and would recommend this hotel.

Our family of four has stayed here several times. We have chosen it because the location is great for the grownups--we walk to the opera, and because it has a pool for the kids and coupons for the kids to eat free at the breakfast buffet (if adults pay the regular price). However, the pool has lost its attraction because it is freezing. We asked about it and were told it's because it's unheated--the water just reflects the ambient temperature of the room. The room is on the exterior of the building and has a glass ceiling, and thus it is not particularly warm in winter. Maybe it's fine in the summer time, but don't expect it to be fun for kids in winter. The rooms are clean and generally somewhat nicer than a typical Holiday Inn and a good value for location in other respects.

I stayed here one night after flying into the Columbus airport. It is really close to the airport and I could occasionally here planes land and take off, but it was surprisingly quiet. The rooms were very clean and new, but my room showed quite a bit of wear and tear. There were a couple tiles in the bathroom that were completely loose. 
The breakfast was fully stocked but the food was very average and everything appear to be made in a factory, like the eggs.

Our wonderful experience of this hotel started at check in. We stayed here - nights in August as part of a -week tour of California from the UK. As we checked in we were informed that they were upgrading us to the Presidential Suite. The suite was amazing with - large double bedrooms, lounge, kitchen and hallway with en-suite bathrooms. The suite is decorated to a very high standard with antiques etc. We arrived on the friday evening and was pleased to discover a party on the roof top for the gay community and travellers alike. The happy hour lasted from - - --pm, we had a great evening and met some great people. The hotel is located right on the edge of the beautiful Balboa Park and within walking distance to the zoo. The city Centre is a short taxi ride away. All the hotel staff were very friendly and very helpful and we would definately stay here again.

I stayed here for - night in April to enjoy the festivities going on that weekend in Downtown Memphis. The hotel is located on the main street trolley line with easy access to Beale Street , Fedex forum and restaurants. This hotel is designed with the business traveler in mind however it is very modern, beautifully decorated and the staff was great. I had the wrap around balcony room, which was wonderful. The room was very clean.

Stayed here - nights, found the location excellent, easy walking distance to all major sites, turn left - blocks for Capitol, right - blocks for Pennsylvania Ave. Breakfast more than adequate and coffee available all day. Very spacious room we had coffee making facilities & microwave which we didn't actually use but there is a Safeway behind the hotel so you could purchase ready meals etc.. My only minor niggle was the traffic noise, we were on the -th floor but as its on a major junction there is a lot of noise at night. Staff all lovely and couldn't help enough.

We stayed at the AKA in May for our first trip to D.C. Overall, this was a very comfortable respite from our otherwise whirlwind tour of the City.
Location: The location of this hotel was great for us. It is about - --- blocks away from the White House. We got in late the first night, and walked over to the White House in about - minutes. Just amazing. It is a small walk to the nearest Metro station, but nothing too bad. There was plenty of restaurants, nightlife and sights to see within walking distance.
Hotel: The hotel itself is very modern, clean and elegant in a modern way. The staff in the lobby is very nice, though we did have one run-in with a front staff guy, no big deal. There is a roof-top terrace that we took advantage of each night to enjoy a cocktail on, great way to get away from the day's heat.
Room: The room was overall great. You could tell that the place was a little older, but a pretty-much complete remodel has left it looking very comfortable and modern. Espresso wood floors, stainless steel appliances in the full kitchen and granite countertops give a high-end feel to the room. The separate room is nicely appointed, yet simple, divided from the rest of the room by a Japanese-inspired opaque window wall. 
Again, overall a very nice place, though a bit on the pricey side, but pretty comparable for D.C.

Not used to staying in - star properties so take my review with a grain of salt. That said, the rate was good, the staff was very nice and they upgraded me to a suite which was spacious. Additional plusses, a toothbrush and razor with toothpaste was in the room...I had left mine in the previous city by accident, so this was nice. 
Weirdly, they made me sign a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no smoking"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" pledge. I say weirdly because the room was clearly very recently a smoking room and had a deep smokers aroma in it. My guess is the hotel was remodeled last in the early ----s. 
The major drawback to me was location. I stayed here to be close to downtown where I had meetings. My normal choices were all booked and featuring rates over $--- (outside company policy). While it was close to downtown, it was in a much seedier neighborhood than I had expected. Many prostitutes and other seedily clientele were observed wandering the property. 
So, on the whole I'd say stay somewhere else if you can afford it.

I'm a -- year old male student on a road trip. I was looking for a decently clean room at low cost. I don't have high standards. After ten minutes in the lobby trying to check in, my friend and I were done w the place. Crickets in the lobby bathroom. Word of the invention of the vacuum has yet to reach this place. 
I have never reviewed a place online before, but this horror movie hotel struck a chord.

Staff were friendly, very helpful, good service with a nice little restaurant and coffee place right in the lobby. Tip-suggestion - if you are doing a priceline bid for a -.- star hotel (expecting a hampton inn or a similar kind), make sure custom hotel is not listed as -.- star. The best bet is go for - star.
