We stayed -nights in that hotel. It is located closed to city center. Although it was noisy at nights (voices comes up from next room, water sound from the radiator) we slept well (because we were so tired(jat leg)
Breakfast was weak, but cannot expect -stars quality breakfast at this room fee.
So it's worth for the money.

We took or two kids for a quick weekend getaway to San Antonio. This hotel was recommended to me by a friend. I have stayed at many Hiltons across the US and some of their Homewood suites. The Home- Suites is about on par with the Homewood. Good size room, clean and somewhat affordable. However, if you are used to Hilton's across the US don't be surprised to find the amenities much lower than other their premium hotels. The breakfast buffet was very poor with heat n serve open faced egg sandwich and a small supply of breads and cereal. Since the kids went with us any pool becomes a center point for them. The pool here is a small lap pool and both times we went, there were no towels to be found other than the dirty ones in the hamper and all over the chairs. Needs to be paid more attention to. One other item of concern was the hot water, or lack of and the relatively noisy AC unit in our room. The staff is courteous and attentive when you need something and Valet was great. I doubt I will stay there again, but I have definitely stay in better and in worse.

Would highly recommend. Located just a couple blocks from Camden Yards and about a -- minute walk to the Inner Harbor. Hotel was clean. Parking was expensive though at $-- per day but for the area I guess it's on par. Common areas were very hot like the AC didn't work in there. Bar in the lobby was good and reasonable too. We got a great rate ($----nt) through the soccer tourney we were attending. I doubt that's the normal rate given the location.

I stayed in this hotel in May ---- and had a wonderful experience. We were originally given a room that while very nice, did not have a bathroom door. We spoke to the gentleman at the front desk and expressed our concerns. He recommended his favorite corner room on a higher level floor which happened to be available and only cost $--.-- per night. It had the most amazing view. The housekeeping staff did a fabulous job and went above and beyond with their meticulous cleaning. Our shoes were even arranged nightly. The doormen recommended local restaurants and were extremely friendly. The bar was small but cozy and the bartender was friendly and pleasant. We only ate at the restaurant for breakfast which was fabulous. I would highly recommend this hotel. Great location as well.

Checked in for an one night stay for the memorial weekend and a celebration for my one yr old son. Requested a baby crib but it was not placed prior to arrival. Saw the room attendant on our way out for dinner and asked for the baby crib again; room attendant did not take the initiative to call for us but urged us to call housekeeping ourselves. Since we were on our way out; we had to ask her to please call for us. =(... Came back to the hotel room; crib was alright - it was just a plain white sheet on it. Hotel room decor gives me the feeling of vegas for some reasons. When we retrieved our car to have dinner; one of the ladies was driving in and she had to get out of her car to ask the doorman if they offered valet parking. That was a bit weird since the doormen were not busy at all but just standing right next to the front doors. Found hair in the bathroom on the wall and the notepad on the desk. Really a bit disappointing....

Maybe I just haven't done enough research but Boston's Logan Airport seems terribly lacking in decent restaurants. So wife and I, returning from Boston on a recent vacation, decided to check in our big bags early, then head off for a few hours to the nearby Hyatt Harborside--there's a free MBTA shuttle bus--to sit out by the harbor and then have a pre-flight meal. The shuttle runs frequently and you can easily catch it back to your Terminal in time for takeoff.
This proved to be an excellent decision and I recommend it to other travellers to Boston.
The view out over the harbor from the hotel grounds is great, as is the view from the dining room itself. My wife pronounced her clam chowder the best she has had in Boston and my fish and chips were splendid, especially enjoyed the lemony tartar sauce accompanying. Nice selection of local beers and wife loved her dessert choice. Service was friendly and efficient. Prices most reasonable for a hotel dining room. What more to ask?

Just stayed there for the National Restaurant Show. The hotel is ok. They upgraded the rooms so they're pretty modern. But for another year my wife and I ate the breakfast buffet in the main lobby... and it is terrible! We travel for business and eat at buffets all over the country... and I think this is the worst. The staff is wonderful and they try to be accommodating but it doesn't make up for the poor quality of the ingredients nor the poor execution of the dishes.

Hotel -- went above and beyond to exceed my expectations. My sister and I were in New York celebrating her --th and birthday and we chose this hotel because its location in Times Square and because it was next door to RENT. The staff was amazing!! Everyone was so friendly and helpful. The room was perfect too!! It was a little small...but we were not in New York to just hang around inside!! It was comfortable and had an amazing view! I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone who wants to stay near Times Square or Broadway!

The rooms were as advertised, well appointed, and clean. We found ourselves in the back on the second floor with a view of a concrete wall, driveway, and railroad track so would request a higher floor. The inhouse resturant was just OK with better choices available across the mall. The hotel is close to many of the museums on the mall and tours leave from the front door. The staff was friendly, and we learned so much about our Capitol, history, and the people that helped create our great country.

The staff was wonderful and tried to be helpful. We chose this location partially for the location and things like the pool-spa. Arrived to find the pool-spa were closed for renovations. The staff comp'ed us breakfast after I asked for it as a consolation.
We were assigned the -rd floor, only floor with a suite left. Came back from night activities to find men in respirators walking around renovating
 the bathrooms. The stench was HORRIFIC. No option given by the staff like a different Marriott to accommodate us, no other suite available in building, didn't have connector or two other rooms available? 
I can't comfortable recommend the hotel to others - staff was as good as they could be the facility was not. How about staff explain these things on check in and let the guest make their own decision to stay or go elswhere

If you're sensitive to noise or smell, or you think that service is important,or you're not in San Francisco to interview the homeless, you can count on a bad time at the Metropolis. Not only does it stink of cigarettes (despite the claims that the hotel is non smoking) but if you complain you will be rudely rebuffed. Some of the highlights; loud guests loitering in hallways, with no response from front desk; broken TV, with insulting response from front desk (""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I can't be bothered with complaints in the middle of the night""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""--it was midnight, when we returned to our room); and after we sent an email to the management to complain, the owner called us, reassured us, and offered a free night in one of his OTHER hotels--coupon in the mail, which, needless to say, never arrived. Don't waste your time and money; FIND SOMEPLACE ELSE TO STAY

I booked the lodge for a friend and I after looking through a lot of places, checking out prices and reviews on this website. Chelsea Lodge had such good reviews and reasonable prices that we went for it. I was a bit nervous about the shower being in the room and the toilet down the hall, but it was absolutely fine. We had a nice method worked out where we read a magazine or watched the tv whilst the other came out of the shower! there were - toilets on our floor and we never had to wait for one. Everything was wonderfully clean and the bed was very comfy. Our window looked out of the back of the property onto the little garden and the gardens that adjoined it. The room is bedroom sized, big enough to sleep in and have our suitcases open and shopping everywhere. A chair to sit on and a little space for hanging things. also we had what looked like an old writing desk with drawers which we could use to put our clothes in and that the tv was stood on. There was a very quaint feel to the building, you could almost forget you were in New York when you were inside. We had a desk in our room that was actually a sewing table with the old sewing machine underneath! They will store your luggage for you whilst you spend your last few hours in the city and even bring it outside for you when you get back late and the taxi is there waiting for you, (ahem)!! This was my third trip to new york, and i've been lucky each time with my accommodation, but this was definitely my favourite. It was on a very quiet street, but you only had to walk a few metres to be on -th Ave, with shops, and plenty of places for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Tube stops were very near and it was greatly located to go up the city, or down. im always going to recommend this place to anyone going there, and I'd certainly stay there next time i go.

I had the pleasure of staying at the Ritz Carlton in San Francisco while visiting friends in town. The hotel is in an ideal location, close to Union Square and in a lovely neoclassical building. Rooms are tastefully done but a little bit generic and in a typical Ritz Carlton fashion. Service is first rate. The spa and fitness center are very nice and the restaurant is supposed to be one of the best in San Francisco (although I did not eat there). During my trip to San Francisco, I visited the Four Seasons and the Mandarin Oriental and think that the Ritz is by far the nicest hotel in the city. I am going back to SF with my wife in March of ---- and we are staying at the Ritz.

Can not fault the Trump, service amazing, staff attentive, rooms spacious and well kept. Walking distance to virtually everything and the Architectural boat tour starts in front of the hotel (highly recommended!)
I think Trump is perceived as being expensive but on comparison is often cheaper than the likes of the Ritz Carlton - Park Hyatt and the rooms are twice the size. Great value for money

Let me begin by saying that I was not totally disappointed with this hotel, I think my expectations were high after reading the reviews on TA before I booked. The hotel's location was great-very convenient to just about anything. I didn't find the rooms to be small, like some reviewers mentioned. We had a double on the --th floor with a great view. The room was equipped with a coffee maker and fridge and I found the beds to be comfortable, but my friend didn't. I guess I thought this hotel would be a bit fancier than it was, but it was pretty basic.....the lobby was not impressive and the rooms were also basic. I have stayed in other large cities at much nicer locations for the same price or less. The carpet in the room was a light color and there were some dirty spots on it......I just didn't get the impression that the room was exceptionally clean, but that's my opinion. As for check-in, we arrived in the city very early -am and I did not expect to get in the room that early. We left our cell numbers for the desk to call when the room was ready--we never got a call, but instead went back to the hotel around ---:--pm and were able to check in. Upon check-out we were able to do a late check-out of -pm.

We had a great experience at Staybridge suites. The room was a city view (not of Empire State though) on the --th floor with a King bed. The bed was not overly comfortable but fine. Even though we did not cook there, having the small kitchen was a nice feature. It was nice to have real dishes and glassware. There is even a dishwasher. Bathroom was a decent size. Most reviewers have mentioned the Port Authority across the street and as commented by several, it was not a problem. We used the Subway station there to get around town. A few of our favorite things were - Grayline bus tours, Empire State Build building (don't care what they say about -- Rock being as good - is still beautiful art deco - we went up at midnight and only a short line), theaters in Times Square (Rock of Ages and Memphis), Juniors for cheesecake and Carnagie deli for Pastrami sandwiches. Buy you theater tickets at the TKTS booth near the Seaport rather than Times Square as the line is much shorter. The hotel is central to all of these things. Check out the Manhattan Sky Club next door at the Marriott for a pre-theater drink. We also enjoyed the daily breakfast at the Staybridge and complimentary happy hour with beer, wine and food mid-week. We waited a little for the elevators but not much of a problem.

We spent the most relaxing and fun week-end in NYC and this Hotel had a lot to do with it.
I came with my -- year old daughter, her friend and her friend's mom for a girls' week-end! When I initially booked online with booking.com, I didn't realize that kids under -- stay for free and paid the equivalent of - adults. So I expected a big hassle to ensue since Booking.com makes it clear the reservations are non-refundable. When I called the hotel to see if they could do anything about this price discrepancy, Wendy was so accomodating, helpful, warm and friendly! She fixed my mistake and refunded the extra charges!! Once at the hotel, we were greeted like family-distinguished guests. The Staff was very warm, friendly and professional! 
The hotel is a quaint boutique hotel with nice lines and modern design. It's sophisticated yet unpretentious. It was sparkling clean (it's new), The rooms were small (but it's New York). I was surprised by how quiet it was, no sirens, traffic noises from the outside, or shouts-giggles-raucous from the inside. (We had asked for a room on top floors, away from the elevators, but I still had expected to hear some NY noises at night)
The top floor is a treat with a bar and great view of the Empire State. 
Breakfast was included - nothing to write home about, but included in the price.
The beds were sooo comfortable with crisp linens, delightful!
The bathrooms were great as well, small sized but new and a zen-like design.
Our only outrage: the minibar in the room. The fridge dispenses cans of drinks or candy-nuts. Once you have taken a can, you cannot put it back and automatically get charged. Not good when you have kids who are curious and don't read the small print!
Fortunately for us, the hotel staff again accomodated our mistake and refunded us for the unused can of m&m's for $-.
We watched the Olympics on High Def flat screen in our room, while eating take-out!
This hotel is nestled in the Fashion district but feels accessible to everything: we walked to our Broadway Show, restaurants, took the subway uptown...
We're coming back, I've never had such a great hotel for such an affordable price in NYC. This is a great value!!

I never had such inconsiderate service ever! When my room card somehow deactivated itself, I explained to the counter clerk what had happened, if she could activate it, and that I was in a rush to get to the airport. At the time, there was a line of folks checking out and she told me I would have to wait until after all the folks checking out were finished before she would help me. I knew it would take only about -- seconds and expressed again my need get to my room so I won't miss my pick up and that it wasn't my fault that the key deactivated itself, but she could care less! After quite a while when all others finished their transacations, it took her about -- seconds to activate my room card and she never apologized for the inconvenience or anything! I later wrote a complaint to the hotel regarding the situation, and they never bothered to write back so I suppose they don't care about customer service and their clerks can get away with being rude and inconsiderate. I'd rather stay at a hotel that practices and teaches their employees good discernment and compassion!

My room wasn't ready when I got there which was after - pm. I was feeling pretty yucky from all the travel and wasn't able to refresh. They said I could leave my bags there and come back later which was not at all convenient; going out without being refreshed. So the next day, they refused to extend my check out time even with this inconvenience.

My husband and I were more than satisfied with our lodging at the Balboa Park Inn (we had booked over the net). Turned out it's right across the street from the zoo and Balboa Park, so the location was great! We stayed in the jungle nook suite which was nicely decorated and perfect for comfort. Gorgeous bathroom with double shower and hot-tub. We WILL recommend it and return next time we're in San Diego. And friendly staff to boot!!!

I was ther with twenty clients. They all loved the place-decor-breakfasts,location and atmosphere. It was a first class stay. A tram stops nearby and for -- cents senior citizens can travel a very long way, It was safe enough at night to walk around.

nice midtown hotel, very close to the Empire State Building and an easy walk to several subways. Plentiful continental breakfast, and staff at reception were helpful. Room was clean and everything worked.The free wifi was dodgy in our room but worked fine downstairs. As we visited in March the upstairs bar was shut, but the downstairs bar was pleasant and has a happy hour! There is also a gym on the top floor if you don't feel you have already walked enough around NY.

My wife and I stayed at the Wellington Hotel during the new year period. Its location is perfect for any New York event. Two blocks from Central Park and a -- minute walk to Times Square. The subway connection directly beneath the hotel is very convenient to access any network of trains across the city. No vibrations either.
The room is typical of New York accomodation, being small and cosy, but truth be said, our room was always warm and comfortable, and in minus - degree temps that was a huge tick for my wife and I. 
Bathroom: shower rose over the bath tub with a curtain only was ok, water pressure was by far the best i have ever experienced. The hotel lobby looks a million bucks but the rooms dont necessarily reflect the same - decor a little dated but not a huge concern.
We paid roughly $--- per night at the hotel for a queen size bed and were very happy. At this price the hotel has two thumbs up from us and should we revisit New York would be happy to book with Wellington again. 
Wifi - came at a cost of $-- a day, otherwise Starbucks across the road - no charge.
If travel arrangements permit, try checking-in late evening as opposed to early afternoon as the hotel lobby reception tended not to cope too well with large volumes of people at once.

Just spent three nights here with my mother and my daughter (age -). It was my second stay at this hotel and I enjoyed it even more than last year. The location is wonderful. We walked to MoMA, American Girl Place, Barney's, the theatre and much more!
 The level of service is excellent and traveling with my daughter seemed to get me even BETTER service than without. Upon arrival one of the staff members gave my daughter a Lizzie Maguire DVD to watch in the room. Our first morning, on the way out the door, the doorman greeted my daughter by name! Our bellman was very grateful for his tips...everyone was fantastic!
 Our room was at the back of the hotel. We needed two double beds so we booked the lowest room category, which is the only way to GET - doubles. It was exquisite! And we still had three large windows, including one in the spacious bathroom.
 We had breakfast every morning at the hotel's restaurant, Atelier.Again, the service is unparalleled. Dinner at Atelier our last night was divine (and now prix fixe); the Master Sommelier was very kind.
 Although I love shopping and exploring downtown...I will never be able to stay anywhere but the Ritz Carlton on central Park - as long as I can afford it. It is absolutely a dream hotel! I'm hoping to take my daughter again this summer.

My husband and I went to Seattle to see a Dave Matthews show, and stayed in the Sheraton (Main Tower- King) for one night. The Hotel is in an EXCELLENT location. There is no need to rent a car. Get a round trip ticket on The Gray Line bus from the airport and you'll be able to walk or use public transportation for the rest of your trip. We were able to check in early, --:-- am. I had read other reviews saying to stay in the newer tower, however, I found the old tower very nice and updated. My only regret is that we only stayed one night!

Tiny rooms; we were told by reception staff that as we were staying for - nights, it would be best if we upgraded as rooms very small. The next size up also very, very small (smaller than out smallest bedroom at home)-hardly any room on either side of double bed(not king size-small double).
Very dark room, too. No hospitality tray for tea, coffee or water.
No mini-bar. No free wifi. No gym.
Staff generally snooty and unhelpful apart from concierge who was great. 
Took about -- minutes for luggage to be retrieved from store. """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Business Centre"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is a joke
We had - nights in the Marriott. After some trouble getting suitable rooms at check-in, the rest of our stay was fine. Rooms are a little small but staff were on the whole helpful and friendly.

The rooms were nice and we were fortunate enough to have a perfect view of Time Square. The bed was a bit too comfortable and made for late starts in the morning. I really can not say a single negative thing about the room It was large by New York standards, well furnished, had a nice sized safe, coffee maker in the room (silly but important to me), and they keep it clean. The location is perfect. You are right on Time Square, and Time Square station is just across the street. You are right in the middle of Manhattan Island so its just minutes on the subway to everything. We didn't eat at the hotel, but the restaurants looked very nice. We ate a couple times on restaurant row which is just two blocks over on --th st and at Carnegie's Deli which is just a couple block up. The hotel is on Broadway in the theater district which is handy if you want to catch a play, but the lines for the theaters reach the hotel. We didn't have a problem but it did get crowded around show times. They sell discount tickets at the hotel. The elevators throw you off the first time you use them but they actually are easy once you figure them out. The staff was extremely helpful. The -th floor check in was a little different, but there were people on the first floor to direct us where to go. I highly recommend this hotel!

Stayed at this hotel two weeks ago. Everything went well. Accommodations are great. Lost drivers license in bar. Followed up with waitress next day who indicated that she had found it and turned it into security. Waitress confronted security guard about the missing ID. Security claimed they never received it...

Great value hotel - rooms were comfortable and pleasant, staff were helpful, everything worked...most importantly it was CLEAN. Obviously not the most plush hotel around, but it is more than functional if you are not going to be spending much time there. Location is excellent, the street its located on is a bit dark and dingy but once you get out onto -th Ave you're in the middle of it all.

Stayed here for - nights, my -nd stay at this hotel.
Fast and friendly valet service, beautiful large lobby, large gift shop (souvenirs, drinks, snacks, magazine, plus everything else which you may have forgotten to pack), Starbucks in the lobby area with a nice selections of pastries and snacks (love the takeout salads too), nice pool area (the lady that works there is very friendly and hard working), large gym area, good housekeeping (my compliments to housekeeper BAN for her friendliness and helpfulness), good room service. Numerous computers and printers in the lobby area as well.
I arrived at --am and was very pleasantly surprised that I able to check in right away, a great way to start my stay. Checkout was friendly as well. Good elevator service, never had to wait long for one to arrive.
Very quiet rooms. Of course you can hear other doors closing in the hallways, but otherwise very soundproof rooms.
Walking distance to Chase Field and US Airways Centre. Close drive to Scottsdale.
This is definitely still one of my very favorite hotels, I look forward to staying here again next time I am in Phoenix.

An excellent hotel in a very convenient position. We stayed for three nights in a spacious room with two double beds for myself, husband and daughter. Following flight cancellations, my husband and I were very grateful the hotel were able to accommodate us both for a further night (my daughter managed to get a flight home) and we were given a room with a king size bed and such a large room. Everything in this hotel was spotlessly clean and nothing was too much effort or a problem for all staff who were courteous, friendly and very helpful. I have to mention the breakfast, which was included in the price. This was much better than the usual coffee, tea and toast that is usually provided. There were cereals, croissants, breads for toasting, bacon or sausage patties, scrambled eggs and you could even make your own waffles and again nothing was too much trouble for the staff who were quite happy to replenish when things ran out. Definitely a hotel I would be happy to recommend and one I will be definitely be back to.

I attended a conference at the Westin and found most of meeting rooms spacious, well lit, and ready for presenters' internet access-projection of PowerPoint presentations. My king bed was comfortable. When I arrived, the bathroom seemed to be clean (new towels, drinking glasses, etc.), but there was no new shampoo or conditioner. Instead, the half-used bottles from the previous guest were left in the shower! I'm all for reduce-reuse-recycle, but this was unexpected. A friend picking me up at the end of my stay had difficulty finding the hotel (the maining address does not match the street address of the pick up-drop off area in front of the hotel when entered into a GPS).

We arrived during the Labor Day weekend. Bay bridge closed.
We found a very helpfull and friendly staff and a hotel conveniently located. The room was clean, the size as expected. For the breakfast, we choose the buffet. The choice was really ok. The service was correct and staff very friendly.
Just one negative : the price for the parking.
Otherwise : outstanding

I stayed for the orioles opener, good staff aranged a cap wenn the shuttle was unable, but the building is a little bit worn out, thin walls , but the fat cockroach in the breakfastlounge was the highlight for my partner... no more pankakes for me!!! its a good location a little overpriced but for a short trip okay..

To sum up our stay at Fort Rapids, it was NOT worth the money!! We stayed in a - bedroom with - bathrooms. The rooms are dark, dreary, and depressing. The rooms had a funny smell. Neither bedroom was directly accessible to a bathroom. The restaurant was empty when we went in to eat, and now we know why. The breakfast buffet was awful! The bacon was basically cardboard. The regular menu items were not much better, pancakes that fell apart. The water park itself was fun, but not the cleanest place, food out, trash. I would absolutely NOT recommend Fort Rapids to anyone.

Loved this hotel and the staff; however, it is not set up appropriately for business travelers...at least my room wasn't. I was upgraded to a pool side room which was beautiful, but I was unpleasantly surprised when I went to plug in my lap top at the desk and there was no outlet to be had. The only outlet I could use was the one of the other side of the bed, so I had to have my laptop charging on my bed all night. Same for my cell phone. Definitely not a friendly hotel for those of us who need to work in the room.
I cannot complain about the room and bathroom-dressing area. Very lovely, and I felt pampered. The staff was extremely attentive except I was surprised that when hosting a guest in the hotel lounge, I had to go to the bar myself to get us drinks. I think when spending $---glass of wine, I should expect to be waited on.
If you stay here, definitely apply for the President's Club. You get free Internet connection that way, and perhaps that's why I was upgraded to a nicer room. One complaint though regarding the TV channels....I ordered a hockey game through NHL Center Ice, but after it charged me, the channel was not available. The hotel credited my account, but I was surprised that it was not offered. Especially since the San Jose Sharks were the team playing.

I stayed at this hotel for work. And trust me, I have stayed at tons of hotels for work. And I have seen a lot of ugly hotels, as well as lots of nice hotels. When I got in to the hotel I thought, wow, the hotel lobby looked brand new and clean. And I have to say that the employees were all very nice. But once I got to my room I could tell that the room was outdated. The colors, carpet, and furniture. But they do have new beds, which were really comfortable, and I did my routine and checked the bathroom, and it was spacious as well as very clean. So I was pretty pleased. The only thing I noticed was some of the pillows had some dark spots at the end that looked like dust or something. But thank god that there were more than two pillows, so I just had to pick and choose. The employees were very accommodating and made sure that I got my toothbrush that I had called down for. They called me half an hour after I had asked for it to make sure that I had received it. The second night I ordered from the room service, and I was really pleased because the food was yummy. The lady at the front desk said that they actually were finishing a renovation, which I really could not even tell, because there was no sign of workers anywhere. She said that they are redoing all the rooms.

This is a wonderful hotel with very obliging staff. Well situated at the head of the Magnificent Mile, all of the big-name shops and stores are within easy walking distance. Hotel staff particularly helpful were concierge Sheryl and bell-boy Craig who both supplied us with information about the best times to visit the cities attractions. Amenities at the Millennium are the usual that one would expect to find at a --star hotel but the bathroom towels and robes, and the oversize bed were particularly delightful. We should point out that we took advantage of a good deal that allowed us a --night stay in a junior suite for $--- per night, which remains available at the time of this review. We look forward to returning to this lovely hotel.

So, here's the scoop on this place:
Rooms: The basic rooms are a good deal at $ ---.-- or under. The suites are above average deals, if that's your thing, at $ ---.-- & up. Hotel is very popular with Europeans & Brits.
Service: very good, very responsive, very friendly.
Neighborhood: safe, residential area known as Murray Hill, plenty of local restaurants around that are open all hours on the weekends, walking distance to basics such as the Empire State Bldg, Herald Square, Grand Central, much more; plenty of cabs cruising Lexington Ave & -rd Ave.
Room service: prompt, fairly accurate (forgot all the condiments & the salad dressing), expensive as hell (I get it, this is NYC, but $ --.-- for a salad, - burgers & - drinks was interesting).
My Experience: our visit began oddly, as the amenity package that I had paid for wasn't in the room & had to be requested (-x); then, it was discovered that the sink wouldn't drain; up to our room came a maintenance gent who worked diligently for -- minutes to resolve the issue on a Friday night; with my help, issue resolved. Not exactly what you want to do after traveling all day, but stuff happens. Next day, the flat screen television failed; ended up watching Winbledon tennis finals on a dilapidated, old tv in the hotel-affiliated bar named 'Rare.'
Front Desk Manager Warren Herrera came through for us - - re-located us on Saturday to the suite up on --. Suite was very roomy & had the feel of an apartment. The AC struggled to keep up with a -- degree day, though, and didn't cool the living room area until well after dark.
BTW, the hotel doesn't AC the hallways. You come out of your room on a hot summer's day & wait a few minutes for an elevator & trust me, you melt. Just thought that no AC in the hallway of a major hotel in mid-town, especially after renovations, was odd - - and off-putting.
Staff: Very professional, very friendly, very responsive to issues.
Eats: recommend Zengo's on -rd Ave for Asian Latin fusion (try the duck appetizer, very good); recommend Scottie's Diner on Lex (open ---- & the best corned beef hash I've ever tasted); Nirvana is Indian food on Lex, basic nothing special; Sushi Yasuda a few blocks away for excellent sushi & great service; the little corner deli on the corner of --th & Lex for that NYC classic, the egg, bacon & cheese on a hard roll sandwich, damn, now that's a tasty & inexpensive item for a quick breakfast. There is free wi-fi in the rooms.
Now, a couple of negatives (though they are small). Location: the hotel is out on a wharf in what had until recently been an industrial zone-port facility. So, while there are other hotels and office buildings in the area (close to the Convention Center) and some well known Boston restaurants (like Anthony’s Pier - – overpriced and over-touristed) the hotel really isn’t close to the action of the city. There isn’t, for example, a nearby drug store or a lot of choices of restaurants, bars and shopping. For all of those things you have to cab or walk more into the center of town – my guess is that it would be at least a mile and a half walk.
Next, I like my rooms cool to cold – especially if I’m staying on the upper floors of a hotel. You couldn’t open the windows and while the thermostat said it was set at --, it never felt cool or cold in the room.
However, these are minor complaints for a good hotel in a area of the city that is quickly being rebuilt.

A little later my husband went into the kinkos check into his flight and print the boarding passes and he found out when he got there that it would be $-- to log on and print... when he mentioned that he was told by the hotel to go there for the service they said that it was still $--, he opted to do it at the airport. My only other complaint, and again, not a big one, is that when you have your car valeted, you don't pick it up out front where you drop it off, you go through a doorway across the lobby, down a hallway and out a service door into the garage. My husband and I got the corner king room while my daughter got a regular king room. What makes the corner king room different is that it's at the end of the hall. My daughters room seemed a little larger as a whole, I preferred the layout of the corner room more because the bed was facing the large window. Short of that feature there wasn't enough of a difference to make the king room more special than the regular king.
Short of the two rather minor issues we really enjoyed our stay at the Grand Hyatt and would stay again.
Love the Kimpton hotels and this one did not disappoint! Great location and helpful staff. I would stay here again!
The hotel is in a great location near the end of the f lines and near the cable cars. Easy to walk to Fisherman's wharf. A little dated, but clean...Parking price is $---night - outrageous....
Great location. Great bed. Great price. All round great spot.

Sexy with just the right amount of seductive irony, Rouge was a great date-night hotel. The room was fantastic-- unbelievable furnishings, floor to ceiling decorative mirror, cool art, nice bathroom, lots of closet space, etc. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""rouge"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" color scheme could easily have become tacky, but the decor is spot on.The service was also outstanding-- check-in and check-out were easy, and we asked for a DVD player, which was promptly brought up to the room at no extra charge. I just returned from spending a weekend at the Catamaran for a friend's wedding and I must say it met all my expectations but I did not have particularly high ones going in. This hotel dates back to the early --'s-late --'s and unfortunately the rooms suffer for it. They have done a nice face lift to the lobby adding a rock sculpture and koi pond but the rooms are a bit on the shabby side with the original kitchenette appliances. My friend and I shared a room on the --th floor of the tower, which was great since we had a view of both the bay and the ocean from our balcony. This included a peek at Sea World's nightly -:-- fireworks from across the bay. However the sliding glass door was off the track and the lock was broken, neither of which inspired a lot of confidence. Both bedside reading lamps were broken as well. Engineering was able to fix the lamps and the door, but not the lock. The showerhead position was permanently fixed to the wall, something difficult to deal with when you are tall and the original installer was not, plus it was green with corrosion. I had a hard time finding extra outlets to charge my cell phone, etc. and the decor could use some updating.
The food served at the wedding was truly appalling. I've had better entrees on airplanes. However the wedding was beautiful as it was on the lawn with the bay as a backdrop and of course ultimately you don't go to weddings for the meal. The banquet rooms were nice and the staff was very well-organized. I did not see any problems or delays which I'm sure was a relief for the brides.
I did not use the pool since it was August and not necessary but it struck me as very crowded with many families and small children packed into it every day. I think a hotel of that size could do with a larger pool, or at least a second one.
The spa however was fantastic as it is only a year old. Both of the women that did my treatments were well-trained and friendly and I felt like a new person after I'd finished. The only complaint is that the spa is hard to find as you must walk through the breakfast area and find an unmarked door. A very kind valet parking attendent walked me all the way back there though. Overall the staff was excellent, very helpful and friendly which made getting around San Diego much easier. The parking was $---day for valet and $---day for self-parking so it almost made as much sense to use the valet as it did to park yourself. There was little or no street parking available in August.
Overall I would not rush to book another trip here but if you are able to get a good discount through AAA or some other organization it might be worth it with children. I think you'd get a similar experience in a nicer setting at one of the B&B's along the bay, or by renting a vacation home for a week. The hotel reminded me of an aging surfer of --+yrs still wearing Jams and trying a little too hard to be youthful. Sort of fun, but kind of not.
Good rooms well kept and clean. Flat screen TV, plenty of bathroom amenities. Coffee maker. Large room and I would be happy to stay here anytime.

The Dakota is the perfect base to explore San Fran. It's cheap, cheerful and has a certain amount of bohemian vibe running through it.
Only - blocks from Union Square this little gem will not disappoint.$-- for a room and bath can't be bad and it's not. Friendly front desk with free coffee in the morning.A traditional birdcage elevator just adds to the place.
I'll be back.

Booked this Grand Ole Dame over Thanksgiving weekend, just one night for a quick getaway to celebrate my husbands birthday. I had stayed at the Fairmont --yrs back and I remember it such an old world charm, with dramatic decor and gorgeous linens. The hotel is indeed still beautiful and they were just putting up all the Christmas decorations so the word magical pops into my head. I would have been totally fine if I had paid $-- but breakfast cost us $-- for - Benedict and a freshly squeezed orange juice. All in all it was a fine stay, but I think we will try the Lenox next time.

We were met by the most friendly & Knowledgeable hotel staff. The Concierge (Jhett) was most helpful. Peter at the front desk went above and beyond to ensure our stay was flawless.

Thank you to the Omni staff who made this stay perfect!

We originally hoped to have a King size bed but reserving on-line, none was available. My mother and I stayed at the Iroquois April --th through May -nd. It was very nice, close to all the big attractions. The street isn't pretty but it is quiet and the hotel's location is safe and convenient for public transport. The staff were friendly and efficient. The room was spacious and clean with a comfortable bed. Breakfast is included in the rate - not the highest quality but substantial and varied so you can find something you like. The hotel has a laundry for guest use - very convenient on a long trip. Would definitely stay here again.

After amix up (not ours) in our hotel booking we found ourselves at the Park Central Hotel. A warm understanding welcome t three harasses travellers and good, quiet rooms. The conceirge staff were extremely helpful booked trips, tickets, booking the shuttle bus to JFK etc.
Great position too.

Our third trip to New York was with our tiny daughter, My mother , and My uncle's family. As we planned to travel a lot and needed a convenient location for a better price we choose Affinia Dumont by chance (priceline) but after seeing the pictures we reserved the second room for my uncles family too. Highly recommend it!!!!!

It's clear the hotel was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""trendy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but I thought it seemed tired and a bit worn. Room was on the small side and bathroom was also small - no tub. I think I am comparing it to my last stay at the Trump Hotel In Chicago which was WOW! No time for the spa so can't say. On busy street (noisy even early Sunday morning) so stay on an upper floor.

We got a discounted price and upgrade on this property which made it a bargan for its location right in the heart of the theatre district. The bistro Saju next door is a great place to dine especially for the great breakfastes which were part of the upgrade. The freebie cocktails the first night was a nice treat too. But even with this upgrade the bath is really small with no surface area to put clothes except on the toilet seat and there were no AC outlets in the bath. Room was nice and fresh and comfortable and there was good lighting for reading (a feature that is getting hard to find these days). Bed was very comfortable. Walked across the street to our musical one night and around the corner the next night. Will certainly check out them out the next time we are in town.

When we arrived there was no air. We were told that it was being fixed, only to find out later that it had been removed by the hotel for replacement and would not be back up and running for another week. The hotel staff was non apologetic, & would not provide us with fans or any compensation (monetary or otherwise). There was never a manager on site to speak with us, after several requests. My husband and I decided to take a trio from St Louis to Chicago for our -- year wedding anniversary. The hotel was fantastic! Last weekend, we stayed - nights at the Liaison Affinia. We've stayed at an Affinia hotel in NYC and enjoyed it, so we were pleased to find this location in DC. We were able to get what we thought was a good special on their website that included valet parking.
This hotel is very well located between the Capitol and Union Station. There are several restaurants nearby, and the closest Metro was at Union Station. We felt comfortable walking in the neighborhood at night.
We arrived on Friday evening and check-in was pleasant and efficient. The room was clean upon arrival. We found the room to be hotter than we found comfortable, so we adjusted the thermostat down in the room. It took about -- hours for the room to cool down, so we weren't sure whether the thermostat had much control over the room temperature. The bed was very comfortable and the pillows were great. Ice was readily available on our floor. It was extremely quiet in our room. Our King room had both a small couch and easy chair.
The normal amenities (shampoo, conditioner, lotion) were supplied and replenished each day. We appreciated that housekeeping noted that we used the regular and not the decaf coffee for the in-room coffee-maker, and provided an extra - of these the next day.
Since we arrived late in the evening, we decided to have a snack and cocktail in the bar. The ArtBar was a highlight of our stay. The food was much better than we expected, and the service was friendly and efficient.
The valet parking was so fast in retrieving our car whenever we needed it that there was no need to call down early for it. 
At first I thought a laptop that was sitting on a pedestal in the front desk was for customer use for accessing the internet, but found it was just for using the Affinia system. I'm not sure why that wouldn't be a front desk function. A bigger sign indicating why the laptop was there would have been helpful. There was a business center with a PC, with a charge for using it. Since all I wanted was to look up directions to a restaurant I had made reservations for, I ended up asking at the front desk. They were very helpful, looking it up on the computer behind the front desk. It would have been nice to use the laptop on the pedestal for that myself. Since you're standing to use it, and it's right next to the front desk, it shouldn't get abused, but would allow front desk employees to take care of things customers can't take care of themselves, and answering the phone.
All in all it was a great stay, and I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

I spent a lot of time seaching hotels on the web for NYC and finally settled on the Broadway Plaza, thanks in large part to reviews on this website. We were not disappointed. When we arrived on a Sat. the area outside the hotel was the most off-putting part of the stay, very crowded street in front of a very small entrance with lots of bootlegged DVDs on display. The staff were very friendly and quite helpful, as was all of New York. I definately will return to NYC and would stay again at the Broadway Plaza.

The entire downstairs staff is excellent. The bathroom was small, there were too few toiletries (one soap), and the shower head was shooting some water into the ceiling, finally the toilet made a horrible sound when it was flushed. I was disappointed that my room didn't have a terrace (as I viewed right into the others around me), but I paid $-- on priceline and was treated like a valued customer.

Bed bugs and poor management, lack of ownership which ruined my vacation. Thanks

The bathroom has a window, because there is always very cold (winter). Heater in the room is very loud and strong running dry the air. Poor sound insulation door. All hear what is happening in the hallway.

Front desk were sometimes a little grumpy yet still helpful and the rest of the service was excellent, would definately stay here again!! Would highly recommend it - I went with another friend and we both were very impressed with the size and cleaniness of the rooms and the location.
Love the Magnolia. Friendly and helpful staff. Great location.

For example, they have no concienrge lounge, no gift shop-news stand and the restaurant is only open until --:-- am. Yes, there's a Palm restaurant downstairs, but it's not open until dinner. You are """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""on your own"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" for lunch, which I found strange for a full service, downtown hotel. I'll also admt that I was not too happy to have to walk two blocks in the rain to get to a --Eleven for bascis that a hotel gift show would offer in most hotels.
Also concerning is the incidental costs at this property. For example, overnight parking is $-- per night. I thought it seemed high when we arrived, but assumed this was the typical cost of parking in downtown Denver. Not so, the Chase bank garage (right across the street) is only $-- per day. I have contacted the hotel to get this refunded, but if you were not paying careful attention, the hotel would have just added charges to your bill after you left. 
For me, even as a loyal Starwood guest, my choice for downtown Denver hotel would be the Hyatt. It's appears to be brand new and is in a very good location. The Westin has just enough shortcomings to knock it off of my list when staying in Denver.

Also, the manager was helpful and very pleasant--We checked out rather late, and then had some extra time before a business appointment. I will stay here again next time I am in San Diego.

We traveled to San Antonio to watch our son's graduation from the Air Force at Lackland AFB. The only complaint I had was the small parking stalls in their parking garage.
