Other than that I highly recommend this hotel if you want to be close to the Riverwalk.

We stayed at the Wyndham Garden in mid-June at a really great rate for NYC. The location is the best attribute of this hotel. Union Square, the Flatiron building, the Empire State building, Little India, and Penn Station are all withing reasonable walking distance. There are two subway stations on different lines within a block of the hotel. Plenty of options for meals, drinks, shopping, etc. Overall, Chelsea is very nice and much less touristy than Midtown.
The hotel was just ok due to a few problems during our stay. We were given a clean room on the -th floor on the back with the view of an airshaft. Free Wi-Fi was nice, but a little slow. The room was pretty small, but NYC generally has small rooms. We had a wardrobe for hanging clothes with an iron, ironing board inside and small coffee maker-set. One of the problems we had was a lack of any places to set anything down in the room (other than the floor). In the entire room, we only had one small nightstand. As a result, you have to try and sqeeze your wallet, keys, guidebook, map, subway card, drink, watch, remote control, clock, etc. on that one nightstand. I am not sure where you are supposed to actually MAKE the coffee. We tried making ours on the top of the toilet tank and on the floor. No closet. No desk or safe in the room although they are listed as amenities on the website. They did deliver a safe to go in our wardrobe when we requested it. I had to go to the front desk to get more shampoo and conditioner because they didn't give us anymore when they cleaned the room. The bed was the highpoint of the room itself. It was a large, King bed with nice linens and pillows.
During our stay, they were in the process of renovating the restaurant downstairs. As a result, we listened to hammers and banging if we were in the room during the day. As others have said, the shower design is terrible. It is impossible to shower and not get most of the bathroom floor wet.
As referenced by a previous reviewer, the first morning we woke up at the Wyndham Garden there was no hot water. The staff apologized and suggested that it might be repaired soon, but we waited for a while and, in the end, took cold showers.
For the same price, I would probably stay at this hotel again and hope that the stay would be better. The location, cleanliness, and price is what would bring me back.

My son reccomended this hotel. He warned us about staying in the downtown area and dealing with parking fees that increases the cost of your stay. Parking is free at this hotel. The hotel is very attractive. We were able to view the mountains from our balcony. The room was attractive and comfortable with a great mattress. My husband spent a lot of time playing with the remote adjusting his side of the bed. We truly slept like babies both nights. Staff was friendly and helpful giving us directions in a friendly and accurate manner. Our dining experience was the only negative. Slow service. Seems like the set up in the bar area kept the servers busy walking long distances to order and pick up the food. Our waiter was pleasant and this made us less gnarly about the slowness. We just decided to sit back and chat with our son and make the best of waiting. The food was hot and appetizing when it finally arrived, making the wait less annoying. My son parked his car at the hotel and drove us all over Denver both days. We were able to do some serious shopping. The Bass Pro is close and we were able to spend time there dining and shopping. We packed a lot of tourist things in those - and --- days. We were able to get off and on the freeway without problem. Great visit.

We enjoyed our --day stay at the Comfort Inn Downtown Memphis. Staff at the front desk was very welcoming and helpful; they were able to switch us from smoking to non-smoking; the room was nice and big; breakfast was great every morning; parking in the garage was okay, but worth having our vehicle in a safe place; the hotel was convenient for everywhere we wanted to go plus the trolley was just a block away.

If your not planning on being in ny very long and will hardly be in the hotel, then it may be tolerable. Aside from that, expect the annoyance of bedbugs, peeling Walls, dirty bathrooms and old furniture. Some floors are being renovated. But most of the rooms and floors looked like something out of a horror movie. Very creepy and old fashioned, even the doors were creepy. Hair in the bath drain, peeling ceilings. Outside our door on floor three ( by room --- ) there were bleached sick stains. Was a very uncomfortable visit. *itching from bed bug bites whilst typing this*

This is my second stay at the Ballantyne Resort. On our first stay a few years ago, we booked the Presidential Suite and were treated very well. However, on this last stay we booked a king room with a balcony view of the golf course. The bed is very comfortable (a plus) but there is no complimentary coffee service in the hotel. The only way to get coffee in your room is to order via in-room dining (way overpriced even though it is Illy brand coffee allegedly). I think this is cheesy. If you consider yourself high end, then you must provide coffee and tea service as a compliment to the guest. I would rather pay a few dollars more on my nightly rate in order to guarantee this service.
Another negative is the fitness center. It appears that many locals use these facilities along with personal training staff, etc. This is fine but it limits the availability of elliptical machines and treadmills for guests. We were not able to get a workout unless we chose """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""odd times"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to exercise. The Ballantyne area is nice but it is a bit of a drive away from Uptown, so if the Uptown location is important and you can afford it, try the Ritz-Carlton.
We have stayed at many five star properties (Four Seasons, Ritz, etc) and this hotel is nowhere close. I know it is considered a --star property and this may be due to the Spa and Golf facilities which are nice. But as a hotel alone, I would give it --stars at best. The staff is friendly but they are missing that """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""it-factor"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that really takes you to the next level. One really positive experience we had was breakfast at the Gallery Restaurant. The chicken-apricot sausage is excellent!

The apartment was very comfortable with good views over Washington. Full kitchen, with fresh coffee beans and grinder, was very welcome. Supermarket (Trader Joes) and Subway about --- metres away. Noise was what you'd expect in a city and didnt disturb sleep
Fabulous location, great rooms and they know it.. be sure to check out all the details on the parking (pricey) and if you can get a breakfast deal or other shopping.

I recently stayed at the Red Lion in downtown Seattle for three nights. I read the TripAdvisor reviews prior to checking in and knew from what I read that the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""paper thin walls"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" would probably be an issue. Believe me, the notes about the walls are not exaggerated. They are incredibly thin. I couldn't believe how well I could hear everything (*every* thing) my neighbors did. It made for restless nights.
Beyond the walls made of balsa wood, the hotel has a bit of a dated feel. Colors are the typical golds, ruby, and forest greens. The polyester bed spread seemed cheesy, the bath towels seemed too thin, and the bathroom fixtures themselves were quite poor. My bathtub filled with water when I showered and drained very slowly. The toilet took --- flushes to get everything taken care of ... oddly enough, since it made quite a stir with its mighty sucking action ... which seemed to do little. 
The iron in the room is cheap, cheap, cheap and left brown smudges on my company shirts I needed to wear to the tradeshow I was attending. The ironing board was quite stained and burnt.
The front desk staff are quite nice and helpful. They are every bit as helpful and friendly as you would expect at a finer hotel. 
The hotel's fitness facility is fairly good. There are treadmills, elliptical trainers, free weights, and a few machines. Towels and water are provided there. My only issue here was that it was very stuffy in the room. They need some fans in there. The hotel also provides guests with the option to purchase a pass to a full service health club nearby for a nominal fee. 
As noted in many previous reviews, the location is superb. But Seattle has many fantastically situated hotels with much better room facilities and upkeep. 
Personally, I'd shell out a few more clams and choose the Mayflower Park, the Andra, or the Hyatt.

-Staff were friendly.
-Clean, big room with desk, bed, room for clothes.
-Great location.
-Free breakfast.
-VERY inexpensive.
-Quick walk from Amtrak.

The Clarion on Park Avenue South is a small, older hotel that you can get for cheap (paid $----night). When I stayed there, they were replacing the furniture in all the rooms, which meant that the already very small lobby was filled to the ceiling with nightstands and headboards, making it impossible to sit in the lobby and enjoy their free wifi. 
The afternoon I checked in (at -:--; the sign at the lobby said check in was any time after -) I was told my room was getting new furniture and to come back in an hour. No apologies, and the clerk was did not seem the least bit concerned that I would be put out by this. I made a fuss at the desk, and within a few minutes was checked in. (funny thing, the next morning, the sign behind the desk showed that check in was -pm) 
Room had very old furniture, carpet was worn, and the bathroom was really tiny. I don't even think the tub was full sized. 
Plusses were: flat screen tv, and a-c worked really well, centrally located, near the subway. 
For $---, it's okay.

The hotel was definitely - star. The rooms were very clean, bed was comfortable, bathroom had a deep tub and stand up shower. Honestly, for someone that doesn't stay --star ever, my favorite part was the electronic curtains. :) All the hotel staff I encountered were friendly and helpful. I did not get a chance to check out the pool or fitness area.

I stayed here for work and was pretty dissapointed. Whatever you do don't do business with the gift shop they won't return anything for a refund and the one ladies is very rude its like dealing with shady people on the street. The hotel allows them to rent that space from them and they shouldn't . Breakfast buffet isn't a great selection and they don't have a brunch. The bathroom was run down and windows dirty in the bedroom. San fran has so many options chooses a different one

If ever in New York City again, I will definitely be staying here again.
We choose to stay in a mini suite which was just fantastic. My friend tends to wake up a little earlier than me, so she could relax in the sitting room without disturbing me. The suite was great, the toiletries were fantastic, the location was right at Time Square, you really could not get a better location to experience Downtown Manhattan. Even though there was so much happening outside on Time Square, the moment you step inside the hotel the noise of the street is left behind. It really is a little gem of a hotel.
The breakfast was very nice and the wine & cheese each evening was a nice touch. The staff are very friendly and helpful. I would have to agree with the other reviews and say that the air-conditioning was very loud but it certainly didn't interrupt our sleep. Unless you are a light sleeper this shouldn't be too difficult to put up with.
If I am fortunate to come back to New York City, I will not even consider staying anywhere else.

Stayed two nights on business- lovely view of the Washington monument. Excellent service although I did witness one of the guests getting pretty bent out of shape at the concierge.
The rooms are very nicely appointed with everything you'd expect in a hotel at this price: flat screen, luxe sheets, huge bathroom, etc. The wifi network is pretty bad though. The concierge did explain that they are upgrading their system so it should get better, or so he said.
The spa was very nice, although totally overpriced. Then again, that pretty much describes the whole thing: outrageously expensive but luxurious pampering.
One thing I didn't like were the doormen- I swear, if I got pushed aside by one more snot-nosed, pushy, scumbag lawyer brat trying to swoop my cab, I was going to clock him. The doorman wasn't very helpful in trying to organize the situation.
Didn't eat there- only had breakfast via room service which was fine. But expensive.
Kind of strange location- convenient to Reagan airport but a little off the beaten track- the cabs know how to get there, but there isn't much in the way of walking distance attractions- the washington monument and other sites aren't too far but I wouldn't stay here if you're looking for a centrally located, convenient, walking distance-type place. Cabs are needed for pretty much everything.

Stayed in room ---. I recieved an early check in, the room was spotless, the staff friendly.
The rooftop terrasse is just amazing, and the location of the hotel unbeattable regarding the price. Will definitely be back. :)

I stay at a lot of Hilton brand hotels for business and this is one of the nicest I've experienced.
I'm not accustomed to Hilton Garden Inn hotels having so many on-site extras, but this hotel had a full-service spa (with weekday happy hour specials), restaurant (with happy hour and weekly-nightly specials), and lunchtime deli. They also offered room service, not something you see all that often at Hilton Garden Inns. And of course the -- hour pantry-snack shop.
Room was very spacious with desk-office space, microwave and mini-fridge. Bed was only okay. Typical neutrogena bath products. Everyone I encountered was very friendly.
The area is very quiet with a mix of residential and business parks. There are some decent restaurants a short drive away. If you like to exercise, there are some trails-paths-bike lanes but it is a pretty hilly area so be prepared for a work out!

The room did not have a microwave or a refridgerator and for the price we paid, it should have had both. The balconies are shared, separated by a metal gate. Furniture in room was damaged and should have been replaced. There is no wireless internet in the rooms, you have to go to the lobby or the lounge. There is """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""high speed internet"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in the rooms that you can plug into, but you have to pay by the hour to use it. I would certainly not stay at this hotel again. The only thing they really had to offer was a single chocolate chip cookie at check-in. I'll be spending my money more wisely elsewhere and buying my own cookies.

There was nothing really significant that stood out about this hotel, except for the complimentary cookies in my room which appeared to be home-made and were warm when I arrived. Other than that the beds were a bit small and the room was comfortable enough but nothing spectacular. The hotel is in a convenient location for shopping, restaurants, etc. There is a starbucks less than a block away and the Cherry Creek Shopping Centre is probably two blocks away.
Excellent boutique hotel. Everything was very clean and great service!

The Hyatt Regency is a great hotel if you plan only a short stay. We stayed for - nights and although the room was excellent, a good gym, nice pool and the staff very good, the little things that can make a difference were missing. We stayed friday to friday and were disappointed to find on friday,the main bar was shut at --.--pm, on saturday it shut at --.--pm even though there were plenty of guests requesting its services. From Sunday until we left it did not open again and the only bar available was in the on site restuarant! You may wonder why the fuss, well what the tourist guides and hotel info do not tell you is that although Downtown Houston has lots of restuarants and bars is that the majority shut by -pm as they cater for the demands of the business people who work downtown during the day! After a day sightseeing and driving its nice too relax in the late evening at the bar and have a quiet drink or two with your travel campanions.There are other districts, but that means a taxi or long walk which we did, but after a long day you sometimes just want to stay local and relax. Another disappointment was that this hotel charges $-.-- a day for Wifi access which considering where it is and the type of client they target is quite unbelieveable, also be aware the cheapest charge for a days parking here is $--.--, valet parking is $--.--!! To sum up, a perfect place to stay for a night or two but no more and only for a business person certainly not for a family.

Hotel advertised in AAA book as having """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""interior corridors"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", but the un-heated, glass-lined corridors seem to be add-ons to what were originally exterior corridors (evidenced by the screened window between the room and the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""corridor"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The room heater was so loud could not hear the TV, and turning up the TV volume gave me a headache. Had to leave the heater off to sleep due to the noise, resulting in a rather cold, uncomfortable night. Misleadingly advertised restaurants are not on the premises. This place is a dump, masqueradeing as upscale. Will notify AAA of misleading ad.

I booked this as an 'unlisted' hotel because we were trying to save money and thought the risk was worth it. Unlisted means you book through a site like hotwire and don't actually know which hotel it is until you complete the booking, you just know the price, general location and rating. Benefit of taking this risk = better price.
When I booked and saw it was Envoy Club I came here to read reviews and was a little concerned. They were hardly universally positive.
But after a week staying there I can say I was pleasantly surprised, and we thought it was perfect for what we were looking for. 
Our room was big, very big by Manhattan standards. The neighbourhood was safe and reasonably convenient (Murray Hill is NOT in the absolute middle of Manhattan, so if this is what you want, choose another place), and the apartment style worked well for us. A doorman plus a staff member (most of the time) was enough to handle all of our requests.
The bed was comfortable, with nice clean sheets, and the room was dark, cool and quiet at night. The two airconditioning units handled the NY heatwave perfectly. 
The kitchen wasn't new but it was clean and very usable. The bathroom was big and clean. As for the carpet - I'm not sure if we had new carpet or if previous reviews saw things that we didn't, but our carpet was ---% fine.
Internet wasn't free, but it worked very well (a lot better than many hotels I've stayed in) so I was happy. 
My conclusion about Envoy Club is that it certainly wasn't as bad as some of these reviews make it sound. Whether you like it or not will all depend on what you are looking for - if you want something brand new, gives you the feeling of being right in the heart of Manhattan, has great views, and a really cool vibe, Envoy Club probably isn't the best bet.
However, if you want great space, very practical pleasant apartment style and excellent value, Envoy Club could be a great option. My fiance and I had both been to Manhattan before, so we didn't need a rockstar place, we just needed a place that was a decent size, good quality, reasonably located (we actually liked getting some extra walking by staying in Murray Hill) and good value. Envoy Club was all of that and we would have no hesitation in going there again.

Our room was on the -th floor and newly painted. The windows were open for the room, as was the door to try to air out paint fumes. It was not bad enough to complain but not pleasant either. The room was average as others have mentioned. I was surprised that they did not have curtains on the windows at all. Just cheap blinds that did not even come down to the bottom foot of the window? 
The -th floor is not high enough to get away from the street noise from cars and emergency vehicles, construction going on nearby (that usually started at night?), and people enjoying their time each night and into the small hours of every morning. Nothing that the hotel can control and I suspect that it is the same for a lot of hotels in this area. 
Still, the location really was ideal for being a part of all of the Times Square excitement. Lots of shopping and food options nearby. As others have mentioned, the deli right next door (Dunhill) was a good stopping place before and after touristing. 
They did ask that you leave your key at the desk when you leave the room each time. Reminded me of the Odessa in Paris, so I liked this quirky aspect. I agree that the front desk staff was fairly glum but they were never rude or surly. 
This hotel is walkable to many many New York tourist sites, but note that taxis here are priced quite fairly (cheap compared to what we are used to), so don't be afraid to step out to any street going the general direction you want to go and hail one.
We would stay here again.

I thought for the money the hotel was nice. However the pillows were horrible. They were so stiff, I felt that I was going to wake up with a pain in my neck. I never found out because I did not sleep and my neck still hurt. The sheets smelled dirty and cheap. The bed was comfortable. I never write reviews, but I felt that this needed to be know. I did complete a comment card so maybe they will fix the problem. It was told to me by the hotel staff they people do complain about the pillows.

I found this hotel to be in an ideal location, minutes from times square but not too close to be noisy. In the other direction about -- mins from Central Park. The room was very large with a -ft bed (deluxe king room on --th floor). A big disappointment was that there were no tea-coffee making facilities in the room. The reception staff seemed very subdued and not very friendly (from the later reviews I think they must have had a whole new set of staff since May). We booked the hotel as a package through Virgin and think we got value for money, mainly for the comfy bed and location. The bathroom seemed a bit dated and had a jacuzzi type bath but the jets were all blanked off. Other reviewers state that there is free continental breakfast. We were never told about this at any stage by virgin or the hotel so didn't partake. Overall I probably would stay here again if the price was right.

We found this to be a very good deal for what we paid. We were only sleeping at the hotel and while we were very disappointed initially at the location of the room, across from the ice machine, bordering on the vending machines and facing the parking lot, it was immaculate and served our purpose well. Despite the location of the room, it was very quiet. The location of the hotel is very good in that it is close to a lot we wanted to do but away from the noise that so often accompanies a city stay.
The decor was nice - the room had recently been renovated and it showed. Good sized room and bathroom, comfortable pillows and bed. We did have a small patio area surrounded by tall plantings that gave a bit of privacy from the parking lot. The grounds were beautiful. I would definitely stay here again and at the great price we got, the room was definitely a good value.

I booked through Trailfinders at fairly short notice ( a month ahead) and for a period during New York Fashion Week so accept that my choice was limited. This was a surprise birthday present for my partner and I wanted it to be as close to perfect as possible. Checking in was fine and the public areas of the hotel are quite stunning if you can cope with the very dim lighting. 
However, I nearly cried when we opened the door to our room. My university hall of residence room back in the --s was bigger than this and this was supposed to be for two people. There was barely space to get in or out of bed except from the bottom end of the bed. Lighting was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""moody"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but useless. Hanging space was minimal and there was nowhere to store luggage. The bathroom was the tiniest I have ever seen on dry land with one of the shelves coming away from the wall so, again, nowhere to put toiletries. No robes, no tea or coffee making facilities, although a hairdryer and iron were provided and the shampoo, conditioner and body lotion were good quality (Aveda).
There was a permanent musty smell and the air conditioning was very noisy. Hardly conducive to a romantic holiday! The room might be OK for a single person but not for a couple no matter how close you are! It might be OK for one night, maybe two, but we were staying for five!
A further disappointment was that on two nights the main bar was closed for a private party and the library bar as well on one night. The rain stopped access to the roof terrrace. As the cost of drinks was pretty outrageous, we were really only interested in people watching but it was made clear that this wasn't going to be an option unless we were prepared to stand all night in a dark corner of the foyer.
All in all, very disappointing.

Stayed at the Trump for two nights mid October ----. My stay could not have been better. Because I am a member of the Leader's Club I was given an complimentary upgrade. Which was really nice. I was whisked away to my suite right away, and was also given a complimentary drink of my choice at my arrival. The suite was beautifully decorated and maintenated - and it had EVERYTHING that I could wish for. It was large - lavish bedroom and a nice living room with a striking city view. The bedroom had a tv, dvd-player, a vcr-player, large closets and an extremely comfertable bed. The living room had a HUGE plasma television with dvd-player and a Nintendo. The living room had a dining area and a huge sofa and a coffeetable. Very spacious and convenient. The kitchen was well equipped and had a large bench, a large oven and a huge refrigerator. The bathrom was rather small, would be a big plus if it was more spacious. But it was nice and it had a whirlpool which is a nice feature after a long NYC-day:) Overall, the suite was so nice and all the technological features was working well, including high speed wireless internet.
The service was execellent - the best ever experienced in NYC. They compete up there with the service of Four Seasons. Everyone was so courteus, humorus, smiling and attentive. Could not have been better. Everything was fixed within minutes. And the attache-service was very attentive and convenient. The food was great too. The personalized stationary and business cards was a convenient feature as well. Everything you could wish for was provided in the room, without a hassle nor a question.
I have stayed at many high-end hotels in NYC, among those Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental, Ritz-Carlton, Soho House, Waldorf Towers, etc. But after this trip the Trump is my new favourite in New York City!!! Everything was so perfect and great, and I don't have a negative thing to say about the hotel. Trump knows what excellent hospitality is!! AND, the hotel was great and outstanding for a nice little romantic getaway:)

The location is great with a short walk to Fishermans Wharf but otherwise the hotel is a very average chain hotel. Rooms are clean and ok, but the noise from the streets and-or neighboring rooms woke us up every morning at six. Would have expected better quality compared with the price.

Unfortunately, our stay at this hotel was far from satisfactory. The bed was so uncomfortable, we changed hotel after just one night. We asked for the hotel to make a booking at a great restaurant for the saturday evening and they failed to make the booking for us despite saying it had been done. Lousy service.

Let's Start with the positive. The hotel offered a free shuttle service from -am (?) to --pm. This was so very welcomed, as it saved us from having to pay the $--$-- (depending on time-location) parking of downtown Denver, and hassle of bad drivers. The driver we had (Larry, of the -- passenger van) was very nice, and fun to talk to. We used it several times to go to the --th Street Mall and back.
The room was clean, no mold, clean bathroom. We did find a few things left over from the previous people on the ground, which tells me the vacuum is terrible, or they just don't do it.
The showers had good pressure and good temperature - always a concern with high rise hotels.
Only two types of beds are available, - double, or - king. No feathers in the pillows - bedding which is a plus for me.
The skybox on the --th floor was nice to eat at in the morning, or to have a quick drink before attempting sleep. It has a nice view looking into the side of downtown Denver.
Random Bits of Info:
Any pictures you see of this hotel online-in the hotel look to be from at least ----- years ago. 
The pool is out of commission, as the concrete surrounding it is gone, but the lights-pumps are still on and the pool has water in it.
The Bad:
The service was sub-par at the desk, and varied between who was there. One person was very rude - short with you if you had any questions, while another took the time to explain things.
The walls of the room are very ... thin. You can hear exactly what is going on in the adjacent rooms and the hallway. On our first day, we were woken up at -am when a bunch of teenagers started to jump around and bang on the walls (with what sounded like a belt sander or power drill) in both the adjacent rooms until -am.
We also walked into what looked like to be a drug deal on our second day - one floor down from ours while searching for a vending machine - heavy marijuana smell, - posted guards at the door and yelling from inside. 
Smoking on the floors is common and unenforced in our experience, even though it is posted as a $--- fine. I asked for someone to get the people to stop, but the desk had a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""we will get around to it eventually, if ever"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" attitude about it.
In summary:
This hotel is good for staying at if you are going to the stadium (not more than --- yards away) or do not intend on sleeping at for another reason than to party.

The best aspect about this property is its convenient location to the Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport, free ---hour airport shuttle (checked in after - a.m.) and really nice, clean, cozy room.
Check-in was very quick to a second floor, queen bed room. The room itself is small, but perfect for a single traveler. Very clean and elegant with nice wardrobe, TV, microwave, small fridge, coffee maker, desk area and free wi fi. The air conditioner was a little noisy, but no biggie.
The sink is near the bed with nice granite countertop. The separate toilet and shower is enclosed by a pocket door. The shower was a strange shape, but felt spacious when inside.
Simple continental breakfast is available, but I woke up too late to try it out.
Considering I got a great AAA-rate for this hotel, I would definitely stay here again if only as an overnighter before heading out to the airport. No nearby restaurants that I could see, so I wouldn't necessarily stay here for more than a night. Nothing bad at all to say about this hotel.

Just returned from a two-night stay at City Club Hotel. After having issues with a Priceline situation, upon arrival they upgraded us to a kind suite with two floors. The staff is extremely helpful & friendly. The location is awesome, two blocks from the center of Times Square. The room is trendy & modern with comfortable linens & very clean bathrooms. The Bigelow toiletries & abundance of towels are a great touch! They even bring you chocolate chip cookies with turn down service. Also, a nice feature for our teens was the free DVD rental from the front desk with many, many movies to chose from. The only downside I had was the noise from the street & other rooms, but we did have a great view with a balcony, so you have to take the good with the bad. After all, it is the city that never sleeps! Don't hesitate to stay here!

This imposing hotel rises right beside Interstate -, and if you get a room facing east the ceaseless traffic noise from the highway will intrude no matter how good your ear plugs are. That being said, rooms are comfortable and nicely appointed, with comfy bedding, lots of different pillows, yummy Aveda bath products and a no-fog mirror in the bathroom. Full breakfast is available ($$$) or you can have a continental Starbucks for - dollars and change in the lounge. Self park your car for a mere $-- under the hotel and bring your own snacks or pay a whopping $- for a bottle of water which you will reach for in desparation because the frigobar in your room is otherwise empty. The R-view rooftop restaurant is, unfortunately, closed Sundays. Do what you can to work a discount at the Renaissance Seattle, whether CAA, senior, military or whatever or expect to pay over $--- per night.

I stayed at this hotel during a business conference in Denver. It is only - blocks from the Convention Center and - blocks from the --th Street Mall. The central location was extremely helpful as I did not have a rental car during my stay and had to rely on public transportation. 
The hotel's bed was very comfortable. I was worried about hallway noise from reading other reviews on trip advisor, but the noise was only a minimal problem for me. The bathroom was large and though there was a note indicating that they would not change the towels unless they asked, they did change them nearly every day.
My room even had a view of the mountains.
I would stay in the hotel again.

This hotel offers outstanding service and impressive ambiance. I always stay there when I go to San Franciscpo which is at least a dozen times. It's easy access to all the site. It's on top of Nob Hill with unbelievable views.

We've been staying here every time we come to San Francisco for about -- years now, once or twice a year to visit friends. This is the nicest Hilton we have stayed in. It was not the most elegant, but definitely extremely nice and comfortable. The rooms were perfect! Very clean and nice. This is a very nice hotel in a great location. The rooms are all mini-suites, with a bedroom area with its own TV that closes off from the sitting area. This was nice for us because I like to get up early and my wife prefers to sleep in a bit, and it's nice to have a hotel room where there's someplace aside from the bed and the desk to sit. 
The rooms are well-equipped with plenty of storage space. The rooms with two doubles have a double set of drawers. Some rooms have pullout couches in the sitting area so it's great if you want to share a room and still have a bit of privacy.
The problem is with the service. I've never seen a decent hotel where the front desk is so underpopulated. When we arrived there were three groups in front of us and only one person at the desk. Several times I called the desk during the stay and got either no answer at all or an answer after well more than -- rings.
The people are nice and try to be helpful, but at one point we had arranged in advance to switch rooms and it took the desk clerk and the bell staff over an hour to find the record (which they did ultimately find) and get a bellman up to the room. This ruined an afternoon for us. Another time it took -- minutes to get a cup of coffee to go at the restaurant because I wanted a muffin and they didn't haven any and instead of telling me they disappeared looking for one for -- minutes.
One other complaint is with the room service menu which is seriously fussy and overdone. For example, there is no club sandwich, but a club sandwich panini with herbed cream cheese. The caesar salad came with a whole poached egg sitting on top.
I think with a small upgrade in staffing and organization, this could be a superb hotel. As it is it's just a good one. I'd still recommend it, but visitors should temper their expectations.

We stayed here using hotel points before an early morning flight out of Midway. Overall, I wasn't too pleased, although my partner says I am over-reacting. The hallway rug on our floor was incredibly stained; one or two is one thing, but it looked like it hadn't been cleaned in a looooong time. Overall, eh, very convenient to the airport, but not the sort of place I'd spend money on. WATCH OUT for the red light camera right across the street! The intersection is confusing, and we got a ticket!
Checked in from long trip and the bed was amazing it was soft and I was a goner...My room was on the side of the freeway but didn't hear a thing very quiet location.

This is a wonderful hotel, the decor is soothing, the people are friendly and the omelettes are awesome. Valet was top notch, ready to give directions and they asked us which mountain we went to ride, daily. Close to --th St., but not too close. Starbucks is right next door too. Mountain views were amazing.

You gotta love a hotel that features local art ... everywhere. As a caveat, I did book this hotel via Priceline, so I guess it was not the hotel's fault that I ended up in a smoking room on a smoking floor as a nonsmoker (though they weren't able to switch me to a nonsmoking room when I called to ask). The one highlight of my short stay was the front desk, which promptly and thoroughly responded to my requests. The many shortcomings of my short stay relate to the state of the hotel. We stayed here because they had a last minute discount. If the -rd was to stay with us, we'd have to pony up additional money.

Does anyone else feel that this """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is used for activities other than sleeping?!

The staff seemed motivated only by money, did not exhibit any """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""customer service,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and there was a slew of policies posted at the front desk that are NOWHERE to be found on the website. This may be listed as a hotel, but it operates as a hostel. A cheap, bad one at that.

The Brookhollow Sheraton is a hotel with nice rooms, struggling with an unwinnable battle against its location. For me, as a person that used to live in Houston, being anwhere near the Galleria and the associated traffic is not a good thing. Additionally, being right on top of the --- loop and --- highway means that you get to listen to freeway traffic all night long. Now, some people regard this as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""white noise"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", and the blackout curtains do contain it to some degree, but I found it unpleasant. Also, the doors on the rooms don't seem to block any noise at all from the hallway, I could even hear the approach of the newspaper person every morning as they dropped papers in front of each room (around -am, slap, slap, slap). 
 Also hurting my impression of the hotel is that it is located in a corporate office - freeway wasteland, so you MUST get in your car to find food, and you will mostly find the usual Texas freeway chains (franging from Taco Cabana to Olive Garden and Chilis). Plus, the hotel is undergoing renovations, so during my stay the main hotel restaurant was closed, and the lobby smelled strongly of fresh paint.
 Which is all really too bad, because the bed, bathroom, and sitting area of the room itself are above average and quite new. That's always a complaint of mine in Houston, and this Sheraton was the first to do it right.
 Frequent Sheraton users will find the Club Level reception room is also above average, with free happy hour drinks and decent finger food along with a good business center. 
 So, for a few nights you will be fine and will enjoy the room. Any longer and it will start to be a drag, especially since you will only have about - channels to choose from on the TV...

Let's get the elephant in the room out of the way first - there is no AC. Luckily, the temps in BLT when I was there were in the --s. Yet i still asked for and quickly received a fan. The front desk acted startled that i mentioned the AC wasn't working but based on prior Trip Advisor reviews, I knew this was a real possibility. The room itself was very large - two large rooms make a suite, one sitting room that included a fridge, microwave, coffee maker, couch, large work area and flat screen tv, the other a long bedroom with flat screen tv. The bathroom was very small. The showerhead was the perfect height for me - but if you're over -'-, you'll need to duck to rinse your hair. Front desk staff and hospitality staff are very friendly, especially David on the top floor. Rooms are clean though showing some age. Also, no wifi in the rooms - just a cable. Views were good from the upper floor. Breakfast was adequate. Like i said, a lot to like but much room for improvement.

Stayed here for - days with my family and my brother's family. Four adults and four kids aged - to --. Everything about this hotel is superior. When ever I come to SF, I stay here. It is always a great stay and they treat you right and like a king. 
Rooms are clean and staff is great. this is a mush stay when in town...

I stayed five nights at this hotel on early March while attending a convention at Moscone Center. For this purpose the location is quite convenient, four long blocks away (about ten minutes walk).
Freaks and odd characters are part of the landscape in the area, buy I was never bothered and they were not different from the ones I saw somewhere else.
The room was clean, the queen bed was confortable, bathroom average, lighting convenient, furniture and heating not top of the line but adequate. There is cable TV and coffeemaker. Also there is coffee and a tray of danish rolls at the office.
The room is bad insulated, because you can hear slamming of nearby doors, steps of passers by and the TV and chatting of your neighbor next door.
Parking is free and one block away (-th and Harrison) stops a bus that takes you into downtown and the tenderloin area where you can find plenty of inexpensive eateries. The manager called Ricky is friendly, helpfull and shows to care about your stay.

I traveled to Chicago on the weekend of June -----. I was with a group of -, it was a special little Mommy-Daughter weekend. We stayed at The Palmer House Hilton and everyone absolutely loved the hotel!! Location was great!! This was my -nd time staying at Palmer House, and plan on staying again next time we visit Chicago!! Thank you!!

This hotel is perfect for young travellers who just need a place to sleep, and who have no needs far beyond that.
The rooms are basic but clean, the beds are comfortable, the bathrooms are clean with hot water but very small showers, and the front desk staff is friendly and helpful, but do not go """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""above and beyond."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Essentially, this is a two star hotel, fair and square.
Bring earplugs, as the walls are paper thin, and there is constant noise either from the street or from other rooms. Even just the people in the room above you moving around is enough to keep you awake at night, since it creates a loud creaking and thumping sound with every step they take.
The area is so-so. It is within walking distance to main areas and attractions, and cab rides are short and cheap from this central location, but I wouldn't want to be walking in the immediate area surrounding the hotel.
The best feature of this hotel is the restaurant. The staff is amazingly friendly, attentive and FAST! Service is top notch. The food is also great for what it is. Don't expect gourmet cusine, by why would you at a hotel of this callibre. It's homestyle American food, and it is good, with oversized portions (perfect for sharing!).
I would stay at this hotel again, but I would bring earplugs.

My wife and I went back to the Holiday Inn to see if things had changed. I can tell you that they made huge improvements. We were very happy witnh our stay this time. I hope they continue to keep up with the much improved customer servcie. The gentlmen that greeted us at the front counter was very friendly and helpful. The room was also very nice and clean. We could not have been happier! We now look forward to staying there again.

Read all the reviews on tripadvisor. It is a beautiful hotel and we were pleasantly surprised to be upgraded to a Junior Suite upon arrival. The morning coffee-tea and snacks are also a nice touch. Location is great, room was clean and comfortable. We will definitely be back.

This was the curt reply we got from a member of the front desk staff when we informed them we had booked a Queen room through our travel agent in the UK as part of our package. the luggage did not fit in the room if we went in there as well, no dress hanging space at all. We ended up piling up unopened cases on top of each other. Room dark, view not what we expected, looking straight into rooms across the alley: undesirable. We kept the curtains and windows shut, but the outdated air-conditioning kept waking us up. We were given a hanging rail for our clothes, but the only place to put it was to lift it over the bed and then down the other side - leaving only one side to climb into bed. Dingy bathroom (wooden shower tray was mouldy at the edges, and no door so we used one of our towels to stop water entering the bedroom). When we asked if we could have a queen room as booked, we were told the hotel was full, but we could upgrade for a supplement (??), plus the above comment. The best thing was the location: there is so much to do in NY but there are many cheaper and (in our opinion from previous NY experience) better quality hotels in the area.

I spent a great deal of time here while my mother stayed here on her visit to Boston. I used to be a hotel manager in Boston, and this is hands-down the best value you are going to get in the city, without question.
One great perk is the self-park, which means you can come and go as you wish, without having to tip a valet each time. Just make sure you bring the ticket that you receive entering the lot, to the front desk to have it validated each time. 
The pool area had a lifeguard on duty, which is quite nice if you have children and like having that extra eye on your kids. The pool area is basic but very clean. There are tables and chairs there and it's sort of like a little oasis in the middle of the city. We also had a room near the pool, but there were no noise issues.
The room is spacious and modestly updated. The only issue in our room was that the television was low, and not exactly in front of either of the double beds, but it was fine for us. 
While there is no breakfast at this hotel, if you walk one block west, you can find Dunkin Doughnuts and other places to eat. 
We did have a dog in the room, and there is an additional charge to have it in the room. Although this is of course not ideal, it is to be expected, considering that no other modestly-priced (under $----night) hotels in Boston even accept dogs. The housekeeping staff was pleasant and always greeted us whenever we walked in the hallways.
Best value in the city, with a great location as the icing on the cake. I am surprised that with how valuable real-estate is at this location, that it still exists and charges such modest prices.
I would absolutely recommend to anyone who seeks a basic, comfortable, value steps away from Copley Square.

The ladies were so nice, they offered so much for us for our - night stay. It is really cramped but it had all that we asked for. They are very welcoming and offer any kind of service they felt we needed. We had one bed with three people, but they brought in an extra roll up bed and extra restroom supplies. There was complimentary breakfast but it was simply beagles, boiled eggs, and fruit that you served yourself.

I hosted a bachelorette party at this hotel in one of their luxury suites. The hotel exceeded my expectations in everyway. The staff was extremely accomodating with all my requests. Kevin at the front desk was expecially helpful and friendly at check in. He had lots of great recommendations! The suite is one the best two room suites I've ever utilized. The master bath was fabulous. It had a very large shower, large soaking tub, separate toilet area, and two large vanities. My only complaint was the restaurant service. We waited for -- minutes before receiving service and when I complained no one appologized. They just shrugged it off like its normal to take an hour and half for breakfast. The food was delicous though so if you are not in a hurry I'd highly recommend it.

Amazing location in the heart of San Francisco, central to everything! The room was impeccable: clean, quiet, elegant, comfortable beds, high end linens and towels... definitely more than a - star experience. Staff was attentive, generous, everyone seemed to be enjoying their jobs. (There seemed to be a sense of pride and excitement, perhaps due to its recent remake into a Marriott.) We happened upon an amazing AAA rate online while browsing for hotels, made a few extra requests (they couldn't guarantee) like early check-in, extra pillows... and they met them all! The only things that we would have liked were a refrig-microwave (not standard in this hotel). We did use the well-equipped and -maintained fitness center and the guest laundry, but did not eat in the restaurant or bar area. The decor throughout the hotel was beautiful--bold vibrant color, modern designs--though understated (did I mention """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""elegant""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""?!)

Small room with two double beds. The window could only be opened with a maximum of my power, and I'm quite strong. Dirty walls with red handprint. Mould growing in the bathroom ceiling and on the floor. Bathroom door with severe moist damages.
But we did not see any bed bugs :-)
Location of this hotel is excellent.

Booked The Library solely off the Tripadvisor review and wasn't disappointed. If you want to stay in a particular neighborhood, then select elsewhere, but if you want to be centrally located so that you can get about easily, then this is a great place for you. A couple of points:
Easy parking a couple blocks away... hotel validation reduced the rate from $-- to $-- for --hrs.
Easy check-in... quick up to the room which was cozy (a nice way of saying small) but very nicely decorated.
Wine and Cheese from ---pm was a nice and inexpensive way to start the evening (very attentive staff)
-.- blocks to Grand Central for easy subway access.
Breakfast wasn't quite up to European standards, but it was a bit better than the standard continental breakfast (very attentive staff).
Checkout was a breeze and they held my bag until later in the day when we could get back from our sightseeing.
Hope that helps... happy travels!

My wife and I stayed at the Residence Inn Center City in November over a weekend when we visited the Renoir exhibit at the Museum of Art. The first thing that hits you at this hotel is the security. You need to use your room key to operate the elevator, that is, to get to any floor. I assume that the management considers this necessary and who am I to question their judgment. After all, upon signing in you have to sign an agreement promising not to party in your room.
After that introduction we approached our room with some trepidation, but it was in fact Marriott clean, although so strangely laid out that we felt like contortionists using the bathroom. This room would be good for one person, but there is just not enough drawer or closet space for two adults. This is a Residence Inn and the kitchen dominated the room. I have been in other Marriotts with kitchen facilities, but in this one I felt as if we were staying in a kitchen with a bed in the room. 
We used the fitness facility, but both elliptical trainers were broken, along with a treadmill. I got a recumbent bike and my wife got the one remaining treadmill, so we did manage to get in a workout. Less can be said about the wireless service. My laptop could not detect a wireless signal of any strength. I called the --- number that the hotel supplied, but it proved to be of no use. So business travelers need to know that the promised wireless service just isn’t there, at least on every floor. 
Breakfast was basic but fine and the staff attending the breakfast were wonderfully helpful and positive. In general the staff were very nice, except at checkout where a surly employee used a calculator to settle my bill. She did this for several minutes, removing the valet parking charges that my package took care of. She finally gave me a bill but called me when I got home to say that she had miscalculated and would be charging an additional amount to my credit card. This is a hotel that is hard to leave.

River Hotel is first and foremost - a great value relative to its location in the middle of Chicago's North Michigan Avenue-North State Street areas. It's close to everything. The rooms are definitely Courtyard quality. Serviceable and clean with fair amenities including free bottled water and WiFi. Service staff were friendly on our trip but as a former Chicagoan - I never asked them to find me a place to eat or attraction to see. The -nd Floor resident's lounge is great as is the health facilities. For the price - it's fabulous along as one calibrates expectations accordingly. As in most large cities, parking is expensive and not efficient! Use the great public transportation systems in the city or walk to a number of great restaurants or attractions. Also, the restaurant in the lobby is quite serviceable for a quick bite.

This hotel was very nice. Pretty new. Great location. Book the B&B package because the breakfast is not included without and it is really good! Well worth the price. Staff very nice. My only negative comment is the noise level. The AC - LOUD. The noise coming from other rooms through the walls - LOUD. The doors - LOUD. That is my only negative. Otherwise, very good stay.

This hotel is not up to the Hilton standards. It looks grandiose when you walk in; they have good reception from -:-- to -:-- and a good breakfast as well in the morning. The rooms however once you enter in are very dirty and look old. It is right to say that they are similar to the ones you will find in Motel -. The hotel just seems very dull and depressing. I will not be staying here again after my first visit.

Had a great - days at the hotel, valet was very curteous (thanks mike) and desk was equally helpfull thanks to all . Yes it is a little noisy but with double glass windows and a couple of margaritas sleeping was easy. breakfast was as described above. take a muffin or roll to your room, use the micro wave and you have a decent start to the day. What a location walk to Longs Drug at Horton Plaza for supplies ie beer, and check out all the activity around you. we enjoyed Ole Madrid, Napa Valley Grill, Ghiradellis, Buca de Bepo, all within - blocks. Will go back.

A special thank you to the front desk staff especially Tina, who played a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""blinder"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in sorting all our needs out.

The Hotel is within walking distance about (-mi) from all the museums. Great Food within walking distance. Room Service is fantastic and so delicious. The rooms are spotless and the beds are extremely comfortable. My dad and I stayed here for one night before an early departure from the Denver airport. We’d reserved a --bedroom --bathroom suite using his Priority Club points. (I haven’t often seen Staybridges—or any hotels, for that matter—that allow you to use points for --bedroom suites, especially for the same number of points as the more basic room types, and with no upgrade fee – but we were able to do that here, which was very nice!)
Check-in went totally smoothly. They found our reservation immediately, and were even able to put us on the top (sixth) floor when we asked if they had any suites of our type available there. The elevators were a little slow going up, but that wasn’t a big deal; it’s a system of two elevators, so there was never really a long wait for one.
The suite was clean as could be and had plenty of space. The first bedroom had a queen bed and a desk; the second had two doubles (no desk in that one). Each bedroom had its own bathroom, of course. The sinks were outside the actual bathroom, which can be good or bad… personally I think it’s kind of annoying, but when you have your own bedroom anyway, it doesn’t matter. One picky point, though: there was only one waste can in the entire bedroom area (including the bathroom). I feel like there should be a minimum of two – one in the bathroom area and one in the bedroom. I know that creates more waste, more work for the staff, etc. – but it’s kind of annoying and inconvenient to have to walk all the way into the bathroom (or wherever you move the waste can to) from wherever you are, each time you need to throw something away. That’s just a small detail that didn’t really detract much from the quality of our stay, but sometimes, the little things can actually turn out to be the big ones.
Shortly after we checked in and got settled in a little, we went downstairs and helped ourselves to the Sundowner evening social, where they have free food and drinks (even beer and wine) for the guests. They had hot dogs that night (which were great!), along with salad, chips, and lots of condiments and side items. (Another picky note: they had sweet relish to go with the hot dogs, but no dill relish. I’m definitely a dill person, but at the same time, I’m not going to sit here and complain about how they didn’t have one particular condiment for the FREE food they gave us!)
We had some laundry that needed to be done, so we took advantage of their free laundry facility. Boxes of Tide were just a buck each from the Bridge Mart (open ----), so Dad bought a couple of those and got the laundry started.
We then decided to go check out the pool. To be fair, I like my pool water a little warmer than I think most people do (I’m an upper --’s kind of guy, whereas I think most people prefer low to mid --’s), but I can tolerate it a little cooler. That being said, this water was just too cold for me to get in. My dad got in but said it felt cold to him, too. This hotel doesn’t have a hot tub, either… so, that aspect of our stay could have been a lot better, but we definitely didn’t let it ruin an otherwise great stay.
The hotel is located in an area with quite a few restaurants close by, but we were in the mood for wings and trivia, so we drove to the Buffalo Wild Wings about -- minutes away and got our fix – definitely worth it. When we got back, the parking out front was full, but they have plenty more behind the hotel, well-lit, with entrances to the hotel from the back as well (just don’t try to go in the pool entrance after it closes; I think it locks around -- pm).
Back in the suite, I got online and killed some time on the web. The internet was a little slow, but about on par for free hotel WiFi. (It was also super easy to connect to.)
The shower was great, with good pressure and plenty of hot water. The curved shower curtain rod was great for having a little more room.
I slept like a rock on that bed, too. (I was in the room with the - double beds, so I just had a bunch of my stuff piled on one of them and slept on the other; it was fantastic.) No noise to speak of or anything… didn’t hear any airplanes flying overhead, and wasn’t kept up by the HVAC system even though it was basically at the foot of my bed. (Interesting note: the living room and my bedroom were on a central air-heat system controlled by the living room thermostat, while the queen bedroom had its own room AC-heat unit [one of those below-the-window units]. I always like central better since it’s usually quieter, provided the HVAC system isn’t super loud [again, no problems with this one], so I was very happy with my room. I don’t think Dad had any complaints about his unit being noisy either, though, so I guess they’re both fine at this hotel. Just thought it was funny [but again, not in a bad way] that they mix-and-match AC-heating types within the same suite.)
Breakfast was great in the morning. Pretty typical selection for a free hotel breakfast – bagels, English muffins, hard-boiled eggs, yogurt, sausage, cereal, milk, juice and the like. I do wish hotels would leave the breakfast open past -:-- AM… most people who are there for leisure as opposed to business aren’t even awake at that hour! They should at least try --:-- or --:-- (and not just on weekends, either, since people travel on leisure all through the week – especially over breaks!). It wasn’t an issue for me this time since we were out of there by -:-- anyway to catch our flight, but it’s the general principle.
Check-out was a breeze. We had a rental car, so we didn’t have to use the airport shuttle or anything. The hotel is really close to the airport; we were probably to the rental car return within about --- minutes if that.
Overall, a pretty great stay. Would I come back again? Possibly… but I think I would probably check reviews of other nearby hotels on here first and try to find one with a hot tub and a better-heated pool. Not that I’ll be back at the Denver airport in the foreseeable future, but if I am, that’s probably what I’ll do. The Staybridge certainly wasn’t bad, but there are so many others in the area, I could probably find one (in the same price range and service level) that I liked a little better.

Liked: Staff is friendly, location very convenient.
