Didn't like: The hotel ordered a limousine service to the airport for me, saying there were no yellow cabs to be found. Fair enough. But, I ended up sharing with other guests. The driver dropped them off at La Guardia aiport, charging them $--. Then, he drove me to JFK, charging me another $---.

We stayed there for three nights. The hotel is conveniently located. The staff was really friendly and gave us complimentary champagne and chocolates on our arrival since I had mentionned it was our anniversary. They also have a daily complimentary wine tasting at - PM. The rooms are not big (it's NY) but well decorated and the marble bathroom was great. We had a top floor room with view of the Empire State Building and the city which was worth the price. It's not cheap but you get a very good value for your money and this is a great address to stay in Manhattan.
The property is located at a very convenient location in the Galleria area. The location is suitable for business and family trips. Very close to the Galleria Mall and restaurants.

We stayed at the Handlery for two nights. From other reviews we expected the rooms to be small, and they were, but very nice and clean. The hotel shows a little wear and tear but is well kept. Our view was not the greatest (of a brick wall and some sort of air vent) but were in San Francisco to experience the city not see it from our hotel room. The staff were wonderful, everyone was friendly and helpful. The location was great, close to all kinds of shopping and restaurants, and close to public transportation. Would stay there again and recommend it to friends.

This was an interesting place to stay. Last time I stayed in Seattle, we rented a car and it stayed parked in a garage our entire stay. Thanks to the other reviewers of Hotel Five, I saw we could take the Light Rail straight from SeaTac airport right to Westlake station - which is just a few blocks from Hotel Five! It only cost $-.-- per person verses a car rental or the $-- cab ride! The location is between the Space Needle and Pike's Place Market, so its a great location! One night we went to Zeke's pizza in Belltown near the needle which felt more local than touristy. (maybe it wasn't and we were blissfully ignorant, but to us it didn't feel like a tourist place!)
Hotel Five has an interesting decor. It seemed like IKEA set in Seattle. It had a lot of reds, bright yellows and reds. However, I don't stay in hotels for the day, so its not a big deal. When checking into our room, the outside of the room had a big handicap symbol right on the room number display. (and the numbers were big!) Gee. Thanks for making us feel so different and point that out to all the other guests that our room isn't like all the others. Honestly, what the hell is the point of making all the other guests know the room is """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""different""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""? Like someone in a wheelchair doesn't get enough stares anyway. I've never seen this before in a hotel and it was somewhat insulting.
Anyway, done with my rant. Back to the room. The floors don't have carpet, but a laminate which looks like wood. It had its pros and cons. The pro is that it felt much cleaner than carpet, but the con was that it could be very loud. Luckily we didn't have loud neighbors, so it wasn't a problem during our stay. They had the soap, lotion and shampoo dispensers. Unlike other hotels I've stayed, Hotel Five did a good job of not making them look tacky. The Air Conditioner was a wall unit, but I knew with the monorail and the floors, noise could be a problem. I brought earplugs with me so if you are a light sleeper, you may want to do the same. The room was decent size, but there are a few improvements I would suggest: 
-. They should have towel racks or hooks inside the bathroom for towels. I would have saved my towels from one day to the next, but there was nowhere to hang them! So, I just threw them on the floor and got new ones after housekeeping came which was very unnecessary 
-. Although it didn't rain on our trip, if you were wearing a wet jacket, there wasn't a hook at the entry of the room to hang it. Not sure where you would put a wet jacket. 
-. We were right next to the elevators. The constant """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""DING!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of the elevators was pretty loud. (louder than most hotels) 
-. Get a real door for the bathroom. The door was on a rail which slides back and forth along the wall - so it doesn't really lock or close tightly. This leaves a lot to be desired for better privacy.
Overall, despite the little issues, I would suggest staying here. It is right next to Top Pot Donuts which seems to be very popular. It is walking distance from the light rail from the airport, and walking distance to the Space Needle and Pike's Place. (plus it is much more reasonably priced that some of the other hotels in the heart of Seattle's downtown!)

Stayed at the Hyatt for - weeks and the staff couldn't have been nicer. From Cherry at the front desk, Philip the manager, Florence Concierge, and Jorge at the Bell Desk. Everyone did a fabulous job! We stayed in room ---- which had a very nice view of the Bay and Ferry Bldg. The location was wonderful! Could get on the Street cars, Muni, Trolley, and Bart just right outside of hotel. Would definitely stay here again! Thanks Hyatt you exceeded my expectations!

The best part about this hotel is the location. Two short blocks from the center of Times Square! There are Broadway theaters all up and down the street, even right across from the hotel! Wonderful staff, provided us with early check in and held our bags for us for a few hours after check out. The lobby is spectacular. Gorgeous chendelier and staircase. Elegant! It looks like a super expensive hotel but it's not. The rooms were modern and nicely decorated, although a little on the small side (BUT, this is normal for NYC! You have to expect small!) Bathroom was small. I felt like I was showering in the closet. But who needs a huge bathroom? You didn't come to NYC to take a shower, did you?!? Beautiful flat screen TV. Would stay here again!!!!

Stayed six nights.
Pros:
*Location: 
Easy access to --st street subway station with the -,-,- trains. If you need to go uptown or downtown on the west side, just take the train one stop down to Grand Central and use the S (shuttle) to Times Square and transfer to another train. Just be careful not to exit the subway station during these transfers (it's easy to just follow everyone else out the exit door without thinking).
Easy walking to Times Square and Central Park South (both about -- minutes).
Starbucks on the next block, Red Stone Pizzaria across from Starbucks, and Cafe Metro (pasta, salad, subs) a few blocks away.
*Quiet: Our room, ----, was away from the street and extremely quiet. Three small windows with views of the sides and roofs of buildings was the trade-off.
*Service: 
Front desk always friendly and helpful. We requested a rollaway bed and we were given the larger - double bed room to accommodate it. Again, no view in this room and it was subject to availability.
Jimmy, the doorman, also friendly and helpful. There were plenty of taxis continuously coming by and Jimmy would hail one quickly. The hotel also had cars and SUV's sitting out front for guests to rent. I took an SUV back to the airport so that we would have AC and more luggage room. The cost was $-- + tolls (the driver gave me a choice of bridge with no toll or tunnel with $-.-- toll). This was only $-- more than a taxi. 
*Room: Beds and pillows were comfortable (too soft for my taste, but most people prefer this). Shades were adequate to block morning sun. Closet with full-sized door mirror, disposable slippers, wooden hangers, ironing board & iron, free safe, and blow dryer. Flat screen TV. Coffee maker. Desk with comfortable chair. We also had two arm chairs, an end table, and one ottoman. The AC was adequate. The bathroom in our room was large with vanity inside.
Our traveling companions had the --th Floor Suite, which was large and beautiful and inlcuded amazing views from the wraparound deck.
*Business Center: Several computers and free access to internet for -- minutes to print boarding passes, but you have to click through the link on the home screen (one person in our party didn't see it and paid $--.-- to use the internet and then the browser didn't have the correct download to print the boarding pass, so be careful not to do it that way). Printing when going through the link was also free.
*Gift Shop: $- for a cup of coffee and she makes it for you in an expresso-cappuccino machine. Plenty of NYC souvenirs, but you will pay for the convenience.
*Elevators: Two sets of four that access different floors. Small, but fast service.
*Meeting Facilities: We did not use these, but saw a Bloomingdale's meeting with a Gucci step and repeat. Appeared to have very attentive staff.
*On-Site Restaurant: I had the breakfast buffet once during the stay, and the food was great. Plenty of choices.
Cons:
*Internet Fee: $--.-- per day and it is from noon to noon, regardless of when you first access it. I called and compained and no charge was on my bill, which I very much appreciated, since I only used it for a few hours. This policy is definitely something that needs to be changed!
*No Pool: But this is typical in NYC. The trade-off is the character of the older buildings.
*No Fan in Bathroom: Again, typical in older NYC buildings.
And just a side note about Marriott customer service: I first attempted to book this hotel through a link on TravelZoo, but there was a glitch on Marriott's site that wouldn't let me complete the transaction at the given price. I called Marriott and they actually gave me the room at a better price.

Overall, our hotel stay was good. It is in a great location, about a -- minute walk to Fisherman's Wharf. The breakfast area was nice with lots of tables, and the food selection ok. The bathroom was pretty small. Be careful of the parking garage. First, the parking fee is $--, and the parking is very tight. We had a minivan, and manauvering was very difficult. Also, there are two flights of stairs from the parking garage to the elevator in the lobby, so you will have to carry up all your luggage. You may want to consider unloading from the street out in front, before parking in the garage. Other than that, we were very happy with our stay, and with the view from out window.

This was a great value guesthouse located in one of Boston's quintessential Victorian brownstones. Newbury Street is a great base for exploring Boston and some of it's many great places to eat. The room was a good size (though the bathroom a little dated) and always clean, the staff were friendly and approachable, and the free breakfast in the morning was a good start to the day. We would definitely stay here again and recommend it to couples, solos or those on business trips.

My boyfriend and I stayed here last year for Thanksgiving and had a great time. The rooms were spacious with standard amenities. The hotel staff was very polite and friendly. We LOVED the continental breakfast. I especially loved that it was held at times I was actually awake rather than those breakfast that are held between ---am when I'm happily snoozing away. There was a good varitety of home-cooking type breakfast foods. We sat outside right by the dock during breakfast every morning and enjoyed the weather and the atmosphere. 
The location was great. We didn't have a hard time getting to the local attractions and I liked that we weren't in the thick of the tourist madness. The staff was helpful in giving us advice on what to do and directions for getting around. Being on the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""island"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" we felt like we were part of a smaller community. We would definitely stay again.

The Universal city Sheraton is a mix bag, 
We stay in a double bed standard room., the only positive thing about this room was the comfortable beds, other than that, notihng more,
the room was very CRAMPED, the restoom it¨s a joke, very uncomfortable, the toilet is located under the vanity table, so you can stay standing only in the front of the mirror and reach your hygiene items , like toothbrush, gel, etc.
The food of the room service restaurant is VERY GOOD, although very expensive, almost like go to dinner to Morton¨s or any other Gourmet restaurant at Sunset Blvd.
The valet parking guys are disorganizated.
For the next time That I will going to Universal studios, I will choose the next door Hilton

We were so happy with the choice of this hotel. All of the employees went out of the way to make our stay successful. The room was clean and plenty big enough for -. The beds were comfortable and the water was hot. There are stores and restaurants nearby and the hotel is close enough to walk to Central Park, Times Square and Rockefeller Center. I would definitely stay here again.

We stayed there for one night. better to stay two nights, because there is a lot to do in beautiful San diego.
The hotel was very nice and the room was clean.
We had the city view on high floor, which was nice- If you are getting a city view room, if it's possible ask for a high floor, because the train is very close...(we slept on the -th floor- it was ok).
It's very good location if you are getting on a cruise.
It also very close to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Seaport village""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""- a nice place to see.
And of course. the bay is amazing!

Come here before it gets expensive or too busy!
We stayed here because it was cheaper than all the other options we were looking at. I had heard that some of the older NYC hotels were a bit shappy so reasoned that here at least it would be new.
When our taxi dropped us off i must admit I didnt like the look of the area, but I'll qualify that straight away by saying we had no problems and it was actually great - we were a short walk from Hells Kitchen for great restaurants and Times Square, and right by Port Authority subway station which took you most places you might want to be.
The hotel is very futuristic and the amenities e.g. Wifi, aircon etc were all great. We had requested a room high up and away from the lifts based on other reviews on here, and reception personally selected our room on these criteria. 
The room itself was spotlessly clean (and kept so throughout our stay) and plenty big enough for the two of us. The mechanical bed was very cool and very useful in increasing room space.
I will admit i was concerned about the bathroom situation. I went with my husband but we are most definitely not one of those bathroom sharing couples. However my worries were unfounded. The curtain blocked off the bathroom area by sight entirely. The loo -shower had a sliding glass door so you rent merely separated by a curtain. And if all else fails, theres a bathroom on Four you can use!!!
Breakfast was a wide variety of coffee and muffins (plus other things if you wanted to pay). Muffins were delicious. 
If you stay over the weekend you also MUST do brunch. Its pricey at $-- but its all you can eat and drink over two hours from a menu of tapas style brunch dishes and cocktails. The brunch dishes were utterly to die for, especially the disco fries. The service was top notch and the cocktails kept flowing (and flowing!) throughout the sitting. We certainly got our moneys worth, and its beautiful to sit on the terrace.
The yobot is s fun and convenient way to store luggage after checkout.
We loved it and would stay here again in a flash.

I enjoyed this particular hotel immensely for various reasons such as it's atmosphere, style, service, and location. The staff was very welcoming and helpful to guests as well as supplying efficient service to us. This boutique hotel is exquisite in that the interior and exterior designs will blow you away. I personally enjoy the fact that each room is set up very prestigiously, each with an amazing view that you would undoubtedly enjoy. Finally, it's location is not too crowded and the area Nolita, where it's located, has distinguished character with many shops and restaurants. And better yet, it has Broadway street right around the corner if you're in the mood to be a tourist or a trendy shopper. All in all, the Nolitan is a must! It was made to be customized for its guests for an amazing experience in the Big Apple.

copley house is in a great location.. just two mins walk to nearest shop to get ur bits (bread milk etc). less than - mins walk to the Prudential centre & subway station. from here you can get anywhere in boston in no time. the house itself is an old building. no complaints though. was clean, comfortable & airconditioned. what more do you need

For first time visitors to San Francisco, the location of the Handlery Union Square could not be better. Public transport is easy and close and some places of interest and shopping areas within easy walking distance. Our room faced O'Farrell Street and, because it is a city, there was some noise, but nothing which greatly disturbed. It was spacious and clean. We had vouchers for breakfast in the Daily Grill and were well set up for the day following our meals there.

This hotel was absolutely wonderful from the moment my car service dropped me off in front of the hotel. A historical structure that has been lovingly restored from top to bottom. An elegant bar next to reception, terrific meeting space that avoids the bland spaces of other hotels, and my room was just spectacular. I even had a large window with a terrific view from my spacious bathroom. The concierge staff was extremely helpful as assisted in obtaining seats for me that evening at the opera house. A perfect introduction to the city of Detroit for this first-time visitor.

We stayed here on our first trip to New York and we were very pleased with the hotel.
Fantastic location as it is next to Grand Central Station and also a short walk to Times Square.
All staff were very friendly and eager to help.
Concierge was fantastic as they booked us on the Sex and the City Tour and also gave us great tips on other shows-tours to do.
I would reccommend staying here to my friends especially if they have never been to NYC
We were a little nervous about going to NYC but we felt safe the entire time we stayed at the Hyatt. Definately thumbs up!!!

Recently stayed at Club Quarters on Wacker. Initially I was very disappointed with the size of the room and the fact that it was NOT made up when I checked in. I admit I was anything but nice to the desk clerk Andreas but he handled the situation brilliantly, was very apologetic and gave me a great room facing the river. Well I couldn't be happier. He also gave me dining-sightseeing suggestions which made my stay indeed very pleasant. Would I go back? Definitely! And hope Andreas will be there.

I recently stayed at this hotel for a weekend where I planned for my friends and family to help celebrate my engagement to my long time girlfriend. I cannot begin to express how delighted the guests were with this hotel and the service. From the second we checked in to the last second when we left, the employees treated us like family. At the front desk, Eddie Ruiz and his partner Nelson did anything and everything in there power to make our stay beyond enjoyable. Every employee should strive to deliver the kind of customer service that these two gentleman delivered to our group. Overall, every employee that we encountered was very helpful and showed pleasure in doing so. The hotel design was gorgeous along with the location and cleanliness being second to none.
The W at Union Square is the best hotel I've stayed in NYC period!

We stayed for - days at this hotel at the tail end after spending a week in Palm Desert. Convenient and quiet location right next to the airport. Staff was good and the food in the restaurant was good. Clean, convenient, quiet and reasonable. Take the shuttle to Manhattan Beach for dinner. Had a great time.

We went to Chicago, booking quite last minute, through an online service. We arrived and were given keys to our room. We got up there, and it was not the layout we were told about. We had booked a suite with separate bedroom--everyone sleeps better that way when - little kids are involved! We called the desk and they instantly put us in an even bigger room than we had booked--what a great surprise! And service at breakfast and all around was excellent.

Located on Colfax Ave,which is the main street for sightseeing but this is at the slightly rougher end so be wary at night. Great location for every kind of fast food ----,although we liked Tom's diner a couple of blocks closer to the centre.
Walking half a mile or so down the street will bring you to the Capitol District which then leads to --th st mall and LoDo. We like to walk everywhere but it was accessible by bus and there was a free shuttle from the hotel to anywhere within a - mile radius (collection too). From the airport bus,you can get off at --th and Downing and get a free transfer on the no-- bus to opposite the hotel,very easy.
Rooms were clean,comfortable and nicely decorated. The lift was slow but we were only one floor up so used the stairs. Restaurant was mid-priced but there were plenty of places within easy walking distance. Likewise there was a ---- and a drugstore a block away for drinks and snacks.

This is the BEST JW Marriott I've stayed at. We stayed over -th of July weekend last year! GREAT activities, events, eateries and contests! 
The ROOM were gorgeous. I believe they just finished a $--- million dollar renovation!
My KIDS LIKE THIS HOTEL BETTER THAN - STAR hotels we have stayed at in Hawaii on the beach. I think that says a lot for a kid to want to stay in No. Phoenix w-o a beach ;) The lazy river was great because it was HOT in July! There were dance parties for the kids. Nickelodean activities at the pool--sliminator & crafts. Character breakfast with Sponge Bob & Dora. Dive in movies. Watermelon eating contests. Cake decorating contests. Bbq buffet that was DELICIOUS. And the restaurant ROY'S :P YUM-O The resort has so much to offer you don't have to LEAVE :) But if you do leave there is an awesome outdoor mall across the street w- Marshall's & other stores & movie theatre.
This is a GREAT MEGA hotel :)))) FRIENDLY workers too!

Typical - star hotel. I expected the hotel to be a bit closer to Union square. It is actuially on top of nob hill neat to the fairmont. Didn't think it was at all """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""worn"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" as some of the reviews say. I did notice a bit of noise. I could hear the doorman blow his whistle for a cab. -- minute uphill walk from Powell BART station. Overall good stay

Generally good hotel in very good location, near by Time Square. Breakfast room very tiny and usually here is no place to eat. But just noticed, that many-most of people take the food and move back to the room. Maybe this is a right decision. Breakfast selection is rather limited, but maybe this is normal for NYC hotels. We were family of - and booked one room with - double beds, but at least for us (and we are not very """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""big"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" people) beds was to narrow as to fit - persons comfortably. But maybe we should think about it in advance. Otherwise good hotel in very good location, clean, friendly, providing free internet. Concierge is helpfull in booking tickets or trips.

Had the opportunity to stay for several nights recently. Hotel is really phenomenal, contemporary, and a GREAT location. Our room however was the size of a closet with a basic furniture in the room making it nearly impossible for people to pass each other navigating the room. To enter the bathroom you had to pass by the door, open it, then enter depending upon which side of the bed you were approaching from. The bathroom could be defined as an excellent use of space, provided you were -' tall. Sitting on the commode, my knees actually touched the wall immediately in front of me.
When I addressed my displeasure with the accommodations with the manager on duty, he quickly spouted of a square footage requirement of the room with a pompous snooty attitude like it was a daily practice. There were NO free options to correct the situation other than a paid upgrade on top of the significant parking fees.
Significant street noise around -AM ... but it is the city. Also a lot of hallway noise penetrating the door.
What can I say, for that kind money and environment, the staff attitude was a real turn off! Considering the glut of rooms in the city right now, I would elsewhere in the future.
Found this Hotel through Trip Advisor. It was clean and the staff were wonderful. $----night in this area was a steal.

Excellent hotel with a great view of downtown Indianapolis. Conveniently located across from Victory Field, attached by skywalk to the convention center and only several blocks from the new Lucas Field host of Super Bowl XLVI.
The hotel staff is attentive and personable. Our room featured a well appointed king, tasteful furnishings, interactive TV, wonderful storage, both drawers and closet. Bathroom is adequate, however I'll warn to be careful in the shower as the door swings outward when balancing to wash your feet. There is in-room coffee and safe, but no frig.
Elevators are segregated by floor, so we used one dedicated to floors ----- and they were super quick, ultra quiet and never a long wait. The elevators require use of a room key to operate, great for security, a pain trying to balance coffee and bags.
The one oversight is that I've is only available on the second floor or through room service. We ate at the High Velocity sports Bar which was great.

love love loved this hotel. great service, friendly, beautiful rooms with lots of light and stunning manhatten views. really made our stay in manhatten special staying here. great restaurant attached to hotel too which is locals eat at too. highly recommend.
Service was great from parking,staff and breakfast crew. Enjoyed the walk to the Detroit Tiger Stadium to watch the game.

We were thrilled during a one night stay here on New Years Eve. This hotel has an excellent location: Close to Grandview, Short North, OSU, and Downtown. The area is very secure and I liked that the parking garage was free, and had limited entrances-exits to deter theft or vandalism. The exterior is very attractive, reminiscent of the style of the Arena District, and is a short walk to several restaurants and a gym in the same complex. 
The lobby and casual dining areas are spacious and stylish, showcasing clean modern contemporary design. There's a wide variety of places to sit and relax, and the colors and finishes make for calming and relaxing environment. It also has a small gym and indoor pool, which we enjoyed swimming in and viewing the December --st Ohio weather outside. 
The modern design flows into the rooms, which are likewise very spacious and finished in calming tones. The rooms are furnished and have a layout you'd expect in a hotel at a higher price point. An L-shaped sofa sleeper could seat --- guests comfortably while enjoying the --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" flatscreen television, which swivels for viewing from the living area or the bed, and a standard mini fridge is another nicety. As a tech-savy person I appreciated that they've built-in a panel beneath the tv with every type of port imaginable for hooking up an iPod, Playstation, or video camera. We also enjoyed the full size shower, which is a huge plus in lieu of a bathtub. Again, they didn't skimp on the finishes as they use granite and faux limestone through the bathroom and kitchenette area. Our king size pillow bed made for a wonderful sleep, and despite some partying going on throughout the hotel since it was New Years Eve, our room was very quite.
Overall I think this is the best value for a hotel in Columbus today. It's apparent that Hyatt has thought out the Hyatt Place brand's design well, and it's very appealing to adult or business travelers who appreciate style and frills at an affordable price. We can't wait for another stay.

I stayed in LA for two nights after deciding not to risk a short flight connection at LAX (which turned out to be a wise move). I booked at the Orlando after reading positive reviews and searching its location. 
The -rd story room was clean and impeccable and particularly noteworthy are the the bathroom, the generously sized TV (if that's important for you) and the responsive air conditioning. The bed was comfortable enough for me to oversleep on my first morning. 
The hotel's location on -rd St is convenient, being a short walk away from two notable shopping areas: the Beverly Center to the west (where I bought jeans and sunglasses) and the Grove to the east (where I caught a film). A cab ride to the main Hollywood blvd strip cost me ~$----- at night. On a corner a few blocks west sits an old inter-war bottle shop, its slanted roof reaching to the ground as walls. Whilst I'm sure many wouldn't give it a second look, buying beer and chatting to the humorous (Russian?) storekeep was a highlight of my trip. 
I appreciated the free WiFi though as others have pointed out, it can be flaky at times and on one occasion I couldn't get a stable connection to use Skype. My only other complaint would be that the hotel's ventilation is a little loud, although in my travels this seems to be a common feature across American hotels built in the last millennium. There was some bass emanating from the downstairs bar on the Friday night, although this didn't bother me too much. 
The staff were friendly when giving me directions and I booked a -:--am wake-up call on the morning of my departure which was gratefully received. The bellhop had no problems securing me a taxi and the trip to the airport cost ~$-- at that time in the morning.
(On that topic, as a result of my sleepiness and Australian upbringing I forgot to tip the bellhop until the cab had already left. The friendly man who was working in the early hours of August --th certainly deserved one). 
Overall, would stay again and recommend to anyone wanting to stay in the area.

I stayed at Hotel Seattle in ---- while I was in town for PAX Prime. The room my friend and I stayed in was smallish, but clean enough, it seemed. It didn't appear to have been updated in a few decades either. Our biggest complaint was the lack of air conditioning, or even a fan. We kept the window open at night which helped a little, but we were there in the middle of a sunshine-y, rain-free - day weekend. Barely even any cloud cover! Needless to say the room was warm, even at night. The water pressure was good, and it stayed hot. WiFi? Nope, only in the lobby. Nice flat screen? Nope, -- inch tube. Mini-fridge? Negative. Microwave? I'll let you answer that one for yourself.
Regardless, I didn't hate the hotel because of these things. I was there to experience Seattle so I did. We only came back to the room when it was time to retire to our little twin-size beds and maybe have a couple of beers before sleeping. If you're looking for a hotel with the most basic amenities at a decent price (I think we paid around -- bucks a night?) that's within walking distance of most things you'd wanna see, Hotel Seattle may be right for you. Just don't come in expecting the Waldorf.

This Hotel was very clean! Very good value. Because of hotel agreement we were able to use the indoor pool of the hotel next to it, which was a plus. Also had an outdoor pool. Stayed for two nights and would stay here again.

We enjoyed our stay at the Best Western hotel in July ----. It was a good value - great location. Really great spot for people watching. Just blocks from everything Theaters, subway, Times Square.Very clean, comfortable room. Lovely soft bed with puffy cover .Nice staff. Helpful bell station.Quiet--although we recommend asking for the backside of the hotel, Con--Small bathroom, but that's not unexpected in NYC.Restaurant--we didn't eat there but looked nice The bar prices on the high side. On the other hand, a glass of wine will cost you $- just about anywhere in NYC.Overall--We'll go back..

As a single grad student I was looking for an good quality hotel for a reasonable price in a good location. When I found a lucky catch deal for this hotel , I grabbed it and it was everything I thought it could be. Although I could not get the room facing the Bay bridge and the Port of SF, my room was clean and quiet. I slept like a baby on the bed, and I like how they isolate the bathroom. My - friends were kinda jealous of the good deal I got for - nights. The location is great ; you are right in front of California Street and Market street...you are right next to the CA street cable car, the Embarcadero BART and MUNI stations and the F Streetcar. The two major downsides are the Internet charge and the fridge charge...but I seldom use the hotel fridge and I went to starbucks or mcdonalds to check the Internet on my iTouch. But this is a hotel I would stay at again.

We needed a place to sleep for two nights--nothing fancy. The hotel is nice enough, but when a wake-up call we didn't request woke us at -:--am, I was annoyed. No apology from the desk, they just told me that they'd make sure it was disabled for the next night. 
The last morning we got breakfast and returned to the room to find that our key cards had been disabled hours ahead of schedule. We left for the airport late, first because we had to wait to get them reprogrammed so we could get our belongings, and then because when we tried to return the cards to check out there was no one but confused patrons standing at the front desk. I have stayed here the past several years traveling on business for a conference. I love this hotel.

Hotel George, if you are reading this note that some people still get freaked out by this. At least give us a fair chance by suggesting we take a cab ride after dark.

The modern bathroom and wet room are great and even though, as a single traveler this would not have been an issue, my bathroom had a solid door from the bedroom!

My partner has said it all in earlier review. She was right! I just want to add """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""all round excellence""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""!!! Keep room --- ready will return for sure. Shout out to Jay who sorted us shuttle to sfo at last minute

My daughter and I stayed at the Holiday Inn - Soho in January. Great location. Loved Canal Street! The staff was very helpful. Subway just down the block.
Room was clean - nice bathroom - concierge gave us great restaurant suggestions. Will be staying here again!

I have stayed at dozens of Residence Inns across the country and like them for the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""home-like"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" environment they provide. In planning our family vacation to Boston, I selected a Residence Inn because I wanted to have most of our meals in the suite. My daughter has severe food allergies and it is difficult to eat in restaurants. My expectation for the kitchen was to have a stove including an oven- something that i thought was fairly common in a Residence Inn. This unit has essentially a hot plate and a microwave. For most folks, this would probably be perfectly fine but again I planned to cook meals. Unfortunately the icemaker in the refrigerator was broken and could not be repaired during our stay but the kitchen gave us a bag of ice. This is not a criticism but rather a failure on my part to research the property better.
I made this reservation in April and at the time there were no two bedroom units available. I continued to check the reservation site for a two bedroom but none ever became available. I reserved a room with two queen beds to accommodate my husband and I and our daughter. Upon checking in, I learned that there are only eight rooms with two queen beds and all of these rooms overlook the busy Charlestown bridge road. This property has a very limited number of two bedrooms and I learned upon check in that for the most part, these are never available. Again, not a criticism but poor research on my part.
Overall this property is fine, the location is lovely, the staff was friendly and willing to help. I would recommend it to someone visiting Boston who did not plan to cook in their suite. We did not participate in any of the food service - breakfast and snacks but the area was always very busy so it must have been good. 
At over $---.-- per night, I expected more.

This is an excellent place to stay for Thanksgiving weekend and the parade as the parade passes directly in front of the hotel. We have also stayed at the Mandarin-Oriental at Columbus Circle which is also an excellent choice but the view for the parade is better at Trump. They have a great viewing area for hotel guests only...make sure you make reservations for breakfast early at the restaurant or just order in room as the restaurant will be reservations only.
The suites are roomy and have a more than adequate kitchen...request a Central Park view and you will not be disappointed. The staff are excellent and the location ideal!

We spent - nights at the hotel which is the perfect initial point for sight seeing and shopping.
 Pros:

Cons:

I stayed here with my wife and daughter as part of a 'split site' holiday between San Diego and Las Vegas. We stopped for -- days and travelled with some concern about the comments made about the hotel by other guests on this and other sites. We are used to stopping at --- star hotels in Europe and this certainly did not compare. However we never expected it to and in truth it provided good value for money. It was clean, had a decent pool and the staff were very pleasant and helpful. The small restaurant was perfectly adequate for breakfast (we never sampled the evening meal but the menu looked ok) Some reviewers have commented on the hotel's poor location. I can only assume they did not have access to a car. We found it was ideally situated to explore all parts of this very large and interesting city. It is very close to - shopping malls and numerous restaurants. Indeed the Fashion Valley Mall is within walking distance of the hotel. I would wholeheartedly recommend San Diego as a holiday destination and if you are looking for a relatively low cost base to base your holiday on would unreservedly recommend this hotel.
The hotel was close to everything. Rooms were fine. Food - bar were both fine. Service was good and people were amazingly friendly.

The Mariott Courtyard at Hotel Circle was not my best hotel stay, particularly in view of the fact that it was located in the heart of a center with hotels catering to conference attendees. Good Point: The room was nice, clean and attractively furnished. The room had a refrigerator and coffee maker, but no microwave oven. The bed was comfortable. 
Bad Points: This was a business trip booked by my employer. The front desk was not helpful in straightening out booking errors. Amenities: -. There was no room service available. -. The food service was poor. It did not have a real restaurant. You have to stand in line to place an order for either take out (a la McDonald's) or you were given a number and the food was brought to your table. -. During the moring hours when guests were disbursing to meetings and trying to grab breakfast on the way, the line at the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""restaurant"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" had as many as -- or so guests attempting to place their orders. The choice of food for breakfast, lunch and dinner was very limited. There was a tiny little shop with no attendant (had to pay at front desk) when you wanted to purchase a limited array of food and other items. -. There was no cocktail lounge. Mind you this is a hotel with several hundred guests. Not my worst, but not my best hotel stay.

What a dump this place turned out to be. This hotel (should really a motel) is old and it shows in the condition of the rooms and corridors. The carpeting in the room and hallways are very dirty. Keep your shoes on! My room had no mini-fridge, and no microwave. The clock radio won't turn off; I had to call room service twice before someone came up with a new one. The bathtub drain ran so slow that when I finished my shower, the water level was at ankle height. The only good thing I could say is that the linens were clean.
This hotel is sort of in the shape of a capital H. Do not accept a room in the middle (horizontal) part of the letter. This part of the hotel can only be reached via an external corridor. It is, in my opinion, the most neglected part of the hotel. At night, the corridor is not lighted. I didn't even feel comfortable walking through there.
Also, the prices they charge are outrageous! $-.-- for a bowl of cereal, $-.-- if you want sliced bananas with it!!! All outgoing calls are $-.-- each regardless of whether it is local, toll-free, or calling card. Parking is $---day.
In conclusion, if you want a hotel close to LAX, I wouldn't choose this one. There are lots of other hotels nearby.

I stayed at the this hotel while on business for a period of five days (four nights). A complete set of towels and wash cloths were next to impossible to find. The cleaning staff did a lack luster job, leaving trash in bins, failing to vacuum anything and on two occasions left the TV on after leaving the room. The indoor-outdoor pool was disgusting, having not been properly cleaned in some time. Above all else though was my experience with the Staff. Often sloppily dressed, they exhibited a sense of not caring what-so-ever to the guests. To make matters worse, when politely asked for a copy of my receipt for the nights spent there, I was given a copy with a smile and cordial tone, nothing seemed out of the ordinary. Later, at my place of business, I was confronted by my supervisor with a complaint from the Hotel, accusing me of being belligerent and demanding. No such incident happened, and as far as I could tell, there was no animosity between myself and the counter staff whom I interacted with. My character is now in question with those whom I work for and since there were no witnesses to the supposed event, I've no way of refuting the claim except for my word. If this is the level of courtesy and professionalism that Wingate and Wyndham hotels has for it's guests, (poor cleaning service, false accusations from hotel staff, and lack of care attitude) then I can never in good consciousness recommend them to anyone I know as a option for any length of stay. There are several other , higher quality hotels on Airport Road Jacksonville at lower prices, that provide a much better experience. I strongly recommend seeking one of those out instead.

The hotel had just been taken over by hilton prior to our stay. The rooms was very small but well equipped and also an extremely comfy bed and a great coffee machine. There was a bar on the ground floor which was very pricey that also served food which was also on the expensive side. The location of the hotel is fantastic, literally - minute walk to the UN buildings and also just a few blocks from the stunning chrysler building. Seeing that every time i left the hotel in the morning was worth the price alone. Also close to grand central station and times square. Also enjoyed the free newspapers every day.

My mom and I stayed at the Affinia last weekend for a girls trip to NYC. We are frequent visitors to the city and generally stay in a different location and different hotel every time we go. This time we chose the Affinia because they were offering a good deal on their website and we liked the location. 
The best part of this hotel is the location. It is right near Penn Station so you can easily jump on the subway and travel to all of the various boroughs. It is also walking distance to Times Square, Herald Square and Madison Square Garden. We walked to and from a show in the theater distract but took the subway to get to Chelsea and the Upper East Side. It was very convenient.
The concierge and receptionists are very friendly. Upon arrival we received a complimentary upgrade to a room with an additional couch and office space. The room had a nice layout and great space. There was plenty of closet space for our coats and a nice sitting area as well.
The bed was very comfortable and the decor in the room was modern and looked recently updated. Our only complaint was the size of the bathroom which was literally smaller than the closet space. You could barely turn around in the shower and literally could not fit more than one person in the space at one time. Because there was only two of us traveling and staying in a room, it was not a problem but definitely do not expect a huge relaxing tub or anything of the sort in the standard size rooms.
The bar at the hotel was always hopping and a really cool place. Our room was on the -th floor and was generally quiet. There is also a Starbucks right across the street so you can grab a quick coffee before you hit up Macy's which is right around the corner (your key to this hotel gives you a --% discount). 
All and all a good stay in a great location. For the price, it is definitely worth it.

I visited Jacksonville for a conference at the Hyatt. Being a student and trying to cut costs, I won this hotel with a $-- Priceline bid which was much more palatable than the $--- a night that the Hyatt wanted. This hotel is in the downtown area and is quite a ways from the airport. I noticed that the GO Shuttle (Florida Limo I think) offers some sort of shuttle service ... might be worth looking into as cab fares seemed to be about $-- or so from the airport.
Arriving in the evening, my first impression of the Wyndham was a positive one. I was promptly greeted at the desk and check-in was a smooth process. It was noted that the hotel needs a credit card on file and places a hold per night ... I found this odd since there didn't seem to be a lot of spending opportunities in the room (minibar,etc). This wasn't much of an inconvenience, though it might be if I relied on a debit card.
I was quickly checked in and given a King, non-smoking room on the third floor overlooking the river. This was a very nice room and it seemed as if a good attempt had been made to make it look presentable for check-in. When I entered, lights were on as well as the AC, keeping the room cool for my arrival. The room was fairly clean overall, though there was a bit of noticeable dirt near the door area.
The room itself was spacious with a king bed, work desk, work chair (with outlets and lab tables), wardrobe, closet, and safe. The hotel offers free wireless internet which was very nice if a bit slow at times. The worst part of the room is the bathroom which, from all similar hotels I've stayed at (Wyndhams that used to be Adam's Mark), is tiny. The sink was separate from the bathroom itself with plenty of room, but the bathroom included just enough space for the stool and a tub ... this was so small, in fact, that you have to step into the tub to shut the door.
Housekeeping was good for my --night stay, straightening up and replace bath products (Bath and Body Works) and coffee (Wolfgang Puck). I was always left plenty of towels.
The rest of the hotel was fine. On the last night of my stay, Friday, there was noticeably more noise from the lobby area and quite a few more kids who liked to slam doors and run up and down the hall. I did not make use of any of the on-site restaurants as they seemed to be typical and overpriced like many hotel eateries.
With that being said about the restaurants, however, there is not much in way of cheaper food in the area. The two closest restaurants are a Morton's Steakhouse and a Ruth's Chris ... definitely not budget eateries. I did not notice any fast food or drug stores in the immediate area for food-snack purchases.
As for the area, I heard some quite negative things concerning safety. My experience was that the streets were mostly empty. It was about a ----- minute walk to the Hyatt across the bridge which was very straightforward and reasonable. A couple of times I also cut across the street and through the Hampton Inn parking lot to the Skyway station to take a tram across the river ($.--). I also took a walk to the San Marco area in the other direction one night for more food options (there was a Jimmy Johns and Subway that way). I never ran into any problems on the street at night (hardly saw any other pedestrians as a matter of fact), but the locals seem to think it's not the best area, so keep that in mind. I used the free wireless to order Pizza Hut one night and it was delivered to the room ... cheaper than the hotel pizza.
In the end, this was a fine hotel with some positives and some drawbacks. It filled my needs nicely, so I can't complain.

We spent a weekend in Chicago and stayed at the Omni Chicago Hotel. It was perfect. The hotel is close to everything we wanted to do and see. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful and the room was outstanding. I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a great place to stay in downtown Chicago.

We loved staying at the standard. We had amazing views of the Hudson river. The deep big bath is great after a big day out in New York! And the beds are very comfortable! The staff are really friendly and allowed us to check in early after a long overnight flight. We loved everything about the hotel and will definitely stay again when we are back in New York. We also went to the Standard Grill for breakfast and dinner and thought that the food and service was high quality.

First, I booked on Orbitz, and ended up overpaying. If I were to stay again, I'd book directly through the hotel.
It's not bad. It's a hostel, so it's a little run down, a little communal, but the staff was extremely nice and helpful. I didn't mind the shared bathrooms - they were clean. The tv was wasted space in the room, as the reception was non-existent. 
I was worried about the door to my room - very flimsy with holes in it. There's no way it would have kept anyone out if they wanted in. Thus I was nervous about leaving my things, and ended up paying to keep my valuables in a locker in the basement.
I'd book again in a pinch, it wasn't so bad.

Stayed there recently on a business trip. Check in line was long so used the kiosk to check in ... worked great. Rooms are a good size and bright. You have access to the health club adjacent to the hotel with great work out facilities and a pool which is nice. You are - min walk to china town and great places to eat. Would recommend it for business travel.

I stay at the hotel frequently for business trips to Chicago. I have found the service to be prompt, attentive and accommodating. Rooms are very clean and modern with flat screen TVs. There is an excellent restaurant in the hotel (a little pricey these days). Great access to Greektown and Chicago's west business loop is a short walk across the Kennedy expressway.

Keeping this quick and simple, as much of my comments have already been said. 
Nice hotel, with recently upgraded and remodeled rooms. Convenient location, especially if you need to be close to the SJ convention center. VERY hit-or-miss service with the valet and front desk staff. However, the concierge and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""At Your Service"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" operator are great.
I did want to underscore another reviewer's comment regarding value. This place really does nickel + dime you for every little thing. For example, the going rate for internet access at most hotels (and nearly all the other Marriott hotels) is $-.-- a day. At the SJ Marriott, it's $--.-- from noon until noon. Making a toll-free (---, ---, --- #) call? That will cost you. Forgot to pack toothpaste? The hotel will provide some but you'll see on your bill later that they charged you for it. 
Finally when booking at this hotel, or anyplace in downtown SJ for that matter, is keep the cost of parking in mind. The hotel only offers valet parking which is $-- a day. Parking next door at the convention center is $---day with no in and out privileges. There's also a $-- and $-- lot a few blocks away. Overnight street parking is not allowed in downtown SJ without a permit.
All of this just adds to the overall frustrating regarding value for your money because so many other hotels include these things as part of the guest experience (or just aren't as expensive).
BTW, this is coming from someone who travels for a living and is away from home ---+ nights a year, so I have quite a bit of perspective on this.

We arrived very late from the east coast and just needed someplace to lay our heads before going on to San Diego in the morning. Checkin personnel were abrupt to the point of being rude. Room was adequate. This is an airport hotel and I have never paid for parking at an airport hotel even at JFK, but they make you pay throught the nose here. I don't remember if the internet was free. They have a big TV and smaller ones in the lobby bar where we watched the World Cup. Overall, just an ok stay for the price- I'd look elsewhere next time.

We were just in town for a few hours and needed a place to stay, so for the price and the great reviews on here, we decided to stay at this hotel. The lobby looks like it's been newly remodeled and is very nice, but the rooms could use some updating. Breakfast in the morning was good, but they ran out of the hot meal and ended up just putting out some warm biscuits even though there was still an hour+ left in the breakfast window. We were more than satisfied though with the other options. Our service was excellent at check-in and later that night when we made a request to the front desk. Rooms could use a little more cleaning, but that may just be because things are older and they look a little worn. Overall, if you don't mind a little outdated room, for the price and the location I'd recommend staying here.

Last August I stayed at Warwick hotel in San Francisco. I must confess that if I ever have to look for a hotel in the future this one will be one of the last on my list. 
First of all on a plus side: 
-. Location is good. It’s located just few blocks from the Union squire.
-. Hotel employees are very helpful.
 Minus side:
-. Rooms are very small. I didn’t see all the rooms, but the one we stayed at was very small. And we are not talking about a budget motel, but pretty overpriced one.
-. Bathroom is very small too.
-. This hotel chain claims that they keep Victorian style and it’s true. The only problem is that it looks like a cheap Victorian style from a second hand furniture store.
Overall you just pay for location. And be careful! Even at this nice location, the area is full of beggars especially at the evening time.

stayed here one night in june. usually stay at w lakeshore. prefer lakeshore as there just seems to be more going on there. this place was nice, but something just seemed to be missing. perhaps it was lack of a nightclub-bar...not sure. vibe was quiet, not happening. the space is cool, but overall i think there's better.

The hotel is at the top end of Market Street which is some way from Fisherman's Wharf but a streetcar will take you there in -- minutes or so for $-. There is some good bars and places for food very close by. It is also reasonably close to the financial district, shopping district of Union Square, and the famous Haight-Ashbury area. If you have any questions or need any assistance the staff are more than happy to help. Couldn't fault the staff actually, they were very friendly and extremely helpful. The rooms are on the basic side and can be a bit noisy due to traffic but this would definitely not stop me staying here again as I slept with no problems at all. All in all, good value and a comfortable stay.

Located in a surprisingly quiet street, still close to Central Manhattan this hotel is an excellent base for exploring the big apple. Walking to Times Square takes less than -- minutes. Room was small, but the standard not too bad (bathroom a little cold in December though). Staff was friendly and offered useful information about restaurants and nearby sights, and room was cleaned every day + tidied up in the evenings. We missed a breakfast room or a coffee shop within the hotel, but there was much to choose from within a five minute radius.
Recommended for a laid-back stay in NY, but would choose something different for the big occasions.

The location is excellent, close to green and orange T stations. 
The reception staff is is most friendly and helpful. 
Room was nice and very clean.
I would definitely recommend Hotel --- to anyone.

I was at first very excited about my stay at the Seaport Hotel, hoping it would be excellent. My first problem was stained sheets. I told my husband they looked as if they had been laundered, but the BROWN stain made me have doubts. The plug in the tub did not work properly, so no bubble bath. The AC in the room did not work well. Although the temperature read as if it were ok, it was very hot and I had trouble sleeping. This discussion came up from another person that I met while at a seminar there. They said the same thing about their room and suggested that I turn the fan on to run all night. This did help. The next night, I ordered a bottle of wine through room service. The cost was to be $-- plus taxes and delivery fee. I was charged $--. I called room service to go over the problem and got no resolution. I had to take the bottle downstairs along with the price list that was in the room. I did get partial credit but not a full credit. WHY? Is it really that hard to calculate? Charge what you post and don't false advertise. I called twice before arriving to double check that the room charge would be put on the corporate card and was told both times, yes, it would. Didn't happen, I had to use my personal card and get reimbursed from my company. The only thing that I enjoyed about my stay was the food. The food was excellent and maybe the best breakfast I ever had in my life. I will say that I did request that maintenance fix the plug in the tub. They did, and I was able to take a bath my second night there.

My wife and I stayed at this """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Best"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Western while she had a course at CHOP (Children's Hospital of Philadelphia). It was the worst place we have stayed in for a long long time. On check in the computers were down and it took at least -- minutes to get a dirty, slimy room. The halls were dirty, everything reeked of smoke and the room on the second floor was more like a jail cell than a hotel room. The front desk lady acted like this was the norm for $--- a night. The ceiling in the bathroom looked like it would fall down any moment. When asked for directions and timing to the Barnes Foundation the front desk woman stated it would take at least an hour to get there when actually it was a -- min. drive. Another woman in my wife's course called and told me she had to change her room because the bed was infested by bed bugs and she actually looked like she had the measles. Beware of this dump...I will never stay there again. I actually will report this place to the Philadelphia Board of Health. Tear it down and start over...the neighborhood is too nice for this blight.

I wasn't going to write a review so didn't take many photos but now I feel obliged to warn any potential guests.
We stayed at the hotel last week & now deeply regret not choosing a different one closer to the centre. However there is a subway outside Marrakech with line -, - & - taking you to the centre in about -----mins but add another --mins for walking in the subway maze. It is a waste of time AND money as the transport in NYC isn't cheap. One ride is $-.-- but on a Metro card is $-.--
Now the hotel itself.
The check-in was fairly quick as there were no other guests at the time but the attitude of the receptionist wasn't what we expected. After checking our room I politely asked if it was possible to change the room but I was refused & told all rooms looked the same. Really?!
We paid $--- for - people, - nights. Overpriced for what we had.
Our room was extremely hot as there's no aircon, very small & there was NO wardrobe to hang the clothes!! just - hangers on the door. Barely any place to move around. The view from the window was... a dirty yard & a brick wall.
The bed was reasonably comfortable but our sleep was disturbed by the annoying noise of some machinery sounding like an ancient air conditioning wannabe from the outside. We had to sleep with an open window as it was unbearably hot. Also the staff seem to make A LOT of noise at -am waking us up every morning.
The bed was made everyday but the sheets were changed only once in - nights we stayed there.
The bathroom was small but fairly clean however I would recommend wearing flip flops in the shower as the floor looked dated & cracked. The towels were changed daily but there was only - face towel for two people on the first night.
The lighting in the room is very dark so forget about reading a book in the evening. 
The room seemed to be cleaned (?) everyday but definitely not hoovered as we kept finding the same rubbish on the carpet every night and we also found A DIRTY SOCK from a previous guest under the bed! 
The only place in the hotel we liked was its lobby - it had a nice Moroccan interior, - small TVs, no bar. Wifi was available only in the lobby but we seemed to have a connection in our room too.
A very important information - there is no lift meaning you have to drag your heavy suitcases to the - floor!! The stairs are narrow & if not careful you can fall easily.
The hotel offers no breakfast but there are plenty places to eat around & a Starbuck downstairs. We recommend Broadway Bagels - mins walking from the hotel, just turn left, its on the corner of ---nd &---st street or Absolute Bagels on ---th Str. on the right from the hotel. There are few decent restaurants around to eat your dinner at in the evening.
All in all I would never go back there & advice others to think twice before choosing Marrakech as its overpriced, far from the centre & hostel like.

My husband and i stayed at Chelsea Pines Inn for -- nights in June. From the moment we first walked in and met Jay, we knew that it was going to be a great place to stay. Our room was on the -th floor of the hotel which had a lovely view of the hotel gardens, our room was very spacious which was exactly what we needed for a -- night stay. The breakfast every morning was great also. 
The location of the hotel is unbeatable and we just loved staying in this part of the city.
There are so many things to do around the Chelsea area, so many great places to eat and drink and the subway is basically at your doorstep aswell. After each day of exploring the city, coming back to the hotel was like walking into another world, away from all the craziness that is NYC, it was a whole other experience which we loved! 
Because we were staying at Chelsea Pines Inn for -- days we got to know the staff quite well which made it feel even more like home, especially having Charlie there. They always had time for a laugh and a chat with us no matter what. They helped us with tickets for Broadway shows and recommendations on restaurants and things to do in the area. We couldnt imagine getting this type of service anywhere else in NYC. 
We cannot speak highly enough of Chelsea Pines Inn and all the staff are awesome: Jay, Al, Troy, Betty, Rumel and everyone else there. We have so many great memories and stories from our stay here, it really is a special place, a home away from home, which made it even harder for us to leave.
We will be back for sure, and If you really want to experience NYC, stay here because you wont be disappointed, these guys ROCK!!!

Incredibly clean! The rooms are small but the space is very organized. The location is great and I'd definitly stay there again. I stayed in a double bed room with bathroom so I can't give my opinion on the shared-bathrooms.
Awesome location in the gaslamp district. Hoel isvery nice and modern. Kids loved the pool area.

stayed - nights mid august. fantastic hotel. quiet and all staff really accommodating. ability to pop back during day for coffee or water certainly a bonus as well as wine and cheese late afternoons gave us time to sit and review our day and plan for the nights ahead. will highly recommend to anyone going to nyc. really could not fault it.

The large double room easily accommodated - rollaways, making it possible to fit our group of - in one room, a la slumber party. They thought ahead and provided plenty of toiletries, towels and pillows.
The location can't be beat. I don't like to pay for parking but in the city where Parking Wars is filmed, $-- for our SUV was not too much to pay. We could walk to the waterfront, the busy happenin' streets nearby with restaurants, bars and ice cream and the Big Bus stopped a block away if we wanted to tour the city. The concierge was VERY helpful and got the Big Bus to send their trolley to pick us up.
DISCLOSURE: I publish TravelingMom.com and was comped this room as part of a press trip. THe review of the room and hotel is my own and cannot be bought.

We stayed at the Four Seasons - nights in early October. We have had the good fortune to travel extensively and have stayed at some of the best hotels in the world. This hotel has outdone them all. At check-in the reservationist came out from behind the counter to give us our keys and take us to the elevator. The bellman was already ahead of us with our luggage. The service here sets the standard for all hospitality businesses. The staff, food, and ambiance at Culina are first rate. The spa is fantastic -- quiet, elegant and staffed by people who make you feel so comfortable. I highly recommend a lady named Dallas for a facial. Off-site we had lunch at the Ivy and also dinner at Villa Blanca. It's not unusual to spot celebrities at these restaurants. When we were leaving the hotel, the valet attendant noticed we had a low tire and took our car and added air to the tire before we drove off. I would live here if I could.

I recently stayed here for a conference that was taking place next door at the Convention Center, and my husband tagged along to spend some leisure time in Seattle.
Location
The location is excellent for easy access to the Convention Center, but about a ----- minute walk from Pike Place Market. Having said that, I was able to walk everywhere I needed to for various receptions (at Columbia Center, Benaroya Hall, Seattle Art Museum) and for shopping (Nordstroms), and even Pike Place was a short pleasant stroll away. We were even able to walk to outdoor gear mecca REI in less than -- minutes. If you are a tourist looking for a waterfront view, however, this location will not deliver.
Value
I paid a slightly discounted rate as a member of CAA-AAA, and the price included a studio suite with king bed and kitchen (full fridge, microwave, stove top, but no oven), a full buffet breakfast, and a light dinner on weekdays. The breakfast is standard buffet style, and does get a bit repetitious after a number of days, as there is no cooked-to-order omelette, unlike at Embassy Suites (another member of the Hilton family). But it is certainly better than most coffee-and-doughnut type offers from other hotels. I did not partake of the light dinners, but my husband did, and he said they were OK as well.
Service
This is where the hotel could use a bit more polish, but I suppose there is a reason that Homewood Suites generally rates below the flagship Hilton brand and its sister Embassy Suites brand. I had checked in a day before my husband arrived, and the day of his arrival, left the extra room key in a sealed envelope with his name on it at the front desk, explaining everything clearly to the front desk staff. The person took it and said it would not be a problem. But when my husband arrived, he had to phone me to see where I was, as the extra room key was nowhere to be found. In my opinion, its not worth the $----night or so they ask for a room, and certainly not a --star quality hotel. If you are offered a deal at less than $--- and don't mind an uncomfortable bed for a couple nights, this place will do.

... we come back here. We've been here for my --th, --th, and --th birthdays. The first time, it was called the Hyde Park suites. If you are considering this property be forwarned that the walls are paper thin and that you can literally hear with great clarity and detail the conversations of those in adjacent rooms. We stayed at the Drake during the Labor Day weekend and loved it. We had a King Suite which was wonderful and a great deal for the price. The view of Michigan Avenue and Lake Shore Drive was beautiful. We also watched two marriage proposals in the park across the street - both successful if the reaction was any indication! My wife and I have decided to make the Drake our destination every Labor Day. The breakfasts in Drake Brothers were very good and tea in the Palm Court was an unexpected joy. But the best was the Coq d'Or. It has always been one of our favorite bars in the world (and we have visited more than a few). For lunch my wife had a potpie about the size of a deep dish pizza! I had the Bookbinder Soup, a roast beef sandwich and home made sorbet; my mouth still waters when I think of that meal. If I had to choose one thing that sets the Drake above most other hotels in Chicago and around the world it would be the quality of their staff. The customer service - from the bellmen to the front desk staff to housekeeping to the waitstaff - is the standard by which all hotel staffs should be measured. I can hardly wait to go back next year.

This hotel was an amazing experience for us on our Chicago Valentine's Day trip. The staff was courteous, our king room was spacious and VERY clean, the hotel itself was a great surprise, very high end and chic looking without the HUGE price tag you would see from other hotels of that nature. The valet service was great and the location could not be better. We will be recommending this to our friends and family! Thanks Allerton!

With the package I parked my car at the hotel, took a hotel shuttle to LAX, flew to Seattle, came back on a late flight one week later, took the hotel shuttle to the hotel and had a very restful night's sleep before driving home. We received a very warm welcome late at night after a very long fight from Australia (two very tired travellers)! Everything was great: the folks at the door and in reception, the very clean room, and the location. We didn't eat at the restaurant but did have late night drinks in the bar which was very pleasant. Would definitely stay here again if we got it for the right price?

They also serve coffee-tea there all day, which was nice. The room was smallish, as expected,but very clean. We were on the --th floor so no trouble with noise from Watts St. which is very busy at rush since it is the entrance to the Holland Tunnell. The only thing that bothered my sleep was the loud HVAC sytem.
The hotel is in a great location...walking distance to close to many restaurants, shopping, and the red line which we used to get up and downtown.
We would definitley stay here again

This property resembles a motel - not at all a resort feel. OK for my purposes but I certainly would try another inexpensive place to stay if I had to be in San Diego for a few days again. Internet was very slow and non-existent frequently. It didn't improve even after reporting the difficulty to guest services.

Stayed here for a work conference, was utterly delighted. My single room was small but perfectly formed, with a deep voluptuous bed, a nicely positioned desk, no Internet problems, and the most exquisite hotel bathroom I've ever seen. All porcelain and wood fittings with a custom-painted ceiling that had its own lighting system. The staff were also very helpful. The historical beauty of the place was very enjoyable; we spent ---hour days in the conference rooms, so I had plenty of time to look at it.
My one quibble is that there is NO security system to keep people who aren't hotel guests out of the elevators, and the lobby sees a lot of traffic from the hotel restaurant. The Il Fornaio restaurant in the hotel is so well known locally that if you plan to eat there as a guest, you should make a reservation - otherwise, no guarantees of a table.

Although the location is good for getting downtown, and although there's a great seafood restaurant close by (Goode's) the minimal fitness center was a disappointment. As always the staff is terrific.

Very nice hotel. There is a coffee bar in the lobby. Hotel restaurant is very good, but expensive- we ate there one night. Easy walk to shopping, restaurants, and the T stations. We did not have a car so cannot comment on parking. Nice room amenities- free internet, umbrellas, robes, nice shampoos-toiletries. I was very comfortable in the bed, but my sister complained that it was too hard. It was quiet while we were there. This was my first stay in Boston- very easy to travel on the metro- would definitely stay here again if we could get a good rate again.

I'm always amazed at the negative reviews some hotels get which don't deserve the wrath that some deliver - such as the person with the mouse problem in June, who didn't decide to tell us about it until December. I don't know what hotel they stayed at, but it wasn't the Omni Shoreham that I stayed at last weekend. 
Summary - we were given a free upgrade because of my wife's birthday - so I will go into this being a bit biased. The old dame that is the Omni is gorgeous, but a bit dated, but that, frankly adds to its charm. I'm a bit sick of brass and dark wood and you won't find that here. If that's what you're looking for, there are plenty of other options. The suite we stayed in was spacious, albeit a bit sparsely decored. We loved the beds and as parents of five children - slept better than we had in months. It was amazingly peaceful and quiet, though we heard road noise from time to time. The restaurant is overpriced, to say the least - especially breakfast - and it appeared that some things were shut down because of the season, but overall we thought it was a wonderful experience. The staff was great, we lacked for nothing. Just a note - the location of the hotel is not the greatest in the winter. If you're a tourist, this hotel is a bit isolated, though very close to the metro if you want to travel around. It's close to Adams Morgan and its international flavor and the zoo, but my experience is that this is a plus much more in the summmer months. Very classy experience with a few minor suggestions (below). You could do much worse and if you like historic hotels, this is certainly got history all over the walls. You don't need a car to stay here - we took the metro from the airport and travelled that way with the exception of a few short (and expensive) cab rides because of time. 
The good:
-Beds were extremely comfortable
-Suites are spacious
-staff was very attentive
-wireless worked very well (I really don't understand the complaints - we used our laptop all weekend)
-Very close to the metro
-beautifully decorated
-elevators were very fast (again, I don't understand the complaints)
-lots to see, huge hotel for walking around
The not so good:
-restaurant was overpriced, especially breakfast (New York prices) limited menu.
-not a great location in winter, much better in the summer (Rock Creek Park, Zoo, Adams Morgan)
-room furniture was sparse and uncomfortable
-coffee needs to be avaialable (free) in lobby. No such animal. We found some in the morning, but it wasn't well advertised.
- grand old lady looking a bit dated, but that adds to its historic charm (for some). 
- TV in the suite was too small for the football field length it was located away from the bed. 
Again - we paid only about $--- a night, which is about what we got in accordance with value. I wouldn't pay more than $---. We overall enjoyed the experience. Would find another place closer to downtown if we return in the winter.

This hotel is absolutely disgusting!
I had read reviews on trip advisor beforehand so kind of knew what to expect but I genuinely didn’t think that it would be that bad! 
We stepped out of the lift on the second floor and couldn’t believe the corridors walking up to the room! They were actually creepy! Really dark corridors with doors on the rooms that were nearly a hundred years old! 
We walked in our room with disbelieve, we didn’t even put our bags down just walked round the room in utter shock. Cobwebs on the ceiling, paint peeling off the walls, stains on the carpet, an old heater in the corner that sounded like a bus when you turned it on! And you needed it on because the draft that was coming through the window was freezing! It actually moved the curtains! 
Our room was on the second floor, I specifically asked for a floor higher up as I had read reviews previously about the lack of sleep people had on lower level floors, I went straight back down to reception where she informed me we couldn't be moved higher for a room with a view, when I explained that was not the case she just dismissed us and said that she didn't have anything and to try again in a few more hours. 
We lasted one night at The Hotel Pennsylvania, after a sleepless cold night’s sleep (I was piling my coats on top of my covers in the end to keep warm) we decided to phone the tour operator and upgrade to The New Yorker, we had to put a few hundred pound to the upgrade but it was well worth while, we couldn’t get out of The Hotel Pennsylvania fast enough!!! 
Seriously people learn from my mistake! It is as bad as people say!

We booked a last minute stay at the Hilton Dallas Lincoln Centre because it is in close proximity to the Galleria and was recommended by friends who visit Dallas often. We arrived early, about - p.m., and went by the hotel in case a room was ready. Understandably, none were at that early hour on a Saturday.. So, onward to the Galleria for a few hours. Upon our return to the hotel at -:--, a room was still not available and the person at checkin suggested that it would be about another hour. So, we decided to wait at the bar and enjoy a drink. After a little more than an hour, I inquired again about the room and was told still none available. The front desk clerk said they had been booked solid the night before and it was taking a while to get all the rooms clean. By this time I was frustrated. Fortunately, we did not have any plans that required the immediate use of a room to get ready for any outing. So,we drove around a bit and went to dinner. When I called the hotel around -:--, the room was finally ready. I've never had this type of delay in getting a room hours after the usual - p.m. checkin time.
