Hmm?
Also, when we closed our bar tab, my husband paid without really looking at it. A minute later, the waitress, who was very sympathetic and gave us suggestions on where to go for dinner, returns to check on what we had to drink because someone thought our tab was wrong. We had one drink each - a Corona for me and a Bombay Saphire gin for hubby, and the cost was $--. The manager then comes up to say that it was cleared up and that what we got was the same amount as the tab we paid. Whatever. I should have asked them to comp us for wasting an hour waiting on the room. It was just another frustration. 
On the plus side, the room, when we finally got into it, was clean, comfortable, and nicely decorated. The hotel has a glass elevator that looks outward to the city and provides a nice view and fun ride. The pool area looked nice as well, but we did not get to use it. I pulled a muscle in my back while sleeping that night - no idea how. So, I got up in a pretty good bit of pain and was ready to get out of there. I can't blame the hotel for my pulled muscle, but it added to my overall impression. I don't plan to stay there again.

The rooms were small (which is fine) but they were FILTHY. We went straight to the lobby to get out $ back and move on. After a battle with the manager he finally stated he would let us out of our reservation. Which left us on the street in January with our luggage. Horrible experience.

The room we had was very nice, and the staff were friendly, but the resort felt very isolated, we had driven down from LAX after flying from Australia and the last thing we wanted to do with our - year old was to get back in the car to find a shop that was open, so we ended up having to order very expensive room service ($-- including tax, tip and delivery fee for a couple of burgers, a couple of beers and a kids meal). When my jetlagged daughter was wanting to watch kids telly at night I had to pay $-- to access a handful of childrens programmes, the choice of channels was very poor, even for adults. And when she wanted a snack there was nothing open in the resort and no way of getting her anything without getting in the unfamiliar rental car in the middle of the night to drive on unfamiliar roads to I don't know where...Add in the charge for parking ($-- - very expensive), the charge for internet ($-- - disguised as a Paradise Pass, which covers everything which should be free in a resort like this), our one night stay here cost over $---, despite the fact we booked online for $---. After we checked out we went somewhere else with free parking, free internet and free breakfast that was closer to downtown and it was much better. 
On a side note, while the room looked nice, our towel rail actually came off the wall and my feet were filthy walking around barefoot in the room, the floor felt very grimy.

We stayed there from Dec -- to --th, excellent staff and locations. NO BED BUGS. Rooms are clean, ideal location on the same street as as subway stations, many restaurants around. I would go back at any time. Spend - nites in room ---, small ( w- kids) but everything was perfect.
Staff are gentle and very helpfull.

We stayed five nights and were pleasantly surprised at how comfortable our spacious room was. Location perfect for historical destinations. Cabs always available if needed. Good breakfast offerings. Very friendly and polite staff. Wireless Internet available only in lobby, but it never worked. Did have a wired station available in lobby. Many great restaurants within walking distance.

Excellent service, beautiful rooms, great food - what more could you ask for? I stayed one night at this hotel, but enjoyed every moment of it. I entered my room and found chocolate dipped strawberries waiting for me. The room was impeccable and the service extraordinary. We dined in the hotel's five star restaurant and had an excellent meal. The hotel is in a great location, too. It's just minutes from the piers, museums, etc. This is a must stay.

We booked this Embassy Suite because of the reviews on Trip Advisor and we were not disappointed. The rooms were big and clean. The beds were comfortable, including the sofa bed. The staff is very friendly. The breakfast was tasty with a big selection and the afternoon reception was plentiful with drinks and snacks for all. The location is also good. It is a little walk to the Metro. Would stay there again and again. We also really liked the free internet kiosk in the lobby, about - stations.

The hotel is attached to McCormick Place, which makes it a convenient, although long, walk if you're attending an event there as I was recently. Other than that, it's a cab ride to anywhere else you want to visit. And, several people cautioned me about walking anywhere nearby at night. So, if I'm going to be trapped in a hotel, I expect a good one. This one is pretty average. It's overdue for an interiors make-over. And, the hotel is currently adjacent to a high-rise construction project. It gets pretty loud when they resume hanging steel each morning. So, beware which side of the hotel your room faces.

Decent room that you can probably get at value price. Very nice staff, but huge hotel and very busy with many outside events. Expensive to park if you have a car. Otherwise, great access to Metro and can walk to zoo, restaurants and nice neighborhoods.

I enjoyed this friendly, helpful, quiet and clean hotel! The rooms are big with a pull out couch. We stayed here in March ---- as part of an organised tour - the accomodation had been booked by a tour company.

Our first problem on arrival was that the key they gave us for the room would not open the door so someone came with another key and this would not open the door either, a third key and we were in. My first thought was to check the fire escape arrangements and there was an external fire escape at the front of the hotel which could be accessed from each corridor and this was fine but the fire escape from the rear part of the upper floors was through two bedrooms on each floor. As the doors were locked I went I went down to the Front Desk and asked how we would get to the Rear Fire Exit in an emergency through the locked doors - he did not know so I asked for the Manager and was told she was not available so I left a message for her to contact me. We then went out for the evening and when we returned we found that the taps would not work so I phoned the front desk and was informed that we had to turn on the valves under the sink - as these could not be turned they sent a member of staff who also could not turn these valves on. We then had to move rooms with no help from hotel staff and when we ran water into the sink the plug would not let the water out and part of the plumbing from behind the sink fell onto the floor. When I went down to the Front Desk I was given a handful of keys and was told to go and choose a room where everything worked. As the Manager had not come back to me about the fire exit problem I selected on of the rooms which lead directly to the rear fire escape.
I also approached the travel company representative who was also staying in the hotel and she indicated that it was nothing to do with her and could I let her have my comments in writing which I did. By the time we left no one was able to answer how we would be able to use the fire escape so on my return I wrote to the travel company again and to the San Francisco Fire Department who have also not replied. I also copied my letter to the Mayor of San Francisco who also has not replied so if you stay here just ask yourself how you will get out in a fire?

The internet at this hotel was awesome. It never dropped and was quite fast for hotel internet. If you need a good internet connection then I certainly recommend this place. Access was free and we had no problems using two laptops on the Wi-Fi.
The A-C worked well. It was no problem keeping the large room cool. 
The parking is an issue at this hotel. The lot at the hotel only has maybe -- – -- spaces. People were parking along the street and even in the fire lane at times. I stayed at the Westin on N. Michigan Avenue during Memorial Day Weekend. First off, we landed in O’Hare and took the subway to the hotel. After switching trains in downtown Chicago and walking - blocks we finally arrived at the hotel.
There are only two things going for the Westin on Michigan Ave, it’s location to shopping and the Westin Heavenly Bed. One of which you could get at another Westin or Starwoods property and the other via taxi.
Check in was quick and since I am a “preferred Starwoods Member” I was told I was upgraded to a higher floor reserved for “preferred members”. The room did not appear to be “preferred”. It was directly behind the service elevators and I could hear the elevators operating all day and night. Luckily I brought ear plugs to wear while sleeping otherwise I would have gotten no sleep. Additionally, the rooms themselves are not quiet. You could hear anyone and everyone in the hallways (and there were lots of unruly screaming children running down the halls too). 
The room itself was on the smaller side, a king size bed, two night stands, a bureau with TV on top, desk and soft chair with ottoman. My one complaint about the furniture, which I don’t usually comment on, was that there were not drawers on the nightstands only doors that opened to the space below. Additionally, there were no drawers in the desk either. The only drawers in the room were the - small drawers in the bureau under the TV. The other part of the bureau housed the refrigerator with stocked overpriced items.
The bathroom was standard for a hotel room and appeared clean although the housekeeping staff never gave us an extra towel or soap or shampoo.
Being a preferred member I also got free Wi-fi access, however, the wi-fi here was pathetic. I had faster service on my -G phone than the wifi, it was a worthless benefit.
A big beef I have with hotels is that the beds are not completely made. After sleeping in the bed once I once again found that the sheets did not reach the bottom of the bed and the mattress and the small mattress pad were exposed. I had to pull off all the sheets and covers so that the staff would correct it. Additionally, the Westin usually gives you extra pillows in the room, this Westin did not, however, housekeeping did provide us with a few extra pillows.
Westin offers a workout facility in each of their hotels. I’ve been to some really nice hotel facilities and some not-so nice ones, this hotel ranks in the middle. They did provide dumbbells but had no cable machine and - plate type machines. There were also a couple of aerobic machines (treadmill-ellipticals) but not many.
Our room did not have a view either. We overlooked another building across the way. 
As I stated in the beginning, the Westin Heavenly bed was the only plus to our visit. Would be stay here again? No, while we like Starwood properties, we would try another first. When you pay more money for a Starwood property, you expect higher service and quality. This property did not deliver.

We also got stuck in Boston due to Hurricane Maria closing the airport. Danielle arranged for us to stay in our room which was a blessing.
Great hotel. I'd stay again.

This HGI is centrally located in the North River neighborhood, convenient to Mag Mile shopping, the Loop, very good restaurants, and CTA transportation. We stayed for a long weekend in mid September and enjoyed the clean, quiet --th floor room. HGI offers a pantry with more than just junk food, so you can buy a microwave meal, say, at -:--am if you need to (which we did!). The Red Line CTA train is right downstairs. A drugstore-grocery is across the street. A starbuck sis in the lobby as well as across the street. The Wrber Grill restaurant in the lobby is excellent--it made the whole lobby smell of flavorful wood smoke, like a crisp autumn day. Free WiFi to those who belong to Hlton's frequent-user plan. Everyone who worked there was very nice and helpful. I did not see a chambermaid the entire time I was there, but my room was always made up promptly. Nothing negative to say, except that the air conditioner thermostat was hard to control and I was cold most of the time. But the comfy, fluffy bed kept me nice and warm nevetheless.

My husband and I stayed at this hotel for a one-night getaway to celebrate our anniversary. We were a little apprehensive after reading some of the reviews but our experience was a pleasant one.
We checked in right away - they wished us happy anniversary when they greeted us. After we checked into our room, we returned to sit in the main area and enjoyed a couple of drinks. Both bartender and wait staff were professional and prompt. In the meantime, our bags were brought to our room and our ice bucket was filled.
Later that afternoon we were surprised by champagne for two and strawberries dipped in chocolate - a great way to start off our evening.
After dinner at Oceanaire (fabulous food - amusing and fun bartenders), we returned to our room; turn-down service was already done - nice lighting and music playing.
Breakfast at the one restaurant was definitely adaequate - small buffet or menu, food was good. Definitely slow on pouring refills for coffee, but the orange juice and water were flowing.
The spa was incredible. Both husband and I did deep tissue massage. The facilities are very clean and peaceful. Definitely one of best massages I've had.
The room itself had a view of the construction surrounding the hotel and the Washington Monument. The train tracks that ran right next to the hotel were of great concern when I first saw them, but the windows must be sound-proofed - we didn't hear much of the slow-rolling cargo trains.
The staff was totally attentive, we were greeted with smiles throughout our stay.
All in all, a pleasant (and expensive) experience.

My wife and I, along with my mother in law, had planned to stay at the hotel for - nights during our recent visit to San Francisco but shortly after arrival decided to leave the next morning. For several weeks prior to our visit I had followed the reviews here on TA and due to the glowing reviews perhaps my expectations were a bit unrealistic. First of all the place isn't at all impressive from outside looking more like a parking garage than a hotel. But in all fairness most reviews noted this but what wasn't noted was the unimpressive decor on the inside. The concrete balconies surrounding the inner courtyard are plain and cold...it reminded me of an Alcatraz cell block. The room itself is indeed spacious but it feels """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sterile"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The carpets are a very strange pattern of dark """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""dashes"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which, to us, wasn't easy on the eyes. I had requested a room with a view, but when I opened the blinds I was shocked to find myself staring at a bare wall only a few feet away. There is somewhat of a veiw from the rooftop, but again the furnishings there are cold and uninviting. Perhaps a family with children might appreciate the kitchen rendering the ability to prepare meals in-house, but don't book this hotel expecting any charm or elegance. It has a bare bones apartment like feel...adequate but nothing special. I will say the staff was very gracious and friendly not holding us to the -- hr. cancellation policy.

Quick check-in and pretty good breakfast choices. i.e. cereal, yougurt, pancakes, sausage, bacon, boiled eggs, omelets, scrambled eggs, biscuits and gravy, bagels, pastries, bananas, milk and juices. Room was small but adequate and very clean. We purchased the pizza delivery package and had a large - topping free pizza and - liter bottle of soda delivered to the room - out of our - days. No bathtub but nice walk-in shower. Comfortable beds, - rooms per floor, hotel was sold out and we had very minimal wait for the elevator. I've stayed in nyc about - other times and would definitely choose this hotel again. The only negative I can think of is the amount of space and tables in the breakfast area. Very tight squeeze between tables and around chairs. Staff was very helpful and our room looked out over --th st. Hotel is just around the corner from -th ave. Computer use on the lower level was an added bonus. There were - computers both with printing capability to print out vouchers, directions etc. My husband and I were both pleased with this hotel.

Stayed here during a conference in Dallas that was actually held at the hotel. 
Upon check in we were offered concierge level for an additional $-- per night (not sure of the regular or seasonal costs) but it was so worth it! The concierge level had snacks out all day long until - pm with non-alcoholic drinks at no cost. During the evening hours they offered three appetizers which consisted of some sort of delicious soup, and two other warm items. Along with a variety of cheeses, fruit, and dessert. After appetizer time was over they bought out various other petite desserts and have a coffee-expresso machine that makes a variety of different coffee drinks. We ended up so full sometimes we skipped dinner. They also offer a warm breakfast that consists of eggs, bacon, and breakfast potatoes. The hotel online description does not say that offer that so its worth knowing. Between all the meals-snacks offered it paid for itself for sure.
The grounds were pretty.
The rooms were nice and the bed covers-sheets were real comfortable.
The TV in the room seemed bigger than most similar quality hotels so that was nice.

This hotel is the biggest in dc! Lovely rooms and surrounding gardens. Easy check in and out. Mlocation is great. Right near a subway station which is about -- to the mall and white house. Good facilities in the hotel and there are lots off restaurants close by as well.

Small lobby area but very welcoming friendly desk staff.
Room was very cozy with a large bathroom. Amenities had a fabulous aroma. 
I only ended up staying here - night as found it a little far up the hill carrying all my shopping. They say its only - blocks from Union Square...and it is..but the top of Union Square. Most of the shops are right down passed the bottom of Union Square. I shopping was not my aim when visiting, I would stay there again.

This is a perfectly fine hotel in a very convenient location. Some of the negative reviews here seem to be from people who somehow expect a huge business-convention-oriented Hyatt to be a five-star establishment with a high level of personal service. If that's important to you, then you need to find a nice upscale boutique elsewhere, but if you just want a clean, comfortable reasonably sized hotel room with the usual amenities (though admittedly no in-room coffee) this will do just fine. While this is not my favorite NY neighborhood, the transit connections just next door at Grand Central Station make it easy to get just about anywhere in Manhattan and beyond via subway -- you'll save on cab fares. Check-in and check-out were quick and painless. Can't comment on the fitness facilities or restaurants as I didn't try them. However, if you don't like the hotel restaurant offerings, there is no shortage of breakfast and lunch places in the neighborhood, though I might venture a little further afield for dinner. The area is bustling because of its proximity to Grand Central, but I heard no street noise at all from my --th floor room. Again, you have to understand what sort of hotel this is, but if you're OK with that I would recommend it.

I stayed here in February, when i seen the hotel I loved it, the foyer was elegant and lovely looking. However once we steeped out the lift there was a horrible smell, the bedroom was tiny with the beds up against the walls with barely any room to move. The view was of the bins in the yard and the ladders made it look so easy to get into our room throught the window. There were no facilities other than a very expensive shop. Would have really appreciated a restraunt or a swimming pool. However, the location of the hotel was excellent, the empire state building was on the next street. Perfect midtown location. But the hotel was terrible and I couldn't put up with it again.

Staying at the Renaissance in downtown Columbus with a - month old grand baby while my daughter attended a conference during the day. First the wireless would not work and after many attempts working with the staff we gave up, they did not charge us for this service. A hotel of this status should be able to provide wireless service to their rooms, it is ----! The maid did not come to clean the room to well after - pm she did not replace the glasses we used, but removed the ones we had used. She left no extra toilet paper or toiletries. She also did not replace all of our towels in the room.

Very Noisy, and I'm not talking about the highway traffic. The room had an odor, a-c didnt work correctly, hairs all over the restroom floor and the bed looked like somebody already slept in it. Very disgusting.

We used Four Points as the hotel to stay at the out of town guests at my wedding. We had a block of rooms set off for the guests and the people that my parents worked with to get this organized were very helpful. My family and friends that are in the area also decided it would be easier to stay and the hotel after the wedding. The rooms were very nice and clean and I would definitely go back again. The only thing that was a problem was the payment. It started to get confusing because some people wanted to pay in cash and some on their card and it started to get confusing because the bridal party couldn't check in at regular time... the paying part was kind of a mess but other than that it was a good time.

I have visited NYC many many times and my room at the Hilton Times Square was by far the largest ever plus there is a coffeemaker in the room (don't get that much either). As with all Hilton brand hotels, the hotel was immaclate, staff friendly and helpful. Conveniently located on West --nd St to theatres, restaurants and bars. All in all, a great place to stay in NYC

We drove up looking for the deals in the Denny's travel books and someplace that had public Net access. We were in for a treat. With only - rooms left we were glad to get one at less than the average cost, even if it was a smoker's room. We made do with the staircase-- there is no elevator. The lobby looks upscale with - comfy waiting areas and *<->* computers with public access. You do not have to have your own PC to access the Net! Complimentary full breakfast was not a farce. Lounge had real Mariachi Thursday night. We stayed two nights. Pool was clean and useable, unlike others that advertise a pool then don't keep it up. Computers were clean and had good connection speeds. Pretty desks, too. Clerks were upper crust, but one was sorta """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""do it yourself."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (oh well). I was pretty impressed compared to where we'd been before and for the price. By the time we left I overheard a clerk talking about only having - rooms available. Now, that speaks for the quality of a place that they are extremely booked. 
The non-affiliated tour van from the hotel was just acceptable; the friendly driver seemed to forget or repeat things. However, we saw a route we wouldn't have known on our own. When we hunted all over for postcards we only found them at the Walgreens on Geronimo and Gateway West.

We stayed three nights and found this to be one of the best Courtyards we have stayed in. Friendly and competent staff, decent food, active bar, good exercise facilities, and an esplanade and park outside the doors. Nearby are shops and restaurants in the former Naval Training Center and a nine hole golf course.

We stayed here for - nights this month and its not a boutique Hotel thats for sure. The reception area and bar look good but the rooms are pretty basic. However, although small, our room was a cool haven after walking around the hot city all day. Our bed was so comfortable, we slept like logs. Our cleaner was fab, the room was pristine every day, we couldn't have asked for more from her. The positive thing about this Hotel is its location. You are in the middle of everything, we walked everywhere from this Hotel, its fantastic. We would stay here again but only because its quite cheap by Chicago standards and the great location. If you want fancy, don't stay here. For us though we only intended to sleep here, we hardly spent any time in our room and so this Hotel served its purpose for us.
A cool thing to do in Chicago is go on a Segway tour. Our first time and we loved it. Recommend it. Eating wise we loved Shaw's Crab House and Yolk for breakfast. We found Gino's East deep dish very disappointing and didn't want to go home to London without trying this deep dish that everybody was raving about and recommended so much. So we tried it another day at Giordano's and it was fabulous. We then understood what all the fuss was about!
Chicago is a fab city, great people and we went back to London happy and that little bit fatter and with a tan from all that walking in that lovely sunshine!
Have fun. x

Stayed Oct ---- for one night before oue cruise. - queen beds were very comfortable and the free breakfast was excellent. Staff was very friendly and the room was wonderful. We could walk a block and we were in the heart of times square and a couple of blocks north and we were at Central Park. Would recommend to anyone and look forward to returning again.

After just returning from Philly, the Alexander Inn deserves praise! What a charming place! I cannot say enough about the service we received while we were guests; every detail is covered! The staff is friendly and helpful; they go out of their way to welcome you & make themselves available for anything.They appear to truly enjoy their job! The Inn is conveniently located and it is easy walking to historic sites, eateries, tour bus stops & shopping. A well-equipped exercise room & internet access was a bonus! Everything is VERY neat, clean, & well-kept. The mattress was good, which is a make-or-break on vacation. The negative; the guestroom & bathroom are quite small, no room to spread out, and we would have liked our air conditioner to cool better. Overall a great experience! We would definitely stay here again!

I went to NYC with a friend and just came back home yesterday. So tired! Anyway, I have to agree with the ealier review. I stayed on the --th floor and I have to say it is a fantastic location and literally on the door step of Times Square. The room i stayed in was very dated, very basic and so was the bathroom. It did the job which was a base to come back to but I was disappointed that the corridor leading to the room and the room itself wasn't up to dated enough. The reception staff were a little abrupted but the other staff were very friendly.

My stay at """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The Palace"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" will be a wonderful memory. My son treated me for my --th birthday and he could not have done better. I rate it a -- star !!

The best I have ever stayed at in NYC. The rooms are spotless, well appointed and quite large after NYC standards. The staff is very friendly, and the locations is great. Will definately stay there again.

After a one night stay we had to come again and so glad we were here for - nights this time. Paid the extra fee for the Griffin Club, not cheap, but definitely got our money's worth! It basically includes breakfast, lunch and dinner (heavy appetizers--plenty for dinner) AND snacks and beverages all day plus full bar after - pm and desserts each evening. What makes it so special is the staff in the Griffin Club--they made us feel so welcome and really wanted to be as helpful as possible--serving food, preparing drinks, acting as a concierge--they did it all especially graciously. All the staff was great and special kudos to Alison. We also like this resort because of the great pools and the lazy river. Lots of kids but not as overrun as some other resorts with water parks. Evening entertainment in the lounge also fun (tho I wish some parents had better control of their small children).

Stayed in this hotel for only one night, and I wish I could have stayed longer (for the same price, of course). We booked through priceline and got an AMAZING deal. The hotel is a little bit hard to find, the taxi driver could not find it, and took us around and we ended up paying more fare. But it's in a great location: Central park is right across the street and Times Square can be reached by walking down Broadway. There is a shopping center right across the street, but we did not have a chance to check it out. We stayed in the pod room, which is super tiny, but extremely clean and decorated really well. Even though the bed is a bit small for two people, it is really comfortable because of the pillow top mattress. The flat screen tv was great, but I would have liked to have maybe a little table or at least a chair to put things on, I think there would have been enough room for a least a chair or a luggage holder. I loved the bathroom, it was very modern and pretty. Toiletries, Q-tips and cotton balls. There was a safe in the closet, a bathrobe and an umbrella to use during your stay. I was disappointed though because there was no hairdryer. The AC in the room worked really well. The staff was great. I would recommend it to everyone and would definitely stay there again.
Great location, beautiful hotel. It was a little loud, but we were downtown and it was Halloween night, its expected.

If you're looking for a clean, comfortable, friendly hotel that is easy walking distance (I'm talking ---- minutes easy) to Times Square, theatres, Central Park, shopping, and subway stations to take you anywhere else you want to go, then Novotel is definitely the place. We stayed there three nights, and our only complaint was that the lobby bar-restaurant closed at midnight. But hey, it's New York, right? There are plenty of other places open late. Parking at a garage just down the street was $-- per day if you get your ticket stamped by the hotel.
Oh, and big rooms, too. Our's (--th floor) overlooked the Hudson river...great view.

I stayed here from -- to -- July ---- on a business trip to attend a Society of Petroleum Engineers (SPE) workshop. Even though SPE had arranged a daily rate but I was charged considerably higher rate because the website did not recognize the SPE supplied code. In a long phone call, the booking person tried to rectify it and said that it is fixed but it was actually not fixed. Upon arrival, no body in the lobby cared and an attendent casually asked whether help was needed to take luggage to the room. He did not bother to show where the lift was and let me drag the suite case up the stairs to the first floor. I had bought break-fast in addition to the room for which tickets were issued on check in. On third day, the Olivetti restuarant manager refused to recognize the value of ticket and insisted on serving a limited menu. That was resolved after an unpleasant argument at the reception. Upon check out, again no one bothered to ask of any help. I did not thoroughly checked the bill and after arriving back found that I had been charged overnight parking fees while I did not have a car and had been charged for beer cans from the minibar while I do not drink alcohol. Thoroughly check your bills with this hotel. Surprisingly, the issue was resolved when I sent a message to the hotel and the over-charge was actually refunded. In summary, the service is very poor. May be there is a racist element in it.

Booked using AAA...rooms were very reasonable. Great location with tons of things to do at the hotel as well as in and around San Diego. There are """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""tower"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" rooms and bungalows. The one bedroom queen bungalow included a living room and kitchenette.

From the moment we booked our stay online we enjoyed our experience with The Benjamin, well situated in Midtown. Since my wife and I were traveling with our two children, we opted for a suite so we would have more space. We chose the Winter Suite package which provided many extras including complimentary parking, which is a great deal. Upon completing the booking process, we were also presented with an upgrade option that, pending availability, would give us an upgraded suite (with a balcony!) for a mere $--. A great strategy to provide the hotel with a modest additional revenue for a room that might otherwise go unbooked. And the traveler receives a better room for a fraction of the cost. A great idea! Our room was quite spacious, very clean with lots of windows that provided good light. But what really sets The Benjamin apart is the service. Not long after completing the booking process, we received a note from Anya, a conceirge who offered her services to help plan a memorable trip, beginning with choosing the type of pillow from their menu of twelve options to help ensure a restful night of sleep. From there, the personal touch continued to Jonathan who greeted us when we drove up, to Jessica at the front desk who made us feel most welcome and Angelo who brought up our bags that were being held for us since we arrived a bit too early for our room to be ready.
The Benjamin places much emphasis on the sleep experience both online and in the hotel literature. One might assume this is just marketing hype; however, Jessica proved they practice what they preach. She ensured we had whatever we needed to make our sleep restful, even providing a fun but effective pillow choice for the kids.
We highly recommend The Benjamin and look forward to a return visit.

I stayed at the Four Point Sheraton next door to this hotel last year and it was horrible! I tried the Sheraton Suites on this trip and it was better. The staff was nice and the rooms were spacious. The hotel reminds me of an old embassy suites. The hotel is showing signs of wear: carpets in the rooms, walls in common areas, etc. I have stayed at much better and much worse. This property is the middle of the road. Next trip I will try the Hilton that is beside it.
Nothing spectacular but a solid choice. Nice pool. Great free breakfast and happy hour. Convenient location. All for a very reasonable price

NYC is a difficult city to find an affordable, easy place to stay, but I wouldn't stay here again. The room was tiny, it smelled bad and apart from the room being painted like ALice in Wonderland, it really had no charm.

Booked threw Priceline 
The hotel room was large and clean and well located for all tourist activities 
The restaurant located in the hotel was ok but over priced ( only had breakfast there the day we left to save time)

This Springhill Suite doesn't measure up to the ones we have stayed at before. The suites were very small, the pull out couch not very comfortable - I love windows that open - there were none. Location is not the best - Shuttle was not free - Breakfast was very good. Needs new pillows. Staff put two guests in different rooms even though they both told them at check in that they were staying together - they checked in hours apart and didn't realize that they were both checked in...

Went through priceline and got this hotel for - days at --$ a night. It was a steal. The service was great, housekeeping divine. The only couple of things we noticed, was there seems to be a lot of loud car stereos in the parking lot, the deep thumping kind. We were a little worried that the noise from the highway would be a factor, but it couldn't be heard at all in the room, and we had a room closest to the road. The room was in good condition with just needing a few minor repairs needed. We would definately stay there again. The hotel offered all the amenities advertised, and the internet worked great. Though the bed..... Ick. Was uncomfortable for me and my boyfriend. Woke up many times throughout the night with sore shoulders, and backs. We can't pinpoint what it was (too soft-hard?) but it served the purpose of allowing us some rest. The hotel is located in far north Austin (Actually on the pflugerville-round rock border practically) which was a small inconvenience since our friends we were visiting were in South Austin.

My granddaughter and I recently stayed at the Hilton on Avenue of the Americas. It was in a good location and I felt very safe. We could walk to Central Park and to the Metropolitian Museum of Art easily. It was also close to Rockefeller Plaza. The staff was very helpful and friendly.

We had a fabulous room on the --nd floor of this hotel with a great view of Boston. The location, close to Boston Common, was ideal and we could walk to everywhere we wanted to go.The room was larger than any I've stayed in before and well-decorated-furnished. On the down side, we were unable to use the computers in the business centre to access or send emails.I presume there is security restriction, but the staff did not tell us this and said they didn't know why we couldn't use Hotmail, even after IT guys had looked at it. This persisted for the whole of our - day stay and other guests had the same problem. So it was great if you don't need that facility.

Person at the front desk was very unfriendly. Furniture in the room was old and broken down, just a terrible room. At checkout the person at the front desk was fast asleep and didnt even see me leave.

My wife and I stayed at Iroquois for five nights in late August. We went on the recommendation of our travel agent who got us a good deal on this property. 
When we arrived in mid-afternoon we were somewhat surprised that there was no door person to greet us and help us with our luggage. When we did get inside the hotel, however, (the lobby is currently under construction), staff were helpful and check in was a breeze. 
As stated in previous reviews, the rooms are quite small. We had requested a Superior Room with king size bed, which we got. The bed took up easily --% of the room. The washroom was big enough, with the usual amenities. The bed and pillows were very comfortable. The chamber staff was very efficient. Rooms were always made by early afternoon. In the evening, the turndown service--complete with Belgian chocolate--was much appreciated. 
Location in the theatre district and close to Times Square was also great. 
While hotel staff was very helpful, the concierge desk was not always staffed. The hotel only has two rather small elevators, which are in great need of upgrade. At times in the morning, the wait for an elevator with space was often more than five minutes.
Overall, the stay was pleasant. But at an average of about $----night, I have a feeling there are other properties which would provide better value for our dollar

Loved the Chelsea Pines Inn. Fantastic location with easy subway access, and a vibrant local neighbourhood surrounded by great dining and shopping options and neighbourhood bars. Owner and staff are extremely professional and helpful with restaurant-bar recommendations, arranging transfers etc. Social events in the common areas provide a great opportunity to meet and mingle with other guests if you so choose. The Hollywood kitch throughout only enhances the charm. We'll be back. Just keep in mind, there's no lift in the building.

Great hotel, especially for one that is associated with a college campus. I was there for business, and this is the hotel that they booked for me. Amenities were nice, staff was young (I think they are college students), friendly, and helpful. Had breakfast at the hotel restaurant, which is standard hotel fare. Room was spacious, neat, and clean. You can only valet park, which is about $--. Self-parking is cheaper, but you have to walk a bit. My room was also designed to accommodate travelers with disabilities. I did not have a tub, so water got all over the floor, but I think it is supposed to be that way. I also did not have any counter space to put my toiletries anywhere. I had to use the counter in the other room. I Would stay there again, if I were visiting Columbus.

We did a last minute getaway through American Express Fine Hotels and Resorts. We booked a club level room. We were upgraded to a one bedroom suite. The club level had great food preparations and alcoholic beverages were included. I loved the afternoon """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""tea"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" service on the club level. It was wonderful to sit and look out over the Public Garden. The service in the hotel was bar was just okay. They were a bit slow. The location was wonderful!

This is a great hotel! It is extremely clean, the rooms are very spacious and nicely appointed, the lobby decor and space and views are all lovely, and the location can't be beat. It's a $-- fare to the airport and a -- minute walk to both -th street and SoCo, and the hotel is literally right on the bike-running-walking path around the lake. They serve coffee and tea in morning and lemonade in the afternoon in the lobby - a lovely touch. The lobby bar scene was also hopping at night. Trio, the restaurant on the first floor, was delicious. The steam room and showers and toiletries at the wonderful spa are free for guests of the hotel, and a few friends had massages and other services there and their reviews were raving. The Four Seasons also offers bike rental, the gym on the first floor is sunny and clean and not overly crowded (and they offer ice water and towels), the pool is nice and they have sunblock, towels, and cool wet eucalyptus oil face cloths when you get too hot, the bellboys in front of the hotel are so fast and friendly, and the bathrooms were spacious and nice. L'Occitaine shampoos and soaps everywhere, too. 
My only complaint is that our large suite shared a wall with the service elevator, so it was difficult to sleep in in the morning b-c of the elevator noises. However, I'm a light sleeper, and my husband snoozed right through it. 
The service was wonderful. The laundry service was extremely prompt and they did a great job on the wedding suits. The Four Seasons Austin was the perfect home base for our weekend trip to Austin - we attended a wedding there, too, and it was extremely nice. The staff was incredibly helpful. I would highly recommend this hotel to a friend staying for the weekend in Austin.

I stayed in the Powell hotel for - days in March ---- when I was attending a conference in the Moscone center. The hotel is very good in terms of locationa and fascilities. It is located in downtown less than one minute walking distance from the bart station. it is so close to the famous mascone conference center ( max -- min walking ).
The place is so clean. Don't listen to those speaking about bed bugs. The bed and the whole room was so clean. you enjoy free breakfast( light breakfast) and free wireless internet in your room. The satff is so friendly.
It is close to the cable car station so some comments spoke about some noise. It should be because it is realy so close but in my case I stayed in room --- and was extremely calm. I would advise to go for the fourth floor rooms or higher to avoid noise.The hotel also provides a shuttle to airport but I think it is paid..
If you are going to San francisco you will probably not stay in the hotel except for sleeping, so get your reservation in the powell hotel and enjoy the convenient price and excellent servise..

We recently visited our son and daughter-in-law in Seattle and stayed at the Paramount Hotel. Little did we know that we would be able to spend four days in the city without a car and get everywhere we wanted to go on foot - including their apartment in the Capitol Hill neighborhood. The room was nice, staff was nice, the hotel restaurant, Dragonfish, was good. We would definitely stay here again.

AT&T is not known for customer service, efficiency, or value. But this hotel is far better than its namesame. We stayed here for SXSW, the annual tech, music, and film festival. It was the last hotel with availability, and apparently we got the very last room because they had to upgrade us to a suite. The room was spacious and comfortable, with a huge balcony overlooking the UT campus. The shower and tub were pristine, and the service was fantastic. I just wish I had had more time to spend inside!

My husband and recently I had the opportunity to spend three days at the Sheraton Inner Harbor. We have traveled extensively and appreciate quality and good service. The rooms were immaculate, beds and pillows were comfortable. The staff was exceptional, (especially Penny-who cleaned our room), they were friendly without being over bearing. We had the Sunday brunch which was a great value and again the wait staff was wonderful. I'd highly recommend this hotel for visitors to the Inner-Harbor and surrounding areas.

Couldn't be in a better spot - right in the heart of Times Square, just across the street from the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Red Steps"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and tckts office. Adjacent to where all of the tour buses start-end their loops.
Nice city centre hotel, nothing spectacular, but the rooms are spotless and very large for a Manhattan Hotel. Ours had - double beds and a put you up couch in the seperate living room.
We ate out every meal [why wouldnt you in NYC!] so can't comment on the hotel restaurant or room service. Didn't use the gym but it looked ok. Did use the Business Centre to check in online for our flight home and this was VERY expensive so beware!!
Ask for a Times Square view room if you can get it-otherise you might get no view at all as many rooms just face a [very close] office block.

Stayed here with my husband for - nights - days. Overall I think the other Marriott properties in close proximity are much better options. Here's the overall positive-negative of my stay at this Residence Inn:
Positives: Location is near to everything. Valets are fantastic--friendly, professional, and doing a great job. Front desk staff were at least friendly but didn't do much to resolve some issues we encountered. -nd floor lounge is updated, modern, and has coffee with to-go cups ----. Loved that. Fitness center and business center looked very nice although I didn't use them. Room was large, clean (albeit awkward design) and shower worked well. No sounds from rooms next door to use even though there were tons of kids staying for a marshal arts competition. It was great to have the full fridge and dishwasher and a real coffee maker. We took advantage of that and used all the appliances. The housekeeping service was very good the entire time.
Negatives: Okay, first of all, if you like aesthetics this is not your place. The front of the building is shabby (scaffolding, residence inn sign is falling off) and the tiny lobby very underwhelming. The rooms, as many mentioned, are worn. Carpet needs a serious upgrade. Weird stain on floor of kitchen that appeared permanent (grout material?) but just looked gross. Weird layout in the room where the TV is off at an angle that makes it hard to watch from the bed. We asked for a king and got a small queen. They could not accomodate our request for a king or two doubles but as a consulation they let us pick a snack out of the (limited) snack bar area for free. (whoo-hoo) The biggest pet peeve of mine is when a hotel toilet doesn't work right. This one didn't flush right the entire time we were there even though we complained and they supposedly fixed it. Internet wireless was unreliable and I had trouble staying connected. the TV options were terrible. No movies to rent or room service, but we knew that going in so I can't gripe too much about it.
Overall it was not a horrible experience, and I know we could've done worse, but it certainly left much to be desired. I would recommend the Courtyard right next door or if you have some extra cash, the full Marriott around the block. It was lovely. If more $$ is put into the Residence Inn, it will be a great hotel. They just need to invest in it.
