There was some noise from the fire engine sirens, but to be honest if you've been out and about all day and night exploring this wonderful City. Then you'll fall straight back to sleep ;) Overall, a lovely hotel to stay in for our visit to New York and we look forward to our next visit :)

We knew nothing about New York but wanted a central location in a pleasant hotel with free WiFi and really good clean facilities for a reasonable price. We got all this and more at the Hotel Mela. Our son visited in July ---- and was equally impressed. Just off Times Square it was ideally located for everything. Our room wasn't huge but our son's was much bigger so clearly room sizes differ. Ask for a room high up or at the back if street noise bothers you as our friends found this a slight problem at the front lower down. The place looked newly renovated and while the lobby is small and the street outside a teeny bit seedy, this was not a problem for us. We felt perfectly safe. Heaps of great restaurants and theatres abound. Try Tony's in the next street - brilliant - or the set price pre theatre menus across the road which were good quality and value for money. Market in the next street on Sunday was a blast for bargains. Bed was great, widescreen TV was great, free WiFi was fast and bathroom was small but perfectly nice. All was super clean. Lifts a bit slow and small but that was only negative. We doubt you will do better for the price anywhere in New York judging from other reviews. Highly recommended.

I'll preface by saying the hotel is being renovated and should be complete in March; we stayed on an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""old"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" floor, so take some things in stride.
 We went for a weekend shopping trip and booked a room because of a decent price and good location. The check-in and all interactions with the staff was excellent. They were friendly, professional, informative, helpful and always pleasant. 
 The room seemed small at first because of the dark colors, but is really adequate with a small kitchenette & nice work area. The work station had a nice-sized desk, comfortable office chair and was well lit.
 I don't hear well, so if I note it, it is definitely loud. The old heat-cooling unit was rather loud (and annoying). The sirens from below bothered my wife (we were on the --th floor). It wasn't a busy weekend, but we both heard everything in the hallway.
 The bed was comfortable for me, too soft for my wife.
 The bathroom was clean, and the rest of the room seemed okay, but had some suspicious deficiencies, such as stains on the chair, drapery, wall and ceiling (don't ask me!). The TV hutch was very dusty on top (we were going to store some purchases out of the way there...we decided against it). The carpet probably could have used a good cleaning. I'm not sure how much they've been delaying maintenance because of the renovation, so some issues might be rectified by. (To be fair, I did not contact the management about the situation).
 Room service is from either the Weber Grill (on the ground floor) or from Buca de Beppo (on block east). We had ribs at the Weber Grill (they were good) but that's another story.
 Given the service, price and location, and assuming that the renovations reduce the noise and cleanliness issues, we would recommend this property as a good base for your time in downtown Chicago.

We stayed here for two nights. As soon as we went inside this hotel bad things started happening...first the keys we got from front desk didn't work so my husband went down and got another set but they didn't work either...then some ---- minutes later handyman came and let us in...did I mention we were with our -- month old daughter. Front desk offered no apologize for key incident not when my husband went not when it didn't work second time. Anyways we got in thInking it's over now....then our sink strated pluging and when my husband went and complained they offered us another room on higher floor saying our top floor is the best one and the higher you take the room the better it will be. But by then -- pm in the night out daughter slept and we couldn't change the room. The key situation kept happening every time we had to use key around - times, we learned to live with the sink problem so the moral of our story Ask for room in higher floors.

We stayed here for - nights. When I tried to check in, they told me I didn't have a reservation. I knew I did, and had printed out the confirmation #, but had left it in our car, which was valet parked at a different hotel. They checked me in, but I asked them to make sure I wasn't charged for a one night no show, on the reservation they couldn't find. They said again that they didn't have any other reservation for me, so I accepted their word. The room was nice, spacious, my girls loved it. The beds were super comfy, and the girls loved the separate shower and tub. The water in the shower took a while to get warm, but it was worth it once it did. We came back in late from a graduation, and asked at the front desk if they had any delivery menus. The clerk acted like he didn't know what we were talking about, then finally gave us one menu for a pizza place. The elevator was non existent when we were trying to go down to check out. When we got to the elevator, another family said they had been waiting -- mins, and we waited about -- more. Then I pressed the up button, and one came right away. I said we'll just ride it up, then down, and the other family got on too. We did that, and after only one stop we were down in a jiffy. Several weeks later I checked my credit card statement, and surprise! I had been charged for - nights on one credit card (correct) and one night on the credit card that I had used to guarantee the reservation that they couldn't find! To their credit, when I called, they took my information and called me back and said they would credit back that night's charge, but they couldn't-wouldn't explain how the mixup happened. With all the nice hotel choices out there, I don't think I will be back to the Swissotel. The bed was comfy, but the negatives outweighed the positives in this case for me.

Blocks of rooms were booked here for a family wedding. We arrived several days early in mid-week and were treated beautifully upon check-in. The room was a very nice size and clean. It was probably the most comfortable bed and pillows I have had in a hotel.
One of the largest problems we had was a shortage of towels. We had to call down every day to get towels. The first day of maid service we had no hand towels. The second and third day they left only one bath towel for two people. The fourth day we left a note requesting - bath towels as we had a rollaway reserved for one of our children arriving that day. They left only two bath towels and no hand towels or washcloths. Every single day we had to call housekeeping to get towels and we did try to reuse them, only to have the towels removed and replaced with fresh towels daily. However, the staff kept giving us new bottles of shampoo, conditioner and body wash, even though we never opened any of them. We would have preferred towels instead.
Luxury bottles of spring water and little chocolates were left nightly along with a set of slippers on each side of the bed. However, a family member never received the water, chocolates or slippers for her two day stay.
Like most older hotels, there was little room on the bathroom counter to hold your toiletries. Since we stayed for - nights, we would have liked to have had a dresser or armoire in which to store our clothing. Instead, there were small shelves tucked way back in the closet and they were difficult to reach. And why do hotels never provide enough hangers?
At $-- per day, the internet was a bit too much to bother with. Service in the bar and patio were pretty poor. Only one of two elevators was in use the entire time we were there. The broken elevator was the only one capable of reaching the penthouse where the bride was staying. We were forced to get off the elevator on one floor and walk the stairs to reach her. It was very hot at all times in the stairwell and elevator.
Several members of our party arrived on Saturday afternoon to be told their rooms were not ready and one man was extremely upset because he reserved a room with two beds - one for him and one for his children and was told they would have to give him two rooms. He was very upset having to have his children in another room that was on the same floor but not even near his room. That was absolutely unacceptable being they had reservations specifically for a room with two beds. To their credit, the staff gave free drink coupons but after several hours, everyone wanted their rooms instead of another free drink.
The location was excellent being so close to Grand Central Terminal. If we had not had the event rate, we would not have chosen to stay here. The hotel had so much potential but with the busy Labor Day weekend, the staff just could not handle all the guests adequately.

We just returned from a wonderful stay at the Hampton Inn in DC. I was truly impressed with everything about this hotel. The rooms were clean with new furniture, a spacious bathroom and a refrigerator and microwave. They had complimentary internet service, and free local phone calls that was great for planning our sightseeing adventures. The breakfast every morning was really convenient and there was a good variety of food to chose from. Our kids enjoyed the pool and I enjoyed the hot tub after a long day of walking to all of the sightseeing attractions!
The hotel is only about - blocks from the Metro and Chinatown. I was initially concerned about the neighborhood but really never had any problems... I don't know that I would recommend walking alone at night but you can find that in any major city. 
The greatest feature about this hotel is the staff. We have traveled many times and I have never come across a more accomodating and friendly staff. I would not hesistate to recommend this hotel to anyone.

I expected much more from this hotel. It is true that there is nothing around for a similar price and the location is fantastic if you wnat to stay in the village, but that´s it.
I paid --- USD , plus taxes, for a room no bigger than a bathroom. To open the door I had to move the suitcases because there was not place for the suitcases. The wardrobe was about one square meter, or less.
The air conditioning unit was not fixed properly so the cool air came into the room. 
The room was very noisy ( you can hear the street noises even in -th floor ) and the pipes in the bathroom make funny noises all the time
Staff: very unfriendly. They never helped us with our questions or with our luggage. the last day they forgot to ring the limousine to get to the airport ( a service that they recommended ) and we almost missed the plane. They said that the car had a flat tyre but it was no true.
There is an exception: a short man with a beard, very nice and helpful.
Next time I will go other place or I will book an apartment but I do not want to stay in this hotel anymore if it costs more than --- USD

This hotel is in a convenient location in the Back Bay area. The lobby is beautiful. I didn't try the restaurant or room service. My single room was small and a little cramped with a small double bed, hardly any closet space and a cramped shower with no tub. The bathroom had hardly any counter space for toiletries, makeup, etc. The shower spray was very powerful, however; I ended up with a huge puddle of water all over the tile floor whenever I used it. Also, there were no available outlets in the room, so I had to unplug a lamp to charge my cell phone. I was told when I checked in that there were no king beds available. I had a choice between the small single room or a room with two double beds. I was alone, so I chose the single room. Had I known how small it was, I would have picked the room with two double beds. I know the hotel was busy and there was a convention being hosted there, but I still find it hard to believe that in a place that size they didn't have any larger single rooms available. Maybe the receptionist gave me a limited choice because I booked the room for a reduced rate on hotwire. Anyway, I was a little disappointed. I expected more from a -.- star hotel. By the way, bring your laptop if you need internet access. It's free in your room, but they charge for it in the business center. I wouldn't stay here a second time. There are better options in the Back Bay area for the price.

Stayed at this hotel over New Year ---- - ---- for - nights.
The bad points:
- Rooms are TINY.
- Beds are hard.
- Rooms at the front of the property are VERY noisy due to poor sound proofing from the street.
- The first room we were in was too warm, and we had no control over the heating.
- No dining facilities on site, so you have to go out for breakfast.
The good points:
- Location is good - close to Times Square, but not so close that it's a nuisance. Also very close to a subway station on the A, C and E lines.
- Staff were helpful in moving us to a slightly larger room that was quieter (near the back of the property).
- Relatively cheap.
Overall, we expected better, and I wouldn't call this a - star hotel.
A little more detail:
On the first night, we asked to be moved to a larger room, and for some padding to be put on the bed (it was like a plank of wood). They said they couldn't do anything until the morning, as the house keeper had gone home and there were no larger rooms available until the next day. In the morning, we checked with them and they said they had a larger room available (at the expense of having a smaller bathroom), which was also quieter (we complained about the noise in the morning, having been constantly woken up in the night be people & vehicles outside). They moved our stuff whilst we were out for the day.
The second room we were in had a bit more space, but the bathroom was tiny (barely room to dry yourself). Happily though, it was away from the road so much quieter, and they'd put a bit of padding on the bed so it was slightly more bearable. The radiators weren't on in the room for some reason, so it was also a more comfortable temperature.
I certainly wouldn't recommend this hotel, as it's pot luck which room you end up with. If you're lucky and get one of the slightly larger and quieter rooms, and don't mind sleeping on hard beds, then it's reasonable value for money. We'll be staying elsewhere next time though.

You'd be surprised to find a place like that downtown Chicago. It has no website and is not featured on Travelocity and the likes (as far as I know). I found it in the Lonely Planet Chicago in the budget section after failing miserably at booking any other place for the Chicago Marathon. Everything was booked - months in advanced, except for $--- and up luxury suites. This place still cost $--, which would buy you a decent room on a day other than the day before the Marathon (but I think prices a much lower the rest of the time).
Anyway, when it says """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Motel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", it IS a motel. Straight out of the '--s. It is not just retro-themed, it is truly retro, so if you like that sort of thing, go for it. I still am not completely sure what that gadget that reminded of an old record player-radio (it wasn't a record player) in the corner was, but artifacts like that ceased to exist at least - years ago. 
The place was really worn out, but with a remodeled bathroom. The sheets and blankets must have been on those beds for generations. It was clean, although still looked kind of sketchy, the kind of place that would be featured in the noir film. 
Customer service was excellent! The gentleman who helped us check in, was one of the most pleasant people I've ever met and that is the reason why I didn't hate the motel. You can't hate a place where such wonderful people work. We also needed some help the next day and the day shift woman was also great.
I would recommend this motel for people on a tight budget who don't care for frills.

First of all let me say that this is my second review of The Pierre, my first was two years ago when we stayed there for the first time. That stay was wonderful so I thought I’d give a brief follow up.
Once again it was a fabulous experience! We arrived on a Wednesday a little after - PM and were shown promptly to our room. We had a Parkview room directly above the one we had - years ago. The view out the large windows is of the northern end of Central Park and is stunning! You can’t get a room anywhere with a much better view.
The room was spotless and with no adjoining doors extremely quiet. The Pierre is a combination hotel-residence with most of the residences on the upper floors facing directly the -th Avenue (Central Park) side. Our floor this year had one large suite, one residence and our Parkview room. Two years ago there was one residence, one Parkview and two standard rooms. Point is that the upper floors are small and there are not a lot of rooms or traffic in the hallways.
Advice here – stay in one of the higher floors.
The bedding was extremely comfortable – so much so that we are ordering “Pierre” pillows for use at home. The room was cool and the room service (we had room service breakfast) was wonderful. Eating breakfast in your pajamas while looking out over Central Park can’t be beat!!
The Hotel has a courtesy car which we used to be taken to the Broadway Theater area for dinner and plays each night. The Concierge Desk was very helpful and knowledgeable. The location can’t be beat! The Hotel is essentially connected to Barneys (--- block away), - blocks north of all the fabulous shopping on Fifth Avenue, and --- blocks west of Park and Madison Avenues.
The only issue we had during our stay was that it was very difficult to connect to the internet. We even had their tech department come to help and ended up having to use the hardwired port. In the end it was easier just to connect via our iPads on the ATT network.
The Pierre still shines as one of the best if not the best hotel we have ever stayed in. We will definitely be back for our next Broadway visit!!

At the St. Regis they treat you like a family member coming home. The only thing more beautiful then the hotel itself is the staff at the hotel. They will go out of their way to help you with anything you need. After coming here for a few years, I have never made a request that they could not fulfill.
The hotel is great for Business or a lovely vacation and the location can not be beat.

Not knowing the name, I was kind of worry after it was booked thru the hitwire. but I was kind of glad after my - days stay. the room was roomy and clean. the very first day I found that there's no internet signal in my room, the staff helped me find a room that has; and both morning-afternoon front desk staff was especially helpful. for the price; it's just as good as days inn- quality inn if not better.

Having read mainly positive reviews about The Grace, and considered other more expensive options in Manhattan, we were pleased with our selection.
We booked a deluxe room, which was still pretty compact, but had room enough for two suitcases and plenty of shopping.
Note, the hotel web site also offers non-refundable rates which are -----% cheaper than flexibile rates.
Things we liked:
- Fantastic location...just off Times Square, but relatively quiet position.
- Beds very comfortable, with sumptuous linen.
- Walk-in monsoon shower.
- Continental breakfast with plump croissants, cereals, yogurt and fresh berries.
- The funky communal areas.
- The first room we were given smelt of stale smoke. I didn't remember being given an option when booking for smoking or non-smoking, but we were immediately given an alternative room.
- Swimming pool and sauna.
Things we didn't like:
- Room could have been bigger, but you get what you pay for.
- Window was draughty, which we fixed with the spare blanket.
- Water pressure in the shower was weak...shame when the wet room is so well designed.
- Heating in room worked well, but was VERY noisy.
Things other people may not like:
- Come Friday and Saturday night, the hotel bar and pool are open to the public and resemble something out of Spring Break. Didn't bother us, but might offend others.
Overall a good experience, and we'd probably stay there again.

We stayed at the Boston Harbor for two nights at the conclusion of a long and busy holiday.
It was a wonderful get away from our get away. The room, facing out over the harbor, was so well appointed, that I, an early riser, was able to sit and watch some morning television without disturbing my still sleeping SO.
The staff were brilliant, even when I had to phone up because I couldn't figure out how to turn a light on (the switch was all the way across the room), they were patient and helpful (I also assume they get that question quite a bit!)
The only real complaint is that any noise in the hallway echos into the room quite badly.

We use Tripadvisor for all our hotel choices when visiting a new city and as Magic Castle was rated #- in Los Angeles and the Hotel's own website shows lovely photos of a hotel """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""completely renovated in ----"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" we booked with confidence.
Apparently the ground floor consists of suites which are renovated, but the other rooms are certainly not renovated and are in fact quite shabby. The cleanliness was well below standard as the room was very dusty in all corners. Very old worn carpets, a functional but run down bathroom, a very noisy dilapidated air conditioning system and hard to control ceiling fan are among the highlights. 
On the plus side the room was a decent size, the bed was quite comfortable, there is an empty fridge which is useful and a desk, plus a large TV and a DVD player. The wardrobe is a fair size with large mirrors and a safe. On our last day we took the complimentary continental breakfast which was very good and we would have taken every day in hindsight, although there wasn't quite enough informal seating to accomodate all the guests wanting to sit outside. We found the staff to be varied - some were helpful when we asked for advice. However there was a general reluctance to change our traveller's cheques each day which seemed incredible - we were often told they """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""didn't have"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" $--- to change, but then go back and ask someone else and they would. 
This is a small apartment style hotel, with the feel of a beach hotel without the beach. The very small pool is the focal point around which the three or four floors of rooms are built - with no ramps or elevators! Getting your cases up the stairs is a nightmare! 
The location of the hotel is it's best feature. Our main reason for visiting was to see a show at the Hollywood Bowl which turned out to be a ----- minute walk which saved being stuck in traffic. The Chinese Theatre and other main attractions are - minutes walk away. However, there are numerous other hotels situated along the same road which would be worth investigating if you wish to stay in this location.
We would almost certainly not return to the Magic Castle hotel and would not recommend it to friends.

I recently stayed one night at this property on a business trip, and for many reasons, I almost wish I could have stayed longer to enjoy my hotel room! It was one of the largest big-city downtown hotel rooms I've ever seen (that wasn't an executive suite). Even for an Embassy Suites (which always have the two-room set-up), the room was exceptionally large. The view from my room of downtown Philly was nice, and the room had two balconies (one in the living area and one in the bedroom) that you could actually go out on and enjoy the city view from. The hallway between the bedroom and bathroom had a mirror, dressing table, and was well-lit, so for a party with multiple people trying to get ready in the morning, this would have been an ideal setup. The front desk staff were very friendly and allowed me to check in an hour early. The free breakfast buffet was fine - not the best I've seen but just fine with a decent variety of hot and cold foods, and it was located in the TGI Friday's on the hotel's property. The only complaint I have about my stay is with the shower. The water pressure was so poor that I actually wondered if there was a plumbing problem in the room. It took forever to get the shampoo rinsed out of my hair with the dribble of water coming out of the showerhead. Not sure if this was an issue for all the rooms or just mine. And, the drain in the shower was clogged with a lot of filth and hair, which floated up into the tub and around my feet while I was showering. So, other than some plumbing issues, which perhaps were only present in this particular room, I can't say anything bad about this hotel, and I would most certainly stay there again.

Location fine for Union Square. Hotel is now decidedly tired in parts. No executive club. Parking much cheaper across street. Wind noise in tower one with balcony room made sleep hard, sp best avoided. Shame, used to be much better. Upgrade has taken far too long.

Fantastic boutique hotel in a great location. Personal service and recognition from the hotel staff members at every turn. Cole, a front desk manager, was a pleasure to meet. 
The rooms are somewhat small, but well appointed. I would gladly return to this hotel.

I have just returned from New York after a - night stay at the Raddisson with my other half and have to confess I was relieved not to have any of the experiences I had read about in other reviews! We arrived before our room was ready but that was not a problem, our bags were sorted out by Mike at the porters desk who was really helpful and nice, all the staff we encountered were. The room itself overlooked the Empire State Building which really made us realise that yes we were in the big apple! the room wasn't massive but I would not describe it as small either, we were on the --th floor. The bathroom was small but there was enough space for us, most hotel bath rooms from my experience are small in any event. We had requested a none smoking room and that is exactly what we got, I have chest problems and we emailed expedia after reading some of the reviews to ensure that we would get a no smoking room and they emailed the manager at the hotel who ensured them that the room would be no smoking.
The location of the hotel is great, two blocks from Macy's, the Empire State Building is also just around the corner and Times Square is no more than a - minute walk away. We didn't eat in the hotel restaraunt which is located next door, it looked nice but we found so many nice places to eat in the area, the hotel is very convieniently situated for sightseeing, shopping, everthing really. The subway is relatively easy to use once you have figured out which way you are travelling. The only thing that we wanted to see which was some distance away was the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island but again this can be accessed via the subway.
The hotel arranged for a car to take us from the hotel to the airport the day we were leaving to continue our trip in Boston, Rebecca on the Concierge desk sorted all of this and again was very helpful and lovely to deal with,
I would stay here again, it was value for money, conveniently located and just what we wanted.

My husband and I stay here almost every Sunday night for business purposes. By far the best for less in San Diego !! The rooms are always fresh and clean and the front desk girl at this hotel is very helpful and friendly, all the time and every time. This is a great mid-price hotel !!

Now that they have completed the room renovations - this once again is a grand hotel!
I've stayed here several times - and on previous stays (prior to renovation) I had to rely on excellent union square location and friendly service - (while overlooking the guest rooms) - to be pleased with my stay. But now post-renovation the rooms are comfy and very tastefully decorated. Loved the new beds, furniture, carpets, drapes, and the art! All brand new and beautiful!
This stay was for my wedding - so we had several out of town guests who all raved about the hotel. (Even though the wedding itself was in wine country - we decided to stay here so our guests could get a taste of the city). All my guests appreciated the great location and the friendliness of the staff.
The hotel staff was fantastic, and I would be remiss if I didn't complement Scala's Restaurant there at the hotel. We had several meals there - both breakfasts and dinners and all were fantastic. For breakfast you must try the crab benedict -- and for dinners the risotto was always amazing. Special complements to DeeDee who was a super cheerful and attentive server.
Thanks for a great stay at a great hotel!

Loved the decor, service, and amenities. Nice rooms, reliable WiFi, nice poolside bar. Very nice fitness facilities. The location of the hotel excellent - right at the entrance to the Gaslamp District, and walking distance to the harbor and baseball stadium. The only downside to the location, especially for the noise sensitive, is the very load train that passes by (and whistles) several times during the night.

This Hotel is worthy of honors all around. From the world class atmosphere, to the Leadership Team of Managers to all of the employees, and even those who are behind the scene give world class care to every guest by treating them as if they were a part of the family. For nearly three years I and my Sister have enjoyed being a resident of Extended Stay Memphis. The quality care of service, the blessings and the privilege of knowing a great Leadership Team such as Operations Manager Eric Jefferson, Hotel Manager Tina, and the entire Hotel Staff make coming to Extended Stay Memphis, like staying at a World Class Hotel like the Four Seasons a dream come true.

Place is clean, creepy little haunt. Old school elevator, strange furniture in the rooms, feels like grandmas apartment. Close to the wharf, union station and chinatown. The price is right and you won't be in your room much so its perfect. They are helpful at the front desk also.
Cons...parking is - long blocks away and --$ a night, free parking if your car is smaller then a mini coupe.For some reason the room we got was above the alley where the loudest and longest trash pick up ever existed....at - am... nobody seemed to be staying there on a mon night in winter, so why not give us a quiet room, perhaps on a lower floor.

This noisy hotel is on the corner of Dearborn and Congress, two major streets with lots of buses and an above ground metro one block away. The double pain windows do not cut the noise. If you are from a city a love noise, then this is your hotel.
The rooms are beautiful and the beds are comfortable. That's a plus. We were upgraded to a corner room #---. Beautiful views. When I commented on the noise and said we could not sleep well, they said the only rooms above ours were suites. We kept our room.Trust me, it's noisy, throughout the night.
NO morning newspapers. NO twice daily maid service. NO bottled water. This used to be a Hyatt, but while claiming to be a boutique hotel they don't even get the most basic of hotel services. There are so few people staying here that the restaurant, Custom House, quit serving breakfasts because there wasn't enough business. If you want ice, you'll be going up to the --th floor to find the ice machine. The hallway carpets, at least on floor five were stained in several places and needed a deep cleaning.
This hotel is a mile from Sears Tower and a mile from Art Institute of Chicago. The same goes for Wrigley Field if you happen to be catching a Cubs game. OTHERWISE, there is nothing close to this hotel. It's on the far south end of the loop and boy did we boo-boo picking this hotel because it's not near anything. Well, the Chicago library is a block away as is the city jail! If you are looking for a hotel in the Miracle Mile area where most of the tourist activities take place, this is NOT the hotel to choose.
The hotel advertises a concierge, but it is really the front desk, which while as helpful as they try to be, are not trained concierges. Wireless service does not work in the lobby, though it does work in the rooms. 
The only reason to stay here is for the rock bottom hotel rates that can be found on some discount websites. There is also a Starbucks on the corner and Orange, a breakfast restaurant around the corner. 
All in all, we would never stay here again. The rooms are great but there is nothing else going on, unless you absolutely have appointments in this area, there are far better hotels with far better services in Chicago....and at similar prices. 
We thought this was a MISS and not a little miss a BIG MISS.

I am a self-proclaimed hotel snob. It's true...I like to stay in """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""nice"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotels, and I am willing to pay a premium to do so. However, with a college friend and her -- year old son coming to visit, I had different goals--namely, I wanted a well located hotel downtown for our -am visit at the White House. After shopping around, I decided on the Hilton Garden Inn on --th Street. 
I have to say, I could not have made a better choice. The price was very reasonable--and several hundred dollars less than the FS, the Ritz Carlton, the Hay Adams, the W, the Willard, etc. I really did shop around before booking! The location was outstanding (only a few blocks to the White House, a short walk to the Smithsonian, etc), they accommodated our --:--am arrival, they provided us with a rollaway for the -- year old for no extra charge, they allowed us a -:--pm checkout, they ran to my car and got my umbrella for me when I forgot it, provided a free ---hour business center with computers and a printer, had free internet in the rooms...simply above and beyond on ALL levels!
The room itself was utilitarian in design, but certainly roomy enough for - of us--- double beds, and the room easily accommodated a roll-away, they have Neutrogena amenities, the water pressure was good, etc. They provide an empty fridge, a microwave, a coffeemaker...all very nice. We had no view at all, except of nearby buildings and an alley, but the result was a nice, quiet room (and we were only on the -th floor, so I was a little worried).
A few people have commented that there are no local restaurants: Across the street to the right is a Five Guys burger joint--fun and quick and good. Across the street to the left (next to the Starbuck's) is the New York Cafe (on NY Ave)--a surprisingly good and cheap breakfast--we did not get the buffet, we all got breakfast sandwiches--but they were good and very reasonable. And the hotel restaurant has one of the best hamburgers I have had in a VERY long time! There is also the Old Ebbett's Grill on --th--a famous restaurant in DC that has very reasonable prices, and we ate lunch at the POV terrace in the W hotel--also on --th St--food and service were so-so, but the views are stunning from the top of the hotel. So, I do not understand the complaint that there is nowhere to eat nearby.
Is it my usual type of hotel? No. Would I stay here again and recommend it to others? In a heartbeat!

I stayed at the Renaissance Boston Waterfront hotel for two nights in September while attending a conference. There’s a lot to recommend about this hotel, as well as a few drawbacks.
It’s new (opened in February ----) and it looks it. Most everything is shiny, polished, and not showing any wear, which is as it should be. There’s a “water theme” throughout, with lots of blues and greens in the color scheme in common areas and the guest rooms. It’s convenient to Logan Airport, easily accessible by the Silver T line, and just two blocks from the World Trade Center stop.
Front desk personnel were gracious and efficient. Upon check-in, I was initially given a room with two queen beds although I had requested a king, and put on a lower floor near the elevator. I immediately went back to the front desk and I was moved to a room on a higher floor away from the elevator, though they still had no king rooms available. I questioned this, as I was checking in about - p.m. -- neither early nor late – but was told there simply were no king rooms available. When paying $--- a night, not getting what one requested is more difficult to accept than if I’d obtained a deeply discounted rate from a booking service.
The on-site restaurant – ---, for the hotel’s address – is described as an “American tappas” restaurant. The dinner menu features six categories ranging from salads and appetizers to main courses to a selection of cheeses. The food is very good and the variety excellent. --- also has a pretty decent wine list. But the service needs some improvement. Most of the wait staff I saw was quite young and, while they seated me, took my order, and delivered my food quickly, they didn’t check back to see if I needed anything until I had finished the food. That area should be targeted for improvement.
Housekeeping could also use some fine-tuning. When attending a conference, I HATE coming back to the room after lunch and finding it had still not been made up, so I called at - a.m. just before I left and requested service. When I returned at - p.m., it still had not been done. I find that very frustrating, especially since I’d requested service five hours earlier. 
The hotel has a well-equipped fitness center with individual TVs on the cardio equipment, as well as a pool and (usually) saunas for both men and women. The men’s sauna was out of order during my stay, which is unfortunate for such a new facility.
Guest rooms are nicely furnished and offer full connectivity (for a fee); they include large, flat-screen TVs (HBO and other movie channels included) which can also be hooked to your computer and doubles as a monitor; and iHome radios by the bed. However, the rooms do lack a few things. There are no in-room safes, which I find very useful when traveling with my laptop. It could also have used a table and chair in addition to the desk; otherwise, any in-room dining would have to be eaten at the desk or on the bed. And the towels are far too thin considering the higher-end nature of this property.
All in all, a pleasant stay and a hotel I would stay at again.

We booked this hotel through hotwire (@ ---night) for a weekend trip to view the bears vs. cowboys. - Bears fans of course :) We thought that being on the actual airport would be out of the way. However it was conveniently located. We stayed in an oversize corner room and it worked out very well for our family of -. Numerous restaurants and shopping malls were close by and the hotel itself appeared not too far away from anything. Parking and internet was free and all of the airport tolls were validated so no extra expense for us. They do have dining options at the hotel but we did not dine due to it being a little pricey and so many other close options. The pool was open, but quite cold. There is a -- hour snack shop in the hotel for those midnight cravings. Customer service was excellent as everyone was helpful. I would recommend this hotel and would stay again. 
FYI: they do offer a shuttle to cowboys games but at -- pp. Parking at the stadium is ----- per car... you do the math.

We stayed at this hotel due to ratings on tripadvisor. It is spotless and beautiful. The hotel is small but it is so gorgeous that the size becomes a non-issue. The windows were open when we checked in and, for this Louisiana mom, that was surprising! But, since we were in San Francisco, it was refreshingly cool and...not a single mosquito! As stated in previous reviews, the wine and cheese hour is nice. My son was also able to enjoy cheese, crackers and soft drinks. We enjoyed coming in at night and getting a fresh chocolate chip cookie in the lobby on our floor. In addition, I cannot say enough about the staff at this hotel. We stayed in - different hotels on this -,--- mile driving vacation and this staff would rate #- of all. Their help and suggestions saved us lots of trial and error getting around an unfamiliar area. I did want to use a microwave one night but did not have access to one. I left a suggestion for the manager that a microwave in the lobby area of the floors that served breakfast might be useful. If I had to name one inconvenience it would be that there is no parking at this hotel. I circled around to this hotel twice before I gave up and called the hotel to ask about parking. We were told to pull up to the front of the hotel and they called a valet service. Parking through this service was $-- a day. I was assured that it was in a secure lot and the staff notified the lot when I was ready for my car. I would highly recommend this hotel and I will definitely stay here again when I'm in the area.

From the initial booking with the manager Paul, everything was perfect and at a great price! We had two rooms- both with queen size pull out sofas. The rooms were modern, comfortable and modern. Breakfast was served every morning in the dining room. Nice choices, fresh fruit, coffee, tea, pastries, cereal, and OJ.
The staff are amazing!! Paul, Milton and company are friendly, kind and so helpful!!!
We thouroughly enjoyed our - day-- night stay at the historic Hotel Brexton and will return there in the future!!!!
Thank you Hotel Brexton for such great hospitality!

My husband and I stayed here and were given a corner room on the --th floor. The room was very nice. The bed was extremely comfortable. While the location is walking distance to everything you want to go to, as well as close to the T, the area is dead at night. Downtown is smelly and filled with homeless people sleeping in the streets. The pool was cold, but the exercise room and steamroom were nice. Overall, this hotel would be a lot nicer if it were - blocks away.

The hotel is located at very good location. We can easily walk to Empire State Building and Macy. It is also walkable to Times Square, Public Library and Central Terminal from the hotel. It is also close to subway station. 
However, hotel provides us a small room with a poorly designed and maintained bathroom. It is very different from the photos showing in websites. 
Though the bathroom is poor, I still recommend this hotel to friends due to the location.

Before even getting to San Diego, we had some problems with our reservations. Pat at the front desk was patient and helpful. When we got to the hotel, we were excited to meet Pat because he was so fabulous over the phone. Pat made sure we had everything we needed. Pat knew a lot about the area, and helped us to decided where to eat and shop etc. When we came in from the beach, Pat always had a smile on his face, and was nice enough to let us tell him about our adventures. Pat always made sure we had plenty of room towels and beach towels. Our stay at the Ocean Park Inn was absolutey perfect. The rooms were very nice, and clean. The location was perfect. The view was amazing. Everything was withing walking distance. The staff at Ocean Park Inn was so helpful the entire stay. Ralph, the security guard made sure we were safe, and Jesus at the front desk was very friendly. We made sure to tell Pat we would miss him when we went, and we hope he is still working there when we come back again because he made our stay so much fun!!!
I can not wait to stay at the Ocean Park Inn again!!!! I may have to wait a whole year and that just makes me sad!!! I had the best time ever!! Thanks Pat!!!

From the moment I arrived every aspect of my stay was first class. The room was luxurious and the staff made me feel like I was at home.
The superb accommodations were complemented by a lineup of magnificent events. The band, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Joy Ride,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" provided a great medley of musical arrangements that included Motown classics at the New Year's Eve Ball. The accompanying disc jockey was a great complement. We also had the opportunity to attend the event at Club Ignite. The evening's host, Sugar Hill Gang, was most gracious. They took time to pose for pictures and discuss the hip hop musical genre. In addition, we had an opportunity to visit """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""INT ICE"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" where Charles and Gwen Scales performed. These types of world class entertainers demonstrate why MGM Grand Detroit is a premier entertainment destination that I will continue to recommend to friends, colleagues and constituents.

Lets face it, it's a highway hotel. Cheap but not exactly cheery. We paid $-- a night each for two rooms. Nice was the wifi and mini fridge. Lots of lighted parking. Downside were the ants in the room... Thin towels and sheets...no continental breakfast like some Red Roofs, or the competing Baymont or Econolodge.
The room was clean enough, but behind the beds are disgusting, so maybe that is why there are ants? I was in room ---.
It's pet friendly.
We'll try elsewhere next time in Austin.

My husband I just got back from a night out to celebrate our anniversary. The hotel was great. The staff was very nice and helpful. The tub and shower are awesome. The room was good, a few things could of been better, our jetted tub didn't work,we asked for a late check out and were told no even though we wanted to blow our money in the casino during that time. Some areas of the hotel smelled like bad cologne. I felt like my lungs were filling with it. I think someone with asthma would find that a problem. I think they are using it to cover smoke smell.
We had a great time with all that said. I do think its worth trying.

After a - day nightmare just up the street at the howard Johnson the Best Western was like paradise. the staff was amazing and the room was even better! clean, spacious, and organized.
they even bumped us up to a mini suite after explaining what we had been through. i would recomend this hotel to anyone working on a budget and still looking for great service.

The shuttle didn't run to Union Station daily as advertised, which is a problem as taxis don't normally come by. There were no restaurants or fast food places adjacent to the hotel as described. Upon checkout there was an additional $-.-- on the bill,( which was removed). The front desk was not knowledgeable or helpful.

The Alexander Inn was great....a beautiful lobby, welcoming staff, excellent continental breakfast, comfortable room, etc. The neighborhood (Washington Square) was mostly gay & has interesting shops, restaurants, etc. 
The hotel has been tastefully decorated; there is artwork in the hallways & jazz softly playing while you wait for the elevator.
The view from our room was of downtown Philly; having grown up in NYC & lived in San Francisco, we enjoy cityscape views, so this was perfect for us. We would definitely recomment the Alexander Inn.

This place is ideally located and overall a good place to stay. the rooms are HUGE for Manhattan standards and well- appointed. The front desk staff are helpful and very professional. I loved the bed, audio in our room and the overall size of our room.
Negatives: tiny elevators and the long wait as one was being serviced. Also there is no free ice or free anything for that matter, then again you are in NYC!
Super cool boutique hotel

The good:
The first ever free breakfast I've encountered that has eggs, sausages, and belgian waffles as options in addition to the regular cereals, etc. Horrid coffee, but I'm a coffee snob. Coffee maker in the room (though no filters, fellow snobs who try to bring your own), clean, pool and hot tub if you're so inclined, basic amenities and basically what you'd expect from a Quality Inn and it's ilk. Free shuttle into town (at least there was one offered for Comic Con, which is why we were there.) Free wireless internet in the room. Practically walking distance to airport and Point Loma Naval Base. If this was all there was to it, I wouldn't complain...
But oh dear lord, the bar. There's a bar downstairs that plays music mercilessly loud (and we're young. And we were there for Comic Con!) until midnight weekdays and two a.m. weekends. The room literally shook with the noise. The air conditioning system is very weak and very loud, so while it may seem smart to just open the windows (since by nightfall it's cooler out there anyway), the noise from the bar prevents this option. So you listen to the rattle of the air conditioner as it tries to drown the music... The prices were EXORBITANTLY expensive for what we got and way over any other quotes here, but they were clearly driven up because of the convention (I believe it was $----night for - people and close to $----night for -...absolutely ridiculous!) For some reason, the shower head is installed at about -'-"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", so you have to go into a full yoga chair pose in order to rinse your hair - I think my -'-"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" friend just didn't bathe the whole weekend because it was too difficult to maneuver. The hotel is a bit far from San Diego itself, but if you plan on driving around to Seaworld, the zoo, etc., it's decently located. But I wouldn't stay here unless you are required by your boss or some other draconian measure.
Summary: good breakfast, nice staff, decent accommodations; horribly loud, bad shower, bad air conditioning.

This hotel was ok. Nothing really all that special about it. It is an element the new brand from Westin, so it has all of that brands little touches. These include: parking spaces for hybrids, recycle bins in your room, and other little """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""green"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""healthy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" touches. I didn't really like the free breakfast a lot, but that is a personal taste. There was absolutely nothing wrong with it. The room was ok, but the shower head did not work very well. This was frustrating, because the weather was cool and a nice hot shower would be nice, but it wasn't because the shower didn't work correctly. There was no bathtub in my room. I also didn't like how housekeeping wouldn't take my trash out of my little trash can. Since I was there for a week, this was frustrating. Again, this hotel doesn't really have any major problems, because it is new, but it isn't really anything special. The rooms are a little uncomfortable, except for the beds, which are nice. I also liked that they had a little port for you to plug in all of your electronics and chargers and such. Good for a low price, but if they charge typical Houston rates I would look elsewhere.

This hotel's location is fantastic. It is a half-block away from the MTA Subway system and just a few blocks from Penn Station. Also very close to ESB and Times Square is walkable. As is typical of most NYC hotels, the rooms are old and very small. I also found my room to be a bit noisy and drafty. But the room was clean and the staff very pleasant. The breakfast is also quite nice.

Myself and my husband and two friends stayed in The Palomar for - nights at the end of August. We were starting our holiday in Chicago and then doing a road trip for two weeks through Wisconsin across to Michigan and finishing back in Chicago.
I had got fantastic rates for the Palomar when I booked for us a couple of months prior to our stay and having stayed in a Kimpton Hotel in San Fransisco last year, knew generally what to expect (including the free evening wine party).
Everything about the hotel was fantastic, the way we were greeeted on arrival, our lovely rooms and the location of the hotel with great restaurants, jazz & blues clubs and bars all nearby. We also received numerous free vouchers for cocktails in Sable bar attached to the hotel as we knew the password for the month when checking in (Check Facebook-Twitter). There is a wonderful terrace on the roof with a pool where you can relax for a while if the weather is good as it was when we were there.
Unfortunately, the rates had greatly increased when we enquired about returning for our last - nights so we stayed elsewhere but all the great reviews about this hotel are accurate and we would have no hesitation in recommending it - go you wont be disappointed.

I just recently spent two weeks at the Bahia for business. I was leery due to some of the comments I read here. Overall, I thought it was a good value and wasn't unsatisfied.
I was in the --- section. My patio opened right up to the bay side beach and the front door was close to the sidewalk that leads to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""boardwalk"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and beach.
Yes, the rooms are somewhat dated and worn, but mine was kept very clean. The staff was very attentive, accommodating, and friendly during my stay. The resort is close to the airport, convenient to bus stops, Seaworld, and the beach.
There are a few good places to eat within walking distance; I especially liked the taco shop on the nearby corner and the pizza place (Big Papas) just a couple of doors down.
I know that some of my coworkers weren't happy with their original rooms but the staff moved them to better ones. It also appeared that they were in the process of doing some renovating; I know that they were replacing carpet and furnishings in the section I was in.
Overall, I would not have any problem with staying here again or recommending this hotel.

There was a mouse in my room. There is little water pressure in the shower and they are hard to turn off; if you're not careful it will run and run. The hotel is not one of the cheapest but there are deals to be had via Expedia and such like. The location was totally fantastic. Could not have asked for better in that regard I could have asked.for free WiFi, and think that it is not too much to ask for. Would recommend only for the location, nothing else, be warned.

This is a large, relatively undifferentiated hotel, well located in the heart of downtown on the main shopping street. It is quite acceptable and comfortable, if unmemorable. It is particularly convenient for events in the conference centre to which it is attached. By the way, it's no fault of the hotel, but the conference center itself is a confusing rabbit-warren. Get clear directions from the concierge if that's your destination!

We needed to drop off our bag and get to the theatre, we pulled up and Waku grabbed our bag, gave us a claim check and got us on our way in a matter of a couple of minutes. Great location, the staff is very outgoing and cannot do enough for you. Kimpton's Wine Hour is a nice way to start your evening. We had a jacuzzi suite and it was really nice and very clean. Located in Times Square it is centrally located. Love their personalized service with handwritten notes from managers-assistant managers (thanks Samantha!).

The Abri is in a great location just --- block from the Market and Powell cable car station, --- block from the BART station and walking distance to a number of restaurants and shopping. 
We were in town for a business trip but brought my toddler with. When I called to get a crib in the room, the staff spontaneously provided us with an upgraded room and inner room. The room was surprisingly quiet. The fixtures are modern. There is no tub in the bathroom.
I had - minor critiques: the living room in the suite did not have a fan or window air conditioning unit. Therefore, it was pretty hot in there at night which is where my mom slept. Secondly, the internet access while free and wireless (big plus) is really slow. 
The hotel staff were so nice and friendly. 
When we are in SF again, we will definitely stay there again.

The location is midtown and it is near Central Park and very close to Times square and all the touristy stuff your little heart might desire to see. I loved being able to walk to the MoMA and Central Park. It was also a lovely walk to all of the -th avenue shops as well.
The hotel appears to be in a state of renovation of some kind. Our first room was totally modern and upgraded. I loved our lovely view of Central Park. Unfortunately we were unable to stay in our room the second night because someone had rented out our whole floor. We were then moved to the exact same room a few floors up. Unfortunately that room was not upgraded and I did not like it nor did I want to stay in it. However, when we complained to the front desk they were super-helpful and moved us. We ended up getting upgraded to a junior suite, which was nice. I appreciated the effort that the front desk put into making our family happy.
From other reviews people seem really annoyed about having to pay for the gym and the pool. It's $-- and you're already paying a lot for a hotel room so... Also you can pay $-- for a gym-pool combo per room. That is seriously not a lot of money, and the pool has a beautiful view of the park. The basement of this hotel is also seriously cool. It has a spa, a blow dry bar, nail salon and a coffee shop. Best little underground cluster ever.
Last but not least, it also has a cool bar and of course Norma's restaurant. Room service was also quite tasty.
Stay here if you are looking for a nice hotel in Midtown :)

While this isn't exactly the Ritz, the price is definitely right ($---). The rooms were clean & nicely furnished, albeit a bit small (although that doesn't really matter to me as I spent very little time other than sleeping in the room). It's in a great spot, very close to the North End which has the best restaurants in the city. The staff was really friendly & helpful - they allowed us to leave our bags, even though we had checked out & let my husband's parents do the same & they hadn't even stayed there! We would have stayed another night, but they ended up booked so we moved to the Club Quarters (which was a bit nicer, but more expensive & in a less ideal location). I don't recommend their restaurant for breakfast, but the lunch-dinner menu was great. I would definitely stay here again, great location!

This hotel was the best! The guest room was large, tastfully decorated, quiet, and comfortable. The front desk personnel, doormen and concierge could not have been more helpful, friendly or courteous. The hotel is also extremely well located, within a short walking distance to Pike's Market, the Art Museum, many fine restaurants, the waterfront, and other Seattle attractions.

Our stay was absolutely fabulous. I have never stayed in such a wonderful hotel with such useful staff. I don't know what the guy from Dallas was talking about, but our stay couldnt possibly be any better. Highly recommended

This is the only - star review I have ever given. 
Since moving from NYC to NJ, my husband and I make a weekend trip to NYC once a month. The last time we stayed at the Benjamin and it was really a flawless stay. When we arrived, our room was not ready, but they were able to upgrade us to a one-bedroom suite. Generally, in NYC, one bedroom suite just means they had enough room to squeeze in a desk, a couple of chairs and a little efficiency kitchenette set. However, my first apartment in NYC was smaller than the suite at the Benjamin. It had a true living room and a separate kitchen area with everything that a longer term guest would need. 
The staff is amazing. Khady checked us in and was incredibly courteous and very quick. The bellman, the doormen, the conceirage, everyone goes out of their way to help you and make sure you are happy. 
The hotel is centrally located with both eastside and westside trains being easily accessible. 
The Benjamin also has -- hour room service. After a very dissapointing diner experience as another restaurant, we came back and order a burger and fries. It may have been the best burger I have ever eaten (sorry mom!). 
I cannot say enough good things about this place. It is a wonderful place with wonderful staff.

Hotel was awesome! Sexy, modern style, on a weekend night you might think you are in a nightclub when you are in the lobby! Bar was awesome, blonde female bartender (cant remember name) was friendly and kept the drinks coming...probably why I cant remember her name. Ate at IPO (hotel restaurant) for breakfast, loved the choriza chicken breakfast burrito! Laurelin, the concierge, gave great dinner recommendations and also gave info on what bars to hit and provided managers names in case we had any trouble getting in on a busy Saturday night. Room Service (chicken sandwich, burger) was fast and good. Overall, cant say anything bad about this hotel. Within walking distance of the Mag Mile and tons of great restaurants, shopping!

Myself and two others stayed in a room here for two nights. I have to admit that I was skeptical going with a small Super - in San Francisco, but I was pleasantly surprised. The rooms seem to have been recently updated with nice crown molding and light fixtures. 
The beds were actually quite comfortable and provided a good nights sleep even with two grown adults sharing one bed. 
The front desk folks were extremely helpful and always available when needed. I had actually seen a hotel down the street with a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lobby closed for the night"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sign at the front door and some unfortunate man locked out and unable to check in. That was not the case at this hotel. 
While we were there I saw many people walk up to check availability so you can tell the location and price was right. 
Just a block walk from a major bus stop that brings you wherever you want! 
Parking is a pain with only about - spots for the entire hotel. I would suggest leaving your car elsewhere or not moving your car during your stay if you actually happen upon a parking spot. 
A great little place to stay and well worth the price! I will definitely be staying here again if I go back to San Fran on vacation.

...and that's a good thing. In a world of wheatgrass patches, plastic chairs and neon lights in the elevator, the Carlton stands out for being a classic New York building. Sure, the lobby has gone modern, but the hallways and rooms are well done and tasteful. I loved this location, easy to two different subways lines, on edge of Union Square, and walkable to Grand Central if you needed. The desk was large enough to work on, and the front desk staff super friendly. Molton Brown products in the bathroom, nice!

I stayed here for business and probably wouldn't pay the $---+-night rate if I had to foot the bill. There are a lot more nicer hotels in the area for about the same amount. The check in was a little intimidating as the staff wasn't very outgoing, however they were very professional and polite. The size of the room was decent and the bathroom was stocked with Philosophy products, which is a definite bonus. Room service from their restaurant downstairs was mediocre bordering on bland. The only truly bad experience I had while staying at the hotel was when I reached up to grab the ice bucket from the ledge in the room and a buckful of WATER splashed all over me. 
Apparently house cleaning didn't bother to empty it out after the last guest.

This hotel is very nice and clean, but for me not a top-notch property. It's like staying at a Wyndham or similar hotel. It would be nice to have a coffeemaker in the room and a fridge would be nice. There is a mini-bar, but you have to call room-service to unlock it. I would like to have a place to keep a chilled bottle of wine or soda. My other beef is with the valet. The hotel's lot fills up and can't accommodate all the guests' vehicles. I took my car out in the evening and asked the valet if I would have any problem when I came back later in the evening and he said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""you shouldn't."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Well I know I shouldn't, but when I returned at midnight the valets were gone and the lot was full. I found an employee to take my car, but he was looking around like he was looking for a place to park it on the street. Not acceptable when you're paying $-- per day just to park your car. 
The hotel is right across from Horton Plaza, so shopping and restaurants are nearby. (Don't miss the St. Tropez bakery-cafe across the street for breakfast). Unlike most hotels whose windows only open a crack, all the rooms have sliding glass doors that open, which is great to get the fresh air. But overall its published rates are outrageously high for what you get.

need i say more....we have stayed there about - times...i wouldnt rate it as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""real"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" clean..our feet were always black. This last time I had to have them replace the matress. I kept smelling pee and finally stuck my nose down to the sheets and wanted to puke.I was extremely upset about it, there is NO excuse but they replaced it and no we did not get a discount. I would suggest you all check your matress because so many children stay there and all they put on it is a very thin flimsy cover.. we love the lazy river and the slide. if you stay off season it is totally worth it but the --- a day on weekends and summer is rediculous. The food is NOTHING SPECIAL and very high but after a few frozen margaritas at the river, who wants to drive. Movie night is fun for the kids and smores.

My friend and I wanted a weekend getaway to NYC for some shopping & girl time. We didn't want to spend a lot, and I was thrilled to find the Belnord which looked nice and was in a good neighborhood AND less than $----night, including tax!
I booked it, and THEN I read the reviews. Bedbugs, tiny rooms, shared bathrooms. We didn't care that the room was tiny, because lets face it: we didn't come to NYC to sit around our room. The shared bathroom we weren't that concerned about either because we figured we were only gone one night, and if it was really nasty, we'd just wait until we got home the next night to take showers. The bedbug reviews, however, totally freaked me out. I knew I couldn't cancel my reservation, and I knew we couldn't afford any other hotels in decent neighborhoods.
My friend's mom made her read - articles and watch a video on bedbugs and GAVE HER A QUIZ before we left! She is so funny. I was feeling okay, though, because I had read other reviews about the Belnord that said other people had read the bedbug reviews after booking, had been really freaked out, but had no problems whatsoever. I relaxed.
THEN we got to the hotel. It was too early to check in, but the nice guy behind the desk let us leave our luggage in a luggage room while we spent some time sightseeing. While we were at the desk, a girl about our age was checking out of the hotel and said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""You might want to look into that room, because I woke up with these bites all over me! Look, I have like -- bites and I itch like crazy! There's definitely something in that room!"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" We flipped out. We listened to her say her room number, which was ----something. We made a mental note in case they tried to give us that room. While we were sightseeing, we tried to come up with a plan. Sleep in bugspray? A scuba suit? Find a dog that was sick with a fever and let it sleep with us, since bedbugs seek out the warmest body???
When we checked in, they did not give us that room. My friend knew what to look for, so as soon as we got to the (tiny) room, we tore it apart. The room was -- feet by - feet, no lie.
