*Staff very receptive and accommodating to requests, from extra towels, linens and just trying to figure out how to get to where we needed to go. Even the staff handling our bags were fabulous.
*Concierge level amazing with offerings.
*Connected to the Prudential and over --- shops.
*Valet parking.
*Amazing view of the Charles River and Hancock Building.
*I will certainly stay here again.
*Lots of closet space.
*T to Prudentail vs Copley stop so you can stay inside vs walking outside.
Neutrals:
*Small bathrooms with sink in the bathroom. Though functional, despite several women and girls having to get ready at the same time.
*First fridge smelled like sour milk and made all our snacks and beverage smell. Though a replacement was obtained quickly.
*Housekeeping overly wanting to get into our room. We put up the do not disturb sign our second night.
*No table and chairs in living room area.
Negatives:
*Valet parking cost $-- a night.
*Torn wallpaper in adjoining room bathroom.
*Not warned about handicapped room.
*Biggest pet peave - hallway filled with dishes, etc throughout each day of our stay (- days). These were not picked up until later in the night, I would say after eight pm. I think this should have been monitored better. One night it was an awful site to see the number of dishes in the hallway, especially when our breakfast dishes were in the hallway later in the evening.
*The pool looks like it's picture on the Marriott website, except the view is not the same as the picture - they must have photoshopped the buildings. The picture view from the pool was an exciting one for us, but the reality was nothing like the picture on the website - I think this was very deceiving by Marriott. The view from the --nd floor was amazing and worth staying in our room for and having a few drinks.

Both me and my husband recently stayed here and was not informed that smoking outside on a balcony constitutes as smoking inside a room. We were charged $--- (more than the cost of our --night stay) for him smoking on the outdoor balcony. This fee was never disclosed and the website even states the fee is to return rooms back to their non-smoking condition. He never smoked in teh room!! I should know becuase I can't stnad the smell of smoke and he would not smoke anywhere around me. This is rediculous and smokers should be warned. All Marriott hotels are nonsmoking and even if you choose to smoke outside, be prepaed for a hefty fine!!
And to make matters worse, God forbid you rent a car or drive there because it's going to cost you $-- a day to park at the hotel even if you're an overnight guest!! Aren't we paying enough already to stay there? You think they'd at least afford us to convience of parking at the hotel for free.

Don't be fooled by the enterance. The rooms are small and to go to the toilet you have to squeeze between the sink and the wall. They use disgusting motel - style soap pumps in the shower and do not even offer a bar of soap for the shower. The windows and walls are extremely thin so I had a horrible night sleep. No HBO or any other free movie chanel. The elevators are extremly slow. They do not supply a basic coffee maker or refrigerator.

Had a conference at the hotel. It's typical of a JW in that it's high end and has a lot of amenities. It is massive though, so not everything is at your fingertips. Lots of walking between rooms and various activities. Enjoyed a massage at Revive Spa. I recommend having lunch at the Spa Cafe. It's healthy and reasonable, compared to other places. Roy's is always a good choice for a very nice meal. The Concierge did a great job of helping us arrange dinners off property. We had a wonderful meal at Ocean Prime, which is across the road, but a $- cab ride, because you wouldn't want to walk over in the heat. I also had to rend a car for the day, but that was super easy because Hertz has a location on site. Because this was for business, I did not go to the pool, but others reported that the pool was really nice. And some even brought their kids and said the water park was terrific.

I'm giving this hotel an average rate because:
- it is in a good location (you can walk to Union Square and the Chinese quarter), there are many nice restaurants nearby (one of them is the French one just beside)
- I loved the hall, it is modern but at the same time has a quicky feeling that is just cool, not too much. You can grab some apples and often there is a woman reading cards... as I said it's quicky enough but in a good way.
- The rooms are modern, I loved that I could plug in mu ipod-iphone and listen to my music, however, the rooms are sooo tiny.... I know it is in line with the stardands of the city but it's a bit exagerate! (I've been to other hotels in SF and had much bigger rooms).
- it's quite pricey for what it offers, I mean, nothing is included and rooms are claustrophobic.
-Last day we had to print our flight booking and they wouldn't allow us to print as they didn;t have a PC for guests. it was kind of an emergency and after soooo long they have printed it for us BUT we had to PAY for each sheet of paper printed. i found this disappointing as in exceptional circumstances, they should have helped as they could.
Overall, you can find hotels with bigger rooms but if you like a modern and quicky feeling, being in the centre of the city, this is for you. Just go with the right expectations!

If it's your first time in NYC, choose this hotel. It's easy to see all the other parts of the city. After all you're in MIDTOWN (!) Manhattan ;-) The price was okay, and the room was bigger than I had expected acually, from what I had heard in advance of the hotel-rooms in NYC. The room was very clean. But - drawbacks: Half of the staff was really helpfull and pleasant, but the other half seemed only semi-interested in the guests. The breakfast area was really small and over-crowded early in the morning. And, what's the deal with the swimming pool? Why not use the space to build a bigger bar-breakfast area? It was so easy to watch in on the people who used the pool thru the glass walls by the elevator and bar that my girlfirend and I were too shy to jump in...
All in all, I enjoyed my stay. And despite these minor drawbacks I would recommend this hotell for couples (and small families with teenagers) who wants to live on the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""crossroad of the world"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" at Times Square.. :-)

We hesitantly booked a stay at the Sheraton after our last bad experience a year ago. Unfortunately, things did not go any better this stay, we had an event happening in the hotel and decided to give it another shot. First the positives, the hotel is pet friendly and the rooms are nice overall. For a Sheraton, this hotel continues to be a huge disappointment. My husband had called to upgrade our room prior to our stay, when we got to the hotel-there was no upgrade, they supposedly had nothing in the reservation, when asked, they did have an upgraded room but we would have had to wait for over an hour or so to get in to it. Luckily, they were able to give us a room with a great view for the Parade of Lights. We were supposed to stay two nights and cancelled the second-good thing. We paid for the club level access which included free wi-fi and breakfast, huge mistake. We went up to the club lounge for breakfast to find there was nothing left, it was messy and the girl working could really care less about all of the people who were coming to eat without having any food available. Mark my words, this was my LAST stay at the downtown Sheraton, with so many other options you would be a fool to stay here!

I had read a few - pretty awful - reviews about this hotel beforehand and was a little dubious about what to expect. Bad service, terrible rooms, noisy? We felt that the service was excellent, especially at reception. The room was enormous and the bed could have slept - comfortably - well, at least -. OK, the decor was a little dated and the TV was in a peculiar place, but you don't visit Washington to watch TV. The location was superb with the Smithsonian museums an easy -- minute walk away. We went on an open top bus and it picked us up and dropped us off directly outside the hotel. What more do you need? I will say that the Foggy Bottom Pub isn't a pub - a pub should have more than three tables and a beer shouldn't cost $-.--. The breakfast was also pricey at $--, but it was a good spread and quite tasty. It was also a little noisy, but that was due to the mass of air-conditioning units the Americans seem to need. We had a room overlooking the pool, but I can imagine a room facing towards the south on the outside would have a problem with traffic noise. 
All in all, I would recommend this hotel and would stay there again. We were told that a major renovation is planned, which began with the gym and will eventually revamp the whole hotel. It does need updating, but was still part of a week we won't forget very quickly :-)

This hotel has a good location near Central Park. I just got back from the hotel. Here's the problem: guests have no way to control the temperature in their room. The first night we were there, the NYC air was unseasonably warm. Being from the south, we like our air conditioning. There was not only no air, but the furnace would not turn off. We called the desk and they said it is centrally controlled--- nothing we could do to turn it off. Finally, about -am, my son and I were sweat down in our bed and we each had a massive headache, so we searched for a way to open the window. After much effort, we got it open, but then the rest of the night we could hear all the street noise, and I ended up sitting up to protect my son in case someone tried to come through the window. A truly miserable night. The hallways are dirty, and there were stains on my sheets. I was so grossed out that I slept in all my clothes and laid a layer of towels over the sheets. I am not particularly a clean freak-- just a normal person-- so if you happen to be a little on the OCD side, you would flip out.
We had intened to stay for a week, but checked out after two nights (because we had to give -- hours notice) and checked into the Hotel Edison in Times Square, which was incredible. We paid the same for each of the two rooms. By comparison, the hotel Edison was a suite with a seperate sitting area and a pullout sofa. Plus it was walking distance to Times Square.
The only thing Park -- has going for it is being near Central Park.

They try. They really try. But the Hotel QT's insistence on being hip gets in its way.
The good: Great location. Tiny room, but that's why they call it a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""boutique"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel. Clean. I hear that breakfast is included, but since it's served starting at -am, I had to miss it to make an -am train. The young woman at the front desk was friendly and helpful, although she sent me to a non-existent restaurant. Oh well. It happens. Nevertheless, these are true strong points.
But, when the designers had to choose between being functional or hip, they went for hip every time. For example, the shower head in my room was stylish. About a foot across, it hung directly above me. Very pretty. But, a foot-wide shower head disperses whatever water pressure it gets. As a result, you can't really shampoo your hair in it (especially if you have more hair than I do, which let's hope you do). And because it's fixed above you, you can't rinse the downward-facing parts of your body. Ahem.
Not to mention that the shower area (an open part of the open bathroom -- very hip, unless you're rooming with someone you don't want to strip in front of) has an outside window as one wall. The window is frosted ... but only halfway up. Why oh why do the QT's designers think we all want to show off our nakedness to the building across the street?
Likewise, the bed is on a platform with a lip jutting out. Since the rooms are not all that well lei, and because I am a klutz (all part of not being hip), I kept barking my shins on it. Just another example of a design decision made with hipness rather than functionality in mind.
if stark, clean lines matter to you more than being able to take a good shower in a private room, then you will genuinely enjoy this hotel. But, either it is too hip or I am not hip enough, so the bottom line is that next time I'm going to look elsewhere.

This is an excellent place for the price. Do not expect a top of the line Hyatt-Wyndahm-Marriott, but then you are not paying for that. We got the package with - breakfasts and they were vouchers for the Du Par's across the parking lot. GREAT breakfasts. 
The location is very close to the beaches or Sea World or Old Town. We were going to stay on the water at a mid range resort (Bahia) but this was bout --- the cost and was just fine. Especially for a family.
Only complaint would be the internet could have been stronger.

My fiancee and I stayed the Liberty as we attended a function in the ballroom. Considering the price of the hotel room, we decided to book with them rather than leave and go to a cheaper hotel. We are quite glad we stayed. We had a late check-in, almost -pm. We were greeted by a friendly front desk employee who gave us a brief history of the hotel as it used to be the Charles Street Jail. We knew that, but we didn't know just how old it was originally (----). We were then given complimentary champagne, a first for us (at least when not in the Caribbean etc)
The ballroom seemed a little small given the reported function size (--- ppl, party) but they had three full bartenders and two beer-wine bartenders, all with their own tables along the border of the room. The passed hors d'œuvre were also quite tasty.
We stayed in a deluxe king room and I had requested a high floor through Expedia. We ended up on the --th (out of --) and our view was outstanding. The bathroom was massive, with a separate bathtub and tiled shower. The water pressure in the shower was unbelievable, we like near fire-hose strength and it was ssssoooo refreshing. The beds were above average however, I still haven't had a bed as comfortable as the Westin Waterfront (Boston). 
Overall, I would definitely recommend the hotel. Quick easy access to Government Center going up Charles St, a leisurely walk around Beacon Hill, or just need a classy hotel to stay at while in the city for the night, I didn't feel like I overpaid.

Spent one night at the Michelangelo. 
Excellent Service from the entire staff.
Booked a standard room and received a complimentary upgrade to a Grand one bedroom suite.
We've stayed in several hotels in NYC but this by far was the best experience ever. 
Location is convenient and within walking distance to theater district, Central Park, Times Square, etc.
Elegant, Classy accommodations which will satisfy the pickiest guest.

After our first night in this hotel I found - bills pushed under our door. One was for us the other for the previous occupant who had apparently checked out early. We then realized the room had not been cleaned nor had the bed been changed before we checked in - we had slept in used linen. We complained at the desk however, the manager was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""not available"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but we were asssured the linens would be changed and the room cleaned while we were out. When we returned later that evening the room had not been touched, the bed was not changed and no cleaning had been done. We were offered another room but that was found to be dirty too. Because Housekeeping had gone home we were presented with clean sheets and towels and told to change the bed ourselves. When I finally managed to reach the manager by phone - after we had returned home he offered to take $-- of the bill and said I couldn't expect to stay at a hotel for free. I finally reached the assistant to the CEO of the Marriott Chain and the cost of our entire stay was refuned. But it will be a long while before I stay in a Marriott hotel again.

You could not ask for a better location, minutes from Time Square, walking distance to central park and all the best theatres. 
The staff were friendley and the porters were especially helpful with dircetions considering we had had such a poor experience at the tourist information office earlier that day we were glad that not all New Yorkers were rude and unhelpful.
The rooms were small (but what can you expect for the price your paying I've stayed in smaller -* hotels in London) but me and my friend were fine once we had unpacked and moved our suitcases out of the way, the bathroom was modern and we always had fresh towels and bedding which was great as it was so hot while we were there. Yes the air con was noisy but not unbearable and cooled the room within minutes.
My only two complaints are that you definatley need a brighter light in the bedrooms as they are quite dark especially the courtyard facing ones and lastley makesure you keep all you valuables in the safe, luckily we did, but had a top and dress stolen from our wardrobe and our souvenir bags rummaged through I hate to think what would have gone missing if we hadn't used the safe, we didn't realise the items were missing till we got home which is a shame as I would definatley brought it up with the manager! 
Overall we had a great stay and I would definatley recomend the hotel to others.

By far the best hotel I've ever stayed in. The rooms were big and extremely clean. The location is just a block from a subway station and within walking distance of the Empire State Building and Times Square. But, the best part of this hotel is the staff. The front desk is very friendly and the concierge, Juber, is the absolute man. He will not steer you wrong in your travels or your stay and he's one of the most personable people I've ever met. If I ever make it back to New York, this is without a doubt the hotel I will stay at..
The best hotel in the world to travel with your dog. The bar-lounge is the best in the city,and you may sit there with your dog too. And the doormen are marvelous.

We recently stayed at the Courtyard Soho and found it to be a nice change of pace from Times Square and Midtown hotels. So quick on the subway up to the hustle and bustle and nice to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""come home"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to a quieter part of Manhattan. Great area near Chinatown and easy walk to ---- Memorial. The hotel is super comfortable and the staff is just awesome! Self parking in a lot around the corner worked out well.

We stayed in the doubletree in the new year, was suprised how small it was ,the loby and lifts were fine but other public areas not so good, needed a good vacum! The breakfast was adequate, nothing special for the money. (no bread for toast )!
 The room was tiny but decorated to a high standard and was clean.
Hotel staff were exeptionally helpful and friendly
The ouside of the hotel is scruffy with big plastic skips full of dirty laundry overflowing.

Fresh cookies at check-in-out counter! If you are lucky, we only caught it once. How do the counter folks stay skinny? Staff was universally pleasant (kudos to Natalie checked us in first night and passed on philly tourist tips, Eugene checked us out, and graveyard shift gent who checked us in) -- almost to the over-the-top level of cruise ship, where the cheeriness feels forced. I appreciate it. Had a recent stay at another downtown philly hotel marred by dour and crabby hotel staff, unpleasant. HGI wiped away the bad feelings about philly hotel hospitality.
Very nice and decent size business center room in the lobby for your office, internet, printing needs. 
Family of -, stayed - nights, -- days apart. Did not try the --th floor lounge-restaurant, except for the complimentary morning coffee... the view from the --th isn't all that great, looking over top of commercial sprawl central philly. Why eat in a hotel when Reading Market is next door?
We had a room near the icemaker which was convenient for icing down sore joints and chilling drinks we brought outside. In-room fridge good for keeping outside drinks cool. The room is basic hotel, with nice office chair and desk, with nothing else particularly of note, which I consider good. I did not go to be pampered, I went to have low stress, relaxing rest, away from home, which I got.
The first night (----) the hotel was prepped for a big convention and was great. Clean and bright and up-to-date, wading pool (- feet deep), hottub whirl pool, compact but fully stocked fitness room.
The following week (----), the place seemed more run down. The pool area was noticeable dirty, with residue at the bottom and around the pool (yuck!). The handle on toilet was very loose (reported it on check-out.) They where fumigating the -th floor rooms, where we stayed... yuck yuck!
The location can't be beat -- right next to the East Market SEPTA train station (we took train from NYC), drug stores, China town, bus station, and Reading Market (#- philly for eats). We avoided the attached parking lot by street parking in Chinatown overnight and early-bird parking at much cheaper parking lots just - or - streets away. 
Some folks might be turned off by some of the shady looking characters hanging around. That is expected in urban centers near public transportation, which HGI is. We live in Manhattan, so they had no impact on us.

With the prices on offer for hotels in Boston this place is in a great location at a reasonable price. The hotel is comfortable but not great and the subway is nearby. If I was staying in Boston again I would stay here.

This place should have been condemmed years ago ..... we tried - different rooms:
Room #- - No shades or curtains, one window would not shut, filthy carpet and odors ... after complaining to the desk clerk we were given another room 
Room #- - Bed not made, dirty linens and towels, phone upside down in middle of room and stunk of vodka ... Totally gross and unaccceptable .... after complaining to the Manager we were given another room 
Room #- - Again dirty, looked like an Army barracks, had two very small single beds, but was the best of the - rooms, we stayed in this room for - nights and hated it !!!

This place is a home away from home - great value for the money, great location, big rooms, comfy bed and wonderful service. Room had full kitchen, reasonable prices on minibar-snacks anad great amenities. Free breakfast was amazing and the service overall was impeccable. Spent three nights here and really felt like I was staying at a home away from home - look no further this is the place.

refer to bottom of page...cant retype it!when i checked in, the room was smelling great! Then i went out to dinner . when i arrived back at my room the smell of cigarette was so much as if someone had just left the room after smoking. I checked to see if all my belongings had been moved and

I travel about --+ times a year for business and personal travel. My stay at the LA Kimpton Palomar was, by far, the best experience I have ever had. EVERY one of the staff we encountered during our --day trip was extra helpful, accomodating, friendly. The digs are ultra cool. My ---year old daugther felt like a movie start. It also helped that the weekend we were staying, the hotel hosted a streaming media industry event. The vibe in the hotel was hot, hip, happening, vibrant. I could have felt old and out of place, but the staff never let me feel that way. The beds are a dream, the room was ultra quiet. We also found a great rate that included parking (a must for this hotel, where your only option is valet hotel parking). The location of the hotel was the best in LA. It was central to everything - the beaches, the nightlife, the sightseeing, the shopping. Yet, each night, we returned to a mellow, safe neighborhood to relax in our great room. Great job Palomar! I will definitely pick your hotels from now on when I travel. Hilton who??

My family was very pleased with this hotel arrangement. We had three children with us. Not many hotels will accomodate a family of five. Our large room and hallways were clean. No unpleasant smell. Yes, the bathroom was on the small side but shower worked fine, plenty of hot water for the five of us. Plumbing worked great. Beds were comfortable to include pull out sofa that my teenager slept comfortably in. Neighborhood was sketchy the later into the night it got but even with three kids with us we didn't feel threatened, merely cautious. Close to bus which we rode daily. Breakfast buffet was ok - boiled eggs, bagels, toast, fresh fruit. Saw us through 'til lunch with no complaints by the kids. Staff was friendly. Lobby was comfortable. Would absolutely stay here again.

We were impressed from arrival to departure. Prompt valet parking assistance, very courteous and efficient greeting and service by front desk personnel. Room was more than spacious and extremely well equipped. Much better than far more expensive S.F. hotels.
The only minor complaint was street noise early in the morning . . . the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""open-able"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (cranked out) windows don't offer the same sound insulation as more modern sealed windows (though we enjoyed the cool air in the late afternoon). We were on the -th floor . . . try for the --th for a quieter room (and more sleep in the early morning).
Our departure was a courteous, friendly and efficient as our arrival. All of the staff members were extremely helpful with a special nod to Jesus Rodriquez.

Like other reviewers, we also found the Residence Inn to be clean, comfortable, and in a great location two blocks from the Inner Harbor. Everything looked new and modern, and I was able to get a goverment-military rate that was very reasonable, and was the same rete for either a studio or one bedroom.
 We arrived on a busy Saturday with an Orioles game going on. Street parking was nonexistent so we opted to use the valet parking at the hotel. $-- was only slightly more than the other area garages charge for overnight parking, and our car was safe and easily retrievable. 
We stayed in a one bedroom suite which was spacious and well equipped with everything you could think of in the kitchen and had a pull out couch in the living room which could have accomodated more guests. Our only minor issue was the bedroom bed, which was supposed to be a king size but was more like a queen. We called the front desk and checked and were told our room did indeed have a king. I'm not sure if there was a mistake made or that's what they think is a king. Anyway, we chose not to pursue it further as a queen bed is OK for us and the room was nice otherwise. I'm sure the courteous and professional employees at the front desk would have changed our room if we wanted. Just FYI for those who need a big bed! 
Breakfast in the morning was plentiful and tasty with many hot-cold choices. When the breakfast room got crowded, the staff helpfully opened up a conference room across the hall for more seating. 
We had no problem hailing a cab in the evening to get to a friend's house. Otherwise we walked wherever we needed. Restaraunts and activites in the Inner Harbor are plentiful. Phillips seafood is hightly recommended!
This will definately be our new place to stay in Baltimore.

We spent a great deal of time debating which area to stay in San Francisco. We plumped for the Financial District because it was close to the Embarcadero, Union Sq and Jackson Sq. We also wanted a view of the bay from our hotel window.
The Hilton offered us all of this - a fab view of the city, and close proximity to bars, restaurants and cafes. Make sure you get a room on a high floor for the best views and the least noise. The hotel was clean and service was great, nice showers and nice free bath products. The hotel does offer parking, but it is $-- per night, but there is a far cheaper car park literally just across the road, which was only $-- per night.
We ate at Chaya on the waterfront, which was busy and lively, and the food was great. About -- minutes walk away. Some good bars and restaurants just round the corner, and the City Lights Book store and the stinking rose are just on Columbus Ave about - mins walk away.
The only thing I would say is that there is a hotel being built next door to the hotel. Building work starts before - every morning (including Saturday). So a sleep in was not optional.
All round, a good hotel.

I agree with other reviewers that the staff were just excellent from beginning to end. Fantastic location one block from Union Square and the Powell-Hyde Cable car line and two blocks from the downtown car hire centre for Alamo, Hertz, etc. Had a very quiet, very clean and spacious room on -th floor facing the back of the hotel with microwave, filter coffee maker and fridge. Loved the fact that it had a huge sofa and armchair and TV and music system (not ipod player though). Large comfy bed too and the bathroom was a good size with decent shower and bath and marble topped sink area. We had breakfast each day at Sears Fine Foods a block away on Powell Street which was delicious.We also ate at Loris Diner on Sutter Street (good diner food with a Cadillac inside the restaurant), E & O Trading on Sutter Street (very good Asian fusion) and Cupola (excellent - Italian in Westfields Shopping Centre, believe it or not, on the -th Floor). Do go up to the Club Lounge at the top of the hotel - where the concierge desk is- for complimentary teas, coffee and cocoa. It is a very comfortable club type area with a balcony for nice days. The only confusion we had was when booking this hotel, in my haste, I accidentally booked the Club Donatello for our last night. Don't worry if you do this - the Club rooms are timeshare rooms at the top of the same hotel and is managed by the same staff. The room we had was lovely - really really big with sofa, armchairs and two kingsize beds and fridge, tv and coffee maker. I cant remember a microwave. The lovely staff moved our suitcases while we were out and so it was no bother. Our Club Donatello room faced the main street but we did not hear a thing up there. We did not eat at the Zingari restaurant so I cannot comment but the live jazz and piano music sounded good coming from it. I recommend this hotel. The lovely helpful staff really make it a great place to stay.

All the good reviews the Andra gets makes me wonder if I stayed at the same place.
My wife and I spent the last three nights of our honeymoon in Seattle at the Andra. I wish it had at least been the first three days of our trip so that we didn't have such an anti-climax.
Having read a previous bad review of this hotel, I contacted the Andra in advance to reserve a room on a high floor away from the elevators as soundproofing is non-existent.
What room did I get? One on a lower floor opposite the elevator. They were only willing to move us away from the elevator but on the same floor.
Our package included champagne and truffles upon arrival. The truffles didn't arrive until our final night after two complaints to the front desk.
I handed an item of clothing in to be laundered. It came back ruined.
Overall, the Andra is a great looking hotel and would get more marks from me but for the poor service.
The only saving grace was the adjacent Lola restaurant which serves up great food.

After staying at the Tribeca Grand (great place) for three nights, I was forced to move to the Affinia my last night for business reasons. First the good:
-. The rooms are very spacious and come with kitchenettes. The rooms are outdated but actually grew on me a little after a few hours. 
-. Aveda toiletries.
Now the bad:
-. This hotel smells terrible! The scent reminded me of my grandma’s closet x --- (the smell of old covered by rose potpourri). The smell is very strong in the lobby and luckily not as bad in the guestrooms. 
-. The service is poor to average. There is no one to greet you and assist with your baggage but the check-in staff seemed friendly enough. There is a staff member who will store your bags until your room is ready but he seems very put upon when he is needed. 
-. The hotel needs a complete re-facing. The décor is very, very bad. The lobby carpet is made up of hot pink, purple, and yellow swirls. Everything is so old that it appears dirty (including the bathtub- shower). 
Up for interpretation: 
-. There were children everywhere. This is great if you are also traveling with children but could be a negative if you are on a weekend get-away. 
-. This hotel still has window unit air conditioners. I like to be able to have a lot of control over the temperature of a hotel room but these are old and noisy. 
I would (only) recommend this hotel to someone on a very tight budget, traveling with children, and needing a kitchenette.

This is a very cool hotel with an ingenious room layout. Rooms are small but very well-designed and comfortable. Location is very good, right next to -th Ave, Hell's Kitchen, which has lots of good bars and restaurants. 
However, I found the staff on the Floor - 'mission control' desk rude. No eye contact and a dismissive, unhelpful attitude even when they were at fault for losing a package. And lots of big, security guys glaring at everyone. 
On the plus side, the staff in the lobby who help with check-in were very helpful and friendly so the first impression was a really good one.

Having read several of the other - star reviews I can't think of any way to top them. I agree wholeheartedly that this is an excellent hotel, with great ambience and retro feel throughout (not new made to look old, but genuinely old, kept in great condition). The staff were very friendly, helpful and attentive. We stayed in a Deluxe King room which was spacious and quiet (we were at the back of the hotel and all we could hear was the occasional ringing of the cable car bells), with a dark warmth to it, immaculately clean and well attended to each day by the chambermaids. There was definitely no standard, off-the-shelf hotel decor and it felt friendly, like a room in a house rather than a hotel. It had proper, old fashioned, opening windows! And very effective blackout curtains.
We didn't have a chance to try the food - after exploring the city all day and having a big lunch, we were too tired and not hungry! We did enjoy the complimentary glass of wine in the wonderfully comfortable, relaxed bar though. 
The location was perfect for us as tourists. It seems like quite an arty area, busy, well lit and safe-feeling at night. A block away from Union Square with its nice cafe and tour bus stops, and a huge variety of high quality department stores and boutique shops. The cable car runs at the end of the block and goes to Fisherman's Wharf, though we found it a fairly easy and interesting walk. 
We also found it very convenient that there was a Seven--- store and a Walgreens almost opposite the hotel.
Though a hotel like this isn't the cheapest accommodation option in San Francisco, it was worth every penny - you definitely get what you pay for ... and more!
If we ever visit SF again, I would feel disappointed if we couldn't stay at the Hotel Rex!

We just read the review regarding the Elysee being bad for a business traveler. We just returned from NYC and actually ran into the traveler who wrote that review on the elevator. Perhaps it's not great for a business traveler, but we met several others who were on business and were happy. We were there for fun, and it was a perfect location and a great value. I don't think you can do better than $--- for a nice high ceilinged spacious room on the East side in walking distance from Central Park, museums, Times Square, and Broadway theaters. The staff was terrific, incredibly courteous and helpful with whatever we asked for (reservations, umbrella, cab, etc). Food and drink were plentiful and very nice; continental breakfast (really nice fresh fruit, yogurt, baked goods, and Nutella, a personal favorite) included in the rate, and the lounge where it's served has snacks and drinks most of the day and night, and from ---pm on weekdays wine, cheese, crudites in abundance, with cheerful lovely servers. We often only ate - meal a day out (usually lunch), and counted on the hotel food for breakfast and a light dinner or evening snack. Regarding the demographic, I am not """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""in your aunt's book club"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". In fact, I'm younger than the critical traveler, and there were quite a few young couples. Great hotel, great deal. Try it!

Great hotel - price was reasonable and people were friendly.
Room was still sort of small - but this is NY (and compared to some NY hotels, this was on the larger side).
I liked the hotel is was clean and resonable priced. I do not know what the other reviews are talking about. For the price no place had free breakfest

We stopped here for a one night refresh before arriving in San Francisco. The front desk was quick and efficient and we checked in with no problems. The room had plenty of space and the amenities were clean and fresh, the bed was also very comfortable. Can’t comment on any of the bars-grills as we didn’t use them; we did however have room service which again was quick and from what I remember, reasonably priced, alongside other hotels on our trip.
In conclusion, it served our purpose of crashing out for the day-night and was very clean and tidy throughout.

I have stayed here many times over the last few years. Yes, the standard cabins are small - but most people are aware of that when choosing the Jane - besides you are in New York - how much time do you need to spend in your room? The rooms come with many extras - wifi, water, ipod dock, robe and slippers, etc, and room service is available from Cafe Gitane, in the foyer. When staying in a standard cabin you are sharing a bathroom. In general I have never had a problem with this, and always found them clean. Occasionally noise from nearby rooms has affected my sleep. The bar is very cool, and the food from Cafe Gitane is good. The staff are very helpful. The location is great - in the west village, easy access to the Highline Park and the meatpacking district, and not far from several subway lines. And for the price? I would easily recommend this to others coming to New York for work or pleasure.

Stayed over the Christmas holidays for - days (my second time staying here) and I have a mixed review. It really isn't totally perfect, nor is it totally bad.
Pros
- GREAT location close to times square
- MODERN renovated rooms with flatscreen TV and modern furnishings
- FAST internet (even though if paid)
- CLEAN rooms
- COMFORTABLE bedsheets-matress
- DO ask for a renovated room because furnishings and more modern, brighter and more comfortable
Cons
- POOR service of staff (from reception taking a long time picking up the phone, to overwhelmed concierge at the lobby and no one picking up the phone etc)
- DIRTY furnishings in room (Even if they are renovated) such as paint peeling off walls, dirty carpets
- POOR water shower pressure
- IMPRACTICAL room design - I was given a accessible room, and the standing shower did not have any sort of height difference or partition with the regular bathroom, and the shower curtain does not reach the floor, and therefore water spilled all over bathroom floor even if you showered with the most care
- Food in in-room dining needs little more attention as it was very mediocre and wasn't great
- EXPENSIVE Internet rates (up to --.-- per day), but very fast

I would still recommend this hotel based on the great location and decent quality, but I would expect more from the brand Hilton in such a large metropolitan city like New York. The hotel does the job just fine, but there really wasn't much class or """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""wow""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""-features in its decor and services.

just came back from a six night stay in this hotel. me and my wife were on our hounymoon and all i can say is that this hotel is just excellent!!!
the rooms are a bit small, but the hotel is new and evrything is very very clean and neat.
the staff is very bery helpful and did there very best to assist and answer our questions.
the location is excellent and you can just about walk to evrywere.
graet hotel for a graet price in top location. will be back again!!!

If you do stay here, ask for a room away from the main street. We were in a corner room on the main street. The walls were paper thin and about - AM some tourists came into the room next store. It was like they were in our bathroom. Morning road traffic was also very loud.
The room was nice but nothing like we expected from reading prior reviews, especially for the price. I guess you pay for the location which is greatl

We stayed - nights at this hotel in May ----. The rooms were small - but we had expected this as it is a city centre hotel. The position is great, within easy walking distance of Boston Common, with lots of good restaurants in the area. What we weren't prepared for was the level of noise in the hotel on w-end nights.There are several nightclub and entertainment concessions on site and there seems to be no attempt made to protect the guests from the noise. We were on the -th floor (the night club is in the basement !!)When I complained (at -am) I was told that the hotel could do nothing about it !!
My view is that this is a good hotel for a stay in Boston - but if you are staying at the w-end, stay at the back of the hotel and as high up as you can.

I have stayed at the Hilton in SF on several occassions for both personal and business travel. Overall it is a good hotel in a good location. The added parking is a benefit if you need to drive in, which I do.

Booked a - night stay with Expedia at the Westin Hotel and what a brilliant time we had. 
Stayed in the Excecutive Club, which gave us complimentary breakfast's each day, and this was surprisingly good, with a fine selection of food and drink, in you own Executive Lounge. The rooms themselves were excellent with Heavenly beds, plasma tv's, Bose radios and PC's, the showers were really very good with twin heads and extremely powerful.
The staff were friendly and helpful, and I had no problems in getting tickets for events or some extra equipment for the room, requested a fridge and it arrived within minutes.
Then there is the location in Times Square, simply stunning, walking distance from most of the major attractions, and with subway and bus connections just around the corner if required.
Not my first visit to New York, but for first time visitors its hard to top Times Square as a location, there's a real buzz to the place and a great atmosphere, with plenty of places to eat at reasonable prices, and despite the big crowds as we arrived at Memorial Weekend, getting seated was no problem.
Great hotel in a great location, thoroughly recommend the Westin and looking to come back to New York as soon as possible.
The hotel was fair. It was were close to the space needle. If traveling on aurora ave, it is quite hard to get to

My wife and I stayed three nights in this Best Western while visiting San Diego. This hotel seems to be one of the older ones on hotel circle. The location is fine, as convenient to San Diego tourist attraction as the others on the circle, as long as you have a car. The property was very large (- or - buildings) and decently maintained, but a pretty dull bare bones chain hotel. I booked the reservation through groupon - a marvelous deal for a awesome place. The king-size suite was very modern and classy. The decor does not make you feel like you are staying in a hotel, but a small studio apartment. The location is great for seeing Chicago. The staff were very attentive and friendly. If I have the money, I would definitely stay here again!!

Just returned from a business trip and highly recommend and praise the staff and hotel. I had a minor A-C issue and Roddy their Director of Room Operations went way above and beyond to take care of it and made sure I was happy. I have never had a problem handled this professionally. Also nice rooms, clean and up-to-date.

We had a long road trip and Dallas was the perfect spot to stay, right about in the middle. This hotel was great and we needed it to just crash. Jody at the front dest was very helpful and gave us a larger room when she saw we were travelling with small children as well as sending up cookies and milk for us. She really went out of her way to make us feel welcome and since we were travelling on the Expedia rate I completely didn't expect it. She made our night!
If you go to the pool watch out! The tiles are very slippery when wet!

Thoroughly enjoyed my three night stay at the Fairfax on business. Not a single complaint, one the bets hotels in DC, on par with Sofitel. Location is close to Dupont Circle, my favourite DC area. Service was outstanding throughout. Painless check-in process, got upgraded to Suite as SPG Gold Member. Everyone was helpful, from front desk personnel to concierge and wait staff at breakfast. Rooms are tastefully decorated and have all the right amenities. I was glad that I could use Internet for free, as SPG Golod amenitiy, extremely critical of most of US hotels charging guests for Internet, not acceptable! Nice building too. Breakfast was quite expensive, ate there only once. Lounge is pretty good too for drinks. Finally, the value was also great, booked directly on SPG site, prepaid rate was quite good,

We stayed two nights at the Monaco in January--our first time but probably not our last. It was perfect for a couple's quick getaway. I got a great rate to begin with, but upon arrival we were upgraded to a riverview room (something i probably could have requested but did not realize) and given a $-- card to use for items in the mini bar, a very nice touch. (I had joined the free Kimpton rewards program online--not sure if the little gift was because of that or if they were giving these to all guests at the hotel.) Our room was nicely decorated and pretty roomy, for a boutique hotel. The staff seemed very willing to help with any questions. We enjoyed the wine hour in the lobby one of the evenings, although it was a bit drafty for those who had to sit closer to the doors (there is a fireplace on the far wall--seats on the couch and chairs there get quickly taken). The lobby also offers coffee and tea from - to -am. (A poster in the elevator says that hot cider and cocoa is offered from - to -pm, but i saw no evidence of this.- We especially loved the location of the hotel--we could walk to the Goodman theater and to shopping, as well as many restaurants.
We often take our three children to Chicago--the Hotel Monaco is not the kind of place for families with young kids. But next time we head to the city by ourselves, we will definitely keep the Monaco in mind.

I live in Manhattan, but my boyfriend and I stayed one night after a nice dinner. They immediately upgraded us to the penthouse suite, which was wonderful. We also called the hotel, asked if there were vacancies, and were there -- minutes later. Incredibly accomodating. The room was amazing. A living room, a bedroom, - balconies overlooking the river. The bathroom was phenomenal. The area is great, but it does shut down earlier than most Manhattan neighborhoods, because it is mainly residential. Buy a bottle of wine beforehand and sit out on your balcony. Highly, highly recommended.

having stayed at hyatts many times it seemed a sensible option for new year in new york. It was not cheap but new york over new year is never going to be. The location is great but having upgraded to regency club i was not over impressed . Usually the upgrade is worth it but not in new york . The selection on offer in the regency lounge was limited and did not include alchoholic drinks something i have come to expect . The lobby is spectacular but the rooms were nothing special. I am not fussy in hotels but i expect value for money which i know i could have stayed at better in new york for the same or less money even over new year. Also noticed room service trays and trolleys left for many hours outside rooms . I would stay again if i got a good deal but would not upgrade to regency club. Before i went i was suprised how low down on trip advisors ratings the hotel was. I am not now. On the plus side the rib eye steak i ordered on room service is the best steak ive ever had and i have had some good ones before. New york itself was great especially the helicopter ride at night up the hudson river.

Perfect hotel with a delightful front end staff. Stayed one night, wish I could have stayed longer. Woman on front desk duty was professional, informative and understood what many front desk people fail to understand -- the guest is important and does not know anything about the hotel or the area. She was just as perfect as the hotel. Would stay again when traveling on --.
Avoid this, if you don't want to sleep with bed bugs.

We just returned from a stay at the Raffeallo. The room itself was a very nice size. We did sleep well. The beds were very comfortable, and I think this may be the quietest hotel in which we've stayed. We were disappointed in two areas. First, the front desk staff was not very helpful. We tried to call multiple times and no one ever answered at the concierge desk, nor was anyone ever seated at the desk. We also tried to call the front desk, and the call went to voicemail. Also, when we were standing in line to check out, two employees were behind the desk. However, the second employee just turned and walked away, while the first employee was trying to help the lady in front of us with reservations for later this year. (We had two families waiting behind us.) The second complaint was the size of the bathrooms. This was our once-a-year getaway, and the bathrooms were very small for the price of the room. (We booked the largest room offered.) The showers were very nice, but there was one small sink and standing-room only. By the way, the restaraunt was closed for remodeling, which was not mentioned on the hotel website. I will say the best thing by far about the Raffeallo was Ferron---the extremely helpful and cheerful bellman!

I recently visited memphis was told to stay at the Peabody. From the moment I stepped into the foyer, I was greeted with southern charm and a beautiful foyer that took my breath away. I was enchanted ;-) Drinks at the bar or in the foyer is a MUST to absorb the grandeur of this place. Don't miss the march of the ducks... it is a lovely sight to behold plus the duck master ;-) twice a day and not to be missed.
My room was huge, and very comfortable. It didn't look onto the street, and so was very quiet. the bathroom was on the small side but spacious enough. All their soaps were shaped like ducks, turn down service with chocolates shaped like ducks and even the butter came in the shape of ducks... too cute. Had the breakfast deal which was great - lovely food with some local delicacies too like grits to try.
Location was great, close to the tram or you could walk down to Beale street. Restaurants GALORE around the hotel too, all within walking distance. 
Loved the place

There is no place like Times Square on earth. Whether the frenetic chaos makes you queasy or motivates your existence, you will have to admit the there is an unrivalled energy here. This was my last night after a short -- days in NY. I was given an amazing room on the --th floor, this was the place to be. To rise above NY from the middle is to stop feeling pressured by it, it reminds you that it is just a piece of land with buildings and people going about their lives, like anywhere else. Here, I could watch and contemplate this. 
The room was beautiful and clean of course, the staff were polite and attentive. It as after dark when I arrived in my room and I could witness the artificial light show that is --nd street. I could see the river lights in the distance and I eagerly awaited the morning view, where a cold crisp winter would greet me in a totally different way.

Located a few blocks from Union Square, walking distance to shops and restaurants. My room was quite stylish though not that spotless. One big plus though is that they had complimentary earplugs, considering that the area is quite busy-noisy. The bathroom was very basic but clean. Lobby is very small and the elevator is quite old, but it added to the charm of the hotel.

we booked an internet breakfast special at a very very reasonable price.... at checkin we have got a free upgrade to a junior suite.... the room was completely new renovated with a sleeping and sitting area with - tv flat screens, a very modern bathroom, a very comfortable bed and untypically for new york: very quiet!!! breakfast buffet was available from - am to --am... with fruits, yogurt, muffins, bagle, toast, bacon, eggs, orange juice,.... staff was very friendly and helpful.... great location (just around the corner of empire state building) and close to - different subway stations... will come back for sure!

We stayed here for - nights early May. The position in San Francisco was great for us. The beds and pillows were the best we experienced on our three week holiday. We were in transit to San Francisco and stayed only one night at The Westin near LAX airport. We didn't have to wait very long for the shuttle to take us back and forth. It was so convenient and the food and the service at the on site restaurant was excellent. The room and the staff were excellent. I highly recommended this Westin.

Hotel is very new and rooms are lovely and for New York a good size with great bathrooms. Sky view room on --th floor had fabulous full length windows with fantastic view. One block away from Times square so just away from hustle and bustle but you can walk everywhere concierge made some great restaurant recommendations

Dick-Karen's review of June --, ----, hit the nail on the head, so I'll keep this brief. My wife, teenage daughter, and I stayed at the Omni Shoreham last week for - nights. True, the convenient metro is close by, but it would have been nice to walk back to the hotel room for a midday break, or at the beginning-end of the day instead of fighting the metro rush hour (e.g., Dupont Circle). With a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""buy two nights get the third night free"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" deal, the hotel was an excellent value.

This has been my -th or -th stay at the Elysian, both with and without kids. There are many wonderful things about this hotel, many other reviewers have documented them. They are smart, charming, witty and ready to serve. What a treat! Each time I visit it feels like home. Business or pleasure, this hotel is a must try - you'll never go back to another. I was a Park Hyatt-Swissotel client in Chicago until the Elysian opened. I will never leave...

I picked this hotel based on the reviews and location. I was very happy with the room and the friendly staff. The location was walking distance from downtown and in the center of Little Italy. The free breakfast was very good. On the weekends, the happy hour starts at noon. I would stay here again.

Except for the extremely small TV in our room, I have no complaints about this hotel. After almost cancelling our reservation upon reading a certain review, I am glad that I didn't. The best thing about this hotel is the FREE parking!! All this for a room rate of $---!!!! This is a great hotel for families, especially during the summer. We will definately be back!!!

The hotel was everything it said and more. The staff allowed our party of -- to use the breakfast room for our take in dinner in the evening. The breakfast room has wonderful views. We were on a road trip across the US with - tween girls. We loved the location near the water. We did not have a lake shore view, we had a city view and loved looking at the architecture of the city. The atmosphere was extremely busy but we all loved that, as we live in the burds, usually, so it was an exciting change! 
It was great to be away from shopping district, as we rented bikes and toured the parks and musuems!

Great, clean hotel in an ideal location. All major T lines were within - blocks. Very convenient for all of our activities. We toured museums, took in a show, saw a game at Fenway abd we were never more than -- minutes from the hotel. Room was immaculate and service was prompt. Used the fitness center everyday and equipment was up to date and pool, while small it was adequate for a workout.

off to bad start, -st room came with a guest in the living room, the place was packed (it was spring break time) the staff kept up well with breakfast though if you know dallas or use a gps this hotel is in the middle of everything -- minutes to alot of things in all directions. hot tub was luke warm at best. no free internet exept in business center (- slow as can be computers)

I have been staying at the Palmer House Hilton for over twenty years. It is my favorite hotel in Chicago. The part of the hotel that I like the best is the very large open lobby that has a mural that stretches across the entire ceiling. In addition, the hotel was recently renovated, now the accomodations have a classic-contemporary look to them. I would definitely recommend staying here to other travelers.

I always get a suite facing Wall Street and the Statue of Liberty on the west side of the building. Service is incredible and the location is perfect if you are spending time in Soho-Downtown-Meatpacking District. Heard it was being sold....so, I hope that does not interfere with the impeccable service.

This is a very small hotel, the parking is underground with limited above ground. We requested & were told our room was non-smoking... yet as we walked into our room the door was open to our across the hall neighbours who had a smoking room...? I suppose they figure smoke doesn't travel across the hall? The room was very small (- queen beds & one chair). There were no face clothes in the room (- hand & - bath towels) The wifi was a nightmare to use... and was not secure. (and we were on the bottom floor close to the office) The bathroom tub had holes in the walls above the shower... and looked like it hasn't had a good scrub down in a long time. Looking around the whole place could use a major reno. Breakfast was the typical; bread, english muffins, cereal & (-) machine to make your own waffles. There was fruit as well including bananas that all looked like they were ripe a couple of days ago. We went down for breakfast at -am, there are only - tables for the whole hotel to sit down... so my family sat at a table while I took a couch as there were no more chairs... soon people were standing to eat.

We arrived at the W and were helped by an incredibly helpful staff. One of the concierge, Jeff Mead, took us personally up to the room and then proceeded to show us the bar at the top of the building. He showed us the sights, gave us a drink coupon, and gave us the advice to go to the Old Ebbitt's Grill. It was a block away and great (we went there twice in three days). The bed was literally the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in, which you need when you are sight-seeing in DC (it really is amazing how tired you are walking up and down the Mall...). The hotel itself is a really cool combination of historic and modern. Overall, it was a great stay. For me the location, the staff, and the bed made it the best choice for our stay in DC.

When we were planning a weeklong trip to Los Angeles to visit family, our son was put in charge of finding us a place to stay. I stand outside the room for about -- minutes waiting for someone to come show me my new room, I get a guy who just confirms my name and hands me a key and walks away. Fine, new room, actually on a lower floor. Was kind of expecting some kind of upgrade or amenity (had an issue with the Westin River North before and they upgraded me when I had to move rooms). 
On the second day I called to request a - pm check-out, which is at this point guaranteed for gold members except at resorts and conference centers (which this location is not). The guy on the phone says he can do - pm. I call him on it and ask him, isn't this guaranteed? He says well, the hotel is busy the next day, can't do it. Not wanting to argue any more, I just accept it. On the way back from dinner, I stop by the front desk and ask again, and at least this time he confirms that it is guaranteed and gives me the - pm check out.
All in all, I've run into too many issues at this one location with little or no compensation. Yes their rates are good but the location is not better than any of the alternatives. Four points will probably be as good of a rate with a better location, Westin River North provided much better service, and I haven't had any major issues with the Westin Michigan Avenue or either W (Lakeshore and City Center). I likely won't be staying at the Sheraton unless the rate is significantly lower than the alternatives.

This place is not in the Texas Hill Country it is located square in the middle of one of the most unsightly examples of suburban sprawl in north San Antonio. All of the facilities try very hard to live up to the JW Marriott name but are not of the unique nature typically found at Marriott's signature resorts. Feels like some outsider's interpretation of the grand Texas hacienda but executed with tilt wall construction and chock full of vinyl reproduction animal prints. It's what happens when cliched interior design gets hold of too much money. The food is average at best but at these prices, a big disappointment. The chef uses a shovel for the salt on savory items and sugar on sweet items. Hard to taste anything else. Fresh fish was not fresh tasting and the menu overall feels like a Disney interpretation of Texas food. Missed opportunity. Biscuits literally buried in sugar as your signature bread? Really? Ugh. I must point out the TPC Live Oak golf course is truly worth the trip and the price of your room. Incredible shape and a challenging course for sure. Bring your sand bucket and toys because you'll spend plenty of time at the beach on this course. And if your tee shot is even slightly in the rough, your odds of finding it are less than -----. I've played every course in Texas public or private and this is in the top - for sure. However the food served on the golf course is pitiful, and golf food expectations are low. The halfway house has virtually no selection and the $- turkey sandwich, once unwrapped, was obviously days old, literally inedible. Even for resort golf food this was complete robbery. As for the service experience of the mega-property overall, it's hilarious. They have so much staff, at times it seems they outnumber the guests. Yet the service is terrible. They all tend to clump together and chit chat versus actually help guests. In the restaurants and bars, they clearly must have some sort of medieval rule about who can wait on exactly which table because whole herds of bored staff will ignore you, you have to find your person. Then there's all these seating areas in bars and restaurants where they won't serve you a drink because """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""those tables are for waiting"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Really, you won't serve me a drink while I wait for a table? In a sports bar? And you have nothing to do but gather at the bar and chat with the other waiters and bartenders? Can anyone say lost revenue? Anyhow, the staff is clearly new, untrained, clueless and entertaining to watch in action. Although I'll point out they were clearly trained quite well in the art of demanding a room number from every guest they talk to. I can only imagine some expensive tabs got walked in the early days and now all guests must be interrogated upon entry to any venue. Dad will like the golf, the kids will like the pool, mom will pay way too much for the spa experience but like it. It's not the place you'll want to stay for long but a golf course worth playing makes the rest of it a nice add on. Puts Hyatt Hill Country to shame and is a step up from La Cantera. Nice but not what a JW Marriott should be, especially in Texas.

I was there on a site visit recently. This is a great place. I would like to make a shout out to one particular staff-- Oscar at the valet. He is the one who asked me to review my experience. I appreciate his attention to details. Thank you Oscar. 
The front desk staff were very attentive and make sure the line moved and needs were met.

I have been reading all the reviews of the hotels that have been ranked above the Mayflower, and I find it very interesting. I live within -- miles of the Mayflower, but every year our dinner club books a night here during the Christmas holidays so that we can eat downtown, experience the city, and not have to drive after we have had many cocktails. This year was no exception. The hotels that were mentioned with a higher rating than the Mayflower are great hotels. However, the Mayflower is far and above the others. This hotel has a much better central location, the rooms are large and very well appointed, the staff is great and courteous AND for the location and room - the price can't be beat. The hotels in the University District and on Lake Union are great - BUT they are a cab ride away from downtown Seattle. The Mayflower is right in the middle of Seattle - within walking distance of the waterfront, Pike Place Market, Nordstrom, Macy's - all the best restaurants. Plus, it is so reasonable. Being a former Bostonian and having worked in some of the area hotels, I can surely tell you that Chandler Inn is one of the best values in town. Yes, it is not fancy, but it is spotless, nicely located, and within walking distance to almost every attraction in town. Not only that, but the subway and Amtrak stations are just footsteps away. Yes, there is no parking at the hotel, but only a block away is a huge public parking garage that is fairly inexpensive. There is a gay bar on the first floor and it is very friendly and all are welcome...almost like a gay version of Cheers. The area restaurants can't be beat....Chandler Inn is in one of the trendiest neighborhoods in town. Lots to choose from. So anyway, if you like high-priced chain hotels with all the amenities, this place is not for you. But if you like a nice, inexpensive hotel in a great area of the city, then don't hesitate to come here. This hotel is great for the sightseer and person on a budget. I always stay here every time I'm visiting Boston. I mean, I could stay at a fancy hotel, but why? I'd rather spend my money having fun in the city than sitting around in some overpriced, generic hotel room all day. Wouldn't you?

I stayed at this hotel with my girlfriend when I was in town for work and loved the staff and hotel. The staff is what makes this hotel an excellent stay.

Everything we read about this fabulous boutique hotel was true. This smaller hotel in the heart of Manhatten fulfilled all of our expectations for a price that was neither at the bottom end of the scale or the top end. Despite the construction, the moment we walked through the entrance of the Casablanca we enjoyed total silence. The rooms are not large but are more than adequate. If comfort and charm are what you are looking for, I would not hesitate to recommend the Casablanca. No complaints here.

Being on gramercy park and away from the office districts of midtown and downtown this well appointed and maintained hotel was a really nice break from the big brands and the national boutiques. My loft room was large and sexy, the bath area large and the lobby area a bit dark but very nice. The staff was excellent. Room service was tasty.

The hotel is perfectly located. The staff are friendly and helpful. The rooms are great. The bed is like sleeping on a cloud! I will stay here the next time I'm in town.

My husband, -- year old son, and I visited San Francisco on a long weekend the first part of October. We stayed at the Hotel del Sol, based on reviews that I had read on TripAdvisor. Well, let me say, that the reviews were right on the money! We loved the Hotel del Sol, and highly recommend it! It is located in a GREAT, safe, in-town neighborhood that is close to everything, but far enough away from the noise and tourist traps. It is located in the Marina district, which is home to great shops and restaurants....all that you can easily walk to. We loved to explore the different streets with the neighborhood restaurants...plenty of outdoor cafes and coffee shops. It is in an upscale, residential neighborhood that was alot of fun. The hotel staff was young, very helpful, and friendly. They gave us lots of great recommendations for restaurants, etc. The rooms were done in bright colors, just like it shows on the website. I don't think you could get a better value for the money in that location. We took the city bus (a stop is located just - short blocks away) everywhere. It's easy to get around in San Francisco without a car! One thing we did that was awesome was.....rent bikes from Blazing Saddles Bikes and bike across the Golden Gate Bridge to Saulsalito! What a fun day we had! You can take the ferry right back across the bay to San Francisco. It's a beautiful boat ride across the bay. We will definately return!

The lounge also had a great view of the sunset. The only issue I had here was when I was trying to call for a taxi during rush hour.

Sadly, this report, on balance is mostly negative. But I am hopeful that this hotel will improve in the future.

Located on -th Avenue just south of West --rd St., it is right across the street from Madison Square Garden, two blocks east of the Empire State building and one block south of the famous Macy's department store. The hotel has a great classic entrance and first floor lobby. The first floor is fully staffed with numerous bellmen and other forms of service. There is a gift shop, a dinner, a small convenience store, a coffee shop-bakery, and a full fine dining restaurant on the first floor. If that was all you needed, you are good. (Noteworthy...one of the bellmen was quite helpful with getting a taxi in a hurry to help some folks in our group make their flight.)
The quality of our room on the third floor was quite poor. The furnishings could have been from the ----'s. The bath room was small and in a state of disrepair. The walls needed new paint. The bed was very uncomfortable. The best I can say about the mattress is that every portion of it was neither planar, nor parallel to the earth's surface, nor perpendicular to the earth's gravitational field. We were there with a group and others reported other types of problems in their rooms such as the siting of roaches. Also the walls are very thin.
Another disappointment is that none of the restaurants in the building offer room service. They all appeared to be separate entities from the hotel.
So if comfort and pleasantness of the room is a significant factor for you, I would avoid this location, at least for the near future. I truly hope that such a grand and historic site can be returned to its former glory. Evidently, they do a lot of low budget conference business, but for my money, the rooms either need to be $--- cheaper or $--- better. (Although, right now, I don't think I would stay there for free.) This visit was our first time at this property and I’m sure it will be our last until further notice of improvements.

A good stay for a layover, very close to the airport so it is convenient when you are jet-lagged. I requested an upgrade and got it but, there is no executive room anymore and I really can't figure out what was upgraded. I did find a bathrobe but the room did not have any upgraded amenities or is any larger than the other rooms. No bath gel and no shower cap...is this the way these mid-teir places are going now? I did appreciate being able to open a window! Thank you Sheraton!
Once again I must comment on Sheraton's ban on people being able to choose smoking or non-smoking rooms. In the hospitality business, everyone should be accomodated. Modern air systems these days can take care of any odors and it is disturbing that those who would like alcohol are readily accomodated....and almost encouraged. I saw a poor guy trying to enjoy his rum and coke and his pipe, standing outside with no place to sit in freezing temperatures. Shame on you , Sheraton for not accomodating everyone! At least put heaters outside in a shelter for those who choose to smoke.
