A great location, short walk to times square and subway station. Lots of shops close by to purchase food drinks etc. Read that the service was poor but i found the hotel staff very freindly except for bell boys who didnt ask for our bags. Room was very big considering that we were in the city. Only negative - the pool looked very old and dirty so didnt go in.
new york in itself - good city very easy to find your way around. excellent pizza at John's pizzeria worth the wait. You must go on the - hour circle line cruise.

My husband was visiting family in San Antonio. He was enjoyinig the continental breakfast at the hotel and suddenly collapsed and fell unconscious. The hotel staff promptly came to my husband's aide and called ---. My husband was having cardiac arrest and was very close to death. EMS arrived promptly and were able to save my husband's life. He was then taken to Methodist Heart Hospital and is now doing fine. The entire hotel staff are kind, caring, and provided us incredible customer service. The hotel is not a - or - star - but I would rather stay at at hotel where the hotel staff sincerely care about their customers.

I stayed for - days in the Hilton Chicago during the conference in Nov ----. I have not spent much time in the hotel, but like the gym and swimming pool that opens very early in the morning. My room, for some reason, has - bathrooms, which will be good for - or more people. However, I stay alone, so it kinds of interesting room to have. The location is very closed to the Art Institute and the Millenium Park and is not too long a walk to Magnificent mile downtown area. The buffet breakfast is good with wide selection. The checkout kiosk allows you to print out your boarding pass, and it is a nice touch.

What a place…! Historic, beautiful, clean and awesome staff. We enjoyed our trip. I stayed in one of the old mansion hotel rooms and the rest of my family stayed in the new side of the property. My wife used the hotel spa, while we went golfing to Los Lagos golf course. For dinner time we went to Orlo’s food was outstanding. It was an affordable hotel great location.

The good points are that it is easy on-off from the freeway, it basically centrally located, under $----night and the bed was comfrotable with clean sheets and there is free parking.The downside was the the room was in pretty bad repair, the bathroom had mold on the walls and ceiling with metal fixtures rusted and the exterior door required a lot of monkeying with to get it to lock.

We stayed two nights. The air conditioner did not work. There was no offer to move us to another room. The manager said nothing would be done until - a.m. the next morning. At noon on the next day, the air conditioner had not yet been repaired and my husband again went to the office where the manager said it could not be fixed that day either. The manager then offered us another room at that time. We had to repack and move. Carpets in both rooms were stained badly. There was dirt under the recliner chair. The dumpster was overflowing and rats were running around.

My buddy and I have stayed here for an Ohio State football game the past two years and have really enjoyed the hotel. It is spacious and very clean - offering a seating area, so that you have more than just a couple of beds. The TV is nice and there is wireless internet. There is a little bistro downstairs, which seems nice, but we generally get in early on Saturday, take a (free) shuttle that runs about every -- minutes over near OSU and don't come back until late that night after the game and an afternoon-evening of eating-drinking. There is the OSU Hall of Fame Cafe next door that is really nice for a night cap and-or late dinner as well. The staff remembered us from the previous year and are very helpful. Great place!

Reserved this hotel via priceline bidding. The sound proof was soooooooooo bad that I could hear very well what was going on between the couple right next door in the middle of the night (trust me, it was not pleasant AT ALL!). 
This hotel certainly does not deserve -.- star; I would rather pay more to stay at a nicer hotel next time when I visit San Francisco.

This Homewood, as its name suggests, is located in an office park area just outside of Phoenix. We had a --bed suite for an extremely reasonable price. The breakfast was as expected from a HWS, and the rooms were comfortable and clean. There was some lingering stench of cigarettes in the hallways, but it may have been related to one chain-smoking guest. All in all, it was a fine stay.

The Drury Plaza Hotel was our home for two days while visiting San Antonio. The hotel is on the Riverwalk and is in a perfect location for Riverwalk activities. Just a walk to the basement of the hotel, a turn to the right and we were at the heart of the Riverwalk. Everyone, from the front desk to housekeeping was friendly and helpful. The room was of average size but very comfortable as was the bed. Parking was valet only and at a cost of $-- a day, but I think it was worth it because my automobile was secure and the valets were very helpful in giving us directions to our destinations. 
 The breakfast was very satisfying as was the -:-- kickback. What other hotel gives you - alcoholic drinks and heavy h'orderves (baked potatoes, mac and cheese, vegtable trays, hot dogs, etc.) every afternoon? 
 The hotel lobby was very spacious and beautiful with stained glass and even an antique car. I am very pleased that I chose this hotel for our visit to San Antonio. I would definitely stay there again and would highly recommend it to my friends.

Am used to staying in a hotel right on Rittenhouse Square but they had no availability for my most recent trip. ---- is a small but well appointed hotel close to the Square. The decor was top rate with high quality accesories including a faux fire which initially I thought was a little odd considering it was July, but looked lovely at night when the room was dark! Free internet access and a clock with speakers for an ipod connection. Small quibble...no ability to make coffee in the room but the cafe opened early and a trip downstairs would have procured some if only I had known it was there! Free continental breakfast with nice pastries but weak coffee and uninspiring cereal...one feels for the price they could have done better than little pre packaged pots. Available hot breakfast extra but I didnt try it. Every member of staff we met was charming and helpful. No parking but good directions to a nearby garage with reasonable prices

I got to the hotel at -pm. The men who worked there were foreign and didn't speak good English. They told me they were full (I had made a reservation - weeks in advance and paid extra for a better room) and that they would put me up in their """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""other"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel. They acted like they couldn't understand me when I told them I didn't want to go anywhere else. I felt like I had no choice but to move. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""other"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel was like an apt. bldg for lower income tennants. The only plus was a refrigerator in the room. It seemed clean enought, but I found live roaches crawling around in the dresser drawers.

We chose this hotel because it is close to Northwest Houston Medical Center, where our daughter had surgery. The rooms were large and clean, had a microwave and small fridge. The breakfast suited our needs for a quick bite. We had toast and cold cereal, but there were other choices. Coffee was surprisingly good. Front desk staff were helpful and professional. Our grandson enjoyed the pool and hot tub, which were well kept. Plenty of restaurants and a grocery store nearby.

Hotel is centrally located. Rooms are large, comfortable and affordable. Staff is friendly and accomodating.
Hotel Valet directed me to a parking lot one block over that SAVED ME over $---night!

The restaurant in this hotel had a fire this past Spring, and the restaurant is under construction, which began July -...not sure why no one else on this site mentioned the noise, because the noise from the jackhammer is incredible. We contacted Travelocity, the site we booked thru, to let them know, and they were not sure if something could be posted to their site...so this posting is going up in case Travelosity doesn't place anything on their site. 
The construction crew works from -:--am--:--pm...so maybe the guests that posted weren't in the room during these hours. According to information provided by the front desk of the hotel, construction on the hotel restaurant will continue until mid-September...so if you're looking to sleep in past -:--am...this is definitely not the hotel for you.

I usually stay at the Meridian or the Vitale , but both were booked. The Wyndham was about --% of the cost. I had low expectations, but was pleasantly surprised. The room and the bathroom were both quite large, the bed was very comfortable, and the staff was pleasant. The hotel was completely acceptable - such that I gave our local office manager the contact so she would have an option of a lower priced hotel. My only complaint was that the towels were a little thinner than I would have liked.

Just got back from a three day weekend at the Iroquois. We visit NYC every few years and this time we went to celebrate our --rd anniversary. We had a great stay. Room was ready early, clean, and the hotel location was excellent.

We booked our holiday on a budget, and being students didn't expect too much for the low price we paid overall. However, having been to Boston before, I was pleasantly surprised when the taxi pulled up outside the Club Quarters, what with it's ideal location in the city. When we walked into the lobby we were greeted by the receptionist who kindly upgraded us to a room with a fridge and microwave. Inside the room, it was spacious with a nice decor, and the bed was very comfortable with feather pillows and a down duvet (we did help ourselves to two extra pillows from the guest request closest). The bathroom was small but did the job. I have terrible eyesight so I found the extendable and magnifying mirror that was attached to the wall very handy when I was putting on my make-up. The club room with internet access was incredibly useful, though we could also access the wi-fi in our room too. We had breakfast in the pub-restaurant next door to the hotel one morning, but didn't particularly like it so didn't bother to go there again. Housekeeping came everyday and we found it very efficient. On the last day, we paid $-- to check-out at -pm as we had a late flight home. We thought this was reasonable as it meant we could make the most of our last morning in Boston. All in all, we would definitely stay in Club Quarters again and recommend it to anyone.

I treated my husband to a late Valentine's weekend in the city and decided to try a hotel that was a little different (we usually stay at the Mayflower or JW Marriott). We were pleasantly surprised by the cute little lobby and the common areas. Check-in was easy and friendly. As others have stated, the room was small, but clean and fun. There were lots of nice little touches. We were on the -th floor.
However, the hallways that we enjoyed so much when we entered the hotel soon became a nightmare. Because they are almost all marble and hard reflective surfaces, the sounds reverberated all night long. There was apparently some sort of function in a nearby ballroom. Catering carts were rolled past our room until well after midnight. When they hit a bump in the floor close to our room, it sounded like a cannon! You could easily eavesdrop on people speaking in normal conversational tones all the way at the other end of the hallway. Doors banged, dogs barked and dish carts rattled all night. Needless to say we didn't get any sleep. I mentioned the problem to the desk personnel on check-out. She offered to make an adjustment in our bill, but since I had pre-paid for the room through Orbitz, there was nothing she could do. She offered us an upgrade the next time we say, but, I don't think there will be a next time. I'll go back to the Mayflower for our next in-city getaway weekend.

I stay here whenever I have a long business trip in the LA area. The staff are friendly, the rooms are great, and the location is perfect to get to your flight in time with their shuttle or if you need to drop off your rental car. The room I was given was overlooking a dog kennel and the barking was unbearable. I called the front desk and they sent up a key to a new room within minutes.

I have to admit after reading some of these reviews, we were nervous about this hotel. What a pleasant surprise!
The outdoor landscaping is very well cared for, and the lobby itself is just beautiful. A great spot for visiting. 
The check in process went smoothly, and we received a friendly greeting from the front desk clerk. We had booked two (-) king rooms-four (-) adults. Each one had a water view, and a nice little patio. The furniture in the room was just fine, and both rooms were very clean. Having the small refrigerator was great to store drinks and some fruit. When it comes to the property being outdated, I would have to say the bedding, linens, and pillows would fall under this category. 
There was a consensus in our group...all of us wished we could have stayed longer, and would not hesitate to stay at this property again.
A big thank you to the staff for being so friendly and helpful!

This was our first time staying at an Aloft. We weren't sure what to expect and we were very pleasantly surprised and pleased. Property is very clean and the staff are extremely accommodating. We had breakfast in the snack area and thought it was very good. We had breakfast sandwiches and they are made to order. We didn't use the pool facilities but we did check them out and it was very nice and clean. Everything about the grounds are very pleasing. We even had a view of the golf course. The lounge is a really neat area however we were there on a Thursday (they have live entertaintainment on Tuesdays and Thursday's) and there was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""single's mingle"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and only one bartender. Made for a little difficulty in getting served but it was fun for people watching. Looked like everyone was having fun and we did, too. The only thing we would have liked to have seen in the room was a light weight blanket for the bed instead of having to use the duvet. We did make that suggestion with person that checked us out. All in all this was a very pleasant stay and we will definitely stay again.

It was one of the nicest hotels I have stayed in. They even upgraded me free of charge. The service was excellent. The hotel was across from the park, and on the route for the open air buses. You could see the lake from my window. And accross at the park they held free dancing lessons every night. I was so close to many attractions. The hotel even has a deli down stairs for light snacks. Also hair dresser, and many more things. The pool was great, and the gym was excellent. Everything was wonderful. Most of all, it was a very clean hotel.

We stayed here in September ---- as a relaxing break prior to a not so relaxing trip to Las Vegas. The hotel was nice, the room was lovely but the customer service was just shocking. Being an animal lover the ducks in the pool were a novelty for the first few minutes but it became apparent that they were not leaving anytime soon and pretty soon the bottom of the pool and the whole edge of the pool was scattered with duck excrement. I went to speak to reception at around --am and was told that it would be cleaned up soon, but hours went by an no cleaner arrived. I went back to complain again as was greeted with 'well I am sorry you feel that way but the ducks were here long before you' and that 'you don't need to worry there is so much chlorine in the pool that you wont catch anything'. I was horrified at the terrible customer service. Eventually my partner went it to complain and was told that the cleaners had gone home and would be back at around -pm to clean the pool. They eventually arrived at around -pm. We went out every evening and asked for a taxi and was given the 'house' car which turned out to be --% more expensive than a taxi. From that night we insisted on a taxi being called for us but the guy was clearly unhappy with this and once he ignored us altogether and called the 'house' car. We refused to get into it on the grounds that it was too expensive and eventually had to get a taxi number from a return journey, call it before we went out and meet it away from the hotel (they would not come to the hotel). There was however one nice gyt and on the day he was on shift he called us a taxi without any issue and didnt even call the 'house' car. I wish I could remember the rude ones name - but he wore glasses and had blonde hair. It is such a shame because the hotel in itself was nice.

OMG !! what a nightmare This was booked months in advance. big mistake
Arrived late --.-- pmafter a long journey.. Booked in and straight out again. Had to spend the next few hours with kids in the car looking for another hotel, but is was still worth it!
The rooms were not very clean, it looked like someone had been sick over the side of the bed. The clean sheets tried to cover a the vile stain.
Ash eveywhere, noisy room next door.
The manager on duty was really nice and let us look at other rooms but this really was not for us.
Give this one a wide berth!
Caroline

My wife stayed at the Hotel Kabuki for five nights last September, to celebrate our --th wedding anniversary. We got an outstanding rate. The corner room was excellent, clean and neat, with rice paper screens in wooden frames that were a neat touch to shade the very-Western sliding glass doors to the two narrow balconies. The deep soaking tub and separate shower with glass doors were very modern and cool. Staff was very prompt and helpful. The hotel (caddy-corner from the Chinese Embassy) was adjacent to the Japanese Memorial pagoda and a Japanese shopping mall. Nearby is Fillmore Street and a Safeway - lots of options within a couple of blocks. Getting to downtown was easy with the bus service (we bought a three-day pass that paid for itself within a day and a half) which made it possible to get anywhere in the SF Bay area on foot, with access to the cable cars and BART. We didn't need a car (the only reason we considered getting one was to go to Marin County) even to go to Berkeley. Would gladly stay at the Kabuki again next time we're in San Francisco!

We took my wife, daughter and babysitter to this hotel just this past weekend for a three night stay. It was exceptional. The location is perfect, the staff is friendly, helpful and very nice. We received an upgraded room which was a wonderful surprise. The room was definitely big enough to house three adults and one baby! The suite with refrigerator, stove and dishwasher is huge! The morning breakfast in phenomenal as well, you have to be there because it is a great start to the day. I would definitely recommend this hotel for families and business. A great place. I see also on a fellow review about a staff member named David. He is excellent and I was going to write to the management of the chain to tell them what an attribute he is to their hotel as well as their other staff.

The hotel is very well-located near the theater district, with great restaurants and a great deli and wine shop just up around -th Ave. We stayed for five nights, and had a comfortable bed and good service, especially from Greg. The only drawback is that here's not much public space and what's there is pretty minimal. The little courtyard is lovely, but not much use at this time of year. Excellently priced for the area, however--you can't have everything unless you really, really want to pay for it.
Had a corner room which gives you an awesome view of Detroit. A bit more expensive than the regular room but worth it. Very clean and the hotel staff was friendly.

Attended a conference here in july ----. also had time to enjoy the resort. we stayed in a villa with bedroom, living are (which was quite large) and bathroom-kitchen. very nice and clean. the grounds are beautiful! the bed was soooo comfortable. went to the main pool which had a hot tub and a bar if you needed a drink:) Excellent. beautiful pool:) Had a drink at the barefoot bar and grille. it was good. friends of ours ate there and said the food was delicious. this resort is in a great location. across the bay from seaworld so you can view the fireworks from the resort. some rooms are on the beach and you can have bonfires on the beach. Great stay!

I recently stayed in this hotel for four nights. The location was everything I needed - it is an easy walk to the Ferry Building, Chinatown, California St cable car, Pyramid Building and Downtown. It was not much further to walk to the Coit Tower, Pier --, Alcatraz Ferry and Glide Methodist church. Staff in the hotel were very friendly and treated me so well. The executive lounge on level -- was small but OK although I was disappointed that no milk was left out during the day if needed in hot tea or coffee and there is no happy hour for alcoholic drinks as is the standard for executive lounges in hotels in other parts of the world. The dining options available here are very good with plenty of choice at reasonable prices. Room was clean, comfortable and quiet and had a balcony which was a bonus. Some of the decor could do with an update and the hotel hallways look very tired, really needing a fresh look. Overall, I recommend this hotel for the business or holiday traveller as a wonderful base for your time in San Francisco. I have stayed in a number of Hilton and other hotels across the USA this month and this one has been the stand out by far. Well done to the team.

My Fiance and I absolutely adore Studio Plus in Philadelphia. What we don't like about it is, when we register for a room and they take our credit card information, they actually charge our card """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""twice"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Once when we make the reservation, and again when we check out, we are charged again. Then we have to call the bank when we get home and have the bank cancel the second charge. We don't feel that the Studio Plus should be double charging us like that. But, other than that, we abolutely love staying there, and we stay there quite often. We figure that the one complaint will not overpower the positive feelings that we have about the Studio Plus. We just wanted to bring it to your attention and hopefully there can be some resolution to the problem of double charging customers. Our overall rating for this hotel = - out of --.

We booked a garden lanai room at Paradise Point off their website. It was supposed to be $--- """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""total"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" per the website. The first thing the woman at reception noted to me was an additional $-- fee for parking. Apparently """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""total"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" does not mean all charges.
When we opened the door to the entry way of our room we were blasted with the musty odor of mold. I'm allergic to mold. Thus, I didn't really enjoy being in our room at all. My nose ran the entire time. I got up at -:-- a.m. and went outside to read to get away from the mold.
The $- million upgrade apparently didn't make it to our room as one of the chairs looked as though someone's cat had sharpened their claws on it . Other pieces were really banged up. The thin, poorly insulated walls brought us a little closer to the family with small children and a baby next door than we might have wished. How many times can small children open and close a hotel room door while their neighbors are trying to take a little afternoon nap? We lost count but we were awake and trying.
The woman at check in put us in a room on a lagoon. She told me that she loves those rooms. The lagoon was an algae filled mud hole surrounded by bare dirt. The algae was huge and biologically fascinating but less than aesthetically pleasing. 
I would happily go back to Paradise Point, walk around the truly beautiful grounds, other than the lagoons area, maybe have a tropical drink in the bar, and then drive away to a fresh, clean room somewhere else in the San Diego area.

Hotel Union Square Date: --th Sept -- 
Reviewer: Carol - London UK.
Apologies for late review. Arrived from UK looking forward to our stay in the Hotel Union Square especially after seeing their website, extremely disappointed. We asked for a non smoking and quite room, we got room --- on the -th floor overlooking the car park, refuse to take this room, you could not swing a mouse let alone a cat in that room, it was the smallest closet I have ever seen, and the bathroom was smaller that a cruise bathroom. My husband immediately went to see about changing rooms, they then offerred us room --- on the same floor - the bathroom was larger, the closet was walk in but still small just enough to put the cases in, but the room was still small, we had no drawer space hence had to live out of our cases. The coffee machine was on the top of the TV, but to make coffee the machine had to be placed on the floor because the flex wire did not reach the plug socket. The view from our bedroom was another guest's room, our windows were opposite each other so when they were in we had to close our curtains. The reception staff were helpful and friendly. But the location is excellent and right in the centre of everything. On leaving the hotel I asked how many of the rooms they had like the one on the website and the picture by the lift, the receptionist told me that they were doing up the rooms and the website is very misleading to guest booking that hotel. Would not ever go there again. The Trading Standards dept in San Francisco should investigate this hotel as it is totally misleading people who book this hotel.

Im sure the cheaper , smaller rooms are worth staying in for $-------, the location is excellent, the lobby very inviting, but $--- plus tax for a studio king is really not worth the money. ---sq ft of trying to be trendy space,more felt like it had been kitted out by Ikea, very drab and uncosy, for the same money you can stay in The Mark or The London or even The Greenwhich down in Tribeca.
The cheap rooms yes, stay there, for real money go elsewhere.

We stayed - night at this property before an early morning flight out of Sky Harbor. It was very convenient to be close to the airport. Took approx. --minutes to arrive at Rental car return.
Wish we could've stayed longer. It was a nice change after having spent the previous - nights at Grand canyon lodging(Yavapai Lodge). After being cramped in the motel type lodging, it was a luxury to have a separate bedroom, sitting area, kitchen & balcony. It was immaculate & looked so new. 
We used the pool & hottub that evening. The size of the pool was adequate & the hottub was pretty large. The pool area was comfortable with a few chairs & loungers. There were smokers under the pavillion which is located by the pool area. Not sure if this was truly a designated smoking area. Thought it was a smoke free property. 
There were guest luandry rooms on our floor which was also a good ammenity offered. W-D was $-.-- each. Dryer ate up my coins & never did start but front desk staff immediately reimbursed me. Just used the -nd dryer in the room. They also had a wheeled laundry cart available for use so you didn't have to use your suitcase or bags to transport your laundry.
There were plenty of parking spaces. Also, many choices of restaurants around the hotel. We didn't have the evening manager's reception since we stayed over a weekend. Missed the free breakfast because of catching a very early flight. So can't comment on these.
We enjoyed staying here even though for only - night. Would recommend if staying in Phoenix especially if needing to be close to the airport.

My husband and I first discovered Hotel -- a few years ago. Since then we have stayed here several times--excellent location, clean rooms and bath, very helpful staff. Staying there makes us feel like part of the neighborhood when we return.

Tiny and cold bedrooms ( even after paying for an upgrade) - dark corridors and despite being a guest paying for - rooms we were denied seating in the bar because tables were reserved for others arriving later. Had an argument with the security person who said he would throw us out if we sat at the table , we ignored him of course. What a pretentious dump , stupid us for choosing style over substance.

Just returned from nine nights at the Hampton Inn and what an excellent Manhattan hotel this is. It's not a luxury hotel but who wants to sit arround their hotel in New York? It's clean, comfortable and has very good facilites. My room at the back on the --th floor was very comfortable and quiet. Beds are very comfortable and room facilites good. There is a good breakfast available, included in the room price providing a good range of foods to get the day started, even allowing for the paper plates and plastic cutlery. The staff are friendly and helpful and the hotel is in a great location for getting around New York. Overall, excellent value for money and highly recommended.

We booked this hotel for our last night before flying home to the UK as it was only -- miles to the airport and close to shops and restaurants. What we didn't know was that it was beside a very noisy highway that had traffic on it all night and we got little sleep. The lorry running its engine in the car park at -.--am for over -- minutes did little to help and reception appeared to be oblivious to it. The restaurants turned out to be fast food joints and the shops were out of town depots. Breakfast was in a room too small for the number of guests with the result that many ended up going back to their rooms with trays, others sat at the top of the stairs and some even went down to the reception area with their trays.

We stayed at The Night Hotel for a week over the St. Patrick's Day parade and absolutely loved it. Fantastic location, good breakfasts, decent size room and bathroom, brilliant amenities, cool staff, especially the doorman. We are returning to NY in October with our kids and were looking forward to staying at The Night Hotel, until we discovered that the rates have increased by a hundred percent and continue to rise each time we contact the hotel. Although this would still be our first choice we cannot understand (or afford) the big difference in price.

Stayed there last night and have to say that the location is fantastic. Close to the subway and to the park. The hotel is very loud and the walls are paper thin. I could hear everything that happened next store. When it rained over night it sounded like it was landing on tin so pretty disruptive to sleep. The bed was comfortable, the bathroom was small but was updated so it was fine. The staff was very helpful. Great for a quick visit but if staying a long time may not get great sleep. But, would probably stay again due to location.

We stayed recently at the Barclay for a weekend and were very impressed. We had a great room that was very spacious and quiet on the top floor. The service was great- the room was absolutely spotless, check-in was a friendly breeze, and everyone we encountered was warm and helpful. The beds were extremely comfortable and we slept great both nights. The lobby was hopping in a good way- this hotel has good energy. If we'd had more time it would have been fun to linger more in the lobby and people-watch. We have stayed further downtown on some previous nyc trips but the convenience to Central Park and the theatre district were fantastic, plus you are close enough to downtown that it is just a short cab ride. Finally, I thought the hotel's.environmental efforts were very cool, and I like that they are focused on being green. We'd happily return!

Being a first time NY visitor, I wanted to be at a good central location, THIS was IT! Empire state building was less than a block from the front door! Subway station, --minute walk from hotel! I have recently returned from a four night stay at the Roosevelt hotel in New York. I travelled there with my daughter, and we found this hotel to be perfectly situated to walk to most of the main attractions.

We choose the room with tow beds as this is what we had requested, but were told that it couldn't be guaranteed. At -pm, it seemd that no-one was given a room before -pm, as there was a very long line of people waiting to be given their room key!
We then found our -th floor room with no difficulty, and our bags soons followed. The room was fine. A little tired but clean and spacious. Very comfortable beds. The bathroom was also clean, but didn't look as though it had benefited from the recent multi million dollar upgrade. 
Plenty of room for storage, including a safe in the wardrobe and a fridge, which was for the use of guests purchases, rather than stufed with expensiive items! Very useful as although the hotel offered a really good room service menu, it didn't seem to provide evening meals, although there were numerous ads for takeaway restaurants in the hotel information folder. We didn't eat at the hotel at all, so can't comment on the standard of food there, but there were so many places to eat very close by.
The only real issue was the noise of the air conditioning unit, although I suppose it drowned out the sound of the traffic and sirens. The room was very warm, despite the air conditioning being on low, although the weather outside was very warm for the time of year!!
The other comment I woud make is that the standard of housekeeping wasn't particularly high.
Overall, the hotel was very impersonal, seeming more like a posh motel, rather than a hotel. Possibly this may be due to it's large size. We found the doormen unhelpful and unfriendly. We asked the concierge one evening to recomend a good mexican restaurant nearby, which she did, very helpfully writing down the directions. We never found the restaurant either that evening nor the next day when we went back to make sure we hadn't missed it.
Despite the little niggles above, I think I would stay at this hotel again, purely for it's situation. This was the first time I had visted New York, so have nothing to compare the hotel to.

Suites adequate for the purpose, but not as thoroughly cleaned as might have been expected - old bits of paper and cellophane in corners, for example, but bathrooms were sparkling. 
Hotel provided breakfasts each day which were plentiful and varied, and had meals three evenings a week, all included in the Room rate.
Staff very courteous and helpful.

Concierge in the front is very helpful if you need any advice. 
Overall, no issues and I would absolutely recommend to a traveler in San Fran.

The location is downtown and the bike and walking paths with river views run for miles along the Hudson and begin in this area. It is a perfect spot to bond with the Statue of Liberty! We like the downtown area because it is quite and has a neighborhood feel. The hotel is close to Tribeca, the Meat Packing district and Soho. The hotel has come a long way since it began it's renovation. The rooms are fully up to speed, but the elevators are a different story.  On a plus side the hotel staff are very friendly and accommodating.

There are not enough sockets. There’s one on the lamp on the desk. The other two are in the bathroom.
There is a hair dryer, but I didn't use it, so I can't comment.

The internet connection is by Ethernet cord, not wireless (at least in my room).

There is a Café Express in the lobby of the hotel. The chicken salad sandwich I got there was actually pretty tasty! The only thing is you can not charge what you buy there to your room and they do not take Amex. The staff at that little café are friendly, and I would recommend it over the room service.
Reading Terminal is only a few blocks away – - minute walk. There are a variety of food stalls to get breakfast or lunch. I had (another!) chicken salad sandwich and apple cider from the Hatville Deli. Very tasty, but I was majorly thirsty for the next couple of hours. I was in SF for the Nike Women's Marathon and with my two boys and husband. I chose Hotel Diva after researching here for suite hotels on Union Square close to the start of the race. Hotel Diva offered a kid's suite that promised a separate room with a tv, Wii, music, karaoke and toys for the kids. When I was making my reservation I asked if it would be fun for eight and -- year old boys. He said he thought so. 
We checked in late and they were very friendly, gave the boys some welcome packages that were a little young for them but they had chocolate! So appreciated. But they didn't give us much information about the perks of staying at the hotel we later learned. The room is located on the third floor in the back of the hotel. The elevators were very cool with blue lights. You walk in the room and to your right is the kids room. It has it's own sink, mirror, closet, dresser, low table with toys and paper to draw on. Bunk beds that the boys said were very uncomfortable. A karaoke machine with only songs like Old McDonald had a farm etc.but you could make cool sounds with it which entertained the boys. And just a flat screen that wasn't a TV, just a dvd player and no Wii was there. The room had a lot of pink girl dress up stuff hanging around, the photos were of girl stuff so this made the boys unhappy. 
There is a good sized bathroom with a toilet, bathtub and a nice shower with great pressure. Sink & mirror outside the bathroom with nice products and a hairdryer. 
In a separate room is the other bedroom. With a queen bed, nice pillows, weepy mattress, dresser, very uncomfortable chair, desk, coffee stand with a Kerig(sp?), closet and a small flat screen on the wall. Also a window that looks directly into the window of a room in the next hotel over(who had much better tv channels) and a view into the windows of the restaurant below.
The room is very quiet with little street noise. The TV is not very good, few channels and difficult to navigate. Wireless was available but really slow on my iphone so I didn't use it.
The next morning we went down and ask for the Wii and they gave us a box with the Wii controller, games and dvds. The games were Wii Resort and other safe and young child games. The dvds were geared to the very young kids as well. The hotel was very clean!
The perks we learned as we were there for - nights:
Little workout room on the second floor: I used the workout room which was fine when I was alone but can't imagine trying to use it with more than two people. 
Rumor of complimentary coffee on the -th floor in the mornings? I just went to Starbucks every morning and spent $--.
Sake in the evenings. We finally discovered this and enjoyed a couple of nights in the tiny lobby with only two seats and tic tac toe. 
Nearby:
Starbucks next door - very happy with this. The Mexican restaurant on the other side: we had wonderful tequila at the bar one night, the food smelled great and it appeared they delivered to the hotel but hard to get a table. Katana-Ya two doors down - great ramen, long lines all day long! The kids loved the ramen. Diner on the corner across the street - yummy, huge servings, good service, great for breakfast(great pancakes) but pricey. Max's diner down the street towards Union Square very good burger (patty melt) the desserts looked heavenly. 
Location is convenient but on the border of rough. Lots of homeless guys asking for money all day long, lots of people smoking outside which made my kids miserable. But close to all the great shopping, lots of restaurants, the cable car, easy (for us we are in good shape) walk to Chinatown, and the ferry terminal. We used the hotel's house car to get back to the airport which was great! About $--. 
In summary: location was good for what I needed, service was nice but could be a bit more helpful and informative, the room was good but not enough space in the adult room(only on the bed) to relax after a long day of walking or running, the kid's room was very spacious but I wish they had more choices for older kids in the movies, Wii games and songs(next time I'll bring my own) and wish the decor would be more neutral for the boys. Yes, I know it's called Hotel DIVA! I would definitely stay again if I need to be in Union Square and I'll consider their other properties as well.

First of all ... let me get this right out of the way. Hotels really need to start being taken to task about these ridiculous fees that border on false advertising! This hotel will put a $-- administrative fee, which is explained as room ammenities into the room cost at the end. I know its only $-- ... but I feel that when you are comparing hotels for value and price, the extra $-- might make a difference. Consider that you will be paying high prices already for parking in the city. Between fees, taxes and parking ... you are looking at an additional $--- per night. I know you cant do anything about the taxes or parking in a city like San Francisco. However ... the fee is crazy. This is not a resort (I am even against resorts charging fees for things like 'lobby refreshments, pool towels, mini-bar' which I rarely use!) This is a hotel ... and its just a scam tactic designed to make the room price look much more attractive against similar hotels up front, and adding it on to the tail end where many guests don't notice. I would never stay at this hotel again based on the (yes, inexpensive for SF) $-- administrative fee. I feel it is sneaky, deceptive marketing and completely unecessary.
The website makes this hotel look a lot better than it is. The rooms are nice and clean, if a bit worn ... and I do love the fact that the shutters open the way the windows do in Italy. It is clear this hotel was going for the whole old world Italy vibe ... even the photographs on the website show a Vespa parked next to the bed in the room with a helmet on the bed. Come on ... really? That is going a bit far!
If you enjoy staying in Italy and don't mind --- square foot rooms with the bare bones ammenities and tighter quarters and classy but sparse lobby decor, this place really does remind you of staying in a cheaper-quality hotel in Rome or maybe Florence. I dig that vibe ... especially in a city like San Francisco which has been called the closest American city to Europe. I dont mind smaller rooms if the vibe transports me back to some cheezy Euro tourist hotel in Rome. But, if you are looking for luxury around the same price, it can be found in San Francisco. The Italian vibe ... maybe in the North Beach section's restaurants. Most people who have stayed in European Hotels that are of the - and - star variety will be at home here. You won't expect central air or huge marbled bathrooms. If you are used to - or - star hotels in the United States, this won't hit the mark for you.
While this isn't a terrible hotel ... I feel they are terribly sneaky. Maybe all the reviews such as this on here who hate on this sneaky fee being added with no good reason to make the rates look lower when booking will make the management understand that many people would rather pay $-- for a hotel they keep coming back to because they feel it is a good fit. Rather than a hotel they avoid because they feel that they were fleeced. One reviewer put it the best when they said it is like being pickpocketed at the train station in Italy.
You'll see this one on a lot of the discount travel websites doing special sales, etc. Its not a terrible hotel ... the value is decent for the city ... and it might transport the Italy-o-phile back to the streets of Roma or Firenze. I've seen reviewers saying they have paid $--- per night on sale websites ... that is along the lines of the value. On the website, at times the regular rooms are between $--- - $---. That is way higher than you would expect them to be.

We were nervous about what we would find as reviews had been rather 'mixed'. We booked at Double deluxe with private bathroom and paid a similar price for - nights accommodation to what most Times Square hotels charge per night.
I have to say we were very pleasantly surprised! the hotel was spotlessly clean ( all common areas ) our room looked as if it had been freshly decorated and the bathroom appeared brand new. the room was cleaned everyday.
We also thought we had a dodgy lock on our door, but much to our embarrassment it was nothing more than us not knowing how to operate it, after overcoming this on our first attempt to gain entry we had no more trouble.
The hotel is right on the doorstep of Times Square, there are a couple of Delis' next door which did great takeout breakfasts and Connelly's pub and restaurant which is - doors away did a fantastic Irish Breakfast.
I don't have any real criticisms...but a few things worth pointing out...there are no tea making facilities in the room and no clock! The view from our window was the flat roof of an adjacent building...but we had the blinds down all the time so it didn't trouble us...we didn't go all the way to New York to sit in our room looking out of the window! The only bin is in the bathroom, again, it would have been handy to have one in the room but it wasn't exactly a hardship!
I would definitely recommend this hotel for anyone looking for a clean comfortable room with no frills at an amazing price and in a great location

I was pleasantly surprised when I stayed here. I knew it would be clean, because TripAdvisor members had said it was, but I didn't expect my room to be as large, or as pretty as it was. My room had a Double bed and a pull out bed for one (from a large chair in the corner). It had a computer and desk with some storage above it, a two drawer dresser, a small closet, and a nice size bathroom with a shower-tub combo. There was an Ironing board and iron in my closet, but I didn't use them. There was bedding for the pull out bed in the closet, too, but I didn't use that either.
The staff were very friendly and helpful. I had left a hat in my room after I checked out, and the maid brought it out to me while I waited for the elevator. My room did face the street, and there was a little street noice, but nothing that kept me up, or woke me up. The subway is just one short block away. There are two theatres on the same block, and many more within walking distance.
The lobby is comfortable, and has a very clean bathroom on the same floor.
I really enjoyed The Mayfair Hotel, and look forward to my next trip.

Okay for business travel. Great fitness facility. Within walking distance of great food and music. Try the happy hour at Serranos ( around the corner) and if you have a sweet tooth try their cream filled churros.

My first impression of the W on Lex was a good one. I had tweeted that I would be arriving shortly and they asked me to DM them my information so they could insure the room was ready. I did in fact DM them, and reiterated that I had called a week prior to request a hypoallergenic room due to a feather allergy. 
Upon my arrival at -PM on a Friday, I was told at check in that this request had not been specified in the computer. They comped us two drinks at the bar and enrolled my husband in the SPG program as they stated it would make it easier to track my allergy in the computer. We were told to enjoy our drinks at the bar and the room on the --th floor (which I believe are larger """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Wonderful"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" rooms) would be prepared without down bedding and they would deliver our keys to us at the bar.
When -- minutes passed, I returned to the check in desk to see if there had been any progress with our room as we had dinner reservations and I wanted to have a shower and get dressed before then. 
The helpful gentleman who originally helped us was with another customer so we were assisted by a very rude man who kept cutting me off when I was trying to explain what I needed. When I started to say """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I wanted to check the status of the availability of my room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" he cut me off and said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""YOU ARE ALREADY CHECKED IN"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" as if I didn't know. He then told me that we were going to be in room ---, on the -th floor. Due to the discrepancy I reconfirmed that this was the down-free room, not the one we were originally assigned. 
I'm not going to allow the actions of this one gentleman to taint my view of the whole establishment as everyone else was super friendly and very helpful. 
I've noticed that a lot of people who have stayed at the W on Lex in the past have complained of small rooms, but in honesty I have stayed in about -- other NYC hotels and they are mostly comparable. 
Our view was of the top of a parking garage, but at least it was quiet.... except when a car alarm started going off at -AM.
The bathroom had an acceptably sized shower with good water pressure and plenty of hot water. The toilet had a good solid flush. The mirror was very well lighted. We were supplied with Bliss Spa bath products which were amazing. You can buy full size varieties at the shop downstairs. The frosted glass door, however, did not have a latch and the door had a tendency to open whenever it felt like it. Though I love my husband very much, there are certain things I don't want to see. And vice versa, I'm sure.
When we first checked in, the room was quite hot and stuffy. I couldn't quite figure out how to get the A-C to the right temp, it seemed to always be running. I managed to get it to turn off then just opened the window a crack and everything was fine. 
The bed and pillows were very comfortable, but there wasn't much on the bed in the way of blankets. Luckily the room was always a little too warm anyhow. 
On the last night of the stay, we arrived back to our room to a cheese and berry plate and a split of Coppola's Merlot. A very nice little treat. 
All in all, I wasn't completely impressed with the room itself but I really appreciate all the staff did to make up for not having the room ready to specifications.

I have stayed at this hotel countless times for a variety of conferences (my first time in ----). I always enjoy staying in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""old part""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""--the Wardman Tower--because I love the charming details of such an older building. However, on this trip, it became really clear to me that that side is desperate for a makeover. (My friends' rooms in the Center town were more recently renovated, but they are a lot darker and smaller than on the Wardman side.) My first room was large, but, during my second day there, it developed a leak from the ceiling directly over the toilet. I discovered this right before going out at -:--PM, so I called down and told the desk. Well, when I got back at --PM, it still wasn't fixed. I called to complain, and they moved me to a full-sized suite, with a balcony. That was great, and I really enjoyed the extra space in that room. (Although it was inconvenient to find that the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""wet bar"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" wasn't wet at all--there was no sink! and the fridge had been removed as well--I had had one in my first room.) However, both rooms were frayed (one of them had a lamp with a literally frayed shade), dingy, and definitely in need of some fabric and carpet upgrades. They were clean (I obsessively check for bedbugs everywhere I stay, and I found zero evidence in either room, nor anywhere else I was in the hotel), but old. For the first time, I actually thought to myself--should I not stay in the Wardman tower? That's sad, because I love its big old windows, crazy chandeliers, and old school crown molding. 
That being said, I was happy that they upgraded me instead of just not fixing my problem, and the service in the hotel was good--room service was decent and arrived quickly, bell service was efficient, and the location of course is excellent for access to the Red Line Metro, walking to Adams Morgan, etc. The internet service is expensive, but it is fast and reliable when you sign up for it. I still like this hotel, but next time, if they haven't renovated the Wardman Tower, I will ask for the Center Tower--which seems such a shame. I can stay in a generic Marriott anywhere--but there's only one Wardman Tower, with its history and charm.

Although the room was small, it was spotlessly clean. The bathroom appeared to be recently renovated with a shower, no bath, but in excellent condition. Staff were friendly and helpful. And all this a half a block from Times Square, within easy walking distance of all the theatres, Fifth Avenue shops, and excellent restaurants. Would definitely make this my hotel of choice for a week-end getaway.

When I started researching hotels in the Chicago area I came across The Trump Hotel and thought to myself could this hotel possibly live up to the reputation of it's huge name sake or is it just hype. If you chose to stay at this hotel, don't do it because it is a hotel name after a famous person do so because by far it is the best hotel to stay in. I liked my stay at this hotel. The only problem that I had was when I reserved the room, I told the lady over the phone, two people would be staying and I wanted two twins. When I went to check in, they said they had a Queen bed and a rollaway bed and that they were going to charge me an extra $-- because there were two people. I was mad! She didn't charge me but it was frustrating because I didn't get what I asked for. Oh and another thing, the guy at the front desk didn't tell us to use our key to use the elevator. So we got on the elevator all confused and it took us to the --th floor and we had to use stairs to get to our floor. From the moment I walked in to the lobby to the time I left - days later this place feels different than any other hotel. I stay in --- hotels each week and nobody does it better than theWit. First let me start off by explaining that I did not spend the night at this hotel. Rather, I spent a lot of time inside it because that was where my work conference was held. However, I observed enough of the place to write a pretty thorough review. 
Positives: The hotel is really unique. I liked the location because it was near many places to eat on our lunch break. Like everyone else said, it's a cool piece of history, and if you like places that are historical or just """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""different"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" you may like this hotel. The lobby is especially interesting and pretty. The conference facilities were really nice. Good food offerings and they kept the temps comfortable. The staff seemed nice except for one exception which I will get to in a moment.
Negatives: There is a worn and overused feel to the place. Carpet is worn and everything aside from the entry feels like it needs refreshed. I understand you want to keep the place accurately historical, but there was a sort of...old smell. Okay, here is the biggest issue: We are sitting in the conference room when suddenly a loud roar is heard overhead and the whole room shakes. That's the train coming in over top of the building. Very distracting to our session, and it happened on the hour. I can only imagine how it must of been to sleep in that commotion. My friends that stayed there were not too pleased. I chose to stay at a hotel down the block because I did my Tripadvisor research. I did peak in a room that had the door open for maid service and it looked clean but a bit dated as far as the furnishings. I saw a small indoor pool and hot tub. They looked clean and nice but they were quite small. One last thing--I had lunch on property in the little place by the front entrance. The service was horrible. Our waiter kept forgetting to bring us stuff we requested, and then he would disapear and forget to check on us. Food took forever--no refills--and when it came it was underwhelming considering how much it cost. The place was semi empty so I do not know what the issue was...but that was my only negative interaction with any staff person. I would consider staying here because it wasn't that bad--except for that train noise!!

My husband and I have recently stayed at the Sheraton in downtown Denver twice; both times exceeded our expectations! Check in was fast and easy and the staff were all very helpful and polite. Our room was a little small, but very clean. And the bed was incredibly comfortable! We had no problems whatsoever during both stays, we will be staying at this hotel everytime we're in Denver.

I stayed here for four nights on business. Rock hard bed, my room smelled of cigarettes, the ac couldn't keep up, the room was humid and dank, and I ate something in the restaurant that had me sick for three days. Yuck.
Hotel Pennsylvania on -th Avenue, opposite Penn station, is the filthiest hotel I've ever visited. Hotestly, I doubt the have cleaned it since it was built long time ago.

I was a little worried about this hotel based on the mixed reviews, but we had a great stay there. The rooms and pool area were very clean. The front desk was friendly. The breakfast was great - it was very crowded, especially on weekends, so be prepared for that. If the breakfast area was a little bigger, it would be perfect. The hotel is a little hard to find but we had a great stay.

The Drury Inn is located at the famous Riverwalk. This is truly a wonderful place for strolling and taking a boattour. The hotel has pleasant rooms and a nice atmosphere. Breakfast is complimentary as well as free drinks and food in the afternoon. The food however is of poor quality, the drinks (- per person) are netter, including wine and cocktails. From the hotel you can walk easily to historic spots such as the Alamo. There is also a good mall, the Riverside Mall.

Stayed here one night and enjoyed it very much. Lovely hotel. Very nice rooms and bathroom. Different than the usual hotel room since it was in a historic building. Very large tub and large flat screen tv. Beds very comfortable and hotel was pretty quiet although we could hear some tv noise late at night from adjacent room and outside equipment so a different location might have been better within hotel. The only negative surprise was the lack of parking and the valet cost of $--.-- per vehicle per night. Pretty high in our experience for the Dallas area. Bolla restaurant was excellent.

Literally just outside the door is Quincey Market and Faneuil Hall. A five minute walk takes you to the North end, Paul Revere's House and the Old North Church. Ten to -- minutes in another direction takes you to Boston Common and the cemetery where Sam Adams. John Hancock and a slew of other well known patriots are buried.
The subway system station (the T) was directly across the street. We bought a seven day """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Charlie card"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The system will take you anywhere including the not to be missed JFK Library and Fenway Park which turned --- this year.
The accommodations are what you would expect of any Marriott. The staff was friendly and quickly handled any request we had.
Close to Lax. Newer Sheraton model. Updated rooms and solid service.

We have just returned from a four night stay in New York. We decided on the Shoreham due to it's fantastic location and were not disappointed. 
Being on --th it is handy for just about anywhere. -th avenue is a matter of yards away, Central Park a five minute walk and Times Square twenty minutes at most.
The hotel itself is bright and modern. Lime green and chrome is its signature. The rooms are small but have everything that you need. I'm not too sure about the frosted glass in the bathrooms though! If somebody uses the bathroom in the middle of the night the other person will be woken up by the light for sure!
The beds are very comfortable and the linen of good quality. The bar and restaurant were being redecorated over our visit, so I cannot comment on them. There is, however, a coffee machine on the ground floor that is free to use and I can highly recommend the coffee itself.
All of the staff were really friendly and helpful and could not do enough for us. There is storage for your cases after you check out, so if you are not leaving until the evening, as we were, you can leave your luggage and make the most of the day. 
All in all our stay was a pleasant one. I am rating it as a three overall as it was not cheap and the sizes of the rooms did not reflect in the cost! Also as the bar and restaurant were not available I cannot judge them.

The Iroquois is very well located and quite charming. The room we stayed in was not large, but it was clean with all needed amenities. The bellman who took us to our room spent time with us giving restaurant recommendations and other tips to make our stay enjoyable.

This was the first hotel I stayed in San Francisco, and my experience was very positive. We arrived and the door staff took our cases, the check-in process was fine and they were happy to upgrade me as my travel agent had made a mistake. The room was clean and adequate. There is free wireless in all the rooms, which is an added bonus. The hotel is located on the doorstep of the Chinese quarter and this was great for getting Chinese food and it is a short walk to the shopping district. The hotel is not served very well by public transport.
As it was our first visit to San Francisco, we approached the concierge who had to be the most helpful man I ever met. He provided some great anecdotes about his various stays around the world. He spent almost half an hour guiding us through the map of San Francisco. You have to ask him about the 'NO' area. He really made our stay.
The decor of the hotel is very pleasant and the bar is very atmospheric in the evenings.

Great choice, everything was perfect !! Go phillies !!

All the staff and the service was excellent. Ask Nicole the conciege for advice, she's fun and she knows everything. We will stay there again next year, no doubt.

The room had pieces of plaster falling from the ceiling and walls. The wait to check in was over -- minutes. The washroom was tiny and did not have a bath tub. Doubletree Hotels are always an added assest to my travels. San Jose Doubletree employees have continuely met my needs and with seamless service every time. I always feel welcome and valued from the van driver to maids and maintence employees. Front desk service top notch! Thank you Doubletree employees!!!

This is the most amazing hotel in the premier location in New York City. We stayed for - nights on the Labour Day weekend.

We were able to check in early and leave our luggage after check out. Newspapers and fruit available at all times. We love walking up and down the marble stairs that open to the lobby. The room is small, but incredibly clean and well laid out -- the cleaning staff do a superb job!! When you deal with white linens -- they'd better be clean (fabulous)!! The complaints about the shower – it is unusual, but there is never any water on the floor!!
The web site is the most accurate you will ever find – it is the sexiest (OK, a little different) hotel in New York City. This hotel is not for stuffy old people that are expecting the Waldorf Astoria and are not in a romantic frame of mind, but I have stayed there and prefer this!!

Chestnut Hill is about - miles north of downtown Philly and is very accessible on the regional railways - each station only about - blocks from the hotel. The hotel was clean and the front desk staff was very solicitous and even friendly. It is an old hotel but the charming area is beyond lovely. On the slightly negative side, walls are thin so when our neighbors decided to entertain guests in their room their jocularity woke us up and kept us up. It is also pretty close cab ride to Navy Pier and to the AMC River East -- movie theater. So overall, if you are looking for a trend setting hip place thats a little pricey but has a great view this would be a place to go.

With all of the people screaming at me in Spanish, it was like an I Love Lucy re-run with me being Lucy!
Easy to get to when visiting the general area. Several one story rooms. Heat wasn't very good but received an extra blanket. Price was right. Breakfast just fine. Simple, clean and convenient.

Was put in a handicap room and I'm not handicap. Shower was very difficult to use since it is meant for the handicap. Much noise from the hallway with doors constantly banging shut at ALL HOURS! Breakfast was mediocre. No newspapers available on weekends -- have to go to the Mariott next door to buy one. No restaurants nearby. Don't expect much from this place. You get what you pay for.

After recent reviews, we were very skeptical of staying here. Let me tell you our stay was fantastic! We had a great corner studio suite on the --st floor with a wonderful view of the Empire State Building. The room was much bigger than we anticipated and was exceptionally clean, which to me matters most when staying in a hotel. I purposely checked everything to make sure it was clean and was completely satisfied. While the furniture in the room may be outdated, that did not matter to us much, as the bed was one of the most comfortable beds we have slept in. The hotel staff was very friendly and accommadating. I will definitely stay here again when visiting New York, and will highly recommend to friends.

I booked this hotel for my daughter and her husband to spend a couple of nights enjoying adult time while I got to spend the time with my grandkids. I am disappointed I didn't spend a bit more and get a nicer hotel. 
The room was a queen and extremely small. My -'-"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" SIL had to let his feet hang off the bed because the queen seems to be a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hotel queen"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" or smaller than a standard queen. They told me the room was tiny but they didn't spend much time in the room so it wasn't a problem. Anyone that has stayed at a historic hotel in San Francisco will understand that historic often means small. 
The air conditioner wasn't working well but the kids never notified the staff until they were checking out so I am not rating down for that.
They did not care for the look of the continental breakfast so they went out. No comments on breakfast.
Things that were great: Location, location, location. Very convenient to the riverwalk. They didn't have to use their car once. They had a room on the Alamo side and their view was amazing. They had taken a white noise machine with them in case they were on the atrium side so the outside noises because of the single pane windows were not a problem.
Customer service seemed very good. I called the day before the kids checked in to request an Alamo view and the clerk took notes even though she couldn't make a guarantee. The next day when the kids checked in she remembered my call and they got a nice room. When the kids checked out and told them about the AC not working the front desk was sorry they had problems that had not been corrected even though that was based on the kids not telling.
If you are short or book a king, travel with a noise machine and like to eat breakfast out rather than depending on the hotel breakfast I think this could be a great hotel for the price.

I chose the hotel for location and price. I was extremely happy with the service during my whole stay. Staff was friendly, responsive and helpful. Location is extremely convenient. Rooms furnishings are not the newest, but that does not detract from the comfort, and it was quiet at night. I did not eat in the restaurant and cannot respond to negative reviews of that restaurant's prices, but I will note that nearby restaurants are all pretty expensive.

The hotel is located one block from Powell St and Market St. Couldn't be a better zone to stay. It's - blocks from Union Square. A lot of shopping stores in this zone.
The hotel is an - star hotel, it's very clean and the rooms are a little small (especialy the bathroom) but it's ok. The room has a flat --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" tv, a small fridge (empty, so you can put your own bottles or food inside). The bed was very comfortable (king size).
The only thing that was a little anoying was the shower water pressure (too low). I talk about it to the frontdesk guy and he sent someone to fix it, it was a little better afterwards. The service was great. The bed sheets and towels were clean.
I'll recommend this hotel to anyone that knows that the hotel is not a luxury hotel but it's a fine hotel to stay.

This is a lovely hotel, across the river from Cambridge. The concierge staff was very enthusiastic about making dinner recommendations and reservations for us during Restaurant Week and answering all our direction questions, even when we called from off site. On the other hand, several of the front desk personnel were less than informative and lacked a hospitable attitude.
The location is isolated, however, right next to Route --. You must take the free quick hotel shuttles to the set locations, Aquarium, Copley Square, Harvard Square; walk about a mile to the T, take a taxi or drive into Boston. We enjoyed excellent weather and were good walkers, but it is a factor for future visits. 
Despite the free chocolate chip cookies on check in, I did feel nickel and dimed, parking was $---day, $---day in room internet, $- each Showtime program. My teenage son refused to buy soda there, it was $-.--. We did not have breakfast or any meals there, again due to the prices, $--.-- for a hot breakfast buffet. We did fine stocking up at the Whole Foods and Trader Joe's across the bridge, using the in room refrigerator and microwave. Excellent coffees and teas were supplied (free). 
We requested and received a river view room. The bedroom had - twin beds, which was okay. The living room couch opened to a fairly comfortable double bed. The decor was excellent, although I could have used a mirror in the bedroom. The HDTV in the living room had a GameBoy controller. The room was very clean, except near the refrigerator. 
The pool was on the small side, but enjoyed by the young set. The hot tub was fine. Apparently the sauna has not worked for a long time, but it is still on the hotel web site.
For the $----nite I paid (AAA rate) plus parking, plus tax, I felt the hotel was market-appropriate. I needed a suite layout and chose this hotel, despite the location, because of the shuttle and did not mind the proximity to Cambridge. Check out the shuttle schedule- it does not make its hourly runs at - or - in the afternoon and stops fairly early in the evening.

The Magnolia is a nicely designed hotel. The historic building (a defunct Houston newspaper was here) is beautifully maintained, and we stayed here because a friend said it was a nice hotel with bigger than average rooms. He was right on all counts. We got a standard king room, and at --- square feet, it was more than adequate. We ran into the manager in the elevator, and he seemed very interested in how our stay was going. We saw him again at the evening reception, when he came by to say hello. 
THE LIBRARY: This room is open to relax-kick back, read a book, or check your email. Yes, this is where you'll find a couple of computers with internet access. It was my favorite room in the hotel. Lots of old books line the bookshelves, and the room is clearly available for conferences.
THE BILLIARD ROOM: I've never been to a hotel with a pool table. It's a separate room next to the bar, and it's a terrific touch. No cost to play.
MILK AND COOKIES BUFFET: This was actually a bit of a dsappointment. The build-up at the hotel's website made me think there'd be a cookie chef or something, and warm, freshly bakeed cookies (not that they made that claim... they did no such thing). No such luck. The cookies were good, but they were cool and sitting on the buffet with three kinds of milk. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""buffet"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is next to the bar; it just looked like no big deal. If I owned the hotel, I'd try to make this feature a bit more interesting.
SERVICE: A little bit of good and a little bit of not so good. The manager, as I mentioned, was terrific and seemed genuinely interested in our comfort. The staff was hit or miss. We had a terrific waitress on Sunday night during the complimentary drinks hour. She recommended a good restaurant (Ninfa's... fantastic!), she called the hotel's car service on our behalf, and she was paying attention The next night, we had another waitress and she was completely indifferent -- almost seemed annoyed that we were getting free drinks. (Maybe she thought it would affect her tip.... it didn't, and that's no excuse anyway). Same problem with the valets. A couple were fantastic, while a couple of others seemed disinterested, annoyed.
PARKING: It's $---day for valet. That's about average, and there is some effort required to avoid it. You may not want the hassle. The garage behind the hotel charges $--day, but there are no in and out privileges. Even worse, the cost only buys you a parking space until -AM the next morning. In otther words, you'd have to get out of bed at -AM(!!), walk a block to the garage to pay $- more, put the ticket on your car, and then go back to the hotel. You can park FREE across the street from -PM - -AM and all day on Sunday. My advice: park on the street at night, and move into the garage at -AM. if you're leaving by -AM, just feed the meter for - hours... it's $-.---hour.
POOL-FITNESS CENTER: They have a pool on the roof, which is open -AM---AM. Although we didn't use it, the hotel says the fitness center is open ----.
INTERNET ACCESS: I love that the hotel doesn't charge for internet. Not only is free access available in the room, you can also use a public computer in the Library. Convenient!
RESTAURANT: None! They have room service, though, and the menu looks pretty good. We never tried it, though. There is a little coffee shop at the front of the hotel. 
BREAKFAST: It's free, but it's small. You can get some breads, fruits, and cereal. They charge $-.-- for the bacon and eggs on the hot bar. The coffee is from Starbucks, both at breakfast and in the room.
FREE SHUTTLE: The hotel has an SUV to give people free rides around the downtown area. This was terrific -- efficient and fast. They gave us rides to Ninfa's and back (for a terrific dinner) and to the Toyota Center. 
SUMMARY: The Magnolia Houston needs to make service a bit more consistently great! But overall, it's got a lot of amenties that other hotels don't. The rooms are big and comfortable (great beds!), and for downtown Houston, it's a good value. The location is pretty terrific, as well.

We asked the valet if we could park in front of the hotel because we were driving expensive cars for Monterey week and didn't want them moved. They charged us $-- each for two hours. When we returned to retrieve our cars, at the end of the two hours, we were peppered with questions from passer-bys, while we stood within -- feet of the valet stand. Consequently, we were ten minutes past the departure time, and well within earshot of our departure when they shook us down for another $--.-- each. I wrote a letter to management and never received a response and I'd never go back. While we were at a different hotel, I'd never consider the Valencia for anything again.

I stayed with a group of friends in one of the two bedroom suites and we couldn't have been happier with our stay. The staff were friendly and helpful and the location was fantastic. Having a full kitchen in our room meant we could make our own meals which was a real bonus. Coming from Australia we took full advantage of the surprisingly generous range of free snacks to sample some of the treats we don't get at home.
the staff was extremely helpful and friendly they were very great with our kids lots of other family travelors pool was great laura and marjie were great employees i will definately stay here again

This was a nice hotel but not the quality I would expect from a Hilton. We were on the highway side so I would expect it to be noisy at night-and it was. I didn't think this was any better than a Comfort Inn. At least Comfort Inn offers a free breakfast and has a microwave-fridge in the rooms. Otherwise, it was a nice stay.
It was a treat to stay in a hotel that is historic with friendly service and many extras. As is true for any hotel in the area, the elevated train noise can be disturbing so bring earplugs.

Stayed here for our first-ever visit to Chicago and were very pleased. Front-desk staff was so helpful with theater, dinner and tour reservations and in assisting me with my husband's wheelchair. Accessible room was well-appointed and comfortable. We were close to the theater and activities we wanted to enjoy. We will be back!

If you make reservations online you will notice rate #-, #- and #-. If you are using your AAA or AARP discount you will not receive the amenities for each higher rate.
