My daughter and I came to celebrate her -th birthday in NYC. We had a great time with all that we did there. The hotel was fantastic, we had whatever we wanted whenever we needed it. The room was very clean and had a great view. The service was great. They took our bags when we checked out so that we could go around town and assisted us in getting a taxi back to the train station. We had especially super service by the doorman Hector Isaza. He was so friendly and helpful and just made for an all around GREAT trip. Thanks for an awesome time and a great -th birthday for my daughter Paige.

I have stayed at this hotel twice and have to applaud the helpfulness of the staff there. They were always helpful and aided me when I needed something. The hotel is pristine and the rooms are cozy. 
The food is way overpriced and the hotel's location is out of the way from the rest of downtown Boston. The worst thing about this hotel is the overly expensive parking fees ($---$--).

One night business trip was made into a wonderful stay by the very friendly staff. The room was very clean, comfortable and modern. Great pillows. Breakfast was yummy. Nice lounge like feel around a soothing water feature in the breakfast area. Overall the staff put it over the top for me. Excellent job!

We went to Memphis for my husband's college fraternity reunion and stayed at this Marriott for - nights. The formal dinner was held at there, too. One day they failed to make up the room. True, I had the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""do not disturb"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sign out until - a.m. but they never came back ! The smell of wet towels greeted us when we returned to the room in the afternoon and we had to turn the a-c down to -- degrees or so to ease the stench after the sun had warmed everything and begun to mildew the room. I called the front desk and was informed that the help had already left for the day, so I made the beds myself and went in search of coffee and toiletries. The one day we partook of the breakfast buffet was memorable for the powdered orange """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""juice"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and probably powdered eggs. Tasteless food except for excess salt. Sadly, the dinner at the function was equally limp and devoid of taste. If we return we will not stay there again.

The rooms are not bad, but nothing exceptional given the price that you pay. Where you really do pay way too much is the service. I was treated so rudely while simply working out that I would not go back to this hotel if I could stay there for free, so unpleasant was the experience. This is what happened. It started while I was working out in the gym. An aerobics instructor parked herself right in between me and the tv, not caring at all that she blocked the view. It took a while but she finally moved and moved just outside the gym. But there she was still talking so loudly that I still could not hear the tv. Given that she was outside the gym the solution seemed easy, I closed the door. Then she erupted and started telling me that I couldn't close the door and that I was an impolite unpleasant person. And that in front of other people. Interestingly, only the aerobics instructor itself was disruptive. Her pupils that were also crossing the room actually did behave normally. The worst thing was that a bit later the director of the spa came to me. Not to apologize! No she came to me to explain to me that this (meaning the gym) was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""a high traffic area"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Well, if the director of the spa thinks you can just choose right in front of tv screens in gyms, then you know what kind of place we are talking about
To be fair, it seems the spa is run by different people and the hotel manager thought this was not acceptable either. But still, I picked this hotel because I thought I could work out.

I visited New York for Christmas in ---- with my partner for seven nights. I didn’t originally want to stay at this hotel but was running out of time to book it and this was the only one within my price range as they had an offer on. It was the best choice I made as all the others I was wishing to stay at turned out to be awful and the Park Central was great.
It’s only a couple of blocks from Times Square and everything is within walking distance. The exterior display looks quite posh at night when all lit up and the lobby was really clean and elegant. The staff were really helpful, especially the concierge who helped us find shops and other attractions nearby. We didn’t have to wait anytime at all for check in but they told us we could have an upgraded room as no non-smoking rooms were available, or wait -- minutes for the standard room. Obviously we took the upgrade. 
We had two double beds and it was a generous sized room and bathroom, much nicer than the ones I had been looking at before booking it. I found the hotels décor all quite contemporary as well which I prefer, unlike most of the other hotels. Our safe wasn’t working so I called reception who sent someone up straight away and fixed it. I was a bit disappointed with the view from our room but to be honest unless you pay for a Times Square view room you won’t be able to see much in any hotel in New York. The room was cleaned everyday while we were out and fresh towels left.
As we were here for Christmas I was glad the staff were all festive and friendly. They had a piano player some nights in the lobby which was nice also and I just generally found the hotel brilliant, especially as I was so dubious at staying there. I recommended it to a friend when I returned home who then stayed there and also loved it.
I’m going back to New York next year but as I booked through Virgin and they don’t offer this hotel I’m not staying there again, although I do want to, I’ll have to see if the next hotel is as good. I would definitely recommend the Park Central as you get good value for money when comparing it to other same rating hotels, plus for the price you won’t find a better place for location. 
Whatever you do don’t get a shuttle to take you to the hotel, was the worst part of any holiday I’ve ever had. The drivers changed twice, drove like lunatics, kept swapping people around, stuffed about - people in one shuttle, and it took two hours to get to the hotel. We got a hotel town car on the way back to JKF and it only took -- minutes and was as cheap as getting a taxi.
If going around Christmas make sure you go ice skating in central park, it was amazing and really festive. Also there is a Jekyll and Hyde restaurant nearby that put on a show while eating and is great fun. All the waiters-waitresses are in character and come round while you eat. We actually ended up going here for Xmas dinner – very untraditional but it was good.

Everything you need is just steps away from your doorstep. Deep-dish pizzas are right around the corner and a grocery store right across the hotel are convenient food options nearby. The hotel itself is a relaxing sanctuary in the middle of the city.

I don't get some of the other reviews on this site. I was in town on a business trip and this place was perfect for me. I had a large room overlooking the harbor. Bed was super comfy and linens were new & clean. The staff told me that the hotel had been refurbished recently and it was clear that it had been. The free wi-fi was great for checking my email. Breakfast was nothing fancy except for the waffles (yum!!) and free too. I had dinner across the road at the Pizza joint and that was very tasty and convenient. There was some road noise but not too bad.

We stayed at the Embassy Row Hotel Aug ---- for -- nights. - Adults and - Teens. The hotel is located right in Dupont Circle, great location for restaurants, shops, walking, and the Metro. Quick bus ride to Georgetown, and if you are energetic you can walk to the Whitehouse. The metro is really easy to use though and almost all of the sites can be reached by the metro! All the staff at the hotel were so friendly and helpful, breakfast is included, cereal, cheese, bagels, yogurt, coffee, tea, etc. The rooms are small, but the bed is great. No fridge, which was difficult for the - of us way too many trips to the ice machine. The restaurant is closed even though the signage states they have one. This was not a problem, as so many are right within a quick walk. We had - connecting rooms. The bathrooms are small and without tubs. The rooms are equipped with hair dryers, coffee makers, TV with movies on demand. New releases are $--.-- but they have many lower price selections. Unfortunately the rooms are in need of an update, peeling paint, carpets are very tired, wallpaper is ripped and ceiling needs help. The hotel has umbrellas if you need them, so don't pack. There are old safes in the hotel, we used them only a couple of times, had no problems. Could hear folks in another room and the AC is incredibly loud, bring ear plugs. Only - suitcase stand, in the room. Be great for a short trip, but if you are staying as long as we did you might want a larger and more updated hotel.

The W group is not what it was. Sure, it's hard to get a room with a decent view in New York, but the cheapest rooms here are not just tiny but look out on air ducts: you have to crane to see a piece of sky. Pictures are falling off the bathroom walls, the service is curt, and the hotel is investing in fake grass in the lobby in a doomed attempt to become the coolest bar in town. Clean, but depressing and characterless.

When you're visiting New York City, your hotel room is about - thing: sleeping. You want to be out in the city walking around, attending shows and eating in some of the great restaurants. You want to go back to your hotel late at night after enjoying this city that never sleeps...to sleep, so you can get up and party again the next day...or get to the airport if you must. It's vitally important, therefore, that the bed be as comfortable as possible and there are blackout drapes to blackout the light that comes in far too early if you've been enjoying some of the nightlife in NYC. 
The second important amenity is a good shower and-or bath. The city is a grimy place and you want to get cleaned up both before you venture out there and when you get back in. You need a good shower head at the very least and a clean place with a good mirror (magnifying if possible) for us ladies to make-up. 
There is a third amenity...a view is always nice in NYC. 
From back to front then....the view from our room was directly over the WTC construction. ---- will always be an extreme example of terrorism, fear, and innocent loss of life. The view, even though the window was as small it could be...(why they did not make the window bigger must be about money because there is no other reasonable explanation), was directly over the WTC construction. This view is both beautiful and sad. There is a --th floor restaurant with a big terrace that has some of the most spectacular views of lower manhattan and the WTC you are likely to find. The view from this hotel is spectacular. 
The bathroom was small but fine for me and my man...we just used it at different times. We're spoiled and at home we have a sink for each of us. One sink is all that could fit in this bathroom. We have a Japanese washlet toilet at home, so anything other than that pales in comparison but the toilet did have a water saving flush system. The towels were fine although not nearly as plush as they could be...but then that's true everywhere unless you're staying at a property like the a peninsula. There was no bathtub and the shower was fine. I hate shower curtains though because they cannot possibly be sanitary unless they are switched for a brand new one between guests. The shower head was a hand held that was attached to a verticals pole to adjust for height. The shower head itself was like one of those waterpik heads. The problem? No hot water. The first time we took a shower, the water was tepid at best. We had just travelled from LA and it was too late for an engineer to fix it until the next morning. They did fix it and it worked fine after that but when the housekeeper cleaned the shower in between guests, did she-he not notice that there was no hot water? How long had it been that way? Had the prior guest in our room just put up with it? Strange. I do appreciate a hand held shower head to rinse all over so that was a plus. Oh, and I was happy to have a magnifying mirror on an arm from the wall. Very nice. 
The room itself was small but fine. We knew we were not getting a - star hotel here...my boyfriend was sent to NYC for business that was taking place in lower manhattan and he could walk to the offices from this hotel. 
The bed was seriously disappointing. We had a king bed...it was two twin beds pushed together with a filler in the middle. It was hard and the sheets were stiff, not soft. The pillows were great, too bad the rest of the bed couldn't have been as nice as the pillows. We are spoiled and have tempurpedic beds at home, so I admit it does take a very special bed to make me happy. But there is no excuse in NYC to have two twins pushed together. The mattresses were hard and the middle filler even harder...makes intimacy difficult because you have to be on one side or the other but not in the middle. The least they could do is put a king mattress topper over this mess to make it better. The room was clean and as other reviewers have said, the water outside your room is nice. However, the walls are very thin in this hotel and you could hear the people on both sides of you. There were good blackout drapes on the tiny window so we could sleep in. 
Since my boyfriends company paid for the room, we could not complain to them but the management should know that really the beds are subpar, and that makes it difficult to give them more than - stars. Get some nice (real) king beds please. 
The staff were great and very helpful with our hot water issue. The location, if you need to be near lower manhattan, is wonderful. However, there is a W hotel across the street with the same view of the WTC so unless club quarters fixes the bed problems, we will stay at the W next time. 
One last thing, yes there is a fitness room. It is a windowless room that no one would want to spend much time in. You're better off going for a run outside.

I stayed at the Hotel Indigo for a recent business trip. I had stayed there several times in its previous incarnation (Claridge Hotel) and had enjoyed the great Gold Coast location; with the remodeling, it's an even better value. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""spa"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" theme is fun, with rooms and lobby in seaside blues and greens. I had a very spacious room with a lounge chair, big separate area with a coffeemaker, and lots of room to move around. Hardwood floors are a nice touch. However, the woman on duty the night I checked in did not know her job. I arrived late in the evening, so went immediately to bed -- and was awakened by another couple entering my room! They had been checked into the same room as I was. Sure, I should have locked the deadbolt, but this is still not what a woman traveling alone wants to happen. I complained to the manager the next day, and while he apologized, I was not offered any discount or even a coupon for a free drink or cup of coffee. Obviously they're still ironing out the kinks with the service staff at the Hotel Indigo.

We stayed one night prior to flying out of LAX the next afternoon. The hotel is beautiful, well appointed, and clean. There's a cool outdoor fireplace on the main level by the pool. We enjoyed the wine hour and the house Cabernet. We spent the evening with friends and returned to see a nice view of the city. It's just off I----, so if you have trouble sleeping - they provide ear plugs. We were above the main hotel driveway, had the a-c on, and slept like babies. The sheets were so soft, but the pillows were firm enough. They provide nice shampoo, conditioner, soap, and q-tips. The valet service ($--) was easy to use and the valets were very nice. A nice place to stay. Free wi-fi was handy.

A gracious, large lobby with elegant furnishings that speak to a bygone era invite you to rest and relax the moment you walk into the door. From flooring to ceiling it sparkles with cleanliness and care. The chandeliers are rumored to be replicas of those aboard the Titanic (shall I mention the chandelier in my sister's bathroom?). Our rooms were among those not yet renovated and I hope renovation will not replace classic beauty with a misguided updated look. A room with four poster beds overlooking Travis Park, a changing room and closet to one side and a bathroom to the other. Exceptional customer service and every staff member was pleasant and helpful. The restaurant provided gluten free alternatives that were gluten free. Knowledgeable employees who readily assisted with accurate, helpful answers. Attention to detail evident throughout. Convenient location, steps away from the Riverwalk and Alamo. Definitely a historic hotel worth keeping!

We have been traveling forn over twos day from Arizona to Washington D.C. And I must say that my stay here at the La Quinta Inn & Suites Memphis East-Sycamore View. Is the best kept secret of the La Quinta Inns. The service was great and the warm and inviting suroundings make my night here a blessing. If you ever travel through this area, you must make this the one stop to relax. Heated pool and spa bring your swimsuit.

I normally stay at the JW Marriott when I'm in Indianapolis but as it was full due to the Indy --- I had a room at the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""old"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Marriott. This is an average hotel that should have a bit of an upgrade. The rooms are fine and the amenities as well. I don't mind the shampoo-conditioner-soap dispenser in the shower but it does have a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""budget"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" feel to it.
The rooms are clean and the beds are fine though the pillow top could be replaced as it is getting soft.
The internet works fine though I did have some problems with the WiFi for my smart phone but could usually get it to work again.
I like the sports bar downstairs and as it was nice weather could sit outside.
The staff are friendly and helpful which makes up for some of the smaller short-comings.

This hotel fit the bill for what we needed-- a last minute hotel in NYC for - night. Som pros are the locations--East side and walkable to lots of things--price & bar on the top of the hotel. Drinks were definately pricey, but the view is great and the perfect place to get a drink before heading back to our room. The room itself was mediocare & very dated. The tv was old, which I can deal with, but very limited cable access (you couldn't even get channels like ESPN). It suited our needs for one night, but I doubt I will be back again.

Good location, especially if you anyway have a car (there is a parking garage just by-under the hotel, extra fee). OK neighborhood for LA which seems quite unusual. The continental breakfast was very good (for a continental breakfast, probably the best we experienced during our - week trip in USA) but the breakfast room was unfortunately very small and often crowded. Very spacious room with a ditto bathroom. Huge and comfortable king size bed. We got a room facing the street so there was some street noise (it’s LA) but not too bad. If you are a light sleeper ask for a room further back in the building. Maybe not the most “fresh” hotel we ever staid at but it was “clean enough”. We recommend it.

my boyfriend and I enjoyed a wonderful weekend at this hotel
-. arrived early after a -am flight, were shown to the breakfast area and told they would try to have our room ready as early as possible, very friendly helpful staff got us in at --am and gave us maps of the area.

-. would highly recommend this hotel, the downside is the breakfast as other reviews have pointed out (very few selections) but they are pleased to point you to other restaurants in the area, and helped us with dinner reservation which was a big bonus!

Stayed here last year right after it opened and was pleased to see the level of service and condition of the hotel are the same. The atmosphere of the resort made me feel at home with all of the history and growth of the resort. The gardens were very enjoyable to stroll thru, the layout and room decor was fun to relax in. My parents stayed here for my mother's birthday and they were very happy with everything. The accommodations were great and their room was upgraded to a room with a view of the park. I could not have been happier with the service they provided and I would definitely stay at this hotel myself. I know my parents would go back as well.

The price could not be beat for being in the city. Even though it is in the Downtown area, close to the seaport - we did not run into any issues finding the place or getting to where we needed to. 
The staff is amazing!! Everyone is so hospitable and very helpful!

I would definitely come back again, I just hope - just like everyone else that the price do not get so high. If it does I'm just glad for the experience. 
Try the Gold St. Diner around the corner, they give --% off to hotel guests. Small discount but it's something! Also the Italian restaurant around the corner from the hotel is superb!!!

Not an imposing facade but, the doorman was very friendly and very helpful to someone who have traveled far. My luggage was cared for and directed me to check-in. No long wait since it is still early; front desk personnel was friendly and assisted me with a genuine and welcoming smile. Check-in done in no time. I was told that I would be informed when my room was ready . They have many amenities at the lobby with free Wi-Fi. Rooms are adequate and very comfortable especially the beds. Very friendly and knowledgeable personnel if you are a conventioner. Great Location to many places. Excellent place to stay for business and personal trip.

Stayed here for - night during a quick trip to DC. We had stayed here a few years ago, and I think we got the room right next to our previous room. Around the corner we ate at a very good restaurant, Cedar, which I would recommend for a delicious, finely prepared meal. The hotel did not have free wifi, which was disappointing.

Firstly WOW, the view from our window -- floors up was breathtaking, read so many reviews about small rooms but when r u in them ?? The bed moves in and out which gave u lots of room loved all the quirky gadgets shower and toilet were funny being see thru but wat people dnt mention there is a curtain u can pull across which separated the bathroom. They do have a galley on each floor that contains free hot drinks and microwave. The only criticisms of our stay that there was no cutlery in galley and most times the machine was not working. We reported it but were told to go to another floor which was also not in use would be better to have tea making in rooms and free muffins and coffee r brill but for breakfast? Free wifi and printing and no charges for local phone calls 
Overall a special unique experience and would definitely stay again. brill location, circle line ferry --- blocks away and bus terminal just up the road recommend gray line bus tours.
Eating in times square expensive hells kitchen is better priced.

I stayed at the Murray Hill East Suites from June --th---st, ----, and we booked it through Priceline (via their name your own price feature). 
I was surprised by what I got for my money when I had """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""won"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" this hotel on Priceline. For those unfamiliar with Priceline you choose the area in which you would like to stay with its star rating (I chose - star, but got a - star so you can luck out that way), and they tell you pretty much right away whether your offer is accepted. I managed to get a whole one bedroom suite (looks like renovated condo) that came with a living room, large one bedroom with king size bed, a small bathroom, and a kitchen. I got all this for an extremely reasonable rate (it would have cost the same for a hostel in downtown manhatten!). 
I was travelling with my fiancee and we were looking for a reasonably priced hotel near all the attractions of NYC since it was our first time. This hotel is on --th street, and Grand Central station is ony --nd so it's pretty close, but not as close as some of the reviews made it sound. It is about a --- minute walk, and it can be a long one in the -- degree celcius heat. Nevertheless it's not a bad location.
The kitchen was small so we didn't end up using it except for the full size freezer-fridge (great for keeping your drinks-leftovers cold). The only suggestion have for ths hotel is to put in microwaves. 
I was impressed by how clean our suite was, and by how large the bedroom and living room were. The tv (although tiny) was good at the end of the day of walking and walking, and there were many channels to choose from.
The bed was huge, and the airconditioning in both the living room and bedroom was nice. The maid did an amazing job with housekeeping every day, making sure the bathroom linens were well supplied and the such.
The concierge downstairs was neither rude nor over hospitable--so if you needed anything it was there but they don't bother you much. 
The hotel did not seem at full capacity which means it was really quiet. The hallways did smell like rancid smoke at times, but our suite was fine. The elevators are old, but I think most buildings would be old like that in manhatten, unless you plan on shelling the bucks for something fancier and much more expensive.
Overall I would say choose this hotel if you are budget minded, and need-want a lot of room, and a place to stay close to everything. We took the subway everywhere, and you can even walk to the Empire State building from the hotel. It's not fancy, but it's good value for your dollar. 
My total trip (hotel & air from Vancouver) was $---- CAD and that is a real bargain for such an expensive city.
Tips:
-) Buy the new york pass. You can buy it there (planet hollywood in times square) or online at newyorkpass.com. Well worth the money and helps you plan your itinerary. You get $-- credit each day of the pass at Planet Hollywood which I used for souvenirs.
The New York pass also allows you to skip ticket lines, like at the busy Empire State Building.
-) Buy an unlimited metropass--it's indispensable and way cheaper than taking a cab in this traffic congested city. You can buy these at the machines there.
-) Credit cards are accepted everywhere! I hardly ever had to fork out cash. Very convenient.
-) Some must see things (all free w- the New York pass):
Radio Music City Hall Tour
Madisson Square Gardens Tour
DO NOT DO THE ROCKEFELLER TOUR unless you want to just look at the art on the buildings for an hour 
NBC Studio tour (go early to reserve your spot--this fills up fast, we had to go the next day)
Circle Line Boat Cruise (we upgraded to the - hour for $- more--nice on a hot day and good to do in the beginning for a good overview of the city).
-) To get to the hotel from JFK airport we opted for the subway instead of a $--+ cab ride (flat rate plus tips-tolls). It is $- for the airport airtrain to the subway and $- for the subway (or you can buy the weeklong unlimited pass for $---week). There are also shuttles you can take like airlink and supershuttle. We used airlink ($-- USD) one way to JFK from the hotel and had a HORRIBLE experience. They billed our credit card, and the driver asked us to pay again in cash! After a LONG discussion we finally got our cash back and was not a nice way to end our trip.
You can prebook Supershuttle online at their website and they give you a discount.
If you found this review helpful please let me know! Your feedback is always welcome.

This was our -nd stay at this hotel. Were there in ----. Location is great. Subway right on corner. Macy's around the corner. Rooms are very clean and bathroom extremely clean.
Staff very friendly. Had view of Empire State Building. Who could ask for anything more!!
Will definitely be back

I recently spent - nights at The Orlando and had a great experience! All of the staff was exceptional - from the valet, to the desk and restaurant. For a very reasonable price, we had a nice sized room, extremely comfortable bed and a nice little balcony with very sound-proof French doors. We enjoyed both the food and drink in the restaurant downstairs and this location cannot be beat. I look forward to staying there again.

I've stayed in other hotels that have been undergoing renovations. From some of the other posts it would appear perhaps normal service has been disrupted a little more than usual.
I found the front desk staff very accommodating, nothing like previous posts. I did ask for a renovated room, having seen some of the posts here before booking, and was given a room on the -th floor. Calling the front desk, ordering room service, laundry...is all that bit more difficult for the business traveller.
It's definitely a business oriented hotel, the seat by the desk is the most comfortable I've ever had, so a big thank you for that. The wireless provided by AT&T and which costs $-- a day is very, very, very poor. By evening when guests are all back, it's unusable. This is something the hotel really needs to address.
I have stayed in down town San Jose in he past, and while I like it, the cost of parking the hire car was extortionate, so free parking here at the Wyndham helps to keep a lid on the expenses.
I didn't have any of the bedlinen issues reported. Everything is clean as you would expect. The bed is very comfortable, and the great quality pillows ensure a good night's sleep. The bathroom area is equally clean and tidy.
When the renovations are done, and they've been through a snagging list I think this will be a very good quality business oriented hotel....but please sort out the wifi, then it will qualify for a very good.
Would I stay here again? Very likely.

Here's just an example of Omni's service: Two of us stayed at the Omni to end a weeklong trip in northern CA. We arrived in a rental car on a busy, rainy Friday afternoon. Our plan was to check in, then drop the car at the airport and return on the train. Bags were unloaded and check-in was smooth and painless. On the way to the airport we realized that neither of us told the bell staff our names or what room we were staying in -- we both thought the other had done it. Our bags were on a cart in the lobby. I figured a --star hotel would leave the bags where they were, a --star hotel would put them aside somewhere and leave us to get them when we returned (this would have been fine in my book), and a --star hotel would check the bag tags, check with the front desk for our names, and have them in the room by the time we returned. Of course the bags were waiting for us in the room, and it was a great worry-free start to a wonderful weekend at the Omni.

I have stayed at several Holiday Inn properties This one is very nice. The lobby is beautiful the rooms are great. There is a nice bar and resturant. Hot coffee in the lobby is a nice touch. The facilities are great. The Staff although very friendly seem a bit less well equipped. I had an issue with cable tv service and had to tell them multiple times about it. and it was clear that one didn't know what the previous one was told. There just seems to be a lack of attention to detail and that is the difference between a good hotel and a great one. Otherwise it is in a good spot with plenty of resturants and shopping and right off the highway. If you get a good rate then I would reccomend it.

Stayed at this hotel for business. The rooms are spacious, clean and the beds are very comfortable. The property is conveniently located off a toll road and there are lots of restaurants close by. Staff was friendly and helpful.

First time SF visitor, the Capri is modest but just fine. Location is quiet, away from traffic and felt safe after dark. Very convenient to shopping, restaurants and buses. Front desk staff very helpful, room service thorough. My only complaint is that the walls are very thin; I could almost follow conversations next door.

The location is good at Lomabrad St. Room and bathroom nice, clean. Free parking, some times you have to leave the key of the car in front desk. Free wifi. You get what you pay for. We had a litlle problem checkin in, it was late, and he couldn´t find our reservation. It took about -- min.

We stayed for a week at the Residence Inn by Marriott in Downtown San Diego and had a very enjoyable stay. My husband was in town for a conference and my - year old son and I tagged along for a vacation - our first time in California. 
The positives: We received a government rate and were able to stay for $--- per night in a - bedroom suite, so clearly the price was right. The location is very good for getting around and within walking distance of Little Italy, Seaport Village, and the ferry to Coronado. You can see the harbor from the front of the hotel. The suite was well furnished, extremely clean, and had nice features like two TVs, a huge couch, a dishwasher, and a full-size fridge with an ice-maker. There was no charge for our son's crib. The pool and hot tub were nice - better than the pictures on their website. The breakfast buffet each morning and manager's reception Mon-Thurs. evenings were convenient and the staff was attentive. The afternoon popcorn snack in the dining room was also a nice touch.
The negatives: Not many negatives, but here's what we came up with. The bed linens (coverlets) were sort of old and tacky. The sheets were fine though. The suite itself was a bit too small. Our son's crib could not fit in the bedroom so he slept in the living room every night. Our main complaint, if there even was one, was that the food at breakfast was not very good in terms of variety or quality. It would have been fine for a few days, but the selection got boring fast. The manager's reception included a different """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""light meal"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Monday-Thursday (ie. The week we were there it was chili dogs one night, pasta one night, baked potato bar one night, and egg rolls one night, and there was always a lettuce salad available too). Not fancy or remotely healthy but who can complain about free beer, wine and soft drinks. 
Overall, we were very satisfied with our stay at the Residence Inn Downtown and would probably stay here again. I would definitely recommend it if this is a location you are still considering after reading this review. 
Oh and about those trains...yea, we heard them. It was really not a big deal to us, although we thought it would be. When we checked in we asked to be closer to the front of the building so we couldn't hear them as much and also I never heard them between -- p.m. and - a.m.

In general a very comfortable stay. Very nice room, quiet, great location, efficient check-in
Just two things to be aware of. I checked in late on Thursday night and payed extra to have a club room on the --nd floor and enjoyed the excellent complimentary breakfast in the Club lounge on the same floor the following Friday morning. However it only opens during the week so was not open on the Friday evening or on Saturday at all so I paid two nights 'club room' premium for one breakfast which was an expensive mistake.
Secondly the lobby is being refurbished so there are no bars or restaurants other than the dark and depressing South Coast Grill on the second floor. I went up to eat, had a quick look inside, saw it had about three lonely diners and went over to the swanky Del Frisco's steakhouse across the road which was buzzing. With so much dining competition across in the Galleria I'm not surprised they are improving the options in the hotel but it looks like it will be a few more months until they're finished.

This hotel is in the first block off Michigan Ave (right across from the Four Seasons) and immediately east of Rush and State Streets. It couldn't have been more convenient. It is an older hotel but our room and bathroom had been totally redone and we were quite pleased with it. The staff that we encountered were exceptionally friendly and helpful. We didn't eat at either restaurant (had already planned our meals before ever arriving...) but there were always folks in them and the food that we could see (some tables are next to windows that face the sidewalks) always looked good! I only have two complaints - (-) they make you pay $-.---day for Wifi (which is typically free at most other hotels I've stayed at), and (-) no coffee maker in the rooms (but it is free every morning in the restaurant area). Out of all the hotels I've stayed in this hotel definitely had the worst customer service. Almost all the front desk staff were incredibly rude. If I was a manager at this chain I would haul the entire staff in to a customer service seminar. In fact, even a basic manners lesson would suffice. The hotel itself is fine. It's older then most residence inn and could use an update, but other then that it's not a bad hotel. Just beware of the pretentious front desk.

We stayed here to attend the Boston Red Sox World Champion, Victory Parade in October. It was a great location, easy walk to Quincy Market, Downtown Crossing, & the Commons. Room was great, pool and hot tub, just right. Parking in adjacent lot was only $--.-- for -- hours. All staff at hotel and resterant were great. We will go back.

The fact that the Radisson staff dealt professionally with a full house of such diverse clientele and did so with a smile says a lot about this hotel. Every staffer I encountered, from the valet to the front desk to the waiter to the housekeeper, was very pleasant and seemed to really care that every guest had an enjoyable stay. Requests for extra towels or retrieval of my car from valet were met promptly and with courtesy that one might not expect from a highly trafficked airport hotel. Check-in and check-out were smooth and painless.
My hotel room faced the south runway, and at first, I was concerned about airplane noise, but noise wasn't a problem at all -- I heard NO airplanes at all! The room was very comfortable and well-appointed. My roomie and I enjoyed the free wi-fi and the availability of an in-room refrigerator.
The only drawback was the bed, which was one of those Sleep Number outfits. I'd never slept on one, and after two nights of fiddling with settings, I'm not in a hurry to sleep in one again. The bed seemed very squishy, even on a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""firm"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" setting. I enjoyed my weekend at the Radisson and would have no qualms about returning. The staff there is really great, and they deserve kudos.

The Westin is a very good hotel as you'd probably expect with this brand and price. We were able to upgrade to a junior suite for a small fee - well worth negotiating when you check in. Our room was extremely spacious with wonderful views over Boston. It has a good location close to many shops, bars and restaurants. It's about a -- minute walk - - minute cab ride into downtown Boston - also about a -- minute walk back from Fenway when we couldn't get a cab. Noise from next door room easy to hear. Breakfast OK. Valet service OK. TV and bed OK. Lobby attractive. Definitely not worth the money. Not the place to stay if you want a comfortable, inviting room, with a place to relax and enjoy a vacation or down time during a business trip.

Just returned from a - night stay at this fabulous hotel. Was quite apprehensive after reading what I would call, some unjust negative comments. Reception and concierge service couldn't have been more helpful. Rooms were spacious and bathroom was adequate enough for a hotel room, can't believe some people complained about the sizes unless they spend all day in a room!! The rooms were cleaned daily and towels changed and left spotless. Every employee was friendly and that's why I entitled it 'full of smiles'. You can't get a more centrally suited hotel which was great for me as I'm recovering from a broken leg. We used a lot of taxis between - of us and it was very cheap, the drivers are extremely friendly and informative. Boston is a beautiful friendly, clean city and seemed very safe too. Thank you Park Plaza for a wonderful stay absolutely no complaints :-)

For $--- a night, we got full breakfast and dinner each day. Fitness room is small but had no problems getting time there. Room was excellent plenty of space and comfortable. Staff was super. Highly recommend!

Check in went very smoothly and we were assigned a nice room on the --st floor with a great view of the city. Bed was very comfortable as Westin beds usually are. Room was large and easily accommodated us.
We were attending a hockey tournament and were not showering in the room somedays so we weren't using the towels. The room attendant kept bringing more towels and by the end of our stay we had a stack of - clean towels on the counter. I just thought it was a bit funny. We walked to many of the tourist and shopping spots as well as Fenway Park. - Subway stops are steps away from the hotel and we had no problem getting around. We didn't eat in the hotel and can't comment on the restaurants or bar.

I've stayed at the Hotel Commonwealth the past two years for the Boston Marathon. It's a wonderful hotel and a great value. The rooms are beautiful, especially the Commonwealth suites. The staff is uniformly gracious, friendly, and helpful. This past stay, the doorman went way beyond the call of duty to help me retrieve my cell phone after I inadvertently left it in a cab.
The location is mixed. It's literally on top of a T stop, which is super convenient. There's also a Dunkin Donuts right next door, which is great if you're a caffeine junky. It's just a couple blocks to the Charles, very nice for a run or stroll. You can walk to Newberry Street, the Convention Center, and Copley, but those are all a solid -- minutes plus. Kenmore Square is not that appealing, and the restaurant selection is limited. It's also a pain having Fenway right there (unless you're going to the game) because it's kind of a zoo before and after the games.
The hotel restaurant (Eastern Standard) is a disappointment. The menu features lots of heavy food which in my experience is not particularly well executed. I've had consistent problems with the service at breakfast.
Nonetheless, I love this place, and will be back for Boston ----.

I needed a hotel room the night movers cleared out my apartment in Cleveland Park, north of the National Zoo. The Days Inn is only one Metro stop away, and is really the only option, short of bed and breakfasts, in that neighborhood... and a good optioin too. There are restaurants and stores right across Connecticut Ave., or down the street. I will definitely stay there again if I need to return to DC.

Stayed at the Four Seasons during the past weekend. We opted to upgrade to a suite and we were given a really nice room overlooking the park. However, upon leaving the room at night for a walk, we noticed that the door was easily opened if you pushed on the door (no key required). We called down to the front desk, they apologized, and a bellman QUICKLY came up to the room to move our luggage to a new room. Overall, would certainly stay here again in the future.

The motel was nice, you could tell it had been recently renovated. The room furnishings looked fairly new, and the plasma TV was nice. The staff was friendly. The rates are very reasonable, I snagged a great deal on it at Travelocity.
My only beef was the location. We planned to do a lot of stuff downtown, so we ended up doing a lot of driving. I should have planned better.
Also, it's not in the nicest neighborhood. We didn't have any incidents though, and it does have a gated parking lot.

The cleaning staff was exellent as well as the wait staff when we had our meals. I like the access that the hotel gives you to the Trolley so that you can go down to Manhattan Beach. Also, the Los Angeles by Night tour was awesome!!!!

I only used the airport-parking service, but from the moment I booked the reservation, through Steve's setting me up with my parking space to the shuttle returning me to my car, this is a full-service class act and an unbelievable value! Thanks for offering this service!

Washington Hilton is perfect for anyone visiting Washington for the first time. The hotel is in a fantastic location with restuarants roundabout for breakfast and meals. The hotel itself is fantastic especially the beds and pillows, we would love to know the make of the beds and pillows which are in the hotel as we did not have one bad night sleep or wake up with any pains after all the walking that we were doing between sightseeing and also on the day of the earthquake we had to walk from Union Station to the Hotel. The hotel should be compliemented on all their services which they provide, especially the cleanliness of all the areas within the hotel. Tour bus tickets can be bought in the hotel and stops right outside the hotel which is even better. We would recommend this hotel for anyone visiting Washington and the Metro is not to far away for anyone not wanting the tour bus but this is a perfect way to see Washington.

I stayed at the Parc -- on two occasions in October for two nights each time. Each room I had was spotlessly clean and furnished to a high standard. On my request I had a smoking room so I was on the -th floor. I obtained my room through Priceline but nevertheless my request for a corner room was granted on my first stay. I preferred to leave the window vents partially open but the noise in the street below after dark funnelled up into the room as my room overlooked Mason Street. The loudness of sirens was disconcerting but it was the shouting and arguments I had most difficulty with. I didn't want to use the earplugs provided as I was worried I wouldn't wake at - AM but it only became quiet outside around - AM. I'm sure it would make a difference according to the level and location of room allocated so I would suggest requesting a room higher up and away from Mason Street. The location of the hotel can't be beaten for access to BART from the airport as the Powell St station is just a few minutes walk away. Any hotel in this location is going to be subject to noise and I was perhaps more sensitive to it being somewhat jet lagged after a -- hour journey when I first arrived.

This hotel was great for a number of reasons. One of the first things we noticed was the friendliness of the staff. Everyone was so helpful. Because we arrived early in the morning our room was not ready, however, they called us on our cell phone as soon as it was available. They were very helpful with restaurant suggestions. Great staff! Perfect location-right by Central Park; subway across the street; Starbucks and Dunkin Donuts just around the corner; -- hour pharmacy at the corner; great breakfast spot just up the street. Shower was great and room was small, but clean. We didn't spend a lot of time there anyway so it didn't matter. Only complaint was that they didn't offer shower caps in the bathroom. Price was very reasonable compared to other N.Y. hotels.

We stayed at this hotel for - nights in April while attending a convention. The hotel is very nice with a beautify lobby. Rooms are small yet well appointed. Rooms and bathrooms were very clean and came complete with a refridgerator and coffee. Room service was very prompt with good food and reasonable prices. This is a very good choice if you need a place close to Pepsi Center or Convention Center. I would guess that it would serve you well also if you are going to Coors or Mile High. The room was updated and nicer than I would expect for this price ($--). The hotel is also pet-friendly, which is a must for me and my two dogs. The hotel offers some kind of shuttle service, but the weather was nice and I walked the -.- miles to downtown and the Convention Center. Just got back from seeing the -th of July fireworks in the Baltimore harbor and we loved our stay at the Four Seasons. We used to go to the Marriott Waterfront, but this property is new and clearly excels over the Marriott. (You pay for the difference and for us it was well worth it.) On a whim we decided that very day to go and were able to reserve a harbor view room…which is unheard of at the Marriott. (Perhaps because they opened in November and people don’t know about the Four Seasons.) The room was well appointed with a huge bathroom. The bed was very comfortable and perhaps no-one was above us, but this was the quietest hotel we’ve ever stayed in. We couldn’t hear the usual doors slamming. The design, engineering, and execution are standards every hotel should strive for. (Although it’s kinda a challenge to figure out how the faucets worked). For Independence Day they had an amazing party with a great band, slow roast whole pig, hot dogs, clams, oysters and lots of other great food for - hours for $-- per person, a great value. Buffets can be spotty at best, but their buffet was top notch, hot, and fresh and the staff pampered you, but in a laid back Maryland way—like a high-end picnic. Then for the fireworks we went up to the -th floor endless pool and grabbed - chaise lounges and had a front row seat to the Baltimore fireworks. The staff was all wonderful and seemed genuinely happy to be there. They also gave us a late check-out, which we really appreciated. It may have been our best -th celebration ever and would recommend the Four Seasons Baltimore to any traveler. Please note: the harbor view room lets you see the smaller fireworks in the inner harbor, but not the larger display more in the marina area. But the pool area and the area outside the restaurant area provides a great view of both displays.

I originally booked at this hotel because I was trying to save money. Well we all have heard horror stories about """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""you get what you pay for"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", not the case at Budgetel. For the low cost I paid, I had low expectations of what was going to be my hotel experience. The staff at the hotel were very friendly. Any questions I had about the hotel or surrounding area, they answered right away. Once I got to my room, I was suprised, it was spacious and clean WITH NO BUGS!!! How awesome is that! I got a good nites rest with no interruptions. No loud hotel guest, no bad kids running wild. I rested very well on my bed and found it to be comfortable. The room had the same kind of amenities you can find at any other costly hostly (tv, desk table, chair, cushion chair, ect) The only negative I found is that no iron or ironing board came with room. Lucky for me I traveled with an iron and just used the bed to straighten my clothes. The hotel location was right off the hwy, so it was convenient to moving around. No cars appeared to had been vandilized so that was comforting. Overall I found my stay well worth the money and would return.

We stayed at the Lowes this past weekend because my boyfriend had a medical conference there. The hotel itself is situated on Market, centrally located to Walnut street shopping, Chinatown, and Rittenhouse square. There are a lot of friendly staff members and bellmen around to assist you, and the lobby has some convenient amenities such as a free terminal for web check-in that prints out your boarding passes on your day of departure. Also, there is a nice table set up with complementary lemonade. The rooms are modern with Kreug coffee makers, and the bed was comfortable. Those are the good things. Now for the bad. 
Without asking us, the reservation assistant put us in a smoking room that smelled very damp and smoky. We went back to the front desk and requested another room without incident. Our new room was a nice corner unit overlooking Market street. The shower fixture was leaking badly and sprayed water all over the floor when we used it. We didn't want to go back to complain so we just dealt with it but it required mopping up the floor after every shower. 
The closet is very small, we couldn't put either of our carryon bags in there because the floorspace was too narrow (it's literally - foot deep). So, we had to put our bags near the front door and step around them. They do not put hair dryers in the rooms, you have to request one to be delivered to the room. 
The elevators in the hotel are extremely slow. We waited -- minutes for one to come on Saturday morning and several times I just took the stairs between floors instead of waiting. Everytime I used the elevator I could overhear people in it complaining about the long wait times.
I went to the business center to check my email and the credit card scanners were not working so I asked the woman working there if the system was down and she laughed at me and said the system was working fine. She didn't get up to assist me and seemed very disinterested in doing her job.
We wanted to go exploring after the seminars finished, so we exited the hotel. If you go to the right, you're immediately in a bad neighborhood. There were seedy looking people walking up and down the streets, and I did not feel safe. If you go to the left, you are headed to Rittenhouse and the museum area which is ok but honestly, the location of it is such that you're better off staying in Rittenhouse and just cabbing it back to Lowes if you have meetings there because it really isn't in a safe location. If you plan to dine out anywhere and are dressed up you will be cabbing it everywhere, as opposed to just being able to walk.
Overall, the stay was average, but if I had to do it again I would most definitely not pick this hotel. You are better off staying at any hotel in Rittenhouse square, where you can safely walk to Walnut and Liberty Mall shops.

Cops we're in parking lot when we pulled in. Not sure if we're in a bad neighborhood or not but at least the cops will show up if you have to call. Room smells kinda funny like musty covered up fragrant carpet powder. Overall good value for price.

New York was our third destination on our American honeymoon and after staying at - amazing - star hotels we knew that the New Yorker Hotel would be just a place to sleep , how wrong. After a long wait to get through customs at JFK we checked in at --.--pm and with a smile I asked for a room with a good view and a bit of space.Mohammed on reception gave us a suite on the --th floor with a seperate lounge,kitchen area and an amazing view of the Empire State so we were really impressed and pleased , on the way out we tipped Mohammed as he didnt have to upgrade us but genuinely seemed happy to do so.The staff at the hotel are really helpful ,we've been to New York before so wanted to do new things.The conceirge recommended a bike ride which we did.We cycled along the Hudson over the Manhatten and Brooklyn bridges through the financial district and up to Central park.Can honestly say this was the best day , saw amazing sights, stubbled across a film set, rode alongside taxi's and had a lock so could chain up anywhere for drinks etc. We also took in a comedy show at the Comedy Lounge and although you have to spend a minimum on drinks we had a really good night.We used the subway to get to and from the airport and although I wouldn't use if I was on my own it was very cheap and convienient.New York is still a fab place to visit but is more expensive than I remember so on a couple of occasions we ate slices of pizza for lunch rather than using an expensive sit down deli.The Tick Tock diner is good value though and they make the best milkshakes.Overall couldn't fault the hotel , it was better than expected just ask for a nice room and if like us you could get lucky, also take more money than you think you need.Will definately return to the New Yorker.

I was very disappointed with my stay at the Westin. To start, the hallway was Very dark and the carpet was torn in a couple of places. The room was in a state of disrepair and it was dark. Let me preface by saying I don't have a princess bone in my body so consider that when reading my recommendations as I don't go on vacation to complain about the small stuff, but I will try to be reasonable :-) . 
We flew into the Sea-Tac airport to attend a concert at the White River Amphitheatre in Auburn, WA. Well, If you are looking for a bathroom and a bed near the Theatre District and the Boston Common, this is the place. The hotel is just huge, full of restaurants and other places to spend money. Very charming boutique hotel. well located, the staff is always there for you, whenever and whatever you need. rooms are spacious and with nice balcony.Very close to good restaurants, by the water and close to the market.

THis is suppose to be a Quality inn., but quality is not what we received. We arrived for a wedding party and this was the location that was suggested. Overall, this all-suite hotel is a very good value for the money.

The Sheraton Gateway LAX has been our choice for years when having to overnight at LAX. We tried somewhere else last year and were disappointed so we went back to the Sheraton this year. My family & I come all the way from Norway. We stayed at the BGH because of great reviews we have read. The rooms were great, a little bit outdated but nice! I must admit, reading the reviews on tripadvisor, I was a litte worried about our stay at the Watermark from August ---. After staying there, I realized that people should not go by a lot of previous reviews - because most of the problems have been addressed. Okay, let's begin.
The Property
One word - excellent. The property is small and quaint, the interiors are beautiul, and there is nothing else like it in San Antonio.
Location
The location is phenominal - Right at the beginning of the main area of the riverwalk. Here's what people have to understand - The Riverwalk is a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""U"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". All the shopping, bars, restaraunts etc. are on the Northern half of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""U."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" So even though the Westin, for example, is just down the street from the Watermark - it isn't by all the action. If you want to be able to walk out of your door and be in the action - the only other places you can stay are the Hyatt, La Mansion, or Drury Inn & Suites. None of these properties even compare to the Watermark - I have visited all of them. All except La Mansion (a lot older) were built right before the World's Fair in the Late '--s...therefore are not that great. The Drury is just...well...your average Drury, The Hyatt is old and outdated (Which is why they are constructing a brand new hotel near the alamodome) and the La Mansion is VERY old, VERY outdated has a very bad smell, and is extremely confusing to navigate. If you want to be near the Rivercenter Mall (a dump, by the way) and the convention center - check out the Marriot Riverwalk or Marriot Rivercenter. Neither are anything special - Just your average Marriot. If you want to be somewhat isolated - check out the Hilton Palacio del Rio (Same as the Hyatt), The Westin (Nice, bad location) Or the Hotel Contessa. If you want to be completely isolated - check out the Crowne Plaza. 
Okay, sorry folks - back to the Watermark.
Guest Rooms
Very well done. Spacious, great colors, comfortable beds, quiet (contrary to previous reviews) , and an excellent bathroom. I had a city view room, which looked out onto a brick wall - but that didn't really bother me. The Riverwalk view rooms are $--- more per night - and are a rip off. There is the riverwalk, then a street. The hotel is on the side of that street oposite the riverwalk itself. So a riverwalk view looks out onto a street that is next to the riverwalk. Not worth $----night.
-th floor Rooftop Pool & Fitness Center
The fitness center is state of the art. All the latest machines with indiviual flat screen TVs. Okay so the pool. The first day I went it was great - all the lounge chairs had towels on them, were made up perfectly, the pool was clean, and I had it all to myself. The second day I went, there was trash and towels thrown all over - (I called the front desk and they sent someone up to clean things right away) but the pool was still clean and I had it all to myself. If I have one complaint about the Watermark - it's the Third Day. I went up to the pool about - o'clock. The chairs were made up decently and the pool was clean, but there were kids. --- Very young children running around, screaming, splashing, yelling and spilling drinks. This hotel is marketed to Adults - and adults shouldn't go up to the pool expecitng a romantic evening and find young kids running around. The hotel should send the kids over to the La Mansion pool - more of a family friendly atmopshere.
Dining
The Rooftop Cafe was decent, but the hotel should have the person on staff there waiting on people at the pool since it's right next door. I didn't eat at the hotels more formal restauraunt Pesce - there are way to many other great options on the Riverwalk to eat overpriced hotel food. Try Acenar, Mi Tierra, Rit'as Ice House, Paesanos, and the Hard Rock Cafe.
Security
The Keycard elevator access was a nice feature. My only complaint was that the door at riverwalk level was always unlocked - it should require a keycard based on the way people behave on the riverwalk. There is a lot of drinking going on. 
Service
Service was excellent for the most part. Housekeeping always made up the room, and turndown service was on time. The front desk staff was very friendly and the bellhops always opened the doors. I was a little unimpressed when I asked the concierge about good dessert - and she led me to a dump of a candy shop in the bottom of the Hyatt - but she was helpful for the most part. My only complaint was when I called the front desk to request pillows, bottled water, etc. they were a little slow, but oh well.
The Spa
Excellent treatments, very well designed and massive.
A few final notes - 
The Internet was high priced, and contrary to what I was told, there was no high speed on the internet on the roof, in the lobby, or at Pesca. Keep in mind the state, county, and city taxes hit you big time. A room that was $--- a night ended up being $--- a night. 
Overall, I would deffinately call this a - star hotel. Obviously they have fixed everything that people have complained about, and the service is excellent. You can't beat the hotel or the location. I will be back for sure.

We stayed at the Catamaran Resort July ----. It's location is ideal if you want to be walking distance to Beach, Bay & Restaurants. Nice Pool area, fitness room just ok. Property is in need of some maintanence and updating, especially considering the price. Wouldn't stay again unless I could be assured an updated room. Restaurant had good food and service, but pricey.

We just spent two nights at the Inner Harbor and the Hyatt's location is very good. You can walk almost anywhere you wish to visit and the water taxi stand is just a short walk away.
Our room was large and clean, but it was not anything special. They do have self-parking at an adjacent garage, which is a real plus. All the little amenities were there, but, again, you are paying for the location.

This was my first time staying at this property. I was impressed with the home like feel.

We booked this hotel for - nights in May as part of our honeymoon based on the review on Expedia, touting it as a boutique hotel.
It definately doesn't warrant the title of boutique, however the room was pleasant and clean and the location was good - especially if you're arriving from the Back Bay Train Station.

Returned today from our second stay at the St. Regis in San Francisco. We will return again one day. We enjoyed one evening in a suite this time. A lower floor so the view was nothing to rave about. The room was excellent though, and the bed and linen first class. Very comfortable. The hotel has a spa which was well appointed. I've been to nicer spas though. My masseuse had garlic breath, and that was no good! We went for a taxi to go out for dinner and the doorman offered the hotel's own car. That was nice and fun. The room service in the hotel was prompt and excellent. The hotel's only drawback, if there is one, is the hotel's location. It is not in Union Square, as some other posters have suggested, it is a few blocks away. I prefer a hotel on nob hill. I prefer an older hotel with character too, and the St. Regis is new and very modern. It lacks character. The room was ultra masculine too. Best part: the free shuttle ride to and from the ball game at Coors Field. Courteous staff. Excellent breakfast. Small but clean room.

We got this hotel on priceline for a fair rate for three nights. Were put in a smoking room on the first night and it was incredibly smokey as soon as I stepped off the elevator. Our clothes smelled like smoke for a couple of days. Management moved us to a non-smoking room as soon as it opened up with no hassle. This hotel is is a good location, close to Union Square,shopping, BART and cable cars.
The kicker for us was after we checked out, the doorman arranged a ride for us to the airport. A few blocks into our ride, we were pulled over by the police because the driver made an illegal turn. We were told that there has been a number of issues with town car drivers robbing customers or worse. I'm not usually a fear monger but I do not trust a hotel who's staff is not concerned about their guests safety, even after they've paid the bill.

My partner and I go to one Red Sox game a year - tickets are expensive! We have stayed at the Hotel Commonwealth for the last six years. The buzz on the street pre-game is great fun. Our typical stay includes a late lunch-early dinner at Eastern Standard. I'll write a separate review for that. Anyone going to a Sox game or visiting a BU student or shopping on Newbury Street (which is totally inaccessible) should stay here.

We had a fantastic time at the resort. They upgraded us to a Casita without our asking, which was a great start to the stay. Place was clean, comfortable and big. Pool-water park was a huge hit for the family. We would certainly return to this resort.

My first impression upon entering the lobby was someone should shampoo this dirty carpet. The room was clean and nice once I was able to get the malfunctioning lock to open. (it took - to - passes of the key card to open the door every time I entered the room.) There was only a shower in the bathroom. This would have been fine if there was decent water pressure in the shower. The highlight of my stay was when I ask for towels at the front desk upon returning for dinner. I had one towel and two people in my room. The towels were brought to the room promptly. At -- pm that night the front desk called the room and woke me up to ask me if the towels has arrived! The Holiday Inn Express was a very nice hotel, with GREAT rooms, friendly staff and great location. The breakfast which is included each morning is very nice, and more than just juice and pastries. The staff is VERY friendly and go out of their way to make you feel welcome. The location of the hotel is in walking distance to just about everything or a short cab ride away. I would recommend this hotel for sure.

I had business in New York City on the Friday leading into the Memorial day weekend. I thought it would be an excellent opportunity for a quick family excursion. Typically, I would have booked this hotel through my Amex Platinum Card Fine Resorts and Hotel program, but I found a much better value by calling the Peninsula's reservation desk. 
The reservationist arranged our accommodations, king with roll-away-bed at 'x' cost per night for a - night stay. Ultimately, they tried to run a scam on us and up sell us unknowingly. Because I planned to meet my family later in the evening after my business meeting, I arranged with the receptionist for my husband and daughter to check in prior to my arrival. I thought the room was lovely, facing -th avenue, with windows that actually opened. While the decor was a little dated, we were comfortable, in a great location, and the room was fresh. Mind you, this is not the Peninsula Beverly Hill's which is one of the most perfect hotel experiences that we have ever had. As some of the reviews have suggested and I should have paid attention to, this is like the budget version of a true Peninsula.
I digress, let me cut to the chase. On check out, there were problems with our billing that I took issue with. The bill was corrected, but a month later, Peninsula NY recharged the expenses to my credit card. I called them to challenge the charges and honestly, they put what sounded like a trainee on the phone who spoke to me in the most condescending manner. When I told him that I would hand the matter over to Amex and tried to end the contact (because honestly I was concerned that I was dealing with someone unstable), he tried to call me again a couple of times. I immediately phoned Amex and the situation was 
handled. I have never had such an insulting experience in all of my days and this was the Peninsula, or so I thought! I should have paid closer attention to all those trip advisor reports that were implicit of something shady going on at that place cause folks, it's true! Bright spots: food was delicious, room adequate value (until they tried to rip me off).

Sharpie graffiti on walls, unsanitary!!! Wouldn't take my worst enemy to stay here. Manager ? Owner refused to refund my money went I went back to the office after I saw what the rooms looked like. You get what you pay for that's for sure!!!!

This motel is perfect for discovering LA, close to the freeway and walking distance from the nearest subway. This motel was one of the cleanest I've visited in a wile. Great relax area in the middle with a pool and jaccuzi. Next time I'm in LA, this will be the place I stay in

We booked this hotel through Sea World vacations and it was a huge mistake! Normally you expect a quality stay with a Marriott hotel brand, but this was worse than staying at a motel!
We were booked in a first floor room that had a cricket infestation problem. As a matter of fact the entire first floor hallway is infested with crickets! Don't let the outside of this hotel fool you... the inside is very nice! There is a bar and a resturant on site, though I did not use them, they looked nice and modern. We loved our stay here over the July - holiday. The room was great, we also enjoyed the breakfast each morning and wine and cheese in the afternoon. We also loved Jeffery.

Our room didn't have air-conditioning, just a ceiling fan, and a portable rotary fan. Facing the small courtyard, there is not really a breeze helping with the stuffiness. The room and bathroom were clean. The kitchenette is great for people who don't mind going around the corner to buy groceries at the supermarket, especially since the room comes without breakfast. The rooftop view is fantastic. Nothing beats a coffee from Starbucks (shares the building with the hotel), and then relaxing in a lounge chair on the rooftop to watch the sunset.

The first room in which they put me was between a service room and the elevators. It had no bathtub, and there was a wind tunnel-machinery noise that was constant. I had asked for a quiet room, as even they admitted. They did not tell me until the next day that they had not reviewed my preferences before holding rooms and that this had been the last room available. Had they done so, I would have moved to another hotel.

After reading numerous poor reviews of this hotel, I decided to take a chance and stay here with my family for the weekend. The deal I got for a - night stay through washington.org was just too good to pass up ($-- Friday, $-- Saturday, $--- Sunday).
While there were blemishes, this had to be one of the best deals ever for a Washington trip! The hotel lobby is very nice and well-kept. The clerk went out of her way to change our room to one that did not have pets (note: the --th floor is the pet floor). The room was clean and attractive, and our room overlooked the Washington Monument. The shower worked great. The hotel restaurant is nice. The hotel is on top of a metro station; it has a metro bus stop, a Circulator bus stop, and a stop for the Open Air Sightseeing bus. However, the best part of the hotel is the location: --- blocks from the Smithsonian. 
On the negative side, the hotel lobby is hard to find coming off the highway. It is set in the middle of a mass of generic office buildings. The bathroom had a slight leak that we were able to take care of with a towel. All-in-all, our positives far outweighed the negatives. This was well worth the money!

This was our last stop before travelling back . When I organised this - weeks California-Nevada roundtrip we thought it would be a nice idea to rest the - last nights in San Diego before driving back to L.A. and fly back to Europe.
We chose this city hotel on purpose as we like to be central because of the restaurants, shopping etc … but we definitely expected more for this hotel.
I read in a few reviews here that the rooms were very small and decided to book - suites as I found a very good deal on Expedia. Having said that I can confirm indeed that the normal rooms are extremely small as I saw them when walking through the hotel.
Our Suites were very cosy and the design was ok but that’s it, here is a summary of our stay
Positive:

- full non smoking hotel
- design of the rooms (pleasant)
- rooms well cleaned
- not far from a big mall
- nice bar & restaurant at the hotel (Currant American Brasserie), with nice waiters
Negative:

You can hear the police and ambulance sirens as if you were sitting in it (They should offer free Quies ear plugs as they do in some hotels is San Francisco). Because of this we were so tired in the morning and were happy to leave the room as you can imagine
- if you arrive on a Sunday afternoon, you better be patient, because the only alternative they offer you in case of a problem is ‘We can change your room’
- very bad internet connections and no WIFI in the rooms but like in the --’s with wire only .When I arrived in my room, I could not access it and called the reception and of course as it was a Sunday evening they could just offer to move rooms and try it again or wait for the day after when an IT person is there). I called again and they answered that it was because I had a MAC, so they gave me a printout with explanation how to change setting in my computer in order to access the internet. After a few hours, I gave up …) the day after I tried again and the line was so low, so slow, it was terrible. I travel a lot around the world but never experience this. Normally as soon as you are in a room (MAC or PC) it should connect straight away but not here and they ask USD --,- a night for this service, sorry this is not normal !! They offered me to use the free lobby Wifi internet but as I had to use my laptop for confidential material (work), this was not possible. In this case, sorry but internet in the room should be free of charge!
- the laptop cable is so short that I had troubles to look at the screen the way I wanted
- if you take a suite, there is only a phone in the sitting area and not next to the bed (what is the logic of this??) so that it the telephone rings anytime and you are in bed, you have to run to the phone
- cleaning is sometimes done very late in the afternoon (--- PM)
I have learned one thing about this stay: if travelling to the U.S. from Europe I would recommend to book hotels though www.expedia.com instead of any of their European websites because if you have a problem like we did when trying the change hotel, due to the time difference it was unfeasible as they need to contact the U.S. Expedia first, etc …. And it is cheaper !!! it is often the same price between the European and U.S. website.
This is definitely not a business hotel and also not a pleasant hotel if you like to sleep at night. People that are sensitive to noisy (sirens, ventilation, next door room doors) DO NOT STAY HERE and recommend to take an hotel at Coronado (superb beach) or La Jolla (as second choice), it is ----- minutes drive if you want to come for dinner in town. I would never recommend this hotel to anyone. STAY AWAY OF THIS HOTEL, especially for long term stay !!!

-) Hotel pool water is VERY cool. Almost unbearable.
-) One of the restaurants is """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sushi-teq"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". If you like japanese food, avoid it. If you want to try japanese food, avoid it. It's not sushi, I was really disappointed.

The staff were nice, and I liked them, but I had to perpetually go back to the front counter to get things sorted out.

The first bill they gave me made little sense, and I had to get to print it again in order to get my receipts reimbursed by my company. They got the Sheraton hotel points mixed up and I had to go back about that too.

Overall this was the perfect hiatus for us...my only complaint was that we didn't stay long enough!

We travelled Friday November -- to Monday December -, we booked the hotel through Hotwire and were looking for a hotel in Times square. Love the service here!! We started staying here for the indoor pool for our young daughter and have continued to stay. The staff recognizes us every time we arrive and are like familia!! The fact that Century -- is located right next door is a definite plus! My hubbie likes to shop! I would not stay anywhere else!

I will start with the ONLY negative I have about this hotel: the elevators are slow and are often full when they stop on your floor. That's it.
