My previous lodging arrangements fell through last minute so I was forced to take the only hotel with only - room left, this one, and a king suite + a sleeper sofa... which wouldn't have been that bad except I'm only one person.
First off there is never any parking in Baltimore. Second, there is REALLY no parking during Otakon. I had the valet park my car, which was wonderful so I didn't drive around looking for parking that doesn't exist. The valets and the bellhops were very friendly and kind. I'm sad to say I can't say that for the front desk staff. I was ignored most of the time, and when I wasn't being ignored they were being snippy with me. Maybe it was because I was in my Otakon costume or something, but that shouldn't matter, my money is as green as the next guest's. Just for a little experiment I'd like to go back there one day dressed in my work suit and see how differently they treat me. I had my accounts compromised - weeks earlier, as such, my bank shut my cards off while the fraud investigation is going on. They are supposed to give me new card numbers, but boy did they pick the most horrible day to shut the old ones off. I used an old one the day before, and it worked, so I wasn't sure exactly when they were going to be turned off. Well, when I tried to check into my hotel, the people at the front desk were really rude about how the card was denied. Well, duh, it was turned off, I knew it was going to happen, I just didn't know when. So there was this whole fuss how they needed another card in case of incidental damages or something like that. The room was already paid for online, while my card still worked... but they wanted another one! So I had to call my mother up and have her fax over copies of HER credit card. It was a big hassle over nothing! The room was already paid for, I was all by myself, all the cash I had was for the convention. They were trying to get me to pay $--- in cash to them for the room I already paid for online! If you think a single, white female roams around in Baltimore with $--- in cash in her pockets you should think again. Though the city was very crowded, even at night, because of the convention. It was a lot safer than normal with so many people at all hours. I did not get hassled by anyone while I was walking back to this hotel in the middle of the night. For all the other women traveling alone out there... be aware of your surroundings all the time know how many people are around you at all times and if you notice any unusual activity (people who are parked next to your car's driver's side and not getting out of their car immediately), stick to the main roads that have street lamps, don't talk to anyone you don't have to, don't stop walking for any reason, don't give money to the beggars sleeping on the benches near the fountain, stay away from people who are talking to themselves, and don't go into any parking garages without an escort. Valet service can save your life...
When I got back to the room, I noticed there was a bachelorette party in the room across the hall... they had taped a sign up on the door. They weren't that noisy, I was surprised. I was so tired I took a shower and fell asleep immediately. The bathroom was ok. The tub needed to be recaulked, though, but atleast it was clean. There was a tiny kitchenette in my room also, which was nice. They gave me free water bottles, and free coffee packets. I wish they would've given me more creamer and sugar though. I thought for sure I'd get a continental breakfast the next morning. Well, they do serve breakfast, but it's not for free, which defeats the purpose of a continental breakfast in my opinion. I think for $--- for one night I should've atleast gotten a muffin or something. But whatever, I bought some peanut butter crackers the day before from a gas station. I went down to see if they would hold my bags for me for the day, dressed normally in jeans and a t-shirt, it was kind of cute how they didn't ignore or act rude to me that day. 
In short, if I was to do it all over again, I'd mix the valet and bellhop service with the Days Inn right in front of the convention center. Maybe then I'd get my free breakfast...

Great location, lots of nice restaurants nearby and close toTimes Square. This hotel is quite 'rough around the edges' however. We thought with a name like skyline we would see some it, we had a brick wall as a view. Have average expectations of the hotel and you will not be disappointed.

This is the best --star hotel I've stayed at in SFO. I've stayed at many marginal --stars recently so my expectations were low.

And of course you can't beat the weather there and the mountain views!

First, the good things: this hotelnis located in a very nice neighborhood in walking distance to Dupont Circle, the subway and many restaurants. The staff was very helpful. There is a clean laundry, good wifi in the rooms and laptop room safes.
However, the room we had was not nearly as good loooking asbthe rooms displayed on the website, but much darker jd not very modern. The kitchen was not very clean, there was a lot ofbdirt between the appliances on the floor. The bathroom could also have been cleaned more throroughly, the bed and linen was clean, however. A major downside tonournroom wasnthat we could hear every word spoken in the next room through the ventilation ... and unfortunatley for us this room was occupied by a group of teenagers. 
Inprobably could imagine to stay there again, but I would also explore oth options.

Overall it was an okay place to stay. The room was nice and looked like it had been recently renovated. We were just in town for one night for a wedding, and got a package that included breakfast and parking. It was the best price we could find at the time and we would feel comfortable staying here again. The staff was nice and friendly and we didn’t encounter any problems. Parking was easy in the structure right next to the hotel. 
Only thing was the breakfast, it was a typical buffet style and nothing special and not worth paying any extra money for.

Before booking our hotel I spent hours reading reviews on all of the travel websites. I had a hard time deciding at first because there were so many hotels. In the end I was so happy about the Hyatt Regency I decided to write a review in case it could help someone else. The hotel is located in probably one of the most strategic positions between Millennium Park and Michigan Ave. This was important for us because we were travelling with a toddler. We could take our child to Millennium Park to play(there is always something going on there) lucky for us there was a children’s festival during the whole time we were there. We could then go back to the hotel or just go directly to Michigan Ave for lunch or shopping. The hotel is so close to every type of public transportation: train, bus, water taxi etc. to take you to Shedd Aquarium, Wrigley Field, Lincoln Park Zoo, Navy Pier just to name a few places. We tried some of them and they were always clean and easy to use and if you don’t want to take public transportation there is always a taxi lined up in front of the hotel. The rooms in the hotel were a nice size and after their renovation you can see that everything has been updated. The hotel is big but there was always someone available to give you directions or to answer your questions or just to say good morning. I was very happy(especially after reading some of the reviews) that with all of the conventions going on, they were so well staffed to take care of everyone. We happened to meet the hotel Social Manager Jennifer and her co-worker Julia one day in the lobby and they sent us something to our room, which was very nice and unexpected. This just shows you how the hotel makes an effort to make their guests stay the best. Our favorite part of the stay though was having breakfast in the hotel every morning. All of the wait staff and hostesses were so nice and accommodating. There are too many people to name, but by the end of the trip we looked forward to seeing everyone and it always started our day off right. I can’t say enough good things about the hotel! The next time we are in Chicago we will stay there without a doubt!

We have stayed two times at this hotel. The location in fashionable and exciting Greenwich Village, between Fifth Avenue and Ave. of the Americas (Sixth Avenue) cannot be beat. You are three-four blocks from much of what is exciting in New York: Washington Square, shops-restaurants in Greenwich Village, the East Village, Chelsea, you name it. Close to Sixth Avenue and -th Avenue Subways. And quick walking distance to the Lexington Ave. line at --th.
Continental breakfast with fresh rolls, coffee, etc. That saved us $-- right there. Free Wifi service (slow sometimes but ample). Self-service elevator.
Tiny room with a bath down the hall, but with a window with a view of back patios of ritzy homes on --th St. Air Conditioned. Our only problem was being next to a room that serves as a kitchen. (Very handy if you want to store stuff in the fridge or use the stove to cook meals. One day some of the permanent residents used it as a meeting room, talking loudly on the phone or whatever. But we called management and they sent someone up within seconds to quiet them down...then no more problems. Very very quiet in the evening as most of the rooms face an inner courtyard.
We stupidly left a cellphone charger there after we checked out. A day later we called the hotel and they HAD it! Amazing. More amazing was that they sent it to us in the mail the next day and did not charge us for the postage or the trouble. Triple amazing. We feel guilty now we didn't tip the maid, but we put a do not disturb sign on the door for the two days we were there.
Stay there, but be sure and leave us a room when we want to stay.
Stayed at the Days Inn Downtown Los Angeles for one night to see a concert at Dodger Stadium. Clean room, friendly staff, would stay again

Our group stayed here at last year's convention. I was already warned that the place has no pool but shocked and disappointed to discover that my room had NO BATHTUB! It turns out that out of all the rooms at this hotel, only six of them are equipped with tubs and it had never occurred to me to ask if I could trade for one that did. The rooms were huge with fully equipped kitchens but that didn't mean anything to me. I suffered in excruciating pain from altitude sickness and had to fill two plastic garbage bins with hot water and Epsom salt to soothe my aching limbs. Those who were fortunate enough to have bathtubs in their rooms complained about lack of counter space. I would have gladly settled for less counter space in favor of a tub!

Stayed at the Hilton Times Square for - nights on the last week of our holdiay. We arrived quite late and the only room available was a smoking room (we are both non smokers), the receptionist advised that he would change us the next day into a non smoking room and had housekeeping freshen up our room until we were moved. The rooms were spacious and clean, although found it quite strange that the tea and coffee facilites were in the bathroom!! You are best to request a room on a high floor facing --nd street which has a great few of the broadway lights at night. the other side has a building site across the street. The hotel is in a great location, just a few steps from Broadway. The bellboys were great, really friendly and helpful. I would definately recommend this hotel to anyone visiting NY.

I will only be reiterating the other reviews on here, but like to get my review on here to help the hotel rating.
This hotel is great for the money you pay in Midtown. Its a fantastic location, Room was plenty big enough for - ladies...unitl the end of the trip when the shoppin bags started to take over a bit!!
Walking distance to everything you could need. Concierge to store your bags if needed and hotel staff more then helpful enough...Especially with finding a chinese not a korean take away at -am!!
The free breakfast is a bit ropey, but hey its free. We only went there once. It consisted of Rolls, bagels, doughnuts and - type danish pastry. then to go with these you had, phillidelphia or butter, then Tea coffe and Oj and a toaster. So very basic.
Defintiely recomend this for a cheap, clean great location hotel.

My friend comes into town from SF for work often and usually stays at The Orlando. On his last trip, I visited with him for the weekend and we played """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""tourist,"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" which was fun since the hotel is located right where everything is. We even walked across the street to a store to buy ice cream at midnight! The staff is so friendly and are always helpful. The valet guys were also helpful as we had two cars and were trying to figure out where to park the other one, etc. One day, I went to the pool area to sit outside and work on my laptop in the sun. Ahhhh..... just lovely! And, the beds are super comfortable too! I would highly recommend this property to anyone who needs to stay in LA but doesn't want to deal with a huge mega-property. It is so easy to get in-out of and I love that the whole building is wireless.

I was thankful to check in to this hotel after spending a night at the Fairfield Inn which was creepy. The bed was fantastic and the service was very warm from everyone we encountered. The room is spacious and attractive. I enjoyed the workout room and indoor pool. They also have a sauna. The buffet breakfast was very pretty good and a great value. I really felt at home at this location.

I recently stayed at the Flathotel and I have to say that for the price I paid there are FAR better hotels available. On the plus side the location is great, incredibly central and so many places are within walking distance. On the downside the rooms are incredibly tired (I am sure they looked swish i the ----'s when they were last decorated) and lack the basics (Mini barswitched on but completely empty??!!) As for the bar-restaurant, well let's put it this way - I ate out for breakfast, lunch and dinner! This hotel could be amazing but needs some serious revamping!

I took my wife here on the tail end of our honeymoon and was nothing less than impressed. The service was so helpful and friendly, the atmosphere was classy and beautiful, and the extras perfect. Our room was beautiful and wonderful after day in the city. Ricks Cafe always hit the spot and was a great escape from hectic time square. We loved our stay!

Stayed at this hotel on the final leg of our road trip through California and Nevada and was not disappointed. Booked two queen beds on executive floor and were allocated a room overlooking the pool area, large, clean with nice Evelyn and Crabtree bath products with complementary breakfast and appetisers after -.--pm and complementary fruit basket (in fact we received a second basket after - days stay). Nice pool, never too busy. 
Ate in the Sierra Cafe for the weekend buffet....fabulous if you like seafood and reasonable at $--.-- per person especially if you have large appetites. 
Very convenient for Universal Studios and Citywalk (for every type of meal). Did'nt bother with the hotel shuttle, the walk was about five minutes away over the pedestrian walkway and invariably we arrived there before the shuttle did. 
When there if it interests you try the Warner Bros VIP Tour.....great fun and a different experience from the Universal Studio Tour, you can get tickets from Warner Bros online. If you want to do the tour of the star homes thing, try Starline also online but we picked up tickets from a kiosk outside Mann's Chinese Theater, also great fun. 
All in all a typical Hilton experience and recommended.

The Silversmith hotel is in a wonderful old building right near millennium park in downtown Chicago. Even though it is right in the middle of tons of shopping and parks it is very quite in the hotel rooms. The room (king bed) was quite spacious and the bed was very comfortable. The hotel has free wifi in both the rooms and lobby, no issues with the number of devices you use. For me this is one of the most important features of a hotel and it worked at a high speed throughout my stay. As with almost every hotel in downtown Chicago the parking is a bit expensive ($---night for valet) but if you are going to stay at a hotel downtown with a car this is likely what you will be paying anyway. However, the room was very reasonably priced.

I was very impressed with this one-year old property. The Contessa is located on a quieter part of the Riverwalk, only minutes away from all the activity. The best way to describe this place is that it is trendy, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""boutique-y"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (I made that word up) without all the attitude you get at a place like the W. Decor is very nice - reminds me of a Ritz or Four Seasons. Whoever did the interior design must be amazing. Room was quite spacious and comfortable. Location was good as well - there's a Riverboat tour nearby as well as the charming La Villita arts village. We got a GREAT deal on Priceline for $----night for a weekend stay. However, I would be willing to pay up to $----night to stay here. Totally worth it.

The only real advantage this hotel offers is its location if you need to be close to the Capitol. The atmosphere is very busy, lots of convention people and the infrastructure a bit run down. The Regency Club is not up to the standard of Park Hyatts, i.e only non alcoholic beverages are for free, the breakfast ist very limited and the space quickly overcrowded.
I will definitively choose the Park Hyatt the next time I will be in Washington!

We stayed in this hotel on ---th street in manhatten. the room was tiny and the double bed was really small. there are no amenities in the hotel like a bar, or restaurant. the heating was either blasting or off. but its in a nce location and the staff were nice. its not as if you soend much time in the room anyway!!

I am a frequent traveler and I have been in alot of hotels in the country. The Doubletree Hotel in Detroit- Dearborn is a very secluded and relaxing hotel not just because of the location but because of the staff. The staff is always accomodating and is always willing to help you when needed. The atmosphere is always pleasureable and suitable to everyones needs. When I come into the hotel I am always greeted with hospitality by Charles, Scott, Megan, Jennifer, and others that I have met throughout the years of a very experienced visit. This is definitely one of the best hotels in the Detroit metro areas.....

A very pleasant couple of days at the Royal Palace. We had a spacious, double queen room with kitchenette. The spa bath was a surprise extra - as was the flat-screen TV. We had wheels (parking was free), but even if you don't have a vehicle, the hotel is conveniently placed in terms of public transport. There is a very good choice of eateries within easy walking distance, including breakfast options if the basic continental provided doesn't quite do it for you. The Wi-Fi worked well. Desk staff were always happy to assist with directions, etc. There can be a bit of street noise emanating from the side alley - but we had the window open to get the breeze and hey - this is Los Angeles! Overall, and considering the price, we were more than satisfied.

Having stayed at two other HK properties, we knew what to expect and were not disappointed. As usual all of the staff were very welcoming and all of the amentities offered make this a most pleasant place to stay. We booked The Library Hotel based on its location since it best served our needs this trip. Depending on the type you select, the rooms can be very small but we have learned that this seems to be the norm in NYC. Since we don't spend much time in the room, we don't consider this to be a big negative. Any time we go to NYC, I immediately check to see if one of their hotels is conveniently located to where we need to be. You should too. You'll be gald you did.

Fantastic hotel I was a bit put off before I went by reading all the negative reviews but we had the most amazing time there!
Safe homely atmosphere with no hassle for security as we were four females a little wary of how safe things are in the heart of the city but the staff put our minds at ease!
The bar was brill wee Francisco the bar man was a gem! And those gin and tonics were lethal!
Small rooms but spotless and cleaned every day...good job as we were a bit messy!
I lost my purse on the way from the hotel to the shuttle bus and the hotel e-mailed me to say they had found it intact with my money,cards, photographs etc and also I had left jewellry in my drawer in the room which I hadn't noticed was missing how's that for service!
I also recommend anyone travelling from UK to buy a $-- phone card as they last for around - hours.
After staying in The UN Millenium Plaza - star two years previous I would definately use this hotel again for service and location after all your only sleeping in the hotel and the rooms were clean!

I had a reservation done thru a travel agency to stay there for a couple of days due to hurricane Sandy leaving me without power. When I got that a very RUDE person at the front desk said, with no apologetic tone, that they didnt have my reservation (or many other that were in line) and that the hotel was all booked, to basically find another place to stay. Not only that, before I even made it to the front desk, another rude employee told me I couldnt bring my pet, a smallish SERVICE DOG. He said he needed to see proof that it was a service dog (which I have) but by law they CANT ask for this, specially if he is wearing his service dog vest. 
I understand it was en emergecny in the city but that doesnt grant that type of behavior. I will never stay on any property from them and I specifically asked Platinum Amex traver service to NEVER EVER work with them again.

The only thing good about this place is the location - easily accesible to Soho and Lower East Side. There is virtually no lobby, no good help in terms of conceirges or check-in and no place to park to unload your car. I booked my room through Quikbook. Thank goodness I had the print-out for my reservation because, without the print-out, they were going to charge me $--- (almost $--- more than what I paid). This place, I think, used to be a Howard Johnson's, and I still felt like I was staying in one. The electronic keys weren't working, the tv was out of service and there is no place to hang more than - articles of clothing in the room. The mustard-colored blanket on the bed looked soiled and gross. All in all, terrible, and I still can't believe I paid what I did for the hotel (even in NYC).

I was there for a conference. The staff could not of been nicer! Yolonda and Monica in banquet services made us feel like we were at - star resturant. Great job ladies! 
Hotel itself is a great location. Right near union square and chinatown. Fun place for a conference. Also, try the view bar at the top of the hotel. Amazing views!

I recently travelled with family (all adults) this was the perfect stay in every way, rooms ( adjoining) very clean beds very comfortable, made use of laundry facilities available. Breakfast was very good highly recommend the waffles. Pool area very nice, front staff were very helpfull. this hotel is perfectly located to accessing public transport. The trolley sevice is a short - minute walk from hotel, San Diego has a very good public transport service available, the front desk are able to provide info on how to get around, we found this extremly helpful. All the transport drivers are very friendly and will go out of their way to assist tourists.
Many excellent restaraunts with in a -- minute walk. Must try the Mexican food at one of the many restaurants in Old Town, there are many other types of food to choose from as well. All food is very well priced. 
I would definately stay at Old Town Inn again, I highly recommend this location.

I've never contributed to an online eval but felt so strongly about our experience at this hotel, that I was determined to do it now. This is the second time we've stayed at the Fairmont Washington, DC; the first time was over Christmas ----. This trip was during the Easter Weekend. When we travel, it includes my mother who is in a wheelchair and can get around via a walker in the hotel room, but needs some specific accommodation to make it easier for her to get in and out of bed and the bathroom on her own. Many hotels these days have those really high mattresses and really small bathrooms. We really have to watch for that. During our December trip we were in a wonderful suite that had two bedrooms attached, but alas, the beds were just a bit too high. We discovered that she could do well with the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""murphy bed"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that was in the parlor area. So when we made reservations for an Easter trip, we booked that suite again. But a week later, the hotel had to change that because of some guests that had extended their stay. With a groan, I contacted the manager, Keith Siebenaler. He and his staff were extremely accommodating to make it right for us in the suite that was available - to the point of exchanging the box spring on her bed so it was a couple inches lower! Considerations for the rate we were charged (it was adjusted down) were great of course, and made it all the better, but just the way we were treated both in the reservation changing process, the check in process and throughout the whole - day trip was superb. The food, whether in the restaurant, room service, or the special brunch in the Colonnade, was great. And we have very high standards! Mr Siebenaler even checked back with us to see if we'd made our brunch arrangements for Easter. When I told him we did, but couldn't get the time or place we wanted, he took it upon himself to get it fixed for us. There is no doubt that when you need something special that the Fairmont staff will do their utmost to make it happen for you. It's not the most inexpensive hotel you'll find, but they do have good packages often. And more importantly, the value is there. You know that whatever you're spending, it's worth it. We look forward to staying there again the next time our travels take us to DC.

The Dupont Hotel is in a great DC location, with easy access via the Metro and within walking distance to a variety of terrific places to eat and assorted city attractions. The hotel amenities are fully in accord with what you'd expect for the price range - in other words, it delivers value for your dollar. Above all, the staff are uniformly friendly, helpful, and bend over backward to take care of any and all details.

We have stayed at the beautiful Watermark Hotel in San Antonio a couple of times. The first time was when we booked - nights at the La Mansion across the river and had a terrible experience all the way around - messed up-lost reservations, filthy, dusty room (not appropriate for our asthmatic child who was unfortunately ill at the time). They promptly moved us to this """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""sister"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel and set us up with - connecting rooms. It was beyond lovely. Very spacious - the bathrooms were to die for. Being that our children took the double queen room in the corner of the hallway (adjacent to our King room), their bathroom was HUGE. We could have fit - people in the tub, alone - no need for the pool! Very elegant-conservative-comtemporary decor which was very calming. The beds are very comfortable - a big plus for a traveler who has back issues like myself. The location is fabulous. We have yet to get a river view, but no matter, the river is a step outside the door. A wonderful way to experience the very special River Walk is to dine at their signature restaurant, Pesca. We've dined there many times since the hotel opened and are NEVER disappointed. They even whipped up something for our finickiest eater (plain buttered pasta, fresh strawberries on the side) which seems silly, I know, but many restaurants would not bother with even such a simple task. Pesca has fantasitc, friendly service, a wonderful menu and wine list (not cheap, but so worth it!). It's a favorite place for us to celebrate a special occasion when in SA, even if we are staying out in the hill country. The conierge desk has never steered us wrong with dinner reservations outside the hotel as well. And if you are with your kids, there is a Johnny Rockets right next door. A favorite of our crew. 
The second time we booked for a spa weekend for an anniversary trip. The spa was wonderful and relaxing and is quite beautiful. Our room, service and dinner reservations were as perfect as we expected and had experienced in the past. 
This is not a place - nor are there really many on the River Walk - for a swimming pool type vacation. It is HOT in Texas in the summer and the small roof top pool can become quite warm. However, we still enjoyed it, with or without our children. There is pool side service from a small cafe next to the pool which has good food and drinks (good margaritas, etc). You will get excellent service for the price of what you would expect at a - or - star hotel. Also worth mentioning is the workout facility. Very nicely done and clean (empty-no other patrons around) with all updated equipment. We enjoyed this, as well. Book the Watermark if you find yourself in or near SA even for one night. You will truly enjoy the experience. We will definitely book it again - for one night or for several!

We had a corner room on a low floor. It only had a view of the street but the room and the bathroom had recently been renovated. It was very nicely done. The staff was also very helpful in helping us print boarding passes, hail cabs, etc. We really enjoyed our stay.

Beautiful hotel with some serious gaps in service. Check in took forever. The Gold Passport dedicated line was nearly as slow as the main check in area. Elevators were extremely slow. Parking garage was a nightmare - crammed with cars, tiny parking spaces, slow garage elevators. Main breakfast restaurant was not able to handle the large Labor Day crowd - waited in line for ----- minutes just to get a table. Once in the dining room there were lots of empty tables. Made me think they were understaffed. Room was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""ok"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Towels in bathroom were in serious need of replacement. Toilet malfunctioned multiple times. """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Top of the Hyatt"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" bar had amazing views. Too bad the windows were dirty and full of smudge marks. It was a disappointing stay. Hyatt can do better.

We have just returned from a - night stay at the Belvedere Hotel and it was an extremely pleasant experience. The hotel location is great, just a few blocks from Times Square and the subway (which is safe as long as you are careful) is around the corner. Great for catching a Broadway show as all the theatres are on your doorstep (Good Vibrations is fantastic but don't go to see Movin' Out - it is awful). The rooms are small but have everything you need including a coffee jug, fridge and microwave, iron, safe and alarm clock. The room had a very comfy bed and the TV has about -- or so US channels. You can watch movies but they cost around -- dollars.
The bathroom is small but very clean and has a great power shower. I did find the walls quite thin, but then NY is noisy anyway from the roads so it wasn't a problem (we had a --th floor room which had fab views).
We did a lot of research on the internet to find a good quality hotel for around £-- per room per night, and found this one on crshotels.com. We checked out the reviews on trip advisor and saw that it looked fine and it was!
I am an extremely fussy traveller and found this - star hotel exactly what it is - - star and ideal as a base for exploring NY. You always return to a clean and tidy room which is lovely and warm!!! (There was air con for the summer too). The staff were really helpful too. :)
If you are looking for a place for breakfast not far from this hotel, the Seattle Cafe just off -th Avenue and --st Street (- minute walk) has the best selection of breakfasts. We were having eggs, toast, home potatoes and a tea of coffee for - dollars each!!!! The cakes are out of this world, what's more - it is open -- hours.
Bubba Gumps is great - the shrimps are out of this world.

Our first stay at this hotel was in November of ---- , the staff was wonderful, the rooms were far better than we expected and the service we recieved while we were there was increddible. We have stayed there every time we've gone back to Denver. We would definately reccomend this hotel if you are just going for a weekend at six flags or romantic getaway, or even for a buissness trip. They have all the ammenities that you would look for in a hotel of it's class. The other thing that makes this hotel so appealing is that it is affordable too!! They also allow your pets along which is a very big plus since we own a dog and he travels with us everywhere. it is akso very kid friendly with an indoor pool sauna,hot tub and also has movie options!! So for anyone looking for a place that they just want to get away i would definately reccomend this hotel!!!!

Nice, clean facility. They certainly are replacing furniture-they were starting to work on the floor we were on when we were checking out, but our non-upgraded room was fine. It was an off peak day & it appears that they had not placed guests on that floor while they were moving furniture around. The room was clean, comfortable & quiet. Is there a great view, not really, but I've been few places in Philly that DO have great views
What really stood out to us was the level of service. We had a couple of small glitches (one unimportant, one involving money) that were resolved in a matter of minutes. Really. It appears that customer service is emphasized and their staff are empowered to solve problems asap. Impressive!
They provide some cute little touches-Philly soft pretzels (more tasty than most-don't eat those nasty things on the street!) and hot cider & cookies in the lobby. 
You are within walking distance of Reading Terminal Market-a foodies delight! The Convention center, of course, and we walked to Independence Hall & the historic sites. It is a short drive to the Battleship NJ & aquarium, both of which we enjoyed.
It is in the city, but I never felt threatened or uncomfortable. Be smart, be aware, but take advantage of friendly people. Take advantage of any package deals-ours made our weekend visit an affordable getaway! (Thanks for the Tastykakes!)
Would certainly stay again!

Our stay at the Grand was delightful though it was shortened by a family emergency. But in our brief stay, we quickly came to love the beautiful, well-maintained grounds, the plentiful accomodations and most impressive, the warm & friendly staff. In particular, Conierge Tim Watkins went above and beyond to
help make our stay as pleasant as possible. His service alone was reason enough to bring us back another time in the future and to recommend this resort to others.
Thank you Tim!!!

As it was our honeymoon, we backed our bed up against the window, flopped down on our stomachs like little kids and watched the Seattle waterfront and sunset slowly fade into evening...Nothing beats opening the windows and hearing the water lap at the pilings under the hotel and the cool breeze gently whistling by while your feet are warmed by the in-room fireplace.
This is a definite anniversary return for additional lifelong-memories.

We drove into Denver on Saturday to avoid snowy and icy roads in the middle of the night to catch a flight. I found the front desk to be very nice and helpful. I found the hotel was not really very sound proof and you could hear people coming and going all night. It is an older building, not as clean as I want in my hotel stays. For myself, I will pay more to stay somewhere else next time as I don't enjoy being able to hear people in the halls and rooms above and next to me. It is priced lower so that is a good value and located close to the airport.

Stayed here for - nights in in May and June and while we loved the rooms we were a bit shocked at the amount of children and the unruly behaviour allowed by their parents.
Standing in line to get breakfast for --- minutes may not be everybody's idea of a good time either and we only tried the afternoon free drinks thing once because of the wait at the bar and the chaotic behaviour of the children.
The hotel itself is great...and if you've got kids it probably makes sense to stay there... If you like your hotel to be more serene and ordered think before booking in here.
The italian restaurant attached to the hotel was a highlight and has delightful food and service.

This hotel does the simply things well. It is very clean and the - double rooms are very adequately sized and fitted out for a family of -. Breakfast was included in the room tariff and the food was better than average. The best part of the hotel however were the two ladies at the reception desk. They were both excellent and couldn't do enough for you. From early check-in, to recommending things to do whilst in Boston. The neighbourhood the property is in is just ok. Not the most aesthetically pleasing but by no means a deal breaker. We walked to the nearest subway each day (about -- minute walk) and felt very safe during the day. It was then about another -- minutes on the subway to get into Boston City. Ample free parking on-site. Limited dining choices in neighbourhood.

In all aspects, from the doorman at our arrival, to the Chief Concierge who saw to every detail to make our weekend truly special, to the delightful piano man at the Ship's Tavern, and the historical, beautiful lobby and restaurants, we found the Brown Palace to exceed all our hopes and expectations. Our room was luxurious and unbelievably quiet with furnishings and decor that were very attractive and of the highest quality. The bed and other furniture were extremely comfortable, so we spent more time in our room than we had expected, though the central downtown Denver location lends itself to endless opportunities for activities. We dined in - of the - restaurants, including the magnificent brunch at Ellyngton's. The food and servce were exceptional. Perhaps the most memorable aspect of the weekend was experiencing the extraordinary customer service from every staffmember we encountered. This is obviously a value engrained in the very culture of the Brown Palace at all levels. We cannot wait to return next year!

W. --th St. and -th Ave. wonderful location especially if you want to Broadway musicals. Go to TKTS at Times Square day of performance for half price tickets. Hotel has a wonderful breakfast buffet. The only reason I do not give this hotel an excellent rating is because to have very recently built a hotel this size and made a miniature pool is idiotic above all in the summer when everyone wants to cool off, you can't even get into the pool and there are not enough chairs. That was really disappointing for an otherwise really great property.

Good value, rooms are small and comfortable-functional. Not the most memorable neighborhood in New York, the commercial heart of mid-town, but hop on to the subway and find yourself anywhere in a flash.

I stayed one night mid-March on a Priceline reservation.

For those of us into service - this is an entirely different hotel.
To be honest some of the following may be due to the newness of staff but the hotel has been open since January.

Guestroom - when you press the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""wake up"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" button on the room phone, it does not connect you to the wake up call service - it takes you to messages. Speaking of messages, my room

I recently returned from a - night stay at Hotel on Rivington. I thought the people staying at the hotel were a bit self important. The hotel itself was trying to be really funky.
