The service was there is you asked for it, but we felt like the hotel was run by kids. Not much experience and not overly friendly, which is fine.
After a few initial glitches (call for room service at - in the morning: wrong room, etc.)it actually improved. I asked the conceiarge a few questions which were well answered and had two surprise lovely breakfasts in the hotel restaurant on the last - days.
All in all, there really is no choice for that area, as it is really the only hotel. Love the location. I suspect this hotel may disappear into oblivivian as it really was trying hard, yet nothing special. I really hope they can make it work.

After - months, I returned to Houston on another business trip, and the Hilton Garden Inn is just as good. Quick easy check in, quicker checkout. All staff were friendly and full of smiles. Hotel is clean, room was clean. Breakfast is good, with a good selection of items, including cooked to order eggs. Many folks had heaped plates of food which is a good indicator. This is a typical reliable garden inn. The only item of note is that it is starting to show its age a bit, and the hot water control was basically on-off.

Upon arrival (-:-- pm on a Thursday) at this downtown Chicago hotel I was greeted by a very welcoming Valet staff who helped us with our luggage and parking the car. We went up to the sixth floor where we were greeted by a friendly, courteous clerk who checked us into our room promptly. We were booked on the --th floor and I noticed immediately when I stepped off the elevator that the hallways were clean. Fresh paint, newer carpet. After a long - hour drive from Kentucky I was pleasantly surprised when I stepped into our room on the --th floor. Clean, Updated, and comfortable.
Since it was -:-- pm my children and I headed back down to the sixth floor for the manager reception where I was expecting to be served chips and gum drops, but instead we helped ourselves to nice, crisp salad greens with all the trimmings, potato wedges, big hot dogs (I think it was opening day at the ballpark in Chicago), and for dessert , warm, chocolate chip cookies straight from the oven. All the soda, beer, or wine you wanted. I was delighted that I could sit down with the kids and get something to eat before heading out to Navy Pier. I have been at other Hilton chain hotels and never received anything as nice and I was impressed by the attention of the staff. They were very pleasant, and helpful removing unwanted plates immediately.
That evening my son enjoyed the indoor pool with all the other kids, and I couldn't have been more satisfied with my comfortable bed that night. 
The next morning we went to the breakfast buffet which included delicious waffles with cherries and whipped cream, fresh pasteries, fruit, and bagels. Eggs, sausage, oatmeal, cereal, juices...all terrific.
When we contacted valet for our car and luggage they were very prompt, courteous, and helpful.
Over all I can't say a bad thing about this hotel! I tavel often and believe this was an excellent value for the money. Staff was top shelf. When I return to Chicago I will gladly book this hotel again!!

Over in Phoenix for a quick business trip, I will admit I was at first put off by the front entrance and the fact that the hotel seemed a bit far off from attractions, shopping centers and restaurants. But quickly and in many ways The Clarendon Hotel made up for the secluded location... rooms are vast and clean, the pool is gorgeous, atmosphere was casual, service was impeccable, convenient free wifi access, free excellent breakfast. No hidden fees, a great price-value deal. There was a hard to define """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cool"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" quality to the Clarendon... It just felt very good staying over and the business trip thanks to the Clarendon felt like a --day holiday. I had never posted a review on trip advisor but felt this hotel deserved I spend - minutes of my busy life doing so.

Very pleased with stay at Hotel --. Ended up coming into NY a day early and they accomadated us in shared bathroom rooms before transferring us to the private bathroom rooms we had booked for the next two nights. No problem with either room, though private bathroom was nicer and as booked well in advance on internet was cheaper than shared bathroom! 
Hotel service was good, looked after bags on day of check out until evening for us, booked car to airport etc.
Location is good, we walked everywhere from top to bottom of ny with no problems. Area is good, feel safe and some nice cafes - restaurants - bella napoli (huge pasta plates), cosi (coffee and sandwiches) and nice little late night deli next door. Bargain for breakfast was basement of manhattan mall - egg and bacon roll and coffee for under - dollars.
You really need to take the shuttle to get to the terminals. It is small and runs every ----- minutes and then takes a long time to get back to the main terminals. Might as well be off airport

This hotel is in a great location for theater and shopping. Room wasn't very big, but nice comfortable king bed. Plenty of hangers in the closet and shelves, no dressers. Air conditioning was adjustable and not noisy. Tiny bathroom, but clean and plenty of towels. Staff were very helpful and friendly. Did not eat in the restaurant. Chose to get breakfast at the Food Emporium. Did not know about friending on FB to get WiFi comped, so that was disappointing.

We stayed here for two days just before Christmas. We were in a suite with two double beds and a fold out couch. There was plenty of room for the four people in my family, which includes two kids (-- & --.) The room was very clean, and the decor was nice and understated. Water bottles were in our room, and unlike most other hotels, there was no charge if we drank them. 
We arrived at Noon, and our room wasn't ready yet, but the very friendly staff invited us to go upstairs to the cafe and eat a snack and refresh ourselves. The cafe was definitely a big hit with my family. There are Pepperidge Farm cookies, small pastries and fruit available, plus an amazing coffee machine that creates lattes, cappuccino, etc. Breakfast was even better, with cereals, oatmeal, bagels, and everything you could want. Finally, the wine and cheese, crackers,
 fruit, etc that was offered very evening was lovely. It was so nice to have this amenity in a city 
where everything is so expensive. 
The staff was friendly and helpful. We felt like they really were interested in making our stay 
pleasant. We loved the goodies they left for us in our room!
We had dinner at the Italian restaurant connected to the hotel, Tony's di Napoli. It was wonderful. I did a separate review for it, it was so good. About $--- for the four of us, and very memorable.
The hotel was a true oasis just a block off Times Square. We were able to easily get to all the 
places we wanted to go (Broadway shows, ice skating in Bryant park, museums) by walking or 
subway. So convenient to the craziness and hustle and bustle, but you absolutely didn't feel any 
of that in the hotel.
Overall, this is one of the best hotels I've ever stayed in. Also probably one of the most 
expensive I've ever stayed in per night ($--- after you include tax and parking), but I think it was 
well worth the extra money. The location and amenities made our time in NYC very special.

On second day of stay, found a letter in my room stating pool and hot tub would be closed for a month due to renovation. Called my travel agent, she confirmed there was nothing on hotel website advising of uncoming work. Management offered nothing and could care less. Stay away from the place.

I stayed here with a bunch of guys for a bachelor party. Perfect! Fenway right next door. Great hotel bar. The bartender Mary Beth is awesome. If you need a place that is reasonable and don't expect much else it's perfect.

Impressive historic hotel. The Lobby and the room was absolutely beutiful. Still price of the room was very reasonable. Staff was very friendly and very fast to help you with requests. Location in down-town San Diego gave easy access to the nightlife in The Gas Lamp district as well as the convention center -- minutes walk away. I stayed in a room with a jacuzzi on the top floor, but was told most rooms only have showers, as it is an old building. A minus was the breakfast which in my opinion was expensive, and not very good. But you can not expect a high quality of food in the US, so it was to be expected.

I recently stayed at Town and Country Resort Hotel for an overnight visit to San Diego. The hotel is centrally located and close to many attractions. The grounds of the hotel are beautiful and the decor is charming. We ate breakfast on the patio at the Trellises and our food server, Pati, was great! She was friendly, attentive, and the food was good! I stayed there as part of a travel promotion and would do so again.

I traveled on september ---- with my girlfriend. Since it was our first time in San Francisco, we wanted a central hotel near Union Square which wasn't very expensive.
We found this hotel and started reading all the reviews in Tripadvisor and saw they were very good. We also contacted the hotel and asked them to send them more pictures, which they did right away.
The hotel is located just - streets of Union Square (and Powell street) and there is a Muni just around the block (free if you buy the city pass) that takes you there.
The rooms are great, confortable queen bed, lcd-plasma tv, big bathroom and a kitchenette with fridge and microwave.
There was free Wifi at the lobby and the staff was very helpful. There was a parking lot just around the corner ($$).
When we arrived, they gave us a key to a room that was already taken. We went to the front desk and they immediately gave us a key to another room.
The only thing that shocked us was that just when we arrived, we had to use the service elevator, which was in pretty bad shape. It had no ceiling and just a lightbulb hanging from it. However, after - days, both of the elevators started working just fine.
If you're on a budget and want a pretty good hotel, this should be your choice.

Treated myself to a night downtown, but prepaid, which was a mistake. The rooms are clean and contemporary, but totally of the the tiny European budget-hotel variety. I appreciate the efforts they're making to go green, but I was wanting a bath and a relaxing night. I ate dinner in the restaurant bar, and that was nice with good service. Free coffee and NY Times in the morning was a plus. Location is good - close to whole foods, but nowhere in your room to sit and enjoy the nice wine and cheese you might get there. If you can get a really good price, I'd recommend it, but only if you don't need a tub or room to move.

We stayed here for two days in a king bed room. The location is great: within walking distance of Water Tower Place, the Hancock Building and all the shopping and restaurants on the Magnificent Mile. The entire staff, including housekeeping, were friendly, courteous and helpful. Our room was comfortable and clean, although smaller than we are used to. Our lunch in the hotel restaurant was delicious, beautifully presented and very reasonable. The downsides were the lack of drawer space, no counter in the bathroom, and a narrow shelf above the sink. There was a large min bar under the television that would have been a great place for drawers. This is a great place and reasonably priced for a short stay.

We came there to meet my son his wife and my grand babies before they shipped out to Germany with the Air force and the first room we got was dirty hairs in the bath tub dirty counters and dirty bedding so we reported it to the manager Tosha. She went way way beyond what we could have ever asked for and upgrades us into an executive suite on the --at floor with views of the city and bay! Plus it had way more room for all of us to stay in! My son and his family had a great time we were all comfortable and enjoyed out stay wee thanks to such and awesome manager as Tosha! I would suggest tasting here it was the best place we have ever been and war sometimes stay at the Hilton when we travel

This hotel is right in the centre of Manhattan. We found it to be small and clean. It is a pain not having en suite toilet etc but not too inconvenient. Towels are a bit on the small side. Other reviews have mentioned noise but we found it to be really quiet. It is ideal if you want to get out an about.

Nice clean room, front desk clerk very nice and helpful. Locate on south freeway close to downtown and shopping. I often stay at another hotel but I will be staying here from now on. Yolanda very helpful directing me to some good places to eat
Great hotel, in a great location. Chilled water at the entrance is a great touch. Have stayed here before, and would gladly do so again.
This hotel is old and tired, recently taken over from Days Inn. The mattress sagged and was not supported. Felt like I was staying in a hotel that hadn't been maintained since the --s.

I have stayed at the Fairmont Hotel in Chicago, Illinois twice now and both times I was very pleased with my experience. The staff was fabulous ... from the front desk, concierge, and inside staff to the doormen and parking garage staff. They treated us very VERY well and always remembered our names, spent time making sure we had whatever we needed. Any calls to the front desk was handled promptly and whatever we requested (more towels, someone to come check something in the room) was done as quickly as possible. The staff went above and beyond in all cases to do with my family and I would totally recommend the hotel to anyone. It is an added bonus that it is close to Michigan Avenue and shopping as well as restaurants and small shops. FABULOUS I cannot say enough about the staff at this hotel.

What a pleasant suprise. We had read mixed reviews about this one but we were happy. The location is fantastic, close to everything. You can walk to get the ferry to Alcatraz, to see sea lions at pier --, to the cable car, to the crooked street and a bus stops just near the hotel to the city or to the baseball park. The breakfast was fine, yes it was crowded but we always got a seat for - and the food had never ran out when we were there. San Francisco is an expensive place to eat so great to fill the kids up before heading out. Front desk were helpful and able to tell us about buses etc that we needed. Room was bigger than we had expected.

Stayed for one night recently at the Inn at the Ballpark. I paid $--- which is exceptional value for this above-average hotel. On a Sunday night, most other --- star hotels downtown or in the Galleria area were asking $---+ and because the Inn's website clearly stated they had smoking rooms (I'm a smoker.), I booked there.
The Inn, as it's name suggests, is located across the street from the baseball stadium. If you're in Houston for a game (which I wasn't), I can't think of a better location; it's also very accessible to downtown Houston. I can't imagine what you'd do in Houston without a car so even if your trip is focusing on the Galleria area, it's not too far a drive (----- minutes). It's also very convenient to the Convention Center which is within a five minute walk. 
The reception staff, both when checking in and out, was the male, college, frat boy type, outright surly when checking in and a little friendlier when checking out. My room, ---, was very clean and quiet, decorated in a baseball theme (as is all the hotel), in dark browns, beiges and green. Good selection of channels on the tv, and a DVD player which I didn't use. In terms of comfort, I would rate it along with a good Sheraton, Marriott, etc., etc. (i.e., above Holiday Inn, but not quiet Westin). The bathroom was average size and stocked with Aveda products. I was somewhat surprised not to find a mini-bar but then again, you often don't get those at other chains.
I didn't order from room service but on the plus side, it is available -- hours a day. I skimmed through the menu and while adequate, it seemed a little limited and not very innovative. (Perfectly acceptable, but nothing extraordinary). As to the business center, there really isn't one. It consist of the concierge's desk whose computer you're free to use; you can print out documents """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""in the back"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" as I was told and they'd be delivered to me. I never waited more than five minutes for my car from the valet service and the valet staff, as the housekeeping staff, were extremely efficient and very friendly.
Bottom line----If you're travelling to Houston, the Inn at the Ballpark is a good, centrally located choice at a reasonable price. I would return with no hesitation and if you're going for an Astros game, this is the place to be.

I stayed at similarly priced hotels in Vancouver and San Francisco on my trip but this was the gem. Very nice hotel indeed with great restaurant attached. Bathrooms were lovely.
I thought the Metropolitan in Vancouver was nice but this definately had the edge on it.

Stayed in the Hotel Beacon with work reasons and I have to say very nice beds and linen. Across the road a very well stocked Supermarket great fresh food with the Hotel Beacon you have a little kitchenette very good for people with children big rooms and very clean. The lift was very slow always had to wait a long time. - minute walk to the subway train and lots of little places to but food of any kind.
Old area but when i was there they were fixing alot of buildings.
there was a craft weekend market about -----min walk north of Hotel Beacon great things to buy and food to eat. over all what a good stay.

This hotel has some nice things to offer but some of the staff are poorly trained and very unhelpful. We stayed there for one night on a rainy Sunday in December. The hotel was empty...you could tell because there was ample parking available in their lot and no one around. We had booked on priceline through the bidding process and gotten a good deal. When we checked in, I asked for a king size bed. The front desk guy refused because he said we had paid so little he could only give us two queens unless we wanted to pay $--'s more. I asked why it would cost the hotel more if we slept in a King vs two queens. He said that was their policy since they get so little $ from Priceline for us staying there. We had stayed at other hotels in the same area with a higher star level for the same price so I'm not sure why he seemed to feel as if we personally were ripping him off. He gave us a room facing the alley on the second floor right on top of where the cars go through the gate to get the garage and right by where a giant intake fan is located in the alley. It was super loud and unpleasant. It was clear he had done his best to give us the worst room they had. The service from other members of the staff was good though...I can only say they guy that checked us in was the worst and made us want to never stay at this hotel again.
Other than the service though, the beds are comfortable, the location is good and the wifi is free.

Pros:
Clean room. Very nicely appointed. Towels and amenities were excellent. 
Location was great, EXCEPT IT WAS HARD TO FIND OFF STREET PARKING. 
PARKING IS UNDERNEATH HOTEL.
Aside from that, no complaints.
Cons:
Parking. A tad bit on the high side.

We stayed here - nights and really enjoyed it. Great base to explore NYC from, very central and great little deli next door to get breakfast from in the morning. However the thing we were most impressed by was after we left. My husband accidentally left his suit and shirt hanging in the wardrobe...we didn't notice until near the end of our holiday when we were in Washington DC. We were put in contact with Frank, the assistant general manager, who found the suit and shirt for us, and Fed Ex'd it straight away to our hotel in DC at no charge to us!! Couldn't have been more impressed with the level of service they provided. Thank you Courtyard and Frank!!

If you are going to Seattle and need a place to stay in the university district, try the Hotel Deca. It has great rooms, is centrally located and the staff is fabulous! It was one of the nicest hotels I have been to in a long time (and I travel a lot) and would highly recommend it.

This is my second time staying at this hotel. By NYC standards you get what you pay for. Nothing fancy, although the TVs are nice, the breakfast was standard Hampton Inn fare (although the Croissants were huge and delicious!), and no signs of bed bugs (yet). What is great about this location is its closeness to the --th street and --rd street subway, it is a short walk to times square, and there are plenty of restaurants close by. We were here for Macy's and it was very close to the parade route. Also, -- blocks up -th is Bryant Park which is a great place to hang out.

After reading the poor reviews, I was bracing for a not-so-good experience for my upcoming - day conference stay. I've stayed in many hotels, so I've seen the good the bad & the ugly. Thankfully, this was a good experience. 
Front desk staff was very accomodating with my early arrival and request for a non-adjoining room. Room was clean & well appointed (and I am picky). 
The Terrance Restaurant was only open in the AM, so I never got to try it. I was not interested in the sushi bar or the - star restaurant, so that left the (upscale) Media Bar & Grill for all my dinners. Good food, nice atomosphere. There were a few shops to browse. From one shop I picked up snacks-water for in the room. 
I did not try the spa or have to park a vehicle, so can't comment on those elements. I brought my MiFi, so I did not have to pay the crazy daily internet charges.
It is worthwhile to take some time to enjoy the huge Asian art collection throughout the - lobbies, the conference center halls and on the mezzanine level. The wide variety of artifacts made for some nice pictures.

My sister & I stayed at this hotel the night before, and the night after a cruise. We loved this place !! The front desk staff were incredibly friendly, efficient and helpful and did their best to answer any questions we had. They even allowed us to check in at --:-- in the morning when we got off our cruiseship. The concierge was great - booked us a great restaurant on Pier -- for dinner, as well as a limo to take us to the airport on our last day. He was a wealth of information and always had a smile for you when you came in. The hotel is perfectly situated on Fisherman's Wharf, and the whole area is safe to walk at any time. We would stay there again in an instant !!

I was scheduled to stay at The Clarendon in October. After having to ask several locals for directions to the hotel (none of whom had heard of it), I finally found it. From the outside, this is an old, unappealing building not resembling a hotel. Having some reservations about staying there, I took a quick walk inside to find a hotel in need of renovations, a completely torn up courtyard (a dirt pit where pool once was) and contractors working on various things (there was no mention of any construction taking place on the website). It appeared to me to be a hotel with long term guests (a few rooms with open windows appeared to be apartments rather than guest rooms. The website suggested a hip, chic, new boutique hotel. What I witnessed was a rundown, neon lit """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""motel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" with a dirt pit courtyard as its center of attraction. Needless to say, I checked into another hotel. The website was one of the most deceptive I have encountered.
By the way, unless a miracle happened, there is no way the pool would be opening on October --th.

We heard about the Ocean Beach Hotel from a co-worker and she said it was pet friendly and fun. She was absolutely correct. The rooms were clean and roomy and they were quite. The place was a perfect location and I felt that I was right in the middle of the ocean hub. We never drove anywhere because everything was in walking distance. And the staff on site were very knowledgeable about the culture and locations to eat. My husband and I and our dogs never had a better time and it was very relaxing and laid back. We wanted to extend our visit but had to work. However, we will be returning very soon with more of our friends.

We were excited to stay at Philly's downtown Marriott given it's beautiful web site - and, honestly, the high price set the expectations high. It was okay. Location is great - easy walks to sites abound. Room was clean, but ceiling paint peeling in bathroom. Housekeeper restocked bathroom and did trash, but didn't make bed. There was no bottled water in the room day-, but it showed up day - - and they charged us $-.-- for it though we hadn't had it. Valet parking staff was very pleasant and helpful. $-- to park with the tax, $-- for Internet if you want both iPads to connect, mini fridge would have cost extra -- those are free at $-- a night hotels, but they charge for them at a $------- a night place? Bury it in your price if you have to and stop nickel-diming me. No room service ... TV and Internet didn't work first night, but it got fixed. Fitness room was nice, but tv on elliptical didn't work one morning. So, it was okay, but not the wonderful experience amidst the conference we'd hoped for when my wife decided to accompany me.

The hotel is ok if you're travelling with family. This is what it is designed for. If only they had paid some attention to style. Even low-range IBIS hotels would be more up-to-date. The interior design is hopelessly stuck somewhere between the American Civil War and the ----s. Service is excellent though and makes up for its lack of style. Prices can be quite competetive if you book one of the specials on the net.

This wasn't our first choice of accommodation. New York is New York though, and hotel space comes at a cost and is also booked up early! You just have to put up with it!
Check in is pretty all over the place. The staff are hit and miss. Lovely door man - scrag reception lady. It seems as though they think they are running a five star hotel??
Our room wasn't ready on arrival(we were quite early), so they were happy for us to leave our luggage and go get some brunch. We returned a while later and it still wasn't ready, so we just waited in the lobby area. Whilst sitting around, I did see several clients waiting around to be attended to while the lady at the front desk chatted on her mobile. Not acceptable in my opinion.
When we finally got to our rooms, we literally could not fit through the door. It was a shoebox (but i kept reminding myself this is new york!). With our suitcases in the room, we could not get in and out the door! 
The air con was broken and the room was extremely stuffy and hot. I tried to open the window, but it can only be opened a small amount due to a stopper fixture. I told them the next day and they fixed it that afternoon.
The front wheel of the bed was broken, and was so noisy every time you moved around. The mattress was also extremely hard, to be honest i didn't have a good nights sleep.
Bathroom facilities were fine - but no space to lay out make-up, toiletries etc. Girls, bring your own hairdryer, as the one provided is rubbish. Felt like only --watts. Surprisingly the shower was powerful and spacious.
Internet is provided via a cable in the room. Wireless isn't needed considering there is no room to move around. I didn't eat in the hotel restaurant - why would you when you have so much choice?
I personally would stay at the Bowery or somewhere nicer next time - if you're used to bigger rooms and more professional service. But if you're a last minute traveller like me - then park south hotel will suffice.

You would never think that this Westin at the airport would be that good, but it is!!! This hotel is tearing up the market due to its great location and superior product. If you are traveling you must check it out.....only thing missing is a draft beer at the trendy bar.

I stayed here for a few days in November on the tail end of a business trip. The room was really large (especially for Manhattan) and beautifully presented. Bed was extremely comfortable (and I long to get one for home. Bathroom was small, but nicely fitted out. The free breakfast was fairly limited (but there are plenty of other places to get breakfast in Manhattan). Bene across the street did fairly good coffee.
I'd certainly stay here again and recommend it to others (which I have).

We had a good price on this hotel, especially compared to other hotels in the Washington DC area. We got good value for it as well.
The room was rather large and clean. Nothing luxurious but very decent.
There is an Avis car rental office --- metres from the hotel, which came in very handy for us.
There is a subway station at about a - minute walk from the hotel, from there you can get to anywhere in the city.
There is also a CVS and a Starbucks at this subway stop by the hotel.

I can not believe this hotel is only in the top --- in NYC - the other --- must be out of this world as On the Ave delivered in every single aspect and made our stay in New York one to remember!!!!
We arrived at On the Ave for my --th birthday (a suprise trip to NYC) and on arrival I was wished happy birthday by the reception staff and found a small gift and a card in my room wishing me happy birthday. Throughout our stay the staff continued to be courteous at all times and went out of their way to ensure we were looked after at all times.
The rooms are great - they are spacious and have all the facilities needed for a break in the city. The beds are extremely comfortable and the bathrooms were lovely.
The location of the hotel was perfect for us - lovely neighbourhood yet only a -- min subway journey down to Times square and beyond!!!!!
Thanks to all at the hotel for a lovely stay and if you are reading this because you are thinking about staing at On the Ave my advice would be to go ahead and make the booking - you will not be disappointed!!!!!!!

My wife and I just returned from a one night stay at the Sofitel New York. Overall I came away with mixed feelings.
The location in mid-town is very convenient to everything within the city. The SoBed! Probably the best feature of the hotel is the bed, or as my wife called it, the Cloud. 
The staff however was quite a disappointment. Despite the fact that we were greeted upon arrival and escorted thru the lobby to front desk, service failed to impress beyond that. Check-in was fairly robotic and we were soon on our way up to our room; Luxury King was booked. The room itself was quite spacious by New York standards but we felt that the use of space poor. The room and facility as a whole felt like it was beginning to show some wear and tear....for some reason they taped duct-taped down the mats at the entry hall as well as at the front desk - this gave off a very janky vibe, not respecting of a - or - star property. Interaction with staff, from room service to the bell staff seemed very cold and uninviting; response time for requests however, was very quick.
All in all, I'd be hesitant to recommend the Sofitel New York. Having stayed at the Sofitel DC a couple of years ago, I had much greater expectations that were brought down by uninspiring staff and mediocre condition of the property. 
Safe Travels!

We reserved - rooms for my graduation so I was thrilled that one of them ended up being a suite at no extra charge. The suite had a lot more room than the room with two double beds. The hotel was very clean and the staff was very friendly. Expect to pay $-- for parking. The front desk will validate your parking ticket so that you can come and go. The only con was the cost of room service. For breakfast we purchased fruit and cereal from the lobby gift shop. Great location for walking to the Inner Harbor and other nearby attractions.

I stayed at the Swissotel Chicago over -th of July weekend. What a great place to stay—especially if you are partaking in the city’s festivities. A very short walk brought me to Grant Park where they had fireworks on the -rd. And afterwards, since the hotel is just slightly off the main drag of Michigan Ave, I was able to retreat quickly back to my room and enjoy the peace and quiet rather than all the noise from everyone walking around. And the view from my room—spectacular! I couldn’t have asked for a more idyllic picture of Chicago right outside my window. The room was quite spacious and very clean. The bed was so comfortable I felt like I was sleeping at home. The hotel was a bit busy during this weekend, but the staff did a great job of helping me with whatever I needed. I would definitely recommend Swissotel as the place to stay when visiting Chicago.

As a recommendation from a friend we stayed here - nights in early December. Having stayed at various NY hotels previously I was initially impressed with the size of the rooms. We stayed on the -th floor. The bathroom was a fair size, with great water pressure. The bed was soft and comfortable. Room was very clean. From reading past reviews we learned the heating was an issue so we decided to turn off the heating and leave the window open a fraction which worked a treat. Room service was prompt although the food was not great. I did not have any problem with the staff at reception at all. They were always helpful and attentive. Overall our stay was a good one. The best feature is the proximity to everything. The subway a short stroll away, and great restaurants nearby. The only negative is they advertised for a complimentary paper each day...we didn't see one in - days.

My first trip to NYC and we stayed in the delightful Milburn Hotel. What a find - close to Broadway, easy to navigate the city. We found a great supermarket nearby, handy when we just wanted to eat in. The hotel supplies a generous continental breakfast, complete with real NY bagels. The rooms were spacious, with a small kitchenette. I would recommend it for anyone that likes space and the convenience of a fridge and microwave. The staff is very friendly.

Had a wonderful - nights at this characterful, glamorous hotel. Stayed in a classic room which was beautiful. Excellent service. Lovely staff. Would not recommend in-room dining though as the food was poor quality, however, they did acknowledge this and didn't charge. Great location. Generally to be recommended!

This Red Roof has been renovated and is worth your time if you're in Columbus and are on a budget. The rates are great and the location is just one block from the Arena District. Rooms are modern. Continental breakfast was weak and you do pay an extra $---day to park but still worth it.

I don't know how much I really paid for the motel: I booked a package deal (flight+accommodation) since the air fares from Europe to Chicago were incredibly high. But it must have been cheap because the all-in-one price with a direct flight from Amsterdam was lower than non-direct flight-only prices.
The room was OK, not super clean, not downright dirty. Not small either, and the bedlinen and towels were clean, too. Free wifi worked as a charm. Two out of three nights I couldn't sleep too well because of road construction work in front of the motel from -am--am but the motel isn't to blame for this (although outside-noise isolation could have been better). I never heard any sound from adjacent rooms. The airco looked ancient - I didn't try it because it wasn't that hot.
Wouldn't book this for a fun stay, but if you're solo on a business trip and don't spend too much time in your room it's good value.

A pig in lipstick is still a pig. Although they may have renovated the check in area the rooms were tired and filthy. Upon check in which they couldn't get a room key to work we had to wait in a disgusting hallway for -- minutes. The front desk said it was my fault until the security guard had the same issue. Once we got in the room with a master key the room was filthy. There were spots in the carpet, furniture and bed. No black light needed here. Also soap from previous guest was left in shower including their hair. I would advise sleeping in your car over this place.

I stayed at the Jane for a little under a week. It was my first trip to NYC and I knew I didn't have a lot of time or money to spare in my short visit, so it was the perfect call. Located in a great neighborhood just a few short blocks walk (not even a hassle despite the cold) from the -th and --th station, everything about this place was great. 
The staff were beyond helpful. I made a rookie traveller mistake in regards to my credit card and they were incredibly patient throughout the entire thing. They helped me with questions when I had them & were always friendly. 
Yes, the rooms are small. European travellers are used to this sort of thing, it's close to the common size of many rooms overseas. But you're in NYC. The last thing you should be doing is spending your time in your room! The beds are comfortable and the temp was perfect if I just opened my window a tiny crack. I showed up during the big bedbug scare and had no problems whatsoever. My room was clean as were the bathrooms. 
I'm planning a trip back in a few months. This trip I have a good deal more money to spent, but even after spending time looking at all the other hotel options out there? I think I'm going to stick with the Jane. Maybe get a captain's just to see the difference, but no matter what room I end up in I know I'm getting a great value & unique experience for my dollars.

Wonderful stay in spacious room with exceptionally courteous staff. The Tex-Mex lunch buffet was outstanding and way too inexpensive. Close to everything in downtown Austin with a great view of town lake.

Central San Fransisco hotels all full so we came across this. Nice location near beach and quiet. Friendly check in and room clean and good size but more basic than other hotels we had stayed in. Flexible about how long we wanted to stay. 
We probably wouldnt come here again but there was no particular problem and I was surprised that it was so low down on trip advisors list of """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hotels in San fransisco"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".

My husband and I stayed here for his --th birthday and from the time we pulled up to check in until we pulled away, our stay was perfect. All of the staff were so friendly and helpful and surprised us on many occasions by calling us by name. We enjoyed a couples massage which was relaxing and romantic and dined at Sixteen for a delicious gourmet meal. They have spent time considering the traveler which makes too many small details to mention but which sets this hotel apart from the others. Another overnight will be in our near future. Fabulous!

My wife and I had the pleasure of staying for - nights at this amazing property. Despite many reviews to the contrary, we found our King Deluxe room fairly spacious (especially by NYC stadards), but the bathroom was indeed a bit """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cozy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". 
The front desk staff was very friendly, and allowed us to check in early. The bellmen and doormen were also quite helpful. The place is extremely modern, with a hip and funky flair. We absolutely loved it. To top it off, the location is among the best in Midtown. We walked almost everywhere, and the subway line is a block away. 
We can't wait to return to this stellar hotel.

There is nothing grand about this hotel except it's next to Grand Central Station. Very misleading. I honestly have to say this is one of the worst hotels I've stayed at and I've probably have stayed at over --- different hotels. My bathroom had mildew all over the bathtub. Worst of all the rooms have no noise insulation so it's very hard to sleep. I could actually hear the maids making up the room next to mine and they were complaining the whole time how they hated their job. Very unprofessional. Do yourself a favor and stay somewhere else.

Really enjoyed our - night stay here in early January. The rooms are fairly basic and the resort is in need of a general refurbishment of areas, eg spa flooring, but the Resort exudes a relaxed colonial charm with lovely pools, good tennis and basketball courts, pleasant lagoons and appealing restaurants. To charge for parking in the off season is a bit rude, although we did get a bit of a discount. Bonus was a coin laundry by one of the pools where I could finally get some washing done, in a very pleasant environment! It was pretty quiet being Winter and we had lots of facilities to ourselves which was great. 
Staff were all friendly and helpful, especially the Lobby Cafe Barista and the Receptionists.

Having only stayed in a Four Seasons Hotel once before (-- years ago in Philadelphia during my wedding), I was extremely excited about staying in the Four Seasons San Francisco for our family vacation. Since my last stay at a Four Seasons, the reputation of the chain has become one of impeccable service. That reputation is well deserved at the Four Seasons in San Francisco. 
Wonderful service, beautiful decor, centrally - if not beautifully - located on Market Street (Union Square, cable cars, BART & numerous restaurants are all within walking distance). The hotel is equally adept at being kid friendly and hosting formal business meetings.
If you are planning a trip to San Francisco - with or without kids - I would highly recommend the Four Seasons. Expensive, yes. Worth it, definitely.

The Sheraton Tribeca is a relatively new hotel downtown, close to the trendy shops in SoHo. My room was stylishly decorated, in good condition and very clean. The room was not very large, but fine for a night's stay, and the bed itself was very comfortable. The bathroom was well appointed and the shower had good water pressure. The bathroom amenities included a hair dryer, soap, shampoo, conditioner and body lotion. There were also coffee and tea making facilities in the room, but no fridge. 
What continues to bug me about the big chains is that they continue to charge for internet access. This was partly mitigated by """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The Link"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" facility in the lobby which consisted of multiple PCs with internet access in a new environment in which you could work. There is free wifi, but from what a colleague said, it sounded like there was a limit to the number of people who could use it at the same time. 
There is a Starbucks in the lobby and there is an onsite restaurant and the staff were friendly. Would I stay here again? If I had a meeting downtown, then maybe, although I suspect there may be slightly cheaper options nearby.

I have stayed at this hotel on all my visits to New York and wouldn't stay any where else. The hotel rooms and furniture style are a little dated but the rooms are more like a small apartment. The rooms have large storage cupboards-wardrobes, kitchenettes with micro wave and bar fridge plus a table to eat at. The lounge has a tv, - armchairs plus a pull out sofa bed (mattress was a bit thin but kids love camping out in a lounge). Two double beds in the bedroom plus another tv. The bathroom is dated but clean with a shower over the bath. 
The location is terrific only two streets from Central Park and in easy walking distance to Times Square. If you need a taxi the friendly doorman will get you one.
Internet connection was a bit expensive. We self catered so did not use the breakfast option available.
One tip don't bother visiting Micky Mantels Bar near Central Park the bar staff are not friendly in fact quite rude and the drinks are overpriced. 
Try to get to a game at Madison Square Gardens it may cost some $$$'s but we saw an ice hockey game and we will never forget it! Also we saw Bill Clinton there....not everyday you see 
an ex president.

First imperssion was, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I am not cool enough to stay here"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", when I checked in on Sunday afternoon. However the crowd changed from mohawks to suits on Monday morning. The room was clean, big, comfy bed, and free Bliss products are the highlights. The gym was great too and the staff was always beyond friendly and helpful. Will stay there again. On the downside it was very expensive in my opinion.

I try and visit New York at Christmas time as often as I can. December ---- was my -nd stay at the the Grand Hyatt Regency located next to Grand Central The location of this hotel is superb. The hotel faces --nd street and is attached directly to Grand Central Station which is nice because if you don't want to put all your warm weather garments on you can walk around all the levels of Grand Central Station. A food court is at the bottom, and there are many shops above to wander in and out of. There is also a great Italian bakery there too. If you go during the winter they have a winter bazaar which has some wonderful gift ideas.
From the location of this hotel it is a comfortable walk to Rockefeller Center and the splendor of -th Avenue. If you wish to venture to other areas of the city there is a subway entry in Grand Central Station, plus buses going every which way are right out the front door.
You can't beat this hotel for convenience either. Bus shuttles both toand from LGA & JFK are right across the street.

We needed a Memphis hotel for one night before catching a flight out. I'd read reviews of hotels close to the airport and wasn't impressed. Although the hotel had recently gone through a renovation - my husband described it as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""putting lipstick on a pig"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". After we had begun unpacking, the front desk called to say they forgot that the room we were in didn't have a working air conditioner.  The staff couldn't accomplish any basic tasks. I called the Hotel as soon as I received the info from Hotwire, and requested a crib to be added to the reservation. The woman I spoke with was dumbfounded and asked if I was coming that day. One positive - the bed was comfortable....
Don't waste your money, I'm sure there are much better hotels in Memphis that will gladly take your money and provide better service and amenities.

I stayed here with - of my girlfriends in June for a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""mom's night out"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and we had a blast. The hotel is clean and beautiful.
