There was plenty of room and it was nice and clean. the reception area was nice, the restaurants were lovely, although we didn't eat there, we checked it out. I'm not sure how late the bar is open, but when we wanted a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""nightcap"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" around - am it was closed. I would not suggest getting a coffee from the starbucks they have there, they do not make the coffees in the same manner as a real starbucks, and there is a real on directly across the street. Will def stay here again, it's location is ideal, we were able to easily walk to just about everything!

Great location. Great price. Friendly & helpful staff. Small rooms, but everything is neat and clean. Loud toilet (very water efficient flushmate http:--www.flushmate.com-), but that is what I have at home. Everything I need in a hotel. I would stay there again next time we are in the area.

I wouldn't stay here again unless of course I was told to as I was in this case. The Room was an average older Hotel Room, the room itself was spacious however the bathroom was not cleaned daily. Towels and amenities were replaced, but sink, floor, toilet and tub were NOT cleaned daily.
The staff were nice, breakfast wasn't worth the mention...

I recently spend a week at the St Francis on business; It was a fright from the moment I got to my floor. The doorman, front desk staff, and bell staff were attentive, but didn't warn me about my room... It was on a newly renovated floor that smelled of mothballs (I was told it was the new carpet), the whole --th floor smelled so my window (which opened) was of little help. The bell staff that escorted me to my room noticed immediately that the room was not made up properly and left to collect the towels, robe, and missing pillow. The amenities were less then I would expect, I've received better at a Hampton Inn. They were happy to press my suits, but were unable to shine my shoes. Housekeeping skipped my room twice during my stay, and the hotel never offered an apology; only a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""they'll be right up."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" All in all, it was a beautiful hotel, but the room was far too small (albeit a old hotel) for the price and the door banged into the bed when I opened it.
For the money, stay at the ritz or four seasons...

I booked this hotel after checking out the Trip Advisor reviews and getting a reasonable price for a well located city hotel on Expedia. The reviews were pretty representative of this place.
It is well located on good bus routes and within -- metres of the Vermont-Beverly metro station. If coming from LAX (I had a one night stay to kill some time after flying in from NZ) I would recommend taking the metro rather than buses unless you want to get a feel for the non-ritzy parts of LA. The buses (- connections) took almost - hours whereas you can get to the hotel in about -----mins by metro. 
I had a Vermont Ave facing room on the -rd floor. Road noise was apparent (but not deafening) and the aircon - same as for the San Diego Comfort Inn - is too noisy to leave on while you sleep; a consideration to bear in mind in staying in the heat of summer.
The room and hotel in general is really quite old-dated but reasonably clean though more fussy people would be a bit disappointed. Certainly wouldn't recommend the stay for a relaxing holiday, but it is ok for a night or two at the right price. Reception staff were reasonably friendly so no complaints there. 
Breakfast is adequate only unless you love making waffles.
I'm unable to compare it to any other inner city hotels of same rating-value but see my review of the Hotel Pepper Tree in Anaheim (great place!!).

This Hilton was a very pleasant surprise. The hotel is located directly next to Clear Lake. Breeze off the lake kept the Houston heat and bugs at bay. We enjoyed the pool and grassy areas beside the lake. A friendly and attentive staff made our stay pleasurable.The hotel seems to be a popular wedding and reunion hotel with a mix of NASA related travelers. We plan to use this facility again when visiting family in Baytown and Pearland. Friday night fireworks from nearby Kemah over the lake were fantastic and unexpected treat.

Nothing to get excited about. Expensive ($-- parking, $-- breakfast) and no free amenities but I guess that is how the hotel business works in downtown Washington DC. Typical Marriott nice but not outstanding. Good location with a metro stop nearby and Georgetown very close. We didn't have to stay in that location but my colleagues wanted to be near Georgetown. I'll recommend the hotel, especially if you want that location and want a Marriott; but otherwise shop around.

We booked this hotel via a travel company for our school trip to New York -th Feb - --th Feb. After reading the reviews on this site, i was very nervous to stay at this hotel. Me and my mates all had rooms on the -th floor. Throughout our stay we had no problems with cockroaches and nobody had bed bug bites. The rooms got cleaned everyday, new bedding everyday too. The rooms did get quite warm so we had the a-c on most of the time. If your looking for a hotel just to sleep in, I would recommend this hotel.

Terrible overall. Location right by the highway, terrible noise isolation, the worst unhealthy breakfast ever, outdated rooms, disgusting shower curtain, overpriced. 
Best to avoid all together.

Metropolitan Lexinton.
Fantastic.
Good location. Great Hotel.
Ask for a king (bigger room). Loved it.
Breakfast is great worth every penny. Ask for very hot water for your tea. 
Loved it, loved it, loved it.

This hotel is very nicely located and has large rooms. Otherwise, there is not anything special. The customer service was lacking, to say the least. We asked two times and still weren't helped with our bags. The conceriege service was border-line rude coupled with not very helpful. There were several other guests in line behind me when we checked in that were discussing the lack of customer service and commented on the number of people having to handle their own luggage. I would not recommend this hotel at all.

We got a good weekend rate for a hotel with a nice pool area, decent fitness and complimentary breakfast. Above all, the place was close to IAH but the setting was more than quiet in a more than nice neighbourhood. Disadvantage: nothing to eat or drink within walking distance. Rooms are comfy and the service was good. My only remark concerns wat we found under the bed. In fact wat was it, because most of wat we saw were unidentified objects. I think this zone is simply forgotten and this should be rectified in the cleaning procedure. Still, we had a nice stay and would certainly return.

Spent one night in this hotel before flying home. Reception friendly and efficient at check-in, rooms clean and beds comfy. Booked free shuttle on check-in but when I checked again later that evening, there had been an error and I found myself without a shuttle and needing to pay for a taxi. The next morning, got up at - -a.m. went to Reception. Pleased to learn there had been a cancellation, and even though I was early for booked shuttle, the driver was called and I was efficiently taken to the airport as the only passenger. Will definitely use this hotel again.

We visit NYC several times a year, Andaz -th Ave is our home away when we are in NYC. We had a corner suites with beautiful views, love the foot bath especially after a long walk all day long :)
Love the coffee bar and breakfast at The Shop was so good, make sure you order Chef Vence's specialty Lemon Poppy Seeds pancakes it is so delicious and please do say hello to chef Vence, he is a great chef.
The staff on this hotel is very friendly and yet professional, always ask if we need anything over drink and wine while waiting for room to be ready or waiting for friend to pick us.
We are looking forward to get back to this hotel.
I stayed only one night, but the location is excelent (close the internacional airport). But, after the midnight, i woke up - times because of the noise cars on the street (sirens).

I stayed here twice, about - months apart. Each time the hot tub by the pool was out of order. That is ridiculous. All they need to do is get it fixed, but they just don't ever get it done. I have called numerous times to inquire when making reservations in Houston, and over many months it is never fixed. They have lost my business many times due to this. It is so simple to fix things like this.. You call a contractor and get it fixed. They just don't seem to have the desire to fix it, it is just not a priority with them. Also the ice machines on every other floor were also out of order. Other than that, the staff is excellent, the rooms are clean, the location is great. They also have security in the parking areas. IF they ever fix the hot tub, I will return. In the mean time, I stay at Courtyard.

Overall, we found this to be a good place in downtown Manhattan. The location makes it easy to access the subway system at Grand Central. The staff were unwaveringly friendly and the concierge gave some excellent food recommendations. We had a cityscape room and the views were nothing short of spectacular. Overall, we would recomned the place, 
There were a few small problems. The first was that we were not asked if we wanted a smoking or non-smoking room. The room we got had clearly just been occupied by a smoker and REEKED of stale cigarettes. It was bad enough that my wife picked up an air freshener for our room when we passed by a CVS on the first day. The second problem was the lack of hot water. The two of us were on the --th floor and whenever I whoever showered second always got a pretty lukewarm shower. 
Finally, avoid the breakfast buffet unless you have money to BURN. it is really tiny (four chafing dishes of eggs, potatoes, and bacon and a couple cheese-fruit plates) and they do not tell you the price in advance--I was SHOCKED to spend $-- for two people to eat a buffet that most restaurants would charge $-- for on a Sunday morning. If they had told us the price in advance, we would have laughed, left and grabbed a bagel around the corner.

I stayed at the Hyatt Regency for a convention in mid-October. It was fairly predictable...a little below typical Hyatt Regency standards (no robe, no mini-bar, no complimetary shoe-shine). I think this is because the city of Denver subsidized the development of the hotel and perhaps there has been some cost cutting for the services. . But overall it was very nice...loved the bar on the top floor. Real shortage of cabs one night when it unfortunately snowing. You might have thought the management would have figured they would have a lot of conventioneers needing to go somewhere. But perhaps there are not so many cabs in Denver anyway. For style I would opt for the nearby Monaco, but the Hyatt was perfectly adequate and reasonably priced.

I stayed at the Super - on Columbia...right in Little Italy. It was my first time in San Diego. It was a fantastic stay! The place was clean and secure...and wicked affordable! I especially liked the staff. They were so accomodating and helpful. I would stay there again, hands down. The view of the harbor is great, too!

This hotel is an overall great place to stay. The staff are friendly (especially the desk clerk, Orlando, who has a warm smile and helpful attitude at all time). The hotel has a free shuttle that will drop off and pick-up at several locations. The free hot breakfast has something for everyone. There is free coffee ---- and free cookies in the lobby in the late afternoon. The suites are spacious and very clean. A reasonably priced hotel with perks you would normally find only in higher priced locations.

I stayed here on a - night trip to the Big Apple, and couldnt be happier. Great helpful staff members, a room up-grade was given without asking. Spotlessly clean. Modern tasteful rooms with a pillow menu!!! Great location - across the road from Maddison Square Gardens, - mins walk away from Penn Station, - minutes from Macy's and -- minutes from Times Square. Could get loud outside noise - but what would you expect from the city that never sleeps. I would recommend a trip to Dunken Doughnuts (right outside) for a cheap and cheerful breakfast (porriage and breakfast muffins on the menu with coffee for under $-)
Would recommend and stay here again.

This hotel was is in a great location in Hollywood. It is connected to the Hollywood mall and is convienient for reaching many of the tourist attractions. The room itself was simple, plain and sufficient. I cannot say enough about the customer service. The man working at the front desk was VERY friendly and so helpful. Also, if you are looking to rent a car there is a Hertz rental within a hotel about a block away. This was important for us. Overall, it is not a luxury hotel but the price and location were right!

The staff was amazing. Everyone is so helpful and always greets you with a smile. When I lost a jacket that was so important to me the security staff made it their priority to find it. Thank you Mr. Shawn Girardin you're the best. 
If you need to stay at a hotel in san diego this is the one to stay at.

We stayed one night prior to our early flight at the end of our vacation in Sedona. We did not want to make the two hour drive from Sedona so early in the morning so we booked one night here. I have stayed in airport hotels before so frankly did not expect much. I was pleasantly surprised. The rooms were spacious. Front desk was very helpful. We returned our car when we arrived and took the car rental shuttle to the airport and was picked up (in less than -- minutes). Then in the morning took the shuttle back to the airport. Very seamless and quick service. The breakfast was wonderful. Again we were not expecting much but was very surprised. My husband even personally thanked the woman who was putting out the breakfast since everything was very good and much more than you usually get at an airport hotel. My husand ate so much breakfast he skipped lunch that day. So if you are looking for a great airport hotel this is it.

Stayed at Hotel Contessa Oct. -----, ---- for a conference. Room was lovely, comfortable and affordable!!! Hotel staff was excellent - especially Francisco (bell man). He was so helpful and cheerful. Happy hour each evening was wonderful and breakfast buffet was very good.
They banquet food that was served for our conference as exceptionally good. Often times that food is a little below par. However, it was hot, delicious and served quickly. We couldn't have been more satisfied.
Your stay with Hotel Contessa should be a delight - Riverwalk location was great!

It is difficult to find the entrance to this hotel and the lobby is so dark its like you've entered a night club. Occasionally there are what appeared to be doormen and other times there wasn't anyone about. When we arrived, admittedly a little early to check in, there was only - member of staff checking people in and we had quite a wait before we could leave our bags downstairs and go out. The room we were given was on the -th floor at the very end of the corridor. Considering it was reasonably high up it was still very noisy all night with trucks going by and a lot of street noise. The room was quite small but fine for the - of us with a large flat screen TV, a desk, room for both of our bags and the bathroom was adequate with nice toiletries although the shower curtain didn't stop the water soaking the floor outside the shower. I wouldn't stay here again - I know NYC hotels are expensive but I've paid the same price for much nicer rooms than this place. No tea-coffee making facilities but this seems common now in city hotels. Plenty of Starbucks, Dunkin Donuts and others around for drinks or breakfast.

I managed to get a great rate for two rooms for two nights thru Priceline for $-- a night. The location of this hotel was great, and we were very satisfied with our stay. The staff went out of their way to be pleasant and helpful. Being greated with free martinis was a nice touch. The room itself was average sized and very clean. Loved the shower. We used the fitness room several times, and also the pool. The fitness room had state of the art equipment and also they supplied you with free fruit and bottled water during your workout. Our daughter enjoyed the swimming pool and informed us that the temperature was *just right*. We did not eat at the hotel and instead walked across the street and ate at the Cheescake Factory. We did hit the hotel bar for a nightcap. Average prices on the drinks. A nice little bar. The couple traveling with us were also impressed with this - star hotel and we all felt that with a little work, this hotel could get a - star rating. A great stay in a great hotel.

I stayed on business for - nights and was pleased with the great location and nice view of the river from my room (#--- - odd numbered rooms on my floor had river views). The bed was great, but the room definitely could have used updating and some attention to details (i.e., one the faucet in the bathroom was set up strangely so you had to turn the handle to the right to get hot water, but the cold water was set up fine - strange). Nothing that was a deal killer though. 
While I was here my phone disappeared while I was in the lobby and various staff in the hotel ranged from very helpful (concierge) to downright rude (front desk) when I asked if it had been turned in by any guests. DO NOT have the hotel store your luggage. When I picked up my luggage before heading to the airport the bellman could not find it and there was also general chaos with people taking luggage but not having their claim tickets checked by the staff. Bags were also kept out in a hallway and generally not secured. After the phone incident, I was not happy with this arrangement. It took about -- minutes for them to track down my bag. I hope that their management can improve their luggage storage situation when they have large groups in the future.

I just returned from my trip back to Baltimore. This was easily our favorite hotel during our vacation. The staff is absolutely the best. It is difficult to find great customer service today, but this place fits the bill.
From check-in to check-out, we have no complaints. The hotel is not in the middle of the tourist attractions, but it is a short ten minute walk. They also have a shuttle that can transport you to the Inner Harbor within a couple of minutes. Fells Point is a better area than the commercialized Inner Harbor anyway.
Stay here!

Great rooms (comfortable, clean and brand new). Great service. Great location. I have - important comments though: 
-) there's a firefighter post next door so you may not have that great sleep you are aiming for
-) I was woken up around - by the loud laughs and conversations of the cleaning ladies in the hall and the room next door... definitely something the managers need to pay attention to
Other than that, I had a wonderful stay and would recommend the hotel to other visitors.

This is a decent hotel, in a really good location. I have stayed at the Chancellor Hotel, and I would say that one was a little bit nicer. It is very close to Union Square, about a -min. walk. The thing we didn't like was that if you made a left outside of the hotel doors, you get to Union Square right away and it was nice, but if you made a left... wow, within --- blocks it's the really dirty part of San Fran, with bums, shelters, crack heads, etc. You don't see this near the hotel at all, but beware of going the wrong way. The staff was nice, the room was small, but clean, and the bathroom was tiny, but very clean. The things that sucked were: you get -- channels on cable, the bed is pretty hard, the rooms without a view aren't as nice, and lastly, there is a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Fusion Lounge-Club"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""basement?"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", which meant you could slightly feel the vibrations from the music (boyfriend had hard time sleeping). Overall, it was clean, had a good location, and was a good price. Good for a younger crowd, but my parents would've preferred something a little quieter... Oh, and parking sucked, research lots, and you can find one for $-- nearby, or you pay --+. Get a muni pass for --.-- (-day) also, so you can ride public transportation unlimited, or its $- one way everytime you ride something

The reviews of this hotel are right on. This hotel is quiet, clean and the staff is very helpful. I had read reviews stating the hotel's complimentary snacks included Haagen-Dazs, but I wasn't really expecting that to be the case. I was wrong! This hotel provides complimentary snacks well above what most hotels provide. I booked online through expedia and received a lower rate than offered on the hotel's website. This is a great hotel!

My wife and I stayed a night at the HIE Rivercenter and were satisfied with the stay. The hotel itself is very easy to find and parking was very convenient. The building looks new, and the interior is very clean and has nice decor. The location is definitely a no thrills area, and I probably wouldn't walk to the river walk even though it's not too far. However, there is a very nice complimentary shuttle service that leaves the hotel every -- mins and picks you up from designated spots in the river walk once you've called. All the employees we encountered during our stay were very helpful and friendly. The room itself was pretty standard, but exceptionally clean. I have a neurotic habit of thoroughly inspected my room, sheets, and mattress and could not find even a hair. The breakfast served in the lobby was above the standard continental type, a few of the options were warm cinnamon rolls, cheese omelettes, and biscuits and gravy. Definitely not gourmet, but certainly edible. There was a small pool and a hot tub outside the hotel.
 All together, I would recommend this hotel for families looking for a more affordable option. The location is close to the freeway (easy access to the local theme parks at a central location) and it's easy to find, and the parking is free. I wouldn't recommend this for a romantic stay.

I stayed in this hotel one night for a conference. I have stayed in many embassy suites and I like them. However, this one had a larger room then the others I had stayed in along with ceiling to floor windows. It was very clean. The check in, housekeeping, and breakfast staff were all very friendly and had smiles on their faces. The breakfast was great. I often stay at hotels on Pacific Hwy prior to flying out in the morning at Seatac, I think this will be my new hotel of choices.. Kudos to them.

Loved the location, so convenient
Free shuttle - just ask at desk - around town made it even easier
Hotel is cozy and the fireplace was a treat :) They are re=doing a lot of things but the room we had was really nice, flat screen tv, - double beds, microwave and fridge
Nice and clean
Pool and hot tub had too many kids in it ...my one complaint would be that they should kick the kids out in the evening at some point ...I never used them
Breakfast was tasty and ample
Best part was the staff...shout out to Tammy..what a sweetheart
John C Hart Jr, the assistant director was wonderful, helped us with shuttle, transport
arranged for - of the gals in my party to return to hotel from cruiseport to hold luggage and take them to airport as they had late night flights, very reasonable for $-- for - 
John C Hart Jr provided us such good service, so helpful, he really is proud of Seattle and this hotel and I just want to say he was the best. Thanks for a great stay,
would tell others to stay here every time

The Four Points is a lifesaver that is nicer than it has to be. Its central location,constant,courteously staffed shuttles to LAX,and it's awesomely priced --hr secured parking for hotel guests is wonderful. There are decent places to get a drink, steak, snack or latte. Shoeshine,laundry etc is all there and efficent. Hotel staff were all kind and never seemed to be idle in lobbies,rooms,restaurants or public lounge areas. Many foreign children and parents had the patient help of the entire staff in keeping toddlers from escaping as parents checked in-out or struggled with more than one child. Not luxurious by any means, but a very unexpected surprise.

Enjoyed our stay at the Casablanca. Service was excellent. Staff was very attentative and friendly. Lots of nice amenieties that you don't get elsewhere. Complimentary wine and cheese reception from --- pm daily. Parking next door to hotel. Great location. Would definitely recommend to family and friends

This Hilton one of the best I have stayed, very comfortable and accommodating. Rooms are specious and clean, elevators are fast, and all are working, receptionists are attentive and efficient, parking is convenient, gym is well equipped and open until midnight. The only observation that you need to be aware of that the local restaurant is empty as there are a lot of very nice restaurant in the shopping district on the opposite side of highway. The breakfast is average, nothing exciting; but overall it is a very nice choice for the business travelers. The Central Market and Whole Foods is a short driving distance.

Stayed here for - nights on our -- day tour of the Western US. The place was picked almost purely from the reviews on this website, and we weren't disappointed. Although we had no upgrade and a view of the car park, the Inn is excellent. A short walk across the island gives fantastic views of the San Diego skyline, my camera was busy. Didn't eat in the hotel, we went to the Red Sail Inn a short distance away for breakfast. It's cheaper and it too has lovely harbour views. The Bali Hai restaurant on the island is superb. We were given a window seat with a nightime view of San Diego, absolutely stunning, and it's not expensive either.

I booked the Hilton due to the location and as the days got closer and I checked reviews I was getting nervous, and thought I had made a mistake. Well, I didn't. From the time we entered the lobby til the time we checked out it was nothing but a wonderful experience. The rep at check-in was very accomidating, my brother who was visiting from Ga. asked if they had a room with a view and she said with a smile as a matter of fact I do. We were given a corner room with a view of Central Park. The room was spotless not even a stain on the carpet and done very tastefully. Maybe we were given an updated room, but it was very nice. We went to the concierge a couple of times and again very accomidating. I did not find the lobby to be extremely large, if you find this lobby to be large you haven't stayed in Atlantic City or Vegas. The location was perfect for visiting Rockerfeller Center, St. Patricks, and Radio City, only a couple of blocks away. The subway was only a block away and Central Park - blocks away. All in All it was a very pleasant stay and I would stay there again and recommend it to anyone wanting to stay in the area.

We had a great stay at the Newbury Guest House. We were able to walk to the Aquarium, which was a little bit of a hike, through the Public Garden and Boston Common, but it was a nice walk. 
Later we were able to shop at Anthropologie which was close, amongst many, many other shops. And we finished the day with some very good Sushi, which was also close. 
We were also able to park behind the hotel for $---night. Not bad, considering we thought about parking at the Aquarium on our way in which would've cost us $-----. Crazy!
One amazing thing, was that I left my personal wi-fi device in the window when we checked out. Headed down --, I was called, and they took my address and mailed my device to me, which was waiting when I got home. Very cool.
Seth

One need only read management’s surly responses to the less-than-stellar reviews to get a good feel for the Blue Moon experience. Staff is eccentric, inhospitable, lacking in grace, and they view their establishment through rose-colored glasses. I can attest to the veracity of the poor reviews; believe them. Granted, the views are great, the morning bagels are yummy, and you won’t find many other NYC hotel rooms this spacious, but these attributes are equally matched by serious lapses. The beds, pillows and linens are sub-par for a hotel at this price, and the toilets don’t flush – definitely not a low-flow-environmental issue. The common lobby area, where a meager continental breakfast is available, is grimy – sticky floors, finger-print covered glass tables and dust. It simply was not clean. Management seems to take pride in the museum-like quality of their establishment, touting the art, the history and the preservation – all very cool. But the Blue Moon is, after all, a hotel and a hotel exists to care for its guests. The Blue Moon isn’t horrible; it would be a decent place to stay if rates were quite a bit lower. But travelers looking for “luxurious” and “lavish” accommodations (descriptions found on their website) will be disappointed.

We actually had a really nice stay here. We loved the architecture in the Old Jail part of the hotel, and we decided to stay in a room in this section for this reason. The exposed brick wall was a nice effect, we had a large floor to ceiling window overlooking the Charles River and Beacon Hill, the bathroom was really nice, and the bed was so comfortable. However, if you stay on a Thursday through Saturday night, the lobby rotunda becomes a very loud nightclub, and the noise was heard loudly in our room until about - am. Luckily we had gone to a show and then stopped for a drink so we didn't get back to the room until -- or so, so we only had to suffer for - hours. Next time I would stay in the tower section. You would not hear any of the noise from there.

Other than the high price, I found this hotel to be everything I wanted: excellent customer service, large room, comfortable beds, sofa, micro & fridge, super free hot breakfast, indoor pool & hot tub, etc. Instead of an adjustment on the A-C there was a thermostat on the wall & I did have to ask them to send someone to fix it. The houseman arrived within the -- minutes they said it would take & fixed it quite quickly. This was a very nice place to stay for several nights.

I'm very pro keeping old buildings around, so was happy to stay in this renovated hotel. My bedroom and bathroom were immaculate, the continental breakfast was great and very well presented, and the free bottle of red wine in my room was certainly appreciated. The elevator (a frequent topic in this hotel's reviews) worked fine, but is """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""vintage"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" so a bit slow and with weight limits. (The sign says - people or --- pounds total, so those need to be - SLIM people!) The location was great and the receptionist was professional yet did smile as well (another complaint in reviews). 
The bar on the second floor seemed very lively on Friday evening, and very quaint and charming, but the noise certainly didn't reach me on the -th floor. That said, the walls are thin, though this is a problem at many hotels. Bring ear plugs! My room had a wall mounted TV, a very modern bathroom, and a pigeon outside the window to gently croon to me. The bedding and bed were awesome. On the down side, there wasn't a peephole on my door or any chain lock, the room is a bit dim at night or with the blinds drawn, and the hall? Let's just say it reminded me of the hotel hall in the Tower of Terror at Disneyland! But it was so funky as to be charming, in its own way, which is overall my impression of the hotel. A little funky and not for those who are only happy with new hotels, but a very reasonable and enjoyable place to stay close to Union Square and China Town. I walked to my class in the Business District, and to the Ferry Building on Saturday morning for the Farmer's Market. Hope to stay here again!

We have been staying at the Farmer's Daughter for several years now and love it. The rates are reasonable and the location is great. It's in the middle of LA and right across the street from the fabulous Farmer's Market and the Grove. The rooms are spacious and clean. They have free internet access and great bathroom amenities.
We haven't visited since they opened their restaurant, TART, but I'm excited to try it. How many other """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""motels"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" have on-site restaurants?
It IS annoying to pay for valet parking when for most rooms you have to walk through the parking lot anyway but I understand why they have to have it. The lot has fewer spaces than rooms and valet parkers can park cars closer together to save room. Also, they needed to have valet parking in order to get the liquor license for the restaurant. Also, in order to get into the parking lot, you have to go through a gate which closes off the rooms to the street. The valet parkers have some sort of remote that opens and closes the gate. Having the gate there makes me feel safer.
We've stayed in the No Tell Room which has a king size bed, a wet bar and a mirror on ceiling. I liked it but found it was a little dark. We've also stayed in their regular rooms. On our next visit, we will stay in a suite because we need more room with our baby daughter.

Best parts: free wine, cheese and hors d'oeuvres from -:---- in the evening, free breakfast, free internet, right at Union Square. The room was cozy, clean, nicely decorated, and quiet. Nice queen size bed (we got the least expensive room). Front desk staff very helpful. The parking garage for the hotel is on Mason, less than a block away.

I recently stayed at the St. Giles - The Court and I must say that I enjoyed every minute of my stay. The room was spacious and clean and the huge walk-in closet made me wish I brought more luggage! Additionally, from check-in to check-out the staff was extremely friendly and and made me feel right at home. If you have not stayed at the St Giles - The Court (or its sister property St Giles - The Tuscany) i highly recommend you do so the next time you visit New York...great hotel in a very nice section of town.

It is a nice hotel in a convenient location - it should be a good place for a business stay. But there were way too many kids with no supervision running wild. The staff was certainly tolerant of them. Considering that Doubletree charges for Internet in the rooms but makes wireless available in public spaces, those public spaces should be civilized enough to do some work....
But wait, there's more. The last night of my - night stay, a fire alarm at -:-- am sounded - and it was really a fire - I have no idea what caused it. Everyone was very calm -- the staff a bit too calm -- I never heard a word from them or saw them budge from their normal desk standing position - eyes down to the counter ignoring the sleepy huddled masses. I decided to huddle in my rental car. It was an hour and a half before the pajamaed people in the car next to mine told me it was okay to return.
It's good the alarm worked, but I won't be rushing back to this hotel anytime soon.

We chose the Westin Times Square specifically based on the good reviews here at Trip Advisor. We stayed for - nights in a Club level room (----) which was a larger corner room. It does not have amazing views being relatively low on the --th floor. As for city noises, it was quiet enough. We heard sirens every now and then but not """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""regular"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" traffic noise. 
The Club lounge (on -th floor) is not extraordinary.......it offers a continental breakfast (only warm item was oatmeal) and then an evening hors d'oeuvres offering, which was much better. Free teas, coffees and soft drinks are available all day long. 
The location of the hotel is excellent........it really is in the thick of it, and maybe even too much for our tastes. Times Square was crazy crowded even just to cross through to get to other midtown locations. There are lots of dining choices, movie theatres and subway stations just out the hotel doors. We normally would stay at the Rihga but it is now """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""The London"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and not family friendly any longer. We had - kids and this room had plenty of roll-around floor space for them. Each window had a window seat for looking out and they liked that. There is also one club chair and one desk chair. We ordered dinner room service and used the beds for seating purposes.
Hotel parking = $-- per day......the steepest we have ever paid in NYC.
My only real complaint is that the bathroom door is glass and anytime someone turned on the light during the night or early morning, the room was lit up as a result. I called for a night light but there were none. A night light would easily fix the problem. The double roller blinds do an excellent job of making the room dark.
Enjoy your stay.

My wife and I just stayed there for our - year anniversary, as we did on our wedding night. We aren't rolling in it, but this is a very good occasional stay in a couple's life-marriage. My wife loves the whole stay and experience of The Adolphus.

We changed our reservation to the Omni not long before we travelled and, boy, are we glad! The hotel was perfect for us in evrey respect. We initiallly were kept waithing for our room and, by way of apology, we were upgraded to a bay view room and were refunded the cost of our first night's accommodation! They knew it was our anniversary and sent up champagne and chocolate strawberries as well!
Now I know these things you would impact on my objectivity with this review but, honestly, even without these lovely touches, the hotel was beautiful. The restaurant was really nice as well and we had a laugh with the conciege who was very attentive. Pool and staff were great as well, The location was perfect for SD first timers. Looking out on to the bay, at the foot of the Gaslamp Quarter, walking distance to USS Midway, cruise terminals and, best of all attached to the ballpark! Cinncinatti were in town and I took the opportunity to watch my first ballgame. Go Padres!
All in all a wonderful five days at a great San Diego hotel.
Thanks Omni!

I was pleased with the hotel and staff. Rooms are clean. I would recommend the hotel to anyone traveling to memphis. Rooms are spacious and clean. Breakfast is good. Close to the airport so its not a far ride if your traveling.

We stayed here - nights in June. Everything was great. The roof terrace is wonderful and a lovely place to enjoy breakfast. We also enjoyed strolling around Gramercy Park. We have been to NYC many times but never stayed at this location. It is one of the best locations - convenient and peaceful.

Stayed at Aloft Tapestry Park for six nights. Great bed, friendly staff and awesome location. The room is basic but for travelling alone, it was an ideal size. The bar downstairs is ideal and is reasonably priced. I didn't have breakfast there as there was a Starbucks next door. The sushi store next door was awesome as was Mellow Mushrooms pizza.

I was put into this property by an airline due to a maintenance issue, although I checked in late at night and had to leave early the next morning, I saw enough that I want to return! The pool area, lobby and view from the balcony were very nice, not what I normally find when traveling and especially not this close to the airport!
From reading others reviews I was not in the main towers, and only complaint was only being on the second floor someone was above me and from the sound they made walking must have weighed --- pounds as it was very loud.
Other than that, I was greeted very nicely and professionally at the desk by a staff member that had a very irate customer on the phone, in spite of him trying his best from the portion of the conversation I heard, he continued to handle himself in a professional manner, then when he place the caller on hold to assist me, was very courteous and professional. As others have mentioned as well, who's night is not made better when checking in and receiving a warm cookie?
The room was nice, comfortable beds, good selection of pillows, nice TV channel selections (was no guide so I had to search for channels). The two sinks were nice (one in the bath portion and one by the closet) that would be a nice feature if traveling with your spouse or children. Also nice view of some trees out the balcony. While the wing I was in appeared to be older, you could tell they try to take care of it and it was very clean.
Overall, a very nice surprise, I have read on here it is best to request a room in the main towers, if not I would definatly ask to be on the top floor. I have also found that requesting rooms at the end of the hall are quieter.
I look forward to returning to this property with my wife and being able to spend more time in the city as well as what the doubletree has to offer!

My wife and I have stayed twice at this beautiful boutique hotel perched right at the top of Beacon Hill. The staff is very warm, friendly, and helpful — from the doormen who greet you upon arrival all the way through the concierge and front desk. The ever present availability of a free chauffeur driven car service is the icing on the cake. The rooms are very well appointed and the bedding in particular is great. If there is a downside to the hotel it is that few, if any, of the rooms have views of the nearby Boston Commons and Public Gardens, but that's pretty much par for the course in this area of town. If you want the views you'll have to stay at the Four Seasons which literally fronts the Commons and the Gardens.

We stayed in San Antonio for three nights and were coming into Austin to visit friends for an evening and then on to Wimberley to the zip line tour. 
There were some great prices available on this location. I have to travel to Austin frequently for work, but am not able to stay downtown due to the high cost. This trip was for fun, and luckily it only cost $-- more to stay downtown than it did to stay further out. 
As a note, the $-- per night for parking (with Tax) is Excessive. The valets will tell you that there is no self parking, this is however NOT the case. Just go right past the valets, turn left on the next street and into a self park garage for $-- per night. 
The location of the hotel is great. The Roaring Fork meal is great and was a wonderful ambiance to meet with friends. Also, don’t miss the view from the second floor bar terrace. Well worth having a drink or two up there. 
The front desk upgraded us from a standard king to a nice corner suite overlooking Congress Avenue. It was a large beautiful room with a couch, desk, closet, and fluffy king bed. Actually this was the best bed I have had in a hotel in quite some time. The bathroom though small was well laid out and very comfortable. 
The one complaint I had about this room is that the TV was in such an awkward position that you can not watch the TV from the bed without playing twister. Also you can not see the TV from the desk. You can however watch from the couch. For a nice romantic night who needs the TV though. 
We did not try room service, nor partake of any of the high cost incidentals such as water, minibar, or internet access. (I have my own Verizon Card.) 
All of the staff we ran across was pleasant. I do not know what their workout facilities are like nor if they have a pool as this was a one night stay. 
I was a bit surprised that they did not upgrade us to the Executive level given I am a Priority Club Platinum, but I do know that Intercontinental has their Royal Ambassador program so maybe that is the reason. Given we were meeting friends for dinner and had breakfast plans off site; I did not push the issue. 
Great stay if you can get the right price. Beautiful historic hotel.

Managed to book a room on a discount deal for a family of four. The room was nice with comfortable beds and the location was near bus routes and easy walking distance to Magnificant Mile. A couple of resturants are available in the hotel but there are plenty resturant just a short walk from the hotel. If you have a car expect to pay high prices for parking.

There's not much more to say about the Hotel Burnham, but we love it just like the rest of the reviewers here. I think it's a great value for the location and everything else about the hotel. Service was great. The only downside was rooms don't have coffeemakers....however, when I asked one was sent to our room immediately. Restaurant was great for dinner and breakfast. This has become """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""our"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel in Chicago. Oh, you can't beat location on blue line of subway, which takes you right to OHare.

My husband and I recently spent the night at the Westin Galleria in order to finish Christmas shopping. The location was the deciding factor in our choice as we normally stay at another Starwood property in Houston when we travel. Upon arrival I was a bit surprised to see the lack of decorations and the rather stark lobby. Check-in went quickly and while not overly friendly the staff was adequate and proficient. When shown to our room, ----, I was surprised to see the condition. Shabby, dated and dirty are all an apt descriptions. Peeling wallpaper, dated furniture, dirty and stained carpets ruined whatever good first impression was made by the staff. The in room mini-bar wasn't operating nor were the coffee machine condiments stocked. The internet connection was not set up for a readily available connection as is standard. In the majority of the Westin's we have stayed you can find an extra pillow in the closet, this had none. Also, the automatic climate control was not functioning properly, leaving the room uncomfortable. During our years as Starwood Preferred Guest we have been happy if not thrilled with our stays in Savannah, New Orleans, Dallas etc sadly I can't say the same about this property, location seems to be the only advantage or incentive to visit. It goes without saying that this will not be a location that we desire to spend time in again. One wonders if Westin is aware of how far this once well maintained hotel has fallen and how it impacts the overall image of the chain.

My husband and I recently spent a week in Seattle and stayed at teh Mayflower Park Hotel. We loved the hotel and the location. The staff was very helpful, the hotel accommodating and very clean. We would definitely recommend this setting to anyone visiting the area.

From the time I checked in the service was wonderful. The time we spent here was wonderful with entertainment for the entire family. 
Ps. The Tequila bar is the best. Each bar tender was excelent.

Don't expect a lot of space, but this place has a great vibe and a cool atmosphere. I traveled to NYC over Thanksgiving weekend and paid $--- a night for a single room with a bathroom. I'm a middle-aged guy and found the double-bed thoroughly comfortable and the clientele (mostly young Europeans) fun to be around. The hotel is a --- to ---minute walk to Times Square, and there are many dining option, expensive and in-, nearby. The hotel bar is comfortable and friendly. The hotel staff is efficient and friendly enough.
A quibble: the room's temperature control was not up to snuff. The old, pre-renovation heating pipes made the room uncomfortable enough that I had to run the AC and-or open the window. And I didn't see the double-occupancy rooms, so I don't know how comfortable the accommodations would be for a duo.
Having said that, this is a hotel to which I'd certainly return and which I'd recommend to those on a shoestring budget.

The Grand Union Hotel isn't perfect, but we couldn't have been in at better place during the last -- days. The price is for that location more than good and what the most important thing is: The rooms we had have been really clean. The stuff was friendly and helped us when there was a problem. I will come back and recommand it to friends.

We booked a room at The Jewel for one night because we were visiting MoMA and going to a late-night show at NBC-Rockefeller Center, so it was the perfect location. 
The lobby is clean, but 'no-frills'. Check in and check out was quick and went smoothly. The room we booked (standard) was very clean, comfortable, well-appointed and roomy for Manhattan standards. This hotel is relatively new, so it has absolutely no signs of wear and tear. Our room didn't have a view (we knew in advance), but we didn't care because we weren't planning on hanging out in the room to look out the window. Wi-fi throughout the hotel was nice. There is a purified water system in the hallway with empty water bottles to fill and refill-- nice touch. For the price we paid, we were very satisfied with the hotel; especially because of the great midtown location.
The hotel does not have it's own restaurant, but there are plenty of great places in Manhattan so we probably would not have dined there anyway. They do have a relationship with a club two doors down for breakfast, lunch, dinner, but we didn't try it. There is a deli a couple doors down, handy for coffee-breakfast in the morning.

This is one of the nicest hotels I have ever stayed. Everything is top notch and immaculate. Service is above and beyond my expectation.

At the time we stayed in early January, the area felt a little deserted, but may have more atmosphere at other times of the year. Limited experience with the locals, and the mounted police (the kids wanted to stroke the horse) was very positive. 
There is a handy lift from the waterfront area up to Pike Place (the market) if you turn left out of the hotel past the fish restaurant you should find it on the left. Not sure how I would feel about walking around in this area late at night though, if necessary I would perhaps check with a local. It may feel better at a busier time of year.
In all the Marriott did feel homely when we were in a completely new place for such a short time.

I was absolutely in love with the look of this hotel. It is gorgeous, the rooms are comfy and clean, and it really feels like you are getting to stay in part of the history of LA. The price was very reasonable for the quality of the hotel.
BUT
The day we arrived there was some kind of MASSIVE event being hosted there (maybe a talent show). The whole place was crowded with teenagers, and I really do mean packed. We walked into very tired (and grumpy) from our journey to a very loud and packed lobby and could barely see the check in desk through the crowd of teens coming and going. There was also a herd of people about - deep waiting for the elevators.
I have been to hotel-conference centers etc. before, but have never previously felt like my enjoyment of a hotel was so severely impacted by its other activities. No the hotel shouldn't be expected to babysit its guests, but equally it does need to take responsibility for the comfort of all guests. Things that could have been done to improve our stay would particularly have included letting use use the service elevator to get to the room with our bags as we clearly couldnt fight our way into the standard elevators with them in the crowd, or implementing some kind of queueing system or reserving one carriage for guests not involved in the event. It would also have been nice if one of the staff had informed the teens when their behaviour was unreasonable (e.g. there was a group of boys practicing their drumming routine in the lobby the entire time we were checking in, and I couldn't believe a) that they thought it was appropriate in a public place, or b) that the staff didn't realise that this might be unpleasant for other guests and put a stop to it).
I initialy thought this may be a one off incident, but the next day the lobby was in similar chaos, and the talent competition had gone and been replaced with some kind of graduation party, so I really dont understand why the hotel wasn't better equipped to handle these situations. 
Given the scale of the event and the impact that it had on our quiet enjoyment of our hotel room, I actually think that the hotel should have put up a warning about the talent event on its website for these dates, as it really isn't something you expect and does seriously affect other guests looking for a quiet place to stay.

The hotel pool is heated and small for the number of people that frequent it, but its still a nice place to hang out and get a drink. My husband and I moved hotels because our original hotel was crowded and busy. The Omni was still busy, but had a more adult feel and we are eternally glad we moved. I would recommend the Omni time and again--it was a great """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""home station"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" from which we explored San Diego.

Let me start my review by explaining that I am not an experienced big city traveler and I usually stay in chain hotels in the suburbs. So my whole experience at this boutique hotel was a first for me, and I often felt like a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""yahoo from the sticks"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Thank goodness the staff is so professional they didn't make me feel uncomfortable. I'm sure I didn't tip the right amounts, sorry.
Your first impression of the hotel is quiet elegance. Then your stress level is greatly lowered when you see the famous brown lab Maverick sprawled out in his bed in the lobby. (he tolerates pats and picture taking). I asked for a quiet room so I was given one overlooking a central area instead of the street. The room was amazing, I don't know what others expected as to size, but I thought it was the same as any other hotel, although the bathroom is a little small. But that is all overcome by the sheer comfort and deluxe decor (although a wall of mirrors is a little retro). The bed was heaven, so plush you climb up into it. Nice reading chair, small desk, flat screen tv on the wall. They allow you to use the honor system mini bar as a refrigerator, which was helpful. I never heard another quest, no slamming doors, no loud a-c unit, just peace and quiet. 
Location was a little inconvenient if you wanted to go downtown to Union Square area or out to Golden Gate Park, took me my whole stay to figure out the buses. Hotel is at the Ferry Building, and the trolley up to Pier -- runs close by. There really aren't any inexpensive eating places or mini marts nearby. 
What makes this hotel so unique is the staff. Dulce was on duty when I had an issue with an internet charge (I used the computer in the lobby and the directions were not clear as to how to get the -- minutes free), she promptly reversed the charge and didn't make me feel like a cheat or liar. I asked about an airport shuttle, they arranged for the pick up (am I supposed to tip for that??) After I got home I completed an on line survey from the hotel and mentioned an error in my final bill of about $-.--, which I wasn't going to hassle with. The manager sent me an email saying he had investigated the charge and was crediting my charge card; now that is service. When I told Dulce she was as famous on Trip Advisor as Maverick, she thought that was the greatest thing ever.
If I come back to San Francisco I would definitely stay here again, now that I have the buses figured out.

We were staying in Phoenix to watch the D-backs and only needed a place to rest. The room was clean and only a - min walk to the tram which dropped you off downtown. The room was a little noisy as the airport is close but its the freight train which you really noticed. That said for $-- a night you can't complain. It was --- degree so leave the a-c all night.

This has been so far the worst hotel that I have been to this year. I was very concerned when I waited in line and watched each check in staff member act as car salesmen. They insisted that everyone """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""upgrade"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" ranging from a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""romance package"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""internet package"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""city view package"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", etc. I was amazed to see people accepting some of these sales tactics too. Basically you pay for everything at this hotel - Internet, pool, gym, business center, parking, etc. Nothing is included in your rate here.
The lobby is open. However, the water feature wasn't working and appeared that it needed some major repairs. The carpets in the lobby needed to be replaced. The elevators were very, very rough - all banged up as people have stated here.
In regards to checking in, I refused the upgrade and still wound up on the --th floor with a city view. Reading through some of these reviews, the rooms must not be of the same quality. My room had two queen beds. The carpets were stained everywhere. I asked for a different room but was denied because there were no others available. I wouldn't walk on the floors without my shoes. I just couldn't believe how bad the carpets were.
The furniture was all beat up - so worn that it looked like it was about to fall apart. The baseboards in the room were in terrible shape. There was at least an inch thick of dust on all the lights - especially the one above the TV.
The bathroom was the only thing that was nice. It had been updated and was very nice. Bath products were a brand from London. Water pressure was strong. No complaints about the bathroom.
The location is not very good. It is on the edge of a bad part of town. Be prepared to be bothered by people when entering and exiting the hotel. I saw a person get forced out of the Starbucks that is attached to the hotel lobby.
Overall, my room was terrible. I was not impressed by the hotel staff because they insisted that everyone upgrade to a better room. This is not a luxury hotel by any means. Stay clear of this. If you do deiced to stay here, make sure you ask to view your room first before accepting it. Enter this hotel with caution.

Wonderful hotel. Fantastic rooms, great food, great service, but a good -- minutes from the city. We stayed overnight before heading to Rockys and had hoped to see something of Denver -- but it's just too far out. The hotel itself is great though and the service is second to none. The free shuttle from the airport is great -- just make sure you call ahead for it. If you get lucky you'll get Casey on his one day a week driving it.

The Crescent is exactly like I expected with the added bonus that it was close to everything. It is an older hotel so it has many of the quirks like a slow elevator that really only accommodates two due to weight limits. We were on the -th floor and down was not issue but we waited for the elevator to go up. 
There is no AC so we had windows open which was fine for the room temp but did make it noisy. 
This is not a modern hotel, but if you want character (it looks just like posted pictures) and location, give it a try. 
We were a couple of blocks from Chinatown, Union Square, and Nob Hill. A safe neighborhood all in all. There were tons of great places to eat.
Breakfast was fresh and plentiful. We skipped it and walked down to one of the amazing French bakeries. 
We would stay here again.
very accommodating staff at a beautiful, older hotel; architecture-furnishings period perfect. good dining experiences; efficient services all around; no ice machines.

I had high expectations for a Starwoods hotel, but check in process killed it. Although it's great that they allow late check out until -pm, check in time is at - so we had to wait over an hour for our rooms to be ready - luckily we had a group checking in for us so the bride never knew we had issues! The manager on duty said she would send us - bottles of champagne for our troubles but they didn't arrive until we called for them - hours later. The rooms (specifically the cool corner rooms) are fantastic but their check out policies should change. Two corner rooms cost over $---- so be prepared to shell out for this new posh hotel. Lighting in the hotel is not conducive to applying make up, and showers have see-through doors, but we made it work. Overall great hotel & location, hopefully some things change to make it even better!

Was pleasantly surprised by how large and roomy the rooms were. So much space, very clean & in a quiet & very safe area close to all the action. Within walking distance to empire state, central station, Rockefeller, MoMa. Very helpful front desk staff. Beautiful lounge in the foyer where we could chill out & use the free wifi. Loved the roof top bar-view of the empire state & Chrysler. Super comfy beds too! Thanks Affinia shelburne for an amazing - night stay!

The hotel is in a good location just opposite quincy market, and the staff is helpful and friendly. Our room had a good size however it smelled very stongly of smoke. Reading the reviews we did not seem to be the only one having had this problem. They could not move us in a different room as the hotel was full and they did not seem too surprised either when we reported the circumstance. Also i have to say that the breakfast staff was not particularly professional.

I just returned from a stay at The Knickerbocker and it was fantastic. The staff is incredibly attentive and the location is outstanding. I loved the Martini Bar and all of the food was really good too. The concierge helped me plan each day of my stay and I was able to maximize my Chicago visit. I would highly recommend this hotel and will definitely return!

This hotel is quiet, near the shopping area (you can enter in a - level NORDSTROM shopping from the hotel elevator), has a correct fitness center, and very good rooms. Try the ---- room, for the king size bed. The service is awesome, with polite and helpfull staff.

I've stayed in this hotel many a times when I travel. It costs a little more than the usual Courtyards I stay at (see my history), but the main Marriot branch definitely has its perks. 
This location has the most comfiest of beds (equivalent to other chain's heavenly bed). 
Spacious and modern lobby and I can't say enough about it's close proximity to Ohare and highway access. This last time I stayed, I can see that nearby parking lot is for train access , though I always rent a car. 
I would stay here more often if budget permitted, though sometimes rates can be comparable to local Courtyard establishments.

This is more like an upscale inn with really small rooms and narrow corridors and with the price you pay for the name Hilton, you would wanna pay a little more and upgrade to one of the many full service hotels nearby.

All the rooms are being re-fitted and we were well pleased with ours, small ,basic but very comfortable. The location is right in the middle of Little Italy with numerous Italian restaurants and the Saturday market on your doorstep.
Car parking in the basement was a bonus as street parking seemed difficult
Hotel Mela is a wonderful boutique hotel in Times Square. We were stranded here during the blizzard, but they made our stay so comfortable and pleasant. Will definitely book in the future.

The Gild Hall has rooms of reasonable size, particularly in New York. This was my second stay at the Gild Hall. Although the rooms are reasonably sized by New York standards, they can be quite dark, particularly on low floors. I find the service here to be quite variable in quality. For example, I found it difficult to get through to room service on the phone. One day I had to call room service-the front desk - times before I was able to connect to room service. Room service did not pick up the phone, so the calls went to the front desk. The front desk promised at least two times that they would have room service call me, which did not occur until I had called - times. It took me over an hour to connect to room service and about -.- hours to get my food. This all occurred at approximately - pm in the afternoon.

Full disclosure: I'm a repeat guest and I believe the experience at this hotel is better when one visits multiple times, but even so, for a first time visitor, this should be a stellar experience. Professional staff, good sized rooms, well-equipped, great views. Overall, my preferred location in Boston for business travel. Only downside I can think of is that it's not the closest walking distance to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""everything"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", but it is still walking distance to most things, as Boston is a small place.

Just got back from a three night stay at the Queen Anne.
First impression of the front desk after two flights and a cab ride: not the most welcoming, unfortunately.
We got in the elevator which had a padded bench and chandelier (very cool) and got to our room. It was a funny old type of key (like a braille reader) which we put in. I loved the room; it was so old style with the decor, heavy drapes, reds everywhere, claw food tables and chairs; I loved it.
There was no attention to detail, however, in things that had been """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""repaired"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" such as a large paint redo in the bathroom that was very uneven (I know it's old, but if you're going to fix it, do it right!). And you could see that the doorhandle on the door had been moved,but it was never properly painted and filled over.
Our room faced the street and the windows rattled all night, which woke us up many times through the night. It was also freezing in our room (early September?) so we woke up being cold as well, even with the heater on.
Breakfast was about what I expected; very simple- hard boiled eggs, cereal, coffee (no cream, only milk), muffins (storebought) and oatmeal, bread and bagels. It was fine as I knew ahead of time, but by day three it was a little tiresome.
Tables were not cleared off quickly, yet there was a box for """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""tips"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Not sure what that was for since I never saw anyone actually working in the dining area. I had to clear a table myself to sit down.
Never made it to have sherry or afternoon tea, but got a yummy cookie later on.
Loved the decor, the feel of the place, but there were a few minor things I would not come back for.
The concierges were both great. Very outgoing and helpful.
Charming and quaint for sure!
PROS: unique place to stay, historic. Free breakfast. Prices don't break the bank.
CONS: cold rooms, noisy room (ours was), breakfast is mediocre, not very close to downtown.

We stayed at the James Hotel for a long weekend and it did not disappoint us. The hotel location is ideal. We were able to walk to everything from the hotel without taking a cab, with the exception of a couple of restaurants in the evening (nice clothes, heals -it's better to take a cab than to rough it!). The concierge at the hotel was very helpful with restaurant reservations - he was able to get us a table at the famous Charlie Trotter's restaurant with only a couple days notice.
I'd say the typical clientele at this hotel was younger (-----s). There was a lot of energy at the hotel during cocktail hour with the bar being packed every night. Even though the bar-lobby was very popular it collectively had a low key vibe that made it very inviting and comfortable. We will definetly try this hotel again with our next trip to Chicago!
RESTAURANT NOTES:
Charlie Trotters: Although the service was exceptional, and the food cooked perfectly, the taste was nothing exceptional and we found that it was not worth the price or rave reviews this establishment has received over the years (we are foodies and are more than willing to pay for great food).
Japanais: Asian Fusion and Sushi restaurant. Very trendy decor, good food, and romantic ambience. I wouldn't classify this as an authentic asian experience, but it was a fun restaurant that I would attend occasionally if I lived in Chicago.
Le Lan: Smaller Vietnamese restaurant a short walk from the hotel. Intimate decor and ambience and excellent food. If you enjoy a non commercial dining experience and Asian food, this is a good choice while in Chicago.
TRU: Very Expensive, but in my opinion woth every penny. We went to TRU many years ago and I still remember it like it was yesterday. The service is second to none ( I had a chair for my purse, and I was escorted to the bathroom - a little over kill, I admit). The waiter to customer ratio for us was -:- for serving the food; we had - in our party. The waiters placed and took away are plates perfectly choreographed as a team. The food was excellent, but not the best I've had. If you want a unique experience with one of the highest rated restaurants in the country this is a solid choice.

Spent a week here for a conference, which I was kept busy working on so didn't leave the premises from Monday morning till Friday night. That wasn't a problem though, as the place is vast and seems to have just about everything one could need. The imposing marble of the lobby is made more human by some quirky artworks, and initial impressions of the staff were warm, friendly and helpful. This was kept up throughout our time there, with every employee I encountered proving both dedicated and personable. Even staff in the bar managed to keep calm and smiling, despite the nightly deluge of conference attendees demanding beer after long sessions.
Food in the restaurant and provided for the conference was decent, and fairly varied too with nice themes for the lunches laid on; breakfast was lovely in the restaurant with a good varied buffet, and not bad if a little restricted when laid on for the meetings. The room we had was a suite and thus, in true Dallas style, absolutely massive, but the bathroom was oddly small, not much bigger than the walk-in closet. Beds were very comfortable.
Among other services, the outdoor, rooftop pool looked great and was apparently very nice, sadly no time to try it myself; likewise the gym I only peeped in at, but I heard from several colleagues that there were problems with many machines not working. This reflects my only issue with the hotel - it could do with a visit from the maintenance fairy, with lots of little jobs needing doing - wobbly shower rails, sticky doors, aged light fittings bodged together with bits of wire etc. nothing terrible, but enough to give the grandeur of the place a rather faded air. 
All in all a solid and impressive place which most people, or at least those who can afford the fairly steep prices, should find thoroughly satisfactory.

The location is not bad being residential and quiet, and close to """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Little Italy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" area of town. The rooms are clean but nothing special. The hotel service leaves to be desired. When I arrived, the key to my room didn't work, and it took me - trips to the reception desk, to get them to fix the problem. I didn't feel a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""welcome"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" feeling in this place, so I was glad when I left.

Average hotel. Nothing bad, but nothing great. The typical decent hotel you would find on the side of an expressway.
Definately can't find anything within walking distance but if you have a car, Austin's South Congress neighborhood is fairly close, maybe -- mintues, another -- mintues up and you're downtown. They have a gym but it's lacking at best. I ended up asking is there was a trail or sidewalk to run and the front desk sent me to a path behind the Best Buy down the street (not a good idea).
I stayed here for about a week and did not have any problems, however my colleague's whole reservation was moved, then canceled. He ended up telling them not to bother getting him a room and he stayed at a friend's in town.
The rooms were good, average, and decently clean. Mine had a bad smell for the first couple days but you run in to that every now and then.

Felipe took care to see that we enjoyed our stay! Our room had a balcony and a great view of the river! Excellent staff! Special touches made the stay a great experience! If you are celebrating a special occasion, this is the place to come!!!

Although the Argonaut Hotel is on Fishermans Wharf which is fine if you want to pay high prices and be amongst loads of tourists - our stay there was poor and our holiday was very nearly spoilt because of the hotel . Firstly when we checked un they asked for a credit card - we only had a debit card - they said that they would need to take --- dollars per night as security and this would be taken from our card along with international charges and not credited until - days after we had left - they said this was standard wherever you go in the world - we have travelled alot and NEVER have we had this! We ended up having to give --- dollars cash deposit - and the receptionist stating that she was doing us a favour!
Our room was clean and large but the walls were paper thin - you could hear everything - and that is no exaggeration.It was really embarrassing at times and we had to bang on the adjoining walls to tell our neighbours to shut up !
We were left a bottle of wine in the room one evening to apologise for excess noise but this did little to compensate for the discomfort.

Had the misfortune of staying at the hotel during a Panthers v Dallas football weekend. Needless to say, noises in the middle of the night were pretty bad. The rest of the stay was fine, however. Excellent service. Comfy bedding. My only complaints were how expensive it was at breakfast (no buffets included here), no small refrigerator in the room, and a way overpriced - oz. of wine in the Champions Bar.

Ok, the hotel is under a huge renovation and yes, the lobby is a mess, elevators are not in the level of the floor ( be careful!), noisy etc etc BUT once you are in your room it wasn´t that bad ....
I stayed three nighst with my two best friends on a shopping trip. The beds are really comfortables, the room was clean, had a cofee maker (great way to start the day!) and the noises began at -:---- am just when we were going out to have breaksfast and go shopping.
