Location is excellent, you ARE in the Galleria so you spend your day shopping and just walk to your room to leave your bag and continue shopping :)
For lunch-dinner there were a lot of options, just be sure to get dinner early, most of them closed at ----pm (I am mexican so we had dinner veeery late, the first night we almost miss dinner!)
Next trip we´ll try the Derek or maybe the Aria in Woodlands (beatiful neigborhood with a lot of shops and restaurants)

I've have stayed in multiple hotels in San Francisco but this was my first time in the W. I was not overly impressed with the rooms, however the service was by far the best. From the moment I checked in, up until my departure I was extremely pleased with the level of service. The entire staff was super friendly and helpful. Two individuals left a lasting impression, the first was Sebastian, loved his accent but even more so his friendly demeanor, interest in what we thought of our stay and willingness to assist. The lobby lounge was very cool and we spent quite some time there hanging out. Mary provided an excellent service, friendly conversation and always made sure we were happy. I definitely will be staying there on my next visit.

They advertise that they have free airport shuttle service. They don't. On arrival, they told us to take a taxi for which they would pay. They did. But when we had to go back to the airport the next moring, we had to wait for more than -- minutes. The worst thing was the room itself. It was a two story suite, with a second bedroom upstairs. When we arrived late at night, all the lights were on inside, including the upstairs bedroom. Freaked us out. Then we discovered we couldn't lock the door. It had been forced open sometime in the past, and the metal lock plate on the edge of the door was all bent so the dead bolt could not be extended. The other surface mounted lock had been ripped off also, and was dangling from the door. And to top it all off, none of the three phones worked at all. When we asked for another room, we initialy were told we would have to pay more. Eventually we got another room, but the whole experience was very unpleasant. Would never ever stay there.

My boyfriend and I stayed here complimentary of his work, so of course free is always nice. Prior to my arrival, my boyfriend had added me to his room so that i could get a key if he wasnt there. The front desk was rude and explained that although I was on the guest list for the room, that did not allow me a key as I was not on the original itinerary. Fair enough I suppose since this makes it more secure.
At any rate, the stay was enjoyable. The restaurant in the lobby has some killer food and drinks. Its in a great location if you are into the nightlife that San Diego has to offer. 
Be warned that although this is a great location, it is also close to downtown so you will experience more noise than you may be use to. Being from Vegas...im use to the noise.

We loved the hotel. As everyone has said, architecture and decor are beautiful. We found everyone to be friendly and helpful, our inside room quiet and very comfortable (we don't care about a small tv and never use minibars) and parking at the Pershing Square lot easy. Restaurant in the rotunda was good and the servers were so gracious . This is where I will stay on future visits to LA.

The hotel gets a very good review from me but the staff gets an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Excellent"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The front desk person named Henry checked me in on Tuesday evening and I could not have asked for a more welcoming and helpful front desk representative. When you're tired and just getting off a plane, a smiling face of greeting at the hotel really makes the difference. Well done to the management of the hotel for putting the right people at the front desk. The scheduled shuttle service was on time and the driver was very friendly. Excellent service all around.
Cons:
Fresh fruit at continental breakfast for Priorty Club Members was delicious but some Granola and some protein would be nice for those of us who need to watch our waistlines as it was a carb fest.
Hotel needs to be refurbished, it looks and feels dated.
Stayed here for a long weekend recently. Hotel staff was excellent. Room was very clean and comfortable. Good location for getting around Austin. Will stay here again!

fantastic location at a very good affordable price. It wasnt the ritz but cleaned room every day on suite heated floors in renovated rooms was brill. Coffee machine in reception only had selected times which was a pain as after a long day you want a hot drink in your room. Empire state building was a stones throw away.. Definatley would stay here again fantastic budget hotel.
Clean, comfortable, well-appointed, reasonable rate, excellent location, friendly and helpful staff. Would certainly go back when in Seattle again!

I wound up here because I have only a few days to find a hotel. The place is horrible. The bathtub didn't drain. Silverfish in the room (at least we didn't have the bedbugs other have reported). The bathtub has peeling paint. The room is not even close to the picture on the web site. The breakfast buffet is $--.-- per person. While they offer on site parking they don't offer a discount if you stay at the hotel so the cost is $--.--. It's the most expensive garage in the vicinity. The walls are the thinest that I have ever encountered to the point were I could hear the elevator bell that was -- feet away. There is also a club downstairs so the music keeps you awake all night.

We stayed at the Belvedere Hotel for - nights from -- Jan--- Jan. This was my -nd trip to NY in the past year. I previously stayed at the Comfort Inn on --th st & there is absolutely no comparison between the - hotels. The Comfort Inn is shabby, old and the rooms are small, the hallways & carpet are dirty. My expectations were thus low after my experience in The Comfort Inn, but the Belvedere passed my high standards with flying colours. For a few dollars more than The Comfort Inn, The Belvedere offers clean, comfortable accommodation in an excellent location. We had a large room with - double beds (advertised on the website as a delux room). The beds were very comfortable, the room huge & the fridge and microwave an added bonus. There was excellent shower pressure & the bathroom was a decent size. I would highly recommend this hotel to other travellers who are looking for a comfortable stay while on holidays. The only minor complaint I did have was that the room was really hot as it was quite mild during our stay for the time of year, however we opened the window a crack & this solved the problem somewhat. 
The subway is close by & all major attractions are within walking distance. We did not eat at the hotel but there are plenty of diners within minutes walk of the hotel. 
I will be staying at the Belvedere again on my next visit to the Big Apple and I would recommend this hotel to everyone.

Planning a weekend trip to Colorado to catch the Cubs and Rockies, I was surprised to get a terrific deal at the same hotel that the Cubs were staying. It was an awesome atmosphere from the fan aspect, and the hotel was terrific. The room was very comfortable, and the location couldn't be beat. The -nd floor bar had a lively crowd each night, and I felt the hotel staff was terrific in catering to our needs.

Room service is non existent. Don't even bother asking for a hot cup of tea, it's apparently unheard of in this hotel. I fell ill unfortunately towards the end of my stay and asked for some assistance loading my suitcases onto the trolley, however this apparently was too much to ask as well. I had to go downstairs to retrieve the - of - trolleys available. Then I had to load all the suitcases myself before waiting for an hour to check out because the hotel only has - people on staff on Sunday afternoon. Ridiculous. If you want quality customer service and convenience, do not book at this hotel. And I haven't even mentioned the appearance of the building - rooms. As the title states - you can find a better place to stay!

My Fiance & I have recently come back from our first trip to NY where we stayed at The Michelangelo. We loved it!! We were on the fourth floor facing -th and had no problem with noise and slept with no problems every night - probably due to the incredibly comfortable bed and being exhausted from sightseeing all day! We had a Junior Suite which was like having our own apartment and made all the difference to come back to and relax after a busy day. The aircon was also very welcome as NY was very hot during our stay!
We had no problems with the staff, who were very helpful when we needed it, or the fact that only pastries were served for breakfast - it was complimentary afterall....
I don't know how much our room cost as the entire holiday was a surpirse; booked by my 'other half' but he said it was excellent value for money for the location, size and comfort of the room and the hotel standard in general. I know that when we make a return visit to finish off our sightseeing (as we ran out of time!!) we shall definitely be staying at this hotel again.
Denise & Jon

The service was good though the hotel is right on Rosecrans making trific noise a problem. Otherwise, the hotel was nice and right near the fishing company we used. It was close enough to the beach and downtown to be good as well. I will stay there again in the future when another fishing trip occurs.

I just returned from spending three nights at the Mark Twain Hotel in San Francisco. It is classified as a boutique hotel, across from a Hilton, at the intersection of O'Farell and Taylor Streets, on the edge of the Union Square shopping district. I found a rate of $---night on BookIt, and took a chance because of others' favorable reviews. The Mark Twain has eight floors, about -- rooms to a floor. My room had two double beds and bathroom, both on the small side but adequate for my needs. Decorating has been updated and is pleasant on the eye. Beds were comfortable, check-in easy. Valet parking is available at $---night, about the average in this city, which I did not use as I easily found taxis across the street at the Hilton. The hotel is sited an easy four block walk to the Westfield Shopping Centre and a bit farther to all the grand shopping mecca at Union Square. I will certainly return to this hotel on my next visit to San Francisco to see my son, who does not have a guest room to host me.
As for the negative, I was there Thanksgiving holiday and found some usual features unavailable. For instance, the hotel's breakfast bar (for a $-- fee) was not available, and the highly rated adjacent Taylor Street Coffee Shop also had closed for the holiday period. Nor was housekeeping service available on Thanksgiving Day, hence no extra coffee was supplied for the in-room coffee pod machine.
But the place was clean, relatively quiet, and inexpensive. I asked for a room at the back of the hotel to avoid street noise and thus only had one noisy night when guests were in an adjacent room loudly talking in an eastern European language until -:--am.
The hotel provides free wi-fi but limited TV channels. If you're not going to stay much in your room--there is so much to see and do in San Francisco!--this is a good place to lay your head. Not perfect, but good enough. I felt safe to walk alone on the streets towards Union Square, but probably wouldn't walk far in any other direction. The Tenderloin is close by, and that has it's own disreputable reputation. You will see homeless people going about their business but not aggressively panhandling. I was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""awarded"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" this hotel through Hotwire based on a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Four Star"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" rating. However, once I learned I had recieved the Crowne Plaza, I researched the property and read the reviews. It is clear, with exceptions of Hotwire affiliated entities (Travelocity, Orbitz) and one or two independent entities, that the overall general public-professional opinion of this hotel is LESS than four stars. I immediately called Hotwire with my concerns, which were ignored. It was explained that this hotel was classified as four star based on the amenities available and even though the Crowne Plaza is listed as an example of a three star hotel on Hotwire's own site, the rates are assigned to individual properties, not chains. So, i was disimissed and told if I encountered problems during my stay, let them know. Even following further complaints and a letter from my attorney, Hotwire refused to refund or change the accomodation. Needless to say, I don't recommend Hotwire either.
We were forced to stay at the Crowne Plaza rather than pay for two hotels. So, let me start with the only positive thing about our stay, the hotel staff was very friendly. Check in and check out was smooth. 
The reviews about parking are correct. The Crowne Plaza charges $-- a day for valet and $-- a day to self park in their garage. We parked in an outside city owned lot adjacent to the hotel and paid $- a day ($-- from about -:-- Friday to -:--am on Sunday). The only drawback is once you park, you can not come and go from the city lot like you can the garage, each time you leave, you pay the fee again! 
Aside from that, the Crowne Plaza is NOT a four star hotel and while “technically” located on the Riverwalk, it is NOT convenient to the shops, restaurants and clubs. If you choose to use the Riverwalk access behind the hotel, you must walk through an area of construction and beggars for several blocks before finding the charm of the Riverwalk District. The hotel is located in a rundown area close to the bus station and again, you must walk through construction and beggars at street level. 
The hotel itself was NOT of a four star quality. The windows in the entryway were dirty, there were dirty room service trays appearing to be from breakfast in the hallway upon our check in at -pm and they were still in the hallway when we returned from dinner after -:--pm. The housekeeper also left dirty dishes in our room one day.The floors looked as if they were never vacuumed during our stay. 
The beds were hard and uncomfortable, the pillows flat and small, hardly of four star quality. The walls were so thin, our first night we were kept awake by children in the room next door who squealed and shouted, thumped the walls and slammed doors well past midnight. Our second night, a local school held their prom, again we were kept awake by slamming doors, loud voices and laughter. Finally, the elevators were slow and consistently full requiring us to take the stairs more than once. 
We ate breakfast at the hotel one morning and were surprised to see other guests in their pajamas at the tables in the restaurant. You don't expect to see that in a four star hotel!
It's probably fine for a business conference, family weekend, or something along that line, but if your looking for a pampering, romantic weekend and are considering a four star hotel, this is not the place to chose!

Your staff made my friend and I feel welcome and took care of any concerns. They were professional and freindly throughout our three different stays. Each stay was for basically one week, and we were made to feel as if we were at home.
I would strongly recommend that people stay for business or pleasure here at the Spring Hill Suites Medical Center-Northwest.
Service was excellent. The desk staff extemely trained, courtious, helpful. Housekeeping did a great job on my room.
I am very impressed! I will stay again!

I am a fan of the Kimpton hotels, and Onyx is no exception. Their service is impeccable. I received an email before my trip asking if I needed anything to make the stay better and if I was celebrating something. It was my birthday, so I let them know. When me and my boyfriend arrived, there was a bucket with beer (- bottles!) on ice and pretzels (they asked me beforehand what was my favorite drink and snack). It was a really pleasant surprise. I was expecting maybe a bottle of a nice brew and a tiny pack of something, after all we were staying for a weekend only! This was a really nice touch.
Staff is very knowledgeable about the area and attractions, and are able to instruct you on places to eat and go out around the hotel. 
It's location is amazing, only three blocks from a subway station, and a short walk (five minutes, if so) from Quincy Market, the wharf and all the attractions there. Also not far for Boston Common. We did most of our sightseeing walking, and the Freedom trail passes a few blocks from the hotel, which allowed us to stop by in the middle of it and relax a bit before continuing! 
Room was wonderful, and very reasonably-sized, with a king-size bed and a bathroom that was much bigger than what I usually see. Everything was spotless and the fact that they can provide you with any toiletries that you may forget is also a plus. 
Also, you get free internet, and if you're a Kimpton hotel member (it's free), you get $-- for the minibar. 
I have no complaint whatsoever. Well, perhaps that I wish Kimpton would expand outside the US!
It's not the cheapest, but it's certainly the best you get in this price range.

My stay at the Hilton Garden Inn on West --th Street was a positive experience. While the room was small, it was well-appointed and modern; I particularly appreciated the fridge and the glass shower. I booked a room with a view and requested an upper floor, and my room was very high up, with a view of the skyline looking north through the picture window. For the most part, the room was clean, though I did find hair on two of the towels. The staff was friendly and helpful, and I appreciated the complimentary, consistent wireless access. The hotel is in an excellent location, less than a block from Herald Square. I was traveling for work and found it centrally located for the Midtown locations that I needed to visit, though I'll probably look for a hotel a few blocks further north the next time I have meetings around-north of Rockefeller Center. Overall, I'd definitely stay at this hotel in the future and would recommend it to fellow travelers for business or pleasure.

Nice """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""chic"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotel in the area around the University of Washington. Great breakfast bar and afternoon drinks and snacks. What a great find! My friends and I had an amazing time in the hotel restaurant. The food and martinis were delicious. The room was adorable with a great view. I will definitely be staying here again.

Rooms were clean, transport to airport provided. Breakfast muffins and coffee like most american taste like tea... But that is just my taste... Cheap, value for money maybe a little bit noicy since very close to airport.

My girlfriend and I had a great stay here. The staff and service were excellent. This will be my go-to spot any time my girlfriend and I decide to visit the city. Highly recommend this place.

Just returned from a - night stay & our first trip to NY! Had booked based on great reviews on TA & was NOT dissapointed. We have stayed at the finest hotels all over the world, and the Hay Adams is right at the top. This may very well be the finest hotel in Washington DC. The location is directly across from the White House, perfect for touring the sites, museums and monuments. The staff is exceptional including Rob and Annika at the Reception, Eric, John and Jack at the Concierge, Alex and Ruben, and Fredy and Luis at the Off the Record Bar located downstairs of the hotel.
We stayed in the John Hay Suite overlooking the White House which was so elegantly decorated with fresh flowers, Bose CD radio, Italian linens and bath amenities and the most lovely turn down service each evening. Sometimes we'd return to have Evian face spritzers on our pillows or perfectly ripe apricots on our bed. The Housekeeping staff is superb and very creative!
Room service each morning was a treat-- especially the fruit parfait (with homemade granola) and freshly baked pastries. The coup de grace was having the Pastry Chef recreate the top of our wedding cake as we were celebrating our First Anniversary away from home. We arrived back to the Hay Adams from an evening out to have this gorgeous rendition of our cake (which was a surprise for my husband) awaiting us in our room with the CD of our choice playing songs from our wedding in the background. No request is too big or too small for the Hay Adams.
This hotel is exceptional, and Mr. Hans Bruland, the General Manager, should take great pride-- afterall, it all starts from the top! We hope to return soon, and highly recommend this wonderful hotel!

The staff is very friendly, they are always available to help you in any kind of need! I went to New York to visit the city and Eventi has the perfect location for that! It doesen't matter if you're just passing by New York on a bussiness trip or if you brought your whole family to visist and walk around the city. Eventi, a Kimpton Hotel will suit all your needs and preferences. Enjoy! :)

Two blocks from Times Square and within -- minute walk to any theatre. Excellent air conditioner and mini fridge, which was appreciated in --degree+ weather. Very quiet at night - for all we heard we might have been the only people in the building.

Absolutely a great place to stay. The problem came after check out... I fell asleep reading my kindle and when I woke up I threw the covers over it and forgot it. I realized my mistake later that night after arriving home. Excellent location, spacious and clean room, great bed, friendly goldfish, happy wine hour, 
good and efficient service ... window seat picnic with the great city view ...
I can only warmly recommend this hotel!

The walls were quite thin - I heard the people next door, plus lots of people walking up and down the corridor at night. There was a fridge in the room but no coffee-tea maker - thankfully, Starbucks was just around the corner.
The bathroom and toilet were ok considering it was a shared facility. The toilet flooded on the last day I was there.
The central location was probably one of the main reasons I picked the hotel. I was able to walk around the city and didn't feel too unsafe at night when walking back to the hotel, despite the neighborhood.
I was able to borrow a hairdryer from the front desk and also print out my boarding pass.
If you have heavy luggage, it's quite a struggle to get to the front desk and your room as you have to walk up a flight of stairs.
There are lots of hotels in the area so I probably wouldn't stay here again.

Came in for a - night stay. We stayed in the corner king on the -th floor
First off...find the place is not to difficult and very nicely located. Its attachment to the mall is a nice touch and easy to get around the area.

Storm or not- Chelsea Pines is the place to be- it is truly a diamond in the rough and one of a kind place to stay- once you come, you will be a friend and have a special place to visit forever. Everything was wonderful- the breakfast in the morning was Divine, the staff and their friendliness and genuine eagerness to help was uncomparable and felt So good! Truly this is a place that puts you at ease-- if you want to find the best spots to visit, they wll help--and the rooms are immaculate, super clean, and adorable-the bathrooms are GREAT! Just a treat
I could not recommend Chelsea Pines any more than I do! If you're looking for a warm and cozy, unique home away from home, and still want all the comforts of a luxury hotel- Look no further!!!

Lovely hotel by the water in a quiet and very charming part of town. Greeted with a complimentary bottle of wine and, included a nice continental breakfast with lots of fresh fruit. The room was at street level and very quiet. Tasteful furnishings coupled with a brick wall with shuttered windows added to the rooms' charm. We would definitely make it back again.

This place could easily be five stars if they would only properly train their staff. The lobby is inviting, until you notice all the trash and sticky surfaces. The desk staff NEVER acknowledge guests coming and going. During a four day stay only one person said hello to us. Housekeep was awful. Nothing was replaced. We had to call every day for glasses, soap. . . We gave up on the coffeemaker since they didn't bring more mugs or coffee and never washed it out. The worst part is that when I brought this to the front desk's attention they didn't really care. At least fake it people! I love small boutique hotels and was very disappointed to not be able to add this chain to my list.

I know this is a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""great hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" chain but what constitutes """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""great."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" It still comes down to basic services and courtesies. Staff was stiff, we had no help with luggage, had to drag the bags up to room. Just returned from a wonderful stay at the Sofitel for a mother daughter birthday celebration. We were in room ----, which has an amazing city view day and night. The location of the hotel is ideal and in walking distance to about anything you would want to do. I would highly recommend this hotel and look forward to another stay soon.

Location is good, bordering Chinatown, walking distance to the Embarquadero, but can be noisy when dumpsters are emptied at - am in the alley below, or from the agreeable bar next door, the Irish Bank. Was first assigned to the Unabomber Cabin room, which was kind of funky at first -- until we realized there was no place to put any of our stuff. We paid $--- a night, and $--- on Sat night, which we thought was a lot for what we got; would probably have liked it more if we had paid less.

I was especially impressed by the front desk service of Gentlejoy. She went our of her way to help me with an email-fax transaction that was time critical. Gentejoy provided her own email address for me to use, as well as waiving any charges to my room. She was so courteous and friendly. Thank you for such great service!

My wife and I celebrated the --st birthday of our twins--by getting away and going downtown to a lovely suite at this hotel. From the moment of our arrival, the staff were very friendly and courteous. The room was a bargain. We wanted a suite, but we did not expect a corner suite with our own separate bedroom and a gas fireplace. After a lovely dinner at a restaurant close by, we returned to a reception of warm chocolate chip cookies. We stayed up late and watched TB, and we slept in. All in all, it was a fantastic get away, though all to brief, made special by our stay at the Magnolia. We will definitely go back.

New, clean, Hilton Garden Inn. However, this place bends over backwards to please. The room is typical of most HGI's. Breakfast was above average for this chain. Only - block from convention center. Valet parking was prompt and efficient. This is first hotel with a service to provide your boarding pass with morning bill under the door on last day. I highly recommend this hotel.

Check-in: Line with ----- people. 
The room: filthy with broken furniture, dirty bathroom and clogged toilete.
I complained to the front-desk manager the second night about the general cleanliness of the room and asked for early departure (I could not stay there even for a few hours) and he was wery rude and didn’t help me but, of course, that night I moved to another hotel without the money I had paid but happy for leaving that place.
It was my -th time in NYC and I alwayshave found good hotels for good prices. This choice was clearly a mistake.

If you're looking for a four star hotel, the Salisbury isn't it. But if you're looking for a clean, comfortable room with a great location and a decent price, there's nothing wrong with this hotel. I had the advantage of staying at both the Salisbury and the Hilton New York (on --th and -th), and of course the Hilton is more luxurious and modern -- but the Hilton also super-pricey. (And the Hilton's elevators were just as slow!) The Salisbury had helpful staff, an ample $- continental breakfast (muffins, bagels, fruit salad, juices, cereals, doughnuts, hard boiled eggs, etc.), clean rooms, and a great location. The hotel building is old, but think of it as having historical charm! It was certainly just fine for a stay where you're not living in your hotel room all day (you can't see the room when you're asleep, anyway!) The location is also excellent -- close to Carnegie, MOMA, Central Park, Rockefeller Center, Broadway, Times Square, etc. It's better than a lot of places I've stayed in around the country, and for the price, I'd stay here again.

For a while this was my defacto hotel in Los Angeles. It was kitchy and clean and neer where I wanted to be. As one could guess the place has a farm theme which could be tired but to me it's a winner. My favorite room was the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Don't tell"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" suite which comes with a wet bar and mirrored ceilings! On the F & B side I can say that the restaurant, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Tart"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was nice for breakfast.

Second, ask if your room is near construction. I tried putting my baby down for a nap and there was drilling and banging going on all afternoon. Needless to say, no on returned my call. This is a swanky hotel for singles and young couples, but not for families w- young children. I tried to contact the general manager during our stay, but his assistant took -- hours to get back to me. In the end, they merely gave us a few starwood points as compensation.

We got great help from the front desk (Rakesh Patel) when we ask for a larger room and a river view. He was helpful in searching for something that would work, even though the hotel was completely booked for a conference we were attending. He also got us some free breakfast coupons and a refrigerator for my medication.
The room was always kept clean and fresh. The staff also made us a dinner reservation one night. We had a good room service dinner and two very good breakfasts.
At check-out, I noticed a $-- charge from the gift shop that was not ours and it was promptly taken off the bill. I would definitely stay here again.

The motel got a new name now it's called the memorial. The carpets are so nasty you get black socks. No fridge. No oven. Bath tub is rusty in the sides and quarter size. Paint is peeling off. We are not staying here one night more.

We stayed at the Bonaventure Hotel several years ago and were """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""wowed"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" by it, but nowadays, it's pretty tired looking. It could really use some spiffing up. The room was quite pricey, was on the small side, but clean, and the bed was comfortable. The view of downtown L.A. from the huge windows in our room was spectacular. The lobby area was beautiful and had lots of shops and restaurants.
The one negative is that the customer service was terrible! We needed assistance with travel to the Staples Center to see the Los Angeles Laker's game and got little help and alot of attitude! Usually the concierge in a large hotel is very helpful, but after calling them twice and also talking to them in person, we were quite disappointed. The front desk staff did seem nice and professional, however. The parking situation was a nightmare, very expensive, and the parking atttendants in valet parking were real jerks.
Should we go back to L.A., we'll not be staying there again.
We came to town for a conference. We found the room to be very clean and the staff very helpful. Very close to the convention center.
Clean rooms, looked quite new. Room key card was already prepared during arrival. Got laundry done, reasonable price for good service. Easy to find, with many shopping and attractions nearby.

I liked staying at the Essex Inn. It had a great location on Michigan Ave. The hotel provided a shuttle to various tourist areas, such as the art museum, the magnificent mile. There's also a bus stop across the street as well as a subway station located a few blocks away. When we were there in Febraury ---- the hotel's parking lot was under construction, but they provided parking at another location. The staff was very helpful telling us how to get around. The room was clean, kinda outdated in style but comfortable. I would recomend this place to a friend.
This is a nice looking Hotel and Bar on the outside buy the parking is pandemonium!

Park Manor Suites in no way deserves a rating higher than - star. This is a decaying old building that is in desperate need of renovations. And by renovations I mean doing a little more than slapping on the umpteenth coat of paint on the walls. I can only imagine the mold and rot that lies just out of sight. You can feel it in the stagnant air of the building, everything is rotting.
We never felt clean the entire time we were there and finally had enough and moved to the Omni downtown. The curtain had a stain on it, our bedspread had holes in it, the bed itself was sagging terribly on one side and creaked loudly at the slightest movement. The walls were chipped all over the place. The bathroom was less than ideal reminding me more of a public washroom than anything else, that is, marginally clean at a glance but probably filthy at it's heart.
The walls and floors are paper thin. Be prepared to hear every single noise your neighbor might make. We could even here the alarm from the person in the room above us! The radiator in the room is constantly generating more noise than heat.
Anyone who gives this more than one star obviously has incredibly low standards or has never stayed in a truly exceptional hotel before.
The only good I can say is that the rooms were quite large and that it was a short drive to the Omni downtown where we spent our last couple of days.

In a continual quest for the resort that can meet our -- twin boys' expectation of fun and our need for comfort with a splash of luxury, we selected the Arizona Grand Resort because of it's water park and - diamond rating. It turned out to be a disappointment for all. Here are my few pros and many cons:
The Room:
Pro: We stayed in a Deluxe Queen Suite and had paid to be in a building near the waterpark. The room was large enough for the - of us. The beds were comfortable and the amenities were nice.
Con: The carpet was wet...we are hoping it was just cleaned? I guess we can take comfort in the fact that they do clean the carpets, but it gave the room a really musty smell and a general sense of unease. The bathroom door was warped and required a contortionist move to close it. The bathroom was extremely small and dark. The TVs were from last century and very small. The sofa bed could hardly be called a bed - the mattress was so thin - and squeaked all night.
The Water Park & Pools:
Pro: They have a water park and they have lots of pools.
Cons: Our boys were bored with the waterpark in under an hour - and my kids love water parks. Maybe if you have younger kids - and-or less adventurous kids - it might work for you? You have to wear a bracelet to get into the park...it's a little annoying as an adult. All the reviews are right that there are not enough chairs. And we found that was more the case at the pools away from the park. For a - diamond resort, the pool towels are small, thin and simply awful.
Food & Beverage:
Pros: N-A
Cons: Other than an order of fries, we never ate at the hotel...not for lack of trying. The wait staff at the park walked by us no less than a dozen times and never once asked if we wanted anything. The ice cream machine at the park was broken. The restaurants at the hotel were so far away from our room (and - Diamond expensive) that we would have needed to take our car anyway, so we went out for dinner. We did attempt to catch lunch before our flight at the Lobby Grill - at --:-- when they said they were open for lunch - but were told we had to wait until all the breakfast guests had finished before she could even seat us. We left.
Other annoyances:
-) The hotel staff uses loud gas-powered golf carts to get around. They beep when in reverse. The staff drives them on the paths in front of the guest rooms - until late at night.
-) A plus for some, but an annoyance for us, they have a kiddie DJ in the waterpark that goes from - - - and the volume is loud. If you have pre-tween or tween girls, this is probably a big hit, but it was a primary reason we fled the hotel for several hours.
-) The whole place just seemed tired. My husband commented that the place needs a good pressure wash.
-) There always seemed to be housekeeping staff in the halls (who had a fabulous knack for leaving their carts blocking passage), but there also seemed to always be dirty dishes and linens in the halls.
-) It is right off the freeway - which is convenient, I guess, but it really doesn't give you the sense that you are """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""getting away from it all.""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""
So, our quest for the ideal vacation resort continues. I guess I am most baffled by how this place has a - diamond rating. I have stayed in Ritz Carltons, Four Seasons and other luxury hotels and there is no way this hotel even comes close.

I wanted to stay near Washington Square Park and Mac Dougal Street but this hotel was even better located for our needs: restaurants and shopping: Filene’s Basement, Nordstrom Rack, Loehmanns, Daffy’s, T.J.Maxx, Marshalls (and so many unique shops) all within walking distance.
We really enjoyed the free buffet breakfast because it made all the difference in the mornings. The breakfast consisted of bagels, toast, various pastries, hardboiled eggs, coffee, juice, fruits etc.The common areas are modern and stylish and since it is very small hotel so no crowds nor long waits for elevator. The staff is friendly and helpful.
We had a queen room which was big for NYC standards. It had windows towards Broadway but we did not keep the curtains open because we could see people in the opposite building, so I thought they could see us as well The subway was indeed very loud but we always travel with earplugs so it did’t bother us. Room was modern except the carpet which I think looked worn. I really enjoyed the new linen, comforter, pillows and bed which was quite firm. We are used to memory foam mattresses at home so this was good for us. 
I got to see the room with two beds and it looked really nice and spacious. I would book that for our next visit if I got a good deal.

As soon as I checked in, the toilet was soiled, and there was hair by the toilet seat! Yuck! Went back downstairs and was switched to another room. Aside from that, the rest of our - night stay was good. We were on the top floor so there were no issues with noise. The room was modern and the bed was comfortable. Also room seemed very cold and could not change thermostat.

Just returned to England from the Cass Hotel, Chicago where I was in town for the Bob Dylan shows. This is one of the best American hotels I have stayed in for location and value for money. It cost $--- (including tax) for three people for three nights in a room with three beds. The room was large enough for the three of us not to feel cramped and was very clean. You can get a good breakfast in the small cafe. 
Best of all is the Sea of Happiness Lounge. This is great bar with draught beer at $-.--. If you call in be sure to say hello to the Captain. The Cass doesn't have the facilities of some of the other larger chains but for price and location it can't be beaten.

This hotel was picked for me by a travel site and I can't believe how lucky I was to get put here. I was visiting LA for the first time in -- years and when we lived there, our housing was taken care of by the venue we performed at so this was my first stay at a hotel in Southern CA.
The only thing I can even remotely begin to complain about is the fact that the valet was $-- a night and that's REALLY finding something to nit pick at. I'm used to New York where parking is like selling your first born.
The room was clean and spacious and more than I needed as a solo traveler and would think a group of three would have been more than comfortable. The room also had a plethora of items for travelers who forgot an item at home or simply for those that like to travel light.
The staff also arranged to mail a package for me so I didn't have to lug it back East on my flight.
It looks as if the hotel offers a lot of amenities but since I am not social by nature, I didn't take advantage of those. The location is near Beverly Hills shopping and that was a day gone right there ;)
I was in town for a celebrity charity event held farther down on Wilshire so I was happy with the proximity of that as well. I hadn't had Jack In The Box in years and there was one a short drive away.
I have horribly poor sleeping habits but - out of my - nights were good. 
I have nothing negative to say really. I usually stay at a Four Season if there is one in the city I'm visiting but I am now a fan of Kimpton properties and stay at them in Chicago, New York and the newly opened one in Philly.
Billed as - stars but in my opinion a very economical hotel. I don't make a lot of money and value where I spend my dollar and was happy I got so much for a good price. Planning on being back in LA in November and December and hope to stay at this property on those visits.

What a waste of money! Expect a long wait when checking in. The lobby is very small and crowded.
We booked a bayview studio thinking since they have their own private beach it should be wonderful. Guess again! The east side of the property is public beach. There were lots of people and screaming children enjoying the public beach all day and night. Every night there were people making bonfires on the beach, getting wasted and cranking up their music. Even with the balcony doors shut you could still hear the thump of the base. One night from our -nd floor balcony, we even got to watch a drunk man stumble to his car and hear him puke several times by his car (which was parked right in front of our room). Oh yeah another bonus...there is a street in front of the balconies which is also public parking...good luck finding a spot to park there! Seems all the cleaning ladies get prime pick of those spots.
The room had an old TV, I guess flatscreens haven't made it to that part of the bay yet. The bathroom floor had dirty corners. 
We ate breakfast at their restaurant. We asked the hostess for a table for -..she took us to a table with - chairs and never offered to get another chair. I had to search one out myself. On top of that we got terrible service there.
Exercise room was full of wet children who must have become bored with overrunning the pool. Free arcade had -- games but - were not working and you have to wait forever to get a turn to play because of all the young children will play the same game and never give some else a chance to play.
For the money, I expected a lot more. Their website sure makes it out to be such a beautiful resort. Try crammed...noisy...and too expensive. This place should not be rated so high. Locals used to rave about it but I can't see why.
The only good things I can say are that the sales woman in the gift shop is very friendly, it is wonderful that they have a couple of rescued seals they care for on their property, and the room was a decent size for a family of four.

I stayed at the Empire hotel for - nights for work and then another - nights with my husband on holidays. Our room for the entire stay was the Superior King Room and work paid for breakfast during the first - days. I have been to NY before and know rooms are small but I was still disappointed that our upgraded superior king room was so small especially the bathroom was extremely tiny! Breakfast is not worth the cost at the hotel. I ate there for the first - days as work had already paid for it but on the - days while staying for pleasure there are plenty of alternative options close by.
Another couple joined us holidaying and they upgraded their room to a suite. The suite was fantastic and if you can afford the extra $s and are staying in NY for a week then the extra room is definitely recommended. The suite had a separate lounge-dining area and a lot more storage-cupboard space as well.
Location is great – close to Lincoln Centre and Central Park. Only --min walk into busy Times Square. Only -mins walk or so to Tiffanys and shopping district of Midtown.
The Empire upstairs bar-club is great and atmosphere good.
The pool on the website looks big but when we went to check it out we laughed at the size of it - well done to the photographer in snapping the pool from a great angle. During the day the pool-lounge-bar area is really cool and spent a long afternoon with cocktails and friends after shopping and it was a fantastic afternoon and the service was excellent.
Beware what items of clothing you get dry-cleaned as two items of mine were shrunk and no longer wearable. I complained at reception and they refunded my dry cleaning but the items were ruined and cost a lot. Dry cleaning is very expensive with the hotel and I’d recommend doing it yourself at a local Laundromat.

- Salon De Ning - The Peninsula Hotel New York – roof top bar – great location and views but expensice cocktails… --- Fifth Ave @ --th Street http:--www.peninsula.com-Peninsula_Hotels-en-default.aspx#-New_York-en-Dining-Salon_de_Ning-

I had a comfortable one night stay at the Hilton at the San Antonio Airport.. Service was friendly and top quality. The hotel itself is physically worn. Still, for the price it was fine and I had a positive experience.
The staff I encountered: both shuttle drivers and front desk staff, were friendly, helpful, and efficient. The airport shuttle was reliable and both arrived at the airport when I was told it was and got me back to the airport as promised. 
The room was comfortable; I had a view of the top of another building. Not a lot to see though but the highways. 
I ate at the restaurant-bar. Food was tasty and served quickly. The staff at the restaurant were neither impressive nor attentive. I'd rate the restaurant average for hotel restaurants but adequate.
There are many choices at the San Antonio airport, and though I'd stay at this hotel again, there was nothing to make my pay more for this hotel over another one.

Better location than I first imagined. Helpful staff. Great dining at the hotel. Rooms were great and even included HERMES bath products. A couple suggestions, the hotel hallways smelled a bit strange (I was not the only one who noticed), and the restrurant was very, very fancy. Overall great hotel!

The inn is great in most respects but there were a few small issues that led me to give it a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""very good"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" rating. First, the pros: the location is super, right above Ghiradelli Square and the Powell-Market cable car line. Good access to most tourist spots. The value is great. I paid $----night plus $-- parking and taxes, which really totaled $----night. Still, a bargain! I had a large suite with stocked kitchen. It was spotless and comfortable. The staff were all friendly and helpful. Laundry machines are on site (although one wasn't working). 
The cons: the light from the interior common area shone through my bedroom and the window curtain didn't keep it out. I like a dark room for sleeping and this was a slight annoyance. The bathroom is small with a tub shower and small counter. I like walk in showers and ample counter space for toiletries. The parking garage, though conveniently on site, is very cramped, making going in and out sometimes a challenge. You are required to leave your key at the front desk because they may need to move your car.
Overall, it was a good stay and I'd recommend and return.

My husband and I stayed in this charming hotel for eleven nights. Though we were initially disappointed to find the Marriott properties near the convention center fully booked, we were completely won over by the brilliant staff and the unique beauty of this historic property. Despite having over --- rooms, the hotel is reminiscent of some of our favorite small boutique hotels in San Francisco, Europe, and the UK. This is unlike any other Courtyard in which either of us have stayed, partly because of the uniqueness of the building itself, but largely because of the excellent staff. For the duration of our stay, at all hours, nearly every staff member we encountered was warm, friendly and helpful.
Having arrived late, we dined in the bar the night we arrived. Our meal was very good and the service excellent. We also had drinks in the bar some evenings and thought the atmosphere congenial and relaxing.
We had the full breakfast buffet a few times and found it a good value. The omelets (made to order) and fresh fruit were first rate, and the coffee was excellent. There was a reasonable selection of milks, yogurts, cereals, and breads (though the quality of the bread & pastries could be improved). As is the case at any buffet, the hot items were a bit soggy if they'd not recently been brought out from the kitchen. 
Our suite was spacious and spotless. The bed was comfortable, and having a mini-bar and microwave was lovely for a long stay (there's a Ralph's grocery store approximately four blocks away). 
The hotel offers free internet access (wired in rooms, wireless in lobby), a nice gym, and excellent complimentary coffee in the lobby (in the morning only). 
The hotel is located roughly eight blocks from the convention center, an easy walk for most people. It's about the same distance to the Maritime Museum. Balboa Park is a bit further away, and the park itself is quite large, so people with small children may wish to take a cab. 
One can find homeless people, buskers, pan handlers, and drunken conventioneers in the center of any large city in the world. San Diego is no different. I walked to and from the hotel day and night, alone and with my husband and never felt unsafe or threatened. As one reviewer said, just use your city skills, to which I'd add use common sense, remain alert, and expect to have a wonderful visit!
We can't wait to return to San Diego next year. When we do, we'll definitely stay at this hotel.

Was there recently for one night for a conference. 
Tried to check-in at -:--pm (the published check-in was -pm), they said my room wasn't ready, where as others coming after me were assigned rooms. Was given a dummy door key card and asked to chill in the lounge on the --nd floor and that they would call on may cell as soon as the room was ready. I chilled there until -pm, no call, so went out for dinner. Came back at -:--pm and asked if my room was ready. The gal said of course yes and give me a key. When asked why no one called me, she just shrugged. 
No, my troubles did not end there. I went to the room and opened the door only to find someone else in the room. Came back to the lobby, then they apologized and gave me another room. I said I was not going to walk-in on somebody else again, so they sent someone with me to open the new room. For all my """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""trouble"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" they reduced my bill by about --%. It was definitely not worth the trouble they put me thru. 
Very bad experience.

My husband and I have stayed here several times when we come into the city for White Sox games. The location is amazing-- close to everything. The rooms are small, but the bed is comfortable and the furnishings are nice. This is usually our go-to hotel downtown, and we can usually book it on Hotwire for a great price. I always recommend staying here!

This is obviously a big convention hotel. It has loads of meeting space and the rooms are spacious enough for a few people to meet if necessary. The bed is very comfortable.
The food left much to be desired. The restaurant was pricey, the service was glacially slow and the food not that great. Fortunately, the hotel is in a great location with lots of dining options in all price ranges...the best is the Five Guys burger joint a couple of blocks away.
I would certainly stay there again for a business trip but maybe not a family vacation.
We ate lunch before leaving for airport, service was absolutely excellent as was the food, reasonable prices great staff and a lovely way to spend our last lunchtime in Chicago. Highly recommend.

went to San Fran with some friends for a long weekend and an excursion out to Wine Country. We got a killer deal on a suite, which I couldn't pass up. I had considered the Westin Market Street, but we got a much bigger room at the Palace for only a little more. We went all out for this trip, and started it in style. We had a Rolls transfer to the hotel from SFO, and the bellman kindly snapped our picture. Check-in was easy.
The room...was huge. We had a view of Montgomery Street below, and tons of room for the - of us to lounge about. The sauna was broken, which was about the only downside...the other being the long line for coffee in the mornings. The pool was nice being on the roof. I love nicer hotels for one main reason: the lack of children! The pool and hot tub were vacant of them. The maids were unseen, as they should be, and arrange the mess of clothes every day...nicely trained, and appropriate tipped later.
Likes: Understated elegance, location, price, and size of suite
Dislikes: line for coffee and the stream of tourist in the lobby also scamming on the aforementioned coffee.
Overall: A San Fran institution. Once the largest hotel, if memory serves me. Worth a visit, if only to drink the coffee in the lobby, haha

New hotel, large rooms, very clean, friendly staff. Good location for easy access to airport. Not many resturants near hotel but a ----- minute drive gets you to many options for food. Area seems very safe.

Checked in very late and left fairly early because of a cancelled flight so did not get a chance to experience more that just the room. While riding up in the elevator I found myself wishing I had more timebecause the lobby, dining area looked great, and inviting. The room was cozy, clean and quiet which allowed for good albeit short night sleep. The security line into the main terminal in the morning was a bit long, made longer by the flight attendants who kept cutting the line. But, other than that, I would not hesitate to stay there again, and may even incorporate a stop there in my travel plans.

I travel to Phoenix for business often, our office is off of Camelback Road in the Biltmore area. I normally stay at the Embassy Suites in that area, but this time it was full, even at my Diamond level. Therefore I had to switch hotels. All the hotels in the Biltmore area were full, there must have been a convention or many spring break travelers. 
This particular Embassy Suites on --th street is very old and out dated. The interior design must be from the --’s and has not been updated since. The rooms were clean and the beds were not old, but the overall feel of the hotel and rooms were very old and uncomfortable. When I closed the door to my hotel room I could see light coming in from the outside. That in its self is not too bad as I have had this happen more than once, but the overall look and feel in the room was straight from the --’s and helped make my first impression worse. I arrived very late and did not have a chance to see if they had room service or if it was good, but the next morning I did try the breakfast buffet and found it to be adequate. The check in area was not updated either, it felt as if they had not remolded since opening day, and as I have already stated the whole hotel felt that same way.
I went for my normal morning run and the location of this hotel is in a business section, which is not bad, but other hotels have more to offer in this regard. Like a lot of locations in Phoenix they are by the canal system and I found the running path along the canal, which is much nicer than running through a crime ridden area. Overall this was acceptable, but when I compare this hotel to that of the one on Camelback Road, the Camelback Road location wins hands down. The Camelback location is located in a fantastic area, by the mall with tons of restaurants, and they have a jogging path mapped out through neighborhoods making it feel like home.
As far as I’m concerned, if you are going to stay at an Embassy Suites in the Biltmore area the one on Camelback Road is by far much better than this one for about the same nightly rate.

Seven years ago, we gave our newly-married daughter and her husband honeymoon accommodations at this hotel. My wife and I, two daughters and son-in-law recently returned there to attend my brother's wedding in Berkeley. All five of us were well-pleased with the hotel. Although the wedding was in Berkeley, we planned to spend most of our visit in San Francisco. The hotel location is excellent for that, with easy access by walking or public transportation to everywhere we wished to visit. It allowed us to avoid renting a car that would have been sitting more than used.
We loved the hotel itself, with all it's charm and history. It is a historic building, and has a few glitches - one of the bathrooms did not ventilate well and had some mildew on the ceiling. The cable TV signal would intermittently drop out and return. The AC unit tended to be a bit on the noisy side.
We very much appreciated the Green option of being rewarded for not requiring housekeeping every day. It allowed us to collect additional Starwood points on our account for future use. The hotel encourages recycling. Staff was attentive to our needs and concerns, and quick to respond.
All in all, a very enjoyable five day stay. Thank you.

If you're not attending a conference at the Conference Center there are much better locations more central to the action. However this hotel's service was superior in every way. Each concierge we spoke to was more than helpful and we found all the hotel staff to be great. 
The rooms are modern and rather small, but nicely appointed as you would expect for a Westin. As it is a newer hotel with a very modern design some might find the lobby cold and impersonal, but the people in the lobby bar make it feel like a second home, we found the service for our nightly hot chocolate night cap excellent - and they really try to remember you, of course we had our -- year old daughter with us so we stood out a bit from the regular business crowd. 
We often walked to downtown, about -- minutes and it was an easy flat walk with lots to see along the way and we felt safe, although it added about $-- to each taxi ride to get back to the hotel - from anywhere we seemed to be from shopping to dinners out. Renting a car was really easy as the concierge arranged to have the car dropped at the hotel - so it was as easy as picking up the keys from them and dropping them off - brilliant!

The pacific inn was a nice little boutique motel. We booked through the phone with a woman named Vicky. We simply wanted a room with - beds because it was me my wife and - little children. She actually recommend the kid suite instead which was a room with one bed and a bunk bed for the kids. When we got to the hotel our room wasn’t ready so the front desk told us we could keep our luggage in the back and we could hang out in the pool area while we waited for the maid to clean it. It was no problem though because the room was ready in -- minutes. When we got into the room the kids were so excited because back home in Louisiana they share one big bed. The next day we ate breakfast at the hotel and went to Sea world. If you have never been to Sea world then you have to go. It was amazing to see all the different animals they had there. The next - nights consisted of going to the zoo and old town. There is plenty to do in San Diego. You will never get bored.

We chose the Donatello for it's combination of location, space, price and favourable Trip Advisor reviews; last time we stayed in the Westin Market Street. Jesus checked us in into a great room at ---- when we were expecting just to drop our cases - what a great guy! In fact, the desk staff, concierges and maids were all super friendly and helpful which made The Donatello a welcoming place to stay. The room was generously sized and being on the back of the hotel, very quiet indeed - we didn't hear a thing from either inside or outside the hotel at night. A kitchenette area allows for snacks or breakfast in the room which was an added bonus. The hotel is just two blocks from Union Square and a few blocks further from cable car and muni stops (The F line tram is quietr than others and a great way to see the sights from The Castro, through Fishermans' Wharf to the Embarcadero) and there's even a parking garage right next to the hotel if needed. I think we made a good choice with the Donatello and would say that it fully lives up to it's positive billing on Trip Advisor and would recommend it without reservation!

Booked a stay at the Seaport Memorial Day weekend after seeing many favorable recomendations. Purpose of trip was get away weekend with no kids.
We were some what disappointed although the hotel did have some good features. I will list the pros and cons:
Room- average but sound proofing was poor. Hotel was very noisy and we were awoken several times during the night from teens in the hall and other rooms (slamming doors-in and out etc). Room was starting to show wear and tear.
Amenities in bathroom such as robe and tolietries were nice quality.
Front desk nice- Clerk gave us a corner room with a nice view of the harbor. The public areas are nice and modern.
Pool-gym- nice but small. Looks they are upgrading the area.
Location- poor. hard to get around city from this location. Think public transportation will be serving the area soon but it was tough when we were there. would not have been bad in nice weather- but not nice walk to nearest T (----- minutes) in cool damp weather. After paying $-- for parking you do not want to to pay to park all over the city- would have been nice to be closer to the T or have some sort of bus service (which in May did not run on the weekends)
The one advantage I see for location is if you are going in the warm weather with kids. The walk to the Childrens museum and aquarium would not be bad and the hotel seems to cater to these type trips.
Overall like I said the hotel is not bad but just very average. I travel a lot for business and stay at many hotels up and down the east coast each year. I was expecting more. Next time we go into Boston for a get away weekend I would try another hotel before going back.

I thought this hotel was great - very new and clean. The location is excellent as far as being central to the Subway and Times Square. The actual street it's located on is not picturesque at all. The front door of the hotel is opposite the massive wall of the Bus Depot. 
For that reason, I would not recommend it to someone who is looking for a romantic, first time getaway to NYC. The most impressive thing is the size of the rooms, the sparkling new bathroom and linens and the relative quiet inside the room. I think it is great value for a big city hotel!

We stayed at this motel for four nights while attending our son's graduation at Lackland AFB. Overall we had a good experience. There is quite a bit of renovation going on, with workers all over the property during the day. In the first room that we were placed in, the remote didn't work (important to my husband) and the light over the sink area didn't work. So we were moved to another room. The remote didn't work here, either, and the safe was closed so we couldn't use it. This time, the front desk guy didn't have a remote that was compatible with our TV, so he promised the maintenance guy would take care of it within a few hours. To make a long story short, it took until the next evening for our room problems to be taken care of. They never did get us a toilet paper roll holder, either. (They did give us a credit on our bill for our inconvenience.)
The breakfast was ok, typical motel continental breakfast. The pool is quite small but it was nice to be able to use an outdoor pool at all in the beginning of November! The roads in the area are pretty confusing and busy for out-of-towners but that's not the motel's fault. 
I would recommend this motel for families attending BMT graduation - it took us less than -- minutes to get to the base from here, a better area than right around the base, and lots of places to eat, things to do.

Expected so much more, will never go back nor send anyone there!! We took our family along with another family to this resort over the holiday weekend, to get away and relax, and enjoy, but that was not the case with this place. We thought we had got a great price on the rooms that included a breakfast package so everyone could eat for free. Well this was not the case. First the breakfast package that you pay for with the room is not a free breakfast. You get vouchers aka coupons for a free meal but you still have to pay tax on that meal, and tip.(I had no problem paying a tip, I work in a restaurant and always expect to tip) So you still end up paying over $-- for the breakfast for a family of - adults and - kids, and - infant(they charged for her too.) Also when we first arrived we didn't even receive enough vouchers for the breakfast so we spent over an hour total between the restaurant and the front desk trying to figure out why we did not receive enough vouchers to begin with, then when we got our bill to check out they charged our room for the same meals that were on the voucher, so again we had to spend time going to the front desk waiting in line for another --mins, hearing other people having similar problems with added charges on the bill that was not theirs. Everything here is an extra charge so have lots of money with you to pay because you will need it. The employees are nice, they all say hi, the bellmen are great very nice and helpful, they warned us about the $-- fee for the fitness center per day, and told us to do the $-.-- per day package to keep that fee lower, but even when we did that we still had issues on being billed wrong as well even after I called and verified it, another trip to the front desk. Also if you can not walk up hills be ready to ride the shuttle they have, and again they expect a tip for the driver. Not impressed at all with a resort I had heard so much about!

Stayed in NYC for - night w- - adult """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""children"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (-- years old). Easy to get to, valet parking very convenient. Able to check in early w-o difficulty and leave bags next day for a nominal fee. Close to EVERYTHING. Staff courteous. Would highly recommend if you are just looking for someplace to sleep. Beds were comfortable as were the pillows. Did not check out amenities as were busy w- shopping, shows and eating. We were on the -th floor, and did not notice any untoward noises mentioned in earlier reviews. Our room was not one of the ones renovated, but was just fine.

My husband and I stayed here at the tail end of our trip of the Pacific Northwest and loved it.
We were lucky enough to get a parking spot out front and did not have to pay the $-- fee for parking. Upon check in we were greeted with very friendly staff and got a room on the -th floor (top floor) with a great view of the Space Needle. (Do not waste your time or money on a Bay View, too many bldgs in the way). We became members of the Hilton rewards before we booked (free) and somehow got a great room out of it.
We checked in at about -pm, asked for an extra suitcase jack (- for me and - for husband) and it was delivered immediately. The light dinner that was served every night we were there (Monday-Thurs) was perfect portions and decent variety everyday (note that only - entree is served with a salad, so you can't be pickey). Adult beverages are also included (beer-wine, lemonade, iced tea, water). The morning breakfast was also decent, but could be served a little later than ---am. There were always breads, bagels, juices, and hot food items like eggs, sausage, and oatmeal. My husband I spent everyday out and about the town after breakfast and were ready for a rest at dinner time. The two meals served by the hotel also kept our budget in check. We chose to splurge on food through out our city travels for lunch and snacks including eating our way through Pike's Market.
The beds were very comfortable and we enjoyed our seperate living room area in case one of us wanted to stay up later to watch TV. The bathrooms were clean, but the water pressure could have been higher. We made use of the kitchenette to store leftovers for late night snacking and keep beverages and popcorn for late night movie watching.
I borrowed a DVD player from the front desk (free) because I brought along some workout-yoga DVDs.
The hotel is conveniently located to the Space Needle area, Duck tour, Science Center, Music and Sci-Fi museum. If you want to go to the waterfront (Aquarium, Pikes, Argosy Tours), walk - blocks to the first pier and catch the FREE BUS that travels the entire waterfront and all the way to Pioneer Square.
If we return to the Seattle area, we wil definately stay again!

My husband, -- year old son and myself stayed at this property the week after Christmas through New Year's. Staff here is extremely nice and helpful. They really go overboard to take care of you. We were upgraded to a suite which I highly recommend. We had a full living room and terrific kitchen with microwave plus a full bathroom and additional sink in the bedroom. Very handy when juggling the morning routine for - people. The location is outstanding. Great restaurants within easy walking distance. Our favorite was across the street and new since September of ---- - Cantina Laredo. Absolutely outstanding modern Mexican. See my review under restaurants. Also the Italian Rosebud Trattoria restaurant located off the hotel lobby is terrific. Wonderful staff and large portions you can share. Highly recommended.
The only negatives for us was the overcrowding of the breakfast room with large families and unruly children. The Hampton Inns do cater to families so if loud noise and children grabbing food (not using the tongs provided), coughing on the food, etc. concerns you this might not be the place for you. We found if we visited the breakfast room between ----- am took our choices to our room it worked better. Families need a nice hotel to stay at as well so I'm not begrudging them the experience but the hotel might be wise to post signs instructing parents to assist their small children with food choices rather than letting them grab at will.
The hotel has a nice pool, sauna and hot tub as well. Prices are reasonable here. A good choice for a moderately prices vacation to a fabulous city.

The Monaco, as is their custom, delivered a wonderful evening and morning stay for us when we got """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""stranded"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in DC during the snowstorm along the east coast right after Christmas. I am a frequent Kimpton guest so their standards are well known to me. This particular evening was just an over-delivery.
Thank you to all the Kimpton staff at The Monaco. You should be proud of your property and your professionalism.

First, this hotel has one of the - best hotel fitness facilities I've ever used. Its hard to maintain a good fitness schedule when travelling a lot for work, especially if you can’t get into a good gym nearby and since most hotel “fitness centers” have only a treadmill, elliptical and maybe a universal fitness machine at best.
The fitness center really is “State-of-the-art” with a bunch of good, newer treadmills, elliptical machines and bikes. There are real free weights! There are several racks of dumb bells, bar bells, and numerous machines that are all clean and well maintained. 
The dining options within the hotel are ok. The service wasn’t the fastest, but they were usually busy. The pricing was a bit high, but it is downtown Dallas, so its to be expected. The room was comfortable; I was in the north tower on an upper floor. There was a little bit of street noise, but not enough that it bothered me. 
The only - complaints I really have are these:
The coffee creamer in my room was bad, and curdled in the coffee.
Wi-Fi-internet isn’t free. In a hotel where we pay so much to stay, I shouldn’t have to pay for Wi-Fi in my room. There is a lobby downstairs with free internet access, but I should be able to work in the comfort of my room without having to pay extra.
Overall, it was a good stay, especially since there’s not much to do in the downtown business area of Dallas.

The staff is wonderful,the room is clean,the free breakfast is good.Neighborhood is great,subway,penn station,deli food,all are so convinent.You can walk straight to Time Square,It is the heart of Manhattan.

Stayed two nights in this hotel and loved it. From the moment I arrived, I was greeted very warmly at the front desk by Jenna, shown the restaurant, bar, excellent fitness center and pool. Great views of the airport if you love airplanes like I do, with almost no aircraft noise. 
Rooms: great size, very comfortable, great views. Bathroom large, shower and bathtub excellent. Beds fairly comortable, TVs nice, channel selection acceptable. 
Bar-Restaurant: Quite expensive as you would expect, but the service is top notch and the food delicious. I had the asian seafood hot pot and it was fantastic, as was the bento box w-sushi, salmon, chicken and asian slaw. Burgers look tasty, as did quesadillas and desserts. 
Fitness Center-Pool: Fitness center had great equipment, all new and in good working order. Chilled towels were a nice touch! The pool, while somewhat small, is outdoors which is nice this time of year. Nice views of the airport from the pool and fitness center
All in all, one of the better hotels I have stayed at, and probably the best airport hotel I have stayed at worldwide, and I make a habit of staying in a lot of airport hotels.

My wife and I decided to celebrate an anniversary at a good hotel in Houston. Based upon the reviews at sites like Tripadvisor we decided on Magnolia. What a complete mistake! Where to start.
