Hotel Union Square's location is amazing. The cable cars, the Mall, and all the amazing shops are literally right outside the hotel. This hotel is perfect for the solo traveler or for couples with no children. We have two small kids and there were no amenities for them. Even their room service menu didn't have a kids meal selection. For the price we got, it was great (because of the location). The staff was OK, they seemed a little robotic and unwelcoming;however, the manager was very friendly & polite. I would definitely recommend this hotel to folks without children.

From the moment we arrived until the moment we left three days later we couldn't have asked for more from the wonderful staff at this lovely hotel. The hotel is in a great setting on the beach and everything from the home made cookies at Happy Hour to the accommodation to the wonderful service made it three days of pleasure. We would recommend this hotel to all.

The room had - windows and therefore, - mini blinds to close with one broke and light that shined in my room all night on my bed. I was on -th floor so the noise from the street was loud and I was awakened at --- am of loud drunks getting out of the bar below on the streets yelling etc. The room was clean and nice. Not real fancy as it is an old building. Service was friendly and helpful. Close walking distance to alot of restaurants and bars.

Hotel Indigo was quite lovely and we enjoyed our - night stay. We were in a perfect location to explore what downtown San Diego had to offer. We were walking distance to both the waterfront for daytime entertainment-exploration, and to the Gaslamp area for evening entertainment-exploration. We were so close to so much, we felt we didn't need to rent a car (and hence pay for parking!). The airport is only several miles away, a cab ride to the hotel was about $--.--, and there is also convenient bus service for $-.-- that goes directly to the airport. 
We had a nice corner room, with a view of Petco Park and also into downtown. The large windows provided an excellent view, and the curtains did an excellent job of blocking A.M. light. The bed was large and comfy, the desk area was ample, and the bathroom was HUGE! Double sinks, a very large shower, and nice Aveda toiletries. There was a Keurig machine provided for morning coffee-tea. 
The fitness area was of a reasonable size, and provided the basics. There was also a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""meditation area"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" outside, next to the gym, which was a nice touch. The -th floor lounge area is small, but a nice place to start your evening.
The staff was efficent and friendly, particularly the bellman who assisted me with my luggage. 
I would definitely stay again when in town!

This was a beautiful, classic hotel. 
The rooms have some amazing views of the city, but also feature electric shades that will completely block out all the light for when you're ready to sleep. 
Pretty good sized rooms for the price. Very high quality and clean!
Great customer service. Will print your plane tickets home for free. 
In a great location -- far enough away from the Fisherman's Wharf that it doesn't feel too, too touristy, without being too far to walk to attractions. 
Only two complaints: 
- The business center that they advertise is NOT free. You must pay to use their two, extremely slow, computers. Had I known I would've brought my own laptop for when I needed to look up attractions.
- They have this auto HVAC unit... I'm not sure if ours was broken but it must have been motion sensored because when we would go to sleep it would completely shut off and then every time one of us would move or get up to use the bathroom it would kick on and then shut off - minutes later. Extremely disruptive.

My friends and I stayed at the BW Tuscan Inn last week and I am so excited to write this review. From beginning to end it was a PERFECT experience. The staff was so friendly and helpful and the concierge service was very knowledgeable. The hotel itself was so beautiful and very boutique-like (don't let the Best Western in the name fool you). My room was clean and nicely decorated - the bed was EXTREMELY comfortable and also had a nice down comforter and comfy pillows. The bathroom was large and private. The room has an honor bar, which I didn't use, but DID use the refrigerator to store some of my own snacks and wine. Another great thing about the hotel is that every day, they offer wine and beer from ---pm for free for all hotel guests. We took advantage of the offer and many other guests did too. It is VERY nice. All in all, HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

The hotel was beautiful. Staff were friendly and helpful. The room was comfortble and clean. There was a safe in the room that was locked by the previous guest. I called about it and someone came to take care of it within -- minutes. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone.

I stayed at this hotel in October- November for just under two weeks and had a great time. Was attending a conference at the convention centre so it was very close. 
The room was massive - I was given the handicap room on the -th floor so I'm not too sure if all the rooms are this large. This room has a separate lounge area, with it's own tv, desk and a L shape lounge. From this room you went into an area which had a fridge, microwave and sink. This was great to keep some food and heat it up if I wanted to. Opposite this area was the bathroom - one of my major issue areas, Firstly I thought it was really strange after the room was cleaned each day they would leave the toilet seat up - was there a reason for this I just don't understand it, I've stayed in hotels around the world and never had this. The shower and bath are all in one, which I didn't like, I prefer to have a separate shower, the shower also didn't have any great pressure which was dissapointing. The other issue with the bathroom was that the room had a sliding door which didn't close all the way - if I was staying in this room with other people I would be concerned about privacy. From this area you then went into the bedroom. This room was large, the bed was awesome had a great night sleep in this bed, once again this room had another TV and a safe which was large enough to put my laptop in it. 
Another issue that I had with this hotel room was the cooling, I would set the system to the lowest it would go, however the room was rather warm despite it being on this setting all day, this needs to be checked out as I know I'm not the only person who has stated this.
Overall the room looks very modern and was comforable - would be great for a long stay or short stay, only had a small amount of noise one evening when there was a group of school age kids staying in the hotel, they were a bit noisy in the early evening but nothing major - could only hear the noise from the lounge area, so I moved into the bedroom and couldn't hear anything. 
Breakfast is included in the room rate which is great however when you stay in a hotel as long as I did you see some issues. The first couple of days the breakfast was great - had no problem serving myself quickly and finding somewhere to sit, however as the hotel filled up throughtout my stay I can't say the same thing. I went several times down for breakfast only to see a massive line - this is because the continental area is easy and quick but everyone lines up for the hot food which takes longer and therefore the line doesn't move very quickly and the line forms infront of the continental foods (cereal, breads ect), very frustrating. Also when they are busy it can take a LONG TIME for everything to be refilled. The wait is worth it for the hot food - pancakes, eggs and omellets to cook but it can cause a major wait for everything. It would be great if this hotel provided a bag that you could take your breakfast away with you as sometimes when it is busy you couldn't find somewhere to eat. I passed on the breakfast on a couple of the days because I just couldn't face the wait.
The staff are very helpful and friendly, always greeting you as you come in. Sometimes the house keeping would not clean my room until very late in the afternoon - - or -pm which was a bit annoying, something that needs to be looked at. There is free internet connection which I did enjoy as some of the other hotels in the area you have to pay for this.
Overall I did enjoy my stay, the issues that I stated above are really only minor but do result in me not giving them - stars. I will be booking for them next year.

I am recently back from a month of solo-travelling in California.
The Mayflower Hotel was my favourite accommodation that I used during this visit.
As I was using public transport, location was an essential factor when choosing accommodation. Mayflower is a ---minute (slightly uphill) walk from the Greyhound bus station. It is only a --minute walk from the Powell Street cable car.
The hotel staff were very friendly throughout and helped me solve two problems. Firstly, my mobile charger (from the UK) was faulty, but I was quickkly supplied with an American one that had been left behind by another guest. Secondly, I was finding it difficult to upload photos on one of the three available computers. A computer technician was soon called and a solution found! Such help and support made me feel very welccome, so much so that I booked a further night.
The hotel is kept in good condition. Breakfast is basic but better than you will find in other places. 
Overall, this hotel is a gem and well worth booking.

We stayed at this hotel on July -th throught July --th. We arrived at the hotel around - PM on Saturday night and the check in was extremely slow. It is a beautiful hotel with only - person at the front desk. The room itself is nice and clean. I have to give credit to our maid. Very sweet and friendly. The pool is nice and clean without any kiddy pool. The exercise room is pretty neat with all the equipments. Next day, we came down to information booth. Another extremely long wait to ask for information of how to get around in Boston. It was a long line and once again with only - person to help. We booked the trolly for $-- per person. My advise, don't bother to book at the hotel. Get onto the trolly and then you can pay them later when they get to the -nd stop at the Aquarium. You can also get a discount there. The only convenient thing about staying at this hotel is that you can catch the trolly right at the front door. In room service is extremely expensive. We ordered in room service breakfast for a wooping $-- for only - person which include - eggs, - bacons, potato, - toasts and - glass of orange juice. So stay away from ordering breakfast. There is a convenient store - Eleven & Dunkin Donuts right down one block from the Hotel. For dining, strongly suggested the Barking Crab. Very affordable with good food. The food was plain and the price is extremely expensive. A large lobster (about - pounds) for $-- and a sole for $--. If you willing to spend a lot of money for dinner with horrible service. Hope this will help with you trip in Boston. Overall, loves Boston. Will definitely come back. Not so sure will stay at this hotel.

This is very clean and comfortable five star hotel. Its short walk to central park, shopping, time square. There are plenty of places close by to grab a quick meal. Great for business or holiday travel. 
Will stay here next time in NY, just so convient to everything. Highly recommend.

Although this is an older hotel, it is a beautiful, well kept property. From the moment my family walked into the lobby, to the time we checked out, we had a great time. At registration, our desk clerk made us feel welcome, and provided for us with a beautiful room. While there, I used the health club facilities, and enjoyed breakfast on the executive floor. All the staff were friendly and helpful, and they helped my family have a delightful time in Chicago. The concierge provided us with great reviews of local restaurants, and she helped us book our Chicago River tour. 
The hotel is conveniently located on State and Monroe streets, just two blocks from Marshall Fields-Macy's, and two blocks from the Art Institute and the Symphony. I would go back to this hotel in a heartbeat. Even if you don't stay at the Palmer House, at least take time to see the Lobby--it is worth it!

I have no complaints about the hotel itself: we enjoyed the room and the price was more than reasonable, but I can't give it the rave review I'd intended on because they completely blew off my traveling companion's wake-up call and his missed his flight, adding -- hours to his trip home that day. On the one hand, this is unlikely to ever happen to a TripAdvisor guest in the future, but on the other hand, the hotel wake-up call is something we've come to rely on as travelers and this failure really had an impact on the trip. Lesson learned.

My husand, kids and I spent a wonderful weekend in D.C. My husband and I had stopped here last year when we were in town for a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""weekend without the kids"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and had some drinks at the bar. We were impressed with the hotel so decided to try it the next time we were in town. My first impression when we walked in was, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""What the heck happened to the cozy feel to the place?"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" It had an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""open feel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" when we had stopped here previously, but there had been wonderful sofas to hang out on and a place in front to sit back and have a few drinks while catching up on old news. That feeling is all gone. Instead, you can't find a good place to sit at all. The sofas are gone and in their place are a few unwelcoming chairs - those you had to search for. Considering the size of the space, it's rediculious that there really isn't any place to sit and read, talk or simply wait for someone to come downstairs. Also, the cute bar area is gone too. The rooms are on the smaller size, though very clean. The bathrooms are a good size, though the shower doors are CLEAR! Forget about allowing your kids to use the bathroom while you're taking a shower. Even me, his wife, was surprised to see my husband standing a-la-natural when I walked in while he was showering-ha! I guess it's called, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""contemporary"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", but it's a bit odd. The walls (like some other reviewers stated) ARE paper thin. We could hear the people in the room beside ours and out in the hallway as though we were standing right beside them. I've stayed at """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""mom and pop"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" motels that had better sound barrier rooms. They have a small swimming pool which the kids enjoyed. We got the room for $---night which certainly made up for the negative stuff (FYI: The week between Christmas and New Years is DC's down season. You can get deals on all the hotels in town at this time). The location simply can't be beat! We parked our car on the street instead of paying the rediculious parking rate and found a spot right around the corner. The streets were lined with cars so others thought the same way. You can also grab a bite to eat at Union Station which is two blocks up the street. I would probably stay here again, but the thin walls really are a discouragement.

I have stayed in this hotel a few times in the last --- years on infrequent trips to the West coast. I did not read any reviews prior to booking, because I knew exactly what I was getting before I even booked my room. I was surprised to read several negative recent reviews, because my experience of just a few days ago could not have been more different. Yes, I will agree that getting around the inside of the building can be a bit challenging because of the multi-level lobby and - different room towers....especially the first time you stay here. However, once you figure out you are in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Red"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" tower, it's pretty simple after that.

In addition, the new flat-panel TV presented a great HD picture. Room Service was very fast , accurate and the food was delicious. Every employee I encountered was friendly and very helpful. Mario in the bar has been there for a long time, and gives terrific service.

I stay at the Sheraton City Center before the Baltimore Running Festival because the location is very convenient and if you park across the street in the self-park facility, you will not be trapped post-race by the road closures and traffic issues. The rooms are quite large and nice, typical of the Sheraton brand. The staff is welcoming and helpful. The bar-restaurant has a great atmosphere especially when there is a big game on tv. It certainly is not the boring-depressing hotel bar that you find in so many places when traveling for business! The bar-restaurant staff is fantastic, there are tons of tvs, and a great beer selection. The only negative is the food at the restaurant. They have a very limited menu and even with that managed to make poor pasta with chicken (soggy). Robert Irvine would be very disappointed! That keeps my review at average, not very good.

I took the wife and kids to Chicago for one last fling before school started back up. When I checked in, the staff was very attentive, I showed a little consideration for the friendly attitude (small tip) and was upgraded to a huge upper floor room complete with a bar! I didn't get the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Priceline"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" glare and it paid off for all involved. The air and water show was underway on the lake front, and we had planes flying over our room. The kids thought it was great. That night we had a great view of the fireworks at Navy Pier. The Sunday morning breakfast buffet at the hotel was very good and the price was not out of reason. The conceirge was very knowledgeable and very friendly. It was one of the best times we ever had in Chicago.

No internet and no idea when it would be fixed, when we left after - day, it was still down. bugs in the bathroom. Very noisy room. beds were lumpy and old. Very rude staff and the front desk staff were clueless and had no desire to help us. The whole motel needs to be remodeled, Its old in a old part of town. The tiny rooms (so called suites) at $--- a night just have either - king or - doubles, and a tiny -- inch cable tv with like -- channels and the tv would get interference on half of those channels. we moved to the comfort suites after - day. Breakfast was ok, nothing special.

I recently stayed here three days for a business trip and overall was very pleased. The location was great, walking distance to the Gaslamp District, Petco Stadium and a quick drive to Coronado Island. The hotel istself was clean and modern ond had a decent view of the bay. I will be staying here again!

This past year has been a very difficult time my daughters and I. So continuing a tradition of coming into the city every year at Christmas when I was married to their Mom was something I still wanted them to experience. We have always stayed at the W hotels because of their wonderful accomadations and staff that you just don't get from most hotels. Staying at a W in Manhattan makes you feel like you live there. What the W staff id for me and my daughters we will never forget. Edna Barkley was amazing. She was so personable and compassionate and was able to give us more than we ever expected. Our WOW experience was just that.....WOW!! The look on my daughters faces when they walked into our room with Santa is something I will never forget. For those brief moments, they were able to forget about the past year and just enjoy the moment. Our experience is cherished memories we will always share. 
With warm regards,
Mark, Alexandria, Jenna and Julia

Not really a family hotel, although they try. There were plenty of families staying there though. Easy to get to destinations. But it is a longer walk than it looks to get to Quincy Market or Aquarium.

Inside and out. Thin walls, doors and windows. Sounds like there was a busy fire station next door on one side an a transfer station on the other. Awful night's sleep. Doors slam loudly by default and there were many late night guests on my hallway
Inviting bar - lounge with incredible lake views. Pleasant and helpful staff. Can't wait to return.

Overall a great experience. Room had modern decor (with interesting mural), nice bathroom, comfortable bed, and very little street noise (we were on the eigth floor). The room was a little on the smaller side, but when we registered and the front desk saw the size of our dogs, they put us in one of the back rooms, which were roomier. Wonderful that it was pet friendly and the floors were wood, so no major concerns about pet hair. The bellman gave us a wonderful recommendation for pet hotel just around the block where we could enroll our boys in doggie day care, which was a life saver! Front desk also gave us a couple of good recommendations for dining in the area.
The only two things I would say that prevented this from being - star was that the bathroom door wouldn't close (I assume this was due to swelling-humidity?) Not a big deal for us, but I supposed some might find it inconvenient. The second issue was the restaurant, which wasn't stellar. And the fact that we had the wrong menu in the room, which made ordering room service a little challenging. I do understand that the hotel and restaurant are separate entities, but it does affect the experience to a certain extent (and the hotel does need to change its menus).
Otherwise it was a very pleasant stay and we would definitely go back!

We stayed here for an anniversary overnight getaway, and found the observations about the hotel facilities from other reviews to be largely accurate, with our own notes below:
* The rooms have a great view with the floor-to-ceiling windows, ask for higher floors if they have. Our room on the -th floor had good views, but was far enough from the ground and upper lounge to be relatively quiet (as quiet as the city can be, anyway!).
* The rooms are smallish, you have a closet with room to hang maybe ---- things, but otherwise you'll be living out of your suitcase. But, you're in the City to explore it, not lounge in the room, so it's not so bad.
* Great location over the High Line Park, entrance just a block south. Heart of the West Village and SoHo within relatively easy walking distance.
* Despite mixed reviews on service, everyone we dealt with was pleasant and helpful when requests were made of them.
It's a hip, trendy, unique place, i.e. very New York City, so check it out if you can.

After reading some of the reviews on the Serrano I was expecting a rather """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""snooty"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" staff. My experience was quite the contrary! The staff was extremely friendly and helpful. The bell captain wanted to know if this was my first stay and proceeded to explain the hotel to me; wine tasting in the lobby from five to six each evening, a business center and gym (which I didn't visit), high speed internet in the rooms.
My room was not large, but well appointed. Even though it was a corner room it was high enough above the street to shut out all by the harshest street noise. Linens were clean and changed regularly, towels were deep and thirsty, and there were complimentary terry bathroobes in the closet, the large kind that embrace you after a shower.
I would recommend the hotel to any traveler.
Very high class hotel. Worth the money spent. Great location, right in the middle of Times Square. Alot of activites to do.

My friend and I go to NYC frequently and have stayed at many different hotels and we both agreed that the Hyatt rates at the bottom of our list. My friend booked our rooms (we each had another guest with us) directly w- Hyatt as she is a frequent business traveler and has stayed at their hotels in other cities. We asked for two doubles and each got a king and had to have roll-a-way beds brought in. In addition to that, they also had our rate incorrect by $--. They corrected this but then wanted to charge an extra $-- for the roll-a-way since they said two doubles was not a guarantee unless you want a room on a smoking floor. Frankly, I think this tactic is an insult. 
So as far as what we got... What was great: the property location. What was good: the bed comfort and the room size (until we had to accommodate the roll-a-way). The bad: the rooms do not have a coffee maker (although we got a complimentary cup upon checkout), no refrigerator (can't bring any drinks or perishable food to your room) and there is no full length mirror. The only mirror is the one above the sink in the bathroom. Not good when two people are trying to get showered and dressed at the same time. Also, the bathroom does not have a fan so it gets pretty steamy in there. We all had cold showers or the water would run cold then suddenly become very hot, then cold again. The towels were rough. Also, this is the only hotel I've ever stayed anyplace that charged guests ($- a bag) for storing bags at checkout so we could spend more time in the city. We're not cheap... we always tip the staff for this service but does Hyatt really need the extra money from their guests?
I know this hotel has been around a long time and is a huge old property to maintain BUT... we're talking Hyatt, one of the biggest names in hotels around the world. They should do better. One other note: the staff was friendly and apologetic. I felt bad for them, we heard complaints from fellows guest as well. I would NOT recommend this hotel unless location is the only important preference.

Although downtown Detroit itself could use some major cosmetic surgery, the Marriott was a complete delight. The highlights of the hotel were not in the rennovated rooms, but in the staff and the restaurant. From the moment I exited the cab, I was treated truly as a guest should be. Everyone was professional and extremely courteous. The RiverCafe was also a delight having some incredible seafood. Nothing unusual, but good quality. I would highly recommend the scallops. The rest of the center, including the so called """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""shops and restaurants"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" near the hotel was a disappointment. There were few shops and the only restaurants I found were in a food court. If you plan on having business meetings and don't expect a lot outside of the hotel, then this is the place to stay. Nice rooms, nice facilities, great staff and terrific food.

Good: clean, decent place to stay.
Bad: title says it all. This place is crawling with sock-headed hipsters. The Carlyle is less pretentious and a lot less annoying. I know that The W is targeting a certain type of visitor, but they really missed the mark on this one. 
Let's start with arrival- You enter on the fifth floor, where the front desk is located. Attached to the lobby is the lobby bar (ok, so far sounds normal, right?) but then they decided to fill the empty space with... A DJ setup. You then have to walk across an empty dance floor with the DJ on your right and bar patrons on your left, disco ball overhead, just to get to the elevator that goes to your room. When you are travel weary and carrying luggage, believe me this is not a relaxing welcome. 
The following morning we woke up to No Coffee in our room. A small sign indicates that there is complimentary coffee on the fifth floor. Great, I'll go grab some cups and dance my way to some java. I'm redirected to the second floor. - bucks plus tip later, I have my coffee. Apparently, the coffee is only complimentary on the fifth floor between ----am. That's just lame. Oh, I can request that a coffee maker is brought to my room. Too little too late. 
Coffee and disco atmosphere aside, it's a clean hotel and a decent place to stay. Grow out some ironic facial hair and get ready to boogie your way to your room each night- you'll fit right in.

I stayed here for a conference. When checking in, my roommate was offered a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""smoking room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" as the only option. The guy at the front desk made it sound like someone had at one time smoked in it and you could barely tell. This was not the case. The room reeked of smoke. Apparently this hotel is behind the times and actually still has """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""smoking rooms"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" complete with complimentary pack of matches (need I say fire hazard). When we went back to the lobby to complain, we were told that the hotel was sold out and that they couldn't change us until the next morning. We ended up checking the gift shop for candles and deodorizers and such. When we found none, we went back to the front desk and requested anything that could possibly help with the smell. They ended up putting an ionizer designed to get rid of pet smells in our room after we complained a few times. This helped a bit, but for a nonsmoker it was horrible. They did finally give us a nonsmoking room the following afternoon, but it was too late. Our clothing still smelled for the rest of the conference. For the price they charge for rooms, this isn't the quality one would expect.

We've stayed here before when it was under a different chain's name. It's been renovated a bit, so the rooms are little nicer but the prices have gone up, they now charge for parking, and the free breakfast has gone away. This is a nice, clean hotel, but the only thing that sets it apart is its location, which is about a ----- minute walk to Seattle Center. We stay here when we attend events at Key Arena, and there are also a ton of great restaurants in the immediate area.
Here are the pros:
 -The front desk staff was very nice and helpful, both at check-in and check-out, with recommendations for restaurants and area directions the next morning.
 -The room was renovated, clean, contemporary, with good beds.
 -Nice bathroom, with fluffy towels and toiletry dispensers in the renovated shower, great water pressure in the shower.
 -Big flat-screen TV on the wall, free water, heat and air are controlled by a thermostat on the wall and the unit is pretty quiet.
 -Housekeeping seemed pretty good.
And the cons:
 -They now soak you -- bucks for parking. This is new (used to be free, and it's not mentioned on their website or in their rate). They mention it quickly and quietly at check-in, like they're embarrassed. The next morning they forgot to put it on my bill, and I certainly didn't remind them, because I think it's a ridiculous charge.
 -They've eliminated the free buffet breakfast, which at $--- a night for a relatively average room should definitely still be included.
 -AVOID THEIR RESTAURANT! It's way overpriced, and the food is mediocre. We had breakfast there. $-- for - small pancakes that were lukewarm and doughy, $-- for ham and eggs. Go to one of the other places in the area.
 -The hotel is in an industrial area. It's quiet at night, but you often get noise in the morning. You get a fair amount of noise from the corridors.
 -The WIFI is free, but it's very slow. The elevators are also slow.
All in all, it's a decent place to stay if you're going to Seattle Center-Key Arena. It's just a little overpriced for what it is.

Very good new hotel. Exciting design, fairly large rooms for Manhattan, friendly and helpful staff. Got good deal through Travelzoo. The only problems, at least for now: slow unreliable Internet in the rooms (but complimentary!), long wait for elevators.

We stayed at -- Lex for the Thanksigiving weekend to get away to the city. Staff was courteous, helpful and friendly. Looking to stay near Rockefeller Center this is a small hotel in a great location. Restaurant-bar """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Brass Lexington"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was very good for breakfast, dinner and cocktails. Room was not too small with an excellent view. Corner suite has a nice sitting room with a great view as well. Our only complaint was that there are only two elevators and you had to wait a very long time in the morning. We got tired of waiting one morning and walked down the -- flights as it was a quicker option. Otherwise this was a great stay and we would be happy to return.

This was my first stay at this property. The room was very clean and comfortable
The staff was very pleasant and extremely helpful
The location is great - close to everything.
This will be my choice for lodging when in Phoenix

This was our first stay at this hotel - I had purchased a discount gift card from the local news channel. We were attending an event at the Majestic, so the hotel locations was great. The hotel itself is quite charming and the staff members were polite. The problem was the temperature in the common areas of the hotel - lobby, bar, restaurant, etc. It was easily -- degrees or warmer in these areas. Worse was the elevator - it was like stepping into a sauna. Luckily there are only three floors on this hotel, but I still broke a sweat every time I used it. We commented (note: not complained) about the temperature with the front desk staff and the bartender in hopes a subtle hint would result in a cooler environment. Didn't happen. The bartender's response was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""yeah, normally it's a lot cooler in here."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I might give this hotel another try, but certainly not until the summer heat subsides.

I stayed at this hotel for business for - days. The room was ok, nothing special. The rooms and the hotel are a bit dated and worn. The bed was a little uncomfortable and a little old. The AC works but if you like a cool room it isnt going to get there. The hotel is in a good location and the rates are pretty good for a NY city hotel, but you arent going to be very impressed with the hotel. Its not a bad hotel but you would expect a little more based on what the web site looks like.
If you can do some bargin shopping for better time square hotels you should, there are some fantastic hotels in the area, this isnt one of them. You wont be completely disappointed but there is nothing at this hotel that will impress you either. All the little things you look for in a full service hotel such as a newspaper in the morning, your bill under the door, furnishings in good order and reliable internet are not here.

Our group of -, including - small children, stayed here in two suites (each was a one bedroom-living room-full kitchen-one bathroom suite) June -----. We found this hotel to be modern and very clean. The staff was very nice, especially the manager. There was a great complimentary breakfast every morning, free newspaper, free parking, free coffee-tea and some fruit available all day long. The hotel is located very conveniently close to I--, but it is up the hill from the freeway and there is no noise.
There was a fire on a construction site beside the hotel a couple of weeks before our stay. It occurred on appoximately June --, ----. The hotel next door that was under construction, and soon to be open, completely burned down. This caused some external damage to one of the wings of the Homewood Suites hotel, and some water damage in the suites of that wing. As a result, the hotel closed that wing for renovations. Otherwise, the hotel is fully operational, including the center courtyard, pool, and hot pool. Other than seeing the external damage to the one wing of the hotel as we drove up, nothing bothered us.
The hotel was easy to find when travelling from the SAN airport. I suggest following the directions as outlined on the Homewood Suites website: Heading I-- North - Take local bypass for state highway --. This is --- yards past the Sorrento Valley Road exit. Exit Carmel Mountain Road and turn right. Drive one third mile to Vista Sorrento Parkway. Turn right on Vista Sorrento Parkway, drive one half mile to the Pacific Plaza traffic light. Make a U-turn at the traffic light and the hotel will be on your right. 
These directions are much more accurate than the ones from mapquest.
The hotel was a great base for tourists exploring San Diego. An approximately -- minute drive to San Diego ZOO and Balboa Park, -- minute drive to Seaworld, -- minute drive to Coronado, -- minutes to Del Mar Beach or La Jolla area. 
Although there are no restaurants next to the hotel, there are restaurants and a Vonns grocery store within a - minute drive. Front desk has a very good information sheet with directions.
Overall we were very happy with this hotel. It helped us have a great vacation in San Diego.

Hotel Grace is simply the BEST! My fiance and I went to NYC for a romantic pre-holiday weekend getaway. We wanted to imerse ourselves into the city at the holidays. Hotel Grace was the perfect place to do that! We were centrally located to everything. The hotel was super cool with a European feel. The rooms were very comfortable. The staff was very cordial and accomodating. The rates were EXCEPTIONALLY fair, especially for the weekend before the holidays (typically the most popular time of year in the city). We travel quite a bit and have been in hotels around the world. This hotel is a great find, especially considering it is in the heart of NYC. We are going to go back to the city in either the spring or fall, and will be returning to Hotel Grace.

Ok first off, when I got to the hotel they acted like I never made reservations. The only reason we stayed there was because we were attending a wedding reception next door and needed a place to stay. We had no lights in the vanity. No hot water in the shower. No cold water in the vanity. When we ran the cold water in the shower, the bathtub wouldnt drain. The bride and groom also stayed at the hotel and they had to sleep in the floor because their bedding hadnt been changed. They also had left over food in their room. It was pure disgusting! The hotel says they have security but they werent around when a fight broke out in the middle of the night. The brides car was also damaged during the one night stay. I wouldnt recommend this hotel to anyone. It's a dump and most of the staff are complete idiots. OH and one more thing. It was the middle of July when we stayed there and the A-C wasnt even on when we got to the room.

We booked in here late in the eveing, the guy at the front desk was helpful and friendly. The room was really spacious and clean. We would stay here again and would ask for a room at the back and were right on the corner of Filmore and Lombard bit noise but great to people watch. the free parking is safe and convient. There is a bus stop close by so no travel problems. Much better than others in San Fran - give it a try

We were in DC for the Cherry Blossom Festival and to see the Terra Cotta Warriors at the NatGeo Museum. Our stay was for - nights. The room was a Jr. Suite King and was very good. Check-in was fast, the room was clean, maid service was great, and the doorman were very attentive. The mini-kitchen was perfect for our needs. We were on the second floor facing the street, it was fairly quiet.
The only drawback was the resturant, breakfast was $-- for eggs, bacon & toast or and order of french toast. Very expensive.

This was my second trip to Washington, DC with my -- year old daughter. I did a lot of research into hotels and the locations of the hotels and decided on the L'Enfant Plaza Hotel. The best thing to be said about this hotel is the location. It can not be beat. I booked an Executive Suite with a monument view. I received a regular room with a view of the highway and river. When I called down to the desk to ask what could be done to correct this, I was put on hold and then disconnected. Around -:-- construction started on the outside of the hotel. The sound was so loud that you could not stay in your room. I again called down to the desk and asked how long this was going to continue and if possibly I should have been told. I was again put on hold and then disconnected. We decided to go to the pool inbetween activitities and the noise. The pool was too cold to swim and so cloudy and dirty you could not see the bottom. Now that I have found my way around the city and used the very convenient Metro, staying at this hotel is no longer the best option. The price, noise, rudeness of the front dest is not worth the location.

When we arrived our reservations were mistakenly made for MGM in Las Vegas. We spoke to a woman named Shahnee who was more than accomodating. She did her best to make us feel welcome and was able to correct the problem and get us a room. She is more than an asset to this company. I have never been so impressed with an employee of any hotel. She was handling many problems that had to be delt with yet never ignored us. She was able to get us a room and i have never been treated so good at any hotel. Our stay was wonderful thanks to her. Our evening which included our Kid Rock concert was great thanks to her. We even won some at the slots. Before i wouldn't of considered staying here. Because of SHAHNEE I would not only stay again but recommend this hotel to my friends. Thank you SHAHNEE for a wonderful stay and the personal and special treatment you gave us. Employees like her are far and few these days.
Very nice hotel. Great modern hotel. Everything is a little dark because of the style but this is a happening hotel. The bar in the Lobby was awesome. Good location and excellent service.
Great Location. Nice clean hotel close to Cable car terminus. Very reasonably priced Thai restaurant on property.

I always enjoy visiting with your friendly and courteous staff, while at your hotel.
Your rooms are always available for me when I arrive, and my stay is always pleasent.
I can't wait until I can return to your hotel again.

We stayed at the Orlando after reading reviews on TripAdvisor. It was a disappointment. The room had a musty smell and the bed was as hard as a rock w- flat pillows. The toilet was hard to flush, the faucets didn't turn off and the bathroom was in need of renovation. We were promised turn-down service with chocolates and noone ever showed up.

I stayed in this hotel for a month while working in the Javits Center and it was a nice -- minute stroll from the hotel. The hotel is in a good location for people wanting to be in the mid-town area.
My room was modern, with a stove, refrigerator, coffee maker, microwave and toaster oven. The room is small, but I was on a business trip and didn't spend much time in doors. The King bed was extremely comfortable and the flat screen television had a pretty good selection of channels.
The breakfast was nothing to write home about but it most often sufficed. There is a bar and restaurant in the lobby of the hotel but I didn't go in so I cannot comment on prices and quality.
There was a decent sized fitness room with modern equipment.
The only problem I had during my entire stay was that the elevators are painfully slow when the hotel is busy. I mean a good - minute wait a few times each week!
The staff were friendly and helpful. Parking is available at a garage just next door, but I did not use it so I don't know prices.
I recommend this hotel for my fellow travelers that can afford it, and I will be returning to this hotel in March.

This a very good located hotel. Nevertheless, I have to make few comments about. The rooms are big enough but it need a renovation, the furniture are quite old. The bathroom need it urgently (we didn't take a shower), The cleanliness is on the limit for the floor and carpet although the bed clothes are right. Despite the comment I have read, I have to say that the breakfast is ok, it has a selection with bagles with cheese, peanut butter or jam. There are also cerals muffins, some juices and te-coffe. Forget it if you like eggs or beans or something for a continental breakfast. If you are not satisfy you have around the corner a Dunkin' donuts. The prices are quite high overall for the value but there are few more options in this area so If I return to Boston probably I 'll repeat.

The hotelier, Andre Balazs, does it again. A very cool hotel experience with a lot more glamor than the average $--- hotel. I was impressed with the room size as they were quite spacious. I thought that would be the place a hotel like this would short you but not here. Man, they really need to open one of these up in London... could use all the help it could get in regards to hotels.

My stay @ the SLS was great! The front desk staff was very professional and personable; and the restaurant service was A+. The only downside I had was that, I used my points to pay for my incidentals, but they charged me on my card also. I have yet to see the credit on my bill, but I understand mistakes happen. The rooms are nice - I had a work-out facility in it and also an outdoor patio, which I didn't get a chance to enjoy. All in all, it was a pleasant stay. Thank you!

We booked on the internet which was probably --- the problem. Booked for - nights smoking room only. We arrived and they said they received the reservation as non smoking and didn't have a smoking room for the length of our stay. After going back and forth and showing the desk mgr our reservation receipt we still ended up changing to - days (the time they had the smoking room for) She basically didn't care what my receipt said as hers said non-smoking and as far as she was concerned, she was right and I was wrong. She wanted to switch us to non smoking for the rest of our stay. We refused and told her to cancel us after the -rd day and we would find other accomodations. I don't understand the logic of taking me out of the room I'm already in to put someone whose going to come in - days in it!
The next day we went to the desk manager in charge (different girl) who listened checked our reservation and switched us back to the original - days in the smoking room. How all of a sudden the room was available when it was not the day before is beyond me. The first desk mgr obviously was having a bad day and decided to take it out on me.
As for the smoking room. It stunk! Just because I smoke doesn't mean I want to be in a room that stinks of stale smoke. I am getting quite tired of being treated like a criminal because I smoke. I started way back when cigarettes were not known to be bad. Got hooked beyond the point of quitting due to the stuff you put in there to accomplish just that but now you want to make me the bad person.. (quite another conversation and lets not get into it OK)
I truly believe a small window with a screen is necessary for ventilation in all smoking rooms. The A-C heating unit doesn't do the trick as it only recirculates the stale smokey air. We bought a can of lysol and sprayed it each time we left the room and by the -nd day the room no longer smelled of smoke. I suggest that Holiday In Express and any other hotel that has smoking rooms stock up on some lysol or other type of air freshener and put in small windows for ventilation.
Now with that being said...other than the two issues above. The stay was fine. The rooms were spacious, the mattresses fine, both wireless and cable broadband internet service. I didn't do the breakfast thing as I made coffee in the room each morning (get the suite - it has a frig & microwave) but my husband and kids did and there was plenty to choose from. The location is good as it was easy to get to all points, beaches, shopping etc etc. The rest of the desk staff was very nice. They gave directions, even printed coupons for various attractions that we asked directions for etc.
All in all, had it not been for the whole smoking issue I'd say that it was a plesant stay. I will stay in the same hotel next time I come, but I will call the property to make my reservation to insure they have it down the way it's supposed to be.

We stayed for a company event and were thrilled to stay in such a nice place. We had a corner room (----) with a great view overlooking Times Square. The room was good sized and clean, though there did seem to be hair product or lotion or something on the bathroom sink. The bed was great, very comfortable. The staff were friendly and helpful enough. The hotel is very secure, you had to use your door key to go anywhere in the elevator and there were lots of staff around. We had a great time at the dance club Whiskey, located beneath the hotel.
Though trendy and modern, the place IS dark. The elevators and hallways were incredibly dim. The shower and toilet were pretty noisy when used, but we didn't really hear noise from the rooms around us. The only real issue we had with our stay was discovering a rattle in our car exhaust that wasn't present when we left the car with the valet service.
We really enjoyed our stay and would recommend this hotel to others.

Booked late for meeting and fortunately found room at Embassy Suites Convention Center. I'm a business traveler and frequent many hotels but this is by far the best ever. Directly across the street from the convention center and only two short blocks to --th Street Mall. Room was great...facility was amazing...fitness center has great equipment....nothing negative to be said. Customer service is awesome....#-..realized after arriving that I'd left my cell phone charger many miles away, visited front desk to ask if they had any chargers in 'lost and found'....Sara told me that she'd check but that they probably didn't since they hadn't been open very long. I left the desk preparing to head downtown to pay for a charger when Sara stopped me...they had found a charger and she wanted to make sure it worked on my phone. #-...Breakfast buffet is tremendous, food and service is great. I met Beatrice...the manager...the first morning and she remembered my name each day. I told Beatrice on my next to last day that I'd miss breakfast the next morning since I had an early flight out...Beatrice told me to check with her before I left and if they were ready, she'd take care of me. When i checked out of the hotel, Beatrice was waiting for me in the dining room and supplied me with a large cup of coffee and a bagel for the ride to the airport. She didn't have to do this....but it certainly got my day off to a good start. Well done....and thanks to Beatrice and Sara.

We stayed here in May ---- for - nights after being recommended by a friend. We also read lots of reviews on Tripadvisor for this hotel and it was a good move to book the hotel. Very quiet considering how many people stay here, good complimentary breakfast but the breakfast room gets VERY busy. Very helpful staff on reception and lovely clean rooms with a very comfortable bed which is much needed after a busy day sightseeing in San Francisco.

Hotel room very good on level -, like a mini suite. Bed huge and very comfortable. Good facilities in room. Look out for extra charges put on meal bills. Breakfast expensive for what you get. Room service burger fantastic and best hot chocolate. Be aware because older hotel shower in bath so not a lot of room. Good location. Close to local bus service. Front desk staff not that helpful to tourists. Not a lot of information for tourists. Good air conditioning. Two lifts,one very small one normal.

We stayed at W San Francisco on --nd floor and really like it. From the room we could see Bay Bridge ( partly ) and the city. The room is clean, modern and the bed is very comfortable. The hotel is in a good location, right next to MOMA and just a few blocks from Union Square. Free coffee, apples and cookies in the lobby is a nice touch. At this time in June they're renovating so the lobby is rather crowded. Parking at the hotel is expensive. We parked our car at Moscone garage nearby. Very convenient and only $-- maximum.

Wow. I am almost at a loss for words. This boutique hotel is absolutely beautiful and it's less than a month old. From the moment you walk into the place and are greeted by both a wonderful staff, a beautiful place, and frozen grapes you know this is going to be an experience. Our room was breathtaking. You have your bathroom with the rain shower head and waterfall stick and a big soaker tub and a tv in the mirror. Then your king sized bed on a platform with another tv and then your sitting area with yet another tv and a beautiful view. Oh and did I mention the curtains and blinds controlled at the push of a button? The bar-small restaurant area is cute and the bartender Chris was an absolute sweetheart. We also met Frank (rooftop manager) who was so nice and friendly. Honestly - the entire staff overall is very friendly and accommodating. Very convenient location. Easy walk to subway-Broadway-Times Square and restaurants on -th Avenue. Room was larger than expected for NYC. Had reserved twin beds but was upgraded to double queens. Beds and pillows very comfortable.
Staff was friendly and very accommodating. Room was clean.
Will stay here again.

You see so many bad stories about bargain hotels in NYC, dirty, bed bugs, unfriendly employees....and to my surprise this is NOT one of them. Location is handy to all NY has to offer by train, and walking distance to Times Square. For a inexpensive get away, where you will be out and about enjoying all that is NYC....this is the place ! Enjoy a great meal or another show with the savings.

I was in town for an audition recently. The hotel was booked and paid for in advance. Since I had a - hour drive I was exhausted by the time I got there to check in. I got the chance to stay at the Camino Real in late September of this year. 
When I first came across the hotel while searching for a place to stay, I was a bit hesitant about it, since I've never heard of it. I did a quick search of reviews on good old TripAdvisor and decided to give it a shot. Upon arriving at the hotel, I was quite impressed with the decor of the lobby and architecture. When I checked in, I had to advise the front desk agent that per the rate I booked (American Express rate) was to include a breakfast. She advised that it was not mentioned in the reservation, so I had to show her via the iPad at the desk for customer surveys. I was told to speak to the clerk at the desk in the morning.
Got to the room and was still impressed with the decor-architecture. Once I entered my assigned room, I did a quick inspection and was impressed with the room size. The bathroom itself, was twice the size of your average hotel bathroom - though it could use better lighting. Light was available over the vanity, but not near the toilet or shower off to the side. 
The was the traditional armoire equipped with an older television. I don't know if they plan to update them to newer plasma-LCDs sometime in the future. 
The only complaints I had with the room were with the bed (worn mattress and bedding) and carpet (worn and could use a nice steam).
The restaurant was predominately clean and had a good selection for the breakfast buffet. I would have liked to have seen better housekeeping with the serving utensils.
I would like to say, overall, the staff was very welcoming and attentive. And I truly loved the architecture of the building. If they would update the rooms, they would have a beautiful hotel - one which I would love to stay in again.

Just returned from a weekend in San Francisco. After traveling cross country we arrived at the Handlery tired and a little cranky. Quickly our car was parked and our luggage delivered to our room by friendly staff. We went to the front desk and were pleased to find we had been upgraded! Fantastic room with plenty of space and all the amenities overlooking the charming courtyard pool! Great location! I was on a cable car riding down the hill to the wharf within minutes of arrival! I highly recommend this hotel!!

We just returned from our - night stay at the White Swan Inn. It is in a great location in Nob Hill and a few blocks from Union Square, Chinatown, the cable cars, and many buses. My husband had a conference to attend everyday and I found it easy to explore the city from this location. The rooms had fireplaces and were large and spacious and located on - floors with an elevator. We had the Ashley Suite which was a two room suite which consisted of a bedroom having a canopy bed, sitting area, fireplace, bathroom, wet bar with refrigerator, TV and it faced the courtyard. The other room faced the front street and had another bathroom, closet, living room with TV, couch, club chair, desk, lounge chair, and another wet bar with refrigerator and coffee maker. Bathrobes were provided for lounging. There was complimentary water, soft drinks and champagne in the refrigerator along with a box of chocolates and chocolates on the bed at turn down. There was always fruit and cookies or cake at the front desk area. Included with your stay is breakfast and afternoon tea with appetizers. Breakfast is served downstairs in a nice area that opens onto the courtyard when the weather is warmer. Breakfast consists of cold cereals, yogurt, fresh fruit, pastries, scrambled eggs quiche, breakfast meats, oatmeal, coffee, tea, and juices. Afternoon tea is served in the adjoining den areas which have comfy couches, wing backed chairs and fireplaces. There is wine, cordials, coffee, tea, cookies or cake, fruit and cheese, something hot like artichoke dip or lasagna or salad. In addition to the china cups and saucers by the coffee and hot water pot, there are also paper cups with covers for those """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""on the go"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". Since we keep kosher, we only had the juice, fruit and cold cereal, but everyone said the food was good. For shabbat, we were able to go to shul at the oldest orthodox shul in the city, Congregation Kenneset Israel on Sutter Streeet, which is only about --- blocks away. You can make arrangements to have dinner and lunch there for shabbat. A few blocks away at the entrance to Chinatown near the arch there is a kosher restaurant, Sabra, which serves good middle eastern food. The Inn also has a small exercise room which has a treadmill and bicycle with a TV to watch while exercising. A computer is also in this room ($-.-- for -- minutes) . There are plenty of brochures about area attractions at the front desk and the staff is very courteous and helpful. This is a great place to stay if you are looking for something other than the cookie cutter large hotels!!!!

On a vacation to NYC in the summer of ----, I discovered the Novotel after horrible experiences at - other hotels (whatever you do, don't stay at the Park Central!!!). That's right, I stayed at - hotels during my - weeks there and as they say, the third time's the charm! The lobby is so fascinating because it is not on ground level. A great retreat from the hustle and bustle of being a tourist in New York City! Great stay!

My husband and I stayed for one night on ----. We were impressed by the modern decor in the lobby, the relatively uneventful check-in, and the inviting lobby lounge with the overstuffed chairs, tables, and plenty of places for people to congregate. We got there early and were able to store our luggage while we shopped a bit. Security was very good as well, as there were staff to monitor the comings and goings near the elevators on all floors. Our particular king room was very, very small, which is probably to be expected for having booked through a discount website! We had a king room in which the bed took up about --% of the available space. The view from our room was of the parking garage. Absolutely nothing impressive - but then we were only there basically to sleep so I wasn't too disappointed. The bathroom was small with only a shower, a handicapped accessible, very loud commercial toilet, and a pedestal sink. Almost no storage space. We felt that some areas of the hotel, particularly the hallways, were in need of some maintenance. We had breakfast the next day in the restaurant which had some very delicious food i.e. eggs made of two parts egg white to one part egg yolk, homemade potatoes and sausage. We have stayed in other hotels in Manhattan and will continue to explore them. Probably won't stay at this one again.

My Husband and I stayed here for -days from --nd to --th September. This trip was to celebrate my --th birthday and we paid extra for deluxe king room however when we booked we where advised that we had been allocated a deluxe queen, the reception staff where very helpful and advised that we could be allocated another room but suggested that we review our room first. We agreed and once in our room where very happy as we had a lovely view (which is very rare in NYC) another nice touch was that when we got into our room I was welcomed with a lovely card and bottle of wine to celebrate my birthday!! The hotel is absolutely gorgeous and will be even more amazing when completely finished - still to finish restaurant though we where not disturbed by any building work. The hotel is decorated to a very high standard and is absolutely spotless, the service was amazing and everyone was always very eager to help you. We only had one small issue with the hotel bar as opening times was quite inconsistent - I think this was due to new staff and would imagine would now be resolved! I would also make sure you get the price of your drinks as the prices where a bit expensive, though we did enjoy a few drinks during happy hour!!
All in all this has been our best trip to New York and I would say this has been one of the best hotels we have stayed in and we are currently planning our next trip and will definitely be returning to the Sanctuary.

Stayed at Old Town Inn for -- nights in March. Trip Adviser was right on. Room was ready at check in. Desk service was exceptional. Good continental breakfast. Close attention to details. Didn't hear a bad word from anyone while there. Recommend highly.

Our stay was one night, quick stop between Denver and Colorado Springs. This was close to hotel and customer service was good. Hotel very clean, staff friendly, would stay again and recommend.

My husband and I stayed at the Amalfi for - nights and chose the hotel based on its location, amenities, and good reviews. We were very happy with our stay and could not have asked for more. Good location, good staff, good rooms, good bar...which along with the restaurant was CLOSED to hotel guests on a Tuesday evening of my recent stay, because of a private party. Not acceptable for a supposed -* hotel. There are plenty of hotels in DC and I'll be choosing one of them for my next stay.

This hotel is not worth of being called a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". I'd rather call it a dump. This is an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""old-style"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" grand hotel with a huge lobby, a few shops on the premises, and a lovely Japanese garden. During my seven nights of stay, the cleaning staff always forgot something, be it forgetting to add soap, tea and coffee bags, or tissue paper. Though there is a big screen HDTV in the room, the few available channels were all NTSC quality and the TV doesn't do a good job of up-conversion. Aside from the room itself, everything else costs extra, the gym, the pool and internet connection are all additional daily-rate charges. You could do a lot worse for the money, but it's not a four star like advertised either.

The hotel provides valet parking for $---night. I chose to park at the Latimer Parking Garage on Latimer Street (on Latimer between --th & --th, the Radisson is on --th). The staff there was awesome and the price was right! $-- per -- hours!!! Best deal downtown.

If you're going to visit Philly stay at this hotel and you won't be disappointed!

Stay here and you won't be disappointed!

room was booked with starwood points, and an upgrade was offered to a premium room. Room was very spacious, two qs beds, several desks and sofas. very clean. outstanding bathroom. Service at reception was also very attentive, e.g. helped finding a medical center and made all arrangements for us.

On parking, a --$ per day fee was quoted for the garage accessible through the hotel (independently owned). Turned out to be --$ per calendar day, resuming counting hours at midnight. gets to --$ for noon-to-noon parking.

Can't wait to come back to Denver and I will def. book my stay here again!! 
Take advantage of the complimentary breakfast. It smelled and looked yummy, unfortunately, I wasn't able to try it..the timing was always off.

We stayed for - nights, two adults and two girls aged - and --. Very pleasant stay, spacious rooms, which comes in handy when you're more than two staying the odd night. There were two switches on the wall, one that turned on every light in the room and another that did nothing. You need to turn on all the overhead lights in the room in order to turn on the bathroom lights. This is probably because of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""peeper"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" art on the wall between the bathroom and bedroom. It would allow you to see someone in the bathroom from the bedroom through the screen painting on the wall if the lights were only on in the bathroom. If you are travelling with friends or family, this could be very annoying.
The hotel may be loved by the trendy crowd that likes odd and uncomfortable. I prefer functional, comfortable and relaxing.

Beautiful grounds? -Yes.
T.Cooks, one of the best restaurants in the country on the property? -Awesome.
Having a car service on the property always ready to go? -Very convenient.
Beautiful view of Camelback? -Fantastic
And...Quiet, Comfy, Laid Back, Un-crowded
Unexpected and Unforeseen Problems:

The location is great, just off Time Square. There are only two very small lifts servicing the whole hotel (only one in the main area), so going up and down was a pain, we ended up taking the stairs on most occasions.

The reason for the low score is that it doesn’t cut the grade for a -*, it’s a very good -* in a very good location.

Igor instantly built rapport without being over familier, and nothing was too much trouble for any of the staff.
Our deluxe room, whilst not huge, but how much time do you expect to spend in your room? was very comfrotable and had everything we had expected including a docking station for our iPod.
Being a small hotel there are no gym facilities etc.. but then the overall theme, ambience and quirkyness is so much more interesting than the run of mill faceless international chains that you will barely notice.
The roof top bar is great, in fact it featured in The Sunday Times --nd July, as one the best roof top escapes in New York, however, it's popularity also means that it is beseiged by the 'after work crowd' especially on Thursday's, and hence you may not be able to get a table. The Library's location was also perfect, close enough to -th Avenue, the Subway, Times Square etc.

All in all well very, very good, I wouldn't hesitate to either recommend The Library or indeed to rebook on our next trip to New York.
Excellant.

We stayed at the Hotel Donatello for - nights and it was a perfect stay. I chose this place primarily for the location and also the fact their amenities included a microwave and a small fridge, so I could make simple breakfast and meals for my toddler. It turned out to be more than I asked for! 
First the location was great. It had the BART, MUNI, and the cable car that would take you up the hills to fisherman's wharf with in very close walking distances, with in a few blocks. It got a bit noisy one part of the night on Saturday but only for about -- minutes. We were glad that we didn't book a hotel at the Fisherman's Wharf after visiting there... there were so many tourists, and just so congested in general. The Union Square area that Hotel Donatello is in was perfect. Not too far from any of the key places, and most places were very walkable.
The service was always prompt and friendly, by everyone including the porter and the concierge. We called the front desk for a taxi at the last minute to get to a wedding, and a limo service was waiting downstairs- and the price was better than what a cab fare would be. In a small drawer are metal utensils, and up on the shelves are mugs, glasses, bowls and plates.

One extra note-- I had left my son's favorite DVD in the room and didn't realize until we got back to the east coast. I called the hotel and they promptly mailed it to me, packaged safely in a cd case and a bubble protected envelope!
Highly recommend!

I don't think we will go back to the Excelsior when there are so many wonderful hotels in New York City.

Would benefit from a visit from the -- minute makeover team. Very run down. Very noisey with doors banging all night & people shouting up & down the hallway at all hours. Curtains all holes. Never again.
Just across Seventh Avenue as you exit Penn railway station with direct link to Newark airport. Nice room, great bar and only -- mins from times square and ESB by foot we stayed four nights

However we were able to hang out on the roof for the Saturday night parade and have a nice view. Booked through Priceline NYOP for $--- a night. Would stay again.

What a great hotel, location couldn't be better.

.Staff were helpful and friendly. 
Right off Times Square ideal location.
Our room was nice and brighta bit small but what can you expect for New York. Hope to be back again next year and would stay in this hotel
The only draw back was the halls were decorated in dark wallpaper which made the hall quite dark.
Don't believe all the bad reports , you just can't please some people

This hotel needs some immediate TLC. No question about it...the bathrooms are very cramped, and the bathtubs are just substandard to say the least. I would not say this is a value for the money. Lassandra who cooks the complimentary breakfasts in the morning always greets me by name with a big smile. Absolute treasure. She sets the tone for a great day.
 Ryan who works the front desk is super-friendly and always makes you feel right at home when you check in, even at --- on Monday mornings he is always upbeat. Great folks.

my family and I stayed for - nights at this and will be back next time we are in San Diego. The staff was pleasant and helpful and the room met our expectations in every way. thank you so much.

We stayed at the Fitzpatrick hotel over July -th weekend, having chosen it based on Tripadvisor reviews. We weren't disappointed. The last thing we were not crazy about was having to call for ice there are no ice machines on the floors.
Having said all this, the Fitzpatrick is still most definitely worth a visit! The pros far outweigh the cons.

Convenient clean. Decent breakfast small pool. Friendly helpful reception. Near to shop at garage when vending machines not working . Easy to find. Easy drive to restaurants. Mission bay and beaches. Free car parking near to rooms.

I took a lot of pictures of this hotel, our room and of Manhattan.
All the rooms are newly renovated, no more stinky carpets, and dirty paints and curtains as posted in old reviews. All are sparkling new (we were allowed to see other rooms for review). We could not hear any pounding or men at work, or the busy streets down below at all. And I am very sensitive with noise (I wake up easily when I hear footsteps several feet away). 
We had a nice view of the Hudson river, watching the sunset is a treat for me and my camera. The towels and sheets were changed everyday. I had a great time exploring New York City after a good night's sleep in this hotel.
Location-wise, it is very close to Macy's, Duane Reade, McDonalds (open -- hours), a subway station we did not try, taxis are everywhere (cheap rate we were surprised)...

The hotel staff and receptionists are very nice and courteous. The security manager even allowed me to take lots of pictures of the hotel. We felt very safe there, and we saw a lot of people checking in on the weeekend. My husband and I were expecting worse, to be honest. But we were very satisfied with our stay there. As for amenities, we did not try out the gym but my husband did go to the laundry room (we ended up going outside for dry cleaning). My husband did not like the washing machines, only half of the machines worked, he said. 
We used the flat iron and the ironing board, which are tucked away in a small closet. The closet is a bit small if you have lots of clothes and bulky luggages. My husband and I had - carry-ons (about -- x -- x --"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", the standard size for Delta airline luggage), and two personal items-I had my camera bag, tripods and my husband had his backpack.
There is a vending machine near our room, so we had steady supply of ice for free, and the diet pepsi costed a dollar which isn't much for us.
We did not eat in the in-house restaurant because we wanted to explore other food and dining.
All in all, we would recommend this hotel for people wanting to get a lower price and a great stay.. If you are looking for a bigger space and room, be ready to spend more money. You get what you pay for.

We then went on to the Korean Monument as we had seen it before and wanted to see how the bushes (to resemble rice paddies) had grown in since we had seen it last. On Saturday we walked to the new Spy Museum to buy tickets. They only had tix for -pm so we bought them and then had Lunch at I think it was called Gordon Biersch or something like that. We then walked (a very long walk) to the Air and Space Museum then walked back to our hotel to freshen up (a very very long walk). Next we took a cab (had enough walking for one day) to the Spy Museum. I will be returning to DC and will be staying at The Hilton Garden Inn for sure.

-) Parking is ~$---night. As this is not really SeaTac (nor downtown) and there is a huge parking lot adjacent to the hotel, this seems a bit tic-tacky for a mandatory """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""fee."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" However...
-) The free breakfast is worth ~$-- and is significantly better than the usual """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""free Continental"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sort of deal you typically get. They offer what I would describe as a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Denny's type"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" breakfast (eggs, omelets, bacon, sausage, pancakes) in addition to breads, fruits, yogurts, cereals and various drinks...all of it included and as much as you want to bust a gut with. -) Free drinks at -:--! Actually, this is a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Manager's Welcome"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sort of deal...whereby you can go to the little bar in the atrium and have a couple of mixed drinks, beer or wine and popcorn or chips & salsa.
