I stayed at the Westin LAX several years ago and had a great stay. This time after I walked in my room and set my luggage down I noticed there was dust on the dresser,tables etc. I don't usually complain but it just seemed like the room hadn't been used in a while. I called the front desk and they sent someone up right away to wipe things down. The hotel was a great location close to LAX and offered a shuttle to and from the airport. This Westin just isn't as nice as other properties I've stayed at but I did enjoy the heavenly bed, very comfortable. Also we used the pool which was ok. The workout facilities were really nice but I didn't get a chance to use them.

My husband and I decided to try The Benjamin in March of ---- because we wanted a more intimate experience than what the larger hotels provided. We were not disappointed. The staff was exceptional, the lobby was elegant and when we got to our room, we were very pleased with the comfort and luxury. We felt very pampered and our every need was met. We loved it so much, we are returning again this weekend (May ----) for our annual trip to NYC. I have no doubt The Benjamin will be our hotel of choice whenever we visit New York in the future.

It was overpriced however expedia made that not matter. It has a great location. It's an old hotel however so the usual can be expected. Bad plumbing, no electrical outlets. WIFI is --.-- per day. THere is no laundry service. Hardly anyone in the hotel speaks english as their first language. The coincerge is overworked and hardly ever available. Make sure you do your planning ahead. You can walk to virtually everything but be careful because it's all hills. I recommend the Sight Seeing Tours in the Double Decker Buses or $-- a piece. It's definitely worth it and you can get on and off at all of the places you would want to visit in downtown San Francisco. The cable cars are $- a piece one way. Make sure you know which direction you want to go though! The coincerge told me to just jump on one and it would take me where I wanted to go....NOT TRUE! After a $- dollar ride down the hill I had to pay another $- dollars to take me back up the hill in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""correct"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" direction. Overall San Francisco lives up to the hype though. It's a cool place but don't think you are going to be able to have fun on a BUDGET. It's a pricey place and stay at one of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""brand"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotels so you get the amenities at no extra charge and where the hotel staff is a little friendlier because of their corporate structures. P.S. There is no laundry service at the hotel. They outsource it so expect to pay TIME AND HALF if you need something the next day. P.S.S There is no pool and parking is $-- dollars a day. Don't pick up anything in the room that looks like food or beverages. It's spring loaded and will charge you automatically. I feel sorry for someone who tried to clean out the fridge to put in their own stuff =) We walked a block to the liquor store and got a bottle of awesome wine for $-- dollars instead of the same bottle in the hotel menu for $---.

Stayed at Staybridge with family, although was two blocks from time square, area was very uncomfortable and not safe feeling. Location is near parole office and parts of area are dingy. Breakfast was boring and same foods rotated every three days. It was nice however to have breakfast available. Elevator was slow and took a long time to reach lobby. Service was good. Staff was accomodating. Free laundry mat available for guest use. Price was reasonable with negotiation, but I personally would not return because of location. I recommend this hotel because it is new, clean and up to date.

I've stayed at this Hilton on multiple occasions for fly in-out trips for business in LA. Unlike some other hotels around LAX, Hilton is clean, well organized, and open late hours. Hotel is in need of updating and I wouldn't recommend it for extended stays for conferences or extended business travel, but for staying close to LAX, it's very well suited.

My husband and I went to the Inner Harbor for a dinner cruise. Stayed at the Sleep Inn & Suites Downtown Inner Harbor and it was wonderful. Rooms are very modern from the flat screen television on the wall to the walk-in shower in the bathroom. Rooms were very clean. Got a great night's sleep. Continental breakfast was also good. Great distance to the Harbor and the front desk was very friendly and helpful on how to get around in the city. We thought it was a great price for the room that we got and we will definitely stay again.

Would stay here again. Easy access to Fort Sam and the airport. Plenty of dining options close by.
The front desk staff was very friendly and professional. The room was a good size with a functional kitchen and a comfortable bed. The free wireless was was fast enough to stream video (much appreciated!). 
Didn't make it to the manager's reception, but the free breakfast was nice. 
Some of the room surfaces are a bit dated, but otherwise an excellent stay.
Friendly staff, clean big rooms, good breakfast and a nice pool for the kids. We would definitely stay at this hotel again.

I live in Washington State but work in San Francisco (computer consultant). I like this Travelodge for a number of reasons. It's very clean and well maintained. The rates are very reasonable for central San Francisco. For me it's cheaper than renting a studio apartment. It's an easy half mile walk to-from work. It's also an easy half mile walk to -- Hour Fitness with whom I have a membership. The rooms have a microwave and a decent sized refrigerator which makes it nice to buy some groceries from the nearby Safeway for use during the week. Being right on Market Street it's easy to hop on one of the MUNI trolley's ($-) that travel from Upper Market all the way down to Fisherman's Wharf. Roger is the manager (owner?) and is always courteous and helpful.
I find it helpful to where earplugs, though, for sleeping because the walls are a bit thin and the street noise can be a bit loud with emergency vehicles and some party-goers at the nearby drinking establishements. I'd recommend asking for a third floor (top) room to avoid noises from occupants in the room above. And the further away from the street the better to minimize noise. I find the king size beds comfortable (firm) and the large firm pillows comfy, too.
I don't have a car in San Francisco so I walk or take public transportation. Parking at the motel is extra ($-- + tax per day) and is reasonable for the area. There's easy quick access to highway --- just a block away.
I recommend this motel.

Everything about this stay was PERFECT - Location, parking, staff, room, bed, noise level (NONE), breakfast. Couldn't get over how friendly and helpful all the staff was Would highly recommend to anyone - I'll be back!

Long check in lines, unfriendly and unhelpful staff, and a tired feel to this hotel make this a low choice in New York City. Lobby nice but for some reason always crowded. Everything an extra including checking baggage and Internet. Front desk was understaffed and undertrained in customer service. Rooms had a worn out feel although clean. Most staff seemed annoyed by guest questions. Restaurant closed outside seating early and clearly wanted to close even though plenty of guests wanted to eat and drink. Overall very average and very disappointing. Will not stay here again. I believe the hotel has been sold - maybe that is why staff was apathetic.

Stayed - nights for business. Free parking, free breakfast, free internet, excellent downtown location - that all for a great price. Free shuttle was a nice surprise. I used it to get to my meeting at the Intercontinental rather than having to pay for their valet. Not sure how old this Holiday Inn is but it looked brand new. I took few shots of my room, which had everything I needed. It was quiet, super clean, with the new modern furniture, good selection of cable channels, lovely bed with soft sheets, full size mirror (important!), good-size working desk, etc. The bathroom is not very big but perfectly suits to a single traveler. It has all the amenities you need. Ladies will certainly appreciate the big mirror (again), good lighting and plenty of counter space. 
The business center has - computers with medium internet speed. This time I drove my own car, so I liked that the parking was gated and they had a security guy on at night. The front desk was efficient. They even called me when I was late for the shuttle -- min before my meeting. Except for the fact that I got lost getting back on freeway going home, everything was superb. I'd stay here again.

I stayed at this hotel for a week at the end of January ---- and found it a very enjoyable experience. The hotel is located a couple of blocks away from Pier -- and the cable car terminal and so is ideally placed for sightseeing and getting to all parts of San Francisco. The reason I am writing this review is not the hotel location but the friendly and helpful attitude of the staff and the quality of the rooms and service. There is an excellent Italian restaurant and bar linked to the hotel reception area. However, the main attraction for me was that the hotel Manager holds a very friendly session every afternoon at - p.m. in the reception area with a selection of free local wines and pizza. It gives a unique opportunity to meet and talk with other guests from around the world.

The hotel's location seems a bit complicated to reach on week-ends due to the Interstate closure due to construction. Again, this is week-ends only for now, BUT, I wouldn't let this stop me from staying here. Comfortable upscale hotel moments from downtown Austin. 
Just ask the great front desk personnel such (like Erin) to print you off directions to downtown using the back way! It's much nicer than the interstate if you ask me! Simply cross over the Interstate and drive to South Congress and just before you cross the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lake"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" you will be in this ultra-hip area called SOCO. Great """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""roach coach"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" choices to enjoy but don't overlook the tacos at Wahoos! 
The staff at this property were pleasant and helpful. The concierge level is worth the extra $$! Restaurant was very good and reasonably priced. My fiance had the hanger steak and was a happy camper! I'd highly recommend this clean friendly property - free parking and an evening shuttle!
Great location, but tired dirty old hotel, friendly receptionists, but the hotel is very tired looking with few facilities,

My husband and I just spent - nights at the Arizona Biltomore where he was attending a conference. Our room was spacious and newly renovated. We had a king-sized bed, large TV and - sinks in the bathroom. We had a patio that overlooked one of the pools. The linens were lovely and the bed was comfortable, although a bit too soft for my liking. There was a clock radio that was also an iPod docking station which was nice. The room had a typical mini bar with overpriced items, but that was to be expected. Instead of a coffee maker there was a hot pot and French press. 
The food and service were good. Drinks were overpriced we thought. There were many places where groups could sit and chat, inside and out. A few areas had large gas fire pits which were nice during the cool evenings. 
This facility felt more like a business conference center than a resort hotel. There were two or three conferences going on most of the guests seemed to be involved in one of those. The pools were fairly deserted, I never saw anyone playing tennis and there were very few children. I rented a bike for an hour one day and rode along the canal. All I saw were the backs of some very uninteresting houses. There didn't seem to be any interesting places nearby to ride to. 
My husband loves this place -- probably because he usually has meetings in office buldings or boring conference centers. For him it was a real treat to spend three days in such a lovely setting. I think everyone in his group felt the same way because they all decided to hold their conference there again next year.

On a budget? Stay here! Extreemly clean, very helpful staff, very safe location, and right off Broadway! The budget price allowed us to enjoy so many more sights in NYC! The beds were SO comfy! We weren't looking for high class, just a clean safe place to rest our weary bodies, and this was it! Close quarters, but plenty big enough. Bring your own shampoo, and if you're a tourist, we highly recommend the New York Pass, get it at Planet Hollywood. This hotel has character! Not much street noise either.

Jsut returned from San Francisco. Our stay at the Marriott on Fisherman's Wharf was great. From the clean room to friendly concierges, our every request was met quickly and with a smile. I would stay there again. We did not eat at the hotel as some local diners were within walking distance. We had a great internet rate and were treated like a King and Queen.

This is a nice hotel that I stayed at to attend a conference that was going on within the hotel. I must say I was shocked when I wanted to order room service at --:--PM and was told they closed at --:--PM. AT $--- (incl taxes) for a one night stay I expected more.
I agree with many of the other reviews that there's room for improvement. Great location though!

Well, it's the Chelsea, and to be honest it was exactly what I expected, good and bad. It was just a single night stay, as we passed through New York on the way home, and I have to admit it gave me a tremendous buzz to walk in through those hallowed portals, with their lists of people who had lived and died here, and march up to the desk saying """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""I have a reservation"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The room was tiny, and we had a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""semi-private"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" - i.e. shared - bathroom which was two corridors away. The room also came with retro egg-shaped chair and complementary dead cockroach. The other downside was that the desk staff only existed to check you in and out - any requests for help, from advice on internet access to taxi-bookings, fell on deaf ears. And yet, and yet, it is great to stay in a living legend. The selection of art down the stairs, the notices, the personalised doors, etc. etc. were a joy to behold. Highly recommended - but for a short stay!

I might have more to say if I actually paid for the place, but I was with my parents so they spotted it. We had a clean room in the mundane bland rooms you'd expect from a Courtyard Marriott. We did get a little lost looking for the place so make sure you got the maps down right (I think google led us astray). Breakfast wasn't free, and in fact quite pricey...but really there are plenty of place to eat in San Antonio so why bother with the food here?

I tend to stay here when I have a flight back home early the next morning….it beats fighting traffic from Bellevue (where I have business)…..Steakhouse downstairs is open for breakfast and there’s a shuttle to-from the airport that runs every ----- minutes…….Never had a bad experience, but I’m pretty easy to please…..

This Hyatt is my favorite in Seattle - gorgeous rooms with nice views, perfect location and great staff. Room rate is unfortunately too high for corporate travel budget nowadays, but for those able to spend a little more for the kind of luxury this Hyatt offers, I'd say it's worth it, particularly for special occasions.

I stayed at the W for - nights (-rd May --th May). I was originally assigned a corner room with a connecting door - which you should definitely avoid - I could hear every conversation happening in the connecting room - and my neighbours were talking in a normal volume. I requested another room and was moved straight away.
My new room was on the --rd floor with a great view of Times Square. Very New York - but if you are particularly bothered by noise and light - it might not be the best place for you. I was awoken early on Saturday morning by a very loud concert in the middle of Times Square and the room is lit up by very bright lights on the side of the building, lighting up giant billboards.
I didn't mind too much as it was part of the experience of being in such a great location - and the room did have blackout curtains. 
Other great things about the hotel were the great trendy atmosphere, comfortable modern rooms, relatively well equiped gym, friendly staff, good security (won't let anybody up to the lobby on the -th floor without a key at night), great comfortable bed, really cool bars and high definition televisions in the rooms.
All in all - a very enjoyable experence.

My name is Tony """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Buck"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Buckner and I recently stayed at this hotel. It is a wonderful place to stay. The rooms are clean and the staff is accomodating, respectful and friendly. You are a third of a block from a bus stop and - short blocks from the trolly and Union Square. The Carran theater is across the street, very nice Blues club around the corner and a night club across from that. Walking distance to shopping, resturaunts of all kinds and theres a Walgreens(for toiletries, medecine, snacks and such) a third of a block up the street. The room only has four channels for the TV but if your going on vacation to watch TV this isn't the place for you. For - dollars you can gey a nice breakfast at Dav's next door which includes eggs, potatoes, toast and meat and it's good. There is a door that lets you into Dave's from the hotel so you don't even have to go outside and the staff is very nice. The front door of the hotel is secure access only with your room key which is nice. You can't go wrong with this hotel if your there to see the city. You can even book tours from the hotel staff and if you need directions they have conveniently provided small free maps and will give or get your directions to any place in the city. I will go back to San Fran again and I will stay at this hotel. There are not many plug in's in the room but I was still able to run my laptop everyday conveniently from the desk in the room. You don't need a fridge because ice is free. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone traveling from overseas because the staff is multi-lingual. You won't go wrong with this hotel.
The staff was also friendly and helpful in addition to the entire facility being very well maintained and spotlessly clean,

This hotel was fantasic, when we arrived they took are bags up to the room for us. When we where leaving the lift was not working so they came up to the room and took the bags down for s as well, the staff where very friendly and gave us information on where to visit and eat etc . 
We where due to live when the hurricane was about start, they informed us that if our flight was cancelled they would do everything they could to give us accommodation or find another hotel. 
The only down side which is not the hotel falut was that the restraint staff where rude and u had to Leave them a tip. 
But I would defiantly come again

For those taken aback by really expensive San Fran hotels, you'll welcome a stay at The Mosser. The rooms are clean though small. But if you're out at a conference as I was, that's not a problem. I did choose to have a room with my own bath. All in all, a very good value.

It is rare tht you find true class in chain hotels.The Le Meredien San Francicsco is pure class -and no trace of snobishness!
Greeted warmly,we were able to check in early,upgraded to a lovely large studio room(jr.suite)with incredibly tastefull furnishings,a fantastic bed,wonderful bathroom stocked with interesting high end bath products,and a great veiw of the sky scapers of San Francisco.
Upon return that afternoon we found a birthday cake and card-very sweet gesture.And the cake was scrumptious!
There is very good coffee and tea set out in the Lobby in the morning.
Every single staff member was smiling and helpful during our stay.
Loved the location.While it might not be Ideal for a family looking to explore SF for the first time,it is a great location for those of us that already know the city.Much nicer than SoMa,Union Square,or Market street.
I look forward to returning to this fine hotel.

Very nice hotel, not the most fabulous but nice enough. The staff were very helpful and pleasant. The only thing was the cleanliness of the bathroom and the window was broken. Otherwise could place to sight see from lots around and easy access to transportation.

We held our annual industry golf tournament at the Palmer course, and not only had a fantastic day, but everything went off like clockwork - the course was in great shape, despite the drought here in Texas, the staff was fantastic (particularly Kelly and Monica on the bev cart), and the lunch afterwards was great - fantastic day at a fantastic facility !!

Our room was quite nice and well equiped with amenities. The staff in the hotel were super nice and the concierge was great! The location of the hotel was about - blocks off Michigan Ave. so it was a little less congested there and quieter. We walked every where; the city was fantastic and all the venues from museums, restaurants, tours were the best! We would definately go to Chicago again and stay at the Talbott.

My wife won tickets to see Chris Daughtry at a venue near this hotel so we booked a room. It was a great stay. We arrived late but had no problem getting a room. The staff was friendly but check in was somewhat slow. There were four customers ahead of us and yet it took about twenty minutes to get through check in. There were two people on staff behind the desk. In and out parking was available and recommended.
 The room itself was large and the bathroom was outstanding (other than there not being an exhaust fan) There was a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""pocket"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" door separating the toilet and shower - tub from the sink area. This was one of the nicer rooms that we have stayed in for some time and I was definitely impressed. While there, be sure to take in the view of downtown from the swimming pool atop the building (--rd floor). There is also a fitness room on this floor. Lastly, don't miss out on the free breakfast buffet served on the second floor. The food was hot, delicious and plentiful.

I entered the hotel, the lobby was HUGE and filled with people. Very nice, but extremely crowded. I kept wondering why all of these people were hanging out in the lobby of the hotel when they paid almost $--- a night for their room. I was told that internet is only free in the public areas unless you're a Hilton Honors member or pay the nightly internet surcharge. They should really review this policy as it makes the hotel look like a encampment of people on their laptops and tablets and detracts from the hotel's beauty. 
I upgraded my room to a top floor with a balcony. For over $--- a night, I guess I expected something more than a typical """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Days Inn"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" or """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Super -"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" room. Other than the balcony with sliding doors on the top floor, this room was nothing special. Very basic. Bed was comfortable, staff were pleasant, but the hotel honestly reminded me of that one time I made the mistake of staying at Circus Circus in Las Vegas. Way over crowded, and people tripping over each other. 
Room service fees were off the charts and the highest I've ever seen in my life of traveling.
Even though there were about -- employees working the front desk, check in was still a long wait. 
The hotel location is optimal, thus my choice of this hotel. However, the management could understand that keeping everyone in the lobby on the internet makes this look like a cheap hotel and customers would be better in their rooms and not making the lobby look like the gate at the airport or a homeless shelter. 
Perhaps for the money and this being a prime location Hilton, I was expecting too much, but it is a Hilton and I've come to expect a lot from them. This hotel failed on many levels. None severe, but it wasn't up to par on the level I expected from Hilton or the price paid. 
There are no vending machines in the hotel, and if you want ice, you have to go through service employee doors and take a service elevator to another floor to get ice. Come on Hilton. This hotel was packed, and you can't put an ice machine in a customer area that is safe and presentable to put an ice machine? Aren't vending machines a common courtesy to have on hand for your guests?

The lobby is nothing impressive, the doormen are useless (I had read comments about that, I'm even wondering if they don't do that on purpose ...)
One of the bar is closed due to work (I asked about it, it's been more than a year, and it is not precise on their beautiful website).
The maid woke me up at --h--, with my hangover I was pretty upset. 
I went for just for one saturday night (it might not be enough to fully enjoy the hotel, as suggested by the receptionist). The bar was small but full (W reputation ?). I ordered some food overnight, it was good. 
The room are spacious, even tough the mirror was not even fixed on the wall. And yeah the bliss product are nice.
The staff is so so (except the last receptionist when I checked out).
Ok, but far from being """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cool"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and obviously overpriced.

We Stayed for a weekend and was ho-hum about hotel. The location was great right off of North Michigan Ave. The room was small & the bathroom even smaller. More of a european type hotel. The hotel was clean but maybe a bit rundown. Service was average. If you can hotwire the hotel for a low price like I did, it's OK, but probably we will not stay here again.

We stayed at this hotel about - years ago and enjoyed it very much. However, this past stay we found the hotel is aging and hasn't had any serious renovations in years. There was mildew on the caulking of some tiles in the bathroom. The television remote inconsistently controlled the volume. The pillows were pathetic (and that isn't an overstatement). The floor lamp near the window was in such a position that the power plug had pulled loose from the outlet and it wouldn't reach to outlet to reconnect it. There was no coffee maker in the room (seriously, in a business hotel, no coffee maker?? This is a standard feature even in a Motel -). There was a light bulb in the main lobby elevator area (outside the elevators in the hallway) that flickered - over three days and no one bothered to change the ballast or the bulb). I called down the concierge twice one morning and no one ever answered the phone and no voice mail or forwarding. Gave us and looked up what I needed on the internet. Would not stay at this hotel again until improvements are made.

We stayed - nights pre-cruise and loved it. It felt like a good, grown-up New York hotel. Room was big, good housekeeping, excellent customer service. Had drinks and apps in the bar one night and that was good. Location is excellent. Got a good deal on Priceline.

The Arizona Biltmore never loses its class. The grounds of the hotel are incredibly beautiful, with the heat of Arizona being the only unpleasant part. The staff is attentive and friendly. The many swimming pools are wonderful and you can always find one that suits your mood. The rooms are updated and exhibit the same timeless charm as the rest of the property. I highly recommend.

This is my third time in New York City and I had an amazing experience every time. This is my first time at a --star hotel and it was tremendous.
The service was impeccable. I could not be happier with The Peninsula.
From the start, the staff are very friendly and helpful. From the bell boy who chatted us up to the concierge who spoke French for your convenience. Everyone smiled and greeted us. The spectacular staircase entry to the beautiful, spacious rooms. Love is certainly in the details. Everything you need is in your room: stationary items, a sewing kit, jogging route, plush slippers, free newspaper delivery, A-C control panel, mood lighting AND music in the bathroom. And on and on. Strangely, no coffee maker. There's complimentary coffee at the pool. 
The breakfast restaurant was near-perfect. We were forgotten about on the first day because we were in the other room, not the main room. Second day, my eggs were not prepared correctly. Wouldn't be a big issue if it weren't for the --star rating. They apologized repeatedly and comped my meal. I do think $- for a cup of coffee is pretty steep. No matter, through Expedia, we got a $-- breakfast credit per room, per day. Great value.
I will be back in September.

The Courtyard Boston Downtown-Tremont is very conveniently located in the theater district. Access to I--- is a few blocks away, and the neighborhood seemed quite safe with plenty of restaurants in the area. 
That exhausts my list of positive things to say about the Courtyard.
 As others have noted, the parking is a startling $---night even though the garage is across the street. My room was very small, which is understandable since this is a fairly old property. What was not understandable was the utter lack of intelligence displayed in the layout of the room. The desk area that occupied the outside wall of the room had a set of --- drawers along the right hand side. The drawers, however, could not be opened because they were blocked by the bureau that sat next to the bed - see the picture below. This bit of room design failure would probably have escaped my notice (I rarely use the drawers in hotels) if it weren't for the fact that the desk was not level and the drawers slid open on their own and came to a rest against the side of the bureau even after being closed. The bathroom is also extremely small - there's just enough room for the toilet and a sink. There's not even a vanity on which to place one's toiletries. Hopefully my room is not representative of others in the building. 
 In short, I simply cannot recommend the Courtyard Boston-Tremont.

I stayed here in October ----. The main reason for me choosing the hotel was due to it's airport location and complimentary shuttle bus as I was on a late arriving flight.
The public areas of the hotel are clean and welcoming, if a little dated. The front desk staff were extremely efficient and helpful on check in and a credit to the hotel.
I had upgraded to a club level room located on the highest floor of the hotel. Whilst the room had all the basic facilities it was most definitely in need of refurbishment. The carpet had several stains and the walls were marked in several places. There was a letter in the room explaining the hotel rooms were undergoing refurbishment, this is much needed as the rooms are very dated and not what you would expect from this brand.
Room service was quick and efficient, all the staff are encountered throughout my stay were friendly and courteous.
If all of the rooms are being refurbished I would definitely stay at this hotel again, although I'm not sure the additional supplement for a club room is worth the money.
The location is great if you are going to be spending time in downtown LA. The common areas are really nice, and the rooms are aged but well kept. Would stay here again if I return.

Excellent for a business stay - staff was very good, hotel was clean 
Parking was very reasonable

I stayed at the Omni on Dec. ----- with hubby and two small kids. Service was great from the get go. My kids were delighted on receiving goody bags filled with toys and candies upon arrival. We were there on our anniversary and noted that on our reservation. When we arrived in our room, we had champagne and chocolate covered stawberries (and lots of it) waiting for us. Very, very nice. They really went out of their way to make our stay enjoyable. This was truly the best hotel experience I or my husband have ever had. I did not have a single complaint during my entire stay. I will definitely stay there again next time I'm in SF.

Stayed at this location due to walking distance from hotel. I would recommend this hotel because it is within walking distance to the airport, which makes it possible for business colleagues to arrive at different times and not worry about transportation. My friend stayed at the hotel next door and preferred to spend the evenings at the Wyndham, so I would assume that says something about the comparison. The rooms were well kept, generally clean, and had no problems with any of the housekeeping responsibilities (towels, beds, straightening up, etc.). The breakfasts were really good and never had any problems with getting food, nothing ran out. The wait staff was also very friendly and prompt, even getting yogurt from the back for a guest when it wasn't at the buffet that day. Very good breakfast service! I only had two complaints. I could not connect to the wireless network since it was not accessible from my room. The lobby was a very strong signal, but it didn't even pop up in my room. I will confess to not attempting to resolve the issue internally with the hotel as I was able to access the neighboring hotel's wireless network using my friend's login information. The second problem was that on my third day, I woke up to find a --inch long red and black cockroach looking insect in my second bed. The location of this hotel was VERY convenient. It was clean and NO BED BUGS which I had been obsessing about. Friendly staff. Jamie and Bradley were very helpful. In June I returned for my third visit in three years to the Hollywood Hills Hotel and I love it a little bit more every time I go.  I travel to Los Angeles often on business but when I get to choose the hotel I always pick the HHH.  This time I stayed for -- nights and more than ever appreciated having basically a luxury apartment with hotel trimmings instead of being cooped up in a hotel room for all that time.  I also save a small fortune on room service!
The hotel has two beautiful pools, one (unheated but quite warm enough when I was there) is right by the apartments but if you prefer a heated pool you can stroll two minutes the hill to the main building (the magic castle hotel).  The main building also has free wifi, which I used every day.  I stayed in a massive - bed suite with kitchen so I often cooked in the room and ate on the balcony and kept the fridge full of snacks.  There were two TVs in the room with millions of channels, a good safe, lots of hanging space and lovely fluffy towels and linen.
For me the main thing about the HHH is the absolutely beautiful views over Hollywood from the apartment rooms.  I spent most evenings sitting on my balcony while the sun went down and it's incredible to enjoy the view of a bustling city from such a tranquil viewpoint.  There are also some very cute squirrels in the area and a friendly local cat.  It's very lush and green up there and feels far removed from the hustle of LA.  The staff are still as friendly as always and make you feel completely at home without being intrusive.  If I win the lottery I plan to move in there forever...
As always, I think it's pretty essential to have a car in LA but I did walk from the hotel to Hollywood Blvd and it only took -- minutes.  You can reach some nice bars, shops and tourist things on foot, but to make the most of Hollywood and the surrounding areas I would recommend you hire a car.

It probably isn't for you if you want the big fancy hotel service experience since they don't do things like room service or laundry but the staff are really helpful and knowledgeable about the local area.  Its perfect for the independent traveller who likes their space and privacy but enjoys amenities like a swimming pool.

The lobby is stunning, the pool is attractive and our room was fun (it reminded me of something out of an Austin Powers movie) as well as comfortable. The staff were generally friendly and helpful and contrary to some other reviews here, we heard no noise whatsoever in our room even though we were on the --th floor and so, not far from the nightclub. It's also in a great location, (literally) on top of a metro stop (Hollywood-Vine) and about ten minutes (slow) walk along Hollywood Bvld to the Dolby Theatre, etc. 
But the whole time I was there—we stayed - nights—I felt like the uncool little sister tagging along to the cool kids party and I think the hotel played a part in making me feel like that. This wouldn't be so bad except for the fact that I was paying for the privilege. 
The lobby (or the Living Room in W-speak) was constantly filled with a variety of posers, wannabes, etc., especially in the evening, but of course the hotel can't really control that and it is supposed to be a profitable business after all. But approaching the doors in the evening, we had to show the doormen our key before we'd be let in—and then do it again to get to the elevators. We stayed there over a weekend, and met many a drunken waif stumbling along the halls. I just didn't feel comfortable there. Honestly, I felt like I was intruding on someone else's good time, and shouldn't be there. When you stay in a hotel, all areas should feel like yours to avail of. I certainly didn't feel like that here. 
But the real issue with the W Hollywood is the nightclub-pool situation. The pool IS the nightclub, or part of it, which is not owned by the W but is a location of Drai's, who are also in Vegas. To access the rooftop pool (level --, I believe) you have to go all the way down to the ground level to get in. There are signs in the elevators saying this is for """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""occupancy control"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but really, it's for admission control. There is a special line for hotel guests, but no preferential treatment. On Saturday evening we approached the concierge about the possibility of getting into Drai's that evening, and he was (very nicely) straight with us: unless we forked out $--- for bottle service—with a rule of one bottle between every - people—we didn't have a hope. (Which made me wonder, who IS going to be in the club?!?!) We went to the lobby bar instead but one of my friends, undeterred, decided to try to get in anyway. She spent -- minutes talking with various members of staff before being finally allowed in for the last -- minutes of the club evening, at a cost of $--. She reported that although the view of the pool was nice, the club wasn't even all that special. 
Clubs in W hotels are not unusual. All Ws have a trendy nightclub atmosphere to some extent. The W Times Square is a good example, but I've stayed there twice and have never felt like anything but a valued and welcomed guest. The problem with the W Hollywood is that their priorities are all wrong, because their priority is the club-nightlife. This is far from a cheap hotel and when you're paying a lot of money, you want to feel like the hotel appreciates that. Here, I felt like the hotel """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""belonged"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to the people in the club and the lobby—who probably weren't even guests—and that I was intruding. 
I gave it --- stars because you really can't fault the decor, the cleanliness or the location. But if I were the management—and especially if I were Starwood—I would think twice about how this hotel is run and sold. As a former front desk agent myself who had to deal with guests complaining about one of our three swimming pools being occasionally closed for private functions, I can't imagine the grief the W's front desk gets about the pool, nightclub, noise, etc. Really, they should detach the club from the property altogether, and stop advertising the fact that they have a pool. Alternatively, guests should be given unlimited access. I just can't imagine why they're not. I think the management forget that although LA residents may expect not to get into places without waiting in line and then, being at the mercy of a bouncer, people from outside of LA—and especially people from outside the US—will see it for what it is: an utter farce. 
If you know what you're getting into and you get a good deal, I'd stay at the W. But if you're a non-celebrity civilian, I'd stay away. Also, I'd NEVER stay here with kids or extended families. It's highly unsuitable. 
In summary, the W is kind of like Los Angeles itself: a magical playground if you're somebody, but depressing and uncomfortable if you're not. But then it's free to walk around LA; it's a small fortune to stay at the W. Why pay to feel like a nobody? I'd happily stay at other Ws because I love the décor, the beds and the Bliss products in the bathroom, but in future I'll be giving this particular one a miss.
A tip for parking: avoid the $-- a day W parking. There is a large parking lot on the same street about -- seconds walk from the door that does overnight for $--. Just make sure to buy your ticket earlier in the day as we came back one night after --pm and there was no attendant. We didn't want to chance parking without a ticket so we had to find somewhere else.

Travelled from the UK and spent a week at the hotel....hoped to see the blossom, but unfortunately we were too late! Were upgraded to a larger room on the -th floor. Rather disappointed to have no view, but in retrospect we were not disturbed by noise at night .... it was the quietest hotel we had ever stayed in! As other reviews have stated, the bathrooms, although modern and attractive, do not take account of one's modesty and the sliding door in particular was a cause for concern as it did not close the gap! I used the towel rail-towels to ensure I couldn't be seen on the lavatory. I was a little shocked at the prices of the 'goodies' and drinks in the room (we didn't buy any) but that maybe something to do with the exchange rate! Hanging space was minimal and we had to put most of our clothes in the drawers. 
We thoroughly enjoyed the steak bar for evening meals and breakfast, although again we found it rather expensive. The roof top bar was amazing and we got some great shots of the city at night. You do have to book in advance however, if you want a seat. Wine was very costly. -- dollars for the cheapest bottle of red which we got at the store round the corner for - dollars! 
The highlight for us was Jon the concierge. He made us feel like we were the only guests in the hotel! He gave us lots of great recommendations, in particular the free organ recital in the beautiful cathedral... amazing and definitely worth a visit. He made sure we got the best seats on the roof for a view of the sunset over the Whitehouse. The hotel should be very proud of Jon.... he is a real asset and would definitely encourage us to return to the hotel. 
I would agree that the hotel must have one of the best locations in the city. We were able to walk quite safely round the city, both day and night... we even walked to Georgetown... and it is within easy reach of all the museums and Capitol Hill. It is also close to the Metro, which we loved as it is so easy to use and inexpensive. 
All in all we returned to the UK much fitter and buzzing from a great experience. We shall no doubt be back!

At first glance the Hotel Whitcomb seems like a beautiful old building that offers rooms at very reasonable prices for San Francisco however my experience with this place was beyond sub-par. I don't recommend it to anyone. For starters, I walked into my room and the light switches did nothing and it was pitch black. I held up my cell phone for a source of light, fumbled through the door with my bags and searched for a lamp. I quickly noticed that a large portion of the ceiling was peeling and the room felt dusty. I went to the bathroom and turned on the light and could barely look in the mirror. The light was terrible and made you feel like you were in a morgue. I proceeded to find hair in the sink (GROSS) and promptly tried to get some sleep. As I went to set the alarm I noticed that the clock was off by about - hours (helpful). The street noise was pretty bad (which on some levels I would expect...it's in the middle of the city on a busy street) but my room was by dumpsters or something because there was a lot of extra noise directly outside which made sleeping incredibly difficult. The next day I asked the front desk for the free wi-fi code and he informed me it was down and I should try again in the morning. When I went back into my room, I experienced the same issue with the light switches and was immediately frustrated once more. Later that evening after I had finally fallen asleep the people in the room next to me came back and I learned just how thick the walls were. It was a -nd night of terrible sleep. I woke up feeling positively exhausted and unable to focus well at work. Since this was a business trip I felt really deflated by my stay. Do yourself a favor, research research research and spend the extra cash on a place that promises to give you a decent night of sleep.

This hotel largely meets the standards of other Kimpton Hotels, as indicated in many of the other reviews. But there are a few things one should know about it.
There are very few truly quiet rooms in this hotel. Many of the rooms overlook Spring Street, a steep grade on which trucks constantly grind their way to the top. Other rooms (the largest and nicest) cluster around the elevators, which chime whenever the doors open. If you don't mind this noise, the hotel will be a fine place for you. (For the others, I think the hotel should have a stock of white noise machines on hand to lend to guests.)
Second, if you bring your own car, be aware that some of the cars are parked in the open, apparently near a colony of large birds. My car was returned to me covered with bird droppings. This, I was told, might happen to about one-third of the parked cars on a busy night.
Finally, although the rest of the hotel measures up to the high Kimpton standards (especially the staff), the rooms lack the usual good FM radio-CD-speaker systems that distinguish Kimpton from the pack. In addition to our TV, we had only a little bedside clock radio. Decent enough in quality, but by no means special.

This was our third stay at the Mayflower Park and each has been pleasant. The staff are courteous, rooms are clean and the restaurant and bar serve good food and drinks.
The hotel is located near the Westlake Center, which is convenient for light rail and bus transportation; Macys and Nordstroms are across the street and other major retailers are nearby.

Been to this hotel twice I recently took a group of trainees there. It is clean comfortable and the staff is very friendly. There is shuttle service from the airport a nice swimming pool and fitness center. It is conveniently located across the street from a huge mall with lots of dining and shopping options. Ideal for business and stopovers.

A small group of us stayed here for the duration of - nights. The hotel is located in the China Town district of Manhattan and is only a - minute from multiple subway stations. The area is a typical Chinatown (although much larger than I am used to) with noise and foreign smells in abundance. The hotel has friendly and efficient front desk staff. The rooms are small but are clean and well decorated. Breakfast is reasonable, but the paltry dining area gets very crowded forcing you to either wait or get some food to take back to your room.

We stayed here two nights while touring around Manhattan and we couldn't imagine a better place to stay. From our room we could see the Statue of Liberty and beautiful sunsets across the Hudson. Wall street and Trinity Church are within walking distance and the local pizza places were fantastic.
We also enjoyed walking over to Battery Park to watch the sailboat races in the late afternoons. The hotel staff was friendly and the rooms were beautiful.

Einstein said that a sign of mental illness is repeating the same behavior over and over and expecting a different result. We have stayed at this hotel on multiple trips even though the very nice junior suites share a connecting door to the next suite, a suite inevitably filled with very noisy guests who seem to rev up after midnight, stretching into the early hours. There is something wrong with the sound-proofing, and perhaps with the clientele. 
 Why do we go back? The rooms are pleasant, the staff helpful, the location excellent. The morning dining room staff are delightful. We keep hoping the last experience with sleep deprivation was just a fluke.
 There has been renovation and the newly decorated rooms are pretty. The bathrooms however would be a little risky for older travellers. There is no grab bar to hold onto getting into the tub for a shower and the tub is slippery. There is also no soap holder for the shower, making soaping up awkward. The toilet is too low--perfect for a five year old or the height challenged.

Really liked the Pacific Terrace hotel. It's a smaller three story hotel overlooking Pacific Beach, separated from the beach by the popular - --- mile boardwalk. Our room was nice, decorated in a Caribbean-tropical theme. Nice limestone bathroom, separate sink area with a mini fridge. 
 Everyone working there is super friendly and helpful. Complimentary continental breakfast included lots of choices: cereals, fruit, yogurt, bagels, pastries, coffee, juice. At breakfast you can also pay for a cooked meal, but lunch and dinner are not offered, nor is there a bar in the hotel. (Complimentary glass of wine delivered to your room on your first night, and of course, lots of watering holes nearby.)
 I think all the rooms have at least a partial ocean view, which is how our room (---) was listed, but I really couldn't have asked for more """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""view."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" Our balcony was good sized, overlooking the ocean and the courtyard where the pool and hot tub are. Didn't make it for a workout in the fitness center which is a small room in the parking garage, but got plenty of exercise on the boardwalk and in the pool.
 The location is great, couldn't be closer to the water, and right on the city bus line. Lots of restaurants and a grocery store within walking distance. Loved Pizza Amore for salad and thin crust New York style pizza. Would not return to the Green Flash restaurant, and the restaurant JRDN (yes, that's spelled correctly) was too hip for us---think """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""ultra lounge"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" but the food was good (and pricey).
 I would definitely return, but probably only in winter. If you're a people-watcher you'll love the ---- walker-jogger-bike-rollerblade-segway-skateboard-dog-stroller traffic (got the picture?) on the boardwalk, but if you like your privacy you might find the constant parade a little intrusive. Even though the courtyard and pool area are walled and gated, a large part of the wall is glass so that you can see the ocean, but the boardwalk users can look into the courtyard and even into your room if you haven't closed your shutters. In January even during bad weather, the boardwalk was used pretty heavily and I'm sure it's crazy crowded in summer. But that's the urban beach scene and I don't fault the hotel itself for that.

I actually booked this reservation with the hotel over the phone and got a great rate -- much lower than the usual price! It was a lovely hotel, beautifully appointed, walking distance from the places we wanted to go. We would highly recommend the Fairmont.

We landed here randomly via Priceline, and were really grateful. It's a lovely hotel -- great beds, nice little gym (very well-equipped), breakfast is pricey but good, amazing cookies for the asking at the front desk, nice Neutrogena toiletries in the rooms (even sunscreen!). But we were just blown away by the kindness of the staff. The manager (whose name I will almost certainly misspell, so I won't even try) was extremely accommodating. Barbara, at the front desk, gave us a coupon for Legoland that saved us $-- -- she just happened to bring it from home on the off chance a hotel guest might need it. The dining room manager. The housekeepers. I could go on and on. Not a single person working at this hotel was ever less than helpful and friendly. One of the most consistently pleasant hotel stays I've ever experienced. We are hoping to go back soon...

Checked in on Friday afternoon. Visiting with friends who were determined to keep me up past midnight, a very tall order.
The hotel is comfortable and we had a nice king room with big windows that weren't blocked by other buildings. The decor is post-modern and the bed was extremely comfortable. So was the chaise lounge where I snoozed after a museum visit.

This hotel is in a great location for a NYC vacation, but otherwise was very underwhelming. The elevators were very small and we almost were stuck in one on the night we were going to Broadway...the elevator jumped and stopped at the next floor down and did not do anything until we tried hitting another floor, then did the same thing again one floor down, we finally were able to get out and walk the stairs for three floors. Other aggravations: espresso machine down, internet down one morning, printer not working, towels very hit or miss, were changed for a Coke from the minibar that we did not take (had to call, will be reimbursed), as we left we being pushed into using their car instead of a taxi for trip to airport.

I get to New York quite frequently, and usually stay on the Upper West Side or in Midtown. On this trip, I was attending a meeting at NYU, so I decided to stay close by.
When I chose this hotel, I had some concerns because it is part of the Choice Hotels group, which I associate with downmarket motels. However, the Solita Soho is part of their boutique Ascend Collection and is absolutely fine, and not a bad value. The room and bath were well-equipped, though it's time for them to replace some of the towels. The staff was friendly and helpful. For me, the main negative point was the flaky Internet service.
The hotel's location is great for lower Manhattan. The hotel is surrounded by Little Italy, Chinatown, Greenwich Village, and SoHo. It's only a -- minute walk to the WTC area with shopping at J&R and Century--. About - different subway lines stop two blocks away on Canal Street, so it doesn't take very long to get around the city. But most of what you might need is within walking distance.
Would I stay here again? Definitely yes.

my boyfriend and I stayed here for - days in order to explore San Diego. Hotel staff were friendly and accomodating. Happy hour in the bar ---pm Monday to Friday with free appetizers. - trolley stops were --- minutes walk from the hotel and the entrance to Gaslamp Quarter just around the corner.
We had asked for a corner room with view and a refrigerator and both were supplied. We had room --- overlooking the convention centre . doggy park and trolley-train line.
The only downside was the loud whistle from the Coaster train a couple of times from midnight to -am....we had been warned about it and ear plugs were supplied. There were many hotels on the same train-trolley corridor so they would experience the same .
I would not hesitae to recommend the hotel to friends and family and would stay there again.

My husband and I stayed here for the final - days of our """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""great California adventure""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""
We booked the -rd floor presidential suite and it was AMAZING. I was lucky enough to use my entertainment book and got the suite for --- price.
We had a huge balcony overlooking the pool and ocean. It had a great table and chairs and we sat for hours enjoying the view and the wine!
The staff was kind and left us some champagne for our anniversary
This was easily the NICEST hotel I have ever slept in!

This place was very noisy: street noise and guest noise from hallway... This is actually more like a motel, and two-stars at most. The floor also seemed to be quite shaky. There are only about -- parking spaces available (maybe less).

This hotel was a little gem. Great location, affordable, clean, super nice staff. Breakfast provided well done. Will stay here again. Only issue, not the hotels fault was the Just Tires store blasts their music at the crack of dawn. Could here that with closed windows. Try to get a room not facing that store.

Very friendly staff. Safe parking. Large room with all the necessary amenities with a fridge. Nearby restaurants with delivery are very convenient. Free internet is a plus, although the connection was not great. Thank you for a great stay.

While the rooms are tiny (no drawers for clothes!) we extremely happy with the deal we got for this room.
The location is great for exploring manhattan. There is a major subway stop just down the block and it was easy to walk to Times Square, Central Park, etc.
The staff was quite friendly throughout the stay, and our room was clean upon arrival and nicely cleaned each day.
Avoid using the hotel business center if possible. The cost is $-.-- for -- minutes.
On the weekend, particularly Friday night, the bar had quite a crowd and seemed popular. We felt too under dressed to go in!

The staff in the hotel are very nice. The hotel itself is a little old school, but clean and quiet. The location is great for getting downtown and to the museums on the metro rail. The price is reasonable compared to other Houston hotels.

We thoroughly enjoyed our stay and will defintely stay at the Edgewater again. We were upgraded to a premium room on the -rd floor on water side and you definitely get a close up view as the hotel is build over the water. The rooms are designed to have a rustic look with lots of wood and a small sitting area by a gas fireplace. The king size bed was very comfortable with lots of pillows for lounging. The bathroom had obviously been upgraded to include a claw-foot tub and separate shower. We only had breakfast in the restuarant, however the food and service was good and we had a lovely banquette overlooking the water. There are a number of good restaurants close by on the water, if you can't get into the hotel restaurant -- and you can enjoy a glass of wine in the lounge or by the fireplace in the comfortable lobby area.

We booked the Halcyon Hotel knowing that is was NOT a five star hotel, but it turned out to be no where near or nothing close to what they advertised on their Web Site!!!!! 
We were put in a front bedroom, downstairs room---which--it turned out was right over top of the boiler!!!!! The room was soooo hot that we could not stand it. When we called the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""night manager"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", he said that he would send over another small fan and get back to us in the morning-------that NEVER happened!!!! We could not leave our window open, because of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""homeless people"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sleeping in the sidewalk in front of the hotel, and besides the only way that we could even leave the window open was with a piece of wood that was left in the room to hold the window up. The room was NOTHING like the pictures and it was so small that our double bed(which had springs poking thru)was touching our teenaged daughters small single bed. There was no kitchenette(as was advertised and showend in the pictures) just an old table with a few, old kitchen items. The bathroom was VERY tiny and the door would not open completely because it hit the bed. Our shower, which only had a glass door and no other door for privacy, was right in the room-----so none of us had a private shower at all.
I would NOT recomend this Hotel, at all, and would encourage the owners of the Halcyon to not try to entice people to book their hotel by posting images that do not show the true appearance of the rooms.

My family and I recently stayed at he Marriott Marquis in Times Square New York. It was the best service I have received in a very long time. We were taking tours kid to NY for the very first time. My wife and I had been there before but this was the first trip for the kids. I had requested in advance a complimentary upgrade(if possible) since we were very close to celebrating our --th wedding anniversary. I also mentioned in my email that this was a family trip and we would appreciate any assistance since we wanted to make this trip extra special for the kids. I arrived first since I was coming directly from a business meeting. Upon arrival I noticed we had been upgraded to a center view room. Our view from our room of Times Square was just outstanding. Shortly after arriving I heard a knock at my door and was shocked to see a large table with an iced champagne bottle, - glasses, several bottles of different kinds of juices for the kids, a box of imported chocolates, a basket of snacks for the kids and a nice 'welcome to our hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" card from management. I'm already a Marriott client and I often stay at Marriott for my business trip but this was beyond what I expected. The hotel management also provided us with concierge lounge access which was very useful. I'm so impressed with the management there and this type of service and is the reason I keep coming back to Marriott. The NY Marriott Marquis was extra special. The hotel is centrally located as well. Nice clean rooms, attentive staff and they have the best workout room I've found in any hotel. While I've enjoyed great service at most Marriotts this was by far the best and the most attentive. It's so nice when you plan a trip and don't regret your choice of hotels. Thanks again to the NY Marriott Marquis management. You've done well and have earned my loyalty.

This hotel was one I would stay at again for business. Location was great. It was clean and staff was nice. However, it was a bit louder than I would have expected being -- floors up, and there is a fire station next door. That being said, I didn't really feel like my sleep was interrupted.

The lobby looks great and the staff is friendly but this hotel needs a lot of improvements. The valet service is slow and you can't self park. You can't get espresso at the coffee bar. The rooms could be cleaner (black stuff around inside of toilet). The walls are thin and noise from hall and surrounding rooms is easily heard. The staff are very friendly but can't make up for the average accommodations.

The hotel is old, with very slow elevators. The rooms are small, though well kept. The location is only - blocks from the Space Needle and related attractions, so it is in a good place. As others say, the carpet is outdated and worn, though the beds and water pressure was good. The breakfast was fine.
We are a family of five. We paid $-- for one room and $--- for another. In retrospect, for less money we could have stayed at a Westin Suite in much nicer accommodations for less. Few frills, high prices. We won't be going back to this hotel.

Located near the WTC the hotel does its best to be a clean, efficient business hotel. Rooms-bathrooms are good sized and the location benefits from being off West Side Highway (without being too noisy) and close to subways and access to NJ and Brooklyn. Navigating the maze of construction can be work but is manageable. Did not use business centre or restaurants but rented card from Hertz which is a five minute walk. Overall, good call and would even consider for non business. Pleasant, renovated, strong WiFi and good staff.

Stayed at the Edison for the second time from --th to --nd August this time with my grandaughter and it was great. The room was spotless and kept that way by the hard working staff. Fresh towels and bed linen daily. We were on the --th floor and had no problem with the lifts,we did not have to wait long for one. There is always a member of staff on duty to monitor who goes in the lifts so security top notch. Cafe Edison can be reached from the lobby and is good value. There is a room on the -nd floor that has computers in and for a few dollars you can stay in touch with friends and family on face book or twitter (more important to some people than others) Also easy to do filght check in and print boarding pass. On the same floor is a free ice machine .Over the last five years I have visted New York once or twice a year with family or friends and have stayed in different hotels in various locations and all more expensive than the Edison. Every single hotel can be improved one way or another whether its the decor or service or cost and customers requirements
vary so an hotel that suits all is impossible to find. I highly recommend the Edison for location, comfort, friendly helpful staff and price. In fact I am already planning next years visit with my daughters.

I got this hotel room for my bf and I to crash in after a concert. We paid a very discounted price b-c I got it on priceline. I would have been horrified if we paid full price for this place, and truthfully if I could have cancelled and gotten my money back upon stepping into the lobby I would have done so. 
It was REALLY dingy, our room was damp, dark, and smelled like mildew. Everything needed updating. The shower-tub leaked. The place was just icky. There just wasn't anything appealing about this place at all.
One pro is that there was complimentary wi-fi.

Why stay here? Many reasons:
Central location: walking distance to everything. Friendly, helpful service: from the front desk to the concierge, everyone is friendly and eager to help. Fully-equipped rooms: full-sized fridge with ice-maker, dishwasher, coffee maker, glass-topped cooking surface, micro, all modern and in good working order; large room, great desk surface, adjustable desk chair, easy chair with ottoman, full bath with plenty of room, views, great TV, lots of drawer space. Bed: very comfortable mattress, pillows, and linens. Sleep: quiet. Breakfast: everything - scrambled eggs, bacon-sausage-ham, toast, fruit, yogurt, juice, milk, coffee, panfries, muffins, hot and cold cereals.
What could be improved? Only a couple of things:
Closet- tiny. Elevators - can be very slow (no freight elevator, so three small elevators just don't do it). Lighting - not bright enough throughout room, and one side of the bed doesn't have an end table or a light. Bathroom lighting isn't good for putting on makeup.
The benefits of this hotel greatly outweigh the few difficulties. We used one suitcase as an endtable, and put things in the many drawers that we might normally put in the closet. We stayed for a week, so we had lots of things with us, and it all worked.
When we return to NYC, we will stay here.

The place was clean ,friendly staff . We could not get our beauty sleep since we could hear from both sides of the walls.. The walls are paper thin. Also this place is VERY pet friendly ....so if you don't want to wake up from dogs barking outside your doors,don't stay there..

We stayed here for one night as part of a park-sleep-fly package which was quite reasonably priced. We didn't see some of the problems other people refer to. Perhaps our vision is bad. It would help to have a GPS when looking for this hotel. Since our flight was so early, we didn't get the included breakfast. If you are here without a car there are not many restaurant choices in walking distance except an expensive restaurant at the adjoining Comfort Inn. A few places deliver to the hotel (Chinese or Pizza).

My husband and I stayed for - nights at the Hyatt, October -th – --th. I would say that yes, it defiantly is not Hyatt quality but it is not horrible like some of the reviews have read. It is in need of renovations, the carpets desperately. The staff was nice and friendly. Location was great! We booked through priceline and so were not guaranteed a specific room. I called a few days ahead of time to request a king size room, we were put in a room with - double beds the first night. They didn't have any king rooms available until the -nd night so they told us to have all of our stuff packed up and they would switch us the next morning. So we went about our day and came back to a king room. I thought that was great that they accommodated our request even though nothing is guaranteed through priceline. The beds were very comfortable, one of the most comfortable hotel beds that we have ever slept on. All in all, it was a great experience; San Francisco is a amazing city. We didn't eat at the hotel due to previous reviews and we feel as though, hotels are in the hotel business, not the restaurant. We have never had a fabulous meal at a hotel so we just choose to stay away from all hotel restaurants.

The hotel ended up being $-- more when we arrived. Then we got to the room and was missing light bulbs and a remote to the TV. We complained to the front office plenty of times and they kept saying they would come and fix it NO they didn't. They later tried to charge me for the light bulb and the remote. I had to talk to - different managers in order for them to take the charges off. Also the place had roaches and the doors would get stuck. Basically the house keeping was very nice. But if you don't have to stay here then don't. After reading the reviews before I stayd I thought it wouldnt be that bad but YES it was!!! And the Wifi only worked in our room if we sat in one spot.
DONT STAY HERE!!!

The hotel is centrally located----the Cherry Creek area of Denver is wonderful for shopping and dining-----this hotel had wonderful service----the restaurant was excellent as we ate there lunch and dinner because it was cold and snowy outside----the rooms were perfectly comfortable

We picked this hotel because of the price, the included breakfast and its location. It was easy to find and we had access to two subway stations that had different lines that ran through them. The hotel room had recently been updated and it was great -- small, but that's to be expected. The pillows weren't very good, but the new decor was really nice. We were on the --th floor and had a gorgeous city view. The lobby was in the midst of a renovation so it was a bit crazy, but they were making fast progress and it was looking really nice. The proximity to the airport and airport shuttle was great, as well as the shuttle driver, who was very helpful. The fact that there was a fridge and microwave in the room was great, since I have special dietary restrictions. The pool and spa area was clean and I enjoyed using them both. The free wifi was excellent and fast. The only negative is that I had a room facing --th Street, and the traffic noise was loud (to me) during the evening and sometimes through the night. Then again, I am used to a very quiet home in the suburbs, so it may not bother you if you are used to city living. I would definitely stay here again!!!

In the center of Charlotte, walking distance of everything, it was just right for our weekend trip. The Bank of America building was our view from our room window. The most important thing was the staff. Everyone was pleasant, ready to answer questions and help out. Even the guys who parked the cars seem to go out of their way to make sure we were taken care of. The hotel was somewhere I would go back to stay and tell others to stay there. The cost was very reasonable.

Disclosure: I am a Chicago native. My friend from college was visiting, and I wanted to find him a hotel with (a) excellent service, (b) outstanding location, and (c) something historical. Because I am a Chicago native, however, my review (perhaps paradoxically) will not be as in-depth. 
I love the feel of this hotel; it is the most unique hotel I stayed in regarding two respects for ME. One, it feels very historical, which I love. Two, the service is something I have not experienced in other hotels. However the system works, the staff seems to always be on top of things. We requested a cot so I could stay with my friend, and without a problem the staff provided it. I also liked the free newspapers in the morning (including Sunday's NY Times). As to the room, it was just perfect. High quality, pleasant, comfortable, and cozy. 
We did not use the hotel's restaurant, however, and we had breakfast and lunch and dinner in the surrounding area. You have many and varied options. I have heard great things about the restaurant, but we did not go because of convenience.
If you are visiting the city, you will love the location. You are in the center of all the action. I have myriad recommendations of what to do, but I will defer to the excellent staff and your own planning. I honestly do not want to bias your trip too much. Chicago has a tremendous amount to offer, and I know you will enjoy your time!

Really cool contemporary design, excellent location. The service is a bit snoby.
What modern hotels should be

The location was excellent as it was so close to Central Park and the Museum of Natural History.
The air conditioner was very noisy so we had to sleep with it off which meant the room was quite hot. An overhead fan would have suited us better, however, overall a good hotel and very grateful that the staff could look after our bags for several hours whilst we went sightseeing the day we checked out.

I'm staying tonight at the Red Roof Inn nearby. $-- a night cheaper, just as convenient, much quieter and cleaner and modern.

We stayed at the Omni La Mansion del Rio for two nights while on family vacation. The hotel was our launchpoint for activities like Sea World, the riverwalk shopping, the riverboat cruise, the Alamo, the market place and the mission tour. Aside from sea world and the mission tour, everything else was within walking distance- although the market place was a pretty good walk for late June. My point is, the hotel is centrally located for many of the major attractions in downtown San Antonio so I was very pleased with the location.
When we arrived Friday evening about -:-- PM, I parked across the street at the city operated parking garage. Cost was $-.-- instead of the $-- for valet parking at the hotel. If I were repeating, I would do the same thing again.
Check-in was simple and I was nearly immediately directed to my room on the -th floor. Even though the hotel was older and our room was --- sq ft with - double beds, it didn't feel cramped. As expected from a hotel of this quality, the room was immaculately clean.
We found the pool smaller than any other hotel pool we've stayed at over the last year, and then since the pool goes to a depth of - ft, only half of the pool was only practical for use by the kids. Combined with the large number of guests in the hotel, it was also VERY crowded and we couldn't even get seats in the chairs - of the - times we were at the pool.
I also had issues with the Omni kids program on Friday night and Saturday night as well. I complained to the front desk on Sunday about my experience and they more than compensated me for my trouble. Although we had problems, they were very attentive and concerned to make things right.
Every employee I interacted with at the hotel was gracious, smiling and accomodating. I felt very welcome.
While TripAdvisor asks us not to disclose actual pricing, I'll simply say that I had a special offer of buy one night and get one night free. While the experience at the Omni was very nice, i would hesitate to stay here again at normal advertised rates.
This is because I find I can get more for my money at other hotel chains. For example, the Omni does not include a complimentary breakfast. We did eat at the Pesca restaurant while here (which has some association with the hotel), and while the food was very nice, the bill for breakfast for a family of - was approximately $--.
Other examples include $---night for hotel parking, $- bottled water, $- in-room snacks, $-- wifi (unless you are a member in their free guests program), etc. I also found the in-room refrigerator full of the expensive hotel drinks so we did not have room to store our own families drinks.
My conclusion is that the Omni La Mansion del Rio hotel is exceptionally nice and I certainly enjoyed our stay, but I work too hard for my money to be so liberal with the dispensation.

Went for a long """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""girls weekend"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and loved this hotel. It's a great botique hotel and sister hotel to the Hotel Monaco. Kimpton really seems to get the botique thing--great hip decor, comfortable beds, really nice linens and room accesorries. Loved the ---pm free wine. (nice wines too . . .)The building is very historic and it's architecture is amazing, much has been preserved. The other great reviews of the staff are true, everyone was very helpful and friendly. H & M is around the corner, as is Marshall Fields (great food court in basement) and right next door is a Walgreens so don't use the mini bar!

We stayed at this hotel March - April ----. The Location was fantastic, with a good view of Alcatraz from our second floor room. The rooms however were slightly shabby but nevertheless clean. The ihop next door was great for breakfast and the check in staff were pleasant and courteous. Average hotel in a great central area.

Despite the fact that the hotel is located at downtown, the area is not very friendly and at night we did not feel really safe. There is a Starbucks right next door to the hotel, but the breakfast buffet is really worth the -- Dollar at the hotel, give it a try! And there is one big downside: The hotel is located next to a police station... you do the math.

River Hotel is priced like most Chicago hotels - expensive - almost ----night, but doesn't deliver anywhere near the service expected for that service. Most disappointing was the room - it was barely could fit in the queen bed that was in there. Its almost as if they cut the rooms in half some time ago to maximize occupancy.
