I don't even know where to start with this hotel... We booked this hotel on Priceline- we figured that since we were only in Memphis for two nights, we didn't really mind too much where we had to stay. I will NEVER make this mistake again. 
The experience at the Crowne Plaza started off on the wrong foot when we got straight up rudeness from the manager who checked us in. However, we brushed it off and went up to our room hoping for the best. I can say, without hesitation that this is the worst hotel room I have ever experienced. The beds are hands down, the WORST beds I've ever slept in (my friends and I actually decided to sleep on the floor the second night). We woke up from a restless right with back and neck pain. The bathroom had some sort of red (blood?) stains in it which freaked us out. The air conditioner was dripping and that wound up soaking one of my travel bags before we realized what was happening. Room service promised -- minute service but it took -- minutes. We tried to take advantage of the pool, but the staff decided to clean it in the afternoon- when people were trying to swim. Parking costs $-- which is kind of ridiculous since this hotel isn't even in the downtown area.
One pro of the hotel is the shuttle service. The drivers were very helpful and friendly. No complaints about that. We did speak to the hotel staff upon departure in regards to all our complaints. We got a lot of excuses but not much we could do at that point.
Last time in Memphis, we stayed at the Peabody- that was one of the BEST hotel experiences I've had. Do not make the same mistake we did. Spend a little more money and go for quality.

I cannot say enough wonderful things about the James. From the room, to the concierge Bill and Toni to the wonderful staff throughout the hotel, gym, etc., this hotel is a hidden gem two blocks from Michigan Avenue. It's beautiful, comfortable, and professional. I cannot imagine staying anywhere else. This is my second time staying there and I was welcomed back (They remembered). They catered to every need we had and were very informative. I can't imagine staying anywhere else in Chicago.

Very typical for this class of hotels. Some high points...some reception personnel very helpful and friendly, rooms are spacious, internet reasonably quick, restaurant and hotel reasonably priced. Some misses...missing light in the room, false alarm fire alarm, hang up call in the middle of the night. My current pet peeve--nice LCD TVs but analog signals. Really, no HDTV in Houston?
The bar has limited seating; only a handful of chairs...if you want to eat dinner and watch tv, you may be out of luck. Restaurant food was OK for what it was, but service was slow. Overall, very satisfactory but forgettable.

My doctor booked my sleep study at this location, thinking it would be better than the sterile environment of a sleep clinic. 
Well, I've had to deal with drilling in the walls starting at --:--pm. It's now -:--am, and this has been going on every -- minutes for ----- minutes at a time.

Never again will I stay in this pit, where they don't value business.

I stay here just about everytime I'm in town to visit friends and family. The hotel underwent significant upgrades since changing from an Adam's Mark to a Marriott. Parking is free and easy since you can park in the front or side of the building yourself. The lobby is spacious and the staff are pleasant and attentive. The rooms and bathrooms have been updated significantly and are now modern and quite clean. The beds come with more than enough pillows and are very comfortable. Free wireless internet is available. Weekend rates are a steal!

I had a quick stay at the Roosevelt this past weekend and I must say I was a little disapointed.
LOCATION-
Perfect for Midtown at --th and Madison. I think it's a great location. There are plenty of restaurants around and all the transportation is close. Bryant Park (my favorite spot in NYC) is just about - blocks away.
LOBBY-
When you arrive you are almost blow away by the stately beauty of the lobby and public areas. Almost stunning. It's been beautifully restored.
ROOMS-
Mine was tiny indeed. Actually it was so tiny there wasn't even a desk for my laptop. But hey this is NYC. The bedding is comfortable with nice linens and pillows. There was also a great flat-screen television.
Okay, so far I have only stated the positives.....
Well, this is one of those hotels that LOOKS and SEEMS great at first glance. And really for all practical purposes, it's OK.......
However, if they don't start to keep this place up, it's going to be nothing more than a run-down tourist hotel within another -- or -- years.

If you get a good deal on the place, I say go for it. With the exception of the shower issue, I think only very experienced travelers would find issues.
The hotel management just needs to get this hotel on it's P's and Q's and it would be fabulous!

We booked this hotel through Hotwire.com. Some other reviewers had bad experiences but ours was fine. Staff treated us well and we got a king-size, non-smoking room, as reserved. The parking garage is somewhat convenient though you have to cross Wabash to get to it. If you have a vehicle, it's easy to get in and out. And the location is great, near a lot of shopping and parks. Other reviewers have mentioned the small room and I would agree but it was accomodating for two people. The bathroom was okay. Conclusion: a clean, nice-looking hotel with great location and service was worth the price we paid.

First, I would like to start by saying the staff at the hotel was wonderful! They were so pleasant and helpful. Next, the location was perfect! It was close to everything. The subway is basically right out the door and everything else was in walking distance. As for the room, we originally booked a - bedroom suite but were completely surprised when we checked in and they upgraded us to a - bedroom suite. I traveled with myself, my husband and our - children and the room was perfect! Both bedrooms had private bathrooms and queen size beds and the living room had another bathroom and a queen size fold out sofa. The kitchen was fully equipped with microwave, full size refrigerator and stove (however, do bring some extra pots-pans if you plan on cooking a lot..they did provide dishes and silverware and one skillet.) Overall, the hotel was GREAT! I would definitely recommend this to anyone and everyone, especially families!

Centrally located (--mt from Magnificent Mile) it's a good hotel with confortable rooms.
Ask for high flow rooms .
Downstairs , close to the hall, a Starbucks where you can have real espresso

Wonderful place to stay for a family of -. Breakfast was phenomenal. It would have been even better if we didnt have to wait -- minutes when checking in. I would stay here again. Great Value for San Diego area including free parking.

this is a well situated hotel in which we had two different rooms for two recent stays within a few days of each other.
The bathroom in one room was so difficult to enter,you almost had to be a contortionist.
My real complaint was the fact that I received and paid two separate bills which were charged to my credit card ,but when I received my card account there was an item for several dollars charged the day we left.There were absolutely no extras to account for this,and onemailing the manager of the hotel as to the reason for this he or she failed to reply.
Not the sort of treatment one expects at a so-called boutique hotel as they describe themselves

I stayed here for - nights in early November ---- on a business trip. The location is not very close to the T, but I took taxis which was fine (and there always seemed to be taxis lined up outside so you don't even have to have the front desk call one for you). The room was spacious and the front desk staff were very nice. I have to say I was very pleasantly surprised as New Englanders aren't exactly known for their welcoming manner, but the people working at this hotel were extremely polite and friendly. I have stayed at Residence Inns before, but this one was by far the nicest. Having breakfast included and free wifi is a nice bonus, too. I would stay here again if traveling to Boston for work.

My friends and I just finished staying at the Club Quarters in Houston (I'm actually typing this from the lobby!) It is very nice. Free high-speed internet, very clean, and very secure. You need a room key to get in the building, activate the elevator, and of course to enter your room. The breakfast they provided was great as well. The reviews that mention it being in a bad part of town are correct, however, it seems that there is no """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""good"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" part of downtown Houston. 
But, unless you are traveling alone, DON'T STAY HERE!. The rooms are by far the smallest hotel rooms I've ever seen. I read the reviews that mentioned this but didn't think much of it. We had two twin beds and there were four of us. Just having one room for four people is understandably our fault, I'm just using this anecdote to illustrate the size of the rooms. With two people sleeping on the floor, there wasn't enough room for our luggage anywhere! We had to keep it in the shower because there was literally no room on the floor. 
The hotel has clearly divided what was once one normal sized room into two tiny rooms. This is evident by the --- window we had that seemed to disappear behind the partition. I'm sure the people in the room next to us were looking out the other half. 
Everything about this hotel is great except for the room size, which a HUGE drawback. It could work for one, but that's it.

Let me start off by saying that this hotel is awful. There is this weird hippie guy that checks you in. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""office"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is a room full of space with a broke down counter in the center of the room. I was just a little bit disappointed by my stay at the Argonaut. I had expected a quirky but stylish and classy hotel, whereas in reality the hotel had a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""theme park"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" feel, like an attraction designed to titillate tourists. The design is fun and our room was very comfortable in all respects. The service was more assembly-line than personal.
Perfect location! Right in the center of the entire area. Great place to have as a home base when traveling about the area.

I would not receommend this hotel for a business traveler. I stayed at this hotel for a business meeting that was to take place at the hotel. I stayed in the hotel part of the resort. First of all, there was no wireless internet. I found this a terrible inconvienance. The only internet connection was found at the desk which was in a different room than the bed. I prefer to work on the bed. Further, when I tried to connect to the internet, it did not work. After spending -- minutes on hold with IT, I was told it was a hotel problem and nothing they could fix. 
There were no vending machines. I am supposing they wanted to encourage you to use the minibar. However, be careful with the minibar charges. I found out on my bill a week later (after looking at my ebill on the website) that I was charged for way more than the water that I took. It took several phone calls to rectify that situation. 
Another reviewer talked about room service but I could not find anywhere where there was room service. I was forced to eat at the worst mexican restaurant in history which was a restaurant choice at the hotel. 
I would recommend this hotel for people on vacation and people with families. There are pools and a variety of restaurants on the property that would make it very convienant for the vacation traveler. Of course I have to admit that the vacation traveler is what this hotel was intended for. However, they have many conference rooms and business rooms for meetings and I am sure they get plenty of complaints from business travelers.

This hotel is located very very central close to tram etc... looks nice reception is really chic... we had an ensuite double room... The sink was in the room rather than in the bathroom, the room was the smallest I have ever stayed at but very clean and had a fan so no problem. Views are of the next door house = none. Close to cinema and food court. Only downside is the room size which was TINY... telly fixed onto the bed on a little stand... We were also at the end of - weeks holiday and had lot of stuff so that did not help but it really was small.

My familiy and I recently stayed at The Palomar ... our stay was terrific..from the time the valet took our keys to the time we were drove away it was a great expirience. High marks in all areas. Considering this was a very hectic weekend the hotel coped with it very well. Our rooms were clean, service was excellent. It was a great location for dinning, shopping and the the Cototn Bowl.

The check in experience was fantastic! Unfortunately we couldn't recall the staff member's name, but he made every effort to ensure the experience was first class and provided us with great sightseeing tips to make our short stay as enjoyable as possible. 
Unfortunately our room had not been occupied in some time - there was a layer of dust on all surfaces and a disconcerting stain sprayed up the curtains - was it blood or red wine?!?!? We used most of the services in the hotel - gym, in room dining and the bar and found the facilities and service all of a high standard. 
The location of the hotel is so close to everything - with the White House less than a block away - making it a perfect base for leisure or business trips to DC.

My husband and I just returned home early from our honeymoon at the Town and Country. Where oh where to begin?
When we arrived, the lady checking us in was very friendly and gave us free breakfast and drink coupons as well as one of the cottage rooms by the pool. The grounds are fantastic, with gardens everywhere you look, but that's about as far as the amenities extend.
The room was marginal. Tiny bathroom (inhabited by ants), semi-clean, hard bed. A room at the Quality Inn is comparable.
The prices at the restaurants on site are way overpriced and serve pretty lousy food. The waitresses at the Terrace Cafe (where the breakfast buffet is held) were scarce and often rude.
But the worst part was when the hotel was invaded by the international aquatic fitness convention. They took over every pool for six hours a day, starting at -:-- in the morning. We tried to find a quiet spot to relax, but their booming music could be heard everywhere on the grounds. The hotel staff offered to move us to one of the tower rooms (where the music was still loud) and said they could do nothing about the problem. We finally gave up and flew home early.
Overall, I would not reccomend this hotel for anyone who wants a relaxing, peaceful vacation. This hotel gets their money from the big conventions in town and are not concerned with the comfort of their other guests.

We often stay at Comfort Suites hotels. Somewhat disappointed in this one - given the good TA reviews. Staff was professional, courteous and friendly. Room could have been cleaner - time for a good deep cleaning in the corners of the one we had.

Great hotel if you want to experience what NYC has to offer. The location is perfect - right next to Timnes Square, yet rooms are as quiet as you can get in such busy city. The service is excellent - our rooms were upgraded free of charge upon our request, breakfast was always fresh and delicious, the concierge was very informative and helpful. Rooms are small but comfortable. The only disadvantage I can think or is lack of places to sit in the lobby - we were a large group and waiting for everyone standing was a bit annoying.

We had to rebook the stay due to Superstorm Sandy, even though I initially booked the stay as a non-refundable rate. The staff was very understanding and honored our old rate for the new dates. Thanks!

We stayed fo one night; it rained from the wall all the night and the hotel answer was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""extra towel""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""!!!! wonderful breakfast from - a.m.; not far from the subway, but in an ugly area of the city.

The Hotel George is an unrated hotel. The entire staff, front desk, concierge were extremely helpful and friendly. They were knowledgeable about the area and were easy to talk to and deal with. The room was very clean ( as was the hallways) there was lots of space to unwind relax in your room. Location is near the Capitol and Union Station so it was easy to get around. But the best thing about the George was it people - they were the best!

Stayed here while on a business trip. Lovely hotel with modern colors and textures throughout. The Domain, where the hotel is located, is a swanky shopping-eating area. Tiffany, Louis Vuitton, Free People, Anthropologie, and Neiman-Marcus are steps away.
The hotel lobby is awash in granite, chrome, sharp right angles and velvety-veloured sofas. They have also paid someone to create musical wallpaper for the lobby: mood-evoking music meant to complement the decor. 
My hotel room was ---. The bed was fantastic except for the pillows, which absolutely sucked. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""heavenly bed"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is phenomenal, really it is. Climate-control system functioned perfectly. Furniture (side chair, task chair) was very pretty but super-uncomfortable.
Bathroom is huge. Huge walk-in shower with glass doors. If you have read any of my previous hotel reviews, you already know how I detest rainfall shower heads. I am happy to report that this shower had a Speakman showerhead with multiple settings.
All this attention to detail....and then I noticed the room service menu. 
It contained eleven...ELEVEN....spelling errors. Serious things, such as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""blackeberry"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Shiner Boch"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""jalepenos"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""buerre blanc"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". How, how, HOW can a place that has created a specific soundtrack for its lobby not run the spell-checker for its in-room menus? I called Starwood customer service at once. They instructed me to turn in the menu to the manager, which I did...with the errors circled and correct spellings added. 
Later that evening, I wanted room service but had no menu, so I called to have one brought up. It was an entirely different menu. Different font, different food choices, different entirely. I am not stupid enough to think that the hotel fixed and reprinted their in-room menus in one day, but being given an entirely new menu was a little bizarre. And there were typos on it as well!
According to the little paper on the back of the door of my room, the rate for my room was $--- per night. At that price, you would think some attention might be paid to the printed materials in the room.
I'd like to give this place - stars but I just cannot forgive the menu debacle.

The Hilton is a reflagged Doubletree that has been renovated and is incredible! One of the nicest hotel rooms I've seen in a long time (and I travel a lot) plus a super nice staff.
Rooms are large and well furnished, feature WiFi, minibars, good TV systems and all of the amenities one expects from a Hilton.
Location is great too. On Post Oak just a couple of blocks from the Galleria!

I attended a conference at the hotel. I was very satisfied with my one night stay. 
Pros:

very nice view from the --th floor
Cons:

room was a little stuffy when I first walked in

Loved the location for a trip to Boston! All around great experience. Comfortable room, nice people. Asked and received a Microwave- Fridge. Easy ride from Airport, easy 'T' ride to Fenway. Perfect spot for Boston Marathon participants. Quick Walk to Expo, Very Quick Walk to Busses, Quick ( But slow :P !!) walk back from Finish. If we Ever qualify again- staying here!!

I was psyched to get a $--- rate for the Warwick--I'm still looking for my favorite NYC hotel. And hey, it's got a cool history and a knockout location. The staff was also top-notch. Unfortunately, the rooms were not. Room #-: not the king bed I requested, and all beat to hell (carpet stains, damaged furniture, ceiling stain). I NEVER complain in hotels, but I this time I had really high hopes so I moved into a smaller, non-view room #- for the night (that REEKED of cologne), with an apology and an assurance to be moved the next day. Stayed here ----, needed to catch an early flight out of El Paso. About a -- minute drive from the airport. Paid $-- plus tax & fees on Priceline - a great price. It is an extended stay hotel, so there is not really a lobby and kind of an awkward check-in - in the manager's office. All in all though it was OK. Room was clean, small with a kitchenette.

My husband and I recently stayed here one night while in NYC. The hotel was well kept- clean, spacious room. It's considered a small luxury hotel. The staff were friendly, and offered ideas for restaurants. The location is great- walking distance to Times Square, Empire State Building, etc. Cabs were very easy to get outside to go to other areas of the city. 
The only downside, and it didn't affect us at all, is they are currently renovating the lobby. I would stay here again and recommend this hotel to everyone.

Very nice rooms and bathrooms, extremely courteous staff (all French), hotel well maintained. A very comfortable place to stay if you are in NYC on business for a couple of days. Well equipped gym and wifi etc. Rooms nice and quiet and no noise from the elevators!

I have stayed at this location on multiple occasions for work travel, and each experience has been positive. This is a nice location very close to Grand Central Station and within walking distance of many resturants. I personally love the wine 'happy' hour that is offered in the late afternoon. It is great to walk in from a long day at work or travel and be offered a glass of wine to relax and welcome you to the hotel. 
I have not eaten at the resturant, but I have had a few glasses of wine with friends, and the staff is always very nice and willing to meet your every need. I would highly recommed this hotel for work or leisure, especially if traveling without children.

Liked the location of this hotel on the end of Fisherman's Wharf. Easy to rent bikes, grab public transportation and get to Alcatraz. John the doorman was especially helpful in directing us to good breakfast restaurants and general city information. Room was very clean and comfortable, comfy bed and free wine at happy hour during the week. Watch out for the street people on Fisherman's Wharf that jump out and yell from behind fake hand held branches or hydrants, scared the daylights out of me! The Fisherman's Wharf area was a little run down and cheesy but it was a little seedy. But the central location was a plus.

Stayed five nights for a conference at the local convention center...Not only is Charlesmark in an excellent part of Boston close to incredible shopping, but the layout is pretty cool....Had drinks in the lobby and shopped until I dropped at Newbury Street and Copley Place...Room was tiny but I was traveling single so it was OK...Loved the bathroom with the speakers piping satellite music in...The shower was gorgeous....Garbage truck woke me up in the wee hours but I feel back asleep.
Fab hotel - fab location... You can't beat the location - accross from Central Park - Awesome staff, etc...

Very impressive lobby. Staff was very helpful. The rooms were tastefully decorated. Complimentary coffee. Excellent location in Union Square - near to everything. I also stayed at another hotel in the Financial District, which is nice but Union Square is better. Would definitely stay again.

My family and I stayed here for - nights to visit the zoo. The floor we stayed on smelled like a sewer. Luckily the smell did not go into our room. The reason I gave it an avaerage rating is that the price of our rooms $----night is not a good value. The pictures of the hotel room and pool area make the hotel seem nicer than it is. The only highlight of our stay here was the maid service did a phenomanal job cleaning our room and the food (not appetizers) at the restaurant was good. Based on all the reviews on this site I was expecting much more and this hotel did not deliver.

We love the location. You are within walking distance of Pike Place Market, the Space Needle, and downtown shopping. Easy cab ride to the cruise ship terminals. The staff was very attentive. Nice amenities (restaurant, fitness room and pool). The rooms have floor to ceiling, wall to wall glass exterior window walls that provide great views. Light sleepers (which we are not) may find these window walls provide the background sounds of the city a little too much. We will return the next time we are in Seattle.

Requested a high floor......ended up on -th floor. Great view of the Air conditioning unit of the building behind the hotel.
-No aeroplane noise
-Hotel room comfortable enough for an overnight. Bed and pillows were good.
-airconditioning cold but rumbled
-Bathroom- small and a low ceiling. At -'-"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" it made me feel a bit closed in. No hot water to start with. 
Next day I had hot water. Shower head loose in wall and had to bend to get under it.
Very noisy room. Between people talking in the corridors and kids running up and down I didnt get much sleep. (went to bed at -pm). Then in the early hours of the morning someone services the soft drink machine next to my room . They werent quiet at all !
This is serviced by the free buses from LAX and is less than - minutes drive.
I arrived at -am and was advised room wasnt available - fair enough as I was early. Asked to come back at -- and it should be ready. Concierge was helpful enought and sol me a ticket to the trolley bus tour that departs almost outside. turns out that didnt leave until -am so had - hours to kill. If you have nothing to do then do the tour- cheap and fills in time. Alternatively take the big blue bus to Santa Monica.
Stay here again ? depends on price. Nicer (but smaller) rooms than the Radison LAX but a lot more expensive.

I've stayed at this facility several times now and continue to enjoy the experience and quality. The staff is always helpful and the rooms: spacious, clean and comfortable. I would recommend this property to anybody at a rate comparable to most hotels.

dirty room that was not cleaned for - consecutive days during my stay. i you can invest a bit more into your stay in baltimore i would go for other places to stay in. the air conditioning was not working and there was no possibility to open the window...

Location is subjective and would not have worked if we had to pay $-- each way to get to and from Convention Center. For us, this is not an issue because Trade Show Organizers planned for this well and arranged Tour Bus Fleet to provide dense service at - minute intervals of --- full busses for comfort + commuting!! 
For LA, the closest hotels were - large blocks away from the convention center, so staying close by is not as beneficial for off site private meetings as other trade show venues where the hotels are across the street. The decision to stay at Kyoto Grand came mainly from positive reviews below on this site. We were not dissappointed. If you enjoy Japanese cuisine and service then this is refreshing as there are dozen or more superior Japanese restaraunts on par with best in any US cities. Ok, that is enough for the area. 
The hotel review, offers very good value at $--- per nite.
In room breakfast choice at $-- with gratuity is excellent, compared to $-- with exactly same food a month prior in San Francisco's W Hotel across street from Moscone Center and local SF breakfast at diner of $--.-- + tip. Was delivered on time.
Funny though, we had to phone each day to request the door hanging order form. You would think Housekeeping would put fresh ones in the room daily, but I have noted this from most hotels I stay in so this must be some trendy cost saving tip amongst hoteliers?
I stayed on -th floor. Decor was tired and old, but not peeling or faded and everything worked well. The bedding was new. Linens were Crisp, clean and as comfortable as any Sweet Sleeper upper scale bed. Slept great but that also could have been the Sake and long days.
Towels were large and very fluffy. Everything was very clean, very! 
Gardens in the back of the hotel were actually refreshing to look at in the morning against the city scape and made me wonder, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""who would engineer that these days with real estate costs being so high?"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", so this is pleasant bonus and helps put you in a nice, calm state. This is well maintained by the hotel as it should be and is a nice esthetic. I am a gardener so this was a bonus. I would recommend Garden View rooms over city view.
The TV was older tube style, but I only watched it briefly, but it makes the decor appear older and not updated. Small change of this would update the room. Hotel's Ibahn wireless service in the room worked perfectly and having cost waved ($-.--) as part of conference booking package was great! Again, barely used it to upload and download few messages so it would have been painful if we had to pay each day.
Lobby bar was well provisioned but underwhelming. OK for meeting or quick drink only. I would not choose to invest more time there than this. A dozen Japanese bars compliment Japanese restaraunts nearby.
The hotel staff is terrific, from whoever answers the phone, the front desk, door men, bell captains, housekeepers, room service and kitchen staff were terrific! 
We did not use the hotel restaraunt as I suspect few do, epecially after reading the reviews here. I looked in and it was closed. At best, it did look subdued. 
If I owned this property, I would re design coffee shop to reflect higher energy and up beat Japanese style, Tokyo contemporary coffee shop with pastries for tea anytime and -- hour operation for breakfast -:-- AM to Midnite for Asian, European and East Coast North American travelers. I did notice from ther bus there is a Starbucks in the hotel, but never visited it. 
I did not visit the health club, but you probably figured that since this review focus is on sleep, drink and food.
The showers worked great. Terrific water pressure. In Japan however, I am always amazed at the terrific tubs and showers. These, though very functional in terms of U.S. standards would be considered sub standard in Japan, only and I suppose a bath make over would be too costly.
Safes are provided at no charge but this hotel is very secure. There are well dressed, polite and competent security people in the hotel and present. We felt secure and safe. I like a safe so I can leave my laptop in the room. I did not see one and called the front desk and within minutes, they brought one up and I was in business.
The service in this hotel is excellent. 
Finally, we were leaving as the Tsunami hit Japan and saw the saw and felt the deep concern of many guests from Japan and the local shops. Our thoughts and prayers go out to our friends in Japan!
Summary: none of the updates I suggest, the decor or bath fixtures or even coffee shop update would make my stay any better and the lack of these 'updates' are subjective and did not make my stay any worse at all.
Strong recommendation for this hotel.

This hotel is located near galleria (even has a shuttle to take you). Their reeds restaurant on site was great (avocado burger, pizza - room service, and breakfast buffet did not disappoint). The room and view were very nice. The front desk staff were extremely friendly and helpful. I definitely plan to stay here again the next time I'm in Houston. Keep up the good work!

We stayed at the Hampton Inn on May ---, ---- and really enjoyed our stay. It is close to The Alamo, Riverwalk, & Mall. It has free parking and we really liked the breakfest. It had your usual plus biscuit and gravy one day and eggs and ham together another day. The rooms was large with king size bed and refrig. The bathroom was exceptional.
We walked to the Alamo which is a must see. Also walked to the riverwalk and did the tour.
The staff was helpful. They asked if we needed any directions or help. Was very helpful when I asked how to do the Mission Trail. 
Would difinately stay there again in a heart beat.

The Mariott Marquis Times Square is an extremly centrally located hotel. Located in Times Square right across from the Forver --, this hotel is a prime location. Request to stay on the top floor with views of Times Square (Thats what I did). Although the hotel was pricey, the view of Times Square was amazing! I didnt spend a moment watching telivision at night, instead just looked out into Times Square. Many couples staying in the hotel, and the glass elevators provided amazing views. The fitness club was average, and the rooms were typical to any Marriott. The Starbucks on the ground floor or -th floor provide a quick location for a quick breakfast. Junior's across the street from the hotel was a great New York Deli for lunch and dinner. The only difficulty with this hotel was looking for a beer, I didnt wanna sit in the hotel bar for a beer so I had to wander down the street to the worlds largest Walgreens. Biggest complaint was NO FREE WIFI. In this day and age, I have been to a small motel in europe and have recieved wifi.....none here....$-- a day. Your better off to sit in a Starbucks with free wifi....
Booked with a group a few weeks ago and we did not even get the rooms we wanted and the sales manger didnt seem to care after our booking. Gee thanks!!!!!!!!!!!!!

My husband and I went to boston for a family vacation with our daughter and her two children. We needed adjoining rooms because our grand-daughter is a child with special needs. They could not guarantee that so they gave us a suite. 
We found the room clean, housekeeping department excellent, room service very accomodating and the front desk very helpful.
We were on the fourth floor overlooking the construction and never at any time of the day or night was disturbed by noise. 
We would not hesitate to stay at the Parker House again or hesitate to recommend it to our friends and family.

close to hollywood blvd only one block away, ---- minutes walk. free parking but very limited, about -- parking spots, so if you go out at night and come back, there might not be a parking spot for you. the hotel info book posted that if there's no parking available they will get you a parking lot nearby but I don't know how close it would be. free breakfast with coffee, milk, juices, croissant, muffins, bread, yogurts. i got - full beds room to me was pretty spacious with a little table with - chairs, microwave, fridge. bathroom clean but the water kinda hard to adjust whether hot or cold, old style. they also charge for extra person for $-- each if you have more than -. we have - adults and - kids so they charged only $--. overall good for the price.

Fairly typical of a chain of hotels the service is fine if a little impersonal. Small reception that nobody really gathered in and we never ate at the restaurent so couldn't comment on that.
The room ---- was on the corner and very small. It did have windows on two walls from which we could see the east river but the pieces of furniture were so big that they just about filled every bit of floorspace. The air conditioning was very effective and extremely quiet. Would have been impossible to survive without it on around the clock.
The location is fine but with temperatures ---+ degrees during mosr of our stay even the shortest walk had us bathed in sweat but this didn't stop us getting out and about even although the hotel is right at the end of East --nd Street on foot or by subway. This does mean that the location is a little quieter than other areas. Grand Central Station, Top of the Rock, Central Park, Dakota, Times Sqaure, Staten Island and Greenich Village easily reached and indeed we managed to get tickets to see Phantom on Broadway. 
Staff were ok but the overall experience and feel about the place is that its a little impersonal although this is not exactly meant as a critisism, more an observation. 
The biggest drawback was the size of the room but I don't think that makes it unique in Manhattan.
Elevator noise in room was terrible; wifi very expensive; business section very small; rooftop Bar very nice, but expensive.
Just what I expected from a W. Cool vibe and great ambiance. Great location.

Our first stay is one of many as we were very impressed with the cleanliness of the hotel. The staff was the most friendly and efficient team I have encountered amongst the many hotels we have stayed in. We traveled with a three year old, two young adults and two adults. The two bedroom suite was well equipped and spacious. The food was yummy...cudos to the baker of the scones! The evening """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""welcome home reception"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" was a nice bonus. I had the opportunity to do laundry and the housekeeper was in there wiping down the equipment...how impressive is that. Great job!!

Was very nervous after reading the reviews of this hotel but it was truly fabulous . The location was excellent and our room was a really good size. Some say the rooms are small but with so much to do in the city why are people in the rooms that long anyway ??? The lobby was gorgeous and we will def be returning. Find it incredible what some people find to complain about on these sites. Food is a little overpriced but its New York - no one forces you to use the restaurant . A lovely hotel with character and charm .

This was our -rd stay at the handlery so we obviously like it!! Staff are extremely pleasant & helpful at all times. The hotel is so central that it's easy to get around on the Muni transport or cable car.

Great hotel, perfect location and very clean. Free breakfast buffet and wifi . All the staff are super friendly and helpful especially Ms. Juicy Villanuena of the front desk. We will consider going back again to New York City and stay at the same hotel and will recommend this hotel to our friends.

This was the worst hotel I have ever stayed in. We went for my birthday and couldn't even sleep in one bed. Not only was there hair on the blankets and pillows, there was also mold on the shower curtain, the celing in the bathroom and hallway, and around the floor in the bathroom. My friend had an allergic reaction to something in the room (she went to her doctor when we got home and found it was the mold) and swelled horribly. My other friends, who were in another room, didn't notice anything amiss. However, they are males, and were quite happy watching t.v.
The hotel lobby is nice, and the desk receptionist was kind. However, we had numerous issues with the hotel itself, and we will NEVER return.

Had a great stay at this brand new fresh build HI Express. Front Desk clerks busy, but very nice and pleasant. Decor is a nice blend of purple, greys, and blacks - the colors look very nice. Has a great pool area for kids, the bigger waterside seems permanantly closed due to needing a life guard, not sure what the story is there. Rooms nice, bathroom sink is one of those new age bowl above the counter and it was pretty difficult for my youngest to brush his teeth. Breakfast was good, pleasant breakfast employee. They have an entertaining instant pancake maker instead of the typical waffle maker. We'll stay here again.

The Intercontinental has definitely kept up with the times... staying here definitely changed my mind about the hotel brand. The design is contemporary (but not stark) and I felt as if I was in someone's beautiful home. The beds and bedding are fabulous and the bathroom was beautiful as well (not your typical hotel decor - so much better!). There is spectacualr fireplace in the lounge where you can sit and relax after a long day out. The restaurant is so warm and comfortable and the food is top notch! I would recommend this to anyone coming to the city for business or pleasure - what a treat!

My daughter and I stayed at the Affinia Shelburne for two nights after the Thanksgiving Holiday. Prior to our stay I read other trip advisor reviews and wanted to make sure we could get a room with - beds. When I contacted the hotel directly I was told that a request could be made but not guaranteed. Having noticed that the assistant general manager had responded to some trip advisor reviews I decided to contact her with my request directly. My e-mail was answered the same day and I was pleased to be guaranteed a room with two beds. Upon our arrival we were greeted by an extremely friendly doorman followed by one of the most pleasant reception clerks I have ever met. This wonderful treatment continued during our entire stay including every single person we came in contact with (housekeeping, maintenance staff in the hall, bellman, checking out). I found this extraordinary. I have traveled to NY many times and have met friendly people but this was every single person. The room was clean, the beds very comfortable and nice workspace. The restaurant next door (can get there without going outside) had yummy breakfasts. All of this plus an excellent location. I would not hesitate to stay there again.

The location of this hotel cannot be beat. Convenient to American and Georgetown Universities as well as shopping in Georgetown and Friendship Heights and sights like the National Cathedral and Monuments our family loved the Savoy. The hotel also offers a parking garage since we found we didnt need to do much driving in DC during our stay. The beds were huge and so were the rooms which was great since we have a family of - and didn't have to spring for an additional room for a change. We stayed here primarily for AU's Graduation which was a great choice since we needed to be on campus for -AM and the Savoy was less than -- minutes away. 
Loved the view from our room too-- we could see the Capital and Monuments which made for a very Washingtonian Experience! This gem is definitely our new top choice for trips to DC.

I was pleasently surprised with this place. We stayed for four nights and had a very good stay. 
We were placed on a high floor, away from the elevator and without much noise from either neighboring guests or the street. I requested all of these things when we checked in and they delivered. 
The room was a bit small, but had all the necessary furniture including desk and chair, mini bar and ample storage for clothing and luggage. Everything was clean and well-maintained. 
The bed was very comfortable and soft. Sheets were clean and soft, and the bed had plenty of blankets and pillows, which was nice as I like lots of pillows. 
Cookies at check-in were a nice surprise, and all of the staff were accommodating.
I would stay here again, I feel it is a good value to stay in NYC, has a premier location in midtown, is clean and spacious enough (it is NYC after all), and has comfortable beds.

My partner and I are fans of Kimpton hotels, and I have stayed at a couple of them in Chicago. I had heard from other reviews that there was a bit of noise in the rooms and the rooms were tiny, but being a fan of Kimpton and all of the fun amenities (wine hour, free coffee and tea, etc.), I gave it a shot. I even paid a little more for what I thought would be a larger room. My partner and I are both pretty petite, and it was even hard for us to maneuver in there, particularly getting into and out of the bathroom, which had these ridiculous mini French doors because a full-size door was really out of the question for this room. Also, every day we were woken up by either people in the hallways or worse, people next door to us who were just carrying on a conversation. Great location, but definitely not worth it for the price and inconveniences. When we return to Chicago, we definitely won't be staying here again.

I liked staying here. I had a city view room in one of the corners, it was great. Seemed like newer decor, but had phone next to toilet and power outlet that didn't match the newer feeling. Little thing, but I noticed. Good views, I'm amazed how far street noise can travel upwards. Conference @ hotel made price more than what I wanted to pay, but in line with other nearby hotels. Can't say enough how good it was to be close to bart entrance and cable car turnaround @ market st. Good neighborhood, some panhandling going on, but not too bad. I would love to stay again next time out.

I agonized over where to stay when taking my son to USC, but shouldn't have worried about this hotel. It is just a few minutes and a straight shot from campus. Although huge, the service was very good - the concierge(s) knew every answer and a request for toothpaste only took -- minutes. The room was beautifully appointed - yes, it was an odd shape because of the shape of the building - and had an oversized workdesk and black-tiled marble bathroom with a great shower. There are several shops and restaurants on various levels, including a very large fitness center, and a wine and cheese shop that also sold fresh muffins and fruit. The food and service in the casual restaurant on the top floor was mediocre - much better in the lobby bar-restaurant. There are also several good restaurants within walking distance. Valet parking is required unless you want to walk a long distance. The price isn't too bad if you plan to go in and out several times during the day.

I travel a lot on business so most of the time I am away from home. Staying at the Highland Gardens didn't make me feel I'm away from home. It is not a five star hotel but it sure has its charm. Unlike other hotels where you feel boxed in, this hotel gives you the feeling of so much space. Having a room with a balcony facing the pool and garden is just perfect for relaxation after a day of meetings. The hotel staff were great. I would definitely come back to this hotel.

Absolutely THE BEST Super - hotel I have ever stayed in! Great location near major highway affords easy access to downtown and surrounding environs. No pool, but who cares. Everything was top notch, clean and service and hospitality was outstanding. The served the very best breakfast I have ever had at any (economy) hotel! You will NOT BE SORRY staying here! A DEFINITE must stay while in Austin. Why pay more and get less at any other place? 
This Super - was a great stay!

First off, I need to disclose that I was previously staying at the Waldorf Chicago where I checked out to go on an overnight trip to Tampa. The Waldorf didn't have availability for the rest of my trip so I chose the Hilton Suites. I needed to adjust my attitude rather quickly.
The stay didn't start out well at check-in, primarily because this seems to be a huge Lufthansa crew hotel. Be prepared for an enormous rush of activity in the very late afternoon when one set of crew check out and then when the next arrive. It was at precisely this moment that I tried to check in and that one desk clerk decided to take a coffee break. After the calm of the Waldorf check in I realized I really needed to adjust my attitude. 
As a Diamond level Honors member I received an upgrade to a lake view room. I was assigned room ----, which trust me was more a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""peep into the neighbors living room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" view with a bit of a lake view to the left...if you squinted. I went back to reception to enquire if there had been a mistake and was assigned ---- with a fantastic view. So far so good.
The room was clean if somewhat dated and given the Chicago heat wave the air conditioning worked well. The rooms come with a microwave, coffee maker and refrigerator. Additionally, there is an ironing board and iron, which I frankly think should be required by law. There is no minibar. The Internet worked well generally, but not necessarily the strongest of signals. The shower was weak, but this seems endemic to all hotels lately which install over zealous flow restricters. (ok, this didn't seem to be the case at the Waldorf).
I found the bed and bedding to be extremely comfortable and I slept well. I found the employees to be very service oriented and felt well taken care of. This hotel is a fine choice for a stay in Chicago as its location next to the John Hancock building is close to Michigan Ave shopping and Rush St nightlife. Room rates are also very reasonable and provide good value.

What a great deal for a nice boutique hotel smack in the middle of downtown Philly. 
I was a little nervous because of the price, but the Alexander didn't disappoint. I stayed in a large and expensive Sheraton near U-Penn the night before and I thought the Alexander was the nicer room and hotel.
Rooms are nicely equipped, with good views of the city and a pretty healthy breakfast is provided every morning. Staff is very friendly and helpful. At less than $--- a night (what it was when I stayed), this place is a steal and I would definitely stay here again. 
One thing to be aware of: the hotel is in 'gayborhood,' which you can guess by the name is the gay enclave of the city. In this day and age it really shouldn't be an issue, but I figured I'd mention it for those who might be uncomfortable with it.

DO NOT BELIEVE WHAT YOU SEE IN PICTURES.
The Dana looks gorgeous in pictures, but in reality there is only one building in the hotel that looks like the pictures. The majority of the buildings look like low income housing units. The rooms themselves are cramped and DARK, i was there for a wedding and had to apply my makeup in the car because the lighting in the room was AWFUL. 
We were placed in the back by the secondary pool which was actually quite nice for children. They had pool toys and a sandy area for the kids, it's also where the pool bar is located. The Infinity Pool in the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""UPSCALE"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" section of the hotel complex did not have a bar or refreshments, but rather was close to a restaurant and was not kid friendly. 
The rooms were fairly clean, the A-C units were installed close to the floor, so they really didn't cool the room at all, but the floor right next to it was nice and crisp.
The location was GREAT for Sea World, they have a shuttle but the hours are limited on it. Kind of a far walk to Mission Beach, if you want to be close to the beach, I'd recommend staying at The Bahia, which is slightly cheaper and much nicer.

My husband and I stayed at the Hilton Times Square for - nights. The hotel concierge was extremely helpful and the overall service was impeccable. I loved being in the middle of Times Square (I noticed that some people did complain about the location). The excitement and energy can't be beat. That's why I love NY...........I highly recommend this hotel!

Price-wise, I was looking for a hotel in the middle range. I don't need fancy, I just need clean, comfortable, and a sense that I'll be safe. I was happy to find the Arena (on Expedia.com) - a good price, a comfortable and clean bed, and within walking distance of the Amtrak train station. Plus, I'm gluten-free, and the complimentary breakfast had fruit (canned) and potatoes and sausage that I could eat. I had one complaint (no bedside clock), which the front-desk clerk noted and said he would pass along to a staff member. I didn't really get a sense of the neighborhood, but it might be a bit depressed (vacant shop fronts), and I wouldn't walk around there alone at night.
Thank you indigo so much for a great family vacation the rooms were amazing and so was the food. And the staff whoa!! amazing!!

The service at this hotel is fantastic, probably one of the best in Seattle. They have this really cool video about the hotel and their staff and it really shows that they are committed to providing a good guest experience. Rooms are BIG, and bed was fine, clean rooms. Their is a vending machine on each floor and also in the bottom floor. Breakfast at the hotel is fantastic value and the food was great, free newspapers are everywhere, at the door, room, restaurant. They also have a airline checkin station in the lobby if your interested that covers all airlines that have webcheckin. They also have no free wifi, but in the business center there was free internet on the computers, which might have been a tech issue because they advertise that they charge for it. Should be free anyway. Price was good value at normal rate on Expedia for $--- with the normal $-- off code so pretty good price for such a big and comfy hotel. If ever in Seattle in the future, or if friend-family head up there I will send them here!
Cons:
-Aircon-Heater unit would not stop! It was that loud that it takes a while to get to sleep sometimes and you cant even change the temperature. 
-To get the shower-bath working, you need to pull out this metal plug thingy in the wall, its an old device to get the water going and coming from another country I had no clue how to get the water going. 
-Location is at the top of the hill and walking into Seattle and back is pretty tiring at times.

My co-worker and I checked in together. She stayed for one night and I stayed for four. The desk clerk was a real jerk. We are both school district employees and he wouldn't accept our tax-emempt certificate. Said he needed another form but didn't provide it. Went online at the motel business center and printed one. He was fully capable of doing the same.
Room was very roomy and clean with a jacuzzi, refrigerator, and microwave. Full hot breakfast was excellent as well as the other desk clerks during the day and evening. Didn't see the guy who checked us in until I left four days later. He checked me out and I discovered was charged an extra night. The man argued with me and I simply told him to do the math. Any fool could have found it was a mistake. He finally credited the extra night's charge to my credit card. My co-worker had the same thing happen to her. She was overcharged an extra night as well. I wonder how many guests had this happen but didn't discover the error? A nice way to make extra money?

I have stayed at all the hotels on hotel circle in this price range, and the vagabond inn stand above the rest. Frequenting the San Diego area on business, it was nice to stay at a place where the rooms were clean (without that odd smell that you just can't place), everything worked, and the staff was courteous: not mention the DELICIOUS WAFFLES. This is the only place I will stay in San Diego.

I usually give positive reviews and reward good companies for their services. I travel for a living, and was on a business trip on Philly for - days. Overpriced, outdated, charges for everything inside the room, $--- + tax per night, poor service, have to pay for everything in the room ($-- wifi, $- for a bottle of water). 
All of this I understand - but this was not ok. I had the extreme pleasure of experiencing The Joule for one night in Dallas last week. My only regret is that I didn't have longer to bask in it fabulousness! Truly spectacular space. The main reason we booked this hotel was the price as we were only going to be staying there a few nights at the beginning of our travels and didnt want to spend a fortune.The location is excellent being about a -- minute walk from Fishermans Wharf. The hotel also had free covered parking. 
When you first enter The hotel it does look like it needs to be redecorated and even though we had booked a non-smoking room we were given one for smokers and it stank of cigarette smoke which was not good. All things considered, for the price we paid and where it was located it was very good value for money.
San Fransisco is a beutiful city and I would like to return and stay longer.

Well worth a stay to spoil yourself!!

This was my second visit to Hotel Giraffe. First was last fall for my birthday and the recent trip was in August for our anniversary. I cant wait to go back! Can't wait to come back & visit Hotel Giraffe! Next time I think Im bringing the girls!

Our stay at Comfort Inn North Conference Center in Columbus was very nice. The rooms were very neat and clean and the desk attendant was very helpful. I have stayed here several times over the past year while I was attending school. After my last stay, I decided I needed to stay elsewhere.
I did not see the light until the next morning as I was getting ready to leave but the splatter on it definitely had me questioning what could have taken place in my room. See attached photo.

When you think of a convention center hotel, this is probably what you have in mind. However, if you're headed to a convention - especially one at the Moscone Center, this is fine place to stay.
The rooms are small but clean. They have been updated recently and have comfortable beds with good bedding. The curtains are especially good at blocking the light if you like a dark room. There's a flat panel television with a good selection of digital channels. The hotel had internet available via ethernet; however, I was able to pick up a free wifi signal from outside the hotel. The bathroom was also small, but had good, soft towels. The water pressure was fine.
I checked in late and left early, so I didn't see much of the staff. However, the gentleman who checked me in was quite helpful. It was late and I was looking for a decent meal outside of the hotel. He gave me a great choice.
If you're looking to have a drink in the hotel, there's a bar on the top floor with amazing views of the city.
All in all, this isn't some amazing must see destination - especially for a city with so many historic hotels. However, if you need a place to spend the night, check your e-mail and then get to a convention, this will do just fine. (Also, don't take this to be condemning the hotel with faint praise. The last thing is what I said in the title – This was the quietest room I have ever stayed in, anywhere. I’m not sure what renovations people are concerned with and if we just got lucky, but quiet and dark!

I usually prefer to stay at this facility when visiting Columbus due to the excellent location straddling Short North and downtown. Overall the facility is very clean and comfortable. Just back from a few day in Chicago and stayed at the Affinnia. what can I say. Hotel is in a perfrect location, ---m off the mag mile and close to everything.

First time here, changing from the Allerton. It was a great experience. The room was extremely nice with great amenities. We just spent four nights at The Benjamin. which for the most part was a great place to stay, but for a few minor niggles and one major sour note. The concierge staff were very helpful and friendly (especially Anya), however this can't be said for the rest of the staff. The front desk seemed disinterested a lot of the time and weren't particularly welcoming (compared to our experiences at The Lenox in Boston) - maybe this is just a New York thing? After an amazing four days in the city we were left with the only negative experience of our entire stay. On our last day we spoke to Anya and she advised us on how best to get to JFK airport - take a taxi ($--) and ask to the driver to take the bridge instead of the tunnel so to avoid the tolls. When we came to leave, we asked the porter to find us a taxi and told him we wished to pay by card (having done so the previous evening). However the doorman then told us that he couldn't hail a yellow taxi as they were all busy and ushered us toward a unmarked, black car and then told us it would be $-- by card or $-- by cash and suggested we withdraw cash from a nearby ATM all of this despite it saying on the side of every yellow New York taxi, $-- fixed to JFK. We were then curtly told this was due to tolls, and according to the hotel porter this had to be paid at every bridge or tunnel going to JFK, (so in effect there was no $-- standard rate) which is at odds with both Anya's advice and the NYC Department of Transportation website, which we checked on our return to the UK. The doorman was very rude and pushy and the whole experience was more akin to what you expect in other less developed parts of the world, which is fine there as it's all part of the fun, but not what you would expect in NYC. On the way to JFK we immediately saw a number of yellow taxis with their lights on and as we crossed the Queensboro Bridge (which just so happened to be toll free!) we started to wonder whether if it was all part of a racket between the door staff and a cab company. The last thing we want to do is get anyone into trouble, but this experience meant our stay in New York ended on a negative vibe. 
The hotel itself is currently undergoing some redevelopment, especially in the lobby, however this caused us absolutely no inconvenience or disruption and looks like it will be complete very soon. Our room was large and modern and exceeded our expectations. However the wifi is not free which was a shame and the signal seemed erratic at best. Given that most - star hotels (and lower) provide free wifi these days, it was a bit disappointing and something that should be addressed. There was a wired internet connection, but with so many people now using iPads and iPhones this is of little help. 
Overall we recommend staying at The Benjamin if you're looking for a good quality four star place in midtown Manhattan, however you should definitely look to make you're own travel arrangements when leaving.

I booked a room in the Hotel Belleclaire this past November for two reasons: it fit my limited budget, and it was not overly far from Radio City Music Hall, where I was going to see a show. However, I would recommend that anyone coming to New York City, even for an overnight stay, look elsewhere when searching for a hotel. There are far better hotels in NYC, and I was extremely disappointed with the Hotel Belleclaire.
I booked through hotels, and the pictures that the hotel posted and the fabulous reviews that it received were a far cry from what I experienced when I was there. The lobby is about the only thing in the entire hotel that actually looks the way it does in the online photos. The outside of the hotel is covered in scaffolding - they are renovating the facade - and the lobby, while decent, is definitely not on par with other lovely old hotels in the city. (I've actually seen apartment vestibules that are better than this lobby.) The elevators are unbelievably tiny - two people and a good-sized piece of luggage are about all that is going to fit on those things. The hotel itself retains very little of its old charm - the marble stairs and the ornate iron handrails are lovely, but the yellowed walls, with their randomly-placed black-and-white photos of NYC, the glaring ceiling lights and the thin, ugly carpeting leaves much to be desired. The entire hotel has the feel of some sort of run-down boarding house and succeeded in giving me a slight case of the creeps. The rooms are a story in and of themselves.
If you must stay at the Hotel Belleclaire, make sure that you book a room with a private bath. Unlike many hotels, Belleclaire offers rooms with a shared bath. These rooms, separated from the others by their own key-carded door, feature three private bedrooms and one bath that you must share with other people. Do not do this! The room I stayed in was mediocre at best, and the bath was an ugly, green-tiled room that had minimal lighting and provided no fan, so steam from the shower built up and clung to everything. Plus, whenever one of my """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""neighbors"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" went in to take a shower, I heard the plumbing creaking and shrieking until they were finished. My room featured the same yellowed walls as the rest of the hotel, an ancient radiator, stained carpeting, and a slightly musty smell. I don't know who took those pictures that are featured on the hotel's website, but with the exception of the lamps, my room did not resemble those rooms at all. There was a sink in my room, and two cheap mirrors (one of which had a fruit sticker plastered onto it - so much for maid service), and the window had no curtains. It did, however, have a shade, which promptly fell down onto the floor when my boyfriend went to pull it up in the morning. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""incredible"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" view you were hoping for? Non-existent, unless staring at brick walls, air conditioning units and the barred-up window of the room across the way really gets you going.
My room featured a decent television, a CD player that was about the size of a stamp, and toiletries that included a limited quantity of thin towels and some plastic drinking cups. The bed had nice, comfortable, clean linens, which was the only really good thing about the room, although the bed itself was rather lumpy and had the exact same low-quality mattress that I slept on in my college dorm. 
The neighborhood surrounding the Hotel Belleclaire isn't bad - it is typical in its West-side grittiness, but is still nothing to complain about - and if you really need to escape from the Hotel Belleclaire, there is plenty to do in the area. However, I would recommend anyone in need of a hotel on the West side to look elsewhere - the Hotel Belleclaire is distinctly lacking in good, up-to-date amenities, and its old-fashioned charm has been ruined by poorly-designed and ill-maintained rooms and decor. You will get far better service at almost any other hotel. Bottom line: book elsewhere.

Permit a pair of qualifiers from the top. First, I apologize for the title, but the riffs on """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Puttin' on the ritz"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" are just too tempting. 
Second, the three stars (neutral rating) came from this thought: I had an unfortunate experience (not inconsistent with several reviews), told a professional woman at the front desk who asked the pregnant question during check out (""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""How was your stay?""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""), and in response I received a substantial credit against the cost of the room.

While the gesture is more important than the size of the credit, at the end of the day, it really is the sheer cost of a room that makes you want to pull your hair out (what I have left) when things go awry. To business:
Location. Overlooking the Boston Gardens (which are in turn adjacent to Boston Common), RC occupies a corner of Arlington and Newberry. This means about three stops on the Green Line to Fenway (you must use the T in Boston), or multiple stops at the highest end shopping district this side of Madison Avenue, which is Newberry Street. In other words, the hotel could not be more conveneient to all of Boston.
Rooms. I booked AMEX Platinum, getting myself an upgrade from a junior suite to the real thing. My living room was huge, bedroom full sized, and bathroom suitably marbled.
Decor. The words """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""stuffy"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""renovate"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" have been put to better use in other reviews. They are accurate. This is the old world version of Ritz Carlton, and if chintz and fleur de lis are not your thing, consider the Ritz Carlton Boston Common (a couple of blocks away), which is their trendy, up-tempo, post-modern version. This venue is for stiffs. Luckily for RC, there appears to be a bottomless supply of them, all vying for rooms at this hotel.
Vibe. See preceding paragraph. But amidst all those cardboard people I noticed a fair sprinkling of business types just trying to get from here to there. 
Food. My only experience was with room service, described below. However, there are a number of very fine restaurants within easy walking distance in the event your instincts send you out of the building. Please note: RC has always been somewhat fussy about decorum. Jackets are required at most meals for men, and denim is not tolerated. The good news is you'll see no baseball hats or track suits in the dining rooms.
Amenities. There may have been a workout room. I was never told, and nothing in my room would have revealed the truth. However, I did see a sign near an elevator suggesting something of the kind exists. Internet access is $---day, but again, not unless you make a few calls to get the info.

At -:--, the lobby was crowded, but that should not explain the harried and hurried front desk. I was asked for my credit card again (I thought I already checked in). Understand that I'm approaching this review as a female traveling alone. If you're the same, or if you're expecting to schlepp your toddlers from the Hilton uptown for a nice family meal, or if you like to have the option of a quick, inexpensive, conveniently located non-hotel meal (which should be a reasonable expectation when you're staying at a downtown hotel) at the end of a long day, this is not the place for you.
This very attractive Hilton is built on a wedge of land that's surrounded by the San Diego Convention Center on one side; the bay on another, a shipping warehouse on a third, and the same wide, busy street that parallels the Convention Center on the fourth side. To get to the Gaslamp Quarter - or just about anyplace else that would be open after business hours - you're going to be walking north about two blocks to the only crosswalk and taking a right at light. That will take you across about five lanes of traffic and the light railway tracks...and then you're only at the entrance of the Gaslamp Quarter...
These other reviewers who comment on this hotel's """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""good location"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" are probably referring to its hardcore proximity to Petco Park. Yes, it's a short walk to get THERE via an elevated walkway that stretches directly from the hotel to the park like a midair Yellow Brick Road. You could practically catch a fly ball while standing in the hotel's driveway. 
Or they might be referring the fact that the building itself practically cantilevers out over the bay - the views are especially beautiful from the hotel's bay-side terraces. 
Despite what I've said about its location, this is a very good place to attend a business conference. The hotel's footprint is big but not gigantic - virtually all of the functions of the meeting I was attending were on the same floor, but the distances were extremely walkable - and the elevators and escalators to the hotel's guest rooms are a stone's throw away from the meeting rooms. 
In short, I suspect that this hotel was designed to cater to convention-goers and meeting attendees. It does these things very well. But if your goal is to immerse yourself in the sights of San Diego, you might consider choosing a hotel specifically located IN the Gaslamp.

Trip Summary:
Length of Stay - - nights each x - visits
Room Class Booked - Standard Non-Smoking
Room Class Stayed - Standard Non-Smoking

Check-In:
Arrived about - PM via taxi - the check in desk was not busy and well staffed. The desk clerk was extremely nice and had me checked in promptly, inquiring if I needed a wakeup call.
Room:

Amenities:
If I had one negative, it would be the lack of a pool. There is a -- hour outdoor hot tub and a decent workout room. The TV offers a full suite of cable channels. There is 'The Market' in the lobby which sells a selection of snacks and RTE meals at reasonable prices.
Food and Beverage:
Each day, the hotel offers a free breakfast in the Hearth Room in the lobby. It's a huge spread, varies daily, but for example today featured scrambled eggs, ham and cheese scrambled eggs, bacon, potatoes, sausage, biscuits, fruit salad, - kinds of cold cereals, make it yourself waffles and french toast. Plus the usual breads and juices.... 
Monday thru Thursday evenings, there is a free reception in the Hearth Room. Not just snacks, these are full meal offerings. The menu changes regularly, but for example one night this week featured Mac and Cheese (with sliced hotdog option), - types of salad, fresh baked whole wheat roles, and vegetarian tomato tortellini soup. There is a cash bar available in the evenings.
Room service is available from the Broker restaurant next door (at comparable prices to the establishment). I didn't use room service this trip, see Location, below.
Location:
The hotel is located less than a - block walk from the --th street mall, a pedestrian walkway over - mile long and featuring a huge assortment of shops and restaurants, both local and chain (hence no room service). A free shuttle bus runs the length of the mall and makes it easy to get to the LoDo section in a quick amount of time.
Coors field is about a -- minute walk (perfectly safe both ways, I did it for a game). 
The hotel is also convenient to many businesses, and by taking advantage of the mall shuttle, less than a -- minute trip to the Pepsi center.
Customer service:
The hotel staff is really top notch and seems to enjoy working at the hotel. One night, the AC in the room made a slight rattling noise. I reported the issue to the front desk in the AM, and the problem was resolved prior to my return to the room. There was a message on the phone indicating the problem had been resolved, and a note in the room from maintenance to let me know they had been there, as they had to move my suitcase.
Hearth room staff kept the tables constantly clean.
Other Notes:
On some nights, the hotel offers bingo tournaments for charity, or other events in the hearth room.
Conclusion:
This is one of the top Residence Inns I have stayed at (and I have stayed at more than a few. I cannot recommend it enough for either a short or long stay in the Denver area.

We arranged for three Deluxe King rooms, for just under a week, for ourselves and two other couples. Three young adult children shared these rooms with their parents for three of the nights. This part of Bush sees light pedestrian traffic and moderate street traffic. Cabs were easy to flag on the day of the wedding. If you don't know SF, the walk from the Powell BART station to Bush is pretty steep if you have luggage. But the effort is well worth it. We've stayed in many - and - star hotels in SF. This one's our favorite.

Too many New York hotels are legendary for having (a) rooms the size of postage stamps, (b) a surround-sound of constant noise, (c) web sites that bear no resemblance to their reality, and (d) prices far higher than the actual level of your experience. Blessedly, none of these things is true of the Affinia Dumont.
This hotel is defined by two physical facts: its location in Manhattan, and its height. The block of East --th Street on which it's located will never be the culminating scene of a romantic Hollywood movie full of visual cliches about New York. But it's fabulously convenient for anyone driving into or out of Manhattan, since it's a couple of blocks from either the exit of the Queens-Midtown Tunnel or the --th Street exit from the FDR Drive, and offers a straight shot west to the Lincoln Tunnel entrance on the other island of the island. The location also leaves the hotel out of the traffic crunch and noise carnival nearer the heart of midtown. And it has great access on foot to the Empire State and Grand Central. Walk a little east and south, and you're in the heart of Murray Hill. 
The hotel's height -- -- stories -- is also crucial, since that means that its rooms above -- stories are remarkably quiet for Manhattan. And rooms on those floors also have commanding, handsome views of the Chrysler Building and other skyscrapers to the north, and the East River to the east.
Room decor in the Affinia Dumont is comfortable and rather corporate, without being fussy or ornate. We had a junior suite for two nights and found it spacious for two people. Beds are very comfortable, mirrors abound, and high-speed Internet connections are in every room. The staff is faultlessly polite and cheerful, and the in-house spa and work-out room are welcoming and well-equipped.
If there's a drawback, it's the absence of any public spaces, shop or restaurant in the hotel proper. The lobby is small and sleek in a nondescript kind of way -- no place where you'd want to linger. The adjoining restaurant, the Barking Dog, is cute as a cafe, but its role in providing room service leaves a lot to be desired, for a hotel that aims to offer luxury-boutique service. For example, breakfast orders are brought to the room in take-out fashion (in paper bags and foam cups), and the food quality is ordinary.
But if you'd like a base of operations in New York that can give you the sensation of having your own quiet, attractive, roomy apartment, with classic Manhattan views and a location from which the whole island can readily be reached, this is it...

The bathroom looked a little Holiday Inn-ish...the paint was cracking onto the floor, the bath rug was torn, and the toiletries were generic. When I pay well over $--- for a room, I expect brand names and un-torn rugs.
