This was a nice place, though, great location, like I said. You can walk to anywhere, and the market on a Saturday is a great place to people watch!

I stayed her last year and the pics on the website seemed very impressive. However the rooms are a little dated even though they are very big. We had an upgrade to a Suite which had a kitchen, sitting area and big sliding door windows overlooking the private beach area. Hotel is walking distance of Mission beach and a few good eateries. Hotel has a small pool with a nice jacuzzi and a small gym. Also they have - tennis courts which dont ususally get used during the day. Overall the stay was satisfactory but if I went to SD again I would look to stay elsewhere as it was a little pricey for what it is.

I absolutly love this hotel. The front desk staff is very friendly and accomadating. I stay at this hotel every time I am in Seattle and I have no complaints. The rates tend to be a little higher than other properties in the area, but the excellent service is totally worth the price.

We welcomed our return each night to the quiet room on an upper floor of this marvelous hotel. No, they do not have certain amenities (pool, gym, etc) but we were looking for close proximity to theaters and convenient transportation. Our stay was for four days and we enjoyed our stay at the Distrikt Hotel. I am always happy when my search of Tripadvisor leads me to a good experience. Check the special hotel deals that TripAdvisor offers and you may find a discounted rate for your stay. As reported, the beds are comfortable and the hotel is clean and the heat-ac unit was not noisy. Also in other reviews, mention is made the surrounding area appears a bit dicey but we did not worry about our safety. There is a lot of movement in the area. 
The Port Authority has a food court if you need to find fast food.
The staff at the hotel is very helpful and pleasant. We asked for a restaurant recommendation before attending the theater and the front desk recommended Becco, an Italian restaurant nearby. We were able to get in without reservations (luckily) and sat in the bar area. We had a lovely meal.

I'm happy to say the Contessa was better than expected. It is a perfect location on the river walk and its a beautifully designed hotel. La Villita is literally right around the corner and the Riverwalk is beautiful to stroll.
The room was a good size with a seperate living room area with a television (not flat screen), a wet bar with granite countertops and they throughly nailed the Spanish Decor. I felt like I was back in Seville! 
The staff was extremely friendly and helpful. Granted the bellmen needed to brush up on where I could catch the correct trolley to the Alamo etc. Turns out the pick-ups were less than -- feet from the hotel for all routes. 
If you go you must try Las Ramblas Restaurant at the hotel. The service was excellent and the waiters are eager to serve. The food was great! Didn't get the chance to try the 'award winning' paella, but their Roasted Lamb made a beliver of me. 
Skip Room Service if you can its overpriced and I felt """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""stiffed"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". If you can, ask for a room not overlooking the road. If you are a light sleeper trucks passing at night will keep you up. 
I would definitely stay at the Contessa again. Great Hotel, Good Food and Great People. Loved San Antonio.

Everyone was very friendly,location was great. Lobby bar was great to relax and get away from the crowds.Room was clean and quiet!!! Bathroom had all the personal touches and great terry robe.Great place to stay..........

I stayed at Club Quarters for about - nights in July ----. The location was great - close to major subway, tourist sites, shops and restaurants. Rooms were pleasant and spacious - clean and comfortable. I like the fact that there is a water dispenser for guests to help themselves with water but there is no fridge in the room. Price of stay was reasonable.

We loved our stay in this hotel! The service and attention to detail from the staff was outstanding! The rooms were clean and beautiful...also a great size compared to most NY hotels. The food from the restaurant was exceptional and THE VIEW!--from the roof deck took my breath away! I will definitely be a repeat guest as will my friends who were there with me!

This was my second stay at this property and it blew me away. It has a lot of different sections, so know what you like before you book. The first time, I stayed in one of the single or double level rooms. I didn't like them because the door and window open on to the main 'street' which made it easy to hear people walking outside. Once I moved to the Royal Towers, though... much better. I liked having that 'hotel room' feel, with a balcony. 
 But it was really the staff who made my trip special. Check in was quick. If you are a business owner, I definitely recommend signing up for their Executive Star club. It's a great deal and includes shuttle transport to and from the airport, wireless internet and daily breakfast for two. They checked me in promptly. I do wish they had the vouchers for the shuttle driver right at the front desk when I arrive because I felt badly that he had to wait (with other customers in the shuttle) for them to get it. Other than that, check in was great. 
 They have a courtesy shuttle within a --- mile radius. And with the largest mall in San Diego right behind the property... no problem. The bellman-valet dropped me off at Target and they came back and picked me up when I finished. 
 When I called for down pillows instead of foam, they were delivered promptly. I needed a refrigerator for my medications and even though they couldn't guarantee it in advance, they were able to get it to my room within -- minutes of my arriving.
 The staff and service was great. I did not use room service due to my strict diet, but my friend did. She was disappointed with the breakfast. 
 Overall though, I loved it.

I have stayed at the Marriott hotel a block away previously for a yearly convention and this time at the Crowne Plaza this year. The courtesy of the staff is by far the best I have ever experienced. The convention draws thousands of people to Downtown San Jose and some hotels would dread the influx but the staff was all smiles the whole weekend and was eager to see everyone arrive and were all eager to help us throughout our stay. Garage is self parking and also offered in and out service, also for this event, parking was restricted to hotel guests only so there would be plenty of space for guests staying at the hotel. Our room was spacious with a king bed and the sofa also was a pull out bed if needed and there was also plenty of available plugs for various electronic power needs. Bathroom was a bit smaller then what I am used to for hotels but its not like it is a main focus on a stay. 
Minor down points, found a potato chip in the sofa under the cushion but being under it might be a reason it was not found when cleaned prior to our stay. The cushion had a strange black stain on it too. Window lock was broken so it slides open easily but locks open just enough for fresh air
 All in all, I will be staying at this hotel next year for my convention.

Stayed - nights at the Casablanca - --- December. We cannot speak too highly of this hotel. Excellent, friendly staff, quiet, well appointed rooms and the unexpected (for NYC) Rick's Cafe with complimentary breakfast buffet, afternoon coffee and evening wine. Well placed off Times Square the Casablanca has none of the unnecessary bling of the large chain hotels or the forced, false coolness of many boutique hotels. Instead it has a warm and friendly ambience from the moment you arrive. The staff make a real effort to get to know you and help make your stay in NYC a good experience.
Have stayed in a number of hotels in NYC over the years but this is the best. Would definitely return and recommend highly.

I stayed here November -- to --. I found the previous reviews helpful and generally accurate. A few additions or corrections:

I was surprised to find there is not even a bottle opener in the suite. (Many hotels have one in the bathroom, but not here.)
Parking is right behind the hotel, and although it isn't beautiful, I didn't get the sense that it was unsafe. Nobody touched my BMW in the - nights it was there.
The staff were uniformly friendly; I was pleasantly suprised at how good they were at this.
Overall, I thought this was a good deal for the price and I'd stay there again.

My wife and I just got home from a six-night stay at this hotel and we cannot say enough about the facility and the staff. This property is second to none. The hotel is extremely clean and very safe. We stayed on the --st floor and the view was awesome. The rooftop pool is a great place to unwind after a busy day exploring this great city. We were blessed to have clear skies and a moon to shine down on us. The hotel is within walking distance to everything. If I am ever afforded the chance to visit Chicago again this hotel will be where I stay!

I thought this hotel was great. We had a corner room on the --th floor and the view was amazing. The room was also very clean and quiet. The bed was large and comfortable and the staff was very friendly and helpful. I also loved the location.

We stayed here for - nights from September --th to the --st.
The good: The hotel's location is unbeatable. It's so close to shopping, restaurants and the Metro. The weather was gorgeous while we were visiting and so we walked to the National Mall, memorials, Smithsonian and Capitol Hill. Everything takes under an hour to walk to. The breakfast was fine, not good but not terrible. It does get really busy between -am and -:--am. If you're ok with cereal, yogurt, juice, tea and coffee, it's good enough. The bad: The hotel is tired. Really tired. The staff are just doing the bare minimum to cover what needs to be done. The price is amazing, but if they charged slightly more, they could use the money to do some renovating. The rooms are small and our hotel room didn't have a tub. 
The ugly: We booked on Priceline for myself, my husband and our two toddlers and I have always called in advance to ask for a room with two double beds or one King bed for us to share. Never an issue (most hotels ONLY have these kinds of rooms.) Here I was told that I would be getting a room with a Queen bed and if I wanted more space, I should have booked two rooms. They could upgrade us to a bigger room for an additional $--- a night. A rollaway would cost an additional $-- a day per child. Not sure where it (or they) would have gone since there was barely space for the Queen bed. One of our sons ended up sleeping in a small portable toddler bed we bought and the other slept between us. Not awesome service at all, considering how long we were staying there.

The location was great. The room decor was better than most Sheratons and it was nice having coffee available in the rooms. The management generally treated me well as a spg platinum.
On the other hand, they sent two bills after checkout by Internet, both with incorrect charges. When calling to fix the errors, I had to wait. Over - minutes on hold waiting for a live operator to answer. At every call, I noted long delays and an annoying ARU. There was a long delay to be checked in at the front desk. There were only - towels in the bathroom.

This hotel is absolutely fantastic. My husband and I, having never been to NYC, picked this off of the Choice Hotel website. It's close to major attractions (Times Square, Central Park, Empire State Building) and the service is amazing. We were always greeted with happy faces and the staff seemed very genuine. The room itself was spacious for a NYC hotel room (or my understanding of a standard NYC hotel room at least!) and was very clean. The bed was extremely comfortable as well. We have absolutely nothing bad to say about this hotel. If you go to NYC, it's a must!

Stayed there for - nights. Prime location: very near to many attractions and very close to most subway lines. Beautiful rooms. Excellent service. Fast wireless internet. 
Fitness club. Very good restaurant and great bar.
Stay on one of the concierge floor and get access to the lounge.

Centrally located (Prudential Center) with bus stops at the front door and ---- taxi stand that worked we enjoyed staying at a Sheraton much to my surprise. While not what I wanted to spend all hotels in Boston were more expensive we thought. We could have stayed further out for less but then what is the point? The Sheraton (and several other hotels)are attached to a two gigantic shopping mall or malls with every variety of price range. and type of shopping and food. Even Legal Seafgood which we enjoyed twice for lunch. Back Bay location near Bewbury street asnd museums was ideal.
We arrived before noon expecting to wait, and had requested a river view room . The front desk clerk immedately gave us several options (the hotel was full). The concierge staff were also exemplary. Our room was good and we could see sail boats racing along the river. The views of the roofs of buildings were less than spectacular but it was still worth it. Any call was answered and responded to rapidly.
With so many options right there we were very happy and the wide screen TV kept the sports fan happy, too.

My husband and I stayed at this hotel over a long weekend with our - year toddler. They were excellent and family friendly. Check in was easy and quick. Parking system was easy in and out. Hotel is nice and clean with cool decor. Our room was awesome, perfect for what we were looking for. Our toddler was able to go to bed in the bedroom and my husband and I were able to hang out in the living room and enjoy our evening. Had no issues at all, would definitely go and stay there again!

I've just received a letter from American Express saying that there has been a breach in the security at the hotel and that my card has been compromised. Somehow this is not surprising: last October I checked my bags with the valet while attending a brunch at the hotel and came back only to find that one was missing. Why am I not surprised that -) they kept my credit card information on file and -) they let it be subjected to fraud??? It's a nice hotel, but their care for guests is not what I am accustomed to.

First of all, never go here if you are two adults with one or two children thinking you can share one room. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""double bed"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" is small - more like a single. My wife and I are not tall by any means, but we were so on top of each other...

Overall, there is nothing truly bad about this hotel - apart from bed size - but the problem is that there was nothing truly positive to say about it either!

The location for this hotel cannot be better. It is central to everything. You can walk to Michigan and the Magnificent Mile, and at the same time there is a subway stop on the next block. Stores, resturants, all within two blocks. There is a resturant on this property, Weber Grill, but we did not eat here. Rooms were pretty standard, they include a micro and a small refrig. 
 There was something going on with the smell at the end of the hall. Huge drying fans were drying out whatever it was, we also noticed this on another floor. Front desk was extremely friendly on the morning shift.

This is a very nice hotel right on San Diego Bay. The rooms are nicely decorated and the beds very comfortable. Every room has a lovely balcony. It is right next to the convention center and has easy walking access to the restaurants and shops of the Gaslamp district. All the staff were very courteous and professional. The perfect place to stay for business or leisure.

Paid $--- on Expedia. Yes, $---, not $--- like you would expect. I've paid more for a Red Roof in Chicago!!
Sure the parking is $-- per day but this is downtown Chicago. It's the going rate.

The second downer was no alcohol at the pool. I guess I'm a bit of a lush, but man it would have been nice to have a cold one in the hot tub.

Georgetown Suites is a great place to stay, whether the trip is for business or a holiday. Our room was very spacious, with an area for a sofa, chair and coffee table - another area for a small dining table and a desk for work. Kitchen was very clean. I would highly recommend this hotel, especially for an extended stay. The location is in Georgetown. The circulator bus services this area and is a great way to get around three key areas in DC. Our first impression- Olga (per her name badge) at the check-in counter provided some of the worst customer service I've seen yet. She was rude, moved at glacial speed, and never once smiled or said thank you. 
The room was small but well decorated. The bathroom was clean but needed some updating. 
The hotel's only restaurant- our last impression, reaffirmed the title of our review. The staff was pleasant but borderline incompetent. The restaurant was empty, yet my wife actually got up, walked out to the main lobby and poured her own coffee from the welcome desk because the staff ignored us for -- minutes. When our food arrived, it was decent, with the exception of the bacon with looked to be about - days old. 
Needless to say, we won't return.

I recently stayed at the Hotel Moderne and the old saying is true - you get what you pay for. The front door handle fell off while I was there, wifi was non-existent (contrary to what was promised) wake up calls were missed, doors squeeked like a haunted house and housekeeping put a plastic lid back on a used water glass with water still in it - yuck - made you wonder about the overall hygiene of the place. The rooms are like a cave with no natural light. The hotel is centrally located which is the only positive thing I can say about it.

What a great hotel! Perfect location - right in the middle of everything. Subway right outside the door. We could see the Empire State Building from our room. It was a small room, but we didn't care. We had enough room for the two of us. Can't comment on any extra service as we didn't require any. The concierge was very nice. They were all very helpful directing us to where we wanted to go. I would absolutely stay here again and would recommend it to anyone.

Location is so important to me. And this hotel is perfectly located in the heart of downtown Seattle. We loved this hotel and I would definitely stay here again. We were within walking distance of Pike Place Market, the monorail which took us to the Space Needle and one of the most delish restarurants - The Dahlia Lounge. 
The hotel is lovely, customer service is excellent and the rooms were elegant and nice - and roomy!!

I travel to NYC all the time and stay at many different hotels. I was extremely impressed by the W by every measure. Starting with the front desk help...very professional, they genuinely """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cared"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" about providing good customer service. The rooms were great...my teenagers loved the iPod chargers and my wife enjoyed the Bliss products. This is a property that is very, very well managed...clearly, the GM runs a tight ship, to the benefit of the customer. Bravo!

Our room was clean and small. Bed comfortable. The building is old and parts were undergoing renovation outside. To be thankful we didn't hear any construction noise. Our window view was of scaffolding and a brick wall! Staff service was average. We did like the complimentary late afternoon wine in the lobby lounge. Boston accomodation prices were ridiculously high we thought.
Tv's ate old and suckie but the hotel made up for it ... I was there for -- days and it was just great

The Westin Rivere North has become my second home, i travel out on business every other if not --- weeks a month. I always stay there - mainly because of its location and above all because of Sam - the gym trainer. I meet with Sam nearly everyday to either box or do a gym program. Sam is so nice and friendly that my day is brightened by my -am workout.

We booked this hotel as a package through British Airways and thought it very good value. It is well located for the airport but in a quiet part of the city. Our room was a standard - but in the US this means greater value than UK hotels. We had a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""living room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" with television, fridge and coffee maker, bathroom area with toilet and shower separate to the sink area, bedroom with television and a balcony which overlooked a car parking area but we were not at all bothered by noise. The bed was a king size and was extremely comfortable with excellent pillows. The air conditioning was extremely efficient and despite this being June with outside temperates of around --- degrees F the room was always comfortable. Our stay was during the US school holidays and the hotel was quite busy, particularly over the weekend but we did not find this a problem. Being visitors from the UK and particularly on our first few days before our """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""time clock"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" had adjusted, we were getting up quite early so sometimes had the pool in our block to ourselves. The lazy river and pool complex located at the back of the hotel were at times busy but on our last evening we had the lazy river to ourselves as families had presumably gone off to have dinner and it was very peaceful and relaxing. However, it has to be said that at times the pool areas were very busy and noisy so you need to choose your time to go and early mornings or late evenings were the times, if you wished to have a peaceful dip. As part of our deal we had breakfast vouchers and used these in the hotel restaurant (Lantina Grille) for the buffet breakfast which was adequate. There is a supermarket a couple of blocks down from the hotel and we bought water and soft drinks there which we kept in the fridge of our room so we always had a cool drink and I had taken tea bags so we used the coffee maker to heat the water and brewed tea this way. How English of us - but it was great to have a cup of tea in the mornings. 
The hotel was in a good spot for getting to restaurants and shopping areas and it only took around -- - -- mins (depending on traffic) to get to Scottsdale shopping and restaurants. Equally easy was getting to the main highways for our trips out of town. We had visited Phoenix twice before and stayed in different hotels but thought this hotel was very good and we would definitely recommend it to others.

I took my daughter-in-law and grand daughter for a girls only weekend. The property is very well maintained, staff was wonderful even took the time to talk to my - year old granddaughter about her doll. Great place to stay if you're wanting to shop 'til you drop!

It's funny because everything I had thought about writing when reviewing this hotel was for the most part, accounted below as well!
Nice and new, modern and fresh - at first glance. Then as you settle in, you realize there are a lot of crumbs and other little things on the floor, mostly in the corners and spots where someone haphazardly vacuuming wouldn't catch. Lots of spills-stains on the carpets.

There were clipped fingernails on the desk. Like a full hand's worth and they weren't hard for me to see and freak out about!

I think that this hotel will be very nice once the major renovations they are doing are completed. However, for our family, we were quite disappointed. We had looked forward to spending some relaxing time at the pool upon arrival - - until we realized we would have to cross - lanes of traffic to get to the pool. At check-in, we were """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""upgraded"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to a suite. We had reserved a room with - queens and the one we got had a king and a pull-out sofa. I will say that the front desk was willing to make accommodations for us (switch rooms, brought more towels promptly as well as bed linens for the rollaway when we asked),but we will not stay here again. This hotel would be fine for the business traveler, but certainly not for a family wanting to use the pool. In addition, there was a general air of stress at the front desk. While waiting to speak with someone at the front desk, another man stormed out 
as he yelled at the front desk person. 
Parking was expensive (even self-park) - - the breakfast was $--.-- per person - - we had two free breakfasts, but we had three people.

The hotel looks a bit old from the outside, but the room we stayed at was very clean and fairly large with a nice sofa. The furniture was old fashioned, but in good shape, with just a few nicks and scratches here and there. The room got a good amount of daylight thanks to the sliding door into the little balcony. No dusty or moldy smell that I sometimes get even in some well known chains. The road noise is quite loud, but it was acceptable if I keep the sliding door closed. 
I can stay here again, but I cannot say I loved it. We definitely prefer the Hilton Garden Inn on the other side of the freeway. It is definitely more elegant. The furniture there is more modern and they have a nice reception area with high ceilings, a fireplace and comfy couches. 
Holiday Inn was undergoing renovations when we stayed there and it seemed they are replacing the furniture. I think our room was among the old ones. Fortunately, we did not hear any construction noise, except in the reception area.

I chose Nine Zero after reading Trip Advisor reviews (thanks Trip Advisor!), and I was not disappointed. I walked from the train station in a cold drizzling rain and was pretty chilled when I walked in the front door. The very friendly front desk clerk asked me if I'd like a complimentary glass of wine to warm me up. I said that would be great if I was a drinker, but what I really needed was a hot cocoa. We both chuckled and I went to my room (which is great, by the way). A few minutes later, as I was putting on my running shoes to go to the fitness center there was a knock at the door. To my surprise and delight a gentleman was standing there with a slice of pie and a tall hot cocoa, complete with marshmallows! He said that he was the night manager and had overheard my conversation with the front desk clerk and wanted to welcome me to the Nine Zero. The hotel is beautiful. The room is great. Kimpton hotels always have great beds, this is no exception. The fitness center is small, but up-to-date and complete. One thing I love about Kimpton hotels is a small thing. They all have a light switch when you walk in that actually turns lights on in the room, instead of just the little hall light you get in most chain hotels. It feels like home. Like I said, it's a small thing, but it's the little things that matter.
Hotel is a breath of fresh air! Meeting space, service and hotels rooms were fantastic!

The employees were friendly and tried to be helpful. The room and sheets were clean. However, neither phone worked. Two lamps were plugged into an outlet that didn't work. The one outlet that did work was overloaded with plugins. We had to pay extra for a microwave that we couldn't plug in because the outlet was full. The furniture was very worn.

Arrived at --.-- hours, Check-in was fast, Staff very helpful with maps and directions to places. Rooms had fridge, microwave and coffee maker and very comfy. The only negative thing is that there is a In-Out burger next door which is very busy, ask for an inside room. Safe is $-.-- per day. Would go back to this hotel if I visited LA again.

That feature with its other attributes makes this the only Charlotte hotel we choose for airport access. We'll stay here the next time we fly out of Charlotte.

My room was a decent size for a urban hotel and was clean. The room has been refreshed recently but has a generic hotel look. Neither breakfast nor internet are included in the room rate even though hotels at the same price point do offer free internet. There are very few rooms on each floor so the elevators invariably make a lot of stops. Although there's a Subway next door and several other hotels within several blocks, there aren't many restaurants or bars in the immediate area.

A couple hundred dollars a night and no Internet. Rooms were so-so. Mini blinds on the windows not what I expected for a W hotel. Customer service was very bad the first two days and better towards the end. Bought a bottle of champagne from hotel and then told we could not enjoy in downstairs 
Do not recommend the restaurant-bar downstairs. Foot was below average and we paid $--.-- for two drinks.

For anyone with pets, especially for an extended stay, the Residence Inn was wonderful. We were on the go quite a bit so didn't take advantage of the food as much as we should have but it would be a significant cost savings for families with children or on a limited budget. The eating area is very spacious. I would definetly stay here again! God Bless You, Sherrill Hooker

was a bit hesitant booking this hotel based on various reviews. But to our suprise was a beautiful hotel, nice small but adequate rooms. Great breakfast. the location was the appeal to us. Easy to jump on a bus or the metro to explore the city if you don't have a car. Would recommend and definitely stay here again. Felt reasonably safe in this area, but hey, where in LA right !!!

I have to say, when we first booked our stay at a Hyatt, I was hesitant just because it is a chain hotel. However, any preconceived notion I had of chain hotels fell to the wayside when I stayed at this location. I have never in my life been met with such great service, especially at a hotel in the US. From the time we checked in with Rachel, to the Regency Club with Ly and Elizabeth, I just couldnt get over how great everything was. Every single person, and I do mean every single person, from the Valet (Hunter) to the lovely maid, was extremely outgoing, friendly, nice and just made you feel wonderful. I have not been met with such great customer service in such a long time, I was in shock. The hotel room was clean and fresh, the ocean view was amazing, the pools perfect, and the ground were kept in a tropical feel. The property itself is in a great location, with gorgeous views, and the people alone make this property a place I want to go back to and visit. The workout room is small but clean and inviting and extremely motivating as it overlooks the marina. I am beyond impressed with the Hyatt and this property and I would, without a doubt, recommend it to anyone staying in San Diego.

The Magnolia was a luxury gift from me to me, and I would go back in a heartbeat. We love staying downtown, but this was such a quiet and lovely place for a romantic getaway. We never heard a soul, despite the fact the place was bulging with people. No sounds from upstairs, next door, hallway, etc. I never saw any children. We upgraded to a suite, which made our bedroom small, but it was way cool to have the living room and kitchen available to us. We missed happy hour both nights, but the cookies were a plus. Breakfast was very hectic due to the Mary Kay convention going on, but it didn't effect the quality of the food. People were so friendly! I heartily recommend this hotel to anyone who deserves the best.

Despite some bad reviews here on the site we stayed at the aloft last time we were in Philly. I actually found a room last minute on priceline I believe.. The room was pretty low cost and high quality. My kids really enjoyed the pool... They got several hours of fun out of the pool and outside patio. The bar was pretty cool later in the evening too... I only had wished there was food available on the premesis.. A hot breakfast would have made this an excellent stay for us. There were no problems checking in or out, and the rooms were modern and Clean. I would stay there again without a doubt.

My husband and I booked this night the same day with a reward certificate on the eve of the Indianapolis Mini Marathon. It's the perfect location to stay for this event. The staff was nice and the rooms were clean. They are on the smallish side of ES rooms, but the bed was very comfortable and the rooms were equipped with nice flat screen tvs. 
We were happy to be able to walk out the door and down the steps to Washington St to join our corral assignments for the half marathon. 
Breakfast was typical of ES fare, but the staff was nice and stayed a bit late for those getting back from the mini marathon which I thought was very kind. 
Will definitely come back to ES Downtown Indy again!

We had a fantastic stay at the Giraffe Hotel. Lovely room, perfectly clean with big, comfy bed, plenty of storage space and great bathroom. Breakfast in the lobby and evening drinks were both very enjoyable. The evening turn down service was also a nice touch. Nice terrace on the roof, though it was too cold to really enjoy it.
The location is perfect, pretty central but away from the noise on quiet Park Avenue. Check out Blue Smoke and Jazz Standard around the corner, and Mexican place next door has geart food and excellent Mojitos.
I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone, and trust me, I'm very picky.
Right in the middle of everything we wanted to get to. It is well presented, and very clean and great value. Have already returned, and will do so again!

We stayed here over the -th of July weekend and had a great time. Not only was it $-- a night for a suite but the room was awesome with a beautiful view. Our son loved the pool area. It was crowded but we still managed to have a good time and try out all the pools and the water slide. Food in the pool area was very expensive but that is to be expected at these resorts so when dinner time we ordered pizza and went and picked it up. Climbing the hills to get to our room was a bit of a trek but it was well worth it. Very pretty grounds.
I hate that there is no free wi-fi.

First off let me state that this hotel in not up to Marrriott standards! I will keep this brief, our room ---, albeit a very spacious one bedroom, was disgusting and run down. The disgusting part was in the bathroom (please see attached photos) the shower was caked in yellow-brown scuz that had obviously been accumulating for a LOONNG time! I gave it the benefit of that doubt that perhaps it was hard water stained BUT NO, it easily scraped off!!! After reading many reviews on this site it is abundantly clear that this hotel has housekeeping issues that need to be addressed since the negative reviews about the lack of cleanliness go back to ----!!!!! We did submit out photos to Marriott corporate and I informed the manager of my actions, she thanked me because they really want a renovation!!! I assertively explained to her that I can overlook the old and out of date decor because you can have """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""clean old stuff"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" BUT you cannot renovate filth!!!! C'mon Marriott I do hope you realize that if you can't upgrade the quality of your housekeeping staff your newly renovated hotel that you so desperately want will also be filthy in no time!!!
 I will also say that the front desk staff is nice and friendly and the location is great BUT, at the end of the day I am not living with the front desk staff in my room and I am not paying to sleep in the Galleria itself, I have paid for a room that is guaranteed to be clean and well appointed at this Marriott property which has obviously been forgotten by corporate's quality assurance team.

From the moment we checked in, we were greeeted by two very pleasant desk clerks. They were very helpfull in giving us directions to places in the area. We were mistakenly given the wrong suite, and upon seeing it and letting the clerks know about it they quickly rectified the situation. After resting for a while we went downstairs where we were each given a shot of Tequilla. The hotel was very clean. At -pm the complimentary wine and cheese and crackers were served on the mezzanine each day. The complimentary breakfast was beyond expectation and choices were more than sufficient. As for noise level, well when your in the downtown area with all of the hustle and bustle, it is to be expected and beyond their control. However the hotel did provide earplugs. We enjoyed our stay and the hotel provided better than average service, they cared.

We came to be close to our family at the time of our grandson's cranial operation at CHOP. We read the reviews written by others prior to our arrival but were not deterred by the negative comments. The hotel staff was most friendly and accomidating. The facility was very clean and pleasant. The fact that it is adjacent to the Childrens Hospital was a decided plus. For an inercity hotel the price is right. If one wants to stay for the amineties of a full service hotel, they should try another. If they want to be close to the child and the family, THIS IS THE Place

I had the pleasure of staying at this property on business. This is a truly beautiful hotel. The staff were polite and professional and the rooms were wonderful. The hotel has many new-high end amenities which made the experience even better. 
This hotel is also situated perfectly in the city near great restaurants and great shopping. I look forward to going back!

This hotel is excellent. Well situated for Central Park, the major stores, Apple,MOMA etc.
I had a suite which was superb - modern,stylish and super comfortable.
The staff could not do enough and were extremely professional. Like I say in the heading, I'm fussy but The London gave me absolutely nothing to complain about.
I wanted a late check out because my plane was leaving in the evning. I spoke to reception who said it was absolutely fine .Most other places pull a face , moan and groan and then relcutantly give you an extra - hours over the check out time, at a charge.I got - hours at no charge.
Would I go back? - Yes. Would I recommend it ? Yes
Go!

We stayed at this hotel June ----- in a junior suite (which was quite large). You couldn't ask for a better location. Close to LOTS of restaurants and shopping in a fabulous neighborhood. Two subway stations are very nearby and cabs were plentiful and easy to come by. There were only a few downsides: -) the beds were awful. Rock hard. So hard, in fact, that we had to sleep atop our comforters and even then, it was only marginally more comfortable than sleeping on the floor. -) the hotel's website said the junior suites had - flat-screen tv's. We did have a small flat-screen tv in the bathroom, but a regular tv (which was quite old) in the main room. They use Dish Network, which provided only a small handful of channels. -) There is no counter space in the bathroom. You can put a couple of things on the large sink's ledge, otherwise you had to put everything on the toilet tank. There were two blow dryers in the bathroom, but with - people in the room, it wasn't practical to have someone in there drying their hair and doing their makeup while two other people were waiting to use the bathroom. There was a very large mirror in the main room that could be used for getting ready, but there was no nearby table or electrical outlet. We actually had to go to Duane Reed and buy an extension cord! -) There were no directories in the room - no phone books, no book of services or nearby businesses. There is a concierge on staff, but only during daytime hours. -) There are - doormen who also serve as the bell hops. Unfortunately, that meant that there was often no one at the door. Not a big deal, unless you were lugging in a bunch of suitcases. That said, the front desk was quite accommodating and quick with any and all of our requests (more blankets, towels, replace battery in remote control, etc...)
Overall, I would recommend this hotel. However, I would check the bed as soon as you get to the room and if it's rock hard, ask for another room. Assuming I could get a room with a better mattress, I wouldn't hesitate to stay at the hotel again. As I said, the location and neighborhood were fantastic and - with the exception of the torturous mattresses - easily outweighs the other minor negatives.

i was in ths hotel for - nights: it is not in line with a - star reting. the room was very small, the bathroom small and not daily cleaned, generally speacking the hotel looks old and for turists who do not needs any additional service; not for business; a - star reting it's more correct i think; the price ocnsequentlly is too high; you can find other better locations in the same block; so there are no reasons to choos this one.

I travel a lot and wanted an ADVENTURE! I wanted out of the chain hotel rut. This is a cool old school hotel. If you are a diva stay away! I liked the old feeling of the hotel it has all of the basic needs of a place to stay. I liked that you can walk anywhere in downtown that you would need to go. The hotel was pretty clean and it was hot-humid so get to your room turn on the air then go to Greektown and chill. By the time you get back your room will be tolerable. Had a good time here but again it is not a big chain and more for the adventurous.

We have returned for weekends several times per year, and enjoy the lobby and room decor. When we manage to book the executive floors, we particularly appreciate the personal attention of Ernest F, who caters to the family's every need. My only grumble is that WiFi could be complementary when we're paying these rates.

Surprised to see all the excellent reviews for this hotel. While the staff were very nice, the rooms are old and tired. In the king deluxe room, the bathroom is very small. There is only one sad chair...fine if you are alone on business but a little awkward when traveling as a couple. The wallpaper in the room was a mess and it obviously had not been replaced in along time. The furniture is also quite worn. If you are going into the city on a weekend there are much better hotels for the same money. On the positive side, Feinsteins at the Regency is a great place to hear live music in a very intimate atmosphere.

This hotel is unimpressive. It is simply a place to sleep. I didn't feel safe sleeping in here. The bathroom door wouldn't fully shut and I could hear everything going on in there. Not a place to go with your significant other. The neighborhood is decent. I would never stay here again or recommend to a friend.

I was stunned to pay $--- a night for this hotel and then find that I'm in a tower that is under rennovation and has earthmoving equipment in the atrium. I am posting a view from my doorway looking into the atrium...there is a horrible construction smell and no AC in the tower (though there is AC in the rooms). But walking from the elevator to the room is a sauna.
I am trying to work in my room and I'm hearing """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""beep. beep. beep."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I spoke to the hotel front desk clerk and said that I cannot be the only one to be shocked and she said -- with a straight face -- """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""actually ma'am, you're the first to mention it."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" I just about burst out laughing.
When I wanted a simple latte and pastry, I was sent to a bar where I waited behind a long line of people being serviced by just one bartender. After he made cosmos and bloodies, he got to my latte. It was so frustrating.
I'm sure this will be great when the rennovation is over, but for now, I'd stay away. The rates should be deeply discounted to entice people to put up with this.

The Hotel is nice and the room is not that small as some previous reviews said. I think it is one of the best in Times Square Area. There is a Subway station just beside the main entrance. 
The only problem that I had was regarding the reservation, that was for a Deluxe High Floor room and they gave me a Regular room in a lower floor. The view of my room was an old office building, but I decided to stay there because the room was nice and it was very quiet, because was not facing the -th ave. They gave me the money back for the room difference at the checkout.
Recommendations: 
-) Tips: There are a lot of people to help you, so you have to tip everywhere. For example, there is a guy who help you with the luggage when you arrive, but he just take the luggage from the street and put inside the hotel. I was expecting that he would be the guy who was taking care of the luggage until the room, but I had to tip him and tip another guy to do that, but ok, they are nice.
-) Restaurant: I asked for a chicken sandwich and it was not nice, in my oppinion. Very expensive and tasteless. 
-) Don't touch the refrigerator: Once you take any beverage from the refrigerator, they are going to charge you. I just took to check some items and decided to don't take it, but they charged me. The front desk accepted to discount the item, but I think it is not really nice.

Modern customer service expectations are so low that to experience the warmth and support of the staff I felt this past weekend at Hotel Palomar initially felt surreal. This was my experience being greeted by the friendly valet-men and the professional bell-hops. My introduction to Hotel Palomar inspired memories of a time when people treated other people like family, folks had pride in their job, and going the extra mile was """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""no trouble at all"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". By the time I made it through the front doors of the hotel, I had a smile on my face, I was relaxed, and I realized that this hotel was special.
I stay at Ritz-Carltons, Hiltons, and many other very nice hotels, but Hotel Palomar takes the cake. It appeared that everyone, at every level, understood that the beautiful physical environment at Hotel Palomar would account for nothing if it was not supported by the most important aspect of a hotel, a friendly supporting staff. 
Upon arrival, the young man at the front desk, Josh, assisted us by giving us a map and describing different parts of town. Throughout our weekend, he assisted us with information on local events we would not have otherwise known about. I called down to the Concierge for a Zagat Rated restaurant that evening. On my way out for the day I was handed a number of different options with more information than I could have ever expected. It was as if the hotel actually cared about making my stay enjoyable.

My friends and I traveled up to San Jose to go watch the gymnastics Olympic Trials a few weeks ago and stayed at the Holiday Inn by the airport. The hotel has complimentary airport shuttle that we fully took advantage of. Upon arriving at the hotel, I noticed that the color scheme reminded me so much of my living room - tropical green with dark brown. So already I felt at ease. We checked in and were impressed with how big the rooms were. The next day we enjoyed a nice afternoon by the pool. We liked that the towels were already on the chairs when we got down there. The ONLY thing missing was a cocktail server. We also had the continental breakfast and liked the selection - eggs, bacon, French toast, fruits, cereal and juices. We were told later that you could actually request any style of eggs you wanted. Next time, for sure. The friendly staff and the cleaning crew were on top of it. We came back to a nice clean room everyday. . Overall, it was nice and pleasant stay.

I was a guest at the Westin Philadelphia on Nov. --th for a quick business trip. It was perfectly pleasant, nothing remarkable but a standard Westin experience. That was until I inadvertently left my Kindle in my room. Despite a quick call to lost and found, along with strong reassurances that the Kindle was not recovered, someone ran up over $-- of charges in a matter of two days. One can only presume a member of the Westin staff is currently enjoying some quiet time with new literature.

This hotel has a convinient parking garage, spaceful and clean rooms but somewhat old furnitures and a bit worn out. Friendly and very helpful staff. The breakfast was good. Location.. Well convinient due to nearby sights.. But a poor area in our eyes (?) Make sure to eat at the sights - no restaurants-diners close by the hotel as far as we could figure out. Laundry close by which was convinient. Subway next door. We stayed only two nights due to road trip in California.

The hotel is the cheapest possible on Manhattan (as far as I know), and the best possible for the price. The rooms can be small, but they are clean; the bathrooms are well taken care of; the staff is friendly; the location is also great, as the hotel is a block and a half from a subway station. If you are looking for the hostel feel, this isn't the place to be because it's structured like a hotel, but it's quiet and can be wonderful substitute for a regular hotel. I was with my boyfriend and, overall, we were both thoroughly impressed and would definitely recommend it to any NYC visitor who is on a tight budget.

The Larchmont's location in Greenwich Village appealed to us and it did not disappoint. Lots of interest within -- minutes walk (eg Washington Square in the evening to listen to the impromtu music) and ease of access to the subway. We felt very safe and relaxed in the area. It was also a good base from which to head to all the major tourist sites.
The room itself was slightly small and modest although it was clean and well serviced every day. Being at the back of the building it was very quiet although a bit dark but no big deal as we were out all day. 
We knew when we booked that we would be sharing toilet and bathroom and would have access to a kitchen. We had no problem with the sharing aspect but what disappointed was the very poor facilites. The shower was over a small narrow bath but instead of the shower being at one end of the bath it was mounted on the wall halfway along the bath. This meant there was hardly any room to turn without catching against the plastic shower curtain. It was absolutely awful so that showers were taken quickly. 
If the bathroom was bad the kitchen was a total disaster area. It had a large fridge, cooker etc but no pots or pans, no cutlery, no plates or dishes ... but it had a table! However the whole area was grubby and very uninviting. We could therefore only use the fridge. We felt cheated as a result. 
As others have said the reception is uninviting and the staff there not very friendly. The corridors and upstairs layout is also not appealing although the decor seemed fresh and clean. Then there was the breakfast room downstairs which was pretty awful and the staff unfriendly. The continental breakfast was very meagre with little choice.
Having said all that, with a little effort like putting bombs under the bathroom and kitchen, smashing the glass wall in reception and sacking all the staff (apart from the cleaners) there could be a perfectly pleasant hotel in a nice part of the city.

This hotel is very centrally located; great restaurants and shopping around this area and you can walk to the museums.
This is more of a business-conference hotel so if you are looking for a nice atmosphere, you might want to look someplace else.
The service is excellent: the staff can give you great advice on sightseeing, restaurant, bars etc. and they really know these things.
Unfortunately the noise isolation is poor: I stayed in the -- floor and could hear the sirens during the nights. You can also hear noises from the corridor; the cleaning crew is eager to start cleaning early, so you can hear them knocking on doors around - o'clock. My advice: use earplugs.
The price for the room is quite high, and they still want to charge you extra for wifi. In my opinion, wifi should be free considering the price and that this is a business hotel.

Stayed here for the first time this week and really enjoyed it. It’s in a great location right in the middle of everything, and the rooms were very clean and comfortable w- comfy bed-duvet, and rooms w- views of St. Patrick’s and Rockefeller Plaza. 
What I especially liked is that in an expensive city, where some (already expensive) hotels continue to charge for every convenience and service, the Jewel has so many free amenities and services -- free purified water on each floor, free wi-fi, nice “living room” lobby for relaxing or working on -nd floor w- free coffee-tea in morning, newspapers, games and books; free computer printing, and even some chargers available for your phone(lots of different types), free fitness center (although I like to get my fitness from walking everywhere in NY), and even free access to the members-only Terrace Club - doors down (and --% discount there on food-non-alcholic beverages). 
It’s also very business-friendly (unlike some hotels, which can be dark, no desks), with plenty of lighting, and practical desks w- free wi-fi, outlets for your computer, phone, etc., and even free printing. It doesn’t have the “grand lobby w- restaurant-bar” or historic feel that I do sometimes like when I’m in New York, but it was perfect and convenient for this trip, and would absolutely return and recommend it.

This place is absolutely not worth the money. This hotel was chosen because of location and because we were told that they were comparable with the Hyatt across the river. The hotel is overpriced - this place should be about $---night at the most and that would be based on location only. The interior of the hotel is very dated and has that damp-old smell to it. There has been updates, but the money was not spent in the right place. The bathrooms are very old - the faucets leak, the drains are rusty and there are stains on the tubs and floors that will not come up no matter how much cleaning you do. The bedding is dingy and dated. The hotel does not tell you that you have to not only pay for parking, but you must have """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cash"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to pay for parking. It is not part of your hotel bill and the parking service is awful. The only good things I can say about this hotel is location and the front desk staff is very friendly.

I stayed three nights for a business trip. The hotel is upscale in atmosphere with professional staff. My suite was extremely comfortable with a convenient layout of the rooms. The breakfast buffet has a good variety, but the quality of the food is just so-so. I found lots of good restaurants near the South Park Mall, just a short drive away, and the hotel is convenient to the airport and major highways.
The biggest complaint was that the public areas were very cold. I visited during an unusually cold spell in Charlotte, and the central tower arrangement of the hotel meant that cold air was sucked in through the front doors and stayed in the lobby, bar and restaurant areas. I had to bundle up - literally - every time I went downstairs. The business center was an ice box. Several guests complained, but it was still unheated the entire time I was there.

Booked an executive terrace room. Large, great balcony with comfortable seating that wrapped around a corner. View was good of the Washington monument. Room was spacious and comfortable. Could have used another light in the sitting area. Bathroom was great, with a large shower. Bedroom was also very nice. Had room service and the food was very good and arrived on-time. Brought our own wine for dinner from a small shop on --th street. However, the wine list was not bad either. Exercise room was good, a few more pieces and a little more floor space than you see in a typical business hotel.
Other than the hotel amenities, it has a good location with easy walking to everything.
Overall, I would stay there again and I will recommend it to my friends.

Nice rooms and clean. Also great location beside Grand Central. However it is a very Big Hotel..almost impersonal. Gym is Ok - but not very big. Breakfast is also somewhat uncomfortable with waiters watching your plate constantly to see what you eat and whether you need to pay more! Staff could also be more helpful-genuine. I found some to be quite indifferent.
A higher end hotel but overpriced for what you get!

Stayed here for a convention at a reduced rate. Room had a high quality -- inch HD TV and was very comfortable. Excellent location close to Moscone convention center, restaurants, cable car, and shopping. I really enjoyed Yerba Buena Garden right next to it and the bar with a terrific view on the --th floor. My only complaint is that there are three sets of elevators going to different floors which was confusing for the first day or two. Guests have to transfer elevators to get from certain floors to other floors.

We stayed in this hotel for - nights in summer ----. When we arrived we got a room with a wet floor due to a malfunctioning airco system. Within a few minutes we got a new room and were upgraded to a larger room. Great service! We were planning to have breakfast outside on the street but a quick glance at the breakfast room made us decide to spend a comfortable hour enjoying breakfast at the hotel. The two days after we didn't even consider to go outside. Great breakfast and great service of the staff. And the old-style room makes you feel at home.

The foyer of this hotel is Amazing and should set you up for a fantastic stay. Unfortunately not. I imagine in its' hayday, this place was the best around. Unfortunately now though it's just mediocre.
It is very similar to nearly every hotel I have stayed in the US. That is the staff are sweet as pie when speaking to your directly, but you they really don't give a damn at the back of it and feel it is their job to give you the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""have a nice day"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" attitude.
The main issue I had with the hotel was the noise. Particularly coming from the internal plumbing. It sounded like it had its' own percussion band trapped inside it!
Would I reccommend this hotel? I wouldn't say don't go, but I would advise to see what else is available first.

I love the Valencia. It is in the heart of Santana Row with fabulous restaurants and shopping all within walking distance. The staff is welcoming and keep busy making guests happy. The valet service even runs to get your car if you fail to call the front desk to request it ahead of time. Any minor repair is instanly addressed - they leave the lights on so you know they were there. The front desk loaned me a charger for my phone after I forgot mine at home, so nice!
I never recieved turn down service - it is only upon request and I didn't ask for it. Things to be aware of: soaps are not replenished consistently. If you pay that much for a hotel and need the little shampoo bottles everyday, you may be disappointed (especially because they smell so good). Santana Row can be loud but all concerts, aerobics classes, and other events are over by -pm for a restful evening. The showers are melt-your-face hot, I love it but you may want to test the water before entering the bath. The pool, hot tub, fitness room, roof top views, and free wi-fi are wonderful - take advantage!
Tip well (--% +) and everyone on the Row remembers you. Amber India has great food and the server brings me my favorite glass of wine as soon as I arrive - even if it's been months between visits. Tha bartenders at Maggianno's make sure the Yankees are on for me even before I ask, again, with months in between visits. Peet's coffee has the greatest coffee in the world and they greet you by name on your second visit. I wish the shops in my home town were as great as they are on the Row. It's a great experience!
The service was great from start to finish! The rooms were clean, extremely comfortable, and I got an excellent night's sleep. I will definitely be back to stay in the future!

This hotel wasn't bad. What makes it is the location! I ran the Nike Women's Marathon and needed a hotel last minute. I couldn't have picked a better location. The hotel was a bit pricey for one night but I think it was because of the event and we were right in Union Square. The rooms are a bit small but we didn't mind since we were only there one night. If we were going to stay longer we would have picked a different room -- or a different hotel depending on the price. The only downside - parking! Parking was horribly expensive. With tax it came up to $---night. YIKES!
All in all, this was a charming hotel. I will probably stay here again with hopes of getting a bigger room.

The Roosevelt is an older hotel with updated rooms. Our room was comfortable with nice bedding. The bathrooms are small but serviceable. The lobby bar is wonderful with good food and friendly staff. The location is excellent with short walks to Times Square, -th ave shops and attractions and restaurents.

It was the perfect spot in uptown. walking distance to everything.
loved the modern lobby and bar and pool table!
Fun, funky atmosphere.
Incredible service and stunning views of the lower Hudson River....

I'm a seasoned Hilton property traveler and have stayed at many of their proporties across the country. I have yet to receive the service and hospitality like I did at the San Diego Mission Valley Hilton. From the valets, to the front desk, to the servers at the restaurant, and even the bartender. This place has its act together in every sense. I have never felt more welcome or appreciated to be a customer. 
The food at the restaurant was outstanding. My evening meals were perfectly prepared and tasted wonderful. The breakfast buffet had everything you could want. They would even prepare eggs to your liking if you prefered. 
If you're ready for a beautifully renovated Hilton and service at every corner, I highly recommend you give this place some consideration.
Free WiFi didn't hurt either.

My daughter went to George Washington University and this was my place to stay whenever I visited her. It's wonderful to have breakfast included and a happy hour in the early evening. The rooms are spacious and the lobby area is pretty. Located not far from a Metro stop so it's easy to get around to see the sites of this great city.

Enjoyed our stay at Morgans and concur with many of the other reviews. But really need to point out the bathrooms are incredibly small. The shower is a pretty much a carved out section from the rest of the floor (with a glass door), the sink is approx - inch from the shower and the toilet is less than a foot from the sink. In terms of depth, let's just say it isn't much better. Other than that, we really enjoyed our stay and the room itself.

I stayed at the Hard Rock for - days and have to say the hotel is nice and has a cool look to it. But like so many people have said it does indeed have dimly lit rooms and equally dim hallways. But as two brothers on a trip to see Chicago it did not bother us. I can see how it would bother a woman trying to do her make up since it is darker than the usual hotel room. The beds were comfortable and the room was clean. Good view of the marina city buildings (aka the corn on the cob twin buildings) from room ---. It is located in a nice area of downtown Chicago with Millennium Park just - minutes away and close to many boat tours on Wacker Drive. We were granted a late check out (-pm instead of noon) so that was nice for us since our flight was not until -pm. The W has become my favorite hotel in San Diego. I am in SPG guy when I travel for business but otherwise I will stay anywhere. We just got back from a week in San Francisco and had a wonderful time despite the cool weather. The Radisson, Fisherman's Wharf is an excellent value. If you're looking for 'touristy' then this is perfect. It's located right in the middle of the Fisherman's Wharf area. If you want to go on a city tour the departure point is right across the street. If you want to go to Alcatraz you only have to walk about --- yards. The Radisson isn't fancy but the rooms are clean and the staff is exceptionally friendly. Try to get a bay view room on an upper floor if possible. The noise from the street at the front of the hotel is significant especially when a bus pulls up and idles while letting passengers on and off. We know, we had one, we asked to be moved and were.
Lots of reviewers have raved about the beds. They are air beds which you can inflate or deflate to your personal comfort. They do take a little getting used to though. Your first night might not be great.
There's no restaurant or dining room in the hotel but there is lots of food within a short walk. The concierge at the hotel is very friendly and knowledgeable when it comes to booking tours or any other need that you may have.
As this isn't intended to be a travelogue on San Fran but a review of the Radisson all I would like to say about SF is that a tour of the city is a great way to start, the trip to Alcatraz is very worthwhile and if you're going to be in town for a few days and will be relying of public transit, buy a - day pass for the MUNI system. The pass covers everything - cable cars (which are $- per ride if you pay the single fare), the F-line, buses and subway. It's worth the $-- for the three day pass.
I'd like to thank all the other Tripadvisor[-] reviewers who posted their remarks which greatly helped me decide on the Radisson Fisherman's Wharf. I'll happily receive and respond to emails inquiring about specific topics.

 The heating system is strange. We like to sleep in a cold room, but could not adjust the temperature and did not have time to ask staff to help. We did request someone to fix the commode which was broken before we took the room. They sent someone, and called to check that it'd been fixed. 
 To note: We made our arrangements on a reservation service, not through the hotel. Nevertheless they treated us like Hilton Honors customers (which we are; but not on this trip!)

Wouldn't stay again unless you've arrived in the area late and want to just put your head down.

The vallet parking is nice - our car was whisked away upon checkin and brought back to us when we checked out the next morning - no need to worry about parking downtown or theft or vandalism. Ruth's Chris Steakhouse in the hotel was nice for visiting with friends in the lounge area. We didn't eat there, just had drinks. There is a Starbuck's in the hotel too, so that's nice for breakfast! The hotel was very clean and we would stay here again. after checking in found hairs all over the turned down sheets- was dismissed as a demanding guest- what a horrifing experience- STAY AWAY

We stayed three nights at the Hollywood Celebrity Hotel in Hollywood in October ----.
Neighborhood

In the same street (more like an alley) there are two other cheap hotels, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Hollywood Orchid Suites"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Liberty Hotel"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""".

Room
The room was large, with a big bed, a sofa and a table. The furniture isn't exactly new, but the bed was comfortable and the sheets were clean. The decor is a bit dated, but since we didn't go to Hollywood to stay in our room, that didn't bother us. There was a fridge and a microwave in the room as well.
Bathroom
The bathroom was nice, with black and white tiles, a tub, a toilet and a sink. Clean and practical. The shower cabinet was a bit hard to close, otherwise ok.
Service
The breakfast included consists of juice, bagels and muffins. Not a full buffet, but a quick bite before you start your day. It was nice to sit out on the patio and sip juice in the shadow of the Kodak Theater. There is a computer in the lobby where you can surf the interenet for free.
Summary
This is a clean hotel with a nice decor. It's comfortable, clean and reasonably priced for LA. We can recommend this hotel for people who plan to spend most of their day out sightseeing or whatever and not hanging out in their room.

After I'd given up on getting into the room we had originally booked, I had to go downstairs because no one was answering at the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""customer service"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" phone. I love this hotel. It is just a few blocks from sixth street. The decor - quality of the rooms is excellent. The staff was very helpful. Couldn't have asked for more. Booked through Priceline and got a really good rate, so the value couldn't be beat!!!

Excellent hotel, can't get any better! A little expensive but it was worth it. The service was awesome. Location is perfect (just a few blocks away from downtown, chinatown, besides a cable car stop). Luxury is found all around the hotel, installations are awesome. I I travle often for business trips and have had the opportunity to stay at several outstanding resorts. When I recieved the info regarding this conference, I was excited to take my family along from everything we saw on website. Unfortunately, our room was the most damp and musty room I've ever stayed in. The air conditioner didn't really work too well, but the smell was almost moldy smelling. The bathroom floor was a bit dirty on arrival and the walls weren't all that clean. The location was great for Sea World, but other than that, cab fare will drive you crazy at this place. There is really nowhere close to the resort as far as local attractions and restaurants. On the flip side, the onsite restaurants served really good food. The bell hops are extremely friendly until you decide to walk to your room. Then the attitude begins. Also, beware on taking their recommendations on cabs. We took their """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""preferred"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" vender and later found out by hailing our own cab, that we were being overcharged compared to the local yellowcab. If you are looking for a place to just hang out and enjoy the resort, you could probably get it, as others at the conference were very happy with their rooms, but make sure you get an updated room. Afterall, it's San Diego, and there's not much bad you can say about that. Be sure to count on a $-- cab fare to anywhere from the resort.

We hosted our -rd Annual Conference with --- attendees at the MCM Elegante. Everyone from the General Manager on down were aligned to accomplish our event with excellence and affordability. This facility is the ONLY hotel that has complimentary shuttle service to both Dallas airports, which is a huge advantage for keeping ground transportation costs to a minimum for attendees. The full breakfast was marvelous each day (included in room rate) and the catering staff met our expectations in food selection and service with a smile.

The James was a random spur of the moment choice for us but it turned out to be great....it's all very new and rooms are incredibly spacious. Super comfy bed's too. Nice big tv's,ipod docks and other cool stuff.
The proximity to the mag mile is great too...all the shopping you can dream of only a block away!
We got a fairly good rate but i've noticed the rates lately seem a little excessive....for us the best part of the hotel is def Primehouse! and being able to get david burke room service!
Even if you never choose to stay at the James make sure you go to dinner there..it is absolute perfection.I was eating there just a month ago and noticed they had a great sunday roast family style special too.
Had a manicure at the hotel salon which was pretty average. Lovely girl though.We have since found better located (for us) places to stay in chicago but I wouldn't hesitate to stay at the James again!

We stayed here for one night. Our room definitely showed some wear and tear and smelled funny. The refrigerator looked like it was from the ----s. Our air conditioning in the living area of the suite was not cooling sufficiently. This hotel just did not have a luxury feel. The pool area was nice and my children enjoyed it. My husband enjoyed the fitness center, however we were surprised to find a ten dollar charge on our bill the next day. I found that to be ridiculous. That is an amenity that should be included with the resort. I have stayed at their sister property, Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak and it is much better than this one!

Great overall stay. Staff was very personable and hospitable. They were aware that it was my birthday and sent complimentary champagne and strawberries to my room. I will definitely return there and would recommend it to anyone visiting San Francisco.

We recently stayed at this Holiday Inn and for visiting the historic area the location can not be beat. As stated parking is reasonable and check in was very smooth. We did have issues and to the staffs credit they tried to make it better. Due to a leak in our first room's bathroom we were moved to another room an a different floor. We returned late at night only to have the bathroom above us have a major water drain break which sent quite a bit of water down on us. The staff moved us to a king room on the top floor which was much nicer than our original rooms. We also received a free breakfast in the restaurant and they gave us enough points for a free nights stay, which seemed very fair to us. Things do happen and they were very quick on making it better. As some have stated the only major complaint was with the heating-ac unit. It was very noisy and there was only a few setting so either we were too hot or too cold. I did suggest to them that they need new units. We thought all three of the rooms we had were clean and didnt notice any problems other than the first two were on the small side. Would have no problem staying here again

On a recent business trip to Autin, I had my choice of staying at another local Hotel or at the Hampton Inn-Arboretum. When I called the other Hotel they were going to charge me the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""week-end"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" although I wasn't showing up at the Hotel on Sunday until later in the evening. They had a coffee """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""buffet"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that looked very appetizing. I dont drink coffee but it was so impressive, I did my entire stay! The staff was very friendly and accomodating. My room was very clean and comfortable.
