Oh and by-the-way....the complimentary breakfast was amazing. Very well put together. I'm all about presentation. And the food was good too!!!!

I got this hotel on Priceline's Name Your Own Price. I just needed a basic hotel to stay overnight for an early morning flight out of Hobby Airport. I was VERY impressed with this hotel and will certainly be back everytime I fly out of Hobby. I could not have found a better hotel at a better price! This hotel is new and still smelled like fresh paint and new carpet. The lobby-front desk area was decorated with modern, tasteful furniture. The staff was friendly & efficient. The rooms were also well-decorated and modern. (For example, the bathroom counter looked like a piece of furniture, not a standard issue hotel sink.) The beds were very tall, plush & comfy, with - pillows per bed. The free bottled water in the room was a nice perk. And the hotel is ---% smoke-free which is a huge plus in my book!

I recently stayed here the weekend of the Penn Relays..... The staff were very helpful and pleasant. Check-in was super fast and the lobby was very nice... The rooms were very clean the sink was seperate from the toilet and shower... Once we sat on the beds we almost fell asleep instantly... So Soft So Comfy!!! I love that there was a Starbucks in the lobby, Dunkin Donuts next door and a -- hour -Eleven across the street.... Now for the negatives... Valet parking was extremely expensive (the attendants were great though) $-- total... The shower pressure was very weak and the toilet was stopped up on the morning we were checking out.... Other than that the hotel was pretty good......

I have nothing but good things to say about this hotel. It is beautifully decorated. Very new. Very clean. Excellent service. Big rooms. Big bathroom. Close to the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""People Mover"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" that can get you anywhere downtown for -- cents. Just a wonderful stay!!!

This Courtyard by Marriott is right across the street from Lake Union with great views of the lake and beyond. Watch the seaplanes land and take off from the lake constantly. Lots of great restaurants nearby and it's a short walk to Space Needle. Had a great stay here.

My son and I stayed at this Hilton Garden Inn while visiting the University of North Florida. The hotel was immaculate and pleasant. I wanted to be sure that we were staying in a safe area and that it would be close to the college. Both were true. I read one review that said the beds were not comfortable. It was correct. The bedding was fluffy, but the mattress felt like a board with foam on top- no spring. Also, be careful when comparing prices since the breakfast buffet was not included. All in all, though, I would stay here again. The hotel was top notch and it was close to everything and anything we needed.

Having recently returned from our first trip to NYC, it is easy to say that our stay at Hotel Elysee was as impressive as any landmark and as fabulous as any Broadway play. Our amenities and accomodations were bountiful and very tasteful. The free morning breakfast met every expectation with a wide variety of morning drinks, fresh fruit, delectable pastries and the oft-missing proteins in addition to the endless supply of morning newspapers, including The New York Times and USA Today. We were most impressed with the accomodating and knowledgable staff who greeted us by name and made sure we had point-precise directions for every outing. The recommendations for restaurants and shows were superb in every way. It would not be fair to review this uniquely personable hotel without noting the daily wines. champagne and cheeses et al served gratis each day. It was the ultimate in Old World elegance and personality. Without a doubt, we were extremely well taken care of and will return to Hotel Elysee as many times as we return to New York; can't wait for the next visit there!

We take monthly weekend trips to SF to escape the Central California heat in the summer, and thought we knew most of the hotels in the Union Square area, but had walked by the Fusion before (we've stayed at the Monticello Inn across the street) without ever noticing it (until this time, when we saw the big sign outside - duh !) We booked it due to their low rates compared to the competition for a Friday night stay, and we were very pleased at how well the building had been renovated - literally everying was in near-brand new condition, and in great shape, from the lobby, to the elevator (there are still a lot of old ones in many of the smaller budget SF hotels), to all the carpeting, windows (which actually open easily), to the furnishings, including a nice wide flat screen tv. Our only minor complaints were that the room was on the small side, as are most SF boutique hotels, the sink is not in the bathroom, but outside it, and we got a full size bed (for - of us), where we'd rather have had at least a queen, and the parking was not very convenient (the valet parking was $--, which we though was too high, so we ended up parking at the Union Square garage and paid about the same - duh on us again - ). The staff was very friendly, and the location is great - just a block from the cable cars, and three blocks from Union Square, and it's a safe area to be in at night. We'd definately stay here again, and would recommend it to singles or couples (but not to families, due to the smaller size rooms).

We recently stayed at the Columbus Hyatt Regency for a conference. Our group of four has traveled together before, and for convenience, we book one room with two double (usually, sometimes queen) beds. Normally we have plenty of space, but this rooms was a bit small to accommodate four adult women. Only two drawers were available, with one drawer occupied by the keyboard that accompanied the television. Shelves in the bathroom and in the initial entry were nice (under the coffeemaker), as were the mirrors. However, the closet was small. Overall, the room we occupied would better accommodate one or two travelers, not four. 
Water pressure in the shower was minimal, and we all encountered difficulty turning off the water in the tub (which I should have mentioned to the employees so they could fix it--they may not be aware it needs repair). 
The employees were very helpful, especially with giving us directions and suggestions on where to go and how to navigate there. They were always pleasant and cheerful. 
While I didn't use the recreation center, one of our group did and said it was fantastic. The pool was small, but it looked very clean and well-maintained. 
I do have to admit that this location was noisy. Street noise, which the hotel cannot control, was loud (lots of sirens this last week!), and we heard the elevators rumble....all night long. These things happen in hotels, and I'm not about to give up my elevator ride and climb the stairs with my luggage, but I do wish the elevators were quieter. 
Valet parking was very convenient, and the employees helped us with our luggage.

The rooms are really amazing, we got upgraded to a suite because we are gold members for Priority Points Club. We had a kitchen, living room, huge bedroom and amazing bath. All was great. The bar-restaurant downstairs has a great atmosphere and if you go, ask for 'Rocket' to serve you, the guy is funny and super friendly. Good times.

I love coming to visit La Jolla, especially when I get this hotel for a great deal on Priceline. I felt that the room was 'okay' perhaps since I booked on Priceline that maybe I got a room that had a few minor issues that I'm not going to really even mention. They do have valet ($---day) and self parking ($---day) but there is plenty of on street parking that is pretty safe, but I would always use common sense. I signed up to be a Hyatt Gold Passport member which I would recommend if you end up getting this room through a site like Priceline-Hotwire. Perks like late check out at -pm. Also, the pool looked nice but didn't use it. Wish there was free wifi.

My husband and I went to New York last month for the very first time. We booked our trip on Expedia and were so excited to stay at the Waldorf since it's such a landmark hotel. After reading some mixed reviews on tripadvisor, I emailed the concierge to ask if my husband and I could be upgraded to a recently renovated room during our stay. I got a prompt email from the head of guest services indicating that he put our request through. We were not disappointed when we checked into our room. Our room was lovely, w-a flat screen t.v., king sized bed, - windows (one facing Park Ave.), nice black & white tiled marble and new fixtures, etc. But the room was just the beginning of our wonderful stay there. From the moment we checked in to the moment we left, the service from everyone from the reception, bell desk, doormen, maids, to every other W=A staff person we encountered was impeccable. Which was very impressive considering that we are in no way people of elite status or means. Everyone is (I hope) treated with equal amount of respect and quality service. Wonderful experience.

I took my wife to Denver for a “babymoon” and a chance to relax for a few days. I decided to stay at the Hotel Monaco Denver after a perfect experience with the Hotel Monaco Chicago last year. I debated staying at the JW Marriott in Cherry Creek, but ultimately was persuaded by a rate which included a continental breakfast (more on that later) and the special attention we had received at Monaco before. In short, at the Hotel Monaco in Chicago, we were overwhelmed by the service and attention to detail, which surpassed what we were used to—and that experience persuaded me to stay at the Monaco in Denver.
We arrived at ---- and were allowed to check in early, which was a plus, but we weren’t welcomed as InTouch Members. Looking back, it was strange that we encountered no doorman, no bellhop, no concierge, and only once receptionist. We were given a room next to the exercise room, which was convenient for us as fitness freaks, but not so great in that when someone is on the treadmill, the room shook, or when someone dropped weights--it was loud and felt like a construction site, which isn’t so nice at -:-- in the morning. By the way, the exercise room is adequate for maintaining fitness with a treadmill, two precor ellipticals, an exercise bike, and some dumbbells (only up to --#). Our room was nice, but not as nice as a similar king room we stayed at Monaco Chicago. There was no flat panel LCD TV and no lounging chair, and the closet was cramped. The bathroom was nice, but not over the top--aside from a granite countertop, it was average. The shower was a bath-shower combo, was not overly large, and the shower head was not very powerful. The only thing that set the room apart from a Marriott room was the tall (~---foot) ceilings. We did receive two water bottles and a (very) small bowl of trail mix from the manager. Oddly, the bedding was very thin and there was no blanket. That night, it took several calls to the front desk before someone answered, but a blanket was promptly delivered. We did enjoy the wine hour, and the people serving the wine were the friendliest we encountered in - days at the hotel. The wine hour is a definite plus and is a great event; they even had a Wii set up. However, the guests didn't seem as into the event as they did when we were in Chicago. In Chicago, there was several hotel staff interacting with the guests, whereas here, there was not.
The next morning, we went to the hotel restaurant, Panzano for our free continental breakfast. The restaurant is nice and the staff was friendly and attentive. Immediately, we noticed that the continental breakfast was the most expensive item on the menu ($--.--). We were disappointed when we got one pastry (cinnamon roll--tasty, scone, or muffin) and a SMALL plate of fruit. The plate of fruit included about - blueberries, and a half slice of cantaloupe, honeydew, watermelon, and pineapple. Needless to say, the portion sizes were disappointing. I wouldn't spend the money on this breakfast when eggs benedict or other similar breakfasts are $--.-- or under. The next day, we asked if we could have a cheaper item on the menu--they allowed my wife to have the oatmeal (~$-)--it was good, but a small bowl of oatmeal; I was not allowed to get the eggs benedict, but I did get a free serving of bacon ($-.--). My cinnamon roll, while delicious, was cold. In retrospect, I would rather have had a cheaper rate and gone to a nearby Corner Bakery for breakfast....the free continental breakfast (which really isn't free) was underwhelming.
The hotel has a good location and is located one block off of the --th street Mall. We easily walked all over downtown, and the free RTD Mall shuttle is a great convenience.
My wife had a prenatal massage at the Renaissance Spa in the hotel. She was happy with the massage ($-- for -- minutes) and had a great experience. She said the spa was nice. I found out later that the spa has a “happy hour”—from Monday through Wednesday, spa services are --% off from ---- and ---. Being a thrifty person, that would have been good to know. 
Lastly, when we received our bill, we were charged for valet parking which we did not use. Lori, the manager, did fix the bill. Another disappointment was that the business center was not free to use (the first -- minutes are) and it is $.-- to print each black and white page. Lesser quality hotels I have stayed in (Courtyard, Fairfield Inn) have free business centers with free printing. This seemed rather cheap to me, especially when the Hotel Monaco is not a cheap place to stay.
All in all the stay reminded me of a stay at a Marriott--a nice hotel, adequate service, but nothing special. It wasn't until the last day of our stay that a doorman actually opened the front door for us. I never saw a concierge at the concierge desk, and there was always a noticeable lack of personnel in the reception area. To compare, in Chicago, you could not get near the front door before someone opened it for you and there was always at least - people at the front desk and a concierge. Another disappointment was we rented a car to take a day trip, and when I pulled in front of the hotel to pick up my wife--the valet asked me to move the car, even after I explained I was a hotel guest there to pick up my pregnant wife. Also, we never received our goldfish, which while not a crushing blow to our stay, was strange. In Chicago, they turned down our beds at night and left mints, but that never happened here.
To sum, the hotel is perfectly nice, and in any other circumstance, I would consider this a great stay, but my prior experience with the Hotel Monaco Chicago had me expecting extraordinary quality in the hotel, a higher level of service, and a more friendly, welcoming environment. For the price ($---), I expected the room to be a little nicer, more attention from the staff and a very high level of overall hotel quality. There seemed to be a shortage of staff, and no one (except the server at the wine hour) was overly friendly. You might ask “why didn’t you complain?” First, we are not ones to complain unless something is seriously wrong. Second, no one ever called us or stopped us to ask how our stay was. If they had, I would have told them about my disappointments. (Once again, at the Hotel Monaco Chicago, someone called the first night to make sure our room was satisfactory and we were happy). For a hotel that touts itself as a Top --- World Hotel, the stay was nothing special. I want to be clear, this is a nice hotel, and if you are used to staying at large chain hotels (Marriott, Omni, Westin, etc) you won’t be disappointed and won’t notice any difference in quality. However, if you have stayed in a Kimpton Hotel before, you have certain expectations of quality and service, and at the Hotel Monaco Denver for this stay, those expectations were not met.

If you're looking for a spacious room for a girls' getaway weekend, this is it. Two comfortable queen size beds, if you don't mind sharing. The sofa bed in the sitting room is not so good for older gals' backs. Two sinks on the vanity and one on the wet bar provided each person her own space. Situated right in the heart of things. Memorable!

We stayed at the Westin LAX during a business conference. The daily rate was very affordable for two ($-- each) and the room was very spacious and well equipped. There are affordable restaurants within walking distance for meals if you decide not to eat at the hotel restaurants (which seemed expensive to us since we are small eaters). The beds were EXTREMELY comfortable and my traveling companion who says she is never able to sleep at night peacefully was sleeping like a baby. We had a glitch with something we had pre-ordered to be put in our room, and the staff bent over backwards to find a solution for us until they could fix the problem. They were very concerned and took full responsibility for the mistake. The parking was convenient and very affordable.

i stayed in the comfort inn for - nights --th---th april staff were great rooms cleaned and fresh towels every day close to everything just a few minutes to times square would deff stay here again would recommend to anyone looking for a clean comfortable hotel in the centre of new york

When we stay in NYC we generally choose the Upper East Side, as we have a CKCS and need to be near the park. This hotel meets all our criteria for the perfect city hotel--there is a warm and gracious staff who can get you excellent restaurant recommendations, a 'boutique-hotel' like feel so you are not just one in a sea of thousands of rooms, and elegant accommodations with QUIET rooms! The Surrey met all these expectations and even delivered more.
Notable positives:
-Front desk, Concierge (Michael) and door staff--all outstanding. Yes, Christopher--we will be back! Hailing a taxi was no problem as well. Any requests we had were met with gracious aplomb. 
-We were offered free bottled water as soon as we arrived which was a nice touch for a day of sightseeing.
-The rooms and decor are strikingly gorgeous in a 'beau-nouveau' style, with some modern art added in. The rooms aren't huge, but this IS NYC, and the arrangement gives you a good-sized sitting area, a large bed, and a fantastic shower! 
-The shower is fantastic. You know those rain head showers never seem to have enough water pressure. This was the perfect combination of great water pressure and relaxing rainhead shower so you can get de-grimified after a long day of walking.
-The proximity to the Park, Barney's-Bergdorf's, and Museum mile cannot be beat. I challenge anyone to stay in Times Square after they've stayed in this peaceful respite and not choose this side of town again. After all, there are taxis and the subway if you want to get downtown.
-The rooftop garden is a must. It's gorgeous at night for drinks. (try the #-- gin cocktail!)
-Along Lexington there are good breakfast options for a cheap bite on the way to the Met, or you can avail yourself of Boulud cuisine in your room or in the rooftop garden. Also, a great little Italian place (Via quadronno) serves a great morning cappuccino (at --rd).
-The room was quiet, quiet, quiet. I cannot stress how important this was for me as I'm a light sleeper. So wonderful!
You don't need to debate about here or the Carlyle down the street--stay here!
The only thing I wish I would have tried was the spa, but the Guggenheim, Met, Moma were all too close not to take advantage of. I hope to try the spa next time. 
We really enjoyed our stay. We will be back!

Great boutique hotel in NYC! Wonderful staff who were very friendly and helped with every request. The rooms are small, but why are you coming to NYC if you are planning to hang out in your room? They were very clean, well designed, and comfortable. The restaurant downstairs serves breakfast, they only have three choices, but all are very well prepared and delicious. There is a Starbucks right next door if you want to pick up something like a pastry for breakfast instead. I thought it was an amazing hotel and will definitely be staying there again when I return to NYC.

Room was damp smelling, airconditioner was noisy and dripping. The fridge looked like it had been salvaged from the local rubbish tip. On our first night, we saw security officers patrolling the corridors and saw Police Officers at one room. Breakfast was awful with no cereal for our children apart from bran flakes ... that was the ONLY cereal they had. From a hotel chain like the Ramada, you expect more. We had been travelling across America on Route -- staying mostly in Best Westerns and only booked this hotel as we couldn't get a Best Western. The rate was pricey for what we got. Breakfast restaurant was hotel prices for awful food, our waffles were rock hard. Probably re-heated. We would have been better going to Dennys. There appeared to be some unsavoury people hanging around the corridors and we got the impression that some people were living there. Final straw came when we were waiting with our daughters a the lift when a -'-"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" man, dressed as a woman in an emerald green cat suit got out of the lift with what appeared to be a runner for a TV company. As they walked away, the whole back side of his pants were cut out revealing all. Not the sort of thing you want your children to see in a hotel lobby. Maybe they were filming an episode for Jerry Springer? Staff were unhelpful and churlish. Don't stay here .. try a Best Western!

We arrived and they sent us to another hotel for one night due to a reservation error from their part. So that was an inconvenience. When we finally got back to the hotel, I have to say they gave us a very pretty room on the top floor with a great view. So that together with the fact that the location of the hotel is amazing, our stay was great. However my boyfriend found a flee and for those who don't like loud music, make sure to ask for a room above the fifth floor to make sure you don't suffer with the bar music.

I Pricelined this hotel, and I know we all worry that our four-star hotel will not be four stars. This one was. I did read some complaints about odd things that happend to a few visitors. I had no such bad luck.
Beautiful, historic hotel right on the park, about five minutes from the Art Institute of Chicago. Granted, it is on the far south end of the park, and most of the action has drifted north. But if you like to walk or take mass transit, this is not much of a problem. It's a straight shot.
I did not love Maracat, the restaurant. Seems like it was stuck in the --s.
The reason I'm rating it as Excellent is based partially on value. You've probably stayed at nicer places, but not at this price in Chicago.

I have stayed at the Dallas Palomar for multiple trips now, and I am impressed every time. The rooms are average sized, but they are always spotless and have everything you need. The staff is extremely friendly and accomodating, and the nightly wine hour from --- is great! The pool area is great with comfortable chairs and great bar service! The location is great. My wife and I stayed here over New Years and though we loved the decor and bones of the hotel, it severely lacked on many levels.
From the moment we checked in, our bathroom had not been cleaned, the phones weren't working properly, housekeeping never showed after - requests, and generally, the staff seemed unqualified. Stayed here for - nights before moving onto NY. The hotel was great, very modern, clean, fresh and very friendly staff. Had a great view from the Hotel room and were very close to local transport links! The Breakfast in the hotel restaurant was nice however I would avoid the maple sausages and bacon, pretty disgusting although seemed popular with others! However we had breakfast in the Hotel's Starbucks which worked out much better on a morning. The TV's in the room were a very good size, the bathroom was spacious and clean, the beds were very comfy and I had no problem sleeping in it and it was all very clean. All in all I would recommend this hotel to anyone going to Boston, good restaurants nearby, in particular the legal test kitchen next door and the Ben and Jerry's stand over the road is great too, great facilities in the hotel, good transport nearby, and very friendly staff!

Excellent reception on arrival, clean large room with king size bedm good sized TV, air conditioning, fridge, freezer plus microwave and basic cooking facilities. Excellent bath and shower facility. Low cost with no frills but very helpful staff. Basic breakfast available, laundry, fitness suite and swimming pool. Free Internet access enabled me to check out tours, pubs and keep in touch with home. My only criticism would be no close bus stop to hotel. Excellent taxi service and plenty of take-out delivery available. I came over for Denvers first international Rugby tournament and would hope to come again next year

I cannot say too many wonderful things about this hotel! First of all, they were so accommodating that it's hard to believe that sort of service still exists. We were there hiking the Grand Canyon Rim to Rim and really needed a little TLC before and after the hike. NO WORRIES. Joel and Nikki took great care of us! We got express breakfast to take with us at -a the next morning (upon check in). They shuttled us from the hotel to downtown Tempe twice and with PLEASURE. They loaded our bags in the shuttle and MET us in Tempe to take us to the airport. WONDERFUL!
Everyone we encountered was just lovely. The rooms were clean and well appointed and the staff cannot be beat. Stay here, you will not regret it! Only downside was not being near any really healthy food BUT you can take the shuttle into Tempe and find anything you'd like to eat or drink. So problem solved!

I did stay three times in the Highland Garden during my travels to CA drom ---- to ---- and always loved the place. They had very decent prices considering the really good location only a - minute walk away from """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Mans Chinese Theater"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" on sunset and the decent rooms.
The hotel has a very unique, for me typical american charm and the interior, which may look somewaht outdated to some people, adds to the overall, typical LA charm of the place
I highly recommend the place for anyone who would like to get started somewhere close to hollywood, sunset and the cinemas-walk of fame in Los Angeles!
cheers,
 Ray

This hotel is located in a Northeast area outside of the city. If you need to be near the University of Charlotte then this is a really great spot to be. There are lots of stores, a lot of restaurant choices, etc. Very convenient. Our rooms were clean and neat. Staff was very nice. Outdoor pool was not open yet (boo hoo). We were there on Easter Sunday so we were a little rushed for breakfast because we had to get out of there by a certain time so they could start their Easter Brunch menu. 
We had dinner at a mexican place in the mall area near the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lake"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". For a few bucks you could rent a paddle boat and paddle around the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""lake"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". It was fun with my -- year old. Something to pass the time. 
If you need to be near the airport, then this is not the hotel for you. It's a good hike to the airport (especially for an early morning flight).

Stayed here with my girlfriend after our flight was cancelled and the airline put us up. I was at the hotel for about - hours and it was better than sleeping inside the airport. Still, like most of the reviews, the hotel needs upgrading including room furniture (just old), TV (worst picture ever - is this ----, get some $--- LCDs in there) and carpet (dirty and disgusting - considered not walking around without shoes).

Booked a two bed suite via Expedia but once we got there we had just a large single room. Re-read the Expedia small print which says something like they can't actually guarantee that what you book is what you'll get (?!) but tried it on with the reception people anyway. We were given a two bedroom suite but had to pay --% extra which, as we were staying for - nights, was worth it to me although I would have appreciated a little more leeway. I gathered that a lot of people were weekend visitors and would have thought we could have been bumped up a lot more than we were. We got a view of a brick wall but hadn't exactly come to New York to stay in the hotel room. Food in house far too pricey to attempt but the hotel has a nice ambience and very friendly staff. Even though it is a very grand hotel you don't feel overwhelmed by any grandeur - it has an informal feel. The location opposite Central Park can't be bettered and it is well within easy walking distance of most of NY's main sights. We were first time visitors to NY and had the holiday of a lifetime. We merely slept at the Essex House Hotel and there will undoubtably be cheaper, just as practical, hotels. But I would recommend it - it's clean, warm. safe, unstuffy, perfectly located and rather splendid.

The hotel itself is super modern in its decor and atmosphere. The staff were extremely helpful and friendly from the moment I walked in. The room was small, similar to European hotels, but this was not a bad thing as I didn't need much room. I forgot to bring a jacket back with me when I left and the staff were extremely helpful and were able to mail it to me within the day. Lastly, the location was fantastic, right next to Chinatown in downtown. Overall a really solid hotel.

I chose this hotel because a) friends recommended it, b) its ideal location close to numerous restaurants, the metro and various museums (including the National Geographic, all within walking distance) and c) its boutique-like atmosphere. The staff greeted us warmly upon arrival ensuring at all times that our needs were met. While its restaurant offered a most appealing menu in a trendy setting, my ---yr old preferred a more casual atmosphere (read: burger and fries) which were plentiful in the neighborhood. Same with breakfast. I would highly recommend this hotel for families and couples alike as its lounge bar is seemingly popular amongst the locals as well as hotel guests.

This hotel was base for our Girl Scout troop's long weekend visit to San Antonio-Sea World. What a perfect place! Our --bedroom suite was exactly the right size for our - person group, very roomy and comfortable. Three TVs and two bathrooms with - teenage girls were appreciated luxuries we can't usually afford! The girls loved the breakfast, (make your own waffels are always a hit!) as well as the selection of fruit, cereal, yogurt and oatmeal (with toppings), eggs and sausage. They also liked the BridgeMart store for small snacks before bed.
The hotel and grounds were exceptionally clean and the staff was extremely friendly and helpful. Easy access to the freeway, plenty of restaurants, gas stations and even an HEB grocery store nearby. Easy drive to downtown-Riverwalk and close to Six Flags Fiesta Texas. A little farther to Sea World but not a bad drive on the weekend.
Stay here and you will be back again and again!

I recently had the pleasure of spending - nights in this location, and again it was a great experience. The room we had faced the front of the building and it was quiet, very clean, linens comfortable and immaculate, towels quite new and fluffy. I enjoyed the bottle of wine that comes with the room. The gym is spacious and has great equipment, and their complimentary breakfast is outstanding. Aside from the great location, the hotel staff went out of their way to help me have and find a great time in Baltimore.

I stayed at this hotel on Thursday night -------. It was nothing spectacular. I was accompanied by my step daughter, granddaughter, and - small dogs. When I returned on the following Sunday night with my wife and no dogs I attempted to check in to said hotel. We had a reservation. We told the clerk that the dogs were not with us anymore.
