My husband and I were recently in San Jose for business and stayed at the Summerfield Suites in San Jose. We had a very pleasant stay at the hotel and they offered a delicious variety of breakfast every morning. 
The rooms were very spacious, clean and comfortable. The only problem we encountered was that our room was on the ground floor and we heard kids running up and down the stairs and in their rooms during the night. However, once call to the front desk took care of the problem immediately. Although we spent the majority of our time in San Francisco, the drive back to the hotel was worth it.

A bit pricey, but if you're looking for quality lodging in Manhattan this is a very good option. We stayed tree nights in a salon with king size bed. The bed was indeed king size and very comfortable. We got an early check in which was a delight and I want to give an extra appreciation to the bell guys down in the lobby who are among the quickest and most service minded I've met so far in all hotels I've stayed in.
Has a spa, business center, fitness center and a nice roof top bar that get's busy after work hours.

The staff was terrific. Our travel agent let us down, but Cris made sure we were got a room...and an upgrade. The room was comfortable, clean and quiet. The location of the doors with each other and the furniture in our suite was a bit bothersome, but for a - night stay we dealt with it. The central location was great for walking all around Manhattan. Room service was good, did not try restaurant-bar.

My daughters and I stayed at this lovely hotel over the past weekend. We felt welcome from the moment we pulled up. Each and every staff person we encountered was friendly and helpful.
We had two rooms. The beds were very comfortable, with good mattresses and nice linens. Everything was clean and the bathrooms were immaculate. Several of us commented that we could stay in the showers all day. Each room has a gas fireplace and it came in handy after we were caught in a drenching rain.
We had drinks and dessert in the hotel's restaurant, Moooo. The cheesecake and butterscotch parfait were out of this world. I would definitely return to try out the restaurant for dinner.
XV Beacon is a hotel that I would not hesitate to recommend to family and friends.

Stayed at The Maxwell for two evening while visiting in Seattle. It was one of the nicest hotels I've had the pleasure staying in. It was comfortable, clean, the staff was very helpful and close to downtown area. Will stay again if ever in Seattle. Two thumbs up.

We got a good deal through Priceline and didn't know what to expect. The staff were friendly and helpful. They would hail a cab for us when we needed it, which was helpful during rush hour and peak times. The room was clean and quiet. The suite was nice so when my fiancee wanted to go to bed early and I wanted to still watch a late game, we both could do what we wanted. The location was great....short cab rides to many attractions and walking distance to Grand Central and the subway. Highly recommended for travellers on a budget.

This was my second visit to New York and decided to stay a little further away from times square. The hotel is set a block from grand central and park ave so close to all transport.
I stayed in a suite on the -th floor and even had a partial view of tje empire state building, which at night, was beautifully lit up. The room consisted of a small kitchenette, large bedroom, plus walk in wardrobe, and cupboard with safe. The main living room had - arm chairs, and sofa bed which was comfy enough to sleep on and always made up every day. The bathroom was clean and had a constant supply of towels, soap etc. It wasnt noisy at night at all. 
The staff were all friendly and helpful, reccomending resteraunts, and easiest routes to get to places.
All in all, a great hotel, with no complaints.
Not a - star hotel. Very run down and old. Not at all what we expected.

Great hotel. There are fridges in the rooms as well. The bathroom is much larger than expected, especially for a downtown hotel. The room is also slightly larger than normal hotel rooms. I would stay here again. Very comfortable and clean. - restaurants. Starbucks. Parking is on the spendy side.

We stayed at the Washington Jefferson Hotel between the -rd and --th December for a deal that cost ----Euros for seven nights with Expedia....which wasn't cheap!!
The hotel kindly provided us with a complimentary bottle of champagne as it was part of our honeymoon. The hotel is in a fantastic location on --st and -th which is only a block from Times Square. There are lots of really good reastaurant within walking distance from the hotel that are really good value
Our room was small however it wasn't an issue as we didn't spend much time in the hotel only to sleep. However there was a horrendous smell in the corridor outside our room which seemed to come from the rooms down the hall. There appears to be people living in the hotel which was very strange!! and one of them liked to play her music a full volume late at night
We tried to use the internet from our room one morning and it wasn't working properly and was incredibly slow so we reported it to the reception and asked them to have the connection charge removed from our bill. We had to deal with -different people before this charge was removed as the initial two staff refused to remove the charge as they said that their records said that we were connected for --minutes. We found the staff to be extremely unpleasant when dealing with this issue and their customer service skills are rubbish
The room itself while small was nicely decorated and had a flat screen tv on the wall. The bathroom while also very small had a good power shower. We also selected this hotel as it advertised that it had a gym however this consisted of a tiny room with a treadmill and little else....so not my definition of a gym. 
In summary the location of this hotel is great but thats about it. We weren't looking for a very fancy hotel as we wanted to spend our money shopping and going out however due to the awful smell and awlful customer service we won't be returning to the WJ and won't be recommending it to anyone

After a full day in LA, we found ourselves too exhausted to drive home, with nowhere to stay. The Ramada Wilshire Center had no vacancies, but we drove a little bit and stumbled upon Dunes Inn. The location was great for us, relatively close to the Wiltern Theater (not walking distance though), and the mostly residential neighborhood--Hancock Park--was quiet and safe. (By safe, I mean, the only entrance is manned by a watchful clerk; there are no vagrants around; nearby are expensive condos, houses, and a few churches; and I would feel comfortable walking around the block, though the streets are quite dark.) The bed was comfortable, but not luxurious. The tv worked fine. Best of all, the bathroom must have been recently renovated, because it was impeccably clean with a nice granite countertop and new tilework. There was a refrigerator, a pool in the atrium, wifi, and a few rooms with a small kitchen, but we didn't use these and can't comment. Since we didn't pay full price, the room was a really great deal. Parking was free and greatly appreciated; since the neighborhood is not within walking distance of restaurants, night life, etc., you'd want to visit with a car. As a side note, some nearby places to visit by car: charming Larchmont Village, Koreatown, Griffith Park & Observatory, Downtown-Japantown, and LACMA. To summarize, Dunes Inn Wilshire is like a Travelodge but with a fancier, cleaner bathroom, and we'd definitely stay here again.

Return to the era of elegance when you stay at the New York Carlyle Hotel. Family and I stayed in one of their large suites and the furnishings were terrific. Dinner at the Carlyle Restaurant was terrific as it had great food, terrific service and splendid atmosphere. Saw Woody Allen and the Eddie Davis jazz band in the Cafe Carlyle which was an absolute highlight, Having stayed in many of the very best hotels in the US I must say the Carlyle is right near the top of the list.

The Sofitel is fine and the staff are extremely helpful and courteous. The room was great, especially the bathroom and the only small complaint would be that the air con system is a little noisy. Fully recommended. (we stayed -----th May ----)
It was a nice hotel with very friendly staff. My only issue is having to pay a daily rate of almost $-- for internet use. I would think in this day and age it would be free.

The Pacific Suite perfectly fit our needs. The in-room amenities were great. We received fresh fruit daily and cookies in the evening. Breakfast buffet was great; good variety and plenty of food. The food choices were alwasy appealing and fresh.
The service was excellent, as well. The staff attended to all of our needs.
The staff was very personable!

I was the event coordinator for an oil&gas conference held here - did rooms, meeting space, and food. Our attendees loved it! The food was great, the rooms are really nice, and the meeting space was very professional. They already had the main AV equipment, so that was a definite plus. Location was a plus as well - close to Memorial City, City Centre, the Galleria, Uptown Park, and Memorial Park. Our international attendees appreciated being able to navigate easily to and from the hotel. 
Only minor complaint was about the general service while moving through the lobby. I personally only had one instance where no one helped me carry things from my car to my room and one of my attendees made a comment along the same lines. Other than that, the employees in the lobby were helpful. Many of the employees are recent immigrants here to get an American education. They have neat stories!

From the minute I walked in the door the staff was exceptionally helpful. I was able to check-in to my room at -am, well before the traditional -pm mark. The location is very convenient to downtown amenities and around a - minute walk to the convention center with hundreds of local restaurants and bars all within walking distance. The hotel restaurant and bar will meet your needs well with very professional service and reasonable pricing. They also have a rooftop pool which is a nice perk.

We stayed at this hotel on a trip to New York city and wanted to experience the small, crampy, noisy NYC rooms that everyone complains about. Surprise surprise! This hotel is nothing like that! Walking distance a few blocks from Times Square and large spacious room. We were on the topmost floor, therefore the view was great and it felt beautiful looking into the giant lit streetscape of NYC. The noise levels were not such that disturbed our sleep.
The room was decorated well and had some beautiful portraits of NYC in black and white.
This hotel must be very popular, and very multicultural and the staff are most friendly. We heard a lot of interesting titbits and got very good guidance on what to see around, places to eat and shows to watch. We didn't eat even once at the hotel restaurant though it looked tempting.
The lobby area is a bit cramped, but thats very little a price to pay for the convenience of the location and quality of the rooms.

I enjoyed this Hilton. I had seen on their website that they had shuttle service and called a week prior to confirm. I was told to just call when I arrive and they would send over the shuttle as it was close to airport. When I arrived, I called and was told there was no shuttle. While that is not insurmountable, it was not expected that I did not have transportation. I did find a reasonable shuttle that I paid for and got there fine.
Check-in was fast. Room was typical of a downtown Hilton, upscale bedding. Thankfully, my package included internet as I usually have to pay from $-- per day and up depending upon location. I did see reviews where guests had to pay. 
View was great looking out over the water and bridge to Coronodo. Housekeeping was attentive. There were several restaurants and a Starbucks in the hotel. I was disappointed to have to pay $-- for a cup soup, salad, iced tea in the sports bar for lunch. Food was fine. We ate there another evening and just got burgers.
It was a great location with a waterfront walk for quite some distance to other restaurants, Seaport Village, USS Midway, and ferry tours. I also was able to walk to Gas Light Village with lots of other restaurants, etc. Great trip to San Diego.

This Westin has a great location--right on Chicago's 'magnificent mile' next to the John Hancock Center. The staff are friendly and helpful. But the only other great thing about this hotel is the Westin bed. The rooms and corridors have been given a slapdash renovation. The in-room dining menu is barely mediocre. Having recently stayed at a Hyatt the difference in standards was immediatly obvious. There are plenty of hotels in this vicintity--I'll look elsewhere next time. One other thing--I chose the Westin partly due to their new no-smoking policy, but this hotel has a smoking-allowed (and very smoky) restaurant on the premises with an entrance off the lobby, and stale smoke lingers in the elevators.

After reading the reviews I didn't know what to expect - but I chose the hotel because of it's price and the proximity to the Wells Fargo Center (formely Wachovia Center). The hotel is definately dated - but for $--.-- total I didn't expect luxury. There was a big dead opossum in the parking lot when we arrived. Like the past reviews said the ice maker did not work & the -nd elevator bank is very scary. One side of the tower offers great views - However, the view on our side was terrible. The room was spacious (two double beds, table, two chairs, TV set, dresser, ceiling to wall mirrors). 
The staff was very friendly. They allowed us to check-in early at no additional fee. They recommended restaurants for us to try, etc. After the front desk staff told us that the hotel shuttle was only to bring guests to & from the airport - the manger stepped in on his own & went above-and-beyond by offering to take us to the restaurant - and then going one-step further by offering to pick us up later that evening after the concert - which was great because it was so late. My toothpaste was confiscated by TSA - which I forgot about until we got back to the hotel in the early A.M. hours - the front desk gave me two things of toothpaste & a new toothbrush at no charge (the Crowne Plaza I stayed at the week before charged for both) 
I recommend this hotel due to it's proximity to all the stadiums - but I recommend it even more for the great service provided by it's dedicated staff. If you're looking for more than a place to crash - you probably wouldn't be happy here - but for $--.-- - it was worth it.

We booked the Stay and Fly package at this hotel--stayed one night before flying out on a two week trip and leaving our car parked in their lot.
The hotel is clean and comfortable and includes most amenities including a pool, restaurant and -- hr. airport shuttle. We arrive about - p.m. and parked our car in their Stay and Fly lot which is well lighted and appeared to be well used as the lot was nearly full. The Boulevard Cafe inside the hotel offers a limited lunch and dinner menu and a free breakfast buffet. Since it was raining and we were taking an early flight we had dinner at the restaurant. It was quite satisfactory. The breakfast buffet opens early so that we were able to have breakfast before taking the - a.m. shuttle to the airport.
When we returned - weeks later, our car was fine. Just a little dirty from sitting outside in the rain.
We would definitely stay at this hotel again when flying from Seattle.
If you are interested in the Stay and Fly package and plan to be gone more than a week, you will need to call the hotel direct. Their website does not list Stay and Fly packages for more than - days.

Stayed -- to -- December - second time visiting which says something.
Decent rooms (ask for a high floor) and nice that the windows open to get real air rather than just a-c [although NY can be noisy!!!).
Very comfortable beds.
Great toiletries from Etro.
Good easy food next door [Foodparc] and plenty of nearby availability.
Free wine hour from - to -.
Decent location although not quite central for touristing.
Stay, especially if you get a good price.

Just came back from a fine stay at the Tremont for two nights. I was a little nervous as others have been after reading the reviews, but was pleasantly surprised. We parked in a parking garage on Delaware one block away to avoid the $-- valet charge. Still $---day, but not bad. Check in was very pleasant. Had two rooms booked on hotwire. Be advised that the hotel pretty much has only single bed rooms only. We were given two rooms, one with a large king bed and one with a queen, both on the third floor so we could be on the same floor. There is only one elevator and it can be slow, but being on the third floor made for an easy trip on the stairs behind the lobby, if you don't mind seeing the kitchen on your way up. The rooms were well decorated I thought, and both had CD players as advertised. Views can vary, one room had a great view of Chestnut St and another the back of the place. Both rooms were very clean. Be advised, they are small though, but that's to be expected. There were some minor spots of peeling paint, but nothing major and nothing that looked unusual for an older hotel. The location can not be beat, we had a close walk to the El, Rush-Division restaurants nightlife. I wouldn't hesitate to stay there again, especially at hotwire prices.

Our first trip to New York so can only compare with hotels elsewhere.
Arrived at -:--pm on a Saturday night for - night stay to be told that the room would not be ready for a further hour !!!
Finally got into the room and basically crashed out after being up for -- hours.
In the morning was awaken by a whining noise, eventually finding the source to be a service elevator drive room adjacent to our room. On checking the room found the toilet damaged, the doors of the wardrobe and bathroom in need of lubrication. The wallpaper was damaged in both bedroom and bathroom. There was a rusted vent cover over the window and the curtain bracket was damaged.
I asked at the front desk for a change of room which was addressed immediately. The new room was excellent with a very comfortable bed and plenty of space and a large TV.
I'm not sure if it's standard in New York hotels that there are no coffee making facilities but I found it strange to see so many people going to Starbucks next door and then queue for the lifts to take the drinks back to the room !!!
As stated in previous reviews the location makes the hotel.

Stayed there after a day at Sea world. It's a -min easy drive.
Checking in: A fairly new hotel on a hilltop, right near a huge cinema, and much shopping and restaurants nearby. Checking in was rapid speed for us, and found the twin beds room to be fairly clean and acceptable. Has a nice lobby, and parking- environment appears safe.
Once you are there: The kids loved the indoor heated pool and the ability to chose their own breakfast at the buffet the following morning. Indoor heater & AC worked fine and clean bathrooms.
Negatives: Just a single elevator that you have to wait and is used heavily. The front desk is manned by a single staff, which you had to find from time to time. Just not easily available.
Would stay here again vs. other bad experiences with other chains in this area.

Expensive property with a nice lobby. I stayed in a corner room that was in need of a renovation - I was told the entire hotel is soon to receive new carpets, etc. High speed internet did not work, I was told no refund, since the provider is a -rd party company. No coffee service in room, unless I want to pay $---night....When you want a nice place to stay, go a few blocks away and choose the Monaco - a truly great hotel.

My boyfriend and I booked this hotel because it was in our budget compared to all the other hotels around the area. We thought we were getting a shared bathroom but turns out someone had cancelled and so we upgraded to one with a private bathroom. 
We paid cash, and were not informed on the website that there is a security deposit also, which is the same amount for the night we stayed, so we paid double the amount and almost did not have enough to even stay. Hotel staff worked in on us being intimate, they were not aware the room was booked i assume. We got back to the hotel rather late, and wanted to sleep but there is a gay bar right down the street and it was constantly loud. we heard some loud noises and my boyfriend decided to baracade the door so that we felt safe (they have crappy locks) but overall great price, very cute room, big windows and lots of space to move around. but it all depends on what rooms they have ready. we had the room right about the cafe on the street.

Only stayed - nights at The Westin. Tried to pick a hotel with a view in the midst of the action because I was taking my nieces to NYC for their first time. The Bellhops and the guys outside that greeted us were fantastic, unlike the clerks at the desk. Very cold and didn't seemed pleased to have me as their customer. Unfortunately our room looked out into a brick wall and I was totally disappointed with that. I expressed my displeasure and they said they couldn't do anything about it but would give us a different room the next day which they did and the view was fantastic. The beds and the location are definately the high points. I've never paid that much for a hotel room so I guess I didn't know what to expect. Seems like a lot of money for what we were receiving but guess that's just how it is. But the beds were great. Or maybe it was just because I was so exhausted!

This new hotel is only a block from Times Square and close to resteraunts and Theatres.
The staff were courteous and the breakfast of Yoghurt and fresh berries at $- and Toast at $- were a cheap way to start the day. Orange juice $- was expensive.
Further down West --th in, -th Street were some really good Italian eating spots. There is also a Laundromat in -th for $--- you can do your wash. The hotel charges $- to launder undershorts, you can buy new ones for less.
Still Intercontinental is a great hotel and we would recommend that if you are looking for a NEW hotel in New York, close to everything in the way of Theatre The Square it is GREAT.

It is a cute little hotel with small, but comfy rooms. Its a bit noisy but its in the heart of the city so you have to expect that a bit. The bath room was rather small, but for the price and location you can look past the smaller rooms and see the quality you are getting!

This hotel will become the first one I try to book on my frequent trips to the DC area. It was a beautiful room and the staff was very attentive. C.J. Tibung in Guest Services went above and beyond on to undo a mistake I had made when checking out. He was just one of the employees who gave their best to ensure I had a great stay. Probably the first time I have had that level of service in the DC area.
Cudos to C.J. et al.

Myself and my family, partner and two kids stayed at the Alex for a long weekend.
We arrived on Thursdasy afternoon and were checked in immediately, no delays all ran smoothly.
We had booked a two room suite which to be honest was quite expensive but this is NYC..
The hotel position is absolutely perfect for seeing all the most important sities of NY so you can basically walk anywhere.
A part from this I would say my only complaints were:
The rooms have the usual NY windows so unable to open and I go honestly get not such a nice smell in the room.
Cleaning of the room could have been better, after brushing my hair in the bathroom hairs were everywhere.
On my retrun I could still see hairs on the ground.
The bar is really nice but as every - star is really costly.
We did not include breakfast in our room rate for which I am now happy as on -rd av there is a really nice cafe' which serves a fab breakfast.
On checking out we handed in our baggage ticket which was fo - pcs. they filled the trunk and told me all was in. True I did not check personally but on arrival at Kennedy one pcs was missing.
I called the hotel and they did immediately put it in a taxi and sent it to me at Kennedy but at my expense.
Absolutely my own fault for not checking but to be honest a five star should have personel that ceck the amounts of baggage on the tickets they give you to make sure they have given you all.
To be honest I dont think I would go back again too expensive and a bit over rated.

This place is a good value based on location. We ran up the coast from here the next day. It is rundown, looks a little questionable on arrival. But the owners were nice. There was no ice machine and they gave us some ice from their residence behind the lobby. Otherwise the room was huge! Don't know if they are all that way, but this one had a kitchenette as well. Ask for the upper end room if you can. Everything worked. A little noisy with the parking around. If you stay here, have breakfast at the Pacific Diner just around the corner!

Having returned from New York, I would recommend the Edison to anyone wanting a clean room -- seconds from Broadway!
We found a fantastic deli just right of the hotel entrance where police and NY yuppies all ate---fantastic! 
If ever I went back to New York, I would use this hotel again---but be warned, no kettle so no tea! How English is that!!

Stayed - night in september at BW Plus Denver International Airport. Good hotel, clean, renovated, comfy, good breakfast and good shuttle service to the airport. At walking distance from Ruby's resto and a -- min. drive to the airport and the car hire companies. Very professional woman at the receptiondesk. Just - negative points. Our friends had problems with their toilet. They were offered another room, but had to pack their luggage again for changing rooms. Not funny. And the replacement of the breakfastbuffet was very, very slowly. You need a lot of time for waiting for new eggs, bacon or burgers.

I stayed three nights at this hotel in early January. The room was typical of New York (on the small side), but was clean and well appointed. There was a good breakfast included every morning with plenty of choices to start your day, and internet was free also. There's a small exercise room on the bottom floor with a few pieces of cardio equipment and a selection of hand weights. My only complaint is that my room (-th floor, on the back side), looked directly into the windows of a yoga studio in the opposite building, so quite often during the day when I put up the window shade there would be a dozen or so sweaty yoga students looking back at me. But the room was clean, quiet, and very close to subway stations and a good selection of inexpensive restaurants, so I would stay here again.

Booked our stay through Expedia, and though we're new InTouch (Kimpton's loyalty program) members, could not get the credit for our nights, but were given all the other great perks ($-- free from mini-bar, choice of pillows, etc- check out their plan). I think I'd try to book directly next time - get a rate at Expedia, make sure it is available and call Kimpton - they say they'll match it, if it's available when you call.
Lovely greeting from Megan when we arrived, effortless check-in and breezed up to our room (----) - queen, premiere view, overlooking the Granary Burial Ground and far off, the Charles River and the Citgo sign. Really loved the room; quiet (tho' still some street noise when we had the window open - YES! a window that opens!), beautifully appointed, great bed. Small tv. We asked for a coffee maker and they delivered it immediately - very thoughtful of our time and would not accept a tip.
Our stay was really great - we wanted to wander around and since we had lived in Boston, really just wanted to catch up with the city again, post Big Dig (you can see how looong it's been since we've been back) - Boston Book Festival, dining, lazing around; great get away and Nine Zero and their staff really made us feel special.

this hotel is an excellent place to stay i stayed - nights and was very impressed, shuttle service is brilliant,staff friendly and rooms fab.right next to airport but no noise whatsoever,very quiet,would definitely stay here again.

We stayed here on the -nd night of our vacation while we passed through Denver. We checked in after attending the Rockies-Phillies game. The young lady that checked us in was very nice and even laughed at my dumb jokes. A couple of complaints though...We pulled into the parking garage to park. The problem is that when you're carrying all of your luggage from the car to the lobby, you need a key to get into the elevator shaft. If you haven't checked in yet, you don't have an elevator key. Maybe I did it wrong, but I guess you need to check in before you park. Anyway, we waited a few minutes and someone came out of the elevator lobby and we snuck in. Overall it was just a minor inconvenience. The rooms are clean, the bed in the bedroom is very comfortable, but the pull out sofa is not. There is no ice maker on the floor, but there is an ice maker in the freezer. Unfortunately that only makes a few rounds of ice and not enough to fill up a cooler. The hotel is conveniently located and I would recommend it to others. I used Marriott points, so I cannot speak to value or price.

My husband and I have stayed in a few different hotels in the Union Square area, and were disappointed by the Palomar. While it has an excellent location, the hotel itself leaves a bit to be desired. Rooms seemed tired, small, with pillows that were covered in either lint or white dog hair. Staff did not seem interested in hospitality- they seemed unresponsive when we stood at the front desk waiting for help (had to finish a personal conversation before helping). Walls are thin. If you like a boutique-hotel feel, then this is the place for you (enjoy the leopard print carpet!) but if you are looking for a more comfortable, - star hotel, look elsewhere.

I have been staying at W San Diego - nights a week for the last several months, home away from home. I've been working in San Diego for the last year and half and W is my top pick. Pretty much, I've stayed in all the high end hotels, Hilton Gaslamp, Marriott Marina, etc... I find W to be warm and comfortable . The hotel offers all the amenities but the hotel staff is what seperates them from the pack. Melissa Humble at the front desk is always attentive to my needs. 
Sure, I am a loyal SPG member but there are half a dozen Starwood Properties in town and no hotel comes close to W. The only negative that I could think of is the location; however the hotel offers free transportation around town.

We have stayed at other Sofitels and found the rooms at this one a bit disappointing. I confess, I was surprised after all the rave reviews on the site. There was nothing actually wrong with the room at all, but it seemed a bit dated in comparison with the rest of the hotel. The lobby bar and public areas are all really funky but the rooms seemed fairly bland in comparison. 
Having said that, despite the styling issues, the room was very comfortable, had a great view and was quiet. The bathrooms were lovely - as usual for a sofitel! 
The breakfast room seemed very small for the size of the hotel and on one morning there was a -- minute wait for a table - although on the other days this wasn't a problem. Food was excellent and service at breakfast was good. 
We didn't eat in the hotel in the evening (there are so many options in Chicago) but one evening when we were tired and tempted to stay in, we did notice the restaurant seemed quite high end and there didn't seem to be an option to have something simple like a Club sandwich in the evening. Only snacks-small plates were served in the bar. Again, I found this unusual for a hotel of this size. 
The location was brilliant - a stone's throw from the magnificent mile and only about -- minutes walk from the river. We loved Chicago and were fortunate enough to see some of the Blues Festival which was fantastic. 
My top tip - take one of the (less well publicised) Chicago Architectural Foundation boat tours if you are even remotely interested in architecture. it was money very well spent and you get some great photo opportunities from the river.

I along with my sister and brother stayed at the Holiday Inn Express, Arrowood on my first visit to Charlotte. Our stay from start to finish was very pleasant. The front desk staff was very nice and easy to talk to. If we had any questions, they didn't hesitate to help us out. Also the rooms were VERY CLEAN and the beds were extremely comfortable. The hot breakfast, which had a lot of options to choose from, was aslo a plus.
Although there wasn't a lot to do around the hotel itself, it wasn't hard to find restaurants and malls. Also, downtown Charlotte was only a ----- minute drive. 
All in all, we really enjoyed our stay. Definintely would recommned this hotel to anyone visiting the Charlotte area.

The Library Hotel is a true exemplar of thoughtful, meaningful experience design and execution. The Library-Dewy Decimal theme is brought to life with delight - books abound (my -- year old was even offered a classic for her personal collection upon check-in) and the cast of characters working at the hotel seem to step right out of a storybook. Elegant and warm. Personal and kind. No detail is overlooked (including the clever staircase painting and the personalized welcome note signed """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""the Librarians""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""). Most notable is that every team member seemed to remember something about us - making all interaction truly memorable. A WOW experience!

I have stayed at the Wyndham every time I travel for business to El Paso - Juarez. It is very convenient to the airport -- a walk away. The staff is very friendly. The breakfast buffet is excellent. Won't stay any where else when traveling to El Paso.

Staying here while at meetings at the convention center. It's right across the street and in the heart of downtown. The room is nice and the beds very comfortable. Each double bed has - pillows which I appreciated. Very clean also and has a program for declining housekeeping if you'd like to not have it every day and save some water-linens.

I stayed at this hotel during a business-pleasure visit to San Francisco and found it to be adequate. The hotel is in a great central location and it is easy to get to restaurants, public transportation and landmark sites in San Fran. The rooms and the staff on the other hand, are nothing to write home about. Overall, it was a decent stay. I recommend the location but encourage San Fran visitors who may be looking for more that a “decent” stay to continue their search.

Most state park lodges are fairly pedestrian affairs, designed for the outdoor recreation crowd and not for the more upscale-minded. Not so with Fort Harrison just east of Indianapolis. The lodge has four-star rooms with a five-star staff. The only negative is that there is no on-site breakfast offered either in the nearby restaurant at the conference center or on property. Otherwise, nothing but raves for this wonderful hotel in a beautiful environment. Maybe one of the best places to stay in central Indiana!

It's true what they say....pictures are deceiving. Aside from the incredibly convenient location for which we were in town for (needed to be near North Bennett Street School in North End - Super Close!) there is nothing more to say to support this hotel. Room was tiny, smelled kinda stale-musty, housekeeping erratic. It appeared, although they really tried, that the hotel is understaffed as they resorted to having a front desk person who'd worked all night acting as the waiter for the breakfast crowd in their small restaurant. That didn't go well - no fault to the kid...he really tried!
Be aware there is a charge for parking ($--.-- per day) that was not disclosed to us when our car was taken away by the valet. Too bad, it seemed good on line!

What a great find and what a great price! Thank you TripAdvisor! I stayed at the Moore for two nights before moving to the Grand Hyatt for a conference I had to attend. In my humble opinion, the Moore's location was infinitely better than the Hyatt's. Although it's --- years old, the Moore glows - the restoration was done well and the rooms are quite comfortable. 
Downtown Seattle, in all its splendor, is just a couple of short blocks away. The restaurants and nightlife of Belltown are right there too. I loved having Starbucks on the next block for my morning coffee, and Pike Place is just a few blocks away for breakfast The young man who worked at the front desk each evening was also fascinating to talk to. I can't wait for my next visit. The Moore is a jewel!

We have just returned from a four night stay at this Hotel. We would normally stay at the Marriott but due to the fact that they have priced themselves out of the market, we decided to stay at the Colonnade. From the very beginning of our stay, we were met with the very friendly staff from Hilary (doorman) to all the reception staff and even the cleaning staff, everybody always smiled and said hello.
The rooms were large, clean and the bed was amazing!!!!!!
We all will all be returning next year for our annual Boston shopping trip.

We booked here because of the location (best for us), price and hot breakfast. We were very surprised when greeted at the front desk with a hospitable woman who told us that she had our reservations and we were being upgraded to a KING SUITE because of our Priority Club membership and then handed us a goodie bag of chips, granola bar and bottle of water! WOW! Membership has it's advantages!
The room was clean and very spacious! The breakfast was good every time that we ate, They offered something a little different each morning.
There were only a couple of things that needed to be improved on. The bathtub was very slippery and needed either a tub mat or new non-slip pads. Also the bathroom needed an exhaust vent.
We had a very comfortable stay and plan on staying there again in the future.

I travel a lot, but have never experienced such bad service anywhere in the world. One thing is that the rooms are very small and the elevator didn’t work while I stayed a week at the -th floor, but the actual problem is the hotel staff.
I was treated very disrespectfully several times by the management of the hotel and I even almost lost my airplane because I had asked the hotel staff to help me arrange transportation (livery service) to the airport ...which they didn’t! Instead they called a private former employee, who showed up in his private car almost - hours later. I had no time to wait for a alternative transportation and was even overcharged.
I will never recommend this hotel to anyone...!

I often stay in this area as it is close to work and have now stayed at most higher end hotels in the area in an attempt to find my favorite. Eventi has now become my go to hotel for a stay in mid town. I highly suggest the small upgrade fee for the corner rooms which do feel more spacious and the desk in these rooms looks out the window which is my preference. They are also incredibly well laid out and street noise is quieter than many other hotels. I love the design!
My only complaints, though minor would be:
-) The noise from the air conditioner units can sometimes be louder than many other hotels, seems strange as they are new
-) I would not consider the curtains to be blackout drapes and they do let light through
-) There is simply too much paper signage in the rooms, most of which ironically talk about their environmental efforts

Decent hotel, that appears to be resort from decades past (perhaps the --s), and hasn't had much updating. It does have a nice location on Mission Bay and is offset from the hustle and bustle of the area, so it was a quite stay.
We had a separate cabin style room - received a complimentary updgrade - which was a nice change of pace from standard hotels, and we didn't have to listen to our neighbors. So, if you can afford it, these are nice accomodations.
Aside from that, nothing special. The beds are a bit hard, and the sheets scratchy (why can't hotels pay more attention to the bed and sheets?).

After complaining upon check-in that our Garden room with balcony had no such balcony, we were given a new room and thought all was well... until i stupidly didnt lock the balcony when we went to sleep. 
Picture this .. its -am.. you've had quite a few drinks, and you are awakened by a screaming partner, you sit bolt up right in bed and see a tall, dark man running out our balcony door and scurrying down the balcony like spiderman.. yep. scary as hell. My partner had woken up and seen him crawling alongside the bed ...welcome to seedy Hollywood Boulevarde, but there is nothing seedy about The Roosevelt and this wasnt there fault at all... PEEPS lock your doors :)
After LAPD arriving and arresting the man that security did promptly find, The Roosevelt and staff proceeded to do EVERYTHING they could to make us feel safe and secure. We were upgraded to the beautiful Thomson Suite in the original hotel, as high up as you could go and on a secure floor .. oh, and no balcony (I am sooo over balconies now :)) The hotel did the usual things i would of expected like a bottle of wine, fruit, a nights credit, but The Roosevelts true class came through with the letter from the manager asking us to let them know if we had any more unease and security regularly checking in on us to ensure we were safe and happy..
The Roosevelt is a beautiful grand dame of a hotel and even after the scare, i loved her.
I'd like to note that what happened to us we were told is NOT a regular occurance but you do need to be on your toes in Hollywood.

I was so impressed with this property. Everything was grade A+. Doorman when we first pulled up was so nice and helpful, friendliness of the front desk staff was great. The room was very clean, such a comfortable bed, awesome shower and you know what.....the drink and food prices of the honor bar were so reasonable that I couldn't resist the $-- bottle of top rate red wine to go with some of the homemade chocolate treats as I enjoy the view and great wifi speed as I catch up on my emails. I'm definitely Dana next time I visit Chicago!

This room was big, but it was by no means properly cleaned!!! The more the night went on the more i saw what was wrong with the room. There was a hole in the wall in one area, someone had thrown up all over the safe that was in the room and it was not cleaned correctly, and the bath room smelled like urine. I would not stay here again. Also the pool was not clean at all!!!

We stayed here for - nights on our first trip to NYC. The hotel is massive (as is everything else in the city!) although the rooms are just about big enough to hold a double bed, writing desk, chest of drawers and little else. 
The room was tidy and the bed comfortable, which is all you need when in New York. There is a diner connected to the hotel, and coffee-croissants available to buy in the lobby every morning.
The staff were very helpful and informative, although there is a small charge to hold your luggage once you've checked out.
Times Square is a few blocks walk, as is -th Avenue and Broadway. The subway which runs by the hotel takes you to many areas of the city, or to a connection to other lines.
 This was the cheapest -* hotel by far, and would definitely stay again

I travelled to SF many times and mostly stayed at the Hilton O´Farrell Street. Always a pleasure, always nice. But a main feature of this hotel used to be the executive lounge on floor -- with stunning views over the bay area. Also the restaurant on floor --. 
Both were closed down due to financial reasons. Breakfast is now served downstairs at a cantina style restaurant, very loud, not very inviting. 
The hotel has very friendly staff and all seem very committed. Rooms are spacy and clean and comfortable.
But there are many other hotels in SF available for the same kind of money, Management should consider this and maybe make use of the - now empty - floors -- and -- again. But then again, they may have their reasons. And we have our choices.
This hotel is fantastic - impressive reception, helpful staff, superb views across the Manhatton skyline, close to the river and fairly central (only about a -- minute walk) to the Times Square.
My entire family including nephews and uncles loved it. Beds were comfortable and the facilities were great.

the hotel was ideally situated for visiting the museums and the capitol building. My room was spacious and comfortable. 
The dining room served good food, reasonably priced and the service was excellent.
the tour desk in the lobby had Old Trolleybus tours which were hop on hop off but much more comfortable than double decker buses.
There was also a Starbuck's on the corner of the hotel and a bar that served light meals. 
I enjoyed my stay there very much.

We arrive at the hotel about noon after a long flight from FL and were greeted by their friendly staff. They took our luggage and locked it up so we could roam the area after they gave us a list of suggested sites to see. The rooms are modern, clean, and large. We had - adults with lots of luggage and it easily accommodated us. We stayed there - nights prior to our cruise and - night on the return. The first leg of the trip we were lucky to have an amazing view of the Space Needle. The last night we stayed there we were facing Denny Way. Both rooms were quiet and there were no noise issues (I'm a light sleeper so that would have been a problem.) The breakfast goes fast and the staff tries to keep up with the demands, but there were a couple times they were out of food. They have an excellent tea-coffee station. Take advantage of the free shuttle it is a wonderful perk and the driver was very knowledgeable about the city and made great dining-entertainment-wine suggestions. Only thing I would advise, one of the hotel staff members recommended walking from the Light Rail station to the hotel (if it was a nice day out). It is not an easy walk with luggage and the hills..take a cab.

If you're searching for a hotel with a little charm that's close to Hollywood and in safe location that won't break the bank, you've found it! This is an adorable little hotel that's a -- minute walk to great bars, restaurants and more in Hollywood and a -- minute walk to the center of Hollywood. We also drove up to Griffith Observatory (about -- minutes away) in the evening, which was beautiful. 
The bathroom is particularly nice with a large, tiled, double-head shower and a large mirror. The bed was comfy and we weren't disturbed by any neighbors, although the maids did wake us up around -.--...the rolling carts are EXTREMELY loud on the tile floor outside the rooms and the maids themselves were also quite loud. 
My only other negative feedback is that self-parking didn't seem to be an option. I'd like to go to my car when I want without having to wait around for the key, but it didn't make the stay any less than great. I would definitely recommend this hotel!

We stayed at the Wyndham Franklin Plaza for - nights and for the most part enjoyed our stay. We didn't spend much time in the room, however, these are the problems we encountered:
-. Could not use our Wyndham By Request number because we booked on Hotwire. (BTW-we only paid $-- a night-a deal in Philly)
-. The fire alarm went off twice in one night at midnight and -am. Needless to say, it was a restless night.
-. Before bed one night we discovered that - pillows had no pillowcases on them...called down to have someone bring them up, but no one ever came!
-. The lobby was filled with high school kids yelling and jumping on the furniture one evening.
The staff was friendly and helpful. You can walk almost anywhere in Center City from this hotel, but at night I'd take a cab back if you're far from the hotel.
Overall, it was okay, but I doubt we'd stay there again.

I absolutely loved how unique the hotel was furnished from the entrance to the rooms. It is like a boutique style hotel. Colors were vibrant & not boring. We had a large group come out for a huge convention and booking group reservations was a breeze! The food at the restaurant was very hearty and good and the servers were very nice. Overall, our experience there was fantastic! The entire staff was welcoming and friendly. We appreciated the complimentary shuttle within a - mile radius and it was a great location since many places we needed to go to were either - mile away or less so we could even walk if we chose. Looking forward to staying here again next year!

I was concerned about the varying reviews, but not to worry, it was an overall good experience. On arrival the receptionists (mainly seem to be students working part-time) were friendly and helpful. We were on a motorcycle tour and they recommended overnight parking in the adjacent street. The room was small but clean, the breakfasts were fresh and plentiful. The area is really central to the main shopping area, Macy's is only - mins walk. We ate at the Grand Cafe a couple of blocks east and would recommend it, great atmosphere. There are a lot of beggars about, but this is true of all areas, I had previously stayed at the Whitcomb Hotel on Market Street and to be honest the area around there was worse. If all you need is a well located clean room, don't hesitate to book the adante.

Having stayed at other properties on this street I had my doubts that this location would compare to them. I was very happy to have had my fears put to rest. This hotel is not so large as to make you feel lost or lose that welcoming feeling with staff yet not so small that you will be lacking amenities. My suite was very large and quiet welcoming. The bed was very comfortable, even the bathroom towels were nice and not scratchy. Given I was in a suite I would have enjoyed some additional glasses for people who came to my room but that's me being picky. Nice stay and would recommend it.

I can't believe how dirty the room was. The bedding was clean, thank heavens! Furniture had dust with finger prints on it, the floor was not vaccumed, at least not very good. I don't mind old, but dirty doesn't do it. YUK! Breakfast bar was out of almost everything, coffee was hot. Pool looked pretty but had scum floating in one corner.

we stayed at Kawada for one week on our honeymoon and it wasnt too bad. Positives were a vending machine on one of the levels, free internet access twice a day for -- mins, staff were mostly nice to us, willing to help out with booking for tours etc which was cool, clean rooms, cleans sheets, a really big bathroom and the cherry pick cafe next door was ACE! negatives were, bit of an old feel to the place, bit dated, no access to stairs- you have to use an elevator which sucks when you hate the bloody things like i do!!!, the hotel was far from tourist attractions and seemed to be a dead end side of town. overall, could have been worse so it was ok for what we paid.

This was my first time at this hotel everytime I come to Boston now I will stay here the staff is the best, I only had one problem the tipping pissed me off, everytime I tried to tip someone they denied it. And said its the policy. Now this is MY MONEY I can do what ever I want with it, if I want to give it to someone who works hard there should be no thought I want them to take it with out me haveing to repet my self

The hotel is nice and has a ton of amenities. I have stayed here quiet a few times. On my most recent stay, my travel agency messed up my reservation. Casey to the rescue!!! Casey worked through the whole process with me (alomost -.- HRS). She did everything in her power to get the issues straightened out. It all turned out in the end but it was because of Casey that I didn't start pulling out my hair. Since I was standing there for so long....I was able to hear and see the professionalism displayed by Karina(?) and Mike. They greated everyone and always had a smile.

We had a pleasant stay at the Palmer House HIlton despite some of the comments. The lobby and Emerald Room are gorgeously rennovated. We stayed on the --th floor and had no problems with getting an elevator. Our room was decorated nicely with four pillows and a long roll pillow. The beds are ultra-comfy...good night sleep here. It was slightly smaller than some hotels but it was newly rennovated and charming. The bath fixtures were not replaced even though the bathroom was redone. Water pressure was much lower than what I expect in a hotel. Wonderful Crabtree and Evelyn toiletries were supplied. Wonderful Lavazza coffee was left in the room. Best brew I've ever had for hotel room coffee. The staff was lovely and helpful. There is a kiosk where you can check in your flights and printer available and a kiosk where you can find local nightlife, restaurants and activities with a printer as well. Have a famous Palmer House brownie in the restaurant or to go..they are delicious. Great location, would return here again.

My husband and I stayed at the Omni Houston Hotel in May ---- for four nights. The pool and the fountains are the highlight of the hotel. The seating area there is nice and relaxing. We were very lucky to have had beautiful weather during out stay in mid-May, and we went to the pool in the late afternoons each day of our stay. There is a pond adjacent to the pool, and we saw four black swans in it—a pleasant surprise! The hotel gym was great with a variety of machines, and it overlooked the pool. The room décor was modern and comfortable, and the bathtub-shower was a bit dated but clean. Housekeeping did a great job each day, and we had turn down service each evening. We ordered room service a few evenings, and our order arrived promptly by a friendly attendant. The front desk, concierge, and pool attendants were also very friendly and accommodating. We also enjoyed going to brunch in the hotel restaurant, and we enjoyed the fresh omelets made for us. The hotel bar was nice, but the food is typical bar food and not of the best quality, especially for the price. There is also an outdoor patio that was very nice, and the fire pits were on one evening. I would definitely stay at this hotel again, especially because of the great pool!

My wife and I spent a weekend at the Greenwich Hotel last month. It was terrific, and we will definitely stay there again on our next trip. Location is great - - block from the Hudson River and great walking-jogging trails along the river, great neighborhood full of small cafes and boutiques and interesting shops.
Our room was very nice. We loved the interesting but comfortable furniture, and the great bed. The rooom felt cozy and comfortable, but also hip and interesting. Appreciated the complimentary soft drinks, snacks, and large water bottles - a nice touch, and so refreshing for a hotel to actually include something """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""extra"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" with your room.
The hotel has a lovely courtyard where you can eat a quiet breakfast (and other meals if you like). Service in the courtyard was a little slow, but not annoyingly so. I just think the place has a laid back feel about it, and who wants to rush when you are sitting on a comfy couch in a pretty courtyard drinking good coffee. We had a very good Sunday brunch meal here. 
Oh, and the spa is worth a visit. We had a short couples soak in the Japanese tub, which was glorious and I only wish we had booked a longer soak, followed by great massages. The pool area is serene!
I enjoyed the Greenwich Hotel. Staying there, I felt lucky and privileged.

The Radisson Hotel at SEATAC is reasonably priced and is located only about a mile from the airport with shuttles leaving every half hour. The rooms are a little worn but clean and comfortable. The hotel staff is helpful and readily available.

This is typical La Quinta fayre. The room we were allocated was on the -st floor right at the end of the corridor. I was surprised that being so near the Freeway we could not hear it inside the room at all. The room was of what I would consider to be Motel style with only the bath-shower and wc in an enclosed room. The basin, hair dryer mirror etc were in the room. This is not ideal but for the price we paid I would not consider this to be a negative point. As I said we only stayed one night and found the room satisfied our needs of a clean and relatively comfortable place to stay. We enjoyed the inclusive breakfast with the normal waffles, bagels , juice and coffee, but this is what we have come to expect of this chain. 
They excelled themselves in the morning. We were taking a flight back to the UK from Houston Intercontinental late in the evening so we enquired about the possibility of a late check out. The front desk informed us that due to the renovations (we saw or heard nothing disturbing throughout our stay!) that the were fully booked for that evening, but she could let us keep our room until -pm. This was fantastic service in my book. It gave our kids a couple of unexpected hours in with the hotels outside pool ( a little cool for the adults in November - but the kids just loved it!) all for no extra charge! These are the little things that make you want to come back!

Got a package deal so I wanted to try out the new Colonnade Hotel in the Back Bay. Loved the spacious rooms with luxurious beds and flat-screen TVs. The rooftop pool bar was nice, but nothing really special. I wasn't very impressed. Here's a list of pros and cons for me. 
PROS:
- Location is prime (across the street from the Prudential center and walking distance to Newbury Street, Boston Public Garden, Boston Commons) and close to T stops
- Spacious rooms 
- Comfortable beds (too many pillows for my taste though)
- Flat-screen TVs
- Mini bar refrigerator in room
- Robes provided

The Carlyle Inn is reasonably priced, clean, and the breakfast was tasty! Our room was spacious and the bed was comfortable. They also have a lovely deck with plush chairs for sunbathing or relaxing. Great stay!

The hotel looks exactly like the pictures on the web...stylish, modern decor. The only thing good about this place was the location - only - blocks from main attractions. The rest was very disappointing. Two big reasons in this case, - is service and - is location. My husband and I were here for - nights because of a Marine squadron reunion that was being held at this location. Super friendly and helpful staff. Love the hotel decor, atmosphere and overall vibe of the entire place :) Awesome restaurant-bar too!

My husband and I just returned from a fantastic stay at Hotel Indigo. It was unlike any hotel we had ever stayed at. The decor had a chic, beachy feel and we couldn't help but smile at all the warm and vibrant colors that surrounded us. The staff was kind and offered their advice for the many questions we had since this was our first trip to Chicago. We had an amazing time at the Warwick. The location is perfect and the service was great! Our first room had problems with the aircondition and they immidiately upgrated us to a bigger an newly renovated room. We left the hotel feeling it had exceeded our expectations.

Stayed here several days over Labor Day Weekend.
I stayed in a queen room towards the back of the hotel (the 'quieter' part of the hotel, as it did not face the street). The price was a really good deal for San Francisco and the location (you'll find that out if you do a hotel research in the downtown area).
As most reviewers have stated, the room I got was very clean and well taken care of. The bathroom was immaculate and the towels were actually soft! The little 'kitchenette' area was a plus. The mini fridge worked fine. I didn't use either the dishes or microwave available. There was a huge closet which I did utilize and a little seating area which I used for my laptop. The bed and sheets were clean and comfortable. The room did get a little stuffy at times with the windows closed (you can open them) but there is a ceiling fan in the room, and I think a heater but I didn't need to use that. The carpet was also clean, the room was a good size for one person, and it was even painted with scenes on the walls and on the door. It was pretty quiet, I didn't really hear my neighbors and only very occasionally people outside the hallway. The floors creaked and I was worried that people below could hear that, but I haven't read any reviewers complain. I got a kick out of the old fashioned elevators. Also, above the lobby on the first floor there are a few computers with internet access and a printer. I did use the printer to print out my boarding pass.
Some amenities that I enjoyed are the free wifi (the access was good in my room), and the breakfast in the mornings, which is okay (toast, cookies, mini scones, oatmeal, applesauce, apples, hard boiled eggs, coffee and oj).
The hotel does have free parking, and I was a little disappointed that I couldn't park my car for the one night I had one because they only have twenty spots available (hey have -- rooms) and you have to reserve it in advance on a first come first served basis which I didn't realize.
The staff was very friendly and helpful and I didn't find any problems with them. 
I liked the location even if it wasn't just a few steps away from most major tourist attractions or transportation. But I think San Francisco is best scene and experienced by foot anyway and I didn't mind the walking (although my feet would argue differently!).
There are two little markets close by, one right next door and one just across the street which I found very convenient for buying water and snacks. There's also a small pizza place close by which is okay, and a couple of laundry mats in the near vicinity.
Overall, I had a really great experience at the Hotel Mayflower and I would and have recommended it to friends and would definitely stay here again if I'm in SF again.

Nice staff, breakfast ok not great selection but adequate. It was warm outside so had to leave air conditioning on and all night long it cycled on and off. Every time it came on sounded like a freight train running through the room. Kept my whole family awake all night long. We were at TCU orientation so lack of any sleep ruined the trip.

Great Staff. Great Price.
Cute, Clean, quite large room with wonderfully comfortable beds. 
Theo will give you an overview of the area you are in which is really helpful.
The hotel is a few minutes walk to Union Square which was handy. $-- - $-- will get you a cab to fishermans warf.
The wine receptions of an afternoon are quite fun. 
It can be a little noisy on the lower floors but with earplugs it is not a problem. 
We found the Public transport in San Fran quite slow but make sure you get the card of a cab driver and give them a call directly as they have to pay the hotel every time you order one from the lobby. 
We will stay here again and are happy to recomend it to anyone going to San Francisco.

Nice hotel, but skip the room service. Ordered room service and promised delivery in -- minutes. After an hour called to inquire and they claim no record of the order. Very poor service for this level of hotel. No apology, no reasoning, no making it right.

Stayed at the holiday Inn for - nights and would definately recommend this hotel to anyone else. It is not one for luxury and pomp, but the rooms were spacious, clean and very pleasant. The location is excellent, within easy walking distance to the wharf and all it can offer, restaurants, outings and even within easy reach to other sights such as Lombard Street and Union Square! For the price, location and cleanliness, this hotel is definately good value for money!

My wife and i travelled to NYC Feb --th ---- for - nights and loved it. The Park South hotel is boutique hotel on E --th street and and it has a subway nearby. The weather was really quite mild so we walked most places. On arrival we didn't feel that we received much of a welcome nor were we told anything about the hotel or where any of its facilities were.Our room did not have an information folder. Our room was an outside facing room which was a good size and the bed, bathroom, etc were all good quality as was expected.The in-room safe was small so we hid our small laptop when not in the room.[ the free wifi was quick and always available] We noticed that the inside facing rooms looked smaller and tended to look onto an inside wall-courtyard? The Edgewater was a recommendation by my travel agent, and as it turns out a great one. Friendly front desk. Gave us great directions! Excellent dinner - food was well prepared & flavorful. Room was immaculate. Beds were like clouds. Wish I could live there!

The Holiday Inn Express was so clean, efficient and enjoyable that we booked three addtional nights at other Holiday Inn Express locations. The Hotel is very convenient to I --- allowing us to get on the road to L.A. and to points of interest to the north.

My husband and I travel a lot, I am a loyal Hilton fan and he is a platinum Marriott member. When I plan the trips I make sure we stay at Hilton's because the Brand has great standards. I wanted to love this property, it sits at such a great location.

The location of this hotel was perfect!!! Literally on Times Squares doorstep!!!! The staff were friendly enough and the concierge Walter was great. He was so helpful. Exercise room made us laugh. It is the size of my home closet with a mirror and - machines in the basement. Good if you want to get a quick run in on the treadmill but don't expect to much.
I am more than happy with this hotel and won't hesitate to stay here again and again each time we go into Boston over night. Had a great weekend!!!

This is in a prime spot in the middle of the city, with nice views of the river and close access to a river walk. Plenty of restaurants and nightlife within walking distance of the hotel. I stayed in king bed room and it was set up nicely, with an area to work, comfortable bed, flatscreen, etc. Hotel decor has a boutique feel to it. The hotel overall is pretty massive and a bit of a maze to find your way around, particularly if you are attending a conference here. There's a coffee kiosk set up on the -st floor to grab a quick Starbucks and muffin in the AM. The gym is set up well, with newer machines. Across from the fitness center is the Spa Di La Fronza, where I wandered in and asked to schedule a massage. Lillian took care of me and did a great job working out the kinks from a long sales conference. Its a full service spa, including barber services as well.

Just returned from - nights at Hotel San Jose. I can't say enough about the hotel's attention to details, which made it such a unique and inspiring place to stay. From the carefully chosen soap, to the local """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Rainwater"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in your room, to the locally roasted coffee waiting for you in the lobby each morning. Our warm and considerate welcome flowed through to every aspect of our stay. The room was most comfortable, the breakfast more than adequate and the staff polite and attentive. To add to the hotels hospitality was the offer of two free drinks in the early evening.
The position of the Magnolia was an added bonus. We were only a -- minute walk to Dealey Plaza , the Tourist Information Centre and the historical and entertainment district. The metro was only a couple of blocks away.

Overall would stay there again without hesitation.

I staid at the Super - Hobby Airport at the --th of june for one night... With a Super - at the Airport i would usually not expect this much, but this one is different. We stayed in the downtown Hyatt during the Thanksgiving weekend and as usual, had excellent customer service. The rooms are very well appointed and comfortable and even though a youth conference was going on, our room was very peaceful. We will stay there again!

We stayed at the Grand Hyatt as the last stop of our honeymoon. Having spent - weeks prior in fantastic hotels on the west coast we were looking forward to staying at the Hyatt (which was about - times the price as any other hotel we'd been in). At first sight the Hyatt is impressive with a busy lobby full of christmas decorations however this luxury was not reflected in the rooms. Firstly, we arrived in the early hours of the morning due to a cancelled flight - I rang them to let them know that we would be this late. When we checked into our double room we found ourselves in a twin room - not so good for a honeymoon couple! I rang reception to ask if we could change to a room with a larger bed and were told they would ring us back - which they didn't. I went down to the lobby to ask and was told there was no further availability but to check again in the morning. When I went back to the room we realised we were also in a smoking room, despite all of our booking information requesting a non-smoking room. In the morning I requested a room change and was given another room - this time it was non-smoking but was still a twin. The rooms have minimal amenities (i.e. A TV, a closet, a safe, some toiletries) and there was mould in the bathroom, ingrained dirt in the tiny bath, and loose light fittings in the bedroom (see photos). We paid an awful lot of money to stay at this hotel (over £--- per night) and, whilst I am aware a good proportion of that money was because it was New York and it was Christmastime, I still think that the price was extortionate for what amounted to a room which wouldn't look out of place in a cheap B&B (and there are a lot of hotels available in New York for the same price which would have been far better value for money). Calmly elegant in a sparse, modern way. Very friendly service. Comfortable and well-appointed rooms with especially comfortable bathrooms. Showing just a bit of wear and tear. The perfect balance of comfort and value. Love the quick access to coastal highway. North to Delmar or south to downtown in a snap. Free parking, free internet, free breakfast...WOW!!!

Awesome price for a place right on the beach in the coolest town. Wasn't fancy but didn't need to be. Pool was clean, on-site restaurant rocked, and the front desk staff were nice. We had just returned from our Alaskan cruise vacation, and the Moore hotel is only - mins taxi journey from the pier. If you have a small bag, its walkable. The hotel has all the amenities you need --pool- fitness center, bar-restaurant and free breakfast. The rooms are large and comfortable, with in-room microwave and mini-fridge; but the furnishings are chipped and the carpet is worn. The bed is overly soft -- like sleeping in a sling -- and the pillowcases are made out of some stiff, yucky material. You hear the toilets flush from the adjacent rooms, and your own toilet is VERY loud in your own room. This hotel caters to business clients, yet it does not offer an in-room safe. Sorry, but that just doesn't feel secure to me. The location is poor. Yes, it's close to the airport, but not to anything else in Boston. It's surrounded by rental car lots. A cab to the North End will cost $-- one way (the concierge explained to me that taxis have to go thru an underwater tunnel, which has a toll), so the only other option is to take the T, back and forth.
