The Town & Country is set in beautiful garden atmosphere. Roses-flowers-palm trees-shrubs are throughout the entire property, with swimming pools in several locations. A very quite place to stay, great place to rest and relax.
The restaurants are great, food very good and service always prompt. Kelly's Steak House has a wide selection menu with most reasonable prices on everything especially their steaks. Excellent place for a family to dine.
From check-in, to bell service, to house keeping and beyond, a most professional staff. Their training shows in the performance of all the employee's. The Staff on the front desk could not be nicer and more efficient. Even with the lobby full of customers waiting to check in, they all maintain an alertness while handling your details and make every effort to make your wait as short as possible.
I have been a customer for some -- years at this fine hotel, and it just gets better with each year. The upkeep of the property is ongoing, and it seems every effort is being made to upgrade the rooms and in these economic rough times that's a gigantic undertaking.
The grounds are impeccable and certainly gives you that home away from home feeling.
Large upscale shopping center within walking distance. Public transportation readily available right at the rear of their parking lot. Close to many family attractions and in fact you can view the fireworks show at Sea World every night right from the property.
Room rates are very competative with the surrounding properties and many times are lower.
Hugh Convention Center facilities available for groups wanting meeting space and not having to leave the property during their stay to tend to business.
Absolutely a great property to stay, with a great staff.

Hotel -- is a great location for a short trip to Chicago. Dead center of the city with easy access to everything (including the airports). Was there to attend my cousins wedding which was held in the hotel. Great idea. The service and reception were held in the penthouse with a great view of the city.

It's old and unimpressive from the outside, but they pay attention to what really matters. It's a great deal for a great location ($---night - in Point Loma right on the bay near the San Diego airport - - min drive from downtown). The front desk was warm and professional and efficient. The room was basic with the exception of a large flat screen TV, a refrigerator, and free wireless internet - plus it was extremely clean. They provided coffee, orange juice and pastries every morning on the pleasant little patio with tables in the nook of the hotel. There were signs posted in various places., exhorting good behavior from the guests (quiet after -pm, no fish in the rooms, etc.) - and that's exactly what the place felt like, like you were staying in a simple home but with an attentive and caring mother.

If location is important..this hotel is fantastic. Walk directly into Macys from the hotel. Great shopping in walking distance of the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""magnificent mile"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The hotel: Check- in was a breeze even though our room was not ready (our fault..arrived too soon.) The desk clerk walked out from behind the desk and literally escorted us to the restaurant where we waited for the room and had a fantastic lunch. How about a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""pork belly flat bread pizza""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""? A """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""cherry smash cocktail""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""?. I know...sounds a little funky but what flavor! And the wild salmon was cooked to perfection. Service was perfect. We were not yet checked in and the servers knew our names...typical Ritz standards. We had a suite with two bathrooms...wife loved that. AC was quiet and able to cool to --....we like it cool when sleeping. Entrance to the hotel is a little congested but the valets handled it efficiently. As a matter of interest, the Hotel is not part of the Ritz Carlton family...only the name licenced some years ago to Four Seasons to provide the Ritz Carlton branding in the Chicago area.
It's a little pricey buy hey...it's a Ritz...or a Four Seasons...either or, it's a winner!

The room was unexpected for the price. Very clean with a mini kitchen. Was expecting just a mini micro and mini fridge, instead it was a full frige, micro and range top stove. Room was very clean. The only problem we had was the hotel doesnt accomodate according to what you've booked. Don't think you will get a King room if you booked one. You will get whatever they have.

The primary benefit of this hotel is it's location in the heart of SF within walking distance of restaurants, shopping and cable car line. We had a spacious corner room on the --th floor with a view of the bay. The hotel is not as luxurious as some other Marriotts, though quiet and comfortable. The one bone I have to pick is that after charging over $--- a night for the room you have to pay an additional $--.-- a day for internet-wi-fi access. Also we were told we wouldn't earn Marriott points because we didn't book through Marriott.

We stayed in mid July for a business-pleasure trip. The hotel is an art deco gem - gorgeous to the last detail. The location is great - - blocks from fantastic Millenium Park and the Art Institute and just a few blocks from the Magnificent Mile. The room was spotless in every way; perhaps a bit small by luxury hotel standards but certainly adequate for -, and it is an old hotel so we were not concerned. Furnishings and decor in the room were beautiful art deco and looked very new. Had a bit of trouble with the in-room internet - easily resolved by very courteous, knowledgeable tech support. Room cleaned perfectly each day. Every staff encounter was lovely - polite, cheerful, helpful - not sure I've ever experienced anythng like it from the front desk to bell men to housekeeping. I noticed quite a bit of attention to keeping the public spaces orderly and clean - a challenge with so much traffic. I have no complaints - only compliments for everything about the Palmer House.

We have just returned from staying at the Crowne Plaza in Times Square. It was my son's --th birthday celebration.
We booked through Hotels.Com - swift and easy and they text me straight back to confirm the booking. Check in was smooth and easy and we had a lovely room on the --th floor overlooking Times Square. 
As it was my son's birthday I had e mailed the hotel before hand requesting a high floor (this reduces noise and it was very quiet on our floor). I also e mailed them about arranging a birthday cake to be delivered. I paid for this service. 
They promptly e mailed me back every time. The cake was great (one of the nicest we have ever tasted) and it was delievered to the room as requested dead on the time I asked for. Two Maitre'd's came in with the cake and sang happy birthday to him!!
The hotel is right on Times Square - a fantastic location right in the heart of everything. 
You could not ask for a better location. You are also right on Broadway.
The rooms were lovely and the beds and pillows are very very comfortable. They make the bed up and change the towels every day. A previous review said that they do not always provide enough towels and so I took a couple of extra with me. There were four of us in the room and we only got enough towels each time for three of us so be aware of this. 
The only gripe I had was that the bath in our room was slightly chipped and the shower and plug in the bath was not working properly - but this was not a problem for us. However I expect these sort of things to be rectified in this quality of hotel. 
The staff were very helpful and polite. We only ate in the hotel once for breakfast as it tends to be very pricey in the hotels. Breakfast cost about $--- for - of us and we only had continental but tea, coffee, juices etc are included in this. However there are hundreds of places you can eat breakfast (and lunch and dinner) for about $- - $-- each!!! Opposite the hotel is a place (Italian sorry can't recall the name). All you can eat breakfast buffett - $-.--!!!
The guides will tell you there are enough places to eat in New York if you wanted to eat breakfast, lunch and dinner in a different place every day for the whole of your life!!
 It's true!
I can highly recommend getting the New York pass before you go. I got mine through Attraction Tickets Direct (who offer a fantastic serv ice). We saved so much money using this pass. It gives you entry into over -- attractions and for some a fast track so you don't have to queue. It also saved us $-- each in Planet Hollywood and gets you discount in Macey's and other shops. Otherwise you are looking roughly at each attraction costing you in the region of $-- or so each person each time you visit.
At this time of the year the queue to go to see the Statue of Liberty is huge. We queued for - hours to get on the ferry (The only attraction the Pass does not fasttrack you!). Get there very early - we got there at --.-- am and there were people later in the day when we got back being told they would not get to the Statue that day.
The all loops tour on the sightseeing buses are a must and the guides are very informative. These are hop on hop off and go in a circular route around Manhattan. The night tour is very very popular. You don't get off this one but to see Manhattan at night and you go over into Brooklyn and look back over the river to see that famous landsscape all lit up is just breathtaking. 
As you walk the streets around Times Square you will be constantly asked by ticket sellers from the two companies that operate these tours. They are on commission so they need to sell sell sell. Once you tell them you have tickets it's not a problem. But there are hundreds of them!!! 
 Pay your respects at Ground Zero, go up Empire State Building - but must agree Top of The Rock (Rockerfella Centre) is by far better. The view is about the same but the whole experience is much nicer. Go up just before sunset and watch the lights come on - it's fantastic. Walk over Brooklyn Bridge - the view looking back towards Manhattan is wonderful and you can take some great photos. 
They will charge you $-- each to go from --th floor which is the observation floor in the Empire State building, to go up to the ---nd floor. It's not worth it - the view is just the same unless of course you want to be able to say you are at the highest point in Manhattan. Again expect some queues (about -- mins) within the Empire State. You get the lift to the --nd floor, come out go around in a circle - have your photo done with King Kong if you wish and then get back into the lifts to go up to the observation floor. It's a bit annoying this really.. We went to New York in February - years ago and we did not do this - so maybe it has something to do with the time of the year and numbers of people.
We pre booked (through Attraction Tickets Direct) to see Mama Mia - had excellent seats could not have picked any better myself. They give you a mini programme for each of you - why can't they do that in the West End ? !!
This is our second trip to New York and I love it. You will feel safe - police and traffic police are everywhere - not like the UK. I feel safer there than I do in London. People are very polite and friendly. One guy pointed out to my husband that the ruck sack bag he was carrying was open and he wanted to make sure that my husband did not loose anything out of it!!!
You can leave your suitcases with the concierge for the day before you fly home that eve. Just make sure they take the bags straight through. We stood and waited for them to do this as they may see to other peoples bags as well and we witnessed one concierge walk off and away from the bags leaving them unattended. 
If you're looking for a great place to stay in Manhattan I cannot recommend this hotel enough. And if you have never been to New York before - YOU'LL FALL IN LOVE WITH IT!! - Have a great time!!

I stayed at this beautiful new boutique hotel in NY. In fact, I was the first person to stay in my room!! Modern furnishings, exceptional attention to detail, staff was extremely friendly and helpful. New opening minor problems as they were still trying to make it all happen. However, more than made up with their outstanding service. I have been doing regular travel for the past -- years. The atmosphere is really unpleasant, the service patchy, the decor totally outdated, faded and the whole place left us cold. The - pluses are - you can walk to the Mall and the Metro is close. If you need a nice, pleasant place to come back to at night...this is not it.

NEVER NEVER NEVER stay here. The halls smelled like urine and mold and were hot as hell. She ought to go stay there for a night.

I stayed at this hotel on March --st, ----. First of all, let me say that this is a wonderful place to stay. The lobby is very nice and very modern, with lots of glass, bright colors, a nice fountain, and several LCD TVs to watch while you wait. 
The front desk staff was very friendly and extrememly helpful, as they went above and beyond to accomodate my needs. I asked for a lower level room, and I was promptly given a room on the main floor, just around the corner from the lobby. This was very convenient for us.
The room was great as well. VERY comfortable bed, nice furnishings, and very very clean. Hilton once again lives up to its reputation in this regard.
The breakfast buffet is also wonderful, and I would encourage others to add it to your room reservation when you book. They only added $-- total to our bill for - breakfast buffets, and I saw that they charge $-- per person if you just go in and order the buffet in person. The cooks were extremely friendly, and the spread for breakfast was quite extensive, with plenty of hot, cooked-to-order food and tons of fresh fruit, etc.
I would stay at this hotel again in a heartbeat, and will probably return again the next time I'm in Memphis. If you do the same, you will NOT be disappointed....

I stay at a lot of Hampton Inns for business and I would rate this property as """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""O.K."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" This immediately followed being approached by a person in the parking lot begging for money--not all that comfortable when you are wheeling luggage and expensive computer equipment. We were told by the front desk clerk that they had been having problems with people accosting guests in the parking lot asking for money and they were working on upgrading their security measures. Until they can confidently control this, I would not recommend this property for a woman travelling alone.

This hotel is absolutely gorgeous. The rooms are lovely, the beds are really comfortable. The hotel restaurant is located right off of the Riverwalk, and has a great menu. The hotel itself is located on the Riverwalk and right downtown San Antonio. The prices are a bit high but we got a great deal, so keep your eyes open. Also, the parking was $---day which was a lot so we parked right across the street where there is public parking for just $--day.

Having just spent a week at this superb hotel, my wife and I agree that the hotel is one of the best city hotels in which we have stayed. However what does come across is that the training given to all levels of staff is self-evident. The ethos of customer service at this hotel is taken to a new level of excellence. Well done, special note of concierge staff, they are the tip of the iceberg of the aforementioned excellence.
If you get a chance to come to this eccentric city, do stay here, you will have a hotel in the best location, with rooms that have size and equipment to match the service.
If you get time, visit Muir Woods and Sausalito. Travel by cable car and stand on the running board - hang on tight!
Our appreciation of the hotel limo and the great public transport system was tempered by the number of drop-outs begging on the streets. Not seen in NYC.

My wife and I stayed here March -- for - nights. Check-in was a breeze. Rooms were decent size with nice beds and TV, but definitely showed wear, especially the bathroom. Hotel location was ok, about a - minute walk to the restaurants and bars of downtown. Hotel restaurant (Shula's) not very good. Breakfast was overpriced for a pretty mediocre buffet. Second night I had to listen to the bartenders argue over which one of them should leave their shift while the manager (Paul, I think) just stood there while they argued. Apparantly they aren't making much in tips and I had to hear all about it.
We were gone all day on Saturday and when we returned around -:-- room was still not cleaned. Maid saw us go in and then knocked and asked if she could clean. I just took fresh towels as we both wanted to shower, not wait for her to finally clean the room.
Overall, decent hotel with decent location. Next time I'll try Hilton which has a much better location.
TIP: Try Zambrano's (short walk) for a great dinner and excellent wine selection. The owner was extremely friendly and service was excellent.

It is a very nice, ornate old hotel but...
I stayed there because it was an overflow hotel for a conference I was attending. It was an unseasonably warm time in DC and as such the hotel and especially my room was HOT!!!!.
When I spoke with staff, they were understanding but said there was nothing they could do about it apparently it's either heat or AC, not both and I guess it was heat time. They put a fan in my room, but it did not help.
Also I use a wheelchair and while they made a attempt to make the place accessible, it was with ramps that followed the slope of the stairs,in other words, ski jumps.

I've stayed at this Hampton several times now, and the only bad experience I have had is the one mentioned in another review--noise from the bar next door. This time I was on the other side of the hotel so I didn't hear anything, but I'm not sure anything was going on, either. This property is located in a part of Jacksonville that is now coming apart almost as fast as it boomed. For example, the nearby Starbucks had closed, along with several of the nearby chain restaurants, and there is an abandoned, half-completed strip shopping center right next to the hotel. This may be a reason the room rates were so cheap. In any event the property itself was fine, and remained clean and well-maintained, though it seemed rather empty. At some point I would expect either a crime spike or a closing of this property as there is no need for it now, but in the meantime, take advantage of it. Incidentally, it is a bit difficult to find as it doesn't really face the street; it shares a common driveway with the Fairfield Inn next door.

Room was large & clean. Bathroom was also large & clean. Couldn't understand why the coffee maker was in the bathroom but it was a quirk that was amusing. Location is handy for Universal Studios. Parking a car at the Hilton is costly but driving is necessary in LA if you want to get around. Location was close to public transport but connections in LA seemed difficult. We stayed & drove to Disneyland. The restaurant we felt was overpriced & the food wasn't that great. There is a much better diner at the bottom of the hill & around the corner that was fantatsic for breakfast. The service that we received on the front desk was great - even when we had to check out in the middle of the night to get to the airport at -am. We stayed as we got a promotional rate & we thinking we might do Universal. If you want to go to Disneyland probably better to stay out there. Handy though for the Hollywood walk, etc.

This was a trip to take my granddaughter to NYC to go shopping. The hotel is located in a great area, close to the tour buses and teenage shops. The room was brand new and on the -th floor with construction on the floor but a wonderful room. Of course, we faced a brick wall from our window but in NYC that's what you expect. We appreciated the room """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""fridge"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to store our leftover pizza and water bottles. I usually stay at Hilton's, but found this hotel was more reasonably priced for the area. The room was clean, bright and the kitchen area was well stocked. I would definitely stay here again.

The hotel had so much going on that night but it never felt crowded. We had a great breakfast the next morning. It is close to everything you need downtown. I would reccommend it to anyone.

Let me start by saying the staff were cordial and efficient. Our disappoint was not with them. The room we had was in need of an update. We were on the fifth floor. The bath tub faucet was loose as was the rusting cover for the shower curtain. Running water would gather unless the drain plug was removed. I stayed at this hotel for a business convention and they handled us well. The room was fine (clean, well appointed) but the facilities downstairs were a little worn (chipped counters, stained sinks, leaking pipes in the restrooms near the ballroom).

Easy checkin.
$-- cab ride from Love Field (includes tip)

While the room was located on the -rd floor, looking onto a small flat area of the roof, it was very comfortable and quiet. The carpet is a little worn and decor was dated but OK. It was a last minute accomodation and they probably did not have the original conference block of rooms available. Delightful surprise when room service was quick, and food was hot and delicious. The crab cakes were outstanding.
Excellent location for a visit and so many dining options within walking distance. The ballroom conference setting weathered the earthquake well but the chandeliers did rock and sway dangerously. 
Drinks in lobby bar were poor.

The resort is beautiful especially at night with the extra special lighting in the canyon. Everyone who works at this resort from the doorman and housekeepers to the grounds keepers smile and acknowledge you. There is a total """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""can do, will do, we want to"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" attitude....it is so refreshing in this day and age.
You pay more at this resort but you get ALOT back.
When you are looking for the extra special place to stay The Grand Del Mar will not disappoint.

I stayed here for one night and it was a pleasant experience. I was able to check in an hour early. The room was typical Marriott. The location was ideal. I walked from there to South Street and then took a cab back for $- . I would not drive there again because valet was $-- a night. The hotel bar is huge and the drinks were good and reasonable priced. My highlight...Starbucks in the lobby!

We stayed on a holiday trip. We arrived on the --th of December and left on the --rd of December. The staff was wonderful,smiling and very friendly. They were extremely professional. The valet staff was really nice. I do not have a complaint about the hotel itself. I didn't have to want for anything. The courtyard was beauitful at night as well as the terrace looking onto the Riverwalk. Amanda T. was great. I would stay again.

I stayed for one night at this hotel becasue EVERYTHING else was pretty much booked in Arboretum and I wasn't sure of staying in Austin Downtown since it was my fist time to the city and I didn't know long things were away from each other.
The hotel does not have a swimming pool> it's close to a highway and it's right next to the mall and cinema. I actually walked to (a HUGE) Whole Foods - it's only - minutes walk, if that.

If you have no other place to stay, this is OK but I would probably look for something a little better..

I found this hotel to be very clean and in a good location. The staff was very helpful and friendly and were always smiling. The room was small, but nicely decorated and had all of the amenities you would need. The beds were comfy. It is a nice, trendy hotel that I would recommend for couples, friends, for business. Also, we had to get room service one evening and it was quite tasty!

My wife, infant daughter and I had the pleasure of being in Washington D.C over the President's Day weekend. I chose the W hotel based mainly on its proximity to the White House, Smithsonian, Washington momument etc. as well as the positive reviews I'd read here. This property is truly fantastic, and despite not being recommended as a family hotel, we did not have any issues in that regard. Two items of note: No pool; and, as with hotels in this class, room service is pricey. 
I would not hesitate to recommend this property to others, and will indeed stay here again when in the D.C area.

We stayed at this hotel for a weekend so we could explore DC. we loved that it was a suite because there were - adults and - child so it was very nice to have the extra room. the building itself is relatively modern, although the rooms seemed a little older, but were clean, so we were happy with that. it was nice to have a kitchen area complete with silverware, dishes, coffee pot (Keurig!), pans, sponge and soap. our main complaint is the PARKING! the first night we were there, we arrived around -p, so there was a spot for us in the miniscule parking lot behind the hotel (probably holds about -- cars max). but the next night, we arrived back around --p and there was no open spot. we circled the hotel and searched for street parking, but nothing. after about -- min of that, we ended up having to park about -- blocks away in the garage for the Hilton. The fee to park - hrs overnight was $--! now in defense of the hotel, they did tell us before hand that if there was no parking, we would have to make use of a public garage. HOWEVER, they said the garage was - blocks away (it was --!), and the fee was $-- (it was $--). of course the next morning when we picked up the car, we returned to the hotel and demanded a refund. they said they had no idea that the price went up (first of all, if you are recommending these garages to guests, you should be aware of the correct pricing!) and they could not refund us, since pricing was at the garage's discretion, not the hotels. they should really come to some sort of deal with the garage for their guests. on the up side, they did give us a free breakfast as a compensation. that was very nice, but it didnt make up for the inconvienence of having to walk so far at night in a strange area, with an infant, and again in the morning. think again about staying here if you have a car...

I have to agree with others who have reviewed the Hyatt. The hotel is very nice and the staff is very friendly and accommodating, but.....
There are little things that you shouldn't find at Hyatt, mostly just an attention to detail things.

Like:
 My room had not been thoroughly dusted, the desk was dusty, the lampshades were crooked. The coffee bar was not open one morning, then open the next day. 
I use a wheelchair and stayed in an accessible room, but it appeared that the room isn't used much (see above dusting comment).
Rooms were not made up until very late (-:--) in the afternoon.
I paid a conference rate for the room, which made the value OK, but if I paid full rate I would say that it would not be worth it.
I do want to mention that the staff was excellent.. they addressed requests immediately, they always greeted you with a smile and were quite friendly.
If they can address those small things, the hotel would be a much better experience.
My one pet peeve, not just with the Hyatt, but most hotels... 
In an wheelchair accessible room, please make sure that the shower head is put in a lower position, if we have to use a wheelchair, that usually meansd we can't stand up to lower the shower....

Nice location, beautiful view. However, the desk person was very unprofessional. During two conversations with him while trying to switch rooms, he mentioned that we had booked through a -rd party while rolling his eyes and making his disgust look. The person in front of us was asking for the same thing, he treated her very well, even offered to move her while she went out. It was my honeymoon and we had a wonderful time. This hotel is right in the heart of all the attractions. It is family friendly which is important to us. Not to far from union station, eateries and attractions such as the Shedd aquarium. My husband and I truly enjoyed ourselves and the best part was when the night was over we came to the hotel for great eats and felt as if we were home.

We booked a Friday night stay at the Doubletree Metropolitan, November is a notoriously busy month for hotels in Manhattan, and although we normally prefer to stay at the W - the cost was prohibitive right before the Holidays . We thought $--- for a king executive room was decent, and the hotel was not disappointing. The Doubletree is not a - star property, it is a - star and a good one at that. I've stayed at several other NYC hotels, paid more, and gotten far less. If I were a traveler on a budget, I'd definitely opt to stay here again.

Just a quick overnight with spouse. XV is beautiful and the location is fantastic. The room was lovely, clean and very comfortable. Bathroom very nice with plenty of room for personal toiletries. Staff very helpful. Concierge cool. In the summer I would imagine that the rooftop terrace is just gorgeous. This is the kind of place you would love to call home. If we ever get to Boston again it's a no brainer. We will stay at XV.

The smell of mildew in the rooms has to be covered, so the Air Conditioner units have an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""air freshener"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" smell blasting through the fan. I traveled to Dallas recently on business and my colleagues and I were all thrilled with our accommodations at the Stoneleigh Resort & Spa. We visited Los Angeles for our first overnight in the metropolis, and chose the Omni for proximity to the event we were attending. Little did we know that we were about to encounter a level of service which can go head-to-head against any of the competitors.

We are looking forward to the updating of the rooms, and will be visiting the Omni whenever an overnight in Los Angeles is in the books.

The Boston Sheraton is walking distance to many great attractions, such as Fenway Park, Newbury Street, Boston Commons... we walked an hour to Harvard Square in Cambridge, in September, and the weather was fine! The hotel lobby connects to a great variety of restaurants and boutiques and you might spend a whole day at the mall next door!
 The rooms were quiet and the bed nice, though, we would have liked a bigger bathroom. There was no safe in the room either, but that's okay. There was instant Starbucks coffee in the room every morning! Plus, the internet service in the lobby was great!

I stayed here in September ----. I had a reservation for - nights, but left after the first night. The room was cramped, and looked and smelled none too clean. Carpets were stained. The hotel was in a good location, with free breakfast and helpful staff. We have stayed at the Four Seasons in Hampshire, England so I was expecting the same experience here in Philadelphia. It didn't knock me off off my feet!

I wouldn't stay here again in Philadelphia. Next time, I will save some money and opt for the Double Tree.

I'm still not sure what 's Mediterranean about Seattle's Medterranean Inn on lower Queen Anne, but I was pleasantly surprised to have had an experience superior to the usual highway chain motels for less than $---. Hotel as such is not good but service when things go wrong are not at the standard a - star hotel should have. Stayed here for one night in August. I had locked all my valuables away, apart from my blackberry, which I foolishly left on the table. I went for a walk and when I came back the blackberry had gone. This is an AWESOME hotel. The room service is excellent. You are --- block from Times Square. If you want to have fun at night, there's a nightclub downstairs. But yet it's also quiet! If you bring a car, not only do they have valet parking, but they also are right next to a parking garage if you want to park yourself. Also, despite what some other reviews say, the rooms are very large (I travel a lot for work so I would know a small room when I see it). And did I mention you're right at Times Square??!!! My stay at Stay was just wonderful! I highly recommend this hotel.

The title describes my experience. The rooms are on good size for a couple, are clean, quiet and you feel safe. Noticed on previous reviews that many guests had problems with the elevators, we didn't experience any problems even on rush hours (breakfast, check-out). I was a little worried about staying in the hotel because of all of the negative reviews I'd read, but I'm glad I did. First and most importantly, the main reason to stay here is the location. Union Sqaure is within walking distance, and Chinatown and the North End are close as well. The hotel itself is fairly small, and the carpet and furnishings are definitely old, but the bathroom and bedsheets were clean. If you're going to spend a lot of time in the hotel, this probably isn't the place for you, but if you only need a place to stay, it works out fine.  My biggest complaint was the street noise, which was very loud during the night. However, overall, the location can't be beat for the price, and though it's not the most luxurious place, it's very suitable for a short stay.

Stayed here on my way home from a family trip, time away for my wife and I. It had a wonderful location in downtown Indy. If I had paid a premium rate for the club access, I would have been extremely disappointed. Breakfast was nice, I was late getting there (after posted hours), but they still had enough that I was satisfied and it was well prepared. The gentleman that staffed the breakfast was very helpful.
The room was nice, plenty of room for two and the bed was comfortable, but the refrigerator situation was weird, never used it but never really figured out what it was all about. The bathroom was very small, adequate for the two of us, but smaller than in any of the last -- hotels that I have stayed at, again I was warned in a prior review, so not surprised. Finally, another funny point, there was only one bathrobe available (even though the reservation was for two adults), luckily my wife desired one and I did not, could have been problematic if we both wanted it.
Overall, nice, clean and we had a good deal, would stay there again under the same circumstances, but would not want to pay more than we did.

There is no way this hotel is legal. Fire exits were blocked with ladders and mops. Rooms are smaller than a jail cell. They are position walls with no ceiling so not even a real room. A girl would feel very unsafe here. Never ever stay at this hotel it would be better to stay on street

The real treasure to this location is you are three minutes from downtown and you can walk to several great restaurants: Charthouse, Morton's or Ruth Chris. This is the real winner for me and why I'll stay here again.

a wonderful restoration of one of Chicago's oldest buildings...warm, intimate rooms (somewhat small), superb service!,,,good food in a dazzling dining room,,great location across from Macy's in the Loop..,just a pleasure in every way

We booked this hotel at the last minute solely based on its proximity to family. We had zero expectations, which was good, because our stay was only so-so. As others have noted, the lobby, bar and Pump Room have all been beautifully re-done. The sitting area near the coffee bar is great. But at night, because this is basically all one big open space, the bar ends up taking over the place and people crowd the whole area. Not a big deal, but it did make coming and going a bit annoying as you're pushing your way through people just to get to the elevator bank. (I'd also say that though we saw some families with young kids, it definitely does not have a family-friendly vibe.)
Our room was very spacious, but the design doesn't make very good use of the space. There is one tiny closet and - drawers for all of your clothes—no dresser. Also, the bed, which is very hard, is basically on the floor. We were on the --th floor (yes, the first place I've ever stayed where they actually have a --th floor!) which gave us a nice view and we appreciated the black out curtains to block the sun in the morning. Bathroom was fairly small, but nicely done. The real problem is the noise: the doors and walls are basically paper thin. We heard people at all hours—talking in the hallways, talking as they came off the elevator, talking (and more than that) coming from the room next door. We had to be up early pretty much every morning we were there and felt exhausted by the time we left.
On the plus side: The Public has one of the nicest hotel gyms I've ever seen. Brand new equipment, nice view, very light, the room the right temperature. We also enjoyed a breakfast at the Pump Room and loved the convenience of being able to grab a quick to-go breakfast from the coffee bar.
All in all, though the location is ideal for us, I probably won't stay here again. I value my sleep too much!

I was recently affected by the west coast power outage and was forced to stay the night in Houston, TX. After searching nearby options, I chose them for their -- hr shuttle, Marriott name and proximity to the airport (especially since I had to return - hrs later). The shuttle driver wa great. Overall this was a great place to lay my head on an unplanned stop in Houston. So good I never heard a plane nor was I awakened by one.

We love the beds and showers and got a complimentary upgrade to the newly refinished Atrium Club which was a terrific perk! Espresso, fresh fruit and oatmeal for breakfast and snacks and drinks in the afternoon. A delightful stay!

I can't say enough about the staff and accomodations at the Hotel Giraffe!! Friendly, helpful, courteous, and knowledgeable staff. Great location. I would highly recommend the Hotel Giraffe. I will certainly be staying there again on my next visit to the Big Apple!!

I was only in NYC for one night, and I stayed in a King room in the Millenium Hilton. Check in was quick, and the clerk was super friendly. I was a little nervous when I arrived to my room, because it was facing the World Trade Center site, and I thought the construction may be noisy. The room couldn''t have been quieter! I chose this hotel based on its size, location and price but it fell short in my eyes on all three levels.
First off, our junior suite was an OK size, it looked like a former apartment with a cramped full kitchen and tiny bath, plus a small living room that unfortunately wasn't separated from the bedroom. Despite its size though, the entire place felt dated (think """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""----s chic"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" without the chic) and thus not at all comfortable. I thought it would be a place my family could hang out and relax in between sightseeing but we couldn't be out of there long enough. The carpet constantly felt dirty and there was still food in the dish strainer when we checked in. Some of the glasses felt greasy upon first use. The trash can lid in the kitchen was broken and the TV was the old-style big-box model type that wasn't very sensitive to the remote control. We woke up with bites after our first night but I checked for bedbugs and didn't find any and my husband guessed that perhaps there were dust mites instead as parts of the room did feel rather dusty and caused his allergies to act up. 
As for the location, I didn't find it convenient at all, and I love to walk. The closest subway is Grand Central, which is great for food but the lines that run through there weren't main ones so we almost always had to transfer anyway. Plus, I thought that being out of Times Square would mean a quieter room but I guess because the building is so old and the walls are so thin, you can hear everything, such as the ambulances wailing by and cars honking below. I could even hear our neighbors' running water or when people were talking outside in the hallway. Speaking of the hallway, it always reeked of smoke, even though the building is supposed to be nonsmoking. Even the elevator smelled like smoke sometimes too.
I guess you get what you pay for though because the price isn't too bad considering its size and that, after everything, is a hotel room in New York. Still, I think we could pay a similar price for a nicer, albeit smaller, more conveniently located room elsewhere.
One other thing I should mention is the staff. While the housekeeping staff was quite friendly and always greeted us, the front desk staff could've cared less when we were standing right in front of them and the doormen-bellmen always looked like they'd rather be anywhere else but helping customers. It was as if we were an inconvenience to them for staying there. I also thought it was odd that although checkin is at -, we arrived at --- and were told our room wasn't ready yet. Now I know we were early, but it was less than an hour before checkin. We've arrived at other hotels as early as - a.m. and have been shown to our room right away; this was one of the rare times we were unable to check in early and although I know it's never a given, just the fact that it was so close to checkin time anyway but were denied makes me wonder.
All in all, next time, I'd stay elsewhere. The good thing was that since we were out so much, we saw everything on our itinerary, plus more, so I guess that's something, right?

Wish I'd read the Trip Advisor reviews before booking but I figured such a great hotel would be a safe bet - I was wrong. I am not sure what is the best hotel I have visited recently, but I am clear on the worst. The Knickerbocker is a dump! Whoever gave this - diamonds should be shot!

My only complaint was the parking, you have to pay for it - though there was a convenient service of $-- a day to go in and out a smuch as you like, otherwise it was $-- every time you left. 
Overall I would recomend the hotel and say it would be a safe bet for anyone visiting the Jacksonville area.

We HIGHLY recommend staying at this quaint hotel - which has a cute courtyard area. The parking is great, with no problems and no additional charges for parking. Laundry facilities are available.
A GREAT place to stay when visiting SAN DIEGO - enjoy!
The BED is amazing as well. :)

I lived in NYC for years, and after deciding to take my husband on his first trip to the Big Apple I searched long and hard for the perfect hotel - I was looking for something small and intimate under $--- per night with all of the usual amenities and a central location. I usually prefer an independent, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""artsier"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" place to the larger chain hotels but I also don't like to experiment when I'm spending this kind of money. However, the descriptions I read of The Muse piqued my interest and I decided to take a chance, booking a standard room with a king sized bed for our five night stay.
When we arrived at about --:-- pm on a Tuesday night, concierge-bellman Igor met us at the front desk and was extremely friendly, helpful and courteous as he escorted us to our room, on the way providing us with a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Time Out New York"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" magazine which was very useful. Much to our surprise and delight, the hotel had upgraded us to a deluxe room with a HUGE balcony (almost unheard of in New York). The room was extremely clean and decorated in an understated, attractive and modern theme. For a New York hotel room, it was large with plenty of room for myself and my husband and a LOT of luggage. The bed was EXTREMELY comfortable and the room was unbelievably quiet considering its' proximity to Times Square - we heard little to no street noise except on Saturday night when a band played at a nearby Irish bar, and we only heard that because we had our balcony door open.
The hotel is in fabulously close proximity to all of the Broadway theaters, good restaurants and subway stations. Although we did not eat at the hotel (too many other choices), there is a restaurant there called The District which has gotten excellent reviews and based on the menu sounds fabulous. Most of the staff was very helpful and attentive, although some of the front desk employees were a little icy, which certainly could have just been a function of how busy they were. 
Overall we had an excellent experience at The Muse, and my only issues are somewhat insignificant in the scheme of things. For one, we could not control the temperature in our room despite the presence of a thermostat, and had to sleep with our balcony door open to keep from roasting at night. I also think that the hotel should provide free in-room internet connection in the more deluxe rooms - for the price of the room it seems a little tacky to charge $-- per day for """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""noon to noon"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" (an utterly inconvenient schedule for travelers who need to handle morning business matters) service. 
In short, I highly recommend this hotel for anyone looking for proximity to the theater district in an upscale, intimate setting. This probably wouldn't be the best place for families with small children (stick with the bigger hotels), but for everyone else The Muse is a great choice!

I went to NYC for business trip. I stayed at Waldorf Tower where is located in the prime area of NYC.
The hotel is really nice and comfortable. The room layout is alike an apartment with elegant decoration. 
The Tower entrance is just around the corner of the Hotel entrance which is a little bit complicated to find.

We came here for our honeymoon in Aug. ----. This hotel is very clean, the staff are so nice. The entire area is so beautiful. The weather was perfect. We rented a car, absolutely the best thing we did. San Diego has so much to offer. We will definitely be back!!!!!

The hip modern design is fun but the hotel could pay more attention to details. For example, there is no comfortable reading chair with good light. The dark wood floors have a European feel and the shower is large and easy to use. We had to have the keys redone at the main desk but other than that, everything was O.K. We didn't use the pool or the fitness center but they looked nice. I enjoyed having an espresso in the large lobby with the dramatic curving ramp. The location is good for Queen Anne hill and the value is excellent.

I like Westins, I always have. However, in the past I would have considered this to be one of the WORST Westins I had ever stepped foot in. On a recent visit it was nice to see that this hotel is getting a makeover-update.... it is in need!
Westins in general are great, so I am hoping this one ends up being that way. I could tell that my room was recently spruced up as it was comfortable. 
I was dissapointed in the cleaning of the room. End tables had been pulled out during cleaning and not pushed back up against the walls etc, and the floors were not vacuumed, however the bathroom was spotless.

This is one of the three pet-friendly Kimpton hotels in Seattle. The others are the Monaco and the Hotel Vintage Park. All three are nice and they all have an afternoon wine tasting. Anyway, back to the Alexis. The service was excellent and the room decor--like the Monaco--was a little eclectic and a nice change from the normal corporate closet. We had our little dog with us, and they had a welcome sign in front of her hotel with her name on it. We were pleasantly surprised to find food and water bowls and a dog bed when we got to the room. It's a perfect location and is close to the ferries and the market. I'm not sure how to rate the price, since that is very subjective. For the deluxe king room I paid $---, which I thought was cheap. I would highly recommend this hotel and I plan on going back.

Arriving at the hotel the staff already had our keys to the room in place, so we just had to present our credit cards in case of any extra charges. Since I am a Keep in Touch member I had a $ -- credit in the mini bar. Keep in Touch members also have free internet acess. By the way, the speed connection is very good. The attendent was very polite and provide us very useful information, such as how to get the bus to Georgetown.
The continental breakfast is actually better than most american hotels with many options to choose. Every day from - to - p.m. the hotel offers free wine (red or white) and they kindly welcome guest to enjoy their wine at the bar.
Altough they don’t have a fitness center they offer a free pass to YCMA just a few steps away.
All staff members are very polite and kind, this make a difference and I would definitely would go back to the Topaz. Thanks for all your smiles!

The common areas are very nice, and the building has a very elegant feel to it. 
However, for the premium rates, there is SO much better to be had. A hotel that aspires to call itself """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""luxury"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" and charges the rates they do should not have so many annoyances.
A few examples:
 - The faucet in the bathroom leaked badly.
 - There was no water pressure in the shower. The only way to get water to reach you was to set the showerhead to that annoying """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""massage-paint chipper"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" mode. All other settings resulted in a dribble that extended no more than an inch.
 - The room was small and cramped
 - There is no power outlet near the *single* nightstand.
 - Walls are paper-thin - not only can you hear every conversation and door slamming in the very long hallways, you'd better be prepared to know far more about your neighbors than you probably want to. Every word, cough, sneeze and episode of flatulence will be yours to enjoy with them.
 - The HVAC controls were right by the door, rather than in the main part of the room. Meaning that it took the thermostat a long time to register temperature changes. This resulted in a continuous freeze-fry cycle in temperatures in the room.
And all of this was from an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""upgraded"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" deluxe room, or whatever they call it.
And the absolute crowning glory: They charge you twenty bucks a day for wifi. 
Seriously? Better check your calendars guys, because charging guests for wifi is going the way of the dodo bird. And even ignoring that, the rate is borderline criminal. 
I called the front desk to confirm that appalling fact, and talked to a snooty young man who told me that yes, they really do charge that much, it was corporate policy, and there was nothing they could do about it. He then said """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""have a nice day"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""", AND HUNG UP ON ME.
I called back and asked to speak with the manager - I figured they would want to know that they have a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""training opportunity"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". The person I spoke with who identified themselves as the manager, assured me that his staff would never do that, and flat out said that I must have misunderstood. He made it very clear that there was no issue and I was wasting his time.
I can overlook most of the small gripes, but the rude treatment is simply inexcusable.
I will sleep in filthy urine soaked rags under a highway overpass before I give this hotel another nickel. Any future corporate event held here will have to make do without me.
If it weren't for excellent and well-managed nearby properties like the Le Meridien, I would be burning my Starwood Preferred card right now.

Hotel was beautiful, excellent service- note that this is a large resort- the nicest rooms are farthest from the restaurants-meeting rooms and lobby, but you cannot beat the bay view rooms if you can stay in them. Plus you can always call for the golf cart to come get you to take you anywhere around the property! Rooms need a few changes- tile floors made room chilly- probably not a problem in the summer, but in the winter time at night- made it chilly even with the heat on! Shower curtain was too short and water got all over the bathroom floor and made it slippery. For some reason housekeeping forgot to clean our room on -nd day- but was not that big of a deal. Was just odd because we had the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""Service Please"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" sign. Would definitely go back- food was also excellent! Internet was spotty in the conference space.

Quick and easy check in. Staff were lovely and very helpful. Our room was nice, not small but not large either. Clean and comfortable, although decor a little dated. Likewise with the bathroom. it was a decent size and clean. I liked the fact that a fridge was provided, there were laundry facilities on site and free internet for priority club members. Unfortunately we got to test out the evacuation procedures at - am when the fire alarm went off but that was nobody's fault! It was only a short walk to the train station which was great and the Smithsonian Air and Space Museum was right down the end of the street. Found that there weren't many places to eat nearby - but we were only here - nights so did not get too much time to explore. Fantastic hotel!

We arrived at the hotel at - in the morning and the staff went out of their way to get a room ready for us - hours before the official check in time. 
The hotel itself is a pretty standard Holiday Inn in terms of decor but it's clean and the location is perfect: literally opposite The Peabody. 
The reception staff were also really helpful with suggestions on where to eat, local shops etc. 
We looked at staying at The Peabody but the Holiday Inn was a good --- pounds cheaper and I'd recommend you save the money and spend it on having a good time. 
A word of warning about Memphis - be careful where you go. We made the mistake of walking to the Civil Rights Museum and it was pretty hairy. It may not look far on the map but get a cab. 
Also - the Sun Studios tour bus picks up on Beale Street so you don't need to make the treck out to the Studio to pick up the tour. Again, we made that mistake and it's a good mile walk through some not so great areas. 
Make sure you go to Graceland - it's amazing!

My husband and I just returned from a trip to SF and stayed - nights at the HI Express FW. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The hotel was extremely clean, had a wonderful breakfast, the staff was nice and the location was perfect. We stayed at another hotel in SF for the first part of our week (wanted to stay in two different areas while we were in the city) and this one far exceeded the other hotel. The breakfast was especially helpful and saved us at least $---$---day. The staff was very friendly and helpful; even helped book our shuttle bus ride back to the airport. The location was perfect because it was one or two blocks from the main attractions; close enough to be very convenient yet not too close to all of the hustle and bustle. Overall, this was an excellent hotel and I would highly recommend it.

I stayed at this hotel because it was the least expensive ($----night!) hotel available during my reunion weekend. My other choices were both near or over $----night, so it was a no-brainer to stay here. 
The staff were very friendly, and accommodated my request for an early check-in. If you're in town to see the historic sights, you won't find a better location -- it can't be more than - blocks from Independence Hall. Overnight parking is $-- for guests, which I think is a pretty good deal for the location. 
But the place looks a bit run-down, and the plumbing in my room wasn't the greatest -- the toilet kept making noises, and my shower drain didn't work. I didn't realize the shower problem until I was running late for an appointment and didn't have time to call the front desk, so I can't report on how the hotel would have responded. In all, I got what I needed -- a clean, serviceable hotel in town, but I would not want to stay here for a special occasion.

Where else but at the Habitat will you be surrounded by plants and birds, have your own fireplace (downstairs rooms only), get the sayings of the Buddha in your bedside table, use tiny sandalwood soaps, and get a generous hot breakfast and Happy Hour with a vegan-vegetarian option? Love this place.....Quiet time after -:-- p.m., friendly staff, big rooms. Child and pet-friendly.

This hotel is all about having a great location a block off Beale Street. It is a decent hotel, but there is nothing special about the place. At $--- per night and $-- for valet parking, you expect something special. 
I had a wonderful view of a trash filled alley behind Beale Street - not what I expected for the price paid. I had an executive suite, but there was no lounge and the suite was a little larger than your standard Holiday Inn - all crammed into one room. 
It is expensive for what you get. If cost is an issue, there are a number of other comfortable hotels in the area that cost a lot less.

Looks like one of the newer Holiday Inns, but renovations haven't been done inside. Rooms are small, breakfast area is small, tubs are small, beds are small. Air conditioning loud and thermostat doesn't work correctly. 
Staff could use some training in basic customer service. Check-in desk employee was more interested in watching whatever was on TV behind the wall then getting my room correct or giving me any information at all on the property. 
On the plus side: Location was easy to find and the mini-fridge worked great and was a good size. 
Better hotels in the area, go a couple more exits on the highway and find one.

Great find in the Galleria area. Set back off the road and very quite for a large urban area. The decor was a tropical theme which was a little quirky. Rooms were clean and updated. he only complaint I had was the shower head spray was not adjustable. Pleanty of parking and walking distance to shopping. Attentive friendly staff. Definately will go back.

Hotel Giraffe was perfect for us! They provided cocktails and appetizers each evening and a European style breakfast each morning at no additional cost. Sarah was great at mapping out our days-restaurants. The rooms were really large considering we were in NYC and very close to the train stop. Each employee was very friendly and always tried to greet us by name. I would definitely recommend this hotel!

We had a corner suite with a separate bedroom and wrap around balcony. The furnishings were well appointed and the bathroom was all marble, but the entire suite really needed a good cleaning and that doesn't include the housekeeper that just walked into the suite while I was undressing. I would have enjoyed this suite a little more if it hadn't been for the BED BUGS! Was really difficult to try and sleep. 
Also, you feel imprisoned on the property, it is difficult to just walk off the property the way it is situated and there is no self-park you must valet and that gets to be a little too much everytime you need to leave and have to wait for your car. 
I wish I could recommend this property, but I found it to be a real turn off!

I really wanted to love this hotel and some aspects I did, but and there is a big but it depends on the room and floor you get. It's location is fabulous,aesthetically very pleasing and the attached museum a big hit with our kids. Visited here with another family of four in Easter ----. We were both located on the -rd floor, our friends with a nice view over the park but our first room, yes first room was on top of Starbucks at the back of the hotel and facing the Irish bar. I have no issues with the bar across the road apart from not wishing to feel I'm sleeping in the middle of the dance floor! The sound proofing in this conversion is questionable, we could here the next room guy coughing like he was sat next to us and the dog barking is another story!
We ended being moved to three different rooms in the middle of the night because of the noise levels. 
This is a beautiful hotel with lots of positives. However, ensure a positive stay by avoid staying on the third floor, kids, families and dogs floor!! Rooms do smell and your not advised if a dog has been in the room before hand so make sure you don't have allergies.
Would I stay here again?? Sorry no Id spend my £----.-- for - nights somewhere else!!

The room was small (no where to put room service tray). I stayed in a non-smoking room, but when sitting at my computer I could often smell smoke from other rooms. The Business Center is a FARCE! It is stated as an amenity on the website, but you have to pay .-- per minute and also pay .-- for each page of printing. They screw you by using VERY slow Internet. There are restaurants in walking distance - which I would recommend because the food choices are limited, overpriced($-.-- for water from machine!), and not that good. """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""High speed internet"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" in rooms is free, but incredibly slow and gets bogged down during hours when other guests must be using it.
I have been staying here for years and find it comfortable and welcoming. Good service, conveniently located. It's not cheap, but that's SF.

My husband, two sons (-- and --) and I stayed here for a week from --th July. The hotel is just off Union Square. Round the corner is where the Powell & Market tram turns to head back to Fishermans Wharf. A couple of minutes walk and you are in Union Square where the City Bus Tours start, where you can pick up various buses to get around the sites on your own and where you will find Macys plus loads of other shops. Out of Union Square at the far corner is the enterance to China Town. Great location. 
The hotel rooms were large enough for two people. They were nicely decorated and furnished, they had queen sized comfortable, clean beds. The rooms were cleaned daily with new bed linen and towels. 
Not that it was watched very much - usually for an update on the weather - but the TVs in both our rooms were old and ours didn't work too well. There was tea-coffee making facilities in the room but no milk or coffeemate? and sad as I am, but I really have to say it - the windows were dirty!! in a lovely hotel like this with lovely drapes and blinds - why didn't they clean them? 
We used the restaurant attached to the hotel called The Daily Grill for breakfast every morning, they had a good selection, the food was good and the staff were friendly. We had lunch and dinner on one occasion and the food and service could not be faulted. If you plan to have dinner best to book a table just to be on the safe side.
The hotel has an outdoor heated pool and a sauna - but we did not use it. The reception and lobby were nicely decorated and there was an internet """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""room"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". It is a lovely hotel in a great location and I would recommend it.

Our one night stay was absolutely wonderful! It was more than we expected. The only negative is: This Super - is a former Best Western hotel. We arrived after dark & passed up the hotel because we couldn't see a Super - sign but the old Best Western sign. When we made the block & arrived at it a second time, we looked & saw a Super - sign over the Best Western sign. Because of the darkness we had not originally seen the Super - sign.
Since we arrived late & the hotel was quite full by the time we arrived, the desk clerk upgraded our reservation from - king size bed to a suite, all at no extra charge. It had more than we needed, including a small refrigerator w-freezer, microwave, & coffeemaker. The room was very clean; we even performed a quick 'inspection' upon arriving, & could only find cleanliness. The bed was very comfortable. The continental breakfast included cereal, muffins, boiled eggs, sausage, biscuits, juice & cold milk. The lady at the front desk working the night shift was very nice & helpful with a great attitude. Did I mention we found a superb price on the internet?
We would definitely stay there again & recommend it to others.

We stayed three nights in the Hotel Adagio, San Francisco at the end of our California trip. Our deluxe queen-sized room was booked through expedia with our third night free. This made the hotel excellent value. Even more so when compared to our hotels in Santa Monica, Santa Barbara, and Big Sur.
We had returned our rental car on arrival in SF, so no hassle with valet parking and the like. Haven't tried the Cortez restaurant or hotel breakfast so can't comment on that.
We explored SF by bus, tram and on foot, thanks to the hotel's great central location near Union Square. We found the staff friendly, attentive and helpful.
No problems with noise from hallway or other rooms. The bathroom was much larger than expected. And we liked the modern decor of the hotel.
Free wi-fi in the lobby, cabled ADSL in the rooms, and two computers with internet downstairs.
All in all a hotel we can definitely recommend.

My experience at this hotel was absolutely great. I checked-in at -am and they were able to accommodate me right away. Tstar tire staff were very friendly and courteous. The room is spacious with a separate living area, walk in closet-change area and fairly big bathroom. The fitness centre is fairly big and well equipped. I didn't have a chance to Gordon Ramsays restaurant at hotel but they were busy. The location is great and the subway is a block away. I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

Given the mixed reviews we were not sure what to expect. I have to say that we had a great time. The hotel is a typically anonymous conference style hotel with a dark and somewhat depressing reception and slow front desk service. Our - adjoining rooms on the --th floor were really good. The beds were comfortable, the views excellent and with all the facilities you would expect. The gym is big and the pool, whilst not so big ,was enough to keep the kids happy. We used the sun terrace and the jacuzzi. And the location is great. So not the place to go if you are looking for character or special hotel experience, but it really did the job for us.

I live in a big city, and am used to sleeping in noisy conditions, but this was just too much. The windows in the rooms are not properly sealed and you can hear ALL the street noise. I'm not talking about not being able to take a nap in the after-noon, which is maybe too much to ask in a city like NY. I'm talking about - AM. A truck comes to pick up the laundry from the Marriot next door. It looks and operated like a big garbage truck. Hydraulically lifts carts full of laundry, dumps it into the truck than drops the carts back on the ground. This goes on for about -- min at -am. No ear plugs can mask that noise.
In all other aspects the hotel is great. Great location, very spacious rooms (not just compared to NY hotels) and very friendly and helpful staff.
I do hope they will do something about soundproofing the windows before the next time I'm in NY, so that I won't have to search for a different hotel.

Super comfy beds, staff helped with bookings and car rentals and printing. - to -- minute walk to Union Square (main shopping & transport hub) and Market Street. Very pet friendly, didn't have time to eat there so don't know about the food but everything else was great. Recent construction works were nearly complete but we didn't notice a thing. Not supermodern, more of a character hotel. Good price online.

Great hotel, lively bar and lounge with a pool table, snack bar, indoor swimming pool and internet stations in the lobby. My wife and I left the kids behind and spent a night in Charlotte. We arrived on Saturday evening, for a - night stay, and we were greeted by a friendly, welcoming staff at the front desk. The rooms and location were perfect for our weekend plans. Great location to walk out and be in the middle of plenty of trendy bars and restaurants. We had a room on the --th floor and it was clean and modern with great views of uptown Charlotte. Nice shower, large tv mounted on the wall of the bedroom, cordless phones, safe, latest issues of popular magazines and a modern-trendy style room. 
Call ahead to get exact directions and cross streets of the parking deck from the hotels automated voice mail system. It seems other reviewers have had problems finding the garage. It’s actually not difficult to find. When we arrived, we told the garage attendant that we were staying at aloft and the fee was only $-- for -- hours to park. The attendant also provided clear instructions on location of the elevator that takes you to the hotels -th floor lobby. 
We didn't have any problems with noise outside of our room, within the hotel, or from the bars below. We didn't hear anything and slept great. It was clean and comfortable with a young, lively atmosphere with lots of energy. A perfect fit for the surrounding area of Uptown Charlotte.
We are usually super critical about the places that we stay and were thoroughly enjoyed aloft. We will definitely stay there again next time we visit Charlotte for the evening.

Not a bad little Best Western. We ended up staying here after finding the accommodations we had previously booked were less than advertised. This is a nice location in Old Town with plenty of shopping and restaurants in walking distance. And close to freeway with access to Zoo, Seaworld, etc. Parking for Bldg. - where we stayed was quite limited, but the room was large and clean with a sitting area, refrigerator and microwave. Service was good.

We stayed at the wellington for six nights last week we found the staff very helpful and the location cant be beaten. After reading some of the reviews we really didnt expect the hotel to be up to much but it was fine. I would have to agree with a previous reviewer on the surface the rooms are clean but they could do with cleaning behind and under the beds. We are planning to return to new york next year and will stay at the wellington. For value for money and location you will find it hard to beat.

I stayed at the Buckingham when visiting New York for the first time last October. Yes, the hotel is an older property with some of the things you expect in an older building (the electric wiring gives off a few sparks in the room, for example). But you need to balance that against the fact that the rooms are really spacious, it's great to have the kitchen available if you want to save some money, and most of all its location is perfect. You can walk to Central Park, to and down -th Avenue, to Time Square - and whn you want to go further afield there's a subway station at each end of the block. You couldn't have a better base for exploring New York. The staff on Reception are friendly and welcoming and happy to advise on where to go and how to get there.

Stayed here on business back in January and it was fine for one night. Much more likely would have driven me stir-crazy. Room was decent - good-sized and clean - but certainly could have used a facelift. Parking was - as noted in other reviews - a bit inconvenient. 
Look elsewhere in the neighborhood if you're staying near the Medical Centers. I certainly will next time.
I had a good exprience here I liked the fact that the funirture and stuff are very unique compared to other hotels of the marriot chain. I it was pleasent to have something different.

The Maxwell hotel is a perfect hotel for folks who wish to stay a little outside the Seattle core but still enjoy all Seattle has to offer. The neighborhood is full of restaurants all with in walking distance. The hotel itself was very clean with colorful well-decorated rooms and very helpfully staff. Free parking and WIFI is also available. Guests should note that the WIFI throughout the hotel is not using any sort of encryption meaning no id or passwords are required to access internet at the hotel. While this makes it easier for the non-techie sort to get online it does potentially leave guests open to security risks associated with an open connection. All in all we loved the Maxwell and hope to return again.
The breakfast was very limited. Only Fruit Loops and some other cereal, some disappointing sticky buns, and coffee. I couldn't even find any juice. No protein to speak of (yogurt? boiled egg?)

I don't know how such a big and busy hotel manages it, but the service at this place is off the charts. Every single person I encountered in my stay here made me feel welcome--kind, friendly, accommodating, and I had some out-there requests, such as last minute photocopies for a business meeting, getting a boarding pass after I'd already checked out, strange check-out times because interviews I was doing ran late. They didn't just get me what I needed, they did it with generosity and smiles. Wow. They are just doing it right at this place--the room felt luxurious, the spa was really well maintained--it is the kind of place that anticipates your needs and caters to them seamlessly. I can only add that the bar and restaurant are superb, with a gracious clubby feeling that also makes you feel welcome.

Hubby and I spent three week nights in early July at the Hotel Belleclaire and really could not have been happier! The room was beautiful, spacious, well maintained and comfortable, we had a fun view looking up and down Broadway and east toward Central Park, and the staff was friendly and professional.
We loved being so close to the Subway stop which made it easy for us to travel all over the city without ever needing a cab, and we also enjoyed feeling like we were in a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""real neighborhood"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""". We felt instantly at home and liked having so many restaurants and gourmet delis-groceries close by.
Someday we may have enough money to stay at one of the elaborate glass tower hotels, but unless something changes for the worse at the Hotel Belleclaire, we'll always stay there.

Negatives: cramped room, thin walls,tired looking furnishings,snooty conceirage,expensive for what you get....
Positives: great location,unbelievable water pressure in the shower. 
We stayed at this location a few years back and had an enjoyable stay...I don't recall the rooms being so small and lacking of any extras, ie refridgerator, coffee maker...breakfast buffet is $---person...walk to Union Station instead (great spot) and grab something there. 
I will check out other hotels on this street for future stays as the location is very good and there are other spots that seem a little nicer.

I was the winning bidder on two nights at this hotel at a charity auction and knew that at some point, I'd be in need of staying over for buisness in NYC. We visited Philadelphia as part of a historic tour of New England. When we arrived in Philadelphia, we were just a little concerned - the city is a little rough around the edges. We found the Holiday Inn and were pleased to find out that the hotel was within a short walking distance from Independence Hall, Benjamin Franklin's house, and the house where Thomas Jefferson wrote the Declaration of Independence. The hotel room was sufficient, although one of the beds had fallen out of the bed frame. We called to the front desk and they had someone up in -- minutes to fix the problem. The bathroom was clean but was showing it's age. All in all, the room was comfortable. There was a nice rooftop pool, which the kids loved. Since the hotel is located in a city, there was considerable city noise. In our case, it was the fire department next door. I just wore earplugs and got a good night's sleep.
We ate at the restaurant in the hotel for dinner - Benton's I think was the name. The food was pretty good and reasonably priced. Our waiter was a kick - he was very easy going and attentive. Another waitress had a tantrum in the kitchen area that was audible throughout the restaurant - that was kind of uncomfortable. Apparently, she had a problem with our waiter and wanted to let him and everyone else know - very unprofessional.
I have to mention about the National Park Service in Philadelphia. They gave FREE tours at Independence Hall, Benjamin Franklin's house, the house where Thomas Jefferson wrote the Declaration of Independence, and at the Visitor Center. The Park Rangers were very knowledgeable and clearly enjoyed their work. The tours were the best we had on our trip. The Rangers were always available to answer a question of provide insight to whatever we were touring. While my favorite tour was of Independence Hall, the presentation on the Underground Railroad was quite informative, too. I have to say that this really made the stay in Philadelphia a """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""must see"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" when touring historical New England and I am glad we visted despite our concerns when entering the city.

Overview:
While the hotel itself is nice.. their management style and 'sticking' their customers with additional charges are not in good taste or in keeping with the traditions and qualities of the Westin Brand. I have included a review that will cover every aspect of this hotel that I experienced both good and bad AND there are a few things you NEED to know before staying here that can save you a TON of money... Enjoy the review!
-. PARKING (READ READ READ).... (Rating - - of --)
This was what initially prompted me to write this review in the first place. This Westin DOES NOT give you the option to self park.. in other words.. Valet Parking is required... Normally, I prefer and recommend using Valet at hotels.. its a great convenience.. HOWEVER, I do not like being 'forced' to use it.. 
***TIP #-**: 
The 'forced' valet system will run you $-- per night to park your car! Which, if I read the sign correctly, included a --% Tip. Now.. where I come from, tips are EARNED for good service... Not mandatory.. another factor in writing this review. In addition, I paid $-- for this room.. SO the parking by itself was --% of my one night stay added on to what I paid! Unacceptable.. I feel the price point here should be around the $-- mark. 
ALTERNATIVE:
Directly across the street is a parking garage. The parking garage will run you $-- per day vs $--.. HOWEVER YOU NEED TO KNOW.. that the $-- per day is charged from - am to - am so if you are staying overnight.. you will end up paying $-- unless you get your car out before - am. Unfortunately at this time.. there are few options of parking. 
-. CHECK IN - CHECK OUT: (Rating - of --)
This process was very efficient. No problems noted.. they asked if I wanted a high floor.. I highly encourage you to ask.. great views. 
-. ROOM OVERVIEW:
My room was #---- in the 'Blue Tower' or Triangle wing of the hotel. Minimal views as it was facing the other tower and toward the ------- Freeways. Very little noise at that height. The overall hotel room was nice and well thought out. Modern and updated with flat screen TV's and a small but very functional multi-function desk. Upon entering room, I noticed the toilet was not clean (Negative). However, with a quick call downstairs someone was at my door in - minutes and did a great job..
