This room also has a refrigerator (small) and a safe located under the TV in the dresser. 
On the POSITIVE SIDE: The water bottles in the room are FREE which many hotels now charge up to $- or more. ALSO there is a program that I was not aware of for fitness fanatics... called the 'Westin Workout'.. which it seems they will 'loan' you workout gear and shoes.. for $-. Kind of neat thing... did not try it.. but something to consider.. I guess for people who want to travel light but still get a workout in. 
-. GYM:
Had the opportunity to get a quick workout in prior to my evening beginning. The gym was very small, HOWEVER, it seems as if they are renovating the gym so it seems as if this is temporary.. not quite sure though. Had very nice treadmills that allowed you to hook in your iPad-iPhone (had a iPhone cord already there-great touch) so its literally plug and play. It also had a spot to plug in a USB Thumb drive as well... 
-. NEGATIVE ITEMS TO WATCH OUT FOR...
a. SHOWER: The water pressure is fine BUT WATCH OUT for the temperature. It will go from cool to inferno hot with a tiny movement of the handle. In addition.. the temperature of the water in the shower will vary ON ITS OWN... not sure if its a function of my room, that tower or of the whole hotel in general.. but watch out.. could burn someone very very easily!
b. COFFEE MAKER: Before using the coffee maker in your room - PLEASE CHECK THE WATER RESERVOIR - prior to putting water in the machine. Ours was extremely dirty.. almost moldy... didn't look like anyone had ran vinegar or cleaned machine since it was purchased. 
c. INTERNET: One of the my biggest peeves when staying at a nice hotel is charging for wireless internet.. again.. sticking their customers. Their charge is $--.-- per -- hours. Again.. completely unacceptable.
d. BUSINESS CENTER: Not only do they charge you in room for internet.. but if you have to print off any document.. you must then go to the business center and 'RENT' their computer AGAIN for an additional charge.. AND THEN pay for the printer. Cant remember exactly but I believe the cost was $-.-- for -- MINUTES plus the cost for what you print out per page!
IN REVIEW:
POSITIVES: 
Free water, Weston Workout, Good - quick response to customers needs, well appointed room, great location, easy check in-check out.
NEGATIVES:
Unreliable water temperature (bordering dangerous), disgusting coffee makers, Internet charges both in room and in business center, HORRIBLE valet and parking charges.
IN CONCLUSION:
Overall would I recommend.. NO.. why? My biggest issue is the parking charges and the forced valet. If this was not an issue for me.. I probably would recommend. This review is based on my direct observation and experiences and should be used as a guide to help you know that when you get a hotel room.. you are also buying or will be required to buy much more than you expect. This needs to stop.

Way cool! The bed which is the most important part of a hotel stay was fabulous! Very comfy and with great support. The linens were nice and soft and the entire room was very comfortable. Would stay here again for sure.

I had a stay for several weeks at the Mayflower. Cost and location were my deciding factors. My first room was overlooking Bush street. LOTS of sun, light, people watching - I loved it. I was not dissapointed and was pleasantly surprised with the easy feel of the place.
Regarding the bathrooms (and kitchens) - they are old but the owners seem to be retaining a lot of the original feel of the original features. There are original porcelain floor and wall tiles and design details in many instances from many many years ago. When they have had to cut into a wall to modernize, I noticed someone paid a lot of attention to carefully matching modern tiles and grout such that the average person may not notice. In my opinion, this kind of bathroom is more interesting than what you would find in any modern hotel. I like to see the patina of wear and appreciate the fine craftsmanship that set all those little porcelain tiles so many years ago. Cleanliness was not an issue.
I found the rooms very clean and of good size. The street side room became quite an issue by the third day as at night the street noise started to bug me. (they have to retain the old originial windows on the facade) On the third night I requested a quieter room which they showed me to in the back of the hotel. It was great - until they started remodeling the room next door. No matter - they offered to change my room again but I declined as I was out in the city during most the day. Otherwise this room near the back was very quiet at night. 
Someone made homemade goodies for breakfast too. In addition the the regular cereal, bread and such, cookies appeared some days and breakfast cakes on others. Gotta try the cinnimon bread toast with butter - yum. The clientele in the morning was a nice mix of Americans, some foreign travellers, and some retired folks. 
There was a small kitchen with mirowave & refrigerator in my room. It had minimal items to make lunch and a simple supper. There is a great market right downstairs and to the left with groceries and some prepared items. A medditerranean flair to the food and they stocked Champagne too!

Arrived at Room Mate Grace -th Dec --, we were given a room on the -rd floor, it was small and had a bunk over the main bed, which wasn't needed as there was only - of us. Unfortunately our room appeared to be above the Bar-Nightclub and even wearing ear plugs the thud of the Bass was pounding through the pillow! After a quick word with reception they re located us immediately to another room on floor -,..... so peaceful! After that initial problem, the rest of the stay was perfect. The bed was so comfortable, the room was cleaned every day, breakfast was well presented and plenty to offer. The location to Times Sq is Brilliant, about ---m away. This hotel in a great location for exploring the city. Literally - min walk to the metro and - min walk to Central Park. The hotel is very contemporary. -. I agree that there should be a cut off time but -am is too early and Housekeeping should always check twice after they have finished other rooms on the floor. -. One morning I saw about - rooms which had their room doors left unlocked and were unattended (door leans against the security bar so that it cannot be closed). This hotel is only a few years old and it shows in its modern design and clean look. The rooms are well appointed and the bathrooms just as good. I'm a big fan of the shower. While the staff still need a bit of work to reach the level of the Ritz up the road but they still do a great job. If you are in town for an event at the Moscone Center or are looking to attend the museum you couldn't pick a better hotel.

My husband and I just returned from a two night stay at the Library Hotel. We have been to New York many times, but we've never had such an all round perfect hotel experience. The """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""pull"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" of the water was non-existent especially when compared to a place like Maui where standing in two feet of water almosts knocks you off your feet. Could'nt make it home one night, so we ended up staying here. Its right downtown so we were able to still go out and eat dinner. Freidnly staff and would come stay again if we had to.

The the rooms were clean and spacious but a bit outdated, could do with some refurbishment with new carpets and colours, but overall it was a great experience. We had a room with view of the Hills which wasn't very pretty but we didn't spend much time in our room, so it didn't bother me too much.

My husband has customers in NYC, and while he comes to NYC frequently for business, I always come along for a pre-Christmas visit, combining business and leisure. rooms are big, but bathroom is quiet small and ramshackle. The service is not very good, staff is rude and hasty. I booked a triple, but the -th bed wasn't ready.

Great stay, the breakfast and evening reception was first class. The staff was super friendly, the GM was very visable and we spoke to him several times. Service like this is hard to come by these days! Good value too.

After reading the reviews I had mixed feelings on how this hotel would rate, but once we checked in we were very pleased. Overall my husband and I were very pleased with our four night stay at the Washington Marriott.

The hotel has a well equipped laundry in the same room as a 'help yourself' eating area where you can purchase machine coffee, snacks and some easy cook microwave meals for which you can pay using the honesty box or by filling in a usage form to add the charges to the bill.

We enjoyed our stay in the San Diego area, as we did our overall journey down the pacific coastal highway. If we ever return to SD, I would probably try somewhere different, but wouldn't rule out a return to Humphreys for it's laid back, tropical feel and decent staff.

We booked the Days Inn after a friend wasn't able to get us a deal at the Magic Castle on the days we were in LA so we opted for the Days Inn on Sunset for it's central-ish location near Hollywood Boulevard which is in walking distance.

The staff were pleasant and friendly - however, do not let them book you a taxi to the airport. We only asked them to book it because our friends couldn't give us a lift. Overall, the hotel is perfectly functionable without any luxury.

Myself my husband and our two children aged -- and -- stayed in this hotel for - nights in Oct --. The staff were very freindly courteous and helpful particularly the bell man who went out of his way each day to suggest places for us to shop and visit. The reception staff were very helpful on the day of check out our bags were stored as our flight was not until -.-- pm that evening this was not a problem and they asked if there was anything else they could help us with prior to our departure just to ask. A couple of mornings our daughter did not join us for brekfast and a take out was provided without question.
The location of the hotel is also excellent certainly beats the touristy times square area. The village was lovely to walk around in the evenings or early morning There are plenty of good restaurants and a good jazz scene The area is also reasonably quiet so we all got a good nights sleep. The hotel certainly added to a very enjoyable stay in NYC I would highly recommend it and from a price perspective it is excellent value. I will definitely return to the WSH

If you are interested in seeing more of the small businesses and boutiques that are unique to New York, I definitely recommend the Tribeca-Soho area.

The room was well decorated and the kitchen included everything needed down to a variety of glasses including wine glasses! It appears that everything one would have in their home kitchen was planned for in the condos.

First let me say that I have stayed at this hotel - or - times over the past year or so and that everytime the hotel seems to get a bit better. Even for a Four Seasons, this hotel stands our for service, food and facility. Everyone on the staff was attentive, happy, helpful. Restaurant was excellent and the rooms and view were as good as any I've stayed in.

The furniture and walls had a few bumps and bruises, but I guess an airport hotel is pretty high traffic so it's to be expected. Bathroom was fine and had doors into both bedroom and living area. After breakfast, I walked across the street and got my car, saving shuttle rides back into the airport, which was a great convenience. The front desk staff were friendly but seemed distracted and my first set of keys didn't work. Also, you have to sign up or be a HHonors member to get free wifi. They should also renovate-refresh some of the rooms which are showing wear and tear. Otherwise, the price is reasonable for the location when you consider the size of the rooms, and I would definitely consider staying here again.

CONS:

Two stars = okay, but some problems. That's what this hotel is: okay.

We had an actual closet and enough room to unpack two suitcases without feeling cramped. However, for the price, you could certainly do better in NYC. 
Our room was OLD; the carpet was worn and the curtains were dusty. The shower had very low pressure and the bed wasn't rock hard, but I wouldn't describe it as comfortable. The walls are paper thin. I was in bed and heard the conversations of the people in the next room very clearly. 
The bathroom in our room was horribly designed. The magnification mirror is mounted directly above the toilet - if you forget to close the lid and accidentally drop your makeup - shaver, it will end up in the toilet bowl. This wouldn't be a major problem if there was counter space. There wasn't - the two inches of counter space is taken up by their glass cups. 
The minibar is the newest item in the room. It dispenses items like a vending machine does (you have to press which item you want and remove it from a dispenser) and it is tucked behind a faux wood paneled door. 
Room service came quickly, the food was mediocre and high-priced, but you'll find that everywhere in NYC hotels.
If you still decide to stay here, please take heed: If you want a cab, *especially* at rush hour, do not use The Warwick's doorman. He's a nice guy, but the cabs all line up across the street at The Hilton. Just go to the Hilton which is cattycorner from The Warwick and you'll have a cab in - seconds. The Warwick's doorman whistled and waved for -- minutes trying to score us a cab, when we went to the Hilton, there was never a wait.
The Warwick's lobby is small, so it always seems crowded. Staff wasn't rude, but there was a definite lack of warmth. If you expect mediocre service and rooms for $--- a night, book this hotel. If you prefer better, look around - there are plenty of hotels in the area and quite a few that are nicer and lower in price than The Warwick. Bottom line: It's an old room in a nice location. Just a room.

There is no coffee set up in the room but you can request it if you'd like. I discovered in advance that Starbucks is immediately next door so I simply dashed down each morning and grabbed my triple espresso and took it back up to my room. 
In addition to the concierge, there is a theater desk in the hotel, and even though I didn't need to use it, I noticed there were always guests receiving assistance there each time I passed. The hotel has a private car service that can be booked. I used it to return to LGA since it was less than $-- more than I'd paid for a cab, and it was perfect for a smooth, comfortable and relaxing ride with no worries about running up the meter while bogged down in rush hour traffic.
So all in all, the Millenium Broadway fit the bill for me. I got a special offer of just under $--- per night, but now that I've stayed there, I will do so again even without that price.

Having stayed at the W in Westwood many times, it’s truly a home away from home for us. We really appreciate the convenience and high standards of this hotel property. The staff throughout the hotel really seems to enjoy what it’s doing. They truly understand the hospitality business. The property is spotless, and the rooms are very clean and modern. We regularly dine at the hotel and major changes have recently occurred. Although we had always been happy with the food at Nine Thirty (which is the street address of the hotel) and the Backyard, we were anticipating the arrival of the new chef, Dakota Weiss, at the beginning of the year. We had heard from Ren Hirose, the GM, and restaurant managers Chris Cazares and Stephanie Sanders that she had survived an amazing round of tastings, up against some ---plus other chefs. No doubt the competition was fierce – sounds like it could have been a ubiquitous reality show. 
We gave her about three weeks to settle in before heading over for our first visit, and the verdict is in. Naturally, in such a short time she hadn’t completely redone the menus, but her touches were already apparent. For example, the previous chef had an appetizer (or “side,” as it’s referred to there) of Brussels sprouts. Many people don’t particularly care for Brussels sprouts, but these were good. Very good. They’re something we never would have previously thought to order off a menu. Dakota Weiss changed the seasonings and made the preparation healthier (grilled rather than fried), and we didn’t miss the old version at all. Being independently creative, Dakota moved on from Brussels sprouts to create an appetizer of baby artichokes in smoked garlic aioli and chopped basil that is also healthy, flavorful and out of this world. 
 Her new creations are full of twists. A very grown up macaroni and cheese uses very small, round pasta (their true name escapes us), with bacon, apple bits and garlic bread crumbs. This is definitely not the fake orange powdered boxed stuff we all made growing up, nor even an adult version of a traditional mac and cheese. Other sides were delightfully different – charred broccoli with lemon, red chili oil and parmesan. Honestly, if all food were prepared and served this way, multitudes of children wouldn’t have grown up afraid to try anything green, healthy and supposedly boring. 
 We’re working our way through the menu – we often order several sides (and “smalls” which are truly a few bites to share), some of which show up time and time again – and entrees (a “large”). There’s something for every palate – seafood, fish, chicken, steak. A favorite is the beef bourguignon – anyone who has watched “Julie and Julia” might try it for that reason alone, but it is quite satisfying. And the desserts are lots of fun and creative – who would think of a chocolate creation, including chocolate puffed rice – in a tall parfait glass? Everything is beautifully plated.
But the most fun is Dakota herself. We asked to meet her after our first meal and have spoken with her several times since, and all we can say is, what fun. She definitely looks the part of a creative person. If you saw her on the street, you might think she was an actress. Always bubbly and charming, her tone indicates her love for what she’s doing, which is good given the long hours and weighty expectations. Although many very creative people are thought of as not being terribly business-minded or organized (yes, it’s a stereotype, but there is a reason they exist!), her comments indicate her seriousness about how she runs her kitchen. There, she’s definitely the captain of the ship and she expects it to be run with precision and excellence -- but for the staff to enjoy it as well. 
We’re looking forward to more dining adventures as Dakota sets new culinary trends.

On a recent trip to Los Angeles, I knew that the Hollywood and Highland area was the place that I wanted to be in. But where should I stay? Should I stay at the Celebrity Hotel or the Orchid Suites? Both have good reviews, were just meters apart and were both in my price range. A difficult choice.
My solution? Divide my stay between the two hotels. Since my actual stay in L.A. would be divided into two by a short trip to San Diego and Anaheim in between, I decided to spend the first couple of nights at the Orchid Suites and the second bunch at the Celebrity.
So having stayed at the Orchid Suites earlier, I was a bit disappointed at the Celebrity upon arrival. And the culprit is the parking area. Aside from it being full with cars (a number double parked), the gate is constantly open. And since my family with small kids arrived close to midnight, this did not offer much in terms of security. I also had to park the car in such a way that a small part of it's tail is exposed out the sidewalk. In effect, I had to repeatedly look out the sidewalk to see if there was anyone around as I opened the trunk.
After the parking lot experience, I entered our hotel room not helping to notice that it was less appointed than that of the Orchid's. The kitchen in particular paled as it didn't have the same number of amenities. An in-room safe was sorely missed, too. 
While wi-fi signal in the room was poor, a wire for broadband access was present in the room. Neat.
Aesthetically though, the room at the Celebrity looked better and newer. The same could be said of the hotel as a whole in comparison to the Orchid, which still looked like an apartment which was just converted into a hotel.
The front desk personnel were helpful when I needed some info during our stay. Not as cheerful in my opinion, but still to the task. 
The biggest difference that the other hotel didn't have was the breakfast that came with the Celebrity's room rate. Though some may complain that it didn't offer much, to me the bagels, muffins and croissants together with juice and coffee were enough to start my day.
I was also pleasantly surprised to find that the amount I payed for our stay here was actually cheaper than that of the Orchid's by $---night. Surprised because the quotes here in T.A. are cheaper for the Orchid Suites.
Lastly, I might be mistaken but I didn't see any elevators. So if your room is in the upper floors and have heavy luggages with you... 
So which to me was a better hotel? Let me sum it up this way: if you have a car, the Orchid Suites might be a better option. But if you don't have one, then let the free breakfast and cheaper rates sway you to the Celebrity instead. 
To expound on the parking situation, firstly, the number of parking slots in the Celebrity is not enough for all their guests. One night, I heard a European man giving his car keys to the person manning the front desk insisting that he park his car. I can tell that he was exasperated from finding a parking slot himself. The front-desk person did not take it reasoning that though parking was available, it is limited.
Second, parking at the Celebrity is actually to the side of the hotel accessed via Franklin Ave. So if you are coming from the direction of Highland (as I always do) in heavy traffic, turning left to the garage entrance is impossible, not to mention illegal in the first place. Turn to Google Earth for a better picture.
In comparison, the entrance to the Orchid's garage is along Orchid Ave., turning left to which from Franklin is aided by a traffic light. No problem.
A solution to the Celebrity's parking woes would be to return late at night when traffic at Franklin is light (drivers at your back will honk at you for stopping to turn left into the garage). But since the garage gates are always open, and chances are yours will be the last car in, one can't help but feel unsafe with nobody around late at night in Hollywood.
Third, if you park farthest from the gate the night before and leave the earliest the next morning, be prepared to wait a while since backing up all the cars blocking your way will take some time.
But despite all this, I would have honestly considered coming back to this hotel. Afterall it is hard to disregard the free breakfast and the slightly cheaper rates. The parking- you get used to it. 
I however have a beef with the front desk person who promised to e-mail me the breakdown of my expenses since their printer was malfunctioning when I checked out. I've e-mailed them a reminder as I got back and still no answer to my request. I just have this impression that they are nice when they need your business but don't care when your business with them is done. 
So it's Orchid Suites for me by a whisker. 
Remember, this is my pinion and I just hope that with this I help you formulate your own.

If you're looking for a hotel experience - i.e. valet parking, restaurant, room service, concierge, bellhop, etc. - this is NOT the place for you. This inn is for people looking for more of a condo experience. You really feel like this is your own little apartment smack in the center of Boston. Here's a summary.
ROOMS: My husband, - year-old daughter and I stayed in the one-bedroom suite (bedroom closed off from living room). Very modern and sleek. For those with young children, rental baby cots are available (--$ flat rate). It fits snuggly in a corner of the bedroom. The Queen bed is very comfy and there's an angled wall-hung flat-screen TV facing the bed, as well as an iPod docking station. The living room is stylish and comfy with another flat-screen TV over the gas fireplace. Our room had a small kitchen area (fridge, microwave, sink, and stovetop) perfect for having breakfast or fixing a quick lunch. All new utensils and dishes. The bathroom is small but efficient. Shower only, but a large one. Plush robes at your disposal. Amazingly enough, even though you are mere steps away from the Prudential Center, rooms are very quiet because the inn is located on a calm side street. My only small complaint was that it was difficult to balance the air conditioning between the bedroom and living room. When the living room was comfortable, we were freezing in the bedroom. Took more than a few tries to get it right.
BREAKFAST: Free of charge. There is a common lounge area downstairs where you can pick up coffee, tea, juice, bagels, yogurt, and English muffins (no plain bread!?). You can eat there, but most people seem to bring everything up to their room.
CHECK-IN-OUT: Super easy and efficient. Two weeks before you check-in, you receive two codes by email. One to open the front door and the other to access your room. No keys to carry around or lose! Codes are functional only from check-in time, i.e. -pm. No front desk, but should you need anything at all, there is an office downstairs manned from -am to --pm.
PARKING: This is the biggest issue for a lot of people wanting to stay here, but it's really not that complicated. Basically, there is no parking, on-street or otherwise. However, as I said, the Prudential Center is steps away and has a large garage. Boston hotels charge on average -----$ a day for parking whereas it will only cost you -----$ a day at the Center (--$ is with an easy-to-find online coupon). If it's full, there are many other indoor garages in the same vicinity that offer approximately the same rate. So just temporarily park in front of the inn, unload your car, take it to Prudential Center, and walk back to the inn in - minutes.
FITNESS: If you need a workout, there's a small fitness center with a couple of machines. No pool.
LOCATION: PERFECT!!! In - minutes, you can walk to the Prudential Center (conference center, shopping, restaurants, and a subway stop). In - minutes on foot, you're on Newbury Street, the main strip for boutiques, restaurants, and cafés. In roughly ----- minutes, you can walk to Copley Square. There's also a neighborhood park for little ones and a plaza with waterworks to cool them off on hot summer days. Finally, there's a --Eleven conveniently located right in front of the inn and a supermarket by the Prudential Center.
All in all, a wonderful stay in a wonderful city. I highly recommend this inn and will absolutely and gladly return next time I'm in Boston.

Advantages: nice views of Boston harbor, shuttle to Logan airport, clean rooms and bathrooms, easy check-in
Dsadvantage: even though it looks like the location is centralized, you have to take the subway to downtown Boston. this is the only reason I gave - stars instead of - stars.

We had read a lot of reviews before we left Australia on this hotel. Most being unfavourable, however, going in with an open mind and no disillusions, we expected the worst. We were thrilled with the location, right around the corner from the Empire State Building and across the road from Penn Station ( subway and trains), a block from Macy's. Yes, the room was small and a bit shabby, in need of a bit of TLC, but all in all, we didn't spend much time in our room, only to sleep and found the convenience of being so close to everything the best thing about this hotel. We didn't eat in the restaurants here, opting for a trip to the Deli for breakfast and late night snacks. All in all our experience was a positive one, bearing in mind we stayed for - days and this was over a very busy period for this hotel , as they housed a lot of overseas competitors from the New York Marathon.

First trip to Washington, chose this hotel as the reviews were good. Chose area as it was fairly central.
Area outside hotel was very busy with tourists, traffic and cafes - very few shops. Hotel staff were friendly and helpful. Room was basic although public areas were a little better. No extras in room e.g. no tea-coffee, no iron, no bath. Coffee was supplied in the lobby from -.-- - -.-- each morning.Have never stayed in a hotel which doesn't supply this. The biggest issue with the room was the en-suite. The wash basin was in the bedroom and the shower and loo were behind an opaque wall. There was no lock on the bathroom door but this didn't present a problem as you could see who was sitting on the loo from the gap between the door and the wall and of course through the wall. Won't be returning.

So, how important is location to you? If you are wanting a downtown, close to everything including convention center activities this may be the hotel for you. The service was accommodating and in general it was very clean. The rooms are very small. If more than oone person is staying in the room you have to schedule movement around the room. No desk, no closet and the smallest Flat Screen TV I have seen outside a airline cabin. As most """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""downtown"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" hotels the street noise was high but you can expect that.

This appears to be an older facility that was purchased by La Quinta. It is not up to the usual standards and the owners-staff are obviously only """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""pet friendly"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" to the extent that La Quinta requires and not because they are animal lovers. Signs all over about the restrictions for the pets including number and size of dogs. I always stay at La Quinta as I do a lot of rescue transports and we are always welcome. My dogs exceeded the weight limit (-- lb TOTAL for - dogs), but I brought them in and out the side door and we left at the crack of dawn. I will never stay here again - Maybe Memphis just isn't a pet friendly city but I won't be back to find out. Will always stay elsewhere from now on.

The hotel is excellent for the price, it was a modest room, but was clean and the service was excellent. The location was wonderful to go anywhere in Manhattan.
Can't wait to go there again!

Absolutely fantastic. This place is funky, hip and totally the place to be if you are running with (or want to run with) the """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""in"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" crowd. Great ambiance, stellar room, and unique bars. Service was top-notch as well. I would highly recommend this hotel to folks who don't mind paying $-- for a shot of Jager and consider it standard fashion to dress to impress for simple cocktails. I don't recommend this hotel for families or those traveling with kids.

I booked this hotel from a Travelzoo promotion and could not have been happier with my experience. From before I checked in until the moment I left, I felt like I was a highly valued guest. The staff was very welcoming and willing to offer help immediately. The room is slightly small, but if you don't need the space, it is perfect. I was more than happy with the quality of the room. It has everything you could need, so the space issue isn't a concern. The decor of the hotel and the room are very modern and I enjoyed how updated it looks since the exterior of the hotel is slightly misleading. It's a small detail but I appreciated that because it was Valentine's Day there was a rose left on the bed and my room was tidied up when I had left for a few hours (not sure how they knew I wasn't there but it was nice regardless!). I wish I could have tried the wine hour and breakfast from the restaurant, but I did not have time. I would definitely come back again and I would recommend this hotel to others in a heartbeat! I have worked and lived in Boston for years and never knew this gem existed but I am definitely a big fan now!

Our Room was nice but the walls are paper thin. There were two college teams staying in the hotel the same night and the noise was horrible. We called the front desk and that helped for a short time but the loud talk, yelling, giggling, and slamming of doors countinued until early in the morning. In short, it was a sleepless night. To make matters worse, there is no free wifi or breakfast

The Galleria Park is an average hotel for San Francisco. Rooms are very small (especially those with a king size bed). Ours had a sink outside of the bathroom-toilet shower area. Room looked a little run down, and I got some sort of bite (spider maybe?) during our first night in the hotel. Upon arrival, the valet was nowhere to be found, but the car was eventually parked. Room was also loud (at night you can easily hear traffic). We ended up leaving - days early and moving to a more expensive hotel, as when I am on vacation, I'd rather spend a little more for higher quality service. However, for the rate-value, this property is average-as expected.

We have stayed numerous times at this Downtown Chicago hotel since it was opened in ---- and there are many reasons we keep returning to this hotel. The rooms are spacious and actual --room suites with a full kitchen and living area. This is a particularly nice hotel for families since it is one of the few hotels in the downtown area with a pool located on the top floor with a very nice view. Some rooms also have - beds in the bedroom and, along with a pull-out couch, a whole family can stay in one room. There are also cots available if needed. My dad enjoyed the work-out room also found on the top floor. There is a full breakfast every morning along with an adequate evening meal during the week. This keeps a family's vacation costs down and we ate a nice meal at some of the finest restaurants in the immediate area at lunchtime. At $----night-family during Spring Break, this hotel can be hard to beat particularly if you make good use of the kitchen along with the Jewel and Trader Joe grocery stores within - blocks of the hotel.
The staff are all very friendly from the knowledgable doormen-greeters-valets at the front door to the front desk staff that had our rooms ready when we arrived. Our rooms were placed together without us asking for this to be done which I have found is not necessarily the case in a lot of hotels. The breakfast area features Connie who has been there for many years and whom we have come to recognize from our previous visits. The management also made a point of visiting in the dining area to be sure everything is going well. 
You can take Amtrak or the Megabus from the Detroit-Ann Arbor area into Union Station and hop onto the --- bus at Canal and Adams to within - blocks of the hotel. The --- bus returns you to the station at the end of your trip. At $---night parking, leaving the car at home is a good plan. This hotel could not be in a better location. Hop on the red line which is - block away to get right to Wrigley Field and the red line runs south to State St for the theaters and shopping. The --- bus also will take you directly to the (free) Lincoln Park Zoo. The --- bus will take you right to the museum campus. All buses can be found on Michigan Ave. - blocks away from the hotel.
Our visit to Chicago was wonderful as usual and our stay at this hotel was pleasurable. It was particularly interesting to meet a friend from home staying here for their third time upon a previous recommendation made by me.

Although the room was small, it was extremely clean and comfortable. We had a room that faced E.--st street, and it was very quiet. Not too much street noise. Hotel is located near the corner of E--st and Madison Ave. Very close to Times Sq, etc. The shower (rainhead) was the best ever, with power force of water. It was a small bathroom, but immaculate. The hotel provides thick, spa-like bathrobes and towels. The towels were heavy and about - ft. long! Flat screen TV was mounted on the wall at the bottom of the bed. Bed was very comfortable. There is a safe in the room (no charge). The doorman will hail the cabs for you. Wonderful hotel. Continental breakfast was too expensive - that's the only negative that I can say.

We stayed at Essex House for - nights - Manhattan side of the hotel, so although next to the Central Park, no view of the park itself. Junior suite is spacious, bed comfortable, wireless internet non-existent (so if you're traveling on business, this one sucks).
Concierge is spotty at best (ie sent us to a closed restaurant, seemed to be not interested in even offering to call them up and make a reservation or just check if they're open).
Booked through AMEX, so we had two breakfasts included - which does not mean *really* two breakfasts - rather a $-- USD daily credit towards breakfast, which does not cover two buffet breakfasts @ $-- each, plus tax and tip. So, """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""breakfast included"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" does not mean quite included.
Recommend to take a short walk South on -th or -th ave. (aka Avenue of the Americas) - plenty of small breakfast shops, where family of - can have breakfast for about $----- with no problem. Particularly pleasant is Lou's Cafe on the corner of -th and --rd - if you're into outdoor, cafe-style, but very urban style.
All in all, not bad, but far from what I expected from Jumeirah... they still need to learn from Fairmont or St.Regis or Four Seasons or....

The only real drawback to this hotel is that it is SO close to the airport that the planes departing ad landing were unbelievably loud. Bed was fine, bathroom fine, breakfast nothing special but ok. If you don't mind the planes, I'd recommend the hotel. If you're noise sensitive, not a good idea.

The bedrooms were soooo small! You could barely move in the bathroom either a bigger person would struggle. The room didn't have a fridge for the minibar, it was all stacked in a drawer! (warm bottled water!) Also the air conditioning units make awful loud 'clanging' noises. 
On the otherhand the actual hotel was lovely, very 'urban chic'...also very clean. 
Although I did enjoy my stay at the Hudson, I would only recommend it for 'small' single people.

Wonderful, wonderful----what else can I say about the Radisson Martinique! The front desk staff and bell staff are the BEST in the business. They treat you like you are the most special guest in the hotel----always smiling, friendly, and helpful. In addition, they greet you by your name and go out of their way to make your stay relaxing. The location is convenient to Time's Square, shopping, the subway, and great restaurants. The restaurant and bar in the hotel is also excellent and well-staffed.
I certainly will be returning and if you are looking for great accommodations, then the Martinique is the best choice.

Our stay at this hotel was very comfortable. The staff was always polite and helpful and more than willing to help with any arrangements you may need. Our room was above average and the bed was fantastic. The whole hotel was very clean. If you stay during the week they offer a free limo service into the business district in the morning. We missed out on this opportunity because we slept in, but it was a nice bonus if you are up in time. We did manage to take advantage of the free internet in the business center to confirm our return flight. That was a nice addition to the stay. The location of the hotel is only two blocks to fisherman's wharf and not too far from north beach. My one and only complaint was that we had a very close view of the tree outside and that was about it. So I recommend that you ask for a room on the fourth or fifth level. Other than that one complaint our stay was smooth and uneventfull, just how we like it:).

Location is the best feature of this hotel provided you want to be in a neighborhood setting as opposed to Mid-town location. We have stayed all over the City so this is not our first rodeo but, by far, our worst experience.
The biggest flaw with this hotel is the terrible management and absence of leadership when there are legitimate problems present. I encountered guests complaining at the front desk - out of the - days in which we stayed at this hotel. The desk clerks handle problems without guidance or direction from management -- or perhaps just incompetent and indifferent management decisions. Staff are left to deal with the frustrated (and sometimes angry) guests while the manager hides out in an """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""office"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" somewhere out of sight. The result is a woeful attempt at service that is lackluster at best and incompetent at worst. It is too bad because this hotel has great potential to be a real gem in the City.

The issue is that my husband has a heart condition that is adversely affected by heat and we needed to have a cooler room for him. I spent a good deal of the late evening (or I should say, wee morning hours) calling other hotels trying to locate another room for the evening while also attempting to keep the air conditioner running without leaking water all over the room. The front staff did not offer any suggestions for other hotels, a phone book or even a courtesy phone call (since my cell phone did not work in our room --- all calls were made by me in the front lobby). In addition, the next morning, the housemaid told me I would have to pay extra laundry fees for the towels used to soak up the a-c leak. Unbelievable! Three attempts to speak with the manager resulted in these comments: """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""you just missed her"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" -- """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""she just left the building"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" --- """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""she just went into a meeting."""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" It may be that if nothing whatsoever unusual happens during your stay, you will be fine. However, if you have any issue crop up....you will live to regret this stay. Personally, I will not risk a stay here again, EVER!

The Renaissance Mayflower is absolutely amazing! We were in a suite and the kids loved it! We walked directly to the White House and the subway was right outside the hotel to easy get around the city. I would recommend going in the fall to really enjoy the city and the history of our wonderful nation. 
We are planning to go back next year for Labor Day weekend!

We booked this hotel for an early morning flight out of PHL. I checked in around -PM and the desk clerk was very friendly and competent. The lobby had a nice, modern feel to it. The hallways, however, look like that of an old college dormitory. They are in the process of renovating the hotel, so maybe the hallways will get an update. The room was a reflection of the rest of the hotel. The foyer and bathroom didn't appear to be renovated, while the sleeping and desk areas had the same modern design as the lobby. The location is great for the airport and easy to get in and out of the city. 
All was on the up and up until we tried to get some sleep. The ac-heating unit was right next to the bed and very loud. The pillows on the bed were extremely worn out and the mattress too firm. Although you didn't hear any noise from the airport or parking lot, the noise in the room really didn't make for a great night's sleep. The extra hour or so of rest I was hoping to get by staying next to the airport was essentially canceled out by the poor sleep quality, so the night was a waste of money.

the palomar was a nice hotel. nothing special, the decorating was a bit generic. the service was excellent, everybody was very friendly and helpful. being so close to union square, it really was right in the middle of tourist central, but it made a good central location from which to explore some of the quieter neighborhoods of SF. if you are coming to shop at the big name stores, you probably couldnt do much better than the palomar for location and value. it is conveniently located close to a bart stop, which i wish i had known on the way there b.c our cab from OAK was $-- whereas the return trip on the bart was about $- per person.

For the most part this was a very good hotel. Some of the minuses are common to all hotels. For instance the make-up mirror would have been perfect for most males or a tall female but not for a short or average height female like myself and my roommate. Although there were two of us staying in the room, there was only one bathrobe provided. The first two days the maid only provided towels for one person. We did not have to request extra towels because I showered after swimming in the pool. The pool was swimmable but small. These, unfortunately seem to be common to all hotels.
Other negatives are not common to all hotels. The bathroom door would not stay open by itself; we propped it open with my backpack so that we could use the mirror on the door. I needed to plug the phone cord in my laptop so that I could dial up my office network but the phone cord on the desk phone was caught in a cable-holder that would not allow me to pull it up onto the desk. The phone cord for the bedside phone was more flexible but there was not an empty electrical outlet to plug the laptop into; this limited the length of time I could work to the battery life. The inflexible desk phone cord also meant that you could not move the phone around the desk. I would have loved to watch TV and work at the desk since there was a very good selection of channels; you cannot see the TV when sitting at the desk.
There was a great CD-radio-alarm clock but there were only instructions for setting the time. We were able to figure out how to set the alarm but a colleague was not able to figure out how to switch to radio from CD.
Although we were in a room with two double beds, there were only two very, very small drawers. This would barely meet the needs of one person in the room but was totally inadequate for two. They did provide us with extra hangers based on my request in my Marriot Rewards profile. Unlike many hotel rooms with two beds, there was plenty of open floor space. We were in an upgraded room at not extra charge. This meant that we faced the river which was a very nice view. Otherwise there were no differences in our room compared to colleagues in non-upgraded rooms. The beds were comfortable and bathroom was roomy and attractive.

We booked the hotel through priceline and were given a tiny room with a double bed. When we asked for a suite we were pressured into paying $--.-- more for the switch. Front desk most unhelpful, didn't know the location of a nearby hotel, didn't know the price of the internet. Hotel is tired, needs refurbishing. It is convenient to the airport and serves an excellent breakfast.

Paying a top price for a room but having to pay for WIFI service in your room is ridiculous. The extraordinary parking comes to $-- a night. Room was pretty and had view of Bay Bridge and the Bay. Good location. Great beds. The hair dryer is a very wimpy one with little power.

Stayed here in March ---- . In San Antonio for a conference at the convention center which is right across the street (very convenient!) Nice big room with wonderful bed! Super mattresses. Nice little balcony overlooking Riverwalk was an added perk. Nice rooftop pool and bar. Just happened to be there for St. Pat's day and the city was a blast! Never knew how nice San Antonio was. Very walkable city. Wonderful restaurants too. Don't miss the Alamo! Hotel was spotless...staff very friendly and helpful. I would definitely stay here again.

It is in a really convenient location. Walking distance from the time square.The staffs were very friendly too. Not a lot of space in the room. The bathroom was not very clean. This hotel is only good for one or two night stay to visit NYC and time square.

The rooms were very clean. 
The staff went above and beyond being friendly and helpful.
Recommended excellant restaurants.
The staff even offered to shuttle our group to and from us the local restaurant if needed.
The free breakfast was very good. 
I will definately stay here again next time in town.

We got a too-good-to-be-true rate from a motor club and I kept waiting for the other shoe to drop. It never did.
The service was excellant, the hotel was gorgeous, no complaints whatsoever. We'll be visitinig DC again in the spring and I'm hoping the supersaver rate is still available then, I'd love to stay at the Omni again

I just got back this morning from New York and I wanted to review the hotel straight away as we'd read some bad reviews... we couldn't fault the hotel. For a start, we got a double bed each and our bathroom had a bathtub. It's in a really good location for getting to the sights, you've got a subway station one block away for those that are a little further away. The staff were efficient and friendly - I wish we could say this about everyone and everything in New York. I'm not concerned about glamorous little extras which weren't present - we got what we paid for. No, there's no flat screen TV, or free internet but our room was cleaned well each day and whenever we needed anything reception were happy to provide it for us. Sometimes I wonder if there is an expectation for everything to be in the room when you arrive. I've come to discover this is a very English thing - but if it's not there, ask and I daresay, it shall be delivered (usually direct to your room door within about - minutes!) The staff had time for us, whether we had questions or requests and I was happy leaving my airport arrangements in their capable hands.

We booked a double hotal room, arrived late to find it was a small air tight box -.-m x -m x -.-m ceilings. There was not enough room to close the door once you put one suitcase in the room. There was no air, no amenitied of any kind except one bed with a used sheet and wet towel screwed up in the small cupboard. Management would not come and check and told us it had been cleaned. They then charged another $--.-- to upgrade to a room where you could at least get inside the room. Wifi did not work. There is no lift and rooms are on -th floor. Do not stay here.

It was too high but maybe that's the going rate for motels these days.
I got an upstairs room because upper levels are usually the cleaner, less-used rooms. 
There are cameras everywhere but the area isn't probably the greatest in the world. It wasn't terribly unsafe but I've stayed at motels that I felt were much more secure than this one.
The ice machine on the ground floor was not working. 
Other than that, no real complaints. I only stayed there one night.
Bed was average, not great not terrible.

This property always comes through with the degree of excellence that you always expect from a Residence Inn.

 I'm happy to say that the front desk staff - including a trainee - went far beyond what they needed to do to accommodate a request I had about room location. It made my --day, weekend stay, very enjoyable.
 For anyone planning on staying here: This property is very peaceful and quiet. But, if you want to, you can experience the pandemonium of a couple of huge shopping areas that are just minutes away.
 It's a great location.

My husband and I frequently this hotel and we make it a good time every visit. The customer service is always great, the quality and taste of the food ordered via room service has yet to disappoint. Our room is always clean and we get to bring our westie with us as it's a dog-friendly hotel. I really like the indoor-outdoor pool, spa is nice, and bartender at the lobby bar makes a delicious mojito. We enjoy requesting a room with a balcony, the view isn't spectacular but being able to open up the space is nice.

This hotel is a great location for a day or - stay. We stayed as an overnight before a flight home, and we found the rooms clean,the service wonderful, and the beds super comfy!
Parking is under the building, and I did feel a little uneasy going down to the car alone. Otherwise it's a nice accommodation. 
We arrived late, checked in used the convenient elevator to get the luggage to the room and headed to Old town.
We ate at Old Town Mexican Cafe where you find ladies making fresh tortillas in the window. I had a wonderful order of shrimp cervich, and a margarita night cap that was really good. 
For breakfast we headed to Perry's cafe which is worth the effort if you have the time. It's across the street from Old Town park and the trolly stop. If you love biscuits and gravy then you will be in heaven. Very tasty home style cooking. Skip the mexican food here!

My husband and I spend Labor Day weekend in NYC. We found Hotel QT through tripadvisor and also various recent publications. Hotel QT was modern, fresh, the free breakfasts were AWESOME and the service was great too! Can't beat the location. 
We orig booked an E room for $----night, but got ugraded to a B room. Although the room was still small, the furnishings maximized the space. The platform around the bed created seating space, and the deep window ledges allowed for some storage space. I loved the two huge windows in the room looking toward times square (we had a corner room). I was really impressed with the iHome unit they had, so we could play our iPod in the room. The shower was amazingly large, and I liked the separate shower-sink-toilet areas. I agree with the previous posts - a place to hang wet towels would've been nice, but we made do with what we had.
My appreciation for Hotel QT grew even more when we moved to the Comfort Inn Midtown for our last night (we used a free nights' stay at Comfort Inn). Comfort Inn is noticeably older. The room was about the same size as Hotel QT's E room, but felt smaller b-c of the traditional furniture. The bathroom was TINY compared to Hotel QT. Perhaps, though, this isn't a fair comparison since Hotel QT's B room is considerably more expensive than Comfort Inn's.
For our next trip to NYC, we will definitely look into staying at Hotel QT again. If you can afford it (ie, get hold of the lower rate rooms), go for it! Otherwise, Comfort Inn Midtown isn't *too* bad of a second choice.

I had no problem with the hotel or the room itself. From the outside and the lobby, the hotel looks quite classy, but the rooms are merely average to nice. 
The problem that I had was with the snobby staff! After dealing with several people who seemed to care less that I was spending money at their hotel, the kicker came when I parked in front of the hotel. The Westgate is on a small street, without a lot of through traffic. I had parked on the curb to allow my friend to take our shopping bags up to our room. An employee in charge of driving the hotel shuttle rudely asked me to move my car (it was all about the tone of voice) so that he could park his there. The entire curb was available, but he just HAD to have my parking spot. I was over it. I won't stay there again.

Hotel Icon is a well-designed hotel built in a former and historic bank building. The entry and lobby bar look both swanky and comfortable, and the bar cocktails are creative and well-made. My tenth floor room was spacious with large windows, a large desk and king size bed. The bathroom was equally large, with both soaking tub and shower. I appreciated some of the small details, like the reading lights on either side of the bed, free newspapers in the lobby, and ample towels in the bathroom. Only two small detractors to the room - the wifi signal was very weak, and the bathroom fixtures were a little worn. Otherwise the room was comfortable and well designed.
The hotel does offer a free shuttle to and from most downtown locations, which was very convenient since the property is on the edge of downtown and there isn't a ton to see or do in walking distance. The light rail runs right past the hotel, and while it's an easy connection on the rail to the museum district, the one rail line doesn't connect to much else.

I booked the Hotel Tomo because I got a good (for San Francisco) price for an en-suite room in a hotel not too close to Union Square. I was really pleased with the result. The staff were very helpful and the room very comfortable. I had asked for a room on a higher floor overlooking the courtyard and that is what I got. (I actually had a good view.) I had no trouble with noise.
The hotel was rather a long bus ride from the Ferry Building (I arrived and left by train), but the bus stop was right outside the hotel. I found the public transport system in SF to be excellent, and most of the places I wanted to visit were about the same distance from the hotel, so the location worked well that way.
I enjoyed staying in Japantown. I was in Japan in ----, and was able to find some dishes I remembered that aren't served in the Japanese restaurants where I live. I also visited the Kabuki spa for a shiatsu massage and soak in the baths, and highly recommend the experience. I was walking distance from a number of other restaurants on Fillmore Street, and never felt that the area was unsafe.

This hotel may not be the most glamorous in SF but it is really comfortable, has free parking and free wifi, is close to EVERYTHING or is close to fun transport options that will get you wherever you need to go. The hotel staff are really knowledgable and helpful and have hot coffee, tea or hit chocolate waiting for you whenever you want it. I would definitely stay here again.

Stayed here for - nights & had a room overlooking the bus depot, which wasn't the greatest. Noise early in the morning was also a problem from the buses. Infrastructure ie. heating-cooling units in the room & old. On our - week trip to the US we stayed in quite a few hotels, and this one was the most disappointing. The bathroom was tiny - like a closet.
Location is terrific.

We stayed for three nights (June ----). The location is good (walk to Penn Station, the High Line, restaurants on -th Ave.). The hotel is modest (tiny lobby, one slow elevator) but I've never encountered such friendly and helpful front desk service (I don't recall the name of the woman who was at the desk most of the time, but she never stopped smiling, always had a greeting for us, immediately helped with the baggage....). There was a good free breakfast (make your own waffles, yogurt, fresh fruit, cereal, eggs, sausage). The room was small but comfortable. Nothing fancy, but for the price, an excellent value for NYC.

We spent - nights in a king castia. The beds are wonderful, the cleaning staff the best I have ever seen. River ranch had a lot to do and the lazy river in a lot longer than it looks. The staff was very helpful. Only complaint is they charge for internet even in their buisness center. Would stay again !!

We booked our flight-hotel package on Expedia and ended up with a great rate for the Buena Vista. We were not disappointed. It's clean with newer carpeting and bathroom fixtures, but could use a paint job in some areas. The front desk staff were extremely friendly and helpful...all were younger males and were very professional. The hotel is a short walk to Fisherman's Wharf, cable cars, restaurants and shops. Very easy to walk around without taking a cab or bus. We took the Hop On - Hop Off city tour, which picked us up right in front of the hotel ($-- ea. for - days) and was well worth it. The first day we rode on the bus for the tour; the second day we did a lot of the stops. For the price, I would highly recommend Buena Vista Motor Inn. Other hotels directly in the Fisherman's Wharf District are about three times as much. The continental breakfast is excellent, too, with quality pastries! Like pretty much any hotel, request a top floor if you don't want to hear constant thumping above from people walking around.

I stayed at the hotel and towers for a conference and loved the place. The rooms were spacious, there was a coffee maker and a refrigerator, and the view over the river was beautiful. The hotel is very conveniently located and the outdoor patios are on the river. All personnel were courteous and helpful and check-in and check-out was a breeze.would definitely stay again and have been recommending it to friends.

Trying to stay within the Marriott family and not wanting to pay for parking, we found the Residence Inn. I’ve never stayed at any of their other Residence Inns, so I was pleasantly surprised with what we got.
After an easy check-in, we got back into our car to drive to our unit. It was easily a studio apartment with a king bed, pull out sofa bed, full kitchen (with a large fridge, stove, and microwave), desk, and a bathroom. I didn’t expect the whole kitchen part, so that was a nice plus. They also had free internet access in the rooms. (At the front desk, they make you sign a waiver saying you won’t throw any ‘parties’ in the rooms. Just an FYI in case that’s what you’re thinking!)
They have free hot breakfasts from - am to -- am on the weekends. I skipped Saturday morning, but the BF came back with bagels. On Sunday, they had other hot breakfast items available including tacos, waffles, yogurt, English muffins, bagels, granola, fresh fruit, etc. It's a pretty decent spread for breakfast. They also have other events going on throughout the week like happy hour that we didn’t get to check out.
We didn’t utilize the pool or the gym that’s open -- hours. 
The microwave popcorn and hot chocolate found in your room is a nice perk too. They even offer to do your grocery shopping for you for free! (You just pay for the groceries.)
My only real complaint was that we called the front desk to inquire about daily cleaning. Since it was after --, we wanted to make sure they could still clean our room. They said that housekeeping would be coming by shortly. When we returned after -, our room still had not been made up. We called the front desk again and they sent someone over right away. We had to sit around for half an hour while things were getting tidied and that affected our schedule a bit.
It’s located right off the freeway and very close to a choice of restaurants. 
$----night plus tax.

We stayed for - nights with our little dog,very friendly staff we were asked several times as we were coming in or out if everything was o.k. There were no problems. The room was large and clean. It was quiet and comfortable. Good place to stay and priced for longer stays. I will definetly stay there again!!

Stayed at the Yotel over the weekend and was very impressed. The thing I liked the best was the soft and white bedding. you could tell with total certainty that everything was clean. EVERYONE at the yotel was friendly and professional. Thanks for making our trip to NYC very enjoyable.

The Blakely is is comfortable is every way: the rooms are nicely furnished, the lnens are good quality, closets are roomy, the bathrooms are well-equipped, the tea-coffee self-service is convenient-- and it is nice having book shelves in the room, with hard-bound books !
The Blakely really distinguishes itself in *service* ! I requested a room with a quiet location, and the request was honored with courtesy. When I arrived, the front desk, serviced by Marleni, confirmed a dinner reservation, and Marleni also took care of requests for small problems with the bathroom tub-drain, quickly, efficiently, and courteously.
The hotel is located on a quiet (for NYC) side street, West --th, about a block from Sixth Avenue, and near Seventh Avenue-Broadway--Times Square -- but the feeling is """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""miles away"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" from the density of those areas.
The Blakely is great !
